title: Add error boundaries: global-error.tsx, error.tsx, and session error handling
body:
## Summary

Implement Next.js App Router error boundaries to prevent raw error pages from reaching users. Currently, one bad session payload crashes the entire dashboard with no recovery path.

## Philosophy

- Error boundaries are the **last resort** — inline errors for partial failures, boundaries for total failures
- `reset() + router.refresh()` together — reset alone won't re-fetch server data
- `dashboard-page-data.ts` silent catch stays as-is — partial dashboard > no dashboard

## Files to Create

### 1. Shared `ErrorDisplay` component (`components/ErrorDisplay.tsx`)

Reusable error UI component used across all error files:

```tsx
interface ErrorDisplayProps {
  title: string;
  message: string;
  icon?: 'error' | 'warning' | 'not-found';
  showReset?: boolean;
  onReset?: () => void;
  showReload?: boolean;
  showBackLink?: boolean;
  error?: Error; // For collapsible technical details
}
```

- Terminal-themed styling matching existing EmptyState pattern
- Dark theme first (root layout forces dark class)
- Design tokens: `--color-bg-base`, `--color-status-error`, `--color-text-muted`, `--color-border-subtle`
- Font: Geist Sans + JetBrains Mono

### 2. `app/global-error.tsx` (true catch-all)

Catches errors in root layout itself. **Must render full `<html>` and `<body>` tags** since it replaces the root layout.

Content:
- Terminal icon with error indicator
- "Something went wrong" heading
- "Try again" button (reset) + "Reload page" button (window.location.reload())
- Collapsible technical details (error.digest, stack)
- Full viewport dark background, centered card

### 3. `app/error.tsx` (route-level boundary)

Catches errors in all pages except root layout. Renders within existing layout (preserves sidebar/nav).

Content:
- Warning/alert icon
- "Something went wrong" / "The dashboard encountered an error"
- "Try again" button — **must call both reset() and router.refresh()**:
  ```tsx
  const handleReset = () => {
    reset();
    router.refresh(); // Re-fetches server data (critical!)
  };
  ```
- "Go to dashboard" link (/)
- Optional error digest

### 4. `app/sessions/[id]/error.tsx` (session-specific)

Content:
- Terminal with X icon
- "Failed to load session"
- Dynamic message based on error type (500, network, etc.)
- "Back to dashboard" link

### 5. Modify `app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`

- Replace manual error state (lines ~170-189) with error boundary handling
- Replace manual 404 handling with `notFound()` call:
  ```tsx
  // Before
  if (res.status === 404) { setError("Session not found"); }
  // After
  if (res.status === 404) { notFound(); }
  ```
- Remove `loading`, `error` state variables now handled by Next.js

**Note:** If page stays as client component, errors must be thrown during render for boundary to catch — errors in event handlers/useEffect won't trigger it.

## What NOT to Change

`lib/dashboard-page-data.ts` silent catch (lines 125-129) — keep it. Partial dashboard is better than no dashboard.

## Design Tokens

- Background: `--color-bg-base` (#0a0d12)
- Surface: `--color-bg-surface` (#1a1d22)
- Error: `--color-status-error` (#ef4444)
- Text: `--color-text-primary` (#f5f5f5), `--color-text-muted` (#8a8f98)
- Accent: `--color-accent` (#6366f1)
- Border: `--color-border-subtle` (#272a2f)
- Sans: `var(--font-geist-sans)`, Mono: `var(--font-jetbrains-mono)`

## Testing Scenarios

1. Throw error in root layout → `global-error.tsx` renders full page
2. Throw error in dashboard component → `error.tsx` renders within layout
3. Visit `/sessions/invalid-id` → `not-found.tsx` (see companion issue)
4. Click "Try again" → data re-fetches and re-renders

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Raw Next.js error pages never appear to users
- [ ] `reset()` actually re-fetches server data (router.refresh included)
- [ ] Partial dashboard data still renders (PR failure doesn't break sessions)
- [ ] Dark theme styling consistent across all error states
- [ ] ErrorDisplay component reused across all error files

title: Add 404 pages and loading states: not-found.tsx and loading.tsx
body:
## Summary

Implement Next.js App Router `not-found.tsx` and `loading.tsx` files for graceful 404 handling and route transition loading states. Companion to the error boundaries issue.

## Philosophy

- **404 is not an error** — use `notFound()` for missing resources, not error throwing
- **Simplicity over perfection** — simple spinners beat inaccurate skeleton layouts for v1
- Loading skeletons that don't match actual content look worse than a simple loader

## Files to Create

### 1. `app/not-found.tsx` (global 404)

Rendered when `notFound()` is called or route doesn't exist.

Content:
- Terminal icon (matching EmptyState pattern)
- "404" or "Page not found" heading
- "The page you're looking for doesn't exist."
- "← Back to dashboard" link

Design:
- Same styling as EmptyState component
- Muted text: `--color-text-muted`
- Link color: `--color-accent` (indigo)
- Centered layout

### 2. `app/sessions/[id]/not-found.tsx` (session-specific 404)

Rendered when `notFound()` is called from session page for invalid IDs.

Content:
- Terminal icon
- "Session not found" heading
- "The session you're looking for doesn't exist or has been deleted."
- "← Back to dashboard" link

This works with the `notFound()` call added in the error boundaries issue:
```tsx
if (res.status === 404) {
  notFound(); // triggers nearest not-found.tsx
}
```

### 3. `app/loading.tsx` (global loading)

Shown during initial page load and route transitions (Suspense fallback).

**v1 — Keep it simple:**
- Centered spinner or pulsing dot animation
- Optional "Loading..." text
- Full viewport dark background
- **No skeleton layouts** for v1 — add later when layout is stable

Design:
- Background: `--color-bg-base`
- Skeleton pulse: `--color-bg-subtle` → `--color-bg-elevated`
- Subtle `animate-pulse` or custom shimmer

### 4. `app/sessions/[id]/loading.tsx` (session loading)

Loading state for session detail page.

Content:
- Centered loading indicator
- "Loading session..." text
- Same styling as current manual loading state (replaces lines ~170-175 in page.tsx)

## Design Tokens

- Background: `--color-bg-base` (#0a0d12)
- Skeleton bg: `--color-bg-subtle`
- Skeleton highlight: `--color-bg-elevated`
- Text muted: `--color-text-muted` (#8a8f98)
- Accent/links: `--color-accent` (#6366f1)
- Radius: `--radius-md`
- Font: Geist Sans + JetBrains Mono, body size `text-[13px]`

## Error Flow (how 404s work)

```
User navigates to /sessions/abc
     |
     v
loading.tsx shown (Suspense)
     |
     v
Fetch session data
  - Success → render page
  - 404 → notFound() → render sessions/[id]/not-found.tsx
  - Error → throw → caught by error.tsx (separate issue)
```

```
User navigates to /nonexistent-page
     |
     v
No matching route → render app/not-found.tsx
```

## Testing Scenarios

1. Visit `/non-existent-route` → shows `app/not-found.tsx`
2. Visit `/sessions/invalid-id` → shows `sessions/[id]/not-found.tsx`
3. Throttle network, navigate between pages → loading.tsx appears
4. Navigate to session page → session loading.tsx appears briefly

## Out of Scope (v1)

- `prs/loading.tsx` — low priority, add later if needed
- Skeleton layouts matching exact page structure — too fragile, defer to v2
- `prs/error.tsx` — root `error.tsx` catches this already

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Invalid session IDs show proper 404, not error page
- [ ] Unknown routes show 404 page, not raw Next.js error
- [ ] Loading states appear during route navigation
- [ ] Dark theme styling consistent with dashboard
- [ ] Simple, clean loading indicators (no skeleton mismatch)

title: POST /api/verify returns 500 instead of 400 for malformed JSON
body:
## Problem

`POST /api/verify` currently returns a `500` when the request body contains malformed JSON.

Other POST API routes in the web app handle invalid JSON bodies explicitly and return `400 Invalid JSON body`, but `/api/verify` calls `req.json()` inside a broad `try/catch`, so parse failures fall through as server errors.

## Evidence

In `packages/web/src/app/api/verify/route.ts`, the route calls:

```ts
const body = await req.json();
```

inside a broad `try/catch`. If JSON parsing fails, the request falls through to the generic error handler and returns `500`.

Other POST routes already handle malformed JSON as `400`.

## Why it matters

Malformed JSON is a client error, not a server error. Returning `500` makes bad requests look like backend failures and is inconsistent with the other API routes.

## Expected

`POST /api/verify` should return `400` with an `Invalid JSON body` error for malformed request bodies.

title: Dashboard: Add multi-project support with project switcher
body:
## Problem

The AO dashboard currently only shows **one project** — whichever appears first in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`. This is hardcoded in `packages/web/src/lib/project-name.ts:15`:

```typescript
const firstKey = Object.keys(config.projects)[0];
```

This means if you have multiple projects configured (e.g., `epos`, `customer-app`, `personal-planner`), the dashboard only ever shows the first one. The Kanban board (Backlog → Plan → Working → Merge), the orchestrator sidebar, session cards, and Quick Actions all scope to that single project.

### Current Behavior

- Dashboard title always shows the first project name (e.g., "ao | DevPel EPOS")
- Session cards only show sessions matching the first project's prefix
- Orchestrator sidebar connects to the first project's orchestrator
- No way to switch between projects without restarting the dashboard or reordering the YAML
- The Inbox section already shows issues across projects (EPOS + Customer App cards visible), but clicking "start" scopes to the default project

### Impact

When spawning agents for a new project (e.g., `ao spawn personal-planner 1`), the session is invisible in the dashboard. Users must use `tmux attach` to monitor progress, losing the visual Kanban workflow, Quick Actions, and session management UI.

## Desired Behavior

1. **Project Switcher** — A dropdown/selector in the top-left (where "ORCHESTRATOR / DevPel EPOS" currently sits) that lists all projects from `agent-orchestrator.yaml`
2. **Per-Project Views** — Switching projects updates:
   - Kanban board (sessions filtered by project prefix)
   - Orchestrator sidebar (connects to that project's orchestrator tmux session)
   - Quick Actions (scoped to selected project)
   - Page title
3. **Cross-Project Overview** (stretch) — An "All Projects" view showing a summary card per project with session counts and status badges
4. **URL Routing** — Support `?project=personal-planner` query param so users can bookmark specific project views
5. **Inbox stays cross-project** — The Inbox section should continue showing issues from all projects regardless of selection

## Technical Context

### Files to Modify

- `packages/web/src/lib/project-name.ts` — Replace single-project lookup with multi-project support
- `packages/web/src/app/page.tsx` — Add project switcher component, pass selected project to child components
- `packages/web/src/app/layout.tsx` — Dynamic title based on selected project
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` — Accept project filter param
- `packages/web/src/app/api/orchestrator/` — Support connecting to different project orchestrators
- Dashboard components that reference `projectName` — make them project-aware

### Config Reference

```yaml
projects:
  epos:
    name: DevPel EPOS
    sessionPrefix: epos
  customer-app:
    name: Keatchen Customer App
    sessionPrefix: capp
  personal-planner:
    name: Personal Planner
    sessionPrefix: planner
```

Each project already has a unique `sessionPrefix` that can be used to filter tmux sessions (e.g., `1c29e45f3db8-planner-*` vs `1c29e45f3db8-epos-*`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Project switcher dropdown in dashboard header listing all YAML projects
- [ ] Selecting a project filters the Kanban board to that project's sessions
- [ ] Orchestrator sidebar connects to the selected project's orchestrator
- [ ] URL updates with `?project=<id>` for bookmarking
- [ ] Default to first project (backwards compatible)
- [ ] Inbox remains cross-project

title: Auto-resume worker sessions on respawn for same issue
body:
## Problem

When an AO worker session dies (crash, rate limit, OOM, manual kill) and is respawned for the same issue, the new worker starts from scratch — zero conversation history, no knowledge of previous attempts. It re-reads the issue, re-analyzes the codebase, and potentially repeats the exact mistake that caused the previous failure.

**The core gap:** AO already has a fully working session restore system (`ao session restore <id>`) that can resume agent conversations via `getRestoreCommand()`. But `spawn()` never uses it. The automated respawn path always calls `getLaunchCommand()` (fresh start) — even when a previous session for the same issue exists in the archive with full conversation history on disk.

## What Already Exists

- **`restore()` function** (`session-manager.ts:2199`) — complete, tested flow that finds archived sessions, validates restorability, restores workspaces, calls `getRestoreCommand()`, and resumes the agent conversation
- **`getRestoreCommand()` interface** (`types.ts:323`) — optional method on the `Agent` plugin interface
- **Claude Code implementation** — finds latest JSONL session file, returns `claude --resume <uuid>`
- **Codex implementation** — streams session file for thread ID, returns `codex resume <threadId>`
- **Metadata archive system** (`metadata.ts:184`) — archives full session metadata (issue, branch, PR, agent, worktree, etc.) when sessions are killed/cleaned
- **`ao session restore` CLI command** — user-facing manual restore that calls `restore()`

## What's Missing

### 1. `spawn()` never calls `getRestoreCommand()`

`spawn()` (`session-manager.ts:1060`) always uses `getLaunchCommand()`. It never checks for previous sessions for the same issue, never queries the archive, and never attempts to resume. The only exception is OpenCode's internal session ID reuse, which is agent-specific and doesn't go through `getRestoreCommand()`.

### 2. No archive search by issue ID

There's no generic function to find archived sessions by issue ID. `findOpenCodeSessionIds()` does this but is hardcoded to `agent=opencode`. We need a general-purpose `findArchivedSessionForIssue()` that searches archived metadata by issue ID and agent name.

### 3. OpenCode and Aider lack `getRestoreCommand()`

Only Claude Code and Codex implement `getRestoreCommand()`. OpenCode has a different session reuse mechanism (via `--session` flag) that only works during `spawn()`. Aider has no resume mechanism at all.

### 4. No context injection fallback

When native resume isn't possible (agent doesn't support it, session files corrupted, agent was switched), there's no mechanism to tell the new worker what the previous session did. Git commits, PR info, and agent summaries are all available in the archive and on the branch — but never injected into the new worker's prompt.

## Proposed Solution

### Fallback chain in `spawn()`:

```
1. workerRespawnStrategy == "fresh"? → skip, launch fresh (current behavior)
2. Previous archived session for this issue + agent? → NO → fresh
3. Agent implements getRestoreCommand()? → call it
   ├─ Returns command → native resume (claude --resume, codex resume)
   └─ Returns null → fall through
4. Build context from archived metadata + git history → prepend to prompt
   ├─ Context available → launch with context injection
   └─ No context → launch completely fresh
```

### Changes needed:

1. **`findArchivedSessionForIssue()` helper** — search archives by issue ID + agent name, return most recent match
2. **Modify `spawn()`** — add the fallback chain before `getLaunchCommand()` call
3. **`buildPreviousSessionContext()` helper** — extract context from archived metadata (summary, status, PR) and git history (commits on branch, modified files)
4. **`workerRespawnStrategy` config** — `"resume"` (default) | `"context-inject"` | `"fresh"` on `ProjectConfig`
5. **`resumedFrom` metadata field** — track session lineage (which session was resumed from)
6. **(Optional) OpenCode `getRestoreCommand()`** — delegate to `getLaunchCommand()` with stored session ID

### Files to modify:
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — `findArchivedSessionForIssue()`, `spawn()` modification
- `packages/core/src/session-context-builder.ts` — new file for `buildPreviousSessionContext()`
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — `workerRespawnStrategy` on `ProjectConfig`
- `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` — `resumedFrom` field
- `packages/plugins/agent-opencode/src/index.ts` — optional `getRestoreCommand()`

### Per-agent behavior after fix:

| Agent | Native Resume | Context Injection Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude --resume <uuid>` | If JSONL file missing/corrupt |
| Codex | `codex resume <threadId>` | If session file missing |
| OpenCode | Via `--session <id>` (if added) | Primary path otherwise |
| Aider | Not available | Always gets context injection |

## Design Doc

Full design doc with code snippets, edge cases, testing strategy, and risks: `docs/design-session-persistence-fix.md`

title: Claude Code bypass permissions prompt blocks worker sessions in tmux
body:
## Problem

After a recent Claude Code update (v2.1.x), the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag now shows an interactive confirmation prompt:

```
WARNING: Claude Code running in Bypass Permissions mode
...
❯ 1. No, exit
  2. Yes, I accept

Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel
```

This prompt requires user interaction (Down arrow + Enter to select "Yes, I accept"). Since AO worker sessions run inside tmux in detached/non-interactive mode, **no one is there to press the keys**. The session hangs on the prompt until it times out and exits.

**Impact:** All AO worker sessions using `permissions: "permissionless"` or `permissions: "auto-edit"` with the Claude Code agent are completely broken. Workers spawn, hit the prompt, and exit immediately — no work gets done.

## Root Cause

- `getLaunchCommand()` in `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` generates `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`
- Previously this flag skipped all permission prompts silently
- Now Claude Code requires interactive confirmation before entering bypass mode
- tmux sessions can't interact with the prompt

## Fix

Wrap the launch command with a background subshell that auto-accepts the prompt by sending keystrokes via `tmux send-keys` after a 3-second delay:

```bash
(sleep 3 && tmux send-keys -t "$AO_TMUX_NAME" Down Enter 2>/dev/null) & claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
```

- Background subshell waits for the prompt to appear (3s delay)
- Sends `Down` (select "Yes, I accept") + `Enter` (confirm) to the tmux pane
- Uses `$AO_TMUX_NAME` / `$AO_SESSION_NAME` env vars (already set by session manager) to target the correct pane
- `2>/dev/null` suppresses errors if the prompt was already dismissed
- Falls back silently — doesn't affect sessions that don't show the prompt

## Files Changed

- `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` — wrap launch command with auto-accept for bypass mode
- `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.test.ts` — updated tests to verify the wrapper is present

## Testing

- All 149 unit tests pass
- Verified live: spawned `ao-114` for issue #816, worker successfully auto-accepted the prompt and started working

title: feat(core): auto-resume worker sessions on respawn for same issue
body:
## Summary

Closes #816

When a worker session dies (crash, rate limit, OOM) and is respawned for the same issue, the new worker now attempts to resume from the previous session instead of starting from scratch. This eliminates wasted context-building time and prevents the new worker from repeating mistakes that caused the previous failure.

### Changes

- **`workerRespawnStrategy` config** (`types.ts`, `config.ts`): New per-project config with options `"resume"` (default), `"context-inject"`, or `"fresh"`
- **`resumedFrom` metadata field** (`types.ts`, `metadata.ts`): Tracks session lineage — which archived session a new session was resumed from
- **`findArchivedSessionForIssue()` helper** (`metadata.ts`): Searches archived metadata by issue ID + agent name, returns the most recent match
- **`session-context-builder.ts`** (new file): Builds context from archived metadata (summary, status, PR, branch) and git history (commits on branch), formats it as a prompt section
- **`spawn()` fallback chain** (`session-manager.ts`): Before launching fresh, checks for previous sessions and attempts resume:
  1. Strategy is `"fresh"` → skip (preserve current behavior)
  2. No previous archived session for this issue → fresh launch
  3. Agent supports `getRestoreCommand()` + strategy is `"resume"` → native resume (`claude --resume`, `codex resume`)
  4. Native resume unavailable/fails → inject context from previous session into prompt
  5. No context available → completely fresh launch

### Per-agent behavior

| Agent | Native Resume | Context Injection Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude --resume <uuid>` | If JSONL file missing/corrupt |
| Codex | `codex resume <threadId>` | If session file missing |
| OpenCode | Not yet implemented | Primary path |
| Aider | Not available | Always gets context injection |

## Test plan

- [x] `findArchivedSessionForIssue` — finds matching archived sessions, filters by issue+agent, returns most recent
- [x] `buildPreviousSessionContext` — extracts context from metadata, returns null when no useful context
- [x] `formatPreviousSessionContext` — formats context into prompt section with all fields
- [x] Spawn with archived session → injects context into prompt, sets `resumedFrom` metadata
- [x] Spawn with `workerRespawnStrategy: "fresh"` → no resume attempted
- [x] Spawn with `getRestoreCommand` returning command → uses native resume command
- [x] Spawn with `getRestoreCommand` returning null → falls back to context injection
- [x] Spawn with `workerRespawnStrategy: "context-inject"` → skips native resume
- [x] Spawn without issueId → no resume attempted
- [x] Spawn without archived session → fresh launch
- [x] All existing tests continue to pass (507 tests)
- [x] Build, typecheck, lint pass

Implements multi-project support as specified in [#813](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/813), enabling agent-orchestrator to manage multiple projects simultaneously from a single daemon instance.

### Core infrastructure (packages/core)
- **Global config registry** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`) — stores project identity (name, path, repo) and shadow copies of behavior config
- **Dual-mode config** — hybrid (local config + global shadow) and global-only modes
- **Config resolver** — assembles `OrchestratorConfig` from global registry entries + shadows
- **Local config parser** — flat behavior-only format (strips identity fields)
- **Auto-migration** — detects legacy single-project configs and registers them in the global registry
- **`loadConfig` fallback** — falls back to global registry when no local config file found

### CLI changes (packages/cli)
- **`ao start`** — registers project in global config, syncs shadow, starts lifecycle workers for ALL configured projects via `Promise.allSettled`
- **`ao spawn --project <id>`** — cross-project spawning from anywhere using global config
- **`ao status`** — falls back to global config, showing all registered projects
- **`ao batch-spawn --project`** — same cross-project support
- **Running state** — merges projects when another daemon is already running

### Dashboard changes (packages/web)
- **Portfolio page** at `/?project=all` — project cards with session counts, active/attention indicators
- **`/projects/[id]`** route — alias for project detail view
- **SSE events** carry `projectId` per session for multi-project filtering

### New types
- `GlobalConfig`, `ProjectRegistryEntry`, `ProjectShadow`, `ConfigMode`

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for global config loader, resolver, local config parser, migration
- [ ] CI: `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test`
- [ ] Manual: `ao start` creates global registry entry
- [ ] Manual: `ao status` from outside project dir shows all projects
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn --project <id>` from anywhere
- [ ] Manual: Dashboard portfolio page with multiple projects

Closes #813

title: fix: detect nested project directories in CLI auto-resolution
body:
## Summary
- fix project auto-detection for `ao start` and `ao spawn` when they are run from a nested directory inside a configured project
- share the path-matching logic in a small CLI helper so both commands resolve projects the same way
- prefer the deepest matching project path when configured project roots overlap

## Why
In a multi-project config, auto-detection was only checking for an exact cwd match against the configured project path. That works from the repo root, but it falls over in common monorepo workflows where commands are run from a nested package or app directory.

This change makes the resolution logic treat any cwd inside a configured project as a match, which feels closer to what users expect from the CLI.

## Testing
- `corepack pnpm -r build`
- `corepack pnpm lint`
- `corepack pnpm -r typecheck`
- `corepack pnpm -r --filter '!@composio/ao-web' test`

Lint completed with the repo's existing warnings, but no new errors were introduced.

title: feat(cli): shared credential resolver — read API keys from OpenClaw config
body:
## Summary

AO should resolve API keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.) from OpenClaw's stored config so users don't duplicate credentials across both tools. Today AO only reads `OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN` from `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` for the notifier path.

## Resolution Order (per roadmap doc)

```
1. Environment variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.)
2. AO config (~/.agent-orchestrator/config or agent-orchestrator.yaml)
3. OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json or ~/.openclaw/keys.json)
4. Prompt user (interactive only)
```

## Implementation

- New `packages/cli/src/lib/credential-resolver.ts` with a `resolveCredential(keyName, opts?)` function
- Reads OpenClaw's stored keys from `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (or wherever OpenClaw persists them)
- Wire into `ao start` / `ao spawn` key validation so agent plugins that need API keys can resolve them
- The existing notifier-openclaw token resolution in `packages/plugins/notifier-openclaw/src/index.ts:21-32` can serve as a reference pattern

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolveCredential("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")` checks env → AO config → OpenClaw config → returns null
- [ ] `ao start` uses the resolver for key validation during preflight
- [ ] `ao spawn` passes resolved keys to agent sessions
- [ ] If a key is found in OpenClaw config, AO uses it without prompting
- [ ] No behavior change if OpenClaw is not installed (resolver silently skips)

## References

- Existing token resolution: `packages/plugins/notifier-openclaw/src/index.ts:21-32`
- OpenClaw config path: `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`
- Roadmap doc: Task 6 (OpenClaw Integration) — "API Key Sharing from OpenClaw"

## Summary

`ao plugin install notifier-openclaw` in non-interactive mode (no TTY) currently installs the package but only prints "Run \`ao setup openclaw\` to finish configuration." The roadmap doc requires one-command, zero-manual-step installation in all modes.

## Current Behavior

- **TTY**: Installs package → runs `ao setup openclaw` wizard interactively → done ✓
- **Non-TTY**: Installs package → prints message → user must run setup separately ✗

## Proposed Fix

1. Accept `--url` and `--token` flags on `ao plugin install` so scripted/CI installs can pass credentials inline
2. When no flags and no TTY: auto-detect OpenClaw on localhost:18789, auto-generate token, run non-interactive setup with those defaults
3. The non-interactive setup path in `setup.ts` already supports `--url`, `--token`, and `--non-interactive` — just need to pipe them through from the install command

## Code Pointers

- Install setupAction handling: `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts:487`
- Non-interactive setup: `packages/cli/src/commands/setup.ts:219`
- Auto-detect: `packages/cli/src/lib/openclaw-probe.ts:88`
- Token auto-generation already exists in setup.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ao plugin install notifier-openclaw --url http://localhost:18789/hooks/agent --token mytoken` completes fully without prompts
- [ ] `ao plugin install notifier-openclaw` in non-TTY auto-detects OpenClaw and auto-generates token if gateway is reachable
- [ ] If gateway is unreachable and no flags provided in non-TTY, fails with actionable error instead of silently deferring
- [ ] TTY behavior unchanged

## References

- Roadmap doc: Task 6 — "`ao plugin install notifier-openclaw` handles install + config + validation in one command"

body:
## Problem

When I use the opencode agent, new .so files are continuously added to the /tmp directory after the ao start command is executed.  The file matchs .*-00000000.so

After an afternoon, the number of.so files had increased to more than 4000. After I executed the "ao stop --all" command, the.so files still existed.

## Why it matters

- After executed for a period of time, the machine resources are used up, causing the service to stop.

## root cause
After I run the ao start command, I find that the "/usr/local/lib/nodejs/node-v20.11.1-linux-x64/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/.opencode install --no-cache" command is continuously executed. Each time this command is executed, a new.so file is created in the /tmp directory. I think this is the root cause of the disk space exhaustion. 

However, I checked that opencode is already installed. After I run the 
node --input-type=module -e "import m from '@composio/ao-plugin-agent-opencode'; console.log(m.detect())" 
command, the command returns true, but the problem still occurs. 

Are there any good suggestions on this issue?

This keeps the feature small, but it makes the terminal workflow noticeably better for anyone monitoring active agent sessions in real time. It feels like a natural extension of `ao status` and does not change any existing session or orchestration behavior.

title: feat: inject checkpoint summary into session restore to prevent confused agent state
body:
## Problem

When `ao session restore` revives a crashed session, it recreates the tmux session and relies entirely on the agent's internal session resumption (e.g. `claude --resume`, OpenCode session reuse). There is **no validation** that the agent actually understands its restored state.

A crash mid-task can leave the agent in a half-baked mental state:
- Agent thinks it committed a file, but the commit never happened
- Agent thinks it completed step 3 of 5, but step 3 was only half-done
-  - Staged/unstaged git changes don't match the agent's conversation history
- Half-written files on disk that the agent doesn't re-read

The lifecycle manager's CI feedback loop catches *some* of this reactively (broken code → CI fail → route errors back), but there's no **proactive** validation at restore time.

## Proposed Solution

Inject a **checkpoint summary** into the agent's context immediately after restore, giving it ground truth about the actual workspace state.

### 1. Periodic checkpoint writing (lifecycle manager)

During each poll cycle, for sessions with `status=working`, snapshot the git state:



### 2. Post-restore injection (session manager)

In `restore()`, after the agent boots:
- Read `git status --porcelain`, `git log --oneline -3`, `git diff --stat`
- Read the checkpoint file if it exists
- Compose a summary message and send it to the agent:



### 3. New module: `packages/core/src/checkpoint.ts
- `writeCheckpoint(session, sessionsDir)` — called by lifecycle manager
- `buildCheckpointSummary(session, workspacePath)` — called by restore

## Files to Change

- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — `restore()`: inject checkpoint after agent boots
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — `pollAll()`: write periodic checkpoints
- `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` — optionally add checkpoint awareness to base prompt
- **New:** `packages/core/src/checkpoint.ts` — checkpoint read/write logic

## Why This Matters

Without this, restore is "optimistic replay" — works great for idle-point crashes, poorly for mid-operation crashes. This turns it into "informed resume" — the agent gets ground truth and can self-correct before continuing.

The existing CI feedback loop remains as a safety net, but this prevents the broken code from being pushed in the first place.

title: feat: inject checkpoint summary into session restore to prevent confused agent state (#842)
body:
## Problem

When `ao session restore` revives a crashed session, it relies entirely on the agent's internal session resumption (e.g. `claude --resume`). There's no validation that the agent's conversation history matches the actual workspace state.

A crash mid-task can leave the agent confused:
- Agent thinks it committed a file, but the commit never happened
- Staged/unstaged git changes don't match the agent's memory
- Half-written files on disk that the agent doesn't re-read
- Agent skips or duplicates steps based on stale conversation history
The CI feedback loop catches some damage reactively, but broken code gets pushed before it's caught.

## Solution

Three-part checkpoint system that gives agents ground truth on restore:

### 1. Periodic checkpoints (`checkpoint.ts` — new module)
- `writeCheckpoint()` snapshots git state (commits, staged/modified/untracked files, branch)
- Called by the lifecycle manager every poll cycle for `status=working` sessions
- Atomic writes (tmp → rename) prevent half-written checkpoint files
- Stored in `sessionsDir` alongside metadata — survives worktree deletion

### 2. Post-restore injection (`session-manager.ts`)
- After `restore()` boots the agent, builds a ground-truth summary:
  - Live `git log`, `git status`, `git diff --stat`
  - Last saved checkpoint for comparison
  - Clear instructions to verify state before continuing
- Waits for agent readiness, then sends via `runtime.sendMessage()`
- Non-fatal — agent still works if injection fails

### 3. Agent prompt awareness (`prompt-builder.ts`)
- New "Session Restore" section in `BASE_AGENT_PROMPT`
- Tells agents to trust git state over their memory on restore
- Instructs agents to check for half-written files before editing

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/core/src/checkpoint.ts` | **New** — `writeCheckpoint()` + `buildCheckpointSummary()` |
| `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` | Import + call `writeCheckpoint()` for working sessions |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | Import + inject checkpoint summary in `restore()` |
| `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` | Add "Session Restore" section to base agent prompt |
| `packages/core/src/__tests__/checkpoint.test.ts` | **New** — 9 test cases covering write, read, summary, edge cases |

## Design Decisions

- **Best-effort, never fatal** — checkpoint failures are silently swallowed. A broken checkpoint must never crash the poll loop or block restore.
- **No external dependencies** — `checkpoint.ts` implements its own atomic write instead of importing `atomicWriteFileSync`, keeping it self-contained.
- **Minimal schema validation** — `readCheckpoint()` checks 3 key fields instead of full Zod validation. Corrupted files gracefully degrade to "no checkpoint found."
- **Checkpoint stored in sessionsDir, not worktree** — survives worktree deletion and recreation during restore.

## Test Results
9/9 passing:
- `writeCheckpoint`: valid JSON, detects untracked/staged files, skips missing workspace
- `buildCheckpointSummary`: includes git state, includes saved checkpoint, handles missing/corrupted checkpoints, returns null for missing workspace

Closes #842

title: feat(cli): add plugin resolution checks to ao doctor
body:
## What changed and why

`ao doctor` already did a good job checking install and runtime health, but it did not verify whether the plugins referenced by the current config were actually resolvable. In practice, that means missing plugin dependencies or config typos often show up later in `ao start`, `ao status`, lifecycle polling, or notifier flows instead of in the command that is supposed to catch setup problems early.

This change adds a config-aware plugin resolution pass to `ao doctor`.

It checks:
- default runtime, agent, and workspace plugins
- per-project runtime, agent, workspace, tracker, and SCM plugin references
- notifier plugins declared in `notifiers`
- notifier references used by `defaults.notifiers`
- notifier references used by `notificationRouting`

It also updates `ao doctor --test-notify` to resolve notifier aliases through the same logic, so configurations like `alerts -> slack` are tested correctly instead of being treated as missing plugins.

## How to test

I validated this in the same order the repo expects contributors to use:

- `pnpm -r build`
- `pnpm -r --filter !@composio/ao-web test`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm -r typecheck`

Targeted coverage added in `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/doctor.test.ts` covers:
- successful plugin resolution for configured defaults and project overrides
- failure when a referenced plugin cannot be loaded
- notifier alias resolution during `ao doctor --test-notify`

Manual spot checks:
- run `ao doctor` with a config that references a missing plugin and confirm it fails with a clear message
- run `ao doctor --test-notify` with a notifier alias such as `alerts: { plugin: slack }` and confirm the alias is resolved to the underlying plugin

## Why this is useful

This makes `ao doctor` more valuable as the first stop for environment and config debugging. Instead of discovering plugin problems only after a start or status command fails, the install health check now surfaces them directly and points at the config location that introduced the reference.

title: feat: Option C foundation + dev-mode dashboard fix

## Summary

- Adds `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()` to the lifecycle manager that fetches individual CI check details and sends them to worker sessions when CI fails
- Follows the same fingerprinting/deduplication pattern as the existing `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog()` for review comments
- On first transition to `ci_failed`, the existing static reaction message fires; on the next poll cycle, detailed CI failure info (check names, statuses, URLs) is dispatched
- New or changed failures trigger fresh notifications; unchanged failure sets are deduplicated
- Tracking metadata is cleared when CI passes, or when the PR is merged/closed

## How it works

1. **Transition poll**: Session transitions to `ci_failed` → existing reaction sends configured static message (e.g., "CI is failing. Fix it.")
2. **Next poll**: `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()` fetches `getCIChecks()`, filters failures, formats a detailed message with check names and URLs, sends to agent
3. **Subsequent polls**: Same failure fingerprint → no re-send. Different failures → new detailed message dispatched
4. **Recovery**: When CI passes or PR closes, metadata tracking is cleared

title: ci: fix deploy by using correct RSA SSH host fingerprint
body:
## What's an SSH fingerprint?

When GitHub Actions SSHs into the VPS, the server presents its public host key to prove its identity. A fingerprint is just a short hash of that public key — it's how you verify you're talking to the right server and not an impostor.

Without a pinned fingerprint, the SSH client connects with `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`, meaning it'll accept any server claiming to be your VPS (MITM risk).

## Why it was failing

We originally pinned the ED25519 fingerprint (`SHA256:mlWd4p7TXI...`), but `appleboy/ssh-action` negotiates RSA. Fingerprints are per key type, so it compared the RSA host key against the ED25519 fingerprint — mismatch, deploy failed.

## Fix

Replace ED25519 fingerprint with the RSA fingerprint. These are both from the same VPS — just different key types.

**Verify independently:**
```bash
ssh-keyscan 91.107.194.138 2>/dev/null | ssh-keygen -lf -
# Should include: SHA256:Yat7fObKrTBZGxr0HGlN40oWhC/LlLN9SpjzPifsLzw (RSA)
```

title: Replace tmux messaging with file-based communication protocol
body:
## Problem

The current orchestrator to agent communication uses tmux send-keys to send messages and tmux capture-pane to read output. This is approximately 70 to 80 percent reliable with the following failure modes:

**Message clobbering.** send-keys injects text regardless of whether the agent is mid-thought, bypassing busy detection.

**Multi-line breakage.** Some runtimes (Codex) cannot handle multi-line input via tmux.

**Long prompt mangling.** Prompts over 2000 characters get corrupted via send-keys or paste-buffer. The codebase already works around this by writing prompts to files.

**No reverse channel.** Agents cannot report back to the orchestrator. Once spawned, they are isolated.

**No idle delivery.** tmux cannot reliably deliver messages to an idle agent. The TUI layer (Ink) interprets piped input differently from physical keypresses.

---

## Phase 1: Communication Protocol

Replace tmux send-keys and capture-pane with file-based JSONL communication. tmux remains for process spawning and interactive human access. Only the messaging channel changes.

### File Layout

```
~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}/sessions/{sessionName}/
    inbox                 orchestrator to agent, JSONL
    agent-events          agent to system, JSONL, only agent writes
    system-events         system to processing layer, JSONL, only lifecycle worker writes
    inbox.cursor          byte offset tracking
    agent-events.cursor   lifecycle worker read cursor
    system-events.cursor  lifecycle worker read cursor
```

Two separate event files. agent-events written only by the agent. system-events written only by the lifecycle worker. Single writer per file. No locking needed.

### Message Format

JSONL. One JSON object per line, append only:

```jsonl
{"v":1,"id":42,"epoch":3,"ts":"2026-03-28T14:30:00Z","source":"agent","type":"escalation","category":"stuck","severity":"high","message":"Cannot resolve merge conflict"}
```

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| v | Schema version (currently 1) |
| id | Monotonic counter per session |
| epoch | Session generation counter. Increments on respawn. Stale epoch messages discarded |
| ts | ISO 8601 timestamp |
| source | "agent" or "system" (event stream messages only) |
| type | Message category |

Inbox messages (orchestrator to agent) additionally carry:

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| dedup | Idempotency key. Prevents duplicate processing on retry |

Concurrent inbox writes (from lifecycle worker, session manager, ao send CLI) are safe. On both macOS (APFS/HFS+) and Linux (ext4), the kernel serializes write() syscalls with O_APPEND through vnode/inode locks. Messages must stay under 4KB.

### Message Types

**Agent events (agent writes):**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| escalation | Agent needs help (stuck, needs input) |
| file_report | Files agent is editing (full snapshot) |
| status | Progress update |
| completion | Task finished |
| ack | Confirms receipt of inbox message |

**System events (lifecycle worker writes):**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| ci_failure | CI checks failing |
| ci_recovery | CI now passing |
| review_pending | PR has review comments |
| review_approved | PR approved |
| merge_conflict | PR has conflicts |
| merge_ready | Approved and CI green |

Agents do NOT report CI or PR status. The lifecycle worker detects these deterministically via SCM plugins.

**Inbox messages (orchestrator to agent):**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| instruction | New task or guidance |
| resolution | Resolved an escalation |
| warning | File conflict alert |
| abort | Stop current work |
| context | Additional context |

### File Watching

fs.watch() on the session events directory. Instant trigger on file change. No polling. On trigger: read from byte offset in cursor file, parse new JSONL lines, update cursor. O(new messages) per trigger. Corrupt JSONL lines logged and skipped. Cursor not advanced past parse failure at end of file to handle partial writes.

### Orchestrator Context Injection

When a message needs to reach the orchestrator agent, it is written to the orchestrator session's inbox file. The orchestrator reads it via three layered mechanisms:

**1. Claude Agent SDK stdin pipe (solves the idle agent gap).** The orchestrator is spawned via the Claude Agent SDK with input-format stream-json. The lifecycle worker holds the stdin pipe. Writing an NDJSON user message to stdin creates a new conversation turn instantly, even when idle. This is the same protocol Anthropic's VS Code extension uses. 100 percent reliable.

**2. PostToolUse hook with additionalContext.** After every tool call, a hook reads the inbox and outputs new messages via additionalContext JSON. Injected directly into context. 10,000 character cap. Covers active agents between tool calls.

**3. Stop hook.** Before the agent goes idle, checks inbox. Unread messages trigger exit code 2 with feedback, preventing idle. Catches the transition into idle.

SDK stdin for idle agents. PostToolUse for active agents. Stop hook prevents going idle with unread messages. No gaps.

For Codex: app-server JSON-RPC, turn/start when idle. AO already has a client.

For OpenCode: plugin hook tool.execute.after fires after every tool call.

### Transport Wrapper

A wrapper that composes with the existing runtime for spawning and uses file-based protocol for communication:

| Method | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| create() | Delegates to inner runtime for process spawning. Creates inbox, agent-events, system-events files. Establishes SDK stdin pipe for supported runtimes |
| destroy() | Delegates to inner runtime. Deletes communication files |
| isAlive() | Delegates PID check to inner runtime |
| sendMessage() | Appends JSONL to inbox file first (persistent record), then pushes via SDK stdin pipe (delivery optimization) |
| getOutput() | Reads new JSONL from agent-events |

Same Runtime interface. Drop-in replacement.

### Control Flow

**Read path:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Agent] -->|writes| B[agent-events]
    C[Lifecycle Worker] -->|writes| D[system-events]
    B -->|fs.watch| E[Processing Layer]
    D -->|fs.watch| E
    E -->|auto-resolve| F[Write to agent inbox]
    E -->|needs orchestrator| G[Write to orchestrator inbox]
    G -->|orchestrator resolves| F
    E -->|unresolvable| H[Notify Human]
```

**Write path:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Orchestrator] -->|decides resolution| B[Session Manager]
    B -->|appends JSONL + dedup key| C[inbox]
    C -->|agent reads| D[Agent]
    D -->|writes ack| E[agent-events]
    E -->|confirms delivery| F[Processing Layer]
```

The processing layer runs as an independent fs.watch() event listener inside the lifecycle worker process. Separate from the existing pollAll() loop.

---

## Phase 2: Processing Layer and Escalation

Built on top of the Phase 1 protocol. The processing layer reads both event streams and makes routing decisions.

### Retry Tracking

Processing layer maintains per-session, per-event-type state:

```
Map<sessionId:eventType, {
  attempts: number,
  lastPrCommentId: string,
  firstAttemptAt: timestamp
}>
```

Config-driven limits via ReactionConfig. After N failed attempts for the same event type since the last PR comment, stop retrying. Escalate to orchestrator with summary: "attempted N times, injected failing context N times, still failing. Can you take over?" Counter resets when a new PR comment arrives.

### Escalation Chain

Three tiers:
1. Auto-resolve: rule-based actions (retry CI, rebase). Write resolution directly to agent inbox.
2. Orchestrator: forward summarized escalation (under 2000 tokens per cycle) to orchestrator. Orchestrator reasons and writes resolution back.
3. Human: notify via configured notifiers. Human sends guidance via ao send.

If orchestrator does not respond within 10 minutes, escalate directly to human.

### Event Deduplication

Fingerprint: sessionId + type + category. 5 minute sliding window. Same CI failure detected 10 times in a row gets processed once.

### Event Superseding

ci_recovery cancels pending ci_failure retries. merge_ready cancels pending merge_conflict retries. When a superseding event arrives, retry tracker for the superseded category is cleared.

---

## Phase 3: Coordination and Reliability

Built on top of Phase 1 protocol and Phase 2 processing layer.

### File Conflict Detection

Agent writes file_report (full snapshot of files being edited) to agent-events. Processing layer maintains an ownership map. When a second agent reports the same file, conflict is detected. Warning written to the second agent's inbox. Ownership resolved by message timestamp (earlier claim wins).

### Session Respawn and Epoch Replay

When a session dies and gets restored:
1. Epoch increments in metadata
2. Replay all unacked inbox messages from previous epoch
3. Replayed messages rewritten with new epoch
4. New agent processes them
5. Event stream messages with stale epoch discarded

Prevents silent message loss when an agent dies between receiving an instruction and acknowledging it.

### Cross-Runtime Support

| Runtime | Injection Mechanism | Status |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| Claude Code | SDK stdin pipe + PostToolUse additionalContext + Stop hook | Validated |
| Codex | app-server JSON-RPC turn/start. Add turnSteer() for abort | Validated |
| OpenCode | Plugin tool.execute.after hook + MCP tools | Validated |
| Cursor | .cursor/rules/ auto rule | Needs validation |
| Copilot | Layer 1 prompt instructions | Fallback only |

### Path Discovery for User-Spawned Runtimes

comms.json at {project-root}/.ao/comms.json for runtimes AO does not spawn (Cursor, Copilot). Contains session name, epoch, inbox and events paths. Created on spawn, updated on restore, removed on kill. Regenerated from session metadata on AO restart.

---

## Key Requirements

| # | Requirement | Phase | Status |
|---|-------------|-------|--------|
| 1 | 100% message delivery | 1 | File on disk = delivered. SDK stdin for context injection |
| 2 | Bidirectional communication | 1 | inbox + agent-events |
| 3 | Replace tmux messaging | 1 | sendMessage() appends to inbox. getOutput() reads agent-events |
| 4 | Idle agent delivery | 1 | SDK stdin pipe creates new conversation turn instantly |
| 5 | System events from lifecycle worker | 1 | CI, PR reviews detected deterministically |
| 6 | Retry tracking with config-driven limits | 2 | Stop infinite loops, escalate with summary |
| 7 | Escalation chain (auto-resolve, orchestrator, human) | 2 | Three tiers, summarize under 2000 tokens |
| 8 | File conflict detection | 3 | Ownership map from file_report snapshots |
| 9 | Epoch replay on respawn | 3 | Replay unacked messages, discard stale epoch |
| 10 | Cross-runtime support | 3 | Validated for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode |

---

## Prior Art

| System | Approach | Takeaway |
|--------|----------|----------|
| Claude Agent SDK (Anthropic) | NDJSON over stdin/stdout | Official protocol for programmatic Claude Code communication. Solves idle delivery |
| Codex app-server (OpenAI) | JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout | Official protocol for programmatic Codex communication |
| Claude Code Agent Teams | JSON inbox files per agent, zero servers | File-based IPC works for local orchestration |
| CAO (AWS Labs) | SQLite inbox, idle detection watchdog | Don't interrupt active agents |
| Spotify (Honk) | Background agent research | Over 2000 tokens per cycle causes 15 to 25 percent degradation |

title: Proposal: Replace split-brain architecture with durable JSONL append-only event log
body:
## **Problem**

The current orchestrator relies on dual state management - an ephemeral in-memory `Map<SessionId, SessionStatus>` in `lifecycle-manager.ts` and a persistent flat-file `metadata.ts`. This split-brain architecture could create fragility, particularly during unexpected process termination.

The approach has the following known failure modes:

* **Lifecycle Manager Restart = State Loss** — If the lifecycle worker crashes, times out, or restarts, all tracked `statesMap` entries are instantly lost from memory.
* **Stale Metadata Fallback** — On restart, the system falls back to reading status from flat-file metadata. Because flat files lack transactional guarantees, they may contain stale values (e.g., marking an agent as "working" when the process has already exited).
* **Checkpoint/Resume Gap** — There is no mechanism to checkpoint lifecycle state mid-poll. If a crash occurs during `pollAll()`, the system restarts and re-evaluates all sessions from scratch without knowing what was already successfully processed.
* **Race Conditions in Concurrent Updates** — Multiple lifecycle workers or concurrent polling calls can write conflicting metadata updates. `atomicWriteFileSync` ensures single-file atomicity, but not cross-session consistency.
* **No Distributed Coordination** — Running multiple orchestrator instances (for HA or multi-project setups) lacks a coordination mechanism, leading to competing instances overwriting each other's metadata.

## **Proposed Solution**

Replace the ephemeral in-memory Map and monolithic flat-file overwrites with an **Append-Only Event Log using JSON Lines (.jsonl)**. 

Instead of constantly updating a single state object and writing it to disk, every state transition is recorded as an immutable event appended to a log. This provides a crash-safe, lock-free single source of truth that remains entirely human and LLM-readable.

## **Architecture / Data Layout**

State will be centralized into a single event log per project config. The directory path is resolved dynamically via `getProjectBaseDir(config.configPath, projectId)`:

```plaintext
~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/state/
    events.jsonl       # NEW: Append-only JSON Lines event log
```
## **Why Append-Only JSONL:**

| Property | Monolithic Flat File (Current) | Append-Only JSONL (Proposed) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Crash Safety** | Subject to corruption if process dies mid-write. | High. Atomic appends mean only the last unwritten line is lost on crash. |
| **Concurrency** | File-level lock only, prone to race conditions. | Multiple writers can safely append to the stream. |
| **Human Readability** | High, but only shows the *current* state. | High. Shows the full historical timeline of session states. |
| **LLM / Agent Integration** | Native JSON/TS is easily parsed. | Native JSON is easily parsed and generated line-by-line. |
| **Complexity** | Low. | Low. Requires no native C++ bindings or external database engines. |

## **Event Schema**

Instead of SQL tables, the log relies on a strict TypeScript interface for events. Every line in `events.jsonl` is a valid, stringified JSON object representing a specific transition in a session's lifecycle.

```json
{"timestamp": 1712300000, "sessionId": "sess_123", "projectId": "proj_abc", "status": "initializing", "metadata": {}}
{"timestamp": 1712300005, "sessionId": "sess_123", "projectId": "proj_abc", "status": "working", "transition_count": 1}
{"timestamp": 1712300010, "sessionId": "sess_456", "projectId": "proj_abc", "status": "error", "error_reason": "timeout"}
{"timestamp": 1712300045, "sessionId": "sess_123", "projectId": "proj_abc", "status": "completed", "transition_count": 2}
```
## Control Flow

### Read/Write Path (Normal Operation)

1. **Initialize & Hydrate:** On orchestrator startup, the system reads `events.jsonl` sequentially from top to bottom. It "replays" the events to reconstruct the current state of all sessions into the in-memory Map. 
2. **Poll Cycle:** The lifecycle manager evaluates sessions.
3. **State Update:** When a session's status changes, a new `SessionEvent` JSON object is created. The orchestrator stringifies it and appends it to `events.jsonl` with a newline character `\n`. This write is extremely fast and lock-free.
4. **Log Compaction (Periodic):** To prevent infinite file growth, a background task periodically reads the current computed state and rewrites a fresh `events.jsonl` containing only the latest known state for active sessions, archiving the old history.

### Crash Recovery Path

1. **Restart:** Lifecycle manager starts up after an unexpected termination.
2. **Parse:** The `hydrate()` function reads `events.jsonl`.
3. **Graceful Recovery:** If the file contains a partial or corrupted JSON string at the very end (e.g., due to a power loss mid-write), the parser safely discards that specific line and recovers the rest of the exact state up to the millisecond before the crash.

---

## Requirements

| # | Requirement | Implementation Strategy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **100% State Persistence** | Append-only logs survive unexpected crashes without corrupting previous entries. |
| **2** | **No Native Dependencies** | Uses standard Node.js `fs` module; no C++ compilation or heavy DB binaries required. |
| **3** | **LLM/Agent Accessibility** | State remains entirely in plain-text JSON, easily readable by support teams and AI agents. |
| **4** | **Auditability** | The log inherently provides a complete timeline of how and when an agent transitioned states. |
| **5** | **Backwards Compatible** | Can be seeded from existing `metadata.ts` files on first run via a migration script. |

---

## Roadblocks & Mitigations

* **File Size & Infinite Growth**
  * *Limitation:* Long-running orchestrators will generate massive `.jsonl` files over time.
  * *Mitigation:* Implement a `compactLog()` utility that squashes the history down to the current state representation when the file exceeds a certain size threshold (e.g., 5MB).

* **I/O Bottlenecks on Large Hydrations**
  * *Limitation:* Reading a massive file line-by-line on boot could slow down startup.
  * *Mitigation:* Node's `readline` module is highly optimized for this. Combined with log compaction, startup hydration will remain sub-100ms.

* **Migration from Legacy Files**
  * *Limitation:* Existing users have state entirely locked in `metadata.ts`.
  * *Mitigation:* Implement a one-time startup migration script that reads the legacy file and converts its final state into the initial entries of the new `events.jsonl` log.

title: fix: resolve @composio/core module not found in dev server
body:
## Summary

title: feat: support multiple concurrent orchestrators with isolated worktrees
body:
## Summary

Implements support for multiple concurrent orchestrators on the same project, each running in an isolated git worktree.

- Adds \`useWorktree?: boolean\` to \`OrchestratorSpawnConfig\` — when \`true\`, each \`spawnOrchestrator\` call gets a unique numbered identity (\`{prefix}-orchestrator-N\`) and creates an isolated git worktree on branch \`orchestrator/{sessionId}\`, enabling multiple orchestrators to work on the same project concurrently without conflicts
- Adds \`reserveNextOrchestratorIdentity\` helper that atomically reserves the next available \`-orchestrator-N\` slot by scanning both active and archived session IDs
- Updates \`isOrchestratorSessionRecord\` (private) and \`isOrchestratorSessionName\` (CLI) to recognize the new \`{prefix}-orchestrator-N\` ID pattern, with the regex anchored to the project prefix to prevent false-positives when \`sessionPrefix\` itself ends with \`-orchestrator\`
- Updates \`getProjectPause\` to pre-filter orchestrator session candidates by name pattern before any file I/O (avoids reading metadata for every worker session)
- Fixes \`send\` and \`claimPR\` to pass \`sessionPrefix\` to \`isOrchestratorSessionRecord\` so \`-orchestrator-N\` sessions are correctly exempt from pause blocks and PR dedup
- Fixes \`repairSingleSessionMetadataOnRead\` and \`repairSessionMetadataOnRead\` to accept and forward \`sessionPrefix\` so worktree orchestrators with missing/corrupted \`role\` metadata are still identified correctly
- Isolates the system prompt file per orchestrator session (\`orchestrator-prompt-{sessionId}.md\`) to prevent concurrent writes to the same file
- Cleans up the created worktree and reserved metadata on every failure path in \`spawnOrchestrator\`: workspace creation failure, intermediate steps (\`setupWorkspaceHooks\`, system prompt write, \`resolveOpenCodeSessionReuse\`), runtime creation failure, and post-launch failure
- Existing single-orchestrator behavior (\`{prefix}-orchestrator\`, project root as workspace, reuse/delete strategies) is fully preserved when \`useWorktree\` is \`false\`/unset

## Test plan

- [ ] \`pnpm --filter @composio/ao-core test\` — all 84 spawn tests pass
- [ ] \`pnpm --filter @composio/ao-cli test\` — session-utils tests pass
- [ ] \`spawnOrchestrator({ useWorktree: true })\` creates session \`{prefix}-orchestrator-1\`, calls \`workspace.create\` with branch \`orchestrator/{prefix}-orchestrator-1\`
- [ ] Second concurrent call creates \`{prefix}-orchestrator-2\` with its own worktree
- [ ] Workspace creation failure deletes the reserved metadata entry
- [ ] Intermediate failure (hooks setup, prompt write) destroys the worktree and deletes metadata
- [ ] Runtime creation failure destroys the worktree and deletes metadata
- [ ] A pause set by an \`-orchestrator-N\` session blocks worker spawns/sends but not other orchestrators
- [ ] Worktree orchestrator with missing \`role\` metadata is still repaired correctly (not treated as a worker)
- [ ] Existing single-orchestrator (\`{prefix}-orchestrator\`) tests unchanged

title: fix: prompt delivery retry
body:
### What changed and why
Previously, if the initial post-launch prompt failed to deliver to a spawned agent (e.g., due to timing issues in tmux), it would fail silently and the session would sit idle in `needs_input`. No one was notified, resulting in wasted time.

This PR fixes this silent failure by:
* **Adding Robust Retries:** Replaced the static 5-second delay in `session-manager.ts` with a 3-attempt retry loop using exponential backoff (3s, 6s, 9s).
* **Explicit Error Logging:** Errors are no longer swallowed; if all 3 retries fail, an explicit error is logged.
* **Metadata Tracking:** Added the `session.metadata.promptDelivered` flag to track whether the prompt actually made it to the agent.
* **User Notifications:** Updated the CLI (`spawn.ts`) to check this metadata flag. If delivery fails, it now outputs a warning instructing the user to manually intervene using `ao send`.

### How to test it
1. **Local Sanity:** Run `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-core test` and `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-cli test`. 
2. **Happy Path:** Run `ao spawn <test-issue-url>`. Verify that the agent successfully receives the prompt and begins working.
3. **Forced Failure:** Temporarily add a `throw new Error('test')` inside the prompt delivery try-block in `session-manager.ts`. Run `ao spawn <test-issue-url>` and verify that the CLI waits through the retries and then explicitly outputs the `⚠ Prompt delivery failed` warning.

### Related Issues
Closes #718

---
✅ **Tests Passed:** Successfully ran and passed all 823 unit tests across `core` and `cli` locally.

title: ao start mis-detects dev mode for npm-linked installs
body:
## Bug

`ao start` can incorrectly launch the dashboard/runtime in **dev mode** for users who installed AO via a symlinked install method such as `npm link` (or any install path that resolves back to the source tree), even when they intended to use the installed CLI normally.

This causes unexpected dev-style terminal logging and behavior even though the user did **not** run `pnpm dev`.

## Observed Behavior

A user installs AO with `setup.sh`, runs:

```bash
ao start
```

and AO starts in a mode that behaves like development mode, logging directly in the terminal.

The user root-caused this to the dev/prod detection heuristic in `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`:

```ts
const isDevMode = existsSync(resolve(webDir, "server"));
```

The current logic assumes:
- `packages/web/server/` exists → run dev mode (`pnpm run dev`)
- otherwise → run production mode (`node dist-server/start-all.js`)

## Root Cause

This heuristic relies on the **filesystem layout** of the package rather than the **intended runtime mode**.

When AO is installed via `npm link`, the installed package is a symlink to the local source tree. The source tree contains `packages/web/server/`, so this check always returns true.

That means:
- linked installs are treated as dev installs
- `ao start` enters dev mode unexpectedly
- normal installed-CLI expectations are violated

In short: **source tree shape is being used as a proxy for runtime mode, and that proxy breaks for symlinked installs.**

## Why This Matters

For end users, `ao start` should default to the normal installed runtime behavior unless they explicitly opt into development mode.

Current behavior is surprising because:
- users did not ask for dev mode
- linked/package-manager install methods should not silently change runtime semantics
- dev mode can have noisier logs, different startup assumptions, and potentially different dependency expectations

## Proposed Fix

### Principle

**Do not infer dev mode from the existence of a source directory.**

Prefer explicit or artifact-based detection instead.

### Recommended approach

1. **Add an explicit runtime mode switch**
   - `ao start --dev`
   - optional env override such as `AO_DEV=1`

2. **Default to production behavior for installed CLI usage**
   - If production build artifacts exist, run production.
   - Only run dev mode when explicitly requested.

3. **Use build-artifact checks instead of source-tree checks**
   - Example: check for `dist-server/start-all.js` or equivalent built output
   - Do **not** use `existsSync(resolve(webDir, "server"))` as the deciding factor

### Suggested implementation outline

Pseudo-flow:

```ts
const forceDev = args.dev || process.env.AO_DEV === "1";
const prodEntry = resolve(webDir, "dist-server", "start-all.js");
const hasProdBuild = existsSync(prodEntry);

if (forceDev) {
  // run dev mode intentionally
} else if (hasProdBuild) {
  // run production mode
} else {
  // optionally fall back to dev with a clear warning,
  // or fail with a helpful message depending on intended packaging contract
}
```

## Plan

### Phase 1 — Fix detection logic
- Replace the current `server/` existence heuristic in `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`
- Introduce explicit `--dev` override (and optional `AO_DEV=1` env support)
- Prefer production artifacts when present

### Phase 2 — Improve UX / errors
- If no production build exists and dev mode was not explicitly requested, show a clear message explaining why AO cannot start in production mode
- Avoid silently switching modes

### Phase 3 — Add tests
- Add tests for:
  - normal packaged install → production mode
  - symlinked / linked install with prod build present → production mode
  - explicit `--dev` → dev mode
  - missing prod build + no `--dev` → clear failure or explicit fallback message

### Phase 4 — Document behavior
- Update install/start docs so runtime mode is explicit
- Document that `--dev` is for contributors/developers, not normal end users

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ao start` does **not** enter dev mode solely because the package resolves to a source tree
- `npm link` / symlinked installs no longer force dev-mode behavior by accident
- production mode is preferred whenever production artifacts are present
- dev mode requires explicit intent (`--dev` / env override)
- tests cover linked-install and packaged-install cases

## Affected Area

- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`

## Related

- #15 — Design and implement end-to-end install & setup experience
- #640 — `ao start` fails with "Dependencies not installed" due to npm hoisting of `@composio/ao-core`

title: fix(cli): ao start fails with "Dependencies not installed" due to npm hoisting of @composio/ao-core
body:
fix(cli): ao start fails with "Dependencies not installed" due to npm hoisting of @composio/ao-core

  Closes [#640](https://github.com/perfect7613/agent-orchestrator/issues/640)

  Problem

  ao start fails with "Dependencies not installed. Run: pnpm install && pnpm build" even after a successful install — both in global npm installs and monorepo setups.

  The original checkBuilt() in preflight.ts had multiple issues:

  1. Hardcoded nested path assumption: It only looked for @composio/ao-core directly under webDir/node_modules/, but npm/yarn hoist scoped packages to a parent
  node_modules/@composio/ao-core. The check always failed in global installs.
  2. findPackageUp was generic but never walked up: The original accepted variadic ...segments but was only called once with the nested path — it didn't actually help with hoisting.

  What this PR does

  Rewrites checkBuilt() with a dedicated findPackageUp that walks up the directory tree checking node_modules/@composio/ao-core at each level, correctly handling both:
  - pnpm workspaces: symlinked in webDir/node_modules
  - npm/yarn global installs: hoisted to a parent node_modules

title: AO installation should not require sudo access
body:
## Problem

AO installation should **not require `sudo` access** for normal end users.

Right now, the documented / implied install path can push users toward a global npm install flow such as:

```bash
npm install -g @composio/ao
```

On many Linux/macOS setups, this ends up writing to a system-owned global npm prefix, which means users are prompted to run the install with `sudo`.

That is a bad default experience for a developer tool intended for broad end-user adoption.

## Why this is a problem

Requiring or implying `sudo` for installation:
- creates friction during onboarding
- makes users uncomfortable installing a CLI with elevated privileges
- increases the risk of environment-specific install failures
- is often unnecessary if the product supports a user-owned install path
- makes AO feel harder to trust than tools that support `npx`, local installs, or user-local binaries

In practice, this is usually not a hard technical requirement of AO itself — it is a consequence of the chosen install/distribution path.

## Desired outcome

A normal user should be able to install and run AO **without sudo**.

The default install guidance should steer users toward one of the following:
- user-local install with a user-owned bin directory on `PATH`
- `npx` / one-shot execution for try-first onboarding
- standalone binary / installer into a user-owned location (for example `~/.local/bin`)

If global install remains supported, it should be optional rather than the primary recommended path.

## Proposal

### Product / UX direction

1. **Do not require or normalize `sudo npm install -g ...` in docs**
2. **Prefer a no-sudo install path in onboarding**
3. Support clean `ao` execution without root by using a user-owned install location
4. Make the first-run docs explicit about recommended install methods

### Candidate approaches

#### Option A — `npx`-first onboarding
- Recommend `npx @composio/ao ...` for first-run / evaluation
- No install or sudo required
- Good for trying AO quickly
- Less ideal for frequent repeated use

#### Option B — user-local install + PATH
- Install AO into a user-owned npm/pnpm prefix or another user-local bin directory
- Add that bin directory to `PATH`
- Users get the clean `ao` command with no sudo
- Likely the best balance for recurring use

#### Option C — standalone binary / installer
- Ship a binary or installer that places `ao` into a user-owned location
- Cleanest long-term UX
- Avoids repeated `npx` and avoids global npm friction

## Proposed plan

### Phase 1 — Decide the primary install story
- Choose whether onboarding should be:
  - `npx`-first
  - user-local install first
  - or both, with explicit positioning for each

### Phase 2 — Update docs and setup flow
- Update README / quickstart / setup docs
- Remove any guidance that implies `sudo` is expected
- Document user-local install patterns clearly

### Phase 3 — Improve CLI/setup messaging
- If AO detects a global/system-owned install context, provide a hint toward a no-sudo install path
- Make setup scripts prefer user-local destinations where possible

### Phase 4 — Validate end-user experience
- Test fresh installation on common Linux/macOS setups without root privileges
- Verify the recommended path yields a clean `ao` command and working startup flow

## Acceptance criteria

- AO has at least one clearly documented **no-sudo** installation path for normal users
- onboarding docs do not imply `sudo npm install -g ...` as the default
- users can get a working `ao` command from a user-owned install location
- install/setup guidance is explicit about the recommended non-root path

## Related

- #15 — Design and implement end-to-end install & setup experience

title: fix: handle unknown flag error from older gh in getCIChecks
body:
## Summary

- `gh` v2.45.0 (and older versions) don't support `--json` for `pr checks`, returning `"unknown flag: --json"` 
- `isUnsupportedPrChecksJsonError` only matched `"unknown json field"` errors, so the `"unknown flag"` error propagated as `"Failed to fetch CI checks"`
- `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails` caught this and silently returned early — `lastCIFailureFingerprint` was never written and no CI failure details were ever sent to agents

The fix extends the error detection in `isUnsupportedPrChecksJsonError` to also match `"unknown flag"` errors, triggering the existing `statusCheckRollup` fallback that works on all `gh` versions.

**Root cause confirmed**: Session ao-112 (PR #814, status=ci_failed) never received CI failure details because `gh pr checks 814 --json ...` fails on this host's `gh` v2.45.0 — all other checks (`getCISummary` via fail-closed, PR enrichment via GraphQL) worked correctly, masking the bug in `getCIChecks`.

title: Feat/issue 813
Honor Linear branchName as single source of truth for spawn worktree branches
body:
## Summary
When spawning from a Linear issue, AO now uses Linear’s `branchName` field (same string as **Copy git branch name** in the UI) as the single source of truth for the git branch on the new worktree. If Linear does not return branchName, behavior falls back to the previous Linear tracker convention (`feat/<issue-id>`), so existing flows keep working.

## Why
Branch names were sometimes out of sync between Linear and AO, which makes reviews and handoffs harder. Aligning the worktree branch with Linear removes that mismatch.

## What changed
`Issue`: optional branchName on the core type.
`tracker-linear`: GraphQL requests branchName and maps it on `getIssue` / list paths.
`session-manager`: after resolving the issue, prefers `resolvedIssue.branchName`, else `tracker.branchName(...)`.
Tests: spawn unit test for the preference; Linear plugin tests; integration assertion when Linear credentials are present.
Docs: `SETUP.md` and `examples/README.md` — SSOT, fallback, and **Linear → Settings → Integrations → GitHub → Branch format** for changing the pattern.
`scripts/claude-batch-spawn`: prompts tell workers to use the branch AO already prepared (avoid conflicting git/branch instructions).
**Changeset**: patch for `@composio/ao-core` and `@composio/ao-plugin-tracker-linear`.

## How to test
1. Configure a project with **tracker linear** and `LINEAR_API_KEY` (and team config as today).
1. Pick an issue that shows **Copy git branch name** in Linear.
1. Run `ao spawn <ISSUE-ID>` from the project directory.
1. Confirm the printed Branch matches that Linear string (SSOT).
1. (Optional) Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` — matches [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) / CI expectations.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused change set (Linear branch naming + related tests/docs/script)
- [x] Changeset added for published packages
- [x] CI green

- `tracker-linear` dynamically imports `@composio/core` (Composio SDK) as an optional dependency for the Composio transport path

- Add `@composio/core` to `serverExternalPackages` so Next.js skips bundling it and leaves it as a runtime `require()`, matching the plugin's optional usage

The plugin already handles the missing SDK gracefully at runtime — if `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is not set, the Composio transport is never used. If it is set but the SDK isn't installed, a clear error message is thrown telling the user to install it.

Closes #866
Supersedes #868 (identical fix)

title: feat(web): single-socket — multiplex terminals + sessions over one WebSocket
body:
## Summary

Replaces three separate real-time channels with a single persistent multiplexed WebSocket at `/mux`.

**Before:**
- One WebSocket per terminal (`:14801/ws?session=<id>`, spawned per tab)
- SSE stream for session status (`/api/events`)
- Legacy ttyd server on port 14800 (dead code, never used by UI)

**After:**
- One persistent `/mux` WebSocket per browser tab (owned by `MuxProvider`)
- Terminal I/O, resize, open/close all flow over mux protocol channels
- Session patches delivered via a shared SSE relay: mux server subscribes once to Next.js `/api/events` and broadcasts to all connected clients — no per-client polling

## Architecture

```
Browser  ←── WS /mux ──→  Mux Server (:14801)  ←── SSE /api/events ──  Next.js (:3000)
          (bidirectional)     TerminalManager         (event-driven push,
          terminal + sessions  node-pty per session    1 shared connection)
```

## Key changes

- **`MuxProvider`** — React context at app root owning the single WebSocket; `DirectTerminal` uses hooks instead of managing its own WS
- **`SessionBroadcaster`** — server-side class maintaining one SSE connection to Next.js, lazily connecting on first subscriber and disconnecting when the last one leaves
- **Manual WS upgrade routing** — works around a `ws` library limitation where two `WebSocketServer` instances with different `path` options on the same HTTP server don't work correctly
- **`useSessionEvents`** — extended to accept mux session patches, skipping SSE when mux is available
- **Removed `terminal-websocket.ts`** — entire legacy ttyd-based server deleted (port 14800, ~450 lines)
