title: refactor(core): port architectural gaps from closed PR #905 — global registry, hybrid config, unified pipeline
body:
## Context

PR #905 (closed) and PRs #857–#862 (merged as main's multi-project stack) were competing designs. They both ship "multi-project," but they mean different things by it:

- **Main's multi-project:** multiple `projects:` entries inside a single `agent-orchestrator.yaml`. One global config file, one hash, one load path.
- **#905's multi-project:** a global registry at `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` that lists registered projects by path, with per-project local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` files that override global defaults. Hybrid config, dynamic registration.

When #905 was closed, its architectural ideas were lost. This issue enumerates what #905 provided that main does not, so we can decide which pieces to port, defer, or drop.

Nothing in this issue is currently breaking users on main — the items below are either (a) structural gaps that block workflows #905 enabled, or (b) hardening that only pays off once those workflows exist.

## Architecture #905 added that main lacks

### 1. Global config registry (`global-config.ts`, 461 lines)
A `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` listing registered projects by path. Each project can have its own local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` that overrides global defaults. On main, there is no global registry — every project must be hand-edited into one shared YAML.

**User-facing consequence:** without the registry, you cannot add a project to AO without editing a central YAML file, which makes `ao` painful to use across many independently-cloned repos.

### 2. Migration / effective-config builder (`migration.ts`, 178 lines)
`buildEffectiveConfig(globalConfig, globalPath, warnings)` merges the global registry with per-project local configs into a single `OrchestratorConfig`. Without it, hybrid config has no composition layer.

### 3. Shared post-build pipeline (`applyGlobalConfigPipeline`)
One function runs `expandPaths → applyProjectDefaults → applyDefaultReactions → collectExternalPluginConfigs/mergeExternalPlugins → validateProjectUniqueness` for both `loadFromGlobalConfig` and the multi-project registration path.

On main, `validateConfig` is the only pipeline; it's the only loader that exists. When the registry is added, a second loader appears, and without a shared function the two drift — e.g. cross-project validation like session-prefix collision detection runs in one path but not the other.

### 4. Per-project effective config hashing (`resolveProjectConfigPath` / `getEffectiveConfigPath`)
Session storage directories (`~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}`) are hashed off the **per-project** effective config path, not the global one. Two projects with the same basename (e.g. `/client1/app` and `/client2/app`) get distinct storage directories.

On main, everything hashes off one global `configPath`, which forces the duplicate-basename constraint below.

### 5. `ao project` command (`packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts`, 199 lines)
Dynamic registration: `ao project add <path>`, `ao project remove`, `ao project list`. Talks to the global registry. Main has no equivalent — all registration is file-edit-driven.

### 6. In-process polling model (different architecture, not missing plumbing)

Main and #905 both have `running-state.ts` + `lifecycle-service.ts` — the service layer landed on main independently via commit `f3f81dad` (onboarding simplification), not via #905. The real delta is **how polling runs**:

- **Main:** `lifecycle-service` forks a separate `ao lifecycle-worker <projectId>` child process per project (`packages/cli/src/commands/lifecycle-worker.ts`, still registered as a live internal command in `program.ts`). Each project's polling loop runs in its own OS process, coordinated by PID files.
- **#905:** deletes `lifecycle-worker.ts` entirely (`-139 lines`). The service runs polling in-process for all registered projects — one long-lived runtime, no per-project forks, no PID files to coordinate.

Trade-offs (both valid, not a clear win either way):
- Per-project subprocesses (main) isolate crashes — one bad plugin or stuck project doesn't stall others — at the cost of fork overhead, IPC, and PID-file lifecycle bugs.
- In-process polling (#905) is simpler to reason about and debug, and avoids the PID-race / zombie-worker edge cases that show up in main's `lifecycle-service.ts`, but makes the service a single point of failure across all projects.

This is a design decision, not a port. Flagging it here so it isn't rediscovered later as "something #905 did differently" — if we re-evaluate, the question is about polling topology, not about adding missing code.

### 7. Error classification in config loading (`isParseOrSchemaError`)
Distinguishes "global config file is broken / unparseable" (fall back to local) from "global config is valid but has a real schema validation error" (surface to user). Main conflates the two because it has a single config source — when the registry is added, conflating them either hides real errors or blocks valid fallbacks.

### 8. Pre-computed orchestrator suffix (`forcedSuffix`)
The CLI scans live sessions, picks the next orchestrator suffix, and passes it to `spawnOrchestrator` so the number shown to the user in the picker matches what gets reserved. On main, `spawnOrchestrator` auto-increments internally, which can drift from what the CLI displayed if another process reserved a suffix between display and spawn.

### 9. Drops basename-uniqueness constraint
#905 deletes the `validateProjectUniqueness` basename-dedup check because per-project hashing (item 4) makes it unnecessary — two projects can legitimately share a directory name. Main still throws `Duplicate project ID detected` when it sees `/client1/app` and `/client2/app` in the same config.

### 10. Unified `orchestratorSessionStrategy` semantics
- Adds `"new"` as a 4th canonical value (alongside `reuse | delete | ignore`)
- Removes the separate `opencodeIssueSessionStrategy` field; routes opencode reuse through `orchestratorSessionStrategy` with `"new"` mapping to `"ignore"`
- Adds a Zod `.transform()` that normalizes legacy aliases (`kill-previous` → `delete`, `delete-new` → `delete`, `ignore-new` → `ignore`) at parse time, so the runtime TypeScript type never exposes legacy values

Main keeps `orchestratorSessionStrategy` and `opencodeIssueSessionStrategy` as separate fields with 6 legacy-inclusive values, and normalizes only at runtime (opt-in).

### 11. `PortfolioPage` web view (203 lines + tests)
Cross-project portfolio view in the dashboard. Main's dashboard is the per-project / merged-sidebar view from the multi-project stack; there is no portfolio-style cross-project overview.

## Smaller hardening items (preparatory, low standalone value)

These are defensive improvements in #905 that don't break anything on main today but become load-bearing once the items above land. Calling them out separately so they aren't confused with user-visible bugs:

### A. Immutable config pipeline
Six pipeline functions mutate the input config on main:

- `expandPaths()` — mutates `project.path`, `plugin.path`
- `applyProjectDefaults()` — mutates `project.name`, `sessionPrefix`, `scm`, `tracker`
- `applyDefaultReactions()` — mutates `config.reactions`
- `processExternalPluginConfig()` — mutates `pluginConfig.path`, `pluginConfig.plugin`
- `collectExternalPluginConfigs()` — relies on the mutation above; should return `{ entries, updatedConfig }`
- `mergeExternalPlugins()` — mutates `existingPlugin.enabled = true`

#905 rewrites all six to spread-and-return, matching the project's CLAUDE.md "never mutate" convention. On main with a single-source config, the mutation isn't observable because no caller retains the pre-validation object — but once hybrid config (item 2) reuses parsed fragments across the registry + per-project merge, mutation becomes observable corruption.

### B. Path resilience in `generateConfigHash` / `validateAndStoreOrigin`
`realpathSync(configPath)` with no fallback throws `ENOENT` on paths that don't exist yet. On main that never happens (all callers pass already-loaded configs). Pending registration (item 5) and the hybrid lookup (item 4) both need to hash paths before they exist, so the `try realpathSync() catch resolve()` fallback becomes necessary when those land.

### C. `generateSessionPrefix` empty/degenerate-input guards
Returns `""` for empty input and for pure-separator inputs like `"---"`. Main never reaches these because `basename(project.path)` never produces those strings for realistic configs. When the registry (item 1) lets users register paths programmatically (not via basename-of-yaml-path), degenerate inputs become reachable.

## Proposed approach

These items are not all one PR. Roughly in dependency order:

1. **Foundations (low-risk prep, can land independently):** A, B, C, plus #10's Zod transform
2. **Shared pipeline:** #3 — lets future loaders share validation
3. **Registry + migration:** #1, #2, #4, #7 — the core of #905's model
4. **CLI surface:** #5, #8 — depends on registry
5. **Polling topology (#6):** design decision, not a code port — revisit only if per-project subprocess coordination becomes a source of bugs
6. **Dashboard:** #11 — depends on registry being queryable
7. **Constraint drop:** #9 — only safe after #4 lands

## Open questions

- Do we actually want #905's hybrid model, or does main's single-YAML approach satisfy the use case? This issue documents the gap but doesn't make the call.
- If we do want it, is this an incremental set of PRs or a single RFC → big-bang replacement?
- Items #10 and #11 are standalone enough that they could be decoupled from the registry work entirely.

## References

- Closed PR: #905 — `feat: multi-project architecture — config, sessions, CLI` (4635 additions / 719 deletions across 44 files)
- Merged multi-project stack: #857, #860, #861, #862

title: Auto-merge not triggered: reviewDecision null not handled as 'none'
body:
## Problem

When branch protection does not require reviews, GitHub GraphQL returns `reviewDecision: null` (not `"none"`). The `gh` CLI converts this to an empty string `""`.

In `lifecycle-manager.ts`, the merge-readiness check only handles `"approved"` and `"none"`:

```typescript
if (reviewDecision === "approved" || reviewDecision === "none") {
    if (mergeReady.mergeable) return "mergeable";
}
```

Since `""` (from null) doesn't match either, the session stays at `pr_open` and never transitions to `mergeable`, even when CI is green and the PR is fully mergeable.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a repo with branch protection that does NOT require reviews
2. Create a PR, wait for CI to pass
3. `gh api graphql` shows `reviewDecision: null`, `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`
4. AO session stays at `pr_open`, never fires `approved-and-green` reaction

## Expected behavior

`reviewDecision` of `null` / `""` should be treated the same as `"none"` — no reviews required, merge-ready if CI passes.

## Suggested fix

```typescript
if (reviewDecision === "approved" || reviewDecision === "none" || !reviewDecision) {
```

## Environment

- AO version: 0.2.4
- GitHub: private repo, Team plan, branch protection with `required_approving_review_count: 0`

title: refactor(core): use markdown template instead of inline md string in ts
body:
### Tl;DR

Request to adopt md template for orchestrator prompts instead of writing them inline in ts.

## Issue

Parent: #1052 

The orchestrator prompt in packages/core/src/orchestrator-prompt.ts is currently maintained as a large inline TypeScript string with embedded interpolation and conditional section assembly. This hurts readability and maintainability. It should be moved into a simple Markdown template, with TypeScript only responsible for reading the template, preparing typed runtime data, and expanding template variables.

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. Open `packages/core/src/orchestrator-prompt.ts` and `packages/core/src/__tests__/orchestrator-prompt.test.ts` and trace how the prompt is currently assembled.
2. Move the main orchestrator prompt prose into a Markdown template file under `packages/core/src/prompts/orchestrator.md` file.
3. Define a typed render-data type whose keys are known ahead of time and map directly to template variables.
4. Refactor `generateOrchestratorPrompt()` so it only:
   - reads the Markdown template
   - prepares the typed render-data object from `config`, `projectId`, and `project`
   - precomputes optional sections such as automated reactions and project-specific rules as strings
   - passes the template and render-data object to a small interpolation helper
5. Add or update focused tests for placeholder expansion, unresolved placeholder handling, and optional-section rendering.
6. Commit only the prompt generator, template file, and directly related test updates. No unrelated files.

## Validation

- Package-level test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test`
- Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck`
- Broader repo checks only when needed: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`

## Constraints

- Keep the scope inside `packages/core` unless shared code must change to fix the prompt rendering correctly.
- Preserve the public API of `generateOrchestratorPrompt(opts): string`.
- Do not introduce a full template engine.
- Keep the Markdown template simple: placeholders only, with no loops or template-level conditionals.
- Keep control flow in TypeScript by precomputing optional sections before rendering.
- Prefer minimal, surgical edits over broader prompt infrastructure refactors.

## Acceptance

- All the previous test cases are still passed.

title: Dashboard orchestrator DTO omits status/activity/timestamps, causing missing orchestrator activity rendering
body:
## Summary

  The dashboard orchestrator DTO does not include enough session fields for the UI to render orchestrator activity/state correctly.

  ## Problem

  The main dashboard builds orchestrator entries via the orchestrator serialization path, but the DTO only exposed minimal identity fields.

  Because of that, the dashboard could not render orchestrator runtime state such as:

  - `status`
  - `activity`
  - `createdAt`
  - `lastActivityAt`

  This caused orchestrator cards/links to lose live state context, even when the underlying core session already had valid activity/status data.

  ## Expected Behavior

  The dashboard orchestrator DTO should expose the same key state fields the UI needs to render:

  - orchestrator session status
  - orchestrator activity
  - created timestamp
  - last activity timestamp

  ## Actual Behavior

  Only basic identity fields were exposed, so the dashboard could not accurately render orchestrator state and activity.

  ## Root Cause

  The orchestrator serialization path in the web layer returned an incomplete DTO shape.

  ## Proposed Fix

  Extend the orchestrator DTO returned by the dashboard serialization layer to include:

  - `status`
  - `activity`
  - `createdAt`
  - `lastActivityAt`

  Also update any tests that assume the smaller DTO shape.

  ## Impact

  Without this fix:
  - orchestrator activity can appear missing in the dashboard
  - orchestrator state rendering is incomplete
  - UI behavior diverges from the actual core session state

title: Codex plugin integration gaps cause incorrect dashboard activity/state detection
body:
## Summary

  Several Codex-specific integration gaps cause AO to mis-detect activity/state in the dashboard and lifecycle paths.

  These issues affect Codex-backed sessions, especially orchestrators, and show up as missing activity, incorrect `active` state, and failure to use native Codex session logs.

  ## Problems Included

  ### 1. Web dashboard backend does not load the Codex agent plugin

  The web service layer does not register the Codex agent plugin, so dashboard-side `sessionManager.get()` / `sessionManager.list()` cannot run Codex activity enrichment.

  Impact:
  - Codex sessions can come through with `activity: null`
  - dashboard falls back to rendering `unknown`

  ### 2. Web package is missing the Codex plugin dependency

  The web package does not include `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex` as a dependency, so the web layer cannot reliably import/register the plugin.

  Impact:
  - runtime/plugin registration failures in the web app
  - broken Codex-specific enrichment path

  ### 3. Codex native JSONL parsing assumes the wrong shape

  Native Codex session JSONL uses nested payload fields such as:

  - `payload.cwd`
  - `payload.model`
  - `payload.msg`
  - nested token usage under payload info

  The current integration assumes older flat fields in some places.

  Impact:
  - session file matching can fail
  - model/thread/cost extraction can fail
  - activity/session info can be incomplete or null

  ### 4. Codex terminal idle prompt is misclassified as `active`

  Fallback terminal activity detection does not properly recognize Codex prompt lines such as:

  - `› ...`

  Impact:
  - idle orchestrator sessions remain incorrectly marked `active`
  - `.ao/activity.jsonl` keeps being refreshed with false `active` entries

  ### 5. Native Codex session matching truncates oversized `session_meta`

  The current cwd matcher reads only the first 4 KB of the native session file when trying to parse `session_meta`.

  For orchestrator sessions, the first `session_meta` line can exceed that size because it embeds large instruction payloads.

  Impact:
  - JSON parsing fails on truncated `session_meta`
  - cwd matching fails
  - AO falls back to `.ao/activity.jsonl` instead of using the native Codex session file

  ## Expected Behavior

  For Codex-backed sessions, AO should:

  - load the Codex plugin everywhere it builds session state, including the web backend
  - correctly parse modern native Codex JSONL payload structure
  - correctly match native session files to worktrees
  - prefer native Codex session files for activity/session info when available
  - classify Codex prompt-idle states correctly instead of marking them `active`

  ## Actual Behavior

  Codex-backed sessions can show:

  - `unknown` activity in dashboard views
  - incorrect `active` activity when idle
  - fallback `.ao/activity.jsonl` behavior even when a native Codex session file exists
  - incomplete session info due to JSONL parsing mismatch

  ## Proposed Fix

  Implement a single Codex integration cleanup covering:

  1. Register Codex plugin in the web service backend
  2. Add `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex` to the web package dependencies
  3. Update Codex JSONL parsing to support nested `payload.*` fields
  4. Update terminal idle detection for Codex prompt patterns like `› ...`
  5. Update native session matching to read a complete `session_meta` line instead of truncating at 4 KB

  ## Tests

  Add or update regression coverage for:

  - web Codex plugin registration
  - nested native Codex JSONL parsing
  - Codex prompt idle detection
  - oversized `session_meta` line matching during cwd detection

  ## Impact

  Without this fix, Codex-backed AO sessions can be misrepresented in the dashboard and lifecycle pipeline, especially for orchestrators, leading to incorrect activity rendering and degraded
  status detection.

title: fix(codex): improve dashboard activity integration and native session matching
body:
## Summary
- register the Codex plugin in the web service layer so dashboard session enrichment can run for Codex sessions
- update the Codex plugin to parse modern native JSONL payload shapes and match oversized `session_meta` lines reliably
- improve fallback terminal activity detection so idle Codex prompt states are not misclassified as active

## Problem
Codex-backed sessions were hitting multiple integration gaps across the web and plugin layers:
- the web backend never registered the Codex plugin, so dashboard-side session managers could not enrich Codex activity at all
- native Codex JSONL parsing still assumed older flat fields instead of nested `payload.*` fields
- native session matching only read the first 4 KB of `session_meta`, which fails for large orchestrator session metadata lines
- fallback terminal parsing treated Codex prompt lines like `› ...` as active work

Together these issues caused missing dashboard activity, incorrect `active` states, and fallback behavior even when a valid native Codex session log existed.

Closes #1178.

## Solution
### Web integration
- add `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex` as a web dependency
- register the Codex plugin in `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts`
- add a regression test asserting the web service registry includes the Codex plugin

### Native Codex JSONL parsing
- support nested native fields such as `payload.cwd`, `payload.model`, `payload.threadId`, `payload.thread_id`, `payload.msg`, and `payload.info.total_token_usage`
- centralize nested field extraction helpers for cwd, model, thread id, and token usage

### Native session matching
- change `sessionFileMatchesCwd()` to read until it has a complete first JSONL line instead of truncating at a fixed 4 KB slice
- keep the read bounded while allowing oversized `session_meta` lines from orchestrator sessions to parse correctly

### Fallback terminal activity detection
- treat Codex interactive prompt lines starting with `›` as idle
- preserve existing waiting-input and active detection behavior for real in-progress output

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex test -- src/index.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- src/__tests__/services.test.ts`

title: feat: add Gitea support (scm + tracker plugins)
body:
## Summary

Add first-class Gitea support to Agent Orchestrator by shipping two new plugins — \`@composio/ao-plugin-scm-gitea\` and \`@composio/ao-plugin-tracker-gitea\` — and wiring Gitea detection into the config defaults. Gitea has a GitHub-compatible REST API (v1) and a growing self-hosted user base (Forgejo, Codeberg), so it's the highest-value third SCM to support after GitHub and GitLab.

## Motivation

Users running self-hosted Gitea/Forgejo instances currently can't point AO at their repos without writing a custom plugin. The existing \`scm-github\` plugin assumes \`api.github.com\` and the \`gh\` CLI; the \`scm-gitlab\` plugin is GitLab-specific. Gitea's API surface is close enough to GitHub's that most of \`scm-github\` can be ported with a different base URL and auth, but it needs its own plugin so host detection, PR creation, and review reactions work out of the box.

## Scope

### 1. \`packages/plugins/scm-gitea\`

Implement the full \`SCM\` interface (see \`packages/core/src/types.ts\`) against Gitea's REST API v1:

- \`createPR\` — \`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls\`
- \`listPRs\` / \`getPR\` — paginated pull list + single-PR fetch
- \`getCIStatus\` — Gitea Actions or external CI via \`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/status\`
- \`listReviews\` / \`listReviewComments\` — \`/pulls/{index}/reviews\` and \`/pulls/{index}/comments\`
- \`mergePR\` — \`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/merge\`
- \`getDefaultBranch\` — \`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}\`
- Webhook validation (HMAC-SHA256, Gitea uses \`X-Gitea-Signature\` header)

Auth: personal access token via \`GITEA_TOKEN\` env var; base URL configurable via plugin config (\`host: gitea.example.com\`, default \`https://gitea.com\`). No CLI dependency — use \`fetch\` directly; Gitea has no universal CLI equivalent to \`gh\`/\`glab\` that's worth assuming.

### 2. \`packages/plugins/tracker-gitea\`

Implement the \`Tracker\` interface against Gitea issues:

- \`listIssues\` — \`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open&type=issues\` (exclude PRs; Gitea returns both in the same endpoint)
- \`getIssue\` — \`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}\`
- \`addComment\` — \`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/comments\`
- \`closeIssue\` / \`reopenIssue\` — \`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}\`
- Label-based filtering (same semantics as the GitHub tracker's \`labels\` config)

### 3. Config inference

Wire Gitea into \`inferScmPlugin\` / project defaults in \`packages/core/src/config.ts\`:

- \`scm.host\` containing \`gitea\` or matching a known Forgejo/Codeberg pattern → \`plugin: \"gitea\"\`
- \`tracker.host\` containing \`gitea\` → \`plugin: \"gitea\"\`
- Update \`agent-orchestrator.yaml\` schema docs / examples

### 4. Documentation & tests

- Plugin READMEs in each new package (auth setup, config knobs, host URL examples)
- Add Gitea to the SCM/Tracker table in \`CLAUDE.md\` and any top-level docs that enumerate supported backends
- Mocked Vitest coverage in \`src/__tests__/index.test.ts\` for each plugin: manifest, \`create()\` shape, all public methods, auth failure paths
- At minimum one integration test pointing at a public Codeberg instance (or Gitea demo) gated behind an env var so CI doesn't block when it's down

## Out of scope

- Gitea Actions-specific CI parsing (use the generic combined-status endpoint for v1; revisit once Gitea Actions stabilizes its API)
- A Gitea-native terminal or notifier plugin (existing notifiers already work)
- \`.gitea/\` workflow file scaffolding (mirror of \`.github/\` is a separate feature)
- OAuth flows — PAT only for v1

## Open questions

1. **Forgejo/Codeberg compatibility.** Forgejo is a Gitea fork and Codeberg runs Forgejo. API parity is ~100% today but has drifted in places. Do we ship one plugin that claims compatibility, or split \`scm-forgejo\` out from the start? Recommendation: one plugin with a \`flavor?: \"gitea\" | \"forgejo\"\` config knob that gates flavor-specific endpoints as they diverge.
2. **CLI wrapper (\`~/.ao/bin/gh\`-style).** Agents using PATH-wrapper metadata hooks (Codex/Aider/OpenCode) currently shell out to \`gh\`. For Gitea repos there's no \`gh\` equivalent we can assume. Options: (a) require users to install \`tea\` (Gitea's CLI) and ship a \`tea\` wrapper, (b) have the wrapper shim translate \`gh\` calls into Gitea REST, (c) skip CLI wrappers for Gitea and require agents that produce PRs via API. Needs a design call before implementation.
3. **Webhook signature algorithm.** Gitea supports both HMAC-SHA256 and a legacy scheme. Confirm we only need SHA256.

## Acceptance criteria

- \`pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm test\` green with the new packages
- \`ao init\` with a Gitea \`repo:\` / \`scm.host:\` produces a working config that passes validation
- Spawning a session against a Gitea repo creates a PR, polls CI, reacts to review comments, and merges — verified against a live Gitea instance in integration tests
- Dashboard shows Gitea-hosted PRs with the same columns as GitHub/GitLab

## References

- Gitea REST API v1: https://docs.gitea.com/api/1.22/
- Existing plugins to mirror: \`packages/plugins/scm-github\`, \`packages/plugins/scm-gitlab\`, \`packages/plugins/tracker-github\`, \`packages/plugins/tracker-gitlab\`
- Plugin standards: CLAUDE.md → \"Plugin Standards\" section

title: Orchestrator shows 'exited' state — it should never exit
body:
## Problem

The orchestrator is displaying an `exited` state. This should never happen — the orchestrator is a long-running supervisor process and should never be shown as exited.

The `exited` activity state is intended for individual agent sessions whose processes have died (see `isProcessRunning` in the agent plugin contract), not for the orchestrator itself.

## Expected behavior

- The orchestrator should never surface an `exited` state.
- If the underlying process/connection is unavailable, surface a connection/health state (e.g. "disconnected", "reconnecting") instead of `exited`.
- `exited` should remain scoped to per-session agent processes.

## Suggested investigation

- Check where orchestrator-level status is computed vs. per-session activity state.
- Verify nothing is conflating a session's `exited` state with orchestrator liveness.
- Likely candidates: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`, `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`.

title: refactor(cli): remove lifecycle-worker subprocess model, run polling in-process
body:
## Goal

Replace the per-project `ao lifecycle-worker` subprocess model with in-process polling inside `lifecycle-service`. Closes the last architectural delta vs closed PR #905 (see #1169 item 6 for context).

## What exists today

- `packages/cli/src/commands/lifecycle-worker.ts` (139 lines) — an internal `ao lifecycle-worker <projectId>` command that runs a polling loop for a single project.
- `packages/cli/src/lib/lifecycle-service.ts` (254 lines) — forks one `lifecycle-worker` subprocess per project, tracks PIDs in files, restarts dead workers, etc.
- `packages/cli/src/program.ts` — registers the `lifecycle-worker` command.
- Tests: `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/start.test.ts`, `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/spawn.test.ts` reference the worker; `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/lifecycle-service.test.ts` covers the service.

## What to build

Fold the polling loop into `lifecycle-service` itself so all registered projects are polled from a single long-lived process:

1. Move the polling body from `lifecycle-worker.ts` into `lifecycle-service.ts` as an internal async loop keyed by `projectId`.
2. Replace per-project subprocess spawning with an in-process `Map<projectId, AbortController>` (or similar) that manages start/stop per project.
3. Delete `packages/cli/src/commands/lifecycle-worker.ts` and its registration in `program.ts`.
4. Remove PID-file coordination (`writeLifecycleWorkerPid`, `clearLifecycleWorkerPid`, `getLifecycleWorkerStatus`) — these exist only to track subprocess state.
5. Update callers in `start.ts` / `spawn.ts` to stop expecting a subprocess handle.

## Design constraints

- **Error isolation:** one project's polling throwing must not stop polling for other projects. Each project's loop needs its own try/catch so an exception is logged and the loop continues.
- **Graceful shutdown:** the service must stop all per-project loops cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM before exit.
- **Concurrency:** polls for different projects can run in parallel; polls for the *same* project must not overlap (skip a tick rather than queue).
- **Observability:** preserve the `createProjectObserver` health reporting that `lifecycle-worker.ts` currently does — per-project health should still surface to the dashboard.

## Out of scope

- Changing the poll interval or the polling contract itself.
- Touching `running-state.ts` — it's the consumer of lifecycle events, not the producer.
- Anything from #1169 items 1–5 or 7–11. This PR is scoped to the polling topology change only.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ao lifecycle-worker` is no longer a registered command (running it should fail with "unknown command").
- Starting `ao start` runs one process, no child `lifecycle-worker` PIDs in `ps`.
- One project throwing in its poll cycle does not affect other projects' polling (covered by a new test).
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` all green.
- Existing `lifecycle-service` tests updated to reflect the new model (no PID-file assertions).
- Manual verification: spawn two sessions across two projects, induce an error in one project's plugin, confirm the other continues polling.

## References

- Parent issue: #1169 item 6 (polling topology)
- Prior art: closed PR #905's deletion of `lifecycle-worker.ts` (+0 / -139)

title: refactor(cli): remove lifecycle-worker subprocess, poll in-process
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the per-project `ao lifecycle-worker` subprocess model with an in-process polling loop inside `lifecycle-service`. All registered projects are now polled from the single long-lived `ao start` process.
- Deletes `packages/cli/src/commands/lifecycle-worker.ts` (and its registration in `program.ts`), rewrites `lifecycle-service.ts` around a `Map<projectId, ActiveLoop>`, and removes all PID-file / subprocess coordination.
- Per-project error isolation preserved (core `pollAll()` already catches per-cycle errors; stop failures don't block other projects). SIGINT/SIGTERM/beforeExit now gracefully stop every registered loop.

Closes #1185

title: Bug: zombie sessions — isProcessRunning() gated behind conditional checks, dead sessions stay "working"
body:
File: packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts — determineStatus(), lines 370–445

Summary

Dead agent sessions stay in "working" status indefinitely. isProcessRunning() — the only reliable check for whether an agent process is actually alive — is gated behind conditional branches that can be bypassed in three distinct scenarios. As a result, ao status, the dashboard, and ao sessions ls all continue reporting "working" when the agent is dead.

Root Cause

determineStatus() in lifecycle-manager.ts has two detection paths. Neither calls isProcessRunning() unconditionally.

Trigger 1 — Stale JSONL (lines 406–419)

const activityState = await agent.getActivityState(session, config.readyThresholdMs);
if (activityState) {
  if (activityState.state === "waiting_input") return "needs_input";
  if (activityState.state === "exited") return "killed";
  // active/idle → proceeds to PR checks
  // isProcessRunning() is NEVER called here
}

When an agent dies uncleanly (Ctrl+C, SIGKILL, crash), the last JSONL entry is often "active". The function proceeds to PR checks without verifying the process is still alive.

Trigger 2 — Empty terminal output (lines 438–443)

} else {
  const terminalOutput = runtime ? await runtime.getOutput(session.runtimeHandle, 10) : "";
  if (terminalOutput) {           // ← gate
    const activity = agent.detectActivity(terminalOutput);
    if (activity === "waiting_input") return "needs_input";
    const processAlive = await agent.isProcessRunning(session.runtimeHandle);
    if (!processAlive) return "killed";
  }
  // empty output → isProcessRunning() never runs → falls through
}

isProcessRunning() is inside the if (terminalOutput) block. If tmux returns empty output (fresh session, cleared screen, idle shell), the process check is skipped entirely.

Trigger 3 — Probe exceptions

// session-manager.ts (8 instances), lifecycle-manager.ts (1 instance)
.catch(() => true)   // probe throws → treated as "alive"

If the plugin crashes or the tmux binary is missing, isAlive() throws, the catch swallows the error, and the session is reported as alive. (Also tracked in Issue #1067 / PR #1068 — independent fix, same symptom.)

Steps to Reproduce

Scenario 1 — Ctrl+C (stale JSONL)

  1. ao start
  2. ao spawn <issue> — agent starts
  3. Attach to tmux, press Ctrl+C — agent exits
  4. ao status still shows "working"; dashboard still shows green dot

Scenario 2 — Empty terminal output

  1. Agent runs clear or tmux pane is empty
  2. getActivityState() returns null (no JSONL for this plugin)
  3. getOutput() returns empty string
  4. isProcessRunning() skipped
  5. Agent dies → session stays "working"

Scenario 3 — Probe exception

  1. Plugin crashes or tmux binary missing
  2. isAlive() throws → .catch(() => true) → returns "alive"
  3. Dead session stays "working"

Expected Behavior

isProcessRunning() should execute on every poll cycle, unconditionally, regardless of what JSONL state or terminal output reports.

Proposed Fix

Move the process check outside all conditional gates in determineStatus():

// After all activity/PR checks complete, before returning final status:
if (session.runtimeHandle && canProbeRuntimeIdentity) {
  const processAlive = await agent.isProcessRunning(session.runtimeHandle).catch(() => false);
  if (!processAlive) return "killed";
}

Fix the fallback path — move process check outside the if (terminalOutput) gate:

if (terminalOutput) {
  const activity = agent.detectActivity(terminalOutput);
  if (activity === "waiting_input") return "needs_input";
}

// Always check, regardless of whether output was present
const processAlive = await agent.isProcessRunning(session.runtimeHandle);
if (!processAlive) return "killed";

Affected Surfaces

All three surfaces read from determineStatus():

Surface | Current behaviour | After fix -- | -- | -- Dashboard | Green dot, "working" | Red dot, "killed" ao status | "working" | "killed" ao sessions ls | "working" | "killed" ## Related Issues & PRs | Issue / PR | Relationship | |---|---| | Issue #1067 / PR #1068 | Fixes `.catch(() => true)` → `.catch(() => false)`. Independent but complementary — both should be merged. |

title: Bug: upgraded CLI silently attaches to stale daemon — no version mismatch detection
body:
## Bug

After upgrading `ao` via `npm install -g @aoagents/ao`, running `ao start` silently attaches to the already-running (old-version) daemon instead of detecting the version mismatch.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1484917231245856808/1491735678156013588/1493014818616119377
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** `eb17f328` (0.2.5 release)

## Reproduction

1. `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@0.2.4 && cd <project> && ao start` — dashboard on 0.2.4
2. Leave running for a day
3. `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@0.2.5`
4. `ao --version` → `0.2.5` ✅
5. `ao start` → "AO is already running" with no version info, no restart suggestion

## Root Cause

Two missing pieces:

### 1. `RunningState` has no version field

`packages/cli/src/lib/running-state.ts:6-12` — the interface stores only `pid`, `configPath`, `port`, `startedAt`, `projects`. No version.

### 2. Already-running detection never compares versions

`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:1276-1351` — the "already running" branch reads `running.json`, displays PID/port/uptime/projects, and offers Open/New/Restart/Quit. No version comparison, no mismatch warning.

Meanwhile, `getCliVersion()` already exists at `packages/cli/src/options/version.ts:5-7` — reads `package.json` version. Ready to reuse.

## Fix

1. Add `version: string` to `RunningState` interface in `running-state.ts`
2. Write `version: getCliVersion()` at registration (`start.ts:1373-1378`)
3. On already-running detection (`start.ts:1278-1283`), compare `running.version` against `getCliVersion()`
4. If mismatch, surface it in the "already running" output and add a "Restart on new version" option (default)

## Impact

- **User confusion:** Dashboard, lifecycle worker, and orchestrator all run on stale code
- **Silent degradation:** Bug fixes and features in the new release don't take effect
- **Workaround exists:** `ao stop && ao start` — but nothing guides the user there

## Priority

`priority: medium` — workaround exists, but it silently runs old code which can mask real bugs.

title: Bug: ETag Guard treats HTTP 304 as failure, defeats caching optimization
body:
## Bug

The ETag guard in graphql-batch.ts treats HTTP 304 "Not Modified" responses as errors, causing it to skip the cache and re-run the full GraphQL batch every 30 seconds — the exact opposite of what the guard is supposed to do.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1358460206377365554/1491735678156013588/1493016732007141537
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** `cef2b3b0`

## Screenshot

```
[next] [ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ComposioHQ/integrator: Command failed: gh api --method GET repos/ComposioHQ/integrator/pulls?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=1 -i -H If-None-Match: W/"0f4d860ddab1672da4867f7c6c43db0f9b50350fddbdba04fb4f1a93998c6ab6"
[next] gh: HTTP 304
```
This fires **every 30 seconds per repo** in the logs.

## Reproduction

1. Start AO on a project that has open PRs (`ao start`)
2. Wait for the first poll cycle to populate the ETag cache
3. Observe logs — every 30 seconds you see `[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed` + `gh: HTTP 304`

## Root Cause

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts`

Both guard functions (`checkPRListETag` lines 336–381, `checkCommitStatusETag` lines 394–440) have the same bug:

1. They run `gh api` with `If-None-Match` header to check if data changed
2. When nothing changed, GitHub returns **HTTP 304** — but `gh` CLI exits non-zero on 304
3. Node's `execFileAsync` throws on non-zero exit — the happy-path 304 check (lines 356–360) is **unreachable dead code**
4. The `catch` block treats it as a failure, logs the warning, and returns `true` ("assume changed")
5. The full GraphQL batch runs unnecessarily (~1.2s per cycle per repo)

```
Lines 353:    const { stdout } = await execFileAsync("gh", args, { timeout: 10_000 });  // THROWS on 304
Lines 356-360: if (stdout.includes("HTTP/1.1 304") || stdout.includes("HTTP/2 304"))     // UNREACHABLE
Lines 373-380: catch block — logs as failure, returns true (run expensive batch)
```

Same pattern in Guard 2 (`checkCommitStatusETag`, lines 431–439).

## Fix

In both catch blocks, check for HTTP 304 before treating it as an error:

```typescript
catch (err) {
  const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
  // gh CLI exits non-zero on HTTP 304 — that's "not modified", not a failure
  if (errorMsg.includes("HTTP 304")) {
    return false; // Not modified — skip batch, use cache (the intended behavior)
  }
  console.warn(`[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}`);
  return true;
}
```

## Impact

- **Log spam:** Warning fires every 30s per repo (2 lines each time)
- **Wasted API calls:** The GraphQL batch runs every cycle instead of being skipped when nothing changed (~1.2s wasted per repo per cycle)
- **Related to #1083:** This is failure point F-09 in the GitHub API redesign — guards fail-open on errors. The full redesign (GhClient) will fix this architecturally, but the one-line catch-block fix resolves it immediately.

## Secondary: "can't find session" race condition (cosmetic)

The logs also show `can't find session: int-orchestrator-4` followed immediately by `[MuxServer] Opened terminal int-orchestrator-4`. This is a harmless race condition — the web dashboard's terminal multiplexer tries to open a tmux session before the session manager has finished creating it. Second attempt succeeds. Cosmetic only, low priority.

**Files:** `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` (line 245 throws on null), `packages/web/server/tmux-utils.ts` (lines 68–102 resolveTmuxSession returns null when tmux session doesn't exist yet).

title: fix(github): ETag Guard treats HTTP 304 as failure
body:
Fixes #1191

## Summary
The ETag guard uses gh CLI with If-None-Match headers to check if PRs changed.
When nothing changed, GitHub returns HTTP 304 — but gh exits non-zero, causing
execFileAsync to throw. The catch block treated this as a failure and returned
true (assume changed), defeating the caching optimization entirely.

Now the catch block checks for HTTP 304 in the error message and returns false
(not changed), which is the correct behavior.

Fixes both Guard 1 (checkPRListETag) and Guard 2 (checkCommitStatusETag).

## Test
1. Start AO on a project with open PRs
2. Wait for ETag cache to populate (first poll cycle)
3. Observe logs — no more [ETag Guard] PR list check failed + gh: HTTP 304 spam
4. GraphQL batch should only run when something actually changed

title: Lifecycle reactions don't route to sessions that open a second PR
body:
## Pain point

When a worker session opens a **second PR** (beyond the one AO originally associated with it at spawn time), the lifecycle reaction system doesn't route review comments, CI status changes, or other PR events to that session. The session only receives events for its originally-tracked PR.

## Concrete example from a recent run

**Session:** `int-3` (project: integrator)
**Original PR (tracked by AO):** ComposioHQ/integrator#1381 — lifecycle reactions work correctly for this PR (bugbot comments auto-forwarded, CI status changes delivered)
**Second PR (opened by the session ad-hoc):** ComposioHQ/integrator#1387 — lifecycle reactions do NOT route to int-3

PR #1387 received 5 Cursor Bugbot review comments (including 1 HIGH severity finding). None of them were forwarded to the int-3 session. The orchestrator had to manually discover the comments via `gh api repos/ComposioHQ/integrator/pulls/1387/comments` and explicitly tell int-3 to read them.

The `ao session claim-pr 1387 int-3` command was attempted as a workaround but failed because the PR's branch was already checked out in the session's worktree:
```
Failed to claim PR for session int-3: Error: gh pr checkout 1387 failed:
fatal: 'feat/stream3-claude-sdk-classifier' is already checked out at
'/Users/equinox/.worktrees/integrator/int-3-workflow'
```

## Why this happens

AO associates one PR per session at spawn time (or via `ao session claim-pr`). The session metadata tracks this PR, and lifecycle reactions use the metadata to route events. When a session opens a second PR via `gh pr create` during its normal workflow, AO has no visibility into that — the PR exists on GitHub but isn't in AO's session metadata.

This is a natural workflow pattern: a session might be asked to do two related pieces of work that should be separate PRs (e.g., "ship the classification results as PR #1381, then ship the classification workflow as PR #1387"). The session correctly opens two PRs, but only the first one gets lifecycle reaction coverage.

## Impact

- **Missed review comments:** Bugbot findings on the second PR go unnoticed until someone manually checks. In our case, a HIGH severity finding (model ID mismatch that would cause 404 errors at runtime) sat on the PR without the session knowing about it.
- **Missed CI failures:** If CI fails on the second PR, the session doesn't get the auto-fix directive.
- **Orchestrator overhead:** The orchestrator has to manually poll each session's PRs and relay findings, which defeats the purpose of the lifecycle reaction system.

## Suggested behavior

When a session creates a new PR (detected via GitHub webhook or polling), AO should automatically associate it with the session and start routing lifecycle events for it. A session should be able to have multiple tracked PRs, not just one.

Alternatively, if multi-PR tracking is architecturally complex, a simpler fix: make `ao session claim-pr` work when the branch is already checked out in the session's worktree (the current implementation tries to `gh pr checkout` which fails if the branch is already there — it should detect this case and just update the metadata without checking out).

## Workaround

The orchestrator manually tells the session to check for review comments on its second PR:
```
ao send int-3 "PR #1387 has bugbot comments that aren't being auto-forwarded. Read them via gh pr view 1387 --comments and address them."
```

Works but requires the orchestrator to know about the second PR and remember to relay events manually.

## Related issues

- #1095 — Per-session worktree support for secondary repos (same pattern: AO defaults that don't match how sessions actually work)
- #1122 — Lifecycle reactions auto-fire on stale commit data (different bug in the same lifecycle reaction system)

title: GitHub API rate limit hit with only 7 sessions — RCA and fix proposals
body:
## Observed behavior

With only 6-7 active agent sessions on one project (`integrator`) plus ~5 orchestrator sessions, the AO dashboard (`localhost:3001`) displays:

> **GitHub API rate limited — PR data (CI status, review state, sizes) may be stale.**

This should not happen at this session count. GitHub's REST API rate limit is 5,000 requests/hour for authenticated users. The AO codebase has specific provisions for managing rate limits (ETag guards, GraphQL batching, TTL caches), but multiple independent subsystems are making API calls without coordinating, and the `ao status` CLI command bypasses all batching.

## Root cause analysis

### Problem 1: `ao status` CLI makes N×4 individual API calls per session (no batching)

**File:** `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts`, lines 128–137

The `gatherSessionInfo()` function makes **4 separate `gh` CLI calls per session** with a PR:

```typescript
const prInfo: PRInfo | null = await scm.detectPR(session, project);  // 1 REST call: gh pr list
if (prInfo) {
  const [ci, review, threads] = await Promise.all([
    scm.getCISummary(prInfo).catch(() => null),      // 1-2 REST calls (pr checks + possibly statusCheckRollup fallback)
    scm.getReviewDecision(prInfo).catch(() => null),  // 1 REST call: gh pr view --json reviewDecision
    scm.getPendingComments(prInfo).catch(() => null),  // 1 GraphQL call: api graphql (reviewThreads)
  ]);
}
```

**Critically, `ao status` does NOT use `enrichSessionsPRBatch()`** — it has no access to the GraphQL batch system at all (confirmed: no import of `enrichSessionsPRBatch` in the CLI package). Every invocation makes independent REST calls for every session.

With 7 worker sessions with PRs + 5 orchestrator sessions, that's:
- `detectPR`: 7 calls (orchestrators are filtered but workers are not)
- `getCISummary`: 7 calls (each calls `getCIChecks` which is `gh pr checks`)
- `getReviewDecision`: 7 calls (`gh pr view --json reviewDecision`)
- `getPendingComments`: 7 calls (GraphQL query for review threads)

**= ~28 API calls per `ao status` invocation**

The orchestrator agents call `ao status` frequently throughout the day. If 5 orchestrators each call `ao status` every 5 minutes, that's:
- 5 orchestrators × 12 calls/hour × 28 API calls = **1,680 calls/hour** from `ao status` alone.

### Problem 2: Dashboard `/api/sessions` endpoint makes N×6 individual calls per session

**File:** `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts`, lines 167–176

The `enrichSessionPR()` function makes **6 parallel API calls per PR** on cache miss:

```typescript
const results = await Promise.allSettled([
  scm.getPRSummary(pr),        // 1 REST call
  scm.getCIChecks(pr),         // 1 REST call
  scm.getCISummary(pr),        // 1 REST call (calls getCIChecks internally, so potentially 2)
  scm.getReviewDecision(pr),   // 1 REST call
  scm.getMergeability(pr),     // 2-3 REST calls (getPRState + getCISummary + pr view)
  scm.getPendingComments(pr),  // 1 GraphQL call
]);
```

**File:** `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts`, lines 90–110

This runs for every session with a PR when the dashboard client calls `/api/sessions`. The client-side hook (`useSessionEvents.ts`, line 14) triggers a full refresh every 15 seconds (`STALE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 15000`) and also on every SSE snapshot change.

With the prCache TTL of 5 minutes (`DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000` in `packages/web/src/lib/cache.ts`, line 13), a cache miss triggers 6+ API calls per session. But within the 5-minute window, cache hits mean zero calls. The problem is the initial burst and the cache expiry cascade (all entries expire at roughly the same time since they were populated together).

### Problem 3: Lifecycle manager's review backlog check adds 2 API calls per session every 2 minutes

**File:** `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`, lines 800–806

The `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog()` function calls both `getPendingComments()` and `getAutomatedComments()` for every active session with a PR, throttled to once per 2 minutes:

```typescript
const [pendingResult, automatedResult] = await Promise.allSettled([
  scm.getPendingComments(session.pr),     // 1 GraphQL call
  scm.getAutomatedComments(session.pr),   // 1+ REST calls (paginated)
]);
```

**`getAutomatedComments()`** (`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts`, lines 880–906) is particularly expensive — it paginates through ALL review comments on a PR using the REST API (`repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments?per_page=100`), making 1+ calls per PR.

With 7 sessions polled every 30 seconds, but throttled to every 2 minutes:
- 7 sessions × 2 calls × 30 invocations/hour = **420 calls/hour**

### Problem 4: `getMergeability()` makes 3-4 cascading API calls internally

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts`, lines 946–1026

`getMergeability()` is called both by the dashboard's `enrichSessionPR()` and by the lifecycle manager's fallback path. Each call makes:

1. `getPRState()` — 1 REST call (`gh pr view --json state`)
2. `gh pr view --json mergeable,reviewDecision,mergeStateStatus,isDraft` — 1 REST call
3. `getCISummary()` → `getCIChecks()` — 1-2 REST calls

That's **3-4 REST calls per `getMergeability()` invocation**, and it's called independently by multiple subsystems.

### Problem 5: No coordination between the 3 independent polling subsystems

The three subsystems that poll GitHub are completely independent:

| Subsystem | Interval | Uses batch? | Uses cache? | API calls per cycle |
|-----------|----------|-------------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Lifecycle manager** (core) | 30s | Yes (GraphQL batch) | Yes (per-cycle Map) | 1 GraphQL batch + 2 REST ETag guards + 2N review calls |
| **Dashboard `/api/sessions`** | 15s (client refresh) | No | Yes (5-min TTL prCache) | 0 on cache hit, 6N on cache miss |
| **`ao status` CLI** | Per-invocation | No | No | 4N per invocation |

The lifecycle manager's batch GraphQL query and its per-cycle `prEnrichmentCache` are **not shared** with the dashboard or CLI. The dashboard has its own `prCache` (5-min TTL in `packages/web/src/lib/cache.ts`), and the CLI has no cache at all.

### Problem 6: `getCISummary` calls `getCIChecks` internally, doubling call count

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts`, lines 686–718

`getCISummary()` internally calls `this.getCIChecks(pr)`, which makes a full REST API call. When both `getCISummary` and `getCIChecks` are called in parallel (as `enrichSessionPR` does), that's 2 REST calls for CI data that could be served from one.

### Problem 7: Backlog poller makes additional tracker API calls every 60 seconds

**File:** `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts`, lines 103, 214–296

The backlog poller runs every 60 seconds (`BACKLOG_POLL_INTERVAL = 60_000`) and calls:
- `tracker.listIssues()` — REST call to list backlog issues
- `tracker.listIssues()` again for `merged-unverified` issues
- `relabelReopenedIssues()` — another `listIssues()` call per project

These are additional GitHub API calls (for the GitHub Issues tracker) that compound the rate limit pressure.

## Rate limit math

Worst-case calculation with 7 sessions with PRs, 5 orchestrators calling `ao status`:

| Source | Calls/hour | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| `ao status` (5 orchestrators, every 5 min) | **1,680** | 5 × 12 × 28 |
| Lifecycle manager (every 30s) | **300** | 120 cycles × (1 batch + ~1.5 ETag guards) |
| Lifecycle review backlog (every 2 min, 7 sessions) | **420** | 30 cycles × 7 × 2 |
| Dashboard `/api/sessions` (every 15s, cache miss every 5 min) | **504** | 12 cache misses/hr × 7 × 6 |
| Dashboard SSE `/api/events` (every 5s) | ~0 | No GitHub API calls directly |
| Backlog poller (every 60s) | **180** | 60 cycles × 3 tracker calls |
| Individual session detail views | ~50 | Ad-hoc, 6 calls per view |
| **TOTAL** | **~3,134** | |

This is already at 63% of the 5,000/hour limit under normal conditions. But the calculation above assumes:
- `ao status` is only called every 5 minutes (likely more frequent)
- Dashboard cache always hits within the 5-minute window (cache stampedes cause bursts)
- No retry storms from failed API calls
- No additional manual page loads or session detail views

In practice, with slightly more frequent `ao status` calls or a few cache misses, this easily exceeds 5,000/hour.

### The critical multiplier: `ao status` from orchestrators

The orchestrator sessions call `ao status` as part of their workflow to check on worker progress. With 5 orchestrators, even calling it every 3 minutes would produce:
- 5 × 20 × 28 = **2,800 calls/hour** from `ao status` alone

This is the single largest contributor and has no rate limit awareness or caching.

## Specific code paths (biggest consumers)

1. **`packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:128-137`** — `gatherSessionInfo()` makes 4 individual REST/GraphQL calls per session with no batching or caching
2. **`packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:167-176`** — `enrichSessionPR()` makes 6 parallel calls per session on cache miss
3. **`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts:946-1026`** — `getMergeability()` makes 3-4 cascading calls internally
4. **`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:800-806`** — `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog()` makes 2 calls per session every 2 minutes
5. **`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts:880-906`** — `getAutomatedComments()` paginates REST API
6. **`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts:686-718`** — `getCISummary()` redundantly calls `getCIChecks()`

## Fix proposals

### P0: Make `ao status` use the GraphQL batch system

The single biggest fix. Instead of 4N individual calls, `ao status` should:
1. Collect all PRs from sessions
2. Call `enrichSessionsPRBatch()` once (1 GraphQL query + 2 ETag guards)
3. Use the returned `Map<string, PREnrichmentData>` for display

This would reduce `ao status` from ~28 calls to ~3 calls per invocation.

### P1: Share a single PR enrichment cache across all subsystems

Currently there are 3 independent caches:
- Lifecycle manager: `prEnrichmentCache` (per-cycle Map, cleared each poll)
- GraphQL batch: `prEnrichmentDataCache` (LRU, persistent across polls)
- Dashboard: `prCache` (TTL cache, 5-min expiry)

These should be unified into a single cache (the `prEnrichmentDataCache` in graphql-batch.ts is already LRU-based and persistent). The dashboard and CLI should read from this cache before making any API calls.

### P2: Deduplicate `getCISummary` + `getCIChecks`

`enrichSessionPR()` calls both `getCIChecks` and `getCISummary` in parallel, but `getCISummary` internally calls `getCIChecks`. Either:
- Remove `getCIChecks` from `enrichSessionPR` and derive the check list from `getCISummary`'s internal call
- Or make `getCISummary` accept an optional pre-fetched checks array

### P3: Add rate limit awareness to `gh` CLI wrapper

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts:64-77`

The `execCli` wrapper has no rate limit awareness. Add:
- Parse `X-RateLimit-Remaining` from response headers (pass `-i` flag)
- When remaining < 100, back off and skip non-critical calls
- Log a warning when approaching the limit

### P4: Reduce `enrichSessionPR` from 6 to 1-2 calls

Most of the data that `enrichSessionPR` fetches (state, CI, reviews, mergeability) is already available from the GraphQL batch enrichment. When the lifecycle manager's batch has run recently, the dashboard should use that data directly instead of making 6 independent REST calls.

### P5: Exclude exited/terminal sessions from `ao status` PR checks

`gatherSessionInfo()` in `status.ts` doesn't check if a session is in a terminal state before making API calls. Sessions that are `merged`, `killed`, or `done` don't need live CI/review data.

### P6: Add a global rate limit budget tracker

Implement a process-level counter that tracks GitHub API calls made across all subsystems. When the budget is low, degrade gracefully (skip review backlog checks, extend cache TTLs, reduce poll frequency).

## Related issues

- #1095 (worktrees) — worktree-based sessions amplify the session count
- #1122 (stale alerts) — lifecycle reactions firing stale alerts may trigger redundant API calls
- #1193 (multi-PR routing) — lifecycle reaction system processing the same PR data multiple ways

body: ## Bug CI check chips (✓ Integration Tests, ✓ run-lint, etc.) in the session detail view are rendered as plain `` elements with no link to their GitHub workflow run. Users can't click through to see the actual CI run details. **Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1491735678156013588/1493069241396756540 **Reported by:** @prateek **Analyzed against:** `cef2b3b` (origin/main) ## Screenshot ![Session detail showing non-clickable CI chips](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1491735678156013588/1493069241165807746/image.png?ex=69dda096&is=69dc4f16&hm=96af5addd82b1800bfc46db8e0a133137def1078e8ac24a53586bb0ad93c10db&) ## Reproduction 1. Open the AO web dashboard 2. Navigate to a session with an open PR that has CI checks 3. Observe the CI check chips (✓ run-lint, ✓ run-tests, etc.) 4. Click on any chip — nothing happens (no link, no navigation) ## Root Cause **`packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx`, lines 867-881:** The CI check chips are rendered as bare `` elements: ```tsx {pr.ciChecks.map((check) => ( {icon} {check.name} ))} ``` The `check.url` field is **never used** in this component, even though: 1. The `DashboardCICheck` type has `url?: string` (`packages/web/src/lib/types.ts:113`) 2. The serializer passes it through (`packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:212`: `url: c.url`) 3. The GitHub SCM plugin populates it from `detailsUrl`/`targetUrl` (`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts:661`) 4. ( e.stopPropagation()}> {chip} ) : chip; })} ``` ## Impact - Every user viewing session detail CI chips can't click through to workflow runs - The data is already available — it's just not wired up in the UI - Low effort fix (~10 lines changed)

title: Bug: Dashboard terminal rendering garbled — xterm.js v5.3.0 missing DEC 2026 synchronized output support
body:
## Bug

Dashboard terminal rendering is garbled/corrupted — characters appear shifted, duplicated, or the viewport yanks unexpectedly during agent streaming output. **Very rarely reproducible**, timing-dependent.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1491735678156013588/1489272853617709087
**Reported by:** @Atul Pandey
**Analyzed against:** `cef2b3b0` (main HEAD)

## Dependencies Involved

| Package | Installed | Latest |
|---------|-----------|--------|
| xterm | ^5.3.0 (Sep 2023) | 6.0.0 (Dec 2025) |
| @xterm/addon-fit | ^0.11.0 | 0.11.0 |
| @xterm/addon-web-links | ^0.12.0 | 0.12.0 |
| node-pty | ^1.1.0 | 1.1.0 |

## Root Cause

**AO's xterm.js is 2+ years and a full major version behind.** v5.3.0 lacks DEC 2026 (synchronized output) support, which is critical for rendering the agent CLIs AO orchestrates.

### Primary cause: No DEC 2026 support (xtermjs/xterm.js#5801)

Agent CLIs (claude-code, codex, copilot-cli) emit DEC 2026 sequences (`\x1b[?2026h` / `\x1b[?2026l`) during streaming redraws to batch display updates atomically. Without DEC 2026 support:

1. The terminal processes `ED2` (`\x1b[2J`, clear screen) inside what should be a sync block as a raw erase
2. This resets `viewportY` to the bottom, yanking the viewport mid-stream
3. The rapid sequence of clear → redraw → clear → redraw produces garbled intermediate states
4. The `minimumContrastRatio` and theme settings don't prevent this — it's a structural rendering issue

This is documented upstream at **xtermjs/xterm.js#5801** — the single biggest rendering complaint for claude-code users (677+ reactions on anthropics/claude-code#826).

### Contributing factor: Missing 2 years of rendering fixes

xterm v6.0.0 includes these fixes absent from v5.3.0:
- **#5328**: Refresh viewport after clear or ED — **directly addresses the garbling**
- **#5411**: Fix teleport when exiting alt buffer
- **#5390**: Fix scrollbar teleport after exiting alt buffer
- **#5437**: Prevent page scroll when scrolling in alt buffer
- **#5278**: Handle glyph widths up to max device texture size
- **#5096**: New viewport/scroll bar implementation (breaking change, fixes many scroll-related rendering bugs)

### Contributing factor: Resize race with addon-fit

In `DirectTerminal.tsx:353-357`, `handleResize()` calls `fit.fit()` then immediately reads `terminal.cols`/`terminal.rows`. If fit's calculation is deferred (it measures DOM elements), the resize sent to the PTY may use stale dimensions. Combined with the PTY reflow, this can produce wrapped/garbled content.

### Why it's rarely reproducible

The garbling is timing-dependent:
1. Only occurs when ED2 sequences arrive during an active render frame
2. Depends on the agent's output rate and the browser's frame timing
3. More likely during streaming output (long agent responses) but still a race
4. Different GPU/browser combos affect canvas renderer behavior

## Reproduction

1. `ao spawn` a session using claude-code or codex agent
2. Open the dashboard and navigate to the session
3. Wait for a long streaming response from the agent
4. Observe occasional viewport yanking or garbled terminal output
5. More reproducible: scroll up during streaming, then observe viewport jump to bottom

## Fix

**Upgrade xterm.js from v5.3.0 to v6.0.0+** and update all addons to their compatible versions.

```diff
# packages/web/package.json
-"xterm": "^5.3.0"
-"@xterm/addon-fit": "^0.11.0"
-"@xterm/addon-web-links": "^0.12.0"
+"xterm": "^6.0.0"
+"@xterm/addon-fit": "^0.11.0"  # check v6 compat
+"@xterm/addon-web-links": "^0.12.0"  # check v6 compat
```

**Breaking changes to handle in the upgrade** (from v6.0.0 changelog):
- `overviewRulerWidth` → `overviewRuler` property (breaking)
- Viewport/scroll bar completely rewritten (breaking)
- Alt→Ctrl+arrow hack removed (breaking, needs manual keybinding)
- ESM support added via esbuild
- New scrollbar integration from VS Code base

**Secondary fix**: Debounce resize in `DirectTerminal.tsx:360` to prevent resize races:
```typescript
const debouncedHandleResize = debounce(() => {
  if (fit) {
    fit.fit();
    resizeTerminalMux(sessionId, terminal.cols, terminal.rows);
  }
}, 100);
window.addEventListener("resize", debouncedHandleResize);
```

## Impact

- All users viewing agent terminal output in the dashboard
- Affects claude-code, codex, and any DEC 2026-emitting agent
- Severity reduced by rarity, but when it hits, the terminal is unreadable until refresh
- Related to #1151 (shared PTY resize) — both contribute to terminal garbling

## References

- xtermjs/xterm.js#5801 — ED2 viewport yanking in DEC 2026 sync blocks
- xtermjs/xterm.js#5453 — DEC 2026 support (merged in v6.0)
- anthropics/claude-code#826 — 677+ reaction complaint about terminal flickering
- anthropics/claude-code#36582 — Claude Code viewport yanking

title: fix(web): upgrade xterm.js to v6 for DEC 2026 synchronized output support
body:
## Summary

Upgrades xterm.js from v5.3.0 (Sep 2023) to @xterm/xterm v6.0.0 to fix garbled terminal rendering during agent streaming output.

Fixes #1197

## Why This Is Needed

**Root cause of the rendering bug:** AO's xterm.js v5.3.0 lacks DEC 2026 (synchronized output) support. Agent CLIs (claude-code, codex, copilot-cli) emit `\x1b[?2026h/l` sequences during streaming redraws. Without support, ED2 clear-screen commands inside sync blocks yank the viewport and produce garbled intermediate states. Tracked upstream at **xtermjs/xterm.js#5801** — the #1 rendering complaint for claude-code users (677+ reactions on anthropics/claude-code#826).

v6.0.0 also includes 8+ rendering fixes absent from v5.3.0, notably **#5328** (refresh viewport after clear/ED — directly addresses our garbling).

## Previous Attempt

Gaurav previously attempted this migration on the `gb-personal` branch (commit `8f8231fe`) but it was never merged — it sat on an orphaned branch. This PR incorporates the same changes plus fixes identified in Gaurav's migration plan (`docs/plans/xterm-v6-migration-plan.md`).

## Changes

### 1. Package rename (`packages/web/package.json`)
- `xterm: ^5.3.0` → `@xterm/xterm: ^6.0.0`
- Addons (`@xterm/addon-fit`, `@xterm/addon-web-links`) unchanged — v6.0.0 tag uses same versions

### 2. Import updates (`DirectTerminal.tsx`)
- `import "xterm/css/xterm.css"` → `import "@xterm/xterm/css/xterm.css"`
- `import type { ... } from "xterm"` → `from "@xterm/xterm"`
- `import("xterm")` → `import("@xterm/xterm")`

### 3. Breaking change: `fastScrollModifier` removed (#5462)
- Removed `fastScrollModifier: "alt"` from Terminal options — this option does not exist in v6 and would cause a TS/build error

### 4. CLI test fixture (`dashboard.test.ts`)
- Updated vendor chunk name from `xterm@5.3.0.js` to `@xterm+xterm@6.0.0.js` (Next.js bundles scoped packages as `@scope+name`)

### 5. Test mocks (`DirectTerminal.render.test.tsx`)
- Updated `vi.mock("xterm")` → `vi.mock("@xterm/xterm")`

### 6. Dev page (`terminal-test/page.tsx`)
- Updated version string from "xterm.js 5.3.0" to "@xterm/xterm 6.0.0"

## Not Changed (verified safe)

- **CSS (`globals.css`)** — `.xterm .xterm-viewport` scrollbar rules: v6's viewport rewrite may affect these, but they're cosmetic auto-hide rules that degrade gracefully. Should be re-tested visually but won't break anything.
- **`node-pty`** — Not an xterm dependency, no changes needed.
- **OSC 52 handler** — Our custom `registerOscHandler(52, ...)` is still needed for tmux clipboard. v6 added OSC 52 support (#4220) but our tmux XDA flow is different from the standard path.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `pnpm install && pnpm build` — verify no TS errors
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — verify tests pass
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — CLI tests pass with new vendor chunk name
- [ ] Open dashboard, spawn session with claude-code or codex
- [ ] Verify terminal renders correctly during streaming output
- [ ] Verify no viewport yanking when scrolling during streaming
- [ ] Verify Alt+scroll still works (fast scroll via `fastScrollSensitivity`)
- [ ] Verify Cmd+C clipboard still works (XDA + OSC 52 path)
- [ ] Check scrollbar styling on terminal (`.xterm-viewport` CSS)

title: Rare garbled terminal rendering during agent streaming (xterm.js v5.3.0)
body:
## Bug Description

The dashboard terminal occasionally shows garbled/flickering content during agent streaming output. The issue is very rarely reproducible but has been observed multiple times when running claude-code, codex, or copilot-cli sessions through the web dashboard.

## Root Cause Analysis

AO's dashboard uses **xterm.js v5.3.0** (package `xterm`). Three rendering gaps in this version converge to cause the garbling:

### 1. Missing DEC 2026 (Synchronized Update) Support
Agent CLIs emit `\x1b[?2026h` / `\x1b[?2026l` to wrap complex multi-line redraws. v5.3.0 does NOT buffer these — it renders every intermediate state as it arrives, causing visible tearing/flickering.
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#5801](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5801)
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#4436](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/4436)

### 2. Viewport Yanking After ED (Clear Screen)
`\x1b[2J` (ED2 clear) yanks the viewport but the render loop doesn't immediately refresh — showing stale content for one frame.
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#5328](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5328)

### 3. Partial Frame Rendering During High-Frequency Streaming
LLM token streaming produces rapid ANSI cursor positioning interleaved with text. v5.3.0's render loop processes rows individually without frame batching.
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#4997](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/4997)

### Why v5.3.0 Specifically
- Released BEFORE DEC 2026 was implemented (added ~v5.5.0, finalized v6.0.0)
- Modern agent CLIs now emit DEC 2026 sequences routinely
- Render loop lacks atomic frame updates — reworked in v6.0.0

## Environment
- **AO Version:** 0.2.5
- **xterm.js:** 5.3.0 (package `xterm`, deprecated)
- **Agents affected:** claude-code, codex, copilot-cli
- **Reproducibility:** Rare

## Reproduction Steps
1. Start AO dashboard: `ao dashboard`
2. Spawn a session with claude-code or codex
3. During active streaming output, observe terminal panel
4. Occasionally (rarely), the terminal shows garbled/flickering content during redraws

## Fix
