title: Rare garbled terminal rendering during agent streaming (xterm.js v5.3.0)
body:
## Bug Description

The dashboard terminal occasionally shows garbled/flickering content during agent streaming output. The issue is very rarely reproducible but has been observed multiple times when running claude-code, codex, or copilot-cli sessions through the web dashboard.

## Root Cause Analysis

AO's dashboard uses **xterm.js v5.3.0** (package `xterm`). Three rendering gaps in this version converge to cause the garbling:

### 1. Missing DEC 2026 (Synchronized Update) Support
Agent CLIs emit `\x1b[?2026h` / `\x1b[?2026l` to wrap complex multi-line redraws. v5.3.0 does NOT buffer these — it renders every intermediate state as it arrives, causing visible tearing/flickering.
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#5801](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5801)
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#4436](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/4436)

### 2. Viewport Yanking After ED (Clear Screen)
`\x1b[2J` (ED2 clear) yanks the viewport but the render loop doesn't immediately refresh — showing stale content for one frame.
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#5328](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5328)

### 3. Partial Frame Rendering During High-Frequency Streaming
LLM token streaming produces rapid ANSI cursor positioning interleaved with text. v5.3.0's render loop processes rows individually without frame batching.
- **Upstream:** [xtermjs/xterm.js#4997](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/4997)

### Why v5.3.0 Specifically
- Released BEFORE DEC 2026 was implemented (added ~v5.5.0, finalized v6.0.0)
- Modern agent CLIs now emit DEC 2026 sequences routinely
- Render loop lacks atomic frame updates — reworked in v6.0.0

## Environment
- **AO Version:** 0.2.5
- **xterm.js:** 5.3.0 (package `xterm`, deprecated)
- **Agents affected:** claude-code, codex, copilot-cli
- **Reproducibility:** Rare

## Reproduction Steps
1. Start AO dashboard: `ao dashboard`
2. Spawn a session with claude-code or codex
3. During active streaming output, observe terminal panel
4. Occasionally (rarely), the terminal shows garbled/flickering content during redraws

## Fix

**PR #1198** upgrades `xterm` → `@xterm/xterm@^6.0.0`. CI green (all 9 checks pass).

| Version | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| v5.4.0 | Viewport refresh sync after ED/clear |
| v5.5.0 | Initial DEC 2026 (BSU) buffering |
| **v6.0.0** | Full atomic frame rendering, complete DEC 2026 integration |

### Migration notes:
- Package renamed: `xterm` → `@xterm/xterm`
- CSS import changed
- `fastScrollModifier: "alt"` removed (deleted upstream)
- Addon names unchanged
- `node-pty` not affected

## References
- [xterm.js v6.0.0 release](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/releases/tag/6.0.0)
- [anthropics/claude-code#826](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/826)

title: Collapse dashboard attention zones from 5 to 4, with feature flag for 5-zone mode
body:
## Enhancement

Collapse the 5 Kanban attention zones on the dashboard to 4 for initial product simplicity. Provide a feature flag to re-enable the detailed 5-zone view.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1491735678156013588/1493018267655077990
**Requested by:** @ashish, @prateek

## Current State (5 zones)

```
WORKING  → don't interrupt
PENDING  → waiting on reviews/CI (nothing to do)
REVIEW   → PR problems (CI failed, changes requested)
RESPOND  → agent stuck, needs human input
READY    → click merge
```

## Proposed (4 zones, default)

```
WORKING  → don't interrupt
WAITING  → nothing to do yet (was PENDING)
ACTION   → you need to do something (was REVIEW + RESPOND)
READY    → click merge
```

**Rationale:** REVIEW and RESPOND both mean "human intervention required." The distinction (agent might auto-fix vs agent is literally stuck) is better shown as card-level badges, not separate columns. 4 zones maps to the user's mental model: *is it working? is it waiting? does it need me? is it ready?*

## Implementation

1. **Config flag** in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   dashboard:
     attention_zones: simple    # "simple" = 4 zones (default), "detailed" = 5 zones
   ```

2. **Changes needed:**
   - `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` → `getAttentionLevel()`: merge REVIEW + RESPOND into ACTION when mode is `simple`
   - `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` → `KANBAN_LEVELS`: switch between 4 and 5 column layouts based on config
   - `packages/core/src/types.ts`: add config type for `dashboard.attention_zones`

3. **Progressive disclosure** — card badges still show granular status (`ci_failed`, `needs_input`, `changes_requested`), just not as separate columns

## Impact

- Simpler first-time user experience
- No information loss — detail moves to card level
- Power users can opt into 5-zone view via config

title: feat(web): collapse attention zones to 4 with 5-zone feature flag
body:
## Summary

- Default dashboard kanban now shows 4 zones: `WORKING`, `PENDING`, `ACTION`, `READY`. The former `REVIEW` and `RESPOND` columns collapse into a single `ACTION` zone that answers "does the human need to do something?".
- New config flag `dashboard.attentionZones` (`simple` | `detailed`, defaults to `simple`) opts into the original 5-zone layout for power users.
- Card-level badges continue to expose granular state (`ci_failed`, `needs_input`, `changes_requested`) — nothing is lost, it just moves off the column headers.

## ⚠️ Breaking visual change for existing deployments

**Existing deployments without a `dashboard` block in their `agent-orchestrator.yaml` will silently switch from 5 zones to 4 on next upgrade.** The Zod schema defaults `attentionZones` to `"simple"`, so any config that doesn't explicitly set it gets the new layout. No session data is affected — this is purely a visual change in the kanban board.

**Release notes suggestion:**
> The dashboard now defaults to a simpler 4-zone kanban (`WORKING` / `PENDING` / `ACTION` / `READY`). Granular state still shows on the session cards. To keep the original 5-zone layout, add to your `agent-orchestrator.yaml`:
> ```yaml
> dashboard:
>   attentionZones: detailed
> ```

## Config

```yaml
dashboard:
  attentionZones: simple      # default — 4 zones
  # attentionZones: detailed  # opt-in — original 5 zones
```

(camelCase to match other `OrchestratorConfig` fields like `readyThresholdMs`, `terminalPort`, `sessionPrefix`.)

## Implementation notes

- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — new `DashboardConfig` / `DashboardAttentionZoneMode` types on `OrchestratorConfig`.
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — Zod schema for `dashboard.attentionZones` (default `"simple"`). Not strict — typos fall back to defaults like every other schema in this file.
- `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` — added `"action"` to `AttentionLevel` and a `mode` param to `getAttentionLevel(session, mode = "detailed")`. Defaults to detailed so existing card-level callers (SessionCard, BottomSheet, ProjectSidebar, PullRequestsPage, sessions/[id]) keep their granular behavior. Only dashboard kanban and SSE server routes thread the mode through.
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` — picks `SIMPLE_KANBAN_LEVELS` vs `DETAILED_KANBAN_LEVELS` based on the prop, same for mobile order, filters, and action strip pills. `ProjectOverviewGrid` shows 4 metrics in simple mode and 5 in detailed.
- `packages/web/src/app/api/events/route.ts` + `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/patches/route.ts` — read `config.dashboard?.attentionZones` and pass the mode to `getAttentionLevel()` so SSE-computed levels stay consistent with the client.
- `packages/web/src/hooks/useSessionEvents.ts` — refactored to take an options object with `attentionZones` as a **required** field. TypeScript refuses to compile any caller that doesn't explicitly pass the mode, preventing the next page from silently re-introducing the PullRequestsPage oscillation bug.
- `DynamicFavicon` — treats `action` as yellow (not red). Since simple mode collapses respond + review into one bucket, escalating `action` would scream critical for routine review work. Only detailed-mode `respond` still triggers red.
- `AttentionZone` mobile chip — `getActionChipLabel()` helper picks the most specific underlying cause (needs input / stuck / errored / ci failed / changes / waiting / crashed / blocked / conflicts) so mobile users keep the reason to intervene.
- CSS: new `data-level="action"` rules mirror `"respond"` styling.

## Review feedback addressed

- **Cursor Bugbot [Medium]** — dropped `.strict()` from `DashboardConfigSchema` to match the rest of `config.ts` (d6bcbfad).
- **Codex [P2]** — `action` stays yellow in the favicon (d6bcbfad).
- **Codex [P3]** — mobile action chip surfaces granular cause (d6bcbfad).
- **Cursor Bugbot [Medium]** — threaded `attentionZones` through `PullRequestsPage` so seed + server SSE + client refresh all use the same mode (09ce0940).
- **Cursor Bugbot [Medium]** — mobile chip correctly distinguishes `exited` (crashed) from `blocked`; `ProjectMetric` for Action uses `tone="orange"` to match favicon severity (a73c9740).
- **Cursor Bugbot [Medium]** — `useSessionEvents` refactored to options object with **required** `attentionZones` field so future callers can't forget (8d27db79).
- **Human review [Medium]** — removed dead `action` field from `ZoneCounts` in sessions/[id]/page.tsx; extracted `getActionChipLabel()` helper with 16 unit tests covering every branch (e9786a91).
- **Human review [Low]** — added comment on `LEVEL_LABELS.action` in ProjectSidebar explaining exhaustiveness + forward-compat intent (e9786a91).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm lint` (0 errors)
- [x] `pnpm test` (core: 594 passed; cli: 316 passed; integration: 190 passed)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` (624 passed: 10 simple-mode + 2 favicon severity + 16 action chip)
- [ ] Manual dashboard smoke: both modes render, card badges still correct, favicon + attention count stay accurate.

Closes #1201

fix(web): session detail page missing restore button for killed/terminated sessions
body:
## Bug

The session detail page (`/sessions/[id]`) shows a **Kill** button for active sessions but shows **no Restore button** when the session is in a terminal state (killed, terminated, done, errored, cleanup). Users must navigate back to the dashboard to restore sessions.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1489612265027014736/1491735678156013588/1493159943736528957
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** `07f01ef6`

## Screenshot

![session detail page showing Kill button but no Restore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-1205/.issue-assets/session-detail-no-restore-1205.png)

## Reproduction

1. Kill a session (via CLI or dashboard)
2. Navigate to `/sessions/<session-id>`
3. Observe: page shows "Terminal session has ended" but only a dead Kill button — no Restore option

## Root Cause

`SessionDetail.tsx` renders `<SessionTopStrip>` with `onKill={() => {}` (a no-op!) and never passes an `onRestore` prop. The `SessionTopStrip` component has no restore button in its template at all — it only renders `onKill`.

Meanwhile, the dashboard `SessionCard` component **already has restore logic** (line 166: `isRestorable = isTerminal && session.status !== "merged"`) with a working restore button and styling (`done-restore-btn` CSS class). The session detail page just doesn't use any of this.

The restore API already exists at `POST /api/sessions/:id/restore` and handles all error cases (`SessionNotRestorableError` → 409, `WorkspaceMissingError` → 422).

### Key files:

- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` — `SessionTopStrip` (lines 127-258): only has `onKill` prop, no restore
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` — main component (line 576): passes `onKill={() => {}` (no-op)
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — doesn't wire kill or restore handlers
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — has working restore pattern to follow
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/[id]/restore/route.ts` — existing restore API

## Fix

1. Add `onRestore` prop to `SessionTopStrip` component
2. In `SessionTopStrip`, when `terminalEnded` is true and session is restorable (terminal + not merged), show a Restore button instead of Kill
3. Wire `onRestore` in the main `SessionDetail` component to call `POST /api/sessions/:id/restore` and refresh session data
4. Reuse the existing `done-restore-btn` CSS class from SessionCard

## Impact

- Users cannot restore sessions from the detail page — must go back to dashboard
- Kill button is shown but is a no-op (doesn't actually kill)

title: Orchestrator button on worker page links to wrong parent session
body:
## Status Update (triage 2026-07-28)

**Partially fixed.** The original lexicographic-first bug has been resolved in the Go/Electron rewrite:

- `findProjectOrchestrator()` in `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts` now filters to **active** orchestrators only and sorts by **recency** (`createdAt` → `updatedAt` → `id`), not lexicographic order.
- Covered by tests in `workspace.test.ts:114-166`.

**Remaining gap (the "sometimes"):** No `parentOrchestratorId` is stored on worker sessions at spawn time. The button always navigates to the *newest active orchestrator for the project*, not the *actual parent that spawned the worker*. With 2+ concurrent orchestrators in the same project, the newest isn't necessarily the parent — so it "sometimes" goes to the wrong one.

---

## Original Bug

On any worker session page, clicking the "Orchestrator" button in the top-right can navigate to the wrong orchestrator when multiple orchestrators are alive.

### Root Cause

1. **No parent tracking (STILL OPEN).** Sessions have no `parentOrchestratorId` field. When an orchestrator spawns a worker, that relationship is never recorded.

2. **Fallback picks wrong orchestrator (FIXED).** The old frontend picked the lexicographically first orchestrator. Now fixed — sorts by recency.

### Fix

#### A — Store parent orchestrator in session metadata (REMAINING WORK)
- When an orchestrator spawns a worker, write `parentOrchestratorId` to the worker session (in the backend spawn flow — `Session` domain + service layer)
- Frontend reads `session.parentOrchestratorId` directly — no API fallback needed for the correct parent

#### B — Smart fallback when parent metadata is missing (DONE)
- ✅ Sort orchestrators by recency (prefer non-exited, then by `createdAt` desc) instead of lexicographic
- ✅ Implemented in `findProjectOrchestrator()` / `newestActiveOrchestrator()`

### Affected files (remaining work)
- `backend/internal/domain/` — add `ParentOrchestratorId` to `Session`
- `backend/internal/service/` — write parent ID on worker spawn
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/` — migration + query
- `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts` — prefer `parentOrchestratorId` over recency fallback
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx` — use parent ID when available

### Priority
P2 — works correctly when only one orchestrator is alive (the common case), but breaks multi-orchestrator workflows.

title: fix(web): orchestrator button links to wrong parent session
body:
## Problem

The orchestrator button on a worker session page (top-right of `/sessions/ao-8?project=...`) links to the wrong orchestrator — e.g., `/sessions/ao-orchestrator-1` instead of the correct `/sessions/ao-orchestrator-9`.

## Root Cause

**Stale closure.** `fetchProjectSessions` is a `useCallback(fn, [])` that reads `session?.metadata?.["parentOrchestratorId"]`. Since the dep array is `[]`, it captures `session` from the initial render — when it is `null`. So `parentOrchestratorId` is **always `undefined`**.

The code falls through to `body.orchestratorId`, which picks `orchestrators[0]` — the first in an alphabetically-sorted list. With multiple orchestrators (`ao-orchestrator-1` and `ao-orchestrator-9`), it always picks `-1` regardless of which one actually spawned the worker.

## Fix (5 files, +42/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` | Add `parentOrchestratorIdRef` + `useEffect` sync (same ref pattern already used for `sessionProjectIdRef`, `sessionIsOrchestratorRef`). Read ref first in the orchestrator ID fallback chain. |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | Record `parentOrchestratorId` in session metadata at spawn time by finding the active orchestrator for the project. |
| `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` | Better orchestrator sort: active sessions first, then by recency (newest first), then alphabetical as tiebreaker. |
| `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` | Pick first orchestrator as default when multiple exist (was only picking when exactly 1). |
| `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` | Add `status` and `createdAt` to `DashboardOrchestratorLink`. |

Closes #1211

title: Dashboard issue link broken: issueUrl set to raw issueId instead of full URL
body:
## Bug

When a session is spawned with `ao spawn <issue-number>`, the dashboard renders a broken link for the issue. Clicking it navigates to `/<number>` instead of the GitHub issue URL.

## Root Cause

In the session serialization function (`ao-web/.next/server/chunks/538.js`, function `cg`), `issueUrl` is set to the raw `issueId`:

```javascript
issueUrl: a.issueId   // "1" instead of "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1"
```

The GitHub tracker plugin already has the correct `issueUrl()` method:

```javascript
// ao-plugin-tracker-github/dist/index.js
issueUrl(identifier, project) {
    const num = identifier.replace(/^#/, "");
    return `https://github.com/${project.repo}/issues/${num}`;
}
```

But it is never called during serialization. The enrichment function correctly calls `tracker.issueLabel()` and `tracker.getIssue()`, but `issueUrl` itself is not enriched — it is passed through as-is from `issueId`.

## Expected

`issueUrl` should be computed via `tracker.issueUrl(issueId, project)` before being sent to the frontend.

## Reproduction

```bash
ao start https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>
ao spawn 1
# Open dashboard -> session card shows issue link -> link href is "1" instead of full URL
```

## API response showing the bug

```json
{
  "id": "hom-1",
  "issueId": "1",
  "issueUrl": "1",
  "issueLabel": "#1",
  "issueTitle": "Create README for the repository"
}
```

`issueUrl` should be `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1`.

## Environment

- ao v0.2.2 (npm @composio/ao)
- macOS (Apple Silicon)
- GitHub tracker plugin

title: feat: improve session display names — derive from task context instead of branch names
body:
## Problem

Session names in the dashboard are unhelpful — they show humanized branch names like **"Orchestrator/Ao Orchestrator 8"** or **"Ao 42"** which tell you nothing about what the session is working on.

### How it happens

The display name follows a fallback chain in `getSessionTitle()` (`packages/web/src/lib/format.ts`):
1. PR title ✅
2. Issue title ✅
3. User prompt ✅
4. **Humanized branch name** ❌ ← where we land when no context is attached

Orchestrator sessions get branch names like `orchestrator/ao-orchestrator-8`, which `humanizeBranch()` title-cases into "Orchestrator/Ao Orchestrator 8" — completely generic.

Single sessions get `ao-42` → "Ao 42" — equally unhelpful.

Additionally, `orchestrator/` is not even in the `humanizeBranch()` prefix strip list.

## Proposed Fix

### Level 1 — Quick cosmetic win
- Add `orchestrator/` to the prefix strip list in `humanizeBranch()`
- Strip the session prefix (e.g. `ao-orchestrator-`) so the branch-based fallback is cleaner
- This makes the dashboard look less messy immediately

### Level 2 — Real fix (derive from task context)
- At spawn time, derive a display name from the issue title or first ~80 chars of the user prompt
- Store this as a `label` or `displayName` field in session metadata
- Add it to the `getSessionTitle()` fallback chain **above** the humanized branch fallback
- Surface it in the dashboard header, kanban cards, and session tabs

### Key files
| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `packages/web/src/lib/format.ts` | `getSessionTitle()`, `humanizeBranch()` — dashboard display names |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | `reserveNextSessionIdentity()`, `reserveNextOrchestratorIdentity()` — session ID allocation |
| `packages/core/src/paths.ts` | `generateSessionPrefix()` — prefix generation from project dir |

## Expected Outcome
Sessions are identifiable at a glance — "Fix login timeout bug (#142)" instead of "Ao Orchestrator 8".

title: Terminal text selection offset on right side due to overlay scrollbar mismatch
body:
## Bug

Mouse text selection in the terminal is offset on the right side — the drag/selection pointer is shifted ~14px to the right of the actual mouse cursor. Left-side selection works fine. Affects macOS desktop (Retina), both fullscreen and normal modes.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1489612265027014736/1491735678156013588/1493159493247176734
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** `07f01ef6`

## Reproduction

1. Open any session detail page on macOS desktop (Retina display)
2. Try to drag-select text on the left side of the terminal → works correctly
3. Try to drag-select text on the right side of the terminal → selection pointer is offset ~14px to the right of the actual mouse position

## Root Cause

**Mismatch between CSS scrollbar override and xterm.js column calculation.**

The chain:

1. **FitAddon calculates column count** in `proposeDimensions()` (`@xterm/addon-fit@0.11.0`):
   ```js
   const scrollbarWidth = scrollback === 0 ? 0 : overviewRuler?.width || 14;
   const width = parentWidth - paddingLeft - paddingRight - scrollbarWidth;
   cols = Math.floor(width / cellWidth);
   ```
   Since `scrollback: 10000` and no `overviewRuler` is configured, `scrollbarWidth = 14`.

2. **CSS overrides the viewport scrollbar** in `globals.css:478`:
   ```css
   .xterm .xterm-viewport {
     overflow-y: overlay !important;
   }
   ```
   `overflow-y: overlay` renders the scrollbar ON TOP of content — it does NOT take up layout space.

3. **Result:** FitAddon subtracts 14px for the scrollbar, but the scrollbar doesn't actually consume that space. The terminal renders fewer columns than the available width supports. The ~14px gap on the right side causes mouse coordinate mapping to be off — the farther right you go, the more the cumulative column offset pushes the selection pointer away from the actual cursor.

**Files involved:**
- `packages/web/src/app/globals.css:478` — `overflow-y: overlay !important` override
- `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx:218` — `scrollback: 10000` (triggers scrollbar width subtraction)
- `@xterm/addon-fit@0.11.0` — hardcoded `scrollbarWidth = 14` fallback

## Fix

**Option A (recommended):** Remove the `overflow-y: overlay` override. Let xterm.js use its default `overflow-y: auto` scrollbar behavior. The FitAddon already accounts for scrollbar width in its column calculation, so the default behavior is correct. If the auto-hide scrollbar aesthetic is desired, use a thin scrollbar via CSS without `overlay`:
```css
.xterm .xterm-viewport {
  overflow-y: auto !important;  /* or remove the rule entirely */
}
```

**Option B:** Keep `overlay` but override the scrollbar width by configuring `overviewRulerWidth: 0` on the Terminal instance. However, this is a hack — the FitAddon uses `overviewRuler?.width` which is meant for a different feature (minimap). Setting it to 0 just to zero out the scrollbar width is semantically wrong.

**Option C:** Use `scrollback: 0` to disable the scrollbar entirely. Not acceptable — scrollback is needed for terminal usability.

## Impact

- Affects all macOS desktop users on Retina displays (high-DPI amplifies the offset)
- Makes text selection unreliable on the right ~30% of the terminal
- Users on non-Retina displays likely see a smaller but still present offset

title: fix(web): terminal text selection offset on right side
body:
Fixes #1221

## Summary

- Changed xterm viewport scrollbar from `overflow-y: overlay` to `overflow-y: auto`
- The overlay scrollbar does not consume layout space, but xterm.js FitAddon subtracts 14px for scrollbar width when calculating terminal columns
- This mismatch causes incorrect mouse-to-column mapping on the right side of the terminal
- With `auto`, the scrollbar takes its natural space, matching FitAddon's calculation

## Root Cause

FitAddon (`@xterm/addon-fit@0.11.0`) calculates `scrollbarWidth = overviewRuler?.width || 14` (14px when scrollback > 0). It subtracts this from the available width to compute column count. But `overflow-y: overlay` renders the scrollbar on top of content without consuming layout space — so the 14px subtraction doesn't correspond to any actual space consumed. The resulting column mismatch causes mouse coordinate mapping to drift on the right side.

## Test

1. Open any session detail page on macOS
2. Drag-select text on the right side of the terminal
3. Selection pointer should align with mouse cursor (no offset)
4. Scrollbar still auto-hides when not hovering (via the CSS thumb rules)

title: fix(web): eliminate xterm terminal right-side text clipping
body:
Fixes #1023

## Problem

Text in the xterm terminal (session details page) is clipped on the right side. The last character's rightmost pixels are cut off, both when the scrollbar is visible and when it's hidden.

## Root Cause

The `xterm-viewport` element is absolutely positioned over the `xterm-screen` element (where text is rendered):

```css
/* xterm.css default */
.xterm-viewport {
  position: absolute;
  right: 0; left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0;
  overflow-y: scroll;
}
```

Our override used `overflow-y: overlay !important` which is **deprecated since Chrome 115** — it now behaves as `overflow-y: auto`. This means Chrome allocates a native scrollbar gutter (5-15px depending on OS) that overlaps the rightmost text pixels.

Additionally, the FitAddon (`@xterm/addon-fit@0.11.0`) reserves 14px for scrollbar width by default (`overviewRulerWidth || 14`), but this deduction only affects column count — it doesn't prevent the native scrollbar gutter from overlapping rendered text.

## Fix

Replace `overflow-y: overlay` with `overflow-y: scroll` + `scrollbar-width: none`:

- **`overflow-y: scroll`** — consistent behavior across all browsers (no deprecated values)
- **`scrollbar-width: none`** — completely removes the scrollbar gutter (no pixels stolen from text)
- Scrolling still works because xterm.js handles scrolling internally via its Viewport class (JavaScript `scrollTop` manipulation), not native scroll events

The existing webkit-scrollbar rules below (5px width, transparent thumb) are kept as a secondary fallback but effectively become no-ops since `scrollbar-width: none` hides the scrollbar entirely.

## Test Plan

1. Open a session detail page in non-fullscreen mode
2. Type or observe a line that fills the full terminal width
3. Verify the last character is fully visible (not clipped)
4. Scroll through terminal output — verify scrolling still works
5. Test on macOS (overlay scrollbar) and Linux/Windows (classic scrollbar)

Fixes #1220. Session cards in the dashboard used to render as noisy humanized branch names like **"Orchestrator/Ao Orchestrator 8"** or **"Ao 42"** — telling you nothing about what the session is actually working on.

title: Session detail page should treat exited activity as restorable
body:
## Problem

The session detail page (`/sessions/[id]`) determines whether a session is terminal/restorable using only `TERMINAL_STATUSES`.

That diverges from the rest of the web UI and core restore logic, which also treat `activity === "exited"` as terminal/restorable.

As a result, a crashed session whose status is still non-terminal (for example `"working"`) but whose activity is `"exited"`:
- does not show the Restore action on the detail page
- may still show the live terminal area instead of the ended-state placeholder
- is inconsistent with `SessionCard` and `sessionManager.restore()`

## Expected

Session detail should use the same terminal/restorable predicate as the rest of the app:
- terminal if `TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(session.status)` or `TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES.has(session.activity)`
- restorable if terminal and status is not in `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Restore appears on session detail for sessions with `activity === "exited"` even if `status` is not terminal
- Terminal area shows the ended placeholder for those sessions
- Session detail behavior matches `SessionCard` and core restore semantics
- Add a component test covering the exited-activity case

title: Enrich events with PR title, description and URL
body:
## Problem

When an AO session transitions state (e.g. `review.pending`, `completed`, `failed`, `stuck`), the event payload sent to external webhooks (e.g. n8n `ao-events`) only includes `sessionId`, `projectId`, `priority`, and a generic message like "ao-146: stuck → review_pending".

There is no information about **what the PR/session is about** — no PR title, description, issue summary, or PR URL. This makes Telegram/Discord notifications unhelpful since you can't tell at a glance what happened.

## Proposed Solution

Include session/PR context in **all** event payloads. Suggested fields:

```json
{
  "event": {
    "type": "review.pending",
    "sessionId": "ao-146",
    "projectId": "agent-orchestrator",
    "priority": "info",
    "pr": {
      "url": "https://github.com/.../pull/42",
      "title": "Fix retry logic in session manager",
      "body": "First 200 chars of PR description...",
      "issueTitle": "Original issue title",
      "branch": "fix/retry-logic"
    }
  }
}
```

The data should already be available in the session state (AO knows the issue, branch, and PR URL once it creates one). Just need to attach it to the outgoing webhook payload for every event type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All event payloads include PR URL, title, and issue title (when available)
- [ ] Events fired before PR creation gracefully omit PR fields
- [ ] Existing webhook consumers that ignore unknown fields are unaffected
- [ ] Notification integrations (Telegram, Discord) can display meaningful context without extra API calls

title: bug(web): Dashboard missing 10 built-in plugins, only 8 of 18 registered in services.ts
body:
The web dashboard's plugin registry in `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts` statically registers only 8 out of 18 built-in plugins. Any project configured to use an unregistered plugin (e.g. `agent: aider`, `agent: codex`, `scm: gitlab`) breaks silently in the dashboard — activity/summary show as `null`, and spawn/orchestrator API calls fail with `"plugin not found"`.

The CLI works correctly because it uses dynamic `import()` via `loadBuiltins()` in core's `plugin-registry.ts`. The web layer can't do that — Next.js webpack doesn't resolve `import(variable)` expressions — so plugins must be statically imported. The existing comment in `services.ts` explains this constraint.

- Currently registered (8)

| Slot | Plugin |
|------|--------|
| runtime | tmux |
| agent | claude-code |
| agent | cursor |
| agent | opencode |
| workspace | worktree |
| scm | github |
| tracker | github |
| tracker | linear |

- Missing (10)

| Slot | Plugin | Package |
|------|--------|---------|
| runtime | process | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-runtime-process` |
| agent | codex | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex` |
| agent | aider | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-aider` |
| workspace | clone | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-clone` |
| tracker | gitlab | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-gitlab` |
| scm | gitlab | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-gitlab` |
| notifier | desktop | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-desktop` |
| notifier | discord | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-discord` |
| notifier | slack | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-slack` |
| notifier | webhook | `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-webhook` |

- Root Cause

`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts` → `initServices()` only imports and registers a subset of what `BUILTIN_PLUGINS` in `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts` defines. When the web server calls `registry.get("agent", "aider")` (or any missing plugin), it returns `null`.

title: feat: add automated weekly release notes skill
body:
## AO Weekly Release Notes — Automated System

### What This Adds

A new skill at `skills/release-notes/ao-weekly-release/` that generates polished, publishable release notes automatically.

### Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `skills/release-notes/ao-weekly-release/SKILL.md` | Skill definition — data collection steps, output format, style constraints, error handling |
| `skills/release-notes/ao-weekly-release/run.py` | Deterministic runner — pulls data from `gh` API, generates markdown release notes |

### How It Works

**Scheduled Mode (Cron — Every Thursday 10:00 IST)**
1. Cron job pulls latest `main`: `git fetch origin && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main`
2. Executes: `python3 skills/release-notes/ao-weekly-release/run.py --mode scheduled`
3. Posts output to Discord channel `1486439595498405950`

**On-Demand Mode**
```bash
python3 skills/release-notes/ao-weekly-release/run.py --mode on-demand
```
Produces identical output. Useful for pre-release review.

### Output Format

Matches the established tone from [surajmarkup.in/research/ao-april-release](https://surajmarkup.in/research/ao-april-release/):
- Release title + date
- One-line positioning statement
- 8–14 highlight bullets (professional, factual)
- By the Numbers (commits, PRs, contributors, stars)
- Install block
- Links section
- Full release command checklist
- Operator checklist (checkbox style)

### Skill Updates

All future changes to the release notes skill go through PRs to this repo. Edit files under `skills/release-notes/ao-weekly-release/`. After merge, the next cron run automatically picks up changes — no manual redeployment needed.

### Error Handling

- No previous release → generates "Initial Release Summary"
- API/network failures → retries 3× with exponential backoff
- Missing optional metrics → omitted gracefully

title: web: sidebar flashes 'No active sessions' on /sessions/[id] and re-renders every 5s
body:
## Symptom

When navigating to `/sessions/[id]`, the project sidebar briefly shows **"No active sessions"** before the real session rows pop in a few seconds later. Additionally, the sidebar re-renders every 5 seconds even when nothing has changed.

This does **not** happen on `/` (the dashboard) — only on session detail pages.

## Root cause

`packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` is a pure `"use client"` component with no SSR. On mount it seeds:

```ts
const [projects, setProjects] = useState<ProjectInfo[]>([]);
const [sidebarSessions, setSidebarSessions] = useState<DashboardSession[]>([]);
```

So the very first paint is, by construction, an empty sidebar. `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:237` then renders `"No active sessions"` because `visibleSessions.length === 0`. The "No active sessions" copy is meant as a *terminal* empty state (the project genuinely has zero work), not as a loading state — using it as a transient placeholder lies to the user on every navigation.

After mount, four separate fetches fire from separate `useEffect`s:
- `/api/projects` (mount)
- `/api/sessions/:id` (mount + 5s poll)
- `/api/sessions` for the sidebar (mount + 5s poll)
- `/api/sessions?project=…&orchestratorOnly=true` (after a 2s `setTimeout` + 5s poll)

Once `/api/sessions` resolves, `setSidebarSessions(body?.sessions ?? [])` runs and the sidebar fills in. That's the flash.

The 5s `setInterval` then re-runs `setSidebarSessions(...)` **unconditionally** with a brand-new array reference, so `ProjectSidebar` re-renders and its `useMemo`s recompute every 5 seconds even when nothing actually changed.

For comparison, `/` (`packages/web/src/app/page.tsx`) is a server component that pre-renders sessions via `getDashboardPageData()` and pipes them through `useSessionEvents()` (which consumes the `MuxProvider` `sessions` topic for live updates). No flash, no polling. The session detail route is the architectural odd one out.

## Why this matters

- **P0** for perceived quality. The sidebar is the primary navigation surface, and it contradicts itself on every session click.
- Layout shift + content shift + semantic shift on every navigation erodes trust.
- The 5s re-render also makes the sidebar feel "alive" in a bad way and burns battery on idle pages.

## Expected behavior

- First paint already shows the populated sidebar (or skeleton rows during loading — never the terminal "No active sessions" copy as a placeholder).
- No re-render when underlying session data is unchanged.
- One data path for sidebar updates, shared with `/`.

## Fix

Two paths exist depending on timing:

### Long-term (already implemented)
The `ashish/feat/multi-dashboard-final` branch already fixes this structurally:
- Deletes `app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` in favor of a server-rendered `app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[sessionId]/page.tsx`
- Hosts the sidebar inside a shared `<DashboardShell>` that pipes SSR sessions through `useSessionEvents()` for live updates
- Uses `<UnifiedSidebar>` instead of the ad-hoc per-route `ProjectSidebar` wiring

When that branch merges, this bug auto-resolves.

### Short-term (until that branch lands)
Minimal patch to `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`, contained entirely in code the multi-project branch deletes (zero merge conflict risk):

1. Initialize `sidebarSessions` to `null` (not `[]`) and pass it to `ProjectSidebar` with a separate `loading` prop. Show skeleton rows while loading; reserve `"No active sessions"` for the genuine empty case.
2. Parallelize the initial mount fetches via `Promise.all` so `/api/sessions` doesn't queue behind `/api/projects` + `fetchSession`.
3. In `fetchSidebarSessions`, diff the new array against the previous one by `id + status + activity + lastActivityAt`. Skip `setSidebarSessions` if unchanged. Kills the every-5s re-render and `useMemo` recomputation.

Optional follow-up: drop the 5s sidebar poll entirely and subscribe to `useMux().sessions` instead — same source `Dashboard` already uses via `useSessionEvents`.

## Affected files

- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — the route with the bug
- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:237` — where "No active sessions" is rendered
- `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` — already has the live `sessions` topic the polling could be replaced with
- `packages/web/src/hooks/useSessionEvents.ts` — the hook `/` uses; the session detail route should also use it

title: fix(web): terminal auth and ownership checks for web terminal access
body:
This PR fixes issue #975 by tightening authorization around web terminal access and keeping the scope limited to the terminal path.

  Before this change, terminal access could be opened too loosely from the browser side. The fix introduces short-lived signed terminal grants that are issued by the
  authenticated web app and verified by the terminal/mux server before any tmux attach happens. That makes terminal access depend on both session identity and ownership,
  instead of trusting a raw session ID alone.

  What changed:

  - Added a server-side terminal auth module that issues and verifies signed, short-lived terminal grants.
  - Added /api/sessions/[id]/terminal so the web app can request an authorized terminal grant for a specific session.
  - Updated the mux terminal open flow to require the signed token and reject unauthorized or stale requests.
  - Updated the browser terminal client to fetch, cache, and refresh grants during reconnects instead of reopening terminals with only a session ID.
  - Moved the legacy terminal URL flow onto the same authorized path so both terminal entry points use the same checks.
  - Preserved existing server/build behavior outside this area and avoided unrelated config churn.

  Regression and hardening work included:

  - Guarded against stale terminal reopen races when a terminal is closed while auth is still in flight.
  - Ignored or actively closed stale opened acknowledgements from the server so closed terminals are not re-tracked client-side.
  - Kept the websocket formatting/build-path changes minimal to avoid the concerns previously raised on the earlier closed PR.
  - Deduplicated shared terminal port normalization used by the related route handlers.

  Validation:

  - Ran targeted web tests covering terminal auth issuance/verification, mux websocket behavior, provider reconnect/auth flow, and API route behavior.
  - Re-ran focused tests for follow-up review fixes in MuxProvider and the terminal API routes.
  - Confirmed the branch remained mergeable against main.

title: Session kill leaks PTY resources: orphaned claude + MCP processes exhaust macOS PTY limit
body:
## Summary

`ao session kill` only runs `tmux kill-session` which does not reliably terminate child processes. Claude Code agents and their MCP server subprocesses survive as orphans, leaking PTY file descriptors. After ~9 sessions are spawned and killed over a few days, macOS hits its default PTY limit (511), causing **all new terminal creation to fail system-wide** — including VS Code terminals, new tmux sessions, and ao's own dashboard terminal.

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.4.0), Apple Silicon (arm64)
- **ao version**: 0.1.0 (`npm install -g @composio/ao`)
- **Node**: v23.10.0
- **Agent**: claude-code v2.1.83
- **tmux**: 3.6a

## Steps to reproduce

1. `ao start` on a project
2. Spawn several sessions over time: `ao spawn <issue>` (×9 sessions over 3 days in my case)
3. Kill some sessions: `ao session kill mono-2`, etc.
4. Observe that processes from killed sessions are still running
5. Eventually, `tmux new-session` fails with `fork failed: Device not configured`
6. ao dashboard terminal shows "CONNECTING..." forever with `posix_spawnp failed` in logs
7. Even VS Code and Terminal.app can no longer open new terminals

## Root cause

### 1. `ao session kill` only calls `tmux kill-session`

From `ao-core/dist/tmux.js`:
```javascript
export async function killSession(sessionName) {
    await tmux("kill-session", "-t", sessionName);
}
```

No process group kill, no PID tracking, no child process cleanup.

### 2. Each session has ~8 processes, not 1

A single ao session spawns this process tree:

```
zsh (shell)
└── claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
    ├── npm exec @upstash/context7-mcp → node context7-mcp
    ├── npm exec @workos/mcp-docs-server → node mcp-docs-server
    └── uv tool uvx elevenlabs-mcp → python elevenlabs-mcp
```

That's **8 processes per session**, each holding PTY resources.

### 3. `tmux kill-session` SIGHUP doesn't propagate reliably

When tmux kills a session, it sends SIGHUP to the session leader (zsh). But:
- Claude Code (Node.js) has its own signal handlers and may not propagate SIGHUP to children
- MCP servers (node + python subprocesses) have their own signal handlers
- Result: claude and all 6 MCP servers **survive as orphans**

### 4. Evidence from a real system

After killing sessions mono-2, mono-5, mono-7, mono-8, mono-9:

```
$ ps -eo pid,tty,command | grep ttys203  # mono-5 was KILLED

60125 ttys203  -zsh
60171 ttys203  claude --dangerously-skip-permissions        ← orphan
60196 ttys203  npm exec @upstash/context7-mcp               ← orphan
60198 ttys203  npm exec @workos/mcp-docs-server              ← orphan
60200 ttys203  uv tool uvx elevenlabs-mcp                    ← orphan
60252 ttys203  python elevenlabs-mcp                         ← orphan
60272 ttys203  node context7-mcp                             ← orphan
60290 ttys203  node mcp-docs-server                          ← orphan
```

All 8 processes still running, holding TTY ttys203 open indefinitely.

### 5. PTY math

```
$ sysctl kern.tty.ptmx_max
kern.tty.ptmx_max: 511          # macOS default

$ ls /dev/ttys* | wc -l
526                               # exceeded limit
```

Each session leaks ~8 processes that hold PTY file descriptors. After 9 sessions × 8 processes = ~72 orphaned processes, plus VS Code/terminal/other usage, the 511 limit is exhausted.

## Impact

- **System-wide terminal failure**: not just ao — VS Code, Terminal.app, any app that opens a PTY stops working
- **Misleading error**: `posix_spawnp failed` looks like a binary compatibility issue, not a resource exhaustion. Took significant debugging to identify.
- **Silent accumulation**: users won't notice until it's too late. No warnings, no cleanup, no monitoring.

## Suggested fix

### Immediate: proper process cleanup in `killSession`

```javascript
export async function killSession(sessionName) {
    // 1. Get the TTY for the session's pane
    const tty = await getTmuxPaneTTY(sessionName);
    
    // 2. Find all processes on that TTY
    const pids = await getProcessesByTTY(tty);
    
    // 3. Kill the tmux session
    await tmux("kill-session", "-t", sessionName);
    
    // 4. SIGTERM the process group, then SIGKILL stragglers
    for (const pid of pids) {
        process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM');
    }
    await sleep(2000);
    for (const pid of pids) {
        try { process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch {}
    }
}
```

### Defensive: add PTY health check

- `ao doctor` should check `kern.tty.ptmx_max` vs current allocation and warn
- `ao status` could show PTY usage when >80% of max
- `ao session kill` should verify all child processes actually exited

### Documentation

- Note in SETUP.md that macOS has a 511 PTY default limit
- Recommend `sudo sysctl kern.tty.ptmx_max=1024` for users running many sessions
- Or better: ao could set this automatically during `ao setup` / first run

## Workaround

For users hitting this now:

```bash
# Raise the PTY limit (resets on reboot)
sudo sysctl kern.tty.ptmx_max=1024

# Find and kill orphaned processes from dead sessions
ps -eo pid,tty,command | grep "claude.*dangerously-skip" | grep -v grep
# Then kill -TERM <pid> for each orphan

# Or nuclear: kill all ao-spawned claude processes
pkill -f "claude.*dangerously-skip"
```

title: fix: fail ao send when killed session delivery is not confirmed
body:
## Summary

Fix `ao send` falsely reporting success for sessions that are already `status=killed`.

When delivery requires restoring a dead session, the send path now requires the restored runtime to become ready and requires delivery confirmation before treating the operation as successful. If restore/readiness/delivery confirmation fails, the CLI now prints the error and exits non-zero instead of printing `Message sent and processing`.

Closes #1074.

## Changes

- make `SessionManager.send()` fail when a restored session never becomes ready for delivery
- require delivery confirmation for sends that depend on restore instead of treating them as soft success
- make `ao send` surface lifecycle-send failures as a user-facing error with exit code `1`
- add core and CLI regression tests covering the killed-session case

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core exec vitest run src/__tests__/session-manager/communication.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli exec vitest run __tests__/commands/send.test.ts`

## Manual Verification

1. In a checkout on `main`, create or identify a killed session:
   - `ao spawn <issue>`
   - `ao session kill <session-id>`
   - confirm `ao session ls` shows `<session-id>` as `killed`
2. On `main`, run `ao send <session-id> "hello"` and observe the current buggy behavior:
   - it prints `Message sent and processing`
   - it exits `0`
   - no message is actually delivered
3. Switch to this branch and build the CLI:
   - `pnpm install`
   - `pnpm build`
4. Run `ao send <same-session-id> "hello"` again.
5. Confirm the fixed behavior:
   - it prints an error like `Cannot send to session <session-id>: session is not running ...`
   - it exits `1`
   - it does not report false success

title: fix(scm-github): handle HTTP 304 correctly in ETag guard catch blocks
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1191 — ETag Guard treats HTTP 304 as failure, defeats caching optimization

## Root Cause

The `gh` CLI exits with a non-zero exit code on HTTP 304 responses. This caused `execFileAsync` to throw before the `try`-block 304-detection code could run (dead code). Both catch blocks in `checkPRListETag` and `checkCommitStatusETag` were treating every HTTP 304 as a failure — logging a warning and returning `true` ("assume changed"). As a result, the full GraphQL batch ran every 30 seconds instead of being skipped when nothing had changed.

## Changes Made

- `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` — Added an early `if (errorMsg.includes("HTTP 304")) return false` check at the top of both catch blocks (Guard 1 in `checkPRListETag`, Guard 2 in `checkCommitStatusETag`). When the error is a 304, the function now correctly returns `false` (not modified — skip batch, use cache). All other errors fall through to the existing warn-and-return-true path unchanged.

## Testing

- All 140 tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github test`)
- The two test files that cover `graphql-batch.ts` directly (`graphql-batch.test.ts` — 65 tests, `graphql-batch.integration.test.ts` — 8 tests) pass with no changes needed

## Notes

The fix matches on `"HTTP 304"` as a substring in the error message, which matches the standard `gh` CLI output format (`gh: HTTP 304`). The existing dead code in the `try` block (checking `stdout` for `"HTTP/1.1 304"` or `"HTTP/2 304"`) is left untouched — removing it would be out of scope for this fix.

Fixes #1191

title: feat(core): opt-in gh CLI tracer + scm/tracker migration (Phase A1a)
body:
## Summary

First slice of Track A from `experiments/PLAN.md` (v2.3): a minimal, opt-in `gh` CLI tracer and the migration of the three current `gh` callsites to use it. No behavior change when the trace env var is unset.

## What's in this PR

**New API** — `@aoagents/ao-core`:
- `execGhObserved(args, ctx, timeout?)` — wraps `execFile("gh", ...)`, writes one JSONL row per invocation to `$AO_GH_TRACE_FILE` on both success and failure paths, returns `stdout.trim()` (same contract as the old helpers).
- `GhTraceEntry` / `GhTraceContext` types.

**Captured per row:** timestamp, component, operation, args, endpoint, method, ok, exitCode, signal, durationMs, stdoutBytes, stderrBytes, statusLine, httpStatus, etag, `x-ratelimit-*`.

**Migrations:**
- `scm-github/graphql-batch.ts` — PR-list ETag guard, commit-status ETag guard, GraphQL batch query
- `scm-github/index.ts` — `gh()` / `ghInDir()` helpers
- `tracker-github/index.ts` — internal `gh()` helper

**Docs** (under `experiments/`):
- `PLAN.md` — the v2.3 Track A/B/C plan
- `ao-lifecycle-gh-cli-interactions.md` — call-catalog reference
- `2026-04-14-etag-verification.md`, `gh-etag-verification-experiment-codex.md`
- `gh-trace-harness.md` + `summarize-gh-trace.mjs`

## What's deliberately NOT in this PR

This is Phase **A1a**, not full PLAN.md v2.3. The following land in A1b:

- `GhRunner.run(): Promise<GhResult>` contract. Today `execGhObserved` still returns `Promise<string>` and rethrows the raw `execFileAsync` error. The trace row is written on the failure path, but callers on the reject side don't yet receive `error.ghResult`.
- **Body capture + redaction.** The tracer records `stdoutBytes` (length only), not body content. No 64 KB cap, no header/body split, no comment-body redaction yet — intentional, because without body capture there's nothing to redact. If we want body capture for debugging, it lands with redaction at the same time.
- **Scorecard baseline.** No recorder summary wired into the 6×2×5 scenario matrix yet. The harness doc + summarizer script are here as scaffolding.

## Known gaps

- Two `gh` callsites not migrated: `graphql-batch.ts:319` (a `gh --version` probe — probably fine to leave) and `web/src/app/api/setup-labels/route.ts:31` (in scope, can fold in either here or a followup).
- Test hook side effect: `setExecFileAsync()` in `graphql-batch.ts` now also overrides the observer path so existing tests bypass the tracer. Tracer has no unit tests in this PR — coming in A1b.

## How to use it

\`\`\`bash
export AO_GH_TRACE_FILE=~/.agent-orchestrator/traces/gh-\$(date +%F).jsonl
# run AO normally; rows append to the file
node experiments/summarize-gh-trace.mjs \$AO_GH_TRACE_FILE
\`\`\`

With the env var unset, nothing is written and there's no perf impact.

## Test plan

- [ ] Type-check: \`pnpm typecheck\`
- [ ] Unit tests: \`pnpm test\` (scm-github + tracker-github)
- [ ] Manual: run with \`AO_GH_TRACE_FILE\` set, verify JSONL rows appear with sane \`httpStatus\`, \`etag\`, \`rateLimitRemaining\`
- [ ] Manual: run without the env var, verify zero overhead / no file created

## Why draft

Posting early for review of the tracer shape, the trace row schema, and the PLAN.md v2.3 direction before A1b lands. Happy to rework the row schema or the wrapper API based on feedback — nothing downstream depends on this yet.

title: fix(web): guard xterm FitAddon against disposed terminal (#936)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #936. The session detail page crashed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')` whenever the xterm.js terminal was disposed (theme switch, reconnect, unmount) while a deferred resize timer/RAF or the reconnect effect still held a stale ref. xterm's `FitAddon.fit()` reads `terminal._core._renderService.dimensions` internally — undefined after `dispose()` or on a zero-size container at first mount — and throws up through React.

## Changes
- New shared `safeFit()` helper wraps every `fit.fit()` call, catches the TypeError, logs a warning, and returns `false` so callers bail instead of crashing.
- Cleanup nulls out `terminalInstance.current` / `fitAddon.current` **before** `dispose()` so concurrent effects see `null` instead of a disposed instance.
- Fullscreen-resize effect no longer captures `terminal` / `fit` in closure — deferred RAF/setTimeout callbacks re-read the refs at call time so a mid-flight re-create (e.g. theme change) can't feed a disposed terminal to `refresh()` / `fit()`.

## Root cause
`DirectTerminal`'s main effect re-runs on `resolvedTheme` / `appearance` / `sessionId` changes. The old cleanup called `terminal.dispose()` but left the refs dangling; the "reconnect" and "fullscreen resize" effects then raced with the next async terminal creation and called `fit.fit()` on the disposed instance — triggering the `dimensions` TypeError reported in the issue. The `Failed to fetch` error mentioned in the issue was a symptom, not the cause: even with data loaded, the race still fired on any theme/layout change.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck` — passes
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 598 passed (4 new `safeFit` tests)
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm build` (web) — production build succeeds
- [x] New unit tests cover: null `fit`, null `terminal`, success path, and the exact `"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')"` TypeError path from the issue

Closes #936

title: feat(openclaw): make ao discoverable and usable from agents (#482)
body:
## Summary

Closes #482. An OpenClaw agent with `ao` installed on the same machine had no way to discover it — no SKILL.md, no tool registration, no prompt hint — so the engineer had to tell the agent "go use `ao`" manually, and even then the agent had to figure out the lifecycle, config location, and error messages on its own.

This PR closes the specific agent-facing gaps called out in the issue so an OpenClaw (or any) agent can discover and drive `ao` without hand-holding:

- **Ship `SKILL.md`** describing the full `ao init` → `ao spawn` lifecycle with concrete recipes and error remediation. `ao setup openclaw` now installs it to `~/.openclaw/skills/ao.skill.md`, making the OpenClaw → `ao` half of the integration no longer one-directional (issue points 1 & 4).
- **XDG config discoverability**: honor `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `~/.config/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator.yaml`. Export `getConfigSearchPaths()` from core; legacy dotfile and `config.yaml` locations still work (issue point 5).
- **`ao status` prints the active config path** as the first line — one call to find out where the config lives (issue point 5).
- **`ConfigNotFoundError`** now enumerates the searched locations and points at `ao init` (not the stale `ao start` suggestion).
- **`ao spawn` / `ao batch-spawn`** translate `ConfigNotFoundError` into a clean, non-stack-trace error with explicit next steps for agents calling `ao` programmatically (issue point 2 — the "hidden prerequisite" story; note that `ao spawn` already auto-starts the lifecycle worker via `ensureLifecycleWorker`, so a separate `ao start` is not required).

**Drive-by fix**: `packages/cli/src/index.ts` and its test had a typo `@composio/ao-core` (should be `@aoagents/ao-core`) that was blocking the CLI package from building or testing at all. Fixed so CI actually runs.

Issue point 3 (ad-hoc repo support — `ao spawn --repo ComposioHQ/integrator --claim-pr 1299`) is intentionally **not** in this PR. It's a meaningfully larger design change (clone + workspace registration + config generation in one shot) and deserves its own PR with more design discussion. Filed as follow-up work.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 601 passed (includes 7 new `config-find.test.ts` tests covering XDG paths, XDG_CONFIG_HOME override, precedence, and the null case).
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` — clean.

Agent process dies but session remains in [working] state, creating orphaned sessions that cannot be   recovered or cleaned up.
body: ## Description Agent-orchestrator currently lacks a checkpoint mechanism for persisting and recovering agent execution state during long-running sessions. When an agent session is interrupted (due to process termination, system crash, or manual cancellation), all work-in-progress is lost. Sessions can become stuck in the working state with no mechanism to resume from the last safe point. The existing recovery system handles dead session cleanup and re-registration, but provides no way to restore the agent's execution context, intermediate results, or task state. This forces users to restart work from scratch, reducing reliability and wasting computational resources. ## Reproduction Steps 1. Start a long-running agent session on a complex task `ao spawn --agent soma --prompt "Analyze the agent-orchestrator plugin system. Include: (1) Architecture overview, (2) 5 core plugins, (3) Extension points, (4) Lifecycle hooks, (5) Best practices. Take 30 seconds."` 2. Observe the session enter working state `ao session ls` 3. Interrupt the agent mid-execution before completion `pkill -9 -f "soma/main.py"` 4. Check session status after interruption `ps aux | grep python3 | grep -v grep` (returns nothing, no process running) `tmux capture-pane -t 23246b1e3409-soma-23 -p` (shell is idle, prompt visible) 5. Attempt to verify work status `ls -lh ~/Desktop/soma/outputs/ | tail -3` (output file may be incomplete or missing if interrupted at right moment) Result: Session cannot be restored because no execution checkpoint exists. All work-in-progress state is lost. User must spawn a new session. ## Actual Behavior 1. No checkpoint mechanism exists. Session state is metadata only: status, createdAt, tmuxName, branch, agent. 2. Interrupting an agent mid-execution loses all work-in-progress including partial outputs, internal state, and execution context. 3. 13+ sessions remain stuck in working status with stale timestamps: Examples: soma-10: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (36+ hours old) soma-11: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (31+ hours old) soma-12: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (31+ hours old) soma-13: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (31+ hours old) soma-14: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (31+ hours old) soma-2: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (6+ hours old) soma-3: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (6+ hours old) soma-4: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (6+ hours old) soma-5: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (5+ hours old) soma-6: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (6+ hours old) soma-7: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (6+ hours old) soma-8: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (6+ hours old) soma-9: status=working, created 2026-04-14 (1+ hour old) 4. Session metadata becomes unreliable as source of truth: shows status=working but ps aux shows no python3 process running. 5. Recovery system can only clean up dead sessions or re-register live ones. Cannot restore execution context from checkpoints because no checkpoints exist. 6. Users must manually restart work, losing intermediate results and task progress. ## Expected Behavior When a session is interrupted: 1. The last safe execution checkpoint is preserved in session storage 2. Checkpoint contains: agent execution state, message history, tool outputs, task progress markers 3. Session status transitions to checkpoint_ready 4. User can resume from checkpoint with full context restoration: ao session resume soma-23 (Agent context is restored, continues from last checkpoint) 5. Multiple checkpoints are retained with timestamps 6. Checkpoints survive orchestrator restarts and process crashes 7. Recovery system validates checkpoint integrity before restoration ## Screenshots

title: Terminal selection vanishes on session update (~5s)
body:
## Bug

Selecting text in the terminal (click + drag) works momentarily, but the selection disappears within ~5 seconds without user interaction.

## Root Cause

`MuxProvider.tsx` (line 400) creates a single `contextValue` via `useMemo` that includes both **terminal operation callbacks** (stable) and **session state** (`status`, `sessions` — changes every ~5s from SSE snapshot).

Every session update changes the context object reference, which triggers `DirectTerminal`'s main `useEffect` (lines 187–402) to re-run — destroying and recreating the entire xterm.js instance. Any active selection is wiped.

## Fix

Split `MuxContext` into two contexts:
1. **`MuxTerminalContext`** — `subscribeTerminal`, `writeTerminal`, `openTerminal`, `closeTerminal`, `resizeTerminal` (stable refs via `useCallback` with no reactive deps)
2. **`MuxSessionContext`** — `status`, `sessions` (reactive, updates freely)

`DirectTerminal` only subscribes to the stable terminal context → no more remounts → selection persists.

## Files

- `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` — split context
- `packages/web/src/hooks/useMux.ts` — export both hooks
- `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` — use stable terminal context
- Any other consumers of `useMux()` that only need session data

## Environment

- Affects all browsers
- Reproducible on any active agent session with terminal output

title: fix(web): eliminate sidebar flash and redundant re-renders on session detail page (#1230)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1230 — web: sidebar flashes 'No active sessions' on /sessions/[id] and re-renders every 5s

## Root Cause

`packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` is a pure client component with no SSR, so `sidebarSessions` was initialized to `[]` (empty array). This caused the `ProjectSidebar` to show "No active sessions" on every navigation — a permanent empty-state message used as a transient loading placeholder — before the `/api/sessions` fetch resolved and filled the list. Additionally, `fetchSidebarSessions` unconditionally called `setSidebarSessions(...)` every 5 seconds with a fresh array reference, forcing `ProjectSidebar` and all its `useMemo` computations to re-run even when no session data had changed.

## Changes Made

- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — Changed `sidebarSessions` initial state from `[]` to `null`; added a `sidebarSessionsRef` for diffing; updated `fetchSidebarSessions` to compare incoming sessions by `id + status + activity + lastActivityAt` and skip `setSidebarSessions` when nothing changed; parallelized the initial `fetchSession` + `fetchSidebarSessions` calls via `Promise.all`; passes `sidebarLoading={sidebarSessions === null}` to `SessionDetail`
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` — Added optional `sidebarLoading?: boolean` prop (defaults `false`); forwards it to `ProjectSidebar`
- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — Added optional `loading?: boolean` prop; added `SessionSkeleton` component that renders 3 placeholder rows with a dimmed dot; renders skeleton rows in place of the sessions list (including "No active sessions") while loading

## Testing

- [x] Existing tests pass (`pnpm test` — 443 tests across all packages; pre-existing `tracker-gitlab` failure unrelated to this change)
- [x] Manually verified: `sidebarSessions === null` on first paint triggers skeleton rows, not "No active sessions"
- [x] Diff check verified: `setSidebarSessions` only fires when `id`, `status`, `activity`, or `lastActivityAt` changes

## Notes

The `SessionSkeleton` rows use two new BEM modifier classes (`--skeleton`) that currently render as unstyled placeholder divs. A follow-up can add a shimmer/pulse animation in `globals.css` if desired — the flash elimination works without it.

The long-term fix (from `ashish/feat/multi-dashboard-final`) replaces this entire route with a server-rendered layout. This patch is intentionally minimal and zero-conflict with that branch since it only touches code that branch deletes.

Fixes #1230

title: bug(npm release): ao doctor fails, and ao update crashes instead of handling npm installs, in @aoagents/ao global installs
body:
## Summary

In a clean global npm install of the currently documented package, `@aoagents/ao`, both `ao doctor` and `ao update` fail because the published CLI tries to execute repo-local shell scripts that are not present in the npm artifact.

Tested with:

- package: `@aoagents/ao@0.2.5`
- OS: Ubuntu on WSL
- Node: `v24.12.0`
- npm: `11.6.2`

## Reproduction

```bash
npm install -g @aoagents/ao
ao doctor
ao update
```

## Actual behavior

`ao doctor` fails with:

```text
Script not found: .../node_modules/scripts/ao-doctor.sh
```

`ao update` fails with:

```text
Script not found: .../node_modules/scripts/ao-update.sh
```

## Expected behavior

For a global npm install:

- `ao doctor` should run successfully without requiring a source checkout
- `ao update` should not crash with a raw missing-script error; it should either:
  - handle npm-global installs correctly, or
  - exit with a clear source-install-only message / manual update instruction

## Why this seems like a real release bug

The README and setup docs present `npm install -g @aoagents/ao` as the normal install path, with source install called out separately for contributors.

The CLI docs describe `ao doctor` as a regular maintenance command. They do describe `ao update` as source-install-oriented, but even with that expectation, the current npm behavior is still broken because it crashes on a missing unpublished file instead of handling the install method deliberately.

## Root cause

The published CLI still delegates to repo script helpers:

- `ao doctor` -> `ao-doctor.sh`
- `ao update` -> `ao-update.sh`

Those scripts exist in the source repo, but they are not shipped in the published npm package, so the installed CLI resolves paths under `node_modules/scripts/...` that do not exist.

## Suggested fix

Detect install method before delegating to repo scripts.

- For source installs, current script-based behavior is fine.
- For npm-global installs:
  - `ao doctor` should run packaged checks directly
  - `ao update` should either perform the npm update flow or print the correct upgrade command / source-only guidance

title: fix(runtime-tmux): multiline ao send leaves message unsubmitted (#1110)
body:
## Problem

`ao send` with multi-line or long messages places the text in the tmux input buffer but never submits it. The agent session sits idle at the `❯` prompt with the message visible — no Enter keypress is delivered. Users had to manually run `tmux send-keys -t <session> Enter` after every `ao send` call.

## Root Cause

Two timing gaps in `runtime-tmux`'s `sendMessage` (the path taken when a session is registered with the session manager):

1. **No delay after `C-u`** — `load-buffer + paste-buffer` started immediately after the clear keypress, before the terminal application had processed it. Short messages are unaffected since they go through `send-keys -l`, but the buffer path is used for all multiline/long content.

2. **Flat 300 ms pre-Enter delay for all messages** — `paste-buffer` is asynchronous; tmux returns from the command before the target application has consumed all pasted keystrokes. 300 ms is enough for short pastes but not for multiline heredocs. `core/src/tmux.ts:sendKeys` already used 1 000 ms for the identical scenario — `sendMessage` was inconsistent.

## Fix

| Change | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Delay after `C-u` | 0 ms | 200 ms (matches `send.ts:sendViaTmux`) |
| Pre-Enter delay (multiline/long) | 300 ms | 1 000 ms (matches `core/src/tmux.ts:sendKeys`) |
| Pre-Enter delay (short text) | 300 ms | 300 ms (unchanged) |

Single file changed: `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts`.

## Testing

All 26 existing `runtime-tmux` tests pass (the multiline tests now correctly reflect the 1 s delay in their runtimes).

```
✓ src/__tests__/index.test.ts (26 tests)
  ✓ runtime.sendMessage() > sends short text with send-keys -l (literal) + Enter
  ✓ runtime.sendMessage() > uses load-buffer + paste-buffer for long text (> 200 chars)
  ✓ runtime.sendMessage() > uses load-buffer for multiline text
```

Fixes #1110

title: fix(cli): make ao start URL cloning interactive to avoid SSH prompt hang
body: Fixes #1256 ## Problem When running `ao start `, the URL clone flow tries multiple strategies (gh -> git+ssh -> git+https). The git+ssh path can trigger an interactive SSH prompt (most commonly first-time `github.com` host-key verification: "Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no/[fingerprint])?"). Because the clone command was executed in a non-interactive way (stdin/TTY not forwarded), the prompt could not be answered. The process would block indefinitely, meaning: - `ao start` appeared stuck - the clone step never errored - the flow never reached the intended HTTPS fallback ## Solution - Run clone/install subprocesses with TTY forwarding (`spawn(..., { stdio: \"inherit\" })`) so prompts accept input and failures are deterministic. - Extend `runInteractiveCommand(cmd, args)` with an optional options bag (`cwd`, `env`, `action`, `installHints`) and reuse it across these flows. - Remove the redundant interactive spawn helper to prevent drift. works now as it accepts input and fallbacks if it fails ## Behavior change - `ao start ` no longer hangs on SSH prompts; users can respond to prompts, and if SSH clone fails, the code can proceed to the next fallback strategy. ## Test plan - On a machine/user without `github.com` in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, run `ao start ` and verify the `yes/no` prompt accepts input and cloning completes (or fails and falls back deterministically). - Verify installer prompts still work and error messages remain well-formatted.

title: fix(ao start): URL clone can hang on SSH host-key prompt (non-interactive exec)
body: ## Summary Running `ao start ` can **hang indefinitely** during the clone step when Git/SSH prompts for interactive input (most commonly **first-time host key verification** for `github.com`). Because the clone is executed in a non-interactive way, the prompt cannot be answered, and the process does not error/return — so `ao start` never proceeds to its intended HTTPS fallback. ## Environment - CLI: `ao start ` - Scenario: machine/user without an existing `~/.ssh/known_hosts` entry for `github.com` (or any case where `ssh` prompts) ## Steps to reproduce 1. Ensure `github.com` is not present in `~/.ssh/known_hosts` (fresh machine/user profile, or remove that entry). 2. Run: ```bash ao start https://github.com//.git ``` 3. Observe output similar to: ```text The authenticity of host 'github.com (..)' can't be established. ED25519 key fingerprint is ... Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no/[fingerprint])? ``` ## Actual behavior - The process becomes **stuck at the SSH prompt** and does not accept `yes/no` input. - `ao start` does not exit, and the clone flow does not advance to the next fallback. ## Expected behavior - If a command requires interactivity (host-key prompt, credentials, etc.), `ao start` should **inherit the user’s TTY** so input can be provided. - If the SSH clone fails, `ao start` should **fall back** to the next strategy (e.g. HTTPS) rather than hanging indefinitely. ## Technical root cause The URL start path performs cloning in multiple strategies (gh -> git+ssh -> git+https). The SSH strategy can invoke `ssh` which prints a prompt and waits for stdin. When the clone is executed via a non-interactive child-process invocation (no TTY/stdin forwarding), the underlying `ssh` prompt cannot be answered. In this state: - the child process waits forever for input, - no exception is thrown, - and the orchestrator cannot continue to the fallback stage. ## Proposed fix Run clone/install subprocesses using `spawn(..., { stdio: 'inherit' })` (or an equivalent helper) so interactive prompts can be answered and the process can either complete or fail deterministically. ## Related PR Fix implemented in PR #1255.

title: refactor(web): replace SSE with WebSocket polling for session updates
body:
## Summary

Eliminates SSE as a protocol from the system. The browser now has exactly one real-time connection: the WebSocket on `:14801`. HTTP is used for on-demand requests.

**Before:**
```
Browser  →(SSE EventSource)→  Next.js GET /api/events
WS Server →(SSE fetch+stream)→  Next.js GET /api/events  (SessionBroadcaster)
```

**After:**
```
Browser  →(WS sessions sub-channel)←  WS Server  →(HTTP poll every 3s)→  GET /api/sessions/patches
```

## Changes

- **Delete `GET /api/events`** — no consumers remain after this PR
- **`SessionBroadcaster`** (`mux-websocket.ts`) — replaces SSE stream fetch + reconnect loop with a plain `setInterval` polling `GET /api/sessions/patches` every 3s (~150 lines → ~40 lines)
- **`useSessionEvents`** — removes `EventSource` block entirely; hook is now WebSocket-only via `mux.sessions`; renames `SSEAttentionMap` → `AttentionMap` and `sseAttentionLevels` → `attentionLevels` throughout
- **`useMuxSessionActivity`** (new) — replaces `useSSESessionActivity`; thin selector over `useMux().sessions`, no network call
- **Deletes** `SSESnapshotEvent`, `SSEActivityEvent` types from `lib/types.ts`
- **Updates** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` to reflect the simplified two-protocol design

## Stats

- **995 lines deleted, 162 added** (net −833)
- 5 files deleted, 1 file created, 12 files modified

- `grep -r "new EventSource" packages/web/src` → 0 results
- `grep -r "api/events" packages/web/src packages/web/server` → 0 results
- `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web typecheck` → clean
