title: fix: default dashboard services to loopback with explicit remote opt-in
body:
## Why

This PR fixes the two verified security findings from the audit without introducing an app-level auth system:

1. the AO dashboard/control-plane HTTP surface was reachable remotely whenever the app was bound off-loopback; and
2. the direct terminal WebSocket (`/mux`) was likewise remotely reachable without built-in auth.

The constraint here was important: keep the OSS workflow simple, avoid bolting on login/auth, and make the smallest realistic change that materially improves the default security posture.

The result is a safer default with explicit remote opt-in.

## What changed

### 1) Dashboard and direct terminal now default to loopback

AO now binds both the Next.js dashboard and the direct terminal WebSocket to `127.0.0.1` by default.

That means a plain `ao start` behaves as a local-only control plane unless the operator explicitly opts into remote exposure.

### 2) Remote exposure is explicit, warned, and still supported

If someone intentionally wants remote access, they can still do it with env vars:

```bash
HOST=0.0.0.0 ao start
```

or more selectively:

```bash
AO_DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0 AO_DIRECT_TERMINAL_HOST=127.0.0.1 ao start
```

Startup now emits warnings whenever either the dashboard HTTP API or direct terminal WebSocket is intentionally bound off-loopback without built-in auth.

### 3) Existing `HOST=...` remote setups keep working

A key compatibility detail: if an existing deployment already uses the older `HOST=0.0.0.0` pattern, the direct terminal now inherits that host unless `AO_DIRECT_TERMINAL_HOST` is explicitly set.

That preserves existing remote workflows instead of silently making the dashboard reachable while leaving terminal access broken.

### 4) Runtime terminal config now includes host metadata

`GET /api/runtime/terminal` now returns the direct terminal host alongside the runtime-selected ports and proxy path.

That allows the browser to distinguish between:
- a directly reachable terminal endpoint,
- a reverse-proxied terminal path, and
- a terminal that is intentionally loopback-only.

### 5) The frontend degrades cleanly when direct terminal is intentionally local-only

When the browser is remote and the direct terminal is loopback-bound, the mux provider now marks the terminal as `unavailable` instead of endlessly retrying a broken connection path.

The DirectTerminal UI now surfaces this state as **"Terminal unavailable"**, which is much clearer than repeated reconnect churn.

### 6) `packages/web` startup scripts are now cross-platform

The web package previously relied on POSIX shell expansion for host defaults. This PR replaces that with a small Node launcher script so `dev`/`start` respect the same host rules on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

### 7) Tests and docs were updated with the new behavior

The PR adds regression coverage for:
- loopback-default host resolution,
- legacy `HOST` fallback compatibility,
- runtime terminal host reporting,
- remote/loopback terminal unavailability behavior, and
- tmux-missing integration environments skipping cleanly.

It also updates the docs so users understand the new defaults and the explicit env-based opt-in path for remote exposure.

## Behavioral summary

### Before
- `ao start` could expose the dashboard control plane remotely depending on bind host.
- direct terminal exposure followed the same general pattern and could be reachable remotely without app-layer auth.
- remote browsers could end up attempting terminal connections that were invalid for the actual network topology.

### After
- `ao start` is local-only by default.
- remote exposure requires an explicit operator choice.
- old `HOST=...` remote setups continue to work.
- remote browsers get a clean unavailable state when direct terminal is intentionally local-only.

## No-auth constraint preserved

This PR does **not** add login, sessions, auth middleware, or proxy-coupled assumptions.

Instead, it tightens the default network boundary and makes unsafe exposure an explicit, operator-controlled decision.

That felt like the right tradeoff for an OSS tool whose normal usage is local-first.

## Docs updated

- `README.md`
- `docs/CLI.md`
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`

These now document:
- loopback-by-default behavior,
- explicit remote exposure examples,
- `HOST`, `AO_DASHBOARD_HOST`, and `AO_DIRECT_TERMINAL_HOST`, and
- the host fallback behavior used by the web launcher/runtime.

## Validation

Passed:

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint` (warnings only; existing warnings remain)
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test`

Note: the direct terminal integration suite now skips cleanly when `tmux` is unavailable, rather than failing the run.

## Reviewer guide

The most important files to review are:

- `packages/cli/src/lib/web-dir.ts`
- `packages/web/server/start-all.ts`
- `packages/web/server/direct-terminal-ws.ts`
- `packages/web/src/app/api/runtime/terminal/route.ts`
- `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx`
- `packages/web/scripts/run-next.cjs`

## Practical operator notes

If you want the old remotely reachable behavior, it is still available — it is just no longer accidental.

Examples:

```bash
# expose both dashboard and direct terminal
HOST=0.0.0.0 ao start

# expose only the dashboard; keep direct terminal local
AO_DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0 AO_DIRECT_TERMINAL_HOST=127.0.0.1 ao start
```

That puts the operator in control of the risk boundary, which is exactly where it should be.

title: feat: code-review plugin slot — AI-powered peer review for worker PRs
body:
## Summary

Add `code-review` as the **9th plugin slot** in AO. When a coding agent opens a PR, AO auto-spawns a lightweight reviewer workspace (not a full AO session), runs the CodeReview plugin in it, posts structured findings, and loops until the code is clean or the human intervenes.

This closes the gap where AO currently depends on external review infrastructure (Bugbot, Copilot, human reviewers) for the first review pass.

**Closes #139**

## How it works

**Where do findings go?** AO keeps findings local — in its own flat-file review store, not as GitHub PR comments. The human sees them on a new **Review Workbench** page in the dashboard. Publishing to GitHub is supported but off by default (privacy, control, and line-mapping fragility).

**How does the coding agent get findings?** The reviewer doesn't talk to the coding agent directly. AO is the intermediary — it takes findings from the review store and delivers them to the coding agent as a restored session prompt. Same mechanism AO already uses for routing GitHub review comments to agents. Manual triage by default, auto-send opt-in.

**What reviewer agent?** Codex has a native `codex exec review --base main` command with structured JSON output (findings with priority, confidence, code locations). The `code-review-codex` plugin is thin plumbing — Codex does the review, the plugin maps findings into AO's domain model. Claude Code support is architecturally supported and is a natural follow-up.

### The handover loop

```
Worker codes → PR opened → Reviewer auto-spawns → Findings posted
    ↑                                                      ↓
    ← Worker fixes ← Findings routed to worker ← Human triages
                                                       ↓
                              Re-review → Clean → Merge
```

1. **Coding agent opens a PR.** Session transitions to `review_pending`.
2. **AO creates a reviewer workspace.** Lightweight worktree at the worker's branch HEAD. The `CodeReview` plugin runs directly in it — no runtime, no agent, no tmux. All reviewer state lives in `CodeReviewRun` records in the review store.
3. **Plugin reads the diff and posts findings.** Structured findings (file, line, category, severity) written to the review store.
4. **Human triages (or auto-send).** Dismiss, send to coding agent, or chat with reviewer for clarification.
5. **Coding agent fixes.** AO restores the coding agent's session with a prompt containing the routed findings.
6. **Re-review.** AO detects new commits (real SHA via `git rev-parse HEAD`), creates a new reviewer workspace. Prior run marked outdated, old workspace cleaned up, findings preserved.
7. **Clean review → merge.** No open findings. Review strip turns green. Human merges.

## Design decisions

| Decision | Choice |
|----------|--------|
| Plugin slot | New `code-review` slot (9th). Not folded into SCM. |
| Reviewer model | **Lightweight workspaces** — NOT full AO sessions. No runtime, no agent, no tmux. The CodeReview plugin IS the reviewer. |
| Reviewer state | `CodeReviewRun` records in flat-file review store. Stores `reviewerSessionId`, `reviewerWorkspacePath`, `linkedSessionId`. |
| Reviewer IDs | Project-scoped: `{sessionPrefix}-rev-N` — allocated from the review store **project-wide** (`listAllRuns()`, not per-worker `listRunsForSession()`) to prevent collisions across workers in the same project |
| Restart safety | All loop state derived from persisted ReviewStore. No in-memory maps for HEAD tracking or reviewer status. |
| HEAD change detection | Real commit SHAs via `git rev-parse HEAD` (not branch names). |
| Dashboard | Compact review strip on worker cards + dedicated **Review Workbench** (`/reviews` route) |
| Coding kanban | Worker cards only — reviewer workspaces not shown on coding kanban |
| Review Workbench columns | RUNNING, AWAITING CONTEXT, DONE, STALLED, TERMINATED |
| Review loop states | Own outcome model — separate from worker `SessionStatus` |
| Termination reasons | Structured: `cycle_cap`, `worker_dead`, `reviewer_failure`, `manual_cancel`, `config_change` |
| Finding fingerprint | Structural anchors: `sha256(filePath\0category\0severity\0anchorSignature)` truncated to 16 hex |
| Stalled detection | Sliding window union — catches flip-flop loops, not just persistent findings |
| Convergence | Dismissals persist across re-reviews via fingerprint matching |
| Findings storage | AO-local-first (flat files in the review store) |
| SCM publish | Optional, off by default |
| Auto-send to worker | On by default (`autoSendNewFindingsToAgent: true`) — autonomous-by-capability |
| Finding composition | Single `composeAndSendFindings()` bundles AO findings + SCM `getPendingComments()` |
| Dead-worker guard | `isWorkerAlive()` check before sending — parks findings with `worker_dead` if worker is gone |
| Workspace cleanup | Lifecycle cleans up outdated/terminated/done/failed workspaces. Reviewing/awaiting_context keep theirs for follow-up. Follow-up after cleanup fails cleanly (API 410, CLI exit 1) — no silent redirect to the project root. |
| GitHub approval | No automatic "approve" from AI reviewer. Explicit opt-in. |
| Re-review | Serialized — one reviewer workspace per worker at a time. Queue, don't preempt. |
| SCM coexistence | Additive — AO findings + GitHub comments bundled via poll-cycle batching |
| Merge readiness | AO review `done` is advisory — worker reaches `mergeable` only when SCM conditions are met |
| Cost control | Configurable `maxBudgetPerRun`, `maxReviewRounds`, `confidenceThreshold`, `severityThreshold` |
| v1 reference plugin | `code-review-codex` (Codex native `review` command, no `--ephemeral` — session persists for follow-up) |

## v1 scope

**In:**
- `code-review` plugin slot + types + config schema
- Review Workbench (`/reviews` route)
- Review strip on worker cards
- AO-owned review store (flat files)
- Conversational follow-up threads (reviewer stays alive for chat)
- Finding fingerprinting + dismissal persistence + stalled detection
- Structured termination reasons
- Configurable cost cap, confidence threshold, severity threshold, custom review prompt
- Manual review trigger via CLI (`ao review run`) and dashboard
- One reference plugin: `code-review-codex`

**Not in v1:**
- `code-review-command` generic CLI adapter (conflicts with stateful thread model)
- Publishing findings to SCM by default
- Multi-reviewer support (one reviewer per project)
- Review analytics or quality metrics
- Auto-retry on reviewer crash

## Design spec

Full design spec with FAQ, Codex integration details, convergence rules, and outcome model:

**Gist:** https://gist.github.com/illegalcall/9232021963fc9867b474111d9be74254

## Status

- [x] Design spec written and reviewed (multiple rounds)
- [x] Storyboard built (interactive 8-step HTML walkthrough of the handover loop)
- [x] Final spec lockdown
- [x] Implementation plan (5 review rounds, all findings addressed)
- [ ] Implementation

## References

- Original feature request: #139

- **Session list cache** (`core`): `listCached()` on `SessionManager` with 35s TTL, invalidated on `spawn`/`kill`; 6 tests covering cold cache, warm cache, TTL expiry, spawn/kill invalidation, and projectId filtering

title: bug(cli): `ao start` in folder A shows dashboard of AO running on different project B
body:
## Bug

`ao start` uses a **single global state file** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json`) to detect if AO is already running. When AO is started for project A, running `ao start` in a completely different folder/project B detects the running instance of A, shows A's dashboard URL and PID, and offers to "Open dashboard" — which opens A's dashboard, not B's.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1491735678156013588/1494538515617157280
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** `8b7a54ba5acb001030d105dee3b455d2ac1bf303`

## Screenshot

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-start-cross-project/.issue-assets/start-cross-project-bug.png)

_User is on `feat/dedupe-classifier-agent` but `ao start` shows the already-running instance from `codex-startup-factory` project._

## Reproduction

1. `ao start` in folder A (project: `codex-startup-factory`) — AO starts normally
2. `cd` to a different folder B with a different `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (different project)
3. `ao start` in folder B
4. See: "AO is already running" with project A's dashboard URL, PID, and project name
5. Default option "Open dashboard" opens project A's dashboard

## Root Cause

`packages/cli/src/lib/running-state.ts` stores a single `RunningState` in a global file:

```ts
const STATE_FILE = join(homedir(), ".agent-orchestrator", "running.json");
```

The `isAlreadyRunning()` function (line 146) does a simple PID-alive check — no project scoping at all:

```ts
export async function isAlreadyRunning(): Promise<RunningState | null> {
  return getRunning();  // checks global file, no project awareness
}
```

When the start command (line 1336) detects a running instance, it shows the existing instance's info regardless of which project the user is currently in. The default prompt option "Open dashboard" opens the *other* project's dashboard.

## Fix

Two possible approaches:

**Option A (simple — scope the check):** In `start.ts`, after detecting a running instance, check if the current project matches any of the running instance's projects. If it matches, show the already-running prompt as-is. If it doesn't match, either:
- Skip the already-running check and start a new instance
- Show a *different* message: "AO is already running for project X, but you're in project Y. Start new orchestrator for this project?"

**Option B (broader — multi-instance support):** Allow multiple AO instances per project, keyed by project ID in the state file. This is more work and relates to #1128 (multi-base-branch orchestrators RFC).

Recommended: **Option A** for now — it's a small, targeted fix.

## Impact

- **Confusing UX**: Users think AO is already serving their project when it's actually a different one
- **Misleading default action**: "Open dashboard" takes them to the wrong project's dashboard
- **Affects multi-project workflows**: Anyone using AO with multiple repos/projects on the same machine

title: Bug: Live Terminal viewport snaps to bottom on drag-start, making text selection/copy impossible
body:
## Summary

In the web dashboard's Live Terminal (xterm.js), starting a drag-to-select
above the viewport bottom causes an immediate snap to the bottom, making
it impossible to select and copy previous output.

This is **not** the same as the xterm.js "rocket scroll" issue
([github/copilot-cli#1805](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/1805)) —
it fires on drag-start, not on wheel-event momentum.

## Environment

- `ao` launcher: `0.1.0`
- `@composio/ao-cli`: `0.2.2` (latest on v0.2.0 release line, published 2026-03-29)
- `@composio/ao-web`: `0.2.2`
- OS: macOS 26.4.1
- Node.js: v24.14.1
- Install method: `pnpm add -g @composio/ao`
- Browser: Chrome (also reproducible in Safari)
- Agent: `claude-code`

## Steps to reproduce

1. `ao start`, open dashboard at `http://localhost:3000`
2. Open orchestrator or any worker session → Live Terminal
3. Wait for streaming to settle (output is static)
4. Scroll up so previous output is visible
5. Mouse-down + drag to start selecting text above the bottom
6. Viewport immediately snaps to the bottom on drag-start
7. Selection is gone before Cmd+C can be pressed

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** Drag-to-select preserves scroll position and selection; Cmd+C copies the selection.
- **Actual:** Drag-start forces viewport to bottom; selection disappears; Cmd+C captures nothing useful.

## Note

`ao doctor` is currently broken (`scripts/ao-doctor.sh` missing from npm tarball),
so no `ao doctor` output is attached.

title: Dashboard worker page shows stale branch after agent changes branches
body:
## Problem

The branch displayed on the worker session detail page does not update when the worker agent changes its branch (e.g., during a rebase, branch rename, or switching to a fix branch). The dashboard continues showing the original branch that was set at spawn time.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Spawn a worker session (e.g., on branch `fix-login`)
2. Worker agent changes its branch (e.g., to `fix-login-v2` or rebases onto a new branch)
3. Check the worker session detail page on the dashboard
4. Branch still shows the original branch name

## Expected Behavior
- The branch field on the worker detail page should reflect the current actual branch the agent is working on
- Should update on the next lifecycle poll cycle when the branch change is detected

## Actual Behavior
- Branch is frozen to whatever was set at spawn time and never updates

## Impact

title: fix(web): cap terminal reconnects, guard SSE enqueue, custom 4004 code
body:
Fixes #964.

## Summary
- **Cap MuxProvider reconnects** at 8 attempts (exponential backoff retained). Once exhausted the provider transitions to a permanent `disconnected` state instead of spamming WebSocket connects forever after a session exits.
- **Guard SSE enqueue** in `/api/events` with a `closed` flag set in `cancel()` (and on any enqueue failure). Heartbeat, poller, and initial snapshot paths now short-circuit cleanly after the client disconnects instead of throwing unhandled `controller.enqueue()` errors.
- **Custom close code `4004` for "session not found"** — added `TERMINAL_CLOSE_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` in `mux-protocol.ts` and mirrored it in the server (tsconfig rootDir prevents shared import). The server now tags the terminal error message with `code: 4004` so the client can distinguish it from a generic policy violation (1008). On receipt, MuxProvider drops the terminal from its re-open set and pushes a visible notice line to subscribers.
- The exited-session placeholder in `SessionDetail` already covers the "session ended" UI path via `TERMINAL_STATUSES` — no change needed there.

title: feat(core): trigger rules — spawn investigator sessions from SCM events via configurable rules
body:
## Summary

Add a triggers section to agent-orchestrator.yaml. When a PR's CI fails and no session is currently handling it, AO spawns an investigator session that reads the CI log, classifies the failure (code bug vs infra noise), comments on the PR with findings, and optionally pushes a fix to the same PR branch without any human running ao spawn.

## The gap

The route at packages/web/src/app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts already handles signature verification, event parsing, and project matching. After findAffectedSessions() runs, if no session is found the event is discarded:

```
const affectedSessions = findAffectedSessions(sessions, candidate.projectId, event);
if (affectedSessions.length === 0) {
  continue;
}
```


When a PR's CI fails today nothing happens unless a human notices and manually runs ao spawn. The contributor is left waiting with no triage, no diagnosis, no suggested fix.

## How it works

```
PR CI fails (workflow_run.completed)
          |
Existing webhook route receives event
verifyWebhook() + parseWebhook()
          |
findAffectedSessions() returns empty
          |
findMatchingTriggers() (new)
          |
flaky guard: re-run CI first
     |              |
  passes          fails again
  (flaky)              |
  ignore         step classification
                 (infra vs code)
                       |
               spawn investigator session
                       |
               agent reads CI log
               classifies failure
               locates relevant files
                       |
               comments on PR with findings
                       |
          on_confident_fix: comment_only (default)
          on_confident_fix: push_fix (opt-in, same PR branch)
```

The trigger rule engine is generic enough to extend to other use cases under the same pattern: merge conflict auto-resolution, new issue triage, Dependabot alert fixes, and stale PR rebases all share the same config shape, flaky guard, and investigator session role.

title: fix(web): refresh orchestrator links from SSE to prevent stale dashboard navigation
body:
Fixes #1103

## Problem

The "Orchestrator" button on the Dashboard linked to killed/stale orchestrator sessions. After an orchestrator was killed and potentially re-spawned with a new ID, clicking the button would navigate to the dead session.

Reported by @Atul Pandey in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1491735678156013588/1494703600293908731).

## Root Cause

`activeOrchestrators` state in `Dashboard.tsx` was frozen at SSR time and only grew via `mergeOrchestrators()` (which adds/replaces by `projectId` but never prunes dead entries). The SSE/refresh cycle in `useSessionEvents` called `/api/sessions` — which **does** include fresh `orchestrators` data in its response — but `useSessionEvents` only extracted `sessions`, discarding the orchestrator data.

## Fix

1. **`useSessionEvents.ts`** — Extract `orchestrators` from `/api/sessions` refresh responses and include them in the reducer state alongside sessions.

2. **`Dashboard.tsx`** — Consume `refreshedOrchestrators` from `useSessionEvents` and use it to update `activeOrchestrators`, so killed orchestrator IDs get replaced with current ones on every SSE refresh cycle (~15s max stale window).

## Test Plan

- [ ] Start an orchestrator session
- [ ] Verify "Orchestrator" button links to the active session
- [ ] Kill the orchestrator
- [ ] Verify the "Orchestrator" button updates (within ~15s) to reflect the killed session being gone, or links to a new orchestrator if one is spawned
- [ ] Verify no regressions on single-project and multi-project dashboard views

title: Add hot-reload / fast-test workflow for agent worktrees
body:
There is no inbuild thing for quickly testing(like hot-reload) the changes made by an agent spawn by `ao` as all agents make a different workflow

## Problem

When you `ao spawn` an issue, AO creates an isolated git worktree (via the `workspace-worktree` plugin) on a new branch. To test what the agent built, you currently have to:

1. Navigate to the worktree directory (e.g. `~/.worktrees/<session-id>`)
2. Install dependencies from scratch (`pnpm install`)
3. Build from scratch (`pnpm build`)
4. Then manually start the dev server or run tests

This is slow and painful — especially when you are iterating on an agent's output and just want to quickly verify it works.

## Current State

AO already has some building blocks:

- **`Workspace.postCreate()` hook** — runs commands after worktree creation (defined per-project in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` via `postCreate` array). Currently used for setup tasks.
- **`project.symlinks` config** — symlinks shared resources from the main repo into the worktree (e.g. `node_modules`). Already implemented in `workspace-worktree` plugin.
- **`pnpm --filter`** — can build only changed packages in the monorepo.

But none of this gives developers a fast path from "agent finished coding" to "I can test it."

## Proposed Solution

Add a **hot-reload / fast-test** mode so developers can quickly test agent worktree changes without full reinstall/rebuild.

### Option A: Leverage existing symlinks config
- Document and encourage using `symlinks: ["node_modules"]` in project config so worktrees share dependencies with the main repo.
- Add incremental build support — only rebuild changed packages via `pnpm --filter`.

### Option B: One-command test shortcut (`ao test <session>`)
- Add an `ao test <session>` CLI command that:
  - Detects the worktree path from session metadata
  - Runs incremental build (only changed packages)
  - Executes relevant tests automatically
  - Reports results back in the terminal

### Option C: Dev server with worktree source swap
- Run `pnpm dev` from the main repo but hot-swap the source from the agent's worktree — similar to Next.js fast refresh, but across worktrees.

## Why This Matters

Speeds up the feedback loop dramatically when reviewing agent output. The current cycle is:

> spawn → wait → cd to worktree → install → build → test → review

It should be closer to:

> spawn → wait → `ao test` → review

The faster developers can go from "agent done" to "I can see it works," the more useful AO becomes as a daily dev tool.

## Notes

- Primarily affects monorepo setups (pnpm workspaces) where each worktree is a full copy.
- The `symlinks` + `postCreate` infrastructure already exists — this is about building a streamlined workflow on top of it.

title: Redo session lifecycle reporting and UI flow
body:
## Summary

Ground-up redesign of the session lifecycle state machine. Replaces the single-axis `SessionStatus` ladder (a chain of `if`/`return` checks in `determineStatus()`) with a **three-axis canonical lifecycle model** — `session`, `pr`, `runtime` — each with explicit `state`, `reason`, and timestamps, persisted as a versioned JSON payload in session metadata.

~+10,000 / −1000 across 100 files, 80 commits.

## Architecture — 5-Stage Rollout

**Stage 1: Canonical Lifecycle Model** (`lifecycle-state.ts`, `types.ts`)
- Three-axis truth: `session` / `pr` / `runtime`, each with `state` + `reason` + timestamps
- Persisted as versioned `statePayload` JSON (`version: 2`) in metadata
- `synthesizeCanonicalLifecycle()` rehydrates pre-upgrade sessions from legacy metadata
- `deriveLegacyStatus()` maps the new lifecycle back to `SessionStatus` for dashboard/events/reactions

**Stage 2: Evidence-Based Recovery** (`lifecycle-status-decisions.ts`)
- New `detecting` state for ambiguous signals (replaces silent `working` defaulting)
- Evidence hashing — counter only resets when evidence actually changes
- Attempt counting (max 3) + time-based escalation (5-minute hard cap)
- Process-probe failures no longer silently treated as alive

**Stage 3: Agent Reports** (`agent-report.ts`, `cli/commands/report.ts`)
- New CLI surfaces: `ao acknowledge` + `ao report <state>`
- Agent-declared states: `started`, `working`, `waiting`, `needs-input`, `fixing-ci`, `addressing-reviews`, `completed`
- Agents **cannot** self-declare terminal states (`done`, `terminated`, `merged`) — AO owns those via SCM/runtime ground truth
- Freshness window (5 min) prevents stale reports from overriding current truth
- Audit trail with before/after snapshots (`AgentReportAuditEntry`)

**Stage 4: Report Watcher** (`report-watcher.ts`)
- Background triggers: `no_acknowledge` (10 min), `stale` (30 min), `blocked`
- Fires reactions on detected conditions

**Stage 5: UI / API Rollout**
- Lifecycle truth panels, activity signals, audit trail panels in web dashboard
- New `ActivitySignal` type replacing raw `ActivityState | null` — carries `state` / `source` / `timestamp` / `detail` for signal confidence
- Freshness classification: strong (<60s), weak (<5min), stale (>5min)

## New Public Surfaces

- **Types:** `CanonicalSessionLifecycle`, `SessionLifecycleAxis`, `PRLifecycleAxis`, `RuntimeLifecycleAxis`, `ActivitySignal`, `AgentReportAuditEntry`, `DetermineStatusAssessment`
- **CLI:** `ao acknowledge`, `ao report <state> [--note]`
- **Core exports:** `synthesizeCanonicalLifecycle`, `deriveLegacyStatus`, `parseCanonicalLifecycle`, `normalizePayloadLifecycle`, `applyAgentReport`, `auditAgentReports`
- **Env var:** `AO_OBSERVABILITY_STDERR` (gates stderr mirroring — was unconditional)

## Breaking / Behavioral Changes

- `ProjectConfig.repo` is now optional (some flows can derive it)
- `Session` gains `lifecycle?: CanonicalSessionLifecycle` + `activitySignal?: ActivitySignal`
- Font library removed from `packages/web/src/app/layout.tsx` (`next/font/google` dropped)
- `runtime.isAlive` failures now surface as `probe_failed` instead of silently treated as alive
- Metadata dual-write: individual keys (`status`, `pr`, `runtimeHandle`, …) **plus** `statePayload` JSON blob

## Backward Compatibility

- `synthesizeCanonicalLifecycle()` rebuilds the 3-axis model for any session created before this PR
- `normalizePayloadLifecycle()` merges persisted `statePayload` with synthesized fallback — no data loss on upgrade
- `deriveLegacyStatus()` keeps existing dashboard/SSE/reaction consumers working without change
- `version: 2` tag on the payload provides a forward migration path

## Test Coverage

~2,000 new/modified test lines:
- `lifecycle-state.test.ts` (parsing + synthesis)
- `lifecycle-status-decisions.test.ts` (decision logic + evidence hashing)
- `lifecycle-transition.test.ts` (transition module)
- `lifecycle-manager.test.ts` (+628 lines — polling loop)
- `agent-report.test.ts` (report parsing, validation, application)
- `report-watcher.test.ts` (all 3 trigger types)
- `observability.test.ts` (+59 lines)

## Architecture Overview
- https://theharshitsingh.com/static/trinity

## Tester

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator.git && cd agent-orchestrator
git checkout sessions-redone
pnpm install && pnpm build
pnpm test
# Smoke: spawn a session, verify dashboard shows lifecycle truth panel
# Upgrade: open a session created before this branch, verify it rehydrates via synthesizeCanonicalLifecycle
# Agent report: ao report working --note "investigating"; verify audit entry appears
# Evidence recovery: kill agent mid-work, verify detecting → stuck transition after timeout
```

title: feat (core): inject worker prompt as instructions file
body:
## Summary

This PR updates worker prompt handling so sessions can pass persistent system instructions separately from task-specific input, and adds OpenCode-specific support for materializing worker and orchestrator system prompts into each session worktree's `AGENTS.md`.

## What Changed

- Split `buildPrompt()` in `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` to return:
  - `systemPrompt`: persistent AO guidance, project context, issue context, and project rules
  - `taskPrompt`: only the explicit user-provided prompt
- Updated worker spawn flow in `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` to:
  - write `systemPrompt` to `worker-prompt-<sessionId>.md`
  - pass `taskPrompt` separately to the agent launch config
  - skip post-launch prompt delivery when no task prompt exists
  - clean up prompt files alongside workspace/metadata on failure
- Added OpenCode worker support by writing the worker system prompt into the worker worktree's `AGENTS.md`
- Updated OpenCode `AGENTS.md` generation in `packages/core/src/opencode-agents-md.ts` to:
  - accept a role parameter (`worker` or `orchestrator`)
  - render a role-specific heading (`## Agent Worker` / `## Agent Orchestrator`)
  - use the current AO system prompt markers
- Fixed restore behavior in `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` so OpenCode restore re-materializes `AGENTS.md` for both:
  - orchestrator sessions via `orchestrator-prompt-<sessionId>.md`
  - worker sessions via `worker-prompt-<sessionId>.md`

## Why

- Codex-style worker sessions need a clean split between persistent instructions and the immediate task prompt.
- OpenCode does not consume `systemPromptFile` directly, so its session-scoped system prompt needs to be materialized into `AGENTS.md` inside the session worktree.
- Worker and orchestrator OpenCode sessions need different `AGENTS.md` headings and restore behavior, even though both use the same helper.

- Added restore coverage for OpenCode worker `AGENTS.md` re-materialization
- Updated OpenCode `AGENTS.md` helper tests for the role-aware output

title: bug: opencode worker ignores --prompt when spawned via 'ao spawn --prompt'
body:
## Bug

When using `ao spawn --prompt "xyz"` (from CLI or from orchestrator), the opencode worker agent starts but does not receive the initial prompt. The agent sits idle with no task instructions.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1484917231245856808/1491735678156013588/1494988286706581636
**Reported by:** @gautam
**Analyzed against:** `2859aa6a`

## Reproduction

1. Start AO with opencode as the agent
2. Run: `ao spawn --prompt "Fix the authentication bug in the login module"`
3. Observe: opencode starts but receives no initial prompt — agent is idle

## Root Cause

The worker `spawn()` path in `session-manager.ts` (line ~1083-1097) does **not** write a `systemPromptFile`. This is different from `spawnOrchestrator()` (line ~1371-1385) which writes long prompts to a file.

### What happens step-by-step:

1. `buildPrompt()` composes a layered prompt (BASE_AGENT_PROMPT ~800 chars + project context + user rules + user's `--prompt` text). Easily 1000-5000+ characters.

2. This full composed prompt is set as `agentLaunchConfig.prompt` (line 1093).

3. The opencode plugin's `getLaunchCommand()` (line 242-280) generates a **two-phase compound shell command**:
   ```bash
   SES_ID=$(opencode run --format json --title 'AO:session-id' --command true | node /tmp/capture.js); 
   if [ -z "$SES_ID" ]; then SES_ID=$(opencode session list --format json | node /tmp/lookup.js 'AO:session-id'); fi; 
   [ -n "$SES_ID" ] && exec opencode --session "$SES_ID" --prompt '<FULL_COMPOSED_PROMPT>'; echo 'error' >&2; exit 1
   ```

4. The full composed prompt (with newlines from BASE_AGENT_PROMPT etc.) is inlined as a single-quoted `--prompt` argument.

5. **If `$SES_ID` is empty** (e.g., `opencode run --command true` doesn't emit a parseable session ID, or the JSON capture fails), the `&&` guard causes the `exec opencode` phase to be **silently skipped**. The tmux session exists but no opencode process runs.

6. **No error is detected** because:
   - The opencode plugin does NOT set `promptDelivery` (defaults to `undefined`, not `"post-launch"`)
   - Session-manager line 1256-1258 unconditionally sets `promptDelivered = "true"` when the agent has a prompt in its config
   - The tmux runtime only verifies the command was *typed*, not that it succeeded

### Key gaps:

| Gap | File | Line(s) |
|-----|------|---------|
| Worker spawn doesn't use `systemPromptFile` for long prompts | `session-manager.ts` | 1083-1097 |
| Opencode plugin doesn't set `promptDelivery` | `agent-opencode/src/index.ts` | — |
| Two-phase launch silently fails when `$SES_ID` is empty | `agent-opencode/src/index.ts` | 276-280 |
| `promptDelivered` set to `"true"` without validation | `session-manager.ts` | 1256-1258 |

## Fix

**Option A (recommended): Write prompt to file for worker spawns too.**
Mirror the `spawnOrchestrator()` pattern in the worker `spawn()` path — when the composed prompt is long (>500 chars), write it to a file and set `systemPromptFile` on the `agentLaunchConfig`. The opencode plugin already handles `systemPromptFile` correctly (line 244-252).

**Option B: Add `promptDelivery: "post-launch"` to opencode plugin.**
This would trigger the session-manager's retry-based post-launch prompt delivery (line 1222-1258). However, this changes the delivery mechanism for ALL opencode spawns.

**Option C: Add error detection for two-phase launch.**
After runtime creation, verify the opencode session was discovered and the prompt was delivered.

## Impact

- **Severity:** High — `--prompt` is the primary mechanism for freeform task spawning. Without it, orchestrator-driven workflows (the core value prop) don't work with opencode.
- **Workaround:** Use `ao send <session-id> "<prompt>"` manually after spawning.
- **Related:** #852 (agents spawning but not doing anything — may be the same underlying issue)

title: fix(core): write long worker prompts to file to prevent truncation
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1304

When `ao spawn --prompt "xyz"` is used, `buildPrompt()` composes a layered prompt (BASE_AGENT_PROMPT + project context + rules + user prompt) that easily exceeds 500 chars. The full string was being inlined into a compound shell command and sent via tmux paste-buffer, where it could silently fail if session ID discovery failed.

**Fix:** Mirrors `spawnOrchestrator()`'s `systemPromptFile` pattern — long prompts (>500 chars) are written to a file, and the agent launch config uses `systemPromptFile` instead of the inline prompt. The opencode plugin already handles `systemPromptFile` correctly via `$(cat ...)` substitution.

Falls back to inline prompt on write failure (non-fatal).

1. `ao spawn --prompt "Fix the authentication bug"` — verify agent receives prompt
2. `ao spawn --prompt "short"` (under 500 chars) — verify inline prompt still works
3. Spawn from orchestrator — verify worker picks up the prompt

title: ao start intermittently kills existing orchestrator and spawns a new one
body:
## Bug
`ao start` intermittently kills the existing orchestrator agent session and starts a new orchestrator instead of reusing the current one / ensuring there is only one stable orchestrator.

## What I observed
On April 18, 2026, running `ao status` in my local setup showed multiple orchestrator sessions for the same project at the same time:

- `aa-orchestrator-1`
- `aa-orchestrator-2`
- `aa-orchestrator-3`

This matches the behavior I’ve been seeing where `ao start` will sometimes replace the active orchestrator by spawning a fresh one, leaving multiple orchestrators around or killing the previously active one unexpectedly.

## Expected behavior
`ao start` should be idempotent with respect to the orchestrator:

- if an orchestrator is already running for the project, it should reuse it (or at least leave it alone), and
- it should not randomly terminate the active orchestrator and create a new one.

## Actual behavior
Intermittently, `ao start` appears to:

- kill the current orchestrator agent, and/or
- spawn a new orchestrator session unexpectedly.

## Reproduction
I don’t have a deterministic repro yet. So far this appears intermittent / timing-dependent.

High-level pattern:
1. Start the project with `ao start`
2. Later run `ao start` again (or restart parts of the setup)
3. Occasionally the original orchestrator gets replaced and a new orchestrator session is created
4. `ao status` then shows multiple orchestrators or an unexpected new orchestrator instance

## Environment
- Repo: `ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator`
- Command: `ao start`
- Local orchestrator/session naming looked like `aa-orchestrator-*`

## Notes
This is disruptive because the orchestrator is supposed to be the stable coordinator process. Replacing it unexpectedly makes it harder to reason about ownership, monitoring, and session continuity.

title: fix: restore dead orchestrators on ao start
body:
## Summary
- restore the most recently active dead-but-restorable orchestrator on `ao start` instead of silently spawning a new one when tmux is gone
- harden startup-lock handling so stale locks are cleaned up promptly, `EPERM` owners are treated as alive, failed lockfile writes do not leak fds, and startup-lock acquisition failures go through the normal CLI error path
- fix worker session orchestrator navigation to prefer the most recently active live orchestrator for the project instead of defaulting to the first sorted orchestrator id
- fix Codex worker restore commands to resume with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` instead of `never`
- replace manual package changelog edits with a single repo-standard changeset

## Why
The main issue in #1306 is the long-gap restart path: when the original tmux-backed orchestrator is gone hours later, `ao start` was treating that orchestrator as terminal and creating a fresh one instead of resuming it.

While fixing that path, two related follow-ups also surfaced on this branch:
- the worker session page could link to the wrong orchestrator when multiple orchestrators existed for a project because it effectively fell back to the first sorted id
- Codex restore commands for worker sessions could resume in `---dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, which is too permissive for restored worker sessions

## Implementation
### `ao start` restore behavior
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` now prefers `sm.restore(...)` for the newest restorable dead orchestrator after checking for live orchestrators
- it only falls back to `spawnOrchestrator()` when there is nothing live or restorable

### startup lock hardening
- `packages/cli/src/lib/running-state.ts` now:
  - checks lock owners during the retry loop instead of waiting for the full timeout
  - treats `EPERM` as alive when probing a PID
  - closes the lockfile fd in a `finally`
  - unlinks a partially-created lockfile if the metadata write fails
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` now acquires the startup lock inside the main `try` path so lock-acquisition failures get standard CLI error handling

### worker session orchestrator button
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` now returns a preferred project-scoped `orchestratorId` for worker session pages by selecting the most recently active live orchestrator, instead of leaving the client to fall back to the first sorted orchestrator id

### Codex restore approval mode
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` now uses restore-specific approval flag handling
- worker restores no longer resume with `--ask-for-approval never`
- worker restores use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ` for permission less mode. 
- permissionless orchestrator restores still use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`

### release metadata
- replaced package-level unreleased changelog edits with `.changeset/fix-start-restore-and-codex-resume.md`

## Evidence
- CLI regression coverage verifies `ao start --no-dashboard` restores the most recently active dead orchestrator instead of spawning a new one
- CLI startup-lock tests cover lock release ordering and lock-acquisition failure handling
- web API coverage verifies project-scoped worker navigation selects the most recently active live orchestrator when multiple orchestrators exist
- Codex plugin tests verify restore commands now use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for worker restores and keep explicit bypass for permissionless orchestrator restores

## Validation
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli exec vitest run __tests__/commands/start.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web exec vitest run src/__tests__/api-routes.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web exec vitest run 'src/app/sessions/[id]/page.test.tsx'`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex exec vitest run src/index.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex exec tsc --noEmit`

Closes #1306.

title: feat(core): auto-terminate sessions on PR merge (#1309)
body:
## Summary

Closes [#1309](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1309) (part of [#536](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/536)). When a session's PR was detected as merged, AO marked the status `merged` but left the tmux runtime alive, the worktree on disk, and the metadata in the active `sessions/` directory. Users were running an external watchdog to archive zombies. This closes the loop inside AO.

- On the `merged` transition (last step of `checkSession`, after reactions fire), invoke `sessionManager.kill()` with `reason: "pr_merged"` to destroy the runtime, remove the worktree, and archive the metadata.
- Guarded by an idleness gate (`session.activity in {idle, ready, exited}` OR grace window elapsed) so we never kill an agent mid-task. Deferred cleanups set `mergedPendingCleanupSince` in metadata and retry each poll.
- Config opt-in under `lifecycle.autoCleanupOnMerge` (default `true`) with `mergeCleanupIdleGraceMs` (default 5 min) — operators can preserve merged worktrees for inspection if they want.

## Why

The cleanup logic in `kill()` already existed and worked correctly — the gap was that nothing called it on the `merged` transition. Adding the call is the minimal fix; the rest of the changes are there to make it safe:

- `kill()` is now idempotent (short-circuits on already-archived/terminated sessions) and takes a `reason` option so auto-terminations don't record misleading `"manually_killed"` lifecycle reasons.
- Scope is deliberately narrow to `"merged"`. `done`/`errored` often need the worktree preserved for debugging, and `killed` is produced by `kill()` itself so auto-triggering it would self-recurse. See commit message for the full rationale.
- Reactions-before-cleanup ordering is preserved so `merge.completed` events and `merge.ready` auto-merge reactions observe a live session before it is destroyed.

## Codex review

Plan was reviewed by Codex before implementation. Verdict: conditional pass. Their concerns (scope narrowing, reactions ordering, idleness gate, real idempotency, config opt-in, more test coverage) are all reflected in the implementation and commit message.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (full workspace) — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 788 passed (+6 new)
- [x] 6 new unit tests in `lifecycle-manager.test.ts` under `auto-cleanup on merge (#1309)`:
  - [x] kills session with `reason=pr_merged` when PR merges and agent is idle
  - [x] defers cleanup when agent is still active and records `mergedPendingCleanupSince`
  - [x] forces cleanup after grace window elapses even if agent is still active
  - [x] does not trigger cleanup when `autoCleanupOnMerge` is disabled
  - [x] does not trigger cleanup for terminated/killed sessions (no self-recursion)
  - [x] retains `merged` status when `kill()` fails so the next poll retries
- [ ] Manual end-to-end: spawn a session, merge its PR, verify `ao status` no longer shows it within one poll cycle after agent idles

## Notes for reviewers

- The `SessionManager.kill` return type changed from `Promise<void>` to `Promise<KillResult>`. All existing callers (CLI, tests) ignored the old return value so this is effectively additive. One test (`lifecycle.test.ts:163`) was updated to match.
- Two new enum variants added to `CanonicalSessionReason` (`pr_merged`, `auto_cleanup`) and `CanonicalRuntimeReason` (`pr_merged_cleanup`, `auto_cleanup`) — additive union widening only.
- No changes to notifier plugins, webhook handlers, or the dashboard. The existing `merge.completed` event is sufficient; cleanup is silent.

title: Draft PRs can be misreported as merge conflicts
body:
## Summary
When a PR is in Draft mode on GitHub, AO can incorrectly trigger the merge-conflicts path and show/send messages like "Your branch has merge conflicts. Rebase on the default branch and resolve them."

## Observed behavior
A draft PR on GitHub caused AO to surface the merge-conflicts message even though the PR was not actually conflicting.

## Expected behavior
Draft PRs should be identified as draft/blocked/review-not-ready, not as merge conflicts, unless GitHub explicitly reports real merge conflicts.

## Repro
1. Open a PR on GitHub.
2. Convert the PR to Draft.
3. Let AO poll/update PR state.
4. Observe that the merge-conflicts message/reaction can be triggered.

## Likely cause
There appears to be a misclassification between GitHub draft/blocking states and AO's merge-conflict handling.

Relevant code paths:
- `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts`
- `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts`
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`

Notes from local inspection:
- GitHub draft PRs can surface `mergeStateStatus = BLOCKED`.
- AO has separate blocker labels for draft / branch protection / conflicts, but the conflict reaction path is still being triggered in this scenario.
- The issue may be in how cached/batched mergeability data is interpreted when draft PRs are polled, rather than in the UI labels alone.

## Suggested fix direction
- Add a regression test for a draft PR where `mergeStateStatus = BLOCKED` but there are no actual merge conflicts.
- Ensure draft/blocked states do not set or propagate `hasConflicts` unless GitHub reports `mergeable = CONFLICTING` (or equivalent explicit conflict signal).
- Verify lifecycle conflict reactions only fire for true conflict states, not generic blocked/draft states.

title: fix(workspace-worktree): resolve symlink source to absolute path
body:
## Summary

`postCreate` in `packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts` builds `sourcePath` with `join(repoPath, symlinkPath)`. When `project.path` is a relative path like `"."`, `repoPath` stays `"."` and `join(".", "node_modules")` returns `"node_modules"` — a relative string. `symlinkSync("node_modules", "/path/to/worktree/node_modules")` then creates a self-referential link:

```
<worktree>/node_modules -> node_modules
```

Symlinks are resolved relative to the **symlink's own directory**, so the link loops back to itself. The next `pnpm install` fails with:

```
ELOOP: too many symbolic links encountered, open '<worktree>/node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json'
```

`ao spawn` only surfaces the top-level `✖ Failed to create or initialize session` / `✗ Command failed: sh -c …` message, so the real ELOOP is swallowed — took a while to find it.

## Fix

Use `resolve(repoPath, symlinkPath)` instead of `join(…)`. `resolve()` anchors a relative `repoPath` against `process.cwd()` and leaves absolute / `~`-prefixed paths unchanged, so existing configs are unaffected.

```diff
- const sourcePath = join(repoPath, symlinkPath);
+ const sourcePath = resolve(repoPath, symlinkPath);
  const targetPath = resolve(info.path, symlinkPath);
```

The adjacent `targetPath` line already uses `resolve()` for the same reason — this just makes the two consistent.

## Repro

```yaml
# agent-orchestrator.yaml
projects:
  myproject:
    path: .
    symlinks: [node_modules]
```

Run `ao spawn` — every spawn fails until `symlinks:` is removed or the `path:` is made absolute.

## Tests

Added `produces an absolute symlink source when project.path is relative` in `workspace.postCreate()`. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix.

- 47/47 tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree test`)
- `pnpm typecheck` clean
- `pnpm lint` on changed files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `prettier --check` clean

Patch-level changeset included.

## Verified in production

Applied the equivalent patch to an installed 0.2.5 instance that had been blocked by this bug for ~2 days. `ao spawn` immediately started producing real sessions that progress through the full lifecycle and open PRs. Reverted once upstream publishes with the fix.

title: fix(web): surface dashboard SSR load failures

## Summary

When `getDashboardPageData` failed (typically `getServices()` or `sessionManager.list()`), the home page still rendered the normal empty dashboard: zero sessions and the default "Ready to orchestrate" empty state. That made config and startup issues look like there was simply no work in flight.

This change captures the thrown error during SSR, passes it to the dashboard as `dashboardLoadError`, and shows an alert banner with the message plus a short pointer to `agent-orchestrator.yaml` and `ao doctor`. Realtime updates (`useSessionEvents`) are disabled in that situation so the client does not keep reconnecting against a broken backend.

title: fix(cli): probe ::1 in isPortAvailable to match its own documented contract
body:
### What changed and why                                                          
                      
`isPortAvailable` had a comment claiming it worked "regardless of whether the occupying process is bound to
`127.0.0.1, ::1, 0.0.0.0, or ::"` 
but the implementation only probed 127.0.0.1. 

  The fix adds a local probe arrow and checks both 127.0.0.1 and ::1 via Promise.all.
   A port is only considered free when both return clear making the implementation
  match what the comment always claimed.                                             
                  
###   How to test

  1. Start any process on port 3000 bound to IPv6 (e.g. node -e                      
  "require('net').createServer().listen(3000, '::1')")
  2. Run ao start — should print Port 3000 is busy — using 3001 instead. and start   
  successfully                                                                       
  3. Run ao start with port 3000 free — behaviour unchanged

title: RFC: Remove polling and move to reactive sync for sessions, file-trees and file content
body:
## Summary

Move the dashboard away from periodic polling (5s SSE interval) to a reactive, push-based sync model for:

1. **Session state** — status, branches, PRs, CI results
2. **File trees** — workspace directory structures
3. **File content** — individual file reads/edits

## Context

Currently the web dashboard polls core every ~5 seconds via SSE, which means:
- Stale data between intervals
- Unnecessary load when nothing changes
- Latency in reflecting agent actions (CI results, review comments, etc.)

A reactive model would push updates only when state actually changes, giving instant feedback and reducing overhead.

## Discussion Points

- (From thread discussion — Dhruv has comments/quesions to address here)
- What transport? (WebSocket events, SSE with selective push, etc.)
- Which state changes should trigger pushes?
- How to handle reconnection / missed events?
- Impact on existing lifecycle-manager polling loop

## Open Questions

- Scope: full reactive rewrite or incremental (sessions first, then files)?
- Backward compat for CLI-only users?
- Performance benchmarks: current polling vs proposed reactive?

---

title: In-memory lifecycle.session.kind leaks orchestrator role for foreign-prefix legacy records
body:
## Summary

Follow-up from PR #1075 (issue #1048). That PR closed the **on-disk** path where foreign-prefix legacy records like \`{projectId}-orchestrator\` (where projectId ≠ sessionPrefix) would get \`role: \"orchestrator\"\` backfilled by the SM repair-on-read path. But there's a parallel **in-memory** path that still misclassifies these records as orchestrators on every \`sm.list()\`.

## Repro

Given a project with \`sessionPrefix: app\` and a leftover on-disk record \`~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-my-app/sessions/my-app-orchestrator\` (no \`role\` metadata — pre-numbered AO version, wrong-prefix bare name):

1. Call \`sm.list(\"my-app\")\`.
2. For each record, \`session-manager.ts\` → \`metadataToSession\` → \`sessionFromMetadata\` (\`packages/core/src/utils/session-from-metadata.ts:46\`) calls \`parseCanonicalLifecycle(meta, { sessionId, ... })\` **without** \`sessionKind\`.
3. \`synthesizeCanonicalLifecycle\` (\`packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts:253\`) falls back to the generic \`sessionId.endsWith(\"-orchestrator\")\` heuristic → returns \`kind: \"orchestrator\"\`.
4. The returned \`Session.lifecycle.session.kind\` is \`\"orchestrator\"\` in memory, even though the on-disk \`role\` field is correctly left undefined by PR #1075's repair gate.

## Blast radius

Four consumers read \`lifecycle.session.kind\` directly and would treat the record as an orchestrator:

- \`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:835\` — uses \`kind !== \"orchestrator\"\` to gate processing.
- \`packages/core/src/report-watcher.ts:90\` — skips orchestrators in report auditing.
- \`packages/core/src/agent-report.ts:214\` — skips orchestrators.
- \`packages/core/src/lifecycle-transition.ts:155\` — **stamps \`role: \"orchestrator\"\` based on \`kind\`**. If any code path feeds a Session-with-wrong-kind through this transition builder and writes the resulting patch back, \`role\` gets persisted to disk anyway — defeating PR #1075's repair gate.

I have not yet found a real call chain that reaches \`lifecycle-transition.ts:155\` for a foreign-prefix record during normal operation, but the escape hatch exists.

## Other unprotected \`parseCanonicalLifecycle\` call sites

- \`packages/core/src/utils/session-from-metadata.ts:46\` (hot path, described above)
- \`packages/core/src/metadata.ts:226, 250\` (read-only lifecycle lookups)
- \`packages/core/src/agent-report.ts:433, 521\` (agent report transitions)

PR #1075 only threaded \`sessionKind\` through one call site (\`session-manager.ts:585\`, the repair loop).

## Suggested fix

Pick one of:

1. **Thread \`sessionKind\` (or \`sessionPrefix\` + internal lookup) through \`SessionFromMetadataOptions\`** and the other \`parseCanonicalLifecycle\` callers. Mechanical, but needs a bit of plumbing since \`session-from-metadata.ts\` doesn't currently know the project.
2. **Drop the \`endsWith(\"-orchestrator\")\` fallback inside \`synthesizeCanonicalLifecycle\` entirely**; rely on \`meta[\"role\"]\` + explicit \`sessionKind\` only. Simpler conceptually but requires auditing every call site to ensure they either stamp role first or pass \`sessionKind\` — same work as option 1, just pushed to the callers.

Either way the scope is similar to PR #1075's fix: ~10 lines of core + a regression test.

## Regression test to add

\`packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/query.test.ts\` already has \`does not backfill role onto foreign bare-id orchestrator records (issue #1048)\` — which only asserts on-disk state. Extend it (or add a sibling) that asserts the in-memory Session:

\`\`\`ts
const sessions = await sm.list(\"my-app\");
const session = sessions.find((s) => s.id === \"my-app-orchestrator\");
expect(session?.lifecycle?.session.kind).toBe(\"worker\");
\`\`\`

## Scope note

Deliberately not in scope for PR #1075 — that fix is already large and the in-memory leak requires an unusual legacy record to trigger (users would need a foreign-prefix bare record on disk from an older AO version that they never cleaned up). Low likelihood in practice, but worth closing for soundness.

## Labels suggested

\`bug\`, \`priority: low\`, \`area: core/session-manager\`

Related: #1048 (original issue), #1075 (partial fix)

title: Lifecycle manager can falsely route agents for already-addressed reviews and non-failing CI
body:
## Summary

The lifecycle manager can send incorrect agent notifications for both:

- review changes requested, even after the review comments were already addressed
- CI failure, even when the PR currently has no failing checks

This causes agents to get re-routed into the wrong work loop and do unnecessary work.

## Observed behavior

On `ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator#1308`, after review comments had already been addressed and replies were posted, the agent still received a "there are review comments on your PR" prompt as if unresolved review feedback was newly pending.

Separately, the agent also received a "CI is failing on your PR" prompt even though the PR did not have an active failing check at that time.

In both cases, the agent acted on a stale/incorrect lifecycle signal rather than current GitHub ground truth.

## Expected behavior

The lifecycle manager should only emit:

- review-requested / address-reviews style prompts when there are currently unresolved review requirements or actionable unresolved review comments
- fixing-ci style prompts when the PR currently has a failing required or relevant check

If the latest GitHub state shows:

- no failing CI
- no new unresolved review action

then no new agent task should be emitted for those categories.

## Why this matters

These false positives create churn:

- agents burn cycles re-checking already-green CI
- agents re-open already-addressed review work
- user trust in AO routing drops because the orchestration state does not match GitHub reality

## Suspected problem areas

Likely one or more of:

- stale cached PR/review/check state being treated as fresh
- lifecycle transitions triggered from older SCM events without reconciliation against latest PR state
- review-comment existence being treated as actionable even when already replied/addressed
- CI-failure state not being cleared when checks return to passing/pending/non-failing states

## Reproduction shape

1. Open a PR
2. Receive review comments and/or a transient CI failure
3. Address the review comments and/or push fixes so CI is no longer failing
4. Observe lifecycle manager still route the agent as if:
   - reviews are still newly pending, or
   - CI is still failing

## Suggested fix direction

Before routing an agent into review-fix or CI-fix flows, reconcile against current SCM ground truth:

- latest review decision
- unresolved actionable inline/top-level comments
- current check run / check suite / status state

In particular, avoid firing based only on historical events without a final "is this still true right now?" check.

title: fix(repo): install matching gitleaks binary for arm64 local runners
body:
## Issue

before pushing code to the origin/main I prefer running the CI workflow locally first using `agent-ci`. security.yml wasn't prepared for this and hence the gitleaks job was failing, blocking local workflow run.

![Gitleaks crash on arm64 local agent-ci runner](https://github.com/yyovil/storage/releases/download/agent-orchestrator%2F1327/agent-orchestrator-1327-s01-gitleaks-crash.png)

## Affected Package

- Package path: `./.github/workflows/security.yml`
- Surface area: `security workflow / gitleaks CI job`

## Reproduction

1. Run `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure` on an Apple Silicon Mac.
2. Let `agent-ci` start the `security.yml > gitleaks` job.
3. Observe the `Run Gitleaks` step in the paused runner after `Install Gitleaks` succeeds.

## Current Result

`The workflow downloads gitleaks_8.24.3_linux_x64.tar.gz, the binary starts under the local arm64 runner, and then crashes with a Go runtime panic (for example: fatal error: lfstack.push). The gitleaks job pauses and must be retried, but the retry fails the same way.`

## Expected Result

`The workflow should select the correct Gitleaks archive for the runner architecture (for example linux_arm64 on arm64 runners) and the Gitleaks scan should run successfully without crashing.`

## Evidence

- Workflow file hardcodes the x64 archive in `.github/workflows/security.yml`:
  - `ARCHIVE_NAME="gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"`
- Local `agent-ci` runner architecture:
  - `uname -m` => `aarch64`
- Paused runner step:
  - `Run Gitleaks`
- Crash excerpt from `/tmp/agent-ci-signals/step-output`:
  - `runtime: lfstack.push invalid packing`
  - `fatal error: lfstack.push`
- The installed binary exists in the runner temp directory:
  - `/home/runner/_work/_temp/gitleaks-bin/gitleaks`

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. Open `.github/workflows/security.yml` and trace how the `Install Gitleaks` step chooses the archive name.
2. Fix the root cause by selecting the Gitleaks archive from the runner architecture instead of hardcoding `linux_x64`.
3. Add or update focused validation around the architecture selection logic if practical for workflow scripts.
4. Run the narrowest relevant validation for the workflow and confirm local `agent-ci` no longer crashes in `security.yml > gitleaks`.
5. Verify the `Run Gitleaks` step executes successfully on arm64 local runners.
6. Commit only the workflow change and any closely related validation updates. No unrelated files.

## Validation

- Workflow validation: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --workflow .github/workflows/security.yml --pause-on-failure`
- Broader repo checks only when needed: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure`

## Constraints

- Keep the scope inside `.github/workflows/security.yml` unless a shared CI helper is required.
- Preserve the existing Gitleaks version and checksum verification flow unless changing them is required to fix the bug.
- Prefer a minimal architecture-selection change over a workflow refactor.
- Note any follow-up CI hardening separately instead of expanding scope inside this issue.

## Acceptance

- `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --workflow .github/workflows/security.yml --pause-on-failure` reaches and completes `Run Gitleaks` on arm64 local runners.
- The workflow downloads the correct archive for the active runner architecture and no Go runtime crash appears in the Gitleaks step output.

title: bug: cross-project spawn tags session with wrong projectId
body:
## Description

When multiple projects are defined in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (e.g. `agent-orchestrator` and `x402-identity`), spawning a session for a non-default project's issue still assigns `projectId` of the project the AO instance was started for.

## Reproduction

1. Add a second project to `agent-orchestrator.yaml`:
```yaml
projects:
  agent-orchestrator:
    name: Agent Orchestrator
    repo: ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator
    ...
  x402-identity:
    name: x402 Identity
    repo: harsh-batheja/x402-identity
    sessionPrefix: xid
    ...
```

2. Start AO for the default project: `ao start agent-orchestrator`
3. Spawn a session for the second project: `ao spawn x402-identity/1`
4. Check the session via API or dashboard

## Expected

- `projectId` = `x402-identity`
- Session prefix = `xid-*`
- Session appears under x402-identity on the dashboard

## Actual

- `projectId` = `agent-orchestrator`
- Session prefix = `ao-*` (default project prefix)
- Session appears under Agent Orchestrator on the dashboard
- Branch and issueId resolve correctly (`feat/x402-identity-1`, `x402-identity/1`), so the issue reference IS being resolved — just the project assignment is wrong

## Environment

- AO version: latest from `main`
- Config: single `agent-orchestrator.yaml` with multiple projects under `projects:`
- Runtime: tmux + claude-code

## Notes

The issue reference resolution works — `ao spawn x402-identity/1` correctly looks up the repo, creates the branch `feat/x402-identity-1`, and sets `issueId` to `x402-identity/1`. It's only the `projectId` and session prefix that fall back to the default running project. Suggest the spawn logic should derive `projectId` from the resolved issue prefix rather than from the running instance's primary project.

title: fix(cli): derive projectId from prefixed issue id on spawn
body:
## Summary

Fixes cross-project spawn tagging the session with the wrong `projectId` when `ao start` is running for a different project than the issue belongs to.

- **New core utility `resolveSpawnTarget(projects, issueRef, fallback?)`** — parses `<prefix>/<rest>` and routes to the matched project. Accepts either a project id (yaml key) or `sessionPrefix` as the prefix; project id wins on collision. Returns `null` when nothing matches and no fallback is supplied.
- **`ao spawn <projectId>/<issue>`** — now routes to the prefixed project and strips the prefix from the issue id. Previously `projectId` fell back to whichever project `ao start` was running for, giving the session the wrong prefix and dashboard column.
- **`ao spawn <sessionPrefix>/<issue>`** — also works (e.g. `xid/1` routes to the project whose `sessionPrefix` is `xid`).
- **`ao batch-spawn`** — groups issues by resolved project and runs preflight once per group, instead of erroring on mixed prefixes.
- **Web `/api/spawn`** — unchanged; it already requires an explicit `projectId`, so it's immune. Any future caller that wants free-form issue refs can opt in by calling `resolveSpawnTarget` before `sessionManager.spawn()`.
- **`SessionManager.spawn()`** — unchanged on purpose. Explicit `{ projectId, issueId }` stays authoritative; the utility is opt-in for callers that want routing.

Fixes #1329

## Design notes

The first commit was a CLI-only fix. The second commit lifts the routing into a core utility so any spawn entry point (CLI, web API, programmatic) can share the same behavior. The CLI now imports `resolveSpawnTarget` instead of duplicating logic.

Prefix disambiguation: project-id match wins over `sessionPrefix` match because yaml keys are unique by construction while `sessionPrefix` values are not guaranteed to be.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 800 tests pass, including 8 new unit tests for `resolveSpawnTarget` covering:
  - project-id prefix match
  - sessionPrefix prefix match
  - project-id wins on collision
  - fallback used when prefix doesn't match
  - returns `null` when nothing matches and no fallback
  - bare issue id passed through
  - leading/trailing slash inputs handled
  - `undefined` issueRef handled
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 485 tests pass, including 3 new `spawn.test.ts` cases:
  - routes `x402-identity/1` → `projectId: x402-identity`, `issueId: 1`
  - routes `xid/7` via `sessionPrefix` → `projectId: x402-identity`, `issueId: 7`
  - leaves `some-org/42` untouched when no project or prefix matches
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` pass
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (33 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [ ] Manual repro: multi-project config, `ao start agent-orchestrator`, `ao spawn x402-identity/1` → session prefix `xid-*`, `projectId` = `x402-identity`, appears under x402-identity on the dashboard
- [ ] Manual repro: `ao batch-spawn agent-orchestrator/1 x402-identity/2` → one session per project, each routed correctly

title: fix(deps): bump vulnerable dependencies so pnpm audit passes cleanly
body:
## Issue

`pnpm audit` reports vulnerable dependency chains in the current monorepo dependency graph. We should bump the affected direct and/or peer-resolved dependencies so the audit passes cleanly instead of relying on workflow tolerance or retry behavior.

## Affected Package

- Package path: `packages/web`, `packages/plugins/notifier-composio`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- npm package: `@aoagents/ao-web`, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-composio`
- Surface area: `security.yml` dependency audit, local `pnpm audit`, local `agent-ci` workflow execution
- Shared code touched: `none expected beyond lockfile and any package manifests needed for the bumps`

## Reproduction

1. Sync a working branch with `origin/main`.
2. Run local workflow validation: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure`.
3. Observe the run pause in `security.yml > npm-audit > Run npm audit`.
4. Reproduce locally with `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate --json`.

## Current Result

`agent-ci` pauses on the audit step, and local `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate --json` reports `5` vulnerabilities (`1 low`, `4 moderate`).

## Expected Result

`pnpm audit` should pass cleanly on the repo dependency graph so `security.yml` and local `agent-ci` runs can complete in the cleanest possible way, without depending on tolerated failures, retries, or workflow-level suppression.

## Evidence

- Workflow step: `.github/workflows/security.yml`
  - `Run npm audit` executes `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate`
- Local reproduction:
  - `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate --json`
  - Result: `5` vulnerabilities, `1 low`, `4 moderate`
- Vulnerabilities observed:
  - `vite@5.4.21` via `GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9`
  - `esbuild@0.21.5` via `GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99`
  - `follow-redirects@1.15.11` via `GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653`
  - `langsmith@0.5.18` via `GHSA-rr7j-v2q5-chgv`
  - `tmp@0.0.33` via `GHSA-52f5-9888-hmc6`
- Example dependency paths from local audit output:
  - `packages/web > @vitejs/plugin-react@4.7.0 > vite@5.4.21 > esbuild@0.21.5`
  - `packages/plugins/notifier-composio > composio-core@0.5.39 > axios@1.15.0 > follow-redirects@1.15.11`
  - `packages/plugins/notifier-composio > composio-core@0.5.39 > @langchain/core@1.1.39 > langsmith@0.5.18`

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. Open `packages/web/package.json`, `packages/plugins/notifier-composio/package.json`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` and trace which direct or peer-resolved dependencies are responsible for the vulnerable chains.
2. Bump the relevant dependencies so the resolved graph no longer includes the flagged vulnerable versions.
3. Prefer real dependency upgrades over workflow suppression; do not solve this by weakening `security.yml`.
4. Update the lockfile with the narrowest dependency changes that eliminate the current audit findings.
5. Re-run `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate` and local `agent-ci` to confirm the workflow now clears the audit step cleanly.
6. Commit only the manifest and lockfile changes needed for the audit cleanup.

## Validation

- Audit check: `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate`
- Strict audit check: `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high`
- Relevant package checks: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test`, `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`
- Broader validation: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure`

## Constraints

- Keep scope focused on dependency bumps and lockfile updates required to clear the current audit findings.
- Do not paper over the issue by changing the workflow to ignore or suppress the audit failure.
- Prefer the smallest version changes that remove the vulnerable resolved versions.
- Note any dependency that cannot be bumped cleanly as follow-up work instead of broadening scope unnecessarily.

## Acceptance

- `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate` exits successfully on the repo checkout
- Local `agent-ci` no longer pauses on `security.yml > npm-audit > Run npm audit`

title: fix(core): dispatch detailed bugbot review comments to agents
body:
## Summary

Fixes #895 — the bugbot-comments reaction was sending a generic message, leaving the agent to rediscover comments on its own. The naive `GET /pulls/{pr}/comments` first-page scan misses new comments on later pages and trusts a stale `gh pr checks` status, causing the agent to falsely report "all reviews addressed."

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`
  - Add `formatAutomatedCommentsMessage(AutomatedComment[])`, mirroring `formatCIFailureMessage`. Lists each comment (severity, bot name, `path:line`, first-line excerpt, URL) and embeds correct-API guidance.
  - In `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`, override the reaction config's `message` with the formatted one for `send-to-agent` dispatches of `bugbot-comments`. Fingerprint/dedup path unchanged.
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — update the default `bugbot-comments` reaction text to embed the `/reviews` → `/reviews/{id}/comments` → paginated `/pulls/{pr}/comments` (checking `in_reply_to_id`) sequence as a fallback for custom configs that don't rely on the dispatcher.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` — update the "dispatches automated review comments only once" test to assert the new message contains comment details AND the correct-API guidance.

## Why this design

The core already paginates `getAutomatedComments` correctly and knows every bot comment. The old code threw that data away when dispatching and let the agent re-query with a broken pattern. Passing the already-fetched data to the agent removes the failure mode entirely; embedding the correct verification steps guards against agents that still want to re-check.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — passes

title: fix(core): fail closed on health probe exceptions in send path
body:
## Summary

- Flip all 8 `.catch(() => true)` occurrences in `session-manager.ts` to `.catch(() => false)` so runtime/agent health probe exceptions are treated as **not verified healthy** rather than silently "alive". Masking those exceptions previously caused messages to be sent to dead sessions with false confidence.
- Make `waitForRestoredSession` throw on deadline instead of returning silently — callers now see a loud failure when a restored session never reaches a ready state.
- `lifecycle-manager.ts` already wraps probes in `try/catch` and marks `probe_failed` / `failed: true`, so no change was needed there.

## Context

Fixes #1067. Before this change, `runtime.isAlive()` or `agent.isProcessRunning()` throwing (tmux lookup failures, plugin crashes, timeouts) was indistinguishable from the session actually being alive. The orchestrator would cheerfully hand messages to sessions that could not possibly receive them.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 795/795 pass

- [x] `pnpm lint` — no new errors
- [x] New regression tests in `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/communication.test.ts`:
  - `triggers restore when runtime.isAlive throws (fails closed)`
  - `triggers restore when agent.isProcessRunning throws (fails closed)`
  - `throws when restored session probes keep failing past the timeout`

Closes #1067
