title: feat: add kimi-2-6-code plugin
proposal: prevent bug regressions across agent sessions via tests + agent-lessons.md
body:
## Context

Each AO worker session spawns a fresh agent with no memory of prior bugs. This already bit us on PR #1334 (fixes #895): the first draft of the detailed bugbot-dispatch guidance was missing `--paginate` on step 2, reintroducing the exact pagination failure mode the fix was meant to prevent. It was caught by a reviewer — not by the agent.

As worker sessions scale up, \"reviewer catches it\" is not a durable strategy. We need a mechanism that makes old bugs physically hard to reintroduce, regardless of which model or session is writing the code.

## Why a memory system alone is the wrong answer

Markdown \"lessons\" files get skimmed, drift out of date, are skipped by context-pruned agents, and have no enforcement surface. We should not build one as the primary mechanism.

## Proposal: three-layer defense, priced by cost and effectiveness

### 1. Regression tests are load-bearing (primary, zero infra)

Every `fix:` PR must add at least one test that fails if the bug reappears. PR #1334 demonstrates:

```ts
it(\"paginates every enumerated gh api command (fixes #895)\", () => {
  // asserts all 3 numbered commands carry --paginate
});
```

A future agent that drops `--paginate` gets a red CI without reading any doc.

**Enforcement**: add a rule to `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` (and the new `.github/copilot-instructions.md` if/when we add it):

> On `fix:` PRs, flag any changed test file that does not reference the issue number (`#N`) or include a `fixes #N` comment.

Bot reviewers already read these files every PR. No infra to build.

### 2. `docs/agent-lessons.md` wired via `agentRulesFile` (secondary)

AO's prompt-builder already has a 3-layer prompt (base → config → user rules). Layer 3 reads `agentRulesFile` from `agent-orchestrator.yaml`. That's our \"memory\" hook — worker sessions load it automatically.

Keep it terse and test-linked:

```markdown
# Agent Lessons

One-liner per past incident. Each bullet must link to the regression test that enforces it; if it can't, write a test first.

- #895: detailed bugbot dispatch must include `--paginate` on all three `gh api` calls.
  Enforced by: `format-automated-comments.test.ts:\"paginates every enumerated gh api command\"`.
- #1360: CI-failing chip reads three sources; they must stay in sync on recovery.
  Enforced by: **TODO** — no test yet.
```

Wire in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`:
```yaml
agentRulesFile: docs/agent-lessons.md
```

This file is an **index of tests**, not a behavior policy. Anything that sits in this file without a test-link is a signal to write the test, not to elaborate the prose.

### 3. Review-bot hints (tertiary)

`.cursor/BUGBOT.md` / `.github/copilot-instructions.md` list anti-patterns bots should flag on every diff. Fresh diff analysis triggered by every PR is strictly more effective than any file a future agent might or might not read. This is what caught the `--paginate` miss in #1334.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Convention documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (or similar): every `fix:` commit references its issue in the commit message; every `fix:` PR adds at least one test that references the issue.
- [ ] `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` updated with the \"fix PR must add a regression test referencing the issue\" rule.
- [ ] `docs/agent-lessons.md` created with #895 as the seed entry, strictly formatted as \"bullet → test reference\".
- [ ] `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (example config / template, not the user's personal one) wires `agentRulesFile: docs/agent-lessons.md` so worker sessions inherit it.
- [ ] (Follow-up, not blocking) add a lightweight check — commit-msg hook or CI step — that `fix:` commits reference an issue number.

## Non-goals

- Building a structured memory database / SQLite / vector store. We don't have enough incidents yet, and everything we could store is more durably expressed as a test + a one-line index entry.
- Forcing every `feat:` PR to add a \"lesson\" — only regression-worthy incidents.

## Seed data (for context)

Incidents that would go into the v1 of `docs/agent-lessons.md`:

1. **#895** — review-check logic misses new bugbot comments from the latest push. Test: `format-automated-comments.test.ts`.
2. **#1360** — session detail shows CI failing when CI is passing (3-way OR + 5-min cache). Test: TODO.
3. Whatever incident inspires us to add it next.

## Why this is worth doing now

Between #895, #1334 (nearly-reintroduced #895), and #1360, we already have a pattern: bugs in the PR-feedback and lifecycle paths recur because multiple agents touch similar code without shared history. The fix is structurally cheap (a test + a one-liner) and compounds — every added entry makes the next agent's diff safer.

title: bug: spawned worker agents consistently fail to start working (stuck at idle, zero changes)
body:
## Problem

Spawned worker agents consistently fail to start working. They land in `idle`/`exited` state shortly after spawn with zero code changes, no commits, and no PR created. This has been reproduced 4 consecutive times across different issues.

## Reproduction

1. `ao spawn --prompt "<task description>"` — session spawns successfully
2. Wait 1-5 minutes, check `ao status` — session shows `idle` with no PR, no changes
3. Check worktree — `git status` and `git diff` show zero modifications
4. Session eventually transitions to `exited` or `stuck`

## Evidence

Four consecutive failures today (2026-04-21):

| Session | Issue | Result | Activity |
|---------|-------|--------|----------|
| ao-2 | #1199 | exited (1m) | zero changes |
| ao-3 | #1199 | exited (47s) | zero changes |
| ao-4 | #1199 | idle (3m+, killed manually) | zero changes |
| ao-5 | #1360 | idle (29s, killed manually) | zero changes |

### ao-2 lifecycle metadata (representative)
```
status=stuck
lifecycleEvidence=signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited
reportWatcherActiveTrigger=no_acknowledge
detectingAttempts=38
```

Key signals:
- `no_acknowledge` — agent never acknowledged the prompt
- `signal_disagreement` — runtime reported alive but process was dead
- `detectingAttempts=38` — activity detection ran 38 times without the agent ever starting work

### ao-1 (issue #1073) is the exception
ao-1 is the only session that successfully started working — it has PR #1 open (though CI is failing). This suggests the issue is intermittent but has a very high failure rate (~80% of spawns).

## Environment

- AO version: current `main` (~`64badbd`)
- Platform: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Agent plugin: claude-code
- Runtime: tmux
- Orchestrator session: ao-orchestrator-1

## Possible causes

1. **Agent process crash on startup** — the claude-code agent process may be crashing before it can read the prompt (consistent with `no_acknowledge`)
2. **Tmux session issue** — the tmux session may not be properly delivering the prompt to the agent
3. **Resource contention** — multiple sessions may compete for resources (tmux sockets, worktree locks)
4. **Prompt delivery failure** — the prompt may not be reaching the agent stdin properly

## Suggested investigation

1. Check tmux pane content for the failed sessions (`tmux capture-pane -t <session>`) to see if the agent binary even started
2. Add logging for prompt delivery confirmation
3. Check if the agent binary path is correct and accessible from the worktree
4. Check system resources (memory, file descriptors) during spawn

title: fix: setup workspace hooks before launching agent to prevent trust prompt
body:
## Summary

- Moved `setupWorkspaceHooks` call before `runtime.create()` in both `spawnSession` and `spawnOrchestrator` flows
- Without this, Claude Code shows an interactive trust prompt in fresh worktrees and the agent never receives its task prompt, causing workers to idle and die

## Root Cause

Claude Code displays "Is this a project you trust?" on first launch in an untrusted directory. The spawn flow was:
1. Launch agent in tmux (triggers trust prompt)
2. Create `.claude/settings.json` via `setupWorkspaceHooks` (too late)

The agent sat at the trust prompt indefinitely, never reaching the task prompt. ~80% of spawns failed (4 out of 5 consecutive attempts).

## Fix

Reorder so `setupWorkspaceHooks` runs **before** `runtime.create()`:
1. Create `.claude/settings.json` (marks workspace as trusted)
2. Launch agent in tmux (skips trust prompt)
3. Deliver task prompt

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 801/801 pass
- [x] `pnpm build` passes

title: Dashboard button in sidebar causes full page reload on every click
body:
## Bug

The small grid icon (4-square) button next to each project name in the sidebar triggers a full page reload on every click instead of a smooth client-side navigation.

## Location

- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — line 473-483 (the `<Link>` with grid SVG icon)
- `packages/web/src/app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx` — `force-dynamic` SSR page

## Root Cause

The dashboard button uses `<Link href={projectDashboardPath(project.id)}>` which resolves to `/projects/<projectId>`. That page is marked `force-dynamic` (SSR on every request), so every click triggers:

1. Server roundtrip to fetch the RSC payload
2. Full re-render of the page from scratch (`getProjectRouteData` + `getDashboardPageData`)
3. Visible loading delay — the screen blanks and everything reloads

This is noticeably slower than the session links in the same sidebar, which use `router.push()` with `e.preventDefault()` for client-side navigation.

## Fix Options

- **(a)** Add a `loading.tsx` skeleton for the `\/projects/[projectId]` route so the transition is visually smooth
- **(b)** Switch the dashboard button to use `router.push()` with optimistic client-side state (matching the pattern used by session links on lines 315-318)
- **(c)** Both — loading skeleton as fallback + `router.push()` for the sidebar shortcut

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the AO dashboard with at least one project configured
2. Navigate to any session detail page
3. Click the 4-square grid icon next to a project name in the sidebar
4. Observe: the entire page reloads with a visible blank/loading delay

title: Stale reaction dispatch: CI failure and merge conflict messages injected repeatedly despite PR being clean
body:
## Bug

The lifecycle manager repeatedly injects "CI is failing on your PR" and "Your branch has merge conflicts" messages to agent sessions even when the associated PR has passing CI and no merge conflicts. The agent dismisses them as stale noise, but they keep coming.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1481732697225539674/1491735678156013588/1496203865740283987
**Reported by:** @prateek
**Analyzed against:** \`59f66f4\` (main)

## Screenshot

See Discord thread — screenshot shows 16+ repeated messages alternating between CI failure and merge conflict dispatches within a single agent session.

## Root Cause

**Status oscillation resets reaction trackers, bypassing retry limits.**

The reaction dispatch chain:

1. **\`checkSession()\`** (\`lifecycle-manager.ts:1634\`) runs \`determineStatus()\` which queries PR state via batch GraphQL enrichment.

2. When \`newStatus !== oldStatus\` (line 1682), the **old status's reaction tracker is cleared** (lines 1712-1718):
   \`\`\`ts
   const oldEventType = statusToEventType(undefined, oldStatus);
   if (oldEventType) {
     const oldReactionKey = eventToReactionKey(oldEventType);
     if (oldReactionKey) {
       clearReactionTracker(session.id, oldReactionKey);
     }
   }
   \`\`\`

3. The **new status's reaction fires** via \`executeReaction()\` (line 1733) — which creates a fresh tracker with \`attempts: 0\`.

4. The \`ci-failed\` reaction has \`retries: 2\`, so it should fire at most 3 times before escalating. But **every oscillation out of \`ci_failed\` clears the tracker, and every oscillation back creates a fresh one** — effectively resetting the retry budget.

**The oscillation trigger:** The \`resolvePREnrichmentDecision()\` path in \`determineStatus()\` (line 739-746) uses batch GraphQL data from \`prEnrichmentCache\`. When the ETag guard (\`shouldRefreshPREnrichment()\` in \`graphql-batch.ts:177\`) says "no changes detected", stale cached data is returned (line 895-916). If the cached data says \`ciStatus: "failing"\` or \`mergeable === "CONFLICTING"\` but the PR has since been fixed, the status incorrectly becomes \`ci_failed\` on every poll cycle — re-firing the reaction.

**Contributing factors:**
- \`statusToEventType()\` (line 139) only considers the **target** status, not the source. So \`working → ci_failed\` and \`pr_open → ci_failed\` both produce \`ci.failing\`.
- \`maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()\` (line 1291) has fingerprint-based dedup, but the **transition reaction** at line 1733 is NOT fingerprint-gated — it fires the static message "CI is failing on your PR. Run gh pr checks..." every time the status transitions to \`ci_failed\`.
- \`maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()\` (line 1424) uses \`lastMergeConflictDispatched\` metadata for dedup, but stale cached \`hasConflicts: true\` from the ETag guard bypass prevents the "conflicts resolved" path (line 1512-1518) from clearing the flag.

## Fix

**Option A (recommended) — Don't clear reaction tracker for the old status on exit.** The tracker should only be cleared when the condition that triggered the reaction is genuinely resolved (CI goes from failing → passing via live check, conflicts confirmed resolved). Change lines 1712-1718 to only clear trackers for states that were verified as resolved.

**Option B — Add a "recently dispatched" timestamp guard.** Before firing \`executeReaction()\` at line 1733, check if the same reaction was dispatched within the last N seconds and skip if so.

**Option C — Live verification before reaction dispatch.** When the batch cache says CI is failing, make a live \`scm.getCISummary()\` call to confirm before injecting the message.

## Impact

- Agents waste tokens repeatedly dismissing false CI/merge conflict alerts
- Agents may attempt unnecessary fixes (rebase, CI check) on clean PRs
- Creates noise in the agent context window, degrading task performance
- Burns GitHub API rate limit on redundant gh pr checks calls from the agent side

title: bug(web): sidebar shows "Failed to load sessions" on session detail page
body:
## Bug

The project sidebar on the session detail page (`/sessions/[id]`) displays **"Failed to load sessions"** with a Retry button, leaving the user unable to navigate between sessions from the sidebar.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1489612265027014736/1491735678156013588/1496205091739275404
**Reported by:** @Ashish
**Analyzed against:** `59f66f4` (main)

## Screenshot

![sidebar showing Failed to load sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-sidebar-error/.issue-assets/sidebar-failed-to-load-sessions.png)

## Reproduction

1. Open the AO web dashboard
2. Navigate to a specific session's detail page (`/sessions/[id]`)
3. Observe the sidebar — it shows "Failed to load sessions" with a "Retry" button
4. Clicking "Retry" may or may not resolve the issue (depends on the underlying cause)

## Root Cause

The error originates from a **client-side fetch** in `sessions/[id]/page.tsx`:

**Trigger chain:**
1. `fetchSidebarSessions()` (line 373) calls `GET /api/sessions?fresh=true`
2. If the fetch fails (network error, 500 from API, timeout), line 392 sets `sidebarError = true`
3. This flows to `<SessionDetail sidebarError={sidebarError} onRetrySidebar={fetchSidebarSessions}>` (line 500–502)
4. `SessionDetail` passes it to `<ProjectSidebar error={sidebarError} onRetry={onRetrySidebar}>` (line 663)
5. `ProjectSidebar` renders "Failed to load sessions" at line 628 when `error === true` and no sessions exist

**Possible failure causes for the API call:**
- **GitHub API rate limiting** (#1083, #1194) — the `/api/sessions` route enriches sessions with PR data via `enrichSessionPR()`, which calls GitHub API. Rate limits cause timeouts/failures.
- **`sessionManager.list()` failure** — if the config file is missing or corrupt, `getServices()` throws before any session data is returned.
- **Network/connectivity issues** between the dashboard server and GitHub API.
- **Timeouts** — the route has a 3s metadata enrichment timeout and 4s PR enrichment timeout. If these are exceeded, the response may still succeed but if any `await` in the chain throws, the catch block returns a 500.

**Key observation:** The error message is **generic** — it says "Failed to load sessions" regardless of the actual cause (rate limit, network, config error). The user has no way to diagnose what went wrong from the UI alone.

## Fix

**Short-term — improve error UX:**
1. Pass the actual error message from the API response to the sidebar instead of a generic boolean. In `fetchSidebarSessions()` (line 378–379), parse the error body:
   ```tsx
   if (!res.ok) {
     const body = await res.json().catch(() => null);
     throw new Error(body?.error ?? `HTTP ${res.status}`);
   }
   ```
   Then surface `err.message` in the sidebar instead of the hardcoded "Failed to load sessions".

2. Detect rate-limit errors specifically and show a targeted message (e.g., "GitHub API rate limited — sidebar data may be stale").

**Longer-term — resilience:**
3. The `fetchSidebarSessions` function should fall back to cached/stale data more gracefully. Currently on error it sets `sidebarSessions` to `[]` (line 393), wiping any previously loaded sessions. It should keep the stale data visible and show a "data may be stale" banner instead (the component already has this pattern at line 363–379 for when sessions exist but the refresh fails).

## Impact

- Users cannot navigate between sessions from the sidebar on the session detail page
- No diagnostic information is provided to help users self-resolve
- Likely triggered by the same GitHub rate-limit issues tracked in #1083 and #1194

title: Dashboard kanban card UX improvements
body:
## Summary

Several UX issues on the session kanban cards that degrade usability and confuse users.

---

### 1. Remove Continue / Abort / Skip preset buttons

**Problem:** These three buttons send the literal words `"continue"`, `"abort"`, and `"skip"` as plain text messages to the agent session. There is no structured backend handling — they are just `handleQuickReply("abort")` etc. From the card there is no way to know what they do. "Abort" looks like it would kill the session, but it just sends a chat message. "Skip" and "Continue" are equally ambiguous.

**Fix:** Remove the three preset buttons entirely. They add confusion without adding value. If quick-reply presets are needed in the future, they should be contextual (e.g. "Fix CI" when CI is failing, "Address review" when changes are requested) — not generic mystery buttons.

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — the `card__presets` div containing the Continue/Abort/Skip buttons (~lines 717–749).

---

### 2. Add Send button to the reply textarea

**Problem:** The reply input (`<textarea>` with class `card__reply`) only supports Enter-to-send (`handleReplyKeyDown` checks for Enter key). There is no clickable Send button. The placeholder says `"(Enter to send)"` but that is easily missed. Users expect a visible send affordance.

**Fix:** Add a Send button (icon or text) next to the textarea that calls `handleQuickReply(replyText)`. Disable it when `replyText` is empty or `sendingQuickReply !== null`.

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — inside the `card__reply-wrap` div (~lines 751–764).

---

### 3. Badge pill next to PR number shows perpetual loading spinner

**Problem:** Next to the PR number badge (e.g. `#17152`), there is an empty dark pill/badge element that sometimes shows a loading spinner indefinitely. This happens when the session is in a `detecting` state or when runtime data is missing — the badge never resolves and spins forever.

**Fix:** The badge should show a timeout state or empty state instead of an infinite spinner. Either:
- Show the badge content when data is available, hide it when not (do not render an empty loading pill)
- Or set a max loading duration after which it shows a fallback (e.g. "—" or no badge)

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — the empty pill badge element near the PR number display.

---

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Continue/Abort/Skip preset buttons removed from session cards
- [ ] Send button added next to the reply textarea
- [ ] No perpetual loading spinner on badge pills — timeout or fallback state
- [ ] No visual regressions on the card layout

title: Finish deprecation of Agent.detectActivity() — remove from interface and callers
body:
## Problem

`Agent.detectActivity()` has been `@deprecated` in favor of `getActivityState()` for a long time, but the migration was never finished. It's still a **required** method on the `Agent` interface and is still called from three places in core/cli, so every plugin must implement it.

**Evidence (verified on current `main`):**

- `packages/core/src/types.ts:483` — declares `detectActivity()` as a REQUIRED method on the `Agent` interface, with a `@deprecated` JSDoc note pointing to `getActivityState()`.
- Still called from:
  - `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:604`
  - `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2167`
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts:58`
- Every agent plugin (`agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-aider`, `agent-opencode`) implements it to satisfy the interface.

`getActivityState()` is already the canonical source of truth — `CLAUDE.md` documents it as the required cascade for all agent plugins, and the dashboard/lifecycle manager/stuck-detection all depend on it. `detectActivity()` duplicates a subset of that signal (just the raw terminal-output classification) and is no longer needed at the interface level — where it *is* still useful (inside `recordActivity`/`classifyTerminalActivity`), it can remain as an internal helper on the plugin.

## Proposed change

1. Migrate the three remaining callers to use `getActivityState()` (or `checkActivityLogState()` / `classifyTerminalActivity()` directly where a raw classification is truly needed):
   - `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:604`
   - `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2167`
   - `packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts:58`
2. Remove `detectActivity()` from the `Agent` interface in `packages/core/src/types.ts:483`.
3. Update agent plugins to drop the public `detectActivity` method. Plugins using the AO Activity JSONL pattern (Aider, OpenCode, Codex-as-safety-net) can keep an internal classifier function and pass it to `recordTerminalActivity()` — that's the only legitimate remaining use, and it doesn't need to be on the interface.
4. Update tests and any plugin docs in `CLAUDE.md` that still reference `detectActivity` as a required method.

This is a mechanical cleanup — no behavior change. The dashboard already consumes `getActivityState()` exclusively.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. Represents an incomplete deprecation: the method was marked `@deprecated` long ago but never actually removed, so plugin authors still have to implement it to satisfy the interface, and callers still invoke the deprecated path.

## Related issues

- #160, #17, #18, #19 — enhancement requests for richer `detectActivity()` patterns on Codex/Aider/OpenCode. These become less relevant once `detectActivity()` is removed from the public interface; the same classification logic belongs inside each plugin's `recordActivity`/internal classifier and should be driven by `getActivityState()` requirements instead.

title: refactor(core): consolidate duplicate interface declarations for PREnrichmentData and BatchObserver in types.ts
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/types.ts` declares two interfaces in two separate locations each, relying on TypeScript's declaration merging:

- `PREnrichmentData` — declared at line 815 **and** line 992
- `BatchObserver` — declared at line 844 **and** line 1023

These are **not pure duplicates** — the second `PREnrichmentData` declaration (around line 1015) adds a `ciChecks` field via TypeScript interface merging, so the behavior is intentional from the compiler's perspective. However, having two declaration sites for a single logical interface is a maintenance trap:

- Developers editing one site can easily miss the other.
- Field additions/removals can silently diverge in intent from the original declaration.
- Interface merging across widely-separated lines in the same file offers no real benefit (unlike cross-file augmentation).

## Proposed change

Collapse each interface into a single declaration site containing all fields:

- Merge the two `PREnrichmentData` declarations (lines 815 and 992) into one, including the `ciChecks` field.
- Merge the two `BatchObserver` declarations (lines 844 and 1023) into one.

Add a brief comment noting why the consolidated shape exists if any field ordering is load-bearing.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviewers. The initial audit incorrectly flagged these as pure duplicate declarations; Codex clarified that they are TypeScript interface merges (the second declarations add fields) rather than redundant copies. The fix is still worthwhile to reduce maintenance risk — a single declaration site is easier to keep coherent than two.

## Related issues

- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (broader backend hygiene)
- #772 — Refactor: Extract shared types package (type organization)

title: refactor(core): unify CanonicalSessionState and SessionStatus — eliminate dual state representation
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/types.ts` defines two parallel state enums for the same concept:

- `CanonicalSessionState` (8 states) — `packages/core/src/types.ts:29-37`
  `not_started | working | idle | needs_input | stuck | detecting | done | terminated`
- `SessionStatus` (18 states) — `packages/core/src/types.ts:117-136`
  `spawning | working | detecting | pr_open | ci_failed | review_pending | changes_requested | approved | mergeable | merged | cleanup | needs_input | stuck | errored | killed | idle | done | terminated`

The `Session` interface at `packages/core/src/types.ts:286-303` carries BOTH fields in parallel:

```ts
export interface Session {
  status: SessionStatus;                    // legacy projection
  lifecycle: CanonicalSessionLifecycle;     // canonical truth
  ...
}
```

A live bridge function, `deriveLegacyStatus()` at `packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts:412`, translates the canonical 8-state enum back into the 18-state legacy enum on every read. It is called extensively throughout `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` (~2077 LOC) and `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` (~2829 LOC), and downstream by CLI/web formatters.

This is a backwards-compat shim from an incomplete migration. Consequences:

- Every state mutation must preserve two representations that can drift.
- New contributors face two vocabularies for the same concept (e.g. `terminated` vs `killed`/`cleanup`/`errored`; `working` vs `pr_open`/`ci_failed`/`review_pending`/...).
- The `deriveLegacyStatus()` bridge encodes status-selection logic (e.g. preserving `cleanup`/`errored`/`killed` when canonical says `terminated`) that is effectively a second small state machine living outside the primary lifecycle.
- Contributes heavily to `lifecycle-manager.ts` complexity flagged in #1341.

## Proposed change

Collapse to a single state model. Concretely:

1. Decide the target shape. The canonical 8-state `CanonicalSessionState` is the smaller/cleaner surface. The 10 extra `SessionStatus` values are a mix of:
   - PR/CI projections (`pr_open`, `ci_failed`, `review_pending`, `changes_requested`, `approved`, `mergeable`, `merged`) — these belong on `PRStateRecord` (already present in `CanonicalSessionLifecycle.pr`), not on session state.
   - Termination sub-reasons (`killed`, `errored`, `cleanup`) — these belong on `CanonicalSessionReason` (already present).
   - Ephemeral (`spawning`) — maps to `not_started` + a reason.
2. Migrate callers (CLI formatters, web dashboard mappers, SCM-derived columns) to read from `lifecycle.session.state` + `lifecycle.pr.state` + `lifecycle.session.reason` directly. Dashboard column mapping and CLI status strings can be derived by a single view helper instead of two enums.
3. Delete `SessionStatus`, `Session.status`, and `deriveLegacyStatus()`. Update persistence in `metadata.ts` to stop writing the derived status field.
4. Update `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES` and other status-keyed sets to use canonical states / reasons.

Expected win: `lifecycle-manager.ts` and `session-manager.ts` each lose a meaningful slice of conditional logic; the state machine becomes 8 states with orthogonal PR/runtime axes instead of 18 conflated states.

This is a breaking change to the core `Session` shape. It should be paired with a changeset and a brief migration note for external plugin authors (though the `Session` consumers inside plugins almost all read `session.status` only for logging, which is easily migrated to `lifecycle.session.state`).

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit, April 2026, cross-validated between Claude sub-agents and Codex review.

## Related issues

- #1341 Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots — catalogs the 16-state machine and the 450-line `determineStatus()` as complexity hot spots; this issue is one concrete simplification from that catalog.
- #344 (closed) Bug: session statuses mix lifecycle, activity, and merge readiness — closed without merging a fix; documented the same overloading of `SessionStatus` with PR/merge concerns that this refactor removes at the root.
- #855 Proposal: Replace split-brain architecture with durable JSONL append-only event log — different concern (persistence), but complementary: collapsing to a single state model makes an event log schema much cleaner.

title: refactor(core): split session-manager.ts (2829 lines) into focused modules
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` is 2829 lines and interleaves many unrelated responsibilities in a single closure returned from `createSessionManager()`. Responsibilities currently co-located:

- Session spawning (`spawn`, line 1083; `spawnOrchestrator`, line 1426) — ~640 LOC combined
- Session identity reservation (`reserveNextSessionIdentity`, line 755; `listRemoteSessionNumbers`, line 723)
- Kill / cleanup (`kill` line 1852; `cleanup` line 1965) — ~275 LOC
- Restore (`restore` line 2560) + `remap` (line 2535)
- PR claiming (`claimPR` line 2411) — ~120 LOC
- OpenCode-specific session operations: `deleteOpenCodeSession`, `fetchOpenCodeSessionList`, `discoverOpenCodeSessionIdsByTitle`, `discoverOpenCodeSessionIdByTitle`, `resolveOpenCodeSessionReuse`, `ensureOpenCodeSessionMapping` (118 occurrences of `opencode` in the file)
- Runtime/process enrichment (`ensureHandleAndEnrich`, `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState`)
- Metadata I/O and session ↔ metadata conversion helpers
- `list` / `listCached` / `get` / `send`

This is a god-object. It's difficult to review changes safely, difficult to unit-test any single responsibility in isolation, and it's the #1 spider file in the core package per the architecture audit (#1341 — 16 direct module dependencies, 33% of core LOC when combined with `lifecycle-manager.ts`).

CLAUDE.md constraint C-04 caps component files at 400 lines. That rule is scoped to web components, but the underlying principle (reviewability, testability) applies equally here — this file is ~7× that ceiling.

## Proposed change

Extract sibling modules from `session-manager.ts`, each owning one responsibility. The public `createSessionManager()` factory stays in `session-manager.ts` and composes them:

1. **`opencode-session-ops.ts`** — all OpenCode-specific helpers: `deleteOpenCodeSession`, `fetchOpenCodeSessionList`, `discoverOpenCodeSessionIdsByTitle`, `discoverOpenCodeSessionIdByTitle`, `resolveOpenCodeSessionReuse`, `ensureOpenCodeSessionMapping`. OpenCode plumbing is already siloed (imports from `opencode-session-id.ts`, `opencode-agents-md.ts`) — it does not belong in the generic session manager.
2. **`pr-claim.ts`** — `claimPR` (line 2411) and its supporting logic. Self-contained: takes a session + PR URL, updates metadata.
3. **`session-restore.ts`** — `restore` (line 2560) and `remap` (line 2535). Restore logic has its own invariants (workspace exists, agent supports `getRestoreCommand`) that deserve isolated tests.
4. **`session-spawn.ts`** (optional, larger lift) — `spawn` and `spawnOrchestrator` plus `reserveNextSessionIdentity` / `listRemoteSessionNumbers`. Largest single block (~900 LOC) and the one with the most branching.
5. **`session-runtime-enrichment.ts`** (optional) — `ensureHandleAndEnrich`, `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState`, `metadataToSession`.

After step 1–3 alone, `session-manager.ts` drops from 2829 → ~1800 lines with clearly-delineated test boundaries. Steps 4–5 would bring it under 1000.

Constraints for the split:
- Public API of `createSessionManager()` (consumed by CLI, web, lifecycle-manager) must not change. This is a pure internal refactor.
- No new plugin slots, no new abstractions — just file-level decomposition.
- Each extracted module gets its own `__tests__/` file so the responsibility can be tested without constructing a full SessionManager.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. The file was also flagged in #1341's Backend Complexity Hot Spots analysis as the largest and most fan-out-heavy module in core.

## Related issues

- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (identifies `session-manager.ts` as the top spider file; this issue proposes a concrete split for the session-manager half of that finding)
- #1169 — refactor(core): port architectural gaps from closed PR #905 (orthogonal — config/registry surface, not session-manager internals)
- #767 — Refactor: Break down Dashboard.tsx (same pattern, applied to the web package)

title: refactor(cli): split 1827-line start.ts into focused subcommands/helpers
body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` has grown to **1827 lines** with **29 internal helper functions** handling at least six distinct responsibilities in a single module:

1. URL cloning + `agent-orchestrator.yaml` auto-generation for new projects
2. Dashboard (Next.js) startup + port management / dev-mode detection
3. Orchestrator session spawning + lifecycle polling
4. Interactive runtime/agent selection prompts
5. OpenClaw credential wiring and notifier provisioning
6. Preflight checks for `tmux`, `git`, `gh` CLI

The result is a spider file that:
- Is hard to unit test (helpers are not exported, and the entry point does I/O, prompts, and process spawning in one call)
- Duplicates logic that would be reusable from other commands (e.g. `ao spawn`, `ao dashboard`, `ao init` could share bootstrap/preflight/dashboard helpers)
- Makes every `ao start` bug fix (#1279, #1256, #1102, #1141, #986, #640, #1359) land in the same hot file, amplifying merge conflicts across the many open bugs currently targeting it
- Puts orchestrator bootstrap logic in the CLI layer where web/API callers cannot reuse it

## Proposed change

Split `start.ts` along its actual responsibilities. A plausible decomposition:

- **`commands/start.ts`** (thin orchestrator, <200 lines): argument parsing + top-level flow only
- **`commands/start-dashboard.ts`** / `lib/dashboard-bootstrap.ts`: Next.js startup, port management, dev-mode detection, stale-cache handling
- **`commands/init-config.ts`** / `lib/config-bootstrap.ts`: URL clone + `agent-orchestrator.yaml` generation (reusable from `ao init` / cwd-registration flow in #1141)
- **`lib/orchestrator-bootstrap.ts`** (moved to `@aoagents/ao-core`): orchestrator session spawn + lifecycle polling, so web/API can reuse it
- **`lib/preflight.ts`**: tmux / git / gh CLI availability checks (already partially reusable)
- **`lib/interactive-prompts.ts`**: runtime/agent selection prompts
- **`lib/openclaw-credentials.ts`**: OpenClaw wiring (already its own concern)

Each module gets its own focused tests. `start.ts` becomes a composition of the above.

This is a pure refactor — no behavior change, no new config surface. It should land before (or alongside) the next round of `ao start` bug fixes to reduce conflict surface.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit April 2026, cross-validated Claude + Codex. Verified:

- `wc -l packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` → 1827
- 29 internal helper functions in the file
- Six distinct responsibility clusters enumerated above

This aligns with the direction of #1341 (Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots), which flagged `session-manager.ts` (2801 LOC) and `lifecycle-manager.ts` (1997 LOC) as spider files. `start.ts` is the CLI-layer equivalent — same anti-pattern, same remediation.

## Related issues

- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (parallel problem in core)
- #1279 — `ao start` in folder A shows dashboard of project B (touches start.ts)
- #1256 — `ao start` URL clone hangs on SSH host-key prompt (touches clone path)
- #1141 — auto-offer to register cwd when `ao start` finds no matching project (would reuse init-config helper)
- #1102 — `ao start` opens stale orchestrator session instead of picker
- #986 — `ao start`: clear stale Next.js cache on version upgrade (touches dashboard path)
- #1359 — `ao start` goes to orchestrator selector instead of last used orchestrator
- #1188 — upgraded CLI silently attaches to stale daemon (touches dashboard/daemon path)

title: refactor(core): split lifecycle-manager.ts (2077 lines) into focused modules
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` has grown to **2077 lines** and mixes multiple unrelated concerns in a single file:

- Polling loop
- State machine transitions
- Reaction engine (events -> side effects)
- PR enrichment caching
- Event emission
- Escalation logic

Complexity is amplified by the dual-state-representation bridge — the file carries `deriveLegacyStatus` calls that translate between `CanonicalSessionState` and `SessionStatus` (see #1414). That extra conversion layer threads through most of the branching logic here.

`CLAUDE.md` itself already flags this file as having "subtle state dependencies" and calls out editing it as a high-risk activity:

> When editing `lifecycle-manager.ts` or `session-manager.ts`: state which invariants your change preserves. These files have subtle state dependencies.

A file of this size with this many concerns makes invariants hard to reason about and raises the cost of every change.

## Proposed change

Split `lifecycle-manager.ts` into focused modules. Suggested extractions:

- **Reaction engine** -> its own class/module. The pattern of "event happens -> run configured reactions (send to agent, notify, escalate)" is cohesive and can live behind a small interface.
- **PR enrichment cache** -> its own module. The caching + invalidation logic for `PREnrichmentData` is orthogonal to lifecycle state transitions.
- **Escalation logic** -> its own module. Retry counters, human-escalation timers, and "stuck" detection are self-contained.

The remaining `lifecycle-manager.ts` would own only the polling loop + state machine transitions + orchestration of the extracted pieces — a much smaller, easier-to-audit surface.

This is a mechanical refactor: no behavior change, existing tests should continue to pass, and the public API of `LifecycleManager` stays stable.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviewers.

Verified evidence:
- `wc -l packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` -> 2077 lines
- Issue #1341 independently measured the same file at ~1997 LOC and listed it as one of the two \"spider files\" with 14+ direct imports from core modules
- `determineStatus()` alone is ~450 lines of nested conditionals (#1341)

## Related issues

- #1414 — refactor(core): unify `CanonicalSessionState` and `SessionStatus` — eliminating the dual state representation will remove the `deriveLegacyStatus` bridge threaded through this file and make the split cleaner.
- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (identifies `lifecycle-manager.ts` and `session-manager.ts` as the two backend spider files).
- #1413 — refactor(core): consolidate duplicate `PREnrichmentData` / `BatchObserver` declarations (sibling slop-audit refactor).
- #1412 — Finish deprecation of `Agent.detectActivity()` (sibling slop-audit refactor).

title: refactor(scm-github): split oversized index.ts and graphql-batch.ts into per-resolver modules
body:
## Problem

Two files in `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/` have grown past the point of being testable and navigable in isolation:

| File | Lines |
|------|-------|
| `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` | 1065 |
| `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` | 1025 |

Both hold batch-resolver orchestration plus query builders and response parsers, so unit-testing any one resolver requires standing up the full module. This also makes review of targeted changes (e.g. one PR field, one CI check) harder than it needs to be.

## Proposed change (per-resolver split)

Split `graphql-batch.ts` into per-resolver modules, and factor out the shared pieces:

- `graphql/batch-runner.ts` — batching loop, rate-limit handling, error aggregation
- `graphql/resolvers/pr-enrichment.ts` — PR state + checks + reviews resolver
- `graphql/resolvers/reviews.ts` — review comment resolver
- `graphql/resolvers/ci.ts` — CI / check run resolver
- `graphql/resolvers/<next-resolver>.ts` — one file per batch target
- `graphql/query-builders.ts` — shared GraphQL query string builders
- `graphql/response-parsers.ts` — shared response-to-domain-type parsers

Then slim `index.ts` down to the `SCM` interface wiring only, moving webhook parsing, comment filtering, and merge helpers into focused sibling files.

Each resolver module should be independently unit-testable with a mocked Octokit / fetch.

## Context

Surfaced during the codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviewers. This is an internal quality fix — no user-facing behavior change intended.

## Related issues

- #827 — refactor: deduplicate GraphQL batch/cache between scm-github and scm-forgejo. Complementary: that issue extracts the shared utilities across plugins; this issue splits the github-internal resolvers. Doing this split first makes the extraction in #827 cleaner because the per-resolver boundaries are already drawn.
- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots. This is one of the SCM-layer hot spots implied by the 14+ method `SCM` interface noted there.

title: chore(cli): decide fate of `ao project` subcommand — built but unwired
body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts` defines `registerProject_cmd()` — a fully built 183-line portfolio management subcommand with `ls`, `add`, `rm`, `relink`, and `set-default` operations — but it is **never registered** with the CLI.

`packages/cli/src/program.ts`'s `createProgram()` does not call `registerProject_cmd`, and a codebase search confirms there are no call sites outside of tests. The function is effectively dead code that nonetheless sits on disk pretending to be a feature.

This leaves us in a stranded state where neither of the following is true:

- **Option A (ship it):** wire `registerProject_cmd` into `createProgram()` and document `ao project` in `docs/CLI.md` alongside the other commands.
- **Option B (cut it):** delete `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts` and its tests.

Additional smell: the naming convention `registerProject_cmd` is non-standard compared to other command registration functions in this package — suggesting the file may have been partially renamed or never finished.

## Proposed change

Pick a direction and execute. The decision is not obvious from the code alone — it hinges on how we want `ao project` to interact with the multi-project work currently in flight:

- #1389 proposes its own `ao project add|remove|list` surface as part of the config split. If that lands, the existing `registerProject_cmd` is either a useful prototype to extend, or duplicative work that should be deleted before it drifts further from the final design.
- #813 (multi-project architecture) and #1141 (auto-offer to register cwd) both imply that a first-class project management CLI will become more important, not less.

Either outcome is fine, but the current \"built, unwired, undocumented\" state is the worst of all worlds — maintenance cost with no user-visible value.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex. Codex confirmed no call sites outside tests after a repo-wide search.

Evidence:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts:31` — `registerProject_cmd()` defined with `ls`/`add`/`rm`/`relink`/`set-default` subcommands.
- `packages/cli/src/program.ts` — `createProgram()` never invokes `registerProject_cmd`.
- No call sites anywhere in the repo outside of `__tests__`.

## Related issues

- #1389 — refactor(config): split monolithic yaml; explicitly proposes a new `ao project add|remove|list` surface that overlaps with the stranded command.
- #813 — feat: multi-project architecture (config, sessions, dashboard, CLI).
- #1141 — feat(cli): auto-offer to register cwd when `ao start` finds no matching project.
- #1169 — refactor(core): port architectural gaps from closed PR #905.

title: chore(cli): remove deprecated 'ao init' command
body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` registers a deprecated `ao init` command that:

- Prints a deprecation warning directing users to `ao start`
- Calls `createConfigOnly()` from `./start.js` (it does *not* delegate to the full `ao start` flow)

Meanwhile, `ao start` already handles auto-config creation on first run in an unconfigured repo, making `ao init` redundant. The command adds to the visible CLI command surface (shows up in `ao --help`), confuses new users with a deprecation warning, and keeps a dead code path alive.

## Proposed change

Remove the `init` command entirely:

1. Delete `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`.
2. Remove the `registerInit(program)` call from the CLI entrypoint.
3. If `createConfigOnly()` is still considered valuable as a standalone action (config generation without launching the full orchestrator), expose it via `ao start --init-only` instead of keeping a separate top-level command. Otherwise, inline it or drop it if only `ao init` used it.
4. Add a changeset noting the removal. Users on the deprecation warning path have already been told to use `ao start`.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit, April 2026. Cross-validated by Claude and Codex. Codex correction on the original finding: the `init` shim does not delegate to the full `ao start` flow — it only calls `createConfigOnly()` — but the behavior is still replaceable by `ao start` (or an `--init-only` flag).

Evidence:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:4` — the entire command body is a deprecation notice + `createConfigOnly()` call.
- Description already reads `[deprecated] Use 'ao start' instead — it auto-creates config on first run`.

## Related issues

- #984 (closed) — `ao start: add interactive init prompt for humans, print ao init for agents`. Context around how `ao start` should behave on a missing config; this proposal is the follow-through that retires the separate `init` entry point.
- #985 (closed) — `ao init: too many prompts — auto-detect defaults and skip confirmation`. Argued for making `ao init` painless; removing it outright is the stronger version of that fix now that `ao start` handles first-run setup.
- #236 (closed) — `fix(cli): ao init missing sessionPrefix, name, and port validation`. Historical validation bug in the same command, further evidence the surface has been drifting.

title: chore: remove orphan root-level files and stale .gitignore entries
body:

title: Decide fate of the Terminal plugin slot — semi-vestigial with no non-test consumers
body:
## Problem

The `Terminal` plugin slot is registered as one of the 8 core plugin slots (per `CLAUDE.md`), but it has **no non-test consumers in the app**. It's a slot in search of a use case.

**Evidence (cross-validated by Claude + Codex review on current `main`):**

- `Terminal` interface is registered as one of the 8 plugin slots in `packages/core/src/types.ts` (4 methods).
- No app call sites for the `Terminal` interface exist outside tests.
- Dashboard uses `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` directly — it opens an xterm.js + WebSocket connection to the tmux PTY and **bypasses the plugin entirely**.
- `ao open` bypasses terminal plugins entirely — it delegates to OS-specific shell commands rather than dispatching through `Terminal.open()` or similar.
- `packages/plugins/terminal-web/` is a ~52-line stub that only logs URLs to the console.
- `packages/plugins/terminal-iterm2/` is registered but is not actually orchestrating the dashboard or `ao open` flows.

Per `CLAUDE.md`:

> \"Plugin slots are the extension point. Don't add configuration surface when a new plugin is the right answer.\"

A plugin slot with no consumers is the inverse: configuration surface without an extension point. It adds interface surface, test maintenance, and cognitive load for plugin authors reading the docs, while providing zero real extensibility today.

## Proposed change (decision required)

Pick one; the status quo is the worst of both worlds.

**Option 1 — Delete the `Terminal` plugin slot entirely.**
- Remove the `Terminal` interface and slot registration from `packages/core/src/types.ts`.
- Remove `packages/plugins/terminal-web/` and `packages/plugins/terminal-iterm2/`.
- Update `plugin-registry.ts`, config schema, and `CLAUDE.md` (\"8 Slots\" → \"7 Slots\").
- `ao open` and the dashboard terminal remain where they are — they already work without the slot.

**Option 2 — Actually wire the dashboard and `ao open` through the plugin.**
- Route `DirectTerminal.tsx`'s connection logic through `Terminal.open()` / equivalent.
- Route `ao open` through the plugin so `terminal-iterm2` (and future `terminal-tmux-attach`, `terminal-kitty`, `terminal-wezterm`, etc.) can override the OS-shell fallback.
- Make `terminal-web` a real implementation rather than a stub.
- Justify the slot by adding at least one additional implementation that wouldn't have been possible without the abstraction.

Option 1 is the simpler answer unless someone has a concrete near-term user for Option 2. If neither option has an owner, Option 1 should be the default.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. This is part of a broader sweep for plugin slots / interfaces / deprecations that were added speculatively and never fully consumed — same category as #1412 (`Agent.detectActivity()` deprecated-but-required).

## Related issues

- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots. Lists `Terminal` as a 4-method interface in the plugin-slot utilization table but does not debate its fate; this issue is the focused follow-up.
- #1412 — Finish deprecation of `Agent.detectActivity()`. Same class of \"interface surface that outlived its consumers.\"
- #1275 — `code-review` plugin slot proposal. Counter-example: a *new* slot being proposed only after concrete consumers exist. Worth contrasting with Terminal's current state.
- #769 — Refactor: Break down `DirectTerminal.tsx` (756 lines). Any Option 2 work would overlap.
- #1387, #975, #1197, #1221, #1248 — open dashboard-terminal bugs. None of these would be fixed by Option 2 alone; they're `DirectTerminal.tsx` / xterm.js / WS issues, orthogonal to the plugin-slot question.

title: Extract duplicated hasRecentCommits() helper into @aoagents/ao-core
body:
## Problem

Two agent plugins have byte-identical copies of a `hasRecentCommits(workspacePath)` helper that shells out to `git log --since=60 seconds ago` to check whether the agent has produced new commits in the last ~60s. This is straight copy-paste — the implementations differ only in their surrounding comments.

**Locations:**
- `packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts` lines 38–49
- `packages/plugins/agent-cursor/src/index.ts` lines 39–50

Both use the same `execFileAsync` call, same args (`["log", "--since=60 seconds ago", "--format=%H"]`), same 5s timeout, same swallow-error-return-false semantics.

As more agent plugins adopt git-commit-based activity detection (a natural signal for agents without native JSONL), this duplication will keep growing.

## Proposed change

Extract to `@aoagents/ao-core` as a shared utility so any agent plugin can import it:

```ts
// packages/core/src/git-activity.ts
export async function hasRecentCommits(
  workspacePath: string,
  windowSeconds = 60,
): Promise<boolean>;
```

- Add re-export from `packages/core/src/index.ts`
- Update `agent-aider` and `agent-cursor` to import from core and delete their local helpers
- Keep the signature generic (parameterize the window) so future agents aren't locked into 60s

This matches the pattern already established for other shared agent-plugin helpers (`recordTerminalActivity`, `classifyTerminalActivity`, `getActivityFallbackState`, `normalizeAgentPermissionMode`, etc.) exported from core.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit April 2026, cross-validated Claude + Codex. A small, low-risk cleanup — no behavior change, just deduplication and a clearer extension point for future agent plugins that need git-commit-based activity signals.

## Related issues

- #783 — Extract shared `isProcessRunning` + `normalizePermissionMode` into core (same pattern: agent-plugin helpers duplicated across plugins should live in core)
- #9 — Cross-cutting convention audit, explicitly calls out duplicated code across agent plugins as a problem to fix

title: Consolidate recordActivity() thin-wrapper duplication across agent plugins
body:
## Problem

Three agent plugins implement `recordActivity()` as an identical 5-line thin wrapper around the core helper `recordTerminalActivity()`. The method is a required interface member, so every new agent plugin that uses the AO Activity JSONL pattern has to copy-paste this same snippet.

**Evidence (verified on current `main`):**

- `packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts:220-225`
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:624-630`
- `packages/plugins/agent-cursor/src/index.ts:317-322`

All three are the same delegation:

```ts
async recordActivity(session: Session, terminalOutput: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!session.workspacePath) return;
  await recordTerminalActivity(session.workspacePath, terminalOutput, (output) =>
    this.detectActivity(output),
  );
}
```

`recordTerminalActivity` is already exported from core (listed under "Core Utilities Available to Plugins" in `CLAUDE.md`) and already does the classify + dedup + append work. The per-plugin wrapper contributes nothing beyond forwarding `this.detectActivity` as the classifier and null-checking `workspacePath`.

This is systematic duplication: the plugin-authoring guide in `CLAUDE.md` even documents the 5-line body as the canonical way to implement `recordActivity`, which is a strong signal that it belongs in core, not in every plugin.

## Proposed change

Two reasonable options — either is fine, (b) is smaller and preferred:

**(a) Core helper plugins alias**

Export a ready-made `recordActivityViaTerminal(classifier)` factory from core that returns the standard `recordActivity` implementation. Plugins become:

```ts
recordActivity: recordActivityViaTerminal((output) => detectActivity(output)),
```

**(b) Make `recordActivity` optional with a sensible default**

Change the `Agent` interface in `packages/core/src/types.ts` to make `recordActivity` optional. Lifecycle manager's caller already needs a null check for plugins using native JSONL (Claude Code) — extend that path so that when `recordActivity` is absent but `detectActivity` is present, core calls `recordTerminalActivity(workspacePath, output, agent.detectActivity)` itself. Plugins that need custom behavior still override.

Either way, delete the three duplicate wrappers in `agent-aider`, `agent-codex`, and `agent-cursor`, and update `CLAUDE.md`'s "For agents using AO Activity JSONL" section to point at the new helper/default instead of prescribing the copy-paste snippet.

No behavior change — the wrappers are pure forwards today.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. This is a small, mechanical consolidation but it pays off every time a new agent plugin is added (see the open requests for Amp #1016, Droid #1017, Pi #1059, Cline #171, kimicode #1384) — each one currently has to copy this snippet.

## Related issues

- #1412 — Finish deprecation of `Agent.detectActivity()`. These two are adjacent cleanups: #1412 removes the deprecated classifier from the public interface; this issue removes the other redundant boilerplate around the same classification path. Worth coordinating so `recordActivity` and `detectActivity` get cleaned up together rather than churning plugins twice.
- #1016, #1017, #1059, #171, #1384 — open agent-plugin requests that will benefit from less boilerplate when implemented.

title: refactor(web): reconcile duplicate SessionDetailPRCard implementations
body:
## Problem

There are two parallel implementations of `SessionDetailPRCard` in the web package, both rendering the same PR-card UI with the same comment-action state machine (sendingComments / sentComments / errorComments, Ask-Agent-to-Fix flow, branch copy, CI chips, etc.):

1. **Standalone file** — `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetailPRCard.tsx` (349 lines)
   - Exported `SessionDetailPRCard` at line 88
   - Richer API: accepts `lifecyclePrReason`, injected `onAskAgentToFix` handler, `BlockerChip` helper, `cleanBugbotComment` util
   - Appears to be the canonical / newer extraction

2. **Inline component** — `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx:732`
   - Local `function SessionDetailPRCard({ pr, sessionId, metadata })` (~230 lines)
   - Used by `SessionDetail.tsx:602`: `<SessionDetailPRCard pr={pr} sessionId={session.id} metadata={session.metadata} />`
   - Simpler signature, inlines its own fix-comment handler

The standalone file is **exported but never imported** — a grep for `SessionDetailPRCard` shows no importers of the standalone module. Meanwhile `SessionDetail.tsx` shadows the name with a local definition and uses that instead.

This looks like a dead extraction or orphaned refactor. Any future change to PR card behavior must be made twice, or one copy will silently drift from the other.

## Proposed change

1. Confirm which implementation is canonical (the standalone file looks newer / more featureful — `lifecyclePrReason`, injected handler).
2. Update `SessionDetail.tsx` to `import { SessionDetailPRCard } from \"./SessionDetailPRCard\"` and pass through the required props (including `onAskAgentToFix`).
3. Delete the inline `function SessionDetailPRCard` at `SessionDetail.tsx:732` and the surrounding section comment.
4. Verify no behavior regression (comment send flow, CI chip rendering, branch copy, blocker chips).

This also drops ~230 lines from `SessionDetail.tsx`, which helps #770.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit (April 2026). The initial audit missed this — it was caught during Codex cross-validation of the audit findings. The duplication is not obvious from a single-file read because the import site uses an unqualified name that resolves to the local function.

## Related issues

- #770 — Refactor: Break down SessionDetail.tsx (728 lines). Removing the duplicate inline card meaningfully advances that refactor.
- #1287 — Add \"Resolve Conflicts\" action button to SessionDetail PR card. Depends on having a single canonical PR-card implementation to extend.

title: CI: integration tests bypass PR checks — only run on manual dispatch
body:
## Problem

Integration tests are not run on pull requests, so broken integration tests can land on `main` without any PR check flagging them.

Two independent gaps combine to produce the coverage hole:

1. `.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml` runs only on explicit trigger (e.g. `workflow_dispatch`), not on `pull_request` or `push` to `main`.
2. The main `.github/workflows/ci.yml` invokes `pnpm test`, which excludes the integration-tests package. At the root `package.json`, the `test` script filters out `@aoagents/ao-web` and does not include `@aoagents/ao-integration-tests` in the regular unit test sweep.

Net effect: neither workflow exercises the integration suite on PR, so regressions are only caught when someone remembers to manually dispatch the integration workflow.

This is a CI coverage gap, not a code/test-quality gap — the tests themselves exist in `packages/integration-tests/`.

## Proposed change

Wire `pnpm test:integration` (or the equivalent workflow job) into the checks that run on every PR:

- Add a job to `ci.yml` that runs `pnpm test:integration`, OR change `integration-tests.yml` triggers to include `pull_request` and `push: main`.
- Mark it as a required check on `main` once it is stable.
- This likely requires provisioning service dependencies and/or test secrets in CI (e.g. GitHub tokens for tracker/SCM plugins, tmux availability on the runner, any other external services the suite exercises). Scope those out as part of the change.
- If certain integration tests genuinely cannot run in hosted CI (e.g. need a real Claude Code binary), split them into a separate tier that still runs on a cron or manual dispatch, and make the PR-blocking tier explicit.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit April 2026, cross-validated Claude + Codex. The audit was looking for CI / coverage gaps that allow silent regressions onto `main`; this is the clearest instance found.

## Related issues

- #271 — \"Write integration tests and configure CI pipeline\" — older, broader scope (auth/DB/CRUD framing, pre-dates current plugin-based suite). This issue is the narrower, still-open CI-wiring piece specific to the current `packages/integration-tests/` package.

title: refactor(web): introduce useAsyncAction hook to consolidate sending/sent/error + timer cleanup pattern
chore(lint): enforce C-04 (400-line component limit) mechanically via ESLint max-lines
body:
## Problem

`CLAUDE.md` declares constraint **C-04: Component files max 400 lines**, but nothing in the repo mechanically enforces it. Today the rule lives only in the contributor doc, so it is routinely violated — and the violations keep growing instead of shrinking.

Current offenders (well over the 400-line cap):

| File | Lines | Has split issue |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | 2829 | #1415 |
| `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` | 2077 | #1417 |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` | 1827 | #1416 |
| `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` + `graphql-batch.ts` | ~1065 + ~1025 | #1418 |
| `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` | 1089 | #770 |
| `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` | 951 | #769 |
| `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` | 3363 | #771 |

Without mechanical enforcement, every new PR can add a 500-line file and no reviewer notices until it becomes another god-file. C-04 is a toothless guideline.

## Proposed change

Add a `max-lines` rule to the root `eslint.config.js` flat config:

```js
{
  rules: {
    \"max-lines\": [\"error\", { max: 400, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }],
  },
}
```

Apply it broadly (core, cli, web, plugins). Use file-level overrides for the existing known offenders so CI stays green while the split issues proceed:

```js
{
  files: [
    \"packages/core/src/session-manager.ts\",
    \"packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts\",
    \"packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts\",
    \"packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts\",
    \"packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts\",
    \"packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx\",
    \"packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx\",
  ],
  rules: { \"max-lines\": \"off\" },
}
```

Or, equivalently, an inline `// eslint-disable-next-line max-lines` / `/* eslint-disable max-lines */` at the top of each offender. The override list *is* the migration TODO list — removing an entry from the array should become part of the acceptance criteria for each split PR.

Relax the cap for test files (`**/__tests__/**`, `**/*.test.ts{,x}`) — test files legitimately grow large due to fixtures and aren't read the same way as production code. A value like `800` or `\"off\"` is appropriate there.

Benefits:
- (a) Stops new god files from landing — any PR that pushes a file past 400 lines now fails CI, forcing the author to either split or add an explicit override (which a reviewer must approve).
- (b) The override list is a visible, auditable migration ratchet. Every entry corresponds to an open split issue; removing entries is the definition of done.
- (c) Gives C-04 the same teeth as the other ESLint rules (`no-explicit-any`, `consistent-type-imports`) already have.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. Same audit produced #1415, #1416, #1417, #1418 (file splits) — this issue is the policy sibling that prevents the problem from recurring after those splits land.

## Related issues

- #1415 — refactor(core): split session-manager.ts (2829 lines) into focused modules
- #1417 — refactor(core): split lifecycle-manager.ts (2077 lines) into focused modules
- #1416 — refactor(cli): split 1827-line start.ts into focused subcommands/helpers
- #1418 — refactor(scm-github): split oversized index.ts and graphql-batch.ts into per-resolver modules
- #770 — Refactor: Break down SessionDetail.tsx
- #769 — Refactor: Break down DirectTerminal.tsx
- #771 — Refactor: Split globals.css (3,363 lines) into modular stylesheets
- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (background motivation)

title: chore(ci): add unused-exports / dead-code detection (knip) to catch stranded code pre-merge
body:
## Problem

We have no mechanical check for unused exports or stranded dead code. Fully built but unwired modules can (and do) ship to `main` without anyone noticing.

Concrete example: `registerProject_cmd` in `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts:31` — a 183-line command surface (`ls`/`add`/`rm`/`relink`/`set-default`) shipped to `main` but was never wired into `createProgram()` in `packages/cli/src/program.ts`. No call sites outside its own tests. Nothing in our CI caught it. See #1419.

A mechanical unused-export detector would have flagged this at PR time. Without one, \"built, unwired, undocumented\" code accumulates quietly and raises the maintenance cost of the repo.

## Proposed change

Add [`knip`](https://knip.dev/) to the repo and run it in CI.

Why `knip` over `ts-prune`:

- Monorepo-aware out of the box (understands pnpm workspaces and `workspace:*`).
- Detects unused files, exports, dependencies, and binaries — broader surface than `ts-prune`'s export-only view.
- Actively maintained; first-class Next.js and Vitest plugins (we use both).
- Config-driven entry points — we can mark plugin entry files, Next.js routes, and `packages/core/src/index.ts` as entries and suppress their exports being flagged.

Rollout plan:

1. Add `knip` as a root devDependency, commit a `knip.json` with explicit entry points:
   - `packages/core/src/index.ts` (public API — all exports are entries)
   - `packages/*/plugins/*/src/index.ts` (plugin default exports)
   - `packages/web` — use the Next.js plugin (App Router routes, API routes, layouts, `globals.css`)
   - `packages/cli/src/index.ts` and the `ao` bin
   - Vitest test globs
2. Add a `pnpm knip` script and a CI job (advisory-only on first run).
3. Triage the initial report — expect false positives from public APIs, plugin entries, and Next.js conventions. Tune config, not code.
4. Flip CI job to required once the report is clean.

`ts-prune` is the lighter alternative if `knip` proves too noisy to tame, but given the workspace layout `knip` is the better starting bet.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex. The `registerProject_cmd` finding is the motivating data point — a tool like `knip` would have reported an unused export at `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts:31` and the stranded command would never have reached `main`.

## Related issues

- #1419 — chore(cli): decide fate of `ao project` subcommand — built but unwired. Direct motivating example: knip would have flagged this before merge.
- #1420 — chore(cli): remove deprecated `ao init` command (adjacent dead-code cleanup).
- #1421 — chore: remove orphan root-level files and stale `.gitignore` entries (adjacent dead-code cleanup).

title: Enforce deprecation decay — require `@deprecated` to include a cutoff version or removal date
body:
## Problem

Code marked `@deprecated` lingers indefinitely in this codebase because nothing tracks *when* it should actually be removed. The JSDoc tag is treated as documentation rather than a commitment, so deprecated surface area accumulates: plugin authors keep implementing deprecated methods to satisfy interfaces, callers keep invoking deprecated paths, and the cleanup only happens when someone notices during an audit.

**Evidence (verified on current `main`):**

- `packages/core/src/types.ts:483` — `Agent.detectActivity()` is `@deprecated` in favor of `getActivityState()`, but is still a **required** method on the interface and still called from 3 places (`lifecycle-manager.ts:604`, `session-manager.ts:2167`, `cli/src/commands/send.ts:58`). Every agent plugin must implement it. No cutoff version or removal date was recorded when it was deprecated, so it has drifted.
- `packages/core/src/types.ts:1558-1581` — `LegacyAgentPermissionMode` retains a deprecated `"skip"` alias for `"permissionless"`. JSDoc says "deprecated" but gives no version, no removal date, and no issue link. There is no signal to anyone reading the code when (or whether) this alias will actually go away.

These are just two examples surfaced in a single audit pass. The pattern is systemic: `@deprecated` without a decay marker is effectively permanent.

## Proposed change

Adopt a deprecation policy and enforce it with a lightweight CI check.

**Policy:** every `@deprecated` JSDoc tag must include a removal commitment. Pick one of two forms:

- `@deprecated v2.0 — use getActivityState()` (version cutoff)
- `@deprecated removeBy=2026-Q3 — use getActivityState()` (date cutoff)

Optionally include a `(#1412)` tracking-issue reference pointing at the removal ticket.

**Enforcement:** a simple grep-based CI check is sufficient to start — no custom ESLint rule needed. Something like:

```bash
# Fails if any @deprecated line lacks a version (v*) or removeBy= marker.
rg -n '@deprecated\b' packages --type ts \
  | rg -v '@deprecated\s+(v\d|removeBy=)' \
  && { echo 'Found @deprecated without cutoff'; exit 1; } \
  || exit 0
```

Wire it into the existing lint GitHub Actions workflow. If the grep approach proves noisy, upgrade to a custom ESLint rule later — but the grep is a one-line policy that catches new offenders immediately.

**Migration:** one-time sweep to annotate or remove the existing `@deprecated` tags (there are only a handful). For `detectActivity()`, annotating with a version points directly at #1412 as the removal vehicle.

## Context

Surfaced during the codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. The policy is cheap to introduce, aligns with the \"Surgical Changes\" and \"Simplicity First\" principles in `CLAUDE.md`, and makes deprecation a commitment rather than a suggestion.

## Related issues

- #1412 — *Finish deprecation of `Agent.detectActivity()`* — the canonical concrete example. A decay marker on the original `@deprecated` tag would have tracked this to completion automatically.
- #1420 — *remove deprecated `ao init` command* — same pattern at the CLI layer: a command kept behind a deprecation warning with no removal milestone.

title: ci: detect unused CSS custom properties in globals.css (warn-only)
body:
## Problem

`packages/web/src/app/globals.css` defines a large number of `--color-*` design tokens (and other custom properties). Over time, tokens drift from actual usage:

- Likely-dead status tokens surfaced during audit: `--color-status-respond`, `--color-status-review`, `--color-status-pending`
- Various `--color-accent-*` entries, some of which duplicate the same hex value under different names
- Backwards-compat aliases such as `--color-bg-primary`, `--color-border-muted` that may no longer have callers

There is no automated signal when a token becomes unreferenced, so dead tokens accumulate silently and `globals.css` grows (see #771 for the broader size problem). `DESIGN.md` is the stated source of truth for the design system, but the CSS tokens drift from the doc over time with no enforcement.

## Proposed change

Add a small CI check (grep/node script, no new deps) that:

1. Parses `--color-*` (and optionally all `--*`) definitions from `packages/web/src/app/globals.css`.
2. Greps `packages/web/**/*.{tsx,ts,css}` (and any other consumers) for usages: `var(--color-foo)` and direct `--color-foo` references.
3. Reports any defined tokens with zero references.
4. Optionally flags multiple token names that resolve to the same hex value as potential duplicates.

Ship as **warn-only** initially (non-failing CI step, or a `pnpm run lint:css-tokens` job that posts a comment / logs a summary) so legitimately-reserved tokens don't block merges. Once the baseline is clean, flip to failing.

Nice-to-haves (not required for v1):
- Cross-reference against `DESIGN.md` so tokens documented there are always considered \"used\".
- Output a grouped report (dead / duplicate-hex / undocumented) to make cleanup PRs easy to scope.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated between Claude and Codex. The audit flagged the tokens listed above as strong candidates for removal, but manual cleanup is brittle without a check that keeps the list honest going forward. This is a low-risk, high-signal CI addition.

## Related issues

- #771 — Refactor: Split globals.css (3,363 lines) into modular stylesheets. Complementary: de-duping before splitting reduces churn in the refactor.

title: test(plugins): enforce non-trivial interface implementations across all plugins
body:
## Problem

Current plugin tests verify *structural* conformance (`create()` returns an object whose methods match the interface shape) but not *behavioral* conformance. A plugin can pass CI while being an effectively empty stub.

Motivating example: `packages/plugins/terminal-web/src/index.ts` is a 52-line file shipped in a \"done\" state. Its `attach()` implementation only `console.log`s the web terminal URL — the plugin is never actually plumbed through the web runtime, yet all existing tests pass because the method exists and returns the correct shape. This was only discovered during a manual slop audit.

The same failure mode can (and likely does) exist in other plugin slots. There is no guard-rail that catches a method body consisting of `return null`, `return \"\"`, `return true`, or a single `console.log` when the interface expects real work.

## Proposed change

Pick one (or combine) of the following:

1. **Runtime behavioral test harness** — a single test file in `packages/integration-tests` that loads every plugin from the registry, calls `create()`, and runs each required method against canned fixtures. Assertions target observable behavior (e.g. runtime `spawn` must actually start a process / return a usable handle; tracker `getIssue` must hit a mocked API and parse the response; terminal `attach` must return a non-stub attachment descriptor).
2. **AST stub-detector** — lint rule or standalone script that scans `packages/plugins/*/src/**/*.ts` and flags methods required by the plugin's declared slot whose body is exclusively `console.log(...)`, `return null`, `return \"\"`, `return true`, `return undefined`, or empty. Gate CI on zero violations (with an explicit allowlist for methods documented as optional no-ops).
3. **Required-methods coverage table** — for each of the 8 plugin slots, enumerate in `CLAUDE.md` (or a dedicated `docs/plugin-contract.md`) the methods that MUST do real work vs. the methods that may legitimately be no-ops. Enforce via (1) or (2) above so the table doesn't rot.

Option 2 is cheapest, option 1 is strongest; a hybrid (AST gate in CI, behavioral test for the critical runtime/agent/scm/tracker slots) would give the best ratio.

## Context

Surfaced during the codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by both Claude and Codex reviewers. The `terminal-web` finding is a concrete instance of a class of bug — plugins passing shape checks without delivering behavior — that the current test suite cannot detect.

## Related issues

- #1422 — Decide fate of the Terminal plugin slot — semi-vestigial with no non-test consumers (same audit; `terminal-web` is the motivating example here)
- #10 — Add comprehensive test coverage across all packages (this issue is a specific sub-problem: shape vs. behavior)
- #1135 — Dashboard does not load third-party agent plugins — activity/summary always null (another \"plugin loads but does nothing\" failure mode)
