title: ETag Guard treats HTTP 304 as error — spams terminal warnings
body:
## Bug

Both ETag guard functions (`checkPRListETag` and `checkCommitStatusETag` in `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts`) treat HTTP 304 Not Modified as a failure.

### Root Cause

`execFileAsync("gh", args)` throws when `gh` exits non-zero. The `gh` CLI exits with code 1 on HTTP 304 responses, printing `gh: HTTP 304` to stderr.

The code that checks `output.includes("HTTP/2 304")` at lines 357 and 419 is **dead code** — the promise rejects before reaching those checks.

The catch blocks log warnings like:
```
[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator: Command failed: gh api ...
gh: HTTP 304
```

And return `true` (assume changed), defeating the entire ETag caching optimization — every 304 triggers a full GraphQL re-fetch.

### Fix

In both catch blocks, check if error message contains "304" and return `false` instead:

```ts
catch (err) {
    const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
    if (errorMsg.includes("304")) {
      return false; // Not modified — ETag cache hit
    }
    console.warn(`[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}`);
    return true;
}
```

### Impact
- Terminal spam on every poll cycle when no PRs have changed
- Unnecessary GraphQL API calls (wasting rate limit budget)
- ETag optimization completely bypassed

title: fix(scm-github): handle gh CLI exit code 1 on HTTP 304 in ETag guards
body:
## Problem

Both ETag guard functions treat HTTP 304 Not Modified as a failure, spamming warnings on every poll cycle:

```
[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator: Command failed: gh api ...
gh: HTTP 304
```

## Root Cause

`execFileAsync("gh", args)` throws when `gh` exits non-zero. The `gh` CLI exits with code 1 on HTTP 304 — so the promise rejects *before* reaching the `output.includes("HTTP/2 304")` checks at lines 357/419, making that code **dead code**.

The catch blocks then:
1. Log a warning (the terminal spam)
2. Return `true` (assume changed) — defeating ETag caching entirely

## Fix

In both guard catch blocks, check if the error message contains `"304"` and return `false` (not modified) instead of logging + returning `true`.

## Impact
- ✅ Eliminates terminal spam during idle periods
- ✅ Restores ETag caching optimization (saves GraphQL rate limit)
- ✅ No behavioral change for actual errors — still logs + returns `true`

Closes #1482

title: Stale enrichment cache causes CI failure / merge conflict injection loop
body:
## Bug Report

**Severity:** High — causes continuous noise to agents, wasting tokens and distracting from real work.

**Symptom:** Agents receive repeated "CI is failing" and "merge conflicts" messages even when their PRs have passing CI and are mergeable. The agent dismisses the messages, but they keep coming every poll cycle.

## Root Cause

Two interacting problems create an infinite oscillation loop:

### 1. Status Oscillation Clears Dedup State (`lifecycle-manager.ts`)

When status oscillates between `ci_failed` and a non-failing state:

- **`maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()`** (lines 1332-1343): When `newStatus !== "ci_failed"`, it **clears** `lastCIFailureFingerprint`, `lastCIFailureDispatchHash`, `lastCIFailureDispatchAt`. Next time status returns to `ci_failed`, the dedup guard treats it as a brand-new failure.

- **`maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()`** (lines 1527-1533): Same pattern — when `hasConflicts` flips from `true` to `false`, it clears `lastMergeConflictDispatched`. Next oscillation to `true` re-dispatches.

- **`checkSession()`** (line 1697): Every `newStatus !== oldStatus` transition fires the full reaction pipeline again, including `executeReaction()` which sends the message to the agent.

### 2. Enrichment Cache Data Oscillates (`graphql-batch.ts`)

The 2-guard ETag strategy does not guarantee cache freshness:

- `prEnrichmentDataCache` (LRU, line 140) persists across poll cycles
- When ETag guards say "no changes" → stale cached data is returned
- But `prEnrichmentCache.clear()` (line 346) in lifecycle-manager is per-poll
- Guard 1 (`checkPRListETag`) uses `per_page=1` — a single PR update can flip the entire repo ETag, causing all PRs to be re-fetched. Between refreshes, the persistent cache serves stale data.

## The Oscillation Cycle

```
Poll N:   Stale cache → ciStatus=failing → status=ci_failed → send "CI failing" to agent
          Agent responds: "Already verified, all PRs pass CI"

Poll N+1: Fresh GraphQL data (Guard 1 triggered) → ciStatus=passing → status=pr_open
          → maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails() CLEARS dedup metadata (lines 1336-1341)

Poll N+2: ETag guard says "no changes" → stale cache → ciStatus=failing → status=ci_failed
          → Transition fires AGAIN (dedup was cleared) → sends "CI failing" AGAIN

Poll N+3: Fresh data → status=pr_open → clears dedup AGAIN
→ Loop forever
```

## Recommended Fix: Don't clear dedup on status transitions

In `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()`, do NOT clear the fingerprint/dispatch hash when transitioning away from `ci_failed`. The fingerprint comparison already handles legitimate state changes — if CI is now passing, `failedChecks` will be empty (line 1367: `if (failedChecks.length === 0) return`), and when it truly fails again with the same checks, the fingerprint will match and be skipped.

Same for `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()` — don't clear `lastMergeConflictDispatched` when conflicts resolve.

**Files to change:**
1. `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — Remove/modify the dedup clearing in `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails()` (lines 1332-1343) and `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()` (lines 1527-1533)

title: bug(web): DirectTerminal can't find session — ao-web resolver doesn't know about the project-name segment in tmux session names
body:
## Summary

`ao-web`'s `resolveTmuxSession` fails to locate any tmux session created by `ao-core` whenever the project's `storageKey` contains a project-name segment (the common case). The dashboard logs `can't find session: <sessionId>` and the terminal never attaches, even though the tmux session exists and the agent is running.

The two packages disagree on the tmux session naming format:

- **`ao-core` writes** names as `{storageKey}-{prefix}-{num}`, where `storageKey` is typically `{hash}-{projectName}` — e.g. `361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1`.
- **`ao-web` reads** names assuming the format `{hash}-{sessionId}` — it strips exactly 13 characters (`{12hex}-`) and does an equality check against the user-facing session id.

Because the project-name segment sits between the hash and the user-facing session id, the equality check always fails, and `resolveTmuxSession` returns `null`.

## Reproduction

1. `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@0.3.0`
2. Create a project config with a `sessionPrefix` that differs from the project key, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   projects:
     smx-foundation:
       name: smx-foundation
       sessionPrefix: sf
       path: /Users/me/smx-foundation
       defaultBranch: main
   ```
3. `ao start`
4. Observe in the logs:
   ```
   ✔ Orchestrator session created
   Orchestrator: http://localhost:3000/projects/smx-foundation/sessions/sf-orchestrator-1
   [direct-terminal] [MuxServer] New mux connection
   [direct-terminal] can't find session: sf-orchestrator-1
   ```
5. `tmux ls` confirms the session actually exists, with the project-name segment embedded:
   ```
   361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1: 1 windows (...)
   ```
6. Open `http://localhost:3000/projects/smx-foundation/sessions/sf-orchestrator-1` — the terminal pane never attaches.

## Root cause

### Generator (ao-core)

`packages/core/src/paths.ts` (compiled: `ao-core/dist/paths.js:132-134`):

```js
function generateTmuxName(storageKey, prefix, num) {
    return `${requireStorageKey(storageKey)}-${prefix}-${num}`;
}
```

`storageKey` is the directory key used under `~/.agent-orchestrator/`. In practice it's `{hash}-{projectName}` — e.g. `361287ebbad1-smx-foundation` — which is confirmed both by the on-disk directory layout:

```
~/.agent-orchestrator/361287ebbad1-smx-foundation/sessions/sf-orchestrator-1
```

and by `session-manager.js` using `generateTmuxName(project.storageKey, orchestratorPrefix, num)` at the reservation site (line 612 in 0.3.0's compiled output).

So the tmux name for orchestrator #1 of project `smx-foundation` (prefix `sf`) is:

```
361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1
```

### Resolver (ao-web)

`packages/web/src/server/tmux-utils.ts` (compiled: `ao-web/dist-server/tmux-utils.js:74-83`):

```js
const output = execFn(tmuxPath, ["list-sessions", "-F", "#{session_name}"], { ... });
const sessions = output.split("\n").filter(Boolean);
const match = sessions.find(
  (s) => HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s) && s.substring(13) === sessionId,
);
```

where `HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN = /^[a-f0-9]{12}-/`.

For `sessionId = "sf-orchestrator-1"` and `s = "361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1"`:

- `HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s)` → `true`
- `s.substring(13)` → `"smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1"`
- `"smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1" === "sf-orchestrator-1"` → `false`

No match → `resolveTmuxSession` returns `null` → `DirectTerminal` logs `can't find session: sf-orchestrator-1`.

`parseTmuxName` in `ao-core/dist/paths.js:139-148` has the same blind spot — its regex `^([a-f0-9]{12})-([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)-(\d+)$` will greedily lump the project name into the `prefix` capture, which means any consumer relying on `parseTmuxName().prefix === project.sessionPrefix` is also broken.

## Impact

- Web dashboard terminal attachment is fully broken for any project where `storageKey !== hash` (i.e. any project whose directory includes the project name — the default on 0.3.0).
- Likely affects every orchestrator/worker session in a multi-project or even single-project install, not just orchestrators. The format mismatch is universal; my repro happened to be the orchestrator because that's the first session the dashboard tries to attach.
- Related issue #1456 references the format as `{projectHash}-{sessionId}`, which is also incorrect — confirming the format contract is under-specified across the codebase.

## Suggested fix

Pick one canonical format and align both sides:

**Option A (minimal, compatible with existing on-disk names):** Teach the resolver that the segment between the hash and the user-facing session id can be a project-name slug. The one-line patch that unblocked my install:

```diff
- const match = sessions.find((s) => HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s) && s.substring(13) === sessionId);
+ const match = sessions.find(
+   (s) =>
+     HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s) &&
+     (s.substring(13) === sessionId || s.substring(13).endsWith(`-${sessionId}`)),
+ );
```

The `endsWith` check is safe because `HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN` already gates the hash, and `sessionId` is already validated against `SESSION_ID_PATTERN` upstream. `parseTmuxName` should get an analogous fix (parse the trailing `{prefix}-{num}` off the end, treat everything between the hash and that as the project slug).

**Option B (cleaner contract):** Have `generateTmuxName` take a bare `hash` argument instead of `storageKey` so the on-wire name is truly `{hash}-{sessionId}` and matches the resolver as written. This is a breaking change to existing tmux session names and would require migration.

Option A is the correct tactical fix for 0.3.1; Option B is the right long-term direction if the team wants the naming invariant to hold without implicit project-name plumbing.

## Workaround

Patch `ao-web/dist-server/tmux-utils.js` in the global install with the diff above, then `kill $(pid from ~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json); rm -f ~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json; ao start`. Confirmed working on 0.3.0.

## Environment

- `@aoagents/ao@0.3.0` (global npm install)
- `@aoagents/ao-core@0.3.0`, `@aoagents/ao-web@0.3.0` (all subpackages on 0.3.0)
- macOS 26.4.1 (ARM, M2 Max)
- Node v25.9.0
- tmux 3.6a (Homebrew, `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux`)

title: fix(web): resolve tmux sessions when storageKey is wrapped ({hash}-{projectName})
body:
## Summary

Closes #1486.

`ao-core` names tmux sessions as `{storageKey}-{sessionId}`, where `storageKey` is either a bare 12-hex hash or the legacy wrapped form `{hash}-{projectName}` (e.g. `361287ebbad1-smx-foundation`). The web resolver only handled the bare-hash form, so DirectTerminal logged `can't find session: <sessionId>` and never attached for any project whose storageKey includes a project-name segment — the default on 0.3.0.

## Fix

The resolver now looks up the owning `storageKey` on disk from `~/.agent-orchestrator/{storageKey}/sessions/{sessionId}`, then asks tmux for the exact `{storageKey}-{sessionId}` name via `has-session -t =`. The on-disk record is the authoritative disambiguator.

Design points:

- **No endsWith matching.** An earlier attempt using `substring(13).endsWith(`-${sessionId}`)` was flagged (review) as ambiguous: a bare session `{hash}-my-app-1` would falsely match a lookup for `app-1`. The on-disk lookup is unambiguous.
- **All candidates probed, not just the first.** If multiple projects happen to own the same `sessionId` on disk, each is checked against tmux in turn so a stale metadata dir can't shadow the live session of another project.
- **Permissive wrapped-suffix pattern.** `STORAGE_KEY_PATTERN` accepts any non-empty suffix after the hash (`^[a-f0-9]{12}(-.+)?$`), because legacy storageKeys are built from `basename(projectPath)` and can contain spaces or unicode. Safe because `storageKey` is passed to `execFileSync` which bypasses the shell.
- **Bare-hash fallback retained.** If the on-disk record is missing (e.g. scrubbed filesystem), the tmux-listing path still recovers bare-hash sessions with the same exact-remainder check as before — no behavior regression there.

## Known pre-existing limitation (not in scope)

If two different projects both have the same `sessionId` *and* both tmux sessions are live, the resolver returns the first match. This is identical to the prior bare-hash behavior (documented by the `returns first match when multiple hash-prefixed sessions exist for same ID` test). A proper fix requires threading `projectId` from the URL through the mux protocol to the resolver — tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [x] 90 unit tests pass, including new cases for wrapped storageKey, ambiguity safety, multi-candidate probing, unicode/space project names, and extraneous AO-base entries.

title: resolveTmuxSession: cross-project sessionId collision — thread projectId through mux protocol
body:
## Summary

When two different projects on the same machine have both (a) the same user-facing `sessionId` (e.g. both have `ao-1`) and (b) live tmux sessions, `resolveTmuxSession` in [packages/web/server/tmux-utils.ts](packages/web/server/tmux-utils.ts) returns the first match. The dashboard terminal may attach to the wrong project's session.

This is a pre-existing limitation. The prior bare-hash code had identical behavior via `Array.find(...)`, documented by the existing test `"returns first match when multiple hash-prefixed sessions exist for same ID"`. It was surfaced during review of #1486 / #1488 but intentionally deferred from that PR to keep scope surgical.

## Root cause

The mux WebSocket protocol's `terminal.open` message carries only `id: string` — no project context — so the resolver has nothing to disambiguate with:

```ts
// packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts
{ ch: "terminal"; id: string; type: "open" }
```

The browser URL at the call site is `/projects/{projectId}/sessions/{id}`, so the information exists; it's just not plumbed through.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `openTerminal` (client-side, [packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx](packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx)) takes `(id, projectId)`.
2. The `terminal.open` protocol message carries `projectId`. Update both `ClientMessage` in [packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts](packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts) and its duplicate in [packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts](packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts).
3. `TerminalManager.open(id, projectId)` forwards `projectId` to `resolveTmuxSession`.
4. `resolveTmuxSession(sessionId, tmuxPath, execFn, fs, projectId?)` uses `projectId` to look up the owning `storageKey` directly (via the config service or by matching directory names), bypassing the scan of `~/.agent-orchestrator/*`.
5. Update the existing `"returns first match when multiple hash-prefixed sessions exist for same ID"` test to assert project-scoped behavior instead.
6. Add a test for the collision case: two projects with the same sessionId, each with a live tmux session — the resolver must pick the one matching the caller's `projectId`.

## Context

- Original bug: #1486
- Fix (scope-limited): #1488
- Review discussion that surfaced this: three-round Codex review during #1488, round 3 P1.

## Impact

Low in practice — requires a multi-project install with a sessionId collision. But the failure mode (attaching to the wrong project's terminal) is confusing and hard to detect.

title: fix(cli): hide legacy second positional from ao spawn help
body: ## Issue `ao spawn --help` shows a `[second]` positional argument even though `ao spawn` only supports zero or one positional argument. The optional positional is the issue identifier; project selection is handled by auto-detection or by the supported prefixed issue form. If users pass more than one positional argument, AO should reject the command with a direct arity error. The important message is that only one argument is accepted and two were passed, for example: ```text ✗ `ao spawn` accepts at most 1 argument, but 2 were provided. Use: ao spawn [issue] ao spawn ``` > [!NOTE] > The following is the fix spec for AI agents. ## Steps 1. Open `packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts` and confirm how Commander renders the hidden second positional. 2. Update the command definition so `ao spawn --help` no longer exposes `[second]` as a public argument. 3. If more than one positional arg is provided, return a concise arity error that says `ao spawn` accepts at most 1 argument and reports how many were provided. 4. Use standard CLI syntax in user-facing help/errors: `[issue]` for the optional issue argument, not ``. 5. Add or update focused CLI command tests around the help output and the too-many-arguments error. 6. Run the narrowest relevant validation for `@aoagents/ao-cli`. 7. Commit only the CLI command/test files required for this fix. ## Validation - Package-level test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` - Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` - Manual smoke check: `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js spawn --help` - Manual smoke check: `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js spawn 1234 2234` ## Constraints - Keep the scope inside `packages/cli` unless Commander requires a tiny shared helper. - Preserve current supported inputs: `ao spawn`, `ao spawn 123`, `ao spawn INT-100`, `ao spawn project-id/123`, and `ao spawn sessionPrefix/123`. - Do not reintroduce `ao spawn ` as supported syntax. - Do not use angle brackets for optional positional args in user-facing examples or help text. - Do not frame the second positional as backwards-compatible behavior; it should only produce a clear too-many-arguments error. ## Acceptance - `ao spawn --help` no longer presents `[second]` as a public argument. - The documented argument name is clear, preferably `[issue]` instead of `[first]`. - `ao spawn 1234 2234` exits without spawning and prints a concise error that says only one argument is accepted and two were provided. - The suggested replacement syntax uses `ao spawn [issue]`, not `ao spawn `. - Focused tests cover both the help output and the too-many-arguments error.

title: fix(web): pin dashboard Next.js workspace root
body:
## Issue

Starting the AO dashboard in foreground mode currently prints a Next.js workspace-root inference warning when another lockfile exists above the repository checkout. The dashboard still starts, but the foreground logs include noisy warning output before `Ready`.

Observed from the complaint screenshot:

```text
[next] ⚠ Warning: Next.js inferred your workspace root, but it may not be correct.
[next] We detected multiple lockfiles and selected the directory of /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json as the root directory.
[next] To silence this warning, set `outputFileTracingRoot` in your Next.js config, or consider removing one of the lockfiles if it's not needed.
[next] Detected additional lockfiles:
[next]   * /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/agent-orchestrator/pnpm-lock.yaml
```

The PR that resolves this issue must make a code/config change in the repo so the warning does not appear again the next time foreground dashboard logs are watched. It should not rely on manually deleting a user-level lockfile.

## Affected Package

- Package path: `packages/web`
- npm package: `@aoagents/ao-web`
- Surface area: dashboard startup / Next.js config / foreground `ao dashboard` logs
- Shared code touched: none expected unless investigation shows the dashboard launch path needs it

## Environment

- AO version: `0.2.5`
- Affected package version: `0.2.5`
- OS: macOS
- Node.js: `v22.22.2`
- pnpm: `9.15.4`
- Browser: not applicable; warning is emitted in foreground server logs

## Reproduction

1. Use a checkout at `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/agent-orchestrator` with the repo `pnpm-lock.yaml` present.
2. Have another lockfile above the checkout, such as `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json`.
3. From the repo root, run `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard`.
4. Watch the foreground logs as the Next.js dev server starts.

## Current Result

Next.js prints a workspace-root inference warning and says it selected the parent directory containing `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json` as the root directory, with the repo `pnpm-lock.yaml` listed as an additional lockfile.

## Expected Result

The AO dashboard startup path should pin the intended Next.js workspace/tracing root for this monorepo so foreground dashboard logs start cleanly without the workspace-root inference warning.

## Evidence

- `packages/web/next.config.js` currently has no `outputFileTracingRoot` setting.
- Local filesystem evidence from the complaint environment has `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json` above the checkout and `pnpm-lock.yaml` in the repo root.
- The visible startup command was `packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard`.

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. Open `packages/web/next.config.js` and the dashboard launch path used by `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard`.
2. Trace why Next.js is inferring the parent directory instead of the AO repository root when multiple lockfiles exist.
3. Fix the root cause with the smallest possible code/config change, likely by setting the Next.js output file tracing root to the repository root from `packages/web/next.config.js`.
4. Add or update focused validation if there is a practical way to assert the config behavior.
5. Run the narrowest relevant validation for `@aoagents/ao-web` and any touched package.
6. Verify foreground startup logs no longer contain `Next.js inferred your workspace root` when running the dashboard with the parent lockfile still present.
7. Commit only the required config/code changes and closely related tests. No unrelated cleanup.

## Validation

- Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`
- Web package test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test`
- Foreground smoke check: `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard` from the repo root while `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json` still exists above the checkout

## Constraints

- Keep the scope inside `packages/web` unless shared CLI startup code must change to fix the bug correctly.
- Do not fix this by asking users to remove parent-directory lockfiles.
- Preserve existing public APIs, config shapes, dashboard routes, and plugin contracts.
- Prefer a minimal surgical edit over a dashboard startup refactor.
- Note follow-up work separately instead of expanding scope inside this issue.

## Acceptance

- Running `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard` from the repo root starts the dashboard without printing `Next.js inferred your workspace root`.
- The validation must be done with the parent lockfile still present, so the fix proves the repo handles this environment directly.
- The PR contains an actual code/config change that prevents the warning in future foreground logs.

title: feat: ao backlog — unified view of sessions, PRs, reviews, and issues
body:
## Problem

There's no single command that gives you a complete picture of what's happening and what needs attention. Right now you have to:

- `ao status` to see sessions
- Check GitHub manually for PRs awaiting your review
- Check GitHub for your open PRs and their CI/review status
- Check GitHub for issues assigned to you
- Attach to individual sessions to see what they're doing

This is fragmented. When you're orchestrating multiple agents across issues and PRs, you need one unified view.

## Proposed: `ao backlog`

A command that **spawns a dedicated agent session** to gather all relevant data and produce a comprehensive HTML dashboard.

### How it works:

1. `ao backlog` spawns a new session (like `ao spawn`)
2. The session's agent gathers all data:
   - Reads AO session metadata (status, branch, PR, reports, activity)
   - Captures tmux pane content for active/stuck sessions
   - Fetches GitHub data via `gh` CLI: open PRs, review requests, assigned issues, CI status, latest comments
3. Produces a beautiful HTML dashboard file
4. Opens it in the browser

### What the dashboard should include:

**1. Session Overview**
- All active/stuck sessions with branch, PR, CI, activity state, last report
- Captured terminal snapshots for sessions that need attention

**2. Needs My Review**
- Open PRs requesting your review
- Whether you've already responded
- Latest comments/activity

**3. My Open PRs**
- Your open PRs with CI status, review status
- Unaddressed review comments
- Which are mergeable

**4. My Issues**
- Issues assigned to you / authored by you (open)
- Labels, priority, last activity

**5. Action Items**
- "PR 123 is approved + CI green — ready to merge"
- "PR 456 has changes requested"
- "Session ao-42 is stuck"
- "3 PRs waiting for your review"

### UX

```bash
ao backlog                    # Spawn session, generate HTML, open in browser
ao backlog --repo owner/repo  # Override repo (default: current project)
```

The spawned session handles all the heavy lifting — fetching, analyzing, and rendering. The HTML file gets saved to a known location (e.g., `~/.ao/{project}/backlog/report.html`) and opened automatically.

### Why spawn a session?

- The agent can use its full capabilities (gh CLI, file I/O, tmux capture, skills like /frontend-design)
- It's consistent with AO's model — everything is a session
- The agent can make judgment calls about what's important and how to present it
- It can generate a much richer HTML report than a static CLI formatter

## Why This Matters

- Orchestrating multiple agents means your attention is the bottleneck — you need to know where to focus
- Reduces context-switching between `ao status`, GitHub UI, and individual sessions
- Enables a "start of day" workflow: run `ao backlog`, get full situational awareness
- Replaces ad-hoc manual report generation

title: fix(cli): ao stop <project> tears down shared host instead of just the named project
body:
## Bug

`ao stop <project>` kills the shared `ao start` parent process and dashboard, taking down ALL projects and the web UI — instead of just stopping the named project's orchestrator session.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1489612265027014736/1491735678156013588/1497595099201404969
**Reported by:** @Priyanchew
**Analyzed against:** `f674422a`

## Reproduction

1. Config with two projects in one `agent-orchestrator.yaml`
2. `ao start` (one parent process hosts lifecycle workers and dashboard)
3. `ao stop project-2`

**Expected:** Only project-2's orchestrator session ends. Dashboard, lifecycle poller for project-1, and the shared host stay up.

**Actual:** Project-2's orchestrator stops ✓, but the shared `ao start` parent process is SIGTERM'd, the dashboard is killed, and `running.json` is wiped. Project-1 loses lifecycle polling (no more state transitions, CI checks, review forwarding) and the dashboard goes dark.

## Root Cause

In `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`, `registerStop()` (line 1570) unconditionally tears down the host after killing the targeted orchestrator session:

```
// Line 1668-1676 — runs REGARDLESS of whether a specific project was named
if (running) {
  process.kill(running.pid, "SIGTERM");  // kills the SHARED ao start process
  await unregister();                      // deletes running.json
}
await stopDashboard(running?.port ?? port); // kills the dashboard
```

This block runs in ALL non-`--all` code paths — including when a specific project is named via `ao stop <project>`. There's no conditional that says "skip the host teardown if the user targeted a single project."

The comment at lines 1660-1664 explains the original design intent:
```
// Lifecycle polling runs in-process inside the `ao start` process
// (registered via running.json). Sending SIGTERM to that PID below
// triggers the shared shutdown handler in `lifecycle-service`, which
// stops every per-project loop.
```

This was written assuming `ao stop` always means "full teardown." But the `[project]` arg and the orchestrator session lookup (lines 1610-1658) make it clear the command is supposed to support per-project stops. The unconditional parent kill contradicts the per-project logic above it.

### Secondary gap: no `stopLifecycleWorker(projectId)`

`lifecycle-service.ts` only exports `stopAllLifecycleWorkers()` — there's no per-project stop function. The `active` map is in-process, so a separate `ao stop` CLI invocation can't call into it directly. This means even if we skip the parent PID kill, the lifecycle worker for the stopped project keeps running (harmless — it polls sessions, finds no orchestrator, does nothing — but wasteful).

## Fix

### Immediate (minimal, correct)

Guard the host teardown behind "no specific project was named":

```typescript
// In registerStop(), lines 1660-1676 — wrap the teardown:
const targetedStop = projectArg !== undefined;
if (!targetedStop) {
  // Full teardown: kill parent, stop dashboard, unregister
  if (running) {
    try { process.kill(running.pid, "SIGTERM"); } catch {}
    await unregister();
  }
  await stopDashboard(running?.port ?? port);
}
```

This makes `ao stop` (no args) and `ao stop --all` do full teardown, while `ao stop <project>` only kills the orchestrator session. The lifecycle worker for the stopped project becomes a harmless no-op (polls sessions, finds none for its orchestrator, does nothing).

### Follow-up (proper per-project lifecycle stop)

1. Add `stopLifecycleWorker(projectId: string)` to `lifecycle-service.ts`
2. Add a file-based IPC signal: `ao stop <project>` writes `~/.agent-orchestrator/stop-lifecycle-{projectId}`, parent checks in poll loop
3. Or add a `DELETE /api/lifecycle/{projectId}` HTTP endpoint on the dashboard server

## Impact

- **Severity:** High — multi-project users lose ALL projects and dashboard when stopping just one
- **Affected:** Anyone running AO with 2+ projects in one config
- **Workaround:** None — `ao stop <project>` always kills the host

## Related

- #92 — `ao stop` logs "Dashboard stopped" even when no dashboard was running (related but different issue)
- #1129 — `ao stop` doesn't kill child agent sessions (also a `stop` scoping issue)

title: fix(cli): scope ao stop <project> to named project only
body:
## Summary

`ao stop <project>` was unconditionally killing the shared `ao start` parent process, dashboard, and `running.json` — taking down ALL projects and the web UI when only one project was targeted.

**Root cause:** `registerStop()` had no conditional to distinguish per-project stops from full teardowns. The parent PID kill and dashboard stop ran on every code path.

**Fix:** Guard the host teardown (parent PID kill + dashboard stop + unregister) behind `projectArg !== undefined`. When a specific project is named, only its orchestrator session is killed. Full teardown (`ao stop` / `ao stop --all`) continues to work as before.

The lifecycle worker for the stopped project becomes a harmless no-op — it polls sessions, finds no orchestrator, does nothing.

Fixes #1495

## Test Plan

- [ ] Single project config: `ao stop` → full teardown (dashboard + parent killed) ✓
- [ ] Multi-project config: `ao stop <project>` → only that project's orchestrator stops, dashboard and other projects stay up ✓
- [ ] `ao stop --all` → full teardown ✓
- [ ] `ao stop <nonexistent>` → error, no collateral damage ✓

title: fix(web): pin Next.js workspace root to silence startup warning
body:
## Problem

Starting the AO dashboard in foreground mode prints a Next.js workspace-root inference warning when another lockfile exists above the repository checkout:

```
⚠ Warning: Next.js inferred your workspace root, but it may not be correct.
We detected multiple lockfiles and selected the directory of ~/package-lock.json as the root directory.
```

## Fix

Add `outputFileTracingRoot` to `packages/web/next.config.js`, pointing it at the monorepo root via `path.join(__dirname, "../..")`. This is the canonical Next.js solution — it tells Next.js exactly which directory is the workspace root, bypassing the heuristic that triggers when it finds lockfiles in parent directories.

## Changes

- `packages/web/next.config.js`: Added `import path` + `import { fileURLToPath }` + `outputFileTracingRoot: path.join(__dirname, "../..")` to the config object.

## Testing

- Config resolves correctly: `outputFileTracingRoot` → `/path/to/agent-orchestrator` (repo root containing `pnpm-lock.yaml`)
- Could not run `agent-ci` locally — `aoagent` user lacks Docker group membership (`EACCES /var/run/docker.sock`). CI will validate.
- Change is a pure config addition with no code logic changes.

Closes #1492

title: ui(sidebar): rework project row — info density, action button overflow, degraded state polish
body:
## Context

`packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` (currently 791 lines) renders both project rows and session rows inline. The project row in particular has a few rough edges that are worth a focused pass.

## Observations

1. **Hit-target crowding** — each project row packs: chevron + name + count badge + Dashboard icon + Orchestrator icon + kebab menu. That's 5 interactive targets in one row, plus the toggle area. On narrower sidebars they jostle before the active state even paints.
2. **Action icon discoverability** — the Dashboard (grid) and Orchestrator (org-chart) icons live without labels. Users won't know what they are without hovering. Consider hiding them behind hover/focus, or moving them into the kebab menu.
3. **Collapsed mode has no per-project expansion** — a project with 30 sessions shows the first 5 + `+25`, but you can't expand without un-collapsing the whole sidebar. A hover/click flyout would help.
4. **Degraded variant is jarring** — uses warning-triangle in place of the chevron, an inline pill, and a "Config needs repair" subnote, but offers no way to fix from the sidebar (the Repair flow lives elsewhere). Either link directly into the repair modal or keep the row collapsed and silent until the user opens it.
5. **Active project styling** is only an amber color shift on the toggle text — easy to miss when the eye is scanning. Consider a left border/accent or background.
6. **\"+\" button placement** — the only way to add a project is the `+` next to the "Projects" header. There's no equivalent affordance to spawn a session from inside a project row; users have to navigate to the dashboard. Worth deciding whether the project row should host a per-project "spawn session" action.
7. **Component size** — at 791 lines, `ProjectSidebar.tsx` brushes the 400-line cap in CLAUDE.md. Extracting a `ProjectRow` (and `SessionRow`, sibling issue) would make iteration easier.

## Out of scope

Session row redesign — tracked in a sibling issue.

## Suggested next steps

- Brainstorm a denser project row layout (single hit target + secondary actions on hover/in menu).
- Decide whether per-project session spawn belongs here.
- Extract `ProjectRow` into its own file as part of the change.

title: ui(sidebar): rework session row — info density, filter clarity, grouping, active state
body:
## Context

The session row inside `ProjectSidebar.tsx` (sibling to the project-row issue) shows very little per session and has a few interaction quirks worth a focused pass.

## Observations

1. **Sparse info per row** — currently: colored dot (attention level) + branch-humanized title + lowercase status word. There's no PR number, no CI/review state, no last-activity timestamp, no agent kind, no issue label. To know anything beyond "is it working", users must click into the detail page. Decide what the minimum useful row is.
2. **Level word duplicates the dot** — the dot color and the trailing word both encode attention level. One of them is redundant; the freed space could carry richer info (PR #, CI badge, age).
3. **`Show session ID` is the only display option** — gated behind a gear popover that holds exactly that one checkbox. Consider folding the toggle inline with the killed/done toggles or removing the popover entirely.
4. **Killed/done filter asymmetry** — `showDone` reveals killed sessions too (they go through the `done` attention branch), so the two toggles overlap in confusing ways. Footer toggles are also icon-only (skull / check) with no labels — non-obvious without hovering.
5. **No grouping inside a project** — sessions are interleaved in arrival order. Grouping by attention level (`respond > review > working > pending > merge > done`) would let users see what needs human action at a glance.
6. **Active session has no strong visual mark** — only an amber title color. No left bar, no background. Easy to lose place when scanning a long list.
7. **`action` attention level is dead code** in the sidebar — `getAttentionLevel` is called without a mode, so `detailed` wins and `action` never appears. Either drop the branch or opt the sidebar into simple mode.
8. **Loading state is global** — when `sessions === null`, every project shows skeletons even if only one is loading. Per-project loading isn't tracked.
9. **`SessionDot` glow** is the only visual heartbeat. No progress, no token/cost hint, no time-in-state — could surface more without much real estate.
10. **Hover tooltip is just `aria-label="Open <title>"`** — a richer tooltip (PR, CI, last activity) would be high-leverage.

## Out of scope

Project row redesign — tracked in a sibling issue.

## Suggested next steps

- Decide on the minimum-viable info per row, then design density variants (compact / standard / detailed).
- Resolve the killed/done filter overlap.
- Extract `SessionRow` into its own file.

title: ui(sidebar): rework footer row — filter toggles, settings popover, theme toggle
body:
## Context

The bottom row of `ProjectSidebar.tsx` (lines ~680–782) crams four unrelated controls into a single horizontal strip: a "show killed" toggle (skull icon), a "show done" toggle (check icon), a gear that opens a popover, and the global `ThemeToggle`. It feels like a junk drawer.

## Observations

1. **Heterogeneous controls in one row** — two filter toggles (per-sidebar state), one settings popover (display preference), and one global app-wide toggle (theme) all share the same visual weight. Nothing tells the user that the theme toggle is global vs. the others are sidebar-scoped.
2. **Icon-only toggles, no labels** — skull = killed, check = done. Non-obvious without hovering. The pressed state (`--active`) is the only signal that they're stateful at all.
3. **Filter overlap with `showDone`** — see sibling issue (#1500); `showDone` also reveals killed sessions, making the two toggles feel redundant.
4. **Settings popover holds a single checkbox** — the entire gear → popover → label flow exists for one option (`Show session ID`). Either inline it as a third toggle or fold it into a richer "View" menu when there's actually more than one option.
5. **Theme toggle placement is incidental** — it lives here because there's no other obvious place, but the sidebar footer is a strange home for an app-global control. Could move to a top-level account/settings menu, or at least visually separate it (divider, right-justify, smaller).
6. **No labels in collapsed mode** — when the sidebar collapses, the footer disappears entirely (collapsed render path returns early), so killed/done filters and theme become unreachable until the user expands. Worth deciding whether the collapsed rail should keep these controls.
7. **Density wastes the only sticky-bottom row in the sidebar** — this is prime real estate (always visible, anchored). Today it shows four icons. Could host a session count summary, a search affordance, or a "spawn session" button.

## Suggested directions

- Replace the icon row with a labeled "View" / "Filter" menu (single button → dropdown) so behavior is discoverable and the footer regains breathing room.
- Move theme toggle to a global place (header, account menu) and use the sidebar footer for sidebar-scoped concerns only.
- Decide what *should* live in this anchored row — search, spawn, status summary — once the legacy controls move.

## Related

- #1499 (project row rework)
- #1500 (session row rework — filter overlap)

title: ui(kanban): rework SessionCard footer + visual hierarchy
body:
## Context

`packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` (1056 lines) renders the kanban card. The footer in particular is awkward — the leftmost label (`footerStatus` from `getFooterStatusLabel`) is wedged next to the kill button with no visual relationship between the two — but the broader visual hierarchy of the card has accumulated rough edges worth a focused pass.

## Footer issues (the original ask)

1. **Leftmost label is semantically homeless** — `card__status` shows either a 60-char-truncated `userPrompt` or one of several `getFooterStatusLabel` outputs (`mergeable`, `detecting`, `ci failing`, or whatever `getSessionTruthLabel`/`getPRTruthLabel` returns). It mixes prompt content (a *task description*) with lifecycle status (a *state machine label*) in the same slot. They should not share a visual treatment.
2. **Kill button placement is incidental** — the destructive action lives next to a status label, with no visual grouping. The only signal that it's destructive is the icon and `btn--danger` class. Two-step "kill?" confirmation is good; placement is not.
3. **Footer = "everything that didn't fit elsewhere"** — currently houses status text *or* a Merge PR CTA *or* a kill button. The merge CTA is a primary action; the kill is a destructive utility; the label is metadata. Three different priorities, one row, no separation.
4. **Truncation logic lives in JSX** — `userPrompt.slice(0, 60) + "…"` inline. Should be a util, and `60` is arbitrary — at narrow widths it still overflows the kill button.

## Broader visual hierarchy problems

Going top-to-bottom:

5. **Header row competes with itself** — activity dot + session id + restore button + terminal link. Restore and terminal are both pill-shaped controls with similar weight, but they mean different things (restore = revive a dead session, terminal = jump to live tty). The id is mono and dim, but it's the only stable identifier and gets less prominence than the icons.
6. **Title** (`card__title`) is the most important field but has no clear hierarchy advantage over `secondaryText` immediately below — both end up as similar small text in practice.
7. **Meta row** (`card__meta`) mixes branch, PR link, and additions/deletions/size with `·` separators. This is fine in isolation but *also* runs as a meta-chip row in the done-card variant, with different styling — two different layouts for the same information.
8. **`secondaryText` is overloaded** — it's `issueLabel · issueTitle` *or* `issueTitle` alone *or* `summary`. Three different meanings in one slot, distinguished only by which is non-null. The merge variant adds a checkmark icon; nothing else does.
9. **`truthLine`** — three-part lifecycle truth string ("Session X · PR Y · Runtime Z") sits as a 10px tertiary line below secondaryText. Useful for debugging, noisy in normal use; should probably be a tooltip or dev-only.
10. **Rate-limit/CI-passing/alerts/quick-reply stack vertically with no separators** — when a card has alerts *and* passing checks *and* a quick-reply pane, the body becomes a wall of small rows. No grouping.
11. **CI strip duplicates information** — passing checks render as `ci-chip--pass` chips (up to 3), failing checks render as alert rows. Two different visual languages for the same underlying data; users have to learn both.
12. **Alerts max at 3** with no `+N more` overflow indicator. If a PR has 4+ issues, the user silently sees only 3.
13. **Quick-reply pane (`level === "respond"`)** is large (agent message + view-context link + 3 preset buttons + textarea). It dominates the card whenever an agent waits for input. Probably correct prioritization but it makes the card height jump dramatically as level shifts.
14. **Done-card variant is almost a different component** — different padding scale (`px-3.5` vs `px-[10px]`), different chip class names (`done-meta-chip` vs `card__diff`), different status pill, different expand-on-click behavior, different action placement. Consolidating the two variants would be a major win.
15. **Frame/accent system** — `cardFrameClass` × `accentClass` produces a 3 × 5 matrix of border treatments (`merge-frame`, `alert-frame`, `fixed` × `merge`, `working`, `respond`, `attention`, `default`). Cognitive load for users; non-trivial to remember which combination means what.
16. **No persistent "now" signal** — `lastActivityAt` exists in the data model but is never displayed on the card. The activity dot animates ("working") but there's no "5m ago" / "2h ago" anywhere.
17. **Cost / token data not surfaced** — agents track this; cards don't show it.
18. **Component size** — 1056 lines, nearly 3× the 400-line cap. Done-card branch alone is ~210 lines. Extract `DoneSessionCard` and `SessionCardFooter` at minimum.

## Suggested next steps

- Split the footer into two zones: **status indicator** (left, neutral) and **primary action** (right, contextual: merge / kill / nothing). User prompt should not live in the footer at all — promote it to its own slot in the body or drop it (it's already the title source for sessions without an issue).
- Decide what the kanban card's *minimum useful payload* is, then design tiers (compact / standard / expanded) instead of stacking everything.
- Consolidate done variant into the standard card with a `--done` modifier.
- Surface `lastActivityAt` as a relative timestamp in the header.
- Extract `SessionCardHeader`, `SessionCardBody`, `SessionCardFooter`, `DoneSessionCard` into separate files.

## Related

- #1499 (sidebar project row)
- #1500 (sidebar session row)
- #1501 (sidebar footer row)

title: kill() archives sessions instead of terminating in-place — breaks kanban, restore, and orchestrator reuse
body:
## Bug

Killing a session (dashboard kanban, `ao session kill`, or `ao stop`) archives it instead of terminating in-place. The session disappears from the dashboard entirely — not in Done/Terminated — so it can't be restored. `ao start` also spawns a new orchestrator number instead of reusing.

**Note:** Archived sessions **can** be restored via the API (`restore()` reads archived metadata at L2719), but since `list()` doesn't surface them, users can't see or click restore on the dashboard.

**Reported by:** @Ashish, confirmed by @Priyanchew
**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1489353072779423905/1491735678156013588/1497655504913174714
**Checkout:** `2bfcbc64` (origin/main)

## Reproduction

1. `ao start` → orchestrator spawns
2. Kill it (kanban card, `ao stop`, or `ao session kill`)
3. Session vanishes from dashboard — not in Done/Terminated
4. Can't restore because can't see it
5. `ao start` again → new orchestrator number

## Root Cause

`session-manager.ts` `kill()` (line 1991-2102):
- Sets `lifecycle.sessionState = "terminated"` ✅
- Writes metadata update ✅
- **Archives immediately** via `deleteMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, true)` (line 2096) ❌

`list()` (line 1847) only reads active sessions — archived sessions are invisible to the dashboard.

This breaks:
1. **Done/Terminated visibility** — `list()` skips archived, `isDashboardSessionDone()` never runs
2. **Dashboard restore** — session invisible, user can't click restore (API `restore()` handles archives fine at L2719)
3. **Orchestrator reuse** — `ensureOrchestrator()` → `get()` returns null → spawns new number

## Fix

Remove line 2096 — don't archive on kill. Keep terminated session in active directory so it's visible in Done/Terminated and restorable. Let `cleanup()` handle archiving later.

## Files

- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — `kill()` (L1991-2102), `list()` (L1847), `get()` (L1938)
- `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` — `deleteMetadata()` (L265)
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` — session list API
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` — `ao stop` (L1646)

title: Add polished skeleton loading states across the dashboard
body:
## Problem

The dashboard has some skeleton loading states today, but they're inconsistent and visually rough — they don't match the dark theme polish of the rest of the UI and in places the loading state is jarring (layout shift, mismatched dimensions, plain spinners instead of skeletons).

## Goal

Audit and rework loading states across the web dashboard so that every async surface shows a skeleton that:

- Matches the actual rendered content's layout (no shift on load)
- Uses consistent design tokens (colors, radii, shimmer/pulse) from `globals.css`
- Feels cohesive with the dark theme
- Replaces ad-hoc spinners where a skeleton would communicate structure better

## Scope (initial sweep)

- Sidebar: project rows, session rows
- Dashboard: kanban columns / session cards
- Session detail: header, metadata, terminal area, PR/CI panels
- Any modal/drawer that fetches on open

## Suggested approach

1. Inventory current loading states (grep for existing skeletons + spinners + `isLoading`)
2. Define a small set of reusable skeleton primitives (e.g. `SkeletonLine`, `SkeletonBlock`, `SkeletonRow`) in `packages/web/src/components/`
3. Replace existing loading UI surface-by-surface, mirroring real layout dimensions
4. Verify against `DESIGN.md` tokens — no inline styles, no new UI libs

## Out of scope

- Changing data-fetching logic (SSE intervals, etc.)
- Redesigning the components themselves — only their loading state

## Summary

- Read every file in `packages/core/src/` (~35 source files, ~7,000 lines)
- Identified 4 critical, 7 high, and 14 medium severity issues
- Written to `CORE-ANALYSIS.md` in the repo root with file:line references, reproduction steps, and suggested fixes

### Critical findings
- **C-01**: Race condition in session ID reservation (TOCTOU between list scan and atomic reserve)
- **C-02**: Shared `fetchOpenCodeSessionList` promise can't recover from rejection across sessions in same `list()` call
- **C-03**: `determineStatus` mutates session objects in place — shared reference causes state bleeding across poll cycles
- **C-04**: `updateSessionMetadata` reads already-mutated lifecycle state, losing auditability

### High findings
- **H-01**: `atomicWriteFileSync` temp file name collisions across containers with same PID
- **H-02**: Non-atomic read-then-write in `deleteMetadata` archiving
- **H-03**: Double-kill race in concurrent `kill()` calls
- **H-04**: Empty `PRInfo` fields from unparseable URLs cause silent API failures
- **H-05**: `getActivityFallbackState` age-based decay doesn't handle `exited` state
- **H-06**: Activity detection overrides confirmed-dead runtime state (probe_failed → alive)
- **H-07**: `parseKeyValueContent` skips `key=#value` lines as comments

title: docs: deep analysis of web dashboard
body:
## Summary
- Comprehensive audit of `packages/web/src/` covering bugs, stale state issues, missing error boundaries, performance problems, SSE/WebSocket handling issues, caching bugs, and UX gaps
- All findings include `file:line` references and severity ratings

## Key Findings

**6 Critical Bugs:**
- SSE snapshot ignores server-computed attention levels on refresh (useSessionEvents.ts)
- Module-level mutable cache in session detail page shared across navigations (page.tsx:63-67)
- `useSSESessionActivity` opens duplicate SSE connections alongside dashboard SSE
- Session detail page polls 3 endpoints every 5s + SSE (8 requests per 5s cycle)
- `enrichSessionPR` mutates DashboardSession in place, breaking React memo comparison
- Race condition in mux reconnect + terminal re-open

**4 Stale State Issues:**
- Rate limit dismiss never resets across rate limit cycles
- Session activity state disagrees with lifecycle state after SSE patches
- SSE snapshot patches don't update PR data or lifecycle facets
- Done-bar expanded state not reset on session changes

**3 Missing Error Boundaries:**
- No error boundary around SessionDetail or DirectTerminal
- Global error boundary may have no CSS variables loaded

**6 Performance Problems:**
- SSE route calls `sessionToDashboard` every 5s per connected client
- `/api/sessions` enrichment waterfall (metadata → PR, sequential)
- Dashboard computes attention levels twice per session
- Session detail uses `JSON.stringify` for deep equality

**5 SSE/WebSocket Issues:**
- SSE connection has no maximum retry limit
- Mux WebSocket backoff caps at 30s, never gives up
- No ping/pong heartbeat on mux WebSocket
- SSE snapshot races with full refresh
- Mux `sessions` state update on every snapshot

**4 Caching Bugs:**
- `processedIssues` Set never cleared (unbounded growth)
- TTLCache `size()` includes stale entries
- PR cache hit doesn't revalidate rate-limit flag
- Issue title cache has no eviction trigger

**7 UX Gaps:**
- No merge confirmation dialog on session card
- No feedback when kill/restore fails in SessionDetail
- No offline state for terminal when mux disconnects
- No loading skeleton matching final layout

title: feat(cli): add preset system to ao spawn (backlog, triage)
body:
## Summary

Adds a **preset system** to `ao spawn` — predefined, trusted multi-line prompts that bootstrap an agent session for a specific task. First two presets ship in this PR: `backlog` (project-wide analysis) and `triage` (single-issue investigation).

**Usage:**
- `ao spawn --preset backlog` — analyze sessions, PRs, issues; produce reports; instruct orchestrator to spawn agents
- `ao spawn 42 --preset triage` — investigate issue #42; post a structured triage comment

## The preset system

New module `packages/cli/src/presets/` with:
- `Preset` interface — `name`, `description`, `prompt`, `issueArg`
- Preset registry with `resolvePreset()` lookup
- Per-preset issue-arg policy: `"required" | "optional" | "forbidden"` (default: `forbidden`)

Spawn integration:
- New `--preset <name>` flag, mutually exclusive with `--prompt`
- Issue-arg validation is per-preset — specific error messages for both directions
- Preset prompts bypass the 4096-char sanitization limit (trusted multi-line markdown)

## Bundled presets

**`backlog`** (issue arg: forbidden)
- Gathers AO session data via `ao status --reports full --json --include-terminated` (with fallback for older AO versions)
- Fetches GitHub state (open PRs, assigned issues, review requests, changes-requested)
- Produces a timestamped markdown report at `$AO_DATA_DIR/backlog/`
- Sends the orchestrator a prioritized list to spawn agents (changes-requested PRs > assigned issues > review-requested PRs > rest)
- Generates a self-contained HTML dashboard
- Cross-platform browser open instructions

**`triage`** (issue arg: required)
- Reads the issue body + all comments + labels + reactions
- Searches related issues/PRs and locates relevant code in the repo
- Attempts reproduction (for bugs)
- Saves detailed markdown report at `$AO_DATA_DIR/triage/`
- Posts a concise triage comment on the GitHub issue
- **Does not commit code, open PRs, close the issue, add labels, or assign anyone** — analysis only

> **Note:** This PR depends on #1466 (`--reports full` flag for `ao status`) being merged first. The backlog preset uses that flag, but includes a fallback for older AO versions.

Closes #1494

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm test` passes (558 tests, 16 new for the preset system)
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn --preset backlog` spawns the backlog analyst
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn 42 --preset triage` spawns triage on a real issue
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn 42 --preset backlog` errors with \"does not accept an issue argument\"
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn --preset triage` errors with \"requires an issue argument\"
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn --preset nonexistent` errors with the available presets list
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn --preset backlog --prompt \"foo\"` errors with mutual exclusivity

title: fix(core): keep terminated sessions in active dir after kill() (#1503)
body:
## Summary

- `kill()` no longer archives sessions immediately. Terminated sessions stay in the active directory so `list()`, the dashboard kanban, and `ensureOrchestrator()` can see them.
- The idempotency path inside `kill()` (fired when kill is called on an already-terminated session) archives the file. This is how `cleanup()` eventually removes it — when it detects a dead runtime, it calls `kill()` again, which hits the idempotency path and archives.
- The `delete` orchestrator strategy still explicitly archives after killing, so `reserveSessionId()` can immediately claim the same session name for the replacement.
- OpenCode cleanup marker is written to active metadata (instead of archived metadata) so the flag survives into the eventual archive.

## Root cause

`session-manager.ts` `kill()` called `deleteMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, true)` immediately after setting `lifecycle.session.state = "terminated"`. This archived the session, making it invisible to `list()` which only reads the active directory. Result: session disappeared from dashboard instead of showing in Done/Terminated column, and `ensureOrchestrator()` spawned a new orchestrator number on the next `ao start`.

## Test plan

- [x] All 887 core tests pass
- [x] All 539 CLI tests pass
- [x] Type checking passes
- [x] Lint passes (0 errors)
- Updated `lifecycle.test.ts`: verifies session stays in active dir with `statePayload` containing `"state":"terminated"` after kill
- Updated `cache.test.ts`: verifies cache is invalidated and session appears as `"terminated"` status after kill (not gone)

Closes #1503

title: Design: AO Activity Events Logging Layer (RCA / self-debugging trail)
body:
## Design: AO Activity Events Logging Layer

Tracking issue for the design and discussion of AO's activity events layer — a lightweight SQLite-backed RCA trail that lets AO diagnose itself when something behaves incorrectly or unexpectedly.

**Design doc (source of truth):** https://gist.github.com/ashish921998/c42db0234370f618fb81a496359831e2

**Author:** @ashish921998

### Summary

The activity events layer is a durable, queryable, local trail of structured events that AO writes as it operates — session spawn/kill, lifecycle transitions, `/api/sessions` results, major UI breakages. When a user reports an issue, AO can query the trail to reconstruct the timeline, identify the likely failure boundary, and guide or make a fix.

This is not a full observability platform, event sourcing system, or analytics product. It is a focused local RCA trail.

### V1 highlights (per the gist)

- SQLite (WAL mode) as durable substrate from day one
- One event envelope, one table, one core write API, one core query API
- CLI reader (`ao events`) — primary V1 read path for diagnostic agents (subprocesses can't rely on the dashboard server)
- Best-effort writes, 7-day retention, sanitization for secrets, 16 KB payload cap
- Initial instrumentation: session spawn, session kill, lifecycle transition, `/api/sessions` count/duration, major UI breakage / sidebar visibility events
- Parallel operation with existing `observability.ts` — no migration required for V1

### Discussion

This issue is the canonical thread for the design conversation. Clarifications, proposals, and tradeoffs will be posted as comments below so we keep everything in one place before V1 implementation lands.

cc @ashish921998

title: bug(web): terminal in session details page renders all output as white, losing ANSI colors
body:
## Bug

The xterm.js terminal in the session details page renders all output as plain white text, stripping ANSI colors (orange, green, red, etc.) that are present in the original terminal output. Claude Code's colored startup screen, status indicators, and other ANSI-colored content all appear monochrome white.

## Screenshot

![Terminal showing all-white output with Claude Code startup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-terminal-colors/.issue-assets/terminal-white-output.png)

## Reproduction

1. Start AO dashboard (`ao start`)
2. Open the web dashboard
3. Navigate to any active session's details page
4. Observe the terminal — all text is rendered in white/foreground color regardless of original ANSI colors

## Root Cause Analysis

**Analyzed against:** `dcfb6fe8` (main HEAD)

Traced the full data flow from tmux → node-pty → WebSocket → xterm.js:

### Data path (confirmed raw passthrough, no stripping):
1. **tmux session** — `TERM=tmux-256color`, `default-terminal=tmux-256color` ✅
2. **mux-websocket.ts** (line 313) — PTY spawned with `name: "xterm-256color"`, `TERM: "xterm-256color"` in env ✅
3. **PTY data** → `pty.onData()` (line 324) → raw ANSI data passed directly to subscribers ✅
4. **WebSocket** → JSON `{ ch: "terminal", type: "data", data: <raw> }` → no transformation ✅
5. **MuxProvider.tsx** (line 131-137) → `callback(msg.data)` → passes string directly ✅
6. **useXtermTerminal.ts** (line 248) → `terminal.write(data)` → xterm.js receives raw ANSI ✅

### Theme configuration (confirmed correct):
- `terminal-themes.ts` — Full 16-color ANSI palette defined for both dark/light themes ✅
- Theme applied at Terminal creation (line 101) and updated reactively (line 350) ✅
- `minimumContrastRatio: 1` in dark mode — no forced color substitution ✅

### What's likely happening:

**Hypothesis: tmux is not passing through 256-color/true-color sequences to the attached PTY.**

The `terminal-features` config is:
```
terminal-features[0] xterm*:clipboard:ccolour:cstyle:focus:title
```

The node-pty attaches as `xterm-256color` (matching `xterm*`), so tmux should enable custom colors (`ccolour`). However, there's a subtlety:

1. When the mux server runs `tmux attach-session` via node-pty, tmux determines the connecting terminal's capabilities from the PTY's `TERM` setting
2. tmux then **re-renders** the session content for that terminal, translating colors based on what it thinks the terminal supports
3. If there's a mismatch between what tmux thinks `xterm-256color` supports and what xterm.js actually renders, colors could be lost

**Alternative hypothesis: xterm.js v6 texture atlas issue.**

xterm.js v6.0.0 uses a canvas-based texture atlas for rendering. The `clearTextureAtlas()` call exists (useXtermTerminal.ts:149) but only runs on `document.fonts` loadingdone. If the atlas is built before the theme colors are applied (race condition during initial render), all glyphs might be rendered with the default foreground color.

### Files to investigate:
- `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` — PTY spawn config (lines 296-319)
- `packages/web/src/components/terminal/useXtermTerminal.ts` — xterm initialization (lines 78-109)
- `packages/web/src/components/terminal/terminal-themes.ts` — color definitions
- `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` — WebSocket message handling (lines 126-163)

## Suggested Fix

1. **Add `terminal-overrides`** to the tmux attach command to force true-color passthrough:
   ```
   tmux set-option -t <session> terminal-overrides "xterm-256color:Tc"
   ```
   The `Tc` flag tells tmux the terminal supports true-color (24-bit).

2. **Or set COLORTERM** in the PTY environment to signal true-color support:
   ```typescript
   env.COLORTERM = "truecolor";
   ```

3. **Verify the texture atlas** — add a debug check after theme application to confirm colors are being used by xterm's renderer.

## Impact

- All users viewing terminals in the web dashboard see monochrome output
- Makes it harder to distinguish error messages (red), warnings (yellow), and status indicators
- Claude Code's colored UI is fully desaturated

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1481733087249174619/1491735678156013588/1497968448805015762
**Reported by:** @somewherelostt 
**Analyzed against:** `dcfb6fe8`

body:
## Summary

- Implements `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-copilot` — full Agent interface for GitHub Copilot CLI
- Hybrid activity detection: native `events.jsonl` for active/ready/idle/blocked + AO activity JSONL for waiting_input (Copilot's events.jsonl lacks permission-prompt events)
- Session discovery via `~/.copilot/session-state/*/workspace.yaml` (honors `$COPILOT_HOME`), with 30s caching
- Pre-trusts the workspace in `{COPILOT_HOME or ~/.copilot}/config.json` so Copilot doesn't block on the "Do you trust the files in this folder?" TUI dialog at launch
- 98 tests covering all 7 required `getActivityState` scenarios, manifest, all public methods, edge cases, concurrent-write retry, and `COPILOT_HOME` plumbing

### Methods implemented

| Method | Approach |
|--------|----------|

title: fix(web): intercept paste to prevent Codex image-paste error on WSL/Linux
body:
## Problem

When pasting plain text (Ctrl+V) into the AO terminal on **WSL** or **Linux/X11**, the Codex CLI (via the `arboard` Rust crate) tries to read the clipboard as an image first. When the clipboard only contains text, `arboard` throws and Codex surfaces:

```
■ Failed to paste image: no image on clipboard: The clipboard contents were not available in the requested format or the clipboard is empty.
```

This blocks or disrupts text paste entirely.

Reported by Maaz (WSL). Does NOT reproduce on macOS or Linux+Wayland.

## Fix

Intercept the `paste` event on xterm's internal textarea *before* it reaches the native paste path that triggers Codex's image-paste codepath:

1. **Prevent default** — stop xterm's native paste from firing
2. **Read text** from the browser `ClipboardEvent.clipboardData`
3. **Wrap in bracketed-paste sequences** (`\x1b[200~` / `\x1b[201~`) — always safe since tmux enables this by default
4. **Send directly through the mux** via `writeTerminal()` — bypasses the agent CLI's clipboard reading entirely

The paste listener is properly cleaned up when the terminal effect unmounts.

## Testing

- [ ] On WSL: copy text, paste into AO terminal running Codex → text appears, no error
- [ ] On macOS: copy text, paste → still works (no regression)
- [ ] Multi-line paste works correctly
- [ ] Image paste is intentionally NOT supported through this path (was broken anyway)

## Upstream

Filed as [openai/codex#19698](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/19698) — the real fix should be in Codex's paste handler to gracefully fall through when the clipboard has text instead of an image.
