title: fix(core): deliver enriched review content on changes_requested transition
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the agent never received actual review comment content when a PR transitioned to `changes_requested`. The agent only got a generic message — *"There are review comments on your PR. Details will follow shortly."* — but the detailed review bodies (file paths, line numbers, authors, comment text) never followed.

Closes #1558

## Root Cause

The review dispatch in `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog` has two paths:

| Path | When | What it sends |
|------|------|---------------|
| **Transition reaction** | Status transitions to `changes_requested` | Generic message from config |
| **Backlog dispatch** | Comment fingerprint changes | Enriched content via `formatReviewCommentsMessage()` |

On the first transition, the transition reaction fired (generic message), then the backlog dispatch recorded the fingerprint hash as "already dispatched" — **without ever sending the actual comment content**. The deduplication logic then blocked the enriched dispatch from ever firing for those comments:

1. **Branch B** (lines 1477-1486): recorded `lastPendingReviewDispatchHash` when the transition reaction succeeded, burning the hash without delivering content
2. **Transition guard** (line 1488): `!(oldStatus !== newStatus && newStatus === "changes_requested")` explicitly skipped the enriched dispatch during the transition poll

This is unlike `ci-failed`, which enriches its transition reaction with actual CI check details from the batch cache. `changes-requested` never got the same treatment — review threads are fetched separately in `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`, not in the batch PR enrichment.

## Fix

- **Remove Branch B** — the block that recorded the dispatch hash when the transition reaction succeeded without sending enriched content
- **Remove the transition guard** — so the backlog dispatch fires in the same poll cycle as the transition
- **Update default message** — remove the "Details will follow shortly" promise since details now arrive immediately

After the fix, the enriched review content (file paths, line numbers, authors, comment bodies, thread IDs) is dispatched in the same poll cycle as the transition. The agent receives two messages back-to-back: the generic transition notification followed immediately by the detailed review content. Subsequent polls skip dispatch because the fingerprint hash matches — no duplicates.

## Files Changed

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — removed premature hash recording and transition guard from `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — updated default `changes-requested` message
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` — updated test to verify enriched content is delivered on transition

## Test plan

- [x] All 1006 core tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test`)
- [ ] Verify agent receives detailed review comments on first `changes_requested` transition
- [ ] Verify no duplicate dispatch on subsequent polls with unchanged comments
- [ ] Verify new comments arriving while in `changes_requested` trigger a fresh enriched dispatch

title: fix(core): notifier system has 7 bugs — silent by default, dead features, missing context
body:
## Summary

The notifier plugin system has 7 distinct bugs that collectively make it non-functional out of the box and degraded even when explicitly configured. Traced end-to-end from event emission in `lifecycle-manager.ts` through routing in `notifyHuman()` to delivery in each notifier plugin.

---

## Bug 1 (Critical): Zero notifications by default — routing fallback is empty

**Location:** `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1729`

```typescript
const notifierNames = config.notificationRouting[priority] ?? config.defaults.notifiers;
```

`config.defaults.notifiers` defaults to `[]` (empty array) in the schema (`config.ts:273`). `notificationRouting` defaults to `{}` (`config.ts:368`).

With no explicit config, `notifierNames` is always `[]`. The `for` loop never executes. **No notifications are ever sent.**

The desktop notifier is registered and functional out of the box (zero config needed), but nothing routes to it. A user who adds `notifiers.desktop.plugin: desktop` but forgets `notificationRouting` or `defaults.notifiers` gets zero notifications with zero errors — just silence.

**Fix:** Either default `defaults.notifiers` to `["desktop"]`, or emit a startup warning when notifiers are registered but no routing points to them.

---

## Bug 2 (Medium): `includeSummary` is a dead config field — declared but never read

**Location:** `config.ts:728`, `types.ts:1208`

The `all-complete` default reaction declares `includeSummary: true`:

```typescript
"all-complete": {
  auto: true,
  action: "notify",
  priority: "info",
  includeSummary: true,  // declared in schema, never read anywhere
}
```

The field is defined in `ReactionConfig` (`types.ts:1208`) and validated by Zod (`config.ts:159`), but `executeReaction()` in `lifecycle-manager.ts` never reads it. The "all-complete" notification just says:

> "Reaction 'all-complete' triggered notification"

No session summaries, no counts, no useful information.

---

## Bug 3 (Medium): `notifyWithActions()` is never called — actions feature is dead code

**Location:** `types.ts:1081`, every notifier plugin's `notifyWithActions` implementation

The `Notifier` interface defines `notifyWithActions?()`, and Slack, Discord, Desktop, Webhook, and Composio all implement it with rich action button support. But the lifecycle manager has **zero call sites** — `notifyHuman()` only ever calls `notifier.notify()`.

Every notifier's `notifyWithActions` implementation (action buttons in Slack, links in Discord, callback endpoints) is dead code.

---

## Bug 4 (Medium): Status transition events missing PR and CI context

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:2019-2025`

When a status transition fires (e.g., `ci.failing`, `review.changes_requested`), the event is created with:

```typescript
data: { oldStatus, newStatus }
```

But the Slack notifier (`notifier-slack/index.ts:55-78`) tries to render:
- `event.data.prUrl` → always `undefined` for status transition events
- `event.data.ciStatus` → **never set by any code path at all**

PR URL is only included in `pr.closed` events (`lifecycle-manager.ts:2078`). CI status is never included in any event's data.

**Result:** Slack notifications for CI failures, review changes, approvals, etc. never show PR links or CI status badges — the rich formatting the Slack plugin was built for is never triggered.

---

## Bug 5 (Medium): Reaction "notify" action produces generic, unhelpful messages

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:1267-1280`

When a reaction with `action: "notify"` fires, it creates:

```typescript
const event = createEvent("reaction.triggered", {
  message: `Reaction '${reactionKey}' triggered notification`,
  data: { reactionKey },
});
```

This is the notification the user receives for `agent-stuck`, `agent-needs-input`, `agent-exited`, `approved-and-green`, and `all-complete` — all configured with `action: "notify"` by default.

The user gets: *"Reaction 'agent-stuck' triggered notification"* instead of something like *"Session my-session has been idle for 15 minutes on project my-project"*. No session context, no project details, no PR link, no actionable information.

The escalation path has the same problem (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1218-1223`):
```
"Reaction 'ci-failed' escalated after 3 attempts"
```

---

## Bug 6 (Low): Several status transitions emit no events

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:232-261`

`statusToEventType()` returns `null` for these transitions:

| Status | Event emitted | Consequence |
|--------|--------------|-------------|
| `spawning` | none | Session creation is silent |
| `detecting` | none | Status ambiguity is silent |
| `idle` | none | Agent going idle is silent |
| `cleanup` | none | Post-merge cleanup is silent |
| `done` | none | Session completion is silent |
| `terminated` | none | Session termination is silent |

The `idle` gap is notable: when a session transitions to `idle`, no event fires, so no notification is sent. A user expecting "notify me when my agent goes idle" has no way to configure it — `idle` is invisible to the event system.

The `done` gap means individual session completion is always silent. Only the aggregate `all-complete` check fires (and per Bug 2, produces a useless message).

---

## Bug 7 (Low): No validation that routing references resolve to registered notifiers

**Location:** `lifecycle-manager.ts:1731-1735`, `notifier-resolution.ts:15-31`

```typescript
for (const name of notifierNames) {
  const target = resolveNotifierTarget(config, name);
  const notifier = registry.get<Notifier>("notifier", target.reference)
    ?? registry.get<Notifier>("notifier", target.pluginName);
  if (notifier) {  // silently skips if null
    await notifier.notify(eventWithPriority);
  }
}
```

If a user has a typo in their routing config (`notificationRouting.urgent: [desktip]`), the registry lookup returns `null`, the `if (notifier)` check silently skips it, and **no notification is sent with no warning**. No startup validation either.

---

## Severity summary

| # | Severity | Issue |
|---|----------|-------|
| 1 | **Critical** | Empty default routing → zero notifications out of the box |
| 2 | Medium | `includeSummary` is dead config — never read |
| 3 | Medium | `notifyWithActions()` is never called — dead code |
| 4 | Medium | Status events missing `prUrl`/`ciStatus` → Slack rich formatting broken |
| 5 | Medium | Reaction "notify" produces generic messages without context |
| 6 | Low | `idle`, `done`, `spawning`, `terminated` transitions invisible to events |
| 7 | Low | Typos in routing config silently produce no notifications |

Bug 1 is the most likely reason it "doesn't work" — even with plugins correctly configured, the routing defaults to empty and nothing fires. Bugs 4 and 5 compound this: even when routing IS configured, the notifications are missing context and rich formatting.

title: bug(scm-github): ETag guards and GraphQL batch spam console with warnings on expected HTTP 304 responses
body: ## Bug The ETag guards and GraphQL batch error handling in `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` use raw `console.warn()`/`console.error()` that fire on every poll cycle. HTTP 304 ("Not Modified") is the **expected** response when the ETag matches — it means nothing changed — but the catch blocks don't distinguish between 304 cache hits and real errors. This floods the orchestrator terminal with noise every poll cycle. ### Screenshot ## All Affected Locations There are **4 raw console statements** in `graphql-batch.ts` that bypass the observer logging pattern: | # | Line | Level | Message | Trigger | |---|------|-------|---------|---------| | 1 | 460 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` | | 2 | 525-527 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 2] Commit status check failed for ${commitKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` | | 3 | 587 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 3] Review comments check failed for ${cacheKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments` | | 4 | 1156 | `console.error` | `[GraphQL Batch Warning] Batch enrichment partially failed: ${errorMsg}` | GraphQL batch query exceptions | Meanwhile, the **other logging in the same file** (lines 1071-1082, 1138) correctly uses `observer?.log("info", ...)` with proper log level management. ## Root Cause All three ETag guard functions (`checkPRListETag`, `checkCommitStatusETag`, `checkReviewCommentsETag`) call `gh api` with an `If-None-Match` header. When the content hasn't changed, GitHub returns 304 and `gh` exits with a non-zero status. The catch blocks fire and log a warning — but they don't check whether the error is a 304 (expected) or an actual failure (network error, auth issue, 5xx). Example from line 460: ```typescript // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- Observability logging for ETag errors console.warn(`[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}`); ``` ## Expected Behavior - HTTP 304 should be handled silently (or at debug level via observer) - Only actual errors (network failures, 4xx other than 304, 5xx) should warn - All logging should use `observer?.log()` instead of raw `console.*` for consistency ## Fix 1. Check for `304` in the error message before warning — skip or downgrade to debug for 304 2. Migrate all 4 instances from raw `console.warn()`/`console.error()` to `observer?.log()` (consistent with the rest of the file) 3. Only log at `"warn"` level for genuine errors, not cache hits ## Impact - **Noise:** Orchestrator terminal becomes unreadable due to warning spam on every poll cycle (3 warnings per cycle × every 5s) - **Misleading:** Operators may think something is broken when the system is working correctly - **No functional impact:** The 304 path works correctly despite the warnings — it just shouldn't log as a failure

title: fix(core): post-launch prompt delivery is unreliable — blind timer, false success, and weak task prompt
body:
## Problem

When a session spawns, the task prompt often never reaches the agent. The agent sits at an empty `❯` prompt with full context in its system prompt but no trigger to start working. This has been reproduced consistently.

### 1. Blind delivery (no readiness check)

The session manager waits a fixed 3 seconds then sends the task prompt via `tmux send-keys`. It doesn't check whether Claude Code has finished starting up. If Claude Code is still loading (banner, hooks, CLAUDE.md), the keystrokes go into the loading screen and are lost.

**Location:** `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:1433-1437`

```typescript
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, baseDelayMs * attempt));
await plugins.runtime.sendMessage(handle, agentLaunchConfig.prompt);
```

### 2. False success (no delivery verification)

The retry logic only catches exceptions from tmux itself. Since tmux successfully accepts the keys — it just pastes them into a loading screen — no exception is thrown. `promptDelivered` is set to `"true"`, the retry loop breaks, and the CLI reports success. The metadata says everything is fine while the agent is idle.

**Location:** `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:1438-1440`

```typescript
promptDelivered = true;
break;
```

### 3. Weak task prompt (causes redundant API calls)

For issue-based spawns, the task prompt is just `"Work on issue: 1580"`. The agent's first instinct is to call `gh issue view 1580` to fetch context — but the full issue details (title, description, labels, code locations) are already in the system prompt. This wastes time and an API call on every spawn.

**Location:** `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts:203-206`

```typescript
taskPrompt: config.userPrompt
  ? config.userPrompt
  : config.issueId
    ? `Work on issue: ${config.issueId}`
    : undefined,
```

## Fix

### Readiness detection before sending

Replace the blind 3s timer with a poll loop that checks for the `❯` prompt via `tmux capture-pane` + `detectActivity()` — the same pattern `ao send` already uses. Only send the task prompt once the agent is confirmed in interactive mode.

### Delivery verification after sending

After sending, poll again to confirm the agent transitioned from idle to active. Only set `promptDelivered = "true"` after confirming the agent is processing. If it stays idle, retry. If all retries fail, set `promptDelivered = "false"` so the CLI warns the user.

### Improved task prompt for issue-based spawns

Change the task prompt from:
```
Work on issue: 1580
```
To:
```
Work on issue #1580. The full issue details are already in your system prompt — you can start implementing without fetching the issue unless you need additional context (e.g. comments, linked issues, or recent updates).
```

## Impact

- Sessions reliably start working on their task without manual intervention
- `promptDelivered` metadata accurately reflects reality
- Agents skip redundant `gh issue view` calls on spawn

title: fix(core): reliable post-launch prompt delivery with readiness polling
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1582 — post-launch prompt delivery was unreliable because it used a blind 3-second timer instead of checking agent readiness. Keystrokes sent during loading were silently lost, and `promptDelivered` was falsely set to `"true"`.

title: fix(ao): ao update runs duplicate updates instead of saying 'Already on latest'
body:
## Bug Description

Running `ao update` twice in a row performs the update process both times, even when already on the latest version. It should detect that no update is needed and print something like `Already on latest` on the second run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `ao update` — updates successfully
2. Run `ao update` again immediately after

## Expected Behavior

Second run should detect the current version is already the latest and print:
```
Already on latest version.
```

## Actual Behavior

The update process runs again (re-downloads, re-installs, or re-links) even though nothing changed. No feedback that the current version is already up to date.

## Environment

- `ao` CLI
- macOS

## Notes

The fix should compare the currently installed version against the latest available version before performing any update steps, and short-circuit with an informative message if they match.

title: fix(cli): skip rebuild when git install is already on latest version
body:
## Summary

- `ao update` on a git install was running the full rebuild pipeline (fetch, pull, pnpm install, clean, build, npm link) every invocation, even when nothing had changed
- After `git fetch`, we now compare local `HEAD` to the remote branch tip; if they match, we print `Already on latest version.` and exit 0
- The npm/pnpm install path already had this guard (`handleNpmUpdate` calls `checkForUpdate()` first) — this brings the git path to parity

## Root Cause

`handleGitUpdate()` in `update.ts` delegates unconditionally to `ao-update.sh` with no version check beforehand. The shell script had no mechanism to detect "nothing to do" — it fetched and rebuilt regardless of whether local HEAD matched the remote.

## Test Plan

title: chore: bump package.json versions on main to match published npm release (0.3.0)
body:
## Problem

`main` ships `package.json` at version **0.2.5** across all workspace packages, but the npm registry's `@aoagents/ao` `latest` dist-tag is **0.3.0**:

\`\`\`bash
$ curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/@aoagents%2Fao/latest | jq -r .version
0.3.0

$ grep '"version"' packages/ao/package.json
  "version": "0.2.5",
\`\`\`

## Why it matters

The update notifier (\`maybeShowUpdateNotice\` in \`packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts\`) compares the locally installed version against the npm registry. For git-checkout installs, "locally installed" comes from \`<checkout>/packages/ao/package.json\` — which is \`0.2.5\` even on a fully up-to-date \`main\`. So every git user sees:

\`\`\`
Update available: 0.2.5 → 0.3.0 — Run: ao update
\`\`\`

…and \`ao update\` can't silence it, because \`ao update\` for git installs fast-forwards to \`main\` (still 0.2.5), not the npm release.

## Reproduce

1. Clone the repo, run \`pnpm install && pnpm build && cd packages/ao && npm link\`
2. Run \`ao update\` — the script reports success
3. Run any \`ao\` command — startup notifier nags about 0.3.0

## Fix

Bump the \`version\` field to \`0.3.0\` (or whatever the next intended release is) across all workspace \`package.json\` files so \`main\` matches what's been published. This is normally done via Changesets at release time — looks like the version-bump step was skipped or not committed back to \`main\` for the 0.3.0 cut.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All workspace \`package.json\` files on \`main\` have \`version\` >= the current npm \`latest\`
- [ ] A fresh git install no longer prints the spurious "Update available" notice

title: chore: align workspace package.json versions with npm registry
body:
## What

Aligns committed `package.json` versions with what's actually published on npm. The in-tree files had drifted to `0.2.5` while releases (via Changesets) had already pushed most packages to `0.3.0`.

The original motivation was the `ao update available` prompt, which compares the installed `@aoagents/ao` version to the npm registry. Source of truth: `packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts` — `getCurrentVersion()` reads `@aoagents/ao/package.json`, and `fetchLatestVersion()` queries `registry.npmjs.org/@aoagents/ao`. So `packages/ao` is the only file the prompt strictly needs. But while we're here, every other workspace `package.json` was also stale relative to what's published, so this PR catches them all up at once.

## Version changes

| Bump | Packages |
|---|---|
| `0.2.5 → 0.3.0` | `ao`, `cli`, `core`, `web`, `agent-aider`, `agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-opencode`, `notifier-composio`, `notifier-desktop`, `notifier-slack`, `notifier-webhook`, `runtime-process`, `runtime-tmux`, `scm-github`, `terminal-iterm2`, `terminal-web`, `tracker-github`, `tracker-linear`, `workspace-clone`, `workspace-worktree` |
| `0.2.5 → 0.2.6` | `notifier-discord`, `notifier-openclaw`, `scm-gitlab`, `tracker-gitlab` |
| `0.1.0 → 0.1.1` | `agent-cursor` |

Each target version matches what `npm view <pkg> version` returns today.

## Test fixes

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/package-version.test.ts`: hardcoded `0.2.5` → `0.3.0` to match the new manifest.
- `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/update-check.test.ts` (`uses cache when fresh and does not call fetch`): the test cached `latestVersion: "0.3.0"` and asserted `isOutdated === true`. That only worked while the repo's installed version was `< 0.3.0`. Once `packages/ao` reaches `0.3.0` (and pnpm makes it resolvable from cli at test time via `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@aoagents/ao`), `getCurrentVersion()` returns `0.3.0`, the comparison flips to false, and the assertion fails. Fix: cache `latestVersion: "99.0.0"` so the test stays meaningful regardless of the repo's real version. The three invariants it guards are unchanged: cache is read, version comparison works, and no network call is made.

## Why

- **The `ao update available` prompt was effectively comparing `0.2.5` (committed) against `0.3.0` (registry) and reporting "outdated" forever** — even on fresh installs.
- The committed files were a misleading source of truth: `git log` and `package.json` disagreed with npm.
- Future Changesets releases work cleanly when the in-tree starting point matches the last published version.

title: Dashboard can lose CSS/JS when production .next artifacts are rebuilt or deleted while ao start is running
body:
## Summary

When AO is started via `ao start`, the dashboard can end up rendering as mostly raw, unstyled HTML if the production Next.js build artifacts under `packages/web/.next` are removed or replaced while the dashboard server is still running.

Observed locally:
- Dashboard at `http://localhost:3000/` rendered with browser-default styles.
- HTML referenced `/_next/static/css/397ea3e60645d3f3.css`.
- Requesting that CSS URL returned `HTTP 400 Bad Request` with a Next.js HTML error page instead of CSS.
- `packages/web/.next` was missing, while `packages/web/.next-dev` existed.
- The dashboard process was still running via `ao start` / `next start`.

## Why this matters

`ao start` runs the dashboard in optimized production mode by default from a source checkout. That server depends on the mutable `packages/web/.next` directory. If a later build/clean operation deletes or replaces `.next` while the dashboard is live, the server can continue serving HTML but fail to serve static CSS/JS assets.

This creates a confusing partially-working state:
- dashboard loads
- sessions may still appear
- styling is gone
- terminal bridge reconnect noise may appear, but the underlying tmux sessions can still be alive

## Likely trigger

`packages/web/package.json` has:

```json
"prebuild": "rimraf .next dist-server"
```

So commands like `pnpm build`, `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web build`, `pnpm clean`, or rebuild paths can remove `.next` while a dashboard started by `ao start` is still serving from it.

## Expected behavior

AO should not allow a live production dashboard to keep serving from build artifacts that are being deleted or replaced.

## Possible fixes

- Stop the running dashboard before `ao start --rebuild` deletes/rebuilds `.next`.
- Add a guard to the web `prebuild` script that refuses to delete `.next` if an AO dashboard is running from the same checkout.
- Use an atomic build/swap strategy for production dashboard artifacts.
- Add a startup or health check that verifies CSS/static asset serving, not just `BUILD_ID` existence.

## Current workaround

Stop AO/dashboard, rebuild, then start again:

```bash
ao stop
pnpm build
ao start
```

or use the appropriate rebuild flow after ensuring the dashboard is stopped.

title: bug: kill+restore session starts fresh chat instead of resuming (multi-project)
body:
## Summary

Kill+restore (and `ao stop` → `ao start`) silently launches a **fresh chat** instead of resuming, but **only for sessions belonging to a project that was never passed to `ao start`**. Sessions in `ao start`'s home project resume correctly; dashboard-spawned sessions in any other globally-registered project do not.

The agent's own `/resume` command from inside the fresh chat finds the prior conversation, so the agent's session data on disk is intact. The failure is in AO's restore decision, not the agent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register at least two projects in the global config (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`), e.g. `project-A` and `project-B`.
2. Run `ao start` from `project-A` only.
3. Open the dashboard and spawn a worker on `project-B` (the project that is **not** the host of `ao start`).
4. Send the worker a few messages so the conversation is recognizable.
5. Kill the session from the top bar.
6. Restore it from the dashboard.

**Expected:** The restored session continues the previous conversation (via `getRestoreCommand`).
**Actual:** Fresh chat. Running `/resume` inside the new agent finds the old conversation.

`ao stop` → `ao start` reproduces the same fresh-chat behavior — same `restore()` code path.

For workers spawned in `project-A` (covered by `ao start`), kill+restore works correctly. The asymmetry is the smoking gun.

## Root Cause (sibling of #1522)

This is a direct consequence of the gap #1522 names but does not yet fix:

> Lifecycle polling … is scoped to the project IDs passed to `ao start` at startup. Projects added to the global config later — by `ao start <URL>`, `ao project add`, manual YAML edits, web `POST /api/projects` — are visible to the dashboard but **not polled** by the running daemon.

#1522 enumerates the consequences for an out-of-scope project: activity state doesn't transition, PR state isn't refreshed, reactions don't fire, `runtime_lost` reconciliation doesn't run. **This issue is one more entry in that list**: resume after kill / `ao stop` is broken for not-polled projects.

### Why polling causes the asymmetry

The dashboard's session manager sees both projects (it loads the global config in `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts:130–149`), so spawn/kill/restore *reach* project-B fine. The asymmetry lives at the lifecycle-worker layer, which is bound to `ao start`'s startup scope (`packages/cli/src/lib/lifecycle-service.ts:30`).

For `project-A`, the lifecycle worker ticks every 30s, exercising `getSessionInfo` (and the same `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl` lookup that `getRestoreCommand` uses) — any slug/UUID drift gets surfaced and resolved before kill. For `project-B`, restore is the *first* time that lookup runs.

If `getRestoreCommand` returns `null` for any reason (slug encoding mismatch, realpath divergence on macOS symlinked paths, missing JSONL), the call site at `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2873` silently substitutes a fresh launch:

```ts
launchCommand = restoreCmd ?? plugins.agent.getLaunchCommand(agentLaunchConfig);
```

No log, no metadata field, no error. The user sees a successful "Restored" toast and a fresh chat.

Additionally, `POST /api/spawn` does not mirror the CLI's `warnIfAONotRunning` guard (`packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts:66–83`), so dashboard spawns silently bypass the check the CLI hard-errors on (commit `469e2627`).

## Why `/resume` works

Claude's `/resume` runs inside Claude itself — it scans `~/.claude/projects/**` using its own canonical encoding and `getcwd()` resolution. It doesn't depend on AO's slugifier or polling.

## Fix Direction

Two complementary changes:

1. **Land #1522 (project supervisor).** Auto-attach a lifecycle worker for any globally-registered project with at least one non-terminal session. Restore on a dashboard-spawned worker stops being a special case once the supervisor is reconciling polling on demand.
2. **Persist the agent's session UUID at runtime, not at restore.** `getSessionInfo` already extracts `agentSessionId` (`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:825`). Persist it as `claudeSessionUuid` in session metadata at first opportunity. `getRestoreCommand` should prefer the persisted UUID over re-deriving it from `session.workspacePath`. Same approach for Codex's `data.threadId` (`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:710–737`).
3. **Surface the silent fallback** — when `getRestoreCommand` returns `null`, write `restoreFallbackReason` into metadata so this regression class becomes visible.
4. **Align the Claude slug encoder with Claude Code** — `toClaudeProjectPath` (`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:244`) replaces only `:`, `/`, `.`. Match the encoding documented in the migration code at `packages/core/src/migration/storage-v2.ts:864–940` (`replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-")`) and share one helper.

#1 is the structural fix and closes both this issue and #1522. #2 makes restore resilient even when polling is unhealthy. #3 prevents the next regression from being invisible.

## Affected Files

- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2729–2876` — `restore()` and the silent `?? getLaunchCommand` fallback at line 2873
- `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:244, 839–867` — slug encoder + `getRestoreCommand`
- `packages/cli/src/lib/lifecycle-service.ts` — fixed-scope lifecycle worker registry
- `packages/web/src/app/api/spawn/route.ts` — missing daemon-polling guard
- `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts:130–149` — dashboard config loading

title: ao update fails refreshing launcher when old global ao shim exists
body:
## Summary

`ao update` can successfully fast-forward, install dependencies, and rebuild packages, then fail at the final launcher refresh step if a user already has a global `ao` binary from the older package name (`@composio/ao-cli`).

The current script labels the first `npm link` failure as a permission problem and retries with `sudo`, but npm still fails with `EEXIST` because `/opt/homebrew/bin/ao` already exists.

## User-facing output

```text
Refreshing ao launcher...
  Permission denied. Retrying with sudo...
Password:
npm error code EEXIST
npm error path /opt/homebrew/bin/ao
npm error EEXIST: file already exists
npm error File exists: /opt/homebrew/bin/ao
npm error Remove the existing file and try again, or run npm
npm error with --force to overwrite files recklessly.
```

On the affected machine, the existing shim was:

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin/ao -> ../lib/node_modules/@composio/ao-cli/dist/index.js
```

The repo has since moved to the `@aoagents/ao` launcher package, so users with the old global shim can hit this during update.

## Why this matters

The expensive parts of the update already completed by the time this fails:

- `git fetch` / `git pull --ff-only`
- `pnpm install`
- clean rebuild of core, CLI, and web

The user is left with a failed update command and unclear guidance, even though the remaining work is only replacing the global launcher shim.

## Expected behavior

`ao update` should refresh the launcher successfully even when a stale global `ao` binary already exists from the old package name.

## Proposed fix

Use forced npm linking for source-checkout launcher refreshes:

```bash
npm link --force
sudo npm link --force
```

Also update the message so the sudo retry is not described as “Permission denied” for every possible npm failure. Something like this is more accurate:

```text
Launcher refresh needs elevated permissions. Retrying with sudo...
```

The same launcher-refresh logic exists in multiple places and should stay consistent:

- `packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-update.sh`
- `packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-doctor.sh`
- `scripts/setup.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- `ao update` overwrites a stale existing global `ao` shim instead of failing with `EEXIST`.
- `ao doctor --fix` and `scripts/setup.sh` use the same robust launcher refresh behavior.
- Error copy no longer claims “Permission denied” for non-permission npm failures.
- Regression coverage simulates an existing `ao` shim / `EEXIST` style failure and verifies `npm link --force` is used.

title: Make update checks install-method aware for npm and git/source installs
body:
## Summary

`ao start` can show misleading update prompts because the update checker currently treats npm latest as the source of truth even when the user is running AO from a git/source checkout.

Example observed from a source checkout on `main`:

```text
Update available: 0.2.5 → 0.3.0 — Run: ao update
```

But the checkout was already at `origin/main`, and the repo package versions still reported `0.2.5`. In this install mode, `ao update` pulls git `main`; it does not install npm latest. So comparing against npm latest creates a false prompt.

Related: #1540
Related launcher-shim issue: #1591

## Desired behavior

Update checks should use the same source of truth that the user's install method uses for updates.

### npm global installs

If AO is installed via:

```bash
npm install -g @aoagents/ao
```

Then the update checker should compare the installed version against npm registry latest for `@aoagents/ao`.

Prompt should recommend:

```bash
npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest
```

### pnpm global installs

If AO is installed via pnpm global, compare against npm registry latest and recommend:

```bash
pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@latest
```

### git/source checkout installs

If AO is running from a cloned repo / source checkout, npm latest should not be used for the startup prompt.

Instead, compare the local git state against the remote branch that `ao update` would pull, usually:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git rev-parse HEAD
git rev-parse origin/main
```

If local `HEAD` is behind the update branch, then prompt with:

```text
Update available from origin/main — Run: ao update
```

If local `HEAD` matches the remote update branch, do not show an update prompt, even if npm has a newer published version.

## Problem details

There are two different update channels:

- npm users update from the npm registry
- source users update from git

A single cache entry like:

```json
{
  "latestVersion": "0.3.0",
  "currentVersionAtCheck": "0.2.5"
}
```

is unsafe because it can be produced under one install method and consumed under another. For example, an npm latest cache can make a source checkout repeatedly show an update prompt that `ao update` cannot resolve.

## Proposed fix

1. Make the update-check cache install-method aware.
   - Include `installMethod` in the cache data.
   - Ignore cache entries whose install method differs from the current install method.
   - Treat older cache entries without `installMethod` as unsafe for git/source installs.

2. Split latest-version resolution by install method.
   - `npm-global` and `pnpm-global`: use npm registry latest.
   - `git`: use git remote branch state, not npm latest.
   - `unknown`: either use npm registry with conservative messaging, or suppress startup prompts if install method cannot be resolved confidently.

3. Keep recommended commands aligned with install method.
   - git: `ao update`
   - npm-global: `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`
   - pnpm-global: `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@latest`

4. Ensure startup notifier and `ao doctor` use the same install-aware cache semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- A git/source checkout at `origin/main` does not show `0.2.5 → 0.3.0` just because npm latest is `0.3.0`.
- A git/source checkout behind `origin/main` does show an update prompt recommending `ao update`.
- npm global installs still show npm registry updates and recommend `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`.
- pnpm global installs still show npm registry updates and recommend `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@latest`.
- Cache entries are scoped by install method and cannot leak between npm/global and git/source installs.
- Tests cover npm-global, pnpm-global, git/source current, git/source behind, stale cache from another install method, and legacy cache entries without `installMethod`.

## Notes

A conservative short-term mitigation is to suppress npm-registry prompts for git/source installs. The complete fix should compare source installs against the git branch that `ao update` actually pulls.

title: bug(web): stale session detail page spam-errors after project switch — dead terminal reconnect loop
body:
## Repro

1. `ao start` on Project A → open session detail page in browser
2. `ao stop` → `ao start` on Project B (different project)
3. Old browser tab is still on the Project A session detail page
4. Terminal gets spammed with errors — `Session not found` / connection failures in the server console

## Root Cause — Three Interacting Bugs

### Bug 1: MuxProvider re-opens dead terminals on reconnect (`MuxProvider.tsx:124-134`)

When the WebSocket reconnects, it blindly re-sends `open` for every entry in `openedTerminalsRef.current`. After a project switch, the old session's tmux session is gone → server throws `"Session not found"` → sends error back. MuxProvider logs it (line 178) but **never removes the dead entry from `openedTerminalsRef`**.

### Bug 2: Context value change triggers terminal recreation (`useXtermTerminal.ts:335-348`)

When mux status changes to `"connected"`, the `contextValue` useMemo in `MuxProvider.tsx:349-360` produces a new object (because `status` is a dep). `useMux()` returns new references → the main `useEffect` in `useXtermTerminal` sees deps changed → **destroys and recreates the entire xterm instance + WebSocket subscription** → re-opens the dead session → error again. This can cycle every time mux sessions update (every 3s from `SessionBroadcaster` polling).

### Bug 3: 404 doesn't show "session not found" after first successful load (`sessions/[id]/page.tsx:505-513`)

```ts
if (normalizedMessage.includes("session not found") || ...) {
  if (!hasLoadedSessionRef.current) {   // ← only triggers on FIRST load
    setSessionMissing(true);
  }
}
```

The polling loop (line 689-696) fires every 2s calling `fetchSession()`. After AO switches projects, the API returns 404 — but since `hasLoadedSessionRef` is already `true` from when the page originally loaded the session, the 404 is **silently swallowed**. The page never shows the "Session not found" error state, so it keeps retrying forever.

## Fix (3 parts)

### Fix 1: MuxProvider — clean up dead terminals on error
When receiving a `terminal.error` message with a permanent failure (e.g. "Session not found"), remove the entry from `openedTerminalsRef` so it doesn't get re-opened on next reconnect. Also clean up from `subscribersRef`.

File: `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` — in the `msg.type === "error"` branch (line 177-178).

### Fix 2: useXtermTerminal — don't recreate terminal on mux status change
Stabilize the effect deps so a mux reconnect doesn't tear down and recreate the entire terminal. The mux functions (`subscribeTerminal`, `openTerminal`, etc.) are already stable `useCallback(fn, [])` — the problem is the `contextValue` useMemo producing a new object when `status` changes. Either:
- Split `status` out of the contextValue useMemo so terminal functions stay referentially stable, OR
- Use `useRef` for the mux functions inside `useXtermTerminal` to decouple from the effect deps, OR
- Handle the "Session not found" error from the `open` response by surfacing it up to the page component

File: `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` line 349-360 and/or `packages/web/src/components/terminal/useXtermTerminal.ts` line 335-348.

### Fix 3: Session detail page — handle 404 after successful load
Remove (or relax) the `hasLoadedSessionRef.current` guard so that if the session was previously loaded but is now gone, it still sets `sessionMissing = true` and shows the error state instead of silently retrying forever.

```diff
 if (normalizedMessage.includes("session not found") || ...) {
-  if (!hasLoadedSessionRef.current) {
     setSessionMissing(true);
-  }
   setLoading(false);
   return;
 }
```

File: `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` line 505-513.

## Severity
High — causes terminal spam and server log noise, makes old tabs unusable, requires manual tab close or page refresh to stop. Common when switching between projects during development.

title: Session restore ignores current config agent — always uses persisted agent from metadata
body:
## Bug

When a session is stopped (e.g. via `ao stop`) and the user changes the agent in their config (e.g. `claude` → `opencode`), restoring that session via `ao start` or `ao session restore` launches it with the **old** agent, not the current config.

Reported by: @Priyanchew, he was on yyovils laptop :)

## Root Cause

`resolveAgentSelection()` in `agent-selection.ts` treats `persistedAgent` as the highest-priority source:

```ts
// agent-selection.ts:45-46
const agentName = persistedAgent
  ? persistedAgent      // <-- short-circuits, config never consulted
  : role === "worker" ? (...) : (...);
```

On restore, `resolveSelectionForSession()` passes `metadata["agent"]` (the agent the session was originally spawned with), so the current config is always overridden.

### Call chain:
1. `session-manager.ts:2818` — `restore()` calls `resolveSelectionForSession(project, sessionId, raw)`
2. `session-manager.ts:889` — `resolveSelectionForSession()` calls `resolveAgentSelection({ persistedAgent: metadata["agent"] })`
3. `agent-selection.ts:45-46` — `agentName = persistedAgent` — config ignored

## Suggested Fix

Add a `preferConfigAgent` flag to `resolveSelectionForSession()`. On restore, set it to `true` so the current config agent takes priority over the persisted one. Only fall back to `persistedAgent` if config doesn't specify an agent.

This is surgical — only affects the restore path, no risk to `list()`/`get()` display behavior.

## Reproduction
1. Start a session with `agent: claude` in config
2. `ao stop`
3. Change config to `agent: opencode`
4. `ao start` — accept restore prompt
5. **Expected:** Session launches with opencode
6. **Actual:** Session launches with claude

## Workaround
`ao session kill` the old session and spawn fresh.

## Severity
Medium — confusing UX when switching agents, but doesn't break anything if config isn't changed between stops.

title: discussion(web): sidebar shouldn't show branch name — replace with something more useful

title: bug(web): orchestrator session restore fails with 409 — getRestoreCommand returned null
body:
## Summary

Restoring an orchestrator session from the dashboard fails with a 409 Conflict. The error states that the agent plugin's `getRestoreCommand` returned null, so the session cannot be restored.

## Repro

1. Have an orchestrator session that has been killed/stopped (e.g. `gi-orchestrator`)
2. Click restore on it from the dashboard

## Error (from browser console)

```
POST /api/sessions/gi-orchestrator/restore → 409 Conflict
Failed to restore session: Error: {"error":"Session gi-orchestrator cannot be restored: claude-code.getRestoreCommand returned null"}
```

## Why this happens

The restore handler asks the agent plugin (`claude-code`) for a restore command via `getRestoreCommand`. When the plugin returns `null` (e.g. because it cannot find a Claude Code session ID to resume against), the API surfaces a 409 instead of falling back to a sensible behavior.

For orchestrator sessions specifically, this is especially problematic — orchestrators should always be restorable. Returning `null` for one of these blocks the user entirely.

## Expected Behavior

Either:
1. Fall back to launching a fresh session (with the existing session ID + workspace) when no resume command is available, or
2. Surface a clear, actionable error explaining what is missing and how to recover (e.g. "no Claude session ID found — start fresh?"), with an option to start fresh from the same UI.

A hard 409 with no recovery path is the worst of both worlds.

## Related

This is also tied to the broader resume bug (#1590) where kill+restore in multi-project setups starts fresh chats. Same general area of code (restore flow + agent plugin `getRestoreCommand` invocation).

## Affected Files (likely)

- The `/api/sessions/[id]/restore` route in `packages/web/`
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` and/or `lifecycle-manager.ts` restore path
- `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` — `getRestoreCommand` returning null

title: fix(agent-claude-code): fold underscores in Claude project slug (#1611)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1611. The orchestrator-restore 409 was the loudest symptom of a slug-encoding bug that silently broke restore for **any** multi-project AO setup (orchestrator or worker, claude-code agent).

## Root cause

`toClaudeProjectPath` in `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` only replaced `/`, `.`, and `:` — but Claude Code's actual on-disk slug also folds underscores (and any other non-alphanumeric character) to `-`. AO names per-project data dirs `<sanitized>_<hash>` (e.g. `graph-isomorphism_d185b44d56`, `screen-ocr_cea728ec80`, `dep-graph_c82cc24448`), so AO's computed slug pointed at a directory that never existed.

Cascading effects:
1. `getSessionInfo` couldn't read the JSONL → `claudeSessionUuid` was never persisted to session metadata.
2. On restore, `getRestoreCommand`'s metadata lookup found nothing AND its workspace-scan fallback also missed (same bad slug) → returns `null`.
3. `session-manager.ts`'s native-restore guard then threw `SessionNotRestorableError` → API returned **409**.

## Disk-level evidence

| Project | Has underscore in dir name? | `claudeSessionUuid` persisted across all sessions? |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-orchestrator` | no | yes (10/10) |
| `graph-isomorphism_d185b44d56` | yes | **no (0/2)** |

Slug AO computed: `…graph-isomorphism_d185b44d56…`
Slug Claude wrote: `…graph-isomorphism-d185b44d56…`

The orchestrator failure in #1611 stood out because orchestrators are killed early, so they don't have other paths to compensate. Workers in underscored projects were silently affected too (same code path, same broken slug).

## Fix

One regex change — replace `[/.]` with `[^a-zA-Z0-9-]` so the slug matches Claude Code's actual encoding:

```diff
 export function toClaudeProjectPath(workspacePath: string): string {
-  const normalized = workspacePath.replace(/\\/g, "/");
-  return normalized.replace(/:/g, "").replace(/[/.]/g, "-");
+  const normalized = workspacePath.replace(/\\/g, "/").replace(/:/g, "");
+  return normalized.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9-]/g, "-");
 }
```

This is the core fix. No carve-outs in `session-manager.ts`, no orchestrator-vs-worker special casing — those would have just been compensating for `toClaudeProjectPath` being wrong.

## Tests

- New `toClaudeProjectPath` direct unit tests (5): plain unix path, dot-dirs, **underscore folding (#1611)**, Windows drive, other non-alphanumerics.
- New regression test in `getSessionInfo` path-conversion suite that exercises an AO-style underscored project path.
- All 158 claude-code plugin tests pass; all 1043 core tests pass.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` clean (only pre-existing warnings).

## Test Plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test`
- [x] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint`
- [ ] Manual: spawn an orchestrator in an underscored-project, kill it, restore from dashboard — should resume the previous Claude conversation instead of 409'ing.

title: feat: add pi.dev agent plugin
body:
## Summary

Adds `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-pi` — a new agent plugin for the [pi.dev coding agent](https://pi.dev). Pi sessions are spawned per worktree like any other agent slot, peer with `claude-code`, `codex`, `aider`, `opencode`.

## What changed

- **New package** `packages/plugins/agent-pi/` implementing the `Agent` interface
  - Resolves the `pi` binary via `which` + npm/Homebrew fallbacks
  - Reads pi's native JSONL at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` with a subdir-scan fallback that matches the session header `cwd` field
  - Aggregates cost from per-message `usage.cost.total` (pi reports cost natively, no estimation needed)
  - `promptDelivery: post-launch` — `pi -p` exits immediately, so prompts go via `runtime.sendMessage` after the interactive process is up
- **Wired into the registry**:
  - `packages/cli/package.json` — workspace dep
  - `packages/cli/src/lib/plugins.ts` — CLI registry
  - `packages/cli/src/lib/detect-agent.ts` — auto-detection
  - `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts` — `BUILTIN_PLUGINS`

## Activity detection

Follows the contract documented in CLAUDE.md (\`getActivityState\` cascade):

1. Process check first → \`exited\`
2. AO activity JSONL handles \`waiting_input\`/\`blocked\` (pi has no dedicated permission_request type in its native JSONL, so terminal-derived state is the source for actionable states)
3. Native pi JSONL timestamps drive \`active\`/\`ready\`/\`idle\`
4. File-mtime fallback when entry parsing fails
5. \`getActivityFallbackState\` as last resort

## Tests

26 cases in \`src/index.test.ts\` covering:

- Manifest, exports, default plugin module shape
- \`getLaunchCommand\` with and without prompt
- \`getEnvironment\` (\`AO_SESSION_ID\`, \`AO_ISSUE_ID\`)
- \`detectActivity\` for idle / waiting_input / blocked / active patterns
- \`isProcessRunning\` for tmux + process runtimes, including the npm dot-prefix case (\`.pi\`)
- All 7 required \`getActivityState\` scenarios from CLAUDE.md

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-pi typecheck\`
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-pi build\`
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-pi test\` → 26/26
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck\`
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck\`
- [x] \`pnpm build\` (full monorepo)
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` (0 errors, pre-existing warnings only)
- [x] Runtime sanity check: \`detect()\` returns \`true\` with pi installed, \`getAgentByName('pi')\` resolves correctly

Pre-existing failures in \`packages/cli/__tests__/commands/start.test.ts\` (8 failures in \`stop command\` and \`Ctrl+C handling\` suites) reproduce on \`upstream/main\` without these changes — unrelated to this PR.

## Notes for review

A few things that need real-world validation with pi running and would be good to verify in review:

1. **Session dir encoding** — implemented as \`/foo/bar → -foo-bar\`. The doc pattern \`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path>--/...\` is ambiguous; the subdir-scan fallback covers other encodings by matching the JSONL header \`cwd\`. Confirm with \`ls ~/.pi/agent/sessions/\` after a real session.
2. **\`detectActivity\` patterns** — used generic regexes (\`(y)es/(n)o\`, \`approval required\`, \`Allow X?\`, \`Do you want to proceed?\`). These should be tightened against real pi terminal output for permission prompts.
3. **JSONL header field** — assumed \`cwd\`/\`workspacePath\` is in the header. Pi's session-format docs document \`id\` and entry types but did not explicitly confirm the cwd field name.

Happy to iterate on any of the above.

title: refactor(core): replace spawn rollback ladder with CleanupStack
body:
## Summary

Replace the four nested try/catch + `cleanupSpawnWorkspaceAndMetadata` helper in `_spawnInner` with a single LIFO `CleanupStack`. Each side effect (reserved metadata, workspace, prompt files, runtime handle) pushes its undo as soon as the resource exists; on success we `dismiss()`, on failure we `runAll()`.

This is **PR 1 of 6** in a planned `ao spawn` refactor. Cleanup-stack lands first because it's a pure internal refactor with zero API surface change — makes subsequent PRs (plugin preflight, claim-PR validation, opencode extraction) safer to land.

## Why

Adding a new spawn step previously required extending every prior cleanup block. Easy to forget; no compiler check. The stack makes rollback structural — a new step pushes one cleanup, no risk of leaving prior resources behind.

`runAll()` is fault-tolerant by design: a throwing cleanup never short-circuits the rest. Without that property the abstraction is worse than the inline ladder.

## What changed

- New `packages/core/src/cleanup-stack.ts` (~55 lines) — `push` / `dismiss` / `runAll(onError?)`. LIFO. Both `dismiss()` and `runAll()` are terminal (push is a no-op afterwards). Errors swallowed by default; `_spawnInner` passes an `onError` callback that logs via `console.error` for debug visibility.
- Refactor `_spawnInner` in `session-manager.ts` to use it. Behavior is identical.
- `spawnOrchestrator` is **not** touched in this PR — same pattern, but bundling would expand the diff and the behavior delta is wider (orchestrator's cleanup doesn't gate on `shouldDestroyWorkspacePath`). Follow-up PR.

## Tests

**9 unit tests** for `CleanupStack`: empty stack, LIFO order, dismiss, async cleanups, fault-tolerance (one throw doesn't skip others), `onError` callback, idempotent `runAll`, push-after-dismiss is no-op, push-after-`runAll` is no-op (symmetric).

**5 characterization tests** for `_spawnInner` rollback paths (none existed before — only `spawnOrchestrator` was covered):
- workspace.create failure cleans reserved metadata
- workspace.postCreate failure destroys worktree + cleans metadata
- runtime.create failure destroys worktree + cleans metadata
- postLaunchSetup failure destroys runtime + worktree + metadata
- one cleanup throwing does not skip subsequent cleanups

These pass against the current code AND the refactored code, locking in the existing behavior.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (47 pre-existing warnings, none from this diff)
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` ✅ 1056/1056
- `tracker-linear` test failures pre-exist (missing `@composio/core` optional dep) and are unrelated to this PR.

## LOC

Production code only (excluding tests): roughly net-zero. The win is structural, not quantitative.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Manual: spawn a session and confirm normal flow still works
- [ ] Manual: deliberately break `runtime.create` (e.g. tmux not running) and confirm worktree gets cleaned up
- [ ] Code review on `cleanup-stack.ts` interface — does the `onError` callback shape feel right?

title: refactor(cli): extract preflight + shutdown from start.ts (PR A)
body:
## Summary

PR A of a 3-PR plan to clean up `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` (currently 2532 lines). This PR is **mechanical extraction** — `start.ts` shrinks from 2532 → ~2140 lines (-390), redistributed into three focused modules.

## What's in this PR

### 1. `lib/install-helpers.ts` (new — 102 lines)

Shared install primitives used by ensureGit, ensureTmux, the agent-runtime installer, and the optional gh install path:

- `InstallAttempt`, `canPromptForInstall`, `askYesNo`
- `runInteractiveCommand`, `tryInstallWithAttempts`, `genericInstallHints`

### 2. `lib/startup-preflight.ts` (new — 244 lines)

Runtime preflight checks (distinct from `lib/preflight.ts`, which validates dashboard build artifacts):

- `ensureGit(context)` — interactive install on missing
- `ensureTmux()` — interactive install on missing
- `warnAboutLegacyStorage()`, `warnAboutOpenClawStatus(config)`
- `runtimePreflight(config)` — top-level orchestrator: tools + state warnings + idle-sleep + OpenClaw credentials, called once from `runStartup`

This collapses ~32 lines of inline orchestration in `runStartup` into a single `await runtimePreflight(config)` call.

### 3. `lib/shutdown.ts` (new — 129 lines)

`installShutdownHandlers({ configPath, projectId })` extracts the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler block (85 lines) from `runStartup`'s closure into its own module. The handler logic is identical: stop lifecycle workers → kill active sessions → record last-stop → unregister → await janitor sweep → exit with code 130/0.

Module-level `handlersInstalled` + `shuttingDown` guards make a second call to `installShutdownHandlers` a true no-op (added in cbbd4ade after review feedback).

## Behavior changes

This PR is **mostly** a mechanical extraction, with **two small behavior corrections** introduced via review feedback (commit `cbbd4ade`):

1. **`warnAboutLegacyStorage` count fix** — pre-existing bug carried over verbatim from `start.ts`: the function gates on the count of non-empty hash dirs but printed `hashDirs.length` (total, including empty dirs). Users with mostly-empty hash dirs would see an inflated migration count. Renamed `sessionCount` → `nonEmptyDirCount` (it always counted dirs, not sessions) and used it in the message. Visible change: the warning's number is now correct.

2. **Shutdown handler is now process-wide idempotent** — the original closure-scoped `shuttingDown` guard was per-invocation, so calling `installShutdownHandlers` twice would have registered duplicate listeners. Module-level guards make it truly idempotent. No visible change today (the function is only called once), but the abstraction now matches its docstring.

Everything else (preflight checks, install helpers, the shutdown logic itself) is byte-for-byte the same as the original.

## What's NOT in this PR (intentional)

- **The duplicated kill-and-record loop in `ao stop`** is left as-is. It has different verbosity (spinner, warnings, per-project output) and different options (`--purge-session`) than the signal handler. Unifying the two paths is a behavior-shaping change that belongs with the daemon/stop restructure planned for PR B.
- **No `Prompter` abstraction yet.** Of the 7 `isHumanCaller()` callsites, only 2 are the "prompt-or-skip" pattern that benefits from a wrapper; the other 5 are behavioral branches that gain leverage only when PR B restructures the §3.x menu. Deferred to PR B.
- **No new unit tests for the extracted modules.** The new files are now independently testable (especially `shutdown.ts` with its multi-project session tracking). Worth a follow-up — out of scope for this mechanical PR.

## Cumulative diff

```
 packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts        | 408 ++--------------------
 packages/cli/src/lib/install-helpers.ts   | 102 ++++++++
 packages/cli/src/lib/shutdown.ts          | 129 +++++++++
 packages/cli/src/lib/startup-preflight.ts | 244 ++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 493 insertions(+), 390 deletions(-)
```

Net core LOC: +103 (interface overhead + the two small correctness fixes). The win here is **organization**, not raw deletion — that comes in PR B.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — green
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — green
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (46 pre-existing warnings, all in unmodified files)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 594 passing, 8 failing
  - The 8 failures are **pre-existing on `upstream/main`** (verified by stashing my changes and re-running). All in `stop command` tests, all fail with the same `process.exit(1)` from the catch handler in `ao stop`. Not regressions from this PR.

## Plan reference

- **PR A (this one):** mechanical extractions — preflight, install-helpers, shutdown
- **PR B (next):** reshape main flow — `ensureDaemon` + `resolveOrCreateProject` + `Prompter`, collapse the running/not-running fork
- **PR C (after B):** drop `startNewOrchestrator` YAML mutation, prune the multi-choice menu

title: Session is locked to its first PR — can't reattach when that PR is closed or replaced
body:
## Summary

A session is permanently bound to the first PR it sees. Once that PR is closed (for any reason — wrong target branch, accidental close, force-close to redo against a different repo), there's no way to point the session at a replacement PR. The session enters a terminal-feeling state and downstream commands (`ao session claim-pr`, `ao report pr-created`) reject further updates.

## Concrete repro (just hit this on PR #1616)

1. `ao spawn` creates session `ao-120`.
2. Agent creates PR `#180` against the user's fork (wrong target).
3. AO records `#180` as the session's PR (`pr_created` state).
4. User closes `#180` because it targeted the wrong repo.
5. Agent re-pushes the same branch and opens PR `#1616` against `ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator` (correct target).
6. `ao session claim-pr https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1616` →
   ```
   Failed to claim PR for session ao-120: Error: Command failed:
   gh pr view 1616 --repo harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator --json state
   GraphQL: Could not resolve to a PullRequest with the number of 1616.
   ```
   The repo argument is hardcoded to the repo of the **original** PR, not derived from the URL being claimed.
7. `ao report pr-created --pr-url <upstream-url>` → `Report rejected: PR already closed`. Session state is sticky.

After step 6/7 there's no documented path forward. The session is functionally orphaned from a tracking standpoint even though the actual work (the new PR) is fine.

## Why this is annoying in practice

The \"close one PR, open another\" flow is common:
- Wrong base branch / wrong repo (this session's case — closing fork PR, reopening against upstream).
- Accidentally `gh pr close` then need to recover.
- Stacked-PR workflows where an intermediate PR gets superseded.
- Reviewer asks for a fresh PR against a different base after a refactor.

In all these cases the **session** is still doing the same work — only the PR identifier changed. AO should let the user say \"this session now tracks PR X instead.\"

## Two ways to fix this

### Minimum (bug fix): allow re-attachment to a different PR

`ao session claim-pr` should:
1. Parse the repo from the provided PR URL, not reuse the cached repo from the previously-attached PR.
2. Accept claims even when the session has a closed/merged PR currently attached. The new PR replaces the old reference; the old one stays in history.

This restores the existing single-PR-per-session model but unbreaks the close-and-reopen flow.

### Stretch (feature): support multiple PRs per session

Some workflows produce multiple PRs from one session legitimately:
- Stacked PRs for incremental review.
- A refactor PR + a feature PR that depends on it, both authored from the same session.
- A test PR that gets merged separately from the implementation PR.

Today the session metadata's `pr` field is a single object. A `prs: PRRef[]` array (with a `primary` flag for dashboard display) would model this cleanly. CI / review polling would iterate the open ones.

## Suggested scope

Land the bug fix first (it's a small change and unblocks today's flow). The multi-PR feature is bigger and deserves its own design discussion — happy to file as a separate issue if the maintainers prefer.

## Files likely involved (from a quick look)

- `packages/cli/src/commands/session.ts` — `claim-pr` subcommand: where the repo gets hardcoded.
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — `claimPR` method (around line 2657 per CLAUDE.md): re-attachment validation and the \"PR already closed\" gate that rejects `ao report pr-created`.
- Session metadata schema (`pr`, `prAutoDetect`) in core types.

I haven't read the exact lines for the rejection path; happy to follow up with specifics if useful.

## Workaround for now

Manually edit the session metadata file at `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}` to update the `pr.url`, `pr.number`, and `pr.state` fields. Not great for non-developers.

title: fix(core): reliable prompt delivery and accurate task prompt wording
body:
## Summary
- **Readiness polling**: Replaces the blind 3-second timer with a poll loop that checks for agent readiness via `tmux capture-pane` before sending the task prompt
- **Delivery verification**: After sending, polls to confirm the agent transitioned to active state; only marks `promptDelivered = "true"` after confirmation
- **Duplicate send prevention**: Tracks `sendSucceeded` flag to avoid re-sending when delivery verification times out (agent may be slow to start)
- **Unified issue reference format**: Uses `#` consistently in both system prompt and task prompt
- **Accurate task prompt wording**: Changes "full issue details" to "title, description, and labels" — addressing reviewer feedback that the original wording was misleading since comments, images, and linked issues aren't included

## Context
Addresses #1582 and review feedback from @illegalcall about the task prompt wording being misleading.

When a session spawns, the task prompt often never reached the agent because:
1. The 3s blind timer didn't account for slow Claude Code startup
2. tmux accepted keystrokes into the loading screen without error
3. `promptDelivered` was set to `"true"` even on failed delivery

## Test plan
- [x] All 1038 core tests pass (20 prompt-builder, 97 spawn tests)
- [x] All 51 tracker-github tests pass
- [x] TypeScript typecheck passes for core and tracker-github
- [x] ESLint lint passes (0 errors)

Closes #1582

title: feat(core): wire activity events into lifecycle-manager failure paths (#1511)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1528 (the activity-events infra). Wires 17 new `recordActivityEvent` emits into `lifecycle-manager.ts` so the diagnostic-agent RCA loop has real evidence to query when something fails. Closes the lifecycle-domain V1 instrumentation slice from issue #1511 (web-domain slice still open separately).

E2E verified live against a real project: agent ran `ao events list --session ta-7`, parsed the new `report_watcher.triggered` + `lifecycle.transition` events, and synthesized a correct root cause unprompted.

## Events wired

Each fires at a previously-silent failure / state-change path. Bundled into 4 commits.

### B1 — Plugin-call failures (`cd6e04d5`)
| Event | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `scm.batch_enrich_failed` | line 540 catch | GraphQL batch failure → all PRs lose enrichment for that cycle |
| `scm.detect_pr_succeeded` | line 578 success | RCA: \"when did AO first see my PR?\" |
| `scm.detect_pr_failed` | line 583 catch | Per-session detect failure |
| `scm.review_fetch_failed` | line 1410 silent catch | Review comments invisible to user otherwise |
| `scm.poll_pr_failed` | line 1053 silent catch | Terminal-PR detection (merge/close) failure |
| `runtime.probe_failed` | line 819 silent catch | `runtime.isAlive` failure |
| `agent.process_probe_failed` (×2 sites) | lines 935 + 983 | `isProcessRunning` failure with `where` discriminator |
| `agent.activity_probe_failed` | line 943 outer catch | Whole activity-probing block bailed |

### B2 — Reaction lifecycle (`22a30ed8`)
| Event | Where |
|---|---|
| `reaction.escalated` | line 1218 (max_retries / max_duration cause) |
| `reaction.send_to_agent_failed` | line 1243 silent catch |
| `reaction.action_succeeded` | combined for send-to-agent / notify / auto-merge |

### B3 — Auto-cleanup + poll cycle + detecting escalation (`3d0c0e8c`)
| Event | Where |
|---|---|
| `session.auto_cleanup_deferred` | line 1762 |
| `session.auto_cleanup_completed` | line 1782 |
| `session.auto_cleanup_failed` (level=error) | line 1805 |
| `lifecycle.poll_failed` (level=error) | line 2250 outer catch |
| `detecting.escalated` | line 1839 with one-shot guard via `detectingEscalatedAt` metadata |

### B4 — Report watcher (`03787c03` + `80a2260d`)
| Event | Where |
|---|---|
| `report_watcher.triggered` | line 2125, with `isNewTrigger` one-shot guard (added in `80a2260d` after live observation showed it firing 116 times in a few hours) |

## Type union additions (`activity-events.ts`)

- `ActivityEventSource`: added `scm`, `runtime`, `agent`, `reaction`, `report-watcher`
- `ActivityEventKind`: 17 new kinds across the four bundles

## Tests

`packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager-instrumentation.test.ts` — 18 tests, all passing:
- One per event for the happy \"emit fires\" path
- B2 invariant test: `lm.check` completes successfully even if `recordActivityEvent` itself throws
- Regression test for the `report_watcher.triggered` one-shot guard

## Verification

- ✅ `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean
- ✅ Targeted suite (`lifecycle-manager-instrumentation`) — 18/18 pass
- ✅ Full core suite — 1058+/1060 pass (the 2 failing are pre-existing OpenCode mock-binary baseline flakes, unrelated to this PR)
- ✅ E2E live: orchestrator running this build emitted the new event kinds (153 total events captured during the test, including `lifecycle.transition`, `activity.transition`, `reaction.action_succeeded`, `report_watcher.triggered`)
- ✅ Independent code review by Codex — chain of reasoning validated, fix shape approved

## Invariants preserved (per CLAUDE.md \"lifecycle-manager has subtle state dependencies\")

- **B1 state-mutate-before-emit:** every emit lands in the same catch / after the same observer call as the existing logic; never moves a state mutation
- **B2 never throws into lifecycle:** proven by the cross-cutting test that mocks `recordActivityEvent` to throw
- **B3 re-entrancy guard on `polling`:** unchanged
- **B4 `Promise.allSettled` semantics:** unchanged
- **B7 reaction-tracker clear ordering:** unchanged
- **B9 report-watcher one-shot:** new emit gated on `isNewTrigger` so it fires once per trigger activation, not every poll while active
- **B11 concurrent `checkSession` interleaving:** unchanged (SQLite WAL handles serialization)

## Out of scope (separate tickets)

- Web-domain instrumentation (gist criteria 9, 10, 11): `/api/sessions` count/duration emit, `POST /api/activity-events` ingestion endpoint, client-side `ui.*` emitters. Pratik's separate ask to Ashish, not landed yet.
- `session.kill_started` event (gist asks for both spawn AND kill start events; Ashish added spawn_started, kill_started skipped — small follow-up if it bothers RCA later).
- Discovered during E2E (not in this PR): `ao start` auto-create writes a wrapped local config (`projects: { id: ... }`) but the new global-resolution loader rejects that as `kind: \"old-format\"`, leaving projects in `degradedProjects` and the supervisor with zero projects to poll. Manual workaround: write GLOBAL `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` with the project registry + LOCAL `agent-orchestrator.yaml` flat (no `projects:` wrapper). Worth a separate CLI/orchestration ticket.
- Suggested follow-up from Codex review: `report_watcher.still_active` milestone event (every Nth poll while persisting) for continued observability without spam.

Closes #1511 (lifecycle-domain slice only — web slice tracked separately).

title: refactor(cli): extract resolveOrCreateProject (PR B.1, stacked on #1617)
body:
## Summary

PR B.1 of the start.ts refactor plan. **Stacked on #1617 (PR A) — review #1617 first.**

Replaces the per-arg-shape project-resolution dispatch in start.ts's not-running path with a single \`resolveOrCreateProject(arg, deps)\` call. The new \`lib/resolve-project.ts\` module dispatches internally:

- \`arg\` is a URL → \`fromUrl\`: clone (or reuse) + load/generate config + match by repo
- \`arg\` is a local path → \`fromPath\`: load existing or addProject or autoCreate
- \`arg\` is a project id or undefined → \`fromCwdOrId\`: loadConfig + global fallback + registerFlatConfig recovery

All return the same \`{ config, projectId, project, source, justCreated, parsed? }\` shape so the caller treats every result uniformly.

## What changed in this PR

| File | Before → After | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| \`packages/cli/src/lib/resolve-project.ts\` | new | 294 lines — the unified resolver |
| \`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts\` | ~2140 → ~1980 (-160) | 85-line dispatch block + the dead \`handleUrlStart\` (~63 lines) deleted; replaced by 12-line call site |

\`handleUrlStart\` had no other callers after the migration and was deleted.

## Behavior

**Preserved exactly.** Each helper is a near-verbatim move of the corresponding inline branch in start.ts. \`fromUrl\` is \`handleUrlStart\`'s body. \`fromPath\` mirrors the original load/autoCreate/addProject cascade. \`fromCwdOrId\` keeps the \`registerFlatConfig\` recovery path with identical semantics.

The same 8 stop-command tests fail on this branch and on upstream/main — verified pre-existing, not caused by this PR.

## Dependency-injection design

\`resolve-project.ts\` takes a \`ResolveDeps\` object holding the start.ts-internal helpers (\`addProjectToConfig\`, \`autoCreateConfig\`, \`resolveProject\`, \`resolveProjectByRepo\`, \`registerFlatConfig\`, \`cloneRepo\`). The caller (start.ts) builds this once and passes it in.

This keeps the new module decoupled from start.ts's other concerns (interactive prompts, agent detection, project-type detection) without forcing a circular import or moving 400+ more lines into the new file.

## What's NOT in this PR (intentional)

The "AO is already running + URL/path arg" branch in start.ts still has its own inline clone+register block. That block deliberately avoided \`handleUrlStart\` because of legacy wrapped-config concerns (see comment at original line 1432). Migrating it to share \`fromUrl\` is a small follow-up before PR B.2 collapses the running-vs-not-running fork.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm build\` — green
- [x] \`pnpm typecheck\` — green
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` — 0 errors (46 pre-existing warnings)
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test\` — 594 passing, 8 pre-existing failures from upstream/main (same set as PR A)

## Plan reference

- **PR A (#1617):** mechanical extractions — preflight, install-helpers, shutdown
- **PR B.1 (this one):** unified project resolution for the not-running path
- **PR B.1 follow-up:** migrate §3.2 inline clone+register to share \`fromUrl\`
- **PR B.2:** \`ensureDaemon\` — collapse the running/not-running fork
- **PR B.3:** drop \`startNewOrchestrator\`, prune the multi-choice menu, Prompter where it falls out

title: refactor(spawn): plugin-owned preflight + collapse project resolution
body:
## Summary

PR 2 of the `ao spawn` refactor (PR 1 = #1616, merged). Three small structural changes bundled because they all touch `spawn.ts`:

1. **Plugin-owned preflight** — replace the CLI's hardcoded `if runtime === "tmux" check tmux` / `if tracker === "github" check gh auth` switches with a 4-line loop that calls each selected plugin's optional `preflight()`.
2. **Project-resolution collapse** — three near-duplicate prefix/no-prefix/no-issue branches → one `resolveProjectAndIssue()` helper using `resolveSpawnTarget`'s fallback parameter.
3. **Micro-deletes** — drop unused `return session.id`, drop now-orphan `checkTmux`/`checkGhAuth` + their tests.

## Why (Change 1, the architectural one)

Before:
```ts
if (runtime === "tmux") await preflight.checkTmux();
const needsGitHubAuth =
  project?.tracker?.plugin === "github" ||
  (options?.claimPr && project?.scm?.plugin === "github");
if (needsGitHubAuth) await preflight.checkGhAuth();
```

This violates the project's own constraint ([CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)):
> "Plugin slots are the extension point. Don't add configuration surface when a new plugin is the right answer."

Adding `runtime-podman`, `tracker-jira`, or `scm-bitbucket` would require editing this CLI switch.

After: each plugin declares its own `preflight()`. The CLI iterates the plugins selected for this spawn and calls them. Adding a new plugin does not touch `spawn.ts`.

## What changed

### `core` — new contract (commit `245257e3`)

- `PreflightContext` describes **intent** (`willClaimExistingPR`, `role`), not CLI flag names. Plugins should never learn about specific flags — translate flags into intent at the CLI boundary so adding a new flag doesn't ripple into every plugin that cares about a related operation.
- Added optional `preflight?(context: PreflightContext): Promise<void>` to `Runtime`, `Agent`, `Workspace`, `Tracker`, `SCM`. Backwards-compatible: existing plugins keep working unchanged.

### Plugins — implementations (commit `d5533810`)

- `runtime-tmux`: checks `tmux -V`, throws platform-appropriate install hint
- `tracker-github`: checks `gh --version` and `gh auth status` (always exercised when tracker is configured — issueId fetch + lifecycle polling)
- `scm-github`: same gh auth checks but **only when `context.intent.willClaimExistingPR` is true** — otherwise spawns that don't touch PRs would unnecessarily require gh credentials

### CLI — orchestration + cleanup (commit `107f6480`)

- `runSpawnPreflight` shrinks to a registry-iterating loop
- `lib/preflight.ts` keeps `checkPort` + `checkBuilt` (still used by `ao start` / `ao dashboard`); drops `checkTmux` / `checkGhAuth`
- Project resolution: three near-duplicate try/catch blocks → one helper

## Verification

- `pnpm build` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — spawn tests **23/23** pass; new plugin-iteration tests cover: surfacing a plugin's preflight error, skipping `scm.preflight` without `--claim-pr`, forwarding `willClaimExistingPR=true` with `--claim-pr`, not iterating tracker when none configured
- Plugin tests (`runtime-tmux`, `tracker-github`, `scm-github`) pass
- ⚠️ 8 pre-existing `start.test.ts` "stop command" failures — verified to fail on bare `upstream/main` too (`git checkout upstream/main -- packages/cli && pnpm test`). Unrelated to this PR.

## LOC

Roughly net-zero on production code. The wins are structural:
- New plugins self-declare prereqs → CLI never edited again for new plugins
- Intent-based context → new CLI flags don't leak into plugin code
- Project resolution: ~25 lines of duplicated try/catch → ~6 lines

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn` with tmux runtime + github tracker, normal flow works
- [ ] Manual: temporarily break gh auth (`gh auth logout`), confirm clean error before spawn starts
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn --claim-pr <pr>` with linear tracker — verify scm preflight runs even though tracker doesn't need gh
- [ ] Code review on `PreflightContext` shape — `willClaimExistingPR` reads as intent rather than flag name; is there a future intent flag worth adding now?
