title: fix(web): source sidebar orchestrator from API field, not session list
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1615. The merged version of "Open orchestrator" never renders for any project because it looks up the orchestrator inside the `sessions` prop — but `/api/sessions/route.ts:121-128` strips ALL orchestrators from that array before returning. They live on a separate `orchestrators` field of the same response, which the merged code doesn't read.

Same root cause silently breaks the pre-existing **orchestrator icon button** next to the dashboard icon in each project row (`ProjectSidebar.tsx:500-527`). Both render conditions are gated on the same dead lookup.

## Repro on `main`

1. Run `ao start` on any project.
2. Confirm an orchestrator session exists on disk (e.g. `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<project>/sessions/<prefix>-orchestrator.json`).
3. Open the dashboard. Hover the project in the sidebar → click the 3-dot menu.
4. **Expected:** "Open orchestrator" entry. **Actual:** menu shows only "Project settings" and "Remove project".
5. Same project row: the orchestrator icon button next to the dashboard icon is also missing.
6. DevTools → Network → `/api/sessions` response: `sessions[]` contains zero orchestrators; the `orchestrators[]` field has them.

## Fix

Add an `orchestrators` prop to `ProjectSidebar`. Each parent passes the data it already has:

| Parent | Source |
|---|---|
| `Dashboard.tsx` | `activeOrchestrators` (already in scope) |
| `PullRequestsPage.tsx` | `orchestratorLinks` (already in scope) |
| `sessions/[id]/page.tsx` | reads the `orchestrators` field already returned by `/api/sessions` and threads it through `SessionPageShell` → `SessionDetail` as `sidebarOrchestrators` |

Both the menu entry and the icon button render off `orchestratorByProject.get(project.id)`. The live-vs-terminal selection lives in the API (`selectPreferredOrchestratorId`) and is no longer the sidebar's concern.

Net **-17 lines** vs the current merged code.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 820/823 (same 3 pre-existing failures as `upstream/main`, all unrelated)
- [x] Sidebar tests refocused: 18/18 pass; the prop is the contract, the API tests cover selection
- [ ] Manual: hover sidebar project with running orchestrator → 3-dot menu shows "Open orchestrator" → click → lands on orchestrator session
- [ ] Manual: orchestrator icon button next to dashboard icon also appears

title: refactor(cli): collapse running/not-running fork via ensureDaemon (PR B.2)
body:
## Summary

Step 2 of PR B in [ao-118's `start.ts` refactor plan](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts). Bundles the deferred B.1 follow-up (the §3.2 inline clone+register block was due to migrate to share `fromUrl`) — that block is now deleted outright by the fork collapse, so the follow-up disappears rather than landing as its own diff.

The three branches in `start.ts` that handled the daemon-already-running cases (§3.2 URL/path, §3.3 project-id, §3.5 non-human info dump) collapse into a single attach pipeline that runs after `resolveOrCreateProject`. The fork between attach and spawn becomes one post-resolve decision point.

## What changed

- New `packages/cli/src/lib/daemon.ts`:
  - `attachToDaemon(running) -> AttachedDaemon { port, pid, notifyProjectChange() }` — pure handle plus a typed `{ok} | {ok: false, reason}` cache-invalidation result, replacing the open-coded fetch + try/catch that lived in two places.
  - `killExistingDaemon(running)` — SIGTERM → `waitForExit` → SIGKILL → `unregister`, used by the "Restart everything" menu option. Replaces the inline restart code in §3.4.

- `resolve-project.ts` gains a `{ targetGlobalRegistry?: boolean }` option:
  - When `true`, `fromUrl` and `fromPath` register against the global config (the daemon's source of truth) rather than into a cwd-local one.
  - `fromUrl`'s global-registry branch is a near-verbatim move of the §3.2 inline clone+register block, including the global-registry dedup and the flat-local-config write that §3.2 deliberately preferred over `fromUrl`'s wrapped yaml.
  - `fromCwdOrId` short-circuits straight to the global registry for project-id args while running, with the same "not registered" error the original §3.3 raised.

- `start.ts` dispatch:
  - **Running + non-human + (no arg | URL | path)** → info dump, exit 0 (preserved §3.5; project-id args still fall through so automation can `ao start <id>` against a live daemon).
  - **Running + human + no arg** → menu preserved (open / quit / add / new / restart). `restart` now routes through `killExistingDaemon`; `new` sets `startNewOrchestrator` and falls through to the attach path.
  - `resolveOrCreateProject(arg, deps, { targetGlobalRegistry: !!running })`.
  - **Running** → `attachAndSpawnOrchestrator` helper. The §3.2 short-circuit (URL/path arg whose project is already in `running.projects` skips the orchestrator-spawn and just opens the dashboard) is preserved.
  - **Not running** → existing `runStartup` + `register` + janitor + `installShutdownHandlers`.

- `attachAndSpawnOrchestrator` unifies §3.2/§3.3 messaging behind a single `justCreated` discriminator:
  - `justCreated=true`: \"Spawning orchestrator session...\" → \"Project '...' registered in the global config.\" → \"Orchestrator session ready: ...\"
  - `justCreated=false`: \"Attaching to running AO instance...\" → \"Orchestrator session ready: ...\" → \"Project '...' reattached to running daemon (PID ...)\"
  - Both flows then `notifyProjectChange` (warns on failure, never throws — the dashboard might be down), print the lifecycle-attach notice when the project isn't yet supervised, and either `openUrl` (human) or print the URL (non-human).

No behavior change. The unified pipeline matches the original §3.2/§3.3/§3.5 paths line-for-line on prints, prompts, exits, browser opens, and dashboard cache invalidation. `startNewOrchestrator` and the §3.4 menu options remain intact. Those are user-visible feature changes that land in PR B.3.

title: feat(pipeline): v0.1 — core types, state machine, flat-file store
body:
Sub-task of #1346 (v0). First in the build order — no dependencies.

All sub-tasks target base branch `pipelines` (not `main`).

## Design decisions (locked from cluster planning — applies to all v0/v1/v2 sub-tasks)

These supersede language in #1345/#1346/#1349/#1350 where it conflicts:

1. **Stops at v2.** No v3 (workstreams).
2. **Fresh session per stage.** Each pipeline stage spawns a brand-new AO session with its own worktree, runtime, and dashboard card. Sessions are killed at stage completion.
3. **Stages are talk-to-able.** A running stage's session accepts mid-task user input via `Runtime.sendInput` exactly like any other AO session. No special chat machinery.
4. **No `Agent.executeTask` plugin contract.** Stages run via existing session machinery. The original spec's non-interactive process model is dropped.
5. **No `Agent.sendFollowUpToTask`.** Mid-task input flows through native agent input handling (Claude Code, Codex both support this) over normal session input.
6. **Findings via convention, not contract.** Stages drop `findings.jsonl` at `{workspacePath}/.ao/pipeline-findings.jsonl`. Engine reads from there. No agent code change required beyond a system-prompt addition (handled in prompt assembly layer 4).
7. **`supportedTaskModes` is a manifest field**, not an interface method. `("review" | "code" | "answer")[]`, defaults to `[]`. Engine validates at config load.
8. **`maxLoopRounds` is per-stage**, not pipeline-global.
9. **Concurrency cap follows spec** — `maxConcurrentStages` defaults to 1 in production until first stable release.
10. `command` executor stages are NOT talk-to-able (they're shell scripts, not agents).

## Scope (this PR)

Pure data-shape and reducer logic. No I/O outside the flat-file store.

- Core types in `packages/core/src/pipeline/`:
  - `Pipeline`, `Stage`, `Artifact`, `LoopState`, `RunState`, `EngineState`
  - Branded IDs: `PipelineId`, `RunId`, `StageRunId`
  - Three-tier exit: stage / run / loop
- Pure reducer + effect interpreter (returns `{ state, effects[] }`, effects executed elsewhere later)
- Flat-file store at `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{projectId}/pipelines/`:
  - `runs/{runId}.json`
  - `stages/{stageRunId}.json`
  - `artifacts/{runId}/{stageRunId}.jsonl`
  - `loops/{runId}.json`
- Two-level state (`EngineState` global counters + `RunState` per run)
- Vitest coverage for reducer transitions and store roundtrip

## Out of scope (this PR)

- All executors
- All CLI commands
- Lifecycle integration / engine ticking
- Web UI
- Plugin contract changes (none planned at all — see decision 4)

## Acceptance

- `pnpm typecheck` clean across `core` and dependents
- `pnpm test --filter @aoagents/ao-core` green
- New tests cover: reducer happy path, reducer invalid transitions, store roundtrip
- No imports from `@aoagents/ao-cli` or `@aoagents/ao-web`
- Component/file size limits respected (≤400 LOC per file where reasonable)
- PR opened against `pipelines` base branch

title: feat(pipeline): v0.2 — agent executor (fresh session per stage, talk-to-able)
body:
Sub-task of #1346 (v0). **Depends on v0.1.**

Base branch: `pipelines`. See v0.1 issue for the full list of design decisions that apply to all v0/v1/v2 sub-tasks.

## Scope

The `agent` executor — the bridge between the pipeline engine and a real AO session.

- New executor in `packages/core/src/pipeline/executors/agent.ts`
- For each stage:
  1. Spawn a **fresh AO session** via the existing session manager (its own worktree, runtime, dashboard card)
  2. Inject the task as the initial prompt via prompt assembly layer 4 (new): stage task descriptor + findings-write-path instructions
  3. Wait for completion: session reaches `idle` AND a `findings.jsonl` artifact exists at `{workspacePath}/.ao/pipeline-findings.jsonl`
  4. Harvest findings, write to artifact store
  5. Kill the session (worktree cleanup goes through normal session-archive path)
- New optional manifest field on agent plugins: `supportedTaskModes?: ("review" | "code" | "answer")[]`. Defaults to `[]`. Engine validates at config load — pipeline configs that route a stage with `task.mode = "review"` to an agent that doesn't claim `"review"` fail at load, not runtime.
- Light lifecycle integration: pipeline engine ticks alongside the existing lifecycle manager (no new polling — piggyback on the 5s SSE interval per C-14).
- During the stage, the session is **fully talk-to-able**: `ao send`, dashboard chat, terminal attach all work as for any session. Messages flow through the agent's native mid-task input handling. (Per locked decision 3 + 5.)

## Out of scope

- `command` and `builtin` executors (v1.2)
- DAG / parallel scheduling (v1.1)
- CLI surface (v0.3)
- UI (v2.x)

## Acceptance

- A 1-stage pipeline can be triggered programmatically (no CLI yet) and runs end-to-end
- The stage's session shows up in the dashboard during execution and accepts `ao send` mid-flight
- Findings appear in the run's artifacts when the agent writes to the conventional path
- `supportedTaskModes` validation rejects mismatched configs at load time with a clear error
- Vitest coverage on the executor (mocked session manager)
- PR opened against `pipelines`

title: feat(pipeline): v1.3 — workspace classes, predicate DSL, exitPredicates
body:
Sub-task of #1349 (v1). **Depends on v1.1.** Can run partially in parallel with v1.2.

Base branch: `pipelines`. See v0.1 for cluster design decisions.

## Scope

Three things that round out v1: workspace classes, the typed predicate DSL, and `Pipeline.exitPredicates`.

- **Workspace classes (revised under fresh-session-per-stage):**
  - The original spec's `shared-ro` / `isolated-rw` classes were designed for a model where stages shared workspaces. With fresh sessions, isolation is the default.
  - Collapses to: `independent` (default, fresh session and worktree) vs `read-siblings` (stage can read prior siblings' artifacts via the artifact store; still fresh session/worktree, just artifact-read access).
  - `WorkspaceGuard`: validates at config load that a stage doesn't claim it needs sibling reads when no upstream stages exist.
- **Typed Predicate DSL** — used in `Stage.routes` (replacing v1.1's hardcoded form) and in `Pipeline.exitPredicates`:
  - Leaf predicates: `all_pass`, `no_open_findings`, `finding_count_below(n)`
  - Boolean ops: `and`, `or`, `not`
  - JSON-schema validated at config load
- **`Pipeline.exitPredicates`** — declarative run-completion conditions. A run reaches the `loop_succeeded` / `loop_failed` terminal state based on these.
- **`CONFIG_CHANGED` distinction** — structural changes (DAG shape) vs tuning changes (predicate thresholds, retry counts) get different handling at engine reload.

## Out of scope

- New executors (already in v1.2)
- API / UI (v2.x)

## Acceptance

- Predicate DSL parses successfully for valid configs, rejects with line-precise errors for malformed
- `read-siblings` stages can read sibling stage artifacts at runtime
- `WorkspaceGuard` rejects orphan `read-siblings` declarations at load
- A pipeline reaches `loop_succeeded` only when its `exitPredicates` evaluate true
- A pipeline reaches `loop_failed` when its `exitPredicates` cannot be satisfied (max rounds reached)
- Vitest coverage on DSL parser and evaluator
- PR opened against `pipelines`

title: feat(pipeline): v0.1 — core types, state machine, flat-file store
body:
Closes #1627. Sub-task of #1346 (v0). First in the build order — no dependencies.

## Summary

Implements the v0 foundation of the pipeline engine: pure data shapes, a synchronous reducer that returns intent-only effects, and a flat-file store. No I/O, no executors, no driver — those land in follow-up sub-tasks.

## What's in this PR

**Core types** (`packages/core/src/pipeline/types.ts`):
- Branded IDs: `PipelineId`, `RunId`, `StageRunId`, `ArtifactId`
- `Pipeline`, `Stage`, `Artifact`, `LoopState`, `RunState`, `EngineState`
- Three-tier exit:
  - Stage tier — `StageStatus` (pending → running → succeeded/failed/skipped/outdated)
  - Run tier   — `RunTerminationReason` (completed / stage_failure / manual_cancel / config_change / outdated / worker_dead)
  - Loop tier  — `LoopStateName` (running / awaiting_context / done / stalled / terminated)
- Two-level state: `EngineState` engine-global indices + `RunState` per run.

**Reducer + effects** (`reducer.ts`, `reducer-helpers.ts`, `events.ts`):
- Signature: `reduce(state, event) → { state, effects }`. Pure, synchronous, never reads the clock — every event carries `now`.
- Events handled: `TRIGGER_FIRED`, `STAGE_STARTED`, `STAGE_COMPLETED`, `STAGE_FAILED`, `NEW_SHA_DETECTED`, `RUN_CANCELLED`, `CONFIG_CHANGED`, `TICK`.
- Effects emitted: `START_STAGE`, `CANCEL_STAGE`, `PERSIST_RUN`, `PERSIST_LOOP_STATE`, `APPEND_ARTIFACTS`, `EMIT_OBSERVATION`.

**Flat-file store** (`store.ts`, `paths.ts`):
- Layout under any root (callers pass `getProjectPipelinesDir(projectId)`):
  - `runs/{runId}.json`
  - `stages/{stageRunId}.json`
  - `artifacts/{runId}/{stageRunId}.jsonl`
  - `loops/{runId}.json`
- All writes go through `atomicWriteFileSync`; artifacts are append-only JSONL.

**Locked design decisions from cluster planning** (encoded in types):
- `maxLoopRounds` is per-stage (not pipeline-global).
- `maxConcurrentStages` defaults to 1 in v0.
- `supportedTaskModes` is a manifest field on agent plugins — no `executeTask` interface method (decision 4).
- Findings surfaced via convention at `{workspacePath}/.ao/pipeline-findings.jsonl` — exported as `PIPELINE_FINDINGS_FILENAME`.

## Tests

30 new tests, all green:
- `pipeline-reducer.test.ts` (19 cases): happy path; invalid transitions emit `pipeline.invalid_transition` observations without state mutation; `NEW_SHA_DETECTED` outdates the in-flight run; `STAGE_FAILED` stalls the run and skips remaining stages; `CONFIG_CHANGED` terminates active runs; `loopRounds` increments on continuation triggers; reducer purity (no `Date.now()` calls, input state unmutated).
- `pipeline-store.test.ts` (11 cases): run/stage/loop save+load roundtrips; JSONL append semantics across calls; null returns for missing files; layout creation for empty stores.

## Out of scope (subsequent sub-tasks)

Executors, CLI commands, lifecycle integration / engine ticking, web UI, plugin contract changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` green (1089 tests, +30 new)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean across core and dependents (after `pnpm build`)
- [x] Lint clean on new files (no errors; pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] No imports from `@aoagents/ao-cli` or `@aoagents/ao-web`
- [x] All source files ≤400 LOC
- [x] PR base is `pipelines` (not `main`)

## Notes for reviewers

- This PR's spec lives in #1627. The current issue's "Design decisions (locked)" supersede the parent #1346 where they conflict — most notably `maxLoopRounds` moved from pipeline to stage, and there is no `Agent.executeTask` plugin interface change.
- Store root is parameterized intentionally — the engine sub-task will wire it to `getProjectPipelinesDir(projectId)` (helper added in this PR).

title: feat(pipeline): v0.2 — agent executor (fresh session per stage, talk-to-able)
body:
Closes #1628. Depends on v0.1 (#1636). Targets `pipelines`.

## Summary

Bridges the v0.1 reducer / store to a real AO session so a 1-stage pipeline can run end-to-end and produce findings.

- **Agent executor** (`packages/core/src/pipeline/executors/agent.ts`)
  - For each stage: spawn a fresh session via the existing `SessionManager` (own worktree, runtime, dashboard card), inject the task as the initial prompt, wait until the session reaches `idle` AND `{workspacePath}/.ao/pipeline-findings.jsonl` exists, parse the file as `ArtifactInput` records, kill the session through the normal archive path.
  - Sessions are fully talk-to-able for their entire lifetime: `ao send`, dashboard chat, terminal attach all work as for any session, since this leans on the standard `SessionManager.spawn()` path.
- **Pipeline engine** (`packages/core/src/pipeline/engine.ts`)
  - Holds `EngineState`, dispatches events through the v0.1 reducer, executes effects (persist, append artifacts, START_STAGE, CANCEL_STAGE), and exposes a re-entrant `tick()` the caller drives off the existing 5s SSE poll. No new polling loop introduced (per C-14).
  - `command` / `builtin` executors are v1.2 — `START_STAGE` for those kinds synthesizes `STAGE_FAILED` so runs terminate cleanly instead of hanging.

title: PTY file-descriptor leak in dashboard mux server exhausts macOS system PTY pool after 10–20h
body:
## Summary

After running AO for 10–20 hours of normal use, the macOS system-wide PTY pool gets exhausted (`kern.tty.ptmx_max=511` on default macOS). Once the cap is hit, **nothing on the system can spawn a new PTY** — not just AO. Symptoms include:

- Dashboard session restore fails: `tmux new-session` errors with `create window failed: fork failed: Device not configured`.
- Any new terminal launch (VS Code, iTerm, etc.) fails: `The terminal process failed to launch: A native exception occurred during launch (posix_spawnp failed.)`.
- `ao spawn` and any other AO operation that needs a fresh tmux session fails for the same reason.

This has happened multiple times now and is fully reproducible on long-running AO sessions.

## Evidence

Captured during a live exhaustion event:

```
$ sysctl kern.tty.ptmx_max
kern.tty.ptmx_max: 511

$ lsof | awk '/\/dev\/ptmx/ {print $1, $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
 486 node 10235          # <-- the leak
  13 Code\x20H 1688
   7 tmux 10301

$ lsof | grep -c '/dev/ptmx'
506                       # 5 fds away from the cap

$ tmux new-session -d -s test
create window failed: fork failed: Device not configured
```

PID 10235 (the leaker) was the parent of `next-server` (the dev stack root), holding **486 PTY file descriptors**. Killing it freed all of them and immediately restored system PTY availability.

## Root cause hypothesis

The leak is in `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts`, the only place AO uses `node-pty`. Each terminal preview in the dashboard spawns a PTY that runs `tmux attach-session -t <sessionId>` to stream output to xterm.js.

The likely root cause is a **client/server protocol asymmetry**:

In `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx:279-287`, the unsubscribe function returned by `subscribeTerminal` only deletes the local subscriber set — it **does not send a `close` message to the mux server**:

\`\`\`ts
return () => {
  const subs = subscribersRef.current.get(key);
  if (subs) {
    subs.delete(callback);
    if (subs.size === 0) {
      subscribersRef.current.delete(key);   // <-- local-only cleanup
    }
  }
};
\`\`\`

On the server side (`mux-websocket.ts:374-406`), \`TerminalManager.subscribe\` only kills the PTY when the per-WS subscription is explicitly torn down — either by the client sending \`{type:"close"}\` or by the WebSocket itself closing.

Net effect: as the user navigates the dashboard and React components for different sessions mount/unmount, the server keeps spawning PTYs that never get killed for the lifetime of the WebSocket. \`openedTerminalsRef\` on the client also keeps growing — and on every WS reconnect it re-opens all of them, which can briefly cause additional spawns.

After ~70 unique terminal previews per hour over ~7 hours = ~486 leaked PTYs, matching the observed count exactly.

Other contributing suspects (lower confidence, also worth verifying with the diagnostic branch):
- Re-attach loop counter reset (\`mux-websocket.ts:331\`): \`reattachAttempts\` is reset to 0 *immediately* after a successful re-attach, so the \`MAX_REATTACH_ATTEMPTS=3\` cap effectively never engages if the new PTY also exits quickly.
- node-pty 1.1.0 has known stability issues on Node 25+ (the dashboard's own \`/dev/terminal-test\` page calls this out).

## Reproduction

Either:
- Leave \`pnpm dev\` and a dashboard tab open for 10–20 hours of normal AO use, OR
- Actively churn through many session previews / spawn-restore-kill cycles for an accelerated repro.

## Diagnostic branch

A diagnostic branch with focused logging is being prepared: \`debug/pty-leak-instrumentation\`. It adds:
- Per-PTY lifecycle logs (\`spawn\`, \`exit\`, \`reattach\`, \`kill\`) tagged with terminal id and current process PTY count.
- Per-WS connection lifecycle logs.
- A periodic sampler (every 60s) of: total PTYs held by the dev-terminal process, \`TerminalManager.terminals.size\`, count of entries with/without an attached PTY, total subscribers, WS client count.
- A \`/debug/pty\` HTTP endpoint on the dev-terminal port that dumps current state on demand.

Once the data is captured we'll be able to confirm the root cause and validate any fix.

## Possible fixes (to discuss after confirmation)

1. **Client-side**: send \`{ch:"terminal", id, type:"close"}\` from \`MuxProvider\` when the last local subscriber for a terminal unsubscribes.
2. **Server-side**: add an idle-PTY timeout in \`TerminalManager\` — kill any PTY whose forwarding subscriber hasn't actually emitted to a connected WS in N minutes.
3. **Both** (defense in depth).

## Impact

- **System-wide failure**, not just AO — once exhausted, no other process on the user's Mac can spawn a PTY until the leaker is killed.
- Affects long-running power users — i.e. exactly the workflow AO is designed for.
- Workaround until fixed: \`tmux kill-server\` + restart \`pnpm dev\` (also kills all your AO sessions, so it's painful).

title: fix(web): bound PTY re-attach loop with grace-period counter reset
body:
## Summary

Fixes the runaway PTY re-attach loop in the dashboard mux server that exhausts the macOS system PTY pool in seconds when a tmux session dies out from under a still-subscribed dashboard (most commonly: running `ao stop` while a dashboard tab is open).

Fixes #1639.

## Root cause

The `MAX_REATTACH_ATTEMPTS=3` cap in `mux-websocket.ts` was supposed to prevent unbounded respawning, but it was never engaging. The counter was reset to `0` immediately after each "successful" `open()` — where success only meant the new PTY was *spawned*, not that it *survived*. When the underlying tmux session is gone, `tmux attach-session` exits ~40 ms after spawn, the exit handler fires again with counter=0, retries, "succeeds", resets to 0, exits, retries... infinite loop.

## Evidence

Captured on the diagnostic branch ([commit log](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1639#issuecomment-4371029091)):

- A single 1.5-second burst produced **119 spawn↔exit cycles** for one terminal id
- Process PTY fd count rose **from ~15 to ~153 in <1 minute**
- `MAX_REATTACH_ATTEMPTS=3` provably never engaged: 506 of 527 spawns were re-attaches, all 506 followed by `pty_reattach_counter_reset`
- Sustained for a few seconds, this exhausts macOS `kern.tty.ptmx_max=511`, after which **nothing on the system** can spawn a new PTY (tmux, VS Code terminal, `ao spawn`, etc.) until the leaking process is killed

## Fix

- Remove the `terminal.reattachAttempts = 0` reset inside the exit handler.
- Schedule a delayed reset in `open()` via `setTimeout`, gated on the closure-captured `pty` reference still being `terminal.pty` after `REATTACH_RESET_GRACE_MS` (5 s).

Effect:
- Tight crash loops can't reset the counter (PTY exits before grace expires) → hit `MAX_REATTACH_ATTEMPTS` within ~150 ms → server emits `"exited"` and stops respawning.
- A long-lived PTY that crashes hours later still gets a fresh retry budget.

## Note on the residual ~1 fd/cycle leak

This PR addresses the dominant runaway behaviour. A separate, much slower leak in node-pty 1.1.0 itself (each spawn opens 3 PTY-class fds in the parent, each exit releases only 2 — observed deterministically across 553 spawn cycles in two independent runs) remains and is tracked in #1639. It will be addressed separately, likely by a node-pty upgrade.

Without this PR's fix, the residual leak still becomes catastrophic the moment the runaway loop kicks in. With it, the residual leak's worst case is bounded by user navigation (~50–70 cycles/hour) instead of ~80 cycles/sec.

## Test plan

New integration test in `direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts`:
- Creates a tmux session
- Opens it via the mux WebSocket
- Kills the tmux session externally
- Asserts `"exited"` is emitted within 2 s

Without this PR, the test hangs and times out — the exact symptom of the runaway bug.

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web exec eslint server/mux-websocket.ts server/__tests__/direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- --run server/__tests__/mux-websocket.test.ts server/__tests__/direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts` — 28/28 pass
- [x] Verified the 3 failing tests in the full web test suite (`api-routes.test.ts`, `page.test.tsx`) are pre-existing on clean upstream `main` and unrelated to this change

This leaves the user in a confusing state where `ao status` and `ao session list` report no active orchestrator, but startup still aborts because git says the canonical branch is already attached elsewhere. ## Reproduction A standalone local repro script is available here as well, which makes review a bit easier on another machine: https://gist.github.com/yyovil/4e86eb5b7000d16c21b6c2f3e729638c It prints the AO version, `ao status`, and `ao session ls --include-terminated` before running the failing startup flow. 1. title: Orchestrator restore fails permanently when codexThreadId is lost — requiresNativeRestore blocks recovery
body:
## Bug

`ao start` fails with:
```
✖ Orchestrator setup failed
Error: Failed to setup orchestrator: Session tr-orchestrator cannot be restored: codex.getRestoreCommand returned null
```

Reproduced with codex and kimicode orchestrators. Same class of bug applies to any agent in `requiresNativeRestore`.

## Root Cause

**Logic error** — orchestrator sessions become permanently stuck when `codexThreadId` is lost.

### Failure Chain

1. `ao start` finds existing orchestrator session marked `isRestorable` → calls `restore()`
2. `session.workspacePath` reconstructed from metadata (`session-from-metadata.ts:89`) via `meta["worktree"] || null` — **no fallback to `project.path`**
3. Enrichment (`session-manager.ts:1081-1092`) tries to populate `codexThreadId` from `~/.codex/sessions/` JSONL files. Fails if session files were cleaned up, or `workspacePath` is null
4. `getRestoreCommand` (`agent-codex/src/index.ts:716-748`) returns null — no `codexThreadId` in metadata, no session file found
5. `requiresNativeRestore("codex")` returns `true` (`session-manager.ts:433-439`) — **blocks `getLaunchCommand` fallback**
6. Throws `SessionNotRestorableError` — `ao start` dies

### Why it is permanent

Agents in `requiresNativeRestore` (codex, claude-code, kimicode, opencode) MUST use native resume. When resume data is lost, there is no escape hatch:
- Cannot restore (no codexThreadId)
- Cannot re-launch (requiresNativeRestore blocks getLaunchCommand fallback)

Triggered when:
- Codex session files in `~/.codex/sessions/` are cleaned up/rotated
- Container/environment restart clears session state
- `worktree` metadata was never written or worktree was deleted

## Fix

**Two changes:**

### 1. Apply workspacePath fallback (`session-from-metadata.ts:89`)
```typescript
// Before:
session.workspacePath = meta["worktree"] || null;

// After:
session.workspacePath = meta["worktree"] || project?.path || null;
```

### 2. Allow fresh launch fallback for stuck sessions (`session-manager.ts:2905-2908`)
When `getRestoreCommand` returns null for a `requiresNativeRestore` agent, fall back to `getLaunchCommand` instead of throwing.

## Impact

- **Severity:** High — completely blocks `ao start` for any project with a stale orchestrator session
- **Workaround:** Manually delete the session directory under `.ao/sessions/` or run `ao stop` before starting
- **Affected agents:** codex, claude-code, kimicode, opencode (all `requiresNativeRestore` agents)

## Key Files

| Component | File | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `requiresNativeRestore` gate | `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | 433-439 |
| Restore flow | `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | 2895-2913 |
| `workspacePath` no fallback | `packages/core/src/utils/session-from-metadata.ts` | 89 |
| Codex `getRestoreCommand` | `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` | 716-748 |
| Codex null on missing workspace | `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` | 720 |
| Codex null on missing session file | `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` | 724 |

title: feat(spawn): surface prompt-delivery progress via onProgress callback
body:
## Summary

Post-launch prompt delivery (Claude Code, OpenCode-interactive, etc.) retries up to 3× with 3s/6s/9s exponential backoff — up to **18s of silent \"Spawning session via core\"** spinner text. The user has no idea what's happening.

This PR adds an optional `onProgress: (text: string) => void` to `SessionSpawnConfig`. The CLI passes a callback that updates spinner text, so the user sees `"Delivering prompt (attempt 2/3)"` instead of a frozen spinner.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/types.ts`**: add optional `onProgress` to `SessionSpawnConfig`. Optional → fully backwards-compatible.
- **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`**: small `reportProgress` helper (try/catch-wrapped so a throwing callback can never break spawn) + one call inside the prompt-delivery retry loop.
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts`**: pass `(text) => { spinner.text = text; }`.
- **Tests**: progress fires once per attempt; a throwing `onProgress` does not break spawn.

Net diff: +95 LOC (10 functional + 16 helper/doc + 69 tests).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- spawn` — 105 pass, 2 new
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean (only pre-existing warnings)
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn` against a Claude Code project, observe spinner text changes during the 3s wait

## Notes

- API is opt-in. Existing call sites (e.g. `ao spawn group` batch mode) don't need to pass it; they don't have a spinner anyway.
- Group-mode `sm.spawn` calls don't pass a `prompt`, so the post-launch loop doesn't fire — no callback needed there.
- The reporter try/catches the callback because UX should never crash core. Same posture as `recordActivityEvent` errors elsewhere.

title: feat(web): allow renaming agent sessions with a custom display name
body:
## Summary

Allow users to give an agent session a custom display name. The session ID stays untouched — only the display name shown in the UI changes.

## Why

When running many parallel sessions, IDs like `ao-101`, `ao-127` are not memorable. A user-given label like "copilot smoke test", "PR 1466 review", "backend cleanup" makes it much easier to:

- Find the right session at a glance from the sidebar/dashboard
- Distinguish multiple sessions working on related tasks
- Recall context after coming back to a session later

## Proposed Behavior

- Add a 'rename' option (in the session detail header or the sidebar 3-dot menu)
- Clicking it opens an inline edit / dialog to enter a new name
- The new name is stored in session metadata
- The session ID (`ao-N`) remains the canonical identifier — used by the CLI, lifecycle manager, storage paths, APIs, and shell commands like `ao send ao-101 "..."`
- Display surfaces use the custom name when present, fall back to the default (issue/PR title, agent type, or session ID — whichever the team lands on for the default)

## Affected Areas (likely)

- Session metadata schema — add an optional `displayName` (or `name`) field
- Session manager / API routes — endpoint to update the name
- Sidebar + dashboard cards — render `displayName ?? defaultName`
- Possibly a CLI command (`ao rename <session> <name>`) for symmetry

## Related

- #1610 — sidebar branch display discussion (this is the mentioned 'addition' from that thread)

title: Make `ao open` redirect user to the dashboard
body:
## Problem

`ao open` (no args) currently opens every live session at once — one terminal tab (macOS / Windows) or browser tab (Linux) per session. With 5+ active sessions across multiple projects this is overwhelming and not what you usually want. Today the only way to be selective is to remember and type the exact session ID.

There's no middle ground between "open just this one I named" and "open everything."

## Proposal

Make `ao open` redirect user to the dashboard. This gives a way to the user to open the dashboard while the `ao start` is running.

fix(workspace-worktree): auto-recover from orphaned worktrees on spawn
body:
## Summary

Closes the long-standing UX bug where a single ungraceful `ao start` exit poisons a project until the user manually `git worktree remove`s the orphan.

**Before:** if `ao start` was killed during setup (Ctrl-C, kill -9, sleep, error), the orchestrator worktree stayed registered with git. Every subsequent `ao start` for that project failed with:

```
fatal: 'orchestrator/<name>' is already checked out at '/some/path'
```

…even when that path had already been wiped from disk. No recovery path other than `cd <repo> && git worktree remove …`.

**After:** two changes to `workspace.create()`:

1. Always run `git worktree prune` at the top. Clears registry entries pointing to paths git no longer sees on disk. Previously this only ran inside `clearStaleWorktreePath`, which early-returned when the path was already gone — exactly the case where prune was needed.
2. After prune, look up which worktree owns the target branch. If at the path we'd create → **reuse** it (the common orchestrator-restart case). If at a different path → throw a **clear** error naming the conflict.

## Why

This caused real user pain — surfaced while debugging a separate dashboard issue. A user had a previous `ao start` for `mercury` that left an orphan; every subsequent start hit the same `'already checked out at /that/path'` error. The recovery (`git worktree remove`) is one command, but unless you happen to know what worktrees are or that `ao` uses them, the error is opaque.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree test` — 53/53 passing
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (full repo) — clean
- New tests added:
  - reuses an existing worktree when it already owns the target branch at the expected path
  - throws a clear error when the target branch is checked out at a different path
  - recovers when git's worktree registry points to a path that no longer exists (the actual user-facing failure)
- Existing tests updated to mock the new `prune` + `list --porcelain` calls via a `mockNoOrphan()` helper.

## Changeset

Patch bump for `@aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree`.

title: feat: interactive canvases in session detail view
body:
## Summary

Adds Cursor-style **canvases** — interactive artifacts rendered in a right-side rail next to the session terminal, so structured agent output (diffs, test results, stats, notes) isn't buried in scrollback.

- Four built-in renderer types: `markdown`, `diff`, `table`, `stats`
- Agents emit JSON to `{workspacePath}/.ao/canvases/{id}.json`
- Core synthesizes a `core-git-diff` canvas from `git diff` so the feature works for every session before any agent integration
- Pluggable: `CanvasProducer` interface declared for v0.2 (agent / SCM / tracker plugins can produce canvases later) but not yet invoked — keeps v0.1 surface minimal

## Why this design (not a 9th plugin slot)

Codex pushed back on my original "new plugin slot" proposal: the existing 8 slots are infrastructure boundaries (where things run, who runs them); a canvas is session output plus a UI artifact type. The chosen design — fixed renderer types in core, file-based emission, schema validation — gives third parties extensibility without shipping React into the supervisor dashboard.

Design doc: [docs/canvases.md](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/claude/happy-spence-e5b227/docs/canvases.md).

## Hardened across 10 codex review passes

18 distinct corner-case fixes before opening this PR:

- working-tree diffs (not just committed)
- merge-base against `origin/<default>`, not stale local ref
- untracked files included with file/byte/lstat caps
- `.ao/` excluded from synthesized diffs
- `core-` id prefix reserved for synthesized canvases (file canvases can't shadow)
- per-effect cancellation + sequence-guarded poll responses (no stale wins)
- `lstat` (not `stat`) on canvas files — rejects FIFO/symlink bypass
- partial-stdout recovery on oversized diffs (truncate, don't drop)
- `session.projectId` (authoritative) — not prefix-matching project resolution
- empty canvases for sessions without `workspacePath` (don't 404)
- diff parser preserves content lines starting with `+++`/`---`, strips marker prefix
- size caps: 256 KB per canvas, 32 canvases per session, 200 files / 5000 lines per diff, 50 untracked files / 4 MB budget

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1057/1057 pass (17 new canvas tests)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test useSessionCanvases CanvasRail` — 8/8 pass
- [x] `pnpm build` — full monorepo builds
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (3 intentional `console.warn` in canvas-log.ts, matching activity-log.ts pattern)
- [ ] Manual smoke test: `pnpm dev`, open session detail, verify rail renders the synthesized git-diff canvas; drop `.ao/canvases/test.json` to verify file canvases; drop invalid JSON to verify silent dropping

## Out of scope (deferred per [docs/canvases.md](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/claude/happy-spence-e5b227/docs/canvases.md) roadmap)

- v0.2 — `CanvasProducer.listCanvases` invoked across agent / SCM / tracker plugins
- v0.3 — mux WebSocket topic replacing 5s REST poll
- Custom React renderers from third-party plugins (security boundary; never planned)

title: Activity events: CLI commands and supervisor lifecycle (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first — that PR ships the `recordActivityEvent` API, the SQLite-backed events DB, and the existing `ActivityEventSource` / `ActivityEventKind` unions this issue extends.

## Goal

Wire `recordActivityEvent` calls into `packages/cli/` so `ao events list` can answer:

- Did AO start cleanly? When?
- Was AO shut down (and how) or did it crash?
- Did `ao spawn` / `ao update` / `ao stop` / `ao migrate-storage` fail, and why?
- Did the auto-restore prompt actually restore sessions?

Today these flows are silent except for `console.error` — invisible to any RCA query.

## New `ActivityEventSource`

Add `"cli"` to the union in `packages/core/src/activity-events.ts`.

## Insertion points (37 total: 14 MUST, 12 SHOULD, 4 COULD, 7 DON'T-but-listed-for-reviewer-context)

### A. `ao start` / `ao stop` / shutdown handlers (18 entries)

| File:line | What's there today | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands/start.ts:1782` | `register({pid,port,projects})` after successful startup — no event | `cli.start_invoked` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:1814` | start action outer catch — stderr only | `cli.start_failed` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:946-955` | orchestrator setup failed (spinner.fail) | `cli.start_failed` (reason="orchestrator_setup") | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:963-972` | project supervisor failed to start | `cli.start_failed` (reason="supervisor_start") | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:1009-1010` | restore prompt accepted, restore loop entered | `cli.restore_started` | SHOULD |
| `commands/start.ts:1033-1037` | per-session restore failure inside loop — warning only | `cli.restore_session_failed` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:1041-1043` | restore loop completed (counts) | `cli.restore_completed` | SHOULD |
| `commands/start.ts:1090-1092` | last-stop handling outer catch — silent | `cli.last_stop_read_failed` | SHOULD |
| `commands/start.ts:1843` | `ao stop` action entered | `cli.stop_invoked` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:1914-1918` | per-session kill failure during ao stop — warning only | `cli.stop_session_failed` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:1957-1964` | writeLastStop after ao stop succeeded | `cli.last_stop_written` | SHOULD |
| `commands/start.ts:1985-1987` | SIGTERM sent to parent ao start | `cli.daemon_killed` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:2005-2011` | ao stop outer catch | `cli.stop_failed` | **MUST** |
| `lib/shutdown.ts:49` | shutdown handler entered (signal received) | `cli.shutdown_signal` | **MUST** |
| `lib/shutdown.ts:62` | force-exit timer fired (10s timeout) | `cli.shutdown_force_exit` | **MUST** |
| `lib/shutdown.ts:79-81` | per-session kill failure during shutdown — silent | `cli.shutdown_session_kill_failed` | SHOULD |
| `lib/shutdown.ts:108` | unregister() returned (clean shutdown done) | `cli.shutdown_completed` | **MUST** |
| `lib/shutdown.ts:109-111` | shutdown body outer catch — silent | `cli.shutdown_failed` | **MUST** |

### B. `ao spawn` / `ao update` / `ao setup` / `ao migrate-storage` (10 entries)

| File:line | What's there today | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands/spawn.ts:117-119` | pre-spawn intent (before sm.spawn) — no event | `cli.spawn_invoked` | SHOULD |
| `commands/spawn.ts:271-273` | `ao spawn` outer catch | `cli.spawn_failed` | SHOULD |
| `commands/spawn.ts:328-336` | batch-spawn group preflight failed | `cli.spawn_failed` (data.batchSize) | SHOULD |
| `commands/update.ts:43-54` | update flow entered (method detected) | `cli.update_invoked` | SHOULD |
| `commands/update.ts:81-103` | `ao update` git script failed | `cli.update_failed` | **MUST** |
| `commands/update.ts:148-153` | npm install path failed | `cli.update_failed` | **MUST** |

| `commands/setup.ts:574` | `writeOpenClawJsonConfig` returned false | `cli.setup_failed` | COULD |
| `commands/migrate-storage.ts:23-28` | migration completed | `cli.migration_completed` | SHOULD |
| `commands/migrate-storage.ts:35-39` | migrate-storage outer catch | `cli.migration_failed` | **MUST** |

### C. Project resolution / config recovery (9 entries)

| File:line | What's there today | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib/resolve-project.ts:131-137` | clone failure in `fromUrl` | `cli.project_resolve_failed` | **MUST** |
| `lib/resolve-project.ts:236-251` | `fromCwdOrId` config-load fallback (auto-create or registerFlatConfig) | `cli.config_recovered` | SHOULD |
| `lib/resolve-project.ts:246-248` | `registerFlatConfig` returned null (recovery failed) | `cli.config_recovery_failed` | **MUST** |
| `commands/start.ts:147-156` | `registerFlatConfig` ran successfully | `cli.config_migrated` | SHOULD |
| `commands/start.ts:1665-1681` | "restart" choice — kill existing instance + waitForExit | `cli.daemon_restart` | SHOULD |
| `lib/running-state.ts:137` | acquireLock timeout throw (>5s) | `cli.lock_timeout` | SHOULD |
| `lib/running-state.ts:246-249` | `getRunning()` pruning a stale entry (dead PID) | `cli.stale_running_pruned` | SHOULD |
| `lib/credential-resolver.ts:69-71` | malformed openclaw.json silent skip | `cli.credential_load_failed` | COULD |
| `commands/project.ts:96-115` | `ao project add` config-load failure | `cli.project_register_failed` | SHOULD |

### D. Explicitly NOT in scope (don't log)

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `lib/project-supervisor.ts:107-115` | per-project reconcile failure | Already observer.setHealth; per-poll volume |
| `commands/spawn.ts:218-225` | argument validation rejection | User error, not RCA-worthy |
| `lib/completion.ts` (all) | tab-completion calls | Per-keystroke volume |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --source cli --since 1h` returns events for any recent CLI activity
- [ ] `cli.start_invoked` + `cli.shutdown_completed` together prove "AO ran cleanly from T₁ to T₂"
- [ ] `cli.start_invoked` followed by `cli.stale_running_pruned` (later) proves "AO crashed at T₁ and was detected on next start"
- [ ] All 14 MUST emits have a regression test asserting the event fires
- [ ] `ao stop`, `ao update`, `ao spawn` failures show up under their failure kinds

## Testing approach

Mirror the pattern from `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager-instrumentation.test.ts`:

```ts
vi.mock("../activity-events.js", async (importOriginal) => {
  const original = await importOriginal<typeof ActivityEventsModule>();
  return { ...original, recordActivityEvent: vi.fn() };
});

it("emits cli.shutdown_signal when SIGINT is received", async () => {
  installShutdownHandlers({ /* deps */ });
  process.emit("SIGINT", "SIGINT");
  await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r));

  const events = vi.mocked(recordActivityEvent).mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);
  expect(events).toContainEqual(
    expect.objectContaining({ kind: "cli.shutdown_signal", source: "cli" })
  );
});
```

Add tests under `packages/cli/src/__tests__/` (or wherever the existing CLI tests live).

## Invariants to preserve (per CLAUDE.md)

- `recordActivityEvent` is **sync** — never `await` it
- `summary` is FTS-indexed and not credential-sanitized; **don't interpolate raw error text** (use `data.errorMessage` instead — see PR #1620 codex review fixes for `lifecycle.poll_failed` and `report_watcher.triggered`)
- **Don't wrap** `recordActivityEvent` in try/catch — it never throws
- **Don't await** the event in shutdown paths; sync emit before `process.exit`

## Sequencing

This is a good candidate for **the first sub-issue to land** (post-#1620): introduces the `cli` source, simple to review, validates the source-extension pattern for the rest of the sub-issues.

title: Activity events: Web API mutation routes (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first.

## Goal

Wire `recordActivityEvent` calls into every `POST` / `PATCH` / `DELETE` route under `packages/web/src/app/api/` so RCA can answer:

- Did the user click "kill session" / "merge PR" / "remove project"? When?
- Did an external system trigger a session via `POST /api/spawn`?
- Did an API call fail before it reached the core layer (validation / 404)?
- Did the API call succeed at the API layer but the underlying core call fail?

Today: **only success/failure status codes** are observable, not the intent. RCA can see "session was killed at T" via `session.killed` (already emitted by session-manager) but can't tell if the kill came from the user, from auto-cleanup, from the CLI, or from `ao stop`.

## Source

`api` — already in the `ActivityEventSource` union (added by #1620 but never emitted from). This issue is its first real use.

## Layered emit policy (read first)

| Layer | What it emits | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **API route handler** | Intent / "user asked for X" | `api.session_kill_requested` |
| **Core (session-manager / lifecycle)** | Outcome / "X happened" | `session.killed` |

Both events fire intentionally. RCA correlates by `sessionId + ts window`. Different kinds = no collision; the duplication is the feature.

**Anti-double-emit rule**: if core was already going to emit a failure (`session.spawn_failed`), don't also emit `api.session_spawn_failed` for the same root cause. Only emit the API failure event when the failure happened *before* core was reached (validation, project lookup, etc.).

## Insertion points (30 entries: 12 MUST, 14 SHOULD, 4 COULD)

### A. Session mutations (13 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |

| `app/api/spawn/route.ts:60` | `POST /api/spawn` success | `api.session_spawn_requested` | **MUST** |
| `app/api/spawn/route.ts:36-54` | project validation failure (404) | `api.session_spawn_rejected` | SHOULD |
| `app/api/spawn/route.ts:84-104` | spawn 500 path (only when no session ID was created) | `api.session_spawn_failed` | SHOULD |
| `app/api/sessions/[id]/kill/route.ts:25` | `POST /:id/kill` success | `api.session_kill_requested` | **MUST** |
| `app/api/sessions/[id]/kill/route.ts:38-58` | kill failure (non-404) | `api.session_kill_failed` | SHOULD |
| `app/api/sessions/[id]/send/route.ts:45` | `POST /:id/send` success | `api.session_message_sent` | **MUST** |
| `app/api/sessions/[id]/send/route.ts:63-82` | send failure | `api.session_message_failed` | SHOULD |
| `app/api/sessions/[id]/message/route.ts:69` | `POST /:id/message` success (duplicate route — emit consistently) | `api.session_message_sent` | **MUST** |
| `app/api/sessions/[id]/message/route.ts:83-107` | message failure | `api.session_message_failed` | SHOULD |

### D. Issue / verify / labels (5 entries)

| `app/api/verify/route.ts:76-97` | `POST /api/verify` success | `api.issue_verified` (data.action="verify"\|"fail") | SHOULD |
| `app/api/verify/route.ts:100-104` | verify failure | `api.issue_verify_failed` | COULD |
| `app/api/setup-labels/route.ts:21-44` | `POST /api/setup-labels` complete | `api.labels_setup` | COULD |

### E. Explicitly NOT in scope (don't log)

| File | Why |

| `app/api/sessions/route.ts` (GET) | High volume; lifecycle/observer cover |
| `app/api/sessions/patches/route.ts` (GET) | Polled every 3s — catastrophic volume |
| `app/api/observability/route.ts` (GET) | Health endpoint |
| `app/api/runtime/terminal/route.ts` (GET) | Static config GET |
| `app/api/filesystem/browse/route.ts` (GET) | Read-only filesystem nav |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --source api --since 1h` returns events for every dashboard mutation
- [ ] When user clicks "kill" in dashboard: both `api.session_kill_requested` AND `session.killed` appear (different kinds, joinable by `sessionId`)
- [ ] When user clicks "merge PR" and merge fails: `api.pr_merge_failed` event captures the reason
- [ ] All 12 MUST emits have a regression test
- [ ] No event leaks message body / project config values into `data` (sanitization rules apply but not foolproof)

## Testing approach

Use Next.js's route-handler test pattern (or vitest + a mock NextRequest):

```ts
vi.mock("@aoagents/ao-core", async (orig) => {
  const m = await orig();
  return { ...m, recordActivityEvent: vi.fn() };
});

it("POST /api/sessions/:id/kill emits api.session_kill_requested", async () => {
  const req = new NextRequest("http://x/api/sessions/sess-1/kill", { method: "POST" });
  await POST(req, { params: { id: "sess-1" } });

  expect(recordActivityEvent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({
      sessionId: "sess-1",
      source: "api",
      kind: "api.session_kill_requested",
    }),
  );
});
```

## Invariants to preserve

- **Don't include request body or response body in `data`** — sanitizer redacts URL credentials but not arbitrary user content; risk of leaking PII or message text
- For `*_message_*` kinds: include `messageLength` (number) but **not** the message itself
- For `project_updated`: record changed *keys*, not values (config may contain tokens)
- For `webhook_unverified` (covered in sibling sub-issue): never include the failed signature value

## Out of scope

- Webhook routes (sibling sub-issue: webhooks + WS server)
- WebSocket terminal events (sibling sub-issue)
- All GET endpoints (volume too high — use access logs / observer instead)
- React component / hook code (browser can't write to SQLite — `ui` source is reserved for the Node-side WS server)

title: Activity events: Webhooks and WebSocket terminal server (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first.

## Goal

Cover two surfaces missed by the broader API sub-issue:

1. **Webhook ingress** at `app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts` — these are external system events with security implications (signature verification failure = potential attack signal)
2. **WebSocket terminal mux** at `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` — drives the live terminal UI; today its lifecycle and failure modes are console-only

RCA today can't answer:

- Did GitHub send us a webhook we rejected on auth?
- How often is the terminal connection flapping?
- Did the PTY actually die or did the user close their browser?

## Sources

- `api` (already in union) — extends with `api.webhook_*` kinds
- `ui` (already in union, never emitted from) — first real use; reserved for **Node-side** WS server, not browser

> **Note on `ui`**: browser code (React components, hooks) cannot write to SQLite — there's no DB connection in the browser. The `ui` source is exclusively for emits from `packages/web/server/`. React/client-side code never emits AE.

## Insertion points (10 entries: 4 MUST, 5 SHOULD, 1 COULD)

### A. Webhook ingress (4 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts:96-100` | webhook signature verification failure (401) | `api.webhook_unverified` | **MUST** |
| `app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts:38-43` | webhook payload too large (413) | `api.webhook_rejected` | SHOULD |
| `app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts:102-112` | webhook accepted (202) — counts of parseErrors / lifecycleErrors | `api.webhook_received` | **MUST** |
| `app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts:113-118` | webhook 500 outer catch (pipeline crashed) | `api.webhook_failed` | SHOULD |

### B. WebSocket terminal mux (6 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server/mux-websocket.ts:434` | mux WS connection opened | `ui.terminal_connected` | SHOULD |
| `server/mux-websocket.ts:600` | mux WS connection closed | `ui.terminal_disconnected` | COULD |
| `server/mux-websocket.ts:451-453` | heartbeat termination (3 missed pongs) — today console-only | `ui.terminal_heartbeat_lost` | SHOULD |
| `server/mux-websocket.ts:317-345` | PTY exited / max-reattach exhausted — today console-only | `ui.terminal_pty_lost` | SHOULD |
| `server/mux-websocket.ts:584-594` | invalid mux client message (parse err — client bug or version skew) | `ui.terminal_protocol_error` | COULD |
| `server/mux-websocket.ts:144-157` | SessionBroadcaster fetch failure — mux-side polling fails, UI sees stale data | `ui.session_broadcast_failed` | SHOULD |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --kind api.webhook_unverified` returns the audit trail for failed signature verifications
- [ ] `ao events list --kind ui.terminal_pty_lost` shows when terminal sessions actually died vs. user-closed-browser
- [ ] `api.webhook_unverified` events include `slug` and `remoteAddr` but **not** the failed signature
- [ ] `api.webhook_received` events include counts (parseErrors, lifecycleErrors) but **not** the payload body
- [ ] WS lifecycle events have at most one emit per connection per state change (not per heartbeat tick)

## Security note (`api.webhook_unverified` is non-negotiable)

This is the one event in this sub-issue that's load-bearing for security audit, not just RCA. Pair with rate counts in the dashboard. Treat 401s on webhooks as a signal worth retaining for the full 7-day window.

## Testing approach

For webhooks: mock the verifier, drive a request with a bad signature, assert the event fires:

```ts
it("rejects unverified webhook and emits api.webhook_unverified", async () => {
  vi.spyOn(verifier, "verifySignature").mockReturnValue(false);
  const req = makeWebhookRequest({ signature: "bogus" });

  const res = await POST(req, { params: { slug: ["github"] } });
  expect(res.status).toBe(401);
  expect(recordActivityEvent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({
      source: "api",
      kind: "api.webhook_unverified",
      level: "warn",
    }),
  );
  // Critical: signature value must NOT be in data
  const call = vi.mocked(recordActivityEvent).mock.calls[0]![0];
  expect(JSON.stringify(call.data)).not.toContain("bogus");
});
```

For WS: drive the heartbeat-loss path by closing the underlying socket without a pong, assert `ui.terminal_heartbeat_lost` fires once.

## Invariants to preserve

- **No raw payloads or signatures in `data`** — webhook bodies can be 16KB+ and arbitrary; record counts and IDs only
- **No client IPs in `summary`** — `remoteAddr` can go in `data` (sanitizer doesn't redact IPs but `summary` is FTS-indexed)
- WS events should not fire on every keystroke / every pong — only on lifecycle state changes
- Volume budget: `ui.terminal_*` events scale with active user sessions (bounded by user count); `api.webhook_*` scale with external system traffic (bounded by webhook subscribers)

## Out of scope

- All POST/PATCH/DELETE non-webhook API routes (sibling sub-issue: Web API mutation routes)
- Browser-side React state changes (no DB access)
- SSE polling (the existing `/api/sessions/patches` is GET — DON'T log)

title: Activity events: session-manager rounding-out (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first.
>
> ⚠️ **Highest-risk sub-issue.** Touches `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — flagged in CLAUDE.md alongside `lifecycle-manager.ts` as having "subtle state dependencies." Prefer landing **after** the CLI sub-issue (which validates the source-extension pattern with low risk) so reviewers have pattern-matching context.

## Goal

Round out `session-manager.ts` instrumentation. PR #1620 added the `session.spawn_started` / `session.spawned` / `session.spawn_failed` / `session.killed` enums but only emits the worker-spawn flow's events. Many failure paths inside spawn/kill/restore/send are still silent.

RCA today can't answer:

- Did the orchestrator spawn fail? (The orchestrator path has *zero* AE today — no `session.spawn_started`/`_failed` envelope)
- Did the agent's startup prompt actually deliver, or did all 3 retries fail?
- Did `runtime.destroy` / `workspace.destroy` succeed during kill, or silently leak?
- Did the `runtime_lost` reconciliation in `sm.list()` fire on this session?
- Did `ao send` actually deliver (it has retry-with-restore logic that swallows failures)?

## Sources

`session-manager` (already in union) + `runtime`, `workspace`, `agent`, `tracker` (already in union for the cross-cutting kinds).

## Insertion points (28 in-scope entries: 8 MUST, 13 SHOULD, 4 COULD, 3 DON'T)

### A. Worker spawn rounding-out (4 entries — C01/C02/C07 are DONE in PR #1620)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:1149-1158` | tracker `getIssue` throws non-`isIssueNotFoundError` | `tracker.issue_fetch_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:1228-1234` | `tracker.generatePrompt` silent catch ("non-fatal") — impacts prompt quality | `tracker.generate_prompt_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:1431-1446` | post-launch `runtime.sendMessage` retry loop, all 3 attempts fail (today: console.error only) | `session.prompt_delivery_failed` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:1467-1476` | spawn outer catch → `cleanupStack.runAll()` rollback | `session.rollback_started` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:1473` | individual cleanup-stack step failure (`onError` callback) | `session.rollback_step_failed` | SHOULD |

### B. Orchestrator spawn (6 entries — currently has NO outer envelope)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:1525-1541` | `spawnOrchestrator` workspace.create catch (no outer try/catch wrapping the whole flow) | `session.spawn_failed` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:1577-1580` | hook installation throw → cleanup → throw (PR tracking broken if this fails) | `session.workspace_hooks_failed` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:1587-1605` | systemPrompt write / `writeWorkspaceOpenCodeAgentsMd` throw | `session.spawn_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:1618-1628` | `resolveOpenCodeSessionReuse` catch in orchestrator | `session.spawn_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:1680-1683` | `runtime.create()` catch in orchestrator (today silent except for throw) | `session.spawn_failed` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:1768-1776` | post-launch metadata write catch in orchestrator (triggers full rollback) | `session.spawn_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:1833-1841` | `ensureOrchestratorInternal` concurrent reservation conflict | `session.orchestrator_conflict` | COULD |

### C. Stale runtime reconciliation (2 entries)

> Per CLAUDE.md: `sm.list()` is "the only place stale runtime state gets reconciled." Today this transition is silent except in metadata.

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:1937-1953` | `sm.list()` persists `runtime_lost` lifecycle to disk | `runtime.lost_detected` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:1950-1952` | `runtime_lost` persist catch (silent) | `runtime.lost_persist_failed` | SHOULD |

### D. Kill flow (5 entries — C27 `session.killed` is DONE)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:2032-2047` | `kill()` enter — kind `session.kill_started` declared but UNEMITTED | `session.kill_started` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:2071-2076` | `runtime.destroy` silent catch in kill (resource leak diagnostic) | `runtime.destroy_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:2086-2091` | `workspace.destroy` silent catch in kill (worktree may be left behind) | `workspace.destroy_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:2104-2109` | `deleteOpenCodeSession` silent catch (`void 0`) — leaves dangling opencode session | `agent.opencode_purge_failed` | SHOULD |

### E. Cleanup loop (2 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:2240-2245` | cleanup loop per-session error (errors collected into result; AE makes them queryable) | `session.cleanup_error` | SHOULD |

### F. Send + restore flows (5 entries)

|---|---|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:2543` | `send()` initial `runtime.sendMessage` attempt (only emit on final failure) | `session.send_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:2580-2599` | `send()` retry-with-restore final failure (currently throws; no AE) | `session.send_failed` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:2479-2484` | `restoreForDelivery` failure (wraps with cause) | `session.restore_failed` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:2832-2837` | `restore()` workspace restore failure (user-initiated; today only throws) | `session.restore_failed` | **MUST** |
| `session-manager.ts:2895-2913` | `restore()` `getRestoreCommand` returns null fallback (RCA: "did AO use native restore or relaunch?") | `session.restore_fallback` | SHOULD |
| `session-manager.ts:2900-2907` | `restore()` SessionNotRestorableError | `session.restore_failed` | **MUST** |

### G. Metadata corruption (1 entry — load-bearing forensic event)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata.ts:358-367` | corrupt JSON detected, file renamed `.corrupt-{ts}` (today: console.warn only) | `metadata.corrupt_detected` | **MUST** |

### H. Explicitly NOT in scope (per-list volume)

| File:line | Why |
|---|---|
| `session-manager.ts:1038-1043` | `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` `isAlive` catch — runs every list (high volume); lifecycle D07 covers |
| `session-manager.ts:1068-1078` | `agent.getActivityState` / `getSessionInfo` catches in enrich — per-list |
| `session-manager.ts:2207-2229` | cleanup `scm.getPRState` / `tracker.isCompleted` / `runtime.isAlive` silent catches — lifecycle covers |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --source session-manager --kind session.kill_started` shows kill intents
- [ ] When `runtime.destroy` silently fails during kill: `runtime.destroy_failed` event makes the leak queryable
- [ ] Orchestrator spawn failures appear under `session.spawn_failed` (today: zero events for orchestrator path)
- [ ] `session.prompt_delivery_failed` fires when all 3 retries exhaust
- [ ] All 8 MUST emits have a regression test
- [ ] **B-invariants from PR #1620** preserved: state mutation BEFORE event emission, no `await` on `recordActivityEvent`, no try/catch around it

## Testing approach

Same pattern as `lifecycle-manager-instrumentation.test.ts`:

```ts
it("emits session.kill_started before destroy attempts", async () => {
  vi.mocked(runtime.destroy).mockImplementation(async () => { /* slow */ });
  await sm.kill(sessionId);

  const events = vi.mocked(recordActivityEvent).mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);
  const startEvent = events.find((e) => e.kind === "session.kill_started");
  const completeEvent = events.find((e) => e.kind === "session.killed");
  expect(events.indexOf(startEvent!)).toBeLessThan(events.indexOf(completeEvent!));
});

it("emits session.prompt_delivery_failed after 3 retries", async () => {
  vi.mocked(runtime.sendMessage).mockRejectedValue(new Error("PTY closed"));
  await sm.spawn({ /* ... */ });

  const events = vi.mocked(recordActivityEvent).mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);
  expect(events).toContainEqual(
    expect.objectContaining({
      kind: "session.prompt_delivery_failed",
      data: expect.objectContaining({ attempts: 3 }),
    }),
  );
});
```

## Invariants to preserve (extends PR #1620's B1–B16)

- **B1**: state mutation BEFORE event emission. `runtime_lost` persist FIRST, then emit.
- **B2**: never wrap `recordActivityEvent` in try/catch
- **B11**: do NOT include prompt content in `data` for `prompt_delivery_failed` — prompts may include report.note style free-form user text (per Ashish's #1620 review)
- **B16**: failure-only — don't emit on every retry attempt, only on final exhaustion
- **B25 (new)**: cleanup-stack rollbacks emit per-step, not in aggregate. The `onError` callback hook fires per failed step.

## Sequencing

Land **after** the CLI sub-issue. Both touch the activity-events plumbing; CLI is lower-risk and validates the pattern.

## Out of scope

- `lifecycle-manager.ts` (already done in #1620)
- Plugin internals (sibling sub-issue)
- Recovery subsystem (sibling sub-issue)
- Per-list enrichment paths (volume too high)

title: Activity events: Config, plugin-registry, and storage migration (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first.

## Goal

Three related domains, all currently silent (or `console.warn`-only):

1. **Config loading** — `config.ts` and `global-config.ts`. Failures here can cause projects to silently disappear from the dashboard.
2. **Plugin registry** — `plugin-registry.ts`. Today only `process.stderr.write` when a plugin fails to load.
3. **Storage migration** — `migration/storage-v2.ts`. One-shot, destructive, partial-failure scenarios are the hardest to debug.

RCA today can't answer:

- Why isn't my project visible in the dashboard? (config validation might have rejected it)
- Why isn't the slack notifier firing? (plugin might have failed to load at startup)
- Did `ao migrate-storage` actually finish? Did it rename `.migrated` cleanly?

## New `ActivityEventSource` values

- `"config"` — config + global-config + project resolve
- `"plugin-registry"` — plugin load / validation
- `"migration"` — storage-v2 migrations

Add all three to the union in `packages/core/src/activity-events.ts`.

## Insertion points (15 entries: 4 MUST, 11 SHOULD)

### A. Config loading (4 entries)

| File:line | Why |
|---|---|
