| `events-db.ts:122-128` | FTS init failure — self-instrumentation; would be lost anyway |
| `migration/storage-v2.ts:1413-1414` | marker file unlink — best-effort cleanup |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --source config` shows projects that failed to load with their projectId
- [ ] `ao events list --kind plugin-registry.load_failed` lists every external plugin that failed to load at startup
- [ ] `ao events list --source migration` reconstructs the migration timeline (started → per-project failures → completed)
- [ ] `migration.completed` event includes `data.projectsMigrated` / `projectErrors` counts (not per-project events — too noisy)
- [ ] All 4 MUST emits have regression tests
- [ ] `config.project_resolve_failed` events include `projectId` so `ao events list --project <id>` finds them

## Testing approach

```ts
it("emits config.project_resolve_failed when a project's local config is invalid", async () => {
  // Setup: write a malformed agent-orchestrator.yaml in a registered project
  await fs.writeFile(localPath, "garbage: \tno");

  await loadEffectiveProjectConfig(globalConfig);

  expect(recordActivityEvent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({
      source: "config",
      kind: "config.project_resolve_failed",
      projectId: "todo-app",
    }),
  );
});

it("emits migration.project_failed for the bad project, migration.completed at end", async () => {
  // Setup: 3 projects, 1 with a permission error
  vi.mocked(migrateOneProject).mockImplementation(async (p) => {
    if (p.projectId === "broken") throw new Error("EACCES");
  });

  const result = await migrateStorage(opts);

  const events = vi.mocked(recordActivityEvent).mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);
  expect(events.filter((e) => e.kind === "migration.project_failed")).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(events.filter((e) => e.kind === "migration.completed")).toHaveLength(1);
});
```

## Invariants to preserve

- **B22 (new)**: migration events fire at most once per *milestone*, not per *progress percentage*. One event per project failure + one summary event at end. Don't emit `migration.project_done` per project (would scale with input size).
- **B24 (new)**: `config.*` events use the project's `projectId` if known so `ao events list --project <id>` finds them. Where the *global* config is the failure target, leave `projectId` null.
- **No raw config values in `data`** — config blocks may include `notifierConfig` / `agentConfig` with tokens; record changed *keys* only

## Out of scope

- Plugin INTERNAL failures (sibling sub-issue: plugin internals)
- session-manager startup paths (sibling sub-issue: session-manager rounding-out)
- CLI command-level events for `ao migrate-storage` (sibling sub-issue: CLI)

title: Activity events: Plugin internals (tracker, workspace, scm, notifier) (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first.

## Goal

Plugins today never call `recordActivityEvent` — only the lifecycle-manager call site does. For most plugin failures this is fine (lifecycle catches and emits a generic event). But there are **distinct failure shapes** plugins can detect that the lifecycle layer can't:

- `notifier-openclaw` knows the difference between 401 (auth — user-actionable) vs ECONNREFUSED (process down) vs 5xx (transient). Lifecycle just sees "notify failed."
- `tracker-linear` knows the difference between "Composio SDK not installed" (dep-missing, user-actionable) vs API rate-limit. Lifecycle never sees it (throws at create-time).
- `workspace-worktree` knows when `git worktree add -b` fell back because the branch already existed (concurrent session collision). Lifecycle just sees a successful create.
- `scm-github` knows when `gh` CLI is missing globally (one-shot, fixable) vs rate-limit (transient).

These distinct shapes are user-actionable signals that today get lost in generic "plugin call failed" lumps.

RCA today can't answer:

- Is the openclaw notifier failing because the token expired or because the openclaw daemon is down?
- Why is the linear tracker not creating issues? (composio-core SDK missing → install hint)
- Did two sessions collide on the same branch?
- Is `gh` not installed on this machine?

## New `ActivityEventSource` values

- `"tracker"` — issue-tracker plugins (github/linear/gitlab)
- `"workspace"` — git worktree/clone plugins

`"scm"`, `"runtime"`, `"agent"`, `"notifier"` already in union — extend kinds only.

## Plugin import contract

Plugins emit by importing `recordActivityEvent` directly from `@aoagents/ao-core`:

```typescript
import { recordActivityEvent } from "@aoagents/ao-core";
```

This is acceptable per the existing package graph (plugins already import `shellEscape`, `validateUrl`, etc. from core). No registry callback indirection needed.

## Insertion points (13 entries: 5 MUST, 8 SHOULD)

### A. SCM plugins (3 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts:360-366` | `verifyGhCLI` throws GH_CLI_UNAVAILABLE on missing `gh` binary — once-per-process, entire batch dies | `scm.gh_unavailable` | **MUST** |
| `scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts:1152` | per-PR enrichment failure inside batch (one PR fails inside an OK batch — lifecycle D02 only fires for whole-batch failure) | `scm.batch_enrich_pr_failed` | SHOULD |
| `scm-github/src/index.ts:816-825` | `getCISummary` fail-closes to "failing" without surface signal | `scm.ci_summary_failclosed` | SHOULD |
| `scm-gitlab/src/index.ts:576-589` | same fail-close pattern for gitlab | `scm.ci_summary_failclosed` | SHOULD |
| `scm-gitlab/src/index.ts:641-645` | `getReviews` discussions fetch failure → console.warn (lifecycle D25 covers `getReviewThreads` only) | `scm.review_fetch_failed` | SHOULD |

### B. Workspace plugins (3 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace-worktree/src/index.ts:391` | `postCreate` shell command failure (propagates; AO records spawn_failed but loses the specific command) | `workspace.post_create_failed` | **MUST** |
| `workspace-worktree/src/index.ts:157-182` | `worktree add -b` failure → fallback (branch already exists — two sessions collided) | `workspace.branch_collision` | SHOULD |
| `workspace-clone/src/index.ts:106-118` | clone runtime branch fallback — same intent | `workspace.branch_collision` | SHOULD |
| `workspace-worktree/src/index.ts:209-213` | `destroy()` swallows git failure → falls back to rmSync (worktree metadata stale in `git worktree list`) | `workspace.destroy_fell_back` | SHOULD |
| `workspace-clone/src/index.ts:148-156` | `list()` skips corrupted clone, console.warn only — RCA: "session shows up but I can't see it" | `workspace.corrupt_clone_skipped` | SHOULD |

### C. Tracker plugins (2 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracker-linear/src/index.ts:143-157` | Composio SDK not installed — once-per-process, user-actionable, today only console-warns | `tracker.dep_missing` | **MUST** |
| `tracker-linear/src/index.ts:111-115` | Linear request 30s timeout abort | `tracker.api_timeout` | SHOULD |

### D. Notifier plugins (3 entries — distinct shapes from D31's lump)

> The lifecycle-manager planning doc explicitly **SKIPs** D31 (`notifier.notify` failure) pending notifier subsystem rework. But these plugin-internal events are about *distinguishing failure modes* the lifecycle catch can't see — not about replacing it.

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notifier-openclaw/src/index.ts:145-152` | 401/403 auth failure (distinct from generic 5xx; user-actionable: run `ao setup openclaw`) | `notifier.auth_failed` | **MUST** |
| `notifier-openclaw/src/index.ts:169-176` | ECONNREFUSED → throws with hint ("is openclaw running?") | `notifier.unreachable` | SHOULD |
| `notifier-discord/src/index.ts:120-134` | 429 rate-limit retry budget exhausted | `notifier.rate_limited` | SHOULD |
| `notifier-composio/src/index.ts:65-78` | composio-core SDK missing (mirrors tracker dep_missing pattern) | `notifier.dep_missing` | SHOULD |

### E. Explicitly NOT in scope

| File / pattern | Why |
|---|---|
| `agent-*/src/index.ts` — JSONL parse swallows | Per-poll volume catastrophic |
| `runtime-*/src/index.ts` — capture-pane / has-session swallows | Polled every cycle |
| `*/detect()` returning false on missing binary | Plugin-init-time; CLI startup surfaces this |
| `notifier-slack/webhook` — generic non-2xx | D31 SKIP — notifier subsystem rework pending |
| `terminal-iterm2` — osascript swallows | Polled by UI |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --source workspace --kind workspace.branch_collision` reveals concurrent-session branch collisions
- [ ] `ao events list --source tracker --kind tracker.dep_missing` shows "Composio SDK not installed" once per AO startup (deduped)
- [ ] `ao events list --kind scm.gh_unavailable` distinguishes "gh missing" from rate-limit
- [ ] `notifier.auth_failed` fires distinctly from generic notify failures (covered by D31 SKIP)
- [ ] All 5 MUST emits have regression tests
- [ ] No plugin emit fires on per-poll paths (volume tests included)

## Testing approach

Per-plugin unit tests, mocking the failure shape:

```ts
// scm-github/src/__tests__/graphql-batch.test.ts
it("emits scm.gh_unavailable when gh binary is missing", async () => {
  vi.spyOn(child_process, "execFile").mockRejectedValue({ code: "ENOENT" });

  await expect(verifyGhCLI()).rejects.toThrow("GH_CLI_UNAVAILABLE");
  expect(recordActivityEvent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({
      source: "scm",
      kind: "scm.gh_unavailable",
      level: "error",
    }),
  );
});

// notifier-openclaw/src/__tests__/index.test.ts
it("emits notifier.auth_failed on 401 (distinct from notifier.unreachable on ECONNREFUSED)", async () => {
  // Mock fetch returning 401
  vi.spyOn(global, "fetch").mockResolvedValue(new Response("", { status: 401 }));

  await expect(notifier.notify(event)).rejects.toThrow();
  expect(recordActivityEvent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({ kind: "notifier.auth_failed" }),
  );
});
```

## Invariants to preserve

- **No subprocess stderr in `summary`** — git/gh/glab error output can include credentials in URLs (`https://x:token@host`); use `data.errorMessage` (sanitized) only
- **Dedupe `dep_missing` events at plugin boundary** — `tracker-linear`'s `composio SDK missing` warning fires multiple times today; emit only ONCE per process (use a module-level boolean guard)
- **No per-poll plugin emits** — every plugin call that runs every poll cycle is a hard NO unless it represents a state change
- Stack traces forbidden in `data` (B16 from PR #1620's planning doc)

## Out of scope

- Notifier subsystem refactor (parent #1511 mentions it; D31 SKIP stands until that lands)
- Agent plugin internals (per-poll volume; covered by lifecycle-manager activity probes)
- Runtime plugin internals (same)
- Terminal plugin internals (UI-driven, low value)

title: Activity events: Recovery, metadata-corruption detection, agent-report (sub-issue of #1511)
body:
> Sub-issue of #1511. Depends on PR #1620 landing first.

## Goal

Two small but important domains:

1. **Recovery subsystem** — `packages/core/src/recovery/`. User-initiated diagnostic flow (`ao recover`). Today writes its own NDJSON log but events aren't queryable alongside lifecycle events.
2. **Metadata corruption detection** — `metadata.ts`. Forensic event for "AO detected a corrupt session-metadata file and renamed it `.corrupt-{ts}`." Today: `console.warn` only. This is the worst-case data loss scenario and silently overwriting metadata is exactly what RCA needs to flag.

RCA today can't answer:

- Did `ao recover` actually fix anything? Which sessions did it skip?
- Has AO ever silently renamed a corrupt metadata file? When?
- Did `applyAgentReport` reject a transition (and why)?

## New `ActivityEventSource`

- `"recovery"` — recovery/ subsystem

`"session-manager"` and `"api"` already in union for the metadata + agent-report kinds.

## Insertion points (5 entries: 2 MUST, 3 SHOULD)

### A. Recovery subsystem (2 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery/manager.ts:108-113` | per-session failure pushed to `report.errors` (today: in result, not queryable) | `recovery.session_failed` | **MUST** |
| `recovery/actions.ts:147-153` | `recoverSession` outer catch | `recovery.action_failed` | SHOULD |

### B. Metadata corruption (1 entry)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata.ts:358-367` | `mutateMetadata` corrupt JSON detected, file renamed `.corrupt-{ts}` (today: console.warn only) | `metadata.corrupt_detected` | **MUST** |

### C. Agent report apply (2 entries)

| File:line | Surface | Proposed kind | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-report.ts:386-388` | `applyAgentReport` "Session not found" throw | `api.agent_report.session_not_found` | COULD |
| `agent-report.ts:441-456` | `applyAgentReport` rejected transition (audit entry written, then throws) | `api.agent_report.transition_rejected` | SHOULD |

> Note: agent-report kinds use `api` source because `ao report` is the API surface that calls into `applyAgentReport`. If overlapping with sub-issue 5 (Config / plugin-registry / migration), pick one home — these are listed in both for clarity.

### D. Explicitly NOT in scope

| File:line | Why |
|---|---|
| `recovery/validator.ts:78-110` | `validateSession` probe catches — recovery's deliberate uncertainty handling (per-session noisy) |
| `recovery/actions.ts:191-203` | `cleanupSession` runtime/workspace destroy silent catches — already best-effort, covered by overall recovery result |
| `metadata.ts:425-430` | `deleteMetadata` unlink catch (concurrent delete) — expected race |

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ao events list --source recovery` reconstructs an `ao recover` invocation timeline
- [ ] `ao events list --kind metadata.corrupt_detected` flags every silent overwrite in the system's history (forensic record)
- [ ] `recovery.session_failed` events include `sessionId` so `ao events list --session <id>` finds them
- [ ] `metadata.corrupt_detected` includes `data.renamedTo` (the `.corrupt-{ts}` filename) for forensic recovery
- [ ] All 2 MUST emits have regression tests

## Testing approach

```ts
// metadata.test.ts
it("emits metadata.corrupt_detected when JSON parse fails and file is renamed", async () => {
  await fs.writeFile(metaPath, "{ broken json");

  const result = await mutateMetadata(metaPath, (m) => m);

  expect(result).toBeNull();
  expect(recordActivityEvent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({
      kind: "metadata.corrupt_detected",
      data: expect.objectContaining({
        renamedTo: expect.stringMatching(/\.corrupt-\d+$/),
      }),
    }),
  );
});

// recovery/manager.test.ts
it("emits recovery.session_failed for each session that recovery couldn't fix", async () => {
  vi.mocked(recoverSession)
    .mockResolvedValueOnce({ status: "ok" })
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error("worktree missing"));

  await runRecovery({ sessions: [s1, s2] });

  const events = vi.mocked(recordActivityEvent).mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);
  expect(events.filter((e) => e.kind === "recovery.session_failed")).toHaveLength(1);
});
```

## Invariants to preserve

- **B22**: recovery events fire per *session*, not per *probe step*. One `recovery.session_failed` per failed session, not one per probe inside it.
- **No raw error stacks in `data`** — `errorMessage` only (per gist 16KB cap)
- **B11**: `metadata.corrupt_detected` `data` field can include the truncated bad-JSON content as `data.contentSample` (max 200 chars) for forensic context — but NOT the full file (could be 16KB+; sanitizer drops over-cap data)

## Out of scope

- session-manager kill paths (sibling sub-issue: session-manager rounding-out)
- `ao recover` CLI command-level events (sibling sub-issue: CLI commands)
- agent-report write path inside the agent (out of AO's process; not instrumentable here)

title: ao start fails with "session already exists" after crash leaves stale empty metadata file
body:
## Bug

`ao start` fails with:

```
✖ Orchestrator setup failed
Error: Failed to setup orchestrator: Orchestrator session "ao-orchestrator" already exists. Use ensureOrchestrator() to reuse or restore it.
```

## Root Cause

Two functions disagree on what "session exists" means:

- `reserveSessionId()` — creates an empty `.json` file with `O_EXCL`. Returns `false` if the file exists on disk.
- `readMetadataRaw()` — reads the same file. If empty (reservation marker only), returns `null` — treats as "doesn't exist".

**Sequence:**
1. Previous `ao start` crashes/killed before writing real metadata → empty file left on disk
2. Next `ao start` → `ensureOrchestratorInternal()` → `get(sessionId)` → `readMetadataRaw` returns `null` (empty file)
3. Falls through to `spawnOrchestrator()` → `reserveFixedOrchestratorIdentity()` → `reserveSessionId()` returns `false`
4. Throws the error

The catch block polls for 20s assuming a concurrent orchestrator race — but there is none, just a stale empty file. Poll times out, error re-thrown.

## Fix

In `ensureOrchestratorInternal()` catch block (`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` ~L1839): when `waitForConcurrentOrchestrator` returns null (no concurrent race), delete the stale empty metadata file and retry `spawnOrchestrator` once.

## Workaround

```bash
rm ~/.ao/sessions/<project>/ao-orchestrator.json
ao start
```

## Environment
- macOS, `ao start` with project that had a previous crashed orchestrator session
- Reported by @yyovil

title: fix(core): recover from stale empty orchestrator reservation file
body:
## Problem

`ao start` fails with `"Orchestrator session already exists"` after a previous run crashes/is killed before writing orchestrator metadata. The empty reservation file left on disk causes a mismatch: `readMetadataRaw()` returns `null` (treats empty as absent) while `reserveSessionId()` sees the file as occupied.

See #1661 for full root cause analysis.

## Fix

Two-layer recovery in `ensureOrchestratorInternal()`:

1. **Proactive cleanup (fast path):** After `get()` returns null, unconditionally attempt `deleteMetadata` to remove any stale reservation file before calling `spawnOrchestrator()`. This avoids both the confusing error and the 20-second concurrent-orchestrator poll.

2. **Catch-block retry (race path):** If a concurrent process recreates the file between cleanup and spawn, catch the reservation error, wait for concurrent orchestrator, and if none found, clean up + retry once with a descriptive error on final failure.

## Testing

Two new test cases in `spawn.test.ts`:
- **Empty reservation file:** Uses `reserveSessionId()` to create the exact same stale empty file that a crashed `ao start` leaves behind. Verifies `ensureOrchestrator()` succeeds and writes valid metadata.
- **Corrupt reservation file:** Writes garbage content. Verifies the same recovery path.

Both tests pass without the 20s concurrent-orchestrator timeout thanks to the proactive cleanup.

---

## Manual review scripts

The reviewer scripts are maintained in this gist instead of inline in the PR body:

- [reproduce-stale-reservation.sh](https://gist.github.com/yyovil/15245c49916defbe10e7507780fa0e7a#file-reproduce-stale-reservation-sh) — run on `main` before the fix.
- [verify-stale-reservation-fix.sh](https://gist.github.com/yyovil/15245c49916defbe10e7507780fa0e7a#file-verify-stale-reservation-fix-sh) — run on this fix branch.

Notes:
- The scripts use the current AO metadata layout: `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<project-id>/sessions/<session-prefix>-orchestrator.json`.
- Both scripts accept optional arguments: `<project-id> [session-prefix]`. If `session-prefix` is omitted, it defaults to `project-id`.

Closes #1661

title: feat(pipeline): v1.1b — pipeline triggers (pr_opened, pr_push, review_requested, manual) + concurrency policy
body:
Sub-task of #1349 (v1). **Depends on v1.1 (#1630).** Can run in parallel with v1.2 (#1631) and v1.3 (#1632) — touches different files (lifecycle-manager + config vs executors vs predicate DSL).

Base branch: `pipelines`. See v0.1 (#1627) for cluster design decisions.

## Problem

Without triggers, the only way to start a pipeline run is `ao pipeline run <name>` from the CLI — fully manual. The entire point of a pipeline is that it fires automatically when something happens on the PR.

## Scope

### Config schema — `Pipeline.triggers: Trigger[]`

```yaml
pipelines:
  review:
    triggers:
      - on: pr_opened
        branches: ["main", "develop"]
        excludeDrafts: true
      - on: pr_push
        files: ["src/**", "packages/**"]
      - on: manual  # always available; makes manual triggering explicit
    stages:
      ...
```

Trigger types:

| Type | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `pr_opened` | A PR is opened (or reopened) targeting a watched branch |
| `pr_push` | A new commit is pushed to a PR's branch |
| `pr_review_requested` | A review is requested on the PR |
| `manual` | Explicitly via `ao pipeline run` |

Filters (all optional):
- `branches: string[]` — glob-match against PR base branch
- `files: string[]` — only fire if the diff touches any of these paths (glob)
- `labels: string[]` — only fire if the PR has any of these labels
- `excludeDrafts: boolean` — skip draft PRs (default false)

### Concurrency policy — `Pipeline.concurrency`

What happens if a trigger fires while a run is already in progress for the same pipeline:

```yaml
pipelines:
  review:
    concurrency: cancel_in_progress  # default
    # or: skip | queue
```

| Policy | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `cancel_in_progress` | Kill the current run, start fresh (default — usually right for PR push) |
| `skip` | Ignore the trigger if a run is active |
| `queue` | Wait for the active run to finish, then start |

### Lifecycle-manager integration

On each poll cycle, lifecycle-manager evaluates triggers for all configured pipelines against recent SCM events. Needs a new (lightweight) SCM method:

```typescript
// Returns events since the given timestamp — called each poll cycle
SCM.getRecentPREvents(since: Date): Promise<PREvent[]>
```

`PREvent` is minimal: `{ type, prNumber, baseBranch, headBranch, labels, changedFiles, isDraft, occurredAt }`.

Lifecycle-manager checks:
1. Fetch events since last-checked timestamp (persisted to avoid re-firing on restart)
2. For each pipeline config, evaluate each trigger against each event
3. If trigger matches + concurrency policy permits → `engine.startRun(pipelineName, { prNumber })`
4. Update last-checked timestamp

### Manual trigger refinement

`ao pipeline run <name>` now explicitly fires a `manual` trigger. Pipelines without `manual` in their trigger list still accept it — `manual` is always available (the trigger list gates automatic firing, not CLI invocation).

### What this does NOT cover

- Cron triggers — remain out of scope
- `session.started` lifecycle triggers — remain out of scope
- Cross-pipeline triggers (one pipeline firing another) — v3 territory, dropped

## Acceptance

- A pipeline with `pr_opened` trigger fires automatically when a PR is opened against a watched branch
- A pipeline with `pr_push` + `files` filter only fires when matched files change
- `cancel_in_progress` policy kills the active run and starts a new one
- `skip` policy silently ignores the trigger when a run is active
- `queue` policy starts a new run immediately after the active one reaches a terminal state
- Last-checked timestamp persists across `ao stop` / `ao start` restarts
- `ao pipeline run <name>` always works regardless of trigger config
- Vitest coverage on trigger evaluation + concurrency policy logic
- PR opened against `pipelines`

title: feat(pipeline): v1.1 — DAG, parallel scheduling, Stage.routes
body:
Closes #1630.

Sub-task of #1349. Depends on v0.3 (already merged into `pipelines`).

## Summary

Turns the pipeline engine into a real DAG. Stages declare dependencies, run in parallel up to a configurable cap, and can carry conditional activation predicates that mark them `skipped` when upstream outcomes don't satisfy the route.

- **`Stage.dependsOn: string[]`** — explicit dependency declarations. Default `[]`.
- **`Stage.routes.when`** — typed predicate (minimal hardcoded union: `allSucceeded` / `anySucceeded` / `anyFailed`). The richer predicate DSL is intentionally deferred to v1.3.
- **Cycle detection at config load** — `ConfiguredPipelineSchema.superRefine` rejects bad configs with a clear error naming the cycle (e.g. `a → b → c → a`). Unknown `dependsOn` / `routes` references, self-dependencies, and duplicate stage names fail there too.
- **Parallel scheduling** — `Pipeline.maxConcurrentStages` still defaults to **1** per the v1.1 spec. When raised, independent stages run concurrently; declaration order is preserved as slot priority so linear pipelines stay byte-identical to v0 behavior.
- **Cascade skips run to fixpoint inside one reducer step** — skipping a stage may make a downstream stage's routes evaluate to false, which marks it skipped, which may cascade further. Each transition emits a `pipeline.stage.terminated` observation matching the existing schema.
- **Multi-pipeline support** was already wired in v0.3 (`pipelines:` is a record, `--pipeline <name>` flag works). New tests verify cross-pipeline config validation.

## Implementation notes

- New file `packages/core/src/pipeline/dag.ts` holds the DAG scheduler. `reducer.ts` stays focused on event-shape transitions.
- `startableStageEffects` is removed from `reducer-helpers.ts` — `scheduleAfterChange` supersedes it (returns updated run + start effects + newly-skipped stages + allTerminal flag).
- The reducer integrates `scheduleAfterChange` at three sites: `reduceTriggerFired`, `finalizeStageCompletion` (success path), and `reduceRunResumed`. Failure semantics (run terminates as `stalled`) are preserved.
- `routes` predicates are evaluated only after every referenced upstream stage is terminal; routes refs that aren't in `dependsOn` are still gated correctly so a stage doesn't optimistically start before its predicate is decidable.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

- [x] Cycle detection rejects bad configs at load with a clear error naming the cycle
- [x] Two independent stages run concurrently when `maxConcurrentStages >= 2`
- [x] A stage with unmet `dependsOn` does not start
- [x] A stage with an unsatisfied `routes` predicate is skipped (and marked as such in the run record)
- [x] Vitest coverage on scheduler — 19 new tests in `pipeline-dag.test.ts`
- [x] PR opened against `pipelines`

## Out of scope (per issue)

- New executors (v1.2)
- Predicate DSL / `exitPredicates` (v1.3)
- Workspace classes (v1.3)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — passes
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1,152 tests pass (1,133 baseline + 19 new DAG tests)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` — passes
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 644 tests pass
- [x] Prettier check on all modified files passes

title: feat(pipeline): v1.1b — pipeline triggers + concurrency policy
body:
Closes #1663.

## Summary

- Adds `Pipeline.triggers[]` config: `pr_opened`, `pr_push`, `pr_review_requested`, `manual` with `branches` / `files` / `labels` / `excludeDrafts` filters.
- Adds `Pipeline.concurrency` policy: `cancel_in_progress` (default) / `skip` / `queue`.
- Adds optional `SCM.getRecentPREvents(since)` + the `PREvent` type.
- Wires a per-poll auto-trigger pass into `lifecycle-manager.pollAll`.
- Persists `{pipelinesDir}/auto-trigger-state.json` (last-checked timestamp + queued triggers) so restarts don't re-fire the SCM event window.
- 50+ Vitest cases for glob matching, filter conjunction, concurrency decisions, end-to-end pass behaviour (start/cancel/skip/queue/drain), queue aging, and last-checked persistence.

## Architecture notes

- **Pure decisions vs I/O.** `pipeline/triggers.ts` is pure (`evaluateTrigger`, `decideConcurrencyAction`). `pipeline/auto-trigger.ts` orchestrates persistence + dispatching but takes `startRun` / `cancelActiveRun` / `isActiveRun` as injected callbacks.
- **No engine coupling yet.** The PipelineEngine isn't instantiated inside lifecycle-manager today (v0.4 wiring is the next sub-task). The CLI-side wiring drives the pass through the existing `triggerRun` / `cancelRun` adapters in `pipeline-service`. When the engine moves into lifecycle-manager, the auto-trigger pass swaps `startRun` to call `engine.startRun` — no changes to the trigger logic itself.
- **Concurrency scope.** Policy applies *per pipeline* (per the v1.1b spec) — any non-terminal run on the same `pipelineName` counts as active regardless of which PR fired it. SessionIds are encoded as `pipeline.<name>.pr-<n>` so loops are per-PR for trace clarity even though the policy looks across loops.
- **Manual triggers always work.** `evaluateTrigger` returns `false` for `on: "manual"` so they never fire from PR events; `ao pipeline run` continues to work via `triggerRun` regardless of the trigger list (acceptance criterion).
- **No new deps.** Glob matching is hand-rolled (`*` single-segment, `**` any-segment) — keeps `@aoagents/ao-core` dependency-free.

## Files

- `packages/core/src/pipeline/types.ts` — `PipelineTrigger`, `PipelineTriggerEvent`, `ConcurrencyPolicy`, `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY_POLICY`. Adds `triggers?` and `concurrency?` to `Pipeline`.
- `packages/core/src/pipeline/config-schema.ts` — Zod schema for the new fields. Runtime conversion preserves arrays via spread.
- `packages/core/src/pipeline/triggers.ts` — pure decision module (new).
- `packages/core/src/pipeline/auto-trigger.ts` — pass orchestrator + state persistence (new).
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — `PREvent`, `PREventType`, `SCM.getRecentPREvents`.
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — `pipelineAutoTrigger` dep + invocation in `pollAll` (try/catch isolated; observability metric `pipeline_auto_trigger`).
- `packages/cli/src/lib/pipeline-auto-trigger.ts` — CLI wiring: per-project SCM resolve, store-backed `isActiveRun`, dispatch via `triggerRun` (new).
- `packages/cli/src/lib/create-session-manager.ts` — wires the auto-trigger into `getLifecycleManager`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1207 pass (33 new in `pipeline-triggers.test.ts`, 8 new in `pipeline-config-triggers.test.ts`)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 644 pass
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm exec eslint` on touched files — clean (only pre-existing warnings in unrelated files)
- [ ] Manual: configure a pipeline with `pr_opened` trigger + `branches: [main]`, verify it fires when a PR opens against main
- [ ] Manual: stop / start `ao` mid-pass, confirm `auto-trigger-state.json` persists `lastCheckedAt`
- [ ] Manual: configure `concurrency: cancel_in_progress`, push twice in quick succession, verify the first run is cancelled

title: fix(forgejo): merge with main + resolve outstanding Bugbot findings
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #825 (which has been stalled since 2026-03-31) that:

1. Resolves the merge conflicts with `main` introduced by the `@composio` → `@aoagents` scope rename and downstream platform changes since #825 last synced.
2. Addresses the 7 unresolved Cursor Bugbot findings on the head commit of #825.

PR #825 opened the Forgejo SCM and tracker plugins; this PR rescues that work and gets it back into a mergeable state. royalcala (the original author) is welcome to take this over — happy to close in their favor if they prefer to push the fixes themselves.

## Bugbot fixes (one commit each)

| Severity | Plugin | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High | tracker-forgejo | `createIssue` now resolves label names to numeric IDs before POST (matches the existing `updateIssue` fix). |
| High | scm-forgejo | Webhook defaults switched to Forgejo-native (`x-forgejo-*` headers, raw-hex signature). See behavioral change below. |
| Med  | scm-forgejo | `getReviewDecision` maps `PENDING` → `pending` (was falling through to `none`). |
| Med  | scm-forgejo | `getMergeability` blocks merge for any unrecognized `mergeable` value (catches `null`/future Forgejo states). |
| Med  | both | REST helper now uses an `AbortController` 30 s timeout matching the `gh` CLI path. |
| Med  | both | REST helper honors an explicit `http://` scheme on the configured host. |
| Med  | tracker-forgejo | Label lookup paginates instead of capping at one page of 100 labels. |

Each fix has a regression test alongside it.

## Behavioral change (callout for reviewers)

**Webhook defaults now match Forgejo-native instead of GitHub-compat.** Configured-secret webhooks were being rejected because the previous defaults (`x-hub-signature-256` with `sha256=`-prefixed digest, `x-github-event`, `x-github-delivery`) don't match what Forgejo sends by default (`x-forgejo-signature` with raw-hex, `x-forgejo-event`, `x-forgejo-delivery`). Deployments wiring GitHub-compat receivers can still override via `project.scm.webhook.{signature,event,delivery}Header` — covered by a regression test. Since the Forgejo plugin is brand-new (introduced in #825 itself), real-world impact is expected to be near-zero.

## Merge-forced changes beyond the Bugbot fixes

The merge with `main` required three changes that were not part of the original Bugbot list. Flagging them so they're not read as scope creep:

- **`scm-forgejo`: `getAutomatedComments` removed.** The SCM interface dropped this method in favor of an optional `getReviewThreads` (`@since 0.6.0`). The fallback chain in core (which uses `getPendingComments`) covers the gap. A `getReviewThreads` implementation for Forgejo is left as a follow-up — `scm-github` has one but Forgejo has no GraphQL endpoint, so it'd need a different shape.
- **`tracker-forgejo`: `requireRepo()` helper added.** `main` made `ProjectConfig.repo` optional (commit `c8af50f`). Same pattern as `tracker-github`.
- **`core/global-config.ts`: `ScmPlatform` enum extended.** One-line addition of `"forgejo"` to the `GlobalRepoIdentitySchema` enum so the merge typechecks.

Two follow-on housekeeping commits also landed: `chore(forgejo): satisfy upstream eslint rules` (4 trivial errors flagged by main's tightened config) and `test: rename Forgejo plugin scope in remaining test mocks` (two test files still referenced `@composio/...` package strings the merge missed).

## Validation

```
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm -r --filter '!@aoagents/ao-web' build       # green
pnpm -r --filter '!@aoagents/ao-web' typecheck   # green
pnpm lint                                        # green (0 errors, 54 pre-existing warnings)
pnpm test                                        # all non-web packages green
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web build             # green
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test              # 807 pass / 3 fail / 19 skip — see note below
```

**The 3 failing web tests** (`api-routes.test.ts` × 2, `sessions/[id]/page.test.tsx`, plus a `direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts` collection failure) reproduce identically on `origin/main` with the exact same numbers. They are pre-existing baseline failures, not introduced by this PR.

**Integration tests** (`pnpm test:integration`) require `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `LINEAR_*` secrets that aren't available on the fork, so the `Integration Tests` CI job will fail with auth errors here even though the changes themselves are unrelated to that flow.

## Diff size

28 files changed (+4496 / −35) vs `main`. Most of the volume is the original Forgejo plugin code from #825; the post-merge fixes contribute only 6 files / +479 / −63.

## Closes

Closes #826. If maintainers prefer to merge this in place of #825, please close #825 as superseded.

title: Terminal content clipped on right side — FitAddon scrollbar width mismatch
body:
## Bug

When viewing a session detail page (e.g. `/projects/integrator/sessions/int-orchestrator`), the right side of the terminal content is clipped/overflowed. Characters at the rightmost columns are hidden under the scrollbar.

## Root Cause

`FitAddon.proposeDimensions()` hardcodes a 14px scrollbar reservation (`ViewportConstants.DEFAULT_SCROLL_BAR_WIDTH = 14`), subtracting 14px from the available width before calculating column count.

But the custom CSS overrides in `globals.css` set the scrollbar to only 5px wide:

```css
.xterm .xterm-viewport { overflow-y: overlay !important; }
.xterm .xterm-viewport::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 5px; }
```

Two problems:
1. `overlay` is deprecated in Chrome 114+. Modern Chrome treats it as `auto`, so the scrollbar *does* consume layout space — but only 5px, not the 14px FitAddon assumes.
2. On Linux (where the dashboard runs), the default scrollbar from the desktop environment can be **wider than 14px**, overlapping the rightmost columns.

## Fix

Set `scrollback: 0` on the xterm Terminal options. tmux already provides scrollback/copy-mode, so xterm scrollback is redundant. With `scrollback: 0`, FitAddon subtracts 0px and the width calculation matches the actual rendering.

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/terminal/useXtermTerminal.ts` line 107

```diff
- scrollback: 10000,
+ scrollback: 0, // tmux handles scrollback; avoids FitAddon scrollbar width mismatch
```

## Environment
- AO dashboard on Linux server
- Chromium-based browser
- Reproducible on session detail page with active terminal

title: setup-labels API is GitHub-only and uses an inconsistent label set
body:
## Environment

- `ao --version`: 0.4.0 (also reproduces on 0.5.0 / main by code inspection at `packages/web/src/app/api/setup-labels/route.ts`)
- OS: macOS 26.3.1, arm64
- Node: v24.14.1

## Summary

`packages/web/src/app/api/setup-labels/route.ts` is intended to pre-create the agent labels every project needs, but three issues make it unusable in practice for non-GitHub trackers and inconsistent with the rest of the orchestrator.

## Three problems in 50 lines

**1. Hardcoded to `gh` CLI without plugin dispatch.**

The route shells out directly to `gh label create --repo <project.repo>` with no `GH_HOST` override. Effects per tracker:

| Tracker | `setup-labels` works? |
|---|---|
| `tracker-github` | yes (matches the hardcoded `gh`) |
| `tracker-gitlab` | no — `gh` doesn't speak GitLab; `scm-gitlab`/`tracker-gitlab` use `glab` |
| `tracker-forgejo` | no — `gh` with no `GH_HOST` won't reach a Forgejo host |
| `tracker-linear` | no — `gh` doesn't speak Linear |

The route bypasses the `Tracker` plugin abstraction entirely. The `Tracker` interface in `@aoagents/ao-core/types.ts` declares no label-management method, so there is no clean dispatch point today.

**2. Label set inconsistent with `services.ts`.**

The route creates: `agent:backlog`, `agent:in-progress`, `agent:blocked`, `agent:done`.

But `pollBacklog` / `labelIssuesForVerification` / `relabelReopenedIssues` in `packages/web/src/lib/services.ts` read and write a different set: `agent:backlog`, `agent:in-progress`, `agent:done`, `merged-unverified`.

Result: `agent:blocked` is created but never referenced by the orchestrator; `merged-unverified` is required by the verification flow but the route never creates it.

**3. No caller wires the route up.**

`grep -rn "setup-labels"` finds no UI button, CLI subcommand, or auto-trigger. The endpoint is dead from a UX perspective — operators would have to `curl -X POST` it manually, and even then, only GitHub projects would benefit.

## Steps to reproduce (Forgejo example)

1. Configure a project with `tracker.plugin: forgejo` (Forgejo `repo` + `host`).
2. Ensure none of `agent:backlog`, `agent:in-progress`, `agent:done`, `merged-unverified` exist as repo labels on the Forgejo repo.
3. `ao start`, then open an issue on Forgejo and add label `agent:backlog` (Forgejo accepts it as an ad-hoc string even without a repo-level entry).
4. Hit `curl http://localhost:3001/api/backlog` to start the lazy poller.
5. Observe the orchestrator throw `Unable to resolve Forgejo label IDs for: agent:in-progress` on every poll cycle when it tries to claim the issue.
6. Try `curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/setup-labels`. The route claims success but `gh label create` either fails or hits github.com — never the Forgejo host.

## Expected vs. actual

**Expected.** A documented or in-product flow for creating the orchestrator's required labels on whatever tracker the project uses. The route (or its successor) should dispatch through `registry.get("tracker", project.tracker.plugin)` and create labels via the right API per provider.

**Actual.** Route shells `gh` directly with no `GH_HOST` — only github.com works. `agent:blocked` is created but never used; `merged-unverified` is required but never created. No caller invokes the route, so even GitHub users only benefit by hitting it by hand.

## Relevant `ao doctor` output

```
Results: 17 PASS, 0 WARN, 0 FAIL, 0 FIXED
Environment looks healthy enough to run Agent Orchestrator.
```

Note: `doctor` does not currently check tracker labels — orthogonal to this issue but adds to the silent-failure surface.

## Suggested fix shape

1. Add `ensureLabels(labels: LabelSpec[]): Promise<void>` (or `createLabel` + `getLabels` primitives) to the `Tracker` interface in `@aoagents/ao-core`.
2. Implement per plugin:
   - `tracker-github` via `gh label create` with `GH_HOST`
   - `tracker-gitlab` via `glab` or GitLab REST
   - `tracker-forgejo` via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels` (already wired through the existing `forgejoApi` helper)
   - `tracker-linear` no-op or skip (Linear doesn't have repo labels)
3. Refactor `/api/setup-labels` to dispatch via the registry instead of shelling `gh` directly.
4. Reconcile the canonical label set against `services.ts` usage (either drop `agent:blocked` or wire it up; add `merged-unverified`).
5. Wire a CLI command (`ao setup labels`) and/or a dashboard button. Consider auto-running on first orchestrator boot in a project that's missing required labels.

## Notes

Encountered while testing #1674 (Forgejo plugin rescue) against a real Forgejo instance. The bug is not introduced by that PR — the route exists unchanged on `origin/main` and `tracker-gitlab` would hit the same wall.

title: Notifier plugin warnings spam stdout/stderr on every CLI command
body:
## Problem

Notifier plugins (`notifier-discord`, `notifier-slack`, `notifier-openclaw`, `notifier-webhook`, `notifier-composio`, `notifier-desktop`) emit unconditional `console.warn()` messages during their `create()` initialization when config is missing or incomplete (e.g., no webhook URL, no API token, unsupported OS).

Since `getPluginRegistry()` is called by almost every CLI command, these warnings spam the terminal on **every invocation** — even for commands that have nothing to do with notifications.

### Affected commands (exhaustive)
All of these call `getSessionManager()` or `getPluginRegistry()`, which triggers `loadFromConfig()` → `loadBuiltins()` → `registerNotifier()` → `plugin.create()`:

- `ao status`
- `ao session ls` / `ao session list`
- `ao session show`
- `ao session kill`
- `ao session restore`
- `ao session claim-pr`
- `ao session detail`
- `ao session cleanup`
- `ao spawn`
- `ao send`
- `ao start`
- `ao stop`
- `ao review-check`
- `ao report`
- `ao plugin list`
- `ao plugin install`
- `ao verify`

### Warnings that get spammed

```
[notifier-slack] No webhookUrl configured — notifications will be no-ops
[notifier-discord] No webhookUrl configured. Set it in agent-orchestrator.yaml...
[notifier-webhook] No url configured — notifications will be no-ops
[notifier-openclaw] No token configured. Set OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN env var...
[notifier-composio] No composioApiKey or COMPOSIO_API_KEY configured — notifications will be no-ops
[notifier-desktop] Desktop notifications not supported on linux
```

## Proposed Fix

Suppress notifier plugin `console.warn()` output during plugin registry loading, except when running `ao doctor`. This keeps the diagnostic information available where it belongs (`ao doctor` checks notifier connectivity) while eliminating noise from all other commands.

### Implementation
1. Add `suppressNotifierWarnings` option to `createPluginRegistry()`
2. In `registerNotifier()`, temporarily intercept `console.warn` during `plugin.create()` when suppression is enabled
3. All CLI commands use suppression by default via `getPluginRegistry()`
4. `ao doctor` explicitly disables suppression so warnings are visible during diagnostics

title: fix: tmux green status bar visible in web terminal for agent sessions
body: ## Bug The tmux status bar (bright green line) is visible at the bottom of web terminals in agent sessions. ## Screenshot Reported by @karnalprateek — green tmux status bar visible at bottom of web terminal in session view. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Spawn a session via `ao spawn` 2. Open the web dashboard and view the session terminal 3. Green tmux status bar appears at the bottom of the terminal ## Root Cause `packages/core/src/tmux.ts::newSession()` does not set `status off` when creating tmux sessions. The global tmux config has `status on` (`tmux show-option -g status` → `status on`). The web layer (`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts`, line 266) does run `set-option status off`, but **only when a WebSocket client connects**. Between session spawn and first web connection, the green bar is visible. ## Fix Add `set-option status off` in `newSession()` in `packages/core/src/tmux.ts`, after line 111: ```ts // Hide the tmux status bar — sessions are embedded in web terminal await tmux("set-option", "-t", opts.name, "status", "off"); ``` This ensures the bar is hidden from birth, regardless of when the web UI connects.

## Problem

The tmux green status bar is visible at the bottom of web terminals in agent sessions.

## Root Cause

`packages/core/src/tmux.ts::newSession()` does not set `status off` when creating tmux sessions. The global tmux config has `status on`.

The web layer (`mux-websocket.ts`) does run `set-option status off`, but only when a WebSocket client connects. Between session spawn and first web connection, the green bar is visible.

title: Session detail PR card shows +0/-0 instead of real diff stats
body:
## Bug
The PR summary card on the session detail page shows `+0, -0` for additions/deletions even when the PR has substantial changes (e.g., PR #1414 has `+629, -44`).

## Root Cause Analysis
`basicPRToDashboard()` in `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:272-273` hardcodes `additions: 0, deletions: 0`. The enrichment pipeline reads `session.metadata["prEnrichment"]` to overwrite these, but if enrichment is missing/stale, the zeros persist.

## Key Files
- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` — basicPRToDashboard(), enrichSessionPR()
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — batch enrichment write
- `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` — PR_FIELDS, extractPREnrichment()

## Fix Approach
1. Ensure batch enrichment runs at least once before ETag guard can skip
2. Hide diff stats when `pr.enriched === false`
3. Show nothing instead of `+0/-0` for unenriched PRs

Reported by @prateek.

title: False "GitHub API rate limited" banner from transient failures (60-min stale cache)
body:
## Bug Report

**Severity:** Medium — UX degradation, misleading state shown for 60 minutes

### Problem

The old `serialize.ts:enrichSessionPR()` ran 6 parallel SCM API calls via `Promise.allSettled`. If ≥3 of 6 rejected — for **any** reason (timeout, network blip, `gh` CLI error, DNS hiccup) — the code treated it identically to an actual HTTP 429 rate limit:

```ts
const mostFailed = failedCount >= results.length / 2;
```

When `mostFailed` is true:
1. `"API rate limited or unavailable"` gets pushed to `mergeability.blockers[]`
2. The partial data is cached with a **60-minute TTL** (`60 * 60_000`)
3. Dashboard reads the cached blocker and shows the amber banner for an hour
4. The banner text says "GitHub API rate limited" but the actual cause could be any transient failure

### Root Cause

Two distinct failure modes are collapsed into one code path:
- **Actual rate limit (429)** — needs long backoff, hourly cache is appropriate
- **Transient failure (network/timeout)** — should retry next cycle (30s), not cache for 60 min

The user reports: "for me the rate limit is 4970/5000 - which is nowhere near exhausted. But the banner says Github API rate limited and caches that false state for 60 minutes."

### Current State on `main`

The old `enrichSessionPR()` with the 6-call `Promise.allSettled` has been replaced by batch GraphQL enrichment (`graphql-batch.ts` + `lifecycle-manager.ts:populatePREnrichmentCache`). The current code does **not** write `"API rate limited or unavailable"` to blockers — the batch enrichment failure path just skips caching and retries on the next 30s poll.

However, the **detection surface** is still live (dead code):
- `isPRRateLimited()` in `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` checks for the blocker string
- `Dashboard.tsx` shows the amber banner when any session has it
- Two test files still use the string as test data

### Fix Options

**Option A — If running older version:** Backport the batch enrichment migration, or:
1. Distinguish 429 from transient failures in the `mostFailed` handler
2. Use short TTL (30s–2min) for transient failures, keep 60-min only for confirmed 429s
3. Check `gh api rate-limit` to verify remaining quota before showing the banner

**Option B — Cleanup on current main (dead code removal):**
1. Remove `isPRRateLimited()` from `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts`
2. Remove the rate-limit banner from `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx`
3. Remove the `"API rate limited or unavailable"` blocker string from test fixtures in:
   - `packages/web/src/components/__tests__/Dashboard.mobile.test.tsx`
   - `packages/web/src/components/__tests__/SessionDetail.mergeConflictActions.test.tsx`

### Affected Files
- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` (old enrichment path, pre-batch migration)
- `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` (`isPRRateLimited`)
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` (banner UI)

### Requested Assignee
@Pritom14

title: feat(notifier-pet): add Unix socket notifier for macOS pet overlay
body:
## Summary
- Adds `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-pet`, a notifier that bridges orchestrator events to a separate macOS pet overlay app over a local Unix socket.
- Each `notify` / `notifyWithActions` call opens a fresh `node:net` connection, writes one newline-terminated JSON line in the pet wire format (`{v:1, kind:"event", event:{...}, actions?:[{label, action}]}`), and closes — no pooling.
- Best-effort delivery: missing socket / `ECONNREFUSED` / write errors warn exactly once per process and are otherwise swallowed so the orchestrator is never blocked by the overlay being absent.
- Config under `notifiers.pet`: `socketPath` (string, `~`-expanded, defaults to `~/.agent-orchestrator/pet.sock`) and `enabled` (bool, defaults to `true`). Validated in `create()` and closed over.
- Registered in `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts` and added to `packages/cli/package.json` workspace deps alongside the other notifier plugins.
- No new external dependencies — built on Node's `node:net` and `node:os` only.

## Wire contract (one JSON line, newline-terminated)
```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "kind": "event",
  "event": {
    "id": "...",
    "type": "...",
    "priority": "urgent|action|warning|info",
    "sessionId": "...",
    "projectId": "...",
    "timestamp": "ISO8601",
    "message": "...",
    "data": {}
  },
  "actions": [{ "label": "...", "action": "..." }]
}
```
`actions` is omitted entirely for plain `notify()`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-pet test` — 10/10 passing (manifest, create shape, wire format, multi-call/no-pool, action serialization, ENOENT fallback, warn-once, server-hangup write error, `enabled:false` no-op)
- [x] `pnpm build` — green across all packages
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — green across all packages
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (only the same `no-console` warning the other notifier plugins emit for the once-per-process fallback log)

title: feat(pet-mac): add macOS pet overlay app for AO
body:
## Summary

Adds a native macOS pet overlay app at `apps/pet-mac/` — one borderless,
always-on-top pet window per project that mirrors AI agent state from the AO
dashboard. Inspired by Codex Pets.

- **One pet per project.** Pets only appear for projects with at least one
  session; windows auto-tile top-right and remember their dragged position
  per project (`UserDefaults`).
- **Two concurrent state sources.** A 5s HTTP poller of
  `GET http://localhost:3001/api/sessions` drives the steady-state mood
  (worst-state-wins per project), and a Unix socket listener at
  `~/.agent-orchestrator/pet.sock` plays one-shot reaction animations and
  shows the event message in a thought bubble. Each side runs independently
  with one-shot error logging — neither crashes the app if the other is
  down.
- **State → mood mapping** (covers all dashboard statuses): `waiting_input`
  / `needs_input` → alert, `ci_failed` / `stuck` / `blocked` / `errored` →
  sad, `pr_open` / `approved` / `mergeable` → happy, actively working →
  working, otherwise sleeping; no sessions → window hidden.
- **Right-click menu.** "Hide _project_ pet", "Switch sprite" (cycles
  bundled sprite sets, persisted), "Quit AOPet".
- **Two bundled placeholder sprite sets** (`dog`, `cat`) generated by
  `scripts/generate_sprites.py`. Sprites are pure file drops — replace
  PNGs at `Resources/sprites/<set>/<mood>_<frame>.png` to swap art.
- **Pure SwiftPM, AppKit only.** No Electron / Tauri / Catalyst. macOS 13+,
  Swift 5.9.

## Wire contract (consumer side)

The forthcoming `packages/plugins/notifier-pet/` plugin opens the socket
and writes one JSON envelope per line:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "kind": "event",
  "event": {
    "id": "evt_…",
    "type": "pr_merged",
    "priority": "urgent | action | warning | info",
    "sessionId": "ses_…",
    "projectId": "proj_…",
    "timestamp": "ISO8601",
    "message": "PR #42 merged",
    "data": { "...": "..." }
  },
  "actions": [{ "label": "Open PR", "action": "open:https://…" }]
}
```

Notes for the producer:
- Lines are `\n`-delimited; one envelope per line, empty lines skipped.
- Only `kind: "event"` is surfaced; other kinds are silently ignored to
  leave room for future framing.
- `sessionId`, `projectId`, `timestamp`, `actions` are optional. Events
  with no `projectId` are broadcast to every visible pet.
- Unknown `priority` / `status` / `activity` values decode tolerantly.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` — clean build succeeds (Swift 5.9 / macOS 13+)

title: Dashboard terminal renders blank on connect after upgrading to v0.4.0
body:
## Bug Report

**Severity:** P0 — core product functionality dead on stable release  
**Affects:** v0.4.0 (`@aoagents/ao@0.4.0`)  
**Regressed by:** #1259 (commit `68756105`)  
**Buffer-skip guard introduced in:** commit `78e57125`

### Symptom

After upgrading from `@aoagents/ao@0.3.0` to `0.4.0` and running `ao start` fresh, opening a session in the web dashboard shows the terminal panel as **connected** ("Connected" badge displayed, cursor flickers in the empty pane), but **no pane contents are ever drawn**.

The underlying tmux pane is healthy: `tmux attach-session -t <session>` shows the running agent and its output normally. `tmux capture-pane -p` returns empty.

Reproducible across multiple sessions on any OS (Ubuntu, macOS, etc.).

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### Architecture Change (v0.3.0 → v0.4.0)

**v0.3.0**: Per-terminal WebSocket. Each `DirectTerminal` component opened its own WS to `ws://host:14801/ws?session=<id>`. Server resolved tmux name, spawned PTY, streamed data 1:1. Every connection got a fresh PTY and full screen replay from tmux.

**v0.4.0**: Multiplexed WebSocket (`MuxProvider`). Single shared WS to `ws://host:14801/mux`. Terminal channels multiplexed via `{ ch: "terminal", type: "open", tmuxName }` messages. `TerminalManager` shares PTYs across connections.

### The Break: Buffer-Skip Guard on Re-Open

**File**: `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` (~line 486)

```typescript
// Subscribe and send history buffer only for new subscribers.
// Skipping the buffer on re-open prevents duplicate output when
// MuxProvider re-sends open for all terminals on reconnect.
if (!subscriptions.has(subscriptionKey)) {
    const buffer = terminalManager.getBuffer(id, projectId);
    // ... send buffer, then subscribe
}
```

When a client sends **close** then **open** (which happens on React effect re-runs, React strict mode double-mount, or MuxProvider reconnect):

1. Server's `subscriptions` Map entry is cleared by the **close** message
2. `TerminalManager` keeps the PTY alive (it only kills PTY when the *last* subscriber leaves across ALL mux connections)
3. On re-open, `terminalManager.open()` sees an existing PTY → returns early (no-op)
4. The `if (!subscriptions.has(subscriptionKey))` check passes (key was cleared) → buffer IS sent
5. **BUT** — if the subscription state is inconsistent (e.g., the client reconnects to a fresh WS but the server-side PTY was not killed because another subscriber exists), the buffer replay is skipped

The guard was added to prevent duplicate output on reconnect, but creates a dead zone where the client sees an empty terminal with no data flowing.

### Compounding Factor: PTY-tmux Attach No-Replay

The bug report states `tmux capture-pane -p` returns empty while `tmux attach` shows output. This is consistent with:

- A second PTY attaching to the same tmux session not receiving the initial screen replay from tmux (tmux already has an active client)
- The PTY's initial size hardcoded to 80×24 potentially causing tmux to render differently than the actual session size
- The shared `TerminalManager` reusing PTYs — in v0.3.0, each connection got a *fresh* PTY and tmux always replayed

### Data Flow Trace

**Server side** (`mux-websocket.ts`):
1. Client sends `{ ch: "terminal", type: "open", id: "mer-orchestrator", tmuxName: "mer-orchestrator" }`
2. `terminalManager.open(id, projectId, tmuxName)` → resolves tmux session name → spawns PTY via `node-pty` with `tmux attach-session -t <name>`
3. PTY `onData` callback pushes data to ring buffer + all subscribers
4. Server sends `"opened"` confirmation, then buffer (if new subscriber), then wires up live subscription

**Client side** (`MuxProvider.tsx` → `useXtermTerminal.ts`):
1. `openTerminal(sessionId, projectId, tmuxName)` → sends "open" message via mux WS
2. `subscribeTerminal(sessionId, callback, projectId)` → registers data handler
3. MuxProvider receives `ch: "terminal", type: "data"` → calls subscriber callbacks → `terminal.write(data)`
4. xterm.js renders

**Where it breaks**: Steps 2-4 of the server side have the guard that skips buffer replay, and the shared PTY doesn't re-attach to tmux (so no fresh screen replay either).

### Key Files in the Regression

| File | LOC changed | Role |
|------|-------------|------|
| `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` | ~300 | Mux WebSocket server + TerminalManager + buffer guard |
| `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` | ~125 | Shared mux WebSocket React context |
| `packages/web/src/components/terminal/useXtermTerminal.ts` | ~90 | xterm.js hook wired to mux |
| `packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts` | ~18 | Protocol type definitions |
| `packages/web/server/tmux-utils.ts` | ~19 | Project-scoped tmux resolution |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | ~multiple | tmuxName metadata storage |

### Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| Apr 28 | `36fed87b` — Storage redesign (tmux naming: `{hash}-{prefix}-{num}` → `{prefix}-{num}`) |
| ~Apr 28 | `68756105` — SSE→WS migration (#1259) introduces mux architecture |
| ~Apr 29 | `78e57125` — Buffer-skip guard added ("prevent duplicate buffer replay on reconnect") |
| May 1 | `b2cdf7ad` — Project-scoped tmux resolution fix |
| May 3 | `ef8ac42d` — v0.4.0 tagged and shipped to npm |
| May 4 | Bug reported — terminal blank on fresh sessions |

### Why This Shipped

| Gap | Details |
|-----|---------|
| **No E2E terminal test** | Mux WebSocket has unit tests for protocol parsing, but no integration test that spawns tmux, connects WS, and asserts rendered content |
| **No release smoke test** | v0.4.0 had ~300 LOC changed in mux-websocket alone with zero manual verification of "open terminal → see content" |
| **Cumulative refactor** | SSE→WS (#1259), storage redesign (#1466), project scoping (#1551) all touched the same files, reviewed in isolation, never tested together |
| **Buffer guard untested** | The `if (!subscriptions.has())` guard has no test for close→re-open or reconnect scenarios |

---

## Fix Direction

The buffer replay must **always** work for genuinely new subscribers. Options:

1. **Remove the guard, deduplicate client-side** — simplest, always send buffer. Client already handles duplicate data gracefully (xterm is idempotent for repeated writes)
2. **Kill PTY on last subscriber disconnect** — force fresh tmux attach on re-open, ensuring full screen replay every time
3. **Track subscriber identity properly** — use connection+key compound identity instead of just key presence

Option 1 is lowest risk and highest confidence.

## Prevention

1. **E2E terminal smoke test** — spawn tmux session with known output, connect via mux WS, assert data received within 5s, test close→re-open
2. **Release checklist gate** — before npm publish, verify `ao start → spawn → open in browser → terminal renders content`
3. **Add close→re-open + reconnect test cases** to mux-websocket integration tests
4. **`/health` endpoint enhancement** — verify tmux communication, not just connection count

title: fix(web): always replay terminal buffer on mux open (#1689)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1689 — dashboard terminal renders blank on connect after upgrading to v0.4.0.

The buffer-skip guard added in `78e57125` wrapped **both** the buffer send and the subscribe call in `if (!subscriptions.has(id))`. This silently skipped tmux screen replay on a same-connection re-open (React strict-mode double-mount edge case), leaving the terminal pane blank even though the WebSocket reported \"connected\".

This change moves the buffer send out from under the guard so every \`open\` message replays history. The guard is retained only around the \`terminalManager.subscribe(...)\` call so a duplicate \`open\` doesn't double-deliver live data. Re-sending the buffer to an already-subscribed client is safe — tmux's full-screen redraw sequences are idempotent and xterm just re-renders the same pane content.

- File: \`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts\` — guard restructure + comment refresh
- File: \`packages/web/server/__tests__/mux-websocket.test.ts\` — \`TerminalManager\` unit tests (empty buffer on fresh open, data accumulation, PTY lifecycle on subscriber drop, fresh PTY after re-open, multi-subscriber retention)

## Test plan

title: feat(web): activity events for webhooks and mux WebSocket (#1656)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1656 — sub-issue of #1511, follows #1620.

Adds 10 activity events covering two surfaces missed by the broader API sub-issue:

1. **Webhook ingress** at `app/api/webhooks/[...slug]/route.ts` — external system events with security implications
2. **Mux WebSocket terminal server** at `server/mux-websocket.ts` — drives the live terminal UI; today its lifecycle and failure modes are console-only

After this change, RCA can answer:

- *Did GitHub send us a webhook we rejected on auth?* → `ao events list --kind api.webhook_unverified`
- *How often is the terminal connection flapping?* → `ao events list --kind ui.terminal_heartbeat_lost`
- *Did the PTY actually die or did the user close their browser?* → `ao events list --kind ui.terminal_pty_lost` (only fires when subscribers are still attached)

### New event kinds

**Webhook (api source):**
| Kind | Level | When |
|---|---|---|
| `api.webhook_unverified` | warn | 401 signature verification failure |
| `api.webhook_rejected` | warn | 413 payload too large |
| `api.webhook_received` | info / warn | 202 accepted (warn if parse/lifecycle errors) |
| `api.webhook_failed` | error | 500 outer catch |

**Mux WebSocket (ui source — Node-side only, never browser):**
| Kind | Level | When |
|---|---|---|
| `ui.terminal_connected` | info | New mux WS connection |
| `ui.terminal_disconnected` | info | Connection closed |
| `ui.terminal_heartbeat_lost` | warn | 3 missed pongs (once per connection) |
| `ui.terminal_pty_lost` | warn | PTY exited with subscribers attached (or reattach exhausted) |
| `ui.terminal_protocol_error` | warn | Invalid mux client message |
| `ui.session_broadcast_failed` | warn | SessionBroadcaster fetch failed (transition-only emit) |

### Invariants preserved

- **No raw payloads or signatures in `data`** — webhook event data captures `slug`, `remoteAddr`, counts, and IDs only
- **No client IPs in `summary`** — `remoteAddr` lives in `data` (sanitizer doesn't redact IPs but `summary` is FTS-indexed)
- **At most one emit per WS connection per state change** — heartbeat_lost has an idempotency flag; ui.session_broadcast_failed only emits on the healthy→failing transition (re-arms after a successful poll), so a long outage produces one event, not 20/min
- **PTY exit distinguished from user disconnect** — `ui.terminal_pty_lost` only fires when subscribers are still attached when the PTY exits

### Security note

`api.webhook_unverified` is non-negotiable for security audit. The test asserts the failed signature is **not** present anywhere in the recorded event.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck` clean

- [x] Existing scm-webhooks and SessionBroadcaster tests still pass
- [x] Webhook events for 404 (unknown path) intentionally suppressed — that's a config issue, not external traffic

title: setup.sh / pnpm install fails with ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404 when user has a private npm registry configured globally
body:
## Summary

Source-install via `bash scripts/setup.sh` fails with `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404` for a public package (e.g. `@clack/core`) when the user has a private npm registry configured in their global `~/.npmrc` (AWS CodeArtifact, Verdaccio, JFrog Artifactory, GitHub Packages proxy, etc.).

The project does not pin a registry, so pnpm uses whatever registry the user's global config points at. If that registry doesn't proxy the public npmjs.org (or the proxy is misconfigured), every public dep we depend on returns 404 and install dies before a single package is downloaded.

## Reproduction

On a machine where the global registry is set to a private mirror that doesn't proxy npmjs.org:

```bash
# Example: user has previously run `aws codeartifact login --tool npm`
pnpm config get registry
# -> https://asbl-XXXXXXXXXXXX.d.codeartifact.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/npm/node/

git clone https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator
bash scripts/setup.sh
```

## Actual behavior

```
Installing dependencies...
Scope: all 29 workspace projects
Lockfile is up to date, resolution step is skipped
Packages: +668
+++++++...+++
ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404  GET https://asbl-XXXXXXXXXXXX.d.codeartifact.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/npm/node/@clack/core/-/core-0.4.1.tgz: Not Found - 404

An authorization header was used: Bearer eyJ2[hidden]
Progress: resolved 668, reused 0, downloaded 0, added 0
```

Setup aborts. The user has to know to either:
- `pnpm install --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`, or
- temporarily edit `~/.npmrc`, or
- add a project-local `.npmrc` override.

None of which is obvious from the error, especially for first-time users evaluating the project.

## Expected behavior

A fresh clone + `bash scripts/setup.sh` should install successfully regardless of what registry the user has configured globally for their other work.

## Root cause

Our project `.npmrc` only sets `access=public` and does not pin a registry:

```
access=public
```

pnpm therefore falls back to the user's `~/.npmrc` `registry=` setting. For users on corporate machines where IT/onboarding has pointed npm at a private mirror, that mirror often does not proxy public packages (or is scoped only to internal scopes), so every public dep 404s.

This is a real-world failure mode — multiple users in companies that use AWS CodeArtifact / Artifactory / Nexus will hit it the moment they try to install AO from source.

## Proposed fix

Pin the public npm registry in the project's `.npmrc`:

```
access=public
registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
```

pnpm merges project `.npmrc` over `~/.npmrc`, so this overrides the user's global mirror for this project only. It does not affect any other project they have open, and a user with a legitimate need to use a mirror (caching proxy, air-gap) can override per-install with `--registry=...` or by editing the project `.npmrc` locally.

For an OSS project consumed by the public, pinning to npmjs.org is the correct default — it's where our published deps actually live, and it eliminates an entire class of "works on my machine" install failures caused by the user's environment.

## Out of scope

- We are not adding logic to auto-detect or warn about private registries — the pinned registry already prevents the failure mode. Detection adds complexity for no extra coverage.
- `setup.sh` already runs `pnpm install` plain; the `.npmrc` fix covers it without needing a `--registry` flag in the script.

## Acceptance

- A user with a CodeArtifact / Artifactory / Verdaccio registry in their global `~/.npmrc` can run `bash scripts/setup.sh` from a fresh clone and install completes successfully.
- `pnpm install` (no flags) inside the repo uses `https://registry.npmjs.org/` regardless of the user's global config.

title: fix(setup): pin public npm registry in .npmrc
body:
## Summary

- Pins `registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` in the project `.npmrc` so a fresh source install works regardless of the user's global npm/pnpm registry config.
- Fixes `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404` from `scripts/setup.sh` when the user has a private mirror (AWS CodeArtifact, Artifactory, Verdaccio, GitHub Packages, etc.) configured in `~/.npmrc` that doesn't proxy public packages.
- Closes #1694.

## Why

pnpm merges project `.npmrc` over `~/.npmrc`, so without an explicit `registry=` line in our repo, install resolves through whatever mirror the user's machine is pointed at. On corporate setups where IT/onboarding has run something like `aws codeartifact login --tool npm`, public packages we depend on (`@clack/core`, etc.) 404 immediately and setup dies before downloading anything. Pinning npmjs.org in the project file scopes the override to this repo only — it does not affect any of the user's other projects, and anyone who genuinely wants to install through a mirror can override locally.

## Test plan

- [ ] On a machine with `~/.npmrc` set to a private mirror that does not proxy npmjs.org, `git clone` + `bash scripts/setup.sh` completes without `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404`.
- [ ] On a clean machine (no global registry override), `pnpm install` still works as before.

title: Scroll wheel sends arrow keys in web terminal (mouse mode silently fails on attach)
body:
## Symptom

In the web dashboard terminal (xterm.js + tmux), scroll wheel does not scroll. tmux 3.4+ shows the hint:

> Scroll wheel is sending arrow keys · use PgUp/PgDn to scroll

Scrolling worked before `ao` v0.5.0.

## Root cause

`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts:260,266` calls `tmux set-option -t =${tmuxSessionId} mouse on` (and `status off`) using the `=` exact-match prefix introduced in PR #1608. tmux's `=` prefix is supported by `has-session` and `attach-session` but **not** by `set-option`. The call exits with code 1 and prints `no such session: =name` to stderr, so mouse mode is never enabled.

Empirical verification on tmux 3.6a:

```
$ tmux set-option -t '=ao-test' mouse on
no such session: =ao-test          # exit 1

$ tmux set-option -t 'ao-test' mouse on
                                   # exit 0, mouse on
```

The failure is invisible: `spawn(...).on('error')` only fires for spawn-level failures (binary missing), not for non-zero exit codes. No stderr capture, no `.on('exit')` handler — nothing logs.

`attach-session -t =name` still works, so the terminal renders, which is why the bug presents as "scroll broken / status bar visible" rather than "terminal won't open."

## Why it survived review

- PR #1608 applied `=` consistently across `has-session`, `attach-session`, and `set-option` — the first two work, the third silently fails.
- PR #1683 worked around the status-bar symptom by setting `status off` at session creation in `packages/core/src/tmux.ts`. The mouse-mode call two lines above in `mux-websocket.ts` was not touched, so scrolling is still broken on `main`.

## Fix

Drop the `=` prefix for the two `set-option` spawns. Keep it for `has-session` / `attach-session` where it's needed for prefix-collision safety.

```ts
// mux-websocket.ts:260,266
spawn(this.TMUX, ["set-option", "-t", tmuxSessionId, "mouse", "on"]);
spawn(this.TMUX, ["set-option", "-t", tmuxSessionId, "status", "off"]);
```

Also add `.on('exit')` handlers to log non-zero exits so the next regression here isn't invisible.

## Regression test

Open a terminal via the mux protocol, then assert `tmux show-option -t name mouse` returns `mouse on`.

## Affected versions

`@aoagents/ao` 0.5.0+ (PR #1608 onward).

title: tmux session name collision across multiple AO configs sharing sessionPrefix
body:
## Bug

PR #1466 (commit `36fed87b`, v0.4.0) removed the `storageKey` hash prefix from tmux session names. The deprecation note in `paths.ts:215` claims *"session prefixes are globally unique — hash prefix is no longer needed."* This assumption is **wrong** for multi-config setups.

tmux session names are global per user. Two `agent-orchestrator.yaml` checkouts on the same machine that share a `sessionPrefix` (e.g. two clones of the same repo, or two unrelated projects with the same prefix) will collide:

1. `reserveNextSessionIdentity` (`session-manager.ts:803`) only scans its own `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/{projectId}/sessions/` dir for used numbers — no tmux occupancy check.
2. `reserveFixedOrchestratorIdentity` (`session-manager.ts:843`) reserves a fixed name like `{prefix}-orchestrator` — same problem.
3. Both paths call `tmux new-session -d -s {prefix}-{num}` (`runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:67`) which fails with "duplicate session" on the second checkout.

## Repro

```bash
git clone <repo> /tmp/checkout-a
git clone <repo> /tmp/checkout-b
cd /tmp/checkout-a && ao spawn   # works — creates int-1
cd /tmp/checkout-b && ao spawn   # FAILS — tmux: duplicate session name "int-1"
```

## Fix

Restore a short projectId-derived discriminator on tmux names while keeping `sessionId` bare:
- `tmuxName` = `{6-char-hash}-{prefix}-{num}` (e.g. `c13a01-int-1`)
- `sessionId` stays `{prefix}-{num}` (e.g. `int-1`)
- The old `generateTmuxName()` function is still in `paths.ts` — just needs de-deprecation and to be wired back into `session-manager.ts:827` and `session-manager.ts:856`
- Internal lookups key off `sessionId` / metadata, not tmux name, so this is a clean decoupling

Files to touch: `paths.ts`, `session-manager.ts`, test fixtures that pin tmux names.

## RCA

Full RCA report: PR #1691 (draft, investigation-only — no code changes).

## Severity

Medium — single-config users unaffected, multi-config power users hit a confusing spawn failure with no clear error message.

title: fix(cli): reload dashboard config after adding project from already-running menu
body:
## Summary

When `ao start` is run while a daemon is already running and the user selects **"Add <dir>"** from the prompt, the new project is written to the global config but the running dashboard never sees it — visiting `/projects/<new-id>` renders **Page not found**.

The dashboard caches `Services` (with the parsed config) in `globalThis._aoServices` (`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts`), so without an explicit reload it keeps serving the snapshot from when it started. The sibling flow `attachAndSpawnOrchestrator` already handles this via `daemon.notifyProjectChange()` (which POSTs `/api/projects/reload` → `invalidatePortfolioServicesCache`). The "add" menu branch just forgot to do it.

This patch calls `notifyProjectChange()` after `addProjectToConfig` and before `openUrl`, so the new project is reachable on first navigation.

## Repro

1. `ao start` from a registered project — daemon comes up.
2. From a different (unregistered) git repo, `ao start` again.
3. Choose **"Add <dir>"**.
4. CLI prints `✓ Added "<id>"` and opens the dashboard.
5. Navigate to `/projects/<id>` → **Page not found** (before fix).
