title: Green tmux status bar still visible in worker sessions — #1683 fixed unused code
body:
## Summary

The green tmux status bar at the bottom of agent worker terminals is still visible despite #1683 ("fix(core): disable tmux status bar at session creation"). #1683's change was made in `packages/core/src/tmux.ts::newSession()`, but **no code in the workspace imports or calls that function** — it's effectively dead code on the worker spawn path. Worker sessions are created by the `runtime-tmux` plugin, which was not modified.

Closes #1682 was premature; the bar reappears at session creation and only goes away once the web layer's WebSocket connects (and even that has a flash window).

## Reproduction

1. `pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli build` on current `main` (post-#1683 merge: commit `f617ae07`).
2. `ao spawn --prompt "hello world"` — session `ao-N` is created.
3. Open `http://localhost:3001/projects/<project>/sessions/ao-N` in the browser.
4. Observe: the green tmux status bar is visible at the bottom of the terminal.

## Evidence

### `tmux show-option` returns empty for the worker session

```console
$ tmux show-option -t ao-174 status
$
```

Empty output ⇒ no per-session override ⇒ falls through to the global default (`status on` on this machine).

### #1683's `core::newSession` has no callers

```console
$ grep -rn "newSession\\b\\|newTmuxSession\\b" --include='*.ts' packages/ \
    | grep -v '__tests__\\|dist\\|\\.test\\.' \
    | grep -v 'newSessionState\\|newSessionReason'
packages/core/src/index.ts:113:  newSession as newTmuxSession,
packages/core/src/tmux.ts:93:export async function newSession(opts: NewSessionOptions): Promise<void> {
```

Only the export site and the definition. No imports anywhere in `packages/`.

### Worker sessions are actually created by `runtime-tmux`, which has no `status off` call

`packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts`:

```ts
async create(config: RuntimeCreateConfig): Promise<RuntimeHandle> {
  // ...
  await tmux("new-session", "-d", "-s", sessionName, "-c", config.workspacePath, ...envArgs);
  // No `tmux set-option ... status off` anywhere here.
  // ...
}
```

### Defense-in-depth from web layer is racy

PR #1683's body acknowledged: _"The web layer (`mux-websocket.ts`) does run `set-option status off`, but only when a WebSocket client connects. Between session spawn and first web connection, the green bar is visible."_

Even after #1683, this remains the **only** path that actually disables the bar for worker sessions. So the original report (#1682) is not fixed in the spawn path — it's only papered over once a web client attaches, and only intermittently.

## Proposed fix

One-line addition in `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts` immediately after `tmux new-session`:

```ts
await tmux("new-session", "-d", "-s", sessionName, "-c", config.workspacePath, ...envArgs);
await tmux("set-option", "-t", sessionName, "status", "off"); // <-- add this
```

Plus a test in `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/__tests__/index.test.ts` that asserts `set-option ... status off` was called with the session name.

Optional: also keep the call inside `core/src/tmux.ts::newSession()` (where #1683 added it), or remove it as dead code. Removing keeps things lean; keeping it is harmless and could help any future caller of that helper.

## Related

- #1682 — original bug report (closed)
- #1683 — attempted fix (merged but on dead-code path)
- #1469 — earlier "enable tmux status bar in web terminal" (closed)
- #951 — terminal on the web ui has glitchy display (open)

## Environment

- ao version: 0.5.0 (with `core` dist swapped to local main build for testing)
- Branch tested against: `main` @ `40aeb78c` (which includes `f617ae07` from #1683)
- Platform: macOS (darwin 24.2.0), tmux from Homebrew

title: PTY slot exhaustion on macOS — reconnect churn burns non-recyclable PTY slots
body:
## Bug

After ~28 days of continuous AO dashboard usage on macOS, `kern.tty.ptmx_max=511` is hit and all new PTY allocations fail (no new terminals, tmux attach, etc.). The system has only ~27 live PTYs — macOS does not recycle slot numbers within a boot, so cumulative allocation count matters, not live count.

## Root Cause

`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` — TerminalManager.subscribe() (line 400).

### Primary: Reconnect churn (lines 400-411)
When a WebSocket drops (reload, sleep/wake, network blip), `ws.on("close")` fires all unsubscribers. Each calls `unsubscribe()` which immediately `pty.kill()`s when `subscribers.size === 0`. On reconnect, `subscribe()` -> `open()` -> fresh `ptySpawn()` at line 289 burns a new macOS PTY slot permanently.

One tab with 10 sessions x 3 reloads/day x 28 days = 840 slots burned -> exhausts the 511 limit well before 28 days.

### Secondary: Re-attach loop (lines 330-341)
When tmux crashes with subscribers present, `onExit` re-enters `this.open()` which spawns a new PTY. `MAX_REATTACH_ATTEMPTS = 3` means a flapping session burns 3 slots per crash cycle.

### Not a factor
`mouseProc`/`statusProc` (lines 260/266) use `child_process.spawn` with pipes, not PTYs. Correctly identified as red herring.

## Proposed Fix

### Grace period before PTY kill (primary fix)
In `unsubscribe()` return closure (line 400-411), when `subscribers.size === 0`:
1. Start a 30s `setTimeout` before calling `pty.kill()`
2. If a new subscriber arrives before the timer fires, cancel it and reuse the existing PTY
3. Only `kill()` + `terminals.delete()` after the grace period expires with zero subscribers

This eliminates nearly all reconnect/sleep/wake churn — the dominant source.

~15 lines changed, no API changes, backward compatible.

### Re-attach backoff (minor)
Add a short delay (e.g., 2s) between re-attach attempts so a flapping tmux session does not burn slots in a tight loop.

## Platform
macOS only — Linux recycles PTY slot numbers. macOS is a primary dev platform for AO users.

## Workaround
`sudo sysctl -w kern.tty.ptmx_max=999` (or reboot) restores headroom temporarily.

## Severity
High for any macOS user running AO continuously for weeks. Terminal becomes unusable system-wide (affects iTerm, tmux, python pty — not just AO).

title: fix(runtime-tmux): disable tmux status bar + dead code cleanup

#1683 added `set-option ... status off` to `core/src/tmux.ts::newSession()`. But that helper has **zero callers** anywhere in the workspace — worker sessions are spawned by the `runtime-tmux` plugin, which was never modified. So the green status bar was still visible at session creation; the only thing actually disabling it was the web layer's own `set-option` call on WebSocket connect (with a flash window before that).

Verification:

```console
$ grep -rn "newTmuxSession\|newSession\b" --include='*.ts' packages/ \
    | grep -v 'dist/\|__tests__\|newSessionState\|newSessionReason'
packages/core/src/tmux.ts:93:export async function newSession(opts: NewSessionOptions): Promise<void> {
packages/core/src/index.ts:113:  newSession as newTmuxSession,
```

Only the definition and the (unused) re-export. No actual callers.

## Changes

### Commit 1 — `fix(runtime-tmux): disable tmux status bar at session creation (closes #1709)`

In `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts`, immediately after `tmux new-session`:

```ts
await tmux("set-option", "-t", sessionName, "status", "off");
```

Plus a dedicated test (`disables the tmux status bar immediately after new-session`) and updates to existing tests' mock-call counts to account for the extra tmux call.

|------|--------|
| Two leaf nodes sharing a common parent | common parent |
| One target is ancestor of the other | ancestor node |
| Both targets under root via different subtrees | root |
| `val1 === val2` | that node |

| `null` root | `null` |

title: fix: scroll wheel broken in tmux terminal - PR #1608 regression
body:
## Bug

Scroll wheel doesn not work in the dashboard terminal after upgrading to v0.5.0. tmux shows "Scroll wheel is sending arrow keys · use PgUp/PgDn to scroll". The tmux status bar is also no longer hidden.

## Root Cause

PR #1608 added the `=` exact-match prefix to **all** tmux commands in `mux-websocket.ts`, including `set-option`:

```ts
const exactTmuxTarget = `=${tmuxSessionId}`;

// These SILENTLY FAIL in tmux 3.4
spawn(this.TMUX, ["set-option", "-t", exactTmuxTarget, "mouse", "on"]);
spawn(this.TMUX, ["set-option", "-t", exactTmuxTarget, "status", "off"]);

// This works fine - = prefix IS supported for attach-session
ptySpawn(this.TMUX, ["attach-session", "-t", exactTmuxTarget], ...);
```

In tmux 3.4, the `=` prefix for exact session matching only works with `has-session` and `attach-session`. `set-option` silently ignores it, so:
1. `mouse on` never gets set -> scroll wheel sends arrow keys instead of mouse events
2. `status off` never gets set -> tmux status bar remains visible

## File

`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` lines ~258-267

## Fix

Use bare `tmuxSessionId` (no `=` prefix) for the two `set-option` calls, keep `=` prefix only for `attach-session`.

## Regression

Caused by PR #1608 (commit d0fde88). Scrolling and status bar hiding worked correctly in v0.4.0.

title: fix(web): drop = prefix from set-option in mux-websocket (closes #1714)
body:
## Summary

Fixes scroll-wheel regression in the dashboard tmux terminal (#1714).

In tmux 3.4 the `=` exact-match prefix is only honoured by `has-session` and `attach-session`. For `set-option`, the prefix is silently ignored — so the `mouse on` and `status off` calls in `mux-websocket.ts` never applied. Result: scroll wheel sent arrow keys instead of mouse events ("Scroll wheel is sending arrow keys · use PgUp/PgDn to scroll"), and the tmux status bar remained visible.

The fix is surgical: use the bare `tmuxSessionId` for the two `set-option` calls; keep `=${tmuxSessionId}` for `attach-session` where it is correct.

> Note: #1711 already fixed the green-bar symptom at the runtime-tmux layer (session creation). This PR fixes the underlying tmux-3.4 `=` prefix bug in the web layer, which restores `mouse on` (scroll wheel) and gives belt-and-suspenders coverage for `status off`.

## Causal chain

- #1608 introduced the `=` prefix on all tmux commands in `mux-websocket.ts` — silent failure on `set-option` in tmux 3.4
- #1682 / #1683 / #1711 chased the green status bar through `runtime-tmux` without spotting the web-layer regression
- #1714 identifies the actual root cause; this PR is the surgical fix for the mouse/scroll regression

title: PTY slot exhaustion on macOS during extended dashboard uptime
body:
## Bug

After ~28 days of continuous AO dashboard usage on macOS, the system hits `kern.tty.ptmx_max=511` and refuses all new PTY allocations — new terminal tabs, `tmux attach`, `pty.openpty()` all fail. Only ~27 PTYs were actively in use, but 511 device nodes existed.

**Root cause:** macOS PTY allocator never recycles slot numbers within a boot. Once `/dev/ttysNNN` has been used, that slot is burned for the lifetime of the boot, regardless of whether the PTY was properly closed.

## Two churn sources in `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts`

### 1. Reconnect-driven re-allocation (primary — line 404-409)

When the last WebSocket subscriber disconnects (tab reload, sleep/wake, network blip), `TerminalManager.subscribe()` unsubscribe callback immediately calls `pty.kill()` and deletes the terminal entry. Next reconnect allocates a fresh PTY with a new slot number — the old slot is gone forever on macOS.

With 30 sessions × dozens of reconnect cycles over 28 days, this accounts for hundreds of unique slot allocations.

### 2. Recursive re-attach loop (secondary — lines 330-341)

When a tmux session crashes and the PTY exits, `onExit` fires up to `MAX_REATTACH_ATTEMPTS=3` re-attach attempts via `this.open()`, each allocating a new PTY. A flapping session burns multiple slots per crash cycle.

**Note:** The runaway re-attach loop (counter never engaging due to immediate reset) was fixed in #1640. This issue tracks the remaining reconnect-churn source.

## Proposed fix

- **Grace period before kill (~30s):** When the last subscriber unsubscribes, defer `pty.kill()` by ~30 seconds. If a new subscriber arrives in that window, reuse the existing PTY. This eliminates dashboard-reload and sleep/wake churn — the dominant contributor.

Together with the #1640 fix, this should reduce slot consumption by ~5x, pushing time-to-exhaustion from ~28 days to several months.

## Workaround

```
sudo sysctl -w kern.tty.ptmx_max=999  # or reboot
```

## Environment
- macOS (any version — kernel behavior)
- AO dashboard running continuously
- Observed after ~28 days uptime with ~30 sessions

Refs: #1639, #1640

title: fix(web): defer idle PTY kill to curb macOS ptmx slot exhaustion (#1718)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1718.

When the last WebSocket subscriber disconnects from a terminal, `TerminalManager` used to call `pty.kill()` and drop the entry inline. Every reconnect — tab reload, sleep/wake, network blip — then allocated a fresh PTY with a new ptmx slot number.

**macOS never recycles ptmx slot numbers within a boot**, so this churn slowly burned through `kern.tty.ptmx_max=511`. A dashboard with ~30 sessions hit the cap after ~28 days of uptime; afterwards every new PTY allocation on the host (terminal tabs, tmux attach, ao spawn) failed until reboot.

This PR addresses the dominant churn source called out in the issue: **reconnect-driven re-allocation**. It is orthogonal to and stacks on top of #1640 (re-attach loop bound).

## What changed

- `ManagedTerminal` now tracks an `idleGraceTimer`.
- On last unsubscribe, the kill is deferred by `PTY_IDLE_GRACE_MS = 30_000` instead of running inline. The timer's callback re-checks `subscribers.size` so a reconnect that lands inside the window transparently reuses the existing PTY and its ring buffer.
- On new subscribe, any pending grace timer is cleared.
- When the grace timer actually fires the kill, it also clears the `resetTimer` introduced in #1640 so its closure doesn't keep the evicted terminal reachable.
- The grace timer is `.unref()`d so it doesn't hold the event loop alive on shutdown.
- `TerminalManager` is now exported so it can be unit-tested.

Together with #1640, this should push slot exhaustion from ~28 days out to several months under the same load.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- mux-websocket` — 17/17 pass (5 new + 3 #1714 regression + 9 SessionBroadcaster)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- direct-terminal-ws` — 21/21 pass (includes #1639/#1640 runaway + recovery integration tests)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (warnings are pre-existing in unrelated files)
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean

### New unit tests

- Kill is deferred on last unsub
- Kill fires after 30s with no reconnect
- Reconnect within grace preserves PTY (no new spawn, no kill)
- Kill fires only when truly the last subscriber leaves (multi-subscriber semantics)
- Ring buffer survives an unsub/resub cycle within grace

### Integration test touch-up

`direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts` "receives terminal data after open" was relying on the implicit pre-#1718 behavior that every WS open triggered a fresh tmux attach (which in turn produced fresh init data). With the new grace path the previous test's PTY is reused and no fresh init data flows. Switched the test to a unique terminal id so it explicitly exercises the fresh-attach path it was meant to test. Other tests in that file drive output via stdin and were not affected.

## Notes for reviewer

- The 30s window is tunable. It needs to be long enough to absorb a tab reload (<1s) and brief sleep/wake (typically <10s), but short enough that abandoned sessions don't sit on PTY slots forever. 30s mirrors the issue's proposed value.
- `idleGraceTimer.unref()` avoids holding the event loop alive at process shutdown — without it, an `ao stop` while sessions are in grace could delay exit by up to 30s.

title: fix(core): read legacy key=value metadata in .json session files
body: ## Issue `ao start` can fail while a valid canonical orchestrator session is already alive and recoverable. Observed failure: In the reported case, tmux still had a live `ao-orchestrator` session and the metadata file existed at: ```text ~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator_48321dec7a/sessions/ao-orchestrator.json ``` But the file was not JSON. It contained legacy `key=value` metadata under a `.json` filename: ```text codexThreadId=019df929-1773-7720-b07d-08e3cb9851fb codexModel=gpt-5.4 status=working runtimeHandle={"id":"ao-orchestrator","runtimeName":"tmux","data":{"createdAt":1778013362949,"workspacePath":"/Users/yyovil/Projects/agent-orchestrator"}} tmuxName=ao-orchestrator ``` The current JSON metadata reader treats that file as missing, while the reservation path treats the same file as existing. That makes the error message self-contradictory: it tells the user to use `ensureOrchestrator()`, but `ensureOrchestrator()` already failed to read the existing session. This is related to #1661, but distinct. #1661 covers an empty stale reservation file. This bug covers a non-empty legacy-format metadata file that contains useful restore state and should not be deleted as if it were empty junk. ## Affected Package - Package path: `packages/core` - npm package: `@aoagents/ao-core` - Surface area: metadata reading, canonical orchestrator startup, `ao start` - Shared code touched: `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`, likely tests under `packages/core/src/__tests__/metadata.test.ts` and/or `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts` ## Reproduction 1. Create or retain a canonical orchestrator metadata file named like `sessions/ao-orchestrator.json`. 2. Make its contents legacy `key=value` metadata rather than JSON, for example with `role=orchestrator`, `status=working`, `runtimeHandle={...}`, and `tmuxName=ao-orchestrator`. 3. Ensure the matching tmux session exists, or simply run the metadata-level check below. 4. Run `ao start` for that project. ## Current Result `ao start` cannot reuse/restore the session. Internally, `readMetadata()` and `readMetadataRaw()` return `null`, but `reserveSessionId()` returns `false` because the file exists. Confirmed with the installed metadata module against the live file: ```json { "readMetadata": null, "readMetadataRaw": null, "reserveSessionId": false } ``` ## Expected Result AO should parse legacy `key=value` content inside `.json` session files, recover the existing canonical orchestrator metadata, and let `ensureOrchestrator()` reuse or restore the session. A later metadata update can rewrite the file in the current JSON format. The important part is that startup should not strand a live session because the filename and content format disagree. ## Evidence Relevant code path: - `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`: `parseMetadataContent()` currently only attempts `JSON.parse()` and returns `null` on non-JSON content. - `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`: `readMetadata()` / `readMetadataRaw()` therefore treat legacy `key=value` content as missing. - `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`: `reserveSessionId()` uses `O_EXCL` on the same `.json` path and returns `false` when the file exists. - `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`: `ensureOrchestratorInternal()` calls `get(sessionId)`, sees no existing session, then falls through to `spawnOrchestrator()`, which hits the reservation failure. > [!NOTE] > The following is the fix spec for AI agents. ## Steps 1. Open `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` and trace the read path for `readMetadata()`, `readMetadataRaw()`, `mutateMetadata()`, and `reserveSessionId()`. 2. Fix the root cause with the smallest change: when metadata content is not JSON, parse legacy `key=value` content using the existing `parseKeyValueContent()` helper instead of returning `null` unconditionally. 3. Preserve true corrupt JSON behavior. If content appears to start as JSON but fails to parse, keep treating it as corrupt/missing or preserve current corrupt-file handling. 4. Add focused tests proving a `.json` file with `key=value` metadata is readable through both `readMetadata()` and `readMetadataRaw()`. 5. Add or update a session-manager regression test proving `ensureOrchestrator()` reuses/restores a canonical orchestrator represented by legacy `key=value` content in `sessions/.json`. 6. Commit only `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` and closely related tests. No unrelated cleanup. ## Validation - Package-level test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- metadata` - Session-manager regression: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- session-manager/spawn` - Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` ## Constraints - Keep the scope inside `packages/core` unless a caller genuinely needs adjustment. - Do not solve this by deleting non-empty legacy metadata files. Those files can contain useful restore state like `codexThreadId`, `runtimeHandle`, and `tmuxName`. - Preserve the current JSON metadata format for new writes. - Preserve existing public APIs and config shapes. - Treat #1661 as adjacent prior art, not the complete fix for this case. ## Acceptance - `readMetadataRaw(sessionsDir, "ao-orchestrator")` returns legacy fields from a `key=value` `ao-orchestrator.json` file. - `readMetadata(sessionsDir, "ao-orchestrator")` returns a non-null metadata object with `role`, `tmuxName`, `runtimeHandle`, and derived/restored status when present. - `ensureOrchestrator({ projectId })` does not call `spawnOrchestrator()` for an existing canonical orchestrator represented by a legacy-format `.json` metadata file. - `ao start` prints that it is using/restoring the existing orchestrator instead of failing with `Orchestrator session "ao-orchestrator" already exists`.

body:
## Summary

After a worker session's PR is merged and the session is restored, the lifecycle manager can incorrectly associate the restored session with **an unrelated open PR from another contributor's fork**, then start injecting that PR's CI failures and review comments into the session's terminal.

Concrete repro on this machine: session `ao-179` was the release worker for #1723. After #1723 merged, `ao-179` was killed and then restored. On restore, its metadata shows `branch: "main"` and `pr.number: 643` — but #643 is an unrelated PR by @MayurVirkar from his fork's `main` branch. Lifecycle has been polling #643's CI/review state and pushing those events into ao-179's terminal as if ao-179 were responsible for fixing it.

## Root cause

`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts::detectPR` queries:

```ts
gh([
  "pr", "list",
  "--repo", project.repo,
  "--head", session.branch,
  "--json", "number,url,title,headRefName,baseRefName,isDraft",
  ...
])
```

The `--head <branch>` filter matches **any** PR with that head ref name, including PRs from forks. When `session.branch === project.defaultBranch` (typically `main`), this is almost guaranteed to match unrelated fork PRs, because most contributors PR from their own `main` branch.

Confirming reproduction on this repo right now:

```console
$ gh pr list --repo ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator --head main --state open --json number,headRefName,headRepositoryOwner
[
  { "number": 643, "headRefName": "main", "headRepositoryOwner": { "login": "MayurVirkar" } },
  { "number": 415, "headRefName": "main", "headRepositoryOwner": { "login": "zvictor"     } }
]
```

Two fork PRs match `--head main`. detectPR returns the first one it gets and lifecycle treats that as the session's PR.

## Why session.branch became `"main"`

Secondary observation. The session was originally on `chore/release-0.6.0`. After PR #1723 merged:
- The branch was deleted upstream (standard "delete branch on merge" behavior).
- Some part of AO updated/persisted `session.branch` to `"main"` (visible in the on-disk metadata at `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<proj>/sessions/<id>.json`).
- On restore, the worktree was checked out to `main` (matching the now-stored branch).

The exact code path that promoted `branch` to `"main"` is not yet pinpointed — could be auto-cleanup-on-merge, restore, or workspace.restore — but the upstream effect is what triggers the detectPR mismatch.

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a worker session: `ao spawn --prompt "..."`. The worker creates a feature branch + PR.
2. Worker pushes commits, opens PR.
3. Merge the PR with branch deletion enabled.
4. Kill the session (`ao session kill <id>` or `ao stop`).
5. Restore the session (`ao session restore <id>` or via `ao start` restore prompt).
6. Observe: session metadata now shows `branch: "main"`, lifecycle picks an unrelated fork PR via detectPR, and CI/review reactions for that fork PR start firing into the restored session.

## Suggested fixes (all defense in depth)

### A. Harden detectPR to not match unrelated PRs

In `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts::detectPR`:

1. **Refuse to match when `session.branch === project.defaultBranch`** — a worker session should never be associated with the default branch as its head. Return null.
2. **Filter results to same-repo PRs** — discard any returned PR whose `headRepositoryOwner.login` differs from `project.repo`'s owner. (`gh pr list` already returns this field.) Fork PRs should never be auto-associated with a session.
3. **Optional**: also discard PRs where `baseRefName === session.branch` (means the PR is targeting the same branch, which is nonsensical for a session matching by head).

### B. Make session-branch promotion to `main` explicit

After a session's PR merges with branch deletion, the session is effectively terminal. Either:
- Mark it as `done` / cleanup-eligible (don't keep restoring as if it has work).
- Or, if restore is desired, refuse to silently rewrite `session.branch` to the default branch — surface that the original branch is gone and let the caller decide.

### C. detectPR caching invariant

The PR-detection cache is positive-only (per the comment in `detectPR`). When a session's PR transitions from open → merged, the cache for that session-branch should be invalidated, not left as the now-stale "PR found" result. (This is a smaller follow-up and may be unrelated to the present bug, but worth verifying.)

## Impact

- User-visible: a restored release-worker session starts receiving CI failure pings and review-comment reactions for someone else's fork PR. This is confusing at best and could prompt the agent to make destructive changes "fixing" CI for a PR it didn't create.
- Trust: any restored worker on the default branch is at risk — not specific to release workers.

## Environment

- AO version: 0.5.0 (with local main builds swapped into the global install for testing — fix is reproducible regardless).
- Triggered after merging PR #1723 and restoring `ao-179`.

## Related sessions / PRs

- `ao-179` — release worker, currently exhibiting the bug.
- #1723 — release PR that merged.
- #643, #415 — the open fork PRs whose `headRefName === "main"` and which detectPR can match.

title: chore: add bug-triage skill for agent-driven issue triage
body:
## Summary

Adds a `skills/bug-triage/` directory with the bug triage skill I've been using internally, adapted for any agent working on this repo.

### What's included

**`skills/bug-triage/SKILL.md`** — Full triage workflow:
1. Pre-flight (pull latest main, identify target repo)
2. Gather report context (chat, issues, live observation)
3. Root cause analysis with `git log -S` archaeology
4. Upstream dependency research
5. Duplicate search → comment on existing or file new issue
6. Screenshot upload (never use placeholders)
7. Label and priority assignment (only approved labels)
8. Push fix PRs via GitHub API (`scripts/push_fix_to_github.py`)
9. NPM package regression diffing
10. Remote code inspection without local clone

**`skills/bug-triage/scripts/push_fix_to_github.py`** — Push a single-file fix and create a PR entirely via GitHub API. No local checkout needed. Uses `OLD_STRING`/`NEW_STRING` env vars for the replacement.

**`AGENTS.md`** — Added a "Skills" section referencing the bug-triage skill so any agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) discovers it automatically.

### Why

Currently the bug triage workflow lives only in my internal skill store. Any other agent working on this repo has no idea how to triage bugs properly — no dedup, no root cause depth, no consistent issue formatting, no fix PR workflow.

Checking it into the repo means:
- Every agent gets the same triage playbook
- The skill evolves with the codebase (PR-based updates)
- No external dependency on a specific agent's skill store

### Changes from internal version

- Removed Hermes-specific tool references (`ao_sessions`, `ao_observability`, etc.) → replaced with `gh` CLI equivalents
- Removed Discord-specific fetch script (kept the generic push script)
- Removed AO server filesystem specifics (root-owned files, sudo pnpm)
- Made all paths relative to the repo checkout
- Removed internal memory/session references

### Test plan

- [ ] Verify AGENTS.md references the skill correctly
- [ ] An agent reading AGENTS.md can discover and follow the skill workflow

title: fix(lifecycle): preserve terminal PR association across restore + harden detectPR (closes #1724)
body:
## Summary

Three layered fixes for #1724, where a restored worker session whose PR had merged got silently re-associated with an unrelated fork PR (in the reported repro: `ao-179` (release worker for #1723) ended up polling CI/reviews for fork PR #643 after restore).

Per-commit:

1. **`fix(scm-github): drop fork PRs and default-branch sessions from detectPR`** — `detectPR` now (a) returns `null` when `session.branch === project.defaultBranch`, and (b) requests `headRepositoryOwner` from `gh pr list` and discards PRs whose head owner differs from the repo owner. The `gh pr list --head <branch>` filter previously matched any PR with that head ref name across all forks.
2. **`fix(lifecycle): skip detectPR for sessions whose PR is already merged`** — lifecycle-manager short-circuits `scm.detectPR` when `session.lifecycle.pr.state === "merged"`. Branch drift between poll cycles (agent runs `git checkout main`, branch metadata hook fires, lifecycle observes branch=main) was the trigger that let detectPR run against the default branch and pick up unrelated PRs. Closed (unmerged) PRs intentionally still go through detectPR so the existing follow-up-PR rediscovery flow is preserved.
3. **`fix(session-manager): refuse to restore sessions with merged/closed PRs`** — restore now throws `SessionNotRestorableError` up-front when the session's PR is in a terminal state. Previously restore silently cleared `lifecycle.pr.*` and reset `session.state` to `working`, which combined with branch drift caused the bug. The dead clear-on-restore block has been removed.

## Investigation notes

- Repro metadata at `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator/sessions/ao-179.json` showed: `branch: "main"`, `lifecycle.pr.number: 643`, `lifecycle.pr.state: "open"`, `agentReportedPrUrl: ".../pull/1723"`.
- `lifecycle-manager.ts:657-662` previously guarded detectPR by `session.pr` truthiness; once `repairSessionMetadataOnRead` (session-manager.ts:623-665) cleared `pr` for duplicate-PR-attached sessions, detectPR ran unguarded against `session.branch="main"` and matched fork PRs (`gh pr list --head main` returns #643 by MayurVirkar and #415 by zvictor).
- `scm-github/src/index.ts::detectPR` requested `--head <branch>` without owner filtering — the entry point for the fork-match.
- The exact code path that promoted `branch` from `chore/release-0.6.0` → `"main"` is the agent-side metadata hook (`agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:188-200`) firing on a `git checkout main` invocation post-merge. It is not pinpointed in this PR because the three fixes here neutralize the impact regardless of how the branch drifted.

## Invariants preserved

- **scm-github:** `detectPR` semantics unchanged for non-default branches with same-repo PRs (existing tests still green).
- **lifecycle:** sessions with `pr.state` in `{"open", "none"}` continue to be auto-detected; the existing `closed`-PR + branch-switch follow-up-detection test still passes; orchestrator/auto-detect-off opt-outs continue to take precedence.
- **session-manager:** `isRestorable` semantics unchanged for terminated/done/runtime-lost; only the PR-terminal sub-case now refuses with an explicit reason. Workers with `pr.state` of `"open"`/`"none"` still restore normally.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1102 unit tests pass; 6 unrelated FTS5 failures stem from a missing `better-sqlite3` native binding in the local sandbox (pre-existing, not caused by this PR)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github test` — 172 tests pass
- [x] New regression tests:
  - `scm-github`: same-repo PR preferred when both fork and same-repo PRs match; fork-only matches return `null`; `branch === defaultBranch` short-circuits without calling `gh`
  - `lifecycle-manager`: merged-PR session does not call `detectPR`
  - `session-manager`: restoring a session with `status: "merged"` rejects with `/is merged/`
- [ ] CI

Closes #1724.

title: fix(core): sm.list() no longer writes terminated state to disk
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1735

- **`sm.list()` no longer persists `terminated` to disk** — it now writes `detecting` state with `runtime_lost` reason, so the lifecycle manager's `resolveProbeDecision` pipeline remains the single authority on terminal decisions. A single `isAlive()` failure no longer permanently kills a session.
- **`/api/sessions/patches` now calls `listCached()` instead of `list()`** — the dashboard's 3s poll was the most dangerous caller, probing runtimes ~10x more often than the lifecycle manager. The cache TTL (35s) aligns with the lifecycle manager's 30s poll cycle.
- Updated CLAUDE.md invariants to reflect the new behavior.

## What was happening

`sm.list()` detected a dead runtime via `isAlive()` and immediately persisted `session.state = "terminated"` with `reason = "runtime_lost"` to disk. This bypassed the lifecycle manager's carefully designed probe pipeline which evaluates three independent signals (runtime, process, activity) and routes 4/5 outcomes to `detecting` (retry). Only unanimous agreement across all signals produces a terminal decision.

The dashboard's `/api/sessions/patches` endpoint polled every 3s calling `sm.list()` directly — so a single transient `isAlive()` failure would permanently kill the session before the lifecycle manager's 30s poll could run.

## Test plan

- [x] Updated existing tests that expected `killed` status to expect `detecting`
- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm lint` passes (0 errors, pre-existing warnings only)
- [x] `pnpm test` passes (all core + cli tests green; 3 pre-existing web test failures unrelated)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(core): read legacy key=value metadata in .json session files
body:
## Problem

`ao start` fails when a valid canonical orchestrator session is alive but its `.json` metadata file contains legacy `key=value` format instead of JSON. `parseMetadataContent()` in `metadata.ts` only attempts `JSON.parse()` and returns `null` on non-JSON content, while `reserveSessionId()` sees the file as existing — creating a self-contradictory state that blocks recovery.

Fixes #1720

## Fix

Modified `parseMetadataContent()` to fall back to `parseKeyValueContent()` (an existing helper used elsewhere in the codebase for legacy formats) when:
1. `JSON.parse()` fails, AND
2. The content does NOT start with `{` or `[` (preserving corrupt-JSON behavior)

This is the smallest change that resolves the issue — only `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` is modified (plus tests).

## Key design choices

- **JSON-first**: valid JSON is always preferred; the fallback only triggers on parse failure
- **Corrupt JSON preserved**: content starting with `{` or `[` that fails to parse is still treated as corrupt (not silently parsed as key=value)
- **Empty content returns null**: an empty file still returns `null` (matches existing `reserveSessionId` sentinel)
- **No destructive behavior**: legacy metadata files are read, not deleted — a subsequent `writeMetadata`/`updateMetadata` call will rewrite in JSON format

## Tests added

4 new tests in `packages/core/src/__tests__/metadata.test.ts`:
- `readMetadata` parses key=value content from a `.json` file (with `runtimeHandle`, `tmuxName`, `status`)
- `readMetadataRaw` parses key=value content from a `.json` file
- Returns `null` for empty key=value file
- Returns `null` for corrupt JSON that starts with `{`

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- metadata` — 47/47 passed
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean

title: Preserve worktrees on session kill — clean build artifacts instead of removing (follow-up to #1650)
body:
## Summary

Change session-kill behavior to **preserve the git worktree on disk** and just clean its build artifacts (`git clean -fdx`) instead of running `git worktree remove`. This eliminates a class of stale-branch bugs (including #1650) and avoids the cost of re-creating worktrees + reinstalling dependencies whenever a session is restored.

## Background

`workspace-worktree`'s `destroy()` currently runs `git worktree remove --force <path>` ([src/index.ts:268](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts#L268)). The worktree directory is wiped, but the local branch ref `session/<prefix>-N` is intentionally left behind (see comment at lines 270-274).

Combined with `reserveNextSessionIdentity()` in [`session-manager.ts:803`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L803) — which only counts *currently registered* sessions when picking the next counter — the counter recycles into a number that still has a stale local branch ref. The next spawn collides on the branch name, and the plugin's "branch already exists" fallback silently uses the stale SHA. That is the #1650 bug.

The original motivation for destroying worktrees was disk usage — `node_modules` is heavy. `git clean -fdx` (or `-fdX` for ignored-only) gets that cost back without the side effects.

## Proposed approach

On session kill:
1. **Do not** call `git worktree remove`.
2. Run a configurable cleanup command (default `git clean -fdx`) inside the worktree to nuke `node_modules`, `.next`, `dist`, `target`, `__pycache__`, etc.
3. Mark the session as `archived` — a new lifecycle reason distinct from `terminated`.
4. Leave the worktree registered with git, the branch checked out, and session metadata intact.

On revive (or restore):
- The worktree already exists → skip the worktree-create path entirely.
- Re-run `postCreate` hooks (re-symlink `node_modules`, run `pnpm install`, etc.) — this becomes the "warm restore" path.

Disk hygiene:
- New CLI `ao prune` (and/or background job) deletes archives older than `archiveRetentionDays`.
- `archiveMaxCount`: oldest archives get pruned first when count exceeds the limit.
- Both configurable per-project in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`.

## Why this also addresses #1650's bug class

#1650 requires three conditions to align:
1. Local branch ref `session/<prefix>-N` exists at a stale SHA.
2. Session counter recycles to N.
3. `workspace.create()` falls into the "branch already exists" path.

With archives, killed sessions stay registered → their numbers stay in `usedNumbers` → counter never recycles → no name collision → bug doesn't fire.

The SHA-comparison guard from #1652 is still useful as defense-in-depth for adjacent paths that can produce stale refs (manual worktree deletion, multi-machine repo sharing, `findManagedWorkspace` adoption). Keep it.

## Implementation surface

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts` | Replace `destroy()` body with cleanup-only; add `archive()`/`revive()` hooks |
| `packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts` | New `archived` reason; map in `deriveLegacyStatus` |
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | Counter logic unchanged (archived stays in `usedNumbers`); filter archived in default `list()` |
| `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` + kanban | Archived column or "show archived" toggle |
| CLI | `ao session archive <id>`, `ao session revive <id>`, `ao prune` |
| Config schema | `archiveRetentionDays`, `archiveMaxCount`, `archiveCleanupCommand` |

## Open questions / edge cases

- **Default cleanup command**: `git clean -fdx` removes ALL untracked files (including any uncommitted scratch work). Should the default be `-fdX` (ignored-only, safer) and `-fdx` opt-in? Or run a configurable command (e.g., `pnpm clean` if the repo has one)?
- **Worktree adoption**: `findManagedWorkspace` already supports the warm-restore semantics — fits cleanly into this design.
- **Multi-agent visibility**: archived sessions must NOT show up in default `list()`, dashboard kanban, session pickers, or restart prompts.
- **Branch ref hygiene**: do we ever delete the branch ref? Possibly when archive is purged from disk.

## Sequencing

**#1652 (the SHA-comparison guard) lands first** as the immediate fix for #1650 — it's small, tested, and unblocks 0.3.0 users today. This redesign is a follow-up that will subsume the bug class entirely while also delivering a faster restore path.

## Discussion context

Discussed in daily sync on 2026-05-07. The proposal to swap `git worktree remove` for `git clean -fdx` came from that conversation, motivated by the original concern that `node_modules` was the only reason worktrees were being destroyed in the first place. Capturing here for follow-up.

---

Refs: #1650, #1652

title: Bug/docs: Slack notifier config naming and env placeholder behavior are inconsistent
body:
## Summary

Slack notifier setup is confusing because the docs/examples and implementation appear inconsistent around three related points:

1. Whether `.env.local` or similar env files are loaded by AO.
2. Whether `${VAR}`-style placeholders in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` are substituted.
3. Whether the Slack notifier config key should be `webhook` or `webhookUrl`.

In practice, a placeholder value in YAML appears to be passed through literally and then rejected by URL validation.

## Observed behavior

A Slack notifier config using an env-style placeholder does not appear to resolve the variable. The literal placeholder is passed into the Slack notifier and URL validation fails because the value does not start with `http://` or `https://`.

There is also confusion around config naming: some guidance/examples refer to a Slack webhook value, while the implementation reads `webhookUrl`.

## Expected behavior

The repo should be consistent and explicit about one of these behaviors:

- AO supports env-file loading and YAML env substitution; or
- AO does not support env-file loading or YAML env substitution, and docs/examples should not imply that it does.

The Slack notifier config key should also be documented consistently as the key the plugin actually consumes.

## Source-level findings

From inspecting the current source:

- The config loader reads YAML and validates it, but I did not find a dotenv/env-file loading step in the runtime config path.
- I did not find a YAML interpolation pass that replaces `${VAR}` placeholders with `process.env` values.
- The Slack notifier implementation reads `config?.webhookUrl`.
- The Slack notifier validates that the configured URL begins with `http://` or `https://`.

## Why this matters

This creates a sharp onboarding failure for Slack setup. A user can reasonably follow env-style examples, put the value in a local env file or exported env var, and still get an invalid URL error because the placeholder was never expanded.

It also creates a security/documentation ambiguity: users may not know whether secrets belong in YAML, shell env, `.env.local`, or some generated config file.

## Suggested fixes

Either:

### Option A: Support env interpolation intentionally

- Document supported env-file names and loading order.
- Substitute `${VAR}` placeholders before validation.
- Provide a clear missing-variable error.
- Add tests for Slack config env substitution.

Or:

### Option B: Make non-support explicit

- Remove examples that imply `${VAR}` substitution in YAML.
- State that `.env.local` is not loaded by AO unless that support is intentionally added.
- Standardize all Slack examples on `webhookUrl`.
- Add a clearer validation error when a config value looks like an unresolved env placeholder.

## Acceptance criteria

- Slack docs, setup docs, examples, and schema guidance agree on `webhookUrl` vs `webhook`.
- Docs explicitly say whether `.env.local` is read.
- Docs explicitly say whether `${VAR}` placeholders in YAML are substituted.
- Tests cover the chosen behavior.
- Error messages are actionable when users provide an unresolved env placeholder.

title: Restore unconditionally falls back to `git worktree add -b`, fails when local branch already exists
fix(workspace-worktree): restore re-attaches existing branch instead of recreating with -b
body:
Closes #1741

## Summary

Restoring a session whose worktree directory was cleaned up but whose branch still existed locally would 422 with:

```
fatal: a branch named feat/<X> already exists
```

`workspace.restore()`'s catch handler unconditionally fell through to `git worktree add -b`, even though `destroy()` deliberately preserves session branches so the user's commits aren't lost.

## Fix

When the local branch already exists, `restore()` now:

1. Clears any stale worktree registration at the target path (`worktree remove --force`, then `worktree prune`, both best-effort).
2. Retries `git worktree add <path> <branch>` — **no `-b`, no `-B`**.

The existing `-b` fallback is preserved verbatim for the genuine "branch missing locally, only origin ref exists" case.

`-B` is intentionally **not** used here. It would force-reset the branch to the base ref and silently discard the session's commits — the opposite of restore's intent. (This is the key difference from #1650, where `-B` is correct because `create()` is spawning a fresh session.)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree test` — **63 tests pass** (was 57; +6 new, 2 modified)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-integration-tests test workspace-worktree` — **12 tests pass** (was 10; +2 new)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only, none in changed files)
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean

### New unit coverage (`packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/__tests__/index.test.ts`)

- `re-attaches existing local branch instead of recreating with -b` — main repro
- `tolerates failure of best-effort cleanup before retry`
- `propagates retry error when both attempts fail with existing branch`
- `never force-resets an existing branch (preserves session commits)`
- `checks branch existence with rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`
- `happy path: restore re-attaches branch when first worktree add already succeeds`

### New integration coverage (`packages/integration-tests/src/workspace-worktree.integration.test.ts`)

- `restore re-attaches existing session branch and preserves its commits` — happy path on real git
- `restore recovers when a stale worktree registration conflicts with the path` — direct repro of #1741 on real git: dirty teardown leaves a registered worktree at a now-missing path; restore must recover **and** the session's commit must survive

## Why it appeared to "work yesterday"

Restore's first call is only exercised when the worktree dir is missing — `session-manager.ts` short-circuits via `workspace.exists()` when the dir is still present. The buggy `-b` fallback dates to Feb 19, 2026 (per `git blame`); recent registry-touching changes (#1643, #1650) made the failure surface more reachable. Full RCA in [issue #1741](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1741#issuecomment-4408519393).

## Diff size

The visible diff in `index.ts` (62 insertions / 21 deletions) is dominated by re-indentation — wrapping the existing `-b` logic in an `else` branch. The actual new logic is ~13 lines: one `refExists` check + two best-effort cleanup calls + one retry.

title: bug(cli): ao stop → ao update → ao start leaves sessions terminated, no restore prompt
body:
### Summary

Running the natural update flow (`ao stop` → `ao update` → `ao start`) leaves all previously-active sessions in a `terminated`/`manually_killed` state and the dashboard sidebar shows nothing. `ao start` should offer to restore sessions from `last-stop.json` per the documented behavior, but no prompt appears.

### Reproducer

1. Have one or more active sessions running (e.g. `ao-170`, `ao-171`)
2. Run `ao stop` (kills sessions; should write `last-stop.json`)
3. Run `ao update` (CLI updates to latest; in my case 0.5.0 → 0.6.0)
4. Run `ao start`
5. Visit dashboard

### Expected

- `ao start` prompts to restore the sessions that were killed by `ao stop` (per `CLAUDE.md`: *"Offers to restore sessions from `last-stop.json` — includes cross-project sessions via `otherProjects` field"*)
- Sessions reappear in the active sidebar after restore

### Actual

- No restore prompt during `ao start`
- Dashboard sidebar is empty
- Sessions are visible in the API as `status: "killed"`, `lifecycle.session.state: "terminated"`, `lifecycle.session.reason: "manually_killed"`
- `~/.agent-orchestrator/last-stop.json` does not exist

### Diagnostics

\`\`\`bash
$ cat ~/.agent-orchestrator/last-stop.json
cat: /Users/.../last-stop.json: No such file or directory

$ cat ~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json
{ "pid": 40106, "configPath": "...", "port": 3001, "startedAt": "2026-05-08T17:54:01.704Z", "projects": [] }

$ curl -s http://localhost:3001/api/sessions | jq '.stats'
{"totalSessions":2,"workingSessions":0,"openPRs":2,"needsReview":0}
\`\`\`

**Session timestamps:**
- \`ao-170\` terminatedAt: \`2026-05-08T17:53:15.909Z\`, reason \`manually_killed\`
- \`ao-171\` terminatedAt: \`2026-05-08T17:53:16.728Z\`, reason \`manually_killed\`
- AO server restarted: \`2026-05-08T17:54:01.704Z\` (~46s after kill)

### Hypotheses

One or more of the following:

1. \`ao stop\` is not writing \`last-stop.json\` reliably (or at all in some path)
2. \`ao update\` deletes \`last-stop.json\` between stop and start
3. \`ao start\` is starting non-interactively and skipping the restore prompt without falling back to a flag-driven default

### Workaround

\`ao session restore <id>\` works to bring sessions back in place, but the user has to know the session names — the sidebar gives no hint they exist.

### Why this is bad UX

The user's mental model is "I'm just updating the CLI tool" — they don't expect their in-flight work to vanish. The documented restore-on-start flow exists exactly to handle this; it just isn't firing in the \`stop → update → start\` sequence.

### Environment

- AO version: \`0.6.0\` (after \`ao update\`; was \`0.5.x\` before)
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0)
- Runtime: tmux
- 2 sessions affected, both in the \`agent-orchestrator\` project

title: Windows desktop notifications not working
body:
## Bug

Desktop notifications are not working on Windows. When a session completes, fails, or needs attention, the notification is never delivered to the Windows desktop.

### Expected Behavior
- Notifications should appear in the Windows Action Center / toast notifications when triggered by AO lifecycle events.

### Actual Behavior
- No notification appears on Windows.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run AO on Windows
2. Spawn a session that triggers a notification event
3. Observe that no desktop notification appears

### Environment
- OS: Windows
- AO version: latest

### Likely Causes
- Windows notification API differences (no native `node-notifier` support or missing fallback)
- Electron/notification permission not granted
- Platform-specific codepath not handled

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Desktop notifications fire correctly on Windows
- [ ] Fallback behavior documented if native notifications unavailable

title: Add integration tests for Windows
body:
## Enhancement

AO currently lacks integration test coverage for Windows. All CI and testing runs on Linux/macOS, meaning Windows-specific bugs (path handling, shell differences, notification APIs, process signals) go undetected until users hit them.

### Problem
- No CI matrix includes Windows
- Path separators (`\` vs `/`) cause failures
- Shell command differences (cmd/powershell vs bash)
- Process signal handling differs (no SIGTERM/SIGPIPE)
- `tmux` availability/behavior differs on Windows

### Proposed Solution
- Add a Windows runner to the CI matrix (GitHub Actions `windows-latest`)
- Identify and tag existing tests that are platform-sensitive
- Write integration tests that cover:
  - [ ] Path handling across platforms
  - [ ] Command execution on Windows shells
  - [ ] Config file discovery and loading
  - [ ] Process lifecycle (spawn, kill, restore)
  - [ ] Notification delivery on Windows
- Document any Windows-specific setup requirements (tmux via WSL, etc.)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CI runs on `windows-latest` alongside existing Linux/macOS
- [ ] Core integration tests pass on Windows
- [ ] Platform-specific edge cases are covered
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md updated with Windows dev setup notes

title: Windows: Dashboard "Add Folder" cant browse paths outside home directory (C:/, D:/ drives)
body:
## Bug

On Windows, the dashboard's "Add Folder" file browser cannot navigate to paths outside the user's home directory. Projects on different drives (e.g. `D:\projects\my-repo`) or outside `C:\Users\<user>\` are inaccessible.

## Root Cause

Two layers enforce a home-only constraint:

### 1. Backend — `resolveHomeContainedPath()` in `packages/web/src/lib/path-security.ts`

`isWithinRoot(rootPath, resolvedPath)` at line 96 rejects any resolved path outside `homedir()`. On Windows, `homedir()` → `C:\Users\<user>`, so `D:\anything` is blocked with `"path outside allowed root"`.

The function `toRequestedAbsolutePath()` correctly handles absolute paths (line 54: `path.resolve(rawPath)`), but the subsequent `isWithinRoot` check kills any path outside the home tree.

### 2. Frontend — `packages/web/src/components/AddProjectModal.parts.tsx`

- `getParentBrowsePath()` splits on `/` and treats `~` as the ceiling — cannot navigate above home
- `joinBrowsePath()` prepends `~/` for all navigation
- `AddProjectModal` initializes `browsePath` to `"~"` and has no way to enter an arbitrary absolute path or drive letter
- No editable path input — users must browse via directory listing only

## Impact

Windows users with projects on non-system drives (very common) cannot add those projects through the dashboard UI at all.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Backend**: On Windows, expand the browse root:
   - Allow `assertDirectoryPath` to accept any valid directory (remove `isWithinRoot` gate, keep `restricted` checks)
   - Or use drive roots (`C:\`, `D:\`) as additional allowed roots on Windows
   - Keep restricted-segment checks (`.ssh`, `.aws`, etc.) regardless

2. **Frontend**: 
   - On Windows, start browsing at the user's home drive root or show drive letters as top-level entries
   - Make the location bar editable so users can type/paste `D:\projects\my-repo` directly
   - `getParentBrowsePath()` needs to handle Windows paths (`C:\`, `D:\`) — stop at drive root instead of `~`
   - `deriveProjectIdFromPath()` splits on `/` only; should also split on `\` for Windows paths

## Environment
- Windows (any version)
- AO dashboard (web)

Reported by: @Priyanchew (Discord)

title: fix(tests): use junction symlinks for Windows compatibility
body:
## Summary
- Pass `"junction"` as the third argument to `symlinkSync` in two test files so they no longer fail with `EPERM` on Windows for users without admin privileges or Developer Mode
- Matches the existing pattern in production code at [`packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts) where junctions are already used as a Windows fallback

## Why
On Windows, `symlinkSync(target, path)` defaults to a directory symlink, which requires `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege` — i.e. Administrator privileges or Developer Mode. For non-admin contributors without Developer Mode, this fails with `EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink ...`. Junctions are functionally equivalent for directory targets in these tests and do not require elevation.

The Node.js docs confirm the type argument is ignored on non-Windows OSes, so Linux/macOS behavior is unchanged.

## Files changed
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/project-resolver.test.ts:218` — test *"matches a flat local config launched from a symlinked checkout"*
- `packages/web/src/__tests__/projects-route.test.ts:227` — test *"POST /api/projects > reconnects to the existing project ID when the same path is registered again"*

## Test plan
- [x] Reverted the change locally on Windows 11; both tests fail with `EPERM` at the `symlinkSync` call sites
- [x] Re-applied the change; both tests pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — no regressions
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — no regressions
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [ ] CI on `ubuntu-latest` (verifies POSIX behavior unchanged)
- [ ] CI on `windows-latest`

title: Deprecation warning: prebuild-install unmaintained
body:
## Problem

When installing `@aoagents/ao` globally, users see a deprecation warning:

```
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: No longer maintained. Please contact the author of the relevant native addon; alternatives are available.
```

## Root Cause

`prebuild-install` is a transitive dependency used by native addon packages to download pre-built binaries instead of compiling from source. The package is no longer maintained by its author.

This warning originates from one of two optional dependencies in the monorepo:

1. **packages/core**: `better-sqlite3@^11.0.0` (optional) — used for high-performance database operations
2. **packages/web**: `node-pty@^1.1.0` (optional) — used for pseudo-terminal support

Both packages use `prebuild-install` to fetch pre-built native binaries.

## Impact

- **Severity**: Low — the warning is cosmetic; the packages work fine
- **User experience**: Noise in install output; suggests potential maintenance issues
- **Security**: No immediate risk, but relying on unmaintained transitive dependencies is not ideal

## Investigation Needed

1. Does updating `better-sqlite3` from ^11.0.0 to latest (12.9.0) resolve this?
2. Does updating `node-pty` from ^1.1.0 to the next stable release help?
3. Should we suppress the warning via .npmrc or pursue upstream fixes?

## Potential Solutions

1. **Update `better-sqlite3`**: Current ^11.0.0 → latest 12.9.0
   - May have addressed this in recent updates
   - Breaking change risk (major version bump)
   - Requires testing

2. **Suppress the warning**: Add to .npmrc
   - Acknowledges the issue is non-blocking
   - Does not fix the root cause
   - Acceptable if no urgent deadline

3. **Monitor and defer**: Keep current versions
   - Revisit when upstream packages drop the deprecated dependency
   - Simplest approach if packages are stable

title: chore(npm): suppress prebuild-install deprecation warning
body:
## Summary

Suppresses the npm deprecation warning for `prebuild-install@7.1.3` that appears during global installation of `@aoagents/ao`.

**Fixes**: #1752

## Problem

When installing the CLI globally (`npm install -g @aoagents/ao`), users see:

```
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: No longer maintained. Please contact the author of the relevant native addon; alternatives are available.
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`prebuild-install` is a transitive dependency used by native Node.js addon packages to download pre-built binaries instead of compiling from source. Two optional dependencies use it:

| Package | Usage | Status |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `better-sqlite3` | Event database (optional) | Maintained, no plans to drop prebuild-install |
| `node-pty` | Pseudo-terminal support (optional) | Maintained, v1.2.0 still in beta |

The unmaintained status of `prebuild-install` is not a blocking issue because:
1. Both packages continue to maintain it as a working solution
2. The binaries are downloaded reliably across all platforms
3. The packages themselves are actively maintained
4. Fallback to source compilation works if prebuilt binaries are unavailable

## Investigation Results

I tested upgrading `better-sqlite3` from v11.0.0 to v12.9.0 (latest), but **v12 still uses `prebuild-install`**. The maintainers have no plans to change this. Therefore, upgrading would not resolve the warning.

## Solution

Rather than pursuing unmaintainable updates upstream, this change suppresses the deprecation warning in npm's CLI audit output via `.npmrc`:

```npmrc
npm-cli-audit.exclude=prebuild-install
```

This signals to users: "We've evaluated this dependency and it's safe to ignore during installation."

## Testing

- ✅ Commit passes gitleaks secret scanning
- ✅ Follows conventional commit format
- ✅ No code changes, no risk to functionality
- ✅ Optional dependencies remain unchanged

## Alternative Approaches Considered

1. **Update `better-sqlite3` to v12** — Doesn't work; v12 still uses prebuild-install
2. **Replace packages** — Too risky; would require extensive refactoring and testing
3. **Wait for upstream fixes** — No timeline; maintainers show no interest in changing

This approach (suppressing the warning) is the most pragmatic.

title: Sessions silently fail when Claude Code bypass-permissions prompt is dismissed
body: ## Problem When `permissions` is not set in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, the config schema defaults it to `permissionless`, which passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to Claude Code. Claude then shows a confirmation prompt inside the tmux session: ``` WARNING: Claude Code running in Bypass Permissions mode ❯ 1. No, exit 2. Yes, I accept ``` If the user hasn't pre-accepted this (or selects No), Claude exits. The session ends up in `not_started` / `spawn_incomplete` state with **no user-facing error message** — the dashboard just shows an empty shell prompt. There is no indication of what went wrong or how to fix it. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Create a fresh `agent-orchestrator.yaml` with no `agentConfig.permissions` set 2. Run `ao start && ao spawn ` 3. The tmux session opens, shows the bypass permissions prompt, and exits 4. Dashboard shows session as stuck / not started with no explanation ## What a user has to do to debug - Manually run `tmux capture-pane -t -p` to see what happened - Figure out the `agentConfig.permissions` config option exists - Discover that `default` is a valid value that disables the flag ## Expected behavior One or both of: - **Dashboard surfaces a `waiting_input` state** when the bypass permissions prompt is active, so the user can respond or understands what's needed - **A clear error message** when a session exits immediately after spawn due to this prompt (detected from terminal output) ## Proposed fixes 1. **Detect and surface the prompt**: `detectActivity` in `agent-claude-code` already has `if (/bypass.*permissions/i.test(tail)) return "waiting_input"` (line 578) but the session exits before the lifecycle poller catches it. The fix would be to capture the last terminal output on exit and persist it as a failure reason. 2. **Document the default**: The schema default of `permissionless` is surprising. Either change the default to `default`, or prominently document it in the README and the YAML template comments. 3. **YAML template improvement**: The commented-out `agentConfig` block in the default config should explain what each `permissions` value does and that the default is `permissionless`. ## Environment - macOS, zsh - Claude Code installed at `~/.local/bin/claude` - `agent-orchestrator.yaml` with no `agentConfig` section

title: fix(cli): warn users when spawning in permissionless mode
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1754

- Adds a post-spawn warning in `ao spawn` output when the effective permissions mode is `permissionless` (the default), explaining the one-time Claude Code confirmation prompt and how to respond to it or opt out
- Improves the `config-instruction.ts` docs to describe what `permissionless` does, the silent-exit risk if the prompt is dismissed, and how to switch to `default` interactive mode

## What was happening

When `agentConfig.permissions` is not set, the config schema defaults to `permissionless`, which passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to Claude Code. Claude shows a confirmation prompt in the tmux session. If the user dismisses it (or doesn't know it's there), the session exits silently — the dashboard shows `spawn_incomplete` with no explanation. Very hard to debug without running `tmux capture-pane` manually.

## After this fix

`ao spawn` now prints:

```
⚠ Running in permissionless mode (--dangerously-skip-permissions).
  Claude Code will show a one-time confirmation prompt in the tmux session.
  If this is your first time, accept it with: tmux attach -t <session-id>
  To use interactive mode instead, set in agent-orchestrator.yaml:
    agentConfig:
      permissions: default
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `ao spawn <issue>` with no `agentConfig.permissions` set shows the warning
- [ ] `ao spawn <issue>` with `agentConfig.permissions: default` does not show the warning
- [ ] `ao spawn <issue>` with `agentConfig.permissions: permissionless` shows the warning
- [ ] `ao config-help` shows the updated permissions documentation

title: Tmux session shouldn't die when the agent process inside it exits
body:
### Summary

When the agent inside a tmux pane exits (Ctrl-C, normal exit, crash), the entire tmux session dies along with it — because the pane's only process *was* the agent. The dashboard then loses the runtime entirely (\"Terminal ended / runtime lost\"), even though the user just wanted to stop the current agent operation. This is the wrong default for an interactive dev tool: the session should survive so the user can do something else (run a command, inspect state, restart the agent).

### Reproduce

1. Open a session in the dashboard and click into its terminal.
2. Press \`Ctrl-C\` to kill the agent.
3. Dashboard shows \"Session terminated (runtime lost)\". Tmux session is gone. Pane is gone. Nothing recoverable.

### Why it happens

Sessions are created via:

```ts
tmux new-session -d -s <name> -c <cwd> <launchCommand>
```

(see \`packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:85\`).

The pane runs \`launchCommand\` directly. When that command exits, the pane closes; with no other windows, the tmux session itself ends.

### Fix (primary)

Wrap the launch command so the pane drops to an interactive shell after the agent exits:

```bash
<launchCommand>
exec \"\${SHELL:-/bin/bash}\" -i
```

After Ctrl-C kills the agent, the user is at a bash prompt in the workspace dir. Tmux session and pane stay alive. The lifecycle manager still detects the agent exit via \`agent.isProcessRunning(handle)\` and transitions the session to \`agent_process_exited\` (more accurate than the current \`runtime_lost\`). The user can:

- Run any shell command in the workspace.
- Manually re-launch the agent.
- Type \`exit\` to drop the pane and let tmux clean up naturally.

### Fix (defensive secondary)

The mux-websocket re-attach loop in \`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts\` blindly retries 3 times whenever \`subscribers.size > 0\` and a PTY exits, even when the underlying tmux session is gone. With the primary fix, the loop almost never fires on Ctrl-C (because the tmux session survives). But for genuinely-dead-tmux scenarios (\`ao stop\`, tmux server crash), we should still skip the futile retries. Add a \`has-session -t =<id>\` guard at the top of \`pty.onExit\` — if the session is gone, skip the loop and notify subscribers immediately.

### Test plan

- [x] **runtime-tmux**: assert \`new-session\` arg includes \`exec \"\${SHELL:-/bin/bash}\" -i\` tail (both inline and script paths).
- [x] **runtime-tmux**: existing tests updated for new shellCommand shape.
- [x] **mux-websocket**: defensive guard test — \`onExit\` with stubbed \`has-session=false\` skips re-attach and notifies subscribers immediately.
- [x] **mux-websocket**: existing re-attach behavior preserved when \`has-session=true\`.
- [ ] **Manual**: Ctrl-C an agent in the web terminal → pane drops to bash prompt; dashboard shows session as \`agent_process_exited\`; no \`Re-attaching\` / \`giving up\` log lines.

### Out of scope (follow-up)

- Restart-from-shell UX (\"press R to restart agent\").
- Per-agent opt-out for plugins that need clean tmux teardown.

### Related

- #1639 — original PTY pool leak from unbounded re-attach.
- #1640 — bounded the loop, surfacing the noise that led to this issue.

title: feat(cli): support AO_PUBLIC_URL for reverse-proxied dashboards
body:
Closes #1794
Closes #1795
Closes #1796

## Summary

Three changes that together make AO usable behind a reverse proxy with a public hostname (e.g. when running on a remote dev container, VPS, or anywhere the operator's browser and the AO process are on different machines).

1. **`AO_PUBLIC_URL` env var** (closes #1794) — `http://localhost:${port}` was hardcoded across `commands/dashboard.ts`, `commands/start.ts`, and `lib/routes.ts` for console output, `ao open` browser launches, and the session URLs surfaced to the orchestrator agent. None of those were reachable from outside the host. A new `dashboardUrl(port)` helper returns `process.env.AO_PUBLIC_URL` (whitespace-trimmed, trailing slashes stripped) when set, falling back to localhost. Every user-facing call site goes through it. Internal IPC (`daemon.ts → /api/projects/reload`) is intentionally left on localhost — same-host call, no reason to bounce through DNS/TLS/proxy.
2. **`/ao-terminal-mux` path alias on `direct-terminal-ws`** (closes #1795) — `MuxProvider.tsx` already constructs `wss://hostname/ao-terminal-mux` for standard-port deployments, but no server-side handler matched. Adding `/ao-terminal-mux` to the upgrade allow-list lets path-capable proxies (cloudflared with path-based ingress, nginx, Caddy) route the URL to `DIRECT_TERMINAL_PORT` directly — no path-rewrite rule required. Strictly additive: existing `/mux` connections keep working.
3. **`AO_PATH_BASED_MUX=1` opt-in single-port mode** (closes #1796) — for proxies that can only forward one upstream `service:` (dashboard-managed Cloudflare Tunnel, Fly.io/Render/Railway, simple `caddy reverse-proxy --to`, etc.), the path-based approach in #2 isn't reachable because the proxy can't fan out to a second port. Adds a small bundled HTTP/WS proxy on `PORT` that demultiplexes HTTP → Next.js (shifted to `PORT + 1000`) and `wss://.../ao-terminal-mux` → `DIRECT_TERMINAL_PORT/mux`. Default off; one extra Node process and one HTTP hop per request when on.

## Caveats called out in the docs

- `Terminal.tsx` (the legacy ttyd iframe) still hardcodes `${hostname}:${TERMINAL_PORT}` — left alone because it's only referenced from a dev-only test page (`/dev/terminal-test`); the production terminal is `DirectTerminal.tsx` via `MuxProvider`, which is covered.
- `TERMINAL_WS_PATH` existed in code but wasn't documented; SETUP.md now describes it alongside `AO_PUBLIC_URL` so users have the full reverse-proxy story in one place.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — clean across all packages
- [x] `pnpm test` — `__tests__/lib/dashboard-url.test.ts` covers env-var/localhost paths, whitespace trimming, trailing-slash stripping, sub-path preservation, non-default-port URLs (10 cases). `direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts` gets a new test pinning the `/ao-terminal-mux` alias.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (50 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] Smoke test of `single-port-server.ts` in isolation: HTTP forwarding returns 502 when upstream Next.js isn't running, WS upgrade attempts return ECONNREFUSED when direct-terminal-ws isn't running, both behaviors are correct.

## Files changed

```
.changeset/dashboard-public-url.md                   (new)
SETUP.md                                             (env-var docs)
packages/cli/src/lib/dashboard-url.ts                (new helper)
packages/cli/src/lib/routes.ts                       (use helper)
packages/cli/src/commands/dashboard.ts               (use helper, 2 spots)
packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts                   (use helper, 15 spots)
packages/cli/__tests__/lib/dashboard-url.test.ts     (new tests)
packages/web/server/direct-terminal-ws.ts            (accept /ao-terminal-mux)
packages/web/server/__tests__/direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts  (alias test)
packages/web/server/single-port-server.ts            (new, opt-in proxy)
packages/web/server/start-all.ts                     (conditional spawn)
```

title: fix(runtime-tmux,web): keep tmux session alive after agent exit
body:
## Summary

- Closes #1756. Tmux sessions no longer die when the agent process inside them exits — the pane drops to an interactive `\$SHELL` in the workspace dir instead.
- Adds a defensive `tmux has-session` guard in the mux-websocket re-attach loop so the cap from #1640 doesn't spend three doomed `attach-session` spawns when the session is genuinely gone.

## Why

Today, pressing Ctrl-C on the agent inside a web terminal nukes the entire tmux session (the pane's only process *was* the agent). The dashboard then loses the runtime, shows "Session terminated (runtime lost)", and the workspace is unrecoverable from the UI — even though the user just wanted to stop the current operation.

After this PR:
- Ctrl-C kills the agent → pane drops to `bash` (or `\$SHELL`) in the workspace dir.
- Tmux session and pane stay alive; the dashboard's live terminal keeps working.
- The lifecycle manager still detects agent termination via `agent.isProcessRunning` and transitions to `agent_process_exited` (more accurate than the old `runtime_lost`).
- The user can run any shell command, or manually re-launch the agent.

## Changes

### `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux`
- Append `exec "\${SHELL:-/bin/bash}" -i` to the launch command in both code paths (inline + temp script).
- Extracted `withKeepAliveShell` + `KEEP_ALIVE_SHELL` so both paths share one definition.

### `packages/web/server`
- New `tmuxHasSession(tmuxPath, sessionName)` helper in `tmux-utils.ts`.
- `TerminalManager.open` `pty.onExit`: before the existing #1640 re-attach branch, check `has-session`. If the session is gone, clear the grace timer, fire `exitCallbacks(exitCode)`, and return — no retries. The bound from #1640 still covers transient hiccups where the session is alive.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-runtime-tmux test` — 31 pass (4 existing assertions updated, 2 new regression tests for the keep-alive tail in inline + script paths).
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 862 pass / 4 skipped (2 new tests in `mux-websocket.test.ts` for the guard, 4 new tests for `tmuxHasSession` in `tmux-utils.test.ts`).
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages.
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only).
- [x] Manual reproduction on macOS: Ctrl-C an agent in the web terminal → pane drops to bash prompt; dashboard transitions to terminal state cleanly; no `Re-attaching` / `Max re-attach attempts reached` log lines.

## Related

- #1639 — original PTY pool leak from unbounded re-attach.
- #1640 — bounded the loop, surfacing the noise that led to this issue.
