title: Removed project reappears after ao stop + ao start
body:
## Bug

When a user removes a project from the dashboard UI, then runs `ao stop` followed by `ao start`, the removed project reappears.

## Root Cause

**Zombie local config file.** The dashboard DELETE handler calls `unregisterProject()` which removes the project from the **global** config (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`), but the **local** `agent-orchestrator.yaml` in the project directory is left untouched.

On `ao start` from that project directory:

1. `findConfigFile()` discovers the orphaned local config on disk
2. `loadConfig()` tries to resolve the flat config against the global config → fails (project was removed)
3. The error recovery path in `resolve-project.ts` (~L465–476) treats this as a **"first-time flat config that needs registration"**
4. `registerFlatConfig()` **unconditionally re-registers** the project into the global config
5. Project reappears in the dashboard

## Key Files

- `packages/web/src/app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts` — DELETE handler (L280–324)
- `packages/core/src/portfolio-registry.ts` — `unregisterProject()` (L351–363)
- `packages/cli/src/lib/resolve-project.ts` — error recovery that re-registers (L465–476)
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` — `registerFlatConfig()` (L127–158)

## Suggested Fixes

1. **`removedProjects` denylist** in global config — `registerFlatConfig` checks it before re-registering. User can override with explicit `ao start <path>`.
2. **`{ removed: true }` marker** in the local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` on DELETE — skip re-registration if marker present.
3. **Delete the local config** in the DELETE handler (aggressive — loses user settings).
4. **Prompt instead of auto-registering** — ask the user rather than silently re-registering.

Reported by @siddarth

title: feat(web): mobile access — end-to-end tracer (hardcoded token, fake middleware, fake WS gate) behind AO_MOBILE_DEV=1
body:
## What to build

Throwaway scaffolding that proves the end-to-end wiring for mobile access works before any real auth lands. Behind `AO_MOBILE_DEV=1` env flag — never reachable in production builds.

The slice cuts every layer:

- **CLI scaffold:** new `packages/cli/src/commands/mobile.ts` with a `--dev` mode that spawns cloudflared via `lib/cloudflared.ts` (also new) and prints the resulting URL plus an ASCII QR.
- **Web scaffold:** stub `packages/web/src/middleware.ts` that checks for a hardcoded `Cookie: ao_mobile=DEV` and gates `/api/*` and dashboard routes; allowlists `/m` and `/api/mobile/login`. Stub `/m` page that sets the dev cookie and redirects to `/`. Stub `/api/mobile/login` that always returns 204 with the dev cookie.
- **WS scaffold:** WS upgrade handler reads cookie header, accepts if it equals `DEV`, rejects 401 otherwise. No origin check, no revocation, no scanner — just enough to prove the upgrade flow gates correctly.
- **Smoke test:** integration test that spawns the dashboard with `AO_MOBILE_DEV=1`, opens a WS upgrade, asserts unauthorized without cookie + authorized with cookie.

This entire slice gets ripped out and replaced over slices 2-4. Its only job is to surface integration bugs early (Edge bundle layout, WS upgrade routing, middleware allowlist behavior) before the real cryptographic primitives land on top.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AO_MOBILE_DEV=1 ao mobile --dev` starts cloudflared, prints tunnel URL + QR, blocks until Ctrl+C
- [ ] Phone (or curl with `Cookie: ao_mobile=DEV`) loads `/` through the tunnel and gets the dashboard
- [ ] Phone without the cookie hitting `/` gets 401 from middleware; `/m` and `/api/mobile/login` pass through unauthenticated
- [ ] WS upgrade to `/ws/terminal` succeeds with the dev cookie, rejects with 401 otherwise
- [ ] Production builds (no `AO_MOBILE_DEV`) compile and run with zero behavior change — middleware is a pass-through, no `/m` route registered
- [ ] Integration test in `packages/web` covering the four cases above

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

title: feat(core+web): mobile-store + signed-cookie auth (real token, HMAC-signed HttpOnly cookie, real middleware + login route + /m page)
body:
## What to build

Replace the throwaway dev-mode scaffolding from #1760 with the real authentication core. After this slice, mobile auth uses a 128-bit token + HMAC-signed HttpOnly session cookie, end to end, but the WS upgrade gate and CLI command are still the dev-mode versions from #1760.

### `packages/core/src/mobile-store.ts` (new)

Persistent state at `~/.agent-orchestrator/mobile.json` (mode `0600`):
- `tokenHash` — `sha256(token)`, hex
- `hmacKey` — base64url, used to sign session cookies; persisted so phone sessions survive `ao stop && ao start --mobile`
- `sessions: { id, iat, exp }[]` — issued sessions
- `revokedSessionIds: string[]` — populated by `ao mobile revoke`
- `failureCount` — atomic counter; ≥10 disables login until cleared on host
- `locked: boolean` — set when failureCount hits threshold

Operations: `verifyToken(token)` constant-time, `issueSession({ ttlMs })`, `recordFailure()` (file-locked atomic via `proper-lockfile`), `isRevoked(sessionId)`, `isLocked()`, `revokeAll()`. Atomic temp-file-rename for all writes.

### `packages/web/src/lib/mobile-auth-edge.ts` (new)

Stateless `verifyCookieEdge(cookieHeader, hmacKey)` — signature + expiry only, no fs imports. Edge-runtime safe. Fails closed on any malformed input (try/catch wraps everything, returns null). Cookie is base64url, exactly 2 dot-parts, capped at 4KB. Expiry uses `<=`.

### `packages/web/src/lib/mobile-auth-node.ts` (new)

`verifyCookieFull(cookieHeader, hmacKey, store)` — calls Edge variant, then adds `store.isRevoked` check. Used by login route post-auth flows and any Node-runtime mutating routes.

### `packages/web/src/middleware.ts` (replace stub from #1760)

Edge runtime. Reads `process.env.AO_MOBILE_COOKIE_KEY` (set by dashboard bootstrap from `mobile.json`). Calls `verifyCookieEdge`. Public allowlist: `/m`, `/api/mobile/login`, Next.js static assets. Sets `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` + `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

### `packages/web/src/app/api/mobile/login/route.ts` (replace stub)

`export const runtime = "nodejs"`. Body cap enforced **while reading the stream** via a `readWithCap` helper (header-only check is bypassable on chunked bodies). Content-type matched with `startsWith("application/json")` (accepts charset suffix). `Sec-Fetch-Site` rejected when present and not `same-origin`. On valid token: issues session via store, signs cookie, sets HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict, 24h TTL. On invalid: increments file-locked counter; ≥10 → 423.

### `packages/web/src/app/m/page.tsx` (replace stub)

Static client component. Reads `#t=…` from fragment, POSTs to `/api/mobile/login`, runs `history.replaceState` to drop the fragment, redirects to `/`. Per-request CSP nonce via middleware. `<noscript>` fallback shows manual instructions.

### Dashboard bootstrap

When `--mobile` is set, read `mobile.json` HMAC key and inject as `process.env.AO_MOBILE_COOKIE_KEY` before Next.js boots. Force-bind `127.0.0.1`; hard-fail at startup if any non-loopback bind is configured.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mobile-store.ts` ships with full unit test coverage: token gen, hash compare constant-time, atomic counter under 100 concurrent failures, lockout fires once, atomic temp-rename writes survive simulated power loss, revocation list grows / reads correctly
- [ ] `verifyCookieEdge` returns `null` (never throws) for: missing cookie, oversized cookie (>4KB), one-dot, three-dot, malformed base64url, bad signature, expired, type-invalid session JSON
- [ ] `verifyCookieFull` calls Edge variant first, then revocation check
- [ ] Edge bundle output verified to NOT include `fs` or `MobileStore` (build-time grep)
- [ ] Login route accepts `application/json; charset=utf-8`
- [ ] Login route blocks chunked body >1KB without `content-length` header (returns 413)
- [ ] Login route returns 415 wrong content-type, 413 oversized, 403 cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site`, 423 when locked, 401 invalid token, 204 + cookie on success
- [ ] `/m` page works with JS enabled, shows fallback with JS disabled, drops fragment via `replaceState`, has CSP nonce
- [ ] Middleware allowlist passes `/m` and `/api/mobile/login` through unauthenticated; all other paths require valid cookie
- [ ] HMAC key persisted in `mobile.json` survives dashboard restart; sessions stay valid across `ao stop && ao start --mobile`
- [ ] Dashboard refuses to start with non-loopback bind when `--mobile` is set
- [ ] WS upgrade gate from #1760 still works (real cookie now, dev-mode env removed for this PR or kept for one more slice)

## Blocked by

- #1760

title: feat(web): WebSocket upgrade gate + process-wide 60s re-verify scanner (real revocation)
body:
## What to build

Replace the dev-mode WS gate from #1760 with the production gate. Adds:

- Path allowlist (`/ws/terminal`, `/ws/events`); unknown paths get 404
- Mandatory `Origin` match against the normalized tunnel origin (scheme + lowercase host, no trailing slash); missing or mismatched → 403
- Cookie verification via `verifyCookieFull` from #1761 (signature + expiry + revocation)
- Async error handling around the whole upgrade handler — any throw → 500 close, no leaked sockets
- Loopback assertion at WS bootstrap (one-shot at startup, not per-handler)
- `liveSockets: Map<sessionId, Set<WebSocket>>` lives in a new `packages/web/src/lib/mobile-runtime.ts` (process-local, NOT a cross-process singleton — `mobile.json` is the source of truth across processes)
- One process-wide `setInterval` (60s) that scans `liveSockets`, reads `mobile.json` for revocation/expiry, and closes matching sockets with code `4001 revoked` or `4002 session_expired`. Timer is `unref`'d so process exits cleanly.

After this slice, an attacker with an already-open terminal has at most ~60s after revoke or expiry — file-mediated, no IPC needed between CLI and dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `verifyUpgrade` runs before `handleUpgrade` on every WS upgrade event
- [ ] Path not in allowlist → 404 reject, no upgrade
- [ ] Missing `Origin` header (with mobile enabled) → 403 reject
- [ ] Origin mismatch → 403 reject
- [ ] Valid cookie + valid origin + allowlisted path → upgrade accepted, socket added to `liveSockets[sessionId]`
- [ ] Async throw inside the handler → 500 close, no socket leak
- [ ] Loopback bind assertion runs once at startup; non-loopback bind hard-fails
- [ ] `mobile-runtime.ts` exports a single `liveSockets` Map, single timer, single `expectedOrigin`
- [ ] Process-wide scanner: write a revocation record to `mobile.json`, two open sockets close with `4001` within ~60s
- [ ] Process-wide scanner: cookie expiry mocked, sockets close with `4002` within ~60s
- [ ] Re-verify timer is `unref`'d (verified in unit test on the WS bootstrap module)
- [ ] Singleton invariant test: import `mobile-runtime` from 3 different module paths in the dashboard process → all see the same `liveSockets` Map reference
- [ ] Dev-mode WS gate scaffolding from #1760 fully removed in this PR

## Blocked by

- #1761

title: feat(web+cli): cloudflared-manager + toggle/status/revoke API routes + `ao start --expose` flag
body:
## What to build

**This issue was substantially rewritten after Prateek's feedback on the design doc.** The earlier "standalone \`ao mobile\` command" scope is gone. Mobile is now a runtime toggle on the existing dashboard process. This issue delivers the dashboard-owned tunnel lifecycle plus the three API routes the UI will consume in #1764.

### `packages/web/src/lib/cloudflared-manager.ts` (new)

Lives in the dashboard process, NOT the CLI. Responsibilities:
- Spawn cloudflared as a child process when called: `cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$PORT --no-autoupdate`
- Stream stderr; match `https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com` for the URL; hard-fail on any other host
- Expose `.url` and `.spawn({port})` / `.kill()` methods
- Tied to dashboard lifecycle: dashboard SIGTERM cascades to the child (5s grace, then SIGKILL)
- On unexpected child exit: flip `mobile-runtime.enabled` to false, log it; no auto-restart in V1

### `packages/web/src/app/api/mobile/toggle/route.ts` (new, Node runtime)

- `POST`: generates token, spawns cloudflared via manager, flips `mobile-runtime.enabled`, returns `{ url: "<tunnel>/m#t=<token>", expiresAt }`. Token is shown to the caller exactly once. Locked-out store rejects with 423.
- `DELETE`: kills cloudflared, calls `killAllSessionSockets()`, wipes sessions in mobile-store, returns 204.

### `packages/web/src/app/api/mobile/revoke/route.ts` (new, Node runtime)

- `POST`: calls `killAllSessionSockets()` immediately in-process + wipes sessions in mobile-store. Tunnel stays up — only the token + sessions are invalidated. Returns 204.

### `packages/web/src/app/api/mobile/status/route.ts` (new, Node runtime)

- `GET`: returns `{ enabled, url, sessionCount, locked }`. Never echoes the token.

All three routes are gated by the same cookie middleware as the rest of the dashboard. The phone CAN call them (it's signed in too) but the air-gap discussion in the design doc notes this is acceptable for V1.

### `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` (modified)

Add `--expose` flag. When set, the dashboard boots with `AO_MOBILE_AUTO_ENABLE=1` (or equivalent) — the runtime auto-flips the toggle on first boot, spawns cloudflared, prints the URL + QR + RCE warning banner to the terminal. No standalone CLI command, no `ao mobile` subcommand.

### `packages/core/src/config.ts` (modified)

Add `mobile: { autoEnable: boolean; tunnelProvider: 'cloudflare' }` to the Zod schema. Default `autoEnable: false`. If true, dashboard auto-enables mobile on every start (same code path as `--expose`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cloudflared-manager.ts` spawns and tears down cloudflared as a child of the dashboard process; SIGTERM cascades correctly
- [ ] cloudflared stderr parser rejects URLs on unexpected hosts (fixture test)
- [ ] `POST /api/mobile/toggle` enables, generates token, returns URL with `/m#t=` path, never bare `/#t=`
- [ ] `DELETE /api/mobile/toggle` kills cloudflared, calls `killAllSessionSockets()`, wipes sessions
- [ ] `POST /api/mobile/revoke` closes ALL live WS connections in the same tick as the response (integration test: open 3 sockets, POST revoke, assert all close before the HTTP response returns)
- [ ] `GET /api/mobile/status` never returns the token; returns `enabled: false` when off
- [ ] All three routes return 401 without a valid cookie; locked state returns 423 on toggle POST
- [ ] `ao start --expose` auto-enables mobile on boot; QR + URL + warning banner printed to terminal
- [ ] `mobile.autoEnable: true` in config auto-enables on every `ao start` (no flag needed)
- [ ] `mobile.autoEnable: false` (default) → `ao start` boots normally with mobile off
- [ ] If cloudflared crashes mid-run, `mobile-runtime.enabled` flips false; UI status reflects "Off (tunnel crashed)"

## Blocked by

- #1761
- #1762

title: feat(web): MobileToggle UI component with first-time RCE/air-gap confirmation modal
body:
## What to build

**This issue was substantially rewritten after Prateek's feedback.** The earlier "ao mobile revoke / status CLI subcommands" scope is gone. Those are now API routes (delivered by #1763); this issue delivers the dashboard UI control that consumes them.

### `packages/web/src/components/MobileToggle.tsx` (new)

Dashboard chrome component (header or sidebar — pick one in the PR). Two states:

**Off state:**
```
┌─ Mobile access ──────────────────────────┐
│  ●  Off                          [Enable]│
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**On state:**
```
┌─ Mobile access ──────────────────────────┐
│  ●  ON · N active session(s)             │
│                                          │
│  https://maple-bear-9341.trycloudflare   │
│  .com/m#t=…(token shown once, copy now)  │
│                                          │
│  [ QR code ]                             │
│                                          │
│  [Copy URL]      [Revoke + Disable]      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### First-time confirmation modal

The first time a user clicks Enable on a given dashboard install (persist a `mobileToggleAcknowledged: true` flag in mobile-store after acceptance), show a modal that explains:

1. Anyone holding the URL+token gets full RCE-equivalent access to this machine.
2. Anyone with dashboard access (browser extension, runaway agent, etc.) can now re-enable mobile in this same place — the earlier "shell required to enable" air gap is gone.
3. Mitigation: the toggle is **ephemeral by default** — dashboard restart returns to Off unless `mobile.autoEnable: true` is set in config.
4. Click Confirm to proceed; Cancel to abort.

After acknowledgment, the modal does NOT show again on subsequent Enable clicks. Acknowledgment is reset when the mobile-store is reset (manual file delete).

### API integration

- Polls `GET /api/mobile/status` every 5s while mounted (use the existing SSE pattern if possible; otherwise polling).
- Enable button → `POST /api/mobile/toggle` → renders the QR + URL with the returned token.
- "Revoke + Disable" button → `DELETE /api/mobile/toggle` (which also wipes sessions and kills cloudflared in one call). "Revoke only" can be a secondary action if needed, mapping to `POST /api/mobile/revoke`.

### Styling

- Tailwind only, no inline styles (per `CLAUDE.md` C-02).
- Dark theme tokens from `globals.css`.
- QR rendered inline via the same encoder used by the CLI (Lane E may package it as a shared util).
- No external UI component libraries (per C-01).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Component renders Off state by default; Enable button calls `POST /api/mobile/toggle`
- [ ] On-state UI shows tunnel URL with `/m#t=` path, ANSI-or-canvas QR, session count
- [ ] First-time Enable shows the confirmation modal with both warnings (RCE + air-gap)
- [ ] Acknowledged flag persists in mobile-store; second Enable doesn't show modal
- [ ] "Revoke + Disable" calls `DELETE /api/mobile/toggle`; UI returns to Off state within one render cycle
- [ ] Polling `GET /api/mobile/status` keeps the displayed session count fresh
- [ ] Component reflects "Off (tunnel crashed)" when `mobile-runtime.enabled` flips false unexpectedly (`/status` returns `{ enabled: false, url: null }` after a crash)
- [ ] Component test covers all three states (off, on, locked) with mocked `/api/mobile/status` responses
- [ ] No inline styles; passes existing ESLint config

## Blocked by

- #1763

title: docs+test: README "Use AO from your phone" + threat model + iOS Safari real-device E2E
body:
## What to build

### README section: "Use AO from your phone"

New section in `README.md` covering:
- One-command setup: `ao mobile` (prerequisites: `cloudflared` on PATH; show install instructions for brew + apt)
- The explicit RCE warning: anyone holding the token gets full RCE-equivalent access to the dev machine until the token expires (24h) or `ao mobile revoke` is run
- Threat model summary — what V1 defends against (passive snooping, port scanners, online brute-force, WS hijack from a malicious page) and what it doesn't (phishing of the tunnel URL, malicious browser extension on the phone, compromised host machine, stolen unlocked phone with a still-valid cookie)
- The fail-closed lockout: 10 failed token attempts disables mobile until `ao mobile revoke` is run on the host. Document honestly as "fail-closed by design, also a remote DoS lever."
- The honest revoke window: live WebSocket connections close within ~60s after `ao mobile revoke`; new requests are blocked instantly.
- Pointer to V1.5 hardening (audit log, cloudflared checksum verify, `ao mobile install`)
- Pointer to V2 hardening (Cloudflare Access SSO for phishing-resistant auth, per-device passkeys)

### Manual iOS Safari E2E

Documented step-by-step that a maintainer runs on a real iPhone before each release tag that touches `packages/{cli,web}/src/**/mobile/**`. Codex specifically called this out as needing real-device testing rather than simulators.

Steps to verify:
1. `ao mobile` on host
2. Scan QR with iPhone camera, open in Safari
3. Confirm `/m` page exchanges the fragment token and lands on dashboard signed in
4. Spawn a session from the phone end-to-end (issue a prompt to a Claude Code agent)
5. Open a terminal WS, type, see output
6. Lock phone, wait 5min, unlock — terminal still works
7. Run `ao mobile revoke` on host — terminal closes within 60s with friendly message
8. Re-run `ao mobile`, scan new QR, confirm the OLD token is rejected (lockout-cleared-by-revoke check)

Capture results in a checklist file under `docs/release-checklists/mobile-access-v1.md` so each release can copy + sign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README section drafted and merged
- [ ] Threat model wording matches the design doc's "what V1 does/doesn't defend against" callouts
- [ ] Release checklist file added under `docs/release-checklists/`
- [ ] At least one round of the iOS Safari E2E completed against the merged code, results captured
- [ ] Any UX gap surfaced by the manual E2E filed as a follow-up issue (or fixed inline if trivial)

## Blocked by

- #1763
- #1764

title: Windows: global config.yaml never created on first `ao start`
body:
## Bug

On Windows, running `ao start` in a new project for the first time creates the local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` but **never** creates the global `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`. This works correctly on macOS.

Reported by @Priyanchew — confirmed cross-platform structural gap masked on Mac by subsequent dashboard interactions.

---

## Root Cause: Three Compounding Windows-Specific Bugs

### Bug 1: `process.env["HOME"]` is undefined on Windows

Two files use `process.env["HOME"]` for tilde expansion instead of `os.homedir()`:

- **`packages/cli/src/lib/resolve-project.ts:336`**
  ```typescript
  const resolvedPath = resolve(arg.replace(/^~/, process.env["HOME"] || ""));
  ```
- **`packages/cli/src/lib/path-equality.ts:42`**
  ```typescript
  const expanded = input.replace(/^~/, process.env["HOME"] ?? "");
  ```

On Windows, `HOME` doesn't exist (it's `USERPROFILE`). The `|| ""` fallback replaces `~` with an empty string, breaking path resolution. Meanwhile, `global-config.ts` correctly uses `homedir()` from `node:os` — so the *read* path for global config works, but any flow going through tilde expansion with `HOME` breaks silently.

### Bug 2: `isCanonicalGlobalConfigPath()` uses strict `===` on paths

**`packages/core/src/global-config.ts:100-102`:**
```typescript
export function isCanonicalGlobalConfigPath(configPath: string | undefined): boolean {
  if (!configPath) return false;
  return resolve(configPath) === resolve(getGlobalConfigPath());
}
```

On Windows, `path.resolve()` preserves drive letter case from the input. If `configPath` arrives as `c:\Users\...` but `getGlobalConfigPath()` returns `C:\Users\...`, the strict `===` comparison fails. This function **guards** the `registerProjectInGlobalConfig` call in `addProjectToConfig()` (`start.ts:721`), so a case mismatch causes registration to silently fall through to the local-only branch.

### Bug 3 (structural, cross-platform): `autoCreateConfig()` skips global registration

**`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:469-607`**

After `autoCreateConfig()` creates the local wrapped `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, it returns `loadConfig(outputPath)` but **never calls `registerProjectInGlobalConfig()`**. The global config is only registered in:
- `registerFlatConfig()` — recovery path for flat local configs
- `addProjectToConfig()` when `isCanonicalGlobalConfigPath()` is true — already at global config
- `fromUrlIntoGlobal()` — URL-based project creation

None of these fire during a simple first-run `ao start` in an empty directory. This is cross-platform, but on macOS it gets masked because the dashboard UI eventually triggers `seedGlobalRegistryFromCurrentConfig()` when the user interacts with it, and the path comparisons work.

---

## Why macOS Works and Windows Doesn't

| Factor | macOS | Windows |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `process.env["HOME"]` | Set correctly ✅ | Undefined ❌ |
| Drive letter case | N/A | Mismatch silently skips registration ❌ |
| Dashboard recovery path | Path comparisons work ✅ | Broken by bugs 1 & 2 ❌ |

---

## Recommended Fixes

| File | Line(s) | Fix |
|------|---------|-----|
| `packages/cli/src/lib/resolve-project.ts` | 336 | Replace `process.env["HOME"]` with `homedir()` from `node:os` |
| `packages/cli/src/lib/path-equality.ts` | 42 | Replace `process.env["HOME"]` with `homedir()` from `node:os` |
| `packages/core/src/global-config.ts` | 100-102 | Use case-insensitive comparison on Windows (or the `pathsEqual()` helper from `path-equality.ts`) |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` | ~606 | Add `registerProjectInGlobalConfig()` call after `autoCreateConfig()` completes |

Per `AGENTS.md` convention: all new fixes should use `isWindows()` from `@aoagents/ao-core` (`packages/core/src/platform.ts`) rather than inline `process.platform === "win32"` checks. See `docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.md` for the full helper inventory and pre-merge checklist.

title: Config hot-reload: changes to agent-orchestrator.yaml not picked up at runtime
body:
## Problem

When a user edits `agent-orchestrator.yaml` while AO is running, the changes are not reflected. Config is loaded once at startup via `loadConfig()` and cached in memory. The lifecycle manager's polling loop monitors session state changes but does **not** watch the config file.

Currently requires a full `ao stop` + `ao start` cycle to pick up config changes — which kills all running sessions.

## Expected Behavior

Changes to `agent-orchestrator.yaml` should be hot-reloaded at runtime without restarting the orchestrator or disrupting active sessions.

## Affected Config Sections

- **Agent plugin settings** (model, temperature, etc.)
- **Project settings** (registry path, etc.)
- **Plugin configurations** (new plugins added/removed)

Some config changes (e.g., adding a new project) may be safe to hot-reload without affecting running sessions, while others (e.g., changing a running agent's model mid-execution) need careful handling.

## Suggested Approach

1. Add a file watcher (e.g., `chokidar`) on `agent-orchestrator.yaml` per project
2. On change, validate the new config against the schema
3. Diff old vs new config to determine which sections changed
4. Apply non-destructive changes in-place (new projects, updated labels, etc.)
5. Queue destructive changes for next session restart (agent model changes, plugin swaps)
6. Emit a config-change event that interested subsystems can subscribe to

## Environment
- AO version: latest main
- OS: all platforms

title: JSON schema (config.schema.json) obsolete — out of sync with Zod schemas after multi-project
body:
## Problem

`schema/config.schema.json` describes the **old single-file config format** (`agent-orchestrator.yaml` with a `projects:` wrapper). After the multi-project refactor, AO now has a **hybrid config architecture**:

1. **Global config** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`) — operational settings + project registry (identity only)
2. **Local project config** (`<project>/agent-orchestrator.yaml`) — flat, behavior-only (no `projects:` wrapper, no identity fields)
3. **Legacy single-file config** (`agent-orchestrator.yaml` with `projects:` map) — auto-migrated to hybrid on load

The JSON schema only describes format #3 (the old format). It does not reflect the global config schema (`GlobalConfigSchema`) or the local project config schema (`LocalProjectConfigSchema`) which are both defined in `packages/core/src/global-config.ts`.

## What needs to happen

### Option A: Split into two schemas
1. **`schema/config.schema.json`** — renamed/rebuilt to describe the **global config** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`): `port`, `defaults`, `projects` (registry entries with identity fields only), `notifiers`, `notificationRouting`, `reactions`
2. **`schema/project-local.schema.json`** (new) — describes the **flat local project config** (`<project>/agent-orchestrator.yaml`): `runtime`, `agent`, `workspace`, `tracker`, `scm`, `env`, `agentConfig`, `orchestrator`, `worker`, `reactions`, `agentRules`, `orchestratorSessionStrategy`, etc. No `projects:` wrapper, no identity fields.

### Option B: Single schema with `$defs` for both
Keep one file but add `$defs/localProjectConfig` alongside `$defs/projectConfig` and a `$comment` explaining the two contexts.

### Specific field-level gaps (still applies)

**Global config schema missing from JSON schema:**
- `projectOrder` (optional array of project IDs for sidebar ordering)
- `GlobalProjectEntry` fields: `projectId`, `source`, `registeredAt`, `displayName`, `sessionPrefix`
- `repo` is now a structured object `{ owner, name, platform, originUrl }` not a plain string
- `defaults.notifiers` default changed to `["composio", "desktop"]`

**Local project config (entirely missing from JSON schema):**
- `env` (per-project environment variables)
- `decomposer` (decomposer plugin config)
- No `projects:` wrapper, no `path`, no `name`, no `sessionPrefix`

**Stale fields to remove from `$defs/projectConfig`:**
- `storageKey` — auto-generated, not user-facing
- `originUrl` — now lives inside the structured `repo` object

**`notificationRouting`:**
- JSON schema hardcodes urgency keys; Zod uses generic `z.record(z.array(z.string()))`

## Source of truth
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — `OrchestratorConfigSchema` (legacy single-file)
- `packages/core/src/global-config.ts` — `GlobalConfigSchema` + `LocalProjectConfigSchema` (new hybrid)
- `packages/core/src/config-generator.ts` — `CONFIG_SCHEMA_URL` points at the JSON schema

title: feat: add config hot-reload via c12
body:
## Summary

Integrates [`c12`](https://github.com/unjs/c12) (the closest Node.js equivalent to Go's Viper) for YAML config file watching and hot-reload, addressing [#1767](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1767).

### What Changed

- **New: `ConfigWatcher` class** (`packages/core/src/config-watcher.ts`) — wraps c12's `watchConfig()` to provide ergonomic config hot-reload with validation
- **Unchanged: `loadConfig()`** — the existing synchronous config loader remains untouched. No breaking changes.
- **Integration: CLI start command** — watcher starts after initial config load, stops on graceful shutdown
- **Safety: validate-before-apply** — reloaded config is validated with the existing Zod schemas. Invalid config is rejected, last-known-good config is kept.

### Config Reload Classification

| Section | Hot-reloadable? | Notes |
|---------|----------------|-------|
| `defaults` (runtime, agent, workspace) | ✅ | New sessions pick up changes |
| `notifiers` | ✅ | Notification routing updates live |
| `reactions` | ✅ | Reaction rules update immediately |
| `dashboard` | ✅ | Dashboard settings refresh |
| `projects.*` (labels, settings) | ⚠️ | New projects visible, running sessions unaffected |
| `projects.*.agent` (model) | ❌ | Requires session restart |
| `plugins` | ❌ | Plugin loading only at startup |

### Usage

No user action required. Config changes to `agent-orchestrator.yaml` are picked up automatically while AO is running.

### Testing

- `pnpm build` passes
- `pnpm typecheck` passes (all 28 packages)
- All 1176 existing tests pass
- No public API changes to existing functions

### Research

Package comparison: [#1767 (comment)](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1767#issuecomment-4413625644)

Closes #1767

title: Web dashboard `posix_spawnp failed` on macOS when `ignore-scripts=true` (PR #638/#1086 postinstall bypassed by Socket Firewall, pnpm 10, etc.)
body:
## Summary

The web dashboard's terminal pane is permanently blank on macOS arm64 because `node-pty@1.1.0`'s prebuild ships `spawn-helper` with mode `0644`. AO already addresses this via two postinstall fixes (PR #638, PR #1086), but **both run only when `npm`/`pnpm` permits lifecycle scripts**. In `ignore-scripts=true` environments — increasingly the default — those fixes are silently neutralized and users hit the same `posix_spawnp failed` symptom that #624 and #987 fixed.

This is not a duplicate of #624/#987; it's the gap their fixes don't cover.

## Symptom

Dashboard tab at `localhost:<port>/projects/<proj>/sessions/<session>` shows the session as `CONNECTED` but the terminal pane never paints. Browser console:

```
[MuxProvider] Terminal error for <session>: posix_spawnp failed.
```

`tmux capture-pane -p -t <session>` confirms the underlying tmux session is healthy and rendered. CLI works fine — only `MuxServer`'s per-tab pty spawn breaks.

## Why the existing fixes don't fire

PR #638 added `packages/ao/bin/postinstall.js` (chmod spawn-helper to `0755`) and PR #1086 extended it to rebuild `node-pty` via `node-gyp` if the prebuild's ABI is wrong. Both are gated by the user's package manager actually running lifecycle scripts.

The reality on a security-conscious 2026 macOS dev machine:

| Tool | Default behavior |
|---|---|
| pnpm 10+ | `--ignore-scripts` is **default** (security hardening since pnpm 10) |
| [Socket Firewall](https://socket.dev) (`sfw npm` shim) | Forces `ignore-scripts=true` to neutralize malicious postinstall vectors |
| `npm config set ignore-scripts true` | Common in shared dev orgs and CI |
| `npm install --ignore-scripts` | Recommended in security guides |
| Renovate / Dependabot bots | Run with scripts disabled by default |

In any of these, `npm install -g @aoagents/ao` lands a working binary tree but skips AO's own remediation, leaving `node-pty/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/spawn-helper` at `0644`. The dashboard then breaks at first WS connect. There is no in-product surface for the failure — only the browser DevTools console mentions it.

## Verified repro on AO 0.6.0

```bash
# Confirm the broken bit on a fresh install:
HELPER=$(find ~ -path '*node-pty/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/spawn-helper' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)
ls -la "$HELPER"
# -rw-r--r-- (mode 0644)

# Confirm it fails to spawn:
node -e 'require("node-pty").spawn("tmux",["-V"],{name:"xterm-256color",cols:80,rows:24,env:process.env});'
# Error: posix_spawnp failed.
#     at new UnixTerminal (node-pty/lib/unixTerminal.js:92:24)

# Confirm the postinstall didn't run (ignore-scripts):
npm config get ignore-scripts
# true   <-- (or via Socket Firewall, pnpm 10 defaults, etc.)

# Manual fix:
chmod +x "$HELPER"
# Refresh dashboard tab — MuxServer reads the helper on each spawn, no ao restart needed.
```

The npm tarball mode is verifiable straight from the registry (no install needed):

```bash
curl -sL "$(npm view node-pty@1.1.0 dist.tarball)" | tar tvz | grep spawn-helper
# -rw-r--r-- ...spawn-helper       <-- 0644 in the published artifact
```

## Upstream context

- microsoft/node-pty#850 — original report (closed)
- microsoft/node-pty#858 / #866 — fix merged (sets 0755 on prebuild spawn-helper at publish time)
- microsoft/node-pty#919 — **open**: requests a `1.1.1` patch release that backports the fix to the `latest` dist-tag. The fix is currently only on `beta` (`1.2.0-beta.12`).

So upstream has a fix; it's stuck on the `beta` channel pending a release-management decision. AO's existing postinstall fixes are a correct workaround for that gap — they just need to survive `ignore-scripts=true` environments.

## Proposed fix

Options A and D are complementary — A is the invisible safety net (fixes silently on first spawn), D is the discoverable check users can run on demand and that surfaces the diagnosis when something is already broken. Pairing them gives you both "it just works" and "I can audit why."

### Option A — Runtime self-heal in `MuxServer.open()` (most robust)

`packages/web/dist-server/mux-websocket.js` already pty-spawns `tmux attach-session`. On `posix_spawnp` failure, do a one-time best-effort `chmod 0o755` on the helper and retry once before giving up:

```ts
// pseudocode at the spawn site
try {
  return ptySpawn(this.TMUX, args, options);
} catch (err) {
  if (err.message?.includes("posix_spawnp") && !this.spawnHelperRepaired) {
    this.spawnHelperRepaired = true;
    const helper = path.join(
      path.dirname(require.resolve("node-pty/package.json")),
      "prebuilds", `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`, "spawn-helper"
    );
    try { fs.chmodSync(helper, 0o755); } catch {}
    return ptySpawn(this.TMUX, args, options);   // retry once
  }
  throw err;
}
```

This survives any install-time policy because it runs in the daemon process at first use. It's also safe — the chmod targets a file inside AO's own `node_modules` tree, not anywhere user-owned.

### Option D — `ao doctor` check with `--fix` auto-remediation

`ao doctor` is already the user's first stop when something is off, and its output already supports a `FIXED` result class (`Results: N PASS, N WARN, N FAIL, N FIXED`). Adding a check is purely additive and reuses the existing remediation pattern.

The check would walk the same path AO's postinstall already knows (`node-pty` resolved via the walk-up resolver from PR #638, then `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/spawn-helper`) and verify the executable bit:

```ts
// pseudocode for the doctor check
const helperPath = resolveSpawnHelperPath();   // reuse PR #638's walker
if (!helperPath) return { status: "skip", reason: "no spawn-helper for this platform" };

const mode = fs.statSync(helperPath).mode;
if (mode & 0o111) {
  return { status: "PASS", message: `node-pty spawn-helper is executable (${helperPath})` };
}

if (opts.fix) {
  fs.chmodSync(helperPath, 0o755);
  return { status: "FIXED", message: `chmod +x on ${helperPath} (was 0o${(mode & 0o777).toString(8)})` };
}

return {
  status: "WARN",
  message: `node-pty spawn-helper is not executable (mode 0o${(mode & 0o777).toString(8)})`,
  remedy: "Web dashboard terminals will fail with `posix_spawnp failed`. Run `ao doctor --fix` or `chmod +x " + helperPath + "` to repair. See ao#1770.",
};
```

### Option B — Pin `node-pty` to `^1.2.0-beta.12`

The published beta has the fix baked into the tarball, so no postinstall or runtime chmod is needed regardless of script policy:

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": {
    "node-pty": "1.2.0-beta.12"
  }
}
```

Trade-off: opting into a `beta` channel for a stable release. Mitigated by the fact that the diff between 1.1.0 and 1.2.0-beta.12 is small and predominantly the spawn-helper packaging fix (per the changelog).

### Option C — Document the failure mode prominently

If neither A nor B is desirable, at minimum surface the failure in-product. Right now a new user with a security-hardened npm hits a blank dashboard with no actionable error anywhere except DevTools. A check at `MuxServer` boot — `if (!fs.statSync(helper).mode & 0o111) console.error("...")` — could log a clear remediation line to the daemon's stdout that `ao` users would actually see.

## Why this matters

The web dashboard is the primary UX in onboarding screenshots and docs. macOS users with pnpm 10, Socket Firewall, or any common security-hardened npm setup hit a silent blank pane on first run. The CLI works, so users don't realize the dashboard is broken until they try to use it — by which point they've already followed setup docs that show working terminal panes. Adding a runtime self-heal closes the only remaining failure mode for this regression.

Happy to send a PR for Option A or Option D (or both — they're complementary, not alternatives).

## Environment

- AO: `0.6.0` (`ao --version`)
- Node: `v24.15.0` (via fnm)
- macOS arm64
- npm wrapped by Socket Firewall (`npm` is a shell function `sfw npm "$@"`); `npm config get ignore-scripts` returns `true`
- Runtime: `tmux` (the only macOS-reliable runtime per AO docs)
- Manual `chmod +x ...spawn-helper` resolves the symptom; verified by smoke-test (`node -e 'pty.spawn("tmux", ...)'` succeeds)

title: feat(doctor): check node-pty spawn-helper exec bit + auto-fix
body:
## Summary

Adds an `ao doctor` check + `--fix` auto-remediation for the long-standing **node-pty `spawn-helper` missing exec bit** issue (`posix_spawnp failed`). Closes part of #1770.

This is the "Option D" pairing from #1770 — a discoverable, auditable, idempotent fix that lives where users already look when something seems off, and that survives every install-policy variant (Socket Firewall, pnpm 10's default `--ignore-scripts`, manual `npm config set ignore-scripts true`, Renovate / Dependabot bots, etc.) where the existing postinstall remediation in #638 / #1086 is silently skipped.

## What changed

**`packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-doctor.sh`**

- New `find_package_up()` helper — bash mirror of `findPackageUp()` from `packages/ao/bin/postinstall.js`, walks up `node_modules/<pkg>` directories from `REPO_ROOT`. Same algorithm so the doctor inspects the same `node-pty` copy the postinstall would have repaired.
- New `check_node_pty_spawn_helper()` — locates `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/spawn-helper`, then:
  - **PASS** when executable.
  - **WARN** with remediation hint when not executable and `--fix` is not set. Mentions both `ao doctor --fix` and the manual `chmod 0755 <path>`, plus a pointer to upstream microsoft/node-pty#919.
  - **FIXED** when not executable and `--fix` is set — `chmod 0755` and report. Falls through to **FAIL** if chmod itself fails (read-only filesystem, permission denied, etc.).
  - Silent skip on Windows (uses ConPTY, no spawn-helper binary), when `node-pty` is not installed (e.g. configurations that disable the web surface), or when no prebuild exists for the current platform-arch (separate concern, tracked in #489).
- Wired into the call list after `check_runtime_sanity`, so all install-layout sanity is verified first.

**`packages/cli/__tests__/scripts/doctor-script.test.ts`**

Three new tests using the existing fake-repo / fake-PATH harness:

- `warns about a non-executable node-pty spawn-helper` — sets up a 0o644 helper, runs without `--fix`, expects WARN, and verifies the file is still 0o644 afterwards (no silent mutation).
- `repairs a non-executable node-pty spawn-helper in --fix mode` — same setup, runs with `--fix`, expects FIXED, and verifies the file now has the exec bit set.
- `passes when node-pty spawn-helper is already executable` — sets up a 0o755 helper, expects PASS and asserts no WARN/FAIL on the node-pty line.

## Why a runtime check, not just an upgraded postinstall

Both PR #638 (chmod) and PR #1086 (`node-gyp rebuild` fallback) live in `packages/ao/bin/postinstall.js`. Postinstall scripts increasingly fail closed in 2026:

- **pnpm 10+** — `--ignore-scripts` is the default
- **Socket Firewall (`sfw npm`)** — forces `ignore-scripts=true` to neutralize supply-chain attack vectors
- **`npm config set ignore-scripts true`** — common in shared dev orgs and CI
- **`npm install --ignore-scripts`** — recommended in security guides
- **Dependabot / Renovate** — run with scripts disabled by default

In any of these, AO's existing remediation never runs and users hit a blank dashboard terminal panel with no in-product error (the `posix_spawnp failed` message is only visible in browser DevTools). A doctor check is the natural next layer because:

1. **Users already run `ao doctor` when something is wrong** — discoverable.
2. **`FIXED` is auditable** — the chmod is reported, not silent.
3. **Reuses existing infrastructure** — the `pass`/`warn`/`fail`/`fixed` reporters and the `--fix` flag in the bash script work out of the box.
4. **Strictly additive** — runs after install-layout checks, doesn't touch hot paths.

This is complementary to (not a replacement for) the existing postinstall — when scripts run, the postinstall fixes things proactively; when they don't, the doctor diagnoses + fixes on demand.

## Test plan

```bash
# Unit tests (added)
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli exec vitest run __tests__/scripts/doctor-script.test.ts

# Manual: simulate the user-facing failure
INSTALL=$(npm root -g)/@aoagents/ao
HELPER=$(find $INSTALL -path '*node-pty/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/spawn-helper' -print -quit)
chmod -x "$HELPER"
ao doctor                # expect: WARN node-pty spawn-helper is not executable (...)
ao doctor --fix          # expect: FIXED node-pty spawn-helper made executable: ...
ls -la "$HELPER"         # confirm exec bit set
```

Tested locally on macOS arm64 / Node 24.15.0 / `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`. All 7 tests in `doctor-script.test.ts` pass (4 existing + 3 new).

## Related

- Closes part of #1770 (Option D)
- Complements #638 (postinstall chmod), #1086 (node-gyp rebuild fallback)
- Upstream context: microsoft/node-pty#850 (closed, original report), microsoft/node-pty#858 + microsoft/node-pty#866 (merged fixes), **microsoft/node-pty#919 (open)** — release-management ask for a 1.1.1 patch that backports the fix to the `latest` dist-tag

title: Windows worktree setup can fail with spawn git ENOENT
body:
## Problem

Running AO from some Windows environments could fail during worktree setup with:

`Failed to setup orchestrator: spawn git ENOENT`

This showed up when running:

`ao start`

The failure happened even on machines where Git was installed.

## Why It Happened

The worktree plugin invoked Git as a bare executable name (`git`) via `child_process.execFile`. That works when Git is available on the inherited `PATH`, but Windows shells launched from GUI apps or constrained environments can have a degraded `PATH` that includes Node but not Git.

In that state, Node could start AO, but the worktree plugin could not spawn Git, so setup failed with a raw `ENOENT` instead of finding the installed Git binary or explaining the missing dependency clearly.

## Impact

First-run and orchestrator startup flows that depend on the worktree workspace plugin could fail before creating or attaching worktrees. This was especially likely on Windows, but the fix needed to remain safe for macOS and Linux too.

## Fix in PR #1776

PR #1776 centralized Git executable resolution in `@aoagents/ao-core` with `getGitExecutable()`:

- Search `PATH` first, preserving normal behavior.
- Fall back to common Git install locations on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Cache the resolved Git executable to avoid repeated filesystem probes.
- Use the resolved executable in the workspace-worktree plugin.
- Improve the error message if Git still cannot be found.
- Add platform-mocked tests for Windows/macOS/Linux fallback behavior.

title: fix(cli): preserve sessions across ao stop → ao update → ao start (closes #1743)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1743.

The `ao stop` → `ao update` → `ao start` flow was silently dropping the restore prompt because `last-stop.json` could be missing from disk by the time `ao start` checked for it. Three layered fixes harden the path:

### Root cause

`ao stop` (and the SIGTERM shutdown handler in `lib/shutdown.ts`) only wrote `last-stop.json` AFTER finishing the kill loop. If the CLI was killed mid-shutdown — SIGKILL, hard crash, or an impatient re-run — the record was never written and `ao start` had nothing to restore.

The atomic write also went through `writeFileSync` + `renameSync` without an explicit `fsync`, so a hard kill that landed immediately after the call could lose the file's data even though the rename had committed the dirent.

### Fix

1. **Pre-write before kill, with fsync.** `ao stop` and the shutdown handler now write `last-stop.json` with every active session id BEFORE running the kill loop, then reconcile (rewrite or `clearLastStop`) once the loop's actual results are known. The new `atomicWriteFileSyncDurable` calls `fsyncSync` on the temp file before `renameSync`, so the bytes are durable even if the process is killed milliseconds later.
2. **Fallback in `ao start`.** When `last-stop.json` is missing or empty, scan recently `manually_killed` sessions (terminated within the last 10 minutes) via `findRecentlyKilledSessions` and synthesize a `LastStopState`. The restore prompt fires with the same wording as the existing record. This protects against future regressions in the write pipeline.
3. **Regression test that `ao update` does NOT touch `last-stop.json`.** The current `ao update` command never reads or writes anything under `~/.agent-orchestrator/`, but adding state-clearing logic in the future would re-introduce the bug. The new test stages a `last-stop.json` in a temp `HOME` and asserts it is byte-for-byte identical after `ao update` runs.

### Before vs. after of the file-write timing

```
Before:                                     After:
sm.list()                                   sm.list()
filter active sessions                      filter active sessions
for s in active: kill(s) ─┐                 writeLastStop(active)        ◄── pre-write, fsync'd
write last-stop.json      │                 for s in active: kill(s) ─┐
killProcessTree(parent) ◄─┘ races with      reconcile last-stop.json  │
                            shutdown.ts     killProcessTree(parent) ◄─┘
```

If the CLI is killed between `kill(s)` and `write last-stop.json` in the old order, the record vanishes. The new order moves the durable write before any teardown work.

## Tests added

- `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/last-stop-fallback.test.ts` (5) — unit tests for `buildLastStopFallback`: window respect, primary vs other-project routing, missing/unparseable timestamps, custom window
- `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/stop-update-start-flow.test.ts` (2) — hermetic stop → simulated update → start flow against a temp HOME, plus fallback path
- `writeLastStop fsyncs the temp file before renaming` in `running-state.test.ts`
- `does not touch ~/.agent-orchestrator/last-stop.json` in `update.test.ts`
- `pre-writes last-stop.json before the kill loop runs` in `start.test.ts`
- `clears last-stop.json when every kill fails` in `start.test.ts`
- `falls back to recently manually-killed sessions when last-stop.json is missing` in `start.test.ts`
- `does not surface fallback candidates older than the recent window` in `start.test.ts`

`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` pass. `pnpm test` shows the same 10 pre-existing failures on this branch as on `main`; my 7 new test cases all pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` no errors (warnings only, all pre-existing)
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run lib/last-stop-fallback lib/stop-update-start-flow lib/running-state` — all green
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run commands/start.test.ts -t "issue #1743|every kill fails"` — 4 pass
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run commands/update.test.ts` — 26 pass (including new regression)
- [ ] Manual: `ao stop` → `ao update` → `ao start` on a checkout with active sessions reproduces the restore prompt

title: feat(release): weekly release train — channels, onboarding, dashboard banner, cron
body:
## Summary

Implements the full release pipeline described in [`release-process.html`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/release-process.html). Combines what would otherwise be five separate PRs into one cohesive landing.

**Supersedes #1525** — incorporates that PR's release infrastructure (canary + release workflows, changeset config, publishConfig on every package) with the cron / no-stale-SHA-guard / no-merged-PR-comment modifications called out in the design doc.

## Sections (mapped to the design doc)

### A. Cron tweaks + release infrastructure
- `.github/workflows/canary.yml` — `cron: '30 17 * * 5,6,0,1,2'` (23:00 IST Fri–Tue) plus `workflow_dispatch`. **No** stale-SHA guard (cron uses `ref: main`); **no** merged-PR-comment step (no merged-PR context from cron).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — `changesets/action` opens a "version packages" PR; merging it publishes `@latest`.
- `.changeset/config.json` — adds `snapshot.prereleaseTemplate: '{tag}-{commit}'`, includes all currently-shipped plugins in the linked group. **`@aoagents/ao-web` stays in the linked group** so its version bumps in lockstep with `@aoagents/ao-cli` (which has a `workspace:*` runtime dep on it via `findWebDir`). The `ignore[]` array contains only `@aoagents/ao-integration-tests`.
- `packages/web/package.json` gains `publishConfig: { access: "public", provenance: true }` plus full metadata (license, repository, homepage, bugs) so it can be published cleanly via `changesets/action`. **It is NOT private** — making it private would 404 every `npm install -g @aoagents/ao` after publish (pnpm rewrites `workspace:*` to the literal published version on release).
- All other publishable packages get `publishConfig: { access: "public", provenance: true }` too.
- New `scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs` walks every publishable package and fails CI if any of them has a `workspace:*` runtime dep on a `private: true` package. Wired into both `release.yml` and `canary.yml` before the publish step so the install-404 class of bug is caught at CI, not at the user's `npm install`.

### B. Channel awareness — `packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts`
- New `updateChannel` field in `GlobalConfigSchema` (`stable | nightly | manual`, default `manual`). Schema is `.optional().catch(undefined)` so legacy / typo'd values don't break config load.
- `fetchLatestVersion(channel)` now reads `dist-tags[channel]` from the registry (full package doc, not the per-tag URL) and falls back to `latest` if `nightly` isn't published yet.
- `isVersionOutdated` compares prerelease segments — numeric segments compare numerically (`rc.1 < rc.2`); **differing non-numeric segments treat current as older** (SHAs are random hex, so lexical compare would misfire ~50% of the time on `nightly-<sha>` tags, and the cache always carries the registry's current dist-tag so any non-numeric mismatch on the same base means we're behind by construction).
- `maybeShowUpdateNotice` and `scheduleBackgroundRefresh` skip entirely on `manual` so opted-out users see no traffic and no nudges.
- Cache file gains a `channel` field; entries from a different channel are ignored. **Legacy entries without a `channel` field are treated as misses** when an explicit channel is provided in the lookup, so a stable→nightly switch doesn't keep returning the pre-switch latestVersion until the 24h TTL expires.

### C. Active-session guard — `packages/cli/src/commands/update.ts`
- `ensureNoActiveSessions()` runs before any install. **Always** loads from the canonical global registry (not project-local), so sessions in OTHER registered projects fire the guard even when `ao update` is invoked from one specific project's cwd. Refuses with `N session(s) active. Run `ao stop` first.` if any are in `working`/`idle`/`needs_input`/`stuck`. Never auto-stops.
- Same guard duplicated in `POST /api/update` so the dashboard returns a structured `409 { activeSessions, message }`.

### D. Onboarding question + `ao config set`
- `packages/cli/src/lib/update-channel-onboarding.ts` — prompts once on first `ao start`. Ask-once gate keyed on the absence of `updateChannel` in the global config; dismissal persists `manual` so we don't re-ask.
- `ao config set updateChannel <stable|nightly|manual>` — also handles `installMethod`. New `packages/cli/src/commands/config.ts`.
- `runStartup` calls `maybePromptForUpdateChannel()` after preflight.
- Channel switches (stable↔nightly) detected via `previousChannel !== activeChannel && !info.isOutdated`; force an explicit confirm prompt with default=no, regardless of soft-install setting.

### E. Dashboard banner
- `GET /api/version` (`packages/web/src/app/api/version/route.ts`) reads the same cache file the CLI writes (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/ao/update-check.json`). Cache-only; never makes a network call inside a request handler. **Git-install special case:** `latestVersion` is `origin/main` for git users (a ref, not semver), so the route trusts the cached `isOutdated` flag for `installMethod === "git"` rather than running `isVersionOutdated` on a ref.
- `POST /api/update` (`packages/web/src/app/api/update/route.ts`) runs the active-session guard, then spawns `ao update` detached with `shell: isWindows()` + `windowsHide: true` so `ao.cmd` resolves on Windows (PATHEXT only consulted under a shell).
- `UpdateBanner.tsx` — top-of-page strip wired into `Dashboard.tsx`. Visible only when `isOutdated`. Click POSTs to `/api/update`. Dismissal persists per-version in `localStorage` and works from any phase (including 409 / error). Tailwind only, `var(--color-*)` tokens, no inline styles. Mount fetch runs synchronously (no `setTimeout`); brittle Dashboard tests now use URL-routed `mockImplementation`.

### F. Bun + Homebrew detection
- `classifyInstallPath` adds `/Cellar/ao/` (homebrew, notice-only — `brew upgrade ao`, never auto-install because brew owns the symlinks) and `~/.bun/install/global/` (auto-installs `bun add -g @aoagents/ao@<channel>`). Cellar check runs first because brew nests the npm tree under `lib/node_modules/`.
- `runNpmInstall` spawns with `shell: isWindows()` + `windowsHide: true` so PATHEXT resolves `npm.cmd` / `pnpm.cmd` / `bun.cmd` on Windows installs.
- New `installMethod` global-config field overrides path detection for users with custom prefixes.

### Shared layer in core
- `packages/core/src/version-compare.ts` — `isVersionOutdated` lives here so the CLI and the dashboard share one tested implementation.
- `packages/core/src/update-cache.ts` — `getUpdateCheckCachePath`, `readUpdateCheckCacheRaw`, `getInstalledAoVersion`. The CLI's `update-check.ts` keeps its richer install-method/channel/git-rev validation on top.
- `packages/core/src/global-config.ts` — `createDefaultGlobalConfig` exported so `persistUpdateChannel` and `ao config set` share one defaults block (uses `getDefaultRuntime()` so Windows users don't get `runtime: "tmux"` locked in).

## Test plan

New tests added (~190 total across CLI + core + web, all green):

- [x] `version-compare.test.ts` (core, canonical) — numeric ordering, prerelease vs stable, SHA-suffix non-numeric difference treated as outdated, numeric < non-numeric.
- [x] `update-check.test.ts` — channel resolution, prerelease compare, `dist-tags` fetch, channel-mismatched cache, **legacy-no-channel cache treated as miss**, manual-channel skip, bun/homebrew classifiers, `installMethod` override, channel-aware `getUpdateCommand`.
- [x] `update.test.ts` — active-session guard (refuse on working/idle/needs_input/stuck, allow terminal statuses), **multi-project proof (sessions from proj-a AND proj-b both appear in refusal output)**, soft auto-install (skip prompt on stable/nightly, prompt on manual), homebrew notice-only, channel-switch prompt, git-only flag rejection on non-git installs, Windows `shell: true` spawn.
- [x] `update-channel-onboarding.test.ts` — ask-once gate, dismissal persists `manual`, no re-prompt after persistence.
- [x] `version-update-api.test.ts` — channel-aware cache reading, channel-mismatched entries ignored, git-install `cached.isOutdated` trusted, 409 active-session refusal, 202 happy path.
- [x] `UpdateBanner.test.tsx` — hides on up-to-date, hides on `manual`, hides when dismissed for current latest, re-appears for new version, POST + 409 surface, dismiss-from-blocked-phase works.

CI:
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean (0 errors)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 706 passed / 4 pre-existing env-dependent failures unchanged from `main`.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 900 passed / 2 pre-existing `projects-route` failures unchanged from `main`.
- [x] `node scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs` — passes; verified it correctly fails when ao-web is hypothetically marked private.
- [x] `pnpm changeset version` dry-run on temp branch — `@aoagents/ao-web`, `@aoagents/ao-cli`, and `@aoagents/ao` all bump to `0.7.0` together via the linked group.

## Manual verification needed

The release workflows themselves can only be exercised by merging — the cron schedule won't trigger from a feature branch and the release environment requires `NPM_TOKEN`. The dashboard banner can be exercised locally by writing a stub cache file:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.cache/ao && cat > ~/.cache/ao/update-check.json <<JSON
{"latestVersion":"99.0.0","checkedAt":"$(date -Iseconds)","currentVersionAtCheck":"$(node -p "require('@aoagents/ao/package.json').version")","installMethod":"npm-global","channel":"stable"}
JSON
ao config set updateChannel stable
ao start
```

Closes #1525

title: feat: enable workers to message the orchestrator via `ao send` (inject AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID)
body:
## Problem

Worker sessions can already be messaged by the orchestrator (`ao send <worker> "<msg>"`), but the **reverse direction** — worker → orchestrator — is undiscoverable today.

`ao send` already routes a message to any session in the same project (`packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts:114-195` → `sessionManager.send` → `runtimePlugin.sendMessage`), and the orchestrator's session ID is deterministic (`${sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`, see `session-manager.ts:421,434,1490`). So the *transport* exists. What's missing is that workers don't know their orchestrator's session ID — agent plugins only inject `AO_SESSION_ID` and `AO_ISSUE_ID` into the worker env (`agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:923,932` and equivalents in codex/opencode/aider/cursor/kimicode).

This means a worker that wants to escalate a blocker, ask a cross-session question, or hand off context to the orchestrator has no clean way to do it.

## Proposal

Smallest viable change — no new transport, no new file format, no new CLI verb:

1. **Add `orchestratorSessionId?: string` to `AgentLaunchConfig`** (`packages/core/src/types.ts:549`).
2. **Populate it in `spawnWorker`** (`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` ~1284-1300) by computing `${project.sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`. Do **not** populate for `spawnOrchestrator` — the orchestrator is not its own parent.
3. **Inject `AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` env var** in each agent plugin's `getEnvironment()` when the config field is present. Plugins to update: `agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-opencode`, `agent-aider`, `agent-cursor`, `agent-kimicode`.
4. **Update worker prompt preamble** in `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` to teach workers the channel exists, when to use it, and how to identify themselves.

## Worker prompt addition (proposed)

```markdown
## Talking to the orchestrator

You can message the orchestrator session with:
`ao send $AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID "<message>"`

Only do this when you genuinely cannot proceed alone — cross-session
coordination, a decision only the human-facing orchestrator can make,
or a blocker outside your repo's scope. Do NOT ping for things you can
resolve yourself (research, retries, normal CI/review fixes go through
`ao report` and the existing flow).

Always include your session ID in the message body — the orchestrator
receives your text as raw input with no `from:` metadata and won't
otherwise know who's writing:
`ao send $AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID "[from $AO_SESSION_ID] blocker: ..."`
```

## Why this and not alternatives

| Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Inject env var + reuse `ao send`** (this proposal) | XS change, zero new code paths, works day one |
| New `ao tell-orchestrator` wrapper command | Pure sugar over `ao send $AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` — not worth the verb |
| File-based inbox at `.ao/inbox/...` polled by orchestrator | New polling loop + new file format + orchestrator must learn to read it |
| New notifier slot routed back into a session | Misuses outbound-only contract, couples notifier to runtime |
| SSE/WebSocket backchannel via dashboard | Doesn't work for headless orchestrators |

## Compatibility

`tmux send-keys` works for every receiver — Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider, Codex, Cursor, Kimi all accept typed input into their TUI. So this works regardless of which agent the orchestrator runs.

## Out of scope (for follow-ups if real usage demands)

- Structured request/response (worker awaiting typed reply)
- Priority/queue semantics
- Audit log of inter-session messages
- A `from:` metadata channel so workers don't have to identify themselves in the body

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AgentLaunchConfig.orchestratorSessionId` exists and is populated in `spawnWorker` only
- [ ] All six agent plugins inject `AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` when the config field is set
- [ ] `BASE_AGENT_PROMPT` (and `BASE_AGENT_PROMPT_NO_REPO`) include the new section
- [ ] Tests in each agent plugin assert the env var is set when config provides it, and absent otherwise
- [ ] Tests assert workers get the env var but orchestrators do not

title: feat: enable worker→orchestrator dialogue via `ao send` with auto-sender prefix
body:
Closes #1786.

## Summary

Workers can already be messaged by the orchestrator (`ao send <worker> "<msg>"`); this PR closes the reverse direction. Two complementary changes:

1. **Literal-render the orchestrator's session ID into the worker's system prompt.** When an orchestrator session exists for the project, `prompt-builder` emits a "Talking to the Orchestrator" section with the bare command — no env var, no shell-syntax variants:
   ```
   ao send my-orchestrator "<your message>"
   ```
   The orchestrator session ID is deterministic (`${sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`) and known at prompt-build time, so the prompt just renders it.

2. **`ao send` auto-prefixes outgoing messages with `[from $AO_SESSION_ID]`** when invoked from inside an AO session. The receiver always knows who's writing, regardless of direction (worker→orchestrator, orchestrator→worker, worker→worker). Humans running `ao send` from their own terminal stay unprefixed.

The PR didn't need to touch any agent plugin or `AgentLaunchConfig` — the dialogue lives entirely in the prompt + `ao send` infrastructure.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts`** — `PromptBuildConfig` gains an optional `orchestratorSessionId`. When set, `buildPrompt` emits a new section between the base prompt and the project context with the literal `ao send <id> "<your message>"` example.
- **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`** — at the `buildPrompt` call site, computes `${project.sessionPrefix}-orchestrator` and passes it through only when its metadata exists on disk (i.e., the orchestrator workflow is in play for this project). Ad-hoc `ao spawn` workers in projects without an orchestrator never see the section.
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts`** — wraps the message with `[from ${process.env.AO_SESSION_ID}] …` when the env var is set. Six lines.
- **Tests:** prompt-builder asserts literal render and conditional omission; `send` test gains auto-prefix coverage (set / unset / via SessionManager) plus an `AO_SESSION_ID` reset in `beforeEach` so tests run cleanly inside AO sessions.

## Why this shape and not alternatives

| Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Literal render in prompt + auto-prefix in `ao send`** (this PR) | Smallest diff, no plugin touched, no shell footgun, sender identity is automatic |
| Inject `AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` env var across 6 plugins | Wider surface area; needs three shell-syntax variants in the prompt (POSIX `$X`, PowerShell `$env:X`, cmd.exe `%X%`); agent has to remember to self-identify |
| New `ao tell-orchestrator` wrapper command | Sugar over `ao send <id>` — not worth a new verb |
| File-based inbox at `.ao/inbox/...` polled by orchestrator | New polling loop + new file format + orchestrator must learn to read it |
| Notifier slot routed back into a session | Misuses outbound-only contract |
| SSE/WebSocket backchannel via dashboard | Doesn't work for headless orchestrators |

`tmux send-keys` works for every receiver — Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider, Codex, Cursor, Kimi all accept typed input — so this works regardless of which agent the orchestrator runs.

## Compatibility

- Workers spawned today without an orchestrator (`ao spawn` directly): unchanged — no section in their prompt.
- Humans running `ao send` from their terminal: unchanged — no `AO_SESSION_ID` so no prefix added.
- Existing scripts that manually prefix `[from foo]` from inside an AO session: get a double prefix `[from $session] [from foo] …`. Redundant but not broken; downstream parsers can read the first as authoritative.
- No `AgentLaunchConfig` field added or removed externally — wider plugin ecosystem unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (50 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] `pnpm test` — touched packages green: core 1179/1179, cli `send` 16/16 (3 new), claude-code 170/170, codex 197/197, opencode 93/93, aider 51/51, cursor 63/63, kimicode 103/103. Pre-existing failures in `tracker-linear` (missing `@composio/core` peer dep) and `cli/start` are confirmed present on `upstream/main` and unrelated to this PR.

## Out of scope (follow-ups if real usage demands)

- Structured request/response (worker awaiting a typed reply)
- Priority/queue semantics
- Audit log of inter-session messages
- A `--from <id>` flag on `ao send` for the dashboard route to set when a human triggers the send via the UI

title: feat(core): support PR handoff history
body:
## Problem

`ao session claim-pr` could attach a new PR to an existing session, but the handoff was lossy: replacing the primary PR erased the previous PR from session metadata, and bare PR numbers were always resolved against the configured project repo. That makes it awkward to recover from closed/replaced PRs or to claim follow-up PRs that live in a different repo.

Closes #1618.

## What changed

- Added `repoOverride` to `claimPR(...)` so callers can resolve a bare PR number against an explicit `owner/repo`.
- Infer the repository from full GitHub/GitLab-style PR URLs before resolving the PR.
- Preserve the replaced primary PR in `prHistory` metadata when a session claims a different PR.
- Return `previousPr` from `claimPR(...)` and show it in `ao session claim-pr` output.
- Added CLI support:
  - `ao session claim-pr 42 app-1 --repo owner/repo`
  - `ao spawn --claim-pr 42 --claim-pr-repo owner/repo`
- Updated the orchestrator prompt and CLI docs so the new handoff options are discoverable.

## Why this approach

The existing single active `pr` metadata field remains the source of truth for lifecycle polling, status derivation, and dashboard behavior. `prHistory` is only a bounded historical trail of replaced primary PRs, so this avoids changing the active PR model while giving users and maintainers the auditability needed for explicit handoffs.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- session-manager/claim-pr`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- commands/session commands/spawn`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core build && pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck`

I also ran `pnpm test`. It reached the CLI suite and failed on the existing environment-sensitive `canonicalCompareKey > expands ~ to HOME` assertion because macOS resolved the temp HOME as `/private/var/...` while the test expected `/var/...`. The feature-specific suites above passed.

title: docs(mobile): V1 design doc for mobile access via Cloudflare Tunnel
body:
## Summary

- Adds [`docs/mobile-access-v1.html`](docs/mobile-access-v1.html) — a self-contained, dark-mode-friendly design doc for adding phone access to AO without Tailscale.
- Design replaces OpenCode's user-chosen-password-over-plain-HTTP posture with a generated 128-bit token delivered via URL fragment, exchanged for an HMAC-signed HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict cookie session over a Cloudflare Tunnel.
- Implementation work is tracked across [#1760](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1760)–[#1765](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1765); this PR is the spec only, no runtime code changes.

## Why this exists

The doc captures every load-bearing decision after three Codex passes and one `/plan-eng-review`:

- **Split Edge/Node cookie verifiers** so the Edge middleware bundle is provably `fs`-free (`verifyCookieEdge` does signature + expiry only, `verifyCookieFull` adds revocation).
- **HMAC key delivery to Edge runtime** via `process.env.AO_MOBILE_COOKIE_KEY` injected at dashboard boot from `mobile.json`.
- **File-mediated revocation** with a single process-wide 60s scanner — no IPC between the `ao mobile revoke` CLI process and the dashboard. Doc states the ~60s window honestly instead of claiming "immediate."
- **`mobile-runtime.ts` as a process-local owner** of `liveSockets` and the scanner timer; `mobile.json` is the source of truth across processes.
- **Persisted HMAC key in `mobile.json`** so phone sessions survive `ao stop && ao start --mobile` and only `ao mobile revoke` kills them.
- **No LAN mode in V1** — Codex flagged binding `0.0.0.0` as the worst attack surface; tunnel-only is non-negotiable.
- **Audit log, cloudflared checksum verify, and `ao mobile install` deferred to V1.5** per the eng-review scope reduction.

## What a reviewer should know

- **No code changes.** Only `docs/mobile-access-v1.html` (962 lines, single self-contained file). Open it in a browser to read.
- **Threat model is explicit about what V1 doesn't defend against**: phishing the tunnel URL, malicious browser extension on the phone reading the URL fragment before JS exchange, compromised host machine, the fail-closed lockout being used as a remote DoS lever.
- **Honest revoke window**: live WebSocket connections close within ~60s after `ao mobile revoke`; new HTTP/WS requests are blocked instantly. Tightening below 60s would require an admin endpoint or Unix socket from CLI to dashboard — out of scope for V1.
- **Implementation guidance** is unusually specific (code sketches for the WS upgrade gate, login route, cookie verifiers) because the design went through enough review iterations to lock those down. The implementation issues reference the doc's section names directly.
- **Dependency chain** for the linked issues: `#1760 → #1761 → #1762 → #1763 → #1764 → #1765`. Most lanes can't safely run in parallel because each replaces a piece of the prior tracer; the doc covers why.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open [`docs/mobile-access-v1.html`](docs/mobile-access-v1.html) in a browser; verify dark/light mode renders cleanly and SVG diagrams are legible.
- [ ] Verify the doc's claims match the linked issues (#1760–#1765) — section names referenced in each issue should resolve.
- [ ] No runtime tests apply; this is spec-only.
