title: fix(lifecycle): re-verify CI/conflict state before dispatching alerts
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1122. Lifecycle reactions were firing 'CI is failing' and 'merge conflicts' alerts against the cached batch-enrichment snapshot, telling workers to take destructive actions (rebase + force-push, 'fix the failing CI') on PRs whose conditions had already been resolved.

- Added dispatch-time re-verification: before firing a CI-failure or merge-conflict alert, call `getCIChecks()` / `getMergeability()` and skip when the condition has cleared. These methods aren't populated by the batch GraphQL path, so they return fresh truth even within the same poll cycle. Verification failures fail open — a flaky API call never swallows a real failure.
- Added `headSha` to `PREnrichmentData`, populated by `extractPREnrichment`, and threaded it into the dispatched message as a 'verified at SHA X' anchor so workers can detect rare staleness slip-throughs and the orchestrator's log has a falsifiable record.
- Updated 2 existing merge-conflict tests to mock `getMergeability` for the new re-verification path; added 3 new tests covering CI suppression, conflict suppression, and SHA annotation.

title: bug(agent-plugins): `ps` timeout conflated with "process not found" — bulk-terminates all sessions when `ps` exceeds 5s
body:
## Bug

Agent plugin `isProcessRunning` implementations conflate **"the probe could not determine the answer"** with **"the process is definitively not there."** A single `ps` invocation that exceeds the 5-second timeout cascades into ALL active sessions being marked `state: terminated / reason: runtime_lost` in a single `sm.list()` pass — typically within a few milliseconds of each other, across every project.

This is the **deterministic mechanism** behind the bulk-termination patterns reported in:

- #1454 — "terminated sessions never revive when probes later disagree"
- #1743 (linked comment chain) — "sessions terminated after stop/start, no restore prompt"
- #1831, #1832 — downstream symptoms (restore leaves stale terminatedAt, dashboard renders Exited from terminatedAt)

This issue isolates **the upstream root cause**.

**Source:** live reproduction this evening on @i-trytoohard's machine
**Reported by:** @i-trytoohard
**Date:** 2026-05-13
**Analyzed against:** `ee2f4256` (origin/main HEAD)
**Confidence:** High — directly reproduced via timing measurements on the affected machine.

## Root cause

`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts::findClaudeProcess` (and the analogous `findCodexProcess` in `agent-codex`):

```ts
const psOut = await getCachedProcessList();
if (!psOut) return null;                            // <-- conflates ALL ps failures
                                                    //     with "process is gone"
```

…where `getCachedProcessList` runs:

```ts
const promise = execFileAsync("ps", ["-eo", "pid,tty,args"], {
  timeout: 5_000,
}).then(...);
```

When `ps` exceeds 5s, `execFileAsync` rejects. The rejected promise propagates up; the outer `try/catch` in `findClaudeProcess` swallows it and returns `null`. The lifecycle manager interprets `isProcessRunning() === false` as a definitive "runtime is gone" verdict and writes `state: terminated, reason: runtime_lost`.

This collapses **three semantically-different cases** into one verdict:

| Case | What it means | What AO should do | What AO does today |
|------|---------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| (A) `ps` succeeds, regex matches | Process is alive | Mark alive | ✅ alive |
| (B) `ps` succeeds, regex misses | Process is genuinely not there | Mark dead | ✅ dead |
| (C) `ps` fails (timeout, ENOENT, fork failure) | Probe could not determine | **Skip; don't write a verdict** | ❌ marks dead |

(C) is the bug. Same applies to `tmux list-panes` failures (also wrapped in the same try/catch).

## Reproduction (verbatim from a live debug session)

`ps -eo pid,tty,args` on my machine, measured in a tight loop:

```
  iter 1: 14199.3ms    ← exceeds 5s timeout
  iter 2: 11063.4ms    ← exceeds 5s timeout
  iter 3:  7551.6ms    ← exceeds 5s timeout
  iter 4:  1883.4ms
  iter 5:   207.6ms
```

`ps` time varies wildly (200ms to 14s) on this host because of process-table size and macOS `kinfo_proc` contention. **Every iteration that exceeds 5s** causes a bulk-termination event in AO.

A 30-minute probe-monitor I ran in parallel (replicating AO's exact regex per session) captured several outliers where ps_ms exceeded 5000:

```
... 5046, 5115, 5233, 5336, 5399, 5432, 5464, 5486, 5540, 5619, 5700, 5824, 5972, 6003,
    6189, 6201, 6204, 6345, 6406, 6511, 6559, 6682, 6802, 6941, 6946,
    7286, 7349, 7544, 7547, 7637, 7667, 7698,
    8557 ...
```

In the daemon's view (one example, captured live tonight):

- At **2026-05-13T20:21:09.956 → 20:21:09.960Z** (4-millisecond window), 15 sessions across 3 projects (`ao-180`, `ao-183`, `ao-184`, `ao-185`, `ao-186`, `ao-187`, `mer-17`, `mer-18`, `mer-20`, `mer-23`, `mer-24`, `mer-25`, `mer-orchestrator`, `ao-orchestrator`-related, `int-3` slightly later) were written `state: terminated / reason: runtime_lost`.
- All 15 sessions had **tmux alive + pane pid running** at the time and after.
- This is a single `sm.list()` invocation iterating sessions sharing the same rejected `getCachedProcessList()` promise.

## Why this is high priority

- It silently terminates active work across every project.
- The failure mode is bursty and tied to system load (process count, fd pressure, zombie/orphan processes — see #1234 and the long-orphan `codex-startup-factory` discussion). Any user with a busy machine is vulnerable.
- It cascades into the downstream issues #1831 (stale `terminatedAt`), #1832 (UI renders Exited), and #1454 (no revival). Fixing this upstream stops the bleeding for all three.

## Suggested fix (smallest viable)

### A. Distinguish probe outcomes in the agent plugin

Change `isProcessRunning` to return a tri-state — or, more pragmatically, throw on "could not determine" so the lifecycle manager can branch:

```ts
async isProcessRunning(handle): Promise<boolean> {
  // ... existing logic ...
  if (psFailed || tmuxFailed) {
    throw new Error("probe_indeterminate");          // <-- new signal
  }
  // ... existing return ...
}
```

In the lifecycle manager (`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`):

```ts
try {
  const alive = await agent.isProcessRunning(handle);
  // ...
} catch (err) {
  if (err.message === "probe_indeterminate") {
    // Don't write runtime_lost. Skip this session in this pass.
    // Optionally: log to observability.
    continue;
  }
  // existing error handling
}
```

### B. Bump the `ps` timeout

The 5s default is too aggressive for macOS hosts with non-trivial process counts. Raise to **30s** (matches the existing 30s timeout already used for the **codex** plugin's `tmux list-panes` call). Single-line per plugin (claude-code, codex, aider, opencode).

### C. Don't bulk-fail in `sm.list()`

If the shared `getCachedProcessList()` rejects, the *cache itself* should be marked indeterminate, and ALL per-session probes in that pass should also return "indeterminate" rather than each independently deciding "dead." Currently the cache is positive-only — extend to also remember "last call failed" as a distinct state and propagate that to callers.

### D. Defense-in-depth (separate issues already open)

- #1454 — make reconciliation bidirectional so a single bad probe isn't permanent.
- #1831 — clear `terminatedAt` on restore.
- #1832 — UI keys off `state`, not `terminatedAt`.

A through C together close THIS bug; D through F close the downstream consequences.

## Reproduction harness for testers

Run on any macOS host with many active sessions / processes:

```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  start=$(python3 -c 'import time; print(time.time()*1000)')
  ps -eo pid,tty,args > /dev/null
  end=$(python3 -c 'import time; print(time.time()*1000)')
  python3 -c "print(f'iter $i: {${end} - ${start}:.1f}ms')"
done
```

If any iteration exceeds 5000ms, AO's `findClaudeProcess` (and `findCodexProcess`) would currently terminate every session in the next poll cycle. The fix should make these timeouts inert.

## Related

- #1234 — Session kill leaks PTY resources / orphan processes (contributes to high `ps` cost).
- #1454 — terminated sessions never revive.
- #1743 — stop/start leaves sessions terminated.
- #1831 / #1832 — downstream UI / restore-data corruption from this issue.

title: fix(agent-plugins,lifecycle): distinguish indeterminate probe from "not found" + bump ps timeout (closes #1838)
body:
Closes #1838.

## Summary
- Adds a tri-state agent process probe model via `ProcessProbeResult = boolean | "indeterminate"` on the core `Agent.isProcessRunning` interface.
- Updates claude-code, codex, aider, and opencode agents so:
  - `ps` OK + regex match → `true` (alive)
  - `ps` OK + regex miss → `false` (dead)
  - `ps`/`tmux` failure or empty process-list output → `"indeterminate"` (no verdict)
- Extends claude-code's shared `ps` cache to cache failed process-list probes as `indeterminate`, so every per-session probe sharing that pass gets the same no-verdict result instead of independently collapsing to dead.
- Raises the claude-code `ps` and `tmux list-panes` timeouts from 5s to 30s; the other three affected plugins were already at 30s for their `ps` probes on current `main`.
- Makes lifecycle/session-manager callers treat indeterminate as a no-op verdict: do not write `runtime_lost`, do not mutate persisted lifecycle metadata, and do not restore/terminate based on that single failed probe.
- Updates integration tests to compare explicitly against `true`/`false` so `"indeterminate"` is never treated as truthy liveness.

## Before / after for the repro
Before: one slow or failed shared `ps -eo pid,tty,args` call was swallowed as `null`/`false`, so a single `sm.list()` pass could persist `state: terminated / reason: runtime_lost` across all active sessions.

After: the same slow/failed `ps` call returns `"indeterminate"`; lifecycle and list enrichment skip the write for that pass and leave existing runtime/session lifecycle metadata untouched.

## Version bump rationale
Ran `pnpm changeset version` after adding a minor changeset for the affected packages. Because this repo links package versions in `.changeset/config.json`, the release train package versions moved from `0.7.0` to `0.8.0`; the affected core/agent package versions and changelogs are included for install verification.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts src/__tests__/session-manager/query.test.ts` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex test` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-aider test` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-opencode test` ✅

title: bug(web,core): test suite breaks on Node 25 — localStorage.clear() missing + lifecycle-manager undefined function references
body:
## Bug

Two test-suite failures occur when running on Node.js 25.x. Both cause \`pnpm test\` to exit non-zero and block CI.

**Source:** observed while running full CI suite locally on Node 25.8.0
**Date:** 2026-05-14
**Analyzed against:** \`ee2f4256\` (origin/main HEAD)
**Confidence:** High — both failures are deterministically reproducible and root causes are identifiable from stack traces.

---

### Failure 1 — web tests: \`window.localStorage.clear is not a function\`

All 8 tests in \`UpdateBanner.test.tsx\` fail with:

```
TypeError: window.localStorage.clear is not a function
  ❯ src/components/__tests__/UpdateBanner.test.tsx:25:25
```

**Root cause:** Node 25 introduces a native \`localStorage\` global (via \`--localstorage-file\`) that takes precedence over jsdom's implementation. When no \`--localstorage-file\` path is configured (the default in vitest), Node 25 installs a stub that exposes \`getItem\`/\`setItem\`/\`removeItem\` but omits \`clear()\`, \`key()\`, and \`length\`. The test's \`beforeEach\` block calls \`window.localStorage.clear()\`, which throws.

Node also emits the warning:

```
Warning: '--localstorage-file' was provided without a valid path
```

This confirms the native stub is active and shadowing jsdom's fully-compliant implementation.

**Affected file:** \`packages/web/src/__tests__/setup.ts\`

**Fix:** add an in-memory \`localStorage\` mock to the vitest setup file that unconditionally replaces \`window.localStorage\` with a spec-compliant object before any test runs. jsdom on Node ≤ 22 already provides this — the mock is only exercised on Node 25+ but is harmless on older versions.

```
const localStorageMock = (() => {
  let store: Record<string, string> = {};
  return {
    getItem: (k: string) => store[k] ?? null,
    setItem: (k: string, v: string) => { store[k] = String(v); },
    removeItem: (k: string) => { delete store[k]; },
    clear: () => { store = {}; },
    get length() { return Object.keys(store).length; },
    key: (i: number) => Object.keys(store)[i] ?? null,
  };
})();
Object.defineProperty(window, "localStorage", { value: localStorageMock, writable: true });
```

---

### Failure 2 — core tests: \`ReferenceError: syncBoardLabelsOnTransition is not defined\`

68 core tests fail at runtime when \`checkSession\` executes in \`lifecycle-manager.ts\`:

```
ReferenceError: syncBoardLabelsOnTransition is not defined
  ❯ checkSession src/lifecycle-manager.ts:2412:7
```

A second reference to \`createFixCardOnCIFailure\` at line 2422 would also throw.

**Root cause:** both functions (`syncBoardLabelsOnTransition` and `createFixCardOnCIFailure`) are called in `checkSession` but are not defined anywhere in the module. TypeScript confirms this — `tsc --noEmit` reports `TS2304: Cannot find name 'syncBoardLabelsOnTransition'` and `TS2304: Cannot find name 'createFixCardOnCIFailure'`. The calls exist without implementations, making the lifecycle manager throw on every status transition.

**Affected file:** `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` (lines 2412 and 2422)

**Fix:** remove the two call sites (and surrounding comment blocks) since the referenced functions do not exist.

---

## Files

`packages/web/src/__tests__/setup.ts` (localStorage mock missing for Node 25)
`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` (undefined function calls on lines 2412, 2422)

title: CLI tests leak ghost projects into ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml
body:
## Symptom

The dashboard project list shows ghost projects with names like:

- `ao-start-test-B0Kakf`
- `ao-start-test-0hyh9q`
- `ao-start-test-fCFbIe`

Each renders with `0` sessions and "No sessions shown". The tmp dirs no longer exist on disk — only the global config entries remain.

## Root Cause

`autoCreateConfig` in `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:575-586` unconditionally calls `registerProjectInGlobalConfig(...)`. The global config path resolves via `packages/core/src/global-config.ts:87-98`:

`AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG` → `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`

The Vitest in `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/start.test.ts:2225-2273` calls `autoCreateConfig(tmpDir)` directly but **does not set `AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG`** — so the write lands in the real user file. Every other suite in the same file (lines 2167, 2339, 2410, 2828) sets `process.env["AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG"] = join(tmpDir, "...yaml")` to sandbox the write. The `autoCreateConfig` describe block is the only one missing that guard.

`afterEach` at `start.test.ts:437-441` removes `tmpDir` but does not revert the global-config mutation, so each test run leaks one entry.

## When This Started

Introduced by PR #1766 / commit `d95c9def` ("fix(cli): first-run startup creates global config with project registered"), which added the `registerProjectInGlobalConfig` call to `autoCreateConfig`. Anyone running `pnpm --filter cli test` since that merged is leaking entries.

## Reproduction

```bash
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test start.test.ts
yq '.projects | keys' ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml | grep ao-start-test
```

Each test run adds a fresh `ao-start-test-XXXXXX_<hash>` entry with `source: local`, `path: /var/folders/.../T/ao-start-test-XXXXXX`, `displayName: ao-start-test-XXXXXX`.

## Cleanup (existing leaks)

```
ao project rm <projectId>
```

…for each `ao-start-test-*` key in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`.

## Fix Direction

1. **Primary fix:** wrap the `autoCreateConfig` describe block in `start.test.ts` with a `beforeEach`/`afterEach` that sets `process.env.AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG = join(tmpDir, "global.yaml")`. Matches the pattern used by every other suite in the file. One-line fix per test.
2. **Defense in depth:** in the top-level `beforeEach` of `start.test.ts`, default `AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG` to a per-test tmp path so future tests can't leak by omission. Restore in `afterEach`.

## Affects

- Every contributor running the CLI test suite locally
- CI hosts (throwaway, no user-visible symptom)

title: fix(web): add localStorage mock for Node 25 compatibility in vitest setup
body:
Fixes #1840

## What

Node.js 25 introduces a native \`localStorage\` global (via \`--localstorage-file\`) that shadows jsdom's implementation. When no file path is configured (the vitest default), Node 25 installs a stub that exposes \`getItem\`/\`setItem\`/\`removeItem\` but omits \`clear()\`, \`key()\`, and \`length\`. This makes all 8 tests in \`UpdateBanner.test.tsx\` fail with:

\`\`\`
TypeError: window.localStorage.clear is not a function
\`\`\`

Node 25 also emits the warning \`'--localstorage-file' was provided without a valid path\`, confirming the native stub is active.

## Fix

Add a complete in-memory \`localStorage\` implementation to \`packages/web/src/__tests__/setup.ts\` that unconditionally replaces \`window.localStorage\` before any test runs. The mock is spec-compliant (implements \`getItem\`, \`setItem\`, \`removeItem\`, \`clear\`, \`key\`, and \`length\`). It is harmless on Node \<= 22 where jsdom already provides a correct implementation.

## Test plan

title: test(cli): sandbox AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG in start.test.ts to stop ghost project leak
body:
## Summary

Closes #1841.

Stops the CLI test suite from leaking `ao-start-test-XXXXXX` entries into the contributor's real `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`. The leaks were surfacing in the dashboard sidebar as ghost projects with 0 sessions.

## Root cause

The `autoCreateConfig` describe block in `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/start.test.ts:2225-2273` calls `autoCreateConfig(tmpDir)` directly but never sets `AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG`. Once PR #1766 (`d95c9def`) added `registerProjectInGlobalConfig` to `autoCreateConfig` (`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:575-586`), every local run of the CLI test suite started writing a fresh `ao-start-test-XXXXXX_<hash>` entry into the real global config. `afterEach` removed `tmpDir` but never reverted the global-config mutation, so entries accumulated — one per test run.

Every other suite in `start.test.ts` (lines 2167, 2339, 2410, 2828) already redirects `AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG` into `tmpDir`. The `autoCreateConfig` suite was the only one missing that guard.

## Fix

Lift `AO_GLOBAL_CONFIG` sandboxing into the top-level `beforeEach`/`afterEach` of `start.test.ts` so that any future test which (intentionally or accidentally) reaches `registerProjectInGlobalConfig` writes into a `tmpDir`-scoped file instead of the real home dir. Per-suite overrides still work — they save/restore against this value.

This matches the spirit of CLAUDE.md's "fix the core first" principle: the test file's setup contract should make leaks structurally impossible, not rely on every test author remembering to add the guard.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` — passes
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- start.test.ts` — 71 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] `pnpm lint` — no new warnings/errors
- [x] Manual: `grep -c ao-start-test ~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` returns the same count before and after running the test suite (no new leaks)

## Cleanup for existing leaks

Run for each `ao-start-test-*` key in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`:

```
ao project rm <projectId>
```

title: perf(web): ProjectSidebar re-renders on every SSE tick even when session data is unchanged
body:
## Problem

The project sidebar re-renders every 5 seconds regardless of whether any session data changed. The SSE polling loop delivers a new array reference on every tick, which causes \`sessionsByProject\` to recompute and all session rows to re-render even when nothing has changed. On dashboards with many active sessions this produces continuous layout thrash and makes sidebar interactions feel laggy.

## Root Cause

Three compounding issues in \`packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx\`:

**1. Unstable memo dependency**
\`sessionsByProject\` lists the \`sessions\` array reference as a dependency. The SSE hook always produces a new array reference every poll cycle, so the memo fires on every tick even when content is identical.

**2. No row-level memoization**
Session rows are rendered inline. Every \`sessionsByProject\` recompute re-renders all rows, even those whose props did not change.

**3. \`SessionDot\` not memoized**
The colored status indicator sub-component re-renders on every cycle with no memo boundary.

## Fix

**sessionsKey + sessionsRef pattern**
Replace the direct \`sessions\` reference in the memo dependency array with a \`sessionsKey\` string derived from each session's \`id\`, \`status\`, \`activity\`, and \`projectId\`. A \`sessionsRef\` holds the latest value so the memo can read sessions without depending on the unstable reference. The memo only fires when content actually changes.

**Memoized SessionRow component**
Extract per-row JSX into a \`SessionRow\` component wrapped in \`React.memo()\`. Rows only re-render when their own props change. \`navigate\` and \`startRename\` callbacks are stabilised with \`useCallback\`.

**Memoized SessionDot component**
Wrap \`SessionDot\` in \`React.memo()\` so it skips re-renders when its \`level\` prop is unchanged.

## Expected Result

A quiet 5-second SSE tick with no session state changes touches zero React components in the sidebar. Rows update only when a session actually transitions.

## Files

\`packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx\`

## Verification

29 ProjectSidebar unit tests pass. TypeScript typecheck passes across all packages.

title: feat(artifacts): right-rail artifacts v1 — markdown + html (supersedes #1653)
body:
## Summary

Adds a right-rail surface on the session detail page that renders structured agent output as cards. Two renderer types in v1: `markdown` (in-app, no HTML pass-through) and `html` (sandboxed iframe, null origin). Agents publish via a staged-file ingest pipeline or the new `ao artifact publish` CLI. Live updates flow over the existing Mux WebSocket.

Supersedes #1653.

**User-facing docs:** [`docs/artifacts.md`](https://github.com/harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator/blob/harshit/artifacts/v1/docs/artifacts.md)

## Why artifacts exist

Today, when an AO agent emits anything structured — test results, a plan, a code-review summary, cost numbers — it scrolls past in the terminal and the supervisor loses it. The richer the output, the worse it gets. Artifacts give that output a persistent, scannable home.

For the **supervisor** (the human watching N parallel agents): glance at the rail and see exactly what each agent is doing. No terminal scrolling, no lost context.

For the **agent**: present rich output without polluting the conversation surface. The terminal stays clean for chat; artifacts hold everything else.

For the **platform**: a general-purpose rendering surface that future features can plug into without core changes. Plugin synthesizers in v0.2, renderer plugins in v0.4. The marginal cost of new artifact-emitting features drops from ~500 LOC to ~50 LOC each because the pipeline already exists.

### Concrete uses

**Live in this PR:**
- `core-agent-status` — auto-rendered every time the agent runs `ao acknowledge` / `ao report <state>`. Shows current state, latest note, PR info, and the last 20 reports as a markdown history. One card per session, updates in place via the Mux push channel. Agent gets this for free; no extra code on their side.

**Near-future producers** (each becomes ~50 LOC once this PR lands):
| Source | What it emits | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `core-git-diff` (Jules-style follow-up) | HTML diff of working tree vs base | See your session's changes without `git diff` in the terminal |
| `scm-github` plugin producer | PR status (state, CI, reviews) | PR state visible without leaving the session page |
| `agent-claude-code` cost producer | Token usage + $ per session | "How much did this session cost?" answered at a glance |
| `tracker-*` plugin producer | Linked issues, blockers | What tickets this work is attached to |
| Shell hooks (`post-test.sh`, etc.) | `vitest` → stats card; lint → table | Agent doesn't even need to know about artifacts; the hook does it |

### What artifacts are NOT for

- **Not a replacement for chat.** Per Codex / Claude-app pattern: questions get answered in the chat input, not on artifact buttons. Artifacts are display, not input. (Interactive artifacts deferred to post-v0.4 with their own consent / CSRF / auth-scope model.)
- **Not real-time log streaming.** Mux cadence is fine for state changes; not for `tail -f`.
- **Not long-running progress bars.** Use the activity state for that.
- **Not for confidential data.** Storage is workspace-adjacent but unencrypted — same trust model as session metadata.

## What's in it

- **Two renderer types.**
  - `markdown` — rendered in-app via `marked`. No HTML pass-through (XSS-safe by construction).
  - `html` — rendered inside `<iframe sandbox=\"allow-scripts\">` *without* `allow-same-origin` → null origin. The iframe can't read parent auth tokens, call dashboard APIs, or touch parent DOM. Even if an agent is prompt-injected and emits malicious HTML, the blast radius is bounded. `color-scheme: dark` set in the srcdoc so the iframe matches AO's aesthetic. `postMessage` size-bridge keeps the iframe sized to its content.
- **Staged-file ingest pipeline.** Agent writes JSON to `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/{projectId}/artifacts/{sessionId}/.staging/{id}.json` — adjacent to the workspace, NOT inside the worktree. A chokidar watcher in the daemon validates against the Zod schema, stamps server-side metadata (`createdAt` preserved across updates, `updatedAt` always now, `source: \"agent\"`, `version: 1`), and atomically moves the file to canonical. Validation failures get an `.error` sidecar next to the staging file. Per-artifact size cap: 256 KB. Per-session count cap: 32 (oldest by `updatedAt` evicted). `lstat` not `stat` so symlinks can't bypass the cap.
- **Auto-rendered agent status** (`core-agent-status`). Hooked into `ao acknowledge` and `ao report`. Reads the full audit trail and renders the latest report + last 20-entry history as a markdown card. Uses the reserved `core-` id prefix so agents can't shadow it via staging.
- **CLI wrapper.** `ao artifact publish --type markdown|html --id ... --title ... --content-file ...` for agents that prefer command-line over direct file write. Polls for the `.error` sidecar for up to 2s so validation errors surface synchronously.
- **Push channel via Mux.** Extends the existing Mux WebSocket protocol with `artifact-update` / `artifact-error` / `artifact-delete` events. `MuxProvider` subscribes to `[\"sessions\", \"artifacts\"]` on every connection. `ArtifactBroadcaster` on the server starts the watcher eagerly at boot so staging files always ingest even with no dashboard tab open. Dashboard live-updates without page reload.
- **Resizable, collapsible right rail.** Mounted in `SessionDetail` side-by-side with the terminal. 1px draggable splitter (width persists to `localStorage`, bounds 240px–65% viewport). Rail itself collapsible via a `›` button — when collapsed, a 24px `‹` handle at the terminal's right edge brings it back. Per-card collapse via a `▾`/`▸` button (state persists per artifact id). Per-card reorder via `▲`/`▼` buttons (order persists per session). All UI state survives page reload.

## Architectural commitments

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Agent integration | Staged-file ingest with CLI wrapper | AO controls metadata; agent keeps file-write ergonomics. Resolves Prateek's \"we control the interface\" feedback. |
| Storage location | `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/{id}/artifacts/{sessionId}/` — adjacent to workspace | Worktree stays clean, no git pollution. Prateek's \"workspace adjacent, not inside\" requirement. |
| Renderer types | `markdown` + `html` only | Per Ashish: \"keep it light + extensible for other people.\" Anything more opinionated (diff, table, stats, prompt) is plugin territory (post-v0.4). |
| HTML safety | Sandboxed iframe, null origin | Agent prompt-injection blast radius bounded. No sanitizer arms race. |
| Push channel | Extend existing Mux (no new poll loop) | One transport, one subscribe path. Reuses `useSessionEvents` reducer. |
| Auto-status artifact | Written by core after `ao acknowledge` / `ao report` | Every session gets useful rail content for free, no agent change required. |

## What's NOT in v1 (deferred explicitly)

- **Interactive artifacts.** Prototyped and removed. Per Codex / Claude-app pattern: chat input is the universal answer surface.
- **`core-git-diff` synthesizer.** Was wired via `diff2html` but the rendering didn't match AO's design language. Jules-style diff viewer is a follow-up PR with its own design conversation.
- **Plugin renderer slot.** Lets third parties ship custom artifact types (flame graphs, Gantt charts, etc.). v0.4 territory. Not blocked by this PR.
- **Plugin producers** (`ArtifactProducer.listArtifacts`). v0.2. Interface is NOT declared in this PR — added when it ships.
- **Mobile rendering.** Rail mounted only when `!isMobile`. Mobile gets bottom-sheet / full-screen in a follow-up.

## File map

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| Core | `artifact-schema.ts`, `artifact-store.ts`, `artifact-ingest.ts`, `artifact-watcher.ts`, `artifact-delivery.ts` (just `sendMessageToSession` — used by `ao send`), `agent-status-artifact.ts`, `paths.ts` additions |
| Web API | `GET /api/sessions/[id]/artifacts` |
| Web push | `mux-protocol.ts` event types, `useSessionEvents.ts` reducer branches, `useArtifacts.ts` hook, `useArtifactUiState.ts` (collapse/order state), `MuxProvider` `subscribeArtifacts` plumbing |
| Web UI | `ArtifactRail`, `ArtifactMarkdown`, `ArtifactHtml`, `ArtifactRailSplitter`, `ArtifactCardControls`, `SessionDetail` mount |
| Server | `ArtifactBroadcaster` wired into `mux-websocket.ts` boot |
| CLI | `ao artifact publish` command, `send.ts` uses the extracted delivery helper, `report.ts` writes the agent-status card |
| Core base prompt | Added \"## Artifacts\" section so every agent knows it can publish |
| Docs | `docs/artifacts.md`, changeset entry |

## Test plan

- [x] Core: 1239/1239 tests passing — schemas, store atomic writes, ingest pipeline, watcher (including explicit Windows path tests), delivery helper, broadcaster lifecycle.
- [x] Web: 942/942 tests passing (+ 4 skipped). GET artifacts route, mux reducer branches, `useArtifacts` hook (REST + mux subscription), all renderers including the sandbox attribute assertion (`allow-scripts` present, `allow-same-origin` absent).
- [x] Integration: 204/204 tests passing. Watcher → ingest happy path. Real chokidar, real fs, real Zod validation.
- [x] CLI: `ao artifact publish` for markdown and html, validation error surface via `.error` sidecar polling.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm build` — green.
- [x] Manual: published markdown and html artifacts against a live AO daemon. Watcher ingested within ~50ms. Cards rendered in the rail. HTML iframe rendered against AO's dark theme. Splitter drag and rail/card collapse persist across reload. Live updates appear without page refresh. `ao report` updates the agent-status card live with full history.

## Migration / breaking changes

None. Net-additive. New storage location with no existing data to migrate. New schema. New CLI subcommand.

## Pre-existing failures (not introduced)

Confirmed against `ee2f4256` baseline (current `main` at branch time):

- `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-linear` — 50 tests fail (missing `@composio/core` dep)
- `packages/cli __tests__/commands/start.test.ts` — 8 tests fail in `stop command` describe
- `packages/cli __tests__/lib/path-equality.test.ts` — 1 test fails (macOS `/private` symlink)

title: bug(cli): `ao stop` and SIGINT leak child processes (next-server, websocket servers, lifecycle-workers) — they survive as PPID=1 orphans
body:
## Bug

`ao stop` (and `Ctrl+C` on the `ao start` foreground process) **fail to kill the daemon'"'"'s child processes**. Each successive stop/start cycle leaves orphaned processes parented to init (PPID=1). They hold open file descriptors, TCP connections, and (historically) listening sockets — and persist for **days to weeks** until manually `kill`ed.

This is a **regression / broader recurrence** of [#645](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/645) (closed 2026-04-14 with a specific dashboard-on-reassigned-port scenario). The pattern now affects more child types than the original report.

**Source:** live observation immediately after `ao stop` tonight
**Reported by:** @i-trytoohard
**Date:** 2026-05-14
**Analyzed against:** `ee2f4256` (origin/main HEAD) + locally hot-swapped 0.8.0 dist from PR #1839
**AO version:** 0.7.0 globally installed, 0.8.0 dist hot-swapped (the orphan bug is independent of the swap)
**Confidence:** High — fresh repro, every kill cycle produces fresh orphans.

## Live repro just now

After running `ao stop` on the running daemon (pid 90236), an immediate `ps`-based sweep:

```console
$ ps -axo pid,ppid,etime,command | awk '$2==1' | grep -iE 'aoagents|/ao |lifecycle-worker'
90350     1   56:27  node next-server (v15.5.15)
```

Details on the orphan:

```console
$ lsof -nP -p 90350 | grep -E 'TCP|LISTEN'
node 90350 ... TCP [::1]:3001->[::1]:49879 (ESTABLISHED)
node 90350 ... TCP [::1]:3001->[::1]:49863 (ESTABLISHED)
node 90350 ... TCP [::1]:3001->[::1]:49873 (ESTABLISHED)

$ lsof -nP -p 90350 | wc -l
100
```

(LISTEN was released — but client-half connections survive until they hit RST/FIN; 100 fds still held.)

## Wider symptom space — orphans found earlier today

Same machine, same root cause. Before tonight'"'"'s ao stop, sweeping the machine turned up these long-term zombies that survived previous `ao stop` cycles weeks ago:

```
pid    ppid age            command
9914   1    28d 08h 55m    node /opt/homebrew/bin/ao lifecycle-worker codex-startup-factory
58454  1    27d 11h 16m    node /opt/homebrew/bin/ao lifecycle-worker integrator
47457  1    36d 01h 41m    node @aoagents/ao-web@0.2.4 dist-server/start-all.js
47575  1    36d 01h 41m    node @aoagents/ao-web@0.2.4 dist-server/terminal-websocket.js
47580  1    36d 01h 41m    node @aoagents/ao-web@0.2.4 dist-server/direct-terminal-ws.js
73117  1    35d 21h 04m    node @aoagents/ao-web@0.2.4 dist-server/terminal-websocket.js
73122  1    35d 21h 04m    node @aoagents/ao-web@0.2.4 dist-server/direct-terminal-ws.js
```

Every one of those was created by a prior `ao start`, abandoned by a subsequent `ao stop`, and reparented to init. **None** had been cleaned up — they were just accumulating until I `kill`ed them by hand earlier today.

The leaked categories are:
1. **`next-server` (Next.js dashboard)** — the original #645 case, still happening.
2. **`terminal-websocket.js` / `direct-terminal-ws.js`** — older `@aoagents/ao-web@0.2.4` server-side processes that ran on a per-port basis (current 0.5.0+ merged into mux but the pattern survives anywhere a server child is spawned).
3. **`lifecycle-worker` (per-project)** — e.g. `codex-startup-factory`, `integrator` — these are long-running supervisor children that should die with the parent.

## Root cause (per #645'"'"'s body, still accurate)

In `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` (and wherever else children get spawned), child processes are launched with `detached: false` but the parent process has **no SIGINT/SIGTERM/exit handler that explicitly kills them**. Node.js does not guarantee signal propagation from a parent to its children — when bash sends SIGTERM to `ao start`, Node simply exits; the kernel reparents the children to init.

`ao stop` separately reaches out to the running daemon via its written PID and sends SIGTERM. The daemon process dies, but if it has no handler that *itself* signals its children before exit, the same orphan-to-init reparenting happens.

The proposed fix in #645'"'"'s body is correct as a minimum:

```ts
process.on("SIGINT", () => {
  dashboardProcess?.kill("SIGTERM");
  // also: websocketProcesses?.forEach(p => p.kill("SIGTERM"));
  // also: lifecycleWorkers?.forEach(p => p.kill("SIGTERM"));
});
process.on("SIGTERM", () => { ... });
process.on("exit", () => { ... });
```

…but needs to cover **every** child the daemon spawns, including:
- The dashboard / next-server child.
- Any websocket server children (current architecture or any historical variants users may still have on PATH).
- Each per-project `lifecycle-worker` process.
- Any one-shot helper subprocesses (e.g. `caffeinate`, postinstall builders) — these are usually fine but worth a sweep.

A more robust pattern, beyond just adding signal handlers: when the daemon starts a long-running child, record its PID into a known per-daemon registry file. `ao stop` reads that registry and explicitly kills each PID with a grace timeout + SIGKILL fallback. Belt-and-suspenders to the in-process signal handlers, and works even when the daemon crashed without unwinding.

## Suggested fix scope

### A. In-process signal handlers (matches #645'"'"'s body)

For every child the daemon spawns, register SIGINT/SIGTERM/exit handlers that propagate the kill. Specifically in:
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` — dashboard child.
- The lifecycle-worker spawning code (wherever per-project supervisors are forked).
- Any websocket server children.

### B. Child PID registry + sweep on `ao stop` (new — belt-and-suspenders)

Maintain `~/.agent-orchestrator/daemon-children.json` (or similar) that records every child PID + role + start time. `ao stop` reads it, sends SIGTERM to each, waits 5s, then SIGKILL stragglers. Also clears the registry. This covers the case where the daemon itself died unexpectedly (no signal handler ran).

### C. Sweep on `ao start` (new — recover from prior crashes)

On startup, scan for any PPID=1 process whose command line matches AO patterns (`@aoagents/ao-web`, `ao lifecycle-worker`, etc.) AND that has no corresponding registered project / daemon. Offer to kill them with a `--reap-orphans` flag or interactive prompt. Without this, machines accumulate orphans indefinitely.

### D. Tests

Integration test: `ao start`, capture child PIDs, `ao stop`, assert all captured PIDs are gone within N seconds.

## Reproduction harness for testers

```bash
ao start &
sleep 5
ao_pid=$(jq -r .pid ~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json)
child_pids=$(pgrep -P $ao_pid)
ao stop
sleep 3
still_alive=$(for p in $child_pids; do kill -0 $p 2>/dev/null && echo $p; done)
[ -z "$still_alive" ] && echo "PASS — no orphans" || echo "FAIL — orphans: $still_alive"
```

## Related

- **#645** — Closed predecessor with the same fix proposal. This issue documents the regression + wider scope.
- **#1129** — `ao stop` doesn'"'"'t kill child *agent* sessions (tmux worker panes). Same `ao stop` cleanup gap on a different child category.
- **#1234** — PTY resource leaks on session kill. Adjacent — same root cause: AO doesn'"'"'t track + reap all the processes it spawns.
- **#1743** — `ao stop → ao update → ao start` leaves sessions terminated. Different symptom but same `ao stop` reliability gap.
- **#1838** — slow `ps` cascades partly caused by the *bloated process table* this bug creates. Closing #1838'"'"'s issue is harder when this one keeps inflating the process count.

## Impact

- Orphans accumulate indefinitely across stop/start cycles.
- File descriptor pressure builds up over weeks (we measured the now-killed orphans holding 100+ fds each).
- `ps` slows down (contributes to #1838 cascades).
- Old port bindings can survive and conflict with new `ao start` (#645'"'"'s original symptom).
- Confusing UX: users believe `ao stop` is clean when it isn'"'"'t.

## Concrete cleanup commands (one-shot, while waiting for the fix)

For anyone hitting this today:

```bash
# Find AO-related PPID=1 orphans
ps -axo pid,ppid,etime,command | awk '$2==1' | grep -iE 'aoagents|/ao |lifecycle-worker|ao-web'

# Then kill each PID it lists
```

title: fix(cli): reap daemon children on stop+SIGINT, sweep orphans on start (closes #1848)
body:
Closes #1848.

## Summary

This fixes the regressed child-process leak class from #645 with an architectural managed-child boundary instead of one-off signal forwarding:

1. **Managed daemon child API + registry**
   - Adds `spawnManagedDaemonChild()` / `registerChildReaper()` in core.
   - Every managed child is recorded in `~/.agent-orchestrator/daemon-children.json` with pid, role, parent pid, command, and start time.
   - The helper owns signal forwarding, process-group termination, registry unregister on child exit, and a stop-time SIGTERM → SIGKILL sweep.
   - ESLint now forbids raw `spawn` imports in the long-running daemon entrypoints so future daemon-owned children go through this interface.

2. **Daemon and dashboard wiring**
   - `ao start` dashboard children now use `spawnManagedDaemonChild()`.
   - `packages/web/server/start-all.ts` uses the same managed API for Next.js and direct-terminal websocket children.
   - `ao stop`, `ao stop --all`, restart, and SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown sweep the child registry before/while stopping the parent.

3. **Orphan recovery on start**
   - `ao start --reap-orphans` scans PPID=1 AO-looking processes and reaps them.
   - Interactive starts prompt before reaping; non-interactive starts print the recovery flag.
   - Detection covers `@aoagents/ao-web` dist-server children, historical `ao lifecycle-worker`, `.ao-messaging/.../ao-msg-watch.mjs`, and `next-server` orphans.

## Before / after

Before (from the issue): after `ao stop`, `node next-server` remained as `PPID=1`, retaining TCP connections and ~100 fds.

After: daemon-owned long-running subprocesses are registered at spawn time and swept by both in-process shutdown and `ao stop`; the integration test starts AO, captures the daemon child pids, runs stop, and asserts the captured children and parent are gone.

## Tests

Passed:
- `pnpm install` (completed; optional `better-sqlite3` native build is incompatible with local Node 25.9.0, but install continued)
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint` (warnings only; no errors)
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- daemon-children`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- start daemon`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-integration-tests exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/daemon-children.integration.test.ts`

Known local environment failures unrelated to this PR:
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` fails in core FTS SQLite tests because `better-sqlite3` did not build on local Node 25.9.0.
- Full `pnpm test:integration` now passes the new daemon child test but has an existing `agent-codex.integration.test.ts` liveness assertion failure in this local environment.

title: ao status is slow and reports inconsistent session count vs tmux ls
body:
## Bug

`ao status` is slow (multiple seconds) and reports inconsistent session counts compared to `tmux ls`.

## Screenshot

![ao status showing 1 session while tmux ls shows 7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-ao-status-slow/.issue-assets/ao-status-slow-performance.png)

## Discord thread

https://discord.com/channels/1481608425505386536/1491735678156013588/1504535676803092490

**Reported by:** @yyovil
**Analyzed against:** `89ad1851`
**AO version:** 0.7.0
**OS:** macOS

## Reproduction

1. Have multiple AO sessions (7 in this case: ao-3 through ao-9)
2. Run `ao status` — observe it takes several seconds
3. Run `tmux ls` — observe 7 active tmux sessions
4. `ao status` reports only 1 active session (ao-9) and says "8 terminated sessions hidden"

## Root Cause

Two distinct issues:

### 1. Session count discrepancy

**Why `ao status` shows 1 session when `tmux ls` shows 7:**

The sessions ao-3 through ao-8 are tmux sessions where the **agent process has exited** but the **tmux session is still alive**. The flow:

1. `status.ts:372` calls `sm.list()` → reads from **metadata files on disk** (not from tmux)
2. For each session, `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` (`session-manager.ts:1019-1065`) calls `plugins.runtime.isAlive()` then `plugins.agent.getActivityState()`
3. `getActivityState` runs `findClaudeProcess` → `ps -eo pid,tty,args` + `tmux list-panes`. If the agent process (e.g., claude/codex) inside the tmux session has exited, `getActivityState` returns `{ state: "exited" }` (`agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:964-967`)
4. `isTerminalSession()` (`types.ts:239-257`) checks `TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES.has("exited")` → **true**
5. `status.ts:377-382` filters these out by default

**This is correct behavior** — the agent process is gone, so the sessions ARE terminal. But the inconsistency with `tmux ls` is confusing. The tmux sessions are orphaned (agent exited but tmux didn't get killed).

### 2. Slowness

`ao status` performs **7+ subprocess/network calls per session** across two phases:

**Phase 1 — `sm.list()` (`session-manager.ts:1876-1939`):**
For each session, `ensureHandleAndEnrich` runs:
1. `plugins.runtime.isAlive(handle)` — `tmux has-session -t <id>` (5s timeout, `runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:200-207`)
2. `plugins.agent.getActivityState(session)` — `tmux list-panes` (30s timeout, uncached) + `ps -eo pid,tty,args` (30s timeout, 5s cache) + file I/O scanning `~/.claude/projects/`
3. `plugins.agent.getSessionInfo(session)` — file I/O scanning session files

This has a **12s timeout per session** (`OPENCODE_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS + 2_000` = 10_000 + 2_000 at `session-manager.ts:104,1922`).

**Phase 2 — `gatherSessionInfo()` (`status.ts:92-174`):**
For each session returned by `list()`:
1. `git branch --show-current` — subprocess (`status.ts:112`)
2. `getTmuxActivity(tmuxTarget)` — `tmux display-message` subprocess (`status.ts:123`)
3. `agent.getSessionInfo(session)` — **DUPLICATE** of Phase 1 call (`status.ts:130` vs `session-manager.ts:1104`)
4. `scm.detectPR(session, project)` — GitHub API via `gh` (`status.ts:157`)
5. `scm.getCISummary(prInfo)` — GitHub API (`status.ts:162`)
6. `scm.getReviewDecision(prInfo)` — GitHub API (`status.ts:163`)
7. `scm.getPendingComments(prInfo)` — GitHub API (`status.ts:164`)

**Total: ~7+ subprocess/network calls per session.** With 7 sessions, that's ~49+ operations. Even with `Promise.all` parallelization, the per-session 12s enrichment timeout creates a floor of 12s for the first phase alone if any session stalls.

**Key bottleneck — `findClaudeProcess` timeout:** `agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:685` sets `timeout: 30_000` for `tmux list-panes` per session, and line 649 sets `timeout: 30_000` for `ps -eo`. While `ps` has a 5s TTL cache (line 627), `tmux list-panes` has **no caching** — it runs fresh for every session on every `status` call.

**Critical duplication:** `agent.getSessionInfo(session)` is called **twice** per session — once in `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` (`session-manager.ts:1104`) and again in `gatherSessionInfo` (`status.ts:130`).

**Confidence:** High — traced exact code paths with file paths and line numbers.

## Fix Suggestions

1. **Cache `tmux list-panes` results** — same as the `ps` cache pattern in `agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:627`. A 5s TTL cache would eliminate redundant tmux calls across sessions.
2. **Deduplicate `getSessionInfo`** — the call in `gatherSessionInfo` (`status.ts:130`) is redundant since `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` already called it. Pass the result through the session object or skip the second call.
3. **Batch tmux operations** — a single `tmux list-sessions` + `tmux list-panes -a` could replace N individual `tmux has-session` + `tmux list-panes` calls with 2 calls total.
4. **Skip enrichment for terminal sessions** — `sm.list()` enriches ALL sessions including terminal ones, then filters. If terminal sessions were detected early (e.g., from metadata status), enrichment could be skipped entirely for the default `ao status` output.
5. **Clean up orphaned tmux sessions** — when `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` detects agent process exited but tmux is alive, kill the tmux session. This addresses the `tmux ls` vs `ao status` discrepancy at the source.

## Related

- [#1321](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1321) — RFC: Remove polling and move to reactive sync (same subsystem)
- [#1081](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1081) — Activity forced to 'exited' when PR merged (same enrichment path)
- [#1225](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1225) — Session detail page should treat exited activity as restorable (same activity detection)
- [#899](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/899) — Fixing Worker Session Persistence on Respawn (session lifecycle)

title: fix(cli): deduplicate enrichment and cache tmux probes in ao status
body:
## Summary

Fixes [#1850](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1850) — `ao status` is slow and reports inconsistent session counts vs `tmux ls`.

Four fixes targeting the highest-impact, lowest-risk improvements:

### 1. Skip enrichment for terminal sessions (`session-manager.ts`)
Sessions already in a terminal state (`killed`/`done`/`merged`/`terminated`/`cleanup`) are hidden from the default `ao status` output. Previously, every such session still ran the full `isAlive()` → `getActivityState()` → `getSessionInfo()` pipeline, adding seconds per session. Now we skip straight to a lightweight orphan check.

### 2. Deduplicate `getSessionInfo` call (`status.ts`)
`enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` already stores the result of `agent.getSessionInfo(session)` in `session.agentInfo`. But `gatherSessionInfo` was calling `agent.getSessionInfo(session)` again to get the summary. Now we reuse the cached `session.agentInfo.summary` and only fall back to a live probe when the cached value is null.

### 3. Cache `tmux list-panes` results (`agent-claude-code/index.ts`)
The `tmux list-panes` call in `findClaudeProcess` had no caching (30s timeout per call), unlike the `ps` call which has a 5s TTL cache. Added the same 5s TTL caching pattern for `tmux list-panes`, so N sessions share results within a cache window.

### 4. Kill orphaned tmux sessions (`session-manager.ts`)
When a session is terminal and the tmux session is still alive (agent exited but tmux lingers), we now kill the tmux session. This prevents the `tmux ls` vs `ao status` count discrepancy.

## Test Plan
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes for `core`, `cli`, and `agent-claude-code`
- [ ] Manual: `ao status` with 10+ sessions — verify speedup
- [ ] Manual: `tmux ls` matches session count after running `ao status`

## Summary
- Add `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-cn` for Continue CLI (`cn`) using the Forge-derived plugin shape.
- Wire `cn` into built-in agent registration for core, CLI detection, and web services.
- Add optional `Agent.promptDelivery` support so interactive CLIs can receive the initial AO prompt after launch instead of via one-shot prompt flags.

## Continue CLI command surface checked
- Package: `@continuedev/cli` 1.5.45 (`npm view @continuedev/cli ...`).
- Executable/detection: `cn`; plugin detection uses `which.sync("cn")`.
- Fresh launch: `cn` starts interactive TUI by default; `-p/--print` is headless/exit mode, so the plugin uses post-launch prompt delivery and does not pass prompt flags.
- Session listing/metadata: `cn ls --json` exposes session IDs/titles/workspace metadata.
- Resume support: `cn --resume` resumes the most recent session only; `cn --fork <sessionId>` forks history into a new session. There is no clean documented command to resume a specific current AO-owned session ID, so this plugin leaves `getSessionInfo()` and `getRestoreCommand()` unsupported/null.
- Waiting-input prompts observed from CLI source/help include tool permission (`Would you like to continue?`), interrupted state (`Press enter to continue`), quiz/default prompts, API-key/free-trial prompts, and auth-required messages.

title: feat: add Droid agent plugin
body:
## Summary
- add a built-in `agent-droid` plugin package following the Forge-style plugin shape (`manifest`, `create()`, `detect()`, default module)
- wire Droid into core built-ins, CLI direct plugin lookup/detection, and web service registration
- align launch args with Droid's top-level interactive CLI surface: system prompts use `--append-system-prompt[-file]`, the user task is passed as Droid's inline initial prompt, and exec-only model/permission flags are not passed
- capture Droid session IDs through documented Droid hooks and use `droid --resume <sessionId>` when metadata is available
- harden activity and process detection so auth failures, stale output, and indeterminate probes are represented correctly

## Droid CLI surface verified
- executable/detection: `droid`, detected with `which.sync("droid")`
- fresh interactive launch: `droid` with optional `--append-system-prompt` or `--append-system-prompt-file`
- prompt delivery: inline positional launch argument through Droid's documented top-level interactive prompt support; AO does not deliver the initial prompt through post-launch `sendMessage()` on this branch
- restore: `droid --resume <sessionId>` when AO has captured a Droid `session_id`
- stable session ID source: documented hook input `session_id`, captured via project-local `.factory/settings.local.json` hooks
- metadata/statistics: no stable non-interactive metadata/cost command found; `getSessionInfo()` only returns captured session metadata

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-droid test`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-droid typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-droid build`
