title: bug(core,web): dashboard read path makes per-session `gh` calls — `gh` is the dominant 20-40s bottleneck (benchmarked), not tmux/ps; #1858 is scoped to the wrong probes
body:
## Bug

The session-detail / sidebar / `ao status` read paths fan out **live `gh` GitHub API calls per session, on every poll**, inline with serving the request. This — not `tmux`/`ps` — is the dominant cause of the 20–40s request times and the "Failed to load session" / next-server-crash cascade (#1855, #1883).

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding + benchmarking | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `667d1ded` | **Confidence:** High (benchmarked, exact code lines) | **Priority:** Critical (root of the platform-down incidents)

## Benchmark — the three probes, as the code invokes them, under load (load avg 14.7, 810 procs)

| Command (exact invocation) | Per call | Calls / session | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tmux has-session -t <id>` (`runtime-tmux:202`) | **4 ms** | 1 | negligible |
| `ps -eo pid,tty,args` (`agent-claude-code:649`) | **82 ms** | 1 (TTL-cached) | minor; *can* spike to 30s under extreme load+N-concurrent per the in-code comment, but cached and not dominant |
| `gh pr view --json state,title,additions,deletions` (`scm-github:231`) | **660 ms** (spikes **1900 ms**) | ≥1 | **dominant** |
| `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` (CI, `scm-github:249`) | **683 ms** | 1 | **dominant** |
| `gh` reviews / reviewDecision (`scm-github:697,739`) | ~700 ms each | 1–2 | **dominant** |

**`gh` is the bottleneck by 1–2 orders of magnitude.** Per session ≈ 2–4 `gh` network round-trips × ~700ms. ~20 sessions ⇒ **~27–40s**, matching the observed RSC TTFB (33–43s in HAR captures on #1855). Concurrent fan-out hits GitHub rate-limiting (#1194), degrading the "parallel" burst toward that serialized number. `tmux`+`ps` together are <0.1s — rounding error.

## Why this happens (code path)

- `fresh=true` (`sessions/[id]/page.tsx:623-685`) ⇒ uncached `sessionManager.list()` (`session-manager.ts:1879`) every 2s.
- Web layer then runs `enrichSessionsMetadata` (`gh` for issue labels/titles) and `enrichSessionPR` (`gh pr view` + `gh api` for CI + review threads) — **per session, on the request path**.
- `list()` task fan-out is `allSessions.map(async…)` + `Promise.all` (`session-manager.ts:1890/1983`) with **no concurrency cap** and a `Promise.race` "timeout" (`:1937`) that **resolves but never cancels** — orphaned `gh` processes from a timed-out request pile onto the next request until next-server's event loop / fd budget / process table is exhausted and it **crashes** (observed: 25s-hang → connection-refused → no `:3001` listener → repeated `web-api` process respawns).

## Triage correction for #1858

[#1858](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1858) ("centralize tmux/ps runtime probes behind a shared observation store", Priority High) is **aimed at the wrong probes**. Its scope is literally `tmux list-panes` / `ps -eo pid,tty,args`. The benchmark shows those cost <0.1s combined; centralizing them yields ~0 improvement. **If #1858 ships as scoped, the 20–40s bottleneck remains.** #1858 must be expanded to cover `gh` (the SCM enrichment path) — or this issue supersedes its performance rationale.

## Fix (target design — same single-writer principle as #1735)

**The dashboard read path must make zero outbound `gh`/`tmux`/`ps` calls.**

1. The **lifecycle manager** (single writer, own cadence, concurrency-capped, with real cancellation) is the only caller of `gh`/`tmux`/`ps`. It persists `additions/deletions/state/ciStatus/reviews/reviewDecision` to session metadata.
2. `/api/sessions*`, the session-detail page, sidebar, and `ao status` **read persisted fields only** — O(1) file reads, no subprocess, no network.
3. This collapses request-path cost from `N × (2–4 × ~700ms gh)` to ~0 and makes next-server crash-proof under load.

Narrow steps already in flight (each a fragment of the above): #1685 (don't drop/await PR enrichment per-request), #1855 (remove `fresh=true` bypass), #1865 (`ps` strategy), #1737 (`listCached`). This issue is the **umbrella**: none of them, alone, removes `gh` from the request path, which the benchmark proves is the only thing that matters.

## Impact

- Primary cause of #1855 (page won't load / "taking too long") and the next-server crash/respawn loop.
- Makes the dashboard a per-poll GitHub API client → rate-limit exhaustion (#1194), false rate-limit banners (#1686), `+0/-0` PR cards (#1685).
- Every open tab × every 2s poll × N sessions multiplies GitHub I/O without bound.

## Related
- #1858 (scope correction — wrong probes), #1865 (ps strategy), #1855 (symptom/cascade), #1883 (sidebar/listCached), #1685 (PR card), #1194 (rate limit), #1686 (false rate-limit banner), #1737 (listCached), #1343 (introduced `fresh=true`), #1735 (single-writer precedent).

title: feat(pipeline): v1.3 — workspace classes, predicate DSL, exitPredicates
body:
Closes #1632. Sub-task of #1349 (pipeline cluster v1).

## Summary

Three v1.3 features that round out v1 on top of v1.1's DAG scheduler:

- **Typed predicate DSL** (`pipeline/predicate.ts`) — `all_pass` / `no_open_findings` / `finding_count_below` leaves + `and` / `or` / `not` combinators. Recursive Zod schema, pure evaluator, ref/depth validation at config load. Used in `Stage.routes.when` (new form alongside the v1.1 hardcoded shapes) and `Pipeline.exitPredicates`.
- **`Pipeline.exitPredicates`** — declarative run-completion conditions. Replaces the hardcoded `allTerminal → done` path with `evaluateRunExitOutcome`, which maps predicate truth + `maxLoopRounds` onto `done` (loop_succeeded), `stalled` (loop_failed), or `awaiting_context` (predicates false but rounds remain). Emits `pipeline.loop.succeeded` / `pipeline.loop.failed` / `pipeline.loop.continuing` observations.
- **Workspace classes** — `Stage.workspaceClass: "independent" | "read-siblings"`. WorkspaceGuard rejects orphan `read-siblings` at config load (no dependsOn, no route refs, no prior-declared stage). At runtime, the engine threads transitive upstream artifacts into the stage prompt as an `## Upstream Artifacts` block; the worktree itself stays fresh — only artifact-read access changes.

Also includes the **CONFIG_CHANGED structural-vs-tuning** classifier (`pipeline/config-diff.ts`). Drivers use it to decide whether a config edit must abort the active run (structural: DAG shape, executor, dependsOn) or can hot-reload (tuning: thresholds, retries, budgets, exitPredicates, workspaceClass).

## Acceptance (from #1632)

- [x] Predicate DSL parses valid configs / rejects malformed with precise paths
- [x] `read-siblings` stages can read sibling stage artifacts (threaded via prompt)
- [x] WorkspaceGuard rejects orphan `read-siblings` at load
- [x] Pipeline reaches `loop_succeeded` only when `exitPredicates` evaluate true
- [x] Pipeline reaches `loop_failed` when `exitPredicates` cannot be satisfied (max rounds reached)
- [x] Vitest coverage on DSL parser and evaluator (57 new tests across 4 files)
- [x] Targeted at `pipelines`

## Backward compatibility

- v1.1 `StageRoutePredicate` shapes (`allSucceeded` / `anySucceeded` / `anyFailed`) still parse — `normalizeRoutePredicate` bridges them into the new DSL for evaluation. No existing pipeline configs need a rewrite.
- `Pipeline.exitPredicates` unset → reducer behaves exactly as v1.1 (every terminal run → `done`).
- `RunState.runArtifacts` is optional, so v1.1 persisted runs deserialize cleanly.

## Files changed

| File | Why |
|------|-----|
| `pipeline/predicate.ts` (new) | DSL types + Zod schema + evaluator + legacy bridge |
| `pipeline/config-diff.ts` (new) | CONFIG_CHANGED classifier |
| `pipeline/types.ts` | `Predicate`, `WorkspaceClass`, `Stage.workspaceClass`, `Pipeline.exitPredicates`, `Pipeline.maxLoopRounds`, `RunState.runArtifacts` |
| `pipeline/config-schema.ts` | Wire DSL into routes + exitPredicates; WorkspaceGuard; ref/depth validation |
| `pipeline/dag.ts` | `evaluateRunExitOutcome`, `predicateContextForRun`, delegate route eval to DSL |
| `pipeline/reducer.ts` | `terminalLoopForRun` selects `done` / `stalled` / `awaiting_context`; populates `runArtifacts` |
| `pipeline/stage-prompt.ts` | `## Upstream Artifacts` block for `read-siblings` |
| `pipeline/engine.ts` | `collectSiblingArtifacts` — transitive `dependsOn` closure |
| `pipeline/executors/agent.ts` | Pass `siblingArtifacts` through to the prompt builder |
| `pipeline/index.ts` | Public re-exports |

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1370 / 1370 passing (1313 baseline + 57 new)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core build` — succeeds
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (only pre-existing warnings)

Tests:
- `pipeline-predicate.test.ts` — schema accepts/rejects, evaluator semantics (leaves + booleans), legacy bridge, transitive ref collection (25 tests)
- `pipeline-workspace.test.ts` — WorkspaceGuard accept/reject, prompt injection on/off (10 tests)
- `pipeline-exit-predicates.test.ts` — `done` / `stalled` / `awaiting_context` mapping, observation events (5 tests)
- `pipeline-config-diff.test.ts` — structural vs tuning classification + structural-wins promotion (17 tests)

## Concurrency notes

Stayed inside workspace-classes / predicate-DSL files to avoid stepping on the in-flight v1.1b (#1665, ao-175) and v1.2 (ao-176) sessions. The legacy `StageRoutePredicate` shape and the `scheduleAfterChange` API surface are unchanged so v1.1b's trigger work and v1.2's executors should layer cleanly on top.

title: feat(pipeline): v1.2 — command executor + builtin router + builtin compose
body:
Closes #1631 (sub-task of #1349).

## Summary

Adds the three remaining pipeline executors so any combination of `agent`, `command`, `builtin/router`, and `builtin/compose` stages can be wired into a pipeline:

- **`command` executor** — spawns the stage as a child process, parses stdout as JSONL (or a single JSON array) into ArtifactInputs, captures stderr into the failure message. Refuses to run a fork PR unless the stage opts in with `Stage.allowFork: true`; the refusal is logged with the documented reason and surfaces as `STAGE_FAILED`. Not talk-to-able (per locked decision 10).
- **`builtin/router` executor** — replaces the original spec's `SEND_TO_AGENT` reducer command. Reads upstream stage findings via `BuiltinTaskContext.readSiblingArtifacts`, formats a payload, and delivers it to a target session (literal `sessionId` or `kind: "self"`) via `BuiltinTaskContext.sendToSession`. Emits a `json` audit artifact recording what was delivered.
- **`builtin/compose` executor** — bundles findings from multiple upstream stages into a single composite `json` artifact for downstream consumption.

## SCM contract extension

- `PRInfo.isFromFork: boolean` added.
- `scm-github` populates it from `gh`'s `isCrossRepository`.
- `scm-gitlab` populates it from `source_project_id !== target_project_id`.
- Threaded through engine `StartRunInput → runMetadata → CommandStartInput` so the command executor can enforce the fork-safety opt-in.

## Other changes

- `BuiltinTaskContext` interface defines what builtins can do — narrow surface (read siblings, send to session) so executors stay testable as pure functions over their context.
- `Stage.allowFork?: boolean` (agent and builtin stages ignore the flag).
- Shared `findings-parser.ts` extracted from `agent.ts` so command + agent stages validate ArtifactInputs the same way.
- Engine `START_STAGE` dispatches by `executor.kind`; missing command/builtin executors now fail the stage with a clear "not configured" message rather than hanging.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all 28 packages
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1343 tests pass (added 35 new pipeline tests)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github test` + scm-gitlab — pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 910 pass
- [x] `pnpm lint` — zero new errors in changed files
- [x] Integration test: `engine + builtin/router` end-to-end verifies that a `command → router` pipeline delivers a payload containing upstream findings to the target session via the wired `sendToSession` callback.
- [x] Integration test: `engine + builtin/compose` end-to-end verifies that two upstream stages get merged into one composite artifact persisted in the pipeline store.
- [x] `command` executor refuses fork PRs unless `allowFork: true`; covered at executor unit test, engine integration test, and verified the refusal message comes through the `onRefuse` hook.

## Out of scope

- DAG (already in v1.1)
- Predicate DSL (v1.3 — concurrent session ao-177)
- Workspace classes (v1.3)

title: fix: sanitize project IDs with dots/special chars on ao start
body:
## Summary

When `ao start` auto-generates a project ID from a folder name containing dots or special characters (e.g. `llama.cpp`, `my.app`), the raw basename fails Zod validation because the project ID schema requires `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`.

## Root Cause

Two code paths in `start.ts` use `basename()` directly without sanitization:
1. `registerFlatConfig()` — registers existing flat configs
2. `autoCreateConfig()` — first-run config generation

Both pass the raw basename as a project key, which later fails Zod schema validation in `config.ts`.

The deprecated `generateProjectId()` in `paths.ts` had the same issue.

## Solution

Sanitize project IDs the same way session prefixes are already sanitized: replace `[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]` with `-` and strip leading/trailing dashes. If the result is empty (e.g. folder named `...`), fall back to `"project"`.

## Changes

- **`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`**: Sanitize `projectId` in both `registerFlatConfig()` and `autoCreateConfig()`. Remove now-redundant `prefixInput` variable since `projectId` is already sanitized.
- **`packages/core/src/paths.ts`**: Apply same sanitization to deprecated `generateProjectId()`.
- **`packages/core/src/__tests__/paths.test.ts`**: Add test coverage for sanitization of dot-containing and all-special-char basenames.

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (15/15 in paths.test.ts)
- New test covers: `llama.cpp` → `llama-cpp`, `my.app` → `my-app`, `my_app-v2.0` → `my_app-v2-0`, `...` → `project`

title: perf(web): persist issue titles to metadata, eliminating gh calls on read path
body:
## Summary

- `enrichSessionIssueTitle()` now reads from `metadata["issueTitle"]` before calling `tracker.getIssue()` (which spawns `gh api`)
- On first successful fetch, persists the title to session metadata for subsequent reads
- Converts the N-session x ~700ms `gh` fan-out into O(1) file reads after first encounter

## Context (from #1885 benchmark)

| Probe | Per call | Impact |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `gh api` (issue title) | ~700ms | Dominant bottleneck |
| `tmux has-session` | 4ms | Negligible |
| `ps -eo pid,tty,args` | 82ms | Minor (cached) |

After process restart, all N sessions hit `tracker.getIssue()` simultaneously since the in-memory TTL cache is cold. This persists titles to disk so they survive restarts.

## Design

Follows the same pattern as `readPREnrichmentFromMetadata()` which already reads PR data from metadata (written by the lifecycle manager). This PR adds the read-side persistence for issue titles. The lifecycle manager can be updated separately to also write `issueTitle` during its enrichment cycle for true zero-network reads from the start.

## Test plan

- [ ] Session with an issue shows title on first load (fetched via `gh`, then persisted)
- [ ] On page refresh / process restart, issue title loads instantly from metadata (no `gh` call)
- [ ] Session without an issue is unaffected
- [ ] Typecheck passes (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`)
- [ ] Existing serialize tests pass (74/75 files pass, 1 pre-existing WebSocket integration failure on main)

Ref #1885

title: "ask to post for review" button hardcodes Slack — should use connected platform
body:
## Bug

The `"ask to post for review"` action button in `scripts/claude-dashboard` hardcodes Slack as the target:

```js
askAgent('${s.name}','Post ${currentPr.url} on slack asking for a review. Do not ask for permission, just post it.',event)
```

**Problem:** If a user doesn't have Slack configured, the button is a dead action — it tells the agent to post on Slack but either fails silently or goes nowhere.

## Expected Behavior

1. **Detect connected platforms** — check which messaging platform(s) are available (Discord, Slack, etc.)
2. **Send to the right platform** — instruct the agent to post the PR link on whichever platform is actually connected
3. **Hide the button** if no messaging platform is configured — no point showing a button that can't do anything

`scripts/claude-dashboard` — line ~737

title: bug(core): stale blocked/waiting_input silently decays to idle, hiding stuck agents from the dashboard
body:
## Problem

`getActivityFallbackState` in `packages/core/src/activity-log.ts:184-191` treats a `blocked` or `waiting_input` entry older than `ACTIVITY_INPUT_STALENESS_MS` (5 min) as `idle`:

```ts
if (entry.state === "waiting_input" || entry.state === "blocked") {
  const ageMs = Date.now() - entryTs.getTime();
  if (ageMs <= ACTIVITY_INPUT_STALENESS_MS) {
    return { state: entry.state, timestamp: entryTs };
  }
  // Stale actionable entry — treat as idle
  return { state: "idle", timestamp: entryTs };
}
```

`checkActivityLogState` (`:139-160`) applies the same cap.

The result: an agent stuck on an error for >5 min shows **"idle"** on the Kanban — exactly when the human most needs to see "blocked". Likewise a permission prompt that no one answers within 5 min disappears from the "respond" zone and re-enters the "working" zone as `idle`.

This is a correctness bug — `AttentionZone.tsx:299` and `lib/types.ts:498-507` both gate the red "respond" column on these activity states.

## Root cause

The staleness cap was added so sessions don't sit on `needs_input` forever if the JSONL entry never gets refreshed. But the cap fires on **wallclock**, regardless of whether the process is still alive or actually doing anything. A live, stuck process gets misclassified.

## Proposed fix

Replace wallclock decay with **liveness-anchored** decay:
- Keep `blocked` / `waiting_input` sticky as long as the process is still running.
- Demote to `idle` only when `isProcessRunning` returns false, OR when a newer entry overrides it.
- If the worry is "what if recordActivity never runs again?" — that's already covered: the next `getActivityState` poll re-runs the agent's native + JSONL cascade and will overwrite the stale entry.

## Test plan (TDD)

In `packages/core/src/__tests__/activity-log.test.ts` (or wherever fallback is tested):

1. Entry: `blocked`, ts = 10 min ago, process alive → expect `blocked`, **not** `idle` (currently fails).
2. Entry: `waiting_input`, ts = 6 min ago, process alive → expect `waiting_input`.
3. Entry: `blocked`, ts = 6 min ago, process dead → expect `exited` (already covered upstream by process check).
4. Fresh `blocked` (ts = 1 min ago) → unchanged behavior.

## Risk / mitigation

- "Ghost blocked forever" risk if the source of the blocked state never clears: bounded by next poll's native re-check, which can transition out of blocked when the agent emits a new event.
- Sticky blocked state could mask other dashboard signals — but those signals (CI/review) live in the lifecycle column system, not in activity, so they still surface.

---
Discovered while mapping the activity-detection system end-to-end. See companion docs PR if/when filed.

title: feat(core): use fs.watch on native JSONL for sub-second activity detection (Claude/Codex)
body:
## Problem

The lifecycle poll loop is fixed at 30s (`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:2842-2847`). When Claude Code or Codex writes a `permission_request` or `error` entry to its native JSONL, the dashboard waits **up to 30 seconds** before updating.

User-facing impact: an approval prompt can sit unnoticed for half a minute while the operator stares at a "working" card. For interactive workflows (`--dangerously-skip-permissions` off, lots of tool approvals) this dominates perceived latency of the whole system.

## Why native-JSONL agents are the right target

`recordActivity` for AO-JSONL agents (Aider/Cursor/OpenCode/Kimi) needs to poll the terminal — there's no event source to watch. So they're stuck with the poll cadence.

But Claude (`~/.claude/projects/.../*.jsonl`) and Codex (`~/.codex/sessions/.../*.jsonl`) write their JSONLs in real time. Watching those files with `fs.watch` gives sub-second responsiveness at zero polling cost.

## Proposed design

Add an optional `watchActivity` hook to the Agent interface (`packages/core/src/types.ts`):

```ts
watchActivity?(session: Session, onChange: () => void): () => void;
// returns an unwatch callback
```

- Claude / Codex plugins implement it: `fs.watch` the resolved session file. On change, debounce 200ms then call `onChange()`.
- Lifecycle manager wires `onChange` to a per-session `checkSession(session)` call, bypassing the 30s tick. Re-entrancy guarded by the existing `polling` boolean.
- Agents that don't implement it keep the current 30s tick. Backward compatible.

## Edge cases

- File doesn't exist yet (agent hasn't started writing) → fall back to polling until first appearance, then watch.
- Slug computation drift (Claude renames its project dir) → watch breaks silently; the AO-JSONL safety net (separate issue) matters as a parallel safeguard.
- File rotation / atomic rename → fs.watch on macOS gives `rename` events; need to re-resolve and re-watch.
- File-descriptor cost: 1 watch per active Claude/Codex session, capped by AO session limits.
- Windows: `fs.watch` on Windows uses ReadDirectoryChangesW — works but emits more spurious events; needs the same 200ms debounce.

## Test plan

1. Spawn a Claude session, write a `permission_request` line to its JSONL → `checkSession` fires within 500ms (currently up to 30s).
2. Watch falls back to polling cleanly if session file doesn't exist yet.
3. Unwatch is called on session termination — no leaked watchers.

## Out of scope

- Push detection for AO-JSONL agents (no event source).
- Replacing the lifecycle poll entirely. Watch supplements it.

title: refactor(core): unify isProcessRunning across 6 agent plugins (shared ps cache)
body:
## Problem

Every agent plugin reimplements `isProcessRunning` with the same shape:
1. tmux runtime → run `tmux list-panes` → run `ps -eo pid,tty,args` → regex-match agent name on each pane's TTY.
2. process runtime → `process.kill(pid, 0)` with EPERM handling.

Sources:
- `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:670-726, 942-945` (uses a 5s `psCache`)
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:703-...`
- `packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts:213-264`
- `packages/plugins/agent-cursor/src/index.ts:305-...`
- `packages/plugins/agent-opencode/src/index.ts:344-395`
- `packages/plugins/agent-kimicode/src/index.ts:294-...`

**Only Claude has the `ps` cache.** With N sessions, every 30s tick spawns roughly N concurrent `ps -eo` processes (one per non-Claude session). On a machine with many sessions this is wasted forks and stalls the poll loop. Related: #1885 already calls out that `ps`/tmux probes are not the dominant bottleneck (gh is) — but they are still unnecessary work, and the duplicated code is fragile.

The regex differs only by agent name (`claude`, `codex`, `aider`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `kimi`).

## Proposed refactor

In `@aoagents/ao-core`:

```ts
export interface ProcessRunningOptions {
  processNameRegex: RegExp;
}

export async function isAgentProcessRunning(
  handle: RuntimeHandle,
  opts: ProcessRunningOptions,
): Promise<boolean>;
```

- One shared `psCache` (already exists in `agent-claude-code` — promote it).
- One tmux-pane scan with TTL.
- Plugins reduce to a one-liner:
  ```ts
  async isProcessRunning(handle) {
    return isAgentProcessRunning(handle, { processNameRegex: /(?:^|\/)aider(?:\s|$)/ });
  }
  ```

Process-runtime branch (PID + `process.kill(0)` + EPERM) becomes shared too.

## Cross-platform note

`isWindows()` guard already exists in each plugin's tmux branch. Move it into the shared helper. The Windows pty-host registry is unrelated and stays in `runtime-process`.

## Test plan

1. Existing per-plugin `isProcessRunning` tests remain green after refactor (same behavior, different code path).
2. New core test for shared cache: 10 concurrent calls across 10 fake sessions trigger one `ps` invocation, not 10.
3. EPERM handling preserved for process-runtime path.

## Risk

Refactor across 6 plugins — mostly mechanical. Risk is the regex translation; verify with integration tests for each agent.

title: bug(agent-claude-code): no AO-JSONL safety net — slug-format drift would silently kill activity detection
perf(core): getActivityState runs twice per poll tick (lifecycle-manager + session-manager)
body:
## Problem

`getActivityState` runs **twice per poll tick** for every session:

1. `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:1070` — inside `enrichSession()`, called from `sm.list()`.
2. `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1001` — inside `checkSession()`, called from `pollAll()`.

Both run within milliseconds of each other on the same session, and both perform the same expensive work:
- Spawn `ps -eo` (or check PID) to verify the process is alive.
- Read the agent's native JSONL or the AO activity JSONL.
- Classify into an `ActivityDetection`.

For 20 sessions × every 30s tick (and again on every SSE refresh = 5s), this is 40+ duplicated reads/spawns per tick. Pure waste.

## Proposed fix

Add a request-scoped cache keyed by `(sessionId, pollCorrelationId)`. The correlation id is already created at `lifecycle-manager.ts:2693`:

```ts
const correlationId = createCorrelationId("lifecycle-poll");
```

Pass it down to `enrichSession`. When `getActivityState` runs, store the result in a `Map<string, ActivityDetection | null>` keyed by `${sessionId}:${correlationId}`. The second call (in `checkSession`) finds the cached result and skips.

Outside the polling loop (e.g. `sm.list()` from a CLI command), no correlation id → no caching → fresh result every time. Backward compatible.

## Alternative

Lift activity detection out of `enrichSession` entirely, into the lifecycle manager. Have the lifecycle manager write `session.activity` / `session.activitySignal` once, and `enrichSession` reads the cached value from session storage. This is cleaner architecturally — `enrichSession` shouldn't be making expensive probes, that's the lifecycle manager's job.

The current double-call is partly because `sm.list()` is called outside the lifecycle loop (e.g. CLI commands) and needs fresh data. But CLI commands could either (a) trigger a one-off `lifecycle.check(sessionId)` first, or (b) tolerate slightly-stale data (30s max).

## Test plan

1. Mock `getActivityState`. Run one full `pollAll()` cycle. Assert it's called exactly once per session (currently twice).
2. SSE `/api/sessions` returns the same `activity` and `activitySignal` values after refactor.

## Priority

Low — this is correctness-neutral, just wasted CPU. Worth tackling only if combined with a broader refactor of `enrichSession` vs `checkSession` responsibilities.

title: refactor(core): redesign activity detection — split inbox vs liveness, retire per-plugin cascade
body:
## Mission

Redesign the activity-detection subsystem to fix a class of correctness bugs (notably #1894) and remove duplicated cascade boilerplate across 6 agent plugins.

This is a tracking issue for the design. Individual code changes ship as PR-A through PR-F (checklist at bottom).

## The core defect (one paragraph)

The `Agent` contract collapses three semantics — **liveness** ("is the agent alive?"), **inbox** ("is there an outstanding event awaiting human action?"), and **terminal** ("is the process gone?") — into one `ActivityState` enum and one `getActivityState()` probe.

That single conflation forces every downstream symptom: sticky events (`waiting_input`/`blocked`) get wallclock-aged because they share a field with liveness; every consumer re-probes because there's no event queue to subscribe to; six plugins reimplement the same cascade because each has to map its world to the one enum; `null` becomes overloaded ("didn't probe" vs "no event") because there's no second channel.

> Codebase principle: "WE DONOT APPLY SURFACE FIXES. WE FIX THE CORE FIRST."

## Evidence: 15 concrete breakages found

**P0 correctness**

1. Stale `waiting_input`/`blocked` decays to `idle` after 5min wallclock — `activity-log.ts:184-191` (= #1894)
2. Auto-cleanup-on-merge can SIGTERM an agent mid-prompt once #1 fires — `lifecycle-manager.ts:2180-2184`

**P1 correctness**

3. **Two probers, divergent writes.** `session.activity` is written only by session-manager (`session-manager.ts:1046, 1073`); `session.activitySignal` is written by both session-manager (5×) and lifecycle-manager (`lifecycle-manager.ts:917`). Both sides also call `getActivityState` independently (double probe work). `session.activity` (session-manager, every SSE tick = 5s) and `session.status` (lifecycle-manager, every poll = 30s) end up divergent at the UI boundary for up to 30s; notifier latency floor inherits that gap.
4. Claude plugin has no AO-JSONL safety net — slug drift kills detection silently (= #1897)
5. Merge cleanup reads stale activity from session-manager path, not lifecycle truth — `lifecycle-manager.ts:2180`
6. Stuck reason becomes `probe_failure` instead of `error_in_process` after `blocked` decays — `lifecycle-manager.ts:1297-1303`

**P2 architecture/perf**

7. ~140 `getActivityState` invocations/min for 10 sessions (double poll + SSE re-enrichment)
8. Triple source of truth — `ao send --wait` constructs its own `detectActivityFromOutput` bypassing reducer paths — `session-manager.ts:2358-2365, 2540-2560`
9. No debounce: multi-step approval flows oscillate `needs_input` ↔ `working` every tick — `lifecycle-manager.ts:1022-1029`
10. **Structural smell, not lost coverage.** The "empty-terminal branch" at `lifecycle-manager.ts:1041-1086` is nested inside `if (terminalOutput)` and doesn't call `isProcessRunning`. However, a standalone fallback at `lifecycle-manager.ts:1130-1160` does catch dead processes when `processProbe.state === "unknown"`, so dead-process detection isn't actually missed in this tick — just routed through an awkward path. Fix is cleanup, not correctness.

**P2 plugin drift**

11. Cursor structurally cannot produce `blocked` — by design (`agent-cursor/src/index.ts:243-248` comment: compiler errors / test failures are too noisy without native JSONL). Plugin coverage gap by intent; closes naturally when the terminal-source contract carries plugin-specific blocked patterns in PR-E. Not a "bug" per se — scope of current detection.
12. Aider/Cursor "active" returns no timestamp → `lastActivityAt` lies on the dashboard — `agent-aider/src/index.ts:186`, `agent-cursor/src/index.ts:278`
13. `hasRecentCommits` false-positives on user/CI commits — `agent-aider/src/index.ts:185`, `agent-cursor/src/index.ts:277`
14. `detectActivity` regex drifted across 6 plugins (idle-prompt, Y/N, error patterns) — no shared corpus or contract

**P3**

15. Recovery validator uses stale `waiting_input` as live-agent evidence; after `ao stop`+`start`, ghosted sessions can be marked alive — `recovery/validator.ts:27-35, 131-138`

## Root-cause synthesis

The 15 reduce to 5 causes, which roll up to the single defect named above:

- **A. Wallclock decay applied to sticky events** → drives #1, #2, #5, #6, partly #15
- **B. Two probers, divergent writes** → drives #3, #7, #8, partly #15
- **C. 30s pull-only polling** → drives #9, motivates #1895, baseline latency for #3
- **D. Per-plugin reimplementation of identical cascade** → drives #4, #10, #11, #12, #13, #14
- **E. `null` overloaded ("missing signal" vs "signal says idle")** → drives #10, partly #4, partly #15

## Robust redesign

Split the contract. Per-session in-core `ActivityReducer` owned by lifecycle-manager:

```ts
interface ActivityReducer {
  snapshot(): {
    liveness: 'active' | 'ready' | 'idle' | 'exited'  // wallclock-decaying
    inbox: 'waiting_input' | 'blocked' | null         // sticky event
    lastEventAt: Date
    source: 'native-stream' | 'native-poll' | 'terminal' | 'process-probe'
  }
  applyEvent(e: ActivityEvent): void
  applyLivenessTick(now: Date): void
  applyProcessProbe(alive: boolean): void
  clearInbox(reason: 'resolved' | 'override' | 'exited'): void
}
```

- `inbox` (sticky): clears only on agent event, override, or process death. No wallclock decay.
- `liveness` (decaying): `active → ready → idle` with current windows.
- `session.activity` (legacy consumer field) computed at boundary: `exited || inbox || liveness`. Existing dashboard/serialize code unchanged.

Plugins declare `ActivitySource`s instead of implementing a cascade:

```ts
interface ActivitySource {
  kind: 'native-stream' | 'native-poll' | 'terminal' | 'process-probe'
  start(session: Session, sink: (e: ActivityEvent) => void): () => void
}
```

| Plugin | Sources declared |
|---|---|
| claude-code | native-stream (fs.watch) + process-probe |
| codex | native-stream (fs.watch) + terminal + process-probe |
| aider | terminal + native-poll (git/chat mtime) + process-probe |
| cursor | terminal + native-poll (git/dir mtime) + process-probe |
| opencode | terminal + native-poll (HTTP) + process-probe |
| kimicode | terminal + native-poll (mtime scan) + process-probe |

#1895 (fs.watch) and #1897 (Claude safety net) both fall out as `ActivitySource` declarations — no special-casing.

## What survives / changes / dies

**Survives:** the 6-state `ActivityState` enum (consumer contract is stable), `ActivityDetection` shape (renamed `ActivityEvent`), `ActivitySignal` confidence wrapper, `isProcessRunning` (becomes process-probe source), the threshold/window constants (apply to liveness only after split).

**Changes:** `getActivityState(session)` becomes a pure O(1) snapshot read — no I/O. `session-manager.enrichSessionWithRuntimeState` stops calling it; reads from reducer instead. `detectActivity` moves off the `Agent` interface; each plugin exports `terminalPatterns` consumed by the shared terminal source.

**Dies:**
- `activity-log.ts` entirely (253 LOC): `recordActivity`, `recordTerminalActivity`, `classifyTerminalActivity`, `appendActivityEntry`, `readLastActivityEntry`, `checkActivityLogState`, `getActivityFallbackState`
- `ACTIVITY_INPUT_STALENESS_MS` constant
- Every `<workspace>/.ao/activity.jsonl` file (one-time migration cleanup)
- `detectActivityFromOutput` closure in `send-await` (replaced by reducer subscription)
- Per-plugin cascade boilerplate across ~5 plugins
- Stale `@deprecated` `detectActivity` on the `Agent` interface (`types.ts:475`)

**Net LOC:** structurally smaller — exact number pending implementation. (Rough early estimate: ~−230, but the new `ActivityReducer` + `ActivitySource` adapters add real lines too; final delta depends on how much consolidates.)

## Shared utilities to extract (consolidation)

Duplicated 5-6 times across plugins; extract to `@aoagents/ao-core`:

1. `isIdlePrompt(lastLine, extraPrompts?: RegExp[])` — `/^[>$#]\s*$/.test(...)` lives in 6 plugins
2. `isYesNoPrompt(tail)` — `/\(Y\)es.*\(N\)o/i` lives in 6 plugins
3. `findProcessByTmuxPane(handle, nameRegex)` — `isProcessRunning` tmux+ps logic duplicated 6×
4. `findLatestFileMatching(dir, pattern, opts)` — variants in claude/codex/cursor/aider/kimi
5. `hasRecentCommits` (currently in aider+cursor with identical false-positive bug) — either consolidate + fix to discriminate agent vs human commits, or remove from cascade once terminal source covers active-state classification

Also consider: `ActivitySignal` confidence buckets (`unavailable`/`null`/`probe_failure`) are differentiated in core but downstream consumers only branch on `valid`/non-valid. Either collapse to `valid | weak`, or actually use the distinction.

## Migration — sequenced, not big-bang

Each PR is independently shippable and reviewable.

- [ ] **PR-A** — Replace wallclock decay with liveness anchor in `checkActivityLogState` + `getActivityFallbackState`. ~30 lines core + tests. **Closes #1894. Unblocks #2, #6, #15** (3 of 4 P1 correctness bugs) by deleting the staleness check.
- [ ] **PR-B** — Add `recordActivity` + AO-JSONL fallback to `agent-claude-code` (mechanical mirror of Codex). **Closes #1897.** **Ship in the first wave with PR-A**, not after PR-D: fs.watch (PR-D) has nontrivial Windows risk per `CROSS_PLATFORM.md`; if PR-D slips, Claude has zero safety net for slug drift the entire time. PR-B is mechanical, low-risk, and de-risks Claude immediately.
- [ ] **PR-C** — Introduce `ActivityReducer` in core. Lifecycle-manager owns it. Session-manager reads snapshot. The two `getActivityState` call sites consolidate to one. `send-await` subscribes instead of running its own detect. 3 core files + 1 web hook touched, no plugin changes.
- [ ] **PR-D** — Add native-stream `ActivitySource` (fs.watch) for Claude/Codex. **Closes #1895.**
- [ ] **PR-E** — Refactor each plugin to declare `ActivitySource`s. Delete per-plugin `recordActivity`. **Split into 6 sub-PRs (one per plugin), not a single bundle**: each plugin has plugin-specific edge cases (Cursor's deliberate no-blocked, OpenCode's HTTP timeout handling, kimicode's md5-cwd path resolution); bundling makes rollback all-or-nothing. Green-gate each on its integration tests. Sequence the highest-traffic plugin (`claude-code`) last so it benefits from lessons learned.
- [ ] **PR-F** — Cleanup pass. Delete `activity-log.ts`, `ACTIVITY_INPUT_STALENESS_MS`, deprecated `detectActivity` on `Agent` interface. Land the 5 shared utilities above. Consolidate `isProcessRunning` (= #1896). One-time `.ao/activity.jsonl` cleanup helper.

PR-A + PR-B together form the surgical first wave. PR-A alone makes 3 P1 bugs disappear by deleting ~30 lines; PR-B de-risks the Claude plugin in parallel.

## PR-A risk callout (must be in the PR description)

Removing the wallclock cap means `waiting_input`/`blocked` persists until process death or a newer entry overrides. Two failure modes:

1. Agent emits `permission_request` to JSONL but the process crashes mid-handling. Inbox stays sticky until the next process-probe (≤30s) catches it. That's fine — 30s is the existing latency floor.
2. Agent emits `permission_request`, the user answers, but the agent doesn't emit a clearing event (e.g., headless one-shot exits without writing `assistant_message`). Inbox would stick forever for that session. The current 5-min cap was the silent safety net here.

**Mitigation:** rely on process-probe to clear inbox on normal exit (already covered), AND have the reducer treat a fresh `liveness="active"` event with a timestamp newer than the inbox entry as evidence to clear stale inbox older than ~2 min. This preserves "agent moved on" semantics without re-introducing the wallclock cap.

## PR-A test plan (bake into PR description)

Tests to add in `packages/core/src/__tests__/activity-log.test.ts` (or wherever the fallback is tested):

1. Entry `waiting_input`, ts = 10 min ago, `isProcessRunning = true` → expect `waiting_input` (currently fails — returns `idle`).
2. Entry `blocked`, ts = 6 min ago, `isProcessRunning = true` → expect `blocked`.
3. Entry `waiting_input`, ts = 6 min ago, `isProcessRunning = false` → expect `exited` (already covered upstream by process check; assert no fall-through to `idle`).
4. Entry `blocked`, ts = 1 min ago → unchanged behavior.
5. **Override semantics (new):** entry `waiting_input` 6 min ago, then a fresh `active`-class entry appended (simulates the agent moving on without explicitly clearing the inbox) → expect the fresh entry wins.
6. **Concurrency (new):** simulate a `recordActivity` append racing with a `readLastActivityEntry` read. `readLastActivityEntry` already handles truncated tails; assert behavior is stable under load.

## Backward-incompat callout

PR-A is a **behavior change visible to operators** who built mental models around the 5-min cap. Sessions waiting on a prompt will now stay in the "respond" zone indefinitely (until the prompt is answered, the agent moves on, or the process exits) instead of silently sliding back to the "working" zone. Worth a one-line note in the changeset and release notes.

**Notifier UX shift:** after PR-A, `waiting_input` no longer decays to `idle` → `hasPositiveIdleEvidence` stays false → the idle-beyond-threshold stuck escalation no longer fires for stuck-on-prompt sessions. That's correct (a sticky inbox is not "idle"), but operators currently get a stuck notification after ~5min + threshold. After PR-A they only get the `needs_input` notification at t=0 and nothing else for that prompt. Surface this in release notes.

## Commit message guidance

When the PRs land, encode the load-bearing context in each commit body so future grep-archaeology works:

- **PR-A:** `Closes #1894`; explicitly call out the semantic change ("`waiting_input`/`blocked` no longer decays on wallclock; clears only on process death or newer entry"); reference `#1899` as the umbrella.
- **PR-C:** note "session-manager no longer calls `getActivityState`; that path is owned by lifecycle-manager via `ActivityReducer`." Highly load-bearing for anyone debugging activity afterward.
- **PR-F:** list every deleted symbol (`ACTIVITY_INPUT_STALENESS_MS`, `recordActivity`, `checkActivityLogState`, etc.) so people searching for these in 6 months find a pointer.

## Reference material

This issue is the canonical reference. Supporting:
- `docs/ACTIVITY_DETECTION.md` — system map with file:line citations (currently on a fork; suggest opening the doc PR as a sibling of PR-A so the canonical reference lands with the first behavior change)
- Related issues: #1894, #1895, #1896, #1897, #1898

Origin: research spawned to investigate "is `needs_input`/`waiting_input` actually broken?" Hypothesis confirmed; this issue is the synthesis (with peer review applied).

title: feat(web): "Launch Orchestrator (clean context)" button
body:
## Problem

When re-launching an orchestrator session, there's no way to start fresh — previous orchestrator context (conversation history, stale state) carries over. Users need a way to spawn an orchestrator with a completely clean slate from the dashboard.

## Proposed Solution

Add a "Launch Orchestrator (clean context)" button to the dashboard that spawns a new orchestrator session without inheriting any state from a previous run. This should:

- Start a fresh orchestrator session with no carryover from prior orchestrator state
- Be accessible from the dashboard UI (likely the project view or orchestrator detail view)
- Clearly indicate to the user that this starts clean vs. resuming an existing orchestrator

## Context

- Related to #1080 — no way to spawn an orchestrator from single-project dashboard
- Related to orchestrator button issues #1362, #1211

title: fix(core): waiting_input and blocked no longer decay to idle on wallclock (closes #1894)
body:
## Problem

PR-A from umbrella #1899 fixes #1894: AO activity JSONL currently lets stale `waiting_input`/`blocked` entries decay to `idle` on wallclock after 5 minutes. That hides live agents that are still waiting on a human prompt or blocked on an error. This PR removes the wallclock cap in `packages/core/src/activity-log.ts` so actionable states persist until process death or a newer entry overrides them.

Closes #1894.
References #1899.

## PR-A test plan

1. Entry `waiting_input`, ts = 10 min ago, `isProcessRunning = true` → expect `waiting_input` (currently fails — returns `idle`).
2. Entry `blocked`, ts = 6 min ago, `isProcessRunning = true` → expect `blocked`.
3. Entry `waiting_input`, ts = 6 min ago, `isProcessRunning = false` → expect `exited` (already covered upstream by process check; assert no fall-through to `idle`).
4. Entry `blocked`, ts = 1 min ago → unchanged behavior.
5. **Override semantics (new):** entry `waiting_input` 6 min ago, then a fresh `active`-class entry appended (simulates the agent moving on without explicitly clearing the inbox) → expect the fresh entry wins.
6. **Concurrency (new):** simulate a `recordActivity` append racing with a `readLastActivityEntry` read. `readLastActivityEntry` already handles truncated tails; assert behavior is stable under load.

## PR-A risk callout

Removing the wallclock cap means `waiting_input`/`blocked` persists until process death or a newer entry overrides. Two failure modes:

1. Agent emits `permission_request` to JSONL but the process crashes mid-handling. Inbox stays sticky until the next process-probe (≤30s) catches it. That's fine — 30s is the existing latency floor.
2. Agent emits `permission_request`, the user answers, but the agent doesn't emit a clearing event (e.g., headless one-shot exits without writing `assistant_message`). Inbox would stick forever for that session. The current 5-min cap was the silent safety net here.

**Mitigation:** rely on process-probe to clear inbox on normal exit (already covered), AND have the reducer treat a fresh `liveness="active"` event with a timestamp newer than the inbox entry as evidence to clear stale inbox older than ~2 min. This preserves "agent moved on" semantics without re-introducing the wallclock cap.

## Backward-incompat callout

PR-A is a **behavior change visible to operators** who built mental models around the 5-min cap. Sessions waiting on a prompt will now stay in the "respond" zone indefinitely (until the prompt is answered, the agent moves on, or the process exits) instead of silently sliding back to the "working" zone. Worth a one-line note in the changeset and release notes.

**Notifier UX shift:** after PR-A, `waiting_input` no longer decays to `idle` → `hasPositiveIdleEvidence` stays false → the idle-beyond-threshold stuck escalation no longer fires for stuck-on-prompt sessions. That's correct (a sticky inbox is not "idle"), but operators currently get a stuck notification after ~5min + threshold. After PR-A they only get the `needs_input` notification at t=0 and nothing else for that prompt. Surface this in release notes.

## Testing

- `pnpm build` ✅ (passes; existing warnings about optional `@composio/core` resolution and `useXtermTerminal.ts` lint warning during Next build)
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm lint` ✅ (0 errors, existing warnings)
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` ✅
- `pnpm test` ⚠️ fails in `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-linear` because optional `@composio/core` is not installed; unrelated to this core-only PR.

title: fix(agent-claude-code): add AO-JSONL safety net cascade (closes #1897)
body:
## Problem

Claude Code activity detection depended only on Claude's native `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl` lookup. If Claude changes that project slug format again, AO silently loses Claude activity detection. Codex already has an AO-JSONL safety-net cascade for this class of failure; Claude did not.

Closes #1897. References umbrella #1899. This is wave 1 alongside PR-A (#1902).

## Scope

- Import the shared AO activity-log helpers into `agent-claude-code`.
- Add `recordActivity()` so terminal observations are written to `<workspace>/.ao/activity.jsonl`.
- Keep native Claude JSONL as primary.
- When native lookup has no usable entry, fall back to:
  1. `checkActivityLogState()` for `waiting_input` / `blocked`
  2. `getActivityFallbackState()` for age-decay
  3. `null` if both are unavailable

No Codex native-file mtime fallback was added.

## Tests

Added coverage for:

1. `recordActivity` writes to `.ao/activity.jsonl` when `workspacePath` is set, and no-ops when null.
2. Native Claude JSONL succeeds and remains primary over AO JSONL.
3. Missing native session file plus fresh AO `waiting_input` returns `waiting_input`.
4. Missing native session file plus aged AO `active` entry decays to `idle`.
5. Both native and AO activity unavailable returns `null`.

## Verification

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint` (passes with existing warnings)
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test`

title: feat(web,core): "Launch Orchestrator (clean context)" button
body:
## Summary

Adds a dashboard action that always replaces the project's canonical orchestrator with a fresh one — killing any existing orchestrator, deleting its metadata, and spawning a new session with **no carryover state**.

- **core:** new `SessionManager.relaunchOrchestrator(config)` method that does **kill → deleteMetadata → spawnOrchestrator**. Ignores `project.orchestratorSessionStrategy` — replacement is the whole point of this entry point.
- **web API:** `POST /api/orchestrators` accepts `{ clean: true }` to route to the new method (default behavior unchanged).
- **UI:** `OrchestratorSelector` renders a second button "Launch Orchestrator (clean context)" that uses `window.confirm()` before discarding an existing orchestrator. No confirm prompt when no orchestrator exists (nothing to discard).

## Why

Users had no way to start an orchestrator with a clean slate from the dashboard. Previous orchestrator context (conversation history, stale state) silently carried over via the existing "Open Orchestrator" flow, which only worked cleanly for first-time spawn anyway.

Per harshit's design decision on #1900: **Replace approach** (kill existing, wipe state, spawn new) — not multi-instance.

## Design notes

- **Coalescing:** `relaunchOrchestrator` uses a **separate** `relaunchOrchestratorPromises` map, **not** the shared `ensureOrchestratorPromises`. Sharing the map would mean a relaunch piggy-backing on an in-flight `ensure` could return the existing orchestrator instead of a fresh one — wrong semantics. Concurrency between `ensure` and `relaunch` on the same project is rare; the `kill` inside `relaunch` handles whichever state lands.
- **No new core invariants broken:** `spawn`, `ensureOrchestrator`, `spawnOrchestrator` are untouched. The new method is purely additive on `SessionManager`.

## Test plan

- [x] Core: 5 new tests in `session-manager/spawn.test.ts` covering fresh spawn, replace-with-existing, ignores `orchestratorSessionStrategy: ignore`, concurrent-call coalescing, and orchestrator-prompt file rewrite. All passing.
- [x] Web API: 2 new tests in `api-routes.test.ts` covering `clean: true` → `relaunchOrchestrator` and `clean: false` → `spawnOrchestrator`. All passing.
- [x] UI: 5 new tests in `OrchestratorSelector.test.tsx` covering button render, confirm-on-existing, cancel skips POST, no-confirm-on-empty, and error surfacing. All passing.
- [x] Full suite: `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` — clean on core (1211 tests) and web (917 tests + 4 skipped). Pre-existing tracker-linear failure unrelated.

Closes #1900
Closes #1080

title: refactor(core): introduce ActivityReducer; consolidate dual getActivityState path
body:
## Problem

Wave 2 of #1899. The activity pipeline still had the tracking issue's "two probers, divergent writes" problem: `lifecycle-manager` and `session-manager` could both call `getActivityState`, and `ao send --wait` had a third terminal-output parser path.

Prior context: #1902 and #1903.

## Scope

- Add `packages/core/src/activity-reducer.ts` with reducer APIs:
  - `snapshot`
  - `applyEvent`
  - `applyLivenessTick`
  - `applyProcessProbe`
  - `clearInbox`
  - `composeActivity`
  - `subscribe`
- Route lifecycle activity observations and process probes through the reducer.
- Remove `session-manager`'s `getActivityState` probe; it now mirrors reducer snapshots into `session.activity` / `session.activitySignal`.
- Replace send-await's `detectActivityFromOutput` closure with reducer subscription for active / waiting-input rising edges.
- Update session-manager query tests for the new single-writer contract.

No plugin changes.

## Reducer behavior

- Splits liveness (`active` / `ready` / `idle` / `exited`) from sticky inbox (`waiting_input` / `blocked` / `null`).
- Ages liveness with the existing active/ready windows.
- Keeps inbox sticky until process death, explicit clear, or override handling.
- Composes legacy activity at the boundary with precedence: `exited > inbox > liveness`.

## Tests

- Added `activity-reducer.test.ts` for sticky inbox, liveness updates, process-death clearing, compose precedence, and subscription notifications.
- Updated session-manager query tests to assert it does not call `getActivityState` and reads reducer snapshots instead.
- Ran:
  - `pnpm build` ✅
  - `pnpm typecheck` ✅
  - `pnpm lint` ✅ (existing warnings only)
  - `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` ✅
  - `pnpm test` ⚠️ run, but existing `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-linear` tests fail because optional `@composio/core` is not installed in this checkout.

## #1899 checklist

- [x] PR-C — Introduce ActivityReducer in core; lifecycle-manager owns it; session-manager reads snapshot; two `getActivityState` call sites consolidate to one; send-await subscribes instead of running its own detect.

-   8c71bde: Harden Claude Code activity detection against five real-world edge cases identified during PR #1927's analysis:

    1.  **Bookkeeping types → false-active.** `file-history-snapshot`, `attachment`, `pr-link`, `queue-operation`, `permission-mode`, `last-prompt`, `ai-title`, `agent-color`, `agent-name`, `custom-title` were falling through to the `default` switch branch and showing as `active` for 30s after Claude finished a turn.     4.  **Process regex too narrow.** `(?:^|\/)claude(?:\s|$)` was missing several legitimate install variants — `.claude`, `claude-code`, `claude.exe`, `claude.js`, and npm shims like `node /opt/.../@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js`. Broadened to `(?:^|\/)(?:\.)?claude(?:[-.][\w-]+)*(?:[\s/]|$)`; still rejects look-alikes (`claudia`, `claudine`).
    5.  **Silent permission-denied.** `findLatestSessionFile` was swallowing every `readdir` error silently — a missing `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/` (ENOENT) is normal, but a permission-denied (EACCES/EPERM) or fd-exhausted (EMFILE) misconfig left the session looking permanently `idle` on the dashboard with zero telemetry. Now logs a single `console.warn` for non-ENOENT errors.

    193/193 plugin tests pass. No public-API change. New helper `resolveWorkspaceForClaude` is re-exported from `index.ts` for downstream consumers.

### Minor Changes

-   73bed33: Wire activity events into webhook ingress and the mux WebSocket terminal server (sub-issue of #1511, follows #1620).

    -   `api.webhook_unverified` (warn) — signature verification failed; data includes `slug`, `remoteAddr`, `candidateCount` (never the failed signature)
    -   `api.webhook_rejected` (warn) — payload exceeded `maxBodyBytes`; data includes counts and `maxBodyBytes` (never the body)
    -   `api.webhook_received` (info|warn) — accepted webhook; data includes `projectIds`, `matchedSessions`, `parseErrorCount`, `lifecycleErrorCount` (never the body)
    -   `api.webhook_failed` (error) — outer pipeline crash with `errorMessage`
    -   `ui.terminal_connected` / `ui.terminal_disconnected` — one event per mux WS connection lifecycle
    -   `ui.terminal_heartbeat_lost` (warn) — fires once on 3 missed pongs (was console-only)
    -   `ui.terminal_pty_lost` (warn) — fires when PTY exits with subscribers attached (distinguishes "PTY died" from "user closed browser")
    -   `ui.terminal_protocol_error` (warn) — invalid mux client message
    -   `ui.session_broadcast_failed` (warn) — emitted on the healthy→failing transition only (re-arms after a successful poll), so a long outage produces one event, not 20/min

    `api.webhook_unverified` is the security-audit event; treat 401s on webhooks as a signal worth retaining for the full 7-day window.

-   94981dc: feat: "Launch Orchestrator (clean context)" action on the orchestrator session page

    Adds a `Relaunch (clean)` action on the orchestrator session page that replaces the project's canonical orchestrator with a fresh one — killing the existing orchestrator, deleting its metadata, and spawning a new session with no carryover state. Backed by a new `SessionManager.relaunchOrchestrator(config)` method that ignores `orchestratorSessionStrategy`. Removes the now-redundant Orchestrator Selector page (`/orchestrators?project=X`) — there is only ever one orchestrator per project, so a selector page is no longer meaningful. Closes #1900 and #1080.

### Patch Changes

-   ee3fb5d: Fix Done/Terminated section on the dashboard not scrolling. The dashboard body now scrolls as a single page — kanban above, Done/Terminated below — so older terminated sessions are reachable when many accumulate. Restores the pre-Warm-Terminal-refresh behavior by dropping the `flex: 1` that was making `.kanban-board-wrap` greedily consume all remaining body height and defeat the body's `overflow-y: auto`.

-   2980570: Add the notifier test harness, dashboard notifications, and desktop notifier setup.

-   07c9099: fix(web): show Restore button for every exited session, including pr_merged

    The Restore button was hidden for sessions exited with `pr_merged` reason (legacy
    status `cleanup`) on the dashboard kanban and absent altogether from the
    session-detail "Terminal ended" panel. The core `isRestorable()` helper already
    allowed restoring these sessions; the dashboard helpers were out of sync. Fixes
    \#1907.

    -   `isDashboardSessionRestorable` now gates on `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES` only,
        matching core's `isRestorable`. Merged-but-running sessions remain
        non-restorable (lifecycle isn't terminal).
    -   `DoneCard` no longer hides Restore for merged sessions.
    -   `SessionEndedSummary` exposes a prominent `Restore session` button next to
        `Open PR` / `Back to dashboard`, so users don't have to find the small
        header icon.

title: feat(web): Show Restore button for all session exit states (including pr_merged)
body:
## Problem

The Restore button is hidden when a session's exit reason is `pr_merged`. The session detail page shows "TERMINAL ENDED" with only "Open PR" and "Back to dashboard" actions.

User expects **every** session to be restorable regardless of exit state.

## Current Behavior

- Sessions exited with `pr_merged` reason hide the Restore button
- Only "Open PR" and "Back to dashboard" actions are shown
- User cannot restore the session to continue work

## Expected Behavior

- **Every** exited session should show a Restore button, regardless of exit reason
- For `pr_merged` sessions, restore could re-spawn the agent in a fresh context or allow continuing work

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a session that creates a PR
2. Merge the PR
3. Navigate to the session detail page
4. Observe: no Restore button — only "Open PR" and "Back to dashboard"

## Screenshot

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd30dc0bd455.png)

## Environment

- Session: `ao-155`
- PR: #1904 (merged)
- Branch: `feat/1900`
- Runtime status: `missing` (tmux gone)

title: Restore: requiresNativeRestore() refuses fallback when no native session ever existed; UI shows Restore button anyway
body:
## Symptom

User spawns an empty session (`ao spawn` with no prompt, no issue → e.g. `ao-157`). Runtime is later lost (`ao stop`, AO restart, Ctrl+C of `ao start`). Dashboard shows:

- Sidebar entry, status `killed`
- Banner: *"Terminal ended — tmux missing. The live terminal is gone, but the session context is still available."*
- Lifecycle: `Detecting runtime truth (runtime lost)`
- Activity signal: `null via_native`
- **Restore** button is offered

Clicking Restore:

```
POST /api/sessions/ao-157/restore → 409 Conflict
{"error":"Session ao-157 cannot be restored: claude-code.getRestoreCommand returned null"}
```

## Context — how this differs from #1611

#1611 had the same surface error but a **different root cause**: `toClaudeProjectPath` was failing to fold underscores, so AO computed the wrong slug and missed an existing JSONL. PR #1612 fixed the slug encoding; in that scenario `metadata.claudeSessionUuid` now gets persisted on every poll and restore works.

The author of #1611 explicitly defended the `requiresNativeRestore` gate at that time: *"The native-restore guard from #1602 is the right behavior; it was firing because the core slug encoding was wrong."*

That defense holds for #1611, but **does not cover #1908**. Here the JSONL was never written in the first place:

- `claude` is launched in interactive REPL with only `--append-system-prompt` (no positional prompt, no `-p`) — see `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:876-913`.
- The keep-alive shell in `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:49,101-115` keeps tmux up even if claude exits, so the runtime survives the spawn.
- Claude sits in REPL waiting for user input. With no conversation, no `~/.claude/projects/{slug}/*.jsonl` is ever written, and `getSessionInfo` never persists `metadata.claudeSessionUuid`.
- When the tmux session is later lost externally, the restore path has **literally nothing to `--resume`** — not a lookup miss like #1611, but a true absence.

So this is the case the slug fix does not address. The gate fires correctly in the sense that there's no native session, but failing instead of falling back to a fresh launch is the wrong response when there was never a native session to begin with.

## Root Cause

`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2911-2925`:

```ts
if (plugins.agent.getRestoreCommand) {
  const restoreCmd = await plugins.agent.getRestoreCommand(session, projectConfigForLaunch);
  if (restoreCmd) {
    launchCommand = restoreCmd;
    updateMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, { restoreFallbackReason: "" });
  } else {
    const reason = `${plugins.agent.name}.getRestoreCommand returned null`;
    updateMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, { restoreFallbackReason: reason });
    if (requiresNativeRestore(plugins.agent.name)) {       // ← fires for claude-code | codex | opencode
      throw new SessionNotRestorableError(sessionId, reason);
    }
    launchCommand = plugins.agent.getLaunchCommand(agentLaunchConfig);
  }
}
```

`requiresNativeRestore` (`session-manager.ts:440-450`) is hardcoded to `claude-code | codex | opencode`. It treats *any* null return as terminal — it does not distinguish "I expected to find a native session and couldn't" from "no native session ever existed."

The semantics should be: **prefer native restore when one existed; otherwise fresh launch is the only sensible action.** The metadata already tells us which case we're in — presence of `claudeSessionUuid` / `codexThreadId` / `opencodeSessionId`.

`getRestoreCommand` returning null is **correct** here (`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:1044-1060`):
- `session.metadata?.claudeSessionUuid` is undefined (only `getSessionInfo` at line 1039 writes it, and it requires a JSONL).
- `findLatestSessionFile` fallback finds nothing — empty spawn never wrote one.

The plugin is doing the right thing; the gate above it is too strict.

## Compounding UI Bugs

### 1. Restore button shown unconditionally on terminal sessions

`isRestorable` (`packages/core/src/types.ts:260-272`) is **pure status math**:

```ts
return isTerminalSession(session) && !NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES.has(session.status);
```

`NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES` is the empty set (`types.ts:236`). So every terminal session — including ones the agent plugin already knows cannot be resumed — gets a Restore button.

`SessionDetailHeader.tsx:266-285` and `SessionCard.tsx:288,517` consume this and render the button. The server knows the action will 409; the UI offers it anyway. Error is surfaced verbatim by `Dashboard.tsx:416-436` and `SessionDetail.tsx:103-116` as *"Restore failed: …"* toasts.

### 2. Sidebar surfaces the broken session as "needs attention"

`packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:289-292` only filters when `getAttentionLevel(s) === "done"`:

```ts
const level = getAttentionLevel(s);
if (level === "done") {
  if (s.status === "killed" ? !showKilled && !showDone : !showDone) continue;
}
```

For a runtime-lost session, `lifecycle.session.state === "detecting"` and `lifecycle.session.reason === "runtime_lost"` (`session-manager.ts:1037-1038`). `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts:488-497` classifies that as **"respond"**:

```ts
if (
  session.lifecycle?.sessionState === "detecting" ||
  session.lifecycle?.sessionState === "needs_input" ||
  session.lifecycle?.sessionState === "stuck" ||
  ...
) return "respond";
```

So the sidebar filter is bypassed entirely — the dead session is permanently visible regardless of "Show killed" / "Show done" toggles, because the system thinks the user needs to act on it. The only action offered (Restore) is the one that 409s.

The classification is *internally consistent* — agent died, surface to human, give them Restore. The bug is that the offered action is broken. Fixing the core gate fixes the sidebar UX too: Restore actually relaunches, justifying the "respond" classification.

## Not a bug

- `MuxProvider.tsx` has no auto-restore logic — confirmed by reading the file. The 409 comes from the user clicking the Restore button, not from automatic recovery.
- Claude exiting on empty launch is not the issue — the keep-alive shell keeps tmux alive. The runtime loss happens externally (user-driven `ao stop` / Ctrl+C / AO restart).

## Reproduction

1. `ao spawn` (no prompt, no issue) → session created, claude in REPL
2. Don't interact with the session
3. `ao stop` (or Ctrl+C of `ao start`) → tmux killed
4. `ao start` → session restored from `last-stop.json` but runtime dead
5. Dashboard shows session in sidebar (cannot be hidden via toggles) with Restore button
6. Click Restore → 409

## Suggested Fix

### 1. Core (root) — `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2911-2925`

Distinguish "lookup miss" from "never existed":

```ts
const NATIVE_SESSION_METADATA_KEYS = ["claudeSessionUuid", "codexThreadId", "opencodeSessionId"];
const hasNativeMarker = NATIVE_SESSION_METADATA_KEYS.some((k) => session.metadata?.[k]);

if (requiresNativeRestore(plugins.agent.name) && hasNativeMarker) {
  throw new SessionNotRestorableError(sessionId, reason);
}
launchCommand = plugins.agent.getLaunchCommand(agentLaunchConfig);
updateMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, {
  restoreFallbackReason: "no native session — relaunched fresh",
});
```

This preserves #1602's protection from #1590 (when a native session previously existed but is now unreachable, we still refuse to silently start a fresh chat) while unblocking the case where no native session was ever recorded.

### 2. UI parity — make restorability agent-aware

Option A: server computes `canRestore: boolean` on `Session` (using the same metadata-marker check) and the UI consults it before showing the button.

Option B: extend `isRestorable` to consult the same metadata markers.

Either way, `SessionDetailHeader.tsx:266` and `SessionCard.tsx:288,517` stop offering an action the server already knows will succeed-via-fallback or 409. Without (1) the button leads to 409; without (2) the button keeps appearing even for sessions the user can't meaningfully restore from native.

### 3. Empty-spawn ergonomics (optional)

`packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts:269-336` could emit a one-line warning when neither `[issue]` nor `--prompt` is given: *"spawning blank session — agent will idle until you type."* Empty spawn is a legitimate flow ("open me a worktree to think in") but should be intentional.

## Related

- #1611 / #1612 — slug encoding fix (different root cause, fixed)
- #1602 / #1590 — added the `requiresNativeRestore` gate this issue is refining
- #1642 — sibling case for codex when `codexThreadId` is lost (same gate, same recommended fix)
- #1475 — `getRestoreCommand` signature loses per-session resolved permissions/subagent — adjacent restore-path bug

title: fix(core): restore falls through to fresh launch when no native marker exists (closes #1908)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1908.

Empty `ao spawn` (no prompt, no issue) never persists a native session marker (`claudeSessionUuid` / `codexThreadId` / `opencodeSessionId`). When the runtime died and the user clicked **Restore**, the `requiresNativeRestore` gate threw `SessionNotRestorableError` with *\"<agent>.getRestoreCommand returned null\"* — leaving no recovery path on the exact session the user was trying to revive.

The semantics of `requiresNativeRestore` should be *\"prefer native when one existed\"*, not *\"forbid relaunch when none ever existed\"*. After this PR:

- **No marker present** → fall through to `getLaunchCommand` (matches non-native agents).
- **Marker present + `getRestoreCommand` returns null** → still throw (the user expected `--resume` of a real conversation; silently relaunching would lose it).

## What changed

- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`
  - New `hasNativeRestoreMarker(agentName, metadata)` checking the per-agent marker keys.
  - Gate at `session-manager.ts:3005` throws only when both `requiresNativeRestore(name)` AND a marker exists; otherwise falls through.
  - `restoreFallbackReason` records *\"(no native marker — relaunched fresh)\"* when the fallback path runs for a native-restore agent.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/restore.test.ts`
  - Repurposed the existing throw-test to assert **fresh launch** when no marker is in metadata.
  - Added a new test: throw when `codexThreadId` IS in metadata but `getRestoreCommand` returns null (defensive behavior preserved).

## Invariants preserved

- Non-native-restore agents (`aider`, `kimicode`, etc.) unchanged.
- Native-restore agents WITH a marker still refuse to relaunch fresh — protecting users from silent context loss.
- `restoreFallbackReason` metadata still tracks the fallback path for audit.
- No plugin file changes.

## Out of scope

The issue body flags a *\"compounding UI bug\"* (Restore button always rendered, server says 409). After this core fix, the documented repro (empty spawn → `ao stop` → click Restore) **succeeds**, so the spurious 409 toast is mooted. A server-computed `canRestore` for the rare marker-orphan edge case (marker present but session file gone) would need new infra (filesystem checks exposed via `Session`) and is left for a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test src/__tests__/session-manager/restore.test.ts` → 28/28 pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` → clean

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` → all packages clean
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn` (empty) → `ao stop` → `ao start` → click Restore → agent relaunches with fresh prompt instead of 409

#1475 (per-session permissions/model/subagent lost on restore) is the sibling restore-path bug and will follow as a separate PR stacked on this one's branch.

title: fix(core): persist resolved per-session permissions/model/subagent for restore (closes #1475)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1475.

> **Note:** stacked on top of #1910 (issue #1908 fix). The session-manager.ts diff includes the #1908 changes; this PR can be merged after #1910 lands, or rebased onto main once #1910 merges.

When a session is restored, the agent was being re-launched against whatever the project's *current* `agentConfig` resolved to — silently dropping the session's **original spawn-time** permissions / model / subagent if the project config had drifted between spawn and restore. Affected every agent plugin that reads `project.agentConfig?.permissions` inside `getRestoreCommand` (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `kimicode`).

## Approach B (zero plugin file changes)

Per the issue body and AO direction, we keep the plugin interface and plugin files untouched. The fix is a thin plumbing layer:

1. **Persist at spawn.** `_spawnInner` and `spawnOrchestrator` now write `selection.permissions` / `selection.model` / `selection.subagent` into session metadata as `spawnedPermissions` / `spawnedModel` / `spawnedSubagent`.
2. **Read on restore.** `resolveSelectionForSession` reads those keys back and passes them to `resolveAgentSelection` as new optional `persistedPermissions` / `persistedModel` / `persistedSubagent` inputs.
3. **Override in selection.** `resolveAgentSelection` mirrors the existing `persistedAgent` pattern — when persisted values are present, they win over project defaults and are written into both the top-level fields AND the returned `agentConfig`.
4. **Propagation is automatic.** `session-manager.ts` already builds `projectConfigForLaunch.agentConfig` from `selection.agentConfig` (lines 2968-2977), so plugins reading `project.agentConfig?.permissions` / `.model` / `.subagent` transparently see the persisted values inside `getRestoreCommand`.

## Files touched

- `packages/core/src/agent-selection.ts` — three new optional inputs + threading them into `agentConfig` and the top-level return.
- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — write `spawned*` keys at both spawn paths; read them in `resolveSelectionForSession`.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/agent-selection.test.ts` — new file, 6 unit tests.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/restore.test.ts` — 2 new integration tests.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts` — 1 new test.

**Zero plugin file changes.**

## Invariants preserved

- **Orchestrator forced-permissionless** still enforced at `projectConfigForLaunch` and `agentLaunchConfig` construction in `session-manager.ts:2968-3003`. `selection.permissions` for an orchestrator may be e.g. `\"auto-edit\"` from persisted metadata, but the override at construction time ensures the agent always launches permissionless. Unit test (\"orchestrator role honors persistedPermissions at resolution time\") documents this seam.
- **`persistedAgent` pattern unchanged.** The new inputs are added next to it and follow the identical shape.
- **Legacy sessions unaffected** beyond what they already did: without `spawned*` metadata they resolve to current project defaults — accepted per the issue body (\"acceptable — they were already broken\"). Test covers this explicitly.
- **No plugin interface changes.** `Agent.getRestoreCommand(session, project)` signature is unchanged; only the contents of `project.agentConfig` flowing through are different.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test src/__tests__/agent-selection.test.ts` → 6/6 pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test src/__tests__/session-manager/restore.test.ts` → 30/30 pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts` → all pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` → 1224 passing (6 pre-existing sqlite-binding failures unrelated)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` → clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` → all packages clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` → 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm build` → all packages
- [ ] Manual: set `agentConfig.permissions: suggest` in yaml → `ao spawn` (verify metadata has `spawnedPermissions: suggest`) → change yaml to `permissionless` → restore session → agent launches with `--ask` (suggest) flag, not `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

## Coordinated with

- #1910 (issue #1908 fix) — sibling restore-path bug, stacked under this PR.

title: feat: add PR review skill for agent-driven and human PR reviews
body:
## What

Adds `skills/pr-review/SKILL.md` — a structured PR review workflow for the Agent Orchestrator repo, usable by both bot agents and human reviewers.

## Why

PR [#1819](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1819) leaked 3 orphaned submodule refs to `main` because neither the bot nor the reviewer caught unintended changes in the diff. This skill makes scope validation a **mandatory first step** for every review.

## Skill Contents

8-step review workflow:
1. **Gather context** — PR metadata, file list, CI status
2. **Scope & hygiene check** (mandatory first) — submodules, unrelated files, stray docs/plans, config drift
3. **Correctness** — optional type fields, cross-platform (`isWindows()`), lifecycle state, config nullability
4. **Code quality** — surgical changes, no speculative features, no debug leftovers
5. **Testing** — reproducing tests for bugs, proportional coverage for features
6. **PR metadata** — conventional commits, linkified refs, issue linking
7. **Verdict** — severity-structured findings (Critical / Warning / Suggestion / Scope Violation)
8. **Submit review** — summary comment + inline comments via `gh`

Also updates `AGENTS.md` to reference the new skill alongside `bug-triage`.

## Key Rule

> Scope violations block merge. Reviewers must explicitly tell contributors that unrelated changes (stray docs, plans, submodules, config drift) can lead to the PR not getting merged.

## Files Changed
- `skills/pr-review/SKILL.md` — new skill (201 lines)
- `AGENTS.md` — added PR Review skill section

@Priyanchew for review.

title: Fix: Sanitize project ID derived from folder name to allow dots and special chars
body:
## Fix: Sanitize project ID derived from folder name

Issue: #1877

**Problem:** When running `ao start` in a directory with dots or special characters in its name (e.g. `llama.cpp`), the project ID is set to the raw folder name which fails validation because project IDs must match `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`.

**Root Cause:** In `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`, line 662:
```ts
let projectId = basename(resolvedPath);
```
This uses the folder name directly without sanitizing invalid characters.

**Fix:** Apply the same sanitization pattern already used elsewhere in the file (line 154):
```ts
let projectId = basename(resolvedPath).replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "") || basename(resolvedPath);
```

This replaces invalid characters with `-` and trims leading/trailing dashes, converting `llama.cpp` to `llama-cpp`.

Closes #1877

title: fix(web): address post-merge Greptile feedback — mobile sidebar, dead variable, sessionStorage race
body:
## Summary

Three issues identified by Greptile post-merge review of PR #1846 (sidebar/dashboard header UI/UX polish).

## Issues

### 1. Mobile sidebar stays open after project switch on root `/` dashboard

The shared-layout refactor dropped `useEffect(() => setMobileMenuOpen(false), [searchParams])` from `Dashboard.tsx`. `ProjectLayoutClient` handles this for `/projects/*` routes via pathname-based close, but the standalone root dashboard at `/` has no equivalent. On mobile, switching the active project via `?project=…` leaves the sidebar overlay stuck open.

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx`

### 2. Dead `_isLoading` variable in `ProjectSidebar`

`const _isLoading = loading || sessions === null` was left in when inline `sessions === null` checks replaced its usage. Never read after the rename.

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx`

### 3. `sessionStorage` IIFE runs on every render (React Strict Mode race)

The IIFE that reads and removes the `ao-session-nav:{id}` key runs as a side-effect inside the render function. React Strict Mode double-invokes the component in dev — the first call consumes and removes the entry, the second call gets `null`. This defeats the navigation-cache optimisation (no-loading-flash when clicking a session from the sidebar) entirely in development.

**File:** `packages/web/src/app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`

## Fix

- Restore `useEffect` to close mobile sidebar on `searchParams` change, guarded with `!isInsideLayout` so it's a no-op on the project-layout path
- Remove dead `_isLoading` variable; rename `loading` prop to `_loading`
- Convert IIFE + `useState(cachedSession)` to a single `useState` lazy initialiser so the sessionStorage read+remove runs exactly once per mount
