title: fix(agent-claude-code): harden activity detection against 5 real-world edge cases
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1927. Closes five edge cases identified in that PR's analysis — all in `activity-detection.ts`, all small, all backed by tests. One cohesive PR rather than five micro-PRs since they live in the same module.

### 1. Bookkeeping types → false-active (the big one)

\`file-history-snapshot\`, \`attachment\`, \`pr-link\`, \`queue-operation\`, \`permission-mode\`, \`last-prompt\`, \`ai-title\`, \`agent-color\`, \`agent-name\`, \`custom-title\` were hitting the \`default\` branch and showing as \`active\` for 30s after Claude finished a turn. This is almost certainly the root cause of \"Claude looks like it's still working when it's done\" reports (the #1908 family). Added explicit cases mapping them to \`ready\`/\`idle\` by age, same as \`assistant\`/\`summary\`. Three existing tests that asserted these returned \`active\` were testing the buggy behavior — updated to the correct behavior.

### 2. Multi-session disambiguation via \`claudeSessionUuid\`

When two Claude sessions are running in the same workspace, \`findLatestSessionFile\` picked newest-mtime — wrong session's JSONL whenever its sibling has just written. \`getSessionInfo\` already captures \`session.metadata.claudeSessionUuid\` but \`getClaudeActivityState\` ignored it. Now: if UUID is set, prefer \`<projectDir>/<UUID>.jsonl\` via \`stat()\`; fall back to newest-mtime when missing or not yet on disk.

### 3. Symlinked workspace paths produce wrong slug

If AO records \`workspacePath\` as a symlink and Claude resolves the target before slugifying, the two slugs diverge and AO looks in an empty dir forever. Added \`resolveWorkspaceForClaude(path)\` (\`realpathSync\` with fallback) and used it in all three slug-computing sites: \`getClaudeActivityState\`, \`getSessionInfo\`, \`getRestoreCommand\`. \`toClaudeProjectPath\` stays a pure string transform.

### 4. Process regex too narrow

\`(?:^|\/)claude(?:\s|$)\` was missing several real install variants — \`.claude\`, \`claude-code\`, \`claude.exe\`, \`claude.js\`, and npm shims like \`node /opt/.../@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js\`. AO would declare these sessions \`exited\` while Claude was running. Broadened to \`(?:^|\/)(?:\.)?claude(?:[-.][\w-]+)*(?:[\s/]|$)\`. Still rejects look-alikes (\`claudia\`, \`claudine\`) — covered by a dedicated test.

### 5. Silent permission-denied on \`~/.claude/projects/\`

\`findLatestSessionFile\` was swallowing every \`readdir\` error. ENOENT (dir doesn't exist yet) is normal and stays silent, but EACCES/EPERM/EMFILE used to leave the session looking permanently \`idle\` with zero telemetry. Now logs a single \`console.warn\` for non-ENOENT errors with the errno and path.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test\` — **193 passed** (was 178 on main; +15 new tests covering all 5 gaps)
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code typecheck\` — clean
- [x] All other plugin tests pass (tracker-linear failure is pre-existing missing \`@composio/core\` dep, unrelated)
- [ ] CI

## What changed

| File | + | − | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/activity-detection.ts\` | ~70 | ~10 | All 5 fixes: bookkeeping cases, UUID-prefer arg, realpath helper, regex, warn-on-non-ENOENT |
| \`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts\` | 3 | 3 | Import + re-export new helper; use it in \`getSessionInfo\`/\`getRestoreCommand\` |
| \`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/__tests__/activity-detection.test.ts\` | ~80 | ~10 | 15 new tests; 3 existing bookkeeping-as-active tests updated to bookkeeping-as-ready |
| \`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.test.ts\` | ~30 | ~15 | 8 new process-regex tests; deleted obsolete \"claude-code rejected\" test |
| \`.changeset/claude-activity-edge-cases.md\` | 17 | 0 | Changeset (patch) |

## What's NOT in this PR

- Collapsing \`active\`/\`ready\` into one state — bigger architectural change, touches \`LIVENESS_ACTIVITY_STATES\` and every \`supportsRecentLiveness\` consumer. Worth its own discussion.
- Removing dead \`tool_use\` / \`result\` switch cases — pure cleanup, behavior-equivalent, separate cosmetic diff.
- Detecting \`blocked\` from terminal regex (currently only via native JSONL \`system + api_error + level:error\` from #1927).
- Slug collisions on \`_\`↔\`.\`↔\`-\` — not really fixable AO-side without breaking compatibility with Claude's existing slugs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(core): `stuck` session with exited runtime never auto-promotes to `terminated` — lingers in sidebar indefinitely
body:
## Repro

Spawn a session, let the agent crash or exit without acknowledging (`reportWatcherActiveTrigger: no_acknowledge`). The lifecycle manager probes, sees `signal_disagreement` between the native activity signal (`activity=exited`) and the initial runtime probe (`runtime=alive`), runs through 50 detecting attempts, escalates, and parks the session at `state: stuck, reason: probe_failure`. The runtime probe eventually updates to `exited`, but the **session-level state never advances**.

## Observed state (real session `ao-165`)

```json
"lifecycle": {
  "session":  { "state": "stuck",  "reason": "probe_failure",  "terminatedAt": null,
                "lastTransitionAt": "2026-05-19T13:14:54.490Z" },
  "runtime":  { "state": "exited", "reason": "process_missing",
                "lastObservedAt": "2026-05-19T13:14:54.490Z" },
  "pr":       { "state": "none",   "reason": "not_created" }
},
"status": "stuck",
"detectingAttempts": "50",
"detectingEscalatedAt": "2026-05-19T12:27:51.146Z",
"lifecycleEvidence": "signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited",
"reportWatcherActiveTrigger": "no_acknowledge",
"reportWatcherTriggerCount": "41"
```

The agent process is gone, the runtime is gone, no PR was ever created — but the session is not terminated.

## Why this is a bug

The sidebar visibility gate in `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:454-457` only hides sessions whose `getAttentionLevel(session) === \"done\"`. A `stuck` lifecycle state routes to `respond` in `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts:504-512`:

```ts
if (session.lifecycle?.sessionState === \"stuck\" || ...) return \"respond\";
```

So the session sits on the sidebar with an orange dot forever. Neither the **Show killed** nor the **Show done** toggle helps — they only gate `done`-level sessions. The only ways to clear it today:
- `ao kill <id>` (manual)
- Click Restore (spawns a new runtime, leaves the record)
- `rm` the JSON by hand

That's not great UX for a session the lifecycle manager has already concluded is unrecoverable.

## Proposed fix (core, not surface)

When `resolveProbeDecision` (in `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`) determines:
- `runtime.state === \"exited\"` or `\"missing\"`, **and**
- native activity signal is `exited`, **and**
- no live PR depends on the runtime (`pr.state ∈ {none, closed_unmerged}`),

…it should promote `session.state` from `stuck` → `terminated` with `reason: probe_failure` (or a new `agent_process_exited` reason). `deriveLegacyStatus` already maps `error_in_process` / `probe_failure` → `errored`, which is in the done bucket, so the sidebar would then hide it by default once `showDone` is off.

Today the lifecycle treats `probe_failure` as \"I can't tell, escalate to a human\". But when *every* signal agrees the agent is gone, there's nothing to escalate — just terminate it.

## Out of scope (separate concerns)

- Restore button correctness: covered by #1908.
- Activity-detection redesign: covered by #1899.
- This is specifically about lifecycle promotion when runtime + native signal agree the agent has exited.

## File:line index

- Visibility gate: `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:454-457`
- `\"stuck\"` → `\"respond\"` mapping: `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts:504-512`
- `isDashboardSessionDone`: `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts:392-410`
- `deriveLegacyStatus` terminal-reason mapping: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts:444-460`
- Probe decision pipeline: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` (`resolveProbeDecision`)

title: discuss: do we need a separate `ready` activity state, or can we collapse it into `active` + timestamp?
body:
## Question

Today the `ActivityState` vocabulary is six values: `active`, `ready`, `idle`, `waiting_input`, `blocked`, `exited`. The distinction between `active` and `ready` is purely an age bucket of "recent activity":

- `active` — last entry within last 30s (`DEFAULT_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS`)
- `ready` — last entry between 30s and 5min (`DEFAULT_READY_THRESHOLD_MS`)
- `idle` — last entry older than 5min

Should we keep `ready` as a first-class state, or collapse to `active` (with the existing timestamp) + `idle` and let consumers derive the rest?

## Where `ready` is currently load-bearing

`packages/core/src/activity-signal.ts:10`:
```ts
const LIVENESS_ACTIVITY_STATES: ReadonlySet<ActivityState> = new Set(["active", "ready"]);
```

`packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:306` uses `supportsRecentLiveness` to keep a session in `detecting` rather than declaring it `exited` when the runtime probe says dead but recent activity argued otherwise. So `ready` is part of the "recently alive" signal.

Both states carry a `timestamp`, so the same consumer logic could be written as `state === "active" && now - timestamp < THRESHOLD` instead of `state in LIVENESS_ACTIVITY_STATES`.

## Trade-offs

### Keep `ready`
- Dashboard can render different colors/labels for "actively typing" vs "recently was working" without doing arithmetic at the view layer.
- Existing consumers (web, CLI status) probably do switch on the state directly today — collapsing would be a wider refactor.
- All agent plugins (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Aider, Cursor, Kimi) emit `ready` — six places to change.

### Collapse to `active` + `idle`
- Smaller state vocabulary, easier to reason about, fewer permutations to test.
- Consumers that need the dashboard-color distinction can derive it from the timestamp: `Date.now() - timestamp.getTime() < ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS`.
- Stuck-detection logic (`supportsRecentLiveness`) becomes a function of `(state === "active", timestamp)` rather than a Set lookup.
- Net code-size win is moderate but not huge.

### Hybrid: keep `ready` only in the state enum, drop the active/ready split in plugin logic
- Plugins always return `active` (with timestamp). Lifecycle/dashboard derive `ready` for display when timestamp is between the two windows.
- Centralizes the decay logic in one place (`activity-signal.ts`) instead of duplicated in every plugin's `getActivityState`.

## Context

Came up while reviewing the Claude Code activity cascade in PRs #1927 and #1932. The plugin code currently has roughly:

```ts
case "user":
case "progress":
  if (ageMs <= activeWindowMs) return { state: "active", timestamp };
  return { state: ageMs > threshold ? "idle" : "ready", timestamp };
```

The same pattern is repeated for every agent plugin (Codex, OpenCode, Aider, Kimi, Cursor) — each implements the same age-decay logic with subtle variations. Centralizing this would also reduce drift between plugins.

## What I'd like to discuss

1. Is the active/ready dashboard color/label distinction actually used today? (I haven't traced the web consumer.)
2. If yes, can we centralize the decay logic in `activity-signal.ts` so plugins only need to emit `(active, timestamp)` and the derived `ready` is computed once?
3. If no, is it worth the cross-plugin churn to collapse the enum?

No PR yet — opening this to align before touching plugin contracts.

title: Next.js dev server OOM crash — JavaScript heap out of memory (~4GB) on ao start
body:
## Bug Report

**Reporter:** @yyovil  
**Environment:** macOS, Nix-managed Node.js 22.22.1 (`nodejs-slim` via Nix store), branch `feat/droid-agent-plugin`

## Summary

Running `ao start` causes the Next.js dev server to consume ~4GB+ of heap memory and crash with a fatal OOM error. The process aborts and the user is forced to kill all running applications to recover system memory.

## Crash Details

```
[next] FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

### Pre-crash errors observed in terminal:

```
[direct-terminal] [SessionBroadcaster] fetchSnapshot error: This operation was aborted
[direct-terminal] [MuxServer] Mux connection closed
```

### GC data (last cycles before crash):

```
Scavenge / Mark-Compact — heap usage ~4087 MB to ~4135 MB
```

### Stack trace highlights:

- V8 engine heap allocation failures (`v8::internal::Heap::AllocateRawWithLightRetrySlowPath`)
- `v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration`
- `Builtins_StringSlowFlatten`, `Builtins_PromiseFulfillReactionJob`
- libuv event loop (`uv__io_poll`, `uv_run`)
- Final: `abort ao start` — process exits with code `null`

### Full native stack trace (37 frames):

```
1: 0x10429c9d4 node::OOMErrorHandler
2: 0x1033d7c40 v8::internal::V8::FatalProcessOutOfMemory
3: 0x103522a30 v8::internal::Heap::AllocateRawWithLightRetrySlowPath
...
11: 0x1033599d4 v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration
...
37: 0x1874c3da4 start [/usr/lib/dyld]
[1] 10191 abort ao start
```

All native frames resolve to `/nix/store/0hwvnfndqy5jzdy05hq3rzwvbs9yask2-nodejs-slim-22.22.1/bin/node`.

## Impact

- **Severity: High** — renders `ao start` unusable on the affected branch/setup
- User had to quit all running applications to recover from the memory leak
- SessionBroadcaster fetchSnapshot errors and MuxServer disconnections precede the crash, suggesting a memory leak in the SSE/WebSocket broadcasting layer

## Possible Root Causes

1. **SessionBroadcaster snapshot polling** — repeated aborted fetch operations may be leaking memory (unaborted fetches accumulating in memory)
2. **MuxServer connection handling** — closed mux connections may not be properly cleaned up
3. **Next.js dev server + SSE stream** — the 5s-interval SSE stream may accumulate uncollected response objects
4. **Node.js slim build** — `nodejs-slim` from Nix may have different memory management characteristics

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `ao start` on branch `feat/droid-agent-plugin`
2. Observe terminal for SessionBroadcaster/MuxServer errors
3. Monitor memory usage — expect rapid growth to ~4GB
4. Process aborts with OOM

title: fix(web): coalesce session snapshot fetches
body:
## Summary
- Share one in-flight SessionBroadcaster snapshot fetch across mux subscribers instead of starting duplicate requests per reconnect/subscriber.
- Abort the active snapshot request when the final mux subscriber disconnects, and do not reuse that intentionally-aborted request for later subscribers.
- Keep the 4s timeout active through response body parsing so stalled `/api/sessions/patches` responses fail instead of hanging indefinitely.

Closes #1935

## Tests
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- server/__tests__/mux-websocket.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web... build`
- `pnpm exec prettier --check packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts packages/web/server/__tests__/mux-websocket.test.ts .changeset/session-broadcaster-fetch-oom.md`

## Notes
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed, with an existing non-fatal `node-pty` rebuild warning from the local Nix/Xcode toolchain (`fatal error: 'functional' file not found`). The package postinstall reports this as non-critical; tests/build above passed.

title: bug(notifier): hanging delivery can block later notifiers and lifecycle polling
body:
## Bug
A slow or hanging notifier delivery can block the rest of the notifier fan-out and the lifecycle poll that triggered it.

**Source:** post-merge review of [PR #1736](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1736) | **Reported by:** post-merge reviewer | **Analyzed against:** `a610601158937082133b9e366235432ed6e441d1` (merge commit under review: `298057044f3f7d36524785a60c90fe4381f88698`)
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
1. Configure at least two notifiers for the same priority, for example:
   ```yaml
   notificationRouting:
     urgent: [webhook, desktop]
   notifiers:
     webhook:
       plugin: webhook
       url: http://10.255.255.1/hang
     desktop:
       plugin: desktop
   ```
2. Trigger an urgent lifecycle notification (for example `session.stuck`) or run the equivalent path through `ao notify test --route urgent`.
3. Observe that delivery awaits the first target before attempting the second target; if the first fetch hangs, the second notifier is not reached promptly and the lifecycle check remains blocked.

## Root Cause
`notifyHuman()` fans out sequentially and awaits each notifier before continuing:

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:2274-2298` loops `for (const name of notifierNames)` and `await notifier.notify(eventWithPriority)`.

Some network notifiers still do not enforce a delivery timeout:

- Slack uses bare `fetch()` without an `AbortController` (`packages/plugins/notifier-slack/src/index.ts:342-347`).
- Generic webhook uses bare `fetch()` inside retry handling (`packages/plugins/notifier-webhook/src/index.ts:42-58`).

Discord setup added an abort timeout in the provider path, which shows the intended pattern (`packages/plugins/notifier-discord/src/index.ts:343-351`).

## Impact
- A misconfigured or unreachable webhook/Slack endpoint can prevent later notifiers in the same route from receiving the alert.
- Lifecycle polling can be delayed by notification delivery, making session state/reaction handling less reliable.
- This violates the notifier isolation goal from the PR: one bad destination should not suppress or substantially delay other destinations.

## Fix
- Add bounded delivery timeouts to all network notifiers (Slack and generic webhook at minimum), preferably configurable with safe defaults.
- Consider changing core fan-out to `Promise.allSettled()` over resolved targets so independent notifiers run concurrently and failures are isolated.
- Keep per-target `recordNotificationDelivery()` observability for success/failure/timeout.

## Related
- [PR #1736](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1736) — introduced the robust notifier routing/setup surface.

title: bug(desktop-notifier): platform checks and localhost defaults bypass cross-platform helpers
body:
## Bug
The new desktop notifier/setup code added platform branching and localhost defaults outside AO's central cross-platform helpers.

**Source:** post-merge review of [PR #1736](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1736) | **Reported by:** post-merge reviewer | **Analyzed against:** `a610601158937082133b9e366235432ed6e441d1` (merge commit under review: `298057044f3f7d36524785a60c90fe4381f88698`)
**Confidence:** High for the code path/guideline violation; Medium for user-visible Windows impact until tested on Windows.

## Reproduction / Inspection
1. Inspect `packages/cli/src/lib/desktop-setup.ts` and `packages/plugins/notifier-desktop/src/index.ts` after PR #1736.
2. Observe direct platform handling:
   - `desktop-setup.ts` imports `platform` from `node:os` and wraps it in local `currentPlatform()` (`lines 1-4`, `68-70`).
   - `desktop-setup.ts` branches on `currentPlatform() === "darwin"` / `!== "darwin"` (`lines 462-464`, `532-534`).
   - `notifier-desktop/src/index.ts` imports `platform` and branches on `os === "darwin"`, `os === "linux"`, and `os === "win32"` (`lines 1-4`, `413-421`, `488-500`).
3. Observe dashboard URLs synthesized with `localhost` in setup (`desktop-setup.ts:366-370`).

## Root Cause
AO's cross-platform rule says platform branching should live in `@aoagents/ao-core` helpers (`isWindows()`, `isMac()`, `isLinux()`, `getShell()`, etc.) and Windows-sensitive networking should avoid bare `localhost` defaults because it can resolve to IPv6 first on Windows.

The PR used a local `currentPlatform()` wrapper and direct `node:os.platform()` comparisons instead of the shared helpers, so this code is not covered by the central platform-mock test pattern and can drift from the rest of AO's Windows behavior.

## Impact
- Windows/macOS/Linux behavior for desktop notifications is harder to test centrally and may regress silently.
- The generated desktop dashboard URL can use `http://localhost:<port>` rather than the safer loopback host (`127.0.0.1`) used elsewhere to avoid Windows IPv6 stalls.
- Future contributors may copy this pattern into other notifier/runtime code, bypassing the documented helper inventory.

## Fix
- Replace ad-hoc platform checks with exported helpers from `@aoagents/ao-core` (`isMac()`, `isLinux()`, `isWindows()`) or add a dedicated helper in `packages/core/src/platform.ts` if needed for desktop notifier behavior.
- Replace synthesized dashboard URLs with `127.0.0.1` (or a shared helper for local dashboard URLs) unless the user explicitly configured a hostname.
- Add tests that mock the shared platform helpers / `process.platform` through the existing central pattern.

## Related
- [docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.md](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.md) — golden rule and helper inventory.
- [PR #1736](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1736) — desktop notifier/setup changes.

title: bug(notifier-routing): lifecycle fan-out can duplicate notifications for duplicate route entries
body:
## Bug
Lifecycle notification delivery does not deduplicate notifier references before fan-out, so duplicate entries in `notificationRouting` or `defaults.notifiers` can send the same event multiple times to the same notifier.

**Source:** post-merge review of [PR #1736](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1736) | **Reported by:** post-merge reviewer | **Analyzed against:** `a610601158937082133b9e366235432ed6e441d1` (merge commit under review: `298057044f3f7d36524785a60c90fe4381f88698`)
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
1. Configure a duplicate route manually:
   ```yaml
   notificationRouting:
     urgent: [slack, slack]
   notifiers:
     slack:
       plugin: slack
       webhookUrl: https://hooks.slack.com/services/...
   ```
2. Trigger an urgent lifecycle notification such as `session.stuck`.
3. Slack receives two copies of the same event.

The same can happen with duplicate aliases or defaults because config validation accepts arrays of strings and does not enforce uniqueness.

## Root Cause
Core lifecycle delivery uses the raw route/default array:

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:2274-2278` sets `notifierNames = config.notificationRouting[priority] ?? config.defaults.notifiers` and iterates it directly.

The manual test harness already deduplicates route refs:

- `packages/cli/src/lib/notify-test.ts:466-467` returns `uniqueRefs(...)` for routes.
- `packages/cli/src/lib/notify-test.ts:511-523` resolves test targets from those deduped refs.

Setup presets also dedupe when they write routes (`packages/cli/src/lib/notifier-routing.ts:147-154`), but hand-edited config, older config, or merges can still contain duplicates. The production lifecycle path is less defensive than the test path.

## Impact
- Users can receive duplicate Slack/Discord/email/webhook notifications for the same lifecycle event.
- Observability records duplicate successful deliveries, making notification metrics misleading.
- `ao notify test` may pass without reproducing production behavior because the harness dedupes while lifecycle does not.

## Fix
- Deduplicate `notifierNames` in `notifyHuman()` before delivery, using the same normalization as `uniqueRefs()` in the CLI harness.
- Consider validating `defaults.notifiers` and each `notificationRouting.<priority>` array for duplicates during config load.
- Add a lifecycle-manager regression test with duplicate route entries asserting one delivery.

## Related
- [PR #1736](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/pull/1736) — introduced routing presets and updated lifecycle routing behavior.

title: agentRulesFile should expand ~/ for consistency with other config paths
body:
## Problem

`agentRulesFile` is the only user-facing path in `ProjectConfig` that does not get `~/` expanded. Setting `agentRulesFile: ~/.agent-orchestrator/shared/foo.md` in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` silently fails to load — the file is never found, and the `catch` in `readUserRules` swallows the `ENOENT`, so there's no signal to the user that their rules file was skipped.

By contrast, `project.path` and `plugin.path` both get `expandHome()` applied during config load (`packages/core/src/config.ts:398, 403, 464`). `~/` is a common YAML convention, so the inconsistency is surprising.

## Root cause

`readUserRules` in `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts:170` resolves `agentRulesFile` directly against `project.path` without expanding `~/`:

```ts
if (project.agentRulesFile) {
  const filePath = resolve(project.path, project.agentRulesFile);
  try {
    const content = readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8").trim();
    ...
  } catch {
    // File not found or unreadable — skip silently (don't crash the spawn)
  }
}
```

`expandHome` is already exported from `@aoagents/ao-core` (`packages/core/src/index.ts:359`) — it just isn't applied here.

## Repro

1. In a project's `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, set:
   ```yaml
   project:
     agentRulesFile: ~/.agent-orchestrator/shared/team-rules.md
   ```
2. Create that file with some recognizable content.
3. Spawn a session.
4. Inspect the assembled prompt (e.g. via `ao spawn --preview-prompt` or by tailing the agent's first turn). The rules file content is missing, with no warning.

## Fix

One-liner in `prompt-builder.ts:170`:

```ts
const filePath = resolve(project.path, expandHome(project.agentRulesFile));
```

Plus a test in `packages/core/src/__tests__/prompt-builder.test.ts` covering the `~/`-prefixed case.

## Recommendation (separate, but related)

The silent `catch {}` at `prompt-builder.ts:176-178` was deliberate — don't crash session spawn if the rules file is missing — but it also hides this kind of config bug from the user. Worth considering: if `agentRulesFile` is declared but unreadable, log a single warning (not throw) so misconfigurations surface. This is a UX change independent of the `~/` fix and could be done in the same PR or a follow-up.

## Scope / non-goals

- `agentRulesFile` has only one reader (`prompt-builder.ts`), so the `~/` fix is contained to that file.

title: RFC: replace Claude Code terminal-regex activity detection with hooks (and a hash-delta safety net)
body:
## TL;DR

Claude Code exposes lifecycle hooks (`UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Notification`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`) that fire deterministically on every state transition. We are using exactly one of them today (`PostToolUse`, for git/gh metadata updates). The other six tell us authoritatively when Claude is mid-turn, waiting on the user, or done — yet our activity detection ignores them and tries to infer the same information by pattern-matching Claude's terminal output. That inference is fragile and we just spent a 15-commit PR (#1932) patching its sharpest edges without removing the underlying class of bugs.

This issue proposes scrapping the terminal regex layer entirely and deriving activity state from hooks. The pane-hash delta (a regex-free read of `tmux capture-pane -p` checksum across polls) is a one-line safety net for the "Claude is computing inside a long tool call with no hook events for 30+ seconds" case.

## Part 1 — what we just did (PR #1932)

For context. Skip to Part 2 if you only want the proposal.

#1932 hardened Claude activity detection across 15 commits, all under the same shape: *find a real-world session that the dashboard reports wrong, identify the regex / mtime / type-list bug behind it, tighten the rule, verify with `tmux capture-pane` and `.ao/activity.jsonl`*. Concrete fixes:

| # | Fix | Real-world repro |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Default `classifyTerminalOutput` from `active` to `idle` | All 6 dormant sessions on the machine (ao-143/144/151/154/160/139) showed as `active` because their pane's last line is Claude's static UI footer, not the `❯` prompt the lastLine idle check expected |
| 2 | Tightened `/bypass.*permissions/i` → `/bypass\s+all\s+future\s+permissions/i` | ao-143/144/151 all flipped to `waiting_input` because the persistent footer `⏵⏵ bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)` matched the old regex |
| 3 | Split bookkeeping types into "turn-end events" (→ ready/idle by age) vs "UI-noise re-snapshots" (→ skip native JSONL, fall through) | ao-144 had 73 trailing `permission-mode` + 73 trailing `ai-title` over 6 dormant days. ao-160 had the SAME PR written as `pr-link` 33 times in the last 200 lines |
| 4 | Removed `Crunched for Ns` from active indicators | ao-154 showed `✻ Crunched for 22s` as the last spinner-glyph line. Past-tense turn summary, not active. The discriminator is the trailing ellipsis (gerund + `…` = present-tense = active) |
| 5 | Bounded blocked detection to last 12 lines | `Unable to connect to API` matched against full `terminalOutput` would permanently false-fire `blocked` after a successful retry pushed the error off-screen but kept it in scrollback (Greptile-flagged) |
| 6 | Multi-session disambiguation via `claudeSessionUuid` | `findLatestSessionFile` picked newest-mtime, wrong session's JSONL whenever its sibling just wrote |
| 7 | Symlinked workspaces → `realpath` before slug | If AO holds the symlink path and Claude resolves the target, slugs diverge and AO looks in an empty dir forever |
| 8 | Broadened process regex | `/(?:^|\/)claude(?:\s|$)/` missed `.claude`, `claude-code`, `claude.exe`, `claude.js`, npm shims |
| 9 | Silent permission-denied → warn-once | `findLatestSessionFile` swallowed every `readdir` error |
| 10 | Removed 4 dead switch cases | `permission_request`, `error` (PR #1927), `tool_use`, `result` (PR #1932) — all unreachable per disk survey |
| 11 | Detect `blocked` from terminal regex when JSONL has scrolled | Empirically captured `Unable to connect to API` / `Retrying in Ns · attempt N/M` patterns |

204 tests pass. The dashboard now correctly reports `idle` for dormant sessions and `active` for sessions running tools. **PR #1932 should still be merged** — it fixes real, observable bugs in shipping behavior.

But every single one of those fixes was a *symptom* of the same root cause:

> We are inferring agent state from rendered terminal output and the file mtime of a JSONL that the agent writes for its own UI purposes, when the agent already exposes events for the exact state transitions we care about.

## Part 2 — why terminal parsing is structurally wrong

Concrete failure modes baked into the architecture:

1. **Claude's persistent UI footer triggers any regex looking for "permissions" / "interrupt" / "bypass".** We tightened ours to `bypass\s+all\s+future\s+permissions`. Tomorrow Claude could change the footer text and we'd be back to square one. The fix-up regex assumes Claude's footer wording is stable, which is not in our control.
2. **Past-tense vs present-tense status lines look identical on a quick glance.** `✻ Worked for 11s` is done; `✻ Working…` is active. Our gerund+ellipsis heuristic distinguishes them today, but it depends on Claude continuing to use `…` for ongoing status. If Claude changes its loading indicator (or localizes it for a non-English locale), the heuristic breaks silently.
3. **The bookkeeping/noise/turn-end taxonomy is empirical and unstable.** We classified types by inspecting one developer's `~/.claude/projects/`. If Claude adds a new top-level type next release, it falls into the default branch and we have no signal for what it means. We're maintaining a hand-curated allowlist of internal-to-Claude entry types — a brittle coupling we should never have taken on.
4. **mtime-based freshness is wrong for any type Claude writes periodically.** `permission-mode` and `ai-title` are written on session attach. `pr-link` is re-emitted minutes after the PR was created. Each one pushes the file mtime forward without indicating activity. The "noise types skip native JSONL" workaround addresses the specific noisy types we've seen, but doesn't help with the next one Claude introduces.
5. **15 commits to fix 11 distinct edge cases**, each found by manually inspecting a dashboard misreport. There are certainly more edge cases we haven't tripped over yet.

The reviewer is correct: this is the wrong abstraction. We should not be reading Claude's rendered UI to infer what Claude is doing.

## Part 3 — what Claude actually exposes (the events we should be using)

Claude Code's hook system supports these event types ([docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks)):

| Hook | Fires when | Authoritative state |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | Claude session created | `ready` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User submits a prompt | `active` |
| `PreToolUse` | About to execute a tool | `active` |
| `PostToolUse` | Tool returned (we already use this for metadata) | `active` (still mid-turn) |
| `Notification` | **Permission prompt shown to user** | `waiting_input` |
| `Stop` | Claude finished the turn | `ready` |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent finished | `ready` |
| `SessionEnd` | Session ended | `exited` (or let process probe handle this) |
| `PreCompact` | About to compact context | `active` |

Each hook runs a user-defined shell command with a JSON payload on stdin describing the event. The hook can emit JSON to stdout to influence Claude (block tool use, etc.) or just exit 0 as a passive listener.

The infrastructure to register hooks already exists in our codebase: `setupHookInWorkspace` in `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` writes `{workspacePath}/.claude/settings.json` with a `hooks.PostToolUse[]` entry pointing at our `metadata-updater.sh`. Adding more hooks is the same pattern repeated.

## Part 4 — proposed architecture

### High-level

```
Claude session
  │
  ├─ hook fires on every state transition
  │     ↓
  ├─ activity-updater.sh / .cjs (one script, dispatches by hook event name)
  │     ↓
  ├─ appends {ts, state, source: "hook", trigger} to {workspacePath}/.ao/activity.jsonl
  │     ↓
  ├─ lifecycle manager polls → reads AO JSONL via existing cascade → reports state
  │
  (parallel) hash-delta safety net inside recordActivity:
  ├─ md5(tmux capture-pane -p) per poll
  ├─ if hash unchanged for > N seconds → write `idle` (covers gaps between hook events)
  └─ if hash changed since last poll AND no recent hook event → write `active`
```

The AO activity-JSONL layer is unchanged. The existing cascade (`checkActivityLogState` for waiting_input/blocked, `getActivityFallbackState` for age-decayed) reads whatever we write into the JSONL. The hooks just become the new producer.

### Hook → JSONL writes

One shared `activity-updater` script, branched by the `$CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_NAME` env var (Claude sets this) or by the `hook_event_name` field in the JSON payload on stdin:

| Event | State written | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | `ready` | Fresh session, no user prompt yet |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `active` | About to start a turn |
| `PreToolUse` | `active` | Tool call beginning |
| `PostToolUse` | `active` | Tool call done, but still mid-turn — Claude may chain more |
| `Notification` | `waiting_input` | Includes the trigger text from the payload |
| `Stop` | `ready` | Turn complete, waiting for next user input |
| `SubagentStop` | `ready` | Same |
| `SessionEnd` | (no-op, process probe handles `exited`) | |
| `PreCompact` | `active` | Background compaction is real work |

Each write follows the existing AO JSONL shape (`{ ts, state, source: "hook", trigger?: string }`). The `source: "hook"` tag distinguishes them from `"terminal"`-sourced entries during the migration.

### Hash-delta safety net (regex-free)

Tested locally: dormant ao-143 pane hash identical across 3 polls 2s apart. Active ao-161 hash changed every poll (spinner timer ticks).

```ts
const paneHashes = new Map<string, { hash: string; observedAt: Date }>();

// inside recordActivity / a new poll callback:
const pane = await tmux.capturePane(handle);
const hash = createHash("md5").update(pane).digest("hex");
const prev = paneHashes.get(session.id);
if (prev && prev.hash === hash) {
  const ageMs = Date.now() - prev.observedAt.getTime();
  if (ageMs > IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
    await appendActivityEntry(workspacePath, "idle", "hash-delta");
  }
} else {
  paneHashes.set(session.id, { hash, observedAt: new Date() });
  // Don't write `active` here — let hooks be authoritative for active.
  // The delta only writes `idle` (the absence of motion).
}
```

The delta is *only* used to write `idle`. Active is hook-driven. This avoids the chicken-and-egg of "Claude is currently running a 30-second tool call, no PostToolUse fired yet, hash is changing because of the spinner".

### What gets removed

- `classifyTerminalOutput` regex patterns (`Do you want to proceed?`, `bypass...`, `Unable to connect to API`, `Retrying in Ns...`, gerund+ellipsis, all the verb fallbacks). The whole function shrinks to "compute pane hash and compare".
- `NOISE_JSONL_TYPES` set and the noise-skip branch in `getClaudeActivityState`. Native JSONL `system + api_error + level:error` → `blocked` stays because it's the only structured-data path for errors.
- The lifecycle-manager terminal-output fallback at `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1041-1087` becomes vestigial — hook-sourced entries cover everything that path was meant to catch.

### What stays

- Native JSONL `system + api_error + level:error` → `blocked` detection (PR #1927). This is the only authoritative blocked signal that doesn't require Claude to render anything to the terminal.
- The `claudeSessionUuid` lookup, symlink realpath, broadened process regex, warn-once on permission-denied (all from PR #1932) — all still relevant.
- The full AO activity-JSONL pipeline (`recordActivity`, `checkActivityLogState`, `getActivityFallbackState`). Hooks just become the new write source.

## Part 5 — implementation plan

| Phase | Work | LOC est | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Extend `setupHookInWorkspace` to register multiple hooks instead of just `PostToolUse`. Refactor the script writing to be a loop. | ~60 | Low — same pattern repeated |
| 2 | Write `activity-updater.sh` (and `.cjs` for Windows). Dispatches by `$CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_NAME`. Each branch appends one JSON line to `{workspacePath}/.ao/activity.jsonl`. | ~80 each | Low — both languages already proven in `metadata-updater` |
| 3 | Register the 7 new hooks in `setupWorkspaceHooks` (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse keeps the existing one, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionEnd) | ~30 | Low |
| 4 | Add hash-delta safety net in `recordActivity` (or a new `recordIdlenessFromPaneHash` callback the lifecycle manager invokes each poll) | ~40 | Medium — need to think about where the per-session hash cache lives (in-memory Map, plugin-scoped, what about restarts) |
| 5 | Delete the terminal regex patterns from `classifyTerminalOutput`. Keep the function as a hash-delta entrypoint. Update existing tests (or delete them — they were testing the regex behavior). | ~100 removed | Low if we delete tests, medium if we rewrite them |
| 6 | Verify on real sessions: spawn 3+ Claude sessions, do tool calls, hit permission prompts, finish turns, leave dormant. Check AO JSONL has hook-sourced entries for each transition. Check dashboard reports match. | 1-2 hours | Low |

Net: ~1-2 days of focused work, removes most of `classifyTerminalOutput`, makes activity detection event-driven.

## Part 6 — testing strategy

Three layers:

1. **Hook-script unit tests** (per `metadata-updater` pattern): pipe synthetic JSON payloads into the script, assert the JSONL line written matches.
2. **Integration test** (new in `integration-tests/`): spawn a Claude session in a temp workspace, simulate a user prompt + tool call + Stop, assert AO JSONL receives one entry per hook event.
3. **Live verification** (manual, documented in PR description): spawn 3+ real sessions, hit each hook (submit prompt, trigger permission prompt, finish turn), `tail .ao/activity.jsonl | jq` and confirm event sequence.

Replace the existing 200+ terminal-regex tests with ~20 hook-script tests + 1 integration test. Massive net reduction in test surface.

## Part 7 — open questions for review

1. **Hook payload format.** Does Claude's `Notification` hook pass the prompt text (so we can use it as the `trigger` field)? Need to verify against docs / live test before finalizing the script.
2. **Hook execution latency.** Hooks run synchronously and Claude blocks until they return. Our script is `node` or `bash` + a single append; should be <50ms. But worth measuring before deploy, especially for `PreToolUse` which runs before every tool call.
3. **Hook failure modes.** What if the script errors? Claude logs a warning but continues. We should make sure script errors don't block Claude (use `exit 0` on every path, log internally).
4. **`SessionStart` vs cold-start.** When AO restarts the daemon, do we re-trigger `SessionStart` for already-running Claude sessions? Probably no — but the AO JSONL would have stale entries. The hash-delta safety net should converge correctly within one threshold window.
5. **Do we want the hash-delta safety net at all?** It's belt-and-suspenders. Could ship Phase 1-5 without it and add later if we see gaps where hooks alone don't cover.
6. **Should the hash-delta also write `active`** (when hash changes between polls AND last hook event is older than X)? Probably yes — covers the "30-second tool call, no events firing" case. But adds complexity.

## Part 8 — what is NOT in this work

- **Native-JSONL classification stays for `blocked`.** `system + api_error + level:error` is the right source for blocked; there's no hook for it.
- **No changes to other agent plugins** (Codex, OpenCode, Aider, Kimi, Cursor). They have their own state-derivation logic and their own platform-event APIs (or lack thereof). The Claude work is a template they can copy if a similar refactor makes sense for them.
- **No changes to the AO JSONL schema, the cascade order, or any downstream consumer** (`checkActivityLogState`, `getActivityFallbackState`, lifecycle manager). Hooks just become a new write source for the existing pipeline.
- **No collapse of the `active`/`ready` activity-state distinction.** Tracked separately in #1934.

## Why now

Two reasons:

1. The terminal-regex layer is one Claude UI tweak away from breaking again. Cheaper to remove it than to keep patching it.
2. We were going to ship #1932 with the regex layer hardened, then a reviewer asked "isn't there a hook for this?" — and the honest answer is yes, we just didn't reach for it. Better to file this design now and converge on the right architecture than to layer another patch on top.

title: PRD: Agent Orchestrator v2 Codex and GitHub SCM plugins
body:
## Problem Statement

Agent Orchestrator v2 does not need to recreate the full v1 plugin matrix. The v1 repo supports many plugin slots and many integrations, but carrying that entire surface into v2 now would add product and implementation drag before the new architecture proves itself.

For v2, the immediate goal is narrower: make the plugin package model real with one agent plugin and one SCM plugin. The first supported agent plugin should be `agent-codex`. The first supported SCM plugin should be `scm-github`. Other agents, issue trackers, notifiers, terminal plugins, runtime plugins, workspace plugins, and marketplace/plugin-store behavior should not be treated as v2 launch requirements.

## Solution

Build the v2 plugins package around two concrete built-in plugins:

- `agent-codex`: owns Codex launch, prompt delivery, environment setup, activity/session discovery, restore metadata, and Codex-specific preflight.
- `scm-github`: owns GitHub repository, branch, PR, CI, review thread/comment, mergeability, and webhook behavior needed by the v2 product.

Keep the plugin contract intentionally small and internal. The v2 app should prove that the app/server/CLI can load and use `agent-codex` and `scm-github` through a clean package boundary. Do not generalize the contract for integrations that are not being implemented in this milestone.

## User Stories

1. As an AO v2 user, I want Codex to be the supported agent plugin, so that the first v2 workflow has one reliable agent path.
2. As an AO v2 user, I want GitHub SCM to be the supported SCM plugin, so that PR, CI, and review state work for GitHub repositories.
3. As an AO v2 user, I want the default v2 setup to make Codex and GitHub SCM available without extra plugin installation, so that I can run the product immediately.
4. As an AO v2 user, I want unsupported agents to be clearly unavailable, so that I do not assume Claude Code, Aider, OpenCode, or other agents work in v2 yet.
5. As an AO v2 user, I want unsupported issue trackers to be clearly unavailable, so that I do not assume Linear, GitLab tracker, GitHub issue tracker, Jira, or other issue sources work in v2 yet.
6. As an AO v2 user, I want Codex prompt delivery to be reliable, so that long instructions do not get lost or truncated at launch.
7. As an AO v2 user, I want Codex restore behavior to preserve the right Codex session/thread metadata where possible, so that restarting a worker does not silently start unrelated work.
8. As an AO v2 user, I want Codex activity state to be visible to the app, so that I can tell whether the worker is active, ready, blocked, waiting for input, or exited.
9. As an AO v2 user, I want GitHub PR state to be visible, so that I can see whether work has an open PR, failing CI, requested changes, approval, or merge readiness.
10. As an AO v2 user, I want GitHub review comments to route back to the worker where appropriate, so that Codex can respond to actionable PR feedback.
11. As an AO v2 user, I want GitHub CI failures to route back to the worker where appropriate, so that Codex can fix failed checks.
12. As an AO v2 user, I want GitHub SCM errors to be actionable, so that missing `gh` auth, missing repo remotes, or API failures explain what to fix.
13. As an AO v2 user, I want the v2 config to expose only the plugin choices that actually work, so that the config stays honest.
14. As an AO maintainer, I want the v2 plugin contract shaped by `agent-codex` and `scm-github`, so that the abstraction follows real usage instead of theoretical slots.
15. As an AO maintainer, I want `agent-codex` to own Codex-specific launch and discovery code, so that core app logic does not know Codex CLI internals.
16. As an AO maintainer, I want `scm-github` to own GitHub PR, CI, review, and webhook code, so that core app logic does not know GitHub API details.
17. As an AO maintainer, I want a tiny built-in plugin registry for these two plugins, so that v2 can resolve built-ins without a marketplace system.
18. As an AO maintainer, I want plugin package boundaries that can grow later, so that future agents or SCMs can be added after v2 proves the shape.
19. As an AO maintainer, I want unsupported plugin categories to be explicitly out of scope, so that workers do not spend time scaffolding unused extension points.
20. As an AO maintainer, I want tests for the actual Codex and GitHub SCM contracts, so that the first v2 plugins are dependable rather than placeholders.
21. As an AO maintainer, I want fake plugin tests only where they validate the loader boundary, so that test coverage stays grounded in the two real plugins.
22. As an AO maintainer, I want cross-platform checks around Codex launch and GitHub command usage, so that v2 does not bake in macOS-only assumptions.
23. As a worker implementing this PRD, I want the scope to say `agent-codex` and `scm-github` only, so that I do not implement unrelated plugins.
24. As a worker implementing this PRD, I want issue tracker support called out as out of scope, so that I do not add `tracker-github` just because GitHub SCM exists.

## Implementation Decisions

- The v2 plugin package milestone supports exactly two built-in plugins: `agent-codex` and `scm-github`.
- The v2 plugin contract should be internal to the product. Do not create a public SDK or a generic marketplace contract in this milestone.
- The only agent plugin contract that must work is the contract needed by `agent-codex`.
- The only SCM plugin contract that must work is the contract needed by `scm-github`.
- Do not implement tracker plugins in this PRD. `scm-github` handles GitHub repository/PR/CI/review behavior; it is not a GitHub issue tracker plugin for this milestone.
- Do not implement notifier, terminal, runtime, or workspace plugin packages in this PRD. Any minimal runtime/workspace behavior needed to exercise Codex can live in the app/core path without becoming a plugin category.
- Keep plugin resolution simple: a built-in registry or direct package map for `agent-codex` and `scm-github` is enough.
- Do not build install, update, uninstall, rollback, remote marketplace, or npm plugin-store behavior unless a later v2 milestone asks for external plugins.
- Keep config honest: supported plugin names should be limited to Codex for agent and GitHub for SCM.
- The app/server/CLI should consume plugins through a small resolved-plugin interface rather than importing plugin implementation details everywhere.
- `agent-codex` should own Codex CLI command construction, system prompt file handling, inline fallback prompt handling, environment variables, preflight checks, process liveness, activity discovery, session info extraction, and restore command behavior.
- `scm-github` should own GitHub auth/repo checks, branch lookup, PR lookup/creation/update where needed, CI summary, review decision, unresolved review threads/comments, bot-vs-human review classification, merge readiness, merge actions where needed, and webhook parsing/verification where needed.
- Keep Codex prompt delivery file-first. Long prompts should go through a prompt file rather than a shell-inlined string.
- Keep GitHub review handling explicit about human review threads versus automated/bot review comments, because those paths drive different worker follow-up behavior.
- Package layout should make the two plugin packages easy to find under the v2 package grouping, for example a plugins package group containing Codex agent and GitHub SCM implementations.
- Avoid naming or documenting unsupported future plugins as if they already exist. Future extension points can be mentioned as future work only.
- Do not restructure unrelated lifecycle, storage, dashboard, terminal, tracker, notifier, runtime, or workspace systems as part of this PRD.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests should assert externally visible behavior: Codex launch inputs, Codex prompt delivery, Codex restore/session discovery, GitHub PR/CI/review outputs, plugin resolution, and clear failure messages.
- Test the v2 loader with only the two supported built-ins: `agent-codex` and `scm-github`.
- Test that unsupported plugin names fail with clear errors rather than silently falling back.
- Test that unsupported plugin categories are not exposed as v2-supported config choices.
- Test `agent-codex` command construction using fake project/session inputs, including prompt file precedence over inline prompt text.
- Test `agent-codex` environment construction and preflight behavior without launching a real Codex session in unit tests.
- Test `agent-codex` activity/session discovery with fixture data, not a live Codex home directory scan.
- Test `agent-codex` restore behavior with stored Codex metadata and with missing/invalid metadata.
- Test `scm-github` GitHub command/API behavior with mocked `gh` or mocked GitHub transport, not live network calls in unit tests.
- Test `scm-github` CI summary mapping, review decision mapping, unresolved review thread parsing, bot comment classification, and error formatting.
- Test lifecycle-facing interactions with fake sessions that use `agent-codex` and `scm-github` as the resolved plugins.
- Add one integration-style test that proves the app can resolve the two built-in plugins and run the supported path without installing external plugins.
- Add cross-platform tests for command/path construction where the plugins touch shell commands or filesystem paths.
- Prior art in the current repo includes agent-codex plugin tests, scm-github tests, plugin-registry tests, lifecycle-manager tests, and CLI command tests. Use those patterns, but keep v2 coverage scoped to the two supported plugins.

## Out of Scope

- Supporting Claude Code, Aider, OpenCode, Cursor, Kimi, or any other agent plugin in v2.
- Supporting GitHub tracker, GitLab tracker, Linear tracker, Jira tracker, or any other issue tracker plugin in v2.
- Supporting GitLab SCM or any non-GitHub SCM plugin in v2.
- Supporting notifier plugins in v2.
- Supporting terminal plugins in v2.
- Supporting runtime plugins in v2.
- Supporting workspace plugins in v2.
- Building a public plugin SDK.
- Building a plugin marketplace, remote registry, npm plugin installer, plugin update flow, or plugin store.
- Scaffolding generic plugin authoring tools.
- Migrating all v1 plugins into v2.
- Redesigning unrelated session lifecycle, storage, terminal transport, dashboard information architecture, or issue intake behavior.

## Further Notes

- This PRD replaces the earlier broad v2 plugin-package scope. The intended v2 milestone is deliberately small: prove the plugin package boundary with Codex as the agent and GitHub as the SCM.
- Future v2 milestones can add more agents, trackers, notifiers, runtimes, workspaces, or external plugin distribution after the Codex + GitHub SCM path is working.
- The key implementation discipline is to avoid building unused extension points just because v1 had them.

title: bug(core): review-backlog dispatch path is uninstrumented — non-injection of PR review comments is undiagnosable
body:
## Bug

When the lifecycle manager *fails to auto-inject* PR review comments into an agent session, there is **no observability anywhere** that explains why. The review-backlog dispatch pipeline instruments only the fetch-*failure* path; the success-via-bypass path and every "decided not to dispatch" branch are silent. This makes the most common review-automation failure mode (comments exist on the PR but never reach the agent) effectively impossible to RCA from logs, metadata, or the events store.

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding — investigating why review comments on mercury#24366 (session mer-32) were not auto-injected while the identical scenario on mercury#23617 (session mer-24) was. **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `8c71bdeb`. **Confidence:** High (exact lines traced; mechanism reproduced). **Priority:** High.

## Concrete incident (why this matters)

- mer-24 (PR #23617) and mer-32 (PR #24366): *identical* scenario — `venkat82` leaves an inline review comment, then `APPROVE`s ~3s later.
- mer-24's thread is now `isResolved=true` (agent addressed it). mer-32's two threads are `isResolved=false` (never injected).
- GitHub GraphQL ground truth confirms mer-32's threads are genuine unresolved, non-bot, fetchable by the daemon's gh identity. So detection/access is fine.
- **We could not determine why mer-32 was skipped or whether mer-24 was even AO-injected**, because:
  1. The successful human/bot dispatch via the throttle-bypass branch calls `sessionManager.send()` **directly** with no observability emission (see code trace).
  2. Success markers (`lastPendingReviewDispatchHash/At`) are cleared to `""` once the thread resolves, and the metadata cleaner strips empty keys — so post-resolution there is zero trace.
  3. The activity-events sink is dead in this environment (better-sqlite3/Node-ABI — see #1930, #1822), so even emitted AE events would be dropped.
- All three blind spots overlap exactly on this path. The lifecycle ndjson shows mer-24 and mer-32 with *identical* sparse events and **no review reaction ever** for either.

## Code trace (`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`, `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`)

- L1715: `recordActivityEvent({...})` — instruments only the `getReviewThreads` **catch/failure** path ("record AE evidence so RCA can answer 'why aren't review comments being dispatched?'"). Good intent, wrong coverage.
- L1814: `await sessionManager.send(session.id, enrichedMessage)` — **human** comment dispatch via throttle-bypass branch. **No `recordActivityEvent`, no `lifecycle.transition.reaction`.** Silent success.
- L1869: same for **bot** (`bugbot-comments`) dispatch. Silent.
- L1821 / L1876 (`executeReaction(...)`) paths *do* emit `lifecycle.transition.reaction` — so coverage is inconsistent depending on which branch fires.
- The **non-dispatch decision points have zero instrumentation**: throttled (`REVIEW_BACKLOG_THROTTLE_MS`, 2min), `pendingFingerprint === lastPendingDispatchHash` (no change), `reactionConfig` null/`auto:false`, `!pendingFingerprint` (no unresolved threads), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`/PR-not-open early return. When AO decides *not* to inject, nothing records the decision or its reason.

## Fix

Emit a single structured observation for **every** review-backlog evaluation outcome, written to the durable lifecycle ndjson stream (not solely the sqlite AE sink, which can be unavailable — #1930/#1822):

- `dispatched` (human/bot, via bypass *or* executeReaction) with: session, PR, fingerprint, comment count/IDs, reaction key, throttled-bypass vs executeReaction.
- `skipped` with explicit reason enum: `throttled`, `fingerprint_unchanged`, `no_unresolved_threads`, `no_reaction_config`, `reaction_auto_disabled`, `pr_not_open`, `terminal_status`, `fetch_failed`.
- Include the post-throttle decision even when no fetch occurred (so "why didn't it even look" is answerable).

This is an observability/instrumentation fix only — no behavior change to dispatch logic itself. It directly enables RCA of the (separate, still-open) question of *why* mer-32-style cases are skipped.

## Impact

- Review auto-injection failures are silent and undiagnosable in production — operators see "comments on PR, agent never told," with no log/metric/event to investigate.
- Inconsistent instrumentation (executeReaction path logged, bypass path not) yields misleading "no reaction ever fired" logs even when a send succeeded.
- Compounds with #1930/#1822 (dead AE sink) and the post-resolution metadata wipe to produce total blindness on this path.

## Related
- #1511 — Activity Events logging layer design (this path was not fully covered by it).
- #1457 — unify lifecycle/runtime/agent logs into a correlated stream (broader; this is a concrete gap).
- #1930 / #1822 — activity-events sqlite sink unavailable (why even emitted events vanish here).
- #614 — send-to-agent reaction silently no-ops (adjacent silent-reaction class).

title: fix(web): externalize ao-core and better-sqlite3 from Next.js bundle
body:
## Problem (Fixes #1930)

Next.js bundles `@aoagents/ao-core` (via `transpilePackages`) into the `.next/server/` output. During bundling, webpack resolves `import.meta.url` to the **build machine's absolute path** and bakes it in as a string literal:

```js
createRequire(file:///tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/core/dist/events-db.js)
```

At runtime on any other machine — especially Windows — this path doesn't exist, causing:
- `TypeError: The argument 'filename' must be a file URL object, file URL string, or absolute path string`
- `[ao] activity-events DB unavailable — events will be dropped: Cannot find module 'better-sqlite3'`

**88 files** in `.next/` had the build path baked in.

## Fix

Add `@aoagents/ao-core` and `better-sqlite3` to `serverExternalPackages` in `next.config.js`. This tells Next.js to not bundle these packages — they're resolved at runtime from `node_modules/`, so `import.meta.url` resolves to the user's actual install path.

Precedent: #1057 / commit `3a108e9b` did the same for `@composio/core`.

## Affected source locations

1. `packages/core/src/events-db.ts` — `createRequire(import.meta.url)(better-sqlite3)`
2. `packages/core/src/update-cache.ts` — `createRequire(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`


`runtime-process/dist/index.ts` also uses `import.meta.url` but is NOT in `transpilePackages`, so it was never bundled and is unaffected.

## Impact on release pipeline

None. This is a code-only change. Goes through the normal changeset → PR → release flow.

title: refactor(agent-claude-code): replace terminal-regex activity detection with hooks (closes #1941)
body:
## Summary

Implements #1941 — replaces Claude Code terminal-regex activity detection with platform-event lifecycle hooks.

PR #1932 spent 15 commits patching the sharpest edges of `classifyTerminalOutput`. Every Claude UI tweak (footer wording, status verb, spinner glyph) regressed a heuristic. The class of bug isn't fixable; the abstraction is wrong. Claude Code already emits a lifecycle hook on every state transition that matters — we use exactly one of them today (`PostToolUse` for git/gh metadata). The rest tell us authoritatively when Claude is mid-turn, waiting on the user, or done.

This PR pivots: hooks become the activity-state writer; terminal regex retires.

## What changes

### `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code` (minor)

`setupWorkspaceHooks` now installs **two** scripts per workspace and registers both in `.claude/settings.json`:

- `metadata-updater` (unchanged) — `PostToolUse(Bash)`, extracts gh/git side-effects.
- `activity-updater` (new) — registered on **every** event that carries activity information:

| Hook | Activity state | Trigger field |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` / `Stop` / `SubagentStop` | `ready` | event name |
| `UserPromptSubmit` / `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` / `PostToolUseFailure` / `PostToolBatch` / `PreCompact` / `PostCompact` / `SubagentStart` | `active` | event name |
| `PermissionRequest` | `waiting_input` | `PermissionRequest (<tool_name>)` |
| `Notification` (`notification_type == permission_prompt \| idle_prompt`) | `waiting_input` | `Notification (<type>)` |
| `Notification` (other types) | **skipped** | — |
| `StopFailure` | `blocked` | `StopFailure (<error_type>)` |
| anything else (`SessionEnd`, `TaskCreated`, …) | **skipped** | — |

Both bash (`.sh`) and Node (`.cjs`, Windows) variants ship. Hook output is appended to `{workspace}/.ao/activity.jsonl` with `source: "hook"`. The script always `exit 0` so it never blocks Claude.

### `@aoagents/ao-core` (minor)

`ActivityLogEntry.source` and `ActivitySignalSource` now accept `"hook"`. No consumer needs changes — the cascade has always read whatever source appeared in the JSONL, and the new tests assert hook-sourced entries flow through `checkActivityLogState` / `getActivityFallbackState` identically to terminal-sourced ones.

### Retired in this PR

- `classifyTerminalOutput`'s regex patterns (~80 LOC). Function kept as a stable `return "idle"` stub for the `detectActivity` interface contract.
- `agent.recordActivity` on the Claude plugin. Lifecycle manager guards `agent.recordActivity?` so removal is clean. Other agents (Aider/OpenCode/Codex fallback) keep theirs untouched.
- `NOISE_JSONL_TYPES` and native-JSONL handling are kept — those operate on Claude's own session files, not on terminal pixels.

## Three things the RFC got wrong (and how this PR handles them)

1. **`$CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_NAME` env var doesn't exist.** Verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks. The event name is on the stdin JSON payload as `hook_event_name`. The script branches on the JSON field.
2. **`Notification` has a `notification_type` field.** Mapping all `Notification` events to `waiting_input` (as the RFC implied) would false-fire on `auth_success` / `elicitation_response` / etc. The script filters to `permission_prompt | idle_prompt`.
3. **`PermissionRequest` is its own event and `StopFailure` exists.** Both more authoritative than the RFC's plan (Notification + native-JSONL `api_error` parsing). This PR registers both.

## What's NOT in this PR

- **No hash-delta safety net.** The RFC's Part 4 proposed an `md5(tmux capture-pane -p)` poll for idle detection. With hooks covering every transition and the existing age-decay handling the gaps (active → ready → idle by timestamp), there's no observed need. Easy to add in a follow-up if a real session shows hooks alone don't cover.
- **No activity-state vocabulary changes.** #1934 (collapse `active`/`ready` into `active` + timestamp) is orthogonal; this PR keeps the existing enum.
- **No changes to other agent plugins** (Codex, OpenCode, Aider, …). The Claude work is a template they can copy if a similar refactor makes sense for them.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — green
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — green
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (62 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 28 tests pass (1 new, asserts `source: "hook"` round-trips)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-claude-code test` — 267 tests pass:
  - 129 in `index.test.ts` (hook setup, idempotency, win32, user-hook preservation)
  - 61 in `__tests__/activity-detection.test.ts` (cascade, hook-sourced JSONL entries, `recordActivity` undefined contract)
  - 25 in `hook-script.integration.test.ts` (metadata-updater, unchanged)
  - 52 in `activity-updater.integration.test.ts` (bash × Node variant parity — every event in the table)
- [x] **End-to-end smoke test on real shell:** piped synthetic Claude hook JSON payloads through both `.sh` and `.cjs` scripts, observed `.ao/activity.jsonl` receive correct entries (`SessionStart → ready`, `PermissionRequest → waiting_input (Bash)`, `Notification(auth_success) → skipped`, `StopFailure → blocked (rate_limit)`, `SessionEnd → skipped`).

## Cross-platform

- `node -p 'new Date().toISOString()'` is used for the timestamp in bash (BSD `date` doesn't support `%3N`). Node is a hard runtime dep of Claude Code so this is always available.
- Windows: `.cjs` variant is functionally identical, written via Node built-ins only (no jq/grep/sed/bash-isms). No `chmod` (Windows uses extension for executability).
- `isWindows()` from `@aoagents/ao-core` for branching; no raw `process.platform` introduced.

## Migration / compatibility

- Existing `.claude/settings.json` files keep their `metadata-updater` PostToolUse entry untouched. The new activity hooks are added as additional array entries — both old AO instances (reading only PostToolUse(Bash)) and new instances (reading every event) coexist on the same settings file.
- Existing `.ao/activity.jsonl` files with `source: "terminal"` entries continue to parse — `"hook"` is added to the valid-sources set, not replacing the others.
- `recordActivity` removed only on the Claude agent — every other agent plugin still implements it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Session header branch link points to wrong repo (uses upstream, not PR head)
body:
## Symptom

In the session detail header (next to Status), the **branch link is broken** — the branch *name* is rendered correctly, but the link target is wrong. It points to the **upstream repo** instead of the actual PR's head branch (which lives in a fork or a different repo for cross-repo PRs).

Clicking the branch chip → 404 or the wrong tree view.

## Expected

The branch link should resolve to the PR's actual head:

\`\`\`
https://github.com/{headRepoOwner}/{headRepoName}/tree/{headRefName}
\`\`\`

…not always upstream's tree. For sessions where the PR is from a fork or another repo (e.g. \`harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator\` → \`ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator\`), the link should go to the fork's branch.

## Repro

1. Spawn a session that creates a PR from a fork (or use any session whose PR has \`isCrossRepository: true\` / \`headRepositoryOwner\` ≠ the upstream owner).
2. Open the session detail view.
3. Click the branch chip in the header.
4. Lands on the upstream repo's branch tree (or 404 if that branch doesn't exist upstream), not the actual head branch on the fork.

## Likely Location

- \`packages/web/src/components/SessionDetailHeader.tsx\` (or wherever the header renders) — search for the branch chip render and where the link \`href\` is built.
- The data layer needs to expose the PR's head repo, not just the branch name. \`gh pr view N --json headRefName,headRepositoryOwner,headRepository,isCrossRepository\` returns the right fields.
- Check the SCM plugin (\`packages/plugins/scm-github\`) — does it surface \`headRepositoryOwner\`/\`headRepository\` to the session metadata? If not, that's the missing data.

## Fix Direction

1. Ensure the SCM/PR enrichment includes \`headRepositoryOwner\` + \`headRepository.name\` in session metadata (or PR shape on \`Session\`).
2. When the header builds the branch link, prefer \`headRepositoryOwner/headRepository.name\` over the upstream \`owner/repo\`. Fall back to upstream only when no PR is attached.
3. For sessions with no PR yet, link to the local upstream branch only if it's been pushed; otherwise omit the link entirely (clicking shouldn't 404).

## Related

- Cross-repo PR support landed via PR #1789 (\`feat(core): PR handoff history\` / cross-repo claim). The fix should consume the same metadata that PR introduced.

title: First-run Codex selection leaves global config on claude-code and breaks dashboard session routing
body:
## Bug

First-time `ao start` with **Codex** selected can create a split-brain config state: the project-local config records `agent: codex`, but the global config keeps `defaults.agent: claude-code`. The CLI then spawns the orchestrator under one project identity while the dashboard resolves the project through the global portfolio identity, so the session detail page shows `Session not found` even though tmux and the worktree exist.

**Source:** local live report / debugging session from Adil Shaikh
**Analyzed against:** `45de80ce3f8bae4f8a2f8ff00bf81b09af874025`
**AO version observed:** `0.8.0`
**Environment observed:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, zsh, Node `v24.15.0`
**Confidence:** High - traced through config generation, global project registration, dashboard resolution, session metadata, and worktree state.

## Reproduction

1. Start from a project without an existing local `agent-orchestrator.yaml`.
2. Run `ao start` for the first time.
3. When prompted for the agent, choose **Codex**.
4. Continue through the release-channel/onboarding prompt.
5. Observe that the project-local config is generated with Codex, but the global config may still retain Claude Code as the default agent.
6. Open the dashboard session detail route for the orchestrator.

Observed route shape from the report:

```text
http://localhost:3000/projects/ao/sessions/ao-orchestrator
```

## Actual Behavior

The local config initially used a wrapped project config shape similar to:

```yaml
port: 3000
defaults:
  runtime: tmux
  agent: codex
  workspace: worktree
  notifiers: []
projects:
  ao:
    name: ao
    sessionPrefix: ao
    path: /path/to/project
```

But the global config still had:

```yaml
defaults:
  runtime: tmux
  agent: claude-code
  workspace: worktree
projects:
  ao_<hash>:
    path: /path/to/project
    sessionPrefix: ao
```

Resulting symptoms:

- Dashboard session page shows `Session not found`.
- Sidebar shows a generated session/project identity such as `ao_0242ccdd19`.
- Project is marked degraded with `config needs repair`.
- tmux session is alive, e.g. `ao-orchestrator`.
- Worktree exists under the older project storage identity.
- After clicking repair, local config is flattened, but existing session/worktree storage is not migrated, so a subsequent spawn can show an older-orchestrator-workspace warning.

Example older-workspace warning from the report:

```text
AO found an older orchestrator workspace for "ao_0242ccdd19" but could not safely reuse it automatically. Your repository is safe. Review the existing workspace, then either reuse it manually or remove it and create a fresh orchestrator workspace.
```

## Expected Behavior

After first-run onboarding selects Codex:

- Local project config should be flat and behavior-only:

```yaml
runtime: tmux
agent: codex
workspace: worktree
agentRules: ...
```

- Global config should persist the selected first-run defaults:

```yaml
defaults:
  runtime: tmux
  agent: codex
  workspace: worktree
  notifiers: []
```

- CLI and dashboard should resolve the same effective project id.
- The dashboard should find the orchestrator session created by `ao start`.
- Repair should not be required immediately after first-run onboarding.

## Root Cause

The first-run path mixed the old wrapped local config model with the newer global portfolio config model.

Likely code path:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` / `autoCreateConfig()` generated a wrapped local config with `defaults.agent: codex` and `projects.ao`.
- The same flow registered the project globally through `registerProjectInGlobalConfig(...)`, which can create a generated global project id such as `ao_<hash>`.
- The selected first-run agent was not persisted into `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` defaults, so global defaults could remain `claude-code`.
- Dashboard and web APIs load through the global-backed config, while the CLI/session metadata from first-run was created under the local project identity.
- `SessionManager.list/get` operates over `config.projects`, so metadata stored under the old project id is invisible when the effective project id is the generated global id.
- Dashboard repair flattens local config, but does not migrate existing session metadata/worktree storage from the old local id to the generated global id.

## Suspected Regression

High-confidence direct regression candidate:

- PR #1819 / commit `d95c9def1` - `fix(cli): first-run startup creates global config with project registered (#1766) (#1819)`

Related architectural changes that made the bug visible:

- PR #1343 / commit `f3ce113c4` - multi-project storage, global/local config resolution, degraded repair
- PR #1466 / commit `36fed87b2` - generated project ids such as `ao_<hash>`
- commit `f674422a6` - canonical `{sessionPrefix}-orchestrator` ids
- commit `be061a398` - older-orchestrator-workspace warning behavior

## Impact

- Breaks first-run onboarding for users who choose Codex when global defaults are still Claude Code.
- Makes the dashboard appear broken even though the orchestrator process and worktree exist.
- Can leave users in a confusing repair loop: `Session not found` -> `config needs repair` -> older workspace warning.
- High severity because this affects the install/start path and makes AO look unusable immediately after onboarding.

## Fix Approach

The first-run path should:

1. Write a flat local project config, not a wrapped `projects:` config.
2. Register the project globally.
3. Persist the selected first-run defaults globally, including `agent`, `runtime`, `workspace`, `notifiers`, and `port`.
4. Reload/return the effective global-backed config so CLI and dashboard operate on the same project id.
5. Add a regression test for first-run Codex selection proving local config is flat and global defaults resolve to `codex`.

A local fix has been validated with:

```bash
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- __tests__/commands/start.test.ts
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck
pnpm build
```

## Notes

The observed repaired state after the fix resolves to:

```json
{
  "effectiveProjectIds": ["ao_0242ccdd19"],
  "effectiveProjectAgents": {
    "ao_0242ccdd19": "codex"
  },
  "effectiveSessionPrefixes": {
    "ao_0242ccdd19": "ao"
  }
}
```
