title: feat(agent-codex): use Codex hooks for activity detection
body:
## Summary

This PR pivots Codex hook work away from raw hook telemetry and into AO activity observations:

- installs a project-local Codex hook activity updater (`.codex/ao-codex-activity-updater.cjs`)
- enables Codex hooks on launch/resume with `--enable hooks`
- pre-trusts only AO's updater hook commands and marks the project trusted so Codex loads project-local hooks
- maps hook payloads directly into normal `.ao/activity.jsonl` entries with `source: "hook"`, `trigger`, and `sessionId`
- removes `.ao/codex-hooks.jsonl` as both an output and an input; raw hook payloads are not persisted

## Activity-state impact from hook entries

- `active`: hook updater writes `active` for `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStart`, `PreCompact`, and `PostCompact`. These decay through the existing AO activity fallback (`active` → `ready` → `idle`).
- `ready`: hook updater writes `ready` for `Stop`; it decays to `idle` through the existing AO activity fallback.
- `waiting_input`: hook updater writes `waiting_input` for `PermissionRequest`, scoped by `AO_SESSION_ID`.
- `blocked`: not affected by hooks. Codex hook payloads currently do not provide a clear blocked/error event, so blocked still comes from native Codex JSONL (`error` / `stream_error`) and terminal-derived AO safety-net activity.
- `idle`: not written by hooks. Idle is produced only by existing age decay.
- `exited`: not affected by hooks. Process exit detection still short-circuits before file reads.

## Precedence and scoping

- Native Codex JSONL actionable states (`waiting_input`, `blocked`) still win.
- Terminal-derived AO actionable activity remains a safety net.
- Hook actionable activity is ignored when it is older than newer native non-actionable Codex JSONL evidence.
- Hook activity entries are ignored when they belong to a different AO session or predate the current session.
- Malformed/partial `.ao/activity.jsonl` lines are skipped.

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core build`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex build`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex test`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex typecheck`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint` (passes with existing warnings)
- `pnpm test` (fails in existing `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-linear` tests because `@composio/core` is not installed; Codex tests pass)

title: chore(cli): quiet down ao start output by default; add --verbose flag
body:
## Problem

`ao start` currently prints a lot of dashboard/plugin chatter that adds no value for the common case (start it, point me at the dashboard, prompt me to restore sessions). Most of it is duplicated, internal infrastructure noise, or hints that don't change between runs.

### Current verbose output

```
harshitsinghbhandari@Harshits-Mac-2 agent-orchestrator % ao start

  ⚠ Found 1 legacy storage directory that needs migration.
    Sessions stored in the old format won't appear until migrated.
    Run ao migrate-storage to upgrade (use --dry-run to preview).

  Preventing macOS idle sleep while AO is running

Starting orchestrator for Agent Orchestrator

⠋ Starting dashboard  Mode: optimized (production bundles)
  Tip: use --dev for hot reload when editing dashboard UI

✔ Dashboard starting on http://localhost:3000
  (Dashboard will be ready in a few seconds)

[notifier-openclaw] No token configured.
  Add hooks.token to your OpenClaw config, or set notifiers.openclaw.openclawConfigPath.
  Run: ao setup openclaw
[notifier-slack] No webhookUrl configured — notifications will be no-ops
[notifier-webhook] No url configured — notifications will be no-ops
⠹ Ensuring orchestrator session[direct-terminal] [DirectTerminal] Using tmux: /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux
[direct-terminal] [MuxServer] Mux WebSocket server created (noServer mode)
[direct-terminal] [DirectTerminal] WebSocket server listening on port 14801
⠼ Ensuring orchestrator session[next]    ▲ Next.js 15.5.15
[next]    - Local:        http://localhost:3000
[next]    - Network:      http://100.88.213.33:3000
[next]  ✓ Starting...
⠴ Ensuring orchestrator session[next]  ✓ Ready in 264ms
✔ Restored orchestrator session: ao-orchestrator
⠋ Starting project supervisor[notifier-openclaw] No token configured.
  Add hooks.token to your OpenClaw config, or set notifiers.openclaw.openclawConfigPath.
  Run: ao setup openclaw
[notifier-slack] No webhookUrl configured — notifications will be no-ops
[notifier-webhook] No url configured — notifications will be no-ops
✔ Lifecycle project supervisor started
```

Notable issues:

1. **Notifier `not configured` warnings print TWICE** — once during `getSessionManager` (CLI process) and again during `startProjectSupervisor` (supervisor reconcile) — because each path calls `getPluginRegistry` with a different `configPath` (local vs global), so the registry cache misses.
2. `[direct-terminal] [DirectTerminal] Using tmux: ...`, `[MuxServer] Mux WebSocket server created`, and `WebSocket server listening on port 14801` are internal boot logs from the dashboard's terminal websocket server — never relevant to humans starting AO.
3. `[next]  ✓ Starting...` and `[next]  ✓ Ready in 264ms` are Next.js lifecycle status lines; the dashboard URL is already shown in the `[next]    - Local: ...` line.
4. `Tip: use --dev for hot reload when editing dashboard UI` shows on every start; once seen, it's clutter. The `--dev` flag is discoverable via `ao start --help`.
5. `✔ Dashboard starting on http://localhost:3000` is duplicated by the `[next]    - Local: http://localhost:3000` line that comes a few lines later.

### Target output

```
harshitsinghbhandari@Harshits-Mac-2 agent-orchestrator % ao start

  ⚠ Found 1 legacy storage directory that needs migration.
    Sessions stored in the old format won't appear until migrated.
    Run ao migrate-storage to upgrade (use --dry-run to preview).

  Preventing macOS idle sleep while AO is running

Starting orchestrator for Agent Orchestrator

⠋ Starting dashboard  Mode: optimized (production bundles)
⠹ Ensuring orchestrator session
⠼ Ensuring orchestrator session
[next]    ▲ Next.js 15.5.15
[next]    - Local:        http://localhost:3000
[next]    - Network:      http://100.88.213.33:3000
⠴ Ensuring orchestrator session
✔ Restored orchestrator session: ao-orchestrator
⠋ Starting project supervisor
✔ Lifecycle project supervisor started

  10 session(s) were active before last ao stop (stopped at 5/20/2026, 1:54:30 PM):
  ao-139, ao-143, ao-144, ao-151, ao-154, ao-160, ao-162, ao-166, ao-168, ao-orchestrator

  2 session(s) from other projects were also stopped:
  harshitsinghbhandari-github-io: har-orchestrator
  donna_00956d65b9: don-orchestrator

│
◆  Restore these sessions?
│  ● Yes / ○ No
└
```

## Proposed fix

Quiet by default, with `--verbose` to recover the diagnostic output.

- Add `ao start --verbose` flag. Default (no flag) sets `process.env.AO_QUIET_STARTUP = "1"` for the parent and (via `stdio: "inherit"`/env propagation) all child processes.
- In `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`: gate the `Tip: use --dev` line, the `spinner.succeed("Dashboard starting on …")` line, and the `(Dashboard will be ready in a few seconds)` line on `AO_QUIET_STARTUP !== "1"`.
- In `packages/web/server/start-all.ts`: when `AO_QUIET_STARTUP === "1"`, drop the known-quiet boot lines (`[DirectTerminal] Using tmux:`, `[MuxServer] Mux WebSocket server created`, `[DirectTerminal] WebSocket server listening`, `[next]  ✓ Starting…`, `[next]  ✓ Ready in …`). Other output passes through unchanged so crashes/errors stay visible.
- In `packages/plugins/notifier-openclaw|notifier-slack|notifier-webhook` `create()`: gate the `No X configured` `console.warn` on `AO_QUIET_STARTUP !== "1"`. This also incidentally fixes the duplicate-print problem — both call sites in the AO start flow read the same env var.

No behavior change for non-`ao start` callers (they don't set `AO_QUIET_STARTUP`).

## Tests

- `packages/cli/__tests__/commands/start.test.ts`: assert that running `ao start` without `--verbose` sets `AO_QUIET_STARTUP=1`, and `ao start --verbose` does not.
- New `packages/web/server/__tests__/start-all.test.ts`: unit-test the line-filter helper for each known-quiet pattern + an unrelated line that should pass through.
- Notifier plugin tests: add a test that confirms `AO_QUIET_STARTUP=1` suppresses the warning, and that absence of the env var preserves today's behavior.

title: chore(cli): quiet down ao start output; add --verbose flag
body:
## Summary

- `ao start` is quiet by default now: notifier "not configured" warnings, the `Tip: use --dev` hint, the `Dashboard starting on …` checkmark, the `(Dashboard will be ready …)` follow-up, the `[direct-terminal]/[MuxServer]` boot lines, and Next.js's `✓ Starting…` / `✓ Ready in …` lifecycle lines are all suppressed. Spinners, the Next.js URL banner, lifecycle success lines, and the restore prompt still show.
- Mechanism: `ao start` sets `AO_QUIET_STARTUP=1` in `process.env` (inherited by child processes) when `--verbose` isn't passed. `start.ts`, `packages/web/server/log-filter.ts` (consumed by `start-all.ts`), and the three notifier plugins (openclaw/slack/webhook) all read that env var. Same env var fixes the notifier-warning duplication that came from the plugin registry being instantiated twice (CLI process + supervisor reconcile against the global config) — both call sites now respect quiet mode.
- `--verbose` opts back into the noisy output.

Closes #1951.

### Before vs after

Before — verbose by default ([see issue](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1951) for the full paste).

After:

```

  ⚠ Found 1 legacy storage directory that needs migration.
    Sessions stored in the old format won't appear until migrated.
    Run ao migrate-storage to upgrade (use --dry-run to preview).

  Preventing macOS idle sleep while AO is running

Starting orchestrator for Agent Orchestrator

⠋ Starting dashboard  Mode: optimized (production bundles)
⠹ Ensuring orchestrator session
⠼ Ensuring orchestrator session
[next]    ▲ Next.js 15.5.15
[next]    - Local:        http://localhost:3000
[next]    - Network:      http://100.88.213.33:3000
⠴ Ensuring orchestrator session
✔ Restored orchestrator session: ao-orchestrator
⠋ Starting project supervisor
✔ Lifecycle project supervisor started

  10 session(s) were active before last ao stop (stopped at 5/20/2026, 1:54:30 PM):
  ao-139, ao-143, ao-144, …

│
◆  Restore these sessions?
│  ● Yes / ○ No
└
```

## Why a single env var instead of passing a flag through

Three independent consumers need to be quiet: the parent `ao start` process (for the dashboard banner lines), the dashboard child process (`packages/web/server/start-all.ts`, which prefixes its child stdout with `[next]` / `[direct-terminal]`), and the notifier plugin `create()` functions (loaded both in the CLI and inside the project-supervisor reconcile loop with a different `configPath` cache key, which is why the warnings showed up twice). A `process.env` flag rides cleanly across all three without rewiring plugin constructors or `spawnManagedDaemonChild` callsites.

## Notes on what's NOT silenced

- Real crashes / restart notices from `start-all.ts` — `exited with code N`, `restarting (attempt X/Y)`, anything that isn't a known boot-time pattern — still pass through, so dashboard breakage stays visible.
- The Next.js URL banner (`▲ Next.js`, `- Local:`, `- Network:`) still prints; only the `✓ Starting…` and `✓ Ready in …` status lines are dropped.
- Non-`ao start` callers (e.g. SDK consumers, tests, other CLI commands) don't set `AO_QUIET_STARTUP`, so notifier warnings keep firing as they do today.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm lint` (no new warnings introduced)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-slack --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-webhook --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-openclaw test` — added a test in each plugin verifying `AO_QUIET_STARTUP=1` suppresses the no-config warning, and that absence of the env var keeps today's behavior.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — added `server/__tests__/log-filter.test.ts` covering the `shouldEmitLog` cases (quiet drops boot lines, verbose passes through, unrelated errors always pass).
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli vitest run __tests__/commands/start.test.ts` — added a `verbose flag` describe block that asserts `AO_QUIET_STARTUP=1` is set when `--verbose` is omitted, and unset when `--verbose` is passed.
- [ ] Manual smoke: run `ao start` locally and confirm the output matches "after" above; `ao start --verbose` matches "before".

`packages/cli/__tests__/lib/path-equality.test.ts > canonicalCompareKey > expands ~ to HOME` fails on macOS (compares `/var/folders/…` against `/private/var/folders/…` — the standard macOS symlink). title: Sidebar re-mounts on every route navigation
body:
## Bug

The `ProjectSidebar` is **not** in the root layout — it's duplicated across multiple page components. Navigating between routes causes a full sidebar unmount/remount, which is visibly jarring and loses local state (collapsed, mobile toggle, scroll position).

## Root Cause

The sidebar lives in **three separate places**:

1. **`app/projects/layout.tsx`** → `ProjectLayoutClient` → `ProjectSidebar` (the "correct" one — persists within `/projects/[projectId]/*`)
2. **`app/page.tsx`** (root dashboard) → `DashboardInner` renders its **own** `ProjectSidebar` with separate `SidebarContext.Provider` and local state
3. **`app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`** (legacy route) → `SessionPageShell` has its **own standalone** `ProjectSidebar` instance

The root `app/layout.tsx` only has `<html><body><Providers>{children}</Providers>` — no sidebar.

When you navigate from `/` to `/projects/...` or to `/sessions/[id]`, you cross layout boundaries. Next.js remounts the entire subtree because each route owns its own sidebar instance. The sidebar is a **page-level concern** when it should be a **layout-level concern**.

## Expected Behavior

- Sidebar renders once in the root layout and persists across all route changes
- Only the main content area swaps on navigation
- Sidebar state (collapsed, mobile, scroll) survives route transitions

## Fix

1. Move `ProjectSidebar` + `SidebarContext.Provider` into `app/layout.tsx` (or a dedicated client layout wrapper)
2. Remove the duplicate sidebar instances from `Dashboard.tsx` (`DashboardInner`) and the legacy `sessions/[id]/page.tsx` (`SessionPageShell`)
3. All pages should consume `useSidebarContext()` from the layout — never render their own sidebar

## Affected Files

- `packages/web/src/app/layout.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/app/page.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/app/projects/layout.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/app/projects/[projectId]/project-layout-client.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/workspace/SidebarContext.tsx`

title: bug(agent-codex): Nix-wrapped Codex runs as codex-unwrapped and is marked exited
body:
## Bug

When Codex is launched through the local Nix-style `codex` wrapper, the actual process in the tmux pane is `codex-unwrapped`, but AO's Codex process probe only matches a path component named exactly `codex`. The session can therefore be running and visible in tmux while AO marks it as `detecting` / `agent_process_exited` / `process_missing`.

**Source:** local Codex chat report from Tanishq on 2026-05-20 (no public URL)
**Analyzed against:** `45de80ce3f8bae4f8a2f8ff00bf81b09af874025`
**Confidence:** High — live tmux/process evidence plus exact probe regex traced.

## Reproduction

Observed on macOS with Codex available through this PATH entry:

```text
/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/.local/bin/codex
```

That wrapper eventually execs:

```text
/nix/store/n6yvqvcmp1jbg031vssnp55hfzsksnm5-codex-0.131.0/bin/codex-unwrapped
```

Steps:

1. Start AO with a Codex orchestrator session (`ao start`).
2. AO launches/restores `ao-orchestrator` in tmux.
3. Inspect the pane and process table:

```text
$ tmux list-panes -t ao-orchestrator -F '#{pane_tty} #{pane_pid} #{pane_current_command}'
/dev/ttys002 96871 bash

$ ps -eo pid,ppid,tty,args | grep ttys002
96871 96867 ttys002 bash /var/folders/.../ao-launch-e9c87491-5443-40e6-ae33-0de3c9ae93b8.sh
96901 96871 ttys002 /nix/store/n6yvqvcmp1jbg031vssnp55hfzsksnm5-codex-0.131.0/bin/codex-unwrapped resume ...
```

4. AO metadata still records the orchestrator as exited/detecting:

```json
{
  "status": "detecting",
  "lifecycle": {
    "session": {
      "state": "detecting",
      "reason": "agent_process_exited"
    },
    "runtime": {
      "state": "exited",
      "reason": "process_missing"
    }
  },
  "lifecycleEvidence": "signal_disagreement runtime=alive process=dead activity_signal=valid via_native activity=exited ..."
}
```

## Root Cause

`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` hardcodes the tmux/ps process matcher to an exact `codex` path component:

```ts
const processRe = /(?:^|\/)codex(?:\s|$)/;
```

That does not match the real Nix-launched process path:

```text
/nix/store/...-codex-0.131.0/bin/codex-unwrapped
```

The false negative flows into lifecycle as `process=dead`, so a live Codex session is marked exited.

Related code:

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:706-735` — tmux pane TTY + `ps -eo pid,tty,args` probe and exact `codex` regex.
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:535-557` — launch command starts from `codex` / resolved binary.
- `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:55-104` — long launch commands run through a temp `ao-launch-*.sh` script and exported PATH.

## Fix Direction

Short-term narrow fix:

- Teach the Codex probe to recognize Nix-wrapped process names such as `codex-unwrapped` while preserving the existing exact `codex` match.
- Add a unit test where `ps` returns `/nix/store/.../bin/codex-unwrapped resume ...` for the pane TTY and `isProcessRunning()` returns true.

Better follow-up:

- Fold this into #1896 / #1899 so agent process matching supports aliases or executable lineage instead of every plugin carrying one fragile regex.

## Impact

- Dashboard and lifecycle state can show a live Codex orchestrator/session as failed or detecting.
- Recovery/stuck logic can run against incorrect `process_missing` evidence.
- This affects Nix/Darwin-style Codex installs where the wrapper command is `codex` but the long-lived child process is `codex-unwrapped`.

## Related

- #1896 — shared `isProcessRunning` refactor.
- #1899 — broader activity/liveness contract redesign.
- #1858 — broader runtime/process observation store discussion.

## Note: separate local shim failure

The original user-visible terminal error was:

```text
/var/folders/.../ao-launch-....sh: /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/.local/bin/codex: /run/current-system/sw/bin/bash: bad interpreter: No such file or directory
```

That part came from the local `~/.local/bin/codex` wrapper shebang and appears environment-level/transient: the wrapper now runs `codex --version` successfully after `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash` exists. The AO bug captured here is the persistent false-negative process detection once Codex does launch.

title: bug(cli): `ao update` on nightly channel silently strands users on old stable — `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>` is always semver-less-than any `0.X.Y`
body:
## Bug

Users on `updateChannel: nightly` whose locally-installed version is any stable `0.X.Y` (≥ 0.1.0) are **silently stranded** by `ao update`. Each invocation reports *"Already on latest nightly (0.X.Y)"* — forever — even though newer code (both new nightlies *and* new stables) is published. The mechanism is a `semver`-comparison gap: nightly tags ship as `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>`, which semver always orders *below* `0.X.Y`, so the locally installed version "wins" the comparison and no update is ever offered.

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding, reproduced on this machine | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `19d2a34f` | **Confidence:** High (reproduced, exact lines + npm dist-tags ground-truth).

## Reproduction

1. Install AO at any stable version, e.g. `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@0.7.0`.
2. Set `updateChannel: nightly` in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` (or via onboarding).
3. Run `ao update`. Output:
   ```
   Already on latest nightly (0.7.0).
   ```
4. npm dist-tags at the same moment:
   ```
   latest  = 0.8.0
   nightly = 0.0.0-nightly-ee2f4256f43ab0edf32a90244e6a5c9ca76ef858
   ```
5. Published-versions sequence on npm:
   ```
   …0.6.0, 0.7.0, 0.0.0-nightly-…, 0.8.0
   ```
   The user can pull **neither** the new nightly (semver says they're ahead) **nor** the new stable (their channel queries `nightly`, not `latest`).

## Root cause

`packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts:265,446`:

```ts
const tag = channel === "nightly" ? "nightly" : "latest";
// → fetches dist-tags[tag] and semver-compares against the local version
```

When `tag === "nightly"`, the remote version is always `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>`. Per semver, `0.0.0-prerelease < 0.7.0` (any released minor). So `latest > local` is *never* true on the nightly channel once the user is on a real stable. The update prompt never fires; the user is silently pinned.

Compounds with [#1743](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1743) (`ao update` kills worker sessions): even if a user *did* notice they're stuck, the path to fix it has its own user-hostile blast radius.

## Fix direction (proposed; choose one or combine)

1. **Treat `0.0.0-<prerelease>` specially on the `nightly` channel.** When the dist-tag's `nightly` resolves to a `0.0.0-<sha>` version, compare by commit/publish date (e.g. fetch `versions[nightly].time` from the npm package document, already requested) instead of semver. If the nightly's commit-time is newer than the install's, offer it.
2. **Cross-channel promotion.** On `nightly`, also check `dist-tags.latest`. If `latest > local`, surface the upgrade too — a newer stable is a legitimate target for nightly users (they tend to want *the freshest code*, however tagged).
3. **At minimum, transparent reporting.** Instead of *"Already on latest nightly (0.X.Y)"*, print *which* remote version was compared against, e.g.:
   ```
   Already on latest nightly (0.7.0).
   Compared against nightly tag 0.0.0-nightly-ee2f4256 (older than local).
   Latest stable is 0.8.0 — switch channel with `ao update --channel=stable` to upgrade.
   ```
   This is the cheapest mitigation and unblocks affected users immediately.

The proper fix is (1) or (2) + (3); (3) alone is at minimum a no-regret information improvement.

Recommended tests:
- Local install 0.7.0, channel=nightly, nightly tag = `0.0.0-nightly-X`, latest = 0.8.0 → `ao update` must offer 0.8.0 or the latest nightly, not say "already on latest."
- Local install 0.7.0, channel=stable, latest = 0.8.0 → must offer 0.8.0 (existing behavior, ensure no regression).
- Local install `0.0.0-nightly-A`, channel=nightly, nightly = `0.0.0-nightly-B` published later → must offer B (existing behavior, ensure no regression).

## Impact

- **Every user on `updateChannel: nightly` with local version ≥ 0.1.0 is silently stuck.** They see `ao update` say "you're on latest" and trust it. Meanwhile bug fixes (e.g., the bottleneck/PR-tracking/instrumentation fixes from the last several days) never reach them. Discoverability of this is effectively zero — there is no visible error.
- Makes the unrelated `pnpm add -g` upgrade friction (virtual-store layout, etc.) much more painful because users can't even tell they're stale.
- Compounds with #1743 to make AO's upgrade story end-to-end broken in production.

## Related
- #1743 — `ao update` kills worker sessions (sibling generic upgrade UX bug)
- #1879 — dashboard update banner dead-end (adjacent UX surface)
- #1540 — stale update prompt for source installs (related comparison bug class)
- #1767 — config hot-reload (related: channel changes don't take effect at runtime)

title: bug(release): nightly snapshot version is `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>` instead of `<actual-version>-nightly-<sha>` — root cause of #1956
body:
## Bug

Nightly releases are published to npm with versions like `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>` — *always* starting with `0.0.0`, regardless of the actual package version at that git SHA. They should start with the real package.json version (e.g. `0.8.0-nightly-<sha>` if the SHA's repo state has `version: 0.8.0`). The `0.0.0` prefix makes nightlies semver-less-than any stable `0.X.Y` (≥ 0.1.0), which silently strands every user on `updateChannel: nightly` (see #1956).

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding. **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `19d2a34f`. **Confidence:** High (exact workflow line + documented `changesets` config option).

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/canary.yml:123`:

```yaml
- run: pnpm changeset version --snapshot nightly
```

Per [changesets snapshot docs](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/snapshot-releases.md), `--snapshot <tag>` produces versions of the form `0.0.0-<tag>-<id>` *by default*. That `0.0.0` is a sentinel meant to clearly distinguish snapshot publishes from real releases — but it has the side effect of making every snapshot semver-less-than the lowest real release.

Changesets supports overriding this exact behavior in `.changeset/config.json`:

```json
{
  "snapshot": {
    "useCalculatedVersion": true,
    "prereleaseTemplate": "{tag}-{commit}"
  }
}
```

With `useCalculatedVersion: true`, snapshots compute the version by taking the current package version (e.g., `0.8.0`) and appending the prerelease suffix → `0.8.0-nightly-<commit-or-sha>`. This is exactly what the user expects ("starts with the actual version at that SHA").

Empirical confirmation:

```
Current published nightly: 0.0.0-nightly-ee2f4256f43ab0edf32a90244e6a5c9ca76ef858
Source @ that SHA:        0.8.0 (in packages/*/package.json)
What it SHOULD be:        0.8.0-nightly-ee2f4256… (or equivalent)
```

The current scheme silently breaks `ao update` on the nightly channel for **every user on any stable ≥ 0.1.0** — see [#1956](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1956) for the user-facing consequence and trace.

## Fix

One-config-file change:

`.changeset/config.json` — add (or merge into) a `snapshot` block:

```json
{
  "snapshot": {
    "useCalculatedVersion": true,
    "prereleaseTemplate": "{tag}-{commit}"
  }
}
```

This is local-only config; the existing `pnpm changeset version --snapshot nightly` line in `canary.yml` does not need to change. Once the next nightly is cut after this lands, the published version becomes `<package-version>-nightly-<commit>` and #1956 disappears by construction (semver-compare works correctly).

### Verification after fix
- Trigger `canary.yml` (workflow_dispatch). Expect the npm `nightly` dist-tag to update to `<current-package-version>-nightly-<sha>`.
- Existing users on stable 0.7.0 with `updateChannel: nightly` should see `ao update` actually offer the nightly (and the next stable 0.8.0+ will also semver-exceed them).

### Migration consideration
Existing published `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>` versions on npm are immutable. After the fix, the *new* nightly tag will jump from `0.0.0-nightly-…` to `<calculated>-nightly-…`, which is a semver-monotonic upgrade for users (any future calculated version beats any 0.0.0 prerelease). So no user is regressed. No npm un-publishing needed.

## Why this is the right level to fix

[#1956](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1956) proposes patches to `update-check.ts` to compensate for the broken version scheme (special-case `0.0.0-*`, cross-channel promotion, transparent diagnostics). Those are real and useful, but they're *workarounds* for the version-scheme defect. **Fixing this issue closes #1956 by construction** — `update-check.ts`'s naïve semver compare becomes correct.

Recommend landing this first; #1956's diagnostic-output improvement (#3 in its fix list) is still worth shipping as a no-regret transparency win.

## Related
- #1956 — `ao update` semver-strand on nightly channel (consequence of this bug).
- #1743 — `ao update` kills worker sessions (sibling generic upgrade UX bug).
- Existing release/canary workflow architecture: `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/canary.yml`.

title: Fix default notifier onboarding: remove Composio defaults, enable dashboard + desktop
body:
## Bug / Product Gap

AO currently defaults notification routing to include `composio` even when the user has not run any Composio setup flow. At the same time, the desired first-run notification experience is not fully wired:

- `dashboard` should be enabled by default for all notification priorities.
- `desktop` should be enabled by default for urgent/critical notifications only.
- `AO Notifier.app` should be installed/configured during `ao start` on macOS.
- Composio, Slack, Discord, Webhook, OpenClaw, etc. should remain manual opt-in through `ao setup ...`.

Current behavior does not match that policy.

**Analyzed against:** `45de80ce3f8bae4f8a2f8ff00bf81b09af874025`
**Observed AO version:** `0.8.0`
**Environment observed:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, zsh, Node `v24.15.0`
**Confidence:** High - traced through global config defaults, effective config loading, notifier setup flows, plugin registration, and live `ao doctor`/setup status output.

## Current Behavior

Fresh/global config defaults still include Composio:

```ts
// packages/core/src/global-config.ts
defaults.notifiers = ["composio", "desktop"]

notificationRouting = {
  urgent: ["desktop", "composio"],
  action: ["desktop", "composio"],
  warning: ["composio"],
  info: ["composio"],
}
```

This can cause `composio` to appear in `~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml` or the effective config even when the user never ran:

```bash
ao setup composio
```

The plugin registry treats `notificationRouting: ["composio"]` as enough to instantiate the built-in Composio notifier with empty config. If no `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` exists, it becomes a no-op and may warn. If an env key does exist, AO may attempt Composio delivery without explicit notifier setup.

Live observed effective config included:

```yaml
notifiers:
  desktop:
    plugin: desktop
    backend: ao-app
    dashboardUrl: http://localhost:3000
  dashboard:
    plugin: dashboard
    limit: 50

notificationRouting:
  urgent: [composio, desktop, discord, dashboard]
  action: [composio, desktop, discord, dashboard]
  warning: [composio, desktop, discord, dashboard]
  info: [composio, desktop, discord, dashboard]
```

`ao doctor` then reported Composio plugin resolution as passing even though there was no `notifiers.composio` setup block.

## Desired Behavior

Fresh `ao start` / fresh global config should produce notification defaults equivalent to:

```yaml
notifiers:
  desktop:
    plugin: desktop
    backend: ao-app
    dashboardUrl: http://localhost:3000
  dashboard:
    plugin: dashboard
    limit: 50

notificationRouting:
  urgent:
    - desktop
    - dashboard
  action:
    - dashboard
  warning:
    - dashboard
  info:
    - dashboard
```

Interpretation:

- “Critical” user-facing notifications map to AO’s current `urgent` priority.
- Dashboard receives all priorities.
- Desktop receives only urgent/critical notifications.
- Composio is absent unless explicitly configured.
- Discord/Slack/Webhook/OpenClaw are absent unless explicitly configured.

## Expected `ao start` Behavior

On first run / startup:

1. Ensure dashboard notifier config exists.
2. Route dashboard to all priorities.
3. On macOS, install/configure `AO Notifier.app` best-effort.
4. Route desktop only to urgent priority.
5. Do not add Composio unless user runs `ao setup composio` or a `composio-*` setup command.
6. Do not add Slack/Discord/Webhook/OpenClaw unless user runs their setup commands.

If desktop setup cannot complete, `ao start` should not fail the whole startup. It should warn and continue with dashboard-only notifications.

## Files / Areas To Inspect

- `packages/core/src/global-config.ts`
  - `GlobalConfigSchema.defaults.notifiers`
  - `GlobalConfigSchema.notificationRouting`
  - `createDefaultGlobalConfig()`

- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`
  - first-run config/global registration path
  - startup onboarding hooks

- `packages/cli/src/lib/desktop-setup.ts`
  - `runDesktopSetupAction`
  - non-interactive default currently routes desktop to `all`

- `packages/cli/src/lib/dashboard-setup.ts`
  - non-interactive default currently routes dashboard to `urgent-action`

- `packages/cli/src/lib/notifier-routing.ts`
  - `applyNotifierRoutingPreset`
  - existing presets may need an explicit startup path for “desktop urgent-only + dashboard all”

- `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts`
  - currently instantiates a notifier when it is referenced by routing even without a config block

## Root Cause

The standard config path was previously changed to make notifications opt-in by default:

```text
722d14298 fix(config): disable all notifications by default — fully opt-in
```

But the newer global/hybrid config path reintroduced Composio defaults in `global-config.ts`, likely during the multi-project/global registry work.

As a result, the effective config can contain Composio routing without explicit setup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fresh global config does not include `composio`.
- Fresh `ao start` configures `dashboard` notifier by default.

title: fix(cli,release): nightly channel update logic + snapshot version scheme (closes #1956, closes #1957)
body:
Closes #1956.
Closes #1957.

## Summary
This fixes the nightly upgrade path end-to-end in two parts:

### Part A — runtime cure for #1956
Nightly update checks now use dist-tag version **identity** instead of semver ordering:

- `nightly`: if the registry's `dist-tags.nightly` version string differs from the installed version, AO treats it as an update.
- `stable` / `manual`: continue to use numeric semver comparison via `isVersionOutdated`.

This is the primary user-visible fix. Nightly users want the freshest snapshot from main, and the `nightly` dist-tag already points at that target. Identity comparison avoids every prerelease/SHA ordering trap, including both lexical directions of `0.0.0-nightly-<sha>`.

The same channel-aware helper is exported from core and used by:
- CLI update checks / cache writes / startup notices.
- Dashboard `/api/version`, so the web update banner agrees with the CLI cache semantics.

### Part B — publish-side correctness for #1957
`.changeset/config.json` now:

- Removes the silently ignored nested `snapshot.useCalculatedVersionForSnapshots` key.
- Uses the stable `snapshot.useCalculatedVersion: true` key supported by the installed Changesets stack.
- Keeps the existing `{tag}-{commit}` prerelease template to preserve the published nightly shape while changing the base from `0.0.0` to the calculated package version.

Part A alone fixes #1956's immediate symptom. Part B alone fixes #1957 by making future published nightlies use the calculated package version. Together they make nightly updates robust now and keep future published versions compatible with the existing hyphen-delimited nightly format.

## Verification

Unit/targeted checks:

```text
pnpm exec prettier --check .changeset/config.json packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts packages/cli/__tests__/lib/update-check.test.ts packages/core/src/version-compare.ts packages/core/src/__tests__/version-compare.test.ts packages/core/src/index.ts packages/web/src/app/api/version/route.ts
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/version-compare.test.ts
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- __tests__/lib/update-check.test.ts
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck
node scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs
```

Test coverage added:
- Nightly `0.0.0-nightly-A → 0.0.0-nightly-B` updates in both SHA lexical directions.
- Nightly exact same version does not update.
- Stable `0.9.0 → 0.10.0` updates (numeric, not string compare).
- Stable `0.7.0 → 0.8.0` updates.

Throwaway worktree dry-run at `19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02` with `@changesets/cli@2.30.0`:

```text
# Before: old nested snapshot.useCalculatedVersionForSnapshots config, ignored by Changesets
pnpm changeset version --snapshot nightly
packages/ao/package.json:   0.0.0-nightly-19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02
packages/cli/package.json:  0.0.0-nightly-19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02
packages/core/package.json: 0.0.0-nightly-19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02

# After: snapshot.useCalculatedVersion: true + {tag}-{commit}
pnpm changeset version --snapshot nightly
packages/ao/package.json:   0.9.0-nightly-19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02
packages/cli/package.json:  0.9.0-nightly-19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02
packages/core/package.json: 0.9.0-nightly-19d2a34f6a6a3fc4d4eb1a85cd4bd7c30a70ca02
```

The dry-run calculated `0.9.0` because current main has pending minor changesets; the important behavior is that snapshots now use the calculated package version instead of the `0.0.0` sentinel while preserving the existing `nightly-<sha>` suffix format.

## Migration note
Existing published `0.0.0-nightly-*` versions are immutable on npm. No unpublish is needed. Part A makes users advance as soon as `dist-tags.nightly` differs from their installed version, and Part B ensures future published nightlies use the calculated package version with the existing hyphen-delimited suffix.

title: bug(web): remove user-facing `XDA` chip from terminal header — it's an internal xterm/tmux protocol acronym with zero user value
body: ## Bug Every terminal pane in the dashboard renders an `XDA` badge in its header, next to the session id and connection status: ``` TERMINAL ao-orchestrator • CONNECTED XDA ``` "XDA" is **Extended Device Attributes** — an internal xterm/tmux protocol handler (CSI `> q`) used to make tmux enable OSC 52 clipboard. It's an implementation detail of the terminal-emulation layer (see `packages/web/src/components/terminal/terminal-clipboard.ts:5,12,16`) and has no meaning to a user looking at a terminal pane. Surfacing it as a chip in the chrome is debug/developer terminology leaking into the production UI. **Source:** orchestrator dogfooding. **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `19d2a34f`. **Confidence:** High (exact render site + protocol semantics verified in code). ## Code location `packages/web/src/components/terminal/TerminalControls.tsx` (around lines 232-241): ```tsx XDA ``` Sits inside the `terminal-chrome-status-row` container alongside the connection-status dot and `statusText`. CSS comment at `packages/web/src/app/globals.css:8554` confirms it's part of the same status row. ## Fix Trivial — delete the `XDA` block in `TerminalControls.tsx` (lines ~232-241). The status dot and `statusText` stay; only the XDA chip goes. Also update the stale layout comment at `globals.css:8554` (`/* Stack: session name on top, status+XDA row below */`) to drop the `+XDA` mention, and the matching `Identity group: session name on top, status+XDA below on mobile` comment in `TerminalControls.tsx:220`. No code logic depends on the chip — XDA *behavior* (the OSC 52 handler registration) lives in `terminal-clipboard.ts` and is unaffected by removing the visual chip. Removing the chip is purely cosmetic; clipboard support continues to work. ## Impact - Cosmetic only, but pervasive: appears on every terminal pane across the dashboard, including session-detail, side panels, and mobile. - Erodes UI polish by exposing an internal protocol acronym to users in the most prominent location of every terminal view. - Sets the wrong precedent for what belongs in chrome (implementation labels vs. user-relevant status). ## Why was it there? Looks like a debug marker that survived a refactor — the protocol handler was added (per `terminal-clipboard.ts` history), and a chip was placed in the header to *visually confirm* the handler was registered. It's the kind of label that helps during implementation/QA but should be removed before shipping. No deliberate user-facing rationale is documented in the surrounding code or the surrounding comments. ## Related - #769 (closed) — Refactor: Break down DirectTerminal.tsx (the surrounding component reorganization).

title: daemon child reaping test opens random-port dashboard tabs
body:
## Bug
Running the daemon child reaping integration test opens real AO dashboard tabs in Chrome on random localhost ports. The tabs are titled `ao | Daemon Integration` and later show `Reconnecting` after the test tears down the backend, which looks like a daemon is repeatedly opening random ports.

**Source:** local user report/chat on 2026-05-20 (screenshot path was provided locally; no shareable URL)
**Reported by:** Adil
**Analyzed against:** remote `main` `ecdf0c73eca18d9e9f837854dc209cb221d22bfb`
**AO version:** `0.8.0`
**Environment:** macOS/Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, Node `v24.15.0`, shell zsh
**Confidence:** High

## Evidence
Chrome history showed repeated AO pages opened by the test:

- `http://localhost:51043/` at 2026-05-20 17:26:33 IST
- `http://localhost:57746/` at 2026-05-20 20:53:51 IST
- `http://localhost:59092/` at 2026-05-20 21:24:22 IST
- `http://localhost:59468/` at 2026-05-20 21:34:12 IST
- `http://localhost:59820/` at 2026-05-20 21:45:26 IST

Each entry had title `ao | Daemon Integration`. Searching the repo finds that display name in `packages/integration-tests/src/daemon-children.integration.test.ts`.

AO activity logs around those exact timestamps showed integration-test-like activity (`migration.completed`, `cli.update_invoked`, `workspace.branch_collision`, config reloads), not normal user dashboard navigation.

## Reproduction
1. Run the integration/default test suite locally in the AO repo, e.g. `pnpm test` or the daemon child reaping integration test.
2. Observe Chrome opening a new AO dashboard tab on a random localhost port.
3. After the test exits, the tab remains open and shows a reconnecting dashboard.

## Root Cause
`packages/integration-tests/src/daemon-children.integration.test.ts` uses the real AO startup path just to verify daemon child cleanup:

- It allocates a random port with `getFreePort()`.
- It writes a test project with `displayName: Daemon Integration`.
- It spawns `ao start --no-orchestrator --reap-orphans`.

`ao start` then follows the normal dashboard startup flow in `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` and auto-opens the browser once the port is ready via `waitForPortAndOpen(...)`.

`waitForPortAndOpen` in `packages/cli/src/lib/web-dir.ts` calls `openUrl(...)`, which uses macOS `open`, causing the visible Chrome tabs.

The test sets `AO_CALLER_TYPE=agent`, but the `ao start` auto-open path does not currently skip browser opening for agent/non-human callers.

## Fix
Preferred fix: replace this integration test with a headless cleanup test that does not run `ao start`:

1. Spawn a simple dummy Node process to represent the daemon parent.
2. Spawn a simple dummy Node process to represent a daemon-owned child.
3. Register the child in `daemon-children.json` with `parentPid = dummyParent.pid`.
4. Write a fake `running.json` pointing to the dummy parent.
5. Run `ao stop --all`.
6. Assert the registered child and dummy parent are terminated.

This preserves the behavior under test (registered daemon-child cleanup on stop) without launching the dashboard, binding random ports, or opening the browser.

Additional hardening options:

- Add `--no-open` to `ao start` and use it in tests.
- Or make `ao start` skip browser auto-open when `AO_CALLER_TYPE=agent` / CI / non-human caller.
- Keep real-service integration tests out of default `pnpm test` if they intentionally bind ports or start dashboards.

## Impact
- Local `pnpm test` can unexpectedly open multiple Chrome tabs.
- Tabs point at random localhost ports and remain stale after the test exits.
- The behavior is confusing and looks like an orphan daemon or malicious port churn.
- It makes the test suite non-headless and disruptive for developers.

## Related
- #1848 / PR #1849 — daemon child reaping/orphan cleanup work in the same subsystem.
- PR #1860 — shutdown/PTY cleanup work in the same area.

title: bug(core): stopping Claude from dashboard terminal goes through detecting → stuck instead of terminating cleanly
body:
## Bug

When a Claude Code session is stopped from the dashboard terminal (Ctrl+C), the session does not transition to a clean terminal state. Instead, the dashboard shows two transient states before settling on "stuck":

1. **"Detecting runtime truth (agent process exited)"** — lifecycle enters `detecting` with reason `agent_process_exited`
2. **"Session stuck (probe failure)"** — after 3 detecting attempts or 5 minutes, escalates to `stuck` with reason `probe_failure`

The expected behavior: session should transition to `terminated`/`killed` promptly, since the agent process has genuinely exited.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1484900948397199371/1491735678156013588/1506746218020212926
**Reported by:** @Hr!shi! (hrishic7)
**Analyzed against:** `ecdf0c73` (main, 2026-05-20)
**AO version:** 0.8.0

## Reproduction

1. `ao start` with a Claude Code agent
2. Open the web dashboard
3. In the dashboard terminal, press Ctrl+C to stop the Claude session
4. Observe the lifecycle states in the dashboard

## Root Cause

The flow when Claude exits via Ctrl+C:

1. **Poll N:** `getActivityState()` detects Claude process is dead → returns `{ state: "exited" }`
2. `lifecycle-manager.ts:1059`: sets `processProbe = { state: "dead" }` and `lifecycle.runtime.state = "exited"`
3. **But** the runtime (tmux) is still alive — it has a shell prompt after Claude exits
4. `lifecycle-manager.ts:1214`: `resolveProbeDecision()` is called with `runtimeProbe = alive, processProbe = dead`
5. `lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:305`: this matches `runtimeProbe.state === "alive" && processProbe.state === "dead"` → **signal disagreement** → enters `detecting` with reason `agent_process_exited`
6. Dashboard shows: **"Detecting runtime truth (agent process exited)"**
7. **Poll N+1, N+2**: Same disagreement, detecting attempts increment (max 3)
8. `lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:149`: attempt limit or 5-min timeout exceeded → escalates to `stuck` with reason `probe_failure`
9. Dashboard shows: **"Session stuck (probe failure)"**

### The problem

`resolveProbeDecision()` treats `runtime=alive, process=dead` as an ambiguous signal disagreement requiring investigation. But when the agent is Claude Code, this is the **normal expected outcome** of Ctrl+C — Claude exits, tmux stays alive with a shell. The lifecycle should recognize this as a definitive terminal state, not an ambiguous one.

### Why it stays stuck instead of recovering

Even when the runtime probe eventually updates to `exited` (if tmux also dies), the session stays at `stuck` because:
- There's no code path that promotes `stuck` → `terminated` when runtime later exits (covered by #1933)
- The `preservingProbeFailureStuck` guard at `lifecycle-manager.ts:1365-1379` actively preserves the stuck state when `activitySignal.state === "unavailable"` and runtime is alive

### The fix

In `resolveProbeDecision()` (`lifecycle-status-decisions.ts`), when:
- `runtimeProbe.state === "alive"` AND `processProbe.state === "dead"` AND
- `activitySignal` confirms the agent exited (state is `valid` with `activity=exited`, or `stale`)

…this should transition directly to `terminated` with reason `agent_process_exited`, not enter the detecting cycle. The tmux being alive is irrelevant when the agent process is confirmed dead — the session is done.

Alternatively (simpler), add a check in `determineStatus()` after line 1063: when `processProbe = dead` AND `lifecycle.runtime.state === "exited"` AND `activitySignal` confirms exit, return `killed`/`terminated` directly, bypassing `resolveProbeDecision()`.

**Confidence:** High — traced the exact code path from agent exit through lifecycle state machine to dashboard display.

## File:index

- `resolveProbeDecision()`: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:290-348`
- Signal disagreement handling: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:303-316`
- `createDetectingDecision()`: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:120-166`
- Detecting escalation to stuck: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:149-156`
- Activity `exited` detection: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1059-1063`
- `preservingProbeFailureStuck` guard: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1365-1379`
- Dashboard serialization: `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:85-108`

## Related

- #1933 — stuck session with exited runtime never auto-promotes to terminated (overlaps: same stuck end-state, different trigger — #1933 is about runtime also dying, this is about runtime staying alive)
- PR #1945 — hooks-based activity detection for Claude (changed how `exited` is detected)
- #1454 — lifecycle state flicker on probe disagreement
- #1414 — unify CanonicalSessionState and SessionStatus

title: bug(core): manually running Claude in orphaned tmux revives stuck session on dashboard
body:
## Bug

After a Claude session is stopped from the dashboard terminal (Ctrl+C) and the session ends up in `stuck` state (per #1966), manually running `claude` inside the orphaned tmux session causes the dashboard to show the session as active/working again.

**Discord thread:** https://discord.com/channels/1484900948397199371/1491735678156013588/1506746218020212926
**Reported by:** @Hr!shi! (hrishic7)
**Analyzed against:** `ecdf0c73` (main, 2026-05-20)
**AO version:** 0.8.0

## Reproduction

1. `ao start` with a Claude Code agent
2. Ctrl+C the Claude session from the dashboard terminal → session goes to `stuck` (bug #1966)
3. SSH into the server, `tmux attach` to the AO-managed tmux session
4. Run `claude` manually inside the tmux
5. The web dashboard shows the previously-stuck session as `working` / active

## Root Cause

Two bugs compound:

1. **#1966**: Session ends up `stuck` with `probe_failure` instead of `terminated` — tmux stays alive
2. **This bug**: The lifecycle manager revives stuck sessions when it detects agent activity

The revival path in `determineStatus()`:

- `lifecycle-manager.ts:1356-1387`: The `isWeakActivityEvidence()` guard only preserves stuck state for **weak** signals (unavailable, stale)
- When Claude is manually running, the activity signal is **strong** (`valid` with `activity=active`)
- The guard is bypassed, code falls through to `lifecycle-manager.ts:1389-1401`
- Line 1392: `session.status === SESSION_STATUS.STUCK` matches
- Returns `WORKING` with `sessionState: "working"`, `sessionReason: "task_in_progress"`
- Dashboard shows the session as active again

There is **no check** for whether the session was previously terminated/stuck due to agent exit, whether the agent was manually launched by AO, or whether the runtime handle is still valid. Any process matching the agent plugin's `isProcessRunning()` check in the tmux session will revive it.

### Why this is wrong

The tmux session is an orphan — AO lost track of the agent. A human manually starting Claude in that tmux is not an AO-managed session. The dashboard should not show it as a managed working session. This creates confusion about what AO is actually orchestrating.

## Fix

Two options (both address #1966 and this bug):

**Option A (minimal, addresses both):** Fix #1966 first — when the agent process exits and runtime is alive, transition to `terminated` instead of `detecting` → `stuck`. Once properly terminated, the lifecycle manager won't poll it anymore and manual Claude usage in the tmux won't revive it.

**Option B (defense in depth):** Add a guard in the `STUCK → WORKING` transition path (line 1389-1401) that checks:
- Was the session previously `killed` or `terminated`? If so, don't revive.
- Is the agent process PID the same one AO spawned? If not, don't revive.

Option A fixes the root cause (session should have been terminated). Option B adds belt-and-suspenders protection against revival of any dead session.

**Confidence:** High — traced the exact revival code path.

## File:index

- Stuck → Working revival: `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1389-1401`
- Weak evidence guard (bypass): `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1356-1387`
- Activity signal classification: `packages/core/src/activity-signal.ts`

## Related

- #1966 — stopping Claude from dashboard terminal goes through detecting → stuck instead of terminating (root cause of orphaned tmux)
- #1933 — stuck session with exited runtime never auto-promotes to terminated
- PR #1945 — hooks-based activity detection for Claude (changed how activity is detected)

title: bug(cli): `ao update` requires killing worker sessions that have nothing to do with the upgrade — gate conflates daemon and worker lifecycles
body:
## Bug

`ao update` blocks if any session is in an "active" status, with the message *"`N` session active. Run \`ao stop\` first, then \`ao update\`."* This forces users to **kill all their worker tmux sessions** in order to upgrade the AO binary — even though worker sessions are independent of AO's binary and would survive the upgrade untouched if the daemon stopped them gracefully.

The gate conflates two completely separate concerns:

1. **Daemon/dashboard processes** load AO code into memory. They legitimately need to restart to pick up the new binary.
2. **Worker tmux sessions** are children of the *tmux server*, running agent processes (codex, claude-code, aider, opencode, etc.). They don't load AO code and don't know or care about the AO binary version. **There is no technical reason killing them is required for an AO upgrade.**

The current gate's reasoning appears to be *"if anything is running, the update might break it"* — overcautious, and it makes `ao update` user-hostile: the only way to upgrade is to lose all your work in flight.

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding. **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `ecdf0c73`. **Confidence:** High (exact gate location + design rationale verified).

## Reproduction

1. Have any worker session in `working` state (e.g. `ao spawn` something; agent is mid-task).
2. Run `ao update`.

```
Current version: 0.7.0
Latest version:  0.9.0-nightly-c8a0dcbf708a1b55c01c4e1aaa687781b0551345
Channel:         nightly

✗ 1 session active. Run `ao stop` first, then `ao update`.

    • ao-orchestrator  (working)
```

3. `ao stop` then kills **every active session across every project** — far broader than the gate's "1 active" suggests; `ao stop`'s actual kill loop (`start.ts:1779`) targets all non-terminal sessions, not just the `"working"` ones the gate counts. So a user who sees "1 session active" and runs `ao stop` may lose 6+ sessions.

The gate and the kill loop disagree on what "active" means, which is its own bug, but the deeper issue is the requirement itself.

## Code

`packages/cli/src/commands/update.ts:~204-218`:

```ts
const active = sessions.filter((s) => ACTIVE_SESSION_STATUSES.has(s.status));
if (active.length === 0) return true;

console.error(
  chalk.red(`✗ ${active.length} ${noun} active. Run \`ao stop\` first, then \`ao update\`.`),
);
// …
return false;
```

The gate runs for both `git` install and `pnpm` install update paths (the same `ensureNoActiveSessions()` is called from both `handleGitUpdate` and the pnpm-global update path).

## Why workers should survive an update

- Worker tmux sessions are launched via `tmux new-session -d -s <session-id> -e <env> ...`. They become children of the **tmux server**, not of the AO daemon. They have no parent relationship to `ao start` or the dashboard.
- Their content is the agent process (`codex`, `claude code`, `aider`, etc.) plus shell. Neither imports AO's CLI code.
- Replacing the AO binary on disk (via `pnpm add -g`) doesn't affect tmux's bookkeeping or the worker shells in any way.
- After the update, restarting the daemon (`ao start`) reattaches to existing worker tmux sessions by name (verified — this is how restore works today).

So a "safe upgrade" doesn't need to touch workers at all. It needs to:
1. Stop the daemon and its dashboard children gracefully.
2. Run the install (`pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@<tag>`).
3. Start the daemon, which reattaches to existing worker tmux sessions.

## Fix direction

**Replace the worker-kill requirement with a daemon-restart flow.** Concretely:

1. **`ensureNoActiveSessions` becomes `ensureDaemonStoppable` (or just remove it).** The gate should check daemon liveness, not worker presence. If a daemon is running, the update tooling stops it (gracefully) and restarts after.
2. **Don't ever kill worker sessions as part of `ao update`.** Their state is orthogonal.
3. **`ao update` should orchestrate** stop-daemon → pnpm-add-global → start-daemon, instead of asking the user to run `ao stop` (which kills workers) first.
4. **Status messaging stays honest.** After update: *"Updated to 0.9.0-nightly-xxx. N worker sessions reattached."*

This is the same architectural direction the team's already moving via the `ao stop` design conversation (whether `ao stop` itself should preserve workers, tracked partially in [#1743](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1743)). Fixing `ao update` here is a forcing function — once it's done, `ao stop`'s kill-all behavior becomes optional rather than mandatory infrastructure.

## Impact

- **Every AO user wanting to upgrade currently has to choose: lose all their work-in-flight, or stay on the old version.** That is the binary choice the current gate presents.
- The gate amplifies the existing bug in #1743 (lost restore state after the kill).
- Reinforces "upgrade is dangerous, do it rarely" — exactly the wrong incentive for a project shipping nightlies.
- For users running the orchestrator session itself as a worker (the recommended pattern), the kill takes their *current interactive session* down — compounding the cost.

## Related
- #1743 — `ao stop → ao update → ao start` loses restore state (downstream effect; this issue removes the need for the kill in the first place)
- #1879 — dashboard update banner dead-end with active sessions (same root, surfaces in the UI)
- #1503 — `kill()` archives instead of terminates in-place (adjacent kill-lifecycle issue)
- Our shutdown-hotfix conversation has been working around this all session via a local `&& false` patch on `shutdown.ts`'s SIGINT path; only the `ao start` Ctrl+C path is hotfixed locally — `ao update`'s `ao stop` path is unprotected and exactly why this issue matters.

title: increase GraphQL batch CI context limit for 18-check PRs
body:
## Bug
AO's GitHub GraphQL batch enrichment only requests the first **11** CI check contexts per PR:

```graphql
statusCheckRollup {
  state
  contexts(first: 11) { ... }
}
```

Our CI now has **18 checks**, so normal PRs can exceed that limit. The overall rollup state remains correct, but individual check details are truncated and AO has to fall back to REST for detailed CI check data.

**Source:** local operator report/chat on 2026-05-21
**Reported by:** Adil
**Analyzed against:** remote `main` `ecdf0c73eca18d9e9f837854dc209cb221d22bfb`
**Confidence:** High — exact query limit and fallback path traced in `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts`.

## Reproduction
1. Open or poll a PR in a repo whose CI produces 18 check contexts.
2. Let lifecycle batch enrichment run.
3. The GraphQL query requests only `contexts(first: 11)`.
4. GitHub returns `pageInfo.hasNextPage: true` for the rollup contexts.
5. AO treats `ciChecks` as incomplete and sets them to `undefined`, forcing REST fallback for check details later.

## Root Cause
`packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` hardcodes `contexts(first: 11)` inside `PR_FIELDS`:

```ts
statusCheckRollup {
  state
  // 11 keeps per-PR node cost under budget for 25-PR batch queries
  contexts(first: 11) {
    nodes { ... }
    pageInfo { hasNextPage }
  }
}
```

The parser correctly avoids trusting truncated data:

```ts
const ciChecks = contextsField && !contextsHasNextPage
  ? parseCheckContexts(contextsField)
  : undefined;
```

That fallback is safe, but because the default CI count has grown to 18, it now triggers on normal PRs.

There is also a stale comment in the extraction path that mentions `contexts(first: 20)` even though the actual query currently uses `11`.

## Recommended Fix
Increase the GraphQL CI context limit from **11** to **20**.

Suggested implementation:

```ts
const CI_CONTEXTS_FIRST = 20;
```

Use the constant in the query:

```graphql
contexts(first: ${CI_CONTEXTS_FIRST})
```

Keep the existing `pageInfo.hasNextPage` behavior so repos with more than 20 checks still fall back safely to REST.

Update comments and tests to reflect the new limit.

## Why 20?
- Current CI has 18 checks.
- `20` covers the current setup with small headroom.
- It avoids unnecessary REST fallback for normal PRs.
- It is safer than setting exactly `18`.
- It avoids a large jump to `50` or `100`, preserving GraphQL batch cost/resource safety.

## Impact
- Avoidable REST fallback calls for normal AO PRs.
- Delayed or less direct failed-check details in dashboard/reaction paths.
- Increased GitHub API traffic despite batch enrichment being intended to reduce API usage.
- Brittle CI visibility as the number of checks grows.

## Related
- PR #637 — introduced GraphQL batch PR enrichment.
- PR #906 — GitHub API rate limiting / batch enrichment follow-up.
- Issue #1083 — prior GitHub rate-limit concerns in this subsystem.

title: bug(cli): `ao stop` (no args) shows a project picker but ignores the selection — contradicts documented "kill all across all projects" semantics
body:
## Bug

`ao stop` with no arguments shows an interactive "Choose project to stop:" picker. Whatever project the user selects, the actual kill loop still terminates **all active sessions across all projects** and stops the global daemon. The picker is a UX lie: it implies project-scoped behavior that doesn't exist, and the user's selection has no effect on what actually happens.

Per the design docs, `ao stop` with no args is *meant* to be the kill-all path — so the picker shouldn't be there at all.

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding. **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `ecdf0c73`. **Confidence:** High (live reproduction + CLAUDE.md doc + code line).

## Documented intent vs. observed behavior

`CLAUDE.md` (project root) states:
> - `ao stop` (no args): kills ALL sessions across ALL projects, sends SIGTERM to parent ao start process, stops dashboard, unregisters
> - `ao stop <project>`: kills only that project's sessions, does NOT kill parent process or dashboard

Live reproduction (user picked **Eng Hiring**):

    Choose project to stop: Eng Hiring
    Stopping orchestrator for Eng Hiring
    ...
    Stopped 6 session(s)
      Eng Hiring: eh-orchestrator
      agent-orchestrator: ao-180, ao-189, ao-191, ao-orchestrator
      mercury_8c1e44e68c: mer-orchestrator

User picked Eng Hiring. AO stopped sessions across Eng Hiring + agent-orchestrator + mercury (3 projects, 6 sessions). The header line *"Stopping orchestrator for Eng Hiring"* is false — it stopped three orchestrators.

## Code

`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:254`:
```ts
const projectId = await promptSelect(`Choose project to ${action}:`, [...]);
```
The picker is invoked for both `start` and `stop`, but `stop`'s downstream code path globally kills + tears down the daemon regardless of which project was selected.

## Fix direction

**For `ao stop` (no args):** remove the picker entirely. Do what CLAUDE.md says — kill all sessions across all projects, SIGTERM the parent, stop dashboard, unregister. No prompt. If a user wants project-scoped behavior, they pass `ao stop <project>` explicitly.

**Optional polish:** a single global confirmation (*"Stop AO and N active sessions? [y/N]"*) is reasonable; project selection is meaningless for the global-stop path and shouldn't be presented as a choice.

For `ao start`, the picker still makes sense — separate `ao start <project>` daemons per project are legitimate.

## Why this matters

- The picker pretends to limit blast radius and then doesn't — users believe they scoped the operation and get burned.
- Documented behavior (CLAUDE.md) and actual behavior disagree.
- Compounds with #1968 (`ao update`'s gate), #1743 (post-stop restore loss), #1495 (`ao stop <project>` too broad). All three rely on `ao stop` having predictable scope handling, which today it doesn't.

## Related
- #1495 — `ao stop <project>` tears down shared host instead of named project (sibling: with-arg form also too broad)
- #1743 — `ao stop → ao update → ao start` leaves sessions terminated
- #1968 — `ao update` worker-kill gate
- #1759 — Removed project reappears after `ao stop + ao start`

title: bug(cli): `ao update` is not a complete upgrade orchestrator — requires manual `ao stop` prerequisite and propagates raw pnpm errors with no fallback or verification
body:
## Bug

`ao update` is positioned as **the** user-facing upgrade command, but it fails to actually orchestrate the upgrade. It exhibits two related defects, both reproduced live tonight:

### Defect 1 — `ao update` requires the user to run `ao stop` first

If any session is in `working` state, `ao update` refuses to run and prints:

```
✗ 1 session active. Run \`ao stop\` first, then \`ao update\`.
```

A proper upgrade orchestrator should perform the stop itself (the kill+restore lifecycle is intentional and desired — see Philosophy B below), then run the install, then start the daemon and offer restore. Forcing the user to run two separate commands (and remember the exact sequence) is a UX failure for a command literally named `update`.

**Philosophy B** (intended design for the kill+restore lifecycle, per @prateek):
> *"I do like the fact that `ao stop` terminates agent sessions and `ao start` recovers them. It's a nice way to save RAM and CPU while you are not actively working on AO."*

So killing workers on update is *fine* — that's the intentional pause-and-resume model. The bug is making the user perform the choreography manually.

### Defect 2 — `ao update` propagates raw pnpm errors with no diagnostic, fallback, or verification

When `ao update` invokes `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@<tag>` and pnpm errors out (virtual-store layout migration, perms issue, network blip, lockfile corruption, etc.), `ao update`:

- Prints pnpm's raw stack trace,
- Exits with pnpm's exit code,
- **Does not verify** that the install actually happened,
- **Does not tell the user** *"AO was not updated; you are still on version X"*,
- **Does not suggest** any fallback (e.g. `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@<tag>`),
- **Does not log** the failure for later diagnosis.

User then has to: parse pnpm's error themselves; google `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` (or whatever); figure out remediation; rerun. For a single-command upgrade tool, the failure path is the most important UX and it's effectively absent.

## Reproduction (both defects, tonight)

**Defect 1:**

```
$ ao update
Current version: 0.7.0
Latest version:  0.9.0-nightly-c8a0dcbf708a1b55c01c4e1aaa687781b0551345
Channel:         nightly
...
✗ 1 session active. Run \`ao stop\` first, then \`ao update\`.

    • ao-orchestrator  (working)
```

**Defect 2** (after manually running `ao stop`):

```
$ ao update
Current version: 0.7.0
Latest version:  0.9.0-nightly-c8a0dcbf708a1b55c01c4e1aaa687781b0551345
Channel:         nightly
...
Updating: pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@nightly
 ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE  Unexpected virtual store location
...
pnpm exited with code 1.
```

→ User is left on 0.7.0, with no indication that the upgrade silently failed mid-flight, no recovery path, no fallback. The daemon is now stopped (from manual `ao stop`) and `ao update` won't bring it back either. To recover, the user must manually run `ao start`.

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding. **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `ecdf0c73`. **Confidence:** High (live reproduction of both defects within minutes of each other; exact gate at `update.ts:204-218`).

## Why this is generic (affects other users)

- **Defect 1** hits **every** user who runs `ao update` with any active session. Universal.
- **Defect 2** is conditional on pnpm install failure — but pnpm can fail for many reasons: virtual-store layout migration (hits anyone whose pnpm version has crossed certain transitions), corrupted lockfile, perms issue, network blip, registry hiccup, expired token. Even a user with a clean install can hit it on a flaky network. AO providing zero graceful handling means every one of those scenarios becomes a debugging puzzle.

Together, these turn AO's headline upgrade command into a footgun for normal users.

## Fix direction

**For Defect 1:** `ao update` should orchestrate the full lifecycle:
1. Detect active sessions and inform the user (*"5 worker sessions will be stopped, then restored after update"*).
2. Run the equivalent of `ao stop` internally — kills sessions, writes `last-stop.json`, stops daemon/dashboard.
3. Run `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@<tag>` (with **Defect 2** improvements below).
4. Run `ao start` internally — restores sessions from `last-stop.json` (no separate interactive prompt unless `--no-restore` is passed).
5. Report final status: *"Updated 0.7.0 → 0.9.0-nightly-…, 5 sessions restored."*

The `--yes` / `-y` flag pattern (or just doing this by default if there are no scary changes) is what most package managers do.

**For Defect 2:** Wrap the `pnpm add -g` step:
- Capture exit code; if non-zero, **classify** the error (parse stderr for known patterns: `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE`, `EACCES`, `ENETUNREACH`, etc.) and print actionable guidance for each.
- For unrecognized errors, surface the raw pnpm output but **prefix with**: *"AO was not updated. You are still on version 0.7.0. The package manager (pnpm) failed with: [paste]. To retry: `ao update`. To install via npm instead: `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@<tag>`."*
- After install, **verify** the upgrade actually landed by running `ao --version` and comparing — error out clearly if the on-disk version didn't change.
- Optionally: fallback automatically to `npm install -g` on certain pnpm-state-corruption errors.

## Impact

- Headline upgrade UX is broken for anyone who isn't already an AO power-user.
- Failed updates leave the user in a worse state than before they ran the command (daemon stopped, sessions killed, install failed, no path forward).
- Multiplies the cost of every other AO bug that requires a fresh install to verify a fix.

## Related
- **#1968** (this issue's predecessor in this session, framed wrong; superseded by this one). Closing #1968.
- **#1970** (`ao stop` no-args picker scope lies) — sibling lifecycle/UX defect; both share the same code path (`start.ts` / `update.ts`) and should be tackled together.
- **#1743** (`ao stop → ao update → ao start` loses restore state) — same architectural area; would be naturally subsumed if `ao update` orchestrated the round-trip itself with `--restore` honored automatically.
- **#1800** (`ao update` leaves workspace half-built when plugin dist/ is stale) — adjacent: also about update leaving the system in a bad state on failure.
- **#1813** (pnpm install ENOENT on Windows during shim creation) — adjacent install-failure case that Defect 2's graceful-handling proposal would also address.

title: bug(release): nightly snapshot publish can include hard deps on workspace packages that never reach npm — breaks install when any package is skipped
body:
## Bug

`pnpm changeset version --snapshot nightly` resolves `workspace:*` deps to concrete snapshot versions (e.g. `@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos@0.9.0-nightly-<sha>`). If the actual publish of any of those packages then **fails or is skipped** (e.g. native build failure, CI environment lacks the toolchain, manual catch-up publishes), the published consumers (`@aoagents/ao-cli`, `@aoagents/ao`) still carry hard `dependencies` entries pointing at a version that **was never uploaded to npm**.

Result: `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@nightly` (or `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@nightly`) fails with `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404` / *"@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos@<version> is not in the npm registry"* — and there's no installable nightly until somebody publishes the missing package.

**Source:** orchestrator dogfooding (reproduced manual catch-up nightly publishes 2× tonight + 1× yesterday). **Reported by:** @prateek. **Analyzed against:** `37d3a86d`. **Confidence:** High (exact mechanism traced; reproduced 3 times).

## Reproduction (what just happened)

1. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm -r build` in a scratch worktree — `@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos` build fails with *"Local package.json exists, but node_modules missing"*. Other packages build fine.
2. `pnpm changeset version --snapshot nightly` mutates every workspace package's `workspace:*` deps to `^0.9.0-nightly-37d3a86d…` (concrete snapshot version).
3. `pnpm publish -r --filter '!@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos' --tag nightly` publishes 28 packages successfully; notifier-macos skipped.
4. **Published `@aoagents/ao-cli@0.9.0-nightly-37d3a86d` declares hard dep `@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos@0.9.0-nightly-37d3a86d`**, which **does not exist** on the registry (nor does any version of `@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos` — it has *never* been published).
5. User `ao update` → `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@nightly` → 404 on `notifier-macos`. Install dies.

## What the existing guard catches and what it misses

`scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs` asserts every `workspace:*` runtime dep of a publishable package is itself publishable (i.e., not `"private": true`). It catches:
- *"cli depends on web, web has `private: true` → would publish a broken cli."*

It does **not** catch:
- *"cli depends on notifier-macos, notifier-macos is publishable in principle but failed to build / was excluded from this run / is platform-specific and not built in CI."*

The guard runs against config, not against the actual publish manifest. The official `release.yml` happens to work because it builds and publishes all packages together in a clean CI env; any deviation (manual catch-up, native-build failure, partial dispatch) silently produces a broken nightly.

Stable `@aoagents/ao-cli@0.8.0` has **no `notifier-macos` reference at all** in its published `dependencies`, suggesting the official release pipeline either successfully publishes notifier-macos alongside (so the workspace dep is preserved AND reachable), or strips/rewrites it before publish. Either way, manual publishes that don't replicate that path produce broken nightlies.

## Fix directions (one or both)

1. **Strengthen `check-publishable-deps.mjs`** to also verify, post-version-snapshot, that every concrete versioned dep in a publishable package **either is being published in this run, or already exists on npm at the same version**. Run this guard between `pnpm changeset version --snapshot` and `pnpm publish -r` — fail the publish entirely if any dep target is unreachable, with a clear error naming the missing package + expected version.
2. **Document and enforce a "publish-everything-or-publish-nothing" invariant in `canary.yml` / `release.yml`.** Don't allow per-package filtering during publish; if a package fails to build, abort the whole canary cut rather than publishing a partial set. Per #1972's broader theme: an update pipeline that silently degrades is worse than one that loudly stops.
3. **Make `@aoagents/ao-notifier-macos` an `optionalDependency`** of `@aoagents/ao-cli` rather than a hard `dependency`, with an `os: ["darwin"]` constraint. This way npm/pnpm gracefully skip it on non-macOS, and on macOS the 404 still surfaces clearly but the rest of the install path isn't blocked downstream of it. (Doesn't fix this bug fully — it still needs to be published on macOS — but it limits blast radius.)

## Impact

- Generic: any user running `ao update` while the npm `nightly` dist-tag points at a partial publish gets a hard install failure.
- Concretely observed: tonight I manually republished after the canary cron silently broke 9 days ago (#1972's adjacent observation). My republishes have the same defect because they don't run the official release machinery — and now no nightly user can `ao update` to `0.9.0-nightly-c8a0dcbf*` or `0.9.0-nightly-37d3a86d*`.
- AO #1973's graceful-failure path catches this on the install side (clear *"AO was not updated"* + restart prior install) — so users aren't *stranded*, but they also can't *progress* until a publishable nightly exists.

## Related
- #1972 — `ao update` orchestration + graceful failure (downstream consumer of this bug's effect)
- #1956 — `ao update` channel comparison (closed, separate)
- #1931 — repo bloat / accidental artifacts (only adjacent because it mentioned notifier-macos)

title: fix(cli): sanitize project IDs derived from folder names
body:
## Summary

When a repository folder name contains special characters like dots (e.g. `llama.cpp`), the auto-derived project ID fails Zod validation on the next config load, throwing:

```
Error: [
  {
    "validation": "regex",
    "code": "invalid_string",
    "message": "Project ID must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ (no dots, slashes, or special characters)",
    "path": [
      "projects",
      "llama.cpp"
    ]
  }
]
```

## Root Cause

`registerFlatConfig` (start.ts) and `ao project add` (project.ts) derive the project ID from the directory basename without sanitizing special characters. The Zod schema at `packages/core/src/config.ts:372` enforces `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/` on project IDs, causing the validated config to reject entries with dots or other special characters.

## Fix

Sanitize the basename-derived project ID by replacing characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` with hyphens, then stripping leading/trailing hyphens. Falls back to the raw name if sanitization produces an empty string.

This matches the same sanitization pattern already used for `sessionPrefix` on the next line of `registerFlatConfig`.

## Testing

- `ao start` in `~/llama.cpp` → project ID becomes `llama-cpp` instead of `llama.cpp`
- `ao project add ~/my.app.project` → project ID becomes `my-app-project`
- Folder names with only valid characters (`my-project`, `my_project`) are unchanged
