title: Manifest <link> emits without crossorigin, breaking deployments behind credential-gated reverse proxies
body:
## Problem

When `ao-web` is fronted by a reverse proxy that gates the dashboard hostname on a session cookie (Cloudflare Access, oauth2-proxy, Pomerium, Tailscale Funnel + Serve auth, etc.), every page load logs a CORS error in the browser console and the PWA manifest never loads:

```
Access to manifest at 'https://<proxy-sso-origin>/cdn-cgi/access/login/<hostname>?...'
(redirected from 'https://<hostname>/manifest.webmanifest')
from origin 'https://<hostname>' has been blocked by CORS policy:
No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.
```

The rest of the dashboard works (HTML, JS, CSS, same-origin API calls all default to sending credentials), but the manifest fetch never carries the auth cookie, so the proxy 302s it to its SSO login on a different origin, and the browser blocks the cross-origin response with CORS.

## Root cause

`<link rel="manifest">` is one of the few same-origin browser fetches that, by spec, **omits credentials unless explicitly opted in via `crossorigin="use-credentials"`**. The current `app/manifest.ts` Next.js special file auto-emits the link tag with no way to set that attribute.

Next.js's `<link rel="manifest">` emission ([`next/dist/lib/metadata/generate/basic.js`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/lib/metadata/generate/basic.tsx)) sets `crossOrigin` to `'use-credentials'` only when `process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'`:

```js
metadata.manifest ? jsx("link", {
  rel: "manifest",
  href: metadata.manifest.toString(),
  // If it's same origin, and it's a preview deployment,
  // including credentials for manifest request.
  crossOrigin: !manifestOrigin && process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'preview' ? 'use-credentials' : undefined
}) : null,
```

This solves Vercel's own basic-auth-gated preview deployments but offers no equivalent for self-hosted deployments behind credential-gated proxies. The `metadata.manifest` Metadata API accepts only a string URL — there's no options object exposing `crossorigin`.

See [vercel/next.js#65964](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/65964) for the inverse complaint (users who got `crossorigin="use-credentials"` auto-added in Next 14 and couldn't remove it for their public manifests). Together, the two cases are evidence that the Metadata API needs a `crossorigin` knob; the Vercel-preview gate is a one-sided heuristic.

## Use case

Running the AO dashboard on a public hostname fronted by Cloudflare Tunnel + Cloudflare Access. The Access policy gates every request on a session cookie set by Cloudflare's SSO flow. This setup is what makes the dashboard reachable from anywhere (mobile, away-from-machine, multi-device) without exposing the orchestrator process to the public internet. The manifest CORS errors are loud and confusing in the console, and the PWA manifest never loads — so install prompts, theme color metadata, and standalone-display behavior all silently fail.

The same pattern would affect any AO operator running behind oauth2-proxy, Pomerium, Tailscale Funnel with auth, or any similar credential-gated reverse proxy.

## Proposed fix

Emit the `<link rel="manifest">` tag manually in `layout.tsx` with `crossOrigin="use-credentials"`, and serve the manifest JSON via a regular Route Handler instead of the `app/manifest.ts` special file. Next's `Metadata` API doesn't expose `crossorigin` on `metadata.manifest`, so the manual emit is the only way to set it on a self-hosted deployment.

Shape of the change (4 files in `packages/web/`):

- `src/lib/pwa-manifest.ts` — extract the existing manifest-building helper as a pure function.
- `src/app/manifest.webmanifest/route.ts` — regular Route Handler that imports the helper and returns `application/manifest+json`. Same URL, same content.
- `src/app/manifest.ts` — delete (this is the Next special file that auto-emits the link tag without `crossorigin`).
- `src/app/layout.tsx` — emit `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest" crossOrigin="use-credentials" />` explicitly in `<head>`.
- `src/app/manifest.test.ts` — update the import to point at the extracted helper. (3 existing assertions unchanged.)

No change to the manifest content, the URL, or behavior for non-proxied deployments. Same-origin fetches now carry credentials, so any future auth-gated proxy in front of AO works without operator-side path bypasses.

Verified locally (Next.js 15.5.15):
- Server HTML emits exactly one `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest" crossorigin="use-credentials"/>`.
- DOM after hydration: same; `link.crossOrigin === "use-credentials"`.
- Manifest URL: `200 application/manifest+json` (in-browser request carries the cookie, proxy validates, dashboard works end-to-end).
- All existing tests pass.

Happy to send a PR if this direction is acceptable.

## Repro

1. Run AO behind any reverse proxy that gates the dashboard hostname on a session cookie (Cloudflare Access is the easy one — set up Cloudflare Tunnel pointed at the local dashboard, then add an Access policy on the hostname requiring SSO).
2. Sign in via SSO in a fresh browser session.
3. Open the dashboard in Chrome with the console open.
4. Observe: manifest fetch redirects to the SSO origin → CORS error logged on every page load. The dashboard otherwise functions normally.

## References

- [vercel/next.js#65964](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/65964) — inverse case (auto-added crossorigin breaking public manifests).
- [Next.js manifest link emission source](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/lib/metadata/generate/basic.tsx) — the conditional that omits `crossorigin` outside of Vercel preview.
- [MDN: `<link rel="manifest">` and credentials](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/link#attr-crossorigin) — same-origin manifest fetches omit credentials by default.

title: tracker-linear: ambient COMPOSIO_API_KEY breaks Linear tracker when @composio/core isn't installed
body:
## Summary

The Linear tracker (`packages/plugins/tracker-linear`) selects its transport by sniffing environment variables in `create()` (`src/index.ts`):

```ts
const composioKey = process.env["COMPOSIO_API_KEY"];
if (composioKey) {
  return createLinearTracker(createComposioTransport(composioKey, entityId));
}
return createLinearTracker(createDirectTransport());
```

If `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is set, the Composio SDK transport wins **unconditionally** — `LINEAR_API_KEY` is never consulted. But `@composio/core` is an *optional* dependency that is **not installed with the plugin** (the dynamic `import("@composio/core")` is guarded precisely because it's expected to be missing). So the Composio branch hard-fails on the first tracker call with:

```
Composio SDK (@composio/core) is not installed. Install it with: pnpm add @composio/core
```

## Impact

Any user who has `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` exported **for any reason** — which is common, since AO is a Composio project and contributors set it globally for unrelated Composio work — gets a completely broken Linear tracker, **even when they have a valid `LINEAR_API_KEY`** that would work via the zero-dependency direct transport.

There is **no fallback**: once `create()` picks the Composio transport, the import failure throws lazily on the first method call and never falls back to the working direct path.

## Reproduction

1. `export COMPOSIO_API_KEY=<any value>` (no `@composio/core` installed in the tracker)
2. Configure the Linear tracker with a valid `LINEAR_API_KEY`
3. Any tracker call (e.g. `getIssue`) throws `"Composio SDK (@composio/core) is not installed"` instead of using the direct Linear API.

This also surfaces in tests: `packages/plugins/tracker-linear/test/index.test.ts` (which exercises the direct transport) fails wholesale on developer machines that have `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` exported, because its setup never clears the ambient var. CI stays green only because it deliberately omits `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` (see the comment in `.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml`).

## Proposed fix

Fall back to the direct transport on import failure: when the Composio SDK can't be loaded **and** a `LINEAR_API_KEY` is available, transparently use the direct transport instead of throwing. Emit the `tracker.dep_missing` event only when there is genuinely no fallback (no `LINEAR_API_KEY`), so a successful fallback doesn't raise a false error-level event. Also isolate `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` in the direct-transport test suite so it's deterministic regardless of the developer's shell.

title: fix(tracker-linear): fall back to direct transport when @composio/core is missing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2009.

`tracker-linear`'s `create()` picks its transport by sniffing env: if `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is set it routes through the Composio SDK, otherwise the direct `LINEAR_API_KEY` API. But `@composio/core` is an optional dependency that isn't installed with the plugin, so any user with `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` exported (common — AO is a Composio project, so contributors set it globally for unrelated work) hit a hard `"Composio SDK (@composio/core) is not installed"` failure on every tracker call, **even with a valid `LINEAR_API_KEY`**. There was no fallback.

This PR:
- Makes the Composio transport throw a typed `ComposioSdkMissingError` when `@composio/core` can't be loaded.
- Adds `withComposioFallback`: when the SDK is missing **and** a `LINEAR_API_KEY` is present, the tracker transparently falls back to the direct transport instead of failing.
- Emits the `tracker.dep_missing` event only when there is genuinely no fallback (no `LINEAR_API_KEY`), so a successful fallback no longer raises a false error-level event.
- Isolates `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` / `COMPOSIO_ENTITY_ID` in the direct-transport test suite (`test/index.test.ts`) so it's deterministic regardless of the developer's shell. (Previously this suite failed wholesale on machines with `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` exported; CI stayed green only because it deliberately omits the var.)

## Test plan

- [x] New `test/composio-fallback.test.ts`: falls back to direct transport when `@composio/core` is missing but `LINEAR_API_KEY` is set; does **not** emit `dep_missing` on successful fallback; **still throws** when no `LINEAR_API_KEY` is available.

title: Push Claude activity events to the dashboard over WebSocket instead of polling
body:
## Problem

After #1941 / #1945, Claude activity state is written to `{workspace}/.ao/activity.jsonl` by lifecycle hooks the instant a state transition happens (`PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `PreToolUse`, `StopFailure`, …). But the dashboard still finds out by **polling**, so a sub-50ms event takes seconds to surface:

```
hook fires (instant)
  → writes .ao/activity.jsonl
  → [waits up to 35s] sessionManager.listCached() TTL before getActivityState re-reads it
  → [waits up to 3s] mux broadcaster polls /api/sessions/patches
  → WS frame → browser
```

Worst case ~38s, typical 3–10s. The browser leg is already a WebSocket push; the lag is entirely in the two pull legs in the middle (the 35s `listCached` TTL in `session-manager.ts` and the 3s `SessionBroadcaster` poll in `web/server/mux-websocket.ts`).

## Desired model

The "activity detected" moment already exists — it's the hook firing. It should flow straight through:

```
hook fires → POST to daemon → daemon pushes WS frame → browser updates
```

No file-watching, no cache, no polling loop.

## Why it isn't already this way

Historical: activity detection was built as "read files on a timer" before Claude hooks existed. #1945 changed *who writes* the activity JSONL (hooks instead of terminal-regex) but deliberately didn't touch the transport — same patch shape, same wire protocol, same UI code. This issue is the transport follow-up.

## The one unavoidable piece

The hook script runs as a child of Claude, in a different process than the AO server, so it must signal the server across a process boundary. That's a single localhost POST — not a complication, just plumbing.

## Proposed change

1. **Activity-updater script** (`ACTIVITY_UPDATER_SCRIPT` / `ACTIVITY_UPDATER_SCRIPT_NODE` in `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts`): after writing the JSONL line, also `POST {sessionId, state, trigger}` to the daemon. Keep the JSONL write as the durable source of truth (so a daemon restart rebuilds state, and a daemon-down scenario loses nothing). The POST must stay fast and `exit 0` even if the daemon is unreachable.
   - Cross-platform: `curl` on Unix, `Invoke-WebRequest` / Node `fetch` on Windows (the `.cjs` variant can use `fetch` directly). The daemon port is injected at spawn time via an env var.
2. **Daemon**: a tiny internal route (e.g. `POST /api/internal/activity`) that takes `{sessionId, state, trigger}` and calls the existing `SessionBroadcaster.broadcast()` / `push()` immediately — the same broadcaster that already fans out to WS clients.
3. **Browser**: no change. `useSessionEvents` already applies WS session patches.
4. **Cleanup**: once events are pushed, the `SessionBroadcaster`'s 3s self-poll and the dependence on the 35s `listCached` TTL for activity freshness can be removed (or the TTL kept only as a periodic reconciliation safety net).

## Cheap interim win (optional, can land first)

Independent of the full push model: the dominant latency is the 35s `listCached` TTL (`session-manager.ts:529`), not the 3s poll. Letting the broadcaster call `list({ fresh: true })` (or shrinking the TTL) takes worst-case from ~38s to ~3s in one line, with zero architectural risk. Good stopgap if the full WS-push work is deferred.

## Check before building

PR #1905 (ActivityReducer refactor) added a `subscribe()` API to core. If that's merged, an in-daemon emitter that fires on activity change may already exist — in which case step 2 becomes "bridge the reducer's subscription to the WS broadcaster" rather than building a new notify path. Confirm its state first.

## Acceptance

- A Claude permission prompt / turn-end / tool call is reflected on the dashboard in <1s (not 3–38s).
- JSONL remains the durable record; restart still rebuilds activity from disk.
- Hook stays fast and non-blocking; daemon-down does not break Claude or lose the JSONL entry.
- Cross-platform (bash + Node variants; Unix + Windows).

## Context

- Builds on #1941 / #1945 (hook-based activity detection).
- Related: #1934 (active/ready state vocabulary), #1905 (ActivityReducer).

title: RCA: orchestrator spawn workspace conflict on fresh install (#1922)
body:
Root-cause analysis only — no code changes. The reporter sees `AO found an older orchestrator workspace for "<project>_<hash>" but could not safely reuse it automatically` on a completely fresh `ao start`, even though no prior worktree, branch, or session metadata exists.

## Root cause

First-run `autoCreateConfig` produces two divergent project identities for the same repo:

- **Local yaml** (`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:574-592`) is written in the legacy wrapped `projects:` format, keyed by `basename(cwd)` (e.g. `feat-reviewer-agent-flow`).
- **Global registry** (`registerProjectInGlobalConfig` → `generateExternalId`, `packages/core/src/global-config.ts:773-790, 49-54`) rebrands the same project to `<basename>_<sha10>` (e.g. `feat-reviewer-agent-flow_24136efca8`).

`autoCreateConfig` then returns `loadConfig(outputPath)` against the wrapped local yaml. `applyWrappedLocalStorageKeys` (`packages/core/src/config.ts:84-121`) does **not** rename the key, so the CLI's subsequent `ensureOrchestrator` runs with `projectId = '<basename>'` and creates the worktree at `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/<basename>/worktrees/<sessionPrefix>-orchestrator` on branch `orchestrator/<sessionPrefix>-orchestrator`.

The dashboard loads from the canonical global config and only ever sees `<basename>_<sha10>`. The wrapped local yaml also makes the project show up as **degraded** (`loadLocalProjectConfigDetailed` returns `old-format`). "Fix Config" calls `repairWrappedLocalProjectConfig`, which rewrites the yaml flat — but does **not** move the worktree or session metadata.

When the user then clicks "Spawn Orchestrator":

- `findManagedWorkspace` (`packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts:414-451`) builds `allowedPaths` rooted at `…/projects/<basename>_<sha10>/worktrees/…`.
- `git worktree list --porcelain` finds the existing worktree on branch `orchestrator/<sessionPrefix>-orchestrator`, but at the **basename** path.
- That path isn't in `allowedPaths` → throws `"outside AO-managed worktree directories"`.
- `classifySpawnError` (`packages/web/src/app/api/orchestrators/route.ts:15-32`) rewrites the message and interpolates the hashed id, producing the reported text.

The conflict is structural (both ids derive deterministically from the repo path/origin), not a race. `findManagedWorkspace` is behaving correctly — the bug is upstream, in the auto-create flow producing two ids.

## Why the issue's hypotheses were close but not quite right

| Hypothesis | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Repair creates state that the spawn sees as stale | No — repair only edits yaml. The diverged state was created in step 8 by the CLI's own `ensureOrchestrator` during `ao start`. |
| Spawn creates half-state and trips on its own retry | No — the conflicting worktree predates the spawn click. |
| Repair → spawn path creates workspace state mid-flight | Indirect — repair only unblocks the Spawn button, exposing the latent divergence. |

## Suggested fix directions (not implemented; awaiting direction)

1. `autoCreateConfig` writes a **flat** local yaml (matching the post-repair format). Eliminates the degraded state and the basename key from `config.projects`. Smallest surgical fix.
2. `autoCreateConfig` reloads via `loadConfig(getGlobalConfigPath())` after `registerProjectInGlobalConfig` so the rest of `ao start` uses the hashed id.
3. Teach `applyWrappedLocalStorageKeys` to rename the local key to the registered hashed id when the global registry already knows the project.
4. Have `repairWrappedLocalProjectConfig` migrate any worktrees/sessions under the basename project dir to the hashed project dir (only needed to recover already-corrupted installs).

(1) addresses the root cause. (1)+(4) together also recover users already affected.

## Note on delivery

The instructions asked me to post the RCA as a comment on #1922. Both `gh issue comment` and the GitHub REST API returned 403 from this sandbox, and the available MCP tools only expose `reply_to_comment` for PR review threads. The full analysis lives in commit `c3f541e`'s PR body and can be pasted to the issue by a maintainer.

title: perf: remove ?fresh=true from 2s polling loop on session detail pages
body:
## Problem

The session detail page (`sessions/[id]/page.tsx` and `projects/[projectId]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`) fires a `setInterval` every 2 seconds that makes **3 concurrent requests all with `?fresh=true`**:

- `/api/sessions?project=X&fresh=true` (kanban)
- `/api/sessions?fresh=true` (sidebar — unscoped, fetches all sessions across all projects)
- `/api/sessions/patches` (broadcaster)

`?fresh=true` bypasses the 35s in-memory cache (`SESSION_CACHE_TTL_MS`) and calls `sm.list()` which runs live enrichment (tmux probes, JSONL reads, GitHub issue lookups) on every session.

## Measured impact (83 sessions, 8 projects)

| Scenario | Fresh p50 | Fresh p95 |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| 1 user (sequential) | **672ms** | 1249ms |
| 3 concurrent users | 2110ms | 2247ms |
| 5 concurrent users | 4011ms | 4799ms |

The cached path costs **36ms p50** — 18× faster than a single fresh call.

Cache hit rate while on a session detail page: **9%** — the cache is effectively unused because the dominant caller always bypasses it.

## Root cause

`?fresh=true` was intended for the initial page load to get live state immediately. It was left on the polling interval by accident. Every 2s the page discards the cache and re-runs full enrichment for all sessions.

## Fix

Remove `?fresh=true` from the `setInterval` callback in both session detail pages. Keep it only on the **initial fetch** (page mount). Subsequent polls use the cached path.

**Locations:**
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — lines 682, 771–775
- `packages/web/src/app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — lines 284–285, 342–345

The 35s cache TTL is long enough that the lifecycle manager's `invalidateCache()` calls (fired on every state transition) keep data fresh in practice.

title: perf: batch tmux has-session probes in sm.list() — replace N subprocesses with one list-sessions call
body:
## Problem

`sm.list()` calls `runtime.isAlive(handle)` for every session independently. The tmux runtime plugin implements this as one `execFileAsync("tmux", ["has-session", "-t", id])` subprocess per session.

With 83 sessions, every `sm.list()` call spawns **83 concurrent child processes**. This is the root cause of fresh-path latency: fork+exec overhead for 83 processes under OS scheduling pressure drives p50 from 36ms (cached) to 672ms (fresh, 1 user).

**Location:** `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:200`

## Measured impact (83 sessions, 1 user)

| Path | p50 | p95 |
|------|-----|-----|
| Cached (no tmux probes) | 36ms | — |
| Fresh (83 `has-session` subprocesses) | 672ms | 1249ms |

## Fix

Replace 83 individual `tmux has-session` calls with a single `tmux list-sessions -F "#{session_name}"` call in the runtime plugin. Parse the output into a `Set<string>`, then answer `isAlive(handle)` as an O(1) set lookup.

Two approaches:
1. **Bulk probe on the runtime plugin** — add a `listAliveSessions(): Promise<Set<string>>` method to the `Runtime` interface, called once per `sm.list()` cycle. Each session's enrichment does a sync set lookup instead of spawning a subprocess.
2. **Batch within `sm.list()`** — before enrichment, pre-fetch alive session IDs once and pass the set down to each session's enrichment task.

Either way: 83 subprocesses → 1 subprocess → expected fresh p50 drops from ~600ms to ~30–50ms.

title: perf: replace NotificationBroadcaster 1s readFileSync loop with fs.watch
body:
## Problem

`NotificationBroadcaster` in `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts` polls the dashboard notification JSONL file every **1 second** using a synchronous `readFileSync` call, unconditionally, regardless of whether any clients are connected or the file has changed.

```ts
this.intervalId = setInterval(() => {
  const result = this.fetchSnapshot(); // synchronous readFileSync inside
  ...
}, 1000);
```

This is blocking I/O on the Node.js event loop — every second, the event loop stalls while the file is read. Currently p50=2ms and p95=7ms (small file), but this grows linearly with notification history.

## Impact

- Constant event loop pressure even when nothing is happening
- File read cost grows with notification file size (no cap on history length)
- Fires even when zero WS clients are connected (the interval starts on first subscriber but `storePath` is always set)

## Fix

Replace the `setInterval` with `fs.watch(storePath, ...)`. Read the file only when the OS signals a change. On first subscriber, do one initial read to send the snapshot. Subsequent reads triggered by `fs.watch` change events only.

This drops notification overhead from **1 read/second always** to **0 reads/second when nothing changes**.

Edge case to handle: `fs.watch` can fire multiple times for a single write (OS-dependent). Debounce the handler with a short delay (~50ms) before reading.

title: perf: SessionBroadcaster polls /api/sessions/patches every 3s — should be event-driven from lifecycle manager
body:
## Problem

`SessionBroadcaster` (in `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts`) is pub/sub in interface but polling in mechanism. Every 3 seconds it fetches `/api/sessions/patches` → `listCached()` → potentially `sm.list()` if the cache is cold.

```ts
this.intervalId = setInterval(() => {
  void this.fetchSnapshot()  // HTTP GET /api/sessions/patches
    .then((result) => { this.broadcast(result.sessions); });
}, 3000);
```

Under load, `listCached()` is blocked waiting for concurrent `sm.list()` calls to finish — broadcaster p95 jumped from 24ms (idle) to **3682ms** under 5-user load.

Even at 1 user, this is architectural waste: the broadcaster polls the HTTP layer every 3s to detect state that the lifecycle manager already knows about the moment it happens (status transitions, new sessions, kills).

## Current architecture

```
lifecycle-manager (ao-start process)
    → writes to disk
    → Next.js API reads disk via sm.list()
    → SessionBroadcaster polls API every 3s
    → WS clients receive patches
```

## Proposed architecture

```
lifecycle-manager
    → emits session-change events (in-process or via lightweight IPC)
    → SessionBroadcaster subscribes to events
    → WS clients receive patches immediately on state change
```

## Options

1. **In-process event emitter** — if lifecycle manager and web server run in the same process, an `EventEmitter` on the session manager (`onSessionChanged`) would let the broadcaster subscribe directly. Zero polling, zero latency.

2. **File-based signal** — lifecycle manager writes a lightweight "dirty" sentinel file; `fs.watch` on that file triggers a `listCached()` read. Eliminates 3s poll, still crosses process boundary cheaply.

3. **Short-circuit existing polling** — as a tactical improvement, reduce the 3s interval and add backpressure (skip poll if previous one is still in-flight, which already exists via `this.polling`). Low effort but doesn't address root cause.

## Impact

- Eliminates the 3s polling latency on kanban updates (currently users see status changes up to 3s late)
- Removes the broadcaster as a load source on `sm.list()`
- Broadcaster p95 returns to <5ms regardless of concurrent user count

title: ux: enrichment timeout in /api/sessions is silent — client receives incomplete data with HTTP 200
body:
## Problem

`/api/sessions` wraps metadata enrichment in a 3-second timeout:

```ts
const metadataSettled = await settlesWithin(
  enrichSessionsMetadata(workerSessions, dashboardSessions, config, registry),
  METADATA_ENRICH_TIMEOUT_MS, // 3000ms
);
```

If enrichment doesn't complete within 3s, the API returns **HTTP 200** with sessions that are silently missing:
- Agent summaries (`summary` field null)
- Issue titles (`issueTitle` field null)
- Potentially stale activity state

The client has no way to know the data is incomplete. There is no `enrichmentTimedOut` flag, no response header, no indicator in the UI.

## Additional issue: the guard protects the wrong bottleneck

Under concurrent load, `sm.list()` (which runs *before* enrichment) is the actual bottleneck — it took 4s p50 with 5 users. The `settlesWithin(3000)` guard only starts *after* `sm.list()` completes, so `sm.list()` itself has no timeout at all and can hang indefinitely.

## Fix

**Short term:**
1. Add `enrichmentTimedOut: boolean` to the `/api/sessions` response body
2. Surface it in the dashboard — e.g. a small banner "Session data may be incomplete" when true

**Medium term:**
3. Add a timeout on `sm.list()` itself (separate from the enrichment timeout), so the API can return a partial response or a clear error rather than hanging

**Locations:**
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` — add flag to response after `settlesWithin` check
- `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` — add `enrichmentTimedOut?: boolean` to API response type
- Dashboard component — show indicator when flag is set

title: perf: sm.list() has no in-flight deduplication — N concurrent fresh calls run N independent full enrichments
tracking: APM investigation — session list latency and broadcaster performance under load
body:
## Summary

APM instrumentation and load simulation were run against a local AO instance with **83 sessions across 8 projects** to establish performance baselines and find bottlenecks. This issue documents the methodology and findings. Individual fix issues are linked below.

## Test setup

- 83 sessions (8 projects × ~10 sessions each, mix of working/idle/stuck/killed)
- All sessions have live tmux processes where applicable
- Simulated load: session detail page pattern — 2 fresh API calls + 1 patches call every 2s per "user"
- APM dashboard at `/apm` collecting enrichment durations, cache hit/miss rates, broadcaster latency, heap trend

## Key numbers

### Session list latency (`/api/sessions?fresh=true`)

| Users | p50 | p95 | p99 |
|-------|-----|-----|-----|
| 1 (sequential) | 672ms | 1249ms | — |
| 3 concurrent | 2110ms | 2247ms | — |
| 5 concurrent | 4011ms | 4799ms | 4828ms |

### Cached path (`/api/sessions`, no `?fresh`)
p50 = **36ms** — 18× faster than 1-user fresh

### Cache hit rate while on session detail page: **9%**

### Broadcaster (`/api/sessions/patches`)
- Idle: p50=24ms
- 5 users: p95=**3682ms** (starved behind concurrent fresh calls)

### Heap
- Peak under load: ~1.5 GB
- Trend: +111 MB over 20 samples during 5-user simulation (GC pressure, not confirmed leak)

## Root cause chain

```
session detail page
  → setInterval(2000) fires
  → fetches /api/sessions?fresh=true   ← bypasses 35s cache
  → sm.list() runs
  → 83× "tmux has-session" subprocesses launched concurrently
  → OS scheduling pressure: 672ms p50 per call (1 user)
  → broadcaster's listCached() queues behind these calls
  → kanban updates lag 3s+ under any concurrent load
```

## What's cached and what isn't

`sessionCache` is a single in-memory `{ sessions: Session[], expiresAt: number }` object with a 35s TTL. It is **written only by `listCached()`** and **never by `list()`**. Because the session detail page always calls the `?fresh=true` path (which calls `list()` directly), the cache is never populated from the heaviest consumer — leaving it cold for the broadcaster and `useSessionEvents`.

## Individual fix issues

| Issue | Priority | Effort |
|-------|----------|--------|
| #2017 — remove `?fresh=true` from 2s polling loop | critical | small — 2 lines |
| #2018 — batch tmux probes: N subprocesses → 1 `list-sessions` call | high | medium |
| #2019 — replace NotificationBroadcaster 1s readFileSync with fs.watch | high | small |
| #2020 — SessionBroadcaster: polling → event-driven from lifecycle manager | high | large |
| #2021 — enrichment timeout is silent: add flag to response + UI indicator | medium | small |
| #2022 — sm.list() in-flight deduplication for concurrent callers | medium | medium |

## Recommended fix order

1. **#2017** — immediate, no risk, 18× improvement for 1 user
2. **#2018** — cuts remaining fresh-path cost from ~600ms to ~50ms
3. **#2019** — low-risk event-loop improvement, independent of above
4. **#2021** — small UX safety net
5. **#2020** — architectural, do after #2017+#2018 reduce urgency
6. **#2022** — only relevant if multi-user scenarios become a priority

title: refactor(core): restructure packages/core/src into domain modules (phased, surface-preserving)
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src` is a flat directory of 60 files with several god-files that are hard to maintain, navigate, and bug-hunt:

- `session-manager.ts` — 3636 lines
- `lifecycle-manager.ts` — 3044 lines
- `types.ts` — 2094 lines (one mega-file imported by nearly every module)
- `global-config.ts` — 1337 lines

There are no domain boundaries, so related logic is scattered and a single concern can't be reasoned about in isolation. This hurts reliability and makes bugs harder to localize.

## Goal

Restructure `core/src` into domain-scoped modules (continuing the pattern `recovery/` already establishes), splitting the god-files along real responsibility seams. Each unit should have one clear purpose and be understandable/testable on its own.

## Hard constraints (every PR must satisfy)

- **No change to the public surface.** `index.ts` and all 13 subpath exports (`./types`, `./session-manager`, `./lifecycle-manager`, `./config`, `./utils`, `./metadata`, `./observability`, `./paths`, `./plugin-registry`, `./activity-log`, `./orchestrator-prompt`, `./scm-webhook-utils`, `./migration`) keep identical export names/signatures. **No other package's imports change.**
- Entrypoint files stay at their paths and become **barrels** re-exporting from new internal modules.
- **Pure moves + barrels — no behavior change.** Splitting a factory = extracting functions verbatim.
- `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` green at the end of every PR.
- Tests migrate alongside the code they cover (internal-only).

## Target layout

```
core/src/
  index.ts            barrel (unchanged)
  types.ts            barrel → types/
  types/              session, runtime, agent, workspace, tracker, scm, notifier,
                      terminal, events, reactions, config, plugin, metadata,
                      services, errors, portfolio   (split along existing banners)
  lifecycle-manager.ts  barrel → lifecycle/
  lifecycle/          manager (+ split parts), state, transition, status-decisions,
                      events, agent-report, report-watcher
  session-manager.ts    barrel → session/
  session/            manager (+ split parts), naming, display, metadata-mapping
  config.ts           barrel → config/
  config/             loader, global, generator, project-resolver
  activity/  notifications/  observability/  paths/  portfolio/  code-review/
```

## Phased PRs

- [ ] **PR 1 — `types.ts` → `types/`**: split along the 17 existing section banners; `types.ts` becomes `export *`. Pure type moves. (First, so later PRs don't fight it.)
- [ ] **PR 2 — `lifecycle/`**: move state/transition/status-decisions/agent-report/report-watcher in; extract `lifecycle-manager`'s pure helpers (event mapping, observability builders, duration); slim the factory behind the barrel.
- [ ] **PR 3 — `session/`**: extract `session-manager`'s helpers (naming, display, metadata-mapping) + split the factory's regions; barrel preserved.
- [ ] **PR 4 — `config/`**: global-config + config + config-generator + project-resolver.
- [ ] **PR 5 — leaf groupings**: activity/, notifications/, observability/, paths/, portfolio/, code-review/ (split into 5a/5b if large).

## Inspiration

Both Claude Code (domain folders: `tools/`, `services/`, each self-contained) and Codex (decomposed crates + nested module dirs) converge on: decompose by domain, co-locate types with the code that owns them, keep a small shared contract surface. This issue applies that internally to `core/src` without touching the external contract.

title: bug(core): indeterminate agent process-probe vetoes authoritative runtime-dead — sessions stuck forever in 'detecting/runtime_lost'
body:
## Bug

Worker sessions whose tmux runtime is genuinely gone get stuck **permanently** on the dashboard sidebar in `state: detecting / reason: runtime_lost` ("Detecting runtime truth (runtime lost)") and never reach a terminal state. The lifecycle probe pipeline lets an **indeterminate** agent process-probe veto the runtime's **authoritative** "dead" signal, then writes nothing — freezing the session in limbo.

This is the **inverse failure mode** of #1838: that issue fixed `ps`-timeout being conflated with "process not found" (which bulk-*terminated* live sessions) by making `isProcessRunning` return `INDETERMINATE` on any probe failure. That fix overcorrected — a definitively-dead tmux session (`tmux list-panes` exits non-zero → throws → caught → `INDETERMINATE`) is now indistinguishable from a transient probe failure, so confirmed-dead runtimes **never terminate**.

**Source:** AO dogfooding — codex smoke-test workers (`ao-180`, `ao-183`) observed stuck on sidebar
**Reported by:** @hrishic7
**Analyzed against:** `5d0b624f` (origin/main HEAD)
**Confidence:** High — traced end-to-end against live on-disk session metadata
**Affects:** all agents (codex AND claude-code share the pattern), tmux runtime

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a codex (or claude) worker in a tmux runtime.
2. Let the tmux session die WITHOUT a manual kill and WITHOUT a PR (e.g. `ao stop` killed the pane, smoke test ended, tmux server reaped).
3. Observe the sidebar: session sits at "Detecting runtime truth (runtime lost)", Runtime: missing, PR: none — and never leaves.

A session that is **manually killed** (e.g. `ao-180`) does leave, because the kill path writes `terminated/manually_killed` directly, bypassing the probe pipeline. That difference is the tell.

### Live evidence

`~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator_1a434010b7/sessions/ao-183.json` (STUCK):
```
session.state = "detecting"   session.reason = "runtime_lost"
runtime.state = "missing"     runtime.reason = "tmux_missing"
terminatedAt  = null
lifecycleEvidence = "idle_beyond_threshold activity_signal=valid via_native activity=idle at=2026-05-22T11:11:38.624Z"  # STALE/frozen
```

`.../sessions/ao-180.json` (LEFT — only because manually killed):
```
session.state = "terminated"  session.reason = "manually_killed"
runtime.state = "missing"     runtime.reason = "manual_kill_requested"
terminatedAt  = "2026-05-22T11:29:18.624Z"
```

The `idle_beyond_threshold ... activity=idle` evidence is **frozen from the last poll while tmux was still alive** (its `at=` exactly matches the last entry in the codex rollout JSONL). It is preserved verbatim by `skipMetadataWrite: true`, NOT recomputed — the runtime is dead, the idle string is a fossil.

## Root Cause

When the tmux session is gone, the two probes disagree by design:

- **Runtime probe is authoritative-dead.** `runtime-tmux` `isAlive` uses `tmux has-session`, catches failure, returns clean `false` → `runtimeProbe.state = "dead"`, `runtime.state = "missing"/"tmux_missing"`.
  `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:200-207`, `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:948-958`
- **Agent probe is indeterminate.** `agent-codex` `isProcessRunning` runs `tmux list-panes -t <id>`; with the session gone this **throws** ("can't find session"), caught by the broad `catch` → returns `PROCESS_PROBE_INDETERMINATE`.
  `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:782-834` (catch at `:831`)
  Identical pattern in claude-code: `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/activity-detection.ts:208-270` (catch at `:267`).
- **`getActivityState` returns `null`** (not `idle`) because it correctly checks process-liveness first and bails on INDETERMINATE.
  `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:666-677`

The pipeline then short-circuits on the indeterminate agent probe **before** `resolveProbeDecision` (which has the authoritative `runtimeProbe.state === "dead"` in hand) can declare terminal:

`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:1179-1200`
```ts
if (processProbe.indeterminate) {
  return {
    status: session.status,                          // stays whatever it was (stuck/detecting)
    evidence: session.metadata["lifecycleEvidence"], // STALE, preserved
    detectingAttempts: currentDetectingAttempts,
    skipMetadataWrite: true,                          // writes NOTHING
  };
}
const probeDecision = resolveProbeDecision({ runtimeProbe, processProbe, ... }); // never reached
```

Two compounding defects:

1. **Indeterminate agent probe outranks authoritative runtime-dead.** `runtime.isAlive` definitively reports the tmux session gone, but the indeterminate agent probe vetoes it.
2. **`detecting` never self-drains for this path.** The escalation budget (`DETECTING_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` / time limit in `createDetectingDecision`, `packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:146-157`) is never even incremented, because `:1179` returns with `skipMetadataWrite: true` before `createDetectingDecision` runs. And even when it *does* fire, it escalates `detecting → stuck` — another **non-terminal** state — so a confirmed-dead runtime never reaches `terminated`.

`sm.list()` writing `detecting/runtime_lost` is correct and intentional (#1735) — a hot read path must not unilaterally terminate sessions + nuke worktrees on a transient probe. The bug is that the pipeline that is supposed to *drain* `detecting` can't, when the agent probe is indeterminate but the runtime is authoritatively dead.

### Why the sidebar keeps showing it
`deriveLegacyStatus` maps `runtime_lost → killed` (terminal) **only when `session.state === "terminated"`** (`packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts:447-449`); `detecting` maps to non-terminal `detecting` (`:459-460`). Stuck at `detecting`, the session is never categorized terminal, so it never leaves the active sidebar. Summary string: `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts:87-88`.

## Fix

Core-first, smallest correct change:

1. **Don't let indeterminate veto authoritative-dead.** At `lifecycle-manager.ts:1179`, when `processProbe.indeterminate` BUT `runtimeProbe.state === "dead"` (and `!runtimeProbe.failed`), do not short-circuit — fall through to `resolveProbeDecision` so the dead runtime drives a terminal decision.
2. **Confirmed-dead runtime should escalate to `terminated/runtime_lost`, not park in `stuck`.** Audit the `detecting`/`createDetectingDecision` escalation so a runtime that is authoritatively dead resolves terminal.

Optional defense-in-depth (avoids reopening #1838): in the agent `isProcessRunning` impls, distinguish `tmux list-panes` exiting with "can't find session" (→ return `false`/dead) from genuine transient failures (→ `INDETERMINATE`), instead of one broad `catch`.

## Impact

- Codex/claude worker sessions accumulate as permanent "Detecting runtime truth (runtime lost)" cards that can only be cleared by manual kill.
- Clutters the sidebar and (per #1991) keeps these zombie records on the expensive enrichment path.
- Stuck-detection / cleanup downstream of terminal state never fire for these sessions.

## Related

- #1838 (CLOSED) — the inverse fix that introduced `INDETERMINATE`; this issue is its overcorrection.
- #1991 — enrichment cost for terminated/runtime-lost sessions (same zombie records).
- #1967 / #1966 — stuck-vs-terminated and revival of stuck sessions (adjacent lifecycle gaps).

title: refactor(core): split types.ts into co-located types/ domain modules (#2024 PR 1)
body:
Part of #2024 — PR 1 of the phased `packages/core/src` restructure.

## What

Decompose the 2094-line `types.ts` god-file into 16 co-located domain modules under `types/`, organized along the file's existing section banners. `types.ts` becomes a documented barrel that re-exports all of them.

```
types.ts            barrel (full architecture-map header) → types/
types/              session, runtime, agent, workspace, tracker, scm, notifier,
                    terminal, events, reactions, config, plugin, metadata,
                    services, errors, portfolio
```

## Surface-preserving by design

This is a **pure relocation** — no API or behavior change:

- `index.ts` is untouched (still `export * from "./types.js"`).
- The `@aoagents/ao-core/types` subpath export still resolves.
- All **136 exported names** are identical before/after (verified by diff).
- The moved declarations are **byte-for-byte identical** to the originals (verified by reconstructing the old file from the 16 modules).

## Build fix (the one non-mechanical change)

`rollup.config.ts` now derives its `input` from `package.json` `exports` instead of two hardcoded entries.

**Why:** the build uses `preserveModules`, which tree-shakes a pure re-export barrel (no runtime side effects) — `index.ts`'s `export *` flattens straight to the underlying modules, so `dist/types.js` was never emitted. `tsc` still emits `dist/types.d.ts`, so typecheck passes while bundler/runtime resolution of the subpath export fails (caught by a Next.js/webpack build, not by tsc). Making every published entrypoint an explicit input prevents this — entry points are never tree-shaken. This also pre-empts the same break for the `lifecycle-manager` / `session-manager` / `config` barrels in later PRs.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` (full graph incl. web/Next.js) — green
- `pnpm typecheck` (all packages) — green
- `pnpm test` (core) — 1323/1323 pass
- ESLint — clean
- All 14 subpath-export `dist/*.js` targets present on disk

## Commits

1. `refactor(core)`: split types.ts → types/ modules + barrel
2. `docs(core)`: expand the barrel header into a full architecture map
3. `fix(core)`: emit a dist chunk for every subpath export entrypoint

title: fix(core): terminate runtime-lost sessions when agent process probe is indeterminate (#2025)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2025. Codex/claude worker sessions whose tmux runtime vanished got stuck **permanently** on the dashboard sidebar in `detecting / runtime_lost` ("Detecting runtime truth (runtime lost)") and never reached a terminal state.

Root cause: when a tmux session is gone, `runtime.isAlive` returns a clean `false` (authoritative dead), but the agent's tmux-based `isProcessRunning` (`tmux list-panes`) **throws** → mapped to `PROCESS_PROBE_INDETERMINATE`. The lifecycle poll short-circuited on the indeterminate probe at `lifecycle-manager.ts` with `skipMetadataWrite: true`, **never reaching `resolveProbeDecision`** — so the session froze in `detecting` forever (which `deriveLegacyStatus` maps to non-terminal `detecting`, keeping the card on the sidebar). The displayed `activity=idle` evidence was a stale fossil preserved by the skip.

## Fix

A process living inside a dead tmux session cannot be alive. When the runtime probe authoritatively reports dead, reclassify the indeterminate agent process probe as `dead`, so the poll falls through to `resolveProbeDecision` → `dead + dead` → `terminated / runtime_lost`.

- **No agent-plugin changes** — single core change in the lifecycle poll.
- **#1838 protection preserved**: this only fires on an *authoritative dead runtime* (`runtimeProbe.state === "dead" && !failed`), never on a flaky/alive one. A transient `ps`/`tmux` timeout still yields `runtimeProbe.failed` (state `unknown`) → indeterminate still short-circuits, no false termination.
- **Recent-liveness guard intact**: a dead runtime with fresh agent activity still routes to `detecting` via the existing `signal_disagreement` branch, so a genuinely-working agent whose runtime probe glitched is not killed.
- `resolveProbeDecision`'s general `dead + unknown → detecting` grace (e.g. no agent plugin to probe) is untouched.

Affects all agents — codex and claude-code share the same tmux-probe pattern.

## User-facing change

When a worker's terminal ends because its tmux session is gone (e.g. the smoke test finished, `ao stop` killed the pane, the tmux server was reaped, laptop sleep/wake) — and the session was not manually killed and has no PR:

**Before**
- The session stayed on the sidebar **forever** showing "Detecting runtime truth (runtime lost)", `Runtime: missing`, `PR: none`, and a stale `activity=idle` line.
- It never moved to a terminal/ended state on its own. The only way to clear it was to **manually kill** it. Zombie cards piled up over time (one per dead worker).

**Now**
- The session promptly resolves to a terminal **ended** state (`terminated / runtime_lost`, shown as `killed`), the same as any other finished session.
- It leaves the active list, moves to the ended/terminated grouping, and becomes eligible for normal cleanup — **no manual kill required**.
- No change for sessions you manually kill, sessions with a live runtime, or sessions whose agent is still genuinely active (a fresh activity signal still holds them in `detecting`, never falsely terminated).

## Test plan

- [x] `resolveProbeDecision` unit tests: dead+dead → terminated; dead+unknown (no agent) → detecting grace; dead+unknown+recent-liveness → detecting (#1838); transient probe failure → detecting (#1838); alive+unknown → null.
- [x] Lifecycle-manager poll regression: runtime dead + agent probe `indeterminate` + null activity → `killed` (`runtime_dead process_dead`), metadata written (not skipped).
- [x] Existing "leaves lifecycle metadata untouched when process probe is indeterminate" (runtime *alive*) still passes — #1838 guard.
- [x] Full core suite: 1329 tests pass. Full monorepo build + typecheck green. Lint clean.

title: Orchestrator prompt missing ao session restore command and recovery workflow
body:
## Summary

The orchestrator agent's system prompt is missing `ao session restore` from its command vocabulary. When a worker session dies with in-progress work, the orchestrator incorrectly advises that recovery is impossible and suggests killing and respawning — losing conversation context unnecessarily.

Additionally, the orchestrator doesn't re-query session state before making claims about whether a session is alive or dead, leading to stale observations after out-of-band restores.

**Note:** The root cause of _why_ the session died (pty-host `beforeExit` self-termination) is tracked separately in #2032.

## Part A — Knowledge Gap

The orchestrator prompt template does not mention `ao session restore`.

- **File:** `packages/core/src/prompts/orchestrator.md` (271 lines)
- Grep for `restore|resume|recover` returns **zero hits**
- The "Available Commands" section (lines 67–84) lists `session ls`, `session attach`, `session kill`, `session cleanup`, `session claim-pr` — but **not** `session restore`
- The "Handling Stuck Agents" workflow (line 223) says: *"Or kill and respawn with fresh context if needed"* — no mention of restore as an option
- Meanwhile, `ao session restore` is a fully implemented CLI command (`packages/cli/src/commands/session.ts` line 507) with a complete restore pipeline in `session-manager.ts` (lines 3271–3618) that recreates worktrees, re-attaches system prompt files, and relaunches agents

### What to Add

1. Add `ao session restore <session>` to the "Available Commands" section (after `session cleanup`)
2. Add a "Session Recovery" section (after "Handling Stuck Agents") covering:
   - `ao session restore <session>` restores a dead session in-place — same worktree, same branch, same uncommitted changes
   - The system prompt file is preserved and re-attached on restore
   - The agent gets a fresh LLM conversation but full code context + session metadata
   - Preferred over kill+respawn when there's meaningful in-progress work (open PRs, uncommitted changes)
   - Always run `ao status` to re-check current state before concluding a session is dead

### Prompt Assembly Chain (for context)

The orchestrator prompt is built in three steps:
1. **Template:** `packages/core/src/prompts/orchestrator.md` — 271-line Markdown template with `{{placeholder}}` variables
2. **Renderer:** `packages/core/src/orchestrator-prompt.ts` — `generateOrchestratorPrompt()` renders the template with project config
3. **Delivery:** Written to disk as `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/{projectId}/orchestrator-prompt-{sessionId}.md`, then delivered to the agent plugin via `systemPromptFile`

The fix goes in step 1.

## Part B — Observability Gap

The orchestrator agent doesn't detect manual/out-of-band session restores. After the user restored a dead session (via the dashboard), the orchestrator's next investigation still reported it as dead because it worked from stale cached observations rather than re-querying `ao status` for current lifecycle state.

The orchestrator should always run `ao status` to get fresh state before making claims about whether a session is alive or dead.

### Environment

- **AO version:** 0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935
- **Windows 11** Enterprise Evaluation 10.0.26200
- **Node.js:** v24.14.1
- **npm:** 11.11.0
- **pnpm:** 9.15.4

title: feat(agent-opencode): hooks-based activity detection
body:
## Summary

Replaces OpenCode's fragile terminal-regex activity inference with authoritative platform events, mirroring the hook-driven model already shipped for Claude Code (#1941) and Codex. Partially addresses #19 (richer activity detection).

OpenCode exposes a plugin/event system (`.opencode/plugins/`, auto-loaded at startup) that streams 25+ lifecycle events. Critically, `permission.asked` is the **only** authoritative source of `waiting_input` OpenCode offers — terminal regex was guessing before.

### What changed
- **`setupWorkspaceHooks`** installs an auto-loaded activity plugin into the workspace's `.opencode/plugins/ao-activity.js` and excludes it from git via a worktree-aware `info/exclude` entry, so it never lands in the agent's PRs (best-effort).
- **The plugin** maps events → states and appends to `.ao/activity.jsonl` with `source: "hook"`:
  - `permission.asked` → `waiting_input`
  - `session.error` → `blocked`
  - `session.idle` → `ready` (never `idle` — AO age-decay derives idle)
  - `tool.execute.*` / `file.edited` / `message.updated` → `active` (coalesced to bound JSONL growth)
  - No-ops without `AO_SESSION_ID`; honors `AO_OPENCODE_HOOK_ACTIVITY=0` opt-out.
- **`getActivityState`** now prefers fresh hook entries over the polled `opencode session list` API for every state; the session-list API remains the fallback when no hook entry exists.
- **`recordActivity` removed** — the plugin is the sole JSONL writer, so terminal-derived writes can no longer shadow authoritative hook events (mirrors Claude #1941). The terminal `detectActivity` classifier stays as the lifecycle's last resort.

### Design decisions (confirmed with maintainer)
- Plugin installed project-local in `.opencode/plugins/` + gitignored (vs. global install or `opencode.json` edit) — auto-loaded, zero config-file edits.
- Hooks win over the polled API for **all** states, not just the actionable ones.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-opencode test` — 106/106 pass
- [x] New integration test executes the **real** generated plugin against synthetic events (mapping, env guards, dedup)
- [x] New unit tests: plugin install + git-exclude (idempotent, best-effort), hook-priority in `getActivityState`, `recordActivity` removal
- [x] `pnpm build` + `pnpm typecheck` green across all packages; `pnpm lint` 0 errors
- [ ] Manual: run an OpenCode session and confirm dashboard reflects `waiting_input` on a permission prompt

> Note: pre-existing local `tracker-linear` test failures are an unrelated missing optional dep (`@composio/core`), not touched by this PR.

title: bug(runtime-process): pty-host self-terminates on empty event loop via beforeExit handler
body:
## Summary

The Windows pty-host process (`packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/pty-host.ts`) self-terminates after ~30–60 minutes of idle activity due to a `beforeExit` handler that fires when Node.js's event loop empties. This causes `runtime_lost` on worker sessions that are otherwise healthy, resulting in silent session death with no error state recorded.

This is not caused by Windows power management, sleep, or external process termination. The pty-host kills itself.

## Root Cause

**Line 384 of `pty-host.ts`:**
```typescript
process.on("beforeExit", () => shutdown("beforeExit"));
```

The pty-host is a long-lived daemon (analogous to tmux's server process) that owns a ConPTY session and exposes it over a Windows named pipe. It's designed to persist after the agent exits (lines 226–233):

```typescript
// Keep the PTY host alive after the agent exits — mirrors tmux behavior
// where the shell session persists after the command finishes. This keeps
// the named pipe reachable so:
//   - isAlive() returns true (pipe connectable)
//   - Clients can still connect and view scrollback output
//   - The STATUS_RES reports alive:false so getActivityState sees "exited"
//   - ao session kill / ao stop will destroy the pipe server via MSG_KILL_REQ
```

But the `beforeExit` handler undermines this. When:
1. The Claude Code agent goes idle (no tool calls, waiting for input)
2. All named pipe clients disconnect (dashboard tab not actively streaming, lifecycle poller between cycles)
3. No pending async I/O remains in the event loop

...Node.js fires `beforeExit`, and line 384 calls `shutdown()`, which kills the PTY and exits the process. The session is then detected as `runtime_lost` by the lifecycle manager.

The `detached: true` spawn option doesn't help — `beforeExit` is a self-initiated exit, not an external kill. The process decides on its own that it has nothing left to do.

## Reproduction

Consistent on Windows with `runtime-process`. Observed pattern:
- Sessions die 30–60 minutes after the agent goes idle
- Timing is non-deterministic (depends on GC, pipe client reconnect cadence, async drain)
- No error state recorded in the activity log — last entry is `active`, then silence
- The pty-host PID simply disappears

## Proposed Fix

Two-part fix in `pty-host.ts`:

**1. Remove or guard the `beforeExit` handler (line 384):**
```typescript
// BEFORE — kills pty-host when idle:
process.on("beforeExit", () => shutdown("beforeExit"));

// AFTER — a pty-host is a daemon, it should never self-exit:
// Remove line 384 entirely.
```

**2. Add a keepalive timer to hold the event loop open:**
```typescript
// After server.listen(), add:
const keepalive = setInterval(() => {}, 60_000);
// Do NOT call .unref() — this timer must keep the process alive
```

This is the same pattern tmux uses — a periodic timer tick keeps the daemon alive even when all sessions are idle. The pty-host should only exit from explicit `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, `SIGBREAK`, `MSG_KILL_REQ`, or `uncaughtException` — never from an empty event loop.

## Incident Data

This was discovered during investigation of session ao-184 dying on Windows. Full session metadata and activity logs are attached to #2029 (comment: https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/2029#issuecomment-4521102995).

### Timeline (2026-05-22, all UTC)

| Time (UTC) | Event | Source |
|------|-------|--------|
| 13:52:36 | ao-184 created | ao-184.json `createdAt` |
| 13:52:49 | ao-184 acknowledged, started working | ao-184.json lifecycle |
| 13:52:40–14:16:47 | ao-184 active — 743 activity entries, continuous hook firing | ao-184 activity.jsonl |
| 13:56:06 | Orchestrator finishes spawning ao-184, becomes ready | orchestrator activity.jsonl line 533 |
| 13:57:16 | Orchestrator transitions to ready | orchestrator activity.jsonl line 536 |
| **13:58:16** | **Orchestrator enters `waiting_input` (idle_prompt notification)** | orchestrator activity.jsonl line 538 |
| **13:58:16–16:27:08** | **Orchestrator silent — 2h28m gap** | orchestrator activity.jsonl lines 538→539 |
| **14:16:47** | **ao-184 last activity entry — then silence** | ao-184 activity.jsonl line 743 |
| **14:16:47–16:51:00** | **ao-184 gap — 2h34m** | ao-184 activity.jsonl lines 743→744 |
| 16:27:08 | Orchestrator resumes (ready state) | orchestrator activity.jsonl line 539 |
| 16:50:57 | ao-184 restored by user | ao-184.json `restoredAt` |
| 16:51:00 | ao-184 activity resumes (ready state) | ao-184 activity.jsonl line 744 |

The orchestrator's pty-host (PID 5232) survived the same period — likely because the orchestrator had an active `waiting_input` notification keeping async work in its event loop, preventing `beforeExit` from firing.

### Environment

- **AO version:** 0.9.0-nightly-a66a087ef678313bf3a78dfe70aadee9adc25935
- **Windows 11** Enterprise Evaluation 10.0.26200
- **Node.js:** v24.14.1
- **npm:** 11.11.0
- **pnpm:** 9.15.4
- **AO runtime:** `runtime-process` (Windows pty-host)
- **Power settings:** never sleep/hibernate, display off after 15min (confirmed not the cause)

### Why Windows Power Settings Are Not the Cause

- Machine configured to never sleep/hibernate
- Connected Standby (S0 Low Power Idle) not supported by firmware
- Power plan: Ultra Performance, processor min state 100% on AC
- Display timeout is 15 minutes but only affects the display, not processes
- No Windows Automatic Maintenance tasks correlate with the timing

title: feat: add agent memory persistence in ticket (Symposium pattern)
body:
***

## Description

This PR implements the **Symposium pattern** for Agent Orchestrator by persisting "Agent Memory" into issue tickets. When an agent fails, gets stuck, or is killed, its context (what it tried, where it failed, and its proposed next steps) is preserved so subsequent attempts can pick up where it left off, and users can inspect the failure history directly from the dashboard.

### Changes Made
- **Core Lifecycle**: Implemented `flushAgentMemory` in `lifecycle-manager.ts`. When a session transitions to `stuck`, `errored`, or `killed`, the manager extracts the agent's summary, tail output digest, and parsed "Next Steps/Errors" and persists it.
- **Tracker Persistence**: The memory is flushed directly to the tracker (e.g., as a hidden HTML comment on GitHub issues) via `tracker.writeMemory`.
- **Dashboard Integration**: Appends the agent's attempt history into `session.metadata["agentMemoryLog"]` to allow zero-API-call rendering in the UI.
- **Web UI**: Created the `<AgentMemoryPanel />` component in the frontend and integrated it into the ended-session view in `<SessionDetail />`.
- **Testing**: Added unit test coverage for `readMemory` and `writeMemory` in the `tracker-github` plugin to ensure `gh` CLI comments are correctly parsed and appended.

### Testing
- [x] Verified `gh` CLI mocking correctly simulates memory read/write cycles.
- [x] Tested unit tests via `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-github test` (All passed).
- [x] Ran `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint`, ensuring everything complies with code conventions (including `.js` extensions and strict types). 

### How it looks
*When a session fails, the dashboard now renders the `AgentMemoryPanel` with a historical timeline of all attempts made on that issue, displaying their duration, outcome, and proposed next steps.*

title: fix(agent-grok): avoid package manifest require in web bundle
body:
## Summary
- remove agent-grok's top-level `createRequire(import.meta.url)("../package.json")` metadata read
- keep the Grok manifest metadata inline so Next.js server chunks cannot rewrite the lookup to a publish-host path
- add regression coverage that prevents reintroducing a runtime `../package.json` import in the agent-grok module
- add a changeset for `@aoagents/ao-web` and `@aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-grok`

Fixes ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator#2004.

## Root cause
`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts` statically imports the Grok plugin so the dashboard can register built-ins. During the published Next.js build, webpack bundled `packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js` and rewrote `createRequire(import.meta.url)` to the build-host URL (`file:///tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js`). At runtime on a user machine, that bundled code tried to resolve `../package.json` from `/tmp/ao-publish-stable/...`, which does not exist, producing the observed `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after `ao start` completed.

## Verification
- `node --input-type=module` targeted reproduction of `createRequire("file:///tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js")("../package.json")` produced the reported `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`

title: fix: align first-run project identity
body:
## Summary

Fixes the first-run project identity split that caused the CLI and dashboard to disagree about the same repo's project ID.

On first `ao start`, the CLI previously wrote a wrapped local config with a basename project key while also registering the repo in the global registry with the hashed project ID. The CLI then loaded the wrapped local config and created sessions/worktrees under the basename ID, while the dashboard loaded the global registry and used the hashed ID. That mismatch caused later dashboard repair/spawn flows to see existing worktrees as belonging to a different AO-managed project namespace.

## Changes

- Generate a flat local `agent-orchestrator.yaml` on first run instead of a wrapped top-level `projects:` config.
- Keep project identity in the global registry by continuing to call `registerProjectInGlobalConfig()`.
- Reload the generated flat local config via `loadConfig(outputPath)`, so the local config resolves through the global registry and uses the same hashed project ID as the dashboard.
- If global registration fails after the flat local config is written, remove the just-created local config before rethrowing. This avoids leaving behind an unresolved flat local config.
- Do not rewrite global operational defaults such as `port`, `defaults.notifiers`, `notifiers`, or `notificationRouting` in this bug fix. That broader preservation/migration policy is intentionally left for a follow-up PR.

## Tests

- Updated the focused `autoCreateConfig` unit coverage to verify:
  - first-run writes a flat local config without `projects:`
  - the generated local config resolves to the global project identity
  - existing global notifier defaults are not overwritten
  - local config is removed if global registration fails
- Added an integration test that runs the real CLI first-run path in a temp git repo and verifies:
  - local config is flat
  - global config has one hashed project ID
  - `loadConfig(localConfigPath)` and `loadConfig(globalConfigPath)` resolve the same project ID and path

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- start.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-integration-tests test -- src/cli-first-run-config.integration.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-integration-tests typecheck`

## Follow-up

There is a related compatibility question around whether first-run, degraded repair, and full migration should preserve top-level operational fields consistently (`port`, `defaults.notifiers`, `notifiers`, `notificationRouting`, etc.). The current fix intentionally matches the degraded repair behavior and keeps this PR scoped to the project identity regression.

title: fix(agent-grok): load manifest metadata via JSON import
body:
## Summary
- Replace agent-grok's top-level `createRequire(import.meta.url)("../package.json")` manifest metadata read with `import packageJson from "../package.json" with { type: "json" }`.
- Add the smallest package-scoped TypeScript config needed for that syntax by moving only agent-grok to `module`/`moduleResolution: "NodeNext"`.
- Add regression coverage for source and emitted runtime modules so package metadata cannot regress to `createRequire`, `require("../package.json")`, or `readFileSync(new URL("../package.json", import.meta.url))`, and any `../package.json` import must use a JSON import attribute.
- Align the affected product runtime package engines/docs to Node `>=20.18.3`, where JSON modules with import attributes are non-experimental.

Refs ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator#2004.
Supersedes the generated-manifest direction from ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator#2035.

## Root cause
`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts` statically imports the Grok plugin to register built-ins. The old Grok module read package metadata at module import time using `createRequire(import.meta.url)("../package.json")`. During the published Next.js web build, webpack inlined that module and rewrote `import.meta.url` to the publish host path (for example `/tmp/ao-publish-stable/packages/plugins/agent-grok/dist/index.js`). On a user machine, the bundled code then tried to resolve `../package.json` from that stale build-host path and failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, causing packaged `ao-web` startup to 500.

## Config changes
- `packages/plugins/agent-grok/tsconfig.json`: package-scoped `NodeNext` module settings so TypeScript accepts and preserves JSON import attributes.
- `package.json`, `packages/ao/package.json`, `packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/web/package.json`, `packages/plugins/agent-grok/package.json`: Node `>=20.18.3` for the affected AO runtime path.
- `README.md`, `packages/ao/README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`: prerequisite text updated to match the engine floor.
- `.changeset/clean-groks-smile.md`: patch release note for AO runtime packages and agent-grok.

## Verification

title: fix(core): auto-terminate sessions when agent exits but runtime stays alive (closes #1933, #1966)
body:
## Summary

When an agent process exits but its tmux runtime stays alive (the keep-alive shell pattern), `resolveProbeDecision` treated `runtime=alive` + `process=dead` as a **signal disagreement**, ran the detecting cycle, and escalated the session to `stuck`/`probe_failure`. Every subsequent poll hit the same branch, so the session stayed `stuck` **forever** — lingering on the dashboard sidebar with an orange dot that no toggle could clear. Closes #1933 and #1966 (same root cause, different trigger).

## Root cause

`packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts` — the `runtimeProbe.state === "alive" && processProbe.state === "dead"` arm of `resolveProbeDecision` routed into `createDetectingDecision`. But when the agent's native activity signal definitively reports `exited` (and the process probe agrees), the runtime being alive is irrelevant — the agent is the source of truth. There was no path promoting `stuck` → `terminated` once all signals agreed the agent was gone.

## Fix

Add a branch at the top of `resolveProbeDecision`: when `activitySignal.state === "valid"` + `activity === "exited"` **and** `processProbe.state === "dead"`, terminate directly with reason `agent_process_exited` (mapped to legacy status `killed` in `deriveLegacyStatus`). The `processProbe=dead` requirement keeps spawning sessions safe — their process probe stays `unknown` until the agent starts (#1035), so they are never killed prematurely.

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-status-decisions.ts` — new terminate-on-exit branch
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts` — map `agent_process_exited` → `killed`

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests for `resolveProbeDecision`: terminates on `activity=exited`, doesn't enter signal_disagreement, still treats `runtime=alive`/`process=dead` as disagreement when the agent has *not* exited
- [x] New `deriveLegacyStatus` test: `terminated` + `agent_process_exited` → `killed`
- [x] Updated the mislabeled existing test ("detects killed state when getActivityState returns exited" was asserting `detecting`) to expect `killed`
- [x] Verified spawning sessions are unaffected (#1035 regression test still green)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1326 passed
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck`, `pnpm lint` (0 errors), full `pnpm build`

title: fix(api): orchestrators route calls spawnOrchestrator instead of ensureOrchestrator on repeat clicks
body:
## Bug

`POST /api/orchestrators` calls `sessionManager.spawnOrchestrator()` when `clean` is not `true`. `spawnOrchestrator` hard-fails with:

```
Orchestrator session "ao-orchestrator" already exists. Use ensureOrchestrator() to reuse or restore it.
```

…if the orchestrator session already exists. This causes every repeat click of the "Start Orchestrator" button in the dashboard to fail after the first successful spawn.

## Reproduction

1. Start AO and open a project in the dashboard.
2. Click "Start Orchestrator" — succeeds, session created.
3. Click "Start Orchestrator" again (e.g. after a page refresh) — fails with 500, terminal never opens.

Activity events confirm the pattern:
```
session.spawned          ✓ first spawn succeeds
session.spawn_failed     ✗ "already exists. Use ensureOrchestrator()"
session.spawn_failed     ✗ same (rapid retry)
session.spawn_failed     ✗ same
```

## Root Cause

`packages/web/src/app/api/orchestrators/route.ts` line 65:

```ts
// current (broken)
: await sessionManager.spawnOrchestrator({ projectId, systemPrompt });

// fix
: await sessionManager.ensureOrchestrator({ projectId, systemPrompt });
```

`ensureOrchestrator` is idempotent — it returns the existing session if one is alive, and creates a new one only when none exists. `spawnOrchestrator` always tries to create fresh and throws if the session already exists.

## Fix

One-line change in `packages/web/src/app/api/orchestrators/route.ts`:

```diff
- : await sessionManager.spawnOrchestrator({ projectId, systemPrompt });
+ : await sessionManager.ensureOrchestrator({ projectId, systemPrompt });
```

The `clean === true` path correctly uses `relaunchOrchestrator` (kill + recreate) and is unaffected.
