title: Spec: Feature releases (per-PR shareable prerelease builds, in-app opt-in install, gated like stable)
body:
## Summary

A **feature release** is a shareable, installable build of a **single unmerged PR**, cut manually so that PR can be dogfooded/demoed in isolation without pulling in the rest of nightly. Input is a PR number; the build comes from the **PR head**, published as a **GitHub prerelease**, gated behind the **same protected `release` environment** stable uses.

It is exposed in-app as a **third update channel** alongside Stable and Nightly. Selecting **Feature Releases** reveals a second dropdown of currently-live feature builds (the "Active Feature Releases" feed); picking one **pins that PR** and the app tracks the PR's newest build like a channel. Your prior Stable/Nightly choice is preserved as **home**: when the pinned PR is merged/closed/deleted, the app clears the pin and falls back to whichever base channel you were on. Feature builds **must never** write `latest*.yml`/`nightly*.yml`.

> **Design note (revised 2026-07-05):** feature releases are now a persistent, subscribable channel (was "one-off install, never persist"). Reconciled with the hard rule "stable/nightly config stays untouched" by keeping the persisted `channel` (`latest`/`nightly`) as *home* and adding a **separate** `feature` pin, so picking a feature build never overwrites your home channel. This reverses the earlier "not subscribable / not auto-updating" non-goals (see §8).
>
> **Maintainer decisions folded in (2026-07-05):** reuse the `release` environment (OQ1); **7-day per-build expiry** that resets on rebuild; **max 5 concurrent** feature builds (fail-fast at cut); **one live build per PR** (rebuild deletes the prior). OQ2 (env-scoping signing secrets) remains the only open item.

Every claim about current behavior carries a `file:line`.

---

## 1. How the current system works (grounding)

**Stable release** (`.github/workflows/frontend-release.yml`)
- Triggers: push tag `desktop-v*` or bare `workflow_dispatch` (no inputs) — `frontend-release.yml:31-35`.
- **Environment gating (the control to reuse):** `environment: release` on the matrix `release` job (`frontend-release.yml:48`) and `release-intel` (`:176`). Intent, verbatim: *"Gates the signed release behind the `release` environment's required reviewers: any write-access user can push a desktop-v\* tag, but only designated approvers can let the build that consumes the signing secrets proceed."* (`:44-47`). `permissions: contents: write` (`:49-50`).
- **Signing/notarization:** composite `./.github/actions/macos-signing-setup` imports the Developer ID `.p12` + stages notary creds (`:68-77`); forge consumes them — `osxSign` on `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `osxNotarize` on `APPLE_API_KEY`/`_ID`/`_ISSUER` (`forge.config.ts:42-55`). Secrets: `CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_API_KEY_BASE64`, `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`. **Cost:** real sign + Apple notarization per mac leg, in a 3x notary-flake retry (`:83-89`).
- **Matrix:** `macos-latest` (arm64), `windows-latest`, `ubuntu-latest` (`:42`) + a dedicated `macos-15-intel` leg for darwin-x64 (`:175`). Artifacts: mac `.zip`, NSIS `.exe`, Linux `.AppImage`/`.deb`/`.rpm`.
- **Publish + manifests:** forge publishes `v<package.json version>`, `prerelease: AO_RELEASE_PRERELEASE === "true"`, `draft: false` (`forge.config.ts:130-142`); repo from `AO_RELEASE_REPO` (`:92`). `publish-feed` then runs `node scripts/feed.mjs dist "${tag#v}" latest` (`:265`) -> `latest*.yml` + blockmaps; not env-gated (`:239-242`).

**Nightly** (`frontend-nightly.yml`) — the isolation template
- Cron + `workflow_dispatch` (`:8-11`); **no `environment:` gate** (unattended). Isolation via `AO_RELEASE_PRERELEASE: "true"` (`:102`) + `feed.mjs ... nightly` (`:211`) -> `nightly*.yml`, never `latest*.yml`. Version `X.Y.(Z+1)-nightly.<ts>+<sha>` (`scripts/nightly-version.mjs`), stamped in-memory (`:71-76`).

**The manifest choke point** — `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs:29-32`: `feedFilename(channel, platform)` returns `${channel}${suffix}.yml`. The `channel` CLI arg is the *only* thing deciding whether a build writes `latest*.yml`, `nightly*.yml`, or anything else. A feature build passes a per-PR channel and is **structurally incapable** of touching stable/nightly manifests.

**Updater** (`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`, `update-settings.ts`)
- `electron-updater` `^6.8.9` (`package.json:72`, `auto-updater.ts:1`); feed provider baked into `app-update.yml` at build (`forge.config.ts:58-76`: `provider: github`, `owner: AgentWrapper`, `repo: agent-orchestrator`).
- Persistent channel in `~/.ao/update-settings.json` — `{ enabled, channel: "latest"|"nightly", nightlyAck }` (`update-settings.ts:4-10,25-27`). `configureFeed(channel)` sets `autoUpdater.channel`, `allowPrerelease = channel==="nightly"`, `allowDowngrade = true` (`auto-updater.ts:18-26`).
- IPC: `updates:check|download|install|getStatus`, push `updates:status`, `updateSettings:get|set`, `app:getVersion` (`preload.ts:78-94`, `bridge.ts:99-109`, `main.ts:800,838-841`). Install = `quitAndInstall(false,true)` (`:121-124`).

**electron-updater channel resolution (VERIFIED against the installed `electron-updater@6.8.9`):** when `allowPrerelease` is true, `GitHubProvider.getLatestVersion()` iterates the releases atom feed and selects the newest release whose **tag's semver prerelease identifier equals the current channel** (`node_modules/electron-updater/out/providers/GitHubProvider.js:60-89`):
```js
const hrefChannel = (semver.prerelease(hrefTag)?.[0]) || null;
const shouldFetchVersion = !currentChannel || ["alpha","beta"].includes(currentChannel);
const isCustomChannel  = hrefChannel !== null && !["alpha","beta"].includes(String(hrefChannel));
if (shouldFetchVersion && !isCustomChannel && !channelMismatch) { tag = hrefTag; break; } // stable/alpha/beta
const isNextPreRelease = hrefChannel && hrefChannel === currentChannel;
if (isNextPreRelease) { tag = hrefTag; break; }                                            // custom channel (pr<N>)
```
The per-platform channel filename comes from `getCustomChannelName(channel)` appending `-mac`/`-linux`/`""` (`Provider.js:44-45`, `util.js:30`), so channel `pr<N>` reads `pr<N>-mac.yml`/`pr<N>-linux.yml`/`pr<N>.yml` — exactly what `feed.mjs` emits. Stable (`allowPrerelease=false`) uses `/releases/latest` (`GitHubProvider.js:158-163`), i.e. GitHub's latest **non-prerelease**. Confirmed on 6.8.9: `semver.valid("v0.2.0-pr2270.202507061200")` is truthy with prerelease id `pr2270`. Three load-bearing consequences:
- **A feature channel is native:** `autoUpdater.channel = "pr<N>"` resolves the newest release whose tag prerelease id is `pr<N>` = the newest build of PR N. This is the subscription behavior, for free, from the existing baked provider.
- **No nightly hijack:** a feature build's prerelease id is `pr<N>`, not `nightly`, so nightly's resolution skips it. Feature releases live safely in the main repo.
- **No stable contamination:** feature builds are prereleases, excluded from GitHub's "latest release" that stable resolves.

**UI** — `_shell.settings.tsx:4-5` -> `GlobalSettingsForm`, dropping `<Card>` sections into a `max-w-2xl flex-col gap-4` column (`GlobalSettingsForm.tsx:9-19`); new section = new `*Section.tsx` returning a `<Card>`. `UpdatesSection.tsx` already models a channel `Select`, "Current version `v{app.getVersion()}`", action buttons, and an inline `UpdateStatusLine`. Primitives in `components/ui/`: `card`, `button` (`primary`/`outline`), `badge` (`neutral`/`accent`/`success`/`warning`/`error`), `select`, `table`, `skeleton`, `tooltip`. DESIGN.md banner: *"clone agent-orchestrator verbatim (SUPERSEDES emdash · 2026-06-10)"* (`DESIGN.md:8-14`); accent `#4d8dff` live-edge only; 8px cards, `h-8` controls, `text-[12px]` labels, `font-mono text-[11px]` versions, lucide icons only. Data via `aoBridge` IPC + `useQuery`/`useMutation` (`bridge.ts:3`), browser-preview fallbacks.

---

## 2. CI: the `feature-release` workflow

New `.github/workflows/feature-release.yml`, a near-clone of nightly's build/publish body with PR-head checkout and a per-PR channel.

**2.1 Trigger — `workflow_dispatch` only** (manual; never a push side effect). Inputs: `pr` (required), `slug` (optional, display-only), `platforms` (csv, default `mac,win,linux`), `allow_fork` (default false).
- **Quota guard (max 5 concurrent, decided 2026-07-05):** the run's first step queries the active feature-release feed (§3) and **fails fast** if ≥5 are already live: *"5 feature releases active — retire one first."* Runs before the environment approval so an approver is not asked to gate a build that will be rejected. Keeps the dropdown at ≤5.

**2.2 Checkout PR head** — `gh pr view <pr> --json headRefOid,state,title,isCrossRepository`; fail if `state != OPEN`; `checkout` the exact `headRefOid` SHA (the approver-vetted commit). **Fork PRs fail** unless `allow_fork=true` is consciously set (building untrusted code with signing secrets is the top risk, §8).

**2.3 Version / identity** — new `frontend/scripts/feature-version.mjs`: `<base>-pr<N>.<UTCts>+<sha>`, e.g. `0.2.0-pr2270.202507051200+a1b2c3d`. `base` = PR-head `package.json.version`. Stamped in-memory like nightly (`frontend-nightly.yml:71-76`); build metadata stripped for the tag (`:207`).
- **HARD CONSTRAINT:** the semver prerelease identifier `[0]` MUST equal the channel name `pr<N>`, because electron-updater keys channel resolution off `semver.prerelease(tag)[0]` (§1). So the version is `<base>-pr<N>.<ts>` and the git/release tag is `v<base>-pr<N>.<ts>`. **The `slug` must NOT be in the version/tag** — `semver.prerelease("0.2.0-pr2270-fixfoo")[0]` is `"pr2270-fixfoo"` and would break matching. Slug is display-only (release name + marker). This corrects the originally-sketched `v<base>-pr<N>-<slug>` tag.

**2.4 Build + signing** — same matrix + intel leg as stable, filtered by `platforms`. Reuse `./.github/actions/macos-signing-setup` verbatim — macOS must be signed + notarized or it won't install/update (`frontend-release.yml:15-17`). Reuse the 3x notary retry.

**2.5 Publish (prerelease) + labeling** — publish step env `AO_RELEASE_PRERELEASE: "true"` (`forge.config.ts:141`) + `AO_RELEASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}`. Repo = **`AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`** (safe: §1 shows nightly is not hijacked, and the shipped app's baked provider already trusts it). GitHub Releases have no native labels, so encode discoverability: release **name** `[feature] PR #<N>: <title>` and a machine marker in the body:
```
<!-- ao-feature-build: pr=<N> base=<base> sha=<sha> slug=<slug> -->
```
- **One live build per PR (decided 2026-07-05):** before publishing, delete any existing `v*-pr<N>.*` prerelease + tag for the same PR, then publish the new build from the new SHA. This resets the 7-day expiry timer (§7), keeps the quota counting unique PRs (not total builds), and prevents stale-build accumulation. The approver re-vets the new head SHA (each dispatch is a fresh approval, §2.7).

**2.6 Isolated feed (critical)** — `node scripts/feed.mjs dist "$version" "pr$PR"` -> `pr<N>.yml`/`pr<N>-mac.yml`/`pr<N>-linux.yml` (+ `.blockmap`). Per `feed.mjs:29-32` this **cannot** emit `latest*.yml`/`nightly*.yml`. These filenames are exactly what electron-updater expects for `channel = "pr<N>"`, so the native channel resolution (§1) reads them directly. Add a guard step asserting channel `^pr[0-9]+$` and no `latest*`/`nightly*` in the upload set — a mechanical block against the #2270 / `latest-mac.yml` 404 poisoning class.

**2.7 Environment gating (identical restriction to stable) — DECIDED: reuse `release`.** Every job that checks out PR code or touches signing secrets: `environment: release` (`frontend-release.yml:48,176`) + `permissions: { contents: write }`. **Enforcement:** GitHub pauses any environment-referencing job until a **required reviewer** approves that specific run (Settings > Environments > release). `workflow_dispatch` is open to write-access users, but the signing job cannot proceed without approval — the same human gate as stable, and **the approver must review the PR head SHA before approving** because the build runs unmerged code with signing-secret access (§8). Every dispatch is a fresh approval (intentional: 8k+ stars, growing attack surface, unmerged-code + signing-secret access). Note: nightly reads the same secrets **without** an environment (`frontend-nightly.yml:77-86`), so today they are **repo-level** secrets and the environment provides the *approval* gate, not secret isolation; env-scoping the signing secrets stays open as optional hardening (OQ2, §8).

**2.8 Cleanup (retirement, CI side)** — `feature-release-cleanup.yml`, two triggers, `contents: write` only, no environment (destructive-only, no secrets):
- `on: pull_request: closed` -> `gh release delete --cleanup-tag` the `v<base>-pr<N>.*` prerelease(s)/tag(s) for the closed/merged PR (immediate).
- `on: schedule` **daily cron** -> sweep every `pr<N>` prerelease whose `published_at` is older than **7 days** and delete it (per-build expiry, decided 2026-07-05; timer resets on rebuild per §2.5).

---

## 3. The "Active Feature Releases" feed + how the app queries it

The app maintains a live catalog, polled from the main process:
- **Query:** `GET /repos/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/releases?per_page=100`, filter `prerelease === true && body has the ao-feature-build marker`. Parse `pr/base/sha/slug` from the marker, `title` from the release name, `published_at` for freshness.
- **Group by PR:** collapse multiple builds of the same PR to the newest (highest version). Each entry = one live PR with its newest build id.
- **Liveness:** drop entries whose PR is `merged`/`closed` (`GET /pulls/<N>`, batched), whose release was deleted, or whose `published_at` is older than **7 days** (expiry window, §2.8 / §7). Client-side filtering hides expired builds before the daily sweep catches up. This is the authoritative retirement detector (the CI cleanup in §2.8 is belt-and-suspenders).
- This query hits the **releases index only** — zero interaction with `latest*.yml`/`nightly*.yml`. Nightly prereleases are excluded (no marker). The result populates the second dropdown (§5) and drives the subscription/fall-home poll (§4, §7).

---

## 4. Update resolution: three channels, one home

**Persisted settings** gain a separate pin (`update-settings.ts`), so home is never overwritten:
```ts
interface UpdateSettings {
  enabled: boolean;
  channel: "latest" | "nightly";        // HOME — the fallback; never set to a feature value
  feature: { pr: number } | null;        // active pin; when set, updates resolve from the pr<N> channel
  nightlyAck: boolean;
}
```

**`configureFeed` extension** (`auto-updater.ts:18-26`): if `feature` is set -> `autoUpdater.channel = "pr" + feature.pr`, `allowPrerelease = true`, `allowDowngrade = true`. Else -> existing latest/nightly logic. Nothing else changes: the baked GitHub provider resolves the newest `pr<N>` build natively (§1). No `setFeedURL`, no generic provider.

- **Pin a PR** (`updateSettings:set` with `feature: { pr }`): write settings, `configureFeed`, then check -> download -> install. `channel` (home) is preserved untouched, satisfying the hard rule.
- **Subscription (auto-track newest build of PR N):** the existing `enabled` auto-update path (`startAutoUpdates`, `auto-updater.ts:66-80`) already checks the configured channel on a schedule; with `channel = pr<N>` it naturally installs newer `pr<N>` builds as they ship. The §3 poll refreshes the dropdown/badge; no extra install logic needed beyond what nightly already uses.
- **Per-platform:** mac `.zip` (arch via `MacUpdater.filterFilesForArch`), Windows `.exe`, Linux `.AppImage` — the same set the manifest lists (`feed.mjs:15-23`); no special-casing.
- **Downgrade edges:** pinning a `0.2.0-pr2270.*` build from stable `0.2.0` is a downgrade; falling home from a future-base feature build is a downgrade. `allowDowngrade = true` (`auto-updater.ts:25`) covers both.
- **Return home (manual):** set `feature = null`; `configureFeed(channel)` resolves the preserved Stable/Nightly channel; check -> download -> install. After reinstall `app.getVersion()` drops `-pr<N>`.

---

## 5. Settings UI

Extend `UpdatesSection.tsx` (or a sibling `FeatureBuildsSection.tsx` in the same Card column). Model the user's two-dropdown flow, DESIGN.md-compliant:
- **Primary channel `Select`:** `Stable (latest release)` / `Nightly (pre-release)` / `Feature Releases`. Choosing Stable or Nightly sets `channel` and clears `feature`. Choosing Feature Releases reveals:
- **Secondary `Select` (only when Feature Releases active):** options from the §3 feed, each label `PR #N — <title>` with a build-id subline (`font-mono text-[11px]`, `v<base>-pr<N>.<ts>`) and a freshness `Badge` (`warning` if stale). Empty state: "No live feature releases." Selecting one sets `feature = { pr }` and triggers install (confirm dialog, since it quits + relaunches).
- **Active-build banner:** when `app.getVersion()` matches `-pr(\d+)`, show `<Badge variant="accent">PR #N</Badge>` + "You're on PR #N's build" + a **Return to <home>** `Button variant="outline"` (label reflects the preserved `channel`: "Return to Stable" / "Return to Nightly").
- **Data:** `useQuery(["feature-builds"], () => aoBridge.featureBuilds.list())`; channel/pin writes via `updateSettings:set`; live progress via `aoBridge.updates.onStatus` (`UpdatesSection.tsx:124-131`). Accent blue stays live-edge only.

---

## 6. Versioning / identity and getting home
- Binary version `<base>-pr<N>.<ts>+<sha>`; `app.getVersion()` returns `<base>-pr<N>.<ts>`, so the UI always detects the active PR and the primary dropdown reflects "Feature Releases".
- Provenance: release name `[feature] PR #<N>: <title>` + body marker; the `pr<N>` prerelease id doubles as the channel key.
- Home is always known: `channel` (`latest`/`nightly`) is preserved through any feature pinning, so "Return to <home>" and automatic fall-home go to wherever the user actually was.

---

## 7. Retirement / lifecycle
- **Triggers:** PR merged/closed, its release deleted, **or the build's 7-day expiry** (decided 2026-07-05; timer resets when the PR is rebuilt, §2.5).
- **Detection:** the §3 poll (PR state + release presence + 7-day window) is authoritative; the CI cleanup (`feature-release-cleanup.yml`, §2.8) removes the artifacts so the entry also vanishes from the feed. electron-updater's `channelFileNotFoundError`/`update-not-available` on the dead `pr<N>` channel is a secondary signal.
- **Fall-home:** clear `feature`; `channel` (the preserved Stable **or** Nightly) resolves on the next check; with `enabled` on, the user is moved home and a toast fires ("PR #N retired — returned you to <home>"). With `enabled` off, clear the pin + show the return banner without forcing a reinstall. **A build expiring while installed never force-quits** — the user falls home on the next check. Merged code is already in nightly, so nothing is lost.

| Scenario | Behavior |
|---|---|
| PR updated, new build cut | Prior build deleted first, new build from new SHA, 7-day timer resets, approver re-vets (§2.5) |
| PR updated, no new build cut | Prior build persists on its original timer; expires at 7 days |
| PR closed/merged | Immediate cleanup (§2.8 `pull_request: closed`) |
| Build expires while installed | Falls home on next check; no force-quit |
| ≥5 builds already live | New cut fails fast at dispatch (§2.1) |

---

## 8. Risks, non-goals, open questions

**Risks**
- **Supply-chain (highest):** builds *unmerged* PR code with signing-secret access. Mitigation: the `release` environment's **required-reviewer approval is the enforcing control** — the approver inspects the PR head SHA before approving; fork PRs refused unless explicitly opted in (§2.2, §2.7). Optional: env-scope the signing secrets.
- **Manifest poisoning (#2270 class):** structurally prevented — feature builds only call feed.mjs with `pr<N>` and the app reads only `pr<N>*.yml` when pinned; `latest*.yml`/`nightly*.yml` are never written or read (§2.6, §4). Backed by a channel-assertion guard + unit test.
- **Nightly hijack by feature prereleases:** ruled out — electron-updater matches by prerelease id (`pr<N>` != `nightly`), **verified against the installed `electron-updater@6.8.9`** (`GitHubProvider.js:60-89`; nightly resolution skips `pr<N>` releases, stable resolves only non-prereleases via `/releases/latest`). This is why the version/tag scheme (§2.3) is a hard constraint. Task 7 keeps a regression test to catch a future electron-updater bump changing this.
- **macOS sign cost/latency:** full sign + notarize per mac leg; `platforms` input skips unneeded legs. Manual + rare, acceptable.
- **Approval friction:** each build needs a reviewer click — the intended gate.

**Non-goals (explicit)**
- Not built from merged PRs — retired on merge; nightly covers them.
- Never writes or reads stable/nightly manifests.
- One pin at a time — a single active feature channel; `app.getVersion()` is the source of truth.
- Not open to arbitrary users to *cut* (env-gated). Anyone may *pin/install* from the feed — that is the point.
- (Reversed from the prior draft, per maintainer decision: feature releases **are** a subscribable channel and **do** auto-update within a pinned PR.)

**Decided (2026-07-05, maintainers)**
- OQ1 — environment: **reuse `release`** (same required-reviewer approval as stable; no new env). Every dispatch = a fresh approval.
- OQ3 — expiry + quota: **7-day per-build expiry** (resets on rebuild), **max 5 concurrent** feature builds (fail-fast at cut), **one live build per PR** (rebuild deletes prior).

**Open questions**
1. OQ2 — env-scope the signing secrets (optional hardening) now or later? (Only remaining open item.)

---

## 9. Phased task breakdown (each sized for one worker)

**Phase 0 — decision (no code).** Confirm environment choice + reviewers. Blocks Task 1.

**Task 1 — `feature-release.yml` workflow.** Dispatch inputs (`pr`,`slug`,`platforms`,`allow_fork`), quota fail-fast (≥5 active), PR-head-SHA checkout with open-state + fork guards, delete-prior-`pr<N>`-build step, `feature-version.mjs` stamp, signed matrix + intel leg, prerelease publish with marker + `[feature] PR #N` name, per-PR `feed.mjs` + channel-assertion guard. *Deps: Phase 0, Task 6.*

**Task 2 — `feature-release-cleanup.yml`.** `pull_request: closed` -> delete release + tag; **daily cron** -> delete `pr<N>` prereleases older than 7 days. *Deps: Task 1.*

**Task 3 — main-process feature engine.** Settings schema `{ channel, feature, ... }` migration; `featureBuilds.list` (GitHub API + marker + PR-state + 7-day filter, grouped-by-PR-newest); `configureFeed` `pr<N>` branch; pin/return handlers reusing `auto-updater.ts` download/status/install; §7 fall-home + retirement poll. *Deps: Task 1 contract (parallelizable).*

**Task 4 — IPC + bridge.** `featureBuilds:list`, extend `updateSettings:get|set` for `feature`, preload types + `bridge.ts` fallback stubs. *Deps: Task 3.*

**Task 5 — Settings UI.** Three-option primary `Select` + conditional secondary `Select` from the feed, active-build banner with "Return to <home>", confirm dialog, wired via `useQuery`/`updateSettings:set`/`onStatus`. *Deps: Task 4.*

**Task 6 — `feature-version.mjs` + parse helper.** Pure `computeFeatureVersion` (asserts prerelease id == `pr<N>`) + `parseFeatureBuild(version)`, unit-tested. Feeds Tasks 1 and 5. *No deps.*

**Task 7 — tests.** feed.mjs channel-isolation assertion; version compute/parse; list filter (excludes nightly + closed PRs + expired, groups newest); **electron-updater prerelease-id channel-matching regression test** (nightly not hijacked by a `pr<N>` prerelease — the behavior is confirmed on 6.8.9 per §1; the test guards against a future bump). *Spans Tasks 1/3/6.*

**Task 8 — docs.** Feature-release runbook (cut, approve, pin, retire) in `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`. *Deps: Task 1.*

Critical path: Phase 0 -> Task 6 -> Task 1 -> Task 2; and Task 1 -> Task 3 -> Task 4 -> Task 5; Task 7 then Task 8.

title: Unify resource lifecycles onto one generic ref-counted lease primitive (ResourceMap/LifecycleMap)
body:
## Problem

AO re-implements the same resource-lifecycle logic in every subsystem, slightly differently each time. The recurring shape is:

> Provision a thing exactly once even under concurrent callers; hand out references; tear it down when the last reference goes away; don't leak it if teardown errors.

That pattern is hand-rolled in at least four places today, each with its own mutexes and edge cases:

- `adapters/workspace/gitworktree` — create/restore/destroy a checkout (provision-once + refuse-teardown-when-dirty).
- `terminal/manager.go` + `attachment.go` — N WebSocket attachments multiplexed onto **one** PTY. This is literally ref-counting: provision the PTY once, fan out, decide last-detach behavior.
- `service/session`, `service/project` — provision a session/project once under concurrent requests (single-flight).
- The new **PTY host** from #2335 — provision-once, adopt, teardown-on-last-attachment, the trickiest semantics in the codebase.

Each is an independent chance for a **provisioning race** (two callers both create), a **leak** (teardown error swallowed, worktree/PTY/host orphaned), or a **double-free** (last-reference logic off by one). Same bug surface, solved four-plus times.

## Why now

#2335 (durable sessions) adds a fifth lifecycle — the detached PTY host — and it's the one where wrong ref-counting means either a leaked detached process or a PTY torn down while an attachment still needs it. The lifecycle spine and durable sessions are the same fight: the ref-counted map of live hosts is exactly what the adopt/handoff snapshot iterates over. Building the primitive makes #2335 cleaner, not just the rest of the codebase.

## Proposed solution

Two generic primitives (Go generics), and every subsystem becomes an *instance* of them instead of a bespoke implementation.

```go
// ref-counted, single-flight provisioning, teardown-on-last-release
type ResourceMap[K comparable, V any] struct { ... }
func (m *ResourceMap[K, V]) Acquire(
    ctx context.Context, key K, provision func(context.Context) (V, error),
) (v V, release func(), err error)

// async-resource state machine with DISTINCT provision-error vs teardown-error types
type LifecycleMap[T any, ProvErr, TearErr error] struct { ... }
```

Migration targets:

- `terminal/manager.go` -> `ResourceMap[SessionID, *ptyHost]`; attachment count **is** the refcount; last release runs the (idle-grace) teardown.
- `gitworktree`, `service/session`, `service/project` -> `Acquire`/`release` instead of bespoke create/destroy bookkeeping.

Provisioning races, teardown ordering, leak-on-error, and "who holds the last reference" get solved **once**, tested **once**, reused everywhere.

## Why it matters

Pure engineering win (correctness + maintainability, no user-facing feature). It de-risks the #2335 code, and it's a force multiplier: every future subsystem gets correct lifecycle for free. This is the discipline that keeps the concurrency surface auditable — one lease/lifecycle machine underneath everything instead of N hand-rolled ones.

## Scope / guardrails

- Land the primitives + tests first (single-flight under concurrency, teardown-on-last-release, distinct error types, leak-on-teardown-error, race-clean).
- Then migrate subsystems one PR at a time — behavior-preserving refactors, no drive-by changes.
- Keep it surgical per `AGENTS.md`; no speculative generality beyond the real call sites listed above.
- `go test -race ./...` is the primary gate — this is concurrency code.

## Prior art

emdash `packages/core/src/lib/resource-map.ts` + `packages/shared/src/lifecycle-map.ts` — the whole app (projects, worktrees, agent processes, terminals) is built from this one family of ref-counted / single-flight / auto-teardown primitives.

## Sequencing

Do this **before** the txid-matched-optimistic-writes CDC work — it's more foundational and is load-bearing for #2335.

title: feat(scm): detect cross-fork PRs by scanning all project remotes
body:
## Problem

When a worker session opens a PR from the fork against an **upstream** base repo (the standard fork -> upstream contribution flow), the session never linked to that PR on the dashboard.

Root cause: the SCM observer only polled a project's push `origin` for open PRs. GitHub lists a PR under its **base** repo, not its head, so an origin-only scan can't see a PR whose base is upstream. Concretely, session `agent-orchestrator-23` opened a PR with head `harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator` and base `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`; the observer polled only the fork, the PR was never discovered, and no `pr` row was written, so the dashboard PR badge stayed empty.

## Fix

Scan **every** GitHub remote in the project checkout (origin + upstreams / mirrors), read from `git remote` at the project path, and attribute a PR to a session only when its head branch lives in that session's push origin.

- `discoverSubjects` now builds one scan target per (session x remote repo); `resolveScanRepos` reads all remotes and dedupes them against origin.
- Attribution moves from a fixed "head == this repo" guard to `candidatesForHeadRepo`: a PR is claimed only when `pr.HeadRepo` equals a candidate session's push origin **and** the branch prefix matches. Same-repo PRs (head == origin == scanned repo) and cross-fork PRs (head == origin, scanned repo == upstream base) both attribute; a stranger's fork PR has a head repo no session owns and is dropped, preserving the existing no-misattribution guarantee.
- Tracked cross-fork PRs are keyed for refresh by their own recorded repo (`subjectRepoForPR` uses `pr.Repo`, the upstream base) so the GraphQL refetch targets the base repo instead of the fork where the PR number doesn't exist.

## Cost

One extra cheap `RepoPRListGuard` ETag check per additional remote per 30s tick (304s when nothing changed). Negligible for the 2-3 remotes AO projects typically carry.

## Known ceiling

Remotes are read once per project per process; a remote added after the daemon started is picked up on restart.

## Tests

- `TestPoll_DiscoversCrossForkPRFromUpstreamRemote`: fork head + upstream base is discovered, attributed to the session, persisted with the upstream base repo, and refreshed against upstream.
- `TestPoll_IgnoresUpstreamPRFromForeignHead`: a matching-branch PR on a scanned upstream whose head lives in a third-party fork is never fetched or persisted.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/observe/...`, and the `observe/scm`, `adapters/scm`, `service/session` suites (181 tests) all pass.

title: Terminated session leaves stale browser preview panel visible
body:
## Summary

When a session is terminated (killed or finished), the browser preview panel on that session's detail page is not torn down. The view remains visible with the old `previewUrl` content, even though the session is no longer running.

## Root cause

Three independent gaps combine to prevent cleanup:

### 1. The poller skips terminated sessions entirely

`backend/internal/preview/poller.go:106-108`:

```go
if sess.IsTerminated {
    continue
}
```

This means the poller never clears the `preview_url` for a terminated session. For workspace-derived URLs this leaves a stale entry in the DB; for explicitly-set URLs (`ao preview http://...`) the poller would not touch them anyway (the `isWorkspacePreviewURL` guard in the clear path would return false).

### 2. The frontend never listens for termination

`SessionView.tsx:52-65` computes the `active` prop for `useBrowserView` as:

```ts
const session = workspaces.flatMap((w) => w.sessions).find((s) => s.id === sessionId);
// ...
const browserView = useBrowserView({
    sessionId,
    active: Boolean(session && hasInspector && (browserPoppedOut || isInspectorOpen)),
    // ...
    previewUrl: session?.previewUrl?.trim() || undefined,
    previewRevision: session?.previewRevision,
});
```

There is no check on `session?.isTerminated` anywhere — the browser view stays active and keeps its URL as long as the session object exists and the inspector is open.

`SessionView.tsx` also has no effect that clears the preview on termination. `useBrowserView.ts:234-247` (the preview-drive effect) has no guard keyed on termination status.

### 3. Explicit (non-workspace) URLs are never cleared

If the user ran `ao preview http://localhost:5173` on a session that later terminates, the poller has no reason to clear it (see point 1), and no frontend hook does either. The `hasUrlRef` guard added in the recent `fix/browser-clear-stale-preview` PR (`useBrowserView.ts:83`) does not help here — the URL is valid and non-empty, so the view is positioned normally.

## Why this is mostly latent (but still a bug)

In practice the gap is limited by session cleanup: when terminated sessions are removed from `ListAllSessions`, the workspace query no longer returns them, `session` becomes `null` in `SessionView.tsx`, and the "Session not found" fallback renders instead. The stale view only persists in the window between termination and cleanup.

## Suggested fix direction

- In `SessionView.tsx`, add a `useEffect` keyed on `session?.isTerminated` that calls `browserView.destroy()` or clears the preview URL when the session transitions to terminated.
- Alternatively, in `useBrowserView.ts`, add a termination-aware branch in the preview-drive effect (line 234) that clears the view when `isTerminated` is true.

## Evidence

File and line references (current `main`):

| File | Lines | What |
|------|-------|------|
| `backend/internal/preview/poller.go` | 106–108 | Poller skips terminated sessions |
| `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx` | 52–65 | `active`/`previewUrl`/`previewRevision` passed without termination guard |
| `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts` | 85–91, 234–247 | No termination-aware effects |
| `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx` | 170–176 | Fallback only renders when session is absent from workspace data, not when terminated-yet-present |

title: Title System prompt delivery is adapter-dependent and can be silently dropped
body:
AO accepts `SystemPrompt` and `SystemPromptFile` in the agent launch contract, but not every adapter can actually deliver those instructions to the underlying agent CLI.

### Some adapters inject the system prompt explicitly

- **Claude Code** uses `--append-system-prompt`
- **Codex** uses `developer_instructions` / `model_instructions_file`
- **Goose** uses `--system`
- **Amp, Droid, Qwen, Pi, etc.** have their own system-prompt flags

### Other adapters intentionally ignore or only partially support it

Because their CLI has no equivalent system-prompt flag:

- **Kilo Code** ignores `cfg.SystemPrompt` / `cfg.SystemPromptFile` and relies on its own config plus `AGENTS.md`
- **opencode** similarly defers system instructions to its own config
- **Cursor** relies on workspace rule files
- **Kimi/Copilot/Crush** appear to have no documented system-prompt injection path
- **Aider** only honors `SystemPromptFile` via `--read`; inline `SystemPrompt` is dropped

`AGENTS.md` helps for static repo/workspace guidance, but it is not equivalent to guaranteed system-prompt delivery. It does not reliably cover dynamic per-session instructions such as orchestrator role, review scope, callback protocol, worker coordination behavior, or safety/restriction instructions. It also depends on each upstream agent honoring workspace rules.

This means callers can provide a system prompt and assume it reached the agent when, for some adapters, it was silently ignored or only partially applied.

### Why this matters

If AO uses system prompts for required behavior, adapter selection can change semantics in a non-obvious way. The same session may behave correctly under Claude/Codex/Goose but miss important standing instructions under adapters without system-prompt support.

### Suggested fix

Add an explicit adapter capability for system-prompt support, for example:

- `none`
- `inline`
- `file`
- `inline_and_file`
- possibly `config_or_workspace_rules_only`

Then surface that capability where launches are created.

At minimum:

- Document the system-prompt behavior per adapter.
- Warn when `SystemPrompt` or `SystemPromptFile` is provided but the selected adapter cannot deliver it.
- Consider failing launches for session kinds where the system prompt is required for correctness.
- Add tests that verify unsupported adapters do not silently appear equivalent to supported ones.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AO has a documented system-prompt capability matrix for agent adapters.
- [ ] Launch code can detect when a provided system prompt will not be delivered.
- [ ] Users/developers receive a warning or error instead of silent dropping.
- [ ] Tests cover at least one fully supported adapter and one unsupported/partial adapter.

title: Add `ao agent` CLI commands for agent discovery and worker spawning
body:
### Summary

Add an `ao agent` CLI group for discovering available agent harnesses and spawning worker sessions with a selected agent. The commands should work both inside an AO orchestrator session and from a normal terminal, while keeping the daemon spawn API as the authoritative validation point.

### Goals

- Add `ao agent ls` for agent discovery.
- Add `ao agent spawn <agent>` for worker spawning with an explicit harness.
- Support project inference from `AO_SESSION_ID` when running inside an AO session.
- Add advisory agent availability/auth preflight before spawn.
- Keep behavior consistent with the existing `ao spawn` command.

### Proposed CLI

#### `ao agent ls`

Calls:

- `GET /api/v1/agents`

Flags:

- `--refresh`: call `POST /api/v1/agents/refresh` before listing.
- `--json`: emit machine-readable JSON.

Default output should show supported agents with install/auth status.

#### `ao agent spawn <agent>`

Spawns a worker session using the selected harness.

Mirrors existing `ao spawn` flags:

- `--project`
- `--name`
- `--branch`
- `--prompt`
- `--issue`
- `--claim-pr`
- `--no-takeover`

Project resolution:

- If `--project` is provided, use it.
- If `--project` is omitted and `AO_SESSION_ID` is set, fetch the current session and infer its `projectId`.
- If neither path provides a project, return a usage error:

```text
--project is required outside an AO session
```

### Agent Preflight

By default, `ao agent spawn <agent>` should run an advisory preflight before calling the daemon spawn API:

1. Call `POST /api/v1/agents/refresh`.
2. Check the selected `<agent>` in the returned/available agent list.
3. Fail before spawn if the agent is unsupported or not installed.
4. Fail before spawn if `authStatus` is `unauthorized`.
5. If `authStatus` is `unknown`, print a warning and continue.
6. Add `--skip-agent-check` to bypass refresh/preflight and go directly to daemon spawn.

The daemon spawn API remains the authoritative validation point; the CLI preflight is for faster, clearer feedback.

### Implementation Notes

- Add a new CLI file, for example:
  - `backend/internal/cli/agent.go`
- Register `newAgentCommand(ctx)` in `NewRootCommand`.
- Reuse or extract existing `ao spawn` request construction, validation, PR-claim, and rollback behavior so these remain consistent:
  - `ao spawn --agent X`
  - `ao agent spawn X`
- Preserve existing CLI error conventions:
  - usage errors return `usageError` and exit 2
  - daemon/runtime failures exit 1
  - preserve daemon error envelopes/request IDs where applicable
- Keep CLI as a thin daemon client; do not move daemon validation into the CLI.

### Docs

Update `docs/cli/README.md` to document:

- `ao agent ls`
- `ao agent ls --refresh`
- `ao agent spawn <agent>`
- `--skip-agent-check`
- project inference from `AO_SESSION_ID`
- behavior when `--project` is omitted outside an AO session

### Suggested Tests

Add CLI tests covering:

- `ao agent ls` calls `GET /api/v1/agents`.
- `ao agent ls --refresh` calls refresh before listing.
- `ao agent ls --json` emits JSON.
- `ao agent spawn <agent>` passes the selected harness to spawn.
- `ao agent spawn <agent>` infers project from `AO_SESSION_ID`.
- Missing `--project` outside AO session returns a usage error.
- Unsupported or not installed agent fails before spawn.
- Unauthorized agent fails before spawn.
- Unknown auth status warns and continues.
- `--skip-agent-check` bypasses refresh/preflight.
- PR claim / rollback behavior matches existing `ao spawn`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ao agent ls` lists available supported agents and statuses.
- [ ] `ao agent ls --refresh` refreshes the catalog before listing.
- [ ] `ao agent spawn <agent>` spawns a worker using the selected harness.
- [ ] `ao agent spawn <agent>` works inside an AO session without explicit `--project` when `AO_SESSION_ID` is set.
- [ ] `ao agent spawn <agent>` returns a usage error outside AO session when no project is provided.
- [ ] Agent preflight blocks unsupported, uninstalled, or unauthorized agents unless skipped.
- [ ] Existing `ao spawn` behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] `docs/cli/README.md` is updated.

title: Browser panel shows white screen with no feedback when navigation fails
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1efcd36d-2179-4460-962f-0607137a612f

Summary

When the embedded browser panel's WebContentsView fails to load a URL — connection refused, server down, wrong port, incorrect url,timeout — the user sees a completely blank white screen with zero feedback. No error message, no retry prompt, nothing. The failure surfaces only as an unhandled promise rejection in DevTools console, invisible to the user.

This affects every navigation failure path: typing a URL in the address bar, clicking reload, clicking back/forward, and auto-detected preview URLs whose server goes down mid-session.

Reproduction

  1. Start a session from a project that has an index.html
  2. Confirm the browser panel renders it correctly
  3. Kill the dev server / delete the file
  4. Click the reload button in the browser panel

Expected: An error message is shown in the panel ("Connection refused", "Unable to load page", etc.)

Actual: White/blank screen, no feedback, unhandled promise rejection in DevTools console:

useBrowserView.ts:229 Uncaught (in promise) Error: Error invoking remote method
'browser:navigate': Error: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (-102) loading 'http://localhost:3012/'

Root Cause

There are two separate gaps that combine to produce this behavior.

Gap 1 — navigate() IPC handler throws instead of returning error state

browser-view-host.ts:178–186, function navigate():

const navigate = async ({ viewId, url }: BrowserNavigateInput): Promise<BrowserNavState> => {
    const entry = ensure(viewId);
    const normalized = normalizeBrowserURL(url);
    if (!isAllowedBrowserURL(normalized.href, options.rendererOrigin)) {
        throw new Error("Unsupported browser URL");
    }
    await entry.view.webContents.loadURL(normalized.href);  // ← throws ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
    return pushNavState(options, entry);                     // ← never reached
};

No try-catch exists. When loadURL rejects, the rejection propagates through the IPC framework back to the renderer. The renderer's withView at useBrowserView.ts:224–229 also has no try-catch, so it becomes an unhandled promise rejection. setNavState is never called, so the UI never updates.

Gap 2 — Native WebContentsView overlay hides the DOM error text

did-fail-load does fire. It does set entry.state.error and send browser:navState to the renderer. The renderer does receive it and call setNavState. The error <p> is rendered in the DOM at BrowserPanel.tsx:119.

But the native WebContentsView is an OS-level window overlay that paints above all DOM content regardless of z-index. The did-fail-load handler never hides the native view, so it continues to paint over the DOM error text. The error exists in the DOM — it is just invisible.

Root cause in one sentence

The native WebContentsView is not hidden when navigation fails, so it paints over the DOM-rendered error message; and the navigate() IPC handler has no try-catch, so loadURL rejections become unhandled promise rejections instead of returning a graceful error state.

Detailed Call Stack

Path A — Address bar (typing URL + Enter)

Step | File | Line | What happens -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | BrowserPanel.tsx | 46–49 | submit() fires void navigate(nextURL) — promise discarded 2 | useBrowserView.ts | 231–233 | navigate(url) calls withView((id) => window.ao!.browser.navigate(...)) 3 | useBrowserView.ts | 224–229 | withView does const next = await fn(id) — no try-catch 4 | preload.ts | 46–47 | ipcRenderer.invoke("browser:navigate", input) 5 | browser-view-host.ts | 236 | IPC handler calls navigate(input) 6 | browser-view-host.ts | 184 | loadURL() throws ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED 7 | — | — | Rejection propagates uncaught through entire chain 8 | useBrowserView.ts | 229 | if (next) setNavState(next) never reached 9 | BrowserPanel.tsx | 49 | void navigate() — rejection silently dropped

Missing Test Coverage

browser-view-host.test.ts

  • navigate() returns error state instead of throwing when loadURL rejects
  • navigate() hides the view on loadURL failure
  • did-fail-load hides the view and sends error state via browser:navState
  • Successful navigation after error restores view visibility

useBrowserView.test.tsx

  • Navigation failure updates navState.error in the renderer
  • did-fail-load event sets navState.error via the event channel
  • No unhandled promise rejection on navigation failure
  • Error state clears on subsequent successful navigation

Edge Cases the Fix Should Cover

  • ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED — DNS failure, same code path
  • ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT — same code path
  • ERR_ABORTED — should NOT show user-visible error (navigation was intentionally cancelled)
  • Malformed/empty URL — normalizeBrowserURL throws synchronously before loadURL, same IPC rejection path
  • Blocked URL via isAllowedBrowserURL — synchronous throw, same path
  • Rapid navigate/reload during in-flight navigation — aborted navigation should not persist error state
  • Session terminated during navigation — clear() races with did-fail-load, error from aborted navigation should not persist after clear

Duplicate Search

No existing issues found for:

  • white screen navigation
  • ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED browser panel
  • did-fail-load
  • unhandled promise rejection navigate

title: Session rename accepts display names longer than the 20-character cap that spawn enforces
body:
### Summary
Session display names are meant to be capped at 20 characters. **Spawn enforces this cap; rename does not.** Every rename entry point — `ao session rename`, `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/{id}`, and the `Service.Rename` layer they share — accepts and persists an arbitrarily long name. This lets a user set a sidebar label that spawn would have rejected, and contradicts the frontend's own comment claiming the daemon enforces the limit.

### Expected behavior
- Rename should apply the same 20-character (rune) cap as spawn and reject overlong names with the same `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG` error, at both the API and the CLI.

### Actual behavior
- `ao session rename <id> "<21+ chars>"` returns success and stores the name verbatim.
- `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/<id>` with a 21-character `displayName` returns `200 OK`.
- The identical body sent to `POST /api/v1/sessions` (spawn) is rejected with `400 DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`.

### Root cause
The cap exists on the spawn path but was never added to the rename path.

1. **Spawn caps it** — `utf8.RuneCountInString(displayName) > maxDisplayNameLen` → `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`.
   `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:130`, and `backend/internal/cli/spawn.go:67`. Covered by `TestSessionsAPI_SpawnDisplayNameTooLong` (`sessions_test.go:692`).

2. **The PATCH handler only trims and rejects empty** — no length check.
   `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:324`

3. **`Service.Rename` only trims and rejects empty** — no length check.
   `backend/internal/service/session/service.go:323`

4. **The CLI only checks non-empty** (arg validator and command body).
   `backend/internal/cli/session.go:305` and `:479`

5. **The store does no truncation** — plain `UPDATE`, and SQLite `TEXT` has no length limit, so the overlong value persists.
   `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/session_store.go:45`

6. **The frontend documents the cap as if enforced server-side — it isn't.** The sidebar input's `maxLength={20}` guards only the desktop UI, not the CLI or raw API.
   `frontend/src/renderer/lib/rename-session.ts:4`, `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:627`

### Steps to reproduce
1. Spawn a session in any project.
2. Run: `ao session rename <session-id> "this-name-is-way-too-long-to-fit"` (32 chars).
3. The command succeeds and the sidebar shows the full overlong label.
4. Confirm the asymmetry: `POST /api/v1/sessions` with the same 21+ character `displayName` returns `400 DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`, while `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/<id>` with it returns `200 OK`.

### Affected files
- `backend/internal/service/session/service.go:323` — add the cap here so all callers inherit it
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:324` and `backend/internal/cli/session.go:305` — optional client-side parity, mirroring spawn
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions_test.go` — add a rename equivalent of `TestSessionsAPI_SpawnDisplayNameTooLong`
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/rename-session.ts:4` — correct the inaccurate comment

title: add a Restart to Update
Restart to update: sidebar row, channel badges, per-channel escalation (revised spec)
body:
Revised spec for the "Restart to update" design, produced by auditing the current nightly codebase. Design intent is unchanged from the original write-up: a non-modal sidebar row directly above Settings while an update is staged, a purple `nightly` badge on the wordmark, and an update pill that flips to orange on per-channel rules. What changed: most primitives the original spec treated as net-new already exist and are wired end to end. The real work reduces to one new publish-side primitive (the `important` flag), one new main-process evaluator, and two renderer surfaces.

## Audit: assumed primitives vs reality

| # | Assumption | Status | Evidence |
|---|------------|--------|----------|
| 1 | `important` flag on releases | MISSING | `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs:37-48` writes only `version`, `files[]`, `path`, `sha512`, `releaseDate`. No workflow input, no feed key, no read side. |
| 2 | stable vs nightly channel | EXISTS | `UpdateChannel = "latest" \| "nightly"` at `frontend/src/main/update-settings.ts:4`; persisted at `~/.ao/update-settings.json`; first-run dialog `ensureUpdatePrefs` at `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:128-171`; Settings UI selector in `frontend/src/renderer/components/UpdatesSection.tsx`. #2207 is closed and fully implemented. |
| 3 | separate `latest.yml` / `nightly.yml` feeds | EXISTS | Custom `feed.mjs` (electron-forge build, not electron-builder) generates `latest*.yml` (`frontend-release.yml:239-269`) and `nightly*.yml` (`frontend-nightly.yml:183-216`), uploaded as release assets. Client selects via `autoUpdater.channel` + `allowPrerelease` (`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:18-26`). Neither channel cross-updates; switching is already an explicit Settings action. |
| 4 | staged / downloaded signal | EXISTS | `update-downloaded` event broadcasts `{state: "downloaded", version}` (`auto-updater.ts:52`); pushed via `updates:status`, pullable via `updates:getStatus` (`main.ts:844`, `preload.ts:83-93`). Surfaced today only in Global Settings (`UpdatesSection.tsx:155-158`, "Restart & install"). No silent install. Gap: no staged-at timestamp is recorded (needed for the stable 48h rule). |
| 5 | nightly semver prerelease versions | EXISTS (scheme differs slightly) | `frontend/scripts/nightly-version.mjs:12-26`: `X.Y.(Z+1)-nightly.YYYYMMDDHHmm` (patch bumped above the latest `desktop-v*` stable tag, 12-digit UTC timestamp; `+shortsha` build metadata stripped before stamping, `frontend-nightly.yml:207`). The compare the spec wants holds: a nightly sorts above the stable it was cut from and below the next stable, so `semver.lt(running, latestStable)` is exactly the behind-stable trigger. `semver` is only a transitive dep today, not in `frontend/package.json`. |
| 6 | sidebar insertion point + colors | PARTIAL | Footer with the Settings menu: `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:262-376` (expanded row at 263, collapsed icon rail at 323). Wordmark span: `Sidebar.tsx:199-201`. Orange exists: `--orange` (`#f59f4c` dark / `#c2410c` light) is `--color-working`, the WORKING dot color (`styles.css:67-68,109,146`). Purple token: MISSING, net-new. |

## Decisions locked by the audit (deltas from the original spec)

- The nightly badge derives from the running binary, not the setting: `app.getVersion().includes("-nightly.")`. The channel setting can be flipped mid-session in Settings; the wordmark answers "what am I running", which only changes on restart. This preserves "channel is identity".
- Do not rely on electron-updater passing an unknown `important` yml key through `UpdateInfo`. The app fetches the feeds read-only itself (T2). This also lets a maintainer retro-flag an already-published nightly (re-upload `nightly*.yml` with `--clobber`); the recompute timer picks it up without a new build.
- Read-only stable lookup: `GET https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest/download/latest.yml` (GitHub resolves `/latest` to the newest non-prerelease). Parse only the `version` key. All feed fetches fail silently; older releases lack manifests (#2270) and this path must never surface an error.
- `stagedAt` lives in memory next to `lastStatus` (`auto-updater.ts:28`). Staged state is per-run (a restart applies the update), so persistence buys nothing.
- Escalation policy lives in the main process, matching the existing layering ("all policy comes from update-settings", `auto-updater.ts:63-64`); the renderer stays a pure view.

## Trigger logic (unchanged in spirit)

```
if status.state != "downloaded":
    render nothing

render sidebar row directly above Settings   # fresh / transparent by default

if channel == "latest":
    escalated = (now - stagedAt) >= 48h
else:  # nightly
    escalated = feed.important
             or semver.lt(app.getVersion(), latestStableVersion)

variant = escalated ? "orange" : "fresh"
# recomputed in main on an interval and re-broadcast, so escalation
# happens while the app stays open; restart always installs the newest
# staged build, so escalation self-clears.
```

## Work breakdown

### T1: `important` flag, publish side (new primitive; touches the release workflow, needs maintainer sign-off; test against a fork release repo via `AO_RELEASE_REPO`)
- `frontend-nightly.yml`: add a `workflow_dispatch` boolean input `important` (default false), forward it to the `publish-feed` job.
- `feed.mjs`: accept the flag and write a top-level `important: true` key into `nightly*.yml` when set (extend its existing test).
- Document retro-flagging: re-run the feed job with the flag set, or edit and `gh release upload --clobber`.
- Files: `.github/workflows/frontend-nightly.yml`, `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`. No app code. Independent of T2-T4; the only shared interface is the key name (`important`, top-level boolean), agreed upfront.

### T2: escalation evaluator, main process (new primitive)
- Add `stagedAt` (epoch ms) when broadcasting the downloaded state (`auto-updater.ts:52`).
- New read-only feed fetch helper: `latest.yml` always, `nightly.yml` on the nightly channel; parse `version` + `important`; silent failure, short timeout.
- Evaluator computes `escalated` per the trigger logic; recompute on an interval (15-30 min) and on every status change; re-broadcast the enriched status `{state: "downloaded", version, stagedAt, escalated}` over the existing `updates:status` channel.
- Add `semver` as a direct `frontend` dependency (already in the lockfile transitively).
- Files: `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`, `frontend/src/main/update-settings.ts` (UpdateStatus type), `frontend/src/preload.ts` (type only). Works before T1 ships: a missing `important` key reads as false.

### T3: sidebar restart row, renderer (wire-up; depends on T2)
- Conditional row inside `SidebarFooter` directly above the Settings trigger: insert before `Sidebar.tsx:263` (expanded) plus an icon-only variant with tooltip before `Sidebar.tsx:323` (collapsed rail).
- Renders only when `status.state === "downloaded"`; zero footprint otherwise. Two lines: `Restart to update` + `vX.Y.Z ready`.
- Fresh = transparent (inherits sidebar background, neutral dot, standard label color). Escalated = orange fill, border, label, dot, reusing the `--color-working` / `--orange` tokens so it speaks the board's existing color language.
- Click calls `aoBridge.updates.install()` (existing, `main.ts:853`). Initial state via `aoBridge.updates.getStatus()`, live updates via `aoBridge.updates.onStatus` (both existing).
- Follow DESIGN.md (clone agent-orchestrator look; the footer block already documents the approved divergence pattern for this zone).

### T4: nightly wordmark badge, renderer (wire-up; independent)
- Purple `nightly` pill after the wordmark span (`Sidebar.tsx:199-201`); hidden in the icon rail along with the wordmark.
- Add a `--purple` token (dark + light values) in `styles.css`; none exists today. Keep it out of the terminal palette.
- Condition: running version contains `-nightly.`, via the existing `aoBridge.app.getVersion()` (`preload.ts:21`). Stable wears no badge.

Ordering: T4 anytime; T2 then T3; T1 in parallel with T2.

## Out of scope (already shipped)

Channel selector, persistence, and first-run prompt (#2207, closed). Feed generation for both channels. Restart plumbing (`updates:install` / `quitAndInstall`). Related: #2270 (missing-manifest 404s must stay silent); T2's silent-fail fetch must not regress it.

title: feat(release): important flag for nightly feed manifests
body:
## What

Adds an `important` boolean input to the nightly workflow and a corresponding `--important` flag to `feed.mjs`. When set, each generated `nightly*.yml` carries a top-level `important: true` key, which the app reads to escalate the restart prompt (consumed in a separate task).

## Why

Part of #2377. The agreed interface is a top-level boolean `important` in the yml feed manifests for the nightly channel.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/frontend-nightly.yml`: adds `workflow_dispatch.inputs.important` (boolean, default false), forwards it as `NIGHTLY_IMPORTANT` env var to the publish-feed step, passes `--important` to feed.mjs when true. Scheduled/push runs are unaffected (flag defaults to false when `inputs.important` is undefined).
- `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`: `buildYml` accepts an optional fourth argument `important` (default false) and emits `important: true` after `releaseDate` when set. `generateFeeds` and the CLI entrypoint thread the flag through. Output is byte-identical when flag is not set.
- `frontend/scripts/feed.test.mjs`: two new cases in the `buildYml` suite, covering flag-off (no `important` key) and flag-on (`important: true` present).

## Retro-flagging

An already-published nightly can be retro-flagged without a rebuild: re-run only the publish-feed job via workflow_dispatch with `important` set to true, or edit the yml locally and run `gh release upload TAG nightly*.yml --clobber`.

## Verification

All feed.mjs unit tests pass (including the two new cases). No live publish was run; this touches the release workflow and needs maintainer sign-off before a real dispatch.

## Notes

- This touches the release workflow: review carefully before triggering a real dispatch with `important: true`.
- Only unit-tested, no live publish run.
- The stable workflow (`frontend-release.yml`) is completely unchanged.

title: feat(sidebar): nightly channel badge on the wordmark
body:
## What

A small purple pill labeled `nightly` appears next to the "Agent Orchestrator" wordmark in the sidebar header when the running build is a nightly release. Stable builds wear no badge.

## Why

Nightly builds have distinct behavior (auto-updates, experimental features) and users should be able to identify the channel at a glance without navigating to settings.

## How

- **Channel detection**: derived from the running version string (`appVersion.includes("-nightly.")`) via `aoBridge.app.getVersion()` (IPC `app:getVersion`). This is intentional: the update-channel *setting* can be flipped mid-session; the binary cannot. Version strings look like `0.10.4-nightly.202607031330`. Dev fallback `0.0.0-preview` shows no badge.
- **CSS tokens**: added `--purple: #a78bfa` (dark) and `--purple: #7c3aed` (light) to `styles.css`, following the existing orange/amber/green/red palette pattern in both `:root` blocks.
- **Badge**: a `shrink-0` span with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--purple) 12%, transparent)` fill and `var(--purple)` text, sized at 10px with `rounded-full` pill shape. Uses `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden` so it disappears when the sidebar collapses to the icon rail (same idiom as the wordmark span itself).
- `useQuery` for `["app-version"]` with `staleTime: Infinity` (version never changes while the process lives), consistent with the pattern in `UpdatesSection.tsx`.

## Verification

vite build (renderer) -- built in 365ms, no errors

body: ## Problem The terminal toolbar header shows the raw **session id** (e.g. `agent-orchestrator-23`). Now that `--name` is compulsory at `ao spawn` (#2299 / merged #2302), every worker session has a display name, so the header should show that name instead of the id, and stay in sync with the name shown in the sidebar. Orchestrator sessions should read `Orchestrator`. ## Current behavior `frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx:102` ```tsx {session?.id ?? "No session"} ``` ## Desired behavior - **Worker session** → show the display name (`session.title`, the same field the sidebar renders, so the two stay in sync). - **Orchestrator session** → show `Orchestrator`. Use the existing `isOrchestratorSession(session)` helper in `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts`. - **No session** → keep `No session`. Sketch: ```tsx {!session ? "No session" : isOrchestratorSession(session) ? "Orchestrator" : session.title} ``` ## Notes - `session.title` is already the display name surfaced elsewhere; reuse it rather than adding a new field. - Keep it reactive so an inline rename (#2301) updates the terminal header too.

title: feat(updater): restart-to-update sidebar row with per-channel escalation
body:
## What

Implements T2 and T3 of the staged-update escalation work:

- Extends `UpdateStatus` with optional `stagedAt` (epoch ms) and `escalated` fields, present on the `downloaded` state.
- Adds a pure `evaluateEscalation()` function (`frontend/src/main/escalation-evaluator.ts`) with 8 unit tests.
- Wires a 30-minute unref'd `setInterval` in `auto-updater.ts` that re-evaluates escalation after each `update-downloaded` and rebroadcasts the status.
- Adds a "Restart to update" row in the sidebar footer, directly above Settings, in both expanded and collapsed (icon rail) variants. Clicking calls `updates.install()`; no confirmation dialog, the row itself is the prompt. Zero footprint unless an update is downloaded.

## Escalation rules

| Channel | Escalates when |
|---|---|
| latest | `now - stagedAt >= 48h` |
| nightly | feed `important: true` on the staged release yml, OR `semver.lt(runningVersion, latestStableVersion)` (skipped if stable version could not be fetched) |

Feed data comes from read-only fetches of the GitHub release yml files (owner/repo regex-parsed from the bundled `app-update.yml`, platform suffix per the feed.mjs convention, 10s abort timeout). Every failure is silent: this path never broadcasts an error state (see #2270) and dev builds skip it entirely, so `escalated` stays false outside the packaged app. No yaml dependency; regex on flat keys is deliberate.

## UI

- Fresh: transparent row inheriting the sidebar background, passive label plus small neutral dot, Settings-row hover treatment.
- Escalated: orange text and dot reusing the `--orange` / `bg-working` tokens, with a subtle `color-mix` orange fill and border matching the existing styles.css idiom.
- Collapsed rail: icon-only RefreshCw button with both lines in the tooltip.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Full vite builds of all three bundles (`vite.main.config.ts`, `vite.preload.config.ts`, `vite.renderer.config.ts`, there is no aggregate `build` script in frontend/package.json): all exit 0.
- `npm test`: 383/383 tests pass across 41 files, including the 8 new escalation-evaluator tests (stable under/at/over 48h, nightly important, nightly behind stable 0.10.4 vs ahead of 0.10.3, missing stable info, unparseable versions).

## Notes

- The `important` feed key ships separately (publish side is a sibling PR); until then the key is absent from nightly release ymls and reads as false, so nightly escalation relies only on the behind-stable semver check.
- New direct dependency: `semver` (plus `@types/semver` dev). It was previously only transitive.

Part of #2377.

title: fix(session): enforce 20-char display name cap on rename
body:
Resolves #2375

title: fix(ci): gofmt manager_test.go to unbreak main
body:
## Problem

`main` is red on the **Go** workflow (`build-test` + `lint`). Both steps flag one file:

```
backend/internal/session_manager/manager_test.go:1915: File is not properly formatted
```

The struct field is misaligned with extra spaces that `gofmt` collapses:

```go
-		Metadata:     domain.SessionMetadata{Branch: "ao/mer-4/root", WorkspacePath: "/ws/mer-4"},
+		Metadata: domain.SessionMetadata{Branch: "ao/mer-4/root", WorkspacePath: "/ws/mer-4"},
```

## Why it slipped through

This file landed via #2350. That merge push never ran the Go workflow (no run recorded for its merge commit), so the violation went unnoticed until the next push to `main` triggered the Go workflow and failed.
