title: fix: prevent stale markdown preview cache in app://md-preview protoco…
body:
## Overview

This PR adds live markdown preview in the Electron browser panel alongside `ao preview` CLI support, file-watching with auto-refresh, and CSS-only theme control. The implementation spans backend (daemon + CLI), frontend (Electron main/renderer/preload), and agent skill assets.

## Features

### Markdown rendering in browser panel
- `.md` files are rendered to styled HTML via `marked` + `DOMPurify` inside the Electron BrowserView using a custom `app://md-preview` protocol handler
- Chromium caching is disabled on the protocol handler (`Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`) so `reload()` always fetches fresh content
- File watching via chokidar with debounce provides live refresh on save — the watcher re-renders on `change`, and the renderer calls `reload()` on the BrowserView

### `ao preview` CLI command
- `ao preview [url]` — opens a URL in the desktop browser panel for the current session; with no argument, opens the workspace's `index.html`
- `ao preview clear` — empties the panel
- Relative paths are resolved to absolute before sending to the daemon
- "File not found" for non-existent paths
- Missing `$AO_SESSION_ID` returns a usage error

### Daemon preview endpoints
- `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview` — set preview URL; accepts file paths (resolved to `file://`), HTTP URLs, or daemon-proxy URLs
- `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview` — clear preview; autodetects `index.html` in the workspace or falls back to blank
- Preview state flows through CDC (SQLite triggers → SSE → `session_updated` event) to the renderer

### File deletion handling
- When a watched `.md` file is deleted, the daemon DELETE endpoint is called, reverting to `index.html` (if it exists) or clearing to blank — no stale content, no error page
- Daemon port is wired into `MarkdownHost` via `reportBoundPort` → `setDaemonPort()` for the HTTP DELETE call

### CSS-only dark/light theme toggle
- Hidden checkbox + `<label for>` hack with `body:has(#theme-toggle:checked)` selectors
- Full-viewport background via `body:has()` instead of `.content` (fixes white border from `max-width: 920px`)
- Smooth `transition: color 0.25s` / `background 0.25s`
- Zero JavaScript — fully CSP-compatible (`script-src 'none'`)

### Agent auto-preview instructions
- `SKILL.md` updated to direct agents to run `ao preview <path>` immediately after creating a `.md` file
- If producing multiple `.md` files, only the last one is auto-previewed (panel shows one at a time)

## Key changes by layer

| Layer | Files | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Backend daemon | `internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` | Preview endpoints + index.html autodetection on clear |
| Backend CLI | `internal/cli/preview.go` | `ao preview` command with relative path resolution |
| Backend tests | `internal/cli/preview_test.go` | Tests for preview, clear, path resolution, missing session, help text |
| Frontend main | `main.ts`, `markdown-host.ts`, `markdown-renderer.ts` | Protocol handler, file watcher, markdown→HTML rendering, daemon port wiring |
| Frontend preload | `preload.ts` | IPC bridge for `renderMarkdown` / `md:fileChanged` |
| Frontend renderer | `components/BrowserPanel.tsx`, `hooks/useBrowserView.ts` | Markdown URL detection, render routing, file-change listener |
| Agent assets | `backend/internal/skillassets/markdown-preview/SKILL.md` | Auto-preview workflow instructions |

## Testing

- CLI unit tests pass on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows
- Full `go test ./internal/...` and `go vet ./internal/...`

title: Enterprise Policy Engine for Agent Governance
body:
Introduce a centralized policy engine that evaluates every agent action before execution. This enables organizations to safely deploy Agent Orchestrator in enterprise environments by enforcing security, governance, and compliance policies across all supported agent adapters.

Problem

Today, agents can execute actions based primarily on their runtime capabilities. Enterprises often require fine-grained control over what AI agents are allowed to do, including:

Executing shell commands
Accessing specific directories
Making network requests
Invoking MCP servers
Performing Git operations
Running deployment commands
Accessing secrets

Without a centralized authorization layer, organizations must rely on external sandboxing or avoid granting agents broader capabilities altogether.

Proposed Solution

Introduce a policy evaluation layer that sits between the orchestrator and the runtime.

Agent
   │
   ▼
Policy Engine
   │
 ┌─┴────────┐
 │          │
Allow     Deny
 │          │
 ▼          ▼
Runtime   Error

Every action generated by an agent would be evaluated before execution.

Example API:

decision := policy.Check(ctx)

where ctx contains information such as:

Agent
Action type
Command
Repository
Workspace
Target files
Network destination
Metadata
Initial Policy Scope

Possible policy categories:

Filesystem
Read
Write
Delete
Shell
Allow/Deny command patterns
Git
Push
Force push
Branch deletion
Network
Allow-listed domains
Block external destinations
MCP
Allow specific MCP servers
Block sensitive integrations
Sensitive Operations
Deployments
Infrastructure changes
Database migrations
Example Policy
version: 1

agents:
  codex:
    filesystem:
      write:
        allow:
          - frontend/**
          - docs/**
        deny:
          - infra/**
          - secrets/**

    shell:
      allow:
        - go test ./...
        - pnpm test

      deny:
        - rm *
        - sudo *
        - terraform apply

    git:
      deny:
        - push main
        - force push

    network:
      allow:
        - github.com
        - api.company.internal
Benefits
Enterprise-ready governance
Consistent authorization across all agent adapters
Reduced operational risk
Easier compliance and auditing
Foundation for future approval workflows and hybrid-cloud deployments
Future Extensions (Out of Scope)
Human approval workflows
Role-based and attribute-based policies
Audit logging
Temporary capability elevation
Policy inheritance
Organization-wide policy bundles

Keeping the initial implementation focused on policy evaluation would make it easier to review and extend incrementally.

title: RFC: Hybrid Local + Cloud Agent Architecture for Enterprise Deployments
body:
As Agent Orchestrator evolves beyond individual developer workflows, it would be valuable to introduce an architecture that allows agent execution to span local machines, enterprise infrastructure, and cloud compute while preserving AO's existing orchestration model.

This RFC proposes separating **task orchestration** from **task execution**, allowing the scheduler to dispatch work to different execution backends based on policy, capabilities, or organizational requirements.

## Motivation

Today, Agent Orchestrator assumes that agent sessions execute on the local machine.

For enterprise deployments, organizations often have additional requirements:

* Sensitive repositories must execute only on internal infrastructure.
* GPU-intensive tasks should run on dedicated cloud machines.
* Long-running agents should continue after a developer disconnects.
* Organizations may have shared pools of agent workers.
* Different teams may require different execution environments.

Instead of treating execution as inherently local, AO could treat execution environments as interchangeable backends.

## Proposed Architecture

Separate the system into two responsibilities:

### 1. Control Plane

Responsible for:

* Task planning
* Agent lifecycle
* Session management
* Worktree management
* CI feedback routing
* Merge conflict handling
* Review routing
* Scheduling

The control plane does **not** execute agents directly.

---

### 2. Execution Plane

Responsible for actually running agents.

Possible execution targets include:

* Local workstation
* Enterprise workstation
* On-prem worker
* Cloud VM
* Kubernetes worker
* GPU worker

Each worker exposes a common execution interface.

```text
                     Agent Orchestrator
                     (Control Plane)
                            │
                   Scheduling Decision
                            │
        ┌───────────────────┼────────────────────┐
        │                   │                    │
        ▼                   ▼                    ▼
 Local Executor      On-Prem Worker       Cloud Worker
        │                   │                    │
        ▼                   ▼                    ▼
 Claude/Codex        Claude/Codex         Claude/Codex
```

## Worker Abstraction

Execution environments implement a common interface regardless of where they run.

Conceptually:

```go
type Worker interface {
    Start(Session) error
    Stop(Session) error
    StreamLogs(Session)
    Health()
}
```

This keeps scheduling independent from execution.

## Scheduling

Initially, scheduling could remain simple:

* Local
* Remote
* Auto

Future scheduling decisions could consider:

* Repository sensitivity
* Available GPU resources
* Cost
* Queue depth
* Worker health
* Enterprise policies

## Why This Architecture

Separating orchestration from execution provides several benefits:

* Local-first development remains unchanged.
* Enterprise deployments can introduce shared worker pools.
* Cloud execution becomes an implementation detail rather than a special case.
* New execution environments can be added without changing orchestration logic.

## Possible Future Extensions

This architecture naturally enables future capabilities such as:

* Hybrid local/cloud execution
* Auto-scaling worker pools
* Organization-wide worker fleets
* Cost-aware scheduling
* GPU-aware scheduling
* Enterprise policy integration
* High-availability execution
* Multi-region workers

## Open Questions

* Should workers maintain persistent sessions or be ephemeral?
* Should worktrees be created locally or remotely?
* How should artifacts and logs be synchronized?
* Should workers pull repositories directly or receive snapshots?
* How should disconnected workers recover running sessions?
* How should execution policies interact with scheduling decisions?

title: bug(session): terminated session reports merged while it still owns an open PR
body:
### Summary

`deriveStatus` reports a **terminated** session as `merged` whenever *any* of its PRs is merged — even if the session still owns an **open** PR. In that case the status should stay `terminated`, matching the function's own documented invariant.

### Where

`backend/internal/service/session/status.go`, the terminated branch:

```go
if rec.IsTerminated {
    if anyMerged(prs) {
        return domain.StatusMerged
    }
    return domain.StatusTerminated
}
```

The docstring right above states the rule: *"Merged/closed PRs only matter once no open PR remains."* The non-terminated branch already enforces it — it computes `open := openPRs(prs)` and returns the aggregated PR status while `len(open) > 0`, only falling back to `anyMerged` once no open PR is left. The terminated branch skips that gate.

### How it regressed

This looks like a leftover from the single-PR → multi-PR change (#230). The branch used to be `if pr != nil && pr.Merged`, which in the single-PR world implied "the one PR merged, so nothing is open." Generalizing it to `anyMerged(prs)` dropped that implicit "no open PR" condition, while the non-terminated branch *was* correctly restructured with an explicit `openPRs` gate. The two branches disagree now.

### Repro

A worker owns a stack: PR A (bottom) and PR B (child of A). PR A merges, then the session is killed while B is still open — so `prs = [{A: merged}, {B: open}]` and `IsTerminated = true`.

- **Actual:** `anyMerged` is true → status `merged`. The dashboard shows the killed session as cleanly merged, hiding the abandoned open PR B.
- **Expected:** `terminated` — an open PR remains, so the session did not complete.

The same thing happens with two independent PRs where one merges and the session is killed with the other still open.

### Suggested fix

Gate the merged short-circuit on there being no open PR, mirroring the non-terminated branch:

```go
if len(openPRs(prs)) == 0 && anyMerged(prs) {
    return domain.StatusMerged
}
```

Existing behavior is preserved (a terminated session whose only PR is merged still reports `merged`); only the `merged + open` combination changes to `terminated`.

title: bug(cli): `ao review submit` and `ao preview` exit 1 (not 2) on arg-count misuse
body:
### Summary

`AGENTS.md` states the convention: *"Return usage errors as `usageError` so CLI misuse exits 2; runtime/daemon failures should exit 1."* Two commands don't follow it for **argument-count** misuse — they exit `1` instead of `2`.

### Where

`ao review submit` and `ao preview` declare their positional-arg validators with a bare Cobra validator:

- `backend/internal/cli/review.go` — `Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)`
- `backend/internal/cli/preview.go` — `Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` (and `preview clear` → `Args: cobra.NoArgs`)

Cobra's arg-count error is a plain `errors.New(...)`. The root's `SetFlagErrorFunc` only wraps **flag**-parse errors as `usageError`, not `Args` validation, so a too-many-args error is not a `usageError` and `ExitCode` returns `1`.

Every other command wraps its validator so arg-count misuse becomes a `usageError` (exit 2): `noArgs` (root.go), `oneSessionIDArg` / the claim-pr and rename validators (session.go), and the inline wrappers in `project.go` and `completion.go`.

### Repro

```
$ ao review submit mer-1 mer-2
Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
$ echo $?
1        # expected 2
```

Same for `ao preview a b` and `ao preview clear extra`.

This is inconsistent with the commands' own tests, which already assert exit `2` for their other usage errors (`TestReviewSubmitMissing*IsUsageError`, `TestPreview_*IsUsageError`). A caller that distinguishes usage misuse (2) from a daemon/runtime failure (1) misclassifies these.

### Suggested fix

Wrap the arg validators so arg-count misuse returns `usageError` (exit 2), matching the sibling commands, and reuse the existing `noArgs` helper for `preview clear`.

title: fix(session): keep terminated status when an open PR remains
body:
Closes #2390.

## What

`deriveStatus`'s terminated branch returned `merged` whenever any owned PR was merged, even when the session still owned an **open** PR. That contradicts the function's documented invariant — *"Merged/closed PRs only matter once no open PR remains"* — and is inconsistent with the non-terminated branch, which gates on `openPRs` before falling back to `anyMerged`.

## Why

Regression from the single-PR → multi-PR change (#230). The branch used to be `if pr != nil && pr.Merged`, which in the single-PR world implied "no open PR remains." Generalizing to `anyMerged(prs)` dropped that implicit condition. A session killed while it still owns an open PR (e.g. only the bottom of a stack merged, or one of two independent PRs merged) was shown as cleanly "merged", hiding the abandoned open PR.

## Change

Gate the merged short-circuit on there being no open PR, mirroring the non-terminated branch:

```go
if len(openPRs(prs)) == 0 && anyMerged(prs) {
    return domain.StatusMerged
}
```

Existing behavior is preserved — a terminated session whose only PR is merged still reports `merged` (the existing `merged-pr` case). Only the `merged + open` combination changes to `terminated`.

## Tests

- Added `terminated-with-open-pr-stays-terminated` to the `deriveStatus` table test. It fails before the change (`got "merged" want "terminated"`) and passes after.
- `go test ./internal/service/session/...` green; full `go test ./...` green apart from the pre-existing Windows-only `TestApplySymlinks`, which needs the symlink privilege and fails on `main` too (unrelated to this change).
- `go vet` and gofmt clean. I couldn't run `go test -race` locally (no 64-bit CGO toolchain on my box) — leaving that to CI.

cc @harshitsinghbhandari — small correctness fix, happy to adjust if you'd rather gate it another way.

title: fix(cli): exit 2 for arg-count misuse on review submit and preview
body:
Closes #2391.

## What

`ao review submit` and `ao preview` (and `ao preview clear`) exited `1` instead of `2` when given too many positional args, breaking the `usageError` → exit-2 convention in AGENTS.md (*"Return usage errors as `usageError` so CLI misuse exits 2; runtime/daemon failures should exit 1."*).

## Why

Their `Args` validators were a bare `cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` / `cobra.NoArgs`. Cobra's arg-count error is a plain error, and the root's `SetFlagErrorFunc` only wraps **flag**-parse errors as `usageError` — not `Args` validation — so `ExitCode` returned 1. Every other command wraps its validator (`noArgs`, `oneSessionIDArg`, the inline wrappers in `project.go` / `completion.go`).

## Change

Wrap the validators so arg-count misuse returns `usageError` (exit 2), and reuse the existing `noArgs` helper for `preview clear`.

## Tests

- Added `TestReviewSubmitTooManyArgsIsUsageError`, `TestPreview_TooManyArgsIsUsageError`, and `TestPreviewClear_TooManyArgsIsUsageError`. Each fails before the change (exit 1) and passes after (exit 2).
- These match the commands' existing usage-error tests, which already assert exit 2 for other misuse.
- `go test ./internal/cli/...` green; `go vet` and gofmt clean.

cc @harshitsinghbhandari — matches the existing usage-error tests on these commands; happy to tweak.

title: release: desktop-release runbook + fix the Prettier CI treadmill
body:
One PR, three related release/CI changes (consolidates #2396 and #2397, now closed):

## 1. `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`: full stable-release runbook
Rewritten from the v0.10.2 cut so anyone can trigger a release: version model (forge names the release `v<frontend/package.json version>`, not the git tag), the tag-only stamp commit recipe, pushing the `desktop-vX.Y.Z` trigger tag, the `release` environment approval gate with the current approver list (@harshitsinghbhandari, @neversettle17-101, @somewherelostt, @Vaibhaav-Tiwari, @Priyanchew) and how to query/approve from the CLI, notes generation, and post-release verification (17 assets, `releases/latest`, updater feed). Also documents that the tag push alone cannot cut a release; the approval gate controls it.

## 2. Format `frontend-nightly.yml` (+1/-1)
The `important` input from #2378 merged with single-quoted YAML that Prettier rewrites. Since the Prettier gate is check-only, main was red and every open PR inherited a failing `format` check for a file it never touched. This was the only tracked file failing `prettier --check .`.

## 3. `prettier.yml`: run on `pull_request`, check only changed files
Root cause of the recurring +1/-1 treadmill: the old `push`-only trigger skipped fork PRs entirely (#2378 had no `format` check at all), and the whole-repo check punished unrelated PRs for rot already on main. Now every PR is checked regardless of origin, and only for the files it changed (NUL-safe diff against the merge base, deleted files excluded, empty diff is a no-op).

**Companion admin change (not YAML):** branch protection on main currently requires zero status checks, so red never blocks a merge. `format`/`test`/`scan` should be made required checks; with the `pull_request` trigger and no path filter, `format` always runs, so requiring it cannot wedge docs-only PRs.

title: security(release): move signing secrets from repo scope to release/nightly environments
body:
## Problem

The six macOS signing secrets (`CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_API_KEY_BASE64`, `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`) are repository-level Actions secrets. The `release` environment (required reviewers: @harshitsinghbhandari, @neversettle17-101, @somewherelostt, @Vaibhaav-Tiwari, @Priyanchew) gates the stable release workflow, but the gate can be bypassed: any write-access user can push a `desktop-v*` tag whose commit edits `frontend-release.yml` to drop the `environment: release` line. The workflow runs from the tagged commit, so it would build ungated and still read the repo-level secrets, producing a fully signed stable release with no approval.

Environment secrets close this: a gate-stripped workflow gets no signing secrets at all.

## Constraint: nightly needs the same secrets

`frontend-nightly.yml` signs macOS builds in two jobs (`release` matrix and `release-intel`) using the same six secrets, runs unattended on a daily cron, and must not require manual approval.

## Plan

Admin steps (AgentWrapper account; secrets cannot be copied, values must be re-entered from the original signing materials):

- [ ] Add the six secrets to the existing `release` environment (Settings > Environments > release). The stable workflow's signing jobs already declare `environment: release`, no YAML change needed.
- [ ] Create a `nightly` environment: **no required reviewers**, deployment branch policy = selected branches, `main` only. Add the same six secrets.
- [ ] While in Settings: confirm `main` blocks direct pushes by write users (the nightly environment trusts code on `main`; its branch policy is the only thing keeping a tampered workflow on another ref away from the secrets).

Repo change:

- [ ] Add `environment: nightly` to the two signing jobs in `frontend-nightly.yml` (small PR, to merge after the environments exist).

Cleanup, only after one nightly and ideally one stable release go green on environment secrets:

- [ ] Delete the six repo-level secrets.

Ordering matters: deleting the repo-level secrets before the environments and YAML are in place makes the next nightly ship unsigned or fail.

## Out of scope (accepted for now)

Any write user can still create a GitHub release directly (`gh release create`) without any workflow; it would be unsigned but becomes `releases/latest`. Restricting `v*`/`desktop-v*` tag creation via rulesets cannot allowlist individual users on a user-owned repo, so this is a trust boundary until the repo moves to an org.

title: ci(prettier): run on pull_request and check only changed files
body:
Kills the recurring +1/-1 formatting-fix-PR treadmill at the source. Two defects in the current `prettier.yml`:

1. **It triggers on branch `push`, not `pull_request`**, so fork PRs get no format check at all. That is how #2378 merged the unformatted nightly workflow: its checks were only `scan` and `test`, `format` never ran.
2. **It checks the whole repo**, so once one unformatted file lands on main, every open PR goes red for a file it never touched (see #2394, red on `frontend-nightly.yml`, a docs-only PR). The wrong people pay for someone else's miss, and the fix is always another +1/-1 PR like #2396 or the gofmt equivalent #2386.

This changes the trigger to `pull_request` (covers same-repo and fork PRs) and checks only the files changed since the merge base (`git diff -z ... | xargs -0 prettier --check --ignore-unknown`, NUL-safe, no-op on empty diff, deleted files excluded). A PR can now only ever be red for its own files, and pre-existing rot on main cannot spread to unrelated PRs.

Verified locally: the changed-files invocation passes on this branch's own diff and is a no-op on an empty diff.

**Companion admin change (not possible in YAML):** none of this blocks a merge while main's branch protection requires zero status checks (`contexts: []` today). To actually end the treadmill, `format` (and `test`/`scan`) should be added as required status checks on main; with the `pull_request` trigger and no path filter, `format` always runs, so requiring it cannot wedge docs-only PRs.

title: SCM multi-PR sessions inject CI/review feedback as low-context single-PR nudges
body:
## Bug
Sessions can now own multiple PRs, including stacked PRs, but SCM lifecycle injection still sends low-context, single-event nudges. When more than one PR in a session has failing CI or review feedback, the agent receives separate messages with generic wording like "your PR" and no PR number/branch context. If one PR has both failing CI and review comments, lifecycle returns after the CI nudge and does not inject the review feedback in the same pass.

**Source:** user report in Codex chat on 2026-07-04
**Analyzed against:** `e74fb65a853f64bc4c8bfec2720cc078b572a3a5`
**Confidence:** High for current behavior; medium for exact product impact without a live multi-PR repro capture.

## Reproduction
1. Create or use a worker session that owns multiple PRs, for example a root PR on `feat/x` and a stacked child PR on `feat/x/auth`.
2. Have more than one PR require attention, such as failing CI on one PR and unresolved human review comments on another.
3. Let the SCM observer poll and lifecycle inject messages into the worker session.
4. Observe that messages are injected per PR with generic wording and no stack/PR context. If a single PR has both failing CI and review comments, only the CI nudge is sent for that lifecycle observation.

## Root Cause
The core SCM/storage/status path is multi-PR aware, but lifecycle injection is still shaped like a single-PR reaction:

- `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go` discovers and persists multiple PRs per session by branch-prefix matching (`discoverNewPRs`) and then calls lifecycle once per observed PR.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:149` handles failing CI first and returns after sending the first failed-check nudge.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:163` handles review feedback only if the CI branch did not return first.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:159` / `:172` dedup by PR URL, so separate PRs can send separate nudges, but the message body does not identify PR number, source/target branch, stack position, or other sibling PR context.
- The observer iterates the observation map, so multiple PR nudges may arrive in nondeterministic order.

This means multiple PRs are tracked correctly in storage/status, but the agent-facing SCM feedback is not composed for a multi-PR session.

## Expected Behavior
For a session with multiple PRs, SCM feedback sent to the agent should be explicit and actionable:

- Include PR number/title/URL and source -> target branch for every CI/review item.
- Batch multiple attention items in a deterministic order, preferably by stack/root and severity.
- If one PR has both failing CI and review comments, include both or send two clearly labeled nudges without one silently suppressing the other.
- Preserve per-PR dedup semantics so already-delivered feedback is not repeated.
- Keep the current suppression for terminated sessions and waiting-input sessions unless the product decision changes.

## Suggested Fix
Introduce a session-level SCM attention composer in lifecycle, or extend the observer/lifecycle handoff so a poll can deliver a deterministic batch of changed PR attention items for a session.

A pragmatic slice:

1. Keep per-PR persistence and semantic hashes unchanged.
2. Build a lifecycle message payload containing all newly changed actionable items for the session: CI failures, unresolved review comments, and merge conflicts.
3. Include PR identity and branch context in each item.
4. Preserve dedup keys per PR/item, but send a single session message when multiple items are new in the same poll.
5. Add regression tests covering:
   - two PRs in one session both need attention;
   - one PR has CI failure and review comments;
   - stack child feedback includes child PR identity;
   - repeated polls do not duplicate already-delivered items.

## Impact
- Agents can receive ambiguous or incomplete instructions in multi-PR sessions.
- Review feedback can be delayed or effectively hidden behind a CI failure for the same PR.
- Stacked PR workflows are harder to recover because feedback lacks PR/branch context.

title: fix(session): export AO_RUN_FILE to spawned sessions so hook delivery finds the spawning daemon
body:
## Root cause

Spawned sessions inherit `AO_DATA_DIR` but not `AO_RUN_FILE`. When the daemon runs with a non-default run file (workspace-local state), every `ao hooks` callback inside a spawned session resolves the default `~/.ao/running.json`, which is stale or absent — hook delivery fails silently: sessions show `no_signal`, and permission dialogs never surface as blocked activity.

## Repro sketch

1. Run AO with workspace-local state using a non-default `AO_RUN_FILE`.
2. Spawn a session that installs AO hooks.
3. Trigger an `ao hooks` callback inside the spawned session.
4. Observe the callback resolving the default `~/.ao/running.json` instead of the spawning daemon's run file; activity stays `no_signal`, and permission dialogs do not surface as blocked activity.

## Fix

Export `AO_RUN_FILE` into the spawn environment alongside `AO_DATA_DIR`, with AO-internal environment variables applied after project env so projects cannot override the run file. If the daemon has no resolved run-file path, omit `AO_RUN_FILE` rather than exporting an empty value.

## Tests

Added/updated session manager provision tests to assert project env cannot override `AO_RUN_FILE` and empty run-file values are omitted.

Validated with:

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go test ./...`

title: bug(lifecycle): a deduped CI-failure nudge starves the review and merge-conflict nudges
bug(scm): UNSTABLE PR wrongly downgraded to `blocked` when CI is failing
body:
### Summary

The SCM observer's mergeability derivation downgrades an `UNSTABLE` PR to `blocked` whenever CI is failing (or changes are requested), even though `UNSTABLE` means the PR *is* mergeable. This contradicts the package's own documented priority order and disagrees with its sibling GraphQL deriver.

### Where

Two byte-identical functions:
- `backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go` — `mergeabilityObservation`
- `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go` — `mergeabilityFromProviderFacts`

Both check `draft` / `ci == failing` / `review` and set `MergeBlocked`, then `return` on blocked — **before** ever reaching the `UNSTABLE` branch at the bottom:

```go
if state == "BLOCKED" { out.State = MergeBlocked; addBlocker("blocked_by_provider") }
if draft { out.State = MergeBlocked; ... }
if ci == CIFailing { out.State = MergeBlocked; addBlocker("ci_failing") }
switch review { ... MergeBlocked ... }
if out.State == MergeBlocked { return out }   // returns here
if state == "UNSTABLE" { out.State = MergeUnstable; return out }   // never reached when CI is failing
```

### Why it's wrong

`doc.go` in the same package spells out the priority (first rule that matches wins):

```
(2) mergeStateStatus == BLOCKED   -> MergeBlocked
(3) mergeStateStatus == UNSTABLE  -> MergeUnstable
(5) reviewDecision == changes_requested -> MergeBlocked
(6) CI == failing                 -> MergeBlocked
```

So `UNSTABLE` (rule 3) must win over changes-requested (5) and CI-failing (6). `UNSTABLE` means the PR is mergeable but has a failing/pending **non-required** check (a *required* failure yields `BLOCKED`). The sibling `mergeabilityFromGraphQL` (`provider.go`) implements the documented order — it switches on `state` first and returns `MergeUnstable` for `UNSTABLE` before consulting CI. The two observer functions don't, and the `UNSTABLE` observer path is untested, which is how the divergence slipped in.

Because an `UNSTABLE` PR's status rollup aggregate is `FAILURE` (→ `ci = failing`), the bottom `UNSTABLE` branch is effectively dead for the common case, and a genuinely mergeable PR is persisted as `Mergeability = blocked`.

### Repro

An optional (non-required) check such as `codecov` fails. GitHub returns `mergeable = MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus = UNSTABLE`, rollup `FAILURE` (→ `ci = failing`), review approved. GitHub still allows the merge, but the observer stores `Mergeability = blocked` with blocker `ci_failing` instead of `Mergeability = unstable`.

### Suggested fix

Move the `UNSTABLE` check above the draft/CI/review blockers in both functions, matching `doc.go` and the GraphQL sibling.

title: bug(agent): grok/devin/continue not marked signal-capable despite installing claude-code hooks
body:
### Summary

The Claude-compat harnesses `grok`, `devin`, and `continue` are reported as **not** signal-capable, so a broken-hook session of one of them is shown a confident `idle` forever instead of `no_signal` — even though they install byte-identical `claude-code` hooks and have a fully working activity pipeline.

### Where

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/dispatch.go`:

```go
func SupportsHarness(h domain.AgentHarness) bool {
    _, ok := Derivers[string(h)]
    return ok
}
```

`SupportsHarness` backs the `SignalCapable` input to status derivation (`daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go` → `service/session/status.go`). If a signal-capable harness stays silent past the 90s `noSignalGrace`, the dashboard shows `no_signal` (a broken hook pipeline); a hook-less harness stays `idle`.

`grok`, `devin`, and `continue` delegate `GetAgentHooks` to the claude-code plugin, installing byte-identical `ao hooks claude-code <evt>` callbacks:

```go
// grok.go / devin.go / continueagent.go
func (p *Plugin) GetAgentHooks(ctx context.Context, cfg ports.WorkspaceHookConfig) error {
    return (&claudecode.Plugin{}).GetAgentHooks(ctx, cfg)
}
```

So they have the same live pipeline as claude-code (routed through the registered `claude-code` deriver at runtime). But their harness *names* aren't keys in `Derivers`, so `SupportsHarness("grok")` / `"devin"` / `"continue"` return false.

### Why it matters

A `grok` session and a `claude-code` session install the same hook bytes, yet only one is treated as signal-capable. If a `grok` session's hooks never fire (broken compat layer, blocked prompt), it should surface `no_signal` like an identical claude-code session — instead it falls through to a confident `idle`, hiding that the session is actually blind.

### Suggested fix

Track the three delegating harnesses in a small set and have `SupportsHarness` consult it, without adding them to the runtime dispatch `Derivers` map (nothing emits `ao hooks grok` — the token they emit at runtime is `claude-code`).

title: fix(lifecycle): stop a deduped CI nudge from starving review/merge-conflict nudges
body:
Closes #2400.

## What

`ApplyPRObservation` drives three independent nudge lanes for a PR (CI failure, review feedback, merge conflict), each with its own dedup key. Each lane did `return m.sendOnce(...)`, but `sendOnce` returned `nil` for **both** a real send and a dedup / attempt-cap no-op. So while a PR's CI stayed failing on the same commit (a normal multi-poll state), the CI lane deduped to a no-op yet still returned — and the review-feedback and merge-conflict lanes below were never reached. A reviewer's "please fix" nudge was silently suppressed for as long as CI was red.

## Change

Make `sendOnce` report whether it actually sent (`(bool, error)`), and have each lane return early only on a real send or an error, falling through to the next lane on a dedup no-op. This preserves the one-nudge-per-tick priority for a *fresh* CI failure while letting independent review/merge-conflict feedback through once the CI nudge is already delivered and deduping. The other `sendOnce` callers ignore the new bool.

## Tests

- Added `TestPRObservation_ReviewNudgeNotStarvedByDedupedCI`: CI fails (nudge #1), then CI unchanged + a new review comment → the review nudge must still fire. Fails before the change (only 1 nudge), passes after.
- `go test ./internal/lifecycle/...` green; `go vet` and gofmt clean.
- I couldn't run `go test -race` locally (no 64-bit CGO toolchain on my box) — leaving that to CI.

cc @harshitsinghbhandari — the independent dedup keys made me read the lanes as intended-independent; happy to adjust if the priority was meant to be strict.

body:
Closes #2402.

## What

`SupportsHarness` backs the `SignalCapable` input to status derivation: a signal-capable harness that goes silent past the 90s `noSignalGrace` is shown `no_signal` (broken hook pipeline), while a hook-less harness stays `idle`. It decided capability by looking the harness name up in `Derivers`.

title: Clarify reviewer targeting for multi-PR sessions
body:
## Summary

AO currently models a worker/agent session as one workspace path and one checked-out worktree, but the session can be associated with multiple PRs. The review flow is intended to use one reviewer per agent session, which means that reviewer may need to review multiple PRs from a single long-lived reviewer pane.

The concern is that a reviewer prompt that says to review the "current checkout" is ambiguous and can be wrong when the session has multiple PRs or when the worktree HEAD no longer matches the PR head being reviewed.

## What we clarified

- A single AO agent session has one primary `SessionMetadata.WorkspacePath` and one active git checkout.
- Git can have many branches, but one worktree can only have one branch/HEAD checked out at a time.
- AO can record multiple PRs against one session, but it does not currently create one worktree per PR.
- PR claim records PR facts and currently does not switch or create checkout state for that PR.
- Therefore, a reviewer assigned the session worktree only sees whatever branch/HEAD is currently checked out in that one worktree.

## Risk

If one agent session creates or owns multiple PRs, a one-reviewer-per-session design can accidentally review the wrong changes if the reviewer relies on `git diff` from the current checkout/HEAD.

Examples:

- PR A and PR B are both associated with the session, but the worktree is currently on PR B's branch. Reviewing PR A via current checkout can inspect PR B instead.
- The session changed branches after opening PR A. AO still has PR A facts, but the worktree HEAD has moved.
- A multi-PR review queue asks one reviewer to review every PR, but only one checkout is available.

## Recommended behavior

For one reviewer per agent session, the reviewer should not mutate or rely on the worker's live checkout to determine the review target.

Preferred default for static review:

- Pass each review task with explicit `PR URL`, `base SHA/ref`, and `head SHA`.
- Instruct the reviewer to review exactly `base...head`.
- Use explicit commands such as:

```bash
git diff <base-sha>...<head-sha>
git log --oneline <base-sha>..<head-sha>
git show <head-sha>:<path>
```

- Do not rely on current checkout HEAD for review identity.

If the reviewer needs to run tests/builds, use reviewer-owned scratch state instead of mutating the agent's live worktree:

- a temporary detached worktree per PR, or
- a reusable reviewer scratch worktree that AO resets to each PR head.

## Why this is acceptable

Using explicit refs/diffs should not materially increase token usage. The main token cost is the diff and files the reviewer chooses to inspect. Passing base/head identifiers and using `git diff <base>...<head>` adds little overhead while avoiding wrong-branch reviews.

## Suggested fixes/tests

- Update reviewer prompt(s) to include the exact workspace path and explicit base/head review target.
- Tell reviewers not to rely on current checkout HEAD for PR identity.
- Add a guard or preflight that verifies the target head SHA is available locally, fetching PR refs if needed.
- For multi-PR queues, require review per explicit base/head pair rather than per current checkout.
- Add tests covering:
  - one session with multiple PRs and one workspace;
  - review prompt includes explicit base/head instructions;
  - reviewer launch/reuse does not imply current checkout equals target PR;
  - stale worktree HEAD differing from PR head is detected or avoided.

## Relevant code areas

- `backend/internal/domain/session.go` - session metadata has one workspace path.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` - spawn creates one workspace and stores it on the session.
- `backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go` - PR claim records PR facts and notes checkout switching is not implemented.
- `backend/internal/review/review.go` - review trigger queues all eligible PRs for the worker session.
- `backend/internal/review/launcher.go` - reviewer launch uses the worker session workspace path.
- `backend/internal/review/prompt.go` - prompt currently frames review around the current checkout.

title: feat(cli): context-aware agent spawn with agent catalog and auth preflight
body:
Summary

This branch adds a CLI-facing agent catalog command and makes ao spawn more context-aware for direct shell usage. The main goal is to let users start worker sessions without always passing every low-level flag, while still keeping the CLI thin and daemon-backed.

What Changed

Added ao agent ls

New command:

ao agent ls
ao agent ls --refresh
ao agent ls --json

Behavior:

  • ao agent ls calls GET /api/v1/agents.
  • ao agent ls --refresh calls POST /api/v1/agents/refresh.
  • ao agent ls --json prints the raw agent inventory response.
  • Table output shows supported agents with install/auth status:
    • authorized
    • auth unknown
    • needs auth
    • needs install

No new backend API was added — this reuses the existing agent catalog endpoints.

Made ao spawn context-aware

ao spawn no longer requires --project, --agent, and --name in every direct CLI invocation.

Supported paths now include:

ao spawn --prompt "Fix failing tests"
ao spawn --agent codex --prompt "Fix failing tests"

Project resolution order:

  1. Explicit --project
  2. AO_PROJECT_ID
  3. Current working directory matched against registered project paths
  4. Otherwise, returns a helpful setup error

Agent resolution order:

  1. Explicit --agent / --harness
  2. Resolved project config worker.agent
  3. Otherwise, returns a helpful config error

Display name behavior:

  • Explicit --name still works and is still capped at 20 characters.
  • If --name is omitted, the CLI derives a short display name from --prompt.
  • If neither name nor prompt gives a name, the CLI omits displayName and lets the API/UI fall back to session id.

Added spawn auth preflight

Before calling POST /api/v1/sessions, ao spawn now checks the agent catalog:

State | Behavior -- | -- Cached catalog shows authorized | Spawn proceeds without refresh Cached catalog can't confirm auth | Refreshes catalog once Refreshed status is unauthorized | Spawn blocked with a clear auth error Auth remains unknown after refresh | CLI warns and proceeds

Spawn remains the final authority for runtime/binary/model failures.

Updated docs

Updated CLI documentation to cover:

  • ao agent ls, ao agent ls --refresh, ao agent ls --json
  • Direct shell usage requirements
  • Daemon requirement for product commands
  • Source checkout build/run example
  • ao spawn project resolution behavior
  • ao spawn default worker.agent behavior
  • Auth preflight behavior

The root README now links to the CLI guide instead of duplicating detailed command instructions.

Files Changed

Main implementation:

  • backend/internal/cli/agent.go
  • backend/internal/cli/root.go
  • backend/internal/cli/spawn.go

Tests:

  • backend/internal/cli/agent_test.go
  • backend/internal/cli/spawn_test.go
  • backend/internal/cli/dto_drift_e2e_test.go

Docs:

  • README.md
  • docs/cli/README.md

Passed:

npm run lint
npm run frontend:typecheck

Manually verified with the local built binary:

./bin/ao agent ls
./bin/ao agent ls --refresh
./bin/ao agent ls --json

  • No OpenAPI regeneration was needed.
  • The CLI remains a thin client over daemon HTTP routes.
  • An unrelated generated frontend route tree change was removed from the branch diff.

title: feat(session): switch a session's agent mid-flight
body:
## What & why

A session's agent (`harness`) is currently fixed at spawn (`SessionRecord.Harness`, resolved once by `effectiveHarness` in `session_manager`) and can never change. Mixing agents on a single task — e.g. **codex** to test, **claude-code** to write, a cheaper model for cost — is impossible without throwing the work away and respawning.

This PR lets you **change a session's agent in place**, keeping the same git worktree (all code + uncommitted work preserved). The new agent launches **fresh** — there is no native resume, since a different harness cannot read the outgoing agent's session. An optional `model` override rides the same path.

## Behaviour

Two cases are handled:

- **Live session → swap in place.** The old agent is torn down only *after* the new launch command validates, so a bad/unknown harness never disrupts the running session. A `BeginSwitch`/`EndSwitch` guard on the lifecycle manager makes the reaper ignore the brief window where the old runtime is gone and the new one isn't up yet — otherwise a "dead" probe would wrongly terminate the session mid-switch.
- **Terminated session → relaunch-as.** When an agent exits (e.g. codex ends its process on completion) the session is marked terminated. Switching such a session restores its worktree and launches the chosen agent fresh under it — the way to bring a finished task back under a *different* agent (plain restore keeps the original harness). Only fully `merged` sessions stay locked.

`lifecycle.MarkSwitched` atomically changes the persisted harness, points at the new runtime handle, and **clears the harness-specific `AgentSessionID`** (which `MarkSpawned`'s metadata merge cannot, since it only sets non-empty fields), resetting activity/first-signal so the new agent re-proves its hook pipeline.

## Surfaces

- **Backend:** `sessionmanager.SwitchHarness` (live + terminated paths) and `lifecycle` guard + `MarkSwitched`.
- **API:** `POST /sessions/{id}/switch` `{harness, model?}` — `400` unknown harness, `404` unknown session, `409` switch-in-progress. OpenAPI spec + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated (pinned `openapi-typescript@7.4.4`).
- **CLI:** `ao session switch <id> --harness <agent> [--model ...]`.
- **UI:** the session inspector's **Overview → Agent** row is now a dropdown that switches the agent in place (or relaunches a terminated one), built from the existing `dropdown-menu` primitive and `AGENT_OPTIONS`; `merged` sessions stay read-only.

## Tests

- live swap clears `AgentSessionID`
- unknown harness leaves the running agent untouched (validate-before-destroy)
- terminated session relaunches under the new agent (restore-as)
- create-failure terminates cleanly (no live-session-with-dead-handle)
- reaper guard suppresses termination during a switch
- `MarkSwitched` changes harness, clears `AgentSessionID`, resets first-signal

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, the full backend `go test ./...`, and frontend `tsc` all pass.

## Notes / follow-ups

- No migration: the `harness` column and `UpdateSession` already exist.
- The target agent's CLI must be installed on PATH — the existing pre-flight binary check rejects otherwise, surfaced inline in the UI.
- Context handoff (carrying the outgoing agent's transcript into the new one) is intentionally out of scope; this leaves a clean seam (the fresh launch's prompt) for it.

title: fix(skills): using-ao skill embedded in daemon but invisible to opencode's skill tool
body:
## Summary

The `using-ao` skill (PR #2365) is correctly embedded in the daemon binary via `go:embed` and installed to `~/.ao/data/skills/using-ao/` at daemon boot. However, it remains invisible to **opencode's** `skill` tool because it is never registered in opencode's skill-discovery mechanism. The two skill systems — AO daemon and opencode — are completely disconnected.

## The two skill systems

| | AO daemon skill system | Opencode skill system |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Give LLM agents (Claude Code, Grok, etc.) a CLI catalog for the `ao` CLI | Give the opencode agent a loadable skill with structured instructions |
| **Discovery** | Hardcoded absolute path in `session_manager/manager.go:aoSkillPointer()` (appended to every spawned agent's system prompt) | `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode/` dir, repo-root `skills/` dir, `~/.config/opencode/` |
| **Skill location** | `~/.ao/data/skills/using-ao/` | `~/.config/opencode/skills/`, repo-root `skills/*/`, `.opencode/skills/` |
| **How agent accesses it** | Agent reads the markdown files at the absolute path when told to in its system prompt | Agent loads it via the `skill` tool (appears in `<available_skills>` block) |

## How to reproduce

1. Build and start the daemon:
   ```bash
   cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao ./cmd/ao && /tmp/ao start
   ```

2. Verify the skill is installed on disk:
   ```bash
   ls ~/.ao/data/skills/using-ao/SKILL.md
   # -> SKILL.md, references.md, commands/ present

   /tmp/ao status
   # -> daemon ready, data dir: ~/.ao/data
   ```

3. Open an opencode session in the repo and inspect available skills via the `skill` tool. Only `customize-opencode` is listed. The `using-ao` skill never appears.

## Root cause

At `backend/internal/skillassets/skillassets.go:23`, the skill is embedded and installed to `<dataDir>/skills/using-ao/`. At `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:1063-1068`, the system prompt builder appends an absolute-path pointer so that AO-spawned agents can read the markdown files. **This is the only consumption path.** There is no code, config entry, symlink, or plugin registration that makes the skill visible to opencode's `skill` tool.

The `ao-activity.ts` plugin (`.opencode/plugins/ao-activity.ts`) is a **one-way bridge**: it maps opencode lifecycle events (`session.created`, `message.updated`, `session.status`) into `ao hooks opencode` commands. It has no reciprocal mechanism to register AO-hosted skills in opencode's skill registry.

## Suggested fixes

### Option A (minimal) — Register skill in opencode config

Add a project-level `opencode.json` (or update the existing `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`) with a `skills` entry pointing at the installed path:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "skills": [
    {
      "name": "using-ao",
      "description": "Catalog of the AO (Agent Orchestrator) `ao` CLI",
      "location": "~/.ao/data/skills/using-ao"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Option B — Plugin registration

Extend `ao-activity.ts` to register the skill at plugin load time via opencode's plugin API. Keeps registration colocated with the existing opencode integration.

### Option C — Symlink from opencode-recognized directory

Have `skillassets.Install()` create a symlink:

```go
link := filepath.Join(os.Getenv("HOME"), ".config", "opencode", "skills", "using-ao")
target := filepath.Join(dataDir, "skills", "using-ao")
os.Symlink(target, link)
```

Opencode scans `~/.config/opencode/skills/` automatically. No config changes needed but couples the daemon to opencode's config path.

### Option D — Inline skill into repo-root `skills/`

Place a `using-ao` skill directory in the repo-root `skills/` alongside `bug-triage/`. Opencode scans repo-root `skills/*/` and registers matching directories as loadable skills. Decouples from daemon embed but introduces drift risk.

### Option E — Daemon endpoint for skills

Expose a daemon HTTP endpoint (`GET /api/v1/skills/using-ao`) that returns the skill content. The opencode plugin fetches it at load time. Keeps the daemon as single source of truth.

## Related

- PR #2365 — original implementation embedding the skill and wiring it into session prompts
- `.opencode/plugins/ao-activity.ts` — existing opencode plugin (lifecycle bridge, one-way only)

title: Bug: Windows installer creates broken Start menu shortcut (wrong exe name + missing icon) — app silently fails to launch
body:
## Bug: Windows installer creates broken Start menu shortcut — silent launch failure

### Summary
The Windows installer (`Agent.Orchestrator.Setup.0.10.2.exe`) creates a Start menu shortcut pointing to `Agent Orchestrator.exe` (with spaces), but the actual installed binary is `agent-orchestrator.exe` (lowercase, hyphenated). This causes **silent launch failure** — clicking the Start menu icon does nothing, no error, no window.

Additionally, the shortcut has no `IconLocation` set, so the Start menu shows a generic Windows document icon instead of the AO robot icon (even though the exe has the icon embedded correctly).

### Environment
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **AO Version:** v0.10.2
- **Installer:** `Agent.Orchestrator.Setup.0.10.2.exe`

### Reproduction Steps
1. Download and run `Agent.Orchestrator.Setup.0.10.2.exe` on Windows
2. Complete installation
3. Click "Agent Orchestrator" from the Start menu
4. **Nothing happens** — no window, no error, no process

### Root Cause

**1. Filename mismatch in shortcut:**
- Shortcut `TargetPath`: `...\Agent Orchestrator\Agent Orchestrator.exe` ❌ (does not exist)
- Actual binary: `...\Agent Orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe` ✅

**2. Missing icon:**
- Shortcut `IconLocation` is empty
- The actual `agent-orchestrator.exe` has the icon embedded correctly

### Evidence
Confirmed by user Deepak Modi on Discord:
```
PS> $resolved = (New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell).CreateShortcut("...\Agent Orchestrator.lnk").TargetPath
C:\Users\deepa\AppData\Local\Programs\Agent Orchestrator\Agent Orchestrator.exe

PS> & "...\Agent Orchestrator.exe"
# Error: not recognized

PS> Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Agent Orchestrator"
# Shows: agent-orchestrator.exe (not "Agent Orchestrator.exe")
```

### Workaround (for affected users)
```powershell
$ws = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell
$lnk = $ws.CreateShortcut("$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Agent Orchestrator.lnk")
$lnk.TargetPath = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Agent Orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe"
$lnk.IconLocation = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Agent Orchestrator\agent-orchestrator.exe,0"
$lnk.Save()

taskkill /f /im explorer.exe
Remove-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\IconCache.db" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer\iconcache*" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Start-Process explorer.exe
```

### Suggested Fix
The Electron Forge / electron-builder config should ensure:
1. The shortcut `TargetPath` matches the actual binary name (`agent-orchestrator.exe`, not `Agent Orchestrator.exe`)
2. The shortcut `IconLocation` is explicitly set

Affects **every Windows user** on a fresh install of v0.10.2.

Reported by: Deepak Modi (@deepakmodidev)

title: bug(cli): wrong exit code on too many args for review submit and preview
body:
I'd like to work on this — planning a small CLI-only fix.

**Scope:** `backend/internal/cli/` only — wrap arg-count validators for `ao review submit` and `ao preview` (including `ao preview clear`) so misuse returns `usageError` and exits **2**, matching `AGENTS.md` and the rest of the CLI.

**Approach:**
- Add/reuse an `atMostOneArg` helper (same pattern as `noArgs` in `root.go`)
- Wire it into `review submit` and `preview`
- Use `noArgs` for `preview clear` instead of bare `cobra.NoArgs`
- Add table tests asserting exit code 2 for too-many-args cases

No daemon/API/OpenAPI changes. I'll open a PR once tests pass locally.
```

---

## Issue description (full body)

### Summary

`AGENTS.md` documents a CLI convention: **usage errors exit 2; runtime/daemon failures exit 1**. Two commands break that convention for **argument-count misuse** — they exit **1** instead of **2** when too many positional args are passed.

Affected commands:

- `ao review submit`
- `ao preview`
- `ao preview clear`

### Expected behavior

When a user passes the wrong number of positional arguments, the process should exit **2** (usage error), consistent with other commands like `ao session get`, `ao completion`, and `ao project add`.

### Actual behavior

Passing too many args exits **1** (generic failure), which misleads scripts and wrappers that distinguish usage misuse from daemon/runtime errors.

### Reproduction

```bash
$ ao review submit mer-1 mer-2
Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
$ echo $?
1   # expected 2

$ ao preview http://localhost:5173 extra
Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
$ echo $?
1   # expected 2

$ ao preview clear extra
Error: unknown command "extra" for "ao preview clear"
# (or similar arg-count error — should exit 2, not 1)
$ echo $?
1   # expected 2
```

### Root cause

In `backend/internal/cli/`:

| File        | Current validator                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `review.go` | `Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` on `review submit` |
| `preview.go`| `Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` on `preview`       |
| `preview.go`| `Args: cobra.NoArgs` on `preview clear`          |

Cobra's built-in arg validators return plain `errors.New(...)`. The root command's `SetFlagErrorFunc` only wraps **flag** parse errors as `usageError`, not **Args** validation errors. So arg-count failures are not recognized as usage errors and `ExitCode()` returns **1**.

Other commands already follow the correct pattern — they wrap Cobra validators so misuse becomes `usageError`:

- `noArgs` in `root.go` (used by `ao start`, `ao stop`, etc.)
- `oneSessionIDArg`, `sessionRenameArgs` in `session.go`
- Inline wrappers in `project.go`, `completion.go`

Existing tests for these commands already assert exit **2** for other usage errors (e.g. `TestReviewSubmitMissingVerdictIsUsageError`, `TestPreview_MissingSessionIDIsUsageError`), but **no test covers arg-count misuse** for review/preview.

### Proposed fix (CLI-only)

1. Add a shared helper in `root.go`:

   ```go
   func atMostOneArg(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
       if err := cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)(cmd, args); err != nil {
           return usageError{err}
       }
       return nil
   }
   ```

2. Use `atMostOneArg` for `review submit` and `preview`.
3. Use existing `noArgs` for `preview clear` instead of `cobra.NoArgs`.
4. Add tests:
   - `TestReviewSubmitTooManyArgsIsUsageError`
   - `TestPreview_TooManyArgsIsUsageError`
   - `TestPreviewClear_TooManyArgsIsUsageError`

### Out of scope

- No daemon, HTTP, SQLite, or OpenAPI changes
- No new CLI commands or flags
- No changes to flag-validation paths (those already work)

### Test plan

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestReviewSubmit|TestPreview' -count=1
go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1
```

Manual smoke:

```bash
ao review submit a b; echo $?    # should print 2
ao preview a b; echo $?          # should print 2
ao preview clear x; echo $?      # should print 2
```

### References

- Contributor convention: [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) — *"Return usage errors as usageError so CLI misuse exits 2"*
- Exit code mapping: `backend/internal/cli/root.go` — `usageError` + `ExitCode()`
- Prior art: `noArgs`, `oneSessionIDArg`, `completion.go` arg wrapper

---

## Files to change

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `backend/internal/cli/root.go` | Add `atMostOneArg` helper |
| `backend/internal/cli/review.go` | `Args: atMostOneArg` on `review submit` |
| `backend/internal/cli/preview.go` | `Args: atMostOneArg` on `preview`; `Args: noArgs` on `preview clear` |
| `backend/internal/cli/review_test.go` | `TestReviewSubmitTooManyArgsIsUsageError` |
| `backend/internal/cli/preview_test.go` | `TestPreview_TooManyArgsIsUsageError`, `TestPreviewClear_TooManyArgsIsUsageError` |

---

title: fix(desktop): opencode wheel scroll + native Windows notifications
body:
Two Windows-surfaced desktop bugs, both from the renderer/Electron layer not
accounting for how the pane app or the OS actually behaves. No tracking issue —
this PR is the writeup.

## 1. Scrolling does nothing in opencode sessions

**Symptom:** in an opencode session you cannot scroll the transcript with the mouse
wheel. PageUp/PageDown work; the wheel does nothing.

**Cause:** the terminal keeps no local scrollback (`scrollback: 0`) and converts
wheel motion into SGR mouse-wheel reports written to the pane. Those only scroll an
app that acts on wheel reports — tmux/zellij copy-mode, or a mouse-driven TUI.
opencode enables mouse tracking (`mouseTrackingMode: "any"`) but scrolls its own
transcript **only by keyboard**, so it silently ignores the wheel reports. On
Windows there is no mux (conpty) to fall back to at all, so nothing scrolls.

**Fix:** the wheel handler now sends **PageUp/PageDown** instead of SGR reports when
the pane can't use them:
- for keyboard-scroll agents (`paneScrollsByKeyboard`, currently `opencode`) on
  every platform,
- on Windows (conpty has no copy-mode, so SGR never helps), and
- for any pane app with mouse tracking fully off.

Every other agent keeps the SGR path, so tmux/zellij copy-mode scrolling on
macOS/Linux is unchanged. Video below shows opencode scrolling on the wheel.

## 2. Native notifications never appear on Windows

**Symptom:** no notification toast ever pops on Windows, even though the in-app bell
and unread badge update correctly.

**Cause:** `Notification.isSupported()` returns true and `show()` runs without
error, but Windows silently drops every toast because the app never declared an
AppUserModelID matching its installer shortcut — a required step for Windows toasts.

**Fix:** call `app.setAppUserModelId("dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop")` (the NSIS
maker's appId) on Windows, before the notification code. No-op on macOS/Linux.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run` (frontend gate) — terminal suite 30/30, incl. new cases: page
  keys on Windows with `mouseTrackingMode: "any"`, and page keys for a
  keyboard-scroll agent under a mux.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Wheel scroll verified live in an opencode session on Windows (video attached).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ecc3c2d-f5f0-4917-8309-9cd520d361fd


## Caveats

- The macOS/Linux opencode wheel path is routed by agent type and is deterministic
  (opencode scrolls on PageUp; tmux forwards plain keystrokes untouched), but I
  could not test it on those platforms — flagging for a reviewer with a Mac/Linux
  box. Trivially revertible: drop `opencode` from `KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS`.
- The notification fix applies to installed/packaged builds; an unpackaged
  `npm run dev` on Windows may still not toast (no installer shortcut carrying the
  AUMID).

## Files

- `frontend/src/main.ts` — Windows AppUserModelID
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` — wheel → page-key routing + `paneScrollsByKeyboard`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` — pass the agent's keyboard-scroll hint
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — coverage…ndows notifications

title: fix(browser): remove excess padding around the inspector browser tab
body:
The inspector rail's Browser tab renders inside `.session-inspector__body`, which applies `18px` padding to every tab. That's correct for the Summary and Reviews tabs, but on the Browser tab it insets the whole preview panel, leaving a visible gap between the terminal (resize handle) and the browser. The panel's own `1px` border and `8px` radius add to the effect.

This drops the body padding and the panel border/radius when the Browser tab is active (and not popped out), so the preview sits flush against the resize handle. The native WebContentsView re-measures from the slot box automatically, so it grows to fill the reclaimed space with no JS change.

The padding removal uses a two-class selector so the narrow-width container query that re-adds inline padding can't override it.

title: bug(desktop): sidebar cannot fully expand/collapse from resized near-collapsed state
body:
## Summary

The desktop sidebar can be collapsed/expanded by clicking the header collapse icon when the sidebar is in its normal expanded width. However, after resizing/dragging the sidebar down to a very narrow, almost-hidden state, the same complete expand/collapse behavior is not available/reliable. Users should be able to fully collapse and fully expand the sidebar from that state too.

## Current behavior

- In the normal expanded sidebar, clicking the collapse icon in the brand/header row collapses/expands the sidebar.
- The sidebar also has a drag resize handle on the right edge.
- When the sidebar is resized down to a very narrow width, the UI appears visually compressed/near-collapsed, but the full collapse/expand affordance does not work the same way as the header icon path.
- The user has to rely on the header collapse icon while the sidebar is sufficiently expanded.

## Expected behavior

- The sidebar should support complete collapse and complete expand consistently from all desktop sidebar states:
  - normal expanded width
  - manually resized narrow width
  - icon/collapsed rail state
- If the resize handle/rail is used to reach a near-collapsed width, the user should still have a clear and working affordance to fully collapse or expand the sidebar.
- The persisted sidebar width should not trap the UI in a narrow intermediate state that behaves differently from the actual collapsed state.

## Repro steps

1. Run the Electron desktop app on Windows.
2. Open the main board with the project sidebar visible.
3. Confirm the brand/header collapse icon toggles the sidebar when it is expanded.
4. Drag the sidebar resize edge left until the sidebar is very narrow/nearly hidden.
5. Try to fully collapse and expand the sidebar from that state.

## Screenshots / user report

User supplied screenshots showing:

1. Expanded sidebar with the header collapse icon visible.
2. Close-up of the working collapse icon in the header row.
3. Sidebar manually resized to a very narrow state where complete expand/collapse should also work.

## Likely files

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/sidebar.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx`

Relevant local observations:

- `Sidebar.tsx` uses shadcn sidebar state (`expanded` / `collapsed`) and a separate resizable width CSS var (`--ao-sidebar-w`).
- The resize handle is hidden in `group-data-[collapsible=icon]`, but narrow resized widths can still visually approximate a collapsed state without necessarily using the sidebar collapsed state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sidebar has a working complete collapse/expand path from a manually resized narrow width.
- [ ] Header collapse icon behavior and resize-handle behavior stay in sync with the actual sidebar state.
- [ ] Persisted `ao-sidebar-w` values are clamped or reset so users cannot get trapped in a bad intermediate width.
- [ ] Keyboard shortcut behavior (`Cmd/Ctrl+B`, if supported on the platform) remains consistent.
- [ ] Add or update `Sidebar.test.tsx` coverage for narrow resized width -> full collapse/expand.

title: fix(sidebar): New Project tooltip opens upward instead of rightward when sidebar is collapsed
body: ## Bug In the collapsed (icon-only) sidebar, every rail tooltip (Settings, Expand sidebar, daemon status, project rows via `SidebarMenuButton`) opens to the right (`side="right"`) since the icons sit flush against the left edge of the window. The "+ New Project" icon is the one exception: its tooltip pops upward (`side="top"`, Radix's default) instead, which looks inconsistent with the rest of the collapsed rail and can visually clip near the top of the sidebar. **Additional UX friction:** because the tooltip opens upward directly over the icon row, it partially covers/blocks the project icon sitting immediately above "+" in the collapsed rail (see "Current" screenshot below) — while the tooltip is showing, that icon is harder to see and click, forcing the user to wait for the tooltip to dismiss before targeting it. Opening the tooltip to the right (matching every other rail icon) removes this overlap entirely. **Source:** internal review of `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx` | **Analyzed against:** `821cda64` **Confidence:** High ## Reproduction 1. Run the desktop app and collapse the sidebar (⌘B / the collapse toggle). 2. Hover the "+" (New Project) icon at the bottom of the collapsed icon rail. 3. Observe the tooltip opens above the icon, while hovering Settings or the daemon status dot opens tooltips to the right. ## Screenshots **Current (buggy):** tooltip opens upward (`side="top"`), overlapping/blocking the project icon directly above the "+" — hard to access while the tooltip is visible. **Proposed (fixed):** tooltip opens to the right (`side="right"`), matching every other collapsed-rail icon (Settings, Expand sidebar, daemon status) and no longer blocking adjacent icons. ## Root Cause There are two separate components backing "+ New Project", not one component restyled via `group-data-[collapsible=icon]` like other rows: - Expanded state: `CreateProjectButton` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:711-732`), mounted at `Sidebar.tsx:242`. - Collapsed state: `CreateProjectListItem` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:734-757`), mounted only when collapsed at `Sidebar.tsx:271` (`{isCollapsed && }`). Both hand-roll their own `...{label}` (`Sidebar.tsx:727` and `Sidebar.tsx:751`) instead of using `SidebarMenuButton`'s built-in `tooltip` prop (which internally sets `side="right"` and `hidden={state !== "collapsed"}`, see `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:502-506`). Neither passes a `side` prop, so both fall back to Radix's default `side="top"` — unlike the other manually-wired collapsed-rail icons (Settings `Sidebar.tsx:358`, Expand sidebar `Sidebar.tsx:393`, daemon status `Sidebar.tsx:205`) which explicitly set `side="right"`. ## Fix Add `side="right"` to the `TooltipContent` in `CreateProjectListItem` (`Sidebar.tsx:751`), matching the convention used by the other collapsed-rail icons. The expanded-state `CreateProjectButton` tooltip (`Sidebar.tsx:727`) is unaffected since that button isn't in the collapsed icon rail. ## Impact - UX friction: tooltip overlap makes the icon above "+ New Project" harder to see/click while hovering, in addition to the visual inconsistency. - Affects: Electron/React sidebar in `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx`, collapsed sidebar state only. **Priority:** low (cosmetic + minor UX friction, no data/functional impact, no matching label exists so stating in body)

title: fix(sidebar): open New Project tooltip rightward when collapsed
body: Fixes #2430 ## Summary - In the collapsed (icon-only) sidebar, every other rail tooltip (Settings, Expand sidebar, daemon status, project rows) opens `side="right"` since the icons sit flush against the left edge. The "+ New Project" icon was the one exception, hand-rolling its own `Tooltip`/`TooltipContent` without a `side` prop and falling back to Radix's default `side="top"`. - Adds `side="right"` to `CreateProjectListItem`'s `TooltipContent` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx`), matching the convention used by the other collapsed-rail icons. - The expanded-state `CreateProjectButton` tooltip is untouched since that button isn't part of the collapsed icon rail. ## Screenshots **Current (buggy):** tooltip opens upward (`side="top"`), overlapping/blocking the project icon directly above the "+" — hard to access while the tooltip is visible. **Proposed (fixed):** tooltip opens to the right (`side="right"`), matching every other collapsed-rail icon (Settings, Expand sidebar, daemon status) and no longer blocking adjacent icons. ## Test - `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — passes. - Manually verified via code inspection against the sibling components (`Sidebar.tsx:205`, `338`, `358`, `393`) that use `side="right"`/`side="top"` explicitly for the collapsed rail.

title: feat(frontend): replace empty board shells with first-run onboarding states
body: ## Problem First launch drops users into the full app shell — four empty kanban columns, an empty sidebar, and zero orientation ([onboarding audit, finding #1, high severity](https://illegalcall.github.io/ao-onboarding-audit/)). Core vocabulary (orchestrator, worker, the four columns) is never defined in-app (findings #2/#4). ## What this does **Global board (`/`) with no projects** — replaces the empty column shells with a centered welcome: what the app does in one sentence, a three-step card (Add a project → Describe a task → Review and merge), and a primary **Add your first project** CTA. Step 3 ends with the four column dots in their exact board colors/styles, so the kanban vocabulary is taught before the columns ever render. The CTA drives the same folder-picker → agent-sheet flow as the sidebar's `+` (shared `CreateProjectFlow`, extracted verbatim from `Sidebar.tsx`). **Project board with no sessions** — a smaller centered "No sessions yet" invitation with the header's Orchestrator (primary) / New task actions, instead of four zeros. title: fix(web): terminal doesn't get keyboard focus when opening a session/agent view
body:
## Bug

When opening a terminal view — clicking an agent from the Kanban board, selecting an orchestrator session, or otherwise navigating into a session's terminal — the xterm.js terminal never receives keyboard focus. The user has to manually click inside the terminal pane before typing does anything.

**Analyzed against:** `860fa5a2` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High — traced exact code path, root cause confirmed by absence of any `.focus()` call.

## Root Cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` owns the real `Terminal` instance (`term`) from `@xterm/xterm`, which has a built-in `term.focus()` method — but nothing in this file ever calls it.
- The handle object it exposes outward, `AttachableTerminal` (defined in `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.ts`), only exposes `cols`, `rows`, `write`, `writeln`, `clear`, `onUserInput`, `onResize` — no `focus` method, so callers have no way to trigger it even if they wanted to.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx`'s `AttachedTerminal` keys the terminal by `terminalHandleId` (`key={terminalKey}`), so React fully remounts `XtermTerminal` (destroy + recreate the xterm.js instance) on every session switch — giving a natural, reliable "just opened" moment via the mount effect, which currently does nothing focus-related.

## Screen Recording

[![Screen Recording](https://img.youtube.com/vi/zBYWUGjXw6I/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/zBYWUGjXw6I)

## Fix

1. Add `focus: () => term.focus()` to the `AttachableTerminal` handle object built in `XtermTerminal.tsx` — exposes the capability (mechanism), without deciding when to use it.
2. Add `focus: () => void` to the `AttachableTerminal` type in `useTerminalSession.ts`.
3. Call `terminal.focus()` in `TerminalPane.tsx`'s existing mount effect (in `AttachedTerminal`), gated on `handleId` being present — `TerminalPane` is the layer that knows whether a session/handle is actually attached (`showEmptyState = !handleId`), so it decides *when* to focus (policy), rather than `XtermTerminal` focusing unconditionally on every mount, which would also steal focus onto the empty-state pane (no session selected).

## Impact

- Low severity, high friction: every session/agent switch currently requires an extra click before the user can type, on every navigation.

title: fix(web): auto-focus terminal when opening a session/agent view
body:
Fixes #2434

## Summary
- Add `focus: () => term.focus()` to the `AttachableTerminal` handle in `XtermTerminal.tsx`, wiring through xterm.js's built-in focus method. `XtermTerminal` only exposes the *mechanism* — it has no knowledge of sessions or when focusing makes sense.
- Add `focus: () => void` to the `AttachableTerminal` type in `useTerminalSession.ts` (and a no-op stub on the test's fake terminal to satisfy the now-required field).
- Call `terminal.focus()` in `TerminalPane.tsx`'s existing mount effect, gated on `handleId` (`if (handleId) terminal.focus()`), right after clearing and before `attach(terminal)`. `TerminalPane` owns the *policy* of when to focus, since it's the layer that knows whether there's an actual session/handle attached (`showEmptyState = !handleId`) — without the gate, the terminal would steal keyboard focus even on the empty-state pane ("No session selected"), which always mounts `XtermTerminal` regardless of whether a session is picked.

Since `TerminalPane` keys `AttachedTerminal` by `terminalHandleId`, every session/agent switch already forces a full remount of `XtermTerminal` — so this effect fires exactly once per fresh terminal view, giving a reliable "user just opened a live terminal" hook with no extra plumbing.

## Screen Recording
[![Screen Recording](https://img.youtube.com/vi/zBYWUGjXw6I/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/zBYWUGjXw6I)

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes
- [x] `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.test.tsx` — 17/17 pass
- [ ] Manual: open a session from Kanban / switch between agent sessions and confirm typing works immediately without an extra click; confirm the empty-state pane (no session selected) does not steal focus

title: Kiro orchestrator launches without input and exits in non-interactive mode
body:
## Summary

  Selecting `kiro` as the orchestrator agent starts a Kiro terminal, but it immediately exits with:

  ```text
  error: Input must be supplied when running in non-interactive mode

  ## Repro

  1. Configure a project with Kiro as the orchestrator agent.
  2. Open/select the orchestrator session.
  3. Observe the terminal output.

  ## Actual Behavior

  AO appears to launch Kiro in headless mode without a prompt:

  kiro-cli chat --no-interactive

  Kiro requires input in non-interactive mode, so it exits.

  ## Expected Behavior

  Either:

  1. Kiro should not be selectable as an orchestrator agent if AO cannot provide valid orchestrator input, or
  2. AO should launch Kiro with valid input for orchestrator sessions, likely by passing the derived orchestrator system prompt when the normal task prompt is empty.

  ## Notes

  Kiro worker sessions with a task prompt should still work because AO launches them like:

  kiro-cli chat --no-interactive -- "<prompt>"

  The issue is specific to promptless orchestrator sessions. AO currently treats orchestrators as promptless and relies on the agent adapter/system prompt path, but the Kiro adapter only appends cfg.Prompt to the command.
