title: Amp worker launches with -x execute mode instead of interactive TUI
body:
## Problem

  Amp workers spawned by AO do not open the interactive TUI when the worker has an initial prompt.

  The Amp adapter currently builds prompted launch commands as:

  ```bash
  amp -x "<prompt>"

  ```
  See:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp_test.go

  -x appears to be Amp execute mode, so AO gets a non-interactive execution path instead of the normal terminal UI. This makes
  Amp behave differently from TUI-first adapters like Kimi and Cline.

  ## Expected Behavior

  AO should launch Amp workers interactively:

  amp

  Then AO should deliver the initial worker prompt after startup through the runtime pane/tmux, same as other TUI-first
  adapters.

  ## Actual Behavior

  AO launches prompted Amp workers as:
 ```
  amp -x "<prompt>"
  ```

  This prevents the Amp TUI from opening reliably and can result in the process streaming output or exiting instead of staying
  attached as an interactive worker.

  ## Likely Fix

  Update the Amp adapter to:

  1. Launch amp without -x, even when LaunchConfig.Prompt is present.
  2. Override GetPromptDeliveryStrategy to return ports.PromptDeliveryAfterStart.
  3. Update Amp adapter tests to expect the prompt to be delivered after startup.
  4. Keep system prompt and permission behavior unchanged unless Amp exposes documented interactive flags for them.

  Relevant reference patterns:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/kimi.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/cline.go

  ## Notes

  This looks like an adapter behavior issue, not a tmux/browser terminal issue. The tmux runtime is already capable of launching
  interactive TUIs; the Amp adapter is selecting the non-interactive command path.

title: fix: launch Amp workers interactively
body:
## Summary

  Fixes Amp worker startup so prompted workers open the interactive Amp TUI instead of sending the prompt through the launch command.

  Previously, Amp launches included the worker prompt in argv:

  ```sh
  amp -- "<prompt>"

  Older reports also referenced amp -x "<prompt>". In both cases, passing the prompt during process launch can select Amp's execute/non-
  interactive path instead of the normal terminal UI.

  This PR makes Amp match other TUI-first adapters such as Kimi and Cline: AO starts Amp interactively, then delivers the initial worker prompt
  after startup through the runtime pane.

  ## Changes

      - acceptEdits -> --permission-mode acceptEdits
      - auto -> --permission-mode auto
      - bypassPermissions -> --permission-mode bypassPermissions

  - Add GetPromptDeliveryStrategy for Amp.
  - Return ports.PromptDeliveryAfterStart so AO injects prompted worker tasks after the TUI starts.
  - Keep system prompt behavior unchanged:
      - Amp still does not receive unsupported system-prompt flags.

  - Update Amp adapter tests to verify:
      - prompted launches do not include the prompt in argv
      - Amp uses after-start prompt delivery
      - permission flags still map as before
      - unsupported system-prompt flags remain absent

  - git diff --check

title: Amp adapter passes unsupported --permission-mode flags
body:
## Description

  The Amp adapter maps AO permission modes to Claude-style `--permission-mode` CLI flags:

  ```go
  func appendPermissionFlags(cmd *[]string, mode ports.PermissionMode) {
        switch mode {
        case ports.PermissionModeAcceptEdits:
                *cmd = append(*cmd, "--permission-mode", "acceptEdits")
        case ports.PermissionModeAuto:
                *cmd = append(*cmd, "--permission-mode", "auto")
        case ports.PermissionModeBypassPermissions:
                *cmd = append(*cmd, "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions")
        }
  }

  Relevant files:

  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp.go
  - backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp_test.go

  Amp’s documented permissions model does not appear to expose a --permission-mode CLI flag. The Amp manual describes permissions through
  settings/plugin behavior instead:

  - amp.permissions
  - amp.guardedFiles.allowlist
  - amp.dangerouslyAllowAll

  Amp also states that it does not ask for approval before running tools by default.

  ## Problem

  When AO launches Amp with a non-default permission mode, it can build commands like:

  amp --permission-mode acceptEdits
  amp --permission-mode auto
  amp --permission-mode bypassPermissions

  If Amp does not support these flags, the CLI may fail on startup or exit before opening the TUI.

  This is separate from the prompt delivery issue. Even after Amp launches interactively without -x / prompt argv, permission modes can still
  make the launch command invalid.

  ## Expected Behavior

  AO should only pass documented Amp CLI flags.

  If Amp does not support CLI permission flags, the Amp adapter should either:

  - omit AO permission-mode flags for Amp, or
  - translate them into Amp-supported settings/plugin configuration if available.

  ## Actual Behavior

  AO currently appends --permission-mode <mode> for Amp when project/session permissions are configured.

  ## Why This Matters

  Projects that configure worker permissions globally can make Amp workers fail to start, even though plain amp works.

  This can be confusing because the failure depends on AO permission configuration, not on Amp installation or auth.

  ## Suggested Fix

  - Remove --permission-mode mapping from the Amp adapter unless Amp documents support for it.
  - Keep default Amp launch as:

  amp

  - Add/update tests so Amp permission modes do not emit unsupported CLI flags.
  - If AO wants to support Amp-specific permissions later, implement it through documented Amp settings/plugin behavior.

title: fix(mobile): shared-terminal co-view, phone zoom/pan, width & Android fixes, authenticated LAN preview
body:
## What

Brings the shared-terminal co-view work (originally proposed in a downstream PR) on top of `main`, plus a set of mobile-app fixes uncovered while testing it on physical devices. and added menu picker for spawing new agents which are auth harnesses.

## Commits

**Terminal (backend) — one authoritative grid for co-viewers**
- `fix(terminal): size the shared PTY to the largest attached client`
- `fix(terminal): size the shared PTY to one authoritative grid so co-viewers (desktop + phone) don't mis-render`

The PTY is now sized to a single authoritative grid so a desktop and a phone viewing the same terminal no longer fight over dimensions and mis-render.

**Mobile — terminal rendering & interaction**
- `fix(mobile): let the phone zoom and pan the shared terminal grid instead of only shrinking it to an unreadable overview` — pinch-zoom between fit and 1:1, one-finger pan while zoomed, double-tap to toggle, cursor auto-follow.
- `fix(mobile): make the terminal fill the screen width on iOS and Android` — zero xterm's phantom mobile scrollbar (overlay scrollbars measure 0px, so its `|| 15` fallback reserved 15px it never used) before measuring, and re-measure a few times as Android layout/fonts settle so the grid reaches full width without needing a keyboard toggle.
- `fix(mobile): stop the Android terminal from crashing to black, and reserve keyboard space on both platforms` — drop `androidLayerType:"hardware"` (a hardware layer composites the xterm `<canvas>` blank on many devices), surface a render-process crash instead of a silent black screen, and reserve keyboard height on both platforms (Android edge-to-edge defeats `adjustResize`).

**Mobile — authenticated previews over the LAN bridge**
- `feat(mobile): serve authenticated previews over the LAN bridge` — the LAN listener gates the preview route behind the connection-password. A preview page's WebView subresource requests (images/CSS/JS) can't carry our `Authorization` header, so the backend now drops a path-scoped, HttpOnly auth cookie scoped to that session's `/preview/files/` path only (it can never authenticate `/kill`, `/send`, or another session). Runs on the LAN listener only; the loopback/desktop path is unchanged. Mobile sends the Bearer header on the top-level preview load.

**Tooling**
- `chore(mobile): patch @fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview via patch-package`

## Verification

Ran the checks CI performs for this diff:

- `gofmt -l`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` — clean
- **golangci-lint v2.12.2** — 0 issues
- `go test -race` on all changed backend packages (httpd, terminal, conpty, tmux) — pass
- `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...` — pass
- **prettier@3 `--check`** on changed files — clean
- Mobile `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- Manually tested on physical iOS and Android devices: terminal fills width, zoom/pan gestures, Android renderer stability, authenticated preview.

## Notes

- The generated `frontend/src/renderer/routeTree.gen.ts` is intentionally not included (a dev-server codegen reformat only).

title: Windows Codex auth probe reports Needs auth when WindowsApps codex.exe shadows npm codex.cmd
body:
## Bug

On Windows, Agent Orchestrator shows Codex as `Needs auth` in the Project agents picker even though the user's installed npm Codex CLI is logged in.

**Source:** local Codex desktop chat report + screenshot  
**Reported by:** @somewherelostt  
**Analyzed against:** `1a056aa1ad93fe7146900629d005f8de0f72e1e9` (`origin/main`, 2026-07-10)  
**AO version:** `dev`  
**Daemon under test:** rewrite daemon, `go run ./cmd/ao status --json` reported `state=ready`, `port=3002`, `dataDir=C:\Users\abuma\.ao\data`  
**OS:** Windows NT `10.0.26200.0`, PowerShell `7.6.3`, Go `go1.24.4 windows/amd64`  
**Priority:** high - Codex is a core agent option and becomes unavailable in the UI on affected Windows installs.  
**Confidence:** High - reproduced locally, traced exact resolver order and failing executable.

![Project agents picker showing Codex Needs auth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-windowsapps-auth/.issue-assets/codex-windowsapps-auth/needs-auth-picker.png)

## Reproduction

1. On Windows, install/use Codex such that both of these exist:
   - WindowsApps packaged Codex executable under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_*\app\resources\codex.exe`
   - npm Codex shim under `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd`
2. Log into the npm Codex CLI.
3. Start AO from latest `main`.
4. Open a project's **Project agents** picker.
5. Observe `Codex` is disabled and marked `Needs auth`.

## Observed

AO's agent probe reports Codex as unauthorized:

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "id": "codex",
    "label": "Codex",
    "authStatus": "unauthorized"
  },
  "supported": true,
  "installed": true
}
```

The UI renders `Codex — Needs auth`.

## Expected

If the user's Codex CLI reports logged in, AO should mark Codex as authorized and allow Codex to be selected.

## Local Verification

The npm shim is authenticated:

```powershell
& "$env:APPDATA\npm\codex.cmd" login status
# Logged in using ChatGPT
# exit=0
```

Windows command resolution returns the WindowsApps packaged executable first for `codex.exe`:

```powershell
where.exe codex.exe
# C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.707.3563.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\app\resources\codex.exe

where.exe codex.cmd
# C:\Users\abuma\AppData\Roaming\npm\codex.cmd
```

Trying to run the WindowsApps executable directly fails:

```text
Program 'codex.exe' failed to run: ... Access is denied.
```

## Root Cause

The Windows branch of `ResolveCodexBinary` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go` checks broad PATH lookup for `codex.exe` before known user-install locations:

```go
for _, name := range []string{"codex.exe", "codex.cmd", "codex"} {
    path, err := exec.LookPath(name)
    if err == nil && path != "" {
        return resolveNativeWindowsCodex(path), nil
    }
}
```

Because `codex.exe` is checked first, `exec.LookPath` can return the WindowsApps package resource before AO checks `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd` or the npm package's bundled native executable.

The auth probe then runs:

```go
exec.CommandContext(probeCtx, binary, "login", "status")
```

That direct child process fails with Access denied before producing `logged in`, so AO falls through to `unauthorized` and the UI incorrectly asks the user to authenticate.

Relevant code path:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`: `AuthStatus`
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`: `ResolveCodexBinary`
- `backend/internal/service/agent/service.go`: catalog/probe maps auth status into agent inventory
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`: displays unauthorized agents as `Needs auth`

## Fix Direction

Prefer known user-install paths on Windows before broad `codex.exe` lookup, especially:

- `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@openai\codex\...\codex.exe`
- `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd`
- `%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin\codex.exe`

Also consider skipping `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_*\app\resources\codex(.exe)` for direct daemon execution, or treating direct-launch `Access is denied` as `unknown` rather than `unauthorized` so the UI does not incorrectly say the user needs to log in.

## Impact

- Codex appears unavailable in AO on affected Windows machines.
- Users who are already logged in through npm Codex are told they need auth.
- Worker/orchestrator agent selection is misleading and blocks Codex selection from the UI.

## Duplicate Search

No matching existing issue or PR found on 2026-07-10 using:

```bash
gh issue list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex WindowsApps auth"
gh issue list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex auth unauthorized Windows"
gh issue list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "Needs auth Codex"
gh pr list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex WindowsApps auth"
gh pr list --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator --state all --search "codex.exe codex.cmd"
```

The only `Needs auth Codex` issue-search hit was unrelated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On Windows with both WindowsApps Codex and npm Codex installed, AO resolves the npm/bundled Codex CLI for auth probing.
- `codex.cmd login status` returning logged in results in AO `authStatus: authorized`.
- Add a regression test covering WindowsApps `codex.exe` shadowing `codex.cmd`.
- UI no longer shows `Codex — Needs auth` for an authenticated npm Codex CLI.

title: fix(frontend): surface daemon failure reason instead of generic "not ready" error
body:
## Bug

When a second checkout's Electron instance cannot attach to the daemon (checkout identity mismatch — but also spawn failure or unexpected exit), the main process computes a specific, actionable diagnostic and sends it over the `daemon:status` IPC. The renderer drops it: every API call surfaces only the generic `"AO daemon is not ready."` error, so the user never learns another checkout owns the daemon or how to fix it.

## Root cause

- `applyDaemonStatus()` (`renderer/lib/daemon-status.ts`) quarantines the base URL for non-ready statuses but discards `status.message`.
- `runtimeFetch()`'s 503 short-circuit (`renderer/lib/api-client.ts`) hardcodes the generic body, so `apiErrorMessage()` can only ever surface the fallback.

The diagnostic is computed in `main.ts` (`daemonIdentityError()`), shipped over IPC, and then dead on arrival.

## Fix

Keep the status message alongside the quarantined base URL (`setDaemonUnavailableMessage`), and let the 503 short-circuit prefer it over the generic fallback — the same `status.message || "AO daemon is not ready."` pattern `_shell.tsx` already uses for project creation. This benefits every `daemonStatus` failure path (identity mismatch, spawn failure, daemon exit), not just the issue's trigger, and complements #2253 (which disables actions and adds a Restart button but does not fix the message masking).

## Testing

- New `renderer/lib/daemon-status.test.ts` regression test: fails before the fix (generic message masks the identity diagnostic), passes after. Also covers the no-message fallback and that a stale reason is cleared once the daemon is ready again.
- `useDaemonStatus.test.tsx`: completed the partial `api-client` mock with the new export.
- Full frontend vitest suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and `prettier --check` on the changed files all pass.

Fixes #2481

title: fix(lifecycle): require consecutive dead probes before terminating a session
body:
## Bug

A single `ProbeDead` reading from the reaper, landing while a session's recorded activity happened to be stale (>60s), terminated the session **immediately and irreversibly**. Hook delivery is explicitly best-effort (`manager.go`), so activity routinely goes stale on genuinely live sessions — long tool calls, dropped hook deliveries. One transient tmux misreading could kill a live orchestrator mid-turn, which is exactly the incident traced in #2501: `pledg-turbo-monolith-4` was marked terminated ~5 minutes *before* its own transcript's `stop_hook_summary`, then silently replaced.

## Root cause

`ApplyRuntimeObservation` killed on the first observation where `Probe == ProbeDead && !hasRecentActivity(60s)`. There was no retry, no requirement for multiple consecutive dead readings, and no reconciliation if the pane turned out to still be alive. `docs/architecture.md`'s own key principle — *failed probes are NOT proof of death* — stopped one step short: a single dead sample against stale activity is no more trustworthy.

## Fix

The lifecycle manager now counts consecutive `ProbeDead` readings per session (in memory, under the existing `mu` — a probe streak is arbitration state, not a durable session fact, honoring the "no transient lifecycle state is stored" rule) and terminates only once the runtime has read dead for **3 consecutive probes** (~10–15s at the reaper's 5s cadence) *and* the existing stale-activity gate agrees.

- An **alive** reading resets the streak — a transient blip can never accumulate into a kill.
- A **failed** probe neither builds nor resets it — a flaky probe must not shield a really-dead session from the backstop, nor count toward its death.
- **Spawn/restore** (`MarkSpawned`) voids readings taken against the previous runtime.
- The streak **accrues while recent activity still vetoes termination**, so a genuinely dead runtime still terminates the moment its activity goes stale — no added latency in the common case. The only slower path is a runtime that dies while activity is *already* stale: 3 ticks (~10s) instead of 1. `SessionEnd` hooks remain the fast path either way.

Updated the key-principle line in `docs/architecture.md` accordingly.

## Testing

New regression tests in `manager_test.go` (all fail against the previous behavior): unconfirmed dead probe does not terminate; alive resets the streak; failed probes preserve but do not extend it; the streak accrues under recent activity; respawn resets it. `go test ./internal/lifecycle/` and `go test -race` pass; `go vet` and golangci-lint clean on the package; full `go test ./...` shows no new failures against main.

Part of #2501 — this addresses the probe-race kill (defect 1). The unlinked, notification-less orchestrator respawn (defect 2) is left for a separate change.

title: [BUG]: npm run dev:web fails on Windows
body:
## Summary

For contributors who want to work on the renderer without launching the full Electron application, the project provides the `npm run dev:web` script which is especially useful when iterating on UI changes 
However, the script currently fails on Windows because it relies on POSIX-style environment variable syntax

## Actual behavior

The command fails with:

`'VITE_NO_ELECTRON' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.`

## Expected behavior

The renderer development server should start successfully on Windows, just as it does on Unix-like systems

## Root cause

The current script is:

`"dev:web": "VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts"`

Inline environment variable assignment is supported by POSIX shells but not by cmd.exe or PowerShell...

## Proposed fix

Use cross-env to make the script platform-independent:

`"dev:web": "cross-env VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts"`

This preserves the existing behavior on Unix-like systems while allowing the same command to work on Windows

> I'd be happy to open a PR for this if it sounds like the preferred approach

title: ao spawn confirmation output omits the display name set via --name
body:
## Bug
`ao spawn`'s confirmation line prints only the generated session ID, never the display name passed via `--name` (or derived from `--prompt`), even though the name is persisted immediately. This makes it easy to lose track of which session ID maps to which name at the exact moment the mapping is freshest, forcing a separate `ao session get`/`ao session ls` call to look it up again.

**Analyzed against:** `69dc21d3` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
```
$ ao spawn --project agent-orchestrator --name "quiet-fox-42" --prompt "..."
spawned session agent-orchestrator-15 (idle)
attach with: tmux attach -t agent-orchestrator-15
```
The string `quiet-fox-42` never appears in the output. Confirmed via `ao session get agent-orchestrator-15 --json`, which shows `"displayName": "quiet-fox-42"` was stored immediately.

## Root cause, and why the fix is documentation rather than code (revised)

`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go` resolves the display name locally before the spawn request is even sent, but the confirmation line is built purely from the API response's `ID`/`Status` fields, never referencing the already-known name. This is a plain oversight (PR [#2302](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2302), which introduced `--name`, wired `DisplayName` through the request/response DTOs but never touched the confirmation string) — not documented anywhere as intentional.

A code fix (echoing the name in the CLI's own output) was implemented and then deliberately reverted after review. Reasoning: an **orchestrator agent** already knows the name in the very same tool call where it typed `--name` — echoing it back in CLI output doesn't teach the agent anything new. What actually causes an orchestrator to report a bare session id to a human isn't missing information, it's a reporting *habit* (relaying raw CLI/tool output rather than translating it). The fix that targets that directly is a **documentation change**: `backend/internal/skillassets/using-ao/commands/spawn.md` now explicitly instructs orchestrator agents to report a spawned session by its `--name`, not its id, when summarizing for the user.

`ao spawn`'s CLI output itself is unchanged from `main` — the literal premise of this issue (the CLI omits the name) is still technically true, and intentionally left that way.

## A second bug this surfaced: stale names after rename

Preferring the display name over the id introduces its own failure mode: **a session's display name is not permanent** — it can be changed after spawn via `ao session rename <id> <name>`, unlike the id, which is fixed for the session's lifetime. An orchestrator agent has no automatic way to learn that a rename happened after it last observed a session; its only "knowledge" of the name is whatever is still sitting in its own conversation memory, which is never invalidated or refreshed automatically. So the "report by name" instruction alone could make an orchestrator confidently repeat a **stale, now-wrong** name — arguably worse than reporting the id, which never goes stale.

Caught live during review: a worker session's display name changed from `investigate-glyphs` to `glyphs` sometime after it was spawned, and the orchestrator only noticed because it happened to re-query the session's current state rather than trust its own memory — otherwise it would have kept reporting the original, now-incorrect name indefinitely.

**Fix for this part**: added a note to `SKILL.md`'s general Conventions section (not `spawn.md`, since staleness applies whenever a session is referenced, not just at spawn time) telling orchestrator agents to re-confirm a session's current name via `ao session get`/`ao session ls` rather than relying on memory, whenever accuracy matters (long conversations, or after any renaming activity).

## Impact
- Orchestrator agents (and humans) previously had no reinforcement of a session's name at spawn time, defaulting to reporting the bare id.
- Fixed via explicit skill instruction, paired with a staleness caveat so the fix doesn't introduce a new "confidently wrong" failure mode via renames.

**Priority:** low — cosmetic/UX, no functional breakage, workaround (`ao session get`/`ao session ls`) always available.

## Related
- [#2299](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2299): added `--name` flag (root feature this issue is about)
- [PR #2302](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2302): implementation that wired `--name` through without updating the confirmation output
- [#2380](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2380): related but distinct — terminal header display name, not CLI spawn confirmation
- Fixed by [PR #2593](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2593) (docs-only: `spawn.md` reporting instruction + `SKILL.md` staleness caveat)

title: fix(agent): stop tool-use hooks pinning copilot/kiro/cline sessions to needs_input
body:
## Summary

This fixes an activity-state regression where **Copilot**, **Kiro**, and **Cline** sessions could become incorrectly stuck in `needs_input` while they were actively executing tools.

The root cause was that each adapter mapped its per-tool `preToolUse`/`PreToolUse` event to the permission-request hook. Since `StandardDeriveActivityState` treats permission requests as the sticky `waiting_input` state, every tool invocation looked like the agent was waiting for user approval—even when it wasn't.

This was especially visible in autonomous approval modes (`--allow-all-tools`, `--allow-all`, `--auto-approve`, `--yolo`, Kiro auto/bypass), where no user interaction occurs at all. The session would remain pinned to `needs_input`, masking the real PR-derived state and triggering false "needs input" notifications.

## Changes

* Add a shared **tool-use activity** signal that derives to `active`.
* Update the **Copilot**, **Kiro**, and **Cline** adapters to emit this signal for per-tool events instead of the permission-request hook.
* Keep the permission-request hook reserved for events that genuinely require user approval (for example, Cursor's `beforeShellExecution`).

This matches the existing behavior of the `agy` adapter and aligns with the architecture principle that `waiting_input` should only represent an agent that is actually blocked on the user.

## Tradeoff

Interactive approval prompts generated from these generic per-tool events will no longer appear as `waiting_input`.

This is intentional: the previous signal fired before **every** tool invocation, regardless of whether approval was actually required, making it overwhelmingly noisy. Removing these false positives results in more accurate activity reporting and is consistent with how Claude Code and Codex avoid inferring a blocking state from generic tool-use events.

## Testing

Added regression coverage for:

* `StandardDeriveActivityState` deriving `active` from tool-use events.
* Copilot adapter tool-use event mapping.
* Kiro adapter tool-use event mapping.
* Cline adapter tool-use event mapping.

Validation completed successfully:

* `go build ./...`
* `go test ./...`
* `go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/...`
* `gofmt`
* `go vet`
* `golangci-lint v2.12.2`

title: Dev daemon state split makes project imports and registry look inconsistent
body:
## Bug

After PR #2465, dev Electron runs its own daemon on port 3002 with state under `~/.ao/dev/data`, while normal/packaged AO and the verified CLI default to port 3001 with state under `~/.ao/data`. This prevents daemon collisions, but it also forks the project registry and import state. A project can appear to already exist in one mode while the other mode shows a different or empty registry, forcing manual reconciliation of local daemon state.

**Source:** User report in local Codex chat on 2026-07-11
**Reported by:** @nikhilachale
**Analyzed against:** `5b0c4f5289c654b51ede4a4a927cced0013808de` / upstream main `5b0c4f52`
**AO version:** `dev` from repo-built `/tmp/ao`
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, zsh, Go 1.26.4
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Have normal AO state in `~/.ao/data/ao.db` with registered projects.
2. Run Electron in dev mode, which starts/uses a dev daemon on port 3002.
3. Observe dev mode reads `~/.ao/dev/data/ao.db` instead of `~/.ao/data/ao.db`.
4. Try to import/register projects and compare what the dev UI shows vs what normal mode/CLI sees.

Observed locally:

- `~/.ao/running.json` pointed at port 3001 and `~/.ao/data`, but was stale/dead.
- `~/.ao/dev/running.json` pointed at live port 3002.
- Direct `curl http://127.0.0.1:3002/readyz` returned ready for the dev daemon.
- `~/.ao/data/ao.db` had active projects including `agent-orchestrator`, `mj-scaffold`, `renz-ui`, and `reverbcode`.
- `~/.ao/dev/data/ao.db` initially had only the dev-mode project row, so the dev UI showed different data from normal mode.

## Root Cause

PR #2465 fixed #2464 by intentionally isolating dev mode from the installed app. The current code in `frontend/src/main.ts` does this unconditionally when `!app.isPackaged`:

- lines 136-141 define `DEV_DAEMON_PORT = 3002` and `DEV_STATE_SUBDIR = "dev"`.
- lines 300-303 make dev read `~/.ao/dev/running.json`.
- lines 390-393 inject `AO_PORT=3002`, `AO_RUN_FILE=~/.ao/dev/running.json`, and `AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/dev/data`.
- lines 567-571 make port probes prefer 3002 in dev.

The backend default remains canonical `~/.ao/data` when `AO_DATA_DIR` is unset (`backend/internal/config/config.go` lines 282-293). Import idempotency checks project IDs in whichever store is open (`backend/internal/legacyimport/importer.go` lines 130-136), and project add rejects active path/id conflicts in the current store (`backend/internal/service/project/service.go` lines 181-196). With two stores, those checks are internally correct but user-visible state diverges across dev and normal modes.

## Related

- #2464: original bug where dev latched onto the installed daemon and killed it on quit.
- #2465: merged fix that introduced isolated port/run-file/data-dir defaults.

## Fix

Do not blindly revert #2465; it fixed a real supervisor collision. Possible fixes:

1. Keep separate ports/run-files/supervisor sockets for dev, but make project registry/import state shared or explicitly synchronized.
2. Make isolated dev data opt-in, while default dev mode attaches to canonical state without linking in a way that can kill the installed daemon.
3. Add an explicit dev-state import/sync path and UI/CLI messaging so users know dev mode is using a separate registry and can reconcile it without direct SQLite/manual API calls.

The safest implementation should preserve the #2464 guarantee: quitting dev Electron must not kill the installed app daemon.

## Impact

- Developers running `npm run dev` see a different project list than the installed app/normal daemon.
- Legacy project import can report rows as already present in one store while the active dev UI is pointed at another store.
- Users have to manually reconcile `~/.ao/data` and `~/.ao/dev/data`, which is brittle and confusing.

title: fix(workspace): recover stale orchestrator worktrees during replacement
body:
## Summary

  This fixes clean orchestrator replacement when AO has an active old orchestrator row whose recorded workspace path is stale.

  Previously, `RetireForReplacement` always called `StashUncommitted` before removing the old orchestrator worktree. If the stored path still existed
  but was no longer a valid git worktree, `git status` failed with `not a git repository`, which bubbled up as an error and blocked replacement. The
  user saw a failed restart even though the stale path was AO-managed state that could be safely recovered.

  ## What Changed

  - Added `ports.ErrWorkspaceStale` to represent AO-managed workspace paths that no longer point to a valid registered git worktree.
  - Updated `gitworktree.StashUncommitted` to return `ErrWorkspaceStale` only after path safety checks, for:
    - missing managed workspace paths
    - existing paths not present in `git worktree list`
    - paths where `git status` reports `not a git repository`
  - Updated `RetireForReplacement` to handle only `ErrWorkspaceStale` as recoverable:
    - skip stash/preserve for the stale workspace
    - clear `session_worktrees` restore markers
    - destroy runtime if present
    - best-effort remove the stale AO-managed folder
    - mark the old orchestrator session terminated
    - continue spawning the fresh orchestrator
  - Kept all other stash/preserve errors fatal, so AO does not delete a real workspace when it cannot preserve work.
  - Added tests for stale classification, unsafe-path behavior, stale replacement recovery, and non-stale preserve failure behavior.

  ## Behavior Covered

  - Valid dirty git worktree: preserve changes, remove old worktree, mark old orchestrator terminated, spawn fresh orchestrator.
  - Valid clean git worktree: remove old worktree, mark old orchestrator terminated, spawn fresh orchestrator.
  - Missing / unregistered / non-git AO-managed path: treat as stale AO-owned state and recover.
  - Real git worktree with preserve failure: fail replacement and leave session/worktree state intact.
  - Path outside AO’s managed workspace root: fail safely and do not touch it.

  ## Data Model

  This does not delete the old orchestrator session row. The old row remains as durable history/debug context. The fix only clears restore/worktree
  markers that could cause incorrect restore behavior, then marks the old orchestrator terminated.
  
  closes #2551

title: feat(cli): add dev command for importing projects from data directory
body:
## Summary

Adds a manual dev-only project registry import command:

```bash
ao dev import-projects
```

This lets a dev AO daemon copy project registry metadata from the normal AO data dir into the current dev AO data dir without sharing SQLite state or copying runtime/session data.

Also namespaces generated branches for the default dev data dir so dev AO worktrees do not collide with normal AO worktrees in the same source repository.

## What changed

### Dev project import

Added:

```bash
ao dev import-projects
```

Flags:

- `--from-data-dir <path>`
- `--dry-run`
- `--json`

Default behavior:

- Source data dir defaults to `~/.ao/data`
- Target data dir is the current `AO_DATA_DIR`
- Typical dev target is `~/.ao/dev/data`

The command copies only active project registry data:

- project ID
- project path
- display name
- repo origin
- project kind
- registration timestamp
- project config
- workspace child repo registry

It does not copy:

- sessions
- worktrees
- runtime or terminal handles
- PR/review/check facts
- notifications
- telemetry
- hooks
- runtime files
- repository folders

### Safety checks

Before writing, the command refuses when:

- the target daemon is live according to the current `AO_RUN_FILE`
- source and target data dirs resolve to the same path

### Conflict behavior

- same ID + same path: update target metadata/config
- missing ID/path: insert into target
- same path with different active ID: skip and report conflict
- same ID with different active path: skip and report conflict
- never archives or deletes target projects

Dry-run uses the same planning path as real writes, including planned insert conflict detection.

### Dev branch namespace

When the daemon uses the default dev data dir:

```
~/.ao/dev/data
```

generated AO branches now use the `ao/dev/...` namespace.

Examples:

```
ao/dev/reverbcode-orchestrator
ao/dev/reverbcode-1/root
```

Normal AO keeps existing branch names:

```
ao/reverbcode-orchestrator
ao/reverbcode-1/root
```

Explicit user-provided `--branch` values are unchanged.

This prevents dev AO from failing with `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE` when normal AO already has the canonical orchestrator branch checked out in another worktree.

## Why

The dev daemon is isolated by port, run file, and data dir, but Git branch checkout locks live in the underlying source repository. After importing project registry metadata into dev AO, both normal AO and dev AO may point at the same repo path. Without a dev branch namespace, dev AO can try to create a worktree for a branch already checked out by normal AO.

The import command keeps state sharing explicit and narrow, while the branch namespace keeps dev and normal worktrees from colliding.

## Verification

Ran:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/devimport/... ./internal/session_manager ./internal/service/session
go test ./internal/cli/... ./internal/service/... ./internal/devimport/...
go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/...
```

All passed.

Working tree is clean and branch is tracking `origin/fix/dev-import-projects`.

closes #2597

title: fix(terminal): force UTF-8 client mode on tmux attach
body: ## Summary Fixes #2603. - Root-causes and fixes the garbled box-drawing/underscore rendering symptom. - `tmux attach-session` infers UTF-8 client capability from `LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LANG` in the attaching process's environment. AO's daemon typically runs without an interactive shell's locale, so tmux silently treats the attach client as non-UTF-8. - A non-UTF-8 client makes tmux's `tty_check_codeset` (tty.c) replace any character it can't map through its legacy ACS table with underscores matching the glyph's display width. Common box-drawing glyphs (│ ─ etc.) are in that ACS table, so they still rendered correctly — which is why an earlier investigation attempt, testing only a box-drawing border character, concluded locale had no effect and marked the theory disproven. Agent CLI status icons outside the ACS table (e.g. Claude Code's spinner `✻` U+273B, its `⎿` U+23BF continuation marker) are not covered and were silently rewritten to `_`. - Passing `-u` to `tmux attach-session` forces `CLIENT_UTF8` on regardless of the daemon's environment, matching how a bare `tmux attach` from an interactive shell (which does have a UTF-8 locale) already behaves — which is why the bug only reproduced through AO, never through a bare terminal attach to the same session. Confirmed with a byte-level repro outside AO/Electron entirely: spawning `tmux attach-session` via a pty with a stripped, locale-less env reproduces `_ _ _` for `✻ ⎿ ←` while `│` still renders correctly; adding `-u` fixes the icons with no change to the box-drawing case. ## Screenshots **Before** (`-u` not passed) — agent status icons (spinner, continuation marker) render as `_`: **After** (`-u` passed) — icons render correctly; box-drawing glyphs unaffected either way: ## Test plan - [x] `go build ./...` (backend) - [x] `go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/...` — updated `TestAttachCommandReturnsExpectedArgv` for the new `-u` flag, both attach-command tests pass - [x] `go test ./...` (backend) — no new failures (4 pre-existing, unrelated `internal/cli` failures confirmed present on a clean checkout too) - [x] Manual byte-level repro: pty-attached to a live tmux session with a stripped env, with and without `-u`, confirmed the underscore substitution and the fix directly against tmux 3.4's actual output bytes 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(terminal): agent CLI status icons render as underscores over tmux attach (AO-only)
body: ## Bug Box-drawing/agent-status Unicode characters in AO's embedded terminal (xterm.js attached to a tmux session) sometimes render as underscores instead of their proper glyphs — e.g. Claude Code's spinner `✻` (U+273B) and its `⎿` (U+23BF) continuation marker both showed up as `_`. Common box-drawing glyphs (`│ ─` etc.) were unaffected. This does not reproduce when attaching to the same tmux session from a bare terminal outside AO. This is a split-off of the garbled-rendering half of issue 2484 (that issue also covered a Ctrl+Arrow/Ctrl+Backspace/Ctrl+V double-fire bug, fixed separately in #2586; the rendering half was left open with only an unconfirmed hypothesis). ## Root cause `tmux attach-session` infers UTF-8 client capability from `LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`/`LANG` in the attaching process's environment, unless `-u` is passed explicitly. AO's daemon typically runs without an interactive shell's locale, so tmux silently treats every attach client as non-UTF-8. A non-UTF-8 client makes tmux's `tty_check_codeset` (`tty.c`) replace any character it can't map through its legacy ACS table with underscores matching the glyph's display width. Common box-drawing glyphs are in that ACS table, so they still rendered correctly — which is why an earlier investigation attempt, testing only a box-drawing border character, concluded locale had no effect. Agent CLI status icons outside the ACS table (Claude Code's spinner, its continuation marker, etc.) are not covered and were silently rewritten to `_`. Confirmed with a byte-level repro outside AO/Electron entirely: spawning `tmux attach-session` via a pty with a stripped, locale-less env reproduces `_ _ _` for `✻ ⎿ ←` while `│` still renders correctly. ## Fix Pass `-u` to `tmux attach-session` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go`) to force `CLIENT_UTF8` on regardless of the daemon's environment — matching how a bare `tmux attach` from an interactive shell (which does have a UTF-8 locale) already behaves. ## Screenshots **Before** (no `-u`, glyphs corrupted): **After** (`-u` passed, glyphs correct):

title: bug(lifecycle): sessions show no_signal right after the daemon restarts/app reopens, even when the agent process never stopped
body:
## Bug

Every pre-existing worker/orchestrator session shows status `no_signal` shortly after the AO daemon restarts (equivalently: after reopening the desktop app) — even when the underlying agent process (tmux session) was never actually stopped, only the daemon itself restarted.

**Source:** live observation, this environment | **Confidence:** Medium — symptom confirmed with direct database evidence; exact mechanism NOT confirmed despite a real investigation attempt (see below).

## Reproduction

1. Have several active worker/orchestrator sessions running normally (e.g. `working`/`idle`/`needs_input`).
2. Restart the AO daemon (or reopen the desktop app).
3. Within ~90s, `ao session ls` shows every pre-existing session as `no_signal`, even though their tmux panes/agent processes were never interrupted.

## Evidence

Direct SQLite inspection (`~/.ao/data/ao.db`) immediately after a real daemon restart:

```
id                     activity_state  first_signal_at   activity_last_at    runtime_handle_id
agent-orchestrator-6   idle            (empty)            <restart time>      agent-orchestrator-6
agent-orchestrator-11  idle            (empty)            <restart time>      agent-orchestrator-11
agent-orchestrator-13  idle            (empty)            <restart time>      agent-orchestrator-13
```

`first_signal_at` NULL and `activity_last_at` stamped to the restart time (not the session's real prior activity) is the fingerprint of `MarkSpawned` (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`) having run for these sessions — which per `deriveStatus()` (`backend/internal/service/session/status.go`) produces `no_signal` once the 90s grace window elapses, since no new hook signal has fired since. `runtime_handle_id` was correctly populated in every case, ruling out "empty handle skips the alive-probe" as the cause.

## Root cause — NOT confirmed; investigation attempted and inconclusive

The reconcile path that's supposed to prevent this (`reconcileLive`/`Reconcile`, `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`, ~lines 887/946) has a documented no-op "adopt" branch for any session where `runtime.IsAlive()` reports true — it should leave `Activity`/`FirstSignalAt` untouched for genuinely-alive sessions.

A dedicated investigation (isolated daemon instance, instrumented `IsAlive`/`reconcileLive`, deliberate kill+restart against known-alive tmux sessions) could **not** reproduce the bug: `IsAlive` correctly returned `true` in ~7ms every time, and `reconcileLive` correctly took the no-op branch. Several code-level hypotheses were ruled out (PATH resolution is one-time at daemon construction, not per-call; `IsAlive` correctly distinguishes "missing" from "probe error"; graceful shutdown doesn't touch live session rows).

Cross-checking the real production DB evidence against tmux's own session-creation timestamps found the affected session's tmux session was recreated at the exact moment of the reset — which is *at least as consistent* with the session having genuinely died and been correctly recovered as with a false "dead" probe reading, since `tmux new-session` fails if a name already exists. This specific data point doesn't clearly support a race-condition theory.

One more loose end flagged during investigation: the currently-running production daemon binary's build isn't cleanly verifiable against any specific worktree commit (non-`-trimpath` builds aren't reproducible across build directories), so a source/version mismatch between the running binary and the code reviewed can't be ruled out as an alternative explanation either.

## Impact

Session status becomes unreliable immediately after any daemon restart or app reopen — a class of event that isn't rare (updates, crashes, manual restarts). For up to 90 seconds (or longer, for sessions nobody happens to interact with soon after), perfectly healthy sessions are indistinguishable from ones with a genuinely broken hook pipeline, defeating the purpose of the `no_signal` status.

## Recommended next steps

Since this couldn't be reproduced from a clean isolated instance, resolving it needs either:
1. Instrumenting the actual production daemon across a real restart (not achievable from an isolated repro), or
2. Confirming what commit actually built the currently-running production binary, to rule out (or confirm) a source-mismatch explanation.

## Related
- [#2501](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2501) — a different, already-confirmed premature-termination mechanism (single bad `ProbeDead` reading + stale activity window). Adjacent subsystem, different mechanism — that one is confirmed root-caused; this one is not.

title: cleanup cannot reclaim archived-project worktrees and hides actionable teardown failures
body:
## Summary

Normal `ao session cleanup` is not enough to reclaim large AO disk usage because archived projects and stale/locked worktrees can strand data under `~/.ao/data/worktrees`.

In one cleanup run:

```text
Cleanup complete. 208 sessions cleaned, 249 skipped.
```

But disk usage stayed around:

```text
~/.ao/data/worktrees 4.5G
```

This confirms the issue is not only the expected behavior that dirty worktrees are preserved. There is also a cleanup lifecycle bug around archived projects and stale worktree states.

## Findings

### P1: cleanup cannot reclaim archived-project worktrees

Evidence from cleanup: many skipped sessions reported `workspace teardown failed`, while daemon logs showed underlying causes like:

```text
project "renzaflow" is archived: session: project repo not resolvable
```

Code cause: `projectRepoResolver.RepoPath` rejects archived projects in `backend/internal/daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go`.

Cleanup still attempts all terminated sessions in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`, but worktree deletion needs the project repo path. Once a project is archived, the resolver refuses it, so cleanup cannot remove those worktrees.

Impact: archived projects can permanently strand large worktree directories under `~/.ao/data/worktrees`.

### P1: cleanup reports generic failure reasons

CLI output showed many skipped sessions as only:

```text
workspace teardown failed
```

The daemon logs had the useful reason: archived project not resolvable, locked worktree, etc.

Code deliberately collapses non-dirty errors to generic text in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`.

Impact: users cannot tell whether to inspect dirty work, unlock a worktree, re-register a project, or manually remove stale archived-project data.

### P2: locked/stale orchestrator worktrees are not recoverable by normal cleanup

Logs showed locked worktree failures such as:

```text
fatal: cannot remove a locked working tree, lock reason: initializing
```

`Destroy` intentionally avoids `--force` in `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go`, which is correct for dirty work safety.

But stale locked worktrees are not dirty-work preservation. They need a distinct recovery path or clearer diagnostic.

Impact: repeated orchestrator sessions sharing the same path can produce many skipped entries for one stale locked worktree.

### P2: documented cleanup dry-run is missing

Docs recommend:

```bash
ao session cleanup --dry-run
ao session cleanup
```

But `ao session cleanup` only defines `--project` and `--yes` in `backend/internal/cli/session.go`.

Impact: users cannot preview cleanup without entering the actual cleanup flow.

## Recommended fix direction

- Allow cleanup to resolve archived project repo paths for teardown only, or store enough repo/path metadata on the session so cleanup does not need active project resolution.
- Return structured skip reasons like `dirty`, `archived_project_unresolvable`, `locked_worktree`, and `missing_repo`, instead of one generic `workspace teardown failed`.
- Add the documented `ao session cleanup --dry-run`.
- Add disk visibility: session id, project, path, size, dirty status, and skip reason.

## Safety note

Do not weaken dirty-worktree preservation. Normal cleanup should still avoid force-deleting uncommitted user or agent work.

title: bug(scm): SCM observer never attributes PRs pushed to a fork remote, leaving 'no PR yet' / empty PR data for the standard fork-contribution workflow
body:
## Bug

The background SCM observer (`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`) silently drops every PR whose branch was pushed to a **fork remote** rather than the project's registered origin — even though the project origin is the correct upstream target for that PR. In this environment (project registered to `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`, with a separate personal `fork` remote used to push branches for PRs against upstream — the standard OSS contribution pattern), this means **the `pr` table in `~/.ao/data/ao.db` is empty (0 rows) across every project**, and every session's Kanban card / PR page shows "no PR yet" regardless of real, open PRs on GitHub.

**Analyzed against:** `821cda64` (main) | **Confidence:** High — traced exact code path, mechanism confirmed, reproduced live against a real PR.

## Reproduction

1. Register a project whose repo is the true upstream (e.g. `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`), with a second git remote (`fork`) pointing at a personal fork used to push worker branches.
2. Spawn a worker session; let it push a branch to the `fork` remote and open a PR from `fork:<branch>` against the project's upstream `main`.
3. Observe: the PR exists and is open on GitHub (confirmed live: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator#2602`, head `mukesher4/agent-orchestrator:ao/agent-orchestrator-14/fix-tmux-attach-utf8`, `isCrossRepository: true`).
4. Query the daemon: `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-14/pr` → `{"sessionId":"agent-orchestrator-14","prs":[]}`. `sqlite3 ~/.ao/data/ao.db "select count(*) from pr;"` → `0`, for **every** session in **every** registered project, not just this one.
5. Dashboard Kanban card and PR page both show "no PR yet" indefinitely — this never resolves because the observer never persists the discovery.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:475` builds each session's `sessionRepo` with:

```go
sessionRepos = append(sessionRepos, sessionRepo{session: sess, repo: repo, headRepo: origin, branch: branch})
```

`headRepo` is unconditionally set to `origin` — the project's registered repo (`p.RepoOriginURL`, resolved from the project's configured/`origin` git remote). It is **never** derived from the actual remote a session's branch was pushed to.

Later, `candidatesForHeadRepo` (`observer.go:685-694`) uses this field as a fork-misattribution guard:

```go
func candidatesForHeadRepo(candidates []sessionRepo, headRepo string) []sessionRepo {
	...
	for _, sr := range candidates {
		if strings.EqualFold(repoFullName(sr.headRepo), headRepo) {
			out = append(out, sr)
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

For any PR pushed to a fork (`pr.HeadRepo == "mukesher4/agent-orchestrator"`), this compares against `sr.headRepo == "AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator"` (the hardcoded origin) — they never match, so `matchSession` is never even reached, and the PR is dropped every single poll, forever. The guard's own doc comment (`observer.go:198-200`) says `headRepo` should be "the repo the session's head branch actually lives in (the push origin)... for a cross-fork PR ... headRepo is the fork origin" — but the implementation never computes it that way; it just reuses the project's single origin repo for every session.

Notably, `resolveScanRepos` (`observer.go:507-526`) *does* correctly enumerate every git remote of the local checkout (including the fork) for the purposes of *which repos to scan for PR lists* — proving the code already has the information needed to also resolve per-session `headRepo`, it just isn't wired into the `sessionRepos` construction.

## Impact

This affects the standard/expected fork-based contribution workflow (project registered to upstream, worker branches pushed to a personal fork remote, PR opened fork→upstream) — which, in this environment, is essentially every worker session. The result: the `pr` table stays empty, Kanban cards and the PR page permanently show "no PR yet"/no PR info even for real, open, active PRs, and downstream features that depend on PR facts (CI/review/mergeability nudges, attention-zone routing, `claim-pr` auto-attach, completion detection) never fire for these sessions.

## Related
- [#2479](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2479) — a sibling gap in the *manual* `claim-pr` path for the mirror-image setup (project registered to a fork, PR against a separately-configured `upstream` remote); already fixed. This issue is the analogous gap in the *automatic background discovery* path, for the (equally common) setup where the project is registered to the true origin/upstream and a separate `fork` remote is used to push branches.
- [#2509](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2509) — different bug in the same subsystem (repo owner/name reload causing check-run 404s), unrelated mechanism.

## Suggested Fix

When building `sessionRepos`, resolve each session's actual push-remote repo (e.g. by matching the session's branch/worktree to its configured push remote, or by trying every git remote parsed in `resolveScanRepos` as a `headRepo` candidate) instead of hardcoding `origin`. `candidatesForHeadRepo` should accept a match against *any* remote the session could plausibly have pushed to, not just the project's single registered origin.

title: feat(config): per-role worker environment profile — MCP, plugins, system prompt, env (claude-code)
body:
## What

Closes #2195. Widens the per-role `RoleOverride` beyond `{agent, model, permissions}` into a full worker environment profile: **system prompt, env, MCP servers, plugins** — scoped per role (worker/orchestrator), defaulting to today's inherit-everything behavior so nothing breaks.

## Why

Today every worker inherits the orchestrator's whole environment from the global `~/.claude`: full MCP set, every plugin, no per-role standing instructions. A code-change worker carries tools and power it does not need — slower, noisier, broader than the task. The per-role mechanism already exists and is proven for `agent`/`model`/`permissions`; this widens the same `RoleOverride` to the rest of the environment.

claude-code already ships a CLI flag for **each** aspect (verified against `claude --help`):

| Aspect | claude-code flag |
|---|---|
| System prompt | `--append-system-prompt` (already mapped) |
| Env | process environment (AO already forwards `project.Env`) |
| MCP | `--mcp-config <json-or-path>` (repeatable) |
| MCP isolation | `--strict-mcp-config` — ignore all other MCP sources ("workers default to none") |
| Plugins | `--plugin-dir <path>` / `--plugin-url <url>` (repeatable) |

## Changes

- **domain** (`backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go`): `AgentConfig` gains `SystemPrompt`, `Env`, `MCP (*MCPConfig)`, `PluginDirs`. `MCPConfig{Configs, Strict}` — Strict alone (empty configs) is valid and means isolation. `IsZero` → `reflect.DeepEqual`; `Validate` checks the new fields.
- **session manager**: `effectiveAgentConfig` merges the new fields (Env per-key with role winning — deep-copied via the existing `mergeEnv` helper so it never mutates the project config); `buildSystemPrompt` appends the per-role `SystemPrompt` inside the guarded region; role `Env` is layered onto `project.Env` at the `runtimeEnv` call sites (spawn + restore).
- **adapter claudecode**: `appendMCPFlags` / `appendPluginFlags` emit the flags in both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` (resume rebuilds from flags, like `--append-system-prompt`). nil/empty → nothing emitted (inherit global, unchanged).
- **CLI** (`backend/internal/cli/project.go`): mirror structs gain the fields; `--worker-mcp-config` (repeatable), `--worker-strict-mcp`, `--worker-plugin-dir` (repeatable); full surface also via `--config-json`.

title: Add app-wide provider credentials/settings for Claude-compatible providers like MiniMax
body:
## Problem

Go AO has app-wide user-scope state under `~/.ao`, but it does not currently model app-wide Claude-compatible provider credentials. The current durable config boundary is:

- daemon config: env/defaults only (`backend/internal/config/config.go`)
- project config: per-project JSON (`backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go`)
- global settings UI: updates/import only

That means using Claude Code against MiniMax today requires one of two weak patterns:

1. put MiniMax secrets in the daemon's inherited process environment, or
2. duplicate provider secrets into each project's `config.env`

The second is the wrong shape: provider credentials are user-scope, not repo-scope.

## Ask

Add an app-wide provider credentials/settings surface for Claude-compatible providers (MiniMax is the immediate use case).

Minimum viable behavior:

- store the MiniMax API key once in AO user-scope settings
- on Claude Code launches that select a MiniMax model, inject the Anthropic-compatible env automatically:
  - `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.io/anthropic`
  - `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<user-scope minimax key>`
  - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<user-scope minimax key>`
- keep per-project config limited to model/harness/other project behavior, not provider secret duplication
- allow project env to override if someone explicitly wants a repo-local exception

## Why this is separate from #2195

#2195 is about widening per-role environment shaping. This issue is narrower: user-scope provider credentials that should be available across projects without copying secrets into each project row.

## Current evidence

- `backend/internal/config/config.go`: app-wide daemon config is env/default only
- `backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go`: durable runtime config is per-project
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.tsx`: current global settings are not provider settings
- `frontend/src/main/update-settings.ts`: existing pattern for app-wide settings exists already

title: fix(browser): keep preview live and under modal dialogs
body:
Fixes #2615

## Problem

With the Browser tab active, any modal dialog opens underneath the browser preview. The preview is a native WebContentsView that Electron composites above the renderer DOM, so no z-index can place a dialog over it. The dialog close button is unreachable until the dialog is dismissed by clicking outside.

## Solution

While a dialog is open, the native view is parked offscreen at full size, still visible, so video and animation playback never pauses. The panel mirrors the view into the DOM under the dialog, using a live display-media stream of the view frame with a capturePage polling fallback. Closing the dialog restores the view and drops the mirror. Mirror grants are one-shot, expire in 5 seconds, and capture and mirror requests are denied for views the renderer does not own.

## Testing

- npx vitest run: 545 passed
- npm run typecheck: clean
- prettier check on changed files: clean
- Verified in the desktop app: dialog stacks above the preview, close button clickable, page animations keep playing while the dialog is open

title: feat(config): per-role worker environment profile — MCP, plugins, system prompt, env (claude-code)
body:
## What

Closes #2195. Widens the per-role `RoleOverride` beyond `{agent, model, permissions}` into a full worker environment profile: **system prompt, env, MCP servers, plugins** — scoped per role (worker/orchestrator), defaulting to today's inherit-everything behavior so nothing breaks.

> Replaces #2611, which was auto-closed when its head branch was deleted during a fork cleanup. Same change, re-based cleanly on `main` (3 commits: feat + env-merge leak fix + defense-in-depth cleanup).

## Why

Today every worker inherits the orchestrator's whole environment from the global `~/.claude`: full MCP set, every plugin, no per-role standing instructions. A code-change worker carries tools and power it does not need — slower, noisier, broader than the task. The per-role mechanism already exists and is proven for `agent`/`model`/`permissions`; this widens the same `RoleOverride` to the rest of the environment.

claude-code already ships a CLI flag for **each** aspect (verified against `claude --help`):

| Aspect | claude-code flag |
|---|---|
| System prompt | `--append-system-prompt` (already mapped) |
| Env | process environment (AO already forwards `project.Env`) |
| MCP | `--mcp-config <json-or-path>` (repeatable) |
| MCP isolation | `--strict-mcp-config` — ignore all other MCP sources ("workers default to none") |
| Plugins | `--plugin-dir <path>` / `--plugin-url <url>` (repeatable) |

## Changes

- **domain** (`backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go`): `AgentConfig` gains `SystemPrompt`, `Env`, `MCP (*MCPConfig)`, `PluginDirs`. `MCPConfig{Configs, Strict}` — Strict alone (empty configs) is valid and means isolation. `IsZero` → `reflect.DeepEqual`; `Validate` checks the new fields.
- **session manager**: `effectiveAgentConfig` merges the new fields (Env per-key with role winning — deep-copied via `mergeEnv` so it never mutates the project config; MCP pointer and PluginDirs slice are also copied, not aliased); `buildSystemPrompt` appends the per-role `SystemPrompt`; role `Env` is layered onto `project.Env` at the `runtimeEnv` call sites (spawn + restore).
- **adapter claudecode**: `appendMCPFlags` / `appendPluginFlags` emit the flags in both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` (resume rebuilds from flags, like `--append-system-prompt`). Both paths also call `cfg.Config.Validate()` for symmetry. nil/empty → nothing emitted (inherit global, unchanged).
- **CLI** (`backend/internal/cli/project.go`): mirror structs gain the fields; `--worker-mcp-config` (repeatable), `--worker-strict-mcp`, `--worker-plugin-dir` (repeatable); full surface also via `--config-json`.
- **Regen**: `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.

## Scope

**claude-code only this pass.** codex/other adapters inherit as today (they do not map these flags yet) — follow-up. UI (`ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`) deferred to a separate pass; config is settable via CLI now.

## Verification

- `gofmt` clean, `go vet` clean, full affected Go suite passes (`session_manager`, `claudecode`, `domain`, `cli`).
- New unit tests: `agentconfig_test.go` (Validate/IsZero for MCP strict+empty, plugin-dirs), `projectconfig_test.go` per-role cases, `manager_test.go` (`effectiveAgentConfig` merge incl. a non-mutation regression test for Env aliasing, `buildSystemPrompt` appends role prompt, `mergeEnv`), `claudecode` launch/restore emit `--mcp-config`/`--strict-mcp-config`/`--plugin-dir[-url]` in correct positions, and restore re-validates config.
- Local review (Claude subagent + Codex adversarial, both approve): all five high-risk areas pass — env-merge mutation leak correctly fixed, merge semantics right per field, MCP Strict-alone isolation works, restore re-applies MCP/plugin flags symmetrically, nil/empty overrides preserve default inherit behavior.

## Note on MCP config shape

claude-code requires `--mcp-config` values in the `{\"mcpServers\": {...}}` shape (not a bare server JSON). This is a user-config detail, not a code issue — worth documenting in the per-role guide if/when UI lands.

title: feat(desktop+config): AO_KEEP_DAEMON keep-alive + per-role worker env profile (claude-code)
body:
Combines two independent, non-overlapping changes into one PR (frontend desktop layer + backend config layer; no shared files). Each was previously open separately (#2231 and #2611) and closed by accident when their head branches were removed during a fork cleanup — this re-opens both, with all maintainer review comments addressed.

Closes #2230. Closes #2195.

---

## Part 1 — `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` (desktop keep-alive) — closes #2230

Opt-in env var: when set, the desktop app spawns its daemon **without** the OS-native supervisor link and skips the orphan-cleanup kill on exit, so the daemon persists across app quit and stops only on an explicit `ao stop`. Default (unset) is byte-for-byte unchanged — the daemon self-stops shortly after the app quits.

Beyond \"power users with long sessions,\" the persistent-daemon mode is a prerequisite for a **detached / remote** topology (a headless daemon in a container, attached from the desktop over an SSH tunnel): without it, closing the desktop window arms-then-fires the supervisor watchdog and kills every running agent session in the container.

Both maintainer (illegalcall) review comments are addressed in the included commits:

- **Cross-launch regression (persist the keep decision with the daemon):** the keep decision is read from the daemon's durable `running.json` owner record (`\"persistent\"` vs `\"app\"`), never the current Electron process env. A daemon spawned keep-alive stays persistent even when the app is later reopened **without** `AO_KEEP_DAEMON`. `shouldLinkOnAttach(\"persistent\") === false` is encoded as a regression test.
- **fd leak:** the parent's `keepDaemonLogFd` is closed immediately after `spawn()` (the child holds its own inherited copy via stdio) and on the spawn-throw path, so each keep-alive start/stop cycle no longer accumulates descriptors.
- **stdio lifetime:** under the flag the daemon's stdio is redirected to `~/.ao/daemon.log` (stdin ignored) and the child is `unref()`'d, so Electron-owned pipes no longer kill the kept-alive daemon on the next stderr log write.
- **truthy parsing:** `keepDaemonAlive` uses an explicit allowlist (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`); `off`/`no` and any unrecognized string keep the default self-stop behavior.

Files: `frontend/src/main.ts`, `frontend/src/main/daemon-owner.ts(.test.ts)`, `frontend/src/shared/daemon-discovery.ts`, `backend/internal/runfile/runfile.go`, `docs/cli/README.md`.

## Part 2 — per-role worker environment profile (claude-code) — closes #2195

Widens the per-role `RoleOverride` beyond `{agent, model, permissions}` into a full worker environment profile: **system prompt, env, MCP servers, plugins** — scoped per role (worker/orchestrator), defaulting to inherit-everything so nothing breaks. claude-code ships a CLI flag for each aspect (`--append-system-prompt`, `--mcp-config`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir`/`--plugin-url`).

- **domain** (`agentconfig.go`): `AgentConfig` gains `SystemPrompt`, `Env`, `MCP *MCPConfig`, `PluginDirs`; `MCPConfig{Configs, Strict}` (Strict alone = isolation, valid).
- **session manager**: `effectiveAgentConfig` merges the new fields — Env per-key via deep-copying `mergeEnv` (a regression test pins that it never mutates the project config), and the MCP pointer / PluginDirs slice are copied rather than aliased (same defense-in-depth). `buildSystemPrompt` appends the per-role prompt; role `Env` layers onto `project.Env` at spawn + restore.
- **adapter claudecode**: `appendMCPFlags` / `appendPluginFlags` emit in **both** `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` (resume rebuilds from flags); both paths call `cfg.Config.Validate()` for symmetry. nil/empty → inherit global, unchanged.
- **CLI**: `--worker-mcp-config` (repeatable), `--worker-strict-mcp`, `--worker-plugin-dir` (repeatable); full surface also via `--config-json`. UI deferred to a follow-up.
- Regen: `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.

**Scope of Part 2:** claude-code only this pass. codex/other adapters inherit as today (follow-up).

## Verification

- `gofmt` + `go vet` clean; affected Go suites pass (`session_manager`, `claudecode`, `domain`, `cli`, `runfile`).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; 26 `daemon-owner` tests pass (incl. the cross-launch and allowlist cases).
- Local review (Claude subagent + Codex adversarial, both approve) on each part independently: no critical issues, all high-risk areas pass (env-merge mutation leak fixed; restore re-applies MCP/plugin flags; nil/empty preserves default behavior; cross-launch keep decision persisted on the daemon record).

## Note

claude-code requires `--mcp-config` values in the `{\"mcpServers\": {...}}` shape (not a bare server JSON) — a user-config detail worth documenting when the UI lands.

title: fix: give resumed sessions proof-of-life via SessionStart
body:
## Summary
- Sessions permanently showed `no_signal` after every daemon restart, even though the agent process never actually died.
- Root cause: `SaveAndTeardownAll`/`RestoreAll` tear down and relaunch every live session's harness process on restart. For Claude Code, resuming via `claude --resume <sessionId>` never resubmits a prompt, so a session idle at restart time never receives an activity-bearing hook callback and permanently downgrades to `no_signal` with no self-healing path.
- Claude Code's `SessionStart` hook already fires on every launch (fresh spawn *and* resume alike) but was previously dropped entirely, since it carries no activity reading of its own.
- Fix: introduce `domain.ActivitySignalOnly`, a wire-only marker distinct from a real `Activity.State`. `SessionStart` now reports it, and `lifecycle.ApplyActivitySignal` special-cases it to stamp `FirstSignalAt` (proof the hook pipeline is wired) without ever touching `Activity.State` — a late or out-of-order signal-only can never stomp a real state that already arrived, so this doesn't weaken detection of a genuinely broken hook pipeline.

Fixes #2604

## Test plan
- [x] `cd backend && go build ./...`
- [x] `cd backend && go test ./...` (all green except 4 pre-existing unrelated failures in `internal/cli` spawn tests, confirmed failing identically on `main` without this change)
- [x] New/updated unit tests: `internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/activity_test.go`, `internal/lifecycle/manager_test.go` covering signal-only seeding `FirstSignalAt` without changing `Activity.State`, and a late signal-only not stomping an already-arrived real state.

title: fix: attribute cross-fork PRs pushed to a non-origin remote
body:
## Summary
- `discoverSubjects` hardcoded `headRepo` to the project's registered origin for every scanned remote, so a PR whose head branch actually lives in a different checkout remote (e.g. a personal `fork` remote used to push branches — the standard OSS contribution pattern) never matched in `candidatesForHeadRepo` and was silently dropped, leaving "no PR yet" forever even though the PR was real and open.
- Fix: pair each scanned repo against every remote in the checkout (including itself) as a `headRepo` candidate, instead of always using origin. `candidatesForHeadRepo` still strictly matches against the PR's actual GitHub head repo, and `matchSession` still requires a branch-prefix match, so over-generating candidates cannot misattribute a stranger's PR — it only allows a genuine cross-fork PR to be attributed correctly instead of dropped.

Fixes #2609

## Test plan
- [x] `cd backend && go build ./...`
- [x] `cd backend && go test ./...` (all pass except 4 pre-existing, unrelated `internal/cli` spawn-command failures that also fail on `main` without this change)
- [x] Added `TestPoll_DiscoversCrossForkPRPushedToForkRemote` covering the exact scenario from the issue: project origin is the upstream base, session pushes to a separate `fork` remote, and the PR opened against origin has its head in the fork — verified this test fails without the fix and passes with it.

title: fix(amp): remove unsupported --permission-mode CLI flags

## What

Removes `appendPermissionFlags` from the Amp adapter. Amp does not support `--permission-mode` CLI flags - its permission model is configured through settings/plugins (`amp.permissions`, `amp.guardedFiles.allowlist`, `amp.dangerouslyAllowAll`), not CLI arguments.

## Why

When AO launches Amp with a non-default permission mode, it builds commands like `amp --permission-mode acceptEdits` which can fail on startup or exit before opening the TUI. Projects that configure worker permissions globally make Amp workers fail to start even though plain `amp` works fine.

Closes #2561

- Removed `appendPermissionFlags` function from `amp.go`
- Removed the call to `appendPermissionFlags` in `GetLaunchCommand`
- Removed the call to `appendPermissionFlags` in `GetRestoreCommand`
- Updated comment on `GetLaunchCommand` to reflect `amp` (no flags)
- Updated tests: all permission modes now produce just `{"amp"}` with no `--permission-mode` flags
- Updated restore command test to expect `{"amp", "--resume", "T-abc123"}` without permission flags

## Testing

title: fix: make dev:web work on Windows with cross-env

The current script `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts` fails on Windows because `cmd.exe` and PowerShell don't support inline environment variable assignment. Contributors on Windows see:

'VITE_NO_ELECTRON' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.

- Changed script to `cross-env VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts`

`cross-env` is the standard solution for this - it sets environment variables in a cross-platform way without changing the command behavior on Unix.

Closes #2589

- On Unix: behavior is identical (cross-env just passes the env var through)
- On Windows: `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` is now properly set before vite runs
