title: fix: make project deletion tolerant of stale session state
body:
## What

Makes project deletion (`DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}`) robust to stale, legacy, or inconsistent session state by making session teardown errors non-fatal during project removal.

## Why

When a project has stale sessions (locked worktrees, archived project refs, missing runtime handles, etc.), `TeardownProject` returns an error and the entire `Remove` call fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The project stays registered and the user has no recovery path from the UI.

The issue (#2598) explicitly says: "local project removal must be robust to stale, legacy, partially missing, or otherwise inconsistent AO-managed state. If the user asks to remove a local project registration, AO should work around bad session/worktree/runtime records and complete the unregister flow wherever it can do so without deleting unpurged session state."

Closes #2598

## How

Changed `Service.Remove` in `backend/internal/service/project/service.go` to ignore the error from `m.sessions.TeardownProject(ctx, id)` instead of propagating it. The project is still archived (soft-deleted) regardless of whether session teardown succeeded.

This means:
- Sessions that can be torn down, will be
- Sessions that cannot (stale, locked, missing) are left for later cleanup
- The project is always archived, so the user can re-add it without a blocked delete

## Testing

Updated `TestManager_RemoveDoesNotArchiveWhenTeardownFails` to `TestManager_RemoveToleratesTeardownFailure`. The test now verifies that:
- Remove succeeds (no error) even when teardown fails
- The project is archived (no longer active) after Remove returns

Run: `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/project/...`

title: fix(codex): prefer npm/cargo paths over WindowsApps on Windows
body:
## What

On Windows, `ResolveCodexBinary` now checks known user-install paths (npm `codex.cmd`/`codex.exe`, cargo `codex.exe`) before falling back to `exec.LookPath`. When `exec.LookPath` is used as a last resort, paths under `WindowsApps` are skipped.

## Why

On Windows machines with both the WindowsApps packaged Codex and an npm-installed Codex CLI, `exec.LookPath("codex.exe")` resolves to the WindowsApps executable first. That binary cannot be launched directly by AO (Access denied), so the auth probe fails and the UI incorrectly shows `Codex - Needs auth` even though the npm Codex CLI is logged in.

Closes #2582

## How

1. Reorder the Windows resolution: check known npm/cargo candidate paths first, then fall back to `exec.LookPath` only if none exist.
2. Add `isWindowsAppsPath` filter to skip WindowsApps results from `exec.LookPath`, since those binaries cannot be spawned directly by the daemon.
3. Add `TestIsWindowsAppsPath` covering forward/back slashes, case sensitivity, and non-WindowsApps paths.

## Testing

- `TestIsWindowsAppsPath` passes on all platforms (pure string matching, no Windows required).
- Existing `TestResolveCodexBinaryFindsNVMInstallWhenPathIsSparse` still passes (Unix path resolution unchanged).
- The reorder only affects the Windows branch; non-Windows code paths are untouched.

title: SCM PR attribution relies purely on branch-name convention with no cryptographic session tie — collision risk widened by #2623
body:
## Summary

Found while reviewing #2623 (cross-fork PR attribution fix) locally. Not a regression introduced by that PR's logic, but the PR does widen an existing, pre-#2623 weakness's surface area — filing separately since it's a distinct concern from what #2609/#2623 fix.

**Core issue**: AO's PR-to-session attribution (`discoverNewPRs`/`matchSession` in `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`) has no cryptographic or authoritative link between a PR and the session it gets attributed to. Attribution is entirely a branch-name-prefix match against the session's namespace (`ao/<session-id>/...`), gated only by a repo-level filter (`candidatesForHeadRepo`). Nothing verifies that the branch was actually created by that session's own agent.

## Concrete scenario

Session `agent-orchestrator-6` has namespace `ao/agent-orchestrator-6` (from its working branch `ao/agent-orchestrator-6/root`) and a legitimate PR from a `fork` remote: branch `ao/agent-orchestrator-6/terminal-focus-fix`.

Now suppose a **second, unrelated** PR exists with the exact same branch name text, but living in a different repo — e.g. someone with push access to `origin` itself creates a branch literally named `ao/agent-orchestrator-6/terminal-focus-fix` and opens a PR from it (same-repo, not cross-fork). Scanning `origin`'s PR list finds this PR; `candidatesForHeadRepo` matches it against the `(to=origin, from=origin)` pair (which always exists — same-repo PRs were never the broken case); `matchSession` then matches purely on the branch name text and attributes it to `agent-orchestrator-6`, with zero verification that this worker's own agent created it.

## Confirmed: this predates #2623, but #2623 widens where it can happen

Traced the pre-fix code specifically to verify: `sessionRepo{repo: repo, headRepo: origin}` — when `repo == origin`, this produces exactly `{repo: origin, headRepo: origin}`, the same-repo pair, which existed unmodified in the original, broken code before #2623 touched anything. So a same-repo branch-name collision (as in the scenario above) was **already possible before #2623**.

What #2623 changes: it adds new valid `(to, from)` pairs beyond the single hardcoded one — e.g. `(origin, fork)`, `(fork, fork)`. So post-fix, a coincidentally- or deliberately-matching branch name living in **any** configured remote (not just `origin`) can now also trigger the same class of misattribution, where pre-fix only a same-repo branch could. The underlying mechanism (branch-name-only matching, no cryptographic tie) isn't new; the number of repos that could be used to exploit it goes up, proportional to how many remotes are configured.

## Why this is unlikely to bite in practice (mitigating factors, not a fix)

- The `ao/<session-id>/...` prefix is a fairly distinctive, AO-specific naming convention — an unrelated human contributor is unlikely to accidentally collide with it.
- In the common "contribute via fork" workflow, most tokens/contributors don't have push access to the project's registered `origin` at all (confirmed in this environment: `push: false` on the upstream repo for this token), which narrows who could even attempt a same-repo collision specifically.
- Cross-fork collisions would require push access to one of the *other* configured remotes, which is typically the contributor's own personal fork — a narrower attack surface than "anyone on the internet."

## Non-goals for this issue

Not proposing a specific fix here — options range from "accept as a known, low-likelihood limitation" to "add an explicit per-PR ownership marker" (which would tie into the hook-based registration design discussed in #2629) to "warn/flag when two PRs would attribute to the same session via branch-name match alone with different head repos, for human review." Filing primarily to have this traced and recorded, not to block or require #2623 on it — this predates that PR and isn't something it introduced.

## Related

- #2609 / #2623 — the fix whose review surfaced this
- #2629 — hook-based PR registration proposal; if built, would give a real, non-heuristic session↔PR link for the fast-path case, incidentally closing this gap for any PR that goes through it (the polling/branch-matching backstop would still carry this risk for anything that falls through to it)

title: feat(scm): targeted per-session backfill check for PRs that merged/closed before AO ever discovered them
body:
## Summary

Discovered while manually investigating why a worker session (`agent-orchestrator-14`, project `agent-orchestrator`) never moved out of `idle` despite its work being long done. Its real PR — [#2602](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2602), a fork PR, merged 2026-07-11 — was **never tracked by AO at all**, and there is currently no way to recover this after the fact.

## Root cause

`ListOpenPRsByRepo` (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go:67-77`) hardcodes `state=open` on the GitHub REST call. Once a PR merges or closes, it permanently drops out of every future listing AO makes — there is no other discovery path that revisits closed history. If a PR completes its entire open→merged (or open→closed) lifecycle during a window where AO's discovery didn't successfully see it while open — e.g. during the #2609 fork-attribution bug's active window, or during any daemon downtime — that PR, and the session it belongs to, is **permanently invisible** to AO. The session just sits at whatever activity-derived status it had (`idle` in this case) forever; the merge/close-triggered auto-termination logic (`ApplyPRObservation` in `lifecycle/reactions.go`) never runs, because nothing was ever tracked to observe a transition *on*.

Confirmed via direct API check this is currently unrecoverable through existing tooling: `ClaimPR` (the only manual "attach a PR to a session" mechanism) explicitly rejects non-open PRs (`claim_pr.go:109-111`, `ErrPRNotOpen`), so there's no way to even manually backfill a known already-merged PR today.

Checked whether this is a widespread pattern right now: it isn't — swept every currently-idle session across all three registered projects and only found this one instance. But it's a real, permanent, silent gap that will recur any time discovery misses a PR's entire open window (daemon downtime, an attribution bug like #2609, etc).

## Proposed approach — targeted, not a broad re-scan

The naive fix (widen `ListOpenPRsByRepo` to `state=all`) is a bad trade: closed/merged PR history only grows over a repo's lifetime and can vastly exceed open PR count for an active repo — paying that cost on every 30s poll forever, for every repo, just to catch a rare "missed it before it closed" case, doesn't scale.

Instead: a **targeted, per-session-branch search**, bounded by the number of live sessions rather than total repo history:

```
gh api search endpoint equivalent of:
gh pr list --repo <origin> --state all --search "head:<session-branch>"
```

This only needs to run for sessions that currently have **no tracked open PR at all** — a session with an already-tracked PR doesn't need it, since the normal refresh cycle already correctly handles that PR's eventual merge/close. Natural trigger points: once when a session goes idle with nothing tracked, or once per daemon boot for any live-but-untracked session — not a recurring per-poll cost. Cost scales with session count (small, bounded), not with total repo PR history (unbounded, ever-growing).

## Related

- #2609 / #2623 — the fork-attribution bug that likely contributed to #2602 being missed while it was still open
- #2631 — the branch-name-collision issue found during the same review, a related but distinct PR-attribution weakness
- #2629 — hook-based PR registration proposal; if built, would reduce (but not eliminate) how often this gap triggers, since a PR registered instantly at creation time never has a "window" where it could close unseen

title: feat: split design tokens into TS modules with generated CSS
body: ## Summary This PR replaces the monolithic hand-maintained `tokens.css` with a **typed TypeScript token pipeline** that generates a single committed CSS bundle. Visual output is unchanged, this is a **maintainability and safety** refactor, not a redesign. Follows up on #2535 (token-based design system) by making tokens the real source of truth: editable in TS, validated by tests, and enforced in CI. --- ## Problem Before this change: - Design tokens lived in **`frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`**, with a large amount of theme/bridge/utility CSS inlined in **`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`** - No compile-time types, no generator, no drift detection - Hard to know where to edit (CSS vs TS vs components) - `frontend/src/renderer/lib/design-tokens.ts` was a thin re-export shim That worked for the initial migration but didn’t scale for ongoing UI work or revamps. --- ## Solution ### New file layout (`frontend/src/styles/`) | File | Role | |------|------| | **`primitives.ts`** | Source of truth for values: colors, typography, space, radius, layout sizes, motion, terminal palette, theme metadata | | **`tailwind-bridge.ts`** | Maps Tailwind v4 `@theme` keys → semantic CSS vars (bridge aliases, font aliases, spacing/icon theme vars) | | **`utilities.ts`** | Token-derived `@utility` rules (dialog widths, purple/surface tints, timeline shadows, etc.) | | **`css-utils.ts`** | Naming conventions: `kebab()`, `layoutCssVarName()`, `parsePx()`, `isLayoutIconKey()` | | **`build-tokens-css.ts`** | Generator script — assembles all sections into one CSS string | | **`design-system.generated.css`** | **Committed generated output** (~631 lines) — do not hand-edit | | **`tokens.ts`** | Public barrel export for app code (`import from "../../styles/tokens"`) | | **`tokens.test.ts`** / **`css-utils.test.ts`** | Parity + convention tests | ## No UI / Visual changes ##Before ## After

title: feat: offer to relaunch sessions when the project default permission mode changes (#2504)
body:
Closes #2504.

When a project's default permission mode changes in Project Settings, running sessions keep their old mode. This adds an opt-in offer to relaunch (kill + restore) the affected sessions with the new mode. Restore already re-reads the project's current default, so a kill+restore picks up the new mode automatically; this PR wires the settings-change to a confirm + batch-relaunch flow.

## Backend
- Persist the launched permission mode on the session (`SessionMetadata.Permissions`, migration-free JSON field), set at spawn and restore, so we can tell which running sessions diverge from a new default.
- `Manager.AffectedByPermissionChange` / `RelaunchForPermissionChange` (`session_manager/permission_relaunch.go`): the affected set excludes terminated sessions, the orchestrator, and non-restorable sessions, and includes only those whose normalized stored mode differs from the project's current effective mode (role-override-masked changes are correctly treated as no-ops). Relaunch does a sequential kill+restore per session, records a per-session outcome, and never aborts the whole batch on one failure.
- Endpoints: `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/permission-relaunch/affected` and `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/permission-relaunch`, plus service wrappers, DTOs, and OpenAPI spec entries (regenerated).

## Frontend
- `RelaunchSessionsDialog`: fires from the settings save flow only when the mode actually changed and there is at least one affected session (auto-dismisses on zero). Lists affected sessions with `from -> to` modes, Cancel is the default (opt-in), reports "Relaunched X, failed Y", and invalidates the workspace query.

## Edge cases
- Orchestrator is never killed.
- Uncommitted work is preserved (kill keeps a dirty worktree, restore restores the branch and resumes the conversation); the dialog warns that an in-progress agent turn is interrupted.
- Sessions already on the new mode (including role-override-masked) are excluded from the count.
- Partial batch failure is reported per session and does not abort the batch; a session left terminated can be restored from the existing session UI.

## Testing
- Backend: `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean; new predicate tests (8 cases) and endpoint tests pass; full suite green apart from 4 pre-existing environment-only `cli/spawn_test.go` failures.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean; dialog and settings-form tests pass.

title: chore(release): stamp desktop app version 0.10.3
body:
## What

Stamp the desktop app version to **0.10.3** in `frontend/package.json` so the stable release cut resolves as `v0.10.3`.

## Why

Stable release builds read the version straight from `frontend/package.json` (`frontend-release.yml` does `v$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")`); unlike the nightly pipeline, the stable workflow does **not** stamp the version from the git tag. The committed value was still `0.10.0` (last touched in the 0.10.0 stamp, #2248), so cutting a release today would publish as `v0.10.0` and clobber the existing 0.10.0 release, and the stable update channel would never advance. This mirrors #2248 exactly (one-line stamp, `frontend/package.json` only).

## Scope

Bumps only `frontend/package.json` (the release-driving pin), matching the #2248 pattern. The `packages/ao*` npm CLI pins stayed at `0.10.0` through both the 0.10.1 and 0.10.2 stable cuts (they are not gated on the desktop release and are not published by CI), so they are intentionally left untouched here. Say the word if you want them synced too.

## Verification (local, on this branch)

- `backend`: `go build ./...` ✅, `go test ./...` ✅ (79 packages, clean env)
- `frontend`: `npm ci` ✅, `tsc --noEmit` ✅ (post-build), `vitest run` ✅, `electron-forge package` (full release build path) ✅
- Release workflow would now read `v0.10.3`.

## Release cut (maintainer, after merge — not done here)

This PR only bumps the version. Tagging, workflow dispatch, and the GitHub Release remain the release owner's manual step from `main`. The `publish-feed` job (needs `release` + `release-intel`) emits `latest.yml` / `latest-mac.yml` / `latest-linux.yml`, and `release-latest-guard.yml` enforces all three are present, so the #2270 missing-`latest-mac.yml` regression is covered.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

... (truncated)

title: Code review: add ability to stop a running review and restart it
body:
Once a code review of a worker's PR is started, there is no way to stop it or run it again. Add both:

- **Stop**: cancel an in-progress review (kill the reviewer run cleanly, mark the review as stopped rather than leaving it hanging).
- **Restart**: re-run a review from scratch, whether it was stopped, finished, or got stuck.

Expose both in the review UI (and `ao review` CLI where it fits). Useful when a review is running against a stale diff, the reviewer wedges, or new commits land mid-review.

title: Idle agents (finished turn, awaiting instructions) show as Working
body: ## Problem When an agent finishes its turn and sits at an empty prompt awaiting the next instruction, its card shows "Working" and stays in the WORKING column. There is no signal that it has stopped and is waiting on me. A session can sit like this for a day and still look busy. | Board: card shows "Working" | Same session: detail shows "Idle" | | --- | --- | | | | ## Expected An idle agent should be visually distinct from an actively working one. Not NEEDS YOU (that is for real questions and permission prompts, which are already handled by waiting_input/blocked), but a calm "stopped, waiting on you" state, ideally with an age like "idle 14h" so a stale one is obvious.

title: fix(board): show idle sessions as idle, not working
body:
Idle agents that finished a turn were rendered as "Working" on the board, in the same orange style and with the same pulsing sidebar dot as an actively running agent, so a finished, waiting agent looked identical to a busy one. This change renders idle sessions as a distinct calm state: a gray "Idle" badge on the board card and a non-pulsing dot in the sidebar. Actively working agents keep the "Working" style, and sessions awaiting a real decision stay in "Needs you", so no new column is added and the four-zone board is unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 550 passed
- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- prettier check on changed files: clean
- Verified in the desktop app: a finished agent shows "Idle" instead of "Working", flips back to "Working" when it resumes, and a permission prompt shows "Needs you"

Fixes #2641

title: Terminal: dragging a file onto a session terminal does nothing
body:
## Problem

Dragging a file (like a macOS screenshot) onto a session's terminal in the AO desktop app does nothing. The file is not inserted and nothing is attached.

In a normal terminal (Terminal.app, iTerm), dragging a file inserts its path, which a terminal agent like Claude Code then picks up as an attachment. The AO terminal does not do this, so there is no way to attach a screenshot to an agent from inside AO.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session and its terminal in the AO app.
2. Take a screenshot (or grab any file from Finder).
3. Drag it onto the terminal area.
4. Nothing happens. In a native terminal the same drag inserts the file path.

## Expected

Dropping a file on the terminal inserts its path, matching native terminal behavior, so an agent can attach it.

title: feat(terminal): insert dropped file paths like native terminals
body:
Dragging a file onto a session terminal did nothing, so a screenshot could not be attached to an agent from inside AO. This adds drop handling: the dropped file's bytes are stashed to a temp file by the main process and its path is inserted through the terminal's paste channel, mirroring a native terminal. Bytes are used rather than the path because a sandboxed renderer cannot resolve a dropped file's path on macOS (getPathForFile is empty for drag-drop in Electron 30-33).

Fixes #2643

Testing
- npm run typecheck / npm test / prettier: clean
- Verified in the app: dropping a screenshot inserts its path and the agent attaches it

title: feat: add Kimchi agent harness with full feature parity
body:
## Summary

Adds full Kimchi (`@kimchi-dev/cli`, binary `kimchi`) as a supported agent harness, achieving feature parity with Claude Code, Codex, and Pi adapters. Kimchi is a coding-agent CLI built on `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. AO drives it interactively (its TUI requires a TTY, which tmux provides), delivers the initial prompt as a trailing positional argument, appends system prompts via `--append-system-prompt`, and maps AO permission modes onto Kimchi's `--auto`/`--yolo` flags.

Session restore uses `--session <id>` — the native session id is captured from hook metadata and stored in AO session metadata. Hooks use Kimchi's native hook adapter (`.kimchi/hooks.local.json`), installed via `ao hooks kimchi <event>` commands. The native adapter is always-on — no user configuration needed for hooks to fire.

This PR also adds Kimchi as a **code-review adapter**, alongside the existing `claude-code`, `codex`, and `opencode` reviewers.

## Feature parity

### Initial implementation

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Core agent adapter (`ports.Agent`) | ✅ | Launch, restore, SessionInfo, GetConfigSpec, GetPromptDeliveryStrategy |
| Launch command | ✅ | `--model`, `--auto`/`--yolo`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--allow-tool`/`--deny-tool` |
| Prompt delivery | ✅ | In-command positional arg with sanitization against CLI option injection |
| System prompt | ✅ | Inline text or bounded file read (128 KB cap) |
| Restore/resume | ✅ | `--session <id>` with re-applied permissions and system prompt |
| Binary resolution | ✅ | PATH + well-known locations via shared `binaryutil` |
| Auth probe | ✅ | Two-tier: `KIMCHI_API_KEY` env → `~/.config/kimchi/config.json` |
| Hook installation | ✅ | 8 managed hooks in `.kimchi/hooks.local.json` (install/uninstall/check) |
| Activity derivation | ✅ | Custom `DeriveActivityState` for all 8 hook events |
| Activity dispatch | ✅ | Registered in `activitydispatch` dispatch map |
| Tool allow/deny scoping | ✅ | Comma-joined flags, comma validation, case-insensitivity awareness |
| Reviewer adapter | ✅ | Launch with `--auto` + read-only allowlist/denylist, message, cancel |
| SQLite migration | ✅ | `0048_allow_kimchi_harness.sql` adds `kimchi` to harness CHECK |
| OpenAPI spec | ✅ | `kimchi` in harness + reviewer DTO enums |
| CLI + README | ✅ | Listed in `--harness` help and supported harnesses |

### Parity fixes (added after feature parity audit)

These commits close the gaps identified when comparing against Claude Code, Codex, and Pi:

| Gap fixed | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `permissions` config field | Exposes permission mode enum in `GetConfigSpec`, matching Claude Code |
| `EmitsSubmitActivity` | Enables session manager confirm loop (Kimchi fires `user-prompt-submit` hooks) |
| `EmitsBlockedActivity` | Full confirm loop with blocked-state clearing (pre/post-tool-use trio allows correlation) |
| Model catalog discovery | Kimchi registered in `modelcatalog` discovery map (`--list-models`) |
| `agentbase.Base` embedding | Uses shared defaults, delegates `SessionInfo` to `agentbase.StandardSessionInfo` |
| PreLaunch trust bypass | Investigated — Kimchi has no first-run trust dialog; documented as non-gap |

### Investigated non-gaps

- **AgentExitDetector** — Kimchi's SessionEnd hook + reaper backstop covers exit detection; non-gap
- **ActiveTurnSteerer / TerminalActivityDetector** — optional capabilities only Codex implements; Kimchi's hooks cover activity detection; deliberate safety default
- **PreLaunch** — verified Kimchi has no trust dialog; non-gap

## Changes

**New adapter package** (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimchi/`):
- `kimchi.go` — adapter: launch, restore, prompt construction, permission flag mapping, tool flag scoping
- `auth.go` — auth probe (checks for API key / credentials)
- `hooks.go` — hook command generation for native Kimchi hook events, writing to `.kimchi/hooks.local.json`
- `activity.go` — activity state derivation from Kimchi hook events
- `install.go` — install path for the Kimchi binary
- `kimchi_test.go`, `auth_test.go`, `activity_test.go` — unit tests

**Reviewer adapter** (`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/kimchi/`):
- `kimchi.go` — reviewer wrapping the kimchi worker agent; implements `ports.Reviewer` + `ports.ReviewerCanceller`
- `kimchi_test.go` — unit tests

**Domain, registry, migration, spec, CLI, frontend**:
- `domain/harness.go` — `HarnessKimchi` constant + `AllHarnesses` registration
- `domain/reviewerharness.go` — `ReviewerKimchi` constant + `AllReviewerHarnesses` registration
- `adapters/agent/registry/registry.go` — register `kimchi.New()`
- `adapters/reviewer/registry.go` — register `kimchi.New()` in `Constructors()`
- `storage/sqlite/migrations/0048_allow_kimchi_harness.sql` — allow `kimchi` as valid harness value
- `httpd/controllers/dto.go` — `kimchi` in harness + reviewer DTO enum tags
- `httpd/apispec/openapi.yaml` — regenerated
- `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` — regenerated
- `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts` — `kimchi` in `AgentProvider` union
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/agent-options.ts` — Kimchi in agent options list
- CLI `--harness` help text, README supported harnesses list

title: fix(tmux): reap pane descendants on destroy
body:
## Summary
- list tmux pane session PIDs before destroying a session

- add unit coverage for pane PID discovery and reaper invocation

## Scope

title: feat(tracker): add Linear provider for issue intake
body:
## Summary

Issue intake now supports Linear alongside GitHub. A project can bind intake to a selected Linear team and auto-spawn worker sessions from that team's open, assigned issues, using the same durable deduplication and read-only guarantees the GitHub path already provides. Provider selection is surfaced in the settings and create-project UI without moving tracker logic into Electron.

Related: #2527, #2325

## What this adds

**Backend**
- New Linear tracker adapter over Linear's GraphQL API: `Get`, `List` (scoped to a team and, when set, the authenticated assignee), `ListTeams`, `AuthenticatedUser`, and `Preflight`, with typed authentication, not-found, and rate-limit errors.
- `ports.Tracker` gains `ListTeams`; the domain gains `TrackerTeam`, a `linear` provider, and a `teamId` field on `TrackerIntakeConfig` with cross-field validation (`teamId` required for Linear, rejected for GitHub; `repo`/`labels` rejected for Linear).
- A multi-provider resolver replaces the single GitHub tracker in daemon wiring. Each provider stays lazily constructed, so daemon readiness is never blocked by credential probing and no token is resolved until an enabled project of that provider is polled. Linear reads `LINEAR_API_KEY`.
- The intake observer now honors tracker-reported rate-limit backoff (Linear `Retry-After` and reset hints) instead of a flat failure window.
- Adds `GET /tracker-intake/linear/teams` (service, controller, OpenAPI spec) to list teams visible to the configured API key.
- Renames the provider-agnostic scope resolver from `scope.Repository` to `scope.Scope` and drops the compatibility alias.

**Frontend**
- Provider select (GitHub / Linear) in both the create-project sheet and project settings form. Selecting Linear reveals a team picker; labels and the matching-issue preview remain GitHub-only.
- `useTrackerIntakeTeams` hook backing the team picker, with loading and error states and a "select a team to start" hint.
- `teamId` is plumbed through the create sheet, settings form, and CLI (`--tracker` config), and cross-provider fields are scrubbed on provider switch so a saved config never mixes GitHub and Linear scope.

## Design notes

- Linear intake is team-scoped and read-only. `List` requests only spawnable open states (`triage`, `backlog`, `unstarted`) for the open filter, mapping Linear state types to the shared normalized issue states.
- Labels and preview are intentionally GitHub-only for this scope; the Linear adapter rejects label filters and the UI hides label/preview controls for Linear.
- All tracker logic stays daemon-owned. The Electron frontend only calls typed loopback API routes.
- Existing GitHub configs remain readable and unchanged; the GitHub intake behavior is untouched aside from the shared resolver and scope rename.

## Validation

- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npm --prefix frontend test` — 51 files, 492 tests passed
- `cd frontend && npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts`
- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...`
- Focused Go suites for the Linear adapter, observer, service, controllers, API spec, domain, daemon wiring, and shared intake scope — all passed
- `npm run api` with no generated OpenAPI or TypeScript schema drift

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- Search daemon logs for `linear tracker intake unavailable: LINEAR_API_KEY is not configured`, `tracker intake: resolve authenticated user failed`, `tracker intake: list issues failed`, `LINEAR_TEAMS_FAILED`, and `LINEAR_TEAMS_UNAVAILABLE`.
- Healthy signals: the team picker lists teams visible to the API key, Linear intake polls only the selected team's open assigned issues, rate-limit responses defer the next poll instead of hot-looping, and repeated polls do not create duplicate sessions.
- Failure signals: intake polling the wrong team, teams failing to load, repeated Linear API failures, or sessions spawned for non-open issues. Immediate mitigation is disabling `trackerIntake.enabled` for the affected project; roll back if the behavior reproduces across teams.
- Validation window: first week after release; owner: Agent Orchestrator maintainers.

title: feat(lifecycle): reap a session's Docker containers on terminal state (the container leg of #2523)
body:
## Problem

AO keys several resources to a worker session and tears some of them down on terminal state — but **Docker containers a worker starts are not one of them**. A worker that needs a database (or any service) commonly runs `docker run …` in its task, reaches a terminal lifecycle state, and the container survives indefinitely. `ao session kill` / cleanup removes the row and (tries to) reclaim the worktree, but never touches containers the worker launched.

This is the **container leg** of the same "tear down what the worker owns on session end" story that #2523 covers for orphan processes and #2608 / #2646 cover for worktrees. Those exist; the container case has no issue and no mechanism.

### Why it bites (real incident, one 16GB macOS machine, ao 0.9.x, tmux runtime)

Across **2026-07-12/13**, workers on a multi-project factory each improvised their own `docker run postgres` (per-branch `<id>-pg`, `<id>-pgmq`, ad-hoc `postgres:16` / `16-alpine` / pgmq images). Nothing tied a container's lifecycle to the session ending, so they accreted: **43 postgres containers running concurrently** ballooned the Docker VM until the host hit "out of application memory" (swap ~20–28GB) and every other worker slowed to a crawl. A manual sweep removed **59** stale containers + volumes (~59GB). A typical worker DB is ~165MB of *data* — the cost is the *processes*, each with its own shared buffers/page cache, not the data.

We now compensate downstream with (a) a machine-level launchd reaper that GCs worker containers by name/`ao.branch` label when the keyed PR closes, and (b) a shared-substrate "one container, one DB per branch" tool so 43 postgres processes become 1. Both are scar tissue for a lifecycle AO is the right owner of — we'd delete them the moment AO reaps a session's containers on terminal state.

## Proposal

Mirror #2523's orphan-process reaper for containers:

- **Auto-label** every container a worker starts with the session id (`ao.session=<id>` / `ao.branch=<branch>`) — e.g. by injecting `--label` when the worker shells out, or documenting the label convention so teardown can key on it.
- **Reap on terminal state / `ao session kill`**: `docker rm -f` the containers carrying the session's label, with an explicit **opt-out for deliberately-shared substrate containers** (a shared postgres, a registry) so a spared resource is a config choice, not an accident. Bias toward sparing on any ambiguity — a wrongly-reaped container can cost a live worker its database.
- Nice-to-have: surface per-session container count / footprint alongside the RSS surfacing proposed in #2523, so a leak is visible before the Docker VM pages out.

Sibling to #2523 (processes) and #2608 / #2646 (worktrees) — same trigger, remaining resource class. Happy to test on our fleet.

🤖 Filed with Claude Code on behalf of @Tonedeath

title: feat(mobile): haptic feedback, and stop long session ids overflowing the card
body:
## What

Two small mobile changes.

**1. Haptic feedback.** The app had none — every interaction was a silent `Pressable`. Adds `expo-haptics` behind a thin `lib/haptics.ts` wrapper (`tap` / `select` / `success` / `warning` / `error`), wired through the shared `ui.tsx` primitives (`Button` / `Pill` / `Card`) so most of the app gets feedback from one place, plus the moments that carry real meaning:

- selection tick on tab switches and filter pills
- light tap on cards, buttons, the spawn FAB, and pull-to-refresh
- `success` / `error` on spawn, send-prompt, kill, and the Settings connection test
- `warning` as the destructive kill confirmation is raised

Terminal keystrokes are deliberately left **silent** — a buzz per key makes heavy typing unpleasant. Every call is fire-and-forget and no-ops on web, so it can never throw into a press handler.

**2. Long session/project labels overflowed the card.** Session ids are minted as `<projectId>-<n>`, so a card printed the project slug twice (plus a third time in the title, which falls back to the id) and ran off the right edge of the screen.

- `shortSessionId()` strips the known project prefix and renders just the `#n` discriminator — this removes a duplicate, so **no information is lost**.
- `shortLabel()` middle-truncates the project (`agent-orch…8d163a851`), keeping the head *and* the hash tail — a plain tail-cut would make two projects sharing a base name render identically.
- Both are length-gated: short names (`web`) pass through untouched.
- Belt-and-braces: `numberOfLines={1}` on both, `flexShrink: 1` on the project so it yields first, `flexShrink: 0` on `#n` so the discriminator always survives.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` in `packages/mobile` — clean.
- `expo-haptics` ships native code, so this needs a rebuild (`expo run:ios` / `run:android`) and a **physical device** — haptics don't fire on simulators. On-device pass: tabs/pills tick, buttons and cards tap, spawn/kill/connect buzz correctly, terminal keys stay silent.

title: bug(scm): PR summary does not live-refresh for metadata-only GitHub updates
body:
## Source

Reported by: human in AO triage chat on 2026-07-13.

Symptom: in the current AO desktop, GitHub PR updates are not reflected in the session summary section. Reporter specifically pointed to SCM as the area to inspect.

## Verified Environment

- Checkout analyzed: `cc68be8f` (`fix: scope reviews tab to open PRs (#2506)`)
- Verified AO binary: built from this checkout with `cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao ./cmd/ao`
- Verified daemon: `/tmp/ao status` reports Go daemon ready on `127.0.0.1:3001` via `/Users/chauhan/.ao/running.json`
- `/tmp/ao version`: `dev`
- PATH note: bare `ao` is ambiguous on this machine; PATH contains `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao` and `/Users/chauhan/.local/bin/ao`, so diagnostics used `/tmp/ao`.

## What Happens

The UI summary section can remain stale when GitHub PR metadata changes without changing the PR scalar lifecycle fields.

Examples of summary-visible updates that can be missed live:

- PR title changes
- head SHA changes after new commits
- source/target branch metadata changes
- additions/deletions/changed-files changes
- author/html URL/provider metadata changes
- provider mergeability detail changes that only affect displayed reasons/links

A manual reload or some later unrelated scalar PR event may refresh the summary, which makes the issue look intermittent.

## Root Cause Trace

Current data path:

1. SCM observer polls GitHub in `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`.
2. It persists normalized PR facts via `Store.WriteSCMObservation`.
3. Desktop summary cards read detailed PR summaries from `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/pr`, implemented by `backend/internal/service/session/pr_summary.go`.
4. Frontend queries this via `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionScmSummary.ts`.
5. Live cache refresh depends on SSE CDC events. `frontend/src/renderer/lib/event-transport.ts` listens for `pr_updated` and invalidates both `workspaceQueryKey` and `sessionScmSummaryQueryKey()`.

The backend trigger is the gap. The active `pr_cdc_update` trigger in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0006_pr_session_changed_cdc.sql` emits `pr_updated` only when these fields change:

- `pr_state`
- `ci_state`
- `review_decision`
- `mergeability`

It does not emit when summary-rendered SCM metadata changes, including `title`, `head_sha`, `source_branch`, `target_branch`, `additions`, `deletions`, `changed_files`, `html_url`, `provider_mergeable`, or `provider_merge_state_status`.

Result: SQLite can contain updated SCM facts, but the renderer receives no CDC event, so the cached `session-scm-summary` query is not invalidated.

## Duplicate Search

Searched open and closed issues/PRs with:

- `SCM summary PR updates`
- `session scm summary`
- `stale PR dashboard`
- `metadata-only PR update`
- `pr_updated metadata`
- `pr_cdc_update summary`

Closest related issues:

- #1361: stale PR number when a closed PR is replaced by a new PR. Related stale dashboard symptom, different root cause.
- #1570: older web dashboard hard-reload/SSE cache issue. Related stale UI class, but points at old web/session event reducer behavior, not the current Go daemon PR CDC trigger.
- #2629: hook-based fast path for PR registration. Related SCM discovery latency, not summary invalidation after SCM writes.

No exact duplicate found for metadata-only SCM updates failing to invalidate the current Electron summary section.

## Suggested Fix Direction

No fix PR opened from this triage because the reporter explicitly asked not to implement a fix.

Likely fix is a new SQLite migration that recreates `pr_cdc_update` so `pr_updated` also fires for summary-rendered PR metadata changes. Do not edit existing merged migrations.

Recommended regression test:

- In `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/pr_cdc_test.go`, persist a PR with `WriteSCMObservation`.
- Write the same PR again with only summary metadata changed, such as `title`, `head_sha`, `additions`, or `changed_files`.
- Assert exactly one `pr_updated` event appears after the initial `pr_created` event.

Keep event type and payload shape stable unless there is a separate API decision to expose changed fields in CDC payloads; the frontend already invalidates the detailed summary query on `pr_updated`.

## Confidence / Priority

- Root-cause confidence: high. The summary query and frontend invalidation path are wired, but the trigger excludes summary-visible metadata-only changes.
- Priority: high. The dashboard summary is a primary live progress surface for SCM state, and stale PR updates undermine trust in session progress.

title: bug(scm): tracked PR can remain open after GitHub merge
body:
## Source

Reported by: human in AO triage chat on 2026-07-13.

Symptom: the `review-ui-runs` session still shows its PR as open even though the PR is merged on GitHub.

## Verified Environment

- Checkout analyzed: `cc68be8f` (`fix: scope reviews tab to open PRs (#2506)`)
- Verified AO binary: built from this checkout at `/tmp/ao`
- Verified daemon: `/tmp/ao status` reports ready on port `3001`, PID `24152`, data dir `/Users/chauhan/.ao/data`
- `/tmp/ao version`: `dev`
- PATH note: bare `ao` is ambiguous on this machine; diagnostics used `/tmp/ao`.
- `ao doctor`: GitHub token valid; SCM credentials are available.

## Concrete Repro / Live State

Session:

- Session id: `agent-orchestrator-37`
- Display name: `review-ui-runs`
- Project: `agent-orchestrator`
- Session status from `/tmp/ao session get agent-orchestrator-37`: `approved`
- Session branch: `ao/agent-orchestrator-37/root`

Local AO PR row in `~/.ao/data/ao.db`:

- PR: `https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2506`
- Number: `2506`
- `pr_state`: `open`
- `is_merged`: `0`
- `is_closed`: `0`
- `review_decision`: `approved`
- `ci_state`: `passing`
- `source_branch`: `ao/agent-orchestrator-37/reviews-open-prs`
- `target_branch`: `main`
- Last local observation: `2026-07-11 22:23:15.796325 +0000 UTC`

GitHub truth from `gh pr view 2506 --repo AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`:

- `state`: `MERGED`
- `closed`: `true`
- `mergedAt`: `2026-07-12T01:03:05Z`
- `closedAt`: `2026-07-12T01:03:05Z`
- `updatedAt`: `2026-07-12T01:03:06Z`
- merge commit: `cc68be8f7501973fec445d5b0f72a957b4d15972`

`change_log` has no event for `#2506` after `2026-07-11 22:23:15Z`, so AO never persisted the merge transition.

## Root Cause Trace

Current path:

1. SCM observer discovers sessions in `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go::discoverSubjects`.
2. It includes locally open tracked PRs via `openTrackedPRs`: PRs with `Number > 0 && !Merged && !Closed`.
3. It decides whether to fetch full PR metadata in `selectRefreshCandidates`.
4. A tracked PR is fetched only when:
   - local state is missing, or
   - the repo open-PR-list guard is not `NotModified`, or
   - the commit check-runs guard is not `NotModified`.

For a locally tracked PR whose GitHub state changes from open to merged/closed:

- The head commit checks often do not change after merge.
- After the repo open-list ETag has advanced once, future polls can see `NotModified` for the open-PR list.
- At that point there is no per-PR metadata/state guard, so the locally open PR is not fetched again.
- The stale local row remains `open`, and session status remains PR-derived (`approved` here) instead of `merged`.

This differs from #2632: there, AO never discovered the PR before it merged. Here, AO did discover and track `#2506`; it failed to observe the terminal state transition after tracking.

## Related Issues

- #2632: targeted backfill for PRs that merged/closed before AO ever discovered them. Related but distinct.
- #1803: older closed TypeScript-era report for merged PR showing open/working; root cause was different and not current Go SCM observer code.
- #2655: summary UI can miss metadata-only PR updates because CDC does not fire. Related stale summary class, but this bug is deeper: SQLite itself is stale.

## Suggested Fix Direction

No fix PR opened from this triage. The reporter previously asked not to implement fixes during this bug-triage pass.

Potential fix options:

- Add a bounded per-PR metadata/state guard for every locally open tracked PR, independent of the repo open-list guard and commit-check guard.
- Or periodically force-fetch locally open tracked PRs after a max age, even when repo/check ETags are unchanged.
- Add a focused observer regression test where a locally open tracked PR is skipped by repo/check guards after its provider state becomes merged, then assert AO eventually fetches and persists `pr_state=merged`.

The fix should preserve the existing behavior that merged/closed local PRs are no longer polled indefinitely.

## Confidence / Priority

- Root-cause confidence: medium-high. Live state proves the tracked PR is stale in SQLite, not just stale UI cache. Code trace shows locally open tracked PRs can be gated entirely by repo open-list/check guards, with no direct PR-state freshness check.
- Priority: high. A merged PR remaining open blocks the lifecycle/session status from reaching `merged`, leaving review/session UI misleading and potentially preventing cleanup or downstream automation.

title: fix: use cross-env for dev:web on windows
body:
## What

`npm run dev:web` fails on Windows because `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1` is Unix-only syntax. Windows cmd/powershell doesn't support inline env vars that way.

## Fix

Use `cross-env` to set the environment variable cross-platform. Added `cross-env` to devDependencies.

Closes #2589

## Before
```
"dev:web": "VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts"
```

## After
```
"dev:web": "cross-env VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts"
```

Replaces #2626 (which had merge conflicts from 11 commits behind main).

title: Orchestrator fails to spawn when a task is already running on a worker — missing default value for harness

title: docs(mobile): rewrite README as a dev-build run guide
body:
## What

Rewrites `packages/mobile/README.md` into an actual end-to-end run guide for the mobile app.

The old README was misleading in two load-bearing ways:

- It told you to run the app in **Expo Go**.
- It told you to point Settings at *"the AO server HTTP API port"*, which reads as `3001` — the **loopback** port a phone can never reach.

## The README now covers

- **Connect Mobile, from the desktop.** Start the desktop app (packaged or `cd frontend && npm run dev`), open **Sidebar → Settings menu → Connect Mobile**, flip **Enable mobile** on, and read the pairing QR / `host:port` / 8-char password. Also documents the loopback `POST /api/v1/mobile/enable|disable` + `GET /status` routes for a headless daemon.
- **The right port.** The phone talks to the LAN bridge on **3011**, not the loopback **3001**.
- **Development builds only — Expo Go is unsupported.** `expo-build-properties` (the Android `usesCleartextTraffic` flag the plaintext LAN bridge depends on) is a build-time config plugin that doesn't exist in Expo Go; the custom `scheme` and app identity don't apply either; and `expo-notifications` remote push doesn't work there at all.
- **Cabled-device setup.** iOS: Developer Mode, `npx expo run:ios --device`, the Xcode signing-team fixup, and the iOS **Local Network** permission (deny it and the app silently can't reach the daemon). Android: USB debugging, `adb devices`, `npx expo run:android --device`, `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081`. Plus simulator/emulator daemon hosts (`127.0.0.1` / `10.0.2.2`).
- **Install traps that actually bite here.** Never `npm install --force` (it hoists SDK-incompatible transitive Expo deps → native crash on launch), and don't remove the `metro.config.js` React pin (two React instances → *"main has not been registered"* at startup).
- Troubleshooting table, project layout, and `npm run typecheck`.

## Notes

- Docs only — no code, config, or dependency changes.
- The package has no `expo-dev-client` dependency today, so `expo run:*` produces a plain RN debug build that talks to Metro with no in-app launcher. The README says so and gives the one-liner to add it, rather than pretending the launcher is there.

title: Session side effects (tmux, branches, agent run-file) collide across AO instances on one machine
body:
## Summary

Several session side effects are keyed on the per-project session id (`<project>-<n>`), which is unique only **within one data dir's SQLite database**. AO also resolves the daemon run-file from the default location rather than from the active data dir. So when two AO instances run on the same machine — for example a packaged app on the default `~/.ao` and a dev build on `~/.ao/dev` — their session-id counters drift apart and their agents address the wrong daemon. Because the tmux server, the git remote, and the agent→daemon hook channel are all shared across instances, a session id created by one instance collides with leftovers from the other.

This causes three reproducible failures.

## Symptoms

**1 — Spawns fail with "duplicate session".** A second instance reuses a session id that another instance already has as a live tmux session, so `tmux new-session` fails with `duplicate session`. Workspace setup rolls back, the seed row is deleted, and the session disappears from the UI. Since the rolled-back id is freed, the counter never advances and every poll retries the same colliding id.

**2 — A stale PR is shown as "ready to merge".** The SCM observer attributes a PR to a session by branch namespace (a `.../root` branch owns every sibling branch, so stacked child PRs attach to their session). A reused session id lands on the same branch namespace an earlier session used, so a freshly-spawned session that has produced nothing inherits an old open PR and is shown as mergeable.

**3 — A working session shows "Needs you" instead of "Working".** Spawned agents receive `AO_DATA_DIR` but not `AO_RUN_FILE`, and the run-file default ignores the data dir. An agent launched by a non-default-data-dir daemon therefore runs its activity hooks against the wrong run-file (`AO daemon is not running`), so the signal never reaches the daemon that owns the session. Its activity stays idle and a session that is actively working never surfaces as `working` (until a PR later changes its status).

## Root cause

Session ids are unique per database, not per machine, and the run-file is resolved from the default location rather than the running daemon. Nothing scopes the shared surfaces — the global tmux server, the git remote, and the agent→daemon hook channel — to the instance that owns the session.

## Fix

Derive a per-instance namespace from the data dir and apply it to the shared surfaces:

- The tmux session name and the session branch prefix are namespaced, so two instances never collide on a name or claim each other's branches/PRs.
- The daemon exports its own resolved run-file to spawned and restored agents, so their hooks always reach the daemon that launched them.

**Backward compatible:** the default data dir yields an empty namespace and already resolves the same run-file agents use today, so existing installs are unchanged with no migration. Only instances on a non-default data dir are scoped.

## Acceptance

- Two instances on different data dirs spawn same-id sessions without a `duplicate session` error.
- A session never inherits a PR from another instance's branch namespace.
- A spawned agent's activity hooks reach its own daemon; an actively-working session with no PR shows `working`.
- Default data dir: tmux names, branch names, and run-file resolution are unchanged (regression-tested).

title: fix(terminal): portable dropped-path escaping and drop-file cleanup
body:
Follow-up to review feedback on #2644 (terminal file drop). Three gaps raised in review are addressed here:

- Path escaping is now platform-aware (POSIX single-quote with `'\''` escaping, double-quote on Windows) and quotes on any unsafe character, not just whitespace. Clean paths stay raw, so the common drop is unchanged.
- Dropped temp copies are pruned when older than a day, before every save, so terminal-drops no longer grows without bound.
- The save and drop logic is extracted into tested modules: basename sanitization and path-traversal refusal, age-based pruning, POSIX and Windows quoting, and the drop flow (single file, multiple files, partial failure, empty).

Testing

title: fix(runtime): scope session side effects per data dir
body:
## Summary

Several session side effects are keyed on the per-project session id (`<project>-<n>`), which is unique only **within one data dir's SQLite database**. When two AO instances run on the same machine (e.g. a packaged app on the default `~/.ao` and a dev build on `~/.ao/dev`), their id counters drift and their agents address the wrong daemon, so a session created by one instance collides with the other on the shared tmux server, git remote, and agent→daemon hook channel. This scopes those surfaces to the instance that owns the session, leaving the default single-instance behavior byte-for-byte unchanged.

Closes #2662

## What this fixes

1. **Spawn "duplicate session".** A reused session id collides with another instance's live tmux session, so `tmux new-session` fails, the spawn rolls back, and the session disappears (the freed id is retried forever).
2. **Stale PR shown as "ready to merge".** A reused id lands on the branch namespace an earlier session used, so a freshly-spawned session inherits an old open PR and is shown as mergeable.
3. **A working session shows "Needs you", not "Working".** Spawned agents got `AO_DATA_DIR` but not `AO_RUN_FILE`, and the run-file default ignores the data dir, so an agent from a non-default-data-dir daemon runs its activity hooks against the wrong run-file (`AO daemon is not running`). The signal never lands and an actively-working session (before any PR) never shows `working`.

## What this adds

- `config.InstanceNamespace(dataDir)` → `""` for the canonical default data dir, `i-<6 hex of sha256(abs path)>` otherwise.
- **tmux:** the runtime carries the namespace and names the session `<ns>-<id>` once (before the existing sanitize rules), stores it in the `RuntimeHandle`, and reuses that handle for attach/probe/destroy — so the create name and the lookup name are always identical. Threaded via `runtimeselect.New(dataDir, log)`; the CLI attach hint uses the same helper.
- **branches:** worker/orchestrator branches become `ao/<ns>/<id>/...` when the namespace is non-empty. SCM attribution reads the stored branch, so instances isolate with no observer change.
- **run-file:** the daemon exports its resolved run-file to spawned and restored agents as `AO_RUN_FILE` (via the shared spawn/restore env builder), so agent hooks reach the daemon that launched them.

## Design notes

- **Backward compatible.** The default data dir yields an empty namespace, and its run-file already equals what agents resolve today. Existing installs get identical tmux names, branches, and hook behavior; no DB migration. Existing sessions keep their stored non-namespaced handle, so boot reconciliation still re-attaches them. Only sessions on a non-default data dir are scoped.
- Session ids are untouched — UI, worktree paths, and the DB are unaffected. No behavior change on Windows/ConPTY.

## Validation

- `gofmt -l` on touched files — clean
- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...`
- `go test ./internal/config/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/... ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/observe/scm/... ./internal/daemon/...` — all passed (real tmux/socket tests included)
- Full `go test ./...` — green except the pre-existing `kilocode` interactive-shell test, unrelated
- New tests: namespace derivation, tmux create==lookup naming under a namespace (matched by command so it's robust to unrelated Create steps), branch namespacing, SCM attribution isolation across namespaces, and `AO_RUN_FILE` presence on the agent env
- Verified end-to-end on a scratch instance: a namespaced spawn succeeded with no `duplicate session`, and the agent env carried the daemon's own run-file so an activity hook flipped the session to `working` (the same hook fails with `AO daemon is not running` without it)

## Post-Deploy Monitoring

- Healthy: two instances on different data dirs spawn same-id sessions without `duplicate session`; no cross-instance PR attribution; an actively-working session with no PR shows `working`; default installs show unchanged names, branches, and hook delivery.
- Failure: `duplicate session` across instances, a session inheriting a foreign PR, a working session stuck idle, or any default-install name/branch/hook change.
- Validation window: first week after release; owner: Agent Orchestrator maintainers.

title: security: add environment: nightly to signing jobs in frontend-nightly.yml
body:
## What

Adds `environment: nightly` to the two signing jobs in `frontend-nightly.yml`:

- `release` (matrix: macOS, Windows, Linux)
- `release-intel` (macOS Intel)

## Why

The six macOS signing secrets (`CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_API_KEY_BASE64`, `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`) are currently repo-level secrets. A write-access user could push a `desktop-v*` tag whose commit edits `frontend-release.yml` to drop the `environment: release` line, and the workflow would still read the repo-level secrets and produce a signed release without approval.

Moving secrets to the `nightly` environment closes this: a gate-stripped workflow gets no signing secrets at all. The nightly environment should have **no required reviewers** (it runs unattended on cron) and branch policy set to `main` only.

## Admin steps (before merging)

- [ ] Create a `nightly` environment in repo Settings > Environments
- [ ] Add the same six signing secrets to the `nightly` environment
- [ ] Set branch policy to `main` only (no required reviewers for nightly)

## Admin steps (after verifying)

- [ ] Delete the six repo-level secrets once a nightly build goes green on environment secrets

Closes #2395

title: fix: use .ico for windows taskbar icon
body:
## Problem

On Windows 10, the app icon shows blank in the taskbar (#2340).

## Root cause

`windowIconPath()` returns `icon.png` on all platforms. While Electron accepts PNG for the BrowserWindow icon, Windows 10 taskbar rendering with frameless windows (`titleBarStyle: "hidden"` + `titleBarOverlay`) is more reliable with a proper `.ico` file that contains multiple sizes.

The `.ico` file (`assets/icon.ico`, 81KB, 6 sizes: 16/32/48/64/128/256 at 32bpp) already exists in the repo but is not shipped as an extraResource and is not used for the BrowserWindow icon at runtime.

## Fix

Two changes:

1. `forge.config.ts`: add `assets/icon.ico` to `extraResource` so the `.ico` is available in the packaged app's Resources directory.

2. `src/main.ts`: `windowIconPath()` now returns `icon.ico` on `win32` and `icon.png` on other platforms. Falls back to `icon.png` if the `.ico` is not found (the `existsSync` check handles this).

No behavior change on macOS or Linux.

Closes #2340

title: fix: force re-fetch open PRs after DefaultPRMaxAge regardless of ETag (#2656)
body:
## What this does
Puts a ceiling on how long a session's open PRs can read stale: once the cached snapshot is older than `DefaultPRMaxAge` (5 minutes), the observer forces a full re-fetch instead of relying on the conditional-request fast path.

## Problem
When a PR is merged or closed on GitHub its head SHA does not change, so the per-commit checks guard correctly returns `304 Not Modified` (the check runs really did not change). The observer only consults that guard and the repo-level PR-list guard, and neither is a conditional request against the PR's own state, so it infers "unchanged" from signals that do not track the merged/closed transition. A PR can therefore keep reading "open" in AO until the next unconditional refresh.

This is a bounded-staleness backstop, not a claim that GitHub violates ETag semantics: it caps how long that inference can persist. The deeper fix (a per-PR conditional request, or making the list guard authoritative for PR state) is a larger change still under discussion in the review thread. Refs #2656.

## Changes
- `backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go` — force an unconditional re-fetch of open PRs once the cached snapshot exceeds `DefaultPRMaxAge`, with the rate-limit trade-off documented (bypasses the 304 savings; all stale PRs refetch in the same tick).
- Adds a regression test for the stale-"open"-PR case that backdates the cache entry past `DefaultPRMaxAge`.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/observe/scm/...` passes, including the new test.

title: fix: persist WorkspaceRepoPath in metadata to avoid projectRepoResolver on cleanup (#2608)
body:
## What this does
Persists the workspace repo path (`WorkspaceRepoPath`) in a session's stored metadata so project/session teardown can locate and reclaim the session's worktree without having to re-resolve the project.

## Problem
Cleanup relied on `projectRepoResolver` to find a session's worktree at teardown time. For archived (or otherwise stale) projects that lookup could fail, so cleanup couldn't reclaim the worktree — leaving orphaned worktrees on disk. Refs #2608.

This change is forward-only: it fixes newly spawned sessions but does not backfill `WorkspaceRepoPath` for sessions persisted before the upgrade, so it does not fully remove the symptom for pre-upgrade sessions. It therefore only references #2608 rather than closing it; a separate backfill is needed before the issue can be closed.

## Changes
- `backend/internal/domain/session.go` — add `WorkspaceRepoPath` to session metadata.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` — populate it on spawn and use it during cleanup instead of depending on the resolver.
- `backend/internal/cli/session.go` — plumb/surface the field where needed; the cleanup command includes a `--dry-run` flag that reports what would be reclaimed without tearing anything down.

## Testing
- Build + targeted package tests green.
- Remote CI green.
- Added a round-trip test pinning the `WorkspaceRepoPath` write (spawn metadata) and read (teardown) sides; mutation-verified to fail if either side is removed.
