title: feat(release): publish Homebrew cask on every stable desktop release
body:
## What

Ships the desktop app as a Homebrew cask, updated automatically on every stable release. Adds a `publish-cask` job to `frontend-release.yml`, a reviewable cask template, and docs.

## Why

macOS users can install and stay current with:

```
brew install --cask agentwrapper/homebrew-tap/agent-orchestrator
```

We ship our own tap (`AgentWrapper/homebrew-tap`), not `Homebrew/homebrew-cask`: Homebrew rejects self-submitted casks whose repo is under any one of 90 forks / 90 watchers / 225 stars, and we are under on watchers. The own tap has no such gate.

## How it works

`publish-cask` runs after `publish-feed`, only on `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` (fork test releases skip it). It downloads the two stable macOS aliases (`agent-orchestrator-darwin-{arm64,x64}.zip`), computes their sha256, renders `frontend/packaging/homebrew/agent-orchestrator.rb.tmpl`, and pushes `Casks/agent-orchestrator.rb` to the tap. It is `continue-on-error: true`, so a tap hiccup never fails the product release.

The cask sets `auto_updates true`: Homebrew installs the initial version, then electron-updater keeps driving in-app updates from the Releases feed, so `brew upgrade` never fights the in-app updater.

## Required before it works

Add secret **`HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`** on this repo: a fine-grained PAT (or App token) with **contents: write** on `AgentWrapper/homebrew-tap`. The default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot push to a different repo. Without it the job no-ops with a log line, so this is safe to merge before the secret exists.

## Validation

- A v0.10.3 cask is already live in the tap (hand-published from this template with the real release sha256s); `brew info --cask` resolves clean (version, `auto_updates`, macOS >= 11, `Agent Orchestrator.app`), no lint warnings.
- Next stable cut (0.10.4) will exercise the automated job.

## Notes

- Homebrew 6.0 requires a one-time `brew trust agentwrapper/tap` when installing from a third-party tap (worth a README line, follow-up).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add command center workflows
body:
## What changed

- adds the Command Center conversation surface with chronological prompt/output history, model/effort/access controls, and worker lifecycle feedback
- replaces the internal “Kanban” wording with the clearer “Task board” label across navigation and headings
- places a **Review decisions** button directly inside the **In review** lane; it opens the full decision cards in a focused dialog
- keeps one background reviewer manager mounted while the dialog is open, so opening the decisions view no longer resets retry/rejection state or starts a competing loop
- shares reviewer progress/errors with the dialog and routes its **Refresh** action back to the background manager
- removes the separate Review mode from the orchestrator terminal
- adds concrete one-click review choices, working Refresh behavior, and per-choice sending feedback
- starts a fresh one-shot reviewer for each new batch instead of writing review prompts into an idle, potentially polluted terminal session
- gives cold reviewer startup 30 seconds and the structured response 90 seconds instead of discarding a healthy reviewer after five seconds
- strictly bounds eight-item reviewer prompts to the daemon's 4,096-byte limit while retaining every session
- pins the dedicated reviewer to the AO-compatible `gpt-5.6-sol` model at low effort
- makes Codex conversation discovery support both AO's legacy `data/codex-home/sessions` location and the current provider-home `.codex/sessions` location
- adds deferred Suggestions, a live Sol/Fable/K3 discussion, and a low-effort Quick request session for git, GitHub, agent-status, and project-location checks
- adds consistent hover, keyboard-focus, and pressed-down feedback across buttons

## Root cause

There were two independent production failures. First, current Codex (`0.144.3`) writes rollouts beneath the provider home at `~/.codex/sessions`, while AO only searched the older AO-scoped `data/codex-home/sessions` tree. Valid responses therefore appeared as `source: unavailable`.

After fixing conversation discovery, the real eight-item project batch still never started: its “compact” request exceeded the daemon's 4,096-byte prompt limit and every retry returned `PROMPT_TOO_LONG`. Because the dialog had passive local state separate from the background manager, it hid that error behind “still turning.” Five-second cold-start handling and reuse of polluted idle helpers compounded earlier attempts.

The fix searches both rollout roots, keeps reviewer ownership stable, generates a strictly bounded valid request, shares manager state with the dialog, launches a clean reviewer for a new batch, and uses realistic startup/response windows.

## Validation

- reproduced the rollout failure with `unreal-projects-52`, then verified the installed backend returned `source: codex` with its exact diagnostic response
- captured the live background-manager state showing `prompt is too long (PROMPT_TOO_LONG)` for batch `a84c8cf3`
- installed the final package; it immediately created `unreal-projects-53`, completed batch `a84c8cf3` in about 21 seconds, and returned eight items with two choices each
- inspected the installed dialog: it showed **Review ready**, rendered all eight decision cards, and no longer displayed “still turning”
- 32 focused renderer tests passed, including oversized eight-item prompt and shared Refresh/error-state regressions
- TypeScript typecheck passed
- `go test ./internal/service/session` passed, including the provider-home rollout regression test
- production Electron packaging passed on Windows

## Notes

The broader `internal/httpd/...` run still has two unrelated pre-existing failures: a Windows port-conflict fallback assertion and a stale embedded OpenAPI check. This change does not modify the API contract.

This remains a draft for upstream review and CI.

title: bug(lifecycle): reaper cannot terminate dead sessions stuck in blocked/waiting_input state (sticky-state zombie sessions)
body:
## Problem

When a session is in a sticky activity state (`blocked` or `waiting_input`) and the agent process dies (crash, SIGKILL, OOM kill), the reaper detects `ProbeDead` but `runtimeClearlyDead` returns `false` because `hasRecentActivity` unconditionally returns `true` for sticky states. The session is never marked terminated and stays as a zombie forever — the dashboard shows "needs input" even though the agent is gone and no process exists to respond.

This is silent: there is no error, no log, no user-facing signal. The session looks alive but is dead. The only recovery is a manual `ao session kill`.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/lifecycle/runtime.go`:

```go
func hasRecentActivity(a domain.Activity, now time.Time, window time.Duration) bool {
    switch {
    case a.State == domain.ActivityExited:
        return false
    case a.State.IsSticky():          // blocked, waiting_input
        return true                    // <-- always "recent", even if the process is dead
    case a.LastActivityAt.IsZero():
        return false
    default:
        return now.Sub(a.LastActivityAt) <= window
    }
}

func runtimeClearlyDead(f ports.RuntimeFacts, activity domain.Activity, now time.Time, window time.Duration) bool {
    observedAt := timeOr(f.ObservedAt, now)
    return f.Probe == ports.ProbeDead && !hasRecentActivity(activity, observedAt, window)
}
```

`IsSticky()` returns `true` for `ActivityWaitingInput` and `ActivityBlocked` (see `backend/internal/domain/activity.go`). The intent is correct: a sticky state should not be aged out by wallclock alone, because a paused agent is still paused until a new signal says otherwise. But when the reaper confirms the process is dead (`ProbeDead`), stickiness should not protect the session from termination. The agent cannot emit a new signal — it is gone.

The existing test `TestRuntimeObservation_InferredDeathSetsTerminated` only covers a stale `active` session (2 min old, outside the 60s window). There is no test for `blocked` or `waiting_input` + `ProbeDead`.

## Impact

- A session paused on a permission dialog (`blocked`) whose agent crashes stays in "needs input" forever. The user waits for a response that never comes.
- A session waiting for user input (`waiting_input`) whose agent is OOM-killed stays "waiting" forever. No notification, no auto-terminate, no restore.
- The `Reconcile` boot-time pass also uses `reconcileLive` which calls `saveAndTeardownOne` — but only if `runtime.IsAlive` reports false. For tmux, `IsAlive` checks "does the tmux session exist" (issue #2089), not "is the agent process alive". So the tmux shell may survive the agent crash, making `IsAlive` return true, and `reconcileLive` adopts the dead session as live. The reaper is the only defense, and it is blocked by the sticky-state guard.

## Proposed fix

`hasRecentActivity` should not return `true` for sticky states when the probe explicitly reports `ProbeDead`. The stickiness guarantee is about not aging out based on wallclock; it should not override a confirmed runtime death.

Option A: Pass the probe result into `hasRecentActivity` and short-circuit:

```go
func runtimeClearlyDead(f ports.RuntimeFacts, activity domain.Activity, now time.Time, window time.Duration) bool {
    if f.Probe != ports.ProbeDead {
        return false
    }
    // A confirmed dead probe overrides stickiness: the agent process is gone
    // and cannot emit the signal that would clear the sticky state.
    if activity.State.IsSticky() {
        return true
    }
    return !hasRecentActivity(activity, timeOr(f.ObservedAt, now), window)
}
```

Option B: Remove the sticky check from `hasRecentActivity` and handle stickiness only in the aging/demotion path (where it belongs), not in the death-detection path.

Option A is minimal and does not change the aging/demotion behavior.

## Test plan (TDD)

In `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager_test.go`:

1. `TestRuntimeObservation_DeadProbeTerminatesBlockedSession` — session in `blocked`, `ProbeDead` → expect `IsTerminated=true`, `Activity.State=exited`. Currently fails (session stays blocked).

2. `TestRuntimeObservation_DeadProbeTerminatesWaitingInputSession` — session in `waiting_input`, `ProbeDead` → expect `IsTerminated=true`, `Activity.State=exited`. Currently fails.

3. `TestRuntimeObservation_StickySessionNotTerminatedByFailedProbe` — session in `blocked`, `ProbeFailed` → expect no mutation (failed probe must not be collapsed to dead). Should pass.

4. `TestRuntimeObservation_StickySessionNotTerminatedByAliveProbe` — session in `waiting_input`, `ProbeAlive` → expect no mutation. Should pass.

5. `TestRuntimeObservation_ActiveSessionStillTerminatedWhenStale` — existing test, still passes (regression guard).

## Related issues

- #1894 (closed): Frontend sticky-state staleness (display layer). The backend counterpart was not addressed.
- #2089: `isAlive` treats tmux-session-exists as agent-alive. Makes the reaper the only defense for crashed agents whose tmux shell survives.
- #1187: Frontend zombie sessions (TypeScript). Different layer, same class of bug.

title: bug(tracker-intake): terminated sessions block re-spawn of their issue (intake never re-assigns killed/crashed issues)
body:
## Problem

The tracker intake observer builds its "already has a session" set from `ListAllSessions`, which includes terminated sessions. When a worker session for an issue is killed or crashes, the issue is still open in the tracker, but the terminated session's `issue_id` is in the `seen` set, so the intake poller skips it forever. No new session is spawned for that issue.

This is silent: the issue stays open, assigned, and unworked on. No error, no log, no notification. The user has to manually spawn a new session.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/observe/trackerintake/observer.go`:

```go
func seenIssueIDs(sessions []domain.SessionRecord) map[domain.IssueID]bool {
    seen := make(map[domain.IssueID]bool, len(sessions))
    for _, sess := range sessions {
        if sess.IssueID != "" {
            seen[sess.IssueID] = true
        }
    }
    return seen
}
```

Called from `Poll`:

```go
sessions, err := o.store.ListAllSessions(ctx)
// ...
seen := seenIssueIDs(sessions)
```

`ListAllSessions` returns every session row including terminated ones (the SQL query has no `WHERE is_terminated = 0` filter). So a killed session's `issue_id` blocks re-spawn indefinitely.

## Scenarios

1. User kills a worker session for issue #42 (agent was stuck). Issue #42 is still open. Next intake poll: `seen` includes issue #42 from the terminated session. No new session spawned. Issue sits unworked.

2. Agent crashes, reaper terminates the session (if not blocked by the sticky-state bug from #2745). Issue is still open. Same result: no re-spawn.

3. Spawn fails (e.g. binary not found). The session row is parked terminated. Issue is still open. Same result.

## Proposed fix

Filter out terminated sessions in `seenIssueIDs`:

```go
func seenIssueIDs(sessions []domain.SessionRecord) map[domain.IssueID]bool {
    seen := make(map[domain.IssueID]bool, len(sessions))
    for _, sess := range sessions {
        if sess.IssueID != "" && !sess.IsTerminated {
            seen[sess.IssueID] = true
        }
    }
    return seen
}
```

This way only active sessions block re-spawn. A killed session frees its issue for a new intake cycle.

## Test plan (TDD)

In `backend/internal/observe/trackerintake/observer_test.go`:

1. `TestSeenIssueIDs_ExcludesTerminatedSessions` - two sessions with same issue_id, one terminated, one live. Expect only the live one in the seen set. Currently fails (both included).

2. `TestPoll_RespawnsIssueAfterKill` - issue has a terminated session. Poll should attempt a new spawn. Currently fails (issue skipped).

3. `TestPoll_DoesNotRespawnIssueWithLiveSession` - issue has a live session. Poll should not spawn a duplicate. Should pass.

4. `TestPoll_SpawnsIssueWithNoPriorSession` - new issue, no session. Poll should spawn. Should pass.

## Related issues

- #2282: Tracker intake feature (original implementation)
- #2344: Tracker intake hardening

title: fix(lifecycle): dead runtime handle terminates sticky states
body:
## Problem

When a session is in a sticky activity state (`blocked` or `waiting_input`) and the agent process dies (crash, SIGKILL, OOM kill), the reaper detects `ProbeDead` but `runtimeClearlyDead` returns `false` because `hasRecentActivity` unconditionally returns `true` for sticky states. The session stays as a zombie forever - the dashboard shows "needs input" even though the agent is gone and no process exists to respond.

This is silent: no error, no log, no notification. The only recovery is a manual `ao session kill`.

Fixes #2745.

## Root cause

`runtimeClearlyDead` checked `!hasRecentActivity()` which returns `true` for sticky states regardless of the probe result. A confirmed dead probe should override the stickiness guarantee - the agent cannot emit the signal that would clear the sticky state because the process is gone.

## Changes

- `runtime.go`: In `runtimeClearlyDead`, check `ProbeDead` first. If the probe is dead and the state is sticky, return `true` (terminate). Otherwise fall through to the existing `hasRecentActivity` check for non-sticky states.

## Test plan (TDD)

Tests written first, verified failing, then implementation added:

1. `TestRuntimeObservation_DeadProbeTerminatesBlockedSession` - session in `blocked`, `ProbeDead` -> terminated
2. `TestRuntimeObservation_DeadProbeTerminatesWaitingInputSession` - session in `waiting_input`, `ProbeDead` -> terminated
3. `TestRuntimeObservation_FailedProbeDoesNotTerminateBlockedSession` - `ProbeFailed` must not terminate sticky session
4. `TestRuntimeObservation_AliveProbeDoesNotTerminateWaitingInputSession` - `ProbeAlive` must not terminate sticky session
5. `TestRuntimeObservation_InferredDeathSetsTerminated` - existing test, still passes (regression guard)

title: Hide reviewer prompts from shared terminals
body:
Resolves #2410 

## Issue

Reviewer sessions received AO’s complete review instructions as terminal-visible prompt text.

Because reviewer panes are shared PTYs, the full prompt could appear on desktop, mobile, and direct terminal attachments. This exposed internal workflow instructions and added substantial noise to the reviewer transcript.

## Fix

Store the complete reviewer task and standing instructions in AO’s private data directory instead of sending them through the PTY.

Reviewer panes now receive only a short reference to the task file. This applies to:

- Initial reviewer launches
- Reused reviewer panes
- Codex
- Claude Code
- OpenCode
- Desktop, mobile, and direct terminal attachments

The short reference includes the task-file path so reviewer panes created before a daemon restart can still process subsequent review requests.

## Files affected

- `backend/internal/review/launcher.go`
  - Writes reviewer task and system prompts under AO’s data directory.
  - Replaces terminal-visible prompts with a short task-file reference for both spawn and notify paths.

- `backend/internal/ports/reviewer.go`
  - Adds system prompt file support to reviewer invocations.

- `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/{codex,claudecode,opencode}/*.go`
  - Passes AO-owned system prompt files through each supported reviewer harness.
  - Preserves OpenCode’s existing inline fallback for direct callers.

- `backend/internal/daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go`
  - Supplies the configured AO data directory to the reviewer launcher.

- Reviewer launcher and adapter tests
  - Verify full prompt text stays in AO-owned files.
  - Verify only the short task reference reaches new and reused reviewer panes.
  - Cover Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.

## Validation

title: Centralize frontend session state presentation and align dashboard status visuals
body:
## Context

AO backend already provides a clean session read model:

```text
session.activity  // raw agent activity
session.status    // derived overall session status
session.prs       // PR facts
```

The backend state flow is correct: session activity is stored as durable facts, PR facts are stored separately, and `session.status` is derived on read from those facts. The problem starts in the frontend, where multiple components independently interpret `session.activity` and `session.status`.

This has caused status visuals to drift across surfaces. For example, the topbar may show the raw agent activity as `Idle`, while the sidebar or board may represent the same session through a different visual language. Recent fixes have addressed individual symptoms, but the underlying issue remains: frontend presentation rules are scattered across components.

## Problem

Frontend components currently decide state presentation locally:

```text
Topbar -> raw session.activity
Inspector -> raw session.activity + status/SCM pills
Board columns -> attentionZone(session.status)
Board card badge -> local sessionBadge(session)
Sidebar dot -> attentionZone(session) + custom idle logic
Browser panel -> session.status === "working"
```

This creates ambiguity because these are different concepts:

```text
Agent activity    = what the agent is doing right now
Session status    = overall derived session state
Attention zone    = where the session belongs in dashboard triage
```

The same word, especially `Working`, is overloaded across all three layers:

```text
activity.active
status.working
attentionZone.working
visual pulse/working indicator
```

These are related, but not equivalent.

## Goal

Keep backend state management unchanged. Centralize frontend presentation logic so every visual component consumes the same interpretation layer.

The frontend should explicitly distinguish:

```text
1. Agent activity view
   Source: session.activity
   Used for: topbar, inspector activity pill, browser "Agent working" indicator

2. Session status view
   Source: session.status
   Used for: board card badges, status labels

3. Attention zone view
   Source: session.status
   Used for: Kanban board columns and sidebar attention indicators
```

## Proposed Solution

Add a shared frontend presentation module, for example:

```text
frontend/src/renderer/lib/session-presentation.ts
```

It should expose helpers such as:

```ts
getAgentActivityView(session.activity)
getSessionStatusView(session.status)
getAttentionZoneView(session.status)
getSessionDotView(session)
```

All status-related visuals should consume these helpers instead of maintaining local switch statements.

## Component Behavior

### Topbar

Use `session.activity`.

Show what the agent is doing now:

```text
active -> Working
idle -> Idle
waiting_input -> Input Needed
blocked -> Awaiting Decision
exited -> Exited
unknown -> Unknown
```

### Inspector activity row

Use the same agent activity view as the topbar.

It may additionally show status/SCM pills such as `No Signal`, `CI Failed`, `Changes Requested`.

### Browser panel

Use raw `session.activity` to decide whether to show `Agent working`.

Do not use:

```ts
session.status === "working"
```

for this behavior.

### Board card badge

Use `session.status` via `getSessionStatusView()`.

Show clear status labels such as:

```text
Working
Idle
Input needed
No signal
CI failed
Changes requested
Review pending
Draft PR
PR open
Approved
Ready
Merged
Terminated
Unknown status
```

### Board columns

Use attention zone derived from `session.status`.

Keep the visible board label `In review` for the pending zone.

### Sidebar dot

Make it an attention indicator, not a mixed activity/status indicator.

It should follow the same attention-zone presentation as the board.

## Dashboard Attention Zones

Keep the current high-level zones:

```text
Ready to merge
Needs you
In review
Working
Done
```

Internal mapping can remain conceptually:

```text
approved / mergeable -> Ready to merge

needs_input / no_signal / ci_failed / changes_requested / unknown
-> Needs you

review_pending / pr_open / draft
-> In review

working / idle
-> Working

merged / terminated
-> Done
```

## Working vs Idle

Do not create a separate top-level Idle column.

Instead, keep idle sessions inside the Working column, but visually separate them into an Idle stack at the bottom.

Desired layout:

```text
Working
  Active sessions

  Idle
    Idle sessions
```

This means:

```text
status = working
-> Working column, active stack unless raw activity says idle

status = idle
-> Working column, Idle stack

status = working + activity.state = idle
-> Working column, Idle stack
```

This preserves the product meaning that idle sessions are still in-progress/not done, while making the current agent activity visually clear.

## Unknown Status

`unknown` is not a real backend business state. It is a frontend defensive fallback for contract drift, invalid/missing data, or frontend/backend version skew.

In the ideal production flow, `unknown` should never appear.

If it does appear, it should be visible and actionable, not hidden under `In review`.

Desired behavior:

```text
unknown -> Needs you
Card badge -> Unknown status
Dot -> attention/warning style
No working pulse
```

We should also consider telemetry/logging when the frontend maps a session to `unknown`, since it indicates a product/API contract issue.

## Expected Outcome

After this change:

```text
Topbar and inspector agree on raw agent activity.
Board card badges use one centralized session-status mapping.
Sidebar and board use the same attention-zone interpretation.
Browser panel uses actual agent activity instead of overall session status.
Idle sessions are visually separated inside Working.
Unknown status is surfaced clearly instead of silently bucketed.
Frontend state presentation rules live in one place.
```

This should reduce future status-display regressions and make the dashboard easier to reason about.

title: Resume agent sessions with their existing transcripts
body:
## Issue

Restoring an agent session restarted the harness with its original prompt instead of continuing the native agent conversation.

The Codex and Claude Code adapters already supported native resume commands, but AO did not persist the native `session_id` supplied by their hooks. Restore therefore received an empty resume handle and fell back to a fresh launch, losing the active transcript context.

## Fix

Capture `session_id` from supported agent hook payloads and persist it as the session's native resume handle.

The change:

- extracts native session IDs from supported hook payloads
- allows metadata-only `SessionStart` reports without fabricating an activity transition
- persists metadata and activity together when they arrive in the same hook
- preserves existing activity, blocked-state, and first-signal behavior
- rejects metadata from unknown harnesses and drops oversized session IDs
- lets the existing Codex and Claude Code adapters resume by exact native session ID
- keeps existing fallback behavior when no trustworthy native ID is available

No transcript scanning, guessed `--last` session, or database migration is introduced.

## Files affected

- `backend/internal/cli/hooks.go`
  - Extracts native session IDs and includes them in hook reports.
- `backend/internal/cli/hooks_test.go`
  - Covers metadata-only hooks, activity-plus-metadata, and unknown harnesses.
- `backend/internal/ports/runtime_observations.go`
  - Carries the optional native session ID through the lifecycle signal.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`
  - Persists native session metadata without changing activity state.
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager_test.go`
  - Verifies metadata-only and same-state signals preserve lifecycle facts.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go`
  - Adds the optional `agentSessionId` hook request field.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go`
  - Validates and forwards activity or metadata-only hook reports.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions_activity_test.go`
  - Covers metadata-only requests, combined reports, empty requests, and oversized IDs.
- `backend/internal/httpd/apispec/openapi.yaml`
  - Regenerates the API contract.
- `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`
  - Regenerates the frontend API types.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/lifecycle`
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers -run 'TestSessionsAPI_Activity'`
- `go test ./internal/httpd/apispec/...`
- `go test ./internal/session_manager -run 'TestRestore'`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode`
- Codex adapter suite passed with two Windows temp-path tests skipped because `filepath.EvalSymlinks(t.TempDir())` failed with OS access denied before reaching their assertions.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- OpenAPI and TypeScript API artifacts regenerated successfully.
- `git diff --check`

### Live Codex verification

Tested against the running development daemon:

1. Spawned Codex session `ao-test-2-8`.
2. Confirmed native session ID `019f6abd-998f-77a1-bb78-6a2d47b69b78` was persisted.
3. Sent the secondary transcript marker `BRAVO-942`.
4. Killed and restored the AO session.
5. Confirmed the native session ID remained unchanged.
6. Asked Codex for the pre-restore secondary marker.
7. Codex answered `BRAVO-942` from the same native JSONL transcript.
8. Confirmed the original launch prompt was not replayed as a new turn.

title: fix(browser): re-measure preview overlay on inspector divider drag (#2693)
body:
## What

Dragging the split-view divider to expand the terminal shrank the inspector column, but the native browser preview kept its old bounds and spilled over the terminal — the "right pane stuck at its previous width / overlapping space" in #2693.

The preview is a native `WebContentsView` overlay positioned from a measured DOM slot. Its `ResizeObserver` does not fire for a divider drag that expands the terminal, so nothing drove a re-measure and the overlay kept stale bounds. This is the fragile `ResizeObserver` interaction #2693 predicted after #2203.

**Fix:** expose `remeasure()` on the browser view model and drive it from the inspector's `react-resizable-panels` `onResize`, which fires on every drag frame and is the authoritative signal that the column changed width. The call sits before the existing drag-only guard so a resize always re-measures, not just a collapse.

Fixes #2693

## Also included (unrelated to #2693)

The second commit is a **separate fix, not required by #2693** — flagging it explicitly so it can be reviewed on its own merits or split out on request.

The same overlay paints above the whole window, so when the terminal pane enters element fullscreen (`CenterPane`'s `requestFullscreen`) the preview painted across it. It now hides whenever a fullscreen element does not contain the preview slot, and settle-measures on `fullscreenchange` so it returns to its slot on exit. Element fullscreen need not resize the window, so the existing `resize` listener alone could miss the transition.

## Testing

- `re-measures the browser overlay on an inspector drag (#2693)` — a live drag frame must drive a re-measure.
- `re-sends the current slot bounds when remeasure() is called` — with the `ResizeObserver` inert (as it effectively is during a divider drag), `remeasure()` must send fresh, smaller bounds.
- `hides the native view while a foreign element is fullscreen, then restores it on exit`.

Full renderer suite green on top of current `main`: **611 tests / 57 files**. `tsc --noEmit` and `prettier --check` clean.

## Notes for reviewers

- Rebased on `main` @ ce98f0f4; no conflicts.
- #2732 (`keep notifications above browser preview`) touched this hook in parallel — it only widened `OPEN_MODAL_SELECTOR`, so the two changes are independent.

title: feat(work-graph): durable project work items, deps, and session ownership
body:
## Summary

Make orchestration a durable, shared plan of work: project-scoped work items with optional dependency edges and session ownership, persisted in SQLite under `~/.ao`, mutated through the daemon, and visible to humans and agents after restart.

Sessions remain the runtime unit (worktree, terminal, PR facts). The work graph is the coordination overlay. Display progress is always derived at read time from durable facts, never stored as board status.

**Success bar:** after killing the orchestrator session and restarting the daemon, a human can still answer "what is blocked on what, and who owns it?" without reading chat history.

**Design doc (proposed):** [durable work graph on Notion](https://app.notion.com/p/batmnnn/durable-work-graph-3a0b156bc370804ca408ce48838fcb25?source=copy_link)

## Problem

Today the product is orchestrator-led in `DESIGN.md`, but coordination is only:

- a `Kind=orchestrator` session plus standing prompts
- `ao spawn` / `ao send` (messages are not durable)
- no parent/child task edges, no plan table

Lifecycle CI/review/conflict nudges go straight to the worker that owns the PR and bypass the orchestrator. Tracker intake can spawn workers without the orchestrator. Parallel work has isolation (worktrees) but not a shared checklist that survives restart.

Prompt-only or worktree `PLAN.md` "graphs" are patches. They fail the success bar.

## Proposed approach (core addition, not a patch)

New first-class domain beside sessions:

1. **`work_items`** — identity, title/body/acceptance, coarse lifecycle fact (`open` / `in_progress` / `done` / `cancelled`), optional tracker identity
2. **`work_item_deps`** — durable edges (`blocks` | `parent` | `related`)
3. **`work_item_sessions`** — ownership bindings (at most one active owner)

Follow AO storage rules:

- facts in SQLite; CDC via DB triggers into `change_log`
- derive `ready` / `blocked` / `in_progress` / `done` in the service layer
- never store board/display status columns
- thin CLI over HTTP; `npm run sqlc` + `npm run api`

API sketch: project-scoped CRUD + deps + claim/release; optional `workItemId` on spawn.

CLI sketch: `ao plan ls|add|dep|claim|done` and `ao spawn --work-item <id>`.

UI: project board (`/projects/$projectId`) Plan tab beside the existing session attention kanban. Session "Needs you" / "Working" stays a live attention badge on bound items, not the item lifecycle itself.

## Non-goals (v1)

- Jira clone (sprints, Gantt, custom fields, multi-user PM)
- Temporal-style workflow engine
- Frontend-owned kanban that writes status into SQLite
- Replacing sessions, worktrees, or SCM worker-directed nudges
- Unsupervised auto-decompose into dozens of nodes
- Requiring every session to have a work item (freeform stays)

## Phased rollout

**MVP**

- Schema + CDC + service derive + HTTP + CLI
- Project Plan list UI
- Soft deps (visibility only; no hard spawn/send gates)
- Optional bind on spawn; claim/release
- Orchestrator / `using-ao` docs for `ao plan`

**v2**

- Hard dep gates (opt-in)
- Auto lifecycle from PR merge / session terminate policies
- Orchestrator event feed for bound worker attention
- Optional tracker bind

**v3 / never unless product expands**

- Sprints, Gantt, Temporal DSL, unsupervised 50-node decompose, cross-project portfolios

## Acceptance criteria

### Design lock
- [ ] Open product decisions in the [design doc](https://app.notion.com/p/batmnnn/durable-work-graph-3a0b156bc370804ca408ce48838fcb25?source=copy_link) answered (or explicitly deferred)
- [ ] Design doc status flipped to Accepted

### MVP implementation
- [ ] Migration for work items, deps, ownership; CDC events wired
- [ ] Service derives ready/blocked/in_progress/done; no stored display status
- [ ] HTTP + OpenAPI + CLI (`ao plan` / spawn bind)
- [ ] Project Plan UI lists items with derived status and owner link
- [ ] Freeform sessions without work items unchanged
- [ ] Soft deps visible; hard gates not required
- [ ] Restart daemon: plan facts intact (success bar)
- [ ] Tests: store/service/HTTP/CLI; cycle reject on write; unbound spawn regression

## Implementation notes

- Prefer sibling domain (`service/work`), do not overload `sessions.kind`, `issue_id`, or `prompt` as the plan SoT
- One write path: HTTP/CLI → work service → store; triggers emit CDC
- PR/session facts win conflicts with stale item facts (auto-complete policy TBD in design decisions)
- Do not route SCM nudges through the orchestrator in MVP

## Related

- Design: [durable work graph on Notion](https://app.notion.com/p/batmnnn/durable-work-graph-3a0b156bc370804ca408ce48838fcb25?source=copy_link)
- Product intent: `DESIGN.md` (orchestrator-led flow)
- Architecture: `docs/architecture.md` (observe → store → derive)
- Nudges bypass orch: `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`
- Session kind only: `backend/internal/domain/session.go`

## Area

- Backend (Go daemon): domain, storage/CDC, service, HTTP, CLI
- Frontend: project board Plan surface
- Docs: design acceptance, STATUS, using-ao skill

title: fix(review): preflight reviewer binary before creating review runs (#2092)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2092 by validating the reviewer binary before creating any `ReviewRun` records.

Previously, if the configured reviewer binary (for example `codex` or `claude`) was not available on `PATH`, the review trigger would:

1. Create `ReviewRun` records in the `running` state.
2. Fail later during reviewer launch when resolving the binary.
3. Mark the runs as `failed` with zero findings.

This made an infrastructure failure appear similar to a completed review with no findings.

With this change, reviewer availability is verified before any review runs are created. If the binary is unavailable, the trigger fails immediately with a clear error and no database state is written.

## Implementation

- Added an optional `ReviewerPreflighter` interface for reviewer adapters.
- Added `Launcher.Preflight()` to perform reviewer availability checks before launching.
- Implemented preflight support for the Codex and Claude Code reviewer adapters.
- Invoked preflight during `Trigger()` immediately after reviewer harness resolution and before any `ReviewRun` creation.
- Preserved the existing runtime failure path (`failRuns`) for failures that occur after a successful preflight (for example process launch failures).

## Testing

Added regression tests covering:

- reviewer binary missing → trigger fails before creating any `ReviewRun`
- successful preflight → existing review flow is unchanged
- launcher preflight delegation
- unsupported reviewer adapters
- missing reviewer adapter

Verified with:

```bash
go test ./internal/review/... ./internal/adapters/reviewer/... -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...

title: Mobile terminal input, repaint, STT, preview, and notification issues
body:
## What I ran into

I use AO from both the desktop app and an Android phone. This surfaced several related problems in the terminal and mobile client.

### Terminal input on Android

Fast typing can lose characters or arrive late. The input field did not show a normal caret or retained text, so it was hard to tell where new text would land. Backspace also failed when the retained input buffer was empty, including just after Enter.

Expected behavior: batched Android and IME updates should reach the PTY once, in order. The input field should show its current text and caret. Backspace should send DEL without being sent twice.

### Terminal sizing and repaint flashes

The phone view needs a fixed 52-row terminal scaled to the available height. Switching apps or tabs, returning to AO, and opening or closing the Android keyboard caused the entire terminal to repaint visibly from top to bottom.

The repaint came from duplicate same-size resize reports. Each report caused another SIGWINCH. Desktop also sent a delayed duplicate resize and cleared the current terminal screen during reconnect, which made the repaint more visible.

Expected behavior: ignore unchanged grid reports from focus and keyboard layout events, but still forward real size changes. A solo mobile reconnect must reopen the terminal and restore the current columns by 52 rows exactly once.

### Speech-to-text

The Android client had no speech-to-text path for composing an AO message. Recognition should use the device locale, stop when the app leaves the foreground, and leave the transcript editable before the user sends it.

### Latest document preview

The Browser button did not reliably surface the newest generated Markdown document. It should choose the newest previewable Markdown or web entry, render Markdown as a preview, and work on both desktop and mobile.

### Ongoing Android notification

There was no ongoing notification for returning to AO or sending a message. The useful behavior is a generic notification with three paths: tap to open AO, Reply to type a message, and Voice to open the correct session speech composer. It must never show mixed PTY output or tool commands as if they were the latest assistant message.

Notification replies also need deterministic session ownership. If there is no safe target, the app should refuse the send instead of guessing. Session changes must not race and clear a newer target.

## Reference implementation

A reviewed implementation is available on this fork branch:

https://github.com/Fmeilrios/agent-orchestrator/tree/mobile-terminal-and-notification

It includes focused tests for terminal input, notification target selection, notification ownership races, foreground voice startup, resize deduplication, and reconnect sizing.

Verification completed on the branch:

- Mobile tests: 13 passed
- Desktop terminal tests: 17 passed
- Mobile and frontend TypeScript checks passed
- Expo dependency check passed
- git diff --check passed

I have not built or installed an APK from this branch yet, so device-level acceptance testing is still needed.

title: Codex ignores role-specific model config on launch
body:
## Problem

AO stores role-specific Codex model settings but does not pass them to the Codex CLI. New workers therefore use the user's global Codex default instead of `worker.agentConfig.model`.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a project with different Codex models for each role:

```json
{
  "worker": {
    "agent": "codex",
    "agentConfig": { "model": "gpt-5.4-mini" }
  },
  "orchestrator": {
    "agent": "codex",
    "agentConfig": { "model": "gpt-5.6-sol" }
  }
}
```

2. Run `ao spawn --project orchestration --name model-check`.
3. Open the worker session and inspect the model.

## Actual result

The worker starts with `gpt-5.6-sol`, the user's global Codex default.

## Expected result

The worker starts with `gpt-5.4-mini`, the configured worker model.

## Suspected cause

`effectiveAgentConfig` resolves the role override and places it in `ports.LaunchConfig.Config`. The Codex adapter's `GetLaunchCommand` never reads `cfg.Config.Model`, so it emits no `--model` argument. `GetRestoreCommand` appears to have the same omission.

The smallest fix should append `--model <trimmed cfg.Config.Model>` for Codex launch and restore commands when the value is non-empty, with focused command-construction tests.

Relevant file: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`

## Environment

- AO desktop: `33.4.11`
- `ao version`: `dev`
- OS: Windows
- Harness: Codex

title: fix: hide browser preview when terminal enters fullscreen
body:
## Summary

In terminal fullscreen, the browser preview overlaps the terminal and renders with no toolbar or window chrome — bare page content painting on top of the fullscreen terminal. This hides the native `WebContentsView` whenever the fullscreen element does not contain its slot, and restores it on exit.

## Before / After

Terminal fullscreen with a browser preview open (`ao preview` active), toggled via the ⤢ button in the terminal pane header.

| Before (bug) | After (fix) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before — browser preview overlaps the fullscreen terminal with no toolbar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/assets/pr-2770-screenshots/before-terminal-fullscreen-bug.png) | ![After — fullscreen terminal renders clean, preview hidden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/assets/pr-2770-screenshots/after-terminal-fullscreen-fixed.png) |

In **before**, the preview keeps painting over the right half of the fullscreen terminal, its web content flush to the top with no toolbar above it. In **after**, the preview is hidden while fullscreen and the terminal owns the whole surface.

## Root cause

The terminal pane's fullscreen button calls `requestFullscreen()` on the pane (`CenterPane.tsx`), which promotes it into the DOM **top layer**. The top layer paints over all other *DOM* content — but the browser preview is a native Electron `WebContentsView` attached to `mainWindow.contentView` (`browser-view-host.ts`), composited by Chromium *above* the page entirely. The top layer has no authority over it, so it keeps painting where it was.

And nothing tells it to move. `useBrowserView`'s measure loop is driven by a `ResizeObserver` on the slot (plus its column) and `resize` / `scroll` listeners. A fullscreen transition fires **none** of these: top-layer promotion doesn't reflow normal-flow siblings, so the slot stays connected and its `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the same box. `measureAndSend` recomputes the identical rect and keeps sending `visible: true`.

That produces both symptoms at once:

- **Overlap** — the preview holds its pre-fullscreen bounds, now sitting over a terminal that expanded to fill the window.
- **Missing toolbar/buttons** — the `BrowserPanel` toolbar and window chrome are React DOM *outside* the fullscreen element, so the top layer hides them; the native view is not hidden, leaving bare page content with no chrome above it.

## Fix

Three changes in `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts`:

1. **`hiddenByFullscreen(node)`** — returns true when a fullscreen element exists and does **not** contain the slot. The `contains` check keeps the view alive if the browser subtree itself is ever the thing going fullscreen. Uses a truthy check rather than `!== null` because jsdom (and older engines) leave `fullscreenElement` `undefined` when nothing is fullscreen.
2. **Measure guard** — `measureAndSend` hides the native view when `hiddenByFullscreen` is true, in the same early-return that already handles inactive / disconnected slots.
3. **`fullscreenchange` listener** — drives a settle-measure (the same settle-and-remeasure the hook already uses for panel transitions) so the view hides on enter and restores at correct bounds on exit, after the macOS fullscreen animation lands rather than mid-flight.

This mirrors the park/hide approach the hook already applies to open modals (`MutationObserver` → park the native view offscreen), so it slots into an existing pattern rather than introducing a new mechanism.

## Testing

- **2 new regression tests** in `useBrowserView.test.tsx`: hide-on-enter, restore-on-exit at measured bounds, and the `contains` guard (view stays visible when the slot itself is inside the fullscreen element).
- **Negative control**: with the guard removed, the hide test fails with the exact reported bug; restoring it passes — confirming the test exercises the real mechanism, not a tautology.
- 65 tests pass across `useBrowserView`, `BrowserPanel`, `SessionInspector`, `CenterPane`; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

**Verification caveat:** this is verified via the unit tests + negative control above, **not** driven live in Electron by CI. DOM fullscreen combined with native `WebContentsView` compositing is exactly what jsdom can't reproduce. The before/after screenshots above are the manual confirmation in the real app.

title: feat: add GitLab SCM integration with multi-provider dispatcher
body:
## Summary

Adds GitLab as a first-class SCM provider alongside GitHub. The daemon's SCM observer, session PR claiming, and CLI now support both providers through a new multi-provider dispatcher that routes calls based on the parsed repository host.

The GitLab adapter is REST-only (unlike GitHub which uses GraphQL) because GitLab's GraphQL coverage for CI pipelines and MR approvals is incomplete. Token resolution chains `AO_GITLAB_TOKEN` → `GITLAB_TOKEN` → `glab auth status --show-token` shell-out, using `Authorization: Bearer` for OAuth2 + PAT compatibility.

## Changes

**New adapter packages** (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/gitlab/`):
- `auth.go` — token source chain: env vars → `glab auth status` shell-out, with TTL-based caching
- `client.go` — REST API v4 client with internal ETag caching and externally-managed ETag support for the observer
- `observer_provider.go` — full `scmobserve.Provider` implementation: MR list, MR detail, CI pipelines/jobs, approvals, mergeability mapping, review threads/discussions, failed check log tail
- `provider.go` — provider struct, constructor, credential availability check
- `doc.go` — package documentation with state mapping tables (GitLab states → domain types)

**Multi-provider dispatcher** (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/multi/`):
- `provider.go` — new `Provider` type that routes `ParseRepository`, guard calls, `FetchPullRequests`, and review/log fetches to the correct sub-provider based on `SCMRepo.Provider`; `FetchPullRequests` partitions refs by provider key and batches each group independently

**Daemon wiring** (`backend/internal/daemon/`):
- `scm_wiring.go` — both GitHub and GitLab providers registered at startup; missing credentials for one provider logs a warning but does not block the other; observer disables itself only when no provider has usable credentials
- `lifecycle_wiring.go` — session service uses `newMultiSCMProvider` instead of GitHub-only provider

**CLI** (`backend/internal/cli/pr_ref.go`):
- Generalized PR reference parsing from GitHub-only to support GitLab MR URLs (`/-/merge_requests/N`), including nested groups (e.g. `group/subgroup/repo/-/merge_requests/42`); SSH remote parsing now handles any host

**Session service** (`backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go`):
- `parseGitHubPRURL` → `parsePRURL` (host-aware), `githubRepoFromURL` → `repoFromURL` (host-aware), `requireSameGitHubRepo` → `requireSameRepo`; new `providerKey()` maps host → `"github"` / `"gitlab"`; `prURLFromParts()` constructs correct URL format per provider

**API contract**:
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` — `SessionPRSummary.Provider` enum expanded from `"github"` to `"github" | "gitlab"`
- `backend/internal/httpd/apispec/openapi.yaml` — regenerated
- `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` — regenerated

**Frontend** (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/pr-display.ts`):
- GitLab MR URL support in browser URL normalization

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/gitlab/...` — 84 tests pass
- `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/multi/...` — 11 tests pass
- `go test ./internal/cli/...` — 160 tests pass (including new GitLab MR claim-pr and spawn tests)
- `go test ./internal/service/session/...` — 309 tests pass (including GitLab MR claim, normalize, and same-repo tests)
- `go test ./internal/httpd/...` — 75 tests pass (spec parity + drift checks)
- `go test ./internal/daemon/...` — 7 tests pass
- `golangci-lint` — 0 issues
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend) — pre-existing errors only, no new errors introduced

## Intentional omissions

- **REST-only**: GitLab adapter uses REST v4, not GraphQL — GitLab's GraphQL coverage for CI pipelines and MR approvals is incomplete
- **No "changes_requested" review state**: GitLab has no native concept; review decision derived from approvals endpoint (`approved` / `approvals_required > granted` / `none`)
- **No token invalidation on auth failure**: The GitLab client does not call `invalidateToken` on 401/403 (unlike GitHub) — the `glab` token source has its own TTL-based cache; `tokenInvalidator` interface and `FallbackTokenSource.InvalidateToken` are wired for future use

title: fix(tracker-intake): exclude terminated sessions from seen issue set
body:
## Problem

`seenIssueIDs` in `backend/internal/observe/trackerintake/observer.go` built
its "already has a session" set from `ListAllSessions`, which returns every
session including terminated ones. Once any session — killed, crashed, or a
failed spawn — had ever existed for an issue, that issue's ID stayed in the
`seen` set forever. The intake poller would then skip the issue on every
subsequent poll, so it never got re-spawned. The issue stayed open in the
tracker, assigned, and silently unworked — no error, no log, no notification.

## Fix

`seenIssueIDs` now also checks `sess.IsTerminated`, so only live sessions
count as "claiming" an issue:

```go
if sess.IssueID != "" && !sess.IsTerminated {
    seen[sess.IssueID] = true
}
```

A killed/crashed/failed-spawn session now frees its issue for the next
intake cycle.

## Tests

Added to `observer_test.go`:

- `TestSeenIssueIDsExcludesTerminatedSessions` — a live session for an issue
  is still seen even when a terminated session for the same issue exists.
- `TestSeenIssueIDsIgnoresOnlyTerminatedSession` — an issue with *only* a
  terminated session is not marked as seen.
- `TestPollRespawnsIssueAfterTerminatedSession` — end-to-end: `Poll` spawns a
  new session for an issue whose only prior session is terminated.

All three fail on `main` and pass with the fix. Full package and full
backend suite pass (`go test ./...`).

## Scope

This PR only touches `seenIssueIDs`'s filtering logic and its tests. It does
**not**:

- Touch the SQL layer (`ListAllSessions` / `session_store.go`) — the
  `IsTerminated` field is already scanned into `domain.SessionRecord` from
  the DB, so no query change was needed.
- Fix #2745 (reaper cannot terminate sessions stuck in
  blocked/waiting_input). If a session is stuck rather than properly marked
  terminated, this fix does not help it — that's a separate root cause and
  separate PR.
- Add any logging/alerting for the silent-skip condition described in the
  issue. Happy to follow up with that in a separate PR if wanted, but kept
  this one scoped to the single root cause.

Fixes #2746

title: `ao start` launches the desktop app un-daemonized; it dies immediately (exit 0) leaving nothing running
body:
## Summary

`ao start` prints its banner, exits `0`, but **no desktop window opens and nothing keeps running** — `ao status` stays `stopped` and no daemon binds `127.0.0.1:3001`. The app is spawned un-daemonized and is torn down the moment `ao start` returns.

Launching the AppImage **directly** works perfectly, so the app itself is healthy — the bug is in how `ao start` spawns/detaches it.

## Environment

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu-family), kernel `7.0.0` (x86_64), Wayland session
- Launcher: `@aoagents/ao@0.10.3` (npm) → platform binary `@aoagents/ao-linux-x64`
- App: `~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage` (0.10.3)
- `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1` (Ubuntu userns restriction is active)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh state: `ao stop` and ensure nothing is on port 3001.
2. Run `ao start`.
3. Observe: banner printed, `exit 0`, then run `ao status`.

**Expected:** desktop app opens and the daemon stays up (`ao status` → `ready`).
**Actual:** no window; `ao status` → `stopped`; no `agent-orchestrator` processes; nothing on `:3001`.

## Root cause (traced)

`strace -f -e execve` on `ao start` shows it execs:

```
execve("~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage", ["...AppImage", "--installed-via=npm-bootstrap"], ...)
```

The AppImage FUSE-mounts, and is then **unmounted almost immediately** — i.e. the child exits right after `ao start` returns. The parent (`ao start`) does not appear to daemonize / fully detach the child (no independent session), so the app dies orphaned.

## Evidence the app is fine when launched directly

Running the same AppImage directly (even with the exact same `--installed-via=npm-bootstrap` arg) stays up and is fully functional:

- AppRun auto-adds `--no-sandbox` (works around the userns restriction),
- daemon logs `daemon listening addr=127.0.0.1:3001`,
- API serves `/api/v1/projects`, `/healthz`, `/readyz` with 200.

So the arg is not the problem, and `--no-sandbox` is handled correctly by AppRun.

## Workaround

Launch the AppImage detached from the shell with `setsid`, so it survives the launcher returning:

```bash
setsid ~/.ao/agent-orchestrator.AppImage >~/.ao/app.log 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

This starts the app + daemon and it persists after the terminal closes.

## Suggested fix

Have `ao start` fully daemonize the spawned desktop app (new session via `setsid`/double-fork, detached stdio) before returning, instead of leaving it as a child that gets reaped when `ao start` exits.

title: Desktop Browser tab renders proxied pages without CSS/images/assets (relative URL resolution broken)
body:
## Bug

The **Browser tab** in the AO desktop app renders websites with **no CSS, no images, and broken layout** — just naked unstyled HTML. The content is there, but all visual styling and assets are missing.

## What happened

When an agent session previews a remote website through the desktop Browser tab, the page loads as plain unstyled HTML. The address bar shows a local daemon proxy URL like:

```
http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/firedc…
```

All relative asset paths (`/style.css`, `/img/avatar.jpg`, company logos, etc.) resolve against the **local origin** (`127.0.0.1:3001`) instead of the original remote server, so every stylesheet and image returns a 404. The result is a broken, unstyled view of the page.

## Expected vs. Actual

**Expected:** The Browser tab renders the website as it would appear in a normal browser (full CSS, images, layout intact).

**Actual:** Only the raw HTML loads — no stylesheets, all images broken, layout collapsed to a left-aligned vertical stack of default-styled links and text.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session that navigates to / previews a remote website (e.g. `https://fireddd.github.io/`)
2. Open the **Browser** tab in the AO desktop app
3. Observe the rendered page — CSS is missing, all images are broken icons

## Impact

The Browser tab is unusable for visual verification of web work. Users cannot tell if an agent correctly rendered or modified a page because everything looks broken regardless of what the agent actually did.

## Likely cause

Relative URL rewriting is not handled when proxying remote HTML through the local daemon endpoint. Asset paths need to be rewritten to point at the original origin (or proxied through the daemon) so they resolve correctly.

## Environment

- AO desktop app (Electron)
- Session browser tab
- Reproduced with: `https://fireddd.github.io/`

---

Reported by @fireddd via Discord

title: Squirrel auto-update poisons daemon/tmux working directory, breaking all subsequent spawns (RCA for #2775)
body:
## Summary

After a desktop auto-update, every new session spawn fails: the terminal shows

```
ENOENT: Bun could not find a file, and the code that produces this error is missing a better error.
shell-init: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories: No such file or directory
job-working-directory: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories: No such file or directory
```

and the agent (Claude Code) never actually starts. This is the root cause for #2775.

The failure is machine-wide (every spawn, every project) and persists across app and daemon restarts. Only `tmux kill-server` clears it, which is a strong hint that the fault lives in the long-lived tmux server, not in the daemon, the database, or the worktrees.

## Root cause

A process in the spawn chain inherits a working directory that then gets deleted, and tmux propagates that dead cwd to every new pane.

1. Squirrel.Mac (its `ShipIt` helper) performs an auto-update by staging the new build in a temp directory, relaunching the app from inside that directory, and then deleting it. The relaunched Electron process is left with `cwd` pointing at a directory that no longer exists. The poisoned path is literally `.../T/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt.<id>/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources`.
2. Electron spawns `ao daemon` as a child, which inherits that dead cwd.
3. The daemon starts a tmux server on the first spawn. The server daemonizes off the `ao daemon` process and inherits the dead cwd. Crucially the tmux server is long-lived and independent of any single daemon instance, so it carries the dead cwd across every subsequent daemon and app restart.
4. On spawn, AO correctly runs `tmux new-session -d -s <id> -c <worktree> <shell> -c <launchCmd>`. But a tmux server whose own working directory has been deleted cannot resolve the start directory and silently drops the new pane into the server's (dead) cwd instead of `-c`.
5. The pane's shell then fails `getcwd()` at startup (the `shell-init` errors), and Claude Code, a Bun-compiled binary, aborts immediately because it needs a valid cwd to resolve files (`ENOENT: Bun could not find a file`). The agent never runs, so no activity hook ever fires and the session looks dead on arrival.

## Evidence (reproduced locally)

- `lsof` on the tmux server showed its `cwd` was exactly the deleted `ShipIt` staging directory.
- Minimal repro isolating the fault to the server: from a shell with a valid cwd, `tmux new-session -d -c <valid absolute worktree path> ...` against the poisoned server still produced a pane whose `pane_current_path` was the deleted dir. The `-c` argument was correct and absolute; the server simply could not honor it.
- Affected sessions had a null first-signal timestamp and zero agent-hook telemetry, consistent with the agent never launching (not with the agent starting and then crashing).

## Impact

Any user whose app auto-updates can land in this state, and once there every spawn on that machine fails until the tmux server is killed. The trigger is not macOS-specific in principle: the same "inherited cwd later deleted" pattern applies to Squirrel.Windows / NSIS relaunch, to the Linux AppImage FUSE mount unmounting after the old instance exits, and to launching AO from a removable or later-deleted directory. The conpty runtime host is a long-lived helper with the same "outlives the daemon" property, so it is exposed to the same class of failure.

## Proposed fix (defense in depth)

The fix must self-apply through the same auto-update that delivers it, with no user action, because the update channel is the trigger. Two changes give that property:

1. `cd <workspace> || exit` at the front of the launch command (both the tmux and conpty runtime launch-command builders, e.g. `buildLaunchCommand` in `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go`). This makes each pane immune even on an already-poisoned server, which is what lets the fix heal the installed base without any forced `tmux kill-server` migration. Keep the existing `-c` as well. The `|| exit` ensures a genuinely missing worktree fails loudly instead of launching in the wrong place.
2. `os.Chdir` the daemon to a stable directory (for example `~/.ao/data`) at the top of daemon startup, before any runtime is spawned. This guarantees every newly started tmux server / conpty host is clean.

Hardening to catch any regression instead of preventing it:

3. After `new-session`, assert `pane_current_path` equals the requested workspace and fail the spawn with a clear error otherwise. This converts a silent fleet-wide outage into one legible error at spawn time.
4. Send the app-mode daemon's stdout/stderr to a rotating file under `~/.ao`. Today it goes to a dead Electron console, which is why this bug was invisible for hours.
5. A regression test on the launch-command builder asserting the `cd` guard, plus ideally an integration test that deletes a server's cwd and asserts the pane still lands in the workspace.

Deliberately out of scope: an unconditional `tmux kill-server` on daemon boot. It would work but destroys live terminals on every restart, defeating session continuity, for a problem the `cd` guard already makes harmless. A conditional recycle (only when the server cwd is actually dead) is a possible hygiene follow-up, not part of the core fix.

## Immediate workaround

Quit the app, run `tmux kill-server`, and relaunch. The new daemon starts a fresh tmux server with a valid working directory. Note that restarting the app alone does not help, because the poisoned tmux server survives the restart.

Refs #2775.

title: Preview browser renders root-absolute asset paths unstyled (served under /preview/files/ sub-path, no <base>/URL rewrite)
body: ## Summary The desktop **Browser** panel serves a workspace under a path prefix — `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions//preview/files/` — but does not account for assets referenced by **root-absolute URLs** (`/style.css`, `/img/…`). The browser resolves those against the daemon **origin root**, so they 404. Any static site built for domain-root deployment (e.g. a GitHub Pages user site) therefore previews with **no CSS and broken images**, even though it renders correctly in production. ## Environment - AO desktop app, daemon at `127.0.0.1:3001` - Observed while previewing a GitHub Pages static site ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open, in the Browser panel, a static site whose HTML references assets with root-absolute paths, e.g. `` and ``. 2. Observe the rendered page. ## Expected The preview looks like the deployed site — styled, images loaded. ## Actual Default serif fonts, unstyled blue/purple links, broken-image icons for every asset. ## Evidence The daemon *does* serve the assets correctly under the prefix — the problem is purely that the HTML's root-absolute URLs escape the prefix: | Request | Result | | --- | --- | | `GET …/preview/files/style.css?v=55` | **200** (`text/css`) — file is there | | `GET …/preview/files/logos/ibm.png?v=30` | **200** (`image/png`) | | `GET …/preview/files/img/avatar.jpg` | **200** (`image/jpeg`) | | `GET http://127.0.0.1:3001/style.css?v=55` | **404** — *this is what the browser actually requests* | Because the served HTML contains `href="/style.css"`, the browser resolves it against the origin root (`http://127.0.0.1:3001/style.css`), not the `…/preview/files/` base — hence the 404. The same site renders correctly at its production root (`https://fireddd.github.io/`), where `/style.css` maps to the domain root. ## Root cause The preview is served under a sub-path without any of: - injecting a `` into served HTML, - rewriting root-absolute `href` / `src` / `url()` references to the prefixed path, or - serving the workspace at a virtual origin root. So every root-absolute reference points outside the preview prefix and 404s. ## Suggested fixes (any one) - **Serve each preview at its own origin** (subdomain or dedicated port) so `/` maps to the workspace root. Most robust; matches real deployment behaviour exactly. - **Rewrite root-absolute `href`/`src`/`url()`** to the preview-prefixed path at serve time. - **Inject a `` tag** pointing at the preview root. Simplest, but note `` also rewrites in-page anchors and JS-relative URLs, so a scoped rewrite is safer. ## Impact Any GitHub Pages / root-deployed static site previews as broken, which is misleading — the site is correct; only the in-app preview misrepresents it.

title: fix(renderer): don't flash onboarding before projects load (#2514)
body:
Fixes #2514.

## Problem

On cold start the Electron app briefly showed the first-run **onboarding page**, then replaced it with the real project list once daemon discovery settled.

Root cause: `fetchWorkspaces()` returned `[]` whenever the daemon's API base URL wasn't trusted yet (its port is discovered at runtime). React Query treated that `[]` as a **successful** empty result, so `SessionsBoard`'s `isSuccess && all.length === 0` rendered `BoardWelcome`. When the daemon later became ready, `_shell` invalidated the query and the real `/api/v1/projects` list replaced it — i.e. the onboarding page was a transient discovery placeholder, not an authoritative no-projects state.

## Fix

Represent "API base not trusted yet" as a **pending** query instead of a successful empty list:

- `fetchWorkspaces` throws `ApiBaseUrlNotTrustedError` instead of returning `[]` when the base URL is untrusted, so it can never resolve as an empty success.
- `useWorkspaceQuery` gates the query on a trusted base URL, tracked reactively via `subscribeApiBaseUrl` + `useSyncExternalStore`, so it flips the moment the daemon reports ready. While untrusted the query stays pending and the board shows its loading shell.
- The `_shell` loader skips the `ensureQueryData` prefetch until the base URL is trusted, so the loader can't cache a bogus empty result either.

No behavior change once the daemon is ready: a genuine empty project list still shows onboarding (real first run).

## Before / After

**What the evidence shows:** both screenshots were taken under the identical condition — the renderer running on the real fetch path with **no daemon**, so the API base URL is never trusted and the state stays stable (no timing race to catch). Only the fix differs between the two.

- **Before (`main`):** the untrusted `[]` resolves as a successful empty result → the first-run onboarding page is rendered (this is what would flash over real projects once they load).
- **After (this branch):** the query stays pending while the base URL is untrusted → the board loading shell is shown instead of onboarding.

| Before (`main`) — onboarding flashes | After (this branch) — loading shell |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fireddd/agent-orchestrator/evidence/onboarding-flash-2514/.github/evidence/2514/pre-fix.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fireddd/agent-orchestrator/evidence/onboarding-flash-2514/.github/evidence/2514/post-fix.png) |

## Tests

- Rewrote the untrusted-path unit test to the new pending contract and added a cold-start regression test (untrusted → trusted → refetch) in `useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx`.
- Added the new `subscribeApiBaseUrl` export to the mocks that drive the real hook.
- Full renderer suite green: **623 passed**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

*Reproduction was by code inspection + a deterministic Playwright screenshot of the two states (renderer on the real fetch path with no daemon); not a live capture of the timing race.*

title: Feat/pi restore support
body:
## Summary

  Implements true PI restore support by installing an AO-managed project-local PI extension that captures PI’s native session UUID and reports it through the existing `ao hooks` activity endpoint.

  No daemon API or storage schema changes are required. PI restore continues to use the existing `MetadataKeyAgentSessionID` path and resumes with:

  ```bash
  pi --append-system-prompt ... --session <native-pi-session-id>
  ```
  ## Changes

  - Adds an embedded PI TypeScript extension at .pi/extensions/ao-activity.ts.
  - Installs the extension from backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi.GetAgentHooks.
  - Captures PI’s native session UUID via ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId() on session_start.
  - Reports PI hook events through ao hooks pi ...:
      - session-start captures metadata only.
      - before_agent_start maps to user-prompt-submit.
      - agent_settled maps to stop.
      - session_shutdown maps to session-end only for terminal quit shutdowns.

  - Adds sentinel-based overwrite protection so AO refuses to replace a non-AO file at .pi/extensions/ao-activity.ts.
  - Adds .pi/.gitignore management for the AO-installed extension.
  - Registers PI in activitydispatch.Derivers.
  - Adds a PI-specific activity deriver:
      - session-start: metadata-only, no activity state.
      - user-prompt-submit: active.
      - stop: idle.
      - session-end: exited.

  - Extends restore manager coverage so PI sessions with captured native ids use native resume.

  ## Why

  PI already supported native resume with pi --session <id>, and AO’s PI adapter already read agentSessionId metadata in GetRestoreCommand. The missing piece was capturing PI’s native session UUID during normal AO-managed launches.

  This change fills that metadata-capture path through PI’s official project-local extension API, avoiding any new daemon routes or schema changes.

  ## Behavior

  With this change:

  - New AO-managed PI sessions install .pi/extensions/ao-activity.ts.
  - When PI starts a native session, AO receives ao hooks pi session-start with:

  {"session_id":"<pi-native-session-uuid>"}

  - AO persists that UUID as agentSessionId.
  - Later, ao session restore <id> and boot-time restore can resume PI with pi --session <uuid>.
  - If no PI native UUID has been captured yet, PI keeps the same fallback behavior as other resumable agents: restore falls back to a fresh launch with the saved prompt when valid.

  ## Safety Notes

  - The extension is AO-owned and guarded by a sentinel comment.
  - Re-running hook installation is idempotent.
  - A user-created file at the managed path is not overwritten.
  - Activity reporting is best-effort and must not break the PI session.
  - session_start is metadata-only so process startup does not incorrectly mark a turn active.
  - stop is emitted from agent_settled, not agent_end, to avoid reporting idle while PI may still auto-retry, compact, or process queued follow-ups.
  - session-end is only reported for session_shutdown.reason === "quit" to avoid marking AO exited during PI /new, /resume, /fork, or reload flows.

  ## Tests

  Added/updated coverage for:

  - PI hook installation writes .pi/extensions/ao-activity.ts.
  - Installed extension contains the AO sentinel.
  - Hook installation is idempotent.
  - Non-AO files at the managed path are not overwritten.
  - .pi/.gitignore includes the AO-managed extension.
  - Embedded extension includes all managed hook commands:
      - ao hooks pi session-start
      - ao hooks pi user-prompt-submit
      - ao hooks pi stop
      - ao hooks pi session-end

  - Embedded extension uses agent_settled for stop instead of agent_end.
  - Embedded extension gates session-end to terminal quit shutdowns.
  - PI activity derivation maps events correctly.
  - activitydispatch recognizes PI as hook-capable.
  - ao hooks pi session-start persists agentSessionId without an activity state.
  - Restore manager passes PI’s captured agentSessionId into native resume config.

title: Copilot kill can leave session live after terminal ends because AO-generated agent file dirties worktree
body:
## Bug

Killing a Copilot-backed session can leave the terminal runtime gone while the AO session row remains live. The desktop then shows:

`Terminal ended`
`This terminal process ended, but the session is not marked terminated yet.`

**Source:** local live report from the AO desktop/dev daemon
**Reported by:** @nikhilachale
**Analyzed against:** `f60884964f829e820513fbc1929a9b9ffb2d98b1`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** high: session kill reports success/degrades the terminal but leaves the session unrecoverable in the live board

## Reproduction

Observed on macOS/Darwin with a dev Electron daemon using `AO_RUN_FILE=/Users/nikhilachale/.ao/dev/running.json` and `AO_DATA_DIR=/Users/nikhilachale/.ao/dev/data`.

1. Spawn a Copilot worker session in a git worktree.
2. Let AO install its Copilot session files, including `.github/agents/ao-<session>.agent.md`.
3. Kill the session from the desktop topbar and confirm kill.
4. The terminal process exits, but the session remains non-terminated in AO.

Live evidence from the reporter machine:

```text
$ /tmp/ao session get agent-orchestrator-96
id: agent-orchestrator-96
project: agent-orchestrator
role: worker
status: needs_input
activity: waiting_input
harness: copilot
terminated: false
created: 2026-07-18T08:36:11Z
updated: 2026-07-18T08:36:29Z
```

`tmux ls` did not include `agent-orchestrator-96`, so the runtime backing the terminal was already gone.

The same worktree showed AO-generated Copilot files as dirty/ignored inconsistently:

```text
$ git -C ~/.ao/dev/data/worktrees/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator-96 status --short --ignored
?? .github/agents/
!! .github/hooks/
```

## Root Cause

There appear to be two coupled problems.

1. `Manager.Kill` destroys the runtime before the worktree teardown. If `workspace.Destroy` returns `ports.ErrWorkspaceDirty`, `Kill` returns `false, nil` before it reaches `m.lcm.MarkTerminated(ctx, id)`.

Relevant path: `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`, dirty-workspace branch in `Kill`.

That means a kill can remove the terminal runtime, return success, and still leave `sessions.is_terminated = 0`. The UI is then correct to say the terminal ended but the session is not marked terminated.

2. Copilot is especially likely to trigger that dirty-worktree branch because AO writes `.github/agents/ao-<session>.agent.md` for the Copilot session profile.

Relevant path: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/copilot/hooks.go`.

The live linked worktree had an exclude entry for the agent profile under the per-worktree gitdir:

```text
# agent-orchestrator Copilot session files
/.github/agents/ao-agent-orchestrator-96.agent.md
```

But `git check-ignore` did not ignore the file. In this linked-worktree setup, Git was using the common repo exclude, not that per-worktree admin `info/exclude`, so AO's own generated Copilot file still made the worktree dirty.

## Expected

- If `POST /sessions/{id}/kill` returns success, `is_terminated` should be true even when the worktree is preserved because it is dirty.
- AO-generated Copilot session files should not make the worktree dirty in linked worktrees.
- The desktop should not be left in the state where the runtime is gone but the session is still live/non-restorable.

## Impact

- Copilot sessions can remain stuck in the active board after kill.
- The terminal is gone, so the user cannot continue the session normally.
- Cleanup cannot reclaim the session because cleanup only targets terminated sessions.
- Users may have to manually edit SQLite to recover.

## Related

- [#2701](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2701): same bad kill invariant (`kill` can return success without persisting termination), but triggered by stale pre-tmux runtime handles rather than Copilot-generated dirty files.

title: Add an in app keyboard shortcuts reference
body: ## Issue Agent Orchestrator has several keyboard shortcuts, but users currently have no in-app reference for discovering or reviewing them. This makes existing shortcuts difficult to learn and gives new shortcuts no consistent place to be documented. ## Fix Adds a lightweight keyboard shortcuts dialog that opens globally with: - `Ctrl + /` on Windows and Linux - `⌘ + /` on macOS The shortcut is handled at the Electron application level, so it works while focus is inside the app shell, terminal, or browser preview. The dialog: - Organizes shortcuts into General, Navigation, and Session sections - Displays platform-specific key combinations - Can be closed with `Esc` - Is also available from **Help → Keyboard shortcuts** in the Windows topbar The design is intentionally simple for now. It provides a clear, categorized reference without introducing search, shortcut customization, or additional navigation surfaces. Those can be added later as the shortcut catalog grows. ### Adding future shortcuts Shortcut metadata now lives in a central `APP_SHORTCUTS` catalog. Adding an existing shortcut to the manual only requires a new catalog entry containing its label, category, and platform-specific keys. The dialog renders entries from this catalog automatically, making new shortcuts easy to document without duplicating UI markup. Shortcut behavior remains explicitly implemented in the relevant React component or application-level handler, preventing a documentation entry from silently changing application behavior. ## Files affected - `frontend/src/shared/shortcuts.ts` - Adds the central shortcut catalog, platform-specific key definitions, and the keyboard-help matcher and IPC channel. - `frontend/src/main/app-shortcuts.ts` - Generalizes application-level shortcut forwarding for new-session and keyboard-help commands. - `frontend/src/main.ts` - Registers application shortcuts and connects the Help menu action to the dialog. - `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts` - Forwards application shortcuts when the browser preview has focus. - `frontend/src/preload.ts` - Exposes the keyboard-help event through the preload bridge. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx` - Renders the categorized, platform-aware shortcut reference. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/WindowTitlebar.tsx` - Adds **Keyboard shortcuts** to the existing Help menu. - `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` - Mounts the dialog globally and opens it in response to the application shortcut. - Shortcut, preload, dialog, and shell tests - Cover platform matching, IPC forwarding, rendering, and opening the dialog. ## Validation - `npm run typecheck` — passed - Vitest suite excluding the environment-blocked supervisor socket test: - 63 test files passed - 694 tests passed - Manual shortcut and Help-menu testing — passed

title: fix: capture grok session ids for restore
