title: fix: merged PR sessions disappear from sidebar AND leak runtime RAM (not torn down)
body:
## Summary

When a session's PR is merged, the session silently disappears from the sidebar and gets buried in the collapsed "Done / Terminated" bar on the kanban board — with **zero user feedback** explaining what happened. Worse, the underlying runtime process (tmux/conpty + agent + worktree) is **never torn down**, so it keeps consuming RAM until the daemon is restarted.

This combines a UX problem (no transition feedback) with a real resource leak (merged sessions are marked dead in the DB but their processes stay alive).

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a worker session that opens a PR
2. Merge the PR (from the dashboard, GitHub UI, or `gh pr merge`)
3. Observe:
   - ❌ The session **vanishes from the sidebar** with no toast/notification
   - ❌ The session **drops into the collapsed "Done / Terminated" bar** on the kanban board (collapsed by default — invisible)
   - ❌ The tmux/agent process is **still alive** and holding RAM (verified by checking `tmux ls` or process list)

## Two Distinct Bugs

### Bug A — RAM leak (the real issue, `priority:high`)

When a PR merges, the SCM observer fires `ApplyPRObservation` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:132-141`), which calls `MarkTerminated`:

```go
// reactions.go:138
if done {
    return m.MarkTerminated(ctx, id)
}
```

But `MarkTerminated` **explicitly does NOT tear down external resources**:

```go
// backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:254
// MarkTerminated marks a session terminated without tearing down external resources.
func (m *Manager) MarkTerminated(ctx context.Context, id domain.SessionID) error {
    // ... only sets is_terminated=true, activity_state=exited
}
```

It only flips two DB flags. The tmux/conpty process, the agent process, and the git worktree all stay alive indefinitely.

Compare with `Kill()` (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:439-477`), which does the **full teardown**:

| | Merge path (`MarkTerminated`) | Manual kill (`Kill`) |
|---|---|---|
| Flags set in DB | ✅ | ✅ |
| tmux/conpty process killed | ❌ | ✅ |
| Worktree removed | ❌ | ✅ |
| RAM freed | ❌ | ✅ |

The reaper (`backend/internal/observe/reaper/`) doesn't help — it **skips terminated sessions** (`reaper_test.go:88`: "terminated sessions must not be probed"). The `reconcileReap` pass only runs at **boot time** (`manager.go:810-817`). `Cleanup()` does tear down terminated runtimes, but it's only triggered manually (CLI/project removal), never automatically on merge.

**Result:** every merged session leaks its process until the daemon restarts. Over a workday of merges, this adds up fast.

### Bug B — Silent disappearance (UX)

The frontend filters merged sessions out without any visible transition:

- **Sidebar** (`frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:433`): `workerSessions(workspace.sessions).filter(sessionIsActive)` strips them out — `sessionIsActive()` returns `false` for `status === "merged"` (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:275-277`)
- **Kanban** (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:327-329`): `attentionZone()` maps `merged` → `"done"` zone → session falls into the collapsed "Done / Terminated" bar at the bottom (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx:214-256`), which is collapsed by default

The lifecycle does fire a `NotificationPRMerged` notification (`reactions.go:320-321`), so the notification *exists* — but it doesn't tell the user *where the session went*. A user who merges from GitHub sees their session vanish with no breadcrumb.

## Suggested Fixes

**For Bug A (RAM leak):** The merge-completion path in `reactions.go:132-141` should trigger actual runtime teardown, not just a flag flip. The lifecycle layer is intentionally a fact-reducer that doesn't own resource teardown — but the merge-completion path crosses that boundary and nothing picks up the teardown. Options:

1. Have the SCM observer's completion signal call through the session manager (which owns `Kill`) instead of stopping at the LCM.
2. Add an automatic post-merge teardown in the reaper for sessions marked terminated-but-not-reaped.
3. Have the merge path call `Kill` directly.

The architectural seam to resolve: `MarkTerminated` lives in the LCM (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`), `Kill` lives in the session manager (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`). The merge path stops at the LCM.

**For Bug B (UX):** Add a visible transition when a session moves to the "Done" zone — e.g., a toast/banner, or don't auto-collapse the Done bar so the user sees where their session went.

## Severity

`priority:high` — Bug A is a core feature broken (merged sessions leak resources) with no workaround for users. Bug B is UX friction.

Reported by @prateek. Triage by @i-trytoohard.

title: Activity timeline: PR number not clickable + missing "Opened PR" timestamp
body: ## Bug: Activity timeline — PR number not clickable, and no "Opened PR" timestamp In the **Activity** section of the session **Summary** pane (right-hand inspector), the PR timeline events render incompletely: 1. **PR number is plain text, not a clickable link.** `Opened PR #2807` should link to the PR on GitHub but renders as inert bold text. 2. **PR events have no timestamp.** "Created worktree & branch" shows `5d ago` and the current status row shows `just now`, but the middle "Opened PR #2807" row shows nothing. ### Screenshot See attached image below. ### Root cause Both issues live in the `ActivityTimeline` component in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`. **1. PR number not clickable — frontend-only, trivial.** The PR number is rendered as plain bold text at three sites: - `SessionInspector.tsx:277` — `Draft PR #{pr.number}` - `SessionInspector.tsx:289` — `Opened PR #{pr.number}` - `SessionInspector.tsx:323` — `Merged PR #{pr.number}` But the `pr` object already carries `url` (`PullRequestFacts.url`, `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:105`). It's just never rendered as a link. Fix: wrap `#{pr.number}` in ``. ~3 lines, pure frontend, no API change. **2. No "Opened PR" timestamp — needs a backend wire change to be correct.** All three PR events hardcode `ts: null` (lines 280, 292, 326). This is not just a frontend omission — the creation timestamp is genuinely missing from the wire. Tracing the data path: | Layer | PR creation time present? | |---|---| | DB `pr` table → `created_at_provider` column | ✅ yes | | `GetPR` query / domain `PullRequest` (`backend/internal/domain/pr.go:59` `CreatedAtProvider`) | ✅ yes | | domain `PRFacts` (slim read model, `pr.go:9`) | ❌ dropped — only `UpdatedAt` | | `GetDisplayPRFactsBySession` query (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/gen/pr.sql.go:50`) | ❌ does not SELECT it | | DTO `SessionPRFacts` (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:244`) | ❌ only `updatedAt` | | Frontend `PullRequestFacts` (`frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts:104`) | ❌ only `updatedAt` | So the provider's creation timestamp exists at the source but is stripped at the `PRFacts` / DTO boundary. To show a correct "opened at" time, `created_at_provider` must be threaded through: the query → `domain.PRFacts` → `SessionPRFacts` DTO → `npm run api` (regen OpenAPI + TS types) → frontend type + `toPullRequestFacts` (`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useWorkspaceQuery.ts:14`) → `ActivityTimeline`. > ⚠️ Avoid a frontend-only stopgap of reusing the existing `pr.updatedAt` — that shows *last updated*, not *opened*, which is misleading for older PRs. ### Suggested fix split - **PR A (quick, frontend-only):** clickable PR links using the already-available `pr.url`. Ships standalone. - **PR B (backend wire change):** add `createdAt` (sourced from `created_at_provider`) to the `SessionPRFacts` wire shape, regenerate API types, then wire it into the timeline for the open/draft/merged rows. ### Severity **Minor** — cosmetic/UX polish, no functional break. But the dead `ts: null` is clearly an unfinished placeholder, so worth closing. ### Environment Observed on the desktop app session inspector (Summary → Activity). --- _Triage by @i-trytoohard._

title: fix(lifecycle): durably deliver worker-idle completions to the orchestrator
body:
# Wake the orchestrator when a worker finishes — durably, exactly-once, without interrupting it

Closes AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator#2820

Supersedes my earlier PR (#2823 ).

## Problem

When the orchestrator spawns a worker, it was never told when that worker finished. Nothing reacted to a worker's active → idle transition, so a completed worker sat silent until the human manually asked the orchestrator to poll (#2820).

## Approach

active → idle is the completion signal, and waking the project orchestrator is preferable to polling every worker. The key design point from review: recording that a worker finished and delivering that fact to the orchestrator are two separate responsibilities. They are now decoupled behind a durable, at-least-once outbox.

**Invariant:** once AO accepts a worker-completion signal, it stays pending until AO successfully attempts delivery to a safe orchestrator. Duplicates after a crash are acceptable; silent loss is not.

## What changed

- **worker_idle_events outbox (migration 0024):** project, worker, transition time, delivery state. A partial unique index on `worker_id WHERE pending` coalesces repeated completions to one pending row.
- **Atomic persistence (RecordWorkerIdle):** the worker's active → idle transition and its outbox event are written in one transaction, so a crash cannot save the worker idle while losing the delivery work.
- **Dispatcher (DispatchProject / DispatchAllPending):** resolves the current orchestrator at delivery time (never bound to one that may be replaced), routes through `sessionguard.Nudge`, and marks an event delivered only when the guard reports a pane write was attempted — suppressed outcomes stay pending.
- **Grounded nudge:** the message tells the orchestrator to run `ao session get <worker>`, embedding no status snapshot that could be stale by delivery time.

## Explicit delivery contract

This reconciles the two review threads (one asked for "idle only"; the other correctly noted that active delivery is safe for harnesses like Codex where Enter steers the current turn, and that "idle only without retention" would itself create a lost-notification path):

| Orchestrator state | Action |
|--------------------|--------|
| Idle | Deliver now |
| Active and harness steers active turns | Deliver now |
| Active without safe steering | Defer |
| Blocked / waiting-input | Defer |
| Missing / terminated | Defer until an orchestrator is available |

Active-turn steering is an explicit harness capability (`HarnessSteersActiveTurn`), defaulting conservatively to `false` for any unknown harness.

## Addressing Reviewer @Vaibhaav-Tiwari  (active-orchestrator behavior)

The contract above makes the description and implementation agree: an active orchestrator is only nudged when its harness can safely steer; otherwise the completion is retained, not dropped.

Added a test: a worker goes active → idle while the orchestrator is active (non-steering) and no nudge is sent — the event is retained and delivered later.

## Addressing Reviewer @illegalcall  (durable at-least-once delivery)

- Typed, project-scoped `worker_idle` event — ✅
- Durable internal outbox (not human-facing dashboard notifications) with project/worker/kind/transition/delivery state — ✅
- Activity transition + outbox event persisted atomically — ✅
- Coalesce repeated completions per worker — ✅ (partial unique index)
- Delivery resolves the current orchestrator at delivery time — ✅
- Route through `sessionguard.Nudge`; mark delivered only on an attempted pane write; suppressed stays pending — ✅
- Retry on: event creation, orchestrator entering a safe state, orchestrator spawn/restore, daemon start, and a low-frequency recovery sweep — ✅
- Active-turn steering as an explicit harness capability, conservative default — ✅
- Grounded nudge (`ao session get <worker>`, no stale snapshot) — ✅
- Test matrix — ✅ (below)

## Tests

- **Lifecycle:** idle orchestrator delivers; steerable-active delivers; unsafe-active / blocked / waiting / missing orchestrator retain; deferred delivery fires when the orchestrator becomes safe; repeated completions coalesce to a single delivery; destination is the orchestrator session id (not merely "a message was sent"); `DispatchAllPending` delivers then does not re-deliver.
- **Store:** atomic record, coalesce, mark-delivered, and pending persistence.
- **Session manager:** an orchestrator spawn triggers dispatch; a worker spawn does not.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and all touched-package tests pass locally.

I could not run `golangci-lint` or `go test -race` in my environment (toolchain limitation), so CI is the first full lint/race pass — happy to fix anything it surfaces.

---
cc @Vaibhaav-Tiwari @illegalcall

title: Fix detection of npm agent binaries from GUI path
body:
## Summary

Fix agent binary detection for npm-distributed adapters when AO is launched from Electron/GUI with a minimal `PATH`.

The daemon currently relies on `exec.LookPath` first, but GUI-launched Electron does not source shell rc files, so nvm/volta/fnm-managed npm global bins are often absent from `PATH`. This caused false "Needs install" results after refreshing agents, especially for adapters like Kimi, Grok, and Droid.

## Changes

- Add shared nvm fallback support in `binaryutil.ResolveBinary`
  - Probes `~/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/<binary>` on Unix.
  - Keeps existing precedence: `PATH` first, configured absolute/home candidates next, nvm candidates last.
  - Sorts nvm matches in reverse lexicographic order for deterministic newest-looking selection.
- Normalize Unix npm fallback paths for npm-distributed `BinarySpec` adapters:
  - `~/.npm-global/bin/<binary>`
  - `~/.npm/bin/<binary>`
  - `~/.local/bin/<binary>`
  - adapter-specific fallback paths afterward.
- Patch custom npm-style resolvers:
  - `codex`: uses the shared nvm helper and now includes npm-global/local fallbacks.
  - `opencode`: adds npm-global, local, and nvm fallbacks.
  - `copilot`: adds npm-global and nvm fallbacks while preserving native-loader resolution.

## Why

Users installing agents globally through nvm-managed npm can end up with binaries only under paths like:

```bash
~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin/kimi
```

Those paths are usually available in an interactive shell, but not in the Electron daemon process. The selector then reports "Needs install" even though the agent is installed.

So if a user launched AO from the terminal, it might work because shell init added nvm to `PATH`. But if a user launched AO as the desktop app, it might fail because the Electron-launched daemon never saw the shell's nvm `PATH`.

What we changed:
- Keep `PATH` lookup first.
- Add shared fallback detection for nvm npm global binaries.
- Normalize npm fallback paths across npm-distributed adapters.
- This makes "Refresh agents" work even when AO is launched from the desktop app with a minimal environment.

## Testing

Ran:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/binaryutil ./internal/adapters/agent/copilot ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/...
go test ./internal/service/agent/...
go test ./...
```

Also ran:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Fixes #2832

title: feat: surface assembled prompt byte metrics during spawn (#2822)
body:
## Fixes

Closes #2822

## Summary

This PR addresses Issue #2822 by surfacing informational prompt size metrics during session spawn.

After the final prompt and system prompt are assembled, AO now measures their byte lengths using `len()` and exposes them through the spawn response and CLI output. This gives users visibility into the size of the prompt AO assembles without introducing any provider- or model-specific assumptions.

## Changes

- Measure assembled prompt and system prompt byte sizes in `Manager.Spawn()`
- Thread the values through the spawn flow using Go multi-return values
- Expose `promptBytes` and `systemPromptBytes` in the spawn response
- Display prompt metrics in `ao spawn` output when non-zero
- Regenerate the OpenAPI specification and frontend API schema

## Design

This implementation is intentionally informational only.

It does **not**:

- estimate tokens
- enforce prompt limits
- introduce provider-specific logic
- modify prompt assembly
- modify prompt delivery
- introduce new abstractions or agent interfaces

The metrics are computed during spawn and are not persisted.

title: Dev daemon isolation from #2465 regressed pnpm dev: revert to shared port/rundir, gate isolation behind ISOLATE_DEV
body:
## What happened

#2465 moved the dev daemon (`app.isPackaged === false`) onto its own port and state dir: `AO_PORT=3002`, `AO_RUN_FILE=~/.ao/dev/running.json`, `AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/dev/data`. Two problems:

1. **Proxied renderer paths have been broken in dev since it merged.** `vite.renderer.config.ts` still defaults its `/api` and `/mux` proxy targets to `http://127.0.0.1:3001`, so anything going through the Vite proxy (notifications stream, `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` browser preview) gets ECONNREFUSED while the daemon sits healthy on 3002. Symptom: UI loads but data-driven surfaces are empty or stale, with `http proxy error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3001` in the dev console.
2. **Dev silently forks app state.** The fresh `~/.ao/dev/data` DB means projects, sessions, and persisted settings (e.g. `pipelines.enabled`) from the installed app vanish in dev with no indication why.

## Decision

The separate port and rundir are the regression, not the lifecycle coupling. The supervisor stopping the daemon on quit is by design: the daemon's lifecycle belongs to whichever app supervises it.

Rework:
- Dev uses the **same port and rundir as the installed app by default** (3001, `~/.ao`).
- The isolation from #2465 moves behind an explicit **`ISOLATE_DEV=true`** opt-in for anyone who wants a sandboxed dev daemon.
- The Vite proxy default must follow the same switch as the daemon port, or both should derive from one shared constant, so the two can't desync again. Hardcoding the port in two files (`main.ts` DEV_DAEMON_PORT vs `vite.renderer.config.ts`) is what let this ship.

## Repro

With an installed AO app present (or a stale `~/.ao/running.json` holding 3001): `pnpm dev` in `frontend/`, open the notifications stream or any proxied path. Observe ECONNREFUSED against 3001 while the dev daemon listens on 3002.

title: feat(desktop): AO_KEEP_DAEMON to keep the daemon alive after the app closes (#2230)
body:
## Summary

Opt-in `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` env var: when set, the desktop app spawns its daemon **without** the OS-native supervisor link and skips the orphan-cleanup kill on exit, so the daemon persists across app quit and stops only on an explicit `ao stop`. Default (unset) is byte-for-byte unchanged — the daemon self-stops shortly after the app quits.

Beyond "power users with long sessions," the persistent-daemon mode is a prerequisite for a **detached / remote** topology (a headless daemon in a container, attached from the desktop over an SSH tunnel): without it, closing the desktop window arms-then-fires the supervisor watchdog and kills every running agent session in the container.

Closes #2230.

## History / why a new PR

This supersedes the combined #2621 for the #2230 part, splitting it per the one-issue-per-PR review feedback. It also continues the **#2231** review thread (closed when its head branch was accidentally removed during a fork cleanup, not for any code reason). All four @illegalcall review points from July 11 on #2231 are addressed in this branch:

- **Cross-launch regression (persist the keep decision with the daemon):** the keep decision is read from the daemon's durable `running.json` owner record (`"persistent"` vs `"app"`), never the current Electron process env. A daemon spawned keep-alive stays persistent even when the app is later reopened **without** `AO_KEEP_DAEMON`. `shouldLinkOnAttach("persistent") === false` is encoded as a regression test.
- **fd leak:** the parent's `keepDaemonLogFd` is closed on the spawn-throw path and after a successful spawn (the child holds its own inherited copy via stdio), so each keep-alive start/stop cycle no longer accumulates descriptors.
- **stdio lifetime:** under the flag the daemon's stdio is redirected to `~/.ao/daemon.log` (stdin ignored) and the child is `unref()`'d, so Electron-owned pipes no longer kill the kept-alive daemon on the next stderr log write.
- **truthy parsing:** `keepDaemonAlive` uses an explicit allowlist (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`); `off`/`no` and any unrecognized string keep the default self-stop behavior.

Rebased clean onto current `main` (`5532fa1b`); the keyboard-shortcut refactor (PR #2795) that landed in the meantime is left untouched.

## Mechanism

- `daemonEnv()` stamps `AO_OWNER="persistent"` under `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` (else `"app"`). The daemon writes `AO_OWNER` verbatim into `running.json` (`server.go`); the attach path reads that durable record (not this Electron process's env, which differs across launches) and skips the supervisor re-link for `"persistent"`.
- Under the flag the daemon's stdio is redirected to `~/.ao/daemon.log` and the child is `unref()`'d; the port-bound supervisor link and the stdio port-scanners are skipped (port discovery falls back to the `running.json` handshake).
- The `process.on("exit")` orphan-cleanup kill is skipped under the flag.

Files: `frontend/src/main.ts`, `frontend/src/main/daemon-owner.ts(.test.ts)`, `frontend/src/shared/daemon-discovery.ts`, `backend/internal/runfile/runfile.go`, `docs/cli/README.md`.

## Verification

- `gofmt` clean; `go build ./...` ok; `runfile` Go suite passes.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing upstream `semver` types error in `escalation-evaluator.ts`, unrelated to this PR).
- 26 `daemon-owner` tests pass, incl. the cross-launch and allowlist cases.

title: feat(mobile): push notifications for iOS and Android
body:
## Mobile push notifications (iOS + Android)

Adds real OS push notifications to the mobile app so a user is alerted — when the app is backgrounded or killed — the moment one of their agents needs attention (needs input, PR ready to merge, PR merged, PR closed unmerged). Tapping a notification deep-links into the relevant screen.

### The design constraint

The "server" is the user's **own daemon** running on their laptop (reached over LAN/Tailscale), not a cloud service. So **the daemon is the push sender**: on each notification it makes an outbound call to the Expo Push Service, which relays to APNs/FCM. This is purely additive to the existing notification pipeline (`lifecycle → notify.Manager → notify.Hub`, which already backs the web dashboard's SSE).

### What's included

**Backend (Go daemon)**
- `internal/mobilebridge/pushdevices.go` — persistent push-device registry at `~/.ao/<data>/mobile/push-devices.json` (Expo token as primary key, idempotent upsert, atomic 0600 writes), co-located with the existing Connect Mobile state.
- `internal/httpd/controllers/push.go` — `POST`/`DELETE /api/v1/push/devices` behind the existing Bearer-password auth, with token validation and OpenAPI operations (route↔spec parity + regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`).
- `internal/push/` — an Expo client (batching, optional `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN`) and an additive `notify.Hub` subscriber (the "dispatcher") that sends to all registered devices and prunes tokens Expo reports as `DeviceNotRegistered`.
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — loads the registry on boot (degrades to no-push on failure) and runs the dispatcher for the process lifetime.

**Client (Expo / React Native)**
- `lib/push.ts` — permission-after-pairing, Expo token acquisition + registration, resilient to unprovisioned builds (no crash on a build lacking push entitlement).
- `lib/PushManager.tsx` — headless coordinator: registers on connect, refreshes on foreground, unregisters when switching daemons, and routes taps (needs_input → session screen; PR events → PRs tab) including cold-start via `getLastNotificationResponseAsync`; marks the record read on tap.
- Settings **Notifications** section — shows push status and the single next action (Enable / Register / Open settings), closing the "denied on first try, no way back" gap.
- Supporting: `lib/api.ts` (register/unregister/mark-read), `app/_layout.tsx` (mount), `expo-notifications` plugin + deps, `eas.json` build profiles.

### Testing

- Backend: `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race`, golangci-lint, and the OpenAPI route↔spec parity test all pass.
- Verified **end-to-end on physical devices**: a real daemon-generated `needs_input` was delivered and correctly deep-linked on **both** a physical Android phone (FCM) and a physical iPhone (APNs).

### Deliberate scope (v1)

- OS-tray push only — no in-app notification center, no app-icon badge, no per-type toggles.
- Immediate `DeviceNotRegistered` token pruning; Expo's delayed-receipt polling is deferred.
- Global device scope (records carry `projectId` for future per-project filtering).
- Hub buffer-drop is accepted (huge relative to human-paced events; the phone catches up via the existing REST poll).

### Notes for maintainers

- `google-services.json` (Firebase Android config) is **gitignored** and re-included for EAS builds via `.easignore` — anyone building the Android app provides their own Firebase config. Push requires an EAS project + FCM V1 (Android) / APNs (iOS) credentials.

title: fix(dev): gate daemon isolation behind opt-in
body:
## What

Restore the shared daemon port and state directory for development builds by default.

- Development now uses port `3001` and the standard `~/.ao` state directory.
- Set `ISOLATE_DEV=true` to opt into port `3002` and `~/.ao/dev`.
- The Vite `/api` and `/mux` proxies now derive their target port from the same shared configuration as Electron.
- Explicit `AO_PORT`, `AO_RUN_FILE`, `AO_DATA_DIR`, and `AO_DEV_API_TARGET` overrides remain supported.

## Why

The previous development isolation behavior caused Electron and Vite to use different daemon ports. It also silently separated development data from the installed application's data.

Fixes #2845.

## How

Added a side-effect-free shared dev-daemon configuration module used by both Electron and Vite.

The shared resolver:

- Uses port `3001` by default.
- Uses port `3002` only when `ISOLATE_DEV=true`.
- Gives an explicit `AO_PORT` precedence in either mode.

Electron only switches the run file and data directory to `~/.ao/dev` when isolation is explicitly enabled.

Regression tests cover the default port, isolated port, and explicit port overrides.

## Testing

- `npm test -- src/shared/dev-daemon-config.test.ts` - 3 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck` - passed
- `npm test` - 66 test files and 712 tests passed
- `git diff --check` - passed
- Started the application with `ISOLATE_DEV=true` and confirmed that the Vite notifications proxy targets `127.0.0.1:3002`

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(storage): add session cleanup-facts table and cleanup_generation (#2811)
body:
Part of #2811 (terminated sessions leaking runtime + workspace resources).

This PR is storage-only and **has no behavior change** — it lays the durable
foundation for reconciling a terminated session's runtime and workspace teardown.

### What's here
- **Migration 0024** — `session_cleanup_facts` (PK `session_id`, FK
  `ON DELETE CASCADE`): the durable disposition of a terminated session's runtime
  + workspace teardown (`workspace_disposition` rollup, `runtime_released_at`,
  capped-backoff retry bookkeeping, `failure_code`). Plus an additive
  `sessions.cleanup_generation` counter. No stored display status (status stays
  derived from durable facts).
- **CDC** — facts-table triggers emit the **existing** `session_updated` event
  (no `change_log` rebuild, no new event_type). Payload is `{id}`-only; the UPDATE
  `WHEN` guard fires only on disposition / runtime-release changes and excludes the
  retry-bookkeeping columns so retry-scheduling writes don't flood CDC.
- **Store / domain** — `cleanup_generation` query fan-out (mirrors
  `preview_revision`), `domain.SessionCleanupRecord`, and a cleanup store with
  upsert/get plus the coarse `sessions LEFT JOIN facts` candidate scan (raw SQL —
  sqlc 1.31's SQLite parser truncates trailing clauses after a `?` placeholder).
- **Tests** — store round-trip, facts-trigger emits `session_updated` with the
  WHEN-guard suppression, and the three candidate-scan branches (no facts row /
  stale generation / pending-and-due).

### Validation
`go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`,
golangci-lint, and `npm run sqlc` all pass. Goose `Down` manually verified via an
Up→Down→Up round-trip (drops triggers, table, and the column cleanly).

title: fix(review): destroy the reviewer pane on cancel instead of only interrupting
body:
The AO reviewer runs as a stable pane (`"review-"+workerID`) reused across
review passes. `Cancel` only *interrupted* that pane, so a cancelled reviewer
left a live pane + agent process running — a standing leak.

This adds a real teardown:
- `Launcher.Teardown(handleID)` destroys the pane via the runtime's `Destroy`
  (idempotent — empty / already-gone handle is a no-op).
- `Engine.TeardownReviewer(workerID)` destroys the deterministic
  `"review-"+workerID` pane under `lockWorker`, so it can't race a concurrent
  (re)spawn; idempotent.
- `Cancel` now calls it, so a cancelled reviewer's pane is destroyed rather
  than left interrupted-but-alive.

### Depends on
Stacked on #2800, which introduces the `reviewerRuntime.Destroy` seam this
reuses. Until #2800 merges this PR's diff also shows that commit — review the
`reviewer-teardown` commit.

### Tests
- launcher `Teardown` destroys the pane + no-ops on an empty handle
- `TeardownReviewer` tears down the deterministic handle, is idempotent, and
  rejects an empty worker id
- `Cancel` now tears the pane down (regression pin for the leak)

### Validation
`go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./internal/review/...`,
`go vet ./...`, golangci-lint — all green.

title: fix: restore Goose sessions by native session id
body:
## Summary

Fix Goose session restoration so AO resumes the original interactive Goose conversation using its persisted native session ID.

## Changes

- Restore Goose sessions with:
  `goose session --resume --session-id <agentSessionId>`
- Preserve the configured approval mode through `GOOSE_MODE`.
- Avoid replaying the original task when restoring a native session.
- Avoid passing `--system`, which is not supported by `goose session`.
- Add Goose session-start hook coverage for capturing `agentSessionId`.
- Add adapter tests using a realistic Goose session ID.

## Why

Goose automatically persists interactive sessions in its local SQLite database. AO already captures the native Goose session ID through lifecycle hooks and stores it as `agentSessionId`.

Using that ID allows a terminated AO session to resume the same Goose transcript instead of starting a new conversation or accidentally restoring the most recent unrelated Goose session.

## Restore flow

1. Goose emits a `SessionStart` hook containing its native session ID.
2. AO records that value in the session’s `agentSessionId` metadata.
3. When the AO session is restored, the Goose adapter runs:

   ```bash
   goose session --resume --session-id <agentSessionId>

title: bug(preview): new session's in-app browser opens non-empty — poller auto-previews a workspace file on first scan
body:
## Bug

When a new worker session is created, its in-app browser panel opens **non-empty**, navigated to a daemon preview-files URL for some Markdown/HTML file in the session's worktree, instead of starting empty.

Observed URLs (reporter created "simple new sessions"):
- `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/safesplit-10/preview/files/website-setUp-for-links.md`
- `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-28/preview/files/test/cli/README.md`

**Source:** Discord `#🧑‍🔧-bug-triage` | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `470a0fb9` (local main, 2026-07-19)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced and reproduced at the unit level (see Reproduction).

![reporter screenshot — new session's browser opened non-empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-new-session-browser-autopreview/.issue-assets/new-session-browser-autopreview/new-session-browser.png)

## Reproduction

A focused test that mirrors the report — a brand-new worker session whose worktree has **no `index.html`**, only Markdown (like essentially every repo):

```go
workspace := t.TempDir()
writeFile(t, filepath.Join(workspace, "README.md"), "# project")
writeFile(t, filepath.Join(workspace, "docs/website-setUp-for-links.md"), "# setup")
svc := &fakePreviewSessions{sessions: []domain.SessionRecord{workerSession("safesplit-10", workspace, "")}}
poller := NewPoller(svc, svc, "http://127.0.0.1:3001", PollerConfig{Logger: discardLogger()})
poller.Poll(context.Background())
```

Result (single `Poll()`):
```
REPRO: new session safesplit-10 auto-previewed to -> http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/safesplit-10/preview/files/README.md
```

That is the exact URL shape the reporter saw — produced on the poller's **first scan** for a session that was never explicitly previewed.

End-to-end repro in the app:
1. Create a new worker session in any project whose worktree contains a `.md`/`.html` file and no `index.html`.
2. Within ~250 ms the in-app browser opens to that file (and the inspector's Browser tab auto-reveals).

## Root Cause

The **preview poller** (`backend/internal/preview/poller.go`), started in `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:136`:

```go
previewDone := preview.NewPoller(store, sessionSvc, "http://"+cfg.Addr(), preview.PollerConfig{Logger: log}).Start(ctx)
```

scans every active worker session every 250 ms (`DefaultPollInterval`). For each one it calls `DiscoverEntry(workspacePath)`:

- `backend/internal/preview/entry.go:43` — if none of `index.html`, `public/index.html`, `dist/index.html`, `build/index.html` exist, it falls back to `mostRecentPreviewable` (`entry.go:57`), which walks the whole workspace and returns the **most-recently-modified** `.html/.htm/.md/.markdown` file. Most repos have several, so this fallback almost always matches.

Then `shouldRefresh` decides whether to write the URL. For a **brand-new** session it returns true:

```go
// backend/internal/preview/poller.go:151
func (p *Poller) shouldRefresh(sess domain.SessionRecord, target string, seenBefore bool) bool {
    current := strings.TrimSpace(sess.Metadata.PreviewURL) // "" for a new session
    if current == "" {
        if !seenBefore {                                    // true: poller's first time seeing it
            return sess.Metadata.PreviewRevision == 0       // 0 == 0 -> TRUE -> auto-set
        }
        ...
```

So the poller immediately calls `SetPreview(id, FileURL(...))` (`poller.go:138`), which writes `preview_url` and bumps `preview_revision` (`SetSessionPreviewURL`, `queries/sessions.sql:42`). The CDC trigger (`migrations/0017/0019`) fans the change out; the renderer invalidates its workspaces query (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/event-transport.ts:53`) and refetches; `SessionView` reads `session.previewUrl` and auto-navigates the browser (`useBrowserView.ts:456`) plus auto-opens the inspector Browser tab (`SessionView.tsx:110`).

This is **intended behavior over-applied**: the poller was designed to auto-surface "a freshly generated report or document" (`entry.go:42`) and static frontends. But the `.md` fallback, combined with firing on the very first poll when `PreviewRevision == 0`, means **every new session in a Markdown-rich repo auto-opens its browser to a repo doc** — directly contradicting the expectation that a new session's browser starts empty.

## Fix

Make auto-preview **opt-in**: a session should only get an auto-discovered preview *after* the user/agent has explicitly run `ao preview` at least once (`PreviewRevision > 0`). New sessions (`PreviewRevision == 0`) stay empty.

Primary fix — one line in `shouldRefresh` (`poller.go:155`):

```go
if current == "" {
    if !seenBefore {
        return false // do not auto-preview a brand-new, never-previewed session
    }
    previous := p.seen[sess.ID]
    return previous.cleared
}
```

After an explicit `ao preview <file>` opts the session in, the `current != ""` branch keeps the preview fresh as the file changes, and `ao preview clear` continues to stop re-discovery. The behavioral cost is that a "freshly generated report" no longer auto-surfaces in a session the user never previewed — which is exactly the behavior this report is asking to remove.

Alternative (more surgical, preserves built-frontend auto-preview): restrict the poller's auto-discovery to real web entry points (`index.html` variants in `entryCandidates`) and do **not** apply the `.md`/`.html` `mostRecentPreviewable` fallback for auto-set. This keeps "auto-surface a built static frontend" while killing the "auto-surface README.md" noise.

The existing poller tests would need updating either way (`TestPollerSetsPreviewWhenActiveWorkerEntryAppears` etc. assert the current auto-set-on-first-poll behavior).

## Impact

- Every new worker session in a normal repo (one with Markdown docs) opens its browser to a seemingly-random repo file — confusing and looks like a state leak. It's the #1 thing a user sees on session creation.
- Workaround: close the Browser tab / run `ao preview clear`. Not data loss.
- **Priority: medium** — UX/confusion, no data loss, workaround exists. (No `preview`/`frontend` labels exist on this repo; applied `bug`.)

## Related observations (found during triage — separate issues, not the cause here)

1. **`NextSessionNum` is non-monotonic** (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.sql:2`): `SELECT COALESCE(MAX(num),0)+1 ...`. It's `MAX` over *surviving* rows, so it recycles a number whenever the highest session row is removed. Session IDs are used as durable keys (browser views, terminal handles, restore markers, CDC cache) and should be unique forever; this is a latent collision risk worth its own ticket. (Today `DeleteSession` only removes seed-state rows, which limits reachability, but the invariant is wrong.)
2. **Native browser views are never destroyed on session close/navigation.** `useBrowserView`'s `ensure`-effect cleanup only hides (`sendHiddenBounds`); the hook's `destroy` (`useBrowserView.ts:482`) has zero call sites in the renderer. So the main-process `entries` map retains a `WebContentsView` per session for the window's lifetime. On its own this is a memory/leak issue, but combined with (1) it would let a recycled session ID adopt a stale view + URL. Worth its own ticket.

## Related

- [#2352](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2352) — preview poller not clearing stale `preview_url` when the workspace entry file is deleted (same subsystem, different symptom).

title: fix(preview): don't auto-preview Markdown docs for brand-new sessions
body:
Fixes #2859

## Summary

A new worker session's in-app browser was opening non-empty — navigated to an arbitrary repo Markdown/HTML file (e.g. `README.md`) instead of starting empty. Reported by @prateek: new sessions showed URLs like `…/sessions/safesplit-10/preview/files/website-setUp-for-links.md`.

**Root cause:** the preview poller (`backend/internal/preview/poller.go`) auto-discovers a workspace file on its very first 250 ms scan and sets `preview_url` for every active worker session. `DiscoverEntry`'s `mostRecentPreviewable` fallback (`entry.go`) returns the most-recently-modified `.md`/`.html` file anywhere in the workspace, so nearly every new session in a Markdown-rich repo matched and got auto-previewed — directly contradicting the expectation that a new session's browser starts empty.

## The fix

Restrict the **never-previewed** (`workspaceOwned == false`) auto-discovery path to real static-frontend entrypoints (`index.html` and its `public/`/`dist/`/`build/` variants). Drop the `.md`/`.html` `mostRecentPreviewable` fallback for that path only.

- New `DiscoverWebEntrypoint(workspacePath)` (`entry.go`) — entrypoint candidates only, no document fallback.
- `DiscoverEntry` is refactored to delegate to `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` first, then `mostRecentPreviewable` — **behavior-preserving** for its other callers (the explicit `ao preview` HTTP path at `sessions.go:733`, and the `entry_test.go` suite).
- In the poller, the fallback after `EntryAtPath` fails now branches on `workspaceOwned`: already-previewed sessions keep full `DiscoverEntry` (so their preview stays fresh as files change, including `.md`), while never-previewed sessions use `DiscoverWebEntrypoint`.

**Behavior after the fix:**
| Session state | Workspace has | Browser on creation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New (never previewed) | only `.md` docs | **empty** (fixed) |
| New (never previewed) | `dist/index.html` | auto-previews the frontend (preserved) |
| Explicitly previewed (`ao preview X`) | `X` changed | refreshed (unchanged) |
| Explicitly previewed, file deleted | other `.md` | full re-discovery (unchanged) |

This is the "surgical alternative" noted in the issue rather than a blanket opt-in: it fixes both reported cases (`.md` repo docs) while preserving the poller's primary purpose of auto-surfacing built static frontends.

## Test

Two new tests in `poller_test.go`:
- `TestPollerDoesNotAutoPreviewMarkdownOnlyNewSession` — a brand-new session with only `README.md` + `docs/setup.md` gets **zero** preview sets (the bug).
- `TestPollerKeepsMarkdownPreviewFreshOnceExplicitlySet` — a session explicitly previewed against `docs/report.md` still gets its preview normalized/maintained (the restriction only affects never-previewed sessions).

All 17 existing poller/entry tests pass unchanged (the entrypoint-selection tests use real `index.html`/`dist`/`public`, which `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` still finds).

```
cd backend
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./internal/preview/...     # 19/19 pass
go test ./...                      # full backend suite green
```

title: feat: standalone shell terminal, not bound to any agent session (#2828)
body: Closes #2828. Adds a shell you can open by hand — from a terminal button in the topbar or ``Ctrl+` `` — with no agent session behind it. Until now every terminal pane in the app was bound 1:1 to a session's runtime PTY, so there was no way to get a plain shell inside AO. ## Screenshots **1. The new terminal button** — sits beside the notification bell, on every route. **2. The terminal itself** — standalone shells render as tabs beside the session's own pane, each with its own close control. ## Approach The issue scoped this as a large change, proposing a new `Source.Spawn` on the terminal mux and describing it as "session-coupled end-to-end." **That turned out not to be the case, and `internal/terminal` is unchanged by this PR.** At `manager.go:353` the daemon already passes the client-supplied terminal id straight through as the runtime handle, with no session lookup anywhere in the package: ```go a = newAttachment(id, ports.RuntimeHandle{ID: id}, c.mgr.src, ...) ``` So the mux was never session-aware — it attaches to whatever handle it's given. And `ports.Runtime.Create` already accepts arbitrary `Argv`. The only missing capability was a way to *create* a session-less PTY. That reframing is what kept this small: no protocol change, no `Source` change, no `sharedTerm` rework. ### Backend New `internal/service/shellterm`, parallel to the session service rather than inside it — a shell terminal has no agent, no worktree, and no lifecycle state machine, and shares exactly one mechanism with sessions (the runtime adapter). - Own id namespace (`shellterm-`), constrained to what both runtime adapters accept (conpty enforces `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`; tmux uses the id as a session name) - Own table (`shell_terminals`, migration `0024`) with no FK to `sessions` and no CDC, so shells can never surface on the board - `GET`/`POST /api/v1/shell-terminals`, `DELETE /api/v1/shell-terminals/{handleId}` ### Lifetime: survives a daemon restart, dies with the app The PTY lives in tmux / a conpty pty-host, both of which outlive the daemon, so surviving a restart is mostly a matter of persisting enough to re-attach. Dying with the app is the harder half, and needs two mechanisms because the clean path isn't enough: 1. **Clean quit** — the supervisor closes shells on exit. 2. **Crash / force-kill** — nothing gets to run, so shells would leak forever. Each row is stamped with an **app-run id** (`AO_APP_RUN_ID`), minted once per app launch and held constant across daemon restarts the supervisor performs. At boot the daemon destroys any shell stamped with a *different* run id. A bare `ao daemon` mints its own id per boot, so its shells correctly do not outlive it. ### Frontend `useTerminalSession` gained exactly one option, `shellTerminalHandleId`. The mux draws no distinction between a shell handle and a session handle, so all the attach/reattach/backoff/resize machinery is shared verbatim — only the handle's source and the session-specific side effects branch. (A shell exit no longer invalidates the workspaces query; it carries no news for the session board.) Shell tabs live in two places: beside the session pane when a session is on screen, and in a standalone `/terminals` view otherwise. Both read the active handle from the store, so they never disagree. ### ``Ctrl+` `` Verified unused — no accelerator, no matcher, nothing in the Electron menu. Same binding on both platforms, matching VS Code (``⌘` `` is taken by macOS for window cycling). **One deliberate tradeoff:** like the other app shortcuts, it's handled in the main process so it fires with focus inside xterm. That means no shell or TUI running in a pane can receive ``Ctrl+` `` while AO owns it. Almost nothing binds that chord and VS Code makes the same trade, but it's a permanent decision worth a reviewer's eye. ## Testing **Verified against a live daemon on Windows (real conpty PTYs), not just fakes:** | Check | Result | |---|---| | `POST /shell-terminals` | `201`, real PTY spawned | | `GET` (runs a liveness probe) | listed | | Daemon restart, **same** `AO_APP_RUN_ID` | survived | | Daemon restart, **new** `AO_APP_RUN_ID` | reaped — `reaped shell terminals from previous app runs count=1` | | `DELETE` | `204`, then `404` on repeat | **Automated:** - 12 service tests, incl. rollback when persistence fails, pruning dead shells, and *not* deleting a shell when a liveness probe errors (an error is not proof of death — same rule `internal/terminal` applies on attach) - 5 store tests against real SQLite - 7 controller tests, incl. the 501 path when the service is absent - 3 e2e tests - OpenAPI route/spec parity passes; `openapi.yaml` + `schema.ts` regenerated and committed ## Bugs found by running the app Two things the test suite passed but the running app did not: 1. **The button and shortcut did nothing outside a session.** The open request was consumed by `SessionView`, which only mounts on session routes — so on the board, or in a project with no sessions yet (exactly when a plain terminal is most useful), the signal was raised and nothing was listening. Fixed by moving ownership to the shell layout, which is mounted everywhere, plus the standalone `/terminals` view. There's an e2e regression test for this case. 2. **The browser-preview build misrepresented the feature** — a selected shell tab still rendered the session's agent transcript, and the mock list couldn't shrink so the close X did nothing visible. Desktop was unaffected, but it made the feature untestable without a daemon. ## Notes for reviewers - **Pre-existing failures, unrelated to this branch** (all confirmed failing on clean `main`): `supervisor-link` (4 tests), `TestNewFallsBackOnPortConflict`, and the `aider`/`grok`/`ptyregistry`/`gitworktree` suites — all Windows environment issues. The existing e2e specs also target `refactor-mux`, a session no longer present in the mock data. - **Not addressed, happy to follow up:** multiple shells in one project share a tab title (`ao-demo`, `ao-demo`) with no `(2)` disambiguation; and shells opened from `/terminals` have no project context, so they start in the daemon data dir rather than the project you came from. - The mux attaches to any client-supplied handle id with no authorization check. Pre-existing and out of scope here, but this PR adds a documented endpoint that mints handles running the user's login shell, which makes that surface slightly more interesting. ## Commits | | | |---|---| | `d6b692e6` | backend: service, storage, REST, daemon wiring | | `a9fada60` | frontend: tabs, topbar button, ``Ctrl+` ``, `AO_APP_RUN_ID` | | `9b3babd3` | preview-build support + e2e | | `a3469456` | fix: open terminals from any route | Happy to squash `9b3babd3` into `a9fada60` — it only exists because the preview path I shipped didn't represent the feature.

title: Add dispatchable unsigned-artifact desktop build workflow (conductor handoff)
body:
## Summary

Add a new `workflow_dispatch`-triggered workflow (`build-artifacts.yml`) that builds the desktop app for all four platform targets and hands the outputs off as run artifacts, so an external release conductor can pin a ref, verify digests, and sign/publish separately. This is additive: the existing `frontend-release.yml` / `frontend-nightly.yml` signed-release paths stay untouched.

## Requirements

- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` with two inputs: `ref` (git ref/SHA to build) and `version` (version string to stamp).
- Build at the pinned `ref`; stamp `package.json` version = `version` before packaging (reuse the existing nightly version-stamping approach).
- Platform matrix: mac arm64 (`macos-latest`), mac x64 (`macos-15-intel`), windows (`windows-latest`), linux (`ubuntu-latest`).
- macOS output is **unsigned** in this workflow (no `osxSign`/`osxNotarize`, no signing secrets referenced).
- `actions/upload-artifact` each platform output with **1-day retention**.
- Emit each artifact's SHA256 as a run output (per-platform), so a downstream consumer can verify integrity.
- Creates **no** GitHub Release and references **no** secrets. Uses only the native `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Out of scope

Removing or changing the existing signed-release workflows, signing, feed generation, or release creation. Those are handled separately once the conductor is live.

title: feat(pipelines): agent pipelines v2, behind AO_PIPELINES
body:
Agent pipelines behind the `AO_PIPELINES` flag (default off, toggled from Settings). When the flag is off no engine, supervisor or trigger bridge starts and every `/api/v1/pipelines/*` route answers 501, so the feature costs nothing until it is switched on.

**This PR now carries pipelines v2.** An earlier revision of this branch shipped v1 (predicate DSL, loop semantics, a findings subsystem with lifecycle states). That design was rebuilt in place: v1's expression language, loop rounds and findings machinery are deleted, and the net diff is v2 only.

## The model

A pipeline is a set of stages connected by `on_success` and `on_failure` edges, triggered by PR events, session events, or manually. A run freezes its definition at trigger time and never re-reads it.

- **Two executor kinds.** `command` stages: exit status is the outcome, full output streams to the run folder. `agent` stages: a real agent session that settles itself with `ao pipeline done` or `ao pipeline fail --reason "..."`.
- **An outcome taxonomy, not pass/fail.** `succeeded`, `succeeded_unverified`, `failed`, `no_output`, `no_signal`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `skipped`. The distinctions are the point: an agent that claimed success without writing its declared artifact (`no_output`) is not the same failure as one that never signalled (`no_signal`).
- **One nudge.** An agent that signals done without producing its declared artifact gets exactly one message asking it to fix that, then settles.
- **A run folder** per run under `~/.ao/pipelines/<project>/<run>/`: the frozen `definition.yaml`, `run.json`, `Context.md`, `agent-outputs/`, `stage-logs/`.
- **Workspaces resolved from the subject**: `session`, `run`, `stage`, `checkout`, `inherit`. Owned trees are destroyed when a run succeeds and kept when it fails, so a failure is still there to look at.
- **Concurrency groups** with `cancel-in-progress` and a queue depth of one.
- **Credentials held by the engine**, injected into command stages only, never into agent stages, and never echoed back by any read path.

## Surface

Visual canvas editor with success and failure edges, stage inspector, settings modal, three starter templates, a Kanban run board, run detail with logs and artifacts, and `ao pipeline list|runs|show|run|cancel|done|fail|credential`.

## Verification

Unit and integration tests throughout, plus live dogfooding against a real daemon: a real agent stage completing under its own power, failure routing with skip cascade, the nudge path, `timed_out` with the session preserved, a PR-subject run through the CDC bridge, cancel-in-progress superseding an older run, restart reconciliation settling lost stages, and workspace teardown checked on the filesystem.

Two bugs that only live dogfooding could find were fixed here: a spawned session's row is seeded `idle` before the harness's first hook lands, which the agent executor read as real idleness (no agent stage could ever have succeeded); and `kill-on` matched outcomes literally, so a stage with no `produces` leaked its session.

## Known gaps

`docs/plans/2026-07-26-pipelines-v2-followups.md` lists every deferred item, every divergence from the design spec, and six findings the drills surfaced that are not fixed. The notable ones: a restart settles a lost stage but leaks its process, run folders are never garbage collected, and `docs/pipelines.md` still documents the v1 vocabulary.

title: feat(ci): add dispatchable unsigned desktop build-artifacts workflow
body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml`, a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow that lets an external release conductor drive a desktop build and consume the outputs as run artifacts:

- Inputs: `ref` (git ref/SHA to build, checked out via `actions/checkout` `ref:`) and `version` (stamped into `frontend/package.json` using the exact nightly stamping mechanism from `frontend-nightly.yml`).
- Platform matrix matching the existing release workflows: mac arm64 (`macos-latest`), mac x64 (`macos-15-intel`), windows (`windows-latest`), linux (`ubuntu-latest`).
- macOS builds are intentionally UNSIGNED: the workflow never invokes `macos-signing-setup` and sets no Apple env vars, and `forge.config.ts` only activates `osxSign`/`osxNotarize` when those vars are present. The conductor signs downstream.
- Pinned artifact contract (per the release conductor): upload-artifact names `mac-arm64`, `mac-x64`, `win`, `linux`, each containing the existing stable alias filename (`agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.zip`, `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.zip`, `agent-orchestrator-win32-x64.exe`, `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`), uploaded with `retention-days: 1`.
- A `digests` artifact contains `digests.json`, a flat JSON object mapping each of those four filenames to its sha256 hex string; the conductor reads it to verify hashes before signing. Digests are also echoed to the step summary.
- Creates no release and references no secrets; `permissions: contents: read` only.

Strictly additive: no existing workflow, signing, or release path is touched.

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean, `prettier --check` clean.
- Real `workflow_dispatch` verification run of the final contract (all four platforms green, artifacts `mac-arm64`/`mac-x64`/`win`/`linux` uploaded, flat `digests.json` emitted): https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/29832852780 (earlier pre-contract run: https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/29775090632)

title: fix(feature-builds): strip doubled title prefix, add GitHub fetch timeout
body:
Two small fixes in the feature-releases code from #2459, both surfaced by an automated review pipeline run (the pipelines feature proposed in #2863 reviewing its own repo):

1. **Doubled title prefix.** The workflow titles releases `[feature] PR #<N>: <title>` and `listFeatureBuilds` passed `rel.name` through raw, so UI labels composing their own `PR #<N>: <title>` rendered the prefix twice (e.g. the pin-confirmation dialog). Now stripped at the parse layer so every consumer gets the bare PR title; titles without the authored prefix pass through unchanged.
2. **No fetch timeout.** `fetchJson` had no deadline, so a wedged connection could hang the updates flow indefinitely for a user pinned to a feature build. Every GitHub API call is now bounded with `AbortSignal.timeout(10s)`.

Tests: two new cases for the title stripping (authored prefix stripped, plain titles untouched); full feature-builds suite 27/27, tsc and prettier clean.

title: fix(preview): send CSP on preview responses to close RCE (#2771)
body:
<!-- Suggested title: fix(preview): set a Content-Security-Policy on preview responses to close the previewed-file → loopback-API RCE -->

## What

The browser-panel preview serves workspace Markdown and HTML as `text/html` with **no Content-Security-Policy**. On the legacy `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview/files/` route the preview document is same-origin with the daemon's control API (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`), so a `<script>` in a previewed file can call that API directly — turning "open the Browser tab on a repository" into arbitrary command execution.

This PR sends a restrictive CSP on every preview response, differentiated by content type so existing functionality is preserved. The header is set in the single shared serving path (`serveWorkspacePreviewFile`), so it covers **both** the legacy route and the newer isolated `*.localhost` preview origin.

## Why

Fixes #2771.

### The vulnerability

Nothing more than a file landing in the workspace — for example a freshly cloned repository opened for inspection — is required to reach the daemon's privileged API. The chain:

| Step | Behavior | Location |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Markdown renderer passes raw HTML through unsanitized (`WithUnsafe()`) | `backend/internal/preview/markdown.go` |
| 2 | The preview is served as `text/html` with no CSP | `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` (`serveWorkspacePreviewFile`) |
| 3 | The newest `.md` in the workspace is auto-selected, so opening the preview is enough to load attacker-controlled content | `backend/internal/preview/entry.go` (`DiscoverEntry`) |
| 4 | The loopback listener is unauthenticated, so the config write is reachable same-origin over the legacy route | `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/projects.go` (`PUT /projects/{id}/config`) |
| 5 | `postCreate` reaches `sh -c` with `cmd.Dir` set to the workspace | `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` (`runPostCreate`) |

Concretely, script in a previewed file can `fetch()` `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/config` to set `postCreate`, which the session manager later executes via `sh -c`.

The preview loads through a top-level navigation (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`, `webContents.loadURL(...)`), so an HTTP-response CSP header authoritatively governs the document and the browser blocks the `fetch`.

### Root cause

The comment in `markdown.go` — *"preview content is workspace-local and agent-trusted"* — conflates **being in the workspace** with **being authorized to execute**. Untrusted workspace content is served in a context that can reach a privileged API, with nothing instructing the browser to contain it.

## How

### The fix

Set a CSP header in `serveWorkspacePreviewFile`, the one function through which both the legacy `/preview/files/` route and the isolated preview origin serve content, with a policy chosen per content type. The load-bearing directive is **`connect-src 'none'`**: the exploit requires a scripted `fetch`/XHR to the API, and because the config endpoint is `PUT`+JSON a `<form>` cannot forge the request either.

Two policies are defined:

```go
// Rendered Markdown: a document needs neither scripts nor network, so lock both
// down while still allowing the inline stylesheet and images/badges.
const previewMarkdownCSP = "default-src 'none'; img-src * data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src * data:; connect-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'"

// Raw files served verbatim (incl. .html, which cannot be sanitized): scripts/
// styles/images still load so a built static app renders, but connect-src 'none'
// blocks fetch/XHR/WebSocket so page script cannot reach the loopback API.
const previewFileCSP = "connect-src 'none'; form-action 'none'"
```

They are applied in the two branches of `serveWorkspacePreviewFile`:

```go
// raw / built-app files (the .html path that cannot be sanitized)
if !previewutil.IsMarkdownPath(clean) {
    w.Header().Set("Content-Security-Policy", previewFileCSP)
    http.ServeContent(w, r, info.Name(), info.ModTime(), file)
    return
}
// ... rendered Markdown ...
w.Header().Set("Content-Security-Policy", previewMarkdownCSP)
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
```

The pre-existing `//nolint:gosec` on the Markdown write is retained, but its justification is updated to cite the CSP rather than the "agent-trusted" assumption that no longer holds.

### Why CSP rather than the alternatives

- **Sanitizing the Markdown** (dropping `WithUnsafe()`) helps only the Markdown path and does nothing for raw `.html`, which is served verbatim. CSP covers both.
- **Validating `postCreate`** is not viable: running arbitrary shell is that field's intended behavior, so there is no "malicious value" to reject.

### Design notes and trade-offs

- **Two policies, not one.** The raw-file policy is intentionally weaker (no `default-src`; scripts still run) so a built static app renders. Containment there rests on `connect-src 'none'` + `form-action 'none'`: untrusted HTML may execute in-page but cannot reach the loopback API.
- **`img-src *`** (rather than `'self' data:`) preserves README badges and remote images. The trade-off is that a previewed file can still issue image `GET`s, an IP-leak channel — not the reported RCE, and tightenable later.
- **The isolated origin also receives `connect-src 'none'`.** Because the header lives in the shared serving path, it applies uniformly to the `*.localhost` origin as well. This is a deliberate defense-in-depth choice; if maintainers would prefer to let a built app fetch its own data on its isolated origin, the raw-file policy can be relaxed on that path specifically.

### Relationship to recent preview work

- **Isolated `*.localhost` preview origins (#2818)** already move preview off the API's origin. This change is complementary: the **legacy `/preview/files/` route is still same-origin** with the API and still needs the header, and on the isolated origin the CSP is defense-in-depth. Setting it in the shared serving path covers both with one change.
- The **workspace-confined `OpenWorkspaceFile` (OpenRoot)** path already blocks the in-workspace symlink escape, so that concern is **not** part of this PR.

### Compatibility

| Use case | Effect |
|---|---|
| Markdown docs / READMEs (incl. remote images & badges) | Unchanged (`img-src * data:`) |
| Rendered-document styling | Unchanged (`style-src 'unsafe-inline'`) |
| Built static app preview — rendering | Unchanged (scripts/styles/images still load) |
| Built app that fetches **its own data at runtime** in preview | Blocked by `connect-src 'none'` — the one behavioral change |
| Agent spawn / `postCreate` / dev-server preview | Unchanged |

### Follow-up (out of scope)

- A **repo-trust model** for the paths that inherently run repository code (agent spawn, `postCreate`) — the remaining defense-in-depth idea, separate from this fix.

### Related work

- #2818 — isolated `*.localhost` preview origins (this PR is complementary).
- #2581 — preview file / absolute-path confinement.
- #2449 — renderer-side `marked + DOMPurify` (separate from this daemon-side path).
- #307 / #1263 — original CSRF/origin hardening and loopback default.

## Testing

From `backend/`:

- `go build ./...` — compiles.
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/` — passes, including the new `TestSessionsAPI_PreviewSendsCSP`, which asserts the CSP header on both the Markdown and raw-file preview responses (and fails without this change).
- `go vet ./internal/httpd/controllers/` — clean.
- `golangci-lint run` on the changed package — 0 issues.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix: pass Codex model config to launch commands

title: fix(kimi): report mid-turn tool activity so working sessions are not shown Idle
body:
Fixes #2814.

## Problem

The activity pill showed **Idle** while a Kimi session was actively working. The Kimi adapter installed only `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`PermissionRequest`/`Stop` hooks — no mid-turn tool-use hooks — and AO's activity state is purely event-driven, so the first `Stop` parked the state on idle for the rest of the turn even while the agent kept executing tools.

## Fix

Mirrors the Claude Code adapter's tool-use trio, per the issue's suggested approach:

- **`kimi/hooks.go`** — `kimiHooksConfigBlock()` now also installs `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` / `PostToolUseFailure` → `ao hooks kimi pre-tool-use|post-tool-use|post-tool-use-failure`.
- **`activitystate/activitystate.go`** — `StandardDeriveActivityState` maps the trio to `active` (the issue's "extend the standard deriver" option: the events are generic, and other standard-deriver adapters are unaffected because they don't install these callbacks).
- `permission-request` deliberately stays `waiting_input`, not `blocked`: Kimi identifies tool calls as `tool_call_id` (not claude-code's `tool_use_id`, which is what `ao hooks` lifts onto the wire and what lifecycle's correlated blocked-clear keys on), so `blocked` could only fail closed until the turn boundary. `waiting_input` is already sticky against tool-use traffic in lifecycle, so the new trio cannot demote a pending approval.

## Verification of the issue's stated assumption

The issue flagged *"Assumption to verify: the Kimi CLI emits PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook events."* Verified against the locally installed Kimi Code **0.27.0** binary, two ways:

1. **Static**: the binary's `HOOK_EVENT_TYPES` (packages/agent-core*/…/hooks/types.ts in the embedded bundle) includes `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, with live `triggerBlock("PreToolUse", …)` / `fireAndForget("PostToolUse"|"PostToolUseFailure", …)` call sites. External hook stdin payloads are snake_cased and carry `tool_name` + `tool_call_id`.
2. **End-to-end**: installed the exact AO-managed hook block via the adapter's own `GetAgentHooks` code path into an isolated scratch `KIMI_CODE_HOME`, shimmed `ao` with a logger, and ran a one-shot `kimi -p` that reads a file. The shim recorded, in order:
   ```
   hooks kimi session-start      | {"hook_event_name":"SessionStart", ...}
   hooks kimi user-prompt-submit | {"hook_event_name":"UserPromptSubmit", ...}
   hooks kimi pre-tool-use       | {"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Read","tool_call_id":"tool_…", ...}
   hooks kimi post-tool-use      | {"hook_event_name":"PostToolUse","tool_name":"Read","tool_call_id":"tool_…", ...}
   hooks kimi stop               | {"hook_event_name":"Stop", ...}
   ```
   so the exact TOML AO writes is accepted by kimi 0.27.0 and the trio fires mid-turn with payloads the deriver maps to `active`. (This session cannot spawn AO sessions; the live kimi sessions on this machine were observed read-only via `tmux capture-pane` for context — they predate hook installation, consistent with the reported symptom.)

## Tests

- `activitystate_test.go`: trio → `active` cases added.
- `dispatch_test.go`: new `TestKimiDerivesMidTurnToolActivity` covering the `kimi` token end-to-end through `Derive` (the exact #2814 regression: mid-turn tool events must derive `active`, `stop` → idle, `permission-request` → waiting_input).
- `kimi_test.go`: asserts the three new hook entries are installed.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` passes; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean. (Pre-existing, unrelated `internal/cli` spawn-test failures reproduce on the base commit on this machine.)

## Known limitation / follow-up

After a permission approval, the pill reads "Input Needed" until the next turn boundary (`waiting_input` is sticky against tool traffic). Matching claude-code's correlated clear would need `ao hooks` to also lift `tool_call_id` as the tool-use id and a look at kimi's PermissionRequest/PreToolUse ordering — left out of scope here; AO spawns kimi in yolo mode so permission prompts are rare. The issue's note about the kilocode/opencode `session.status(busy)` variant is also untouched (separate adapter path).

title: feat(web): right-click context menu in terminal pane (Copy / Paste / Select All / Clear)
body:
## Summary

Right-clicking inside an orchestrator/agent terminal pane does nothing. There is no context menu, so users cannot Copy, Paste, Select All, Clear, or Search with the mouse. The only way to interact is via keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V), which is not discoverable and impossible on touch/mobile.

## Current behavior

- Right-click in any terminal pane → nothing happens (no native browser menu either, since xterm.js captures the event).
- Copy/paste only works via keyboard shortcuts.
- No way to Clear or Search the terminal buffer via mouse.

## Expected behavior

A context menu appears on right-click offering at minimum:

- **Copy** — copy current selection (if any) to clipboard
- **Paste** — paste from clipboard at cursor
- **Select All** — select entire scrollback buffer
- **Clear** — clear the terminal (`term.clear()`)
- **Search** (optional / nice-to-have) — search the scrollback buffer

Menu should respect theme (dark/light), position at cursor, and dismiss on outside click / Escape.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` and `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` register **no `contextmenu` event listener**. A repo-wide grep for `contextmenu`, `context-menu`, `rightclick`, `right-click`, and `oncontextmenu` under `frontend/src/` returns **zero hits**. xterm.js does not ship a built-in context menu, so nothing renders on right-click.

The handle object exposed outward (`AttachableTerminal` in `useTerminalSession.ts`) exposes `cols`, `rows`, `write`, `writeln`, `clear`, `onUserInput`, `onResize` — no `focus` or selection/clipboard helpers, so even the building blocks for a context menu are not fully exposed yet.

## Proposed implementation

1. Add a `contextmenu` handler on the xterm.js container element in `XtermTerminal.tsx` (or `TerminalPane.tsx`).
2. Render a themed floating menu (existing UI components/menus in the frontend can be reused).
3. Wire menu items to:
   - Copy → read `term.getSelection()` → `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`
   - Paste → `navigator.clipboard.readText()` → write to pty / `term.paste(...)` (xterm `@xterm/addon-clipboard` or manual)
   - Select All → `term.selectAll()`
   - Clear → `term.clear()`
4. Expose any missing primitives (selection, clipboard write) through `AttachableTerminal` if needed.
5. Prevent default browser context menu inside the terminal container.

## Related issues

- #1295 — [ENH] Copy text from terminal on dashboard (a context menu would address part of this)
- #1248 — Terminal selection vanishes on session update (~5s)
- #1221 — Terminal text selection offset (overlay scrollbar)
- #2434 — Terminal does not get keyboard focus on open
- #2537 — Drag file onto terminal does not insert path
- #237 — fix(terminal): OSC 52 clipboard, resize frame cap, hardcoded height (clipboard plumbing)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Right-click inside a terminal pane opens a themed context menu.
- [ ] Copy copies the current selection to the system clipboard; disabled/hidden when nothing is selected.
- [ ] Paste inserts clipboard contents at the terminal cursor.
- [ ] Select All selects the full scrollback buffer.
- [ ] Clear runs `term.clear()`.
- [ ] Menu dismisses on outside click, Escape, and after an action.
- [ ] Menu follows the active app theme (dark/light).
- [ ] No regressions to existing keyboard shortcut behavior (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V).
- [ ] Works across orchestrator and worker session terminals.

title: fix(frontend): deep-link PR notifications to sessions

## Summary

Fixes #2726 (AO-09, P1). PR-type notifications only opened the external GitHub PR link and never navigated into the owning AO session — the in-app navigation path was unreachable because the PR branch returned early.

This removes the early `return` after `window.open(...)` in `NotificationCenter`, so clicking a PR notification now:

Backend already carries session context for PR notifications (`service/notification/service.go`, `httpd/controllers/notifications.go` set `Kind: "pr"` with `SessionID`), so no backend change is required.

Ports the fix merged on the fork PR xuelongmu/agent-orchestrator#196.

## Changes
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NotificationCenter.tsx` — drop the early return in the PR-target branch.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NotificationCenter.test.tsx` — regression tests:
  - project-scoped PR → navigates to scoped session route
  - unscoped PR → navigates to unscoped session route
  - session-kind notifications unchanged
  - PR without session id → opens PR link, no in-app nav

## Notes / follow-ups
- `ao.renderer.notification_opened` now emits twice for a PR click (`target: "pr"` then `target: "session"`). Flagging in case dashboards assume one event per click — can adjust telemetry in a follow-up if intended.
