title: feat(runtime): Daytona sandbox runtime adapter (phase 2)
body:
Phase 2 of AO Cloud: a Daytona-backed sandbox runtime + workspace adapter, so the unmodified session manager / lifecycle manager can run a cloud session. Runs in parallel with the phase-2 control-plane work — this PR deliberately touches nothing under `backend/cmd/ao-cloud` or `backend/internal/cloud/`.

Design doc (API survey + port mapping + attach story + hooks contract + cost model): `docs/cloud/daytona-runtime.md` — written from verified 2026 Daytona docs, both OpenAPI specs, and the official Go SDK source.

## What's implemented (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/daytona/`)

- **Thin REST client** (`client.go`): platform API (create/list-by-label/start/stop/delete) + per-sandbox toolbox API (exec, git clone, PTY-over-WebSocket via the repo's existing `coder/websocket`). No new dependency tree; a narrow `Client` interface is the test seam. Live state is found by sandbox label `ao/session=<handle>` — no in-memory maps, so daemon restarts re-adopt cloud sessions like boot reconcile re-adopts tmux ones.
- **Runtime** (`daytona.go`, `attach.go`, `process.go`): tmux **inside** the sandbox, driven over toolbox exec, mirroring the tmux adapter's semantics (launch line with env exports + keep-alive shell, exact-match targets, chunked `send-keys` + delayed Enter #2342, capture-pane scrollback). Implements `ports.Runtime`, `ports.Attacher` (fresh PTY per attach running `tmux attach`; outbound-only, no inbound sandbox ports), `ports.RuntimeRestarter` (wake-from-park rebuilds tmux under the same handle), `ports.SupervisedProcessInspector` (#2802 pane-descendant walk via remote `ps`), and the `runtimeselect.Runtime` union (compile-time assert added).
- **Workspace** (`workspace.go`): sandbox provision (snapshot + boot-env credential injection per the locked custody model) + clone + session-branch checkout; dirty-refusal `Destroy`, `ForceDestroy`, remote `StashUncommitted`/`ApplyPreserved` (same temp-index / cherry-pick sequences as gitworktree), `AddExclude`, and `Park` (Daytona stop).
- **Hooks path** (`internal/cli/client.go`): `ao hooks` (and the whole CLI client) honors `AO_API_BASE` + `AO_API_TOKEN` — inside a sandbox there is no loopback daemon, so activity events post to the injected base with a bearer token. The loopback listener is untouched (still 127.0.0.1, unauthenticated).
- **Idle/cost mapping**: sandbox auto-stop (default 15 min, configurable/disable-able) + explicit `Park`. Parked = `IsAlive true` / supervised-process dead → AO's existing exited→resume flow wakes it via `Restart`. Cost: ~$0.067/h running (default size), ~$0.0003/h parked, $0 archived.

## Tests

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, full `go test ./...` and `-race` on the touched packages — green (the 5 pre-existing `internal/cli` spawn-test failures under an AO worker shell come from inherited `AO_SESSION_ID` env; they pass with a scrubbed env, unrelated to this PR).
- Contract tests over an in-memory fake Daytona (mirroring the tmux fake-runner seam): launch-line construction (no host-PATH leakage), parked-liveness, never-kill-on-transient probes, #2802 generations, dirty refusal + re-park, preserve-ref stale/clean/conflict mapping, chunked send round-trip, handle parity with `tmux.SessionName`.
- Live smoke (`smoke_live_test.go`), **skipped unless `DAYTONA_API_KEY` is set**: (1) sandbox+exec+PTY WebSocket round-trip, (2) full lifecycle — workspace create (clone) → tmux-hosted process → output capture → message round-trip → park → wake/restart → clean teardown, (3) opt-in real-agent demo via `AO_DAYTONA_AGENT_ARGV` (e.g. `["claude","-p","say hello"]`) with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` injected.

## Live validation (2026-07-28) — DONE, all green against real Daytona

Run with the maintainer's test org + the pushed `ao-agent-sandbox:dev` snapshot + a real `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (credentials via env only):

| Test | Result | Proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestLive_ClientSandboxLifecycle` | **PASS 4.4s** | sandbox create→started ~2–3s, exec, PTY-WebSocket round-trip + resize, delete |
| `TestLive_RuntimeSessionLifecycle` | **PASS 14.4s** | workspace (sandbox+clone) → tmux agent → scrollback → send round-trip → park → wake (same handle) → synchronous teardown |
| `TestLive_RealAgentSession` | **PASS 13.6s** | real Claude Code **authenticated with no browser flow** (boot-env token injection), answered a prompt; keep-alive shell held after exit |

The live runs surfaced three real async-state behaviors (stop/delete return 200 while state lags; list trails GET) — fixed + regression-tested in 475d285f8. Terminal streaming is validated at the port level (PTY WebSocket ↔ `ports.Stream`); in-app rendering awaits phase-3 per-session runtime selection — **merging this PR changes nothing for local installs** (`runtimeselect` still picks tmux/conpty by OS; no `AO_RUNTIME=daytona` gate is included). Confirmed gap: sandbox→daemon activity events need the control plane's reachable `AO_API_BASE` + per-session token (CLI side unit-tested). Full details: `docs/cloud/daytona-runtime.md` §6.

## What I need from you (maintainer) — ✅ both provided; live suite green

1. A Daytona org + API key (https://app.daytona.io/dashboard/keys, scopes: write/delete sandboxes) exported as `DAYTONA_API_KEY` to run the live smoke: `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/daytona/ -run TestLive -v`. ~$200 free credit covers this many times over (each run is a few sandbox-minutes).
2. For the full real-agent demo: a custom snapshot with tmux/git/node + Claude Code (+ the `ao` Linux binary for hooks) — `daytona snapshot create ao-agent --dockerfile …`; I can write that Dockerfile as a follow-up. Until then the lifecycle test best-effort apt-installs tmux into the default snapshot.

## Known gaps / follow-ups (documented in the design doc)

- Control plane must supply: reachable `AO_API_BASE` + per-session token minting/validation, the agent-harness snapshot, repo-URL resolver + git credentials for private repos (the default resolver reads local `origin` for the hybrid local-daemon setup).
- Spawn attachments / per-project provisioning write local files today — cloud sessions need those uploaded via the toolbox fs API (control-plane concern, phase 3).
- Preserve refs live on the sandbox disk; pushing them to `refs/ao/preserved/*` on origin is a follow-up.
- Parked sessions lose tmux scrollback (Daytona stop kills processes); agent transcripts survive on disk and native resume works.

title: bug(preview): bare `ao preview` auto-opens arbitrary Markdown docs in browser panel
body:
## Bug

Bare `ao preview` (no args) — which agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) run automatically on new sessions via the `using-ao` skill — auto-discovers and opens an arbitrary workspace Markdown file (e.g. `test/cli/README.md`) in the browser panel instead of staying empty.

**Reported by:** @prateek in Discord (#bug-triage thread)
**Analyzed against:** `218c39199` (main, 2026-07-29)
**Confidence:** High — traced exact code path, specific lines, mechanism fully explained

## Reproduction

1. Start a new worker session in a Markdown-rich repo with no `index.html` (e.g. agent-orchestrator itself)
2. The agent learns `ao preview` from the `using-ao` skill and runs it with no arguments
3. Browser panel opens to `http://ao-preview.<hash>.localhost:3001/test/cli/README.md` instead of staying empty

## Root Cause

This is an **incomplete fix of issue [#2859](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2859)**. PR [#2860](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2860) fixed the **poller** path (`backend/internal/preview/poller.go`) to use `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` (index.html-only, no `.md` fallback) for never-previewed sessions. But the **HTTP controller** path — which bare `ao preview` triggers — still calls `DiscoverEntry` with the full `.md`/`.html` fallback.

The code path:

```
Agent runs bare `ao preview`
  → CLI: POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview  {url: ""}
  → setPreview handler (sessions.go:442)
  → discoverPreviewEntry(workspacePath)        ← BUG
  → previewutil.DiscoverEntry(workspacePath)
      → no index.html found
      → falls back to mostRecentPreviewable()
      → walks workspace, finds newest .md (e.g. test/cli/README.md)
  → sets preview_url → frontend browser panel navigates there via CDC
```

The fix at `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:859`:

```go
// BEFORE (buggy):
func discoverPreviewEntry(workspacePath string) (string, bool) {
    entry, ok := previewutil.DiscoverEntry(workspacePath)  // .md fallback
    return entry.Path, ok
}

// AFTER (fixed):
func discoverPreviewEntry(workspacePath string) (string, bool) {
    entry, ok := previewutil.DiscoverWebEntrypoint(workspacePath)  // no fallback
    return entry.Path, ok
}
```

This function is called from three handlers:
- `setPreview` (line 442) — `POST /preview` with empty URL (bare `ao preview`)
- `preview` GET (line 258) — returns the auto-discovered preview entry
- `previewOriginEntry` (line 328) — serving preview without a stored entry

PR #2860's commit message says `DiscoverEntry` was kept "behavior-preserving for its other callers (the explicit 'ao preview' HTTP path)" — but that assumption breaks down when agents call `ao preview` automatically rather than a human choosing to.

## Fix

One-line change: `DiscoverEntry` → `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` in `discoverPreviewEntry`. Mirrors the poller fix exactly.

Fix PR: coming in this issue.

## Impact

- Every new agent session in a Markdown-rich repo opens its browser panel to an arbitrary `.md` file
- Annoying UX noise, not a functional break
- Severity: P2

## Related

- [#2859](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/2859) — original "new session browser opens non-empty" bug (poller path, closed)
- [PR #2860](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2860) — poller fix that introduced `DiscoverWebEntrypoint` (did not fix the HTTP controller path)

title: fix(preview): don't auto-discover Markdown docs via bare ao preview

title: docs: explain the macOS Gatekeeper block on the download page
body:
Refs https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3260

Does **not** close that issue. It mitigates the symptom; the cause is still unknown.

> Note when merging: the first commit message (`355ce6d39`) contains a stale `Closes #3260` line from the original version of this PR. Please drop it from the squash body, or 3260 will auto-close while the cause is still open.

## Problem

A teammate could not install from https://aoagents.dev/download/. macOS refused to open the app with "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified", offering only Move to Trash and Cancel. They retried four times (Finder had reached `Agent Orchestrator 4`) before giving up.

The artifact is not at fault. I downloaded the exact build they had (stable v0.11.0 arm64, matched by bundle size at 269.8 MB decimal versus 279.3 MB for x64) and it passes every check, including with a Chrome-style `com.apple.quarantine` attribute set and with Gatekeeper caches bypassed:

```
codesign -dvvv     Developer ID Application: Prateek Karnal (X9LNSP8MC2)
                   flags=0x10000(runtime), Notarization Ticket=stapled
spctl --assess --ignore-cache --no-cache   accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID
syspolicy_check distribution               App passed all pre-distribution checks
codesign --verify --deep --strict          valid on disk, satisfies its Designated Requirement
```

@harshitsinghbhandari reproduced this independently and also confirmed the alias and versioned assets are byte-identical.

**Why one machine refused it is unknown.** An earlier revision of this PR claimed Gatekeeper performs an online ticket lookup against `api.apple-cloudkit.com` that a VPN or DNS filter had blocked. That was wrong and has been retracted: the observation came from `xcrun stapler validate -v`, which is stapler's own validation path and performs that lookup whether or not a ticket is already stapled, so it says nothing about the launch check. Stapling exists so first launch works offline. Details in the review thread below.

What remains true is the part that matters for the page: the build is signed and notarized, so the dialog is not evidence the download is unsafe, and users should not be left concluding it is.

## Change

Documentation only. No packaging, signing, or CI changes.

- `frontend/src/landing/src/app/download/page.tsx`: an "If macOS blocks the app on first launch" section below the Stable/Nightly grids. Symptom-only. States that builds are Developer ID signed and notarized, gives the right-click and Open steps (noting that double-clicking offers only Move to Trash, which is what made the reporter retry instead of getting through), and otherwise asks for diagnostics.
- Second card collects what we need to find the cause: `sw_vers`, `codesign -dvvv`, `spctl -a -t exec -vvv`, and `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.syspolicy"'`, with a link to open an issue.
- `README.md`: the same guidance in two sentences, since the README is the other main download entry point.

Deliberately not documented: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`. Publishing it would tell every visitor to strip quarantine from an app before macOS has evaluated it, which is bad advice on a public page independent of this bug, and it would mask the cause. A code comment records that so it does not get added back later. An earlier revision also had a `curl` snippet that avoided the flag rather than clearing it; same objection, also removed.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` on the landing tsconfig: clean.
- Rendered at `http://localhost:3112/download/` and asserted against the server HTML that `xattr`, `com.apple.quarantine`, `curl -L`, `ditto`, and the "could not reach Apple" wording are all absent, and that the right-click steps, diagnostics block, and issue link are present.
- Card classes, theme tokens, and 2-space indentation match the surrounding file. Both `<pre>` blocks are wrapped in `overflow-x-auto` so long commands scroll instead of breaking the page.

Not verified visually: the browser automation extension timed out and no local headless Chrome was available. Content and structure are confirmed by executing, but not pixels. Worth a look at the preview deploy.

## Notes

- Different failure from https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3034 and https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3152, which are Squirrel.Mac ShipIt auto-update on existing installs. This is first install: no ShipIt, no blockmap. The stapled ticket is a regular file at `Contents/CodeResources`, so the AppleDouble/xattr gap in those issues cannot strip it.
- Out of scope here: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` 301-redirects to `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`, so the stable download links in `constants.ts` and the README take an extra hop. They work because the redirect is followed, but they should be repointed.

title: fix: prevent foreign PR auto-attribution
body:
## What changed

- resolve and cache the human account authenticated with the GitHub provider
- ignore foreign-authored PRs during automatic branch-based discovery
- keep the existing discovery fallback when identity is unavailable or belongs to a bot/app

- add regression coverage for owner filtering, case-insensitive logins, fallback behavior, caching, and exact-match priority

## Why

The SCM observer previously attributed PRs using only the head repository and branch name. In shared repositories, another developer could create a PR from a colliding branch name and have it attached to the wrong AO session, potentially causing incorrect lifecycle behavior.

Authenticated identity remains provider-scoped and in memory; it is not persisted on sessions. Explicit `ao pr claim` remains the override when another user opens a PR for a session branch.

title: Plan: move macOS first-install distribution to .dmg, keep zip for auto-update (supersedes #3152)
body:
## Summary

Move macOS distribution to a `.dmg` for first install, while keeping the existing `.zip` publishing for electron-updater's auto-update path. This supersedes #3152. References: #3034, #3151, #3152.

Priorities, in order:
1. First install should have no extraction step, so the class of failure where a third-party unzip tool mishandles AppleDouble entries and breaks the code signature seal cannot happen at all.
2. Electron auto-update keeps working. Hard requirement, no regression.
3. Get blockmaps right, including deciding whether macOS differential updates can be re-enabled.

## Why this supersedes #3152, not just extends it

#3152 proposes replacing `@electron-forge/maker-zip` with ditto-based packaging in `forge.config.ts`, on the premise that matching electron-builder's own zip format (via ditto) is what makes mac auto-update reliable. That premise does not hold, on two independent lines of evidence:

- Pulkit7070's own investigation on #3152 found that `app-builder-lib` 26.15.3 does not use `ditto` for its mac zips (it uses `zip -q -r -y`), that electron-builder's real zips contain zero AppleDouble (`._*`) entries, and that adding them "changes nothing measurable." Their read of #3034 is that the actual corruption came from a blockmap differential-download bug, not from zip-format mismatch, and that #3151 (already merged, forces full downloads on mac) already fixes it pending one real auto-update cycle to confirm.
- Reading `app-builder-lib`'s blockmap generator directly (`packages/app-builder-lib/src/targets/blockmap/blockmap.ts`, tag `electron-builder@26.15.3`) confirms this independently: it chunks the file as an opaque byte stream via Rabin fingerprinting. It has no zip-structure awareness at all, so AppleDouble entries were never relevant to blockmap correctness.

So the ditto-zip-format question and the blockmap-corruption question are separate, and #3152 conflated them. A `.dmg` for first install sidesteps the original bug class architecturally (no user-driven extraction step at all) rather than trying to make the zip format extraction-tool-proof, and #3151 already covers the auto-update corruption path independently. Recommend closing #3152 in favor of this plan.

## Decisions

### 1. Maker: bridge to `app-builder-lib` via `buildForge`, not `@electron-forge/maker-dmg`

Add `frontend/makers/maker-dmg.ts`, mirroring the existing `maker-nsis.ts` pattern (a thin `MakerBase` subclass that calls `app-builder-lib`'s `buildForge` with a `mac: ["dmg"]` target), instead of using Forge's own `@electron-forge/maker-dmg`.

Why: `maker-dmg` wraps `electron-installer-dmg` -> `appdmg`, neither of which have any notarize/staple code (confirmed from source, both packages). It only optionally codesigns the dmg via a passthrough option. `app-builder-lib`'s dmg target has the exact same limitation (`dmg.sign` defaults to `false`, and its own docs warn against enabling it: "Signing is not required and will lead to unwanted errors in combination with notarization requirements"). So neither maker solves signing for us out of the box, and the choice comes down to consistency: `app-builder-lib` is already a direct dependency and already proven for a second-target bridge (NSIS), so reusing that pattern avoids introducing a second, unrelated packaging engine (`appdmg`) into the project for a single platform. `buildForge` also needs no extra host tooling beyond `hdiutil`, which is already required either way and is standard on macOS runners.

Tradeoff: `maker-dmg` is Forge's own first-party maker and has a smaller, simpler API. But since it buys us nothing on signing, and we would need the same manual notarize/staple postMake step regardless of maker choice, the consistency win favors `app-builder-lib`.

### 2. Auto-update: confirmed, zip stays required forever

Confirmed from source, `packages/electron-updater/src/MacUpdater.ts` at tag `electron-updater@6.8.9`:

```ts
const zipFileInfo = findFile(files, "zip", ["pkg", "dmg"])
if (zipFileInfo == null) {
  throw newError(`ZIP file not provided: ...`, "ERR_UPDATER_ZIP_FILE_NOT_FOUND")
}
```

`findFile` explicitly excludes `.pkg` and `.dmg` from candidates. `MacUpdater` hands the zip to Electron's native Squirrel.Mac updater, which only knows how to unzip and swap the `.app` bundle. There is no code path anywhere in this file that can install an update from a `.dmg`. This confirms the brief's expectation exactly: **the zip and `latest-mac.yml` must keep publishing forever**, unchanged. The dmg is first-install only, additive to the existing darwin maker-zip entry in `forge.config.ts`, never a replacement.

### 3. Signing: the dmg needs its own explicit sign + notarize + staple step

Confirmed: neither `maker-dmg` nor `app-builder-lib`'s dmg target notarizes or staples the dmg container by default. The `.app` inside is already fully sealed by Forge's existing `packagerConfig.osxSign`/`osxNotarize` (unchanged, runs before any maker). Concretely, what has to happen:

1. `packagerConfig` signs + notarizes + staples the `.app` as it does today, before any maker runs. No change.
2. New `maker-dmg.ts` packages that already-sealed `.app` into an **unsigned** dmg (leave `dmg.sign` unset).
3. New `hooks.postMake` in `forge.config.ts`, scoped to the darwin dmg artifact, runs:
   - `codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --timestamp "$DMG_PATH"`, reusing the same `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`/`CSC_LINK` resolution already used for `osxSign`.
   - `xcrun notarytool submit "$DMG_PATH" --wait`, reusing the same two credential shapes already supported (`AO_NOTARY_PROFILE` keychain profile locally, `APPLE_API_KEY`/`APPLE_API_KEY_ID`/`APPLE_API_ISSUER` in CI).
   - `xcrun stapler staple "$DMG_PATH"` on success.
4. Verify with the same method the brief used to confirm v0.11.1's zip: `spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature -v "$DMG_PATH"` expecting `accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID`, plus `stapler validate`.

This is deliberately explicit and self-contained rather than relying on Gatekeeper propagating the `.app`'s stapled ticket through an unsealed dmg container, since that is exactly the failure mode the brief's verified facts are guarding against.

### 4. Blockmap: do not guess, run the concrete experiment first

Now that mac zips are ditto-built (per the verified facts), the immediate question is whether that alone unblocks re-enabling differential updates. It does not, and it was never the blocker: as shown above, `app-builder-lib`'s blockmap algorithm is a pure byte-stream Rabin chunker with zero zip-structure awareness, so the zip-building tool was never what made diffs succeed or fail. Also worth noting: the blockmap format's `version` field is hardcoded `"2"` regardless of which tool built the underlying zip, so switching zip-building tools does **not** trigger any automatic "format changed, do a full download" safety fallback in `DifferentialDownloader`. A bad diff between an old-format zip and a new-format zip would silently attempt a byte-level patch rather than detecting incompatibility.

Per #3152's own thread, the real suspected cause of #3034 was corruption in the differential-download/patch-apply path itself, which #3151 sidesteps by disabling mac blockmaps entirely (always full download). Re-enabling requires proving that path is actually sound now, not just that the zip format looks right. Concrete experiment, do not skip steps:

1. Publish two consecutive real mac releases through the actual production pipeline (whatever the private signing/release pipeline currently does, ditto re-zip included).
2. Temporarily generate `.blockmap` sidecars for both (run `writeBlockmap` locally against the two real published zips; do not need to touch the live pipeline for this step).
3. Run `computeOperations`/`DifferentialDownloader` against the two blockmaps and confirm: it completes without a "version is different" or corruption error, the log line `Full: X, To download: Y (Z%)` reports a sane percentage for the actual delta between the two versions, and the reconstructed `.app` after patch-apply passes `codesign --verify --deep --strict` and `spctl --assess` exactly like the brief's v0.11.1 check.
4. Only after that round-trip is clean, revert #3151's mac skip in `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs` (re-add `writeBlockmap` for mac) and update the release pipeline guard to require the mac blockmap sidecar again.
5. Prove this on a non-production release channel first (the existing `AO_RELEASE_REPO` dev-loop override), not on a real user-facing release.

The first update crossing from a pre-ditto zip to a ditto zip will predictably show a poor (near-100%) diff. That is an expected one-time format-switch cost, not evidence the mechanism is broken.

### 5. `ao start` bootstrapper: keep the zip, no change

`backend/internal/cli/start.go` already extracts with `ditto -x -k` specifically because plain unzip corrupts the signature (see the comment at `start.go:282`-ish). This is a non-interactive, fully automated flow with a hardcoded extraction command, so it never suffers the failure class the dmg is meant to fix (a human picking the wrong unzip tool). Switching it to dmg + `hdiutil` would add real new failure modes (mount/detach races, leftover mounted volumes on a killed process) for zero benefit, since the current path is already correct. Recommend leaving `assetName()` and `fetchAppDarwin` unchanged.

### 6. Homebrew cask: switch to the dmg

Current cask (`AgentWrapper/homebrew-tap`, `Casks/agent-orchestrator.rb`) installs directly from the versioned zip with per-arch sha256:

```ruby
url "https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/v#{version}/agent-orchestrator-darwin-#{arch}.zip", ...
app "Agent Orchestrator.app"
```

Recommend switching `url` to the versioned dmg asset once it publishes, and updating `sha256` accordingly. The `app "Agent Orchestrator.app"` stanza does not need to change: Homebrew Cask natively handles both zip-unzip and dmg-mount-and-copy as first-class install mechanisms, so this is a low-risk, well-trodden change on Homebrew's side. This removes Homebrew's own unzip step from the picture too, consistent with goal 1. This lives in a separate repo and is not part of this repo's PR.

### 7. Link surfaces

Two separate concerns, do not conflate them in one PR:

**Extension change (zip -> dmg), scoped to this work:**
- `frontend/src/landing/packages/shared/src/constants.ts`: `DOWNLOAD_URL_MAC_ARM64`, `DOWNLOAD_URL_MAC_X64`.
- `README.md`: the macOS rows of the download table.
- Homebrew cask `url`/`sha256` (separate repo, see above).

**Org rename (`AgentWrapper` -> `Untrivial-ai`, confirmed live: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` 301s to `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`):** a much larger, unrelated surface: `forge.config.ts` (`DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO`), `backend/internal/cli/start.go` (`releaseRepo`), `frontend/scripts` comments, docs (`docs/development.md`, `docs/plans/*`, `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`), landing content (`changelog.mdx`, `docs/changelog.mdx`, `examples.mdx` x5, `guides/multi-project.mdx`, `installation.mdx`, `migration.mdx`, `troubleshooting.mdx`), `install.sh`, the agent-skills route, `AppMockup.tsx`, `mdx.tsx`, `changelog.ts`, test files, `report-problem.ts` (+ test), `packages/build-binaries.sh`, `skills/bug-triage/SKILL.md` (18 refs), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, issue/PR templates. Only `release-latest-guard.yml` has been updated so far. Recommend repointing only the exact lines this dmg work already touches (the constants and README rows above) to `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` while we're in there, and filing the full org-rename cleanup as its own separate follow-up issue. Not proposing that broader cleanup here.

### 8. Rollout and rollback

Assume both zip and dmg are published during the whole transition; the zip never stops publishing (see decision 2).

1. Land `maker-dmg.ts` + the darwin makers list addition in `forge.config.ts` (added alongside the existing `maker-zip` entry, not replacing it).
2. Land the `postMake` sign+notarize+staple hook for the dmg, reusing existing credential env vars.
3. Test end-to-end on the existing dev-loop fork (`AO_RELEASE_REPO` override), verify with `spctl`/`stapler validate` the same way v0.11.1 was verified.
4. Hand the requirements below to that repo's orchestrator and wait for readiness there.
5. Cut one real release publishing both zip and dmg, with the update feed (`latest-mac.yml`) and zip untouched. Verify the dmg installs cleanly and the existing zip-based auto-update is unaffected.
6. Only after that real-world verification, flip the download-page and README links from zip to dmg (decision 7). Update the Homebrew cask separately.
7. Rollback is cheap by construction: since both artifacts publish throughout, rolling back is just reverting the link-surface change in step 6, no release pull, no version bump, no auto-update impact. If the dmg maker or signing itself breaks, drop the darwin dmg maker entry and stop publishing it; the zip remains the only mac asset exactly as today.
8. Never drop the zip as a published release asset, only potentially as a *download-page default* far downstream, since `MacUpdater` requires it permanently (decision 2).
9. Blockmap re-enablement (decision 4) is fully independent of this rollout and should not be bundled into it; it can land before, after, or separately, with its own experiment gate.

## Changes needed in the private signing/release pipeline (separate repo, not touched here)

Handing these to that repo's orchestrator as precise requirements, since that pipeline currently owns the actual signing/re-zip/publish steps and the public `frontend-release.yml` workflow is paused:

- Publish the new `.dmg` build output as a release asset alongside the existing zip (mirror whatever alias-naming convention it already uses for the zip, e.g. `agent-orchestrator-darwin-{arch}.dmg`).
- Confirm its post-build re-zip/re-sign step (the `ditto -c -k --keepParent` step referenced in the verified facts) only globs `*.zip` outputs and does not touch or re-wrap the `.dmg` file, since the dmg is signed/notarized/stapled inline during `npm run publish`'s own `postMake` hook (decision 3), not by that pipeline step.
- No new signing credentials or steps should be needed there for the dmg specifically, since dmg sealing is self-contained in this repo's Forge config. Flag if that assumption is wrong given how that pipeline is actually structured.

## Non-goals

- Not proposing to un-pause the release workflows. That decision belongs to whoever owns that switch.
- Not proposing the full org-rename cleanup (decision 7), only the specific lines this work already touches.
- Not modifying the private signing/release pipeline directly; the section above is a handoff list only.
- Not re-enabling mac differential updates as part of this rollout; decision 4 is a separate, gated follow-up.

title: Orchestrator and worker sessions share the same numeric ID space — can't tell them apart by name
body:
## Problem

Orchestrator and worker sessions in the same project share one numeric counter (`sessions.num`, unique per `project_id`), so session IDs like `myproject-114` give no indication of the session's `kind` (`orchestrator` vs `worker`). The two are visually indistinguishable in:

- tmux session names (`tmux ls` just shows `myproject-114`)
- worktree paths (`~/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/<session-id>` for workers vs a fixed `orchestrator/` subfolder for the orchestrator — but nothing in the *session id itself* signals this)
- shell prompts inside the session
- casual mentions in logs/messages between sessions

## Why this matters

When the orchestrator crashes or its shell gets stuck (e.g. cwd removed out from under it), there's no quick way to tell "which of these dozens of `myproject-N` sessions is the orchestrator I need to recover" without cross-referencing the database (`ao session get`, or querying `sessions.kind` directly). In a project with 100+ historical sessions, scanning `ao session ls` output for the one `orchestrator` entry among many `worker` entries is slow and error-prone, especially under time pressure while debugging a crash.

## Suggested fix

Make the session's role visible directly in its identifier/display, e.g.:
- Prefix or suffix the id/display name for orchestrator sessions (e.g. `myproject-orch-114` or `myproject-114 (orchestrator)`)
- Or at minimum, make `ao session ls` / `ao orchestrator ls` visually distinguish kind more prominently than requiring a separate lookup
- Or give the orchestrator a stable, predictable id per project (since there's usually at most one active orchestrator) instead of sharing the worker counter

Any of these would make it much faster to locate/recover the orchestrator session by name alone, especially during incident response.

title: fix(assets): tighten ao-logo viewBox to square around artwork
body:
The AO logo's viewBox was `150 80 870 760` — a rectangle with uneven padding, leaving the mark off-center wherever it lands in a square slot (favicon, app icon, README 160×160, `size-4` header img).

Computed the exact geometry bbox across all 22 paths (cubic Bézier extrema plus `translate` transforms; fills only, so no stroke bleed): x `170.86–908.09`, y `129.79–789.50` = **737.23 × 659.70**. One zero-area path at `(961.116, 398.09)` renders nothing and was excluded — it had been inflating the apparent width by ~53 units.

New viewBox: `170.86 91.03 737.23 737.23` — square on the wider axis, vertically centered. Horizontally exact-tight; ~38.8 units above and below, the minimum possible for a square since the mark is wider than tall. Square over tight-rect because every consumer slot is square, so the padding is better explicit and centered than left to each renderer to letterbox or stretch.

Path data untouched. One-line change per file; all four copies remain byte-identical to each other.

- `assets/ao-logo.svg`
- `frontend/assets/ao-logo.svg`
- `frontend/src/landing/public/ao-logo.svg`
- `frontend/src/landing/public/favicon.svg`

1. First install should have no extraction step, so the class of failure where a third-party unzip tool mishandles AppleDouble entries and breaks the code signature seal cannot happen at all.
2. Electron auto-update keeps working. Hard requirement, no regression.
3. Mac differential updates stay permanently disabled (full download only). Document why, and what evidence would be needed to ever revisit that.

#3152 proposes replacing `@electron-forge/maker-zip` with ditto-based packaging in `forge.config.ts`, on the premise that matching electron-builder's own zip format (via ditto) is what makes mac auto-update reliable. That premise does not hold, on two independent lines of evidence:

A correctly-formed ditto zip with the full AppleDouble set still corrupted on the differential path. The AppleDouble-format theory in both #3034 and #3152 is not the operative cause.


Recommend switching `url` to the versioned dmg asset once it publishes, and updating `sha256` accordingly. The `app "Agent Orchestrator.app"` stanza does not need to change: Homebrew Cask natively handles both zip-unzip and dmg-mount-and-copy as first-class install mechanisms, so this is a low-risk, well-trodden change on Homebrew's side. This removes Homebrew's own unzip step from the picture too, consistent with goal 1. This lives in a separate repo and is not part of this repo's PR.

### 7. Link surfaces

Two separate concerns, do not conflate them in one PR:

**Extension change (zip -> dmg), scoped to this work:**
- `frontend/src/landing/packages/shared/src/constants.ts`: `DOWNLOAD_URL_MAC_ARM64`, `DOWNLOAD_URL_MAC_X64`.
- `README.md`: the macOS rows of the download table.
- Homebrew cask `url`/`sha256` (separate repo, see above).

**Org rename (`AgentWrapper` -> `Untrivial-ai`, confirmed live: `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` 301s to `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`):** a much larger, unrelated surface: `forge.config.ts` (`DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO`), `backend/internal/cli/start.go` (`releaseRepo`), `frontend/scripts` comments, docs (`docs/development.md`, `docs/plans/*`, `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`), landing content (`changelog.mdx`, `docs/changelog.mdx`, `examples.mdx` x5, `guides/multi-project.mdx`, `installation.mdx`, `migration.mdx`, `troubleshooting.mdx`), `install.sh`, the agent-skills route, `AppMockup.tsx`, `mdx.tsx`, `changelog.ts`, test files, `report-problem.ts` (+ test), `packages/build-binaries.sh`, `skills/bug-triage/SKILL.md` (18 refs), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, issue/PR templates. Only `release-latest-guard.yml` has been updated so far. Recommend repointing only the exact lines this dmg work already touches (the constants and README rows above) to `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` while we're in there, and filing the full org-rename cleanup as its own separate follow-up issue. Not proposing that broader cleanup here.

### 8. Rollout and rollback

Assume both zip and dmg are published during the whole transition; the zip never stops publishing (see decision 2).

1. Land `maker-dmg.ts` + the darwin makers list addition in `forge.config.ts` (added alongside the existing `maker-zip` entry, not replacing it).
2. Land the `postMake` sign+notarize+staple hook for the dmg, reusing existing credential env vars.
3. Test end-to-end on the existing dev-loop fork (`AO_RELEASE_REPO` override), verify with `spctl`/`stapler validate` the same way v0.11.1 was verified.
4. Hand the requirements below to that repo's orchestrator and wait for readiness there.
5. Cut one real release publishing both zip and dmg, with the update feed (`latest-mac.yml`) and zip untouched. Verify the dmg installs cleanly and the existing zip-based auto-update is unaffected.
6. Only after that real-world verification, flip the download-page and README links from zip to dmg (decision 7). Update the Homebrew cask separately.
7. Rollback is cheap by construction: since both artifacts publish throughout, rolling back is just reverting the link-surface change in step 6, no release pull, no version bump, no auto-update impact. If the dmg maker or signing itself breaks, drop the darwin dmg maker entry and stop publishing it; the zip remains the only mac asset exactly as today.
8. Never drop the zip as a published release asset, only potentially as a *download-page default* far downstream, since `MacUpdater` requires it permanently (decision 2).
9. Blockmap/differential updates stay disabled throughout and are not part of this rollout at all; decision 4 documents why and is not expected to change absent a new upstream fix.

## Changes needed in the private signing/release pipeline (separate repo, not touched here)

Handing these to that repo's orchestrator as precise requirements, since that pipeline currently owns the actual signing/re-zip/publish steps and the public `frontend-release.yml` workflow is paused:

- Publish the new `.dmg` build output as a release asset alongside the existing zip (mirror whatever alias-naming convention it already uses for the zip, e.g. `agent-orchestrator-darwin-{arch}.dmg`).
- Confirm its post-build re-zip/re-sign step (the `ditto -c -k --keepParent` step referenced in the verified facts) only globs `*.zip` outputs and does not touch or re-wrap the `.dmg` file, since the dmg is signed/notarized/stapled inline during `npm run publish`'s own `postMake` hook (decision 3), not by that pipeline step.
- No new signing credentials or steps should be needed there for the dmg specifically, since dmg sealing is self-contained in this repo's Forge config. Flag if that assumption is wrong given how that pipeline is actually structured.

## Non-goals

- Not proposing to un-pause the release workflows. That decision belongs to whoever owns that switch.
- Not proposing the full org-rename cleanup (decision 7), only the specific lines this work already touches.
- Not modifying the private signing/release pipeline directly; the section above is a handoff list only.
- Not proposing to re-enable mac differential updates. Decision 4 treats full-download-only as the settled baseline and documents the evidence bar for ever revisiting it.

title: Landing page: dead anchors, stuck hash, unstyled scrollbar, and placeholder testimonials
body:
## Summary Four defects found on the marketing site during a pass over the landing page and shared UI package. Two are P2 (broken navigation, credibility), two are P3 (interaction polish, visual polish). All four are confirmed in code with file/line references below. | # | Issue | Severity | Effort | |---|-------|----------|--------| | 1 | Footer "Features" / "Agents" are dead anchors | P2 | Small — add IDs | | 2 | `#see-it` hash persists in URL after scroll | P3 | Small — router fix | | 3 | Scrollbar unstyled, clashes with dark theme | P3 | Trivial — CSS | --- ## 1. Footer "Features" and "Agents" are dead anchors — P2 Both footer links point at anchors that do not exist on the page. | Link | Points to | Reality | |------|-----------|---------| | Features | `/#features` (`Footer.tsx:35`) | `FeaturesSection.tsx:29` has no `id` on its `
` — only `className` | | Agents | `/#agents` (`Footer.tsx:36`) | No `id="agents"` exists anywhere on the page — zero matches | `NAV_ITEMS` in `packages/shared/src/constants.ts:48` also uses `/#features`, so the same broken anchor is live in the nav. **Proposed fix** - Add `id="features"` to the `
` in `FeaturesSection`. - For "Agents": there is no agents section on the landing page. Either remove the footer link, or give an existing section an `id="agents"` (`HarnessCoverageDemo:251` already mentions Agents and is a reasonable target). - Keep `NAV_ITEMS` consistent with whatever anchors end up existing. **Why P2:** broken navigation, not cosmetic — clicking the link does nothing. --- ## 2. `#see-it` hash stays in the URL after scrolling — P3 The `see-it` section does exist (`VideoSection.tsx:29`). The problem is Next.js App Router default behavior: clicking `/#see-it` sets the hash and scrolls, but the hash is never cleared when the user scrolls away. Clicking "Demo" a second time does nothing, because the browser considers the target already current. **Repro** 1. Click "Demo" in the nav → scrolls to the video section, URL becomes `/#see-it`. 2. Scroll back to the top. 3. Click "Demo" again → nothing happens. **Proposed fix** (any one of): - Add an effect that strips the hash once the scroll settles (e.g. a `usePathname` watcher or scroll-end handler). - Replace the raw anchor with a click handler that calls `router.push('/')` and then `scrollIntoView` manually. - `scroll-mt-*` on the section improves the landing offset but does **not** fix the hash behavior on its own. **Why P3:** first click works; only repeated clicks are affected. No data loss or breakage. --- ## 3. Scrollbar is unstyled and clashes with the dark theme — P3 No scrollbar styling exists anywhere in the codebase: - `globals.css` imports `packages/ui/src/globals.css`, which contains no `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules. - The only related utility is `scrollbar-hide`, used to hide scrollbars inside internal demos. - The main page and docs therefore render the browser default scrollbar, which reads light against the dark site. **Proposed fix** — add themed scrollbar rules to `packages/ui/src/globals.css`: ```css ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10px; height: 10px; } ::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: transparent; } ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--muted-border); /* or appropriate theme token */ border-radius: 6px; border: 2px solid transparent; background-clip: content-box; } ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background: var(--border); background-clip: content-box; } /* Firefox */ * { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--muted-border) transparent; } ``` Should use theme tokens so it works in both light and dark modes. **Why P3:** pure polish, but the default scrollbar makes an otherwise premium-looking dark site feel unfinished.

title: fix: replace terminal tab strip session picker with a new-terminal button
body:
Fixes #3208

## Problem

PR #3138 turned the "+" at the end of the terminal tab strip into a `DropdownMenu`
listing every worker session, so Session B's terminal could be pinned as a tab on
Session A's page. `availableSessions` in `SessionView.tsx` flattened **all**
workspaces, so sessions from other projects showed up too. Users expect "+" to
create a terminal, not browse sessions.

## Changes

**`CenterPane.tsx`** — the dropdown is gone. The button at the end of the strip is
now a terminal icon (`aria-label="New terminal"`) that calls `onNewShellTerminal`
directly. Dropped with it: `isTabLauncherOpen` / `showAllSessions` / `sessionSearch`
state, `COMPACT_SESSION_LIMIT`, the search `Input`, and the
`projectSessions` / `availableProjectSessions` / `onAddProjectSession` /
`onCloseProjectSession` / `onSelectProjectSession` / `tabOwnerSessionId` props. The
strip now renders the session's own tab plus its shells.

**`SessionView.tsx`** — new shells open with `{ projectId: session?.workspaceId, sessionId }`,
i.e. the session on screen, instead of the pinning owner's ids. The daemon's
`resolveShellTerminalWorkingDir` prefers `SessionWorkspace(sessionID)` over the
project root, so this is what puts the terminal in the right worktree. Shell-tab
filtering keys on `sessionId` for the same reason.

**Dead-code removal** — the picker was the only writer of the pinning state, so
leaving it would strand tabs pinned before the upgrade (they'd rehydrate from
localStorage with no way to remove them). Removed `sessionTabsByOwner`,
`addSessionTab`, `removeSessionTab` and the `ao.sessionTabs` persistence from
`ui-store.ts`; the `?tabOwner=` search param from both session routes and
`_shell.tsx` (the Ctrl+Shift+` handler now scopes to the route's own session).

## Verification

- **Manual, real desktop app.** Clicking the button on a live session opened a shell
  in `~/.ao/dev/data/worktrees/ao/orchestrator/ao-orchestrator` — the session
  worktree, not the project root at `E:\ao`.
- **Daemon contract, live.** `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` with `{projectId, sessionId}`
  (what the renderer now sends) returns `workingDir` = the session worktree;
  with `{projectId}` alone it returns the project root. That difference is the fix.
- **Renderer, driven in a browser.** Exactly one "New terminal" button, `menu` and
  `menuitem` counts both 0 on click, shell tabs 0 → 1 → 2 and back on close, and a
  second session shows none of the first session's shells.
- **Unit:** typecheck clean; affected suites pass. Full suite last run at 1180 passed /
  4 failed — all in `src/main/supervisor-link.test.ts` (`listen EACCES` on unix
  sockets), pre-existing on Windows and untouched here.
- **e2e:** `shell-terminal-tabs.spec.ts` test 1 passes again (see below).

## Notes for the reviewer

- **`shell-terminal-tabs.spec.ts` was already broken by #3138.** It expects a tab-strip
  button named "New terminal", which #3138 had renamed to "Add tab". This PR restores
  that name, and I fixed the spec's session-tab selector (the old `getByTitle("Session terminal")`
  stopped matching once the label truncates, and a plain role+name match collides with
  the sidebar). It now passes.
- **One test in that file is still red and I left it alone:**
  `opens a terminal from the board, where no session view is mounted` expects a
  board-level "New terminal" button. No such button exists anywhere in the codebase —
  the board's only entry point is Ctrl+Shift+`, which is an Electron menu accelerator
  and unreachable in the browser-based e2e run. Fixing it means either restoring a
  board button or dropping the test; that's a product call, not part of this fix. The
  regression it guarded is covered by `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx`.
- **Unrelated, but worth a follow-up:** `playwright.config.ts` uses
  `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 npm run dev:web`, which fails on Windows
  (`'VITE_NO_ELECTRON' is not recognized`). I started the dev server by hand to run e2e.
- The repo has no Prettier config or format script, so I matched the surrounding style
  by hand rather than running a formatter (a default Prettier run reflows these files
  completely).
  
---

cc @illegalcall

title: fix: agent logos in the README, sourced from the renderer asset folder
body:
## What was wrong

The Supported Agents list pointed 13 of the 23 icons at `frontend/src/landing/public/docs/logos/`, a directory that contains only 5 files. Those 13 rendered as broken images: grok, droid, crush, qwen, copilot, goose, continue, devin, kimi, kiro, kilocode, vibe, pi. Five more had no icon at all: amp, agy, auggie, cline, autohand.

Fixing the paths surfaced two further problems in the icon set itself: the `copilot` icon was the wrong logo, and several marks are single-color in a way that makes them disappear against one of the two themes.

## One set of logos, not two

All 26 references (23 worker, 3 reviewer) now point at `frontend/src/renderer/assets/agents/`, the folder the board already renders from. An earlier revision of this PR added a second copy under `docs/assets/readme/logos/`; that copy is deleted, because two sets would drift apart the first time a brand mark changed.

## Icon fixes, applied in the renderer folder

The board folder had the same defects the README exposed, so the fixes land there and both surfaces pick them up:

- `copilot` was the GitHub Octocat, not Copilot. Replaced with the Copilot mark already shipped at `app-icons/copilot.svg`, which the landing hero uses.
- `codex` was a white rounded card, so on a light surface the card vanished and only the inner glyph showed. Replaced with the transparent gradient mark.
- `goose` was a pure black glyph and `kilocode` a dark opaque tile, both invisible in the app's dark theme. Replaced with the bare marks from the landing set.
- `cursor`, `opencode` and `cline` were pure white, invisible in the app's light theme and against a light README. Recolored to `#6e7681`, which reads on both grounds.
- `agy`, `auggie` and `autohand` had no asset at all. The board fell back to a lettered tile and the README showed no icon. Added, and wired into `AgentAvatar`.

`AgentAvatar` is updated for the three new marks and for the three files whose extension changed.

## Still carrying a background

`aider` (dark green), `crush` (light lavender), `droid` (black), `grok` (white) and `kiro` (purple) keep their opaque tiles: no background-free version of those marks exists in the landing app-icons, the renderer assets, or the docs site logos. `crush` and `kiro` are brand-colored tiles that read on either ground. `droid`, `grok` and `aider` each clash with one theme. Fixing them needs the official marks from upstream, which is out of scope here.

`devin`, `kimi` and `pi` are dark ink on transparent, so they are weak in the app's dark theme. Pre-existing and likewise unfixable from in-repo assets.

## Verification

- Every `src=` in README.md resolves to a file on disk. 13 did not before.
- Every `AgentAvatar` import path resolves, every file in the renderer folder is imported, and the three new `LOGOS` keys match existing backend adapters (`agy`, `auggie`, `autohand`).
- Rendered the full README locally through marked with GitHub's stylesheet in both themes: 26 logo images present, 0 unresolved image sources.
- Audited all 24 assets programmatically for opaque backgrounds and single-color fills, which is where the list above comes from.
- Not typechecked or built: the frontend dependencies are not installed in this worktree, so the `AgentAvatar` change is verified by resolving import paths rather than by compiling. Worth a CI check.
- Not compared against GitHub's own renderer; browser automation was unavailable in this environment.

## Judgment calls for the reviewer

- Recoloring `cursor`, `opencode` and `cline` to a neutral gray changes the board's appearance in dark mode, where they were previously white. It is the only way one file serves both themes, but it is a deviation from those brands' own monochrome marks.
- The README now references paths inside `frontend/src/renderer/`, which couples the docs to the app source tree. That is the trade for having a single set of icons.
