title: feat(topbar): add an Open in editor button beside Kill
body:
## Summary

Adds a split `Open` control to the session topbar, immediately left of Kill,
modelled on the VS Code opener in t3 chat. The main half opens the session's
worktree in the detected editor and focuses the file the agent changed most
recently, so a session that was fixing the download button lands on that file.
The chevron offers a folder-only open and a picker for the other installed
editors.

Detection covers VS Code and its forks (Cursor, Windsurf, Trae, Kiro, Positron,
VSCodium, Insiders), Zed, Sublime Text, and the JetBrains IDEs including Android
Studio and Fleet. Each resolves from PATH, the Homebrew and /usr/local prefixes,
the JetBrains Toolbox scripts directory, and on macOS the app bundle's CLI shim,
since the daemon is not launched from a login shell. The button hides itself when
no editor is found rather than offering an action that cannot succeed.

Xcode is deliberately excluded: its `xed` shim ships with the Command Line Tools
and fails unless `xcode-select` points at Xcode.app, and Xcode opens projects
rather than arbitrary folders.

### New API

- `GET /api/v1/editors`
- `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/open-editor`

Path resolution and the launch both happen in the daemon. Worktree paths are
deliberately absent from the session DTOs, so the renderer sends only a session
id and an optional workspace-relative path, and the response carries no absolute
path. A controller test asserts that.

Sessions with no live worktree (never spawned, or cleaned up) fall back to the
project checkout with no file focused.

### Icons

Each editor renders its own mark, tinted where the brand actually has a colour.
VS Code's blue is sampled from its own app icon; the rest are simple-icons'
published hexes. Cursor, Windsurf, Zed and the JetBrains marks are monochrome
brands, so they inherit the text colour and stay legible in both themes.

## Verification

Driven end to end in the running desktop app against real sessions, capturing the
launcher's argv to confirm what was actually opened: newest changed file on a
dirty worktree, folder alone for "Open folder only", the chosen editor rather than
the default from the picker, folder-only on a clean worktree, the project-checkout
fallback for a session whose worktree was deleted, and correct isolation across
projects. Rapid clicks produce a single launch. API abuse probes (path traversal,
absolute path, directory, missing file, unknown editor, unknown session, malformed
body, wrong method) all return the appropriate 4xx with a specific code.

Backend and frontend suites, typecheck, and golangci-lint are clean.

## Risks and follow-ups

- Bundle sub-paths are confirmed against a real install for VS Code, Cursor and
  Zed only; the other seventeen follow vendor documentation. A wrong sub-path
  degrades to "not detected", never to launching the wrong editor, and the PATH
  lookup still finds the editor whenever its shell command is installed.
- `editorResolveError` cannot distinguish "not supported by AO" from "not
  installed", so an unsupported id returns "That editor is not installed". Only
  reachable via the API, since the UI offers only detected editors.
- The empty-detection path (button hidden) is unit-tested but was not driven in
  the app, as it needs a machine with no editor installed.
- Editor choice is not persisted. A setting would be the natural follow-up.

## Screenshots

The control in the session topbar, immediately left of Kill:

![Open in editor button in the session topbar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-20/pr3284-assets/pr-topbar.png)

Closer in. The two halves read as one pill, with the joining edge squared and a
divider between the label and the chevron:

![Open control, zoomed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-20/pr3284-assets/pr-zoom.png)

The chevron menu: folder-only open, then every editor detected on the machine,
each with its own brand mark:

![Open in editor dropdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-20/pr3284-assets/pr-menu.png)

Full window for context:

![AO with the Open in editor button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/ao/ao-20/pr3284-assets/pr-full.png)

Rendered from this branch in a headless browser against the mock demo workspace,
so no real project or session data appears.

title: bug(browser): native WebContentsView overlays agent session when switching sessions
body:
## Bug

The native browser preview `WebContentsView` renders on top of the active agent session — even when the Browser inspector tab was never clicked. Reported by @neversettle17-101 (Aditi) on Discord with a screenshot showing a different session's content (demo/dashboard-screenshot) overlaid on the "reviewer flow update" session.

Related to #2491 (positioning) but distinct — this is a **visibility/lifecycle** problem, not a coordinate misalignment.

## Repro

1. Have a session with `ao preview <url>` active (e.g. a demo session loading a localhost dev server).
2. Navigate to a different session in the sidebar.
3. The previous session's native browser view paints over the new session's terminal/inspector area.

## Root cause (traced from code)

The native `WebContentsView` is a window-level overlay Chromium composites above the entire DOM. Two independent systems control its visibility — and they are not coordinated:

### 1. Renderer-side (`useBrowserView.ts`)
All lifecycle effects are `useEffect` (lines 229, 274, 483), which run **after the browser paints**. When `sessionId` changes:
- React commits the new session's DOM
- **Browser paints** — the old session's native view is still visible at its last bounds
- `useEffect` cleanup runs → `sendHiddenBounds(oldViewId)` → IPC to main process → view hidden

There is a one-paint-frame window where the old view overlays the new session. If the preview page is a dev server with HMR, repeated navigations can make this flash persistently visible.

### 2. Main-process-side (`browser-view-host.ts`)
`wireNavEvents` calls `entry.view.setVisible?.(true)` on every `did-navigate` event (line 571), and `navigate()` calls it after `loadURL` (line 304). This happens **without notifying the renderer**. If a hidden view's page navigates (HMR, SPA redirect, reload), the main process re-shows it. The renderer has no listener for this on sessions it's no longer managing — the `onNavState` callback bails early when `state.viewId !== viewIdRef.current`.

After `sendHiddenBounds`, the view's bounds are `OFFSCREEN_BOUNDS` (0×0 at −10000,−10000), so `setVisible(true)` alone should not paint. But the one-frame flash from the `useEffect` timing gap is the primary visible symptom.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Use `useLayoutEffect` for the view-hiding cleanup** in `useBrowserView` so the old view is hidden before the browser paints the new session. This eliminates the one-frame flash.

2. **Track a `rendererVisible` flag in the main process** per view entry. `did-navigate` should only call `setVisible(true)` if the renderer has previously indicated the view should be visible (via a `setBounds({ visible: true })` call). This prevents the main process from un-hiding a view the renderer intentionally hid.

3. **Forward `did-navigate` visibility changes to the renderer** so it can re-evaluate whether the view should be shown, even for sessions that are no longer the active route.

## Files

- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts` — lifecycle effects, `measureAndSend`, `sendHiddenBounds`
- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts` — `wireNavEvents` (`did-navigate` → `setVisible(true)`), `navigate`, `setBounds`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx` — `useBrowserView` instantiation, `active` flag computation

## Environment

Reported on macOS (Aditi's machine). Issue #2491 reported similar positioning problems on Debian Linux. Likely cross-platform given the architecture is platform-agnostic.

title: fix(landing): remove unshipped machine-readable API links
body:
## What changed

- removed dead MCP docs, docs `llms.txt`, comparison `llms.txt`, and Getting Started links
- kept `/agents.md`, but rewrote it for the shipped local desktop app, daemon, and `ao` CLI
- removed inherited hosted MCP, OAuth, A2A, API catalog, API `llms.txt`, and auth discovery routes that AO does not ship
- normalized remaining machine-readable links to live canonical routes

## Why

The landing replacement inherited hosted API metadata from its predecessor and rebranded it to `api.aoagents.dev`. AO has no hosted MCP/OAuth service, that hostname has no DNS record, and the repository architecture supports only the local daemon plus the explicitly enabled authenticated LAN listener. Publishing those files sent agents to dead URLs and misrepresented the product security boundary.

## Impact

AI clients now receive only live documentation and accurate local-product guidance. The static export no longer publishes six unsupported hosted-service discovery routes.

## Validation

- clean generated-state `npx tsc --noEmit`
- clean `npm run build` (84 static routes)
- generated machine-link check: 10 internal URLs checked, none missing or non-canonical
- verified removed discovery files are absent from `out/`
- source scan found no remaining `api.aoagents.dev`, dead docs paths, OAuth, or hosted-account claims
- `git diff --check`

Closes #3282

title: fix(landing): live section anchors, clean hash navigation, themed scrollbar
body: Fixes #3269 . ## What was broken **1. Dead footer anchors (P2).** `Footer.tsx` linked `/#features` and `/#agents`. `FeaturesSection` rendered no `id`, and no `#agents` target existed anywhere on the page — both clicks did nothing. **2. Stuck `#see-it` hash (P3).** Clicking "Demo" set the hash and scrolled, but the hash then stayed in the URL forever. Scroll away, click "Demo" again → nothing, because the browser treats the target as already current. **3. Scrollbar (P3).** The issue reported the scrollbar as unstyled. The actual cause is the opposite: `site-theme/tokens.css` was *explicitly hiding* it: ```css html, body { -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none; } html::-webkit-scrollbar, body::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; } ``` So the page had no scroll affordance at all. ## What changed **Anchors.** `id="features"` on `FeaturesSection`; `id="agents"` on `TrustedBySection` ("Use the agents you already trust" — the actual agents content on the page). **Hash navigation.** New `HashLink` component. Same-page `/#` clicks call `scrollIntoView()` directly and never write the hash, so the link behaves identically on every click. Modified clicks (ctrl/meta/shift/middle), cross-page navigation and unresolvable targets all fall through to normal `Link` behaviour, so it still degrades to a real navigation without JS. Used by Footer, DesktopNav and MobileNav — every `/#` link on the site now goes through one path. **Header offset, without hardcoding.** Anchors were landing under the fixed 56px header. Instead of per-section `scroll-mt-*` (which has to be remembered for every new section and silently rots when the header height changes), a single `--header-height` token now: - sizes the header itself (`h-(--header-height)`), - drives `scroll-padding-top` on ``, which offsets both `#hash` landings and `scrollIntoView()`, - feeds the mobile nav's `top` / `max-height`, which previously duplicated `3.5rem`. There is no pixel math anywhere in `HashLink` — `scrollIntoView()` is called with no arguments and the CSS supplies both the offset and the smoothness (with a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out). **Scrollbar.** The hide-hack is replaced with themed scrollbars declared through both standard properties (`scrollbar-width` / `scrollbar-color` — Firefox, Chrome 121+) and `::-webkit-scrollbar*` pseudo-elements (Chrome, Edge, Safari), plus `color-scheme: dark` so Safari/iOS overlay scrollbars and form controls render dark too. Colours come from new `--scrollbar-thumb` / `--scrollbar-thumb-hover` tokens alongside the rest of the theme. The `scrollbar-hide` utility used inside the demos still wins — it sits in the utilities layer and outranks the bare `*` / `::-webkit-*` base selectors. ## Not included Item 4 (placeholder testimonials) is named in the issue title but has no section in the body. It is real — `WallOfLoveSection/constants.ts` has three fabricated entries (`maria-garcia`, `luke-tanaka`, `rachel-kim`) with `url: "#"` and no avatar, rendered as `` so clicking them jumps to the top of the page. Deliberately left out of this PR; worth its own issue. Two other corrections to the issue's analysis, for the record: - `NAV_ITEMS` in `packages/shared/src/constants.ts` has zero importers — the nav is driven by `PRODUCT_LINKS` / `RESOURCE_LINKS` in `Header/constants.ts`, which never had a Features link. The broken anchor was footer-only. `NAV_ITEMS` is left as-is (dead, but both of its `/#` hrefs now resolve). - `packages/ui/src/globals.css` is a one-line stub, not the theme entry point. The scrollbar rules belong in `site-theme/tokens.css`. ## Verification 21/21 assertions pass under Playwright/Chromium against `next dev`, plus `tsc --noEmit` clean: - `#features`, `#agents`, `#see-it` each resolve to exactly one element. - Footer Features/Agents and nav Demo all land at `top=56px` — flush under the header. - Demo click #1 → `scrollY=4579`, URL stays `/` with no hash. Scroll to top, click #2 → `scrollY=4579` again. The reported bug does not reproduce. - Cross-page `/changelog` → `/#features` lands correctly, and re-clicking from home still scrolls even with the stale hash in the URL. - Mobile (390×844): nav closes, `body.style.overflow` is restored before the scroll runs, scroll succeeds, no hash. - Scrollbar measured in headed Chromium: document gutter `10px` (was fully hidden), `.scrollbar-hide` element gutter `0px`. Firefox and WebKit were not executed — those Playwright binaries aren't installed locally. Both engines are covered by the declared CSS, but worth a manual look before merge. --- cc @codebanditssss

title: macOS release hardening: e2e update test, verification gate, feed guard, single publisher, and dmg distribution
body:
## Summary

Two separate mac failures over 28-29 Jul burned two days, partly from misdiagnosis:

- A user could not install from the download page ("developer cannot be verified"). The artifact itself was fine. The false trail came from someone running `codesign --verify` on a copy extracted with plain `unzip`, which leaves stray `._*` files inside the bundle and breaks the seal. That produced a convincing but wrong "the signing pipeline corrupts the seal" conclusion, which paused all releases and nearly shipped an `xattr -cr` patch.
- Separately, a user hit the #3034 ShipIt failure doing an in-app update. Differential mac updates have never worked reliably. Mitigated by deleting all darwin `.blockmap` sidecars from the last 15 releases and by PR #3151, which makes full-download-only permanent going forward.

Two corrections to the record, since the wrong lesson is worse than no lesson:

- **Why the `xattr -cr` patch was wrong.** Not because it would have broken a working seal; it would not have. Extended attributes are not part of an Electron bundle's seal (signatures live in the Mach-O binaries and `_CodeSignature/CodeResources`, and the staple ticket is a regular file), and `xattr -cr` is Apple's own documented remedy for xattr detritus (QA1940). The actual reason it was the wrong patch: a client-side `xattr -cr` strips the quarantine flag, which bypasses Gatekeeper and masks whatever the real bug is. Not shipping it was correct, for that reason.
- **The `unzip` breakage is real but artifact-specific.** It holds for our zips because they embed AppleDouble entries per-directory (ditto without `--sequesterRsrc`). A `--sequesterRsrc` zip puts them in a sibling `__MACOSX` directory and can survive `unzip` extraction. So "unzip always breaks the seal" is true of our artifacts, not universally.

This is now a full macOS release-hardening plan, not just the dmg migration. Each workstream below is independently pickupable as its own PR. References: #3034, #3151, #3152. The dmg workstream's full decision record lives at #3267 and is folded in here as workstream 6.

All electron-updater claims below were checked against the published npm tarball of the pinned version (`electron-updater@6.8.9`), not against monorepo `master`, since line positions there drift. All `codesign`/`spctl` claims were checked empirically on macOS 27.0.

## Workstream priority order

0. End-to-end update test, highest priority in the whole plan.
1. Post-staple verification gate, highest priority after the update test.
2. Shared verify script, pairs directly with the gate above.
3. Feed-derived publish guard.
4. Single publisher, documented.
5. Explicitly out of scope (no work, listed for completeness).
6. macOS dmg distribution (detail at #3267).

## Workstream 0: end-to-end update test

**What changes.** An automated test that does what a real user does: install version N-1, point it at version N's real feed, confirm the update downloads, applies, and the relaunched app reports the new version and is actually alive. This is the single highest-value item in this entire plan. It would have caught both #3034 (July) and the 29 Jul incident before any user saw them.

**Feasibility, checked against the actual code.** `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`'s `startAutoUpdates(stateDir)` runs on every packaged-app launch and needs no UI interaction: it reads `~/.ao`'s update-settings file, and if `enabled: true`, calls `checkForUpdates()` with `autoDownload: true` and `autoInstallOnAppQuit: true`. `ensureUpdatePrefs` only prompts the first-run dialog when no settings file exists yet. So a harness can pre-seed that settings file before first launch and the check/download path runs non-interactively. No new IPC or UI automation is needed for the core flow.

The install-and-relaunch half is where the harness needs care. Three specifics, each verified against `MacUpdater.js` in the 6.8.9 tarball:

- **The sentinel must key off the NATIVE updater's event, not electron-updater's.** In `MacUpdater.updateDownloaded()` (tarball `out/MacUpdater.js`, inside the `server.listen` callback, lines ~209-227), `this.dispatchUpdateDownloaded(event)` fires FIRST, and only then does `if (this.autoInstallOnAppQuit) { this.nativeUpdater.checkForUpdates() }` kick Squirrel into fetching from the local proxy. So electron-updater's `update-downloaded` event fires before Squirrel has fetched or staged anything. A harness that quits on that signal stages nothing, installs nothing, and reports a false failure or flaps. The correct hook is the native `require('electron').autoUpdater`'s own `update-downloaded` event, which is exactly what MacUpdater itself listens to in order to set `squirrelDownloadedUpdate = true` (tarball lines ~22-25). Recommend the env-gated sentinel (`AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL=<path>`, no-op when unset) hang off that native event.
- **A plain quit installs but does NOT relaunch.** Relaunch only happens via `handleUpdateDownloaded()` calling `nativeUpdater.quitAndInstall()` (tarball lines ~231-238), and that is reachable only through electron-updater's own `quitAndInstall()` (lines ~240-254). On an ordinary app quit, ShipIt swaps the bundle and stops. Electron's own autoUpdater docs say the same thing: a downloaded update is applied on next start. So the harness must relaunch the app itself (`open -a`), and must wait out the ShipIt swap first, since there is no clean completion signal for it. Budget for a bounded poll on the bundle's `Info.plist` version rather than a fixed sleep.
- **Verifying the result.** Read `CFBundleShortVersionString` from the relaunched app's `Info.plist` (no app change needed) and confirm it matches N. Confirm the app is actually alive, not just that a process exists, by reusing the existing `running.json` plus loopback-HTTP daemon-liveness pattern already in `backend/internal/cli/e2e_test.go`, rather than inventing a new liveness check.

**Which repo.** Public (agent-orchestrator): a CI job plus the one small native-event sentinel addition to `auto-updater.ts`.

**Priority.** P0, highest in this plan.

**Rough size.** L. Not because the app needs heavy new automation surface (it mostly does not, per above), but because of the CI shape: a real macOS runner, a real signed N-1 build, a real signed N feed, and cross-process orchestration (launch, wait for native staging, quit, wait for swap, relaunch, verify).

**Cost and scope, stated honestly.** macOS CI runner minutes are materially more expensive than Linux, and this project ships nightlies frequently. The actual production failure was specifically a nightly-to-stable channel switch, so recommend making this a hard required gate on every promotion to the stable channel (exactly that transition), while treating nightly-to-next-nightly coverage as optional and lower-frequency pending real per-run cost data.

**How it gets verified.** The test is the verification mechanism. Report actual per-run runner-minute cost once implemented so the nightly-coverage question can be settled with numbers.

## Workstream 1: post-staple verification gate

**What changes.** Today the pipeline runs `codesign --verify` before notarize and re-zip, so the bytes that actually ship are never checked. Add a gate on the final artifact, after notarize, staple, and re-zip: extract with `ditto -x -k` (never `unzip`), then assert all three:

```
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$APP"     # seal intact
spctl -a -vv -t exec "$APP"                  # accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID
xcrun stapler validate "$APP"                # ticket actually stapled to the artifact
```

Publish blocks if any fails. Two notes on why these exact commands, both checked empirically on macOS 27.0 rather than assumed:

- `spctl -a -t exec` **needs `-vv`**. Without it, an accepted artifact prints nothing at all and merely exits 0, so a gate grepping its output for `Notarized Developer ID` would never match. An earlier draft of this plan had that bug.
- `spctl` alone does not prove stapling: it can satisfy a notarization check via Apple's online lookup, so it can pass on a notarized-but-unstapled artifact whenever the runner has network. `xcrun stapler validate` is the check that actually proves the ticket is attached to the bytes we ship, and it exits non-zero when it is not, which makes it the clean gate. (For the record: `codesign -dvvv` **does** emit a `Notarization Ticket=stapled` line on current macOS, and it does discriminate correctly. That contradicts commonly-cited 2019-era writeups. It is fine as a diagnostic, but `stapler validate` is the better gate because it validates rather than merely reports, and gates on exit code.)

This is precisely the check that would have caught the 28-29 Jul incident: the false positive came from checking an `unzip`-extracted copy, and from checking before the final packaging step rather than after.

**Which repo.** The private release/signing pipeline. Not touched here; routing as a requirement to that repo's orchestrator.

**Priority.** P1, highest after workstream 0.

**Rough size.** S/M: a handful of commands plus wiring into that pipeline's existing pass/fail gate.

**How it gets verified.** Dry-run against the last several real published releases before making it blocking, confirming it passes on known-good builds and fails loudly on a deliberately `unzip`-extracted copy, so it does not itself trigger a false-positive release pause on its first run.

## Workstream 2: shared verify script

**What changes.** Add `frontend/scripts/verify-mac-artifact.sh <path-to-zip>`, doing exactly the three checks in workstream 1 (`ditto -x -k` extract, then `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, `spctl -a -vv -t exec`, `xcrun stapler validate`), usable identically by CI and by a human debugging locally. This directly targets the root cause of the 28-29 Jul incident: a human ran the check by hand, the wrong way, and got a convincing wrong answer. One canonical script removes that failure mode by construction. `backend/internal/cli/start.go:282` already encodes the "ditto, not unzip" rule correctly, but only inside the Go binary; this makes the same rule reusable standalone.

**Which repo.** Public (agent-orchestrator).

**Priority.** P2. Pairs directly with workstream 1; that gate should shell out to this script rather than reimplementing the checks, so this lands in lockstep with or just ahead of it.

**Rough size.** S. A small dependency-free bash script, matching the dependency-free convention already used in `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs` and `nightly-version.mjs`.

**How it gets verified.** Fully mocking `codesign`/`spctl`/`xcrun` is not realistic without real Apple signing material, so state coverage honestly: a local smoke test asserting usage-error behavior (missing args, nonexistent file, non-zip input), runnable in any CI environment with no signing material, plus real-artifact exercise via workstream 1's gate, which is the meaningful verification of the core logic.

## Workstream 3: feed-derived publish guard

**What changes.** The publish guard currently hardcodes expected blockmap filenames, which can silently desync from `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`'s actual output since one is public and the other private; this already nearly broke publish when #3151 merged. Replace the hardcoded list with a guard that parses each generated feed yml (`latest.yml`, `latest-mac.yml`, `latest-linux.yml`, and nightly equivalents) and asserts: every asset referenced in `files[].url` exists among the release's uploaded assets, its `sha512` and `size` match what the yml claims, and sidecar presence matches actual policy.

**Correction to the sidecar policy model, and a real bug it exposes.** An earlier draft of this plan stated the policy as "win: required, linux: required, mac: none." The linux half is wrong, and it is wrong in a way worth fixing rather than encoding into a guard. Verified against the 6.8.9 tarball:

- The sidecar `.blockmap` path lives in `AppUpdater.differentialDownloadInstaller()`, and it is called from exactly two places: `NsisUpdater.js` and `MacUpdater.js`. Windows genuinely does fetch `<installer>.blockmap` sidecars.
- `AppImageUpdater` never fetches a sidecar. Its differential path uses `FileWithEmbeddedBlockMapDifferentialDownloader`, which reads the blockmap from the AppImage's own tail via `offset = fileSize - (packageInfo.blockMapSize + 4)` and therefore hard-requires `blockMapSize` in the yml. `feed.mjs` deliberately never writes `blockMapSize`.

Net effect: **linux differential updates are already dead** (no `blockMapSize` means the embedded path cannot run, so it errors and falls back to full download), and **every linux `.blockmap` sidecar `feed.mjs` generates is consumed by nothing.** So the guard should assert against what `feed.mjs` actually emits, but the rationale is "win sidecars are load-bearing, mac has none by policy (#3151), linux sidecars are currently dead weight," not "win and linux both require them."

Two follow-ups fall out of this, both small and both in the public repo:
- The comments at `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs:40` ("blockMapSize is never written (forces sidecar differential)") and `frontend/scripts/blockmap.mjs:14-15` carry the same drift: accurate for windows, false for linux. Worth correcting so the next person does not re-derive the wrong model.
- Consider dropping linux sidecar generation entirely, since nothing consumes it. Flagging rather than folding it in, since it is a behavior change and deserves its own decision.

**Which repo.** Guard: the private release/signing pipeline (handoff). Comment/dead-generation cleanup: public.

**Priority.** P3.

**Rough size.** M for the guard; XS for the comment corrections.

**How it gets verified.** Run it against several past real releases, including the exact release where #3151 merged, and confirm it would have caught that desync had it existed then.

## Workstream 4: single publisher, documented

**What changes.** Document, prominently, that exactly one designated release-conductor identity is authorized to run real publishes, with no ad hoc human-triggered publish outside it. Add this as an explicit rule in `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`, cross-referenced from `AGENTS.md`'s Distribution section. Between 22 and 24 Jul two different publishers emitted divergent mac zip formats on alternating days, which is a large part of why the incident evidence was unreadable: builds differed for reasons unrelated to the actual bug.

**Which repo.** Public (agent-orchestrator), docs only.

**Priority.** P4. Cheapest item here and it unblocks nothing else, but it directly prevents the evidence-pollution failure mode that made 28-29 Jul harder to diagnose than it needed to be.

**Rough size.** XS. Docs only.

**How it gets verified.** Review only; this is a process rule, not code. If the private pipeline can technically enforce "only this identity publishes," that is a natural extension of workstream 3, not required here.

## Workstream 5: explicitly out of scope

Staged rollouts, canary channels, and extra hashing beyond what exists. `digests.json` already proves transport integrity, and the existing draft-then-flip publish already prevents a broken build from becoming visible. Both worked correctly throughout the 28-29 Jul incidents and neither was implicated in either failure. No work proposed.

## Workstream 6: macOS dmg distribution

Full decision record at #3267: maker choice (bridge to `app-builder-lib` via `buildForge`, mirroring the existing NSIS pattern), confirmed from `MacUpdater` source that the zip must keep publishing forever for auto-update, explicit dmg sign/notarize/staple steps, blockmap treated as a settled full-download-only baseline, `ao start` unchanged, Homebrew cask update, link-surface changes, and a rollout/rollback plan publishing both zip and dmg throughout the transition.

The load-bearing claim there re-verified against the 6.8.9 tarball: `MacUpdater.doDownloadUpdate` calls `findFile(files, "zip", ["pkg", "dmg"])` and throws `ERR_UPDATER_ZIP_FILE_NOT_FOUND` when absent, so a dmg can never serve as the auto-update artifact and the zip must keep publishing permanently.

**Which repo.** Public (agent-orchestrator), plus a small handoff to the private pipeline (asset passthrough only, detailed in #3267).

**Priority.** Below the process-hardening workstreams above: the two real incidents this plan responds to were process and testing gaps, not distribution-format gaps. The dmg work is independently ready per #3267 and does not block or depend on workstreams 0-4.

**Rough size.** L: new maker file, `forge.config.ts` changes, download page/README/Homebrew link updates.

**How it gets verified.** Per #3267, plus the corrected command set from workstream 1 (`spctl -a -vv -t exec` and `xcrun stapler validate`) applied to the built dmg, and a staged rollout publishing both formats before flipping any first-install links.

Note on blockmap, since it comes up in both places: mac differential updates are a settled permanent baseline (disabled, full-download only, PR #3151), not an open question. A real incident (a nightly-to-stable channel switch) reproduced the #3034 corruption against a target zip that was already correctly ditto-built with its full AppleDouble set and a published blockmap sidecar, so the corruption is in the differential mechanism itself, not the zip format. Deleting the sidecars is a safe mitigation: a failed blockmap fetch is caught and logged as "Cannot download differentially, fallback to full download," so clients degrade to a full download rather than breaking. Full detail and the evidence bar for revisiting is in #3267's decision 4.

## Non-goals

- Not proposing to un-pause the release workflows.
- Not modifying the private release/signing pipeline directly; workstreams 1 and 3 are handoff requirements only.
- Not proposing the broader org-rename cleanup beyond the specific lines workstream 6 already touches (see #3267).
- Not re-enabling mac differential updates (see #3267 decision 4).

title: fix false-positive claude-code auth detection, document ao daemon
body:
Found while running v0.11.0 headless on a Linux server.

`claudeLocalAuthStatus` treats a non-empty `userID` in `~/.claude.json` as proof the CLI is authorized. That field sticks around after logout (and exists on machines that never finished login), so a logged-out box shows up as authorized:

```
$ claude auth status
{ "loggedIn": false, "authMethod": "none", "apiProvider": "firstParty" }
$ ao agent ls
claude-code  Claude Code  installed  authorized
```

You then spawn a worker and it dies on its first turn.

The `claude auth status` probe is already the right source of truth; the problem is only the config-file fallback. This change keeps `hasAvailableSubscription` and a populated `oauthAccount` as valid evidence, but a bare `userID` now returns Unknown instead of Authorized, so the probe decides. Added tests for the stale-userID cases plus a fake-binary harness for the probe path.

Second commit fixes docs/cli/README.md, which still says `ao start` starts the daemon. In 0.11 it fetches and opens the desktop app; the headless entrypoint is `ao daemon`, which wasn't documented anywhere. Table updated to match.

`go build ./...` and the claudecode package tests (incl. -race) are green. Full `go test ./...` has 5 pre-existing failures in internal/cli on my machine (daemon test harness 404s); they fail identically on a clean checkout so I left them alone.

title: feat(macos): release hardening (update e2e, verify script, dmg maker, single-publisher rule)
body:
Implements the public-repo workstreams of #3288 (macOS release hardening). Workstream 1 and the workstream 3 publish guard live in the private signing/release pipeline and are not touched here.

One PR by request, kept reviewable as one commit per workstream:

| Commit | Workstream |
| --- | --- |
| `feat(updater): add env-gated e2e sentinel and macOS update test harness` | 0 |
| `feat(scripts): add shared macOS artifact verification script` | 2 |
| `docs(scripts): correct blockmap sidecar model for linux and mac` | 3 (public part) |
| `docs(release): add the single-publisher rule and shared verify step` | 4 |
| `feat(macos): add dmg first-install maker with explicit sign, notarize, staple` | 6 |

## Workstream 0: end-to-end update test

- `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`: an `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL` sentinel that writes a marker file once an update is actually staged. It is a complete no-op when the env var is unset, which is always the case in a user-facing build.
- `frontend/scripts/e2e-mac-update.mjs`: the harness. Installs nothing itself; it takes an already-installed N-1 bundle, points it at the real feed, and proves N downloads, stages, installs on quit, and that the relaunched app reports N and is alive.
- `frontend/scripts/e2e-mac-update.test.mjs`: unit tests for the flag contract.
- `.github/workflows/mac-update-e2e.yml`: the macOS CI job.

Three things here are counter-intuitive and are per #3288's verified facts, so flagging them for review:

1. **The sentinel keys off the NATIVE `require("electron").autoUpdater` event, not electron-updater's.** In `MacUpdater.updateDownloaded()`, `dispatchUpdateDownloaded(event)` fires first and only then does `nativeUpdater.checkForUpdates()` kick Squirrel into fetching from the local proxy. Keying on electron-updater's `update-downloaded` means quitting before anything is staged, so nothing installs and the test flaps.
2. **A plain macOS quit installs but does NOT relaunch.** The harness quits the app to trigger the install, then relaunches it itself with `open -a`.
3. **The ShipIt swap has no completion signal**, so the wait is a bounded poll on the installed bundle's `Info.plist` `CFBundleShortVersionString`, never a fixed sleep. Liveness reuses the `running.json` plus loopback `/healthz` pattern from `backend/internal/cli/e2e_test.go`.

The workflow is `workflow_dispatch` plus `workflow_call` only, and is deliberately not wired into any release workflow. Those are paused, and #3288 asks for real per-run cost data before deciding whether nightly-to-nightly coverage is worth macOS runner minutes. The job prints its wall clock to the step summary so that question can be settled with numbers. The header comment shows the two-line snippet to wire it as a stable-promotion gate when that decision is made.

## Workstream 2: shared verify script

`frontend/scripts/verify-mac-artifact.sh <path-to-.zip-or-.app>`, plus a smoke test. Extracts with `ditto -x -k` (never `unzip`), then runs the three checks:

```
codesign --verify --deep --strict
spctl -a -vv -t exec
xcrun stapler validate
```

`-vv` on spctl is mandatory: without it an accepted artifact prints nothing at all and merely exits 0, so any grep for `Notarized Developer ID` can never match. `spctl` alone does not prove stapling either (it can satisfy the check through Apple's online lookup), which is why `stapler validate` is the gate. Exit codes follow the repo convention: 2 for usage errors, 1 for a failed check.

It accepts a `.app` directly as well as a `.zip`, so the update-e2e job can verify what ShipIt actually swapped onto disk with the same script. The private pipeline's post-staple gate (workstream 1) should shell out to this rather than reimplementing the checks.

The workflow 1 gate is the meaningful verification of the core logic; see the honest-coverage note below.

## Workstream 3, public part: blockmap comment drift

`feed.mjs` and `blockmap.mjs` both claimed that omitting `blockMapSize` "forces sidecar differential" on win and linux. True for win, false for linux: `AppImageUpdater` never fetches a sidecar. It uses `FileWithEmbeddedBlockMapDifferentialDownloader`, which reads the blockmap from the AppImage's own tail and hard-requires `blockMapSize`, which `feed.mjs` never writes. So linux differential updates are already off, and every linux `.blockmap` we publish is read by nobody. Both comments now state the real per-platform model.

Also corrected the mac rationale in `hashFile`, which still asserted the AppleDouble zip-format theory as the likely corruption source. #3267 decision 4 disproved that with a production repro against a correctly ditto-built zip carrying its full AppleDouble set. Leaving a known-false rationale in place is the exact failure mode this workstream exists to fix. This is comment-only; no behavior change.

**On dropping linux sidecar generation: kept, deliberately.** Two reasons, both documented in the code. The release publish guard lives in the separate private pipeline and currently asserts on the hardcoded linux sidecar filenames, so deleting the files here reds that guard out of band while another worker is actively rewriting it. And #3288 itself flags this as a behavior change deserving its own decision rather than something to fold in. The dead-weight status is now written down at the generation site so the eventual removal is a two-line change made together with the guard.

## Workstream 4: single publisher, documented

New "Hard rule: exactly one publisher" section at the top of `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md`, with the reason stated plainly: between 22 and 24 Jul two publishers emitted divergent macOS zip formats on alternating days, which made the 28-29 Jul incident evidence unreadable. It also separates approving a release (any approver) from triggering one (conductor only), and points people at the fork dev loop for test builds.

Cross-referenced from `AGENTS.md`'s Distribution section, along with two adjacent rules that kept getting re-derived wrong: use `verify-mac-artifact.sh` rather than hand-typed checks, and macOS ships both a zip and a dmg with the zip publishing forever.

While in `desktop-release.md`, corrected the release verification section: it still claimed every installer ships a `.blockmap` sidecar, which stopped being true for macOS at #3151.

## Workstream 6: macOS dmg distribution

`frontend/makers/maker-dmg.ts` bridges `app-builder-lib`'s `buildForge` with a `mac: ["dmg:<arch>"]` target, mirroring `maker-nsis.ts` closely. Per #3267 decision 1, Forge's own `maker-dmg` (electron-installer-dmg to appdmg) has no notarize or staple code and neither does app-builder-lib's dmg target, so no maker solves signing for us; given that, consistency with the existing bridge wins over adding a second packaging engine for one platform.

- **Strictly additive.** The darwin `maker-zip` entry is untouched, and now carries a comment saying it can never be removed: `MacUpdater.doDownloadUpdate` calls `findFile(files, "zip", ["pkg", "dmg"])` and throws `ERR_UPDATER_ZIP_FILE_NOT_FOUND` when absent. A dmg can never be the auto-update artifact.
- **The dmg container gets its own explicit seal.** A new `hooks.postMake` in `forge.config.ts` calls `sealDmg()`: `codesign --sign --timestamp`, then `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then `xcrun stapler staple`. It reuses exactly the credentials `packagerConfig` already consumes (`APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`/`CSC_LINK`, and either `AO_NOTARY_PROFILE` or the `APPLE_API_KEY` trio). No new secrets.
- **`mac.identity` is `null`** so electron-builder can never re-sign the already signed, notarized and stapled `.app` that `packagerConfig` produced before any maker ran.
- **`dmg.sign` is false**, per electron-builder's own warning that signing during dmg creation conflicts with notarization. The container is sealed afterwards instead.
- **No credentials means a warned no-op**, not a build failure, so unsigned local builds and the unsigned desktop-testing pipeline still produce a dmg. When credentials ARE present, any failure throws and fails the build: a silently unsigned dmg published as a release asset is the outcome this work exists to prevent.

**Download links intentionally NOT flipped in this PR.** `DOWNLOAD_URL_MAC_ARM64`/`_X64` and the two macOS README rows still point at the `.zip`. No published release carries a dmg yet, so flipping them at merge time would 404 for every macOS visitor until the next release, and the release workflows are paused. #3267 decision 8 step 6 makes this ordering explicit: flip only after a real release has published both formats and the dmg is verified. There is now a comment at the constants explaining the pending flip and naming the README rows, so the rollout step is discoverable from the code rather than only from the issue. Say the word if you would rather take the flip here and accept the gap.

The private-pipeline handoff for dmg asset passthrough is in #3267 and is owned elsewhere.

## Verified here

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`): clean.
- Full frontend vitest suite: 1216 passing, 0 failing. That includes the new `frontend/scripts/verify-mac-artifact.test.mjs` (9), `frontend/scripts/e2e-mac-update.test.mjs` (9) and `frontend/makers/maker-dmg.test.ts` (10).
- `verify-mac-artifact.sh` parses under `bash -n`, is committed executable, and every usage/precondition path exits 2 with the right message. Portability detail: it avoids `mapfile` because macOS ships bash 3.2.
- `.github/workflows/mac-update-e2e.yml` parses as YAML.
- The maker's `buildForge` call shape is asserted against a mocked `app-builder-lib`, and `sealDmg`'s exact command lines are asserted against a stubbed `execFile` for all five credential combinations, including the failure path.

## NOT verified here, and why

Being explicit rather than implying more coverage than exists.

- **Nothing was signed, notarized or stapled.** No Apple credentials in this environment. `sealDmg`'s command construction is unit-tested, but no real `codesign`, `notarytool` or `stapler` invocation was ever made. First real exercise is a signed build.
- **The three verification commands were never run against a real artifact.** Fully mocking `codesign`/`spctl`/`xcrun` needs real signing material, and a mock that always passes proves nothing about a gate. So the smoke test deliberately covers only the usage and precondition paths, which is the half a runner with no signing material can honestly assert. The meaningful verification is the private pipeline's post-staple gate (workstream 1) running this script against real published artifacts. #3288 recommends dry-running it against several past releases before making it blocking.
- **No dmg was actually produced.** `npm run make` does not complete in this worktree: it dies during electron-packager's "Finalizing package" step, before any maker runs. Confirmed environmental rather than caused by this change, since plain `npm run package` on otherwise unmodified code dies at the identical step. So `buildForge` accepting `mac: ["dmg:arm64"]` end to end, and `hdiutil` producing a mountable image, are both unverified and need a macOS build to confirm.
- **The postMake hook has never executed.** Same reason.
- **The update e2e job has never run.** It needs a real macOS runner, a real signed N-1 release with its `agent-orchestrator-darwin-arm64.zip` alias, and a live N feed. None of that exists here. The sentinel's event wiring is per source reading of the pinned `electron-updater@6.8.9` tarball, not observed at runtime. The first real run should be a `workflow_dispatch` against two existing published releases before anyone considers making it a gate.
- **Timeout defaults in the harness (20 min download, 5 min swap, 3 min launch) are estimates**, not measured. All three are flags, so the first real run can tune them.

## Out of scope, confirmed untouched

No changes to the private signing/release pipeline. No release workflow un-paused. No re-enabling of mac differential updates. No broader `AgentWrapper` to `Untrivial-ai` org rename.

Closes nothing on its own; #3288 stays open for workstreams 1 and 3's guard.

Refs #3288, #3267, #3151, #3034.

title: fix(notifications): clickable rows, unseen/unresolved sections, auto-resolution
body:
Closes #3210

## What

Three fixes to the notification dropdown.

**1. The whole row is a click target.** Previously only the title text was
clickable, despite the row showing a `hover:bg-interactive-hover` background
that implied otherwise. Clicking anywhere now navigates to the session, by
mouse or keyboard (`role="button"`, Enter/Space).

**2. The redundant terminal button is gone.** With the row navigating to the
session, the `SquareTerminal` button duplicated it. The PR title stays a real
`<a>` with `stopPropagation`, so a PR row still offers both destinations: link
opens the PR, row opens the session.

**3. Unread/All tabs replaced by Unseen/Unresolved, with no manual controls.**
Both mark-as-read affordances (per-item checkmark, header "Mark all read") are
removed.

## How

Notifications now carry two independent axes instead of one read flag:

| Column | Meaning | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | has the user **seen** it | cleared wholesale when the panel opens |
| `resolved_at` | is the underlying issue still **open** | lifecycle only — never a user action |

They are genuinely independent: a notification you already looked at stays in
Unresolved until the thing it reported goes away.

Auto-resolution triggers:

- session leaves the needs-input family, or terminates → `needs_input` resolves
- PR merges, closes, or stops being mergeable → `ready_to_merge` resolves
- daemon startup re-checks open rows against durable session/PR facts, because
  a transition observed while the daemon was down never reaches lifecycle

`pr_merged` / `pr_closed_unmerged` are excluded from Unresolved — they report
something that already happened, so they are worth seeing once and never worth
resolving.

Dedupe moves from `status = 'unread'` to `status = 'unread' OR resolved_at IS
NULL`. Keying on unread alone would let a seen-but-still-unresolved
notification be duplicated by the next observation of the same fact.

SSE gained a `notification_resolved` event so an open panel drops rows live;
the push dispatcher ignores it (nothing new to buzz a phone about).

## Notes

- Migration `0039_notification_resolution.sql` back-fills pre-existing read
  rows as resolved. They have no live resolution tracking behind them, so
  treating the acknowledgement as the resolution is better than resurrecting
  three-day-old rows into the new section.
- The panel renders a snapshot captured at open, because acknowledging empties
  the unread cache and a row must not vanish under the cursor.
- `PATCH /api/v1/notifications/{id}` is kept for the mobile client; only the
  renderer's use of it is removed.
- API additions: `status=unresolved` filter, `resolvedAt` field,
  `unresolvedCount`. `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` regenerated.

## Testing

- Renderer suite: 62 files / 852 tests pass
- Backend: every touched package passes (`notify`, `push`,
  `service/notification`, `lifecycle`, `storage/sqlite/store`,
  `httpd/controllers`)
- `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass
- `golangci-lint`: no issues in any changed file
- Manually verified in the desktop app against a seeded daemon

Some pre-existing failures on the Windows dev box are unrelated to this change
and touch no files here: 4 `supervisor-link` tests (`EACCES` on a Unix-domain
socket path) and 4 backend packages (`config`, `adapters/agent/fake`,
`adapters/runtime/tmux`, `daemon`) that assume POSIX paths or hit Windows file
locks.

title: fix(terminal): scope the tab strip to one session, restore one-click new terminal
body:
## Problem

https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3138 let a session's terminal strip pin tabs for *other* sessions, across projects. Two things came out of that:

- The strip stopped being about one session. Session 1's tab bar could show session 2's terminal, which makes it ambiguous which session you are typing into.
- The everyday action, "open a terminal", moved behind a dropdown whose first item was "Terminal", so one click became two.

## Change

The strip is one session's own again: its tab, then the shells it opened.

- The `+` opens a terminal on a single click. The session launcher, its search box, and the "Show all sessions" list are gone.
- The session's own tab is the first tab and has no close affordance. Ending a session stays the topbar's Kill.
- Removed the cross-session plumbing: the `tabOwner` search param on both session routes, `sessionTabsByOwner` and its localStorage persistence, and the add/close/select project-session props on `CenterPane`. Net 543 deletions against 149 insertions.
- Closing a shell now drops the tab optimistically instead of waiting on the round trip.

## On the close latency

The optimistic update is only half of it. The daemon's DELETE blocks for about 5 seconds before answering, which is a separate bug with its own root cause on the Go side; that fix is https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3328. This PR makes the tab disappear on click regardless of how long the daemon takes.

## Verification

Drove the renderer in a browser: `+` adds a terminal with no menu in the DOM, right click no longer produces a launcher, the session tab has no close button, and the tab disappears on click. A unit test pins the optimistic behavior properly by holding the DELETE unresolved and asserting the tab has already left the query cache, which the browser run could not prove on its own since the preview build has no daemon.

`npm test` (1184 tests, 92 files) and `npm run typecheck` both pass.

## Pre-existing failures, not addressed here

`frontend/e2e/shell-terminal-tabs.spec.ts` has two failures that #3138 introduced. Confirmed against a detached worktree at `6b6190deb`, so they predate this branch, and they fail at the same points with it applied:

- The board-route test expects a "New terminal" button on `/#/projects/:id`, and nothing renders one there anymore.
- The session-route test gets further with this branch (the button is found and opens a terminal again) but then fails at `getByTitle("Session terminal")`: the session tab only carries that title when its label is not truncated (`CenterPane.tsx`), and the demo label truncates.

Both are worth their own fix. The second overlaps the tab-bar visual pass, which is deliberately not in this PR.

title: fix(macos): address the seven review findings from #3294
body:
Follow-up to merged PR #3294, fixing the seven findings from the post-approval review on that PR. Tracking issue: #3288. Decision record for the dmg work: #3267.

One PR, five commits. Nothing here changes the release workflows, un-pauses anything, re-enables mac differential updates, or flips any download link from `.zip` to `.dmg`.

## P1-1. maker-dmg passed the wrong path to `buildForge`

**Bug.** `buildForge`'s `dir` becomes electron-builder's `prepackaged`, and on macOS that value IS the app path, not the package directory. `macPackager.packMacTargets` does `appPath = prepackaged ?? join(computeAppOutDir(...), "<productFilename>.app")` and hands `appPath` straight to the dmg target, which copies it into the image renamed to `<productFilename>.app` (`dmg.ts` `computeDmgOptions`' default `contents` entry). Passing Forge's package directory therefore copied the entire package directory in under that name, producing `Agent Orchestrator.app/Agent Orchestrator.app`: an outer bundle with no `Contents`, which cannot launch.

**Change.** Pass `path.join(dir, `${appName}.app`)`. Take the output directory from Forge's own `makeDir` instead of re-deriving it from a path that no longer points at the package dir (`buildForge`'s own default is `dirname(dir)/make`, which would now land inside the package directory).

**Why maker-nsis gets away with the bare `dir`.** Checked, not assumed. `winPackager` goes through the generic `platformPackager.pack`, whose `computeAppOutDir` returns `prepackaged` as the app OUT directory, and the NSIS target wants exactly that directory. Windows has no `.app` wrapper to descend into. The asymmetry is in electron-builder, not in these makers. maker-nsis is left alone.

**Verified.** Read against the installed `app-builder-lib@26.15.3` in `node_modules`, plus a layout-level maker test asserting the exact `dir` handed to `buildForge` and that it is not the package directory.

## P1-2. `sealDmg` failed open on partial credentials

**Bug.** A signing identity with no notary credentials logged a warning and returned success, so a signed but unnotarized dmg could reach publishing. Notary credentials with no signing identity returned even earlier and did nothing at all. Either way the build went green with an artifact Gatekeeper would reject.

**Change.** Exactly one incomplete state is tolerated: neither a signing identity nor notary credentials, which stays a warned no-op so unsigned local builds and the unsigned `desktop-testing.yml` pipeline keep producing a dmg. Every partial combination throws, in both directions, including a partial App Store Connect key trio. `sealDmg` now returns whether it actually sealed, which is what gates the new verification step below.

**Verified.** Unit tests for both directions, the partial trio, and the preserved zero-credential no-op.

## P1-3. postMake sealed the dmg but never verified it

**Bug.** `sealDmg` exiting 0 only says three commands ran on the build machine. It does not say Gatekeeper accepts the published bytes with a stapled ticket. A bad signature, assessment or ticket state could reach publishing unseen.

**Change.** `verify-mac-artifact.sh` now accepts a `.dmg` alongside `.zip` and `.app`, and `forge.config.ts`'s postMake runs it immediately after `sealDmg`, only when `sealDmg` reports it actually sealed (an unsigned local build has nothing to verify and must not fail a check it can never pass).

The dmg check is deliberately not the `.app` check. A dmg is not executable code, it is a container Gatekeeper assesses on open, so it uses `spctl -a -vv -t open --context context:primary-signature`, which is what #3267 decision 3 step 4 specifies. `-t exec` would assess the wrong thing. The existing `.zip`/`.app` path is untouched: still `-t exec`, still `ditto -x -k` extraction, never `unzip`. `-vv` stays mandatory on both, since without it an accepted artifact prints nothing and merely exits 0.

**Verified.** Ran the extended script against a real unsigned dmg built with `hdiutil` on macOS 27.0. All three checks dispatch on the dmg branch, `spctl` accepts the new flag combination and returns a real assessment (`rejected`, `source=no usable signature`), and the script exits 1. The smoke test stays runnable with zero signing material.

## P1-4. The N-1 baseline predates the sentinel

**Bug.** The harness waits on `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL`, but that listener only exists from #3294 onward. Every currently published release ignores the env var, so the first real run would wait out the full 20 minute download timeout and report a "never staged" failure that looks like a broken update.

**Choice.** Require a sentinel-capable baseline, with a fail-fast capability check. Observing staging externally would mean inferring Squirrel's internal staging state from the filesystem, which is exactly the kind of inference the sentinel exists to replace (see #3288's note on why the native event is the only trustworthy signal).

**Change.** `assertSentinelCapable` probes the packaged bundle for the env var name before anything slow runs and fails in seconds with a message naming the cause and telling you to pick a newer baseline. The probe is a substring scan of `app.asar`, because the name survives bundling as a plain string literal (`auto-updater.ts` reads it as `process.env[E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL_ENV]`). The workflow calls the same function in its own step, so there is one implementation and an unmistakable red step in the log.

**Verified.** Behavioral tests over synthetic bundles: capable, incapable, and not-a-packaged-bundle.

## P1-5. It cannot be a stable-promotion gate as written

**Bug.** The job needs version N and `latest-mac.yml` to already be public before it can start, so real stable clients can take the update before the check finishes. The header offered it as a stable-promotion gate anyway.

**Choice.** Document it honestly as post-release monitoring and remove the gate framing. The isolated-candidate-feed option is the better end state and the mechanism exists in principle (the `AO_RELEASE_REPO` build-time override, #3267 decision 8 step 3), but pointing this job at a candidate feed requires the private signing/release pipeline to build and publish there, and that repo is explicitly out of scope for this work. Claiming a gate we do not have is worse than not having one, because it invites someone to trust it as a pre-promotion barrier.

**Change.** The header now says post-release monitoring, states what a real gate would require, and says not to re-label it before that isolated feed exists. The "to wire it as a stable-promotion gate later" snippet is gone. No release workflow is wired up or un-paused.

## P2-6. `dmg-builder` emits a `.dmg.blockmap`

**Bug.** `DmgTarget.build` does `this.options.writeUpdateInfo === false ? null : createBlockmap(...)`, so the default is on. The blockmap is computed before postMake's `sealDmg` rewrites the dmg bytes, so Forge could publish a stale macOS sidecar against the permanent full-download-only policy (#3151, #3267 decision 4).

**Change.** `writeUpdateInfo: false` in the maker config, plus a filter on the returned artifact list. That list is the array Forge hands its publisher, so filtering there is what actually keeps a sidecar off a release, and it also covers a caller re-enabling the option through `cfg.dmg`.

Linux `.blockmap` generation is untouched, per the out-of-scope list.

**Verified.** Option name and default read from the installed `dmg-builder@26.15.3`, and `packager.js` confirmed that every emitted artifact file (the blockmap included) lands in `buildResult.artifactPaths`. Tests assert both the flag and that no dmg blockmap survives in the returned artifacts.

## P2-7. State-dir overrides never reached the app

**Bug.** `--state-dir` and `--run-file` were parsed and used by the harness but never handed to the app. The direct-spawn launch passed only the sentinel; the `open -a` relaunch passed nothing deterministic. The harness seeded and polled paths the app never used, so it could only time out.

**Change.** Both launches share one environment carrying `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL`, `AO_RUN_FILE` and `AO_DATA_DIR`. The relaunch spawns the swapped bundle's executable directly rather than going through `open`, re-reading the executable name from the swapped bundle so a rename between N-1 and N is picked up.

**Which relaunch mechanism, measured not assumed** (macOS 27.0, minimal probe bundle that writes its environment to a file):

| mechanism | sentinel | AO_RUN_FILE | AO_DATA_DIR |
|---|---|---|---|
| direct spawn | reached | reached | reached |
| `open -a` | not reached | only via the caller's ambient env | only via the caller's ambient env |
| `open --env VAR=value` | reached | reached | reached |

`open --env` works on macOS 27, but it is undocumented in `open`'s usage output on older releases, so relying on it would tie the harness to the runner image's macOS version. Direct spawn is the same mechanism the first launch already uses.

**Two path details that came out of tracing what the app actually does.** Update settings are seeded into `dirname(AO_RUN_FILE)`, because `main.ts`'s `initAutoUpdates` computes `stateDir = path.dirname(runFilePath())` and reads `update-settings.json` from there. Seeding `--state-dir` instead left the first-run dialog up whenever the two diverged, which would have blocked the whole flow. `AO_DATA_DIR` mirrors `backend/internal/config` `resolveDataDir`'s default of `<ao home>/data`.

**Run-file deletion constrained.** The run file is deleted before each launch, so `--run-file` must now be an absolute path ending in `.json` and `--state-dir` must be absolute. `rmSync` without `recursive` already refused directories, so this closes the remaining case: a typo can no longer aim that delete at something unrelated.

**Verified.** Behavioral tests over the launch environment, the derived settings and data directories, the path guards, and that `seedUpdateSettings` writes where the app will look.

## What was verified here, and what was not

Verified locally on macOS 27.0:

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` clean.
- Full frontend vitest suite: 1235 passing, 0 failing.
- The extended `verify-mac-artifact.sh` against a real unsigned `hdiutil`-built dmg (dispatch, flag acceptance, exit 1).
- The `open` vs direct-spawn environment behavior, with a purpose-built probe bundle.
- `app-builder-lib` / `dmg-builder` 26.15.3 behavior by reading the installed sources in `node_modules`, not from memory.

**Not verified here, and a reviewer should treat these as unproven:**

- **No dmg was built.** `npm run make` does not complete in this environment: it dies during electron-packager's "Finalizing package" step, and `npm run package` alone dies at the identical step on unmodified code, so this is environmental and not caused by these changes. P1-1's corrected layout and P2-6's absent blockmap are therefore covered by source reading plus unit tests against a mocked `buildForge`, not by inspecting a real image. The first real macOS build should confirm that the dmg contains one launchable `Agent Orchestrator.app` and that no `.dmg.blockmap` appears among the artifacts.
- **No signed or notarized artifact was checked.** Everything requiring Apple signing material (the accepted-artifact side of `spctl`, `notarytool`, `stapler staple`) is unexercised. The dmg `spctl` invocation was proven to parse and assess, not proven to return `accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID` on a good artifact.
- **The e2e workflow has never run.** It needs a macOS runner, a real signed baseline, and a live target feed. The new capability check and the environment propagation are covered by unit tests only.
- **P1-5 is a documentation fix, not a mechanism fix.** The job still cannot gate a stable promotion. Making it one needs an isolated candidate feed owned by the private release pipeline.

## Commits

1. `fix(makers)`: P1-1, P1-2, P2-6 (all in `maker-dmg.ts`)
2. `feat(scripts)`: P1-3
3. `fix(scripts)`: P2-7 and the harness half of P1-4
4. `docs(ci)`: P1-5 and the CI half of P1-4
5. `refactor(makers)`: drops a single-use local left over from commit 1

Closes nothing. Refs #3288, #3267, #3294.

title: test(config): use portable override paths
body:
## What

  Make TestLoadOverrides use platform-native temporary paths instead of hard-coded /tmp/... paths.

  ## Why

  The test failed on Windows because filepath.Abs correctly normalizes /tmp/... to the current drive, such as D:\tmp\..., while the test expected the original
  POSIX path string.

  This is a test portability issue only. Production path normalization remains unchanged.

  - Create an absolute temporary directory with t.TempDir().
  - Build the run-file and data-directory paths with filepath.Join.
  - Compare the loaded configuration against those generated paths.
  - Leave config.go and runtime behavior unchanged.

  ## Testing

  Validated on Windows:

  cd backend
  go test ./internal/config -count=1
  go vet ./internal/config

  Both commands pass.
