title: Terminal theme desyncs on toggle — xterm colors lag behind app shell
body:
## Bug

When toggling the app theme (dark ↔ light), the embedded xterm terminal does not update its colors to match. The terminal retains the **previous** theme while the rest of the app shell switches correctly — resulting in a jarring mismatch (e.g. light terminal background on a dark app, or vice versa).

Reported by **@Pyasma** in Discord (#🧑‍🔧-bug-triage), with screenshot showing a light terminal (`#f5f5f4`) inside a dark app shell.

## Reproduction

1. Open AO desktop app in dark mode
2. Create/open a session with a terminal
3. Toggle theme to light (Ctrl+K → Toggle theme, or Command Palette)
4. **Observed:** app chrome switches to light, but the terminal background/foreground stay dark
5. Toggle back to dark → terminal now shows light colors (one toggle behind)

## Root cause

Two compounding issues in `frontend/src/renderer/`:

### 1. React effect ordering race (`_shell.tsx` vs `XtermTerminal.tsx`)

When `resolvedTheme` changes in the Zustand store, two `useEffect` hooks fire on the same commit:

- **`_shell.tsx:380`** — `applyDocumentTheme(resolvedTheme)` sets `data-theme` on `:root` (the attribute the CSS variables key off)
- **`XtermTerminal.tsx:274`** — calls `buildTerminalThemes()` which reads those same CSS variables via `getComputedStyle`

React fires effects **bottom-up (children before parents)**. `XtermTerminal` is a descendant of `_shell`, so its effect runs **before** `_shell` updates `data-theme` on the DOM. When `buildTerminalThemes()` reads the CSS vars, they still hold the **old** theme values.

### 2. `buildTerminalThemes()` returns identical dark & light objects

```ts
// terminal-themes.ts
export function buildTerminalThemes() {
  const dark: ITheme = {
    background: cssVar("--color-bg-terminal"),  // reads current :root
    foreground: cssVar("--color-text-terminal"),
    ...
  };
  const light: ITheme = {
    background: cssVar("--color-bg-terminal"),  // ← SAME var, SAME moment
    foreground: cssVar("--color-text-terminal"),
    ...
  };
  return { dark, light };
}
```

Both `dark` and `light` read the **same CSS variables from the same DOM state** at call-time. The variables are scoped by `data-theme` in `tokens.css`, so both objects get whatever theme is currently on `:root`. The `dark !== light` selection in `XtermTerminal.tsx:278` (`props.theme === "dark" ? dark : light`) is therefore a **no-op** — both branches return identical palettes.

### Combined effect

The terminal always reflects the theme that was on the DOM **before** the current toggle, and never catches up.

## Suggested fixes (any one)

1. **Apply `data-theme` synchronously** in the Zustand `setThemePreference` action (or in a `useLayoutEffect`) instead of a `useEffect` in `_shell.tsx`, so the DOM is updated before child effects read CSS variables.
2. **Make `buildTerminalThemes()` theme-aware** — accept a `theme` param, read CSS vars from the correct scoped selector rather than from live `:root`.
3. **Defer the terminal theme read** with `requestAnimationFrame` after `resolvedTheme` changes, ensuring the DOM has settled.
4. **Hardcode both palettes** in `terminal-themes.ts` instead of reading from CSS variables at runtime.

## Files involved

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/terminal-themes.ts` — `buildTerminalThemes()` reads same CSS vars for both themes
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:274-279` — theme update effect
- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx:380-382` — `applyDocumentTheme` in a `useEffect`
- `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` — `--color-bg-terminal` / `--color-text-terminal` scoped by `data-theme`

title: feat(mobile): light/dark theming, native sheets, and the rebuilt app shell
body:
Rebuilds the mobile app around a real theme system and native sheets, and reworks every screen on top of it.

The app was dark-only, its modals were hand-rolled on top of RN's `Modal`, a fresh install could not connect at all (wrong default port), and there was no way to un-pair a phone. This addresses those together because they are welded by the theme: removing the exported `theme` const is what forces every screen to migrate, so the palette and the screens cannot land separately.

## What's in

- **Light/dark theming** with a persisted `light`/`dark`/`system` preference. Light is derived from the desktop's `tokens.css`, with surfaces following the iOS grouped-list convention and semantic colours darkened rather than reused — both documented on the palette.
- **Native `formSheet` routes** for project, agent, theme and manual-connect, so drag-to-dismiss and the grabber come from the OS.
- **Rebuilt board, orchestrator, PR and settings tabs**, plus a session composer with the eight control keys a phone keyboard lacks.
- **First-run onboarding** and a rebuilt pairing flow.
- **Notification history**, backed by the daemon's durable record rather than only what push delivered live.
- **Disconnect & forget server** — previously impossible; clearing the host by hand left the device registered and still receiving pushes.
- **Per-harness brand marks**, ported from the desktop's agent assets.

## Fixes that fall out

- **Default port 3011, not 3001.** 3001 is the desktop/CLI daemon, which binds loopback only and can never be reached from a phone.
- **Auth lockout during re-pair.** The daemon locks a device out for a minute after 5 failed auths. A stale password cost 4 failures per poll tick, arming the lockout in a tick or two — so scanning a fresh pairing code failed with 429 before the new password was ever checked. `/sessions` is now probed first and alone, capping a bad-credential tick at one failure.
- **QR scanner picked the wrong lens on iOS.** `expo-camera` matches `selectedLens` against `AVCaptureDevice.localizedName`, not a `DeviceType` identifier, so `"builtInWideAngleCamera"` matched nothing and left the default — on a Pro that is the ultra-wide, which cannot focus close enough to read a QR code off a laptop screen.
- **Session titles disagreed with desktop.** `sessionTitle` now falls back to `issueId`, where the daemon stores the task name.
- **The input dock jumped twice when the keyboard appeared** — the root view and the dock were both compensating.
- **Android sheets sat behind the keyboard.** `react-native-screens` only expands a sheet for the IME when it has more than one detent, so the one-detent `fitToContents` form could not get out of the way.

## Structure

Pure decision logic is split from React Native / Expo side effects throughout (`prView.ts` ↔ `PRCard.tsx`, `onboarding.ts` ↔ `onboardingStore.ts`), following the existing `pushStatus.ts` / `push.ts` split, so the rules are unit-tested without a renderer. That is where most of the new test coverage lives.

The 16 commits are ordered and self-contained; reviewing them in sequence is much easier than the squashed diff.

## Deliberately not included

- **Voice dictation** — follows in a separate PR stacked on this one, to keep the speech dependency and its permissions reviewable on their own.
- **The app icon** — that is #3304.

## Note on #3304

Both PRs touch `app.json`. #3304 owns `ios.icon` and `adaptiveIcon.monochromeImage`; this PR owns `userInterfaceStyle`, `infoPlist`, `softwareKeyboardLayoutMode` and the notification colour. The blocks are adjacent, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase there. No other overlap.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — 18 files, 237 tests passing

title: feat(mobile): push-to-talk voice dictation
body:
> **Depends on #3399 — draft until that merges.**
>
> This branch is built on `feat/mobile-theming-and-shell`, but a PR base must live in the upstream repo, so this targets `main` and currently shows #3399's commits too. **Only the last two commits are new here.** The moment #3399 merges, this diff collapses to just those two on its own and I will mark it ready.
>
> Just the voice work: https://github.com/Prasad-D-Ware/agent-orchestrator/compare/feat/mobile-theming-and-shell...feat/mobile-voice-dictation

Adds push-to-talk dictation to the session composer: hold the mic to speak, release to insert, or swipe up to latch it hands-free.

Typing prompts on a phone keyboard is the slowest part of driving a session from one, and it is the reason a phone session tends to become read-only in practice.

## The mic is the phone's, never the harness's

The obvious-looking implementation is to drive the harness's own voice mode — Claude Code exposes `/voice`, and the key row already sends arbitrary bytes to the PTY, so it is trivially deliverable.

It does not work, and the reason generalises. The harness records through the **daemon host's** microphone: the machine running the agent, which is not the machine the user is holding. It would also only ever work for the harnesses that ship a voice mode at all.

Capturing on the phone inverts both. The transcript is just text, so it leaves through the same `sendPrompt` path as anything typed, and every harness gets dictation for free.

## Choices worth flagging in review

- **On-device recognition** (iOS `SFSpeechRecognizer`, Android `SpeechRecognizer`) rather than cloud: free, private, no API key, no per-minute cost. Dictation is the kind of feature people leave on, and a metered recogniser would be quietly expensive. The provider interface is shaped so a cloud backend is an additive file, not a rewrite.
- **The transcript lands as an editable draft, not a send.** This text reaches an agent with tool access, and speech-to-text mishears code vocabulary often enough that silent submission is not acceptable. Phrases append, so several held bursts build one prompt.
- **The recogniser is biased toward agent vocabulary** — otherwise "git" comes back "get" and "npm" comes back "MPM". `contextualStrings` on iOS, `EXTRA_BIASING_STRINGS` on Android.
- **The live partial sits above the dock, not in the field.** It changes on every syllable, and rewriting text under the user's caret is hostile.
- **Warm-up says "Keep holding...", not "Listening".** The mic is not capturing yet, and the latter invites speech that gets dropped.

## Permissions

`expo-camera`'s `microphonePermission: false` is dropped, since the app now genuinely wants the microphone. The usage descriptions live on the `expo-speech-recognition` plugin, covering both microphone and speech recognition.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — 19 files, 268 tests passing (31 new, covering the provider's permission, lifecycle and mode handling)

title: feat(telemetry): add kill switch, daemon version stamping, and update telemetry
body:
## Summary

Follow-on to #3314 and #3388, which fixed the PostHog spend problem. Reconciling the bill against the code surfaced three gaps that those PRs did not cover.

**Kill switch.** Every existing telemetry control is compiled into the build, so silencing a noisy stream meant shipping a release and waiting for users to install it. That is why the `ao hooks` firehose ran for weeks. `AO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED_EVENTS` names streams that must not reach PostHog:

```bash
AO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED_EVENTS="ao.v2.app.active, ao.renderer.*"
```

Entries ending in `*` match by prefix, matching is case-insensitive, and either the internal name (`ao.app.active`) or the exported alias (`ao.v2.app.active`) works, so the name visible in PostHog needs no translation. It sits outermost on the remote chain, so a silenced stream consumes no aggregation window, no rate-limit slot, and no export. Local SQLite is deliberately unaffected, so a stream silenced in production stays debuggable locally. Unrecognized entries are inert rather than fatal, because the switch has to be usable during an incident.

**Daemon version stamping.** Every daemon event shipped with no version at all. All 18,661 `ao.session.spawned` / `spawn_failed` events in the current billing period have an empty `ao_version`, so the observed 23.5% session-spawn failure rate cannot be attributed to any release. The daemon binary has no version that release tooling overrides (`cli.Version` is still `"dev"`), so the supervisor passes `AO_TELEMETRY_APP_VERSION` from `app.getVersion()` and the sink stamps `app_version`/`ao_version`. An unset value leaves the properties off rather than reporting a misleading `"unknown"`.

**Update telemetry.** The app auto-downloads updates and installs them on quit, but 1,148 installs sit on 0.10.3 against roughly 70 on 0.11.x, and there is no signal about why. A stuck install looks identical whether the check failed, the download failed, or the user simply never quits the app. Adds `ao.renderer.update_failed`, `ao.renderer.update_downloaded`, and `ao.renderer.update_unsupported`, carrying a coarse `error_category`, the `phase` that failed (`check` or `download`), and the target version.

The updater's raw message is bucketed into a category rather than sent, because it can contain feed URLs and local staging paths. `downloading` is deliberately not reported: it fires per percent tick, the UI already shows it, and repeating streams are what caused the original volume problem. Emitted from the existing `useUpdateStatus` status channel, so it inherits the renderer's per-name rate limits and sanitization.

Also in scope, both small and previously identified: the renderer now sets `advanced_disable_flags` and `disable_surveys` (it reads no flags and ships no surveys, so those polls were requests for data nothing consumes), and unpackaged builds default `AO_TELEMETRY_REMOTE=off` so dev loops no longer export to the production project.

## Validation

Ran the daemon against a local capture endpoint rather than relying on tests alone.

Version stamping, with `AO_TELEMETRY_APP_VERSION=0.11.2`:

```
{"event": "ao.daemon.started",  "app_version": "0.11.2", "ao_version": "0.11.2"}
{"event": "ao.v2.cli.invoked",  "app_version": "0.11.2", "ao_version": "0.11.2"}
{"event": "ao.v2.app.active",   "app_version": "0.11.2", "ao_version": "0.11.2"}
```

Kill switch, with `AO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED_EVENTS="ao.v2.app.active, ao.daemon.*"`. Only the undenied stream is exported:

```
{"event": "ao.v2.cli.invoked", "app_version": "0.11.2", "ao_version": "0.11.2"}
```

And local storage still holds all three, confirming the switch is remote-only:

```
telemetry_event: [('ao.app.active', 1), ('ao.cli.invoked', 1), ('ao.daemon.started', 1)]
```

Also run:

- `go test ./internal/adapters/telemetry ./internal/config ./internal/daemon ./internal/httpd ./internal/telemetrymeta`
- `go vet` and `gofmt` on the touched packages
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/telemetry.test.ts src/renderer/lib/update-telemetry.test.ts` (38 tests)
- `npm run typecheck`

Note: `go test ./internal/cli` fails 6 tests (`TestBrowserRequiresSessionAndValidWait` and 5 spawn tests) on this branch. They fail identically on `origin/main` with and without `AO_*` environment variables set, so they are pre-existing and unrelated.

## Risks and follow-ups

- The kill switch is env-driven, so it reaches an installed build only through the supervisor. Genuinely remote control needs a hosted config endpoint the daemon polls; that is the natural next step and is not attempted here.
- Version stamping only covers daemon events launched by the supervisor. A directly launched `ao daemon` still exports without a version, which is correct, since there is no app version to report.
- Not included: the 52% orchestrator spawn failure rate is a product defect present on every version including the latest, and needs its own investigation rather than more telemetry.

title: fix(cursor): stop activity state sticking on "Input Needed" all turn
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3306.

Cursor's `beforeShellExecution`/`beforeMCPExecution` hooks were dispatched to AO as `permission-request`, which the shared `activitystate.StandardDeriveActivityState` maps to `waiting_input` (a sticky state). No `afterShellExecution`/`afterMCPExecution` hook was installed to demote it back, and no fallback terminal-activity detection exists for cursor (unlike codex). So once the first tool call flipped the badge to "Input Needed", nothing cleared it until the turn's `stop` hook — even while the agent was visibly editing files and running commands for the rest of the turn.

The `permission-request` mapping was also the wrong model to begin with: AO always launches `cursor-agent` with `--trust` (`cursor.go`'s `GetLaunchCommand`/`GetRestoreCommand`), so these hooks never represent a real blocking permission decision — they fire on every auto-approved tool call. They're functionally equivalent to claude-code's `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` trio, not to a permission dialog.

## Change

Rather than reusing `permission-request` and bolting on the same `toolFlight`/`blockedCandidate` correlation machinery `manager.go` uses to safely clear claude-code's sticky `blocked` state, this follows the simpler half of the existing pattern:

- **`cursor/hooks.go`**: `beforeShellExecution`/`beforeMCPExecution` now dispatch as `pre-tool-use` (was `permission-request`). Their previously-unregistered `afterShellExecution`/`afterMCPExecution` counterparts are now installed too, dispatching as `post-tool-use` — the same sub-command names claude-code uses for its own tool-use trio.
- **`cursor/activity.go`** (new): cursor gets its own `DeriveActivityState`, replacing the shared `activitystate.StandardDeriveActivityState`. `pre-tool-use`/`post-tool-use` both map to `active` (matching how claude-code's trio maps to `active`, not `waiting_input`/`blocked`). `session-start`/`user-prompt-submit` → `active`, `stop` → `idle`.
- **`activitydispatch/dispatch.go`**: registers `cursor.DeriveActivityState` for the `"cursor"` token.

Because cursor's tool-use signals now always resolve to `active`, the session never enters a sticky state in the first place — so the existing precedence guard in `manager.go` (`isToolUseEvent`, `applyToolPrecedenceLocked`) doesn't need to change, and no per-tool correlation tracking is needed for cursor.

**Trade-off**: cursor sessions can no longer show "Input Needed" at all, since Cursor exposes no separate hook that fires only for a genuine blocking dialog (unlike claude-code's distinct `PermissionRequest` event). Given `--trust` means that indicator was never trustworthy to begin with (same "many-to-one collapse" already flagged in `copilot/hooks.go`), this seemed like the honest trade rather than leaving a misleading sticky state in place.

The forum-sourced caveat in #3306 (that `beforeMCPExecution`/`afterMCPExecution` may not fire for the `cursor-agent` CLI) is left as an open follow-up — registering them is harmless dead weight if unconfirmed, consistent with the issue's own suggested fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` passes (all packages, including `cursor`, `activitydispatch`, `lifecycle`)
- [ ] Manual repro from #3306: start a Cursor session, hit "Input Needed", send a follow-up, confirm the badge reflects "active" through subsequent tool calls instead of sticking

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Ship a .rpm package for Fedora/RHEL
body: We ship a .deb and an AppImage for Linux, but no .rpm, so Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE users have no native package. Add an rpm target to the Linux build (electron-builder supports an `rpm` target alongside deb/AppImage), publish it as a release asset like the .deb, and wire it through the build-artifacts workflow and the release conductor.

title: ci(build-artifacts): ship the Linux .rpm as a release artifact (#3405)
body:
Closes #3405.

## What

The rpm target was already configured (`frontend/forge.config.ts` has `@electron-forge/maker-rpm`) and it already builds on the ubuntu leg of `build-artifacts.yml`: the run log for the current workflow shows `Making a rpm distributable for linux/x64` succeeding, because `ubuntu-latest` ships `rpmbuild`. The output was simply never collected, so the release conductor had no `.rpm` to verify or attach and Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE users got no native package.

This wires it through, mirroring exactly what the `.deb` got in #2986:

- `Collect Linux .rpm and compute digest`: copies `out/make/rpm/x64/*.rpm` to `dist-rpm/agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.rpm` and folds its sha256 into the existing `linux-x64.digest.json` fragment, so the `digests` job still reads one fragment per platform.
- `Upload Linux .rpm artifact`: uploads it as the pinned `linux-rpm` artifact name (own directory, so the `linux` artifact's `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.*` glob cannot swallow it).
- README: adds the `.rpm` row to the download table, and the `.deb` row alongside it (the deb has been a published release asset since #2986 and was never documented).

Artifact name `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.rpm` follows the existing stable-alias convention (`agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`, `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.deb`), which is what `releases/latest/download/...` links and the conductor's staging step expect.

No `forge.config.ts` change is needed and no signing is involved.

## Conductor follow-up

The private release conductor needs two lines in `_pipeline.yml`'s `Verify and stage build artifacts` step: `mv artifacts/linux-rpm/agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.rpm dist/` and adding the filename to the digest verification loop. Publishing is already automatic (`gh release upload "$TAG" ... dist/*`), and the feed manifests are untouched: the `.rpm` is not an updater target, exactly like the `.deb`. That change is tracked separately in the conductor repo.

## Verification

- Dispatched this workflow on the fork branch; the linux leg produces and uploads `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.rpm` with its digest in `digests.json`.
- Workflow YAML parses; frontend typecheck + unit tests and backend `go build`/`go test` pass.
- Note: the rpm cannot be built on a macOS dev machine (`maker-rpm` needs `rpmbuild`), which is why the check is a CI dispatch.

title: [Bug]: Windows: claude-code trust pre-seed writes backslash path keys in .claude.json, but Claude Code only reads forward-slash keys — trust dialog blocks every session (no_signal)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, AO pre-seeds Claude Code workspace trust by writing `projects["<worktree>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true` into `%USERPROFILE%\.claude.json` — but it writes the path key with **backslashes** (`"D:\\...\\worktrees\\<project>\\<session>"`). Claude Code keys the same map with **forward slashes** (`"D:/.../worktrees/<project>/<session>"`) and its trust lookup only ever matches forward-slash keys. The keys never match, so the pre-seeded flag is never read. Claude Code then renders the interactive workspace-trust dialog inside AO's ConPTY and waits for a keypress forever.

Consequence chain: agent never starts → no hook (`ao hooks claude-code <event>`) ever fires → `sessions.first_signal_at` stays NULL → AO reports `no_signal` for every claude-code session.

This looks like the Windows follow-up to #2119: the pre-seeding approach adopted there is defeated on Windows by the path-separator mismatch.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows, AO 0.11.2, `claude` resolving to the native `claude.exe` on the daemon's PATH.
2. ```powershell
   ao project add --path <repo> --id demo --name Demo --worker-agent claude-code
   ao spawn --project demo --harness claude-code --name demo --prompt "Create src/demo.txt containing exactly DEMO OK."
   ao session ls --json    # idle → no_signal after ~90 s, no file created
   ```
3. Inspect `%USERPROFILE%\.claude.json`: AO's entry for the worktree uses backslashes; every entry written by Claude Code itself uses forward slashes.

To see *why* it hangs, run AO's exact agent argv under a PTY (e.g. `winpty` from Git for Windows) and read the screen:

```text
 Accessing workspace:
 D:\...\worktrees\<project>\<session>
 Quick safety check: Is this a project you created or one you trust? ...
 > 1. Yes, I trust this folder
   2. No, exit
 Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel
```

## Expected behavior

The trust key AO writes is the one Claude Code actually reads; worker sessions start unattended on Windows.

## Actual behavior

AO writes:

```json
"projects": {
  "D:\\...\\worktrees\\<project>\\<session>": { "hasTrustDialogAccepted": true }
}
```

Claude Code reads/writes its own entries in the same file as:

```json
"D:/.../repo": { "hasTrustDialogAccepted": false }
```

Keys never match → blocked interactive prompt → `no_signal`.

**Proof by inversion:** adding the *same* trust entry keyed with forward slashes, changing nothing else, removes the dialog; the session reaches activity (`POST /api/v1/sessions/<id>/activity status=200`), creates the requested file, and kills cleanly.

## AO version

0.11.2 (desktop app; bundled daemon `resources\daemon\ao.exe`)

## Environment

Windows 10 Pro (10.0.19045) x64; ConPTY runtime; native `claude.exe` (not the npm `.cmd` shim)

## Logs / extra context

- Claude Code's trust check **walks up the directory tree** (any ancestor with `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true` passes). Operational workaround until fixed: trust `%USERPROFILE%\.ao\data\worktrees` once, interactively — it covers every future worktree AO creates beneath it, with no per-session prediction. Per-session pre-seeding with forward-slash keys, and answering the dialog via `ao send --session <id> --message "1"`, both also work but are per-session only (Claude Code does not persist the dialog answer for AO-created worktrees, and each session gets a fresh path).
- Suggested fix: write the `projects` key in the format Claude Code reads on Windows (forward slashes).
- Side note: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` appears to be unknown to AO (no occurrences in the binary) — trust is always written to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude.json` regardless of that variable.
- Downstream effect: the blocked process holds the worktree directory as its cwd, so `ao session kill` fails post-kill cleanup with INTERNAL_ERROR (filing separately).
- Duplicate search: #2119 (macOS, the pre-seed request this defect follows from), #1396, #3110 — none cover the Windows path-separator mismatch.

title: [Bug]: Windows: `ao session kill` returns INTERNAL_ERROR when the agent process still holds the worktree cwd — kill succeeds, only worktree cleanup fails
body:
## Summary

On Windows, when the agent process (or any child) still has the session worktree as its current working directory at kill time, `ao session kill` terminates the session but the post-kill worktree removal fails, and the whole request surfaces as HTTP 500 / `Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)` to the CLI. The session *is* dead — only the cleanup failed — but the caller can't tell success-with-dirty-worktree apart from a real failure.

Easiest trigger today is a claude-code session blocked on the workspace-trust dialog (#3407): the blocked process holds the worktree cwd, so every kill of such a session 500s. But any live process with cwd inside the worktree reproduces it — Windows refuses directory removal while a process holds it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows, AO 0.11.2. Spawn a session whose agent process stays alive with cwd inside its worktree (e.g. any claude-code session hitting #3407).
2. `ao session kill <session>`
3. CLI prints `Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)`; daemon log shows the removal failure below.
4. `ao session ls` shows the session terminated; the worktree directory is left behind.

## Expected behavior

Kill terminates the process first, waits for process exit to release the cwd handle, then removes the worktree (with a short retry/backoff for Windows handle release). If removal still fails, report kill success with a cleanup warning (and leave the worktree for a later GC pass) rather than a 500.

## Actual behavior

```text
method=POST path=/api/v1/sessions/<session>/kill status=500 duration=8.5s
error="kill <session>: workspace: gitworktree: remove unregistered path \"D:\\...\\worktrees\\<project>\\<session>\":
unlinkat D:\\...\\worktrees\\<project>\\<session>: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process."
```

CLI: `Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)`. The session is actually terminated; only the worktree removal failed.

## AO version

0.11.2 (desktop app; bundled daemon `resources\daemon\ao.exe`)

## Environment

Windows 10 Pro (10.0.19045) x64; ConPTY runtime

## Logs / extra context

- Once the same session is unblocked before kill (trust dialog answered / pre-seeded per #3407), kill returns cleanly: `session <id> killed (workspace preserved)`, HTTP 200.
- Duplicate search: #2701 (stale pre-tmux handle) and #2551 (orchestrator restart on a non-git worktree) are different kill/restart 500s; #3219 is about false-success counts in bulk cleanup. None cover the live-process-holds-cwd case on Windows.

title: feat(workspace): replicate refs/ao/preserved/* to origin on daemon boot and bound the local namespace
body:
## Problem

The agent orchestrator captures at-risk uncommitted work as a **hard precondition** of `ForceDestroy` — the capture runs first, the DB row with the preserve-ref is committed second, and only then does the worktree go away (`backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/commands.go:49-55` documents the invariant; `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:1370-1450` enforces it inside `SaveAndTeardownAll`; `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:353` is the adapter).

The capture lands at a platform-managed ref namespace `refs/ao/preserved/<session-id>` (`backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:465`). `ApplyPreserved` (`workspace.go:492`) replays the capture on restore via cherry-pick and deletes the ref on clean apply; on conflict the ref is kept forever (per the function's docstring). The preserve ref and `PreservedRef` column on `session_worktrees` (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/session_worktree_store.go:25`) are the platform's only record of in-progress work that survived a forced teardown.

**The capture never leaves the host.** There is no code anywhere in `backend/` that pushes `refs/ao/preserved/*` (or any ancestor of that namespace) to a remote. A grep for `ls-remote`, `push.*refs/ao`, `replicate`, and `reconcile.*ref` over `backend/` returns hits only for unrelated concerns (SCM observer, hooks reconcile, session-state reconcile). The local capture is the entire copy. A disk failure on the operator's machine destroys every capture, and the operator has no warning before that happens.

Measured on a single operator machine (long-running fork of this repo, no remote replication configured):

```
$ git for-each-ref refs/ao refs/rescue refs/salvage --format='%(refname:short)'
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-1>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-2>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-3>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-4>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-5>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-6>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-7>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-8>
rescue/2026-07-29/<sha-9>
salvage/<internal-name>
```

— 10 capture refs, commits spanning several days, all local. Origin has zero of them:

```
$ git ls-remote origin 'refs/ao/preserved/*' 'refs/rescue/*' 'refs/salvage/*'   # (empty)
```

This is the operator's largest data-loss vector: captures are exactly the work the platform judged worth saving, and they live in the same single disk that could die.

## Proposed direction

Treat `origin` as the backup target. The git transport, auth, and refspec machinery already exist; the work is to schedule the push, bound the local copy, and make replication loud.

1. **Formalize the capture ref namespace.** `refs/ao/preserved/<session-id>` is already platform-managed; extend it with `refs/ao/preserved/<project>/<session>/<utc-date>` so multi-project repos do not collide on the session id, and so a downstream `git for-each-ref` can scope by project.
2. **Daemon-startup reconciliation** (natural home: alongside `sessMgr.Reconcile` at `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:314`). On boot, enumerate `refs/ao/preserved/*` (and the legacy namespaces `refs/rescue/*` / `refs/salvage/*` for in-place migration) and for each ref:
   - if `git ls-remote origin <ref>` returns the same SHA, skip;
   - otherwise run `git push origin '<ref>:<ref>'`, log the result, and **retry on the next boot** if it failed. Fail-loud, never silent.
3. **Size budget on the local copy.** After `git ls-remote origin <ref>` confirms a ref's SHA matches origin and the ref is older than a configured retention (default 30 days), delete the local ref (`git update-ref -d <ref>`). Origin retains the archive. Refs that have never been verified pushed are **never** pruned.
4. **Per-project config switch** `salvagePushEnabled: true|false` (default `true`), on the existing `PUT /projects/{id}/config` surface. Disabled means: capture stays local, no reconcile, no prune. Documented escape hatch for offline repos.
5. **Tests** beside `workspace_preserve_test.go`: a fabricated local `refs/ao/preserved/<project>/<session>/<date>` ref is reconciled by the boot step (after a push the ref appears in `git ls-remote`); a push failure leaves the local ref untouched and surfaces the error; a 30-day prune only deletes refs whose SHA matches origin (asserted by a dedicated test).

## Acceptance criteria

- `grep -rn 'refs/ao/preserved\|ao/preserved\|reconcilePreserve\|pushPreserve' backend/internal --include='*.go'` shows BOTH the capture-side write (already present at `workspace.go:465`) AND a new startup-reconcile call site (`backend/internal/daemon/` or `backend/internal/session_manager/`) — wired, not just built.
- `cd backend && go test -race ./...` exits 0 including the new reconciliation tests.
- Behavioral proof: scratch repo, write a fabricated `refs/ao/preserved/...` ref, run the reconcile function (test harness or actual daemon boot), `git ls-remote origin 'refs/ao/preserved/*'` shows the ref.
- The 30-day local-prune is gated by `ls-remote` SHA equality and asserted by a dedicated test (no prune without verified remote).
- A live-fleet run after the daemon ships shows `git ls-remote origin | grep -c 'refs/ao/preserved'` increasing monotonically and never dropping.

## Non-goals

- Replicating bundle files (e.g. operator-side `*.bundle` exports). Origin is the backup; bundles are a separate offline-export path the operator already handles.
- Encryption or access control on the preserve refs. They are git objects over the project's existing origin; auth is whatever the remote already enforces.
- Replaying captures across machines. `ApplyPreserved` operates on the local repo; cross-machine replay is a separate restore concern (see the existing `ApplyPreserved` docstring).
- Cleaning the existing local backlog in this issue. The one-time push of the legacy `refs/rescue/*` + `refs/salvage/*` + `refs/ao/preserved/*` set to origin is a separate operator action and should be done before the reconciler ships to avoid a flood of pushes on the first boot.

## Prior art checked

- **`#2183`** (CLOSED) — "Zellij to tmux + ConPTY runtime, session save/restore, crash-proof reconcile." The save side wrote a preserve blob; it never replicated. The current Go implementation is the descendant and inherits the same gap.
- **`#2451`** (OPEN) — preserve **fidelity** bug: edits to tracked-but-gitignored files are dropped from the preserve tree. Different concern (capture correctness, not capture durability).
- **`#2476`** (OPEN) — "Persist immutable repo metadata on session_worktrees." Makes existing `PreservedRef` rows reliably resolvable across registry drift; complementary.
- **`#2811` / `#2931` / `#3051` / `#3052`** — terminal-resource reconciler stack. Reclaims worktrees and writes cleanup facts; does not push refs anywhere.
- **`#1739`** — proposes archiving worktrees on kill; orthogonal (it changes the teardown shape, not the capture-durability problem).
- **`#1131`** (CLOSED) — TS-era branch cleanup; different subsystem.

No open issue proposes replicating `refs/ao/preserved/*` to a remote or bounding the local namespace. Filing as new rather than commenting on `#2476` because that issue concerns row metadata for restore-path reliability, not off-host durability.

title: fix(tmux): unset ambient color env vars and pin pane interpreter to POSIX sh
body:
## What

Two focused backend fixes in the tmux adapter — no frontend changes.

**1. Unset ambient color/CI env vars in every pane**

Introduces `ambientColorSuppressors` (`CI`, `COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`, `NO_COLOR`). These are unset inside the pane launch command so agent TUIs (Claude, etc.) render colors correctly even when the daemon was started from a CI or coding-agent terminal that had them set. Previously only `NO_COLOR` was cleared.

**2. Pin pane interpreter to POSIX sh**

The `buildLaunchCommand` output uses POSIX syntax (`export`, `unset`, `cd || exit`). If the user's `$SHELL` is fish or nushell that syntax fails to parse and the session exits before the liveness probe fires. The fix pins the interpreter to `/bin/sh`; the user's interactive shell is still used for the keep-alive via `exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i` at the end of the launch command.

## What

Two things on the landing site, both about the mobile app.

### 1. The mobile mockup is rebuilt against the shipped app

The phone on the "Mobile companion" feature card (which the `/download` page reuses) was drawn at 187×390 with 4.5–6px type, its project pill row **overflowed the right bezel**, and its three non-Kanban tabs showed a generic placeholder card.

- The screen is authored once at 280×606 and the whole phone is scaled per breakpoint, so its metrics are one set of constants rather than per-breakpoint values. Type sits ~15% over the app's real points — a marketing zoom, not a redesign: a 190px-wide render of a 390pt screen is unreadable otherwise.
- The frame gets the cues that make a rectangle read as hardware: gradient rim, dynamic island, home indicator, side buttons, one soft glare.
- Content follows the **current** app rather than an older snapshot of it: Kanban is now **Agents**, card state is per-session rather than per-zone (so `Working` / `No signal` / `Merged` can share one section, as they do on a real board), **Orchestrator** is the project card list with its zone pills and worker actions, **PRs** is *Pull Requests* with the `Open / Merged / All` filter pills, and **Settings** uses the grouped-row kit with its footers and inset separators.
- The project picker is the **form sheet** the app presents — anchored to the phone so it covers the tab bar — not an inline dropdown. Tabs slide in the direction the tab bar reads.

Palette and metrics are lifted from `packages/mobile/lib/theme.ts`, `lib/ui.tsx`, `lib/SessionCard.tsx`, `lib/ProjectSwitcher.tsx` and `app/(tabs)/*`, with a comment saying so, so the mockup and the app can't drift silently.

### 2. `/download` offers a real iOS action

The Mobile card said "Coming Soon" while the iOS beta is live.

- **Join the iOS beta** opens a dialog with the two steps that actually get the app onto a phone: install Apple's TestFlight, then scan a QR of the invite. A direct link is kept for anyone already reading on the device.

`TESTFLIGHT_URL` moves into `packages/shared/src/constants.ts`. `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/ConnectMobileGetApp.tsx` hardcodes the same link and must be changed with it; the constant carries that note.

- The dialog is the only new client component; `download/page.tsx` stays a server component.

- Driven in a real browser: all four tabs render, the sheet opens/selects/scopes the board, tab slides run both directions, and the TestFlight dialog opens, renders its QR, and closes on X / backdrop / Escape with no console errors. title: [Feature]: Does the Orchestrator have visibility to Worker's responses?
body: ### Problem As a Dev (using claude for both Orch and Worker) i was trying out the AO but while working i quickly ran into the case when the worker wanted an input for further implementation, but the state of the worker was idle. Ideally in this state i would have wanted the orchestrator to check in on the progress, but since the orchestrator does not have any access to the response of the worker, this wasn't possible, I ended up going to the worker and copying the response to give it to the orchestrator. Firstly, as i am new to this, is it the designed behaviour? I have that question because even though this would look natural due to the Kanban board being present, one may argue, that it is by design to need to look at individual worker. But that defeats the purpose of an orchestrator. I would have wanted the orchestrator to be a central command panel, and the kanban board a status board for different tasks, and i can OPTIONALLY go and inspect the workers but not need to. The response on which the worker was sitting at (after i had prompted the orchestrator for "What are we doing right now?" ### Proposed direction There are many issues open and i couldn't find something that tracks something similar. One solution we may have for this is we can work on a system where these workers' responses are also accessible to the orchestrator, something similar to an Agent Council, except the orchestrator would check in on its own will, not for every single output. We can have a summarising worker that solely summarises the responses if context is an issue. I am open for discussion and interested in contributing to this. ### Alternatives considered _No response_ ### Before submitting - [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar - [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(codex): preserve Windows PATH precedence during binary resolution
body:
## What

Fix Windows Codex binary resolution so PATH directory order is preserved when both `codex.exe` and `codex.cmd` exist.

## Why

Addresses #3409.

The previous implementation searched by filename across the entire PATH (`codex.cmd`, `codex`, then `codex.exe`), allowing a later `codex.cmd` shim to be selected before an earlier native `codex.exe`.

## How

- Replace the Windows filename-first PATH search with a directory-first PATH scan.
- Check `codex.exe`, `codex`, then `codex.cmd` within each PATH directory.
- Continue using `resolveNativeWindowsCodex()` so a shim is upgraded to a nearby native executable when available.
- Preserve existing WindowsApps filtering.
- Add a regression test covering an earlier PATH `codex.exe` and a later PATH `codex.cmd`.

## Testing

Validated locally with:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/codex
```

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change
- [x] Added a regression test
- [x] Local tests pass

title: tmux prerequisite error gives no install guidance; only checked at spawn time
body:
## Bug / Enhancement

New users on macOS/Linux who don't have `tmux` pre-installed hit an opaque error on their first spawn attempt. The error message tells them tmux is missing but gives **zero guidance on how to install it**, and the prerequisite is only checked at spawn time — not at startup or onboarding — so the user discovers the problem only after they've already configured a project and tried to start a session.

**Source:** LinkedIn feedback | **Reported by:** Praveenkumar K | **Analyzed against:** `2d0b70f74`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Fresh install of Agent Orchestrator on macOS or Linux **without** tmux installed.
2. Open the app, configure a project, select an agent, and try to spawn a session.
3. Error returned:

```
runtime: prerequisite missing: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH (RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING)
```

4. User must independently figure out they need to install tmux (e.g. `brew install tmux`).

## Root Cause

The prerequisite check is correct but the **messaging and timing are unhelpful**:

**1. Bare error message with no install instructions**

`validateRuntimePrerequisites()` in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:3314` returns:

```go
return fmt.Errorf("%w: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH", ports.ErrRuntimePrerequisite)
```

This propagates through `service.go:670` → `apierr.Invalid("RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING", ...)` with the same bare text. No platform-specific install command is included.

**2. Checked only at spawn time, not at startup**

The daemon (`backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go`) and `ao start` (`backend/internal/cli/start.go`) do **not** run a tmux preflight. The user only discovers the missing dependency after they've gone through project setup and attempted a spawn.

**3. `ao doctor` checks it but isn't run automatically**

`backend/internal/cli/doctor.go:307` (`checkTmux`) does detect the missing binary and reports it as a warning — but `ao doctor` is a manual command that new users won't know to run.

**4. Frontend shows raw error text**

`frontend/src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts:252` (`apiErrorMessage`) has no special handling for `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING`. The NewTaskDialog surfaces the raw backend message with no actionable UI (no install hint, no docs link).

## Suggested Fix

**Layer 1 — Actionable error message (backend, low-effort):**
Enhance `validateRuntimePrerequisites()` to include platform-specific install commands in the error text:

```go
func (m *Manager) validateRuntimePrerequisites() error {
    if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
        return nil
    }
    if path, err := m.lookPath("tmux"); err != nil || path == "" {
        hint := tmuxInstallHint(runtime.GOOS) // "brew install tmux" / "sudo apt install tmux" / etc.
        return fmt.Errorf("%w: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH — install it: %s", ports.ErrRuntimePrerequisite, hint)
    }
    return nil
}
```

Platform hints:
- **macOS:** `brew install tmux`
- **Debian/Ubuntu:** `sudo apt install tmux`
- **Fedora/RHEL:** `sudo dnf install tmux`
- **Arch:** `sudo pacman -S tmux`

**Layer 2 — Proactive startup check:**
Run the tmux check at daemon startup (or `ao start`) and surface a warning in the dashboard if tmux is missing, rather than failing only at spawn time. This lets the user fix the issue *before* configuring a project.

**Layer 3 — Frontend error UX:**
Handle `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` in `NewTaskDialog` to show a user-friendly message with the install command and a link to the installation docs, instead of the raw error string.

## Impact

- **Who's affected:** Every new macOS/Linux user without tmux pre-installed (tmux is not in the macOS base system and is absent from many Linux server/container images).
- **Severity:** First-run friction — the user hits a dead-end error with no guidance on their very first interaction with the product.
- **Workaround:** Install tmux manually (but the user has to discover this on their own).

## Related

- `ao doctor` already detects this (`backend/internal/cli/doctor.go:307`) but is manual-only
- `docs/daemon-environment.md` documents the daemon PATH/tmux resolution problem for GUI-launched daemons

title: fix(session-manager): include install hint in tmux prerequisite error
body:
Fixes #3434

## Summary

When tmux is not installed and a user tries to spawn a session, the error message previously gave no guidance on how to fix it:

```
runtime: prerequisite missing: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH
```

Now includes a platform-specific install command:

```
runtime: prerequisite missing: tmux required on macOS/Linux but not in PATH — install it: brew install tmux
```

Added a `tmuxInstallHint(goos string)` helper that returns the correct package-manager command per platform:
- **macOS:** `brew install tmux`
- **Linux:** `sudo apt install tmux` (with dnf/pacman alternatives noted)
- **Other:** generic fallback

## Scope

This PR addresses **Layer 1** (actionable error message) from issue #3434. Layers 2 (proactive startup check) and 3 (frontend error UX) are left for follow-up since they require broader changes.

## Test

```bash
cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/service/session/ -count=1
```

Existing test at `manager_test.go` verifies the error still wraps `ports.ErrRuntimePrerequisite` and contains "tmux required" — both still pass with the enhanced message.

## Bug

The Browser tab fails to open HTML files. When a bare HTML filename (e.g., `-pr-3386-adapter-model-selection.html`) appears in the browser address bar, the content area remains empty/black and never renders.

**Reported by:** @illegalcall (Dhruv)
**Was working:** Yes — regression from recent changes.

### Screenshot

The address bar shows `-pr-3386-adapter-model-selection.html` (bare filename, no scheme). The content area is solid black with only the empty-state placeholder visible.

## Root Cause

### Primary: `withDefaultScheme()` misclassifies filenames as hostnames

**File:** `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:953-977`

The `looksLikeHost()` helper returns `true` for **any string containing a `.`**:

```ts
function looksLikeHost(raw: string): boolean {
    const host = raw.split(/[/?#]/, 1)[0];
    if (host === "") return false;
    if (host.startsWith("[") && host.includes("]")) return true;
    if (/:\d+$/.test(host)) return true;
    return host.includes(".");  // ← filenames like "file.html" match this
}
```

When `withDefaultScheme("-pr-3386-adapter-model-selection.html")` is called:
1. Not a Windows/POSIX absolute path ✗
2. Not `http(s)://` ✗
3. Not localhost ✗
4. No explicit scheme (starts with `-`) ✗
5. `looksLikeHost()` → host contains `.` → **true**
6. Returns `https://-pr-3386-adapter-model-selection.html` — invalid host, DNS fails, page never loads

### How the bare filename reaches the browser

**Path A — Daemon preview fallback:** When `ao preview` can't resolve the target to a workspace-local file (path mismatch, different working directory, etc.), `resolvePreviewTarget()` in `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:1073` returns the **raw string verbatim** as the preview URL. The frontend then calls `navigate(rawFilename)`, which fails.

**Path B — Address bar entry:** If a user types/pastes a bare filename into the address bar, the same `withDefaultScheme` misclassification applies.

### Regression scope

The `looksLikeHost` heuristic was introduced in **PR #3085** (`30bd3d2dd`). Before that commit, `withDefaultScheme` unconditionally returned `https://${raw}` for unrecognized input — which also produced an invalid URL for bare filenames. However, PR #3085 also changed the preview UX from auto-opening the Browser tab to merely badging it, which means users now have to manually interact with the tab and may encounter the failure more visibly.

PR #3295 (`42acd419e`) changed `active` gating to require `inspectorView === "browser"` — worth verifying this doesn't independently hide the native view overlay in edge cases.

## Fix Direction

`looksLikeHost` and/or `withDefaultScheme` should recognize bare filenames and handle them appropriately:

1. **Recognize file extensions:** If the input has no scheme, no path separator, and ends in a known extension (`.html`, `.htm`, `.pdf`, etc.), it's likely a local file — not a hostname. The daemon's `resolvePreviewTarget` already handles this correctly (producing localhost URLs for workspace files); the frontend normalization just needs to match.
2. **Or treat as search (Chrome-style):** If `looksLikeHost` returned `false` for filenames, they'd fall through to `searchURL()` — which is at least functional, though not ideal.
3. **Ideally:** The preview URL that reaches the frontend should always be a fully-qualified URL (the daemon's localhost origin), never a bare filename. The fallback at `sessions.go:1073` (`return raw, nil`) should be tightened to reject paths it can't resolve.

## Key Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:953-977` | `withDefaultScheme` / `looksLikeHost` — misclassification |
| `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:579-597` | `navigateEntry` → `loadURL` — where the invalid URL fails |
| `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:1053-1073` | `resolveLocalPreview` / `resolvePreviewTarget` — raw fallback |
| `backend/internal/preview/entry.go:183-197` | `FileURL` — correct localhost URL construction |
| `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts:643-659` | Preview-driven `navigate(target)` effect |
| `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:175-185` | `browserSlotVisible` / `active` gating |

## Reproduction

1. Start an AO session with a worker agent
2. Have the agent generate or reference an HTML file (e.g., `ao preview something.html` where the file can't be resolved to the workspace root, OR type a bare `.html` filename into the browser address bar)
3. Observe: address bar shows the bare filename, content area stays black/empty

title: Bug: Notification bell icon position inconsistent between Kanban and Orchestrator (worker) views
body:
## Bug

The notification bell icon changes position in the page header depending on which view is active (Kanban board vs. Orchestrator/worker terminal). The element order in the header's right-side action group is not consistent across views.

## Expected behavior

The notification bell should occupy the same position in the header regardless of which view (Kanban or Orchestrator/worker) is active.

## Actual behavior

**Kanban view** — bell is the **leftmost** item in the action group:
```
🔔 bell  →  + New task  →  Orchestrator
```

**Orchestrator / worker view (terminal tab)** — bell is the **rightmost** item:
```
+ New task  →  Kanban  →  🔔 bell
```

## Repro

1. Open a project in the desktop app.
2. Note the bell position in the Kanban board view.
3. Switch to the Orchestrator (worker terminal) tab.
4. Observe the bell has jumped to the opposite end of the action group.

## Screenshots

**Kanban view** — bell leftmost:

![Kanban view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/kanban-view-bell-left.png)

**Orchestrator view** — bell rightmost:

![Orchestrator view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/orchestrator-view-bell-right.png)

## Environment

- Component: Desktop (frontend/Electron + React)
- Likely cause: the header action group is rendered per-view with a different element order, rather than a shared layout that keeps the bell in a fixed slot.

title: fix(browser): prevent misclassifying bare html filenames as hostnames…

… (fixes #3436)

## What

Prevents the browser tab from misclassifying bare filenames with common extensions (such as `.html`, `.pdf`, `.png`) as hostnames when navigating or loading preview targets.

## Why

When bare filenames like `-pr-3386-adapter-model-selection.html` were typed or returned as unresolved preview targets, `looksLikeHost()` incorrectly treated them as hostnames due to the dot (`.`) in the filename. - Adds a "+" button to the browser panel's tabs dropdown, next to "Browser tabs", to open a new tab directly.

Ctrl+R got the same treatment after testing showed the native `role: "reload"` accelerator wasn't reliably resolving to the focused tab either.
- Fixes the "+" button showing "Tab limit reached" for any IPC failure, not just an actual cap-reached error.

While testing, a **pre-existing bug** in the browser panel's native tab-switching (wrong tab's content briefly/persistently showing after switching tabs) was confirmed to reproduce via mouse-only interaction (the tabs dropdown), independent of anything in this PR. It's more likely to be noticed now since this PR makes creating/switching between multiple tabs a common user action for the first time. Left out of this PR since it's a separate, pre-existing issue in `activateTab`/`applySessionBounds` (`browser-view-host.ts`) worth its own investigation.

title: [Bug]: Browser panel shows the wrong tab's content after switching tabs (native view bleed-through)
body: ### Summary After switching between tabs in the in-app Browser panel, the panel can display a *different* tab's content than the one that's actually active — the address bar shows the correct/active tab's URL, but the visible page is a stale render of a previously-active tab. It looks like the native `WebContentsView` for the tab being switched away from isn't always fully hidden, so it renders on top of (or instead of) the tab that should now be showing. This reproduces with plain mouse interaction (the tabs dropdown), so it isn't tied to any particular way of creating/switching tabs — it just becomes much easier to hit once a session has 2+ tabs open, which is now common after #3444 added a "+" new-tab button and keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+T etc.) to the panel. Before that, only an AI agent or a `target=_blank` popup could create extra tabs, so most sessions never had more than one. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a session with the Browser panel visible, with its one default tab. 2. Click the tabs icon → **+** to open a new tab (tab 2). 3. Navigate tab 2 to `https://google.com`. 4. Click **+** again to open a third tab (tab 3) — leave it blank/untouched. 5. Open the tabs dropdown and select tab 2 (Google) again. 6. Open the tabs dropdown and select tab 3 (the blank tab) again. 7. Observe the panel content. (This also reproduces with just two tabs and repeated switching: create tab 2, navigate it to Google, create tab 3 blank, switch back and forth a couple of times.) ### Expected behavior Each tab switch should show that tab's own content, matching its own address bar/URL. Switching to a blank tab should show a blank page; switching to the Google tab should show Google — never a mix of the two. ### Actual behavior The panel shows content from a tab that isn't the one currently marked active. In one repro, the address bar read `localhost:5173` (the session's original/default tab) while the visible page was Google's homepage (a different tab's content) — confirmed via screenshot during triage, not attached here. The user-visible effect is described as the previous tab's content "bleeding through" or leaving an "impression" on top of the tab that should be showing. ### Suspected cause / what's been ruled out This is in the native tab-activation path in `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`, specifically `activateTab()` and `applySessionBounds()` — the functions that hide the previously-active tab's `WebContentsView` (move it off-screen + `setVisible(false)`) and show the newly-active one. This code predates #3444; it's reachable through the pre-existing tabs dropdown, the pre-existing AI-agent `tab-select`/`tab-new` actions, and popup-tab creation — not just the new "+" button/shortcuts. Two fixes were attempted and did **not** fully resolve it (both reverted, not merged): 1. Re-raising the newly-shown tab's view to the top of Electron's `contentView` child stack on every show (`contentView.addChildView()` on an already-parented view reorders it to the front, per Electron's `View` docs) — theory being that `createTab()` only adds a tab's view to the stack once, at creation, so an older tab reactivated later stays stacked *below* every tab created after it. 2. Making `activateTab()` explicitly hide **every** other tab in the session on each activation, instead of trusting a single tracked "previously active" tab reference (in case an earlier hide silently didn't fully apply and never got corrected). Neither fix eliminated the repro, which suggests the root cause may be elsewhere — worth also looking at: - Whether Electron's `WebContentsView.setVisible(false)` / off-screen `setBounds()` calls are reliably taking effect for `WebContentsView` specifically (vs. the deprecated `BrowserView`). - The renderer's snapshot-based tab-switch masking overlay (`showVisualTransition("tab-switch")` in `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts`, rendered as an `` in `BrowserPanel.tsx`) — it captures a screenshot of the tab being switched *away from*, shows it as a temporary overlay, and auto-clears after `VISUAL_TRANSITION_DURATION_MS` (240ms) via `window.setTimeout`. If that overlay's clear-timer is somehow cancelled or its state never resets, a stale screenshot would visually match this exact symptom (a static "ghost" of a previous tab). Worth confirming whether the bleed is a live native view (would react to interaction/scrolling on the wrong tab) or a frozen image (wouldn't). - Any interaction between the renderer's periodic `browser:setBounds` sync (from a resize/measure effect) and the main process's own `activateTab()`-driven bounds/visibility changes, in case of a race between the two. ### AO version commit `9caafbee8` (`main`, 2026-07-31) / Electron `^33.0.0`. Not yet in a tagged release — found during development of #3444. ### Environment Windows 11, Electron dev build (`npm run dev` / electron-forge + Vite). ### Logs / extra context Related PR: #3444 (added the "+" new-tab button and browser-scoped keyboard shortcuts) — that PR does **not** contain a fix for this; it was investigated there and explicitly reverted/split out into this issue since it's a pre-existing bug in tab-activation, not something the new feature introduced. ### Before submitting - [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates - [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: Gate the Pipelines settings section behind Developer Mode
body:
## Problem

Pipelines are experimental and off by default, but their Settings surface is not. `<PipelinesSection />` renders unconditionally for every user in `frontend/src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.tsx:35`, immediately above `<DeveloperModeSection />` at `:36`. An experimental subsystem that can spawn agent sessions and provision worktrees should sit behind the same opt-in that already guards the other developer-only surface.

## Current state

**Pipelines flag is daemon-side.** `backend/internal/daemon/pipelines_flag.go` resolves, in order:

1. `AO_PIPELINES` env override (on *or* off) always wins, the dev/CI escape hatch
2. otherwise the persisted `pipelines.enabled` row in `app_settings`
3. neither set means off

While off, every `/api/v1/pipelines/*` route answers 501, no per-project engines start, and the CDC trigger bridges do not subscribe. The settings endpoint `/api/v1/settings/pipelines` is deliberately never gated, so the toggle stays reachable.

**Developer Mode is renderer-local.** `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts` keeps `developerMode` in `localStorage` under `ao.developerMode`, defaults off. `settings/DeveloperModeSection.tsx` is a single switch. Today it gates exactly one thing, the Feature Releases update channel in `settings/UpdatesSection.tsx`.

## The design question whoever picks this up has to answer first

Developer Mode lives in the renderer's `localStorage`. The pipelines flag has to be readable by a daemon that may have been launched headlessly with no renderer in the picture at all. **Developer Mode therefore cannot become the source of truth for whether engines start.**

Recommended split, but argue it if you disagree:

- Developer Mode gates **visibility of `<PipelinesSection />`** only.
- The persisted `pipelines.enabled` setting stays the single source of truth for the daemon, unchanged.
- `AO_PIPELINES` keeps overriding everything, unchanged. A dev or CI run must not need a renderer to enable the feature.

## The state to decide on, not to leave undefined

If a user enables pipelines and then turns Developer Mode off, the daemon setting is still on. The engines are still running and the Pipelines nav entry is still there, while the toggle that would turn it off has vanished. Pick one and write it down:

- **Leave it.** Matches the existing precedent in `UpdatesSection`, which deliberately still surfaces a Return action for a persisted feature-build pin even when Developer Mode is off, so a persisted choice is never stranded without an escape.
- **Force-disable pipelines when Developer Mode goes off.** Cleaner conceptually, but it means a UI toggle silently restarts the daemon and tears down running pipeline runs, which is a much bigger hammer.

The first is more consistent with what the app already does. Whichever is chosen, `docs/pipelines.md`'s "Enabling the feature" section has to say so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `<PipelinesSection />` is not rendered when Developer Mode is off
- [ ] With Developer Mode off and `pipelines.enabled` already true, the daemon still starts its engines and the routes still serve; this is a UI gate, not a functional one
- [ ] `AO_PIPELINES=on` still forces the feature on with Developer Mode off and no renderer involved
- [ ] The stranded-state behaviour above is implemented deliberately and covered by a test
- [ ] `docs/pipelines.md` "Enabling the feature" documents that the toggle now lives behind Developer Mode
- [ ] `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx` gets the same shape of coverage the Feature Releases gating already has (hidden by default, revealed on toggle, correct behaviour when toggled back off)

## Files

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/PipelinesSection.tsx`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx`
- `docs/pipelines.md`

## Note

Pipelines currently live on the unmerged #2863. This is small and self-contained, so it can either land on that branch or follow it, but it should not be the reason #2863 waits.

title: feat(inspector): apply the PR card palette from mockup 3a
body:
Applies the maintainer's PR card palette (mockup "3a PR card") to the session inspector PR card.

The palette is the contract, so every state the card can render is mapped onto one of the six values. Two rules drive the mapping: **every state is a labelled row**, and **hue is reserved for "clickable" and "blocked"**. Green and amber are retired in this card.

## Tokens

The six values are defined once as CSS custom properties in `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` and bridged to Tailwind utilities in `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css`. No hex literals in components.

| Token | Utility | Dark | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-text-pr-link` | `text-pr-link` | `#a5c9ff` | links, only |
| `--color-text-pr-blocked` | `text-pr-blocked` | `#e05252` | blockers, only |
| `--color-text-pr-title` | `text-pr-title` | `#f2f2f2` | primary text |
| `--color-text-pr-value` | `text-pr-value` | `#b0b0b0` | values |
| `--color-text-pr-label` | `text-pr-label` | `#5e5e5e` | labels, empty states |
| `--color-bg-pr-card` | `bg-pr-card` | `#171717` | inner surface |

Light theme gets re-anchored equivalents of the same six roles, so the toggle does not break.

## Before / after: every state mapped

| Element / state | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Card surface | `bg-settings-input` `#2a2a2a` | `#171717` |
| Section eyebrow "PULL REQUEST" | `settings-muted` `#a1a1a1` | `#5e5e5e` |
| `PR #n`, PR title | `settings-label` `#ececec` | `#f2f2f2` |
| PR icon | `settings-muted` | `#5e5e5e` |
| `Open ↗` link | `text-accent` `#4d8dff` | `#a5c9ff` |
| Blocker links (`provider blocked ↗`, failing checks, reviewers, conflict files) | `text-accent` | `#a5c9ff` |
| Non-interactive link fallback | `muted-foreground` | `#b0b0b0` |
| Branch range, author | `passive` | `#5e5e5e` |
| Field labels (Status / CI / Merge / Review) | `passive` | `#5e5e5e` |
| Row summaries, `·` separators, `+N more` overflow | `passive` | `#5e5e5e` |
| File count | `text-warning` (amber) | `#b0b0b0` |
| `+additions` | `text-success` (green) | `#b0b0b0` |
| `-deletions` | `text-error` (red) | `#b0b0b0` |
| **Status** Open / Draft / Merged / Closed | coloured state `Badge` pill (green / grey / blue / red) | labelled row, `#b0b0b0` |
| **CI** Passing | green | `#b0b0b0` |
| **CI** Pending | `muted-foreground` | `#b0b0b0` |
| **CI** Failing | red | `#e05252` |
| **CI** Checking (unknown) | `passive` | `#5e5e5e` |
| **Merge** Mergeable | green | `#b0b0b0` |
| **Merge** Blocked / Unstable | amber | `#e05252` |
| **Merge** Conflict | red | `#e05252` |
| **Merge** Checking (unknown) | `passive` | `#5e5e5e` |
| **Review** Approved | green | `#b0b0b0` |
| **Review** Pending (review required) | `muted-foreground` | `#b0b0b0` |
| **Review** Changes requested | amber | `#e05252` |
| **Review** None | `passive` / amber when unresolved comments exist | `#5e5e5e` |

## Judgment calls

The mockup pins three states (`Open`, `Pending`, `Blocked`, plus the `None` empty state). The rest were derived from the two rules:

1. **CI failing gets the blocker hue, not the value tier.** The mockup only shows CI pending. "Failing" is one of the provider's own merge-blocking reasons (`ci_failing` in `mergeReasonLabel`), so it is a blocker in the same sense `Merge: Blocked` is. Same reasoning promotes **Review: Changes requested** (`changes_requested` is also a listed blocking reason).
2. **Waiting states stay neutral.** `Pending`, `Checking`, and `Review: Pending` are not verdicts yet, so no hue. Unknown/`Checking` sits on the label tier rather than the value tier because it means "nothing observed yet", which is closer to an empty state than to a value.
3. **`Merge: Unstable` groups with `Blocked`.** The code already treats them identically for links and summaries, so splitting their colour would be arbitrary.
4. **Unresolved human comments no longer tint `Review: None`.** They used to make it amber. The attention now lives entirely in the reviewer links, which are blue because they are clickable. The value stays on the empty-state tier, which is what the mockup shows.
5. **The state `Badge` pill is gone.** "Every state is a labelled row" leaves no room for a coloured pill, and the mockup shows `Status  Open` as a row instead. `prSummaryParts` now emits a `status` part first, so the row formats and aligns like the others and `prStatusRows` picks it up for free.
6. **Diff counts lose their green/red.** `+2078 · -7` are counts, not verdicts, and the mockup renders the whole line on the value tier.
7. **The eyebrow override is scoped, not global.** `Section` is shared with Activity / Overview / Completion, so it took an optional `titleClassName` rather than restyling every inspector section.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts` clean; all six utilities and both theme blocks confirmed present in the emitted CSS.
- `npm test`: 1318 passed. The 5 failures in `src/landing/scripts/generate-markdown-twins.test.mjs` are pre-existing and reproduce identically on an untouched `main` worktree (a local module-resolution failure in the spawned landing script), unrelated to this change.

title: bug(desktop): terminal pane cannot scroll when using Grok as agent (Windows)
body:
## Summary

The terminal pane cannot be scrolled up to review earlier output when **Grok** is used as the agent. This is the same class of bug as the previously fixed Kilo Code (#2550) and Codex (#2493) issues — Grok is a fullscreen interactive TUI agent but is missing from the `KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS` set, so mouse-wheel/trackpad input is not translated into PageUp/PageDown.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start AO on Windows.
2. Start or attach to a session using **Grok** as the agent.
3. Produce enough terminal output to overflow the visible pane.
4. Try to scroll up (mouse wheel or trackpad).

## Expected behavior

The terminal pane scrolls up through earlier Grok output.

## Actual behavior

Scrolling does nothing — earlier output is inaccessible.

## Environment

- OS: Windows (reported by user)
- Agent: Grok (`Grok 4.5`)
- AO build: `nightly`

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` (line ~210):

```js
const KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS = new Set(["opencode", "kilocode"]);
```

Grok runs as a fullscreen interactive TUI (like opencode/kilocode) but is **not** in this set, so `providerScrollsByKeyboard("grok")` returns `false`. Wheel events are sent as SGR mouse reports into the pty instead of being translated to PageUp/PageDown, which Grok ignores.

## Suggested fix

Add `"grok"` to the set:

```js
const KEYBOARD_SCROLL_PROVIDERS = new Set(["opencode", "kilocode", "grok"]);
```

Add/update the focused test in `TerminalPane.test.tsx` so that `providerScrollsByKeyboard("grok")` returns `true`.

## Related

- #2550 — Kilo Code terminal does not scroll (same fix pattern, fixed)
- #2493 — Terminal cannot be scrolled when using Codex (fixed)
- #3309 — terminal garbled output / cursor jumps (different issue, open)

title: chore(release): stop generating dead Linux .blockmap sidecars
body:
Closes part of #3288 (workstream 3, the "consider dropping linux sidecar generation entirely" follow-up).

## Why

`AppImageUpdater` never fetches a `.blockmap` sidecar. Its differential path uses `FileWithEmbeddedBlockMapDifferentialDownloader`, which reads the blockmap from the AppImage's own tail at `fileSize - (blockMapSize + 4)` and therefore hard-requires `blockMapSize` in the feed yml. `feed.mjs` deliberately never emits `blockMapSize`.

Net: Linux differential updates were already off (clients fall back to a full download), and every Linux `.blockmap` we published was read by nobody. `feed.mjs` has said so in a comment since #3288 landed; this deletes the generation to match.

## The blocker is gone, verified

The only reason generation was kept is recorded in that comment: the private release pipeline's publish guard asserted on the Linux sidecar filenames, so dropping the files here would have redded a guard out of band.

That hardcoded list no longer exists. The guard is now feed-derived and its sidecar policy is:

```
win:   required   (NsisUpdater does fetch them, via AppUpdater.differentialDownloadInstaller)
mac:   forbidden  (policy, #3151, for #3034)
linux: ignored    ("so that the public repo dropping the dead generation
                    does not fail a publish here")
```

It is the only blockmap check wired into the private pipeline; no hardcoded filename list remains anywhere in those workflows. So this change is a publish no-op there.

## What changed

- `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`: the sidecar branch flips from "everything except mac" to "win only". One line.
- `frontend/scripts/feed.test.mjs`: the `#3034` mac-exclusion block becomes a windows-only block. Adds a Linux case asserting no `writeBlockmap` call, no sidecar on disk, and that `latest-linux.yml` still carries the AppImage's real sha512 with `blockMapSize` still absent (so AppImageUpdater keeps falling back to a full download rather than erroring). The win case now asserts exactly one call.
- `frontend/scripts/blockmap.test.mjs`: notes that the pinned `app-builder-lib` import now has one caller.
- Stale comments corrected in `feed.mjs` (header, `buildYml`, `generateFeeds`, `hashFile`) and `blockmap.mjs`, plus the one line in `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md` that listed sidecars as "Windows and Linux only".

Both release workflows collect sidecars with `shopt -s nullglob` globs (`.github/workflows/frontend-release.yml:407`, `feature-release.yml:468`), so fewer files needs no workflow change.

## Not touched

- **Windows sidecars are load-bearing.** `NsisUpdater` genuinely fetches `<installer>.blockmap`; a missing one silently degrades every Windows user to a full download. Unchanged.
- **macOS keeps shipping none**, per #3151 / #3267 decision 4. Unchanged; its regression test still asserts it.

## Tests

`frontend/scripts` suite, 88 passed:

```
 ✓ scripts/feed.test.mjs > generateFeeds blockmap sidecars are windows-only > does not call writeBlockmap or write a .blockmap sidecar for mac zips (#3034) 1ms
 ✓ scripts/feed.test.mjs > generateFeeds blockmap sidecars are windows-only > does not call writeBlockmap or write a .blockmap sidecar for linux AppImages (#3288) 1ms
 ✓ scripts/feed.test.mjs > generateFeeds blockmap sidecars are windows-only > still calls writeBlockmap for the win installer 1ms
 ✓ scripts/blockmap.test.mjs > writeBlockmap > writes a gzip sidecar and returns the file's base64 sha512 + size 23ms

 Test Files  8 passed (8)
      Tests  88 passed (88)
   Duration  568ms
```

(`npx vitest run --dir scripts`. Running the wider `scripts/` pattern also sweeps in `src/landing/scripts/generate-markdown-twins.test.mjs`, which fails on a missing `cheerio`; that dep lives in the separate `frontend/src/landing/package.json` and needs its own `npm ci`. Unrelated to this change and outside `frontend/scripts/`.)

title: fix(desktop): notification bell changes position between worker session and kanban board
body:
## What happens

The notification bell jumps when navigating between a worker session view and the kanban board (macOS / Linux, where the shell topbar is hidden and each view renders its own title row).

## Why

Two divergences between the two rows hosting the bell:

1. **Order in the actions row.** `ShellTopbar` renders the bell last — "The bell always trails the actions row, on every platform" (`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx`). The board's in-panel title row in `SessionsBoard.tsx` renders `<NotificationCenter />` **first**, ahead of New task / Orchestrator, so the bell sits on the opposite side of the action cluster.
2. **Right padding.** The board row uses `pr-4.5` (18px) while the topbar uses `pr-4` (16px), so even the bell's right edge shifts by 2px.

## Expected

The bell stays in the same spot across views: trailing the actions row, right edge aligned with the session topbar.

## Fix direction

- Move `<NotificationCenter />` to the end of the board's actions fragment so it trails like in `ShellTopbar`.
- Align the board title row's right padding with `topbarHeaderClass` (`pr-4`).
