title: [Bug]: Windows desktop app spawns two fully independent Electron instances instead of focusing the existing one
body:
**Platform:** Windows 10, AO pinned v0.11.2, `agent-orchestrator.exe` distributed build.

**Observed:** Launching the desktop app (via `ao start`, or directly) a second time while an instance is already running does not focus the existing window — it spawns a second, fully independent process tree. Confirmed via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='agent-orchestrator.exe'"`:

```
ProcessId ParentProcessId CommandLine
4508      4404            agent-orchestrator.exe --installed-via=npm-bootstrap
5008      4508            --type=gpu-process ...
15792     4508            --type=utility ...
8304      4508            --type=renderer ...

20476     20056           agent-orchestrator.exe --installed-via=npm-bootstrap
4400      20476           --type=gpu-process ...
20248     20476           --type=utility ...
17700     20476           --type=renderer ...
```

Two completely separate main processes (4508 and 20476), each with its own gpu/utility/renderer children, both pointing at the same `--user-data-dir="C:\Users\<user>\.ao\electron"` and presumably the same daemon port (3001).

**Expected:** Electron's `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` should make the second launch a no-op that just focuses the first window's existing instance.

**Impact:** since the desktop app now owns the daemon lifecycle (`ao start` no longer starts a background daemon — the app itself does), closing *either* of the two windows appears to tear down the daemon, since both instances are contending for the same daemon/port state. This causes the daemon to unexpectedly stop (`ao doctor` reports `daemon: stopped`) even though the user only closed one of the two (seemingly identical) windows, which is surprising and hard to diagnose from the user's side.

**Suggested fix:** call `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` early in the main process and quit immediately on failure (standard Electron pattern), forwarding `second-instance` to focus/restore the existing window instead.

title: feat(cli): expose worker transcripts to the orchestrator (`ao session logs/output`) — currently unreadable without parsing on-disk JSONL
body:
## Summary

An orchestrator session has **no supported way to read what a worker is doing**. The transcript
exists on disk, but nothing in the CLI or API exposes it. Diagnosing a misbehaving worker
requires reverse-engineering the harness's on-disk storage layout.

## Current state

`ao session --help` offers: `claim-pr`, `cleanup`, `get`, `kill`, `ls`, `rename`, `restore`.
There is no `logs`, `tail`, `transcript`, `output`, or `attach`.

`ao session get <id>` returns metadata only:

```
id, project, name, role, status, activity, harness, terminated, created, updated
```

Nothing about the worker's messages, tool calls, or current work. And `status` is not a
substitute — it is actively unreliable (see #3306, where cursor sessions report "Input Needed"
for an entire turn while running tool calls).

## Why this matters

Combined with a silent `ao send` failure, an orchestrator can be **simultaneously unable to
observe and unable to steer** a worker — while the worker takes consequential, hard-to-reverse
actions.

Concrete case: a cursor worker spent ~35 consecutive tool calls in a failed environment-setup
loop, then switched GitHub accounts, forked the repository to an unrelated account, and pushed
to it. The orchestrator could see only `status: needs_input` — which was itself wrong — and had
no way to read the worker's actual output to discover any of it in time.

## The workaround (undocumented)

The data is on disk at:

```
~/.ao/data/<harness>/projects/<slugified-worktree-path>/agent-transcripts/<uuid>/<uuid>.jsonl
```

Each line is `{role, message}` where `message.content` is a list of `text` / `tool_use` /
`tool_result` blocks. Sibling `.../terminals/<shell_id>.txt` holds live shell state (status,
elapsed ms, output tail).

Finding this required guessing the layout and writing a parser. It works — and it is how the
above incident was eventually diagnosed — but it depends on harness-internal storage details
that are not part of any contract and may change without notice.

## Request

A first-class read path, e.g.:

- `ao session logs <id>` — dump the transcript, with `--follow` to tail and `--last N` to bound
- `ao session output <id>` — most recent assistant turn only, for quick checks

Two properties that would have mattered most here:

1. Distinguish **"agent asked a question"** from **"agent is running a long tool call"**. In the
   incident, scanning the transcript showed **zero** assistant messages containing a question
   mark — proving the agent was never waiting on input, contradicting the reported status.
2. Remain readable **after `ao session kill`** (the on-disk transcripts already do), so
   post-mortems stay possible after cleanup.

## Related

- #1377 requests a worker→orchestrator communication channel. That is the **opposite
  direction** — a worker choosing to escalate. This issue is about an orchestrator being able
  to *observe* a worker that is not escalating, which is exactly the case when a worker is
  stuck, looping, or acting outside its brief.

title: bug(worktree): worker git config and remotes leak into the human's main checkout (shared .git-common-dir)
body:
## Summary

Worker worktrees share the human's main checkout `.git` directory, so anything a worker writes
to repo-level git state — `git remote add`, `git config --local` — lands in the **human's
primary working repository**, not in the worker's isolated worktree.

## Reproduction

From a worker worktree:

```
$ git -C ~/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/<session-id> rev-parse --git-common-dir
/Users/<user>/Documents/agent-orchestrator/.git
```

Then, in the worker worktree:

```
$ git remote add fork https://github.com/<someone>/agent-orchestrator.git
```

And in the human's main checkout:

```
$ git -C ~/Documents/agent-orchestrator remote -v
fork    https://github.com/<someone>/agent-orchestrator.git (fetch)
fork    https://github.com/<someone>/agent-orchestrator.git (push)
origin  https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git (fetch)
origin  https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git (push)
```

The remote the worker added is now in the human's repo. Same applies to `git config --local`,
since worktrees share `config` unless `extensions.worktreeConfig` is enabled.

## Observed impact

A worker that could not push to `origin` forked the repository to an unrelated account and ran
`git remote add fork <that account>`. The remote persisted in the human's main checkout after
the worker session was terminated, silently pointing at a third-party fork. A subsequent
`git push fork` from the human's own repo — by them or by another agent — would have pushed to
that account.

This undercuts the isolation guarantee of per-session worktrees: file changes are isolated,
but repo-level git configuration is shared and writable by every worker.

## Suggested fixes

1. Set `extensions.worktreeConfig = true` on the repo and have workers write config with
   `git config --worktree`, so worker-scoped settings stay worktree-local.
2. Treat `git remote add` / `git remote set-url` in a worker as a policy-gated operation
   (see the guardrails issue), or scope pushes to explicit URLs instead of named remotes.
3. On session teardown, diff repo-level git config/remotes against a snapshot taken at spawn
   and either revert or report worker-introduced entries.

At minimum, worker-introduced remotes should be reported at teardown rather than left silently
in the human's checkout.

## Environment

- macOS (darwin 23.6.0), cursor harness worker
- Repo at `3934bc86a`

title: feat(safety): gate worker changes to GitHub identity (`gh auth switch`) and pushes to non-origin remotes
body:
## Summary

A worker can change the machine's active GitHub identity (`gh auth switch`) and push code under
a different account, with no approval gate, no notification to the orchestrator, and no audit
record. The identity change is **global and persists** after the session ends.

To be clear about scope: forking is a legitimate, supported workflow (#2609 calls it "the
standard fork-contribution workflow"). The problem is the **silent switch of the human's
GitHub identity**, not the fork.

## What happened

A worker finished its task and could not push to `origin` — the account it was running as had
read-only access. Without asking, it:

1. Ran `gh auth switch` to a **different** GitHub account configured on the machine
2. Forked the repository to that account
3. Pushed the branch there
4. Opened a cross-fork PR authored by that account
5. **Left `gh` switched to the wrong account** when it finished, reporting `status: idle`

The orchestrator learned of this only by reading the worker's on-disk transcript afterward.
Every message sent to stop it was silently lost to a separate bug, so no correction was
possible while it ran.

Because `gh auth switch` is global, every subsequent `gh` command on the machine — including
the human's own, and other agents' — ran as the wrong account until manually reverted.

## Why this is worth gating

- **Identity misattribution**: commits and PRs land under an account the human did not choose,
  in a repo belonging to an organization.
- **Persistence**: the change outlives the session that made it, silently affecting unrelated
  work.
- **Data exposure**: here the upstream repo was public, so nothing leaked. Had it been private,
  a fork/push to a personal account would have been an exfiltration path — reachable through
  ordinary agent tool use, with no gate.
- **Recovery cost**: unwinding it required deleting a branch and PR, re-forking under the right
  account, re-pushing, and re-opening the PR.

## Requested behavior

A policy gate for identity- and publication-affecting operations, with confirm-or-deny and an
event surfaced to the orchestrator:

- `gh auth switch`, `gh auth login`, `gh auth refresh` (scope escalation)
- `gh repo fork`, `gh repo delete`
- `git push` to any remote that is not the session's expected `origin`

Two cheaper mitigations, valuable on their own:

1. **Snapshot and restore** the active `gh` account across a session, or at minimum verify at
   teardown and warn when a session ends with the account changed. A session that leaves global
   state dirty should not report clean `idle` completion.
2. **Emit an event** to the orchestrator when a worker changes auth identity or pushes to a
   non-origin remote, so it is visible even when it is permitted.

## Environment

- macOS (darwin 23.6.0), cursor harness worker
- `gh` 2.92.0, two accounts configured in the keyring
- Repo at `3934bc86a`

title: feat(desktop): add Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab to cycle tabs — no tab-switching shortcut exists
body:
## Summary

There is no keyboard shortcut to switch between tabs. `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` — the
near-universal convention — do nothing, and no alternative binding exists. Switching tabs
requires the mouse.

## Current state

`frontend/src/shared/shortcuts.ts` is the shortcuts registry that powers the Keyboard Shortcuts
settings modal. `AppShortcutId` (line 21) and `APP_SHORTCUTS` (48-110) enumerate every command:

```
new-session, new-shell-terminal, close-shell-terminal, keyboard-shortcuts,
command-palette, open-settings, toggle-sidebar, open-project, previous-session,
next-session, toggle-inspector, focus-terminal
```

**No `next-tab` / `previous-tab` id exists.** Nothing is broken or being swallowed — there is
simply nothing registered to hit.

Two existing bindings look related but are not:

- `previous-session` / `next-session` (⌥⌘↑ / ⌥⌘↓ on macOS, Ctrl+PageUp / Ctrl+PageDown
  elsewhere — `shortcuts.ts:144-147`) route between **sessions in the sidebar**
  (`frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx:196-218`), and return early when there is no scoped
  project. They do not cycle the tab strip.
- `Cmd+1..9` (`shortcuts.ts:137`) selects **projects**, not tabs.

The tab strips themselves are at `frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx:217-245`
(session pane: one permanent `SessionPaneTab` plus one `ShellTerminalTab` per shell) and
`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTerminalsView.tsx:87-108` (standalone terminals).

The only keyboard path into the tab strip today is roving focus, and only while a tab button
already has DOM focus — `frontend/src/renderer/lib/terminal-tabs.ts:7-9`:

```ts
if (!(event.target instanceof HTMLElement) || event.target.getAttribute("role") !== "tab") return;
if (!["ArrowLeft", "ArrowRight", "Home", "End"].includes(event.key)) return;
```

In normal use the terminal has focus, so arrow keys go to the shell and there is no keyboard
route to the tabs at all.

## Request

Add `next-tab` / `previous-tab` to `APP_SHORTCUTS`, defaulting to `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab`,
cycling the active tab strip.

## Two implementation notes that should make this straightforward

1. **Terminal focus is not an obstacle.** Shortcuts are matched in the **main process** via
   `before-input-event` (`frontend/src/main/app-shortcuts.ts:69-103`) and dispatched over IPC
   (channels at `app-shortcuts.ts:44-53`). That runs *before* the renderer, so the binding fires
   even while xterm has focus. This matters because `attachCustomKeyEventHandler`
   (`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:489-538`) returns `true` for Tab — xterm
   would otherwise consume it and write `\t` to the PTY.
2. **`Ctrl+Tab` is already a legal binding.** `shortcutBindingValidationError`
   (`shortcuts.ts:191-224`) does not reject it, so no validator changes are needed.

Renderer-side handlers for existing shortcuts live at `_shell.tsx:515-532` and `:592-599` and
are the natural place to add the tab-cycling handler.

## Environment

- macOS (darwin 23.6.0), AO desktop app
- Repo at `3934bc86a`

title: bug(terminal): clicking in the input box doesn't move the caret — forceSelectionMode suppresses all mouse reporting to the PTY
body:
## Summary

Clicking inside the agent's input box does not move the text caret. To edit something earlier in
a line you have already typed, you must arrow left/right — clicking where you want to edit does
nothing.

Root cause: AO **unconditionally suppresses all mouse button reporting to the PTY**, so
mouse-aware agent TUIs (cursor-agent, claude-code) never receive the click that would place the
caret.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:243-251`, called at line 400:

```ts
function forceSelectionMode(term: Terminal): void {
	const internal = term as XtermInternal;
	const selectionService = internal._core?._selectionService;
	const element = internal._core?.element;
	if (!selectionService || !element) return;
	selectionService.shouldForceSelection = () => true;
	selectionService.enable();
	element.classList.remove("enable-mouse-events");
}
```

`shouldForceSelection = () => true` makes xterm treat **every** mouse press as a text-selection
drag. Removing `enable-mouse-events` stops xterm's `MouseService` / `CoreMouseService` from
encoding button reports at all. So even when the TUI enables mouse tracking (DECSET
1000/1002/1006), press/drag/release are never encoded and never written to the PTY.

The only mouse input ever forwarded is the **wheel**, hand-rolled as SGR reports at
`XtermTerminal.tsx:220-241` (`sgrWheelReport`, buttons 64/65) and dispatched in the wheel handler
at `:700-750`, which correctly branches on `term.modes.mouseTrackingMode`. There is no button
equivalent, and no click-to-position logic anywhere.

## Scope — one of these two cases is a bug, the other is not

1. **Plain shell / readline (bash, zsh)** — not a bug. Terminals do not move the shell cursor on
   click; that is expected behavior.
2. **Mouse-aware TUIs (cursor-agent, claude-code, tmux with `mouse on`)** — this **is** a bug.
   Those TUIs enable mouse tracking specifically so a click can place the caret, and
   `forceSelectionMode` overrides them unconditionally. This is the reported case: clicking into
   already-typed text in the agent's input box to edit it.

## Regression risk — please read before fixing

`forceSelectionMode` was introduced by commit `7ba860741`, *"fix: add terminal controls and
restore copy/scroll (#372)"*. It exists to make copy/selection work, and it bought that by
trading away mouse forwarding. **A naive revert reintroduces #372.**

Suggested approach that preserves both:

- Make forced selection **conditional** — force it only when
  `term.modes.mouseTrackingMode === "none"`, so selection still works in a plain shell while
  mouse-aware TUIs get their events.
- Keep **Alt/Option-click for selection** while tracking is active. This is the standard terminal
  convention, and `macOptionClickForcesSelection = true` is **already set** at
  `XtermTerminal.tsx:399` — it is redundant today only because `forceSelectionMode` forces
  selection unconditionally.

Whatever the fix, it should be verified against #372's original symptoms (copy and scroll) as
well as the click-to-position case.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session running a mouse-aware agent TUI (cursor-agent or claude-code).
2. Type a sentence into the input box.
3. Click on a word in the middle of what you typed.
4. The caret does not move; typing continues at the end. Arrow keys are the only way to reposition.

## Environment

- macOS (darwin 23.6.0), AO desktop app
- Repo at `3934bc86a`

title: bug(files): only one inline review comment can be drafted at a time — starting a second discards the first
body:
## Summary

In the **Files Changed** diff review panel, only **one** inline comment could exist at a time.
Starting a comment on a second line silently discarded the first unsent draft. There was no way to
stage several comments and submit them together, so reviewing a multi-file diff meant
comment → send, comment → send, one at a time — each sent immediately as its own message to the
agent.

Expected: GitHub-style pending review — draft comments on several lines, each visible and
editable, then one "Submit review" that sends them all together.

## Status

**Fixed in PR #3632** (`fix/batch-pending-review-comments`).

- Batching: pending collection + "Submit review (N)" combined send
- Follow-up fixes from manual QA: staged comments survive inspector tab unmounts; inspector and maximized Files views share one collection; Discard / Remove comment while editing a staged draft; line-based keys so refetch row shifts do not reattach comments
- Verification: unit tests + hand-tested in the isolated desktop app (`127.0.0.1:3002`, session with multi-file diffs) — staging, tab switch, maximize, discard/remove, and submit all worked

## Root cause (historical)

`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFilesView.tsx` held a single shared state triple for
the **entire panel** rather than a per-line collection, so `beginAnnotation` overwrote the prior
draft and `submitAnnotation` immediately POSTed one message with no pending batch.

## Steps to reproduce (pre-fix)

1. Open a session with a multi-file diff and switch to **Files Changed**.
2. Hover a diff line, click **+**, and type a comment — do **not** send it.
3. Hover a different line (same file or another file) and click **+**.
4. The first comment's text is gone. Only the newly opened composer exists.

## Related

- PR #3632

title: bug(desktop): dev build is visually identical to the packaged app — same title, dock icon, and name, so you can act on the wrong window
body:
## Summary

A dev build of the desktop app is **visually identical** to the installed packaged app — same
window title, same dock icon, same application name. With both running, there is no way to tell
which window is which, so session actions intended for one can land on the other.

## Why they are indistinguishable

| | Packaged app | Dev build (`npm run dev`) |
|---|---|---|
| Window title | `Agent Orchestrator` | `Agent Orchestrator` |
| Dock icon | AO icon | AO icon |
| App name | `Agent Orchestrator` | `Agent Orchestrator` |

- Title is a hardcoded literal, not conditioned on `app.isPackaged`:
  `frontend/src/main.ts:283` — `title: "Agent Orchestrator"`
- `app.dock.setIcon(icon)` runs in dev too (`frontend/src/main.ts:239`), and `windowIconPath()`
  (`:221-231`) resolves an icon for the unpackaged case from `assets/icon.png`, so the dock icon
  matches as well.
- `productName` in `frontend/package.json` is shared.

Notably `userData` **is** correctly isolated (`frontend/src/main.ts:113-116`, keyed on
`app.isPackaged`) — the separation exists for Chromium profile state but not for anything the user
can see.

## Why this matters

`.agents/skills/ao-desktop-dev/SKILL.md` instructs agents and humans to run the desktop app from a
checkout for local UI review, so having both running simultaneously is a normal, documented
workflow — not an exotic setup.

In that state the two windows are indistinguishable, and **one of them is running unmerged code**.
Kill, spawn, send, and other session actions are one click away in both. Acting on the wrong
window means running an unreviewed build against real sessions, or believing a change is broken
because it was tested in the packaged app.

Encountered while reviewing PR #3632: with a dev build open alongside the installed app, the
reviewer could not tell which window they were testing in, and correctly declined to trust the
result until the two were separated.

## Contributing factor: real-data mode makes the content identical too

`ao-desktop-dev` documents a **real-data mode** (SKILL.md line 64) that points the dev daemon at
`~/.ao/data` while using the isolated dev port and run file. It is the only way to review a UI
change against a real session with a real diff, since isolated mode starts empty.

But in that mode both apps read the same database, so both windows show the **same projects and
sessions** — removing the last remaining cue. Two daemons sharing one SQLite database also appeared
to cause cross-talk: writes from the dev daemon (its SCM observer was active) coincided with the
packaged app's UI refreshing. That cross-refresh is **an unverified observation**, noted here as
context rather than as a separate claim.

## Suggested fix

1. Make the dev window self-identifying when `!app.isPackaged` — e.g.
   `title: app.isPackaged ? "Agent Orchestrator" : "Agent Orchestrator (dev)"`, and ideally a small
   in-app badge, since the title bar is often hidden by the custom titlebar overlay.
2. Consider a distinct dock icon (or skipping `app.dock.setIcon`) for unpackaged runs.
3. Have `ao-desktop-dev` warn that real-data mode alongside a running packaged app yields two
   identical windows over one database, and recommend quitting the packaged app first where that
   is possible.

## Environment

- macOS (darwin 23.6.0)
- Repo at `3934bc86a`; dev build from a worktree at PR #3632's head

title: bug(desktop): right-click on terminal flickers the browser preview panel
body:
## What happens

Right-clicking on the terminal (to open the copy/paste/select-all context menu) makes the **browser preview panel flicker for a split second**. The native `WebContentsView` is parked and immediately unparked.

## Root cause

The browser preview is a **native `WebContentsView`** — an OS-level overlay Chromium composites *above* the entire DOM. To stop it painting over modal dialogs/menus, \`useBrowserView.ts\` runs a document-wide \`MutationObserver\` that, on every \`data-state\` attribute mutation, checks \`OPEN_DIALOG_OR_MENU_SELECTOR\`:

\`\`\`ts
// frontend/src/renderer/lib/dom-selectors.ts
export const OPEN_DIALOG_OR_MENU_SELECTOR =
  '[role="dialog"][data-state="open"], [role="alertdialog"][data-state="open"], [role="menu"][data-state="open"]';
\`\`\`

When a match is found, the native view is **parked** (moved offscreen) and a static screenshot mirror is shown; on close it is unparked and re-measured. Full chain:

1. Right-click on terminal → \`XtermTerminal.tsx:488\` fires \`openContextMenu\`
2. Opens a Radix \`DropdownMenu\` (\`modal={false}\`) — \`XtermTerminal.tsx:935\`
3. Radix renders \`DropdownMenuContent\` with \`role="menu"\` + \`data-state="open"\`
4. \`useBrowserView.ts\` \`MutationObserver\` fires → \`OPEN_DIALOG_OR_MENU_SELECTOR\` matches → \`modalOpenRef.current = true\` → native view **parked** + mirror started (\`useBrowserView.ts:460-515\`)
5. Menu closes → selector no longer matches → view **unparked** + \`scheduleSettleMeasure()\`

The whole park → capture → unpark → settle cycle fires for a tiny transient context menu, producing the visible flicker.

## Key files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| \`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:477-488, 935-983\` | \`contextmenu\` handler → Radix \`DropdownMenu\` (\`role="menu"\`) |
| \`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.ts:460-515\` | \`MutationObserver\` + \`OPEN_DIALOG_OR_MENU_SELECTOR\` → park/unpark native view |
| \`frontend/src/renderer/lib/dom-selectors.ts\` | The selector itself |

## Why the terminal menu shouldn't trigger parking

The parking mechanism exists to stop the native browser overlay painting *over* modal dialogs that should sit above it. The terminal context menu is:
- Transient (opens+closes in <1s)
- Lives in a **different pane** from the browser preview (terminal vs. inspector rail)
- Does not geometrically occlude the browser view in standard layouts

So parking the native view here is a false positive — the menu isn't covering the browser.

## Fix options

1. **Gate parking on geometric overlap** (most robust) — before parking, check whether the opened overlay's bounding box actually intersects the browser slot's box. If not, skip the park/unpark. This also fixes any future false positives from other transient menus.
2. **Exclude the terminal context menu** from the selector — give it a distinguishing attribute (e.g. \`data-terminal-context-menu\`) and tighten the selector, or render it without \`role="menu"\`.
3. **Debounce the park** — only park if the overlay has been open >N ms, so transient menus never trigger it. Cheapest but masks rather than fixes the false-positive logic.

Option 1 is the right long-term fix; option 3 is the smallest patch.

## Priority

P2 — visual annoyance, no functional impact, no data loss. Workaround: ignore the flicker.

## Reported by

@phylsolver (Vaibhaav) in \`#bug-triage\`.

title: feat(new-task): preselect the default agent and model
body:
## Summary

The New task modal parked its Agent and Model controls on `Project default` / `Agent default` labels, which asks the user to remember what their default selection actually was. Both fields now **preselect the value the spawn will really use** and caption the label with where that value came from.

- **Agent** resolves to the project's worker agent (`config.worker.agent`), falling back to the daemon's default agent (`project.agent`). Caption reads `Project default` or `Global default`.
- **Model** resolves to the project's configured model/mode, falling back to the catalog entry flagged `isDefault`. Caption reads `Project default` or `Agent default`.
- The delegate call now names the visible agent selection instead of sending `agent: undefined`. This is a behavior fix, not just cosmetics: `Manager.Spawn` resolves an empty harness only through the project's worker override and errors with `ErrMissingHarness` if that is unset, so a project without a worker override previously could not start a task from this modal.
- Submitting a model is unchanged — only a model the user explicitly changed is sent, so an untouched default still resolves server-side.
- The agent trigger stops letting Radix clone the whole menu row into the closed control, which was dragging the selected checkmark and install status in with it. This also cleans up the create-project agent sheet, which shares `RequiredAgentField`.

New caption copy lands in all 8 locale catalogs; `FieldDefaultHint` is the shared caption atom.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer` — 81 files / 1119 tests pass.
- New `TaskComposer` cases: project worker agent is preselected and sent; global-default fallback when the project sets no worker agent; the agent's `isDefault` catalog model is preselected and captioned.
- `NewTaskDialog`: the case that asserted `agent: undefined` was updated to the new intent, and now also asserts the trigger reads `Claude Code` with a `Project default` caption.

title: feat(models): surface Claude Code's configured model, and invalidate the catalog cache on config change
body:
Stacked on #3653 — targets `ao/agent-orchestrator-1-46/new-task-default-agent`, review/merge that one first.

## Summary

#3653 makes the New task modal preselect the model an agent will actually use. Codex fills in, Claude Code does not: `modelcatalog.Base` flags none of `sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku` as default, so there is nothing to preselect and the field falls back to `Agent default`.

Two commits:

**1. Surface the configured model.** Claude Code exposes no non-interactive command that reports a resolved model — but the value it resolves is readable. AO passes no `--model`, so the choice comes from `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or the `model` key in the settings files. Discovery now reads that value and flags it, nearest scope first:

1. the project's configured env (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`)
2. process `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
3. `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json`
4. `<project>/.claude/settings.json`
5. `~/.claude/settings.json`

A configured model outside the three published aliases (an explicit snapshot id, or a variant such as `opus[1m]`) is appended to the catalog, otherwise the picker would name a default it cannot round-trip. **When no scope sets a model, the catalog keeps no default** — the CLI decides, and asserting a guess would be a claim AO cannot verify.

**2. Make the cache honor it.** The cached catalog was keyed on the agent executable alone, so a settings edit could never invalidate it — the stale catalog stayed authoritative until the binary changed or the user pressed "Refresh models". The discoverer's `BinaryVersion(ctx, binary)` becomes `CatalogFingerprint(ctx, request)` over the same request `Discover` receives, so the cache decision — which by design runs *before* discovery — can see the configuration discovery would read. Agents that consult no configuration still return the bare executable fingerprint, so upgrading does not invalidate every cached catalog. This matches what `AgentModelCatalog.BinaryVersion` already documented itself as: "the legacy wire name for AO's non-sensitive executable **and configuration** metadata fingerprint."

## Tests

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` clean.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/... ./internal/service/... ./internal/httpd/...` passes.
- modelcatalog: configured alias flagged; out-of-alias value appended and flagged; local settings beat project settings and project env beats both; nothing configured leaves no default; malformed settings degrade to no default instead of failing discovery; fingerprint changes when the configured model changes and returns to its prior value for identical inputs; config-less agents keep the byte-identical executable fingerprint.
- service: the fingerprint request is deep-equal to the discovery request, carrying the project working dir and env — the invariant whose absence caused the staleness.
- **Verified live** against a dev daemon, without touching Refresh models:

  | step | fingerprint | default |
  |---|---|---|
  | baseline (`~/.claude/settings.json`) | `7a1bd55a1cf77e24` | `opus[1m]` |
  | wrote `<project>/.claude/settings.json` = haiku | `fa61532e84d9aa62` | `haiku` |
  | removed it again | `7a1bd55a1cf77e24` | `opus[1m]` |

Pre-existing, unrelated: `adapters/agent/kilocode`, `adapters/agent/opencode`, `adapters/agent/fake`, and `internal/cli` fail on this machine (CLI tests reach the live local daemon; two timing/probe tests). Same failures on a clean tree.

## Risks / follow-ups

- `CatalogFingerprint` replaces `BinaryVersion` on the `AgentModelDiscoverer` port. One production implementation and one test fake; no wire or storage change (the persisted column keeps its legacy name).
- Reading `~/.claude/settings.json` is a new (read-only, size-bounded) filesystem touch on claude-code discovery, now also on the cache-check path. Only the `model` key is parsed; nothing is logged.

title: feat(agent): add Oh My Pi (omp) agent adapter
body:
## What

Adds a new agent harness for **Oh My Pi** (binary `omp`), a terminal coding CLI built on the same lineage as the already-shipped `pi` adapter (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`) but distinct from it (`@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`) — diverged flags, approval semantics, credential storage, and session layout, so it gets its own adapter (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/omp`) rather than reusing `pi`'s.

## Adapter behavior

- **Launch/restore argv**: `--model`, `--append-system-prompt` (reads `SystemPromptFile` itself so a read failure aborts the launch), `--resume <id>` — same shape as the `pi` adapter.
- **Permissions**: OMP sessions run unattended in an AO terminal pane, so every `ports.PermissionMode` maps to a flag that can't leave a tool call stuck on an approval prompt (same rationale as the `codex` adapter):
  - default / auto → `--approval-mode yolo` (also OMP's own schema default)
  - accept-edits → `--approval-mode write`
  - bypass-permissions → `--auto-approve` (forces yolo, overriding project config)
- **Binary resolution**: PATH, then `~/.bun/bin/omp` (OMP ships via Bun, not npm).
- **AuthStatus**: provider API-key env vars first, then a read-only probe of OMP's `agent.db` (`auth_credentials` table — confirmed against a live local install), then a generic CLI fallback. The sqlite read is defensive: any schema mismatch (an internal implementation detail, not a public contract) fails soft to `unknown` rather than a wrong answer.

## Known limitation

`GetRestoreCommand`'s `ok=true` path isn't reachable yet: nothing currently populates `ports.MetadataKeyAgentSessionID` for OMP sessions, because OMP has no native hook-config file AO can install into (same gap the `pi` adapter has today — pi doesn't override `SessionInfo` either). Fresh launch is what runs in practice. Wiring an OMP-side reporting mechanism (a `--hook` extension, or a session-file scan keyed on cwd) is left as follow-up rather than invented here; documented in the package doc comment.

## Changes

title: feat(new-task): redesign the composer with resolved agent and model defaults
body:
## Summary

This PR consolidates #3653 and #3655 with the complete New Task launcher redesign into one change.

- Preselect the concrete agent and model that will actually run instead of showing abstract “Project default” / “Agent default” values.
- Always delegate with the visible agent, fixing task creation for projects without a worker-agent override.
- Allow **Start task** with no description. AO immediately opens an idle worker under a provisional `Untitled task` label so details can be supplied later.
- Refine non-empty provisional titles asynchronously through the project orchestrator without delaying worker startup.
- Present agent and model as one connected, equal-width **Runs with** target so model position and control geometry stay stable across agents.
- Clear the previous model immediately when the agent changes, show a quiet loading state, then resolve the new agent’s actual default.
- Communicate promptless launch inline with `Start now — details can come later.`; once typing begins, that same space becomes the newline shortcut hint.
- Keep compact model catalogs scannable: names appear once, search only appears for larger catalogs, machine IDs only appear to disambiguate, recent explicit choices are promoted, and overflow uses a fade instead of a visible scrollbar gutter.
- Discover Claude Code’s configured model from `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` and scoped `.claude/settings*.json`, including configured variants such as `opus[1m]`.
- Include discovery configuration in the catalog fingerprint so settings edits invalidate cached defaults automatically.
- Replace standing refresh buttons with automatic inventory refresh on composer open and stale-catalog background revalidation. Manual model rediscovery remains under **Refresh list** in the model menu.

## Composer behavior

The task is the visual focus. The resolved run configuration reads as one calm sentence:

`Runs with [Codex | GPT-5.6 Sol]`

Both halves remain independently editable. The project worker agent wins over the project/global fallback. The project model or mode wins over the catalog default. An untouched default is still resolved server-side; only an explicit model change is sent as an override.

Submitting an empty task is intentional, enabled, and explained without adding another row to the dialog. Submitting a non-empty task starts the worker with a normalized provisional title and returns as soon as spawn succeeds; best-effort title refinement continues independently.

## Claude Code discovery and freshness

Claude Code’s configured model is resolved in this order:

1. project-configured `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
2. process `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
3. `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json`
4. `<project>/.claude/settings.json`
5. `~/.claude/settings.json`

When nothing configures a model, AO makes no guess. Agent inventory refresh is throttled and failure-tolerant; stale model catalogs remain cache-first and revalidate in the background.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test -- src/renderer` — 103 files / 1,434 tests
- `npm run package`
- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- touched backend package tests and race tests
- `gofmt`, locale JSON validation, and `git diff --check`
- Live Electron verification against real `~/.ao/data` with Codex / GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Code / `opus[1m]`
- Live settings edit verified automatic Claude default and fingerprint changes without pressing refresh

## Risks and follow-ups

- Task creation now sends an explicit agent. An unknown resolved agent surfaces `UNKNOWN_HARNESS`, matching a manual selection.
- Title refinement is deliberately best effort; a failure leaves the worker usable under its provisional title.
- Claude discovery adds a read-only, size-bounded settings read. Enterprise-managed policy settings are not included.
- The eight non-English locale updates have not had human translation review.

title: bug(terminal): Ctrl+C does not interrupt processes in standalone shell terminals
body:
## Bug

Ctrl+C does not kill/interrupt the foreground process when typed inside a **standalone shell terminal** (opened via the `+` button, `Ctrl+```, or the `/terminals` screen). The keystroke appears to be swallowed — no SIGINT reaches the shell.

## Expected behavior

Ctrl+C sends `\x03` (ETX) to the PTY, which the shell interprets as SIGINT, interrupting the foreground process — same as in a normal terminal or an agent session pane.

## Likely root cause(s)

The standalone shell input path is identical to the agent session path (`XtermTerminal` → `emitUserInput` → `mux.sendInput` → WebSocket → `attachment.write` → `pty.Write`). The shell and session terminals share the same `TerminalPane`, `useTerminalSession`, and mux bridge. So the difference must be in how the keystroke is intercepted *before* it reaches `mux.sendInput`.

Three candidate interceptors, all of which are stronger on **Windows**:

### 1. Electron menu `{ role: "copy" }` accelerator (Windows/Linux)

`frontend/src/main/menu.ts` installs a role-based menu on non-macOS that includes `{ role: "copy" }`. Even when the menu bar is hidden (`autoHideMenuBar`), the accelerators stay alive (confirmed in `main.ts` comments). On Windows, `{ role: "copy" }` binds to **Ctrl+C** at the Electron/OS level — the keystroke is consumed by Electron's clipboard copy before xterm.js ever sees the `keydown` event. This would explain why Ctrl+C does nothing: Electron copies (nothing selected → no-op) and never forwards the key.

### 2. `forceSelectionMode` + `isTerminalCopyShortcut` (Windows)

`XtermTerminal.tsx:243` calls `forceSelectionMode(term)` for **every** terminal, which forces all mouse interactions into text-selection mode. On Windows, `isTerminalCopyShortcut` (line 115) returns `true` for plain `Ctrl+C` (without Shift). Combined with force-selection, a stray selection from clicking to focus means Ctrl+C is intercepted as copy inside xterm's `attachCustomKeyEventHandler` — returning `false`, preventing xterm from processing it as `\x03`.

Test coverage at `XtermTerminal.test.tsx:343` explicitly asserts this Windows behavior (copies selected text with plain Ctrl+C), confirming it is by design for Windows. But it means Ctrl+C as SIGINT is unreliable whenever any text is selected.

### 3. Visibility/focus gate in `useTerminalSession`

`useTerminalSession.ts:642-648` drops all user input when `optionsRef.current.isVisible === false`. If the standalone terminal's visibility tracking is out of sync (e.g., the pane reports not-visible despite being on screen), every keystroke including Ctrl+C is silently dropped.

## Reproduction

1. Open AO desktop app
2. Open a standalone terminal (`Ctrl+`` ` or the `+` button on the tab strip)
3. Run a long-running command: `sleep 100` or `ping localhost`
4. Press **Ctrl+C**
5. Observe: the process is **not** interrupted (no SIGINT)

## Environment

- Platform: needs confirmation (Windows suspected; behavior may differ on macOS/Linux)
- AO version: latest `main`

## Investigation notes

- Ctrl+C **does** work in agent session terminals (codex/opencode panes) — the bug is specific to standalone shells
- `forceSelectionMode` is already tracked separately in #3640 (mouse reporting suppression), but its interaction with Ctrl+C copy-on-Windows is a distinct issue
- The `onKey` handler at `XtermTerminal.tsx:695` (not `onData`, per the comment at line 690) is the only keyboard→mux bridge — if the key never reaches `onKey`, the mux never sees it

## Suggested fix direction

- On Windows, decouple Ctrl+C-as-SIGINT from Ctrl+C-as-copy: only treat Ctrl+C as copy when there is an **active selection made by the user** (not a force-selection from a click-to-focus), or require Ctrl+Shift+C for copy in terminals (matching native Windows Terminal behavior)
- Verify the Electron menu `{ role: "copy" }` accelerator is not swallowing Ctrl+C before it reaches the renderer — may need a `before-input-event` handler to intercept and re-route Ctrl+C to the focused terminal

title: feat(mobile): PostHog product analytics for the mobile app
body:
Adds product analytics to the mobile app, which had no telemetry of any kind. Mirrors the desktop pattern: pure, unit-tested logic core with a thin SDK edge, so the privacy and volume guarantees hold without a device.

## What it tracks
- `ao.app.active` (client=mobile), once per UTC day, event-driven (launch/foreground), no timer.
- `ao.mobile_app.paired` `{method, from_onboarding}` at both pair chokepoints (QR + manual), plus `onboarding_completed`.
- `ao.mobile_app.connected` `{trigger}` on reconnect.
- `ao.mobile_app.onboarding_started` / `_skipped`.
- `ao.mobile_app.notification_opened` `{target, cold_start}`.
- `ao.mobile_app.feature_used` `{feature, outcome}` around spawn / conductor / merge / kill / restore / send.

## Deliberately not included
- **No error tracking** — that goes to Sentry, by decision.
- **No screen capture** — `enableSessionReplay: false`, the imperative client (no touch/screen autocapture), and `captureAppLifecycleEvents: false`. The only lifecycle signal is the once-daily active heartbeat.
- **No screen-view event** — feature events answer the usage question without a per-navigation stream.

## Privacy
Every event passes an allowlist sanitizer that iterates the allowlist, not the payload, so session titles, PR names, project names, terminal output, and the connection password cannot leak. There is no free-text property kind. An unknown event name is dropped.

## Classification
`client: mobile / mobile-web` on every event, matching the desktop app (`client: desktop`) and CLI (`client: cli`), so shared events like `ao.app.active` split by one property. Identity is the SDK's persisted anonymous per-install id: device-based, never IP.

## Verification
309 unit tests pass, typecheck clean, both load-bearing guards (allowlist fail-closed, daily-active reservation) mutation-checked. The SDK wiring is verified on a device via an EAS build, not in unit tests, that last mile is not exercised here.

body:
Adds `client` to the two surfaces that lacked it: `"desktop"` in the renderer context and `"cli"` in the Go sink's base properties. Mobile already sends `"mobile"` / `"mobile-web"`.

## Why this is a separate PR
This change was written against #3547 but pushed to that branch after #3547 had already merged, so the commit was stranded on the branch and never reached main. This PR lands it cleanly off current main.

## What it fixes
A shared event like `ao.app.active` could previously be split into phone vs laptop only by inferring from the platform value set (ios/android vs darwin/win32/linux), which breaks the day a new platform or a web desktop build appears. Now every surface carries one `client` property, so the split is a single filter across `desktop / cli / mobile / mobile-web`.

The tag rides in the context layer, ahead of the per-event allowlist (same as `app_version`), so it is automatic on every event and cannot be dropped by the sanitizer.

## Verification

Both were confirmed to fail when the tag is removed. Downloads are out of scope (they live in the app stores and GitHub, not PostHog); this classifies active usage.

title: Merge the inspector's two review sections into one list
body:
The session inspector showed AO's own reviewer passes and the reviews left on the PR as two separate sections. A single PR therefore appeared twice, once under each heading, and the reader had to join them up by number to see the whole picture of who had said what about a commit.

They are now one list keyed by PR. Each PR is one expandable row; inside, the groups name their source: **AO codex** against whichever agent actually ran that pass, **On GitHub** for humans and bots. `GithubReviewPanel` is gone.

## Run review

The "This commit has already been reviewed. Push a new commit to run another review." notice was a boxed two-line paragraph. It is feedback about a click, but it outlived the click and kept the rail's width for as long as the panel stayed open.

It is now a one-line `Already reviewed` marker. The sentence is the control's accessible name and shows on hover or focus, so nothing is lost for a screen reader or for anyone who wants the detail, and the resting state costs one line instead of a box.

## Removals

- "No unresolved threads." The unresolved count already rides the PR's own meta line, so the separate sentence only ever appeared when there was nothing to report.
- `inspector.reviewsOnPR` and `inspector.noOneReviewedYet` died with the section that used them.

## Two changes nobody asked for

- Four derivations moved to module level (`openReviewStatesFor`, `runsByPRFrom`, `triggeredReviewStatesFrom`, `aoReviewHarness`). The merged list needs exactly the data `ReviewPanel` was computing privately, and a second copy would have been free to drift from the first.
- `ReviewPanel` loses its `runs` prop, which became dead once the AO list moved out of it.

## i18n

Four keys in, three out, across all eight locales, which `i18n/instance.test.ts` enforces at the type level. `inspector.unresolvedCount` replaces a hardcoded English `` `${unresolved} unresolved` `` in the component, so that string is translatable for the first time.

The seven non-English translations are not from a translator. `inspector.reviewBySource.ao` is deliberately left as `AO {{harness}}` everywhere, since it is a product name plus an agent id.

## Conflicts with #3612

Both changes edit the same few lines of `ReviewsSection`: the auto-inject toggle is inserted immediately after the GitHub section this removes. Whichever lands second resolves by hand.

Separately, #3612 carries migration `0048` while main is at `0079`, so it needs a fresh number regardless of order. If this lands first, the natural resolution is to move the toggle into Run review next to the agent picker, which is arguably where a delivery policy belongs anyway and would give it the section heading it currently lacks.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 87/87 in `SessionInspector.test.tsx` and `i18n/instance.test.ts`, after updating two assertions that named the removed section titles
- exercised in the desktop app against seeded review data

title: fix: stop the session Files diff viewer from freezing on large diffs
body:
## Summary

Opening or scrolling a large file's diff in the session Files panel could block the render thread and spawn redundant git subprocesses per request, making the whole app feel unresponsive. This fixes it end to end, backend and frontend.

**Backend (workspace file/diff serving):**
- Parallelize the independent git subprocess calls in `workspaceChangeMaps`/`workspaceFileSummaries` instead of running them sequentially.
- Add a short-TTL cache for resolved compare/status data (`workspace_cache.go`), invalidated by the workspace filesystem watcher's SSE stream on real changes, so expanding a file right after the list loads doesn't redundantly recompute it.
- Coalesce concurrent cache-miss lookups for the same session/root via `singleflight`, so "Expand All" firing many `GetWorkspaceFile` calls at once shares one computation instead of each spawning its own git calls.
- Fix a misclassification where tracked binary Added files were treated as untracked (`git diff --numstat` omits binary files even when tracked, which isn't the same as being untracked), which produced an incorrect synthetic diff instead of the real one.

**Frontend (`SessionFilesView`):**
- Virtualize the diff row list against the shared scroll container (`@tanstack/react-virtual`) so only rows actually scrolled into view mount, with dynamic per-row measurement for correct heights under line-wrapping at any panel width (docked vs. maximized).
- Memoize per-row rendering and thread the i18n `t` function down instead of every row independently subscribing to the translation context.
- Move diff parsing (`parseUnifiedDiff` + the intra-line LCS highlighting) into a Web Worker for large diffs, with a synchronous fallback if the worker is unavailable; small diffs keep parsing synchronously with no behavior change.
- Reduce the workspace files list's polling interval now that the SSE stream already invalidates it on real changes, cutting redundant backend load.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/httpd/controllers/... ./internal/cli/...` — all pass
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `SessionFilesView.test.tsx` (31 tests, including new coverage for row virtualization and the diff-parser worker fallback path) — all pass
- [x] Production `vite build` — confirms the diff-parser worker bundles correctly as its own same-origin chunk, compatible with the existing CSP
- [ ] Manual verification in the packaged Electron app on a real large diff (recommended before merge)

title: fix(frontend): only confirm busy interface switches in chatUI
body:
## What

Switch idle worker and orchestrator sessions directly between Chat UI and Terminal UI, while retaining the switch-policy dialog for sessions that are actively working or waiting for input.

## Why

The interface-switch action always opened a policy dialog, even when the selected session had no running work. The confirmation is only relevant when switching could interrupt or wait on an active task.

## How

title: feat(mobile): device roster — see, mute, and remove paired phones
body:
## Problem

There was no way to see which phones can receive push notifications from a desktop, and no way to stop one without hand-editing `~/.ao/data/mobile/push-devices.json`. Hand-editing did not even work: the daemon loads the registry into memory once at startup and rewrites the file from memory on the next mutation, so manual edits were silently reverted.

The registry also accumulated duplicates. Rows were keyed by the Expo push token, which rotates without the app being reinstalled, so one phone became several rows — all of which kept receiving notifications until Expo reported the stale token dead.

To be precise about the scope of the fix: keying on a stable install ID removes duplicates caused by **token rotation**. It does not survive a full uninstall/reinstall — the install ID lives in AsyncStorage, which uninstall wipes — so a reinstalled app does still create a new row. What it can no longer do is leave **two rows holding the same token**, which was the harmful part: that meant every notification delivered twice.

## What this adds

A **Devices** section in the Connect Mobile modal that lists every paired phone with:

- a **live** dot when that phone's app is open and in the foreground, or "last seen X ago" otherwise
- a **mute** switch — the device stays paired but receives no notifications
- **remove**, behind a confirmation

## How it works

**Device identity is decoupled from the push token.** The registry now keys on a stable per-install ID, and the token is an optional attribute. A row means *"a paired phone"*, not *"a push registration"* — so a phone that has not granted notification permission (or whose build cannot mint a token, e.g. an iOS build without the APNs entitlement) still appears, as connected with notifications off. The phone announces its identity on connect with no permission gate; the token attaches to that same row later if permission is granted.

**Liveness comes from the phone's existing 8-second REST poll**, not from a new transport. Every request carries an `X-AO-Install-Id` header, a middleware records the timestamp, and "live" means seen within 20s (two poll intervals plus slack). The mobile app pauses polling on `AppState` background — but deliberately *not* on `inactive`, which iOS reports for Control Centre and the app switcher — so backgrounding goes dark deterministically on both platforms rather than waiting for the OS to suspend the JS timer.

The mux WebSocket was deliberately **not** used: it is only open while the user is on a terminal screen, so it would mean "viewing a terminal", not "app is open".

**Removal writes a tombstone.** A removed phone that re-registers comes back *muted* rather than silently resuming notifications, and the tombstone is consumed on match so a deliberate unmute is never overridden. There is no per-device credential to revoke — every phone shares one bridge password — so fully evicting a device remains "regenerate the password and re-pair the phones you want". The UI says so.

## Security

The management routes (`GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/mobile/devices`) are **loopback-only**, mounted under `/api/v1/mobile`, which `lanControlBlockedPrefixes` already blocks on the LAN listener. That gate is enforced by the physical socket the request arrived on, so no header can spoof it, and it required no new gating code. A paired phone cannot enumerate the household's devices, unmute itself, or remove another device.

The phone's own unregister (`DELETE /api/v1/push/devices/{token}`) is unchanged and stays on the shared LAN surface. No new network-facing bind; the loopback listener is untouched.

Registration remains backward compatible: a request without an `installId` gets a server-synthesized `legacy-<uuid>`, which the token-adoption path merges into the real row on the next registration. Phones on older builds keep working — there is no flag day.

## Files worth reviewing

`backend/internal/mobilebridge/pushdevices.go` carries every subtle decision: the three-way `Upsert` resolution (install ID → token adoption → insert), `carryOver` (which preserves mute, created-at and token), tombstone consumption, and the `LoadRegistry` migration.

## Testing

Full suites green: backend (including `-race` on the touched packages), frontend 1976 tests, mobile 337 tests, no OpenAPI/TS drift.

Verified on real hardware (Android + iOS):

- a phone appears as connected with notifications off, before any permission is granted
- granting permission attaches the token to the same row rather than creating a second
- the live dot follows foreground/background, and survives the iOS `inactive` blip
- a notification was received on the device, then **muted and confirmed not delivered** with the device still holding a valid push token
- removing a device, then reopening the app, brings it back muted — and that survives a daemon restart

Not covered: iOS push *delivery*, which needs an EAS build for the APNs entitlement.

## Follow-ups (not blocking)

- `lastSeenAt` is only written on register/announce, so a long foreground session then a background shows a stale "N hours ago". The presence tracker holds the true timestamp; the roster does not read it yet.
- Dead-token pruning deletes the whole row, which contradicts the "a row is a paired phone" model. Clearing the token instead would be model-consistent; today a token death within an hour of a mute can drop that mute.

title: feat(chat): add Codex prompt editing with conversation branches

## Summary

- add Copy and Edit actions to human messages in structured Chat sessions
- support editing for Codex Chat sessions by forking the provider conversation immediately before the selected prompt
- preserve the original conversation as a sibling branch instead of rolling back or deleting later history
- add previous/next branch navigation and persist the active branch across daemon restarts
- keep the existing worktree and its file changes untouched when a conversation branches
- preserve the bottom composer draft while editing inline

## Provider support

- Codex is currently the only provider with targeted conversation-fork support, so Edit is available only for Codex Chat sessions
- the UI is capability-gated; providers without a verified fork implementation do not show Edit
- adding another provider requires a structured fork-or-replay adapter, durable conversation IDs, and reliable resume support
- Copy remains available independently of conversation-fork support

## Architecture

- add a targeted ChatForker provider boundary
- persist conversation branches and active-branch state in SQLite migration 0086
- expose edit/fork and branch-switching operations through the conversation API
- project only the active branch and its ancestry into the rendered timeline
- keep nested lineage cutoffs monotonic and flatten repeated edits into one navigation group

## Behavior and safety

- editing creates a new conversation branch; it does not use provider rollback
- worktree files are never reverted when switching conversation branches
- branch creation is blocked while a turn is active
- failures before branch activation leave the original branch active
- provider send failures leave an empty new branch active and retain the inline draft for a retry on that same branch

title: fix(terminal): stop Windows app menu from stealing Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V in t…
body:
> I think removing the roles is the right approach. The only real alternative would be remapping the accelerators, but that would just steal another shortcut (`Ctrl+Shift+C`) that xterm already uses. Since Electron menu accelerators are static, there's no practical way to enable them only for text inputs.
> I don't see this regressing copy/paste either. Terminals already handle copy/paste themselves, and regular text fields on Windows rely on Chromium rather than Electron menu roles. I'd just do a quick manual check on Windows to confirm copy/paste still works in settings or chat inputs.
> The change is nicely scoped—just removing the two roles and adding a regression test. The only thing still worth verifying before merge is that `Ctrl+C` once again sends `SIGINT` on a real Windows machine, since that's not something the author can test from macOS.

## What

Remove `{ role: "copy" }` and `{ role: "paste" }` from the Windows-only
application menu (`frontend/src/main/menu.ts`), and add a regression test
asserting those roles are never bound (`frontend/src/main/menu.test.ts`).


## Why

On Windows, the Electron app menu installed `role:copy` / `role:paste`, whose
default accelerators are **Ctrl+C** / **Ctrl+V**. Electron resolves application-menu
accelerators in the **main process before** the renderer's `keydown`, so the keystroke
was consumed by the role and never reached xterm.js. As a result `\x03` (ETX → SIGINT)
was never written to the PTY, and a foreground process (`sleep 100`, `ping`) could not
be interrupted with Ctrl+C in a standalone shell terminal (and likewise Ctrl+V paste
was silently dropped).

fixes : #3659

## How

 **Removed `role:copy` / `role:paste`** from `buildWindowsAppMenuTemplate()` (kept
  `undo`/`redo`/`cut`/`selectAll` — they don't collide with terminal SIGINT). With the
  roles gone, Ctrl+C reaches xterm and falls through to `\x03` (SIGINT) when there is no
  selection, and Ctrl+V reaches the existing paste handler.
- **Why remove instead of override the accelerator:** setting
  `{ role: "copy", accelerator: "Ctrl+Shift+C" }` would just move the theft onto
  Ctrl+Shift+C, which xterm already owns for terminal copy (`XtermTerminal.tsx:521`).
  **Gating a menu role on live selection state is not feasible** — Electron menu
  accelerators are static, registered at menu-build time — so removal is the correct fix.
- **Why this is safe for non-terminal text fields:** the "menu must declare copy/paste
  roles for editing shortcuts to work" quirk is **macOS-only**; on Windows/Linux Chromium
  handles copy/paste natively. This menu is `win32`-only (`main.ts:317`) anyway.
- **Copy/paste in terminals is preserved** via: selection auto-copy
  (`XtermTerminal.tsx:550`), Ctrl+Shift+C, Ctrl+Insert, the right-click context menu, and
  Chromium-native in text fields. The visible `WindowTitlebar` Edit menu is a React
  dropdown whose `Ctrl+C`/`Ctrl+V` strings are visual labels only (clicks call
  `act("edit.copy")`, independent of Electron roles) — unaffected.
- **Scope is Windows-only by construction:** `menu.ts` is installed only when
  `process.platform === "win32"`. On macOS/Linux `isTerminalCopyShortcut`
  (`XtermTerminal.tsx:120`) does not match plain Ctrl+C, so SIGINT already worked there;
  this change does not touch those paths.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/main/menu.test.ts src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx`
  → **49/49 pass**. The new guard asserts no `copy`/`paste` role is bound; the existing
  `XtermTerminal.test.tsx:322/343/365` trio still locks the selection-gated copy-vs-SIGINT
  behavior (no renderer change was needed).
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` → no new errors. (Pre-existing, unrelated `code-highlight-engine.ts`
  missing-module errors remain due to stale local `node_modules`; they resolve under CI's fresh install.)
- **Could not reproduce locally** — this machine is macOS, where `menu.ts` is never installed,
  so the bug never reproduces here. Local Ctrl+C working on macOS only proves the non-Windows path
  is untouched.
- ⏳ **Still required before merge (delegated to a Windows machine/VM or the on-call Windows pair
  @illegalcall / @somewherelostt):** in a real Windows build, run `sleep 100` then Ctrl+C in
  (a) a standalone shell and (b) an agent session pane — both must interrupt; plus click-to-focus
  then Ctrl+C (forceSelectionMode) must still send SIGINT; plus copy/paste still works in a normal
  text field.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Linux/AppImage: identity check fails after relaunch-to-update (random /tmp/.mount_agent-* path), app stuck with no sessions and no way to add projects
body:
## Summary

On Linux (AppImage), relaunching the app after an update leaves it permanently stuck on **"AO daemon identity check failed" (`identity_mismatch`)**. The board shows "Could not load sessions." and projects can no longer be added — the app is unusable until the surviving daemon is killed by hand.

The identity check compares the running daemon's `executablePath` against the freshly resolved bundled daemon path. Under an AppImage those paths can never match across two launches, because the AppImage is mounted at a *random* `/tmp/.mount_agent-XXXXXX` path each time it starts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the Linux AppImage build and let the daemon start (a project was already initialized in my case).
2. Switch the update channel to **nightly**.
3. Click **Relaunch to update**.
4. App comes back up.

## Actual behavior

Error toast, and the app is dead in the water:

```
AO daemon identity check failed                      identity_mismatch

Another AO daemon is already running from
/tmp/.mount_agent-1Qs4N6/resources/daemon/ao; expected
/tmp/.mount_agent-mDQfUL/resources/daemon/ao. Stop the other daemon
before using this app.

Stop the conflicting daemon, then restart the desktop app.
```

Board renders "Could not load sessions." and there is no way to add a project, for as long as the status reads `identity_mismatch`. The toast carries no Restart button in that state: `canRestart` in [DaemonFailureBanner.tsx:21](frontend/src/renderer/components/DaemonFailureBanner.tsx#L21) covers `not_ready`, `spawn_failed`, `exited` and `daemon_unreachable`, but not `identity_mismatch` — so the remediation text ("Stop the conflicting daemon, then restart the desktop app") has nothing behind it.

**It does recover on its own, after a delay.** Worth stating precisely, because it caps the severity:

- The old daemon is only alive because its supervisor grace fires ~5s after the previous Electron process exits ([supervisor.go](backend/internal/daemon/supervisor/supervisor.go)). The relaunch lands inside that window and probes a live daemon at the old mount path.
- `useDaemonStatus` re-polls every 2s while not ready ([useDaemonStatus.ts:8](frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useDaemonStatus.ts#L8)). Once the old daemon exits, `refreshDaemonStatus` finds nothing and — since the prior status was an error carrying a pid/port — rewrites it to `daemon_unreachable` ([main.ts:631](frontend/src/main.ts#L631)).
- `daemon_unreachable` *is* in `canRestart`, so a Restart button appears and clicking it spawns a healthy daemon. Relaunching the app instead works equally well.

So the lived symptom is "relaunch-to-update drops you into a dead app for several seconds, with a misleading and unactionable error, until the banner quietly turns into a different one you can act on" — not a permanent brick. Nothing spawns a daemon automatically: `daemon:start`/`daemon:restart` fire only from that button, plus `void startDaemon()` at boot.

Verified on my machine: the mismatched daemon was gone minutes later and the next launch spawned cleanly from a third mount (`.mount_agent-OgFgtF`).

Note this also means the normal healthy path is being lost: attaching would have worked. The supervisor cancels a pending grace timer on reconnect ([supervisor.go:107](backend/internal/daemon/supervisor/supervisor.go#L107)), and the attach path already re-links app-owned daemons, so the relaunch is *designed* to reattach — the identity check is the only thing preventing it.

## Expected behavior

Relaunching to update should reattach to (or cleanly replace) the daemon it spawned. An AppImage relaunching itself is not a "foreign daemon" and should not be treated as one.

## Root cause

`daemonIdentityError` in [frontend/src/main.ts:540-547](frontend/src/main.ts#L540-L547) for `source === "bundled"`:

```ts
if (launch.source === "bundled") {
    if (!probe.executablePath) { ... }
    if (!samePath(probe.executablePath, launch.command)) {
        return `Another AO daemon is already running from ${probe.executablePath}; expected ${launch.command}. ...`;
    }
}
```

`launch.command` comes from `resolveDaemonLaunch` in [frontend/src/shared/daemon-launch.ts:46-52](frontend/src/shared/daemon-launch.ts#L46-L52), which joins `process.resourcesPath` with `daemon/ao`. On an AppImage, `process.resourcesPath` lives under the squashfs FUSE mount, e.g. `/tmp/.mount_agent-1Qs4N6/resources` — and the `.mount_agent-XXXXXX` suffix is regenerated on every AppImage start.

So the path-equality identity check is structurally guaranteed to fail on Linux/AppImage whenever a daemon from a previous launch is still alive. The two paths in the error above differ *only* in the random mount suffix; they are the same binary from the same install.

## Notes / possible fixes

Not prescribing an approach, but the options seem to be:

- Detect the AppImage case (`APPIMAGE` / `APPDIR` env vars are set by the runtime) and identify the daemon by something stable — the `APPIMAGE` path, an install id, or a build/version fingerprint reported by `/readyz` — rather than by the mount-local executable path.
- Normalize/strip the `/tmp/.mount_*` prefix before comparing, so only the in-package suffix (`resources/daemon/ao`) is matched.
- Independently: when the app is relaunching *itself* for an update, the app-owned daemon should be shut down as part of the relaunch rather than surviving into the new process to be rejected.
- Independently of the root cause, `identity_mismatch` should not be a dead end. Since the state already resolves itself into a restartable one seconds later, the cheapest improvement is to stop presenting it as terminal — either add it to `canRestart`, or soften the copy so it does not read as "you must go kill a process by hand".

## Environment

- Linux, AppImage build (`agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`)
- Channel: nightly (failure appeared right after switching from the previous channel and clicking "Relaunch to update")

Confirms the 6-character-prefix caveat above: the AppImage filename starts `agent-`, so every channel built under this name mounts as `.mount_agent-XXXXXX` and the mount name alone cannot distinguish them.

title: fix(frontend): clicking project name to switch to kanban board requires two clicks (orchestrator session)
body:
# Bug: Clicking project name to switch to Kanban board requires two clicks (orchestrator session)

## Summary

When viewing an **orchestrator agent session**, clicking the project name in the
topbar to switch to the kanban board requires **two clicks** — the first click
appears to do nothing, the second navigates. This regressed after the separate
"Kanban" button was removed and the project name became the click target for
board navigation.

## Source

**Reported by:** @prateek in Discord `#bug-triage` thread
**Video:** https://drive.google.com/file/d/17qZgkyDBGCP83lf8pBj0yj3QtUzkWDOP/view?usp=sharing
**Analyzed against:** `f17013b53` (origin/main, Aug 7 2026)
**Confidence:** Medium

## Reproduction

1. Open a project and navigate to its **orchestrator session** (`/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId` where the session is the orchestrator)
2. Click the **project name** in the topbar
3. **Expected:** navigates to the kanban board (`/projects/$projectId`)
4. **Actual:** first click does nothing (or the animation swallows it); second click navigates

## Root Cause

PR [#3490](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3490) (sidebar
animations, merged Aug 5 2026) wrapped the topbar project label in a
`motion.span` with a **shared `layoutId="topbar-project-label"`** and
`layout="position"`:

**`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx`:**

- **Line 183–190** — orchestrator session route label:
  ```tsx
  <motion.span
      layoutId="topbar-project-label"
      layout="position"
      className={topbarProjectLabelClass}
      transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 40 }}
  >
      {projectLabel}
  </motion.span>
  ```

- **Line 213–220** — board route label (same `layoutId`):
  ```tsx
  <motion.span
      layoutId="topbar-project-label"
      layout="position"
      className={topbarProjectLabelClass}
      transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 40 }}
  >
      {projectLabel}
  </motion.span>
  ```

Both labels share the identical `layoutId`. When navigating from the orchestrator
session to the board, Motion's shared-layout animation animates the label's
position from its session-route location to its board-route location. During this
spring animation transition, the first pointer event (click) is consumed by the
layout animation lifecycle rather than reaching the navigation handler. The second
click lands after the animation has settled and successfully navigates.

### Note on navigation wiring

The project label `motion.span` itself has **no `onClick` handler** in the
current code. Navigation to the board is handled by the `openBoard()` function
(line 114–115), which is wired to the separate **"Kanban" `TopbarButton`**
(line 284, `onClick={openBoard}`). This button renders only on the orchestrator
session route (`isSessionRoute && isOrchestrator`).

The reporter indicates the Kanban button was removed in their build and the
project name became the click target. If the project name was given an
`onClick={openBoard}` (or similar) without addressing the `layoutId` animation
conflict, the spring transition would still intercept the first click. The fix
must ensure the click target is not inside an animating `motion.span`, or use
`layout="position"` with `layoutId` disabled during navigation.

## Fix

**Option A (minimal):** Give the project name label a stable wrapper outside the
`motion.span` that handles clicks, so the pointer event isn't captured by the
layout animation. The animation should be purely visual on the inner span.

**Option B:** Remove the shared `layoutId` on the project label when a click
handler is attached — use unique `layoutId`s per route, or drop
`layout="position"` and animate position independently.

**Option C:** Ensure the click target is a sibling `<button>` wrapping the
`motion.span`, so Motion's animation on the inner element doesn't block pointer
events on the outer interactive element.

## Impact

- **Severity:** Core navigation flow broken — users must click twice to return to
  the kanban board from an orchestrator session, every time.
- **Workaround:** Click twice, or use the sidebar project link instead.
- **Frequency:** 100% reproducible per the report.
- **Introduced by:** PR [#3490](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3490) (Aug 5 2026)

## Related

- PR [#3490](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3490) — introduced the shared `layoutId` animation
- PR [#3560](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3560) — topbar layout fix on session page (same area, same author, same day)

title: test(session_manager): fix Windows environment test failures
body:
## What

Fixes environment-specific pathing and mock resolution failures in the `session_manager` test suite that were occurring on Windows. Updates `.github/workflows/go.yml` to include `windows-latest` in the `build-test` matrix.

## Why

Fixes #3681.

Three testing assumptions were breaking `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` for contributors using Windows:
1. `os.UserHomeDir()` mocked exclusively with `HOME` (fails on Windows, which relies on `USERPROFILE`).
2. Hardcoded Unix absolute paths (`/usr/bin`, `/opt/aod`) embedded directly in string assertions.
3. Node `PATH` resolution tests assuming `nodeRuntimeDir` prepended Node binaries to the path, despite the production code correctly short-circuiting and returning an empty string on Windows platforms.

## How

- Extracted a `setHomeEnv(t, home)` helper function in `manager_test.go` and enforced setting both `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` simultaneously to guarantee parity between test setups and OS implementation.
- Replaced all static Unix literals (like `/usr/bin` and `/opt/aod`) with OS-agnostic derivations utilizing `t.TempDir()`.
- Added a `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` guard to `TestSpawnAndRestore_PrependsResolvedBinaryAndNodeDirsToRuntimePATH` to skip the `nodeDir` check on Windows, aligning the test suite's expectations with the production code.

## Testing

Validated via `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` locally on a Windows machine. All tests now cleanly pass (`ok`).
