title: fix(desktop): recognise own daemon across AppImage relaunches via stable AO_APPIMAGE identity
body: ## What Fixes the Linux/AppImage daemon identity check so the desktop app recognises its own daemon across launches. The daemon now reports the stable outer `.AppImage` file path (`AO_APPIMAGE`, set by the Electron app at spawn, echoed as `appImagePath` in `/healthz`/`/readyz`), and the app compares that value when running under AppImage instead of the transient `/tmp/.mount_*` executable path. Outside AppImage the exact `executablePath` comparison is unchanged. Also adds a Restart action to the `identity_mismatch` failure banner so a genuine foreign-daemon conflict is actionable instead of a dead end. ## Why Fixes #3679. On Linux/AppImage, every launch mounts the app at a random `/tmp/.mount_agent-XXXXXX` path. After "Relaunch to update", the surviving daemon (kept alive ~5s by the supervisor grace) reported its executable under the *previous* mount, so the exact-path identity check could never match. The app showed `identity_mismatch`, the board rendered "Could not load sessions", and the banner had no recovery action until the old daemon exited and the status degraded into `daemon_unreachable`. ## How - `backend`: `daemonProbePayload` includes `appImagePath` when `AO_APPIMAGE` is set (dedicated env var, matching the `AO_OWNER`/`AO_APP_RUN_ID` family; no OpenAPI impact — health routes are outside the generated spec). - `frontend/main`: passes `AO_APPIMAGE: process.env.APPIMAGE` to the daemon at spawn; the bundled branch of `daemonIdentityError` delegates to a pure, unit-tested helper. - `frontend/shared/daemon-launch.ts`: new `bundledDaemonIdentityError()` — under AppImage compares the probed `appImagePath` against this process's `APPIMAGE`; otherwise falls back to the exact `executablePath` check. Probes that cannot prove identity fail closed, as before. - `frontend/shared/daemon-attach.ts`: `DaemonProbe`/`parseDaemonProbe` carry `appImagePath`. - `DaemonFailureBanner`: `identity_mismatch` added to `canRestart`. Restart only re-runs attach/spawn; it never kills a daemon this process didn't spawn, so a truly foreign daemon simply re-surfaces the error. Trade-off / rejected alternative: stripping the `/tmp/.mount_*` prefix and comparing the in-package suffix was rejected — the suffix is identical across every build and channel, so it would silently attach to a genuinely different install's daemon. Killing the daemon inside `quitAndInstallUpdate` was rejected as racy and insufficient (doesn't cover crash-restart or quick manual relaunch within the grace window). Known one-time limitation: the first update *into* a build with this fix still hits the old behaviour once (a pre-fix daemon doesn't report `appImagePath`), fails closed for the ~5s grace window, then self-resolves — now with a Restart button. ## Testing - `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/shared/daemon-launch.test.ts src/shared/daemon-attach.test.ts src/renderer/lib/daemon-failure.test.ts` — 49 tests pass, incl. new cases: cross-mount reattach (the bug scenario, using the exact paths from the issue), foreign-install mismatch, and fail-closed when identity is unprovable. - `cd backend && go test ./...` — pass (new `TestHealthProbesIncludeAppImageIdentity` covers `/healthz` + `/readyz` with `AO_APPIMAGE` set and unset). - `golangci-lint` v2.12.2 — 0 issues. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean on touched files. - Not yet verified: the real Linux/AppImage relaunch-to-update flow (needs a Linux machine; the bug cannot be reproduced on macOS/Windows). Reviewer smoke test: launch AppImage → switch channel → Relaunch to update → app reattaches with no `identity_mismatch` banner. frontend tests : backend test (added) : ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Workspace import dead-ends on 48 raw errors: origin/worktree validation too strict + no remediation UX
body:
## Bug

Workspace import blocks users behind a wall of 48 raw errors with no path forward except "Cancel." The user picked a legitimate folder (`~/Desktop/AIOS_coding`) containing multiple git repos, and the import modal became a dead-end error screen instead of a usable flow.

**Source:** [Discord #bug-triage](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1535228014290403368) | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `fb0f85fa4`
**Confidence:** High — traced both the frontend pre-scan and backend validation paths.

## What the user sees

Three screenshots were provided in the Discord report. The import modal shows:

> **IMPORT FAILED · WORKSPACE NOT REGISTERED**
> Workspace child repositories must have an origin remote configured (`WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED`)
>
> ❌ `AIOS_HomeServices` — Origin remote is required.
> ❌ `aios-dashboard-slack-step1` — Linked worktree children cannot be ...
> ❌ `wt-ask-chip-fix` — Linked worktree children cannot be ...
> … (scrollable list of **48** failed repos)
>
> Footer: **"Resolve 48 failed repositories to continue"**
> Only action: **Cancel**

This is a UX dead-end — no "import anyway," no "skip failures," no remediation guidance, no explanation of what a linked worktree is.

## Root Cause

Two layers of over-strict validation combine to block the user, and the frontend renders the failure as an unrecoverable wall.

### Layer 1 — Frontend pre-scan (`frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts`)

`scanGitRepo()` (line 126) runs a hard validation on every child directory:

- **`.git` is a file (not a dir) → instant failure** with `"Linked worktree children cannot be imported."` (line 144). This rejects all git linked worktrees — a legitimate workflow (the user clearly uses `wt-*` worktree dirs).
- `scanRepoValidationReason()` (line 192) hard-fails any repo missing an `origin` remote: `if (!hasRemote) return "Origin remote is required."` (line 203). A local-only repo, a fork without a remote, or a freshly `git init`'d experiment all fail here.

The scan result feeds `CreateProjectFolderDialog` (`CreateProjectFlow.tsx:483`):

```tsx
const failedRepos = scan?.repos.filter((repo) => repo.status === "error" || !repo.hasRemote) ?? [];
```

`failedRepos` drives:
- The error banner (shown when `error` is set, lines 544–558)
- The footer: `"Resolve {{count}} failed repositories to continue"` (line 487)
- **No continue/import button exists** — the only action is `Cancel` (line 609).

### Layer 2 — Backend validation (`backend/internal/service/project/workspace_registration.go`)

Even if the frontend didn't block, `validateWorkspaceChild()` (line 186) enforces the same hard constraints server-side:

- `.git` is a file → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_IS_WORKTREE` (line 193) — hard reject.
- No origin URL → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` (line 217) — hard reject.
- Unborn repo (no HEAD) → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_UNBORN` (line 204).
- No default branch → `WORKSPACE_CHILD_DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNKNOWN` (line 211).

Both layers require **every** child repo to have an `origin` remote and to be a standalone (non-worktree) repo. This is an over-constraint: workspace folders legitimately contain local-only repos, work-in-progress without remotes, and git worktrees.

### Why the UX is a failure (prateek's point)

> "Our UX should never allow users to see such ugly bug messages, it should nudge them towards the right behaviours, and in worst cases, just make decisions for them. They should not be allowed to configure a project in a wrong way in the first place."

1. **Dead-end with no remediation** — 48 errors, only "Cancel." No "import the N valid repos," no "skip failures," no "set up remotes" guidance.
2. **Raw internal error codes** surfaced to end users (`WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED`).
3. **Over-strict validation masquerading as a bug** — a workspace folder with local repos or worktrees is a valid configuration, not an error state.
4. **No prevention at folder-selection time** — the wall appears only after the user has committed to a folder, not as a guided pre-check.

## Proposed Fix

This needs product/UX decisions before implementation. Direction:

### 1. Relax the origin requirement (backend + scan)
Make `origin` optional for workspace children. A child without an origin is included with a `RepoOriginURL` of `""` and flagged as "local only" — SCM operations that need a remote can degrade gracefully. The `WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` hard reject should become a soft warning.

### 2. Allow worktree children (or auto-detect and skip cleanly)
Git worktrees are a legitimate pattern. Either:
- **(a)** Support them as workspace children (register the worktree path), or
- **(b)** Detect them at scan time and silently exclude from the import set with a non-blocking info note ("N worktrees excluded"), rather than flagging as errors.

### 3. Redesign the failure state as a guided flow, not a wall
Replace the dead-end error modal with actionable UX:
- **"Import N repositories" (primary CTA)** — proceed with the valid repos, showing which are included.
- **"Skip M repositories"** — let the user exclude problematic children and continue.
- **Per-repo remediation hints** — e.g., for missing origin: "Click to set up a remote" (or at minimum, a one-line explanation).
- **Human-readable messages** — replace `WORKSPACE_CHILD_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` with "This repository doesn't have a remote configured. [Set up origin]"

### 4. Pre-check at folder selection
When the user picks a workspace folder, run the scan immediately and show a summary ("Found 12 valid repos, 48 need attention") before they commit — not after.

## Impact

- **All users** with workspace folders containing local-only repos or worktrees hit this wall.
- The user in the report has **48 of ~50+ repos failing** — the feature is effectively unusable for their (common) setup.
- P1: core workflow (workspace creation) broken with no safe workaround for affected users.

## Related

- [#2222](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2222) — Complete backend support for workspace projects (tracking issue)
- [#2720](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2720) — UI/UX Audit 1

## Reproduction

1. Create a folder with multiple git repos, some without `origin` remotes and some that are git worktrees (`git worktree add`).
2. In the AO desktop app, create a new project → choose "Workspace" → select that folder.
3. Observe: the import modal shows a wall of errors with only a Cancel button.

title: fix(session): resolve PR fallback compare base to merge-base
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #3203: the Files tab could report far more changed files than a PR actually has (e.g. 2 files on GitHub vs. 36 in AO).
- Root cause: the PR fallback in `resolveWorkspaceCompare` used the provider's current `pr.BaseSHA` (the target branch's live tip) directly, instead of the merge-base of `HEAD` and that SHA. When the target branch advances after a session forks and no diff base is recorded, the raw-SHA diff also picks up every base-only change in reverse, alongside the session's own edits.
- Fix: resolve `git merge-base HEAD pr.BaseSHA` and use that as `CompareBaseSHA`, keeping the PR's target branch as `CompareBaseRef`. File status, numstat, and per-file diff/patch all read from the same `workspaceCompareTarget`, so this single change fixes all three surfaces.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `TestWorkspaceFilesPRFallbackUsesMergeBaseWhenTargetBranchAdvances`, which reproduces the reported scenario (target branch advances independently after the session forks, no recorded diff base) and asserts base-only files are excluded and only the session's own file shows as added.
- [x] `go test ./internal/service/session/...` — pass, including the existing `TestWorkspaceFilesPRFallbackPrefersDefaultTargetPR` (unaffected).
- [x] `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` — clean.
- [x] `go test ./...` — same 3 pre-existing failures reproduce identically on `main` without this change (Windows PATH-separator formatting in `session_manager`, fsnotify timing in `workspacewatch`); unrelated to this fix.

title: feat(auth): add native WorkOS desktop sign-in
body:
## Summary
- add native WorkOS AuthKit PKCE sign-in through the system browser and return to the desktop app through the registered `ao-app://callback` protocol
- encrypt access and refresh tokens with Electron `safeStorage`, deduplicate refreshes, preserve credentials on retryable failures, and make explicit sign-out authoritative over in-flight refreshes

- terminal refresh-token failures clear the session; network, rate-limit, timeout, and server failures retain encrypted credentials for retry
- Linux AppImage protocol registration uses the standard XDG applications and MIME-association locations; AO runtime state remains under `~/.ao`

title: fix(release): stop baking the pre-rename AgentWrapper org into release config
body:
## What

`DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO` in `frontend/forge.config.ts` and `DEFAULT_REPO` in `frontend/src/main/feature-builds.ts` still hardcoded `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` -- the org this repo was renamed away from. Any build path that doesn't set `AO_RELEASE_REPO` explicitly bakes the stale owner into the shipped `app-update.yml`, including `build-artifacts.yml`'s dispatchable unsigned build, which never sets it at all.

Today auto-update only keeps working because GitHub's org-rename redirect (`AgentWrapper` -> `Untrivial-ai`) happens to still resolve. That redirect breaks permanently the moment the still-existing `AgentWrapper` account creates any repo named `agent-orchestrator`, at which point every fleet install baked with the stale owner loses auto-update for good.

## Fix

- `frontend/forge.config.ts`: `DEFAULT_RELEASE_REPO` -> `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`.
- `frontend/src/main/feature-builds.ts`: `DEFAULT_REPO` -> `{ owner: "Untrivial-ai", ... }` (kept in sync with the forge default per its own comment).
- `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml`: set `AO_RELEASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` on the make step, matching the pattern `frontend-release.yml` already uses, so forks and dispatched builds bake their own owner instead of falling through to the production default at all.

## Scope note

This addresses the part of #3523 that lives in this repo. The issue also calls out the external `ao-releases` conductor and a macOS update-e2e regression guard; I don't have access to that conductor repo and don't have a macOS environment to build/verify an e2e guard, so I left both out rather than guess. Happy to take a pass at the e2e guard if someone can point me at how `mac-update-e2e.yml` is normally exercised.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` over the frontend: clean (after `npm ci` to pick up the current lockfile).
- `npx vitest run src/main/feature-builds.test.ts src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`: 61/61 passing, no regressions.
- `.github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml` parsed with `js-yaml` to confirm the edited step is still valid YAML.
- Grepped the touched files for any remaining `AgentWrapper` reference; only the intentional historical note in the `forge.config.ts` comment remains.

I don't have a way to actually run the Electron packaging step or a macOS/Linux release build in this environment, so I wasn't able to verify the baked `app-update.yml` output end-to-end -- the fix is a straightforward default-value substitution plus an explicit env var mirroring an existing working pattern, but flagging that gap for reviewers.

title: Activity timeline events not sorted chronologically
body:
## Bug

The session inspector's **Activity timeline** does not sort events chronologically. Events are displayed in category-group order (Created → Drafts → Opened → Merged → Done) rather than by timestamp, causing recently-opened PRs to appear below older events.

**Reported by:** @prateek in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1535215769460408392)
**Analyzed against:** `f17013b53`
**Confidence:** High — traced exact code path, fix verified by tests

### Screenshot evidence

The reported session shows:

| Position | Event | Timestamp |
|----------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | Working | (live) |
| 2 | Merged PR #3647 | 18h ago |
| 3 | Opened PR #3647 | 1d ago |
| 4 | **Opened PR #3683** | **53m ago** ← most recent historical event, but buried at position 4 |
| 5 | Created workspace | 1d ago |

"Opened PR #3683" (53m ago) should appear at position 2 (just below Working), not position 4.

## Root Cause

`ActivityTimeline` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx` (line 997):

```typescript
const events = [current, ...history.reverse()];
```

The `history` array is built by pushing events in **category groups**:

1. Created workspace
2. All draft PRs (in PR-number order)
3. All opened PRs (in PR-number order)
4. All merged PRs (in PR-number order)
5. Done (if merged)

`.reverse()` simply flips this category order — it does **not** sort by timestamp. When two PRs are in the same category (e.g. both "opened"), they remain in PR-number order regardless of when they were actually opened. PR #3683 (53m ago) gets placed after PR #3647 (1d ago) because 3683 > 3647 numerically within the "opened" group.

This is invisible when a session has only one PR (the category order happens to be chronological), but breaks for any session with multiple PRs opened/merged at different times.

## Fix

Replace `history.reverse()` with a proper reverse-chronological sort by timestamp:

```typescript
const sortedHistory = [...history].sort((a, b) => b.sortTs - a.sortTs || b.seq - a.seq);
```

Each history entry now carries a `sortTs` (epoch ms parsed from `createdAt`/`stateChangedAt`/`updatedAt`) and a `seq` (push order, used as a tiebreaker when timestamps are equal or missing — preserving the semantic grouping as a fallback).

## Impact

- **Severity:** Medium — confusing UX, not data loss. Users rely on the timeline to understand session history at a glance.
- **Affects:** Any session with multiple PRs where events don't happen in PR-number order.
- **Workaround:** None (users see incorrect ordering).

## Test Coverage

- Updated existing test to use realistic timestamps (previously used artificial equal timestamps that masked the bug).
- Added regression test reproducing the exact reported scenario (PR #3683 opened 53m ago vs PR #3647 opened 1d ago).

title: fix(frontend): sort activity timeline chronologically by timestamp
body:
Fixes #3698

## Summary

The `ActivityTimeline` component in `SessionInspector.tsx` built its history array by pushing events in **category groups** (Created → Drafts → Opened → Merged → Done), then called `.reverse()`. This flipped the category order but did **not** sort by timestamp — so a recently-opened PR (e.g. 53m ago) could appear below an older PR (e.g. 1d ago) when both were in the "opened" group.

**Fix:** Replace `history.reverse()` with a proper reverse-chronological sort:
```typescript
const sortedHistory = [...history].sort((a, b) => b.sortTs - a.sortTs || b.seq - a.seq);
```

Each history entry now carries:
- `sortTs` — epoch ms parsed from `createdAt`/`stateChangedAt`/`updatedAt`
- `seq` — push order, used as a descending tiebreaker when timestamps are equal or missing (preserves the semantic grouping: Done > Merged > Opened > Draft > Created)

## Root Cause

`SessionInspector.tsx:997` — `const events = [current, ...history.reverse()];`

The `.reverse()` call only reversed array push order, not chronological order. Within a category group (e.g. two "opened" PRs), events stayed in PR-number order regardless of their actual timestamps.

## Test

- Updated existing ordering test to use realistic SCM summary timestamps (the original used artificial equal timestamps that masked the bug)
- Added regression test reproducing the exact reported scenario: PR #3683 (53m ago) vs PR #3647 (1d ago)

```
cd frontend && npx vitest run src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx
```

All 76 tests pass.

title: fix(desktop): detect wedged updater network stack and nudge restart
body: ## What Hardens the desktop auto-updater against a wedged Chromium network stack (net::ERR_FAILED on every updater request until app restart): 1. Manual "Check for Updates" failures with a Chromium network error (net::ERR_*) now show restart guidance instead of the raw Chromium string. 2. Consecutive automatic-check failures with network-level errors are counted; after 3 in a row (~3h of hourly checks), the Settings → Updates section shows a non-error warning nudge: "Updates haven't been able to check for a while — restarting the app usually fixes this." ## Why Fixes #3526. A long-running app instance can end up with a wedged Chromium network stack. Every updater request then fails with net::ERR_FAILED until the app is restarted. Two UX problems resulted: - Manual checks surfaced the raw net::ERR_FAILED … string with no guidance. - Automatic (hourly) check failures are deliberately UI-suppressed (telemetry only), so a wedged instance went silently stale — the maintainer's instance missed two published nightlies with no visible signal. ## How - `frontend/src/shared/update-telemetry.ts`: new exported `isNetErrorMessage()` (`/^net::/i`, anchored) — the single definition of the wedge signature. Telemetry bucketing already categorized these as "network"; unchanged. - `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`: - `updateRequestErrorMessage()` swaps the raw `net::` string for restart guidance (original message kept in parentheses for diagnostics), applied in both manual-failure paths: the `checkForUpdatesNow` rejection catch and the error-event fall-through in `wireUpdaterEvents`. Hardcoded English in main, matching the existing manifest-404 message convention. - A module-level streak counter increments on net-level automatic-check failures — in the error handler AND in `runAutomaticUpdateCheck`'s own catch (a wedged stack can reject `checkForUpdates()` without emitting an error event). A per-operation guard prevents double counting when one check surfaces both ways. `update-available` / `update-not-available` / `download-progress` reset the streak, since any of them proves the network works. - `broadcast()` (the single status choke point) stamps `staleCheckNudge: true` on outgoing statuses once the streak reaches `STALE_CHECK_NUDGE_THRESHOLD = 3`. The nudge rides on the normal status object, so it never clobbers state and the automatic-failure UI suppression stays intact. - `frontend/src/main/update-settings.ts`: `UpdateStatus.staleCheckNudge?: boolean`. - Renderer: `UpdatesSection.tsx` renders the nudge as a text-warning line (same pattern as the nightly warning), independent of status state; new i18n key `settings.updates.networkStale` added to all 8 locale files. Intentional omissions: - Issue item (3) — investigating whether the wedge is an Electron network-service crash, attempting session recreation, and sizing via PostHog — is investigation-only and out of scope for this PR. - No automatic remediation (e.g. session recreation); this PR is detect + message only. ## Testing - `npx vitest run src/shared/update-telemetry.test.ts src/main/auto-updater.test.ts src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n/renderer-coverage.test.ts` — 76/76 pass, including new cases: - manual check rejecting with net::ERR_FAILED → friendly restart message (raw string preserved in parentheses), both rejection and error-event paths - non-net errors stay verbatim - 3 consecutive net-failed automatic checks → `staleCheckNudge: true` on the restored status; 2 → no nudge - non-net automatic failures never nudge - one check emitting error AND rejecting counts as a single failure - a successful check clears the nudge - renderer: warning line renders with the normal status still shown - `npm run typecheck` — clean for all touched files (only pre-existing lowlight/highlight.js resolution errors in `code-highlight-engine.ts` from missing node_modules in the local checkout; unrelated). Ui changes (before): Ui changes (after): ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(mobile): make Connect Mobile pairing work over Tailscale, including iOS
body:
## Problem

The Connect Mobile dialog has a LAN/Tailscale segmented control, but the toggle only swapped instruction text — the QR always carried the LAN address. A user who selected **Tailscale** and scanned paired their phone to an address it could not reach, and the resulting error told them to check they were on the same Wi-Fi: the exact opposite of what a Tailscale user is doing.

Fixing that surfaced a second, deeper problem. Even with the correct `100.x` address in the QR, **iOS still could not pair**. App Transport Security permits cleartext HTTP only to RFC 1918 ranges, and Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is RFC 6598 — so iOS blocked the request before a packet left the device. Confirmed empirically: Safari (exempt from ATS) reached the address fine while the app reported "Reached nothing". Android was unaffected, since `usesCleartextTraffic` is global.

## What this does

**The QR now follows the mode.** LAN encodes the LAN address; Tailscale encodes the Tailscale address.

**A new opt-in "Secure pairing (TLS)" mode** solves iOS. The desktop runs `tailscale serve` to front the bridge with Tailscale's own certificate, and the QR carries the MagicDNS hostname on port 443 with `secure: true`. HTTPS to a cert-backed domain satisfies ATS outright — **no ATS exception, no `app.json` change, nothing to justify at App Store review** — and the traffic becomes genuinely encrypted rather than relying on WireGuard alone, so the "not encrypted" warning is correctly suppressed in that mode.

Two pre-existing bugs are fixed along the way:

- With no address available, the modal used to encode `host: ""`, which the app rejects as *"not an AO pairing code"* — an incoherent error for a QR the desktop generated itself. It now shows an explanatory hint instead.
- A scan overrode host/port/password but **inherited `secure`**, and the `v: 1` payload had no way to clear it. A user who enabled TLS manually and then scanned a LAN QR silently kept `secure: true`, hit the same misleading error, and stayed stuck across restarts because the flag is persisted.

## Compatibility

**The payload stays at `v: 1`, and `secure` is emitted only when true** — every plaintext QR is byte-identical, so no already-installed build regresses. Secure pairing is off by default, so an older build only ever sees a QR it understands.

## The one adoption caveat

Secure pairing needs **HTTPS certificates enabled on the tailnet** (admin console → DNS), which is not on by default, and the `tailscale` CLI on `PATH` (App Store installs of Tailscale don't add it). The feature detects both, plus a missing MagicDNS name and a failed proxy, and shows targeted setup steps rather than a QR that cannot connect. Where it isn't usable, it degrades to today's plaintext behaviour — which still works on Android.

## Design notes worth a reviewer's attention

- **The bridge has no fixed port.** `LANManager.Start` falls back to an ephemeral port when its default is taken (observed: bound `54014` because another instance held `3011`). A `serve` config pinned to a stale port is this feature's primary failure mode, and `serve` config persists inside `tailscaled` across restarts. `Apply` is therefore called with the port `Start` *actually returned*, on every listener start — enable, password rotation, and boot restore. Boot restore routes through `BridgeService` for this reason rather than driving the listener directly.
- **A `serve` failure never takes the bridge down.** It is recorded and surfaced as a reason while the bridge stays up in plaintext mode.
- **`reason` is a fixed enum**, never a raw error string — raw errors are untranslated and can leak filesystem paths to the UI.
- **`serve`, never `funnel`** — the proxy is tailnet-only; nothing is publicly exposed. `/api/v1/mobile` remains 404 on the LAN listener by prefix, so the new route is unreachable from the network with no extra work, and the pairing password never leaves loopback.

## Testing

Automated: backend packages pass with `go vet`/`gofmt` clean; renderer 1448/1448; mobile 349/349; `tsc --noEmit` clean in both TS packages.

Verified on real hardware (macOS + iPhone 13 + Android):

- Secure scan on iPhone **over cellular with Wi-Fi off** — pairs with no typing, including the `/mux` terminal WebSocket.
- Flip back to LAN and re-scan — connects, confirming the stale-`secure` trap is gone.
- Android regression check — both modes still pair.
- Desktop restart with secure pairing on — the proxy re-points at the new bridge port with no re-scan.
- Security: `/api/v1/mobile` returns 404 over the Tailscale address and over the LAN address; unauthenticated data routes 401; authenticated 200.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not here

- Emitting `no_magicdns` distinctly — `tailscale status` cannot distinguish a missing CLI from disabled MagicDNS, so both currently surface as `no_cli`, whose copy covers both.
- Automatic enabling of HTTPS certificates or MagicDNS: both are tailnet-wide administrative changes AO should not make on a user's behalf.

title: Chat session cannot resume after its controller stops
body:
## Summary

When a Chat-mode agent controller stops, the desktop can show **The agent controller stopped**, but clicking **Resume agent** fails with:

> The agent is still running; only exited agents can be resumed (AGENT_NOT_EXITED)

This leaves the preserved conversation unrecoverable from the advertised recovery action.

![Controller stopped banner and AGENT_NOT_EXITED error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-controller-resume-conflict/docs/issue-assets/chat-controller-resume-conflict.png)

## Source

Reported from the desktop app in a local user session on 2026-08-07/08. No public chat URL is available. The screenshot above is the original report attachment.

Analyzed against `main` at `f7e0fe65bd6fda711f39642798c70b9f0da248df`.

## Reproduction

1. Start and use a Chat-mode agent session.
2. Let the Chat controller stream close without a successfully projected explicit `chat.controller.stopped` event (or let it stop while lifecycle activity is `blocked`).
3. Observe the controller-stopped recovery banner.
4. Click **Resume agent**.

## Expected

The stopped Chat controller is reflected as exited lifecycle activity, and **Resume agent** relaunches the Chat controller using the preserved provider conversation.

## Actual

The durable session may remain `idle`, `active`, or `blocked`, so resume rejects it with `AGENT_NOT_EXITED`. Even if activity is corrected to `exited`, Chat resume then fails because the generic resume path requires a terminal runtime handle, which Chat sessions intentionally do not have.

## Root cause

High confidence, backed by focused failing regression tests:

1. `service/chat.Controller.project` marks only its in-memory controller state stopped when the provider event stream closes; it does not report lifecycle `exited` unless an explicit stopped event was projected first.
2. Lifecycle tool precedence suppresses `chat.controller.stopped` while the current activity is `blocked`, because that event is not classified as a turn boundary.
3. `session_manager.ResumeAgentWithMode` unconditionally requires a `RuntimeHandleID`, even though Chat-mode sessions intentionally launch without terminal runtime handles.
4. Existing sessions already stuck in a non-exited durable state need safe reconciliation: recovery should be permitted only when the Chat controller registry confirms there is no live controller.

## Proposed fix

- Always report lifecycle `exited` when a Chat controller event stream ends.
- Treat `chat.controller.stopped` as a lifecycle turn-boundary event so it can clear `blocked` state.
- Make resume preconditions mode-aware: retain terminal runtime-handle requirements for TUI, but relaunch Chat without one.
- For stale pre-fix records, allow Chat recovery only when no live controller exists; continue returning `AGENT_NOT_EXITED` for a genuinely live controller.
- Add focused tests at the Chat controller, lifecycle, and session-manager boundaries.

## Impact

Affected users cannot recover some Chat sessions from the desktop despite the UI explicitly offering **Resume agent**. The workaround is to abandon the preserved session and start another one or manually open a shell.

## Related, not duplicate

- #3360 — parent structured Chat-mode work
- #3087 — broader remaining session lifecycle correctness gaps

title: fix: recover Chat sessions after controller stops
body:
## What

- report Chat lifecycle `exited` whenever the provider event stream ends, including abrupt disconnects without a final controller-state event
- allow `chat.controller.stopped` to clear sticky `blocked` activity
- make agent resume mode-aware so Chat sessions relaunch their provider conversation without a terminal runtime handle
- recover stale pre-fix Chat activity only when no live controller exists, and wait for a stopped controller's final cleanup before replacement

## Why

The desktop can correctly show **The agent controller stopped** while **Resume agent** fails with `AGENT_NOT_EXITED`. Some sessions remain durably idle/active/blocked after their Chat controller dies; sessions that do reach exited then fail the TUI-only runtime-handle precondition.

## How

The controller's provider-stream closure now emits the same generation-fenced lifecycle signal as an explicit stopped event. Lifecycle treats that event as a turn boundary so a dead controller cannot remain blocked.

Session Manager keeps TUI resume semantics unchanged. For Chat, the in-memory controller registry prevents duplicate recovery of a live controller and permits stale durable rows to recover when no controller remains. The Chat service distinguishes a stopped registry entry from a usable controller and waits for its projector cleanup before launching the replacement generation.

No frontend or API contract changes are required; the existing recovery action works once daemon state and resume semantics agree.

title: New-task composer discovers TUI-only agents only after failed Chat spawn
body:
## Bug

When Chat is the default session interface and a user selects a TUI-only agent such as Cursor, the new-task composer sends a guaranteed-to-fail Chat request. It then renders the raw SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED backend error and only afterward offers Create as Terminal UI.

AO already knows Cursor is TUI-only before submission, so the composer should choose the supported interface automatically.

![Cursor selected, followed by a raw unsupported-Chat error and delayed Terminal UI fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-proactive-chat-tui-fallback/.issue-assets/proactive-chat-tui-fallback/report.png)

**Source:** local desktop report on 2026-08-08 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** local user  
**Analyzed against:** f7e0fe65bd6fda711f39642798c70b9f0da248df  
**AO version:** dev  
**Platform:** macOS arm64  
**Priority:** medium  
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Set the default session interface to Chat.
2. Open the new-task composer.
3. Select Cursor, which has no Chat driver.
4. Choose Start task.
5. Observe SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED and the delayed Terminal UI retry.

## Root Cause

- The daemon already returns defaultSessionMode and chatHarnesses from GET /api/v1/settings.
- TaskComposer did not consume that capability metadata.
- It only offered TUI after the delegate request returned a typed Chat preflight error.

## Fix

- Resolve the effective interface from defaultSessionMode, chatHarnesses, and the selected agent before submission.
- If Chat is the default but the selected agent has no Chat driver, send the delegate request once with mode tui.
- Keep the ordinary Start task UI; do not show a warning or alternate action.
- Preserve the existing server-error fallback for stale or unavailable capability metadata.

The backend contract remains explicit: the frontend sends mode tui rather than asking the backend to silently reinterpret a Chat request.

## Impact

- Removes a guaranteed failed request and raw backend error.
- Starts TUI-only agents in one click.
- Keeps interface selection out of the way when there is only one supported option.

- #3360 — Chat and TUI interface architecture
- #3472 — Chat UI and typed post-failure recovery

title: fix(opencode): detect agent exit via AO's process supervisor
body:
## Problem

The `opencode` adapter does not implement `ports.AgentExitDetector`, so it falls back to runtime-only liveness.

AO launches every seat as:

```
bash -c '<agent> ...; exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i'
```

The trailing interactive shell is deliberate — it keeps the pane usable after the agent finishes. But it means the tmux pane **outlives the agent process**, so `tmux has-session` keeps answering "alive" long after `opencode` has exited or been killed.

Consequences observed on a worker seat whose agent was killed:

- the reaper never observes a dead worker, so the session is never marked terminated;
- `session restore` then refuses the session as not-restorable, because AO still believes it is alive;
- the seat is effectively unrecoverable without manual intervention.

Fixes #2089.

## Fix

Opt `opencode` into `AgentExitDetectionSupervisor`, exactly as the `codex` adapter already does (`adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`). The launch argv is then wrapped in `ao agent-process supervise`, which reports the real process exit back to the daemon, and `RuntimeLaunchID` is populated so the workload-death signal is no longer fenced off.

This is the mechanism AO already ships; the adapter simply was not opted in.

## Verification

Built from this branch and run as an isolated daemon (separate port, data dir, run file and `TMUX_TMPDIR`), against a scratch git repo:

1. Spawned an `opencode` worker seat; confirmed it did real work in its worktree.
2. `kill -9` on the `opencode` process.
3. **Before the patch:** session stayed `running` indefinitely; the tmux pane was still alive, and `has-session` still reported alive.
4. **After the patch:** session moved to `exited` within a few seconds of the kill, while the pane remained (as intended).
5. The seat could then be recovered in place via `POST /sessions/{id}/activity {"state":"exited"}` followed by `POST /sessions/{id}/resume-agent`, and the resumed agent wrote a new file into the preserved worktree — so the session became genuinely restorable, not merely relabelled.

`go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/...` passes, including the added case.

## Notes

- No behaviour change for any other adapter.
- One incidental finding while testing, reported separately rather than folded in here: `respawnPaneArgs` targets `<session>:0.0` unconditionally, so on a machine with `base-index 1` / `pane-base-index 1` in `~/.tmux.conf` the pane is `1.1`, and `resume-agent` fails with `can't find window: 0`. That is independent of this fix and needs its own change (a tmux target that does not assume index 0, e.g. `{start}.{top-left}`); happy to open a separate PR for it.

body:
## Bug

Switching an idle Terminal UI session to Chat UI with the drain policy can remain at **Waiting to switch…** forever when terminal input is newer than the last durable idle activity fact.

**Source:** Interactive report with screenshot on 2026-08-08  
**Analyzed against:** `f7e0fe65bd6f`  
**Priority:** P2 — interface switching is significantly degraded, but Cancel and Stop now remain safe workarounds.  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced with a permanent regression test and traced through the terminal input barrier and session transition loop.

## Reproduction

1. Open an idle Codex session in Terminal UI.
2. Type and erase a character at the composer without submitting a turn, leaving the composer visibly idle.
3. Select **Switch to Chat UI**.
4. Observe the transition remain in the draining phase with **Waiting to switch…** indefinitely.

## Root Cause

`BeginInputDrain` correctly records the newest terminal input accepted before closing the input gate. The TUI drain then rejects an idle activity fact older than that barrier, because buffered PTY input could still be processing.

Codex does not emit a new activity hook for non-submitting input, and same-state idle reconciliation does not refresh the idle timestamp. The drain loop therefore had neither a second authoritative idle signal nor a deadline for this contradictory stale-idle state. Trusting the old row would be unsafe because a just-submitted turn could be destroyed; waiting only for a newer row causes the permanent hang.

## Expected

The transition should either prove the source is quiescent and switch, or fail safely while leaving the source controller available. It must not wait forever or infer runtime death from a failed probe.

## Fix

- Gate terminal input before checking quiescence.
- Preserve the existing path for an idle fact newer than the last accepted input.
- For a contradictory stale-idle row, wait for a post-input quiet window and require three consecutive adapter-confirmed idle samples.
- Use one cumulative five-second deadline for terminal capture and runtime liveness checks.
- On unresolved ambiguity, fail with `DRAIN_QUIESCENCE_UNVERIFIED`, release the input gate, and leave the source running.
- Keep reported active turns and user-paced decisions unbounded and cancellable.

## Intentional Scope

No confirmation dialog or unsent-draft warning is part of this fix. Draft policy remains unchanged.

## Verification

Session-manager tests cover the stale-idle reproduction through the detector port, fresh durable idle facts, unavailable and ambiguous detection, alternating samples, the liveness deadline, confirmed runtime exit, input-gate release, cancellation, source preservation, and Active/WaitingInput/Blocked states. Existing Codex adapter tests continue to cover idle, working, approval, and ambiguous terminal markers.

title: fix(session): prevent stale-idle interface drain hangs
body:
## What

Prevent TUI-to-Chat drain transitions from waiting forever when accepted terminal input is newer than the last durable idle fact.

## Why

The input gate correctly rejects that stale idle row because buffered PTY input might still submit work. Non-submitting Codex input produces no newer hook, however, so the transition previously had no safe proof path and no bound.

title: Chat timeline shows image attachments as file paths instead of previews
body:
## Bug

When a PNG is attached to a message in a chat-mode session, the composer stages it successfully and the agent can read it, but the human message in AO's transcript shows AO's generated attachment instruction and workspace-relative file path as literal text. The transcript never renders the image.

**Source:** In-app AO chat report on 2026-08-08  
**Reported by:** AO desktop user  
**Analyzed against:** `f7e0fe65bd6f` (`origin/main`, frontend `0.10.3`, daemon version `dev`)  
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64; verified Go daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P2 — the attachment still reaches the agent, but the visible conversation is degraded and the only workaround is opening the staged path separately.  
**Confidence:** High — a deterministic renderer regression test exercises the exact persisted message shape and fails because the human-message component emits text only.

![Chat message rendering the attachment as a path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-image-attachment-path/.issue-assets/chat-image-attachment-path/attachment-path-in-chat.png)

## Reproduction

1. Open a chat-mode AO session.
2. Paste, drop, or choose a PNG in the chat composer.
3. Send the message.
4. Inspect the human message in the conversation timeline.

### Actual

The bubble contains text like:

```text
Attached files (read these files in the workspace):
- .ao/attachments/attachment-d9014f798f.png
```

No image element is rendered.

### Expected

AO should render staged image references as inline image previews while retaining the file in the worktree for the agent.

## Deterministic repro

```bash
cd frontend
npm test -- src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx -t "renders staged image references in human messages as images"
```

The test fails with `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "img"` and shows the generated reference block as the bubble's complete DOM text.

## Root Cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx` intentionally appends staged paths to the outgoing text because worktree files are the provider-neutral delivery mechanism.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` exposes conversation messages with `text` but no structured display attachment metadata.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx` renders `HumanMessage.message.text` verbatim and does not recognize AO's generated attachment suffix.
- The existing workspace-confined `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/preview/files/*` route can serve the bytes, but the packaged renderer CSP currently does not allow loopback image sources.
- Spawned prompts use the closely related header `Attached files (read these files in the workspace for context):`, so both AO-generated variants need coverage.

## Fix

Parse only AO's terminal attachment-reference block in human messages, render supported staged image types through the existing session preview-file route, show non-image attachments as file labels, and preserve malformed or ordinary user text unchanged. Pass the session ID through the timeline and allow the already-trusted loopback daemon origin in `img-src`. Add regression coverage for both generated header variants and URL encoding.

## Impact

- Images still reach agents, so there is no data loss.
- Users cannot visually verify which screenshot/image they sent from the transcript.
- Image-only messages appear as internal implementation instructions rather than the intended content.

## Related

- [#2722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2722) — original task-composer attachment request; adjacent composer behavior, not transcript rendering.
- [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — structured Chat/TUI session work that introduced the current chat surface.

title: docs: move README translations into translations/
body:
## What

Moves the seven translated READMEs out of the repo root into a dedicated `translations/` folder, and relocates the language switcher row into the centered header block of every README.

## Why

The repo root carried eight `README*.md` files. On GitHub's file listing they crowd out the actual project directories, and it isn't obvious which one GitHub renders. Grouping the translations under one folder keeps the root to a single `README.md`.

Separately, the language row sat *outside* the `<div align="center">` header, so it rendered left-aligned and orphaned between the hero screenshot and the first `---` — easy for a non-English reader to scroll past.

## How

- `git mv README.<lang>.md translations/` for `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN` (detected as renames, not delete+add).
- Rewrote relative paths inside the moved files: `LICENSE`, `docs/*`, `assets/*`, `frontend/*` links and image `src` attributes are now `../`-prefixed. Sibling language links stay relative within `translations/`.
- Root `README.md` language row now points at `translations/README.<lang>.md`; translated files point back at `../README.md`.
- Moved the language row inside `<div align="center">`, directly under the badge block, so it renders centered and above the fold.
- Dropped the `**Languages:**` label. It was hardcoded English in every localized README; the language names identify themselves without it.

No content translation changes — only paths and placement.

## Testing

- Grepped the repo for references to the moved filenames: only the READMEs themselves referenced them. No workflow, script, `package.json`, or `.gitattributes` entry points at them.
- Verified every relative link and image `src` in the moved files resolves from `translations/`.
- `git diff --numstat` shows 45 changed lines per translated file (link rewrites + header row) and 2 in the root README — no incidental reflow or line-ending churn.

title: fix(browser): prevent cancel-frame race from flaking Go CI
body:
## Bug

The race-enabled Go suite can intermittently fail because `TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame` times out waiting for the browser runtime cancel frame. The same race can leave an Electron browser command running after its caller has canceled the request.

**Source:** [failed `main` Go run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/31251765230) after [PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) merged  
**Failure commit:** `b264e7765`  
**Reproduced against:** `a3fbf8850`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P2 — intermittent CI failure and bounded browser-command cancellation leak; rerunning CI is a workaround.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd backend
GOMAXPROCS=1 go test -race ./internal/browserruntime \
  -run '^TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame$' -count=300
```

The original test failed twice in an initial 100-iteration run. Independent 300-iteration runs failed under `GOMAXPROCS=1`, `2`, and `8`. A deterministic `net.Pipe` regression reproduces it by pausing immediately after the runtime receives the command bytes and canceling before the broker's write call returns.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/browserruntime/broker.go` checks `ctx.Err()` after the complete command frame has already been written. If cancellation lands in that narrow interval, `write` reports `context.Canceled`; `Broker.Execute` treats the command as unsent and returns through its early write-error path, so it never emits the required cancel frame.

The write-interrupt `context.AfterFunc` also was not joined before the connection deadline was cleared, allowing its expired deadline to race with the next write.

[PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) did not introduce this code; its merge run exposed the pre-existing race from [PR #3066](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3066).

## Fix

- Treat a fully delivered frame as a successful write even when cancellation arrives concurrently, so `Execute` reaches its cancellation branch and sends the correlated cancel frame.
- Wait for an already-started deadline-interrupt callback before clearing the connection deadline.
- Replace the timing-dependent cancellation test with a deterministic post-delivery interleaving.

## Impact

- Removes a flaky failure from required Go CI.
- Ensures a delivered browser command receives a cancel frame when its request context is canceled.

## Related

- [PR #3066](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3066) — introduced the browser runtime bridge.
- [PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) — unrelated merge whose `main` run exposed the flake.

title: fix(browser): preserve cancel frames after delivered writes
body:
Fixes #3732

## Summary

- preserve a successful browser-runtime write when request cancellation arrives after the complete command frame has been delivered
- wait for an already-started write-deadline interrupt before clearing the connection deadline
- make the cancel-frame regression deterministic by pausing immediately after the fake runtime receives the command bytes

## Root cause

`Broker.write` checked `ctx.Err()` after writing the complete command frame. If cancellation landed between delivery and the write returning, `Execute` treated the command as unsent and exited through its write-error path without emitting a cancel frame. The runtime could keep executing the browser command, and `TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame` intermittently timed out.

[PR #3727](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3727) did not introduce the bug; its [`main` Go run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/31251765230) exposed the pre-existing race from the browser bridge.

## Test

```bash
cd backend
go test -race ./internal/browserruntime -run '^TestBrokerCancellationSendsCancelFrame$' -count=1000
go test -race ./internal/browserruntime -count=100
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test -race -p 4 -count=1 ./...
cd ..
GOFLAGS=-p=4 npm run lint
```

## Risk

Low. The change is limited to the daemon's serialized browser-runtime write path. Incomplete writes retain the existing context/error behavior; only fully delivered frames are treated as successful so `Execute` can send their correlated cancellation.

title: fix: align Chat recovery with TUI lifecycle
body:
## What

- make Chat controller startup follow TUI's prepare/start/commit/release ordering
- publish connecting-controller ownership before any fallible post-provider work, while gating provider event projection until `MarkSpawned` commits the generation
- distinguish controller liveness from registry ownership so stopped or failed-to-close controllers still prevent duplicate recovery and workspace teardown
- treat every authoritative `ActivityExited` signal as a lifecycle turn boundary, independent of whether TUI or Chat reported it
- align Chat kill, restore, resume, and failed-spawn cleanup with TUI's one-controller and workspace-safety rules

Follow-up to #3711. Fixes parity and rollback gaps found while comparing that recovery path directly with TUI lifecycle behavior. Relates to #3710.

## TUI parity

| Lifecycle invariant | TUI | Chat after this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One controller owns the session | runtime handle and launch generation | controller registry owner and controller generation |
| Signals cannot beat durable launch commit | pending-launch gate | connecting controller plus activation gate |
| Durable launch completion | `MarkSpawned` records runtime metadata | `ControllerReady` calls the same `MarkSpawned` with provider metadata |
| Authoritative death signal | process supervisor/reaper emits `ActivityExited` | provider event-stream closure emits `ActivityExited` |
| Failed stop protects workspace | runtime destroy must succeed before teardown | registry ownership must be released before teardown |
| Duplicate recovery is rejected | live runtime/generation guard | live or cleanup-owning controller guard |

The mechanisms remain adapter-specific: TUI has a terminal runtime and reaper; Chat has a provider process, conversation ID, controller registry, and event stream. The durable lifecycle ordering and safety invariants are now shared.

## Behavior covered

- a provider event emitted immediately at startup cannot overwrite or precede `MarkSpawned`
- commands cannot reach a connecting, uncommitted controller
- an uncommitted generation's buffered provider events are discarded
- a generation-claim or lifecycle-commit failure retains ownership if provider close times out
- a second start/restore cannot create another provider writer while ownership remains
- failed spawn or kill cannot destroy a workspace still owned by a provider
- stream closure clears blocked state through generic exited semantics
- stale pre-#3711 Chat rows remain recoverable when no controller owner exists

## Testing

- `GOFLAGS=-p=1 npm run lint` — pass, 0 issues
- `cd backend && go build ./...` — pass
- `cd backend && go test -race -p 1 ./internal/service/chat ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/session_manager ./internal/daemon` — pass
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — pass

## Checklist

- [x] Based on current `main`
- [x] Focused follow-up to #3711
- [x] Regression tests cover lifecycle ordering, duplicate ownership, failed cleanup, and workspace preservation
- [x] No frontend or API contract changes

title: fix: recover Codex interface switch readiness
body:
## Summary

- invoke Codex lifecycle hooks with the running AO executable's absolute, shell-quoted path, so Codex's login shell cannot redirect callbacks to a stale or foreign `ao`
- recheck only the transient `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` interface status, allowing **Switch to chat UI** to enable as soon as a successful `SessionStart` hook records the thread id
- implement Codex's native-history probe so a reserved UUID with no active rollout starts fresh instead of issuing a doomed `thread/resume`

## RCA

Three independent gaps produced two similar-looking symptoms:

1. **The native id never arrives for some users.** Codex runs command hooks through the user's login shell. AO previously emitted bare `ao hooks codex ...` commands and only prepended the daemon directory to the child process's inherited `PATH`. A login-shell startup file can replace or reorder that `PATH`; the hook then invokes another AO installation (or no AO), exits, and never records the native Codex thread id. This depends on each user's shell setup, which explains why only some users reproduce it indefinitely.
2. **The renderer can cache an early missing-id response.** Even when the hook succeeds, the initial interface-status request can race the asynchronous `SessionStart` callback. The query returned `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`, but idle status queries did not refetch, leaving the button stale until some unrelated remount/refetch.
3. **A UUID is not necessarily resumable history.** Codex app-server can reserve and return a thread UUID before the first user turn writes an active rollout. AO treated every non-empty Codex UUID as resumable, passed an unmaterialized id to `thread/resume`, and surfaced `no rollout found for thread id ...`.

## Why the earlier fixes did not cover this

- #170 prepended AO's daemon directory to the spawned session `PATH`. That helps ordinary child-process lookup, but it does not survive a login shell that reconstructs `PATH` before running a hook.
- #3711 recovers a stopped Chat controller. It does not make a missing Codex rollout resumable and therefore cannot fix `no rollout found`.
- #3719 prevents a stale-idle transition drain from hanging. It is a separate transition-lifecycle failure.
- #3717 changes frontend chat links/text selection and is unrelated.

## Reproduction and evidence

### Real desktop reproduction on `main`

1. Launch the actual AO Electron app against an isolated data directory.
2. Start a Codex 0.147 TUI session and send `Reply with only OK`.
3. Observe Codex return `OK`, while **Switch to chat UI** remains disabled and Activity shows **No Signal**.
4. In the reproduced shell, `zsh -lc 'command -v ao'` resolves a stale package-manager shim; invoking it exits 1 because its old module target no longer exists. Therefore the `SessionStart` callback never reaches this daemon.
5. To isolate the second bug, record the valid native id directly. The daemon then reports `{supported:true,targetMode:"chat"}`, but the already-mounted UI remains disabled because it never refetches the earlier `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` result.

### Real desktop verification on this branch

1. Start the same Codex flow from the fixed app.
2. Inspect the live launch command: every Codex hook contains the absolute daemon executable and the isolated daemon run-file environment.
3. Send the same prompt. The real `SessionStart` callback records the native id, the button becomes enabled, and Activity becomes **Idle**.
4. Click **Switch to chat UI**. The transition completes and Chat UI displays the original `Reply with only OK` prompt and `OK` response. The reverse **Switch to terminal UI** control is enabled.

### Automated regression evidence

- Before the absolute-path implementation, the launch/restore command tests failed because the generated hook command still contained bare `ao hooks ...`; after the change, the same tests pass with the current AO executable embedded.
- The renderer regression test starts at `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`, advances the mocked daemon to `supported: true`, and proves the hook refetches exactly once. A second test proves permanently unsupported harnesses are not polled.
- Session-manager tests prove a missing Codex rollout uses the fresh-conversation sentinel, while a non-empty active `.jsonl` rollout preserves the native id.
- Adapter tests additionally cover missing, zero-byte, archived, active, and compressed active rollout files.

## Change-by-change necessity

| Change | Required? | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Absolute, shell-quoted AO hook executable | Yes | Fixes the indefinite, user-specific failure where no native id is ever recorded. Quoting is required for packaged paths such as `Agent Orchestrator.app`. |
| Error propagation from launch/restore | Yes | A session launched without working tracking hooks recreates the same unrecoverable disabled state. Failing the launch is safer and diagnosable. |
| Targeted one-second `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` poll | Yes | Absolute hooks can still finish after the first HTTP read; polling closes that legitimate async race. It stops immediately when ready and never runs for permanently unsupported harnesses. |
| Codex active-rollout probe | Yes | Prevents `thread/resume` from receiving an id that Codex has reserved but cannot resume. |
| Missing/zero-byte/archived vs active/compressed tests | Yes | These are the exact provider states that decide whether continuity is safe. |
| Frontend permanent-unsupported test | Yes | Guards the UX/performance boundary: Cursor and other unsupported harnesses must not begin background polling. |

No API, schema, storage, or UI-component change is needed.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/codex ./internal/session_manager -count=1`
- `go test ./...` (via the repository lint command)
- focused `golangci-lint` for the changed backend packages: `0 issues`
- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run package` (production Electron bundles and macOS package)
- actual AO Electron + Codex 0.147 TUI-to-Chat handoff against isolated data

The repository-wide linter process also scanned stale sibling worktrees on this machine and reported pre-existing/generated findings from those other paths. The changed packages themselves lint clean, and CI remains the clean-checkout authority.

body: Fixes [#3714](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3714) ## Summary - `ao project set-config` did a full replace — any field not supplied was silently wiped to its zero value, with no warning. A routine one-setting change (e.g. updating the model) would drop unrelated settings like env vars, worker config, and setup commands. - `buildProjectConfig` now starts from the current config fetched via GET and overlays only flags the user explicitly passed (using cobra's `Changed()` check). - `--config-json` deep-merges into the existing config instead of replacing it wholesale. - A new `--replace` flag opts into the old full-replace behavior for users who want it. `--clear` still wipes everything. - Help text updated: "Set" → "Update", mentions merge-by-default and `--replace`. ## Tests - `cd backend && go test ./internal/cli/... -run TestProjectSetConfig -v` (7 passed) - `cd backend && go test ./internal/cli/... -run TestBuildProjectConfig -v` (1 passed) - `cd backend && go test ./internal/cli/...` (full CLI suite passed) - `cd backend && go vet ./internal/cli/...` ## Manual verification Verified against a local daemon: setting `--env FOO=bar` then later `--model claude-opus-4-5` preserves `FOO=bar` (was silently wiped before). `--replace` restores old behavior. `--config-json` with a partial object merges into existing config. `--clear` still wipes everything.

title: fix: sanitize project IDs derived from folder names with dots/special chars
body:
## Summary

When a user runs `ao start` in a directory like `llama.cpp`, the derived project ID would fail validation with:

```
Error: [
  {
    "validation": "regex",
    "code": "invalid_string",
    "message": "Project ID must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ (no dots, slashes, or special characters)",
    "path": [
      "projects",
      "llama.cpp"
    ]
  }
]
```

## Changes

- Modified `defaultProjectID` in `backend/internal/service/project/service.go` to:
  1. Replace non-alphanumeric characters (except `_` and `-`) with hyphens
  2. Trim leading/trailing hyphens/underscores that could violate validation
  3. Fall back to "project" for edge cases (e.g., folders with only special chars)

## Test Cases

| Input | Output | Valid |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `llama.cpp` | `llama-cpp` | ✓ |

| `test@domain` | `test-domain` | ✓ |
| `special!@#$chars` | `special-chars` | ✓ |
| `.config` | `config` | ✓ |
| `@myproject` | `myproject` | ✓ |
| `---test---` | `test` | ✓ |
| `...` | `project` | ✓ |

- All existing tests pass: `go test ./internal/service/project/... -race`
- Build passes: `go build ./...`

Fixes #1877

fix: reject spawn for closed/cancelled tracker issues
body:
## Summary

Running `ao spawn <issue-number>` on a **closed or cancelled issue** proceeds through the entire spawn pipeline — session ID reservation, worktree creation, tmux pane, and agent launch — without ever checking whether the issue is still open. This spawns a full session on already-resolved work.

## Changes

- **Gate the spawn on issue state** inside `withIssueContext` (`backend/internal/service/session/issue_context.go`), the single funnel for CLI, HTTP and dashboard spawns. When the fetched issue is in a terminal state (`done` or `cancelled`), return `apierr.Conflict` `ISSUE_CLOSED` before any session/worktree/tmux is created.
- **Factor the terminal-state predicate** onto `domain.NormalizedIssueState.IsTerminal()` so `lifecycle` and the session service share one source of truth instead of a duplicated inline check.
- **`Service.Spawn`/spawn** propagate the error instead of proceeding to `manager.Spawn`.

`in_progress` and `review` issues still spawn normally (matches `isTerminalTrackerState` in `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`).

## Test coverage

- `TestSpawnRejectsTerminalIssueState`: done and cancelled issues return `ISSUE_CLOSED` and never reach `manager.Spawn`.
- `TestSpawnAllowsInProgressIssueState`: an in-progress issue still spawns.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `go test ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` — pass
- `go vet ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/lifecycle/...` — clean
