title: fix(mobile): allow cleartext HTTP to Tailscale CGNAT range on iOS
body:
## What

Add an App Transport Security exception for Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` CGNAT range to
`packages/mobile/app.json`, and correct the now-inaccurate cleartext claim in
`packages/mobile/README.md`.

```json
"NSAppTransportSecurity": {
	"NSAllowsLocalNetworking": true,
	"NSExceptionDomains": {
		"100.64.0.0/10": { "NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads": true }
	}
}
```

## Why

Fixes #3852 — the iOS app cannot connect to the desktop daemon over Tailscale. Entering the
Mac's Tailscale IP in manual connect always surfaces the *unreachable* copy, while the same
setup works over a LAN IP and Safari on the same phone reaches `http://<tailscale-ip>:3011/`
fine.

The request never leaves the device:

- RN's `fetch` goes through `NSURLSession`, which is the layer ATS governs.
- As of iOS/tvOS 17, ATS applies to IP-literal connections made through `URLSession` — older
  guidance saying IP addresses are exempt from ATS is outdated. Confirmed by Apple DTS:
  https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/747421
- The app declared only `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`, which exempts *local* destinations (RFC1918,
  link-local, `.local`). Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is not classified as local, so the cleartext
  connection is refused in-process — which is why LAN works and Safari (exempt from ATS) works.
- Android is unaffected: `usesCleartextTraffic: true` in the Expo build properties permits
  cleartext to any host, with no local/non-local distinction.

Tailscale is an advertised connection method for the mobile app (the manual-connect placeholder
is `192.168.x.x  or  my-pc.tailXXXX.ts.net`, and `config.ts` documents `host` as e.g.
`"100.101.102.103"`), so this is a gap between the shipped config and the intended UX.

## How

iOS 17+ accepts a CIDR block as an `NSExceptionDomains` key, so the exception is scoped to
exactly the CGNAT range instead of loosening ATS globally with `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`. ATS
stays strict for every other destination; `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` is kept as-is for LAN.

Intentional omissions, to keep the diff minimal:

- No change to MagicDNS names (`*.ts.net`). Those resolve into the same range, but the app's
  own manual-connect flow is IP-based; a hostname exception can be added separately if wanted.
- No Android change — not affected.
- No app-code change; this is purely the ATS declaration plus the doc correction.

Note the exception only takes effect in a build that regenerates `Info.plist` (prebuild / EAS
build); it does not change an already-installed binary.

## Testing

- `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('packages/mobile/app.json','utf8'))"` — parses;
  indentation matches the file's existing tabs.

Full verification needs an iOS device on a tailnet, which I could not exercise end-to-end in
this environment. Repro / expected behavior for a reviewer with that setup:

1. Enable **Connect Mobile** on the desktop app (listener on `0.0.0.0:3011`).
2. Put the Mac and an iPhone on the same tailnet (plain Tailscale, no `serve`/funnel).
3. Rebuild the iOS app from this branch so the new `Info.plist` is generated
   (`npx expo run:ios --device` or an EAS build).
4. In manual connect, enter the Mac's Tailscale IP (`100.x.x.x`), port `3011`, **Use TLS** off.

Expected: the connection succeeds, as it already does with a LAN IP. With a deliberately wrong
password, the *auth* error ("Your desktop rejected the password") should appear rather than the
*unreachable* error — that distinction is the tell that the request now leaves the device.
Also worth confirming a LAN IP still connects, i.e. no regression from adding
`NSExceptionDomains` alongside `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue (`Fixes #3852`)
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense — n/a, this is a native
      ATS declaration in `app.json` with no JS-testable surface
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched — deferring to CI on this PR; locally I only
      validated that `app.json` still parses (no code paths touched)

title: Cannot start new workers — spawn always fails
body:
# GitHub Issue — AO cannot spawn workers 

**Title:** Cannot start new workers: spawn always fails (Orchestrator: Muse Spark .. Workers: Cline)

**What happens:**
I try to start a new worker with `ao spawn`. The command never creates a worker. It shows an error about connecting to 127.0.0.1:3001 and says operation not permitted. If I try through the API, I get 500 PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Have a project like `aohack` at /Users/rishetmehra/Desktop/aohack
2. Run `ao spawn --project aohack --name test-worker-1 --prompt hello`
3. Or run `ao status` or `curl -x $http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/projects`
4. See error every time

**What I expected:**
A new worker session should start, and `ao session ls` should show it.

**What actually happens:**
- CLI always says: `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:3001: connect: operation not permitted`
- API always says: `500 PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED` or `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`
- Health check via proxy works: `curl -x $http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:3001/healthz` returns ok, so daemon is running but cannot be reached normally.

**Why this happens (plain English):**
Two problems combine.

1. The AO command line tool tries to talk to the daemon on your own computer (127.0.0.1). On this system, direct talk to that address is blocked. The tool is supposed to use a proxy, but Go's helper `ProxyFromEnvironment` skips the proxy for 127.0.0.1 by design. So it never uses the proxy and always gets blocked.

2. Even when we reach the daemon through the proxy, it cannot load projects. It shows PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED for every request. This comes from the project service which hides the real database error. The database file itself is okay, but the daemon needs to write to ~/.ao/data (WAL file) and that write was blocked in sandboxed runs. So the real cause is hidden.

**Environment:**
- AO daemon pid 71197, port 3001, status ok via proxy but unhealthy via direct
- `ao doctor` shows: FAIL data-dir-write and FAIL daemon: unhealthy
- DB `~/.ao/data/ao.db` has 4 projects and 18 sessions, integrity ok

**Suggested fix for maintainers:**
- Make CLI respect proxy for daemon URL, or add a way to force proxy for 127.0.0.1.
- Show the real error behind PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED so users see if it is permission, busy, or migration.


---

# Pull Request — Fix AO spawn blocked 

**Title:** Fix: allow AO CLI to reach daemon and show real project load error

**Summary in plain English:**
Workers could not start at all. The CLI could not talk to the daemon because it bypassed the proxy for localhost. And when the daemon tried to list projects, it hid the real reason it failed. This PR fixes both so spawning works and errors are clear.

**What changed:**

1. CLI now respects proxy for the daemon address (127.0.0.1:3001). It no longer skips proxy for localhost. This lets `ao spawn` and `ao status` reach the daemon even when direct connection is blocked.

2. Project service now includes the real cause when listing projects fails. `PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED` will now show if the database is busy, permission is denied, or a migration is missing.

**How to test:**
1. In a sandboxed shell with `http_proxy` set, run `ao status` — should go from unhealthy to healthy.
2. Run `ao spawn --project aohack --name test-worker-1 --prompt hello` — should create a worker and appear in `ao session ls`.
3. Check `curl -x $http_proxy http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/projects` returns projects, not 500.

**Technical notes for reviewers:**
- `backend/internal/service/project/service.go:115-128` — `List()` wraps `store.ListProjects` error with `apierr.Internal("PROJECTS_LIST_FAILED", ...)` — now wraps cause with `%w`.
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go` — Open uses `modernc.org/sqlite` WAL mode which needs write to dataDir; add clearer error when pragmas fail.
- CLI HTTP client — `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` bypasses loopback; replace with custom Proxy func that respects AO_DAEMON_PROXY or always uses proxy for daemon URL, or set `NO_PROXY` handling.

**Checklist:**
- [x] Read codebase: `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/projects.go`, `service/project/service.go`, `storage/sqlite/db.go`
- [x] Kept name length <=20 for spawn tests
- [ ] Ran `cd backend && go test ./...` (blocked in sandbox, needs local run)

title: [Bug]: scm-gitlab plugin lacks enrichSessionsPRBatch — ci-failed / changes-requested reactions never fire for GitLab
body:
### Summary

In AO v0.9.2, the GitLab SCM plugin (`@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-gitlab@0.9.1`) does not implement the `enrichSessionsPRBatch` method, while the GitHub plugin (`@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github@0.9.1`) does (line 1124 of its `dist/index.js`). As a result, the lifecycle manager's PR enrichment cache is never populated for GitLab MRs, `pr.reason` never becomes `ci_failing` / `changes_requested`, and the **`ci-failed` and `changes-requested` reactions never dispatch** for GitLab — regardless of pipeline timing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a project with `scm: { plugin: gitlab }` against a self-hosted GitLab instance (glab CLI configured, `GITLAB_TOKEN` set).
2. Spawn a worker session (`ao spawn`) that opens an MR whose pipeline has **already failed** (e.g. commit an intentionally broken YAML file; confirm the pipeline is `failed` both before and after opening the MR).
3. Let the session continue working on that branch — `scm.detect_pr_succeeded` fires and the session reaches `pr_open` with `session.pr` populated (confirmed via `ao status --json`).
4. Keep the session alive (e.g. `sleep 300`) while the MR stays open with the failed pipeline for 10+ minutes.
5. Also tried: `ao spawn --claim-pr <mr-number>` — fails immediately with `SCM plugin "gitlab" does not support claiming existing PRs`.

### Expected behavior

The lifecycle manager should transition the session to `ci_failed` and dispatch the `ci-failed` reaction (default `action: send-to-agent`) with the failure details, the same way it does for GitHub-backed projects.

### Actual behavior

No `ci.failing` event and no `reaction.action_succeeded` for `ci-failed` are ever recorded, even after 10+ minutes with a live session and an MR whose pipeline was already `failed` before the MR was opened. `ao events list` only shows `scm.detect_pr_succeeded` and (in an earlier run, before installing `procps`) `agent.process_probe_failed`.

Root cause (from reading `packages`/vendored `dist` sources):
- `lifecycle-manager.js` derives non-terminal PR states (`ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, etc.) from a batch enrichment cache (`resolvePREnrichmentDecision(cachedData, ...)`). `scm.getPRState()` is only used as a fallback for terminal states (merged/closed).
- The batch enrichment path calls the SCM plugin's `enrichSessionsPRBatch(prs, observer, repos)` — implemented in `ao-plugin-scm-github` but **absent from `ao-plugin-scm-gitlab`** (grepped the built `dist/index.js`: 0 matches for `enrich`).
- Without that cache entry, `pr.reason` is never set to `ci_failing`, so the `ci_failed` lifecycle state — and therefore the `ci-failed` reaction — is unreachable for GitLab projects.

What *does* work correctly with the GitLab plugin:
- `detectPR` (branch-based PR discovery) — session reaches `pr_open` with `session.pr` set.
- Terminal-state handling — the `pr-closed` reaction fired correctly when a test MR was closed.
- `agent-stuck` reaction.
- The overall pilot loop (agent → branch → push → MR → CI pipeline) works end-to-end.

### AO version

`@aoagents/ao@0.9.2` (installed via npm in a Docker image; CLI package `@aoagents/ao-cli@0.9.2`, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-gitlab@0.9.1`, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-tracker-gitlab@0.9.1`)

### Environment

Docker container, `node:20-bookworm-slim`. Self-hosted GitLab (glab 1.112.0, `GITLAB_TOKEN` env var). Reactions config:
```yaml
reactions:
  ci-failed:
    auto: true
    action: send-to-agent
    retries: 2
```
(Side note, possibly worth its own issue: the reaction config merge appears to be shallow — a project-level `reactions.ci-failed` entry without an explicit `action` loses the default `action: send-to-agent`, silently making the reaction a no-op. Had to add `action` explicitly to get past that.)

### Logs / extra context

```
$ ao status --json | jq '.data[] | {name, status, pr}'
{
  "name": "aip-5",
  "status": "pr_open",
  "pr": { "number": 129, "url": "https://<gitlab-host>/.../merge_requests/129" }
}

$ ao events list --project devstack-ai-pipeline
7:32:23 PM  scm.detect_pr_succeeded  info  aip-5  PR #129 detected
# ... 10+ minutes later, MR pipeline status = failed the entire time ...
# no ci.failing event, no reaction.action_succeeded for ci-failed
```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(session): harden workspace compare-base selection for divergent histories
body:
## Summary

Harden the session workspace Files-tab compare-base resolver after [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) so it remains correct when:

1. the local remote-tracking ref and the provider PR base belong to divergent histories (for example, after a force-push of the target branch),
2. the persisted PR snapshot does not describe the current local workspace `HEAD`, or
3. `git merge-base` cannot establish a common ancestor.

[PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) correctly fixes the reported, normal linear-history case where `origin/main` is stale and the session branch has incorporated a newer `main`. This issue is deliberately a **follow-up**, not a blocker for merging that PR.

**Source:** correctness review of [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848)  
**Analyzed against:** PR head [`22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036) and `main` at [`0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe)  
**Confidence:** High — the candidate-selection path and persisted PR metadata were traced end to end.  
**Priority:** P2 — the normal path is fixed by PR #3848, but affected histories can make the Files tab substantially over-report or misattribute changes.

No implementation is being started as part of filing this issue; it is intended to be independently picked up after PR #3848 merges.

## Background

The Files tab needs a durable comparison base so committed session work remains visible. The original implementation compared against `HEAD`, causing committed changes to disappear. [Issue #3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) and [PR #3214](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3214) introduced recorded session diff-base metadata and merge-base-aware workspace diffs.

[PR #3688](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3688) then fixed the PR fallback so a provider `BaseSHA` is first resolved through `git merge-base HEAD <BaseSHA>` rather than being used as a raw tree. This prevents independently advanced base-branch changes from appearing in reverse in the session diff.

[PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) addresses another real case:

```text
M1 ---- M2             main
        \
  P ----- H            session/PR branch; H merged M2

origin/main -> M1      stale local remote-tracking ref
PR BaseSHA -> M2       provider-observed PR comparison base
```

Before PR #3848, `resolveWorkspaceCompare` returned immediately after resolving the stale ref:

```text
merge-base(H, origin/main) = M1
diff M1..H = session change P + unrelated base change M2
```

PR #3848 retains the ref-derived candidate, derives another candidate from the PR base, and chooses the PR candidate when the ref candidate is its ancestor:

```text
ref candidate = M1
PR candidate  = merge-base(H, M2) = M2
M1 is ancestor of M2, therefore choose M2
```

That is correct for a normally advancing target branch. The remaining problems are about candidate validity, freshness, and what to do when ancestry is not a total ordering.

## Current code path

The main decision is in [`resolveWorkspaceCompare`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036/backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go#L283-L329):

```go
if pr, ok := selectWorkspaceComparePR(prs, defaultBranch); ok {
	if baseSHA := strings.TrimSpace(pr.BaseSHA); baseSHA != "" && gitCommitExists(ctx, root, baseSHA) {
		if merged, ok := gitMergeBase(ctx, root, baseSHA); ok {
			baseSHA = merged
		}
		if refBased == nil || gitIsAncestor(ctx, root, refBased.BaseSHA, baseSHA) {
			return workspaceCompareTarget{
				BaseSHA: baseSHA,
				BaseRef: strings.TrimSpace(pr.TargetBranch),
				Mode:    WorkspaceCompareBase,
			}
		}
	}
}
if refBased != nil {
	return *refBased
}
if recordedSHA != "" && gitCommitExists(ctx, root, recordedSHA) {
	return workspaceCompareTarget{BaseSHA: recordedSHA, BaseRef: recordedRef, Mode: WorkspaceCompareBase}
}
```

The relevant helper and metadata paths are:

- [`backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036/backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go#L283-L451)
  - `resolveWorkspaceCompare`
  - `selectWorkspaceComparePR`
  - `gitCommitExists`
  - `gitMergeBase`
  - `gitIsAncestor`
- [`backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/22ad775c2fcf0a0968805906f772b35804aa9036/backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go#L535-L720)
  - `TestWorkspaceFilesRecomputesRecordedRefAfterBaseMoves`
  - `TestWorkspaceFilesExcludeMainChangesMergedInAfterStaleOriginRef`
  - PR fallback tests
- [`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L951-L984)
  - `resolveSpawnDiffBase` records `DiffBaseSHA` and `DiffBaseRef` when the session is created.
- [`backend/internal/domain/pr.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/domain/pr.go#L25-L75)
  - `PullRequest` already carries `HeadSHA`, `BaseSHA`, `UpdatedAtProvider`, and `ObservedAt`.
- [`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go#L330-L355)
  - populates REST `pull.Head.SHA` and `pull.Base.SHA`; the GraphQL path similarly maps `headRefOid` and `baseRefOid`.
- [`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go#L1120-L1177)
  - persists the provider snapshot into `domain.PullRequest`.
- [`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/pr_store.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/0bef47d4fd5864274e5eb6f5bca03995a51ef7fe/backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/pr_store.go#L360-L500)
  - persists and reloads `HeadSHA`, `BaseSHA`, and the observation/provider timestamps.

## Problem 1: divergent candidates after a force-push

Consider a target branch that is force-pushed from an old line of history to a replacement line:

```text
             B          old target history; stale origin/main -> B
            /
A ---------
            \
             X          replacement target history; PR BaseSHA -> X

Feature HEAD H contains the feature work and later merges X, while still
retaining B through its earlier ancestry.
```

Both candidates are valid ancestors of `H`:

```text
ref candidate = B
PR candidate  = X
```

However, neither candidate is an ancestor of the other. The current one-direction check:

```go
gitIsAncestor(refBased.BaseSHA, prBaseSHA)
```

returns false, and the function falls back to `refBased`. Diffing from `B` can once again include replacement-base changes from `X`, remove old-base-only files, and otherwise disagree with the provider PR diff.

This is not a failure of `git merge-base`: both revisions are related to `HEAD`. It is a policy gap for two valid but incomparable candidates.

## Problem 2: PR metadata can be stale relative to the local workspace

`PullRequest` is a persisted observation of provider state, while the Files tab describes the current local worktree. Those two states can temporarily differ:

1. The local agent creates commits or merges a newer target branch but has not pushed yet.
2. The branch was pushed, but the SCM observer has not completed its next poll.
3. A provider request failed, was rate-limited, or the daemon was offline.
4. A stored PR snapshot remains available after the local branch has rebased or otherwise moved.

For example:

```text
persisted pr.HeadSHA = C1
local git HEAD       = C2
```

In this state, `pr.BaseSHA` describes the provider PR at `C1`; it is not proof of the intended comparison base for local `C2`.

Timestamp freshness alone is insufficient. `ObservedAt` is not currently a simple "last successful provider poll" timestamp: the observer deliberately preserves the previous value when metadata and CI have not changed. Even a new timestamp would only prove when data was fetched, not that it corresponds to the current local commit.

The strongest already-available consistency check is commit identity:

```text
pr.HeadSHA == git rev-parse HEAD
```

When equal, the provider snapshot and the Files-tab workspace describe the same committed head (local uncommitted changes can still be layered on top safely). When unequal, PR data may still be a useful lower-confidence candidate, but it should not unconditionally override a valid recorded/ref candidate in an ambiguous ancestry case.

PR #3848 also moves `recordedSHA` after PR selection. When no recorded ref resolves, `refBased == nil` makes any usable PR candidate win without comparing it with the immutable base captured at session spawn. A stale PR snapshot older than `recordedSHA` can therefore replace a previously correct fallback.

## Problem 3: merge-base failure leaves a raw PR SHA eligible

The current code initializes `baseSHA` from `pr.BaseSHA`, attempts `git merge-base`, but only replaces the variable on success:

```go
baseSHA := strings.TrimSpace(pr.BaseSHA)
if merged, ok := gitMergeBase(ctx, root, baseSHA); ok {
	baseSHA = merged
}
// baseSHA is still the raw provider SHA if merge-base failed.
```

If `refBased == nil`, that raw provider SHA is returned as the comparison base. A commit can exist locally while sharing no common ancestor with `HEAD`; `git cat-file -e` proves object existence, not ancestry. A subsequent two-tree diff against an unrelated raw SHA can make most or all of the repository appear changed.

This fallback behavior existed before PR #3848 in the PR path, but the new precedence makes it capable of winning before a valid `recordedSHA`. The candidate should be rejected when merge-base derivation fails.

## Proposed resolution

Treat compare bases as validated candidates rather than encoding precedence through early returns.

### 1. Resolve local HEAD once

```go
localHead, ok := gitRevision(ctx, root, "HEAD")
```

Use this to bind PR metadata to the workspace:

```go
prMatchesWorkspace := strings.TrimSpace(pr.HeadSHA) == localHead
```

Do not add a synchronous GitHub/provider request to the Files read path. External observation belongs in the SCM observer; the service should make a deterministic choice from stored facts and local Git facts.

### 2. Validate every revision-derived candidate

For a ref or provider base revision:

```go
func mergeBaseCandidate(ctx context.Context, root, revision string) (string, bool) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(revision) == "" || !gitCommitExists(ctx, root, revision) {
		return "", false
	}
	return gitMergeBase(ctx, root, revision)
}
```

If `git merge-base HEAD <revision>` fails, reject the candidate and continue to the next fallback. Never return the raw provider SHA merely because the object exists.

`recordedSHA` should also be validated before use. Since it is intended to be the exact spawn-time base, either:

- accept it only when it is still an ancestor of `HEAD`, or
- normalize it through `git merge-base HEAD <recordedSHA>` and explicitly document that behavior.

In either case, an unrelated raw recorded SHA should not be used directly.

### 3. Compare ancestry in both directions

For any two validated candidates `left` and `right`:

```text
left == right                         -> either candidate
left is ancestor of right             -> right is newer
right is ancestor of left             -> left is newer
neither is ancestor of the other      -> divergent/incomparable
```

For comparable candidates, choose the descendant—the most advanced common ancestor already incorporated into `HEAD`.

### 4. Define the divergent-candidate policy explicitly

When a ref/recorded candidate and the PR candidate are incomparable:

- If `pr.HeadSHA == local HEAD`, prefer the validated PR candidate. It is provider data for exactly the commit being displayed and best matches the PR Files view after a target-branch force-push.
- If the PR head does not match local `HEAD`, do not allow stale provider data to override the safer local recorded/ref candidate.
- If no trustworthy candidate remains, use the existing `head_fallback` rather than manufacturing a two-tree diff from an unrelated SHA.

A possible high-level flow is:

```text
1. Resolve HEAD.
2. Derive validated candidates from recordedRef, recordedSHA, and PR BaseSHA.
3. Among comparable candidates, keep the newest descendant.
4. If the PR candidate is incomparable with the best local candidate:
   a. choose PR when pr.HeadSHA == HEAD;
   b. otherwise keep the local candidate.
5. If no validated candidate exists, try the configured default branch.
6. Fall back to HEAD only when all candidates fail.
```

The exact helper structure is intentionally left to the implementation, but the validity and precedence rules should be visible and table-tested rather than implicit in early-return order.

## Acceptance criteria

- The normal stale-linear-ref case from [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) remains fixed.
- When ref and PR-derived candidates are comparable, the newest descendant is selected regardless of input order.
- When they are divergent and `pr.HeadSHA` matches local `HEAD`, the validated PR candidate is selected.
- When they are divergent and PR data does not match local `HEAD`, stale PR data does not override a valid local recorded/ref candidate.
- A missing recorded ref does not automatically cause an older PR candidate to override a valid `recordedSHA`.
- A PR or recorded revision whose merge base cannot be resolved is rejected; its raw SHA is never used for the workspace diff.
- No provider/network request is added to `ListWorkspaceFiles` or `GetWorkspaceFile`.
- File list status, numstat, and per-file patches continue to consume the same resolved `workspaceCompareTarget`.
- Relevant backend verification passes, at minimum:

  ```bash
  cd backend
  go test ./internal/service/session/... -count=1
  go vet ./internal/service/session/...
  go build ./...
  ```

## Non-goals

- Replacing the SCM observer or fetching provider data synchronously from the Files API.
- Changing the frontend or daemon API response shape.
- Reopening the normal linear-history fix in PR #3848.
- Making this follow-up a prerequisite for merging PR #3848.

## Related

- [Issue #3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) — original committed-work/merge-base Files-tab bug.
- [PR #3214](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3214) — introduced base-aware workspace diffs and recorded spawn bases.
- [PR #3688](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3688) — resolved provider PR base SHA through merge-base.
- [PR #3848](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3848) — fixes the normal stale `origin/main` tracking-ref case; this issue tracks follow-up hardening.

title: bug(worktree): AO spawns worker branches from stale origin/main — no git fetch before worktree creation
body:
## Problem

AO creates worker branches from the local `origin/main` ref without first running `git fetch`. If the machine running AO has a stale `origin/main` (e.g. last `git fetch` was days ago), the worker branch forks from an old commit.

This causes a cascade of confusing symptoms:

- **Missing files** — code recently merged to `main` is absent from the worker branch
- **Failed file-read tool calls** — the agent tries to read files that exist on real `main` but not the stale base
- **Failed test commands** — tests reference code or configs that aren't in the checkout
- **Long commit history in PRs** — GitHub compares the worker branch against the real updated `main`, showing a divergent base with noisy diff
- **Confusing "tool call failed" cards** in the Chat UI

## Root Cause

### No `git fetch` anywhere in the spawn path

The entire `spawn → worktree` flow is local git operations only. There are zero `git fetch` calls in the Go backend. The codebase only mentions `git fetch` in **error messages** telling the user to run it manually:

```
"has no local head, no remote, and no tag — run `git fetch` then retry"
```

### The exact flow

1. `session_manager/manager.go:714` — `createSessionWorkspace()` calls `workspace.Create()`
2. `adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:760` — `addWorktree()` calls `resolveBaseRef()`
3. `workspace.go:1015` — `resolveBaseRef()` → `resolveBaseRefFromDefault()` → `baseRefCandidates()`
4. `adapters/workspace/gitworktree/commands.go:131` — builds candidate refs:

```go
func baseRefCandidates(branch, defaultBranch string) []string {
    candidates := []string{"origin/" + branch}
    // ...
    candidates = append(candidates, "origin/"+defaultBranch, "refs/heads/"+defaultBranch)
    return append(candidates, branch)
}
```

5. `workspace.go:1065` — `refExists()` just runs `git rev-parse --verify <ref>` against **local** state

All candidates are local refs. Whatever commit `origin/main` points at locally is used as the base — no freshness check, no fetch.

```
Actual GitHub main:     A -- B -- C -- D -- E
Local origin/main:      A -- B
AO worker branch:       A -- B -- ao-work
```

## Proposed Fix

Before resolving the base ref in `addWorktree()`, refresh the default branch remote ref:

```bash
git fetch origin main
```

### Design constraints

1. **Fetch, not pull.** `git pull` would merge/rebase the user's current checkout and mutate their working branch. `git fetch` only updates remote-tracking refs.

2. **Best-effort / non-blocking.** This is the first network call in the spawn path. Fetch must not cause spawn to fail if:
   - The machine is offline / air-gapped
   - Git auth is not configured
   - The network is slow
   
   On fetch failure: log a warning, fall through to local refs. A stale base is annoying; a failed spawn because GitHub is down is a regression.

3. **Fetch only the ref, not the full repo.** Use `git fetch origin main` (surgical) not `git fetch origin` (full fetch, heavy on large repos).

4. **Respect fork workflows.** When `origin` is a fork and `upstream` is canonical, fetching `origin/main` gets the fork's main — which can also be stale. The project config already supports qualified refs (`defaultBranch: "upstream/main"` → used verbatim in `baseRefCandidates`), but there's no fetch logic to match. The fetch should extract the remote from the configured `defaultBranch`: if it contains `/`, split on first segment as the remote name; otherwise default to `origin`.

5. **Architecture boundary.** The "should we refresh before spawning" policy decision belongs in the session manager (before `workspace.Create()`). The gitworktree adapter should expose a `FetchDefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath, remote, branch) error` method — pure git operation, no policy.

### Proposed flow

```
spawn
  → session manager: decide to refresh
    → detect remote from DefaultBranch ("upstream/main" → remote=upstream, else origin)
    → gitworktree.FetchDefaultBranch(ctx, repo, remote, branch)
      → if error: log warning, continue (non-blocking)
      → if success: origin/main is now fresh
  → workspace.Create (unchanged)
    → addWorktree → resolveBaseRef → finds fresh origin/main
```

## Affected Code

| File | Location | Role |
|------|----------|------|
| `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go` | `addWorktree()` :760 | Where fetch should be inserted (or called from session manager) |
| `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go` | `resolveBaseRef()` :1015 | Reads local refs only |
| `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/commands.go` | `baseRefCandidates()` :131 | Builds candidate list (all local refs) |
| `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` | `createSessionWorkspace()` :714 | Policy decision: trigger fetch before Create |
| `backend/internal/domain/projectconfig.go` | `DefaultBranch` :21 | Config source — no canonical-remote concept today |

## Existing Tests to Update

- `manager_test.go:920` — `TestSpawnRecordsRemoteTrackingDiffBaseWhenLocalDefaultBranchLags` explicitly tests the current stale-ref behavior. Will need updated expectations after the fix.

## Related Issues

- #3810 — workspace spawn forces root repo's default branch on child repos (different problem, same area)
- #3857 — harden workspace compare-base selection for divergent histories (related: diff base after the fact)

title: bug(frontend): orchestrator session left showing TERMINAL ENDED after settings save replaces agent — no navigation to replacement, confusing dead-end
body:
## Bug

When a user changes the **Default orchestrator agent** in Project Settings → Agents and clicks **Save changes**, AO tears down the old orchestrator session and attempts to spawn a replacement. But when the replacement fails (in the reported case, the old orchestrator was terminated by a stale activity/terminal-idle race — see the "Interface switch failed" banner in the video), the **old orchestrator session stays visible in the UI showing "TERMINAL ENDED / [process exited]"** and the user is left on a dead session page with no automatic navigation to the new one or any other recovery action.

The user is stuck looking at a terminated orchestrator terminal with a confusing dead-end UI (exit text, red status dot, and a stale "Interface switch failed" banner), with no indication that a replacement was attempted or how to recover.

**Source:** Reported by @nikhilachale in Discord (#bug-triage thread), with screen recording | **Reported at:** 2026-08-12 ~04:55 IST
**Analyzed against:** `419fb3ba7` (origin/main HEAD)
**Confidence:** High — traced the exact frontend code path
**Priority:** high — core workflow (settings save) produces a confusing dead-end with no automatic recovery; affects any user who changes the orchestrator agent

## Reproduction

1. Open a project that has an active orchestrator session running
2. Open Settings → Agents tab
3. Change the **Default orchestrator agent** (e.g., from one agent to another, or change its model)
4. Click **Save changes**
5. Observe: the old orchestrator's terminal shows "TERMINAL ENDED / [process exited]" with a red status dot
6. If the replacement spawn fails (stale activity race, terminal-not-idle, etc.), the UI stays on this dead session indefinitely

## Root Cause

The save handler in `ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` (lines 208-220) calls `spawnOrchestrator(projectId, "settings", true)` with `clean=true` — which tears down the existing orchestrator and spawns a replacement — but **does not navigate to the new session's ID on success**, and **only surfaces a small text error on failure**.

```tsx
// ProjectSettingsForm.tsx:208-220
if (
    form.orchestratorAgent !== initialOrchestratorAgent ||
    (activeOrchestrator && activeOrchestrator.provider !== form.orchestratorAgent)
) {
    try {
        await spawnOrchestrator(projectId, "settings", true);
    } catch (error) {
        return {
            replacementError:
                error instanceof Error ? error.message : t("settings.project.replaceOrchestratorFailed"),
        };
    }
}
```

**Two defects:**

### 1. No navigation to the replacement session on success

Compare with every other spawn call site:
- **`ShellTopbar.tsx:152-157`** — spawns, invalidates workspace query, then **navigates** to `/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`
- **`restart-orchestrator.ts:43-48`** — spawns, invalidates workspace query, then **navigates** to `/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`

`ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` spawns but **never navigates**. On success, `spawnOrchestrator()` returns the new session ID, but the return value is **discarded**. The mutation's `onSuccess` only calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries` and `onSaved()` — it does not navigate. So even on a successful replacement, the user stays on whatever view they were on. If the workspace query refetch hasn't propagated yet (React Query cache timing), the old (now-terminated) orchestrator's "TERMINAL ENDED" view can persist.

### 2. Confusing dead-end on failure

When `spawnOrchestrator` throws (replacement failed), the old orchestrator is **already terminated** (the `clean=true` path calls `RetireForReplacement` before spawning the new one — `service.go:371-376`). The user sees:
- The old session's terminal showing "TERMINAL ENDED / [process exited]"
- A red status dot on the Orchestrator tab
- Potentially a stale "Interface switch failed" banner (if the termination raced with an interface transition)
- A small `replacementError` text in the settings footer (easy to miss — it's `text-warning` text-xs, line 494)

There is no prominent error state, no "retry" CTA, and no navigation away from the dead session. The `SaveChangesFooter` shows the error as small warning text at the bottom of the settings form — which may be scrolled out of view or dismissed by closing settings.

## Impact

- **Core workflow broken:** Changing the orchestrator agent is a common settings operation; it should not leave the user stranded on a dead session.
- **No recovery path:** The user has no obvious way to get back to a working orchestrator — they must manually spawn a new one from the topbar or sidebar.
- **Confusing UX:** "TERMINAL ENDED" + "Interface switch failed" banner + red dot is a jarring combination with no explanation of what happened or what to do next.

## Fix

**Frontend fix** in `ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`:

1. **Navigate to the new orchestrator session on success.** Capture the session ID from `spawnOrchestrator()` and navigate to it (matching `restart-orchestrator.ts` pattern). This requires passing a `navigate` function into `SettingsBody` (or lifting the spawn/navigate into the parent component that has router access).

2. **Surface replacement failures more prominently.** The current `replacementError` text-xs in the footer is insufficient. Consider:
   - Keeping the settings modal open with a visible error banner when replacement fails
   - Adding a "Retry" or "Spawn new orchestrator" CTA button next to the error
   - Showing a toast/notification instead of (or in addition to) footer text

3. **Handle the already-terminated case gracefully.** When the old orchestrator is already terminated (by the clean replacement path) but the new spawn fails, the user needs a clear path to recovery — not a dead terminal view.

## Related

- [#2501](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2501) — orchestrator terminated mid-turn by stale-activity/probe race, then silently replaced with no linkage (same underlying lifecycle race that can cause the replacement to fail)
- [#3300](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/issues/3300) — killed/exited session page is a confusing dead-end (same UX pattern: dead session shown with no recovery CTA)

title: bug(orchestrator): fresh orchestrator spawn crashes claude with "invalid session id", leaving an unrecoverable exited/non-terminated session
body:
## Summary Spawning a new **orchestrator** session (`ao spawn --kind orchestrator ...`) for a specific project intermittently fails immediately: the tmux pane shows `invalid session id` and the underlying `claude` process never starts. This has recurred across several days on the same project, and there is no recovery path — `restore` refuses the resulting session, and killing + respawning reproduces the exact same failure. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Have an existing orchestrator session for a project (harness `claude-code`, mode `tui`). 2. At some point the session's activity flips to `exited` while `terminated` stays `false` (observed after a daemon/tmux restart, e.g. Mac sleep — but also reproduced via a **fresh** spawn, see below). 3. `ao session get ` shows: ``` status: exited activity: exited terminated: false ``` 4. `ao session restore ` refuses: ``` Session is not restorable (SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE) ``` 5. `ao session kill ` succeeds and flips `terminated: true`. 6. `ao spawn --project

--kind orchestrator --branch --name orchestrator --mode tui` creates a **new** session id, but the tmux pane immediately shows: ``` invalid session id ``` and stays there — no `claude` process is running in the pane (`tmux list-panes -F "#{pane_current_command}"` shows a bare `cat`, not `claude`). The corresponding `ao agent-process supervise ... -- claude ...` wrapper process is also gone (it exited alongside the crashed `claude` child), leaving a dead pane with nothing supervising it. 7. The new session is left in the same broken state as step 3 (`status/activity: exited`, `terminated: false`) — no further recovery via CLI. This reproduced on a fresh `ao spawn` (not just `restore`), which rules out a single stale/orphaned resume-id as the sole cause — something about how the `--session-id`/`--resume` value is generated or accepted for this project's orchestrator role is rejected by the `claude` binary outright. For contrast, doing the identical kill+respawn dance on a **different** project's orchestrator (same `claude-code` harness, same `claude` binary version) recovered cleanly — the new session started normally with a live `claude` process in the pane. So this is not a global daemon/tmux issue; it is scoped to specific project/session state. ## Observed ``` $ ao session get status: exited activity: exited terminated: false ``` Pane content: ``` invalid session id ``` No `claude` process; `ao agent-process supervise` wrapper also absent (crashed together with the child). Pane is left running a bare `cat` keep-alive with no supervisor watching it. ## Why this is bad - The session is stuck in a state with no CLI verb to recover it: not `terminated` (so `restore` refuses), not actually alive (so nothing else works either). - The only workaround found is `kill` + respawn, which is destructive and, in this case, **reproduces the identical failure** — there is no way back into a working orchestrator session for the affected project without deeper manual intervention (unclear which project-level state is at fault). - `daemon.log` does not capture this at all — the daemon's own log file was stale (last write far in the past despite the daemon actively serving requests), and grepping it for "invalid session" or the failing session's id returns nothing. There is no first-class signal anywhere (log or `ao session get`) pointing at *why* the harness rejected the id. ## Environment - `ao version dev` (self-built) - `claude` (Claude Code) 2.1.228 - macOS, daemon runs under the desktop app (`Agent Orchestrator.app`) - harness: `claude-code`, role: `orchestrator`, mode: `tui` ## Possibly related - #2702 — restore recreates the tmux session but never relaunches the agent (zombie session). Related but not identical: that issue is about `restore` after a daemon restart; this reproduces on a **fresh spawn** as well, and even kill+respawn doesn't recover it for the affected project. - #1521 — different "Invalid session ID" error (path basename `.` at spawn time, rejected by a regex check in the runtime plugin) — different code path, not orchestrator-specific, doesn't match this symptom (that one fails *at spawn time* with a clear validation error; this one fails *inside the harness process* after the tmux pane is already up). Happy to provide further `ao session get` / `sqlite3` state dumps — keeping project specifics generic since this is from a private setup.

title: fix(cli): allow dots in sessionIDPattern to match projectIDPattern
body:
Code changes: +32 -20  
Tests: +124 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Any project whose id contains a dot (for example `myproject.example`) fails to spawn or restore sessions. The agent process never starts: the terminal runtime is left at its keepalive process and the session lands in `exited` / `is_terminated=false` limbo.

Closes #3875. Also covers the Windows ConPTY boundary reported in #4479.

## Root cause

AO session ids are generated as `{ProjectID}-{num}`. Project ids permit dots, but several downstream session-id validators used a narrower alphabet. The hidden `agent-process supervise` command rejected a dotted id before launching the agent; Windows ConPTY and the headless-review submit allowlist carried equivalent copies of the narrower contract.

## Fix

- Define the canonical AO session-id alphabet in the domain package: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`.
- Reuse that contract in supervisor, hook, telemetry, ConPTY, and reviewer-submit validation.
- Keep runtime launch-id validation separate and narrow.
- Continue rejecting leading dots, slashes, traversal payloads, whitespace, and shell metacharacters.

The supervisor still validates its internal CLI boundary before starting a child, but it no longer maintains an independent definition of a valid session id.

## Testing

- Unit accept/reject coverage for the canonical session-id contract.
- End-to-end supervisor coverage proving `my.project-16` starts its child.
- Traversal rejection coverage for `../evil`, `a/b`, and `.hidden`.
- ConPTY coverage for dotted ids and unsafe inputs.
- Headless-review permission coverage proving a dotted worker id can submit its result.
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...`
- `cd frontend && npm run build`

## Manual verification

Reproduced on the installed `0.13.1-nightly.202609241911` app with project `ao.dotted-repro-test`: spawn initially returned `idle`, then became `exited` with `isTerminated=false`; the terminal contained `invalid session id`.

Re-tested the same repository and project id in the rebased dev Electron app using isolated data. The session remained `idle`, had a live supervisor and Codex child, and successfully completed an `exit-agent` → `resume-agent` cycle. The native dev UI showed `Dotted ID Fixed · Codex · Idle`.

`npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --all` could not run the artifact workflow locally because `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` is unavailable; that job is left to remote CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: bug(chat): nested Codex turns can drain queued automation before the root completes, leaving a permanent phantom Working turn
body:
## Bug summary

AO can permanently show **Working** after the provider is idle and all real work has finished.

This is not merely a stale animation and it is not a long-running tool call. In the captured incident, a nested Codex child turn completed while the root turn was still active. AO treated that child completion as if the whole conversation had become idle, drained a queued automation request too early, and created a second durable AO turn. Codex accepted the automation message into the still-running root transcript rather than starting the provider turn AO had assigned. The assigned AO turn therefore received no provider lifecycle events, remained `running` forever in SQLite, and kept the frontend spinner alive.

**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1  
**Reported/reproduced:** 2026-08-12, from a live packaged AO desktop session  
**Packaged version:** `0.12.1-nightly.202608101434` (bundled daemon reports `dev`)  
**Code inspected:** current `origin/main` at `f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9`  
**Codex CLI:** `0.147.0`  
**Environment:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64

## User-visible failure

The UI had remained in this state for about 88 minutes when captured and was still stuck afterward:

![Permanent orphaned Working turn after 1h27m](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-nested-turn-orphan-20260812/.issue-assets/chat-nested-turn-orphan/orphan-working-1h27.png)

The visible child-agent review was DONE, there was no new chat activity, and the relevant Codex processes were sleeping at 0% CPU. Restarting/re-rendering the UI cannot repair this because the durable turn row itself is still `running`.

## Observed event timeline

Session: `agent-orchestrator-1-95`  
Conversation: `c1f16460…`

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 05:31:11.935 | Root AO turn `8819be57…` starts; provider turn `019ff474…` |
| 05:32:05.454 | PR review automation is queued while the root is active |
| 05:39:35.091 | Nested child turn `ab357b31…` completes |
| 05:39:35.145 | Only 54 ms later, AO prematurely dispatches queued automation as AO turn `6765ffd1…`, assigning provider ID `019ff47b…` |
| 05:39:37.317 | The automation message appears in the native Codex transcript tagged with the **original root** provider ID `019ff474…`, not the newly assigned ID |
| 05:42:13.774 | The real root turn completes |
| 07:07:48 | Screenshot: assigned automation turn has been `running` for 88.2 minutes with zero activities and zero provider events |

The queued automation was dispatched while the actual root still had another 158.6 seconds of work remaining.

The native Codex transcript ends normally with `task_complete` for `019ff474…`. The orphan provider ID `019ff47b…` never appears anywhere in that transcript.

## Contradictory live state

At the same instant:

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| SQLite turn row | automation turn = `running` |
| Turn activities | zero |
| Normalized provider events | zero |
| Controller snapshot | `ready` |
| Provider thread state | `idle` |
| Session activity | `idle` |
| Frontend | **Working** indefinitely |
| Codex app-server / code-mode host | sleeping, 0% CPU |

This rules out a live tool call. It is a durable/provider lifecycle split.

## Deterministic code path

The controller models a conversation with one mutable `pendingTurnID` / `ackedTurnID` pair ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L131-L140)).

1. Dispatch creates/binds the queued AO turn and records it as pending ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L750-L762)).
2. **Every** provider `turn.started`, including nested child turns, overwrites `pendingTurnID` and `ackedTurnID` and marks the controller busy ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1315-L1322)).
3. **Every** `turn.completed`, regardless of whether it matches the dispatched root, sets the controller ready ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1350-L1359)).
4. After projection, every completion reports the session idle and drains one queued request ([controller.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1697-L1705)).
5. The Codex adapter has the same single-slot assumption: every provider start overwrites `activeTurn` ([conversation.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go#L150-L157)), and interruption targets that value ([conversation.go](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go#L486-L499)).
6. The frontend considers any durable `running` turn active ([conversation.ts](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/frontend/src/renderer/types/conversation.ts#L746-L750)), so the orphan has no natural recovery path and the Working indicator remains ([ChatWorkspace.tsx](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx#L1848-L1860)).

## Why the other reports looked similar

Two earlier screenshots were not permanent backend freezes:

![Short-lived parent activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-nested-turn-orphan-20260812/.issue-assets/chat-nested-turn-orphan/short-parent-working.png)

![Parent still active after visible child completed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-nested-turn-orphan-20260812/.issue-assets/chat-nested-turn-orphan/overlap-parent-working.png)

In those cases the root was genuinely active and completed shortly afterward. However, `groupByTurn` anchors the entire parent group at its first sequence position ([ChatWorkspace.tsx](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/f0ae54b9fc2fe7a3b47076e43edbbbb90f5349b9/frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx#L1719-L1785)). Later parent activity can therefore render above completed child cards. At the bottom of the transcript the user sees “DONE” beside “Working,” with no visible evidence of what is still active.

That is an adjacent presentation defect which makes a healthy overlap indistinguishable from this permanent orphan.

## Proposed fix

### Lifecycle correctness

- Track the AO-dispatched **primary/root provider turn** separately from nested provider executions.
- Do not let nested `turn.started` replace primary ownership.
- Do not let nested `turn.completed` set the conversation Ready/Idle or drain the request queue.
- Drain only when the root thread is actually quiescent.
- Add acknowledgement recovery for an AO-dispatched provider ID that never emits `turn.started`.
- Make adapter interruption target the primary AO-dispatched turn, not the most recently started nested turn.
- Reconcile a durable `running` row when the controller is ready and the provider is authoritatively idle, while preserving the rule that failed/unknown probes are not proof of death.

Avoid inferring parentage only from timing or adding a heuristic `parentTurnId` to `ConversationTurn`. The normalizer currently discards provider thread identity, and overlapping events can also be compaction, replay, or resumed work. Codex exposes explicit thread/source metadata; AO should preserve enough of that identity, or model nested provider runs separately from user-request turns.

### UI clarity

- Show the latest activity and age of the active primary turn, with a way to jump to it.
- Keep later parent activity visible after child completion rather than anchoring it entirely above child cards.
- Surface child execution as nested/structured activity.
- If a durable turn has no provider events for a threshold, show an advisory recovery state; do not declare it dead solely from elapsed time.

## Regression coverage / acceptance criteria

- [ ] A nested child start does not replace the primary dispatched turn.
- [ ] A nested child completion does not settle the parent, report the session idle, or drain the queue.
- [ ] Automation queued during root work remains queued until root completion.
- [ ] Root completion dispatches the next request exactly once.
- [ ] A dispatched turn that never acknowledges eventually reaches a recoverable terminal/error state.
- [ ] Stop targets the primary provider turn.
- [ ] Compaction, replay, and resumed-thread flows remain correct.
- [ ] An overlapping parent/child transcript keeps the current parent activity visible.
- [ ] No durable turn remains indefinitely `running` while controller and authoritative provider state are idle.

## Impact

- Misleading multi-hour “Working” state.
- Queued PR-review automation is injected into the wrong provider turn.
- Future queue work may remain blocked behind an orphan.
- Stop/recovery can target the wrong nested turn.
- Users cannot distinguish legitimate hidden parent work from a lifecycle failure.

## Related work

- [Issue #3749](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3749) has the same terminal symptom (durable/in-memory turn-state desync) but a different trigger: projection transaction failure.
- [PR #3752](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3752) adds Stop-time reconciliation and post-commit memory mutation for that path. It can provide manual recovery after Stop, but it does not prevent nested start/completion events from changing primary ownership or prematurely draining the queue.
- [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) is the broader structured Chat work.

title: Chat/ACP broken on Intel Macs: bundled acp-runtime Node signed without allow-unsigned-executable-memory → V8 crash (exit 133), "peer disconnected before response"
body:
## Summary

Chat (ACP) is completely broken on Intel Macs: the app-bundled Node runtime in `Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node` is Hardened-Runtime signed **without** `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. On x86_64 that entitlement is required for V8 to make JIT memory executable (`allow-jit`/MAP_JIT only covers the arm64 path), so the ACP adapter process crashes at V8 tier-up before it can answer `initialize`. The daemon surfaces this as:

```
switch interface <session>: resume chat: chat driver incompatible: ACP initialize:
{"code": -32603, "message": "Internal error", "data": {"error": "peer disconnected before response"}}
```

The "chat driver incompatible" label is misleading — no version incompatibility exists; the bundled Node cannot run *any* JavaScript on Intel.

## Environment

- Agent Orchestrator **0.12.3** (`dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`), also reproduced on the previous build (0.12.x, ~2 days earlier)
- macOS **15.7.8**, native **x86_64** Intel Mac (Mac Pro, Xeon W) — no Rosetta involved
- Bundled Node: **v22.23.2** (`Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node`)
- ACP adapter: `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` **0.64.2** (bundled)

## One-line repro (no AO involvement needed)

```console
$ /Applications/Agent\ Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node --version
v22.23.2
$ /Applications/Agent\ Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node -e 'console.log(1)'
# V8 fatal: "Check failed: 12 == (*__error())" in v8::base::OS::SetPermissions
#   -> MemoryAllocator::SetPermissionsOnExecutableMemoryChunk
# stack includes Runtime_BytecodeBudgetInterrupt_Ignition (first JIT tier-up)
$ echo $?
133
```

`--version` works (no JIT reached); any real script dies. Piping an ACP `initialize` request into the bundled adapter under this Node crashes identically with no JSON-RPC response — which is exactly what the daemon reports as "peer disconnected before response". macOS crash reports (`~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/node-*.ips`) show the same signature with parent process `ao`, i.e. the daemon's own spawns hit it, not just manual runs.

## Root cause

Signature of the bundled node (`codesign -d --entitlements -`):

```
CodeDirectory v=20500 flags=0x10000(runtime) TeamIdentifier=X9LNSP8MC2
[Key] com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit                 -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.audio-input           -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.bluetooth             -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.camera                -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.print                 -> true
[Key] com.apple.security.device.usb                   -> true
```

It looks like the Electron app's entitlements file was reused for the helper. Missing: `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` (official Node.js macOS binaries ship with it in addition to `allow-jit`, precisely because Intel V8 calls `mprotect(RWX)` rather than using MAP_JIT).

Proof the adapter itself is fine: the identical bundled `dist/index.js` run under a system Node (signed with `allow-jit` + `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`) answers `initialize` correctly in under a second (`agentInfo: claude-agent-acp 0.64.2`).

## Impact

- Every chat/ACP interface switch fails on Intel Macs, in ~1.5–3 s, 100% of the time (this machine's DB shows 6/6 failed `tui -> chat` transitions across two builds, zero successes ever).
- Because the failure is wrapped as "chat driver incompatible", users are steered toward version debugging instead of the packaging defect.

## Suggested fix

Sign the bundled `acp-runtime` Node with `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` (matching official Node.js distribution entitlements) for the x64 build — or use the official Node binary untouched. Ideally also make the daemon include the peer's stderr in the ACP initialize error, which would have surfaced the V8 fatal directly.

title: fix(session): harden workspace compare-base selection for divergent histories
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3848 (which fixed the normal stale-linear-`origin/main` case) addressing the three gaps identified in [issue #3857](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3857), a correctness review of that PR:

- **Divergent candidates after a force-push** — the ref-derived and PR-derived compare bases can both be valid ancestors of `HEAD` with neither an ancestor of the other (e.g. after the target branch is force-pushed to a replacement line). The prior one-directional ancestor check silently fell back to the ref candidate here, which can disagree with the provider's PR diff. Candidates are now compared in both directions; when genuinely incomparable, the PR candidate is only trusted when its `HeadSHA` matches the local workspace's actual `HEAD`.
- **Stale PR metadata vs. local workspace** — a persisted PR snapshot can describe an earlier local commit than the one currently checked out. The PR candidate is now weighed against a properly validated local candidate (ref-derived, or the spawn-time `recordedSHA` re-derived through merge-base) instead of unconditionally winning whenever no ref-derived candidate was found.
- **Raw SHA fallback on merge-base failure** — `pr.BaseSHA` was initialized as the candidate and only replaced with the merge-base result on success, so a commit sharing no common ancestor with `HEAD` (object exists locally, but unrelated history) could be returned as a raw, unrelated diff base. Every revision-derived candidate (ref, `recordedSHA`, and PR base) now goes through a single `mergeBaseCandidate()` validator that rejects the candidate outright when merge-base derivation fails.

Fixes #3857

## Test plan
- [x] Added 6 new tests covering each acceptance criterion: divergent force-push histories (PR-head-matches and PR-head-stale), comparable candidates regardless of order, a missing recorded ref not letting a stale PR override a valid `recordedSHA`, and two variants of rejecting a PR base with no common ancestor (with and without a local fallback candidate present). Each new test fails against the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.
- [x] `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/session/... -count=1` (all pass, including every pre-existing workspace-files test)
- [x] `go vet ./internal/service/session/...`
- [x] `go build ./...`
