title: feat: add native Android emulator (Track A)
body:
## What

Adds a native, in-app Android emulator: a Settings-gated "Emulator" tab (default off) that boots a real, AO-managed Android device (Google's own SDK/emulator binary, not a from-scratch emulator) directly inside a session, with a live view, tap/swipe/keyboard input, and an agent-facing `ao android emulator` CLI surface (`screenshot`, `inspect-ui`, `tap`/`swipe`/`type`/`press-key`, `find-source`) so the agent can see and drive the device too.

This is **Track A (Android) only** — cross-platform on **Windows, macOS, and Linux**. iOS Simulator support (Track B, macOS-only) is a separate, not-yet-built follow-up.

## Why

Lets an agent build and verify a mobile app end-to-end without leaving AO — install the SDK, boot a device, see the screen, tap through the app, and locate the source behind what's on screen, the same way a developer would with Android Studio's embedded emulator.

## How

- **SDK acquisition** (`androidsdk`): downloads/verifies `platform-tools`, `emulator`, and one pinned system image directly from Google's public repository manifests — no JVM/`sdkmanager` dependency.
- **Device lifecycle** (`androidemulator`): one persistent, shared, headless emulator process with quick-boot snapshots and crash/restart-with-backoff, driven over the loopback `EmulatorController` gRPC service the SDK's own emulator binary exposes (insecure/no-auth by default, confirmed during an earlier spike — no WebRTC in the standard SDK, so the transport is `getScreenshot` polling at ~5fps, not smooth video).
- **Renderer**: new "Emulator" tab in the session inspector (same pattern as Browser/Files), gated behind a Settings toggle so it costs nothing when unused.
- **Agent-facing CLI** (`ao android emulator ...`, surfaced to agents via the `using-ao` skill): screenshot, `uiautomator`-based UI tree inspection, tap/swipe/type/key input, and heuristic identifier→source-file lookup.
- **Env integration**: `ANDROID_HOME`/`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`/`PATH` are injected into session and standalone terminals once the SDK is installed, and `ao doctor` reports SDK/virtualization status.
- **Process supervision fix**: `Kill()` now terminates the whole process tree (`taskkill /T /F` on Windows, process-group kill on Unix), not just the tracked PID — the emulator binary is a launcher whose actual VM backend runs as a separate child process, and a single-PID kill left it orphaned, holding the AVD's lock files and breaking every subsequent boot.

**Known constraint, not a bug**: the emulator needs real host headroom (~3-4GB RAM, a few CPU cores) once booted. On a memory-constrained host it can boot but then show in-guest ANRs ("System UI isn't responding") under contention — expected on any Android emulator (Google's own guidance is 16GB+ RAM for a comfortable experience), not specific to this integration.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` all clean.
- `go test ./...` passes for every android-related package (`androidsdk`, `androidemulator`, `daemon`, `cli`, `session_manager`'s new env-injection tests); a handful of pre-existing, unrelated flakes on this Windows dev box (nvm-version PATH test, a workspace-watcher timing test) are unaffected by this branch — verified they fail identically on `origin/main`.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run` (121 tests across `EmulatorPanel`, `useAndroidDevice`, `android-frame-stream`, `android-stream`, `ui-store`, `GlobalSettingsForm`, `SessionInspector`) all pass.
- Manually exercised end-to-end on Windows: settings toggle → SDK install → device boot → live interactive Pixel home screen → pop-out → tap/swipe/type.

## Testing this PR (Windows / Linux)

1. Check out this branch, `npm install` in `frontend/`.
2. Run the desktop app in dev mode.
3. Settings → toggle on the Android Emulator.
4. Open a session → new "Emulator" tab → Install Android SDK (~2GB download) → Start.
5. On Linux, hardware acceleration needs KVM (`/dev/kvm` readable by your user) — `ao doctor` reports acceleration status if it's unavailable.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change (Android emulator only — no unrelated files)
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass (go build/vet/test, frontend typecheck/test)

title: feat(workspaces): remote workspaces — run agents on a VM over SSH
body:
Closes #3853.

## Problem

If your laptop is a thin client and your VM holds the code, compute and
credentials, AO can't help you: the desktop app spawns a daemon on the machine
it runs on, and every session runs there. Discussion #2855 asks for exactly
this; issue #13 listed it before being closed as rewrite cleanup.

## What this does

A **workspace** is a machine that runs its own AO daemon. `local` is unchanged.
A remote workspace is an SSH target the supervisor reaches through a loopback
port-forward:

```
ssh -N -L <freePort>:127.0.0.1:<remoteDaemonPort> <target>
```

The renderer already addresses the daemon through one mutable base URL handed
to it on `daemon:status`, and the mux WebSocket and SSE derive from that base.
So publishing the forward's local end as the daemon port makes **the entire
renderer work against a remote daemon unmodified**. Pick the machine in
Settings → Workspace; aliases come from your `~/.ssh/config`.

## Why this shape

The alternative — one laptop daemon that *places individual sessions* on a VM —
was designed in full first, and the design argued against it. Routing must be a
pure function of `RuntimeHandle.ID`, which forces the host into the handle id,
and that id space is mintable from project names, so a folder can forge a remote
handle and get a healthy session reaped. Plus `gitworktree` bypasses its own
command runner in ten places, `binaryutil.LookPath` puts *laptop* paths in the
remote pane's `argv[0]`, hooks and the system-prompt file are written locally at
the remote path, and `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` would be exported to a third
machine. All solvable; all existing only because one daemon is acting on a
filesystem that isn't its own. It remains the better answer to "run this one
task on the big machine" and can layer on later — see the ADR.

## Security posture

- **No bind change, no new listener.** Both daemons stay `127.0.0.1`-only, so
  unlike ADR-0001 this needs **no exception** to the loopback-only hard rule.
- **Auth is SSH's.** AO shells out to your `ssh`, holds no key material, writes
  no `known_hosts`. `~/.ssh/config` governs.
- `BatchMode=yes` is load-bearing — the supervisor has no tty and can answer
  neither a passphrase prompt nor an unknown-host-key prompt.
- **`StrictHostKeyChecking` is never set.** An unknown key is surfaced to you
  with the instruction to connect once and see the fingerprint; a *changed* key
  is reported as the security event it is.
- **AO never installs anything remotely.** A host without `ao` is reported with
  the command to run.

## Verification

Verified end to end against a real VM, not just unit tests: the app attaches to
the remote daemon (or starts one), serves the whole UI from it, and upgrades the
terminal-mux WebSocket through the tunnel (HTTP 101).

Real-host testing found **four bugs that unit tests structurally could not**,
each now with a regression test:

| Bug | Why tests missed it |
|---|---|
| `ssh` rejoins argv and the remote shell re-splits it, so `command -v ao` ran the no-op `command` builtin — **preflight passed on a host with no `ao`** | tests asserted the *local* argv, which was correct |
| `ControlMaster`+`ControlPersist` makes `ssh -N` **fork and exit 0**; supervisor read that as "tunnel died" and leaked the forward | a fake child process doesn't fork |
| **Remote port was guessed**; 3001 was taken on the VM so the daemon bound elsewhere and the tunnel hit an unrelated service | no fake reproduces a busy port |
| Concurrent connects each spawned a tunnel | the local path's de-dup guard runs after the remote branch |

1578 tests pass. The 5 failing `landing/generate-markdown-twins` tests fail
identically on a clean `main` and are unrelated.

## Deliberately out of scope

Moving a session between workspaces; a cross-workspace board; `ao` CLI parity
(still local-daemon only); Windows as the client (the failure path is graceful —
a missing `ssh` is reported as such — but it is untested).

## Review order

The commits are meant to be read in order, ADR first.

title: bug(chat): restart recovery deletes image attachments from conversation history
body: ## Bug Chat image attachments are stored only inside the session's disposable Git worktree. When daemon startup recovery recreates a Chat session worktree, `.ao/attachments` is omitted from preservation and deleted. The durable conversation still contains the old workspace-relative paths, so inline previews eventually become broken images and the agent can no longer read those historical attachments. **Source:** Live AO Chat report and two observed restart cycles on 2026-08-11/12 **Reported by:** @illegalcall **Affected build:** `v0.12.1-nightly.202608101434` (nightly commit `2da84a242`) **Analyzed against:** `21fd51acd` (`origin/main` on 2026-08-12; mechanism remains present) **Environment:** macOS 26.5.1, Darwin 25.5.0, arm64, zsh, Go 1.26.5; verified Go daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001` **Priority:** P1 — AO permanently loses attachment content from durable Chat history; no safe in-product recovery exists after the bytes are removed. **Confidence:** High — reproduced across two restart/recovery cycles, traced through the exact storage/lifecycle/preview code path, and verified with filesystem checks plus deterministic cache-busted HTTP requests. ## Reproduction 1. Create or open a non-scratch Chat-mode session. 2. Paste/drop/select an image and send it. 3. Confirm the image renders inline and the daemon preview URL returns `200 image/png`. 4. Restart AO Desktop such that its daemon restarts and startup recovery runs. 5. Reopen the conversation. 6. If the image remains temporarily visible, wait for Chromium to revalidate it or request the preview URL with a unique query parameter. Example request: ```bash curl --path-as-is -i \ 'http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions//preview/files/.ao/attachments/.png?cache_bust=' ``` ### Actual ```http HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 {"error":"not_found","code":"PREVIEW_FILE_NOT_FOUND","message":"Preview file not found",...} ``` The message and attachment path remain in SQLite, but the referenced file no longer exists in the recreated worktree. The inline image is broken, and the agent cannot reopen it. ### Expected Attachments referenced by durable Chat history must survive daemon/app restarts and worktree recreation. The same preview URL should continue returning the original bytes, and the same `.ao/attachments/...` path should remain readable by the resumed agent. ## Observed evidence This was observed twice in the same session, plus once in an older session: | Cycle | Evidence | |---|---| | First restart | Worktree recreated at **2026-08-11 17:12:02 IST**; daemon started at **17:12:05 IST**. Attachments created before recovery were absent and returned `404`. An attachment uploaded at **17:12:53 IST**, after recovery, returned `200`. | | Second restart | Newer images were attached after the first restart. Worktree was recreated again at **2026-08-11 20:07:40 IST**; daemon started at **20:07:43 IST**. Every one of five historical attachment paths was absent on disk and returned `404`; the same cache-busted request returned `404` in three consecutive runs. | | Separate older session | Its durable message predated the next worktree recreation; both referenced attachments were absent afterward and returned `404 PREVIEW_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. | Git reflog for each recreated worktree recorded a reset at the same second as recreation. The installed nightly did not change between the observations. ### Why disappearance can be delayed Chromium may continue painting its cached image after the backing file has already been deleted. In the first observation, an old image remained visible immediately after restart and disappeared later without another restart. Cache-busted requests already returned `404` during that interval. Therefore browser cache timing can mask the loss, but does not cause it. A renderer-only reload or Electron relaunch that leaves the daemon/worktree intact is not sufficient. The destructive trigger is daemon recovery recreating the Chat session worktree. ## Root cause The durable and ephemeral lifetimes are mismatched: 1. [`StageAttachments`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_attachments.go#L50-L76) writes the only copy under `/.ao/attachments` and adds that directory to Git's local exclude list. 2. Conversation persistence retains the generated `.ao/attachments/` reference in message text, but does not retain the attachment bytes or durable attachment metadata. 3. On daemon startup, [`reconcileLive`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1911-L1942) treats every Chat controller as unable to survive the daemon and sends the session through `saveAndTeardownOne`. 4. [`StashUncommitted`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go#L344-L420) intentionally preserves tracked and non-ignored changes only. An attachment-only worktree appears clean, and ignored `.ao/attachments` content is skipped. 5. [`saveAndTeardownOne`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1837-L1885) records the restore marker, then force-removes the worktree. Restore recreates Git-visible state but has no source for the ignored attachment bytes. 6. The preview route [`previewFile`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go#L416-L427) serves only from the current workspace, so historical attachment URLs resolve to `PREVIEW_FILE_NOT_FOUND` after recreation. 7. The renderer added by [PR #3724](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3724) correctly recognizes the durable path and creates an `` URL; it cannot recover bytes the backend deleted. The behavior is cross-platform in principle because it follows shared session-manager and Git-worktree logic, although this reproduction was on macOS. ## Fix direction Introduce a daemon-owned attachment-storage module whose canonical bytes live under AO's durable data directory, for example: ```text $AO_DATA_DIR/attachments// ``` Keep `.ao/attachments/...` as the agent-facing projection so existing prompts and conversations remain compatible. Required behavior: 1. **Stage atomically:** validate the input, atomically write the canonical `0600` copy under `$AO_DATA_DIR`, then materialize it into the session worktree. Return the existing worktree-relative path. 2. **Serve durably:** for strictly validated AO-generated attachment paths, serve the canonical copy rather than relying solely on the disposable worktree. Keep ordinary preview files confined to the worktree as today. 3. **Restore projection:** after recreating a worktree and before relaunching its controller, rematerialize that session's durable attachments into `.ao/attachments` and restore the local exclude entry. 4. **Upgrade safely:** before the first destructive recovery under the fixed build, import legacy worktree-only `.ao/attachments` into durable storage. Otherwise updating to the fix can itself delete attachments created by the affected build. 5. **Tie cleanup to durable ownership:** remove canonical attachments only when the owning session/conversation is permanently deleted—not when its runtime is stopped or its worktree is recycled. 6. **Preserve security properties:** validate generated names, reject traversal and symlink escapes, retain attachment size/type limits, and never expose one session's files through another session ID. Optional SQLite metadata can record attachment identity, MIME type, size, and message/turn ownership, but large binary blobs do not need to live in SQLite. ### Do not fix by - removing `.ao/attachments` from Git exclusion, which would dirty user worktrees; - forcing ignored binary files into Git preserve commits, which would pollute the project object database and blur AO-owned/user-owned state; - changing cache headers or retrying in the renderer, which can only hide a missing-file response; - storing only another ephemeral path without a durable byte owner. ## Regression coverage Add a lifecycle-level test that exercises the real failure seam: ```text start daemon with data dir A → create Chat session → attach an image → assert preview returns 200 and exact bytes → stop/restart daemon using data dir A → allow startup recovery to recreate/restore the session → assert the same preview URL returns 200 and exact bytes → assert the resumed agent can read the same .ao/attachments/... path ``` Also cover: - legacy worktree-only attachment import before teardown; - multiple attachments and collision-free stable names; - image and non-image attachment persistence; - traversal, malformed name, symlink escape, and cross-session access rejection; - permanent session/conversation cleanup; - direct HTTP success after restart without relying on Chromium cache. The existing [`TestChatAttachmentIsStagedIntoTheWorktreeAndReadableByTheAgent`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/21fd51acd/backend/e2e/chat_composer_test.go#L87-L152) verifies only immediate readability and clean Git status; it does not cross a daemon restart/recovery boundary. ## Impact - AO loses attachment bytes while retaining apparently valid history references. - Historical screenshots cannot be reviewed by the user or agent after recovery. - Image-only prompts can lose essential context. - Browser caching makes the bug appear intermittent and delays visible failure. - Reattaching is possible only if the user still has the original external file; AO itself cannot recover already-deleted attachments. - The problem affects every attachment type staged under `.ao/attachments`, although images expose it most visibly. ## Related - [Issue #3722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3722) — fixed rendering attachment paths as inline previews; adjacent but not a duplicate. - [PR #3724](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3724) — introduced the renderer path that exposes this underlying lifetime mismatch. - [Issue #2722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2722) — original task-composer attachment capability. - [PR #3691](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3691) — stages delegated-task attachments in worker worktrees. - [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) / [PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) — Chat controller persistence and restart architecture.

title: fix(chat): keep nested Codex turns from draining queued work
body:
## Summary

- preserve Codex's provider thread identity on normalized turn lifecycle events
- let only lifecycle events from the AO-owned root thread claim or release the controller's primary turn
- keep nested child turns durable for transcript correlation without reporting the session idle or draining queued work
- apply volatile turn ownership only after the SQLite projection commits
- serialize lifecycle projection, queue dispatch, and handoff quiescence checks at one dispatch boundary
- prevent nested child notifications from replacing the Codex adapter's fallback Stop target

## Root cause

Codex app-server multiplexes child-agent thread lifecycle notifications over the root conversation connection. AO discarded the notification's `threadId`, stored only one mutable active turn, and treated every `turn/completed` as conversation quiescence.

A child completion could therefore release queued automation while the root was still running. Codex accepted the message into that root, while AO had already minted and bound a different durable turn. Because that assigned provider turn never started, the row stayed `running` and a Chat → TUI drain waited indefinitely.

The CI race run also exposed the adjacent quiescence gap: dispatch marks a queued row running in SQLite just before installing its in-memory active-turn ID. A handoff checking those facts without the dispatch lock could briefly see neither queued nor active work and finish early. The handoff now evaluates both facts under the same lock as dispatch.

The added handoff regression covers the complete user-visible sequence: child completion cannot finish the handoff or release its accepted queue; root completion releases that queue; the handoff finishes only after the queue settles.

## Verification

- controller regression passed 50 consecutive times with the race detector
- focused controller/normalizer/adapter regressions passed 20×
- `go test -p 4 ./...`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver`
- golangci-lint v2.12.2 with fresh Go/lint caches: 0 issues

Related follow-up: #3950 / #3951 durably acknowledge the recovered transition notice so the same historical recovery does not resurface after remounts or restarts.

Fixes #3878

title: fix(chat): persist attachments across restart
body:
## Summary

- store every new chat and spawn attachment canonically under the AO data directory while retaining the worktree-relative path agents read
- import legacy worktree-only attachments before kill, cleanup, replacement, and restart teardown; rematerialize image and non-image files before restored controllers relaunch
- serve strictly validated AO attachment preview URLs from canonical storage so history does not depend on a live worktree or Chromium cache
- remove canonical bytes only with permanent session ownership cleanup, never on runtime stop or worktree recycling

## Review repairs

- anchor canonical and worktree operations with `os.Root`; reject traversal, unsafe generated names, symlink parent escapes, cross-session aliases, empty roots, non-regular files, SVG, and over-limit content
- make canonical creation atomic and no-overwrite, retry randomized chat-name collisions, and preserve historical bytes
- pass `context.Context` through every public attachment-store I/O operation
- restore the Git exclude only when canonical files were materialized, and stop destructive teardown when a present legacy source cannot be imported safely
- add the required real daemon restart/recovery test, including exact cache-busted HTTP bytes and a resumed agent reading the same path

## Root cause

Conversation history persisted only the `.ao/attachments` path. The bytes existed only in an ignored worktree directory, so `StashUncommitted` omitted them and restart reconciliation force-removed the only copy. Chromium cache temporarily made some images appear to survive.

## Verification

- `GOFLAGS=-p=4 npm run lint`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go vet ./...`
- `cd backend && go test -p=4 ./... -count=1`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/attachmentstore ./internal/session_manager ./internal/httpd/controllers -count=1`
- Windows amd64 cross-compile of `internal/attachmentstore` tests
- `AO_CHAT_E2E=1 go test ./e2e -run ^TestChatAttachmentSurvivesDaemonRestartRecovery$ -v -count=1 -timeout=10m`

## Known limitation

An older build may already have deleted an attachments only copy. This change migrates legacy files that still exist in a live or retained worktree, but cannot reconstruct bytes deleted before upgrade.

Closes #3884

title: fix(conpty): scope pty-host registry to the daemon instance
body:
## Summary

- The Windows ConPTY runtime's pty-host registry (`~/.ao/windows-pty-hosts.json`) was hardcoded to the default AO home directory via `os.UserHomeDir()`, ignoring the `AO_RUN_FILE`/`AO_DATA_DIR` overrides every other piece of daemon state (`ao.db`, `running.json`) already respects.
- Two AO daemon instances on one machine (e.g. a headless dev daemon at `~/.ao/dev` and the desktop app at `~/.ao`) therefore shared one registry file even though they're otherwise fully isolated.
- Session ids are numbered per-project within each instance's own local DB (`NextSessionNum`), so two instances with the same project can independently mint identical session ids (e.g. `demo-website-2`). The second instance's registration would then silently overwrite the first's pty-host address in the shared registry — attaching that session's terminal to the *wrong* process.
- `ptyregistry.SetRunFilePath` now scopes the registry to the directory containing the calling instance's own `running.json`, wired through `conpty.Options.RunFilePath` and a new `runFilePath` parameter on `runtimeselect.New`, sourced from the daemon's already-resolved `cfg.RunFilePath`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `go test ./...` — new/changed packages pass cleanly; pre-existing failures on this Windows dev environment (`TestStabilizeWorkingDirectoryChdirsToDataDir`, tmux `/tmp`-path tests, `TestWriteAgentHandoffFileIsPrivateAtomicAndImmutable`, `TestSpawn_*` branch-namespace tests, `workspacewatch` watcher timing) reproduce identically on the unmodified base branch and are unrelated (none of those packages import `conpty`/`ptyregistry`/`runtimeselect`)
- [x] New regression test (`TestTwoInstancesWithDifferentRunFilePathsDoNotShareRegistry`) reproduces the exact cross-instance collision and verifies it no longer occurs

title: fix(desktop): preserve Intel Node JIT entitlement
body:
Refs #3879.

## What changed

- Applies a per-file entitlement override only to the bundled ACP Node at `Contents/Resources/acp-runtime/node/bin/node`, and selects it **from the binary content**: the override applies iff the Mach-O header of the file being signed contains an x86_64 slice (a thin x64 binary, or a universal carrying x64). arm64-only binaries keep the default `allow-jit`.
- **The signing host's architecture is never consulted.** `@electron/osx-sign` passes `optionsForFile` only `(filePath)`, and the canonical downstream signer processes both arm64 and x64 artifacts from one host, so `process.arch` was the wrong selector (review follow-up). The new `frontend/makers/macho-archs.ts` parses the Mach-O header (thin `MH_MAGIC_64`, fat `FAT_MAGIC`/`FAT_MAGIC_64`; endianness derived from the magic, cputype-only classification) and `macSignOptionsForFile` keys off it. Tests stub `process.arch` to `x64`, `arm64`, and a nonsense value and pin identical results.
- **Fails closed**: an unreadable or unparseable file at the nested-Node path throws out of `optionsForFile` and aborts the signing pass — no silent fallback to defaults, which is exactly the #3879 crash.
- Preserves `allow-jit` and adds `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, which x64 V8 needs when Hardened Runtime blocks executable-memory permission changes.
- Leaves every other bundle file on `@electron/osx-sign` defaults.
- Wires the override through both supported Forge signing inputs: `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` and `CSC_LINK`; unsigned local packages remain unsigned.
- Documents the canonical signing contract in `frontend/docs/desktop-release.md` ("macOS signing contract for the bundled ACP runtime"), including pre-publication duties: inspect the nested Node's entitlements in the final artifact and execute the final x64 zip's Node on a native Intel runner, keeping the arm64 verification.
- Extends `frontend/scripts/verify-mac-artifact.sh` to inspect the final nested Node entitlements and execute it only after codesign, Gatekeeper, and stapler all pass. The script is the local diagnostic and the public mac-update-e2e baseline check; the pre-publication gate remains the release conductor's verifier, which now has a documented contract to mirror.

Scope note: the public CI build in `build-artifacts.yml` stays intentionally unsigned, so `osxSign`/`optionsForFile` do not run there — the entitlement decision is enforced wherever signing actually happens (locally signed builds today; the canonical signer once it mirrors the documented contract).

The branch is rebased on current `main`.

## Review follow-up addressed

- Arch selection is keyed off the artifact being signed, not the host (`arch` parameter removed).
- The public verifier is documented as the local diagnostic counterpart, not the publication gate.
- Removed the unrelated `AgentModelCombobox` locale-formatting commit and the net-zero screenshot add/remove pair (tree verified byte-identical apart from the locale file).
- `Closes` demoted to `Refs` until the paired conductor-side change lands (contract in `desktop-release.md`).

## Tests

- Focused suites: 69 passed — new Mach-O parser tests, forge.config signing/postMake, maker-dmg, verify-mac-artifact smoke.
- Mach-O parser coverage: synthetic thin/fat fixtures (incl. `FAT_MAGIC_64`, byte-swapped thin, arm64e cputype-only classification, i386 not masked into x86_64), truncated/garbage/non-Mach-O headers throw, host-arch independence, macOS sanity check against a real Mach-O.
- Frontend typecheck and e2e typecheck: passed. Full frontend suite: 267 files; 3,594 passed, 7 skipped, and 12 failed — all 12 in `browser-profile-import.test.ts`, from a local `better-sqlite3` build carrying the Electron ABI after a local packaged build (environment artifact; neither the module nor that file is touched by this branch).
- Shell syntax and shellcheck: passed.
- Trust-order regression: a mocked untrusted app fails `spctl` and the nested Node sentinel is never executed.
- Real signer A/B (original round): official Node v22.23.2 x64, `@electron/osx-sign` 1.3.3, Hardened Runtime — the entitlement list is unchanged; only the selection mechanism moved from host arch to file content.

## A/B evidence

The screenshots are attached as review evidence and are not part of the PR code diff.

### A — current Forge defaults produce a valid seal but Node crashes

![Before: x64 V8 crashes with exit 133](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-3896/.issue-assets/pr-3896/a-before-intel-node-crash.png)

The final x64 Node has `allow-jit` but not `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. The outer app seal is valid, yet JavaScript hits the reported V8 `SetPermissions` assertion and exits 133.

### B — the selector signs the same Node with the required x64 entitlement

![After: x64 Node executes JavaScript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-3896/.issue-assets/pr-3896/b-after-intel-node-runs.png)

The same signed Node and command exit 0. This exercises the exact Packager → osx-sign → nested Node/V8 boundary changed by the PR.

## Remaining for #3879

The change that reaches users is the canonical signer's entitlement step in the private release repository. This PR ships the public contract (`desktop-release.md`), the content-based reference implementation (`machoHasX86_64Slice`), and the local diagnostic; `Closes` returns once the conductor side lands:

1. its signing step applies the entitlements per the documented contract (x64-slice predicate, fail-closed);
2. its final-artifact verifier inspects the nested Node and executes the final x64 zip on a native Intel runner.

title: fix(browser): re-measure preview bounds on OS-level window resize/move
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2491.

The native browser preview's `WebContentsView` bounds are computed entirely
renderer-side (`useBrowserView`): a `ResizeObserver` on the placeholder slot
plus a `window` `resize`/`scroll` listener measure the slot and send bounds
to the main process (`browser:setBounds`), which clamps and applies them
directly via `view.setBounds()`.

There was no main-process listener for the `BrowserWindow`'s own
`resize`/`move`/`maximize`/`unmaximize` events. All re-sync depended
entirely on the renderer's own DOM signals firing for those OS-level
changes — which the issue's traced investigation flagged as the likely
fragility behind the view rendering at stale/misaligned bounds.

## Fix

- `main.ts`: forward `resize`/`move`/`maximize`/`unmaximize` from the
  `BrowserWindow` to the renderer over a new `window:remeasure` IPC event
  (mirrors the existing `window:fullscreen` channel/pattern).
- `preload.ts`: expose it as `window.ao.window.onRemeasure`.
- `useBrowserView.ts`: settle-measure (immediate + ~280ms settle re-measure)
  on that signal, the same handling already used for pop-out and inspector
  collapse/expand transitions — both of those are also position-only shifts
  the `ResizeObserver` alone can miss.

This closes the gap called out in the issue without guessing at the
DPI/compositor-level question (Wayland vs X11 vs fractional scaling) — it
makes bounds re-sync independent of whether the DOM's own resize signals
fire for a given OS-level window change, on any platform.

## Tests

- Added a renderer test asserting a `window:remeasure` signal triggers a
  re-measure and re-send of bounds using the slot's latest geometry.
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.test.tsx
  src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts` — 82 passed.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- Full `npx vitest run` — only pre-existing failures in unrelated
  `src/landing/**` tests (missing `cheerio` dependency in that
  subproject), no relation to this change.

title: bug(agent-switch): local-zone activity_last_at strands the switch saga in stopping_source and makes the daemon unbootable
body:
### Summary

An agent switch can strand itself in `stopping_source` with no way out, and the daemon then **refuses to start at all**: boot reconciliation returns the same error the switch failed with, so the whole app is unusable until the row is repaired by hand.

The root cause is not in the saga. It is a storage detail: `sessions.activity_last_at` is written from a bare `time.Now()` in two places, and the SQLite driver stores a `time.Time` by its `String()` form.

### Root cause

`modernc.org/sqlite` stores a `time.Time` by its `String()` rendering, so a value written from a local-zone clock keeps both its offset and its monotonic reading:

```
2026-06-28 18:45:08.349363 +0800 CST m=+25660.013723251     <- what a local clock leaves
2026-06-28 10:45:08.349363 +0000 UTC                        <- what every other writer produces
```

`activity_last_at` is compared **directly in SQL**, and SQLite compares these as strings. A `+0800` wall clock sorts *above* the UTC rendering of a later instant, so such a row stops behaving like a timestamp.

`MarkSessionAgentSwitchSourceStopped` gates on `activity_last_at <= stopped_at`. Against a mismatched row it matches **zero rows** — which the caller reads as "ownership changed concurrently", not as "the timestamp is malformed".

The two writers producing these values:

- `backend/internal/observe/reaper/reaper.go` — default clock
- `backend/internal/observe/activity/observer.go` — its `now`, which becomes the observation `Timestamp`

### Impact chain

1. Source agent is already stopped, but the confirm matches 0 rows → `confirmed=false`, `err=nil`.
2. Saga stays in `stopping_source`; the in-memory operation gate stays held.
3. Resume answers `AGENT_RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` (misleading — nothing is resuming, a *switch* is stuck).
4. Repeating the switch fails identically.
5. `Manager.Reconcile` propagates the error at boot → **the daemon does not start**.

On one affected profile, 184 session rows carried the malformed form.

### Fix (PR to follow)

Three levels, because each alone leaves a gap:

- **Sources** — both clocks emit UTC.
- **Storage** — `normalActivity` normalizes `LastActivityAt` to UTC on every write path, rather than trusting each caller's clock.
- **Data** — a migration rewrites rows already stored in the local-zone form.

The store-level regression test fails without the storage fix with exactly the production symptom: `confirmed=false, err=nil`.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

Two things worth flagging separately, not fixed here:

- A single stranded saga making the daemon unbootable is arguably its own bug — boot reconciliation could quarantine the row instead of refusing to start.
- Saga reconciliation runs only at daemon boot; there is no periodic pass and no state timeout, so a saga stuck mid-flight stays stuck until a restart.

Also note `AGENT_RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` does not distinguish operation kind, which is why a stuck *switch* reports itself as a *resume* and sends you looking in the wrong place.

title: fix(sessions): store activity timestamps in UTC so SQL comparisons hold
body:
Fixes #3899.

An agent switch could strand itself in `stopping_source` with no way out: the source agent was already gone, resume answered `AGENT_RESUME_IN_PROGRESS`, a repeat switch failed the same way, and the daemon then **refused to start** because boot reconciliation returned the same error.

The cause is a storage detail, not a saga bug. `modernc.org/sqlite` stores a `time.Time` by its `String()` form, so a value written from a local-zone clock keeps its offset and monotonic reading:

```
2026-06-28 18:45:08.349363 +0800 CST m=+25660.013723251
```

instead of the form every other writer produces:

```
2026-06-28 10:45:08.349363 +0000 UTC
```

`activity_last_at` is compared directly in SQL, and SQLite compares these as strings — a `+0800` wall clock sorts above the UTC rendering of a *later* instant. `MarkSessionAgentSwitchSourceStopped` gates on `activity_last_at <= stopped_at`, so against such a row it matches zero rows, which the caller reads as "ownership changed concurrently".

### Changes

Three levels, because each alone leaves a gap:

- **Sources** — `observe/reaper/reaper.go` and `observe/activity/observer.go` emit UTC.
- **Storage** — `normalActivity` normalizes `LastActivityAt` on every write path, rather than trusting each caller's clock. This is the durable guard: a future writer with a bare `time.Now()` cannot reintroduce the bug.
- **Data** — migration `0088` rewrites rows already stored in the local-zone form.

### Migration notes

The migration matches on `activity_last_at NOT LIKE '% +0000 UTC'` rather than on the monotonic suffix, because both shapes occur in the wild (`… +0700 +07 m=+995.1` and `… +0700 +07`). The offset is located by search rather than at a fixed column, since Go trims trailing zeros from fractional seconds and that moves the sign's position. Fractional digits are carried over verbatim — `strftime`'s `%f` renders milliseconds only and would truncate microseconds.

### Tests

- `agent_switching_store_test.go` — fails without the storage change with exactly the production symptom: `confirmed=false, err=nil`.
- `migrate_activity_zone_test.go` — 6 cases (monotonic, short fraction, no-monotonic local zone, midnight crossing, west-of-UTC, already-canonical). It reads via `CAST(activity_last_at AS TEXT)`: scanning the column into a string lets the driver re-render it as RFC 3339 and hide the very difference under test.

Verified on an affected profile: 184 malformed rows → 0, the stranded saga moved `stopping_source` → `failed`, and the daemon boots again with sessions intact.

title: fix(terminal): bound retained terminals and stop black-pane latches
body:
Refs #2333, #3803, #3787.

Terminal panes go black and stay black: the backend session is healthy, tmux has the content, but the pane paints nothing. Switching away and back does not help; only restarting the app clears it — which is why it reads as intermittent.

Two independent causes, both addressed here.

### 1. The retained-terminal cache is unbounded

`MAX_RETAINED_TERMINALS = 6` was removed in 4986af7d0 ("fix: retain terminals without eviction"). Since then every visited session keeps a mounted xterm — with its WebGL context and its mux lease — for the entire lifetime of the renderer process. Past Chromium's per-page WebGL context cap, the browser forcibly loses the *oldest* contexts, so the panes that go black are the ones visited earliest, not the ones doing anything wrong.

This restores the six-entry LRU. Eviction deletes the cache entry rather than only removing the host node: dropping the entry drops its portal on the next render, which unmounts `XtermTerminal` and releases both the terminal instance and its mux lease. Removing the container alone would clean up the DOM node and leak the rest.

The currently-active terminal is never evicted, and eviction considers only parked entries.

### 2. Activation and replay had no failure path

The activation state machine (`parked → preparing → ready → revealed → visible`) holds the pane at `visibility: hidden` during `preparing`. Any throw or rejection between those states leaves the cover on permanently — a black pane over a perfectly healthy session. Five such latches are closed:

- `showLatestOutput` wrapped, so a scroll failure costs one imperfect redraw instead of the pane
- a bounded watchdog on `prepareForActivation` (plus try/catch around `scheduleStableFit`), so a fit that never settles cannot hold the cover forever
- rejection handlers on the three `.then()` chains that drive attach, cached activation, and replay paint

The `replayPaintPending` latch was found by the added test rather than by reading the code: the opaque cover was never lifted when the replay-paint promise rejected.

### Relationship to the WebGL-loss work

The context-loss fallback in xuelongmu/agent-orchestrator#209 addresses the *reaction* to a lost WebGL context. This change removes the *accumulation* that causes contexts to be lost in the first place. They compose; neither subsumes the other.

### Tests

`TerminalPane.test.tsx` covers retention up to the cap and eviction of the oldest parked entry beyond it, plus the two rejection paths. 39 tests pass on this branch.

Note that `src/renderer/components/settings/AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx` fails on this branch — it fails identically on an untouched `main`, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

title: fix(restore): fall back to a fresh launch when the native conversation is gone
body:
A session whose provider never persisted a conversation cannot be restored: every attempt resolves to a native resume against an id the agent has never heard of, and fails with

```
No conversation found with session ID: <uuid>
```

on every retry. The work in the session's workspace — its branch and commits — is still there, but unreachable through the UI.

This happens when a session is torn down before its first turn, or when a switch away from it fails after the source has already stopped.

### Cause

`GetRestoreCommand` returns `ok=true` for any id it can produce, including a deterministically computed UUID that was reserved but never used. Having an id is treated as proof that a conversation exists behind it, so restore always chooses `--resume` and always fails.

### Fix

Ask the agent before trusting the id. `ports.AgentInterfaceHandoffHistoryProbe` already exists for exactly this distinction — it is implemented by both claude-code and codex — but was only consulted on interface transitions, never on the restore path. When it reports the conversation missing, relaunch into the same workspace instead.

Agents that cannot answer (no probe, or a probe that errors) are treated as *present*, so this never turns a restore that might work into one that refuses.

The promptless relaxation is deliberately narrow — `allowPromptless = conversationLost`, not an unconditional `true`. Reaching the point of reserving an id is not the same as having nothing to restore, but a worker that never got that far (no id **and** no prompt) must stay unresumable; two existing tests guard that case and a broader relaxation breaks them.

### Tests

`TestRestore_LostNativeConversationRelaunchesFresh` fails without the change with `restore mode = "native"` — the doomed path. `TestRestore_PromptlessWorkerNotResumable` and `TestRestore_AgyAndCopilotPromptlessWorkersWithoutAgentSessionIDNotResumable` still pass, confirming the narrower case is untouched.

Verified live: `POST /resume-agent` returned 200 with `"resumeMode":"saved_prompt"` and the agent came up in its own worktree with all commits intact.

### Adjacent, not fixed here

`POST /restore` returns 409 `SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` for an `exited` session with `is_terminated=0`, because it requires `IsTerminated=true` (#2702). `/resume-agent` is the correct path for that state and is what the UI button uses.

title: fix(browser): position preview view against content-view bounds, not screen coordinates
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2491.

`clampBoundsToWindow()` in `browser-view-host.ts` clamped the incoming
renderer-measured rect against `mainWindow.getContentBounds()`. On a
`BaseWindow`, `getContentBounds()` returns the window's bounds in **screen**
coordinates (`{x, y, width, height}` with `x`/`y` being the window's position
on the display), not bounds relative to the content view's own origin.

`view.setBounds()` on a child `WebContentsView` expects coordinates relative
to the parent content view (`{0, 0, width, height}`-origin) — the same space
`window-composition.ts` already uses via `contentView.getBounds()` to
position the shell view itself.

Since `clampBoundsToWindow()` only reads `.width`/`.height` off the passed
bounds (not `.x`/`.y`), this mismatch didn't show up as a naive off-by-x/y
sizing bug in every case, but it does mean the preview view's positioning
logic was built on the wrong coordinate space, and any future width/height
derivation (or a window not positioned at the primary display's origin,
which is exactly the reporter's repro) can push the view off its intended
slot — matching the symptom described in the issue (browser view rendered
offset from the placeholder UI).

## Fix

Use `mainWindow.contentView.getBounds()` (content-view-relative) instead of
`mainWindow.getContentBounds()` (screen-relative) when clamping the incoming
bounds, with a fallback to `getContentBounds()` for hosts that don't expose
`contentView.getBounds()` (kept for type-compat / older test mocks).

## Tests

- Updated `browser-view-host.test.ts` mocks to model a window that is *not*
  at the display's top-left corner (`getContentBounds` now returns nonzero
  `x`/`y`), so the mock no longer accidentally hides screen-vs-content-view
  coordinate confusion.
- Added a regression test asserting the view is clamped against the content
  view's own (0,0-origin) bounds rather than the window's screen position.

```
cd frontend
npx vitest run src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts   # 56 passed
npx vitest run src/main/                            # 313 passed, 1 skipped
npx tsc --noEmit -p .                                # clean
```

## Notes

The issue also raises a separate, unconfirmed concern about a missing
main-process window move/resize listener (all re-sync is renderer-driven).
That's left as a follow-up — this PR addresses the coordinate-space bug
that's independently reproducible regardless of the resize-listener gap.

title: fix(scm): make PR attribution strict and stable
body:
Code changes: +45 -90  
Tests: +242 -72  
Others: +0 -0  

## Summary

- Require a known authenticated human identity matching the PR author before creating a new automatic attachment, independently for each supported provider/host. Remove the legacy single-identity fallback.
- Keep the existing head-repository guard; prefer exact branches, then the longest stack namespace. Reject equal-ranked matches between distinct sessions.
- Preserve explicit `claim-pr` validation and takeover behavior, including claims of another author's PR.
- Keep existing attachments stable while refreshing PR metadata, CI, reviews, and merged/closed status. Remove ownership reconciliation, attachment provenance, detach operations, and the migration.
- Clear incomplete discovery ETags/cursors when identity is unavailable so recovery retries a full listing, even after the incremental overlap window.

## Tests

- Regression coverage includes mismatched/missing authors; missing, bot, and failed identities; provider/host isolation; ambiguous matches in either order; duplicate candidates for one session; identity recovery with cold, changed, and unchanged ETags; and durable automatic/explicit attachments.
- Integration tests exercise the production multi-provider dispatcher with real SQLite and lifecycle handling.
- Passed locally on the merged source: focused observer/integration/storage/session suites; build; vet; clean golangci-lint v2.12.2; sqlc regeneration without drift; and race-enabled SCM observer/integration packages.
- The local full race sweep reached the repository tail but had unrelated timing/concurrency failures in `TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination` and `TestModelsSerializeBinaryResolutionPerAdapter`.
- All eleven remote checks passed on `3a3774ab26c53d6feec13073290a6849c2107987`, including the complete backend race suite, Windows workspace tests, CLI E2E on Linux/macOS/Windows, container smoke test, lint, secret scan, and SQL/API drift checks.
- Frontend typecheck could not run in this worktree because frontend dependencies are not installed; this PR has no frontend diff and remote CI covers the merged source.

## Scope

Historical incorrect attachments are intentionally left untouched. Repairing existing associations is deferred, rather than guessing user intent or undoing an explicit claim.

Related to #3259.

title: fix(terminal): defer xterm disposal and force the activation resize
body:
Refs #2333, #3803, #3787.

Stacked on #3901 — please review that one first; this PR's diff is the last commit only.

Two independent hardening changes around terminal activation and teardown. Neither is the primary black-pane fix; both close windows that can produce the same visible symptom.

### 1. Deferred disposal — a port of #3804

**This is not my work.** #3804 is open and unmerged; I am carrying its fix here because it becomes materially more relevant after #3901. Happy to drop this half if #3804 lands first, or to close it in favor of that PR.

xterm 5.5 schedules `Viewport.syncScrollArea` with a zero-delay timer during `open()`. Disposing in that same task clears `RenderService`'s renderer first, so the pending callback throws while reading its dimensions. Detaching listeners and the transport stays synchronous; only the final `term.dispose()` moves behind one macrotask, and every AO listener and attachment is already detached by then, so the terminal is inert for that tick.

Why it matters more now: #3901 restores an LRU cap on retained terminals, which means eviction disposes terminals far more often than the previous unbounded retention ever did. A race that was rare under "never dispose anything" is no longer rare.

### 2. Force the activation resize

The activation promote could never reach the daemon in the most common case.

A parked terminal reattaches at 0×0 and is then refitted back to the size it already had, so the grid being republished is usually byte-identical to `lastPublishedGrid`. `syncVisibleSize` returned early on exactly that equality, and even without the early return the daemon deduplicates repeat resizes — there is an explicit test for that, `TestServeDeduplicatesResizeUnlessExplicitlyForced`. So tmux was never asked to redraw, and the pane could stay blank.

The `force` flag already existed in the mux protocol and the backend already honored it. The renderer simply never sent it. Now this one activation path sends `force: true`; ordinary resizes stay deduplicated, preserving the behavior that backend test guards.

### Tests

The forced-resize regression fails without the change with an empty resize list — the daemon received nothing at all.

Note `src/renderer/components/settings/AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx` fails on this branch; it fails identically on an untouched `main`, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

title: fix: hide Codex app-server window on Windows
body:
## Summary

- add a Windows-only regression test for `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and `HideWindow`

A controlled AOS-Bridge -> AO Chat REST task completed with `BRIDGE_OK`, then left `codex.exe app-server` and a visible Windows Terminal host alive. The live chain was AO daemon PID 8976 -> Codex app-server PID 13940; Windows created OpenConsole PID 33580 and WindowsTerminal PID 21792 with a nonzero window handle and the Codex path as its title. `spawnAppServer` used raw `exec.Command`, unlike AO's other Windows launchers.

The app-server is intentionally session-owned for follow-up turns; this change fixes the visible console without treating it as an unowned process or killing unrelated tasks/runtimes.

## Tests

- Windows regression test added: `TestConfigureAppServerProcessHidesConsoleWindow`
- AOS-Bridge full suite: 29/29 pass; TypeScript typecheck pass
- Go tests not run locally: the reproduction host does not have a Go toolchain installed; CI requested

## Safety
No Bridge code or AOS/IBKR runtime policy changed. No process enumeration or name-based killing is introduced. Parallel sessions and existing session-scoped cleanup remain unchanged.

title: Board conflates technical recovery states with human “Needs you”
body:
## Summary

The session board currently maps `no_signal`, `exited`, `ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, and `unknown` into the same `action` zone as `needs_input`. The zone label is “Needs you,” so routine technical recovery work is presented as requiring a human decision.

This makes the board’s attention contract unreliable: users cannot tell a genuine input request from a hook failure, crashed process, failing CI, or agent-owned review correction.

## Current behavior

On current `main`:

- `packages/product-ui/src/session-presentation.ts` defines `zone.action` as “Needs you.”
- `attentionZone()` maps `needs_input`, `exited`, `no_signal`, `ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, and `unknown` to that zone.
- Desktop board, command-palette, adapter, and tests consume the shared presentation model.
- Existing tests encode `no_signal -> action` as intended behavior.

A real session with a broken/missing hook receipt therefore appears in “Needs you” even when there is no question the user can answer.

## Expected behavior

Reserve “Needs you” for a genuine user-input or user-decision state. Give technical recovery states a distinct, truthful presentation such as “Technical attention” (exact copy can follow the existing product vocabulary), without hiding their status badges or severity.

## Implementation contract

1. Add a distinct technical attention zone to the shared product-UI presentation model rather than relabeling all action states.
2. Keep `needs_input` in the human “Needs you” zone.
3. Move at least `no_signal`, `exited`, `ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, and `unknown` into the technical zone.
4. Preserve each session’s specific status badge (“No signal,” “CI failed,” and so on); the column/zone communicates attention ownership, not a replacement status.
5. Update board ordering, counts, empty states, responsive layout, command-palette grouping/filtering, sidebar/attention helpers, accessibility labels, and translations/adapters that depend on the closed `AttentionZone` union.
6. Keep desktop and any shared/mobile consumers semantically aligned through `packages/product-ui`; do not duplicate a second classification table in the renderer.
7. Ensure a technical state does not trigger user-input-specific affordances or copy. It may remain visually prominent and discoverable.
8. Do not infer that AO itself will automatically repair every technical state. The UI claim is only that the state is technical rather than a human question.
9. Do not change backend session-status derivation, hook grace windows, CI/review lifecycle rules, or SessionStart receipt handling in this ticket.
10. Preserve terminated/archive behavior and existing merge/review/working classifications.

## Acceptance checks

- Table-driven tests cover every `SessionStatus` and assert exactly one attention zone.
- `needs_input` remains under “Needs you.”
- `no_signal`, `exited`, `ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, and `unknown` render under the technical zone and never under “Needs you.”
- Board column counts/order and empty states are correct with mixed human, technical, review, working, and merge-ready sessions.
- Command-palette and sidebar helpers distinguish human input from technical attention.
- Status-specific badges and inspector timelines remain unchanged.
- Keyboard navigation, accessible names, narrow-width behavior, and shared/mobile adapters remain valid.
- Existing product-UI, desktop renderer, typecheck, lint, and snapshot suites pass.

## Non-goals

- No new backend status or workflow engine.
- No external tracker/capacity integration.
- No promise of automatic remediation.
- No change to the separate false-`no_signal` fixes in #2604 / #3315 and PRs #2622 / #3316.

## Why this is separate

Receipt fixes can reduce false `no_signal`, but genuine technical failures will still occur. Even with perfect status detection, the board needs to distinguish who owns the next action.

title: fix(desktop): stop Cmd+Alt+I from crashing the main process on macOS
body:
Pressing the DevTools shortcut on macOS takes down the main process:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toggleDevTools')
  at webContentsMethod (node:electron/js2c/browser_init)
  at Object.execute / MenuItem.click / a._executeCommand
```

The user sees the "A JavaScript error occurred in the main process" dialog and the app is gone.

### Cause

The trace runs through `MenuItem.click`, so the failure is in Electron's **default** menu, not in any AO handler. `buildWindowsAppMenu` is gated on `win32`, so macOS never installed an application menu and the default one stayed active — including its View → Toggle Developer Tools entry, which uses the built-in `role: "toggleDevTools"`.

That role resolves its target as `focusedWindow.webContents`. In AO focus normally sits on a `WebContentsView` (the Browser panel) rather than on the `BrowserWindow`, so the role reads `webContents` off `undefined`.

Worth noting that AO's own three DevTools paths were already guarded against exactly this — the toolbar shortcut, the `menu:action` IPC handler, and the Windows menu item. Only the default menu was outside that guard, which is why the crash looked arbitrary: it depended on where focus happened to be.

### Fix

Install a macOS application menu so the crashing role is never used. Every other entry stays a role; DevTools routes through the same guarded toggle the other three paths already use, extracted here as `toggleDevToolsForFocusedSurface` and shared with the Windows menu.

The app submenu (`about`/`services`/`hide`/`hideOthers`/`unhide`/`quit`) is spelled out deliberately: replacing the default menu also replaces the standard items, and silently losing Cmd+Q would be a worse regression than the bug being fixed. There is a test pinning those roles for that reason.

### Verification

Beyond the unit tests, I confirmed against the built bundle that the shipped macOS View menu carries `{label: "Toggle Developer Tools", accelerator: "Alt+Command+I", click: …}` with no `role`, and that `setApplicationMenu` runs on the `darwin` branch. Cmd+Opt+I now opens DevTools for the focused surface instead of terminating the main process.



Closes #4308

title: fix(ui): separate technical attention from Needs you
body:
## What

- add a shared `technical` attention zone and keep `needs_input` exclusively in human-facing **Needs you**
- classify `no_signal`, `exited`, `ci_failed`, `changes_requested`, and `unknown` as technical attention
- update the five-lane board order, counts, zero states, accessibility labels, command-palette quota/order, tray presentation, translations, and responsive desktop layout
- align the existing mobile adapter, section order, counts, and narrow-screen stats with the shared product contract

## Why

The previous presentation contract grouped technical failures and review blockers under **Needs you**, conflating sessions that require human input with sessions that need technical investigation. This change separates those concepts without changing backend status derivation or the status-specific badge and timeline semantics.

Fixes #3909

## Scope

This is intentionally a product-UI contract change only. It does not change SessionStart, hook grace periods, restore behavior, routing, controllers, or backend status derivation. Native/toast input notifications also remain specific to `needs_input`.

## Compatibility notes

- Mobile has no dependency on `@aoagents/product-ui`, whose public entry also exports DOM components. Its existing adapter is therefore kept semantically aligned through an exhaustive status table instead of adding a broader package/Metro dependency.
- Concrete mobile technical statuses now override a stale generic server attention bucket; explicit `unknown` is technical, while an absent/null status retains the existing working fallback.
- The tray attention-zone union is internal and ephemeral; it now carries `technical` alongside `action` and `merge`, with no persisted wire migration.

## Validation

title: bug(reviews): default reviewer label ignores the worker's harness, naming claude-code while a different agent runs
body:
## Summary

The Review panel's default-reviewer label does not agree with the daemon's own resolution rule. For a worker whose harness is not `claude-code`, and whose project configures no reviewer, the picker reads `claude-code` while the review actually runs on the worker's harness.

Observed with a Codex worker: the picker showed `claude-code`, and pressing Run started Codex. Choosing `Claude Code` explicitly from the menu is what makes the label and the run agree, because that writes a session-level preference and both sides then take the same first branch.

## Root cause

The daemon resolves the reviewer in four steps (`Engine.reviewerHarness` → `ProjectConfig.ResolveReviewerHarness`):

1. session preference (`sessions.reviewer_harness`)
2. project config `reviewers[0].harness`
3. **the worker's own harness**, when that harness is one of the inherited set (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `muse`, `kimchi`)
4. `claude-code` as the final fallback

The renderer computes the same label in three steps and omits step 3 (`SessionInspector.tsx`):

```ts
const harness = latest?.harness || config?.reviewers?.[0]?.harness || "claude-code";
```

With no prior run and no project reviewer, the frontend jumps straight to the `claude-code` fallback while the daemon stops one step earlier at the worker's harness. Every non-`claude-code` inherited worker is mislabeled.

## Secondary: the label is a wire id, not a display name

The same label is rendered from the raw harness id rather than the existing display-name table, so the trigger reads `claude-code` while the menu entry for the very same agent reads `Claude Code`. The two look like two different, separately selectable agents, which is what makes the mismatch read as "there are two claude-code entries and the lowercase one is wrong".

A third source of lowercase labels: `ReviewerSelect` builds its pre-catalog fallback options as `{ id, label: id }`, so before `/api/v1/agents` resolves the whole menu is lowercase ids, then flips to proper names once the catalog arrives.

## Reproduction

1. Start a worker on a harness other than `claude-code` (e.g. Codex) in a project with no `reviewers` entry.
2. Open the session inspector, Reviews section, before any review has run.
3. The reviewer picker reads `claude-code`.
4. Press Run — the review runs on the worker's harness, not claude-code.

## Expected

The picker names the agent the daemon would actually pick, and names it with its display name.

## Note

The current behaviour is pinned by a test asserting the lowercase fallback for a Codex worker, so fixing this necessarily updates that expectation.

title: fix(desktop): label the default reviewer with its display name
body:

- The `__default__` menu entry (`defaultOptionLabel={resolvedDefaultHarness}`) shows `codex` instead of `Codex`.
- The "Review in progress · ${activeReviewerHarness}" strip shows the same raw id.

Now that the default is resolved dynamically rather than hardcoded to `claude-code`, this is more visible: the same agent can read as two different names within the same menu (raw id for the default entry, display name for every other catalog entry).

## Change

Builds on #3959 — reuses its harness-resolution logic unchanged and only wraps the label-facing strings in `agentLabel()`:

- `ReviewerSelect.tsx`: fallback agent entries now label with `agentLabel(id)` instead of the bare id.
- `SessionInspector.tsx`: `defaultOptionLabel` and the "Review in progress" strip now go through `agentLabel()`.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (pre-existing unrelated `motion/react` module error in `packages/product-ui` aside).

title: fix(frontend): skip slide-in spring for sidebar peek overlay
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #3372: the sidebar hover-preview vanished before the cursor could reach it.
- Root cause: while the peek overlay slides in via a Motion spring transition, the global `pointermove` handler in `_shell.tsx` reads `getBoundingClientRect()` on the sidebar container to decide whether to keep it open. During the animation that rect reflects the mid-transition position, not the resting one, so the 140ms auto-close timer can fire before the slide-in settles.
- Fix: when the sidebar renders as a peek overlay (`overlay` prop), skip the spring transition so it appears at its resting position instantly — matching the "cleanest" option suggested in the issue. This removes the race entirely since `getBoundingClientRect()` is correct from t=0.

- [x] `npm test` (vitest) — `Sidebar.test.tsx` passes (54/54); remaining failures are pre-existing/unrelated (landing-page tests missing the `cheerio` dependency)

title: [Feature]: Codex reviewers cannot configure model or reasoning effort independently
body:
### Problem

As a user who assigns different responsibilities to implementation workers and reviewers, I need to configure the Codex reviewer's model and reasoning effort independently because the best cost/performance profile for implementation is not necessarily the best profile for review.

For example, I may want to run:

- Worker: `gpt-5.6-luna` with `max` reasoning
- Reviewer: `gpt-5.6-sol` with `xhigh` reasoning

Today AO lets a project choose the reviewer harness, but the Codex reviewer does not expose reviewer-specific model or reasoning-effort configuration. It therefore falls back to the Codex/default configuration rather than allowing the reviewer role to be tuned independently.

Changing the user's global Codex configuration is not a good substitute because that also affects unrelated Codex sessions.

A local workaround is to hard-code `--model` and `model_reasoning_effort` into the Codex reviewer launch arguments, but that is not suitable as a general solution.

### Proposed direction

Allow reviewer configuration to optionally carry Codex model and reasoning-effort overrides, independently from worker and orchestrator configuration.

Conceptually, something like:

```yaml
reviewers:
  - harness: codex
    agentConfig:
      model: gpt-5.6-sol
      reasoningEffort: xhigh
```

The exact schema is up to the maintainers.

Expected behavior:

- Reviewer model can be configured independently.
- Reviewer reasoning effort can be configured independently.
- When unset, current/default behavior remains unchanged.
- Reviewer settings do not affect workers or orchestrators.
- Invalid reasoning-effort values fail validation instead of silently falling back.
- Existing Codex reviewer read-only/sandbox behavior remains unchanged.
- The configuration applies consistently to reviewer launches and subsequent review passes.

Related: #3166 adds per-role Codex model and reasoning configuration for workers and orchestrators. Extending the same underlying configuration concept to the reviewer path may provide a consistent model.

This request is specifically for reviewer configuration; it does not require changing the default reviewer model or hard-coding a particular model.

### Alternatives considered

I considered a few workarounds:

- Hard-code `--model` and `model_reasoning_effort` in the Codex reviewer launch arguments. This works locally, but it is not configurable and is not suitable as an upstream solution.
- Change the global Codex configuration. This affects unrelated Codex sessions and does not provide reviewer-specific behavior.
- Reuse the worker/orchestrator model configuration for reviewers. This couples roles that may intentionally need different cost/performance profiles.

A reviewer-specific optional configuration seems preferable because it preserves the current defaults while allowing projects to tune review independently.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: bug(scm): stale transferred PR row can surface false merge conflict
body:
## Bug
AO can continue to show a resolved/nonexistent merge conflict for a PR after the PR has moved from the old `AgentWrapper` GitHub URL to the current `Untrivial-ai` URL. GitHub and the current AO PR observation both say the PR is not conflicted, but the desktop still surfaces a stale `Merge conflict` state from an old PR row attached to the same session.

**Source:** local user report in AO desktop on August 13, 2026  
**Analyzed against:** `461a6df56` (`origin/main`, `feat: add per-PR CI failure injection policy (#3772)`)  
**AO daemon under test:** locally built `/tmp/ao`, `dev`, loopback daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced from the daemon API and traced to stale PR rows/aliasing.

## Screenshots

![PR card shows stale merge conflict](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-stale-pr-conflict-2870/.issue-assets/stale-pr-conflict-2870/pr-card.png)

![Activity rail shows Conflict](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-stale-pr-conflict-2870/.issue-assets/stale-pr-conflict-2870/activity-conflict.png)

## Reproduction / observed state

Live case: [PR #2870](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2870), session `agent-orchestrator-31`.

GitHub reports the current PR as mergeable but blocked on review/branch protection, not conflict:

```json
{
  "url": "https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2870",
  "mergeable": "MERGEABLE",
  "mergeStateStatus": "BLOCKED",
  "reviewDecision": "REVIEW_REQUIRED",
  "headRefOid": "b960b45af86951ff3770a8f51ae4d2fffcd4d22f"
}
```

AO's session API returns both the current PR row and a stale row from the old repo owner:

```json
{
  "prs": [
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2870",
      "number": 2870,
      "mergeability": "blocked",
      "updatedAt": "2026-08-13T03:08:46.531282Z"
    },
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2870",
      "number": 2870,
      "mergeability": "conflicting",
      "updatedAt": "2026-07-26T16:19:15.891494Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

The detailed PR endpoint also returns both rows. The stale `AgentWrapper` row has old provider mergeability values:

```text
url=https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2870
head_sha=6273ce786a300757e2cdcf2f2d6ea59ea4435992
mergeability=conflicting
provider_mergeable=CONFLICTING
provider_merge_state_status=DIRTY
updated_at=2026-07-26 16:19:15 UTC
```

The current row is correct:

```text
url=https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2870
head_sha=b960b45af86951ff3770a8f51ae4d2fffcd4d22f
mergeability=blocked
provider_mergeable=MERGEABLE
provider_merge_state_status=BLOCKED
updated_at=2026-08-13 03:08:46 UTC
```

## Root Cause

The issue appears to be AO local state/enrichment, not GitHub/SCM:

- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/pr.sql` returns all PR rows attached to the session via `ListPRsBySession` / `ListPRFactsBySession`.
- `backend/internal/service/session/pr_summary.go` groups aliases via `groupPullRequestAliases` before returning `/api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/pr`.
- `backend/internal/service/session/pr_alias.go` only collapses transferred-repo aliases when the alias key matches. When source branch and head SHA are present, the key includes the head SHA. In this live case the old `AgentWrapper` row has an older head SHA, so it does not collapse with the current `Untrivial-ai` row.
- The stale row remains `open` and `conflicting`, so the desktop can render its obsolete conflict state even though the canonical/current PR is not conflicted.

There is also stale `last_nudge_signature` data containing a prior `merge-conflict:` key, but the direct UI problem is reproducible from the stale PR row returned by the API.

## Expected Behavior

If GitHub redirects/resolves an old repo URL to the current PR, AO should not show stale conflicting state from the old URL. The session should surface the current PR facts only, or supersede/close/filter the stale alias row.

## Suggested Fix

Handle repo-transfer/redirect aliases at the daemon/store/read-model boundary. Possible approaches:

1. When observing a PR, if the provider returns a canonical `html_url`/URL different from the requested/stored URL, migrate or supersede the old row instead of keeping both open.
2. In the session PR read model, collapse or filter stale aliases for the same session + PR number + source branch/target branch when one URL is canonical/current and the older URL is the previous repo owner, even if the head SHA changed.
3. Avoid surfacing stale conflict nudges as current state; clear or ignore `merge-conflict:` dedupe entries once `mergeability != conflicting`.

The fix should be careful not to collapse unrelated same-number PRs in different repos. There are already tests in `backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go` around PR aliasing; add a regression for "old owner stale conflicting row + new owner current blocked/mergeable row with newer head".

## Impact

- False-positive merge conflict warnings in desktop.
- Agents/users may waste time rebasing already-mergeable PRs.
- Status cards become inconsistent with GitHub and with the current AO PR observation.

## Related

- [#2173](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2173) — opposite direction (conflict not surfaced), same SCM mergeability area.
- [#1122](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1122) — stale commit data caused noisy lifecycle reactions; not a duplicate, but similar stale SCM-data class.

title: fix(scm): reconcile stale transferred PR rows to prevent false merge conflict
body:
## Summary

- normalize the historical `AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator` and current `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` repository identities before mutable branch/head alias checks
- collapse transferred PR rows by GitHub's stable PR number and retain the newest authoritative observation
- cover the live #2870 shape: stale `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` old-owner row plus newer `MERGEABLE`/`BLOCKED` current-owner row with a different head SHA
- verify a newer genuinely conflicting current observation is still surfaced

## Before / after

Before, both session and detailed PR endpoints returned two rows for transferred PR #2870. The desktop PR card and activity rail could therefore render the stale old-owner row's `conflicting` state.

After, both read models treat those URLs as aliases of the transferred repository and return only the newer current-owner row (`blocked`, `review_required`). Alias handling remains unchanged for unrelated repositories, and a current real conflict still wins.

## Verification

- read-only reproduction against local session `agent-orchestrator-31` through both daemon endpoints
- `cd backend && env -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_SESSION_ID go test ./...`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`

No frontend source changed; the visible card/activity correction follows from the corrected daemon payload, so no separate preview artifact was applicable.

Closes #3922
