- `TestInterfaceTransitionStatusBlocksFreshStartWithoutHistoryProbe` — empty native id + no probe → `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`

title: fix: reset model scope across agent switches
body:
## What

Reset model and mode overrides when switching a conversation between agent harnesses.

- Clear the source harness model/mode before resolving the target launch configuration.
- Persist the switched conversation without retaining stale overrides.
- Reset renderer controls and cached catalog state so the target harness supplies its own defaults.
- Add backend, storage, hook, and dialog regression coverage for both switch directions.

## Why

A model selected for one agent could be reused after switching to a different agent. That stale model might not exist in the target harness and could make the next request fail.

## How

Agent switching now establishes a fresh model scope. The backend clears source overrides and resolves the target harness configuration independently. The renderer mirrors that invariant by resetting selected model/mode state and refetching the target catalog after a successful switch. Sends omit the model when the target is using its default.

The SQLite query was updated and its generated code regenerated through the repository workflow.

## Testing

- `npm run lint`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- Manual Electron verification: Codex → Claude and Claude → Codex, confirming the model resets and `hi` succeeds without a cross-agent model error.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing an existing PR branch (`codex/agent-switching-ux`)
- [x] One focused change; no related issue supplied
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior

title: fix: update Agy hooks for current Antigravity schema
body:
## What

Update the Agy hook integration to use the current Antigravity workspace hook format.

This replaces the legacy Agy hook configuration:

```text
.gemini/hooks.json
SessionStart
SessionEnd
BeforeAgent
AfterAgent
AfterTool
```

with the current Antigravity workspace hook configuration:

```text
.agents/hooks.json
PreInvocation
PostInvocation
PostToolUse
Stop
```

AO keeps its existing internal activity commands:

```text
PreInvocation  -> ao hooks agy before-agent
PostToolUse    -> ao hooks agy after-tool
PostInvocation -> ao hooks agy after-agent
Stop           -> ao hooks agy after-agent
```

## Why

Agy workers could launch and run normally, but AO could still show them as `No signal`.

The generated worktree contained `.gemini/hooks.json`, while current Antigravity did not consume those legacy workspace hooks. AO therefore never received an activity callback, so the worker eventually became `no_signal`.

This was reproduced with a real AO-managed Agy worker:

```text
harness: agy
activity.state: idle
status: no_signal
```

After using the current `.agents/hooks.json` schema, the same session began reporting activity correctly:

```text
harness: agy
activity.state: idle
status: idle
```

A fresh worker was then validated end-to-end and created `.agents/hooks.json` automatically without any manual worktree modification.

## How

- Move Agy workspace hooks to `.agents/hooks.json`.
- Use `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, `PostToolUse`, and `Stop`.
- Preserve AO's existing internal activity event handling.
- Treat `Stop` as idle rather than process/session exit.
- Store AO hooks under a dedicated `agent-orchestrator` top-level definition.
- Preserve unrelated user-defined hooks.
- Make installation idempotent.
- Remove only AO-managed hooks during uninstall.
- Report hooks as installed only when the complete AO-managed definition is present.
- Stop generating legacy `.gemini/hooks.json`.

## Testing

Added/updated tests covering:

- installation into `.agents/hooks.json`
- current Antigravity event mappings
- absence of legacy `.gemini/hooks.json`
- idempotent installation
- preservation of user-defined hooks
- uninstall removing only AO-managed hooks
- incomplete managed definitions reporting as not installed

Validated locally with:

```bash
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... -count=1 -v
go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1
go test ./...
```

Also validated end-to-end with a fresh Agy TUI worker; the worker transitioned to `idle` instead of `no_signal` and generated `.agents/hooks.json` automatically.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch based directly on current upstream `main`
- [x] One focused Agy / Antigravity compatibility fix
- [x] Existing user hooks are preserved
- [x] Hook installation is idempotent
- [x] Legacy `.gemini/hooks.json` is no longer generated
- [x] Fresh Agy worker validated end-to-end
- [x] Relevant Go tests pass

title: [Bug]: Unset defaultBranch still forces workspace roots to main
body:
## Bug

After [#3810](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3810) was fixed for workspace children, an unconfigured workspace root still receives `main` as its base branch. A workspace whose root default branch is `trunk`, `master`, or another non-`main` branch therefore still fails to spawn with `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` unless the user manually configures that branch.

**Source:** Follow-up to [#3810](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3810) | **Reported by:** @subbu-fw | **Analyzed against:** `0f43574f20aa`

**Priority:** medium — workspace spawn is broken for non-`main` roots, but explicitly setting `defaultBranch` is a workaround.

**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Register a workspace whose root repository advertises `origin/HEAD -> origin/trunk` and has no `main` branch.
2. Leave project `defaultBranch` unset.
3. Spawn a worker or orchestrator.
4. Observe `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` for the workspace root.

A deterministic manager regression assertion reproduces the bad handoff:

```shell
cd backend
go test ./internal/session_manager -run '^TestSpawn_WorkspaceProjectRecordsRootAndChildWorktrees$' -count=1
```

Current failure:

```text
root base branch = "main", want empty so adapter infers the repo default
```

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` resolves an unset workspace root with `project.Config.WithDefaults().DefaultBranch`. `ProjectConfig` currently defaults `defaultBranch` to `main`, so the manager passes a non-empty `BaseBranch` to the git-worktree adapter. A non-empty value bypasses the adapter's per-repository `origin/HEAD` inference.

The same default leaks into settings: when config omits the field, the form falls back to the project's resolved `defaultBranch` and can persist `main` while saving unrelated settings.

## Fix

- Make automatic repository-default resolution the default branch-selection mode (`auto`).
- Translate automatic mode to an empty `BaseBranch` only at the workspace interface, where empty means infer `origin/HEAD` per repository.
- Preserve explicitly configured branch refs.
- Keep `main` only as the last-resort Git initialization/adapter fallback.
- Prevent settings saves from turning automatic mode into an explicit `main` pin.
- Cover the root plus mixed child defaults through the manager and real git-worktree adapter tests.

## Impact

- Workspace roots no longer require a `main` branch.
- Single-repository projects also follow their Git default unless explicitly pinned.
- Existing explicit branch configurations keep their current behavior.

## Related

- [#3810](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3810) / [PR #3830](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3830) — fixed per-child branch inheritance.
- [#2329](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2329) — persist child repository default-branch metadata.

title: enhancement(files): git-state-aware diff view — staged/committed sections, aggregate summary, in-app commit
body:
## Summary

The Files panel (`SessionFilesView`) is a capable read-only diff viewer, but it models the worktree as a single "working tree vs base" delta. It does not distinguish what the agent has committed from what is staged or still unstaged, has no commit history, no aggregate +/- summary, and no in-app commit/push. This issue proposes moving to a git-state-aware model and lays out the gaps side by side.

## Current approach (verified)

Backend: `backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go`
- Compares the worktree against a single recorded base (`sessions.diff_base_sha` / `diff_base_ref`, migration 0040), falling back to `head_fallback`.
- One flat file list with statuses `unmodified|modified|added|deleted|renamed` and per-file `additions`/`deletions`.
- Per-file detail on demand: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/file?path=`.
- Caps: 5000 files / 256 KB content / 512 KB diff, with whole-list and per-file truncation.

Frontend: `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFilesView.tsx`
- Search, expand/collapse-all, j/k navigation; unified and split views; virtualization over 150 rows; Web Worker diff parsing; intra-line LCS highlighting.
- Live refresh: SSE invalidation (`subscribeWorkspaceFileChanges`) plus a 30s polling safety net.
- Feedback-native: per-file and per-line annotation, and select-text → Copy / "Explain this change" / "Make these changes", routed to the agent via `/send`.

## Problems & challenges with the current model

1. **No git-state classification.** Everything is one "changed vs base" bucket. When the agent stages some edits, leaves others unstaged, or has already committed work, the panel flattens all of it into one list. You cannot answer "what has landed vs what is still dirty" from the panel.
2. **No commit history.** There is no list of commits made on the session branch, so review is limited to the final working-tree delta; you cannot see the commit series that produced it. (Related closed bug #3203 shows this class already bites: committed work looked like "0 changes".)
3. **No aggregate workspace summary.** The panel shows per-file +N/-N badges but no rollup (files changed / total additions / total deletions). A board or sidebar showing many sessions cannot cheaply surface "+96 -10" without computing full lists.
4. **Read-only + agent-routing only.** There is no in-app edit, commit, or push. A human reviewer who wants to make a small fix or commit the agent's work must leave the app or spend another agent round-trip.
5. **No ahead/behind / upstream context in the panel.** PR facts partially cover mergeability, but the Files panel itself has no branch ahead/behind or push/pull counts.
6. **Whole-list recompute, no revisioned snapshot.** Every refresh/invalidation recomputes the full file list. There is no cached, revisioned status snapshot, no summary-first read path, and no separation of invalidation sources (index vs HEAD vs refs). Large worktrees pay the full git cost on every poll.
7. **Coarse truncation.** Whole-list truncation (5000 files) and per-file diff caps can hide the interesting tail of a large change without a summary that tells you what was cut.

## The alternative (git-state-aware) model

An alternative model structures the workspace diff as a first-class, state-classified capability rather than a single delta. Concretely:

- **Sections by git state**: `against-base`, `committed` (with a commit list), `staged`, `unstaged`, and `untracked` rendered as separate groups, plus branch `ahead`/`behind` and push/pull counts and an `isDirty` flag.
- **Aggregate summary, summary-first reads**: a cheap workspace summary carrying totals (`files`, `additions`, `deletions`) plus per-section counts, so a sidebar can render many sessions' `+A -D` badges without loading patches; only the active workspace subscribes to a live stream.
- **Lazy per-file diff on demand**: full patch text is computed only for files that are visible/open, with an optional small cache evicted when the workspace revision changes.
- **Invalidation-driven refresh, not polling**: a cached status snapshot with a monotonic revision, invalidated from three git-truth sources (worktree filesystem events; git-dir `index`/`HEAD`/`ORIG_HEAD`/`logs/HEAD`; common-dir refs), debounced to a single recompute, and emitting `invalidated` / `status-updated` / `overflow` events that clients use to mark data stale.
- **In-place editing + commit/push**: unstaged files are editable in the viewer with revision-based conflict reconciliation; changes can be committed and pushed from the view.

## Side-by-side

| Capability | AO Files panel (today) | Alternative model | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Changed-files list | ✅ flat list, per-file +/- | ✅ grouped sections | — |
| Git-state classification | ❌ single "vs base/HEAD" bucket | ✅ staged / unstaged / committed / untracked | **Missing** |
| Commit history | ❌ none | ✅ commit list on branch | **Missing** |
| Aggregate workspace summary | ❌ per-file only | ✅ totals + per-section counts, batched for many rows | **Missing** |
| Ahead/behind, push/pull | ❌ (partial via PR facts) | ✅ in the panel | **Missing** |
| Lazy per-file diff | ✅ on expand | ✅ on demand + small cache | Parity |
| Unified/split + intra-line highlight | ✅ | Partial | AO ahead |
| Live refresh | SSE + 30s poll, full-list recompute | Revisioned snapshot, per-source invalidation, debounced | AO recomputes whole list |
| Feedback to the agent | ✅ file/line + explain/make changes | ❌ (edit-first) | AO ahead — keep |
| In-app edit / commit / push | ❌ | ✅ | **Missing** |

## What's missing / what to improve (priority order)

1. **Git-state sections + commit list** — the highest-value gap; directly addresses the "committed work looks like 0 changes" confusion and gives reviewers the commit series.
2. **Aggregate workspace summary (+files/+adds/-dels)** — enables cheap sidebar/board badges and a summary-first read path; also fixes the coarse-truncation blind spot.
3. **In-app commit/push** (editing optional) — at minimum, review-and-commit without leaving the app; full in-place editing can follow.
4. **Revisioned, invalidation-driven snapshot** — replaces whole-list recompute; consistent with the existing SSE plumbing and the broader "remove polling → reactive" direction in #1321.

## Impact

- Reviewers can see what the agent actually committed vs what's still in flight, and commit from the app.
- The board/sidebar can show cheap per-session change badges.
- Removes the "0 changes" confusion for sessions with committed work (recurring theme of #3203/#3857).

## Related

- [#3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) — committed work vs HEAD showed 0 changes (same root-cause class).
- [#3857](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3857) — compare-base selection hardening.
- [#1321](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1321) — remove polling in favor of reactive sync (the invalidation piece).
- [#3641](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3641) — inline review-comment drafting limitations (feedback side of the panel).

**Priority:** medium (enhancement; workarounds exist via external git). **Analyzed against:** `9b8395e`.

title: fix(workspace): resolve automatic repository defaults
body:
## Summary

- make `auto` the default branch-selection mode without treating it as a literal Git branch
- choose each repository's primary remote using `checkout.defaultRemote`, then `origin`, then a sole remote
- resolve the live symbolic remote `HEAD`, fetch that exact branch, and fall back only to the same remote's cached `HEAD`
- allow an already-fetched request-specific remote branch to seed a session even when the remote has no symbolic `HEAD`
- resolve every repository in a workspace before creating session branches, preventing partial workspace state
- persist each repository's resolved base ref so diffs can recompute the merge base after rebases or upstream advances
- preserve explicit branch settings and AO-initialized remoteless repositories, including backfilling repositories created by older AO versions
- return `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` with repository-specific Git remediation instead of guessing the current branch, `main`, or `master`
- omit the internal `auto` sentinel from agent branch context

Fixes #3981

## Behavior

A temporary local checkout no longer changes the base branch AO selects. Workspace roots and child repositories resolve independently, so a workspace can safely mix defaults such as `trunk`, `dev`, and `main`.

The adapter returns the authoritative base ref it selected. Single-repository sessions store it in their diff metadata, while workspace sessions store one base SHA and ref per repository. Review and workspace diffs therefore remain accurate after rebases and default-branch updates.

For a single repository or workspace root with no authoritative Git default, configure `defaultBranch` explicitly. For an unresolved workspace child, configure its primary remote and cached remote `HEAD` with Git. AO-created remoteless repositories use the branch AO recorded during initialization.

## Storage

Migration `0095_session_worktree_base_ref.sql` adds the per-repository `base_ref` needed by workspace comparisons.

## Verification

- `go test -p 1 ./... -count=1`
- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- focused race tests for the resolver, git-worktree adapter, project service, session manager, session service, and SQLite store
- diff-scoped `golangci-lint`: 0 issues
- frontend typecheck
- import scan and project settings tests: 41 passed

title: fix(boot): resilient first-run, tmux bundling, and daemon boot classification
body:
Fixes #2427
Fixes #3800
Fixes #2443
Fixes #3564
Fixes #2206

## Before

- `tmux has-session` reported both a genuinely absent socket and permission/reachability outages as the same infrastructure error. Boot reconciliation could not safely recover the former without also masking the latter.
- A clean macOS/Linux install discovered the tmux prerequisite only when the first terminal session failed.
- A partial or cross-platform Electron postinstall on Windows surfaced later as Forge's misleading “Electron failed to install correctly” error.
- The stable-release guard checked updater manifests but not the unversioned launcher aliases used by `ao start`, allowing the 404 reported in #2427 to recur.

## After

- Add the typed `ErrRuntimeServerAbsent` subset. Exact tmux “no server running” and missing-socket/ENOENT diagnostics are recoverable during restart and boot reconciliation; permission and other ambiguous connection failures remain fail-closed and leave durable session state untouched.
- Restore the pre-rewrite one-time interactive tmux setup at `ao start`: Homebrew on macOS and apt/dnf/pacman/zypper/apk on Linux, using sudo only when available. Noninteractive launches never mutate the machine and print the exact remediation command. Windows continues to use ConPTY.
- Validate Electron before every Forge development/package/make/publish path, repair an incomplete official Electron download once, reject copied binaries for the wrong platform, and fail early on unsupported Node versions.
- Require macOS arm64/x64 ZIPs, Linux AppImage, Windows installer, and updater manifests on the latest stable release.

This intentionally uses the interactive auto-install option agreed in #3564 rather than embedding an unsigned tmux binary in every desktop artifact.

## Tests

- `env -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_SESSION_ID go test ./...`
- isolated-cache `golangci-lint v2.12.2` (`0 issues`)
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c ./internal/cli`
- `npx vitest run scripts/ensure-electron.test.mjs` (5 tests)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run package` (macOS arm64)

## Clean-environment verification

- Installed `packages/product-ui` and `frontend` from their lockfiles with `npm ci`, then ran `npm run package`. The resulting `.app` contains arm64 Mach-O Electron, daemon, and agent-browser executables.
- Simulated the Windows first install with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, confirmed Electron had no `path.txt`/binary, then ran `npm_config_platform=win32 npm_config_arch=x64 npm run electron:ensure`. It downloaded and verified `electron.exe`; `file` identified it as `PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64, for MS Windows`. Running the ensure step again for macOS detected the foreign marker and repaired it back to the local arm64 binary.
- Ran installation under Node 26 and confirmed `.npmrc` now fails immediately with `EBADENGINE`, pointing users to the supported Node 20/22/24 LTS range instead of failing later inside Electron.
- Verified the tmux-less/noninteractive path locally with injected package-manager discovery and `/dev/null`: it never prompts or invokes an installer and emits the exact install command. GitHub's clean Debian container smoke test also passed with tmux deliberately absent.
- Queried current stable release `v0.12.4` and confirmed all newly guarded launcher aliases and updater manifests are present.

## CI

All required jobs pass, including race tests, lint, API drift, frontend tests, renderer smoke, security scan, clean container smoke, and native Windows/macOS/Linux packaging.

title: fix(chat): stop freezes, attachment loss, and turn-state desync
body:
Fixes #3945, fixes #3884, fixes #3878, fixes #3749 — the P1 reliability/data-loss cluster in the Chat UI surface.

These four bugs share one theme: durable conversation state, in-memory controller state, and the disposable worktree had mismatched lifetimes and authority. This PR makes durable state authoritative for what the user sees and can act on, and stops ephemeral state (worktrees, nested provider turns, capped output deltas) from destroying or wedging it.

## #3945 — Chat UI freezes when a command exceeds the output cap; Terminal unreachable

**Root causes fixed:**
- `AppendConversationActivityOutput` (and its streamed-text sibling) kept bumping `revision`/`updated_at` on every delta after the 64K cap, firing a CDC event → SSE push → full snapshot refetch per delta for bytes that could no longer change. A vite dev server past the cap turned that into a re-render storm that froze the page. The queries now skip the row entirely once its truncation flag is set (`AND command_output_truncated = 0`), so capped deltas produce **zero** CDC traffic. The settled aggregate on `item/completed` still lands.
- An interrupt-policy chat→TUI handoff waited forever for the provider to settle the cancelled turn. If the provider is wedged on the very command the user is escaping, the switch never completed ("policy dialog that cannot complete"). `BeginHandoff` now bounds that wait (`handoffSettleWait`, 10s default) and reconciles the durable turn as interrupted so the switch always completes — the terminal is the escape hatch and must always be reachable.

## #3884 — restart recovery deletes image attachments (data loss)

Attachment bytes now have a durable owner: `$AO_DATA_DIR/attachments/<session-id>/` (new `internal/attachments` package), with the worktree `.ao/attachments` copy demoted to a projection. Follows the fix direction laid out in the issue:

- **Stage atomically:** canonical copy first (tmp+rename, 0600); a failed durable write refuses the attachment instead of accepting bytes that vanish on the next restart. The existing worktree-relative refs are unchanged.
- **Serve durably:** the preview route serves strictly-validated `.ao/attachments/<name>` references from durable storage when the worktree copy is missing; a live worktree copy still wins; ordinary preview files stay confined to the workspace.
- **Restore projection:** `RestoreAll` rematerializes the session's durable attachments into the recreated worktree (and re-adds the git exclude) before the controller relaunches.
- **Upgrade safely:** `saveAndTeardownOne` imports legacy worktree-only attachments into durable storage *before* `ForceDestroy` — the exact seam that used to delete their only bytes. Covers attachments staged by pre-fix builds, including spawn attachments.
- **Cleanup tied to durable ownership:** canonical bytes are never removed on runtime teardown or worktree recycling.
- **Security:** strict name validation (no separators/traversal/hidden files), symlinks never followed into or out of durable storage, cross-session access impossible by construction.

## #3878 — nested Codex turns drain queued automation prematurely

Applies the fix from PR #3890 by @Dhruv-Sharma01 (rebased cleanly onto main; commit authorship preserved): `ChatEvent` carries `ProviderConversationID`, only root-thread lifecycle events can claim/release primary turn ownership, in-memory ownership updates move to post-commit (`applyCommittedTurnLifecycle`), nested completions no longer report idle or drain the queue, handoff quiescence is serialized behind `sendMu`, and adapter interrupts target the root turn.

## #3749 — "Stop turn" returns CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN while the UI shows a running turn

Composes the approach from PR #3752 by @xRealBlue on top of the nested-turn lifecycle fix:

- **Durable-state fallback:** when memory says nothing is running but SQLite has a `running` turn (failed projection, restart, dispatch race), `Interrupt` reconciles it instead of refusing — serialized behind `sendMu` so a mid-dispatch state can't be misread.
- **Provider-refusal reconciliation:** `ErrChatNoActiveTurn` for a turn memory still tracks now settles the durable row rather than surfacing a bare error that leaves the user stuck on "Working".
- **`reconcileDurableTurn`** delivers the full Interrupt contract in one place: best-effort provider cancel, settle as interrupted, clear memory, cancel the queue behind it, report idle.
- **Client resilience:** the renderer and mobile clients refetch the conversation when an interrupt fails, so a stale "Working" bar is discovered instead of kept.

The projection-transaction half of the desync (memory mutated inside a rollback-able transaction) is fixed structurally by the post-commit lifecycle handling from the #3878 fix.

## Tests

New coverage (all requested seams):
- **Attachment survival across restart:** `TestAttachmentsSurviveTeardownAndRestore` (manager-level, incl. legacy import), `TestSessionsAPI_PreviewServesDurableAttachmentAfterWorktreeLoss` (HTTP incl. traversal + cross-session rejection), `internal/attachments` unit tests (validation, symlink skip, atomic store), and the lifecycle-level e2e `TestChatAttachmentSurvivesADaemonRestart` (real daemon, real codex, real restart — the exact repro from the issue).
- **Stop-turn authority under desync:** `TestInterruptReconcilesStaleRunningTurnOnDisk`, `TestProviderRefusalReconcilesTheDurableTurnAsInterrupted`, `TestInterruptReconciliationCancelsQueuedTurns`, `TestInterruptReturnsNoActiveTurnWhenNoRunningTurnAnywhere`, and `TestProjectionFailureThenStopStillStopsTheTurn` (the exact #3749 sequence: failed `turn/completed` projection, then Stop).
- **Output-cap non-wedge:** `TestCappedOutputStopsBumpingRevision` (revision frozen after truncation), `TestInterruptHandoffCompletesWhenProviderNeverSettlesTheTurn` (bounded escape to Terminal).
- **Nested-turn automation ordering:** `TestNestedTurnCompletionDoesNotDrainQueueWhilePrimaryTurnRuns`, `TestChatHandoffDrainWaitsForRootAfterNestedTurnCompletes`, plus adapter/normalizer tests (from #3890).

Validation run:
- `go test ./...` — green (the `internal/cli` spawn tests fail only when AO_* env vars from a live AO session leak into the test env; they pass with a clean env and fail identically on unmodified `main`).
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — clean.
- End-to-end: `AO_CHAT_E2E=1 go test ./e2e/ -run TestChatAttachmentSurvivesADaemonRestart` — real daemon binary, real codex session, attachment staged → daemon stop → recovery → same preview URL serves the same bytes and the resumed agent reads the same path.

## Known follow-ups (out of scope)

- #3878's "acknowledgement recovery for a dispatched provider ID that never emits turn.started" is not implemented here (nor in #3890); Stop-based reconciliation covers user recovery in the meantime.
- The `groupByTurn` presentation defect (parent activity anchored above completed child cards) from #3878's "UI clarity" section is a separate rendering change.
- #3950/#3951 (interface-switch recovery banner persistence) remain separate.

## Relationship to open PRs

- #3890 (nested turns) is included as its own commit with original authorship — this PR supersedes it only by also carrying the three sibling fixes; happy to rebase if #3890 lands first.
- #3752 (stop-turn desync) is re-implemented here on top of the nested-turn lifecycle (the two PRs conflict in `controller.go`); its author is credited as commit co-author.

title: fix(lifecycle): cap concurrency, GC worktrees, and recover dead orchestrators
body:
Hardens the orchestrator/session lifecycle so AO survives large multi-worker runs. Fixes the #3921 cluster at its root causes: unbounded spawn concurrency, unrecoverable dead orchestrators, and terminal-state teardown that leaked worktrees/branches with no GC to reclaim them.

Closes #3921. Closes #2811. Closes #3402. Addresses #2523 (memory ceiling; the orphan-process reaper already shipped in tmux `Destroy`).

## Root causes → fixes

**A. No concurrency cap in the Go rewrite (#3921 factor 1, the OOM driver).**
`AO_MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS` (daemon-wide) and `maxConcurrentSessions` (per-project config, `ao project set-config --max-concurrent-sessions`) now cap concurrent non-terminated sessions. Worker spawns over the cap fail with a typed `SESSION_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` 409 **before any durable state is created**; the count-then-create window is serialized so racing spawns can't overshoot. Orchestrator spawns are exempt so a project at the cap can always be recovered. Boot-time `RestoreAll` honors the same cap, so a restart can't resurrect a 40-worker pile-up into the same OOM that killed it. Default is 0 (unlimited) for back-compat; the spawn skill doc now tells orchestrators to keep 3-4 workers on 8 GB machines.

**B. A dead orchestrator was unrecoverable (#3921 factor 2, the "delete the project" symptom).**
Two independent fixes:
1. *Crash finalization.* Reaper-observed runtime death used to only flip `is_terminated` — the worktree stayed on disk with the canonical orchestrator branch checked out, so every replacement spawn failed forever. The LCM now late-binds a crash finalizer that runs the shutdown-style capture-then-destroy sequence: uncommitted work preserved at `refs/ao/preserved/<id>`, restore marker recorded, runtime + orphaned pane children reaped, worktree force-removed. The session stays restorable (user-driven Restore now also replays the preserved ref, previously only boot restore did) and its branch is freed.
2. *Spawn-time release.* Even when teardown failed (disk pressure) or predates the finalizer, spawning an orchestrator now first releases terminated orchestrators' leftover worktrees (capture first, then force-remove, markers consumed). A dead orchestrator can no longer wedge a project.

**C. No worktree/branch GC; cleanup non-idempotent and unobservable (#3402, #2811, #3921 factor 3).**
- The `session_cleanup_facts` layer (migration 0030, previously dead code) gets its production callers: every cleanup attempt persists a durable disposition (`removed` / `preserved_dirty` / `pending` / `failed`) with attempt bookkeeping, capped backoff, and a machine failure code.
- `ao session cleanup` is now idempotent: sessions already reclaimed under the current generation are skipped instead of re-listed forever; `cleanup_generation` is bumped when a session revives so stale facts never shield a re-termination.
- A new hourly `RunTerminalResourceGC` daemon pass walks `ListTerminalCleanupCandidates` and reclaims worktrees leaked by *any* terminal path. Dirty worktrees are never force-deleted (park as `preserved_dirty`; manual cleanup is the user-triggered retry).
- Cleanup, the hourly GC, the crash finalizer, and the spawn-time terminated-orchestrator release all take the session's exclusive operation gate, so no unattended pass can destroy a worktree under a concurrent Restore.
- Tracker-driven termination (issue Done/Cancelled) now routes through the full Kill teardown instead of a bare `MarkTerminated` (#2811's remaining path; merge termination was already fixed by #2980's completion terminator).

**D. Per-spawn resource guardrails (#2523).**
Opt-in `agentConfig.maxMemoryMB` wraps the agent launch (inside the AO supervisor) in `sh -c 'ulimit -v …; exec …'`, so a runaway child is OOM-killed instead of swapping the machine out from under the fleet. Applied on spawn and restore/resume; no-op on Windows. Surfaced as `--max-memory-mb`.

**E. Prior lifecycle-audit leftovers.**
- Finding 4: `terminate_on_pr_merge` is removed from the full-row `UpdateSession`, so a stale lifecycle read-modify-write can never silently revert the user's terminate-on-merge flip (regression test pauses between read and stale commit).
- Finding 5: the inspector Activity timeline sorts historical milestones by actual event timestamps (test: child PR opened after root merged).
- Finding 6: the command palette requires `sessionIsActive` before promoting merge-zone sessions into Needs attention; terminated merged sessions stay search-only.
- Findings 1 (scratch resume) and 3 (Resume/Kill arbitration) were verified already fixed on `main` (project-kind-aware resume validation; the shared exclusive session-operation gate).

## Before / after

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator spawns 40 workers overnight on 8 GB | unbounded spawns → OOM killer takes the orchestrator/daemon | spawn 5+ (configured cap) refused with `SESSION_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT`; orchestrator waits and retries |
| Orchestrator runtime OOM-killed mid-run | terminated flag only; worktree keeps canonical branch; replacement spawn fails forever; user deletes the project | work captured, worktree freed, restore marker written; "new orchestrator" click just works; old one restorable with its work replayed |
| PR merged / tracker issue closed with terminate-on | worktree orphaned on disk forever (`MarkTerminated` only / no GC) | full Kill teardown; anything left behind reclaimed by the hourly GC with durable facts |
| `ao session cleanup` run twice | same sessions re-listed and re-torn-down every run; failures opaque | second run is a no-op; every attempt has a persisted disposition + failure code |
| Daemon reboot after mass worker crash | RestoreAll relaunches everything at once → OOM again | restores up to the cap; the rest keep their markers for later |

## How the load failure was reproduced

I couldn't OOM an 8 GB Mac in CI, so the reported sequence is reproduced deterministically at the integration level against the real SQLite store (`backend/internal/integration/`):

- `TestDeadOrchestratorRecoverableWithoutProjectDeletion` — spawn orchestrator → reaper reports runtime dead → assert worktree freed + marker written → replacement spawn succeeds and supersedes the old markers. Fails on `main` (worktree survives, marker absent).
- `TestOrchestratorSpawnReleasesLeftoverWorktree` — the harsher variant where crash teardown never ran: terminated row + worktree intact on disk; the replacement spawn reclaims it. Fails on `main`.
- `TestCleanupIsIdempotentAndRecordsFacts`, `TestTerminalResourceGCReclaimsLeakedWorktrees`, `TestTerminalResourceGCPreservesDirtyWorktrees`, `TestCleanupFactsGoStaleWhenSessionRevives` — the #3402 GC/idempotency matrix.
- Concurrency cap: `concurrency_test.go` (cap refusal with no durable residue, slot freed on termination, orchestrator exemption, per-project override).
- Crash finalizer: `crash_finalize_test.go` (lifecycle hook ordering + idempotency), `finalize_crashed_test.go` (capture/teardown/restore round-trip, live/stale guards).

## Tests run

- `cd backend && go vet ./... && go test ./...` — pass, except 6 pre-existing `internal/cli` spawn-context tests that fail identically on the base commit in this environment (`daemon returned HTTP 404` against the stub daemon; unrelated to this change).
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — pass.
- `npx vitest run` on the touched renderer suites (`command-palette.test.ts`, `SessionInspector.test.tsx`) — 107/107 pass.
- `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api` regenerated; generated files untouched by hand.

## Known risks / follow-ups

- The concurrency cap defaults to **unlimited** for back-compat; the reporter's machine still needs `AO_MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS=3` (or the project config) set. A memory-aware default is a possible follow-up.
- Crash finalization writes the same boot-restorable marker as graceful shutdown, so a crashed session auto-restores at the next boot (bounded by the cap). If auto-restore of crashed workers proves surprising, a distinct marker state is a small follow-up.
- `maxMemoryMB` is not applied on the agent-*switch* launch path (rare; follow-up).
- The prior audit's finding 2 (tmux respawn committed but probe fails, leaving an unfenced generation) is NOT addressed here; it needs its own ownership-boundary work.

body: ## What Removes the "Clear" context-menu item from the terminal pane (`XtermTerminal.tsx`), along with its associated test coverage and now-unused i18n strings across all locales. ## Why The Clear action only cleared the local xterm.js buffer (`term.clear()`). For shell panes this looked correct, but for agent TUI panes (Codex, Claude Code, etc.) the agent process owns and continuously repaints its own transcript from memory on every redraw (resize, tick, etc.), so the cleared view would immediately repopulate — making the button appear broken/inconsistent depending on pane type. Investigated a proper fix (runtime-level scrollback truncation for tmux/conpty, plus a provider-aware "Clear conversation" action sending `/clear` to the agent). On review, decided against shipping either: - Runtime-level clear only ever fixes the shell-pane case; it can't stop a TUI from repainting its own transcript. - A "Clear conversation" button would just duplicate a command (`/clear`) every supported agent CLI already exposes natively — users can type it directly in the terminal today, no UI needed. Given that, the button wasn't earning its complexity. Removing it entirely rather than shipping a partially-working or duplicative feature. ## How - Removed the "Clear" item from the terminal context menu and its handler in `XtermTerminal.tsx`. - Removed the corresponding test case in `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`. - Removed the now-unused `terminal.clear` (or equivalent) i18n key from all locale files (`en`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN`). - No backend changes — this is a pure UI removal. - Intentional omission: no replacement action was added. Users who want to clear an agent's transcript/context can already type `/clear` directly in the terminal, which is the native, provider-supported way to do it. ## Testing - `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` - Targeted vitest run for `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` - Manual: opened the terminal context menu on both a shell pane and an agent (Codex) pane in dev — Clear item no longer appears in either. before : after: changes(suggested) - two diffrent buttons changes(approved by @illegalcall) ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): make Stop authoritative for durable running turns
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3749

## Summary

- Treat the durable running turn rendered by the UI as actionable when Stop finds no in-memory turn.
- Make Stop linearize with dispatch under `sendMu`, capture the exact pre-Stop target and queue cutoff, and wait for that turn acknowledgment without following ownership to newer work.
- Reconcile every running turn visible on the active branch, including overlapping root and nested provider turns, while keeping provider cancellation best-effort.
- Move controller-state memory changes after the durable projection commits so a rollback cannot recreate the memory/SQLite split.
- Refetch the desktop conversation after an interrupt error so stale cached Working state is not left on screen.

PR #3890 is merged into `main` and supplies the nested-turn ownership rules this recovery path relies on. This PR is based directly on current `main` and contains only the focused recovery work for #3749.

The implementation was adapted from PR #3752 by @bluwwi and extracted from the tested recovery work in PR #3986. Contributor attribution is preserved in the commit history.

## Regression coverage

- The exact #3749 projection-rollback sequence: SQLite remains `running`, the provider refuses Stop, and reconciliation settles the durable state.
- A durable running turn with no in-memory pending ID.
- A genuine absence of both durable and in-memory running work.
- Stop racing an in-progress dispatch waits for provider acknowledgment.
- Root and nested visible running turns are both settled, while Stop targets the same oldest/root turn shown by the UI.
- Queue cancellation during recovery without accidental dispatch of pre-Stop work.
- A prompt submitted after Stop survives durable fallback and provider-refusal recovery.
- A completion committed before provider refusal is not overwritten.
- Controller state changes only after projection commit.
- Recovered interrupted turns have no error message.
- Desktop interrupt errors invalidate the conversation query.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go test ./...`

title: fix(spawn): pre-flight the agent binary instead of failing mid-spawn
body:
Closes #3941.

A missing agent CLI was the single largest cause of spawn failures (~47% of them over 14 days: `AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND` + `RUNTIME_PREREQUISITE_MISSING`), and it is a setup gap rather than a spawn-engine bug. It was also detected as late as possible: `validateAgentBinary` only runs once argv has been built, which is after the seed session row, the worktree, workspace provisioning (which may run commands like `pnpm install`), and the attachment writes. Every spawn with an uninstalled harness paid for that work, rolled it back, and told the user nothing actionable.

## Daemon: catch it before anything durable exists

`preflightSpawnEnvironment` (new `backend/internal/session_manager/spawn_preflight.go`) runs the terminal-runtime check and a new agent-binary check before `Spawn` creates any state, asking the adapter's own `ports.AgentBinaryResolver` so no workspace or launch command is needed.

It is deliberately one-sided. Only a definitive `ErrAgentBinaryNotFound` blocks; an adapter without a resolver, or a probe that fails for any other reason, is not evidence the CLI is absent, so the pre-launch argv[0] guard stays authoritative there. Chat mode is untouched: it reaches its provider through `PreflightChat`, which probes the driver itself.

Failures are also readable now: missing tmux names the platform install command, an unknown harness points at `ao agent ls`, and the missing-CLI error names the CLI plus the agent docs link.

## Renderer: don't let the click become a spawn request

The daemon refusal is cheap, but the user still spent a round trip to learn their CLI is missing, and the refusal landed in spawn telemetry looking like a broken spawn engine.

`assertAgentInstalled` (new `frontend/src/renderer/lib/agent-install-preflight.ts`) checks the selected harness against the agent catalog and, because that catalog is a boot-time snapshot, re-checks a "missing" verdict against a fresh `POST /api/v1/agents/{agent}/probe` before believing it. Same one-sided rule as the daemon: an unset or unsupported agent, an older daemon without the probe endpoint, or any transport failure defers to the daemon. Blocking a spawn that would have worked is worse than the cheap failure this replaces.

The gate lives inside `spawnOrchestrator` for the same reason the telemetry triad does: the board, topbar, sidebar, command palette, restore dialog, settings, restart, and project-add launchers all reach the daemon through it, so none of them has to remember to check. The worker path is gated in `TaskComposer.createTask`, where the resolved default agent can be one the picker would have disabled.

Refused spawns read as install guidance with an "Agent docs" button rather than as a failed spawn, on the board, the topbar, the sidebar, and the task composer. The sidebar's orchestrator button previously swallowed every spawn failure into `console.error` with no user-visible feedback at all.

## Verification

Verified against the live daemon that the payloads the gate reads are what it expects:

- `GET /api/v1/agents` returns `{supported,installed,authorized}` of `{id,label}`
- `POST /api/v1/agents/goose/probe` returns `{"agent":{"id":"goose","label":"Goose"},"supported":true,"installed":false}`; `claude-code` returns `installed:true`
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}` returns `config.orchestrator.agent`

Verified the daemon preflight against the real adapter registry (throwaway test, not committed): of the 26 shipped harnesses, the 23 not installed on that machine were each blocked with **0 session rows and 0 worktrees created** and a message naming their CLI; the 3 that were installed passed the preflight and proceeded.

Tests:

- `backend`: `go build ./...`, `gofmt`, and `go test ./...` match clean HEAD (the `internal/cli` failures are pre-existing and environment-dependent, confirmed by running the same suite at HEAD in an isolated worktree). New `spawn_preflight_test.go` covers missing binary blocked with no row/worktree/runtime, inconclusive probe allowed through, resolver-less adapter skipped, chat mode skipped.
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; 109 renderer test files / 1523 tests pass. New: 8 `agent-install-preflight` cases, 2 `spawn-orchestrator` cases (a blocked spawn issues no `/orchestrators` POST; an unreadable project config still spawns), a `TaskComposer` case asserting the install message, the docs button, and no delegate request, and a `Sidebar` case asserting a refused spawn now reaches the user.
- New i18n keys added to all 8 locale catalogs.

## Notes and follow-ups

- The launcher buttons are not visually disabled ahead of the click. The only pre-click signal is the advisory catalog, and disabling on a stale snapshot would grey out a button that works; the fresh probe on click is strictly better.
- The docs link is the `/docs/plugins/agents` index rather than a per-agent deep link: most per-agent pages 404 (`/agents/crush`, `/agents/prime-agent`, and `/agents/copilot`, which the README links).
- No install *commands* are shipped per agent. The repo holds no such metadata, and inventing 26 of them is worse than a message that names the CLI and links the docs. Adding them as adapter metadata would be a reasonable follow-up.
- `AGENT_REQUIRED` and `UNKNOWN_HARNESS` from the issue's scope note were already validated before any durable state; only their wording changed.
- Adds one PATH-resolution probe (2s ceiling) per TUI spawn, plus two cached GETs before an orchestrator spawn. For node-managed CLIs the probe includes the Volta/nvm/fnm candidate globs, the same work `GET /api/v1/agents` already does.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(telemetry): track per-session agent token usage and cost
body:
## What

Adds an end-to-end pipeline to capture agent LLM token usage and dollar
cost per session, sliceable in PostHog by user, session, and harness.
There is no token/cost data captured anywhere today, so this is a new
pipeline rather than a new chart.

## Events

- `ao.session.turn_usage` (aliased to `ao.v2.session.turn_usage`): one per
  model turn, with `model`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
  `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `cost_usd`,
  `model_priced`, `harness`, `kind`.
- `ao.session.usage` (aliased to `ao.v2.session.usage`): one per session at
  end, same fields plus `turn_count` and `duration_ms`.

Both auto-carry the install `distinct_id` and hashed `session_id`, which is
what enables the per-user / per-session / per-harness cuts.

## How it works

1. The claude-code `Stop` / `SessionEnd` hook payload carries
   `transcript_path`. `ao hooks claude-code stop|session-end` parses the
   transcript JSONL for per-turn usage, resuming from a persisted byte
   offset so a turn is never counted twice, and POSTs to the daemon.
2. `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/usage` decodes the report; token counts are
   clamped non-negative and the body is size-capped.
3. `Service.RecordUsage` reads harness/kind/project from the stored session
   record (so tags cannot be spoofed by the caller), prices each turn from a
   list-price table, and emits the two events. Unknown models record tokens
   with `cost_usd: 0` and `model_priced: false`.

The hook path is best-effort throughout: a missing transcript, read error,
or unreachable daemon all exit quietly so the agent is never disrupted.

## Pricing

Single editable table of Anthropic list prices (USD per million tokens),
with cache-write at 1.25x input and cache-read at 0.1x input:

| Model  | input | output | cache write | cache read |
|--------|-------|--------|-------------|------------|
| Opus   | 15    | 75     | 18.75       | 1.50       |
| Sonnet | 3     | 15     | 3.75        | 0.30       |
| Haiku  | 0.80  | 4      | 1.00        | 0.08       |

## Scope

claude-code only for now; other harnesses emit no usage until their
transcript parsers are added, so a "by harness" view shows one slice until
then. Per-turn events are unaggregated by design (both per-turn and summary
were requested); a long session emits one event per turn.

## Verification

Ran the daemon against an isolated data dir and drove the endpoint with a
real session (fake harness):
- Opus turn 1M in + 1M out reported `cost_usd: 90`; a gpt-4o turn reported
  `cost_usd: 0` / `model_priced: false` with tokens intact; summary
  `cost_usd: 90.045`, `turn_count: 2`, `duration_ms: 4200`.
- A body with `"harness":"evil"` was ignored; the event recorded
  `harness: fake` from the stored record (Sonnet priced at $3).
- Error paths: unknown session 404, empty body 400 `USAGE_EMPTY`, malformed
  JSON 400 `INVALID_JSON`, GET 405.

Unit + integration tests cover pricing, the transcript parser (partial-line
no-double-count, malformed/zero skip, single-pass summary+duration), the
service emit/pricing path, the negative-token clamp, and the CLI hook
through a test server (incremental stop reporting, offset dedup, session-end
summary, non-claude ignored). `gofmt`, `go vet`, and the OpenAPI route/spec
parity check pass.
