title: feat(telemetry): price agent usage and export cost to PostHog
body:
## What

main already collects per-session token aggregates locally
(`internal/service/usage` + `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions`), but it has
**no dollar cost** and emits **nothing to PostHog**, so cost can't be
seen across users, days, sessions, or harnesses. This adds that missing
half, and only that half, without duplicating collection.

## How it works

The ingestion pipeline applies each parsed usage chunk exactly once
(a durable source cursor guards re-processing). This change hangs a
priced telemetry emit off that same exactly-once seam:

1. `observe/usage` gains an optional `OnUsageApplied(sessionID, events)`
   callback on the ingestor, invoked only after `ApplyUsageChunk`
   commits. Because the cursor has advanced, each event fires the
   callback exactly once, **no dedupe marker or DB migration needed**.
   The package stays free of any telemetry/pricing dependency.
2. `service/usagecost.Emitter` prices each event (`internal/pricing`)
   and emits `ao.session.turn_usage`. Fresh uncached input is billed at
   the input rate; cache read/write are separate line items. Harness,
   kind, and project come from the stored session record, so tags can't
   be spoofed. Unknown models emit tokens with `cost_usd: 0` /
   `model_priced: false`.
3. The daemon wires the emitter into the ingestor; the event is
   allowlisted with its `ao.v2.session.turn_usage` alias.

Best-effort throughout: a nil sink or a failed session lookup emits
nothing and never blocks or errors ingestion.

## Pricing

Single editable table of Anthropic list prices (USD per million tokens),
cache-write at 1.25x input, cache-read at 0.1x input:

| Model  | input | output | cache write | cache read |
|--------|-------|--------|-------------|------------|
| Opus   | 15    | 75     | 18.75       | 1.50       |
| Sonnet | 3     | 15     | 3.75        | 0.30       |
| Haiku  | 0.80  | 4      | 1.00        | 0.08       |

## Why this shape

An earlier attempt (#4000, now closed) reimplemented collection with a
separate parser/endpoint/hook and collided with main's shipped feature.
This version reuses main's collector and adds only pricing + emission.

## Verification

- The `OnUsageApplied` callback fires with the parsed events and the
  correct session id after a real ingest (integration test over the
  sqlite store, a real transcript file, and the durable cursor).
- The emitter prices Opus 1M uncached-in + 1M out at $90, records an
  unknown model at $0 / `model_priced:false`, tags harness from the
  record (not the caller), and no-ops on a nil sink or empty events.
- `pricing` unit tests (families, unknown, negative clamp).
- The daemon boots to ready with the emitter wired and shuts down clean.
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, and the touched-package tests pass.

Not driven live end-to-end to PostHog, that would require injecting into
the real `~/.claude` transcript roots; the new code paths are exercised
through the ingest pipeline and the emitter in tests.

title: feat(landing): Product Hunt launch analytics and UTM link registry
body:
## What

Adds a self-contained Product Hunt launch analytics layer to the landing
site, plus the canonical UTM link registry. Built to merge in a hurry:
**all new files under a `launch/` module + two components; the only edit
to existing code is one mount line in `app/layout.tsx`.**

## Deliberately scoped ("only the relevant things")

Most of the launch spec already exists on the site, so it is not
re-implemented:
- **PostHog autocapture** already gives page views, sessions, session
  duration, bounce, referrer, country, device, browser, unique visitors.
- **`campaign.ts`** already captures and persists `utm_*` across the tab.
- **Existing events:** `download_clicked`, `waitlist_signup`,
  `install_command_copied`, `section_viewed`, `video_*`,
  `outbound_link_clicked`.

App-side product events from the spec (`signup_completed`,
`workspace_created`, `agent_created`, `workflow_*`, `orchestrator_created`,
`*_connected`, ...) are **not** added here: they happen inside the desktop
app/daemon, which emits its own usage events. Faking them on the marketing
site would be wrong.

## What this adds (the real gap)

- **UTM link registry** (`launch/utm.ts`): one tagged `aoagents.dev` link
  per channel (Product Hunt, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Discord, GitHub, and an
  Instagram placeholder since no account exists yet).
- **Normalized attribution** (`launch/context.ts`): collapses the visit
  into `source` / `campaign` / `user_type` / `device`.
- **PH-specific events** (`launch/events.ts`): `ph_referral_visit`,
  `ph_badge_click`, `ph_upvote_cta_click`, `return_visit`.
  (`ph_comment_cta_click` is intentionally omitted until a comment CTA
  actually exists on the site.)
- **`LaunchAnalytics`** (mounted once): registers `source`/`campaign`/
  `device` as PostHog **super-properties**, so every event, including
  autocaptured pageviews and the existing CTA events, becomes attributable
  to the launch source **without touching those call sites**. Fires
  `ph_referral_visit` and `return_visit`.
- **`ProductHuntBadge`**: drop-in badge to our PH page that fires
  `ph_badge_click`.

## The funnel

`PH visit → CTA click` is covered here (`ph_referral_visit` / `source` on
the existing CTA events). `signup → workspace → first agent → first
successful orchestration` are **app-side** events in the same PostHog
project; the README explains the boundary.

## Caveat on the numbers

The site is opt-out by default behind cookie consent, so counts are "of
consenting visitors" and undercount raw PH traffic. Read rates/trends, not
absolutes. Documented in the README.

## Testing

- **Unit tests (verified passing, 14/14):** `launch/utm.test.ts` +
  `launch/context.test.ts` cover UTM link building, source/device
  classification, and the channel registry. Run:
  `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/landing/src/lib/analytics/launch`.
- **Browser:** run the landing dev server, open
  `/?utm_source=product_hunt&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=launch_day`,
  accept consent, `posthog.debug()`, and confirm `ph_referral_visit` plus
  `source: product_hunt` on every event (steps in the README).

I verified the pure logic by running the real test files under vitest. The
two React components and the `track()` wrapper follow existing conventions
and were not driven live end-to-end to PostHog (that needs the dev server +
a PostHog key); the browser steps above are how to confirm that path.

title: fix(chat): keep fitting files after an oversized batch item
body:
Fixes #4080.

## What changed

The production `useFileAttachments.addFiles` loop now skips only a file that exceeds the remaining 25 MiB budget and continues evaluating later files in the same paste, drop, or file-picker batch. The count cap intentionally still stops the loop because no subsequent file can fit once the attachment count is full.

This PR was rebased onto current `main` and narrowed during review to this one issue. The unrelated attachment-only steering fix has moved to its own issue and PR. Changes to the unused `useImageAttachments` hook were removed so this stays on the live Chat path.

## Tests

- Regression test proves a 9 + 9 + rejected 9 + later 5 MiB batch retains the first, second, and fourth files.
- Focused test: 5 passed.
- Frontend typecheck: passed.
- Full frontend suite: 191 files; 2,505 passed and 1 skipped.

## Real Electron A/B evidence

The same four files were selected in the same order through the native file input, with a fresh isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` for each build. These screenshots are attached as review evidence and are not part of the PR code diff.

### Before — current main aborts at the rejected file

![Before: later fitting file is silently dropped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4005/.issue-assets/pr-4005/a-before-batch-aborts.png)

Only the first two 9 MiB files remain. The later valid 5 MiB file is silently lost.

### After — this PR keeps evaluating the batch

![After: later fitting file remains staged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4005/.issue-assets/pr-4005/b-after-later-file-kept.png)

The non-fitting third file still gets inline feedback, while the later 5 MiB file remains staged for a valid 23 MiB total.

title: Linux AppImage won't start on a clean Arch install — it's built with the old FUSE2 runtime
body:
Ran into this while setting up AO on a fresh Arch box (Omarchy). The Linux AppImage from the releases page just doesn't start:

```
$ ./agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage
dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2

AppImages require FUSE to run.
You might still be able to extract the contents of this AppImage
if you run it with the --appimage-extract option.
```

Exit code 1, no window, nothing else. `ao start` hits the same wall since it downloads and runs that same artifact.

### Why it happens

The AppImage is being built with electron-builder's old FUSE2 runtime, which needs `libfuse.so.2` at runtime. Arch dropped that from the default install a long time ago — it only has fuse3 now.

It comes down to one missing config key. `frontend/makers/maker-appimage.ts` passes a config to `buildForge` without `toolsets`:

```ts
config: {
  appId: cfg.appId,
  productName: cfg.productName ?? appName,
  protocols: cfg.protocols,
  directories: { output },
  publish: null,
  linux: { ...(cfg.icon ? { icon: cfg.icon } : {}) },
  appImage: { ...cfg.appImage },
}
```

app-builder-lib treats a missing `toolsets` as "use the legacy runtime". From `out/targets/appimage/AppImageTarget.js`:

```js
const appimageTool = this.packager.config.toolsets?.appimage;
if (appimageTool == null || appimageTool === "0.0.0") {
    updateInfo = await buildLegacyFuse2AppImage({ ... });
}
```

and `out/toolsets/linux.js` confirms what that means:

```js
const isFuse2 = appimageToolVersion === "0.0.0" || appimageToolVersion == null;
```

which pulls `appimage-12.0.1` — the AppImageKit type-2 runtime that dlopens libfuse2.

It's in the published artifact too, not just theory. Running `strings` over the first chunk of the v0.12.4 release:

```
dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2
AppImages require FUSE to run.
Cannot mount AppImage, please check your FUSE setup.
```

### Why nobody's hit this yet

I nearly convinced myself it wasn't real, because the AppImage launched fine on my machine at first. Turned out `fuse2` had been pulled in a few minutes earlier as a transitive dependency of an unrelated `pacman -S` batch. Once I masked `libfuse.so.2` again (bind-mount over it in a throwaway mount namespace, nothing permanent) and re-ran the actual downloaded AppImage, it failed exactly as above.

So plenty of people will never see this — anything that drags in fuse2 hides it. It's clean installs that get bitten, which is unfortunately the first-run path. For what it's worth, Omarchy's own base package list (`omarchy-base.packages`, 151 packages) has no fuse package in it at all.

### Fix

app-builder-lib supports newer static runtimes that don't need libfuse2 — `1.0.2` and `1.0.3` are both in its checksum table. Setting the toolset in the maker should be enough:

```ts
toolsets: { appimage: "1.0.3" },
```

Worth a sanity check on the deb/rpm makers too, though those don't use this code path.

### Environment

Arch Linux (Omarchy), kernel 7.1.4, Hyprland/Wayland, fuse3 only, no fuse2. Tested against the `v0.12.4` release asset `agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage`.

Happy to pick this up — I'll raise a PR for it.

title: fix(desktop): build the AppImage with a non-legacy runtime so it starts without libfuse2
body:
## What

Pin the electron-builder appimage toolset to `1.0.3` in `frontend/makers/maker-appimage.ts`, so the published Linux AppImage is built with the static runtime instead of the legacy FUSE2 one.

## Why

Fixes #4006.

`toolsets.appimage` was never set. app-builder-lib treats that as `"0.0.0"` and builds with the AppImageKit runtime, which `dlopen`s `libfuse.so.2` before it can mount its own squashfs. Distros that ship only fuse3 — Arch, and any install without the `fuse2` compat package — can't launch the artifact at all:

```
$ ./agent-orchestrator-linux-x64.AppImage
dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2
AppImages require FUSE to run.
```

Exit 1, before Electron starts. `ao start` hits the same wall, since it downloads and runs this same AppImage.

The branch point is `app-builder-lib/out/targets/appimage/AppImageTarget.js:66`:

```js
if (appimageTool == null || appimageTool === "0.0.0") { buildLegacyFuse2AppImage(...) }
else { buildStaticRuntimeAppImage(...) }
```

## How

One config key, plus a test.

**On picking a beta.** `toolsets.appimage` accepts only `"0.0.0" | "1.0.2" | "1.0.3" | null`. `"0.0.0"` is the bug, `null` is treated identically, and both remaining values are documented upstream as betas — so "fix this" and "stay on a stable toolset" are mutually exclusive within this option. `1.0.3` and `1.0.2` ship the *same* `Runtime 20251108`; `1.0.3` is a re-release with an upstream fix, so it strictly dominates.

Alternatives I ruled out:

- `AppImageOptions` exposes only `license` and `compression` — no runtime override.
- `APPIMAGE_TOOLS_PATH` still branches on this same flag for its expected directory layout, so it isn't an escape hatch.
- **Bundling libfuse2 inside the AppImage can't work by construction** — the legacy runtime dlopens it *in order to mount* the squashfs, so anything inside the image is unreachable at that moment.
- Telling Linux users to install `fuse2` contradicts the reason this artifact exists ("a single self-contained executable... with no system package manager").

**Two side effects reviewers should know about**, both from `buildStaticRuntimeAppImage`:

1. **Compression flips gzip → zstd.** The artifact got *smaller* (183,309,089 → 171,448,948 bytes, −6.5%), but the bytes change wholesale, so the first delta update across this release is effectively a full download. A very old `unsquashfs` without zstd support would also fail on a manual `--appimage-extract`; the bundled runtime handles it fine.
2. **The `--no-sandbox` default drops out of the desktop entry** (`AppImageTarget.js:26` only adds it for the legacy toolset). This looks self-healing: the generated `AppRun` probes `unshare -Ur true` and re-adds `--no-sandbox` at runtime when user namespaces aren't available, on both the desktop-entry path and `ao start`'s direct exec. Worth a second opinion from someone who knows the sandbox story better than I do.

Build-time network is unchanged — actually one download fewer. The legacy path fetched `appimage-12.0.1.7z` *and* `7zip-linux-x64.tar.gz`; the static path fetches only `appimage-tools-runtime-20251108.tar.gz`. AppImage type-2 magic is preserved, so appimaged/AppImageLauncher still recognise the file, and both paths emit the embedded block map.

Deliberately out of scope: `toolsets.nsis` and `toolsets.wine` also still default to legacy `"0.0.0"`. Different platforms, different issue.

## Testing

Environment: Arch Linux, fuse3 only, no `fuse2` package, no `/usr/lib/libfuse.so.2`.

**Unit:** `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts makers/` → 24 passed. The new test pins the exact version rather than asserting "not 0.0.0", because app-builder-lib treats `null` the same as the legacy toolset, so a looser assertion would stay green on a regression.

**A/B build.** Built this branch with `npx electron-forge make --platform=linux --targets=appimage`, and a control from the same packaged tree with the `toolsets` key omitted:

| | this branch | control (key omitted) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strings` over the full artifact | no `libfuse` / `AppImages require FUSE` matches | `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`, `AppImages require FUSE to run.` |
| `file` | `static-pie linked` | `dynamically linked` |
| `ldd` | not a dynamic executable | dynamic |

**Launch with libfuse2 unavailable.** Ran both under `unshare -r -m` with `/dev/null` bind-mounted over `/usr/lib/libfuse.so.2` (and `AO_DATA_DIR`/`AO_RUN_FILE` pointed at /tmp):

- this branch: starts fully — Electron up, daemon logged `daemon listening addr=127.0.0.1:3001`. Incidentally stricter than intended, since the setuid `fusermount` also loses privilege in that namespace, so it ran with neither libfuse2 nor a usable fusermount.
- control: dies immediately with the dlopen error above.

Unmasked run also works normally and unmounts cleanly on exit.

**What I could not verify:** no CI job builds an AppImage on a PR — `build-artifacts.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only — so this change isn't exercised by the checks on this PR. It needs a Linux `npm run make` and a launch on a fuse3-only host before merge. I've done that above and am happy to re-run against any variation you want.

Unrelated local snag worth flagging for anyone reproducing this: under Node 26, `electron-forge package` silently stalls extracting the Electron zip and exits 0 with no artifact. Node 22 builds fine, and CI pins 22/24, so it only bites locally — but it looks like a success.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(desktop): render reviewer terminal inside Chat surface instead of swapping in CenterPane
body:
## Bug

In a **Chat-mode session**, clicking the Reviewer tab in the chat header tears down the entire chat surface and swaps in the terminal UI (`CenterPane`). The chat timeline, composer, and scroll position are lost; the tab strip the user just clicked disappears from under their cursor. The design intent — chat UI stays when available, terminal is the fallback — is inverted: a terminal-only construct (the reviewer pane) replaces the whole chat surface instead of rendering inside it.

**Source:** chat report | **Analyzed against:** `1ec3acf9f353a7dfda3065f7e2931a6f600fc289`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Open a worker session in `mode: "chat"` with a PR
2. Trigger a review (inspector → Run Review, or agent pushes with auto-review on)
3. The Reviewer tab appears in the chat header
4. Click it → the entire chat surface unmounts and `CenterPane` (terminal UI) mounts in its place
5. Chat history scroll position, composer draft, and the chat tab strip are gone; to get back you must find the worker tab in `CenterPane` and click back

Expected: the chat surface stays mounted. The reviewer tab renders the reviewer `TerminalPane` as the *content* of the chat surface, exactly like `CenterPane` renders it as content of the terminal surface. The worker chat tab remains one click away in the same header.

## Root Cause

`SessionView.tsx` gates the whole surface on the terminal target:

```tsx
// frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx
const showChatSurface = session?.mode === "chat" && routedTerminalTarget.kind === "worker";
```

When the reviewer tab (added in PR #3962) calls `selectReviewerTerminal`, `terminalTarget.kind` becomes `"reviewer"`, `showChatSurface` flips to `false`, and the ternary mounts `CenterPane` in place of `SessionChatSurface`. The reviewer tab lives in `ChatWorkspace`'s `ChatHeader` (`aria-label="Chat tabs"` tablist), so the surface it belongs to is replaced the moment it is used.

`TerminalPane` itself is surface-agnostic — it owns its xterm/mux lifecycle, works under the shell-level `TerminalCacheProvider`, and reviewer panes intentionally skip the retained terminal cache (`terminalTarget?.kind === "reviewer"` returns no cache key). Nothing structural prevents rendering it inside the chat surface.

## Fix

Make the chat surface a tabbed container:

1. `SessionView.tsx`: treat reviewer targets as part of the chat surface in chat mode — `showChatSurface` when `mode === "chat" && target.kind !== "shell"`. Pass `terminalTarget`, `daemonReady`, and `theme` into `SessionChatSurface`.
2. `SessionChatSurface.tsx`: forward those props.
3. `ChatWorkspace.tsx`: derive the active tab from `terminalTarget.kind`; render `<TerminalPane terminalTarget={...reviewer...}>` as the body when the reviewer tab is active; render the existing timeline/composer when the chat tab is active. The existing font-size controls already span 11–24px, matching the terminal range, so they apply to whichever content is active.
4. Mark the active tab properly (`aria-selected`) in the `ChatHeader` tablist.

Shell terminals keep their current behavior (they remain terminal-surface tabs in `CenterPane`).

## Impact

- **Severity:** medium — feature reachable (PR #3962), but the mode-swap UX destroys chat context
- **Affected users:** all Chat-mode sessions that run reviews
- **Workaround:** switch back via the worker tab in `CenterPane` after viewing the reviewer

## Related

- [#3939](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3939) — original report: review terminal disappears in Chat UI mode (closed by PR #3962)
- [PR #3962](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3962) — added the Reviewer tab + target-preservation guard; this issue covers the residual surface-swap UX
- [#3303](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3303) — reviewer terminal should open as a tab instead of replacing the worker terminal (TUI-mode counterpart)
- [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — Chat/TUI session modes design doc

title: Chat UI: command rows never show the command text (Claude Code) — 'Ran command' header + output-only body
body:
## Bug

In the Chat UI, command activity rows for **Claude Code** sessions show only the command's *output* — the command itself is never displayed anywhere: not in the collapsed row header (which just says "Ran command"), and not in the expanded body (which renders output, agent-typed input, and file diffs, but never the command string).

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` thread | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `ee2c58a57` (main, 2026-08-15)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced at both layers.

## Reproduction

1. Spawn/switch a session to the Chat interface with the **claude-code** harness.
2. Ask the agent to run any shell command.
3. Observe the timeline: the collapsed row says only `Ran command`; expanding it shows the output block (e.g. `(Bash completed with no output)` or the streamed output) with the caveat footer — but never *what* ran.

Screenshot (reporter's): two "Ran command" rows; first shows `(Bash completed with no output)`, second shows an `ao session`-style listing. No command text anywhere.

For comparison, the **codex** driver does populate `detail.command`, but the frontend still never renders it on a command row — so the bug has two layers.

## Root Cause

Two independent gaps compound:

### 1. Backend — ACP driver never sets `detail.command` for Claude Code execute tools

`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/client.go`, `toolEvent()` (~line 552-593): the activity detail map is built with `protocol`, `toolKind`, `locations`, `input` (the **raw** `rawInput` JSON object — for Claude Code's Bash tool this is `{"command": "...", "description": "..."}`), `output`, `content`, plus copied `claudeCode`/`terminal_info`/`terminal_exit` metadata. It never extracts a `command` string.

The neutral detail contract (`frontend/src/renderer/types/conversation.ts:182` `CommandDetail.command`) is only honored by the codex driver — `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/normalize.go:1196-1204` (`activityDetail`) sets `detail["command"] = unwrapShell(cmd)` + `rawCommand`. The ACP path (claude-code, opencode, gemini, droid, crush — every ACP-backed harness) leaves `command` undefined even though the data is present one key away in `rawInput`.

### 2. Frontend — command rows never render the command string, even when present

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx`:

- `splitSummary()` (~line 651-660) intentionally labels command rows by category ("Ran command" / "Explored N files" / "Checked repository") and returns no `path`/target for them. That's a deliberate design (landed with the Chat UI in #3472) — but it means the collapsed header never carries the command.
- The expanded body of `GenericActivityRow` (~line 508-524) renders `files`, `detail.reason`/`detail.text`, `detail.terminalInput`, and `detail.output` — **not** `detail.command`. So even on codex sessions where the data exists, the command text is unreachable in the UI.
- `detail.command` *is* rendered for auto-review rows (~line 1169) and approval cards (~line 1470) — just not for ordinary command rows.

## Fix

1. **Backend** (`acp/client.go` `toolEvent`): for tools whose `kind` maps to `domain.ActivityKindCommand` (`ToolKindExecute`), extract the command string from `rawInput` (`command` key for Claude Code Bash; fall back to other common keys or skip) into `detail["command"]` (+ `rawCommand` for the verbatim form), mirroring `codexappserver`'s `activityDetail`.
2. **Frontend** (`ChatTimelineItems.tsx` `GenericActivityRow`): render `detail.command` in the expanded body (mono line above the output block), and include `detail?.command` in the `hasBody` check so a command row with no output is still expandable.

Step 2 alone fixes the symptom for codex; step 1 is required for Claude Code (and every other ACP harness).

## Impact

- Chat UI is unusable for auditing *what* an agent ran — a trust/safety-relevant gap for a supervisor tool. The workaround (switch to the Terminal tab and scroll) exists but defeats the point of the chat transcript.
- Affects all ACP-backed harnesses (claude-code confirmed; opencode/gemini/droid/crush share the driver).
- Rows that produced no output render as `(Bash completed with no output)` — maximally uninformative combination.

**Priority:** P2 — feature degraded, workaround exists (Terminal tab).

## Related

- #3360 — immutable Chat/TUI session modes (broader chat surface tracking)
- #3945 — chat output-cap freeze (same command-activity rendering area, different failure)

title: fix(terminal): stabilize xterm viewport, session-switch render, colors, and activity state
body:
Fixes #3803, fixes #2333, fixes #2529, fixes #2047.

## What

Four terminal-stability fixes across the renderer and the activity lifecycle.

### #3803 — disposed-viewport crash on handle replacement
`XtermTerminal` unmount cleanup disposed the xterm instance synchronously while queued write/viewport work (WriteBuffer callbacks, `Viewport.syncScrollArea` microtasks) could still land in the same task, crashing the renderer with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')`. Cleanup now detaches all listeners/observers/timers synchronously but defers the final `term.dispose()` one macrotask, and the attachable handle drops `write`/`writeln` after disposal (still invoking `done` callbacks so attachment flow control can finish).

### #2333 — blank/glitched terminals after session switching
Two root causes:
- The retained-terminal cache became unbounded (4986af7d0), so each visited pane held a live WebGL context; past Chromium's per-page context cap the oldest contexts are force-lost and the earliest-visited panes render black. Retention is re-bounded at `MAX_RETAINED_TERMINALS = 6` with least-recently-shown eviction (evicted panes remount fresh on revisit).
- A rejected `prepareForActivation()` could leave the activation cover (`visibility:hidden`) down forever. All call sites now tolerate rejection, and a 2s activation-stall watchdog force-completes a stuck activation.

### #2529 — ANSI colors don't match a real terminal
The truecolor plumbing (tmux `-u -T RGB`, `TERM`/`COLORTERM`) already landed in #2980; the remaining gap was the palette itself. The 12 chromatic ANSI slots in `tokens.css` were a softened house mix (and the light theme darkened them further, with bright-white near-black — inverting TUI emphasis). Both themes now use the de-facto standard terminal values (VS Code integrated-terminal defaults), which agent CLIs are designed against. Neutral endpoints stay tuned to AO's terminal plate, per DESIGN.md's "terminal keeps its own palette".

### #2047 — Claude sessions misreport activity state
The `exited` activity state could pin wrongly and never self-correct (only `user-prompt-submit` could resurrect it; the reaper only transitions *into* exited). Two fixes in the lifecycle manager:
- Live-agent evidence — tool-use events and `permission-request`, which are executed by the agent process itself — now resurrects an exited state (turn-boundary callbacks like `stop`/`notification` still cannot). A wrong resurrect self-corrects on the reaper's next workload probe (~5s); a wrong exited previously pinned forever.
- The workload-dead→exited transition is skipped while a session mutation (spawn/restore/agent-switch) is in flight, matching the guard the termination path already had — probing an old process tree against new metadata mid-relaunch no longer desyncs the session to exited.

## Tests
- `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`: dispose is deferred past unmount; writes to a dead handle are dropped with `done` still invoked.
- `TerminalPane.test.tsx`: retention-cap eviction (7 visited → 6 retained, LRU evicted, fresh remount on revisit).
- `manager_test.go`: tool-use and permission-request resurrect exited; turn-boundary events do not; workload-dead observation is suppressed during session mutation.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck` and full renderer suite: 177 files, 2233 passed / 1 skipped.
- `go test ./...`: all green (AO_* session env cleared for `internal/cli`).
- Palette change verified visually via an `ao preview` before/after harness (dark + light).

## Risks / follow-ups
- Eviction cap (6) restores the pre-4986af7d0 bound; panes beyond it lose scrollback on revisit (replay repaints latest output). If unbounded retention is wanted back, it needs a non-WebGL fallback for parked panes instead.
- Exited-resurrect intentionally excludes turn-boundary hooks; delayed `stop` events after a real exit remain ignored.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(chat): show the command text on command activity rows
body:
Fixes #4009.

## What changed

Chat UI command rows showed output but not the command itself.

- The ACP chat adapter now extracts execute-tool commands from `rawInput`, normalizes one shell-wrapper layer, and preserves the verbatim value in `detail.rawCommand`.
- ACP and Codex share the same command normalization instead of maintaining duplicate shell helpers.
- Expanded command rows render `detail.command` above the output.
- Command-only rows are expandable even when no output exists.
- Collapsed headers intentionally retain their category labels such as **Ran command**.

Only `command` and `cmd` keys are accepted from ACP input; unknown provider shapes keep the existing fallback instead of guessing.

## Tests

- Full backend `go test -p 4 ./...`: passed.
- Race tests for the affected chat-driver packages: passed.
- Focused frontend command-row regression: 19/19 passed.
- Frontend typecheck: passed.
- All 10 GitHub CI jobs: passed.

## Real Electron A/B evidence

Both runs used the real AO Electron app at the same viewport and an isolated data directory. The prompt was: `Use the Bash tool to run echo PR4011_AB_PROOF exactly once. Then reply done.` These screenshots are attached as review evidence and are not part of the PR code diff.

### Before — current main hides the command

![Before: command missing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4011/.issue-assets/pr-4011/a-before-command-missing.png)

The expanded activity row shows output but not `echo PR4011_AB_PROOF`.

title: Windows desktop flashes command prompt windows during startup and background probes
body:
## Bug
On Windows, AO can visibly flash transient Command Prompt windows while starting the desktop app and while the daemon performs background work. A user report included a screenshot of a black command window popping up over AO, with the note that it appears and closes repeatedly around 5-6 times while using AO.

**Source:** Local Windows user report and screenshot shared during triage on 2026-08-15. Startup logs were also provided from `frontend/npm run dev` showing daemon startup and background probes.
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
1. On Windows, run `cd frontend && npm run dev`.
2. Wait for Electron Forge to launch the desktop app and daemon.
3. Observe transient Command Prompt windows appearing and disappearing during startup.
4. Continue using AO in flows that trigger background CLI probes; command windows can also flash during normal use.

## Root Cause
Windows GUI apps that spawn console subsystem executables without hidden process creation flags can show visible console windows. AO had two affected paths:

- Developer mode launched the daemon with `go run ./cmd/ao daemon`, which can spawn Go compiler/linker helper processes and make startup especially noisy on Windows.
- Several daemon-owned non-interactive probes used raw process spawning instead of AO's hidden-process wrapper, so downloaded Windows app users could also see command windows from Git, Docker, Tailscale, provider version probes, reviewer probes, or ACP provider processes.

A related Windows dev issue was observed after switching to a fixed prebuilt `frontend/daemon/ao.exe`: active sessions can keep that exe locked, making the next `npm run dev` fail with `EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink ...\frontend\daemon\ao.exe`.

## Fix
Use a Windows-specific dev daemon launch path and hide daemon-owned helper processes:

- Build Windows dev daemons into versioned `frontend/daemon/dev-*` directories and pass the selected exe through a dev manifest.
- Keep macOS/Linux dev startup unchanged.
- Keep packaged daemon resolution unchanged.
- Add hidden-process flags for Node build/probe spawns.
- Route daemon-owned non-interactive CLI probes through the existing backend hidden-process wrapper.
- Preserve Windows ACP process-tree cleanup while also suppressing console windows.

## Impact
- Windows developer mode should stop flashing command prompt windows during daemon startup and avoid locked fixed `ao.exe` rebuild failures.
- Downloaded Windows app users should not see background helper/probe command windows flash during normal app use.
- macOS and Linux behavior should remain unchanged.

title: fix(windows): hide daemon child process consoles
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4012

## What happened
On Windows, AO can show black Command Prompt windows for a moment and then close them again. A user reported that this happens repeatedly while using AO, sometimes 5-6 times, and it looks broken.

This is mainly a Windows problem. When a desktop app starts console programs in the background, Windows can show a command window unless the process is started with hidden-window flags.

## Why it happened
There were two places where this could happen:

1. In dev mode, `npm run dev` started the daemon through `go run`. On Windows, `go run` starts extra compiler/helper processes, so startup could flash several command windows.
2. In the normal downloaded Windows app, the daemon also starts background tools like Git, Docker, Tailscale, agent version checks, reviewer tools, and ACP provider processes. Some of these were not using AO's hidden process wrapper.

There was also a related dev-mode problem: if an old AO session was still using `frontend/daemon/ao.exe`, Windows could keep that file locked. The next `npm run dev` could then fail while trying to delete or replace it.

## What changed
- Windows dev mode now builds the daemon first and starts the built `ao.exe` instead of using `go run` at app startup.
- Windows dev builds use versioned daemon folders, so an old running session does not block the next build.
- Background helper processes launched by the daemon now use the existing hidden-process wrapper on Windows.
- ACP provider processes still keep their process-group cleanup behavior, but no longer need to show a console window.
- Mac and Linux dev behavior is unchanged.
- Packaged daemon location is unchanged.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b6f5464-251b-4336-b757-69ca42bce39c





## After 
it works fine :)

title: fix(scm): prevent transient PR fact regressions
body:
## Summary
- separate partial PR discovery from authoritative SCM observation writes so repository listings can never erase CI, review, mergeability, metadata, or observer cursors
- identify listed PRs by the provider's canonical base repository and canonical URL, deduplicating stale remotes that redirect after repository transfers
- project successful in-app merges into durable PR state immediately, emit existing CDC, and run lifecycle reactions without waiting for the next poll
- preserve nested GitLab namespace parsing and document the durable-facts-first boundary

## Root cause
The observer used one full-snapshot upsert for two different fact strengths. A lightweight repository listing was treated as if it were an authoritative detailed observation. When both a canonical remote and a stale redirecting remote found the same PR, the partial discovery row overwrote rich readiness facts, producing a temporary **Checking merge readiness** state until the detailed refresh repaired it.

The merge action had the inverse consistency gap: it mutated the provider but did not project that confirmed result locally. Frontend invalidation therefore refetched stale SQLite facts until polling caught up.

## Verification
- `npm run sqlc`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `npm run lint` (all AO runtime environment variables removed so CLI tests exercise their isolated harness)
- focused observer, SQLite store, SCM adapter, PR action service, and daemon tests

## Related issue

Part of #4033 — closes its shell and agent-switch gaps.

## Summary

Two constructs that work in Terminal UI now work the same in Chat UI, without leaving the conversation:

**Shells are tabs in the chat header (Gap 1).** Previously `showChatSurface` only stayed mounted for `worker`/`reviewer` targets, so opening a shell unmounted the entire chat surface — timeline, composer draft, scroll position — and swapped in `CenterPane`. Now a shell target renders its `TerminalPane` as the tab body inside the chat surface (the routed `TerminalTarget` passed straight through, mirroring `reviewerTarget` from #4027), and the conversation panel hides with `hidden`/`inert` instead of unmounting — drafts, attachments, edits, and scroll survive.

Shell tabs use the shared `ShellTerminalTab` (already used by `CenterPane` and the terminals screen "so the three never drift"), which brings select/close/**rename** along for free. The desktop next/previous tab shortcuts (Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab) now cycle chat → reviewer → shells in strip order.

**Agent switching has an entry point in chat (Gap 2).** `CenterPane` rendered `TerminalSwitchAgentButton`; the chat surface had nothing, even though `useSwitchAgent` was already chat-aware (it invalidates conversation queries). The same control now renders in the chat header's action region. The mutation state lives in `SessionChatSurface` — which owns query wiring — so `ChatWorkspace` stays a provider-free pure view (its documented contract; enforced by existing fixture tests).

## Changes (6 files, +377/−28)

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `SessionView.tsx` | `showChatSurface` stays mounted for `shell` targets; passes the routed shell target + shell list/select/close/rename into the chat surface. |
| `SessionChatSurface.tsx` | Forwards shell props; owns the agent-switch dialog state + mutation; hands the button and a body-container ref down. |

| tests | ChatWorkspace: shell pane hides-not-unmounts the conversation, target passthrough, Ctrl+Tab cycling. SessionView: shells-from-chat stay inside the chat surface. SessionChatSurface: switch control offered in chat. |

- **Full tab-strip unification (Gap 3 remainder):** the chat/reviewer tabs remain hand-rolled in `ChatHeader`; extracting one shared strip with `CenterPane` remains a follow-up on #4033.

## Bug

The terminal-scoped **Switch agent** selector has two related interaction regressions:

1. The provider/model card expands to the terminal panel width instead of remaining a compact centered card like the in-progress switch presentation.
2. Clicking the toolbar switch button while the selector is already open closes and immediately reopens the dialog, replaying its fade animation.

**Reported by:** @whoisasx (local desktop report)  
**Analyzed against:** `0fbe25e168b27ee35814286f541e426622f4cab0`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P2 — the workflow remains usable, but the selector presentation and repeated interaction are visibly degraded.

## Reproduction

1. Open an active Claude Code or Codex worker terminal.
2. Click the **Switch agent** toolbar button.
3. Observe that the selector card spans almost the complete terminal width.
4. Click the same toolbar button again while the selector remains open.
5. Observe the selector fade out and back in.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/dialog.tsx` supplies `w-full` from the shared dialog primitive.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SwitchAgentDialog.tsx` also supplied the custom `w-dialog-md` utility. `tailwind-merge` does not classify the custom utility as conflicting with `w-full`, so both classes survive. Tailwind emits `.w-full` later, making the computed width 100% rather than the intended 420px.
- The selector uses a non-modal Radix dialog. A pointer-down on the toolbar button is treated as an outside interaction and emits `onOpenChange(false)`; the button's unconditional click handler then emits `onOpenChange(true)`. A focused component test records the exact `false → true` sequence.

These paths were introduced together by [PR #3770](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3770).

## Fix

- Use an unambiguous arbitrary width utility that replaces the shared `w-full` through `tailwind-merge`.
- Ignore toolbar pointer/click activation while the selector is already open, before Radix can treat it as an outside dismissal.
- Cover the computed width in the renderer Playwright harness and the repeated activation state sequence in the component suite.

## Impact

- The selector no longer visually matches the compact centered switch-progress UI.
- Repeated activation causes a distracting close/reopen animation and unnecessary remount.
- Existing tests only checked for a class name and the first open action, so neither browser-computed geometry nor repeated activation was protected.

title: fix(frontend): stabilize switch agent selector
body:
## What

- keep the terminal-scoped Switch agent selector at the 420px dialog token on wide panes and within a 16px gutter on narrow panes
- make repeated activation of the already-open toolbar control a no-op instead of closing and reopening the Radix dialog
- cover the browser-computed wide/narrow geometry and the repeated activation state sequence

## Why

Fixes #4039.

The shared dialog primitive contributes `w-full`, while the custom `w-dialog-md` class was not recognized as a conflicting Tailwind utility. Both survived merging and the later full-width rule won. Separately, the non-modal dialog treated a pointer-down on the toolbar control as an outside dismissal before the control's click handler reopened it.

## How

- use an arbitrary width utility so `tailwind-merge` replaces the shared `w-full`; cap it against the terminal containing block rather than the viewport
- intercept pointer activation only while the selector is already open, with an `onClick` guard covering keyboard and assistive-technology activation

title: bug(cline): completed turns stay working/active at the idle prompt
body:
## Bug

A live Cline worker remains **Working** with `activity.state=active` after its turn has completed and the Cline TUI has returned to the empty `Ask anything…` composer. The agent is quiescent and waiting for a new user prompt, but AO reports it as actively working indefinitely.

**Source:** AO maintainer report (internal task, 2026-08-15) | **Reported by:** AO maintainer | **Analyzed against:** `736782b4afc76aeefb4c2707959456380f64cb0d`
**AO binary:** freshly built Go rewrite from the analyzed checkout (`version: dev`) | **Daemon:** healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Cline:** `3.0.55` | **OS:** macOS 14 / Darwin 23.6.0 arm64 | **Shell:** zsh
**Confidence:** High — reproduced against the live rewrite daemon, captured the TUI, inspected durable state/change history, and traced the adapter/observer capability boundary.
**Priority:** P2 — the dashboard's core working-vs-idle signal is wrong for Cline sessions, but impact is bounded to that harness.

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a TUI worker with `harness=cline` and a prompt (live reproduction: session `agent-orchestrator-133`, display name `quick hello`, prompt `how's it going?`).
2. Let Cline finish its response and return to its empty composer.
3. Verify the terminal is idle. The live tmux pane ended with:

   ```text
   ❯ Ask anything...
   Claude Opus 5 (medium) ...  ○ Plan ● Act (Tab)
   agent-orchestrator-133 (ao/agent-orchestrator-133/root)
   ⏵⏵ Auto-approve all enabled (Shift+Tab)
   ```

4. Query the same session using the freshly built rewrite CLI:

   ```json
   {
     "id": "agent-orchestrator-133",
     "harness": "cline",
     "activity": {
       "state": "active",
       "lastActivityAt": "2026-08-15T23:09:13.940388Z"
     },
     "status": "working"
   }
   ```

5. Observe that it remains `working/active` even though the TUI is awaiting a new prompt.

The SQLite `change_log` corroborates the missing transition: the session was created idle, then recorded a single `active` transition at `23:09:13.940388Z`; there is no later idle transition.

## Root Cause

Cline has hook installation but **no activity classifier file and no terminal detector** under `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/`.

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/hooks.go:49-60` installs `TaskStart -> session-start`, `UserPromptSubmit -> user-prompt-submit`, `PreToolUse -> permission-request`, and `TaskCancel -> stop`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/dispatch.go:50` routes Cline through `activitystate.StandardDeriveActivityState`, so task/prompt start sets `active` and only `stop` can set `idle`.
- Cline's normal successful turn completion does not fire the installed `TaskCancel` hook. The live worktree confirms these are the only four AO-managed hook scripts; there is no normal-completion hook that can clear `active`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/cline.go:40-41` only asserts the base adapter/agent interfaces. It does not implement `ports.TerminalActivityDetector` or `ports.ContinuousTerminalActivityDetector`.
- The safety-net observer therefore exits at `backend/internal/observe/activity/observer.go:111-113` and never reconciles the visible idle composer back to `idle`.

The result is deterministic: a successfully completed Cline turn stays active until a later cancellation/exit or another external state change.

## Fix

Add a Cline terminal activity classifier following the established Codex/Muse pattern:

- recognize Cline's current empty composer (`❯` + `Ask anything...`) together with its status/footer markers as authoritative `idle` evidence;
- strip ANSI control sequences and restrict matching to recent terminal lines so transcript prose cannot trigger a false idle;
- opt Cline into continuous terminal reconciliation so a completed turn clears on the next observer tick instead of waiting for the stale-active threshold;
- leave generation/tool states hook-driven unless the TUI provides an equally authoritative current-state marker;
- add captured-frame tests for the idle composer and false-positive/active cases.

## Impact

- Sidebar, board, and inspector show quiescent Cline sessions as busy.
- Humans and orchestrators cannot reliably tell whether a Cline worker is still progressing or ready for more work.
- Any automation keyed to `active` vs `idle` inherits the false working state.

## Related

- [#3115](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3115) / [PR #3117](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3117) — same stuck-active symptom for Codex; added terminal idle reconciliation.
- [PR #3683](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3683) — Muse had no classifier and gained continuous TUI classification; closest implementation pattern.
- [#2047](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2047) / [PR #4010](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4010) — Claude activity misreport family and lifecycle hardening.
- [#3387](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3387) — Kimi stuck working after an error because it lacks a terminal detector.
- [#3306](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3306) — inverse-direction Cursor sticky activity misreport caused by incomplete adapter signals.

title: fix(cline): reconcile completed turns to idle
body:
Fixes #4048.

## Summary

- install Cline's native `TaskComplete` hook so successful turns clear `active` immediately; error termination remains covered by Cline's existing `TaskCancel` dispatch
- add a continuous terminal activity classifier that recognizes Cline's empty `Ask anything...` / `Plan something...` composer as idle and its `Thinking... (esc to cancel)` indicator as active
- use recent, ANSI-normalized terminal markers with newest-marker precedence to avoid transcript false positives
- cover live idle-composer output, active generation, retained-marker ordering, completion-hook coverage, and transcript rejection

## Tests

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/cline ./internal/observe/activity ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch`
- `cd backend && env -i HOME=\"$HOME\" PATH=\"$PATH\" TMPDIR=\"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}\" go test ./...`

## Risks / follow-ups

- Terminal detection necessarily follows Cline's rendered labels; the native completion/cancel hooks are the primary path, while the classifier is a fallback for missing callbacks. Tests pin the current Cline 3.0.55 markers observed during reproduction.
- Like the existing Codex/Muse continuous detectors, detector-based message-delivery readiness remains bounded by the caller timeout if no authoritative TUI marker matches.

title: bug(review): reviewer loses AO bookkeeping when daemon is unavailable during submit
body:
## Bug

A reviewer can successfully post its review to GitHub, then fail at AO bookkeeping with:

```text
AO daemon is not running — start it with `ao start`
```

The reported sequence was:

```text
ao review submit --session agent-orchestrator-113 --reviews -
```

The preceding reviewer output showed a completed review result, but the AO submit step could not record it because the daemon was unavailable.

**Source:** user report in chat | **Date:** 2026-08-16 | **Analyzed against:** `300d5b7db0224163f626ad9370018418fe6c6f03` | **Confidence:** Medium

## Reproduction

1. Start AO and trigger a review for a worker with an open PR.
2. Let the reviewer post its GitHub review successfully.
3. Stop/restart AO before the reviewer executes `ao review submit --session <worker> --reviews -`.
4. Observe that the submit command exits with `AO daemon is not running — start it with `ao start``, and the review result is not recorded in AO.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/cli/client.go:117-130` requires `running.json` to exist and its PID to be alive before any API call. `ao review submit` has no retry or recovery path when the daemon is temporarily restarting, so the provider-side review and AO-side review run can diverge. The CLI error itself is accurate for the observed state; the reliability gap is that the two-step reviewer workflow has no durable handoff when AO is unavailable between the steps.

The reviewer prompt makes GitHub posting and AO submission independent steps in `backend/internal/review/prompt.go:25-43`. A successful GitHub post therefore does not guarantee that the corresponding `review_run` transitions out of `running` when the daemon is down.

## Impact

- The review is visible on GitHub but AO may leave the run in `running`/unrecorded state.
- Review readiness and dashboard state can remain stale until the result is manually submitted or the run is cancelled.
- A transient desktop/daemon restart can lose reviewer bookkeeping even though the external side effect succeeded.

**Priority:** P2 — significant degradation with a manual workaround.

## Suggested Fix

Choose and document one or both of:

- Make reviewer result submission durable/retryable across a daemon restart, with bounded retry after the daemon becomes ready.
- Add reconciliation for provider reviews created by the reviewer when AO bookkeeping was not submitted, using the review run, target SHA, PR, and reviewer identity.
- Preserve the reviewer result in an AO-owned location outside the worktree so it can be replayed after the daemon returns.

## Workaround

After AO is running, manually submit the result with the run id and verdict, or cancel the stuck run:

```text
ao review submit <worker-session-id> --run <run-id> --verdict approved
# or
ao review cancel <worker-session-id>
```

## Related

- [#3755](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3755) — same two-step failure class when `ao` was missing from reviewer PATH; reviewer launch PATH pinning is now fixed.
- [#3716](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3716) — review operation failure caused by concurrent/mixed-version daemons sharing a data directory.
- [#2604](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2604) — session state after daemon restart.

title: bug(orchestrator): workers spawned by orchestrator ignore configured role model (codex sol instead of luna) — ao spawn has no --model and native subagents bypass AO config
body:
## Bug

Changing the default worker/orchestrator model in project settings (e.g. to Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`) does not affect workers spawned **by the orchestrator**: they keep running on `gpt-5.6-sol`. Explicitly telling the orchestrator to spawn a luna worker also has no effect.

**Source:** Discord #bug-triage (reported by aditi, forwarded user report) | **Reported by:** Fedora 43 user
**AO version:** v0.12.3 (tag `b48c98c94`, released 2026-08-11) | **OS:** Fedora 43 Linux
**Analyzed against:** v0.12.3 tag + `main` @ `9a5882086`
**Confidence:** Medium — resolution chain traced end-to-end and clean for daemon-spawned sessions; the failure vector is one of two candidates below, needs one data point from the reporter to pin (see "Data needed").
**Priority:** high — a configured default model silently not applying, with no error anywhere.

## Reproduction

1. Project settings → set worker model and orchestrator model to `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex), save.
2. Ask the orchestrator to do implementation work so it spawns worker sessions.
3. Workers run on `gpt-5.6-sol` (codex default).
4. Explicitly telling the orchestrator "spawn a luna worker" changes nothing.

## What is NOT broken (traced at v0.12.3)

The full settings → spawn chain was traced at tag `v0.12.3` and is correct for sessions the daemon itself spawns:

- Settings UI persists per-role models: `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` — `buildRoleAgentConfig(...)` writes `worker.agentConfig.model` / `orchestrator.agentConfig.model`. Present at v0.12.3.
- Spawn resolves the role override: `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` `Spawn` → `effectiveAgentConfig(kind, project.Config)` merges `roleOverride(kind, cfg).AgentConfig.Model` over the base (v0.12.3 line 767).
- Codex TUI launch forwards it: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go` `appendModelFlag` → `codex --model <id>` (fixed by #2869, merged 2026-07-21 — **included in v0.12.3**; regression test asserts `--model gpt-5.4-mini` at v0.12.3 `codex_test.go:390`).
- Codex chat launch forwards it: `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/driver.go` `Start` → `thread/start` params include `model` when set (present verbatim at v0.12.3).
- Chat spawn resolution: `backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go:107` → `ChatStart.Model` → driver (present at v0.12.3). (Note: v0.12.3's chat path lacked `applySpawnAgentConfig` for per-spawn overrides — added Aug 13 in #3843 — but per-**project** role models, which is what settings writes, resolved correctly.)
- Restore re-resolves the role config at relaunch (v0.12.3 `manager.go:1652`).

So a worker spawned directly (`ao spawn` from a human shell, or New Task) picks up the configured luna default at v0.12.3.

## Root cause (candidate vectors)

The orchestrator does not spawn workers through an API call — its standing instructions tell it to **run `ao spawn` as a shell command inside its session** (`backend/internal/session_manager/prompt.go:190-191`, `manager.go:2619`). Two consequences:

1. **`ao spawn` has no `--model` flag** (#3331, open). "Explicitly telling it to spawn a luna worker" is unexpressible: the orchestrator LLM has no mechanism to carry a per-worker model, so it runs `ao spawn` plainly and the request is silently dropped (the LLM may also claim compliance without effect). `POST /api/v1/sessions` (`SpawnSessionRequest`) likewise carries no model field — only the delegate endpoint does.
2. **Codex native subagents bypass AO entirely.** If the orchestrator (codex) ignores the standing instruction "Do not use the agent runtime's built-in subagent or task-delegation tools" and invokes codex's built-in collab/subagent tool, those subagents run on codex's own default model (`gpt-5.6-sol`) inside the orchestrator's terminal — invisible to AO's config resolution. This is not technically prevented, and AO's own usage tracking for codex subagents (`backend/internal/observe/usage/codex_subagents_test.go`) demonstrates such subagents occur in AO sessions in practice. To a user watching the orchestrator terminal announce workers, this looks exactly like "AO keeps spawning sol workers".

**Reporter's hypothesis ("maybe OS specific", Fedora 43) is not supported:** nothing in the traced chain branches on OS — the Linux path is identical to macOS/Windows modulo `--no-alt-screen`. The mechanism above is OS-independent.

## Data needed to pin the vector

1. After a "sol worker" appears: does it show up as an **AO session in the sidebar/board**, or only as output inside the orchestrator's terminal? (AO session → vector 1 or a persistence bug; terminal-only → vector 2, native subagents.)
2. `ao project get <id>` (or GET `/api/v1/projects/{id}`) output after saving — confirm `worker.agentConfig.model == "gpt-5.6-luna"` actually persisted.
3. The spawned worker's launch line from `~/.ao/daemon.log` — does argv contain `--model gpt-5.6-luna`?

## Fix

- Vector 1: implement #3331 (`ao spawn --model`) and teach the orchestrator prompt that per-worker model selection is available; alternatively surface the delegate endpoint (which already accepts `Model`) to orchestrator-session use.
- Vector 2: detect codex subagent/collab activity in orchestrator sessions (the usage observer already parses these events) and either steer the orchestrator or surface a warning that native subagents ignore AO model policy.

## Impact

- Configured model policy silently not applied to orchestrator-delegated work; users on metered/different models get wrong-model usage with no error.
- Erodes trust in settings ("I set it and it saved, but nothing changed").

## Related

- #3331 — `ao spawn --model` missing (vector 1)
- #2869 — the reference per-adapter model-forwarding fix (Codex TUI, merged)
- #2883 / #2884 / #2886 / #2887 / #2891 — same symptom class, other harnesses dropping `cfg.Config.Model`
- #3607 — daemon env inherited unfiltered can silently change effective model

body:
## What

Fixes browser tabs that could not be closed after multiple tabs were opened, and improves DevTools button visibility while it is active.

## Why

UI-created tabs were added directly to AO’s Electron tab list after the native agent-browser daemon had already connected. The daemon therefore did not know about those tabs, causing close commands to fail with “Tab not found.”

The active DevTools button also inherited the ghost button’s dark hover styling, making the icon difficult to see.

## How

- Route UI tab creation through the existing native `tab-new` lifecycle so AO and agent-browser stay synchronized.
- Preserve direct tab creation as the fallback when the native runtime is unavailable.
- Give the active DevTools button a persistent high-contrast accent state, including hover.
- Expose the DevTools toggle state through `aria-pressed`.
- Add regression coverage for the seven-tab workflow and native tab lifecycle.

## Files affected

- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`
  - Synchronizes UI-created tabs with the native browser runtime.
- `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts`
  - Covers creating multiple UI tabs after daemon initialization and closing one.
- `frontend/src/main/agent-browser-runtime.test.ts`
  - Verifies native tab creation and closure using the bundled agent-browser binary.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel.tsx`
  - Improves active DevTools button contrast and accessibility state.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel.test.tsx`
  - Verifies the DevTools active state and styling.

## Testing

title: Linux: fixed titlebar nav cluster ghosts over Board crumb when sidebar is collapsed (broken clearance + undefined --size-titlebar-content-offset-linux token)
body:
## Bug

On Linux, with the sidebar collapsed, the fixed titlebar navigation cluster (sidebar toggle + back/forward history arrows) paints **on top of the "Board" crumb** in the framed shell topbar. The disabled back/forward arrows render at 55% opacity over the title text, producing a "ghosted chevrons bleeding through the Board label" look.

![screenshot: ghosted nav chevrons overlapping the Board title on Linux](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-linux-titlebar-ghost/.issue-assets/linux-titlebar-ghost/board.png)

**Source:** Discord `#report-bugs` thread "broken UI" | **Reported by:** Piyush (OS: Omarchy / Arch + Hyprland, Linux)
**Analyzed against:** `9a5882086` (2026-08-14) | **Confidence:** High — full geometry traced in code
**Priority:** P2 — cosmetic/layout degradation with an easy workaround (expand the sidebar); no data or functionality loss. But it also blocks a click-target: the ghosted arrows sit over where users expect to read/click the crumb.

## Reproduction

1. Run the desktop app on Linux (any distro; confirmed on Omarchy/Wayland).
2. Collapse the sidebar (PanelLeft toggle or shortcut).
3. Navigate to the root Board route (`/`) — the framed ShellTopbar shows the "Board" crumb.
4. The fixed nav cluster (sidebar toggle, back arrow, forward arrow) at `left-0` now overlaps the crumb: the toggle/grid icons sit beside the title and the two disabled chevrons ghost over the "Board" text.

Sidebar expanded → no overlap (the cluster sits over the sidebar's reserved band instead).

## Root Cause

Two layers collide because the Linux clearance path was only half-built:

**1. The nav cluster is `fixed left-0` and never moves when the sidebar hides.**
`frontend/src/renderer/components/TitlebarNav.tsx:63-67` — on Linux (`!isMac`) the cluster is `left-0`, `top-0.75`, pinned to the window's top-left "within the reserved titlebar band" (comment at lines 60-62). It is rendered once at shell level (`frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx:786-791`) precisely so it does *not* follow sidebar state — by design on macOS, where the topbar pads around it.

**2. The framed `ShellTopbar` only reserves clearance for that cluster on macOS.**
`frontend/src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.tsx:85-90`:

```ts
const targetPaddingLeft =
    !embedded && mac && !isSidebarOpen      // ← mac only
        ? isFullScreen ? PADDING_CLEARANCE_FULLSCREEN : PADDING_CLEARANCE  // 112 / 170px
        : PADDING_DEFAULT;                  // 18px on Linux
```

When the sidebar is hidden, the center panel expands to the window edge (`.sidebar-hidden .center-panel-shell { padding-left: 16px }`, `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:456-460`), so the "Board" crumb (padding-left 18px) slides under the fixed cluster. The back/forward buttons are disabled at the board root (`useCanGoBack()` false → `disabled:opacity-55`, `TitlebarNav.tsx:134`) — hence ghosting rather than a solid overlap.

**3. A partial mitigation exists for session routes only — and it is itself broken.**
PR #3480 added `.session-topbar-titlebar-clearance-linux` (`styles.css:523-525`) applied on session routes when `!isSidebarOpen` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/CenterPane.tsx:528`, `chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:638`). But it sets:

```css
.session-topbar-titlebar-clearance-linux {
    padding-left: var(--size-titlebar-content-offset-linux);
}
```

and **`--size-titlebar-content-offset-linux` is never defined anywhere** — the only occurrences of that token in the repo are this one usage (`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:524`) plus `--size-titlebar-cluster-left-linux: 6px` (`frontend/src/styles/tokens.css:306`), which is a different token and is never referenced. An undefined CSS custom property resolves to the guaranteed-invalid value → the declaration is ignored at computed-value time → **0 extra padding**. The session-route "fix" has been a no-op since it landed (commit `bbea40a5a`, 2026-08-03, PR #3480).

**Timeline:**
- `28c8fa284` (2026-07-26, PR #3129) introduced the Linux fixed titlebar cluster ("match mac shell chrome") — earliest version of the overlap geometry.
- `bbea40a5a` (2026-08-03, PR #3480) added the broken Linux clearance class (session routes only, undefined token).

## Fix

Two lines of defense, both small:

1. **Define the missing token** in `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` next to its siblings:
   ```css
   --size-titlebar-content-offset-linux:
       var(--size-titlebar-cluster-left-linux) + var(--size-titlebar-cluster-width) + var(--size-titlebar-content-gap);
   ```
   (6px + 92px + 12px = 110px). This repairs the existing session-route mitigation.

2. **Extend `ShellTopbar`'s `targetPaddingLeft` to Linux**: treat `!isSidebarOpen` the same as the mac branch but with the Linux offset — e.g. `mac ? PADDING_CLEARANCE : isLinux ? PADDING_CLEARANCE_LINUX : PADDING_DEFAULT`, with `PADDING_CLEARANCE_LINUX = 110` (or read the token). Apply it wherever the crumb renders (root board route and session identity), mirroring how `PADDING_CLEARANCE` is applied today. Alternatively, gate it purely in CSS via the existing `--size-titlebar-content-offset-linux` token on `topbarHeaderClass` for `.platform-linux`.

Note the arrows still overlap the crumb on **project board routes** (`/projects/$id`) where the crumb is the project name — same mechanism, so the fix should cover both (the `boardActionsInPanel` branch at `ShellTopbar.tsx:204-205` renders the crumb for Linux on all non-session routes).

## Impact

- Linux users with a collapsed sidebar see ghosted navigation chevrons over the Board/project crumb on every board visit; the cluster's hover states also light up over the title area, making the top-left of the topbar feel broken.
- The session-route mitigation shipped in #3480 is silently dead CSS (undefined token) — worth fixing regardless of the board-route work.
- macOS is unaffected (its 170px clearance path works); Windows uses its own `WindowTitlebar`, unaffected.

## Related

- [#3129](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3129) — introduced the Linux fixed titlebar cluster
- [#3480](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3480) — added the (broken) Linux session-route clearance
- [#3372](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3372) — same subsystem (sidebar hover-preview race), not a duplicate

title: Provide a global/project default to enable Auto review for new sessions
body:
## Problem

In AO 0.12.5, **Auto review** is available in the Reviews panel, but it is disabled for every newly created issue/task/worker session. Users must enable it manually for each session.

## Additional reproduction

When the worker is still in progress and no pull request has been opened, the Reviews panel only shows **Automatically send reviews**. The **Auto review** toggle is not available, so it cannot be enabled proactively. Users must wait until the work ends and/or a pull request exists before enabling Auto review, which is too late for that session review workflow.

## Request

Add a global or project-level default for auto_review_enabled, configurable through AO settings or project configuration (for example, autoReviewEnabled: true). When a session is created, it should inherit that default while retaining the per-session toggle as an override.

Please consider:

- applying the setting to all newly created sessions, including issue/task/worker sessions;
- making the setting available before or at session creation;
- preserving existing-session behavior, or providing an explicit migration/backfill option for existing sessions;
- keeping reviewer-agent selection and **Automatically send reviews** as separate settings.

## Current workaround

Enable **Auto review** manually for every session, but the control may not appear until the worker has finished or opened a pull request.

## Related

This request is for enabling the Auto review feature by default, not for the separate automatic injection/send-review-feedback setting. Related issue: #3468.

title: bug(daemon): fixed 30s readiness timeout vs. O(N) serial worktree restore — 40 sessions takes 4m36s to become ready
body:
### Summary

The desktop app reports `AO daemon is not ready yet` / `not_ready` on every launch. The daemon is healthy — it just takes 4m36s to pass its readiness check, because startup stashes uncommitted changes in every session worktree serially while the readiness timeout is a fixed 30s. Startup cost is O(sessions) but the budget is O(1), so past roughly 5 sessions on Windows this fires on every single launch.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Accumulate ~40 sessions in a single project (mine: 23 idle/working, 1 needs-you, 3 in review, 7 ready to merge, 1 merged, 6 archived — 40 worktrees under `~/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>`).
2. Launch the desktop app.
3. Wait 30 seconds.
4. `Restart daemon` from the error panel reproduces it identically.
5. Leave the app open and idle for ~5 minutes — the board then loads correctly on its own.

### Expected behavior

The daemon becomes ready and the board loads, without the user having to wait out a five-minute error state on every launch. Readiness should not be gated on restoring every session's worktree, or the timeout should scale with the amount of restore work queued.

### Actual behavior

At 30s the app shows:

```
AO daemon is not ready yet
Code: not_ready
Message: AO daemon did not finish starting within 30 seconds.
```

Sidebar shows `Could not load projects. / AO daemon API is not ready` and the board shows `Could not load sessions.`

The daemon has not crashed — it keeps restoring worktrees for another four minutes and then comes up fine. `running.json` is written at 19:02:01 (`startedAt: 2026-08-16T18:02:01Z`, pid 3804, port 3001) against a daemon start of 18:57:25 — **4m36s**. The UI recovers on its own at that point and all 40 sessions appear correctly.

Secondary bug: the log display in the error panel freezes at whatever line it had reached when the timeout fired, and never updates again even though the daemon is still logging progress. That makes a daemon that is still working look hung — I initially misdiagnosed it as a hang for exactly this reason, because the panel sat on `session=my-edotmw-15` for minutes while the daemon was in fact up to `my-edotmw-42`.

### AO version

0.12.1-nightly.202608161349

### Environment

Windows 11, Electron desktop app (native conpty runtime). ao.db 137 MB, ao.db-wal 8.3 MB, 40 worktrees.

### Logs / extra context

```shell
### Cold start


time=2026-08-16T18:55:35.041+01:00 level=INFO msg="built per-session agent resolver" default=claude-code registered="[agy aider amp auggie autohand claude-code cline codex continue copilot crush cursor devin droid goose grok kilocode kimchi kimi kiro muse opencode pi prime-agent qwen vibe]"
time=2026-08-16T18:55:35.048+01:00 level=WARN msg="tracker disabled: no usable token" provider=github err="github tracker: no token configured"
time=2026-08-16T18:55:35.051+01:00 level=WARN msg="tracker disabled: no usable token" provider=gitlab err="gitlab scm: no token configured"
2026/08/16 18:55:47 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-8 skipped_count=0
2026/08/16 18:55:51 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-10 skipped_count=0
2026/08/16 18:55:55 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-12 skipped_count=0
2026/08/16 18:56:00 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-14 skipped_count=1
[timeout fires ~18:56:05]


### Warm restart via `Restart daemon` — same shape, one session further


time=2026-08-16T18:57:24.963+01:00 level=INFO msg="built per-session agent resolver" ...
2026/08/16 18:57:31 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-8 skipped_count=0
2026/08/16 18:57:38 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-10 skipped_count=0
2026/08/16 18:57:42 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-12 skipped_count=0
2026/08/16 18:57:46 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-14 skipped_count=1
2026/08/16 18:57:49 INFO gitworktree: StashUncommitted skipping ignored paths session=my-edotmw-15 skipped_count=0
[timeout fires ~18:57:55]


### Progress continues after the timeout

The panel log stops here, but worktree directory mtimes under `~/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>` keep advancing through the remaining sessions:


19:01:11  my-edotmw-36
19:01:15  my-edotmw-37
19:01:23  my-edotmw-38
19:01:30  my-edotmw-39
19:01:38  my-edotmw-40
19:01:45  my-edotmw-41
19:01:53  my-edotmw-42


`~/.ao/running.json` appears at 19:02:01. Total daemon start → ready: **4m36s**.

### Two distinct costs

- **~12s before the first stash** on cold start (~6s warm), between the resolver line and `my-edotmw-8`.
- **~7.6s per worktree** in steady state (5 sessions across the 38s from 19:01:15 to 19:01:53).

7.6s for a local `git stash` is itself suspect. On Windows this smells like Defender real-time scanning every file git touches, and excluding the AO data directory does look like it would help a lot locally — but that's a user-side mitigation. The structural bug stands regardless: even at a fraction of that per-session cost, N sessions cannot fit into a fixed 30s budget.

### Suggested fixes

1. **Don't gate readiness on full session restore.** Restore lazily or in the background and let the daemon serve as soon as the API is up. This is the real fix.
2. If restore must block, **scale the timeout with session count**, or parallelize the per-worktree stashes.
3. **Keep streaming daemon logs into the error panel after the timeout fires**, so a daemon that is still making progress doesn't look hung.

### Related

- #2958 (closed) — generic `AO daemon is not ready` error, should surface the actual cause. This is a concrete case where the surfaced detail still didn't explain the cause.
- #2935 — show a loading state while restoring existing projects.
```

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(daemon): recover sessions without false startup failure
body:
Fixes #4064

## What changed

- Relaunch dead TUI and Chat controllers in their existing registered worktrees during startup instead of serially stashing, removing, recreating, and reapplying every worktree.
- Bound live-session reconciliation with four workers and reuse successful Chat capability probes for the daemon lifetime.
- Keep the durable capture/marker/teardown path as the safety fallback when an in-place relaunch cannot commit.
- Treat the Electron supervisor's 30-second threshold as slow progress while the child is still alive: use polite status semantics, keep startup details fresh, omit the misleading restart action, and transition automatically when readiness arrives.

## Why

The reported 4m36s startup was dominated by an O(N) destructive restore cycle. A machine reboot or native-runtime loss does not require AO to move a registered worktree at all: the durable session and worktree are already the state to recover. Relaunching the controller in place avoids expensive Git/antivirus work and removes the riskiest part of normal startup. The UI change also stops a healthy, progressing process from being labeled as failed if recovery still exceeds 30 seconds on slower machines.

## End-to-end verification

I launched the real Electron app from this checkout against an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` and `AO_RUN_FILE`. The fixture used a real SQLite database, Git repository/worktrees, tmux sessions, and `ao agent-process supervise`; only the final model executable was a deterministic local stub so the drill made no provider calls.

1. Registered one project and spawned eight real sessions (`Recovery 01` through `Recovery 08`).
2. Added a unique uncommitted sentinel to every registered worktree and recorded each SHA-256 plus the original launch generation.
3. Stopped the app and killed only those eight runtime sessions, leaving all eight durable session rows live.
4. Restarted the real daemon. Resolver log to loopback listener: **1,174 ms**. All eight controller generations rotated; IDs and workspace paths stayed unchanged; all eight sentinel hashes were identical; no restore markers, stash operations, force-destroys, or fallback teardowns occurred.
5. Launched the real Electron supervisor behind a controlled startup gate. At **53 seconds**, the app still showed progress with live details, zero alert roles, and zero restart actions. Releasing the same supervised process cleared the banner automatically and loaded all eight sessions on the real board.

The local runtime drill used tmux on macOS. Windows ConPTY follows the same runtime contract; dead-runtime and Chat recovery, fallback safety, uncertain-commit handling, and worker concurrency are covered at the manager boundary.

### Slow startup after 53 seconds

![AO shows a neutral slow-start status with live details and no restart action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-daemon-startup-readiness-4064/.issue-assets/daemon-startup-readiness-4064/01-slow-start.png)

### Automatic transition to the recovered board

![AO board after the same supervised process becomes ready, showing eight recovered sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-daemon-startup-readiness-4064/.issue-assets/daemon-startup-readiness-4064/02-recovered-board.png)
