title: feat: validate workspace import before worker harness selection
body:
Closes #3955

## Problem

Workspace imports can currently advance to worker agent harness selection (CreateProjectAgentSheet) even when the folder scan includes only unresolved child repos (
eeds_init). The user configures worker and orchestrator agents, clicks submit, and only **then** receives a backend rejection (WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS or WORKSPACE_REPOS_REQUIRED). The validation should happen earlier in the flow so the user is blocked sooner.

## Solution

Added a **workspace preflight scan** in CreateProjectFlow.chooseDirectory() that mirrors the existing single_repo preflight pattern:

1. After the user selects a workspace folder, the frontend calls scanImportFolder({ path, mode: 'workspace' }) before setting selectedPath.
2. It checks whether any child repo is fully resolved (status !== 'error', hasRemote, and not 
eedsGitInit).
3. If **no ready repo exists**, the flow blocks and shows CreateProjectFolderDialog with the scan results and an appropriate error message. The agent harness selection sheet is never opened.
4. 
eeds_init child repos remain visible as **informational rows** (green check + 'Needs git init' label), matching the existing post-error recovery UI.
5. If the scan itself fails (edge case), the code silently falls through and lets the backend validate as before.

The backend WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS / WORKSPACE_REPOS_REQUIRED checks in workspace_registration.go remain untouched as the authoritative backstop.

## Changes

###  rontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx`n- Added workspace preflight validation block (21 lines) in chooseDirectory() between the checkAncestorRepo call and the setSelectedPath call.
- Two distinct error messages: one for zero repos detected, one for repos found but none fully resolved.

### i18n locale files (8 files)
Added two new keys to all locale files (en, de, es,  r, ja, ko, pt-BR, zh-CN):
- createProject.workspaceNoReadyRepos - shown when repos exist but none have an origin remote
- createProject.workspaceNoRepos - shown when the folder has zero child repos

## Verification

- 
pm run typecheck passes with zero errors in changed files (pre-existing errors in the unrelated packages/product-ui package are not affected).
- The change is purely additive: it adds an early-exit guard path using the same scanImportFolder and CreateProjectFolderDialog infrastructure already used by the post-error recovery flow.

## Notes

This is a follow-up to PR #3729, as noted in the issue.

title: fix(desktop): add AO_DISABLE_GPU escape hatch for broken GPU drivers
body:
## What

Read `AO_DISABLE_GPU` before app ready in `frontend/src/main.ts` and call `app.disableHardwareAcceleration()` when it is set, so a user whose GPU driver stack crashes Chromium can start the app anyway.

## Why

Fixes #3961.

AO sets no Electron GPU or Ozone options anywhere — `frontend/src/main.ts` and `frontend/forge.config.ts` have zero matches for `commandLine`, `appendSwitch`, `disableHardwareAcceleration`, or `ozone`, and the only `--disable-gpu` in the tree is a test harness (`test/e2e-pod/real-app.spec.ts`). So a user on a broken driver has no supported way to skip the crashing path: patch the source, or live with a GPU process that aborts repeatedly until Chromium gives up and drops to software rendering.

The abort itself is not AO's or Electron's. Symbolizing the core dump from a crash on this machine puts it squarely in Mesa:

```
#2  abort ()                                              libc
#3  _iris_batch_flush   (ret = -12  /* -ENOMEM */)        iris_batch.c:995
#5  iris_fence_flush                                      iris_fence.c:247
#8  dri_create_fence_fd                                   dri_helpers.c:131
#9  dri2_create_sync    (EGL_SYNC_NATIVE_FENCE_ANDROID)   egl_dri2.c:2880
#14 EGL_CreateSyncKHR                                     <Electron's bundled libGLESv2.so>
```

The kernel's i915 batch-submission ioctl returns `-ENOMEM`; Mesa's iris driver does not classify that as a recoverable context loss, so it falls through to an unconditional `abort()` that kills the host process. That is a Mesa policy decision and the real fix belongs upstream in `mesa/mesa`, not here. What belongs here is the missing escape hatch.

## Correcting my own issue text

Two things in #3961 were wrong, and I'd rather amend them here than have a reviewer find them:

1. **"No way to disable hardware acceleration" overstates what this achieves.** `app.disableHardwareAcceleration()` does **not** stop a GPU process from spawning — `getAppMetrics()` still reports a `GPU` type. What it drops is the *system GL driver* — Mesa here — falling that process back to Electron's bundled SwiftShader. That covers the reported abort, which happens inside Mesa, but it would not help a crash inside ozone-wayland/gbm: the child still carries `--ozone-platform=wayland` and still maps the system buffer allocator.
2. **The issue suggested `process.env.AO_DISABLE_GPU === "1"`.** That is the weakest parse in the repo and would silently ignore `AO_DISABLE_GPU=true` from a user whose app is crashing — the worst possible failure mode for an escape hatch. This PR uses the `keepDaemonAlive()` allowlist instead (`frontend/src/main/daemon-owner.ts`): trim, lowercase, accept `"1" | "true" | "yes" | "on"`, treat everything else as unset. That file's own comment explains why an allowlist beats "anything but 0/false" — it stops `"off"`/`"no"` from doing the opposite of what the user meant.

## How

One guard in the existing pre-ready block in `frontend/src/main.ts`, between `app.setAppUserModelId` and the `~/.ao` `userData` pin. It sits above the `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` / `app.exit(0)` bailout so it always runs, and `disableHardwareAcceleration()` throws if called after ready — verified it does.

Used the API rather than `app.commandLine.appendSwitch("disable-gpu")`. Measured on Electron 33.4.11: `getGPUFeatureStatus()` and the GPU child's switches are byte-identical between the two, but the API fails loudly when mis-ordered while a late `appendSwitch` fails silently. Did **not** add `--disable-software-rasterizer` — it flips `webgl`/`webgl2` to `disabled_off`, which would break WebGL in the renderer and the browser panel.

Docs: a row in the env table at `docs/cli/README.md` (`AO_KEEP_DAEMON` is the precedent there — also an Electron-main-only var), plus a symptom row in the frontend troubleshooting table in `docs/development.md`.

## Testing

Environment: Arch Linux (kernel 7.1.8), Hyprland/Wayland, hybrid Intel Raptor Lake-P UHD (`i915` + Mesa `iris`, the active renderer) + NVIDIA RTX 5050 Max-Q, Mesa 26.1.7, Electron 33.4.11.

**A/B on the real app**, same build, same session, `npm run dev` each way, inspecting the GPU child's `/proc/<pid>/maps` and `cmdline`:

| | flag unset | `AO_DISABLE_GPU=1` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU-process `SIGABRT` (core dumps) | **2**, 18s apart | **0** |
| `GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=134` | yes | **none** |
| `Cannot create bo ... usage=SCANOUT` | 6 | **0** |
| GL switches | none | `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader-webgl` |
| Active GL driver | Mesa (`libgallium`, `libEGL_mesa`) on the Intel iGPU | Electron's bundled SwiftShader (`libvk_swiftshader.so`) |

Crashes counted from `coredumpctl`, not just the log — the terminal output undercounts them, because Chromium restarts the GPU child and the later aborts land after the first burst of log lines. The same pattern reproduced on an earlier run of this branch's base: three aborts at 18–20s intervals.

Both runs reached a working app — daemon listening on `127.0.0.1:3002`, `/api/v1/{projects,sessions,agents,notifications,shell-terminals}` all 200.

`npm run typecheck` → 0 errors. `npm test` → 189/189 files, 2485 passed, 1 skipped.

**No unit test, deliberately.** `frontend/src/main.ts` has zero `export` statements and no importer, so a test cannot load it without firing `app.setName`, `app.setPath`, `requestSingleInstanceLock`/`app.exit(0)` and `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` at import time; no `main.test.ts` has ever existed. Playwright can't reach it either — `playwright.config.ts` runs `dev:web` with `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1`. Extracting a `shouldDisableGpu()` module purely to make one equality chain testable is what `AGENTS.md` line 82 rules out ("Add helpers only when they remove duplication across real call sites"). The sibling env flags in this file, `AO_OPEN_DEVTOOLS` and `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_PATH`, have no tests either. Happy to add one if you'd rather — the moment this guard takes a second input (a Wayland auto-detect, an `AO_OZONE_PLATFORM` switch, a `0`/`off` vocabulary) it should become `shouldDisableGpu(env, platform)` in `frontend/src/main/` with a table test next to `tray-lifecycle.test.ts`.

## Scope notes

- **Where the variable reaches.** `AO_DISABLE_GPU=1 ao start` works on Linux: `backend/internal/cli/start.go` passes no `Env` and `backend/internal/cli/process.go` leaves `cmd.Env` nil, so os/exec inherits the full environment. A menu/`.desktop` launch only sees the graphical session env, so those users need it in `~/.config/environment.d/` or the compositor env, not `~/.bashrc` — that entry is rewritten on every `ao start`, so hand-editing `Exec=` doesn't stick. On macOS `ao start` goes through `open --args`, which does not forward the caller's environment.
- The flag does not reach the agent-browser runtime child; `frontend/src/main/agent-browser-runtime.ts` rebuilds that process's env from a name allowlist with no `AO_*` entries. Irrelevant to this startup crash, but worth stating.
- A persisted in-app setting would be the nicer long-term shape, but it can't serve this case: the app has no window when the aborts happen, and `disableHardwareAcceleration()` must run pre-ready while the settings modules are async and post-ready.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense — justified above
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: Desktop: consolidate sidebar footer — separate 'Sign in'/'Account' row duplicates the Settings entry point
body:
## Feedback
The sidebar footer shows two stacked rows that should be one control: the AO Cloud account row ("Sign in" with a user icon, which becomes the signed-in email after auth) directly above the **Settings** button. The account entry point should be consolidated — e.g. live inside Settings — rather than existing as a separate always-visible row.

**Source:** Discord `#report-bugs` thread "we don't need two separate buttons" | **Reported by:** @piyush | **Analyzed against:** `3348277ec` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High (component verified on current main) | **Priority:** low — cosmetic/design, no functional breakage

### Screenshot
![Sidebar footer: "Sign in" row above "Settings" row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-sidebar-signin/.issue-assets/sidebar-signin/sign-in-settings.png)

## Current behavior
`frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx` renders in the `SidebarFooter` (expanded variant, lines ~446-461):
1. `<CloudAccountRow>` (~L1053) — when unauthenticated: full-width row with `User` icon + "Sign in" (`shell.signIn`), aria-label "Sign in to AO Cloud"; when authenticated: user email with a sign-out dropdown.
2. A separate Settings `<button>` (~L448-460) — `Settings` icon + "Settings", opens global settings.

Both rows share `NAV_ROW_CLASS` and are visually identical in size/shape — they read as two peer buttons stacked at the bottom of the sidebar (the screenshot shows the Settings row in its highlighted/hover state). The collapsed icon-rail repeats the same duplication via `<CloudAccountRailButton>` (~L1115) next to the Settings icon (~L466-481).

## Suggested direction
Pick ONE account entry point. Options (need maintainer decision):
- **A. Move account into Settings** — a "Account" section in the global settings view; remove `CloudAccountRow`/`CloudAccountRailButton` from the sidebar entirely. Cleanest footer: just Settings.
- **B. Merge into one row** — single account row that hosts settings (or vice versa), e.g. the signed-in email row opens a menu containing Settings + Sign out.
- **C. Show the account row only when signed in** — footer is just "Sign in-less" for unauthenticated users; account management moves behind Settings.

Any option should update both the expanded row and the collapsed rail button consistently, and keep the WorkOS PKCE `signIn()` flow from `useCloudSession` reachable.

## Impact
- Footer occupies two rows for what is conceptually one settings/account surface; extra visual noise on every screen.
- i18n keys `shell.signIn` / `shell.signInToAOCloud` / `shell.signedInAs` / `shell.signOut` are used only by these rows — consolidation should review all locales.

## Related
- None found (searched "sign in button", "cloud account sidebar" — no duplicates).

title: bug(orchestrator): stuck on "Preparing the orchestrator terminal" forever after the daemon is killed mid-spawn
body:
### Summary

If the daemon dies while an orchestrator session is being created, the project's orchestrator is broken permanently. The Orchestrator tab shows "Preparing the orchestrator terminal" forever, on that launch and every launch after it. Restarting the daemon does not help, and neither does reinstalling, because the bad state is a row in `ao.db`.

Starting a session happens in two steps: AO writes the session row first, then creates the git worktree. If the daemon is killed between those two steps, the row survives with no workspace and no terminal. AO's cleanup code (`rollbackSpawnSeedRow`) only runs when a spawn returns an *error*, so a spawn that is killed mid-flight leaves the row behind.

That leftover row is harmless for a worker session, but not for an orchestrator. `EnsureOrchestrator` returns the newest **active** orchestrator instead of spawning a new one, and the leftover row counts as active. So every future click on the Orchestrator tab gets handed the same dead row. Boot reconcile does not clean it up either: `reconcileLive` returns early when `WorkspacePath == ""`, so the row is skipped on every restart.

This happened to me twice in two days, on two different projects, during normal use. I did not have to do anything unusual to hit it.

### Steps to reproduce

Scripted version, hit on the first attempt (uses a throwaway data dir, does not touch your real `~/.ao`):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/{data,repo} && cd /tmp/repro/repo
git init -q -b main . && echo hi > README.md
git add . && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -qm init

AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/repro/data AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/repro/running.json AO_PORT=39201 ao daemon &

curl -s -X POST localhost:39201/api/v1/projects -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"path":"/tmp/repro/repo","projectId":"repro","config":{"defaultBranch":"main","orchestrator":{"agent":"claude-code"},"worker":{"agent":"claude-code"}}}'

# start an orchestrator, then kill the daemon while the worktree is being created
curl -s -X POST localhost:39201/api/v1/orchestrators -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"projectId":"repro"}' &
sleep 0.35
kill -9 $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('/tmp/repro/running.json'))['pid'])")
```

`defaultBranch` matters. Without it the local repo has no remote to resolve from, the spawn fails cleanly, and rollback deletes the row correctly — that is the healthy path, not this bug.

Result:

```
id       kind          is_terminated  runtime_handle_id  workspace_path  branch
repro-1  orchestrator  0              (empty)            (empty)         (empty)
```

Now restart the daemon on the same data dir and ask for the orchestrator again:

```
DB after reboot:              repro-1 | orchestrator | 0 | (no handle)
POST /api/v1/orchestrators:   {"orchestrator":{"id":"repro-1", ...}}
```

The dead row survives the restart and is handed straight back. In the desktop app that is the "Preparing the orchestrator terminal" screen.

In the app, the same thing happens if you open a project's Orchestrator tab and the daemon is hard-killed within about half a second (quit the app, force-quit it, or `kill -9` the daemon pid from `~/.ao/running.json`). A graceful stop is fine: the context cancels, the spawn errors, and rollback works as intended. The window is exactly as long as `git worktree add` takes, so a large repo makes it easier to hit.

### Expected behavior

Asking for a project's orchestrator either gives you a session with a working terminal, or fails with a visible error. A row that never got a workspace should not be able to block every future orchestrator for that project.

### Actual behavior

The Orchestrator tab shows "Preparing the orchestrator terminal. This can take a moment while AO creates the workspace and starts the agent." indefinitely. Nothing is actually being prepared; there is no work in flight. The daemon is healthy, the API answers, and worker sessions in the same project spawn and attach normally.

On my install, two orchestrators were in this state, from two projects:

```
id             kind          is_terminated  runtime_handle_id  workspace_path
aohack-161     orchestrator  0              (empty)            (empty)
omnicommand-1  orchestrator  0              (empty)            (empty)
aohack-164     worker        0              aohack-164         .../worktrees/aohack/aohack-164
```

`GET /api/v1/sessions` agrees: both orchestrators come back active with no `terminalHandleId` and no `branch`.

The reaper sees the problem but cannot act on it, so the daemon log carries this every 5 seconds indefinitely:

```
level=WARN msg="reaper: session has no runtime handle metadata, skipping" session=aohack-161
```

There is no way to recover from inside the app. The only fix I found is `POST /api/v1/sessions/<id>/kill` against the daemon by hand.

### Where the problem is

- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` — `Spawn` calls `m.store.CreateSession(...)` before `m.createSessionWorkspace(...)`. Every error path calls `rollbackSpawnSeedRow` / `rollbackSeedSpawnWorkspace`; process death bypasses all of them.
- `backend/internal/service/session/service.go` — `EnsureOrchestrator`: `if len(existing) > 0 { return newestSession(existing), nil }`, where `existing` is any non-terminated orchestrator, working terminal or not.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` — `reconcileLive`: `if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || ... { return nil }` skips the row on every boot.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx` — shows `terminal.preparingOrchestrator` whenever `handleId` is empty, which looks identical to a spawn that is genuinely still working.

### Not fixed by #4071

This is a different bug from #4064, and PR #4071 does not fix it. That PR changed how the reconcile pass *runs* (serial loop to a parallel worker pool) and how the supervisor reports a slow boot. The `WorkspacePath == ""` early return in `reconcileLive` is unchanged on `main` as of 3348277, so these rows are still skipped.

I verified this directly: built `main` at 3348277, reproduced with the script above, restarted, and the dead orchestrator was still returned by `POST /api/v1/orchestrators`.

The two bugs do feed each other, though. A `not_ready` banner invites the user to click "Restart daemon", and a daemon restarted mid-spawn is one way to create this state.

### Suggested fix

In `reconcileLive`, before the existing early return, treat "no workspace path **and** no runtime handle" as a spawn that died before its workspace existed, and mark it terminated. Both conditions are only true together before `createSessionWorkspace` returns, so a session that has a workspace but a dead runtime still takes the existing save-and-teardown path that preserves work. Reconcile runs before the API binds, so no in-flight spawn can be seen mid-write.

With that change applied to the same data dir from the repro:

```
WARN msg="reconcile: terminating interrupted spawn with no workspace or runtime" sessionID=repro-1
DB after boot:                repro-1 | orchestrator | 1  (terminated)
POST /api/v1/orchestrators:   {"orchestrator":{"id":"repro-2", ...}}
repro-2 → real runtime handle, real worktree, live tmux session
```

I have a branch ready with this change and a regression test, and am happy to open the PR. If you would rather fix it at the other end — having `EnsureOrchestrator` ignore orchestrators with no runtime handle when picking the active one — tell me and I will do it that way instead.

### AO version

Desktop app 0.12.6 (macOS). Also reproduced against `main` at 3348277.

### Environment

macOS 26.5.1 (Apple silicon), tmux 3.7b, git 2.50.1. 164 sessions in `ao.db`, 15 worktrees. `ao doctor` fully green.

title: Chat attachment batch drops valid files after one exceeds the remaining size budget
body:
## Bug

When a user selects several attachments at once, encountering one file that exceeds the remaining 25 MiB batch budget stops processing the batch. Valid smaller files later in the same selection are silently discarded even when they fit.

Source: reproduced while reviewing [PR #4005](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4005).

## Reproduction

Analyzed against main at `d380279b5`.

Select these files in one native Electron file-picker operation, in this order:

1. `a-9mb.txt` — 9 MiB
2. `b-9mb.txt` — 9 MiB
3. `c-rejected-9mb.txt` — 9 MiB and does not fit
4. `d-later-5mb.txt` — 5 MiB and does fit

Expected: the first, second, and fourth files remain staged; the third is rejected with the existing inline size feedback.

Actual: only the first and second files remain. Processing aborts at the third file, silently losing the fourth.

## Root cause

The production `useFileAttachments.addFiles` loop uses `break` for the total-byte cap. That is correct for the count cap, where no subsequent file can fit, but incorrect for a byte cap, where a later smaller file may fit.

## Impact

This can silently lose user-selected input during paste, drop, or file selection. The workaround is to reselect each missing file individually.

Priority: P2. Confidence: high.

## A/B evidence

**Before — current main silently drops the later fitting file**

![Before: later fitting file is silently dropped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vanshx999/agent-orchestrator/f31df7890/docs/screenshots/pr-4005/a-before-batch-aborts.png)

**After — PR #4005 rejects only the non-fitting file and keeps the later one**

![After: later fitting file remains staged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vanshx999/agent-orchestrator/f31df7890/docs/screenshots/pr-4005/b-after-later-file-kept.png)

Both captures use the real Electron desktop app, the native file input, browser `FileReader`, identical files, and fresh isolated AO data.

title: Attachment-only Chat drafts enable an impossible steering send
body:
## Bug

During an active Chat turn, selecting **Steer this turn** and staging an attachment with an empty text field enables the send button even though the steering boundary only accepts text. Clicking send or pressing Enter then does nothing: no steer request, no queued message, and no feedback.

Found while separating the two independent defects originally bundled in [PR #4005](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4005).

## Reproduction

Analyzed against main at `d380279b5`.

1. Start a Chat turn and keep it streaming.
2. Select **Steer this turn**.
3. Attach a file.
4. Leave the text field empty.
5. Press Enter or click the enabled send button.

Expected: an impossible steering submission is visibly disabled. The attachment remains staged so the user can add steering text or switch to **Queue for next**.

Actual: send appears enabled but silently performs no action. The attachment remains with no explanation.

## Root cause

`ChatComposer.canSend` counts staged attachments as sendable in every mode, while the steering handler intentionally rejects empty text. The visual eligibility rule and the actual steering contract disagree.

## Impact

The primary composer action advertises an operation that cannot succeed, making user input appear swallowed. Switching to **Queue for next** is a workaround, but the UI does not guide the user there.

Priority: P2. Confidence: high.

## A/B evidence

**Before — current main enables an attachment-only steering no-op**

![Before: attachment-only steering misleadingly enables send](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/e814f114a/docs/screenshots/chat-steer-attachment/a-before-enabled-noop.png)

**After — patched build disables the impossible action and retains the attachment**

![After: attachment-only steering is disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/e814f114a/docs/screenshots/chat-steer-attachment/b-after-disabled-retained.png)

Both captures use the real Electron desktop app with a live Claude turn and fresh isolated AO data. The patched run also verified that switching to **Queue for next** re-enables send with the same attachment still staged.

title: fix(chat): disable attachment-only steering sends
body:
Fixes #4081.

## What changed

While a Chat turn is running, attachment-only drafts no longer enable the composer send action when **Steer this turn** is selected. Steering accepts text only, so the button and Enter path now match that contract.

The staged attachment is deliberately retained. Adding text makes steering valid; switching to **Queue for next** immediately re-enables send and preserves the attachment for the queued message.

This was split out of #4005 during deep review so each PR owns one issue.

## Tests

`ChatSteer.test.tsx` now exercises the actual keyboard boundary:

- focuses the textarea before pressing Enter;
- proves attachment-only steering disables send;
- proves Enter calls neither steer, queue/send, nor attachment staging;
- proves the attachment stays present;
- proves switching to Queue re-enables submission and then stages/sends the attachment.

Verification:
- focused ChatSteer suite: 19 passed;
- frontend typecheck: passed;
- full frontend suite: 190 files; 2,501 passed and 1 skipped.

## Real Electron A/B evidence

Both runs used a live streaming Claude Chat turn, **Steer this turn**, `steer-proof.txt`, an empty textarea, and a fresh isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`. The screenshots are attached as review evidence and are not part of the PR code diff.

### Before — current main exposes an enabled no-op

![Before: attachment-only steering misleadingly enables send](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4082/.issue-assets/pr-4082/a-before-enabled-noop.png)

Pressing Enter sends no steer request, queues no message, and gives no feedback.

### After — impossible action is disabled

![After: attachment-only steering is disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4082/.issue-assets/pr-4082/b-after-disabled-retained.png)

The attachment remains available, and the same live run verified that switching to Queue re-enables send.

title: fix(kanban): track OpenCode activity and required reviews
body:
## Summary

Improve Kanban status tracking for OpenCode sessions and ensure GitHub pull requests awaiting review appear in the In Review column.

Fixes #4087.

## Changes

- Report OpenCode session creation, prompt submission, tool execution, and resumed permission/question flows as active work.
- Observe OpenCode's real generic events: `permission.asked` and `question.asked` move a session to Needs You; reply/reject events return it to Working.
- Remove the ineffective `permission.ask` plugin hook, which OpenCode declares but does not invoke in its active permission flow.
- Continue reporting OpenCode idle transitions from session status events.
- Add normalized active and permission-blocked activity mappings to the OpenCode adapter.
- Give required-review facts precedence over generic provider merge blockers so pull requests awaiting review display as In Review instead of PR Open.
- Add regression coverage for supported OpenCode events/hooks and the required-review status combination emitted by GitHub.

## Kanban behavior

For OpenCode activity:

- Session start, prompt submission, tool execution, or a prompt response -> Working
- Permission approval or explicit answer required -> Needs You
- Session idle -> the applicable idle or SCM-derived status

For tracked pull requests:

- Review required -> In Review
- CI failing -> CI Failed
- Changes requested or unresolved review feedback -> Changes Requested
- Mergeable -> Ready to Merge
- Merged -> Merged

Live agent activity takes precedence over SCM status. Once OpenCode becomes idle, the applicable pull-request status is shown.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`
- `go test -p 1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- Focused OpenCode, activity-dispatch, and CLI tests
- Bun compilation of the installed OpenCode plugin

title: feat/headless-remote-daemon
body:
## What

Adds supported headless/remote-daemon mode to AO across two commits:

### Backend

* Adds `ao headless`, a foreground and systemd-friendly entrypoint.
* Starts the normal loopback daemon and enables the existing authenticated remote/mobile listener.
* Supports `--remote-port` with `3011` as the default.
* Enables and verifies Tailscale Secure Pairing before reporting readiness.
* Fails closed with a non-zero exit and clear error if the Tailscale CLI, MagicDNS certificates, or `tailscale serve` cannot establish HTTPS.
* Reuses persisted credentials across restarts and prints the tailnet URL/retrieval instructions without exposing the password.
* Adds `ao remote status|credentials|rotate|enable|disable [--json]` as thin loopback CLI clients over the existing `/api/v1/mobile/*` routes.
* Adds numeric API compatibility via `daemonmeta.APIVersion = 1` in `/healthz` and `/readyz`.

### Desktop

* Adds **Settings → Daemon connection** with:

  * Local (default)
  * Remote (HTTPS root URL + password)
* Adds strict URL validation and **Test and connect / Disconnect / Forget remote** flows.
* Remote mode uses a random-port loopback forwarding proxy supporting:

  * HTTP request/response bodies
  * SSE streaming
  * Bidirectional WebSocket for terminal mux
  * Bearer credential injection
  * Renderer-origin preservation for CORS
  * Hop-by-hop header stripping
  * Redirect rejection when credentials could cross origins
  * Normal TLS certificate validation
* Passwords are encrypted using Electron `safeStorage`, with an in-memory-only fallback when unavailable.
* Credentials are never written to logs, telemetry, URLs, or renderer payloads.
* Remote mode disables machine-local functionality such as file drop and browser preview, and uses explicit remote path entry instead of local file pickers.
* Loopback-only mobile controls are hidden in remote mode.

## Why

AO currently has no supported way to run persistently on a headless host such as a server or Raspberry Pi and connect the Mac desktop app to it.

The only existing workaround was the undocumented `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` + SSH tunnel approach.

This adds a supported remote-daemon path without weakening AO's existing security boundary:

* The primary daemon listener remains `127.0.0.1`-only and unauthenticated by design.
* Remote access uses the existing opt-in authenticated second listener from ADR 0001.
* Tailscale HTTPS is the only documented transport.
* Plaintext remote access is never silently substituted.
* Mobile pairing behavior remains unchanged.

## How

The implementation intentionally reuses the existing remote/mobile infrastructure instead of introducing a parallel authentication system.

`ao headless` drives the existing `mobilebridge`, secure-pairing, and restore-on-boot paths. Existing `/api/v1/mobile/*` routes, persisted state, lockout behavior, and `lanControlBlockedPrefixes` gating remain unchanged.

The headless startup path verifies Tailscale HTTPS end-to-end before reporting readiness, including:

1. Tailscale CLI availability
2. MagicDNS certificate availability
3. `tailscale serve` configuration
4. Serve target matching the authenticated remote listener

Reviewers should primarily focus on:

* `backend/internal/cli/headless.go`
* `backend/internal/daemon/headless*.go`
* `frontend/src/main/remote-proxy.ts`
* `frontend/src/main/remote-settings.ts`

In remote mode, the Electron app does **not**:

* inspect `running.json`
* spawn a local daemon
* perform local identity checks
* call remote `/shutdown`

Quitting the desktop app only closes its local forwarding proxy; the remote daemon remains running.

### Intentional V1 omissions

* Only one saved remote daemon.
* Tailscale HTTPS is the only documented transport.
* No Tailscale Funnel/public-internet exposure.
* No browser-served dashboard.
* Browser preview and local file drop remain disabled remotely because those bridges are machine-local.

Known cosmetic issue: `ao remote status --json` can surface the existing `"traffic is not encrypted"` warning from the pre-existing mobilebridge payload even when secure pairing is active. This is a backward-compatibility issue and can be addressed separately.

## Testing

### Backend

```bash
go test ./...
go test -race ./...
go vet ./...
```

Added/updated coverage includes:

* `backend/internal/cli/remote_test.go`
* `backend/internal/daemon/headless_test.go`
* `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/mobile_test.go`
* `backend/internal/httpd/server_test.go`
* `backend/internal/mobilebridge/magicdns_test.go`

Covered:

* Fail-closed startup
* Missing Tailscale CLI
* Certificate/serve failures
* Mismatched `tailscale serve` target
* Credential restoration
* `--remote-port`
* Clean shutdown
* All `ao remote` subcommands
* JSON output
* Missing daemon/error envelopes
* Credential rotation
* Disabled remote access
* LAN authentication regression checks
* Lockout behavior
* Loopback-only gating
* Mobile compatibility
* Primary listener binding

### Frontend

```bash
npm run typecheck
```

Also covered:

* Remote URL validation
* Proxy behavior
* Settings-store behavior
* SSE streaming
* WebSocket duplex communication
* Bearer credential replacement
* Redirect rejection
* 401 mapping
* Corrupt persisted state
* `safeStorage` unavailable fallback

### End-to-end

Validated on a macOS host over a real tailnet:

* Headless startup fails closed without Tailscale.
* `tailscale serve` correctly exposes the authenticated listener.
* REST endpoints return expected `401/200` responses.
* `/mux` WebSocket works.
* Full chat turn works through the tailnet.
* Password rotation invalidates old credentials.
* Daemon restart restores remote access without re-pairing.
* Quitting the desktop app leaves the remote daemon running.

Not yet tested:

* Real Raspberry Pi/cross-machine deployment
* Mobile-app pairing against `ao headless`
* Remote-mode UI gates beyond unit tests

The matching headless Linux archives (`x64`/`arm64`) are planned as a follow-up PR, including CI builds and testing on real runners.

## Checklist

* [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
* [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
* [x] Follows [[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
* [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
* [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(agy): restore Kanban activity tracking
body:
## What

Restore AGY Kanban activity tracking by migrating AO's workspace integration to the current Antigravity hook contract.

- Install one AO-owned named hook at `.agents/hooks.json`.
- Map `PreInvocation` and `PostToolUse` to Active.
- Map `Stop` to Idle.
- Advertise submit activity support while keeping blocked activity unsupported.
- Return the valid empty JSON object required by modern AGY hook handlers.

## Why

The AGY adapter still wrote the obsolete Gemini-style `.gemini/hooks.json` schema and event names, so current AGY releases did not invoke AO's activity callbacks. Sessions therefore could not reliably move between active and idle Kanban states.

## How

AO owns only the `agent-orchestrator` top-level entry in `.agents/hooks.json`. Installation is idempotent, preserves other named hooks and unknown fields, rejects malformed JSON without overwriting it, and uninstall removes only AO's entry.

The adapter intentionally does not claim blocked/Needs You support because AGY does not expose a reliable permission-wait lifecycle event. Process exit remains runtime-derived. SCM-derived statuses—In Review, Changes Requested, CI Failed, Ready to Merge, and Merged—continue to come from AO's shared SCM observer.

Legacy `.gemini/hooks.json` installation is intentionally removed rather than dual-written to avoid duplicate callbacks and incompatible schemas.

## Testing

- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-agy-modern-hooks-go-cache go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... -count=1`
- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-agy-modern-hooks-go-cache go test ./internal/cli ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/... ./internal/session_manager/... -count=1`
- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-agy-modern-hooks-final-go-cache go test -p 1 ./...`
- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-agy-modern-hooks-final-go-cache go vet ./...`

title: feat(renderer): zero-friction in-product user surveys
body:
## What

Zero-friction, one-tap in-product surveys to learn what behavioral telemetry
cannot: is a repo **work / personal / learning**, is there a **team**, would
users **miss us** (PMF), and what **broke**. Each question is anchored to a
moment the user is already in (a repo they just added, a spawn that failed) so
the answer is an obvious fact, never a "which kind of user am I?" deliberation.

## Why custom, not PostHog native surveys

The renderer deliberately sets `disable_surveys` and `advanced_disable_flags`
(in `lib/telemetry.ts`) because `/surveys` and `/flags` poll PostHog on init and
are billed per request, pure cost for ~2k users. Turning native surveys on would
re-introduce that. So this ships a tiny prompt and records the answer as an
ordinary captured event (`ao.renderer.survey_answered`). No extra network
requests, no `survey:write` key, nothing to configure in PostHog.

## The surveys

`repo-who`, `repo-purpose` (on project added) · `pmf` (≥3 spawns) · `what-broke`
(spawn failed) · `why-ao` (2nd session) · `would-pay` (≥5 spawns, only Work +
My-team users). Guarantees, enforced in `surveyController.ts` and unit-tested:
**at most one survey per user per week**, never re-ask an answered/dismissed one,
activation gates, and `would-pay` never reaches a student.

## Structure

- `lib/survey/definitions.ts` — surveys as data.
- `lib/survey/surveyController.ts` — pure, injectable gating (8 unit tests).
- `lib/survey/index.ts` — singleton + `onProjectAdded` / `onSessionSpawned` /
  `onSpawnFailed` triggers + the store the prompt subscribes to.
- `components/SurveyPrompt.tsx` — one dismissible bottom-right card.
- Wired at spawn success/failure (`spawn-orchestrator.ts`), project-added
  (`_shell.tsx`), and mounted once in `__root.tsx`.

## The payoff

The `README.md` includes the cross-tab that joins survey answers to actual
retention: the segment with the highest still-active rate among "I'd be lost" +
Work + My-team users is the ICP, discovered from data, to target in onboarding,
messaging, and pricing.

## Verification

`surveyController` gating is unit-tested (8/8: weekly cap, no-re-ask, minSpawns,
would-pay work+team-only, dismiss-skip, event emission). The React wiring
(triggers + mount) follows the existing `captureRendererEvent` conventions; the
full renderer typecheck/build runs in CI (not run locally, no workspace install
in this environment).

title: bug(opencode): approval and question prompts remain Working
body:
## Bug

OpenCode sessions remain in **Working** when the TUI is waiting for a user permission approval or an explicit answer. The session should move to **Needs You** until the user responds.

**Source:** User report in Codex task on 2026-08-18  
**Analyzed against:** PR branch `fix/opencode-permission-blocker-detection` at `b9bebee90694baa09f4f2515eeae8ee35979ff67`  
**OpenCode:** `1.18.18`  
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Start an AO worker using OpenCode with permissions configured to ask.
2. Prompt OpenCode to perform an operation requiring approval, or have it invoke the question tool.
3. Wait for OpenCode's approval/question form to appear in the TUI.
4. Observe the AO Kanban card remains in **Working** instead of moving to **Needs You**.

## Root Cause

[PR #4083](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4083) added a `permission.ask` plugin hook in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/assets/ao-activity.ts`.

OpenCode's active permission implementation does not invoke that hook. It publishes `permission.asked` and `permission.replied` through the generic plugin `event` callback. User questions similarly publish `question.asked`, `question.replied`, and `question.rejected`.

Because AO listens to the dormant hook, no `permission-blocked` activity callback reaches the daemon and the last durable state remains `active`/Working.

OpenCode upstream references:

- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7006
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/9229
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/plugins.mdx

## Fix

- Observe `permission.asked` and `question.asked` in the generic event handler and emit AO's blocked activity signal.
- Observe the corresponding reply/reject events and emit active so the sticky blocked state clears immediately.
- Remove the ineffective `permission.ask` handler.
- Add regression coverage for permission and question event transitions.

## Impact

- OpenCode approval prompts are easy to miss because cards stay in Working.
- Needs-input notifications are not emitted.
- Explicit questions from OpenCode have the same failure mode.

## Related

- [PR #4083](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4083) — existing OpenCode Kanban activity fix branch where this correction will land.

title: fix(lifecycle): deduplicate review feedback across internal and SCM lanes
body:
## What

Prevent duplicate worker nudges when AO's internal reviewer and the SCM observer surface the same GitHub review feedback through separate lifecycle lanes.

This change:

- correlates an internal AO review with the later GitHub review observation;
- suppresses duplicate formal-review and inline-comment nudges for that same review;
- deduplicates review comments at the review-thread level so replies in an already-notified thread do not wake the worker again;
- persists the thread-level marker so the suppression survives a daemon restart;
- keeps genuinely new review threads actionable.

## Why

AO's internal reviewer delivery and SCM observation are separate lifecycle paths. The same GitHub review can therefore be delivered once by `ApplyReviewBatch` and then observed again by `ApplyPRObservation`, causing the owning worker to be nudged twice for one finding.

Inline review comments have a related duplicate path: a reply in the same review thread receives a new provider comment ID and can otherwise look like a new actionable finding.

## How

- Request each GraphQL review comment's parent `pullRequestReview.url` and carry it transiently through the SCM/PR observation ports. No database migration is added.
- Persist cross-lane coverage after successful internal review delivery using the GitHub numeric review/database ID.
- Suppress formal-review and inline-comment nudges when that same provider review was already delivered internally.
- Deduplicate review comments by `ThreadID` when available, falling back to comment ID when necessary.
- Persist the covered thread marker so suppression survives daemon restart.
- Fail open on coverage lookup errors so genuine review feedback is not silently dropped.

Intentional trade-off: follow-up comments in the exact same existing review thread remain deduplicated. A distinct new review thread or distinct new review still produces a nudge.

## Testing

Validated after rebasing onto current `main`:

```text
go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/scm/github ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/observe/scm ./internal/ports
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff origin/main...HEAD --check
```
All of the above pass.

Regression coverage includes:

- internal review followed by the same formal SCM review;
- inline comment from the same SCM review;
- worker reply in the same review thread;
- persistence across daemon restart;
- a genuinely new review thread still nudging;
- GraphQL parent-review URL projection through transient observation types.

A pre-rebase `go test ./...` run on this Windows host had platform/environment-dependent failures. A clean detached worktree at the same base commit produced the same failing package set, so those failures were not introduced by this patch.

`go test -race` could not be executed locally because this Windows Go environment has `CGO_ENABLED=0` and no C compiler installed. CI should provide the authoritative race result.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` and rebased onto current `main`
- [x] One focused change; no matching existing issue/PR found
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for the affected behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: SCM observer drops fetched PR observations after repo rename/transfer — PR panel stuck at 'Checking merge readiness'
body:
## Bug
The session PR panel shows a mostly-stuck **"Checking merge readiness"** ("Waiting for the latest checks and review state.") even when GitHub has a fully resolved answer. Review state stays current, but CI and mergeability never resolve. Reported across MANY agent sessions — systemic on any install whose stored PR rows carry a pre-transfer repo name.

**Source:** maintainer chat report (triage session agent-orchestrator-139)
**Reported by:** @AgentWrapper
**Analyzed against:** `d380279b5` (origin/main, 2026-08-18)
**AO version:** packaged desktop daemon (`ao version` → `dev`), port 3001
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced; pre-fix regression test reproduces the production fingerprint byte-for-byte

## Corrected symptom + second mechanism (added 2026-08-19)

Maintainer follow-up: the state is **not permanently stuck — it flaps**. Correct merge status appears intermittently, then reverts to "Checking merge readiness", and severity increased after recent updates. A live DB watch (5s sampling on the affected machine) captured one full cycle for PRs #4069/#2870:

```
15:47:56  Untrivial-ai/...  passing/blocked   title set, hashes set        (heal)
15:48:27  AgentWrapper/...  unknown/unknown   title gone, hashes WIPED     (clobber)
15:49:02  Untrivial-ai/...  passing/blocked   title set, hashes set        (heal)
```

**Mechanism 2 — discovery baseline clobber.** The project checkout carries a stale `upstream` remote (`AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`), so `resolveScanRepos` scans **two identities for one repository**. Whichever identity the row does *not* currently carry finds the PR "not in subjects" during `discoverNewPRs` and persists a baseline row — and `UpsertPR` (`queries/pr.sql`) overwrites `ci_state`, `mergeability`, `repo`, `title`, and the semantic hashes unconditionally. Healing requires a same- or later-poll detail fetch whose observation key matches a live subject.

The two mechanisms compose into the observed behavior:
- **Pre-#3923**: `obs.Repo` echoed the requesting ref, so every fetch healed under either identity — the clobber existed but the unknown window was sub-poll and invisible (its visible artifact was #3922's duplicate rows instead).
- **Post-#3923**: the stale-identity heal path is dead (Mechanism 1, the key-mismatch drop), so after an `AgentWrapper`-side clobber the row stays `unknown` until the `Untrivial-ai` listing happens to re-discover it — windows of many polls, matching "stuck most of the time".

**Fix implications:** [PR #4090](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4090)'s minimal seam fix makes every tracked-subject fetch heal again, shrinking the visible unknown window to at most one poll — but the clobber/repo ping-pong churn (hash wipes forcing refetches and lifecycle redelivery) remains. Only the ProviderID-primary identity cleanup (see architectural scope below) removes it: discovery dedupes listing entries against tracked subjects by provider identity, so a second scan name for the same repo never re-baselines a tracked row.

**Immediate workaround on affected machines:** remove the stale remote (`git remote remove upstream` in the project checkout) and restart the daemon (the scan set is memoized per process).

## Concrete case (verified live)
Session `agent-orchestrator-138`, PR [#4069](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4069). GitHub GraphQL (replayed with the daemon's exact batch query, which succeeds via the rename redirect): `state=OPEN, mergeable=MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED, reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED, statusCheckRollup=SUCCESS` (single check `scan`, COMPLETED/SUCCESS).

Meanwhile `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-138/pr` returns `ci.state="unknown"`, `mergeability.state="unknown"`, `review.decision="review_required"`, `title=""`, `changedFiles=0` — and the daemon's `pr` row shows:

```
repo = AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator   <-- pre-transfer name
ci_state = unknown, mergeability = unknown
review_decision = review_required        <-- current (review_hash set, real thread IDs)
title = '' , provider_mergeable = '' , metadata_hash = ''
```

**11 tracked PRs** on the machine share this exact fingerprint (`repo=AgentWrapper/…`, empty metadata, unknown CI/mergeability, fresh review), all stamped by the same poll. The frontend is innocent: `prCardPresentation` (frontend/src/renderer/lib/pr-display.ts:230) correctly renders "Checking merge readiness" whenever `ci.state` is `unknown`/`pending` or `mergeability.state` is `unknown` — the daemon just never resolves them.

## Root Cause
Repo identity is baked into the observation dispatch key, and a GitHub repo rename/org transfer makes the two sides of the key disagree forever:

1. `repoForTrackedPR` (backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:879-886) derives the tracked subject's repo from the **stored PR row** (`AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator`), so refs are fetched under the stale name.
2. The batch fetch succeeds through GitHub's rename redirect, but `scmObservationFromGraphQL` (backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go:475-478) canonicalizes `obs.Repo` from the PR URL to the **new** owner/name (`Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`).
3. `Poll` (backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:487) and `reconcileTerminalGitHubPRs` (:1428) key fetched observations with `prKeyFromObs(obs)` — the canonical key — then look up `selection.subjectsByPR[key]`, which only contains the stale key. **The observation is silently dropped every poll**, and `chunkSeen` misses the ref key so the repo is additionally marked refresh-incomplete (ETag/cursor pinned).
4. `refreshReviews` (observer.go:1607-1656) keys by the subject and fetches per-ref directly, so review facts stay fresh — while its `observationFromLocal` fallback persists review-only writes that keep re-asserting the stale repo name and empty metadata. Hence the exact split symptom: review current, CI/mergeability `unknown` forever.

The pre-fix regression test reproduces the production fingerprint exactly: `persisted PR = repo "old/r" title "" ci "unknown" mergeability "unknown"`.

## Reproduction
1. Track an open PR in a session (row in `pr` table with `repo=<old-owner>/<name>`).
2. Transfer/rename the repository on GitHub so the canonical owner changes.
3. Let the observer poll. CI/mergeability stay `unknown` indefinitely; the PR panel shows "Checking merge readiness" while the Review row is correct.

## Fix
PR incoming on branch `ao/agent-orchestrator-139/scm-rename-rekey`: resolve the dispatch key by falling back to the requesting ref (matched by PR URL / URL alias) when the canonical key matches no ref, in both the normal batch loop and terminal reconciliation. Persistence then records the canonical repo on the row (`domainFromObservation` uses `obs.Repo`), so the tracked identity self-heals on the next poll. Focused regression tests included; they fail without the fix with the exact production fingerprint.

## Impact
- Merge-readiness surface permanently broken for every PR tracked before a repo transfer/rename (org migrations are routine).
- CI state, failing-check links, diff stats, and title all stuck empty; lifecycle decisions that depend on CI/mergeability facts never fire.
- The repo is marked refresh-incomplete each poll, pinning list ETags/cursors.

## Related
- [#3252](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3252) — covers the *discovery/attribution* facet after a transfer (new PRs not attached; stale project origin; gh wrapper PATH). This issue is the complementary *enrichment* facet: PRs that ARE tracked never get CI/mergeability. The observation-drop also explains why re-discovery could not repair already-tracked rows on the affected machine.

## Architectural scope: stable PR identity (added 2026-08-18)

Maintainer review identified this bug as a regression from [PR #3923](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3923) and the fourth member of a rename-bug cluster ([#2509](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2509), [#3922](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3922), [#3252](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3252)). The structural cause: PR identity is derived independently in five layers (stored row `repo`/`url`, observer subject key, observation dispatch key, repo scan set, store `provider_id`/alias machinery), and a repo rename/transfer makes them disagree. The stable identity — the provider node ID (`PR_kwDO…`, GitLab MR global ID) — has been captured on every observation and enforced unique in storage since #3923's migration 0097, but the observer never dispatches on it.

**Expanded scope for this issue:** [PR #4090](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4090) will grow from the minimal seam patch into the ProviderID-primary identity cleanup, pending approval of the architecture doc (`docs/scm-observer.md`, added in that PR):

- one identity helper owning key construction: `provider:host@provider_id` when known, legacy `provider:host:repo#number` as a self-retiring fallback for rows without a provider ID;
- subjects, observation dispatch, review refresh, and per-PR caches keyed by identity; repo-level guards/ETags/cursors stay name-keyed;
- discovery dedupes subjects by identity, closing the two-scan-names→two-rows class (#3922) at the source;
- rows self-heal to canonical repo/URL on the next successful fetch — no schema change (0097 suffices), no data migration;
- a cross-layer transfer scenario test suite covering discovery, batch fetch, reconciliation, review refresh, and legacy-row fallback.

Out of scope (remain on #3252): project-origin refresh, gh-wrapper PATH precedence, doctor checks.

title: fix(scm): single-source PR identity — end the merge-readiness flap after repo transfers
body:
Fixes #4089

## Summary
The "Checking merge readiness" flap traced to one structural cause: **PR identity was derived independently in five layers** (stored row, subject key, observation dispatch key, repo scan set, store `provider_id`/alias machinery), and a repo rename/transfer makes them disagree. This PR gives identity one owner and lands in three stages (see the "Simplification pass" note below):

1. **`fix(scm)` — the dispatch seam**: canonical observations for renamed repos are delivered to their tracked subjects instead of being dropped every poll.
2. **`refactor(scm)` — single-source identity**: a PR's identity is **`(provider, host, provider_id)`** — the rename-proof node id both adapters already stamp and migration 0097 already enforces unique. Repo name, number, and URL are mutable display coordinates.
   - `identityPRKey` / `keyForTrackedPR` own key construction; the legacy `repo#number` key survives only as a **self-retiring fallback** for rows that predate provider ids (their first successful fetch stamps one).
   - Subjects, per-PR caches, and review refresh are identity-keyed. Repo-level list ETags/sync cursors/commit guards deliberately stay name-keyed — listing genuinely is a per-name operation.
   - **Discovery dedupes by identity**: a listing served under a second scan name (stale `upstream` remote after a transfer) recognizes tracked PRs by node id and never re-baselines them — the fact-wiping clobber (#4089 mechanism 2, captured live flapping every ~45s) becomes structurally impossible, not merely quickly repaired. This prevents a second scan name from creating a new duplicate row for an already tracked provider-native PR (#3922's discovery artifact); existing legacy id-less duplicates remain handled by the store's identity/alias machinery.
   - Rows self-heal to the canonical repo/URL on their next fetch. **No schema change, no data migration** — 0097 suffices. In-memory caches only change key shape.
3. **`refactor(scm)` — positional fetch contract** (the simplification pass): `FetchPullRequests` results are **positionally aligned with the requested refs** (`result[i]` answers `refs[i]`; a PR the batch query cannot resolve leaves a `Fetched=false` placeholder at its index — documented on the port). The observer records which subject each ref was issued for and attributes `batch[i]` directly, so the whole observation-matching layer (`observationSubjectKey`, `prKeyFromObs`, the `keyByRef` bridge, `chunkSeen`/`reconcileSeen` bookkeeping, and the interim URL/alias fallback from stage 1) is deleted outright. GitLab and the multi dispatcher already honored alignment; GitHub was the lone outlier. Legacy id-less rows are covered by the same mechanism — no fallback needed. Net, `observer.go` is smaller than `origin/main` while carrying the rename fix and the clobber kill.
4. **`docs`** — `docs/scm-observer.md`: the SCM architecture doc — pipeline, durable-state invariants, the five-way identity split, the live flap capture, and this design.

## Evidence
- Live daemon returned `ci=unknown, mergeability=unknown` while GitHub said `MERGEABLE/BLOCKED` with green checks; 11 PR rows shared the stale-repo fingerprint.
- A 5s DB watch captured the flap: healthy → clobbered (`AgentWrapper/…`, facts + hashes wiped by discovery baseline) → healed (canonical fetch), cycling every ~45s. Details in #4089.

## Tests
- `TestPoll_IdentityKeyedDispatchSurvivesRename` — canonical (renamed-repo) observation reaches its tracked subject; the fixture's stored URL deliberately differs from the canonical URL so no content-based join could explain the delivery.
- `TestPoll_SecondScanNameDoesNotRebaselineTrackedPR` — the clobber regression; fails pre-change with the exact live fingerprint (`CI:unknown, Repo:old/r`, hashes wiped).
- `TestPoll_RenamedRepoObservationPersistsUnderTrackedRef` / `…ReconciliationPersistsUnderTrackedRef` — renamed-repo observations persist through both the batch and terminal-reconciliation paths (positional attribution; legacy id-less rows covered by the same mechanism).
- `TestKeyForTrackedPR` — key resolution table: identity key when a provider id exists, legacy name key otherwise.
- Full `observe/…`, `adapters/scm/…`, `storage/…`, `lifecycle/…`, `service/…` suites green; `go vet` clean.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Legacy id-less rows register under the name-based key until their first successful fetch stamps a provider id. With only an already-renamed remote, discovery may write one baseline before that fetch; positional attribution still delivers the observation and makes the fallback self-retire.
- Discovery dedupe requires the listing to carry a provider id (both adapters stamp it since #3923); an id-less listing entry against an id-less row still dedupes by name.
- The remaining transfer facets (project-origin refresh, gh-wrapper PATH, doctor checks) stay on #3252.

title: fix(chat): preserve image attachments when steering
body:
## Summary

- stage pending chat attachments before steering, using the same durable worktree references as queued sends
- forward negotiated native image blocks through the renderer client and daemon steer endpoint
- settle in-flight paste/drop reads before submission so an immediate Enter cannot send a text-only steer
- synchronously guard submission and disable composer controls so key repeat cannot issue duplicate steers
- preserve the draft and attachments when the provider refuses a steer, then restore textarea focus for keyboard retry
- render the durable staged image inline in the landed steer bubble, hide the internal attachment suffix, and avoid duplicate native thumbnails
- regenerate the OpenAPI contract and typed frontend schema

## Root cause

The composer deliberately treated steering as text-only: attachment-only drafts left the steer button disabled, and text-plus-image steers bypassed attachment staging. The frontend steer request and HTTP DTO also omitted attachments, even though the chat service and Codex/ACP driver layers already support structured image content during steering.

The first review follow-up found that paste/drop starts FileReader asynchronously, but submission inspected render-time attachment state. Pressing Enter before a large image finished reading could therefore steer the existing text alone and leave the image behind in the composer.

The second review follow-up found a re-entrancy window before onSteer set its external pending state. Repeated Enter during the file read or staging await could run two submissions concurrently, each with a fresh client message ID, producing duplicate guidance. Disabling the active textarea exposed a retained-draft focus regression on refusal/failure, so the composer now restores focus after re-enabling.

Native testing then exposed a separate history-rendering asymmetry: ordinary human messages parsed AO staged attachment references, while SteerMessage printed the internal path suffix and rendered only optional native content blocks. A successfully delivered staged image could therefore exist and open in Browser without appearing in chat history.

## Evidence

### Before the fix

The regression probes reproduced the loss and concurrency points:

    ChatComposer: expected “Steer the running turn” to be enabled; received disabled
    useConversation: POST /conversation/steer omitted attachments
    conversation_steer controller: service received Content == nil
    immediate-paste regression: onSteer received only “inspect this” while FileReader was pending
    double-Enter regression: attachment staging was called twice before FileReader completion
    history regression: landed steer had no inline image despite its durable .ao/attachments reference

### After the fix

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Immediate-paste/double-Enter regression | Two Enter events are batched before React re-renders; controls disable immediately, staging runs once, and onSteer runs once with text plus native image bytes |
| Retained-draft regression | refusal/failure keeps text and attachments and restores textarea focus for the next Enter |
| Steer-history regressions | staged image renders inline, internal path suffix stays hidden, and matching native content does not duplicate the thumbnail |
| Focused affected suites | 5 files passed; 155 tests passed |
| Frontend typecheck | passed |
| Changed HTTP/spec packages | passed, including route/spec parity |
| Generated API artifacts | regenerated with no diff |
| Full renderer suite | 191 files passed; 2,525 tests passed; 1 skipped |
| GitHub Actions | 10/10 checks passed on rewritten/rebased head d46e2f2d1 |

Actual Electron evidence is attached in [this PR comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4092#issuecomment-5330876245). The corrected after capture visibly places the AO elephant inside the landed steer bubble with Summary selected and Browser unselected. The live renderer reported a complete 1024×1024 image, and the session preview request returned HTTP 200.

## Known local suite issue

The broad backend suite still reports five unrelated internal/cli spawn-context tests returning HTTP 404. No CLI files are changed here; the changed HTTP/spec packages pass. Two unrelated interactive-shell auth tests timed out only under the fully parallel run and passed immediately in isolation.

title: fix(usage): collect cost data for Chat sessions
body:
## Summary

- collect usage for Chat workers from their provider conversation identity
- keep TUI collection on the hook-derived agent session identity
- apply the identity selection consistently during lifecycle reactivation, hook fallback, and daemon-start backfill
- cover both the live Chat controller lifecycle and startup recovery paths

## Root cause

A fresh Chat controller persists its native transcript identity in `provider_conversation_id`. It has no terminal hook, so `agent_session_id` remains empty. The usage collector previously consulted only `agent_session_id`, which meant it could not create a usage binding or discover the provider JSONL transcript for Chat-only sessions.

Switching the same session to TUI copied the native identity into `agent_session_id`. That made the existing transcript discoverable immediately, which is why cost observability appeared to start working after the interface conversion.

This change selects `provider_conversation_id` for committed Chat sessions and preserves `agent_session_id` for TUI sessions. Older migrated Chat records still fall back to their hook-derived identity when no provider conversation ID exists.

**Root-cause confidence:** High — confirmed through the lifecycle call path, persisted SQLite state, transcript timestamps, API responses, a red-before-green regression, and the native Electron flow below.

## Actual Electron end-to-end evidence

The reproduction and verification used the real Electron checkout with isolated state under `~/.ao/dev`; neither screenshot comes from a mock or browser-only preview.

### Before

A fresh Chat Codex worker had already completed its turn and the conversation endpoint reported 18,213 tokens, while `/api/v1/usage/sessions/<id>` remained empty and the board card had no token badge. Converting that exact session to TUI exposed the same 18,213 tokens immediately without another model turn.

![Before the fix: the Chat cost check card has no token badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/e622b94379eb4e2c3625224ffd130bdeacb607ae/.pr-assets/chat-cost-observability/before.png)

### After

A new post-fix Codex worker remained in Chat mode with empty `runtime_launch_id` and `agent_session_id`. Its provider-conversation usage binding became active, `/api/v1/usage/sessions/<id>` returned 18,218 tokens, and the board rendered `18.2K tok` without any interface conversion.

![After the fix: the fresh Chat worker shows 18.2K tokens without switching to TUI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/e622b94379eb4e2c3625224ffd130bdeacb607ae/.pr-assets/chat-cost-observability/after.png)

The immutable evidence assets are stored at commit [`e622b943`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/e622b94379eb4e2c3625224ffd130bdeacb607ae).

title: fix(chat): support agent switching without a terminal runtime
body:
Addresses the remaining functional agent-switch gap in #4033 and follows the UI entry-point work in #4036.

## Summary

- make the switch-agent control available for real Chat sessions, which intentionally have no terminal handle
- add a Chat-specific durable handoff that replaces structured controllers without manufacturing a TUI runtime
- fence source/target ownership with controller generations, atomically activate the target, and preserve Chat mode with empty runtime metadata
- restore the source controller when target activation fails and reconcile every in-flight Chat switch state after daemon restart
- make the renderer fake model Chat sessions accurately and add unit, SQLite, and Playwright regression coverage

## Root cause

The UI-only follow-up in #4036 wrapped `TerminalSwitchAgentButton` in `session.terminalHandleId`. That condition can never be true for a correctly formed Chat session: Chat is driven by a structured provider controller and deliberately persists `terminalHandleId: null`.

The same hidden assumption existed in the backend. Agent-switch admission required a runtime handle for every mode, and the switch saga only knew how to destroy and replace a terminal runtime. The fake renderer bridge assigned terminal handles to Chat fixtures too, so tests modeled a state production never creates and masked both failures.

This change uses the durable Chat controller generation as the ownership fence, while retaining the existing runtime-launch fence for TUI sessions.

## Live Electron A/B evidence

Both captures use the actual AO Electron app and daemon with a live idle Chat worker. This is not the `dev:web` fake bridge.

| Build | Session mode | `terminalHandleId` | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Base `3f5ca81bf` | `chat` | `null` | switch control absent |
| Feature build | `chat` | `null` | control visible; dialog opens |

### Before — production-shaped Chat session has no switch control

![Before: idle Chat session without a switch-agent control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4096/.issue-assets/pr-4096/chat-agent-switch-before.png)

### After — the same session shape opens the switch dialog

![After: switch-agent dialog open in an idle Chat session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-4096/.issue-assets/pr-4096/chat-agent-switch-after.png)

The evidence images are hosted separately on `pr-assets-4096` and are intentionally excluded from this PR's source diff.

## Verification

Verified again after merging current `origin/main` (`3369f00c7`) into the branch:

- `cd backend && go test -p 4 ./...` — passed
- focused backend race suites for ACP, Codex, Chat service, session manager, and SQLite store — passed
- `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs` — 0 issues with an isolated cache

The backend regression matrix covers successful Chat-to-Chat ownership transfer, activation rollback, ambiguous commit resolution, all durable restart states, and the invariant that Chat never acquires terminal runtime metadata.

title: Disable DevTools on blank browser pages
body:
## What

- Disable the browser DevTools button until the active tab has loaded a page.
- Prevent shortcuts and menu actions from opening DevTools on a blank target.
- Automatically close DevTools when:
  - the active page is cleared;
  - the user switches to a blank tab.
- Preserve the existing docked-right behavior for loaded pages.

## Why

Blank browser targets use `about:blank` and their native page view is intentionally hidden so AO can display its empty-page UI.

Docked Chromium DevTools is attached to that hidden native view. As a result, DevTools was reported as open but remained invisible. Detached DevTools appeared because it used a separate window.

This change prevents the unsupported invisible state instead of unexpectedly changing the user's DevTools placement.

## How

- Added a main-process check for empty URLs and `about:blank`.
- Kept DevTools closed when an open request targets a blank page.
- Closed existing DevTools during page clearing or when activating a blank tab.
- Updated the browser toolbar to enable DevTools only when the active tab has a page. The close action remains available during in-flight state updates.
- Added regression coverage for blank targets, page clearing, blank-tab switching, and toolbar availability.

## Testing

title: fix(inspector): remember a session's inspector tab across session switches
body:
## What

Fixes the inspector rail's active tab (Summary/Browser/Files) resetting to Summary when switching back to a previously-visited session, discarding whatever tab the user had left it on.

## Why

Reported symptom: work on the Files (FILE DIFF) or Browser tab in one session, switch to another session, then switch back — the previous tab selection is gone and Summary shows instead. The right-panel state should persist per session across session switches.

Root cause: the session-entry effect in `SessionView.tsx` that defaults a **brand-new** session to the Summary tab (added in #3864) tracked only the single most-recently-initialized session id (`initializedInspectorSessionIdRef`, a plain `string | null` ref). Re-entering *any* session that wasn't the immediately preceding one looked identical to a first-ever visit, so the effect unconditionally forced it back to Summary via `setInspectorViewForSession(sessionId, "summary")` — even though that session's tab selection was already correctly persisted per-session in the ui-store (`inspectorSessions[sessionId].view`).

## How

Track every session id this view has ever initialized in a `Set<string>` instead of a single last-seen id, so the "default new sessions to Summary" effect only fires once per session's *lifetime*, not once per "was this the last session I looked at." This mirrors the existing `current?.browserContentRevealed === undefined` guard two lines below in the same effect, which already handled this correctly for that field.

No changes to the native browser-view (WebContentsView) visibility plumbing — investigated that path first (it's per-session and correctly scoped) before finding the actual bug was purely in this React-level tab-selection effect.

**Update from review (@neversettle17-101):** the component-local `Set` was itself recreated whenever `SessionView` unmounts (e.g. across a route transition), so re-mounting an already-visited session still looked like a first-ever visit. Moved the "initialized" marker into the ui-store's persisted `inspectorSessions[sessionId]` state via a new, idempotent `initializeInspectorSession(sessionId, hasBrowserContent, hasInspector)` action (no-ops once `initialized` is already true), so it survives unmount/remount, not just re-renders of one mounted instance. `hasInspector` is threaded through in addition to the reviewer's suggested signature so sessions without an inspector (orchestrators) still never gain a store entry, matching the prior behavior.

## Testing

All testing below was run locally in the worktree at `.claude/worktrees/fix-browser-view-session-switch-race` (branch `fix/inspector-tab-resets-on-session-revisit`).

- `remembers the tab a session was left on when returning to it after visiting another session` (`SessionView.test.tsx`) — opens Files on session A, switches to session B, switches back to A, asserts Files is still selected. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code (`data-view="summary"` instead of `"files"`) and passes after.
- `remembers the tab a session was left on after unmounting and remounting the view` (`SessionView.test.tsx`) — selects Files on session A, unmounts `SessionView`, remounts the same session, asserts Files is still selected. Added per review feedback; independently reverted just the source (keeping the test) to confirm it fails against the component-local-ref version (`data-view="summary"`) and passes against the store-backed version.
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/SessionView.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.test.tsx` — 185/185 pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` — clean.
- Full frontend suite: only pre-existing, unrelated failures (macOS-only path assertions running on Windows, landing-page/analytics tests, network-socket tests) — none touch the changed files.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene

- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (frontend)
