title: fix(ci): make gitleaks scans incremental
body:
## What

Replace the legacy gitleaks v1 wrapper with its same license-free, pinned gitleaks v7.4 container and an explicit commit list:

- pull requests scan only commits introduced by the PR;
- pushes to `main` scan only commits introduced by that push (`before..after`).

The repository's existing `.gitleaks.toml` rules and redacted output remain unchanged.

## Why

The legacy wrapper does two repository-wide things that make unrelated history break current work:

1. On pull requests it scans both sides of `base...HEAD`, so newer base-only commits can fail a queued or stale PR.
2. On every push to `main` it scans every fetched ref. Recent runs scanned roughly 8,100 commits, took about 6.5 minutes, and repeatedly failed on an old placeholder RSA header in commit `56f64bd` rather than the newly merged change.

That makes every subsequent merge inherit the same historical failure. Incremental ranges preserve secret detection for all new code without repeatedly rescanning unrelated history.

## Testing

- Reproduced the current gitleaks v7.4 failure directly against historical commit `56f64bd`.
- Replayed the previous `main` push range (`5240327..63b5ffb`): one new commit selected, no leaks found in 16 ms.
- Replayed a stale PR range: base-only commits excluded and all PR-side commits retained.
- `go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.7 .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml`
- The PR's own gitleaks workflow runs the new container path.

title: Design for the kanban columns and display status
Implement sorting sessions into Kanban Columns
body:
# Kanban Column Derivation

## Goal

Derive a stable Kanban placement for every worker session from durable facts. The column answers where the session is in its delivery lifecycle and who owns the next step. It is independent from the existing display `SessionStatus`.

```text
Building -> Validating -> Needs Review -> Ready
                                     \
                                      Archive (terminated only)
```

## Scope

This issue adds only the derived Kanban column and board grouping. It does not redesign display statuses, pills, or card content.

Review-run CDC is assumed to be available. It causes the normal workspace refresh; the backend recomputes the column from durable facts on every session-list read.

## Current Implementation

Today:
1. Backend derives one `SessionStatus`.
2. Frontend `attentionZone()` maps that status to the current `working`, `action`, `pending`, and `merge` board lanes.
3. The board separately archives terminated sessions.

The new column must be backend-derived rather than added to the frontend mapping: review-run state, PR-head freshness, and review ownership are durable-fact rules, not UI rules.

## Proposed Contract

Add a derived `kanbanColumn` to each session response:

```text
building | validating | needs_review | ready | archive
```

Do not persist this value. Derive it during `GET /sessions`, alongside the existing derived status.

## Inputs

Build a narrow internal read model from:
- Session facts: worker kind, termination, auto-review and auto-inject settings.
- PR facts: lifecycle, draft/open/merged/closed, current `headSHA`, CI, approvals, and mergeability.
- AO review-run facts: PR URL, target SHA, status, verdict, and GitHub review ID.
- Source-aware SCM review facts: external/human approvals and requested changes, separate from AO-authored reviews/comments.

A review run is current only when `reviewRun.targetSHA == pr.headSHA`.

AO-authored provider reviews must be identified through `reviewRun.githubReviewID`. Do not use aggregate `PRFacts.Review` alone to choose between Validating and Needs Review, because it combines AO and external review signals.

## Column Derivation

First, derive a placement for each PR:

```text
session terminated?
  yes -> Archive

no PR exists?
  yes -> Building

PR is draft?
  yes -> Validating

PR is merged or closed without merge?
  yes -> Ready

PR is approved or mergeable?
  yes -> Ready

AO-owned review/fix/test loop active?
  yes -> Validating

auto review enabled?
  yes -> Validating

otherwise -> Needs Review
```

An AO-owned loop includes current-head AO review work, AO CI fixing, and AO addressing AO-originated review feedback.

Once a PR is in the review lifecycle, worker activity must not move it back to Building. A new head SHA is a new validation cycle:
- Auto review on: Validating.
- Auto review off: Needs Review.

## Multiple PRs

Derive placement per PR, then select the session’s representative PR.

1. Exclude merged and closed PRs while at least one live PR exists.
2. Among live PRs, choose the highest-priority actionable placement:
   1. Ready (mergeable/approved)
   2. Needs Review
   3. Validating
   4. Building
3. Use merged/closed states only when no live PR remains.
4. Add a deterministic tie-breaker, initially latest PR update time.

This ensures a terminal PR does not hide a live PR that needs validation or human review.

## Implementation Steps

1. Define the backend `KanbanColumn` enum and add derived `kanbanColumn` to the session API DTO/OpenAPI contract.
2. Add a pure `deriveKanbanColumn(facts)` reducer next to, but separate from, existing `deriveStatus`.
3. Build the reducer input from session, PR, review-run, and source-aware SCM review facts.
4. Add/read the required review data in the session-list path with bounded queries; do not issue per-card unbounded lookups.
5. Generate API types after changing the DTO.
6. Change `SessionsBoard` to group active workers by `session.kanbanColumn`.
7. Render `archive` through the existing archive section.
8. Leave existing display-status labels and card detail untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every worker session returns one derived `kanbanColumn`.
- Terminated sessions always derive to `archive`.
- No-PR worker sessions derive to `building`.
- Draft and current-head AO validation work derive to `validating`.
- Auto-review-off review-ready PRs derive to `needs_review`.
- Approved/mergeable PRs derive to `ready`.
- A stale review run for an old SHA cannot determine the current column.
- AO and external review signals lead to the appropriate ownership column.
- Multiple PRs select the highest-priority actionable live PR, with deterministic ties.
- A review-run CDC update reaches the existing workspace refresh path and the refreshed session returns its newly derived column.
- Unit, service/API, and board-grouping tests cover the rules above.

title: Implement deriving display status for each agent session
body:
# AO Kanban Status Derivation

This document describes how AO should derive the Kanban presentation for a session from durable facts. The board should stay lifecycle-oriented and mostly unidirectional, while the display status explains what is happening right now.

The proposed active board has four columns:

```text
Building -> Validating -> Needs Review -> Ready
```

Terminated sessions should move out of the active board into a separate archive section.

## Implementation Model

Derive Kanban presentation in two stages:

1. **Derive the Kanban column** from stable lifecycle and ownership facts: session termination, PR existence, PR state, whether auto review is on, whether an internal review/fix/test loop is already active, and whether the PR is approved, mergeable, or finished.
2. **Derive the display status** from the most important current fact inside that column: worker activity, hook freshness, CI, changes requested, review runs, review verdicts, approvals, mergeability, and terminal PR state.

This keeps the column stable and user-facing, while allowing the display status to carry detailed state.

| Stage | Answers | Main inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column derivation | Where is this session in the lifecycle, and who owns the next step? | Session termination, PR existence, PR state, auto-review setting, active internal review/fix/test loop, human approval, mergeability | `Building`, `Validating`, `Needs Review`, `Ready`, or archive section |
| Display status derivation | What is happening or needed right now? | Worker activity, hook freshness, CI status, changes requested, review run status, review verdict, human approval, mergeability | `Working`, `Blocked`, `Reviewing`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Needs human review`, `Mergeable`, etc. |

## Kanban Columns

| Column | Meaning | Typical display statuses |
|---|---|---|
| Building | AO/agent is creating the change before a PR exists. | `Working`, `Awaiting PR`, `Blocked`, `No signal`, `Exited` |
| Validating | AO is checking, reviewing, testing, or iterating on the PR. This column should be driven by PR existence and AO-owned facts: draft PRs, AO review runs, AO reviewer comments/verdicts, CI fixing, and future AO testing/artifact validation. | `Draft`, `Review scheduled`, `Reviewing`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Checks failing`, `Addressing comments`, `Blocked`, `Exited`, `Review pending`, `Needs review` |
| Needs Review | The PR is review-ready, but AO is not currently responsible for the internal review/fix loop. This column should be driven by current human/external SCM review facts, such as external comments, external requested changes, or missing human approval. | `Needs human review`, `Needs review`, `CI failing`, `Changes requested`, `Commented`, `Addressing comments` |
| Ready | The PR is approved, mergeable, merged, or closed without merge. | `Approved`, `Mergeable`, `Checks failing`, `Merged`, `Closed without merge` |

## Column Derivation Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Fetch durable facts] --> S[Session facts]
    A --> P[PR facts]
    A --> RS[Review session facts]
    A --> RR[Review run facts]

    S --> D[Derive Kanban column]
    P --> D
    RS --> D
    RR --> D

    D --> T0{Session terminated?}
    T0 -->|yes| AR[Archive section]

    T0 -->|no| PR0{Does PR exist?}
    PR0 -->|no| B[Building]

    PR0 -->|yes| PRS0{PR state}
    PRS0 -->|draft| V
    PRS0 -->|merged| RD[Ready]
    PRS0 -->|closed without merge| RD

    PRS0 -->|open| READY0{Approved or mergeable?}
    READY0 -->|yes| RD

    READY0 -->|no| LOOP0{Internal review/fix/test loop active?}
    LOOP0 -->|yes| V[Validating]

    LOOP0 -->|no| AUTO0{Auto review on?}
    AUTO0 -->|yes| V
    AUTO0 -->|no| NR[Needs Review]
```

## Display Status Derivation

After the column is selected, derive the display status with a priority list for that column.

### Building

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[Building column] --> W0{Worker activity}
    W0 -->|active| W[Working]
    W0 -->|waiting_input or blocked| BL[Blocked]
    W0 -->|exited| EX[Exited]
    W0 -->|idle| H0{Hook signal missing past grace?}
    H0 -->|yes| NS[No signal]
    H0 -->|no| AP[Awaiting PR]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worker activity is `active` | `Working` |
| 2 | Worker activity is `waiting_input` or `blocked` | `Blocked` |
| 3 | Worker activity is `exited` | `Exited` |
| 4 | Worker is hook-capable and hook signal is missing past grace | `No signal` |
| 5 | No PR exists and worker is idle | `Awaiting PR` |

### Validating

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    V[Validating column] --> W0{Worker activity requires attention?}
    W0 -->|waiting_input or blocked| BL[Blocked]
    W0 -->|exited| EX[Exited]

    W0 -->|no| CI0{Current CI failing for PR head SHA?}
    CI0 -->|yes| ACI0{Auto CI injection on?}
    ACI0 -->|yes| FCI[Fixing CI failures]
    ACI0 -->|no| CIF[Checks failing]

    CI0 -->|no| CH0{Current unresolved AO review changes requested?}
    CH0 -->|yes| AR0{Auto review/fix on?}
    AR0 -->|yes| FCH[Addressing comments]
    AR0 -->|no| IRN[Needs review]

    CH0 -->|no| REV0{Current review run exists for PR head SHA?}
    REV0 -->|no + auto review on| RS[Review scheduled]
    REV0 -->|yes| RUN0{Review run status}

    RUN0 -->|queued or running| RV[Reviewing]
    RUN0 -->|failed| NR[Needs review]
    RUN0 -->|cancelled| RP[Review pending]
    RUN0 -->|completed changes_requested and auto-fix on| FCH2[Addressing comments]
    RUN0 -->|completed approved| DONE[Column should become Needs Review or Ready]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worker activity is `waiting_input` or `blocked` while AO owns the loop | `Blocked` |
| 2 | Worker activity is `exited` while AO owns the loop | `Exited` |
| 3 | CI is failing for the current PR head SHA and auto CI injection is on | `Fixing CI failures` |
| 4 | CI is failing for the current PR head SHA and auto CI injection is off | `Checks failing` |
| 5 | Current unresolved AO review changes are requested and auto review/fix is on | `Addressing comments` |
| 6 | Current unresolved AO review changes are requested and auto review/fix is off | `Needs review` |
| 7 | No review run exists for latest PR head SHA and auto review is on | `Review scheduled` |
| 8 | Current review run is queued or running | `Reviewing` |
| 9 | Current review run failed | `Needs review` |
| 10 | Current review run was cancelled | `Review pending` |

### Needs Review

Needs Review is entered only after AO/internal review is approved, not required, or intentionally skipped because auto review is off. Once a card is in this column, display status should be derived only from current CI state and human/external SCM review signals.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    N[Needs Review column] --> CI0{Current CI failing for PR head SHA?}
    CI0 -->|yes| CIF[CI failing]

    CI0 -->|no| EXT0{Current unresolved external review input?}
    EXT0 -->|no| NHR[Needs human review]

    EXT0 -->|yes| AUTO0{Auto-inject review comments on?}
    AUTO0 -->|yes| AC[Addressing comments]

    AUTO0 -->|no| TYPE0{External input type}
    TYPE0 -->|changes requested| CR[Changes requested]
    TYPE0 -->|comment only| COM[Commented]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CI is failing for the current PR head SHA | `CI failing` |
| 2 | Current unresolved external changes are requested and auto-inject review comments is on | `Addressing comments` |
| 3 | Current unresolved external comments exist and auto-inject review comments is on | `Addressing comments` |
| 4 | Current unresolved external changes are requested and auto-inject review comments is off | `Changes requested` |
| 5 | Current unresolved external comments exist and auto-inject review comments is off | `Commented` |
| 6 | No current unresolved external comments or changes are present | `Needs human review` |

### Needs Review Implementation Plan

1. Enter Needs Review only after column derivation has decided that AO/internal review is approved, not required, or intentionally skipped because auto review is off.
2. Do not re-check AO review existence or AO review verdict inside the Needs Review display-status resolver.
3. Fetch only current human/external SCM review signals for the selected PR head SHA.
4. Ignore resolved, outdated, or non-current review threads/comments.
5. Exclude AO-authored reviewer comments and AO review-run output from external review signals.
6. If CI is failing for the current PR head SHA, show `CI failing`.
7. If current unresolved external input exists and auto-inject review comments is on, show `Addressing comments`.
8. If auto-inject review comments is off, distinguish the external input type:
   - external changes requested wins over external comments and shows `Changes requested`;
   - external comments without requested changes show `Commented`.
9. If there is no current unresolved external input, show `Needs human review`.

### Ready

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Ready column] --> M0{PR merged?}
    M0 -->|yes| M[Merged]

    M0 -->|no| CL0{PR closed without merge?}
    CL0 -->|yes| CL[Closed without merge]

    CL0 -->|no| MG0{PR mergeable?}
    MG0 -->|yes| MG[Mergeable]
    MG0 -->|no| CI0{Checks failing?}
    CI0 -->|yes| CIF[Checks failing]
    CI0 -->|no| AP[Approved]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PR is mergeable | `Mergeable` |
| 2 | PR has required approvals but checks are failing | `Checks failing` |
| 3 | PR has required approvals but is not mergeable yet | `Approved` |
| 4 | PR is merged | `Merged` |
| 5 | PR is closed without merge | `Closed without merge` |

### Archive Section

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Archive section] --> T0{Session terminated?}
    T0 -->|yes| T[Terminated]
```

| Priority | Condition | Display status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Session is terminated | `Terminated` |

## State To Kanban Mapping

| Derived status | Kanban column | Display status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `awaiting_pr` | Building | `Awaiting PR` | Worker is not actively changing code and no PR exists yet. |
| `working` | Building | `Working` | Worker is actively changing code before the PR/review lifecycle starts. |
| `worker_blocked` | Building | `Blocked` | Worker is waiting for input or blocked before a review-ready PR exists. |
| `no_signal` | Building | `No signal` | Hook-capable worker has not reported activity after the grace period. |
| `exited` | Building | `Exited` | Worker process exited or is unavailable before AO owns a PR validation loop. |
| `draft` | Validating | `Draft` | PR exists but is still draft, so AO can complete internal validation before human/external review. |
| `fixing_ci` | Validating | `Fixing CI failures` | CI failed on the current PR head SHA and AO is fixing it. |
| `checks_failing` | Validating | `Checks failing` | CI failed on the current PR head SHA and auto CI injection is off, so surface the failing checks. |
| `fixing_changes` | Validating | `Addressing comments` | AO review comments or AO requested changes exist and AO is fixing them. |
| `needs_review` | Validating | `Needs review` | AO review or validation needs attention while the card is still in the internal validation loop. |
| `review_scheduled` | Validating | `Review scheduled` | Auto review is enabled and latest PR SHA has no current review run yet. |
| `reviewing` | Validating | `Reviewing` | Current AO review run is queued or running. |
| `review_failed` | Validating | `Needs review` | Current AO review run failed while AO owns the validation loop. |
| `review_pending` | Validating | `Review pending` | Review run was cancelled; the PR head still needs an AO review decision. |
| `blocked` | Validating | `Blocked` | AO owns the validation/fix loop, but the worker is blocked or waiting for input. |
| `exited` | Validating | `Exited` | AO owns the validation/fix loop, but the worker exited. |
| `ci_failed` | Needs Review | `CI failing` | CI failed and AO is not automatically fixing it, so a human/external decision is needed. |
| `changes_requested` | Needs Review | `Changes requested` | Human/external SCM reviewer requested changes. |
| `commented` | Needs Review | `Commented` | Human/external SCM reviewer commented without requesting changes. |
| `needs_human_review` | Needs Review | `Needs human review` | AO review is done, unavailable, or intentionally skipped because auto review is off. |
| `approved` | Ready | `Approved` | Required approvals exist, but PR is not mergeable yet. |
| `mergeable` | Ready | `Mergeable` | PR is approved and SCM says it can merge. |
| `checks_failing` | Ready | `Checks failing` | PR has required approvals, but checks are failing and blocking mergeability. |
| `merged` | Ready | `Merged` | PR has merged. |
| `closed_without_merge` | Ready | `Closed without merge` | PR closed without merge; the session stays visible as a final PR outcome. |
| `terminated` | Archive section | `Terminated` | Session is terminal and should be shown outside the main active board. |

## Multiple PRs Per Session

When a session has multiple PRs, derive the state for each PR independently and then pick the PR/status that best answers:

> What should the user care about next for this session?

This means actionable or landable PRs should outrank terminal PRs. A merged or closed-without-merge PR does not require user action, so it should not hide another PR that is still in validation or needs review.

For this ranking, keep review sources separate:

- **AO/internal review facts** come from AO review runs and AO-authored reviewer comments/verdicts. These can place the card in Validating.
- **Human/external review facts** come from SCM review state and non-AO reviewers. These can place the card in Needs Review.

### Selection Rule

1. Derive each PR's column and display status using the two-stage model.
2. Assign each derived PR state a priority score.
3. Pick the highest-priority actionable state for the session card.
4. Use the selected PR's column and display status as the session's Kanban presentation.
5. If only terminal PR states exist, show the best terminal state in Ready.
6. If no PR exists, fall back to session/worker facts and show Building.

### Priority Order

| Priority | Derived state | Column | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mergeable` | Ready | User can merge now. This is the highest-signal landing state. |
| 2 | `approved` | Ready | PR is close to landing, but may still need final checks or mergeability resolution. |
| 3 | `checks_failing` | Ready | PR is approved but checks are failing, so it is close to merge but still blocked. |
| 4 | `ci_failed` | Needs Review | CI failed for the current PR head SHA. |
| 5 | `changes_requested` | Needs Review | Human/external SCM reviewer requested changes. |
| 6 | `commented` | Needs Review | Human/external SCM reviewer commented without requesting changes. |
| 7 | `needs_human_review` | Needs Review | Human/external review is the next step. |
| 8 | `blocked` | Validating | AO owns the validation loop, but the worker is blocked. |
| 9 | `fixing_ci` | Validating | AO is actively fixing CI. |
| 10 | `checks_failing` | Validating | CI is failing while the card is in Validating, but auto CI injection is off. |
| 11 | `fixing_changes` | Validating | AO is actively fixing AO review comments or AO requested changes. |
| 12 | `needs_review` | Validating | AO review requested changes or validation needs attention. |
| 13 | `review_failed` | Validating | AO review automation failed and needs attention. |
| 14 | `reviewing` | Validating | AO/reviewer is currently processing. |
| 15 | `review_scheduled` | Validating | Auto review is expected for the latest PR head SHA. |
| 16 | `review_pending` | Validating | Review was cancelled or still needs an AO review decision. |
| 17 | `draft` | Validating | PR exists as a draft and is still in AO validation. |
| 18 | `working` | Building | Worker is actively building before review. |
| 19 | `worker_blocked` | Building | Worker is blocked before the review lifecycle. |
| 20 | `exited` | Building | Worker exited before the review lifecycle. |
| 21 | `no_signal` | Building | Worker signal is missing before the review lifecycle. |
| 22 | `awaiting_pr` | Building | No PR exists yet. |
| 23 | `merged` | Ready | Terminal PR state with no user action required. |
| 24 | `closed_without_merge` | Ready | Terminal PR state with no user action required. |
| 25 | `terminated` | Archive section | Terminal session state. |

### Examples

| Session facts | Selected presentation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| PR #10 is `merged`, PR #11 is `changes_requested` | Needs Review / `Changes requested` | The merged PR is terminal; the changes-requested PR still needs action. |
| PR #10 is `closed_without_merge`, PR #11 is `reviewing` | Validating / `Reviewing` | The closed PR is terminal; active AO validation work is more relevant. |
| PR #10 is `mergeable`, PR #11 is `fixing_changes` | Ready / `Mergeable` | Mergeable is immediately landable, so it wins. |
| PR #10 is `approved`, PR #11 is `review_failed` | Ready / `Approved` | Approved is closer to landing. |
| PR #10 is `merged`, PR #11 is `closed_without_merge` | Ready / `Merged` | Only terminal PRs remain, so show the best terminal outcome. |

## Notes

| Note | Detail |
|---|---|
| Column meaning | Columns represent lifecycle phase and next-action ownership, not literal agent activity. |
| Unidirectional flow | The intended movement is `Building -> Validating -> Needs Review -> Ready`. A card should not bounce back to Building just because AO is fixing review comments or CI. |
| Validating scope | Validating is the AO-owned loop: AO review, CI fixing, review-comment fixing, and future testing/artifact validation. |
| Needs Review scope | Needs Review is the human/external-review stage. For an open, review-ready PR that is not approved or mergeable, if auto review is off and no internal loop is active, the default column is Needs Review. |
| Building width | If Building has more than 5-10 visible sessions and users must scroll heavily, widen Building because many sessions naturally accumulate there. |
| Stale facts after new comments | Stale or newly-arrived facts are handled by deriving status from the current PR head SHA and current unresolved review/CI facts. For example, if CI fails while review comments are being addressed and AO owns the fix, the card stays in Validating with display status `Fixing CI failures`. |
| External comment currentness | Needs Review should only consider unresolved comments or current review threads. Resolved, outdated, or non-current external comments should not keep the card in `Commented` or `Changes requested`. |
| Review fact currentness | Review facts should be tied to the current PR head SHA or SCM's current review decision. Stale approvals, comments, or requested changes from older commits should not control the current display status. |
| External review priority | For external SCM input, `Changes requested` should win over `Commented`, and both should win over generic `Needs human review`. |
| Auto review off | If auto review is off, AO should not force adversarial review. A review-ready PR can go directly to Needs Review with display status `Needs human review`, unless it is already approved or mergeable. |
| Draft PR when auto review is on | Once the Building stage is done, or whenever a PR is raised for a session with auto review on, the PR should be opened as a draft so AO can complete internal validation before human/external review. |
| Archive section | Terminated sessions should move out of the main four-column board into a separate archive section. |

## Open Questions

| Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|

title: feat(observability): Sentry-ready error capture + triage classification (renderer)
body:
First, shippable slice of the Sentry error-handling work. **Dormant until a DSN exists**, so it can merge now and go live the moment the Sentry account is ready — no code change at ship time beyond adding the dep + setting the DSN.

## What this adds
- **`shared/observability.ts`** — pure `classifyError()` turning any failure into triage tiers: **severity** (P0 fatal → P3 expected) and **fault owner** (`ours` / `user` / `external` / `environment`), on top of the existing `category`/`code`. Additive: unknown errors fall back to a safe `P2/ours`, never unlabelled. Fully unit-tested (14 cases).
- **`renderer/lib/sentry.ts`** — a Sentry sink fed from the two **existing** telemetry seams, so there is one capture path, not two. No-op unless: (1) telemetry consent is granted (same gate as PostHog), and (2) `VITE_AO_SENTRY_DSN` is set. Scrubs local URLs/paths from messages/stacks; attaches only safe enum/id tags (`platform, surface, domain, operation, category, code, http_status, severity, owner`).
- **Wiring** — `captureRendererException` (render crashes / unhandled) and `reportApiError` (every classified daemon API failure) now also mirror into Sentry.

## Why no `@sentry/electron` dependency yet
The SDK is loaded lazily only when a DSN is present, so this **builds and tests green with no new dependency today** and doesn't touch the lockfile.

## Ship steps (when the DSN email arrives)
1. `npm i @sentry/electron` (convert the lazy import in `sentry.ts` to a static import — one line).
2. Set `VITE_AO_SENTRY_DSN` (renderer) / `AO_SENTRY_DSN` (main).
3. Verify with a forced error (daemon has a `/panic` route).

## Scope / follow-ups (separate PRs)
- Main-process init: native crashes + autoUpdater errors.
- Mobile: `@sentry/react-native` (Expo).
- Daemon: `sentry-go` + request-id correlation so a client error links to its server cause.

## Verification
- Classification: 14/14 unit tests.
- Existing telemetry + api-client suites: 86/86 across touched files, unaffected.
- Typecheck: clean for all touched files.

Plan + full error taxonomy: see `plan.md` / `error-catalog.md`.

title: fix(chat): fail fast on immutable history replay
body:
## What

- add an optional `ChatHistoryRefresher` port for history sources that can make a new authoritative provider observation
- read every native history source once, then retry only through that explicit refresh operation
- keep ACP `session/load` replay snapshot-only so an incomplete replay fails immediately instead of polling the same cache for 45 seconds
- make Codex refreshable through its real `thread/read`, preserving bounded convergence where it can actually make progress

## Why

Fixes #4123.

ACP captures replay once during `Resume`; every later `ReadHistory` returns the same frozen events. The generic settle loop nevertheless reread that cache every 100ms for up to 45 seconds when it was unsettled or missed AO's checkpoint. That delayed a guaranteed handoff failure and rollback without observing any new provider fact.

## How

This follows ACP v1's actual boundary: [`session/load` is a finite replay whose response follows the replayed entries](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol/blob/main/docs/protocol/v1/session-setup.mdx), not a standardized repeatable history read.

- `ChatHistoryReader` represents one authoritative history observation.
- `ChatHistoryRefresher` promises that `RefreshHistory` performs provider I/O or waits for a real provider signal.
- `Controller.importNativeHistory` keeps its bounded timeout around the initial read and refresh loop, but immediately returns `ErrChatHistoryUnsettled` when an incomplete source cannot refresh.
- Codex implements refresh by issuing another `thread/read(includeTurns: true)`.
- ACP deliberately does not implement refresh; the PR never reissues `session/load`, adds a grace sleep, or infers provider state from a load response.

Intentional omissions: this focused fix does not change trailing-user-only turn classification, introduce load-versus-resume intent, or adopt draft ACP v2 lifecycle/replay types. Those require separate state/evidence contracts and should not be coupled to #4123.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver -count=1`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/ports ./internal/service/chat ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver -count=1`
- `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE=/tmp/ao-lint-cache-4123-fresh npm run lint` — full backend tests and golangci-lint, 0 issues

Regression coverage verifies:

- an immutable unsettled replay is read exactly once and fails immediately
- an immutable settled replay behind AO's checkpoint is read exactly once and fails immediately
- a refreshable unsettled source converges through one initial read plus one refresh
- a refreshable settled-but-stale source refreshes until it reaches AO's checkpoint
- cancellation before refresh preserves the typed unsettled error and context cause
- Codex refresh performs a second wire `thread/read`
- ACP conversations do not advertise refreshability

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for the changed boundary and user-visible failure behavior
- [x] Relevant build, race, test, and lint checks pass

title: bug(daemon): reaper WARN-spam on handle-less sessions floods the 'not ready' details buffer; boot stuck un-ready 10+ min on ~11 sessions (post-#4071)
body:
## Summary

Post-[#4071](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4071) build (verified: banner shows the new copy "AO daemon is still starting. Session recovery can take a while." and the details view keeps updating instead of freezing — both #4071 behaviors). Reporter's daemon stayed un-ready for **10+ minutes** on ~11 sessions (macOS, nightly), and the "not ready" details panel shows **only** reaper WARN spam — no boot-progress landmarks — because the reaper warns every 5s forever on permanently-unprobeable sessions and floods the supervisor's 12k stderr capture buffer.

Two distinct problems in one report:

1. **Reaper warn-spam on handle-less sessions floods the startup details buffer** (High confidence, traced).
2. **Daemon un-ready 10+ min for ~11 sessions on macOS nightly** — #4071's in-place relaunch should be far faster; unclear whether Reconcile is slow or hung (Medium confidence — evidence likely evicted from the buffer by problem 1; needs full stderr).

## Source

**Reported by:** Rishet11 in Discord `#bug-triage` (thread "Wasnt this issue already resolved?"), 2026-08-20 20:36–20:46 IST
**Machine:** macOS (reporter is a mac + nightly user); AO version TBD (asked)
**Analyzed against:** `e9918fc3a` (origin/main, 2026-08-20)
**Confidence:** High (problem 1) / Medium (problem 2)

## Observed

Banner: `AO daemon is not ready yet / AO daemon is still starting. Session recovery can take a while.` Screenshot + two details dumps spanning 20:36:25→20:46:20 IST (one continuous boot — reaper warns present from the first captured line).

The entire visible details buffer is:

```
level=WARN msg="reaper: session has no runtime handle metadata, skipping" session=agent-orchestrator-10   (every 5s)
level=WARN msg="reaper: session has no runtime handle metadata, skipping" session=agent-orchestrator-11   (every 5s)
level=DEBUG msg="scm observer: project has no supported SCM origins" project=aohack                        (every 30s)
```

No `browser runtime: listening`, no `supervisor: listening`, no `daemon listening` — i.e. no evidence the HTTP bind ever landed within the captured window. Reporter: "this is just growing."

## Root cause (problem 1 — traced)

- `backend/internal/observe/reaper/reaper.go:209` (`probeOne`): a non-terminated, non-chat session with empty `Metadata.RuntimeHandleID` logs `WARN "reaper: session has no runtime handle metadata, skipping"` **on every 5s probe pass, forever** — no dedupe, no backoff, no once-per-session suppression. The reaper starts before `sessMgr.Reconcile` (`backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:182` vs `:346`) and runs for the daemon's lifetime, so the spam spans the whole boot window and continues after readiness.
- Handle-less **non-terminated** sessions are a real state: `preserveFailedSpawnWorkspace` (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:1072-1076`) records the workspace path but clears `RuntimeHandleID`/`RuntimeLaunchID` when a runtime was destroyed during spawn rollback, and not every caller of it terminates the row (`rollbackPreparedSpawnWorkspace`, manager.go:1040-1053, parks the workspace without terminating — callers decide).
- Such TUI sessions are **permanently unrestoreable** — `resume` rejects empty `RuntimeHandleID` with `ErrIncompleteHandle` (manager.go:~1615) — and `reconcileLive` for them falls through to `saveAndTeardownOne` (manager.go:1944-1971), which should terminate them on the next boot. The fact that -10/-11 are still warning at 20:46 means the live pass hasn't completed for them (stuck/slow on an earlier session, or erroring — `reconcile: live pass failed` is logged at ERROR but would also be evicted from the buffer, see below).
- **Buffer flood:** the supervisor captures daemon stderr into a 12k-char `daemonOutput` ring (PR #2972) surfaced by the banner; #4071 keeps it fresh. The warn pair is ~280 bytes per 5s ≈ **3.4 KB/min**, so ~3.5 minutes of spam completely fills the ring — every real boot/restore/reconcile line (including any ERROR explaining a hang) is evicted. The user sees a "growing" log with zero progress signal, which reads as "stuck doing nothing."

## Reproduction (from report)

1. macOS, nightly desktop build (post-Aug-17), ≥1 project with sessions including at least one handle-less non-terminated session (failed spawn with preserved workspace).
2. Launch the desktop app; banner appears at 30s and persists.
3. Open details: only repeating reaper WARN lines for the same session IDs; buffer keeps growing.

## Fix direction

- Dedupe the no-handle warn: warn **once per session per daemon run** (or demote to Debug after first occurrence, matching the Chat-mode skip which is silent by design). The condition is durable, not transient — repeating it every pass adds no information.
- Consider excluding permanently-unprobeable sessions from the probe list, or reconciling them to a terminal state at boot so they leave the running set.
- Defense-in-depth in the supervisor capture: rate-limit identical consecutive lines, or reserve part of the 12k ring for non-repeating lines, so one noisy logger can't evict boot landmarks and errors from the user-visible buffer.

## Data needed from reporter

- [ ] AO version (About dialog / nightly date)
- [ ] Does the board eventually load if the app is left open? If yes after how long?
- [ ] `cat ~/.ao/running.json` once the banner has been up >10 min (bind landed or not)
- [ ] Session/worktree count: `ls ~/.ao/data/worktrees/<project>/ | wc -l`
- [ ] Full daemon stderr: quit the app, run the bundled daemon binary directly in Terminal (`"/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao" daemon`), watch for `daemon listening` and any `reconcile:` ERROR lines

## Impact

- Startup diagnostics are destroyed exactly when they matter most (slow/stuck boot): the banner shows noise instead of the actual failure reason.
- Persistent log noise for the daemon's lifetime (continues after readiness) for any user with a handle-less session in the running set.
- Reporters of genuinely-hung boots (like this one) can't self-serve the real cause, and maintainers get flood instead of evidence.

## Related

- [#4064](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4064) — original 30s vs O(N) restore issue (CLOSED)
- [PR #4071](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4071) — the fix this build includes (merged 2026-08-17)
- [#2972](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2972) — introduced the 12k `daemonOutput` capture surfaced in the banner

**Priority:** medium — no data loss, but it breaks diagnosability of every slow boot and spams stderr forever.

title: feat: automate agent catalog refresh
body:
## Summary

Remove manual agent and model catalog refresh controls and move catalog freshness behind the existing cache-first daemon boundary.

The resulting read path is:

`UI → TanStack Query cache → daemon API → SQLite cache → local CLI discovery only when refresh/revalidation is due`

## What changed

### Persist the agent installation inventory

- Add a singleton `agent_inventory_cache` SQLite table containing the last successfully observed installed/authorized snapshot and its observation timestamp.
- Hydrate the daemon's in-memory inventory from SQLite on the first read after startup, without running agent CLI probes.
- Reconcile persisted IDs against the adapters supported by the current daemon build so removed adapters are not shown and current labels win over stale cached labels.
- Persist the next snapshot after a successful bounded inventory probe.
- Keep installation and authorization state advisory: session spawn remains the authoritative runtime validation boundary.

### Trigger refresh automatically

- Keep the existing daemon startup refresh so installations are reconciled in the background whenever the daemon boots.
- Refresh the inventory through `refreshAgentsIfStale()` when Project Settings opens, then update the TanStack Query cache with the result.
- Preserve the existing create-project stale refresh behavior already present on `main`.
- Continue rate-limiting and serializing inventory probes so multiple UI reads cannot stampede local agent CLIs.

### Make model revalidation actually refresh

- Continue serving cached model catalogs immediately.
- When the trust window expires, let the frontend revalidate in the background.
- Fix `RevalidateModels` so it performs discovery even when the binary/config fingerprint has not changed. This covers provider-side catalog drift that a local fingerprint cannot detect.
- Preserve stale/fallback catalog behavior and warnings when rediscovery fails.

### Remove manual catalog controls

- Remove the Project Settings “Refresh agents” row.
- Remove worker and orchestrator model refresh buttons.
- Remove the optional model-menu rediscovery action and now-unused product UI refresh props.
- Keep explicit daemon refresh endpoints/helpers for background refresh and older-client compatibility; only the manual UI controls are removed.
- Leave unrelated reload/update controls (browser reload, application update checks, retry actions) unchanged.

## Why

Catalog refresh is application bookkeeping, not a decision users should need to make. Persisting the last known inventory makes the UI useful immediately after restart, TanStack Query avoids repeated renderer fetches, and background daemon probing repairs stale installation data without blocking normal reads.

This also avoids repeatedly invoking agent CLIs during routine navigation while still converging after installs, removals, daemon restarts, or aged model catalogs.

## Failure behavior

- A missing, corrupt, or temporarily unreadable inventory snapshot falls back to the daemon's supported catalog and can be repaired by the background startup refresh.
- A failed live agent probe does not erase supported adapters; the next automatic trigger can retry.
- A failed inventory-cache write does not publish or rate-limit the probed snapshot, so the next refresh retries persistence instead of reporting a false success.
- A failed model rediscovery retains the fuller cached catalog when available and surfaces its warning.
- Spawn remains authoritative if cached installation/auth data has become stale.

## Verification

- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build go test ./internal/service/agent ./internal/storage/sqlite`
- `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/go-build go test ./internal/daemon`
- `npm run sqlc`
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck`
- Focused renderer tests: 44 passed
- `npm --prefix packages/product-ui run typecheck`
- Product UI tests: 61 passed

## Notes

- No API contract shape changed, so OpenAPI regeneration is not required.
- Migration `0104_agent_inventory_cache.sql` uses the next available migration number after merging the latest `main`.

title: fix(updater): check disk space before update and surface failed installs (#3528)
body:
## What

When the disk is nearly full, the updater now checks free space before downloading and before installing, and reports install failures that happened after the app quit, which previously were invisible to the user.

## Why

Fixes #3528. Squirrel.Mac extracts the update into temporary folders and stages a backup of the app, needing about 1.5 GB. With no room, the extraction truncates and the install fails after the app has quit, so nothing in the app ever surfaces it. The user just sees the "Restart to update" row again with no explanation, and retries keep failing.

## How

- Before an automatic or manual download, the updater checks free space on the cache volume against a 250 MB reserve. Below that, the download is skipped with an actionable "free up space" message instead of truncating mid-way.
- Before quitAndInstall, free space is checked on the app volume and the cache volume against a 1.5 GB reserve. Below that, a dialog says how much space to free instead of handing the update to a doomed post-quit install.
- quitAndInstall now writes a small install-attempt marker first. On the next launch, if the attempted version never became the running version, the app shows "The last update didn't install" together with the tail of the Squirrel ShipIt stderr log (this is where the misleading "file ... doesn't exist" error appears).
- The telemetry phase set now includes "install", so install failures are measurable instead of being a blind spot (it was previously only check|download). See shared/update-telemetry.ts.
- Every check fails open: if statfs reports nothing, the update proceeds exactly as it did before.

## Testing

- 80 vitest tests pass across the updater suites: auto-updater, update-disk-space, update-settings, update-telemetry.
- New tests cover the blocked-install dialog and telemetry, the fail-open path, install-attempt marker persistence, and the launch-time failure report with the ShipIt log tail.
- Typecheck passes for all touched files.
- Live behavior on an actual full disk was not exercised; that needs a packaged build.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(frontend): make dev:web start on Windows
body:
## What

Make `npm run dev:web` start on Windows, and add a test so the bug class cannot come back.

## Why

`dev:web` set the renderer's browser-preview flag with a POSIX env prefix:

```json
"dev:web": "VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts"
```

npm runs scripts through `cmd.exe` on Windows, which has no env-prefix syntax, so the script died before vite ever started:

```
> VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite --config vite.renderer.config.ts --port 5199 --host 127.0.0.1
'VITE_NO_ELECTRON' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
```

That also took `npm run test:e2e` down with it, since the Playwright `webServer` boots `dev:web`. A Windows contributor has no renderer-only dev loop and no renderer e2e suite today.

## How

Pass `--mode web` and let the renderer config inject the flag, so the value reaches `import.meta.env` on every platform:

```ts
define: mode === "web" ? { "import.meta.env.VITE_NO_ELECTRON": '"1"' } : {},
```

Only `web` defines the key. electron-forge dev/package and vitest run under other modes and leave it undefined exactly as before, so the packaged renderer is untouched and the comment in `useWorkspaceQuery.ts` still holds.

Two alternatives I discarded, in case they come up in review:

- **A tracked `.env` file** — `.gitignore` excludes `.env*` (only `.env.example` is negated), so it could not be committed.
- **`cross-env`** — I tried it and backed it out. Any dependency change rewrites `package-lock.json` on Windows, and that rewrite drops the optional `@emnapi/*` entries bundled under `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi`, which Linux installs need. The lockfile churn was worse than the fix. The config route needs no dependency and leaves the lockfile untouched.

The second commit adds `frontend/npm-scripts-portability.test.ts`, modelled on `release-workflows.test.ts`: it reads the root and frontend manifests and fails on any script that sets an environment variable with a POSIX prefix. Nothing else catches this class — the prefix is valid `sh` and CI is Linux-only.

## Testing

Windows 11, Node 24.13.0, npm 11.6.2, Go 1.27.0.

- `npm run dev:web -- --port 5199 --host 127.0.0.1` — starts (previously exit 1). Confirmed the flag actually lands by fetching a transformed module from the dev server:
  ```
  import.meta.env = {"BASE_URL":"/","DEV":true,"MODE":"web","PROD":false,"SSR":false,"VITE_NO_ELECTRON":"1"}
  ```
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` — both clean.
- `npx vitest run` — 2612 passed / 2625 total, exactly +2 from the new test versus the pre-change baseline of 2610 / 2623. The 12 remaining failures are the pre-existing macOS/POSIX-only specs (maker-dmg, relocation, auto-updater translocation, supervisor-link unix sockets, the `verify-mac-artifact.sh` exec-bit check) and are identical before and after this change.
- New test verified by reintroducing the prefix: it fails and names the offending script.
- `npm run dev` — full Electron app launches from this branch, daemon on 127.0.0.1:3002, renderer serving `/api/v1/projects` and `/api/v1/sessions` 200s.

I could not run the Playwright renderer suite end to end here (no browsers installed on this machine), so the `test:e2e` claim covers the `webServer` command starting, not the specs passing.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(lifecycle): fence chat activity by controller generation
body:
Fixes #4125

## Summary
- require every Chat lifecycle signal to carry the current internal controller generation, so inherited provider hooks cannot rewrite the parent session identity or activity
- treat non-exited activity from that current controller as liveness evidence, allowing a live Chat session to recover from a stale `exited`
- add regressions for foreign `session-end` metadata/state corruption and active, idle, and waiting-input resurrection

## Root cause
The reducer only validated `ControllerGeneration` when the incoming signal supplied one. Public provider hooks never supply it, and Chat sessions have no runtime launch ID, so those signals bypassed both ownership checks. The SQLite write fence could not compensate because it compared against the generation copied from the already-read session row.

## Tests

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/chat`
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` with an isolated cache: 0 issues

## Risk
TUI hook semantics are unchanged. Chat controller generations are already claimed before event consumption and included on every internal activity report; no API or schema change is required.

title: bug(cli): transient daemon restart is reported to agents as a hook error on stderr
body:
## Summary

Every hook that fires while the daemon is restarting prints `AO daemon is not running (stale run-file at ...) — start it with \`ao start\`` onto stderr. Hooks run inside the agent's own process, so that text lands in the agent's context as if the tool had failed.

The hook itself is fine — it exits 0, and reconciliation recovers the missed activity from process state. The problem is purely that an expected, transient condition is reported to the agent as an error.

## Why it happens

The desktop app's daemon takeover removes the old run-file and the new daemon writes a fresh one (`frontend/src/main.ts:1261`). Between those two steps the run-file still holds the **previous daemon's dead PID**.

Any CLI call in that window hits `backend/internal/cli/client.go:129`:

```go
if !c.deps.ProcessAlive(info.PID) {
    return fmt.Errorf("AO daemon is not running (stale run-file at %s) — start it with `ao start`", cfg.RunFilePath)
}
```

The error is an untyped `fmt.Errorf`, so `reportHookFailure` (`backend/internal/cli/hooks.go:450`) cannot distinguish "the daemon is mid-restart" from "the daemon returned 500", and unconditionally writes it to `c.deps.Err`.

The same applies to the `info == nil` branch just above it (no run-file at all).

## Observed impact

From one machine's `$AO_DATA_DIR/hooks.log`, **56 occurrences across 9 distinct restart windows** since late June. All hook events are affected:

| hook | count |
|---|---|
| `claude-code session-end` | 27 |
| `agent-process process-exited` | 7 |
| `claude-code user-prompt-submit` | 4 |
| `claude-code session-start` | 3 |
| `claude-code pre-tool-use` | 3 |
| `claude-code post-tool-use` | 3 |
| `claude-code stop` | 3 |
| `claude-code notification` | 3 |
| `opencode user-prompt-submit` | 2 |
| `opencode session-start` | 1 |

One representative window lasted ~35 seconds and hit 6 concurrent sessions across 5 projects. Where agent transcripts recorded the invocation (12 of them), every one shows `"exitCode": 0` — confirming the hooks worked and only the message was spurious. `agent-process process-exited` fires after the agent is gone, so it appears in `hooks.log` only, which does not record an exit code.

Session-start context injection is unaffected: it is read from disk and emitted before any daemon call (`hooks.go:311`), so it still reaches the agent during a restart window.

Both agent adapters that use hooks are affected, so this is not `claude-code`-specific.

## Impact

- Agents receive a spurious "daemon is not running" error in their context and may act on it — re-running work, reporting failure, or asking the user to run `ao start` when the daemon is in fact healthy.
- The message is indistinguishable from a genuine daemon outage, so real problems are harder to spot in `hooks.log`.

## Reproduction

No live daemon required — `ProcessAlive` is already injectable via `Deps` (`backend/internal/cli/root.go:70`):

```go
func TestHooks_DaemonNotRunningStaysOutOfStderr(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("AO_SESSION_ID", "ao-7")
	cfg := setConfigEnv(t)
	if err := runfile.Write(cfg.runFile, runfile.Info{
		PID: 999999, Port: 3001, StartedAt: time.Unix(100, 0).UTC(),
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write run-file: %v", err)
	}

	_, errOut, err := executeCLI(t, Deps{
		In:           strings.NewReader(`{"reason":"logout"}`),
		ProcessAlive: func(int) bool { return false },
	}, "hooks", "claude-code", "session-end")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("hooks must exit 0 when the daemon is down, got: %v", err)
	}
	if errOut != "" {
		t.Errorf("daemon-down must not reach the agent's stderr, got %q", errOut)
	}
}
```

Currently fails with the stale-run-file message on stderr. The `info == nil` variant (no run-file, `ProcessAlive` returning true) reproduces the second branch.

## Suggested fix

Make the condition a sentinel so callers can classify it:

```go
var ErrDaemonNotRunning = errors.New("AO daemon is not running")
```

wrap it with `%w` in both branches of `doJSONPathWithHeadersAndTimeout`, and in `reportHookFailure` skip the stderr write when `errors.Is(cause, ErrDaemonNotRunning)` — still appending to `hooks.log` so the event stays diagnosable. Genuine daemon errors keep reaching stderr unchanged, and interactive commands keep the identical message text.

Happy to raise a PR (branch ready, red test → fix → green, mutation-checked).

title: fix(cli): keep daemon-down out of hook stderr
body:
Closes #4210.

Hooks run inside the agent's own process, so anything they write to stderr lands in the agent's context. During the desktop app's daemon takeover the run-file briefly points at a dead PID, and every hook firing in that window printed `AO daemon is not running (stale run-file at ...)` at the agent — even though the hook exits 0 and reconciliation recovers the missed activity from process state.

## Change

`doJSONPathWithHeadersAndTimeout` returned an untyped `fmt.Errorf` for both daemon-down branches, so `reportHookFailure` could not tell a restart apart from a real delivery failure.

- Add `ErrDaemonNotRunning` and wrap it with `%w` in both branches (`info == nil`, dead PID). Message text is unchanged, so interactive commands read exactly as before.
- In `reportHookFailure`, skip the stderr write when `errors.Is(cause, ErrDaemonNotRunning)`. The notice still goes to `hooks.log`, so the event stays diagnosable.

Genuine daemon errors (HTTP 5xx, transport failures) keep reaching stderr — covered by the existing `TestHooks_DaemonErrorIsSwallowed`, which is untouched and still asserts stderr is written.

## Tests

`TestHooks_DaemonNotRunningStaysOutOfStderr` is table-driven over both branches and needs no live daemon — `ProcessAlive` is injectable via `Deps`. It asserts exit 0, empty stderr, and a recorded `hooks.log` line.

Verified red before the fix (both sub-cases), green after. Mutation-checked: removing the `errors.Is` guard fails the test.

`go test ./internal/cli/` passes; `gofmt -l .` and `go vet ./...` are clean across the module.

title: bug(chat): transient Codex network loss is misreported as a fatal thread error
body:
## Bug

When a Codex Chat turn exhausts its reconnect attempts during a transient network outage, Codex app-server briefly reports the thread as `systemError`. AO persists that status and the desktop renders a banner claiming the provider thread is broken and future turns will usually fail. The prognosis is false: once connectivity returns, the next message succeeds on the same thread.

**Source:** AO chat report with read-only evidence from session `agent-orchestrator-140` | **Observed:** 2026-08-20 PDT | **Analyzed against:** `52fde0279` | **AO version:** locally built `dev`, daemon on port 3001
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — Chat is degraded and the banner discourages the working recovery path, but sending a new message after connectivity returns is a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Codex session in Chat mode and begin a turn.
2. Disconnect the machine from the network long enough for Codex to exhaust its response-stream reconnect attempts.
3. Observe Codex app-server emit `thread/status/changed` with `status.type = systemError`, followed by `turn/completed` with a failed turn and a transport error such as `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses)`.
4. Observe AO render “The agent's thread hit an internal error” and say new turns will usually fail.
5. Restore connectivity and send another message. The same thread becomes `active`, answers normally, and returns to `idle`.

Concrete incident timeline (2026-08-20 PDT):

- 14:57:26 — turn `01a0212d-d469-75c1-b54b-4707757194be` became active.
- 15:03:44 — laptop entered clamshell sleep and Wi-Fi dropped; Codex emitted two five-attempt reconnect cycles, including macOS DNS lookup failure and an error sending the responses request.
- 15:24:33 — provider emitted `systemError`, then completed the turn as failed with the transport error.
- 16:59:43 — next user turn `01a0219d-c59c-73c2-8921-d12975cef2b9` became active on the same provider conversation.
- 17:07:55 — that turn completed normally and the thread returned to idle.

## Root Cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/normalize.go` maps every Codex `systemError` thread status directly to `domain.ThreadStatusSystemError` without correlating it with the immediately following failed turn.
- The same normalizer preserves the `turn/completed` error text but does not classify transport signatures or repair the pessimistic thread state.
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` persists thread-state updates independently. Therefore the transient `system_error` is sticky until a later provider status report replaces it.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatStatusBanners.tsx` treats every `system_error` as a durable provider-thread fault and explicitly predicts that new turns will usually fail.

Read-only durable evidence from the incident shows this exact event order:

1. `thread.state = active`
2. `thread.state = system_error`
3. `turn.completed = failed`, error `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (...)`
4. on the next message, `thread.state = active`
5. `thread.state = idle`
6. `turn.completed = completed`

This falsifies the theory that AO derives `system_error` from any failed turn: Codex reports it. AO's bug is interpreting and persisting that provider status without the transport-failure context it reports milliseconds later.

## Fix

- Classify known transient Codex transport failures from the failed turn's error signature.
- Preserve the turn as failed and preserve its error text.
- Correlate the transport failure with the preceding `systemError`, restore the thread to a healthy idle state, and retain a current “connection lost during this turn” notice until the next turn begins.
- Render recovery-oriented copy that tells the user to send a message again.
- Keep genuine unclassified `systemError` behavior unchanged.
- Add adapter/service and renderer tests for transient versus genuine system errors and for clearing the connection-loss notice on the next active status.

## Impact

- Users are told a healthy, reusable conversation is probably permanently broken.
- The incorrect state remains visible throughout an outage and after connectivity returns, until another turn is attempted.
- Users may abandon context or restart work unnecessarily.

## Related

- [#4120](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4120) — also involved a failed Chat turn, but concerned TUI→Chat history settlement rather than transient thread-state classification.

title: feat(chat): retry a failed turn without retyping the prompt
body:
## Problem

When a Chat turn fails after transient network loss, AO preserves the failed turn and its error correctly, but the user has no one-click way to submit the same prompt again. They must retype or manually copy the original message.

This is especially confusing when the recovery guidance says to send the message again.

**Source:** Follow-up from [#4212](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4212) | **Analyzed against:** `52fde0279`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — the core recovery path works, but avoidable re-entry friction follows a common transient failure.

## Current Behavior

- A failed turn is durable and its original human message remains in the timeline.
- The turn boundary displays `Failed` and the provider error.
- Rollback and edit/branch operations exist, but no operation means “dispatch this failed human prompt again as a new turn.”
- The composer retains attachments only when the initial send itself fails before acceptance; it does not restore content for an asynchronously failed provider turn.

## Proposed Behavior

Add a **Retry turn** action to eligible failed-turn boundaries that:

1. Reuses the durable original human message content and attachments.
2. Creates a new turn rather than mutating or relabeling the failed attempt.
3. Preserves both attempts in history and keeps provider-turn correlation explicit.
4. Uses the conversation's current next-turn settings unless product design deliberately chooses to preserve the failed attempt's settings.
5. Is disabled while another turn is running and reports daemon/provider refusals in place.
6. Is safe against double-clicks and uncertain delivery; it must not silently execute the work twice.

## Scope Notes

This should be a dedicated daemon/API operation, not renderer-side reconstruction of message text. The daemon owns ordering, attachments, delivery state, and idempotency. Reusing the existing edit/fork path would change conversation history semantics and is not equivalent to retrying after a recoverable failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Retry is offered only for an eligible failed human turn.
- Clicking once creates exactly one new queued/running turn with the same content.
- The original failed turn remains failed and visible.
- Attachments are reused or a clear validation error explains why they cannot be.
- Busy, unsupported-provider, stale-branch, and uncertain-delivery cases are tested.
- Renderer tests cover visible, hidden, disabled, pending, and error states.

## Related

- [#4212](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4212) — classifies transient Codex network failures and provides accurate recovery guidance.

title: fix(chat): classify transient Codex transport failures
body:
Fixes [#4212](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4212).

## Summary

- classify narrow Codex response-stream transport signatures after the provider reports `systemError`
- preserve the failed turn and exact provider error while restoring the reusable thread to healthy `idle`
- retain a recoverable connection-loss notice until the next turn becomes active
- render accurate recovery guidance instead of predicting that future turns will fail
- leave genuine/unclassified provider `systemError` behavior unchanged
- regenerate OpenAPI and renderer API types for the optional connection-loss timestamp

## Evidence

In session `agent-orchestrator-140`, Codex emitted `thread/status/changed = systemError` immediately before a failed `turn/completed` with `stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (...)`. The same provider conversation accepted the next turn, became active, completed normally, and returned to idle. The durable AO event order confirms the status came from Codex; AO's fault was retaining and presenting it without the transport context reported milliseconds later.

## Tests

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_DAEMON_URL -u AO_RUN_FILE -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_PORT npm run lint`

- `npm run api`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd frontend && npm test` — 2,630 passed, 1 skipped

## Risk / follow-up

Classification is intentionally limited to response-stream failures with known DNS/send/reset/closed/timeout transport signatures. Unknown errors continue to display the provider's genuine `systemError` state.

A one-click retry action is intentionally separate because it needs a daemon-owned, idempotent history/dispatch operation: [#4215](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4215).

title: feat: add provider-neutral subscription usage
body:
## Summary

Adds a provider-neutral subscription usage system for Codex, Claude, and future coding-agent adapters. The feature tracks provider-reported plan capacity, current rate-limit windows, credits/balances when available, bounded usage history, refresh failures, and threshold alerts without estimating prompts or tasks from token totals.

## Implementation

### Provider adapter layer

- Introduces a neutral quota model in `backend/internal/domain/quota.go` for provider accounts, limits, balances, capabilities, history points, and alerts.
- Adds quota ports so adapters can publish snapshots without the service depending on provider-specific payloads.
- Maps Codex app-server `account/rateLimits/read` and rate-limit update payloads into neutral quota snapshots, including:
  - account-level rate limits
  - model-scoped limits from `rateLimitsByLimitId`
  - Codex credits from `rateLimits.credits`
  - reset credits from `rateLimitResetCredits.availableCount`
  - duplicate-window collapse when Codex reports identical primary/secondary windows
- Maps Claude ACP usage metadata and structured plan usage into neutral quota snapshots, including:
  - partial push-based usage updates from ACP metadata
  - full sessionless reads through `ao-claude-plan-usage.mjs`
  - five-hour, seven-day, OAuth app, Opus, Sonnet, and model-scoped windows when Claude reports them
- Keeps provider-specific parsing inside the relevant adapter packages so future adapters can add quota support by implementing the same neutral contracts.

### Quota service

- Adds `backend/internal/service/quota` to merge provider observations, coalesce refreshes, cache fresh reads, derive severity, and emit transition-only alerts.
- Supports complete and partial snapshots so provider pushes do not erase previously known buckets.
- Refreshes per provider account rather than per session, which avoids multiplying provider calls when multiple conversations share one subscription.
- Registers daemon-owned providers and refreshes stale accounts on startup, periodically, on Plan Usage page entry, and after relevant idle transitions.
- Persists a first refresh failure for registered provider accounts so installed-but-broken providers appear as actionable error cards instead of disappearing from the page.

### Storage

- Adds SQLite migration `0102_provider_quota.sql` with:
  - `quota_accounts` for latest provider/account state
  - `quota_limits` for latest limit buckets
  - `quota_balances` for latest credits/balances
  - `quota_history` for bounded trend data
  - `quota_alerts` for threshold transitions
- Inserts history only when the meaningful quota state changes.
- Compacts history automatically:
  - last 24 hours: at most one point per minute
  - 24 hours to 30 days: at most one point per hour
  - 30 to 90 days: at most one point per day
  - older than 90 days: deleted

### API and frontend

- Adds daemon API endpoints for:
  - listing provider quota snapshots
  - fetching one provider account
  - refreshing one provider account
  - reading bounded history
  - reading recent quota alerts
- Regenerates OpenAPI and frontend TypeScript schema.
- Adds a Plan Usage page in the Electron UI with:
  - generic provider cards
  - current remaining/used values
  - compact credits and balances rows when reported
  - retry action for failed provider refreshes when the account supports reads
  - AO-aligned settings-style layout
- Adds sidebar navigation and notification integration for quota alerts.

## Scalability

- Provider-neutral domain and API keep the UI independent of Codex/Claude-specific payloads.
- Capability flags let the UI render whatever a provider can truthfully report without hardcoding provider names.
- Reads are coalesced with `singleflight`, and fresh account snapshots are reused.
- Storage is account-level, not session-level, so many sessions can share one provider subscription state.
- History is bounded and compacted; this is cached operational state, not an append-only billing ledger.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` was run; the full parallel suite hit unrelated adapter timing flakes, and each failed package passed individually.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `go test ./internal/service/quota ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/storage/sqlite ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/httpd/controllers`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/fake -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/kilocode -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/primeagent -count=1`
- `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs`
- Focused Plan Usage frontend test: `PlanUsagePage.test.tsx`
- `git diff --check`

## Notes

- AO only displays provider-reported values. It does not infer remaining prompts, tasks, or spend from token totals.
- Credits are shown only when the provider reports stable credit/balance fields.
- Claude structured usage is accessed through the ACP SDK's usage query rather than by sending `/usage` into a visible chat conversation.
- Quota history remains persisted and compacted for future trend/alert use, but this PR does not currently render an observed-usage history sparkline in the simplified Plan Usage card.
