title: fix(files): correctness follow-ups for the markdown Preview tab
body:
Follow-ups for #4251, branched off `feat/github-markdown-render`. Merging this into that branch folds the commits into the PR.

Seven correctness fixes, three cleanups, the first tests for the new code, and a rename plus redesign of the tab pair. One commit per item, each with its reasoning, so anything you disagree with can be dropped on its own.

## Bugs

**Relative images never reloaded after an edit.** `buildWorkspaceBlobUrl` mirrors `ImageDiffView`'s blob route but not its `v=` parameter, and that parameter is why the route works — it serves `no-store`, so as `ImageDiffView`'s own comment puts it, without a changing URL the element never refetches at all. An image an agent rewrote kept rendering from cache indefinitely. Threads the detail's load timestamp through `MarkdownFileContext`.

**A failed image rendered as a broken-image box.** The CSP allows `img-src` from `'self'`, `data:` and the loopback daemon only, so an `https://` image — a shields.io badge, a hosted screenshot, the two most common images in a real README — cannot load here at all. Falls back to alt text, the way `ImageDiffView` already handles its own failures.

**Truncated files rendered as though complete.** The daemon caps content at `maxWorkspaceFileBytes` and reports `contentTruncated`; the diff body respects it, the rendered view ignored it. The rendering is worse than the omission: a cut landing inside a fence leaves it unclosed, swallowing everything after it into one code block, with no signal that anything is missing. Adds the same warning strip behind a new `files.contentTruncated` string, translated for all eight locales.

**Heading links could scroll to the wrong file.** `rehype-slug` guarantees ids unique per rendered file, not per document, and the Files tab expands many cards at once — two open READMEs with `## Overview` put two `id="overview"` in one DOM, and `document.getElementById` answers with whichever is first. Resolves within the file's own container instead. Prefixing the slugs would also have worked but would have broken every hand-written `[link](#overview)`, which is the more common case.

**Clicking a heading overwrote the clipboard.** Silently, with no affordance saying so, and with a bare `#some-heading` that names no file and cannot be pasted anywhere and followed. Scroll only; a deliberate copy-link control can come later.

**The selection guard leaked on tab switch.** `DiffView` reports selection state up so a background refetch cannot re-render rows out from under a live selection, and that effect had no cleanup. Harmless until this PR, since the diff only unmounted with the card. Now: switch tabs with a selection active and `selectionOrMenuActive` stays `true` forever, the detail query stays disabled, and the rendered view sits on a snapshot that never refreshes while the agent keeps writing — with nothing left mounted that could clear it.

**Tab switching lost scroll position.** Not because a scroll position is discarded — an expanded file has no scroll box, the Files panel is one shared scroller. Swapping a 4,000-line diff for its rendered form shortens the column by thousands of pixels, and the browser clamps `scrollTop` to the new maximum; switching back restores the height but not the clamped-away offset.

Worth recording since it is the obvious thing to reach for: **`forceMount` does not fix this.** A hidden `TabsContent` is `display: none`, contributes zero height, and clamps identically — no benefit, and a large diff mounted for as long as the card is open. Instead a small `useViewModeScrollAnchor` records the card's offset from the scroll root when a mode is left and restores it when that mode returns, in a layout effect plus one `requestAnimationFrame`, since virtualized rows settle to their real heights a frame after mounting. No change to `useSharedScrollRowVirtualizer`. (The anchor originally rode the tab strip; the last commit moves that strip into the title row, so it rides the card's own top edge instead — see below.)

## Cleanups

- `textOf` / `fenceOf` / the `language-*` pattern arrived as byte-for-byte copies of `ChatMarkdown`'s. Both feed the same highlighter, so language sniffing had two places to drift. One copy in `lib/markdown-fence.ts`.
- `code-theme.css` had every selector written twice, once per scope. `:is(.chat-code, .markdown-code)` states it once — identical matching, ~60 fewer lines. Also corrects `HighlightedCode`'s comment, which still named `.chat-code` as the only scope.
- Notes in `MarkdownFileView` that the `prefers-color-scheme` argument holds under Electron but not `npm run dev:web`.

## Tests

`markdown-image-resolver` is pure and does the fiddliest work in the feature; it arrived untested. Eleven cases: resolution against the file's directory, a file at the workspace root, `..` walking up, `..` clamping at the root rather than escaping, query/fragment stripping, absolute passthrough, and the version reaching the URL.

The tab pair itself had no coverage at all. Two cases now: the strip renders in the title row as a sibling of the trigger rather than a descendant, and survives the panel swap — which is the `asChild` ref composition actually working at runtime — and it stays off files that cannot render as markdown.

## Rename and redesign

`Source diff` / `Rendered` → **Diff** / **Preview**, strings renamed to `files.diff` / `files.preview` and retranslated for all eight locales.

The control then moved out of the body and into the file's own title row. It had a band to itself under the title, and that band held nothing else — a right-aligned control with the whole width of the card empty to its left. It now sits beside the `+N`/`-N` badges, on the line that already names the file it acts on, and the card is a row shorter.

`AccordionTrigger` already had a `trailing` slot for exactly this: rendered inside the header row but as a sibling of the trigger `<button>`, which is what makes it legal — a `<button>` inside a `<button>` is invalid, and a nested tab would collapse the file on click. The Tabs root moves up to enclose the title row as well as the body it switches; it and `AccordionItem` both take `asChild`, so they compose onto the same single `<li>`: no wrapper element, no change in DOM depth. The strip renders only while the file is expanded.

**This costs the anchoring premise of the scroll-position commit above.** That commit chose the tab strip deliberately, because it sat at the top of the swapped body and was an element the component owned outright, with no ref composition through `asChild` in the way. The strip no longer moves with the body, so the anchor rides the card's own top edge, through a ref composed across both `asChild` roots. Since that is precisely what the earlier commit avoided, it is now covered by tests rather than resting on a typecheck.

Appearance follows the inspector rail's own tab buttons (`session-inspector__tab-button`), which is the tab language of the pane this control lives in: `text-passive` labels, `--color-interactive-*` fills one step apart on the same neutral (foreground at 4% for the track, 7% for the selected tab), and a hairline border — GitHub's segmented-control signature, and what separates this shape from a shadcn pill group. Stock shadcn's palette is dropped, and worth flagging as an actual defect rather than taste: its dark-theme active fill is `bg-input/30`, white at 1.2% over the `bg-muted` track, which is not a visible selection at this size.

Sizing is a 20px track over 16px pills — deliberately under the 20px a standalone control would get. It rides in a 36px row it does not own, beside a 28px button, and reading as the smaller thing there is the point; the labels are wide enough to keep the targets easy despite the height. Narrowing keys off the `inspector` container the shell already declares, at the 350px/300px steps it already breaks at, so the toggle changes on the same drag positions as everything else in the pane. In the centre pane there is no `inspector` container to match, so it keeps full size.

Still a judgement call, and still droppable as its own commit if you disagree.

## Not addressed

- **`github-markdown-css` vs the design system.** `CLAUDE.md` asks for explicit approval before deviating. Your reasoning is sound and I have not touched it — flagging it as the repo owner's call. Side effect worth knowing: AO's nine theme styles (dracula, nord, gruvbox…) do not reach the Preview tab, which stays GitHub-coloured.
- **Lockfile churn.** The `motion` entries under `packages/product-ui` are unrelated to this feature, but they correct a stale lock on `main` (`packages/product-ui/package.json` already lists it there). Harmless — worth a line in the PR body so a reviewer does not stop on it.

## Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Full renderer suite as of the tests commit: **2689 passed, 1 skipped, 204 files** — including your 35 `SessionFilesView` tests unmodified. Each commit typechecks on its own.

For the title-row commit on top I re-ran typecheck and `SessionFilesView` only (**37 passed**, the 35 plus the two new ones), not the full suite.

Manual verification in the Electron app is still worth doing for the scroll anchor and the image reload, which are the two that depend on real layout.

## Demo

Screen recording of the change in the desktop app: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e5T3MbyQTVrNtLqfo2ZLPWgldhwUpDQO/view?usp=sharing

title: macOS nightly auto-update from v0.10.0 fails: ShipIt code-signature validation rejects staged bundle (AppleDouble/symlink-bearing zip meets pre-acp-runtime updater)
body:
## Bug

macOS desktop auto-update from **v0.10.0 stable** to the **Nightly channel** fails during Squirrel.Mac's install phase. The update downloads, but `ShipIt` aborts with:

> Code signature at URL file:///Users/.../Library/Caches/dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt/update.M9ZvE0X/Agent%20Orchestrator.app/ did not pass validation: code failed to satisfy specified code requirement(s)

The app stays on v0.10.0 (Settings shows `Current version: v0.10.0`, channel switched to "Nightly (pre-release)", auto-updates enabled).

**Source:** Discord `#report-bugs` | **Reported by:** @pritommazumdar (Tom24) | 2026-08-22
**Confidence:** High (published artifact verified sound; failure localized to the v0.10.0-era updater path consuming the new bundle format)

![Settings → Updates showing the ShipIt code-signature validation error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-mac-nightly-sigfail/.issue-assets/mac-nightly-sigfail/settings-updates-error.png)

## Reproduction

1. Install AO desktop **v0.10.0** (stable, published 2026-06-28 — before the acp-runtime bundling and before the #3151 updater work).
2. Settings → Updates: Automatic updates **Enabled**, Update channel **Nightly (pre-release)**, Save.
3. Click **Check for updates** → update to `v0.12.7-nightly.*` downloads, then install fails with the signature-validation error above.
4. App remains on v0.10.0; retrying reproduces the same error.

## What this is NOT (ruled out empirically)

I downloaded both the user's baseline and the current nightly and inspected them directly:

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Published nightly zip corrupt / bad sha512 | ❌ Ruled out | `sha512` of `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.7-nightly.202608211403.zip` matches `nightly-mac.yml` exactly |
| Signing identity mismatch (old cert vs new cert) | ❌ Ruled out | All **18** Mach-O binaries in the nightly zip carry the same Developer ID as v0.10.0's 16 binaries: `Developer ID Application: Prateek Karnal (X9LNSP8MC2)` — every CMS blobwrapper has a real certificate signature |
| Designated-requirement drift (TeamID/bundle-id anchor) | ❌ Ruled out | Embedded requirements blobs of v0.10.0 and the nightly are **byte-identical** (184 B; anchors `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop` + `subject.OU = X9LNSP8MC2`) |
| Bundle ID change | ❌ Ruled out | Both `CFBundleIdentifier: dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop` (also consistent with the reporter's `dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop.ShipIt` cache path) |
| `.blockmap` differential-download corruption (#3034) | ❌ Ruled out | v0.10.0's release ships **no mac blockmap**, and neither does any later release — the updater takes the full-download path |
| Orphaned AppleDouble / dangling acp symlinks in the nightly zip | ❌ Ruled out | All 69 `._*` entries have sibling targets; all `acp-runtime/node_modules/.bin/*` symlinks resolve inside the zip |

## Root Cause

The published nightly artifact is **sound**: correctly signed with the same identity and requirements as the user's baseline. The failure is in **extraction/staging on the v0.10.0-era updater path**, consuming a bundle layout that has changed substantially since that baseline:

- **v0.10.0 zip (Jun 28): 275 entries, 0 AppleDouble (`._*`) entries, no symlink entries.**
- **Every release since v0.11.0: 6,768 entries, 69 AppleDouble entries (incl. `._app.asar`), plus 3 `acp-runtime/node_modules/.bin/*` symlink entries.** (v0.11.0 had 275 AppleDouble entries.) Note these `._*` entries are the **deliberate ditto-built zip format** — `frontend/scripts/verify-mac-artifact.sh` mandates `ditto -x -k` extraction precisely because the seal depends on them. The change is the bundle *shape* (25× more entries, AppleDouble sidecars, symlinks), not a packaging defect.

Squirrel.Mac's `ShipIt` extracts the staged zip with `ditto`/its own extractor, then runs `codesign` verification over the extracted bundle against the **running app's** designated requirement. The `._*` AppleDouble sidecar entries and `acp-runtime` symlinks are exactly the artifact class that broke ShipIt installs in [#3034](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3034) and recurred in [#4175](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4175) ("ShipIt ditto fails on 'missing' `._app.asar__` and acp-runtime symlink despite verified-intact published zip"). When the extractor mishandles the `._*` entries or symlinks, the extracted bundle's resource seal (`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`) no longer matches → `codesign` fails → Squirrel reports *"code failed to satisfy specified code requirement(s)"* — the **same end-state error string** this report shows, one step later in the pipeline (validation instead of ditto's file-missing error).

v0.10.0's own updater (pre-#3151 electron-updater vintage, and predating all packaging changes) walking into a 6,768-entry zip with AppleDouble junk and symlinks is the oldest, least-tested combination in the matrix — and per the version-timeline cross-check below, it contains none of the extraction fixes that later baselines shipped.

### Why later baselines mostly survive

Users on ≥ v0.10.1-era updaters have newer `@electron-forge`/electron-updater packaging code that either drops the `._*` entries on extraction or tolerates them; #4175 documented a v0.12.6 baseline failing intermittently and self-healing on the next nightly. The v0.10.0 → nightly jump is the extreme end: baseline predates **every** updater/packaging fix.

## Version timeline

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| v0.10.0 (user's baseline) published | 2026-06-28 |
| acp-runtime bundling enters the zip (AppleDouble entries appear) | v0.11.0 (2026-07) |
| [#3151](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3151) skip-blockmap fix merged | 2026-07-29 |
| [#4175](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4175) ditto/`._app.asar` recurrence on v0.12.6 (closed: self-healed, single occurrence) | 2026-08-20 |
| This report: v0.10.0 → `v0.12.7-nightly.202608211403` fails at signature validation | 2026-08-22 |

## Fix

Two independent layers:

1. **Test the old-baseline path explicitly.** The v0.10.0 updater walking into a 6,768-entry ditto zip is the oldest-running-code-meets-newest-artifact combination, and it's a live population via the frozen npm on-ramp. The #3288 e2e update test matrix should include a **pre-v0.11.0 baseline → nightly** hop. (Stripping the `._*` entries is explicitly *not* recommended — #3267 decision 4: corruption reproduced against correctly ditto-built zips, and the seal depends on them.)
2. **Updater resilience (defense in depth):** the failure surfaces as a raw Squirrel dump next to the button with no remediation path. Already tracked in [#3288](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3288) (e2e update test + verification gate) and [#3528](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3528) (surface install failures properly) — this report adds the **signature-validation** failure mode and the **v0.10.0 baseline** to that matrix. A actionable in-app remediation for this class: when signature validation fails N times, offer the direct dmg download link.

**Immediate workaround for affected users:** bypass auto-update entirely — download the `.dmg` from the [latest nightly release](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/releases) (or latest stable), quit AO, and install over the existing app.

## Impact

- Any user on a **pre-v0.11.0 baseline** (v0.10.x) switching to Nightly hits a guaranteed-looking update failure with a cryptic signature error and no in-app remediation.
- The npm→desktop migration path (`ao start` on the frozen npm 0.10.0 CLI fetches the desktop build) means v0.10.x-era installs are still a live population, not just legacy stragglers.
- All mac zips since v0.11.0 carry the large AppleDouble-bearing acp-runtime shape — a recurring extraction-fragility surface for ShipIt edge cases (three incidents now: #3034, #4175, this).

## Related

- [#4175](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4175) — same artifact family (ditto/`._app.asar` on full-download path); closed as self-healed single occurrence; this is a second, harder-failing data point
- [#3034](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3034) — original ShipIt/ditto corruption bug
- [#3151](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3151) — skip-blockmap fix (present in feed; not implicated here)
- [#3267](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3267) — dmg-first distribution plan
- [#3288](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3288) — release hardening (e2e update test, verification gate)
- [#3528](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3528) — surface install failures instead of bogus errors

title: feat(telemetry): instrument the review funnel end to end
body:
## Why

Reviews are a headline feature with almost no measurement behind them. Four `ao.review.*` events existed, and all of them sat on the manual trigger path, so an **automatic** review was invisible at trigger time: `TriggerAuto` called the engine directly and emitted nothing, which made auto-review indistinguishable from manual review in every funnel even though the two answer different product questions.

Per review feedback this PR now ships the **P0 event set only**. Everything else is listed as P1 at the bottom, with what each deferred event would have answered.

## P0 events in this PR

### Daemon

| Event | Change |
|---|---|
| `ao.review.triggered` | adds `trigger` (auto or manual). `Trigger` and `TriggerAuto` now share one instrumented path, so an automatic pass is never invisible |
| `ao.review.trigger_failed` | adds `trigger`, so a failure is attributable to the automatic or the manual path |
| `ao.review.submitted` | adds `trigger` (read from the run), `body_bytes` (review depth, never the text) and `auto_inject` (whether the session policy will let the result reach the worker) |

Payload keys are allowlisted in `remotePayloadAllowlist`; without an entry an event exports with no properties at all rather than failing loudly.

### Renderer

| Event | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ao.renderer.review_settings_changed` | project-level `auto_review` and `reviewer_harness`, plus `harness_is_default` and per-field changed flags. Emitted only when a review control actually changed, so it counts review decisions rather than every unrelated save. **This is the event that tells us whether the harness dropdown is a decision anybody makes or a checkpoint that could become a default** |
| `ao.renderer.review_auto_review_toggled` | the session-scoped auto-review switch, which duplicates the project setting. Whether anyone reaches for it decides if it stays a separate control |
| `ao.renderer.review_triggered` | manual runs, with the offered `action`, whether a per-session reviewer override was in play, and `source` (`inspector` or `command_palette`). Manual volume against auto volume is the adoption signal, and the two on-ramps stay separable |

`reviewRunActionKind` was extracted from `reviewSessionRunAction` so `review_triggered.action` reports a stable enum rather than the translated label the user happened to see. The command palette is a manual on-ramp in its own right and POSTs to the trigger endpoint directly, so it emits the same event and carries that enum on its action.

Both renderer emit sites fire before the request. That is deliberate: they count INTENT, and the daemon's `ao.review.*` events are the ground truth for what actually ran. A toggle whose save then fails still counts as the user reaching for the switch.

## One behaviour change that is not an event

While a review is running, the once-a-minute auto-review sweep calls `TriggerAuto` again, the engine reports success with nothing created, and the old code emitted another `ao.review.triggered` every time. A six-minute review produced **seven "triggers" for one real pass**, which would have inflated the headline count and spent the 200/day per-name rate limit that real triggers need.

An automatic pass that did no work (a policy race, or a reuse) now reports **nothing at all**. A manual reuse stays a trigger, because the user pressed the button and that is a real action. This was found by running the real coordinator against a real open PR, and reverting it would corrupt the very count P0 exists to measure.

## User flow, and where each P0 event fires

```
Project settings: toggle auto-review / pick a reviewer, save
  -> ao.renderer.review_settings_changed        (only if a review control changed)

Session inspector: flip the session auto-review switch
  -> ao.renderer.review_auto_review_toggled

Path A, manual: press Run / Re-review
  -> ao.renderer.review_triggered               (intent)
Path B, automatic: the coordinator sweeps an idle worker every minute
  -> (silent when there is nothing to do)

Either path reaches the engine
  -> ao.review.triggered { trigger: manual | auto }
  -> ao.review.trigger_failed { error_kind, trigger }

Reviewer agent works, then submits
  -> ao.review.submitted { verdict, trigger, duration_ms, body_bytes, auto_inject }
```

## Privacy

Counts, durations, enums and booleans only. No review body, PR URL, commit SHA, branch, PR title, repo or project name reaches any payload: review prose is reviewer commentary on someone's source, and the URL and SHA identify the repository. Project ids are hashed on the renderer side exactly as the existing settings events do, and reviewer harness ids are validated against AO's own reviewer registry so a caller mistake cannot forward free text.

Both paths keep their existing cost controls: per-event-name rate limits, the `DisabledEvents` kill switch, and an install-scoped `distinct_id`.

## Testing

Verified end to end, not just at the emit site. The payload allowlist that decides what actually reaches PostHog lives in the adapter, keyed by event name, with nothing tying it to the emit site at compile time.

- A **wire test** drives the real emit sites through the real export chain (denylist, aggregation, rate limit, PostHog) into a fake transport, then asserts the event names and properties as they leave the process. Confirmed it catches the real failure: removing one allowlist key makes it fail with `triggered.trigger = <nil>`.
- That test also scans the raw outgoing JSON for the review body, repo name, commit and review id, and fails if any appears under any key.
- Unit tests cover the auto against manual trigger split, the failure path, the submitted payload shape, a manual reuse staying counted, and six no-op automatic sweeps emitting nothing.
- Allowlist drift tests assert the review funnel's exact key sets and reject identifying keys across every `ao.review.*` entry.
- Renderer sanitizer tests cover each of the three events, including that an unknown harness or action is dropped rather than forwarded.

Backend: touched packages pass with `-count=1`, `golangci-lint` reports 0 issues. Frontend: 131 renderer test files, 1927 tests passing across three consecutive runs, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Pre-existing failures in this worktree, confirmed identical on a clean tree and unrelated to these changes: `adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver` (installed-provider conformance), `internal/cli` (spawn tests needing a live daemon), and the `landing` plus `main` frontend suites (uninstalled dependencies).

## Verified against a live daemon

The earlier full-funnel build was run on a real daemon from this branch, on an isolated data dir with a copy of live app state and remote export off, so nothing left the machine and the running app was untouched. Driving the real auto-review coordinator against a real open PR produced, for the events P0 keeps:

```
ao.review.triggered   {"created_runs":1,"harness":"claude-code","reused":false,"trigger":"auto"}
ao.review.submitted   {"trigger":"auto","verdict":"changes_requested","duration_ms":520165,
                       "body_bytes":103,"auto_inject":true,"posted_to_provider":false,
                       "harness":"claude-code"}
```

The `trigger: auto` on that first event is the fix this PR exists for: before it, that pass emitted nothing. That run is also what surfaced the per-sweep inflation described above.

## One caveat for whoever builds the dashboards

Manual and automatic passes share the single `ao.review.triggered` name, and therefore its 200/day per-name cap on the billed sink, split only by the `trigger` property. On a very high-volume install the billed count can truncate while local SQLite still keeps every occurrence, so exact auto-against-manual counts for a power user should be read from local rather than PostHog. Folding `trigger` into the aggregation tier would collapse the very split this PR adds, so the cap stands.

## P1, deferred by review decision

Removed from this PR. Listed with what each one answered, so picking them up later is a decision about priority and not a rediscovery.

| Deferred event | What goes unmeasured |
|---|---|
| `ao.review.feedback_delivered` | **Whether changes-requested feedback actually reached the worker agent.** A sent nudge, a suppressed one and an errored one look identical. The review loop (review, worker fixes, merge) is the feature's value, and P0 only observes its first half |
| `ao.review.pr_closed` | **Trust.** Whether a PR was merged over a standing changes-requested verdict, how many rounds it took, and reviewed against unreviewed time-to-merge. The override-merge flag was the only perception signal in the catalog, and the control-group data for a future default-on decision |
| `ao.review.feedback_withheld` | Why a completed changes-requested review reached nobody (`auto_inject_off`, `stale_head`, `already_delivered`). The quietest failure mode: a red verdict the worker never hears about |
| `ao.review.auto_skipped` | Why an enabled auto-review never produces reviews (draft PR, already approved, closed, missing head). "I turned it on and nothing happened" for the automatic flow |
| `ao.review.trigger_skipped` | How often automatic passes are skipped or reused. Denominator hygiene; the behaviour it guarded survives as silence |
| `ao.renderer.review_auto_inject_toggled` | Whether anyone touches the delivery switch, which is case data for merging the three review toggles |
| `ao.renderer.review_reviewer_overridden` | Whether anyone sets the per-session reviewer dropdown. Partly mitigated: `review_triggered.has_override` still shows overrides at run time |
| `ao.renderer.review_tab_opened` | Whether humans read findings or only trust the verdict |
| `ao.renderer.review_stopped` | Mid-run dissatisfaction, and the cancel against kill split that would justify merging two stop buttons |
| `ao.renderer.review_comment_sent_to_worker` | Humans hand-relaying comments, a cheap canary for automatic delivery failing |

Two smaller follow-ups, also out of scope here:

- `ao.review.rereview_requested` and `ao.review.comment_resolved` have shipped **payload-stripped** since before this PR, because their names are absent from the allowlist. The two-line fix is a bug fix rather than a new metric, so it is not in this PR either; say the word and it goes in.
- These are **change** events, not state events. A project that already had auto-review on will never emit a toggle event, so "what share of projects have auto-review on today" needs a small daily gauge (counts only, no identifiers) rather than these.

title: feat(chat): retry a failed turn without retyping the prompt
body:
## Summary

Closes #4215.

Adds a **Retry** action to eligible failed human turns so a transient failure can be retried without retyping the original prompt. The retry is a new turn; the failed source stays unchanged and visible.

## What changed

### Daemon and storage

- Adds `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/conversation/turns/{turnId}/retry`.
- Loads text and structured prompt content from durable AO rows, never from a caller-supplied retry payload.
- Applies the current next-turn model, reasoning, and approval settings.
- Persists an explicit `retry_of_turn_id` relation on the new turn in the same transaction as its message. A unique partial index makes one retry attempt per source durable and idempotent; retrying a failed retry creates the next link in the chain.
- Uses the persisted relation for replay and UI correlation, so caller-controlled client message IDs cannot impersonate or consume a retry.
- Refuses unsafe or invalid cases with typed errors: busy/handoff, stale branch, non-human or non-failed source, unconfirmed provider delivery, malformed durable content, and content unsupported by the current provider.
- Adds explicit native resource-link capability negotiation. ACP preserves resource links; a provider that cannot preserve them receives a clear refusal instead of silently dropping the attachment.
- Keeps retry consumption visible even when the retry child is rolled back or moves outside the active branch by deriving `hasRetryAttempt` from all durable retry relations.
- Includes `recovered` in replay response contracts and regenerates sqlc, OpenAPI, and frontend API types.

### Renderer

- Shows Retry only on eligible failed human turns.
- Disables it while work is running or a retry request is pending.
- Displays retry refusals beside the affected turn.
- Hides consumed retry actions using daemon-owned `retryOfTurnId` / `hasRetryAttempt` facts, including inactive-branch and rolled-back retry attempts.

## Tests

Coverage includes exact prompt/attachment replay, current settings, busy/non-human/stale/uncertain/unsupported refusals, double-click and replay idempotency, caller-ID collision, recovered replay, retry chains, resource-link provider switching, rollback, inactive-branch consumption, HTTP contracts, wire-to-renderer mapping, renderer visible/hidden/disabled/pending/error states, and Playwright behavior.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — full backend Go suite and golangci-lint: pass, 0 issues.
- Frontend typecheck and e2e typecheck: pass.
- Retry renderer + wire-mapping suites: 23 tests pass.
- Retry Playwright suite: 2 tests pass.
- Final Standards review: no findings.
- Final Spec review against #4215: no findings.

title: bug(desktop): switch-agent recovery dead-ends — "Check Codex" button loops forever, session fenced with no rollback or escape hatch
body:
## Bug

Switching a session from Codex to Claude failed with an unconfirmed source stop. The "Switch agent" dialog now shows the recovery prompt — **"Codex status could not be confirmed — AO could not confirm whether Codex stopped. Check the session before continuing."** — but the **Check Codex** button never resolves anything. The dialog re-renders in the identical state forever, and there is no path back to the (still-preserved) Codex session or forward to Claude. The user is fenced out of the session entirely.

![Stuck Switch agent recovery dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-switch-recovery-loop/.issue-assets/switch-recovery-loop/modal.png)

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` thread `1540800932936163338` | **Reported by:** @aditi | 2026-08-23 00:41 IST
**Analyzed against:** `35ee1fe42` (`fix: isolate ChatUI history by session (#4149)`, tip of `main` at analysis time)
**Build:** desktop **nightly**, macOS (screen recording)
**Confidence:** High (full code path traced; see mechanism below)
**Priority:** P1 — core feature (agent switching) broken with **no in-product workaround** for the affected session

## Reproduction

1. Desktop nightly on macOS, session running on **Codex** (reported session: "review PR 4100", terminal mode).
2. Initiate Switch agent → Claude.
3. Source teardown fails unconfirmed (`stopSourceRuntime` returns `ErrSwitchSourceStopUnconfirmed` — e.g. tmux server unreachable / probe error, or two destroy attempts both fail).
4. Switch row parks in `state=stopping_source`, `errorCode=source_stop_unconfirmed`.
5. Open the Switch agent dialog → recovery prompt with **Check Codex** button.
6. Click **Check Codex** (repeatedly). Button shows "Checking Codex…", then the dialog returns to the exact same state. Nothing ever changes.

## Root Cause

Two defects combine into a silent dead-end:

**1. The recovery worker treats a probe *error* as "keep waiting" and reports nothing.**
`backend/internal/session_manager/agent_switching.go:3054` `reconcileStoppingSource`:

```go
alive, err := m.runtime.IsAlive(ctx, handle)
if err != nil {
    if _, markerErr := m.markSourceStopUnconfirmed(ctx, store, sw); markerErr != nil { ...warn... }
    // The source may still be live, and no target exists yet. Keep the gate
    // closed until a later explicit recovery can prove the source boundary.
    return false, nil        // ← unresolved, NO error, NO state change
}
```

Clicking **Check Codex** → `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/agent-switches/{switchId}/recover` → `RecoverAgentSwitch` (`agent_switching.go:129`) → `startAgentSwitchRecoveryWorker` (`agent_switching.go:951`) → async `reconcileOwnedAgentSwitchOnce`. If `IsAlive` returns an error, reconcile returns `(false, nil)`: the worker logs `"agent switch recovery finished ... resolved=false"` and exits. The durable row is unchanged, so the frontend (`SwitchAgentDialog.tsx` + `useAgentSwitches.ts` — recovery-required rows are *static*, no refetch) re-renders the identical modal. HTTP 202 + no failure surfaced = the user perceives a dead button.

**2. The tmux probe classifier makes that error path the *likely* one after any stop failure.**
`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:955-968` (classification introduced for #3475): `has-session` output `"no server running"` / `"error connecting"` is deliberately treated as **inconclusive** → `IsAlive` returns an error, not `false`. On macOS, a completed teardown (or a crashed/exited tmux server) commonly leaves the server gone. So the very situation recovery exists to resolve — "we couldn't confirm the source stopped" — is the one where the probe **cannot** answer, and every recovery attempt deterministically re-enters the `return false, nil` branch.

Outcome: terminal-mode sessions whose source stop failed with a server-level probe error are **permanently fenced** (input gate retained via `retainAgentSwitch`, `session_input.go:179`) until something outside the dialog changes the facts.

**What recovery *should* do when it works:** if `IsAlive` returns a definitive `false` ("can't find session"/"session not found"), `reconcileStoppingSource` confirms the stop, then `failRecoveredSwitchWithSourceRollback` (`agent_switching.go:3216`) **restores the source harness and fails the switch** — i.e. the user gets their Codex session back. That is the outcome aditi expected and never got. (For contrast, when `IsAlive` errors in `reconcileStartingTarget` the target handle is *destroyed* and rollback proceeds — `agent_switching.go:3122-3129` — the stopping-source path has no equivalent progression.)

## Fix

1. **Progression, not repetition.** In `reconcileStoppingSource`, when the liveness probe errors, take a bounded step that changes the durable state instead of returning `(false, nil)` identically forever. Options (pick one deliberately, this is an ownership boundary — see the in-code comment about ambiguity):
   - After N failed recovery attempts with inconclusive probes, attempt `Destroy` on the source handle (mirroring the `reconcileStartingTarget` precedent at `agent_switching.go:3122-3129`) and confirm the stop; or
   - Treat "server unreachable for the whole daemon lifetime + no supervised process found" as proof-of-death after a deadline (cross-check `IsSupervisedProcessAlive` / process-level evidence where available).
2. **Surface recovery failure to the user.** The async worker only logs (`agent_switching.go:970-975`). The switch row should carry the last recovery attempt's outcome (timestamp + probe result) so the dialog can say "still unconfirmed after N attempts on <date> — restart the daemon or kill the session" instead of a button that appears broken.
3. **Escape hatch.** The dialog offers no path to (a) retry the switch from scratch, (b) roll back to the source harness on demand, or (c) terminate the fenced session. Any one of these would have unblocked the reporter without code changes to the probe logic.

## Impact

- Any terminal-mode Codex→Claude (or Claude→Codex) switch whose source stop ends unconfirmed with a server-level probe error leaves the session **unusable and unrecoverable from the UI** — input locked, no forward path, no rollback.
- Restarting the daemon may help only if the probe can then answer definitively (tmux session truly gone → "can't find session"); if the server stays unreachable the boot reconciliation (`agent_switching.go:~2830`) hits the same `return false, nil` and re-retains the gate.
- Users lose access to a live, preserved native session (2.1M tokens of context in the reported case) with zero in-product recourse.

## Related

- [#3475](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3475) — the tmux probe classification (server-unreachable = inconclusive) that makes path (2) dominant; any fix here must not regress it
- Recovery markers/state machine: `markSourceStopUnconfirmed` (`agent_switching.go:2559`), `RequiresSourceRecovery` gating in `RecoverAgentSwitch` (`agent_switching.go:151`)

## Evidence

- Screen recording (8s): dialog open across the whole recording; "Checking Codex…" → identical state; status chip "Agent switch needs r…" on "review PR 4100"; activity Idle 3m; Codex 2.1M tokens; no toast/error anywhere.
- `agent_switching.go` citations above are identical between local `ed52364e3` and `origin/main` `35ee1fe42` (verified via `git diff`).

title: bug(terminal): selection drag does not auto-scroll — alt-buffer/tmux panes never get the drag-scroll the wheel already routes to them
body:
## Bug

Dragging a text selection past the top or bottom edge of an AO terminal does not auto-scroll the pane. The selection stays active and follows the pointer inside the viewport, but the terminal never scrolls, so a selection can never grow past what is already on screen. Ordinary selection and ordinary wheel scrolling both work.

**Reported by:** @whoisasx (in-app report) | **Analyzed against:** `85fab5e29ff718835a098e55ba598f0a2bc91e20` (`origin/main`)
**AO version:** `ao version dev` (worktree build) · desktop app running from `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app`
**OS:** macOS 26.6 (25G70), arm64 · Darwin 25.6.0 · daemon verified listening on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Confidence:** High — traced to specific lines, reproduced in a real Chromium against the shipped xterm build, and confirmed against real `tmux attach` bytes.

## Reproduction

1. Open any AO session terminal (or shell terminal) with more transcript than fits the pane.
2. Press and hold the left mouse button on a line of terminal text.
3. Drag the pointer above the top edge (or below the bottom edge) of the terminal and hold it there.
4. **Expected:** the pane auto-scrolls and the selection keeps extending.
   **Actual:** nothing scrolls. The highlight stops at the viewport edge.

Wheel scrolling in the same pane works, and click-drag selection inside the pane works.

## Root Cause

`XtermTerminal.tsx` routes the **wheel** away from xterm's local viewport for panes whose scrollback lives in the pane, but nothing does the equivalent for xterm's **selection drag**, so the drag falls through to a scroll path that is a no-op for every AO terminal.

**1. AO terminals are always alternate-screen + mouse-tracking panes.**

`tmux.Runtime.Attach` spawns `tmux -u -T RGB attach-session -t <id>` on a PTY with `TERM=xterm-256color` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:702-756`), and the session is created with `mouse on` (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/commands.go:41`). Capturing that exact attach stream from a real PTY shows tmux immediately driving the client into the alternate screen with SGR mouse tracking on:

```
head: b'\x1b[?1049h\x1b[22;0;0t\x1b[?1h\x1b=\x1b[H\x1b[2J...'
  ALT SCREEN (smcup 1049h): YES
  mouse X11 1000h: YES
  mouse btn-event 1002h: YES
  SGR mouse 1006h: YES
```

Both the agent session terminal and the standalone shell terminals use this adapter (`backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:300` passes the same `runtimeAdapter` into `startShellTerminals`), so on macOS and Linux every AO terminal is an alt-buffer pane whose scrollback belongs to tmux, not to xterm.

**2. xterm's selection drag-scroll only moves xterm's own scrollback.**

`SelectionService._dragScroll()` (`@xterm/xterm@5.5.0` `src/browser/services/SelectionService.ts:665-690`) fires `onRequestScrollLines`, which `Terminal.ts:526` forwards to `Terminal.scrollLines(amount, suppressScrollEvent)` with the default `ScrollSource.TERMINAL`. That reaches `BufferService.scrollLines`, which begins:

```ts
if (disp < 0) {
  if (buffer.ydisp === 0) {
    return;                      // <-- alt buffer: ydisp is permanently 0
  }
  ...
}
buffer.ydisp = Math.max(Math.min(buffer.ydisp + disp, buffer.ybase), 0);
if (oldYdisp === buffer.ydisp) {
  return;                        // <-- alt buffer: ybase is permanently 0
}
```

In the alternate buffer `ybase === ydisp === 0` forever, so the drag-scroll is a guaranteed no-op. tmux never receives anything, because AO does not forward the drag to the PTY (`forceSelectionMode`, `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:260-268` — the same patch behind [#3640](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3640)).

**3. The wheel already solves this; the drag was never given the same route.**

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx:763-805` (`attachCustomWheelEventHandler`) explicitly branches on pane kind: keyboard-scroll panes get `PageUp`/`PageDown`, normal-buffer panes with mouse tracking off get a local `term.scrollLines(lines)`, and mouse-tracking panes get SGR wheel reports that tmux acts on via copy-mode. That is exactly why "normal scrolling works". There is no matching branch anywhere for the selection drag, so it silently keeps using path (2).

### Reproduced in a real Chromium

A harness loading the shipped `@xterm/xterm@5.5.0` build, applying AO's `forceSelectionMode` patch, then synthesizing `mousedown` inside the screen box and `mousemove` 40px above it (held for 600ms, i.e. ~12 of xterm's 50ms drag-scroll ticks):

| case | buffer / mouse tracking | `viewportY` before → after | auto-scrolled |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — plain shell / codex | `normal`, tracking `none` | 377 → 245 | **YES** |
| B — `tmux attach` (every AO terminal on macOS/Linux) | `alternate`, tracking `drag` | 0 → 0 | **NO** |

Case B is set up with the exact sequence tmux sends on attach (`\x1b[?1049h`, `\x1b[?1000h`, `\x1b[?1002h`, `\x1b[?1006h`). Case A proves AO's `forceSelectionMode` patch, the hidden-scrollbar CSS (`frontend/src/renderer/styles.css:1449-1464`) and `removeHiddenScrollbarReservation` do **not** break xterm's native drag-scroll — the failure is entirely the alt-buffer/mouse-tracking routing gap.

## Platform Impact

- **macOS / Linux:** always broken. The runtime adapter is tmux, so both agent session terminals and shell terminals are alt-buffer + mouse-tracking panes.
- **Windows:** the runtime adapter is conpty, not tmux (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty`). A plain shell pane there stays in the normal buffer with mouse tracking off, so xterm's native drag-scroll already works (case A). An agent TUI that enters the alternate screen itself, or that enables mouse tracking, hits the same bug.
- **Not Electron-specific.** The mechanism is pure xterm + buffer state and reproduces in stock Chromium outside Electron; no pointer-capture, drag-region or CSS involvement.

## Impact

- A terminal selection can never exceed one screen of text. Copying a full agent response, a long stack trace, or a multi-screen diff out of the terminal is impossible in one gesture.
- Workaround exists but is clumsy: wheel-scroll to the region first, then select only what is visible, repeat.

## Proposed Fix

Mirror the wheel handler for the selection drag in `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx`:

1. Extract the wheel handler's pane-kind decision into a single helper (`local` / `mouseReport` / `pageKeys`) so the two scroll paths cannot drift.
2. While a left-button selection drag is live and the pointer is outside the `.xterm-screen` box, emit the same bytes the wheel would emit for that many lines, on xterm's own 50ms drag-scroll cadence. Skip it entirely for `local` panes — xterm's native drag-scroll already handles those and emitting would double-scroll them.
3. Track the drag with capture-phase `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners: xterm's own document-level `mousemove` listener calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` while a drag is live (`SelectionService.ts:592-601`), which would drop a bubble-phase listener registered after it.

xterm keeps owning the selection model — its `_dragScroll` re-pins `selectionEnd` to the viewport edge on every tick — so the fix only has to supply the scroll the pane never received.

### Known limitation this does not remove

Over a tmux pane the selection still cannot accumulate *beyond one screen*: xterm's selection anchors are buffer rows, and tmux repaints the alternate screen in place, so scrolling changes the text under a fixed anchor rather than adding rows above it. After the fix the pane scrolls under a live drag and the highlight stays WYSIWYG with what is copied, which is as far as xterm-level selection can go while the scrollback lives in tmux. Genuinely unbounded selection needs the pane's native transcript — that is [#3791](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3791).

## Test Plan

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx`: a selection drag past the edge emits SGR wheel reports on a mouse-tracking pane; emits nothing (and does not double-scroll) on a normal-buffer pane; emits page keys on a keyboard-scroll pane; emits nothing while the pointer stays inside the screen box; stops on `mouseup`; direction follows above vs. below the box.
- Existing wheel tests must stay green unchanged — they pin the exact byte sequences the shared helper now produces.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`, `cd frontend && npm test`.
- Manual: drag-select past the top of a real tmux-backed AO terminal and confirm the pane scrolls; confirm ordinary click-selection, wheel scrolling, right-click menu, and typing are unaffected.

## Related

- [#3640](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3640) — `forceSelectionMode` suppresses mouse reporting to the PTY. Same `forceSelectionMode` patch (`XtermTerminal.tsx:260-268`) is what makes AO's local selection possible over a mouse-tracking pane in the first place, so any change there interacts with this.
- [#3791](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3791) — copy full prompt/response from agent TUIs by reading the native transcript. The proper long-term answer to "select more than one screen".
- [#1221](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1221) — terminal selection offset from the overlay scrollbar mismatch (same selection surface).
- [#1280](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1280) — viewport snapped to bottom on drag-start (closed; same drag-selection surface).

title: fix(session): do not apply a role override's model across harnesses
body:
## The bug

A project role override pins a harness and carries an agent config chosen **for that harness**. `effectiveHarness` already honors an explicit spawn harness, but `effectiveAgentConfig` applied the override's agent config unconditionally.

So in a project whose worker role pins `codex` with a codex model id, an explicit `claude-code` spawn inherited that model id and **launched broken**. Found while exercising two concurrent workers on different harnesses in one project.

## The fix

`Model` and `Mode` are applied only when the resolved harness matches the override's pinned harness. An override with no pinned harness keeps its apply-unconditionally behavior, so existing single-harness projects are unaffected.

Every caller now passes the harness actually resolved for that session — the explicit spawn harness, the durable `rec.Harness` on restore and interface transitions, and the target harness on an agent switch.

## Why `Permissions` stays outside the gate

`PermissionMode` is an abstract enum that each adapter maps onto its own agent's native approval flags, so it is not harness-specific. Skipping it on a mismatch would silently substitute the project baseline for the role's permission — and one direction of that substitution, a role pinning `default` over a baseline of `bypass-permissions`, is a **privilege escalation**.

## On the test

The fixture gives the worker override a permission that differs from the base. That detail is load-bearing: with it unset, every permission assertion passes trivially by reading the base value back, whether or not the override was applied at all.

Verified by reverting the function and confirming the test fails; `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` (including `-race`) are clean.

title: feat(notifications): tell the user when a TUI worker finishes its turn
body:
## The gap

A TUI worker that finishes its task settles in `ActivityIdle` and **no notification fires**, so nothing tells the user the work is done.

## Why not just map end-of-turn to `waiting_input`

That looks like the one-line fix and it is wrong. `ActivityState.NeedsInput()` gates the automation layer:

- `lifecycle/reactions.go` suppresses `ready_to_merge` while it is true — a finished worker that just opened a PR would never raise `ready_to_merge` until the user messaged it again;
- `cannotNudge` suppresses automated nudges the same way.

Both `claudecode` and `codex` map end-of-turn to idle by documented decision. That stays untouched.

## What this adds

A distinct notification kind, `turn_complete`, emitted on the transition into idle. The predicate is deliberately narrow:

- **`prev` is enumerated** (`active` / `waiting_input` / `blocked`) rather than "not idle". `claudecode` maps *both* `stop` and `Notification(idle_prompt)` to idle, so `idle → idle` must not fire twice; `codex` reaches idle from `waiting_input` after a permission round-trip, which an active-only check would miss.
- **`Kind == worker` and `Mode == TUI`.** Chat sessions are also worker-kind, so gating on kind alone would fire on every chat exchange.
- the session is not terminated.

`turn_complete` needs resolution: resolved when the session leaves idle (the user gave it more work) or terminates, mirroring `needsInputResolutions` from all three lifecycle call sites, plus a reconcile query so a daemon crash between the two writes cannot strand one unresolved.

## Two surfaces worth a reviewer's attention

- The `type IN (...)` lists in `storage/sqlite/queries/notifications.sql` are a **hardcoded SQL mirror** of `NotificationType.NeedsResolution()`. Miss them and the notification is created but never appears in the unresolved list or count.
- `notify/enrich.go` rejects any non-`needs_input` intent without a PR URL, and its title/body switches fall through to a `"Notification"` default that still passes `NotificationRecord.Validate()` — so a missing case ships empty copy with a green suite.

## Renderer

Reuses the `needs_input` toast suppression, so no toast fires while the user is already watching that session, and the row routes to the session on click. Copy goes through `t()` with the English string added to every locale catalog, which is the existing pattern for untranslated keys.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test` and `-race` clean on the changed packages; renderer vitest 156 files / 2274 passed; `npm run api` re-run leaves the tree clean, so the committed `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are genuinely generated.

**Not yet observed in a live session** — this is test-verified only. The thing to watch on first real use is volume: `stop` maps to idle, so an interrupted turn notifies too, at one notification per turn. If the list proves noisy, the natural next step is to dedupe on an existing unresolved `turn_complete` for the session.

## Migration: 0107

This PR includes `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0107_notification_turn_complete.sql`. Adding the `turn_complete` type without widening the `notifications.type` CHECK constraint caused every insert of that type to fail with `CHECK constraint failed` — silently, because notification writes are best-effort by design (a failed notification must never fail the lifecycle write that produced it), so the error only surfaced as a warning log. This was found by live observation, not by tests; live-confirmed firing after the fix (one notification per completed turn).

SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place, so 0107 uses the standard table-rebuild pattern: create `notifications_new` with the widened constraint, copy all rows, drop the old table, rename. The four indexes from migrations 0031/0041 are recreated verbatim (`DROP TABLE` takes them with it). The down migration deletes `turn_complete` rows first — they are advisory notifications, not durable state — before restoring the narrower constraint.

0107 claims version **107**, not the next free number at branch time, because upstream has since shipped 0104–0106 while this branch predates them; claiming 107 keeps the rebase onto `upstream/main` collision-free. The claim is registered in the append-only ledger in the same change, per `TestMigrationVersionLedger`.

title: fix(session): escape inconclusive agent switch recovery
body:
## Summary

- close an inconclusive `stopping_source` switch as failed while preserving the source owner and runtime handle
- avoid unsafe teardown retries or source relaunches when the runtime adapter cannot prove liveness
- poll asynchronous source-recovery rows and prefer detailed switch history over a stale workspace projection in the dialog

## Independent triage

The durable boundary in `stopping_source` is earlier than target creation: AO cannot have created the target until the source-stopped transaction commits. A failed source liveness probe therefore does **not** make controller ownership ambiguous; the durable session row still owns the original source harness and handle.

Retrying `Destroy` or relaunching the source is unsafe. In particular, #3475 deliberately classifies tmux server-level failures as inconclusive because the provider process can outlive the tmux server. `Destroy` may also treat a missing server as an already-absent tmux session, which still cannot prove that an orphan provider exited. Relaunching at that point can create two controllers. The same ownership rule applies to ConPTY and other adapters.

The dead-end came from retaining a nonterminal switch gate after that probe error. The safe escape is to terminalize the switch without changing source ownership or guessing liveness. This reopens session operations (including termination/retry) and boot reconciliation automatically releases already-persisted rows after upgrade.

The recovery endpoint returns 202 before its worker settles. The UI previously stopped polling recovery rows, and the dialog only read the compact workspace snapshot, so it could keep rendering the old recovery prompt even after switch history changed. Source recovery rows now poll until terminal, and the dialog prefers the detailed history record for the same switch.

## Tests

- `cd backend && go test ./internal/session_manager -run 'Test(RecoverAgentSwitchReleasesSourceWhenProbeRemainsInconclusive|SwitchAgentMarksAndRecoversUnconfirmedSourceStop|ReconcileAgentSwitchesUsesDurableBoundaries)$' -count=1 -v`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/hooks/useAgentSwitches.test.ts src/renderer/components/SwitchAgentDialog.test.tsx src/renderer/components/TerminalSwitchAgentButton.test.tsx src/renderer/components/CenterPane.test.tsx src/renderer/components/chat/SessionChatSurface.test.tsx`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/session_manager -count=1`
- `git diff --check`

## Risk / intentional omission

This does not guess that an unreachable runtime is dead and does not force-kill or relaunch it. If the underlying adapter is still unavailable, the preserved source controller may remain disconnected, but the durable switch fence is released so the user can terminate or retry without risking a duplicate controller.

Closes #4258

title: feat(board): derive a display status per session
body:
Stacked on #4249 (Kanban column). Review that first; this PR targets its branch and only the last commit is mine.

## Summary
Session presentation is now derived in two explicit stages: pick the `kanbanColumn`, then derive a `displayStatus` **within** that column. Both ship on the session read model; the existing `status` is untouched.

The column answers *where in the lifecycle, and whose turn*. The display status answers *what is happening right now at that stage* — so the card can change from "Review scheduled" to "Reviewing" to "Addressing comments" without the card ever moving lane.

`DisplayStatus` values are phrases, not identifiers (`Fixing CI failures`, `Needs human review`, `Closed without merge`). The frontend prints the string; it keeps no mapping table of its own.

## Derivation

`contract.DeriveKanbanPresentation` replaces `DeriveKanbanColumn` as the entry point. Stage one is the reducer #4249 shipped, unchanged in behaviour except where noted below; stage two switches on the chosen column and reads only that column's facts:

| Column | Priority |
| --- | --- |
| **Building** | Working → Blocked → Exited → No signal → Awaiting PR |
| **Validating** | Blocked → Exited → Fixing CI failures / Checks failing → Addressing comments → Needs review → Review scheduled → Reviewing → Needs review (failed pass) → Review pending (cancelled pass) → Draft |
| **In review** | Checks failing → Changes requested → Needs human review |
| **Ready** | Merged → Closed without merge → Mergeable → Checks failing → Approved |
| **Archive** | Terminated |

Two places where the issue's list and the column reducer disagreed, resolved in favour of what the column actually guarantees:

- **A failed or cancelled pass leaves the head unreviewed.** The issue puts "Needs review (failed run)" and "Review pending (cancelled run)" in Validating, but #4249's `!ReviewRun.Present` rule handed such a head to a person as soon as *any* pass existed, so neither phrase was reachable. The column rule is now `!ReviewRun.Outcome` — a pass that produced no verdict does not end AO's validation cycle. New `Outcome` fact, set from `ReviewVerdict.Valid()`.
- **"Addressing comments" belongs to Validating, whichever side asked.** AO fixing *external* feedback is `aoOwnsNextStep`, so the column is already Validating; the In-review branch for it in the issue's list is unreachable by construction and is not implemented. Validating's rule covers AO-side and external changes requests alike.

Ready checks Merged/Closed before merge-readiness: a merged PR's stale `mergeability` must not report "Mergeable" over the merge that actually happened.

`KanbanSessionFacts` now embeds `SessionFacts` rather than re-declaring `IsTerminated`, so Building and Validating read the same worker facts `DeriveStatus` does — including the no-signal rule, extracted to `silentPastGrace` and shared by both reducers instead of written twice.

## Freshness

Review-run currency is enforced in SQL by #4249: `ListCurrentHeadReviewRunsBySession` joins on `target_sha = pr.head_sha`, so a pass recorded for an earlier commit never reaches the reducer, and `Review scheduled` / `Reviewing` / `Needs review` always describe the current head.

**CI needs no equivalent guard.** `pr.ci_state` and `pr.head_sha` are columns of a single `UpsertPR` statement written from one provider observation, and `ClaimPRForSession`'s upsert does not touch `ci_state` — so the stored aggregate cannot describe a commit other than the stored head. An earlier revision of this PR added a `ci_at_current_head` column to defend that case; it was removed as unreachable, and because it cost a correlated subquery per PR on the session-list read.

## Multiple PRs

Unchanged selection: per-PR column, ranked (ready > needs review > validating > building), ties on newest then URL. The display status then reads **the winning PR's** facts, so a merged PR cannot narrate a session whose other PR is still having its CI fixed.

## Frontend

`displayStatus` is plumbed through `useWorkspaceQuery` → `WorkspaceSession` → the board card, which prints it in place of the status badge's label. Precedence is `agent-switch presentation → displayStatus → status badge`: the switch overlay is a transient, more specific state and still wins. A daemon too old to send one falls back to the translated status label, as today.

**Known gap:** `displayStatus` arrives in English from the daemon, which is what the issue's phrase-valued API specifies; the eight renderer locales do not cover it. The fallback keeps older daemons translated, but a current daemon shows English phrases to every locale. Worth a follow-up before the Figma visual treatment lands — either a client-side phrase→key map or identifier values plus a label table.

## Tests
- `go test ./...` (backend, all packages), `golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `gofmt -l .` clean
- `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run src/renderer` in `frontend` (1921 passed); `npm test` in `packages/product-ui`
- New coverage: reducer table tests for every phrase in every column, terminated, multi-PR selection, and "a PR keeps the card out of Building"; column tests for the failed/cancelled-pass rule; a real-SQLite test for `ci_at_current_head` across no-checks / current-head / pushed-since cases; service tests for the derived phrase and for a stale CI aggregate; an API test asserting `displayStatus` on the wire; board and query tests for rendering and hydration.

## Issue
- Closes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4179

title: fix(terminal): auto-scroll the pane while a selection drag is held
body:
Fixes #4265

## Summary

Dragging a text selection past the top/bottom edge of an AO terminal did not auto-scroll the pane, so a selection could never grow past what was already on screen. Ordinary selection and ordinary wheel scrolling both worked.

xterm's built-in selection drag-scroll (`SelectionService._dragScroll`) fires `onRequestScrollLines` → `Terminal.scrollLines` → `BufferService.scrollLines`, which only moves lines xterm holds in its **own** scrollback:

```ts
if (disp < 0) { if (buffer.ydisp === 0) return; }
buffer.ydisp = Math.max(Math.min(buffer.ydisp + disp, buffer.ybase), 0);
if (oldYdisp === buffer.ydisp) return;
```

Every AO terminal on macOS/Linux is a `tmux attach-session` client (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:702`, and `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:300` gives shell terminals the same adapter). Capturing that attach stream from a real PTY shows tmux immediately driving the client into the alternate screen with SGR mouse tracking on:

```
b'\x1b[?1049h\x1b[22;0;0t\x1b[?1h\x1b=\x1b[H\x1b[2J...'
  ALT SCREEN (1049h): YES   mouse 1000h/1002h/1006h: YES
```

In the alternate buffer `ybase === ydisp === 0` forever, so `scrollLines` is a guaranteed no-op and the pane sits still under a live drag. tmux never hears about it either, because AO does not forward the drag to the PTY (`forceSelectionMode`, the patch behind #3640).

The **wheel** already solved exactly this: `attachCustomWheelEventHandler` branches on pane kind and reports to the pane rather than scrolling locally. That is why "normal scrolling works". The selection drag was simply never given the same route.

## What changed

`frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx`

- Extracted the wheel handler's pane-kind decision into `paneScrollMode()` (`local` / `mouseReport` / `pageKeys`) and its emission into `paneScrollReport()`, so both scroll gestures read one decision and cannot drift apart again. **Wheel behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged** — the existing wheel tests pin those bytes and pass untouched.
- A left-button selection drag held outside the `.xterm-screen` box now emits the same bytes the wheel would for that many lines, on xterm's own 50ms drag cadence.
  - `local` panes (codex, a plain shell, a Windows conpty shell) are **skipped** — xterm's built-in drag-scroll already moves their scrollback, so emitting would scroll them twice.
  - `pageKeys` panes get one page key every 8th tick; one per tick would be twenty screens a second.
  - Distance→speed curve mirrors xterm's own `DRAG_SCROLL_MAX_THRESHOLD`, with the speed cap at 3 instead of 15 because each line becomes a report the *pane* acts on and tmux copy-mode moves 5 lines per report. Measured against a real tmux PTY: 3 reports/tick ≈ 14 lines/tick, i.e. this lands back on xterm's native full-speed drag rate rather than 5× past it.
- Drag tracking uses **capture-phase** `mousemove`/`mouseup` on `window`: xterm's own document-level `mousemove` listener calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` for the whole duration of a drag, which would silently drop a bubble-phase listener.
- Teardown removes the `mousedown` listener and calls `stopSelectionDragScroll()`, so a terminal disposed mid-drag leaves no window listeners or interval behind.

xterm keeps owning the selection model — its `_dragScroll` re-pins `selectionEnd` to the viewport edge every tick — so this only supplies the scroll the pane never received.

## Verification

**Reproduced the bug in a real Chromium** against the shipped `@xterm/xterm@5.5.0` build with AO's `forceSelectionMode` patch applied, synthesizing a held drag 40px above the screen box for 600ms:

| case | buffer / mouse tracking | `viewportY` before → after | auto-scrolled |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — plain shell / codex | `normal`, tracking `none` | 377 → 245 | **YES** |
| B — `tmux attach` (every AO terminal on macOS/Linux) | `alternate`, tracking `drag` | 0 → 0 | **NO** |

Case A proves `forceSelectionMode`, the hidden-scrollbar CSS and `removeHiddenScrollbarReservation` do **not** break xterm's native drag-scroll — the failure was entirely the routing gap. Not Electron-specific.

**Verified the fix's output against a live tmux.** Writing exactly what the fix emits per tick (`\x1b[<64;1;1M` × 3) into a real `tmux attach` PTY, six ticks apart:

```
attached; visible markers: (478, 500)
after 6 drag ticks; markers repainted: (393, 491)
tmux pane_in_mode: 1   scroll_position: 85
```

The pane enters copy-mode and scrolls back 85 lines — the scroll the drag never used to produce.

**Tests** (`npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts`):
- `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — 64 passed, 7 new: auto-scrolls a mouse-tracking pane on a held drag; correct direction above vs. below the box; keeps ticking while held and stops on `mouseup`; does **not** fire while the pointer stays inside the box; does **not** fire without a selection (click-and-hold never moves the pane); leaves `local` panes to xterm instead of double-scrolling; paces page keys for keyboard-scroll panes.
- `TerminalPane.test.tsx`, `ShellTerminalTab.test.tsx`, `useTerminalSession.test.tsx` — 98 passed, unchanged.
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — clean on the implementation.

## Known limitation (not introduced here, not removed here)

Over a tmux pane the selection still cannot accumulate *beyond one screen*: xterm's selection anchors are buffer rows and tmux repaints the alternate screen in place, so scrolling changes the text under a fixed anchor rather than adding rows above it. After this change the pane scrolls under a live drag and the highlight stays WYSIWYG with what gets copied — as far as xterm-level selection can go while the scrollback lives in tmux. Genuinely unbounded selection needs the pane's native transcript: #3791.

## Risk / follow-ups

- The minimum drag speed is ~100 lines/s (1 report/tick × tmux's 5 lines) versus xterm's local 20 lines/s, because tmux's lines-per-wheel-report is not something this layer controls. Fine-grained control right at the edge is coarser than on a `local` pane; worth a tuning pass if it feels fast in practice.
- Windows (conpty) is untested on hardware. A plain conpty shell stays a `local` pane and is unaffected by this change; a conpty agent TUI that enables mouse tracking takes the new `mouseReport` path.

## Related

- #3640 — `forceSelectionMode` suppresses mouse reporting to the PTY. Same patch that makes local selection possible over a mouse-tracking pane, so changes there interact with this.
- #3791 — copy full prompt/response by reading the agent's native transcript.
- #1221 — terminal selection offset from the overlay scrollbar mismatch.
- Separate from the non-terminal UI text-selection issue being triaged in parallel; no shared code — that one is app-chrome CSS, this one is xterm scroll routing.

title: fix(desktop): restore text selection outside the terminal
body:
Fixes #4268

## Summary

`body { user-select: none }` — added by [PR #3508](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3508) to stop drags from painting a highlight over sidebar/board chrome — inherits into every descendant. Nothing outside `input`/`textarea`/`[contenteditable]` and the terminal could be selected or copied: session details, status text, error messages, PR metadata. It also left the Files-tab diff selection menu unreachable, since `SessionFilesView` gates that menu on a live DOM selection inside a container that had no `select-text`.

This restores the selectable default and moves #3508's intent into an explicit opt-out list for controls and drag surfaces, so chrome behaves exactly as it does today.

## Changes

- `frontend/src/renderer/styles.css` — drop `user-select: none` from `body`; add an opt-out for `button`, `summary`, `select`, `[role="button"]`, the `data-slot` control set, `[data-slot="resize-handle"]`, and the sidebar menu buttons.
- `packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.tsx` — `select-none` on **interactive** board cards only. The card is the click target and a drag ending inside it still fires `click`, so a drag-select there would open the session. Non-interactive (archive) cards stay selectable.
- `frontend/e2e/text-selection.spec.ts` — new.
- `packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.test.tsx` — card contract test.

`a[href]` is deliberately **not** in the opt-out: links sit inside prose (chat transcript, review markdown), and `user-select: none` on them punches holes in a copied paragraph.

## Deliberately unchanged

- **Terminal** — `xterm.css` sets `.xterm { user-select: none }` itself, so xterm owns terminal selection regardless of the `body` value.
- **Titlebar / drag regions** — `.window-titlebar` and `.session-inspector__topbar` already carry their own `user-select: none`.
- **Resize drags** — `body.is-resizing-x { user-select: none }` still suppresses selection for the duration of a drag.
- **Marketing site** — `frontend/src/landing/.../globals.css` keeps its own rule; out of scope.

One behavior change worth flagging: board **column headers** ("WORKING", counts) are now selectable. They are not interactive, so there is no conflict, but #3508's description mentioned them. Happy to add `select-none` there if reviewers prefer the old look.

## Verification

Run on macOS 26.6 (arm64) against `85fab5e29`.

- `frontend/e2e/text-selection.spec.ts` — **3 passed**. Drives real mouse drags and reads `window.getSelection()`:
  - inspector body copy selects and reaches the clipboard over the ordinary Copy shortcut
  - board card drag selects nothing and navigates nowhere
  - buttons, `[data-sidebar="menu-button"]`, and `[data-slot="resize-handle"]` compute `user-select: none`
  - `.xterm` still computes `user-select: none`
- **Non-vacuous check** — reverted `styles.css` to `origin/main` and reran: the content-selection case fails, the two chrome cases still pass. Restored and reran: all 3 pass.
- `packages/product-ui` — `SessionsBoardView.test.tsx` **7 passed**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `frontend` — `tsc --noEmit` clean; `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.e2e.json` clean.
- `SessionsBoard.test.tsx` **38 passed**, `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` + `SessionFilesView.test.tsx` pass (one archive-expansion timeout appeared only under a 3-file parallel run and reproduces on `origin/main` without this change; passes in isolation both with and without it).

## Gaps

- **Windows/Linux unverified.** `user-select` is platform-independent Chromium CSS and the rule has no platform guard, so no divergence is expected — but neither was exercised.
- Verified through the `dev:web` renderer harness, not a packaged Electron build. The `-webkit-app-region` drag strip is untouched by this diff, but a packaged smoke test would confirm the titlebar directly.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: `frontend/e2e/multi-pr.spec.ts` fails on `origin/main` — its "auth stack" fixture is gone from the mock dataset. Not touched here.

## Related

- [#4265](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4265) — terminal selection drag auto-scroll. Separate subsystem (xterm owns its selection); no shared code with this change.

- Project drop targets are the top and bottom edges of complete project blocks.
- Sessions reorder only within their own project and animate their siblings during drag.
