title: feat(files): bulk/queued inline feedback in file & diff viewer — annotate multiple lines, review batch, send together
body:
## Feature Description

> Scope (clarified by requester): the **file viewer / file diff viewer** in the desktop app — session inspector → Files tab (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFilesView.tsx`).

Today inline review feedback is strictly **one-at-a-time**:

- Clicking annotate on a file row or diff line opens a **single** draft composer (`beginAnnotation`).
- Submitting **immediately** sends exactly one formatted message via `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` — `formatFileAnnotationMessage` packages the feedback with file context (path, side, line numbers, diff line kind, quoted code).
- The composer then shows sending → sent and auto-closes (~1.2 s). The model holds one target and one draft; there is no way to queue a second annotation before the first is sent.

Reviewing a real changeset usually produces feedback on **several lines across several files**. The user must repeat the full click → type → submit cycle for each one, and the agent receives N separate messages, each triggering its own delivery/confirmation cycle.

## Proposed Behavior

- **Queue multiple annotations** in one review pass: annotate line A in file 1, line B in file 2, all of file 3, …
- **Batch review step** before sending: a list of pending annotations (path + line + feedback text), each editable and removable.
- **Bulk send** delivers the batch, either:
  - one combined message — numbered feedback items, each carrying its file-context block — or
  - sequential queued deliveries, one per annotation.
- **Per-item status** (queued / sending / sent / error), with retry for failed items.

## Implementation Notes

- The browser panel already has a queueing pattern to reuse: `useBrowserAnnotationQueue` serializes annotation sends while the session is working and **keeps failed annotations queued for retry**. The file viewer could adopt the same model.
- If batching into a single message, respect `MAX_FILE_ANNOTATION_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (4096): split into multiple messages or truncate per item rather than silently dropping context.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep one-at-a-time sends and let the user stack messages manually — still N delivery/confirmation cycles, no batch review or edit before send.

---

Requested by @phylolver in the AO Discord (#feature-requests). Scope clarified in-thread: this is about the file viewer / file diff viewer annotation flow.

title: fix(desktop): embed tmux terminfo fallback
body:
Fixes #4382

## Summary

- build ncurses's matching `tic` and `infocmp` tools, then embed the pinned `xterm-256color` entry into the static libtinfo used by bundled tmux
- avoid host `pkg-config` dependency by pointing tmux directly at AO's pinned static utf8proc archive
- replace the version-only artifact check with a real pseudo-terminal attach while `HOME`, `TERMINFO`, and `TERMINFO_DIRS` point to nonexistent paths
- bump the native build revision so release jobs cannot reuse the broken cached artifact
- preserve pre-bundling TUI sessions by using the system tmux client for the legacy default socket while retaining AO's bundled client for the private `ao` socket
- pin every migrated legacy probe, command, and PTY attach to `-L default`, preventing inherited `TMUX` from redirecting AO to a nested or unrelated server
- distinguish conclusively absent infrastructure from an inconclusive legacy inspection: missing clients, protocol mismatches, and transient connection failures now return `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, which boot/restart/reaper paths cannot treat as session death or permission to create a replacement

## Upgrade-path coverage

- **Pre-regression → fixed:** legacy sessions are discovered and operated through the system tmux from `PATH`, avoiding tmux client/server protocol mismatches with AO's pinned bundled version. All legacy operations explicitly target the historical `default` socket. New sessions use the private socket and bundled client.
- **Broken nightly → fixed:** existing private-socket sessions continue through the bundled client, while the new app version stages the fixed binary at its own durable versioned path.
- **Mixed state:** exact private-socket probing remains first; sessions absent there are classified against the pinned legacy socket. The selected socket/client pair is cached for every subsequent operation.
- Only a conclusive `no server running` result is recoverable infrastructure absence. A missing/incompatible client or transient `error connecting` result preserves the existing controller and propagates an actionable, inconclusive error.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm run build:tmux` (macOS arm64; real PTY attach passed with no host terminfo database)
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run forge.config.test.ts src/shared/bundled-tmux.test.ts` (12 tests passed)
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`
- clean AO environment: `npm run lint` (all Go tests and golangci-lint passed)
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux ./internal/session_manager`
- repeated tmux runtime package integration suite (`-count=3`)
- live protocol compatibility on macOS arm64:
  - system tmux 3.6b successfully queried the 16-session legacy default-socket server
  - bundled tmux 3.5a reproduced `server exited unexpectedly` against that server
  - bundled tmux 3.5a successfully queried the 11-session private `ao`-socket server
- real three-server integration regression:
  - creates isolated `default`, private `ao`, and spoof sockets
  - injects `TMUX` pointing at the spoof server with a colliding session namespace
  - verifies AO adopts the real default-socket session and rejects the spoof-only session
- unit regressions cover unavailable legacy client, incompatible-client output, transient legacy `error connecting`, client routing, and explicit `-L default` PTY attachment
- session-manager regressions prove boot reconciliation and explicit restart propagate inconclusive legacy probes without Create, Restart, Destroy, termination, or workspace changes
- `otool -L frontend/tmux/bin/tmux` (system libraries only)

## Risk

The terminfo fallback is intentionally limited to `xterm-256color`, which is the exact terminal AO forces for bundled tmux attachments. Legacy default-socket sessions depend on a compatible system tmux remaining available from the daemon's inherited `PATH`, matching the dependency that created those pre-bundling sessions. If it is unavailable or incompatible, the session and controller are preserved and AO surfaces an inconclusive runtime error; it is not archived, destroyed, or duplicated. Linux and macOS Intel release artifacts still need to pass their native release-runner attach smoke tests.

title: feat(files): GitHub-style "Viewed" checkboxes on files in the session diff viewer
body:
## Feature Description

Add GitHub-style **"Viewed" checkboxes** to the file list in the session inspector's Files tab (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFilesView.tsx`), so users can track review progress across a changeset.

Parity target: GitHub's PR file tree — each file row gets a checkbox; checking it marks the file as reviewed and (on GitHub) collapses it; review progress is visible at a glance.

## Current Behavior

- The Files tab lists changed files with expand/collapse for diffs, but holds **no review state at all** — `expandedPaths` is plain component state that resets every time the view remounts.
- Reviewing a 20-file changeset means keeping mental (or external) track of which files you've already gone over. Nothing in the UI records it.

## Proposed Behavior

- **Per-file "Viewed" checkbox** on each file row (file tree and/or flat list).
- **Progress summary** — e.g. "7 / 12 files viewed" — near the filter control; optionally a filter toggle to show only unviewed files.
- **Persistence**: viewed state should survive view remounts and app restarts for the lifetime of a review pass. Options (open design question):
  - renderer-local (localStorage keyed by session + file path) — simplest, no API/contract changes;
  - daemon-side per session — syncs across devices, but adds storage + API surface.
- **Invalidation**: if the file's diff changes (agent pushes new commits), the viewed mark should be cleared or flagged as stale — otherwise a "viewed" check on an outdated diff is a false green. GitHub does this when the file content changes.
- Keyboard-friendly: `j`/`k` already move focus between file rows; the checkbox should be reachable/toggleable from that flow (Enter/Space already expand rows — e.g. `v` to toggle viewed, or checkbox is a tab stop).

## Relationship to Other Issues

- Complements #4384 (bulk/queued inline feedback in the same viewer) — together they turn the Files tab into a real review surface: walk files, mark viewed, queue feedback, send in batch.

## Alternatives Considered

- Collapse-as-reviewed heuristic (files you expanded and collapsed count as viewed) — implicit, error-prone, can't be un-done deliberately.

---

Requested by @phylolver in the AO Discord (#feature-requests).

title: fix(topbar): surface the real reason when opening an editor fails
body:
## Summary

Opening a session whose worktree is gone (terminated, merged, cleaned up) put
Electron's IPC plumbing straight into the topbar actions row:

> Error invoking remote method 'editorHandoff:open': Error: Session workspace is not available

Reproduced against real local data, where 27 of the first 40 sessions have no
resolvable workspace (`/api/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/workspace` returns 404).

## What was wrong

Two separate things, and the guard that exists is not the problem.

`TopbarOpenEditorButton` already disables itself when `getState` reports
`workspaceAvailable: false`, and that works. Confirmed live: on a terminated
session the control is disabled with the tooltip "Session workspace is not
available".

What bites is staleness. `useEditorHandoffState` caches with
`staleTime: 10_000` and nothing invalidated it on failure, so a worktree that
disappears *after* the state was read leaves the button enabled. The click
fails, the state is never refreshed, and the button stays enabled to fail again.

Separately, the message shown was raw plumbing.
`TopbarOpenEditorButton.tsx` rendered `open.error.message` verbatim, which is
Electron's wrapper around anything an `ipcMain` handler throws.

## The fix

Renderer-side, in `useEditorHandoff.ts`:

- Strip the `Error invoking remote method '<channel>': Error:` wrapper and
  rethrow a clean error, so the topbar shows what the main process actually
  said. This covers the other failure paths too, which were equally buried:
  "That editor is not installed", "Could not open <name>".
- Invalidate the handoff state query on error so the control re-checks
  availability rather than inviting the same failing click.

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed in the running desktop app against real session data, not
just in tests. Before: the raw wrapper. After: the disabled control carries the
clean reason as its tooltip.

Five unit tests on the normalizer plus a component regression test that clicks
through and asserts the rendered alert. The regression test is not vacuous:
with both changes reverted it fails with `expected 'Error invoking remote
method...' not to contain 'Error invoking remote method'`.

Full frontend suite: 2867 tests across 217 files. Typecheck clean.

## Notes for review

The code being fixed came from commit 728400ca8 in #3284, which replaced an
earlier HTTP implementation with this IPC one. I did not write it, so a look
from its author is worth having.

This treats the symptom in the renderer. Arguably `open()` in
`frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts` should also resolve the workspace inside
its `try`/`catch` so the failure comes back as a friendly message at the source
rather than as a raw throw. Left alone to keep this change narrow; happy to
fold it in.

title: fix(acp): accept stdio MCP servers without an optional MCP capability
body:
## What

Delete the blanket MCP capability gate in the ACP driver so **stdio** MCP servers are accepted regardless of `mcp_capabilities`, while `http` and `sse` stay gated on theirs.

## Why

Fixes #4380.

`normalizeMCPServers` refused **every** per-session MCP server unless the agent advertised one of `mcp_capabilities.acp` / `.http` / `.sse`. stdio is the baseline transport the ACP spec requires every agent to implement — the schema text on `McpServer.Stdio` in the vendored `acp-go-sdk@v0.13.5` (`types_gen.go:2718`) is **"All Agents MUST support this transport"** — so an agent advertising `mcpCapabilities: {}`, the normal shape for a stdio-only agent, was refused the one transport it is guaranteed to speak. Both entry points were affected: `Start` (`driver.go:158`) and `Resume` (`driver.go:242`).

**Severity, stated honestly: this is latent today, not user-visible.** No production caller populates `StartConfig.MCPServers` — `ChatMCPServerConfig{}` is constructed only in `driver_test.go`, and the sites in `internal/service/chat/{service,history}.go` merely forward `cfg.MCPServers`. So `normalizeMCPServers` currently receives an empty slice and returns at the `len(configs) == 0` early exit. I noted this on the issue as a correction to my own initial report.

The argument for landing it now is that it is a three-line deletion, and the MCP wiring work would otherwise be built on top of a gate that silently refuses the mandatory transport — with two existing tests asserting that refusal is correct, so it would read as intentional to whoever adds the wiring.

## How

Three things showed the gate was a coarse "does this agent do MCP at all" proxy rather than a real capability check:

- the transport switch immediately below already gates itself: `case "http"` checks `caps.Http`, `case "sse"` checks `caps.Sse`, and `case "", "stdio"` deliberately checks nothing — which is correct;
- **`caps.Acp` had no other use in the function.** There is no `case "acp"` at all, so an acp-typed config falls through to `default: unsupported ACP MCP transport`. The gate consulted a capability whose transport this code cannot construct, and which the SDK marks **UNSTABLE**;
- the existing test said so out loud: *"any MCP capability is sufficient — the transport-specific check happens later."*

**Docs:** `docs/harnesses/pi.md` documented a per-harness contract — that a session configured with per-session MCP servers is *rejected* during ACP setup rather than silently ignored — and that rejection had exactly one implementation: this gate. pi never had MCP-specific code; it inherited the refusal as a side effect. That row is corrected to describe what actually happens, and flags the resulting gap explicitly rather than papering over it. Deliberately **not** fixed here: giving pi a real per-harness refusal is a product decision and a feature, not part of a spec-conformance bugfix — happy to open a follow-up if you want that behaviour back.

## Testing

Tests were written **before** the fix and confirmed failing on unfixed source, then passing.

- `TestNormalizeMCPServersAllowsStdioWithoutCapabilities` — inverts the old `…FailsWithoutCapabilities`, which asserted the bug was intended behaviour.
- `TestNormalizeMCPServersDefaultTypeIsStdio` — the omitted-type spelling, also stdio.
- `TestNormalizeMCPServersStillGatesNonBaselineTransports` — 4-case table pinning the other half of the contract: http/sse refused without their capability **and** accepted with it, each asserting the correct `McpServer` union arm so a regression routing http into the `Stdio` arm cannot pass.
- `TestACPDriverSendsStdioMCPServersToSpecMinimalAgent` — driver-level: a fake agent advertising `AgentCapabilities{}` receives the stdio server through the real `Start` and `session/load` paths, so the fix is proven end to end rather than only at the helper.

The misleading `…SucceedsWithHttpCapability` case was replaced; its comment stated the model this change corrects.

```console
$ go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/...      # 15 packages
ok
$ go test -race ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/...
ok
$ go vet ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/...
$ golangci-lint v2.12.2 run ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/...
0 issues.
```

Full backend suite is green apart from two failures that reproduce identically on unmodified `main` on this machine and are unrelated to this change: `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` (the tmux base-index bug, #4222 / #4224) and `TestCopilotClassicPATIsNotAnAuthorizationSignal` (fails whenever a classic GitHub PAT is present in the environment).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (based on `c9a0adb21`)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go test`, `-race`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`)

title: Packaged tmux can read and control user-owned tmux state
body:
## Bug

The packaged macOS/Linux app invokes AO's bundled tmux binary, but the runtime is not fully isolated from tmux state owned by the user.

**Source:** User report and follow-up design discussion in an AO task on 2026-08-24/25 (no public chat URL)
**Analyzed against:** `5e408467b`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P1 — a socket collision can direct AO input, restart, or destroy operations at a user-owned tmux session.

## Reproduction

1. Start a user tmux server using the named socket `tmux -L ao`, or keep a same-named session on the default server.
2. Configure `~/.tmux.conf` with options/hooks that are inappropriate for AO.
3. Launch packaged AO and create or restore a TUI session.
4. Observe that AO uses the fixed `-L ao` namespace, allows a newly started server to load user configuration, and probes the default tmux socket when the AO-named server does not contain a matching session.

A custom `TMUX_TMPDIR` also changes where `-L ao` resolves, so the apparently private namespace is still controlled by inherited host environment.

## Root Cause

- `frontend/src/main.ts` injects the constant `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME=ao`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go` invokes tmux with `-L ao`, without an explicit `-f` configuration.
- The adapter caches socket discovery in memory and falls back to the machine default socket using only a matching session name as evidence.
- The tmux control process inherits a surrounding `TMUX` identity.
- `backend/internal/tmuxbin/resolve.go` may fall through to a PATH tmux if a recognizable packaged layout is missing its bundled sibling.

## Fix

- Derive a stable absolute socket path from the daemon run-file identity and use `-S` for every tmux operation.
- Keep the socket inode beside the run file; use a bounded, validated `/tmp` directory alias only when macOS's AF_UNIX path ceiling requires it.
- Pass `-f /dev/null` so AO never loads system/user tmux configuration or plugins.
- Remove automatic named/default socket discovery; every control operation stays on the AO-private socket.
- Remove only tmux identity/internal selector variables while preserving the user's workload environment, and refresh that environment for every new or respawned pane.
- Fail closed when a packaged daemon's bundled tmux is missing.
- Keep Windows on the existing ConPTY adapter.

## Impact

- User tmux servers and AO can collide across socket namespaces.
- AO may inherit user hooks/plugins/options and fail unpredictably.
- A stale AO handle plus a same-named user session can cause AO to operate on foreign state.
- Machines without system tmux should continue to work through the bundled artifact; the terminfo regression in that artifact is tracked separately.

## Related

- [Issue #4382](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4382) / [PR #4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385) — bundled tmux terminfo artifact failure.
- [PR #4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293) — introduced bundled tmux and the fixed `-L ao` namespace.
- [Issue #2662](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2662) / [PR #2664](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2664) — broader cross-data-dir session namespace collision.

title: fix(updates): prevent stuck manual check loader
body:
Regression follow-up to #4284. This replaces the update-card styling approach attempted in #4292; the two UI diffs should not be merged together.

## Summary

- consume every updater status push before React can batch away an intermediate terminal event
- clear a manual check only from its matching request ID, while preserving a previously staged update
- simplify the status card and keep long Nightly versions readable with aligned actions
- cover the real main-process event order, the renderer race, and the reported downloaded + Nightly geometry

## Root cause

With an update already staged, a failed manual manifest check can publish these statuses synchronously:

1. `error` for the current manual request ID
2. restored `downloaded` state carrying the earlier staged request ID

The fix in #4285 cleared local loading from a React effect that only observed the latest committed status. React batches both pushes, so the matching terminal event could be discarded before that effect ran. The local request ID stayed set and forced the card back to `checking` forever, even though the updater had restored a valid downloaded state.

`useUpdateStatus` now exposes a lossless per-event callback. `UpdatesSection` uses it to clear only the matching manual request before updating the rendered snapshot, so the following staged status renders normally.

The new renderer regression test failed against the old implementation with `Checking for updates…` where `Downloaded. Restart to finish updating.` was expected.

## Visual evidence

This deterministic renderer state matches the report: dark mode, automatic updates enabled, Nightly selected, a staged download, and the long installed Nightly version. The Playwright test also asserts that the version stays on one line and both actions have equal height.

![Settings Updates after: downloaded Nightly state with readable version and aligned actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pr-assets-update-loader-lost-status/.issue-assets/update-loader-lost-status/after-dark.png)

The screenshot is visual-state evidence. The updater behavior itself is proven separately by the main-process producer test and renderer regression test.

## Native Electron verification

The branch was launched in the real Electron app with isolated AO data and the real preload bridge. Settings → Updates rendered correctly, and clicking **Check for updates** completed with `Updates are only available in the installed app.`, leaving the button enabled and `aria-busy=false`.

Unpackaged Electron intentionally has no release feed, so the exact packaged staged-update sequence is reproduced at its two real boundaries in tests rather than claimed from the screenshot.

## Tests

- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run` — 218 files passed; 2,875 tests passed; 1 skipped
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/main/auto-updater.test.ts` — 152 passed
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed
- `cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/updates-settings.spec.ts --reporter=line` — passed
- `cd frontend && npm run package` — production Electron package completed

- derive a stable per-run-file private tmux socket, force an empty tmux config, and never probe or adopt user/default tmux state

title: feat(observability): wire Sentry DSNs into desktop + mobile builds
body:
## What

Bakes the two Sentry DSNs as committed default constants, mirroring how `DEFAULT_POSTHOG_PROJECT_KEY` already ships, so **nightly and stable both pick them up with no CI or secret setup**. Client DSNs are write-only ingest endpoints; volume is bounded by each project's Sentry-side spike protection + rate limit (both enabled: 300 events/min).

Two separate Sentry projects (`ao-desktop`, `ao-mobile`) so desktop and mobile crash waves, quotas, and native symbolication stay independent.

## Changes

- `shared/sentry-config.ts` (desktop) and `packages/mobile/lib/sentry-config.ts` (mobile) hold the two project DSNs.
- Fallbacks: renderer `VITE_AO_SENTRY_DSN`, Electron main + daemon `AO_SENTRY_DSN`, and mobile `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` all fall back to the baked constant; an explicit env still wins.
- `main.ts` stamps `AO_SENTRY_DSN` onto the spawned daemon env (**off in dev**, matching the PostHog remote gate), so the Go daemon — whose `sentry-go` SDK is already compiled in via #4346 — captures 5xx and panics on the next non-dev build.
- **Privacy:** `daemon.go` now gates `sentryobs.Init` on `cfg.Telemetry.Events`, the same consent switch as the remote telemetry sink, so a user who turned telemetry off never has daemon faults reported even though a DSN is now baked in.

## Activation status

| Surface | State |
|---|---|
| **Daemon (Go)** | **Live on next non-dev build** — SDK vendored (#4346), activates from the env stamp. This is where the ~230k INTERNAL_ERROR 500s originate. |

title: fix(updates): make the sidebar update row actionable and surface a failing updater
body:
## How it looks Sidebar footer, expanded. Captured from the real component driven by real click handlers. | Available (was inert, now downloads on click) | Downloading | | --- | --- | | | | | Staged (unchanged) | Checks failing (was blank) | | --- | --- | | | | The staged shot shows the pre-existing truncation noted under "Out of scope": `v0.12.8-nightly.202608…` loses the word "ready". The available row no longer does, which is the third commit here. Images live on the `assets/pr-4397` branch so they stay out of this diff; it can be deleted once this merges. ## Context Two problems that together made the sidebar's update affordance look like it had been removed. **The available state was a dead end.** Since #4285 the sidebar renders `available` as an inert `
` rather than a button. A manual check leaves `autoDownload` off, so a build discovered that way never advances to the `downloaded` state that carries the click action. The row announces an update and offers nothing to act on. **A failing updater was invisible.** The sidebar returned `null` for `idle`, `checking`, `not-available` and `error`, and automatic check failures were never broadcast at all (`restoreAutomaticCheckPreviousStatus()` returns without sending a status). The one safety net could not help: `staleCheckNudge` needs three consecutive `net::ERR_*` failures, and `recordAutomaticCheckFailure` resets that counter on any non-net error, so the manifest 404 that actually strands a nightly install never trips it. A stranded install and a healthy one were pixel-for-pixel identical. Separately, automatic nightly checks used electron-updater's plain GitHub provider, which discovers prereleases through `releases.atom`. The repo already had an API-based resolver for the newest release carrying a manifest, but only manual checks used it. ## What changed - `available` is a button in both the expanded row and the collapsed icon rail; clicking it downloads. `downloading` stays informational with the percentage; `downloaded` keeps the existing restart action and escalation treatment. - A second failure counter that does not care *why* a check failed. Past three in a row the status carries `checksFailing` and is broadcast once per streak, and the sidebar turns that into a retry row that runs a manual check. Settings gets a matching line. - Automatic nightly checks resolve the release tag through the same API helper manual checks use, failing open to the normal provider so rate limits or an outage cannot break checks. Only nightly takes the extra await, so other channels keep their existing event ordering. Two deliberate non-changes: - The suppressed automatic failure still does not overwrite the state. An error the user never asked for must not replace a truthful `idle`/`not-available`, so only the flag rides along. - The retry row ranks **below** a staged build. An update ready to install is more actionable than "checks are failing". A test covers the ordering. ## Tests - `auto-updater.test.ts`: the automatic nightly check skips an in-progress release and points the feed at the newest one with a manifest, then restores the normal provider; the failing-check streak is announced once rather than once per failure; the streak clears as soon as a check reaches an answer. Each was confirmed to fail without the production change. - `Sidebar.test.tsx`: the available row is a labelled button calling `updates.download()`; an in-flight download offers no second one; a staged build outranks the failing-checks retry; a one-off failure stays quiet. - Seven pre-existing #3526 tests asserted the old blanket silence by whole-object equality. Updated so the behaviour they were protecting (restart guidance only for a wedged network stack, never for a 404) is asserted explicitly instead of implied. Ran locally: 62/62 `auto-updater.test.ts`, 66/66 `Sidebar.test.tsx`, 161/161 across the four related files, `npm run frontend:typecheck` clean. The `src/landing/**` failures in the full suite are pre-existing and unrelated (the base branch fails more of them than this branch). ## Verified by running, not just reading The renderer path was exercised end to end against a scripted bridge: real component, real click handlers, real `updates:status` push channel. Clicking `available` really transitions through `downloading` to `downloaded`. Rendering it against real nightly version strings is what caught the third commit here, where the subline truncated to `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251200…` and lost its trailing word. ## Risks and limits The main-process updater is gated on `app.isPackaged` and cannot run in a dev build, so the actual download-and-install is covered by unit tests against a mocked `autoUpdater`, not by a packaged run. The feed change is confined to the nightly channel. ## Out of scope - The stuck manual-check loader in Settings is handled by #4392 (https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/4392). - On the staged row the version line still truncates and loses the word "ready" — the same flaw fixed here for `available`, but it predates this branch (#2381), so it is left alone. - Observed on a real install while verifying: a build already staged in `pending/` was re-downloaded in full (168MB) on a later check. Worth its own investigation; not addressed here.

title: bug(windows): worker ao browser can resolve to broken npm shim
body:
## Bug

On Windows, a worker can fail before `ao browser` even reaches the desktop browser runtime:

```text
@aoagents/ao: no prebuilt binary for win32-x64.
The optional dependency @aoagents/ao-win32-x64 is not installed
```

This is confusing because the desktop app does ship a working AO daemon binary. The worker should be using that pinned daemon binary, not falling through to whatever old npm `ao` shim happens to be on the user's PATH.

## What seems to be happening

Windows treats environment variable names case-insensitively, but parts of our launch environment handling were treating them as case-sensitive.

That means a worker could inherit something like:

```text
Path=C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\npm
```

and AO could also add:

```text
PATH=C:\Program Files\Agent Orchestrator\resources\daemon
```

Those two entries can survive together. In practice the inherited npm path can win, so `ao browser ...` resolves to the npm shim. If that npm install was done with optional dependencies omitted, the shim dies with the missing `@aoagents/ao-win32-x64` error.

## Expected behavior

Workers on Windows should resolve bare `ao` commands to the AO daemon/app binary that launched the session. The user's global npm install should not decide whether `ao browser` works inside an AO worker.

## Impact

This blocks browser-panel control from affected Windows workers. The workaround is to repair the npm install with optional deps, but users should not need npm at all for this path.

## Fix direction

When merging worker launch environments on Windows, replace environment keys case-insensitively so AO's pinned `PATH` replaces inherited `Path` instead of coexisting with it.

title: Import project dead-ends on PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED with no 'go to that project' option
body:
## Bug

Importing a local folder that is **already registered** as a project dead-ends the Import project modal: it shows the raw daemon error `A project at this path is already registered (PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED)` with only *"Choose a different folder to try again"* + **Cancel**. There is no path to the already-registered project, even though the daemon tells the client exactly which project it is.

Reporter's ask: instead of this error, offer an option to **go to that project**.

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` (2026-08-25)
**Reported by:** @maaz
**Analyzed against:** `origin/main` @ `4c3f4d72e`
**Confidence:** High — full chain traced end-to-end (daemon → envelope → apiClient → CreateProjectFlow)
**Priority:** medium — degraded UX, workaround exists (find the project manually in the sidebar)

## Reproduction

1. Have a project registered at path `P` (it is in the sidebar)
2. `+` → **Import project** → *Choose a project folder* → select `P` in the OS picker
3. Confirm creation in the agent sheet
4. Daemon returns `409 PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`
5. Modal re-opens in the bare folder-picker state: red error box with the raw message, footer *"Choose a different folder to try again"*, only **Cancel** available — a dead end

![Import project modal showing the PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED dead-end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-import-registered-deadend/.issue-assets/import-registered-deadend/modal.png)

## Root Cause

The daemon already returns everything needed to recover — the renderer discards it at every layer.

**The daemon side is fine:**

- `backend/internal/service/project/service.go:196-200` — `Add()` returns `apierr.Conflict("PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED", "A project at this path is already registered", map[string]any{"existingProjectId": existing.ID, "suggestedProjectId": ...})`
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go:44` — `Details map[string]any json:"details,omitempty"` — so `details.existingProjectId` **is on the wire** in the 409 response.

**Where the renderer drops it:**

1. `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` (`createProject`, ~L424-432):
   ```ts
   const failure = new Error(apiErrorMessage(error)) as Error & { code?: string };
   failure.code = apiErrorCode(error);
   throw failure;
   ```
   Only `message` + `code` survive. `error.details` — which carries `existingProjectId` — is dropped on the floor. There is no `apiErrorDetails()` helper at all (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts` has `apiErrorMessage` / `apiErrorCode` / `apiErrorRequestId` only).

2. `frontend/src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts` (`apiErrorMessage`) renders `` `${body.message} (${code})` `` — which is exactly the `(PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED)` suffix visible in the screenshot. Raw daemon code leaked into UI copy.

3. `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx:212-235` (`createProject` catch): `code` **is** extracted (line 213) but is only branched on for `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` / `PROJECT_UNBORN` repository-setup recovery. There is no branch for `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED` / `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED`. So: `setError(message)`, and since `shouldScanCreateFailure()` (line 421-426) *explicitly returns `false`* for `(PATH|ID)_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, `validationScan` stays `null` → `CreateProjectFolderDialog` renders the bare dashed picker + error box + footer `createProject.footerChoose` ("Choose a different folder to try again", `en.json:166`).

4. Pre-flight doesn't help either: the folder scan (`frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts`, `scanGitRepo`) only knows git facts (bare, unborn, no remote, reserved name). It has no access to AO's registered-project list, so the user learns about the conflict only **after** confirming.

## Fix

1. **Carry the conflict payload**: in `_shell.tsx` `createProject` (and `cloneProject` for symmetry), attach `error.details` (or minimally `existingProjectId`) to the thrown error, e.g. add an `apiErrorDetails(error)` helper in `api-client.ts` next to the existing ones.
2. **Branch on the code** in `CreateProjectFlow`'s catch: for `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, render a dedicated state in `CreateProjectFolderDialog` — "This folder is already registered as a project" with a primary **Go to project** action (navigate to `existingProjectId` via the existing project navigation; the project is already in the sidebar) and secondary *Choose a different folder*. Same pattern applies to `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED`.
3. **Optional belt-and-braces**: during the folder scan, flag the selected repo as "already registered" (the renderer already has the workspace/project list) so the user finds out at picker time, before confirming.

## Impact

- Any user who re-imports a folder that's already registered (new machine, restored disk, or simply forgetting it's in the long sidebar list) hits a hard dead-end that reads like a system fault rather than guidance.
- The error copy exposes the raw daemon code (`PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`) verbatim, inconsistent with the rest of the import flow's human-readable messaging.

## Related

- #2721 — same flow, non-Git/nested import error messaging (different failure class, same "raw error in modal" shape)

title: fix(browser): stop auto-sending browser errors
body:
## What

Stops browser console and failed-request diagnostics from being injected automatically into an active agent conversation.

Browser failures remain available through an explicit `ao browser errors` query for manual or agent-driven inspection.

## Why

The always-on browser signal path posted batched errors to the daemon session send endpoint. That unsolicited message could interrupt work already in progress and wake unrelated or idle agent sessions.

## How

- Removes the daemon-port and `net.fetch` auto-send path from the browser view host.
- Retains a session-local FIFO history of the latest 200 browser failures.
- Caps each retained entry at 16 KiB before storage.
- Preserves timestamps, console/network source classification, and untrusted-content boundaries.
- Detaches webRequest listeners and clears retained diagnostics when a session is destroyed.
- Merges retained diagnostics into the existing explicit browser errors response.
- Adds regression coverage proving the former five-second window performs no outbound send.

title: [Bug]: OMP TUI workers stay idle while working
body:
### Summary

TUI workers launched with `--agent omp --mode tui` stay `activity_state=idle` forever. `ao session ls` / `ao session get` report idle even while the omp TUI is actively reading files and coding.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Spawn a worker with `--agent omp --mode tui` (omp has no chat driver for this path).
2. Watch the TUI work (read files, edit, code).
3. Run `ao session get` for that session.
4. Inspect SQLite `sessions.activity_state`.

### Expected behavior

While the omp TUI is working, `activity_state` should become `active` and `activity_last_at` should advance. After the turn settles, it should return to `idle`.

### Actual behavior

Status stays idle. `activity_last_at` is stuck at spawn time. `sessions.activity_state` never becomes `active`. There are no `conversation_turns` because this is TUI, not chat.

Root cause: activity for TUI harnesses is driven by `ao hooks <harness> session-start|user-prompt-submit|stop|...`. Grok installs Claude-compat hooks; Pi installs `.pi/extensions/ao-activity.ts` and passes `--extension` on launch. The OMP adapter does neither — it only builds `omp [--append-system-prompt] [--model] [prompt]`. OMP v17 has `--hook`/`--extension`, but AO never installs an activity extension, so hooks never fire.

### AO version

ao version dev

### Environment

macOS 27.0 arm64 (Darwin 27.0.0), omp 17.2.12

### Logs / extra context

Reproduced locally against Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator. No `ao hooks omp` callbacks are installed, so the daemon never receives activity signals for TUI omp sessions.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(omp): report TUI activity via managed extension
body:
## What

OMP TUI workers now report activity through a managed workspace extension, the same way Pi does. `ao session get` / `ao session ls` can show `active` while omp is working instead of remaining idle at spawn time.

## Why

Fixes #4407.

TUI activity is driven by `ao hooks <harness> …`. The OMP adapter never installed an extension or passed `--extension`, so hooks never fired and `sessions.activity_state` stayed `idle`.

## How

- Install gitignored `.omp/extensions/ao-activity.ts` from `GetAgentHooks` (sentinel-guarded overwrite, plus `UninstallHooks` / `AreHooksInstalled`).
- Pass `--extension` on launch and restore so reporting does not depend on project auto-discovery.
- Map OMP v17 events: `session_start` → idle, `before_agent_start` → active, `session_stop` → idle, `session_shutdown` → exited.
- Register the omp deriver in `activitydispatch`. Chat-mode activity is unchanged; no tmux scraping.

OMP has `session_stop` rather than Pi's `agent_settled`; stop is reported from that settle event.

## Testing

```bash
cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/omp/... ./internal/adapters/agent/pi/... ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/...
```

title: feat: bring back ao report for worker-to-orchestrator reporting
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

# Spec: `ao report` — worker → orchestrator reporting

**Status:** draft expansion of locked 2026-08-22 spec

## Purpose

Workers self-report meaningful state changes to the orchestrator.

The reporting surface should be expressive enough for workers to communicate important progress, outputs, decision boundaries, and completion without turning ordinary execution progress into orchestrator context noise.

Report type answers:

> **What happened?**

`--note` answers:

> **What should the orchestrator know about it?**

## Command surface

```bash
ao report --pr-created --note <url>
ao report --artifact --note <uri|path-ref>
ao report --checkpoint --note <text>
ao report --needs-input --note <text>
ao report --stuck [--note <text>]
ao report --done [--note <text|path-ref>]

ao report <free-form text>
```

`--note` is metadata available on report types. It is not itself a report type.

Examples:

```bash
ao report --pr-created \
  --note "https://github.com/org/repo/pull/482"

ao report --artifact \
  --note "file:///tmp/benchmark-results.json"

ao report --checkpoint \
  --note "parser migration complete; starting evaluator"

ao report --needs-input \
  --note "Both API shapes are viable. Need a decision on whether empty results should return 200 or 404."

ao report --stuck \
  --note "Cannot reproduce the nondeterministic test failure locally."

ao report --done \
  --note "Review complete; no blocking issues."
```

Free-form and `--note` text have a **hard cap of 1000 characters**. Larger output must be passed by reference.

Example:

```bash
ao report --artifact --note "file:///tmp/report-1234.md"
```

## Report types

### `--pr-created`

The worker created a pull request.

The PR URL is supplied through `--note`.

```bash
ao report --pr-created \
  --note "https://github.com/org/repo/pull/482"
```

This is informational. PR creation does not imply that the worker's assignment is complete.

A worker may therefore emit:

```bash
ao report --pr-created --note "https://github.com/org/repo/pull/482"
ao report --done --note "Implementation and validation complete."
```

as separate reports.

### `--artifact`

The worker produced a durable output that may be useful to the orchestrator or another worker.

Examples include:

* investigation reports
* benchmark output
* generated files
* traces
* patches
* branches
* commits
* datasets
* screenshots
* analysis documents

The artifact reference is supplied through `--note`.

```bash
ao report --artifact \
  --note "file:///tmp/perf-results.json"
```

`--artifact` says that something reusable now exists. It does not imply completion.

`--pr-created` remains a dedicated convenience signal even though a PR is conceptually also an artifact.

### `--checkpoint`

The worker reached a meaningful intermediate milestone.

A checkpoint should represent a state transition that could materially help the orchestrator understand or re-plan the work.

Examples:

```bash
ao report --checkpoint \
  --note "Root cause isolated to retry accounting."

ao report --checkpoint \
  --note "Backend migration complete; frontend integration remains."

ao report --checkpoint \
  --note "All existing tests pass. Starting regression coverage."
```

### `--needs-input`

The worker can reason about the task but cannot responsibly continue without an external decision, missing information, permission, or choice.

This is distinct from `--stuck`.

```bash
ao report --needs-input \
  --note "Both API designs satisfy the requirements. Need a decision on backward compatibility."
```

Other examples:

```bash
ao report --needs-input \
  --note "Need credentials for the staging environment."

ao report --needs-input \
  --note "Spec does not define whether deleted records should remain queryable."
```

### `--stuck`

The worker cannot make meaningful progress on its own.

```bash
ao report --stuck \
  --note "Cannot reproduce the race after exhausting the known paths."
```

`--stuck` is the strongest worker-originated attention signal.

It is edge-triggered, not level-triggered. Repeating the same stuck state should not repeatedly interrupt the orchestrator.

### `--done`

The worker's assignment has reached a terminal state.

`--done` covers all completion forms:

* implementation
* PR work
* RCA / exploration
* review
* research
* validation
* other assigned worker tasks

Examples:

```bash
ao report --done \
  --note "Implementation complete and tests pass."

ao report --done \
  --note "RCA complete. Full report at file:///tmp/rca-1234.md"

ao report --done \
  --note "PR review complete; no blocking issues."
```

There is no per-completion-form flush behavior. All `--done` reports follow the same settlement rule.

## Free-form reports

Workers may still send informational reports without a semantic flag:

```bash
ao report "flaky test quarantined; rerunning suite"
```

These are ordinary informational messages and accumulate in the outbox.

They should be used when none of the structured state transitions apply.

## Delivery semantics

| Report          | Default delivery          |
| --------------- | ------------------------- |
| free-form       | Batch                     |
| `--pr-created`  | Batch                     |
| `--artifact`    | Batch                     |
| `--checkpoint`  | Batch                     |
| `--needs-input` | Attention / fast delivery |
| `--stuck`       | Immediate interrupt       |
| `--done`        | Settle flush              |

### Batch

Informational reports accumulate without immediately entering the orchestrator's context.

The normal 30-minute fallback timer applies.

A flush caused by another event includes all accumulated informational reports.

### Settle flush

The first `--done` opens a 5-minute flush window.

Further reports during that window join the same batch.

At T+5 minutes, the accumulated batch is delivered as one orchestrator wake-up.

### Attention

`--needs-input` requires faster treatment than ordinary informational reporting because work may be waiting on the orchestrator.

### Urgent

`--stuck` is delivered immediately.

Rate limit:

```text
1 interrupt per worker per 3 minutes
```

Repeats inside the rate-limit window coalesce into the worker's pending batch with a repeat counter.

### Piggyback

Whenever the user sends a message to the orchestrator, all pending worker reports are appended before the orchestrator reasons about the new user message.

This gives the orchestrator current worker state without requiring another turn.

## Why there is no `--failed`

`ao report` is a worker-originated mechanism.

If a worker process, runtime, or box dies, that worker cannot reliably report its own failure.

Runtime failure therefore belongs to worker lifecycle/event machinery rather than the reporting protocol.

A live worker that concludes an investigation unsuccessfully can still terminate its assignment with `--done` and explain the result:

```bash
ao report --done \
  --note "Could not reproduce after exhausting the available traces and test environments."
```

A worker that still expects intervention before giving up should use `--stuck` or `--needs-input`.

title: feat: allow safe initial prompt edits without forking
body:
## What

Enable Edit for the first provider-backed prompt even when the active chat provider does not advertise history forking. Keep later prompts gated behind the existing `fork` capability, and hide the first-prompt affordance when older history has not loaded.

## Why

Cursor chat sessions currently expose no Edit action because Cursor ACP does not provide AO with an anchored historical fork primitive. AO already handles editing the initial prompt safely by starting a fresh conversation, so that limited case can be enabled without replaying history, mutating provider storage, or adding a dependency.

## How

- Pass the edit handler to the timeline independently of provider fork support.
- For fork-capable providers, preserve editing for every provider-backed turn.
- For providers without fork support, expose editing only on the first known provider turn.
- If `hasMoreBefore` is true, expose no edit action because the UI cannot prove the visible turn is the first prompt.

Intentional omission: later Cursor prompt editing remains unavailable until Cursor ACP exposes an anchored fork or rewind operation. This PR does not simulate that behavior by replaying transcript history.

## Testing

- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx -t "offers only the first prompt|withholds first-prompt editing" --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism --testTimeout=30000`
- `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit`
- Earlier full `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` run: 65/65 passed.

The repository-wide frontend run was also attempted locally; unrelated suites require separately installed landing-page modules and loopback listener permissions unavailable in the sandbox. The focused chat suite and frontend type-check pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(workspacewatch): one missing git-listed directory aborts the whole workspace/events subscription with a 500
body:
## Summary

`GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/events` returns 500 and the live-file SSE subscription never starts when the session's git worktree references a directory that no longer exists on disk. One missing directory aborts the whole subscription.

## Root cause

For a git worktree, `addInitialDirectories` (`backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go:152-193`) builds the watch set from `git -C <root> ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` (`watcher.go:120`): for every listed file it adds the file's directory and all ancestors up to root **without stat'ing them**, then calls `watcher.Add(dir)` on each. `fsnotify.Add` does an `lstat`, so a directory that git still lists (via the index, `--cached`) but that was removed from disk — an unstaged deletion, a sparse/partial checkout, or a dir deleted while the request is in flight — returns `no such file or directory`.

The loop returns on the **first** such failure (`watcher.go:186-192`) with no per-directory tolerance, so the entire subscription aborts. The untyped error reaches `streamWorkspaceChanges` (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:622`) and `envelope.WriteError`, which has no typed mapping for it and defaults to `http.StatusInternalServerError` (`backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go:77`). The workspace *root* is already guarded (`os.Stat` at `watcher.go:85` -> typed 404); this is specifically the partially-present-worktree case (root exists, a git-listed subdirectory does not).

## Reproduction (verified)

```
git init <root>; mkdir <root>/sub; echo x > <root>/sub/file.txt; git -C <root> add sub/file.txt
rm -rf <root>/sub                      # tracked dir deleted, deletion not staged
# git -C <root> ls-files --cached  still prints  sub/file.txt
workspacewatch.Watch(ctx, <root>)      # or open the session Files view -> GET .../workspace/events
```

Observed:

```
watch workspace directory "<root>/sub": lstat <root>/sub: no such file or directory
```

The endpoint returns 500 and the subscription never establishes. Combined with the no-backoff EventSource reconnect (#4323) this repeats in a tight loop.

## Expected

A directory that has gone missing should be **skipped** (log-and-continue) so the subscription still establishes for the directories that exist. A partially-present worktree should not 500 the whole live-files stream.

## Affected code

- `backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go:120,152-193`
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:622`
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go:77`

## Related

- #4323 (SSE reconnect with no backoff amplifies a transient setup 5xx) — the amplification is filed there; this is the specific setup-failure root cause.
- #4325 (untyped service errors collapse to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR).

title: bug(usage): session usage aggregation 500s with "no such table: openai_usage_event_details" on schema-drifted DBs
body:
## Summary

Every session usage-summary request returns 500 with `SQL logic error: no such table: openai_usage_event_details` on any database whose migration ledger records `0102_canonical_usage` as applied but where the `openai_usage_event_details` / `anthropic_usage_event_details` tables were never physically created. Unlike the equivalent 0052 case there is **no reconcile/self-heal**, so the database stays broken permanently.

## Root cause

- `AggregateUsageBySessionHarnessModel` (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/usage.sql:437-438`) `LEFT JOIN`s `openai_usage_event_details` and `anthropic_usage_event_details`, so it hard-requires both tables at execution time.
- Those tables are created **only** in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0102_canonical_usage.sql` with plain `CREATE TABLE` (lines 106, 113), **not** `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` — unlike `usage_bindings` / `usage_sources` / `model_usage_events` in the same migration (lines 10/22/42). No later migration recreates them.
- 0102 is a `-- +goose NO TRANSACTION` migration, so goose writes the "applied" ledger row in a separate write from the migration body. An interrupted/partial upgrade (daemon killed, crash, power loss) can leave 0102 recorded as applied while the detail tables are absent; 0102's own header documents this "recorded without physical tables" hazard.
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:688-702` self-heals the analogous 0052 case (it deletes the burned `goose_db_version` row and re-applies when `model_usage_events` is physically missing) but has **no equivalent check** for the 0102 detail tables (verified: zero references to `openai_usage_event_details`/`anthropic_usage_event_details` in `db.go`). Once 0102 is marked applied with the tables missing, goose skips it forever.
- `backend/internal/service/usage/summary.go` -> `ListUsageModelAggregates` (`backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/usage_store.go:453`, untyped `fmt.Errorf`) -> `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/usage.go` -> `envelope.WriteError` -> 500 on every summary request.

## Reproduction (verified)

Apply migrations through 0102, then drop the detail table while leaving the ledger at 102 (the same end state a partial 0102 apply produces):

```
sqlitetest.Open(dir)                        // runs migrations, creates the tables
DROP TABLE openai_usage_event_details;      // via a second connection; goose_db_version stays 102
st.ListUsageModelAggregates(ctx, "any-session")
```

Observed:

```
aggregate usage for session any-session: SQL logic error: no such table: openai_usage_event_details (1)
```

Restarting the daemon does not repair it (schema reconcile has no check for these tables), so every usage-summary request 500s from then on.

## Expected

Either (a) create the detail tables idempotently (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) **and** add a reconcile check that re-applies 0102 when the tables are physically missing, mirroring the 0052 repair at `db.go:688-702`; or (b) make the aggregation degrade gracefully when the detail tables are absent.

## Affected code

- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/usage.sql:437-438`
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0102_canonical_usage.sql:106,113`
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:162,688-702`
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/usage_store.go:453`
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/usage.go`

## Related

- #4335 (schema drift swallowed to a WARN while /readyz reports ready, request 500s) — same family, different table.
- #3476 (skipped migration under goose WithAllowMissing -> 500) — same mechanism.

title: feat: enable Cursor chat and TUI handoff
body:
## Summary

- preserve Cursor's provider-native conversation ID across Chat UI and Terminal UI
- resume Chat → TUI with Cursor's exact single-argument form `agent --resume=<session-id>` (using AO's resolved Cursor executable); do not replay the transcript to Cursor or trigger an extra model turn
- render AO's durable user/assistant transcript directly into terminal scrollback before Cursor starts, because Cursor does not hydrate ACP-created Chat history into its local TUI store
- exclude system prompts, tool output, attachments, standalone redaction placeholders, ANSI escapes, and unsafe control characters from that display-only transcript
- consume the bounded mode-0600 transcript artifact once, with crash recovery and cleanup for cancellation, rollback, shutdown restore, termination, and superseding transitions
- restore TUI → Chat through ACP `session/load`, reconciling Cursor's native transcript so Chat and terminal turns remain visible once and in chronological order
- wire the production daemon's Chat adapter to the durable transcript reader (the cause of the reported “Cursor Chat history reader is unavailable” failure)

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/service/chat ./internal/session_manager ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/cursoracp`
- `go build ./...`
- `git diff --check`
- regression test verified red before the daemon adapter forwarding method and green after it

## Local desktop validation

Launched the PR checkout as the real Electron desktop app in isolated mode using `~/.ao/dev`. Verified the rebuilt daemon at `127.0.0.1:3002`, renderer at `localhost:5173`, and successful project API response. The pre-fix test session was terminated during the required backend restart, so a new Cursor Chat session is required for the next manual handoff attempt.

title: fix(mobile): drop the computed import() that breaks every Metro bundle
body:
## Summary
- Since #4394 every mobile bundle fails with `SyntaxError: lib/sentry.ts: Invalid call at line 90: import(spec)` — Metro rejects a computed `import()` in app code at bundle time, it doesn't skip it.
- Replace the placeholder with a `loadSdk()` stub that returns `null` until `@sentry/react-native` is actually installed. Sentry stays a no-op, as before.
- Add `sentry.test.ts` covering the no-op path.

## Test plan
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` — 477 pass
- `npx expo export --platform ios` / `--platform android` — both bundle again; both fail on `main`
- Worth a separate PR: run `expo export` in `mobile.yml` so this can't land again

title: bug(chat): Claude Plan mode promises no tool execution but writes outside the worktree
body:
## Bug

Claude Code Plan mode is described as **“Planning mode, no actual tool execution.”** In native ChatUI QA it executed tools and persisted a plan file under `~/.claude/plans`, outside the session worktree, even though the prompt explicitly prohibited tools and file changes.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; relevant paths rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built `ao` (`dev`), verified daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P1 — the UI presents a false safety boundary  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced natively, filesystem side effect captured, and rendering/forwarding path traced

## Reproduction

1. Open a Claude Code session in ChatUI.
2. Select **Plan** in the permission-mode menu.
3. Prompt it to produce a plan while explicitly saying not to execute tools or modify files.
4. Observe Read/Write activity and a new Markdown plan under `~/.claude/plans`.
5. Deny the later “Ready to code?” prompt; the plan file already exists.

## Expected

Either AO enforces a genuine no-tool/no-write boundary, or the menu truthfully explains provider-native Plan mode, including possible file inspection, tool use, and provider-owned plan files outside the worktree.

## Actual

AO renders an absolute “no actual tool execution” promise while passing the provider mode through without enforcing that boundary.

## Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/config_options.go:172` forwards provider descriptions.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.tsx:544` renders the categorical description without qualification.
- Mode changes are forwarded to ACP; AO does not currently impose a tool/write policy at this boundary.

## Fix direction

Prefer truthful provider-specific disclosure unless AO can enforce a strict read-only mode. Add a provider contract test that observes writes outside the worktree.

## Acceptance

- Plan-mode copy never promises a boundary AO does not enforce.
- Claude-specific behavior explains provider-owned plan artifacts before selection.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-01` passes in strict mode.

## Evidence

![Claude Plan mode writes a plan file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/22-plan-mode-writes-plan-file.png)

- [Full finding and expected/actual details](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/manual-qa-report.md)
- [Captured filesystem evidence](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/evidence/plan-mode-created-file.md)

## Related

- [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — local-only regression harness and QA evidence
- [#3745](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3745) — separate read-only reviewer-harness work; not a duplicate

title: bug(chat): Stop turn silently cancels queued messages and queue items cannot be controlled
body: ## Bug The only visible **Stop turn** action interrupts the active turn and cancels every accepted queued prompt. The label does not disclose that consequence, and queued items have no per-item cancel/promote controls in the desktop queue dock. **Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) **Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA **Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; relevant paths rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57` **Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built `ao` (`dev`), verified daemon on port 3001 **Priority:** P1 — already accepted user instructions are silently discarded **Confidence:** High — reproduced natively and destructive backend path traced ## Reproduction 1. Start a long-running Chat turn. 2. Submit two follow-ups in Queue mode and confirm they are shown as queued. 3. Press **Stop turn**. 4. Observe both the active turn and all queued messages become stopped/cancelled. 5. Inspect the queue dock; no cancel-one or promote-next actions are available. ## Expected - Stop either preserves queued work or explicitly names how many queued messages it will cancel. - Each queued item can be cancelled independently. - Existing promote-next capability is exposed in the queue dock. - Stop-all remains a separate, clearly destructive action. ## Actual The active and queued turns are cancelled together through a control labelled only for the active turn. ## Root cause - `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:1619` couples active interruption with queue cancellation. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:2441` renders a display-only queue dock. - `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.ts:320` exposes promotion, but `SessionChatSurface.tsx:292` does not wire it into the dock. - `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/conversations.go:64` has no cancel-one route. ## Fix direction Add cancel-one service/API semantics, wire promote/cancel controls into each queue item, and expose the exact Stop-all consequence in the accessible label/confirmation. ## Acceptance - Cancelling one queued item does not affect the active turn or sibling queue items. - Promoting a queued item changes the next durable turn deterministically. - Stop-all names and confirms its queue consequence. - `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-02` passes in strict mode. ## Issue-specific evidence Real AO desktop queue dock with independent Promote-next and Cancel controls while the active turn remains **Working**: Stop-all confirmation names the exact remaining queue scope and consequence: Settled state distinguishes undispatched queue cancellation from interrupting an active agent: Local source screenshots and general QA reports remain outside the repository and uncommitted. ## Related - [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — local-only MQA-02 contract - [#3634](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3634) — queued-delivery timing, not queue controls - [PR #3838](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3838) — existing queue promotion plumbing

title: bug(desktop): persist Chat drafts across session navigation, interface switches, and restart
body: ## Bug Unsent Chat text is stored only in the mounted composer. It disappears without warning when Chat unmounts, when navigating between sessions, on renderer reload, and after a full app restart. The same ownership puts staged attachments and inline-edit state at risk. **Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) **Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA **Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; relevant paths rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57` **Environment:** macOS arm64, isolated Electron data under `~/.ao/dev`, todo-app session **Priority:** P1 — direct loss of unsent user input **Confidence:** High — reproduced at four lifecycle boundaries with a positive mounted-shell control ## Reproduction Type a unique unsent draft, then test each boundary independently: 1. Switch Chat to Terminal and back. 2. Navigate to another session and return. 3. Reload the renderer. 4. Stop and relaunch Electron/daemon using the same isolated data. The composer is empty after each boundary. As a positive control, an auxiliary worktree-shell tab round trip preserves the draft because Chat remains mounted. ## Expected Draft text, edit target, and recoverable attachment metadata are scoped by session and restored across ordinary navigation/restart boundaries. Accepted sends clear only that session’s committed draft. ## Actual Unsent text disappears without warning whenever the Chat subtree is recreated. ## Root cause - `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:158` owns text, attachment state, and staged-delivery refs locally. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:1311` owns inline-edit state locally. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:1142` replaces the Chat subtree when committed mode changes. - There is no session-scoped durable draft store/API. ## Fix direction Persist a versioned session-scoped draft synchronously, including text and inline-edit metadata. Persist staged attachment descriptors only when their bytes are safely recoverable; otherwise block the boundary with precise discard copy. Clear a draft only after definitive send acceptance or explicit discard. ## Acceptance - Text survives interface round trips, cross-session navigation, renderer reload, and app restart. - Drafts never leak between sessions. - A successfully accepted send is not resurrected. - Cancelling inline edit keeps the independent composer draft. - `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-04` passes in strict mode. ## Issue-specific evidence Real AO desktop draft lifecycle using an isolated Electron/data directory and the local todo-app fixture: 1. Exact unsent draft before Chat → Terminal handoff: 2. Chat interaction subtree locked while the handoff is pending: 3. Native Terminal UI after the switch: 4. Exact draft restored and editable after returning to Chat: The screenshots are GitHub-hosted issue evidence. Local source captures and general QA reports remain outside the repository and uncommitted. ## Related - [#4033](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4033) / [PR #4036](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4036) — fixed only the mounted shell-tab subset - [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — deterministic lifecycle contract

title: bug(chat): busy Chat-to-Terminal switch interrupts work without consent
body:
## Bug

Switching from a busy Chat session to Terminal immediately selects destructive `interrupt`, cancelling the active tool/turn and queued instructions without a Finish-versus-Stop choice. The reverse Terminal-to-Chat direction already presents that policy dialog.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; exact hard-coded path remains on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built AO, verified daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P1 — active and queued work can be destroyed without consent  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced natively and exact transition policy traced

## Reproduction

1. Start a Chat turn that runs a long tool, such as `sleep 20`.
2. Optionally queue a follow-up.
3. Click the top-bar action to switch to Terminal UI.
4. Observe no policy dialog; the transition begins immediately.
5. The native TUI shows the tool/turn as interrupted.

## Expected

Idle/no-queue Chat may drain directly. Active or queued Chat must show **Finish work, then switch** (safe default) versus **Stop now and switch**, name affected queue/draft state, and make no interrupt request before explicit consent.

## Actual

The renderer sends `policy: interrupt` immediately and temporarily exposes a mismatched surface while the destructive transition runs.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:704` hard-codes `interrupt` for Chat-to-Terminal before checking busy/queued state.
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:1389` applies interrupt semantics, cancelling the durable queue and provider work.

## Fix direction

Reuse the existing policy dialog in both directions. Derive the safe default from active/queued state and prove no transition POST occurs before user choice.

## Acceptance

- Busy Chat always offers drain versus interrupt.
- Default focus is **Finish work, then switch**.
- Drain preserves accepted active/queued work.
- Interrupt occurs only after explicit **Stop now** consent.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-05` passes in strict mode.

## Evidence

![Busy Chat switched directly to interrupted Terminal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/33-busy-chat-to-terminal-transition.png)

- [Full finding](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/manual-qa-report.md)

## Related
