- [PR #3957](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3957) — introduced unconditional Chat-to-Terminal interrupt behavior
- [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — two deterministic MQA-05 policy contracts

title: bug(chat): unscoped hook checkpoints permanently block TUI-to-Chat recovery
body: ## Bug After **Stop now and switch** interrupts a busy Claude TUI turn, target Chat startup can fail `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`. In the reproduced session, five retries—including a successful recovery turn, daemon/Electron restart, and native-identity refresh—continued to fail. The session remained usable only in Terminal, and the AO-2L interface-failure notice offered Dismiss but no targeted recovery. **Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) **Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA **Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; source paths rechecked and tagged regression remains red on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57` **Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built AO, verified daemon on port 3001 **Priority:** P0 by QA definition / repository P1 label — a normal interface flow permanently removes ChatUI for a healthy session **Confidence:** High — extended native reproduction plus failing session-manager contract ## Reproduction 1. Start a long command in native Claude TUI. 2. Choose **Stop now and switch** to Chat. 3. Observe `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` / AO-2L “switch interface failed.” 4. Retry while idle. 5. Complete a new successful native turn and retry. 6. Restart daemon and Electron, refresh native identity, and retry. 7. Every Chat startup remains blocked. ## Expected A fresh, generation-fenced provider-history observation can recover transient state. If an untrusted legacy text checkpoint remains poisoned, AO offers explicit provider-history recovery while retaining trusted AO high-water/terminal-history safety. Terminal must remain usable. ## Actual Stale/unscoped text facts become hard replay checkpoints and survive every normal recovery boundary; the renderer provides no actionable recovery. ## Root cause - `backend/internal/cli/hooks.go:188,325` extracts prompt/assistant aliases across hook events without main/subagent provenance. - `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go:1280` preserves older non-empty facts indefinitely. - `backend/internal/service/chat/service.go:240` promotes those facts into hard replay checkpoints. - `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:421` requires exact latest-completed text matches. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInterfaceSwitch.tsx:276` gives `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` no recovery action. ## Fix direction Qualify checkpoint provenance by provider, native conversation, controller generation, event kind, main/subagent source, and trust. Retry only refreshable snapshots. Return typed mismatch dimensions. Permit explicit legacy/untrusted provider-history recovery without weakening trusted current-generation gates. Add Retry / Use provider history / Stay in Terminal actions and an announced failure state. ## Acceptance - A first incomplete target snapshot can recover using a fresh observation. - Stale/subagent/old-generation hook text cannot poison a new target. - Trusted current-provider mismatches still fail closed. - Recovery never duplicates provider transcript or mutates the worktree. - AO-2L exposes actionable, accessible recovery. - `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-06` and both tagged Go contracts pass strictly. ## Issue-specific evidence Real authenticated Claude Code TUI → Chat recovery in the isolated AO Electron app: 1. AO-2L fails closed and offers accessible recovery choices: 2. **Use provider history** completes the handoff and replays the original turn once: 3. The recovered ChatUI remains usable for a new Claude turn: The screenshots are GitHub-hosted issue evidence. Local accessibility snapshots, manifests, and general QA reports remain outside the repository and uncommitted. ## Related - [#4120](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4120) / [PR #4121](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4121) — similar permanent symptom from a different AO high-water cause - [#4123](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4123) / [PR #4186](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4186) — removed blind polling of immutable ACP replay - [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — browser and Go MQA-06 contracts

title: bug(chat): imported Terminal turns show misleading OUTCOME UNKNOWN
body: ## Bug Completed Claude Terminal/TUI turns are imported into ChatUI with the visible divider **OUTCOME UNKNOWN**. This reproduced for both a simple `TERMINAL_OK` reply and a drained busy turn that visibly completed `BUSY_DONE`. **Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) **Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA **Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; presentation path rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57` **Environment:** macOS arm64, Claude native TUI → ChatUI **Priority:** P2 — handoff succeeds but reports materially misleading provenance **Confidence:** High for presentation; Medium for provider-native status availability ## Reproduction 1. In Claude Terminal UI, submit a prompt that returns a distinctive successful answer. 2. Let the turn finish, then drain-switch to ChatUI. 3. Observe the imported prompt and assistant response followed by **OUTCOME UNKNOWN**. ## Expected Preserve exact native completion state when the provider supplies it. When it does not, say neutrally: **Imported from Terminal UI — completion status unavailable**. Do not visually imply that the visible exchange itself may have failed. ## Actual Every recovered ACP turn is rendered with the generic unknown-outcome divider. ## Root cause - `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/history.go:67-78,169-175,245-262` closes ACP replay boundaries as `TurnStateRecovered` because `session/load` has no terminal outcome. - Codex can preserve native status in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/history.go:116-127,183-188`. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx:2235-2253` maps every recovered turn to **Outcome unknown** without import provenance. ## Fix direction Carry status source/provenance with replayed turns. Map exact provider state when present; otherwise render neutral import copy. Never infer success only from assistant text. ## Acceptance - Exact native completion state is retained where available. - Unavailable state uses neutral Terminal-import copy. - Failed/interrupted native turns remain distinguishable. - `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-08` passes in strict mode. ## Issue-specific evidence Deterministic outcome-state coverage after the fix: Real AO desktop Terminal → Chat handoff preserving a completed turn: - [Detailed local verification comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4425#issuecomment-5412423041) - General QA reports and local evidence remain ignored and uncommitted. ## Related - [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — broad Chat/TUI architecture, not this presentation defect - [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — deterministic MQA-08 contract

title: bug(chat): @file chips imply embedded context but send only path text
body: ## Bug Chat’s `@file` autocomplete renders an atomic file-shaped chip, but sending serializes only ordinary worktree-relative path text. AO does not read, upload, snapshot, attach, or grant permission for the file, and the chip exposes neither that limitation nor the full path. **Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) **Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA **Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; source semantics rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57` **Environment:** macOS arm64, Claude Chat, todo-app workspace **Priority:** P2 — the affordance materially misstates what context the agent receives **Confidence:** High — reproduced and serialization contract traced ## Reproduction 1. Type `@READ` in Chat and select `README.md`. 2. Observe an attachment-like `README.md` token. 3. Send the prompt. 4. Observe plain `README.md` path text in the human turn. 5. The agent requests normal Read/tool access because no content was embedded. ## Expected The token is named and described as a **path reference**. It explains that the agent reads current filesystem contents with normal permissions, exposes the full path on hover/focus and to assistive technology, and distinguishes duplicate basenames. ## Actual The basename-only file chip resembles supplied context while silently degrading to plain path text. ## Root cause - `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ComposerEditor.tsx:143-145,168-172` renders a basename chip but serializes the relative path without `@`. - `ComposerEditor.tsx:147-163` exposes neither full path nor reference-only semantics. - `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.test.tsx:662-667` explicitly contracts verbatim path transport. - The file catalog is loaded once and is not refreshed after workspace changes. ## Fix direction Keep path-only transport unless product semantics deliberately change, but make that contract visible and accessible. Refresh the file index on workspace change events and surface index failures. ## Acceptance - The selected token is announced as a path reference, not attached content. - Full relative path is discoverable on hover, focus, and accessibility APIs. - Duplicate basenames remain distinguishable. - File suggestions refresh after workspace changes. - `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-09` passes in strict mode. ## Issue-specific evidence Real isolated AO Electron verification of truthful path-reference behavior: 1. Duplicate basenames remain distinguishable before selection: 2. Keyboard focus exposes the complete path and path-only transport explanation: 3. The sent human message contains ordinary relative-path text, without an attachment or byte payload: The screenshots are GitHub-hosted issue evidence. Local source captures and general QA reports remain outside the repository and uncommitted. ## Related - [PR #4331](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4331) — introduced inline path chips with path-only serialization - [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — two MQA-09 contracts

title: bug(a11y): Chat delivery and settings controls omit selected-state semantics
body:
## Bug

ChatUI visually highlights Queue/Steer and the current model, effort, permission, and choice values, but the accessibility tree does not expose their selected state. Queue/Steer are plain spans inside a group; settings are generic menu items with styling-only `data-active`.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; semantics rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64; accessibility-tree inspection of Claude and Codex Chat  
**Priority:** P2 — primary turn controls are not reliably perceivable to screen-reader users  
**Confidence:** High — DOM/role state and source traced

## Reproduction

1. Open a busy Chat session.
2. Inspect Queue and Steer in the accessibility tree.
3. Toggle the visible selection.
4. Open model/effort and permission menus and inspect the selected item.
5. No radio/check/pressed state identifies the current values.

## Expected

The accessibility tree exposes a named single-selection group and current value—radiogroup/radio, toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`, or `menuitemradio` with dynamic checked state. Keyboard behavior and announcements match the chosen roles.

## Actual

Selection is primarily a visual styling convention.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:782-817` renders plain spans; a source comment mentions `aria-pressed`, but no state is emitted.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ui/option-menu.tsx:103-114` maps active only to visual `data-active` on generic items.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.tsx:305-367,510-575` uses those items for mutually exclusive settings.

## Fix direction

Use actual interactive single-selection patterns for Queue/Steer and Radix radio-menu primitives for mutually exclusive settings. Preserve existing keyboard shortcuts while ensuring role, focus, selected state, and announced updates agree.

## Acceptance

- Queue/Steer are keyboard-operable and expose exactly one current value.
- Model, effort, permission, boolean, and enumerated choices expose checked state.
- State changes are announced without duplicate live-region noise.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-11` passes in strict mode.

## Evidence

![Visually selected Steer control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/14-chatui-steer-selected.png)

- [Codex permission menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/48-codex-permission-mode-menu.png)
- [Full finding](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/manual-qa-report.md)

## Related

- [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — deterministic assistive-technology contract

title: bug(chat): provider error rows discard actionable failure detail
body:
## Bug

`providerErrorCopy` extracts safe actionable detail such as exhausted credits and a billing link, but `ErrorActivityRow` renders only the generic headline. Current tests explicitly assert that the useful detail is absent, leaving users with reconnect/status copy instead of the action that can resolve the failure.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and local regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419), strict `GAP-01` contract  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Priority:** P2 — recoverable provider failures are presented without their recovery action  
**Confidence:** High — normalized detail exists and is deliberately dropped by the renderer

## Reproduction

1. Render a provider failure whose normalized detail says the account has no credits and includes the official billing URL.
2. Open the Chat timeline.
3. Observe only the generic error/reconnect headline.
4. The credit detail and **Add credits** action are absent.

## Expected

Show safe normalized detail and a constrained actionable link when one exists. Preserve generic copy for unknown/untrusted provider text and never make raw arbitrary URLs clickable.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatTimelineItems.tsx:1453-1454` destructures only `headline` from `providerErrorCopy`.
- `providerErrorCopy` around line 1466 already returns normalized actionable information.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatProviderSignal.test.tsx:300-344` currently asserts the useful “no credits” detail is not rendered.

## Acceptance

- Known safe failure classes render normalized detail and their specific action.
- Unknown provider details remain safely escaped and non-linkified.
- Reconnect status does not replace the causal provider error.
- The `GAP-01 implemented-but-unmounted signals` provider-error contract in [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) passes strictly.

## Related

- [PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419) — deterministic actionable-error contract

title: feat(cloud): integrate the AO cloud offering into the monorepo (AWS/NodeOps, flag-gated)
body:
## Summary

Integrates the entire AO cloud offering into this monorepo so one repository serves
both the local desktop app and the hosted cloud product. The cloud control plane
(previously a separate private repo) is vendored as a `cloud/` Go module wired
through a Go workspace (`go.work`). Everything cloud sits behind a single
Developer Mode-gated Settings toggle that is off by default, so the app runs
exactly as it does today with zero behavioral change until a user deliberately
enables the offering.

## Gating (additive, zero local regression)

The cloud offering is a persisted daemon preference, off by default:

- **Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode** reveals a **Cloud** toggle; enabling it
  shows an explicit "early, highly unstable preview" confirmation first.
- The toggle is stored daemon-side (`app_settings.cloud_offering`, PATCH
  `/api/v1/settings/cloud-offering`) so desktop, mobile, and headless spawns
  resolve the same gate.
- `cloudEnabled = (toggle || AO_CLOUD_OFFERING env force-on) && control-plane URL`.
  The control-plane URL and the WorkOS client id are public client configuration
  and ship as baked defaults; the env vars remain development overrides only.
- There is no per-client entitlement in the gate anymore; abuse control is
  server-side (per-org sandbox quotas, with control-plane entitlement as a
  follow-up).

When cloud is off (the default) the daemon imports no cloud code, the renderer
skips every control-plane call, and local sessions are authoritative — the app
behaves exactly as before.

## What is included

- `cloud/` module: Postgres control plane (HTTP API, WorkOS RS256 JWT auth,
  reconciler, worker transport), sandbox provider interface with NodeOps CreateOS
  and Docker implementations, and the AWS deploy path (ECR, ECS, migration task,
  scan gate, auto rollback).
- Local vs cloud projects: local projects run local sessions; cloud projects run
  cloud sessions, each worker in its own isolated sandbox.
- Electron main process control-plane proxy so the WorkOS token stays in the main
  process and the renderer never talks to the control plane directly.
- Separate migrations by design: cloud uses Postgres migrations under
  `cloud/internal/postgres/migrations`; local keeps its SQLite migrations. The two
  are structurally disjoint (different engines, databases, directories).

## Reliability fixes in this branch

- Public repository checkout: `AO_CLOUD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_GITHUB_CHECKOUT` lets a
  worker clone a public repository directly when the checkout broker denies a grant.
  Previously only the Docker provider enabled this, so NodeOps workers on a public
  repo project without a GitHub App connection failed checkout with a 403 and
  crash-looped. GitHub App checkout for private repositories is the follow-up.
- Terminal startup ceiling: a worker that never checks in was repaired in place on
  every tick forever, which kept resetting the provider auto-pause timer and billed a
  permanently broken session indefinitely. A configurable ceiling
  (`TerminalStartupTimeout`, default 10m, clamped above the startup timeout) now
  stops the repair storm, best-effort stops the compute to halt billing, and parks
  the sandbox as `terminated`. It is gated on "never checked in" so a once-healthy
  worker that goes silent is still repaired normally.
- Sandbox `terminated` state migration: the `terminated` verdict above was written by
  the reconciler but never allowed by the `ao_sandboxes_observed_state_check`
  constraint, so every write failed (SQLSTATE 23514) and a ceiling-hit sandbox could
  never settle -- it was re-reconciled every tick and the session terminal looped
  forever on "worker is not connected". Migration `00030_sandbox_terminated_state.sql`
  adds `terminated` to the constraint so the verdict persists and the sandbox settles.
- Frontend UX: cloud auth resolves instantly on cold open (the on-disk session is
  returned immediately and the WorkOS token refreshes in the background) instead of
  blanking the sidebar for seconds; the New Project flow shows an explicit
  Local | Cloud choice with a caption for each and a sign-in prompt when
  unauthenticated; the cloud terminal shows a calm "Connecting..." on first attach
  (rather than "disconnected -- reattaching"), no longer gates on the local daemon,
  and lifts its replay cover cleanly with no blank flicker.

- Bounded sandbox deletion: a provider box that cannot be reclaimed (e.g. a
  NodeOps VM stuck in "failed", whose DELETE is accepted but never converges)
  no longer keeps the reconciler re-requesting deletion forever; past a
  deadline (default 15m) the row is released and the orphan logged.
- Sandbox quota counts only live sandboxes (terminated/failed/deleting no longer
  block new sessions) and the per-org cap default is 1000.
- Connect latency: the worker bootstraps once the sandbox is actually running
  (not at create time), within the same reconcile claim, and launches
  template-baked binaries after a hash check instead of uploading them; the
  sandbox templates come in per-harness slim variants selected by the session's
  harness; the terminal polls readiness at a flat 1s before first attach.
  Median session connect measured at ~5s (from ~60-90s), with occasional
  ~15s outliers when the provider schedules onto a host without the cached
  template.
- Cloud project/session UX: signing out hides cloud projects immediately and
  drops the cached cloud data; the orchestrator button on a cloud project spawns
  an orchestrator session in its own sandbox instead of falling through to
  project settings; coding-agent credentials are managed in-app (post-sign-in
  prompt plus a Cloud page in Settings).

## Verification

- Cloud module builds and vets clean; reconcile, config, worker, and sandbox unit
  tests pass, including new reconcile tests (terminate at the ceiling, park without
  resume, still honour deletion, repair within the ceiling) and a config test.
- Deployed to AWS staging and validated end to end: a cloud session on a public
  repository provisions a NodeOps sandbox, the worker reaches `worker.ready`, the
  agent runs the prompt, and the turn completes (returns to idle), then tears down
  cleanly.
- Local paths verified: with cloud disabled, the daemon runs the local app
  unchanged.

---

## How to test this branch (for developers)

The cloud control plane is already deployed to AWS staging, so you do **not**
deploy it, and **no environment variables are needed** — the staging control-plane
URL and the WorkOS client id ship as baked defaults. Everything below is what a
developer needs end to end.

### Prerequisites

- **Go** (per `go.mod` / `go.work`), **Node 20+** and **npm**, **git**, and **gh**.
- **A Claude Code setup token** (`claude setup-token`) or an Anthropic API key —
  the cloud sandbox runs the agent with *your* credential (step 4).
- **Free ports:** `3000` (WorkOS sign-in callback), `3002` (dev daemon), `5173`
  (Vite dev server). An installed build uses `:3001`, so it can run alongside.

### 1. Check out and run

```bash
gh pr checkout 4434          # or: git fetch <fork> && git checkout feat/cloud-offering-aws
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

`predev` builds the Go daemon, the browser runtime, and the ACP runtime
automatically. Dev state is isolated under `~/.ao/dev` (daemon on `:3002`, Vite on
`:5173`), so it never touches an installed build.

### 2. Enable the cloud offering

**Settings** (gear, bottom-left) → **Advanced** → turn on **Developer Mode** → a
**Cloud** toggle appears beneath it → turn it on and confirm the unstable-preview
warning. "Sign in to AO Cloud" appears in the sidebar immediately.

Sanity check: `curl http://127.0.0.1:3002/api/v1/settings` shows
`"cloudOffering": true, "cloudEnabled": true`.

(Env overrides still exist for CI/headless: `AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=true` force-enables,
`AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` / `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` / `AO_CLOUD_AUTH_REDIRECT`
override the baked defaults.)

### 3. Sign in (WorkOS auth)

Click **Sign in to AO Cloud** in the left sidebar. A browser opens WorkOS AuthKit;
after login it redirects to the loopback and the app stores the session (the token
stays in the Electron main process and never reaches the renderer). You are placed in
your **own personal org** automatically, so cloud projects are isolated per developer.

### 4. Connect your coding-agent credential (one-time, per org)

Creating a cloud session requires a validated coding-agent connection (the sandbox
worker runs the agent with your token). The app now prompts for this itself: right
after your first sign-in, a **"Connect a coding agent credential"** dialog opens
when your org has no valid connection yet. Pick the harness (Claude Code / Codex /
Cursor), paste a setup token or API key, and Connect -- expect "Credential
connected". You can reopen it any time from the sidebar account menu ->
**Coding agent credentials**.

For Claude Code, a setup token comes from `claude setup-token` (or use an Anthropic
API key). The credential is validated by the control plane and stored encrypted;
it is never shown again.

Headless/CI alternative: `python3 cloud/scripts/dev-connect-agent-credential.py`
does the same PUT from a terminal. It reads the token from `CLAUDE_CRED`, then
`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, then the macOS Keychain; signs in via WorkOS once
(loopback `:3000`, cached at `~/.ao/cloud-dev-token.json`); flags `--login`,
`--delete`.

### 5. Add a cloud project and open sessions

- **New Project** -> the **Local | Cloud** choice appears (cloud enabled + signed in)
  -> pick **Cloud**.
- Use a **public** repository, e.g. `https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World`, default
  branch `main`, and create it.
- Inside the cloud project, create one or more sessions -- **each provisions its own
  sandbox**. Create several to confirm N independent sandboxes.
- A brand-new session's terminal shows **"Connecting..."** for a few seconds
  (typically 4-6s: the sandbox template pre-bakes the worker binaries, the
  reconciler bootstraps in the provision tick, and the repo then checks out).
  A session occasionally takes 15-20s when the provider schedules its sandbox
  onto a host that has not cached the template yet (the pull happens inside the
  provider's create call); hosts warm up with use.
- **Orchestrator:** click the orchestrator button on the cloud project (sidebar
  hover, board CTA, or topbar). It spawns an orchestrator session **in its own
  sandbox** and opens its session view, exactly like a worker session (it must
  not land you in project settings -- that was the local-only fallback).

### GitHub / repositories

- **Public repos work** -- the sandbox worker clones them anonymously; no GitHub auth
  needed.
- **Private repos are not supported yet** (GitHub App integration is the follow-up).
  A private repo's worker cannot check out, so the session's worker never starts and
  its terminal keeps retrying "Connecting...". Use a public repo for now.

### Verify local is unchanged (toggle off)

Turn the Cloud toggle off (Settings > Advanced). `curl :3002/api/v1/settings` now
shows `"cloudEnabled": false`: the sidebar shows no cloud sign-in, cloud projects
disappear from the board, New Project shows no Cloud tab, and no control-plane
calls are made. The app is byte-for-byte the local app (the daemon binary imports
zero cloud code). A fresh install is in this state by default.

### Troubleshooting

- **No Cloud toggle in Settings:** Developer Mode (Settings > Advanced) is off.
- **No "Sign in to AO Cloud":** the Cloud toggle is off, or `/settings` shows
  `cloudEnabled: false`.
- **Session create returns 422 `agent_provider_required`:** your org has no valid
  coding-agent connection yet -- connect one via the account menu dialog (step 4).
- **Terminal stuck on "Connecting..." past ~3 min:** the sandbox worker never
  started -- almost always a private repo (use a public one) or a stale/dead session.
- **Port already in use:** free `3000` / `3002` / `5173` (an installed build uses
  `:3001`, so it does not conflict with the dev build on `:3002`).

## Follow-ups

- Server-side entitlement: with the per-client env check removed from the gate,
  restrict who can actually use the hosted control plane on the server (org
  allowlist or entitlement flag) before widening distribution; per-org sandbox
  quotas are the current control.

- Connect latency (accepted at 4-7s median for now): the remaining levers are a
  warm sandbox pool (sub-2s and removes the cold-host tail), per-harness slim
  templates (~770MB vs 1.4GB, halves the tail), and asking NodeOps to
  pre-distribute the template fleet-wide.
- Republish the NodeOps sandbox template when a deploy changes `ao-worker` or the
  `ao` helper (`cloud/scripts/publish-nodeops-template.sh` with
  `AO_CLOUD_CP_IMAGE=<deployed control-plane image>`), then point
  `default_rootfs` at it. A stale template keeps working - the bootstrap
  hash-check falls back to uploading the binaries - it is just slower.

- GitHub App integration for private repository checkout.
- Deploy pipeline: the ECR scan gate currently blocks on unpatched base-image
  `openssl` CVEs (allowlist them or bump the base image).

title: fix(chat): label imported Terminal outcomes neutrally
body: Code changes: +88 -39 Tests: +156 -10 Others: +21 -7 ## What this fixes This PR fixes **misleading outcome wording after a successful Terminal UI → ChatUI handoff**. It does not change whether the interface switch succeeds. The fix is **not** to remove every status line after a handoff. It replaces the generic **OUTCOME UNKNOWN** line with truthful Terminal-import provenance and keeps that provenance attached to the imported turn. Before this fix, AO could import a visible prompt and response from Terminal UI but receive no reliable final-status metadata from the provider. ChatUI then rendered **OUTCOME UNKNOWN**, which made a successful-looking exchange appear failed or suspect. After this fix, AO records that the turn came from Terminal UI and renders the neutral, truthful label: > **Imported from Terminal UI — completion status unavailable** AO does not guess that a turn completed merely because response text exists. When the provider supplies an exact completed, interrupted, or failed outcome, that exact outcome is still preserved. ## Expected behavior | Turn | Available provider state | ChatUI result | | --- | --- | --- | | Imported from Terminal UI | Exact completed/interrupted/failed state | Preserve that exact state | | Imported from Terminal UI | No reliable final state | **Imported from Terminal UI — completion status unavailable** | | Recovered ordinary ChatUI turn | No reliable final state | Keep the ordinary recovered-Chat wording | | New native ChatUI turn | Normal live state | Render normally; never inherit the Terminal-import label | ## Exact-head desktop evidence The following flow was run in the real Electron desktop app from exact product head `62e0c8448df23dc4c86c95aea8a20e6c203cd3a1`, with isolated AO data and a disposable clone of `todo-app`. > **Reading these screenshots:** both are post-fix snapshots of the same cumulative conversation. They are not a before/after pair. Screenshot 2 still contains the imported `QA4435_NATIVE` turn from screenshot 1, then adds a new native `QA4435_CHAT` turn below it. ### 1. After the fix: the imported Terminal turn gets truthful provenance 1. Started a Claude Code orchestrator in Terminal UI. 2. Sent `Reply with exactly QA4435_NATIVE`; Claude returned `QA4435_NATIVE`. 3. Switched Terminal UI → ChatUI using the real interface control. **What changed:** `QA4435_NATIVE` survived the handoff. At the divider where the old UI said **OUTCOME UNKNOWN**, ChatUI now says **Imported from Terminal UI — completion status unavailable**. The status line remains because AO still cannot truthfully infer completion; the fix makes that uncertainty specific and non-misleading rather than removing it or inventing a successful `Done` state. ### 2. Scope guard: a later native ChatUI turn does not inherit the label After the handoff, sent `Reply with exactly QA4435_CHAT` directly from ChatUI. **What to observe:** the import label near the top still belongs to the same earlier `QA4435_NATIVE` turn shown in screenshot 1—and it should remain attached to that historical turn. Look below it: the newly sent `QA4435_CHAT` exchange renders normally and has no Terminal-import label. This proves the copy is scoped to the imported turn rather than leaking to the whole conversation. ### 3. Durable provenance matches what the UI shows SQLite was checked after the same run: | Persisted turn | `imported_from_terminal` | | --- | ---: | | Recovered `QA4435_NATIVE` Terminal turn | `1` | | New `QA4435_CHAT` ChatUI turn | `0` | This ensures the renderer is using durable provenance carried through storage and the API, not guessing from message text. The two screenshots remain GitHub attachments only; they are not committed to the repository. ## Automated regression evidence The deterministic MQA-08 scenario covers the outcome combinations that a live provider cannot reliably produce on demand: **What to observe:** - top: an imported turn with unavailable status receives the new neutral label; - middle: a known completed outcome remains completed; and - bottom: a known interrupted outcome remains **Stopped**. The earlier `TERMINAL_CODEX_OK` desktop screenshot proved that a provider-supplied completed outcome survives a real handoff, but it did not visibly exercise the unavailable-status branch. It is intentionally no longer presented as the primary proof of this fix. ## Implementation - persist Terminal-import provenance only when required TUI → Chat native-history replay adopts the turn; - carry `imported_from_terminal` through SQLite, domain/service/HTTP DTOs, generated API types, and the renderer; - default historical rows to `false` rather than inventing provenance during migration; and - apply the neutral label only to recovered Terminal imports, preserving all existing completed, interrupted, failed, and ordinary recovered-Chat outcomes. ## Verification - independent Standards review: **approved, no actionable findings** - independent Spec review: **approved, no actionable findings** - focused renderer outcome/provenance coverage: **28/28 passed** - full renderer: **3,025 passed, 1 skipped** - focused backend, HTTP, SQLite migration, provider-history, and session-manager tests: **passed** - race-enabled Chat service/store verification: **passed** - frontend and E2E TypeScript checks: **passed** - `golangci-lint` v2.12.2: **0 issues** - serialized full backend suite (`go test -p 1 ./...`): **passed** - fresh GitHub CI for the exact head: **10/10 passed** - current integration status: `main` advanced after this exact-head run; the PR now needs a restack and revalidation before merge because `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrate_burned_versions_test.go` conflicts with the updated migration ledger ## Scope This product PR contains no regression-harness files, screenshots, reports, or generated QA artifacts. The opt-in, never-CI harness remains isolated in draft PR #4419. Fixes #4425 ## Current takeover integration Merged main `ab968d5e7`, preserving persistent-provider acknowledgement retries, unpublished-conversation cleanup, and explicit Terminal-import provenance. The unmerged migration is now 0142 to avoid the shipped migration range and other active PRs. Updated current provider-adoption tests and the provenance migration upgrade test. Focused import/native-history/store/migration checks pass. Build, vet, and lint pass. The local full race run was interrupted by shared tmux collisions and host disk exhaustion. All 14 hosted checks pass on 00fd04f94, including the complete Linux race suite and frontend suite. Earlier validation entries refer to their named prior heads.

title: bug(chat): successful agent switch keeps the previous provider's model controls
body:
## Bug

After switching a ChatUI session successfully from Claude Code to Codex, the composer still shows Claude model and reasoning controls. In the reporter reproduction, the new Codex conversation was active while the composer still displayed **Opus (1M context) · High**.

**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma during local latest-main ChatUI testing on 2026-08-25
**Environment:** macOS arm64, AO Electron development build, orchestrator session
**Confidence:** High for the visible stale state; Medium for the cache-race root cause

## Reproduction

1. Open a Claude Code session in ChatUI.
2. Use the in-place agent switcher to switch the session to Codex.
3. Wait for AO to report that the switch succeeded and for the Codex conversation to become interactive.
4. Inspect the model/reasoning controls in the composer.

## Expected

The old provider catalog is unavailable while the handoff is settling. Once Codex is active, the composer shows only model/config options reported by Codex. No Claude model or reasoning choice survives the controller epoch change.

## Actual

The switched Codex conversation remains paired with Claude controls, including **Opus (1M context) · High**. This makes the successful handoff look internally inconsistent and may let the user attempt a setting that the active provider does not own.

## Likely race / code path

- frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSwitchAgent.ts invalidates conversation, models, and provider config in the mutation onSuccess handler. That handler runs when POST /switch-agent is accepted (202), before the asynchronous durable switch has completed.
- The model and provider-option query keys are scoped only to the stable session id. A refetch during handoff can therefore repopulate the same cache entry from the outgoing Claude controller.
- The durable success observation in SessionChatSurface does not explicitly clear/refetch provider catalogs for the new controller epoch.

This is a hypothesis to verify, not a claimed final root cause.

## Acceptance

- Outgoing provider controls are hidden or disabled as soon as switching begins.
- Durable switch success invalidates/removes model, config-option, and skill catalogs from the outgoing controller epoch.
- Claude → Codex shows only Codex controls immediately after success.
- Codex → Claude shows only Claude controls immediately after success.
- Failed/recovered switches restore the source provider controls without mixing catalogs.
- A deterministic test uses distinct source/target catalogs and proves stale values cannot survive.

## Evidence

Reporter-provided screenshot will be attached directly to this issue; it must not be committed to the repository.

## Related

- #3317 — in-place semantic agent switching
- #4419 — local-only ChatUI regression harness (draft)

title: chore(desktop): de-duplicate the bundled tmux version literal
body:
## What

`build-tmux.mjs` and the `postPackage` verification gate in `forge.config.ts`
each hardcode the bundled tmux version (`"3.5a"`) independently. Hoist the
version and its checksum into a single `frontend/scripts/tmux-version.mjs` and
have both files read it.

## Why

Two literals for the same truth drift silently. Bumping the version in
`build-tmux.mjs` alone leaves the gate checking the old one, so a deliberate
version change turns into a packaging failure:

```
Error: packaged tmux failed verification at <path>/tmux: tmux 3.5a
```

The gate runs `tmux -V` and rejects anything that isn't the literal string. The
only correct fix to date has been to remember to edit the gate too — easy to
miss, and the failure mode is late (after a full package).

## Test plan

No behavior change; `3.5a` is preserved. `node --check` on the new module and
the builder's own self-verification (`tmux -V` vs `TMUX.version`) are unaffected.
The postPackage gate now reads the same constant the builder uses.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: report live workspace branch in sessions
body:
## Summary

- resolve each active git session's branch from its managed worktree when assembling session read models
- keep the durable spawn-time branch as a fallback when the worktree is unavailable or detached
- validate the workspace path against AO's managed root before running the single read-only Git probe

## Root cause

`SessionMetadata.Branch` is captured when a session is spawned, but an agent or host can change the worktree branch directly with Git. Session GET/list responses continued projecting that seed value, so the API could report `ao/<session>/root` while the worktree and claimed PR were already on a feature branch.

The fix treats the checked-out branch as mutable external state and overlays it at service read-model assembly time. This also covers spawn, restore, and resume responses that use the same assembly path. It does not perform a checkout or mutate SQLite.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/service/session ./internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree ./internal/daemon -count=1` (pass)
- `go build ./...` (pass)
- `go vet ./...` (pass)
- Windows/amd64 cross-compile of the three affected test packages (pass)
- `go test ./... -count=1` in the Linux Go 1.25.7 container reaches unrelated environment-sensitive baseline failures:
  - fake-agent lifecycle hook log is not created in the container
  - mobilebridge chmod-based write-failure tests run as container root and remain writable
  - one session-manager test requires tmux, which is not installed in the build container

No frontend or API schema shape changes are required.

title: Chat-driven orchestrator spawn fails: CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE — Claude Code CLI has no ACP support
body: ## Summary Spawning a chat-driven Orchestrator session fails immediately with `CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE` because Agent Orchestrator appears to spawn the `claude` CLI directly and expect it to speak ACP (Agent Client Protocol) — but the Claude Code CLI does not implement ACP at all, in any published version. ## Error ``` spawn monorepo-1: chat controller: chat driver incompatible: ACP initialize: {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"error":"peer disconnected before response"}} (CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE) ``` (Screenshot of the app's error dialog to follow in a comment.) ## Environment - Agent Orchestrator desktop app (macOS, Darwin 24.6.0), `ao daemon` - Claude Code CLI `2.1.245` — confirmed via `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code version` that this is the latest published version, not a stale install - Project registered as a `single_repo` with `orchestrator.agent = "claude-code"` ## Root cause The installed Claude Code CLI has no ACP support whatsoever: ``` $ claude --help | grep -i acp (no output — zero mentions across the full help text) $ claude acp ✘ unknown command "acp" └ Did you mean claude mcp? ``` This isn't a version-skew issue — there is no `claude acp` subcommand, `--acp` flag, or documented/undocumented env var exposing an ACP server mode in the Claude Code CLI, in its current or past published releases. ACP support for Claude is instead implemented by a **separate, officially maintained bridge binary**: `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` (previously published as `@zed-industries/claude-agent-acp`, now deprecated in favor of the new package name), which wraps the Claude Agent SDK and exposes ACP over stdio: ``` npm install -g @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... claude-agent-acp ``` It looks like the "chat driver" here spawns `claude` directly and performs an ACP `initialize` handshake against it, which will always fail — `claude` exits immediately on the unrecognized interaction, surfacing as "peer disconnected before response". ## Suggested fix Let the chat-driver / orchestrator spawn path target `claude-agent-acp` instead of (or in addition to) `claude` — e.g. auto-detect `claude-agent-acp` on `PATH`, or add a configurable "ACP agent binary" setting per project/harness — rather than assuming the Claude Code CLI itself speaks ACP. ## Repro steps 1. Register a project with `orchestrator.agent = "claude-code"`. 2. Click "Spawn Orchestrator" (chat-driven mode) from the project board. 3. Observe immediate failure with the `CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE` error above. 4. As a workaround, "Create as Terminal UI" works fine — it drives Claude Code via plain CLI flags (`--resume`, `--append-system-prompt-file`, etc.) instead of ACP.

title: fix(dev): point the dev-server proxy at the daemon that is actually running
body:
## What

Resolve the Vite dev-server proxy target from the run file the daemon actually wrote, instead of a fixed `http://127.0.0.1:3001`.

## Why

Investigation for #4324, where 502s were reported on `/api/v1/*` with no matching code path in the Go daemon. There isn't one — the daemon never emits 502. This proxy does.

`frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts` proxied `/api` and `/mux` to a fixed `127.0.0.1:3001`. That is correct for a standalone daemon (`config.DefaultPort`), but `npm run dev` has Electron supervise its own daemon on `DEV_DAEMON_PORT = 3002` (`frontend/src/main.ts:223`). Vite's proxy error handler is `res.writeHead(502, …).end()` (`vite@8.0.16`, `dist/node/chunks/node.js:17938`), so an unreachable target becomes a 502.

Captured on `main` @ `dd47a7547`, with a healthy daemon running:

```console
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3002/api/v1/projects
200                                     # daemon, direct
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://[::1]:5199/api/v1/projects'
502                                     # same daemon, through the dev proxy
```
```
[vite] http proxy error: /api/v1/projects
Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3001
```

**Not limited to `npm run dev:web`.** The renderer's API base in dev is `window.location.origin` (`renderer/lib/api-client.ts:9,13`) until the daemon reports ready and `renderer/lib/daemon-status.ts:6-11` redirects it to the real port, so plain `npm run dev` has the same exposure for anything requested before that redirect.

Provenance: the `3001` default has been there since the scaffold (`c2c4404c7`, #168); `f2da70d3b` (#2465) later introduced `DEV_DAEMON_PORT = 3002` without touching this config.

## How

`AO_DEV_API_TARGET` still wins outright. Otherwise the resolver walks the run files in the order the daemon's own writers pick one — `AO_RUN_FILE` first (AO agent sessions and isolated checkouts set it, which is why `ao-desktop-dev`'s launch command `env -u`s it), then the Electron dev supervisor's dev-scoped file, then the standalone `ao start` default — and finally falls back to `expectedDaemonPort(env)`, which honours `AO_PORT`.

Deliberately reuses what already exists rather than re-deriving it: `parseRunFile` and `defaultRunFilePath` from `daemon-discovery.ts`, `expectedDaemonPort` and `DEFAULT_DAEMON_PORT` from `daemon-attach.ts`. One parser and one default for this on-disk contract, so there is no second copy to drift when `runfile.Info` changes.

**A recorded port is used only when its pid is still alive.** `running.json` is removed on graceful shutdown only, so a hard-killed `npm run dev` leaves one behind; trusting it would aim the proxy at a dead port and reproduce this same 502 with the ports swapped — a case the fixed default happened to get right. Liveness uses `process.kill(pid, 0)`, matching `main.ts:1259-1265`.

The file is written temp-then-rename (`runfile.Write`), so a reader never observes a partial write; the risk being guarded is staleness, not tearing.

Resolution happens once at config load, stated in the config comment: start the daemon first, or set `AO_DEV_API_TARGET`. Per-request resolution would mean reaching into Vite's proxy internals for a case an env var already covers — happy to go further if you'd prefer it.

## Testing

New `frontend/src/shared/dev-api-target.test.ts`, 15 cases: the `AO_DEV_API_TARGET` override short-circuiting before any file is read, each run-file candidate in precedence order, `AO_RUN_FILE` winning, the standalone fallback, a stale pid being skipped in favour of a live later candidate, `AO_PORT`, and six malformed-run-file shapes that must degrade rather than throw.

```console
$ npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts        # whole frontend suite
Test Files  219 passed (219)
     Tests  2935 passed | 1 skipped (2936)
$ npm run typecheck
0 errors
```

End-to-end, with a daemon on a non-default port (3007) recorded in a run file: `/api/v1/projects` and `/api/v1/sessions` return **200** through the dev proxy with zero proxy errors, where `main` returns 502.

## Note

The investigation also turned up a second, **shipping** 502 source that this PR does not touch: `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` (`mobilebridge/tailscaleserve.go:36-40`) puts tailscaled's `ReverseProxy` in front of `/api/v1/*` for Connect Mobile, and `ShutdownServe` runs only on the graceful path, so an ungraceful exit strands `:443` on a dead port. Details are on #4324; happy to file it separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (based on `dd47a7547`)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for the behaviour being changed
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (vitest, typecheck)

title: optimisation on the events and sessions data to avoid failures
fix(systeminstall): pin winget source and add gh direct-download fallback
body:
Fixes #4449.

## What happens today

On a completely fresh Windows machine, `planWinget` resolved to a bare `winget install -e --id <id>`. With no source pinned, winget also queries the **msstore** source — which on a fresh profile has never been initialized, so its first use blocks on an interactive Y/N prompt (Terms of Transaction + 2-letter region consent). The daemon runs installs via `systemexec` with no TTY attached, so the prompt can never be answered and winget exits:

```text
Do you agree to all the source agreements terms? [Y] Yes [N] No:
An unexpected error occurred while executing the command: 0x8a150042 : Error reading input in prompt
```

`0x8A150042` = `APPINSTALLER_CLI_ERROR_PROMPT_INPUT_ERROR`. Every fresh-Windows user clicking Install on the "No coding agent found" screen got a guaranteed-failing job, forever retryable, never succeeding. Upstream reference: microsoft/winget-cli#2819 (same prompt, same code path in any non-interactive session).

## The fix (layered options 1 + 3 from the issue)

**1. Pin winget to its community source (`planWinget`)**

```text
winget install -e --id <id> --source winget --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements
```

`--source winget` bypasses msstore entirely for both Windows targets (`GitHub.cli`, `SST.opencode`), and the accept flags make sure no remaining source/package agreement prompt can ever block a headless run. This is deterministic — it doesn't depend on per-user winget state at all.

**3. Direct-download fallback when winget is absent (`planGHWindows`)**

A machine without winget on PATH previously dead-ended as Unsupported ("winget was not found"). Since a truly fresh machine can't be assumed to have winget either, `gh` now falls back to a hardcoded PowerShell script that:

- fetches the latest release metadata from `api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/releases/latest`,
- downloads the official `gh_<ver>_windows_amd64.zip`,
- copies `bin\*.exe` into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps` — already on the default per-user PATH, so the installer's post-run `LookPath("gh")` verification succeeds with no registry edits or shell restarts,
- cleans up staging files.

Same security invariant as the rest of the package: the script is a package-level constant; no caller-supplied string ever reaches the argv. The fallback is deliberately gh-only — `opencode` without winget stays Unsupported (pinned by test).

## Tests

- Updated `TestPlanFor`: winget rows assert the full pinned argv; new row pins that opencode-without-winget remains Unsupported.
- New `TestGHWindowsFallsBackToDirectDownload`: pins that the no-winget gh plan is runnable, non-interactive (`-NoProfile -NonInteractive`), and targets the official cli/cli releases + `WindowsApps` destination.
- `go test ./internal/service/systeminstall/...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint v2.12.2` all pass.

Note: `TestCrushLocalAuthStatusDoesNotUseProviderCatalog` in `internal/adapters/agent/crush` fails on clean `upstream/main` too (verified by stashing this change) — pre-existing and untouched here.

title: bug(chat): structured sessions never receive their browser capability
body:
## Bug

Chat-mode sessions launch their structured provider controller with `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` explicitly empty and never persist a `browser_capability_verifier`. As a result, `ao browser` and capability-protected preview-server commands fail for every Chat worker even when the current bundled rewrite binary and Electron browser runtime support them.

**Source:** Independently reproduced in disposable AO-managed Chat session `agent-orchestrator-214` while reassessing the externally hosted process attached to session `agent-orchestrator-211` (211 was not contacted or modified)  
**Reported:** 2026-08-25  
**Analyzed against:** [`dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99) (`origin/main`, exact match to the triage checkout)  
**AO version:** freshly built rewrite CLI reports `dev`; bundled daemon reports `dev` and SHA-256 `3bb56a325b7e10ff35560386e118b2a5d2b7c258724c1f7cc9c586d89e251fb3`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, Go `1.26.4`, daemon healthy/ready on port `3001`  
**Confidence:** **High** — reproduced with an explicit current rewrite binary and traced through issuance, persistence, provider-env injection, authorization, tests, and introducing history.  
**Priority:** **P2** — browser automation is unavailable to all Chat sessions; switching/creating as TUI is a bounded workaround.

## Scope correction: managed Chat vs externally hosted process

Session `agent-orchestrator-211` does **not** establish this managed-Chat defect. Its durable AO row is `tui`, has nonempty runtime handle/launch IDs, and already stores a 43-character browser verifier. The process reporting the missing environment variable is a separately hosted `node_repl` process carrying AO session/worktree context, not the AO-managed TUI runtime that received the launch credential. A recovered/stale bearer presented from that external process correctly failed with `BROWSER_CAPABILITY_INVALID`.

AO has no repository-owned refresh/delegation endpoint that can safely disclose a new bearer to an already-running arbitrary external process, and possession of `AO_SESSION_ID` alone must not authorize browser control. Whether hosted-process attachment should gain a separate authenticated capability-delegation protocol is outside this issue and requires an explicit security design.

This issue remains valid and is scoped only to **AO-managed structured Chat controllers**, independently proven by session `agent-orchestrator-214`: it was created through `ao spawn --mode chat`, has provider conversation and controller generation IDs, has no terminal runtime IDs, received commands through the durable Chat conversation, and reproduced both an empty verifier and missing environment bearer.

## Reproduction

1. Build the exact current rewrite CLI and verify it is talking to the Go daemon, not a legacy PATH binary:

   ```sh
   git checkout dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99
   (cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro ./cmd/ao)
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro version
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro status --json
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro browser --help
   ```

   Observed: version `dev`; daemon state `ready`, health `ok`, port `3001`; `browser` includes `status`, `open`, `snapshot`, and the other current commands.

2. Spawn a fresh disposable Chat worker using the same absolute binary:

   ```sh
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro spawn \
     --project agent-orchestrator \
     --name triage-chat-browser \
     --harness codex \
     --mode chat \
     --prompt 'Report whether AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY is set, then run /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro browser status.'
   ```

3. The fresh controller reports:

   ```text
   AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY=unset
   ao browser requires the owning session capability (AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY is not set)
   ```

   The absolute rewrite command exits `2`.

4. Inspect only verifier lengths, never credential values:

   ```sql
   SELECT id, session_mode, length(browser_capability_verifier)
   FROM sessions
   WHERE id = '<fresh-chat-session>';
   ```

   Observed for disposable `agent-orchestrator-214`: `chat | 0`. Existing TUI rows launched on the same daemon have verifier length `43`.

The disposable session was terminated after reproduction.

## Expected

Every AO-managed Chat controller should receive a fresh, unguessable, session-scoped browser bearer in its own provider/runtime environment, while only the one-way verifier is durably stored before the worker can present the token. The owning Chat worker should pass `ao browser status`; another session, a stale launch token, an empty token, and a terminated session should remain unauthorized.

## Root cause

The shared environment builder intentionally clears all browser credentials:

- [`runtimeEnv`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3773-L3796) sets `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`, `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, and `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_STDIN` to empty values.
- [`launchRuntimeEnv`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3799-L3813) is the only layer that calls the browser authority, injects the bearer, and returns its verifier.
- [`persistBrowserCapabilityVerifier`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3815-L3830) stores the verifier before process launch to close the eager-worker authorization race.

TUI spawn and restore use the secure launch path and persist the verifier:

- [TUI spawn](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L899-L905)
- [TUI restore](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1978-L1985)

Every structured-controller launch bypasses it:

- [fresh Chat spawn](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go#L128-L147) calls `runtimeEnv` and passes the cleared map to `StartChat`;
- [Chat restore/reconcile](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go#L290-L329) repeats the same call;
- [direct Chat agent switching](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/agent_switching_chat.go#L27-L40) builds the target environment with `runtimeEnv` and later hands that map to the target `StartChat`.

The provider layer faithfully passes `cfg.Env` into both driver start and resume, so the credential is already absent before the Codex/ACP boundary: [chat service dispatch](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/service/chat/service.go#L340-L370).

Authorization then correctly rejects the request because Chat has neither half of the split credential: [browser service authorization](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/service/browser/service.go#L77-L94).

### History

[PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) introduced Chat on 2026-08-06 with `runtimeEnv` as its environment seam. [PR #3473](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3473), merged on 2026-08-08 as commit [`c9e1c676b`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/c9e1c676baee8ab2e860a8110f2539a460e73a11), split browser credentials into an ephemeral bearer plus durable verifier and changed the terminal spawn/restore paths to `launchRuntimeEnv`; it did not update the already separate Chat launch paths. `git blame` still attributes both Chat calls to PR #3472.

## Affected modes and paths

- **Affected:** fresh Chat sessions for every harness whose structured driver receives `ChatStart.Env` (confirmed live with Codex; generic code path also covers ACP Chat drivers).
- **Affected:** Chat controller resume/reconcile after daemon/controller recovery.
- **Affected:** TUI → Chat interface transitions and Chat source rollback paths that relaunch through `resumeChatController`.
- **Affected:** Chat → Chat agent switching and its target/recovery launches.
- **Not affected:** normal TUI spawn/restore, which already issue, persist, and inject the credential.

## Security requirements for the fix

This is an authorization-availability omission, not evidence of an auth bypass. The existing boundary must remain intact:

- mint a fresh random bearer for each controller launch and bind its verifier to the AO session ID;
- persist **only** the one-way verifier before the provider process can run an eager browser command;
- inject the bearer only into the owning Chat provider environment; never store it in SQLite, metadata/DTO JSON, logs, error envelopes, conversation events, or frontend state;
- continue clearing privileged `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN*` values so the Electron runtime credential cannot leak to a worker;
- rotate on relaunch so stale controller tokens fail, and preserve cross-session rejection;
- sequence rotation correctly during interface/agent switching: do not invalidate a still-live source controller prematurely, and ensure rollback/recovery receives a newly matching token/verifier pair;
- do not weaken browser/preview authorization or introduce a global/shared capability to make Chat pass.

The current domain field is already `json:"-"`, and the authority uses constant-time comparison with a verifier bound to the session ID; those properties should remain unchanged.

## Required tests

1. Fresh Chat spawn issues exactly one pair, persists the verifier before `StartChat`, injects a nonempty bearer into `ChatStart.Env`, retains the verifier through `ControllerReady`, and authorizes only that session.
2. Project/inherited env cannot supply or override `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` or either privileged browser-runtime secret.
3. Issuer failure or empty credentials aborts Chat spawn before controller start and exercises the existing workspace/session rollback contract.
4. Chat resume/reconcile rotates the pair before provider resume; the new bearer succeeds and the old bearer fails.
5. TUI → Chat transition, Chat → Chat agent switch, source rollback, and restart recovery each end with one matching bearer/verifier pair without invalidating a still-running source during a reversible phase.
6. Cross-session, empty, stale, and terminated-session capabilities remain rejected; no bearer appears in stored session records, API responses, logs, or durable conversation events.
7. End-to-end regression: start the desktop/browser runtime, spawn a fresh Chat worker with an explicit rewrite binary on `:3001`, and verify `ao browser status` succeeds without relying on PATH.

Current tests cover `launchRuntimeEnv` and browser authorization in isolation, and Chat tests assert only that a generic env/session ID reaches the controller. No test asserts issuance or verifier persistence for Chat.

## PATH shadowing is separate

A bare `ao browser status` in the disposable worker also resolved to a legacy binary and returned `unknown command "browser"`. That is **not** the cause established here: the same worker reproduced the missing-capability error with the absolute current rewrite binary. This report therefore does not combine the capability defect with legacy/PATH pinning behavior.

## Recommended implementation scope

Introduce one controller-launch credential preparation boundary shared by fresh Chat launch, Chat resume/reconcile, interface transition, and Chat agent switching. It should return the provider env plus verifier, durably establish the verifier at the correct lifecycle/saga boundary before `StartChat`, preserve/rotate it through controller commits, and explicitly model rollback/recovery ordering. Reuse the existing authority and storage column; no schema/API relaxation should be necessary.

This is not a trivial one-line fix because agent/interface switching has reversible pre-stop phases and post-stop rollback/recovery. No speculative fix PR was opened during triage.

## Verification performed

```text
go build ./...                                                        PASS
go test ./internal/session_manager -run 'Test(RuntimeEnv|ChatSpawnStartsControllerAndNoRuntime|ResumeExitedChatSessionDoesNotRequireTerminalRuntimeHandle)' -count=1  PASS
go test ./internal/service/browser -count=1                          PASS
```

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`, `browser_capability_verifier`, `owning session capability`, `chat ao browser`, `chat browser automation`, and `session owned browser`. No duplicate report or fix was found.

## Related

- [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — Chat/TUI architecture and lifecycle invariants.
- [PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) — introduced the structured Chat controller paths.
- [PR #3473](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3473) — introduced session-owned browser automation and the split bearer/verifier security model.

bug(chat): accepted inline edit can remain locked after lost response and restart
body:
## Bug

The durable Chat draft work in #4422 deliberately fails closed when an inline branch edit may have been accepted but its HTTP response was lost. After a renderer reload or app restart, the renderer can restore the exact edit request and stable client ID, but the conversation snapshot does not expose enough request identity to prove that this edit was already accepted.

**Discovered while fixing:** #4422
**Priority:** P2 — bounded failure mode, no duplication or data loss, but automatic recovery can remain blocked
**Confidence:** High — verified against the current edit response, conversation DTO, and branch-anchor behavior

## Reproduction

1. Start an inline edit of an existing user turn.
2. Let the daemon accept and apply the edit.
3. Lose the 202 response before the renderer records acceptance.
4. Reload or restart the renderer.
5. Choose **Retry edit safely**.

The renderer correctly reuses the original client ID. However, the active branch now contains the replacement turn, so ConversationEditAnchor may reject the retry. The restored journal stays locked because the conversation snapshot cannot correlate the accepted replacement with the original edit request.

## Expected

A retry with the same edit client ID is idempotent: it returns the previously accepted edit result, or the conversation snapshot exposes enough accepted-request identity for the renderer to reconcile and clear the journal.

## Actual

The safe retry can be rejected after the edit already changed the active branch. The renderer remains fail-closed with visible saved text and an unconfirmed-delivery notice.

## Safety properties already preserved by #4422

- No retry uses a fresh client ID.
- No duplicate edit is dispatched.
- Saved edit text is not erased.
- The locked state is visible rather than silent.
- Accepted-clear recovery does not call the edit API again.

## Likely root cause

ConversationMessageResponse and the conversation snapshot omit the edit request client ID/result mapping. Branch-anchor validation therefore runs before an identical accepted edit can be recognized as an idempotent replay.

## Acceptance

- Persist accepted inline-edit request identity and result durably.
- Repeating the same client ID returns the original accepted result without creating another branch.
- A restored renderer can reconcile the exact accepted edit and unlock automatically.
- A different client ID still receives normal anchor validation.
- Tests cover accepted-response loss followed by full renderer restart and safe retry.

## Evidence

This is a contract-level edge discovered by the #4422 regression tests and code review. No local screenshots or QA reports are committed; focused test evidence will be linked from the implementing PR.
