title: fix(chat): surface normalized provider error detail and action link
body:
Fixes #4431

## Problem

`providerErrorCopy()` already unwraps Codex JSON error envelopes (including truncated, `provider error: `-prefixed ones) and returns `{ headline, detail }`, where `detail` carries the actionable part — e.g. "You have no credits remaining. Add credits to continue using the API at https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing". But `ErrorActivityRow` destructured only `headline`, so users saw the generic reconnect copy while the recovery action was silently dropped. The tests explicitly asserted that absence.

## Change

- **`ErrorActivityRow`** now renders:
  - the headline (in its own span, keeping it a single text node for queries),
  - the normalized `detail` as escaped plain text below it — unknown/untrusted provider text stays inert,
  - a constrained action link when one applies.
- **New `providerErrorAction()` helper**: scans detail for URLs but only linkifies an allow-listed host + exact path (`platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing` → "Add credits"). Arbitrary provider URLs are never made clickable (no phishing surface); look-alike paths on the real host do not trigger the action. Links open via the existing `openLinkInSystemBrowser` external-link policy.
- **Tests** flipped from asserting the credits detail is absent to asserting it renders with the correct `href`, plus two new cases: an unknown host's URL stays non-clickable, and a look-alike billing path produces no action.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/ChatProviderSignal.test.tsx` — 35 passed
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat` — 20 files, 340 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck` — only the pre-existing `motion/react` error in `packages/product-ui`, which reproduces on clean `main` and is unrelated to this change.

Branch based on upstream `main` at `c9a0adb21`.

title: fix(chat): require consent before interrupting busy work
body: Closes #4423 ## Summary - require an explicit **Finish work** versus **Stop now** choice before a busy or uncertain Chat session switches to Terminal UI - keep ordinary sends plus Claude Edit/Retry work scoped to the initiating session from pending request through exact durable-turn observation - preserve accepted and in-flight work across navigation, same-route rerenders, and full Chat-surface unmount/remount - scope transition start/cancel/ack mutations, pending state, errors, and cache invalidation to their initiating session, including overlapping mutations in multiple sessions - prevent a deferred transition for session A from closing a newer consent dialog for session B - suppress rapid duplicate composer submissions without hiding genuine transport failures - retain the safe direct-drain path for confirmed-idle work ## Root cause and final review fix Chat-to-Terminal previously submitted destructive `interrupt` immediately, before asking the user whether active and queued work could be cancelled. During final independent review, a second race was found: each TanStack `MutationObserver` remembered only its most recent mutation. If session A started a transition, session B then started another, and the user returned to A, A could appear idle while its request was still pending. The final commit keys start/cancel/ack mutations and aggregates pending/error state by target session. Its public-hook regression was proven red before the fix and green afterward. ## Regression coverage MQA-05 and focused adversarial tests cover: - busy Chat showing the policy dialog before any transition request - **Finish work** waiting for running work before switching - **Stop now** interrupting only after explicit consent - pending and accepted Send/Edit/Retry work remaining busy through stale idle snapshots - accepted work remaining busy through full surface remount - in-flight requests remaining busy through a board round-trip - session navigation not transferring consent, pending state, errors, or cache invalidation - overlapping A/B transition mutations remaining independently pending - a deferred A completion not closing B's newer policy dialog - rapid double-submit invoking transport once ## Exact validation - product head: `ce9183ea87d18273efed6c6ac3b776fcab065927` - base: `be21597e7a24cbee2e6e9103ae669ff18c3b56b1` - opt-in harness head: `cc760a23ca74e8b110c12f11faa337064ca8d106` in draft PR #4419 - exact product+harness integration: `72c9e0f474cce9b709450a9fd7e28caefd2a6d02` - focused renderer tests: **222/222 passed** - full renderer: **3,013 passed, 1 intentional skip** - frontend typecheck: **passed** - E2E typecheck: **passed** - strict `MQA-05`: **2/2 passed** - backend suite: **passed** - GolangCI with an isolated cache: **0 issues** - `git diff --check`: **passed** - independent Standards review of the exact head: **approved, no findings** - independent Spec review of the exact head: **approved, no findings** - worktree: **clean** ## Native Electron evidence The real AO Electron app was exercised on macOS in isolated mode with `todo-app`, Codex, renderer `http://localhost:5173`, daemon `127.0.0.1:3002`, and AO state under `~/.ao/dev`. At `3e1d9cad0`, immediately before the final reviewer-only mutation-state commit: 1. a real Chat turn ran `sleep 30`; 2. clicking Terminal showed the required **Finish work** / **Stop now** dialog while the command was active; 3. **Finish work** kept Chat active until the command completed; 4. Terminal opened only afterward and displayed `QA_4423_EXACT_DONE` in the native conversation. The final `ce9183ea8` commit changes only session-keyed renderer mutation bookkeeping and its regression test; the complete focused/full/typecheck/strict-MQA matrix above was repeated on that exact head. **Busy Chat turn requires Finish/Stop consent** **Finish work completes before Terminal UI opens** **Returning to Chat shows the completed response in the earlier full round-trip capture** Local native screenshots remain under `~/.ao/qa/4423-native-3e1d9cad0/`; exact final strict artifacts remain under `~/.ao/qa/4423-mqa05-strict-ce9183ea8/`. They are outside the repository and uncommitted. ## Boundary Hard renderer reload/quit draft durability is owned by #4422. Within #4423 alone, a forced reload can lose richer renderer-local pending metadata, but it never grants interrupt consent: the automatic path remains drain-only. ## Harness separation This PR contains only the #4423 implementation and focused product tests. Draft PR #4419 owns the manually triggered ChatUI regression harness; it does not run automatically in CI. No screenshots, reports, traces, local AO state, or QA artifacts are committed. ## Review follow-up (`fb1bf9741`) The two remaining re-review edge cases are fixed on the latest `main`: - the accepted POST transition is written into the initiating session's cache before invalidation, so inactive queries or transient refetch failures cannot re-enable Chat controls while backend intake is fenced - transition settlement is keyed by session and transition, and each refresh has an attempt token; A → B → A navigation cannot leave settlement latched or let an older A refresh clear the restarted A settlement Added focused regressions for inactive invalidation, failed invalidation, navigation during settlement, and overlapping old/new settlement attempts. Exact-head validation: - hook regressions: **16/16 passed** - hook + SessionView matrix: **103/103 passed** - full renderer: **3,067 passed, 1 intentional skip** - frontend typecheck: **passed** - `git diff --check`: **passed** - mergeability against `main` at `5913376b1`: **MERGEABLE** - worktree: **clean** No screenshot, trace, report, or local evidence file is committed.

title: bug(update): tmux namespace changes falsely exit sessions and spawn duplicate controllers
body:
## Bug

Updating to the private hashed tmux runtime makes every pre-cutover session on tmux's legacy default socket render as **exited** when opened, even though the durable session is non-terminated/idle and the original tmux pane and supervised agent process are still alive.

This is a false terminal exit, not an agent exit. The daemon's `/mux` reports `type:"exited"` because it probes only the new private socket, and the renderer converts that frame into `[process exited]` plus the ended strip.

**Source:** live local report/triage by @AgentWrapper on 2026-08-25 (no public chat URL)
**Installed app:** `0.12.8-nightly.202608251410`
**Bundled daemon VCS revision:** `0b7758c7f19e34f00d92bb2eb306f565fa571bf4` (`vcs.modified=true`)
**Daemon:** healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Analyzed through current main:** `f3d64ab84a384fdf9ba4cbc2b992c7815af9e1f7`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P1 — existing live terminal sessions become inaccessible from the desktop after an ordinary update; Restore risks creating/replacing runtime state and is not a safe workaround.

## Exact live evidence

Seven existing sessions reproduce identically:

| Session | Display name | DB state | DB handle | Legacy pane |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-orchestrator-124` | scm pr attribution | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 23243 |
| `agent-orchestrator-147` | pr discovery nudge | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 24095 |
| `agent-orchestrator-149` | pr author avatar | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 26773 |
| `agent-orchestrator-151` | network err banner | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 26311 |
| `agent-orchestrator-152` | tab hit area fix | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 24924 |
| `agent-orchestrator-153` | readme download cta | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 25736 |
| `agent-orchestrator-154` | stacked pr no review | `idle`, `is_terminated=0` | same as session id | `pane_dead=0`, PID 25472 |

The private socket is:

```text
~/.ao/tmux-c30770fb243592f92df80569b4463182.sock
```

It contains only the newly-created `agent-orchestrator-211`. The legacy default server contains all seven sessions.

For every affected id:

```text
bundled tmux -S ~/.ao/tmux-c30770fb243592f92df80569b4463182.sock has-session -t <id>
=> can't find session: <id>

system tmux -L default has-session -t <id>
=> exit 0
```

A read-only mux open against the installed daemon reproduces the desktop result without reaching or resizing the live legacy pane:

```text
client: {"ch":"terminal","id":"agent-orchestrator-124","type":"open","cols":0,"rows":0}
server: {"ch":"terminal","id":"agent-orchestrator-124","type":"exited"}
```

The stored `runtime_launch_id` also differs from the supervisor `--launch` visible in every live legacy pane:

| Session | DB launch | Live pane launch |
|---|---|---|
| 124 | `96f06e1e-ca42-4693-adff-f176e08f89a7` | `084a9650-8d7f-4497-9877-05342ce237d3` |
| 147 | `9139a6af-fc05-47cd-9d4f-d4aa03ac1f4b` | `b9ea8bd0-434a-4003-91db-a768c603df5c` |
| 149 | `755e6cde-39eb-4973-adfb-39ce60552d6e` | `d34c593c-96c4-4dff-be3b-4997e701a953` |
| 151 | `bec6d60d-f22c-4792-86c2-852b62cad4eb` | `4087d827-87f5-4a30-9633-8c97b74050a8` |
| 152 | `0b326a64-30c0-4815-ad6b-cdb878d5ee08` | `b4b0bcc3-95ae-47c5-a070-e5b909c8e662` |
| 153 | `114a3d64-1399-49bb-8478-5d0ec23f6e56` | `bf9ee0ec-5d39-4c73-8a94-0a5e546f8086` |
| 154 | `79ef446b-e9d4-4903-93e4-2e1ab7dbd103` | `f8809754-10ee-437c-8983-36475a58aa46` |

That generation mismatch means an adoption/migration policy cannot rely on the current DB launch id alone. The pane name, worktree cwd, AO supervisor command/session id, and historical socket provenance still agree.

## Root cause

[PR #4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385) explicitly covered this upgrade path. It added `socketForSession`, probed the new socket first, then used the system tmux client with explicit `-L default` for legacy sessions, cached the chosen socket, and routed `IsAlive`, attach, output, input, restart, and destroy consistently.

[PR #4393](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4393) intentionally removed that mixed-socket routing in commit `2aeba22c0` as a strict security cutover. The PR says legacy sessions “remain running but are not adopted.” This creates the user-visible regression:

1. `runtimeselect.New` constructs one tmux adapter with only the hashed private `SocketPath`.
2. `tmux.managedArgs` pins **every** command to `-S <private-socket> -f /dev/null`.
3. `terminal.attachment` calls `IsAlive`; a missing same-named session on that private server returns `alive=false`.
4. The mux emits `type:"exited"` immediately, without checking the durable `is_terminated` fact or the legacy server.
5. `useTerminalSession` treats that frame as an actual process exit, writes `[process exited]`, and `TerminalPane` shows the ended strip.

There are no later terminal/runtime commits between the installed revision and current `main` that restore the legacy upgrade path.

## Logs and request correlation

The current packaged daemon does not persist its active stdout/stderr logs: both are Unix pipes back to Electron. `~/.ao/daemon.log` is stale (last modified 2026-06-17), so it contains no evidence for this 2026-08-25 update. macOS unified logging also returned no matching AO terminal/tmux entries.

`telemetry_event` contains no `ao.renderer.terminal_attach_failed` for this path because an `exited` frame is treated as a successful lifecycle outcome, not an attach failure. `/mux` frames carry no request id, and the successful session GET response exposes no request-id header. This leaves the false-exit attach without a correlatable persisted request id; the raw mux request/response above is the strongest direct reproduction.

## Expected behavior

An update must preserve safe terminal access to AO-owned legacy sessions while ensuring new sessions use only the hashed private socket. If ownership cannot be proven, the UI must report an explicit “legacy runtime not adopted / recovery required” error—not `process exited`—and must not offer Restore as though the pane were dead.

## Fix constraints

Do not blindly re-enable same-name adoption from the user default socket; that would regress the ownership issue fixed by [#4391](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4391). A safe migration needs explicit AO provenance/ownership and a durable socket classification, or a one-time controlled migration that does not destroy or respawn the live pane.

Until that policy exists, the minimum correctness fix is to make “absent from the new private socket during a known cutover” inconclusive/recovery-required rather than emitting `exited` for a durable non-terminated session.

## Required regression coverage

1. Start multiple AO sessions on the historical tmux default socket with live panes and distinct launch ids.
2. Persist their handles as non-terminated sessions, including a realistic stale/different DB `runtime_launch_id`.
3. Upgrade/restart into a build using the hashed private socket.
4. Assert legacy sessions are not killed, restarted, resized, or sent input during reconciliation.
5. Assert `/mux` attach to an owned legacy session returns `opened` and terminal data (or an explicit recovery-required error), never `exited` while `pane_dead=0`.
6. Spawn a new post-update session; assert it exists only on the hashed private socket and attaches there.
7. Keep both socket classes live across a second desktop restart and assert routing remains stable.
8. Add same-name collision coverage on default + private sockets and prove AO never adopts or mutates a foreign tmux session.
9. Cover missing/incompatible system tmux as inconclusive without session termination or replacement.
10. Cover a real legacy pane exit and verify that only this case produces the mux `exited` frame.

## Safe recovery guidance

Do **not** press Restore, Kill, Cleanup, or send/nudge these sessions from the affected build. Their worktrees and tmux panes are still live.

For read-only inspection, `system tmux -L default capture-pane -p -t <session>` preserves the pane. Interactive `tmux -L default attach -t <session>` bypasses AO but can resize the pane and accepts input, so it is not a read-only diagnostic.

A build based on the post-[#4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385), pre-[#4393](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4393) behavior can reattach through `-L default`, but changing installed builds/restarting should only be done after preserving state and validating that startup reconciliation will not respawn or replace these handles.

## Related

- [#4382](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4382) — bundled tmux terminfo regression; similar post-update attach symptom, different root cause.
- [PR #4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385) — implemented the exact legacy-default + private-socket mixed upgrade path, later removed.
- [#4391](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4391) / [PR #4393](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4393) — ownership isolation and the intentional strict cutover that introduced this regression.
- [#4417](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4417) — stale staged tmux binary can also break private-socket attachment, but does not explain these sessions being present and live only on `-L default`.

title: feat: add durable scheduled automations
body:
Code changes: +3551 -41  
Tests: +2309 -3  
Others: +2857 -6  

## What

Adds Phase C durable scheduled automations across the Go daemon, SQLite storage, HTTP API, CLI, and Electron supervisor.

- Creates, lists, updates, enables/disables, deletes, and inspects automation run history.
- Supports daily, weekly, cron-subset, and custom recurring schedules in named IANA timezones.
- Materializes durable occurrences with bounded catch-up, leases, non-overlap, restart reconciliation, and session linkage.
- Adds the AO-styled Automations route, creation dialog, inline validation, keyboard-friendly time entry, run history, toggles, and destructive confirmation.

## Why

AO needs unattended recurring sessions that survive daemon restarts, preserve run history, respect local wall-clock time across DST, and launch through the same session boundary as manual work.

## How

- SQLite definitions and run rows are the durable source of truth; unique occurrence keys and transactional claims prevent duplicate dispatch.
- A daemon observer reconciles startup state, projects session completion, materializes at most three missed occurrences, and dispatches eligible runs.
- Session launch completion is persisted separately from the automation origin marker. Crash-surviving seed rows are never treated as successful launches; incomplete launches are torn down after lease expiry and recorded as failed.
- The packaged daemon embeds IANA timezone data. Finite COUNT/UNTIL rules, conflicting embedded TZIDs, and schedules capable of sub-minute execution are rejected explicitly.
- Latest run summaries are loaded in one batched storage query; expanded run history polls and displays fetch failures.
- Frontend strings use AO's locale catalogs, and the shell/sidebar route identity follows existing desktop patterns.

Intentional scope: finite RRULEs are rejected because Phase C models recurring definitions with a non-null future cursor. The cron compatibility surface is deliberately limited to minute/hour plus optional weekday expressions rather than silently translating unsupported cron semantics.

## Testing

Passed after rebasing onto current upstream main:

- `go test ./... -run '^$'`
- `go test ./internal/service/automation ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/httpd ./internal/cli ./internal/observe/automations ./internal/storage/sqlite ./internal/lifecycle -count=1`

title: macOS updater can remain indefinitely at the last progress value when a download stalls
body:
## Bug

On macOS, an electron-updater download can stop receiving bytes while Settings remains indefinitely in `downloading` at the last emitted percentage. There is no timeout, terminal status, retry guidance, or indication that the displayed progress is stale.

**Source:** Live maintainer report during terminal-regression containment, 2026-08-25
**Observed:** macOS, installed `0.12.8-nightly.202608251410`, bundled commit `0b7758c7f19e34f00d92bb2eb306f565fa571bf4`, Updates channel `latest`
**Target:** stable `0.12.7`
**Confidence:** Medium — the persistent partial transfer and missing UI watchdog are confirmed; the reason Electron stopped receiving bytes is not yet isolated.
**Priority:** Medium — update is blocked and the UI never reaches an actionable error, but restarting/retrying may recover it.

## Reproduction / exact evidence

1. Start installed `0.12.8-nightly.202608251410` with Updates enabled and channel `latest`.
2. Because `allowDowngrade = true`, the updater offers stable `0.12.7`.
3. Observe Settings report download progress around 2% indefinitely.

On the affected instance:

- App PID `79499` started `2026-08-25T22:06:20Z`; updater progress began immediately.
- Target asset `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.7.zip` is 168,658,927 bytes.
- Partial cache file `~/Library/Caches/agent-orchestrator-updater/pending/temp-Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.7.zip` stopped at 3,798,105 bytes (2.25%), mtime `2026-08-25T22:06:27Z`.
- Electron's helper retained an `ESTABLISHED` TCP connection to GitHub (`185.199.110.133:443`) with zero receive queue, but the partial file did not advance.
- An independent 1 MiB HTTP range request against the exact same release asset completed with HTTP 206 in 0.537 seconds at about 1.95 MB/s. The GitHub asset and machine's general network path were available.
- The two regressed `0.12.8` nightly releases had already been drafted, so the stable-channel target was the published stable release, not a removed nightly asset.

No app restart, updater-cache deletion, or release mutation was performed during collection.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts` publishes `downloading` only when electron-updater emits `download-progress`, and replaces it only on a later progress, `update-downloaded`, or `error` event. There is no inactivity watchdog around `downloadUpdate()` or automatic downloads. If Electron leaves the request established without emitting an error, the renderer displays the last percentage forever.

The lower-level reason this fresh Electron network request stopped after 3.8 MB remains to be isolated. This differs from a missing release manifest or unavailable asset.

## Suggested fix

- Track the timestamp of the last download-progress event.
- If no bytes/progress arrive for a bounded interval, publish a terminal/retryable stalled state and cancel or safely retry the updater request if electron-updater supports it.
- Ensure a retry does not create concurrent downloads and preserves request-ID ownership.
- Include target version, transferred bytes, total bytes, and time since progress in telemetry.
- Test stalled automatic and manual downloads with fake timers, including recovery after later progress and after retry.

## Related

- [#3526](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3526) — Chromium updater network stack can wedge until restart; this report is a fresh process with a silently stalled transfer rather than immediate `net::ERR_FAILED`.
- [#4291](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4291) — update card feedback can make working downloads look inert; here the cached bytes confirm the download itself stopped.
- [#4284](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4284) — stale renderer feedback/request correlation.

title: fix(updates): never resolve a prerelease update through a draft release
body:
Stacked on #4397. Base is `ao/ao-41/sidebar-update-action`, so this diff is just the one commit; retarget to `main` once #4397 merges.

## The bug, observed in production

GitHub's `releases.atom` lists **draft** releases, and electron-updater discovers prereleases through that feed. Draft assets are not public, so the channel manifest 404s. On the automatic path that error is deliberately swallowed, so the install silently goes stale against a release the user could never have downloaded.

Checked against the live feed on 2026-08-25, the newest atom entry was the draft `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410`:

```
nightly-mac.yml -> 404
latest-mac.yml  -> 404   (electron-updater's fallback)
```

Meanwhile `v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` was published, complete and downloadable. Every nightly install was aiming at the draft and reporting nothing.

## What this changes

The nightly channel already sidesteps the atom feed by resolving the newest completed release through the API, which filters `draft: false` and requires the platform manifest. A **pinned feature build did not**: `configureFeed` sets `allowPrerelease` for `pr<N>` and leaves discovery to the atom feed, so a draft `pr<N>` build strands the pin the same way.

This generalizes the resolver from `"nightly"` to any prerelease channel and routes feature pins through it. Stable is untouched: it resolves via `/releases/latest`, which excludes drafts and prereleases by definition, so it takes no extra request.

## Tests

- A pinned feature build skips a draft `pr<N>` release and resolves the newest published one, and the pin still outranks a newer nightly. **Confirmed to fail without the production change.**
- A draft nightly is skipped in favour of the newest published release. This one **passes without the change** and is labelled in the source as a regression guard rather than new behaviour, since nightly draft filtering already existed. It is pinned because the atom feed really does list drafts, making this filter the only thing between a prerelease install and an undownloadable release.

65/65 `auto-updater.test.ts`, 162/162 across the update-related files, `frontend:typecheck` clean.

## Scope

This is the **client half only**. It stops a draft from stranding an install. It does not stop drafts appearing in the feed, and it cannot fix a release pipeline that publishes a build and later returns it to draft.

Two things seen while investigating that this PR does not address, and that no workflow in this repository appears to own (there is no nightly release workflow here):

- A **draft build was downloaded onto a real machine** (`0.12.8-nightly.202608251410`, 168MB, staged 2026-08-25 20:03) while the release is a draft now and its assets 404. That implies the build was published and later returned to draft.
- Two **published** nightlies, `202608241447` and `202608242034`, carry **no mac manifest at all**, so they 404 the same way for any client that selects them.

Both look like release-pipeline problems and probably deserve their own issue.

title: ci: guard the nightly feed head the way stable is guarded
body:
## Why

`release-latest-guard.yml` protects the stable channel from a `/releases/latest` that electron-updater cannot install from. Nightly had no equivalent, and nightly is the channel that actually breaks. Of the six nightlies cut between 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-25:

| Release | State | Manifests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410` | draft | **missing** |
| `v0.12.8-nightly.202608250759` | draft | ok |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` | published | ok |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608242034` | **published** | **missing** |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608241447` | **published** | **missing** |
| `v0.12.7-nightly.202608241408` | published | ok |

Any one of these at the head of the feed strands **every** nightly install.

electron-updater discovers prereleases through `releases.atom`, takes the **first** entry matching the channel, fetches that release's manifest, and on 404 retries exactly one fallback before giving up. It never walks to the next entry. So one bad release at the top wedges every client even with a good release directly beneath it — which is the current state:

```
feed head:      v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410
  nightly-mac.yml -> 404
  latest-mac.yml  -> 404   (the single fallback)
  => ERR_UPDATER_CHANNEL_FILE_NOT_FOUND, gives up

one entry down: v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031
  nightly-mac.yml -> 200   (never reached)
```

The failure is invisible. Automatic check errors are suppressed by design, so affected installs show nothing at all and simply stop updating. On one machine this had been going on for two days across an app restart.

## What it does

Fails when the nightly feed head is a draft, or is missing `nightly.yml` / `nightly-mac.yml` / `nightly-linux.yml`, and says what to do about it.

It reads `releases.atom`, not the API, on purpose: the API omits drafts, the Atom feed lists them, and a draft's assets are not public, so a draft at the head 404s for everyone. Checking the API would miss exactly the case that broke this week.

Same shape as the stable guard: hourly schedule, release triggers, and the `github.repository` condition so forks do not fail red.

## Verified against the live feed

Ran the check logic against real releases:

- `v0.12.8-nightly.202608251410` (draft, no manifests) → **fails**, reports the draft
- `v0.12.7-nightly.202608242034` (published, no manifests) → **fails**, names the three missing files
- `v0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` → passes
- `v0.12.7-nightly.202608241408` → passes

So it catches both real failure modes and does not fire on healthy releases. Note this guard will fail on `main` until the current feed head is fixed — that is the point, not a defect in the workflow.

## Scope

This detects the breakage; it does not prevent it. Nightlies are cut by hand (`frontend-nightly.yml` was removed in #3070) and the manifest generation is a separate step from the artifact publish, which is what makes it easy to skip. Automating the nightly cut so the manifests cannot be forgotten is the real fix and is a larger change than this.

Related: #4397 and #4462 harden the client so it skips drafts and manifest-less releases and resolves to the newest installable one. This guards the release side; those guard the client side.

## Latest fix — Claude queued/delayed Stop identity

[Commit `c6f7c1967`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/c6f7c1967e6b6e392c3b63c885fbfba753265343) stays in this PR. **Queued completed-turn handoff is now natively verified. This is not blanket merge approval:** interrupted native turns, marker-write recovery, and the other outstanding cases in the historical record remain unresolved. Current-head CI has started; previous-head green checks are not this commit's result.

**Problem:** Claude `UserPromptSubmit` for queued B reports executing A's `prompt_id`. Stop A then arrives before Stop B. Matching only that ID—or the latest prompt text—can certify B's prompt with A's answer, permanently blocking TUI → Chat.

**Fix:** give each submission a UUID via the prompt hook's `additionalContext`, and persist that same UUID with the activity observation. Claude stores the hook attachment under the actual native user UUID. After the source stops, the Claude adapter verifies all retained submissions/Stops against native transcript ancestry. Chat admission requires the latest exact native user UUID and its answer in completed ACP replay. It retains AO's durable history boundary and explicit consent for legacy/untrusted text. Claude Stop alone no longer marks the display prompt complete.

This adds a small per-prompt context marker and a durable evidence column. It is not invisible/free context. Missing native identities, unsupported/compacted ancestry, old trusted checkpoints without witnesses, pending/interrupted turns, or evidence overflow **fail closed**, not silently repaired. Limits: 512 observations, 64 MiB transcript, 4 MiB record. Hook reporting still does not guarantee delivery during persistent failures.

## Problem

TUI → Chat could get stuck on **“Interface switch failed” (AO-2L)** even when the provider's conversation history was valid.

AO used `latest_user_prompt` / `latest_assistant_update` as replay checkpoints without knowing which conversation, runtime generation, or hook event produced them. Stale text, subagent output, or AO coordination prompts could become mandatory history matches. Retrying kept hitting the same mismatch.

## Fix

- **Track checkpoint provenance:** persist conversation ID, runtime generation, event origin, and trust. Main-agent origin is checked, but this alone does **not** verify Claude turn identity; delayed Stop remains unresolved.
- **Separate stale text from real history conflicts:** **Use provider history** can bypass a legacy/untrusted text mismatch. Trusted checkpoints, native-conversation identity, pending turns, and AO's durable replay boundary remain strict.
- **Make recovery explicit and race-safe:** show **Retry / Use provider history / Stay in Terminal**. Bind consent to the exact failed transition, import without duplicate turns, and confirm the target controller has stopped before retry or rollback. Unconfirmed shutdown requires a restart.

Result: an old checkpoint without trustworthy conversation/runtime metadata can be bypassed with explicit **Use provider history** consent. This does **not** bypass trusted mismatches or fix every TUI → Chat failure; current-head QA below still found failures.

Closes #4424.

**Limits:** no OS-level unkillable-process injection, mobile UI, native Terminal `/fork`, exhaustive provider/auth/network outages, or long soak. Shutdown fencing has deterministic race-test coverage. Historical user-level Claude hooks referenced a missing old `ao.js`; global configuration was left untouched, so hook-related attribution needs a clean-config follow-up.

<details>

These are September 12 captures at `9a34cdad2`, not before/after comparisons. Files are GitHub attachments, never committed.

**5. Passing Codex Chat-start edit control:** the edited branch accepts a new native Terminal turn; that reply is imported once on returning to Chat.

</details>

## Historical observations

| Scenario | Provider | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Stop now and switch** during a busy Terminal turn; subsequent idle retries, a new successful turn, and restart still failed. | Claude Code | Original [#4424 reproduction](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4424): five persistent `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` / AO-2L failures. |
| A cancelled prompt remained in `latest_user_prompt` for four days, although it was absent from completed provider history. No interruption during the switch was needed. | Claude Code | [September 11 field report](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4424#issuecomment-5636832085): eight failures at ~46s; clearing that field allowed the same session to switch in 2.6s. Main's #5248 narrow guard is preserved here. |
| Deliberately injected a nonexistent legacy checkpoint into an otherwise valid conversation. | Claude Code | Native screenshots below: strict switch rejects; explicit **Use provider history** succeeds. Controlled fault injection, not a natural failure. |
| Exchanged ~2 Terminal messages, then switched to Chat without AO-2L or lost history. | Codex | [August 26 reviewer report](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4466#issuecomment-5431084085). Historical happy-path verification, not a fresh current-head run or proof of every recovery failure path. |

Stale-generation, subagent, coordination-prompt, and missed-prompt-hook cases also have deterministic contracts. Those tests use simulated provider events; they are not native Claude/Codex observations. The historical natural failures in this table were Claude cases; the fresh Codex failure is documented separately in current-head QA above.

## Editing a previous message, then switching again

Relevant flow: **TUI → Chat → edit earlier message → TUI → Chat**, including additional switches before the edit.

An AO-managed edit is different from invoking `/fork` directly in Terminal: it updates the active branch and session's `provider_conversation_id` together. The expected round-trip resumes the **edited branch**, not its parent; an edit alone should not cause a handle mismatch.

A native fork preserves provider-owned history. Without native fork support, AO can create a new provider conversation seeded with earlier textual context (`approximate_context`); that is not an exact copy of the provider transcript. Both paths need round-trip verification.

**Coverage by revision:** the initial `9a34cdad2` matrix above remains a historical failure record. #5302 subsequently verified the imported-origin edit and its edited-branch roundtrip; #5322 verified the false-draft fix. The September 13 integration above additionally verifies the original-branch revisit. These are focused passing cases, not a claim that every edit, interruption, or native fork works.

<details>
<summary>Other switch errors that remain possible</summary>

These are implemented failure conditions, not newly reproduced failures on both providers.

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Legacy/untrusted checkpoint text is absent from provider replay. | `TARGET_HISTORY_UNTRUSTED_TEXT_MISMATCH`; explicit provider-history recovery is available for this mismatch only. |
| Replay lacks trusted completed work, has an unresolved turn boundary, or conflicts with trusted checkpoint identity. | `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`; provider-history consent cannot waive the safety check. |
| Active Chat branch, session resume handle, or returned provider ID disagree. | Resume fails; provider-history consent does not reconcile different conversations. |
| Native transcript is missing, or the current Terminal launch has not confirmed its conversation ID. | `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` / `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED`; switching is blocked. |
| Provider history is unavailable, resume fails, or provider/auth/binary prerequisites fail. | `TARGET_HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE`, `TARGET_RESUME_FAILED`, or the corresponding preflight error. |
| AO cannot confirm the target controller stopped. | `TARGET_STOP_UNCONFIRMED`; restart required, with input/switching blocked to prevent concurrent controllers. |

</details>

## Validation

**Fresh September 12 runs at the same head:** 165 frontend tests passed across interface-switch, SessionView and transition-hook suites; race-enabled edit/history/transition/lifecycle suites passed; additional provider-history/shutdown race tests passed; SQLite edit/branch/history tests passed. These green automated suites did **not** catch all four native failures above. No product edits or new commits were made in this QA run.

Head `9a34cdad2`: **13/13 CI checks passed**, including [full Go race tests](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34665073118/job/103475209567), [frontend tests](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34665073107/job/103475209396) (4,449 passed, 6 existing skips), typechecks, lint, and API/sqlc drift. Independent Standards + Spec reviews: no actionable findings.

<details>
<summary>Local validation details</summary>

Passed: 169 backend packages without race detection, build/vet, focused backend tests, and 147 focused UI tests. Broad local frontend/race runs had timing failures under heavy host load; some follow-up checks were stopped. Those runs are not claimed as passing. The exact-head CI suites above completed successfully.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Historical screenshots — earlier heads and controlled renderer fixture</summary>

Real Electron + Claude Code against an isolated `todo-app` session. The legacy mismatch was deliberately injected into disposable QA data; this is controlled reproduction, not a naturally occurring failure. Images are attachments, not committed files.

**1. Strict rejection + recovery actions** — native capture at `9a726bc59`. Provider history lacks the injected legacy prompt, so the strict switch rejects it and preserves Terminal.

![Strict history mismatch with recovery actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd932493-5885-4153-85ab-d775cb3e545e)

**2. Explicit recovery succeeds** — same session and revision. After **Use provider history**, the original Terminal reply appears once in ChatUI.

![Same conversation recovered into ChatUI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50f67143-3246-44b5-b821-d1abdf694cb3)

**3. Recovery + continued chatting on the main-based branch** — native capture at `445d399d7`, based on main `e2417dc8e`. Top: imported `QA4466_LATEST_MAIN_NATIVE` turn. Bottom: new `QA4466_LATEST_MAIN_CHAT` reply. SQL checks confirmed one user/assistant pair per marker; composer cleared. Main's separate #5274 composer fix is included unchanged.

![Recovered Terminal turn followed by a new successful Chat turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5d8a165-9e7c-4cf5-a3e6-b419b5d7078d)

These are earlier native captures, **not fresh screenshots of cleanup head `9a34cdad2`**. That head's automated validation is listed above.

**4. Unconfirmed shutdown blocks further switching** — controlled renderer fixture, **not a real provider shutdown failure**. `TARGET_STOP_UNCONFIRMED` shows a restart instruction and disables Terminal interaction; retry/cancel cannot bypass it. Backend tests separately cover controller shutdown ordering.

![Unconfirmed shutdown requires restart and blocks Terminal input](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da14d44d-0afd-4bd0-a9ba-19615acea0de)

</details>

## Remaining focused follow-up

1. Land/review the separately verified #5301 fix in #5322; it retains rejection of real unsent drafts.
2. Preserve native Claude interruption provenance so busy-stop switching can validate the real interrupted turn safely.
3. Determine the original missed Codex hook cause; the exact-turn fix above prevents matching a different occurrence but does not recover identity missing from old stored checkpoints.

No mobile provider-history consent controls; blocked-state presentation and manual status recheck are included. The manual local QA harness stays in draft #4419 and is not enabled on CI. title: chore(desktop): frontend/package.json version (0.10.3) is stuck, doesn't track GitHub release tags (v0.12.7)
body:
## Problem

`frontend/package.json`'s `version` on `main` is stuck at **0.10.3**, while the latest published GitHub release is **v0.12.7** (and nightly is already past `v0.12.8`).

```
$ git show origin/main:frontend/package.json | grep version
	"version": "0.10.3",

$ gh release list --repo Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator --limit 1 --exclude-pre-releases
v0.12.7	Latest	v0.12.7	2026-08-25T05:57:51Z
```

This is the same class of bug as #1586 and #1957 (a package version field on `main` drifting out of sync with what's actually published/tagged) — just recurring in a different spot now that the repo layout has moved to `frontend/package.json` + Electron/`electron-forge` packaging instead of the old npm workspace.

## Why it matters

The desktop app's Settings → Updates screen reads `CFBundleShortVersionString`, which electron-forge derives from `frontend/package.json`'s `version`. So every build — including official releases — shows "Current version — v0.10.3" regardless of what's actually running, making the in-app version display useless for diagnosing which build a user has.

## Fix

Bump `frontend/package.json`'s `version` to track the release tag going forward (ideally as part of whatever step cuts a GitHub release), same acceptance criteria as #1586:

- [ ] `frontend/package.json`'s `version` on `main` matches (or is ≥) the latest published release tag
- [ ] The in-app Settings → Updates screen shows a version that corresponds to the actual release

## Related
- #1586 — same defect class, old npm-workspace `packages/*/package.json`
- #1957 — same defect class, nightly snapshot versioning

title: fix(chat): clarify live file references
body: Code changes: +115 -88 Tests: +113 -10 Others: +32 -0 ## Summary - describe selected `@file` chips as localized, focusable path references instead of implying that file contents were attached - expose the complete worktree-relative path and path-only semantics on pointer hover, keyboard focus, and through accessibility APIs - share the existing workspace-file cache, keep cached suggestions available after a refresh failure, surface load/refresh failures, and poll only while recovery is needed - reject filenames containing carriage returns or line feeds because they cannot round-trip as one atomic token through the plain-text composer ## Already present on `main` Comparative native-Electron testing found that `main` already provides: - basename file chips after selection - parent-directory labels and duplicate-basename disambiguation in the suggestion menu - plain worktree-relative path serialization, including quoting paths containing spaces - live create, rename, and delete updates through the existing workspace event stream This PR preserves those behaviors. It does not introduce the chip, duplicate-name labels, path-only transport, or live refresh. ## Root cause The existing composer renders an attachment-shaped basename chip while serializing only ordinary relative-path text. On `main`, the selected chip has no path-reference accessible name or description, is skipped by Tab, and offers no full-path explanation after selection. The user therefore cannot discover from the selected token that AO did not attach or embed the file contents. ## Verification Exact candidate: `700d81ccd97709f7d7d00eb1a54502257901c637` - real Electron comparison against `main` (`768ab5034b9815e76edbc936e14a4780beec8fc9`) using the same isolated session - `main`: selected chips are not keyboard-focusable and expose no path-only description; duplicate-name labels and live create/rename/delete already work - PR: Tab focuses the selected chip and pointer hover/focus exposes its full path and path-only description - PR: a real filename containing a line feed is excluded from suggestions - focused renderer suite: **4 files / 185 tests passed** - explicit pointer-hover tooltip test: **1 passed** - `npm run typecheck`: passed - `git diff --check`: passed Failure/recovery states are covered by component tests rather than a manufactured live-daemon outage: initial load failure is announced, cached suggestions remain usable with a stale-data warning after refresh failure, and polling runs only while recovery is needed. ## Native Electron evidence ### New behavior: selected chips disclose their actual semantics Pressing Tab focuses the chip and exposes the complete path-reference-only explanation. Pointer hover exposes the same tooltip. ### Preserved behavior: transport remains ordinary path text The daemon snapshot contains a relative path string and no embedded content, attachment, or resource payload. This is the pre-existing transport contract that the new chip description now states truthfully. ```json { "role": "user", "text": "packages/mobile/lib/config.ts please echo the referenced path only.", "content": null, "attachments": null, "resources": null } ``` ## Deliberate simplification Draft restoration keeps canonical path text instead of persisting renderer-only semantic token ranges. Semantic draft persistence can be added later if product requirements explicitly require chips to survive a remount. Closes #4426

title: bug(desktop): #4465's revert is backend-only — main.ts still sets AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME, so packaged builds still strand legacy default-socket sessions
body:
## Problem

#4465 reverted the backend half of the private-hashed-tmux-socket migration (#4393) — `runtimeselect.New()` now calls `tmux.New(tmux.Options{})` with no `SocketPath`, so `socketForSession`'s `r.socketName` is empty by default and legacy sessions are found directly on the machine's default socket.

However, the desktop Electron main process still independently opts every packaged launch back into the private socket:

```
frontend/src/main.ts:845
...(bundledTmuxBinary ? { AO_TMUX_BINARY: bundledTmuxBinary, AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME: "ao" } : {}),
```

`tmux.New` reads `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME` from the environment when `Options.SocketName` is empty (`tmux.go:287-289`), so any packaged desktop build with a staged bundled tmux binary — the common case — still runs with `socketName = "ao"`, and hits the exact symptom #4465 set out to fix.

## Reproduce

On a machine with tmux sessions that predate this whole migration (i.e. living only on the default socket):

```
$ /path/to/bundled/tmux -L ao has-session -t <session-id>
error connecting to /private/tmp/tmux-<uid>/ao (No such file or directory)

$ /path/to/bundled/tmux -L default has-session -t <session-id>
(exit 0 — session is alive)
```

`socketForSession` (`tmux.go`) only crosses the migration boundary to the legacy default socket when the private-socket probe output matches `sessionMissingOutput` ("can't find session"/"session not found") or `serverNotRunningOutput` ("no server running"). Neither matches "error connecting ... No such file or directory" — the exact message tmux gives when the private socket file was never created, which is guaranteed on first launch of a build with this env var reintroduced against pre-existing legacy sessions. The probe returns `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, and every legacy session's terminal pane shows "Terminal disconnected — reattaching…" indefinitely, with `reconcile: reap pass failed` / `reaper: probe error reported as failed fact` log spam for every session.

## Why this survived #4465's testing

#4465's revert is real and correct for the backend default, but its own repro/verification path (`env -u AO_TMUX_BINARY ... npm run lint` etc., per the PR body) unsets `AO_TMUX_BINARY`, which also disables the `bundledTmuxBinary` branch in `main.ts` that sets `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME`. So the revert's own verification never exercises the actual packaged-desktop code path where the symptom reappears.

## Fix options

- Drop the `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME: "ao"` half of `main.ts:845` (keep `AO_TMUX_BINARY` only) so the packaged desktop app matches the reverted backend default, or
- If the private socket is still wanted opportunistically from the desktop launcher, extend `socketForSession`'s migration-boundary check to also treat "error connecting ... no such file or directory" as definitive (this is what a private socket that was simply never created looks like — distinct from a running server going transiently unreachable, which the existing `transientServerFailureOutput`/#3475 guard is right to keep ambiguous).

## Verification after fix

On a machine with pre-existing default-socket sessions, launch the packaged desktop app and confirm the terminal pane attaches immediately instead of showing "Terminal disconnected — reattaching…", and `daemon.log` has no `reconcile reap ...: probe: ... liveness probe inconclusive: error connecting` entries for those sessions.

## Related
- #4465 (this issue's cause — the backend-only revert)
- #4393 (original migration)

title: bug(chat): selected composer text has no visible highlight
body:
## Bug

Dragging across text already typed into the Chat composer creates a real DOM selection, but the highlight is effectively invisible. Users cannot tell which part of a draft is selected before replacing, cutting, or copying it.

**Source:** AO chat report on 2026-08-26 | **Analyzed against:** `c4abb8afc4a305fbd20c6d3955a2c7808d78e7d4` | **AO version:** `dev` (desktop `0.10.3`)
**OS reproduced on:** macOS 26.5, arm64 | **Daemon:** ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Priority:** P2 — draft editing is significantly degraded; keyboard-only selection is possible but still has no visual confirmation.
**Confidence:** High — the exact pointer path is automated, the DOM range remains non-collapsed, and the rendered selection/surface contrast is measured.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Chat-mode session with an existing conversation.
2. Type a multi-word draft in the composer.
3. Drag the pointer across part or all of the draft.
4. Observe that no visible highlight appears, even though `window.getSelection()` contains a non-collapsed range.

The focused Playwright reproduction types a wrapped draft, drag-selects it through actual pointer events, verifies the DOM selection, then measures the composited selection-highlight contrast. On current `main` it fails:

```text
Expected: >= 1.5
Received:    1.013160847557346
```

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ComposerEditor.tsx` styles selected text with:

```text
selection:bg-accent/30
```

In Tailwind's theme bridge, `accent` is the subtle surface token (`--accent`), not the stronger product accent. In the light theme it is `oklch(0.967 0.001 286.375)` over the composer's `oklch(0.985 0 0)` card surface. At 30% alpha the composited contrast is only `1.013:1`, so the browser paints a valid selection that looks unselected.

This was introduced with the Lexical composer in [PR #4331](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4331), commit `b8e3d57f25`.

## Fix

Use a theme-aware foreground/primary selection tint with enough alpha to remain visibly distinct from the composer surface, and keep an E2E regression that proves both:

- pointer drag creates a durable selection of the typed draft;
- the composited highlight/surface contrast is at least `1.5:1`.

## Evidence

Before — the draft is selected in the DOM, but no highlight is perceptible:

![Before: invisible chat composer selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/before.png)

After — the same automated pointer selection is visibly highlighted:

![After: visible chat composer selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/after.png)

## Impact

- Users cannot safely replace or cut a portion of a drafted instruction.
- Copy/cut may operate on text with no visible confirmation of the range.
- The failure looks like pointer selection is broken even though the browser selection model is working.

## Related

- [#4268](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4268) — read-only surfaces inherit `user-select: none`; adjacent symptom, different mechanism. The composer already computes `user-select: text`.
- [PR #4443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4443) — restores selection on read-only content surfaces; it does not change the composer's selection highlight.

title: fix(chat): make composer selection visible
body:
Fixes #4471

## Summary

- use an explicit inverse semantic selection pair so both the highlight and selected draft text remain visible in every supported theme
- add a T0 Playwright regression that fills the real chat composer, pointer-drags across wrapped text, asserts a non-collapsed DOM selection, and checks both contrast relationships across every supported palette

## TDD reproduction

Before the styling change, the new test reproduced the report: the pointer drag selected the text, but the original composited highlight contrast was only 1.013:1.

The first review follow-up expanded the regression to all nine supported styles in light and dark mode. The prior 25% primary tint failed that 18-combination matrix at 1.279:1 on Gruvbox light, so it was increased to 45%.

The second review follow-up added the selected-text assertion before changing the implementation. That assertion failed with the 45% primary tint at 2.275:1 in Solarized dark. The final `selection:bg-foreground selection:text-background` pair gives the limiting Solarized dark case 4.111:1 highlight-to-surface contrast and 4.748:1 selected-text-to-highlight contrast.

After the change, the same pointer-drag test passes consistently across all 18 combinations (3/3 serial repeated runs).

## Visual proof

![Visible and readable text selection in the chat composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/after.png)

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- focused Playwright composer-selection regression, 3/3 serial repeated runs
- real Electron dev launch using isolated AO data on 127.0.0.1:3012; daemon, main, preload, and renderer bundles launched successfully
- user verified the fixed selection behavior in the native app

title: feat(terminal): add native macOS PTY host
body:
## Summary

- launch new macOS TUI sessions in a detached native PTY host and stream raw terminal bytes over the existing loopback protocol
- preserve every persisted unprefixed macOS runtime handle on tmux; version only newly created direct-host handles
- retain styled viewport reads, process supervision, replay, resize, input, teardown, restart, daemon-restart recovery, and a tmux creation fallback
- serialize registry updates so concurrent host starts cannot lose recovery entries
- show macOS direct-terminal scrollback with a slim app-owned, draggable thumb that is not suppressed by the OS auto-hide preference
- hide the thumb for alternate-screen TUIs, so legacy tmux sessions keep their existing behavior and never gain misleading scrollback chrome

## Compatibility and rollout

- Existing macOS agent sessions are never migrated in place and continue through tmux.
- New macOS sessions use the native PTY host; a host startup failure falls back to tmux with an unprefixed handle.
- Linux remains on tmux and Windows remains on the existing ConPTY host.
- No dependency changes, xterm upgrade, or advanced wheel tuning are included.
- tmux remains available for legacy macOS handles and fallback.

## Verification

- `go test ./...`
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run` — 0 issues
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/runtimeselect`
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/runtimeselect ./internal/terminal`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — 61 passed
- focused Playwright scrollbar test — visible normal-buffer thumb, pointer drag, alternate-screen suppression
- real Electron macOS check — direct shell with 500 output lines, wheel scroll, thumb geometry, and pointer drag
- Windows amd64 cross-compile: conpty and runtimeselect tests
- Linux amd64 cross-compile: conpty tests
- macOS end-to-end host test: detached re-exec, real PTY, env propagation, input/output streaming, resize, request-context independence, and teardown

## Preview bug fix

- Fixes #4538: percent-decodes direct-host shell handles at the HTTP boundary, restoring close-button, Command-W, and rename behavior without changing persisted handles.
- Verified through the generated frontend client and the real isolated Electron UI; closing removes both the tab and its PTY.

## Preview polish follow-up

- Fixes [#4539](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4539): removes a closing terminal tab optimistically while retaining safe rollback when a live PTY fails to close.
- Removes the duplicate chat-terminal wrapper inset so TerminalPane remains the single owner of the left content gutter.
- Makes the macOS overlay thumb appear during scrolling or dragging and fade 700 ms after interaction goes idle; edge hover still exposes the draggable control.
- Adds mutation, idle-fade, and chat-layout regression coverage. The full renderer suite passes: 2,130 tests.
- Native isolated Electron verification measured the tab leaving the DOM before the 204 response and the thumb transitioning from visible during scrolling to fully hidden after idle.
- No dependencies changed.


## Immediate shell UX follow-up

- Publishes the shell returned by the open request directly into the terminal list, eliminating the extra list round trip before a new tab can render.
- Requests keyboard focus whenever an auxiliary shell becomes active, including shells inside Chat sessions.
- Removes a closing shell pill before an in-flight list query finishes cancelling, while preserving rollback for real close failures.
- Keeps replay coalescing and tail reveal intact but makes the replay cover permanently silent, so users never see `Loading latest output...`.
- Preserves native xterm normal-buffer wheel scrolling and the requestAnimationFrame-throttled macOS thumb; no wheel multiplier, xterm upgrade, or dependency change is included.
- Verification: frontend typecheck; focused terminal tests (263 passed); full renderer suite (152 files, 2,173 tests).



## Terminal search follow-up

- Adds an AO-native find overlay backed by the already-installed xterm SearchAddon; no dependency or transport changes.
- Opens from Command/Ctrl+F or the terminal context menu, searches incrementally, reports the active/total match count, and supports case-sensitive and regular-expression modes.
- Enter and Shift+Enter, Command/Ctrl+G and Command/Ctrl+Shift+G, or visible previous/next buttons navigate matches; Escape and the close button clear decorations and return focus to the terminal.
- Validates regular expressions before search and contains the known xterm narrow-grid decoration exception so a search cannot take down the terminal surface.
- Adds localized UI strings for all eight AO locales.
- Verification: frontend typecheck; targeted terminal/i18n tests (81 passed); full renderer suite (152 files, 2,180 tests).

title: feat(mobile): over-the-air JS updates via EAS Update
body:
## What

Adds `expo-updates` + EAS Update so JS-only changes reach installed builds without a store release. Native changes still go through the store.

- Cold start: checks in the background, applies on the next launch. Never blocks the splash.
- Back from 15+ minutes in the background: applies a downloaded update (a JS reload; sessions live in the daemon), otherwise checks silently. Same as Bluesky / CodePush `ON_NEXT_RESUME`. Shorter absences do nothing, so nobody is reloaded mid-prompt. No banner.
- Settings → About → App updates: manual check / restart. Version row and bug reports now carry update id, channel and runtime; the build number is read from the binary (with `appVersionSource: remote` the old row had none).
- Dev builds: `expo-updates` is disabled, so all of this is inert.

## Runtime version

`fingerprint` rather than `appVersion`: native modules have landed on `main` between version stamps, and a fingerprint makes any native change a new runtime automatically, so an update can't reach a build that lacks the native code it calls. `fingerprint.config.js` ignores `google-services.json`, which is gitignored and differs between a laptop, CI and EAS Build; without that the Android hash differs per machine. Verified with `runtimeversion:resolve`.

## Privacy

Each check sends platform, runtime, channel, current update id and a random per-install UUID (`EAS-Client-ID`) to `u.expo.dev`. No user or daemon data. The store privacy policy should name Expo before the next store build.

## Activation

Nothing happens until a build with this config exists. Publishing is a local, deliberate step (`eas update --channel <c> --environment <c> -m "..."`, see the README); there is no CI publish and no Expo token in the repo.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (495, 18 new); `npx expo export` for both platforms
- Release builds on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator, against a local expo-updates protocol server: cold-start download, applied on the next launch, still running after the server reports no update. On iOS a deliberately broken bundle rolled back to the embedded one.
- The Android build's runtime version matched `runtimeversion:resolve` (`2bdcb69b…`) with the placeholder `google-services.json` in place, so the ignore in `fingerprint.config.js` holds end to end
- Debug build: no requests, row reads "Off in development builds"
- Not tried on a device: the 15-minute resume path (unit-tested)

title: fix(observability): drop request-cancellation noise from daemon Sentry
body:
## Why

With daemon Sentry live, `context.Canceled` and `context.DeadlineExceeded` errors are the dominant, un-actionable churn in the issue feed (client/renderer disconnecting mid-request, or a request/op running past its deadline). They are not server bugs, and they bury the real faults.

## What

`CaptureHTTPError` now drops any error that is or wraps `context.Canceled` / `context.DeadlineExceeded` before capture, via a new `IsNoiseError` (`errors.Is`, so wrapped chains like `list prs for x: context canceled` and the bare `context deadlineExceededError` are both caught).

Genuine slow-path/contention stays observable elsewhere: the aggregated `ao.http.5xx` rollup still counts it, and retryable DB contention has the typed 503 path.

## Tests

- `IsNoiseError` over nil / plain fault / canceled / deadline / wrapped / deep-wrapped.
- Recording-transport test: three cancellation errors produce **zero** captured events; a genuine fault (`no such table: ...`) still reaches the wire.

Observed in production feed: `context canceled` / `context deadline exceeded` across `list prs`, `pr facts`, `skills/list`, `conversation`, and bare deadline errors — all now suppressed.

title: bug(workspacewatch): one-fd-per-directory watch exhausts the fd limit on large workspaces, aborting workspace/events with a 500
body:
## Summary

On a workspace with many directories, `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/events` fails with `watch workspace directory "...": open ...: too many open files` and the live-file SSE subscription never starts. The watcher registers one OS watch per directory (one fd on macOS/kqueue, one inotify watch on Linux), so a large tree (node_modules, vendored deps, a monorepo) exhausts the process/system fd limit.

## Root cause

`addInitialDirectories` (`backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go:152-193`) collects **every** directory in the workspace — for a git worktree, the directory of each `git ls-files` entry plus all ancestors; otherwise a full `filepath.WalkDir` — and calls `watcher.Add(dir)` on each with no bound on the count. fsnotify opens an fd per watched directory (kqueue) / consumes an inotify watch, so once the number of directories exceeds `RLIMIT_NOFILE` (or the inotify `max_user_watches`), `watcher.Add` returns `too many open files` (EMFILE/ENFILE). The loop returns on the **first** such failure (`watcher.go:186-192`); the untyped error reaches `streamWorkspaceChanges` (`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:622`) -> `envelope.WriteError` -> 500, and the no-backoff EventSource reconnect (#4323) then retries in a loop.

## Reproduction (verified)

Create a git worktree with 400 directories each containing a tracked file, lower `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to 128 to model a daemon already near its ceiling (a real machine hits the macOS default of 256 with a typical `node_modules`), then call `workspacewatch.Watch(ctx, root)`:

```
watch workspace directory ".../pkg264": open .../pkg264: too many open files
```

The endpoint returns 500 and the subscription never establishes.

## Why it matters

Unlike #4414 (a single missing directory, fixable by skip-and-continue), skip-and-continue does **not** help here: the watcher fundamentally registers an unbounded number of per-directory watches, so any sufficiently large workspace fails, and the descriptor pressure can degrade the whole daemon/machine, not just this endpoint.

## Expected / options

- Bound the number of watches, or watch coarsely (watch the root recursively where the platform supports it, or watch a capped/most-relevant set and reconcile) rather than one-per-directory unbounded.
- At minimum, when `watcher.Add` fails with EMFILE/ENFILE, skip that directory and continue (partial coverage) instead of aborting the whole subscription with a 500, and return a typed degraded response rather than an untyped 500.

## Affected code

- `backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go:152-193`
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:622`
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go` (untyped error -> 500)

## Related

- #4414 (same watcher aborts on a single missing directory) — sibling root cause in the same loop.
- #4323 (no-backoff SSE reconnect amplifies a transient setup 5xx).
- #4325 (untyped service errors collapse to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR).

title: bug(observability): Sentry path scrubber leaks local paths containing spaces (e.g. iCloud "Mobile Documents")
body:
## Summary

The daemon Sentry path scrubber (`sentryobs.scrub`) fails to redact local filesystem paths that contain a **space**, so an error message referencing such a path ships the un-redacted tail off the machine. macOS iCloud Drive paths (`.../Library/Mobile Documents/...`) and any user directory with a space are affected.

## Root cause

`scrub` (`backend/internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go`) redacts home paths with `homePath = /(?:Users|home)/[^\s"']+`. The `[^\s"']+` character class stops at the first whitespace, so a path with a space is only partially matched: everything from the space onward survives.

## Reproduction (verified)

```
scrub(`... open /Users/aey/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/vault/rules.md: no such file`)
=> ... open [redacted-path] Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/vault/rules.md: no such file
```

The redaction stops at the space in `Mobile Documents`; the vault path — and implicitly the folder layout and which app the user runs — survives into the event payload.

## Why it matters

It defeats the deny-by-default privacy guarantee for any path containing a space, which is common on macOS (`~/Library/Mobile Documents/...` for iCloud Drive, plus user folders like `My Project`). Usernames, project names, and directory structure can reach the error backend.

## Expected

Redact home/user paths regardless of embedded spaces — anchor on the home/user prefix (and the macOS `.../Library/Mobile Documents/...` form) and consume to a real path boundary rather than the first space. Add scrub test cases for spaced paths.

## Affected code

- `backend/internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go` (the `homePath` / `winPath` regexes and `scrub`).
- The renderer and mobile scrubbers (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/sentry.ts`, `packages/mobile/lib/sentry.ts`) use the same `[^\s]`-terminated approach and almost certainly share the defect; fix all three.

title: [Bug]: Killing a TUI session whose tmux is already gone returns HTTP 500
body:
## Bug

Closing or killing a TUI session whose tmux runtime is already gone (daemon restart, missing tmux session, inconclusive legacy-socket probe) returns HTTP 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` instead of marking the session terminated.

**Source:** live daemon reproduction (`ao session kill dse_today-6` and `dse_today-2/4/5`) | **Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc`
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Spawn TUI sessions (omp/grok).
2. Restart the daemon so their tmux sessions disappear (`tmux ls` has no matching sessions).
3. `ao session kill <id>` (or close the tab in the desktop UI).

Already-terminated chat sessions kill OK on the same daemon.

## Root Cause

`Manager.Kill` (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`) fails closed on:

- `runtime.Destroy` errors, including `ports.ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` from `tmux.socketForSession` when the private socket lacks the session and the legacy default socket cannot be inspected.
- `terminateNativeSession` errors (stale grok/prime native ids).

Unmapped errors become 500 via `toAPIError`. tmux `Destroy` already treats a missing session / unreachable server as success, but the probe-inconclusive path still 500s the whole kill. The session is never `MarkTerminated`, so the zombie tab stays on the board.

Telemetry fingerprint for `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/kill`: `aad9192f2c617588`.

## Expected

Kill is idempotent. Missing tmux, inconclusive probe, already-dead runtime, or failed native terminate must still `MarkTerminated` and return 200. Closing a zombie tab must never 500.

## Impact

- Users cannot close zombie TUI tabs after a daemon restart.
- Session list stays cluttered with live-looking sessions whose runtimes are gone.
- Chat kill is already best-effort and is not rewritten here.

## Related

- [#2701](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2701) — pre-tmux/legacy handle kill 500s (same symptom, different handle class).
- [#3475](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3475) — probe misreads must not be treated as per-session death for *liveness*; kill teardown is the inverse (user asked to terminate).

title: fix(session): make kill idempotent when runtime is already gone
body:
## What

Make kill, resume-agent, and orchestrator replacement succeed when the TUI runtime is already gone (missing tmux, stale private socket, missing default socket, inconclusive legacy probe, failed native terminate).

Fixes [#4481](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4481).

## Why

After a daemon restart, a project orchestrator (and other TUI sessions) whose tmux server is gone cannot be talked to, resumed, closed, or replaced:

- `POST /sessions/{id}/send` → 409 `AGENT_EXITED`
- `POST /sessions/{id}/resume-agent` → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` (fingerprint `f05be741f335dfad`)
- `POST /sessions/{id}/kill` → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` (fingerprint `aad9192f2c617588`)
- Spawn orchestrator without `clean` returns the zombie; restart (`clean=true`) hits the same Destroy 500.

Live repro: `ao-killfix-2` (grok TUI orchestrator, handle `ao-killfix-2`, no `ptyhost-v1:` prefix). Private socket `/tmp/tmux-501/ao` had no server; default socket was `error connecting ... (No such file or directory)`. `socketForSession` classified that as `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, so resume/kill/replace all 500ed.

## How

- tmux `socketForSession`: a missing legacy default socket (`error connecting ... no such file`) is both-sockets-gone, same as `no server running`. `IsAlive` then reports `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` instead of inconclusive. Transient `connection refused` is unchanged.
- tmux `Destroy` treats `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` / `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` as already-gone.
- `Kill` and `RetireForReplacement` log and continue on native-terminate failure and already-gone runtime Destroy, then still mark terminated.
- User-initiated `restartRuntime` (resume-agent) treats those runtime sentinels as "no existing runtime" and creates a replacement. Boot `reconcileLive` still refuses to recreate on `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`.

## Testing

```bash
cd backend && env -u AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME go test ./internal/session_manager ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux
```

Added/updated:

- `TestIsAliveReportsPrivateServerGoneAndLegacySocketAbsentAsUnavailable`
- `TestDestroyIsIdempotentWhenPrivateServerGoneAndLegacySocketAbsent`
- `TestResumeAgent_InconclusiveRuntimeProbeRecreates`
- `TestRestartRuntime_InconclusiveProbeCreatesReplacement`
- `TestRetireForReplacement_RuntimeProbeInconclusiveStillTerminates`
- `TestRetireForReplacement_NativeTerminationFailureStillTerminates`

Unexpected runtime destroy errors still leave the session active. Chat kill is not rewritten.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
