title: bug(release): manifest-less feed heads strand desktop update checks
body:
## Bug

A published desktop release can become the updater feed head without its channel manifests. Every installed client selecting that release then fails update checks until a later complete release displaces it. The app correctly surfaced the repeated-failure warning on this machine, but it could not determine whether a newer build existed.

**Observed:** 2026-08-26 19:57 IST (14:27 UTC), local installed AO desktop app  
**Installed app:** `0.12.8-nightly.202608250759`, packaged arm64 macOS app  
**Settings:** automatic updates enabled, `nightly` channel, no feature pin  
**Daemon identity:** bundled `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`, healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**OS:** macOS 27.0 (26A5388g), arm64  
**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)  
**Root-cause confidence:** **High**

![Settings showing repeated update-check failures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-update-feed-head-missing-manifests-20260826/.issue-assets/update-feed-head-missing-manifests-20260826/update-check-failing.png)

## Reproduction / timeline

1. Install a packaged nightly and enable automatic updates on the `nightly` channel.
2. Publish a newer nightly release without `nightly.yml`, `nightly-mac.yml`, and `nightly-linux.yml`.
3. Leave the app running for at least three scheduled checks.
4. Open Settings → Updates.
5. The warning appears: “Update checks keep failing. The app can't tell whether a newer version is out.”

Concrete incident:

- `v0.12.8-nightly.202608252327` was published at `2026-08-25T23:43:08Z` with installers but **no updater manifests**.
- At screenshot time (`2026-08-26T14:27Z`), that manifest-less release was still the newest published nightly.
- `v0.12.8-nightly.202608261410` uploaded `nightly-mac.yml` at `14:31:41Z` and was published at `14:31:48Z`, about four minutes after the screenshot. The current nightly feed is therefore healthy and the exact incident self-healed when this later complete release displaced the bad head.
- Stable is still affected independently: current latest release `v0.12.7` has installers but no `latest.yml`, `latest-mac.yml`, or `latest-linux.yml`; `/releases/latest/download/latest-mac.yml` redirects to that release and returns 404.

## Root cause

The updater behavior and UI classification match the release state:

- `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts` counts consecutive automatic failures of any kind and stamps `checksFailing: true` after three. Manifest 404s intentionally do not set the separate `staleCheckNudge`, which is reserved for `net::ERR_*` and restart guidance.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx` renders the exact screenshot copy when `checksFailing` is true and `staleCheckNudge` is false.
- Nightly release creation is currently manual after `.github/workflows/frontend-nightly.yml` was removed in `939e0c975` / #3070. Manifest generation/upload is separable from publishing, so a release can be public and selected by clients while incomplete—or remain permanently incomplete.

This is a release-metadata publication failure, not local updater cache corruption, signing/install failure, wrong binary/port, or an auth problem. No updater state was deleted, no app was reinstalled/restarted, and no release state was mutated during triage.

## Impact

- All clients whose selected channel head lacks its platform manifest cannot discover updates.
- Automatic failures accumulate silently until the third failure; users can remain stranded between or beyond releases.
- Nightly recovered only because a later complete release was published. Stable remains unable to resolve its current macOS manifest.
- Workaround is operational rather than user-local: backfill the missing manifests or publish a complete newer release.

## Recommended next action

1. Backfill updater manifests for current stable `v0.12.7` and audit published nightly heads for missing manifests.
2. Merge and enable [PR #4464](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4464), which adds a nightly feed-head guard and already documents this failure class.
3. Make publication atomic from the client’s perspective: keep a release draft/non-discoverable until installers and all channel manifests are present and validated, then publish once.
4. Keep the client-side resolver defensive: skip draft or manifest-less prereleases and select the newest installable release (related [PR #4462](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4462)).
5. Add stable/nightly post-publish probes for every required manifest and alert immediately on 404.

## Related

- [PR #4464](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4464) — open nightly feed-head guard; directly addresses detection of this regression.
- [PR #4462](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4462) — open client hardening around draft/prerelease resolution.
- [#2220](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2220) — closed original absence of updater feed metadata; same user-visible boundary, different current release-process mechanism.
- [#2237](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2237) — closed feed publication blocked after installers were available.
- [#2270](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2270) — closed handling for manifest 404 errors.
- [PR #4397](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4397) — merged UI/failure counter that correctly exposed this incident.

- Validate structured states, required notes, free-form messages, output references, and pull request URLs across the CLI, daemon API, service, and domain.

- Recover claimed reports atomically on daemon restart and fence acknowledgements with claim tokens.
- Regenerate sqlc, OpenAPI, and frontend TypeScript artifacts.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./...`
- Focused Worker Reports race suite, including restart recovery and token fencing
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`
- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run`
- `npm run sqlc && npm run api && git diff --exit-code`

## Scope

This PR provides the Phase 1 Worker Reports contract and durable outbox foundation. Report delivery coordination and downstream context rendering remain outside this phase.

title: bug(delegation): task-title control message pollutes orchestrator conversation and context
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Bug

Direct task delegation injects an internal `AO TASK TITLE UPDATE` instruction into the project orchestrator as an ordinary agent message. The message is visible in the human-facing orchestrator conversation/terminal, becomes provider transcript and context, and can overwrite the session's recorded latest user prompt. Naming a worker is internal coordination and must not consume or perturb the project orchestrator's conversation.

**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)  
**Introduced by:** `753cacb4c8e980353474996e45a2b4e80d13cc3d` ([PR #3443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3443), 2026-08-05)  
**Confidence:** **High** — exact construction and both Chat/TUI delivery paths traced; current tests explicitly assert the leaking send.

![AO TASK TITLE UPDATE rendered in the orchestrator conversation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-task-title-control-context-leak/.issue-assets/task-title-control-context-leak/ao-task-title-update-leak.png)

## Reproduction

1. Have a project with a running, exited, or absent orchestrator.
2. Create a direct task through the desktop New Task composer (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`) with a nonblank brief.
3. AO spawns the worker immediately.
4. In the background, AO selects the newest running project orchestrator, resumes the newest exited orchestrator, or spawns a new orchestrator solely for title refinement.
5. Once message delivery is ready, AO sends this into the orchestrator agent:

```text
AO TASK TITLE UPDATE
A worker was already spawned directly with the user's task. Do not spawn another worker or orchestrator, and do not implement the task in this orchestrator session.
Choose a concise task title from the brief and run:

 ao session rename <worker-id> "<title, max 20 chars>"
```

Promptless delegated workers are the exception: an empty brief skips title refinement. Readiness, resume, or send failures can also prevent delivery. Otherwise every direct delegation with a brief attempts this injection.

## Expected behavior

After direct delegation spawns the worker, **that spawned worker** should choose and apply its own concise title with:

```text
ao session rename <its-own-session-id> "<title, max 20 chars>"
```

The project orchestrator must never receive title-control text and must never be spawned, resumed, or woken for naming.

## Actual behavior and source evidence

### Delegation deliberately targets the project orchestrator

`backend/internal/service/session/delegation.go`:

- `DelegateTask` spawns the worker, then calls `refineDelegatedTaskTitleInBackground` for every nonblank prompt (`:44-86`).
- `refineDelegatedTaskTitle` resolves a project orchestrator, waits for its input readiness, and calls `s.manager.Send(ctx, orchestratorID, taskTitleDelegationMessage(...), nil)` (`:89-124`).
- `taskTitleOrchestrator` chooses a running orchestrator, resumes an exited one, or calls `SpawnOrchestrator` when none exists (`:127-161`).
- `taskTitleDelegationMessage` constructs the exact screenshot text (`:175-191`). Git blame attributes that message to `753cacb4c8`; it remains verbatim on current `upstream/main`.

Later commits changed the mechanics but preserved the leak:

- `3934bc86a45ee5c8a2fc4299b9a04aefcae85548` ([PR #3627](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3627)) added the provisional 20-rune display name and made refinement best effort.
- `9c475bf718e81cbf82cc112b3d6aa113c0223623` ([PR #3657](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3657)) made refinement asynchronous and added orchestrator resume/create behavior.

### TUI mode: visible input, transcript/context, and prompt-metadata pollution

`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:2917-2983` routes `Manager.Send` through `prepareOutboundMessage` and `messenger.DeliverWithPostWrite`. `backend/internal/daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go:291-320` resolves the runtime handle and invokes `runtime.SendMessage`, which pastes/submits the text into the live TUI pane.

After delivery, `Manager.send` calls `RecordSessionLatestUserPrompt` with the control message (`manager.go:2971-2978`). This contradicts the domain contract in `backend/internal/domain/session.go:42-45`:

> `LatestUserPrompt` is the latest real user-authored task direction; internal AO coordination messages must not replace it.

Consequences:

- The control message is visible in the terminal transcript.
- The provider treats it as a user turn and includes it in future context.
- It can replace the real `LatestUserPrompt`, contaminating continuation/handoff facts.
- It wakes an otherwise idle orchestrator and spends a provider turn solely on naming.

### Chat mode: persisted visible conversation turn and provider input

`backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go:222-256` routes `Manager.Send` through `RelayChatTurn`. `backend/internal/service/chat/service.go:1175-1210` creates a `ChatUserMessage` with `Origin: automation`, but it remains a **user-role inbound turn**, is stored in the conversation, and is dispatched to the provider.

Automation attribution does not make the message internal or invisible. `TestRelayedMessageIsAttributedToAutomation` (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller_test.go:3181-3205`) explicitly asserts that the message appears in the conversation snapshot and that the provider receives the exact text.

## Current tests protect the leak

`TestDelegateTaskSpawnsWorkerThenRequestsTitleFromNewestActiveOrchestrator` in `backend/internal/service/session/delegation_test.go:14-80` asserts that:

- the title request is sent to `orch-new`;
- delivery readiness is awaited for that orchestrator;
- the sent message contains `AO TASK TITLE UPDATE`;
- it contains “Do not spawn another worker or orchestrator”;
- it instructs `ao session rename mer-9 ...` and includes the worker brief.

Other tests explicitly require the current orchestration side effects:

- `TestDelegateTaskResumesNewestExitedOrchestratorBeforeRequestingTitle`
- `TestDelegateTaskStartsMissingOrchestratorBeforeRequestingTitle`
- readiness/send failure and asynchronous-return tests

These tests need to be inverted around the decided worker-self-rename behavior.

## Decided behavioral boundary

The session service may coordinate naming with the **newly spawned worker only**. It must not use the project orchestrator as a title generator or command executor.

After worker spawn:

1. Ask the spawned worker to derive a concise title from its own task brief.
2. Instruct it to run `ao session rename <its-own-id> "<title, max 20 chars>"`.
3. Keep the existing provisional `delegatedTaskDisplayName` as the immediate/failure-safe label.
4. Treat worker self-rename as best effort and never roll back a successful worker spawn if naming fails.
5. Do not discover, spawn, resume, wake, wait on, or message a project orchestrator for naming.

This boundary belongs in `backend/internal/service/session/delegation.go` and the worker-spawn/prompt handoff. Hiding automation rows in the renderer is not a fix: the provider would still receive and retain the control message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A nonblank direct delegation spawns exactly one worker with the user's task and provisional display name.
- [ ] The spawned worker receives a bounded internal title instruction identifying its own session ID and the 20-character limit.
- [ ] The worker—not a project orchestrator—runs or is asked to run `ao session rename` for itself.
- [ ] No title-control message is sent to any project orchestrator in Chat or TUI mode.
- [ ] Naming does not list/select an orchestrator, call `SpawnOrchestrator`, resume an exited orchestrator, wait for orchestrator message readiness, or wake an idle orchestrator.
- [ ] The human-facing orchestrator conversation, terminal transcript, provider context, and `LatestUserPrompt` remain unchanged after direct delegation.
- [ ] Naming failure remains non-fatal after the worker-spawn commit point; the provisional title remains usable.
- [ ] Promptless worker behavior remains intentional and covered.
- [ ] `OrchestratorID` remains empty on the delegate response unless the wire field is removed through a compatible API change.

## Required tests

- Service test: direct delegation records one worker spawn and **zero** orchestrator spawn/resume/readiness/send calls.
- Targeting test: title instruction references the spawned worker ID and is delivered only through the worker-owned startup/self-rename path.
- TUI regression test: `AO TASK TITLE UPDATE` never reaches the orchestrator runtime messenger and never replaces its `LatestUserPrompt`.
- Chat regression test: no title-control message appears in the orchestrator conversation snapshot and no such text reaches the orchestrator provider.
- Failure test: worker title/self-rename failure does not fail or terminate the successfully spawned worker and leaves the provisional display name intact.
- Promptless test: preserve the explicitly chosen behavior for an empty brief without contacting an orchestrator.

## Impact

- Every ordinary direct delegation can add irrelevant control text to a human conversation and provider transcript.
- The orchestrator may be created or resumed solely to rename another session.
- Provider context and tokens are consumed for internal UI metadata.
- `LatestUserPrompt` can cease to represent the human's latest direction, degrading continuation and agent-switch handoffs.
- The control turn can interrupt or distract subsequent orchestration work.

## Related

- [#3912](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3912) — same naming flow, but tracks ugly provisional titles and silent refinement failure rather than context leakage.
- [#3911](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3911) — missing/invalid worker names on orchestrator-driven `ao spawn`.
- [PR #3443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3443) — introduced the direct-delegation title message.
- [PR #3627](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3627) — added provisional titles/best-effort refinement.
- [PR #3657](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3657) — moved refinement to background and added orchestrator resume/create.

title: feat(onboarding): infer worker and orchestrator defaults from role-specific usage
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Enhancement

New-project onboarding currently defaults both **Worker agent** and **Orchestrator agent** to the same generic authorized-agent choice. It should instead infer each role's default independently from the user's actual AO session history.

**Analyzed against:** `d32434d9da8868e2a768d0942fade073be06cddc` (`upstream/main`, 2026-08-26)

![Worker and orchestrator agent defaults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-role-aware-agent-defaults/.issue-assets/role-aware-agent-defaults/project-agent-defaults.png)

## Current behavior

When the create-project agent sheet opens, it computes one `defaultAuthorizedAgent(...)` result from the available agent catalog and assigns that same agent to both roles. This commonly produces Claude Code for both fields regardless of which harnesses the user actually uses for workers and orchestrators.

## Desired behavior

Choose defaults independently for the worker and orchestrator roles:

1. Count the harness used by existing sessions of that role.
2. Select the most frequently used eligible harness for that role.
3. If multiple harnesses have the same highest count, select whichever tied harness was used by the most recently spawned session of that role.
4. If no session history exists for that role, default to Claude Code.

Examples:

- Worker history: 5 Codex, 2 Claude Code → default worker to Codex.
- Orchestrator history: 2 Claude Code, 2 Codex, with the newest tied session using Codex → default orchestrator to Codex.
- Orchestrator history: 2 Kimi, 2 Codex, with Codex used more recently → default orchestrator to Codex.
- No orchestrator sessions yet → default orchestrator to Claude Code.

Only installed/authorized agents that can currently be selected should become defaults. If the historical winner is unavailable, continue through the same frequency/recency ordering among eligible agents before using Claude Code as the final fallback.

The inference applies only while the user has not manually changed the field. Existing touched-field behavior must remain: asynchronous catalog/history refreshes must never overwrite an explicit user selection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Worker and orchestrator defaults are inferred independently.
- [ ] The most-used eligible harness wins for each role.
- [ ] Equal counts are broken by the newest spawned session among the tied harnesses.
- [ ] With no eligible history for a role, Claude Code is selected when available.
- [ ] If Claude Code is unavailable, onboarding remains usable by selecting the next valid authorized fallback rather than producing an invalid value.
- [ ] Manual selections are never replaced by a later refresh.
- [ ] Tests cover unequal counts, equal-count recency, separate role histories, unavailable historical winners, empty history, and touched fields.

## Scope

This changes only the initial suggestion shown during new-project onboarding. It does not alter existing project configuration or automatically rewrite saved worker/orchestrator defaults.

title: fix(gitworktree): retry worktree removal on macOS/Linux, not only Windows
body:
The bounded worktree-remove retry was gated to Windows (`removeAllRetryEnabled = runtime.GOOS == "windows"`), but the transient race it absorbs is not Windows-only. On macOS/Linux a just-killed agent child can still hold the worktree dir briefly after `ao session kill` destroys its shells, so `os.RemoveAll` fails with a transient `unlinkat` EACCES/ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY. Gated to Windows, that stranded the worktree and returned a 500 on Unix.

Observed in production as `kill X: gitworktree: remove unregistered path: unlinkat ...` and `retire replacement: force destroy` (the two are among the top daemon errors).

Fix: default the retry on for every platform. The ctx-bounded ~7.25s budget and the early ErrNotExist exit are unchanged; a caller that gives up cancels ctx. The var is kept so tests still exercise the disabled path; drops the now-unused `runtime` import; adds a guard test that the default stays enabled.

QA audit finding SESS-1.

title: fix(session): map ErrNoController to a typed 409 on the send path, not a raw 500
body:
A send to a session whose chat controller is not live (daemon just restarted, controller stopped, mid-reconnect) returned `chatsvc.ErrNoController`, which had no case in `toAPIError` and fell through to a raw 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, shipping `send <id>: no live chat controller for session` to the client and Sentry. The conversation-send path already maps this to 409 `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`; the session-send path (orchestrator relay, `ao send`) diverged.

Fix: add the `ErrNoController` case to `toAPIError` returning the same typed 409, plus a regression test. No import cycle (service/chat does not import service/session).

QA audit finding CHAT-1 (production error AO-DESKTOP-5).

title: bug(terminal): high-output flood tears down the whole terminal WebSocket (crash loop)
body:
## Summary
A high-output command in an attached terminal (a build, `yes`, a verbose test run) tears down the entire terminal WebSocket, then reattaches, replays, floods again, and dies: a crash loop.

## Root cause
`attachment.copyOut` reads 32KB chunks (`backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:191-204`) into `connState.enqueue` (`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:529-535`) on a 1024-frame channel (`defaultWriteBuffer`, `manager.go:36`). On overflow the `default` branch calls `c.cancel()` (`manager.go:533`), tearing down the whole connection and every pane on it. The PTY read loop never blocks, so there is no upstream backpressure; a flood fills 1024 frames faster than JSON+base64 WS writes drain.

## Expected
Coalesce/drop data frames (the client only needs the latest output), or apply flow control (stop reading the attach PTY so tmux/conpty throttles) instead of killing the connection.

## Suggested fix
On a full buffer, coalesce consecutive `msgData` frames for the same terminal id into the tail rather than cancelling; or batch multiple 32KB reads into one frame in `copyOut` as a stopgap.

## Notes
UNTESTED live (needs a running daemon+renderer); verified from code. QA audit finding TERM-1. Effort: 30-min stopgap, ~2-4h correct. Scaling risk: high.

title: bug(browser-preview): managed preview dev-server crash is invisible in the panel
body:
## Summary
When a managed preview dev-server crashes after launch, the Browser panel keeps showing the stale page with no error; `ao preview status` later reports plain `stopped`.

## Root cause
`waitForExit` flips the run to `StateFailed` (`backend/internal/previewserver/manager.go:499-506`) but does not call `SetPreview("")` and emits no event. The panel's only failure hook, `did-fail-load` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:1828`), fires on navigation, not on an already-rendered page whose backing server dies. After `failedStatusRetention` (5 min) the failed run is deleted (`manager.go:511-518`), so status then reports `stopped` with no error.

## Expected
On a non-stopping exit, clear/mark the session preview so the panel shows a dead-server state.

## Suggested fix
Add an `onExit(sessionID, Status)` callback to `Manager`, call it from `waitForExit` when `!run.stopping`, and wire it to `SetPreview(ctx, id, "")`; SSE already fans session updates to the renderer.

## Notes
UNTESTED live; verified from code. QA audit finding PREV-1. Effort: ~30 min detection, +1-2h for a polished panel state. Scaling risk: high.

title: security(connect-mobile): LAN bridge is plaintext HTTP; bearer password sniffable on shared Wi-Fi
body:
## Summary
The Connect Mobile LAN bridge is plaintext HTTP bound to `0.0.0.0`, and the connection password rides as a `Bearer` header, so on any shared L2 network a passive sniffer captures the password from the first request. That password authorizes terminal input, spawn/kill, and PR actions. The docs say "do not use on public Wi-Fi," and users will.

## Root cause
`backend/internal/httpd/lan_listener.go:138` binds `0.0.0.0:<port>` and serves a plain `http.Server` with no TLS. The password is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <pw>` (`packages/mobile/lib/config.ts:29`), and `packages/mobile/app.json` sets `usesCleartextTraffic: true` / `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`.

## Expected
TLS on the LAN listener (self-signed cert pinned during pairing). Short of that, gate `Enable()` behind an explicit home-network confirmation and surface `mobileUnencryptedWarning` prominently in the mobile app, not only on desktop.

## Suggested fix
Add TLS to the LAN listener with a cert pinned at pairing time; until then make the plaintext warning blocking in the app.

## Notes
UNTESTED as a live capture; verified from code. QA audit finding MOB-1. Effort: warning ~0.5 day, TLS 2-4 days. Scaling risk: critical.

title: feat(windows,shell-terminals): selectable default shell for standalone terminals (Git Bash, PowerShell, cmd)
body:
## Feature Description

On Windows, standalone shell terminals always launch whichever shell the daemon finds first in a **hardcoded probe order** — `pwsh.exe` → `powershell.exe` → `ComSpec` → `cmd.exe`. There is no way for the user to choose a different default shell, and **Git Bash is never considered at all**.

Requested: a user-facing option (app setting and/or per-terminal picker) to select the default shell for standalone terminals, with Git Bash as a first-class choice alongside PowerShell / cmd.

## Current behavior (code anchors)

- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/loginshell.go` — `resolveUserLoginShell()` → `resolveWindowsShell()`: hardcoded candidate list `["pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe"]` then `ComSpec`/`cmd.exe` fallback. No user preference is consulted, no Git Bash probe (e.g. `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`), no override hook.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` — `OpenShellTerminalInput` has no shell/shellPath field, so `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` cannot express a shell choice per open request either.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` (`runLoginShell`, ~line 635) — login-shell env detection runs a shell too; a changed default should be honored consistently there.
- Unix already prefers `$SHELL` (`loginshell.go:24`), which is why this reads as Windows-only — but note the Unix sibling bug with non-POSIX shells: #3788 (fish).

## Motivation

- Reported by a Windows user who lives in Git Bash: **SahilG** in the `#feature-requests` Discord thread *"default terminal option"* — currently the **most upvoted feature request** there.
- Git Bash is a daily-driver shell for many Windows developers; getting PowerShell instead makes the standalone terminal pane a pane they immediately `exit` out of.
- PowerShell-first probe order also surprises cmd users the same way (SahilG perceived "only cmd is supported" — either way, the user loses).

## Proposed Solution

1. **Setting:** add a `shell` preference (e.g. `"auto" | "git-bash" | "pwsh" | "powershell" | "cmd" | custom path`) to app settings, surfaced in the desktop app's Settings UI.
2. **Resolution order:** `resolveUserLoginShell()` should consult the preference first; `"auto"` keeps today's behavior. Git Bash detection: `where git` → `<Git>\bin\bash.exe` (or `bash.exe` on PATH), launched with `--login -i`.
3. **Wire API:** optionally extend `OpenShellTerminalInput` with an optional per-request `shell` override so the UI can offer a per-terminal picker (⊞ new-terminal dropdown) without extra round-trips.
4. **Validation:** reject-with-message or fall back to `auto` when the configured shell path doesn't exist at open time (consistent with the "must not open something unusable" rule in `loginshell.go:17-19`).
5. **Regenerate API artifacts** (`npm run api`) if DTOs change.

## Alternatives Considered

- Environment-variable-only override (e.g. `AO_SHELL`) — cheap but undiscoverable; fine as a power-user extra, not a substitute for a setting.
- Doing nothing / documenting PowerShell-first — rejected: most-upvoted request, and the fix is well-bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Windows user can set Git Bash as the default shell; new standalone terminals launch in Git Bash (`--login -i`)
- [ ] PowerShell (pwsh + Windows PowerShell) and cmd remain selectable; `"auto"` preserves current behavior
- [ ] Custom shell path supported, with clear error/fallback when it's missing
- [ ] Preference honored by the login-shell env detection path (`runLoginShell`), not just terminal spawn
- [ ] Unix behavior unchanged (`$SHELL` still wins)
- [ ] OpenAPI spec + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated if request DTOs change

## Environment

- OS: Windows (feature is Windows-facing; Unix already honors `$SHELL`)
- Surface: standalone shell terminals (`/terminals` screen) — shellterm service → daemon → ConPTY

_Filed from Discord thread "default terminal option" (#feature-requests). Reporter: @SahilG; picked up by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari._

title: fix(observability): harden daemon Sentry capture (re-land #4352)
body:
Re-lands the daemon-Sentry hardening from #4352 that never reached main: a PR-head desync left #4346 merging the pre-hardening commit, so `origin/main` still has the shared-hub capture, double panic-capture, and all-503-suppressed policy. This is the exact verified change from that work, cherry-picked onto current main.

## Fixes
1. **Request-isolated hub.** `CaptureHTTPError`/`CapturePanic` used package-level `sentry.WithScope`/`CaptureException` on the process-global `CurrentHub`, so concurrent requests could interleave scope push/pop and stamp one request's request_id/fingerprint onto another's event. Each capture now resolves a hub from the request context or clones the current hub. Covered by a `-race` test that fails if reverted.
2. **Single panic capture.** The recover middleware captured a panic (fatal, with the Go stack) and the outer 5xx logger then manufactured a second generic `HTTP 500` event with a different fingerprint. Recovery now marks the request via a request-scoped flag and the logger skips its capture when set. Exactly one event, verified through a recording transport.
3. **Code-aware 503.** `ShouldCaptureStatus(status)` dropped every 503, but AO also uses 503 for typed outages (`SCM_UNAVAILABLE`, `BROWSER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, `DEVICE_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE`). Replaced with `ShouldCapture(status, errorCode)`: only the deliberate `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` backpressure is suppressed.

Adds `Disable()` for shutdown/tests. All tests pass under `go test -race`.

Note: overlaps `internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go` with the noise-filter PR #4475; whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

title: fix(observability): scrub local paths containing spaces
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4477.

The Sentry path scrubber stopped at whitespace, so local paths such as `~/Library/Mobile Documents/...` could leak the remainder of the path. The scrubber now handles spaces in Unix and Windows paths while preserving the existing error-message suffix behavior.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/observe/sentryobs`
- `gofmt -w internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs.go internal/observe/sentryobs/sentryobs_test.go`
- `git diff --check`

The repository-wide `go test ./...` command was also run; it remains red on unrelated Windows/environment-sensitive tests and provider fixtures. `go test -race ./...` cannot start in this environment because CGO is disabled.

title: feat(preview): suggest detected ports in the Browser panel
body: ## What The Browser panel offers the ports a session is actually serving on, next to the address bar. Clicking one opens it the way `ao preview ` does. Same view from the CLI via `ao preview ports [--json]`. ## Why Finding a dev server's port meant reading it out of terminal scrollback and typing it into the address bar. ## How Detection is scoped to a session two ways, and a process qualifies on either: it descends from the session's root process, or its working directory is inside the session's worktree. Both are needed — the root process differs by mode (a tmux pane's shell for terminal sessions, the provider process for chat), and neither survives an agent backgrounding a dev server, since a detached process is reparented to init. The worktree does not move and belongs to one session. `internal/portscan` reads `/proc` on Linux and shells out to `lsof` elsewhere, then credits each port to the deepest process holding it — a server started from a shell is reported by every ancestor that inherited the descriptor. Everything fails open: a missing `lsof`, an unreadable process table, a permission denial, or a session with no live process all yield an empty list, never an error. Windows detects nothing for now (`portscan/windows.go`); its socket enumeration lands separately. `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview/ports` carries no capability header — it starts nothing — and is blocked on the LAN listener instead (`httpd/lan_listener.go:84`), so the list never leaves the machine. ## Testing `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test` pass on `internal/portscan`, `internal/cli`, `internal/httpd/...`, `internal/session_manager`. Cross-compiled `portscan` for `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=darwin`. `BrowserPanel.test.tsx` passes 58/58. Not verified in the running desktop app. ## When Server is not Live ## When Server is Live ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Feature]:   Worker Context and Shared Memory
body:
### Problem

## Why this matters

- Shared context would let a new worker inherit project facts, recent decisions, rejected approaches, and task boundaries without repeating discovery.
- In team or Cloud settings, several humans and several workers may act in parallel on the same repository, so useful context should survive beyond one chat transcript.
- The orchestrator will make better decisions if it knows what has already been tried, what is blocked, which product decisions are still active, and which codebase areas are already owned.


### Proposed direction

## Questions to answer

- What should be session-local, worker-shared, project-shared, and user-shared?
- What information is safe and useful to persist versus too noisy or too risky to store?
- How should humans inspect, correct, and delete memory when the system is wrong?

## Outcome

Define the smallest shared context model that improves both worker quality and orchestrator decision-making.


### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: bug(agents): goose harness availability detection matches the pressly/goose DB migration tool (name-only binary resolution)
body:
## Bug
The goose **agent harness** availability detection matches the **pressly/goose database migration tool** because both ship a binary named `goose`. On systems that have only the migration tool, AO's agent inventory reports the **Goose AI agent as "installed"** (visible in orchestrator/agent settings), and orchestrators can then pick goose for worker spawns — launching the migration CLI with Block-Goose arguments.

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` thread (2026-08-26) | **Reported by:** @Akash
**Analyzed against:** `c4abb3d0e` (origin/main, fetched 2026-08-26 IST)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced; reporter independently confirmed the false "installed" entry in his orchestrator settings.

## Reproduction
1. Install only the DB migration tool: `brew install goose` (pressly/goose) or equivalent, so `goose` on PATH is the migration CLI. Do **not** install Block's Goose agent.
2. Run the desktop app / `ao agent list` (or open orchestrator settings → agents).
3. Goose is listed under **installed** agents.
4. Observed by reporter: the orchestrator attempted to spawn a goose worker (first time ever) and failed/misbehaved, because the launched binary is the migration tool, not the agent.

## Root Cause
Binary resolution for the goose harness is **name-only** — first executable named `goose` wins, with no identity/version probe:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/goose/goose.go:259` — `gooseBinarySpec` lists `Names: []string{"goose"}` plus fallback paths `/usr/local/bin/goose`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/goose`, `~/.cargo/bin/goose`, and npm-global locations. Several of these are exactly where the **migration tool** installs (Homebrew's `goose` formula is the pressly migration tool → `/opt/homebrew/bin/goose`).
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/binaryutil/binaryutil.go:94` — `ResolveBinary` does `exec.LookPath(name)` over the spec names and returns the **first** hit. There is no check that the resolved binary is the Block Goose CLI rather than the migration tool.
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/goose/goose.go:276` — `ResolveGooseBinary` is a thin wrapper over that resolver.
- `backend/internal/service/agent/service.go` — the inventory `refresh()` and `FindInstalledBinary()` treat a successful resolve as **installed**. The service's own doc comment (line 23) states this by design: *"only resolves executable paths; it never starts an agent CLI or probes"* — so the false positive is a structural gap, not a regression.
- The inventory is advisory UI metadata, but it is what surfaces Goose as a choice in orchestrator settings, and the orchestrator prompt advertises `--agent <name>` for workers (`backend/internal/session_manager/prompt.go:194`). A name collision therefore propagates from PATH → inventory → "installed" → orchestrator spawn attempt.
- The launch command built for the harness (`goose run [--system ...] -t "" --interactive`, `goose.go:104`) targets Block-Goose CLI semantics and does not exist in the migration tool, so any spawn against the wrong binary is broken by construction.
- The reviewer adapter injects the same resolver (`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/goose/goose.go:54`), so it inherits the same false positive.

## Fix
Add an identity check to goose binary resolution instead of trusting the name:
1. After a candidate path resolves (PATH or fallback), run a bounded probe (e.g. `<binary> version` / `--help` with a short timeout) and require a Block-Goose-specific marker (e.g. `run`/`session`/`recipe` subcommands or the Block version output format). pressly/goose exposes `up`/`down`/`status`/`create` instead — distinguishable.
2. Recommended shape: an optional `ValidateIdentity func(ctx, path) bool` field on `binaryutil.BinarySpec` so the whole resolver fleet can adopt per-harness identity checks; goose opts in first.
3. There is precedent for bounded CLI probes in the daemon: `backend/internal/adapters/agent/authprobe/authprobe.go` (`CLIStatus`) already runs agent CLIs with timeouts for auth status — the same pattern applies to identity.
4. On identity failure, report goose as **not installed** in the inventory (and surface a hint like "found `goose` on PATH but it is the DB migration tool").

## Impact
- False "installed" state for the Goose agent on any machine with the pressly migration tool (common on dev boxes with DB work).
- Orchestrators can select goose for workers based on that false availability, producing broken spawns.
- Desktop startup prerequisite gate (`FindInstalledBinary`) can pass on the migration tool alone, deferring the real "no usable harness" failure to spawn time.
- Generalizes: any harness whose binary name collides with an unrelated CLI is affected by the same name-only resolution (see related codex resolver bug below).

## Related
- [#3409](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3409) — another binary-resolver robustness bug (codex `.cmd` vs `.exe` preference); same resolver class, different failure mode.

title: bug(kimi): OAuth worker starts without model in AO-managed home
body:
## Bug

AO-managed Kimi TUI workers can start without a model and reject the injected task with:

```text
Error: LLM not set, send /login to login
```

The same Kimi binary works when launched manually in the same worktree. This affects the normal Kimi device-code OAuth profile shape: `config.toml` has a `default_model`, provider/OAuth mapping, and model definitions, while the provider `api_key` is intentionally empty and tokens are stored in the referenced credential JSON.

**Source:** live same-machine reproduction in AO worker `reverb-45` on 2026-08-26  
**Analyzed against:** `c4abb3d0e` (`origin/main`)  
**AO:** packaged Go daemon `0.12.7-nightly.202608250031` on `127.0.0.1:3001` (CLI version currently reports `dev`)  
**Kimi:** `0.38.0`, macOS arm64  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced and traced to the exact config-seeding predicate  
**Priority:** P1 — the normal OAuth-backed Kimi worker path is unusable until the managed profile is manually repaired

## Reproduction

1. Authenticate native Kimi with its device-code OAuth flow.
2. Confirm the native Kimi profile contains a non-empty `default_model`, a provider with an OAuth credential reference, model definitions, and usable access/refresh credentials, but no non-empty literal `api_key`.
3. Spawn an AO Kimi worker with a non-empty task.
4. Observe that Kimi starts with no LLM, rejects the task with `Error: LLM not set, send /login to login`, and the AO session later derives `no_signal`.
5. Run plain `kimi` manually from the same worktree; it loads the native model/profile successfully.

No credential values need to be logged or exposed to reproduce this.

## Root Cause

AO intentionally isolates Kimi under its own data directory:

1. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/kimi.go` sets `KIMI_CODE_HOME=<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi` for managed launches.
2. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kimi/hooks.go:installKimiConfigHooks` prepares `<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi/config.toml` and merges AO lifecycle hooks.
3. `seedKimiCredentials` can securely copy a usable native OAuth credential into the isolated home on first use.
4. `kimiSeedConfig`, however, copies the matching native `config.toml` only when `kimiConfigHasAPIKey(source)` finds a non-empty literal `api_key`.
5. Device-code OAuth profiles intentionally keep authentication in `credentials/kimi-code.json`; their config still carries the required `default_model`, provider/OAuth mapping, aliases, services, permissions, and model tables. The API-key-only predicate rejects that config.

The result is an inconsistent managed profile: AO has a credential and its four lifecycle hooks, but no default model or provider/model graph. Kimi therefore reports an unset LLM before it can create a native session or emit AO lifecycle hooks. `no_signal` is a downstream symptom, not a dead-process or readiness-classification bug.

Sanitized local evidence:

- native `~/.kimi-code/config.toml`: keys include `default_model`, `providers`, `models`, `services`, `permission`; the managed provider has an OAuth reference and no non-empty API key
- AO `<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi/config.toml`: contains only the four AO-managed hook entries
- both credential files exist with mode `0600`; values were not printed or compared in this report
- the AO daemon is healthy on port 3001 and the Kimi process remains live

## Correct Fix and Security/State Behavior

When the AO target config is empty or contains only AO's managed hook block, seed the **complete native config** if either:

- it has a non-empty literal API key (existing behavior), or
- its declared OAuth credential reference resolves to a locally usable access/refresh credential.

Then merge exactly one AO-managed hook block as before.

Copying the whole config is deliberate: selectively copying `default_model` would risk separating it from its provider, OAuth storage reference, model aliases, services, permissions, and related settings. This matches the existing first-use behavior for API-key profiles.

Security/state invariants:

- Keep `KIMI_CODE_HOME` under `AO_DATA_DIR`; do **not** point managed sessions at or write hooks into the native profile.
- Copy secrets only into the AO-managed home with owner-only permissions; never log or commit credential contents.
- Preserve native config/credentials byte-for-byte.
- Preserve any AO config containing non-hook user state; only merge/update AO's owned hook block.
- Preserve an existing AO-managed credential rather than overwriting an independently refreshed or explicitly logged-in managed profile.
- Do not seed OAuth-shaped config when its referenced credential is missing or unusable.

## Remaining Limitations

- Native and AO-managed credentials intentionally diverge after first seeding. If the managed credential later becomes unusable, the user must log in within the managed Kimi profile (or deliberately remove it to allow first-use reseeding); AO should not silently overwrite an existing managed secret from the native profile.
- OAuth configurations whose real token lives only in an external store and cannot be positively verified from the referenced local credential remain outside this fix; that advisory-auth variant is tracked separately in #4031.

## Duplicate Search / Related

No exact issue was found after searching all open and closed issues for the error text, `Model: not set`, `KIMI_CODE_HOME`, `default_model`, OAuth config seeding, and managed Kimi login failures.

- #4031 is related but not a duplicate: it covers OAuth configurations with empty local token fields/external storage where AO reports auth unknown or unauthorized. Here the local credential is usable and AO can report `authorized`; launch fails because the matching model/provider config is not seeded.
- PR #2960 identified the same config-seeding gap, but is currently conflicting with `main`, has no closing issue, and includes storage-layout follow-up changes beyond this exact reproduction. A current-main surgical PR should supersede only the missing OAuth-config predicate/test coverage.
- PR #3648 added first-use OAuth credential copying while intentionally preserving existing managed credentials; it did not retain OAuth profile-config seeding.

## Impact

- OAuth-authenticated Kimi installs can appear ready but fail every AO-managed task before creating a session.
- Workers can remain live while surfacing `no_signal`, obscuring the actual missing-model cause.
- Manual `kimi` remains functional, which makes the failure look terminal- or worktree-specific when it is actually managed-profile inconsistency.

title: fix(kimi): seed OAuth config into managed home
body:
## What

Seed the user's complete native Kimi config and its exact referenced OAuth credential into AO's isolated Kimi home when the source profile uses device-code OAuth, not only when it contains a non-empty literal `api_key`.

The change keeps the existing first-use boundary: only an empty or AO-hook-only managed config is seedable, after which AO merges exactly one lifecycle-hook block.

Fixes #4520.

This is a surgical current-`main` replacement for the remaining config-seeding delta in #2960, which is currently conflicting and also carries broader storage-layout work. Original contributor @serhatsayat is credited in the commit.

## Why

AO worker `reverb-45` reproduced the failure on current `main`: Kimi `0.38.0` launched by AO displayed `Error: LLM not set, send /login to login`, while the same binary launched manually in the same worktree loaded its model and worked.

### RCA

AO deliberately launches Kimi with `KIMI_CODE_HOME=<AO_DATA_DIR>/kimi` so lifecycle hooks and Kimi state remain isolated under `~/.ao`. Hook preparation already copied a usable native OAuth credential into that home, but `kimiSeedConfig` accepted the matching native `config.toml` only when `kimiConfigHasAPIKey(source)` found a non-empty literal API key.

Kimi's device-code OAuth profile intentionally has empty API-key fields. Its config still carries the required `default_model`, provider/OAuth mapping, model aliases, services, permissions, and model definitions. The API-key-only gate therefore produced an inconsistent managed profile:

- credential: present
- AO lifecycle hooks: present
- default model/provider/model graph: missing

Kimi rejected AO's injected task before creating a native session or emitting lifecycle hooks, so `no_signal` was a downstream symptom rather than a process crash or readiness bug.

The regression is the untested intersection of two existing paths: API-key profile-config seeding and OAuth credential seeding.

## How

- If the native config has a non-empty API key, preserve the existing path.
- Otherwise, parse each provider OAuth reference, resolve it through Kimi's existing `kimiOAuthCredentialPath` mapping, and positively verify the exact referenced access/refresh credential before seeding the native config.
- Copy usable referenced credentials to their matching AO-managed paths; retain `credentials/kimi-code.json` only as a legacy fallback when no OAuth reference was persisted. An unrelated default credential is not copied when the config references a scoped key.
- Copy the complete config rather than cherry-picking `default_model`; the provider/OAuth reference, aliases, services, permissions, and model definitions form one internally consistent profile.
- Merge AO's hook block exactly once.

### Intentional security/state behavior

- `KIMI_CODE_HOME` remains under `AO_DATA_DIR`; managed sessions never point at or write hooks into the native `~/.kimi-code` profile.
- Credential contents are neither logged nor committed. First-use copies continue to be written owner-only (`0600`) inside AO-managed state.
- Native config and credentials remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Any AO config containing non-hook state is preserved; only AO's owned hook block is merged/updated.
- An existing AO-managed credential is never overwritten. This preserves an independent managed login or a token that Kimi refreshed inside the isolated profile.
- A token-less/missing native credential does not make an empty-key profile seedable.

### Intentional limitations

- Native and AO-managed credentials can diverge after first seeding. If an existing managed credential later becomes unusable, the user must log in within the managed Kimi profile or deliberately remove it to allow first-use reseeding; AO does not silently overwrite an existing managed secret.
- OAuth profiles whose usable token exists only in an external credential store and cannot be positively verified from local credential JSON remain outside this change; the advisory-auth variant is tracked by #4031.
- Existing AO configs with non-hook content are not repaired or replaced automatically, even if they are incomplete.

## Testing

The original OAuth regression tests and the scoped-reference review tests were run against their respective old gates and failed for the expected missing-config/missing-credential reasons; they pass with the fixes.

- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi -count=1`
- `cd backend && go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/kimi`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/registry ./internal/session_manager -count=1`
- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" npm run lint`
  - full `go test ./...`
  - golangci-lint v2.12.2: `0 issues`
- `git diff --check`

Coverage verifies:

- OAuth config + first-use credential seeding into an empty managed home
- recovery from the exact hook-only managed config state in the reproduction
- complete default-model/provider/OAuth/model graph preservation
- exactly one AO hook block
- native config and credential immutability
- preservation of an existing, divergent AO-managed credential
- scoped OAuth keys such as `oauth/kimi-code-env-<hash>` with and without an unrelated default credential
- copying only credentials referenced by the seeded config

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Focused regression tests added with a verified red-green cycle
- [x] Relevant backend tests, build, vet, and lint pass

title: feat: add harness login actions in settings
body:
## Summary

- add daemon-owned authentication plans for all 27 Harness settings entries
- launch vendor-owned login/setup flows through either an inline AO terminal or, where no reliable setup command exists, official documentation
- add explicit **Open login** and **Open setup** terminal actions for interactive TUI adapters; AO never guesses readiness or submits `/login` or `/auth` automatically
- route Aider setup to its official API-key guide instead of launching a normal `aider` coding session
- isolate every interactive auth flow in its own empty `~/.ao/auth-workspace/<terminal-id>` directory and remove that directory only after the terminal is confirmed dead
- show login-specific and configuration-specific actions/statuses in Harness settings, then reconcile advisory authentication through #4589's daemon-owned readiness coordinator
- recognize Aider's OpenRouter OAuth credentials in `~/.aider/oauth-keys.env`

## Stack

This PR was originally stacked on #4221, which is now merged into upstream `main`.

- Upstream base: `main`
- Head: `nikhilachale:feat/harness-install-settings-main`

## Login and setup flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["User opens Settings → Harness"] --> B{"Harness installed?"}
  B -- No --> C["Show Install action"]
  B -- Yes --> D["Load daemon-owned auth plan"]
  D --> E["User clicks Login or Set up"]
  E --> LM{"Launch mode"}
  LM -- Documentation --> DOC["Open official vendor setup guide"]
  DOC --> T["User returns and clicks Check configuration"]
  LM -- Terminal --> F["POST /api/v1/agents/:agent/auth with agent ID only"]
  F --> G["Daemon resolves fixed reviewed command through harness adapter"]
  G --> H["Create private auth workspace and inline AO terminal"]
  H --> I{"Authentication entry point"}
  I -- Native login or setup command --> J["CLI opens its vendor-owned login or provider flow"]
  I -- Pi / Droid / Prime Agent / OMP --> K["Start native TUI"]
  K --> L["AO enables Open login after terminal attachment"]
  L --> M["User waits for TUI, then clicks Open login"]
  M --> N["AO offers fixed /login input to the active attachment"]
  I -- Qwen --> QA["Start qwen TUI"]
  QA --> QB["AO enables Open setup after terminal attachment"]
  QB --> QC["User clicks Open setup"]
  QC --> QD["AO offers fixed /auth input to the active attachment"]
  N --> O{"Input accepted?"}
  QD --> O
  O -- No --> RETRY["Keep the current action enabled for retry"]
  O -- Yes --> J
  J --> P["User completes vendor-owned login or provider configuration"]
  P --> Q{"Terminal attachment state"}
  Q -- Exited --> R["Start targeted authentication verification"]
  Q -- Error --> S["Keep workflow open for reattach or close"]
  B -- Yes --> T
  T --> R
  R --> U["Invalidate this agent's cached auth observation"]
  U --> V["#4589 readiness coordinator performs a fresh targeted ensure"]
  V --> W{"Normalized authentication state"}
  W -- Authorized --> X["Show Logged in or Configured"]
  W -- Unauthorized --> Y["Show Not logged in or Not configured"]
  W -- Unknown --> Z["Show unverified and keep retry/check available"]
```

### Complete agent authentication matrix

| Adapter | AO action | Launch mode | Terminal command / destination | Follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/installation) | **Login** | Terminal | `claude auth login` | Complete browser/device flow |
| [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | **Login** | Terminal | `codex login` | Complete browser/device-code flow |
| [Cursor](https://docs.cursor.com/en/cli/installation) | **Login** | Terminal | `cursor-agent login` | Complete browser flow |
| [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) | **Login** | Terminal | `opencode auth login` | Choose provider in the native CLI |
| [Aider](https://aider.chat/docs/config/api-keys.html) | **Set up** | Documentation | Official Aider API-key guide | Configure an environment variable, `.env`, or `.aider.conf.yml`, then click **Check configuration** |
| [GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/install-copilot-cli) | **Login** | Terminal | `copilot login` | Complete GitHub device/browser flow |
| [Grok](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview) | **Login** | Terminal | `grok login` | Complete native login; device auth remains available |
| [Kimi](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/) | **Login** | Terminal | `kimi login` | Complete browser flow |
| [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) | **Login** | Terminal | `pi` | Click **Open login** to send `/login` + Enter |
| [Amp](https://ampcode.com/manual) | **Login** | Terminal | `amp login` | Complete browser flow |
| [Auggie](https://docs.augmentcode.com/cli/overview) | **Login** | Terminal | `auggie login` | Complete browser flow |
| [Droid](https://docs.factory.ai/droid-cli/cli-reference) | **Login** | Terminal | `droid` | Click **Open login** to send `/login` + Enter |
| [Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush) | **Login** | Terminal | `crush login` | Complete Charm Hyper login; GitHub Copilot remains available |
| [Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline) | **Login** | Terminal | `cline auth` | Complete native authentication flow |
| [Goose](https://block.github.io/goose/index.html) | **Set up** | Terminal | `goose configure` | Configure the provider in Goose's native prompt |
| [Qwen](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/) | **Set up** | Terminal | `qwen` | Click **Open setup** to send `i` → Backspace → `/auth` + Enter |
| [Continue](https://docs.continue.dev/cli/quickstart) | **Login** | Terminal | `cn login` | Complete browser flow |
| [Devin](https://docs.devin.ai/get-started/devin-intro) | **Login** | Terminal | `devin auth login` | Complete browser flow; manual-token flow remains available |
| [Kiro](https://kiro.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/) | **Login** | Terminal | `kiro-cli login` | Complete browser flow; device flow remains available |
| [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli) | **Login** | Terminal | `kilo auth login` | Complete browser flow |
| [Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe) | **Set up** | Terminal | `vibe --setup` | Complete Vibe's native provider setup |
| [Muse](https://ai.meta.com/llama/) | **Login** | Terminal | `muse login` | Complete native login flow |
| [Agy](https://github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli) | **Login** | Terminal | `agy` | Complete first-run browser sign-in |
| [Autohand](https://docs.autohand.ai/working-with-autohand-code/cli-reference) | **Login** | Terminal | `autohand login` | Complete Autohand account sign-in |
| [Kimchi](https://docs.kimchi.dev/docs/service-keys) | **Login** | Terminal | `kimchi login` | Complete browser login flow |
| [Prime Agent](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/quickstart.md) | **Login** | Terminal | `prime-agent` | Click **Open login** to send `/login` + Enter |
| [OMP](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) | **Login** | Terminal | `omp` | Click **Open login** to send `/login` + Enter |

Aider has no reliable general-purpose login/configure command. Selecting **Set up** therefore opens its official API-key documentation rather than starting a normal coding session. AO never receives the credential. After configuring Aider through its supported environment or configuration-file mechanisms, the user returns to Harness settings and selects **Check configuration**. The row reports **Configured**, **Not configured**, or **Configuration status unknown**.

Goose and Vibe do expose dedicated setup entry points, so they remain inline terminal flows using `goose configure` and `vibe --setup` respectively.

For Pi, Droid, Prime Agent, and OMP, AO starts only the native TUI. The button stays disabled until the terminal is attached. After the TUI is visible, the user selects **Open login** and AO offers the complete daemon-reviewed `/login` sequence to the existing terminal input path.

Qwen remains a setup flow, not a login flow. Its discontinued Qwen OAuth option is no longer represented as a login action: AO starts `qwen`, labels the action **Set up Qwen**, and exposes **Open setup** to enter `/auth`, where the user configures Alibaba ModelStudio, a third-party provider, or a custom provider, as described in the [official Qwen authentication docs](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/). Qwen's `i` + Backspace prefix works in both supported editor states: in optional Vim NORMAL mode, `i` enters INSERT and Backspace is harmless on the new empty prompt; with Vim mode disabled or already in INSERT, Backspace removes the literal `i`.

Autohand uses the dedicated `autohand login` command from its [official CLI reference](https://docs.autohand.ai/working-with-autohand-code/cli-reference). Pi uses the documented plain `pi` startup before the explicit `/login` action; `--verbose` is not added.

The UI changes to **Login opened** or **Setup opened** only after the active attachment accepts terminal input; a rejected attempt stays retryable. There are no startup-output markers, locale overrides, launch arguments containing slash commands, or automatic submissions.

All provider selection, browser/device flow, credential entry, and credential storage remain inside the vendor CLI or vendor-documented configuration surface. AO does not render or own a provider credential panel.

Authentication verification follows the readiness boundary introduced by #4589. The compatibility `POST /api/v1/agents/:agent/probe` route invalidates only that agent's authentication observation, then performs a targeted launch-purpose readiness ensure. Harness settings requests `POST /api/v1/agents/readiness/ensure` with `purpose=display` and caches the normalized snapshot. Authentication status remains advisory; normal session spawn is the authoritative validation boundary.

The terminal is bounded by the Settings component lifecycle: navigating away closes an in-progress auth terminal, and the frontend also requests closure after 15 minutes. Attachment errors do not imply that the daemon-side process exited and therefore do not trigger verification. A failed close keeps a retryable cleanup state until deletion is confirmed.

## Security model

- the renderer starts terminal flows by sending only the fixed agent ID
- launch mode, terminal argv, and documentation URL come from the daemon-owned plan registry
- launch argv is resolved through the registered harness adapter
- the optional terminal input is returned only from the selected daemon-owned plan; arbitrary commands are not accepted from the start request
- each terminal action requires an explicit user click and is marked complete only after the active attachment accepts it
- every auth terminal gets a unique private child workspace
- interactive bytes pass through AO's existing terminal transport, but AO does not persist or log raw input; the harness controls credential storage
- documentation flows open only the fixed vendor URL and never collect credentials in AO
- authentication/configuration status comes from the daemon-owned readiness coordinator and remains advisory

## Validation

- regenerated OpenAPI and frontend TypeScript contracts
- frontend TypeScript typecheck
- focused frontend Vitest suites: 25 tests passing
- affected Go auth service, controller, and API-spec tests passing
- golangci-lint v2.12.2: 0 issues
- `git diff --check`

The unrestricted frontend/backend sweeps are not used as the focused validation command in this checkout: unrelated socket, optional-dependency, and timing-sensitive suites can fail under sandbox or CPU contention. The focused changed-area suites pass serially.

body:

## Summary

This intentionally does not change reconciliation, restart, runtime replacement, DB state, or the steady-state `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` classification. It borrows the narrow ENOENT distinction discussed in [PR #3801](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3801) without taking that PR's broader lifecycle changes.

title: feat(chat): keep native harness processes alive across daemon restart and desktop update
body:
## Problem

Chat-mode sessions are called runtime-less and each controller owns a provider child process (`codex app-server` or ACP). Daemon/Desktop shutdown calls `chatSvc.StopAll`, closes every child, marks the durable session Exited, and boot launches a replacement provider process plus native resume/history import. This interrupts AO's active controller generation and makes desktop updates materially different from terminal/tmux sessions, whose harness process survives and is adopted.

**Analyzed against:** `4cbb4b6ced1ad93f79641a2347d2342f1ffd218a` (`v0.12.9-nightly.202608262313`)
**Confidence:** High — shutdown, child ownership, recovery, and observed process/timing paths were traced locally.
**Priority:** P1 — closing/updating the desktop interrupts active Chat work; there is no continuity-preserving workaround other than keeping the whole old daemon alive, which conflicts with applying daemon updates.

## Required architecture

Introduce a provider-neutral, per-session Chat host outside the daemon:

- The host owns provider stdio and remains alive when its daemon control client disconnects.
- A versioned authenticated loopback control transport permits exactly one daemon controller owner and reconnects after restart.
- Provider output is sequence-journaled while detached and replayed before live output; daemon acknowledgements allow bounded compaction. Native history remains the correctness repair path.
- Durable controller generations continue fencing SQLite projection. Host attachment additionally enforces one live transport owner.
- Credentials remain only in the host/child environment. Host metadata stores an opaque endpoint, protocol version, process identity, and a random 0600 capability; never provider credentials.
- Protocol compatibility is negotiated. An incompatible new daemon must leave a live old host untouched and surface a typed recovery error. Idle hosts can later be rolled to a new binary; active turns are never killed merely to update the host.
- Explicit session kill terminates the host. Daemon crash/desktop close/update only detaches. Boot reaps authenticated hosts for missing/terminated sessions; it must not infer death from a failed probe.
- Window close may keep the daemon or detach according to desktop ownership policy, but neither path kills a Chat host. Full quit/update stops the daemon and detaches hosts. OS reboot/provider crash falls back to existing native resume.

## Smallest end-to-end slice

1. Add a detached `ao chat-host` process with a stable v1 authenticated loopback protocol and atomic 0600 descriptor under `AO_DATA_DIR`.
2. Integrate Codex Chat first: initial controller starts the host/provider; daemon restart reconnects to the same app-server without a second `initialize`/`thread/resume`; explicit kill shuts it down.
3. Buffer/replay provider JSONL emitted while no daemon is attached, with bounded failure behavior. Keep native `thread/read` import on reconnect for projection repair.
4. Reconcile host descriptors against durable sessions on boot and preserve existing restart/resume fallback when no live compatible host exists.
5. Add process-level tests proving provider PID and in-flight output survive daemon-side disconnect/reconnect, exclusive attachment, authentication, explicit shutdown, incompatible-version refusal, and orphan cleanup.

The ACP drivers can migrate to the same host transport after the Codex slice proves the lifecycle contract.

## Safety invariants

- Never send provider `turn/interrupt` or close provider stdin on daemon detach.
- Never let two daemon controllers consume one provider stream.
- Never kill a live host solely because protocol probing failed or a new daemon is incompatible.
- Never persist provider credentials or expose an unauthenticated control listener.
- Never mark the replacement controller ready until replay/history reconciliation and generation fencing commit.

## Related

- #2335 — terminal session lifetime was decoupled from the daemon; closed before Chat mode existed.
- #2230 / PR #2847 — optional whole-daemon persistence; PR explicitly deferred old-daemon/update compatibility.
- PR #3472 — introduced runtime-less Chat controllers.
- PR #4071 — resumes Chat controllers after restart but necessarily starts new provider processes.

title: Merge-conflict nudge does not re-fire after conflict is resolved and later returns
body:
## Bug

AO notifies a worker the first time a tracked PR becomes conflicting, but does not notify it when that conflict is resolved and a later base-branch advance makes the same PR conflicting again.

**Reported from:** AO worker session `agent-orchestrator-149` while handling PR #4165
**Observed:** 2026-08-26
**Analyzed against:** `4cbb4b6ce`
**AO:** locally built `dev`, daemon healthy on port 3001
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — missed automation notification; the user can manually steer the worker as a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Track an open PR owned by a live worker session.
2. Make the PR conflicting and allow the SCM observer to deliver the merge-conflict nudge.
3. Rebase the PR so it is clean/mergeable.
4. Advance the base branch so the same PR becomes conflicting again.
5. Observe that AO does not deliver a second merge-conflict nudge.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go` queues merge-conflict nudges with key `merge-conflict:<pr-url>` and the constant signature `conflicting`. `sendOnce` persists that key/signature in `pr.last_nudge_signature`.

A later non-conflicting observation does not clear or re-arm the merge-conflict dedup entry. When conflict returns, `sendOnce` sees the same key/signature and treats it as already delivered. The persisted state makes the suppression survive daemon restarts.

Live state for PR #4165 confirmed:

- durable mergeability: `conflicting`
- seen signature: `merge-conflict:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4165 = conflicting`
- attempts: `1`

This exactly explains why the first conflict notification arrived and the later one did not.

## Fix

Re-arm the merge-conflict reaction after a definitive non-conflicting observation (but not an `unknown` transient): remove/reset that PR-specific seen signature and attempt count, persist the updated reaction payload, and add lifecycle plus observer integration coverage for:

`mergeable -> conflicting (notify) -> mergeable (re-arm) -> conflicting (notify again)`

Identical consecutive conflicting observations must remain deduplicated, including across daemon restart.

body:
Refs #4526
