title: fix(mobile): declare the iOS privacy manifest to match the store labels
body:
Follow-up to the App Review rejection of 1.2.0 (guideline 5.1.2(i)). The privacy
labels in App Store Connect have been corrected there; this closes the matching
gap in the binary.

The generated `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` shipped an empty `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes`
while App Store Connect declares two data types. Expo merges `ios.privacyManifests`
from the app config into the generated manifest, so they are declared there now:

- **Product Interaction** — analytics, not linked, not used for tracking. The
  PostHog event stream, anonymous by construction: `personProfiles: "never"` at
  `lib/telemetry/runtime.ts` and nothing in the app calls `identify()`.
- **Device ID** — app functionality, not linked, not used for tracking. The Expo
  push token minted in `lib/push.ts` and registered with the daemon so
  notifications can be delivered.

`NSPrivacyTracking` stays `false`, which is accurate: no IDFA, no AdSupport, no
advertising or attribution SDK, and nothing shared with data brokers. Apple's
5.1.2(i) rejection was based on the store labels, not on app behaviour.

Also corrects `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`, which described camera-related
pairing rather than attaching images. The `expo-image-picker` plugin's
`photosPermission` already overrode it in the built `Info.plist`, so no shipped
build carried the wrong string — this just stops the two from contradicting each
other.

Static plist declaration only; no runtime code. Takes effect on the next prebuild.

title: fix(preview): clear session preview URL when managed dev server crashes (#4500)
body:
## Summary

When a managed preview dev-server crashed after launch, the Browser panel
kept showing the stale page with no error; `ao preview status` later
reported plain `stopped` (issue #4500).

`waitForExit` flipped the run to `StateFailed` but did not call
`SetPreview("")` and emitted no event. The panel's only failure hook,
`did-fail-load`, fires on navigation, not on an already-rendered page
whose backing server died. After `failedStatusRetention` (5 min) the
failed run was deleted, so status then reported `stopped` with no error.

## Fix

- `previewserver.Manager` gains an `OnExit(sessionID, Status)` callback
  fired from `waitForExit` when the run was not user-stopped. It runs
  off the manager's lock with a fresh 5s context.
- `daemon.go` registers an `OnExit` that clears the session's
  `PreviewURL` via `sessionSvc.SetPreview(ctx, id, "")` only when the
  session's current preview URL still matches the dead server's URL, so
  unrelated static-file previews are not clobbered. The existing
  `session_updated` CDC event fans the change out to the renderer.
- The Browser panel is not changed. Issue #4500 calls the polished
  panel state a separate "+1-2h" follow-up; this PR gives the panel
  the necessary session-update signal so it can drop the dead URL on
  its next render.

## Tests

- `TestManagerFiresOnExitWhenServerCrashesAfterLaunch` — boots, becomes
  ready, crashes; callback fires with `StateFailed` and a non-empty
  `Error`.
- `TestManagerDoesNotFireOnExitWhenStoppedByUser` — callback stays
  quiet on `Stop`.

Both new tests pass alongside the existing `previewserver`,
`httpd/controllers` (preview routes), and `service/session`
(`SetPreview`) suites.

## Out of scope

- Polished Browser panel dead-server UI (issue notes this as a
  follow-up).
- `failedStatusRetention` behavior. The callback fires immediately on
  crash; the run is still available via `Status` for 5 min before
  being deleted, matching the existing contract.

title: fix(codex): invoke Windows hook executable with PowerShell call operator
body:
## Summary
On Windows, AO injects Codex hook commands that begin with a quoted absolute path, but no PowerShell call operator. Codex executes these command hooks through PowerShell, so `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `Stop` fail before `ao.exe` starts.

## Reproduction
1. Use the AO desktop install on Windows and start a Codex session.
2. AO emits a hook command equivalent to:
   ```text
   "<AO executable path>" hooks codex stop
   ```
3. Run that command in PowerShell.

### Actual result
PowerShell returns:
```text
Unexpected token 'hooks' in expression or statement.
```
The hook exits with code 1. The same generated form is used for `session-start` and `user-prompt-submit`.

### Expected result
The command should execute the binary and return its status.

## Root cause
In `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/hooks.go`, `shellQuoteHookExecutable` returns `"<path>"` on Windows. In PowerShell that is a string expression, not an invocation.

## Proposed fix
Generate the Windows prefix as:
```text
& "<AO executable path>"
```
so the final command is:
```text
& "<AO executable path>" hooks codex stop
```
Alternatively, invoke through `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with correct quoting.

## Verification
The literal generated command reproducibly exits 1 in PowerShell. Adding `&` invokes the same `ao hooks codex stop` command successfully with exit 0. No credentials, payloads, or user content are required to reproduce.

title: feat: add failure-only observability for agent switching
body:
## Summary

- add a complete failure taxonomy and durable failure-only outbox for async agent switching
- cover admission, lifecycle, runtime, recovery, delivery, storage, policy, and frontend visibility branches
- add strict consent generations, purge/drain ordering, ownership-based duplicate suppression, throttling, and privacy-safe Sentry envelopes
- add operator runbooks for all 71 failure points

Successful switches emit no Sentry reports. Production capture remains disabled until the documented privacy and Windows durability gates are approved.

## Complete design package

The complete design—including the original one-layer tree, the expanded end-to-end decision tree, all 71 failure points, subsystem coupling, suppression rules, consent flow, privacy boundary, severity model, and release gates—is attached in [this PR comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4598#issuecomment-5454529824).

Committed source-of-truth documents:

- [Approved design](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/codex/agent-switch-failure-observability/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-agent-switch-failure-observability-design.md)
- [Implementation plan](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/codex/agent-switch-failure-observability/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-28-agent-switch-failure-observability.md)
- [Runbook for every failure point](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/codex/agent-switch-failure-observability/docs/runbooks/agent-switch-failure-points.md)
- [Telemetry and privacy contract](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/codex/agent-switch-failure-observability/docs/telemetry.md)

## Behavioral changes included in this PR

This is not an observability-only change. Correct failure classification requires the switching code to distinguish a write that definitely failed from a response that was lost after another actor committed progress, and to avoid starting or restoring a runtime whose ownership cannot be recovered. The PR therefore includes deliberate runtime and policy changes.

### 1. Idempotent target-acknowledgement readback

Target acknowledgement now uses an authoritative readback in both the session-manager path (`acknowledgeAgentSwitchTargetWithReadback`) and the lifecycle path (`acknowledgeAgentSwitchTarget`). If the acknowledgement write returns an error, reports `changed=false`, or races with another transition, AO reloads the durable switch before deciding the outcome.

- If the exact target generation is durably acknowledged, the acknowledgement is accepted even when the original write response was lost.
- If the switch is already terminal or has left the expected `delivering`/target-generation predicate, the callback is treated as stale or superseded rather than as evidence that the active switch failed.
- If the same delivery predicate is still current and the acknowledgement is absent, AO returns a real acknowledgement error; it does not infer success.

This prevents a committed acknowledgement or a concurrent winning transition from being misreported as a new switch failure while preserving failures where the durable acknowledgement genuinely did not stick.

### 2. Lost/stale Chat acknowledgement semantics

The Chat continuation path now yields successfully and marks its call stale when acknowledgement readback proves that the switch has already moved beyond the callback's `delivering` state or target generation. A delayed callback can therefore no longer terminalize, retry, or emit a failure for a switch whose authoritative state has already advanced elsewhere.

This is intentionally narrower than “ignore acknowledgement errors”: AO only yields when durable readback proves that the callback's predicate is obsolete. An unacknowledged switch that remains in the same delivery predicate still follows the normal failure path.

### 3. ConPTY restart-registry reservation and partial-effect evidence

On Windows, ConPTY `Create` now reserves the restart-registry record before spawning `pty-host`. Failure to create that reservation fails `Create` before a child process can be started. If spawning subsequently fails, AO rolls the reservation back.

If reservation removal itself fails, `Create` now returns the retained handle as `effect=possible` and `cleanup=failed`. The session manager therefore keeps the recovery gate and can perform exact cleanup; it does not incorrectly restore the source while a reservation or process may still exist.

The restart registry is a hard prerequisite for Windows session creation. AO must not create a live terminal process that is absent from crash-recovery state and cannot be safely identified, fenced, or reclaimed after daemon restart.

### 4. Conservative tmux ownership after preserved-shell/manual relaunch

An existing tmux pane without the expected AO supervisor is no longer treated as proof that the fenced generation is dead. Because the preserved shell may contain a manually relaunched workload, the probe returns `unknown/identity_missing` unless exact death is affirmatively established. Recovery retains the gate instead of restoring the source and risking two live owners.

### 5. Legacy recovery-marker migration

The observability migration is now `0119` after merging the latest `main`. During the table rebuild, legacy rows stored as `failed/source_stop_unconfirmed` are normalized to the retained-recovery state `stopping_source/source_stop_unconfirmed`. Existing databases with this valid legacy marker can upgrade without violating the new constraint, and the marker remains available for safe reconciliation.

### 6. Opt-out is a provider-call barrier, not only a capture flag

Sentry capture uses a synchronous transport behind a policy-controlled intake gate. Disabling reporting first closes intake, drains dispatcher work and every already-entered provider call, then acknowledges the off generation. Once opt-out completes, no queued SDK event can begin a later provider request. The failure-reporting preference remains separate from existing PostHog product analytics: disabling agent-switch failure reports neither disables PostHog nor purges its queues.

### 7. Provider and filesystem boundaries remain adapter-owned

The core domain owns normalized failure vocabulary, validation, and severity only. Sentry JSON/envelope encoding now lives in the Sentry adapter and is injected through an encoder port. Authority-file I/O, symlink/mode checks, bounded JSON parsing, and validation live in a filesystem adapter injected through an authority-reader port. Safety-critical policy, lease, settlement, expiry, receipt, and backlog statements use generated sqlc queries so authorization predicates have one maintained source.

### Why these changes remain together

These behaviors provide the state-certainty and ownership guarantees used by the failure-only classifiers: committed-response-lost versus genuine write failure, stale callback versus active failure, and recoverable runtime versus unidentifiable process. Keeping them in this PR avoids an intermediate implementation where observability would classify ambiguous outcomes without the durable readback and fencing semantics it relies on. They are called out separately here so reviewers and future revert work can identify their runtime impact independently from the reporting pipeline.

## Verification

- merged latest `main` and resolved the migration and frontend conflicts
- targeted backend runtime, domain, policy, Sentry adapter, session-manager, SQLite/store, and daemon suites passed
- frontend TypeScript check passed
- focused frontend shared/renderer telemetry suites passed (67 tests)
- sqlc regeneration completed; generated artifacts are committed
- `git diff --check` and conflict-marker scan passed

title: feat(omp): track TUI session activity
body:
## What

Add AO-managed OMP TUI lifecycle hooks so Kanban session status reflects active work, idle turns, approval waits, session switches, and process exit.

## Why

OMP TUI sessions had no structured activity integration, so their Kanban status could remain idle while the agent was working or waiting for user approval.

## How

- Install a project-local `.omp/extensions/ao-activity.ts` extension and load it explicitly for launch and restore.
- Map OMP lifecycle and approval events into the existing AO hook pipeline and activity-state derivation.
- Filter every callback to the top-level UI context so inherited subagent extension runners cannot alter the root AO session.
- Handle `session_switch` so `/new`, `/resume`, and `/fork` immediately refresh the native resume ID while preserving idle state.

title: feat: support ao:// deep links to sessions
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Feature

Register and handle a stable `ao://` deep-link protocol for navigating to Agent Orchestrator resources, beginning with sessions.

Canonical session URL:

```text
ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}
```

The path-based form is deliberate: project and session identifiers remain distinct, percent-encodable path segments instead of being ambiguously packed into a dotted hostname.

## User value

Links copied from AO, terminals, browsers, issue descriptions, and other applications should open the referenced session in Agent Orchestrator. Session IDs remain stable when display names change, so shared links remain valid.

## Scope

- Define a versioned parser/resolver for the `ao://` scheme.
- Support `ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}` first.
- Register the Electron app as the operating-system protocol handler on supported macOS, Windows, and Linux packaging paths.
- Route links into the existing AO window when it is running; launch AO and navigate after readiness when it is not.
- Focus the target session's appropriate surface, including retained history for terminated sessions.
- Show a clear error when a project/session is missing, inaccessible, malformed, or unsupported.
- Provide a copy-link action using the canonical URL.
- Keep the parser/navigation contract reusable by in-app Chat and TUI session links.

## Security boundary

- Deep links navigate only; they must never execute shell commands or silently send messages, spawn/kill sessions, mutate GitHub state, or merge work.
- Allowlist route types and validate/decode every path segment.
- Reject credentials, unexpected authorities, malformed encoding, extra action parameters, and unsupported routes.
- Do not pass raw URLs to a shell.
- Navigation requires an explicit user link activation outside any documented OS launch behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Clicking a canonical session URL outside AO opens or focuses AO at the correct project/session.
- The same URL resolves inside an already-running AO instance without opening a duplicate window.
- Session renames do not invalidate links.
- Terminated sessions open in their supported read-only/history view.
- Missing and malformed targets fail safely with actionable UI feedback.
- Protocol registration and second-instance routing work in packaged builds on macOS, Windows, and Linux where supported.
- Unit tests cover parsing, encoding, allowlisting, malformed URLs, unsupported routes, and stable IDs.
- Packaged-app tests cover cold launch, warm launch/second instance, and unavailable targets.

## Product questions

- Should initial support be limited to sessions, or reserve documented routes for projects and PRs without implementing them yet?
- On platforms where system registration is unavailable, should AO expose a copyable web fallback or report that deep linking is unsupported?

## Related work

A companion issue will cover rich session references and clickable navigation inside Chat and the in-app TUI using this resolver.

title: feat: render rich session links in Chat and TUI
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Feature

Allow any AO participant—not only an orchestrator—to reference another session using rich, clickable session links in Chat and the in-app TUI.

Example canonical target:

```text
ao://sessions/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator-255
```

An agent or user may include that target in a response. AO should render or detect it as a session reference and navigate only after the user clicks it.

## User value

Workers frequently hand off investigation, implementation, review, or follow-up work to other sessions. Today the user must locate the target manually in the sidebar. A session reference should show useful identity/status and open the correct session directly.

## Scope

### Chat

- Recognize allowlisted session URLs in messages from users, workers, orchestrators, and automation; do not role-gate the feature.
- Support Markdown links and raw canonical URLs.
- Render a rich session chip/link when target metadata is available, with a safe plain-link fallback.
- Display the current session name, role/harness, and useful status without making the display name part of identity.

### In-app TUI

- Register a terminal link provider for canonical `ao://sessions/...` text and supported OSC 8 links.
- Make activation explicit, using the platform-appropriate modifier/click behavior where needed to avoid interfering with terminal selection.
- Intercept the URL inside AO; never pass it to the shell or an external browser.

### Shared behavior

- Use one strict parser/resolver/navigation path across Chat and TUI.
- Resolve by stable project/session IDs so renaming does not break old messages.
- Open terminated sessions in retained history/read-only mode when available.
- Show an actionable error for missing, inaccessible, malformed, or unsupported targets.
- Do not navigate automatically while content streams or merely because an agent emitted a URL.

## Security boundary

- This feature is navigation-only.
- An agent must not force a route change or encode actions such as send, spawn, kill, merge, or shell execution.
- The Markdown sanitizer and terminal detector must allow only the canonical AO route shape and reject lookalike/malformed schemes.
- Link labels are untrusted presentation; resolved session metadata supplies authoritative identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- The same canonical session URL works in Chat and the in-app TUI.
- Messages from every supported origin/role receive identical link behavior.
- Clicking opens the exact project/session in the current AO app.
- Rendering never causes automatic navigation.
- Renaming the target changes its displayed metadata without breaking the stored link.
- Missing and terminated-session behavior is explicit and tested.
- TUI parsing handles line wrapping and adjacent punctuation without consuming unrelated terminal text.
- Tests cover Chat Markdown/raw URLs, sanitizer behavior, TUI raw/OSC 8 detection, modifier activation, renamed/terminated/missing targets, and malicious URL variants.

## Product questions

- Should the first UI be a compact inline chip or a conventional styled link with a hover preview?
- Should a click always open Chat, or restore the target's last active inspector surface?
- Should generated messages expose a structured session-reference entity in addition to parsing canonical URLs?

## Related work

- #4602 defines system-level `ao://` registration and the shared canonical session URL contract.

title: Add Neovim to the supported "Open in Editor" targets
body:
## What

Add Neovim as a supported target in the "Open in Editor" handoff feature (`frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts`, `frontend/src/shared/editor-handoff.ts`).

## Current state

`EDITOR_IDS` in `frontend/src/shared/editor-handoff.ts` lists 20 supported editors (Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders, VSCodium, Windsurf, Zed, Trae, Kiro, Positron, Sublime Text, and the JetBrains family), each mapped in `frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts` to a detection command and macOS app name. Neovim is a common editor for engineers working in this kind of terminal-first tool; right now there's no way to jump from an AO session's worktree straight into it the way you can with VS Code or the JetBrains IDEs.

title: fix(mobile): restore native PTY terminal rendering
body:
## What

Restore mobile rendering and viewport behavior for native PTY terminal sessions introduced by the recent macOS PTY rollout.

- resolve terminal streams through the daemon terminal handle
- preserve ANSI 256-color and truecolor capability in spawned PTYs
- keep the desktop PTY grid authoritative while mobile uses a local cropped viewport
- make the mobile plus/minus controls zoom in place without remounting or detaching the terminal

## Why

Native macOS PTY sessions could appear missing or monochrome on mobile. When a desktop-sized terminal was shared with mobile, fit-to-width made it unreadably small, and changing zoom remounted the WebView, briefly blanked the screen, and then returned to the same apparent size.

## How

The daemon now normalizes PTY color environment variables while respecting explicit overrides. Mobile uses the daemon-provided terminal handle and applies viewport transforms inside the existing xterm WebView, leaving PTY rows and columns unchanged.

Native pinch gesture recognition is intentionally not included in this fix; plus/minus viewport zoom is covered here.

title: fix(chat): surface Claude retry status and backoff
body:
Fixes #4612

## Summary

- surface Claude API and transport retries instead of leaving Chat on the generic `Working` status
- preserve retry attempt counts and backoff timing through the packaged Claude ACP adapter
- normalize provider failures into durable AO activities and clear the live warning when provider output resumes
- keep one live retry row per AO turn, so new upstream incident IDs update the warning instead of stacking duplicate rows
- render the live retry status accessibly in the active turn

## Root cause

The pinned Claude ACP adapter discarded `api_retry` events. The newer adapter gates failure notifications behind an advertised client capability and still drops `retry_delay_ms`. AO also ignored the extension metadata, so the renderer only knew the turn remained active and displayed `Working`.

During the native local reproduction, I found one additional edge case: Claude creates a fresh incident ID for every retry. AO initially used that ID as the rendered item identity, which caused prior attempts to accumulate. The final implementation scopes the retry item identity to the AO turn, so the latest attempt replaces the prior one.

## Test plan

- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/service/chat`
- ChatWorkspace renderer suite: 82 passed
- ACP runtime helper suite: 7 passed
- frontend typecheck
- fresh ACP runtime build

## Native desktop demo

Reproduced in the real AO Electron app from this branch using isolated state under `~/.ao/dev/claude-retry-demo-v2`, daemon port `3012`, and renderer `http://localhost:5174`. I forced only Claude's provider endpoint to an unreachable loopback address (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9`), which recreates the lost-provider/network path without disconnecting the machine.

### Before — original report

AO stayed on the generic working state with no retry details.

![Original report: AO remains on Working](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-chat-retry-status/.issue-assets/claude-chat-retry-status/original-report.png)

### After — local native reproduction on this branch

AO displays one live warning row with the provider retry count, maximum attempts, and current backoff. The captured state reads: **“Reconnecting to Claude, attempt 5 of 10. Connection error. Trying again in 8.6s.”** Earlier attempts updated this same row rather than accumulating.

![Local AO desktop demo showing Claude retry count and backoff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-chat-retry-status/.issue-assets/claude-chat-retry-status/local-demo-fixed.jpeg)

title: bug(chat): Claude retries are hidden behind generic Working status
body:
## Bug

When a Claude Code Chat turn loses network access, Claude retries the API request with an attempt count and backoff delay. AO hides that state and continues to display only the generic Working timer.

**Reported by:** subbu in Discord
**Reported:** 2026-08-28
**Analyzed against:** 5a51a3f90c4b649c21f92d1fcd58204e5e8e1a89
**Confidence:** High — the exact Claude SDK event, ACP adapter behavior, daemon normalization boundary, and renderer fallback were traced and reproduced with deterministic protocol events.
**Priority:** Medium — Chat remains usable after recovery, but users cannot distinguish productive work from a disconnected provider or understand retry timing.

## Original report

> I lost internet connection in my session. In vanilla Claude Code, if there is a network issue it shows API error and retry count and backoff time. In AO it just shows working.

![AO remains on Working during a Claude connection failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-chat-retry-status/.issue-assets/claude-chat-retry-status/original-report.png)

## Reproduction

1. Start a Claude Code session in AO Chat mode.
2. Send a prompt that reaches the Claude API.
3. Disconnect the machine from the network while the turn is active.
4. Observe the active turn status.

## Expected

AO shows the connection/API failure, retry attempt and maximum, and the next backoff duration, then clears the warning when output resumes.

## Actual

AO continues to display Working for ... with no indication that Claude is retrying.

## Root cause

- The bundled claude-agent-acp 0.64.2 adapter discarded api_retry SDK events.
- The current adapter publishes retry failures only when the ACP client advertises the AIR sessionFailure extension.
- The adapter omitted retry_delay_ms from that extension.
- AO ignored session-info failure metadata, leaving the renderer with only the durable running-turn state and its generic Working fallback.

## Fix

[PR #4611](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4611) upgrades and patches the packaged adapter, negotiates the failure capability, normalizes failures into durable activities, renders them in the active turn, and settles the warning when provider output resumes.

## Related

- [PR #4216](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4216) — analogous transient transport-failure UX for Codex Chat.

title: fix(mobile): make OTA updates actually reach builds
body:
## What

Makes the OTA feature from #4474 actually deliverable, and removes the `google-services.json` temp-commit dance.

`main` today produces builds whose fingerprint runtime version **no publishing machine can reproduce**, so no update would ever reach them. The publish succeeds, the dashboard says the update is live, and every device silently stays on the embedded bundle.

## Four divergence sources, all closed

`eas.json`, `.gitignore`, `google-services.json` delivery, and Expo patch drift. Measured under the old flow: a build came out at `84c9dff7` while the same tree published at `53ad3ec1`. After this change both states resolve identically on both platforms.

| Source | Why it diverged | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eas.json` | Holds local-only App Store Connect submit credentials, kept out of the public repo with `git update-index --skip-worktree`. EAS Build reads the committed file; the publishing machine reads the local one. | `ignorePaths` |
| `.gitignore` | The temp-commit dance deleted a line from it to force `google-services.json` past EAS's VCS client — and `.gitignore` is itself a fingerprint input. | Dance removed; `ignorePaths` as belt-and-braces |
| `google-services.json` | Gitignored (origin is public), so EAS Build never received it. | `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` file environment variable + `app.config.js` |
| Expo patches | `expo` pinned with a caret against exactly-pinned peers, so a lock regeneration drifted them apart and failed `expo-doctor`. | Patch bumps, settled before the build |

`app.config.js` copies whatever absolute path EAS provides to the fixed `./google-services.json` that `app.json` already points at, rather than emitting that path into the config. Emitting it would make the resolved config differ between EAS Build and this machine — the same bug one level up. Verified: with `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` set to an unrelated absolute path, both the resolved `googleServicesFile` and the fingerprint are identical to a plain local checkout.

## Verified on device

Preview builds on both platforms, each with its build fingerprint matching the publishing machine — Android `307dee3c…`, iOS `66d18d1d…`.

- Baseline: no update id on the version row, **App updates** reports `Up to date`
- Manual path: check → download → `Ready — tap to restart` → applied, version row gains the update id
- Cold start: applied on the **second** launch, not the first (Android)
- Rollback to embedded with populated storage — onboarding, a saved chat draft, a changed theme — no crash, data intact, both platforms

**Not verified:** the 15-minute resume path. `onForeground` has unit coverage; the `AppState` wiring around it has never run on a device. Recorded as such in the README rather than left implied.

## Also

Removes the temp-commit dance entirely, so there is no longer a state where one `git push` leaks Firebase config to a public repo.

The README gains the build-or-update decision rule and the operational traps found while testing — two of which are incident-grade: updates published *before* a build are invisible to that build (`useEmbeddedUpdate` prefers the newer embedded bundle), and `roll-back-to-embedded` is per-runtime, so an incident needs it run once per platform. During this testing Android sat rolled back for an hour while iOS stayed on the test bundle, which is exactly how that would play out unnoticed in production.

title: feat(mobile): connect from any network by racing every advertised endpoint
body:
## What this does

Lets a phone reach the daemon from any network, without the user knowing what a LAN address or a tailnet is.

The QR previously carried a single address — in practice the LAN one. Off that network, pairing failed and the user landed in manual entry, Tailscale setup, or a certificate problem. The code now carries **every** endpoint the machine has, and the phone races them, verifying it reached the right machine before trusting any of them.

Same three onboarding steps as before. The change is that they now work from cellular.

## How it works

Three endpoint kinds are advertised and raced, preferred cheapest-first (`lan > tailscale > tunnel`):

- **LAN** — every reachable interface address, not just one
- **Tailscale** — when present
- **Tunnel** — a `cloudflared` quick tunnel the daemon supervises, giving reach from anywhere plus a publicly trusted certificate (which also satisfies iOS ATS and retired the MagicDNS/tailnet-certificate branch of the old flow)

The race verifies host identity on every candidate via a new `GET /api/v1/identity`, so a phone cannot be steered onto the wrong machine by a stale or reused address. Endpoints are refreshed on every successful connect, so a rotated tunnel hostname or a changed DHCP lease heals without re-pairing.

Which machine the app talks to is explicit: `activeHost()` answers with a selection where one has been made and the most recently used machine otherwise. Pairing and manual connect both set it; forgetting a machine clears it along with the machine and its token.

## Notable decisions

**One unauthenticated route.** `GET /api/v1/identity` returns only `{hostId, apiVersion}` and is exempt from the bearer-password middleware, because the race must be able to tell machines apart *before* it has a credential to offer. Documented in `docs/adr/0003-unauthenticated-identity-probe.md`, with `AGENTS.md` amended to name it as the single exemption; any further unauthenticated route needs its own ADR.

**Waiting for DNS happens on the phone.** A quick tunnel's hostname is registered before resolvers know it. The daemon cannot check that honestly — probing from the machine that owns the tunnel tests its own resolver, and probing early caches an NXDOMAIN locally that outlives propagation (measured: `curl` still failed 30s after `dig` had begun resolving the same name). So the daemon holds the hostname back briefly and the phone retries a tunnel candidate that does not resolve yet, which is where the deciding resolver actually lives.

**Installation identity survives hardware changes.** The host id belongs to the AO data directory, not to the current network hardware. Fingerprints are diagnostic metadata only, so docks and NIC replacement do not silently unpair every device. Copying the complete `~/.ao` directory also copies this identity; backups and migrations must therefore be protected, and resetting identity is an explicit removal of `~/.ao/mobile/identity.json` while AO is stopped.

**Cloudflare terminates TLS.** The phone's session is with Cloudflare, not with the user's machine, so tunnel traffic is encrypted in transit but not end to end. What that exposes, when the tunnel is chosen, and what would change it are in `docs/adr/0004-cloudflare-tunnel-for-remote-mobile-access.md`. The race preference is what keeps the tunnel to a last resort.

**v1 pairing codes are no longer accepted.** They predate the identity probe, so a daemon old enough to emit one answers 404 to every probe and the race can never complete — the compatibility was advertised but unreachable. A v1 code is still recognised, so the app says "update AO on your computer" rather than "this is not a pairing code".

## Known limitation: SSE does not stream over the tunnel

Measured against a live quick tunnel: response bodies are forwarded in ~128 KB chunks (a 121 KB replay produced nothing; larger ones arrived in exact multiples of 128 KB). A chat event is a few hundred bytes, so it is held indefinitely. WebSocket is unaffected — 11 ms round trips for small frames — because after the upgrade it is a raw tunneled stream rather than a buffered response body. That is why terminals felt normal over the tunnel while chat did not.

Two polling intervals compensate, **both stopgaps**, both active only while the tunnel is the chosen endpoint: the main poll drops 8s → 2s, and the chat screen polls its conversation, which it otherwise never does. They turn "over a minute, and only after reopening the screen" into roughly two seconds, at a cost in battery and data.

**The exit condition is concrete:** conversation events move to the existing `/mux` WebSocket, which already reaches the same daemon and already round-trips small frames in 11 ms over the tunnel. When that lands, both stopgaps are deleted.

## Verified on a physical device

Identity probe · race · migration from the single-server config · LAN → Tailscale → tunnel failover (~4s) · terminal following the raced endpoint · chat on all three paths · agent input prompts over the tunnel · sustained terminal output over the tunnel · tunnel crash detection and restart · hostname rotation picked up without re-pairing · orphaned connector reaped · enable/disable · images and navigation on a preview (production-bundle) build.

Four defects were found that way and fixed here: the app never returning to LAN once it fell to the tunnel; a black screen on open, caused by treating "no config yet" as "not configured" while the race resolved; a connector left running after the daemon quit; and endpoint lists losing a kind depending on when a refresh landed.

## Review round

- Migration lost the password for the oldest upgraders — it read only SecureStore, but older builds kept it in the config blob and the code that relocates it runs *after* migration
- "Disconnect & forget" did not forget: `removeHost` had no callers, so the machine and its token survived and the next launch reconnected to it
- A manual connection did not stick — it wrote only the legacy config, so resolution replaced it with the previous machine on reload
- A restarting connector could delete its replacement's pid file, leaving a live tunnel that boot reaping could never clean up
- Nothing installed `cloudflared`, so on a machine without it the QR looked normal and only ever worked on the local network. It is now a seventh `systeminstall` target, offered where the limitation is stated
- A dock or a new network card reissued the host id and unpaired every phone
- A rotated tunnel hostname produced a bare "can't connect" the phone could not recover from; it now names the one action that works
- Dead code removed (`connectionAction.ts`), and the multi-machine claim corrected — see below

## Not covered

- **There is no host switcher.** Up to 10 machines are stored with per-host tokens and per-host event cursors, and `activeHost()` owns the selection — but nothing in the UI lets you choose one, so a second machine is reachable by pairing with it, not by picking it from a list. The plumbing is here; the picker is not.
- **Per-device revocable tokens.** There is one shared connection password, and removing a phone from the device roster deletes its registry row without revoking access — it can reconnect immediately. This predates the PR, but the PR raises the stakes since pairing now works from anywhere. Tracked as a bug; the fix changes `authMiddleware` and needs a migration, so it belongs in its own PR.
- **A provider interface for endpoint sources**, deliberately deferred: there is no second provider today, and a relay we run ourselves is a real possibility whose shape would likely reshape the interface.
- **Named tunnel mode**, for the same reason — a stable hostname would remove the rotation problem, but it needs an account and a domain, and we have not settled on Cloudflare as the destination.
- **`cloudflared` on Linux** resolves to instructions rather than an install, like every other Linux target, because AO never asks for an administrator password.
- **Battery and data cost** of the 2s tunnel poll is unmeasured.
- **Secure pairing** is not carried in a v2 code: the endpoint list only ever marks the tunnel secure. Whether that matters depends on whether iOS allows plain HTTP to a `100.x` tailnet address in a release build, which is untested. Recorded as a test documenting current behaviour rather than asserted away.
- **Network-change detection** takes 9–33s (poll interval plus request timeout). Root-caused; the fix needs `expo-network`, which changes the native fingerprint, so it is deferred.

## Testing

`go test ./...`, `npm test` in `packages/mobile`, frontend suites, `npm run lint` clean, and `npm run api` reproduces the committed spec with no diff.

title: [Bug]: Bundled static tmux 3.5a SIGFPEs on session create — AO can't spawn any agent

### Summary


AO: 0.12.9 (Linux x64 AppImage) · Host: Ubuntu22.04.5, glibc 2.35, kernel 6.8

Symptom: Every spawn fails with  500 ... tmux runtime: create session ...: server exited unexpectedly . No agent can start.

title: fix: sign packaged Node runtime for JIT so Chat sessions start on Intel Macs
body:
## What

Fixes the Chat-driven Claude Code session failing immediately on Intel Macs with `CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE`, and makes the next runtime failure of this shape report itself instead of surfacing as a bare disconnect.

Two commits:

1. Sign AO's packaged Node runtime with `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`.
2. Retain the ACP adapter's stderr tail and fold it into the initialize error.

## Why

Fixes #4442.

That issue's original diagnosis (AO spawns `claude` and expects it to speak ACP) is **wrong** — I filed it and have corrected the record [in a comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4442#issuecomment-5459101802). AO already packages `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` and passes `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE`; that code needed no change.

The real cause: **AO's packaged Node crashes on Intel Macs.** It aborts inside V8 on first tier-up:

```
# Fatal error in , line 0
# Check failed: 12 == (*__error()).
 3: v8::base::OS::SetPermissions(...)
15: v8::internal::GenerateBaselineCode(...)
```

`@electron/osx-sign`'s default entitlements grant `allow-jit` but not `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. Electron's own Chromium build tolerates that because it maps JIT pages with `MAP_JIT`; a stock nodejs.org build does not. On x86_64 V8's baseline compiler makes its code pages executable with plain `mprotect`, which the hardened runtime refuses without that entitlement. arm64 maps JIT pages differently and is unaffected — which is why this shipped.

Isolating the signature alone on the shipped 0.10.3 runtime:

| Signing config | Result |
| --- | --- |
| As shipped | crash |
| Signature removed | works |
| ad-hoc + hardened runtime + `allow-jit` only | crash (exact reproduction) |
| ad-hoc + hardened runtime + `allow-jit` + `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` | works |

The second commit exists because the crash was invisible: `spawnAgent` drained the adapter's stderr into `io.Discard`, so the V8 trace was written and thrown away, leaving only `peer disconnected before response`. That is what sent diagnosis toward the wrong subsystem.

## How

**Entitlements** — `optionsForFile` scopes the override to `acp-runtime/node/bin/node` by exact path segments. Every other file returns `{}` so `@electron/osx-sign` keeps applying its own defaults, notably the inherit entitlements Electron's helper apps require; a blanket `entitlements` override would break their signature. The new plist reproduces the signer's macOS defaults plus the one missing key, so nothing the runtime had today is dropped.

**stderr** — draining stays unbounded, so a chatty adapter still cannot fill its OS pipe and deadlock the protocol. Only what is *retained* is capped (8 KiB, last 12 lines in the message). `conv.Close()` is called before reading the tail so the process has driven its stderr pipe to EOF.

Intentionally **not** in this PR, both called out in the issue comment:

- A crashed adapter is still classified `CHAT_DRIVER_INCOMPATIBLE`. It is not a protocol mismatch, but correcting the classification is a behavioural change that deserves its own PR.
- `claudeacp`'s probe runs `node --version`, which exits 0 on a runtime that cannot execute JavaScript. Tightening the probe is likewise separable.

## Testing

**The entitlements fix is verified end-to-end against the real artifact**, not just unit-tested: re-signed the shipped 0.10.3 `acp-runtime` Node with the committed plist under `--options runtime`, then drove the shipped adapter through a genuine ACP `initialize`. It returns a valid result instead of aborting.

```
backend:  go build ./...                                    OK
          gofmt -l internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/         clean
          go vet ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/          OK
          golangci-lint v2.12.2 (changed package)             0 issues
          go test -race ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/...     all ok
frontend: tsc --noEmit                                        OK
          vitest forge.config.test.ts                         8 passed
```

New tests: `process_test.go` covers stderr retention through a real spawned process, the tail cap, and the error formatting. `forge.config.test.ts` gains coverage that the predicate matches only the packaged runtime and leaves Electron's helpers alone.

Two pre-existing failures on this machine, confirmed against a clean `main` and unrelated to these changes: `TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination` (timing-sensitive, fails under full-suite load on slower hardware) and `src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts`.

Verification was done on the affected hardware — Intel Core i7, macOS 15.7.7.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (rebased on `upstream/main` @ ae890182d)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend)

title: sqlc regenerate breaks the build: app_settings.cloud_offering hand-typed as bool without a sqlc.yaml override
body:
## What's wrong

Running the documented regen command on a pristine `main` breaks the build:

\`\`\`
cd backend && go run github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1 generate
go build ./...
# internal/storage/sqlite/store/app_settings_store.go:41:23: cannot use row.CloudOffering (variable of type int64) as bool value in struct literal
# internal/storage/sqlite/store/app_settings_store.go:67:18: cannot use enabled (variable of type bool) as int64 value in struct literal
\`\`\`

## Root cause

`app_settings.cloud_offering` is declared as a plain `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (cloud_offering IN (0, 1))` (migration `0112_app_settings_cloud_offering.sql`). sqlc cannot infer `bool` from that shape without an explicit override — and unlike its sibling boolean-ish columns (`pr_comment.resolved`, `sessions.auto_review_enabled`, `agent_switches.semantic_handoff_included`), `backend/sqlc.yaml` never got a `column: "app_settings.cloud_offering" go_type: "bool"` entry.

The committed `gen/models.go` and `gen/app_settings.sql.go` do type `CloudOffering` as `bool` (matching every consumer — `store/app_settings_store.go`, `service/settings/service.go`, `daemon/settings_wiring.go`, `httpd/controllers/dto.go`) — but that file was hand-edited to add `bool`, not generated. Two tells confirm it:
- `GetAppSettings`'s `row.Scan` is a single-line call; sqlc emits it multi-line once a struct has 4+ fields.
- `SetCloudOffering` is appended at the end of the file; sqlc orders declarations alphabetically, so it belongs before `SetDefaultSessionMode`.

This violates the repo's own "do not hand-edit `gen/*`" rule, and nothing catches it: CI regenerates and diff-checks the OpenAPI spec (`schema.ts`) but has no equivalent step for sqlc's `gen/` output, so the drift went unnoticed since it was introduced (feat(cloud) — the AO cloud offering integration).

## Fix

Add the missing override to `backend/sqlc.yaml`, alongside `app_settings.default_session_mode`:

\`\`\`yaml
- column: "app_settings.cloud_offering"
  go_type: "bool"
\`\`\`

Regenerating with that in place reproduces the current committed types exactly (plus the two cosmetic normalizations above). Also worth adding a CI guard mirroring the existing `schema.ts` drift check: `npm run sqlc && git diff --exit-code -- backend/internal/storage/sqlite/gen/`, so hand-edited `gen/` output can't silently ship again.

## Repro

\`\`\`
git clone <repo> && cd agent-orchestrator/backend
go run github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1 generate
git diff -- internal/storage/sqlite/gen/models.go   # CloudOffering flips to int64
go build ./...                                        # fails
\`\`\`

title: fix(sqlc): repair the hand-written go_type overrides in sqlc.yaml
body:
## Problem

`sqlc generate` on a pristine `main` is broken twice over:

1. **sqlc.yaml doesn't parse.** `cf350730b` (#4598) hand-wrote the `go_type` overrides for `agent_switch_failure_policy.enabled` and `app_settings.cloud_offering` with a leading tab on each column line:

   ```
   $ cd backend && go run github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1 generate
   error parsing sqlc.yaml: yaml: line 244: found character that cannot start any token
   ```

2. **The new entry carries no `go_type` at all.** Even with the tabs fixed, `agent_switch_failure_policy.enabled` is a bare list item — a generator run would type it `int64`, while the committed `gen/` and every consumer (`agent_switch_failure_store.go` uses `!policy.Enabled`) expect `bool`. `app_settings.cloud_offering` (#4621) is the same story: a plain `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (cloud_offering IN (0, 1))` column, typed `bool` in the committed `gen/` by hand — its sibling boolean-ish columns (`pr_comment.resolved`, `sessions.auto_review_enabled`, `agent_switches.semantic_handoff_included`) all carry an explicit override, that one didn't.

## Fix

- Repair the indentation (same alignment as the sibling entries).
- Give both entries `go_type: "bool"` — the type the committed `gen/` already uses and the only one the store code compiles against.

## What this PR intentionally does not include

A regenerated `gen/` (or a `sqlc-drift` CI job, as sketched in an earlier revision of this PR): after #4598 the committed `agent_switching.sql.go` is itself hand-written — sqlc now emits named `GetAgentSwitch*Row` structs the store code doesn't use, so a generator run diverges from `gen/` no matter what `sqlc.yaml` says. Reproducible `gen/` remains the bigger ask tracked in #4621; this PR restores the config to a parseable, semantically correct state so the next attempt starts from a working generator.

## Testing

- `cd backend && go run github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1 generate` — parses and completes
- `go build ./...` — passes (with the committed, untouched `gen/`)
- `gofmt -l .` — clean

Fixes #4621

title: feat(codex): add assisted profile switching
body:
## What

Adds Phase 5 assisted Codex profile switching as a stacked PR on Phase 4.

- Ranks authenticated profile candidates from daemon-owned auth/capacity snapshots.
- Requires explicit user confirmation for every switch, including acknowledgement for unknown, stale, or unsupported capacity.
- Persists a crash-recoverable profile-switch saga and immutable continuation relationship.
- Waits for a safe source boundary, builds a bounded verified handoff, stops the exact source generation, and transfers exclusive ownership of the existing workspace.
- Creates a new related AO session with an immutable target-profile binding and a fresh native Codex thread.
- Archives the predecessor only after the exact target acknowledges handoff delivery.
- Adds recovery/source-restoration paths, structured Chat `usageLimited` attribution, API routes, thin CLI commands, and the local desktop confirmation/progress surface.

## Why

When a bound Codex profile approaches or reaches its provider-reported limit, users need a safe way to continue with another authenticated profile without mutating the original binding, copying credentials, or allowing two sessions to write to one workspace.

## How

### Stack

- **Base:** `codex/phase-4-codex-profile-subscription-capacity`
- **This PR:** `codex/phase-5-codex-assisted-profile-switching`
- Retarget to `main` after Phase 4 merges.

### Durable coordination

- Adds migration `0119_codex_profile_switches.sql` with compare-and-swap phases, idempotency fingerprints, workspace ownership, generation fences, continuation relations, and the predecessor `archived_at` fact.
- Reconciles non-terminal operations during daemon startup before accepting session mutations.
- Keeps archived predecessors readable through continuation links while rejecting mutation/adoption/cleanup paths.
- Stores only safe operation facts and the private handoff reference/hash; profile homes, credentials, auth metadata, capacity, provider payloads, and handoff bodies are not persisted in SQLite.

### Isolation and handoff

- Strictly rediscovers and verifies the selected profile, installation, refreshed authentication, capacity, canonical home, source, and descriptor before source shutdown.
- Reuses the Phase 3 launch resolver and Phase 4 shared process semaphore.
- Transfers the existing worktree ownership row; it does not create or copy a workspace.
- Starts a fresh target native thread under the selected binding and never searches, resumes, or copies native history across profile homes.
- Uses one bounded optional semantic handoff plus deterministic fallback context with private permissions, symlink checks, atomic writes, and SHA-256 verification.
- Recovery retries only the existing target or explicitly restores the source; it never silently cascades to another profile.

### Intentional omissions

- No automatic profile switching.
- No changing either immutable source or target binding.
- No capacity, subscription, quota, credential, or historical-usage persistence.
- No reset-credit consumption.
- No profile deletion, rename, reorder, logout, API-key entry, or device login.

title: bug(agent): startup binary probe can discard a successful result
body:
## Summary

At desktop startup, `FindInstalledBinary` can report that no supported agent is installed even after one resolver has successfully found a binary.

## Reproduction

The race is exposed by repeatedly running:

```bash
cd backend
go test -race ./internal/service/agent -run '^TestFindInstalledBinary_ResolvesWithoutRefreshingInventory$' -count=1000
```

Before the fix, the stress loop intermittently fails with `expected a supported agent binary to be found`.

## Root cause

The method waits on two channels: a buffered successful-result channel and a separate completion channel. A resolver can enqueue a successful result, then the wait group closes the completion channel. When both select cases are ready, Go chooses one pseudo-randomly, so the completion case can incorrectly win and return `false`.

## Proposed fix

Close the result channel after all resolver goroutines finish, and receive from that single channel with the two-value form. A value means an agent was found; a closed empty channel means all resolvers completed without success. Context cancellation remains a separate case.

## Impact

Intermittent false-negative startup detection. This was first exposed by CI while working on #4611, but it is unrelated to Claude retry telemetry and should ship independently.

## Verification

- Stress regression test under the race detector
- Agent service package tests
- Backend build/test checks

Reported by @illegalcall.

title: fix(agent): avoid startup binary probe completion race
body:
Code changes: +0 -0  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## Conflict resolution — 2026-09-08

Merged current `main` (`be85b3d98`) and preserved the shared readiness coordinator introduced by #4589. That implementation already rechecks the buffered match when its completion signal wins, so it prevents the original false-negative race.

The resolved PR has **no remaining code diff against main** and is superseded by #4589. The original summary and verification below are retained as historical context.

Post-resolution validation passed: startup/readiness tests repeated 1,000 times under the race detector; the complete agent and system-check package suites under the race detector; `go build ./...`; and `go vet ./...`.

## Summary

- close the resolver result channel only after every startup probe finishes
- distinguish a successful result from a closed, empty channel
- remove the competing completion channel that could randomly discard an already-buffered success

## Why

`FindInstalledBinary` selected between a successful-result channel and a completion channel. Once both were ready, Go could choose completion and return `false` even though a resolver had found an installed agent.

Fixes #4625.

## Verification

In the current rewrite, `CenterPane` requested terminal focus only for shell and special agent-switch states. Chat is unaffected because `ChatComposer` explicitly restores editor focus on session changes.

## Fix

- Keep Chat sessions out of the worker-terminal focus path.
- Guard xterm autofocus when dialogs or menus are open or another deliberate control owns focus.
- Allow the selected session navigation button (`button[aria-current="page"]`) to hand focus to the destination TUI.
- Preserve retained-terminal focus when the destination becomes visible.

## Verification

- Session/Chat regressions: `SessionView`, `ChatComposer`, and `ChatWorkspace`, 3 files, 225 tests passed.
- Frontend typecheck: passed.
- Renderer Vite build: passed, with existing large-chunk warnings only.

Native isolated launch evidence: Electron Forge launched the checkout; the renderer reported `http://localhost:5173/`; the daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:3002`; and the isolated API returned both TUI and Chat sessions.

The reporter manually verified the implemented keyboard-focus behavior on the current rewrite.

title: fix  : invoke Windows hook executable with PowerShell call operator
body:
Fixes #4596

## Problem

On Windows, AO injects Codex hook commands that begin with a quoted absolute path but no PowerShell call operator. Codex executes command hooks through PowerShell, so `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `Stop` all fail before `ao.exe` ever starts:

```
"<AO executable path>" hooks codex stop
# PowerShell: Unexpected token 'hooks' in expression or statement. (exit 1)
```

## Root cause

`shellQuoteHookExecutable` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/hooks.go` returned `"<path>"` on Windows. In PowerShell a bare quoted string is a string expression, not an invocation.

## Fix

Generate the Windows prefix with the PowerShell call operator:

```
& "<AO executable path>" hooks codex stop
```

Non-Windows quoting is unchanged. The literal-assertion test helper `sessionHookFlags` (which mirrors the emitted `-c` flags so format drift fails loudly) was updated to match.

## Verification

- On Windows, the old literal form reproducibly fails with "Unexpected token" (exit 1); the `&` form invokes the binary successfully.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/codex/ -count=1` passes (Windows host, so the Windows path is exercised).
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/codex/` clean.
- Pre-existing `primeagent`/`registry` test failures on this host were confirmed to fail on the base commit too (environmental, unrelated).

title: feat(codex): add automatic profile switching
body:
## What

Adds explicit, continuation-chain-scoped automatic Codex profile switching on top of Phase 5.

- Persists revisioned ordered fallback policies and durable exhaustion attempts in migration `0120`.
- Accepts only structured, bound Chat usage-limit/capacity signals or a direct TUI boundary capacity read.
- Verifies candidates sequentially in the user-configured order and accepts only fresh `authorized` + `available` profiles.
- Delegates exactly one target to the existing Phase 5 switch, handoff, workspace-transfer, archive, and recovery engine.
- Exposes policy and cancellation APIs, thin CLI controls, and a session-details editor with ordered drag-and-drop fallbacks.
- Keeps the feature behind `AO_DEV_CODEX_AUTOMATIC_PROFILE_SWITCHING=1` while the live recovery exit matrix remains outstanding.

## Why

Phase 5 requires a user to confirm every assisted continuation. Phase 6 provides an explicit opt-in for a single continuation chain so confirmed exhaustion can safely use a user-approved fallback without introducing another launch or recovery path.

## How

- This PR is **stacked on Phase 5** (`codex/phase-5-codex-assisted-profile-switching`).
- Automatic switching is disabled by default and opt-in is scoped to one continuation chain.
- Only user-approved `existing` and managed profiles are considered, in the exact order configured by the user.
- Only confirmed exhaustion triggers evaluation; near-limit state never triggers it.
- Only a freshly authenticated profile with fresh `available` capacity qualifies.
- Phase 5 remains the sole switching, handoff, workspace, launch, archive, and recovery engine.
- Exactly one automatic target is delegated per exhaustion attempt, with no silent cascade after Phase 5 starts.
- New tasks, normal forks, reviewers, subtasks, and delegated children do not inherit permission.
- There is no global or project-wide policy, capacity ranking, cooldown guessing, polling, refresh control, or terminal-output parsing.
- Credentials, provider capacity, reset times, and historical usage are not persisted.
- One additive SQLite migration is included; existing migrations are unchanged.
- Architecture documents remain external and are not copied into the repository.
- CI will not be polled automatically; reported failures will be addressed when provided.

The PR is intentionally a draft because the daemon-local development gate remains enabled until the full live Phase 5 recovery and Phase 6 exit matrix is exercised.

title: fix(desktop): keep update status reactive across settings and sidebar
body:
## Reproduction

1. Open Settings → Updates.
2. Click Check for updates.
3. Let the check complete.
4. The visible Last checked timestamp can retain the mount-time value until Settings is closed and reopened.

The regression test reproduces the ordering directly: a completed-check push arrives first, then the older mount-time IPC snapshot resolves.

## Root cause

Each `useUpdateStatus` caller owned an independent `getStatus` request and `updates:status` listener. Snapshot hydration started before the listener was registered, and a late snapshot was always applied. An older response could therefore overwrite a newer pushed status, including `checkedAt`; Settings and the sidebar could also hydrate divergent local copies.

The renderer now uses one shared external updater store. It subscribes before requesting the initial snapshot and revision-gates that snapshot so a newer push wins. This remains a projection of the existing main-process updater state machine.

## Latest-main relevance audit (2026-09-01)

Rebased onto `main` at `8a88be0c7`.

`main` now includes #4729, which independently added the proactive sidebar update affordance, download/restart/retry states, tests, and per-version dismissal. Those older UI changes from this PR were intentionally dropped during conflict resolution so the newer product behavior remains authoritative.

The underlying reactivity bug is still present on latest `main`: `useUpdateStatus` still creates per-consumer state, starts independent snapshots, and permits a late snapshot to roll back a newer status push. The shared store fix remains relevant and now keeps the existing Settings and #4729 sidebar surfaces synchronized.

## Tests

- `npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx` — 123 passed
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run typecheck:e2e`

## Scope

After the rebase this is a focused two-file change: the shared updater status store plus the immediate Last checked regression test. The current sidebar UX from `main` is unchanged.

title: fix: align session usage costs and card metrics
body:
## Summary

- price fresh provider-native usage when the active catalog has exactly one owner for the reported model, recording the route as `inferred` so later observed Claude routing can still replace attribution and cost
- preserve honest unknowns: unidentified Claude proxy routes and models absent from the catalog remain unpriced
- extend the compact usage API with the canonical token/category totals already used by the detailed session view
- render exactly one Kanban scan metric: reliable dollar cost, otherwise reliable compact tokens, otherwise nothing (including no orphan separator)
- share the detailed token and cost-category breakdown between the developer-mode session inspector and the card's hover/focus tooltip

## Root cause and harness coverage

Fresh Claude Code records can carry native token counters before a billing route is observed. Live ingestion deliberately left those rows unattributed and relied on legacy repair, but repair runs at startup/settle or when route evidence changes. A newly spawned, continuously active worker could therefore accumulate reliable tokens while remaining unpriced until a later repair pass, producing `Unavailable · 5.2M` on its card.

Live ingestion now uses unique catalog ownership as explicitly inferred evidence. This is covered end-to-end for Claude Code, Codex records missing provider metadata, and Kimi wire usage. Provider-specific counters remain intact. Observed routes still win; unknown catalog models and the explicit unidentified-proxy sentinel do not receive fabricated costs.

## UI rules covered

- reliable estimate: `$1.24` only, including reliable `$0.00`
- no estimate + reliable usage: `5.2M` only
- neither: no metric and no separator
- no literal `Unavailable` card placeholder
- hover and keyboard focus disclose fresh input, cache reads, output, cache-hit rate, input/cache/output costs, coverage, and observed/inferred attribution context

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/observe/usage ./internal/service/usage ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/httpd/...`
- sanitized worker environment: `go test ./...`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` (144 passed)

## Preview evidence

Opened and kept the completed browser-preview target available for human inspection in this AO session with:

`go run ./backend/cmd/ao preview http://127.0.0.1:5174/`

Automated inspection through the AO Browser panel was blocked because this worker was provisioned with an empty browser capability and empty persisted verifier. The capability cannot be safely reconstructed for a running worker, so no direct Browser API fallback or relaunch was attempted.

Separate non-panel visual QA against the same preview build at 1440×1000 reproduced all three branches together: `$1.24`, `5.2M`, and omitted; zero visible `Unavailable` placeholders. Hovering `$1.24` showed the shared token/category and dollar-component breakdown with the provider-pricing explanation.

title: feat(mobile): prompt when a newer native build is on the store
body:
## What

OTA covers JS only — with `policy: fingerprint` a native change mints a new runtime, so a build in the field silently stops being offered updates the moment a newer binary ships. This says so and takes the user to the store.

- Cold start, once, after pairing. Android asks Play In-App Updates, so Play compares the installed `versionCode` itself. iOS has no such API, so it queries the iTunes lookup by bundle id against `CFBundleShortVersionString` from the binary — not the JS bundle's version, which OTA can change independently.
- Two tiers: `inAppUpdatePriority >= 4` hands over to Google's updater (still cancellable, so an insistent nudge rather than a lock); everything else is a dismissible sheet, once a day and three dismissals per store version, a swipe counting as one. The first ask waits until Play has known about the update for three days.
- Settings → About → App Store / Play Store checks on demand. Sideloaded, offline or not yet listed all read as "no update"; dev builds are inert.

## Version floor

`EXPO_PUBLIC_AO_MIN_APP_VERSION` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_AO_LATEST_APP_VERSION`, both unset so they ship inert. They are EAS environment variables, so moving one is an `eas update` rather than a store release, and app JS is not a fingerprint input, so it reaches builds already in the field. This exists because iOS cannot be asked at all while unlisted, and because `inAppUpdatePriority` is immutable once a release has rolled out.

**The floor may only escalate an update the store independently confirmed.** It can raise a confirmed update from dismissible to blocking; it can never invent one. So a mistyped floor cannot strand anyone, iOS stays nudge-only while unlisted, and it starts blocking on its own once listed. That is asserted directly in the tests, not left to statement order in `tierOf`. The soft tier needs no confirmation — the only way to surface anything on iOS during TestFlight — and the copy follows the source, so a floor-driven prompt reads "Version 1.3.0 is available." rather than naming a store page that doesn't exist.

`expo-in-app-updates` is **excluded from Apple autolinking**: Android-only code here, and linking the unused pod would put it in the iOS fingerprint, changing the iOS runtime on every dependency bump. It binds via `requireOptionalNativeModule`, which answers `null` on iOS instead of throwing. Play's flexible flow is never started — it calls `completeUpdate()` the moment the download lands and restarts the app unannounced.

## Activation

No CI, no secret, nothing automatic. The floor does nothing until someone creates the two EAS variables with **plaintext** visibility — secret ones aren't readable outside EAS servers and would silently resolve to empty. It is also only as granular as our version stamping: `version` has read `1.2.1` across several commits, and `autoIncrement` moves the build number instead.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` (538, 43 new); `npx expo export` both platforms
- `npx expo-doctor` 20/21 — measured on the base commit too, where it is also 20/21 with the same three packages, so the failure is `main`'s and not this branch's
- `npx expo prebuild --clean` then real native builds on both platforms
- `runtimeversion:resolve` twice per platform, stable. iOS unchanged from base (`e259e922…`) — the autolinking exclusion holding — while Android moves, as a native module must. The floor moves neither, being pure JS
- Lockfile is `main`'s plus one dependency, **zero re-resolutions**, verified by diffing every package version
- On device, both platforms: module linked on Android; `checkStore()` fails open silently on a Play-less emulator; iOS launches with the pod excluded; sheet in light and dark; snooze written, honoured and reset when the version moves. With a floor set, both read "Version 9.9.9 is available." — the value inlined, the store confirming nothing
- Not exercised: the real Play update flow (needs internal app sharing), iOS against a real listing (we have none — the lookup was tested against the live iTunes API with a published bundle id), the stalled-update resume path, and a real `eas update` carrying a floor

title: agy (Antigravity) AuthStatus() is hardcoded to Unknown, never reflects real login state
body:
## Bug

`AuthStatus()` for the Agy (Antigravity) adapter always returns `Unknown` once the binary resolves, regardless of whether the user is actually authenticated. This is a real, live-verified gap distinct from the model-catalog work in [#3385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3385)/[PR #3386](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3386) (merged) and [PR #3960](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3960) (open, fixes an Agy model-discovery pipe-drain bug) — those cover model discovery, not auth detection.

**Source:** live reproduction on a user's machine via Claude Code session | **Analyzed against:** `main` @ current HEAD (fetched directly, confirmed unchanged from the fork checkout) | **Reported by:** @Hendrixx-RE
**Confidence:** High

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/agy/auth.go`:

```go
func (p *Plugin) AuthStatus(ctx context.Context) (ports.AgentAuthStatus, error) {
	if _, err := p.ResolveBinary(ctx); err != nil {
		return ports.AgentAuthStatusUnknown, err
	}
	// Antigravity authenticates through its OS keyring and browser sign-in. The
	// official CLI does not expose a documented non-interactive credential file
	// or status command, so local auth cannot safely be inferred here.
	return ports.AgentAuthStatusUnknown, nil
}
```

The comment's premise is out of date: the real `agy` CLI (confirmed real binary, `agy --version` → `1.1.22`) has a documented `models` subcommand that already IS used for model discovery elsewhere in the codebase (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go`: `"agy": {args: []string{"models"}, parser: parseIDLines}`). Running it directly:

```
$ agy models
Fetching available models...
gemini-3.7-flash-high	Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)
...
claude-opus-4-6-thinking	Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)
```

succeeds non-interactively with no login prompt when the user is authenticated (it fetches live data from a remote service). A successful `agy models` call (which AO already runs for the model catalog) is a usable, already-computed signal of auth state — but `AuthStatus()` doesn't consult it, or any other signal, and unconditionally reports `Unknown`.

## Impact

Every Agy/Antigravity user sees an uninformative "unknown" auth indicator in AO's UI regardless of actual login state, with no way to distinguish "not logged in, spawn will fail" from "logged in and ready." This surfaced in the wild as "AO can't detect my Antigravity auth."

## Suggested Fix

`AuthStatus()` could reuse the model-catalog discovery call (or a cheap equivalent) as a proxy signal: a successful `agy models` call implies authenticated; a failure that looks like an auth/login prompt implies not authenticated. Since the model catalog fetch (`modelcatalog` package) already runs this exact command and caches results, `AuthStatus()` may be able to piggyback on that cache instead of shelling out separately, avoiding duplicate CLI invocations.

## Related

- [#3385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3385) — adapter-aware model selection RFC, merged via [PR #3386](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3386); covers model discovery for Agy, not auth.
- [PR #3960](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3960) — open, fixes an Agy-specific model-discovery pipe-drain timeout bug; same subsystem, different bug.
- [#4031](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4031) — same class of problem for a different adapter ("bug(kimi): OAuth-managed auth is reported unknown or unauthorized").

title: fix(agy): report real auth status instead of always Unknown
body:
Fixes #4639

## Summary

Antigravity's `agy` adapter has no documented status/whoami command, so `AuthStatus()` was hardcoded to always return `Unknown` regardless of actual login state. `agy models` already fetches its catalog from a remote service and only succeeds when the CLI is authenticated — and AO already runs that exact command elsewhere for the model picker (`modelcatalog.Discover`, wired up in `commandSpecs["agy"]` per #3385/PR #3386).

This reuses that same discovery call as a proxy signal:
- success → `Authorized`
- failure → stays `Unknown` (not `Unauthorized` — a failed run could mean "not logged in", "offline", or a transient CLI hiccup, and there's no documented way to tell those apart without guessing at error text, so this only ever turns a `Unknown` into a `Authorized` when it can prove it, never invents a false negative)

## Verification

Reproduced live against the real `agy` CLI (v1.1.22): `agy models` succeeds non-interactively with no login prompt when authenticated, returning a tab-separated `<id>\t<label>` list. Confirmed the fix reports `Authorized` in that case via a table-driven test with an injected `discoverModels` seam (no real subprocess/network call in the test itself, per repo test-hygiene conventions).

The existing test's original intent — unrelated `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (Google ADC) must never be mistaken for Antigravity auth — is preserved as its own subtest.

## Test plan

```
go build ./...
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/... -v
go test ./...
go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/...
gofmt -l internal/adapters/agent/agy/auth.go internal/adapters/agent/agy/agy_test.go
```
All pass; full backend suite green.

## Related

- #4639 — the bug this fixes
- #3385 / PR #3386 — merged model-catalog discovery work that already exercises `agy models`, reused here
- PR #3960 — open, separate fix for a model-discovery pipe-drain timeout bug in the same subsystem; unrelated to this auth-status change

## What

Fixes GitLab issue intake: nested group repo paths are now preserved, and the intake observer uses the multi-tracker (GitHub + GitLab) instead of a GitHub-only adapter. Also restores the `gh auth token` CLI fallback for the GitHub tracker that was accidentally dropped during the wiring refactor.

## Why

Two issues prevented GitLab issue intake from working:

1. **Nested group paths truncated** — `cleanRepoPath` took only the last two path segments (same as GitHub), dropping the full namespace for nested groups like `group/subgroup/repo`. GitLab API lookups failed with 404.

2. **Intake observer hardcoded to GitHub** — `startTrackerIntake` wired a `SingleTrackerResolver` with a GitHub-only lazy adapter. Projects with `provider: "gitlab"` always failed with "no adapter for provider gitlab" and entered an endless failure-backoff loop.

## How

- `cleanRepoPath` now takes a `provider` argument. For GitLab it preserves the full namespace path; for GitHub it keeps the last-two-segment behavior.
- `startTrackerIntake` now accepts a `ports.Tracker` and is wired with `newMultiTracker` (GitHub + GitLab), matching the session service's existing pattern. The `SingleTrackerResolver` uses an empty `Provider` so the multi-tracker dispatches by each project's configured provider.
- The GitHub tracker token source restores the full fallback chain (`AO_GITHUB_TOKEN` → `GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gh auth token` CLI with 5-min cache), mirroring the GitLab tracker's `DefaultTokenSource` (env → `glab` CLI).

## Testing

- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go test ./internal/daemon/...` passes
- [x] `go test ./internal/observe/trackerintake/...` passes
- [x] Manual verification: daemon with GitLab intake config successfully polls GitLab API, finds assigned issues, and spawns worker sessions

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)
