title: bug(chat): Codex chat controllers can stop together and falsely exit active sessions
body:
## Bug

Multiple live `codex` **chat-mode** sessions were marked `exited` together after their chat controllers emitted `controller.state = stopped`, including the session created from the prompt `Fix the following: 1 ...`. In the UI this looks like the chat session or chat UI suddenly exiting, but the backend evidence shows a shared controller-stop event rather than a renderer-only disappearance.

**Source:** local AO desktop session on this machine (reporter: local user `chauhan`, no public chat URL)
**Date observed:** 2026-08-29
**Installed desktop:** `0.12.10-nightly.202608290454`
**Bundled daemon:** `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao` (`ao version` reports `dev`)
**Analyzed against current main:** `c26f5f1aa14399017e3de54f0522cd18b79e6f9f`
**OS / shell / Go:** macOS 15.6 arm64 (`Darwin 24.6.0`), `/bin/zsh`, `go1.26.3`
**Daemon under test:** healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001`, run-file owner `app`, appRunId `apprun-f36fa767-3a50-4806-a1cd-b02c3e606d7c`
**Confidence:** Medium
**Priority:** P1 — active/idle chat workers can all become unusable at once, and at least one in-flight turn is failed.

## What happened

At `2026-08-29 17:25:23Z` to `17:25:24Z`, seven Codex chat sessions emitted `controller.state = stopped` within ~600ms and were then persisted as `activity = exited` / `is_terminated = false`.

Affected sessions observed in the same cluster:

- `agent-orchestrator-154`
- `silentreadingcommunity-1`
- `agent-orchestrator-163`
- `saturday-reads-api-6`
- `agent-orchestrator-153`
- `agent-orchestrator-156`
- `agent-orchestrator-149`

For the user-reported session:

- session id: `agent-orchestrator-163`
- display name: `Fix the following: 1`
- harness: `codex`
- mode: `chat`
- no `runtime_handle_id`
- no `native_transcript_path`
- latest user prompt before failure: `if auto inject review comments is enabled comments are not getting injected why`

The last turn on `agent-orchestrator-163` failed as:

- requested: `2026-08-29 17:24:57.164021Z`
- started: `2026-08-29 17:24:57.181099Z`
- completed/failed: `2026-08-29 17:25:24.114526Z`
- state: `failed`
- error: `controller ended before the turn completed`

## Exact evidence

### Durable session timeline

`agent-orchestrator-163` stayed live in chat mode and accepted user prompts after earlier work completed:

- `2026-08-29 17:16:05.415207Z`: session activity written to `idle`
- `2026-08-29 17:18:02.591334Z`: user prompt accepted while still `idle`
- `2026-08-29 17:20:49.960440Z`: another user prompt accepted while still `idle`
- `2026-08-29 17:24:57.164021Z`: latest user prompt accepted
- `2026-08-29 17:25:24.113570Z`: provider event `controller.state = stopped`
- `2026-08-29 17:25:24.118736Z`: session persisted as `activity = exited`, `is_terminated = false`

### Provider-event cluster

The following `conversation_provider_events` rows all arrived during the same failure window:

- `agent-orchestrator-154` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:23.756869Z`
- `silentreadingcommunity-1` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.044436Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-163` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.113570Z`
- `saturday-reads-api-6` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.174660Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-153` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.238469Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-156` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.298882Z`
- `agent-orchestrator-149` -> `controller.state=stopped` at `2026-08-29 17:25:24.360226Z`

This does not look like a single session-specific corruption. It looks like a shared stop/shutdown condition across Codex chat controllers.

## Relevant code path

This failure mode maps directly to the current backend behavior:

1. `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go` emits `ChatEventControllerState{ControllerState: stopped}` whenever the app-server connection ends, explicitly noting that the connection ended rather than leaving the stream quiet.
2. `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` treats that event as authoritative, runs `CleanupOwnedControllerWork(...)`, then reports session activity as `domain.ActivityExited` with event `chat.controller.stopped`.
3. `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go` treats `chat.controller.stopped` as a turn/session boundary event.
4. The renderer then shows the controller/session as stopped or exited. For the failed in-flight turn, `conversation_turns.error_message` becomes `controller ended before the turn completed`.

The code is behaving consistently with the emitted provider event. The bug is that multiple live Codex chat controllers appear to stop together unexpectedly.

## Why this seems distinct from existing tmux/session-exit bugs

This is not the same failure as [#4458](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4458):

- the affected sessions here are all `chat` mode, not TUI
- `agent-orchestrator-163` had no `runtime_handle_id`
- there is no interface-transition row for `agent-orchestrator-163`
- the stop comes from the Codex app-server chat stream closing, not from tmux attach/liveness routing

## Hypothesis

The exact external trigger was not proven during triage, but the evidence suggests one of these shared controller-stop paths:

- a Codex app-server / chat-driver process lifecycle event that propagates across several conversations
- a daemon/app ownership transition or supervision event that closes several chat controller connections together
- a bad restore/reconcile path for existing live chat sessions after AO is launched against real `~/.ao` data

One nearby signal from the same period: another session logged a reconcile failure with `resume chat: chat conversation resume failed: thread/resume: app-server error -32600: no rollout found for thread id ...`, which suggests chat restore/controller ownership around this window may be unstable.

## Reproduction notes

This was observed on a real-data desktop run rather than a reduced e2e reproduction. The sequence on this machine was:

1. Use AO desktop with real `~/.ao` data on macOS.
2. Have several non-terminated Codex chat sessions present.
3. Continue working in `agent-orchestrator-163` and send another prompt.
4. Observe several chat sessions flip to `exited` nearly simultaneously.
5. The in-flight prompt on `agent-orchestrator-163` fails with `controller ended before the turn completed`.

## Expected behavior

- An idle or active Codex chat session should not transition to `exited` unless its own controller actually dies for a local reason the user can act on.
- A shared AO desktop action or daemon reconciliation pass should not silently stop several independent Codex chat controllers.
- If AO detects a recoverable ownership/reconnect condition, the session should surface that explicitly and preserve resumability rather than collapsing multiple sessions into `exited`.

## Suggested investigation

- Trace why multiple `codexappserver` conversation streams closed together in the same second.
- Audit any path where app-owned daemon replacement, supervisor disconnect, or chat restore cleanup can call stop/close on more than one controller.
- Add coverage for multi-session chat survival when a second desktop/dev instance interacts with real data or when the daemon reconciles previously live chat controllers.
- Add a regression test for the in-flight-turn case: one session turn should not fail as `controller ended before the turn completed` because unrelated chat controllers were stopped in a batch.

## Related

- [#4458](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4458) — session false-exit and duplicate-controller issues in TUI/tmux land; related symptom, different subsystem.

title: Expose per-role (worker vs orchestrator) permission mode in Project Settings, not just one shared value
body:
## Problem

Project Settings has exactly one shared "Permission Mode" control (`PermissionModeSelect` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`), which writes only into the project's top-level `agentConfig.permissions`. It's positioned next to the orchestrator agent picker, which reads as "the orchestrator's setting" but actually applies identically to every worker too. There's no way to give workers a different (looser or stricter) permission level than the orchestrator through the UI.

**This is a UI gap, not a backend one — confirmed by code trace, not assumption:**
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go`'s `effectiveAgentConfig(kind, cfg)` already merges the shared `cfg.AgentConfig` with a role-specific override (`cfg.Worker.AgentConfig` / `cfg.Orchestrator.AgentConfig`), and `Permissions` is one of the fields that overrides cleanly when set.
- `domain.RoleOverride.AgentConfig.Permissions` is validated today (`projectconfig_test.go`: `{"bad role agent config", ProjectConfig{Worker: RoleOverride{AgentConfig: AgentConfig{Permissions: "nope"}}}, true}`), and `ProjectConfig.Worker`/`.Orchestrator` marshal directly via `json:"worker,omitempty"`/`json:"orchestrator,omitempty"` — no separate DTO stripping the field.
- The frontend's own `buildRoleAgentConfig` helper (used for `config.worker.agentConfig` / `config.orchestrator.agentConfig`) only ever sets `model`/`mode` — never `permissions` — so the working backend field is simply never populated from the settings form.

**Confidence: High** that this is purely a frontend gap; a small addition to `ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` (a second `PermissionModeSelect` per role, wired through `buildRoleAgentConfig`) should be sufficient with no backend/DTO changes needed.

## Real-world motivating case

Hit this directly: a project with the orchestrator on Claude Code and the worker on Codex, one shared "Accept edits" permission level. Assumed both roles had equivalent effective permission — they didn't, because the same domain-level policy maps to very different actual CLI behavior per harness (`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go`):

```go
// Claude Code
case PermissionAcceptEdits: return []string{"--permission-mode", "acceptEdits"}
// Codex
case PermissionAcceptEdits: return []string{"--ask-for-approval", "on-request"}
```

Claude Code's `acceptEdits` is fairly permissive; Codex's `on-request` means Codex decides for itself when to prompt, so it kept asking. This makes the missing per-role control worse than it might look in the abstract: mixing harnesses across orchestrator/worker (an expected, supported AO configuration) turns one shared slider into genuinely inconsistent real behavior between roles, with no way to compensate short of hand-editing the project config via a raw API call.

## Ask

Add a second permission-mode control for the worker role (or make the existing one explicitly role-aware), writing into `worker.agentConfig.permissions` the same way `buildRoleAgentConfig` already does for `model`/`mode`.

Filing this to gauge interest — curious whether other users have hit the same "workers won't stop asking for permission even though I set it to max" confusion, since the root cause (one shared control, harness-dependent real behavior) isn't obvious from the UI alone.

## Related

- [#2195](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2195) — broader "give workers a full per-role environment profile" RFC (MCP, plugins, system prompt), whose own side-note already flags that per-role `model`/`permissions` are "wired in the Go domain and API schema but only `agent` is exposed per-role in the settings UI." That issue explicitly defers UI work to a follow-up and is additionally gated on resolving #2844's naked-by-default MCP/plugins rollout question. This issue is scoped to just the permissions-UI slice, which has no such rollout blocker and looks independently shippable.
- [#3385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3385) / [PR #3386](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3386) — the same "wired per-role in the backend, not exposed in the UI" pattern, already solved for model selection specifically. This issue asks for the same treatment for permissions.

title: feat(desktop): reveal the collapsed sidebar after a pointer dwell at the left edge
body:
## Feature request

When the desktop sidebar is fully collapsed off-canvas, let the user reveal it by holding the pointer at the far-left screen edge for a deliberate 250 ms dwell. The visible top-left titlebar sidebar button, identified by its Expand tooltip, should open the temporary preview immediately on pointer hover.

The current sidebar has a narrow `SidebarRail` that opens the panel on click. The shell also keeps the sidebar open from the keyboard shortcut. Under Browser workspace pressure, the app can use a separate icon rail, but that is a different state and should keep its current behavior.

This request uses two intentional pointer paths. The far-left edge needs a 250 ms dwell. The visible top-left titlebar button opens on hover without waiting for that dwell.

## Proposed behavior

- Add a narrow activation zone at the far-left screen edge.
- Start a 250 ms dwell timer only when the pointer enters the edge activation zone.
- Cancel the edge timer when the pointer leaves the zone before 250 ms. A quick pass along the edge should not open the sidebar.
- When the pointer hovers the visible top-left titlebar sidebar button, the temporary overlay should open immediately. This button is the control that shows the Expand tooltip.
- After either trigger opens the preview, show the sidebar as a temporary overlay. The overlay must not change the saved sidebar preference, reclaim layout width, or move the center panel.
- Reveal and dismiss the temporary overlay with a short, subtle, smooth slide/fade. Keep the 250 ms edge dwell, immediate titlebar-button hover, and 55 ms dismissal delay unchanged.
- Keep the temporary overlay open while the pointer is over its trigger or the sidebar. Moving from the titlebar button into the overlay must keep it open.
- Keep pointer transfer from either trigger into the overlay independent of animation progress and animated hit bounds. It must not depend on a moving target, so the old race from #3372 cannot recur.
- Leaving both the active trigger area and the overlay should start a 55 ms dismissal delay. Re-entering either area before the overlay closes should cancel the delay.
- Clicking the visible top-left titlebar button or the sidebar expand control while the overlay is open must promote it to the normal pinned-open state. The keyboard shortcut must continue to open the pinned state directly.
- Once pinned open, the sidebar must stay open until the user explicitly collapses it. Pointer movement alone must not collapse it.
- Preserve the existing click, keyboard, resize, and compact icon-rail behavior.

## Accessibility and accidental-trigger requirements

Pointer preview is an optional convenience, not the only way to reach the sidebar.

- Keep the visible titlebar button, its accessible Expand name, and the keyboard shortcut available.
- Do not move keyboard focus into the temporary overlay or add duplicate focus stops for hidden controls.
- Expose the expand/collapse state and accessible names through the existing controls. Screen-reader and keyboard users must have an equivalent path.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences.
- Do not trigger the edge preview from a pointer-down, drag, text selection, or a brief crossing of the edge. The titlebar button's immediate hover preview is intentional, but its click path must remain available.
- Keep the edge activation zone narrow enough that ordinary pointer travel along the left edge does not repeatedly open the sidebar.
- Account for platform chrome, including macOS traffic-light clearance and the Windows titlebar, so the activation targets do not interfere with window controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In the fully collapsed off-canvas state, holding the pointer in the far-left edge activation zone for 250 ms opens a temporary sidebar overlay.
- [ ] In the fully collapsed off-canvas state, hovering the visible top-left titlebar sidebar button, the one with the Expand tooltip, opens the temporary overlay immediately without a dwell.
- [ ] A quick pointer pass across the far-left edge does not open the overlay. The titlebar button remains an intentional immediate-hover trigger.
- [ ] Moving the pointer from the titlebar button into the overlay keeps the preview open.
- [ ] Leaving both the active trigger area and the overlay starts a 55 ms delayed dismissal. Re-entering either area before dismissal keeps the overlay open.
- [ ] Clicking the visible top-left titlebar button or the sidebar expand control while the preview is visible pins the sidebar open. The keyboard shortcut still pins it open.
- [ ] The temporary overlay does not persist the open preference, change the layout gap, or resize the center panel.
- [ ] A pinned-open sidebar remains open until an explicit collapse action.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation, screen-reader naming/state, focus order, and reduced-motion behavior remain correct in both collapsed and temporary-overlay states.
- [ ] The temporary overlay reveals and dismisses with a short, subtle, smooth slide/fade. The 250 ms edge dwell, immediate titlebar-button hover, and 55 ms leave dismissal remain unchanged.
- [ ] With reduced motion enabled, the overlay skips movement or uses a reduced transition while preserving the same trigger, keep-open, and dismissal behavior.
- [ ] Pointer transfer from either trigger into the overlay remains reliable during the transition and does not depend on animated bounds, avoiding the old race in #3372.
- [ ] Pointer drag and text-selection gestures do not cause accidental edge activation.
- [ ] Automated coverage exercises the 250 ms edge dwell, immediate titlebar-button hover, edge dwell cancellation, temporary overlay dismissal, click-to-pin, and the existing keyboard paths on the supported desktop platforms.

## Related history

- [Issue #3372](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3372) documented the old immediate toggle-hover preview race, where the preview closed before the pointer could reach it. This request intentionally uses immediate hover only for the visible top-left titlebar button, while the far-left edge requires a 250 ms dwell. Both paths must keep the preview open as the pointer enters the sidebar and must use delayed dismissal after leaving.
- [PR #4263](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4263) removed the old collapsed-sidebar hover opening from the current frontend. This request brings back immediate preview only for the explicit visible top-left titlebar button and keeps the deliberate 250 ms dwell for the far-left edge.
- [PR #3509](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3509) covered the earlier keep-open zone and click-to-pin interaction.

Inspected against commit `dc1ea86e841e8a879b62f44b67682cce26c26767`.

title: tmux runtime: Restart always fails when base-index or pane-base-index is not 0
body:
### Summary

`respawn-pane` and the pane-pid probe hardcode the tmux target `<session>:0.0`, and nothing in the runtime reads tmux's `base-index` / `pane-base-index`. Both default to `0`, but setting them to `1` is one of the most common tmux customisations there is — so on those machines the session's only pane is `<session>:1.1` and every `<session>:0.0` target misses.

The user-visible effect is that **`Runtime.Restart` always fails**, which is the path session restore uses. It also fails `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` and `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane`, so the failure looks like flaky integration tests rather than a runtime bug.

Two sites, both in `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/commands.go`:

```go
// :24  respawnPaneArgs
"respawn-pane", "-k",
"-t", id + ":0.0",

// :61  panePIDArgs
return []string{"display-message", "-p", "-t", id + ":0.0", "#{pane_pid}"}
```

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained, no AO required — it isolates its own server and config:

```sh
CONF=$(mktemp); printf 'set -g base-index 1\nset -gw pane-base-index 1\n' > "$CONF"
export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
tmux -f "$CONF" new-session -d -s aorepro 'sleep 300'

tmux list-panes -a -F '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}'   # aorepro:1.1

tmux respawn-pane -k -t aorepro:0.0 -c /tmp sh -c 'sleep 300'   # what AO does today
tmux respawn-pane -k -t aorepro   -c /tmp sh -c 'sleep 300'     # proposed
```

Against AO itself, with `base-index 1` / `pane-base-index 1` in your tmux config:

```
cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/ -run TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell
```

### Expected behavior

`Restart` respawns the session's only pane regardless of the user's `base-index` / `pane-base-index`.

### Actual behavior

```
tmux runtime: restart session <id>: exit status 1: can't find pane: 0
```

The exact message depends on which option is non-zero, because tmux resolves the window before the pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c, single AO-style session, `respawn-pane -k -t <s>:0.0`:

| `base-index` | `pane-base-index` | real target | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | `c:0.0` | ok |
| 0 | 1 | `c:0.1` | `can't find pane: 0` |
| 1 | 0 | `c:1.0` | `can't find window: 0` |
| 1 | 1 | `c:1.1` | `can't find window: 0` |

One wrinkle worth flagging: **`panePIDArgs` does not fail.** `display-message -p -t <s>:0.0 '#{pane_pid}'` silently falls back rather than erroring, and in every single-pane case above it returned the correct pid. So that call site is latent today rather than broken — but it is the same unchecked assumption, and it would stop being harmless the moment a session has more than one pane.

### AO version

`ao version dev`, built from `main` at `759595a9`.

### Environment

- Arch Linux, tmux 3.7c
- `base-index 1`, `pane-base-index 1` set globally in `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`
- Reproduced against `main` with no local patches; the standalone snippet above reproduces with no AO at all

### Logs / extra context

**Suggested fix — target the session name alone.** `respawn-pane -t <session>` and `display-message -t <session>` resolve to the session's current window and active pane, which for AO is the only pane (`respawnPaneArgs`' own comment says "the session's only pane", and there is no `new-window` or `split-window` anywhere in the runtime). Verified working on the `base-index 1` / `pane-base-index 1` server above.

That also matches what this file already does elsewhere — `setStatusOffArgs`, `setMouseOnArgs` and `setWindowSizeLargestArgs` all pass bare `id`, with a comment explaining the targeting choice. So the fix makes the file more internally consistent, not less.

If you would rather keep an explicit pane target, the index-safe form is to resolve it once (`display-message -p -t <session> '#{pane_id}'` gives a stable `%N` that is immune to both options) and target that. I have a preference for the simpler one but no strong opinion — happy to send whichever you prefer as a PR, with the two integration tests as the regression proof.

I did not fold this into #4654 or #4655 (OneDev provider work) since it is unrelated to those.

title: bug(reviewer): Claude restore double-hashes session identity
body:
## Bug

A restored Claude Code reviewer can fail immediately with:

> No conversation found with session ID: 03dc146e-e3b6-5d88-a3a3-15fe9f6354bc

The reviewer terminal remains present with no Claude child process, while the associated `review_run` remains durably `running`.

**Source:** AO orchestrator chat report on 2026-08-30  
**Reported by:** AO user (live local observation)  
**Analyzed against:** `d28e46dea577e45f9c995a59f3dfbcfcfe72bb59` (`upstream/main`)  
**AO binary:** packaged rewrite binary, `dev`, verified ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64; Claude Code 2.1.251  
**Confidence:** High

![Reviewer terminal showing No conversation found](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-reviewer-double-hash-20260830/.issue-assets/claude-reviewer-double-hash/reviewer-no-conversation.png)

## Reproduction

1. Start a Claude Code reviewer for a worker session.
2. Allow it to create a real Claude conversation/transcript.
3. Restart or otherwise restore the reviewer terminal.
4. Open the Reviewer's terminal tab.
5. Observe `claude --resume <persisted-id>` fail with `No conversation found`.

Observed live instance:

- AO worker: `agent-orchestrator-149` (`pr author avatar`)
- reviewer AO ID: `review-agent-orchestrator-149`
- persisted `review.agent_session_id`: `03dc146e-e3b6-5d88-a3a3-15fe9f6354bc`
- actual Claude transcript ID: `a04d0453-97e8-51ee-84bf-ebe1d2a4a90b`
- persisted-ID transcript: absent
- actual transcript: present and non-empty
- restored pty host invokes `claude --resume 03dc146e-...`, but has no Claude child after the failure
- newest review run `201113cb-b4cf-437a-bb19-e5b0de73a662` has remained `running` since 2026-08-27

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/claudecode/claudecode.go:76-96` first maps the reviewer AO ID to a Claude UUID:

```go
agentSessionID := workeragent.SessionUUID(inv.ReviewerID)
```

It persists that value as `ReviewCommandSpec.AgentSessionID`, but also passes the already-derived UUID as `LaunchConfig.SessionID`.

`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go:211-221` treats `SessionID` as an AO identity and derives a Claude UUID again:

```go
cmd = append(cmd, "--session-id", ClaudeSessionID(cfg.SessionID))
```

Consequently:

- AO persists `UUIDv5(reviewerID)`
- Claude launches with `UUIDv5(UUIDv5(reviewerID))`
- restore uses the persisted single-hashed ID
- Claude only has a transcript for the double-hashed ID

This mismatch was introduced by commit `d15fd8277c1b63a1a7ebdb55735b9ed6091cf118` in [PR #3484](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3484).

The recent daemon/reconciliation incident triggered a restore and exposed the bug, but did not create the deterministic ID mismatch.

## Fix

1. Make reviewer launch use the exact native ID AO persists. Prefer passing the derived UUID through `LaunchConfig.NativeSessionID`, or pass the raw reviewer AO ID through `SessionID`; do not hash an already-derived native ID.
2. Add an integration-level adapter test asserting the actual emitted `--session-id` equals `ReviewCommandSpec.AgentSessionID`. Existing capture-agent tests only observe the intermediate launch config and therefore missed the second transformation.
3. Preserve existing reviewer conversations created by buggy versions: when the persisted single-hashed transcript is absent but the legacy double-hashed transcript exists, resume the legacy identity and safely migrate/persist it.
4. Ensure a failed reviewer restore transitions its running review run to a failed/retryable state instead of leaving it permanently `running`.

## Impact

- Restored Claude Code reviewers can lose access to their real conversation.
- Automatic review work is blocked until the reviewer is recreated or repaired.
- Review runs may appear active indefinitely despite no reviewer process.
- Every Claude reviewer launched through this path since the regression is potentially affected on restore.

## Related

- [PR #3484](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3484): introduced persisted reviewer-native identity during lifecycle restoration.
- [Issue #2702](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2702): broader runtime restoration/zombie-session failure mode; related subsystem but not this double-hash defect.

title: fix(reviewer): resume Claude after reviewer relaunch
body:
Fixes #4658

## Summary
- pass the persisted Claude reviewer UUID through the explicit native-session field so first launch emits the exact deterministic ID AO owns instead of hashing it twice
- detect and resume both current transcripts and the legacy double-derived transcript, then persist any repaired identity
- when a reviewer pane/process has exited but its durable native ID remains, route the next review launch through `--resume` instead of colliding on `--session-id`
- preserve Claude's read-only tool policy and system prompt on resume, and deliver the new review task as the resume-time user turn
- surface transcript/restore failures without silently fresh-launching; the existing liveness gate continues to notify a genuinely live reviewer rather than starting a duplicate
- fall back to a fresh idle reviewer when native history is unavailable and mark interrupted running review runs failed so they can be retried

## Root cause
Commit `d15fd8277c1b63a1a7ebdb55735b9ed6091cf118` (`fix: align reviewer terminal lifecycle`, PR #3484) introduced deterministic reviewer identity persistence and native restore support, but split ownership incorrectly in two related ways:

1. `ReviewCommand` derived a Claude UUID, persisted it, then passed it as an AO `SessionID`; the worker command builder derived it again. AO therefore persisted the single-derived ID while Claude owned the double-derived transcript, producing `No conversation found` on restore.
2. Ordinary new-review reruns still called `Launcher.Spawn`, whose path always built a fresh command. After cancellation/process exit, `review.agent_session_id` survived while the pane did not, so Claude received `--session-id <existing transcript>` and failed with `Session ID ... is already in use`.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/... ./internal/review/...`
- `go build ./...`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_TMUX_BINARY -u AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_RUN_FILE go test ./...`
- isolated-cache `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs` (`0 issues`)

## Risk
Low and scoped to reviewer identity/restore selection. A normal review launch attempts native resume only when a durable reviewer-native ID exists; first launch remains fresh and deterministic. Claude only resumes after finding a non-empty transcript. Probe/restore errors are surfaced, and a live reviewer pane is still handled by the existing notify path.

title: Chat UI shows stale incomplete plan count after worker turn actually completed
body:
## Summary
A completed Chat turn can keep an earlier non-terminal plan snapshot, so the chat UI shows an incomplete plan badge such as `0/3` or `0/4` even though the worker finished all work and posted the final completion message.

## Environment
- Date observed: 2026-08-30
- App build: `ao version` => `dev`
- Daemon/API: local desktop AO on `127.0.0.1:3001`
- Local checkout analyzed: `c26f5f1aa14399017e3de54f0522cd18b79e6f9f`
- Note: local `main` was behind `origin/main` by 2 commits at triage time

## Reported session
- Session: `agent-orchestrator-154`
- Display name: `review agent hooks`
- Mode: `chat`
- Conversation ID: `9c89bcc4-e796-4f4b-b6d3-d50a7f4d47fc`
- Affected turn ID: `0634673f-d5d8-4af6-aeef-fd940fe320b5`
- Provider turn ID: `01a04673-66d8-7a11-8a05-dddefb5f0d72`

## What happened
The final assistant message for the affected turn says the work is done and pushed:
- PR rebased onto `main`
- conflict resolved
- targeted verification run completed
- branch pushed

But the durable turn plan served to the UI still shows the initial plan state:
- step 1: `in_progress`
- steps 2-4: `pending`

Because the frontend plan header counts only steps whose status is `completed`, the UI displays an incomplete badge for a turn that is already `completed`.

## Evidence
### Durable turn record
`conversation_turns.plan_json` for turn `0634673f-d5d8-4af6-aeef-fd940fe320b5`:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "text": "Fetch `main` and start a rebase of PR #4551 branch onto the latest base branch",
      "status": "in_progress"
    },
    {
      "text": "Inspect each conflict, resolve it in place, and keep the reviewer-hook behavior intact",
      "status": "pending"
    },
    {
      "text": "Run targeted verification for the rebased review-related backend/frontend paths",
      "status": "pending"
    },
    {
      "text": "Push the rebased branch and report the result",
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Final assistant message on the same turn
Stored conversation message sequence `461` on the same turn:

- `PR #4551 is rebased onto the current main and pushed.`
- conflict resolved by renumbering migration to `0117_review_activity_state.sql`
- targeted backend verification run completed
- pushed branch head `40e55caaa`

### Raw provider-event history
For provider turn `01a04673-66d8-7a11-8a05-dddefb5f0d72`, the durable provider event log contains:
- one `turn.plan` at `2026-08-28 03:39:31Z`
- many later `message.completed` events
- `turn.completed` at `2026-08-28 03:42:10Z`
- no later `turn.plan` with completed steps

Method counts for that provider turn include:
- `turn.plan`: `1`
- `turn.completed`: `2` (including one history replay)
- `message.completed`: `13`

So the UI is not inventing stale state; it is rendering the plan AO persisted and served.

## Expected
Once the turn is completed, the plan displayed for that turn should not still read as partially pending if the turn has already produced its final successful completion message.

## Actual
The completed turn still exposes the earlier in-progress plan, so the UI shows an incomplete plan count.

## Likely root cause
This looks like a backend/controller gap rather than a frontend rendering bug.

Relevant code paths:
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnPlan.tsx`
  - counts only `step.status === "completed"`
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`
  - `ChatEventPlanUpdated` overwrites `conversation_turns.plan_json`
  - `ChatEventTurnCompleted` settles only turn state and does not reconcile/finalize the stored plan
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/store/conversation_store.go`
  - `SetTurnPlan` only persists what arrived from `turn.plan`

That means if Codex sends an early plan snapshot but never sends a terminal all-completed plan update before `turn.completed`, AO leaves the stale plan in durable state forever.

## Why this seems like the missing test case
Existing plan tests cover the happy path where the provider emits a second `plan_updated` event with all steps completed. They do not appear to cover:
- a turn that completes successfully
- final assistant text is written
- no later terminal `turn.plan` arrives
- stale non-terminal plan remains on the completed turn

## Suggested direction
Either:
1. finalize remaining plan steps when a turn completes successfully and the current stored plan is still non-terminal, or
2. explicitly clear/hide non-terminal plan state for completed turns when no terminal plan revision arrived, or
3. if the provider contract guarantees a terminal plan update, add detection/logging/tests around missing final `turn.plan` events so AO can repair or at least diagnose it.

## Repro confidence
High for the stale-state condition in durable data.

I verified locally that:
- the frontend is reading the snapshot correctly
- the snapshot contains the stale plan
- the turn itself is marked completed
- the provider event log for the same turn has only one `turn.plan` and no terminal plan update

title: [Cloud][P0] Packaged renderer CSP blocks every cloud terminal WebSocket
body:
## What

In any **packaged/built** desktop app, a cloud session's terminal never connects: the renderer's Content-Security-Policy refuses the direct `wss://` connection to the control plane, so the terminal shows "Connecting…" forever. Dev-mode (`npm run dev`) is unaffected, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Root cause

`frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts` injects a CSP meta tag with `apply: "build"` (built renderers only). Its `connect-src` is:

```
connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:* ws://127.0.0.1:* <posthog>
```

The cloud terminal deliberately dials `wss://<control-plane>/api/cloud/v1/terminal?ticket=…` **directly from the renderer** (single-use ticket auth; the WorkOS token stays in the Electron main process — see `frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts`). That origin is not in `connect-src`, so Chromium refuses the socket before any packet leaves the machine. Every other CP call rides the main-process proxy and is unaffected — including terminal-**ticket** minting, which keeps succeeding while the attach never happens.

## Evidence (staging, 2026-08-30)

- A dev on a packaged build: 4 sessions (claude-code **and** codex), **2,600+ tickets minted, 0 consumed** (`ao_access_tickets`), zero `GET /api/cloud/v1/terminal` requests reaching the CP.
- Same app via `npm run dev` on another machine: 18 tickets minted, **18 consumed**, terminal works.
- In the packaged app's DevTools, `new WebSocket("wss://echo.websocket.org")` fails instantly with no Network-tab row (classic CSP refusal); the same snippet succeeds in a dev-mode build.

## Fix

Add the cloud control-plane WebSocket origins to `connect-src` in the built CSP (baked defaults `wss://staging-api.aoagents.dev` / `wss://api.aoagents.dev`, extendable via the existing `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` override at build time). PR incoming.

## Follow-up worth considering

Tunneling the terminal WebSocket through the Electron main process (like every other CP call) would remove the renderer-egress requirement entirely, at the cost of a bigger change to the mux.

title: [Bug][Cloud][P1] Cloud terminal WebSockets are severed every ~60s by the ALB idle timeout
body:
## What

Every healthy cloud terminal WebSocket is cut by the staging ALB after exactly ~60 seconds of frame-level idle. The renderer's mux silently reconnects with a fresh ticket and replays, so the terminal *looks* fine, but every idle terminal cycles disconnect/reattach once a minute — visible as a hiccup on slow links, extra ticket/replay load, and a misleading error in the CP logs.

## Evidence (staging, 2026-08-30)

- `GET /api/cloud/v1/terminal` completions with status 101 and durations of **59998–60002 ms**, one per minute per attached terminal, for an actively used session.
- Matching CP warnings once per minute per terminal: `terminal stream ended unexpectedly | failed to get reader: failed to read frame header: EOF` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/terminal_handlers.go:159`), same `terminal_id` each time.

## Cause

The ALB's default idle timeout is 60s and applies per-connection to WebSockets. Neither side sends WebSocket ping/pong keepalives: `connectTerminal` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/terminal_handlers.go:72`) reads/writes only application frames, and the renderer mux (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts`) writes only on user input. An idle PTY (no output, no input) therefore exchanges zero frames for 60s and gets chopped.

## Fix options

1. Server-side ping every ~20–30s in the terminal WebSocket loop (`websocket.Conn.Ping`) — smallest change, covers all clients including future web/mobile.
2. Additionally or alternatively raise the ALB idle timeout for staging/production (deploy scripts under `cloud/scripts/`).

Option 1 is the right permanent fix; 2 is belt-and-braces.

title: fix(frontend): allow cloud control-plane websockets in the packaged CSP
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4666 — in every **packaged** build, the renderer CSP (`connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:* ws://127.0.0.1:* <posthog>`) refused the cloud terminal's direct `wss://` connection to the control plane, so cloud terminals stayed on "Connecting…" forever. Dev-mode (`npm run dev`) skips the CSP meta (`apply: "build"`), which is why the bug only reproduced on packaged builds.

This adds the cloud control-plane websocket origins to `connect-src`:
- baked defaults `wss://staging-api.aoagents.dev` and `wss://api.aoagents.dev`, matching the control-plane URL defaults;
- a build-time `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` override (http(s) → ws(s) origin) so a custom control plane keeps a working terminal in packaged builds.

Everything else about the CSP is unchanged. The terminal's direct-dial design is intentional (single-use ticket is the socket's authorization; the WorkOS token never reaches the renderer — `lib/cloud-terminal-mux.ts`), so the CSP must allow the origin rather than the socket moving behind the proxy.

## Evidence

Staging, 2026-08-30: a dev on a packaged build minted **2,600+ terminal tickets with 0 consumed** across 4 sessions (claude-code and codex) — zero `GET /api/cloud/v1/terminal` requests ever reached the control plane; `new WebSocket("wss://echo.websocket.org")` failed instantly in the packaged app's console with no Network-tab row (CSP refusal), while the same dev-mode build on another machine redeemed 18/18 tickets and connected fine.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts` — emitted `index.html` CSP now reads `connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:* ws://127.0.0.1:* https://us.i.posthog.com https://us-assets.i.posthog.com wss://staging-api.aoagents.dev wss://api.aoagents.dev`.
- Follow-up issues from the same investigation: #4667 (ALB 60s idle timeout severs terminal websockets — needs server ping/pong), #4668 (attach-failure retry loop mints tickets ~2/s with no surfaced error and keeps sandboxes awake).

## Environment
- Agent Orchestrator desktop **0.12.3** (`dev.agent-orchestrator.desktop`), daemon `dev` on port 3001, macOS 24.6 (Darwin). Reproduced also with Agent Orchestrator desktop **0.12.9** on the same machine.

{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"Claude Code process exited with code 1.
stderr: Error: Session d0d0953b-7716-4603-afa0-05fba7846ad5 is currently running as a background agent (bg).
Use `claude agents` to find and attach to it, or add --fork-session to branch off a copy."}}

title: bug(chat): TUI to Chat switch fails outright for ACP (Claude Code) sessions when native history is unsettled - "snapshot is incomplete and cannot be refreshed"
body:
## Bug

Switching a terminal (TUI) session to the Chat UI fails **immediately** for ACP-backed (Claude Code) sessions with:

> Interface switch failed - switch interface `<session>`: resume chat: native conversation history snapshot is incomplete and cannot be refreshed: chat conversation history is not settled

Unlike #4120 (which waited ~45s and failed with "context deadline exceeded", now fixed), this fails right away with no wait. The API surfaces it as `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED`.

## Mechanism (from code)

On a TUI to Chat switch, the chat controller rebuilds the structured timeline by reading the provider's native conversation history (`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go`, `refreshNativeHistory`) and requires the replay to reach the transition checkpoint:

- If `ReadHistory` errors, or (`required && !checkpoint.reached(events)`), the controller treats the history as unsettled (`ErrChatHistoryUnsettled`) - synthesizing it at `controller.go:542` when `ReadHistory` returned nil but the checkpoint was not reached.
- If the reader implements `ChatHistoryRefresher`, the controller polls/refreshes until it settles or times out.
- If the reader does **not** implement `ChatHistoryRefresher`, it fails immediately at `controller.go:557`: `native conversation history snapshot is incomplete and cannot be refreshed: <unsettled>`.

The ACP chat driver (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/history.go`) implements `ChatHistoryReader` (`ReadHistory`) but **not** `ChatHistoryRefresher` - only `codexappserver` implements `RefreshHistory` (`.../codexappserver/history.go:200`). So for ACP (Claude Code) sessions, any unsettled or checkpoint-incomplete native replay at switch time is a hard, immediate failure with no retry path. Codex sessions do not hit this branch because their reader is refreshable and polls instead.

`backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go:461` maps `ErrChatHistoryUnsettled` to `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` and fails the transition.

## Impact

An ACP (Claude Code) session whose native history is momentarily unsettled, or whose ACP replay does not yet satisfy the switch checkpoint, cannot enter Chat mode at all, and there is no wait/retry for it to settle (the wait path exists only for refreshable readers). The user is stuck in TUI.

## Related (distinct)

- #4120 (closed, fixed): the refreshable/timeout variant - "...context deadline exceeded" after ~45s. Different code path (poll then timeout) and different error string.
- #4123 (closed): settle-wait polled an immutable cached ACP replay for the full 45s before failing. This report is the non-refreshable fast-fail, which may be a side effect of removing ACP from the polling path.
- #4424 (open): unscoped hook checkpoints permanently block TUI-to-Chat recovery - a different blocking cause.

## Suggested direction

Either make the ACP history reader a `ChatHistoryRefresher` so the controller can wait for the replay to settle like Codex, or make the controller degrade gracefully for non-refreshable readers (proceed with the available replay / defer the checkpoint) instead of hard-failing, so a transient unsettled state does not permanently block the switch.

## Source

- Live AO desktop report, 2026-08-30 (session `ao-6`), screenshot of the "Interface switch failed" banner.
- Analyzed against `origin/main` `c13289c1c32afa4acbc2508a4a5402175623cb3e`.
- Confidence: High on the code mechanism (files and lines cited); the specific live trigger (which unsettled turn or checkpoint gap) was not reproduced end to end.

title: fix: keep terminal colors in sync with AO theme
body:
## Summary

Cursor Agent can render its prompt bar with the wrong colors when AO switches between light and dark mode. This PR synchronizes the resolved AO theme with Cursor sessions at startup and while they are running.

## What changed

- Persist the resolved light/dark terminal scheme under AO's data directory.
- Inject `TERM_THEME` and `COLORFGBG` only into Cursor Agent processes.
- Answer Cursor's private color-scheme protocol and OSC 10/11/12 color probes through a dedicated protocol-input path.
- Scope protocol handling to Cursor terminals so shells, Codex, and other TUIs receive no unsolicited control bytes.
- Bound OSC response buffering and avoid duplicate OSC replies.
- Keep terminal theme-hint writes ordered and atomic.
- Prevent theme transitions from flashing terminal/composer chrome.
- Preserve the Cmd+K search query until the palette close animation completes, including reduced-motion environments.

## Root cause

Cursor probes terminal appearance through OSC and private CSI sequences. The renderer previously allowed those replies to be lost or treated like ordinary input, while new theme changes could leave Cursor's prompt bar using stale colors.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/termtheme ./internal/adapters/agent/cursor`
- `vitest run src/renderer/lib/osc-color-report.test.ts src/renderer/lib/cursor-color-scheme.test.ts`
- `npm --prefix frontend test -- src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.test.tsx src/renderer/components/CommandPalette.test.tsx` — 120 tests passed
- `git diff --check`

The full frontend typecheck is currently blocked by the shared `packages/product-ui` workspace because its React/motion dependencies are unavailable in this checkout.

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Start a Cursor session in light mode; prompt bar is light.
- [ ] Start a Cursor session in dark mode; prompt bar is dark.
- [ ] Toggle the theme with an existing Cursor session open; colors update without restarting.
- [ ] Open a shell or non-Cursor terminal; no unsolicited control bytes or input corruption.
- [ ] Search in Cmd+K, select Toggle theme with Enter, and confirm the query does not flash empty while the palette closes.

title: fix(reviewer): resume Claude after dead-pane relaunch
body:
Fixes #4658
Supersedes #4659

## Summary
- keep first-launch Claude reviewer identity ownership exact: AO persists the same deterministic native UUID emitted through `--session-id`, including migration of the legacy double-derived transcript identity
- when a reviewer pane/process is dead but its native conversation is retained, route a new review launch through the reviewer restore boundary so Claude uses `--resume` instead of colliding on `--session-id`
- detect the existing Claude transcript before resuming, preserve the reviewer read-only tool policy and system prompt, and deliver the new review task as the resume-time user turn
- propagate transcript/restore failures instead of silently fresh-launching; the engine's existing liveness gate still notifies a genuinely live reviewer rather than starting a duplicate
- keep idle restore fallback explicit and mark interrupted running runs retryable when native history is unavailable

## Root cause
Commit `d15fd8277c1b63a1a7ebdb55735b9ed6091cf118` introduced deterministic reviewer identity persistence and a native restore adapter, but ordinary review reruns continued through `Launcher.Spawn`, which hard-coded fresh command construction. After cancellation or process exit, the durable `review.agent_session_id` survived while the pane did not, so the next task launched Claude with `--session-id <existing-id>` and Claude rejected the already-owned transcript.

The related `No conversation found` symptom had the same identity-ownership regression: the first implementation passed an already-derived Claude UUID as an AO `SessionID`, causing the command builder to derive it a second time. AO persisted the single-derived ID while Claude owned the double-derived transcript.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/... ./internal/review/...`
- `go build ./...`
- `env -u AO_SESSION_ID -u AO_PROJECT_ID -u AO_TMUX_BINARY -u AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME -u AO_DATA_DIR -u AO_RUN_FILE go test ./...`
- isolated-cache `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run --path-mode=abs` (`0 issues`)

## Risk
Low and scoped to reviewer launch/restore selection. A native restore is attempted only when a durable reviewer-native ID exists; first launch remains fresh. Missing transcripts fall back through the existing adapter behavior, while probe/restore errors are surfaced and never converted into a second fresh launch.

title: fix(project import): require explicit defaultBranch for remote-less committed repos (#4679)
body: Closes #4679. ## What this fixes A committed, non-bare local Git repository with no remote could be registered as a project, but its workers failed to spawn because AO had no way to know which branch to base new worktrees on. The strict spawn resolver (added in PR #3983 on upstream main) deliberately refuses to infer from a temporary checkout, so the remediation `git remote set-head` was impossible for the very repos that needed it. ## Implementation (this fork) This fork already has the spawn-side fallback (`baseRefCandidates` falls back to `refs/heads/` when no `origin/<...>` candidate resolves), so the missing piece was the import contract: confirm the base branch at import time rather than at spawn time. 1. `scanImportFolder` exposes `hasCommit` and `checkedOutBranch` on every repo entry (`frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts`). 2. `remotelessDefaultBranchCandidate(repo)` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx` returns the repo's current symbolic HEAD (read from `checkedOutBranch`) iff `hasCommit && !hasRemote`. No hardcoded branch name. 3. The agent sheet (`CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`) renders an editable "Default branch" field prefilled with the candidate. The user can edit, confirm, or clear. 4. Confirmed value is sent as `config.defaultBranch` and persisted in `ProjectConfig.DefaultBranch`. The existing API contract already accepted this field — no `npm run api` regen needed. 5. The fork's existing `gitworktree` adapter picks the persisted value up via `WorkspaceConfig.BaseBranch` and uses `refs/heads/` as a base candidate, so a remote-less repo with confirmed `trunk` spawns worktrees based on `trunk` instead of `main`. ## Evidence (live AO desktop, AO 0.10.0, this branch) **SCREENSHOT A — import preflight offers trunk** The agent sheet renders an editable "Default branch" field prefilled with `trunk` for committed remote-less repos. (TUI shot from the live AO app showing the prefilled value at submit time.) **SCREENSHOT B — Default branch persisted as `trunk`** Project Settings → Workflow for the imported project shows "Default branch: trunk" — i.e. `config.defaultBranch` round-tripped through the daemon. (Settings panel shot.) **SCREENSHOT C — orchestrator session running from a worktree based on trunk** The live orchestrator session for the `repo` project is active and running `run_commands` in its worktree at `~/.ao/dev/data/worktrees/repo/orchestrator/repo-orchestrator/`. This worktree was created from `refs/heads/trunk` (the user-confirmed default), proving the spawn path that previously failed with `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` is now unblocked for remote-less repos. ## Tests - 3 vitest files, 19 tests, all green (incl. 2 new `import-folder-scan` cases for committed/unborn repos, 5 `remotelessDefaultBranchCandidate` cases, 2 new `_shell-create-project-config` cases for `defaultBranch` propagation). - No new Go test added: `TestWorkspaceIntegrationCreateInRemotelessRepo` already covers the spawn side, and `TestManager_AddDetectsNonMainDefaultBranch` (existing) already asserts that an explicit `Config.DefaultBranch` round-trips through the service to the read model. The new code paths reuse both contracts. - `tsc --noEmit`: clean. ## Notes - The spawn-side state-aware remediation wording described in the upstream fix plan is not applicable to this fork: the `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` code path introduced by upstream PR #3983 does not exist here. The fork's spawn path already accepts any explicit `BaseBranch` and falls back to `refs/heads/` for remote-less repos, which is exactly the behavior the import confirmation is now feeding. - No schema or API regen required. The `defaultBranch` field was already present on the daemon's `ProjectConfig` and the controller's `AddInput`; this PR only sends it from the renderer.

title: feat(files): select between workspace and associated PR diffs
body:
## Feature

The Files explorer currently—and correctly—shows files from the session's live workspace checkout. A session can also own one or more pull requests whose source branches are checked out in separate worktrees or are not checked out locally at all. Add a source selector so users can choose whether the explorer displays the current workspace or a specific associated PR.

## Example

Session `agent-orchestrator-153` owns [PR #4692](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4692), but the two sources are different:

```text
Workspace branch: ao/agent-orchestrator-153/root
Workspace HEAD:   333ae81bb356
Workspace change: private/ao-cloud (deleted)

PR source branch: ao/agent-orchestrator-153/readme-download-section
PR head:          fc60f070fa81
PR change:        README.md
```

The current Files explorer correctly displays the workspace deletion:

![Files explorer showing the current workspace change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-files-pr-workspace-mismatch-20260830/.issue-assets/files-pr-workspace-mismatch/changed-files-sidebar.png)

To inspect `README.md`, the user currently has to leave AO and open the provider's PR Files view.

## Proposed UX

Add a source dropdown to the Files explorer header, near the existing search and Changed only controls.

Example options:

```text
Workspace · ao/agent-orchestrator-153/root   (default)
PR #4692 · readme-download-section
PR #4701 · follow-up-tests
```

- **Workspace** remains the default and preserves today's behavior. It shows committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes from the session worktree using the existing workspace comparison base.
- Add one option for each PR associated with the session. The label should include the PR number and enough branch/title context to distinguish multiple or stacked PRs.
- Selecting a PR displays that PR's exact `base...head` file list and diffs, even when its branch is checked out in another worktree or is not the session's current checkout.
- Switching the display source must be read-only: it must not check out branches, alter the worker's worktree, move HEAD, touch the index, or disturb dirty files.
- Clearly show the active source above the file list and in empty/error states so users know whether they are reviewing Workspace or PR changes.
- Preserve the selected source per session while the inspector remains open; if the selected PR disappears or becomes unavailable, fall back to Workspace with an explanatory message.

## Backend/read-model direction

The existing endpoint `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/files` is intentionally workspace-backed. Keep that semantic intact. Add either a PR-specific endpoint or an explicit source parameter/read model that returns:

- source kind (`workspace` or `pull_request`);
- source identity and display label;
- workspace branch/HEAD or PR number/URL/source branch;
- comparison base SHA/ref and head SHA;
- file summaries and per-file content/diff for that exact source.

PR mode should use the persisted/provider `baseSHA` and `headSHA`, fetching the necessary refs or using isolated temporary review state when objects are not locally available. It must not assume the session worktree HEAD equals the PR head.

File/line feedback sent to the agent should carry the selected source identity so a comment on PR #4692 cannot be mistaken for a workspace-only path or another associated PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- Files explorer defaults to the current Workspace source.
- A session with one associated PR can switch between Workspace and that PR.
- A session with multiple sibling or stacked PRs can select each PR independently.
- PR mode matches the provider's changed-file set for the selected base/head pair.
- PR mode works when the PR branch is in a separate worktree or not checked out.
- Switching sources never mutates the session workspace or dirty state.
- Search, Changed only, unified/split diff, file expansion, and annotations work for every source.
- Empty, missing-ref, deleted-branch, and provider-unavailable states identify the selected source and provide a safe fallback.

## Why this matters

AO deliberately supports multiple PRs per session while each session has one primary workspace checkout. The Files explorer should make both concepts available without conflating them or forcing users out to GitHub/GitLab for PR-specific review.

## Related

- [#2408](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2408) — the same one-workspace/multiple-PR targeting constraint for automated reviewers.
- [#3982](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3982) — broader git-state-aware Files explorer improvements.
- [#3203](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3203) — base-aware workspace diff behavior.

title: bug(desktop): Browser compaction moves the sidebar toggle out of the titlebar
body:
## Bug

Opening the docked Browser in a session can automatically compact the left sidebar. When that happens on macOS/Linux, the sidebar toggle jumps from its stable titlebar position into the icon rail below the AO logo. The control should retain one fixed top-left position across expanded, compact, and hidden sidebar states.

**Source:** AO session report with attached screenshot  
**Reported:** 2026-08-30  
**Analyzed against:** `ed88a86d12027e0e37aa793d2f016165dde18e83` (`origin/main`)  
**Environment:** macOS (Darwin arm64); verified Agent Orchestrator daemon on port 3001  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** Low — visual/interaction consistency regression; the control remains usable

![Compact sidebar with the toggle below the AO logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-sidebar-toggle-jumps-browser-compact/.issue-assets/sidebar-toggle-jumps-browser-compact/compact-sidebar.png)

## Reproduction

1. Open an agent session with the sidebar expanded.
2. Open/select the docked Browser inspector at a window width where the Browser workspace requires more room.
3. Observe that the shell automatically switches the sidebar to its 48 px compact icon rail.
4. Compare the sidebar toggle before and after compaction.

**Actual:** the fixed titlebar toggle disappears and a replacement toggle appears below the AO logo in the rail.  
**Expected:** the same toggle remains in its fixed top-left/titlebar position throughout the transition.

## Root Cause

The Browser pressure path is intentional, but compact mode swaps the control's owning component and layout context:

1. `SessionView.tsx:682-689,714-718` publishes Browser-only workspace demand while the docked Browser is open.
2. `_shell.tsx:132-156` converts that width pressure into `isSidebarAutoCollapsed`; `_shell.tsx:836-847` then passes compact state to `Sidebar`.
3. `TitlebarNav.tsx:53-60` explicitly returns `null` when `sidebarIsCompact` is true, removing the fixed titlebar control.
4. `Sidebar.tsx:638-650,653-720` switches to the icon-collapse variant and renders a separate `PanelLeft` button after the brand/logo inside `SidebarHeader`.

That second button participates in the sidebar's vertical flow and traffic-light/topbar offset, so it necessarily appears lower. This contradicts the shell invariant documented in `_shell.tsx:895-897`: the titlebar cluster is rendered once so the controls never move when the sidebar collapses or expands.

This behavior was introduced by [PR #4409](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4409), merged 2026-08-29. Existing tests codify the swap: `TitlebarNav.test.tsx:64-68` expects the fixed nav to disappear, while `Sidebar.test.tsx:1625-1632` expects the replacement compact toggle inside the sidebar header.

## Suggested Fix

Keep a single sidebar-toggle owner in the fixed titlebar layer for expanded, compact, and off-canvas states. Remove the compact-only duplicate from `SidebarHeader` (or keep only compact history controls there if their vertical rail behavior remains desired). Add regression coverage asserting that the titlebar toggle remains mounted with unchanged positioning classes through Browser-driven compaction.

The fix should separately verify macOS windowed/fullscreen and Linux geometry because `TitlebarNav` has platform-specific offsets.

## Verification Notes

- Source path and regression commit were traced on current `origin/main`.
- The checked-in tests explicitly assert the current component swap.
- Attempted targeted Vitest execution, but this worktree has no installed frontend dependencies (`vitest: command not found`). No code was changed.

## Related

- [PR #4409](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4409) — introduced Browser-only adaptive sidebar compaction and the compact-rail control swap.
- [Issue #3372](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3372) — separate compact/collapsed sidebar interaction bug; not a duplicate.

title: bug(lifecycle): Chat session with stale runtime launch never becomes active
body:
## Bug

A live structured-Chat worker can remain durably `idle` for its entire running turn, so the session sidebar dot never pulses even while the agent is actively producing output.

This was observed live on `readme download cta` (`agent-orchestrator-153`). The provider turn ran from `2026-08-31T03:28:01Z` to `03:31:39Z`, while every session CDC event continued to publish `activity: "idle"`.

**Source:** live AO fleet report  
**Analyzed against:** `ed88a86d12027e0e37aa793d2f016165dde18e83`  
**AO build:** packaged nightly `0.12.10-nightly.202608301738`; bundled CLI reports `dev`; daemon verified healthy on the Go rewrite's loopback port `3001`  
**OS:** macOS  
**Confidence:** High for the activity-signal rejection mechanism; Medium for the original path that reintroduced the stale terminal metadata

## Reproduction

1. Start a worker in TUI mode.
2. Complete a TUI → Chat interface transition. The affected live session completed this transition on 2026-08-26.
3. Reach a state where the Chat session row still or again contains terminal ownership metadata (`runtime_launch_id` and `runtime_handle_id`) while also containing the current Chat `controller_generation`.
4. Send a Chat prompt and allow the provider turn to start.
5. Observe that the conversation turn and provider thread are running, but `sessions.activity_state` remains `idle` and the sidebar dot does not pulse.

Live affected row during the running turn:

```text
session_mode=chat
activity_state=idle
runtime_launch_id=bf9ee0ec-5d39-4c73-8a94-0a5e546f8086
runtime_handle_id=agent-orchestrator-153
controller_generation=3146af78-db54-4fb8-90a1-35d2db5732f6
```

The matching running turn used the same controller generation. Provider events included a root `turn.started`, the durable turn was `running`, and the provider thread state was `active`.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` reports `chat.turn.started` with a valid current `ControllerGeneration`, but intentionally does not attach a terminal `LaunchID` because structured Chat has no terminal runtime generation.

`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go` applies the generic runtime-launch fence first:

```go
if rec.Metadata.RuntimeLaunchID != "" && s.LaunchID != rec.Metadata.RuntimeLaunchID {
    return nil
}
```

For the affected Chat row, `RuntimeLaunchID` is non-empty while the Chat signal's `LaunchID` is empty, so the lifecycle manager silently returns before validating the matching Chat controller generation or writing `ActivityActive`.

The renderer is behaving consistently with the bad durable state: `frontend/src/renderer/lib/session-presentation.ts` only treats raw `activity.state === "active"` as working, and `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx` only adds the pulse animation when that view says to breathe.

A clean Chat spawn intentionally clears `RuntimeHandleID` and `RuntimeLaunchID`, and `CommitControllerEpoch` also clears them during an interface-mode change. The affected row nevertheless regained or retained both fields after its completed transition, so the lifecycle reducer also needs to remain safe if stale TUI metadata is present on a Chat-owned session.

## Expected

A current structured-Chat controller's matching generation is sufficient ownership proof for Chat activity. `turn.started` should set the session to `active`, and `turn.completed` should settle it back to `idle`, regardless of stale terminal launch metadata that is irrelevant to the current Chat owner.

## Suggested Fix

- Make runtime-launch fencing mode/owner aware: terminal `LaunchID` should fence TUI hook signals, while Chat signals should be fenced by the current `ControllerGeneration`.
- Preserve rejection of missing or foreign controller generations for Chat sessions.
- Audit TUI → Chat transition/restart paths so stale `runtime_handle_id` / `runtime_launch_id` cannot be reintroduced after `CommitControllerEpoch` clears them.
- Add regression coverage for a Chat record with stale runtime metadata and a matching controller generation:
  - current generation `turn.started` becomes `active`;
  - current generation completion becomes `idle`;
  - missing/foreign generation remains rejected;
  - sidebar-facing session CDC publishes the updated activity.

## Impact

- Users cannot tell that affected agents are working from the sidebar.
- Any feature consuming durable session activity receives `idle` throughout the turn, not only the renderer.
- The failure is silent because the lifecycle fence returns `nil`; normal session CDC continues, repeatedly carrying the stale state.
- Scope is bounded to Chat rows that retain or regain terminal launch metadata, with TUI → Chat / recovery paths the known trigger class.

## Related

- [#4125](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4125): Chat activity ownership can be corrupted by signals lacking controller-generation attribution.
- [PR #4204](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4204): strengthens Chat activity fencing by controller generation and documents the assumption that Chat sessions have no runtime launch ID.
- [#3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360): introduced structured Chat/TUI session modes and interface transitions.

title: fix(cloud-terminal): stop infinite ticket minting and surface error on WebSocket failure (#4668)
body: ## What When a cloud terminal WebSocket fails (CSP block, proxy, firewall), the app was retrying indefinitely at ~1-2 mints/sec with no user-facing error. This fix adds a circuit-breaker on the frontend and a lease-refresh guard on the backend. ## Why Fixes #4668 Two costly side effects of the infinite loop: 1. The sandbox never idle-paused — IssueTerminalTicket refreshes interactive_until on every mint, so billing ran indefinitely. 2. The failure was invisible — users saw "Connecting…" forever. ## How Frontend (useTerminalSession.ts + TerminalPane.tsx): - Added cloudConnectFailures counter to the runtime object. - In scheduleReattach(), if a cloud session has never attached and the counter hits CLOUD_CONNECT_MAX_FAILURES (8), transition("error") is called and the retry loop stops (~8 seconds of trying). - TerminalPane detects this specific error via isCloudConnectError and renders a CloudConnectError full-screen overlay (not the generic banner) with a "Retry connection" button that resets the counter via attach(). Backend (worker_transport_store.go): - Before refreshing interactive_until, count unconsumed terminal tickets minted in the last 2-minute window. - If the count exceeds unconsumedTicketThreshold (10), the CASE clause skips the lease extension. Sandbox wake (paused → running) still fires. - A slog.Warn is emitted with org_id, session_id, and count for observability without requiring a metrics system change. Intentional omission: no integration test for the backend path — the postgres package has no unit-test infrastructure and the lease suppression SQL is covered by private CI's integration suite. ## Testing Frontend — 4 new Vitest tests in useTerminalSession.test.tsx: npm test -- src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.test.tsx → 50 passed (50) Manual repro (DevTools Network → Offline mode → open cloud terminal): - Before: "Connecting…" forever, ~2 ticket requests/sec in Network tab - After: overlay appears after ~8s, Network tab goes quiet, Retry button reconnects once Network is restored Backend — package compiles and vets clean: go build ./cloud/internal/postgres/... go vet ./cloud/internal/postgres/... ## RESULTS ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(orchestrator): give replacement a lifecycle timeout
body:
## Summary

- give `POST /api/v1/orchestrators` a dedicated three-minute lifecycle bound while ordinary REST requests retain their configured timeout
- carry the closed renderer source enum into the daemon request and persist a correlated request event locally

## Why

In [#4700](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4700), a clean replacement began retiring a live Codex coordinator. The ordinary 60-second request deadline returned HTTP 500 after 62 seconds, retirement finished afterward, and that request created no successor orchestrator.
