title: bug(browser): popup tab drift can send agent actions to the wrong authenticated tab
body:
## Summary

After a page opens a popup/new AO browser tab, `ao browser tabs` can report that the new tab is active while `snapshot`, `act`, `click`, `get`, `screenshot`, `errors`, and `dialog` remain attached to the prior tab. IDs returned by `ao browser tabs` can then be rejected by `ao browser tab select`, and queued native commands can appear to stall.

This is a correctness and safety bug: an agent can inspect one authenticated tab in metadata and mutate a different authenticated tab.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31, macOS 14.6 arm64, packaged desktop browser transport `electron-webcontents-debugger`  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Confidence:** High. The exact unsafe fallback remains in current source and explicitly documents that subsequent actions may hit a different tab.

## Sanitized reproduction

1. Open page A in an AO Browser panel.
2. From page A, open page B through `target=_blank` or `window.open()`.
3. Run `ao browser tabs --json`; observe `activeTabId: "t2"`.
4. Run `ao browser snapshot --interactive --json`; observe page A's boundary/content.
5. Run a harmless action whose target exists only on page A; observe page A changes while the tab list still marks t2 active.
6. Run `ao browser tab select t2 --json`; it may fail with:
   `Tab t2 not found; run agent-browser tab to list open tabs (AGENT_BROWSER_COMMAND_FAILED)`.
7. Commands queued behind the popup target-sync operation may fail to return within the caller's 10-second window.

The original report used an authenticated government site. Signed parameters and personal data are intentionally omitted; a local two-page fixture is sufficient.

## Root cause

AO currently has two active-tab registries:

- `session.tabs` / `session.activeTabId` own the Electron `WebContentsView` tabs.
- `agentBrowserRuntime` keeps an independent native tab registry and active target.

In `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`, `ensureNativeActiveTab` tries `tab-select`, refreshes with `tabs`, and retries. If the retry still returns `AGENT_BROWSER_COMMAND_FAILED`, it deliberately logs and **accepts the drift**, then assigns:

```ts
session.nativeActiveTabId = tabId;
```

The adjacent source comment already states the consequence: a later `click/fill/snapshot` can silently land on a different tab. Because the cached field is now equal to AO's active tab, subsequent commands skip synchronization and operate on the runtime's stale target.

Popup activation compounds this through `queueNativeActiveTabSync`, which is fire-and-forget and serialized on `session.nativeOperationQueue`. An unresponsive native select can hold later commands behind the queue; cancellation of a later request does not remove the already-running predecessor.

The unsafe convergence behavior was introduced in `745c26841` and merged through PR #4169. PR #4169 fixed an unbounded retry/stuck-tab problem, but traded it for silent wrong-target execution. Closed issue #3445 is not a duplicate: it concerned visual native-view bleed-through, whereas this report proves automation-target divergence and mutation of the wrong page.

## Expected invariant

One AO tab identity must be authoritative. If AO reports t2 active, every command must either target t2 or fail closed before performing any read or mutation. It must never silently fall back to t1.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove the path that marks `nativeActiveTabId` synchronized after native selection failed.
- If registries cannot be reconciled, return a stable structured target-mismatch/unavailable error; do not execute the requested action.
- IDs returned by `ao browser tabs` round-trip through select and close.
- Bound and cancel popup target synchronization so it cannot hold unrelated commands indefinitely.
- Do not expose `agent-browser` recovery instructions in AO CLI errors.
- Include target identity in action results (at minimum AO tab ID plus URL/origin after the action) so callers can verify where the action ran.
- Add a regression test with page A opening page B: all read/mutation commands target B, switching back targets A, and forced native registry drift fails closed without mutating A.
- Add a queue/cancellation regression proving a failed popup sync does not wedge later commands.

title: bug(browser): tabs output leaks full signed URLs into agent transcripts
body:
## Summary

`ao browser tabs --json` returns each tab's title and URL verbatim. For signed SSO/handoff links, this emits the full query string—including opaque one-time or credential-like parameters—into agent tool output and retained transcripts. When a page uses the URL as its title, the secret-bearing URL is duplicated.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31 on an authenticated government portal; all secret values are intentionally omitted  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Confidence:** High. Current source returns raw values.

## Sanitized reproduction

1. Open a page whose URL resembles:
   `https://example.test/access?param1=<opaque>&param2=<opaque>&param3=<opaque>`
2. Make the page title equal to that URL (the observed site did this).
3. Run `ao browser tabs --json`.
4. Observe the complete URL and query values in both `tabs[].url` and `tabs[].title`.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts` builds tab results directly from:

- `entry.view.webContents.getURL()`
- `entry.view.webContents.getTitle()`

There is no output-boundary sanitization. The same file already has `sanitizeNetworkURL`, which strips credentials/fragments and redacts query values for captured network metadata, but tab results do not use an equivalent policy.

## Impact

- Signed handoff/SSO material is copied into agent transcripts and diagnostic logs.
- A URL-shaped title duplicates the exposure.
- Long opaque URLs can exhaust tool-output budgets.

No matching open or closed issue was found for browser-tab URL redaction.

## Acceptance criteria

- Default tab output is safe to retain: preserve origin/path while redacting query values, credentials, and fragments.
- Sanitize URL-shaped titles as well as `url`.
- Apply the policy at the trusted Electron/daemon response boundary so text and JSON output are both protected.
- Keep an explicit, clearly unsafe opt-in only if full URL retrieval is genuinely required.
- Cover ordinary URLs, query strings, fragments, embedded credentials, URL-shaped titles, opaque/high-entropy values, and malformed URLs.
- Audit browser errors and other tab metadata paths for the same raw-URL exposure.

title: bug(cli): browser screenshot ignores path with --json and floods output with base64
body:
## Summary

`ao browser screenshot <path> --json` accepts the positional path but silently ignores it. It writes no PNG and prints the entire image as base64 JSON, which can flood and truncate agent tool output.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Confidence:** High; current CLI implementation has this exact branch.

## Reproduction

```sh
ao browser screenshot /tmp/ao-browser-test.png --json
test -f /tmp/ao-browser-test.png
```

Observed:

- command returns a very large `result.data` base64 field;
- the requested file does not exist.

The user report measured roughly 46,000 tokens before truncation.

## Root cause and contract conflict

In `backend/internal/cli/browser.go`, screenshot handling calls the browser action first and then immediately serializes the full response when `jsonOutput` is true. Positional-path handling exists only in the non-JSON branch.

The bundled browser guide currently documents base64 for `--json`, but the Cobra contract says `screenshot [path]` and describes the command as capturing to a PNG file. Accepting a path and silently discarding it is unsafe and surprising even if the behavior was documented elsewhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a path is supplied, write the PNG in both text and JSON modes.
- JSON output for a file write returns compact metadata: resolved path, byte size, width, and height.
- Inline image data requires an explicit opt-in such as `--base64`; it is never the accidental result of combining a path with `--json`.
- Preserve overwrite protections and path-validation behavior.
- Add CLI tests for absolute/relative paths, `--json`, file bytes, compact output, overwrite refusal, and explicit inline mode.
- Update the bundled browser guide and help text so they agree.

title: feat(browser): support action postconditions and report cancelled navigation
body:
## Problem

Browser actions can report that an element was matched and a low-level click/keypress was dispatched while the application produces no observable result. On guarded or authenticated sites, an agent can misread that as the intended action succeeding and may retry a consequential control.

**Reported by:** external AO user; report relayed by the project operator (public handle/source URL not supplied)  
**Observed:** 2026-08-31 on an authenticated Angular application  
**Analyzed against:** `main` at `ab17197b0d1bdc8d4d9849ef46675e067fc77119`  
**Classification:** Product/observability enhancement, not yet a confirmed AO interaction bug.

## Evidence

A visible `Start New Filing` button was present in the snapshot. `act`, `click`, `dblclick`, focus + Enter, and focus + Space all reported a matched/dispatched interaction. The control visibly received focus, but the URL and subsequent snapshots did not change. Chromium also logged a blocked `beforeunload` confirmation.

A physical-click control result was not available, so the report does **not** establish whether AO synthetic input, the site's route guard, or site JavaScript prevented navigation. Current `act.outcome: "matched"` describes deterministic element matching, not application-level success, but that distinction is easy to miss.

## Desired behavior

Allow callers to state an expected postcondition and distinguish:

- element matched;
- input dispatched;
- navigation/dialog/DOM effect observed;
- navigation cancelled, blocked, or timed out;
- no observable effect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add optional postconditions such as expected URL, text, dialog, navigation, or DOM change.
- Include before/after URL and document generation/navigation facts in action results.
- Surface blocked/cancelled navigation and dialog signals in the correlated action response when available.
- Clearly document that `matched` is element-resolution status, not proof of application success.
- Avoid automatic retries of non-idempotent actions after an unknown outcome.
- Add a local integration fixture with `beforeunload`/route-guard behavior and tests for satisfied, unmet, and cancelled postconditions.

title: bug(desktop): Switch agent dialog opens and immediately closes itself
body:
## Bug

Clicking **"Switch agent"** in the session actions dropdown (topbar `...` menu) opens `SwitchAgentDialog`, and it immediately closes again in the same tick — the dialog flashes and disappears instead of staying open.

## Repro

1. Open any active worker session.
2. Click the session actions `...` menu in the terminal topbar.
3. Click **"Switch agent"**.
4. Expected: the switch-agent dialog opens and stays open.
5. Actual: the dialog opens and is dismissed immediately (visible as a brief flash).

## Root cause

Two independent Radix dismissal mechanisms fire on the same click:

1. `TerminalSwitchAgentButton.tsx` renders the menu item as a `DropdownMenuItem` with `onSelect={() => handleOpenChange(true)}`. `onSelect` does not call `event.preventDefault()`, so Radix's default post-`onSelect` behavior closes the parent `DropdownMenu` (`SessionActionsMenu.tsx`) in the same tick `SwitchAgentDialog`'s `open` prop flips to `true`.
2. `SwitchAgentDialog.tsx` renders `<Dialog modal={false} ...>` — intentionally non-modal so it doesn't fight `xterm`'s own focus/keyboard handling underneath it (the dialog is portaled into a container inside the terminal pane, not `document.body`). Because it's non-modal, Radix's `Dialog.Content` relies on `DismissableLayer`'s document-level `pointerdown`/`focusout` listeners for outside-click dismissal instead of a focus trap. The dropdown item is unmounting and returning focus in the very same event cycle the dialog mounts, so `DismissableLayer` treats the residual pointer/focus activity as "outside" and immediately closes the just-opened dialog.

A prior fix (`263ba3b82` / PR #4572, "unify session actions, terminal tabs, and naming") already moved `SwitchAgentDialog`'s render site from inside `TerminalSwitchAgentButton` into `SessionView`, specifically so the closing dropdown wouldn't *unmount* the dialog before it opened. That solved the unmount race but left the `DismissableLayer` outside-click race untouched, which is what's reported here. Possibly related to the closed #4039 ("fills terminal and reanimates on repeated activation") — different symptom, likely same family of dropdown/dialog interaction issues around this control.

## Fix

A PR is attached that adds an `onPointerDownOutside`/`onFocusOutside` guard on `SwitchAgentDialog`'s `DialogContent`, ignoring only outside events whose target is inside the just-dismissed menu/trigger (`[role="menuitem"]`, `[role="menu"]`, `[data-session-actions-trigger]`), so a genuine outside click still closes the dialog normally. Pattern matches the existing `onEscapeKeyDown`/`onPointerDownOutside` guard already used in `InstallDependencyDialog.tsx`.

Covered by a new regression test (`SessionActionsMenu.switch-agent.test.tsx`) that drives the real `DropdownMenuItem` click path — unlike the existing tests, which either mock the button out or open the dialog directly with `open=true` and so don't exercise this race.

title: fix(frontend): prevent switch-agent dialog auto-dismiss race with dropdown menu
body:
Closes #4710.

## Bug

Clicking **"Switch agent"** in the session actions dropdown opened `SwitchAgentDialog` and then immediately closed it again in the same tick — the dialog flashed and disappeared instead of staying open.

## Root cause

`263ba3b82` (#4572) already moved `SwitchAgentDialog`'s render site from inside the button into `SessionView` to stop the closing dropdown from *unmounting* the dialog before it opened — that fixed the unmount race but left this `DismissableLayer` outside-click race untouched.

It fails against `main` with the exact reported symptom before the fix (verified via `git stash`), and passes after.

- Full `frontend` vitest suite: 3189 passed / 1 skipped / 4 failed, all 4 pre-existing and unrelated (confirmed via `git stash` — they fail identically with and without this change; they're a known machine-locale `toLocaleString` issue in `AgentModelCombobox`/`ChatTimelineItems`/`ChatWorkspace`).
- `npm run typecheck` — clean.

## Manual verification

- Verified in the real Electron desktop app (dev build on this branch, pointed at real session data) — clicking "Switch agent" from the session actions menu now opens the dialog and it stays open and interactive; a genuine click outside still closes it.
- Verified again against a full self-build of the packaged desktop app + Go daemon (not just the dev harness): this branch merged onto a freshly upstream-synced fork main, `.app` repackaged and daemon restarted, then re-tested live against real session data. Confirmed by the reporting user directly in the rebuilt production app: "все работает, я подтверждаю" ("everything works, confirmed") — the dialog opens and stays open, no more flash-close.

title: fix(terminal): resolve reboot reattach loop and add native auto-resume (#4641)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4641.

This PR addresses two related issues with terminal session persistence and lifecycle:

### 1. Bug Fix: Infinite reattach loop after PC reboot
- **Root Cause**: In `tmux.go`, `IsAlive` classified `serverNotRunningOutput` ("no server running") as `ports.ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (a retryable/transient error) rather than `(false, nil)`. Because it was treated as transient, `attachment.go` retried with linear backoff, but the frontend's 3-second open timeout tore down the socket and reconnected first, resetting the backend's retry counter. This resulted in two retry loops perpetually interrupting each other in an infinite "reattaching" state instead of reaching a clean "session ended" state.
- **Fix**: Reclassified "no server running" as permanent death `(false, nil)`, identical to the "session not found" case. `attachment.go` immediately marks the session as exited. (Darwin native PTY host already uses this classification via `isConnRefused`).
- **Tests**: Updated `TestIsAliveReportsNoServerAsPermanentDeath` and integration test expectations.

### 2. Feature: Auto-resume terminal-only agents into fresh session
- **Behavior**: When a user opens/interacts with a confirmed permanently dead terminal session (`state === "exited"`):
  1. Calls `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/auto-resume-agent` (`AutoResumeAgentWithMode`), which checks if the agent adapter's `GetRestoreCommand` returns `ok=true` (supported for agents like Cline, Claude Code, Goose, etc. that persist native conversation IDs on disk).
  2. If `ok=true`: Launches a fresh terminal process with native resume argv, attaches transparently, and displays a one-line banner: `"Session expired after restart — resumed via <agent>'s native session recovery"`.
  3. If `ok=false`: Returns `SESSION_NO_NATIVE_RESUME` (mapped to HTTP 409), falling back cleanly to the existing "session ended" state with no silent relaunch.
  4. Gated strictly on definitively-dead terminal state, never on transient errors.

## Test Coverage
- `TestIsAliveReportsNoServerAsPermanentDeath` in `tmux_test.go`
- `TestAutoResumeAgent_SucceedsForNativeRestore` in `manager_test.go`
- `TestAutoResumeAgent_FailsWithErrNoNativeResumeWhenNotResumable` in `manager_test.go`
- `TestAutoResumeAgent_RequiresLiveExitedSession` in `manager_test.go`
- `autoResumeAgent` endpoint test in `sessions_test.go`
- Full backend suite passing (`go test ./...`)

title: [Bug]: `ao spawn --model X` records an empty model — mergeMetadata drops Metadata.Model
body:
### Summary

`ao spawn --model <model>` succeeds, but the session records no model at all. The `sessions.model` column is written as the empty string and `GET /api/v1/sessions` omits the field, so nothing can report which model a session resolved to.

The agent itself launches correctly — this is a record/read-back defect, not a launch defect.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
export AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-model AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/ao-model/running.json AO_PORT=3095
mkdir -p "$AO_DATA_DIR"
cd backend && go run ./cmd/ao daemon
```

In a second shell, register any git repo with a resolvable default branch and spawn with an explicit model:

```bash
cd backend
go run ./cmd/ao project add --path /path/to/a/git/repo --id demo --name demo
go run ./cmd/ao spawn --project demo --harness claude-code --skip-agent-check \
  --mode tui --name m1 --model sonnet

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3095/api/v1/sessions | grep -o '"model":"[^"]*"'   # no output
sqlite3 "$AO_DATA_DIR/ao.db" "SELECT id, quote(model) FROM sessions;"
```

### Expected behavior

The resolved model is recorded and read back:

```
demo-1|'sonnet'
"model":"sonnet"
```

`domain.SessionMetadata.Model` documents exactly this — *"the agent model this session resolved to at spawn time, including any per-spawn --model override"* — and the schema carries a dedicated `model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` column for it.

### Actual behavior

```
demo-1|''
```

and the API response has no `model` key.

### Root cause

`session_manager` builds the spawn metadata with `Model: resolvedModelForMetadata(...)` and hands it to `MarkSpawned`, which merges it into the existing row:

```go
rec.Metadata = mergeMetadata(rec.Metadata, metadata)
```

`seedRecord` never sets `Model`, so the base side is empty. `mergeMetadata` (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`) copies seventeen fields by an explicit allowlist and `Model` is not among them, so the empty base value wins and the resolved model is discarded.

This is the failure mode the package already documents. `TestMarkSpawnedPersistsChatControllerFacts` carries this comment:

> mergeMetadata is an explicit allowlist, so a field added to SessionMetadata without a line here is silently dropped on every spawn and restore. That happened to the chat resume handle: the provider still held the conversation, but AO forgot its id, so no restart could ever resume it — and nothing failed loudly, the column was just empty.

`Model` is the same omission one field over.

### Scope

Only two things read `Metadata.Model` — the session DTO (`httpd/controllers/sessions.go`) and the `sessions.model` column (`storage/sqlite/store/session_store.go`). No relaunch or resume path consumes it, so no session has been running the wrong model; the value is simply never recorded.

### AO version

Built from source at `dbd87a21e` (current `main`).

### Environment

Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3, x86_64, Go 1.25.12, tmux 3.7c.

### Logs / extra context

Found by running the daemon against an isolated data dir and cross-referencing the observed behaviour with the code path. Happy to open a PR — the fix is one line in the copy-if-non-empty group, plus a regression test.

title: fix(lifecycle): carry the resolved model through mergeMetadata
body:
## What

Adds the missing `Model` line to `mergeMetadata`, so a spawn's resolved model is recorded instead of discarded.

Fixes #4716.

## Why

`ao spawn --model X` persists an empty model. `sessions.model` is written as `''` and `GET /api/v1/sessions` omits the field, so nothing can report which model a session resolved to.

`session_manager` builds the spawn metadata with `Model: resolvedModelForMetadata(...)` and hands it to `MarkSpawned`, which does `rec.Metadata = mergeMetadata(rec.Metadata, metadata)`. `seedRecord` never sets `Model`, so the base side is empty; `mergeMetadata` copies seventeen fields by explicit allowlist and `Model` is not one of them, so the empty base wins.

This is the hazard the package already warns about. `TestMarkSpawnedPersistsChatControllerFacts` says it plainly:

> mergeMetadata is an explicit allowlist, so a field added to SessionMetadata without a line here is silently dropped on every spawn and restore. That happened to the chat resume handle ... nothing failed loudly, the column was just empty.

`Model` is the same omission one field over.

## How

One line, in the `set` (copy-if-non-empty) group rather than an unconditional assignment: a relaunch that resolves no explicit model must leave the recorded value alone. That is the opposite of the neighbouring `ControllerGeneration`, which is assigned precisely because rotation is the point — the test covers both directions.

**Scope — deliberately narrow.** This is a record/read-back fix, not a launch fix. The agent already started with the correct model; `session_manager` passes the adapter its own resolved config, and `Metadata.Model` exists for the API view. Its only readers are the session DTO (`httpd/controllers/sessions.go`) and the `sessions.model` column (`storage/sqlite/store/session_store.go`), so no session has been running the wrong model — AO just forgot which one it picked.

I have not audited the rest of `SessionMetadata` for further allowlist gaps in this PR. If you would like that swept as a follow-up, say so and I will do it separately rather than widen this one.

## Testing

`TestMarkSpawnedPersistsResolvedModel` asserts both halves: the resolved model reaches storage, and a later relaunch resolving none leaves it intact. It is committed **before** the fix so the failure is in the history:

```
manager_test.go:3711: model = "", want "sonnet"; a spawn's resolved model must survive the merge
```

Verified against a real daemon on an isolated data dir, before and after:

```
ao spawn --project demo --harness claude-code --model sonnet

before   sessions.model = ''          GET /api/v1/sessions -> model absent
after    sessions.model = 'sonnet'    GET /api/v1/sessions -> model='sonnet'
```

`go test -race ./internal/lifecycle/...` passes. Full backend suite: 161 packages pass. Three failures on my machine are pre-existing and unrelated to this change, all reproducing on a clean `main` checkout — `TestCopilotClassicPATIsNotAnAuthorizationSignal` (fails whenever a classic GitHub PAT is in the environment) and `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` / `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane` (both `base-index`, #4222).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: fix: resume dead orchestrator's conversation before cold respawn
body:
## Summary
- `attachment.go`: `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (e.g. tmux's "no server running" after a reboot) is a definitive, permanent signal, but the reattach loop routed it through the same failures/backoff counter as an ordinary transient probe error. That raced against the frontend's ~3s open timeout — which tears down and reopens the attachment on every timeout, resetting the counter to zero — producing the infinite "reattaching" loop reported in this issue. It now reports a clean exit on the very first probe.
- `service.go`: `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=true)` always spawned a brand-new, unlinked session, discarding a retired orchestrator's conversation even though its history is fully intact on disk and the daemon already has a working resume mechanism (`RestoreWithMode` -> `restoreArgv` -> `GetRestoreCommand`). It now attempts that resume for a single retired orchestrator before falling back to a fresh spawn, and sends an explicit notice into the new session when resume genuinely fails, instead of silently swapping in a blank coordinator.
- **`tmux.go` (root cause, found via live reproduction while testing this branch):** on a real host reboot, `/tmp` is commonly tmpfs, so the *entire* per-user tmux socket directory disappears, not just one socket file. tmux then reports `error connecting to <path> (No such file or directory)` instead of `no server running`. `IsAlive` only recognized the latter as `ErrRuntimeUnavailable`; the reboot message fell through to the broader transient `error connecting` match and was reported as `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` instead. Since an inconclusive probe is deliberately never treated as proof of death (to avoid regressing #3475), this left `reconcileLivePass` **permanently unable to ever recognize a session as dead after a real reboot** — it just stays `idle` forever with no live runtime and no automatic resume attempt, regardless of harness. This is very likely the actual, dominant cause of "sessions never come back after a restart" on Linux.
- No frontend changes needed: the topbar "Orchestrator" button and `RestoreUnavailableDialog` both already call `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=true)`, so the resume path is reachable from the existing recovery UI.

basically linux tmpfs is ram based so its sessions were getting cleared everytime I fixed it

Fixes #4641.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./backend/internal/terminal/...` — `TestAttachmentExitsImmediatelyOnRuntimeUnavailable` pins the reattach-loop fix
- [x] `go test ./backend/internal/service/session/...` — `TestSpawnOrchestratorCleanResumesRetiredOrchestrator`, `TestSpawnOrchestratorCleanFallsBackWhenResumeFails`, updated `TestSpawnOrchestratorCleanRetireNoticeIsBranchNeutral`
- [x] `go test ./backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/... -tags integration` — `TestIsAliveReportsMissingSocketDirectoryAsRuntimeUnavailable` pins the reboot-message classification fix; updated `TestIsAliveReportsErrorConnectingAsProbeInconclusive` to a genuinely-ambiguous message so the inconclusive path keeps real coverage
- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] Manually reproduced against a live snapshot of real post-reboot session state (dev daemon, `AO_DATA_DIR` copy): before this fix, reconcile logged the reboot error as inconclusive and never touched the session again; after it, the same sessions are classified `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` and reconcileLive proceeds into its relaunch-in-place path

title: feat(codex): add accounts and global switching
body:
## Summary

- Stacked only on `codex/phase-1-shared-harness-readiness`.
- Adds a secure AO vault for multiple Codex accounts and makes the selected account the device-global Codex account.
- Ordinary AO Codex launches use the normal effective `$CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex`; AO does not create a private runtime or copy native histories.
- Reconciles and safely imports an eligible file-backed device login, and supports interactive inline Add account / Sign in again flows.
- Switching atomically installs the selected credential and restarts only AO-owned running Codex controllers, preserving AO session IDs, worktrees, interface modes, and native Codex thread IDs.
- External Codex clients may report an account-changed error and require a manual restart or resume after a switch.
- Retains structured plan, capacity, activity, reset-credit, logout, and signed-out inactive account deletion flows.

## Architecture and safety

- Treats `auth.json` as opaque secret bytes: it is never parsed, logged, returned by the API, or persisted in SQLite.
- Device-global switching is enabled only when the effective Codex credential store is safely file-backed.
- Serializes account mutations and uses a durable immediate stop / credential activation / exact resume transaction with recovery.
- Keeps account actions on the primary loopback listener, enforces the configured renderer-origin boundary, and excludes them from the optional LAN listener.
- Uses `activeAccountId` as the sole authority for the active account.
- Includes one additive migration: `0123_codex_account_management.sql`.

## Explicit omissions

- No per-task account selection.
- No assisted or automatic switching.
- No AO-private Codex runtime, configuration projection, profile binding, history backfill, or native-history copying.
- No new continuation session, handoff, archive, or worktree transfer during switching.
- No account rename, reorder, or in-place replacement.
- No token/JWT parsing, credential logging, billing scraping, or raw provider-payload persistence.

## Stack

This PR preserves the Phase 1 readiness authority and does not include the discarded Phase 2–6 profile architecture. After Phase 1 merges, it can be retargeted/rebased onto `main`.

The branch history was rebuilt into five focused commits from the current Phase 1 tip after sanitation and review.

title: bug(daemon): packaged Windows desktop v0.12.10 fails to start — Daemon exited with code 1 (needs stderr details)
body:
## Bug
AO desktop (packaged, Windows) fails to start with the banner **"AO Daemon failed / Daemon exited with code 1"** while opening a project, on v0.12.10 (released ~5 hours before the report). The real daemon error is in the banner's **Show details** stderr block, which the reporter did not include. Not reproduced locally (Linux); no sibling reports on v0.12.10 at filing time.

**Source:** [Discord #bug-triage thread](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1543924640294895616) | **Reported by:** @pyaesonephyothu, relayed by Maaz | **Report generated:** 2026-08-31T10:04:08Z
**Analyzed against:** `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator@5cb411aca2c0` (current `main`) and tag `v0.12.10` | **Confidence:** Medium — symptom confirmed, exact mechanism unconfirmed pending stderr
**Priority:** P1 — packaged desktop cannot start on a fresh stable release; suspected update-induced persistent-boot-failure class

## Environment
- AO 0.12.10, packaged desktop build, Windows (Win32)
- Daemon: stopped, message "Daemon exited with code 1"
- Route surface: other
- Feedback generated 2026-08-31T10:04:08.957Z

## What v0.12.10 changed in the daemon boot path
Diff `v0.12.9...v0.12.10`: 55 commits / 300 files. Startup-relevant files changed: `backend/internal/config/config.go`, `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go`, `lifecycle_wiring.go`, `preview_wiring.go`, plus **10 new SQLite migrations (0109–0118)** — a fresh-update store/migration risk window.

## Hard-fail candidates (exit code 1 = clean `return err` in `daemon.Run()`, not a panic)
Enumerated from `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go` on current `main` — every pre-bind `return err` site:

| Line (main) | Failure | stderr/details prefix |
|---|---|---|
| L79/L85/L94/L100 | `config.Load`: bad `AO_PORT`/`AO_DATA_DIR`/`AO_RUN_FILE`/`AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` env | `resolve ...` / `invalid AO_...` |
| L115 | run-file unreadable | `inspect run-file: ...` |
| L117 | A live daemon genuinely owns the port | `daemon already running (pid N, port M); refusing to start` |
| L125 | SQLite open/migrate failure | `open store: ...` |
| L171 | CDC pipeline start | CDC error |
| L215 | Agent resolver wiring | `wire agent resolver: ...` |
| L303 | Session-service wiring | `wire session service: ...` |
| L321 | Scratch-project seeding | seed error |
| **L430** | **`ReconcileStartupSafety` fails → daemon refuses to bind** | **`reconcile sessions on boot: ...`** |
| L526 | browser-runtime address publish | `publish browser runtime address` |
| L653/L666–672 | scratch-project seed / working directory | `seed scratch project:` / `daemon working directory: ...` |

**L430 is the strongest candidate.** `sessMgr.ReconcileStartupSafety(ctx)` is the "startup safety boundary": *"durable agent-switch and interface-transition recovery … if AO cannot prove and close every active saga, do not bind a usable API"* (`daemon.go` L418–431). An un-closable saga refuses boot **persistently across restarts** (the saga row survives in SQLite), which would match a failure that repeats each time the project is opened — the report shows one occurrence; persistence is unconfirmed. Sibling issues #4696 / #4700 (below) show stale-runtime / restart-recovery states are a live bug class in the 0.12.x line.

Ruled out: goose duplicate-version panic (panics exit 2, this is exit 1; and no duplicate versions exist on `main` or the `v0.12.10` tag); Windows dev-mode `0xc000013a` console-kill (packaged build, and that exit code differs); supervisor/browser named-pipe failures (both warn-and-continue, non-fatal); ephemeral-port fallback already handles port conflicts.

## Candidate causes ranked (pending stderr)
1. **`reconcile sessions on boot:` (L430)** — persistent refusal via `ReconcileStartupSafety` on a stuck agent-switch/interface-transition saga. Matches persistence + while-opening-project timing.
2. **`open store:` (L125)** — one of the 10 new migrations (0109–0118) failing on the reporter's existing data, or AV/file-lock on `ao.db` (Windows Defender lock → SQLite open fails — known Windows pattern).
3. `daemon already running` (L117) — a still-live predecessor daemon with a valid `/healthz`.
4. `config.Load` env validation (unlikely on a packaged build — requires `AO_*` env vars set).

## Investigation next steps (cheapest first)
1. **Get the stderr.** Reporter: reopen app → banner → **Copy details** (12k captured stderr, PR #2972) and paste it into this issue or the Discord thread. This single artifact discriminates every candidate above.
2. `Test-Path ~/.ao/running.json` then `Get-Content ~/.ao/running.json` — absence = daemon never bound; presence = bound earlier.
3. `Get-Process ao` — is a predecessor daemon still alive?
4. Run the bundled daemon manually for un-clipped stderr (PowerShell): `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\agent-orchestrator\resources\daemon\ao.exe" daemon` — adjust path to the actual install location; read the first error line.
5. If it prints `reconcile sessions on boot: ...`: the follow-on error names the exact stuck saga — check the saga/agent-switch rows in `~/.ao/data/ao.db` for the project being opened, and cross-reference #4696/#4700 for the manual unwedge.
6. If it prints `open store: ...`: copy `~/.ao/data/` aside first (do not delete user data), then identify the failing migration by opening the DB copy with sqlite3.
7. If the manual run binds and stays up: the failure is in the Electron supervisor path (`frontend/src/shared/daemon-launch.ts`) — capture the daemon child's stderr at spawn time.

## Impact
- Packaged Windows desktop on v0.12.10 cannot open projects (single day-0 report so far).
- If L430-class: persistent across app restarts, no in-app remediation.
- If L125-class (migration/store): potential upgrade blocker for the wider v0.12.10 population as auto-update rolls out.

## Related
- #4696 — chat session with stale runtime launch never becomes active (stale-runtime class)
- #4700 — restart can leave a project without a working orchestrator (stale-saga class)
- #4657 — chat per-delta SQLite writes / migration 0105 (store write-path family)
- #3037 — historical goose duplicate-version startup panic (ruled out here, kept for context)

title: [Cloud] New terminal uses local daemon instead of the cloud workspace
body:
## Bug

Opening **New terminal** from a cloud worker session fails instead of opening a shell in that session's sandbox.

**Source:** Live report in an AO development session on 2026-09-01  
**Analyzed against:** `7a8856f6306cdca2721ad829ba6813d0fb00d028` on PR #4624  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1 — a primary workspace interaction is unavailable for every cloud session.

## Reproduction

1. Run the Electron app with the cloud offering enabled and signed in.
2. Create a cloud project and worker session.
3. Open the worker session.
4. Click **New terminal** (or use the new-terminal shortcut).
5. Observe that no usable workspace shell opens.

## Root Cause

`SessionView` and the persistent shell shortcut handler call the local `useOpenShellTerminal` mutation for every session. That mutation always POSTs to the loopback daemon's `/api/v1/shell-terminals` endpoint. A cloud-only session does not exist in the local daemon, so its session/workspace cannot be resolved and Coder is never contacted.

There is a second routing defect in `TerminalCacheProvider`: every cloud terminal mux is hard-coded to request `kind: "agent"`. A shell tab must request `kind: "workspace"` so the control plane asks the sandbox worker to open a shell PTY rather than attaching Claude's existing PTY.

The control plane also retires every existing workspace terminal and caps active terminals at agent + one shell, which prevents the desktop's multi-terminal UI from working against cloud sessions.

## Fix

- Preserve the cloud session identity when opening a terminal.
- Keep cloud shell tab metadata in the Electron renderer instead of the local daemon.
- Route shell targets to a `kind: "workspace"` ticketed control-plane WebSocket.
- Allow bounded concurrent workspace terminal sessions.
- Cover the button, shortcut, cloud tab lifecycle, and terminal-kind mapping with tests.

## Impact

Cloud users cannot open an interactive workspace shell from AO even though Coder's own terminal works.

## Related

- PR #4624 — Coder sandbox-provider integration and isolated preview.
- #4666 — separate cloud terminal WebSocket CSP failure, already fixed.

title: bug(cloud): Coder pause/resume loses agent conversation and workspace state
body:
## Bug
A Coder-backed Cloud session loses coding-agent conversation continuity when the workspace is auto-paused and resumed. The desktop briefly shows `Terminal disconnected - reattaching...`; after recovery, the terminal is backed by a fresh Claude process/conversation.

**Source:** Live design-partner POC report on 2026-08-31
**Reported by:** Prateek
**Analyzed against:** `a78744b0e` (preview release `terminal-preview-7a8856f63`)
**Priority:** high — session continuity and uncommitted workspace state can be lost on a normal idle pause
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction
1. Create a Cloud project/session using the Coder sandbox provider and the current Docker-based Linux template.
2. Let the session reach the configured idle-pause threshold.
3. Open the session terminal so the desktop requests terminal tickets and wakes the workspace.
4. Observe `Terminal disconnected - reattaching...` while Coder resumes.
5. After recovery, inspect the workspace process: Claude was launched afresh with `--session-id` rather than restored with `--resume`.

## Live evidence
- Session `00ac3284-fd41-4d53-9077-a0cf7cc1f01e` auto-paused at `2026-09-01T02:15:36Z`; its replacement `ao-worker` started at `02:16:57Z` and Claude at `02:17:08Z`.
- Session `07ad6206-aeb5-4b8e-b3fb-4aa61ee69241` auto-paused at `02:16:36Z`; its replacement `ao-worker` started at `02:18:43Z` and Claude at `02:18:50Z`.
- Worker epochs advanced to 15 and 16 and new agent terminal rows were created.
- The Coder containers mount a durable volume only at `/home/coder`.
- `/workspace/repository` exists only in the container filesystem.

## Root Cause
`cloud/internal/reconcile/reconciler.go:workerSpec` hardcodes:
- `AO_WORKSPACE_DIR=/workspace/repository`
- `AO_DATA_DIR=/workspace/.ao/worker`
- `HOME=/workspace/.ao/home`
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/workspace/.ao/home/.claude`
- `CODEX_HOME=/workspace/.ao/home/.codex`

`cloud/internal/sandbox/coder/client.go:bootstrapCommand` creates and owns `/workspace`, but the approved Coder template's persistent volume is mounted at `/home/coder`. Stopping and starting the workspace recreates the container and discards `/workspace`.

`cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go:interactiveRestoreIdentity` correctly restores only when the Claude JSONL exists under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Because that directory was discarded, it falls back to a fresh launch. The same path mismatch also puts the checked-out repository and uncommitted changes at risk.

## Fix
Define a provider-specific durable workspace root contract. For Coder:
- use a template-backed persistent directory for repository, AO worker data, harness homes, and repository credentials;
- make the persistent path configurable or derive it from an explicit Coder template contract rather than assuming `/home/coder`;
- validate persistence across a stop/start before enabling idle pause;
- test Coder pause/resume for repository files and Claude/Codex conversation restoration.

The terminal UI should separately communicate `Resuming workspace` and `Restoring agent`, but that does not replace the persistence fix.

## Related
- [PR #4624](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4624) — Coder sandbox provider integration.

title: feat(cloud): honor Coder auto-stop and make resume user-driven
body:
## Goal

Treat customer-configured Coder auto-stop as a normal lifecycle event instead of immediately undoing it, while keeping active AO work alive and making resume explicit and visible.

## Current behavior

- If Coder reports a workspace stopped while AO still desires running, the reconciler calls Start again.
- Minting any terminal ticket changes an AO-paused sandbox back to running.
- Cloud terminal reconnects mint fresh tickets automatically, so retained/background panes can wake compute without a new user gesture.
- AO worker traffic is not one of the activity types Coder documents as extending autostop.

## Required behavior

- Observe Coder-native stops as a paused/stopped runtime state rather than automatically restarting them.
- Add an explicit per-session resume intent/API.
- Opening a specific session, sending a user message, opening a shell, or requesting a workspace operation may resume it.
- Listing projects/sessions and background terminal reconnects must not resume compute.
- While an AO turn is queued/running or a user is actively operating a workspace, extend the Coder workspace deadline using the workspace extend API; stop extending it when genuinely idle.
- Expose desired/observed lifecycle state and resume progress to the desktop.
- Show Paused by Coder, Resuming workspace, Waiting for Coder agent, Starting AO worker, Restoring agent, and Connected states.

## Acceptance

With Coder autostop enabled, an idle AO workspace stops and remains stopped. Opening its AO session visibly resumes it. An active AO turn is not stopped. A hidden/reconnecting terminal does not wake it. Files and agent conversation remain intact via #4731.

Depends on #4624. Related: #4731.

title: bug(cloud): Coder bootstrap reports success before install and worker launch complete
body:
## Bug

Coder BootstrapWorker returns success after the archive upload acknowledgement rather than after extraction, installation, and AO worker launch succeed.

## Root cause

bootstrapThroughPTY returns after receiving __AO_UPLOAD_DONE__. It does not await the existing final __AO_BOOTSTRAP_OK__ or __AO_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED__ result. Closing at that point can also leave streamPTYOutput blocked on an unconsumed unbuffered channel.

## Required fix

- Keep the buffered PTY connection alive after upload completion.
- Await explicit bootstrap success/failure or process/transport termination.
- Propagate extraction, sudo/user creation, binary installation, and worker-launch failures to the reconciler.
- Ensure all stream goroutines terminate on success, failure, cancellation, and disconnect.
- Add tests for success, post-upload command failure, transport closure, and cancellation without goroutine leaks.

## Acceptance

BootstrapWorker returns nil only after __AO_BOOTSTRAP_OK__. A post-upload __AO_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED__ reaches reconciliation as an error. No output goroutine remains blocked when the method returns.

This is a merge blocker discovered in the independent review of #4624 and must be merged into the #4624 branch before that PR lands.

title: fix(cloud): preserve Coder workspace state across resume
body:
## Stack

- Stacked on #4624 (`ao/agent-orchestrator-211/coder-sandbox-provider`).
- This is a baseline blocker that must merge into #4624's source branch before #4624 can land.
- Keep this PR in draft; do not merge it directly to `main` or mark it ready while the parent integration is still under review.

Fixes #4731.

## Summary

- add a required, validated `AO_CLOUD_CODER_DURABLE_ROOT` template contract and persist the Coder owner, template, parameters, selected agent, and root in each session plan
- resolve every Coder reconcile/recovery operation from that durable session profile while retaining only the deployment-scoped connection credential
- reject workspace owner, deterministic name, or template mismatches during create, `FindBySession`, persisted-ID lookup, and bootstrap before worker credentials can be uploaded
- derive the repository, AO worker data, repository credential helper, `HOME`, Claude config, and Codex home from the provider-specific durable root while preserving the existing `/workspace` layout for other providers
- require a real non-symlink mount, write a session identity marker on first bootstrap, and fail closed after stop/start if the marker is missing or belongs to another session
- wait for PTY shell readiness, retry transient pre-ready closes, await the post-upload bootstrap result, and verify the detached worker remains alive so setup/launch failures reach the reconciler instead of being reported as success
- make Codex honor the configured durable `CODEX_HOME`
- extend focused tests and the opt-in live Coder lifecycle test to verify repository, Claude, Codex, restore-marker, session-profile authority, and mismatch behavior

## Template and configuration requirements

- Set `AO_CLOUD_CODER_DURABLE_ROOT` to the approved template's exact persistent-volume mount point; AO does not assume `/home/coder`.
- The path must be absolute, normalized, non-root, no longer than 1024 bytes, and free of control characters.
- The path must exist in each workspace as a non-symlink mount point and the template must provide `mountpoint`.
- Configure `AO_CLOUD_CODER_OWNER` as the canonical owner name returned by Coder, not an alias such as `me`.
- The mount must survive Coder `stop` then `start`; run the documented `TestLiveLifecycle` gate against the exact template/root before enabling idle pause.
- Hosted `coder` Secrets Manager JSON now requires `durable_root`; deployment validation fails closed when it is absent or unsafe.

- `cd cloud && go vet ./...`
- `cd cloud && go test -race ./...`

No ECS or shared AO staging service deployment was performed.

## Risk / rollout

Coder session rows created before this contract do not contain the complete durable profile and fail closed rather than falling back to singleton deployment defaults or ephemeral `/workspace`. Before any rollout, supply the new secret field, update and verify the approved template, run the live stop/start gate, and create fresh sessions or explicitly migrate preview-only rows in a separate reviewed change.

title: fix(cloud): send server-side websocket pings to prevent ALB idle timeouts (#4667)
body:
## What

Added a periodic WebSocket server-side ping loop (`pingTerminalConnection`) every 25 seconds during cloud terminal sessions.

## Why

Fixes #4667. Every healthy cloud terminal WebSocket was being severed by the AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) after 60 seconds of frame-level idle time.

## How

- Added `terminalPingInterval = 25 * time.Second` constant to give 2x headroom inside the ALB's 60s idle timeout window.
- Added `pingTerminalConnection(ctx, connection)` goroutine spawned during `connectTerminal`.
- Evaluates `connection.Ping(ctx)` on every ticker interval without acquiring `writeMu` (since WebSocket Ping control frames do not block application data frames).
- Exits cleanly when session `ctx` is cancelled or when the socket closes.

## Testing

- Verified Go compilation (`go build ./...`) and lint checks (`go vet ./...`).
- Validated server-side keepalives locally using in-memory WebSocket test servers (`httptest.Server` + `coder/websocket`) without requiring full Docker Compose or AWS cloud credentials.
- Executed Go unit tests (`go test -v ./internal/httpapi`) confirming Ping control frames flow over TCP and context cancellation cleanly terminates the keepalive goroutine.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: bug(daemon): reconcileLive silently ignores sessions with empty WorkspacePath, leaving them permanently stuck
body:
## What happened

After a daemon restart (app update), a previously working orchestrator session shows:

- **"The agent controller stopped"** banner with "Resume agent" / "Open shell" buttons
- **"Session is missing runtime or workspace handles (SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE)"** when clicking Resume
- **"Session workspace is not available"** in the topbar editor button area
- **"The controller is not connected"** as the composer placeholder

The session is permanently stuck. Deleting the workspace project and re-adding the same folder does not fix it because the orphaned session row persists in the database.

*(screenshot attached in comment below)*

## Reproduction

1. Add a repository as a workspace folder and spawn an orchestrator session.
2. Update AO (or force-kill the daemon mid-flight to simulate a crash).
3. Reopen the desktop app.
4. The orchestrator session shows all four error symptoms above.
5. Click "Resume agent". It fails with SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE.
6. Delete the workspace from AO and re-add it. The broken session still appears.

## Root cause

The session's `Metadata.WorkspacePath` is empty. This can happen when:
- The daemon crashed or was killed between `store.CreateSession` and `lcm.MarkSpawned` during spawn.
- A Chat controller launch failed after the seed row was created but before workspace metadata was persisted.

On daemon restart, `reconcileLive` (`manager.go:2246`) checks for empty handles and returns nil without doing anything:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || (rec.Metadata.Branch == "" && projectKind != domain.ProjectKindScratch) {
    return nil
}
```

The session stays non-terminated, no controller starts, no cleanup runs. It sits in limbo forever.

`SaveAndTeardownAll` (`manager.go:2140`) has the same silent skip:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || rec.Metadata.Branch == "" {
    continue
}
```

## Three distinct bugs

1. **`reconcileLive` does not terminate sessions with empty handles.** It should call `m.lcm.MarkTerminated(ctx, rec.ID)` instead of returning nil. (`manager.go:2246`)
2. **`SaveAndTeardownAll` skips sessions with empty handles without terminating them.** Same fix needed. (`manager.go:2140`)
3. **No startup sweep for spawn-orphaned rows.** If a spawn was interrupted, the half-initialized session row survives daemon restarts indefinitely. Startup should identify and terminate (or delete) these rows.

## Error chain (code references)

| UI symptom | Backend source | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| "The agent controller stopped" | `ChatWorkspace.tsx:897` | `controller.state === "stopped"` |
| "SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE" on Resume | `service/session/service.go:916` mapping `ErrIncompleteHandle` | `ResumeAgentWithMode` guard at `manager.go:1629` finds `WorkspacePath == ""` |
| "Session workspace is not available" | `service/session/workspace_location.go:28` | `WorkspacePath` empty or path doesn't exist on disk |
| "The controller is not connected" | `ChatComposer.tsx:568` | Composer disabled when `controller.state === "stopped"` |

## Suggested fix

In `reconcileLive`, terminate instead of ignoring:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || (rec.Metadata.Branch == "" && projectKind != domain.ProjectKindScratch) {
    m.logger.Warn("reconcile: terminating session with incomplete handles",
        "sessionID", rec.ID, "workspacePath", rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath, "branch", rec.Metadata.Branch)
    return m.lcm.MarkTerminated(ctx, rec.ID)
}
```

Same pattern in `SaveAndTeardownAll`.

## Verification query

```sql
SELECT id, is_terminated, metadata FROM sessions
WHERE json_extract(metadata, '$.workspacePath') = ''
   OR json_extract(metadata, '$.workspacePath') IS NULL;
```

## Related issues

- #3649 — spawn-time `INTERNAL_ERROR` leaving orphaned worktrees (same `SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE` symptom, different trigger: spawn atomicity)
- #4700 — Restart leaving project without a working orchestrator (different trigger: restart timeout)
- #4531 — transient "workspace unavailable" flash on new sessions (frontend caching race, self-recovers)

## Environment

- macOS (darwin arm64)
- AO desktop app, latest build
- Workspace-type project with previously working orchestrator

title: fix: avoid xterm viewport callback after StrictMode disposal
body:
## Summary

- eliminate a development-only xterm lifecycle pageerror during React StrictMode cleanup
- invalidate the AO terminal handle immediately, then defer physical xterm disposal one task so xterm 5's queued viewport-open callback can finish
- cover the exact disposal ordering with a deterministic regression test

## Diagnosis and scope

The live cloud terminal path is healthy: deeper inspection found 752 xterm buffer lines and a visibly rendered Claude prompt including AO_CODER_WORKER_OK. The cached dimensions exception is therefore not evidence of a blank-pane or replay failure.

The exception itself is reproducible and narrowly understood. xterm 5 schedules an uncancellable zero-delay Viewport.syncScrollArea callback from Terminal.open. React StrictMode cleans up its first development mount in the same task. Immediate disposal releases the renderer before that callback runs, so it reads RenderService.dimensions after disposal and raises a pageerror.

This PR only removes that lifecycle pageerror. It does not change cloud ticketing, replay coalescing, attachment ordering, or local/cloud mux behavior, and it should not be treated as a product-blocker fix.

## Exact verification run

- npm test -- XtermTerminal.test.tsx TerminalPane.test.tsx useTerminalSession.test.tsx --run (167 passed)
- npm run frontend:typecheck (passed)
- lifecycle regression failed before the production change: the fake xterm open timer observed prior disposal; after the change, queued open work runs first and disposal still occurs exactly once
- PR CI passed: frontend test, renderer-smoke, and gitleaks

## Native visual-verification follow-up

A second real Electron instance was intentionally not launched because agent-orchestrator-211 owns the shared AO dev Chromium profile and ports 5173/3002 for active user hands-on testing. This PR did not stop or modify that instance, its preview, its ports, or its profile, and did not launch against the production/shared AO_DATA_DIR.

Follow-up requested: after agent-orchestrator-211's user test is explicitly finished and the shared dev resources are released, rerun this branch in the real Electron app and confirm terminal mount/navigation produces no xterm dimensions pageerror.

No staging or production deployment was performed.

title: fix(chat): finalize plans on successful turns
body:
## What

Finalize every remaining structured plan step when a conversation turn settles successfully, and add migration 0119 to repair completed turns that already persisted a stale non-terminal plan.

## Why

A provider can emit an initial `turn.plan` and then finish with `turn.completed` without sending a terminal plan update. AO previously stored the completed answer and turn state while leaving the plan at `0/N` or partially pending.

Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4663

## How

- Treat successful turn completion as the terminal durable fact for the turn plan.
- Update the turn plan and matching plan activity in the same transaction.
- Preserve the raw provider-event archive.
- Do not infer completion for failed, interrupted, recovered, or cancelled turns.
- Backfill only stale plans attached to already-completed turns.

## Testing

title: fix(lifecycle): preserve Chat and TUI status across desktop restarts
body:
Fixes #4458

## Outcome

This replaces the original narrow tmux compatibility patch with a complete restart-continuity fix for both Chat and TUI sessions.

Existing sessions recover automatically when the desktop app starts. There is no import command, migration script, or user action required.

## Why this regressed

The visible failure came from several changes interacting:

- #4330 exposed the daemon API before startup reconciliation finished, so the UI could render stale durable `Exited` facts.
- #3711 treated every Chat stream closure—including a planned desktop shutdown—as terminal and persisted `Exited`.
- #4393 moved TUI sessions to a deterministic private tmux socket; #4465 later removed that runtime without retaining recovery for the private-socket cohort.
- #4071 limited startup recovery to four workers, explaining why larger boards appeared to repair themselves in waves or after the later reaper pass.

tmux was therefore one cause of legacy TUI recovery failures, but it was not the common cause of the false `Exited` state seen by both Chat and TUI.

## What changed

### Startup visibility

- Gate session/state API routes until startup reconciliation succeeds, so the renderer never observes a partially recovered board.
- Keep startup unready when ownership is ambiguous or a probe is inconclusive; do not mutate the board or launch a replacement.

### Chat continuity

- Treat desktop shutdown as a planned Chat detach rather than conversation termination.
- Reattach Chat sessions to their persistent host and exact provider conversation.
- Recover complete Codex history through paginated `thread/turns/list`, with compatibility fallback for older `thread/read` servers.

### TUI continuity

- Recover modern PTY protocol-v3 and shipped protocol-v2 hosts using exact runtime/process-incarnation evidence.
- Preserve inconclusive PID semantics on Windows, tolerate Linux's exact post-update ` (deleted)` executable suffix, and give cold Windows legacy identity proof a dedicated bounded deadline.
- Discover historical private, named, and default tmux namespaces and canonicalize a proven owner automatically.
- Persist canonical tmux routing with the server PID, native session ID, pane ID, owner session, and launch ID.
- Fence tmux reads, writes, attach, destroy, and recovery to the proven object; fully canonical handles never fall back to broad name rediscovery.

## Safety properties

- Failed or unknown probes are never treated as proof that a session died.
- Ambiguous ownership leaves durable state and live runtimes untouched.
- Existing identities are upgraded in place only after ownership is proven.
- Same-name runtime replacements are rejected rather than adopted or mutated.
- Recovery is automatic; historical sessions are not copied, imported, or recreated.

## Packaged desktop E2E

The real packaged Electron app exercises six simultaneous cohorts:

1. Chat
2. native PTY protocol-v3 TUI
3. shipped PTY protocol-v2 TUI
4. historical private-socket tmux TUI
5. named-socket tmux TUI
6. default-socket tmux TUI

Across five app launches it verifies:

- first and second cold restarts
- immediate daemon-owner handoff
- startup API readiness and zero visible `Exited` state
- exact provider/runtime identity preservation
- real terminal input/output through every recovered PTY and tmux route
- survival beyond the reaper interval
- fail-closed behavior under deliberately ambiguous ownership

Final exact-HEAD packaged result: `1 passed (1.5m)` on `9e0f32e45`.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` and pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2 with an isolated cache — 0 issues
- focused adapter, lifecycle, reaper, session-manager, and storage tests
- race tests for Chat, PTY, runtime selection, and tmux recovery
- Linux and Windows ConPTY cross-builds; Windows vet
- Linux PTY arm64/amd64 race stress for the CI fixtures
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck:e2e`
- packaged desktop restart-continuity Playwright E2E

### Summary
On Linux, `Menu.setApplicationMenu()` was previously omitted in `frontend/src/main.ts`, causing Electron to fall back to its built-in default application menu template (File / Edit / View / Window / Help). title: feat(import): add project import validation and Git preparation API
body:
## Goal
Implement the backend contract for the Import as project onboarding flow. This is the shared foundation that workspace import will extend.

## Scope
- Add POST /imports/validate for importKind: project.
- Validate the selected folder without mutating Git or the filesystem.
- Return the shared ImportValidationResult DTO with isValid, blockingErrors, root, optional childRepos, and nextStep.
- Populate root Git state: isRepo, hasCommit, hasOrigin, isEmptyFolder, needsGitInit, requiredActions, and blockingErrors.
- When the root is not Git-initialized but direct child repositories exist, return childRepos and nextStep: choose_import_kind. This is informational; project preparation must not modify child repositories.
- Add POST /imports/prepare-git.
- Require explicit approval for every requested action.
- Execute only missing approved actions, strictly in order: git_init, then git_commit, then set_remote.
- Do not overwrite an existing origin automatically.
- Return or stream GitPreparationEvent values with pending, running, success, and error states.

## Shared DTO Direction
- RepoGitStatus includes repoPath, isRepo, hasCommit, hasOrigin, isEmptyFolder, needsGitInit, requiredActions, and blockingErrors.
- ImportValidationResult includes importKind, isValid, blockingErrors, root, childRepos, and nextStep: error | choose_import_kind | prepare_git | continue.
- Keep this contract reusable for workspace import, where childRepos carries each direct child repository's status.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A non-Git folder requires git_init, git_commit, and set_remote.
- A Git repository with no commit and no origin requires only git_commit and set_remote.
- A Git repository with a commit but no origin requires only set_remote.
- Invalid or unreadable folders return isValid: false with user-displayable blocking errors.
- A non-Git root with child repositories returns the workspace suggestion state without mutating children.
- Tests cover the scenarios above, plus rejected unapproved actions.
- Regenerate OpenAPI and frontend API types.

## Related
- Workspace UX/remediation context: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3686

title: feat(import): add project import onboarding flow
body:
## Goal
Implement the Import as project onboarding flow using the backend validation and Git-preparation API from [#4755](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4755).

## Scope
- Update CreateProjectFlow to call POST /imports/validate immediately after the user selects a folder with importKind: project.
- Block all downstream onboarding until validation completes.
- If isValid is false or nextStep is error, show blockingErrors and do not show the next onboarding modal.
- If nextStep is continue, proceed with the existing project creation flow.
- If nextStep is prepare_git, show a Git preparation modal for the root repository.
- Show detected Git state, only the missing Git steps, an editable remote URL, Back, and Continue.
- On Continue, call POST /imports/prepare-git and show per-step progress from GitPreparationEvent.
- Run the displayed steps sequentially in the UI: do not show the next action as running until the prior action succeeds.
- On failure, show the failed step with retry and back actions.

## Special Project Choice
When validation returns nextStep: choose_import_kind because the root is not Git-initialized but child repositories exist, show an informational choice:
- Try importing as workspace: return to import-type selection while retaining the selected folder.
- Continue as project: continue using the root only.

Do not present child repositories as targets for Git preparation in the project flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Non-Git root shows git_init, git_commit, and set_remote.
- Git root without a commit or origin shows git_commit and set_remote only.
- Git root with a commit but no origin shows set_remote only.
- Blocking errors stop onboarding before harness selection.
- The workspace suggestion choice appears only for the non-Git-root-with-child-repositories case.
- Component tests cover ready, blocked, preparation-required, workspace suggestion, progress success, and progress failure states.

## Dependency
- [#4755](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4755)

title: feat(import): add workspace import validation and Git preparation API
body:
## Goal
Extend the shared import validation and Git-preparation backend for Import as workspace. Reuse the contract delivered for project import; do not create a separate workspace-only API.

## Scope
- Extend POST /imports/validate to support importKind: workspace.
- Validate the selected workspace root without mutation.
- Return root Git status and direct child repository statuses in ImportValidationResult.
- For every child repository, return isRepo, hasCommit, hasOrigin, isEmptyFolder, needsGitInit, requiredActions, and blockingErrors.
- Identify the root separately from child repositories so the frontend can explain whether the root is a repository and which children are ready or need setup.
- Extend POST /imports/prepare-git to accept approved actions for multiple repositories.
- Run each repository's approved missing actions sequentially, and emit GitPreparationEvent values for every repository and step.
- Keep approval explicit: no Git mutations before user approval, only missing approved actions, and never overwrite an existing origin automatically.

## Error Handling
Return typed, user-displayable validation errors for invalid paths, unreadable folders, unsupported folder structures, repository discovery failures, Git failures, and worktree resolution failures. Build on the remediation direction in [#3686](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3686); avoid raw internal errors in the UI contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A workspace validation result clearly distinguishes the selected root and child repositories.
- Child repositories that need Git initialization expose needsGitInit: true and their required actions.
- Ready children are represented without preparation actions.
- Partial setup is represented per repository: missing commit and/or remote must not be treated as needing git init.
- If the selected root is already a repository with an origin remote and direct child repositories are detected, the backend returns a non-blocking warning that AO will import it as a project rather than a workspace.
- Preparation supports an explicitly approved set of affected repositories and emits per-repository, per-step progress.
- Tests cover an empty root, root repo, ready child repos, partially initialized children, non-Git children, invalid paths, and execution failure.
- OpenAPI and frontend API types are regenerated.

## Related
- [#4755](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4755) establishes the shared project-import contract.
- [#3686](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3686) documents the existing workspace import remediation problem.

title: feat(import): add workspace import onboarding flow
body:
## Goal
Implement the Import as workspace onboarding flow using the shared validation and Git-preparation APIs. Reuse the project import preparation modal and progress UI where possible, extending them to show multiple repositories.

## Scope
- Call POST /imports/validate after a user selects a folder with importKind: workspace.
- Block downstream onboarding until validation completes.
- Show blocking errors before harness selection.
- Render the selected root separately from child repositories.
- Group child repositories by ready, needs Git initialization, needs commit, needs remote, and blocked states.
- Show a reusable Git preparation modal with the workspace context, affected repository list, per-repository required actions, editable remotes, Back, and Continue.
- Let the user review and approve only the repositories and actions that will be changed.

## UX Requirements
- Never show workspace or orchestrator creation options before validation passes.
- Do not present raw internal error codes to users.
- Make the scope of every Git mutation explicit before execution.
- Reuse the project import modal and progress primitives, but add the multi-repository grouping and approval UI required for workspace mode.

- A workspace with ready child repositories can continue without Git preparation.
- A workspace with partially initialized children displays only each child's missing steps.
- A non-Git child displays git_init, git_commit, and set_remote.
- The root repository status and child repository statuses are visibly distinct.
- Each repository's progress is visible during preparation.
- If a child fails, the UI explains which repository and step failed and provides recovery actions.
