title: fix(editor): discover per-user Windows editor installs (#4767)
body:
## Problem

Fixes #4767. On Windows, VS Code and Cursor installed via per-user installers (e.g. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin`) were not discovered by the editor handoff, because `executableNames` returned a bare `#!/usr/bin/env sh` script before a `.cmd` shim, and PATH-only scanning missed non-system installs.

## Changes

**`frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.ts`**
- Added `winInstallDirs` per candidate (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Trae, etc.) + `WIN_INSTALL_ROOTS` map resolving `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, `%ProgramFiles%`, `%ProgramFiles(x86)%`.
- Added `winInstallDirsFor()` + `resolveInDirs()` to probe Windows install dirs after PATH misses.
- Reordered `executableNames()` on win32 so PATHEXT-appended `.cmd`/`.bat`/`.exe` shims are tried **before** the bare extension-less name (prevents sh script being picked up).
- Moved editor/terminal resolution from construction-time to a per-call `resolveAll()` so an editor installed after startup is discovered.

**`frontend/src/main/editor-handoff.test.ts`**
- Added tests: win32 shim-over-script preference, non-win32 does not scan install dirs, Linux extra-search-dir regression, dynamic re-resolution after handoff creation.

## macOS / Linux safety

All new code is gated behind `platform === "win32"`. The `executableNames` win32 reorder, `commandSearchDirs` extra dirs (darwin/linux untouched), `resolveEditor` `.app` fallback (darwin-only), and `resolveTerminal` are byte-for-byte identical for non-win32 platforms. No regressions introduced; typecheck passes cleanly (0 errors).

title: fix(settings): render the pairing QR dark-on-light so Android can scan it
body:
## The bug

The pairing QR could not be scanned by the AO Android app. It scanned fine from iOS, from Android's system camera, and from Google Lens — which is why it read as a flaky per-device camera problem rather than a rendering bug, and why it survived this long.

`StyledQRCode` took its colour from `--color-text-settings-title` over a `transparent` background. In the dark theme that renders **light modules on dark** — an inverted code.

Apple's AVFoundation and Google Lens both decode inverted codes. The bundled `com.google.mlkit:barcode-scanning` that `expo-camera` uses on Android does not. So the code was readable by every scanner except our own app's.

## How it was isolated

A single-variable sweep, scanned in the AO app on a device that reproduced the failure. Module size, logo size and finder shape were each held constant so only one factor varied at a time, with a known-failing and a known-passing control bracketing the round:

| variant | polarity | logo | finders | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (control) | inverted | 0.45 | round | fail |
| V1 | inverted | 0.25 | round | fail |
| V2 | inverted | **none** | round | fail |
| V3 | inverted | 0.45 | **square** | fail |
| V5 | inverted | 0.25 | square | fail |
| V4 | **light** | 0.45 | round | pass |
| V6 | **light** | 0.25 | square | pass |
| V7 (control) | **light** | 0.25 | square | pass |

Every inverted variant failed; every dark-on-light variant passed. Nothing else predicted the outcome.

This rules out the plausible suspects: **not** the logo (V2 has none and still fails), **not** finder shape (V3 fails), **not** module size (V6 passes at the original 240px panel), and **not** the device (its system camera reads all of these).

## The fix

Render dark-on-light with an opaque background. The logo, rounded dots, round finder corners and EC level M are all left alone — the sweep showed none of them mattered.

Because `StyledQRCode` is shared, this also fixes the TestFlight and Play Store QRs, which were equally unreadable on that device.

## Also included

**Quiet zone measured in modules, not as a fraction of rendered size.** Modules are the unit a scanner reads clearance in, and a short payload has fewer, larger modules — so a percentage tuned on the long pairing code left the small store codes badly short:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Pairing (v18) | 4.0 | 4.0 |
| Pairing (v23, long payload) | 3.1 | 4.1 |
| Play Store (v5) | **2.4** | 4.2 |
| TestFlight (v3) | **1.9** | 4.3 |

The pairing QR hit the required 4 modules by coincidence. The store codes — the ones people scan to install the app — did not.

**Panel 240px → 320px, and the code fills its card.** Not required for the fix. The card was insetting the code on top of the quiet zone `StyledQRCode` already draws, stacking two margins and shrinking the modules for nothing. Removing the inset halves the white border *and* takes a full-length payload from 0.47mm to 0.66mm per module, so it scans at arm's length instead of needing the phone against the screen.

## Verification

- **Paired a real Android and a real iOS device** against a dev daemon; both completed the full `identity` → `endpoints` → `push/devices` handshake and went on to poll sessions and events.
- Every code type (pairing at 516/652/780 chars, Play Store, TestFlight, placeholder) decodes, rendered from the component's own constants.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; 80 tests pass across 15 files.

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

- **Payload length is unbounded.** It grows with endpoint count and hostname length, so some machines get a denser code than others. A CI assertion capping the QR version for a representative payload would stop this silently regressing — which is how the original problem arrived.
- **A slim v3 pairing format** (516 → ~267 chars, v18 → v12) is the real structural win for weak cameras, but it is a wire-format change: `parsePairingCode` hard-rejects any version but `2`, so it needs sequencing with a mobile release.
- **Upstream `expo-camera` bug:** `startFocusMetering()` builds its metering point at `createPoint(1f, 1f)` — the bottom-right corner, not the centre (`ExpoCameraView.kt:640`). Dormant today because the pair screen never sets `autofocus`, but it will bite whoever enables it.

title: feat(cloud): full Docker-local sandbox testing (no NodeOps)
body:
## What

Makes the **entire AO cloud flow runnable on local Docker** — orchestrator/worker sessions, terminals, repo checkout, agent launch, browser panel — with **zero NodeOps sandboxes and zero credits burned**. The Docker sandbox *provider* was already implemented; this closes the two real gaps: **local bring-up tooling** and **desktop-app local auth**.

Combines two pieces (cherry-picked, disjoint files):

### Phase A — one-command local bring-up
- New `cloud/scripts/cloud-local-up.sh`: interactive, stays-up (no self-teardown), fixed loopback ports (CP `127.0.0.1:8081`, PG `54329`), persists stable keys under `~/.ao/cloud/` so `down`/`reset` match, builds the worker + CP images, `docker compose up`, waits for `/readyz`, and prints the desktop launch hint.
- Restored the missing `cloud:local` / `:down` / `:reset` / `:smoke` / `cloud:staging` npm aliases (lost in the #4434 vendoring).
- Fixed stale docs (Docker provider is shipped; corrected the removed `:3000` UI claim + submodule note).

### Phase B — Electron dev-mode local auth (the real unlock)
- The desktop app only spoke WorkOS; the local Docker CP runs `AO_CLOUD_LOCAL_AUTH` and accepts only email/password `/auth/local/*` opaque tokens. Added a **dev-only, loopback-gated** local-auth path: `cloud-auth-local.ts` (register/login/logout + one gate predicate), routed `getCloudSession`/`getCloudAccessToken` to return the local opaque token (so the CP proxy and ticketed terminal WS authorize unchanged), a shadcn sign-in dialog, IPC/preload wiring, and i18n across all 8 catalogs.
- **Gate:** permitted only when unpackaged (or `AO_CLOUD_LOCAL_AUTH_DEV=1`) **and** the CP host is loopback — enforced authoritatively in the IPC handlers and again before any fetch, so an email/password can never be sent to a remote host. WorkOS path untouched.

## Testing — E2E verified on real Docker, no NodeOps

Ran the full flow against a live Docker-backed CP (`cloud-local-up.sh` → `/readyz` 200):
```
register (local-auth) → ao_local_ opaque token       ✓
credential connect → project (public repo) → session ✓
Docker worker container spawned                      ✓
session runtimeState = running                       ✓
worker: bootstrapped → anonymous checkout → repo cloned (/workspace/repository)  ✓
agent terminal: state=open, output_bytes=951         ✓   ← agent launched + producing output
```
That last line is the same milestone that was broken on staging's #4683 build (0 bytes) — here it works. Plus: Phase B's 126 renderer unit tests pass + clean typecheck; Phase A validated live (stack up/down/reset, idempotent, keys persisted 0600).

## Dev loop after this

```bash
npm run cloud:local                                   # Docker CP + workers up on 127.0.0.1:8081
cd frontend && AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on \
  AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 npm run dev
# in-app: SIGN IN with the seeded account (dev@local.test / localdevpass123)
#         → create a cloud project on a public repo → session → terminal
npm run cloud:local:down                              # stop (data retained)
```

Provider capability gaps vs NodeOps (in-place resume, idle auto-pause, public per-port ingress) are by-design and don't affect this testing flow — the browser panel proxies through the CP, and the terminal rides the CP transport, not ingress.


---

## How to test it (step by step)

1. **Bring up the Docker control plane** (builds images the first time, then reuses them):
   ```bash
   npm run cloud:local
   ```
   Waits for `/readyz` on `http://127.0.0.1:8081` and prints the launch hint. Nothing hits NodeOps.

2. **Launch the desktop app pointed at it** (dev mode — the local-auth path is gated to unpackaged + loopback):
   ```bash
   cd frontend
   AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 npm run dev
   ```

3. **Sign in — no register step needed.** `npm run cloud:local` seeds a default account after the CP is ready, and the success banner prints the credentials. The cloud sign-in opens the local email/password dialog (only under the dev+loopback gate); just use the **Sign in** tab:

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Email | `dev@local.test` |
   | Password | `localdevpass123` |

   Tokens are opaque `ao_local_…`, valid 720h.

   > The seed is best-effort and idempotent (201 creates it, 409 means it already exists — the bring-up never fails on it). The **Register** tab is still there if you want a second account; it needs email, display name, password (**≥ 12 chars**), org slug (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}$`), and org name.

4. **Create a cloud project on a PUBLIC repo** — e.g. `https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World` (default branch `master`). Private repos need a GitHub App and won't check out locally by design.

5. **Connect a coding-agent credential.** For just exercising the *infrastructure*, any string works (the local CP skips credential validation). For **real agent output**, paste a valid `claude setup-token` in the credentials dialog — otherwise claude launches but shows an auth prompt (the terminal still renders).

6. **Create a session** → a Docker worker container spawns (`docker ps` shows `ao-worker-…`), checks out the repo, and the **terminal renders** with the agent. Orchestrator sessions can `ao spawn` workers; the browser panel works too — all local.

7. **Tear down:**
   ```bash
   npm run cloud:local:down    # stop, keep data
   npm run cloud:local:reset   # stop + wipe the local DB
   ```

> Note: the local-auth dialog appears **only** when running from source (`npm run dev`) against a loopback CP. Packaged nightly/stable builds have `app.isPackaged = true`, so this path is off and users get WorkOS as normal.

title: fix(review): retry submit during daemon restart
body:
Fixes #4054

## Problem

A reviewer can post its review to GitHub and then run `ao review submit` while the desktop daemon is restarting. The CLI currently reads and parses the result once, makes one daemon request, and immediately exits when `running.json` is temporarily absent/stale or the loopback connection drops. The provider-side review then exists while AO can leave the matching `review_run` in `running`.

## Root cause

The launch/PATH fix from #3755 ensures the reviewer can invoke the correct AO binary and run file, but submission still has no transient-daemon recovery. #3716 addresses mixed-version daemons sharing SQLite, and #2604 addresses lifecycle signal restoration; neither preserves this already-produced review result across an ordinary daemon replacement.

## Fix

- classify missing/stale daemon discovery and loopback transport failures with an internal typed error while preserving existing CLI error text
- make only `ao review submit` retry that typed availability failure for a bounded 30-second window
- retain the already-parsed single or batched result in memory and replay the exact same run id, verdict, body, and provider review id
- return daemon validation/API errors immediately without retrying
- remain cancellation-aware, with at most the 250 ms retry interval added to cancellation latency

This deliberately does not add a CLI-side SQLite/file outbox or infer runs from observed GitHub reviews. The CLI remains a thin HTTP client, no review prose is written into a worktree or new durable store, and AO does not risk attributing a human/provider review to the wrong reviewer run.

## Safety

The daemon review service already makes exact re-submission idempotent: a matching completed run is accepted without rewriting or re-emitting submission telemetry, while a changed verdict, body, or provider review id is rejected. That makes retry safe even if the first connection drops after the daemon committed the result. The existing run/worker ownership checks, lifecycle delivery rules, and GitHub review creation path are unchanged.

Permanently unavailable daemons still produce the established actionable error after the bounded window; the command can then be repeated safely. No retry goroutine or provider network call is introduced.

## Tests

Added deterministic coverage for:

- a batched stdin result surviving a missing run file followed by daemon readiness
- an uncertain transport failure replaying byte-identical idempotency fields
- daemon API rejections returning without retry
- context cancellation stopping an unavailable-daemon retry

Local checks completed:

- `gofmt -d backend/internal/cli/client.go backend/internal/cli/review.go backend/internal/cli/review_test.go`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`

GitHub checks passed on head `eae94e513baa011557823d7f1a3f5353f42bd3ff`:

- Go `build-test`
- Go `lint`
- `api-drift`
- `gitleaks` scan
- CLI E2E native Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows
- CLI E2E container

The focused local Go test command was attempted with build, temp, and module caches redirected to `D:` because the Windows host's `C:` drive was full. Host-wide Go/package I/O remained stalled before any test began; no local test pass is claimed. The repository's Linux `build-test` workflow completed successfully.

## Intentional omissions

- no unbounded wait or automatic daemon start
- no disk queue owned by the thin CLI
- no heuristic SCM reconciliation
- no change to #3716 mixed-daemon locking or #2604 lifecycle restoration

title: fix(lifecycle): ignore stale TUI metadata for Chat activity
body:
Fixes #4696

## Problem

A structured Chat session could retain terminal runtime metadata from an older TUI ownership epoch. Chat activity signals correctly carried the current `controller_generation`, but lifecycle applied the generic `runtime_launch_id` fence first. Because Chat signals intentionally have no terminal launch id, the reducer silently discarded `chat.turn.started` and `chat.turn.completed`, leaving durable activity stuck at `idle`.

## Root cause

The SQLite activity write fence was already mode-aware: TUI writes compare `runtime_launch_id`, while Chat writes compare `controller_generation`. The in-memory lifecycle reducer was not. It applied the terminal fence to every mode before checking the optional Chat generation.

Current Chat startup already clears `runtime_launch_id` through metadata merging, and interface-transition epoch commits clear both runtime fields. However, `runtime_handle_id` was merged only when non-empty, so a legacy/recovered Chat row could retain a stale terminal handle across another successful Chat startup.

## Fix

- Make lifecycle ownership checks mode-specific:
  - TUI signals remain fenced by the current runtime launch id.
  - Chat signals must carry the exact current controller generation and ignore irrelevant stale terminal metadata.
  - controller-generation signals remain invalid for TUI mode.
- Clear stale runtime handle and launch metadata whenever a current Chat controller is successfully committed.
- Document `ControllerGeneration` as the required Chat activity ownership fence.

## Safety

- Preserves existing TUI launch-generation fencing.
- Preserves stale/foreign Chat-controller rejection and additionally rejects generationless inherited provider hooks.
- Does not infer activity, bypass the durable owner CAS, change interface-transition sequencing, or add a second activity source.
- Cleanup occurs only when a Chat controller with a non-empty generation is successfully committed; a failed controller commit leaves the previous durable owner untouched.
- CDC behavior is unchanged: the existing SQLite session update and trigger remain the only durable/event path.

## Tests

Passed locally with Go 1.26.5:

- `go test ./internal/lifecycle -run 'Test(MarkSpawnedPersistsChatControllerFacts|ActivitySignalFencesChatByControllerGenerationDespiteStaleRuntimeMetadata)$' -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/lifecycle -count=1`

The regression proves that a Chat row containing stale runtime handle/launch metadata:

- accepts `active` and `idle` from its current controller generation;
- rejects a generationless stale TUI hook even when its launch id matches the stale value;
- rejects a foreign Chat generation; and
- scrubs stale terminal ownership metadata on successful Chat startup.

Broader `internal/service/chat` and `internal/session_manager` validation was attempted with build/module/tmp caches moved to a secondary disk because the host system drive was full. Dependency preparation did not complete within a bounded 15-minute local wait under concurrent builds, so those results are not claimed; CI remains the authoritative broad run. A focused `go vet ./internal/lifecycle` attempt likewise did not complete within the bounded local wait.

## Related scope

PR #4204 / issue #4125 address the separate sticky-`exited` resurrection and controller shutdown ordering problem. This PR deliberately does not copy those controller/interrupt changes. It aligns the ownership terminology with #4204 while fixing #4696's distinct ordering defect: terminal launch fencing must not precede and veto current Chat generation ownership.

title: fix(browser): fail closed on popup target drift
body:
Fixes #4705

## Problem

AO and the native agent-browser runtime keep separate tab registries. After a popup activated a new AO tab, a failed native `tab-select` could survive the existing `tabs` refresh plus retry. The host then accepted that drift and recorded the AO tab as natively active anyway, allowing later reads, screenshots, or mutations to hit a different authenticated tab while AO reported success.

The popup synchronization was also fire-and-forget on the per-session native queue and inherited the runtime's 60-second command timeout. Screenshots bypassed the target gate entirely.

## Root cause

`ensureNativeActiveTab` correctly tried one real registry refresh before retrying selection, but its second-failure branch logged and then fell through to `nativeActiveTabId = tabId`. That cached an unproven invariant. Because later commands trust the cached ID, the system could no longer distinguish AO's selected WebContentsView from the runtime's actual target.

## Fix

- preserve the existing one-time `tabs` refresh and retry for transient legacy registry drift
- fail closed with stable `BROWSER_TARGET_MISMATCH` after the retry instead of inventing synchronized state
- bound popup target synchronization to five seconds with an AbortSignal passed through to the native process
- keep the internal queue chained to in-flight work even when a caller cancels, preventing later commands from overtaking it
- route screenshots through the same target gate as other native commands
- return sanitized `target.tabId`, URL, and origin evidence for native page results
- make IDs returned by `tabs` round-trip through CLI select/close; provider-close fallback only closes the AO-owned WebContentsView with that exact logical ID
- map the stable mismatch to the existing HTTP conflict response class

## Safety

- no read or mutation proceeds after an unproven target switch
- no raw agent-browser recovery instructions cross the AO API boundary
- cancellation remains prompt while queue ordering is preserved
- the bounded background attempt does not create a second target or retry a page mutation
- URL evidence is sanitized using AO's existing browser URL policy
- the only local fallback is exact-ID tab close, which cannot mutate a different page
- existing single-refresh recovery and legacy UI tab behavior remain intact

## Interaction with #4783

This change is independent of #4783 and does not copy or depend on its action-postcondition work. Both PRs touch `browser-view-host.ts`; whichever lands second should retain this target gate/identity invariant while resolving the textual overlap around native action dispatch. No postcondition behavior is changed here.

## Tests

Passed locally:

- `browser-view-host.test.ts`: 124/124
- `agent-browser-cdp-bridge.test.ts` + `agent-browser-runtime.test.ts`: 26 passed, 2 skipped
- deterministic pre-fix regression: failed on main by resolving after the log `accepting drift`, proving the original wrong-target path
- `git diff --check`

Not completed locally:

- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers ./internal/cli` was terminated after more than one hour while the shared Windows host was still compiling a fresh dependency cache under heavy concurrent Go/disk contention. It produced no test failure before termination; CI should provide the authoritative backend result.

## Manual validation

The target lifecycle, native queue, cancellation, popup, exact-ID close, and stable error paths were verified with deterministic host/runtime fakes. I did not perform a live authenticated-site or real agent-browser popup run.

title: Reported: 'Star Us' button 404s on click
body:
## Bug
Reporter says clicking the "Star Us" button on the AO desktop app's home page takes them to a GitHub 404 page.

**Source:** reported directly by @Hendrixx-RE in an orchestrator chat session (no external thread URL) | **Analyzed against:** `e71a5f99c` (upstream/main, fetched 2026-09-03)
**Confidence:** Low

## Reproduction
1. Open the AO desktop app.
2. On the home page, click the "Star Us" button (top-right, star icon, added in #4549).
3. Reported result: browser opens to a GitHub 404 page.

Not independently reproducible from source — see Root Cause section. No screenshot, AO version, OS, or exact repro sequence was provided by the reporter (falls short of the minimum-viable-report bar); flagging `to-reproduce` rather than guessing further.

## Root Cause
Investigated the obvious hypothesis — a hardcoded pre-org-transfer URL (repo moved from `AgentWrapper`/`aoagents` to `Untrivial-ai` in July 2026, per the comment at `frontend/forge.config.ts:14`) — and could **not** confirm it for this specific button:

- The button's URL is built in `frontend/src/renderer/components/HomePage.tsx:56` from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_URL` (`HomePage.tsx:10`), which is `https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` — already the correct, current org. `git log -S` shows this constant has only ever had this one value since it was introduced in #4549 (2026-09-01); it was never wrong.
- `frontend/package.json` (`homepage`, `repository.url`) and `frontend/forge.config.ts:260,272` (deb/rpm maker `homepage` fields) **do** still hardcode the stale `https://github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator` — verified present on `upstream/main`. But neither is read at runtime by the renderer/main process (no `require`/import of `package.json` for `homepage`, confirmed via search); they only affect Linux package manager metadata and npm bookkeeping. They cannot be the mechanism behind an in-app button 404.
- `gh api repos/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` confirms the repo exists, is public, and the owner is `Untrivial-ai` — the button's target repo is valid.
- Tried to directly verify `https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/stargazers` (the exact URL the button opens) via curl and WebFetch: both returned 404. However, the same tools also return 404 for `https://github.com/torvalds/linux/stargazers` — a definitely-valid, definitely-popular repo's stargazers page — so this is GitHub blocking automated/bot requests to that specific route, not evidence the link is actually broken for a real user's browser.

Three hypotheses traced (button constant, `package.json`, `forge.config.ts`), all ruled out as the mechanism. Could not reproduce the reported 404 against current source.

## Fix
No fix pushed — the only genuinely broken thing found (stale `aoagents/agent-orchestrator` in `frontend/package.json` and `frontend/forge.config.ts`) is real but doesn't explain the reported symptom, so pushing it as "the fix" here would be a guess. Recommend:
1. Reporter re-test against a fresh build and share OS + AO version + a screenshot of the 404 page (URL bar) if it recurs.
2. Separately worth fixing regardless: stale `aoagents/agent-orchestrator` references in `frontend/package.json` (`homepage`, `repository.url`) and `frontend/forge.config.ts:260,272` (deb/rpm `homepage`) should be updated to `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` for packaging-metadata hygiene, independent of this issue.

## Impact
- Cosmetic/trust issue if genuinely reproducible (broken CTA on first-run home screen), but unconfirmed in current source.

- GitHub's `/stargazers` (and `/watchers`) sub-page currently returns 404 for unauthenticated requests — confirmed on `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`, `torvalds/linux`, and `microsoft/vscode` alike, while `/forks`, `/issues`, `/pulls` all resolve fine anonymously on the same repos. So this isn't an org-rename artifact; it's that GitHub now gates that specific listing page behind a session, and anyone clicking the button from a fresh system browser (no active GitHub login) lands on a 404.
- Point the button at the repo's main page instead, which loads anonymously and has a visible Star control for the user to click themselves.

## Test

- No existing test asserted on the button's target URL (checked `frontend/src/renderer/__tests__/_shell-index-home.test.tsx`).
- Manually verified via `curl`/WebFetch that the repo's root page returns 200 anonymously while `/stargazers` returns 404 across multiple unrelated repos, isolating this to a GitHub-side behavior on that specific sub-path rather than anything repo-specific.

title: fix(renderer): bounded exponential backoff for SSE reconnects
body:
## Problem

The renderer schedules its own `EventSource` rebuild once the browser gives up (`readyState` CLOSED), and every consumer used a flat delay: 5s in `event-transport.ts` and `notifications.ts`, 5s +/- 1s in `workspace-file-events.ts`. Nothing grew the delay and nothing capped the attempts, so a stream the daemon keeps refusing knocked every ~5s indefinitely.

That is the amplification in #4323. When the daemon returns a transient 5xx during stream setup, every open session's stream fails at once and they all retry in lockstep. The retry traffic is itself what keeps the daemon from recovering, so a brief hiccup sustains itself.

## Change

New `sse-backoff.ts` with `computeSseRetryDelayMs(retries)`: doubles from 5s to a 60s ceiling, scaled by jitter in `[0.5, 1)` so streams that failed together desynchronise, with the exponent clamped so a long-dead stream cannot reach `Infinity`. All three consumers track consecutive scheduled rebuilds and reset on a successful open, so a one-off failure still reconnects fast. This mirrors the bounded backoff `main/supervisor-link.ts` already uses for the daemon links.

Two details worth calling out, both from review of the first commit here:

- The exponent is driven by a `retries` counter, not the existing `failures` counter. `workspace-file-events` also increments `failures` on non-terminal `onerror` (readyState CONNECTING, where the browser retries on its own) to drive the "degraded" label. Those are not rebuilds we scheduled, and counting them made the first real failure wait the 60s ceiling instead of ~5s, which is slower to recover than the flat delay being replaced.
- All three consumers reset the counter when the API base URL changes. A daemon that comes back on a different port is a fresh target and should not serve the delay the dead port earned. `workspace-file-events` already did this; the other two did not.

## Verification

`sse-backoff.test.ts` covers growth, the ceiling, the jitter band, reset, and non-finite input. Stream-level tests assert that each wait is longer than the last, that a successful open drops back to the initial delay, that the browser's own non-terminal retries do not inflate the delay, and that a new daemon port starts over.

Every new test was mutation-tested rather than just observed passing. Reinstating the flat delay fails 4 tests; breaking the reset-on-open fails 1; reinstating the conflated counter fails the non-terminal test; dropping either port reset fails the corresponding test.

Full renderer suite: 3389 passed. The 5 failures in `src/landing` reproduce identically on `origin/main` and are unrelated to this change. `tsc --noEmit` is clean for every file touched here.

Two existing tests hardcoded the flat 5s and now derive the expected delay from the helper.

## Scope

Renderer only. The optional daemon-side `Retry-After` from #4323 is not included.

Supersedes #4340, whose branch predates the #4388 rewrite of `workspace-file-events.ts` and no longer applies.

Refs #4323, #3963

title: fix(desktop): keep Linux app available from tray
body:
Fixes #4811

## Problem

Linux never initialized AO's tray controller, and the generic non-macOS last-window policy immediately quit the app. That made closing the window terminate the desktop supervisor and provided no tray affordance for reopening it.

## Root cause

`isTrayEnabled` hard-excluded every non-macOS platform, while `window-all-closed` treated Linux like Windows regardless of whether a tray existed.

## Fix

- enable the existing tray controller on Linux in development and packaged builds
- make last-window quit behavior depend on whether Linux actually created a tray controller
- catch native `Tray` construction failures, report them, and retain the prior quit behavior instead of leaving an inaccessible background process
- preserve the existing macOS release gate and Windows close behavior

Electron documents StatusNotifierItem with GtkStatusIcon fallback on Linux: https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/tray/#platform-considerations

## Safety

- Linux stays resident only after successful native tray construction
- a missing icon, empty native image, or constructor failure leaves the controller null and therefore quits on last-window close
- macOS and Windows policies remain unchanged
- tray session routing and attention-state behavior are untouched

## Tests

- regression state confirmed first: 4 failures before implementation
- `npm test -- src/main/tray-lifecycle.test.ts src/main/tray.test.ts` (31 passed)
- full local `npm run typecheck` produced no diagnostics but did not complete on this resource-constrained Windows host; CI is the authoritative full typecheck

## Manual validation

No live Linux desktop-environment validation was performed here. CI covers the deterministic policy and adapter tests; a maintainer should still smoke-test packaged builds under the supported Linux desktop environments.

title: fix(sessions): keep session teardown off the request path
body:
## The bug

Deleting a session could answer `500 Internal server error` and leave the session half dead: the agent stopped, the worktree half gone, and the row still reading as alive in the sidebar.

Reproduced against a local daemon with a session worktree holding 60,000 ignored files (a `node_modules`-sized tree):

```
POST /api/v1/sessions/repo-4/kill
{"error":"internal","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal server error"}   HTTP 500
daemon: kill repo-4: workspace: gitworktree: worktree prune: context deadline exceeded
```

Two causes, both about teardown running inside the HTTP request:

1. `git worktree remove` unlinks the session's whole directory, and a worker checkout is mostly ignored build output (`node_modules`, `target/`, `.venv`, caches). Measured at roughly 2s per 60,000 files, so a real session took tens of seconds and a large one ran past the daemon's 60s REST cap.
2. `Kill` used the request context. When the cap hit, the sequence was cancelled partway, so the session was already dead everywhere except the row the UI reads.

## The fix

**`gitworktree`** gains a discard path (`discard.go`). `Destroy` applies the checks git would have applied (registered, unlocked, clean), moves the directory into `<data>/worktrees/.discarded` with one rename, prunes the registration, and unlinks in the background. Every inconclusive probe falls back to the existing git-driven path, so git stays the authority on refusals and their messages. A refusal found after the move restores the directory, so a dirty worktree is preserved exactly as before. `ForceDestroy` and `forceDestroyPath` take the same path, which also removes the stall from daemon shutdown and orchestrator replacement. Leftovers from a daemon that died mid-unlink are swept at construction.

**`Kill`** runs its teardown on `context.WithoutCancel` under a 90s ceiling: past the 60s REST cap so a teardown that was going to finish still finishes coherently, short enough that a wedged call cannot hold the session's agent-operation lock for minutes.

**Renderer**: the kill mutation awaited a full workspace refetch inside `onSuccess`, and a mutation stays pending until `onSuccess` settles, so the delete control kept spinning for an extra round trip after the daemon was done. It now writes the terminated session into the cached board and refreshes in the background.

## What this does not change

Deleting still archives the session and removes the worktree directory. The session row, its branch and every commit are kept, and restore rebuilds the worktree from the branch. Uncommitted work still blocks removal: the worktree stays on disk and the session archives with `freed: false`. Gitignored files are still not preserved, which is what `git worktree remove` already did.

## Verification

Live, against a daemon on a fresh data dir with the default 60s timeout:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| clean worktree, 60,006 files / 234 MB | `200` in **0.635s** (was `500` at the cap), `freed: true`, path gone on return |
| disk reclaimed | `.discarded` empty within seconds, data dir back to 4.8 MB |
| session after delete | `terminated`, column `archive`, branch retained |
| commit made in the session | `6902ecf agent work` still on `ao/repo-1/root` |
| restore from archive | worktree rebuilt, `kept.txt` and the commit back |
| worktree with uncommitted work | delete refused, `wip.txt` intact, session still archived |

Checks: `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean; `golangci-lint` 0 issues; `-race` clean on the workspace adapters and the kill path (this change adds a goroutine); frontend `typecheck` clean; renderer session suites pass. Four `TestSpawn_*` failures in `session_manager` are environmental (no tmux on the test machine) and fail identically on the base commit.

New regression tests, each confirmed to fail without its fix: the discard fast path and its dirty refusal, the post-prune rollback hazard, `ForceDestroy` taking the fast path (asserted on the git calls, not just the end state, since the end state looks identical either way), the discard sweep, `Kill` completing after caller cancellation, and the renderer mutation settling without the refetch.


---

## Second cause, added after testing against real data

A session can also fail to delete **permanently**, which is what the reporter was actually hitting: one session had been sitting in the sidebar for two hours with `Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR)` pinned to its trash icon.

Teardown runs every git command as `git -C <project repo> ...`. When the project folder is deleted from disk (here `/Users/psudokit/zero_to_one`, still registered, 14 live sessions), each one exits 128 with `cannot change to ...: No such file or directory`, so `Kill` fails, the row never terminates, and retrying can never help. Reproduced on a live daemon by deleting a registered project's directory and then deleting one of its sessions:

```
kill repo-3: workspace: gitworktree: worktree prune:
  git -C /tmp/ao58f/repo worktree prune: exit status 128:
  fatal: cannot change to '/tmp/ao58f/repo': No such file or directory
```

Teardown now reports an unreachable repository as `ports.ErrWorkspaceRepoUnavailable` and treats it the way an uncommitted worktree is already treated: the directory is left alone, the session terminates, kill answers `freed=false`. Deleting a session has to let it leave the sidebar whether or not the worktree can be reclaimed. `ao session cleanup` reports it with an actionable reason instead of the generic teardown failure.

## Verified in the desktop app

Ran this branch's Electron build against an isolated data dir seeded with both failure shapes, including sessions in two real repos:

| session | condition | result |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha-3` | project folder deleted mid-flight | `200`, archived, worktree preserved |
| `8x-bookmark-2` | 238 MB / 60,350 files in a real repo | `200`, archived, worktree removed |
| `beta-4` / `armor-iq-3` | uncommitted file present | archived, file intact |

One number worth stating plainly: with a live agent still running, delete takes ~5.6s end to end. None of that is the worktree any more; it is the tmux reap grace waiting for the agent's child processes to exit after SIGTERM. That path is untouched here and is a candidate for the same treatment.

title: feat: import existing Claude Code and Codex conversations into AO
body:

AO users can import existing Codex and Claude Code conversations without starting an agent. They can either import eligible sessions for one project or search by session title and import one result. title: fix(desktop): bound stalled update downloads
body:
Fixes #4461

## Problem

A macOS update download could stop receiving bytes while electron-updater kept its request open. AO retained the last `downloading` percentage indefinitely, kept the updater operation queue occupied, and offered no retryable terminal state.

## Root cause

AO forwarded `download-progress`, `update-downloaded`, and `error` events, but never bounded the time between real byte/percentage advances. Automatic downloads expose a provider-owned cancellation token, and manual downloads can receive one, but neither path used it.

## Fix

- add a two-minute inactivity watchdog shared by automatic and manual downloads
- reset the deadline only when transferred bytes or percentage actually advances
- capture progress emitted before `checkForUpdates()` returns its download promise
- cancel the exact electron-updater token when the deadline expires
- publish a terminal error with existing Check Again recovery in Settings
- preserve serialized request ownership so a queued retry starts only after cancellation releases the first operation
- suppress late progress/downloaded events from the cancelled attempt until a new download owns the stream
- report safe stall telemetry with target version, transferred bytes, total bytes, and inactivity duration

## Safety

- does not start a concurrent replacement download
- does not mutate or delete the updater cache directly
- keeps automatic/manual request ownership intact
- timer is cleared on every success, rejection, or cancellation path and is unref'd
- ordinary updater errors and staged-update behavior remain unchanged
- raw updater errors, URLs, and paths remain excluded from telemetry

## Tests

Passed locally:

- `npm test -- src/main/auto-updater.test.ts -t '^(?!.*(?:shows an actionable dialog instead of installing|shows the dialog when the app bundle|shows the dialog when the enclosing directory|disables install-on-quit)).*$'` (64 passed, 4 host-incompatible macOS-only cases skipped)
- `npm test -- src/shared/update-telemetry.test.ts src/renderer/lib/telemetry.test.ts` (55 passed)
- focused watchdog/telemetry regression run (5 passed)
- `git diff --check`

The four excluded install-location cases fail unchanged on an untouched pre-branch worktree on Windows because they exercise macOS bundle/translocation behavior.

`npm run typecheck` reached only existing workspace dependency-resolution failures in the shared junction (`@electron-forge/plugin-auto-unpack-natives` and product-ui React packages); it reported no changed-file diagnostic. Clean CI is the authoritative complete typecheck.

## Manual validation

No live stalled macOS provider transfer was induced. Coverage is deterministic fake-timer/provider-event verification of the real electron-updater token and event ordering.

title: fix(review): prevent Claude reviewer permission stalls
body:
Fixes #4810

## Problem

Claude Code 2.1.257+ can route commands that its Bash analyzer cannot prove safe to an interactive permission prompt before AO's allow rules settle the request. The Claude reviewer is unattended, so a prompt can park the review forever and prevent its GitHub review or AO verdict bookkeeping from completing.

## Root cause

AO launched the restricted Claude reviewer in `auto` mode and relied on broad command allow rules, including blanket `Bash(gh:*)`. The review protocol also embedded arbitrary review JSON directly in `printf` operands. Newer Claude analyzers can reject that content shape before an allow rule prevents the prompt. The reviewer correctly prohibited file writes, leaving no safe payload-file fallback.

## Fix

- add an internal, launch-only `deny-unapproved` policy and map it to Claude's native `dontAsk` mode
- use that policy for fresh and restored Claude reviewer sessions, so unknown/unparseable actions are denied instead of opening an unattended prompt
- tell Claude reviewers to base64-encode reporting JSON and decode it in the existing pipe, keeping payloads off disk and out of analyzer-sensitive shell operands
- allow only the two base64 decode forms needed by Linux/macOS
- replace blanket `gh` access with the required `gh api --method POST repos/...` review-post path
- explicitly deny `gh pr merge`, destructive API methods, and gist access as defense in depth
- preserve both the GitHub review and `ao review submit` bookkeeping channels

## Safety

- reviewer file-edit tools remain denied
- no temporary-file or worktree write permission is added
- commands outside the allowlist fail closed without interaction
- reviewer restore reapplies the same policy
- the project/user permission vocabulary is unchanged; the new policy is internal-only
- other reviewer harnesses and ordinary Claude worker sessions are unchanged

## Tests

Passed:

- `go test ./pkg/agentruntime ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode ./internal/adapters/reviewer/claudecode`
- `go vet ./pkg/agentruntime ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode ./internal/adapters/reviewer/claudecode`

A broader reviewer-adapter run reached the unchanged host-dependent suites, where unrelated Windows tests require locally installed reviewer binaries or Unix permission semantics. Every changed package passed in that run. CI is the authoritative broad check.

## Validation boundary

This is deterministic command/policy coverage plus verification against current official Claude Code permission and hook documentation. Claude Code is not installed on this host, so no live-provider review cycle is claimed.

title: [Bug]: Codex Auto permission launches on-request and still asks for approval
body:
## Summary

AO v0.12.10 resolves a project and role permission value of Auto, but both Codex launch paths translate that value to on-request approval. Codex workers therefore stop in needs_input on ordinary commands even though the AO UI and API show Auto. This makes unattended orchestration hang.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a project worker as Codex with permissions set to Auto.
2. Save the project, restart AO, and confirm the project API still returns permissions: auto for the project and worker role.
3. Spawn a Codex worker in TUI mode or Chat mode.
4. Ask the worker to run an ordinary read-only command such as gh pr view.
5. Inspect the launched Codex process arguments for TUI, or the thread/start parameters for Chat.

The problem reproduced across multiple Codex workers. A TUI worker can sometimes edit inside its trusted worktree, but network commands can still request approval. Chat workers entered needs_input on their first command.

## Expected behavior

Auto should be a genuinely unattended mode: Codex receives approval policy never, does not present per-command approval prompts, and can complete a local write/test flow plus a read-only GitHub CLI command without entering needs_input.

If Auto is intentionally not unattended, the setting must be renamed and a separate Never ask mode must be exposed and persisted consistently in the UI, API, and spawned session.

## Actual behavior

The TUI launch path emits:

    --ask-for-approval on-request -c approvals_reviewer="auto_review"

The Chat/app-server path sends:

    approvalPolicy: on-request
    sandbox: workspace-write

This happens even when the resolved AO configuration is Auto.

The mapping is visible in the v0.12.10 source:

- https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.12.10/backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go#L187-L196
- https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.12.10/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/driver.go#L375-L392

The tests currently encode on-request for Auto, so this appears to be a semantic mapping defect rather than a stale display value.

## AO version

AO Desktop v0.12.10. The local CLI reports ao version dev.

## Environment

macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64; Codex CLI 0.146.0. Reproduced with Codex GPT-5.6 Terra workers. The same project uses GPT-5.6 Sol for the orchestrator.

## Acceptance criteria

- Saved project and role Auto values reach the spawned session.
- TUI and Chat map unattended Auto to Codex approval policy never.
- Auto suppresses command approval prompts without using dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox as a workaround.
- UI, API, and effective launch values agree after restart.
- A spawned worker completes a read-only gh command and a local write/test flow without needs_input.
- Tests cover both Codex launch paths and fail if Auto regresses to on-request.

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and pull requests for duplicates.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, credential values, or private telemetry are included.

title: [Bug]: mobile "Switch to Chat" stays unavailable on a new session until you leave the screen and come back
body:
### Summary

Tap the chat icon on a freshly spawned claude-code TUI session and I get "Chat unavailable" with the daemon's Go error. The daemon clears that state after ~1.3s, but the app only fetches the status once, so the button stays dead until I leave the screen and come back.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Spawn a claude-code worker with `mode: tui`.
2. Open it on the phone immediately.
3. Tap the chat icon.
4. Back out to the board, reopen the session, tap again.

### Expected behavior

Button enables itself once the daemon is ready, same as desktop.

### Actual behavior

Step 3:

```
Chat unavailable

session: native conversation id is not confirmed for the current
terminal launch for claude-code
```

Step 4 works.

Daemon side is fine. It returns `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` until the session-start hook lands, then flips to supported. Across four spawns that took 1.2s to 1.4s.

App side, on `d6350bc47`:

- `packages/mobile/lib/session/useInterfaceTransition.ts:54-56` fetches once on mount.
- `:58-62` only starts an interval when `interfaceTransitionPollInterval(status?.transition)` returns a number, and `packages/mobile/lib/session/interfaceTransition.ts:23-25` returns one only while a transition is already active. Readiness codes get nothing.
- `packages/mobile/lib/session/TerminalSessionScreen.tsx:1022-1030` alerts with `status?.reason`, which is the raw Go error.

I patched `fetch` in the running app to count requests: one status call at t+0.2s, none after. Daemon flipped at t+1.3s.

Desktop already solves this. `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts:167-177` refetches every 1000ms while the reason code is `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` or `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED`. That went in for #3753, which is this bug on desktop. Mobile never got it.

I have a patch: same readiness poll, one refresh on tap before alerting, plain-language copy for the two readiness codes, plus tests. Can open a PR.

### AO version

0.12.11-nightly.202609011721 (packaged app); mobile built from origin/main d6350bc47

### Environment

macOS 26.5 arm64, iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5, Expo dev build, Node 22

### Logs / extra context

```shell
$ curl -s $AO/sessions/$ID/interface-transition
t+0.1s {"supported":false,"targetMode":"chat","reasonCode":"NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED"}
t+1.3s {"supported":true,"targetMode":"chat"}

app fetches, origin/main: 1  (t+0.2s, the unverified answer)
app fetches, patched:     2  (unverified, supported, then stops)
```

### Before submitting

- [X] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [X] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: [Bug]: interface-transition status reports supported while POST returns 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
body:
### Summary

On a claude-code TUI session that has not been prompted, `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interface-transition` returns `supported: true` while `POST` to the same path returns 409 `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`. The status does not change after the failure, so a client draws an enabled control that can never succeed.

### Steps to reproduce

```
AO=http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1

ID=$(curl -s -X POST $AO/sessions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"projectId":"scratch","harness":"claude-code","kind":"worker","mode":"tui"}' \
  | jq -r .session.id)

# send it nothing, then:
curl -s $AO/sessions/$ID/interface-transition
curl -s -X POST $AO/sessions/$ID/interface-transition \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"targetMode":"chat","policy":"drain"}'
```

### Expected behavior

The two agree. Either the status reports the session as not switchable until it is, or the start succeeds.

### Actual behavior

```
GET  {"supported":true,"targetMode":"chat"}
POST 409 {"error":"conflict","code":"NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING",
          "message":"The agent has not exposed a native conversation
                     that can resume in the other interface"}
```

Six rounds over 25s, same both ways every time, and the GET still says supported after each 409. Not a race with the session-start hook.

Where the two paths differ, on `d6350bc47`:

- The status handler resolves the id with `nativeConversationID` only, `backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go:97`.
- `StartInterfaceTransition` calls that at `:160`, then `persistedNativeConversationID` at `:164`, which asks the adapter whether the provider transcript exists. Claude Code does not write the JSONL until the conversation has content, so it does not.
- `nativeConversationNotStarted` at `:542` would allow a fresh handoff, but returns early at `:550` because `NativeTranscriptPath` is already set by the hook. Path set, file absent.

I know the split is partly deliberate. The doc comment on `InterfaceTransitionStatus` says "Read-only: target binary/auth checks happen on POST so a status render never launches a provider process." That reasoning covers binary and auth probes. The transcript check is a file stat on the source side and launches nothing, so it could run in the status path without breaking that rule. Alternatively the status could surface it as a distinct not-ready reason so clients can disable the control.

Session row while it was failing: `agent_session_id` set, `runtime_launch_id` == `agent_session_id_launch_id`, `latest_user_prompt` empty, `native_transcript_path` set, and that file missing on disk.

Send the session one prompt and both paths agree.

Not the same as #4122 (unverified after a `--resume` relaunch, where the status correctly reports unsupported) or #4681 (`TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` further along in the chat controller), but the same area.

### AO version

0.12.11-nightly.202609011721 (packaged app); daemon from origin/main d6350bc47

### Environment

macOS 26.5 arm64, Go 1.25

### Logs / extra context

```shell
round 0  GET supported=True | POST 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
round 1  GET supported=True | POST 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
round 2  GET supported=True | POST 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
round 3  GET supported=True | POST 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
round 4  GET supported=True | POST 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
round 5  GET supported=True | POST 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING
after 25s of failures, GET still: {"supported": true, "targetMode": "chat"}
```

title: [Bug]: mobile board hides every session when the saved project filter points at a project that no longer exists
body:
### Summary

`ao.activeProject` is restored from AsyncStorage and never checked against the projects the connected daemon reports. If that project is gone, the board filters every session out, Settings reports "All projects", and the spawn sheet 404s. With one project left there is no switcher, so nothing in the app can clear it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register two projects so the project switcher appears on the board.
2. On the phone, set the active project to the second one.
3. `ao project rm <that-id> -y` on the desktop.
4. Open the Agents tab.

Also reproduces by pointing the app at a second machine whose projects differ. That is how I hit it first.

### Expected behavior

An unknown id falls back to all projects. Failing that, the empty state says the board is filtered and offers a way to clear it.

### Actual behavior

Board: "No active agents / Spawn a worker to put your fleet to work", with three sessions running on the daemon.

Settings > Active project: **All projects**. It is not all projects.

New agent: opens on "Choose a project", and shows `404 not found - Unknown project` under the task field. The dead id goes out in both `GET /projects/{id}` and `GET /agents/{harness}/models?projectId=`.

No way out inside the app. I cleared storage.

On `d6350bc47`:

- `packages/mobile/lib/store.tsx:186-188` restores the value with no validation against `projects`.
- `packages/mobile/lib/ProjectSwitcher.tsx:24` returns null below two projects, so the control that would fix it is hidden exactly when you need it.
- `packages/mobile/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:81` falls back to "All projects" on a lookup miss.
- `packages/mobile/app/spawn.tsx:131` and `:153` pass the id straight through.

Simulator only, not tried on a physical device, but nothing here looks device-specific.

macOS 26.5 arm64, iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5, Expo dev build

title: [Bug]: mobile shows "Session not found" for a session the daemon returns
body:
### Summary

The mobile session screen resolves an id from the board's cached lists only, with no fallback fetch. Anything not in those lists shows "Session not found" while `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}` returns it. Older orchestrators are never in the lists, and `needs_input` notifications navigate to this route.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Restart a project orchestrator so the project has more than one.
2. Open the older orchestrator on the phone at `/session/<id>`.

I navigated to the route directly rather than waiting for a matching notification to arrive. `packages/mobile/lib/notificationView.ts:34-36` sends `needs_input` there, so a stale notification lands in the same place.

### Expected behavior

Fetch the session on a cache miss. If it comes back terminated, say that instead of "not found".

### Actual behavior

"Session not found." The daemon returns the same id as `kind: orchestrator`, `isTerminated: true`.

On `d6350bc47`:

- `packages/mobile/lib/api.ts:398-403` keeps one orchestrator per project, preferring a live one and otherwise the newest. Every earlier orchestrator is dropped before the screen ever sees it.
- `packages/mobile/app/session/[id].tsx:20` looks only in the store's `sessions` and `orchestrators`. Its refresh refetches the same filtered lists, so waiting does not help.

title: [Bug]: mobile mergePR posts no request body, so the call can only 400
body:
### Summary

`mergePR` in `packages/mobile/lib/api.ts:773-775` posts to `/api/v1/prs/{id}/merge` with no request body. The endpoint requires `prUrl` and `expectedHeadSha`, so the call can only return 400. Nothing calls it today, so it is latent, but it will bite whoever adds a merge button.

### Steps to reproduce

```
# exactly what the helper sends
curl -i -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/prs/2/merge
```

### Expected behavior

The helper sends a `MergePRRequest`, or it is removed until something needs it.

### Actual behavior

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"bad_request","code":"INVALID_JSON","message":"Invalid JSON body"}
```

The store wraps this in a `merge` action (`packages/mobile/lib/store.tsx:454-461`) that also has no caller, so both are dead code right now.

Worth knowing before someone wires a button to it: the daemon refuses to merge unless CI is passing and a review is approved. `MergeReadiness.ReadyToMerge` in `backend/internal/domain/pr.go:226-238` treats unknown CI as not ready. I hit that on a test repo with no checks at all. The PR card in the app read Mergeable, and a correctly formed merge call came back 422 `PR_PRECONDITIONS_UNMET`. So a merge button needs a disabled state with a reason, not a request that fails.

### AO version

0.12.11-nightly.202609011721 (packaged app); mobile from origin/main d6350bc47

macOS 26.5 arm64

```shell
$ curl -i -s -X POST $AO/prs/2/merge
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"bad_request","code":"INVALID_JSON","message":"Invalid JSON body"}

# correctly formed, on a repo with no CI checks:
$ curl -s -X POST $AO/prs/2/merge -H 'content-type: application/json' \
```

title: [Bug]: notification titles read as broken sentences when the session name is truncated
body:
### Summary

A delegated worker's display name is the task brief cut at 20 runes with no ellipsis, and the notification template splices it straight into a sentence with nothing marking where the name ends. The result reads as broken English rather than as a name plus a message.

I spawned a worker with the brief `build a function for palindrome number`. Twenty runes lands exactly on `build a function for`, and `"%s needs your input"` turns that into `build a function for needs your input`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Spawn a worker with a brief whose first 20 characters end mid-phrase, e.g. `build a function for palindrome number`.
2. Let it stop for input.
3. Open notifications, desktop or mobile.

### Expected behavior

A title that reads as a sentence. Quoting the name would do it, or cutting on a word boundary with an ellipsis.

### Actual behavior

```
Title: build a function for needs your input
Body:  Your agent is waiting on you to continue.
```

Straight from the daemon's tables, so the split is unambiguous:

```
sessions.prompt        = 'build a function for palindrome number'
sessions.display_name  = 'build a function for'   (20 runes, hard cut)
notifications.title    = 'build a function for needs your input'
```

The same session now reads `Palindrome number fn needs your input` after the orchestrator renamed it, which is what the template is supposed to produce.

`delegatedTaskDisplayName` in `backend/internal/service/session/delegation.go:164-173` does the hard 20-rune cut. `backend/internal/notify/enrich.go:36` builds `"%s needs your input"` from whatever came out, via `sessionLabel` at `:82-90`.

Nearby but not the same: #3033 is this template with a session id rather than a display name, and #3912 covers the truncation scoped to the sidebar. Neither open PR fixes it either. #4267 adds a second template on the same helper (`"%s finished its turn"`), and #4490 keeps the 20-rune provisional name.
