title: fix(ui): put the caret where you have to type
body:
Three defects with one symptom: the caret is not where you have to type, so you click before you can start.

## 1. A TUI session never focused its terminal

Opening a `mode=tui` session, or switching between two of them, left focus on the sidebar button that was clicked. Keystrokes were dropped entirely until you clicked into the terminal. This is the one that bites hardest, since most worker sessions are TUI.

In `CenterPane`, `presentation` is the *agent-switch* presentation and is `undefined` unless a switch is in flight, so this only ever fired mid-switch:

```jsx
focusRequested={target.kind === "shell" ||
  (target.kind === "worker" &&
    (Boolean(presentation?.allowSourceInput) || Boolean(displayedSuccessNotice)))}
```

A terminal you can type into now holds the caret as soon as it is on screen, the same as the chat composer. Worker input is still left alone while it is genuinely disabled, during an interface transition, a locked agent switch, or an open handoff dialog, which is the condition that already marks the surface `inert`.

## 2. New task opened from a menu had no caret in the prompt

Opening **New task** from the sidebar project menu (dropdown or right-click) left the composer prompt empty of focus, while the board's New task button worked, which is why it looked intermittent. The composer was autofocusing correctly; a closing Radix menu took the caret back, twice:

1. **The menu still traps focus during the commit in which it closes.** `onSelect` opens the dialog and closes the menu in the same React commit, so when the textarea's `autoFocus` fires, the menu's `focusin` trap is still attached and pulls focus back into the menu.
2. **FocusScope restores focus to the menu trigger a tick after the menu unmounts** (it defers through `setTimeout`), landing on top of the already-open dialog.

`useOverlayAutoFocus` (new, in `packages/product-ui`) claims focus from an effect and re-asserts for two frames while focus sits *outside the field's overlay*, so a user who deliberately tabs to the agent picker keeps it. This replaces the `autoFocus` attribute, which loses the race in step 1.

`menu-focus.ts` (new), wired into the shared `DropdownMenuContent` and `ContextMenuContent`, skips the trigger restore when another surface already holds focus. A menu that closes without opening anything leaves focus on `document.body`, so Escape and ordinary item selection keep Radix's normal return-to-trigger behaviour that keyboard users rely on.

## 3. Closing a menu-opened dialog stranded focus on `document.body`

Skipping the restore is not sufficient on its own: the dialog cannot hand focus back afterwards, because Radix captured its return target when the dialog mounted and that was the menu item, which no longer exists. So the menu records where focus should return to while it is open (the trigger for a dropdown, the previously focused element for a context menu, the same targets Radix itself would use) and hands it back once the surface that borrowed the caret releases it.

The menu change is in the shared components, so it applies to every menu. That caught a second real bug: the **Switch agent** dialog opened from the Session actions menu used to leave focus on the trigger behind it, so the next Tab escaped the dialog entirely.

## Known consequence off macOS

The command palette deliberately hands plain `Ctrl+K` to a focused terminal so readline's kill-to-end-of-line keeps working (`CommandPalette.tsx`). Because the terminal now holds focus from the moment a session opens, that rule applies immediately rather than only after the user clicks into the terminal. Net effect on Windows and Linux: `Ctrl+K` right after opening a session goes to the terminal, and the palette opens once focus is anywhere else. macOS is unaffected, since it uses `Cmd+K`.

This follows the existing documented intent, but it is a real change in default behaviour and a reviewer may want to weigh it. Both halves are pinned by tests.

## How to test

```
cd frontend
npx playwright test e2e/session-terminal-focus.spec.ts e2e/new-task-focus.spec.ts e2e/cross-platform-focus.spec.ts
```

By hand: open a TUI session and type without clicking; switch to another session and type again. Then open a project's `...` menu in the sidebar, choose New session, type without clicking, and press Escape to confirm focus returns to the `...` button. Same via right-click, and via Session actions > Switch agent.

## Verification

20 e2e cases across three new specs, each confirmed red before the fix and green after. Each of the four mechanisms was reverted individually to check that the tests that should fail do.

- TUI: caret in the terminal on open, after switching, and after switching back, with each session receiving only its own keystrokes.
- New task from the board button, sidebar dropdown, sidebar right-click, and the command palette: all take typed text with no click.
- The sidebar-menu cases run with and without reduced motion, because the menu's exit animation decides whether Radix's deferred restore lands before or after the dialog mounts.
- Escape out of a menu-opened dialog returns focus to the menu trigger, not `document.body`.
- Switch agent keeps focus inside the dialog and returns it to Session actions on close.
- Switching sessions focuses the chat composer (already correct, covered to keep it that way).

Also on this branch: renderer and product-ui unit suites, the full Playwright suite (53 passing), and `tsc --noEmit` for `frontend`, `packages/product-ui`, and `tsconfig.e2e.json`.

## Cross-platform

Developed and hand-verified on macOS only. Two things mitigate that:

- CI runs the renderer unit suite and the `@T0/@P0` e2e gate on `ubuntu-latest`, and every new test here is tagged `@T0`, so Linux coverage is real rather than assumed.
- `e2e/cross-platform-focus.spec.ts` fakes the platform and runs the terminal-switch and menu flows as macOS, Windows and Linux, plus the `Ctrl+K` behaviour above. Note that `isMacPlatform()` reads `navigator.userAgent` as well as `navigator.platform`, so the fake overrides `platform`, `userAgent` and `userAgentData` together. Overriding only `platform` silently keeps the macOS branch on a macOS machine.

What that does **not** cover: a real Windows or Linux Electron build. The changes are renderer-only and Electron ships the same Chromium on all three, and none of the touched code branches on the OS, but no packaged non-macOS app was launched.

## Risks

- The shared menu change touches every dropdown and context menu in the renderer. Existing `onCloseAutoFocus` callers (`DiffSelectionMenu`, `XtermTerminal`, the settings option menus) are unaffected: they either already `preventDefault` or only do so on pointer closes, and the guard short-circuits on an already-prevented event.
- The two-frame re-assert in `useOverlayAutoFocus` is a race against a closing menu's focus trap. It only reclaims focus while focus is outside the overlay, so it cannot fight a user who moved to another control in the dialog.

title: bug(desktop): topbar tab strip renders overlapping unreadable text after TUI → Chat switch (finish-work/drain)
body:
## Bug

After switching from Terminal UI to Chat UI with the **"Finish work, then switch"** (drain) policy, the session topbar strip renders multiple overlapping UI layers — the tab labels, the "Browser" action area, and the interface-switch status pill ("… Cancel") paint on top of each other and the text is unreadable.

![Screenshot: overlapping tab text in the topbar after a TUI→Chat drain switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-tui-chat-tab-overlap/.issue-assets/tui-chat-tab-overlap/tui-chat-tab-overlap.png)

**Source:** Discord #bug-triage thread ([message](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1544981986949595216)) | **Reported by:** @Dhruv Sharma (Dhruv#0, AO Discord) | **Analyzed against:** `d6350bc47` (origin/main, 2026-09-03)
**Confidence:** High on the overlap mechanism (two independent headers portal into the same host and can render concurrently); Medium on the exact render-order race.
**Priority:** medium — feature degraded but readable after re-render/navigation; no data loss. (No `P3` label exists; body-stated per repo convention.)

## Reproduction

1. Open a session running in Terminal UI with an agent turn in flight (busy state — this is what triggers the policy dialog).
2. Click the interface-switch button and choose **Finish work, then switch** (policy `drain`).
3. Watch the topbar during the `draining → target_starting → activating` phases and immediately after completion.

The strip shows stacked/overlaid fragments — in the reporter's crop: what looks like "…hat UI" (session tab), "Browse…" (browser/inspector action label), "Cancel…" (the switch pill's Cancel button) all composited in the same ~24px row, with the chat composer's "Tip: New Use /fast to enable …" hint visible directly below the strip.

## Root Cause

The session topbar is a **single portal host** shared by two mutually-exclusive surfaces, and during/after a drain switch the ownership handoff races:

1. **Both headers portal into the same host.**
   - Terminal topbar: `CenterPane.tsx:632` — `{isFullscreen ? terminalTopbar : <SessionTopbarPortal>{terminalTopbar}</SessionTopbarPortal>}`
   - Chat header: `ChatWorkspace.tsx:1076` — `return inline ? header : <SessionTopbarPortal>{header}</SessionTopbarPortal>;`
   - Host: `SessionTopbarHost` at `SessionView.tsx:825` (`data-testid="session-topbar-host"`). The portal host is a plain `<div>` whose children are **appended**, not replaced — `SessionTopbarPortal.tsx:40` does `createPortal(children, context.host)`. If two portaled headers are alive in the same commit, both mount side-by-side/overlaid inside the same host row with no reconciliation between them.

2. **The surface swap is keyed on `session.mode`, which flips independently of the transition lifecycle.**
   - `SessionView.tsx:627-629`: `showChatSurface = session?.mode === "chat" && …`. When the backend commits the mode change (before the transition reaches `completed` and while `SessionInterfaceSwitchButton` is still rendering the active-transition pill with Cancel), React swaps `CenterPane` → `SessionChatSurface` in one commit: the old terminal topbar unmounts and the chat header mounts **into the same host** in the same render pass, while the switch pill (`SessionInterfaceSwitchButton`, rendered from `SessionView.tsx:528` into the header actions region) is still visible.

3. **Both headers also pin their tab-region width to a measured pixel width**, which can be stale across the swap:
   - `CenterPane.tsx:534-536`: `style={{ width: terminalBounds.width > 0 ? terminalBounds.width : "100%" }}`
   - `ChatWorkspace.tsx:987`: `style={{ width: topbarBounds.width > 0 ? topbarBounds.width : "100%" }}`
   If the measured width persists across the surface swap while the action-region content changes (switch pill + browser label), the tab strip and the trailing action region are laid out to overlap rather than flex apart.

The result is exactly the reported crop: tab label + "Browser…" + "…Cancel" text drawn over each other in one row, with the chat surface (and its composer tip) underneath.

## Fix

- Make the portal host **own exactly one child**: on mount, a `SessionTopbarPortal` should clear any previous portal content (e.g. keyed single-child slot in `SessionTopbarHost`, or an effect that removes stale portaled nodes), so two surfaces can never composite in the same row.
- Alternatively/additionally, gate the switch pill and the header swap on the same lifecycle flag: don't unmount `CenterPane`'s topbar until `interfaceSwitch.transition.phase === "completed"` (or render the chat header only after `settling` is false), so the handoff is sequential rather than concurrent.
- Re-measure (or reset to `width: "100%"`) when the surface identity changes rather than reusing the previous surface's measured bounds.

## Impact

- Topbar unreadable after every TUI→Chat drain switch when it reproduces; user can recover by switching sessions back and forth or resizing (forces re-render/re-measure), but nothing tells them that.
- Keyboard/AT users get a tablist (`role="tablist"`) whose tab labels are visually merged — the a11y tree has two overlapping tab strips.

## Related

- [#3939](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3939) / [PR #4008](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4008) — Chat surface replacing CenterPane hid reviewer/shell tabs; the shared-host topbar architecture this bug rides on came out of that fix.
- [#4062](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4062) — same visual class (ghosted overlapping topbar chrome), different root cause (titlebar clearance tokens).
- [#4422](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4422) — also tracks behavior across interface switches (draft persistence).

title: fix(updates): repair the desktop update path and rebuild the Updates UI
body:
Supersedes #4548, and overlaps #4633 / #4832 (see *Relationship to open PRs* below).

## Why

The Updates page was unreliable in ways that compounded: a background loop nobody could see, a check button that swallowed clicks, and a layout that fell apart in exactly the states that matter. Each section below is a separate defect with its own regression test.

### 1. The updater re-staged an already-staged build on every check

electron-updater does not treat "already in the cache" as done. On a cache hit `executeDownload` still runs the download task's completion path, and `MacUpdater` uses that path to copy the whole zip to `update.zip` and hand Squirrel a fresh install request. With `autoDownload` left on, that repeated for as long as the user went without quitting.

Measured on a real nightly install (`0.12.11-nightly.202609011721`, with `0.12.11-nightly.202609021713` staged since Sep 2 23:04):

- `ShipIt_stderr.log` recorded a Squirrel install request **every 15 minutes** — the nightly check interval — 41 on Sep 1, 36 on Sep 2, **526 in total, against 10 actual installs since Jul 4**.
- Watched across a cycle boundary: `update.zip` was rewritten in full (174,750,820 bytes) at 02:48:52 while `pending/*.zip` stayed frozen at its Sep 2 mtime, and ShipIt logged the next install request at 02:48:55. No network re-download, but a 175 MB local copy and a full re-stage every 15 minutes.

Auto-download is now suspended for the build already staged. Anything genuinely newer is still fetched.

### 2. The same event killed escalation

`update-downloaded` re-stamped `stagedAtMs` and re-armed the 30-minute escalation timer on every re-stage. The staged clock was never more than one check interval old, so the latest-channel 48-hour rule in `escalation-evaluator.ts` could never fire, and re-arming a 30-minute timer every 15 minutes meant the loop never got a turn.

### 3. Settings hid the only way to check for updates

The check control was not rendered when the state was `available`, `downloading` or `downloaded`. A user sitting on a staged build that would not install had one Restart button and no other action on the page.

### 4. The check button swallowed the first click

It was disabled by any `checking` status, including a background one. Opening Settings during a background check — as often as every 15 minutes on nightly, and the nightly path adds a GitHub API round trip first — rendered it already disabled. It now blocks only on the user's own request, which is safe because updater operations are serialized in the main process.

Two backstops: a watchdog releases a pending request that never settles, and a check that resolves without emitting any event now lands a terminal status. electron-updater returns the in-flight promise when a check is already running, so nothing otherwise moved the status off `checking` — and Settings rendered `checking` as `sr-only`, so the page wedged with a disabled spinner and no visible explanation.

### 5. Switching channel installed the wrong build

Staging is not reversible. `MacUpdater` calls `nativeUpdater.checkForUpdates()` when `autoInstallOnAppQuit` is set, and the resulting ShipIt sits waiting for the app to exit. Clearing `autoInstallOnAppQuit` afterwards does not disarm it: `MacUpdater extends AppUpdater`, and `addQuitHandler` appears **zero times** in `MacUpdater.js` — it exists only in `BaseUpdater` for Windows/Linux. On macOS that flag is read once, at download time, to decide whether to hand the build over.

So nightly staged → user picks Stable → Settings said "Restart to switch to Stable" → the next quit installed the **nightly**. Returning home from a pinned PR build had the same shape.

Each completed download issues a fresh install request that supersedes the last, so staging the right build over the wrong one is the only reliable fix. A staged build whose channel no longer matches is dropped from tracking and **forces** a download on that check, regardless of the automatic-download preference — otherwise a user with automatic updates off could never escape it.

**Known gap:** between the switch and the replacement finishing, the old build is still armed, so a quit in that window still installs it. Nothing in electron-updater or Squirrel.Mac can cancel a staged build once handed over.

### 6. Staged provenance did not survive a restart

`stagedVersion`/`stagedChannel` were module state, so a relaunch that did not install came back knowing nothing about the build still armed in the cache, and a later channel switch could not detect the stranding. Now persisted beside the update settings and reloaded at launch — synchronously, because awaiting a real filesystem read there reordered the launch-check tests.

### 7. The sidebar row blinked out on every check

`UpdateStatusRow` keyed off `state`, which a routine check drives through checking → available → not-available while the staged build is untouched. Every status now carries a `staged` stamp, alongside the existing `staleCheckNudge` and `checksFailing` stamps.

### 8. Restarting quit the app on one click

The sidebar row and Settings called `updates.install()` straight through. That is harmless for sessions that survive a quit and destructive for those that do not, and nothing told the user which they had.

Both now open a confirmation showing the build's release notes and naming the sessions that would actually lose work. Which sessions those are is **not** "all of them":

| Session kind | Survives a quit? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| TUI | Yes | detached tmux/conpty runtime, adopted next boot |
| Chat, Codex provider | Yes | `chatdriver/persistenthost`, which only `codexappserver` uses |
| Chat, any other driver | **No** | daemon-owned process lifetime |

Only that last group is named, and only in `working` or `no_signal`. Warning on every live session would cry wolf on most of them.

Release notes come from `UpdateInfo.releaseNotes`, which AO was discarding. They are the remote release body and routinely contain HTML, so they are stripped to plain text and length-capped **in the main process** rather than forwarded as markup.

### 9. The page read as broken when nothing was wrong

- The version was one heading carrying the whole nightly stamp, so it wrapped mid-token; the primary action carried the full stamp too and grew across it until they overlapped.
- The status area was an absolutely positioned `h-5` strip with a cross-faded "Last checked"; a two-line error overlapped it and the blur left it looking half-rendered.
- `available` had no status line at all — the button was the only clue.
- The nightly note was a red-orange bordered box. It is a standing property of the chosen channel, and `--color-warning` sits one step from `--destructive`, so a permanent note read as a permanent failure. Now muted helper copy with an info icon. **Red now appears in exactly one place at a time**, reserved for failing checks, a wedged network stack, and update errors.
- An earlier revision of this PR added a border and accent fill to the release block. Removed: `--primary` is `oklch(0.92 0.004 286.32)` in dark and near-black in light, both effectively neutral, so it drew a meaningless grey frame.
- "Automatic Updates" reads as "install automatically" but only governs downloading. Both it and "Updates channel" now carry a sub-label. `SettingsRow` gained an optional `description`; rows without one are unchanged.

## Relationship to open PRs

- **#4548** — same channel-switch defect. Its fix clears tracking and sets `autoInstallOnAppQuit = false`, which cannot disarm an already-handed-over build on macOS (see §5). Its persist-across-restart idea was the one thing missing here and is now included as §6. Superseded.
- **#4633** — a real `useUpdateStatus` bug this PR does **not** fix: `getStatus()` is called before `onStatus` is registered and the snapshot is applied unconditionally, so a push in that window is lost and a late snapshot overwrites a newer one. Worth keeping.
- **#4832** — stalled downloads freezing with no retryable terminal state. Not covered here. Worth keeping.
- **#4812** — feature-build feed resolution. No overlap.
- **#4526** (issue) — if native harness processes survive a desktop update, §8's warning narrows further or becomes unnecessary.

## Tests

3005 frontend tests pass. `typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` clean. `playwright test updates-settings` passes.

New coverage: 14 cases in `auto-updater.test.ts`, 5 in `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`, 6 in `update-install-risk.test.ts`, 3 in `build-channel.test.ts`, 3 in `update-telemetry.test.ts`, 2 in `Sidebar.test.tsx`, 2 in `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx`. Every behavioral case was confirmed to fail against the unfixed code.

Two test-infrastructure fixes were needed and are included:
- The Playwright base port is now `AO_E2E_PORT`-overridable. 5173 is not ours alone — another worktree's `electron-forge start` listens there, and with `reuseExistingServer` the suite silently ran against *its* Electron-mode renderer and failed for unrelated reasons.
- `auto-updater.test.ts` gets one fresh state dir per test. The provenance persist is fire-and-forget, so against a shared directory a write from one test could land after the next test's cleanup.

The `updates-settings` e2e spec's `Check for updates` assertion was flipped from `toBeHidden()` to `toBeVisible()` — which also makes the button-height comparison two lines below it coherent, since it had been measuring an element it asserted was absent.

## What is not verified by execution

**The install step itself has never been run.** It needs a packaged, signed build. Everything about Squirrel's behaviour in §5 is read from `electron-updater`'s source plus the ShipIt log on one machine, not executed. The `releaseNotes` in §8 are also unconfirmed end to end: the nightly path uses `setFeedURL({provider: "generic"})`, and the generic provider may not populate that field, in which case the dialog shows its "no release notes" fallback on nightly.

No Sentry data informed any of this — no Sentry connector is configured in this workspace.

title: fix(mobile): poll native-session readiness so Switch to Chat enables itself
body:
## Summary

- A freshly spawned Claude Code TUI session reports `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` until its session-start hook lands, ~1.3s after spawn. Mobile fetched the interface-transition status once on mount and only polled while a transition was already active, so the chat icon stayed unavailable until you left the screen and came back.
- Recheck the two transient readiness codes once a second — same codes and cadence as desktop's `nativeSessionReadinessPoll` (`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts`), added in #3735 and extended to `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` in #3953. Mobile never got it. #3753 is the same bug reported on desktop.
- Refresh once on tap, so a tap landing between two polls does not alert.
- Stop the recheck on a rejected status and keep it on a transient one, reusing `shouldKeepPolling` (`lib/connectionError.ts`) — the rule the board poll already applies. A 1s poll into a rotated password would otherwise arm the bridge's five-failures-per-minute lockout in five seconds and hold it for as long as the screen stayed open. A successful recheck, or the tap-refresh above, resumes it.
- Give the readiness states plain language instead of the daemon's Go error. Every other reason is still passed through.

The Chat screen shares the hook and picks up the poll, but only the Terminal screen re-asks on tap and shows the new copy. `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` — the code a freshly spawned TUI session hits — is TUI-only: `interface_transition.go:526` gates it on `mode == SessionModeTUI`. `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` (`:519`) is not mode-gated, so a Chat session that has not started its provider conversation can sit in the same wait; its menu hint keeps the existing reason text.

Known limitation: on a never-prompted session the status now flips to `supported: true` while the POST still 409s `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`. That is #4842, filed separately; the new copy names the workaround.

Fixes #4841

## Test plan

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (77 files / 710 tests) in `packages/mobile`
- `npx expo export --platform ios` — CI does not bundle, so this is the only local guard against a Metro-level break
- iPhone 17 Pro simulator against a packaged daemon, `fetch` wrapped to count calls: `origin/main` made 1 status call and stopped; patched made 2 (unverified, then supported) and stopped. The chat icon enables itself ~1.3s after spawn without leaving the screen.
- The stop-on-rejection rule reuses `shouldKeepPolling`, covered by `lib/connectionError.test.ts`. This package has no hook-test harness, so that path is not separately exercised in the hook itself.

title: [Bug]: mobile board re-renders every card on every poll tick, even when nothing changed
body:
### Summary

The Agents board redraws on a timer rather than on a change. `getSessions` re-maps the daemon's response into fresh objects on every poll, so `setSessions` installs a new array identity even when the daemon returned exactly what it returned last time. `groupSessions` re-buckets and re-sorts the fleet, the section list rebuilds, and every visible card re-renders.

Measured on a Debug build against a packaged daemon, board idle with two visible cards, counters inside `FleetScreen` and `SessionCard`:

```
90s idle, nothing changing, poll = DIRECT_POLL_MS (8s)

  FleetScreen renders   12
  SessionCard renders   24     (2 cards x 12)
```

Twelve renders for eleven ticks that carried no new data. The card figure scales with what is on screen, and the tunnel path polls four times as often — which is the path where the phone is on battery and cellular.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair a phone and open the Agents tab with a few sessions on the board.
2. Leave it idle — nothing spawning, no agent working.
3. Every poll tick re-renders the board and every visible card.

### Expected behavior

A quiet tick touches nothing. Cards re-render when a session actually changes.

### Actual behavior

On `9f9a0f432`:

- `packages/mobile/lib/store.tsx:294-298` — four of the five setters take freshly mapped objects with no equality guard (`setOrchestratorId` at `:297` takes a string, so it is already stable). Seventy-six lines up, `reloadConfig` at `:218` does the opposite for the config object (`sameServerConfig(prev, c) ? prev : c`) for exactly this reason.
- `packages/mobile/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:39` memoizes `groupSessions` on the array and `:169`'s `renderItem` is inline, so a new array re-renders every visible `SessionCard`.
- `useApp` is plain `useContext` (`store.tsx:93`) and the context value is memoized on that array, so every store consumer re-renders on the tick, not just the board — `app/notifications.tsx:177`'s relative stamps are redrawn by it too.
- `packages/mobile/lib/pollInterval.ts` sets the cadence: `DIRECT_POLL_MS` 8s, `TUNNEL_POLL_MS` 2s.

The daemon's side is stable. Polling `/sessions`, `/orchestrators` and `/projects` twice at 9s apart, and again at 45s apart, against a 12-session fleet returned structurally identical payloads every time — so this is work on a fixed schedule for data that did not move.

Same shape as #1844 (`perf(web): ProjectSidebar re-renders on every SSE tick even when session data is unchanged`), fixed on web in May. Mobile never got it.

I have a patch: keep the previous value when the mapped payload is unchanged, the idiom `reloadConfig` already uses. The same measurement on the patch gives 1 board render and 2 card renders in 90s, which is the relative-timestamp clock rather than the poll. Can open a PR.

### AO version

mobile built from origin/main `9f9a0f432`; packaged daemon 0.12.11-nightly.202609011721

### Environment

macOS 26.5 arm64, iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5, Expo dev build (Debug), Node 22

title: fix(mobile): re-render the board on a change, not on the poll tick
body:
## Summary

- Keep the previous value when the mapped payload matches, the idiom `reloadConfig` already uses for the config object at `store.tsx:218`. New `keepUnchanged.ts` compares structurally — deep rather than a field list, because `DashboardSession` carries two dozen fields plus a nested PR, and a hand-written comparison goes blind to the next field someone adds, which fails the wrong way by dropping a real update.
- `activeEndpoints` was in the context value but missing from its `useMemo` deps. The churn was hiding it: the value object was rebuilt every tick anyway, so a re-raced endpoint list reached consumers by accident. Fixed here rather than left as a landmine, and guarded the same way, since `activeHost()` re-parses storage into a fresh array on every resolve.
- Relative timestamps were riding on that churn. The board and the notifications list now own a one-minute clock (`useNow.ts`) — the coarsest step `relativeTime` takes — instead of redrawing on someone else's schedule.

Deliberately not memoizing `SessionCard` here: the array reuse is the fix, and per-row memo is only worth adding once it has been measured.

Fixes #4853

## Test plan

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (78 files / 717 tests) in `packages/mobile`
- `npx expo export --platform ios` — CI does not bundle, so this is the only local guard against a Metro-level break
- iPhone 17 Pro simulator, Debug build against a packaged daemon, render counters inside `FleetScreen` and `SessionCard`, board left idle for 90s with two cards visible:

  | | FleetScreen | SessionCard |
  |---|---|---|
  | guard bypassed (`main`'s behaviour) | 12 | 24 |
  | with the guard | 1 | 2 |

  The one remaining render is the minute clock, not the poll.
- Guard is not inert: `/sessions`, `/orchestrators` and `/projects` polled twice at 9s apart and again at 45s apart on a 12-session fleet came back structurally identical every time, so a quiet tick really is a no-op.

title: workspacewatch: unbounded directory watches exhaust fd/inotify limits and one failed Add kills the whole watch stream
body:
## Summary

On `main` ([`86c023249`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/86c023249ed8639bbc5ca90bebe777eb288418a7)), `backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go` registers a filesystem watch for **every** directory in a session worktree with no cap, and a single failed registration takes down the entire workspace watch stream.

## What happens

1. **Unbounded watches.** `addInitialDirectories` calls `watcher.Add(dir)` for every directory of the tree (git-tracked dirs when git is available, a full `WalkDir` otherwise), and `addCreatedTree` does the same for every directory created at runtime. fsnotify consumes one descriptor per watched directory (kqueue fd on macOS, inotify slot on Linux), so large worktrees (`node_modules`, build outputs, vendor trees) eventually exhaust `RLIMIT_NOFILE` / `max_user_watches`.

2. **One failed `Add` kills the whole subscription.** In `addInitialDirectories` a failed `watcher.Add` returns an error which aborts `watchRoot`, so `Watch` fails entirely and the SSE model-refresh stream for the session dies — even though a degraded watch (root-only) would keep the stream usable:

   ```go
   // addInitialDirectories
   if err := watcher.Add(dir); err != nil {
       ...
       return fmt.Errorf("watch workspace directory %q: %w", dir, err)
   }
   // watchRoot
   if err := addInitialDirectories(ctx, watcher, root, git); err != nil {
       _ = watcher.Close()
       return nil, err
   }
   ```

3. **Silent coverage gap in created trees.** In `addCreatedTree`, `WalkDir`'s callback returns the `watcher.Add` error, which aborts the walk; the error is discarded at the call site (`_ = addCreatedTree(...)`), so all directories after the first failure in a newly created tree are silently never watched.

## Expected behavior

- Directory watches should be bounded (a cap that both the initial walk and runtime-created trees share), and watches should be released when directories are removed/renamed so the budget is reused under churn.
- Watch failures should degrade (skip the directory, count and log an aggregated warning) instead of failing the whole watch stream.

## Environment

- Analyzed against `main` at `86c023249` (`backend/internal/workspacewatch/watcher.go`).
- Affects all platforms; on Windows there is an additional related defect: `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` returns forward-slash paths, so the `metadataFiles` keys built with `filepath.Join` use mixed separators and never match fsnotify's backslash event names — `.git/HEAD` / `packed-refs` changes (branch switches) do not trigger a refresh on Windows.

## Priority / confidence

P2 (significant degradation: git status/diff invalidation stream dies for large workspaces; workaround is restarting the session or polling manually). Confidence: high — verified by direct code inspection on current `main`.

title: fix(tmux): classify an absent socket file as conclusive server absence
body:
## Summary

- tmux ≥ 3.4 words an absent server `error connecting to <socket> (No such file or directory)` instead of the classic `no server running on <socket>`. Our output classifiers only recognized the old wording, so after a host reboot every liveness probe of a tmux-runtime session returned `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` — forever.
- That dead-ends every recovery path at once: boot reconciliation's `reconcileLive` (explicitly designed for this case — "Normal after a machine reboot: the runtime is conclusively gone" — keyed off `ErrRuntimeUnavailable`) falls into "a failed probe is not proof of death: leave the session as-is"; `kill` 500s inside `Destroy` ([#4481](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4481)); `restore` refuses with `SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` because the session is not terminal. Sessions stay `isTerminated=false`, live-looking but unrecoverable, while the reaper logs inconclusive probes indefinitely ([#4776](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4776), reproduced on macOS 26.6 / tmux 3.6b; the same dead-end also blocks `restart-all`).
- Fix: treat the absent-socket text as what it is — conclusive **server-level** absence, equivalent to `no server running`:
  - `IsAlive` maps it to `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (checked before the transient branch, since the text contains "error connecting");
  - `socketForSession`'s legacy fall-through resolves on it instead of returning inconclusive before `IsAlive` even runs;
  - `migrationSocketAbsentOutput` → `serverSocketAbsentOutput`, since it now describes both the private and the legacy target.
- The [#3475](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3475) safety boundary is preserved: the text is never per-session death evidence — a conclusive per-session miss still requires `can't find session`, `Connection refused` stays inconclusive, and the reaper keeps treating probe errors as failed facts. What changes is that the designed consumers of `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (boot reconcile, `restartRuntime`/restore, `reconcileReap`, idempotent `Destroy`) finally get consulted instead of the loop retrying forever.

## Test

- `go test ./...` (one pre-existing machine-dependent failure in `internal/adapters/agent/crush` that fails on clean `main` as well)
- `go test -race` on `runtime/tmux`, `session_manager`, `lifecycle`, `observe/reaper`; `gofmt -l .` and `go vet` clean
- New/updated tests: absent-socket text → `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (flipped from the old inconclusive expectation, which was written against the pre-3.4 tmux wording); both-sockets-absent reboot case for `IsAlive` (asserts private → legacy → resolved-private probe chain) and idempotent `Destroy`; `Destroy` idempotency for the new wording

Fixes #4776
Fixes #4481

title: workspacewatch: upward git-repo detection leaves nested workspaces with a dead change stream
body:
## Summary

`backend/internal/workspacewatch` can silently produce a **completely dead change stream** whenever the session workspace is located **inside another git repository** (a parent repo above it in the directory tree, including a stray `.git` in the user's home directory). The watcher then registers almost no directory watches, so file changes never invalidate the git status/diff model — with no error surfaced anywhere.

Related: [#4510](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4510) (same file, orthogonal cause — this is not fixed by the limiter work there).

## Root cause

1. `discoverGitWorkspace` detects "is this a git repo" with `git -C <root> rev-parse ...`. **Git searches upward** for a repository, so it can resolve a *parent* repo instead of the workspace (e.g., a stray `C:\Users\<user>\.git`, or any project nested under another repo).
2. `git ls-files` against that parent repo returns **zero tracked files** for the workspace, but `available` is set to `true`.
3. With `git.available == true`, `addInitialDirectories` skips the `WalkDir` fallback entirely and builds the watch set **only from the (empty) git file list**: the root directory plus the *parent* repo's metadata dirs (watched outside the workspace, e.g. `C:\Users\<user>\.git`).
4. fsnotify (`v1.10.1`) is **non-recursive** on Windows (and Linux inotify is always non-recursive), so watching only the root dir sees **no events for any subdirectory**.
5. Additionally, `gitIgnored` runs `git check-ignore` from the workspace, but git resolves the **parent** repo — the parent's `.gitignore` can wrongly drop root-level events too.

## Evidence (reproduced on Windows, commit `86c023249`)

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/workspacewatch/...` fails: `TestWatchReportsExistingAndNewDirectoryChanges` — `timed out waiting for workspace change` (4/4 runs). Green in CI only because CI temp dirs are not nested under a repo.
- Probe: `discoverGitWorkspace(ctx, tmpDir)` on a machine with a stray `~/.git` returns `available=true, files=0`, with `metadataFiles` pointing at `C:\Users\<user>\.git\HEAD` etc.
- Probe: with only the root directory watched (exactly what `addInitialDirectories` registers in this state), writing a file into a watched workspace's subdirectory produced **zero fsnotify events**.
- Probe: `git -C <workspace> rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to the parent (`C:/Users/<user>`), confirming the upward-search mis-detection.

## Expected behavior

Only trust the git-derived watch set when the discovered repository actually belongs to the workspace — e.g. `git -C <root> rev-parse --show-toplevel` must resolve to `root` itself (or the discovered git dir must be inside `root`). Otherwise fall back to the existing `WalkDir`-based watching, which works for non-git and nested workspaces alike.

## Priority / confidence

- **P2**: silent stale-git-model for a realistic layout (workspaces nested under another repo / machines with a stray home-dir `.git`); no crash, no error, just a dead invalidation stream.
- Confidence: high — reproduced locally with package tests and standalone fsnotify probes; root cause confirmed against `main` at `86c023249`.

title: bug(chat): failed provider turn drains queued updates through the same outage
body:
## Bug

A terminal provider failure on a busy Chat conversation causes Agent Orchestrator to dispatch the next durable queued turn immediately. If the provider failure is systemic, each queued turn fails in turn and the entire queue is drained into failed history.

Observed on AO v0.12.10 with a Codex Chat orchestrator during the OpenAI incident on 2026-09-03: https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M1KWEDH417T2CF44YYHZDFCR

The provider returned:

```text
Error running remote compact task: unexpected status 404 Not Found
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

One provider failure became 35 failed AO turns in 83 seconds, including 33 automatic remote-compaction failures. Most were queued automation updates accepted while a long root turn was running. The messages remained in SQLite, but every turn was marked failed and none was processed.

The identical AO controller generation and Codex provider thread later compacted and completed a turn successfully without daemon restart or reauthentication. Other Codex Chat sessions using the same account also completed turns during the interval. Same-day reports reproduced the endpoint 404 across OSes, versions, regions, and brand-new chats: openai/codex#42546 and openai/codex#42555.

## Root cause in AO

On current `main` at c42aab92feb4e4d313e34f5a9ff7375efe853473:

- `drainLocked` deliberately stops when synchronous dispatch fails because the next request likely would fail too. That protects the undispatched remainder of the queue.
- An asynchronous provider failure arrives as `turn/completed` with state `failed`.
- `afterProject` calls `drainLocked` after every primary `ChatEventTurnCompleted`, regardless of terminal state.
- `SendTurn` accepts the next queued message and returns a provider turn ID, so the synchronous guard does not run. When that provider turn asynchronously fails, `afterProject` drains again.

Source:
- https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/c42aab92feb4e4d313e34f5a9ff7375efe853473/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L1390-L1452
- https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/c42aab92feb4e4d313e34f5a9ff7375efe853473/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L2679-L2686

## Minimal deterministic reproduction

Against that exact `main` SHA:

1. Start a turn with the existing fake conversation harness.
2. Queue one automation message while the first turn is running.
3. Emit `ChatEventTurnCompleted` for the first turn with `TurnStateFailed`.
4. Assert that the second turn remains `queued` and the provider received only the first prompt.
5. Repeat with `TurnStateRecovered`. In AO v0.12.10 this proves terminal durable history, not a portable success/failure outcome, so it must also hold the queue.

Current results:

```text
--- FAIL: TestFailedTurnDoesNotDrainQueuedWork
queue after provider failure: second="running", want queued

--- FAIL: TestRecoveredTurnDoesNotDrainQueuedWork
queue after recovered turn: second="running", want queued
```

Each focused command completes in about half a second after compilation.

## Expected

Only a proven `completed` turn may automatically release queued work. A failed, provider-interrupted, or outcome-unknown `recovered` completion must keep queued messages durable, visible, editable, and retryable until explicit recovery.

Intentional Stop semantics must remain intact: apply the existing cancellation cutoff, cancel pre-Stop queue items, and still permit new messages accepted after Stop to dispatch.

This is the same safety shape Codex adopted for disconnected external app-server sessions in openai/codex#41911: preserve drafts and queued input, block automatic replay, and quarantine uncertain work.

## Package-tested proposal

In a throwaway checkout, I tested a `drainLocked` shape that accepts an `allowDispatch` decision:

- `afterProject` passes true only for `completed`.
- Cancellation cutoffs are still applied on failed/interrupted/outcome-unknown completions.
- A cutoff then re-enables dispatch for messages accepted after an intentional Stop.
- Other explicit drain callers preserve current behavior.

Both queue-hold regressions failed before the completed-only decision and passed afterward. The full `backend/internal/service/chat` package passed after accounting for the post-Stop message behavior. This package result narrows the proposal; it is not proof of upstream-wide safety or a shipped fix, and upstream ownership/review remain required:

```text
ok github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/service/chat
```

## Recovery UX still needed

Pausing is safer than destructive replay, but AO should make recovery explicit:

- identify that queued messages were held after a non-success terminal turn;
- offer a deliberate resume/retry after provider health returns;
- never silently duplicate a partially executed or outcome-unknown turn;
- permit operator reconciliation of failed automation turns, which the current human-only `RetryTurn` path rejects.

Local lifecycle intake and redacted evidence: menard-software/setup-agent-orchestrator#290

title: fix(workspacewatch): verify git toplevel belongs to the workspace (#4860)
body:
Closes #4860.

## Summary
- `discoverGitWorkspace` trusted `git rev-parse`, which **searches upward** for a repository. A workspace nested under another repo (worktrees under a repo, projects inside a monorepo, or a machine with a stray `.git` in a parent/home directory) resolved the **parent** repo with an empty file list for the workspace.
- With `available=true` and no files, `addInitialDirectories` registered only the root directory (plus the parent repo's `.git` metadata dirs, outside the workspace), and the non-recursive fsnotify backends (inotify on Linux, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows) never reported subdirectory changes — the invalidation stream died silently.
- The fix: run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first and only use the git-derived watch set when the toplevel **is the workspace root**; otherwise fall back to the existing `WalkDir`-based watching. Added `sameWorkspaceDir` to compare paths (git prints forward slashes on Windows; the FS is case-insensitive there).
- Note: this is orthogonal to [#4510](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4510) (watch-cap/degradation work in the same file); no conflicts expected, and it composes with the limiter once both land.

## Test
- New regression: `TestWatchStillReportsChangesWhenWorkspaceIsNestedInAnotherRepository` — parent repo `git init`, workspace nested inside, write into a subdirectory, expect a change. Fails on all platforms without the fix (inotify is non-recursive too).
- `cd backend; go test -race -count=1 ./internal/workspacewatch/` — all green, including `TestWatchReportsExistingAndNewDirectoryChanges`, which failed 4/4 on a machine with a stray `~/.git` before the fix.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` — clean.

## Reproduction notes
On a machine where `C:\Users\<user>\.git` exists: `git -C <any tmp dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolved `C:/Users/<user>`, so `discoverGitWorkspace` returned `available=true, files=0` with `metadataFiles` pointing at the home-dir `.git`. Root-only fsnotify watch delivered zero events for a write into `src/` (probed directly), matching the package test timeout.

title: fix(desktop): keep the interface-switch pill out of the session tab
body:
## What

Renders the interface-transition status pill in the session topbar's action region instead of passing it into `SessionPaneTab` as a tab action.

## Why

Fixes #4848.

After a TUI → Chat switch, the topbar painted the tab label, the action labels and the switch pill's `Cancel` on top of each other, leaving the strip unreadable.

The cause is not the shared portal host. Tab actions are absolutely positioned over the tab (`TerminalTabFrame`), and the label button reserves only a fixed icon-width gutter (`pr-9`) for them — sized for the overflow-menu trigger that normally sits there.

During a switch, that same slot instead holds the pill: a spinner, the phase copy (`Stopping controller… Chat UI`), and a `Cancel` button, all `whitespace-nowrap`. That is far wider than the reserved gutter, and being absolutely positioned it contributes nothing to layout, so it painted straight over the tab label. The overlap landed in a different place on each attempt because every phase string has a different width.

## How

The pill is session-level status, not a per-tab control, so it moves to `sessionHeaderActions`. That region is a real flex row, so the pill takes space and the tab strip (`shrink` + `min-w-0`) yields and truncates instead of being overdrawn. Both surfaces already route this through `session-action-region` (terminal via `topbarActions`, chat via `headerActions`), so one change covers both.

Side benefit: this moves a `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` element out from inside `role="tablist"`, so the tab strip is no longer announced with a live region nested inside it — one of the accessibility complaints in the issue.

Notes for reviewers:

- The issue's stated root cause (two headers portalling into the same host concurrently) did not reproduce. Instrumenting `SessionTopbarHost` with a `MutationObserver` showed the host's child count never exceeded 1, and the tab and action regions were always exactly adjacent (`[241→1009]` / `[1009→1303]`, `scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0`). The overlap was between `"Orchestrator"` and the pill's own text, inside the tab.
- `SessionActionsMenu`'s `inlineStatus` prop now has no caller. Left in place to keep this diff surgical; happy to remove it here or in a follow-up if preferred.
- In compact chrome the pill does not collapse the way `ShellTopbar`'s labels do. `.session-topbar-surface` is `overflow: hidden`, so a very narrow window clips rather than overlaps.

## Testing

Verified locally on Linux against a real drain switch (`Finish work, then switch`) with an agent turn in flight.

Instrumented the host to log geometry and flag any two overlapping text nodes:

Before — the pill sits in the tab and collides with the label:

```
headers=1 leaves=5 action=[1009→1303 w=295] *** OVERLAP(1): "Orchestrator"@268 X "Chat UI"@234
headers=1 leaves=5 action=[1009→1303 w=295] *** OVERLAP(1): "Orchestrator"@268 X "Terminal UI"@283
```

After — the action region grows to hold the pill, no overlaps:

```
headers=1 leaves=4 action=[1009→1303 w=295] actionOverflow=0 ok   (idle)
headers=1 leaves=5 action=[762→1303  w=541] actionOverflow=0 ok   (switching)
headers=1 leaves=5 action=[742→1303  w=562] actionOverflow=0 ok
headers=1 leaves=4 action=[1009→1303 w=295] actionOverflow=0 ok   (settled)
```

Also ruled out GPU compositing as a cause — the overlap reproduced identically with software rendering (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`).

Checks run:

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` — clean
- `npx vitest run` over `SessionView`, `SessionInterfaceSwitch`, `CenterPane`, `ChatWorkspace`, `SessionChatSurface` — 268 passed
- Added a regression test in `SessionView.test.tsx` asserting the status pill renders in the header action region and not in the session tab's action slot. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix commit and passes after.
- Remaining full-suite failures (`src/landing/*`, `src/main/browser-profile-import`) reproduce identically on an unmodified checkout and are unrelated to this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(chat): chat route crashes when a select config option has no choices
body:
## Summary

Opening a `claude-code` session crashes the entire chat route with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')`. The user sees the red **"Something went wrong!"** error boundary instead of the chat UI.

The crash happens whenever the provider advertises a `select` config option that currently has **no choices** — which is the normal state for the `model` option before the ACP agent has sent its model catalog.

## Impact

Total loss of the chat surface for that session, not a degraded control. Because it depends on catalog timing, it reproduces intermittently, which makes it easy to misread as a flake.

Side effect: the Plan Mode toggle from #4483 never becomes reachable, because the `mode` option (which *does* carry valid `plan` choices) renders in the same component that has already thrown.

## Reproduction

1. Open a session on an ACP-backed harness — `claude-code` (`claudeacp.New(claudecode.New(), log)`, registry.go:69).
2. Open the session before the agent has advertised its model catalog.
3. The chat route crashes immediately on render.

Live payload from `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/config-options` at the moment of the crash:

```json
{
  "options": [
    { "id": "model", "name": "Model", "category": "model", "type": "select" },
    {
      "id": "mode", "name": "Mode", "category": "mode", "type": "select",
      "currentValue": "default",
      "choices": [
        { "value": "default", "name": "Default" },
        { "value": "plan",    "name": "Plan" },
        { "value": "auto",    "name": "Auto" },
        { "value": "yolo",    "name": "YOLO" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Note the `model` option has **no `choices` key at all**. `GET /conversation/models` returned an empty list at the same moment.

## Stack trace

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')
    at optionCurrentLabel (src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.tsx)
    at ClubbedConfigPicker (src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.tsx)
    ...
The above error occurred in the <ClubbedConfigPicker> component.
```

## Root cause

`optionCurrentLabel` (TurnSettingsBar.tsx:882) dereferences `choices` unconditionally:

```ts
return option.choices.find((choice) => choice.value === option.currentValue)?.name
```

The TypeScript type declares `choices` as required (`src/renderer/types/conversation.ts:561`), but the server omits it — see #4869.

## Scope — this is not a one-line fix

`optionCurrentLabel` is only the first call site to run. `.choices` is dereferenced without a guard in **9 places** in `TurnSettingsBar.tsx`: lines 475, 476, 504, 675, 676, 775, 815, 817, 882.

## Suggested fix

1. Make the type honest first — `choices?: ChatConfigChoice[]` in `conversation.ts:561`. This makes the compiler surface all 9 sites instead of relying on manual review.
2. Guard each site with `(option.choices ?? [])`.
3. Consider skipping render entirely for a `select` option with no choices, since there is nothing to pick.

The frontend should stay defensive regardless of the server-side fix, since a newer renderer can talk to an older daemon.

## Environment

- Commit: `2d01919c2` (current `main`)
- App version: 0.10.3
- Platform: Windows 11
- Harness: `claude-code`

title: fix(settings): scratch projects show a bare section title instead of an explanation in Intake and Workflow
body:
## Summary When you open Settings for a scratch project and go to the Intake section, the panel shows only the words "Tracker intake" as grey text. There is no toggle, no controls, and no explanation. It looks like the settings failed to load. The same problem exists in the Workflow section, where the panel shows only the word "Workflow". Intake and Workflow are genuinely not supported for scratch projects, so hiding the controls is correct. The bug is that the message meant to explain this was never wired up, so the user sees a bare section title and assumes the UI is broken. ## What the user sees Settings dialog titled "Intake". Body contains one line of muted grey text reading "Tracker intake". Nothing else on the panel. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open any scratch project. 2. Open project Settings. 3. Go to the Intake section. 4. The panel shows only the text "Tracker intake" with no controls. 5. Go to the Workflow section for the same result with the word "Workflow". ## Cause `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx` uses the section title key as the fallback message. Intake, around line 611: ```tsx {!isScratchProject ? ( ) : (

{t("settings.project.trackerIntake")}

)} ``` Workflow, around line 594, does the same thing with `t("settings.project.workflow")`. Both keys resolve to short titles rather than explanations: ``` "settings.project.trackerIntake": "Tracker intake" "settings.project.workflow": "Workflow" ``` So the fallback branch renders the section title where a sentence was intended. ## Evidence that a real message was intended `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/renderer-coverage.test.ts` lists these two sentences in its approved literals for this exact file: ``` "No workflow settings for scratch projects." "Tracker intake is not available for scratch projects." ``` Neither sentence exists in `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/en.json`, and neither appears in the component. The allowlist entries are leftovers. `git log` points to commit `57d98ff0f`, "feat(settings): convert settings page to a modal (#3497)". Before that commit the block was `{!isScratchProject && (...)}`, which rendered nothing at all for scratch projects. That PR added the else branch and added the two sentences to the coverage allowlist, but shipped the wrong translation key and never added the strings to `en.json`. The coverage test still passes because unused allowlist entries are harmless, so nothing caught this. ## Why this is not environment specific The wrong key is in the component source, and the missing strings are in the shared `en.json`. Both are present on current `upstream/main` at `213dfe391`. No local setting is involved. Any scratch project on any machine reproduces it. ## Suggested fix 1. Add the two strings to `en.json`, for example `settings.project.trackerIntakeUnavailable` and `settings.project.workflowUnavailable`. 2. Use those keys in the two fallback branches instead of the title keys. 3. Remove the two stale entries from the coverage test allowlist. It may also be worth checking whether other fallback branches in the settings modal reuse a title key the same way. ## Environment - Commit: `2d01919c2`, with the same code confirmed on `upstream/main` at `213dfe391` - App version: 0.10.3 - Platform: Windows 11

title: perf(mobile): mux.ts hand-rolls a slow base64 decoder to avoid atob, which Hermes provides and the app already uses
body:
### Problem

Every PTY frame from the daemon is base64-decoded on the JS thread by `base64ToBytes` (`packages/mobile/lib/mux.ts:62`, called per frame at `:204`). The implementation pre-filters its input by concatenating a new string one character at a time (`:63-66`) and accumulates into a boxed `number[]` (`:68`) before copying that into a `Uint8Array` — the output length is known up front, so neither allocation is necessary.

The comment justifying the hand-rolled version (`mux.ts:54`) is the reason it is still there:

```ts
// These helpers avoid depending on atob/btoa (not guaranteed in Hermes).
```

That caution is stale for this app. `atob`/`btoa` aren't ECMA-262, so it was a reasonable general statement, but this package already depends on both:

- `packages/mobile/lib/pairingCode.ts:32` calls `atob` — reached at runtime from the pair screen (`app/pair.tsx:84`). If Hermes lacked it, QR pairing would already be broken.
- The xterm WebView bridge reaches native `btoa` through js-base64 on every terminal write.

And the desktop renderer already does this exact job the fast way — `frontend/src/renderer/lib/terminal-mux.ts:35-41` is `atob` plus a pre-sized `Uint8Array`.

**Measured**, Hermes CLI, 32 KiB frame (the daemon's cap — `backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:196`), output byte-identical across all variants:

| variant | relative |
|---|---|
| current (`mux.ts` as written) | 1.0x |
| pre-sized `Uint8Array`, no prefilter | ~4x faster |
| `atob` + `charCodeAt` copy | ~7x faster |

### What this is not

Being straight about the size, because it changes how it should be prioritised:

- **Not a correctness bug.** Every variant produces byte-identical output. `enhancement`, not `bug`.
- **Not user-visible in the normal case.** Watching an agent TUI repaint a small grid costs roughly 2% of the JS thread. It only bites on the worktree-shell tab under sustained output — a build log, a test run, a `cat`. Nobody has reported it.
- All numbers come from a desktop-class Hermes CLI. No physical device was tested.

The reason it seems worth the half hour anyway: the replacement already exists in this repo, and the dependency it avoids is already taken twice by this same app.

### Proposed direction

Replace `base64ToBytes` with the desktop's version and correct the comment at `:52-54`.

Two things for whoever picks it up:

1. `bytesToBase64` (`:81`) still needs the `B64` table for the keystroke path — either convert both or keep the table.
2. `atob` throws on malformed input where the current loop silently prefiltered it away. To save anyone the trace: **the daemon cannot produce input that `atob` rejects.** Terminal payloads have exactly one encode site — `backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:444`, `base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString` — and Go's `StdEncoding` structurally cannot emit whitespace or line breaks (`Encode` has no wrapping branch, and `NewEncoding` panics outright if the alphabet contains `\n` or `\r`). Nothing re-encodes in transit either: the LAN listener serves the same `http.Handler` as loopback rather than proxying, and JSON escaping only touches `<`, `>` and `&`, none of which are in the base64 alphabet. So a guard at the helper or the `:204` call site is defensive hygiene, not a fix for anything the daemon can send. (The reverse path is safe too, if `bytesToBase64` is ever swapped for `btoa`: the daemon decodes keystrokes with non-strict `StdEncoding` at `manager.go:392`, which is more permissive than what `btoa` emits.)

`packages/mobile` has no `mux.ts` test at all today, so this should come with a round-trip test mirroring `frontend/src/renderer/lib/terminal-mux.test.ts`.

### Alternatives considered

Keep the hand-rolled loop but pre-size the `Uint8Array` and drop the prefilter — about 4x, with no engine API dependency at all. Slower than `atob` but the most conservative option if the original caution is still preferred.

### Context, not duplicates

#4499 and #4552 cover high-output terminal behaviour on the **daemon** side. This is the client-side decode cost and is independent of both — no claim is made here that it contributes to that crash loop.

title: mobile: no expo-router ErrorBoundary is registered, so a render-time error terminates the app
body:
### Problem

`packages/mobile` registers no React error boundary anywhere. A repo-wide grep for `ErrorBoundary`, `componentDidCatch`, `getDerivedStateFromError` and `screenErrorBoundary` across the package returns zero matches, and the root layout mounts none.

expo-router does ship a fallback screen, but it is **opt-in**: a route has to `export const ErrorBoundary`, or a layout has to set `unstable_settings.screenErrorBoundary`. The app does neither, so nothing catches a render-time throw.

What actually happens then is worse than a stuck screen. React classifies an uncaught render error as fatal (`onUncaughtError` → `ExceptionsManager.handleException(error, true)`), which on iOS reaches `RCTFatal` and, with no fatal handler and `maxReloadAttempts` at 0, an uncaught `NSException` → SIGABRT; on Android it is `throw JavascriptException`. **The app terminates.** Relaunching lands on the same screen and crashes again until the daemon or the app changes.

The plausible trigger fits this product exactly: the phone runs a store/OTA build against a daemon the user upgrades independently, and a payload shape a screen doesn't expect throws in render.

For comparison, the desktop renderer already covers this — `frontend/src/renderer/components/TelemetryBoundary.tsx`, mounted at `main.tsx:93`.

There is also no in-app diagnostic for render errors: `lib/sentry.ts:81-83` has `loadSdk()` returning `null` (the SDK is deliberately not installed), and the `ErrorUtils.setGlobalHandler` hook in `TelemetryManager.tsx` structurally never sees React render errors, since RN calls `ExceptionsManager.handleException` directly rather than going through that hook.

### The constraint that makes this a design question

**Do not simply wrap the root.** expo-updates installs itself on RN's fatal path, and that is the anti-bricking net behind EAS Update. A root boundary that renders a fallback causes content to appear, which calls `markSuccessfulLaunchForLaunchedUpdate()` — so a bad OTA update gets permanently recorded as a good launch and can never roll back. That converts a self-healing crash-loop into a permanently bricked "Something went wrong" screen.

Once first content has appeared, the rollback pipeline no longer holds the launch tasks (and the fatal handlers are released about 10 s later), so a boundary on a navigated screen costs nothing.

So the ask is **which screens, and how to keep launch-time rollback intact** — not "add a root boundary".

### Proposed direction

Sketch, deliberately loose because the placement is the real decision:

- Per-route `export const ErrorBoundary`, or `unstable_settings.screenErrorBoundary` on the tabs layout, so only navigated screens are covered and launch stays on the fatal path.
- Or a boundary whose `componentDidCatch` re-reports fatally until the launch is known-good, and only renders a fallback after that.
- Verification wants a release build both ways: throw on a navigated screen → fallback shows; throw at launch → rollback still fires.

### Alternatives considered

Leaving it as is, which is a defensible default — RN marking render errors fatal is *why* the anti-brick net works, and a crash is at least visible in App Store Connect / Play Console where a swallowed error would not be. The counter is that "remote control for when you're away from your desktop" is the one product shape where terminating on a malformed payload is the worst available outcome.

### Honest scope

No reproduced instance — local QA runs across pairing, chat, spawn, approvals and the full PR lifecycle on both simulators recorded no render crash. Filing as hardening/parity, not as a bug.

Worth pre-empting: #1084 → PR #1254 removed custom route error boundaries from the old Next.js web app. That was the right call there because Next.js ships a default boundary; expo-router does not unless a route opts in.

title: chore(mobile): internal APK profiles build all four ABIs — 25 MB of unusable 32-bit x86 per build
body:
### Problem

Both internal EAS profiles force a universal APK, so every internally distributed build carries all four ABIs.

`packages/mobile/eas.json:7-20`:

```json
"development": { "developmentClient": true, "distribution": "internal",
                 "android": { "buildType": "apk" } },
"preview":     { "distribution": "internal",
                 "android": { "buildType": "apk" }, "channel": "preview" }
```

`production` (`:21-24`) sets no `android.buildType`, so the store build is an app bundle and Play splits per device. **End users are unaffected** — this is about internal distribution only.

Measured on a local `expo run:android --variant release` APK (120,914,006 bytes), unzipped per ABI:

| slice | size | share |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/x86` | 24.9 MB | 20.6% |
| `lib/x86_64` | 24.1 MB | 19.9% |
| `lib/arm64-v8a` | 22.6 MB | |
| `lib/armeabi-v7a` | 15.5 MB | |
| everything else | 32.9 MB | |

Of that, only **32-bit `x86` (24.9 MB) is unambiguously dead** — no current device or emulator runs it. `x86_64` is deliberately reachable: the `development` profile is the documented path for someone without a native toolchain, and Android emulators are x86_64, so dropping both wholesale would break that.

With the default `useLegacyPackaging=false` the libs are stored uncompressed, so the dead slice occupies device storage as well as download.

Frequency is low, and worth saying so: no CI builds an APK (`mobile.yml` is `npm ci` → typecheck → tests, and nothing in the repo runs `eas build`), the documented contributor path is a local `npx expo run:android`, and OTA means a tester pays these bytes once per native release rather than per fix.

### Proposed direction

Two routes, and the choice matters more than the diff:

1. **Narrow, zero-risk** — add `"buildArchs": ["armeabi-v7a", "arm64-v8a", "x86_64"]` to the `expo-build-properties` android block already present at `app.json:73`. The plugin already supports it (it overrides `reactNativeArchitectures`) and is already a dependency (`package.json:23`). Drops the dead 32-bit slice, keeps emulators working.
2. **Preview-only, fuller cut** — a per-profile `gradleCommand` with `-PreactNativeArchitectures=armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a` on `preview` in `eas.json`, leaving `development` emulator-capable. Saves the full 49 MB on that profile.

**Fingerprint caveat, which decides the route:** `fingerprint.config.js` ignores `eas.json` but not `app.json`, so option 1 moves the OTA runtime version and has to land at a native-release boundary. Option 2 avoids the bump entirely.

### Alternatives considered

ABI splits instead of a restricted list — more moving parts for the same outcome on an internal-only artifact.

### Measurement caveats

The numbers come from a local release APK, not from an actual EAS preview build. EAS prebuilds from the same template with the same `reactNativeArchitectures` default, so the shape should match, but it is inferred rather than measured on EAS.

Note also that `android/gradle.properties` — the obvious place to look — is gitignored (`packages/mobile/.gitignore`) and not in the repo, so it is not an editable fix point. The two knobs above are the checked-in ones.

title: fix(runtime): recover when legacy tmux socket is gone
body:
## Summary
- classify a missing legacy default tmux socket as unavailable runtime infrastructure after the private-socket lookup misses
- let explicit tmux teardown and interrupt treat that unavailable controller as idempotently stopped
- retain fail-closed liveness semantics, so reaper/attach paths do not infer process death from a missing tmux socket

## Root cause
After a daemon restart, legacy socket ownership is rediscovered. The private lookup could fall back to the default socket, but a missing default socket was returned as `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` before `Destroy` reached its existing idempotent server-unavailable handling. `Kill` therefore stopped before lifecycle termination; `Interrupt` also failed on the same resolver path.

A missing tmux control socket does not prove an agent process is dead, so `IsAlive` still returns an unavailable-runtime error rather than per-session death. The recovery is deliberately limited to explicit stop/teardown operations.

## Tests
- `npm run lint` (with AO_* environment scrubbed and isolated golangci cache)
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/adapters/runtime/tmux -count=1`

## Risk / follow-up
An unavailable tmux control endpoint can leave an orphan process; this PR preserves existing fail-closed automated liveness behavior and only makes explicit user-requested stop paths idempotent.

title: bug(chat): mermaid fences render as plain code instead of diagrams
body:
## Problem

```mermaid fenced blocks in agent chat output render as plain monospace code, not as diagrams. Agents frequently emit architecture flows as mermaid (e.g. in plans/specs), so the reader gets source text instead of the picture.

## Repro

1. Have an agent emit (or paste into chat):
```
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User] --> B[AO]
```
```
2. Observe the timeline shows a code block labeled "mermaid" with raw source, no diagram.

## Root cause (checked on `main` @ 213dfe39)

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx` routes every fence through `CodeBlock` -> `HighlightedCode`.
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/code-highlight.ts` `canonicalLanguage('mermaid')` returns `undefined`, so it renders plain monospace and loads no grammar.
- No `mermaid` dependency in `frontend/package.json`; same path in `frontend/src/renderer/components/markdown/MarkdownFileView.tsx` (markdown file Preview tab).
- Dedup: searched issues for `mermaid` / `diagram` / `markdown rendering`. Only hit is #4514, which merely embeds a mermaid flow in its own body as documentation, not a rendering bug. No existing rendering issue.

## Expected

- ```mermaid fences in chat render as SVG diagrams (with source fallback + copy), respecting light/dark theme and not breaking the existing no-raw-HTML sanitization story.
- Same handling in markdown file Preview if cheap; at minimum chat.

## Scope note

Renderer CSP is `script-src 'self'` with no `wasm-unsafe-eval` (see `vite.renderer.config.ts`, `code-highlight.ts` header). Implementation must work within that (mermaid is plain JS, but its SVG output needs sanitized injection rather than the current token-tree-only path).

title: Session worktrees are untrusted, so Claude Code workers stop at the trust dialog and the allowlist never applies
body:
## Summary

Every AO session gets a fresh git worktree. Claude Code has never been trusted
in that brand-new directory, so the worker opens the interactive trust dialog
instead of starting work. `No, exit` is the pre-selected option and no human is
attached to the tmux pane, so the session stalls or exits. The permissions in
`.claude/settings.local.json` never apply.

From the outside this looks like a permissions bug. It is a trust bug, and the
distinction cost us three sessions.

## Environment

- AO **v0.12.10**, Linux x64, running headless under systemd with Xvfb.
- Claude Code 2.1.258 in the guest; 2.1.260 on the machine the probe ran on.
- Ubuntu 24.04 guest.

## Why it happens

AO runs agents through its bundled tmux
(`~/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.10-linux-x64/tmux`), so the worker gets a real PTY
and Claude Code starts in **interactive** mode. Interactive mode enforces
workspace trust. Print mode (`-p`) skips the trust check entirely, which is why
this is easy to miss when testing by hand with `claude -p`.

The worktree layout:

```
~/.ao/data/worktrees/sandbox/sandbox-12/.git
  -> gitdir: /home/rose/sandbox/.git/worktrees/sandbox-12
```

`~/.ao/data/worktrees/sandbox/sandbox-12` is new on every session, so it is
never in `~/.claude.json`'s `projects` map.

## Reproduction

Independent of AO — a fresh repository and a real linked worktree:

```sh
git init probe-repo
cd probe-repo && git commit --allow-empty -m init
git worktree add ../probe-wt
mkdir -p ../probe-wt/.claude
cat > ../probe-wt/.claude/settings.local.json <<'JSON'
{"permissions":{"allow":["Bash(touch:*)"],"deny":[],"defaultMode":"default"}}
JSON
cd ../probe-wt && claude --setting-sources=user,project,local
```

With neither the worktree nor its parent repository trusted, the session opens
with:

```
Quick safety check: Is this a project you created or one you trust?
⚠ This folder pre-approves 1 tool permission in .claude/settings.local.json:
    Bash(touch:*)
  These will apply without asking. Only proceed if you trust this configuration.
❯ No, exit
  Yes, I trust this folder
```

Vary the trust state in `~/.claude.json` and re-run:

| Trusted path | Result |
|---|---|
| nothing | blocked at the dialog above |
| the worktree itself | starts normally |
| the worktree's `git-common-dir` repository | starts normally |

Either path satisfies the gate on its own.

## Suggested fix

When AO creates a session worktree, mark that worktree trusted for Claude Code
— set `projects["<worktree path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true` in
`~/.claude.json` (honouring `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` where set). AO created the
directory and chose its contents, so it is in a position to vouch for it.

Trusting the `git-common-dir` repository instead also works and covers every
future worktree cut from it, but it grants trust to a directory outside the one
AO made, so the worktree-scoped version seems the better default.

## Second, smaller point

Whatever the resolution, the reason is currently invisible. The dialog text is
clear and specific, but it exists only on the PTY — we could not find it
surfaced in AO's UI, its API, or its database. A worker that stops for this
reason reports nothing that distinguishes it from a worker that hit a genuine
permission denial. Surfacing the stall reason would have saved most of the time
this took to isolate, independently of the fix above.

(We did not read AO's source for this; the observation is from the outside.)
