title: sessions.branch is never reconciled with the branch the session actually pushed (18 of 21 session-to-PR pairs disagree)
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.* Measured against **AO v0.12.10** on
> 2026-09-04, across three separate AO instances (a Linux VM install, a macOS
> host install, and an OrbStack VM install). Repository names and URLs are
> withheld because the repositories are private; everything below is
> product-level state.

## `sessions.branch` is never reconciled with the branch the session actually pushed

AO sets `sessions.branch` to the branch it creates with the worktree —
`ao/<session-id>/root`. When the worker then does `git checkout -b <name>`,
commits, pushes and opens a pull request, `sessions.branch` is never updated.

AO **does** learn the real head: it lands in `pr.source_branch` on the row AO's
own poller writes, in the same database. The two fields then disagree, and the
one the session view shows is the wrong one.

## Measured

Joining `sessions` to `pr` on `session_id`, per instance:

| Instance | Pairs | Disagree |
|---|---|---|
| Linux VM | 4 | **3** |
| OrbStack VM | 17 | **15** |
| macOS host | sampled | disagrees on the sampled session |

**18 of 21 session-to-PR pairs disagree**, across two repositories and both the
`claude-code` and `codex` harnesses.

Representative rows:

```
session=A-4    sessions.branch=ao/A-4/root    pr.source_branch=ao/A-4/range-span
session=A-15   sessions.branch=ao/A-15/root   pr.source_branch=ao/A-15/geometric-mean
session=A-16   sessions.branch=ao/A-16/root   pr.source_branch=ao/A-16/geometric-mean
session=B-1    sessions.branch=ao/B-1/root    pr.source_branch=ao/B-1/gui-save-settings-finding
session=B-8    sessions.branch=ao/B-8/root    pr.source_branch=ao/B-8/urgent-intake
```

The API surfaces the stale value directly. `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>` for a
session whose pull request is open and mergeable:

```json
{
  "id": "A-16",
  "status": "mergeable",
  "branch": "ao/A-16/root",
  "prs": [
    { "number": 14, "state": "open", "ci": "passing", "mergeability": "mergeable" }
  ]
}
```

`branch` says `ao/A-16/root`. That branch holds none of the work. The commits
are on `ao/A-16/geometric-mean`, which is in the same response's `prs[0]` and in
`pr.source_branch`.

## Not always

Two of the 21 agree, so the field is not inert — some path does set it. On the
agreeing rows the recorded branch *is* the pushed one. Whatever writes it did not
run for the other nineteen. I did not identify which path that is.

## Why it matters

`branch` is what a person reads to go and find a session's work. For 18 of 21
sessions it names an empty branch while the same record already holds the right
one. It is also the field most likely to be used to reconcile a session against
a remote, so a consumer that trusts it will look at the wrong ref and conclude
the session produced nothing.

## Suggested fix

Reconcile `sessions.branch` from the observed head when the SCM poller writes a
`pr` row for the session — the value is already in hand at that moment. Failing
that, have the session API return the head from `pr.source_branch` when one
exists, so the two surfaces cannot disagree.

## Verified read-only

Every measurement was a `GET` or a query against a copy of the database. No AO
state was mutated.

title: Archiving or removing a project strands its open pull requests with no path to closure
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.* Measured against **AO v0.12.10** on
> 2026-09-04, across three separate AO instances (a Linux VM install, a macOS
> host install, and an OrbStack VM install). Repository names and URLs are
> withheld because the repositories are private; everything below is
> product-level state.

## Archiving or removing a project strands its open pull requests with no path to closure

When a project is archived or removed from the board, AO keeps its sessions and
its `pr` rows, but the project no longer appears in `GET /api/v1/projects`. Any
pull request those sessions opened is then held by a **terminated session in a
project the board does not list**. Nothing drives it, nothing surfaces it, and
no other AO instance will adopt it.

## Measured

Two pull requests on one repository have been open since 2026-09-03 with no path
to closure:

| PR | Head branch | Owning session | Owning instance | Session state | Project state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #6 | `ao/<proj>-19/rolling-average` | `<proj>-19` | macOS host install | `terminated` | project absent from `/api/v1/projects`, its 29 sessions retained |
| #11 | `ao/sandbox-21/rolling-average` | `sandbox-21` | OrbStack VM install | `terminated` | project row present with `archived_at` set |

The macOS host instance still returns PR #6 attached to its session, with live
mergeability:

```json
{ "id": "<proj>-19", "projectId": "<proj>", "status": "terminated",
  "branch": "ao/<proj>-19/root",
  "prs": [ { "number": 6, "state": "open", "mergeability": "conflicting",
             "review": "none" } ] }
```

So the data is not lost. It is unreachable: the project it belongs to is not on
the board, and the session that owns it is terminated, which also means a review
cannot be run on it.

## The multi-instance part, which makes it worse

These three AO instances point at the same Git repository. Each instance's `pr`
table contains only the pull requests its own sessions opened, which is correct
per instance — but it means **no instance is authoritative for the repository**.
An operator looking at any one board sees a subset and reasonably concludes the
other pull requests do not exist. That is exactly the wrong conclusion, and it is
how these two went unnoticed for a day.

## Why it matters

An archived project is the normal end of a piece of work. If archiving silently
abandons open pull requests, then over time a repository accumulates open pull
requests that no board shows and no user knows to look for. There is no AO
surface that lists "pull requests AO opened that are still open", so the only way
to find them is to go to the forge and read them by hand — which is what turned
these two up.

## Suggested fix

Any of these would close the hole; the first is the smallest:

1. **Warn on archive.** When archiving or removing a project, count its sessions'
   pull requests that are still open and say so, rather than archiving silently.
2. **Keep them reachable.** Let an archived project's sessions still be listed
   and filtered, so a pull request AO opened is never invisible to the board that
   opened it.
3. **Offer closure at archive time.** An explicit "close the pull requests these
   sessions opened, or leave them" choice, since abandoning them is sometimes the
   right answer and should be a decision rather than a side effect.

Related: #3402 (cleanup is non-idempotent, no session-delete lifecycle) and
#2608 (cleanup cannot reclaim archived-project worktrees) are the same family —
archived projects leaving state behind that nothing can reach.

## Verified read-only

Every measurement was a `GET` or a query against a copy of the database. No AO
state was mutated, and neither pull request was closed, edited or commented on.

title: Bug: Model selection is not preserved when switching from Chat UI back to TUI
body:
### Description

Model selection is not preserved when switching from the Chat UI back to the TUI. The model chosen in Chat UI is not reflected in TUI after the switch.

### Steps to reproduce

title: feat(session): add an optional pre-spawn launch gate (#4895)
body:
Refs #4895, #4888. Downstream incident: menard-software/setup-agent-orchestrator#418 (see also #427, #428 there).

**Draft.** This is the boundary only — the smallest change that makes the rest of #4895 possible. It is not the whole lifecycle.

## Why

Process creation is not successful startup. An agent child can be spawned and then stop *before* its agent loop — at a workspace-trust prompt, at a permission acknowledgement, or on a conversation that no longer exists — and AO reports that as ordinary work in progress.

That is what #418 recorded: a group of retained Claude workers sat at startup prompts while the board showed `Exited` or `working`, `ao send` returned `AGENT_EXITED`, and a live reviewer tab coexisted with an absent main child. A human had to open individual panes to find out why.

Nothing outside the daemon can fix that. A helper called after `POST /sessions` is already too late to give the exact child its environment, and external code must not infer or overwrite AO's own lifecycle state.

## Where

`Manager.Spawn`, immediately after the existing agent-binary check and before `superviseAgentProcess` / `runtime.Create` — the last point at which every trusted value is resolved and no child exists.

The seam deliberately mirrors `validateAgentBinary`, which already establishes the shape. That check exists because *"tmux happily creates a session+pane around a missing command, so an unresolved binary would leak through as a live session that never ran."* A child that parks at a trust prompt leaks through the same way, one step later.

## What

```go
type LaunchGate interface {
    PreLaunch(ctx context.Context, req PreLaunchRequest) (PreLaunchDecision, error)
}
```

- **`PreLaunchRequest` carries only daemon-owned values** — session id, kind, harness, the AO-created workspace, its git common dir *resolved by git* rather than guessed from the path, the resolved permission mode, and the exact child argv. Nothing comes from the task or the agent.
- **`PreLaunchDecision` may contribute environment entries for that exact child** — the half a post-spawn helper cannot do (a per-session `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, for instance). Keys AO already set are **not** replaced: a gate contributes, it does not take over.
- **The zero decision refuses.** A gate that returns nothing by mistake stops the launch rather than waving it through. A gate error is also a refusal, not a warning — an unreachable gate must not silently degrade into an ungated launch.
- **A refusal fails the spawn** with `ports.ErrLaunchNotReady` under a new `ErrSpawnLaunchGate` stage, carrying the gate's reason and optional machine-readable prompt kind to the caller.
- **Nil gate disables it** and leaves spawn behaviour unchanged. That is the default, and one test asserts it.

## Tests

Seven, at the real spawn seam, modelled on `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingAgentBinary` so they assert the same two facts a pre-spawn refusal must produce: `runtime.Create` does not run, and the workspace is torn down.

Each check was **negative-tested by disabling it**, so none of them can pass for the wrong reason:

| Breakage | Result |
|---|---|
| gate never consulted | 6 of 7 fail |
| refusal downgraded to allow-anyway | the two refusal tests fail, alone |
| gate error swallowed | the gate-error test fails, alone |
| AO-owned env override permitted | the override test fails, alone |

```
go build ./backend/...                                        ok
go vet ./backend/internal/session_manager/ ./backend/internal/ports/   ok
go test ./backend/internal/ports/                             ok
go test ./backend/internal/session_manager/ -run 'TestSpawn_LaunchGate|TestSpawn_WithoutLaunchGate'   ok, 7/7
```

Full `./backend/internal/session_manager/` has **four failures on this machine — all pre-existing**, not from this change: `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingAgentBinary`, `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`, `TestSpawn_ValidatesBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`, `TestSpawn_MissingBinaryPreservesNonEmptyScratchWorkspaceForRetry`. Each fails with `tmux required on macOS but AO's configured, bundled, or system tmux was not found`. I verified this by stashing the change and reproducing the same failures on unmodified `main` at `56ea59b`, rather than assuming.

## Deliberately not in this change

The rest of #4895, which this boundary is the prerequisite for:

- persisted readiness handshake bound to `(session, launch, conversation)`, so a stale child cannot make a replacement launch ready;
- `needs_input` / `launch_failed` / `resume_invalid` as first-class statuses rather than generic `exited`;
- delivery states and refusal of `ao send` before readiness;
- separate main-child, supervisor and reviewer liveness, so a live reviewer cannot mask a failed main child.

Each wants its own change and its own tests. Happy to follow this with them, reshape the contract, or move the seam if you would rather it sat elsewhere — the position and the naming are the parts I would most like maintainer input on.

## Scope note

No credential, GUI automation, PTY injection, or destructive session action is involved. Base resolved immediately before push: `56ea59b`.

title: bug(projects): a project whose local folder was deleted from disk returns an opaque 500 with no way to flag or cleanly remove it
body:
## Bug

When a project's local source folder is deleted from disk (moved, removed, or on an unmounted volume), the daemon has no clean way to represent it. Any List/Get or session read that reaches the filesystem or git for that project fails with an opaque `500`, so a client cannot tell "the project's folder is gone" apart from a genuine internal fault, and there is no surfaced affordance to remove the now-dangling project.

## Impact

- The desktop project list / sessions board shows an error (or a 500) with no explanation and no recovery path.
- A git worktree whose owning repository was deleted fails with an exit-128 "not a git repository" that surfaces as a raw 500.
- The user is stuck with a project entry they cannot act on.

## Expected

- Detect the missing-folder condition on read (List/Get) only, without auto-deleting/archiving/sweeping.
- Surface it as a clear signal: a `folderMissing` flag on the project read model and a `404 PROJECT_FOLDER_MISSING` (rather than a raw 500) for reads that reach the gone repository.
- Skip default-branch resolution for a missing folder (fall back to `auto`).
- Allow clean removal through the existing `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}` flow, and show a badge/banner in the UI.

## Notes

Only `os.ErrNotExist` (or a non-directory at the path) should count as missing; other stat errors should be logged and leave the flag false rather than guessing.

title: fix(updates): preserve staged replacement provenance
body:
## Summary

Keep staged update A's durable provenance while B is discovered, downloaded, or fails. A versioned atomic journal records candidate and operation identity, failure, supersession, and restart reconciliation. Settings and Sidebar retain the quit warning and guard AO's install action.

Integrated current main `d06b2162d0a84887d67105cae392184255032e21`, preserving #4812 feed resolution, #4849 restaging suppression/escalation/release notes/restart UX, #4922 Windows/Linux quit protection, and #4929 upstream claim support. The legacy staged record migrates; channel changes no longer discard A or use a competing legacy writer.

## Review fixes

Head: `8b59160e283c6f6b2245b7767473cceedda65bce`.

- Keep A/B on macOS after MacUpdater's ZIP response resolves. That only proves transfer, not Squirrel acceptance. Late native errors retain A and block AO installation. The real MacUpdater loopback regression exercises this boundary.
- Preserve superseded native candidates in the journal and quit warning. Returning to A abandons pre-native B, or retargets A while retaining B's native uncertainty.
- Use file sync and atomic rename everywhere, with directory sync on POSIX only. Windows unsupported directory flushing no longer rejects every journal write. This is not a promise of POSIX-equivalent directory durability on Windows power loss.
- Keep the live transition chain coherent across queued write failures. Only the latest successfully persisted snapshot can clear a persistence failure and permit installation.
- Respect same-channel automatic download opt-out and expose an explicit Download action. Forced channel-switch replacement remains supported.
- Project only progress metrics into journal-derived status so unrelated broadcasts cannot replace A/B state or version.

## Verification

- Focused updater, journal, reducer, adapter, sidebar, settings, and restart tests: 264 passed.
- Frontend and E2E TypeScript checks passed.
- Playwright update flow: 3 passed. Renderer smoke: 55 passed.
- Production renderer build passed.
- Full frontend suite on final head: 278 files passed, 3,775 tests passed, 7 skipped. Local Electron resolution used `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` for the installed binary.
- All final-head CI checks passed: frontend test, renderer smoke, and gitleaks. Reviewer approval is still required.

## PR3 dependency

macOS replacement remains conservatively in native-handoff with AO restart disabled until relaunch into the expected candidate reconciles the journal. External quit may install A, B, or another retained native candidate. PR2 alone cannot safely enable AO restart after a macOS replacement. Verified native completion with operation identity and safe cancellation remain PR3 requirements. This PR neither claims atomic native replacement nor enables blockmaps.

title: feat: harden macOS differential v2 production client
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the production client contract for macOS differential v2 while preserving strict isolation from old clients. The runtime gate and production trust keyring remain intentionally inactive until the release conductor publishes and verifies the matching signed same-release assets.

## Client behavior

- Keeps conventional macOS `.zip.blockmap` assets and bridge releases absent. Windows and Linux behavior is unchanged.
- Requires a signed, canonical, same-release manifest that binds channel, architecture, minimum client version, baseline and candidate identities, versioned asset URLs, sizes, and SHA-512 digests.
- Enforces manifest issuance, expiry, and public key ID validity windows. Unknown, expired, future, malformed, or mismatched authorization fails closed.
- Reauthorizes every verified final-cache hit against the signed current candidate, then hashes the candidate bytes before native handoff.
- Uses the supported protected `dispatchUpdateDownloaded` boundary to make cancellation safe through native handoff.
- Cleans corrupt, missing, denied, or stale cache state before one full ZIP fallback. HTTP 416 also settles and cleans before fallback.
- Preserves restart and retry behavior through atomic private cache markers.

## Verification

Head: `419c1496a`.

- 102 focused differential tests passed after merging current `main`.
- 184 auto-updater tests passed.
- Frontend typecheck passed.
- Byte-identical reconstruction passed for arm64 and x64 fixtures.
- Measured total HTTP savings were 42.55% for arm64 and 36.38% for x64.
- Coverage includes bad, expired, future, and mismatched manifests; key validity; corrupt and missing baselines; corrupt and missing final cache; HTTP 416; cleanup before full fallback; cache reuse; cancellation at native handoff; and restart/retry.
- The complete frontend run reached 4,522 passed and 7 skipped. Environment installation gaps caused unrelated failures. The one affected progress assertion was corrected and its 184-test suite passed afterward.

## Native acceptance and rollout dependency

The preserved exact arm64 target passed the repository macOS artifact verifier, including codesign, Gatekeeper, stapler, architecture, entitlement, and bundled runtime checks. A real Squirrel swap to these exact bytes remains blocked because the exact target is not published: its SHA-256 is `2ad0d149f662d5b22fa0f536cab55165cfbb0cd2c2351dd2ace1c4f6f97f4369`, while the published `v0.13.0` arm64 ZIP is `53124dbed831082d15911e3b545f2c631851b9add618d3527954a709d9e44276`. No production upload or feed activation is authorized.

AO Releases PR #36 at `c99d214d` directly matches this client wire contract. It independently verifies the historical baseline ZIP identity before signing, keeps that ZIP outside candidate inventory, and verifies the candidate ZIP, both maps, and manifest. Production keys and exact-target native acceptance remain unresolved rollout prerequisites.

No public release dispatch, production asset upload, feed activation, or merge is included.

title: Codex account bootstrap failure is sticky and blocks task creation until restart
body:
## Bug

A failed one-time Codex account bootstrap leaves the daemon permanently unable to start Codex tasks until the daemon is restarted. Task creation returns HTTP 503 with:

```json
{
  "error": "unavailable",
  "code": "CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "Codex account setup did not complete",
  "requestId": "..."
}
```

![Codex task creation blocked by account bootstrap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-bootstrap-sticky-20260904/.issue-assets/codex-bootstrap-sticky-20260904/account-setup-unavailable.png)

**Source:** User report with screenshot on 2026-09-04  
**Environment:** macOS arm64; Electron development build; Codex CLI 0.146.0  
**Analyzed against:** `feef57bcba40d2e485dec53e9ea138db7277be22`  
**Introduced by:** #4722, squashed as `c02317774`  
**Confidence:** High for the sticky bootstrap lifecycle defect; medium for the original transient trigger because the underlying error is discarded.

## Reproduction

1. Start the daemon with Codex installed and force the first device-global account reconciliation to fail, for example by making the account client `Open` or `account/read` return a transient error.
2. Open **Create a new task**, select Codex, and start the task.
3. Observe `503 CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` with “Codex account setup did not complete.”
4. Restore the underlying account client and retry task creation without restarting the daemon.
5. Observe that every retry returns the same error.
6. Restart the daemon; bootstrap runs again and task creation can succeed.

## Root cause

`WarmCodexAccounts` starts account bootstrap asynchronously. `codexAccountManager.bootstrap` is guarded by `sync.Once`. If `bootstrapInner` returns an error, the manager stores it in `bootstrapErr`, closes `bootstrapDone`, and can never run bootstrap again during that daemon lifetime.

Every ordinary Codex controller launch calls `acquireCodexControllerAdmission`, which calls `WaitCodexAccountBootstrap`. Once the first bootstrap has failed, `WaitCodexAccountBootstrap` converts the stored error to the generic `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` API error. Consequently, an otherwise transient local failure becomes a process-lifetime launch outage.

The original bootstrap error is also lost at this boundary. `WaitCodexAccountBootstrap` does not wrap it or expose a safe reason, and the bootstrap runner does not log it. The screenshot and HTTP response therefore cannot distinguish among app-server launch/initialize failure, `account/read` error or timeout, SQLite failure, account-directory failure, or credential reconciliation conflict.

The HTTP status compounds the problem: `apierr.Unavailable` advertises a retryable 503, but retrying cannot work because `sync.Once` prevents another bootstrap attempt.

This is not an account-switch URI mismatch:

- Task creation uses `POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`.
- Account switching uses `POST /api/v1/agents/codex/account-switches`.
- Bootstrap talks to `codex app-server` over local stdio JSON-RPC (`initialize`, then `account/read`), not a remote switching URI.

Within #4722, `2983de577` introduced the one-time account bootstrap and `47aaebede` made Codex controller admission wait for it, exposing the sticky failure on every launch.

## Expected behavior

A transient bootstrap failure should remain safely serialized but should be retryable without restarting the entire application. The daemon should retain a safe, diagnosable failure reason.

## Suggested fix

- Replace the `sync.Once` terminal failure with a single-flight bootstrap state machine: idle/running/succeeded/failed, allowing a later bounded retry after failure while keeping concurrent callers serialized.
- Distinguish retryable native/SQLite/time-out failures from permanent configuration or credential-safety failures.
- Log the safe wrapped bootstrap cause and a classified reason code without credential content or paths.
- Keep controller admission closed while bootstrap is running; after failure, trigger or join a bounded retry rather than replaying the stale error forever.
- Preserve the stable API envelope and request ID. Consider returning a sanitized reason code in `details` for supportability.

## Test coverage

Add tests for:

- first bootstrap attempt fails, second succeeds without daemon restart;
- concurrent launch callers join one bootstrap attempt;
- a permanent safety failure remains fail-closed with a stable classified reason;
- the delegate endpoint returns the expected 503 envelope during failure and succeeds after retry;
- the account-switch endpoint is not involved in ordinary task creation.

Current tests cover successful bootstrap, individual reconciliation failures, and admission waiting, but not retry after a failed bootstrap.

## Impact

- All new and restored Codex sessions can be blocked for the remainder of the daemon lifetime.
- Other harnesses are unaffected.
- Restarting AO is the current workaround, but the UI does not explain that.

title: fix(chat): keep the ChatUI-selected model across the ChatUI ↔ TUI handoff
body:
Code changes: +103 -3  
Tests: +544 -0  
Others: +19 -0 (generated sqlc)  

## Summary

Fixes #4893 — model selection was not preserved when switching from Chat UI back to TUI.

### Root cause

When ChatUI hands off back to TUI, the interface-transition coordinator rebuilds the TUI via `relaunchSessionWithPolicyAndGeneration`, which derived the harness config from `effectiveAgentConfig(rec.Kind, project.Config)` — the **project-configured** model. A model chosen later in ChatUI (persisted only in conversation settings) was silently discarded, so the rebuilt TUI resumed with the project default (e.g. "5.6 Full") instead of the user's pick (e.g. "5.6 Luna").

### Fix

1. **Persist the selected model before routing the prompt.** `chat.Service.SetTurnSettings` now invokes a new `OnModelChanged` callback whenever the user picks a model; the daemon wires it to the new `sessionmanager.Manager.PersistChatModel`, which writes the model onto the session's durable `Metadata.Model` — a model-only write that never touches the conversation identity or terminating state. The callback is invoked synchronously at pick time, i.e. before any subsequent prompt routes.
2. **Refresh the latest model from the daemon when rebuilding TUI.** Both `relaunchSessionWithPolicyAndGeneration` (the rebuild) and `preflightInterfaceTarget` (which validates the exact restore command the rebuild will run) now override the project-derived `Config.Model` with the session's persisted `Metadata.Model` when set.
3. **Pass the model into every harness restore command.** Codex and Cursor already forwarded `Config.Model` on restore. **Claude Code did not, at two layers**: the adapter's `GetRestoreCommand` now passes `Model`, and `agentruntime.buildClaudeRestore` now appends `--model <model>` (mirroring its own launch path).
4. **Conversation/history preserved, no new session.** Nothing in the change touches resume identity; restore still resumes via the native `agentSessionId`, and the tests pin this.

### Regression tests

- `TestInterfaceTransitionChatToTUIRebuildUsesChatModel` — the Chat→TUI handoff race: interrupt + stop of the old Chat terminal, then the TUI rebuild; asserts both the target preflight and the rebuild carry the ChatUI model (not the project default) while resuming the same native conversation, with exactly one runtime created and the controller order intact.
- `TestRestore_RefreshesModelFromSessionMetadata` — daemon restore picks the session model over the project default and completes in `RestoreModeNative` (no new session).
- `TestPersistChatModel` — the model lands on durable metadata; conversation identity, runtime handle, and activity state are untouched; an empty model never clears a durable choice.
- `TestPersistChatModelPreservesConcurrentLifecycleUpdate` — a real SQLite interleaving proves a model selection cannot replay stale state over a concurrent termination/controller replacement.
- `TestSetTurnSettingsPersistsModelBeforeRouting` — a ChatUI pick persists immediately, re-selecting the same model is a no-op, and a later change supersedes it.
- `TestGetRestoreCommandAppendsConfiguredModel` (Claude Code adapter) and `TestBuildRestoreCommandAppliesModel` (Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor restore argv).

### Validation

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` green.

### Intentional omissions

- **No frontend change.** The ChatUI already `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/settings`, which is exactly the surface extended here; the persistence and handoff behavior is entirely daemon-side.
- **No API-contract change**, so `npm run api` was not needed: `session.Metadata.Model` was already served by `GET /api/v1/sessions`.

title: feat(cloud): configure multiple sandbox providers on one control plane
body:
Implements #4911.

## What and why

Today the sandbox provider is a single control-plane wide setting chosen at deploy time, which forces a separate control plane per provider (for example the NodeOps staging CP and the Coder preview CP). This change lets one control plane offer more than one provider and lets a client pick which provider a session runs on, so we do not have to stand up and operate a CP per provider.

Exclusivity for a customer still comes from deployment topology (a CP configured with the providers we want it to offer), but a single CP can now serve both NodeOps and Coder and select per session.

## Control plane

- `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS`: optional comma-separated list of every provider a CP offers. Defaults to just `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER`, so existing single-provider deployments are byte-for-byte unchanged. The default provider is always included, duplicates are dropped, order is preserved (default first), and hosted deployments may only list coder and nodeops (mirroring the existing single-provider rule).
- `config.Load` now validates every available provider's config, not just the default, so a CP configured with both providers fails fast at boot if either is misconfigured rather than on the first session that selects it.
- `newSandboxReconciler` builds every available provider client and hands them all to `sandboxresolve.New`, which already routes per sandbox record by `record.Provider`.
- `createSession` accepts an optional `provider` field. When set it is validated against the available set and stamped onto the session via the new `SessionPlanForProvider`. When unset it uses the deployment default. An unavailable provider is rejected with `422 provider_unavailable` before it can reach provisioning.
- `/me` now reports `sandboxProviders` (available plus default) so a client can render a selector limited to what the CP offers.

The `ao_sandboxes.provider` column and the resolver were already per session, so this builds on existing plumbing rather than reworking it. No migration.

## Frontend contract

- `CloudCpMeResponse.sandboxProviders` and `CloudCpCreateSessionRequest.provider`. The client already forwards the whole create-session body, so the field flows through with no client change.

## Gating

The user-facing selector will appear only when Developer Mode is ON and the Cloud toggle is ON, then a Provider selector (NodeOps or Coder, mutually exclusive, exactly one). Auth is out of scope and unchanged.

## Tests

- `resolveAvailableProviders`: default-only, list parsing, dedup and trim, unknown rejection, hosted-only rules, and coder plus nodeops allowed when hosted.
- `SessionPlanForProvider`: explicit override selects a non-default provider, empty override falls back to the default, and `SessionPlan` stays equivalent to the default.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -race ./...` all pass on the cloud module.

## Scope and follow-up

This PR lands the control-plane capability and the client contract. The in-app provider selector UI component (behind the Developer Mode and Cloud gates) and its i18n are the next commit on this branch; the `/me` availability signal and the create-session `provider` field are already in place for it to build on.

## Dependencies

Built on top of the Coder sandbox provider (PR #4624 and its stack), since the selector needs a second provider to choose. Base branch is the coder-sandbox-provider branch.


## Orchestrator children inherit the parent's provider

The provider a session runs on is now consistent across a whole orchestrator tree. Before this, a spawned worker child resolved its provider from the control plane default, so on a control plane offering both providers a NodeOps orchestrator's workers silently landed on the default provider instead of NodeOps. The in-app toggle only stamps the provider for top-level sessions, so nothing carried a provider into an `ao spawn`'ed child.

`createWorkerChild` now reads the parent orchestrator's provider from its immutable sandbox row (new `Store.OrchestratorSandboxProvider`) and builds the child plan with `SessionPlanForProvider`. A NodeOps orchestrator therefore spawns NodeOps workers and a Coder orchestrator spawns Coder workers on the same control plane. A parent that is not an active orchestrator maps to 403, and an inherited provider with no valid config on this control plane returns 500 rather than falling back to another provider.

The default provider stays NodeOps for hosted deployments (`defaultSandboxProvider`); Coder is only ever an explicit opt-in for an eleven_x control plane. New tests in `worker_orchestration_handlers_test.go` cover NodeOps inheriting over a Coder default, Coder inheriting over a NodeOps default, the missing scope path, a non-orchestrator parent, and a misconfigured inherited provider.

title: [Bug]: Chat session that was never prompted cannot switch to terminal UI, and the app shows no error
body:
### Summary

If a Chat session has not been prompted yet, "Switch to terminal UI" does not work and the app says nothing. The menu item is there and looks normal, but clicking it does nothing at all. No error, no message, no spinner. The session just stays in Chat. Sending one message first makes the switch work. Behind the scenes the daemon rejects the request with 409 NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING, but the desktop app never shows that to the user.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a project and create a session in Chat UI.
2. Do not send any message.
3. Open the ⋮ menu in the session topbar. "Switch to terminal UI" is there and clickable.
4. Click it.

Nothing happens. Clicking again just repeats the failed request.
Now send one message, wait for the reply, and try the switch again. It works.

Video:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1d7f72d-401d-46ce-b2ec-ecb7679dae85


### Expected behavior

One of these:

- the switch works, since a Chat session with no messages has no conversation to lose, or
- the app tells the user why it cannot switch, and ideally greys out the menu item until it can

Silently doing nothing is the problem.


### Actual behavior

```
POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interface-transition  ->  409

{"error":"conflict","code":"NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING",
"message":"The agent has not exposed a native conversation that can resume in the other interface"}
```

but the status endpoint still says the switch is available:

```
GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interface-transition  ->  {"supported":true,"targetMode":"tui"}
```

Nothing is written to `session_interface_transitions`, so it is refused during preflight.

**Why the user sees nothing.** Checked on `2e0614fc2`:

- `SessionView.tsx:931` starts the switch.
- `SessionView.tsx:937-940` catches the failure in an empty `catch` block.
- The error is only ever displayed in one place, `SessionView.tsx:1687`, where it is passed to `SessionInterfaceSwitchDialog`.
- That dialog only opens when the session is busy and the user has to pick drain or interrupt. A plain switch does not open it, so the error has nowhere to render.
- `useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts` has no `onError` on the start mutation, and there is no global handler either.

So the error is captured and then dropped.

**Why the daemon refuses.** For claude-code, AO checks whether the conversation exists by looking for the transcript file at
`~/.claude/projects/<project-key>/<uuid>.jsonl`. Claude reserves the session UUID immediately but does not write that file until the
conversation has content, so on a fresh session the file is not there.

There is a fallback, `nativeConversationNotStarted` at `interface_transition.go:542`, that allows a fresh handoff when nothing has started. It
does not help here because its first condition (`interface_transition.go:547`) requires the session to be in TUI mode.

Worth flagging for whoever fixes this: just removing that TUI check would not be enough. The fallback proves "nothing started" by reading the terminal output, and a Chat session has no terminal and an empty `runtime_handle_id`. The Chat direction needs different evidence, for example "this conversation has no messages".

### AO version

0.10.3 dev build, reproduced on commit 2d01919c2. Code unchanged on current main 2e0614fc2, and all line numbers above refer to 2e0614fc2.

### Environment

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS x86_64, kernel 6.14, Node v22.16.0, Electron dev build

### Logs / extra context

```shell
Daemon log while reproducing, every attempt the same:


level=INFO msg="http request" method=POST path=/api/v1/sessions/clove_v2-7/interface-transition status=409 bytes=215 level=INFO msg="http request" method=POST path=/api/v1/sessions/clove_v2-8/interface-transition status=409 bytes=215


  Session row while it was failing: `agent_session_id`, `runtime_launch_id`, `native_transcript_path`, `latest_user_prompt` and
  `latest_assistant_update` all empty, `session_mode` chat.

  I also checked this against all 20 sessions in my local database. Every session whose conversation UUID had a transcript file on disk could
  switch, and every session without one got the 409.
```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(updates): stop a stranded build installing on quit on Windows and Linux
body:
Follow-up to #4849, which is merged.

## Why

#4849 handles a staged build whose channel the user has left by dropping it and staging a correct one over it. Superseding is the only lever **macOS** has: `MacUpdater` reads `autoInstallOnAppQuit` once, at download time, to decide whether to hand the build to Squirrel, and the ShipIt process then waiting on app exit is not recallable.

Windows and Linux are not stuck with that. `BaseUpdater.addQuitHandler` re-reads the flag inside the quit handler:

```js
// BaseUpdater.js
if (!this.autoInstallOnAppQuit) {
    this._logger.info("Update will not be installed on quit because autoInstallOnAppQuit is set to false.");
    return;
}
```

AO never cleared it. `applyInstallOnQuitPolicy` consulted only the macOS location blocker, and `getMacInstallBlocker` returns `undefined` off darwin, so the flag stayed `true`. Between the channel switch and the replacement download finishing, `downloadedUpdateHelper` still pointed at the old installer — so quitting in that window installed the channel the user had just left, on the two platforms where that was avoidable.

## The fix

Install-on-quit is off from the moment a stale build is discarded until a replacement is staged.

- **Windows / Linux** — closes the window completely.
- **macOS** — a no-op. Documented as such in the code, so the asymmetry does not read as an oversight later.

The location blocker still outranks it: nothing installs from a translocated or unwritable bundle whatever is staged. There is a test for that ordering.

If the replacement never lands (the new channel offers nothing, or the download fails), install-on-quit stays off. That is the correct direction: the only build in the cache belongs to a channel the user is no longer on.

## Tests

Three cases in `auto-updater.test.ts`; the two behavioural ones were confirmed to fail without the change. 3188 tests pass, typecheck clean.

## Not verified by execution

Same standing caveat as #4849: **the install step has never been run on any platform.** This is read from `electron-updater`'s source — `BaseUpdater.addQuitHandler` for the Windows/Linux behaviour, `MacUpdater.js` for why macOS cannot do the same. Nobody has exercised a real signed update end to end, on any OS.

title: fix: support upstream PR claims from fork-backed projects
body:
## Bug

AO refuses to claim or spawn against an upstream pull request when the registered project repository is the user's fork, even when the local Git repository has the PR repository configured as its `upstream` remote. The error forces users and orchestrators outside the intended one-project workflow and can tempt creation of duplicate AO projects for the same codebase.

**Reported by:** @harshitsinghbhandari  
**Observed:** 2026-09-04 / 2026-09-05  
**Analyzed against:** `fccadda53028f5f22dcc64e9410b95c9b47a8b09`  
**AO version:** `dev`, daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** High — blocks claiming and continuing upstream PRs from the normal fork-based development checkout.

## Reproduction

1. Register a local project whose `origin` is `https://github.com/harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator.git`.
2. Configure `upstream` as `https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git`.
3. Spawn a worker in that registered project.
4. Run:
   ```
   ao session claim-pr <worker-session-id> https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4849
   ```
5. AO returns:
   ```
   PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH
   PR does not belong to the session project
   ```

The same boundary prevents `ao spawn --claim-pr` from keeping work inside the already registered project.

## Current behavior

`backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go::requireSameRepo` compares the PR URL only with the single persisted project repository URL. It requires an exact host, owner, and repository match. It does not model a fork's canonical upstream or consider an explicitly configured Git remote.

The strict check correctly prevents unrelated and cross-provider claims, but it also rejects the standard fork → upstream contribution topology.

## Expected behavior

AO should support upstream PR ownership without requiring users to register a duplicate project or rewrite their Git remotes.

The product needs an explicit, safe repository-identity model. Possible designs include:

- Persist a canonical/upstream SCM repository separately from the checkout/push fork.
- Discover and persist an explicitly selected upstream remote during project setup.
- Add a deliberate project configuration field listing trusted claim targets.

Do not silently accept arbitrary remotes: the accepted upstream identity should be explicit and durable, and host/provider/repository checks must remain strict.

## Acceptance criteria

- A project checked out from a fork can claim a PR in its explicitly configured canonical upstream repository.
- AO continues rejecting unrelated repositories, cross-provider matches, and same-name repositories on different hosts.
- `ao session claim-pr` and `ao spawn --claim-pr` share the same behavior.
- The UI/CLI explains how to configure canonical upstream identity when a claim is rejected.
- Existing sessions and projects require no duplicate AO project.
- Tests cover GitHub fork→upstream, GitLab fork→upstream/nested namespaces, unrelated remotes, cross-host, and cross-provider cases.
- Migration/config compatibility is documented if repository identity becomes durable project state.

## Impact

- Blocks normal contribution workflows where `origin` is a personal fork.
- Prevents AO workers from owning upstream PR lifecycle, CI, and review state.
- Encourages duplicate project registrations and fragmented session history.

## Related context

This was reproduced while attempting to continue upstream PRs #4849 and #3563 from the existing `agent-orchestrator` project.

## AI assistance

This issue was drafted with AI assistance and verified against the live AO error and current source boundary.

title: fix(projects): reject equivalent repository path registrations
body:
Registering a repository through two filesystem aliases creates duplicate AO projects. Reproduced during native import validation on macOS: the CLI registered /tmp/... while the picker returned /private/tmp/..., and importing it created a second project and orchestrator.

Compare directory identity against active registrations under the existing Add lock before preparing or storing a project. Return PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED with the original project ID for equivalent paths. Preserve existing stored paths and exact-path conflict behavior; distinct repositories remain independent.

This is a separate daemon defect discovered while validating #4403. PR #4926 handles consuming the conflict in the UI; neither PR depends on the other to build.

Validation:
- Both real→symlink and symlink→real regressions failed before the fix and pass afterward.
- All project Add tests pass; HTTP endpoint test verifies 409, original identity, and one registered project.

title: fix(codex): retry account bootstrap failures
body:
Follow-up to [issue #4908](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4908) and [PR #4924](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4924).

## Summary

- build on the merged safe bootstrap-failure classification and API diagnostics from PR #4924
- replace its demand-driven 1–32 second cooldown with daemon-owned automatic retries after 10 seconds, 20 seconds, 45 seconds, 90 seconds, and then every 3 minutes
- keep exactly one native bootstrap attempt active while concurrent task launches join the same attempt
- keep shared bootstrap work on the daemon context so cancelling one request does not cancel recovery
- invalidate stale retry timers by generation when a caller or another timer has already started an attempt
- cache success permanently and run existing capability, authentication, and capacity warming exactly once
- preserve permanent credential/storage safety failures as fail-closed and non-retryable
- preserve account-switch routes, operation/account-mutation gates, frontend behavior, OpenAPI, and storage schemas

## Context

[PR #4722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4722) originally added a process-lifetime `sync.Once` bootstrap, causing a transient first failure to block every later Codex task launch until daemon restart. PR #4924 removed that terminal latch and added safe reason codes, permanent-vs-transient failure classification, and a real delegate-route regression test.

This PR retains those reviewed protections and changes retry ownership: recovery is scheduled by the daemon rather than requiring a later task-launch request to trigger another attempt.

## Retry behavior

- one native bootstrap attempt may run at a time
- failures remain fail-closed and retain the existing `503 CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` code/message
- only failures already classified as retryable schedule automatic work
- retry delays are 10 seconds, 20 seconds, 45 seconds, 90 seconds, then a 3-minute cap
- calls during backoff receive the safe existing failure immediately
- calls during an active attempt wait for that shared attempt
- daemon shutdown cancels pending timers and prevents further retries

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./...`
- `cd backend && go test -p 1 ./...`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/agent ./internal/session_manager ./internal/integration`
- `cd backend && go test -race ./internal/service/agent ./internal/session_manager`
- `cd backend && go vet ./internal/service/agent ./internal/session_manager ./internal/integration`
- scoped golangci-lint v2.12.2 for the changed packages: `0 issues`
- `git diff --check`

The full suite is run serially because unrelated wall-clock-sensitive adapter fixtures have previously flaked only under repository-wide parallel contention.

title: fix(storage): preserve literal data paths and guard legacy databases
body:
A data directory containing `#`, `?`, or percent escapes was interpolated into a SQLite URI without escaping. SQLite could open a different file, and two distinct data directories could share records. This escapes the filesystem path for both normal and read-only connections.

If the intended database is absent but the old URI points to an existing SQLite database, startup now refuses to create an empty replacement and identifies the legacy file for explicit recovery. Existing intended databases take precedence. No data is moved automatically because multiple directories may have shared the legacy file.

Validation:

- Real SQLite tests cover physical file placement, read-only enforcement, path isolation, legacy-data preservation, and intended-database precedence.

No API, schema, or migration changes. Native Windows results depend on CI; manual recovery of historical misplaced data is intentionally not automated.

title: fix(cleanup): stop counting already-gone workspaces as reclaimed
body:
## What

`ao session cleanup` now reports three outcomes instead of two: **cleaned**, **already gone**, and **skipped**. A workspace whose directory was already missing is no longer counted as reclaimed.

## Why

Refs #3219.

The count was derived from a single signal: did `Destroy` return an error. That is not the same question as "was a workspace released".

When a worktree directory is already gone on disk:

1. `git worktree remove` fails, but that error is only ever re-read inside the `findWorktree(records, path)` branch
2. `git worktree prune` succeeds and clears the stale registration
3. `findWorktree` then returns false, so the failure from step 1 is never looked at
4. `os.RemoveAll` returns nil, since it is documented to succeed on a missing path
5. `Destroy` returns nil, and the session is counted as cleaned

Nothing was released, but the run reports otherwise. In a batch that is how a cleanup reports hundreds of sessions cleaned while disk usage does not move, and why running it again never lowers the number.

The scratch adapter had the same shape: `os.Remove` is deliberately tolerated on a missing path, so an absent scratch directory also tore down "successfully" without releasing anything.

## How

`Destroy` keeps its signature and its behaviour. It is in the `ports.Workspace` interface, implemented by three adapters plus test fakes, and changing that contract for a reporting fix would touch every implementation for no functional gain.

Instead this adds an optional capability interface, matching the pattern already used for `AgentInterfaceHandoff`, `TerminalSurfaceInspector` and friends:

```go
type WorkspaceReclaimer interface {
    DestroyReclaim(ctx context.Context, info WorkspaceInfo) (WorkspaceReclaim, error)
}
```

- `gitworktree` and `scratch` implement it; the existing `Destroy` bodies were extracted into a shared `destroy` so there is one code path, not two.
- `router` forwards it, and falls back to `Destroy` for any adapter that does not implement it.
- `Manager.Cleanup` type-asserts for the capability and falls back the same way, so an adapter that does not report reclaim outcomes keeps the previous meaning of a nil error.
- The outcome flows out through `CleanupResult`, `CleanupOutcome`, `CleanupSessionsResponse` and the CLI summary.

Two details worth a reviewer's eye:

- **The path is sampled before any teardown step runs**, not after. Sampling afterwards would always report "absent", because teardown has by then removed it.
- **Only a definite `ErrNotExist` counts as already-absent.** A stat that fails for any other reason (permissions, a racing writer) stays on the removed path, so an unknown is never reported as "there was nothing to do".

API note: `alreadyGone` is added to the cleanup response, so `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated and committed alongside. The field is always serialised as `[]` rather than `null`. No frontend, mobile or packages client calls this endpoint today.

## Testing

`go build ./...`, `go test -race` on the touched packages, `golangci-lint run` (v2.12.2, as CI runs it) reporting 0 issues, `gofmt -l` clean, `npm run frontend:typecheck`, and `npm run api` leaving no spec drift.

The backend suite has 20 pre-existing failures on this machine (`codexappserver` protocol conformance and the Codex account catalog tests). I confirmed they are unrelated by stashing this change and running the same packages on a clean `main`, which reproduces them identically.

New tests: `DestroyReclaim` reporting `already_absent` for a missing worktree and `removed` for a present one (real git repo), the same pair for scratch, `Cleanup` routing an already-absent workspace into its own bucket, and the CLI summary keeping the two apart.

End to end, I built the daemon and CLI from `main` and from this branch and ran each against its own isolated copy of a real data directory, with the project repo cloned locally so nothing touched the original:

```
BEFORE (main)          Cleanup complete. 14 sessions cleaned, 6 skipped.
AFTER (this branch)    Cleanup complete. 6 sessions cleaned, 8 already gone, 6 skipped.

Disk reclaimed in both runs: 11M -> 6.9M
```

Identical teardown work, honest count. Running cleanup a second time on the same data shows the difference more sharply, since by then there is nothing left to reclaim at all:

```
BEFORE, second run     Cleanup complete. 14 sessions cleaned, 6 skipped.
AFTER,  second run     Cleanup complete. 1 session cleaned, 13 already gone, 6 skipped.
```

One detail from that run that shows the accounting working: several terminated sessions shared one orchestrator worktree. The first of them is reported as cleaned because the directory was there, and the rest as already gone. The old code called all of them cleaned.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Bug]: single-user PR stays “Review pending” after AO reviewer approves current head
body:
### Summary

In a single-user GitHub repository, an AO reviewer can complete successfully with
an `approved` verdict, but the PR remains shown as **Review pending** and cannot
be merged through AO.

The worker, PR author, AO daemon, and reviewer all use the same GitHub account.
GitHub does not permit users to approve their own pull requests, so the review
submitted by AO is recorded as `COMMENTED` rather than `APPROVED`.

AO then ignores its own completed `approved` verdict and requires an external
GitHub approval, even when the repository does not require approving reviews.

## Environment

- AO desktop: `0.12.10`
- Platform: macOS, Apple silicon
- SCM: GitHub
- Repository: personal/single-user repository
- Branch protection: no approving review required
- Required CI checks: none
- PR author and authenticated `gh` user: same GitHub account
- Reviewer harness tested: Codex
- The same underlying behavior was also encountered while trying Claude Code


### Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate AO/`gh` as the owner of a personal GitHub repository.
2. Use an AO worker to create a branch and open a pull request.
3. Run **Review PR** from the AO session inspector.
4. Let the reviewer complete with an approved verdict.
5. Open the session Summary pane.

### Expected behavior

AO should provide a viable merge workflow for single-user repositories that do not require GitHub approvals.

Possible expected behaviors include one of the following:

Treat an empty GitHub review decision as “approval not required” when the repository's merge rules require zero approvals.
Allow a completed, current-head AO approved verdict to satisfy AO's own review gate when GitHub does not require an external approval.
Make the external-approval merge gate configurable per project.
Clearly document that AO requires a separate GitHub reviewer identity and provide a supported way to configure reviewer-specific credentials.
At minimum, the UI should distinguish:

“AO review approved”
“GitHub approval required”
“GitHub approval not required”
“Approval impossible because the reviewer is the PR author”
rather than displaying the generic “Review pending” state.

### Actual behavior

AO records the internal review successfully:

```json
{
  "status": "complete",
  "verdict": "approved",
  "targetSha": "<current-pr-head>"
}
```

The target SHA matches the current PR head.

However, GitHub records the submitted review as:

```
{
  "state": "COMMENTED",
  "reviewDecision": ""
}
```
This is expected GitHub behavior because the authenticated reviewer is also the PR author.

AO consequently continues to show:

```
Review status: Review pending
```
The green Merge button is not displayed. ao pr merge <number> also rejects the merge because the backend applies the same approval requirement.

GitHub otherwise reports the PR as open, clean, and mergeable. The repository does not require an approving review.




### Why this matters
The current state is impossible to satisfy in a normal single-user setup:

AO uses the existing gh authentication for GitHub operations.
The same identity authors the PR and submits the review.
GitHub cannot record that review as APPROVED.
AO nevertheless requires APPROVED before exposing or executing its merge action.
Users must leave AO and run gh pr merge even after AO has reviewed and approved the current head.

Creating a second account or approval bot should not be required for a personal repository whose GitHub rules require zero approvals.

### Related issues
#1173 reported that an empty/null GitHub reviewDecision prevented a no-review-required repository from becoming mergeable. Its proposed fix was closed during the ground-up rewrite rather than resolved in the current code.
#2073 proposes configurable merge-gate exclusions, including review_required.
#1275 describes AO review completion as advisory and separate from SCM merge readiness.

### Additional context
This report is specifically about the mismatch between:

AO's internal, current-head reviewer verdict: approved
GitHub's unavoidable same-author review state: COMMENTED
The repository's actual rule: no approval required
AO's derived state: Review pending
It is not a stale-review, merge-conflict, CI, or GitHub authentication issue.

### AO version

AO 0.12.10

### Environment

macOS 26.5.1, Apple silicon, M1 Max

### Logs / extra context

```shell

```

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates
- [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(mobile): Android keyboard inset and orchestrator restart visibility
body:
Two Android-only mobile fixes. Both are pure JS/TS — no native module, config plugin, or `app.json` change.

## 1. Keyboard covered the input dock on every Android device

React Native's Android keyboard event does not report the keyboard's height above the screen bottom. From `ReactRootView.checkForKeyboardEvents`:

```java
Insets barInsets = rootInsets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars());
Insets imeInsets = rootInsets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.ime());
int height = imeInsets.bottom - barInsets.bottom;   // nav bar subtracted
```

So `e.endCoordinates.height` is the keyboard height **with the navigation bar already subtracted**. The terminal, chat and spawn screens padded their root view by exactly that value, but the root view draws edge-to-edge underneath the nav bar, so the keyboard actually covers the full `imeInsets.bottom`.

Every Android device was short by exactly the nav-bar inset:

| Nav mode | Inset | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| Gesture | ~24dp | input row cut in half |
| 3-button | 48dp | input row hidden behind the keyboard |

iOS was unaffected — its event measures from the screen bottom and already spans the home indicator.

New `rootKeyboardPad(platform, height, insetsBottom)` owns that platform difference; `screenKeyboardAvoidance` now takes the inset as a **required** argument so a call site cannot silently reintroduce the bug. `useSafeAreaInsets().bottom` is the correct addend: `react-native-safe-area-context` builds its bottom inset from `statusBars | displayCutout | navigationBars | captionBar` on API 30+ and clamps the IME out on the older path, so it is exactly the `barInsets.bottom` RN subtracted.

Verified on a Pixel 7 emulator (API 35) in both nav modes, and on the terminal and chat docks.

## 2. Orchestrator card offered Restart only when nothing needed restarting

The card rendered Restart when `state === "running"` and hid it otherwise — the inverse. A healthy orchestrator carried a destructive retire-and-replace button, while one that had exited offered "Start orchestrator", which reads as though the app had lost track of a session that has clearly already run.

| State | Footer now |
|---|---|
| running | `Open` only |
| stopped (exited) | `Restart orchestrator` |
| missing (never started) | `Start orchestrator` |

`launchIntent` keeps its running branch: it is still the correct answer to what a launch would do, and the destructive path must keep its confirmation if the card ever offers it again.

Both footer actions are now the shared `Button` rather than a 32x32 `IconButton` and a bespoke 32pt pill, so the tap target is a full-height labelled control. The card itself stays deliberately inert — the zone pills open the board, so a whole-card target would send two taps a few pixels apart to different screens.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — exit 0
- `npx vitest run` — 709 passed (up from 708; new tests written red-first)
- Both changes exercised on a live Pixel 7 / API 35 emulator against a real daemon

The new `launchIntent` test asserts the two labels **exactly** rather than with `/start/i` — "Restart" contains "start", so a loose match passes whichever label is wrong.

## Shipping

JS-only, and this branch's Android fingerprint `bcfb745ef3a294b08d2324b090febfc0a900bc0f` matches production build `ed8bcf7e` (1.3.0, versionCode 8), so this is deliverable over EAS Update on the `production` channel.

## Not verified

The stopped/missing orchestrator footer is covered by unit tests only — every project on the test daemon had a running orchestrator, and staging the state would have meant stopping a live one.

title: fix(tmux): target bare session in respawn-pane and pane-pid probe
body:
Fixes #4656.

## What
`respawn-pane` and the pane-pid probe hardcoded the target `<session>:0.0`, assuming tmux's `base-index` / `pane-base-index` are both `0`. With either set to `1` (a very common customization) the target misses and `Runtime.Restart` — the path session restore uses — always fails with `can't find pane: 0` / `can't find window: 0`.

## How
Target the bare session name instead (`respawn-pane -k -t <session>`, `display-message -p -t <session>`), which resolves to the active window/pane regardless of either option. AO sessions have a single pane, so this is exact. It also matches the file's existing convention: `set-option`, `send-keys`, `capture-pane`, and `paneCurrentPathArgs` already use the bare id. The alternative (resolving a stable `#{pane_id}` first) was left out as unnecessary complexity for single-pane sessions.

`panePIDArgs` was latent rather than broken (`display-message` falls back silently) but carried the same unchecked assumption, so it gets the same fix.

## Tests
- Updated `TestCommandBuilders` (both arg builders) and `TestRestartRespawnsExistingPaneAndPreservesHandle` (restart call-site assertion).
- Targeted tests pass; `go vet` clean; build passes.
- Full `tmux` package run has 4 failures (`TestNewUsesSystemTmuxForLegacyDefaultSocket`, `TestExecRunnerRunsFromStableDir`, `TestExecRunnerFallsBackWhenTempDirMissing`, `TestIsUnsupportedMatcher`) that fail identically on unmodified `main` — pre-existing Windows-environment issues (TempDir/socket preconditions), unrelated to this change.
- The issue's Linux integration tests (`TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell`, `TestAttachmentStreamsRealTmuxPane`) need real tmux and can't run on this Windows box; CI should cover them.

title: claim-pr never checks out the PR branch, and `ao session claim-pr` prints "checkout: already on PR branch" for exactly that case
body:
## Summary

`ClaimPR` never checks out the claimed PR branch — the service layer says so itself in a `TODO` — and the CLI then prints **`checkout: already on PR branch`** for exactly that case. The one code path that checks nothing out is the one that reports the checkout as done.

The `TODO` and the printer disagree, and the printer wins.

## Source, verified on current `main` `95246e9bdb1eeccafe08151b2ab18abc91709a75`

**`backend/internal/service/session/claim_pr.go`** — the service leaves `BranchChanged` false and states the CLI contract it expects:

```go
// L135-138
// TODO: implement workspace branch checkout. Until then, leave BranchChanged
// false and let CLI output omit the checkout line rather than claiming the
// session was already on the PR branch.
res := ClaimPRResult{PRs: prs, BranchChanged: false, DonorWasTerminated: outcome.OwnerTerminated}
```

**`backend/internal/cli/session.go`**, `writeClaimPRResult` (L427) — does not omit the line; it prints the affirmative wording for the false value:

```go
// L440-444
checkout := "already on PR branch"
if res.BranchChanged {
    checkout = "switched to PR branch"
}
if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(out, "  checkout: %s\n", checkout); err != nil {
```

Since `BranchChanged` is unconditionally `false` at the only place it is set, `"switched to PR branch"` is unreachable and `"already on PR branch"` is printed on every claim — true only by coincidence, when the workspace happened to be on that branch already.

## Reproduction

Observed on a claim of an existing PR whose branch the workspace was **not** on. Sanitized; exit status and output wording are verbatim.

```
$ ao session claim-pr <PR>
session <session-id> claimed PR #<PR>
  pr:       https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<PR>
  checkout: already on PR branch
$ echo $?
0

# read-only, immediately afterward, before any edit:
$ git -C <workspace> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
ao/<session-id>/root          # not the PR branch
$ git -C <workspace> rev-parse HEAD
<live main sha>               # not the PR head
$ git -C <workspace> status --porcelain
                              # empty — nothing was touched
```

The claimed PR's branch existed both locally and on `origin` at the PR head, and was checked out in **no** worktree, so nothing was contending for it. Session metadata was updated correctly; only the workspace claim in the output is false.

## The two CLI forms differ, and both are affected

| Form | Prints a checkout line? | Checks anything out? |
|---|---|---|
| `ao session claim-pr` | **yes — `checkout: already on PR branch`** | no |
| `ao spawn --claim-pr` | no (prints `spawned session … (claimed <url>)`) | no |

`spawn` posts to the same `sessions/{id}/pr/claim` endpoint (`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go` L154) and never calls `writeClaimPRResult`, so it makes no checkout claim — but it also performs no checkout, leaving the new worktree on its root branch while reporting a successful claim. The false *statement* is specific to `ao session claim-pr`; the missing *behavior* is common to both.

## Why it matters

A caller that trusts the successful response can edit the wrong base, overwrite unrelated work, or push a reconstruction that silently omits the current PR head — most dangerously during takeover, recovery, or cross-engine handoff, which is exactly when `--claim-pr` is reached for.

## Expected behavior

Either of these is fine; the present state is neither.

1. **Atomic claim + checkout.** Do not report success until the workspace is actually based on the exact current provider PR head. Session PR-ownership metadata, local `HEAD`, local branch/upstream, and the provider head agree, or the operation fails closed with an actionable error. A provider head that moves during setup aborts rather than silently using stale data. Existing owner/session/worktree content is never deleted or reset as a side effect.
2. **Truthful partial success.** If metadata-only claiming is the intended behavior for now, honor the `TODO`'s own contract: omit the checkout line, or state plainly that the workspace was not changed. The machine-readable `branchChanged` field already carries this correctly — it is only the human-facing line that is false.

Option 2 is a small change and would remove the misleading output immediately, independent of when the checkout lands.

## Tests requested

None currently assert this line. Both CLI forms need coverage:

- `ao session claim-pr` when the workspace is **not** on the PR branch — assert the output does not claim a checkout that did not happen.
- `ao session claim-pr` when the workspace **is** already on the PR branch — the one case the current wording is true for; it should stay distinguishable from the case above.
- `ao spawn --claim-pr` — assert the new session's workspace base against the exact claimed head, or that the command fails closed.
- `branchChanged` in the JSON response stays consistent with whatever the human-readable line says, in both forms.
- Once checkout is implemented: an already-owned PR, takeover, `--no-takeover`, a provider head that moves mid-setup, a dirty preserved prior worktree, and a provider/network failure.

## Related

- **#4890** — `sessions.branch` is never reconciled with the branch the session actually pushed. Related but distinct: that is drift *after* a push; this is a checkout that never happens *at claim time*. Neither causes the other.
- I searched open and closed issues for `BranchChanged`, `already on PR branch`, `claim_pr`, `claim does not check out`, `worktree stays on main`, `claim reports success`, and `session claim checkout` before filing; nothing covers this.

Downstream tracking lives in a private repository, noted for provenance rather than as a reachable link: `menard-software/setup-agent-orchestrator` issue #391, with a read-only pre-flight verifier and its evidence in PR #395. That verifier only *detects* the mismatch before a worker's first edit; the fix belongs here.

## Environment

Source verified by reading this repository at `main` `95246e9b` on 2026-09-05. The reproduction was run against a locally built CLI that self-reports `ao version dev`, so I am not attributing it to a tagged release; the two source locations above are unchanged at `main`, so the behavior follows from current code rather than from that build.

title: fix(import): preserve workspace root branch for orchestrator startup
body:
Workspace import could add a local Git root without saving its branch, then fail to start the orchestrator with `DEFAULT_BRANCH_UNRESOLVED` for `__root__`. The error incorrectly demanded a remote for a “child repository,” and the imported-project failure was invisible in the Windows/Linux board layout.

This change preserves the checked-out branch for existing workspace roots, while preventing plain nested folders from inheriting an ancestor repository’s branch. Child repositories still resolve their own defaults. Startup errors name the workspace root, retain the underlying diagnostic, and appear in both the macOS and Windows/Linux layouts.

Refs #4679. This covers the workspace-root variant of local import; it does not close the broader remote-less import issue. Existing registered projects can set their intended root default in Project Settings and retry. Remote/authentication failures remain enforced. `AGENTS.md` also records the requested requirement to run complete CI validation locally, report exact local gaps, and verify remote checks before handing over PRs.

Validation:

- All 61 board unit/integration tests passed after waiting for the loaded board before rendering the Windows/Linux error banner. The full CI suite caught this loading-state race; the existing empty-board regression now passes.
- Real Git integration reproduced unresolved startup without an explicit root default, then successfully created and destroyed root/child orchestrator worktrees with root `trunk` and child `dev`.
- Browser regression passed for macOS, Windows, and Linux platform detection. It exercises real renderer dialogs and the API client with mocked native picker/daemon responses, asserting the saved branch, orchestrator request, and visible actionable error.

All 11 GitHub checks passed, including the complete Go build/vet/race suite (17m20s), lint, API drift, Windows workspace tests, CLI smoke on all three OSes, fresh-install container smoke, and secret scanning.

title: feat(daemon): add quota-exhaustion and zero-output fallback detectors
body:
Partial slice of #4918 (intake: quota-aware provider/model fallback handoff).

## Summary
Pure domain detectors for acceptance bullets 2-3, decoupled from the switch saga (#3317) and launch gate (#4895):
- `RateLimitsExhausted` — 100% used via existing `WorstUsedPercent`; absent/stale/NaN telemetry reports no signal
- `CodexSnapshotExhausted` — reuses coordinator-derived snapshot `State`, stays consistent with the display surface
- `IsZeroOutputStop` — completed turn + timestamps + no assistant text, diff, plan, or production (command/file_change/plan/mcp_tool) activity

Fail-closed throughout: uncertain input never triggers. Policy (hold, fallback chain, `ao-capacity-gate`) intentionally left for later slices.

Fixes #4918 (partial: detection slice)

## How this helps #3317 and #4895
- **#3317 (switch saga):** the saga executes handoffs but its deferred "automatic quota-based fallback" item has no trigger. These detectors are that trigger — the saga can call them to decide *when* to reassign, without changing its state machine.
- **#4895 / #4897 (launch gate):** the pre-spawn gate decides whether a spawn may proceed. The exhaustion detectors give it a fail-closed quota input: a real 100% reading can HOLD, while absent/stale telemetry stays silent instead of causing a false HOLD or a false GO.
- Both consume these as plain function calls over state they already hold. No shared state, no new dependencies, no coupling — which is also why this PR cannot conflict with either workstream (2 new files, 0 edits to existing code).

## Test
`cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...` — full suite green (171 packages ok, 0 fail). `golangci-lint v2.12.2`: 0 issues. Race on `internal/domain`: pass.
