title: perf(chat): reduce live refresh and rendering overhead
body:
## What and why

Busy chats could wait for event traffic to stop before refreshing, then hold already-received text behind the streaming animation. Large syntax blocks also occupied the main thread, while every scroll repeatedly measured the loaded transcript.

This PR reduces that overhead without changing AO's daemon/API, session lifecycle, persistence, approvals, model selection, Markdown semantics, or chat layout.

- Bound CDC batching to the first event's 150 ms deadline; preserve active requests and catch up after intervening events. Cover reconnect/target overlap and disposal races.
- Memoize grapheme segmentation, append only new text, and flush the animation backlog on the first frame at/after 200 ms, including hidden-tab resumes.
- Cache minimap anchor geometry until content/layout changes; keep every loaded turn mounted for find and selection.
- Tokenize large code blocks in a lazy worker using the existing engine, bounded pending work, and readable plain-code fallback.
- Save the requested local/remote CI validation rule in `AGENTS.md`.

## Live benchmark evidence

Identical real-renderer fixtures on pinned baseline `a96322315` and this branch; three serial repetitions per workload on Apple M5/macOS, Node 24, Chromium 148, 1440×1000. Inputs/bridge are synthetic: these measure AO renderer overhead, **not provider inference latency**.

| Median measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First query fetch starts | 2,070 ms | 152 ms |
| Fetches during continuous event stream | 0 | 10 |
| Received Unicode burst fully visible | 2,857 ms | 213 ms |
| Highlight maximum main-thread callback gap | 65.0 ms | 27.2 ms |
| Anchor measurements over 120 scroll steps | 60,001 | 251 |

**Tradeoff:** first worker highlighting completes in 128.5 ms versus 62.6 ms, including startup/transfer in the development renderer. It leaves the main thread available more often; plain code remains readable. Scroll frame-gap ranges overlap, so no general FPS claim is made.

[Method, commands, ranges, validation details and limitations](https://github.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/blob/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/README.md) · [24 raw measurement records](https://github.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/blob/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/measurements.json)

## Validation

- Full frontend suite: **3,751 passed**, 6 skipped, 275 files.
- Full browser renderer smoke suite: **52 passed**.
- Frontend/E2E types, shared-package generation/drift/tests/build/package checks, pinned browser runtime, production renderer build: passed.
- Baseline and changed-build benchmarks: **12/12 each**, including source-text/copy and 250-mounted-turn integrity checks.
- Native isolated AO startup: real daemon/preload, projects/sessions API 200, actual home screen. Built worker also ran over `app://renderer` with the production CSP and exact Unicode preservation.
- Gitleaks v7.4.0: **9 commits scanned, no leaks** using the workflow config.

The first remote renderer job exposed missing product-ui dependencies when typechecking the new real-component benchmark fixture. The workflow now installs them. A local clean-dependency reproduction failed before this step, passed afterward, and all 52 browser tests passed again.

An initial settings “Saved” timing assertion failed; its full 40-test file passed on baseline and branch, followed by a passing complete frontend rerun. Early resource-contended runs and native ABI setup failures are documented, not counted as passes. The all-workflow wrapper stopped at a missing release-build variable; no publishing job ran. Docker later became unavailable, so the pinned scanner was built and run locally. GitHub runner status is tracked in this PR's Checks tab.

## Screenshots

Same 250-turn chat, before and after; no layout redesign:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before AO chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/assets/baseline-history.png) | ![After AO chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/assets/after-history.png) |

<details><summary>Native isolated AO startup</summary>

![Native AO startup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pulkit7070/agent-orchestrator/d5b310de0dff91787255419a5f42d8210a7b6c48/docs/performance/chat-responsiveness/assets/native-home.png)

</details>

## Intentional scope

Mermaid remains untouched. Full historical refreshes remain necessary because CDC does not identify changed item ranges; narrowing them can leave old tools stale or skip pagination-boundary items. Transcript virtualization, incremental Markdown parsing, and persistence batching are excluded to preserve behavior. Worker failure/saturation or oversized source leaves plain code; it does not discard source text.

Open Agent Orchestrator. 2. Add a workspace (in my case a Scratch workspace at `D:\Gateway-alt`). 3. Open the "Workspace agents" dialog. 4. title: bug(storage): malformed sqlc.yaml prevents pinned generator from running
body:
## Summary

The documented, pinned sqlc command fails on pristine current `main` before generation because `backend/sqlc.yaml` contains tab-indented sequence entries at lines 244-245. This is a syntax failure distinct from, but adjacent to, #4621. It blocks reproducible generated storage changes needed by #4951.

## Minimal reproduction

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator
npm run sqlc
```

Observed at `d06b2162d0a84887d67105cae392184255032e21`:

```text
error parsing sqlc.yaml: yaml: line 244: found character that cannot start any token
exit status 1
```

The authoritative command in `package.json` pins `github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1`. `AGENTS.md` requires changes to queries/migrations followed by `npm run sqlc` and forbids hand-editing generated files. CI currently has an API-generation drift job but no sqlc regeneration drift job.

## Cause

These entries begin with tabs rather than the surrounding YAML indentation:

```yaml
	          - column: "agent_switch_failure_policy.enabled"
	          - column: "app_settings.cloud_offering"
            go_type: "bool"
```

They also appear to collapse two intended column overrides under one `go_type`. A minimal correction must preserve both boolean overrides and then regenerate with the pinned version. Regeneration currently exposes additional agent-switch query drift, so that output should be reviewed rather than hand-maintained or folded silently into unrelated feature work.

## Expected

`npm run sqlc` succeeds from a clean checkout and `git diff --exit-code -- backend/internal/storage/sqlite/gen` is clean. Consider enforcing that command in CI.

## Related

- #4621: earlier reproducibility report for `app_settings.cloud_offering`
- #4951: durable orchestration outbox work currently blocked from producing an isolated, reproducible generated diff

title: fix(updates): honor saved channels and recover stalled checks
body:
## What and why

Update checks can leave Settings showing “Checking for updates” indefinitely: automatic checks did not settle a returned result when a completion event was absent, and a hung metadata request kept electron-updater's cached check promise and AO's operation queue occupied.

Both automatic and manual checks now settle returned results. A 60-second deadline cancels metadata requests through their cancellation tokens, displays an actionable timeout, and waits for the original check to unwind before allowing a queued retry. The adapter wraps only the updater executor's metadata `request` method during a serialized check and restores it afterward; download cancellation remains separate. This uses electron-updater's internal executor field, verified against the installed library in a real Electron probe. Closing the network session alone did not release the check promise in that probe, so the implementation cancels the requests instead.

The saved channel remains a persistent preference. A user running `0.12.11-nightly.202609051608` who selected Stable is offered stable `0.12.10`, including after restarting or retrying a failed check. That cross-channel downgrade is intended; the original downgrade screenshot alone does not establish a bug. Older releases within the installed channel are rejected. Fresh nightly installs retain Nightly when automatic downloads are declined, existing explicit choices are preserved, and rejected manifests do not redownload the cached staged candidate.

## Validation

- Five new regressions failed before this fix: automatic result settlement and stalled manual, automatic, and return-home checks.
- Updater/settings suite: 117 tests passed, including cancellation/queue ordering and keeping the check deadline away from downloads.
- Real Electron probe of the changed production code against a local stalled manifest: timeout surfaced, followed by a successful retry that discovered version 99.0.0. The probe shortened only the deadline to two seconds; production uses 60 seconds.
- Frontend and E2E typechecks passed. Cloud client generation/typechecks/21 tests/package dry run and product UI typecheck/120 tests/package dry run passed.
- Full local frontend run: all 3,754 assertions passed, but an unexpected HTTP GET hit browser-runtime-link.test.ts's JSON socket and produced an unhandled error. A complete rerun again encountered HTTP socket interference (273 files passed; that file had one failed test and unhandled parse errors). This is **not a clean local full-suite pass**. An earlier interrupted run also had a roughly 14-minute timing jump and UI timeouts; subsequent runs used a temporary sleep inhibitor. The full suite requires verification on the isolated CI runner.
- Local renderer smoke: 53 passed, 2 failed on initial chat/terminal rendering timeouts. A full rerun encountered 6 UI timeouts and was interrupted (4 passed, 1 interrupted, 44 not run). This is **not a clean local renderer-smoke pass**. All three checks passed on final head `5a4ee39d6cbbe8043927f157d55de6abd5efc79c`: frontend tests (5m19s), isolated Linux renderer smoke (2m14s), and gitleaks (20s).

Local checks use Node 24.20.0. Docker is unavailable locally, so the pinned Linux renderer-smoke container and gitleaks also require remote verification. No publishing workflow is used for validation.

## Limits and rollout

This does not cancel an already staged native installer or implement the separate recovery work in #4905. Release manifests, publication schedules, and signing configuration are unchanged. Installed clients need a conductor-built release containing the fix.

title: fix(desktop): improve embedded browser toolbar and import UX
body:
## Problem
The embedded browser toolbar has several related UX inconsistencies:

- Compact URLs are left-aligned while docked, but editing should remain left-aligned and maximized mode should keep the full URL.
- There is no address-bar action to open the current page in the system browser.
- The Browser Controls button appears selected merely because a profile or DevTools is active.
- Closing the Browser Controls menu can queue and display its tooltip even though the pointer is no longer hovering it.
- When a pinned tab rail drops to one tab, the toolbar trigger disappears and Recently Closed becomes unreachable.
- Browser-profile import exposes raw Electron/SQLite errors when a source browser still holds its database.

**Source:** Reported and reproduced during a local AO desktop development session
**Platform:** Windows
**Analyzed against:** `5186c8d7d2069a6a6444a3be0dff172d0b9249bd`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P2 — browser workflows remain usable, but common navigation and import paths are confusing or inaccessible.

## Reproduction
1. Open AO's embedded browser in docked and maximized modes and inspect/focus the address bar.
2. Activate a saved browser profile or DevTools and observe the Browser Controls button.
3. Open Browser Controls, dismiss it outside, and observe focus returning to the trigger.
4. Pin the tab rail, reduce the browser to one tab, and try to access Recently Closed.
5. Attempt to import from a running Chromium-family browser whose profile database is locked.

## Root cause
The browser panel used unconditional input alignment, treated configuration state as a pressed-button state, allowed Radix focus return to reopen the controls tooltip, and hid the tab trigger solely from the pinned flag. Import errors were surfaced directly from the IPC rejection without classifying locked/inaccessible source databases.

## Expected behavior
The address bar should use context-appropriate alignment, expose a system-browser action, keep Browser Controls visually neutral, show its tooltip only from actual hover, preserve access to Recently Closed, and provide browser-agnostic recovery guidance for locked or inaccessible profile databases.

title: bug(daemon): importing a single-repo folder as a workspace tells the user to git init their subdirectories instead of suggesting "Import project"
body:
## Bug

"Import workspace" applied to a folder that is itself a single, fully valid git repository fails with `WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS`, and the error's remediation pushes the user in the wrong direction.

### Repro

1. Have a normal single-repo project (the typical layout of a plain repo — no nested repositories):

```
~/code/my-app/          ← git repo, origin configured, clean main
├── src/
├── dashboard/
├── config/
├── scripts/
└── docs/
```

2. Desktop app → New project → **Import workspace** → pick `~/code/my-app`.
3. Every child directory is listed as `Needs git init`, and the import fails:

> **IMPORT FAILED · WORKSPACE NOT REGISTERED**
> Workspace project must contain at least one fully resolved git repository with an origin remote (`WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS`)
>
> Initialize at least one child repository with a remote origin, then retry.

### What's wrong

- The workspace scan (`detectWorkspaceChildren`) only inspects **direct children** of the picked folder; the root's own `.git` is not counted. That is correct for the workspace model (a container folder + child repos), but it means a single-repo folder can never pass.
- The `suggestedFix` ("Initialize at least one child repository with a remote origin") is actively harmful in this shape: following it means running `git init` inside `src/`, `docs/`, etc. — corrupting the layout of what is actually a perfectly fine single repository.
- Nothing in the error points at the actual right action: this folder should have been imported via **"Import project"** ("Import a single Git repository as one project"). The two modes sit next to each other in the create flow, and this mistake is easy to make.

### Suggested fix

Before emitting `WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS` (`backend/internal/service/project/workspace_registration.go`, the `hasReady` check), detect the "wrong import mode" shape and return a targeted error instead:

- **Condition:** the parent itself is a standalone, non-bare repo with a resolved `HEAD` and an origin remote, **and** none of the children is a git repository.
- **Message:** e.g. `WORKSPACE_PARENT_IS_SINGLE_REPO` — "This folder looks like a single git repository, not a folder containing several repositories. Use 'Import project' to add it."

This combination already fails registration today, so redirecting the message is pure UX — no currently-working configuration changes behavior. A workspace parent that is itself a repo remains legitimate (the `adoptWorkspaceParent` path), because in that case at least one child is a real repo and the new condition doesn't fire.

### Related

- #3686 covered the opposite import failure shape (many child repos failing child-level validation → a wall of errors). This is the zero-children-repos case, where the folder simply isn't a workspace.

Analyzed against `d06b2162d`.

title: Cloud session startup improvement and other bug fixes
body:
# Cloud startup, private GitHub repos, and dynamic orchestrator agent

## What

Improve the Cloud session startup and private-repository experience:

- Start worker transport before repository checkout completes.
- Run checkout and coding-agent initialization in parallel.
- Keep the Cloud terminal on a continuous `Connecting…` state until the agent TUI emits its first output.
- Add encrypted, user-scoped GitHub PAT support for private GitHub repositories.
- Dynamically choose the Cloud orchestrator harness from connected Cloud credentials instead of always using Codex.
- Remove temporary startup timing instrumentation.

## Why

Cloud sessions had unnecessary perceived startup delay and visible blank terminal transitions:

- Repository checkout blocked worker and terminal availability.
- The terminal could attach before Codex had drawn, exposing an empty terminal between loading states.
- Private GitHub repositories could hang or fail without a checkout credential.
- Cloud orchestrators always requested Codex, even when the user had only connected Claude Code or Cursor.

This improves the Cloud parity and startup roadmap. 

Issue #4575 

## How

- Worker transport, heartbeat, checkout renewal, PR bridge, and review bridge start independently from repository preparation.
- Agent input remains queued until checkout completes, preventing work from running in an empty workspace.
- `worker.ready` signals transport availability; `agent.ready` signals coding-agent terminal startup.
- Cloud terminal replay remains covered until the first agent terminal bytes are rendered. Local terminal replay behavior is unchanged.
- GitHub PATs are encrypted in the existing user-scoped provider credential store:
  - no GitHub OAuth flow;
  - no validation request is made when saving;
  - the secret is never returned or logged;
  - only a worker for a session created by that user can retrieve it.
- The orchestrator reads valid organization and personal Cloud credentials, then chooses:
  1. Codex
  2. Claude Code
  3. Cursor

The worker image still intentionally supports only those three installed harnesses. This does not add arbitrary-harness support.

## Testing

Validated locally with:

```bash
cd cloud && go test ./cmd/ao-worker ./internal/reconcile
```

```bash
cd frontend
npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts \
  src/renderer/hooks/useTerminalSession.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/lib/cloud-orchestrator.test.ts

npm run typecheck
```

Also verified:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Manual scenario validated with the local Docker Cloud control plane:

- Signed in to local Cloud.
- Saved a GitHub PAT in Cloud Settings.
- Created a Cloud project backed by a private repository.
- Confirmed private repository checkout succeeds.
- Confirmed the terminal stays on `Connecting…` until the agent TUI renders.

## Checklist

- [x] Continuing the existing `cloud/bug-fix` branch
- [x] Focused Cloud startup/private-repository improvement; no related issue supplied
- [x] Follows [[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for terminal loading and orchestrator harness selection
- [x] Relevant Cloud Go and frontend checks pass

title: bug(opencode): provider-only model override reaches ACP without actionable validation
body:
## Bug
OpenCode Chat accepts a provider display name as a model override and forwards it to ACP. A reported Windows orchestrator launch sent `TensorMux`, producing `Invalid params: model not found: TensorMux` inside `CHAT_CONTROLLER_FAILED`.

AO should reject an override without the required `provider/model` shape before launching the provider and explain how to recover. The attached report showed `tensormux/glm-4-7-flash` in OpenCode configuration, but `TensorMux` in the AO error. The report does not establish how that override was entered, and this issue does not claim AO converted a valid model ID into a provider name.

## Evidence and reproduction
- Source: user-provided screenshots; reporter and installed AO/OpenCode versions are unavailable.
- Analyzed against main `7e8a66229`.
- Reproduced at the real OpenCode Chat driver boundary with an injected plugin: both Start and Resume with `Model: "TensorMux"` proceed to binary resolution instead of returning a model validation error.
- A valid OpenCode override uses `provider_id/model_id`: [OpenCode model documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/models/#set-a-default).
- Confidence: high for the missing validation; no claim of an end-to-end reproduction on the reporter's Windows machine.

## Scope
Wire an OpenCode-specific `ValidateTurnSettings` callback into the existing ACP lifecycle. Reject missing or empty provider/model parts with `ErrChatConfigOptionInvalid` and recovery guidance. Keep empty overrides (Agent default) and custom, provider-qualified IDs unchanged.

TensorMux credential validity and provider configuration are outside this issue. `opencode auth list` in the report already lists a stored credential; that does not prove it authenticates successfully. No provider settings or credentials need to be modified.

Workaround: select `tensormux/glm-4-7-flash` in AO, or clear AO's model override to let OpenCode choose its configured default.

title: [Bug]: Project settings never load for a cloud project and show a raw PROJECT_NOT_FOUND error
body: ### Summary Opening Project settings on a cloud project shows "Loading project settings..." and then fails permanently with the raw daemon error "Unknown project (PROJECT_NOT_FOUND)". The settings form queries the local daemon by project id, but a cloud project only exists in the cloud control plane, so the lookup can never succeed. This reproduces for every cloud project, regardless of how it was created. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run a cloud control plane locally: `npm run cloud:local` 2. Start the desktop app against it: AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 npm run dev 3. Sign in with the seeded dev account and connect any agent credential 4. Create a project through New Project -> Cloud tab 5. Open that project's settings (kebab menu -> Project settings, or the Settings deep link) ### Expected behavior Project settings should open for a cloud project and show the project's real values from the cloud control plane, laid out like the local settings page, with every field read-only for now. A raw daemon 404 message should never be surfaced to the user. ### Actual behavior The panel shows "Loading project settings..." briefly, then renders the daemon's raw error text in red: "Unknown project (PROJECT_NOT_FOUND)". Every section is affected and the state never recovers. Desktop daemon log: GET /api/v1/projects/{cloud-project-uuid} status=404 ### AO version commit 7e8a66229 (upstream/main) ### Environment Ubuntu Linux 6.14 x86_64, Node v22.16.0, local cloud control plane via npm run cloud:local(provider=docker) ### Logs / extra context ```shell Root cause frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx makes two unconditional calls to the local daemon: line 82 apiClient.GET("/api/v1/projects/{id}") loads the project line 258 apiClient.PUT("/api/v1/projects/{id}") saves it Neither branches on where the project lives. A cloud project is never registered in the local daemon's project store, so the GET always 404s and the error text is rendered verbatim by the form's error branch. Same bug class as #4570 (open-in-editor surfacing a raw "Unknown session" for cloud sessions), which was fixed by branching on the project kind. The discriminator already exists and is already available inside this component: types/workspace.ts:181 CLOUD_PROJECT_KIND = "cloud" useWorkspaceQuery.ts:225 cloud projects are mapped with kind: "cloud" ProjectSettingsForm.tsx:135-138 the component already calls useWorkspaceQuery() and resolves its own workspace entry Planned fix 1. Branch on kind === CLOUD_PROJECT_KIND before either local call. 2. Read the cloud project from the cached cloud projects list. The cloud contract has no single-project GET (only PATCH and DELETE on /orgs/{orgId}/projects/{projectId}), and the renderer already caches the list under cloudProjectsQueryKey, so this needs no new API call. 3. Render with the existing read-only primitives already used by the local page (ProjectSettingsValueRow inside ProjectSettingsSection in @aoagents/product-ui), so no new view component and no editable controls. 4. No save path, so the local PUT is simply never reached for cloud projects. ``` ### Before submitting - [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates - [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: feat(lifecycle): add durable orchestration event outbox
body:
Closes #4951. Related generation prerequisite: #4953.

## Summary

- Persist normalized AO-owned worker/SCM orchestration facts with stable revisions and transactional lifecycle enqueue.
- Dispatch daemon-owned, bounded reconciliation turns to the current safe orchestrator with explicit Chat/TUI acknowledgement.
- Recover terminal facts, expired leases, and missing human-visible attention alerts at startup; deduplicate/re-arm transitions and bound retries/dead letters/retention.
- Expose project-scoped delivery observability and explicit dead-letter retry APIs.
- Document behavior, configuration, supported modes, upgrade, and rollback.

Idle/agent-settled emits `worker_turn_settled`, never task completion. Payloads contain only AO-owned IDs/enums/revisions and explicitly grant no authorization. No Electron, SSE, shell-polling, cron, launchd, Pi-only extension, installed-app/database, or dew-app change is involved.

## AC-1..AC-22 evidence at `b83d27a94`

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 1 honest types | `TestNormalizedActivityEventNeverCallsIdleCompletion`; distinct settled, blocked, terminated, ready, and merged kinds. |
| 2 stable identity | `TestOrchestrationEventStoreDedupeRearmLeaseAndAcknowledge`, `TestOrchestrationSourceStateDedupesAndRearmsSCMTransition`; source ID hash plus persisted generation forms the revision. |
| 3 re-arm | `TestNormalizedActivityEventDedupesRepeatsAndRearmsTransitions`, `TestPRReadyOrchestrationUsesCanonicalReadiness`, `TestTerminatedEventReconciliationClosesCrashWindowAndRearmsPerLaunch`; terminal PR observations clear readiness before merged/closed handling. |
| 4 atomic/fault boundaries | `TestActivityAndOutboxCommitRollsBackOnInjectedInsertFailure`, `TestFaultBoundariesDoNotClaimUncommittedDelivery`, `TestDispatcherAcceptsSynchronousTUIHookAcknowledgement`; terminal mutation crash window is deterministically reconstructed. |
| 5 restart | `TestOrchestrationEventStoreRestartReclaimsExpiredLease`, `TestRecoverReclaimsBeforeSynchronousProjectDispatch`, terminal reconstruction and attention-recovery tests. Startup recovery runs before HTTP health. |
| 6 client independence | Dispatcher is wired only in the daemon and consumes store/timer/wake-channel inputs; no Electron dependency. |
| 7 reconnect independence | Dispatcher does not consume general or notification SSE. Durable Notification Center rows provide reconnect catch-up. |
| 8 real turn/timing | One-second cancellable daemon scan, immediate lifecycle wake channel, real Session Manager transport; Chat admission and Pi prompt-submit admission are explicit acknowledgements. Live provider wall-clock exercise is environment-limited and is not represented as a hermetic CI test. |
| 9 busy/burst | `TestBusyTUIDefersWhileBusyChatQueues`, `TestPromptIsBoundedAndExcludesUntrustedProviderText`; Chat queues by stable message ID, TUI waits for idle, and due work remains pending. |
| 10 safe deferral | `TestGuard_AutomationFailsClosedAtJITBoundary`, `TestSendAutomationTUIRechecksStateAndAcknowledgementCapability`, `TestUnsafeOrMissingDestinationPerformsNoWrite`; JIT lease/re-read covers blocked, waiting, active TUI, exited, terminated, startup, and input gate. |
| 11 replacement | `TestDispatchResolvesCurrentDestinationAndAcknowledgesAcceptedBatch`; store state fence records the current destination only. |
| 12 ambiguity | `TestSubmittedTUIBatchRemainsUnacknowledgedForRestartRecovery`, `TestDispatcherAcceptsSynchronousTUIHookAcknowledgement`, `TestHooks_PiPromptSubmitCarriesExactAutomationBatch`, exact token/destination fence tests; ambiguous TUI gets at most one physical retry, Chat reuses the client message ID. |
| 13 bounds | `TestPromptIsBoundedAndExcludesUntrustedProviderText`; 50 events/32 KiB, remainder stays pending. |
| 14 retry/dead letter | `TestTransportFailureRetriesAndSanitizesError`, `TestOrchestrationRetryDeadLettersAndRequiresMatchingProjectForRearm`; 5-second attempt, persisted capped exponential jitter, 8 attempts/15 minutes, durable attention. |
| 15 no destination | `TestAttentionNotificationIsCreatedOnceAndResolvedByDelivery`, `TestOrchestrationMissingDestinationAttentionAndRetentionAreDurableAndDeduplicated`; no attempt consumption, 15-minute alert, 30-day/10,000-row visible dead-letter retention. |
| 16 recovery | Project-scoped retry controller tests plus explicit store re-arm test; success resolves per-worker attention. |
| 17 injection boundary | `TestPromptIsBoundedAndExcludesUntrustedProviderText`, `TestOrchestrationBatchIDRequiresExactSafeMachinePrefix`; provider text, control sequences, logs, comments, and titles never enter payload. |
| 18 authorization | Machine-origin warning in the bounded payload plus automation-specific JIT guard; no permission-prompt approval or unsafe Enter path. |
| 19 observability | Project API/controller tests expose every required delivery field; `TestTransportErrorsPersistOnlyTypedCredentialSafeClass`; `orchestration_attention` is stored, streamed, rendered, deduplicated, resolved, and reconstructed after notification/publisher failure. |
| 20 no polling | Daemon channel plus cancellable Go timer only; repository inspection contains no shell watcher/cron/launchd loop. |
| 21 upgrade/rollback | Migrations 0128/0129 and migration tests preserve existing rows/indexes; synchronous startup recovery precedes HTTP health; official docs describe backup, downgrade, and reinstall recovery. |
| 22 modes/fail closed | Pi TUI hook-to-lifecycle exact acknowledgement, Chat stable-id acknowledgement, JIT mode safety, ambiguity/restart tests. Unsupported TUI harnesses fail before pane write and enter bounded alerting. |

## Supported and unsupported production paths

Chat controllers use durable idempotent provider admission. TUI automation is supported only for `claude-code`, `codex`, `continue`, and `pi`, whose managed hooks can report the exact submitted prompt. Every other TUI harness is intentionally unsupported: it fails closed before a pane write, retains the event, and reaches the bounded human-visible alert rather than claiming delivery. This policy is documented in `docs/orchestration-events.md`.

No live authenticated provider is available to the repository test harness, so AC-8's provider wall-clock observation is environment-limited; the production path below it (daemon scheduler -> Session Manager -> Chat idempotent admission or TUI exact hook acknowledgement) is covered at its real package boundaries. This limitation is not presented as green live-provider evidence.

- PASS: `go test ./internal/orchestrationevents ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/storage/sqlite ./internal/storage/sqlite/store ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/daemon`

- PASS on the prior change: targeted golangci-lint v2.12.2, 0 issues.

- `go test ./internal/session_manager`: tmux prerequisite wins before agent-binary assertions in `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingAgentBinary`, `TestSpawn_MissingBinaryPreservesNonEmptyScratchWorkspaceForRetry`, `TestSpawn_ValidatesBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`, and `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingBinaryAfterEnvPrefix` when the configured/bundled/system tmux is absent.
- `go test ./internal/cli`: tests contact the active local daemon and return HTTP 404/current-daemon behavior (`TestBrowserRequiresSessionAndValidWait` and spawn project-resolution cases).
- The earlier broad run also reproduces pre-existing Crush user-auth discovery and systemcheck real-tmux-vs-stub failures. These are baseline/environment exclusions, not weakened assertions or #4951 changes.

## sqlc prerequisite and security

This diff does not hand-edit generated sqlc artifacts. The pre-existing malformed `backend/sqlc.yaml`/generation drift is isolated in #4953 (related #4621); handwritten transactions follow the store's existing locked `inTxDB` convention and generated schema contracts are not bypassed.

Wake payloads exclude provider-controlled text and secrets. Persisted transport failures are typed (`transport_timeout`, `transport_cancelled`, `transport_error`) rather than raw errors. API/log tests cover credential-bearing URLs, bearer/API-key-shaped values, control characters, and transcripts. The daemon remains loopback-only; this PR adds no new network trust boundary.

title: fix(cloud): load project settings from the control plane
body: ## What Cloud projects now load their settings from the cloud control plane and render read-only, laid out like the local settings page. ## Why Fixes #4966. `ProjectSettingsForm` queried the local daemon by project id with no branch on where the project lives: ``` line 82 apiClient.GET("/api/v1/projects/{id}") loads the project line 258 apiClient.PUT("/api/v1/projects/{id}") saves it ``` A cloud project is only ever registered with the cloud control plane, so that lookup could never succeed. Every cloud project showed "Loading project settings..." and then the daemon's raw `Unknown project (PROJECT_NOT_FOUND)` text, in every section, with no recovery. `SettingsDialog` had the same gap one level up: it offered a Save control for any project settings, including one whose form the cloud path does not render. This is the same bug class as #4570, which fixed the open-in-editor control by branching on where the session lives. ## How Read-only rather than editable was agreed with maintainers before implementation, because the cloud contract cannot back an editable form today: `UpdateProjectInput` accepts only `displayName` and `defaultBranch`, and the cloud project carries none of the agent, workflow, intake or reviewer configuration the local form edits. - **New `useCloudProject(projectId)` hook.** Two surfaces need the same answer, so the lookup lives in one place. The cloud contract has no single-project read (only `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/orgs/{orgId}/projects/{projectId}`), so it resolves against the already-cached project list; React Query dedupes it. - **`isKnownLocal` is deliberately not "no cloud project found".** A pending list is not proof that an id is local, so the local lookup is held until the answer is known. That is what prevents the 404 flashing during resolution. A local-only deployment resolves immediately, because the cloud query is disabled there. - **`CloudSettingsBody` composes the existing read-only primitives** (`ProjectSettingsValueRow` inside `ProjectSettingsSection`) rather than reusing `ProjectGeneralSettingsView`, whose name row is an editable input. Composing the primitives is what guarantees nothing is editable. - **Sections without a cloud equivalent say so** instead of rendering an empty shell, matching how scratch projects already report the sections they do not support. - **`SettingsBody` is untouched**, so the local path keeps its existing behavior; the only change on that side is the `enabled` guard on the query. Notes for reviewers: - Identity shows name, id, type and repository. `Path` is dropped because a cloud project has no local checkout. - Workflow shows the default branch, which is where the local page keeps it. It is a single row because cloud has no session prefix or reviewers yet. The local page groups it under a visible "Worktrees" heading; that heading is omitted for cloud, which has no worktrees. - If a cloud project disappears while its settings are open, the panel falls back to the local lookup and reports that it could not load. That matches what already happens for a removed local project, so it is left as is. - #4910 refactors this same file. Happy to rebase on top of it if that lands first. ## Testing ``` npm run typecheck clean npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer 188 files, 2731 passed ``` New tests, all verified to fail when the fix is reverted (7 failures): - `ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx` — the local daemon is never asked for a cloud project; identity renders as read-only values with no textbox and no edit control; the default branch renders read-only under workflow; agents and intake report no cloud equivalent; and a local project still loads from the daemon while the cloud offering is on. - `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` — the save control is offered for a local project, withheld for a cloud project, and withheld until the project is known to be local. Verified manually on Linux against a local control plane (`npm run cloud:local`, docker sandbox provider): a cloud project opens all four sections with no error and no editable control and no Save button, and a local project's settings still load, edit and save unchanged. The 9 test files failing outside this area (`src/landing/**`, `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`) fail identically on a clean `main`: the landing subpackage is not installed and `better-sqlite3` bindings are unavailable in this environment. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Bug]: A deleted cloud project reserves its repository URL forever
body: ### Summary Deleting a cloud project and then creating a new one for the same repository fails with "The resource conflicts with an existing record." The URL can never be used again in that organization, even though no visible project holds it. Deleting a project archives its row, but the uniqueness rule on the repository URL still counts archived rows. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run a cloud control plane locally: `npm run cloud:local` 2. Create a cloud project for any repository, for example https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife 3. Delete that project 4. Create a new cloud project for the same repository URL ### Expected behavior Creating a project for that repository succeeds, because no live project holds it any more. Only a second live project for the same repository in the same organization should be refused. ### Actual behavior Creation fails and the repository URL stays unusable in that organization permanently: POST /api/cloud/v1/orgs/{orgId}/projects -> 409 {"error":"Conflict","code":"conflict","message":"The resource conflicts with an existing record."} The message names neither the repository nor the archived project, so there is no way to tell from the product why the URL is refused. ### AO version commit 7e8a66229 (upstream/main) ### Environment Ubuntu Linux 6.14 x86_64, Node v22.16.0, local cloud control plane via npm run cloud:local (provider=docker) ### Logs / extra context ```shell Root cause Two migrations disagree about what deletion means. The founding schema created the projects table when deletion still removed the row: 00001_founding_schema.sql:150 UNIQUE (org_id, repository_url) Project deletion later became a soft delete, so session history, events and the audit trail survive it: 00013_project_archival.sql ADD COLUMN archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ CREATE INDEX ... WHERE archived_at IS NULL That migration scoped the listing index to live rows but left the uniqueness rule untouched, so it still counts archived rows. `ArchiveProject`(cloud/internal/postgres/project_session_store.go:142) sets archived_at and keeps the row, so the repository URL stays reserved for good. The insert then fails with 23505, which normalizeConstraintError maps to the generic ErrConflict, which the API renders as the message above. All three project creation paths share the constraint and are affected: plain create, GitHub project creation, and GitHub scratch creation. Verified on the running local stack: create project for Spoon-Knife -> 201 delete it -> 202 create again, same URL -> 409 conflict Notes - Nothing uses repository_url as a lookup key, and no ON CONFLICT clause targets this constraint, so scoping it to live rows has no other caller to break. - The schema already uses this pattern elsewhere, for example ao_org_invitations_pending_email_key scopes uniqueness to pending invitations. - Related but separate: #4891 covers archiving stranding pull requests on local projects. ``` ### Before submitting - [x] I searched existing issues for duplicates - [x] I removed secrets / tokens from logs and screenshots

title: fix(cloud): stop archived projects reserving their repository URL
body:
## What

Deleting a cloud project no longer reserves its repository URL. A repository whose project was deleted can be used for a new project again, while one active project per repository per organization still holds.

## Why

Fixes #4971.

Two migrations disagreed about what deletion means.

`00001_founding_schema.sql:150` created the table when deletion still removed the row, so its rule covered every row:

```sql
UNIQUE (org_id, repository_url)
```

`00013_project_archival.sql` then made deletion an archive, so session history, events and the audit trail survive it. It scoped the listing index to live rows but left the uniqueness rule counting archived ones:

```sql
ADD COLUMN archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
CREATE INDEX ao_projects_org_active_created_idx ... WHERE archived_at IS NULL;
```

`ArchiveProject` keeps the row, so a deleted project held its repository URL for good. Creating a project for that repository failed with a conflict that no visible project explained, and the URL was unusable in that organization from then on. All three creation paths share the constraint: plain create, GitHub project, and GitHub scratch.

## How

Scope the rule to live projects with a partial unique index, the way `ao_org_invitations_pending_email_key` already scopes uniqueness to pending invitations:

```sql
ALTER TABLE ao_projects DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ao_projects_org_id_repository_url_key;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ao_projects_org_active_repository_url_key
    ON ao_projects(org_id, repository_url)
    WHERE archived_at IS NULL;
```

The conflict a caller can still hit now names itself. Creating a second live project for a repository returns `PROJECT_REPOSITORY_EXISTS` with a message that says which rule was hit, following the shape `SANDBOX_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` already uses, rather than the generic conflict envelope that gave the user nothing to act on.

Notes for reviewers:

- Only that one violation is special-cased. `normalizeProjectConstraintError` matches the index by name and defers to `normalizeConstraintError` for everything else, so other unique, check and foreign-key violations keep their existing mapping.
- `UpdateProject` is deliberately left on the generic path: it accepts only `displayName` and `defaultBranch`, so it cannot reach this constraint.
- Nothing depended on the dropped constraint. No foreign key references it (all three reference `ao_projects(org_id, id)`, which is untouched), no `ON CONFLICT` targets it, `repository_url` is never used as a lookup key, no caller branches on `ErrConflict`, and no client branches on the error `code`. The spec needs no change either: `ErrorEnvelope.code` is a free-form string and the other specific codes are not enumerated there.
- The index cannot fail to build on an existing database, because the constraint it replaces was strictly broader.
- The fix is retroactive and needs no data cleanup: every repository URL that an archived project is holding today becomes available again the moment the migration runs, with no backfill and no manual intervention.
- The down migration restores the original constraint, which requires that no organization holds both an archived and a live project for the same repository. That is a state this migration deliberately allows, so the comment says to resolve such pairs before rolling back.

## Testing

```
cd cloud
go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l .     clean
go test -race ./...                              pass
```

`normalizeProjectConstraintError` is covered by a table test: the live repository index reports the project conflict, wrapped errors are still recognized, and other unique, check and foreign-key violations plus unknown errors keep their existing mapping. There is no PostgreSQL harness in this module to hang a store-level test on, so the schema behavior was verified against a running control plane instead.

Verified end to end on Linux against `npm run cloud:local` (docker sandbox provider).

Before the migration:

```
create project for octocat/Spoon-Knife   201
delete it                                202
create again, same URL                   409 conflict
                                         "The resource conflicts with an existing record."
```

After the migration, the same URL, still held by archived rows:

```
create again, same URL                   201

display_name | repository_url                         | state
before-test  | https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife | archived
after-fix    | https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife | archived
reuse-test   | https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife | LIVE
```

The rule still holds, and now explains itself:

```
create a second live project, same URL   409 PROJECT_REPOSITORY_EXISTS
                                         "This organization already has a project for that repository."
```

The last two were driven through the desktop app's New cloud project dialog, not only the API.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(codex): Settings auth can disagree with launch readiness
body:
## Bug

AO can show the active Codex account as signed in and ready in **Settings**, and the native CLI can report `Logged in using ChatGPT`, while the next Codex worker spawn fails immediately with:

```text
Add or sign in to a Codex account in Settings before starting a Codex session
(CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED)
```

The failed spawn then changes the same active account from `authorized` to `unauthorized`. Returning to or focusing Settings can change it back to `authorized`, so the UI oscillates between a reassuring display result and the stricter launch result.

**Source:** live maintainer report and reproduction, 2026-09-05  
**AO:** `0.12.11-nightly.202609041654`, macOS arm64  
**Codex CLI:** `0.153.4`  
**Analyzed against:** `7e8a662296d6d3015e89766007b4bb92937d6a23`  
**Introduced by:** #4722, merged as `c02317774`  
**Confidence:** High — the live API transition and the two different `account/read` request modes agree exactly.

No credential contents were inspected or logged.

## Reproduction

1. Have AO's active Codex account backed by the device-global `~/.codex` login after logging out and signing into another Codex account.
2. Open or focus **Settings > Codex accounts**.
3. Observe that the active account is shown as valid and authorized. `codex login status` also reports `Logged in using ChatGPT`.
4. Spawn a new Codex worker.
5. Observe `CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED`; no partial session is created.
6. Read the account state again. The active account is now fresh/unauthorized with “Codex needs authentication.”
7. Focus Settings or call the account ensure endpoint again. The same active account returns to fresh/authorized with “Codex appears signed in.”

## Live evidence

Before spawn, three stable reads of `GET /api/v1/agents/codex/accounts` reported the active account as:

```text
status=valid
authentication.state=authorized
authentication.freshness=fresh
reason="Codex appears signed in."
```

`GET /api/v1/agents` also reported Codex authorized, and `codex login status` reported `Logged in using ChatGPT`.

The attempted `Hello world` Codex worker admission then failed with `CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED`. Immediately afterward, the active account was:

```text
authentication.state=unauthorized
authentication.freshness=fresh
checkedAt=2026-09-05T21:10:15Z
reason="Codex needs authentication."
```

At `2026-09-05T21:27:04Z`, `POST /api/v1/agents/codex/accounts/ensure` changed the same active account back to fresh/authorized without a new login. The inactive second account remained authorized throughout and must not mask the active account's launch readiness.

## Root cause

Settings and launch intentionally ask different authentication questions but expose both as the same `authorized` state:

- The Settings ensure path calls `ensureAuthentication(..., AgentReadinessPurposeDisplay, false)`, so its Codex `account/read` request has `refreshToken=false`: [`codex_accounts.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/7e8a662296d6d3015e89766007b4bb92937d6a23/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_accounts.go#L282-L303).
- Launch readiness calls the same function with `refreshToken=true`: [`codex_account_service.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/7e8a662296d6d3015e89766007b4bb92937d6a23/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L17-L51).
- The adapter passes that flag directly to Codex app-server's `account/read`. A non-refresh read can return an account from locally cached credentials, while the refresh-capable read can return `requiresOpenaiAuth`: [`account.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/7e8a662296d6d3015e89766007b4bb92937d6a23/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/account.go#L304-L316).
- Spawn correctly rejects the fresh unauthorized launch result: [`service.go`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/7e8a662296d6d3015e89766007b4bb92937d6a23/backend/internal/service/session/service.go#L261-L278).

This is not the AO daemon being behind the terminal login. The active managed record uses the device-global Codex home, and the native status command and Settings both prove only that account material is locally present. Spawn is the first path that asks Codex to refresh it.

The renderer's account query uses infinite stale time and relies on account events/explicit ensure writes, which can compound the confusing display lag, but the primary defect is semantic: a non-refreshing display observation is labeled fresh/authorized even though it has not established launch readiness.

## Expected behavior

- Settings must not present the active Codex account as launch-ready when the authoritative refresh-capable check will reject it.
- The active account's launch readiness must be visually distinct from “local account material exists” if both observations are retained.
- A failed launch auth check must update the visible account state and reauthentication CTA immediately, without closing/reopening Settings.
- An authorized inactive account must not make Codex look ready when the selected active account needs reauthentication.
- Successful reauthentication should restore both the Settings state and Codex worker admission.

## Suggested fix

Use one authoritative launch-ready authentication semantic for the active account. The implementation should decide whether to:

1. run a bounded refresh-capable check for the active account during Settings ensure, or
2. represent non-refresh display discovery as a separate “account present / launch not verified” state rather than `fresh/authorized`.

Avoid refreshing every inactive account merely to render the list. Preserve the existing account-mutation serialization and credential-safety boundaries. Ensure the launch failure's published account event updates the renderer cache immediately.

## Regression coverage

- Display `account/read(refreshToken=false)` returns an account, but launch `account/read(refreshToken=true)` returns `requiresOpenaiAuth`: Settings must not claim the active account is ready to launch.
- Spawn returns `CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED` and the open Settings view immediately shows the reauthentication state/CTA.
- With two accounts, an authorized inactive account cannot mask an unauthorized active account.
- After successful reauthentication, the active account becomes launch-ready and spawn proceeds.
- The account ensure/focus path cannot overwrite a fresh launch-auth failure with the weaker non-refresh result.

## Impact

New Codex workers are blocked even though AO explicitly tells the user Codex is logged in. The workaround is to sign in again, but the Settings state contradicts that instruction and can flip back to authorized after focus, making the core recovery path difficult to discover and trust.

## Related

- #4722 — introduced multi-account/global switching and the divergent display/launch checks.
- #4908 / #4924 — separate sticky account-bootstrap failure and recovery.
- #4296 — separate stale OAuth behavior in already-running Codex Chat app-servers.
- #4937 — analogous reauthentication-state/UI mismatch for Claude Code.

title: fix(codex): make Settings auth agree with launch readiness
body:
Fixes #4973.

## Problem

Settings and launch asked Codex two different questions and published both as the same `authorized` state:

- Settings ensure called `ensureAuthentication(..., Display, false)` -> `account/read(refreshToken=false)`, which can answer from locally cached credentials.
- Launch called it with `refreshToken=true`, and that read can return `requiresOpenaiAuth`.

So AO showed the active account as fresh/authorized ("Codex appears signed in"), the next Codex spawn failed with `CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED`, and focusing Settings (or calling the ensure endpoint) flipped the same account back to authorized without a new login.

## Fix

One authoritative launch-ready semantic for the active account:

- The active account -- the one every spawn launches with -- is always observed with the refresh-capable read, for display as well as launch. Inactive accounts are still not refreshed merely to render the list.
- Observations now record whether they were launch-verified. A cached display observation cannot satisfy a launch check, an in-flight display read cannot answer a joining launch request, and a non-refresh result cannot clear a fresh launch-verified failure.
- Global reconciliation's identify-the-device-account read is non-refresh, so it now goes through the same discovery guard. This was the second path that turned the account back to authorized on Settings focus.
- An unauthorized read reports no account and therefore no identity, so it no longer overwrites the slot's saved label/email/method. That keeps the account named in its reauthentication CTA and stops reconciliation from losing its identity match (which otherwise imported a duplicate account record).
- Settings' collapsed Codex summary reports the active account's authentication state instead of plan/capacity when it needs sign-in, so an authorized inactive account cannot make Codex look ready.

Account-mutation serialization and the credential-safety boundary are unchanged. No credential contents are read or logged, and no API contract changed.

## Regression coverage

Backend (`backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_launch_readiness_test.go`), against a fake Codex whose non-refresh read returns an account while its refresh-capable read returns `requiresOpenaiAuth`:

- Settings ensure does not present the active account as launch-ready, and launch agrees without repeating the native read.
- A fresh launch-auth failure survives the ensure/focus path after the display window expires.
- A display read in flight cannot clear a required reauthentication.
- An authorized inactive account does not mask the active account, and inactive accounts are never refreshed for display.
- After successful reauthentication the active account is launch-ready again and the launch check passes.

The first four fail on the pre-fix behavior.

Renderer (`CodexAccountsSection.test.tsx`):

- The reauthentication state and "Sign in again" CTA appear as soon as the failed launch's account event lands, with no refetch and without reopening Settings.
- An authorized inactive account does not mask the active account's signed-out state.
- A successful reauthentication event restores the signed-in state and summary.

## Tests run

- `go test ./internal/service/agent/`, `go test -race ./internal/service/agent/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/` -- pass.
- `go test ./...` -- pass except pre-existing environmental failures in the tmux runtime adapter, untouched by this change.
- `golangci-lint run` -- 0 issues.
- `vitest run` on the Codex account settings/hooks/event-transport suites and `npm run typecheck` -- pass (typecheck errors remain only in `packages/product-ui`, whose deps are not installed in this worktree).

## Tradeoff

Making display truthful costs one refresh-capable `account/read` for the active account per display window (5 min TTL, plus one at daemon warm-up) instead of a cheaper local read. That asks Codex to refresh the active account's token slightly more often, which is exactly the work launch already does; inactive accounts keep the cheap read. The alternative -- keeping both observations and rendering "account present / launch not verified" as a distinct state -- avoids that call but leaves users reading two auth states per account.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Accounts whose refresh legitimately fails now surface as signed-out in Settings sooner. That is the intent, but it will make #4908/#4924-style bootstrap failures more visible.
- The renderer change was verified by tests, not a live desktop preview: reproducing it in the app needs a Codex account whose cached credential no longer refreshes.

title: Cline hooks never fire on Windows: AO installs extensionless bash scripts, Cline only discovers <Event>.ps1
body:
### Reporter
Reported by @ApexYash11 via live triage session (2026-09-06).

### Commit analyzed
`847991a3ef2dcd2bc23f7698f1b1a60b716f2403` (branch `fix/cline-bypass-yolo-headless-4944`)

### Versions
- AO: dev build from the commit above (`ao version` -> `dev`), daemon on port **3001** (verified binary)
- Cline CLI: `3.0.61` via `cline.ps1` shim (`%APPDATA%/npm`)
- OS: Windows 11, PowerShell / ConPTY runtime
- Adapter baseline: `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/cline/... ./internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch/... ./internal/adapters/reviewer/cline/...` -> ok

### What happened
On Windows, Cline sessions produce **zero hook callbacks** to the daemon: no `TaskStart`, no `UserPromptSubmit`, no `stop`. Consequences:
- hook-derived activity state never updates; status is blind
- no native session id is captured -> resume (`GetRestoreCommand`) always falls back to a fresh launch
- `hooks.log` shows no entries for the session

### Where
`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/hooks.go` — `renderClineHookScript` (bash, extensionless) + `GetAgentHooks` (writes files named after the event, e.g. `TaskStart`).

### Root cause
Cline's Windows hook discovery only executes `<Event>.ps1` files (run via `powershell -File`); extensionless hooks are intentionally ignored on Windows (per Cline's hook-factory: "wrong-platform naming is silently ignored"). Independently, Windows itself cannot execute extensionless bash scripts (no shebang support).

AO writes exactly the wrong shape on Windows:
- `renderClineHookScript` emits `#!/usr/bin/env bash` scripts
- filenames are extensionless (`TaskStart`, `PreToolUse`, `TaskCancel`, `TaskComplete`, `UserPromptSubmit`)

### Repro (verified live, consistent)
1. Register any git repo, spawn a Cline worker session (daemon :3001, Windows).
2. While the session is alive, inspect the worktree: `<dataDir>/worktrees/<project>/<session>/.clinerules/hooks/` contains only extensionless scripts, **no `.ps1`**.
3. Direct exec of the extensionless hook fails:
   ```
   exec: "...\\hooks\\TaskStart": executable file not found in %PATH%
   ```
4. Control: writing the same wrapper as `TaskStart.ps1` and running `powershell -File TaskStart.ps1` succeeds and prints `{"cancel": false}` -> naming/platform is the sole blocker.
5. `hooks.log` has zero entries for the session; `ao session get <id>` shows frozen `lastActivityAt`.

A Go repro test (`TestReproIssue2_WindowsHooksNeverFire`) demonstrated all of the above against this checkout.

### Suggested fix
In `hooks.go`, branch on `runtime.GOOS == "windows"`: emit `<Event>.ps1` PowerShell wrappers (read stdin JSON, forward to the AO hook dispatcher, emit `{"cancel": false}`), mirroring the Windows branch the auggie adapter already has (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/auggie/hooks.go`). Update `UninstallHooks`/`AreHooksInstalled`/`isManagedClineHook` to recognize the `.ps1` names.

### Related but separate (same session, MEDIUM)
The wrapper body invokes bare `ao hooks cline <sub>` from PATH; on machines with a second AO install, callbacks can reach the wrong daemon. Pin the absolute daemon executable (the auggie adapter pins it too). Daemon log warning observed live: "session PATH not pinned to the daemon binary; `ao hooks` callbacks may resolve to a different ao".

Related: [#4944](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4944) (fixed by 847991a3 — `--yolo` headless conflict).

**Priority:** P1 (core Cline workflow — activity tracking and resume — broken on Windows, no workaround). **Confidence:** High (live repro + control experiment).

title: bug(cline): Windows hooks are extensionless bash scripts — Cline can't run them, status never updates and resume falls back to a fresh session
body:
## Bug

On Windows, AO installs Cline's workspace hooks as extensionless bash scripts. Cline can't run them on Windows, so AO never hears about anything the session does. Session status stays stuck and "resume" starts a new session instead of continuing the old one.

**Source:** [Discord #bug-triage](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1545910244578824302) | **Reported by:** Yash (Discord) | **Analyzed against:** `ed52364e3` (origin/main tip)
**Confidence:** High — traced both sides (AO's writer + Cline's runner)
**Priority:** P2 — core tracking + resume broken for the Cline-on-Windows combo; workaround is using a different harness or OS

## Reproduction

1. On Windows, create a Cline session in AO for any project.
2. Look in `<worktree>\.clinerules\hooks\`: AO writes `TaskStart`, `TaskCancel`, `TaskComplete`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse` — extensionless, each a bash script starting with `#!/usr/bin/env bash`.
3. Run a task in Cline. Nothing reaches AO: status never leaves its initial state, and AO's hooks log stays empty.

Proof from the reporter's worktree (`C:\Users\ACER\.ao\dev\worktrees\...`), showing the extensionless bash scripts and zero `.ps1` files:

![TaskStart hook proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-cline-windows-hooks/.issue-assets/cline-windows-hooks/taskstart-proof.png)

## Root Cause

Two sides to trace.

**AO side** — `backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/hooks.go` writes the same scripts on every OS, with no Windows branch:

- `renderClineHookScript` (line 163) hardcodes `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and a fixed body:
  `ao hooks cline <subcommand> || true` then `echo '{"cancel": false}'`.
- `GetAgentHooks` (line 85) writes each script under its bare event name (`TaskStart`, ...), mode 0700.

**Cline side** — what Cline does with those files on Windows depends on the surface:

- **Cline CLI** (what AO launches; `cline` from npm): the SDK's file-hook loader (`sdk/packages/core/src/hooks/hook-file-config.ts`) accepts extensionless files on all platforms, so the hook is *found*. But execution goes through `inferHookCommand` (`sdk/packages/core/src/hooks/hook-file-hooks.ts`, line 327): it parses the `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang down to `bash <path>` and spawns it. Windows has no `bash`, so the spawn fails (ENOENT) and the hook never runs.
- **Cline VS Code extension**: discovery itself is Windows-restricted — `findWindowsHook` (`apps/vscode/src/core/hooks/hook-factory.ts`, line 988) only looks for `<HookName>.ps1` and its comment says "Extensionless hooks are intentionally ignored on Windows."

Either way the result is the same: on Windows, none of AO's five hook scripts ever execute.

**Impact chain:** no hook fires → `ao hooks cline session-start/stop` never runs → no activity transitions and no native session id is ever captured. `GetRestoreCommand` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cline/cline.go`, line 126) returns `ok=false` when `MetadataKeyAgentSessionID` is empty, so "resume" silently falls back to a fresh launch with no prior context. Status stays stuck on its initial derived state.

The reporter's screenshot summary said Windows "won't execute" the file because it has no extension. For the CLI that AO launches, the more precise mechanism is: the file is discovered but its shebang demands `bash`, which Windows doesn't have. The fix target is identical either way.

## Fix

In `GetAgentHooks`, branch on `runtime.GOOS`:

- **Windows:** write `<Event>.ps1` per hook with the same logic in PowerShell — read stdin, pipe it to `ao hooks cline <subcommand>`, print `{"cancel": false}`. Keep the `# ao-managed-cline-hook` marker line (it's a valid PowerShell comment, so `isManagedClineHook` idempotency and uninstall keep working unchanged).
- **Unix:** keep the current extensionless bash scripts.

Why `.ps1` on Windows: it satisfies both Cline surfaces — the VS Code extension's `findWindowsHook` looks for exactly `<HookName>.ps1`, and the SDK's `inferHookCommand` maps `.ps1` to `powershell -File <path>` on Windows. Don't write `.ps1` on Unix: Unix discovery ignores it (extension surface) or would demand `pwsh` (SDK path).

Also confirm `ao` resolves inside the hook's environment on Windows (the session PATH pin should cover it, but it's worth a check when implementing).

Tests: extend `cline_test.go` with a GOOS-dependent expectation (or inject the platform) asserting `.ps1` content + marker on Windows and unchanged bash on Linux/macOS.

## Related

- [#3410](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3410) — OpenCode Windows hooks invoked via `sh -c`; same family: Unix shell assumptions breaking Windows hooks
- [#4596](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4596) — closed Codex variant: Windows hook executable invoked via PowerShell call operator
- [#3110](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3110) — Windows PostToolUse hooks failing with exit code 1

title: fix(codex): preserve explicit model selection
body:
## What
Preserve explicit Codex model choices and stop showing the catalog default when it is not the selected model. For example, a Nano-configured thread or an unlisted Nano selection must not be displayed as Astra.

## Why
A user reported that Nano worked in PowerShell but appeared to switch to Astra and fail in AO. Investigation confirmed misleading model labels and an orchestrator instruction to retry rejected explicit models using the default. The original Windows launch failure remains unverified because the exact error and successful command were not supplied.

## How
- Use the effective Codex thread model when marking the conversation catalog default; clear the generic default when that model is absent.
- Preserve an explicit model ID in the picker when the catalog lacks it, without borrowing another model's reasoning-effort choices.
- Instruct the orchestrator to report a rejected model and request an alternative instead of dropping `--model` automatically. This is a prompt-policy change, not a new CLI enforcement mechanism.
- Add regression coverage for configured and unlisted models and the orchestrator policy.

## Testing
- Reproduced the backend default mismatch and frontend `Astra High` mislabel before the fix; focused backend tests and all 15 picker tests passed afterward.
- Current-base `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and formatting check passed.
- API regeneration has no drift; Cloud client and product UI typechecks, tests, and package dry-runs passed.
- Remote CI passed: frontend typechecks and full Vitest suite, renderer smoke, lint, API drift, secret scan, CLI E2E on Linux/macOS/Windows, fresh-install container, and Windows workspace tests. Go build/test is still running.

- No original-account Windows reproduction or screenshots are claimed.

title: feat(chat): show Cursor's Ask and Agent as execution modes
body:
## Problem

Cursor Chat advertises three execution postures in a single ACP `mode` option. Captured from a live `cursor-agent acp` `session/new`:

```json
"modes": { "currentModeId": "agent", "availableModes": [
  { "id": "agent", "name": "Agent" },
  { "id": "plan",  "name": "Plan"  },
  { "id": "ask",   "name": "Ask"   } ] }
```

`TurnSettingsBar` split that option with a **global** `plan|agent` word list. `Ask` matched neither, so it fell through into the approval menu, and the execution control was left holding choices it could not render as a Plan switch.

## Change

**Classify per option, not globally.** `executionChoiceValues` inspects one option's own advertised choices. Plan and Agent name a posture wherever they appear; **Ask only counts as an execution mode when the same option also advertises Agent**. A harness whose `mode` option means "Ask for approval" is untouched — that stays a permission policy. Classification runs on the provider's advertised choices *before* AO synthesises Claude's Agent Mode, so that synthesis can't retroactively promote an approval choice.

**Generalised the picker.** `ExecutionModePicker` names the choice currently in force and lists every advertised posture, sending the provider's own opaque value (`ask`, `agent`, `plan` — and bracketed model ids like `grok-4.6[effort=high,fast=true]` elsewhere) untouched. Labels may normalise for display; **no wire value is ever hardcoded or re-derived from a label.** This covers Ask/Agent, Plan/Agent and future multi-mode providers.

**Layout.** The two-choice Plan/Agent pair keeps its switch inside the model menu, exactly as before. A provider with more postures than that gets its own trigger instead of being buried under the model picker — a choice that changes whether the agent may edit at all shouldn't hide behind a model name.

**Scope kept clean.** Cursor's approval policies stay in Project Settings; manual/default, accept edits, auto review and bypass permissions are not mixed into this picker. The ACP `agent` option (provider-owned multi-agent internals) remains hidden and is not confused with AO's Switch agent.

## Tests

13 new cases in `TurnSettingsBar.test.tsx` (27 total, all passing): paired option classification, initial Ask, selecting both exact advertised values, exactly one execution control, Ask absent from the approval menu, a lone approval-flavoured Ask staying a permission, unchanged Plan/Agent switch and its `manual` wire value, unchanged Claude and generic/Codex approval menus, and no Switch-agent confusion — plus a group built from the real captured Cursor payload.

## Verification

- `npm test -- TurnSettingsBar` → **27 passed**
- `npm run typecheck` → **clean**
- Renderer bundle build (`vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts`) → **succeeds**. Note: this repo has no `npm run build` script in `frontend/`; this is the equivalent bundling step.
- Full renderer suite: 3719 passed. The 9 unrelated failing files (landing-page tests with uninstalled deps; `SessionsBoard`/`GlobalSettingsForm`/`browser-history-store` timeouts under parallel load) were confirmed **pre-existing** — they reproduce identically with and without this change, and pass in isolation on both.
- **Real Electron app** from this checkout (isolated mode, daemon `127.0.0.1:3002`, `~/.ao/dev/s285/data`): launched, created a live Cursor Chat session, and round-tripped the real option through the same endpoint the picker writes to — `GET config-options` returned the three-posture `mode` option, `PATCH mode {"value":"ask"}` returned `currentValue: "ask"`, and `"agent"` restored it. That is the exact data path `TurnSettingsBar` renders and writes.

### Environment limitation

Pixel-level confirmation in the Electron window was **not** possible: `screencapture` fails with `could not create image from display` because this environment lacks macOS Screen Recording permission. The app ran and its live Cursor data path was verified end-to-end via the daemon API, and rendering is covered by component tests built from that same captured payload — but I did not visually see the trigger render "Ask"/"Agent" on screen.
