title: Windows: maximized embedded browser blacks out behind tooltips and menus
body:
## Bug
On Windows, the embedded browser viewport turns completely black when AO is maximized and a renderer-owned overlay appears above the native browser view. This reproduces both with toolbar tooltips and the Browser Controls three-dot dropdown.

**Platform:** Windows
**Reported from:** Local AO desktop testing
**Analyzed against:** `9202d685162ec1d4bccca7865757b77c16163ffd`
**Confidence:** Medium — the composition boundary is identified, but the attempted workaround was reverted after local testing.
**Priority:** P2 — the browser remains usable when overlays are closed or the window is not maximized, but common controls become visually unusable in maximized mode.

## Reproduction
1. Launch the AO Electron desktop app on Windows.
2. Open a session's embedded Browser panel and navigate to a page.
3. Maximize the AO window.
4. Hover a browser-toolbar button until its tooltip opens.
5. Observe that the browser/content area becomes black while the tooltip is visible.
6. Click the Browser Controls three-dot button.
7. Observe the same blackout while the dropdown menu is open.

## Expected behavior
Tooltips and dropdown menus should render over the embedded browser without changing, blanking, or blacking out the page beneath them. Tooltip placement should remain conventional; moving tooltips above the toolbar is not an acceptable workaround.

## Observed behavior
The content beneath the overlay becomes a solid black surface for the lifetime of the tooltip or menu, especially when the native window is maximized.

## Working root-cause analysis
AO renders the shell and live browser in sibling Electron `WebContentsView` surfaces. Renderer-owned Radix overlays require the transparent shell surface to be raised over the native browser surface. On Windows, especially for a maximized `BaseWindow`, the transparent sibling surface can be composed as opaque black instead of preserving the browser pixels below it.

Bounds nudges, visibility toggles, and compositor refreshes do not reliably repair this because they still depend on unsupported or unstable transparent sibling composition. Related Electron reports:

- https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/45104
- https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/40515
- https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/1690

## Attempted fix and current state
A Windows-only captured-frame handoff was attempted in commit `3904594a0`, then reverted by `7eee2fbb2` after local testing showed the change was not acceptable. The issue remains open and needs a solution that is validated in the real maximized Windows Electron window.

## Acceptance criteria
- No blackout when any browser-toolbar tooltip opens in a maximized Windows window.
- No blackout while Browser Controls or its nested menus are open.
- No tooltip-placement workaround.
- Browser tabs, device presets, profiles, DevTools controls, and resize behavior remain functional.
- Verified in the actual Electron desktop app on Windows, not only renderer tests.

## Related
- https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4958 — browser controls PR where the regression was observed.
- https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4955 — related toolbar/import UX work; does not cover this blackout.

## Evidence
Two local screenshots demonstrate the tooltip and Browser Controls menu cases. They are intentionally not uploaded because they contain a local AO preview URL and may expose session metadata.

title: feat(spawn): make task creation crash-safe and recoverable
body:
## Why

A spawn is a chain of side effects — session row, worktree, provisioning, attachments, provider process — and a daemon crash or a cancelled request can land between any two of them. Nothing durable recorded how far it got, so the next boot could neither finish the launch nor safely clean it up. Two concrete failures fall out of that: a worktree survives with no session claiming it, and a session survives claiming a controller that never existed.

This adds a durable `spawn_phase` and hangs recovery off it.

## Scope: Cursor only

`domain.SpawnPhaseTrackingEnabled` gates the whole feature to the Cursor harness, by product decision.

To be explicit about what that does and does not mean: the underlying failure is **not** Cursor-specific. `resumeAgentRecordWithPolicy` raises `ErrIncompleteHandle` (surfaced as `SESSION_INCOMPLETE_HANDLE`) with no harness branch at all, so a Codex or Claude Code session can be stranded in exactly the same state — "The agent controller stopped", a Resume that always fails — and this PR deliberately leaves that unfixed for them. The gate limits rollout blast radius, not the reach of the bug.

The gate is the single harness check in the feature, and it sits at the *source* of the fact rather than at each consumer: a tracked harness seeds `preparing` and checkpoints its workspace; every other harness seeds straight to `controller_ready` and behaves exactly as before — no checkpoint, no worktree row at spawn time, no recovery, no relabelled UI. Reconcile, Retry routing, and the renderer all still read the phase alone, so widening this later is a one-function change.

## What

**`spawn_phase`: `preparing` → `workspace_ready` → `controller_ready`**

Migration `0128` adds the column. Live rows with no controller identity migrate to `preparing`; everything else — including terminated rows, whose history is closed and must not be re-reconciled — keeps `controller_ready`. Rows written before the column existed read back as `controller_ready`, so an upgrade never makes an established session look half-spawned.

**The checkpoint**

Immediately after `createSessionWorkspace` succeeds — before per-project provisioning, attachment writes, provider startup, or ACP negotiation, all of which can block for minutes — the spawn commits the workspace path, repo path, branch, original prompt, and resolved model together with `workspace_ready`, plus an active `session_worktrees` row for single-repo projects. Before it commits, no worktree is attributed to the session; after it, the worktree is the user's. The write is guarded on `spawn_phase = 'preparing'` in SQL, so a retry or a late write from an abandoned attempt cannot move an advanced session backwards.

**`controller_ready` is never published without a controller identity.** The phase advances inside the same lifecycle write as the runtime handle/launch id (TUI) or Chat controller generation, alongside the workspace metadata it describes.

**Bounded, cancellation-proof rollback**

Every rollback path now runs on `context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), spawnCleanupTimeout)`. The request context is usually already cancelled by the time rollback runs — that cancellation is frequently *why* the spawn failed — so reusing it made every cleanup call fail instantly in exactly the case where cleanup matters most. Rollback destroys only workspaces it confirms safe (never force-removing a dirty worktree), keeps the `session_worktrees` record when a destroy is refused so a worktree still on disk stays discoverable, retracts the checkpoint and deletes the seed row when the workspace is confirmed gone, and otherwise terminates the session while preserving the workspace.

**Recovery**

| Phase | Durable reality | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `preparing`, no workspace | Only a row exists | Delete the seed row |
| `preparing`, with workspace | Migrated from an older build | Promote, then recover |
| `workspace_ready` | Worktree is real; no controller committed | Reopen worktree, reapply hooks and standing instructions, start the selected Codex/Claude/Cursor provider **fresh**, replay the checkpointed prompt |
| `controller_ready` | Controller identity committed | Ordinary native resume |

Fresh is the only correct start below `controller_ready`: there is no provider conversation to resume, and because the prompt was never delivered to any controller, replaying it there delivers it **exactly once**. Correspondingly, a Chat session with no provider conversation id may fresh-launch **only** at `workspace_ready` — anywhere else an empty id means the id was lost, not that none was minted, and starting fresh would silently abandon a live conversation.

**UI**

`spawnPhase` and a derived `workspaceAvailable` flow through the API. An unfinished spawn shows **Starting agent** / **Preparing workspace** instead of a stopped-controller alarm, and offers no Resume — there is no conversation to resume. Open shell appears only for a checkpointed workspace. A recovery that failed after the checkpoint shows **Agent failed to start**, **Your workspace was preserved.**, and **Retry agent**, which re-runs the interrupted-spawn fresh recovery rather than a native resume. The inspector and command palette relabel the same action for that case (all 8 locales updated).

**Topbar**

`Session workspace is not available.` was rendering as a red error whenever the worktree was missing — true during startup, but misleading, since nothing is wrong and there is nothing for the user to fix. A spawn in progress now shows a neutral `Preparing workspace…` status instead. The launch actions stay disabled either way: there is genuinely nothing to open yet.

## Tests

New coverage for the timeout/crash points: checkpoint visible before anything slow; pre-checkpoint failure leaves no worktree and no row; rollback completes after request cancellation; a dirty worktree is preserved with its record; seed-drop, fresh recovery, native-resume-preserved, and failed-recovery-preserves-workspace reconcile paths; retry-uses-fresh-recovery; Chat prompt delivered exactly once and not re-delivered at `controller_ready`; store checkpoint guards; migration classification; lifecycle `controller_ready` commit and its identity guard; and the UI status/action rules.

**Run after rebase onto `66fb21ae5`:** `npm run sqlc`, `npm run api`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), `npm run frontend:typecheck`, plus `go test` on `session_manager`, `lifecycle`, `httpd/...`, `storage/...`, and the touched frontend suites.

### Rebase notes

Rebased onto current `main`. Two things this PR previously carried are now upstream's and were dropped from the diff: the `sqlc.yaml` tab fix and the `agent_switches` `failure_point` projection reorder both landed independently, so only the `sessions.spawn_phase` override remains in `sqlc.yaml`. `0127` was taken by `0127_session_permissions.sql`, so this migration is now `0128` (ledger and migration test updated). `seedRecord` merges cleanly with the new `Metadata.Permissions` seed, and `InsertSession`/the session `SELECT` lists carry both `session_permissions` and `spawn_phase`. One upstream test, `TestRememberProjectPermissionsPinsExistingSessions`, compared a read-back record against an unnormalized in-memory one; it already normalized `Mode` for exactly this reason, so it now normalizes `SpawnPhase` alongside it.

**Pre-existing failures, unrelated and reproduced on the base commit:** four `TestSpawn_*MissingBinary*` / `*ValidatesBinaryAfterEnvPrefix` cases fail on this machine with `tmux required on macOS but AO's configured, bundled, or system tmux was not found`. Ten frontend suites fail for environment reasons (uninstalled `src/landing` deps, plus `browser-history-store`, `GlobalSettingsForm`, `MarkdownFileView`, and a Cursor-button test) — none touch files in this PR.

## Omitted

The daemon-owned background spawn operation (moving the launch off the request goroutine entirely) is deliberately **not** in this PR. It changes the ownership of the whole spawn path and would obscure the crash-safety change this PR is about; it remains a clean follow-up now that the durable phase exists.

title: fix(updater): recover from a staged build the installer rejects
body:
Makes a rejected install **recoverable** instead of a dead end, and restores the update-hop coverage that should have caught it.

> **Scope note.** This does **not** fix #4254. What corrupts the occasional extraction is still undiagnosed — an earlier transport-truncation theory of mine was disproved (Node's `server.close()` is graceful, and the operation lock is wider than I claimed). This PR is a resilience and honesty layer: stop promising a restart that cannot work, and say something actionable when it fails.

## What is actually wrong

Not signing, not packaging. Both published ZIPs for the hop in the latest report (v0.12.10 → v0.12.11-nightly.202609052046) were independently hash-matched, `codesign --deep --strict` verified, stapled and Gatekeeper-accepted, and the same hop installed cleanly on my machine today (`ShipIt_stderr.log`: `2026-09-05 14:44:52 Installation completed successfully`, five successful installs over five days, zero errors). Nothing here touches signing, packaging, or the nightly no-DMG policy.

Two separate defects turn a *single* install rejection into a permanent one, and hide it from CI.

### 1. The retry cannot possibly work

`MacUpdater` re-emits every native Squirrel failure onto electron-updater's own `error` event:

```js
this.nativeUpdater.on("error", it => { ...; this.emit("error", it) })   // MacUpdater.js:18
```

so ShipIt's `did not pass validation: code failed to satisfy specified code requirement(s)` arrives in our error handler — where it was treated as a generic check failure, and on the automatic path suppressed entirely.

Then, from the published `electron-updater@6.8.9` tarball:

```js
async validateDownloadedPath(updateFile, updateInfo, fileInfo, logger) {
    if (this.versionInfo != null && this.file === updateFile && this.fileInfo != null) {
        // update has already been downloaded from this running instance
        // check here only existence, not checksum
        if (isEqual(...) && (await pathExists(updateFile))) return updateFile
```

Once the running instance has downloaded a build, the cached copy is re-served on **existence alone** — never re-hashed — and nothing in electron-updater clears that cache when the *native install* fails. So every subsequent check hands Squirrel the identical staged bytes rather than a fresh download. Whether that then fails again depends on where the fault actually is: a maintainer's machine recovered on its own within ~60s on 2026-09-06, so "fails forever" is **not** supportable — but the UI keeps offering a restart-to-install with nothing having re-verified it, and the archive is never re-hashed while the process lives.

**Fix:** when a build is staged and the error is an install rejection, disarm the staged build, drop the cached pending download so the next check becomes a real download-and-verify instead of a replay, and broadcast an actionable message rather than a raw Squirrel dump. This branch runs *before* the automatic-check suppression, because suppress-and-retry is precisely what does not work for this class.

### 2. There was no update-hop coverage, and its absence was invisible

`scripts/e2e-mac-update.mjs` learns that an update actually **staged** by waiting on an `AO_E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL` listener in `auto-updater.ts` (added by #3294). An unrelated reformat in #3012 (`9caafbee8`, 2026-07-31) deleted it:

```
$ git log --oneline -S"E2E_UPDATE_SENTINEL_ENV" -- frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts
9caafbee8 fix(updater): suppress auto-update error dialogs ... (#3012)   <- removed
0bdfbe6b6 feat(macos): release hardening ...                (#3294)     <- added
```

The guard (`assertSentinelCapable`) only inspects a **built** `app.asar`, and it fails by *refusing to run* with a message about picking a newer baseline. So the failure reads as "you chose an old baseline", not "the app no longer emits the signal" — and the macOS update-hop job has been unrunnable against **any** baseline for five weeks. I verified the string is absent from the real published v0.12.10 bundle.

**Fix:** restore the listener (verbatim from #3294, still hung off the *native* updater — electron-updater's own `update-downloaded` fires before Squirrel has fetched anything, so keying on it stages nothing), and assert the coupling from a unit test so a future tidy-up fails in the same commit instead of silently disabling a job. Verified the guard bites: renaming the constant fails the new test.

## Scope, and what I deliberately did not do

- **The direct-download remediation after repeated failures stays with #3528.** This PR only stops the loop and replaces the raw Squirrel string with something actionable.
- **The pre-v0.11.0 baseline hop stays with #3288** — and it needs design work first, not just a matrix entry: v0.10.0 predates the sentinel, so it can never signal staging and `assertSentinelCapable` will reject it by construction. Testing that baseline needs a different staging signal (polling the ShipIt cache dir).
- **No free-space / ENOSPC handling.** Ruled out by the entry-order evidence below, and the maintainer confirms disk space was not a problem on the affected Mac. A disk-space preflight (#3528) would not have prevented this.

## Reproduction and evidence

Disk space is **ruled out**, not merely unconfirmed — see the elimination below. No free-space handling is added here.

Fully isolated: separate `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `AO_DATA_DIR`, `AO_RUN_FILE`, Electron `userData`, updater cache and ShipIt cache, launched with `env -i`. Production AO data, the installed app and the real updater cache were never touched. Adequate free disk throughout (>9 GB).

### The published artifact is sound (independently re-verified)

Downloaded `Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.12.11-nightly.202609052046.zip` fresh: size `176688854` = feed exactly; SHA-512 `RQ/iTIQvANcRTh2f…qA==` = feed exactly; `ditto -x -k` rc=0; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` rc=0; **passes `-R` against the running app's designated requirement** (the one ShipIt actually checks); `stapler validate` OK; `spctl` accepted as Notarized Developer ID.

### What the error string actually means

Electron v33.4.11 patches Squirrel.Mac (`patches/squirrel.mac/fix_use_kseccschecknestedcode_kseccsstrictvalidate_in_the_sec.patch`), so the effective verify call is:

```objc
SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors(staticCode,
    kSecCSCheckNestedCode | kSecCSStrictValidate | kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures,
    (__bridge SecRequirementRef)self.requirement, &validityError);   // = 0x19
```

against the *running* app's designated requirement. The patch exists precisely "to ensure Squirrel.Mac validates the nested bundles (nested Frameworks)". `codesign(1)` applies its own defaults and cannot model this, so I called the API directly and mutated the verified bundle one way at a time:

| Mutation of the staged bundle | `0x1` | `0x9` | **`0x19` (effective)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| control / all xattrs stripped | PASS | PASS | **PASS** |
| root executable removed or zero-length | -67062 | -67062 | **-67062** |
| nested helper `.app` executable removed | -67062 | -67062 | **-67062** |
| `Electron Framework` / `Squirrel.framework` binary removed | -67062 | -67062 | **-67062** |
| `_CodeSignature/` removed | -67023 | -67023 | **-67023** |
| `Resources/daemon/ao`, `tmux`, `agent-browser` zeroed | -67054 | -67054 | **-67054** |

`-67062` = `errSecCSUnsigned` = *"code object is not signed at all"*. Identical across all three flag sets.

So the report means: **the staged bundle's root code object, or a nested helper `.app`/framework binary, is missing or unsigned.** Seal damage (-67023) and sealed-resource damage (-67054) are excluded. The error cannot distinguish root from nested.

This also confirms the two reports in the issue are different failures: the original v0.10.0 one (`code failed to satisfy specified code requirement(s)`) is a requirement failure, so the AppleDouble/symlink theory does not explain this one.

### Reproduced: the repeated-request loop strips a staged bundle

Ran a real **v0.12.10** baseline against the live Nightly feed, fully isolated. It resolved and downloaded `0.12.11-nightly.202609052046` (arm64). Sampling the ShipIt staging directory once a second:

```
17:24:54  update.okxiJh2  exe=69632   helper=ABSENT   fw=0  plist=ABSENT   <- extracting
17:24:57  update.okxiJh2  exe=69632   helper=122000   fw=8  plist=ok       <- complete, valid
17:39:57  update.okxiJh2  exe=ABSENT  helper=122000   fw=8  plist=ok       <- *** executable gone ***
17:39:58  update.4hDq9mS  exe=69632   helper=ABSENT   fw=0  plist=ABSENT   <- next request stages afresh
17:40:00  update.4hDq9mS  exe=69632   helper=122000   fw=8  plist=ok
```

At **17:39:57** — 15 minutes on the dot after the first staging, one second before the next request — the completed staging directory had its **main executable removed while `Info.plist`, the helpers and all 8 frameworks remained**. That is byte-for-byte the `root executable removed` row above, i.e. **exactly the state that yields `errSecCSUnsigned`**. 9 install requests were recorded in ~20 minutes.

So the pre-#4849 repeated-request loop demonstrably produces the precise corrupt staging state this bug reports. What I did *not* observe is a verification landing inside that window — this run's install completed successfully and the app ended on `0.12.11-nightly.202609052046`. The corrupt state and the race window are reproduced; the collision itself remains timing-dependent, which fits the intermittency and the self-healing in #4175.

### Why truncation — and therefore ENOSPC — cannot be the cause

Entry order in the published ZIP (7,152 files):

| Entry | Position |
|---|---|
| `Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources` | **#5** |
| `Contents/MacOS/agent-orchestrator` | **#7** |
| `Contents/Info.plist` | **#7,151 (last)** |

The executable comes out essentially first and `Info.plist` last, so any short read loses `Info.plist` and keeps the executable — the opposite of the observed failure. Confirmed empirically: `ditto -x -k` on a 116 MB prefix of the 176 MB ZIP produced a full 69,632-byte `MacOS/agent-orchestrator`, no `Info.plist`, and `bundle format unrecognized`. Independently, `ditto` exits non-zero on a short ZIP and Squirrel captures that as `SQRLZipArchiverExitCodeErrorKey`, so a truncated download surfaces as a **ZIP error, never a signature error**.

### The trigger: v0.12.10 predates #4849

```
v0.12.10           published 2026-08-31T05:19:26Z
190df05fc (#4849)  merged    2026-09-05 02:16
merge-base --is-ancestor 190df05fc v0.12.10  -> NO   (v0.12.10 lacks the fix)
merge-base --is-ancestor 190df05fc 7e8a66229 -> YES  (the offered nightly has it)
```

#4849's live measurements on a pre-fix install: a Squirrel install request **every 15 minutes** — **526 total against 10 actual installs since Jul 4** — with `update.zip` rewritten in full and ShipIt logging the next install request 3 seconds later.

So an affected v0.12.10 machine re-extracts ~175 MB into a fresh `update.XXXX/` under one shared ShipIt cache root and verifies it, every 15 minutes, indefinitely, while the user sits on a staged build. Overlapping extract → verify → cleanup cycles over one staging root can leave a tree whose nested code objects are gone while its structure survives — exactly the signature above. Consistent with my isolated repro of **142 ShipIt relaunches in ~5 minutes** and with this machine's 5/5 successes on a build that *has* #4849.

**Why that does not make this PR redundant:** #4849 fixes the trigger but is undeliverable to the population that needs it, because receiving it requires the update that is failing. A stranded v0.12.10 user cannot reach the fix by updating, so a recovery path is the only way out.

### Other prioritized hypotheses, checked

- **Architecture / feed selection — sound.** `MacUpdater.filterFilesForArch` selects on the `arm64` substring in the filename; the feed lists both slices with correct sizes/hashes; an arm64 host selects the arm64 ZIP (my isolated run logged exactly that). Rosetta hosts deliberately also take arm64.
- **Designated requirement drift — none.** The running app's DR is the standard Developer ID form (`X9LNSP8MC2`), and the freshly downloaded nightly validates against it.
- **Quarantine / translocation — not implicated.** The installed app carries no `com.apple.quarantine` and is not translocated; ShipIt clears quarantine itself (`clearQuarantineForDirectory:`), and stripping every xattr still passes verification.
- **Unsigned feature build behind a "Nightly" dropdown — ruled out.** Feature builds are properly Developer ID signed (`Authority=Developer ID Application: Prateek Karnal (X9LNSP8MC2)`, `flags=0x10000(runtime)`), verified by pulling the first 8 MB of a `pr<N>` release. Checking it did surface a separate display bug — `UpdatesSection.tsx:159` ignores a non-null `feature` pin for display unless `developerMode`, while `configureFeed` gives the pin absolute priority, so Settings can read "Nightly" while the updater is pinned to `pr<N>`. Not this bug's cause; flagged on the issue for its own ticket.
- **Cached/staged artifact identity — this is the real exposure.** `validateDownloadedPath` reuses the cached ZIP on existence alone within a process, and `updateDownloaded` serves it to Squirrel with `Content-Length` taken from the **feed** (`zipFileInfo.info.size`), never from the file on disk. Nothing re-hashes between "verified download" and "handed to Squirrel". That is why a mutated staged copy is replayed indefinitely, and it is what this PR fixes.

### Not reproduced

I could not make the hop fail on a healthy machine: it succeeded here (5/5 ShipIt installs over 5 days, including this exact hop today). The mutation is environmental — a concurrent staging cleanup or an external agent touching `~/Library/Caches` are both consistent with the signature — so this PR fixes AO's *response* to it, which is cause-agnostic, rather than guessing at the trigger.

Worth flagging separately: my isolated run reproduced **142 ShipIt relaunches in ~5 minutes**, each failing `ShipItState.plist … no such file`, and **each relaunch truncates `ShipIt_stderr.log`**. That is why reports in this family only ever carry the last error and never the first one's cause. Combined with the note at `auto-updater.ts:1240` that a cache hit "hands Squirrel a fresh install request", concurrent installers sharing one staging directory is a plausible in-house trigger for the post-extraction removal — but I have not reproduced that, so it is flagged, not claimed.

## Tests

- `staged install rejection`: clears the cached download and disarms the staged build; surfaces the failure even on an automatic check (where it would otherwise be suppressed); leaves an ordinary download failure completely alone.
- `e2e staging sentinel`: writes from the **native** updater's `update-downloaded` and *not* from electron-updater's; registers nothing when the env var is unset.
- `update-hop coverage is wired to the app`: fails if the listener is deleted again.


---

## Added: update status pushes never reached the renderer at all

Found while chasing a separate report ("Last checked" not moving until Settings is closed and reopened). It turned out to be undelivered IPC, and it **blocks this PR's own fix**, so it is fixed here rather than separately.

`broadcast()` pushed status by walking `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()`. Since **#3750** (`22c121720`, 2026-08-09) the shell is a `BaseWindow` hosting the UI in a `WebContentsView`:

```ts
mainWindow = new BaseWindow(windowOptions);
const composition = createWindowComposition({ mainWindow, WebContentsView, preload: preloadPath() });
```

`BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` only returns `BrowserWindow` instances, so that loop matched nothing and **every `updates:status` and `updates:telemetry` push has been dropped since 2026-08-09**, shipped in v0.12.11.

It stayed invisible because `invoke` replies to its own sender regardless of window type, so `updates:getStatus` kept working — the UI was correct on every open and frozen while open, which reads as a renderer caching bug. Confirmed from a user's devtools: after clicking Check, `updates.check` resolved and **no push arrived at all**.

`main.ts` already had the right pattern for its one other push — `getShellWebContents()?.send("daemon:status", …)` — so the updater now sends to the same target via an injected resolver (`main.ts` owns the shell handle), resolved per send so a recreated window keeps receiving.

**Three distinct user-visible symptoms, one cause.** Every `updates:status` push goes through `broadcast()`, so all of them were dead, not just the timestamp:

| Symptom | Push that never arrived |
|---|---|
| "Last checked" frozen until Settings is reopened | `broadcastCompletedCheck` |
| Download bar stuck at a stale percentage | `download-progress` → `broadcastUpdaterStatus` |
| Install rejection surfaced nothing | the status this PR adds |

The download-bar case was reported on `0.12.12-nightly.202609061620` while this PR was still open, i.e. against a build without the fix — independent confirmation from a second symptom.

**Why it belongs in this PR:** the install-rejection status added above is broadcast through exactly this path. Without this fix the actionable message never reaches the user, and the recovery is silent.

**Regression lock:** the mock window registry in `auto-updater.test.ts` is now empty, matching the packaged app, so all 119 cases exercise the real delivery path instead of a fake window that hid the bug. Restoring the old walk fails 8 of them. Three added cases pin it directly: pushes must not touch `BrowserWindow`, the sink is resolved per send, and a missing sink must not throw.

Note this invalidates an earlier claim in my own analysis that the main process was "provably correct" — that test mocked `getAllWindows()` to return a fake window, which is precisely what concealed this.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| `npm run typecheck:e2e` | pass |
| `npx vitest run` (full suite) | **280 files, 3872 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** |
| GitHub Actions on this PR | `test`, `renderer-smoke`, `scan` all pass |

Node 22.22.3 locally vs CI's Node 24 — the one gap I cannot close here. `mac-update-e2e.yml` itself is `workflow_dispatch`-only and needs a published baseline plus a live feed, so it cannot run locally; it should be dispatched once a build carrying the restored listener is published, which is the first time it will have been runnable since 2026-07-31.

Refs #3288, #3528, #3034, #4175

title: refactor(agents): share the signed-in authentication predicate
body:
Stacked on #4974 — targets that branch, so review/merge it after #4974. Cleanup only, no behavior change.

## Why

"Signed in" means `authorized` **or** `not_applicable`: a harness that needs no authentication must never be presented as needing a sign-in. That rule was open-coded at **11 backend sites** and **4 renderer sites** with no shared definition:

- `codex_account_service.go` ×4, `codex_account_reconcile.go` ×3, `codex_account_login.go`, `codex_account_mutation.go`, `codex_accounts.go`, `readiness.go`
- `CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx`, `agent-select-options.ts`, `codex-accounts-state.ts`, `test/agent-readiness-fixtures.ts`

Any one of them could drift to comparing against `authorized` alone and silently exclude API-key and no-auth harnesses. This came out of review discussion on #4974: the display-vs-launch bug there was a shared function with a divergent flag, but it prompted a look at what else in the auth path is duplicated.

## What

- `domain.AgentAuthenticationState.SignedIn()` and the renderer's `agentAuthenticationSignedIn` mirror (new `frontend/src/renderer/lib/agent-auth.ts`), both documented with the reason the second state exists.
- Every open-coded copy now calls one of them. `codexAccountAuthorized` delegates rather than re-implementing.
- `agent-select-options.ts` now imports the state union instead of redeclaring it.

Each replaced expression is logically identical to the predicate — several were the negated form, which reads better as `!observation.Authentication.SignedIn()`.

## Deliberately not changed

- **Three exhaustive switches** keep their `case Authorized, NotApplicable` arms: `readiness.go` `readinessInfo`, `lifecycle_wiring.go` `AuthStatus`, and `EffectiveAgentReadiness` itself. There the two states are one arm of a total mapping over every state, not a predicate; rewriting them as if-chains would read worse and lose exhaustiveness.
- **`HarnessSettingsSection.tsx`** compares `ports.AgentAuthStatus`, a different three-value probe result that has no `not_applicable` state.
- **`agent-inventory-telemetry.ts:35`** filters on `state === "authorized"` only, while the daemon's `projectInventory` counts `authorized || not_applicable` as authorized. That looks like a real inconsistency, but changing it moves telemetry numbers, so it needs a product decision rather than a silent refactor. Flagging it here as a follow-up.

## Tests

- New `TestAgentAuthenticationStateSignedIn` pins all four states plus an unknown value, and asserts the invariant that `SignedIn` agrees with `EffectiveAgentReadiness` for every state — so the predicate and the readiness derivation cannot drift apart.
- `go test ./internal/domain/ ./internal/service/agent/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/` — pass.
- `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean (remaining errors are only in `packages/product-ui`, whose deps are not installed in this worktree).
- Full `vitest run` — 7 failed files / 5 failed tests, **identical to the baseline on the parent branch**, all in `src/landing/**` from uninstalled landing deps in this worktree.

title: fix(settings): align the Updates status icons with their text
body:
Reported from the Updates page: the icons and their text do not line up. There are **two** defects in that block, both visible at 1x. ## 1. The status icon sits ~2.5px high ```tsx
{icon !== null && {icon}} ``` `--size-icon-sm` is **13px**; the first line is `text-sm leading-5`, a **20px** line box. Centring the icon on that line needs `(20 − 13) / 2 = 3.5px`. The wrapper carried `mt-px` — **1px**. `items-start` is correct and stays: `detail` renders a second line and the icon belongs to the **first** one, so `items-center` would drift it down as soon as a build version is shown. The wrapper now takes that line's own height and centres inside it, which removes the hardcoded nudge — a number that would have gone wrong again on any change to the icon token or the text size. ## 2. The two stacked lines start in different columns | Row | Icon | Gap | Text indent | |---|---|---|---| | `You're on the latest version.` | 13px (`size-icon-sm`) | `gap-2` (8px) | **21px** | | `Last checked …` | 12px (`size-3`) | `gap-1.5` (6px) | **18px** | Two lines directly on top of each other, staggered by 3px. The second row now matches the first and pins its icon to the first line the same way, so a wrapped timestamp cannot re-centre the clock across both lines. This makes the clock 12px → 13px. That is the direction that reaches column alignment while using the design token instead of a raw `size-3`; shrinking the status icon to 12px would align them too but moves a tokenised size to a literal. ## Verification Rendered both states against the real token values and lucide geometry at 4x, before and after — the fix was checked by eye, not by reading class names. Before: the check glyph sits above the text's optical centre and the clock row hangs 3px left of the column. After: both icons are centred and both rows share one text column. No test added: the change is entirely utility classes, and asserting class strings would pin the implementation rather than the result while breaking on any restyle. The existing `UpdatesSection` tests (`data-testid="update-checked-at"` and siblings) still pass unchanged. | Check | Result | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck` | pass | | `npx vitest run` (full suite) | **278 files, 3804 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** | Independent of #4981 (updater install-rejection recovery); branched from `main`, touches only this component. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Qwen Code has no Chat UI — harness not registered in the chat-driver registry
body:
## Summary

Qwen Code sessions have no Chat UI. The interface toggle that other agents get (TUI ⇄ Chat) simply isn't offered for qwen — every session opens straight into the terminal UI.

Reported by **anthony** in [#bug-triage on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1545990670932508714) ("qwen code dosnt have the chat ui"), with a screenshot showing a qwen session's tab strip where other agents show the Orchestrator/Chat toggle.

## Why it looks like this

This is not a regression — Chat is opt-in per harness by design. The chat-driver registry (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/registry.go`) says it directly:

> Every other harness stays TUI-only until the same is true of it.

`Build()` registers Chat drivers for 9 harnesses on current `main` (codex, claude-code, opencode, droid, kimi, kimchi, pi, cursor, omp). Qwen is not in the list, so `SupportsChat("qwen")` returns false and the desktop never shows the toggle. Asking for a driver returns `ErrChatUnsupported` instead of quietly producing a TUI session — the gate works as intended, qwen just hasn't been added.

## Feasibility: a native ACP binding should work

Qwen Code is a gemini-cli fork and exposes an ACP mode today: `qwen --experimental-acp` (flag is recognized in `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` on QwenLM/qwen-code; the `--acp`/`--experimental-acp` fast-path exists, and upstream has an active ACP track — e.g. issues #8545, #10061, #11070, plus #8871 noting `--acp` vs `--experimental-acp` naming wobble in serve mode).

AO already has the reusable pieces:

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/nativeacp/` — binds a harness's existing agent plugin to the shared ACP transport (binary resolution + auth come from the plugin, so no second install/login answer).
- The qwen agent plugin (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/`) already resolves the binary, checks auth, and installs hooks — everything a binding needs.

So the work is a `qwenacp` package (Configure adds `--experimental-acp` plus the existing approval/model flag mapping from `qwen.go`'s `appendApprovalFlags`/`appendModelFlag`) and one line in the registry. Same shape as the recent cursor/omp/pi additions.

## Caveats to check during implementation

- **Flag stability**: upstream still calls ACP "experimental" and there's an open naming wobble (`--acp` vs `--experimental-acp`, QwenLM/qwen-code#8871). A VersionProbe like kimchiacp's would gate on a minimum version.
- **Upstream ACP gaps**: #11070 (approval mode lost across cold resume) and #8545 (subagent visibility) are open upstream — resume/approvals may be rougher than claude-code's binding. The production floor (streaming, approvals, interrupt, resume) needs verifying against a real qwen install.

## Fix

Add a `qwenacp` native ACP binding and register it in `chatdriverregistry.Build()`.

**Analyzed against:** `9c271fc0a` (origin/main)
**Priority:** medium — feature gap with a clear workaround (use qwen in TUI), but qwen is a first-class agent in the picker and every other major agent now has Chat.
**Confidence:** High — traced the exact gate; no driver registration is the whole story.

title: bug(codex): CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE survives daemon restart on v0.12.11 (Windows)
body:
## Bug

On Windows, every Codex spawn fails immediately with `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, and unlike #4908 it is **not** cleared by a daemon restart.

```text
ao spawn --project <proj> --name "noop-codex" --agent codex --prompt "..."
→ Codex account setup did not complete (CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE)
  [request Manu-Galaxy-Book5Pro-360/8PEgzM7LDB-000109]
```

**Env:** AO `0.12.11` (stable, installed 2026-09-06) · Windows 11 Home SL 10.0.26200 (x64) · Codex CLI `0.145.0` · claude-code `2.1.263`

## Relationship to #4908

#4908 (closed COMPLETED) reported the same error code, with the defining symptom that **restarting the daemon lets bootstrap run again and task creation succeed**. That fix (`2ae83e096e213b405119e98c677339e513db71ad`) is an ancestor of the `v0.12.11` tag I'm running, so the sticky-`sync.Once` fix is present in this build.

The remaining failure is worse than the one #4908 described: the documented recovery path no longer recovers. A full `ao stop` + restart, verified fresh pid and `healthz: ok`, returns the identical error on the next spawn.

This is also **not** #4973 — that one surfaces `CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED` via the `refreshToken` display/launch mismatch. Here the error code is the bootstrap-unavailable one, and my account state never flips to `unauthorized` after a failed spawn; it stays `authorized` throughout.

## Reproduction

1. Windows 11, Codex CLI installed and logged in (`codex login status` → `Logged in using ChatGPT`).
2. `ao spawn --agent codex --project <any> --name <name> --prompt <any>`
3. Observe `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, returned instantly.
4. `ao stop`, wait for daemon to come back, confirm new pid via `ao status`.
5. Repeat step 2. Same error.

## Evidence that this isn't local auth

Every AO-side probe reports Codex ready, both before and after the failed spawn:

```text
ao agent ls        → codex   installed   authorized
ao doctor          → PASS codex: ...\npm\codex.cmd (codex-cli 0.145.0)
codex login status → Logged in using ChatGPT
```

Ruled out:
- **Not auth.** CLI is logged in; AO itself reports `authorized`.
- **Not sticky bootstrap state.** Full daemon restart, fresh pid, `healthz: ok`, `readyz: ready` — same error.
- **Not spawn in general.** `--agent claude-code` spawns successfully in the same project, same session.
- **Not the readiness warning.** `--skip-agent-check` does not bypass it.

## Expected

A Codex session spawns, as `claude-code` does. Failing that, the error should name the underlying bootstrap failure rather than the generic `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` — #4908 already noted the original error is discarded at the `WaitCodexAccountBootstrap` boundary, and from the outside there is still no way to tell *why* bootstrap failed.

---

## Secondary: `codex-launch-flags` warning has the wrong root cause (Windows path escaping)

Possibly unrelated to the above, but it reproduces on the same machine and the diagnosis in `ao doctor` is misleading:

```text
WARN codex-launch-flags: codex rejected AO's launch flags (...): exit status 1
— codex sessions may spawn without activity hooks; a codex CLI update likely
  changed its flag/config surface
```

The "codex CLI update changed its flag surface" guess is wrong. `codex features list` and all the config keys work fine on 0.145.0. The actual cause is the unescaped Windows backslash path interpolated into the `hooks.*` command string.

Isolating the flags AO passes, holding everything else constant:

```text
-c check_for_update_on_startup=false                       → exit 0
-c notice.hide_rate_limit_model_nudge=true                 → exit 0
-c projects={'C:\Users\...\Temp'={trust_level="trusted"}}  → exit 0
-c hooks.SessionStart=[{...command="& \"C:\Users\...\ao.exe\" ..."}] → exit 1
```

```text
Error: invalid type: string "[{hooks=[{type=\"command\",command=\"& \\\"C:\Users\...\ao.exe\\\" hooks codex session-start\",timeout=5}]}]", expected a sequence
in `hooks`
```

Reduced to just the path style inside the hooks command:

```text
command="& \"C:\Users\manuj\ao.exe\" hooks codex stop"     → exit 1
command="& \"C:/Users/manuj/ao.exe\" hooks codex stop"     → exit 0
command="& \"C:\Users\manuj\ao.exe\" hooks codex stop"  → exit 1   (doubling doesn't help)
```

So the `ao.exe` path interpolated into `hooks.*` needs proper escaping (or forward slashes) when building the `-c` value on Windows. Note `projects={...}` is fine as AO sends it — it's single-quoted, so only the `hooks.*` values are affected.

---

**Minor:** `ao version` prints `dev` on the released 0.12.11 install, which makes version reporting in bug reports confusing.

title: fix(cline): write .ps1 hooks on Windows so Cline discovers and runs them
body:
Fixes #4976. Reproduction and main-branch verification in #4975.

## Problem

On Windows, Cline sessions produce **zero hook callbacks** to AO. AO writes Cline's workspace hooks as extensionless bash scripts (`TaskStart`, `PreToolUse`, `TaskCancel`, `TaskComplete`, `UserPromptSubmit`) into `.clinerules/hooks/`, but on Windows Cline never runs them:

- **Cline VS Code extension**: `findWindowsHook` looks only for `<Event>.ps1` — "Extensionless hooks are intentionally ignored on Windows."
- **Cline CLI SDK** (what AO launches): `inferHookCommand` parses the `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang down to `bash <path>`, which doesn't exist on Windows (ENOENT).

Impact chain: no hook fires → `ao hooks cline session-start/stop` never runs → no activity transitions and no native session id is captured → `GetRestoreCommand` returns `ok=false` → "resume" silently falls back to a fresh launch and status stays stuck.

Verified against `main` at `7e8a66229` (clean worktree): the bug reproduces there unchanged — code inspection (`hooks.go` had no `GOOS` branch), direct exec of the extensionless hook fails with `executable file not found in %PATH%`, and the identical hook written as `TaskStart.ps1` executes successfully via `powershell -File`.

## Fix

Branch on `runtime.GOOS` in the cline hook adapter (mirroring the auggie adapter's Windows handling):

- **Windows**: emit `<Event>.ps1` PowerShell wrappers — `try { $input | ao hooks cline <sub> 2>$null } catch {}` then `Write-Output '{"cancel": false}'`. Satisfies both Cline surfaces: VS Code discovery looks for exactly `<Event>.ps1`, and the SDK maps `.ps1` to `powershell -File` on Windows.
- **Unix**: unchanged — extensionless bash scripts.
- The `# ao-managed-cline-hook` marker is a comment in both dialects, so `isManagedClineHook` idempotency and uninstall keep working unchanged.
- `GetAgentHooks` / `UninstallHooks` / `AreHooksInstalled` now resolve script paths through a platform-aware `clineHookScriptName`; the workspace `.gitignore` entry follows the real filename.

## Testing

- New unit tests cover both renderers, the platform-aware naming, and that `GetAgentHooks` writes only the current platform's script names (all pass on Windows; the bash renderer is exercised as a pure function so the Unix path stays covered on any host).
- Existing cline hook tests (install idempotency, user-hook preservation, uninstall) updated for platform-aware names and passing.
- **Live end-to-end check on Windows**: the fixed `GetAgentHooks` writes `TaskStart.ps1`, and `powershell -NoProfile -File TaskStart.ps1` executes it exactly as Cline does → exits 0 and prints `{"cancel": false}`. (Pre-fix, the extensionless file failed with `executable file not found in %PATH%`.)
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/cline/`, and `go vet` on the touched package are clean.

Note: full `go test ./...` on Windows has pre-existing failures in unrelated packages (aider/crush auth-status tests, tmux runtime, persistenthost's `syscall.Kill` in a race test, etc.) — none touch the cline adapter.

## Intentional omissions

- Hook wrappers still invoke bare `ao` from PATH. The session PATH pin (`hookPATH`) resolves it to the daemon binary inside spawned sessions, so callbacks reach the right daemon; making the wrapper invoke the absolute daemon executable (like auggie does) is a small follow-up, tracked in #4975 as a related MEDIUM item.
- Reinstall/uninstall across OSes (hooks installed by a Linux build found by a Windows build) is out of scope; a fresh session install writes the correct platform shape.

See [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions: surgical change, no drive-by refactors.

title: bug(desktop): orchestrator sessions permanently show "Session workspace is not available" — the handoff endpoint has no answer for orchestrators
body:
## Bug

Every orchestrator session permanently shows the red **"Session workspace is not available"** alert in the topbar (next to the Open-in-editor button), because the desktop workspace-location endpoint returns 404 for orchestrator sessions — they are not assigned a per-session worktree, so there is nothing for the handoff to resolve.

The orchestrator itself is healthy: the session is idle/active, chat works, only the editor-handoff surface is dead.

### Repro

1. Open any project, spawn an orchestrator (or restore an existing one).
2. Open the orchestrator session tab.
3. The topbar shows a persistent "Session workspace is not available" alert; the Open-in-editor button can't do anything useful.
4. Worker session tabs of the same project show no alert — their worktree resolves fine.

Observed on macOS desktop; every orchestrator session of every project shows it.

### Root cause

`GET /api/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/workspace` (Electron main's editor-handoff probe) goes through `session.Service.WorkspaceLocation` (`backend/internal/service/session/workspace_location.go`):

- a worker session resolves `Metadata.WorkspacePath` (its worktree under `~/.ao/data/worktrees/...`) → 200;
- an orchestrator session has **no** `Metadata.WorkspacePath` — orchestrators run directly in the project checkout, and AO deliberately does not assign them a worktree — so the endpoint returns `SESSION_WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (404);
- the topbar renders that 404 as the permanent alert.

The deliberate no-fallback is correct for workers (`TestWorkspaceLocationDoesNotFallBackToProjectCheckout`: a worker whose worktree vanished must not silently redirect the editor to the project checkout), but it leaves orchestrator sessions with no resolvable workspace at all, and the handoff surface doesn't account for that.

### Suggested fix

In `WorkspaceLocation`, resolve orchestrator sessions (explicitly `Kind == orchestrator`) to their project checkout:

- `record.Kind == orchestrator` → load the project record and return its `Path` (after the same absolute-path + directory-exists validation); unknown project or missing directory still yields `SESSION_WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`.
- Workers and legacy records with no kind keep the strict `Metadata.WorkspacePath`-only contract, so the existing no-fallback guarantee is untouched.

That makes the topbar banner disappear for orchestrators and gives the Open-in-editor button a correct target (the project the orchestrator manages).

title: fix(session): resolve orchestrator workspace to the project checkout for desktop handoff

title: fix(updater): recover from macOS staging missing-file failures
body:
## What

Recover from macOS `ditto ... .ShipIt/update... .app/...: No such file or directory` errors by dropping AO's failed ready-to-install state and allowing the selected release to be offered again.

## Why

Related to #4175. After native preparation fails, AO can retain its staged stamp, keep offering Restart & install, and suppress another automatic download of that same version. This handles the reported missing-file error; it does not establish what originally removed the temporary files on the affected Mac.

## How

- Recognize the macOS ShipIt/ditto missing-file error, surface plain-language retry/manual-install guidance even during background checks, and retain the raw error in logs.
- Remove the failed staged stamp and reject stale install actions. Order persisted stamp writes/removal so a failed record cannot overwrite or remove its replacement. Ignore escalation results for a discarded/replaced build.
- Finish failure recovery inside the serialized operation before releasing a queued retry. An older rejected check/download/return must not discard the replacement staged by that retry.
- Preserve manual request IDs for reject-only failures, including failures before AO records a staged build.
- Leave the downloaded ZIP and native ShipIt files alone. Retrying the download hands the ZIP back to the native updater; there is no asynchronous cache deletion racing another download.

This is narrower than #4981's signature-rejection work and overlaps its error-handler area. Channel selection/downgrade policy is unchanged. Clearing AO's stamp/quit flag does **not** cancel an already-armed native macOS installer, and this does not move AO's downloaded event to native staging completion.

## Testing

- Reproduced the reported error with a failing regression test before the fix; all 117 updater tests now pass; new queued check/download/return regressions failed before the queue-ordering correction and pass afterwards.
- Full frontend Vitest suite: **280 files, 3,875 passed, 6 skipped** (`AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TEST_BINARY=... node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=2`, Node 24).
- Renderer smoke: **55 passed** (`CI=true AO_E2E_PORT=5291 npm run test:e2e:renderer -- --workers=1`).
- Frontend `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- Cloud client generation/drift check, typecheck, 21 tests, and pack dry-run: pass. Product UI typecheck, 120 tests, and pack dry-run: pass.
- Initial concurrent local runs had one settings test failure and three renderer smoke failures. The settings/updater files passed together (149 tests), then both full suites passed on rerun without code changes.
- Local host is macOS; the pinned Linux smoke container and gitleaks action were verified in GitHub CI (Docker daemon unavailable locally). Native signed-app failure/retry has not been reproduced end to end; unit tests verify AO's recovery state, not elimination of the underlying ShipIt file-loss trigger.

GitHub CI on `5af86c7ad`: frontend `test`, `renderer-smoke`, and gitleaks `scan` all passed. [Frontend run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34038758833).

The revised head is also included in #5002, where its overlap with native restart preparation has been resolved and tested.

title: fix(cloud): inject role prompts for Claude, Codex, and Cursor
body:
## Bug

Docker/hosted Cloud sessions do not receive AO role instructions consistently across the three shipped Cloud harnesses.

**Reported by:** @nikhilachale in Codex chat
**Analyzed against:** `6b536dbba`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P1 — worker sessions lack their standing implementation role, and Cursor orchestrators lack the Cloud orchestration role.

## Reproduction

1. Start the Docker-backed Cloud control plane with `npm run cloud:local`.
2. Create worker and orchestrator sessions using Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
3. Inspect the command construction in `cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go`.

## Root cause

- `HarnessBuilder.BuildInteractive` selects a system prompt only for `kind == "orchestrator"`; workers receive an empty prompt.
- Claude Code and Codex map a supplied prompt through the shared `backend/pkg/agentruntime` command builder.
- Cursor's interactive builder has no native system-prompt flag and currently drops `SystemPrompt`; it needs an AO-owned always-apply plugin rule.
- The Cloud prompt is a short, separate constant and has drifted from the local daemon's role policy.

## Fix

- Give both Cloud roles complete standing instructions with Cloud-supported `ao` commands.
- Keep the provider-neutral role prompt separate from the user task prompt.
- Inject it through native prompt-file configuration for Claude Code and Codex.
- Materialize an AO-owned Cursor plugin with an always-apply rule and launch Cursor with `--plugin-dir`.
- Reapply the prompt on fresh and restored interactive launches.
- Add deterministic tests for every role/harness combination and verify prompt files stay outside the repository checkout.

## Impact

- Cloud workers may not follow AO's implementation-worker boundaries.
- Cursor orchestrators receive only the visible kickoff prompt rather than trusted standing instructions.
- Behavior differs materially from ordinary local AO sessions.

title: fix: detect Windows agent binaries after install
body:
## Problem

Agent installation can succeed on Windows while AO still reports the agent binary as missing. This affects users whose installer adds the executable to a persisted Windows `Path` or installs an npm/WinGet shim outside the daemon's startup environment.

The failure is most visible when installing Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor from the desktop app: installation completes, but the immediate post-install version check cannot resolve or launch the newly installed binary.

## Root cause

There are three Windows-specific gaps in the agent installation path:

1. The AO daemon keeps the `Path` inherited when it started. Windows installers update the user or machine environment in the registry, but they do not update an already-running process.
2. npm-installed CLIs are commonly exposed as `.cmd` or `.bat` shims. Passing those files directly to Go's `exec.CommandContext` does not execute them correctly on Windows.
3. The agent fallback search omitted common per-user npm and WinGet link directories used by affected installations.

This PR is scoped to agent installation and agent-binary resolution. It does not change the Git or GitHub CLI checks in `systemcheck`.

## Changes

- Refresh the daemon's process `Path` after a successful install by merging:
  - the existing process `Path`
  - the machine environment from `HKLM`
  - the current-user environment from `HKCU`
- Preserve existing path entries and deduplicate them case-insensitively.
- Execute `.cmd` and `.bat` shims through Windows `ComSpec` for installer capability checks, installation commands, and post-install version checks.
- Add fallback candidates for:
  - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm`
  - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Links`
  - `%ProgramFiles%\WinGet\Links`
  - `%ProgramFiles(x86)%\WinGet\Links`
- Add Windows-specific resolution coverage for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.

## Expected behavior

After AO installs an agent on Windows, the same running daemon can immediately locate and verify it without requiring the user to restart AO or manually edit `Path`.

## Validation

- Focused Go tests passed for `systemexec`, `binaryutil`, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and `systeminstall`.
- `go vet` passed for the affected packages.
- Windows cross-build passed for `systemexec`.
- Windows test binaries compiled for `systemexec`, `binaryutil`, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Test-suite note

A full local `go test ./...` is currently blocked by unrelated upstream module-graph drift: the workspace graph requests missing `modernc.org/libc` packages, while the standalone backend module reports that `go.mod` needs tidying. The focused affected packages pass with `GOWORK=off` and `-mod=readonly`.

No API or generated artifacts are changed.

title: fix(desktop): clear opaque browser-popout-frame under native composition
body:
## What

Fixes the Windows maximized-window blackout of the embedded browser (issue #4979) when a renderer-owned overlay (toolbar tooltip, Browser Controls dropdown) appears above the native page.

When any `[data-browser-native-overlay]` opens, the transparent shell `WebContentsView` is raised above the native browser view (`setOverlayOpen(true)`). Every shell layer stacked over the page must be transparent for the duration, or it blanks the page. The native-composition cascade clears the `.browser-popout-overlay`, `.browser-popout-backdrop`, shell roots, and the browser panel viewport — but the popped-out maximized browser is portaled (SessionView) into a `.browser-popout-frame` wrapper that paints its own **opaque** `background: var(--bg)` plate. That rule was missed, so raising the shell for a tooltip/menu painted the opaque frame across the whole maximized page → solid black on Windows until the overlay closed.

## Change

- `styles.css`: clear `background` on `html[data-native-browser-composition="true"] .browser-popout-frame` alongside the existing overlay/backdrop clears.
- `native-composition-cascade.test.ts`: pin the contract so any future opaque ancestor of the popped-out browser panel is caught at source level, like the other settle/cascade tests.

## Root cause

The overlay/menu/tooltip backgrounds are intentionally opaque and correct. The black-out source was the always-present opaque `.browser-popout-frame` ancestor behind them, which the `:has(.browser-popout-overlay)` shell clears can never match (the portal pops out of `#root`).

## Verification

- Manual: reproduced in the real Electron desktop app on Windows — maximized window, embedded Browser panel; toolbar tooltip and Browser Controls/device dropdown open with the live page remaining visible underneath. Tabs, device presets, profiles, DevTools, and resize all still work.
- `frontend` `npm run typecheck`: pass.
- `vitest run src/renderer/native-composition-cascade.test.ts`: 6/6 pass.
- BrowserPanel + useBrowserView suites: pass.

Note: the full renderer suite has 2 pre-existing unrelated failures (`ChatTimelineItems`/`ChatWorkspace` "yesterday and older messages" date-label tests), present on `main` independent of this change (date-boundary/locale issue in chat tests).

title: fix(updater): add macOS repair installer and reliable restart progress
body:
## Problem and behavior

On macOS, a downloaded ZIP or persisted staged-version record does not prove that the native installer can replace and reopen AO. Restart could silently fail, preparation errors could retain misleading readiness, and shutdown cleanup could prevent the installer from proceeding.

This PR waits for native readiness for the confirmed version, restores remembered handoffs, preserves release notes and intentional channel downgrades, and supplies a separate helper that observes completion or shows recovery. Main has been integrated so #5047's live sidebar progress and duplicate-download protection are preserved.

## Approach by reported symptom

- **Slow/repeated discovery:** revalidate the one cached public GitHub release response with `If-None-Match`. A 304 reuses the already parsed records with no response body; a changed response replaces them. No cached result is used on a network failure or for another repository. The first lookup still requests up to 100 records to preserve existing highest-version selection; replacing that with a small channel manifest requires release-conductor work and is not claimed here.
- **Timeout and duplicate errors:** retain the 60-second metadata cancellation deadline so requests and their cached promises settle before queued retries. The message no longer attributes the error to the user's connection. Display the same check failure once, while preserving distinct failures. This includes the display fix from #5067.
- **Missing files / rejected prepared copy:** discard unusable staging, keep preparation serialized, and permit recovery without deleting files concurrently with native preparation. Existing verification handling retries preparation and then discards a repeatedly rejected archive; it does not bypass signing or prove every reported corrupt copy's original cause.
- **Restart does nothing / app stays closed:** wait for the version-specific native event, acknowledge the helper before quitting, and bound explicit-update shutdown cleanup to 15 seconds. Restore the window after a failed native handoff when the process survives. The helper stays hidden on the normal path and shows recovery if progress stalls; successful completion requires the replacement app's acknowledgement (with a compatibility path for older targets).

Native preparation has a three-minute deadline. Since Squirrel has no cancellation API for that stage, a timeout requires a fresh AO process; a late event cannot authorize an overlapping retry. The sidebar and install action now derive readiness from this same state. Windows/Linux also reject an install request without a staged build.

The restart dialog passes the confirmed version through IPC. If the target changes, it displays the new version/notes and requires confirmation again before a remembered target's replacement is downloaded or armed.

## Exact code map

| Behavior | Code |
| --- | --- |
| Release-response revalidation | [frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:451](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a192f4eb1af197c09d75eb6785dce20ced67c75a/frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts#L451) |
| Missing-file staging recovery | [frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:774](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a192f4eb1af197c09d75eb6785dce20ced67c75a/frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts#L774) |
| Verification rejection recovery | [frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:1570](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a192f4eb1af197c09d75eb6785dce20ced67c75a/frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts#L1570) |
| Native install-readiness gate | [frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts:2306](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a192f4eb1af197c09d75eb6785dce20ced67c75a/frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts#L2306) |
| Bounded explicit-update shutdown | [frontend/src/main/update-quit.ts:2](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a192f4eb1af197c09d75eb6785dce20ced67c75a/frontend/src/main/update-quit.ts#L2) |
| Duplicate error suppression | [frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx:586](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a192f4eb1af197c09d75eb6785dce20ced67c75a/frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx#L586) |

The 60-second metadata deadline (`auto-updater.ts:813`), operation queue (`:952`) and two-minute no-progress watchdog (`:225`) are retained safeguards, not removed or claimed as proven causes of the reported timeout.

## Repair installer and release gate

The optional .pkg builder accepts an already signed/notarized/stapled app, validates the payload, requires signing/notarization for production, and refuses unsafe destinations or an active AO/ShipIt. It preserves user data and does not terminate processes or auto-launch as root.

This is **not a published recovery download**. The conductor must wire Installer signing and publish it. Existing old clients cannot gain new recovery UI remotely. Signed upgrades from affected 0.12.10/0.12.11/nightly builds, data preservation and automatic relaunch remain a release gate on an isolated supported Mac. No publishing, signing bypass, or installed-user-app replacement was performed as validation.

## Validation

Head: `a192f4eb1`. The runtime changes are in `7df883540`; the follow-up only adds `as const` to the Windows/Linux test table after CI caught widened string types. The full local typecheck passed again after that correction. Node 24 validation:

- Focused updater, shutdown/helper, restart-dialog and settings tests: 224 passed.
- Frontend and E2E TypeScript checks passed.
- Complete renderer smoke: 58 passed on macOS, one worker, unchanged time limits.
- Cloud client: generation/drift, types, 21 tests, package dry-run passed. Product UI: types, 124 tests, package dry-run passed.
- Both macOS helper architectures compiled and passed lipo checks; Swift state tests and 13 helper/repair packaging tests passed.
- Full frontend suite: 289 files, 4,055 passed, 6 skipped (two workers, unchanged test timeouts). Initial parallel runs were interrupted; launching the isolated Electron app rebuilt better-sqlite3 for Electron and invalidated the first unit-suite attempt. The final complete run used the restored Node 24 binary.
- Isolated desktop launch compiled successfully, but its window remained blank and computer-control calls timed out; the test instance was stopped. A second launch after the parallel suites finished also could not be inspected because computer control timed out; that isolated instance was stopped too. Native UI interaction and a signed installation/relaunch are **not verified** on this head.
- On `7df883540`, remote Mac helper, renderer smoke and security scan passed; the frontend job caught the test-table type error described above. CI is rerunning on the corrected head. Local macOS smoke is not a substitute for the pinned Linux CI container.

- Regression: disabling release-response reuse fails the conditional-request test; new release discovery remains covered.
- Regression: Windows/Linux install requests without staged builds failed the new rejection test before the guard.
- Live GitHub transport probe: first response 2,524,329 bytes / 7.04 seconds; unchanged conditional response 304 / zero body bytes / 1.27 seconds. A second probe using Node 24 fetch with the exact request options measured 1.94 seconds / 2,524,329 bytes initially and 0.041 seconds / zero body bytes on revalidation. These are single transport samples, not an app-install benchmark or diagnosis of the reported user's timeout.

## Existing UI fixture

This screenshot demonstrates the existing component's preparation state with sample release notes. It is a test-bridge fixture, not evidence of a signed installation.

title: bug(tasks): New Task rejects valid briefs over 4 KiB
body:
## Bug

The desktop **Create a new task** dialog rejects otherwise valid task briefs as soon as their UTF-8 payload exceeds 4,096 bytes. The user sees `Task is too long (TASK_TOO_LONG)` and cannot start the task, even when the selected agent can accept the prompt.

**Source:** Local report via Codex desktop  
**Reported by:** Local AO user  
**Analyzed against:** `e97026f75bed85545ee6c6df13c662bd0122b4d9` (`origin/main`)  
**AO build:** `dev`, verified daemon ready on port `3001`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** Medium — core task creation is blocked for pasted setup guides/reference documents; shortening the input is a lossy workaround.

![Create a new task showing TASK_TOO_LONG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-long-task-prompt-limit/.issue-assets/long-task-prompt-limit/task-too-long.png)

## Reproduction

1. Open the desktop **Create a new task** dialog for a local project.
2. Enter a task brief whose UTF-8 length is 4,097 bytes or more (for example, paste a documentation/setup guide).
3. Select an agent and start the task.
4. Observe HTTP 400 with `TASK_TOO_LONG`; the session service is never called.

Minimal automated reproduction:

```bash
cd backend
go test ./internal/httpd/controllers -run '^TestSessionsAPI_DelegateTaskAcceptsLongBrief$' -count=1
```

Before the fix this fails with:

```text
delegate long brief = 400, want 202; body={"error":"bad_request","code":"TASK_TOO_LONG","message":"Task is too long",...}
```

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` defines `maxPromptLen = 4096`. The delegation handler reuses it and rejects `len(in.Brief) > maxPromptLen` before calling `SessionService.DelegateTask`.

Git history shows the 4 KiB value came from the first Go sessions controller and was later reused by the New Task delegation endpoint. It is not a model context-window limit. LAN memory protection is already handled independently by `http.MaxBytesReader` and the spawn/delegation body cap.

A finite task-prompt bound is still useful because several TUI adapters place the initial prompt in process argv and AO supports Windows, whose command line is bounded. The current 4 KiB value is unnecessarily small, however.

## Fix

- Raise the shared initial-task prompt/brief ceiling from 4 KiB to 16 KiB.
- Keep follow-up-message and request-body limits unchanged.
- Return an actionable error stating the 16 KiB ceiling.
- Regenerate the OpenAPI contract.
- Add regression tests proving 4,097-byte briefs are accepted and briefs above 16 KiB are rejected before the service call.

## Impact

- Pasted documentation and setup guides between 4 KiB and 16 KiB can be used directly when creating tasks.
- Direct session spawn and delegated New Task creation remain consistent.
- Oversized process arguments and unbounded LAN request bodies remain guarded.

## Related

- [#2822](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2822) — broader prompt truncation/reference design; related size-boundary concern, but not this pre-spawn desktop rejection.
- [#3326](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3326) — Codex assembled system prompt can exceed Windows/provider limits; different code path and failure point.

title: fix(tasks): allow longer initial task prompts
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5004

## Summary

- raise the shared initial spawn/delegation prompt ceiling from 4 KiB to 16 KiB so ordinary pasted setup guides and reference documents can create tasks
- align automatic tracker intake with the same 16 KiB boundary
- preflight the fully escaped Windows launch command against the 32,767 UTF-16-unit OS limit before process creation, including wrapper arguments and the terminating NUL
- return actionable errors for both the request limit and the platform-specific launch limit
- regenerate the OpenAPI contract and add regression coverage for HTTP, tracker-intake, and Windows quote/backslash boundaries

## Root cause

The New Task delegation handler reused the original Go session controller's `maxPromptLen = 4096` validation. That value was not tied to an agent context window, and it rejected the request before the session service or selected agent was called. LAN request-memory protection is handled independently by the existing bounded-body reader.

The 16 KiB request limit remains a predictable application boundary. Because Windows argument escaping can expand prompt content, the ConPTY runtime now separately validates the actual escaped command instead of assuming every 16 KiB prompt is launch-safe.

## Local verification

- verified the real Electron app with a 16,127-byte task brief; the modal stays fixed and the task field scrolls internally
- verified the running daemon passes 16,127 bytes through length validation and rejects 16,385 bytes with `TASK_TOO_LONG`

title: fix: preserve attachments when editing queued messages
body:
## What

Queued messages support adding, retaining, removing, and replacing image attachments. Saving or canceling an edit restores the ordinary composer draft and its attachments.

## Why

The queued-edit UI rejected native images with “Queued message edits cannot include attachments.” The daemon's text-only update also cleared stored delivery content, so editing text could silently remove images before provider delivery. Entering an edit reused the ordinary draft's attachment state.

## How

- Extend the existing queued-edit API with new images, retained content indices, and the editor's message revision. Keep image bytes in daemon storage; reject stale indices and turns that have already dispatched. Text-only callers that omit retention preserve existing content.
- Update queued text and delivery content atomically, preserving queued-state guards. Populate the existing domain content field so snapshots expose attachment summaries.
- Reuse the transcript's staged-file parser to open removable attachment chips. Keep path references and native content as separate chips: they have no shared persisted identity, even when their counts match. Removing either representation preserves the other.
- Count only retained and newly added native images against the combined eight-image limit. Resource summaries and path references do not consume this image limit; existing staging limits still apply to newly attached files.
- Keep ordinary and edit drafts separate, retain failed saves, and invalidate unfinished file reads when an edit is discarded.
- Count actual decoded bytes against the combined 25 MiB image limit, accepting exactly 25 MiB and rejecting one byte over without changing stored content.
- Regenerate OpenAPI, TypeScript API types, and sqlc output. No schema migration or unrelated cleanup.

## Testing

Current head: `f0c50dc434cb76ea6694eb507ab77905e5518f19`.

- **Frontend:** full Vitest suite passed: **281 files, 3,872 tests, 6 skips**, using Node 24, the pinned agent-browser runtime, and `--maxWorkers=4`. Project and E2E typechecks passed. All 13 queued-attachment tests pass, including independent path/native removal, eight resources plus an image, nine-resource text edits, the nine-image rejection, and eight images plus a text file. The new regressions exposed the old behavior before the fixes.
- **Renderer smoke:** all **56 tests passed**, including add/retain/remove/cancel (`CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer -- --workers=2`).
- **Real Electron:** this checkout ran against isolated daemon/data state. Removing an unrelated path preserved the native image; after dispatch Claude returned its printed code, `CEDAR-1E885B`, with zero tool activities. The stored image was independently inspected to confirm the code. Eight resources plus an image and a nine-resource text-only edit each saved with HTTP 204, revision 1, and all intended content persisted. The ordinary text/image draft was restored after all saves.
- **Native-run limitation:** the combined UI script passed all save/content assertions, then cleanup returned 409 because the extra turns had already dispatched. Later provider turns were blocked by the provider. A separate verification of daemon responses, persisted content, the successful first image delivery, and the restored draft passed. No successful provider delivery is claimed for the later resource turns.
- **Shared packages:** cloud-client generation/drift check, typecheck, tests and pack dry run; product-ui typecheck, tests and pack dry run passed again for this follow-up.
- **Unchanged backend and CLI:** at `e33b3ea`, full backend race suite, build, vet, gofmt, golangci-lint v2.12.2, API/sqlc drift, native macOS CLI E2E and the fresh-install Docker check passed. All 16 SQLite/provider table cases passed. This follow-up changes only four frontend files (+48/−14); those backend checks were not repeated locally.
- **Secret scan:** passed in CI for the current head. The local pinned-container rerun could not start because Docker stopped responding, including to a bounded read-only container query.
- **Remote CI:** all **11 checks passed** on `f0c50dc434cb76ea6694eb507ab77905e5518f19`, including both frontend jobs, the full Linux backend test job, lint, API drift, Windows workspace tests, native CLI on all three platforms, the container CLI check, and the secret scan. Linux/Windows-native validation comes from CI, not this macOS host.

Screenshot attachments from the earlier verified add/retain/replace/cancel flow remain in [the evidence comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5006#issuecomment-5567697539). New screenshots were captured locally; the browser upload tool rejected the attachment attempt. No evidence files are committed.
