title: bug(codex): account import refreshes the copied credential, then writes the stale one back over it
body:
## Bug

AO's Codex account import refreshes the copied credential in a throwaway folder, then writes the stale pre-refresh credential back over the account it just created. The refreshed credential is thrown away. The stored one is left in a used state, so the next refresh attempt fails and the account gets signed out.

Both sign-out events in the incident below may have other causes. This issue claims the mechanism, not the whole incident. See "What this does not explain".

**Reported by:** @Rishet11 and his audit agent in AO chat, 2026-09-06, times IST
**Analyzed against:** `e97026f75` (Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator main)
**Codex source:** `openai/codex` main, `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs`, read 2026-09-06. One maintainer has not independently confirmed this side yet; noted per claim below.
**Confidence:** High on the mechanism. Every step verified in source, AO side and codex side.
**Related:** [#4973](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4973) (display vs launch divergence, different bug), [PR #4974](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4974) (does not touch this path)

## The defect

`backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_reconcile.go`, the new-account import branch inside `reconcileGlobalInner`:

```
L265  writePrivateFileAtomic(home/auth.json, globalCredential)  // copy device credential into a temp home
L274  checked, checkErr := verifiedClient.Read(verifyCtx, true) // refresh=true: codex may rotate and persist new tokens in that temp home
L281  record, err = m.catalog.commitPending(pendingDir, checked) // temp home becomes the saved account
L287  writePrivateFileAtomic(filepath.Join(record.Home, codexCredentialFilename), globalCredential) // writes the PRE-refresh bytes back over it
```

L287 is unconditional. It runs on the freshly imported branch and on the matched-record branch alike. Either way the account ends up holding the old credential, and the rotated one from L274 exists nowhere.

### Why this is a mistake, not a design choice

The same file already knows the rule. `verifyOpaqueGlobalCredential` (L398) does the same temp-home verification and passes `false`:

```
// Reconciliation only needs to prove that the opaque global credential is
// usable from a file-backed home. A proactive refresh here can race Codex's
// live global credential and rotate the copied refresh token, incorrectly
// classifying the device account as unmanaged. Strict refresh remains part
// of login and switch admission, where no duplicate live credential is being
// introduced.
```

The comment carves out an exception for paths "where no duplicate live credential is being introduced." The import branch at L274 is exactly such a path and passes `true` anyway. Three files away, `codex_account_mutation.go` L242-243 shows the correct write: after a switch it re-reads the possibly-refreshed credential and stores the refreshed bytes.

### Codex side: refresh persists, it does not rotate in memory only

Claim source: `openai/codex` main, `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs`, read 2026-09-06, not yet independently confirmed by the other investigator.

`refresh_and_persist_chatgpt_token` (L3012) documents itself: "Refreshes ChatGPT OAuth tokens, persists the updated auth state." It calls `persist_tokens` (L1556), which loads `auth.json` from the client's home, replaces the refresh token with the one from the refresh response, stamps `last_refresh`, and calls `storage.save`. `save` writes the file (`auth/storage.rs` L206-223, with a keyring fallback path).

So with `refresh=true`, if the credential is near expiry, codex rotates the refresh token and writes the new one to the home the client was opened on. AO opened that client on the temp home. The rotation lands in the temp home. L287 then restores the retired token over the committed account.

OpenAI's OAuth rejects a reused refresh token and revokes the family. Codex's own error strings name the outcomes: "refresh token was already used", "refresh token was revoked", "you have since logged out or signed in to another account."

## When the branch runs

`matchGlobalAccount` (`codex_account_reconcile.go:312-352`) matches saved accounts on structured identity, not credential bytes, and a record at status `SignedOut` still matches. So the import branch fires only when the device credential belongs to no saved record: first import of an account, or re-import after that account's record was deleted.

This matters for scoping. The bug is a landmine, not a timer. It is dormant while an account sits in the list, and fires on import or re-import.

## Incident evidence

Source: reporter's machine, 2026-09-06, times IST. Timestamps from `~/.codex/log/codex-login.log`, desktop logs, and on-disk credential files.

- Sep 5, 15:51:31: first 401 on a cached token, original account signed out. Cause still unknown.
- Sep 6, ~17:40: worker spawns fail with `CODEX_ACCOUNT_AUTH_UNVERIFIED`; existing orchestrator session keeps working (send reuses the running process, spawn runs the launch check).
- Sep 6, 17:48: reporter deletes the old, signed-out account record.
- Sep 6, 17:48-49: workers 357 and 358 launch fine.
- Sep 6, 17:53:25: AO writes `auth.json` into a saved account's credential home. Consistent with reconcile re-importing the device credential into the vacated slot.
- Sep 6, ~18:06: launches fail again. About 13 minutes after the write. Fits the burn cycle: import refreshes, overwrite restores the retired token, first refresh attempt on the retired token kills the family.
- Sep 6, 18:50: the long-running session dies too. It had held its access token in memory; that expired like any other.

The 17:48 delete forcing re-import is the strongest single piece of evidence, but it is still timing correlation, not proof of the mechanism.

## What this does not explain

- Sep 5, 15:51 sign-out of the original account. The import branch was dormant then. Open question.
- Account B dying a day after switching, with no delete or new account in between. No verified mechanism. Open question.

We are not attaching those to this bug. Next step for Sep 5 is reading the logs before the first 401, not after.

## Fix

One-line change plus a test:

1. Pass `Read(verifyCtx, false)` in the import branch at L274, matching `verifyOpaqueGlobalCredential` and the rule in its comment. Or, if a refresh-capable check is wanted there, keep `true` and persist the refreshed bytes instead of the L287 overwrite. The first option is smaller and matches the codebase's own convention.
2. Regression test: fake credential near expiry, a client whose refresh persists rotated credentials into the home it was opened on, then import. Assert the credential in the committed record's home is the rotated one after reconcile completes, and that no stale write follows `commitPending`.

Fix PR is in progress by the reporter's agents on top of worktree 357, which already carries uncommitted regression tests (`codex_accounts_test.go` modified, `codex_import_refresh_incident_test.go` untracked). Will cross-link here. No credential contents were read or logged at any point.

title: fix(onboarding): automatically start and focus GitHub login PTY
body:
## Bug

The GitHub onboarding notice performs an initial authentication check, but when that check reports that `gh` is signed out it waits for the user to click **Sign in with GitHub**. The requested onboarding behavior is to start the reviewed `gh auth login` command automatically in the embedded PTY. The inline PTY also mounts without requesting focus, so users can see the prompt while their keyboard input remains on the previous control.

**Reported by:** @nikhilachale  
**Date:** 2026-09-06  
**Analyzed against:** `e97026f75` (`Untrivial-ai/main`)  
**Observed packaged version:** `0.12.12-nightly.202609061223`  
**Priority:** P2 — authentication has manual workarounds, but onboarding is confusing.  
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Start AO with GitHub CLI installed but signed out.
2. Open the home/empty-board onboarding surface.
3. Wait for the initial GitHub authentication check to finish.
4. Observe that AO shows a sign-in button instead of starting the reviewed login terminal.
5. Click the sign-in button and immediately type without clicking inside the terminal.
6. Observe that the PTY prompt is visible but does not own keyboard focus.

## Root Cause

- `GitHubOnboardingNotice` starts the login mutation only from the button's click handler; it has no effect that reacts to the initial signed-out result.
- Its inline `TerminalPane` does not set `focusRequested`, unlike normal active terminal surfaces.
- The daemon endpoint and terminal mux are healthy: a live `POST /api/v1/system/github-auth/terminal` produced the interactive `gh auth login` prompt, accepted Ctrl-C through `/mux`, and emitted an exit event.

## Fix

- Keep the existing one-time advisory authentication check.
- When it resolves as signed out and `gh` is available, automatically open exactly one GitHub login terminal.
- Request focus for that inline terminal.
- Preserve the explicit retry button for startup failures and the post-exit auth check needed to dismiss the notice after successful login.

## Impact

- Signed-out users enter the GitHub login flow without an extra click.
- Keyboard input goes to the PTY as soon as it appears.
- Already authenticated users remain unaffected because the initial check hides the notice and never starts a terminal.

## Related

- [PR #4970](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4970) — introduced the GitHub authentication onboarding surface.

title: fix(onboarding): automatically start GitHub login PTY
body:
Fixes #5008

When GitHub CLI is installed but signed out, AO opens the native `gh auth login` flow in an embedded terminal. Users retain the installed CLI's choices of host, protocol, and authentication method. AO polls while login is active, closes the terminal after successful authentication, and provides retry/check actions after an interrupted login.

The renderer checks the daemon's shell-terminal list before starting login and adopts an existing standalone “Connect GitHub” terminal. This recovers a login after window reloads without spawning another PTY. A failed list request prevents creation. Renderer query state retains the handle and dismissal state across navigation. Failed close requests retain the handle, and retry starts a replacement only after successful closure.

Cursor-position replies are correlated with PTY requests, including requests split across chunks. The initial visual buffering window can contain fresh PTY output, so its writes retain live protocol handling, including during teardown flushing. The mux has no history/live boundary: suppressing historical DSRs based on arrival timing would also suppress fresh login prompts. All production writes share one protocol path; the unused replay/live argument and test-only replay branch have been removed. Cursor theme requests continue to receive replies during buffered output.

Authentication uses `gh auth status --active --json hosts`, accepting an active successful account on GitHub.com or Enterprise. An empty host map is definitively signed out and does not fall back. Unsupported or malformed JSON and validation failures for configured hosts fall back to local `gh auth token`, discarding token output. This is a credential-configuration advisory, not a guarantee that a configured token remains valid; the fallback can accept expired or revoked local credentials. The fallback paths share one implementation. Each subprocess has a three-second budget, so fallback may take up to six seconds. Polling is limited to active login terminals.

The change also preserves deferred development-only xterm disposal for StrictMode and translated success/retry copy. GitHub remains optional for local workflows.

Validation:

- Backend systemcheck tests passed (`GOCACHE=/private/tmp/ao-go-cache GOWORK=off go test ./internal/service/systemcheck`).
- 186 targeted frontend tests passed across XtermTerminal, useTerminalSession, useSystemRequirementsGate, board-empty-states, and osc-color-report. The final XtermTerminal test adjustment was rerun separately (87 passed).
- Coverage includes a split DSR through the real attachment hook and XtermTerminal protocol handling with a simulated xterm parser, pending CPR credits, Cursor theme replies, renderer-restart adoption, failed terminal-list reconciliation, failed close/retry retention, and definitive empty-host sign-out.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Frontend typechecking reports only the missing local `mermaid` dependency in unchanged `mermaid-diagram.ts` (lines 93 and 100); no changed-file errors remain. Native Electron validation was not repeated for these review fixes.

title: fix(cloud-terminal): resume replay cursor across reconnects, keepalive, and fix the connect breaker
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #4763 (SSH-parity real-time cloud terminal). After that shipped, the cloud terminal WebSocket churned: it opened, died about a second later, and reconnected endlessly, so the pane stayed blank or "flashed back to the beginning" on both nodeops and coder sessions. Typing a line and watching the whole scrollback re-render from the top was the visible symptom.

## Root cause and fixes

Three related fixes, all confined to the cloud terminal path:

1. **Replay-cursor resume (primary).** The hook rebuilds the terminal mux on every reconnect, and each fresh mux sent `after=0`, so the control plane replayed the entire scrollback again and the stream never settled. `createCloudTerminalMux` now takes a shared cursor ref, and each pane gets one stable cursor so a rebuilt mux resumes from the last sequence it received instead of replaying from 0. A genuine server reset frame drops the cursor to 0 and wipes the pane before the fresh replay.

2. **Server keepalive (folds in #4792).** A `keepTerminalAlive` goroutine pings every 20s with a 5s pong deadline, so the ALB's 60s idle timeout stops severing idle terminals. A missed pong closes the stream cleanly. The ping serializes with Write on the websocket write mutex, so no extra locking.

3. **Connect-failure breaker with its false positive fixed (folds in #4668).** The mux now reports a mint 409 (worker still provisioning) as a distinct `waiting` state instead of `closed`, and the breaker counts only genuine post-mint socket failures. A slow cold start no longer false-fires the "check proxy/firewall/CSP" overlay; a real CSP or proxy block still trips it after 8 socket failures and surfaces a retryable overlay. Backend lease-suppression is included so a broken looping client can no longer hold a sandbox awake and billed.

## Tests

- `cloud-terminal-mux.test.ts`: cursor resume across reconnects, and reset frame drops the cursor and clears the pane.
- `useTerminalSession.test.tsx`: breaker semantics (the `waiting` state never trips, `closed` trips at 8, resets on attach).
- `cd cloud && go build ./... && go vet ./...` green; frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean for the changed files.

## Scope

16 files, but 8 are the i18n locale catalogs (one new error string) and 2 are test files. The real logic is 5 files, all cloud-terminal. No migrations. Provider-neutral: fixes nodeops and coder terminals the same way.

title: feat(cloud): auto-link a project's UI-created worker to its active orchestrator
body:
Part of #4574 (orchestrator drives its worker sessions end to end).

> **Draft, stacked.** Base is `feat/cloud-provider-selector` (#4912), which this needs to compile (the `provider` field on `createSessionRequest`). It must also land after #4676 for the reverse channel to function. Retarget the base to `main` and rebase once #4912 merges. Do not merge before #4676 and #4912.

## Problem

A cloud orchestrator only saw workers it spawned itself. Everything the orchestrator uses to see and drive its workers, `ao list`, the Workers view, `ao send` / `ao kill`, and the `ao report` reverse channel, keys off `parent_session_id`. A worker created directly from the UI composer comes in as a top-level `kind=worker` with no parent, so it was invisible to the project's orchestrator. This diverged from local AO, where the orchestrator sees every worker in the project regardless of who created it.

## Fix

`createSession` now looks up the project's single active orchestrator (`ProjectActiveOrchestrator`) when creating a top-level worker and, if one exists:

1. Stamps `parent_session_id` onto the worker, so it shows in the orchestrator's `ao list` and Workers view and is controllable via `ao send` / `ao kill`.
2. Inherits the orchestrator's sandbox provider, so the project's whole worker tree stays on one provider (nodeops or coder), matching `ao spawn`ed children.
3. Grants the worker `worker:report` scope so it can report back up the reverse channel.

## Guardrails (all covered by tests)

- A worker created before any orchestrator exists stays standalone. No retroactive linking.
- An orchestrator is never auto-linked to another orchestrator.
- If the client selected a different provider than the orchestrator runs on, the orchestrator's provider wins, so the tree cannot split across providers.

## Tests

`cloud/internal/httpapi/resource_handlers_autolink_test.go`, three cases:
- auto-links a UI worker to the project orchestrator and inherits its provider over the client selection and the control-plane default,
- leaves a worker standalone when there is no active orchestrator,
- never auto-links an orchestrator.

`cd cloud && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./internal/httpapi/...` green on the stacked base.

## Scope

4 files, 219 insertions, 1 deletion. 144 of those lines are the test file. The logic is the handler lookup, the store query, and the `ParentSessionID` DTO field. No migrations (reuses the existing `parent_session_id` column).

title: bug(windows): Plan Mode toggle disappears after clicking it in a fresh OpenCode task
body:
## Bug

On Windows, in a fresh OpenCode chat task, clicking the Plan Mode switch makes the entire Plan Mode row disappear from the model/settings menu. Closing and reopening the menu does not restore it, leaving no visible control to revert the selection.

## Reproduction

1. In the Windows desktop app, open a project's actions menu and choose **New session**.
2. Select **opencode**, leave the prompt empty, and click **Start task**.
3. Wait for the composer controls to initialize. The test resolved to **OpenCode Zen/Big Pickle**.
4. Open the composer's model/settings menu. **Model** and **Plan Mode** are visible; the Plan Mode switch appears off.
5. Click the Plan Mode switch.
6. After the UI updates, the **Plan Mode row disappears**, leaving only **Model**.
7. Close and reopen the menu. Plan Mode is still absent.

**Expected:** The Plan Mode control remains available, reflects the selected mode, and allows switching back.
**Actual:** The control disappears after clicking it, preventing the user from reverting through the menu.

No prompt was sent in the fresh task, so an active/completed turn is not required to reproduce this.

## Verification and environment

- Reproduced in the installed Agent Orchestrator Windows desktop app.
- Fresh task: **Untitled task**, project **22**, workspace label **ao-22-10**.
- Harness: **OpenCode**. Displayed model: **OpenCode Zen/Big Pickle**.
- Exact Windows and installed AO versions have not been recorded.
- UI reproduction confidence: **high** (observed before clicking, after clicking, and after reopening).
- Root cause: **unconfirmed**. The UI observation does not establish whether the underlying session successfully entered planning mode.
- The repository was updated to main at f40e7c18ce9e474bda72cc2c27226586f187209c before filing; verification used the installed desktop app, not a new build of this checkout.
- Original report: @somewherelostt.

Earlier verification in existing tasks showed the control already missing. The fresh-task test above establishes the transition that triggers the visible failure.

## Original reporter screenshots

![Model menu showing only Model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-windows-plan-toggle-20260906-dd3d176d/.issue-assets/windows-plan-toggle-20260906-dd3d176d/screenshot-1.png)

## Investigation needed

Trace the execution-mode change response and subsequent config-option state for OpenCode. Determine why the mode control is removed after clicking Plan Mode, preserve a reversible mode selector, and verify the underlying mode matches the UI.

title: Add Qwen Code Chat UI via native ACP
body:
## Summary

Give Qwen Code sessions the same Chat UI the other agents already have.

Fixes #4987. Follow-up handoff tracked in #5420. Upstream approval-mode thread: QwenLM/qwen-code#11887.

## The problem, in plain language

1. A Qwen session always opened in the terminal view. There was no Chat option, while agents like Cursor, Pi, and OMP all offer one.
2. This is not a crash or a regression. Chat is switched on separately for each agent, and Qwen was simply never switched on.
3. In code terms: Qwen had no entry in the chat-driver registry, so the app treated it as terminal-only.

## What this PR does, point by point

1. Adds a small Qwen Chat driver (`qwenacp`). It starts the Qwen program you already have installed, in its Chat mode (`qwen --acp`). Nothing new to install, no second login.
2. Registers Qwen in the chat-driver list, so Settings and the session tab now offer Chat for Qwen like the others.
3. Maps AO permission modes onto Qwen modes (Default to Ask Permissions, accept-edits to auto-edit, auto to auto, bypass to yolo). Qwen enforces them over `session/request_permission`, verified live on 0.23.4, so ask-me Chat genuinely asks.
4. Requires Qwen Code 0.16.0 or newer. Older versions get a clear error message instead of a broken Chat.
5. `POST /api/v1/orchestrators` accepts `approvalMode`, and the replacement dialog offers Start without approvals exactly when the daemon reports missing approvals with bypass allowed, mirroring the worker fallback.
6. Bundled fix for the harness reinstall flow: a reinstall from Settings could leave the daemon launching the old binary path, because `codex` cached it. This adds `AgentBinaryResolutionInvalidator`, implemented by `codex` and `qwen` (both cache the path), and the reinstall path calls it so the next readiness, model-discovery, or launch resolves the current install. It lives here because the 0.16.0 floor pushes Qwen users through exactly that reinstall.
7. Qwen TUI sessions can now switch to Chat live: the TUI adapter declares the shared native session identity plus a transcript-existence probe, mirroring Codex. Sessions that still cannot hand off say so in plain words instead of daemon jargon.

## How to check it by hand

1. Run this branch in the desktop app.
2. Open Settings, General, Session interface, pick Chat.
3. Spawn a Qwen worker: the Chat surface renders with picker, composer, and the approval menu (Default / Auto Edit / Auto / YOLO, see screenshot).

![Qwen Chat surface with approval picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95c34ed3-3512-40a6-9e02-3419eaee9572)
4. Ask it to run a non-read-only shell command: an approval card appears. Deny it and the command never runs.
5. You need Qwen Code 0.16.0 or newer installed and logged in. An API key in the environment alone is not enough; pick an auth method inside Qwen first.


## Verification so far

- Unit tests pass: driver flags, permission mapping, model option, version check, registry list, session spawn/delegate/orchestrator endpoints, orchestrator bypass predicate, dialog, handoff copy.
- Live approval-channel test (`TestLiveQwenACPApprovalChannel`, env-gated) passes against Qwen 0.23.4.
- Live end-to-end on a dev daemon: standalone Qwen Chat spawn admitted, turn completed with exact text, `rm` raised a 4-option approval, deny returned 204 with the file intact.
- Typecheck clean. Backend and frontend suites green apart from pre-existing environment gaps (landing `cheerio`, main-process native bindings) and two load flakes that pass isolated.

## Notes for reviewers

- Qwen still ships an older `--experimental-acp` flag, but it prints a deprecation warning, so this PR uses the stable `--acp`.
- TUI to Chat live-switch for Qwen is implemented here and closes #5420: a TUI worker switched to Chat with history intact and a follow-up Chat turn completing, verified live on a dev daemon.

title: fix(windows): hide persistent chat provider console
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5018

## Summary
- launch persistent chat-provider children through AO's shared process helper
- suppress the provider console window on Windows without changing non-Windows behavior

## Root cause
The persistent chat host launched Codex with raw `exec.Command`, bypassing AO's Windows process attributes (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and `HideWindow`). Windows therefore allocated a visible console for the provider. Closing that console terminated the provider, so AO correctly reported the session as exited.

Passed locally on Windows:
- focused native regression: `TestDetachedHostProviderDoesNotAllocateConsoleWindow`
- `go test ./internal/process -count=1`
- `go build ./...`
- Linux/amd64 compile-only check for `internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost`

Local suite limitations:
- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and the pinned golangci-lint run encounter existing Windows failures, led by `host_race_test.go` using unavailable `syscall.Kill`; the linter also reports existing findings in unrelated Windows files.

title: fix(updates): only confirm a restart when work is actually at risk
body:
Reported: clicking **Restart & install** in Settings → Updates opens a confirmation dialog *on top of* the Settings modal.

With no session mid-turn, that dialog carries nothing — no warning, a copy of the release notes, and a line explaining the build installs on the next quit regardless. A modal over a modal to repeat what the button already said.

## Why it was there, and why that reason had a scope

The confirmation was added by #4849 because a single click used to quit the app unasked. That reason holds only when a session would actually lose an in-flight turn.

`update-install-risk.ts` already makes exactly this argument, for *which sessions to list*:

> Quitting is NOT uniformly destructive, and treating it as if it were would warn on almost every session and **teach the user to click through**.

It just was never applied to *whether the dialog should open at all*. A confirmation with no warning in it is that same failure one level up.

## Change

Both entry points — the sidebar restart row and the Settings button — now share one decision:

- **A session would lose a turn** → the dialog opens, unchanged, warning list and all.
- **Nothing at risk** → install directly.
- **Workspace list unresolved** → still confirms. Unknown is not safe; this matches the `no_signal` bias inside the risk filter.

Release notes lived *only* in that dialog, so skipping it would have hidden them. They now render in the Updates panel, which has room the dialog never did.

## Implementation note

The decision reads the workspace list from the query cache instead of calling `useWorkspaceQuery`. Both callers are mounted for the whole shell's lifetime and need this only on click, and that hook pulls in the cloud org/session queries — routing it through the hook made **37 sidebar and Settings tests fail** demanding cloud bridge mocks they have no reason to provide. The dialog's own comment warns about the same coupling.

Local projects only: a cloud session does not die when this desktop app quits, so it is never at risk here.

## Verification

Rendered before/after against the real token values rather than reasoning about it:

- **Today:** dialog stacked over the Settings panel, contentless.
- **After:** panel shows status, last-checked and What's new; the button installs.
- **At-risk case:** dialog still appears with its warning list.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| `npx vitest run` (full suite) | **281 files, 3864 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed** |

Four new cases cover the decision directly: installs directly with only safe sessions, confirms with an at-risk session, confirms when the list has not resolved, installs directly with no sessions.

Independent of #4981 (updater install-rejection + status delivery); branched from `main`.

title: feat(cli): extend `ao doctor` to probe all 26 registered agent harness binaries
body:
### Problem

`ao doctor` currently defines a hardcoded slice of only 3 agent harnesses (`claude-code`, `codex`, `muse`) under `doctorHarnesses` in `backend/internal/cli/doctor.go`. 

However, the backend agent registry (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/registry`) supports 26+ agent harnesses. Users running `ao doctor` cannot verify whether their installed CLI binaries (such as `opencode`, `aider`, `goose`, `grok`, `cursor`, `agy`, `copilot`, `cline`, `continue`, `droid`, etc.) are recognized on `PATH` or configured properly.


### Proposed direction

Extend `doctorHarnesses` in `backend/internal/cli/doctor.go` to list all 26 registered agent harness adapters:

- **Tier A (with `--version`):** `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `muse`
- **Tier B (with `--version`):** `aider`, `goose`, `grok`, `devin`, `kimi`, `kiro` (`kiro-cli`), `kilocode` (`kilo`), `omp`
- **Tier B (PATH existence fallback):** `cursor` (`cursor-agent`), `copilot`, `amp`, `agy`, `crush`, `cline`, `auggie`, `continue` (`cn`), `droid`, `kimchi`, `pi`, `qwen`, `vibe`, `autohand`, `prime-agent`

Add comprehensive unit test assertions in `backend/internal/cli/doctor_test.go` to ensure all 26 harnesses remain registered and tested without drift.


### Alternatives considered

Leaving `doctorHarnesses` hardcoded to only 3 agents requires users to manually verify executable resolution on `PATH` for all other supported agent harnesses.

- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: feat(board): show token counts on kanban session cards

## Feature

Show **token counts on the kanban session board cards** — each session card should display tokens processed, per user feedback: "we should have tokens shown for each session in kanban."

**Requested by:** Rishet11 in #dev-chat, 2026-09-07

*(Re-scoped 2026-09-07: this issue previously targeted Codex account cards in Settings — wrong surface. The ask is the session board cards, not Settings.)*

## Current state

- Board cards already have a usage chip: `toUsagePresentation` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoardAdapters.tsx` renders it in the card footer next to the timestamp.
- The chip is **hidden entirely** unless `usage.processedTokens` is non-null and > 0. `processedTokens` comes from `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions` and is nulled when any usage event row is missing input/output values.

## Proposal

1. Always render the usage chip on session cards when usage data exists for the session — fall back to token count when cost is unknown, and vice versa. Don't blank the chip.
2. Show the **token count** (e.g. `128k`) on the card; exact count in tooltip/aria-label.
3. Keep the no-misleading-zeros rule: no chip when the provider reported nothing (`processedTokens` null/0).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every board card with usage telemetry shows its token count.
- [ ] Exact figure available via tooltip or aria-label.
- [ ] Cards with no telemetry render no chip (no zeros).

title: fix(updater): own a download the check itself started
body:
Closes a verified serialization leak in the updater: three entry points can start a download and then let it outlive the operation that started it.

## The defect

With `autoDownload` set, `doCheckForUpdates()` starts the download and returns its promise **without awaiting it** — deliberately, marked `noinspection ES6MissingAwait` in `AppUpdater.js:416-422`. On macOS that promise does not resolve until the whole archive has been served to Squirrel over the localhost proxy (`executeDownload` awaits `done()`, which resolves on the HTTP response's `finish` event).

So when the promise escapes, the serialized operation settles while the download, the handoff and the native staging behind it are still running. The queue then hands the updater to the next operation on top of them, and the manual check's `finally` restores the feed while the download is still using it.

### The automatic path had it in its most surprising form

```js
autoUpdater.autoDownload = staleStaged || (settings.enabled && !hasStagedBuild());
// ...
if (settings.enabled) {
  if (result?.downloadPromise) await result.downloadPromise;   // never reached when disabled
}
```

`staleStaged` forces a download **precisely when the preference is off** — that is the case the force exists for, since a build from a channel the user has left is already armed with the OS installer and must be superseded, or quitting installs the build they moved away from. The existing comment in that block says exactly this; the gate below it then skipped the await for those users.

`checkForUpdatesNow` and `returnToHome` set `autoDownload = staleStaged` and awaited only the check.

## The fix

One invariant, applied to all three paths via a new `awaitStartedDownload()`:

> If a check returns a download promise, own and await it **regardless of the auto-update preference.** The preference gates only the separate decision to *start* an additional download.

The helper also sets the download phase, so a failure is attributed to the download rather than to the check that began it. Both manual paths capture that phase in a local box, because `runSerializedUpdaterOperation` clears global operation state in its own `finally` before their `catch` runs — a manifest 404 during a forced download now reads "Download failed — the update file was not found on the server." instead of the check wording.

No new access to library internals: `downloadPromise` and `cancellationToken` are both on the public `UpdateCheckResult`.

## Tests

Four new cases, each **verified to fail against the previous behaviour**:

- automatic path owns a forced download with auto-download **off**
- manual check stays open until the forced download finishes
- return-home stays open until the forced download finishes
- the **next queued operation** does not start until it finishes

Two probes were run to prove they bite. Removing ownership everywhere fails all four plus one pre-existing test that already depended on it. Restoring just the `settings.enabled` gate fails **exactly one** — the automatic path with the preference off, which is the defect this PR fixes.

`typecheck` clean; full suite `3852 passed`. Unrelated local failures: `browser-profile-import.test.ts` (a `better_sqlite3` native ABI mismatch from running tests on node 20.19, because vitest will not start on this machine's node 22.11) and one `Sidebar.test.tsx` timing flake that passes in isolation — neither is reachable from this main-process change.

## Risk and scope

Low blast radius on the manual paths: they only set `autoDownload` when a staged build is stale, so behaviour is unchanged in the common case. The automatic path changes for users with auto-download **disabled** and a stale staged build — who previously got an unowned download.

Deliberately not in scope: readiness/staging semantics (`stagedAtMs` still lands on electron-updater's optimistic `update-downloaded`) and the install-rejection recovery in #4981. Both are tracked separately; this PR is independent of #4981 and touches no overlapping regions.

title: bug(omp): fresh session restore passes --resume with a UUID OMP never persisted
body:
## Summary

A fresh OMP TUI session fails on restore because AO passes `omp --resume <uuid>` with a native session UUID that OMP never persisted to its local session store. OMP exits immediately with `Error: Session "<uuid>" not found`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a fresh OMP TUI session via `+ Task` or API
2. OMP starts, AO captures the native session ID from the JS extension hook
3. Daemon restarts (or any event that triggers reconciliation/restore)
4. AO calls `GetRestoreCommand`, which sees the captured `agentSessionId` and builds `omp --resume <uuid>`
5. OMP rejects the UUID because its session data lives in the old worktree or was never flushed

## Observed

```
Error: Session "01a07a5f-dd88-7537-9bbd-7165ecba238f" not found.
Run 'omp --resume' without an argument to pick from recent sessions, or 'omp' to start a new one.
[process exited]
```

Activity shows "Exited" with "Resume agent" button, but clicking Resume triggers the same error in a loop.

## Expected

AO should either:
- Verify the native session exists before passing `--resume` (similar to Claude Code's `NativeConversationExists` check)
- Fall back to a fresh launch when `--resume` fails with "not found"

## Environment

- AO: built from source (main branch, commit f7d6c9c)
- OMP: v18.1.12 via npm, Bedrock provider
- macOS (Apple Silicon)

## Related

- #4936 (Ctrl+C strands OMP sessions — exit detection)
- #3875 (fresh orchestrator spawn crashes with "invalid session id" — similar pattern for Claude Code)
- #2702 (zombie sessions after daemon restart)

title: bug(terminal): desktop relaunch destroys session side shells and standalone terminals
body:
## Bug

Closing and reopening the AO desktop app removes user-opened shell terminals, including side terminals inside a surviving agent session. The primary agent terminal remains available. Users can run agents, builds or servers in these side shells, so this loses running work, not merely tab layout.

**Source:** maintainer report in AO chat, 2026-09-07. No public chat URL available.
**Environment:** macOS arm64; installed app `0.12.13-nightly.202609061848`; packaged daemon verified ready on loopback port 3001.
**Analyzed against:** current main `4ffcd10462839233c8761b6528e78cc5818d4c58`.
**Confidence:** high in the code mechanism. The full desktop restart was reported by the user; I did not restart the live app or destroy its terminals during triage.

## Reproduction reported by the user

1. Open an agent session and an additional shell terminal in that session.
2. Run a long-lived command or another coding agent in the side terminal.
3. Fully quit the desktop app and reopen it.
4. The main agent session/terminal survives, but the side terminal disappears. Standalone shell tabs are affected too.

Closing only a macOS window without quitting the app is a distinct path and has not been established as affected.

## Established mechanism

This is an explicit existing lifetime policy, inherited from the original ephemeral-shell design, which does not match the reported expectation:

- `frontend/src/main.ts:980` mints a new `apprun-${randomUUID()}` per desktop process; `:1031` passes it as `AO_APP_RUN_ID` to the daemon. It stays the same across supervised daemon restarts, but changes across desktop relaunches.
- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/service.go:50` documents that shells survive daemon restarts but die with the app. Shell rows record `AppRunID`, even when session-scoped.
- `backend/internal/daemon/shellterm_wiring.go:42` calls `ReapShellTerminalsFromPreviousAppRuns` at daemon startup.
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/shell_terminals.sql` selects every row with `app_run_id <> current`, with no exemption for a surviving session.
- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/service.go:570` destroys each selected runtime and deletes the row after death is confirmed. The list endpoint also filters to the current app-run ID (`:532`).
- The existing `TestReapShellTerminalsFromPreviousAppRunsDestroysOrphansOnly` explicitly expects the old run's PTYs to be destroyed. `TestListShellTerminalsForCurrentAppRunReturnsSurvivingTerminals` covers the narrower same-app-run daemon restart.

The boot-time destroy path alone explains loss after close/reopen. This report does not assert an independently reproduced exact time of process death during shutdown versus startup.

## Validation

`cd backend && go test ./internal/service/shellterm -run 'Test.*(Reap|AppRun)' -count=1` passed. These existing tests confirm the implemented destruction/reconnection policy with fake runtime and storage boundaries; they are not a fresh live-desktop restart reproduction.

## Desired behavior / fix direction

User-opened side and standalone terminals should reconnect across desktop restart/update when the runtime is still alive. Treat them as durable terminal resources, not disposable resources owned by one app launch.

- Reconcile previous-run rows by actual runtime liveness and ownership; do not destroy them solely because the desktop launch ID changed.
- Restore session/project association, working directory, title, and attachable handle; adjust list filtering as well as startup reaping.
- Keep explicit terminal close, confirmed process exit, and parent-session/worktree teardown as legitimate cleanup boundaries.
- Preserve unknown/error liveness results rather than treating them as dead.
- Distinguish temporary authentication/command terminals from user-opened shells if those need different cleanup policies; avoid making every transient terminal immortal.
- Test desktop relaunch (new app-run ID), daemon restart (same ID), explicit close, session/worktree teardown, and failed liveness probes. Use an isolated daemon/runtime fixture, not the maintainer's running sessions.

## Related restart-safety gap

[PR #5021](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5021) bases restart confirmation on agent sessions. Arbitrary commands or a coding agent launched inside a side shell are not represented by that predicate. While side shells retain the current destructive lifetime policy, update/restart may therefore proceed without warning about that work. This should be accounted for in the lifecycle fix or a focused interim confirmation change.

## Related work

- [#2828](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2828): original standalone terminal feature, described ephemeral lifetime.
- [#4538](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4538): fixed close/rename behavior for direct-host shell handles; different issue.
- [#4526](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4526): persistence of native chat providers; separate from shell-terminal ownership.

Searches across open and closed issues/PRs found no existing report matching the explicit app-run reaping problem.

title: feat(desktop): make sidebar updates a live download-to-install flow
body:
Human Summary
the updates ui will be updated more frequently with accurate and live data instead of cache'd data. example flow - 
1. the updates check every 15 minutes (nightly) and 60 minutes (stable)
2. update arrives, the sidebar will show a box - Downloading for users with Automatic Downloads on and a button to click Download for users with that toggle off, it also shows the percentage downloaded on sidebar and settings update ui
3. once it downloads, it turns the sidebar box green and shows Preparing Update soon replaced by Install Update
4. once prepared, if you click Install Update, it checks for worker liveness, informs that workers will be stopped for updating and gives the users a option to install or not. 

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem

The user reports that parts of Updates appear stale until Settings is closed and reopened. Sidebar discovery, download progress, preparation, and installation should form one continuous, visible flow. Installed version, target version, check timing, and failure states must remain clear without reopening Settings.

Source investigation used upstream/main at `4ffcd10462839233c8761b6528e78cc5818d4c58`. This is a user-reported UX problem plus a source-based behavior specification, not a reproduced runtime failure.

## Agreed flow

1. Keep automatic discovery every 15 minutes for unpinned Nightly and every 60 minutes for Stable or a feature pin, plus the existing startup/manual checks. These are discovery intervals, not UI refresh intervals.
2. As soon as AO discovers an update, show it above Connect Mobile/Account in the sidebar and begin downloading immediately when automatic downloads are enabled. Preserve the existing automatic-download preference; disabled users get an explicit Download action.
3. Immediately show `Starting download…` when a download is requested, before the first bytes arrive. Prevent duplicate download actions while it starts.
4. Show `X% downloaded` and a compact progress bar in the sidebar. Keep percentage current while bytes arrive. Settings shows the same progress with downloaded/total MB and clearly separated `Running vX` and `Updating to vY` values.
5. At 100% transfer, show `Preparing update…` while verification/native staging remains outstanding. Only when actually installable, turn the sidebar action green and label it `Install Update`. Download completion alone is not native readiness on macOS.
6. Clicking `Install Update` checks current worker interruption risk. If no worker is at risk, install and restart immediately without a prompt. Otherwise show the affected workers and explain that installing restarts AO and may interrupt their current tasks, with `Cancel` and `Install and restart` actions. This flow must not deliberately terminate workers that can survive restart.

## Live state and Settings behavior

- Sidebar, collapsed sidebar, Settings, and the restart confirmation must reflect the same current update state. Closing/reopening Settings must never be necessary to refresh it.
- Use downloader progress events immediately. Add a lightweight local status reconciliation every few seconds while Settings is open or an update is active, if needed to recover missed notifications. This must not repeatedly check GitHub or restart a download. Percentage must represent real transferred bytes, never simulated progress.
- If progress stops, expose a waiting/stalled/error state with an appropriate retry action instead of leaving a frozen percentage without explanation.
- Clicking Check immediately shows `Checking now…`. Completion shows `Checked just now`, with sufficient timestamp precision to distinguish repeated checks. Failures remain explicit; do not imply a successful check when one failed. Relative timestamps should age while Settings remains open.
- Running version comes from the current app process and changes after restart into another build. Available/downloaded versions are separate and update live.
- Keep channel, feature pin, release notes, errors, and readiness current too. Background checks must not hide an already valid staged update or overwrite newer download progress. Sidebar-only dismissal must not hide status in Settings.

## Restart risk: verified existing behavior to preserve

Current `sessionsAtRiskFromInstall` treats live non-Codex chat sessions in `working`, `needs_input`, or `no_signal` as potentially interrupted. Terminal/TUI sessions and Codex chat use detached runtimes/hosts and are designed to survive daemon replacement. The warning should describe interrupted current tasks, not imply every running worker is killed.

`useRequestUpdateInstall` already installs directly with a fresh safe workspace snapshot, but prompts when the snapshot is missing, stale, invalidated, fetching, or failed. Refresh current worker state on click before deciding so an old cache alone does not produce an unnecessary warning. If current state cannot be established, retain a confirmation rather than treating unknown as no active work. Keep the confirmation's affected-worker list current.

Evidence at the investigated commit:

- [Existing risk classification](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/4ffcd10462839233c8761b6528e78cc5818d4c58/frontend/src/renderer/lib/update-install-risk.ts#L39)
- [Current install decision](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/4ffcd10462839233c8761b6528e78cc5818d4c58/frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useRequestUpdateInstall.ts#L20)
- [Backend Close versus Terminate semantics](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/4ffcd10462839233c8761b6528e78cc5818d4c58/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L2032)
- [Existing test: daemon shutdown preserves persistent conversation](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/4ffcd10462839233c8761b6528e78cc5818d4c58/backend/internal/service/chat/controller_test.go#L3666)

## Implementation entry points and validation

Relevant files: `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`, `main.ts`, `preload.ts`, `renderer/hooks/useUpdateStatus.ts`, `renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx`, `renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx`, `renderer/hooks/useRequestUpdateInstall.ts`, and `renderer/components/RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx`.

The current investigated commit already includes shell WebContents delivery and listener-before-snapshot protection. Do not assume the older dropped-push or late-snapshot regressions are still present.

Use mocked updater events, fake timers, IPC tests, and component tests to verify the complete flow, missed-event recovery, 100%-but-not-ready staging, stale worker-data refresh, conditional confirmation, and consistency without remounting Settings. No real install/restart experiments or interruption of live workers are authorized. No wake/reconnect discovery expansion or change to the 15/60-minute cadence is required by this issue.

title: [Bug]: workspace file with a backslash in its name resolves to the wrong file on Linux/macOS
body:
### Summary

A workspace file whose name contains a backslash cannot be opened through the workspace-files API on Linux or macOS. The request either fails or, worse, silently resolves to a different file.

### Steps to reproduce

In any session workspace, create a file with a backslash in its name — legal on Linux and macOS:

```bash
cd <session worktree>
mkdir -p dir
printf 'real\n'  > 'dir/weird\name.txt'
mkdir -p 'dir/weird' && printf 'decoy\n' > 'dir/weird/name.txt'
```

Then request the first file through the API:

```bash
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/<id>/workspace/file?path=dir/weird%5Cname.txt"
```

### Expected behavior

The contents of `dir/weird\name.txt` — the file that was asked for.

### Actual behavior

The contents of `dir/weird/name.txt`. The backslash is treated as a path separator, so the request reaches a different file entirely. With no decoy present the read simply fails.

### Root cause

`cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` in `backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go` normalizes unconditionally:

```go
trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ReplaceAll(raw, "\\", "/"))
```

Backslash is a path separator only on Windows. On Linux and macOS it is an ordinary filename character. The file contains no `runtime.GOOS` reference at all, so the Windows-only normalization is applied on every platform.

The silent-wrong-file case is the part that concerns me more than the failure: nothing surfaces an error, and the caller gets plausible content from a path it did not ask for.

### AO version

Built from source at `8845575a` (current `main`).

### Environment

Linux (Arch/Omarchy), kernel 7.1.9, x86_64, Go 1.27.1.

### Logs / extra context

Found by reading the path-handling code while working in this area, then reproducing against a local daemon.

I have a fix ready and will raise a PR for it: gate the replacement on `runtime.GOOS == "windows"`, with a regression test for the POSIX case and a second test pinning that the existing traversal guards (absolute paths, `..`, empty input) still reject as before.

title: Kiro auth probe reports unknown: kiro-cli whoami --format json appends non-JSON profile trailer
body:
### Summary
`ao agent ls --refresh` always reports `kiro auth unknown`, even when `kiro-cli whoami` proves a valid, active login. The daemon's Kiro auth probe classifies `kiro-cli whoami --format json` output with the generic keyword matcher in `authprobe.StatusFromText`, but that JSON output never contains any of the recognized keywords (`logged in`, `authenticated`, `"loggedin": true`, etc.), so a signed-in session is always classified as `unknown`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Sign in to Kiro (`kiro-cli login`, or via IAM Identity Center / SSO).
2. Confirm the session is valid: `kiro-cli whoami` prints a "Logged in with..." message and an email.
3. Run `kiro-cli whoami --format json` directly and inspect stdout (see "Actual behavior" below).
4. Run `ao agent ls --refresh` (or open the New Task / agent catalog UI).

### Expected behavior
`ao agent ls --refresh` reports the `kiro` row as `installed` / authorized (or at least not `unknown`) when `kiro-cli whoami` proves an active login.

### Actual behavior
The `kiro` row shows:

```
kiro  Kiro  installed  auth unknown
```

Root cause, reproduced locally with `kiro-cli 2.21.1` on macOS:

`kiro-cli whoami --format json` prints a JSON object followed by a plain-text trailer, so stdout as a whole is not valid JSON (`jq .` on it exits 5):

```
{"accountType":"IamIdentityCenter","email":"<redacted>","region":"eu-west-1","startUrl":"https://d-<redacted>.awsapps.com/start"}

Profile:
KiroProfile-us-east-1
arn:aws:codewhisperer:us-east-1:<redacted>:profile/<redacted>
```

Exit code is 0 in all cases (`--format json`, `--format json-pretty`, and plain format). The plain format instead prints `Logged in with IAM Identity Center (https://...)` then `Email: ...` then the same `Profile:` block.

The probe function `kiro.kiroWhoamiAuthStatus` (in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/auth.go`, called from `kiro.(*Plugin).AuthStatus`) runs `kiro-cli whoami --format json` and hands the raw output straight to `authprobe.StatusFromText` (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/authprobe/authprobe.go`), which only recognizes generic phrases like `logged in`, `authenticated`, `"loggedin": true`. None of those appear in the JSON identity object above (its fields are `accountType`, `email`, `region`, `startUrl`), so the probe falls through to `AgentAuthStatusUnknown` even for a fully authenticated session — independent of, and in addition to, the JSON-plus-trailer parsing issue.

### AO version
`dev` (built from `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator@main`, `go run ./cmd/ao`; `ao version` reports `dev` in this build)

### Environment
macOS (darwin/arm64), Go 1.25.4, kiro-cli 2.21.1

### Logs / extra context
No daemon crash or error — this is a silent misclassification. All account identifiers above are redacted placeholders (`<redacted>`), not real values.

---
This issue was generated by Claude Code Agent.

title: fix(workspace): keep a backslash in a filename on Linux and macOS
body:
## What

Applies the backslash-to-slash normalization in `cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` only on Windows.

Fixes #5044.

## Why

Backslash is a path separator on Windows and an ordinary filename character everywhere else. `cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` folded it unconditionally, so on Linux and macOS a workspace file named `weird\name.txt` could not be read through the workspace-files API — and where a `weird/` directory happened to exist, the request silently returned a *different* file's contents instead of failing.

The file carried no `runtime.GOOS` reference at all, so a Windows-only rule was being applied on every platform.

## How

One conditional around the existing `ReplaceAll`.

The traversal guards are untouched: empty input, absolute paths, `..` and `../`-prefixed paths are still rejected. A second test pins that, so this cannot be read as loosening validation while widening what filenames are accepted.

## Testing

`TestCleanWorkspaceRelativePathKeepsBackslashOnPOSIX` fails without the fix with:

```
workspace_files_path_test.go:22: got "dir/weird/name.txt", want "dir/weird\name.txt";
a backslash must stay part of the filename on this platform
```

It skips on Windows, where the folding is correct. `TestCleanWorkspaceRelativePathStillRejectsEscapes` covers the guards. Package tests pass.

title: fix(scm/github): stop sending an ignored `since` to the pulls endpoint
body:
## What

Stops sending `since` to the pull-requests endpoint, and applies the incremental watermark client-side instead.

Fixes #5045.

## Why

`ListPRsByRepo` passed `since` to `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`. That endpoint has no such parameter — `since` belongs to the Issues API — and GitHub silently ignores unknown query parameters rather than erroring. The incremental watermark therefore did nothing: every repository with any change re-listed all of its open PRs, and paged through all of them, on every poll.

Nothing surfaced this, which is why it survived: the code reads as though it were filtering.

## How

The filter moves to the client, where it is exact rather than best-effort. The query already asks for `sort=updated&direction=desc`, so the first PR at or before the watermark means every remaining one is older — the loop returns there instead of walking the remaining pages.

An unparseable `updated_at` keeps the PR rather than dropping it. A redundant observation costs one extra comparison; a missed one loses a PR update.

## Testing

`TestListPRsByRepoFiltersOnWatermarkWithoutSinceParam` asserts both halves — that the request carries no `since`, and that only PRs newer than the watermark come back. Without the fix it fails with:

```
request carried since="2026-01-02T00:00:00Z"; the pulls endpoint ignores it
```

`TestListPRsByRepoZeroWatermarkReturnsEverything` pins that a zero watermark still returns a full listing, so the change cannot be read as filtering more than it should. Package tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: fix(copilot): exclude session agent profiles with one glob, not one line per session
body:
## What

Excludes AO's Copilot session profiles with one glob instead of one line per session, and prunes the per-session lines earlier versions left behind.

Fixes #5046.

## Why

The adapter writes a role profile to `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` and adds it to the workspace's `.git/info/exclude`. `ignoreCopilotPath` already guards against duplicates:

```go
if pattern == "" || strings.Contains(string(data), pattern) {
    return nil
}
```

but the pattern it receives is the literal profile path, and `copilotAgentName` returns `"ao-" + sessionID`. Every session therefore presents a different pattern, the guard can never match a previous entry, and each session appends another line to a file that belongs to the user rather than to AO. Nothing removes them.

Worth being explicit since the guard looks correct at a glance: the duplicate check works exactly as written — it is the value being checked that makes it ineffective.

## How

Exclude `/.github/agents/ao-*.agent.md` once. One line covers every session, past and future.

The same write also prunes the superseded per-session lines, so existing repositories are repaired rather than merely stopping the growth. Only lines matching the exact shape this package wrote are removed: the regex is anchored and rejects a `*`, so a user's own entry under that directory is left alone. A test pins that unrelated rules in the file survive.

## Testing

- `TestIgnoreCopilotPathWritesOneGlobForAllSessions` — three calls leave exactly one pattern.
- `TestIgnoreCopilotPathPrunesPerSessionLines` — pre-existing `ao-work-1` / `ao-work-2` lines are removed, the glob is present, and the user's own `# user's own rules` / `/build` entries are untouched.

Three existing tests asserted the literal per-session line. They now assert the glob: their intent — "the profile is git-excluded" — is unchanged, and the glob covers the same file. Package tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched

title: fix(mobile): apply a saved project filter only when the daemon still lists it
body:
Fixes #4843.

## What

The board's project filter is now derived from the saved choice **and** the project list the daemon returns. A saved filter naming a project the daemon no longer lists applies as **All projects**; Settings and the switcher label the filter honestly while the list cannot name it; the spawn sheet drops a seeded project the list turns out not to have; and when a valid filter hides every session, the board's empty state says so and offers **Show all projects** instead of "No active agents / Spawn a worker".

## Why

`ao.activeProject` was restored from AsyncStorage and never checked. `ao project rm` on the desktop, or pairing the phone with a machine whose projects differ, left it pointing at an id no session carries. The board filtered everything out, the spawn sheet posted the dead id and showed the 404, and nothing said the board was filtered: the switcher hides below two projects, and Settings labelled the stale id "All projects" because its lookup missed. The reporter's way out was clearing app storage.

## Changes

- `lib/projectFilter.ts` (new, pure, RN-free) — owns `ALL_PROJECTS` (moved from `ProjectPickerSheet`, its only user) and three helpers:
  - `resolveActiveProject(id, projects)`: the id when the list names it, `"all"` when it does not. **An empty list is not evidence**: it is the initial state before the first fetch, and `getSessions` substitutes `[]` when `/projects` fails so the board can still render. Judging against either would drop a valid filter on every cold start or every blip. A daemon with no projects has no sessions to filter, so nothing is lost by waiting for a list that names something.
  - `activeProjectLabel(id, projects)`: the name, "All projects", or the raw id while the list cannot name it. The "All projects" fallback is what hid the stale filter from the reporter.
  - `filteredEmptyCopy(label, {live, archived})`: names the filter and counts what Show all projects would put on the board; archived-only gets its own sentence rather than "0 agents".
- `lib/store.tsx` — the saved choice becomes `chosenProjectId`; `activeProjectId`, which every consumer already reads, is `useMemo(resolveActiveProject(chosen, projects))`. **Derived, not reset-and-written-back**, on purpose: the project can disappear while the app is open and the stored value can land after the first list does; storage is only ever written by a tap, as before; a late response from a machine the user just left cannot discard the filter they picked on the new one; and the choice comes back if the project does.
- `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` — a third empty state between the error and "No active agents", rendered only when the filter is not all and the daemon returned sessions for other projects. Live and archived counted apart via the board's own `isArchived`. `errorActions` became `emptyActions` since two empty states now share the row.
- `app/spawn.tsx` — the seed effect re-checks its `projectId` with the same helper and re-seeds when the list does not have it, so a dead id captured before the list landed is not posted. A pick from the picker is always on the list, so a pick is never overridden.
- `app/(tabs)/settings.tsx`, `lib/ProjectSwitcher.tsx` — labels via `activeProjectLabel`; the switcher keeps its colour logic.
- `lib/projectFilter.test.ts` — 10 tests over the three helpers.

## Scenarios

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Cold start, saved filter names a listed project | kept | kept, no storage write |
| Cold start, saved filter names a removed project | board empty, Settings "All projects", spawn 404 | applies as all from the first list; storage untouched |
| Storage read lands after the first list | same as above | same, on that render |
| `ao project rm` while the app is open | board empties at the next poll | the next poll's list makes it all |
| `/projects` fails on a tick (`getSessions` substitutes `[]`) | filter untouched | filter untouched; a stale one shows "Filtered to <id>" with Show all projects until the next good tick |
| Daemon lists no projects | — | filter untouched, nothing to show either way |
| Re-paired to another machine | stale filter from the old machine | validated against the new list on its first fetch; the old machine's choice is kept in storage |
| Late response from the previous machine after re-pairing | transient display glitch | still only that: nothing is written back |
| Spawn sheet opened before the list lands, saved filter dead | dead id posted, 404 | seed dropped when the list lands; re-seeds from the store |
| Filter valid, project has no sessions, others do | "No active agents" | "No agents in this project. Filtered to X. N agents are in other projects." + Show all projects, New agent |
| Same, but the other projects hold only archived sessions | "No active agents" | "… Other projects have only archived sessions." + the same buttons |

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — 719 passed (709 on main + 10)
- `npx expo export --platform ios` — bundles
- iPhone 17 Pro simulator, Debug build, packaged 0.12.11 daemon (one project `scratch`, three live sessions, one terminated session left from a removed project `ao-mobile-pr-test`). Set `ao.activeProject = "ao-mobile-pr-test"` by editing the AsyncStorage manifest with the app closed, launched on `main`, then on this branch:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Board | 0 working · 0 need you · 0 mergeable, Archive 1 | 2 working, both live cards, Archive 8 |
| `ao.activeProject` after launch | `ao-mobile-pr-test` | `ao-mobile-pr-test` — storage untouched, the fallback is derived |

## Not verified

- The filtered empty state and the spawn re-seed on a device: the test daemon has one project, so a valid filter cannot hide anything there and the sheet's seed is always on the list. Both are covered by the helper tests and the walk-through above.
- Android: JS-only, nothing platform-specific.

## Not changed

- `ProjectSwitcher` still hides below two projects. With the fallback in place a stale filter never needs the escape, and a one-project row would show a value that cannot change.
- `getSessions` still folds a failed `/projects` into `[]`, which is why the helper treats an empty list as unknown. Keeping the last good list instead (`catch(() => null)` + `setProjects(prev => next ?? prev)`) would also stop the switcher and Settings flickering to "All projects" on a failed tick, but that changes a shared response shape and is its own issue.

## Known limitation

A stale filter and a permanently failing `/projects` keep the board empty, with the filtered empty state naming the id and offering Show all projects. The daemon cannot say what it has, so the app does not guess.

title: bug(updates): nightly build timestamp is interpreted as local wall time instead of UTC
body:
## Bug

The Updates UI shows the UTC nightly build stamp as if it were already local wall time. Users outside UTC therefore see the wrong instant. The visible clock time stays equal to the UTC digits instead of being converted to the device timezone.

Analyzed against upstream main commit `c8308e64983014ac640f05df87888b7b85a25a2a` on 2026-09-07.

**Confidence:** High. The timestamp producer, parser, every renderer consumer, and current tests were traced.

**Impact:** User facing timestamp correctness only. Stored release metadata and update ordering remain correct. Stable versions and the separate Last checked timestamp are unaffected.

## Reproduction

1. Run AO in a non UTC timezone, for example `Asia/Kolkata`.
2. Install or stage nightly `v0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`.
3. Open Settings, then Updates.
4. Observe that the build time is displayed as Sep 7, 10:35 AM.
5. The embedded stamp is 2026-09-07 10:35 UTC, so the equivalent local time in India is Sep 7, 4:05 PM.

The same input currently renders 10:35 AM in `America/Los_Angeles`; the correct local time is 3:35 AM. Timezones near a date boundary can also receive the wrong calendar day in the sidebar and restart dialog.

## Timestamp source and storage distinction

GitHub release metadata remains an absolute UTC ISO timestamp. For example, the current release API returns `published_at: 2026-09-07T10:56:41Z` for `v0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`. The generated updater feed likewise stores `releaseDate` as `new Date().toISOString()` in `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`.

The affected UI does not currently render `published_at` or `releaseDate` directly. It derives the displayed build time from the `YYYYMMDDHHMM` stamp embedded in the nightly version. That stamp is also UTC:

1. `frontend/scripts/nightly-version.mjs:19-24` creates it with `getUTCFullYear`, `getUTCMonth`, `getUTCDate`, `getUTCHours`, and `getUTCMinutes`.
2. `frontend/src/renderer/lib/build-channel.ts:18-28` extracts those UTC fields but passes them to `new Date(year, month, day, hour, minute)`.
3. That Date constructor interprets its fields in the device local timezone. The represented instant is already shifted before `Intl.DateTimeFormat` receives it.
4. The locale formatter then behaves correctly for the wrong instant, so it reproduces the UTC clock digits instead of converting UTC to local time.

The stored UTC ISO timestamps, UTC nightly stamp, and ordering semantics should remain unchanged. This is an interpretation and presentation bug.

## Affected surfaces

1. Settings, Updates: `frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx:394-397,476-485`. This displays the full incorrect local date and time for the installed nightly.
2. Sidebar available or ready update row: `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx:2111-2123`. This can display the wrong local calendar day.
3. Restart to update dialog: `frontend/src/renderer/components/RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx:47-57`. This can display the wrong local calendar day.
4. Shared parser tests: `frontend/src/renderer/lib/build-channel.test.ts:24-33` assert local getters and therefore encode the incorrect interpretation. Their result also depends on the test process timezone.

The Last checked value in `UpdatesSection.tsx:418-420` is epoch milliseconds formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; it already represents an absolute instant and is not part of this bug.

## Root cause

`parseNightlyVersion` parses a UTC encoded version stamp with the local component Date constructor. It should construct the instant from UTC components, for example with `Date.UTC`, and validate against UTC getters. Once the Date represents the right instant, the existing `Intl.DateTimeFormat` calls will render the equivalent time or date in the user local timezone by default.

The defect was introduced with the current nightly presentation in commit `190df05fc21494cdca637a70622a3fbfa6273684` through [PR #4849](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4849).

## Expected behavior

For nightly stamp `202609071035`:

1. The parsed instant is `2026-09-07T10:35:00.000Z`.
2. `Asia/Kolkata` renders Sep 7, 2026 at 4:05 PM.
3. `America/Los_Angeles` renders Sep 7, 2026 at 3:35 AM.
4. All renderer surfaces use the device local timezone and locale.
5. UTC storage, feed metadata, release metadata, and version ordering do not change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Parse the nightly version stamp as UTC, not local wall time.
2. Settings Updates renders the equivalent device local date and time.
3. Sidebar and restart dialog render the correct device local calendar date, including UTC day boundary cases.
4. Existing stable, feature, malformed version, and trailing commit stamp behavior remains unchanged.
5. The separate Last checked display remains unchanged.
6. No UTC timestamp in GitHub metadata, updater feeds, or version strings is rewritten to local time.

## Tests

1. Update `build-channel.test.ts` to assert `builtAt.toISOString()` or `builtAt.getTime()` against `Date.UTC(...)`, not local getters.
2. Add positive offset and negative offset coverage showing the same UTC instant renders to the expected local time.
3. Add a day boundary case for the date only sidebar and restart dialog consumers.
4. Keep coverage for malformed stamps and trailing commit metadata.
5. Add or update component assertions for the Settings full timestamp and the two date only surfaces.

## Related

1. [Issue #2377](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2377): original restart to update and Updates screen specification.
2. [Issue #5041](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5041): recent sidebar update flow work using the shared nightly label.
3. [PR #4849](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4849): introduced the shared nightly parser and current display consumers.

## Duplicate search

Searched all issue and pull request states using: `updates timezone UTC nightly built`, `updates local time timestamp`, `nightly build date timezone`, `GitHub release timestamp UTC`, `parseNightlyVersion`, `nightly timestamp`, `built time`, `local timezone`, and `nightly date wrong`. No exact duplicate was found.
