title: bug(updater): restored staged update leaves Restart & install waiting for native preparation that never starts
body:
## Bug

On macOS, after reopening AO, both Sidebar Restart to update and Settings / confirmation Restart & install can do nothing while the UI advertises a staged newer nightly.

Reported by the maintainer in AO chat, 2026-09-07, with screenshots. Installed: `0.12.13-nightly.202609070711`; saved and natively extracted candidate: `0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`. No restart or install was triggered during this investigation.

## Live evidence preserved before changing anything

- `~/.ao/staged-update.json` records candidate `0.12.13-nightly.202609071035`.
- Native ShipItState.plist points at an existing extracted app of that candidate version.
- ShipIt log: install request at 04:07:33; installation begins 04:23:03; abort at 04:24:24 because one target app instance is still running, `SQRLInstallerErrorDomain`, code `-9`, `App Still Running Error`.
- The current AO process started at 09:33:48, later than that native attempt. The evidence does not establish why the earlier process remained running.
- Installed bundle remains the 07:11 nightly. AO's native helper is not currently running.

Copies of staged metadata, native state/logs, process start information, a clone of the current native staging directory, and an isolated control-flow probe are preserved locally in `.ao/scratch/restart-noop-evidence/`. These paths are evidence locations, not public attachments. No cache was deleted and no real application was quit.

## Mechanism: saved readiness outlives process-local native readiness

1. `restoreStagedBuild` restores `stagedVersion` and `stagedAtMs` from JSON across process launches.
2. `hasStagedBuild` and same-version checks treat that as staged; the automatic check suppresses another download/handoff for the same candidate.
3. The shared install IPC path calls `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(false, true)`.
4. In electron-updater 6.8.9, a newly constructed MacUpdater starts with `squirrelDownloadedUpdate = false`. Only a native `update-downloaded` event in that instance sets it true.
5. With that flag false and `autoInstallOnAppQuit = true`, `quitAndInstall` subscribes to native completion but does NOT initiate native checking. If no preparation is running, it waits indefinitely, with no progress/error shown to the user.

A saved JSON record and an extracted app on disk do not initialize the new process's native updater or its localhost handoff.

Confidence: high in this control-flow mechanism; no debugger was attached to the live process, so the individual live click's IPC execution and internal flag values were not directly observed.

## Reproduction evidence

An isolated VM evaluation of the published MacUpdater 6.8.9 source, with fake Electron and a minimal base updater, reproduces the no-op: fresh instance + autoInstallOnAppQuit=true + quitAndInstall => zero native checks and zero quits. Emitting native completion as a control triggers quit. This runs no real Electron application; it verifies the specific library branch, not an end-to-end installed-app reproduction.

A full regression should stage a candidate, restart the desktop process without completing installation, restore AO metadata, then request install. It must re-establish native preparation, show progress and reach native readiness before requesting quit; repeated clicks must not start overlapping native attempts or stack listeners.

## Fix direction and related work

Restore staged JSON as unconfirmed provenance. Re-establish an owned handoff for the remembered candidate before offering/executing installation; do not simply flip the library's internal readiness flag or call native quit against uninitialized state. Surface preparation progress and failure instead of silently accepting the install request.

[PR #5002](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5002) describes re-establishing remembered handoffs and native-ready install ownership; it is broader and still needs integration/review. This issue supplies a concrete live failure case for that work.

[#4254](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4254) concerns signature validation. No new signature rejection was observed here. The previously planned readiness work remains relevant even though [PR #4981](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4981), [PR #5032](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5032), and [PR #5021](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5021) have shipped.

title: feat: complete durable worker report delivery
body:
Code changes: +1865 -16
Tests: +1179 -2
Others: +1266 -0

## Summary

- Preserve the reviewed Worker Reports ingestion, validation, storage, restart recovery, and claim-token fencing foundation.
- Instruct project workers in their generated system prompt to persist checkpoints, input requests, stuck states, completion, and outputs with `ao report`.
- Deliver reports durably through Chat and supported TUI semantic boundaries, with a shared fixed one-hour ordinary fallback and a fixed five-minute first-done settlement window.
- Deliver needs-input immediately without interruption. Deliver stuck immediately with durable per-worker three-minute interruption throttling and repeated-report coalescing.
- Resolve the active project orchestrator at each attempt, never auto-spawn one, and recover delivery across daemon and orchestrator replacement.
- Acknowledge only after the target adapter accepts the semantic message. Reuse a durable batch identity so retries are idempotent and reports arriving after a lost response are not silently consumed.
- Piggyback pending reports onto a same-turn human Chat message with one wakeup.
- Expose an independent read-only project report projection for the separate Summary consumer. Summary does not claim or acknowledge delivery.
- Keep outputs independent from state, artifacts opaque, and report claims separate from lifecycle status.

## Runtime boundary

Chat delivery uses the existing semantic Chat send API. Supported TUI adapters wrap each delivery with a durable batch identity and acknowledge only after the native accepted-prompt hook reports that exact identity for the current runtime generation. A raw pane write is never accepted delivery. TUI adapters without that semantic acceptance capability reject submission so reports remain pending. Background consultation remains deferred.

## Verification

- `npm run sqlc`
- `npm run api`
- Focused backend suites for report service, SQLite store, CLI, lifecycle, session manager, HTTP, and daemon
- Focused `go test -race` suites for all changed report delivery boundaries

- Generated artifact drift and `git diff --check`
- Pinned golangci-lint for touched packages

- Frontend-only typecheck reached missing monorepo package dependencies. The package build reached the expected tmux download boundary. No frontend runtime logic changed.

body:

A failed update check can populate both `message` and `checkError` with the same timeout. Updates rendered both the primary error and a second red notice, making one failure appear twice.

## Limits

This fixes the duplicated error shown in the reported screenshot. It does not establish why that user's metadata request exceeded 60 seconds, change network timeout/cancellation policy, or claim to eliminate real network failures. Existing cancellation/queued-retry tests pass, but are not a reproduction of the affected Mac's network conditions.

No fresh native AO interaction was performed: the isolated dev port is occupied by another daemon, which was left untouched. Docker is unavailable locally, so the exact Linux browser-container validation is delegated to CI. This PR is separate from #5002 and does not resolve its current merge conflicts.

title: bug(daemon): workspace projects can never attribute a PR — observer requires /root, ClaimPR ignores WorkspaceRepos
body:
## Bug

A worker session in a `workspace` project can never get a pull request attached to it, by **either** available mechanism:

- the SCM observer cannot match a workspace session's branch shape, and
- `ao session claim-pr` — the documented fallback, and the remediation #4984 relies on — rejects every child-repo PR with `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`.

The PR never appears in the session sidebar and there is no supported way to attach it. `workspace` is a first-class project kind (`domain/project.go:9`, in the storage `CHECK` constraint, backend support closed in #2222), so this is an unhandled kind rather than an unsupported configuration.

**Source:** live report from a worker session that opened two PRs across two child repos of a workspace project
**Date:** 2026-09-07
**Analyzed against:** `4f5c0c899` (`origin/main`)
**Installed:** desktop 0.12.12; daemon binary written 2026-09-06 18:34 UTC; daemon **process** restarted 2026-09-07 10:43 UTC
**Confidence:** High for both root causes (predicates read from source, reproduced against durable SQLite state). Medium for the regression attribution in Root cause 2, which is inferred from behaviour across a dated daemon restart rather than from a recorded version string.

> Org and repository names below are replaced with placeholders (`<org>`, `child-a`, `child-b`) and session ids shortened to `ws-283` / `ws-275`. Happy to share the real identifiers privately — nothing else about the evidence is altered.

## Reproduction

1. Register a workspace project (`kind: workspace`) with child repositories, each with its own GitHub origin. The parent root repo need not have a remote.
2. `ao spawn` a worker. `workspaceProjectBranch` (`adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go:1409`) names the session branch `ao/<id>`, disambiguating collisions as `ao/<id>-2`, `-3`, … — **never** `<namespace>/root`.
3. In a child repo, create a PR branch. The child form the worker prompt instructs (`<session-branch>/<topic>`) is impossible here: `refs/heads/ao/<id>-2` exists as a ref, so Git refuses `refs/heads/ao/<id>-2/<topic>`:
   ```
   fatal: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/ao/ws-283-2/topic':
   'refs/heads/ao/ws-283-2' exists; cannot create ...
   ```
   The only available shape is a hyphen sibling: `ao/<id>-2-<topic>`.
4. Open the PR and wait past the observer's poll interval → never attributed.
5. `ao session claim-pr <pr-url>` → `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH`.
6. Follow the advice in that error, `ao project set-config <id> --canonical-repo-url <https-url>` → rejected with `canonicalRepoURL: project must have a valid checkout origin repository`.

Durable state after step 4, with a single_repo project on the same daemon for contrast:

```text
session    sessions.branch      PR head branch                 attributed?
ws-283     ao/ws-283-2          ao/ws-283-2-body-887           no
emuil-43   ao/emuil-43/root     ao/emuil-43/triple-ready       yes, within seconds
```

## Root cause 1 — the observer can never match a workspace session's branch

`observe/scm/observer.go:1251` widens attribution to sibling branches only for a `/root` leaf:

```go
func sessionBranchPrefixes(branch string) []string {
	prefixes := []string{branch}
	if namespace, ok := strings.CutSuffix(branch, "/root"); ok && namespace != "" {
		prefixes = append(prefixes, namespace)
	}
	return prefixes
}
```

`matchSession` (`:1227`) then accepts only an exact match or `strings.HasPrefix(sourceBranch, prefix+"/")`. For a workspace session:

```text
sessions.branch : ao/ws-283-2
PR head         : ao/ws-283-2-body-887
```

Not equal, and not prefixed by `ao/ws-283-2/` — the next character is `-`. Both arms fail, deterministically, for every PR the session opens.

The comment above `matchSession` states the intent: *"The default worker branch is a leaf named `<namespace>/root`; for that shape the session also owns sibling branches under `<namespace>/...` so Git can create child PR branches without colliding with the root ref."* Workspace projects never get that leaf, so they get neither the namespace widening nor the ability to use the child form that would satisfy the predicate.

**Relationship to #4984.** Same predicate, different and stricter trigger. #4984 describes a session that *leaves* `/root` and loses its **second** PR; the workspace case never has `/root` at all and loses **every** PR including the first. #4984's fix as scoped (sibling attribution for topic branches) would incidentally cover this half. Naming workspace session branches `<namespace>/root` would too.

## Root cause 2 — `ClaimPR` is not workspace-aware

`service/session/claim_pr.go:62`:

```go
if err := requireSameRepo(prURL, project.RepoOriginURL); err != nil {
    if project.Config.CanonicalRepoURL == "" || requireSameRepo(prURL, project.Config.CanonicalRepoURL) != nil {
        return ClaimPRResult{}, err
    }
}
```

and `:389`:

```go
func requireSameRepo(prURL, repoOrigin string) error {
	if strings.TrimSpace(repoOrigin) == "" {
		return ErrProjectMismatch
	}
```

`project.RepoOriginURL` is the parent root's origin. A workspace project's child remotes live in `WorkspaceRepos` — which the observer already reads (`observer.go:843,846`, via `ListWorkspaceRepos`) and `ClaimPR` never does. `claim_pr.go` contains zero references to `ProjectKindWorkspace` or `WorkspaceRepos`, though it does explicitly special-case another kind at `:86`:

```go
if project.Kind.WithDefault() == domain.ProjectKindScratch {
    return ClaimPRResult{}, ErrSessionNotClaimable
}
```

**This is not limited to a remote-less root.** `requireSameRepo` compares the PR's owner/repo against the root origin, so a workspace rooted at `<org>/parent` still rejects a PR on `<org>/child-a` — different repository. No workspace project can claim a child-repo PR under any configuration. An empty root origin merely fails one line earlier.

**The prescribed escape is a closed loop.** The error tells the user to set `canonicalRepoURL`; `domain/repository_identity.go:83` then refuses one:

```go
checkout, err := ParseRepositoryIdentity(origin)
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("canonicalRepoURL: project must have a valid checkout origin repository")
}
```

— requiring exactly the valid single origin a workspace project does not have. It is also a single URL where a workspace has N children, so it could bless at most one repo even if accepted.

**Regression window.** `requireSameRepo` landed in `d06b2162d` (2026-09-05 12:47 UTC, #4929). The same project, with the same hyphen-sibling branch shape, was attaching PRs the day before:

```text
2026-09-06 18:34 UTC   new daemon binary written to disk
2026-09-06 22:10 UTC   ws-275 attaches child-a PR   (old daemon process still running)
2026-09-07 09:17 UTC   ws-275 attaches child-a PR   (old daemon process still running)
2026-09-07 10:43 UTC   daemon process restarted onto the new binary
2026-09-07 17:12 UTC   ws-283 opens two PRs -> neither attaches, both claims refused
```

Those earlier attachments cannot have come from the observer: the `/root` narrowing is `9ae9f0888` (2026-06-18), long predating them, and `ao/ws-275-warn-on-host` against `sessions.branch = ao/ws-275` fails `matchSession` identically. They were claims. The restart is what removed the fallback that had been quietly carrying this project kind — which is why the breakage looks sudden despite Root cause 1 being three months old.

## Existing coverage gap

`ClaimPR` has a dedicated test for the one kind it does handle — `TestClaimPRRejectsScratchProject` (`service/session/service_test.go:3754`) — and no workspace equivalent. The three `ProjectKindWorkspace` fixtures in that file (`:1849`, `:1928`, `:1983`) are spawn/branch-resolution tests, all well above the `ClaimPR` block. `claim_upstream_test.go` covers the fork-backed single_repo case only.

A regression test asserting that a workspace project can claim a PR on any repo in `ListWorkspaceRepos` would have caught Root cause 2 when `d06b2162d` landed.

## Suggested fix

1. **`ClaimPR`:** for `ProjectKindWorkspace`, validate the PR repo against `ListWorkspaceRepos` (match any child origin) in addition to `RepoOriginURL`, mirroring `workspaceSCMSessionRepos`.
2. **Branch shape:** either have `workspaceProjectBranch` produce `<namespace>/root` (matching `single_repo`), or widen `sessionBranchPrefixes` past the `/root` special case — see #4984.
3. **Error text:** `PR_PROJECT_MISMATCH` should not direct users to `--canonical-repo-url` for a project kind whose validator rejects it. Either accept it for workspace projects or say why it does not apply.

Items 1 and 2 are independent; either alone leaves the kind half-broken.

Workspace cleanup can delete a worktree still used by a live session (data loss)
body:
## Problem

`Manager.Cleanup` reclaims the workspaces of terminated sessions. It only checks whether the **session** is terminated. It never checks whether the **workspace path** is still used by another, live session.

When two sessions share one persistent worktree, terminating one of them can destroy the workspace out from under the other. Files and uncommitted work in that worktree are lost.

## Where

- `cleanupOne` passes a workspace to `workspace.Destroy` based on `rec.IsTerminated` alone.
- `ErrWorkspaceDirty` only guards uncommitted changes. It does not protect a worktree that another live session is actively using.

## Repro shape

1. Point two sessions at the same persistent worktree.
2. Terminate one session.
3. Cleanup reaps the shared workspace while the second session is still running.

## Status

Diagnosed by @polymath-orchestrator in PR #2487 (now closed as stale after 62 days of silence, branch remains open to reopen). The guard this PR adds is still missing on main, so the bug is live.

Maintainers: the fix in #2487 is small and is the only known patch for this. Worth picking up or re-triaging.

Credit to @polymath-orchestrator for the diagnosis.

title: bug(project import): reported existing repository incorrectly shown as needing git init
body:
## Report: existing repository shown as “Needs git init”

During a real-project desktop test on 2026-09-08, AO's **Import an existing project** flow (single Git repository mode) displayed `Needs git init` for an existing local repository. A read-only `git -C <selected-folder> rev-parse --verify HEAD` succeeded for the same folder.

## Environment

Native Electron development app associated with [PR #4830](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4830), macOS, isolated daemon/data on port 3002, real project folder. Checkout HEAD `8e808a00cf001a9ddfb20c687426e738a261fbbb` with pre-existing uncommitted changes; not verified against a released build.

## Steps observed

1. Choose **Import an existing project** from the home page.
2. Select a real existing repository through the native folder picker.
3. The dialog explicitly says `Import a single Git repository as one project` and displays the selected folder with `Needs git init`.
4. Verify `.git` exists and `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` succeeds. The notice remained on a subsequent observation.

The user did not proceed with Git initialization; no source-project files were changed.

## Expected

Recognize the existing repository. If another prerequisite is missing (such as origin/default-branch configuration), report that prerequisite instead of suggesting Git initialization. While detection is pending, show a pending state rather than a definitive missing-Git diagnosis.

## Confidence and limits

Medium confidence in the displayed mismatch; low confidence in its cause. Later computer-control accessibility state and screenshots diverged, so this needs confirmation with a fresh pinned build and captured directory-probe response before changing repository detection. Do not treat the later dialog-control problems as separately confirmed AO bugs.

Inspect single-project probe results, loading/error handling and the mapping to `Needs git init` in `CreateProjectFlow.tsx`.

Related but not an exact duplicate: [#4959](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4959) concerns selecting **workspace** mode for a single-repository folder. This observation was explicitly in **single-project** mode. [#4679](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4679) covers remote-less repositories; a missing remote has not been established as this report's cause.

Priority: medium. No fix or reliable cross-project reproduction is claimed yet.

title: bug(codex): Windows ancestor ACL validation rejects valid Codex home
body:
## Bug

On Windows, Codex account bootstrap can fail before any Codex process is launched because the private-directory admission check rejects an otherwise usable Codex home ancestor.

The observed path is:

-  ootstrapInner calls cleanupPendingCredentialHomes before econcileGlobal.
- cleanupPendingCredentialHomes calls ^[nsurePrivateDirectory.
- ^[nsurePrivateDirectory calls alidateCodexDirectoryAncestors before creating or launching the account app-server.
- The validator can reject the volume root (C:\\) based on its owner/ACL checks, producing ^Gccount_storage_unsafe and the public CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE error.

This is a distinct pre-launch failure mode from account app-server environment handoff issues.

## Impact

Users receive the generic account-management error even though Codex itself is installed and authenticated. No Codex process starts, so PATH propagation fixes cannot affect this path.

## Relationship

This is related to #4989 but should be tracked separately because #4989 may include multiple Windows failure modes. Independent reproduction and trace: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4989#issuecomment-5576910008

## Expected

Valid Windows installations should not be rejected solely because an ancestor such as C:\\ has system-managed ownership or non-inherit-only ACL entries. If the directory cannot be safely accepted, the returned diagnostic should expose the specific ancestor and reason.

title: bug(board): idle session card spins a loader next to a green "Mergeable" label
body:
## Bug

A worker session card on the Kanban board renders an animated loader ring next to its status label even though the agent is idle and the label itself reads a settled **Mergeable**. The card sits in the **Ready** lane, so nothing about it is in progress, yet the ring spins continuously at one revolution per second for as long as the card is mounted.

The reporter read the spinner as "this session is Working", which is exactly what it looks like.

**Reported by:** the maintainer, in the AO desktop app (first reported 2026-09-06, still reproducing 2026-09-08)
**Analyzed against:** `ddf1e54f18f9e27dacbfa0d1d90ce37a1c37228e` (origin/main)
**Environment:** AO desktop app, bundled daemon `ao version` = `dev`, daemon healthy on `127.0.0.1:3001` (`readyz: ready`); macOS 14.6 (23G80) arm64
**Confidence:** High — exact lines traced, mechanism explained, reproduced by a deterministic unit test (below)
**Priority:** medium — the board's primary status signal is misleading; workaround is to open the session and read the topbar activity pill

### Screenshots

First report (2026-09-06):

![board card 2026-09-06](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-board-mergeable-spinner/.issue-assets/board-mergeable-spinner/card-2026-09-06.png)

Still present (2026-09-08), same session, still idle:

![board card 2026-09-08](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-board-mergeable-spinner/.issue-assets/board-mergeable-spinner/card-2026-09-08.png)

## Reproduction

Deterministic unit reproduction (no live session needed) — add to `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx`:

```ts
boardSession({
  id: "s-mergeable",
  title: "mergeable-card-task",
  status: "review_pending",
  displayStatus: "Mergeable",
  kanbanColumn: "ready",
  activity: { state: "idle", lastActivityAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" },
})
// expect(within(card).getByTestId("session-status").querySelector(".animate-spin")).toBeNull();
```

Fails on `ddf1e54f`:

```
AssertionError: expected SVGSVGElement{ …(2), …(2) } to be null
+ Received:
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-loader-circle mr-1 size-icon-2xs animate-spin" ...>
  <path d="M21 12a9 9 0 1 1-6.219-8.56" />
</svg>
```

Live reproduction, for reference — a session with several open PRs where at least one is not yet mergeable:

1. Session `analyze Coder PR` has PRs #4624 (`review_required`, `conflicting`), #4787 and #4796 (both `mergeable`), #4434 (merged).
2. `GET /api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-211` returns `activity.state: idle`, `status: review_pending`, `scmStatus: review_pending`, `kanbanColumn: ready`, `displayStatus: Mergeable`.
3. The board card shows the Ready lane, a green `Mergeable` label, and a spinning ring.

## Root Cause

`packages/product-ui/src/SessionsBoardView.tsx:245-251`:

```ts
const showStatusLoader =
    !needsAttention &&
    session.displayStatus !== "Needs human review" &&
    (session.status === "working" ||
        session.status === "review_pending" ||
        session.displayStatus === "Fixing CI failures" ||
        session.displayStatus === "Addressing comments" ||
        session.displayStatus === "Reviewing");
```

rendered at `SessionsBoardView.tsx:337`:

```tsx
{showStatusLoader ? <LoaderCircleIcon aria-hidden="true" className="mr-1 size-icon-2xs animate-spin" /> : null}
```

Two independent problems meet here:

1. **The loader and the label read different daemon fields.** The label comes from `displayStatus` (`SessionsBoardView.tsx:242`), which the daemon derives from the session's **best** PR — `DeriveKanbanPresentation` picks the highest-ranked column, `ready` first (`backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go:254-266`, `kanbanPriority` at `:167-178`). The loader comes from `status`, which the daemon derives from the session's **worst** open PR (`backend/pkg/contract/status.go:192-215` plus the severity table at `:226-244`). For the session above, #4624 is `review_required` + `conflicting` and yields `review_pending` (severity 3), beating the two mergeable PRs (severity 6). So one card renders the best PR as text and the worst PR as an icon.

2. **The loader never consults agent activity.** `showStatusLoader` has no `session.activity` term at all, so an idle agent cannot switch it off. The card reads activity in only two places, neither reachable here: `boardSessionNeedsAttention` (`:360-373`, which only looks at `activity.state === "blocked"` when `displayStatus` is undefined) and `statusPresentation` (agent-switch, absent). The animation itself is unconditional CSS — `.animate-spin{animation:var(--animate-spin)}` with `--animate-spin: spin 1s linear infinite` — so it has no terminating state.

`review_pending` is also the odd member of that predicate's set. Every other member describes something actively turning (`working` = the agent is running a turn; `Fixing CI failures` / `Addressing comments` / `Reviewing` = AO-driven loops). `review_pending` is a *waiting* state: the app's own taxonomy maps it to the `pending` attention zone, not `working` (`packages/product-ui/src/session-presentation.ts`, `attentionZone`), its own label reads "Review pending", and at the daemon it comes from `prPipelineStatus`'s `case pr.Review == ReviewRequired` (`backend/pkg/contract/status.go:257`) — GitHub reporting that a required human review has not happened.

Introduced in `8162e8da3` (2026-08-26, "feat(board): add active status loaders"), keyed on `session.status` from the start. The only existing test for the loader (`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx:501-523`) exercises `status: "working"` with `activity: active` — the genuinely busy case — so the `review_pending` arm shipped untested.

## Fix

Make the loader agree with the label the card actually renders, without touching the multi-PR aggregation in the daemon (that aggregation is deliberate and out of scope here):

- Spin when the agent is genuinely working (`status === "working"`).
- Otherwise spin only when the **rendered `displayStatus`** is itself an in-progress phrase — `Review pending`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Addressing comments`, `Reviewing`.
- Fall back to the old `status === "review_pending"` check only when the daemon sent no `displayStatus` (older daemon against a newer client).

This keeps `Review pending` cards spinning and stops `Mergeable`, `Approved` and `Merged` cards from spinning, which is exactly the behaviour requested in #4725.

## Impact

- Every multi-PR session whose PRs disagree shows a permanent spinner on a settled card.
- The board's most prominent liveness cue is decoupled from agent activity, so users cannot tell from the board whether an agent is running.
- Cosmetic only — no data loss, no incorrect merges.

## Related

- [#4725](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4725) — open design task that already specifies "Mergable should not show a loader / Review pending should show loader / Go over where we show loader". This issue is the concrete bug and evidence behind the first two bullets.
- [#2944](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2944) — closed: sidebar dot + kanban badge locked to PR status, agent working/idle invisible once a PR exists. Same family (PR state masking agent state) on different surfaces, not a duplicate.
- [#2345](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2345) — closed: topbar pill showed a breathing "Working" for `pr_open`/`draft`. Same class of defect on the topbar; this one is the board loader.

title: fix(board): stop spinning a loader on settled session cards
body:
Fixes #5081

## Summary

A board card read its status **label** from `displayStatus` but its **loader** from `status`. The daemon derives those two from opposite ends of a session's PR set — `displayStatus` from the session's best PR (`contract/kanban.go`, `kanbanPriority`, `ready` first), `status` from its worst open PR (`contract/status.go`, `aggregatePRStatus` + severity table). A session with one mergeable PR and one still awaiting review therefore rendered a green **Mergeable** label next to a loader that spun forever. The predicate contained no `session.activity` term, so an idle agent could not switch it off, and `animate-spin` is `spin 1s linear infinite` with no terminating state.

The fix keys the loader off the label the card actually renders:

- keep the loader while the agent is genuinely working (`status === "working"`);
- otherwise show it only when the rendered `displayStatus` is itself an in-progress phrase — `Review pending`, `Fixing CI failures`, `Addressing comments`, `Reviewing`;
- fall back to the old `status === "review_pending"` check only when the daemon sent no `displayStatus`, so an older daemon against a newer client is unaffected.

`Review pending` keeps its loader and `Mergeable` loses it, which is exactly what #4725 specifies ("Mergable should not show a loader / Review pending should show loader").

**The daemon's multi-PR aggregation is deliberate and is unchanged** — this is a presentation-only fix in `packages/product-ui`.

## Test

Three new cases in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.test.tsx`, covering both directions:

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| idle agent, `status: review_pending`, `displayStatus: "Mergeable"`, `ready` lane | **no** loader (the reported bug) |
| idle agent, `status: review_pending`, `displayStatus: "Review pending"` | loader present (#4725 intent) |
| active agent, `status: working`, `displayStatus: "Mergeable"` | loader present (truly-active still covered) |

The first case fails on `ddf1e54f` with `expected SVGSVGElement … to be null` (the `lucide-loader-circle animate-spin` node) and passes here. The pre-existing `status: "working"` + `activity: active` test is untouched and still passes.

Verification run locally on node 24 (matching `.github/workflows/frontend.yml`):

```
npm --prefix packages/product-ui run typecheck   # clean
npm --prefix packages/product-ui test            # 10 files, 124 tests passed
npm --prefix packages/product-ui run build       # built
npm --prefix frontend run typecheck              # clean
cd frontend && npx vitest run src/renderer       # 197 files, 2828 passed, 6 skipped
```

### Environment limitation, proven not a regression

The full `frontend` suite in this checkout also reports 17 failures across 8 files — all under `src/landing/**` and `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`. None of them import the board or `product-ui`. Two independent checks confirm they are pre-existing environment gaps, not regressions from this change:

1. **Baseline on pristine `origin/main`.** Reverting this PR's two files and re-running *only those 8 files* reproduces the identical 8 files / 17 tests failing. Failure mode is `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and missing native deps.
2. **CI is green on this PR.** The `test` job runs the same full `npx vitest run`, but only after `npm ci --prefix src/landing` and `npm run browser-runtime:prepare` — two setup steps this local checkout never performed. It passed in 5m29s, alongside `renderer-smoke` (2m50s) and `scan` (17s).

So the local failures are missing landing sub-app and browser-runtime dependencies here, and no unrelated code was touched to make anything pass.

title: feat(browser): explicit `ao preview` / `ao browser open` should reveal the Browser panel for the session you are viewing
body:
## Summary

An explicit `ao preview <target>` or `ao browser open <url>` from the session the user is currently viewing succeeds, but the Browser panel is **not** revealed — the inspector only badges the Browser tab as unseen. The user has to notice the badge and click the tab to see the thing they just asked for.

This is **current, intentional behavior**, not an accidental regression. [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) ("non-disruptive preview reveal") deliberately replaced the force-reveal with a badge, and `CLAUDE.md` documents it. This issue asks to narrow that rule, not to revert it.

**Reported by:** @itrytoohard (maintainer), relayed via an AO worker session
**Analyzed against:** `ddf1e54f1`
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced below.

## Current behavior

`frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`

- The preview-target effect (around `SessionView.tsx:1330`) fires when `previewUrl`/`previewRevision` changes. If the Browser panel is already visible it clears the badge; otherwise it calls `setBrowserUnseen(sessionId, true)` and returns. The `setInspectorViewForSession(sessionId, "browser")` + `setInspectorOpenForSession(sessionId, true)` pair was removed by [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) (commit `30a7c20f6`).
- The agent-activity effect (around `SessionView.tsx:1369`) badges on *any* `browserView.agentBrowserActive`, so `ao browser open` is treated identically to a passive `snapshot`, `click`, or `errors` call — badge only, never reveal.

Net effect: the two commands whose entire purpose is "show me this page" are the ones that don't show it.

## Why [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) was right, and what it over-corrected

[PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146)'s rationale — quoted from its own code comment — is that a new preview target used to "force-switch the inspector to the Browser tab and pop it open, even if the user was looking at something else entirely (Reviews, a different session's Files tab, mid-typing in chat)."

The genuinely disruptive case there is a **background** session grabbing the foreground. That is worth preventing and must stay prevented. But the fix was applied to *all* preview targets, including one the user is staring at right now, having just asked for it. Since `SessionView` is mounted only for the routed session (`routes/_shell.projects.$projectId_.sessions.$sessionId.tsx`), "the session whose `SessionView` is mounted" is already exactly "the session the user is viewing" — the disruptive cross-session case and the wanted same-session case are separable with information the renderer already has.

## Requested behavior

| Trigger | Session being viewed | Other session |
|---|---|---|
| `ao preview <target>` (new preview target) | **Reveal** Browser panel | Badge only (unchanged) |
| `ao browser open <url>`, `ao browser tab new` | **Reveal** Browser panel | Badge only (unchanged) |
| `ao browser snapshot` / `click` / `fill` / `act` / `errors` / … | Badge only (unchanged) | Badge only (unchanged) |
| No browser content / terminated session | No badge (unchanged) | No badge (unchanged) |

Revealing means: open the inspector and switch it to the Browser tab for that session. It does **not** mean raising the OS window, changing the routed session, or changing projects — a background worker must never pull the user's navigation to itself.

## Intent contract — already present, no API change needed

The renderer can already tell explicit-open from passive inspection:

- `BrowserAgentActivityState` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:110`) already carries `action` and `phase`, pushed on `browser:agentActivity` and surfaced by `useBrowserView` as `agentBrowserActivity`.
- The action strings come straight from the CLI: `ao browser open` sends `"open"` (`backend/internal/cli/browser.go:91`) and `ao browser tab new` sends `"tab-new"`; every passive command sends its own distinct verb.
- `previewRevision` only changes when someone runs `ao preview`, so a preview-key change is inherently explicit.

So this needs no daemon route, no OpenAPI change, and no contract regeneration — it is a renderer-side policy change over signals the main process already emits.

## Acceptance criteria

1. From the session on screen, `ao preview README.md` opens the inspector on the Browser tab showing the rendered file, with no unseen badge left behind.
2. From the session on screen, `ao browser open http://localhost:5173` does the same.
3. A `ao preview` / `ao browser open` in a **different** session badges that session and does not change what the user is looking at.
4. `ao browser snapshot` / `click` / `fill` / `errors` on the viewed session while the Browser tab is hidden still only badges — no reveal.
5. Revealing never steals OS window focus and never changes the routed session or project.
6. A terminated session's stale `previewUrl` still reveals nothing (existing `hasBrowserContent` guard).

## Reproduction

1. Open a session in the desktop app and park the inspector on Summary (or Reviews).
2. From that session's worker shell, run `ao preview README.md`.
3. Observed: the command reports success; the Browser tab shows an unseen dot; the panel stays on Summary.
4. Expected: the inspector opens on Browser with the rendered README.
5. Repeat with `ao browser open http://localhost:5173` — same observed result.

## Related

- [PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) — introduced the current badge-only behavior (the behavior this issue narrows).
- [PR #3359](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3359) — the earlier "open first browser content automatically and badge background activity" split this builds on.
- [#2809](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2809) — agents opening the OS browser instead of the AO in-app preview; same "the preview must actually be seen" goal.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` currently instructs agents that `ao preview` "does not steal focus or force the Browser tab open" and to tell the user to check the Browser tab. That guidance needs updating alongside the behavior change.

title: fix: serialize mobile bridge state transitions
body:
## What

Serialize Connect Mobile state changes and synchronize the status error snapshot.

## Why

Share post-start connector setup and restore the previous authentication hash if boot startup fails. Active LAN connection shutdown is a separate follow-up.

title: feat(browser): reveal the Browser panel for explicit preview/open commands
body:
Fixes #5083

## Summary

`ao preview` and `ao browser open` succeeded but only badged the Browser tab as unseen, so the two commands whose entire purpose is "show the user this page" were the ones that didn't show it — the user had to notice a dot and click the tab.

[PR #4146](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4146) made every preview badge-only, deliberately, to stop a preview grabbing the foreground while the user was looking at something else. **This narrows that rule rather than reverting it.** The disruptive case #4146 was protecting against is a *background* session pulling focus; that protection now comes from `SessionView` being mounted only for the routed session, not from refusing to reveal at all.

- A new `ao preview` target reveals Browser for the session on screen.
- `ao browser open` / `ao browser tab new` reveal too — they are the agent-side equivalents of the same explicit request.
- Every passive agent verb (`snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `act`, `errors`, …) keeps badge-only treatment, as does any preview/open in another session.
- Revealing opens the inspector on Browser and nothing else: no OS window focus, no change to the routed session or project.

The reveal is deduped on `commandId` so a command's `finished` push cannot reopen a panel the user closed mid-command.

## Intent contract — no API change

Explicit-vs-passive was already distinguishable from the existing API, so nothing crosses the daemon boundary and no contracts were regenerated:

- `BrowserAgentActivityState` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`) already ships `action` + `commandId` on `browser:agentActivity`, surfaced by `useBrowserView` as `agentBrowserActivity`.
- The action strings come straight from the CLI — `ao browser open` sends `"open"` (`backend/internal/cli/browser.go:91`), `ao browser tab new` sends `"tab-new"`, every passive command sends its own verb.
- `previewRevision` only changes when someone runs `ao preview`, so a preview-key change is inherently explicit.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `vitest run SessionView.test.tsx BrowserPanel.test.tsx useBrowserView.test.tsx SessionInspector.test.tsx` — 346/346 passing. Three tests that asserted the old badge-only preview behavior were rewritten for the new rule; the `ao preview clear` test keeps its real subject (clearing neither reveals nor badges) with updated surrounding assertions. New coverage: reveal on `open`/`tab-new`, badge-only on `snapshot`/`click`/`fill`/`errors`, no re-reveal on the `finished` push, no reveal on a terminated session.
- [x] **Verified in the real Electron app** (isolated dev profile, driven over CDP; native `WebContentsView` target URLs read as ground truth):
  - Parked on Summary → `ao preview <url>` → Browser tab becomes selected.
  - Parked on Summary → `ao browser open http://127.0.0.1:3007/healthz` → Browser tab selected **and** the native view's target URL is that URL.
  - Parked on Summary → `ao browser snapshot` → stays on Summary, Browser shows the unseen badge.
  - Viewing session B, ran `ao browser open` **and** `ao preview` against background session A → route and tab both unchanged.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md`'s agent guidance said `ao preview` "does not steal focus or force the Browser tab open"; updated to describe the explicit-vs-passive split.

## Known limitations

- Reveal is scoped to the routed session because only that `SessionView` is mounted. If a future change keeps multiple `SessionView`s alive at once, the cross-session guard would need to become an explicit check rather than an emergent property — called out in the comment at the preview effect.
- Unrelated pre-existing behavior seen while testing: on an exited fake-harness session the daemon clears `previewUrl` shortly after `ao preview` sets it (bumping `previewRevision` with an empty URL). That is upstream of this change and left alone.

title: fix: close active LAN connections when mobile access stops
body:
## What

Disabling Connect Mobile now closes active LAN streams and WebSockets before reporting the listener stopped.

## Why

A shutdown timeout could leave HTTP clients connected, and Go's HTTP shutdown does not close hijacked WebSockets. Disable also returned early on a shutdown error without saving the disabled preference, so a stopped bridge could return on the next daemon boot.

## How

Give each listener its own cancellation context and connection registry. Serialize Start/Stop, force-close remaining connections after the grace period, and retain shutdown errors while completing disabled-state persistence. The connection wrapper preserves TCP half-close and efficient response copying.

This is independent of #5084's controller transition locking; their combined HTTP race tests pass. LAN authentication and route boundaries are unchanged.

title: fix(scm/github): stop reporting a job that never started as a CI failure
body:
## What

Classifies a GitHub Actions job that never started as `unknown` rather than a failed check.

Addresses **item 3 of #4850**. Deliberately not `Fixes` — that issue tracks three separate defects and the other two are untouched here.

## Why

When a repository hits its Actions spending limit, GitHub reports every job as `conclusion: FAILURE` with no steps recorded, an empty runner and no log to fetch. AO's rollup read that as a red check, moved the owning worker to `ci_failed`, and nudged the agent to go fix a test that never executed.

The reporter measured a refused job retried eight times in about forty minutes, every attempt the identical billing refusal, every one producing a fresh `ci_failed` wake-up until the PR was closed to break the loop.

## How

`steps(first:1){ totalCount }` joins the CheckRun selection so the two cases can be told apart, and a `FAILURE` with a **present-and-zero** step count is classified `unknown`.

Three limits on the rule, each with a test:

- **Only `FAILURE`.** `STARTUP_FAILURE`, `TIMED_OUT` and `ACTION_REQUIRED` still fail with zero steps — an invalid workflow file records no steps and is a real defect the user must see.
- **Present-and-zero only.** A missing `steps` block means the caller did not request it, not that the job did nothing; treating absent as zero would decay every real failure to unknown.
- Unparseable counts fall through to the previous behaviour.

`unknown` is the existing vocabulary for "undetermined", so this needs no new domain status, DTO field or API surface. `ciSummaryFromGraphQL` already treats unknown as neither failing nor passing, so a never-started job stops producing `CIFailing`.

One thing worth a maintainer's eye: `runner_name` is REST-only and not exposed on the GraphQL `CheckRun` type, so the step count is the signal available on this code path. I confirmed against the live schema that `CheckRun.steps` exists and `CheckStepConnection` has `totalCount`.

## Testing

`TestCheckStatusNeverStartedJobIsNotAFailure` and `TestCISummaryNeverStartedJobIsNotFailing` fail without the change:

```
provider_neverstarted_test.go:29: status = "failed", want "unknown"; a job that never started is not a failing test
provider_neverstarted_test.go:70: ci summary = "failing", want anything but CIFailing for a never-started job
```

`TestCheckStatusRealFailuresStillFail` covers the six cases that must keep failing. Package tests pass.

title: fix(lifecycle): do not re-nudge the agent when a failed check is merely re-run
body:
## What

Stops the agent being nudged again when a failing check is merely re-run.

Addresses **item 3 of #4850**, the amplification half. Companion to #5088, which fixes the classification. Deliberately not `Fixes` — #4850 tracks three defects and the other two are untouched.

## Why

`ciFailureSignature` included the check's URL. GitHub mints a new check-run URL for **every attempt**, so re-running an unchanged failing check produced a different signature, the dedupe in `sendOnce` missed, and the agent was nudged again.

During the spending-limit outage in #4850 a refused job was retried eight times in about forty minutes. Every attempt was the identical billing refusal, and every one produced a fresh `ci_failed` wake-up until the PR was closed to break the loop.

Nothing caps this. CI nudges are queued with `maxAttempts: 0`, and `sendOnce` reads `0` as unlimited:

```go
if maxAttempts > 0 && attempts >= maxAttempts {
```

so the signature is the only thing between a retried check and an unbounded stream of injections. (The review-comment path caps at `reviewMaxNudge`; CI has no equivalent. I have not added one here — that is a policy change and belongs in its own PR if you want it.)

## How

The URL is dropped from the signature. Name, commit, status and log tail identify the *failure*, which is what must not repeat.

## Worth stating for review

**AO does not re-run checks.** There is no rerun or rerequest call anywhere in the tree, so this does not stop the retries — it stops AO reacting to each one as though it were new. The issue notes the reporter had not pinned down which component re-ran the job; as far as AO's source goes, it wasn't AO.

## Testing

`TestCIFailureSignatureIgnoresPerAttemptURL` fails without the change:

```
reactions_ci_rerun_test.go:24: signature changed across a re-run of the same failure; the agent would be nudged again
```

`TestCIFailureSignatureStillSeparatesRealChanges` pins that a new commit, a changed log, a different check name and an additional failing check each still produce a distinct signature — the dedupe must not swallow real news. Package tests pass.

title: feat(usage): global usage summary API + usage statistics page
body:
## What to build

First vertical slice of the usage statistics dashboard. Add a global (cross-session) usage summary to the daemon and a minimal "Usage Statistics" page in the desktop app that displays it.

Daemon: a summary endpoint that aggregates the existing V1 usage pipeline data (per-model usage events with token metrics and durable nano-USD costs) over an optional time range, returning:

- total tokens consumed (input incl. cached + output), broken into the four display components: uncached ("new") input, cached input ("cache hit"), cache creation (Anthropic), output
- total estimated cost (durable cost totals)
- total request count — semantics: count of usage events for now (token-event granularity); true request-level semantics arrive with the timing pipeline slices
- cache hit rate = cached input / (cached + uncached input)

Frontend: a new "Usage Statistics" route/page showing the summary card (large total-token number, total requests, total cost), the four component cards, and a cache-hit-rate progress bar. Time range defaults to today with simple presets (today / 7d / 30d); source/model filters land in a follow-up slice.

No derived or display state is persisted: all numbers are computed at read time from the usage tables.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Summary endpoint returns totals (token components, cost, event count, cache hit rate) for an optional from/to range; DTOs added to the OpenAPI spec and frontend schema regenerated via `npm run api`, both committed with the Go changes
- [ ] New aggregate queries follow the sqlc flow (new migration/queries only; no edits to already-merged migrations, no hand-editing gen/)
- [ ] "Usage Statistics" page renders the summary card, four component cards, and cache-hit-rate bar from live daemon data (TanStack Query, invalidating via the existing SSE CDC usage invalidation)

- [ ] Tests cover: happy-path aggregation over seeded usage rows, empty range, and controller response shape / CLI-HTTP wire compatibility

title: RFC(usage): request-level timing metrics design for chat and TUI sessions (ADR)
body:
## What to build

Design decision (ADR) for request-level timing metrics across BOTH chat and TUI sessions: per-request/turn first-token latency, LLM elapsed time, tool-call elapsed time, output tok/s, and per-session aggregates (rounds, steps).

Today the usage pipeline certifies token/cost facts only; no timing data is captured anywhere. Chat conversations already persist turn timestamps (requested/started/completed) and tool activities, so chat-mode timing is largely read-model work. TUI/native sessions have no timing facts — the ADR must decide how to derive them (transcript event timestamps vs hook ingress vs both) or scope that explicitly.

The ADR must decide:

1. Data sources per mode: chat turns/activities read-model vs native-transcript derivation for TUI (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi at minimum), consistent with the usage pipeline's "certified usage sources" contract.
2. Storage shape: new timing table(s) vs extending usage events; how rounds/steps are defined; session-level aggregates must be derived at read time unless there is a durable-fact reason to store them (repo rule: no derived/display status persisted).
3. tok/s and first-token definitions (per request; session average) and how unknowns are represented (nil, never zero — match existing usage semantics).
4. Backfill policy: re-scan historical transcripts, or timing starts at deployment.
5. Retention, and interaction with change_log/CDC triggers.

This is a HITL slice: the decision needs a human architecture review before the implementation slices proceed.

Deliverable: an ADR under `docs/adr/` (next number) with the decision and a storage sketch. The "ingest timing metrics", "request log duration columns", and "session runtime stats bar" slices are blocked on this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR merged under docs/adr/ covering all five decisions above
- [ ] Storage sketch reviewed against the durable-facts / derived-status rule
- [ ] Follow-up slices re-scoped (if needed) and unblocked per the decision

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: fix(codex): make Windows Codex account storage usable
body:
Fixes #5080. Very likely related to #4989, though that is not independently confirmed by this change.

## Problem

On stock Windows, Codex account management is unconditionally unavailable. `ensure`
returns:

```
{"error":"unavailable","code":"CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
 "message":"Codex account setup did not complete",
 "details":{"reasonCode":"account_storage_unsafe","retryable":false}}
```

This fires on the very first line of `bootstrapInner` —
`cleanupPendingCredentialHomes` → `ensurePrivateDirectory` →
`validateCodexDirectoryAncestors` — before the Codex binary is ever launched. That also
explains why `~/.ao/data/harnesses/` never gets created on affected machines.

### Bug 1 — the ancestor walk rejects the Windows system drive root

`validateCodexDirectoryAncestors` (`codex_secure_fs_windows.go`) walks from
`%USERPROFILE%\.ao\data\harnesses\codex\pending` up to `C:\` and requires every existing
ancestor to have a trusted owner and no untrusted allow-ACE carrying any bit in
`codexWindowsMutationMask`. Stock Windows `C:\` fails both checks:

| check | stock Windows value | AO's rule |
|---|---|---|
| owner | `NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller` | trusted = {current user, LocalSystem, BUILTIN\Administrators} → false |
| DACL | `NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(AD)`, mask `0x00000004` = `FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY` | mask includes `codexWindowsAppendData` → unsafe |

Both of these are Windows defaults (`(Get-Acl C:\).Owner` is `NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller`
on every stock install), so **this reproduces on every stock Windows machine** — not just
misconfigured ones. That matches reports that Codex account management worked prior to
v0.12.11, before this ancestor check was added.

### Bug 2 — POSIX mode-bit check on a managed credential home

Separately, `AccountFactory.Open` gated managed homes on `info.Mode().Perm() != 0o700`.
Windows has no POSIX mode bits: a directory created with `os.Mkdir(path, 0o700)` comes
back from `Lstat` as `0777`, so this comparison can never succeed on Windows. Every
`Managed: true` open therefore failed: opaque-global-credential verification, device
account import, login verification, and switch verification. Bug 1 masks bug 2 today —
but with only bug 1 fixed, account count would still read 0 and adding an account would
still fail.

## Fix

* **`backend/internal/service/agent/codex_windows_security.go`** (new) —
  `codexWindowsAncestorMutationMask`, the vault mask minus `FILE_ADD_FILE` and
  `FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY`, used by a new `codexWindowsAncestorACLIsSafe`. Creating a new
  entry beside the vault chain cannot rename, delete, or redirect an ancestor that
  already exists, so `DELETE`, `FILE_DELETE_CHILD`, `WRITE_DAC`, `WRITE_OWNER`,
  `GENERIC_ALL`, and `GENERIC_WRITE` still disqualify an ancestor. The vault's own mask
  (used for the leaf directory that actually holds credentials) is unchanged.
* **`backend/internal/service/agent/codex_secure_fs_windows.go`** — `NT
  SERVICE\TrustedInstaller` (`S-1-5-80-956008885-…`) added to the trusted-owner and
  trusted-principal sets. It's a service SID that no interactive account can assume
  without already holding SYSTEM, so it's at least as trustworthy as
  `BUILTIN\Administrators` — and it's the unavoidable owner of `C:\` on every stock
  Windows install.
* **`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/account.go`** plus new
  `account_home_unix.go` / `account_home_windows.go` — the `Perm() != 0o700` gate becomes
  a platform-specific `managedHomePrivate(path, info)`. Unix keeps the existing 0700
  comparison. Windows instead verifies what AO actually applies when it creates a managed
  home: the current user owns it, its DACL is protected from inheritance, and no
  untrusted principal holds an effective allow ACE.
* **Regression tests** — `codex_windows_security_test.go`
  (`TestWindowsAncestorACLPolicyAcceptsDefaultSystemDriveRoot`: add-child rights are now
  accepted for ancestors, real mutation rights are still rejected for ancestors, and the
  vault's own (stricter) mask is unchanged) and `account_home_windows_test.go` (asserts
  Windows really reports `0777` on a directory created with `0700`, that a directory with
  an inherited DACL is still rejected, and that an owner-only protected DACL is accepted
  — so the new check isn't a no-op).

## Verification

A/B tested with two separately built binaries (unmodified `v0.12.12` control vs. this
branch), same Go toolchain/flags as `packages/build-binaries.sh`'s `win32-x64` target,
run against an identical sandboxed environment (isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, own
`AO_DATA_DIR`/port, a copy of a real Codex credential):

**Unmodified v0.12.12 (control):**

```
ensure -> CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE, reasonCode=account_storage_unsafe, retryable=false
ao spawn --harness codex ... -> Codex account setup did not complete (CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE)
```

Byte-identical to the reported symptom in #5080 / #4989.

**Patched, identical sandbox:**

```
Codex capability check completed  account_read=supported account_management=supported capacity_read=supported
agent readiness check  harness=codex  outcome=ready
GET /agents/codex/accounts -> 1 account, status valid, authorized, authMethod chatgpt
  capabilities: nativeLogin / resetCreditConsume / globalSwitch all "supported"
ao spawn --harness codex ... -> spawned session (idle)
```

The account was imported through the `Managed: true` path, so bug 2's fix is exercised
too, not just bug 1.

`go vet` is clean on both touched packages. The new targeted tests pass:

Make local SQLite and PostHog telemetry queues safe when events arrive during or after shutdown.

## Why

Emit could send on a channel that Close had already closed, causing a panic. Both queues date back to [ReverbCode #307](https://github.com/aoagents/ReverbCode/pull/307).

title: fix(updates): parse nightly build stamps as UTC, not local wall time
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5059.

`parseNightlyVersion` read the UTC-encoded nightly stamp (e.g. `202609071035`) with the **local** component `Date` constructor, so the parsed instant shifted by the machine's UTC offset. Every renderer surface that shows the nightly build date — the sidebar update row, the Settings Updates section, and the restart-to-update dialog — then rendered the wrong time (or the wrong calendar day near UTC midnight).

Reproduced against `main` (commit 24e101914): with `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` the stamp `202609071035` parsed to `2026-09-07T05:05:00.000Z` instead of `10:35:00.000Z` (rendered "Sep 7, 10:35 AM" instead of "Sep 7, 4:05 PM"); with `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` it parsed to `17:35:00.000Z`. Under UTC it was correct only by accident. The existing parser tests asserted local getters, so they passed in every timezone and encoded the wrong interpretation.

## Root cause

The stamp digits encode the build time in UTC. `new Date(y, m-1, d, h, min)` interprets them as local wall time; the subsequent validity check also used local getters (`getMonth`).

## Fix

`frontend/src/renderer/lib/build-channel.ts` — two functional lines:

- construct the instant with `Date.UTC(...)`;
- validate the round-trip with `getUTCMonth()` instead of `getMonth()`.

No consumer changes are needed: `Sidebar.tsx`, `settings/UpdatesSection.tsx`, and `RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx` all format through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which renders the equivalent device-local time once the `Date` represents the correct instant.

## Tests

- `build-channel.test.ts`: parser assertions rewritten to `builtAt.toISOString()` / `getTime()` against `Date.UTC(...)` (no local getters, timezone-independent), plus new positive/negative offset coverage (`Sep 7, 4:05 PM` in `Asia/Kolkata`, `Sep 7, 3:35 AM` in `America/Los_Angeles`) and a UTC day-boundary case. Malformed/stable/feature and trailing-commit coverage kept.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx`: new staged-nightly case at the UTC day boundary; the expected date-only label is derived from the absolute instant, so the assertion holds in every timezone.
- `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`: same day-boundary coverage for the dialog label.
- `UpdatesSection.test.tsx` (new): covers the full device-local "Built {{date}}" timestamp for an installed nightly.

All validated locally under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`: build-channel 7/7, RestartToUpdateDialog 6/6, UpdatesSection 1/1, Sidebar 97/97.

## Intentional omissions

- The separate "Last checked" display is untouched: it formats epoch milliseconds and was never affected (per the issue).
- No UTC timestamps in GitHub metadata, updater feeds, or version strings are rewritten anywhere; only the renderer-side parse was wrong, matching the issue's acceptance criteria.

title: feat(telemetry): capture project SCM provider and GitHub org for usage ranking
body:
## What

Adds per-project SCM telemetry so we can answer "which providers do our users use" from PostHog, including how many users are on GitLab.

- **`scm_provider`** (new): classifies the project's git remote into a closed vocabulary `github` / `gitlab` / `bitbucket` / `other`, emitted on `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added`.
- **`github_org`** (earlier commits on this branch): the GitHub org owner, for attributing/ranking usage by organisation.

## How

- `scmProvider(remote)` + `remoteHost(remote)` in `project/service.go` parse the remote URL (scp-style `git@host:...`, https/http, ssh, git protocol), stripping userinfo and port, and map the host to a provider category.
- Only the category is derived. The host, owner, and repo are never emitted. Self-hosted instances resolve to `other` because the host is not published.
- `scm_provider` is added to the remote payload allowlist in `adapters/telemetry/posthog.go`; without that the sanitizer strips it before it reaches PostHog.

## Testing

- `TestScmProvider` covers github/gitlab/bitbucket across URL forms, self-hosted GitLab -> `other`, gist -> `other`, unknown host -> `other`, empty -> "".
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and gofmt clean.
- `go test ./internal/service/project/ ./internal/adapters/telemetry/` pass.

## Notes / risks

- Not retroactive: only projects added after this ships carry `scm_provider`.
- Self-hosted GitLab/GitHub Enterprise report as `other` by design (host is not shipped). Counting those specifically would require emitting more host detail, which this deliberately avoids.
- The review event's `posted_to_provider` (a boolean) is left unchanged; this PR scopes provider identity to project-add, which is the right signal for per-user provider usage.

Once merged and deployed, GitLab users is:

```sql
SELECT count(DISTINCT person_id) AS gitlab_users
FROM events
WHERE event = 'ao.projects.created' AND properties.scm_provider = 'gitlab'
```

title: fix(project-settings): allow up to 100-char display names and surface save errors (#3937)
body:
## What

1. Raised project display name maximum length from 20 to 100 runes across backend DTOs, domain service logic, client models, and OpenAPI spec.
2. In `backend/internal/service/project/service.go`:
   - Validates `in.Name` on `Add()`, and truncates auto-derived names from repo folder paths to 100 runes so projects cannot enter the database with an invalid length.
   - In `UpdateSettings()`, allows updating settings for existing projects with unchanged legacy display names exceeding 100 characters.
3. In `packages/product-ui/src/project-models.ts`:
   - Added `name_too_long` code to `validateProjectSettings` for display names exceeding 100 characters.
4. In `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.tsx`:
   - Mapped `name_too_long` validation error to localized string.
5. In `frontend/src/renderer/components/SettingsDialog.tsx`:
   - Rendered visible error alert message below the Save button when `projectSaveState.phase === "failed"`.
6. Added localized translation key `settings.project.nameTooLong` across all supported languages (`de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN`).

## Why

Fixes #3937

When a project's repository folder or display name exceeds 20 characters (such as `yandex-direct-mcp-plugin` [24 chars]), saving any project settings (including agent defaults, workflow, intake) failed silently because:
1. `Add()` allowed any folder name to become the display name without length enforcement, while `UpdateSettings()` rejected names > 20 characters with `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`.
2. `SettingsDialog.tsx` only surfaced the save error in an invisible screen-reader `sr-only` element, leaving the user with a generic "Save failed" button and no visible explanation.

Raising the limit to 100 aligns with GitHub's repository name length limit and prevents valid repositories from becoming un-saveable.

## How

- Raised `maxDisplayNameLen` constant and OpenAPI `maxLength` to 100.
- Preserved backward compatibility by permitting updates to existing projects if `displayName == row.DisplayName`.
- Surface `projectSaveState.error` visually directly below the Save button with `role="alert"`.
- Regenerated OpenAPI specs and client types via `npm run api`.

## Testing

- `npm run product-ui:check` (126/126 tests passed)
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` (clean)
- `npm --prefix frontend test src/renderer/components/SettingsDialog.test.tsx src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n/renderer-coverage.test.ts` (47/47 tests passed)
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/service/project/... ./internal/httpd/...` (passed)
- `golangci-lint run` (0 issues)
- Manual verification on live Electron app: verified that names <= 100 characters save successfully, and names > 100 characters display visible alert `Project name must be 100 characters or fewer.`

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: Optimistic project import: load board first, provision in background
body:
## Summary

Importing an existing project no longer blocks on the full setup chain. The board navigates immediately after registration while the orchestrator spawn (git fetch + worktree + runtime) finishes in the background behind a provisioning gate with progress banner, 120s timeout escape, and retry. The pre-submit branch lookup IPC is removed and registration git probes run concurrently.

## Why

Importing an existing project showed 3-4s of blocking latency after agent selection: serial branch lookup, serial registration probes, blocking orchestrator spawn, and a 3x250ms session poll loop. Total work is unchanged; it is moved off the critical path so time-to-board drops to well under a second.

## Tests

- [x] `cd backend && go build ./...`
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/service/project/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/`
- [x] `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- [x] vitest: CreateProjectFlow, Sidebar, SessionsBoard, board-empty-states, shell-new-session-shortcut, ShellTopbar, i18n parity
- [x] live daemon timing run: POST /projects before/after on a 248MB repo

## Files impacted

- `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` — optimistic navigate, background spawn, 120s guard
- `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts` — provisioningProjectIds, gated requestNewTask
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionsBoard.tsx`, `BoardEmptyStates.tsx`, `ShellTopbar.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx` — banner + gating
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx` — no blocking branch lookup
- `backend/internal/service/project/service.go` — concurrent registration probes
- `frontend/src/renderer/i18n/*.json` — shell.provisioning keys (8 locales)
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx`, `__tests__/integration/board-empty-states.test.tsx` — coverage

## Measured numbers

Live daemon (`ao daemon`, isolated data dir) against a 248MB / 3408-file clone, 3 runs each:

| Stage | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| POST /projects | ~28-32ms | ~17-21ms |
| getRepositoryBranch IPC (2 git procs) | ~10ms | removed |
| git worktree add | 1.1s blocking | 1.1s backgrounded |
| git fetch (up-to-date) | 33ms | 33ms backgrounded |
| session poll loop | up to 750ms | single awaited refetch |

Note: per-spawn git costs are ~5ms on fast SSDs and 50-200ms on typical macOS/Windows machines, so slow-hardware savings scale proportionally. Full spawn could not run to completion in the sandbox (no agent binary/tmux); it correctly rejects pre-workspace with AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND.

title: fix(session-manager): don't inherit role model on harness mismatch
body:
## Summary

A spawn that selects a harness other than the project's configured `Worker.Harness`/`Orchestrator.Harness` still inherited that role override's `Model`/`Mode`, leaking a provider-specific model alias onto the wrong agent.

The agent-switch path already guarded against this. This moves that gating into `effectiveAgentConfig` itself so every caller — spawn, restore, chat spawn/restore, interface transition, and switch — shares one rule:

- `Model`/`Mode` are inherited only when the launch harness matches the role's pinned harness (an unset role harness means "not pinned" and matches anything).
- `Permissions` is harness-neutral and is always inherited.

The post-hoc `config.Model = ""` gate in `agent_switching.go` is removed; that path now passes the target harness into `effectiveAgentConfig` instead.

## Tests

- `TestEffectiveHarnessAndAgentConfig` extended: a mismatched harness drops model/mode but keeps permissions; an unpinned role override still applies to any harness.
- New `TestSpawn_DropsRoleModelOnHarnessMismatch`: `Worker.Harness=opencode` with `Model="custom/gpt-5.5"`, spawn with `Harness=codex` → launched model is empty (codex uses its own default), permissions still `auto`.
- `npm run lint` (full `go test ./...` + golangci-lint v2.12.2) passes.

## Risks / notes

- Behavior change beyond the bug itself: in the switch path, a role override with **no** harness pinned previously had its model dropped on every switch; it now applies to any harness, consistent with the new "empty = not pinned" rule. Happy to restore the stricter behavior there if that was intentional.
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` was not run — `tsc` is not installed in this worktree. The change is backend-only Go.

title: fix(session-manager): don't inherit role model on harness mismatch
body:
Closes #4873.

## Summary

A spawn that selects a harness other than the project's configured `Worker.Harness`/`Orchestrator.Harness` still inherited that role override's `Model`/`Mode`, leaking a provider-specific model alias onto the wrong agent.

The agent-switch paths already guarded against this with a post-hoc `config.Model = ""` block. This moves the rule into `effectiveAgentConfig` itself so every caller — spawn, restore, chat spawn/restore, interface transition, and both switch paths — shares one definition:

- `Model`/`Mode` are inherited only when the launch harness matches the role's pinned harness (an unset role harness means "not pinned" and matches anything).
- `Permissions` is harness-neutral and is always inherited.

The duplicated gates in `agent_switching.go` and `agent_switching_chat.go` are removed; those paths now pass the *target* harness into `effectiveAgentConfig` instead. Restore keeps pinning `rec.Metadata.Permissions` over the project config, unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestEffectiveHarnessAndAgentConfig` extended: a mismatched harness drops model/mode but keeps permissions; an unpinned role override still applies to any harness.
- New `TestSpawn_DropsRoleModelOnHarnessMismatch`: `Worker.Harness=opencode` with `Model="custom/gpt-5.5"`, spawn with `Harness=codex` → launched model is empty (codex uses its own default), permissions still `auto`.
- Both mandatory gates run locally and pass on this base: `npm run lint` (`go test ./...` + golangci-lint v2.12.2) and `npm run frontend:typecheck`.

## Risks / notes

- The stricter behavior for unpinned overrides is **kept**. An earlier revision of this branch treated a role override with no harness pinned as "applies to any harness"; that reopened the same leak by a second route, since a role `Model`/`Mode` saved without an agent would reach whatever harness launched. The second commit drops model/mode from an unpinned override instead, normalizing in `roleOverride` — the single point both `effectiveHarness` and `effectiveAgentConfig` read through — so the harness-match rule in `effectiveAgentConfig` is unchanged and simply has no model left to inherit. `Permissions` remains harness-neutral and is still inherited.
- The settings form already enforces this (the role agent is required, and changing it clears the role's model/mode). `ProjectConfig.Validate` does not, so a config written through the API, hand-edited, or saved before the agent became required can still carry the shape. Normalizing on read repairs those rather than failing to load them — deliberately not a `Validate` error, which would make existing stored configs fail to load.
- Catalog-based model validation was considered and rejected: codex is `CustomModelEntryDirect` (`modelcatalog/catalog.go`), so `custom/gpt-5.5` is a legitimate free-form value there and a catalog cannot distinguish the leak from a deliberate alias.
