title: bug(chat): brand-new Chat sessions show a false "The agent controller stopped" crash banner for the first seconds of startup
body:
## Bug

A brand-new Chat session paints a **red crash banner for the first few seconds of its own startup**. Before the daemon has created the session's conversation row, the chat surface shows all three of:

- topbar: `Session workspace is not available` (red)
- banner (`role="alert"`, destructive): **`The agent controller stopped`** — "History is kept. Resume the agent or open a shell in the same worktree." with **Resume agent** / **Open shell** buttons
- composer placeholder: `The controller is not connected`

Nothing has stopped. The controller has never started. It resolves on its own a few seconds later.

**Source:** reported in AO chat by the maintainer while spawning worker `agent-orchestrator-327` | **Reported by:** @itrytoohard
**Observed on:** macOS arm64 (Darwin 23.6.0), desktop `0.12.13-nightly.202609081718`, daemon built from `7040909db96e14036043f6623c0698d300035a82` (`vcs.time=2026-09-08T16:39:12Z`, `vcs.modified=true`)
**Analyzed against:** `4748d55c3f737705be9d23dd77c6a1d1d0fbd69e` (`origin/main`)
**Confidence:** High — exact code path traced, and the timing window measured directly in the live durable store.
**Priority:** P2 — self-resolving, but a routine spawn is presented as a crash with recovery affordances, and the offered action ("Resume agent") is meaningless for a session that has never run.

### Failure (first seconds after spawn)

![new session showing a false crash banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-new-session-controller-stopped/.issue-assets/chat-new-session-controller-stopped/startup-false-alarm.png)

### Same session, seconds later — nothing was wrong

![the same session working normally](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-new-session-controller-stopped/.issue-assets/chat-new-session-controller-stopped/settled-working.png)

## Reproduction

1. Spawn a new Chat-mode worker session (any harness) from the desktop app.
2. Watch the chat pane immediately, without navigating away.
3. For the first ~3–13 seconds the pane shows the red "The agent controller stopped" alert and the "The controller is not connected" composer.
4. It clears itself once the controller opens the conversation.

## Root Cause

`Service.Snapshot` reports `stopped` as the default controller state for a session that has *never had a conversation*:

`backend/internal/service/chat/service.go:958-968`

```go
conversation, err := s.store.ConversationForSession(ctx, id)
if errors.Is(err, domain.ErrNoConversation) {
    // A chat session has no conversation until its controller first starts.
    // That is an empty conversation, not a failure — returning an error here
    // would make a brand-new session look broken.
    return Snapshot{
        SessionID:  id,
        Harness:    record.Harness,
        Mode:       domain.NormalizeSessionMode(record.Mode),
        Controller: ports.ChatControllerStopped,
    }, nil
}
```

The comment is right about the error, but the fallback state makes the same claim by another route: `stopped` is a statement that something ran and ended. `SnapshotPage` has the identical branch at `backend/internal/service/chat/service.go:1013-1023`.

The renderer then does exactly what it is told:

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx:1590` — `ControllerBanner` maps `stopped` to the destructive `role="alert"` "The agent controller stopped" with Resume/Open-shell recovery buttons.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:882` — the composer placeholder for a disabled controller is "The controller is not connected".
- `ChatWorkspace.tsx:1183` / `:881` — the composer and the turn-settings bar disable on `state === "stopped"`.

`ControllerBanner` already suppresses the same false alarm for the interface-transition case (`if (transitioning && controller.state === "stopped") return null;`, `ChatWorkspace.tsx:1571-1574`) — the never-started case is the identical class of false claim and has no such guard.

### The window is real and measured

Queried read-only against the live store (`~/.ao/data/ao.db`), session row vs. conversation row creation:

| session | session row created | conversation row created | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-orchestrator-326` | 21:10:48.938Z | 21:10:51.771Z | 2.83s |
| `agent-orchestrator-327` | 22:48:01.376Z | 22:48:07.069Z | **5.69s** |
| `agent-orchestrator-328` | 22:51:25.519Z | 22:51:31.692Z | 6.17s |
| `agent-orchestrator-329` | 22:52:42.350Z | 22:52:55.302Z | 12.95s |
| `agent-orchestrator-325` | 08:00:48.707Z | 08:00:57.398Z | 8.69s |

`agent-orchestrator-327` is the session in the screenshot (`created: 2026-09-08T22:48:01Z`, `updated: 2026-09-08T22:48:17Z`). Every snapshot poll inside that 5.69s gap returned `stopped`.

The durable session row is created before the worktree/provisioning/controller work runs, so the topbar `Session workspace is not available` is the same shape of gap on the workspace-path field.

## Fix

Report the durable fact instead of a crash. A session with no conversation has never had a controller, so `connecting` is the honest reading; `stopped` stays reserved for sessions that actually terminated or exited:

```go
// A session with no conversation has never had a controller, so "stopped" is a
// claim about an ending that never happened. Terminated and exited stay stopped,
// so a genuine failure is never masked.
func startingControllerState(record domain.SessionRecord) ports.ChatControllerState {
    if record.IsTerminated || record.Activity.State == domain.ActivityExited {
        return ports.ChatControllerStopped
    }
    return ports.ChatControllerConnecting
}
```

This is derived from durable state only — no age/grace-period masking, so a session that really did stop is still reported as stopped from the first poll.

On the renderer side, `connecting` already renders as a muted spinner with "Connecting to the agent…" and `role="status"`. The composer and settings bar must stay disabled while starting (there is no controller to `Send` to — `Service.Send` returns `ErrNoController`), which the existing `controllerTransitioning` path already expresses with the same "Connecting to the agent…" copy.

## Impact

- Every Chat session spawn shows a false crash for 3–13 seconds.
- The banner offers "Resume agent" for a session that has never run.
- It devalues the real banner: a user who learns to ignore the red alert on every spawn will ignore it when a controller genuinely dies.

## Related

- [#4531](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4531) / [PR #4532](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4532) — the topbar half ("Session workspace is not available") of the same startup gap; merged as `8f6438c3c` and **not present in the build this was observed on**. It does not touch the chat controller state.
- [#4573](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4573) — the same false-crash presentation, but for *existing* sessions during desktop restart recovery (conversation exists, controller not yet reconciled). Different window, adjacent problem.
- [#5069](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5069) — genuine repeated controller stops after network change/suspend on Linux. Real failures; must keep reporting `stopped`.
- [#4991](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4991) — orchestrator sessions *permanently* show "Session workspace is not available" (no handoff answer for orchestrators), as opposed to this transient window.
- [#4850](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4850) — lifecycle recording "could not" as "did not"; same family of state-honesty defects.

title: fix(codex): stop Default permission mode from bypassing approvals
body:
Code changes: +113 -36  
Tests: +367 -25  
Others: +0 -0

Closes #4840.

## Summary

Codex Default and unknown permission values no longer select the bypass fallback. Terminal launch and restore emit no approval or sandbox override; Chat start and resume omit approval policy, reviewer, and sandbox keys. Only explicit Bypass Permissions selects unrestricted execution.

The Chat picker calls Default "Default approvals". Remembering that choice preserves `default` in project configuration instead of converting it to `bypass-permissions`.

Permission tracking follows successful turns, so switching an observed bypassed conversation back to Default restores approval prompts and the workspace sandbox. Rejected permission changes leave the last accepted state intact.

Merged `main` at `5137c2ccb`, preserving the published commit history, upstream's reconnect effort setting, and menu accessibility roles while retaining the permission regression assertions. The resulting source tree exactly matches the fully validated tree.

## Coverage

- Explicit mappings for Default, Accept Edits, Auto, Bypass Permissions, empty, and unknown values.
- Complete terminal launch/restore arguments, including durable read-only execution mode.
- Actual Chat start/resume wire payloads and successive permission changes using an in-memory provider.
- Project API round-trips for all four modes, saved-preference tests, and separate picker labels.

## Validation

- Backend build, vet, formatting, golangci-lint v2.12.2, and full `go test -race -p=4 -timeout=20m ./...` pass.
- Cloud build, vet, formatting, and full race suite pass.
- Frontend: both typechecks pass; 4,630 tests pass with 6 skipped; all 60 renderer smoke tests pass. Supporting package checks and package dry runs pass.
- Storage and API regeneration produce no drift. Native Linux CLI end-to-end tests and the fresh-install container check pass. Gitleaks v7.4 scans all five PR commits, including the merge, with no findings.
- Portable update-helper tests pass (12 passed, 1 platform-specific skip). No live permission-bypass session was launched.

Validation used Go 1.26.5 as required by the workspace and Node 24.21.0, with bounded concurrency. One backend test initially inherited personal shell startup settings; the full suite passed after isolating shell configuration. The renderer suite passed in full with one worker after an initial startup timeout. Native macOS and Windows validation require CI and were not run locally. Remote checks run on the published merge commit `dafce3c64`.

## Behavior limits

Default delegates to native configuration and does not independently guarantee filesystem confinement. Permission history from before a resume/reconnect is not reconstructed. Previously saved `bypass-permissions` values are preserved because stored configuration cannot distinguish an explicit choice from the old conversion.

title: fix(chat): stop reporting a starting controller as a crash
body:
Fixes #5131

## Summary

A brand-new Chat session showed a **red "The agent controller stopped" crash banner for the first seconds of its own startup**, with a "Resume agent" button for an agent that had never run, and a "The controller is not connected" composer. It cleared itself once the controller came up.

`Service.Snapshot` / `Service.SnapshotPage` used `ChatControllerStopped` as the fallback for a session with **no conversation row yet** (`backend/internal/service/chat/service.go`). But `stopped` is a claim that something ran and ended, and the renderer faithfully paints it as a destructive `role="alert"` with recovery affordances (`ChatWorkspace.tsx:1590`, `ChatComposer.tsx:882`).

This reports the durable fact instead: **a session that has never had a conversation has never had a controller, so it is connecting.**

```go
func preConversationControllerState(record domain.SessionRecord) ports.ChatControllerState {
	if record.IsTerminated || record.Activity.State == domain.ActivityExited {
		return ports.ChatControllerStopped
	}
	return ports.ChatControllerConnecting
}
```

The reading comes from durable state alone — **no age check, no grace period**. A terminated session and one whose agent process exited keep reporting `stopped` from the first poll, so a genuine failure is never masked by a startup window.

On the renderer, the composer and turn-settings bar stay disabled while starting (there is no controller to `Send` to — `Service.Send` returns `ErrNoController`), but reuse the "Connecting to the agent…" copy the existing `controllerTransitioning` path already shows. `ControllerBanner` already renders `connecting` as a muted spinner with `role="status"`, so no banner change was needed.

A *reconnecting* controller that does have a conversation keeps its live composer — a send against it is durably queued, and disabling it would be a regression. That distinction is `!snapshot.conversationId`, and it is covered by a test.

The wire enum already carried `connecting` (`dto.go:2105`), so there is no API contract change.

## Measured window

Read-only against the live store, session row vs. conversation row creation:

| session | gap |
|---|---|
| `agent-orchestrator-326` | 2.83s |
| `agent-orchestrator-327` (the reported one) | **5.69s** |
| `agent-orchestrator-328` | 6.17s |
| `agent-orchestrator-329` | 12.95s |
| `agent-orchestrator-325` | 8.69s |

Every snapshot poll inside that gap returned `stopped`.

## Test

New coverage, each verified to **fail without the fix and pass with it**:

**`backend/internal/service/chat/startup_controller_state_test.go`** (real SQLite store, no controller ever started)
- `TestSnapshotReportsAStartingControllerRatherThanACrash` — never-started session reports `connecting`
- `TestSnapshotPageReportsAStartingControllerRatherThanACrash` — the paged read the desktop app actually calls
- `TestSnapshotStillReportsStoppedForSessionsThatReallyEnded` — terminated, and agent-process-exited, both still report `stopped` on both read paths
- `TestSnapshotReportsStoppedOnceAConversationExistsWithoutAController` — a conversation with no live controller is the genuine stopped case and keeps its banner

**`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`**
- brand-new session: no alert, no "Resume agent", no "The controller is not connected"; `role="status"` says "Connecting to the agent…"; composer inert; recovers to a live composer when the controller is ready
- reconnecting controller *with* a conversation keeps its live composer

Verification run:
- `go test ./internal/service/chat/... -count=1` — ok (20.1s)
- `go vet ./internal/service/chat/` — clean
- `npm run test -- src/renderer/components/chat` — 25 files, 513 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors under `frontend/src` (the reported errors are all in the uninstalled sibling `packages/product-ui` workspace, pre-existing and unrelated)

## Risks / follow-ups

- **The risk this change carries is masking a real failure behind a startup spinner.** It is bounded by using only durable facts: `IsTerminated` and `ActivityExited`. A chat session whose spawn fails without ever setting either would sit on "Connecting to the agent…" rather than "stopped" — a known gap in how lifecycle records "could not" versus "did not" (#4850), not introduced here.
- The topbar half of the same startup gap ("Session workspace is not available") is #4531 / #4532, already merged; untouched here.
- #4573 is the same false-crash presentation for *existing* sessions during desktop restart recovery (conversation exists, controller not yet reconciled). That window is deliberately left reporting `stopped` by this change and needs its own fix.

title: fix(settings): send support email to prasad with prateek on cc
body:
## What

Settings → Help → **Report a problem** addressed the email handoff only to `prateek@untrivial.ai`. This makes `prasad@untrivial.ai` the primary recipient and puts `prateek@untrivial.ai` on Cc, so both receive support mail.

## Changes

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/report-problem.ts` — `SUPPORT_EMAIL` is now `prasad@untrivial.ai`; new `SUPPORT_CC_EMAIL` holds `prateek@untrivial.ai`.
- The copied draft gains a `Cc:` line under `To:`.
- The mailto URL sets a `cc` param: `mailto:prasad@untrivial.ai?cc=prateek%40untrivial.ai&subject=...&body=...`.

Cc was chosen over two comma-separated `To:` addresses because every mail client honors the `cc` param, while classic Outlook for Windows needs "Allow comma as address separator" enabled to parse a multi-recipient `mailto:` path.

No change needed in `frontend/src/main/external-open.ts` — it allowlists the `mailto:` protocol, not a specific address.

## Testing

`npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/report-problem.test.ts src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx` — 44 passed, run on this branch against the latest `main`. Assertions for the recipient and the new Cc were updated in both suites.

- Renderer smoke suite: 58 passed (Node 24, Playwright v1.60.0-noble Linux container, two workers).

title: bug(sidebar): deleting active session from sidebar leaves main screen stuck instead of shifting to remaining session
body:
### Summary
When viewing an active session on the main screen and deleting/killing that session via the sidebar trash button (`SessionActions`), the session is terminated and removed from the sidebar list, but the main screen remains stuck displaying the terminated/dead session. The application does not automatically navigate away to the adjacent/most recent active session in the project, forcing the user to manually click another session in the sidebar.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a project with two or more worker sessions (e.g., Session A and Session B).
2. Click on Session B so it is open and active on the main screen (`/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId`).
3. In the sidebar under the project list, hover over the active Session B and click the trash can icon (**Kill session**).
4. Observe the sidebar and the main view.

### Expected Behavior
Upon terminating the active session from the sidebar:
- The main view should automatically shift/navigate to the adjacent remaining active session in the project (or the project orchestrator if no worker sessions remain, or the project board `/projects/$projectId`).
- The user should not be left staring at a dead/terminated session canvas.

### Actual Behavior
- Session B disappears from the sidebar list.
- TanStack Router remains on `/_shell/projects/$projectId_/sessions/$sessionId`.
- The main canvas remains stuck displaying Session B (in a terminated/exited state) until the user manually clicks another session or navigation link.

### Environment
- **OS**: macOS 
- **App Version**: `0.10.3`
- **Component**: `frontend` (Electron + React supervisor)

### Root Cause & Code Analysis
In `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.tsx`:
- `SessionActions` defines the trash button:
  ```tsx
  <button
      aria-label={t("shell.killSession")}
      onClick={(event) => {
          event.stopPropagation();
          terminateSession(session);
      }}
  >
      <Trash2 aria-hidden="true" />
  </button>

Unlike `ShellTopbar.tsx` (`TopbarKillButton`) and `SessionInspector.tsx` (`SessionControls`), which define `onKilled` navigation handlers when killing a session, `Sidebar.tsx`'s `SessionActions` performs no navigation when the terminated session is the active one (`selection.activeSessionId === session.id`).

### Proposed Solution
- Pass an `onKilled` callback from `ProjectItem` / `Sidebar` through `SessionRow` into `SessionActions`.
- When the deleted session is the currently active one:
  1. If other active worker sessions remain in the project, navigate to the adjacent remaining session (`remaining[currentIndex - 1]` or `remaining[0]`).
  2. If no worker sessions remain, navigate to the project's active orchestrator session if one exists.
  3. If neither exists, navigate to the project board (`/projects/$projectId`).
- If an inactive session is deleted from the sidebar, remain on the currently active session without navigating.

title: fix(frontend): shift to last active session when deleting active session from sidebar
body:
Code changes: +226 -55  
Tests: +351 -20  
Others: +0 -0  

Closes #5142

### Problem
When terminating an active session from the sidebar, topbar, or session inspector:
1. Deleting from the sidebar terminated the session in the list, but left the active route stuck on `/_shell/projects/$projectId/sessions/$sessionId` viewing the dead session (because the row unmounted upon cache update before the mutation's `onSuccess` callback could fire).
2. Optimistic removal could bounce (appear -> disappear) if a background CDC event or workspace refetch interval wrote back a still-alive server snapshot while the termination was in flight.
3. Deleting from the Topbar kill button or Session Inspector kill controls jumped directly to the orchestrator or project board even when adjacent active worker sessions remained in the project.

### Solution
- **Shared Kill Navigation**: Extracted `resolveNextNavigationAfterSessionKill` in `frontend/src/renderer/types/workspace.ts` to unify navigation logic across all three affordances:
  1. If other active worker sessions exist in the project, automatically shifts to the adjacent worker session (previous session in display order, or first remaining).
  2. If no other worker sessions remain, shifts to the active orchestrator if alive.
  3. If no active sessions remain, falls back to the project board (`/projects/$projectId`), or home (`/`) for standalone agent sessions.
- **Optimistic & Refetch-Safe Termination**:
  - Wired `onOptimistic` in `useTerminateSession.ts` to trigger navigation and row removal in `onMutate` rather than waiting for the server round-trip.
  - Added `optimistic-session-kills.ts` to track in-flight kills and re-apply them across CDC / workspace refetches (`fetchWorkspaces`) so rows do not bounce back while the kill is in flight.
  - Cancels in-flight workspace queries on mutate, reinforces cache on success, and rolls back on failure.
- **Sidebar, Topbar & Inspector Integration**:
  - `Sidebar.tsx`: Session actions execute optimistic navigation immediately upon clicking kill.

title: fix: join telemetry aggregation before downstream shutdown
body:
## What

Wait for the telemetry aggregation ticker to finish its active flush before sending the final rollup and closing the downstream sink. Concurrent `Close` callers share one shutdown operation.

## Why

If shutdown starts while a ticker flush is emitting, the previous implementation could close the destination before that flush finished. It also called downstream `Close` again for subsequent callers. This addresses the aggregation portion of backend audit finding AD-02.

## How

- Join the flush loop, flush the remaining buckets, then close downstream exactly once.
- Stop accepting aggregated events when shutdown starts. Preserve immediate forwarding for event names outside the aggregation set.
- Let each caller stop waiting when its context is canceled. Shutdown continues in order using the first caller's context; delivery remains best effort.

Companion to #5112, which protects destination queues against concurrent and late emitters. This branch is independently based on `main` and has no code dependency on #5112. Prefer merging #5112 first because pass-through events and other emitters still need its destination protection. Both changes are needed to complete AD-02.

## Testing

Local validation passed at `23add584f853` on Linux. The checked-in workspace selected Go 1.26.5. Test subprocesses used a clean environment with a POSIX shell and isolated tmux sockets.

Added regressions cover a blocked ticker flush during shutdown, final rollup ordering, concurrent close callers, downstream errors, caller cancellation and late aggregated events.

title: fix: prevent invalidated workspace loads from repopulating cache
body:
## What

Prevent an in-progress workspace Git lookup from repopulating the cache after a filesystem change invalidates its session.

## Why

Invalidation previously removed completed cache entries only. A lookup already running could publish its old compare/status result afterward, so subsequent list and file-detail requests reused stale data until the cache expired. This addresses backend audit finding CORE-10.

## How

- Reserve publication for each session/root before resolving the compare base and running Git queries.
- Remove both cached entries and active reservations when invalidating a session, including all its repository roots.
- Publish only while the load still owns its reservation. Deferred cleanup releases failed loads without removing a replacement reservation or its cached result.

Concurrent callers still share one in-progress lookup. Callers joining an invalidated lookup may receive its uncached snapshot; the first request after it completes recomputes the data. The existing three-second TTL and nil-cache behavior remain. Watcher sharing, broader cache eviction and cancellation of shared Git work are outside this change.

## Testing

title: fix: preserve GitLab response and cache consistency
body:
## What

Reject incomplete GitLab response bodies and make a `304 Not Modified` response reuse the body paired with the validator sent by that request.

## Why

Response read errors were ignored, allowing truncated content to reach callers or cache state. Separately, a concurrent request could replace or evict the cached body while another request was revalidating it, causing the latter to return a different body or no body. This addresses AD-03 and the GitLab portion of AD-05 from the backend audit.

## How

- Check body reads in ordinary GET, caller-managed ETag, merge and paginated requests before consuming content or publishing validators. Preserve both read errors and status-derived errors, including rate-limit hints.
- Capture the cached ETag/body pair before sending a GET and use that request's snapshot for a subsequent 304 response.
- Reject a 304 without a usable cached body and retain the sent validator if the response omits its ETag.
- Copy bytes when storing and replaying cached bodies so callers cannot mutate cache contents through a returned response.

This changes the GitLab client only. The GitHub portion of AD-05 remains separate, and this PR does not redesign cache eviction or provider pagination contracts.

title: fix: retain partial push delivery and receipt progress
body:
## What

Keep tracking accepted push deliveries when a later send batch fails, and retain unresolved receipts for later sweeps instead of losing them after one unsuccessful lookup.

## Why

The sender can return an accepted prefix of tickets together with an error. The dispatcher previously discarded that progress. It also removed due tickets before fetching receipts, so a transport failure or omitted receipt permanently ended tracking and prevented later invalid-device cleanup. This addresses backend audit findings SUP11 and SUP12 through one focused dispatcher change.

## How

- Process returned tickets even when sending reports an error, preserving their order against the filtered device messages. Track accepted tickets and prune explicitly rejected devices without resending messages.
- Keep unresolved tickets at their original send time and capacity position. Process terminal receipts from partial responses and retry omitted or nonterminal results on later sweeps.
- Resolve only tickets included in the request snapshot. Preserve expiry and the 10,000-ticket cap, including expiry or new admissions during a receipt fetch.
- Deduplicate receipt IDs and prevent ambiguous IDs associated with different device tokens from pruning either token. Preserve that ambiguity after expiry or capacity eviction; perform device removal outside the pending-ticket lock.

Receipt tracking remains bounded and in memory. Durable delivery queues, automatic resend of failed batches and broader dispatcher lifecycle changes are outside this PR.

## Testing

title: fix(desktop): stop leaking the shell renderer when the window is closed
body:
## Problem

Closing the desktop window with **Cmd+W** (or the red close button) and then
reopening the app leaves the startup loader spinning forever. **Cmd+Q** and
relaunch works fine.

## Root cause

`WindowComposition.dispose()` read `options.mainWindow.contentView` *outside*
the try/catch:

```js
dispose: () => {
    options.mainWindow.contentView.removeListener("bounds-changed", resize); // throws
    try { options.mainWindow.contentView.removeChildView(shellView); } catch {}
    try { shellView.webContents.close(); } catch {}   // never reached
}
```

On window close, Electron destroys the native `BaseWindow` and *then* emits
`closed`. By the time `dispose()` runs, `options.mainWindow.contentView` is a
getter on a dead object and throws `TypeError: Object has been destroyed` on
the first line — so:

1. `shellView.webContents.close()` never runs → the window's renderer process
   is orphaned and keeps polling the daemon. **Every Cmd+W leaks another
   renderer.**
2. The throw escapes the `.finally()` in `main.ts`'s `closed` handler as an
   **unhandled promise rejection**.

Reopening (`app.on("activate")`) then builds a fresh window alongside the
orphans, which wedges the loader. Cmd+Q is unaffected because it exits the
whole process.

### Reproduced in the real app

Every Cmd+W logged `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: TypeError: Object has
been destroyed at Object.dispose (window-composition.ts)`. After 4
close/reopen cycles the app had **5 renderer processes alive instead of 1**.

## Fix

- `window-composition.ts` — move the `removeListener` / `removeChildView` pair
  inside the existing try/catch so `dispose()` can no longer throw and the
  shell `WebContents.close()` is always reached.
- `main.ts` — add a `.catch()` to the `closed`-handler teardown chain as a
  backstop so a future throw is logged instead of unhandled.
- `window-composition.test.ts` — new test asserting `dispose()` still closes
  the shell WebContents when the `BaseWindow` is already destroyed.

## Testing

- `vitest run src/main/window-composition.test.ts` → 5 passed.
- Manually verified in the dev app: after the fix, Cmd+W → reopen comes back
  cleanly with no renderer leak and no unhandled rejection.

title: bug(codex): device reconciliation failure still disables local account management
body:
## Summary

Codex account management currently treats two different jobs as one bootstrap gate:

1. loading AO's local saved-account store, and
2. inspecting/reconciling the device-global Codex account.

Because device reconciliation runs inside bootstrap, a temporary Codex app-server/read failure makes the entire local account-management feature appear unavailable. Saved accounts can already be present and structurally valid, but Settings hides their usable state, Add/Reauthenticate operations fail with `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, and ordinary Codex launch admission can be rejected.

PR [#4924](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4924) fixed the original daemon-lifetime sticky failure by allowing bounded, demand-driven retries. It did **not** separate local account-store readiness from device reconciliation. A fresh issue is needed for that remaining architectural defect.

Analyzed against `main` at `aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212`.

## User report

The reporter had three Codex accounts added and working in the dev Electron app. The app was not opened for roughly two to three days. When it was opened again:

- all three saved accounts were still present;
- each row showed `Authentication unknown`;
- Settings said the active device account could not be verified;
- usage information was shown as potentially out of date; and
- clicking **Sign in again** failed with `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`.

![Codex account management unavailable while saved accounts remain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets/codex-account-reconciliation-20260909/.issue-assets/codex-account-reconciliation-unavailable.png)

The important point is that an inconclusive device read is not proof that every saved account is signed out, nor proof that AO's local account catalog is unusable.

## Current behavior and verified code path

### 1. Bootstrap still includes device reconciliation

`bootstrapInner` performs local cleanup, refreshes the saved-account catalog, loads the durable active pointer, and then calls `reconcileGlobal` in the same success/failure boundary: [`codex_account_reconcile.go#L116-L153`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_reconcile.go#L116-L153).

Therefore a temporary native Codex failure leaves `bootstrapped=false` even when all AO-owned local state was loaded successfully.

### 2. #4924 retries, but only on later demand

The new gate retries after a 1–32 second cooldown when another caller arrives, but the code explicitly has no timer/background retry loop: [`codex_account_reconcile.go#L18-L77`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_reconcile.go#L18-L77).

This removes the permanent `sync.Once` poisoning from #4908, but local account management is still unavailable between failures/retries and will not recover by itself while idle.

### 3. Unrelated operations wait on the combined gate

The combined bootstrap is currently used by:

- ordinary Codex launch authentication: [`codex_account_service.go#L17-L24`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L17-L24);
- account ensure/list refresh: [`codex_account_service.go#L84-L90`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L84-L90);
- Add Account and Reauthenticate: [`codex_account_service.go#L167-L204`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L167-L204);
- logout/delete and other account operations: [`codex_account_service.go#L219-L251`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L219-L251); and
- switch-target verification: [`codex_account_service.go#L393-L403`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L393-L403).

`WaitCodexAccountBootstrap` maps every categorized bootstrap failure to the same public `CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` envelope: [`codex_account_service.go#L334-L349`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/service/agent/codex_account_service.go#L334-L349).

### 4. Interrupted switch recovery can still make this daemon-fatal

If a durable Codex account switch was nonterminal when AO stopped, startup safety waits on the same combined bootstrap before restoring the switch fence: [`codex_account_switch.go#L1202-L1216`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/session_manager/codex_account_switch.go#L1202-L1216).

That error propagates through `ReconcileStartupSafety`: [`manager.go#L2725-L2731`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L2725-L2731), and the daemon exits before serving the API: [`daemon.go#L642-L654`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/aeb923f79b0e733f0067be6c14608021ee4bc212/backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go#L642-L654).

The switch fence is a real safety boundary, but ordinary device discovery should not be a prerequisite for reconstructing the durable fence or for serving unaffected AO features.

## Root cause

Three independent concepts are collapsed into one boolean `bootstrapped` state:

1. **AO account-store initialization** — can descriptors, account homes, and the durable active pointer be loaded safely?
2. **Device reconciliation** — which account, if any, is currently selected by the canonical device-global Codex credential?
3. **Saved-account authentication verification** — can a particular saved account's credential still authenticate/refresh?

A failure in (2) currently fails (1), and the UI then presents (3) as unknown for every account. That coupling is the defect.

## Expected behavior

Once AO's local account store is safe and readable:

- saved account rows remain visible;
- Add Account remains available;
- inactive-account reauthentication/logout/delete remain available under their existing eligibility rules;
- a temporary device reconciliation failure preserves the last durable active pointer but does not claim it is verified;
- no account receives an **In use** badge until device reconciliation has conclusively matched the canonical account;
- ordinary Codex launch falls back to the native readiness/auth check when the account manager cannot answer conclusively;
- background reconciliation retries and recovers without restarting AO or any Codex session; and
- only operations that mutate the canonical device account remain fail-closed until reconciliation succeeds.

## Proposed implementation

### A. Make local account-store initialization its own gate

Replace the broad bootstrap contract with `WaitCodexAccountStoreReady` (or equivalent). It should only:

- validate/create AO-owned account roots;
- safely clean abandoned pending-login and switch-staging data;
- load and validate descriptors/account homes;
- classify isolated broken descriptors and missing credentials per account where containment is safe; and
- load the durable active-account pointer and revision.

It must not call Codex app-server, inspect provider authentication, query capacity, reconcile the device account, mutate the canonical credential, or touch sessions.

Unsafe account-store root/ownership/database failures should remain fail-closed. A malformed contained descriptor should mark only that account broken; a missing account credential should mark only that account signed out.

### B. Model device reconciliation independently

Maintain ephemeral daemon state such as:

- `not_checked`
- `checking`
- `verified`
- `temporarily_unavailable`
- `blocked`

Expose a redacted projection with `status`, `activeAccountVerified`, safe `reasonCode`, `retryable`, and relevant attempt/verification/retry timestamps. The durable `activeAccountId` remains the last known pointer, but it is not synonymous with a currently verified device account.

### C. Add daemon-owned, bounded background retries

Use singleflight and an injected clock/timer. A reasonable backoff is `1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s max` with bounded jitter.

Trigger reconciliation after local initialization, on retryable failure, successful account login, explicit ensure/Settings focus, relevant auth invalidation, and before a device-global mutation. Native calls must be timeout-bounded and owned by the daemon context rather than by an individual HTTP request.

Outcome rules:

- conclusive native signed-out state: clear the active pointer, retaining saved accounts;
- known device account: select it safely;
- new valid device account: import and select it safely;
- inconclusive/temporary failure: preserve the pointer, mark reconciliation unavailable, retry;
- ambiguous/unmanaged/unsafe state: expose a safe blocked state and disable device-global mutation; and
- device state changed during inspection: abort without mutation and retry.

The conclusively identified device-global account has priority over AO's previous pointer, but reconciliation must not stop or restart existing sessions.

### D. Split admission by safety requirement

Operations that need only local account-store readiness:

- list/read saved accounts;
- add and save a new inactive account;
- reauthenticate an inactive account;
- log out an inactive account;
- delete an eligible inactive signed-out account; and
- read cached account/capacity information.

Operations that require fresh, verified device reconciliation plus commit-time revalidation:

- switch the device-global account;
- active-account logout;
- active-account reauthentication that updates canonical credentials; and
- first-account auto-activation when the device is conclusively signed out.

If first-account login succeeds while device reconciliation is temporarily unavailable, save the account but leave it inactive until the device state can be verified.

### E. Keep ordinary Codex launch independent

The durable switch/recovery fence remains authoritative. A launch may wait while the exclusive credential gate is actively held, and it must remain blocked for a nonterminal/recovery-required switch.

However, after a failed reconciliation releases the gate, the failure itself must not permanently reject launches. The account manager should return `handled=false` (or equivalent) when it cannot conclude authentication, allowing existing native Codex readiness to decide. If native Codex is authenticated, launch proceeds.

This must not create session-switch records, change native session IDs/controller generations, alter usage bindings, or restart running sessions.

### F. Recover interrupted switches without making optional account discovery daemon-fatal

Reconstruct the durable switch/recovery fence from the local store and switch journal first. Do not require ordinary device reconciliation before restoring that fence.

If recovery cannot complete immediately, keep affected Codex operations/sessions fenced and expose recovery-required state, while allowing the daemon to serve unaffected features. Do not silently reopen input and do not weaken rollback verification.

### G. API/SSE behavior

- `GET /accounts` returns cached local rows while reconciliation is checking/unavailable.
- `POST /accounts/ensure` triggers or joins reconciliation but returns a `200` snapshot for temporary device failures.
- Return `503 CODEX_ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` only when the AO local store itself is unsafe/unavailable.
- Device-global mutations return a distinct safe error such as `503 CODEX_DEVICE_ACCOUNT_UNVERIFIED`.
- SSE publishes reconciliation transitions so Settings recovers without reload.
- Never expose tokens, raw Codex output, credential paths, or secret-bearing provider errors.

### H. Settings behavior

- Keep account rows and Add Account visible during temporary reconciliation failure.
- Show concise status such as: `Couldn't confirm the active Codex account. Retrying.`
- Do not mark every saved account signed out/unknown because device reconciliation failed.
- Show **In use** only when the verified device identity matches the account.
- Keep local-only actions available; disable only the device-global mutations that cannot be performed safely.
- Preserve the last successful usage/capacity snapshot with the existing stale indicator.
- Update degraded/recovered state through SSE without requiring app/daemon restart.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Local account-store initialization succeeds while the global Codex read times out/fails.
- [ ] Saved accounts remain visible and Add Account remains usable during that failure.
- [ ] Inactive reauthentication/logout/delete remain usable according to existing rules.
- [ ] An inconclusive device read never clears the active pointer or marks every account signed out.
- [ ] The pointer is cleared only after a conclusive native signed-out result.
- [ ] No account shows **In use** while device reconciliation is unverified.
- [ ] Background retry succeeds without AO restart, manual reload, or session restart.
- [ ] A conclusively identified external device account safely wins over AO's previous pointer.
- [ ] Switch, active logout, and active reauthentication fail closed until device identity is verified.
- [ ] Ordinary Codex launch can proceed when native authentication is valid, despite reconciliation being temporarily unavailable.
- [ ] Durable switch/recovery fences still block unsafe launch/input.
- [ ] A nonterminal switch can restore/retain its fence without making the entire AO daemon unavailable.
- [ ] Reconciliation never changes existing session IDs, controller generations, or usage bindings.
- [ ] API/SSE/frontend tests cover checking, unavailable, blocked, recovered, and redacted error states.
- [ ] Concurrent callers join one initialization/reconciliation attempt and repeated focus/API requests cannot create a Codex process storm.

## Explicit non-goals

- No session restart when the device account differs from AO's previous pointer.
- No change to live-session account propagation policy.
- No account-profile runtime redesign.
- No usage/capacity collection redesign.
- No weakening of the durable switch/rollback/recovery safety boundary.
- No assumption that a temporary provider failure means the account is signed out.

## Impact

The current failure mode blocks the recovery action itself: users can see their saved accounts and are asked to sign in again, but the sign-in flow is rejected because an unrelated device reconciliation attempt failed. It also makes temporary provider/transport problems look like corruption of all saved accounts, and in the interrupted-switch case can prevent the whole daemon from serving.

## Related work

- [#4722](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4722) — introduced Codex multi-account management/global switching.
- [#4908](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4908) — original sticky bootstrap failure report (closed).
- [#4924](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4924) — added demand-driven bootstrap retries; prerequisite mitigation, not this separation.
- [#4973](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4973) / [#4974](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4974) — active-account display readiness vs launch readiness; related auth semantics, separate defect/fix.

title: fix(cloud): delete cloud projects and their sandboxes
body:
Fixes #4605

## Problem

Removing a cloud project from the sidebar always failed. The board merges cloud projects into the same workspace list as local ones (`useWorkspaceQuery.ts`, `kind: "cloud"`), but `removeProject` unconditionally called the local daemon:

```ts
await apiClient.DELETE("/api/v1/projects/{id}", …)   // _shell.tsx
```

A cloud project has no daemon record, so that call could only ever answer "project not found", and the confirmation dialog surfaced the error. The control-plane client already had `deleteProject` (`lib/cloud-cp/client.ts`) and nothing in the app ever called it.

The control-plane side was already correct and is unchanged here: `DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/projects/{projectId}` → `Store.ArchiveProject` stamps `archived_at` **and** flips every sandbox belonging to that project's sessions to `desired_state = 'deleted'` with `reconcile_after = now()`; the reconciler's deletion path (`reconcileDeletion`) issues the provider `Delete`, waits for the box to converge, and calls `CompleteSandboxDeletion` to release quota. Routing the click there is what also tears the sandboxes down.

## Changes

- **`lib/cloud-project.ts`** (new) — `deleteCloudProject()`: calls the control-plane DELETE, then invalidates the cloud project and session queries. The local workspace cache never held this project, so the existing `updateWorkspaces` filter was a no-op for it.
- **`routes/_shell.tsx`** — `removeProject` dispatches on `kind === CLOUD_PROJECT_KIND`; local projects keep the daemon path unchanged. Telemetry (`project_remove` step, `project_removed` event, exception capture) fires on both paths. The client and org come from `useCloudCp`/`useCloudOrg`, which the shell's `useWorkspaceQuery` already subscribes to, so this adds no extra requests.
- **`components/Sidebar.tsx` + 8 locale catalogs** — the confirm dialog claimed removal "keeps the repository folder and stored history on disk", which is false for a cloud delete. Cloud projects now show `shell.removeCloudProjectBody`: the sandboxes are destroyed, session history is kept.

## Tests

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-project.test.ts` (new): deletes via the control plane with the org id and refreshes both cloud queries; refuses without a resolved org; propagates a control-plane failure without invalidating.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx`: a cloud project's confirm dialog warns about sandboxes and no longer promises a folder on disk.
- `frontend/src/renderer/test/shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx`: added a `useCloudOrg` mock alongside the existing `useCloudCp` one — that harness has no `QueryClientProvider`.

```
cd frontend && npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/cloud-project.test.ts \
  src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/test/shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx \
  src/renderer/i18n src/renderer/hooks/useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx
npm run frontend:typecheck
```

Full frontend suite matches the pre-change baseline (the remaining failures are files that fail at import on missing local deps — `mermaid`, `lexical`, landing, forge — and are unrelated).

## Not verified

The sandbox teardown itself is pre-existing Go that I verified by reading, not by running: Docker is unavailable in my environment, so `npm run cloud:local:smoke` skips.

Supersedes the approach in #4913, which is built on the pre-monorepo `backend/internal/cloud/**` layout.

## What

Avoid repeated SQLite migration setup in store tests by using a pre-migrated test database path for cloned fixtures.

## Why

Store fixtures were calling `sqlite.Open()` on already-migrated database clones, causing the full migration/repair path to be re-entered repeatedly. This became a significant bottleneck under `-race`.

title: feat(cloud): launch baked worker + self-update instead of re-uploading each provision
body:
## Why

Provisioning a cloud sandbox spent most of its ~1.5 min post-boot on the control plane **uploading the ~13 MB worker binary** into every new box (a file PUT on nodeops, a 17 MB base64 PTY stream on coder). This PR removes that upload: the CP launches the template-baked worker, and the worker heals itself to the CP's exact build only when its baked copy is stale.

## Verified constraint (why not "boot self-start like docker")

Docker bakes `ENTRYPOINT ["/ao-worker"]` and self-starts from create-time env. That model is **not portable** to the other providers, confirmed empirically on staging:

- **nodeops/CreateOS**: PID 1 is `fc-spawn` (Firecracker microVM), there is no systemd, and create-time envs reach **only the exec API's commands**, never PID 1, `/etc/environment`, or profile.d. There is no init to auto-run a baked service and no boot-visible ticket.
- **coder**: the workspace template is customer-operated and external; the create-time secret-env channel is deliberately avoided, so we cannot bake into it or hand a boot process the ticket.

So nodeops must launch the worker over the exec API and coder over the PTY. What we can remove uniformly is the **binary upload**, not the launch.

## What this does

- **worker**: `selfUpdateIfStale` compares the running `ao-worker` (and the `ao` helper) against the hashes the CP advertises in the environment. If stale, it fetches the exact build from the new content-addressed endpoint into a worker-owned dir already on PATH (`$AO_DATA_DIR/bin`, since the baked copies at `/usr/local/bin` are root-owned) and re-execs. `connect()` reuses a persisted token so a restart skips a fresh ticket.
- **control plane**: `GET /worker/binary/{sha256}` serves the content-addressed binaries (not secret, they ship in every image). `GET /worker/reconnect` returns the durable launch context for a token-reuse restart. The reconciler advertises `AO_WORKER_EXPECTED_SHA256` / `AO_WORKER_HELPER_EXPECTED_SHA256`, so self-update stays completely inert when the bake already matches.
- **createos**: launch the baked worker whenever it is present (drop the hash-gated upload fast path); upload only when the binary is missing entirely.
- **docker**: unchanged. Its image is byte-identical to the CP (`verify-image-contract.sh`), so its worker is never stale and self-update is a no-op.

## Scope / follow-ups

- **coder stream elimination**: the launch env already carries the expected hashes so a baked coder worker self-heals, but omitting the 17 MB PTY stream needs the external customer template to bake `ao-worker` at Destination. Documented in `coder/client.go` as a fast-follow (cannot bake or test it from this repo).
- **resume/persistence stays provider-appropriate**: nodeops resumes its VM in place to keep the filesystem; docker/coder recreate. The unification here is the binary lifecycle (baked, self-healing, never uploaded), not the persistence model.
- Keeping the nodeops template in sync with the CP (republish on deploy) keeps self-update a no-op; with self-heal, byte-identity is now a latency optimization rather than a correctness gate.

## Testing

- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green in `cloud/`.
- New unit tests: worker self-update (hash diff, download+verify+replace, helper heal), CP binary serve + `reconnect`, reconciler hash-env advertisement.
- **Staging E2E pending** (per plan): provision a nodeops box and confirm no binary upload, worker connects, and a deliberately stale bake self-heals.

Targets #5023 (`test/cloud-e2e-happy`) for combined E2E before merge.

title: bug(desktop): Files tab — back from a file preview collapses the tree to the workspace root instead of the folder the file was in
body:
## Summary In the session inspector's **Files** tab (docked in the rail), expanding folders down to a file and opening it, then pressing the back arrow (←), brings back the file tree **collapsed at the workspace root**: every expanded folder, the scroll position and the selection are gone. Browsing a worktree therefore costs a full re-expand of the folder path for every single file you look at. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open a session, open the inspector rail, switch to the **Files** tab. 2. Expand a nested folder chain, e.g. `frontend` → `src` → `renderer` → `components`. 3. Click a file — the docked explorer swaps the tree for the file preview. 4. Press the back arrow ("Back to file tree") in the preview header. ## Expected behavior The tree comes back exactly as it was left: `frontend/src/renderer/components` still expanded, the file still highlighted, same scroll offset — i.e. back goes *back*, one step, to the folder the file was opened from. ## Actual behavior The tree is back at the workspace root with every folder collapsed, scrolled to the top. ## AO version Desktop `0.12.12` (macOS). Also reproduces on `main` @ `808d55724`; `frontend/src/renderer/components/FileTree.tsx` is unchanged between `v0.12.12` and `main`. ## Environment macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Electron desktop build. ## Root cause `SessionFileExplorer` deliberately keeps the tree **mounted** while a file is previewed, so expansion and scroll survive — it only hides it: ```tsx // frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionFileExplorer.tsx
``` `hidden` is `display: none`. But `FileTree` only renders react-arborist's `` once its container has a non-zero measured size: ```tsx // frontend/src/renderer/components/FileTree.tsx const observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => { if (!entry) return; const { width, height } = entry.contentRect; setSize({ width, height }); // 0 x 0 while display:none }); ... {size.width > 0 && size.height > 0 ? : null} ``` Chromium fires the `ResizeObserver` with a `0 x 0` content rect when the element loses its box, so `size` drops to zero and **`` unmounts** — the one thing the "keep it mounted" design was trying to avoid. react-arborist holds the open/closed map in a redux store created inside `TreeProvider`'s `useRef` (`react-arborist/dist/module/components/provider.js`, seeded by `state/initial.js` from `initialOpenState`). Unmounting destroys it; remounting re-seeds from `initialOpenState` (not passed) with `openByDefault={false}` → everything collapsed. The lazily fetched `lazyData` survives, because it lives in `FileTree` itself — which is why the folders are still *there*, just closed. Verified in real Chromium (playwright): observing the tree container across `display:none` → visible logs ``` [[316,400],[0,0],[316,400]] ``` `316` is exactly the docked inspector rail width. ## Fix Ignore `0 x 0` measurements in `useContainerSize` and keep the last real size, so the hidden tree stays mounted and react-arborist keeps its state. Regression test added to `FileTree.test.tsx` (fails before, passes after). ## Impact - Every file opened from the docked Files tab costs a re-expand of the whole folder path. - Tree scroll position and selection highlight are lost too. - The maximized/popped-out explorer is **not** affected: it renders tree and content side by side, so the tree is never hidden.

title: fix(files): keep the docked file tree expanded when returning from a file
body:
## What

Keep the docked Files-tab tree mounted while a file is previewed, so the back arrow returns to the folder the file was opened from instead of a collapsed workspace root.

## Why

Fixes #5168.

`SessionFileExplorer` deliberately keeps the tree **mounted** behind the docked file preview — it only hides it (`cn("min-h-0 flex-1", selectedPath && "hidden")`, i.e. `display: none`) so expanded folders and scroll position survive the round trip.

`FileTree`, though, only renders react-arborist's `<Tree>` once its container has a non-zero measured size:

```tsx
{size.width > 0 && size.height > 0 ? <Tree ... /> : null}
```

Chromium fires the `ResizeObserver` with a `0 x 0` content rect when an element loses its box, so hiding the tree zeroed `size` and unmounted `<Tree>` — exactly what the "keep it mounted" design was avoiding. react-arborist holds the open/closed map in a redux store created inside `TreeProvider`'s `useRef`, so the unmount destroyed it and the remount re-seeded from `initialOpenState` (not passed) with `openByDefault={false}` → every folder collapsed. `lazyData` survives (it lives in `FileTree`), which is why the folders were still there, just closed.

Reproduced against the shipped desktop build `0.12.12` on macOS; `FileTree.tsx` is unchanged between `v0.12.12` and `main`.

## How

`useContainerSize` now ignores `0 x 0` measurements and keeps the last real size, so a hidden tree stays mounted with its state intact. One guard clause, no change to the render path or to the maximized layout (which shows tree and content side by side and was never affected).

Considered and rejected: threading react-arborist's open map out into `FileTree` state via `initialOpenState` + `onToggle`. It reimplements state the library already owns and would still lose the tree's scroll offset on every unmount.

## Testing

- New regression test in `FileTree.test.tsx` — expands `src`, drives the ResizeObserver to `0x0` and back (what `display: none` does), and asserts `src/app.go` is still visible. Fails on `main`, passes with this change.
- Verified the underlying browser behavior in real Chromium (playwright): observing the tree container across `display:none` → visible logs `[[316,400],[0,0],[316,400]]`; `316` is the docked inspector rail width.
In `frontend/`:

- `npm run typecheck` — pass
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` — pass
- `npx vitest run` — 291 files, 4003 tests, all passing (7 skipped)

In `packages/product-ui/`: `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` — pass.

Not run locally: the `renderer-smoke` Playwright job (needs the pinned `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright` container) and the packaged build jobs — verified in CI instead.

title: fix(lifecycle): verify cleanup and recover interrupted startup
body:
## What

Session termination and active review cancellation now verify that owned processes stopped before discarding their runtime identity. Interrupted startup records enough ownership information to roll back with a separate deadline or retain a visible, retryable recovery state.

Confirmed Actions billing refusals remain blocked/unknown instead of generating code-repair requests. Equivalent check reruns no longer generate duplicate repair notifications.

## Why

Addresses [#4850](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4850), including the CI behaviors previously proposed in closed, unmerged [#5088](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5088) and [#5089](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5089).

## How

- Persist tmux process birth identities before removing panes, verify exit after TERM/KILL, and retain ownership for retries across daemon restarts. Linux signalling uses pidfds. Runtime mutation waits respect cancellation.
- Stop active reviewers before atomically cancelling their runs and clearing the selected handle. Preserve completed history and idle inspection. Guard reviewer start paths during startup cleanup.
- Add migration 0130 for durable startup ownership, preserving upstream migration 0129. Use one detached rollback budget, compare operation/launch ownership before destructive work, preserve partial or dirty workspaces, and emit startup changes through the existing database trigger. Persistent Chat shutdown acknowledgements retain ownership until provider exit can be verified.
- Carry explicit billing evidence through single, batch, and paginated observation into persistence and PR display. Preserve real failures. Deduplicate repair notices by substantive failure content rather than attempt URLs, ordering, or transport timestamps.

## Testing

- Backend `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, formatting, and golangci-lint v2.12.2 passed with zero findings.

title: bug(chat): Reload retains failed MCP servers after they are disabled or removed
body:
## Problem
Disabling optional MCP servers in Codex configuration and clicking Reload in an existing AO chat does not clear their previous failed states. The chat continues showing “2 tool servers did not start” for tools the user intentionally disabled.

## Reproduction
1. Start a Codex chat with Paper and MCP_DOCKER configured while their local applications are stopped; both fail startup.
2. Set `enabled = false` in both `[mcp_servers.paper]` and `[mcp_servers.MCP_DOCKER]` in the user Codex configuration.
3. Wait until the turn finishes, then click Reload in the failure banner.
4. Reload succeeds, but both disabled servers remain failed in the conversation snapshot and the banner remains.

Expected: after a successful authoritative configuration/inventory refresh, disabled or removed servers no longer appear as current failures. Preserve failures for servers that are still enabled.
Actual: disabled servers retain their historical failed states after repeated reloads.

## Verified evidence
Reproduced locally on Windows on September 10, 2026, against PR #5020 head `33ed97c49c3d3bfd0be423e6ac765885a67392a8` with uncommitted local Windows account-storage and MCP reload fixes. This is not a clean-main reproduction.

The local MCP reload fix replaces unsupported `detail: "summary"` with the provider-declared `toolsAndAuthOnly` value and only reports positively initialized inventory entries as ready. The stale-state behavior persists after that protocol fix.

Latest verification:
```text
paper enabled = false
MCP_DOCKER enabled = false
POST /api/v1/sessions/<session>/conversation/mcp/reload
HTTP 200, elapsed 5.71 seconds
GET /api/v1/sessions/<session>/conversation
paper: failed
MCP_DOCKER: failed
```
The screenshot/user report shows the same two-server failure banner remaining after Reload. No credentials or private configuration are included here.

## Code findings
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:2857`: `applyMCPServers` merges updates by name into `c.mcpServers` and preserves `mcpServerOrder`; names absent from an update are never removed.
- `controller.go:2915`: an empty reload result explicitly returns the previous server list unchanged.
- `controller.go:2930`: a nonempty reload result uses the same merge path, so omitted disabled/removed servers also survive.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/conversation.go:767`: the reload contract returns a server slice without distinguishing a complete inventory from partial notifications or an unavailable inventory.

The merge behavior is appropriate for individual startup notifications, but cannot reconcile removed servers after configuration changes. An empty slice also cannot safely distinguish “no configured servers” from “inventory unavailable.” Do not simply clear every failure on any successful reload; that could hide real enabled-server failures or erase state after an incomplete refresh.

## Suggested coverage
- Failed server is disabled/removed, then successful authoritative reload omits it: remove stale failure from snapshot and banner.
- All servers disabled: authoritative empty inventory clears the list.
- Inventory read fails or is partial: retain known state.
- Still-enabled failed server remains visible.
- Startup notifications arriving during reload are reconciled without losing current state.

Related: #3748 covers a nondismissible banner and Reload disabled during an active turn. This report is about stale server state after a successful idle reload, not dismissibility or mid-turn behavior.

title: feat(mobile-telemetry): tag chat vs tui on spawn, conductor, and handoff
body:
## Why

The mobile app runs a session in one of two interfaces, a native **Chat UI** or the agent's **TUI**, chosen per session via the `mode: "chat" | "tui"` field (`lib/api.ts`). Nothing recorded which one, so "how many sessions run in chat vs TUI, and do people switch" was unanswerable from PostHog. `ao.session.spawned` only carries `client = cli | null`, no surface split.

## What

Adds a single closed-enum `mode` (`chat` | `tui`) to `ao.v2.mobile_app.feature_used` and sets it on every place a mode is chosen:

- **spawn** (`lib/store.tsx`) tags the interface the session is created with.
- **conductor** / orchestrator launch (`lib/store.tsx`) does the same for the second spawn path, so it isn't undercounted.
- **handoff** (new `feature` value): a live in-session Chat<->TUI switch, instrumented once at the hook both call sites funnel through (`lib/session/useInterfaceTransition.ts`). Its `mode` is the target the user switched to, which in a two-mode world also names the direction (to `tui` = from chat).

This lets you separate:
- **what they choose** at creation (spawn/conductor `mode`), from
- **whether chat is carrying the work** (handoff volume and direction).

`trackFeature` gains an optional `context` arg so the `mode` rides on both the success and failure event without touching the action's own result.

## Privacy

`mode` is a closed enum in the allowlist (`lib/telemetry/events.ts`); the mobile contract's "no free-text property" rule is preserved, so no title, path, or prompt can ride along. Sanitisation still iterates the allowlist, and a `mode` outside `chat`/`tui` is dropped (covered by a test).

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit): clean.
- `npm test` (vitest): 787 passed, including new `sanitize.test.ts` cases for `mode` being kept on spawn/handoff and dropped when outside the enum.
- Both are exactly what `.github/workflows/mobile.yml` runs.

## Notes

- Not retroactive: only spawns/handoffs after this ships carry `mode`.
- `feature_used` for `merge`/`kill`/`restore`/`send` stays mode-agnostic (no `mode` passed), by design.

title: bug(browser): stabilize native surface during resize, maximize, and overlays
body:
## Bug

The embedded browser can lag behind its React slot, flicker, or briefly expose a stale/blank native surface when the AO window or inspector is resized quickly, the browser is maximized/restored, or a side panel/renderer-owned overlay opens while the live page is visible.

**Reported by:** @Vaibhaav-Tiwari in an AO implementation session
**Date:** 2026-09-10
**Analyzed against:** `1d89c93dede0`
**Environment:** macOS 26.4, arm64; AO development checkout with Electron 33
**Reproducibility:** intermittent under ordinary use, readily exposed by rapid repeated transitions
**Confidence:** High — the current renderer-to-main geometry and native stacking paths are traced below, and earlier fixes document the same compositor boundary.
**Priority:** P2 — the browser remains recoverable, but a core review/development surface becomes visibly unstable during common layout operations.

## Reproduction

1. Open a session's embedded Browser panel and navigate to a non-blank page.
2. Drag the inspector resize handle quickly back and forth.
3. Maximize and restore the Browser panel or AO window repeatedly.
4. Open/close a side panel, toolbar menu, tooltip, or dialog while the browser is visible.
5. Observe the native page lagging behind its React frame, flickering, or briefly painting stale/blank content.

## Current architecture and root cause

AO correctly keeps the browser page in a live Electron `WebContentsView` owned by the main-process browser registry. The React renderer owns the placeholder/toolbar layout and measures the browser slot with `getBoundingClientRect()`. It sends fire-and-forget `browser:setBounds` messages to main, which scales/clamps the rectangle and calls `view.setBounds()`.

This becomes unstable under fast transitions because:

- React/CSS layout and Electron's native compositor advance independently.
- `ResizeObserver` does not cover every position-only transform; AO compensates with an immediate measurement plus a fixed 280ms settle timer.
- resize/maximize/panel transitions can produce many intermediate bounds with no revision or acknowledgement identifying the final layout.
- the renderer globally observes Radix `data-state` mutations and body resize classes, then reorders the transparent shell above/below the native page. That adds app-wide observation work and exercises a native restacking path with known stale/black-surface behavior.
- maximize/pop-out handoff uses additional frame/timer sequencing, so interrupted or overlapping transitions can temporarily expose the wrong compositor state.

This is presentation drift, not loss of the centralized browser registry or browser/agent lifecycle.

## Proposed fix

- Keep the live browser `webContents`; do not restore the old JPEG/mirror parking implementation removed by PR #3750.
- Add a single revisioned browser-surface coordinator and make Electron main the sole bounds/visibility writer.
- Coalesce intermediate measurements, reject stale layout revisions, and acknowledge the final applied rectangle.
- Drive resize/maximize/dock/overlay phases explicitly rather than relying on a fixed settle timer and document-wide overlay scans.
- Keep native view ordering fixed where possible; use synchronous visibility/interaction handoff only while a renderer overlay actually occludes the browser.
- Preserve the current surface-refresh nudge strictly as recovery, not the normal correctness mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria

- No stale bounds, black/blank flash, or persistent flicker across 200 rapid resize/maximize/overlay cycles.
- Final native bounds match the React slot within one physical pixel.
- Stale layout updates cannot override a newer layout.
- The browser view and `webContents` are never recreated for presentation changes.
- Tabs, profiles, history, annotations, downloads, DevTools, fullscreen, recently closed tabs, and agent browser control continue working.
- Resize handles retain pointer ownership when crossing the native page.
- No document-wide `data-state` overlay query on unrelated UI mutations.
- Verified in the real Electron app, with cross-platform CI coverage and an explicit Windows manual-verification follow-up if a Windows host is unavailable locally.

## Related

- #2491 — earlier stale-position report; closed, with PR #3898 still open and limited to extra remeasurement.
- #2949 — rapid overlay toggle race under the older parking/mirror implementation.
- #4979 — Windows maximized overlay blackout, later addressed by #5001.
- #3750 — introduced the current live native-composition architecture and removed screenshot/mirror parking.
- #4167 — raises the shell while dragging so the resize handle retains input.
- #4136 and #5001 — compositor/opaque-shell fixes around browser overlays and maximized mode.

title: fix(browser): stabilize native surface layout
