title: fix(session): defer worktree removal instead of 500 on kill (#3408)
body:
Fixes #3408

## Problem

On Windows, `ao session kill` returned INTERNAL_ERROR (HTTP 500) when the agent
process still held the worktree's cwd. The kill path treated a failed worktree
removal at kill time as a kill failure, even though the session itself was
already terminated.

## Fix

Introduce a `ports.ErrWorkspaceDeferred` sentinel. The gitworktree adapter
returns it (wrapped) when an unregistered-path removal cannot complete past the
async handle-release retry budget. The session manager treats it as a preserved
workspace:

- `Kill` marks the session terminated and returns success — the kill never
  fails because of worktree cleanup trouble at kill time.
- The deferred worktree is retried on a later `Cleanup` pass; while it is still
  in use, cleanup reports the skip reason
  `"worktree is in use; will retry on a later run"` instead of an error, and
  reclaims the worktree on a subsequent pass once the handle releases.

No API or storage contract changes; cleanup status remains derived from the
sessions' durable facts.

## Tests

- Kill still succeeds and the session is terminated even when workspace
  teardown defers (`TestKill_DeferredWorkspaceRemovalPreservesAndTerminates`).
- Deferred workspace-project row removal is defers, not errors
  (`TestKill_WorkspaceProjectDeferredRowDefersRemoval`).
- Cleanup reports the deferred skip reason and later reclaims the same worktree
  once it is removable (`TestCleanup_ReportsDeferredWorkspaceRemoval`).

`go build`/`go vet` clean on touched packages; session-manager, workspace, and
session-controller suites pass on Windows (pre-existing platform failures
unchanged).

title: perf(project): tear down a project's sessions concurrently
body:
## Problem

Removing a project with several live sessions tore the sessions down strictly
one after another, so project-removal wall time grew linearly with the number
of sessions.

## Fix

`service/session.TeardownProject` now fans out one kill goroutine per live
session and waits for all of them, so project sessions are torn down
concurrently and removal time is bounded by the slowest session, not the sum.
The first error (in session order) is still returned, and workspace cleanup
still runs afterwards.

Because concurrent teardown can now touch the same repository at the same time,
the gitworktree adapter serializes git worktree teardown per repository via a
per-repo lock. Lock keys are canonicalized through `physicalAbs`, so relative,
trailing-separator, and symlinked spellings of the same repository share one
mutex. Same-repo Git sequences stay ordered while different repositories
still tear down in parallel.

## Impact

Measured with 16 sessions at 150 ms per kill: ~151 ms vs ~2.4 s sequential
(~16x faster). No API or storage contract changes; derived status, PR/check
facts, and cleanup skip semantics are untouched.

## Tests

- `TestTeardownProjectKillsActiveSessionsConcurrently` — kills are issued
  concurrently; total time approaches max, not sum.
- `TestDestroySerializesGitCommandsPerRepository` — same-repo destroy
  operations never overlap; different repos do run in parallel.
- `TestRepoTeardownLockCanonicalizesRepositoryPath` — equivalent path
  spellings select the same teardown mutex.

All 11 PR checks pass, including native macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows runners,
the Windows workspace suite, build/test, lint, drift checks, container, cloud
build, and scan.

title: fix(chat): hold queued turns when a turn fails instead of draining
body:
Fixes #4861.

## Problem

A terminal provider failure on a busy chat conversation dispatched the next durable queued turn immediately. On a systemic provider outage every queued turn failed in turn and the whole queue drained into failed history. The original report saw one OpenAI incident become 35 failed AO turns in 83 seconds.

## Root cause

`afterProject` called `drainLocked` after every primary `ChatEventTurnCompleted` with no check on terminal state. `drainLocked` only guarded on the pending turn and the Stop cutoff, never on whether the turn that just ended succeeded. So a `failed` or `recovered` completion released the next queued turn into the same broken provider, which failed the same way, and by induction the queue emptied.

The existing sync-dispatch-error guard does not help here: a systemic outage takes the async path (dispatch succeeds and returns a provider turn ID, the failure arrives later as `turn/completed` with `failed`), so the sync guard never runs.

## Fix

`drainLocked` now takes an `allowDispatch` decision:

- `afterProject` passes `true` only for a proven `completed` turn.
- A `failed`, `recovered`, or status-less completion holds the queue at `queued`, durable and retryable.
- The Stop cutoff inside `drainLocked` still re-enables dispatch, so messages typed after an intentional Stop are sent. This is the subtlety a naive "drain only on completed" would break: the Stop path relies on the completion event draining the post-Stop survivors.
- The three explicit drain callers (handoff claim, interface drain, interrupt reconcile) keep dispatching.

## Reproduction

Reproduced on current `main` both as a deterministic unit test and live in the desktop app against a fake 404 provider: a running root turn plus three queued automation messages all drained into the outage and settled `failed`.

## Tests

- New `controller_hold_queue_test.go`: `failed` and `recovered` primary turns hold the queue; the provider receives only the first prompt.
- The existing suite already covers `completed` draining (`TestSendWhileBusyQueuesUntilTheTurnEnds`) and post-Stop delivery (`TestMessageTypedAfterStopIsStillDelivered`, `TestInterruptDurableFallbackPreservesPostStopSend`).
- Full `npm run lint` (`go test ./...` + golangci-lint) is green locally.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The issue also asks for explicit recovery UX. Held automation turns currently re-release only when a later turn completes successfully. An explicit operator resume/retry, plus extending `RetryTurn` to accept automation turns (it rejects them today), is worth a separate issue.

title: [Feature]: Near-duplicate detection before tracker-intake auto-spawns a worker
body:
### Problem

## Problem
Tracker intake (backend/internal/observe/trackerintake/observer.go) polls a
project's issue tracker and spawns one AI worker session per eligible open
issue, autonomously and without human review. It already dedupes exact
repeats: `seenIssueIDs` (observer.go:244) skips an issue ID already present
in the session table, and `pollProject` (observer.go:203) checks that set
before calling Spawn.

What it doesn't do is catch two different issue IDs that describe the same
underlying problem in different words. Nothing in `issueMatchesConfig` or
the spawn loop compares issue content across IDs. So if issue #A ("app
crashes on Windows startup") and issue #B ("Windows: fails to launch, exit
code 1") are both open and both match the intake filter, intake spawns two
independent paid AI sessions to solve the same bug and produces two
competing PRs that a human then has to untangle.

This already happens with human-filed duplicates in this repo: #4407 was
fixed by #4601, and a second, independent fix (#4408) was opened for the
same bug and is still sitting open, unmerged. Tracker intake would hit the
same failure mode on its own, repeatedly, at real compute/API cost, with no
human around to notice.

### Proposed direction

## Proposed direction
Add a near-duplicate check to the intake poll, before Spawn is called:

1. Embed each candidate issue's title and body (any off-the-shelf or local
   embedding model, kept pluggable, similar to the "no mandatory external
   dependency" approach in #3967's reflection design).

2. Compare against embeddings of issues already spawned this poll cycle,
   and ideally against already-open PRs in the repo too.

3. If similarity crosses a threshold, skip the spawn and flag it instead
   (a comment on the issue, or some "needs review" surface in AO). It
   should stay advisory, not silently merge or close anything, since a
   false positive here means a real issue never gets worked. That's the
   same posture as the read-only insights model in #3967.

A reasonable first slice: a standalone comparison function
(`isNearDuplicate(a, b domain.Issue) bool`) wired into `pollProject`'s loop
before the existing `seen[issueID]` check, with the embedding backend
behind an interface so it can start as a no-op (always false) and grow from
there. That way intake's default behavior doesn't change until a backend
is actually configured.

### Alternatives considered

## Alternatives considered
Cheap text-similarity (Jaccard/n-gram) instead of embeddings would be
cheaper and dependency-free, but weaker at catching same-bug-different-words
cases like #4407/#4408, which is the actual failure mode this is meant to
target.

Handling this downstream by deduping PRs instead of issues was another

title: fix(chat): decode percent-encoded ACP approval request ids
body:
## What
Allow and Deny in Electron Chat both failed for Cursor/ACP sessions because the resolve routes did not decode percent-encoded request ids.

## Why
Persistent ACP hosts mint ids such as `acp-request:<host>:<n>`. The Electron client posts through openapi-fetch, which encodes the colons as `%3A`. `chi.URLParam` leaves that encoding in place, so the daemon looked up a different id than the one still pending and returned `CHAT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING` for every decision.

This is the same trap `ActivateBranch` already handles for `conversation-1:root`.

## How
Unescape `{requestId}` on approval and structured-input resolve, matching the existing branch-id path. Invalid encodings are refused as `CHAT_REQUEST_INVALID`.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/ -count=1`
- New tests cover escaped ACP ids on both `/approvals/{requestId}/resolve` and `/inputs/{requestId}/resolve`

## Test plan
- [ ] Open AO Electron, import a project, start a Cursor (or other ACP) Chat session in Default approvals
- [ ] Send a prompt that causes a shell/MCP permission card (Allow once / Deny)
- [ ] Click **Allow once** — the command should run and the card should resolve
- [ ] Repeat with **Deny** on a later command — the card should resolve without `this request has already been answered or is no longer waiting`

title: bug(desktop): saved error-reporting opt-in retries apply-policy every second behind the release gate
body:
## What happens

When AO starts with error reporting already enabled, it keeps asking the daemon to apply that preference once per second. The daemon returns HTTP 200, but reporting stays off because this release has it disabled. The desktop treats that valid response as a failure and retries indefinitely.

Settings then says **“Telemetry is off locally. Daemon cleanup is still pending.”** Nothing is waiting to be cleaned up; reporting is intentionally blocked by the release.

- **Checked against:** latest `main`, `a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6`, September 10.
- **Original reporter:** @notlevi911, as credited in the supplied report. Reproduced there on macOS arm64, Darwin 25.6.0, packaged 0.12.12 and dev `378f9f713`.
- **Local verification:** clean Electron dev build on Windows, isolated data, daemon on `127.0.0.1:3019`. The code mismatch was reproduced in a focused test. The macOS timings below are from the original report.

## Reproduction

On macOS, start with an existing valid `~/.ao/data/telemetry_policy.json` whose `events_enabled` is `true`. The relevant condition is that reporting is still enabled **at startup**.

1. Quit AO completely.
2. Launch the packaged app with its output visible:

   ```sh
   "/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/MacOS/agent-orchestrator" 2>&1 \
     | grep --line-buffered apply-policy
   ```

3. Watch `POST /internal/agent-switch-observability/apply-policy` return 200 once per second.
4. Turn reporting off, quit and repeat. The reporter saw one startup call, then no more retries.

The original report measured **60 requests in 60 seconds** on the dev build and **346 in 5m46s** on 0.12.12. All 346 packaged responses were 200, accounting for 346 of 379 daemon HTTP requests in that run.

## Where it goes wrong

[The desktop client](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/frontend/src/main/daemon-telemetry-policy-client.ts#L21-L25) rejects any mismatch:

```ts
if (acknowledgement.eventsEnabled !== eventsEnabled)
  throw new Error("daemon telemetry acknowledgement policy mismatch");
```

But [the controller already allows an off acknowledgement when the release gate is closed](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/frontend/src/main/desktop-telemetry-controller.ts#L206-L210). It never gets to make that decision because the client throws first.

The daemon cannot return enabled here: [the production gate is false](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/backend/internal/domain/agent_switch_observability.go#L17-L19), [authorization requires that gate](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/backend/internal/observe/agentswitch/policy.go#L273-L283), and [the HTTP response uses the authorization value](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/backend/internal/httpd/router.go#L103).

The policy stays `cleanup_pending`, so [the one-second timer](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a8df5228460cbc338173bce6bf47770f65193ce6/frontend/src/main.ts#L2588) keeps retrying. There is no backoff or stopping condition for a permanent restriction.

## Local verification

Tested the actual latest-main controller and client with a simulated HTTP 200 acknowledgement containing the matching generation, `eventsEnabled: false`, `gateDrained: true` and `purgeConfirmed: true`.

| Starting condition | Requests after startup + 60 retry calls | Final state |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Acknowledged preference off | 1 | `applied`, `release_blocked` |
| Acknowledged preference on | 61 | `cleanup_pending`, `daemon_cleanup_pending` |
| Actual Windows policy authority | 0 | `cleanup_failed` |

All three focused checks passed. These were explicit retry calls, not a 60-second wall-clock measurement. Windows fails earlier, before HTTP, because durable policy replacement is unsupported there.

### Windows screenshot

The actual Windows app shows a disabled **Share error events** switch and a permanent cleanup failure message in Settings → General. No reporting preference was changed. This captures the related Windows failure, **not the macOS HTTP loop**.

![Windows Settings: Share error events disabled with a permanent telemetry cleanup failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/423fca22b46dcfbdcc9b4bd76a7bb5fbeee3384d/.issue-assets/telemetry-retry/windows-settings.png)

An additional existing Go check, `go test ./internal/observe/agentswitch -run 'Policy|Production' -count=1`, failed on Windows in `TestPolicyOperationsDoNotOvertakeAtomicApply` with `atomic policy apply did not start`. It is not counted as passing validation.

## Expected behavior

Accept the matching-generation, disabled acknowledgement when the release blocks reporting, as the controller already intends. Settle the policy and show the existing message:

> Error reporting is disabled by this release's safety gate.

Keep the generation check and opt-out drain/purge checks intact. Also stop retrying permanent restrictions such as unsupported Windows durability; backoff alone would still retry forever.

**P2:** unnecessary local requests, log noise and misleading Settings status. At the reported cadence, that is about 86,400 local policy requests per day while the app stays open—not 86,400 PostHog events. Battery impact has not been measured.

## Related

[#5030](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5030) was closed `NOT_PLANNED`. [@i-trytoohard's triage](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5030#issuecomment-5563366293) already identified the Windows retry path.

Filing separately because the release-gate mismatch also affects a supported durable authority. Fixing only Windows would leave this path in place. No matching open issue or fix PR turned up in the duplicate search.

title: fix(review): remove host-trusted reviewers
body:
## Summary

Remove Vibe and Qwen from the supported reviewer set, while retaining them as normal agent harnesses for worker/orchestrator use.

## Why

### Vibe
Vibe cannot provide both properties AO needs from a reviewer: its `plan` agent is read-only but still pauses for confirmation before applying the plan, while its unattended `auto-approve` agent can edit files and run commands. The standalone `--auto-approve` flag approves tool calls but does not bypass the interactive apply-plan transition. Because AO cannot currently configure Vibe as both read-only and fully unattended, Vibe is removed from reviewer selection rather than exposing a reviewer that can stall or modify the checkout.

### Qwen
Qwen does not have auto-approve + read-only access support. These are lesser-used harnesses — if any user requests it in the future, we will implement a custom solution. Not P0.

Continue and Goose remain unavailable for reviewers as they do not meet AO's unattended execution requirement.

All three (Vibe, Qwen, Continue, Goose) remain available as worker/orchestrator agent harnesses.

## Validation

- \`go test ./internal/domain ./internal/adapters/reviewer ./internal/httpd/... -count=1\`
- \`npm run frontend:typecheck\`

title: fix: surface Claude subscription errors in chat
body:
## Problem

When a user without an eligible Claude subscription sends a prompt in Agent Orchestrator, chat appears unresponsive instead of showing the subscription/access error returned by Claude.

The reporter investigated the affected account and found that it is currently on Claude's free plan. The supplied screenshot shows repeated short prompts, no visible assistant response or explanatory error, and the session marked **Idle**.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Claude account on the free plan without the subscription/access required for the selected Claude integration.
2. Open a Claude chat session in Agent Orchestrator.
3. Send a prompt.
4. Observe whether Claude's subscription/access failure is surfaced in chat.

## Actual behavior

The user's prompts appear in chat, but no useful response or error is shown. The session remains idle, leaving the user unsure why nothing is happening.

## Expected behavior

- Display the actual subscription/access error returned by Claude when a prompt is rejected for this reason.
- Preserve the provider's explanation and any actionable guidance so the user understands what is required to continue.
- Show the failed prompt outcome clearly rather than leaving an apparently silent, idle session.

## Validation

Reproduce with an account that triggers Claude's subscription/access rejection and confirm the returned error is visible in AO chat. Verify that eligible accounts can still send prompts successfully.

## Investigation notes

The account's free-plan status is reported by the investigator. The exact provider error text and underlying failure path have not yet been captured; verify these during reproduction rather than hard-coding an assumed subscription message.

Related: #4937 covers a similar silent-chat symptom caused by expired OAuth credentials. This report concerns subscription/access rejection.

title: fix(desktop): settle a release-gated telemetry opt-in instead of retrying forever
body: ## What Stops the desktop re-POSTing `/internal/agent-switch-observability/apply-policy` once per second when error reporting is enabled and the release gate is closed, and gives permanently-restricted policies a terminal state instead of an endless retry. Measured on this branch's parent (`a8df5228`), app left idle with no user interaction: **6,716 requests in roughly two hours**. After this change: **1**, at startup. Following review, this PR also: - **Paces retries against an unreachable daemon**: bounded backoff instead of once a second. - **Stops a gated opt-in from carrying into a release that opens the gate.** Accepting the gate's refusal keeps the opt-in on disk, so a future release would otherwise start reporting on consent given while Settings said reporting was disabled. That opt-in is no longer resumed, and the user is **asked again** on launch. ## Why Fixes #5196. `AgentSwitchFailureProductionEnabled` is `false`, so the daemon correctly answers an enable with `eventsEnabled: false` and HTTP 200. `DaemonTelemetryPolicyClient.applyPolicy` threw on *any* difference between the requested and returned `eventsEnabled`: ```ts if (acknowledgement.eventsEnabled !== eventsEnabled) throw new Error("daemon telemetry acknowledgement policy mismatch"); ``` That fired before `DesktopTelemetryController.acknowledges` could run, and `acknowledges` already ends with `return ack.eventsEnabled || !productionEnabled`: it was written to accept exactly this when the gate is closed. So the view never left `cleanup_pending`, and the 1-second timer in `main.ts` re-POSTed for the life of the process. Settings reported "Telemetry is off locally. Daemon cleanup is still pending." when nothing was pending. The follow-ups address both points raised in review ([consent](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5216#discussion_r3984103293), [backoff](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5216#discussion_r3984103685)). ## How ### 1. The retry loop (#5196) - **`daemon-telemetry-policy-client.ts`**: only the unsafe direction throws. Asked to enable and got disabled is the release gate working, so the controller judges it. Asked to disable and got enabled still throws. The generation check and the opt-out drain/purge proof are untouched. - **`telemetryPolicyRetryable()`** plus an early return in `retryPendingCleanup()`: a platform without durable policy replacement is terminal, not retried. It keys on `durabilitySupported`, not on `reason`, which the controller's `catch` rewrites. - **`GeneralSettingsSection.tsx`**: a permanent restriction no longer renders as "Reporting remains disabled while cleanup retries". Reuses existing copy. ### 2. Backoff for an unreachable daemon `retryPendingCleanup` waits 2s, doubling to a 60s ceiling, measured from when the attempt **failed** so a hung daemon burning the client's 2s abort timeout cannot shorten it. It resets when the policy settles and on an explicit toggle. An hour of outage is **64 requests instead of 3,600**, and it still settles within a minute of the daemon returning. No jitter: one desktop process retries its own loopback daemon, so there is nothing to desynchronise. Same shape as `main/supervisor-link.ts`. ### 3. Consent given while the gate was closed - **`telemetry_policy.json` moves to `schema_version: 2`** with `consent_production_enabled`: whether the gate was open when the choice was written. Version 1 records read as `false`, since the gate has never been open in any release. - **Once the gate is open, an opt-in recorded while it was closed is not resumed.** While the gate stays closed, nothing changes. - **This is a backend change too.** The daemon reads the file itself every second and decides enablement from it, so the rule lives on both sides: `telemetryPolicySnapshot` on the desktop, `readAuthority` in `agentswitch`. The Go reader accepts both versions. Changing only the desktop would make the daemon reject every new record as malformed and reject the policy hint as a mismatch, which brings the #5196 loop back. - The policy view gains `consentRenewalRequired`. ### 4. Asking again `TelemetryConsentRenewalDialog`, mounted in the shell, asks on launch when `consentRenewalRequired` is set: - **Keep off** and **Turn on** carry equal weight. This is a consent decision, so neither is styled as the one to pick. - Either answer writes a new choice and the dialog does not come back. Closing it is not an answer, so it asks again on the next launch. - Hidden under an environment veto or without durable policy support, where turning it on would be refused anyway. - Copy added for all 8 locales. Review also turned up a bug in the shared store: two choices sent in the same tick both reached main, and the second, rejected as stale, left `saveError` set after the first succeeded. `setEnabled` now ignores a second choice while one is saving. This affected the Settings toggle too. 34 files, +885 / −75. The design spec's consent-authority section is updated to match. ### Worth knowing - **Every existing packaged install will see the prompt when the gate opens**, not only users who toggled it. Packaged builds write `events_enabled: true` by default on first launch, and all of those records were written while the gate was closed. New installs after the gate opens still default on, with no prompt. - **Downgrading**: an older build rejects a version 2 record and fails closed, so reporting reads as off. Safe for privacy, but not transparent. - **Translations**: only English is verified. de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR and zh-CN follow each locale's existing tone and terminology but need a native check. ### Intentional omissions - No new copy for a failed save in the dialog; it reuses the Settings failure message. - `invalid_authority` from an authority rejected as unsafe at load is also terminal, since `writable` can never flip back, but the view has no field expressing writability, so `telemetryPolicyRetryable` does not claim to handle it. ## Testing ### The retry loop Same starting condition in both clips: `events_enabled: true` on disk, release gate closed, app left idle. Left pane is AO, right pane counts `apply-policy` requests against elapsed seconds. **Before**, `a8df5228`. Requests climb in lockstep with elapsed time. Settings reports a cleanup that is not pending. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2f3883a-48af-40fd-85e8-91b1dee8e6f5 **After**, this branch. Requests stay at zero; the single startup call happened before recording began. Settings names the release gate. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a15d2aa4-65c4-422c-949b-53ffe3329076 | | Before (`a8df5228`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | --- | | `apply-policy`, idle | 6,716 over ~2h | **1**, at startup | | Policy state | `cleanup_pending` / `daemon_cleanup_pending` | `applied` / `release_blocked` | | Settings → General | "Telemetry is off locally. Daemon cleanup is still pending." | "Error reporting is disabled by this release's safety gate." | ### Asking again What a user whose opt-in was saved while the gate was closed sees on launch, once a release opens the gate. The gate is closed in every current release, so this cannot be reached in a real build yet: it is the real `TelemetryConsentRenewalDialog` rendered in the Playwright renderer harness, fed the policy view the real controller produces for that record. ### Commands run locally - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean - `npx vitest run src/renderer src/shared src/main`: **3,845 passed**. 14 failures, all pre-existing and unrelated: 12 in `browser-profile-import` (`better-sqlite3` built for a different Node ABI) and 2 date-dependent chat tests. - `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 59 passed - `go build ./...`, `go vet` on the touched packages: clean - `go test ./internal/adapters/telemetry/... ./internal/observe/agentswitch/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/daemon/...`: ok Each behaviour change had a test that failed before it. A few guards pass either way by design: recovery after an outage, the delay curve, and the closed-gate cases. - **Loop**: a gate-refused startup driven through 60 retries contacts the daemon once, wired to the real `DaemonTelemetryPolicyClient` over a stub fetcher. - **Backoff**: the attempt schedule over an hour of the 1s tick, a hung daemon whose idle gaps must match the schedule, and recovery once the daemon answers. - **Consent**: the parser and Go reader for both versions and every mismatched shape; the rule on both sides; desktop and daemon agreeing on the hint with the gate open and closed; and a real authority and controller across a restart for "asked again", "turned back on" and "declined". - **Dialog**: shown and hidden states, both answers, closing without choosing, a failed save, and the double-save guard. The dialog cannot be exercised in a real build until a release opens the gate. The desktop paths are driven with `productionEnabled: true`, the daemon with `ProductionEnabled: boolPtr(true)`. **Not claimed as passing:** - **Windows**, not run on Windows hardware. The terminal-state path is covered by a test driving the real `TelemetryPolicyAuthority` with `platform: "win32"`, and every branch it touches is a `process.platform` comparison that returns before any filesystem call. Needs CI or a Windows reviewer. - `TestPolicyOperationsDoNotOvertakeAtomicApply`, which #5196 notes failing on Windows, is a pre-existing backend failure unrelated to this change. It passes on macOS. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix: bound preview log retention by bytes
body:
## What

Bound preview logs to 256 KiB of retained text using a circular completed-line buffer.

## Why

Audit SUP04 found that completed preview log lines had no byte limit. A single completed line could retain its entire large input, and every write into a full 200-line buffer copied the retained string slice. Status reads also copied all lines before selecting the requested tail.

## How

Retain the newest 16 KiB of each completed or partial line, keep the existing 200 completed-line cap, and evict old completed lines as partial text grows beyond the shared budget. Clear evicted string slots and own retained bytes so small suffixes cannot pin giant input strings. Last copies only the requested suffix.

CRLF normalization and chunked writes remain consistent, including eager byte eviction before a trailing CR is removed by LF. Clipping is byte-based. Process management, readiness and API shapes remain unchanged; PTY scrollback changes are separate.

## Testing

Full local validation covers commit `58dadf22e3672df1b1cd708c674a4b9d915a3136`. The original-source regressions fail on the selected base and pass with the fix. Regression coverage includes oversized completed/partial lines, total retained bytes, CRLF/chunk boundaries, circular wrap, tail limits, snapshot ownership and concurrent access.

- Full backend: formatting, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, fresh `go test -count=1 -timeout=15m ./...`, and fresh `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=15m ./...`.
- Full `golangci-lint` v2.12.2 ruleset.
- Native Linux CLI e2e: `go test -tags e2e -count=1 -v ./internal/cli/...`. Exact fresh-install Docker build and smoke run also passed.
- Node 24 `npm ci`, `npm run api`, and generated spec/types drift checks.
- Pinned gitleaks v7.4.0 scan of the single introduced commit.
- Independent source review and combined build/vet/affected-package race checks across all five batch patches.

Affected package tests cross-compiled for Windows amd64 and macOS arm64. Native execution of those package suites was not run locally; remote native jobs cover the workflow's scoped CLI e2e tests.

Repeated benchmarks reduced writes to a full 200-line buffer from 3,512 to 24 allocated bytes per operation, and Last(1) from 3,456 to 16 bytes. These are helper benchmarks, not production profiles.

Publication preflight against `main` at `715e0e06f4746bea969efa30349b26b82116a063`: a clean synthetic merge passed the affected package race suite. The unchanged prepared head also passed `npm run sqlc` using sqlc v1.31.1, with no tracked or untracked generated-code drift. Local checks used Linux, Go 1.26.5 (the workspace version) and Node 24.

## Checklist

- [x] One independent commit from `main` at the recorded batch base
- [x] One focused change for local audit SUP04
- [x] Repository conventions and relevant regression coverage
- [x] Applicable local Linux validation passed; platform gaps documented
- [x] All 10 remote CI checks, including scoped native Linux/macOS/Windows jobs

## Summary

Improves the Editor Handoff user experience by relocating the "no supported editor found" guidance message from an alarming, truncated red alert in the top navigation bar into the options dropdown menu and hover tooltip. Additionally, adds native discovery support and the official brand icon for Antigravity IDE.

## What We Did

- **Topbar Error Cleanup**: Decoupled missing editor guidance from genuine system errors in `TopbarOpenEditorButton`. `<TopbarActionError>` (bright red `role="alert"`) is now reserved exclusively for actual launch failures (`launchError`) and inaccessible workspaces (`!workspaceAvailable`).
- **Dropdown Guidance**: Added a non-destructive informational note (`role="note"`) inside `DropdownMenuContent` below the native fallback options (File Explorer and Terminal), styled with `text-passive text-micro` to match design system tokens.
- **Tooltip Explanation**: Preserved the complete, untruncated guidance in the editor handoff button's hover tooltip.
- **Antigravity IDE Detection**: Added `"antigravity"` to `EDITOR_IDS` and configured candidate detection in `editor-handoff.ts` (`antigravity-ide` and `antigravity` CLI shims, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Antigravity IDE\bin`, `%ProgramFiles%\Antigravity IDE\bin`, and macOS app bundle names).
- **Icon & Branding**: Added the official Antigravity SVG mark and exported `AntigravityIcon` in `icons.tsx` using `BrandGlyph`, registered in `TopbarOpenEditorButton` with its Google Blue `#4285F4` brand color.
- **Tests**: Added Antigravity detection coverage in `editor-handoff.test.ts` and updated `TopbarOpenEditorButton.test.tsx` to assert the clean topbar and dropdown guidance note.

## Before and After Behaviour

Use File Explorer or ..."`), crowding out navigation controls and giving the false impression that the workspace or session had crashed. Furthermore, Antigravity IDE was not recognized as an editor even when installed.
- **After**: The top navigation bar remains clean and free of false-alarm red text. The guidance is presented gracefully inside the workspace options dropdown menu (under File Explorer and Terminal) and on hover in the button's tooltip. title: fix(cloud): no-lag terminal reconnect to idle/paused sandboxes (Layer 1, provider-neutral)
body:
## What

Makes writing to the terminal of a cloud session that has been idle for a while lag-free and lossless, for **both** providers (nodeops and coder). Fixes the class of bug seen on orchestrator a-22: an idle-paused sandbox's terminal went dead (keystrokes silently dropped) and an actively-used agent/orchestrator terminal got re-paused underneath the user.

This is **Layer 1** of the two-layer plan: a provider-neutral control-plane fix. It lives entirely in `queueTerminalRequest` + the reconciler pause path, so it applies to every provider on this branch without provider-specific code.

## Why

Two verified gaps in the existing interaction-lease machinery:

1. **Agent/orchestrator terminals never kept the box alive.** `RefreshTerminalInteraction` refreshed the lease only for `workspace` terminals, and the idle timer is driven solely by the last chat message (terminal I/O was deliberately excluded). So an actively-typed agent terminal was re-paused ~1 min after resume.
2. **Typing into a paused box neither woke it nor delivered.** The terminal-input path never set `desired_state=running` (chat does), and pausing did not disconnect the worker connection, so keystrokes were enqueued to a dead worker and expired unclaimed after 15s, with no wake and no error.

## How

Three provider-neutral changes:

- **`queueTerminalRequest`**: `terminal.input` / `terminal.resize` now refreshes the interactive lease (throttled) and wakes a paused sandbox (`desired_state paused -> running`), for both terminal surfaces. An in-use box stays warm and never idle-pauses; a box that did pause resumes on the next keystroke instead of dropping it. Mirrors the existing wake in `IssueTerminalTicket`, for the in-session case where the box paused under an already-open terminal.
- **Reconciler pause path**: disconnects the session's worker when the box is paused, so the input readiness check honestly reports "no worker" and wakes the box instead of enqueuing to a dead connection. On resume the worker reconnects under a fresh epoch.
- **`interactionRefreshThrottle`**: bounds the lease rewrite so a fast typist does not update `ao_sandboxes` on every keystroke (at most once per ~90s within a 2 min lease).

Keep-alive is on real input, not on a merely-open stream, so an idle-but-open terminal still pauses normally (no billing regression).

## Provider coverage

- **nodeops**: pause is an in-place suspend, resume is in-place in seconds, so keep-warm + wake-on-input make reconnect feel instant and lossless. Fully covered here.
- **coder**: the same keep-warm/wake logic runs (coder is on this branch). Because a coder stop destroys the container (only the durable volume persists), a genuinely cold resume is still slow until the worker binary is baked into the customer template. The control plane already advertises `AO_WORKER_EXPECTED_SHA256` for coder self-heal; baking the template is the Layer 2 fast-follow below.

## Testing

- New reconciler tests: pausing a running box stops the provider and disconnects the worker; an already-stopped box is not re-stopped or re-disconnected on subsequent ticks.
- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green for the cloud module.
- Recommend an E2E pass on staging: idle-pause a nodeops session, then type into its terminal and confirm it resumes and delivers without a dropped keystroke, and that an actively-used terminal is not paused underneath the user.

## Layer 2 (not in this PR)

The coder-specific latency work is infra/customer-side or existing PRs, not new code here:
- Bake `ao-worker` into the eleven_x Coder template so a cold resume self-heals (~100s -> ~seconds) instead of re-streaming the binary over PTY. Gated on the external customer template; CP self-heal env already wired.
- Honor Coder autostop + deadline-extend active work (existing PR #4737) and tune `AO_CLOUD_IDLE_PAUSE_THRESHOLD` (deploy config) so in-use coder sessions are not stopped.
- Warm/standby pool of pre-baked sandboxes: deferred (can be done later).

## Notes

- No schema migration.

title: feat(mobile): derive app icons from the desktop Ruto icon
body:
## Summary

#5079 refreshed the desktop app icon (bright-blue Ruto on a black tile) for macOS and Windows, but the mobile app still shipped icons generated from the old `ao-logo.svg` artwork. This makes the mobile icons match the desktop one.

The macOS `icon.icns` and Windows `icon.ico` contain the same artwork, so everything is derived from one source: `frontend/assets/icon.png`.

## How

`packages/mobile/scripts/icon-build/from-desktop.py` (run via `scripts/generate-icons.sh`, Pillow only):

1. Strips the macOS tile's transparent margin, bevelled silver rim and rounded corners. Mobile OSes draw their own tile shape, and a baked rim stacks with iOS's own glass edge.
2. Fits the tile face's diagonal shade (lighter top-left) and un-mixes Ruto, drop shadow included, from it.
3. Re-lays the pieces per platform, mapping the desktop tile's edge to the platform's mask so Ruto keeps the same size and position.

| Output | What it is |
|---|---|
| `AO.icon` (iOS 26) | Ruto layer over a tile-face layer. System specular and shadow are off on Ruto because the artwork already has the desktop's gloss, and the system pass washed the blue out (55,180,249 → 94,178,243). The face is a layer, not the fill, because Icon Composer ignores a linear-gradient fill's `orientation` (always vertical). It's hidden in the tinted appearance so iOS draws its own tinted tile. |
| `icon.png` | Full-bleed flat version (iOS ≤18, Expo Go, Android legacy). |
| `android-icon-background.png` / `-foreground.png` | Adaptive icon. `app.json` now uses `backgroundImage` (the face shade) instead of `backgroundColor`. Ruto is fitted to the 66dp safe circle so the wand tip survives circular masks, which leaves him ~20% smaller relative to the tile than on desktop. |
| `android-icon-monochrome.png` | Themed-icon silhouette. |
| `splash-icon.png`, `favicon.png` | Splash artwork and web favicon. |

The old SVG pipeline (`render-svg.mjs`, `separate.py`, `compose.py`, `icon-build/icon.json`) and the old `AO.icon` layers are removed, and `generate-icons.sh` now reads the desktop icon. If the desktop icon changes again, rerunning the script updates mobile.

## Verification

- `ictool` renders of `AO.icon` (Default/Dark) match `icon.png` within 1/255 on the tile face and on Ruto. `icon.json` validates clean. Tinted and clear renditions render with the system tile.
- Installed and eyeballed on an iPhone 13 (iOS 26.6, real Liquid Glass edge), a Samsung M31 (One UI rounded-square mask), the iOS 26.5 simulator, and a Pixel emulator (circle mask).
- `packages/mobile` CI job locally on Node 20: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm test` (79 files, 787 tests) all pass.

## Notes

- **Needs a new native build.** App icons are native assets, so this ships with the next store build, not via OTA. `app.json` changes also change the fingerprint runtime version.
- **iOS shows Apple's glass edge, not the Mac's crisp silver ring.** The Mac ring is painted into `icon.icns`; iOS 26 adds its own edge on device (the simulator draws it flat). Android has no system rim, and a painted ring can't follow launcher-chosen mask shapes.
- **Not included:** the in-app mascot (`assets/mascot.png`, used on onboarding and Settings) is still the old Ruto. Left for a separate PR.

title: fix(electron): return cancellation results for aborted browser-runtime commands
body:
## Summary

When the Electron browser-runtime link reconnects or disposes, in-flight and queued daemon commands were aborted without sending a `result` frame. The Go broker kept waiting until its own timeout.

This change:
- Tracks every accepted command in `activeCommands`
- Emits `BROWSER_COMMAND_CANCELED` result frames synchronously before socket teardown
- Clears `activeCommands` before aborting controllers to avoid duplicate cancellation frames
- Tears down on socket `end` as well as `close` so cancellation can still be written
- Keeps async cancellation for daemon-initiated `cancel` frames only

## Problem

`respond()` returned early on `AbortSignal` without writing a result. Per-session queued commands never started `respond()` at all, so they also sent nothing. The daemon-side broker correlates by `requestId` and hung until timeout.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test -- src/main/browser-runtime-link.test.ts`
- [ ] Reconnect/dispose the desktop app during an in-flight agent browser action; daemon should get `BROWSER_COMMAND_CANCELED` instead of hanging

title: fix(chat): ignore replay checkpoints from unsettled turns
body:
Interim guard for #4424. Deliberately narrow: two files, +148/−0, no schema change.

> [!NOTE]
> This does **not** replace #4466. That PR carries the full model — checkpoint trust/provenance columns, coordination-prompt handling, recovery-consent fencing, and the **Retry / Use provider history / Stay in Terminal** actions — and should still land. It is currently stacked on the unmerged #4463 and its migrations (`0120`/`0121`) now collide with `main` (already at `0135`), so this guard closes the hole in the meantime.

## Problem

A session whose newest hook fact came from a turn the provider never settled can **never** return to Chat. Every `tui -> chat` transition fails `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` after the full 45s `nativeHistorySettleLimit`, then rolls back to Terminal.

`nativeHistoryCheckpoint.reached` requires the latest completed user message in the ACP `session/load` replay to text-match `sessions.latest_user_prompt`. A cancelled turn's prompt is never replayed as a completed message — Claude forks its next prompt from the pre-cancellation transcript entry — so the comparison can never succeed. `lifecycle/manager.go` only overwrites that field with a non-empty value, so the poisoned fact never ages out on its own.

`captureAOHighWater` already refuses to anchor on non-completed turns, with a comment noting that requiring one "would make every future switch time out". That is precisely what happens here — the hook-derived text facts simply had no equivalent filter.

## Evidence from a live reproduction

Session `meetyou-26`, packaged nightly `v0.12.13-nightly.202609091711` (daemon `378f9f713b`), Claude Code over ACP. `sessions.latest_user_prompt` held `"Say hi to"` from **2026-09-07**, and `conversation_turns` shows the turn requested at that exact timestamp is `state = cancelled`.

Eight consecutive attempts failed, each at ~46s. Clearing that one field — changing nothing else — produced this:

| Time (UTC) | Phase | Error | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:28:47 | failed | TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED | 46.4s |
| **15:29:59** | **completed** | — | **2.6s** |

Same daemon process, same provider transcript, 72 seconds apart. Other sessions (`meetyou-24`, `oddswell-24`) completed `tui -> chat` in ~4s throughout, ruling out provider health, account rate limits, and anything global.

## Fix

`dropUnsettledHookFacts` retires checkpoint text that AO durably recorded on a cancelled, interrupted or failed turn, applying the rule `captureAOHighWater` already uses for its own anchor.

It only acts **on evidence**: a checkpoint AO cannot tie to one of its own turns is left in place, because absence of a row is not proof the work was unsettled, and these facts are what stop a stale replay from being imported as current. The newest matching turn decides, so re-sending a prompt after a cancellation restores it as a valid gate.

## Tests

`TestCheckpointIgnoresPromptFromUnsettledTurn` — cancelled / interrupted / failed, modelled on the rows above. Fails on `main`, passes here.
`TestCheckpointStillGatesOnCompletedPrompt` — control: a settled prompt the replay has not reached must still block the import. Passes both before and after, so the guard is not over-broad.

```
go test ./internal/service/chat/...    ok  17.610s
go test ./internal/session_manager/... ok  21.620s
go vet ./internal/service/chat/        clean
gofmt                                  clean
```

## Limitations

The guard acts only on evidence, so it covers a **subset** of poisoned sessions: those whose checkpoint text can be tied to one of AO's own conversation turns. Two cases are **not** covered, and both fail identically to the user, with no way to tell them apart:

- **A session that has only ever run in TUI.** TUI turns are never projected into `conversation_turns`, so there are no rows to consult and nothing is dropped. In the reproduction session the rows stop at 2026-09-07 while the TUI work preceding the failures ran on 2026-09-11 — it was rescued only because it had been in Chat days earlier. Since #4424's own reproduction is "Stop now and switch" on a busy TUI turn, this is plausibly the more common shape.
- **A turn cancelled before its user message is projected**, which leaves no matching row either. (Raised by @Pulkit7070 in review.)

Extending the guard to those would mean distrusting the hook text with no evidence — in practice, after a previous `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED` failure — which imports possibly-stale provider history automatically. That is what #4466 puts behind explicit consent via **Use provider history**, and it belongs in that trust model rather than in an interim guard.

## Impact

Within the evidenced subset, a poisoned session recovers on its next switch attempt with no SQL edit and no migration. Outside it, the behaviour is unchanged and #4466 remains the fix.

Today the only escape from any of these is `update sessions set latest_user_prompt='' where id='<session>'` against `ao.db`, which is not something a user can reasonably be asked to do — the switch simply keeps failing with no actionable UI, and on mobile the screen bounces back to Terminal with nothing surfaced at all.

title: fix(chat): preserve native history across Terminal/Chat switches
body:
Code changes: +969 -379  
Tests: +1835 -150  
Others: +136 -39  

Fixes #5228

Editing an earlier message or forking in Terminal can change the native conversation ID. Chat kept the old ID, so returning from Terminal failed with a provider-handle mismatch. Stale checkpoints from the previous conversation could also block replay.

The switch now resumes the verified current conversation in a separate history scope. Earlier messages stay visible behind a context boundary. History, controller ownership, and cleanup of pending work commit atomically. Ordinary resumes still require an exact ID match; trusted checkpoints remain mandatory.

Codex IDs are scoped in storage and decoded for native calls. Copied fork history is shown once only when ancestry, stable turn/item identity, and completed content agree—even when persisted item IDs are missing. AO approval/input records stay visible without being mistaken for native transcript content. Original rows are never deleted. Legacy IDs remain compatible.

Launch configuration is shared, replay modes are mutually exclusive, and live handoff is separate from recovery. Migration 0147 upgrades current main without colliding with its migrations.

Regression tests use the production Codex adapter with scripted provider responses to cover fork → Chat → restart, changed/unrelated history, tool output, retained approvals, and missing item IDs. A populated-database test covers the migration.

Local checks pass: full backend suite (after a LAN-test retry; the LAN suite also fails on unchanged main), affected-package and migration race suites, build, vet, lint, generated-file drift, frontend/E2E typechecks, CLI E2E, all 60 renderer tests, and 4,731 frontend tests. title: fix(chat): tolerate an approval mode the selected model does not offer
body:
## What

Checks the agent's advertised mode choices before calling `session/set_mode`,
and skips the call (reporting `ErrACPSetterUnsupported`) when the mapped mode
isn't among them, instead of failing the turn.

## Why

Fixes #6147

Claude Code only offers the `auto` classifier mode for models whose SDK
reports classifier support. Selecting a model without it (e.g. Haiku) left
the static AO-vocabulary mapping asking for a mode the live session never
advertised, and the turn failed outright rather than degrading gracefully.

## How

`modeFor`'s static mapping stays as the source of the AO-vocabulary → agent
mode translation; this only gates the live `session/set_mode` call behind
whether the agent's current advertised choices actually include that mode.
When absent, it returns `ErrACPSetterUnsupported` — the same error class
`Start`/`Resume` already tolerate elsewhere, since an initial mode can
legitimately reach the agent via launch-time flags instead of the setter.
Also skips `set_mode` entirely when the requested approval mode already
matches the session's current one, so an unchanged setting can't fail a turn.

**Cross-provider scope — please double-check if you maintain one of these**:
this touches the *shared* `internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp` package, not
Claude-specific code. Ten provider drivers build on it (claudeacp, piacp,
cursoracp, kimchiacp, ompacp, droidacp, opencodeacp, kimiacp, nativeacp).
`legacyMode` is set dynamically per-session from whichever agent's own
initialize response includes legacy mode data, not statically per provider,
so any of them could exercise this path. I only tested Claude Code and
opencode by hand. Before submitting I confirmed the change builds and all 8
other providers' own test suites still pass — but none of them, including
Claude's own `claudeacp` package, had any test coverage of mode-switching
before or after this patch, so that confirms no regression *elsewhere* in
those packages, not that mode-switching itself is correct for the untested
providers. The change can only convert a would-be hard protocol error into
graceful degradation for a mode the agent's own live catalog doesn't list —
the one risk I can't rule out without live-testing all ten is a
non-compliant agent that would accept `session/set_mode` for a mode it
doesn't advertise as a choice.

## Follow-up after rebase (review feedback from unolife)

After rebasing onto `main`, #5208 already covers this fix on `main`: `applyTurnSettings` applies the model first, then falls back from a model-unsupported Auto to `default` (only when the live `mode` option is advertised and lacks Auto; an absent `mode` option is asked exactly as before) and records the effective mode in `permissionMode`. I verified each review claim against that code:

1. Raising default->auto on a session that never offered auto: no longer fails (falls back to `default`). My original `ErrACPSetterUnsupported` gate would have reintroduced the failure in `SendTurn`.
2. First `set_mode` skipped at Start by the `!= currentPermission` short-circuit: valid for my original patch, a real regression. `main` has no such short-circuit.
3. Bookkeeping out of step: valid for my original patch; `main` records the effective mode.
4. `legacyMode &&` gate: moot; `main` keys on the `mode` config option, not legacy modes.

title: fix: skip session cleanup of a workspace still used by a live session
body:
Fixes #5074

`Manager.Cleanup` only checked `IsTerminated` before deleting a workspace directory. A terminated predecessor and a live successor can share one persistent worktree (the orchestrator's is reused across respawn), so cleanup would delete the live session's cwd out from under it.

Added `liveWorkspacePaths` to build the set of paths still held by non-terminated sessions before the cleanup loop runs. A terminated session whose path is in that set is skipped (recorded in `Skipped` with reason) - but its runtime handle is still destroyed so the keep-alive shell is always reclaimed. Paths are normalized with `filepath.Clean` so trailing slashes or `.` segments don't cause false misses.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode chat ignores selected reasoning effort and uses lowest variant
body:
### What went wrong?

In AO native Chat using the OpenCode harness, selecting a high reasoning effort does not match the variant recorded by OpenCode on subsequent requests. AO displays/saves the selected effort while OpenCode uses the lowest effort. I have tested this in multiple sessions.

| Model (provider: `opencode-go`) | Selected in AO | Recorded by OpenCode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | `xhigh` | `minimal` |
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `Max` | `low` |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an OpenCode-backed conversation in AO native Chat.
2. Select `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` with effort `Max`, or `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with effort `xhigh`.
3. Send a prompt.
4. Compare AO's selected effort with OpenCode's session/message metadata: OpenCode records the lower variant.

This has been tested in multiple sessions. The specific database evidence below comes from one existing orchestrator conversation in which DeepSeek was used before switching to Muse.

### Evidence

Read-only inspection of the local databases, before applying a workaround, found:

- AO's `conversations` row stored `model = opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` and `reasoning_effort = xhigh`.
- OpenCode's session model stored `{"id":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","providerID":"opencode-go","variant":"minimal"}`.
- Recent OpenCode user messages recorded `model.variant = minimal` for Muse; assistant messages also recorded `variant = minimal`.
- The preceding DeepSeek assistant messages recorded `variant = low` despite my having selected Max. The previous AO effort value was not independently recovered from historical database state.

The mismatch is visible in request metadata before the model answers; it is not an inference from answer quality or reasoning-token counts. No provider HTTP request capture was performed.

### Expected behavior

AO should apply the selected effort to OpenCode before prompting and keep the displayed setting consistent with the effective setting. If it cannot apply a selection, it should report that rather than silently continuing with a lower effort.

### Environment

- AO installed package version: `0.12.12`
- OpenCode session version recorded locally: `1.18.30`
- Linux, AO installed from the Debian package
- AO interface: native Chat
- Harness: OpenCode
- Provider: `opencode-go`

### Suspected integration path (not a confirmed root cause)

Inspection of the installed OpenCode bundle showed that its ACP model setter can reset the effort variant when the model ID has no explicit variant. Its fallback prefers a variant named `default`, otherwise the first available variant. This is consistent with Muse selecting `minimal` and DeepSeek selecting `low`.

The AO/OpenCode handoff should be investigated for an omitted effort, a reset on model selection, or stale settings being reapplied. The responsible call sequence or component has not been conclusively isolated. Relevant AO code includes the ACP conversation `applyTurnSettings` and config-option handling.

### Workaround attempted

After collecting the evidence, custom variants named `default` were added in the user OpenCode configuration: `reasoningEffort: xhigh` for Muse and `reasoningEffort: max` for DeepSeek. JSON validation passed, but the effect of this workaround on a subsequent request has not yet been verified. This does not establish a fix for AO's explicit effort selector.

I searched existing issues for OpenCode effort reports and did not find an exact duplicate. No credentials, conversation bodies, or private project files are included in this report.

title: Windows npm-installed Block Goose (.cmd shim) goes undetected after identity validation
body:
## Problem

PR #5267 narrowed the Goose adapter's Windows binary candidates to `goose.exe` only and dropped the `{npm, goose.cmd}` candidate from `gooseBinarySpec.WinPaths`. This was deliberate — `.cmd`/`.bat` shims need shell-specific launch semantics (`cmd.exe` wrapping) that are tracked separately under #3409, and the PR deliberately does not introduce them.

However, `npm install -g @block/goose` (or equivalent) on Windows produces a `goose.cmd` shim in `%APPDATA%\npm\`, **not** a `goose.exe`. A Windows user whose only Block Goose install is the npm `.cmd` shim will now get **"not installed"** instead of detected — a regression for that install path.

## Before (pre-#5267)

```go
WinNames: []string{"goose.cmd", "goose.exe", "goose"},
WinPaths: []binaryutil.WinPath{
    {Base: binaryutil.WinAppData, Parts: []string{"npm", "goose.cmd"}},  // dropped
    {Base: binaryutil.WinAppData, Parts: []string{"npm", "goose.exe"}},
    ...
},
```

Any `goose`-named executable was accepted (false-positive risk with Pressly's migration CLI).

## After (#5267)

```go
WinNames: []string{"goose.exe"},
WinPaths: []binaryutil.WinPath{
    {Base: binaryutil.WinAppData, Parts: []string{"npm", "goose.exe"}},
    ...
},
```

Identity-validated, but `.cmd`-only installs are invisible. `isNativelyLaunchableWindowsGoose` rejects non-`.exe` before any process launch.

## Scope

**Affected:** Windows users who installed Block Goose via npm and only have the `.cmd` shim (no native installer, no cargo, no scoop/choco `.exe`).

**Not affected:** macOS/Linux (fully covered). Windows users with a native installer, cargo, scoop `.exe`, chocolatey `.exe`, or WinGet `.exe`.

**Severity:** False-negative (undetected install) — better than the old false-positive (wrong tool detected), but still a regression for a legitimate install path. Users in this bucket will see Goose as "not installed" and be prompted to install it again.

## Relation to #3409

#3409 tracks Windows `.cmd`/`.bat` launching, command quoting, process ownership, and ConPTY lifecycle. This issue is the **detection gap** that #3409's launch work will close: once `.cmd` shims can be safely exec'd through `cmd.exe`, the identity probe can validate them and `WinNames`/`WinPaths` can re-include `.cmd` candidates.

This issue exists so the gap has its own tracking and isn't lost behind the broader #3409 work.

## Suggested follow-up

- Confirm whether Block Goose's npm package also ships a `goose.exe` alongside the `.cmd` shim (some npm packages do via a `bin` preinstall step). If so, the gap may be smaller than expected.
- When #3409 lands `.cmd` launch support, re-add `goose.cmd` to `WinNames` and the `{npm, goose.cmd}` `WinPath` candidate with identity validation enabled.

title: feat(onboarding): device-code GitHub login without auto-opened browser
body:
Replaces the embedded login terminal with a one-click browser device flow.

**How it works**
- Daemon runs fixed `gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --clipboard` in a hidden PTY with `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` (survey prompts wait on terminal responses no hidden PTY answers, so prompt-disabled mode is what keeps the login from stalling).
- Daemon extracts the OAuth device code from PTY output (ANSI-stripped regex, 20s bounded wait) and returns it as `deviceCode` on a new `GitHubAuthTerminalEnvelope` (spec + `schema.ts` regenerated together).
- Dialog shows the code with copy plus a user-triggered **Open GitHub** button (`github.com/login/device`). AO never opens a browser by itself.
- Home notice hides once `github-auth` reports satisfied (also in dev).

**Verification**
- Backend: `systemcheck`, `shellterm`, `httpd/...` green; `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean.

title: feat(browser): add an on-demand browser panel for orchestrators
body:
## What

Give orchestrator sessions an on-demand Browser panel. Plain HTTP(S) links in Chat or terminal output now open inside AO. The orchestrator starts at full conversation width with the panel closed; users can also open it using the existing inspector toggle or shortcut.

Fixes #4247.

## Why

The shared link handler previously discarded orchestrator clicks after native navigation had been cancelled. Orchestrators also had no inspector rail, so simply removing the link guard was insufficient to display an in-app browser.

## How

- Reuse the worker Browser panel, animated rail, sizing, resizing, and pop-out behavior.
- Limit the orchestrator inspector to Browser, with a plain heading and no Summary, Reviews, or Files navigation tabs.
- Reveal the orchestrator Browser on its first new preview target or agent browser activity. This follows actual browser activity, not keywords in the conversation.
- Preserve the user's close choice across later background activity and session navigation; the panel can be reopened through the toggle or a link click.
- Preserve worker preview routing, modifier-click system-browser behavior, URL validation, and active-session checks.

## Testing

- 105 tests passed across ChatMarkdown, SessionChatSurface, and TerminalPane.
- 231 tests passed across SessionView and SessionInspector, including orchestrator defaults, shortcut opening, preview/activity reveal, closing, session navigation, and browser-only content.
- 15 shared SessionInspectorView tests passed.
- Frontend TypeScript typecheck and `git diff --check` passed.

### Manual verification

1. Open an active orchestrator session: conversation starts full-width and Browser is closed.
2. Plain-click an HTTP(S) link in Chat: the right Browser panel opens and loads the URL.
3. Confirm only Browser is available, then resize and pop out the panel as with a worker.
4. Close and reopen the panel with the inspector toggle/shortcut; confirm the conversation expands when closed.
5. In a fresh orchestrator session, run an actual browser command or publish a preview URL: Browser opens on first activity. Close it and confirm subsequent background activity does not reopen it.
6. Switch between worker and orchestrator sessions and verify their panel state is independent. Worker tabs and modifier-click external opening should behave as before.

title: fix: forward reasoning effort to OpenCode ACP sessions
body:
Fixes Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#5268 — native Chat with the OpenCode harness ignored the selected reasoning effort and OpenCode fell back to the lowest variant (`minimal`/`low`).

**Root cause (two drops in the AO -> OpenCode handoff):**
- `opencodeacp/sessionOptions()` mapped only `Model` and discarded `Effort`, so no per-turn effort ever reached OpenCode via `session/set_config_option`.
- `ChatStartConfig` had no `Effort` field, so ACP `Start()` applied `{Model, Approval}` while `Resume()` already applied `{Model, Effort, Approval}`.

OpenCode''s model setter resets the variant to `default`, else the first variant, when no explicit variant is given — hence `minimal` for Muse and `low` for DeepSeek despite AO storing `xhigh`/`Max`.

**Changes:**
- `ports/chat.go`: add `Effort` to `ChatStartConfig`.
- `chatdriver/acp/driver.go`: `Start()` validates/applies `{Model, Effort, Approval}` like `Resume()`.
- `chatdriver/opencodeacp/driver.go`: forward `Effort` as the advertised `effort` option (category `thought_level`), model first then effort so the reset happens before the variant is applied. New `TestSessionOptionsForwardsEffortAfterModel`.
- `service/chat/service.go` + `history.go`: pass durable `cfg.Effort` into every `driver.Start`/`Resume`.
- `chatdriver/codexappserver/driver.go`: `Start()` now sends `config: {model_reasoning_effort}` like its `Resume()` does (same fresh-start drop class; per-turn `turn/start` already carried it).

**Intentional omissions / notes:**
- No OpenAPI regen: only internal port structs changed, no controller DTOs or `apispec` operations.
- No live OpenCode verification in CI: needs a local OpenCode install + credentials (`AO_LIVE_OPENCODE_ACP=1` test stays skipped). Unit-level repro confirmed the drop before the fix and the forward after.
- `codexappserver` full suite fails on Windows (`/tmp/ws` not absolute) — pre-existing, fails at the `IsAbs` guard before any changed code.

title: feat(desktop): add a custom notification sound
body:
Code: +593 −8
Tests: +290 −1
Files removed: 0

## What

A "Notification sound" row under General settings (choose / test / reset icon buttons) so AO plays a user-supplied audio file instead of the OS beep.

## Why

Fixes #5035. The Windows chime is unpleasant and changing it system-wide is not an option for people who rely on it elsewhere. AO had no sound of its own: `shell.beep()` in `frontend/src/main.ts`, plus the toast's own chime on top.

## How

- `frontend/src/main/notification-sound.ts` copies the picked file to a temp name under `~/.ao/notification-sound/`, renames it into place, and stores only its path in `ui-settings.json`. Nothing leaves the machine. The system beep stays the default.
- `notificationSound:choose` does copy → persist → prune, so a failed settings write leaves the old file and old path in agreement. `uiSettings:set` drops `notificationSoundPath`; only choose/clear can set it.
- Reads resolve both sides through `realpath` and require a single segment under the managed dir, so a symlink cannot point a read outside it; the 10 MB cap applies on read as well as import.
- Main cannot play audio, so it reads the bytes once and sends them to the renderer (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/notification-sound-player.ts`). Main still decides when a sound plays. Decode/play failures report back over `notificationSound:playbackFailed`; main beeps and drops the cache so the file is re-read next time.
- While a custom sound actually plays I mark the toast `silent` so the chime does not stack on it. One global sound only; per-type sounds were out of scope.

## Testing

`notification-sound.test.ts` (temp/rename, prune ordering, symlink and size-cap rejection), `notification-sound-player.test.ts` (failure reporting), plus extended ui-settings, ui-locale, and store tests. `npm run typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass. I ran the app on Linux and exercised the settings row; I did not run this on a real Windows or macOS build.

title: bug(tests): nightly build-date assertions are timezone-dependent and fail east of UTC+7
body:
## Bug

Two update-label tests hardcode a calendar day that only holds in timezones at or behind roughly UTC+6:46. They pass on CI, which runs UTC, and fail for any developer east of that.

```
frontend/src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx
  > names the channel and build date for a staged nightly
frontend/src/renderer/components/RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx
  > shows what the build changes
```

Both assert:

```
expect(...getByText("Nightly 0.12.11 · Sep 2")).toBeVisible();
```

against the stamp `0.12.11-nightly.202609021713`.

## Why it fails

`202609021713` is 17:13 UTC on Sep 2. After #5115 fixed #5059, the label correctly follows the device-local calendar day of that instant. In UTC+9 that day is Sep 3, so the hardcoded `Sep 2` no longer matches.

The code is right; the assertion is what is timezone-fragile. The test added immediately below it by the same fix is already timezone-safe and shows the intended shape:

```js
const expected = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en", { month: "short", day: "numeric" })
  .format(new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 8, 7, 3, 0)));
expect(...getByText(`Nightly 0.12.11 · ${expected}`)).toBeVisible();
```

The two older assertions were left hardcoded.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd frontend
TZ=UTC          npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx   # passes
TZ=Asia/Seoul   npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx   # fails
```

Measured on `upstream/main` at `4ad71cc24`, in a clean worktree with no local changes:

| TZ | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UTC, Europe/London, America/New_York, Asia/Kolkata | pass |
| Asia/Seoul, Asia/Bangkok | fail |

Asia/Kolkata is UTC+5:30 and still passes, which places the boundary between +5:30 and +7.

## Why CI never sees it

No workflow in `.github/workflows/` pins `TZ`, and GitHub runners default to UTC.

## Suggested fix

Derive the expected label from the absolute instant in both tests, the way the neighbouring test already does, rather than pinning `TZ` in CI. Pinning would keep the suite green while leaving the same blind spot for the next date-formatting change.

Filed from a private downstream fork; happy to send a PR if useful.

title: feat: add Qoder CLI harness (worker, reviewer, chat)
body:
Adds Qoder CLI as a harness: a worker adapter, a reviewer, and a Chat driver over its ACP surface.

Qoder CLI is a gemini-cli fork whose CLI and hook surfaces mirror Claude Code — `--session-id` / `--resume`, `--permission-mode`, `--append-system-prompt[-file]`, and a hook system whose event names, payload fields, notification types and session-end reasons are Claude's. So it is driven as a TUI + hooks harness, and activity derivation delegates to `claudecode.DeriveActivityState`.

Opened as a **draft**: every acceptance criterion that needs a live `qodercli` process is still unverified (see Testing below). Happy to split this into three PRs (worker / reviewer / chat) if you prefer — the three surfaces are separate packages; the shared enums, migration and regenerated spec are what tie them together.

## Where it deviates from the Claude Code template, and why

- **Hooks, workspace trust and the auto-update switch travel in one AO-owned `--settings` file**, written under the session's data dir, instead of `<worktree>/.qoder/settings.local.json`. Qoder CLI gitignores only `AGENTS.local.md`/`*.local.md`, so a settings file in the checkout would show up untracked in every worktree; and passing the payload inline is not free either — Qoder CLI stages inline JSON into a content-addressed file in the shared temp dir, never cleaned up.
- **Trust is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** In an untrusted directory Qoder CLI forces `--permission-mode` back to `default`, blocks system-scoped hooks, and opens a modal trust dialog *while the initial task is submitted behind it* — so an unattended pane answers nobody and finishes nothing. (AO's own hooks are flag-scoped and exempt from that gate, so activity reporting itself survives; I verified this rather than assuming it.) The settings file grants trust for the session's workspace, listed under both its literal and symlink-resolved path, since trust is realpath containment.
- **The reviewer composes its own argv** with `--permission-mode dont_ask` and `--tools Read Grep Glob Bash`. `auto` is unusable here: it routes every approval through a classifier model and fails when none is configured. `dont_ask` refuses instead of prompting, so an unattended pane cannot stall, and `--tools` is real containment — every built-in outside the list is denied, where `--allowed-tools` only pre-approves.
- **Restore never carries the new turn on the command line.** `--resume` is resolved asynchronously inside the TUI while `-i` auto-submits from an unrelated effect, so a command-line turn can land in a session that has not finished loading; an unresolvable id opens the session-picker modal rather than exiting, which would strand the pane. The turn goes into the pane after startup instead, and `NativeConversationExists` is scoped to the workspace's own transcript bucket so a same-id transcript from another checkout cannot trigger that path.
- **`SubagentStop` is not installed** (no activity signal, and its payload would overwrite the session summary with a subagent's last line), and the deriver adds Qoder CLI's `elicitation_dialog` notification, which Claude has no equivalent for — without it a session parked on an AskUserQuestion form reads as active.

Chat runs `qodercli --acp` behind a ≥ 1.1.37 version probe (the release that introduced the current ACP mode vocabulary). It declares plans, diffs and usage, but **not** history: Qoder CLI replays a loaded session's history after answering `session/load`, by which point AO's capture window has closed.

## Testing

- `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` — clean, apart from two pre-existing failures on this machine (`crush` and `grok` local-auth probes read the real CLI credential files; they fail on `main` too).
- New tests cover launch/restore argv, the settings payload shape, transcript-bucket scoping, the elicitation activity mapping, the reviewer's read-only policy on both launch and restore, ACP mode mapping, and the version floor. `TestMigrateRepairsQodercliHarnessConstraint` covers a database where 0136 was recorded without its effect.
- `npm run api` regenerated; `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are committed.

**Live validation** against a daemon built from this branch (isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`, throwaway project), qodercli 1.1.50:

- **Chat over ACP** — AO spawned the session as `ao chat-host … qodercli --acp --append-system-prompt … --settings …`; the agent completed its task inside AO's git worktree and the session settled to idle.
- **Terminal session** — the settings file landed at `<DataDir>/agent-runtime/qodercli/<session>/settings.json` with exactly the designed payload (9 hook events, no `SubagentStop`, 30-second timeouts, the worktree trusted); activity moved active → idle through the hooks; the task file was written; and `latest_user_prompt` / `latest_assistant_update` were captured, which exercises the `cli/hooks.go` conversation-facts switch.
- **Native id round trip** — the stored `agent_session_id` equals the UUID the adapter derives for that session, so `--session-id` → hook → store is closed.
- **Exit and restore** — `exit-agent` drove the session to `exited` via the SessionEnd hook; `restore` relaunched it and a hook posted within seconds, returning the same `agent_session_id` under a new launch id.
- **Trust** — tested A/B against an isolated `QODER_CONFIG_DIR`: with the trust entry, no dialog and the mode held; without it, the modal appeared with the task submitted behind it.
- **Reviewer containment** — running the exact argv the reviewer adapter builds: the mode read `Don't Ask`, a read task succeeded, and an instructed write was refused outright (no file created, no dialog, turn ended cleanly). Incidentally, qodercli auto-allows provably read-only shell commands such as `ls`, which stays within the read-only intent.

That run found the two defects fixed in the second commit (the realpath transcript bucket, and the null `hooks` key), and corrected the trust claim above.

**Still not verified, and I'd ask CI to confirm:**

- `golangci-lint` is not installed on this machine (`go vet` passes).
- The JS toolchain is not installed (no `node_modules`), so `npm run typecheck` could not run. The TypeScript change is three literal additions plus one test table; the compile-time exhaustiveness check in `reviewer-harnesses.ts` is satisfied by the regenerated schema.
- **AO's review pipeline end to end** — trigger → verdict → `ao review submit` needs a session with a real GitHub PR. The reviewer's launch argv and its read-only containment were verified directly (above), but the surrounding flow was not. That is the remaining reason this is a draft.

## Deliberately not included

- **A brand logo.** AO falls back to a lettermark, and this PR does not invent a vendor asset; the README logo table is untouched for the same reason. Happy to add it if Qoder supplies one.
- **Default reviewer inheritance** (`ResolveReviewerHarness`): only the original unattended-safe set is inherited, and adding a new harness there would silently change existing projects.
- **Usage/cost tracking** for the terminal harness, and model-catalog discovery (`--list-models` has no JSON output, so the harness uses free-text model entry).
- **The CN build** (`qoderclicn`, `.qoder-cn`, `QODERCN_*`): the site is fixed at build time, so supporting it means site-aware paths throughout.

## Known limitations, documented in `docs/harnesses/qodercli.md`

- A repository's committed `.qoder/settings.json` is not loaded in AO sessions: the trust value that gates workspace settings is computed from the user's settings file alone, before AO's flag is merged.
- Under strict environment sanitization (`GITHUB_SHA`, or `SURFACE=Github`) Qoder CLI strips AO's variables from hook processes and activity reporting goes quiet. Pinning a subset into the hooks was considered and rejected as strictly worse: a pinned `AO_SESSION_ID` would outlive a stripped `AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID` and post reviewer activity to the session endpoint.
- `CI=true` / `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` force Qoder CLI into headless mode, which is incompatible with a TUI session.
