title: fix(chat): explain a failed Codex turn instead of settling it empty
body:
Fixes #5289.

## Summary

Failed Chat turns could be stored without an explanation, and native history replay could erase an explanation already recorded. This PR covers the production native Codex adapter as well as ACP.

- Native Codex live completions and history imports share failure handling. Provider messages are preserved; missing details receive an honest fallback that distinguishes failed, unknown, and absent status.
- History reconciliation preserves failure explanations for explicit failed outcomes and recovered outcomes. Incoming provider errors take precedence over stored explanations, which take precedence over synthesized fallbacks. An internal structural error marker avoids comparing display text. Completed and interrupted outcomes do not inherit stale failure text.
- ACP stop-reason failures receive an explanation. An accepted local stop followed by a failing stop reason settles as interrupted. Successful completion races, rejected stops, compaction, and existing separate error activities retain their behavior.

Shared SettleTurn semantics remain unchanged. No new error activity is emitted for a completion fallback.

## Verification

- New native, cancellation and reconciliation regressions reproduced the old behavior before their fixes.
- A SQLite-backed failure/reconnect test checks persisted snapshots and archived completion details, then repeats the history import to prove no duplicate rows. It fails against the pre-fix controller.
- New regressions passed ten repetitions under the race detector.
- Full backend build, vet, non-race tests, race tests, and pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2 passed.
- Cloud build, vet, and race tests passed.
- Linux native CLI end-to-end suite and rebuilt fresh-install container smoke check passed.
- API and sqlc regeneration passed with no drift using Node 24 and pinned generators.
- Formatting and whitespace checks passed. The pinned secret scanner checked all three PR commits and found no leaks.
- All 11 remote CI checks passed for commit 85dda9a208bdde40227ff27bb6ff947eb0d41387, including backend race tests and the Windows/macOS checks.

## Limits and follow-up

- Future handling only. Already-archived empty failures are not backfilled, and deduplicated events are not forcibly reprocessed.
- No HTTP, OpenAPI, database schema, or UI changes. Existing UI rendering consumes the stored explanation.
- No automatic retries or guessed root causes. Missing provider details remain explicitly unknown.
- Root dependency installation reported three existing audit findings. Dependency manifests and lockfiles are unchanged.

```
{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"error":"context deadline exceeded"}}
```

Reported by @Pyasma on Discord. Screenshot: [switch-error.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-acp-refresh-32603/.issue-assets/acp-refresh-32603/switch-error.png)

## Repro

Claude Code session in the Terminal UI, switch to Chat. Provider rejects the history refresh, switch rolls back to Terminal.

## Root cause

The settle wait (`importNativeHistory`, `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:632-668`) polls `RefreshHistory` every 100ms for up to 45s. Each poll is `refreshableConversation.RefreshHistory` (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/history.go:62`): re-send ACP `session/load` to replay the transcript. The provider answers every load with JSON-RPC `-32603 Internal error`, `data: {"error":"context deadline exceeded"}`, so the switch exhausts the 45s budget.

Gaps:

1. `normalizeACPError` (`driver.go:621`) maps only `-32000` and `-32601`. A `-32603` from `session/load` falls through as a generic error at `controller.go:653`.
2. No session-level timeout wraps the load. The deadline the provider hits is its own.

Not covered by #4123 or #4681 (fixed by PR #4770, which made ACP refreshable). The failure is inside that new refresh path.

## Fix direction

Give the `session/load` failure its own transition error code. Cap or back off the retries instead of hammering it for the full 45s.

**Confidence:** Medium on the fix, high that the refresh call fails with the provider's error.

## Related

- [#4681](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4681), fixed by [PR #4770](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4770)
- [#4123](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4123): earlier full-budget burn on an immutable replay

title: feat(scm): add GitCode provider for PR observation and Kanban
body:
## What

Adds a GitCode (gitcode.com) SCM provider so AO can observe GitCode pull requests on the Kanban, alongside GitHub and GitLab.

## Why

GitCode hosts a large share of open-source activity for Chinese communities (Ascend model contests, CANN ecosystem), but AO's PR/CI/review integration currently only supports GitHub and GitLab. A user tracking GitCode-based projects gets no PR column on the board and no `ao session claim-pr` support. This adds first-class GitCode support through the existing multi-provider dispatch (`multi/provider.go` was explicitly designed for "future providers").

## How

- New `backend/internal/adapters/scm/gitcode` package implementing the observer `Provider` contract against GitCode's public **v5 REST API** (`/api/v5/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`). GitCode v5 is Gitee-shaped, so the GitLab adapter cannot be reused.
- **PR states** normalize as `open/merged/closed` (plus `draft`); mergeability maps from GitCode's boolean `mergeable` field; `mergeable=false` reports `MergeBlocked` with a generic blocker (the API does not explain why).
- **Review threads** are derived from PR comments grouped by `discussion_id` (GitCode v5 has no dedicated review/discussion endpoint). Thread-resolved state is not exposed, so threads report `Resolved=false`.
- **CI is intentionally reported as `unknown`** with zero checks: GitCode v5 exposes no pipeline/status endpoints (verified: `/commits/{sha}/status`, `/checks`, `/statuses`, `/pipelines` all 404). `CommitChecksGuard` and `FetchFailedCheckLogTail` are no-ops rather than fabricating a passing state.
- **Pagination** follows the `total_page` response header (GitCode sends no `Link` header); `ListPRsByRepo` stops early at the `updatedAfter` cursor since the listing is `sort=updated&direction=desc`.
- **Guarding**: `RepoPRListGuard` uses a synthetic ETag (`updated:<newest updated_at>`) as the cheapest change signal; v5 sends no ETags.
- **Auth**: `AO_GITCODE_TOKEN` / `GITCODE_TOKEN` env vars (same pattern as `AO_GITLAB_TOKEN`). Anonymous mode reads public repos without an Authorization header; identity resolution uses `GET /user` with the token.
- **URL parsing** is wired through all three layers: `cli/pr_ref.go`, `service/session/claim_pr.go`, and `domain/repository_identity.go` all recognize `gitcode.com` and its `/owner/repo/merge_requests/N` PR path (no `-` segment, unlike GitLab).

## Testing

- Unit tests in `observer_provider_test.go` cover ParseRepository (https/ssh/scp-like + non-GitCode host rejection), pagination + cursor early-stop, positional alignment with `ErrSCMNotFound` placeholders, state normalization, discussion-thread grouping with bot detection, synthetic-ETag guard NotModified, anonymous fallback, error classification, flexTime edge cases, and mergeability mapping.
- End-to-end verified locally against a real GitCode repository: registered a GitCode project → spawned a session → `ao session claim-pr <sid> 4645` → Kanban shows the PR number and 1 review thread from GitCode comments. `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/gitcode/` green; `go vet` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: bug(chat): project-scoped imported conversation edits fail before provider work
body:
## Bug

Editing a Chat message in a project-scoped orchestrator conversation imported from Terminal fails with HTTP 409 `CHAT_EDIT_UNCERTAIN`. No edited branch is created; **Retry edit safely** repeats the error.

**Source:** native QA requested by @illegalcall in [PR #4466](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4466).
**Observed:** 2026-09-12, macOS arm64, Claude Code 2.1.269 / Opus 5, AO checkout `9a34cdad21b6a2567da863b24b13fbf56548f6f6`.
**Priority:** high. **Confidence:** high in the ownership mismatch; regression test pending.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Claude orchestrator in Terminal and complete prompts A/B.
2. Switch to Chat and complete prompts C/D.
3. Edit C and submit.
4. Retry the same saved edit with **Retry edit safely**.

Expected: one edited branch and replacement reply, with idempotent safe retries.
Actual: both requests fail; original eight messages/root branch remain.

## Evidence and cause

![Imported-origin edit fails before provider work](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b91e402-120e-4dc5-8c4a-ba608670ce2b)

The durable delivery remains `reserved`, `provider_work_started=0`. The SQL `BeginConversationEditProviderWork` in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/conversations.sql` joins `sessions.id = conversations.session_id`. For this project-scoped conversation, `session_id` is NULL while `current_session_id` contains the live orchestrator. The same join is present on main `0fae4c289`. Separate session-scoped Chat-start edit controls pass.

This is not evidence that the provider actually received the edit. Unlike [#4454](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4454), the failure occurs before provider work, not after losing an accepted response.

## Acceptance / focused plan

- Gate provider work on the conversation's current owner and exact live Chat generation.
- Cover project/session scopes, project rebinding, stale generations, terminated/TUI owners, and repeated starts with SQLite-backed tests.
- Rerun the original native imported-conversation edit and subsequent TUI/Chat round trip.
- Keep screenshots and local state out of git.

title: perf(mobile): decode PTY frames with atob instead of the hand-rolled loop
body:
## Summary

`base64ToBytes` runs once per PTY frame. It pre-filtered its input by building a new string one character at a time, then accumulated into a boxed `number[]` before copying that into a `Uint8Array` — neither allocation is necessary, since the output length is known up front.

The comment that kept it that way is stale for this app:

```ts
// These helpers avoid depending on atob/btoa (not guaranteed in Hermes).
```

`lib/pairingCode.ts:32` already calls `atob` on the live pair path (reached from `app/pair.tsx:84`), so QR pairing would be broken if Hermes lacked it. The desktop renderer already does this job with `atob` plus a pre-sized `Uint8Array`, at `frontend/src/renderer/lib/terminal-mux.ts:35-42`.

Closes #4876.

## Numbers

Simulator Hermes `250829098.0.17`, one full 32 KiB frame — the daemon's PTY read buffer (`backend/internal/terminal/attachment.go:196`) — 200 iterations after warm-up. All three variants returned byte-identical output:

| variant | ms/frame | vs current |
|---|---|---|
| current | 9.84 | 1.0x |
| pre-sized `Uint8Array`, no prefilter, no atob | 3.56 | 2.8x |
| **`atob` + `charCodeAt` copy (this PR)** | **2.24** | **4.4x** |

Two corrections, because the issue's estimate was wrong and I would rather flag that than repeat it:

- #4876 quoted ~7x for the atob route, from a desktop-class Hermes CLI. On the simulator's Hermes it is 4.4x.
- **These came from a Debug bundle**, where Hermes compiles at runtime without `-O`, so read 4.4x as an upper bound. The direction is still safe: Hermes has no JIT, so optimised bytecode is still interpreted while `atob` is native. The split shows which half is at risk — old → pre-sized (2.8x) is JS-vs-JS and sensitive to compilation quality; pre-sized → atob (1.6x) is interpreted-vs-native and is not.

I did not measure a release build. Doing that properly means putting benchmark code in the app, which does not belong in this PR — say the word if you want the number before merging.

## Changes

- `base64ToBytes` → `atob` plus a pre-sized `Uint8Array`.
- `bytesToBase64` keeps its lookup table. It runs once per input event, not once per frame, so it never sees the sizes that motivate the change; switching it would mean adopting the desktop's chunked `String.fromCharCode` spread, whose argument-count limit is engine-dependent, for no gain on that path.
- Both are exported so they can be tested. `lib/mux.test.ts` is this module's first test.

## The one behaviour change

`atob` throws where the old loop silently pre-filtered. `handle` is called *outside* the `JSON.parse` guard in `ws.onmessage`, so a throw would escape the socket callback — `base64ToBytes` is therefore total, and a payload it cannot read yields an empty frame.

The daemon cannot send one: terminal output has a single encode site (`backend/internal/terminal/manager.go:449`, `base64.StdEncoding`), which structurally cannot emit whitespace or line breaks.

It drops silently because the `JSON.parse` guard directly above it is `catch { return; }`, also silent — warning here but not there would be inconsistent, and the case is unreachable from the daemon. Happy to add a `__DEV__` warn if you would rather have the breadcrumb.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on **ios and android** — CI runs only `npm ci` → typecheck → `npm test`, so nothing upstream catches a Metro-level break.
- `npx vitest run`, in a clean worktree off `main`: **787 → 802** (+15).
- **Revert test.** Restoring the old decoder (keeping the exports, so the tests still import) fails **1 of 15**: the empty-frame case. The other 14 pass on *both* implementations by design — they pin the wire contract, which must stay byte-identical. Saying so rather than implying all 15 catch the change.
- Fixtures are Go `base64.StdEncoding` output, not `bytesToBase64` output, so the encoder and its test cannot drift together unnoticed.
- **Hermes, not Node.** vitest runs on Node, which proves nothing about the shipping engine, so every `atob` case in the file was re-run on the simulator's Hermes over CDP:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| `typeof atob` | `"function"` |
| `atob("QU\nJD")`, `atob("QU JD")` | `[65,66,67]` — whitespace stripped |
| `atob("not base64!")`, `atob("QQ=")` | both throw |
| `atob("QQ")` unpadded | `[65]` |
| `atob("ABtbMzFt//5/gAo=")` | `[0,27,91,51,49,109,255,254,127,128,10]` |

## Not verified

- **iOS simulator only.** Hermes is pinned once for both platforms in this RN (`sdks/.hermesversion` → `hermes-v0.17.03`, RN 0.86.3), so the `atob` semantics are not iOS-specific — but Android was checked by `expo export`, not by running it.
- **No physical device, no release build** (above).
- **No renderer in `packages/mobile`** — 79 `*.test.ts`, zero `*.test.tsx` — so `handle`'s dispatch to `onTerminalData` is covered by reading, not by running.

title: fix(session): make interface transition status match start readiness
body:
Code: +25 −11
Tests: +93 −0
Files removed: 0

## What

Make the interface-transition status (GET) run the same native-conversation readiness check as the start (POST), so the switch control is disabled until the session can actually switch.

## Why

A fresh Claude Code TUI session has a hook-confirmed native id but no transcript on disk yet (Claude only writes it after the first prompt). GET only checked the id and said `supported: true`; POST also required durable history or positive fresh-start proof and returned 409 `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`. The UI drew an enabled switch that failed with a toast.

Fixes #4842

## How

- `backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go` — I added `handoffNativeConversationID`, which runs `nativeConversationID` then `persistedNativeConversationID`, and call it from both `InterfaceTransitionStatus` and `StartInterfaceTransition`.
- The status path now stats the provider transcript and may read the current terminal screen; it still never launches a provider process (doc comment updated).
- Review follow-up: the status path can now hit `loadProject` and `NativeConversationExists` errors that map to no reason code. Instead of failing the polled GET (which stops the client poll when it is the first load), I report `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` so the control stays disabled and the client keeps polling. POST still fails hard on those errors.
- No frontend change: `useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts:173` already polls on `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` / `NATIVE_SESSION_UNVERIFIED` and re-enables the control once the first prompt lands.

## Testing

- Added `TestInterfaceTransitionStatusBlocksReservedNativeIDWithoutHistoryOrFreshProof` (GET and POST both report missing), `TestInterfaceTransitionStatusAllowsReservedNativeIDWithUntouchedTerminalProof` (fresh handoff still allowed with untouched-terminal proof), and `TestInterfaceTransitionStatusReportsUnverifiedWhenInspectionFails` (probe error degrades GET to unverified, POST still errors).
- `go test ./backend/internal/session_manager/ ./backend/internal/httpd/controllers/ ./backend/internal/service/session/` passes; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.
- Not yet verified in the desktop app.

title: fix(reviews): stop probing every reviewer's CLI when the menu opens
body:
Fixes #5307

## What was wrong

`ReviewerSelect` prefetched a model catalog for **every** selectable reviewer harness the moment the menu opened. That read is not free: the daemon answers a cold catalog with the agent's own CLI, so a single menu-open ran the binary of all 21 reviewer harnesses — including agents the user was not choosing and had never signed in to.

For Kiro that discovery command is its **chat entrypoint**:

```go
// backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go:58
"kiro": {args: []string{"chat", "--list-models", "--format", "json"}, parser: parseJSONModels},
```

which is how picking an unrelated reviewer could pop a Kiro OAuth sign-in in the reporter's browser.

## What changed

Only the harness in effect is read up front — the trigger label needs it anyway. Each option now fetches its own catalog if and when its submenu is opened. Clicking a harness that is *not* the current one selects it outright rather than opening its submenu, so the common path needs no extra read at all.

One menu-open goes from 21 catalog reads to 1.

## Tests

New `ReviewerSelect.test.tsx` counts which agents a menu interaction reads catalogs for. Two of the four fail on `main` with exactly the reported shape:

```
× does not read a catalog for harnesses the user is not choosing
× reads a harness catalog once its own submenu is opened
  AssertionError: expected [ 'claude-code', 'codex', …(19) ] to not include 'kiro'
```

All four pass here. The other two guard the reads that *should* still happen (the harness in effect; a submenu the user deliberately opened) so this cannot be "fixed" by removing catalog reads altogether.

Also run: `npm run typecheck` clean; renderer suite `207 passed / 3203 passed`, matching `main` exactly plus the 4 added tests. The one remaining renderer failure (`GlobalSettingsForm > renders the settings sections`) reproduces on unmodified `main`.

## Scope / what this does not do

This narrows what a **passive** menu probes. It does not change what an explicitly chosen or launched agent may do — selecting Kiro as your reviewer still reads its catalog, and so may still trigger a sign-in.

Two deeper questions are left open and written up on the issue rather than guessed at here:

- Kiro's discovery command being `chat` rather than a dedicated subcommand. Fixing that needs someone who can verify `kiro-cli`'s actual surface.
- Gating discovery on the adapter's existing side-effect-free auth probe (`kiro-cli whoami`). That looked attractive but its effectiveness is unproven — [#5048](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5048) documents that probe returning `unknown` for a genuinely signed-in user, so a gate keyed on it may simply not fire.

title: fix(electron): return cancellation results for aborted browser commands
body:
## Summary
- When the Electron browser runtime link reconnects or disposes, emit `BROWSER_COMMAND_CANCELED` result frames for every accepted command (including queued per-session work) before tearing down the socket.
- Handle daemon-initiated `cancel` frames by returning a structured cancellation result instead of silently dropping the response.
- Tear down on socket `end` as well as `close`, and clear `activeCommands` before aborting controllers to avoid duplicate cancellation frames.

## Problem
If the daemon-to-Electron browser bridge dropped while a command was in flight, the frontend aborted locally but never told the daemon the command failed. The broker kept waiting on the pending request until TCP disconnect was detected or the command timed out.

## Test plan
- [x] `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/main/browser-runtime-link.test.ts` (6 tests pass)
- [ ] Verify `ao browser wait` recovers promptly after restarting the desktop app mid-command

title: fix(electron): bound browser profile data operation waits
body:
## Summary
- Add a 60s timeout (`BROWSER_PROFILE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS`) for profile clear/delete work and for browser commands waiting on that queue in `ensureSessionReady()`.
- Wrap Electron `clearStorageData` / `clearCache` with the same bound so a stuck storage call cannot hold the profile operation queue forever.
- Fail with `BROWSER_PROFILE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` instead of leaving automation hung for the session.

## Problem
Before running a browser command, the desktop app waits in a `for (;;)` loop until bound profile clear/delete operations finish. That wait had no timeout. If profile data work stalled (for example on Electron session storage APIs), `ensureSessionReady()` and every subsequent browser command for that session would wait indefinitely.

## Test plan
- [x] `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/main/browser-profile-store.test.ts` (8 tests pass, including new timeout case)
- [x] Added `browser-view-host` regression test for stuck profile-operation wait (runs in CI)
- [ ] Manually start a profile clear, simulate a hang, and confirm `ao browser snapshot` fails within ~60s with `BROWSER_PROFILE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` instead of hanging

### What went wrong?

title: fix(terminal): prevent Claude titles from becoming false drafts
body:
Code changes: +95 -1  
Tests: +141 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## Problem and fix

After a Claude Terminal reply, **TUI → Chat could fail with `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT` even though the composer was empty**.

Claude emits an OSC window-title update containing `✳` (`E2 9C B3`). AO's passive VT parser misreads the UTF-8 byte `9C` as String Terminator and paints the remaining title into the composer. The draft guard then rejects that fake text.

Strip only **OSC 0/1/2 title payloads**, introduced by either `ESC ]` or C1 `0x9D`, from passive capture. Keep escape boundaries, raw PTY replay, the visible terminal, and every draft/history guard unchanged. Real unsent drafts must still block switching. No dependency upgrade or history-recovery changes.

Closes #5301.

## C1 OSC review follow-up — `48d5cbc5f`

Addressed [the review's 8-bit OSC bypass](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5322#discussion_r3999115730). A standalone `0x9D` now enters the same title filter as `ESC ]`. UTF-8 continuation tracking also covers text outside titles, so Unicode containing that byte is not mistaken for OSC.

The new regression failed before the patch: an empty prompt became `Draft`, and a real draft was overwritten by title text. It now passes for OSC 0/1/2, BEL/7-bit ST/8-bit ST, every two-chunk split and byte-at-a-time delivery. Tests also preserve real drafts, UTF-8 text, non-title OSC examples and partial ESC/CSI cancellation.

This follow-up changes only the filter and two test files: **code +30 −19; tests +66 −5**. No dependency, renderer, raw PTY, draft-guard or history-recovery changes.

Validation at this head: full backend build, vet, non-race suite and `go test -race -p 2 -timeout=15m ./...`; focused ConPTY/Claude/terminalui race suites; 20 consecutive filter/title-regression runs; CLI E2E; pinned golangci-lint 2.12.2; and API/sqlc zero-drift checks all pass. Independent review results: **Standards: 0 actionable findings; Spec: 0 actionable findings**. **New-head CI: 11/11 passed**, including the [full backend race job](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34752514827/job/103711315496) (21m 5s total job). Local host: Go 1.26.5, macOS arm64. Docker daemon and native Linux/Windows runners are unavailable locally; the new-head remote container and all three native CLI jobs passed.

C1 evidence is a deterministic terminal-stream reproduction, not a claim that the saved Claude trace naturally emitted `0x9D`. Historical native screenshots below retain their original revisions.

## Earlier validation at `671694237`

- Regression reproduced red before the fix; empty, unsent, multiline and busy composer cases now pass.
- Streaming coverage: all two-chunk splits, byte-at-a-time UTF-8, BEL/ST/cancellation, partial ESC/CSI, and non-title OSC preservation.
- Saved native Claude 2.1.269 trace replay: idle + empty at chunk sizes 1, 7, 4096 and the full 16,039 bytes.
- Independent Standards and Spec reviews caught a partial-escape cancellation edge; fixed and re-reviewed with no remaining actionable findings.
- Local: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, golangci-lint 2.12.2, CLI E2E, frontend typecheck and API/sqlc zero-drift checks passed.
- Full backend `go test -race -p 2 -timeout=15m ./...` passed. The first unrestricted run hit two timing/concurrency failures in untouched fake-agent/catalog tests; both passed targeted reruns and the complete reduced-concurrency rerun. No unrelated test changes.
- Remote: **10/10 CI checks passed** at `671694237`, including the [full backend race suite](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/34738753583/job/103674723575) (21m 2s total job). Docker is unavailable locally; the remote fresh-install container and native macOS/Linux/Windows jobs passed.

<details>
<summary>Independent code-review results at 671694237</summary>

## Standards

No remaining actionable standards violations or baseline smells against `cadde8c9f`. Preserving OSC boundaries fixes cancellation of preceding partial ESC/CSI sequences; the rendered-state regression and focused filter/surface tests pass.

## Spec

No remaining actionable spec or correctness findings. The rendered partial ESC/CSI regressions retain the complete draft. Conpty, Claude adapter and terminalui tests pass; raw replay and draft/history gates remain unchanged.

Final totals: Standards 0; Spec 0. The earlier cancellation finding is resolved in both axes.

</details>

## Native evidence

Before: visibly empty composer rejected because title text leaked into the passive capture. Claude 2.1.269, previous QA integration; [root-cause investigation](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5301#issuecomment-5647534383).

![Before: false unsent-draft error on an empty composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1a4e4bc-718f-41dd-9cf0-5ba75c47bf49)

Fresh native verification: main `cadde8c9f` + head `671694237`, macOS arm64, Claude 2.1.270, isolated data and a local todo-app clone. Native UI actions were checked against the real daemon's transitions/history and detached host's raw/styled capture.

### 1. After: empty composer, no title text

Claude replied `C5301_TERMINAL_B` and emitted `ESC ] 0 ; ✳ C5301_CHAT_A BEL`. The visible composer **and** host capture contained only an empty prompt. No clear/discard action was used.

![After: Terminal reply finished, composer empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/738d6c70-de21-4bfb-94e9-399e730d5f79)

### 2. Strict switch succeeds

Clicked **Session actions → Switch to chat UI**. The strict/drain transition completed in 2.7s, with `C5301_TERMINAL_B` present exactly once. A subsequent Chat turn replied `C5301_CHAT_AFTER_SWITCH`. The “recovered” label is the normal imported-turn label, not an error.

![After: strict handoff imports the Terminal reply once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22092aaa-af4f-443b-a798-0709e429fbfe)

### 3. Safety control: a real draft still blocks

Typed `C5301_KEEP_THIS_UNSENT_DRAFT` in Terminal without submitting. Switching returned `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT`, retained Terminal and preserved that text. Clearing only this disposable QA draft allowed the strict switch.

![Expected rejection: real unsent draft is preserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/272b4f7d-5edd-49a9-8219-247861c76049)

### 4. Edited branch also passes

Edited the last Chat message to `C5301_EDITED_BRANCH` (branch **2/2**, reconstructed context), switched to Terminal, submitted `C5301_EDITED_TERMINAL`, then switched back strictly. Both replies appear once on the edited branch; the original suffix is absent.

![After: edited branch and its new Terminal reply survive switching](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/880c7a14-f4fe-45a3-b8ae-3c0683782c5d)

### 5. Codex control passes

Codex 0.153.4: Chat → Terminal, send `X5301_TERMINAL_B`, strict Terminal → Chat. The original `X5301_CHAT_A` and new Terminal reply are present exactly once (four messages total).

![Codex: original and new Terminal reply imported once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36261831-9030-4f0a-9592-600c75724269)

### Separate history failure — verified with companion #4466

**Original observation, this capture-only PR on main:** selecting the original branch and immediately returning TUI → Chat passed the empty-composer gate but failed later with `TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED: context deadline exceeded` after 46s. AO restored Terminal. The screenshot below records that failure, not a pass.

Read-only DB evidence matched the original provider IDs, but the hook checkpoint still contained the edited branch's `C5301_EDITED_TERMINAL`. **September 13 follow-up: verified with #4466 included**, alongside #5302 and this PR, at local integration `79bba1e6c` on fetched main `cadde8c9f`. The old poisoned session requires explicit provider-history recovery once. After a new edited-branch Terminal turn, the original-branch Chat → TUI → Chat return passes strictly in **3.30s**, repeated in **4.16s**, without another prompt or bypass. Original history is retained once, edited suffix absent, and a new Chat reply completes.

#4466 already clears outgoing hook checkpoints on Chat → TUI; its new regression `c55c17e09` catches removal of that reset. **No history logic was added to this capture-only PR.** [Before/after screenshots and exact validation](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4466#september-13--original-branch-return-verified).

![Remaining failure: original branch hits history settling, not draft detection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58013d41-7362-47e5-8631-627ab5a1d121)

Screenshots, raw traces and QA state are attachments/local files, never committed. This does not address the separate Claude busy-stop history mismatch or native conversation-ID conflicts.

```
typescript
{
```

title: fix(chat): keep controllers registered until StopAll detach finishes
body:
## Summary
- During daemon shutdown, `StopAll` now holds each session's controller gate and keeps registry entries until the controller's event stream actually ends.

## Problem
`StopAll` removed chat controllers from the in-memory registry before their detach/close completed and did not take the per-session controller gate. A concurrent `Start` could observe an empty registry while the old controller was still shutting down and create a second writer for the same session.

title: fix(frontend): offer merge when the provider requires no review
body: ## What In a repository that does not require reviews, a PR authored and reviewed from the same GitHub account showed **Review pending** and **Not mergeable yet** in the session inspector, and AO hid the Merge action. The PR card now reads **No review required**, reports the PR as **Mergeable**, and offers **Merge**, which is what the daemon's merge gate already allowed. ## Why Fixes #4935. GitHub never records a self-review as `APPROVED`, so in a single-user repository the review decision stays empty (`reviewDecision: ""`), which AO stores as `none`. `none` means GitHub requires no review: a branch protection rule or ruleset that requires one makes GitHub return `REVIEW_REQUIRED` and `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` instead. The daemon already treats `none` as satisfied. `domain.MergeReadiness.ReadyToMerge`, which `POST /api/v1/prs/{id}/merge` checks against a fresh fetch, only blocks on requested changes, unresolved human comments, CI and provider mergeability. The renderer did not: - `SessionInspector` offered Merge only for `review.decision === "approved"`. - `prCardPresentation` labelled a PR Mergeable only when approved, otherwise "A required review must be completed before this PR can merge." - `reviewStatusDetail` fell through to **Review pending** for `none`. The "Review pending" in the report is that renderer string, not the backend `review_pending` session status, which only `review_required` produces. ## How - **One rule for the label and the button.** `prCanMerge()` in `lib/pr-display.ts` mirrors `ReadyToMerge`: open, checks passing, provider mergeability `mergeable`, review decision `approved` or `none`, and no unresolved human review comments. `prCardPresentation` and `SessionInspector` both use it. - **`none` reads "No review required"** (new `pr.review.notRequired`, all 8 locales). - **Two consequences of sharing the rule**, both matching what the daemon already enforces: - An approved PR the provider reports as `blocked` or `unstable` is no longer labelled Mergeable. The detail reuses `pr.merge.providerBlocked`. - A PR with unresolved human review threads no longer shows Merge; clicking it used to fail with `PR_PRECONDITIONS_UNMET`. This matters for #4935 specifically: the AO reviewer posts inline comments from the author's own account, so they count as human. The reason is a new `pr.merge.reasonComments`, kept in English in every locale like the other `pr.merge.reason*` strings. - **No backend behaviour change.** `TestActionServiceMerge_MergesAPRThatNeedsNoReview` pins the daemon side so the two cannot drift apart. **Scope.** This does not treat AO's own review verdict as an approval and does not relax any provider blocker. #2073 was closed on the basis that AO should keep respecting required reviews and merge blockers; this change only acts where GitHub itself reports that no review is required. ### Intentional omissions Found while tracing #4935; each is a separate problem: - **`ao pr merge ` cannot succeed.** The CLI posts `{}`, and since #3599 the merge endpoint rejects a body without `prUrl` and `expectedHeadSha` with 400 `INVALID_PR`. That, not an approval check, is why the CLI refused in the report. Fixing it means deciding how the CLI supplies the head SHA it expects to merge. - **A repository with no CI checks never becomes mergeable in AO.** With no status rollup the CI state is `unknown`, which both the card and `ReadyToMerge` treat as a blocker. If the reporter's repository has no workflows at all, this PR alone does not unblock them. - **AO's own inline review comments count as human comments.** `review_comments` in `pr.sql` lacks the `review_run` exclusion that `external_comments` has, so they block merge until resolved. - **Existing copy left as is:** `pr.merge.reasonConflict` says "One approval is sufficient…" whatever the review requirement. ## Testing ### Before and after The same PR state in both: open, checks passing, GitHub mergeable, no review decision. These are the real Session inspector rendered in the renderer harness (`dev:web` with `installFakeAgent`), with the PR summary served for a placeholder `acme/notes-app#7`, not a live GitHub PR. None of the commits on `main` since the before capture touch the PR card. | Before (`main`) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | | | | | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Review status | Review pending | **No review required** | | Readiness | Not mergeable yet: "A required review must be completed before this PR can merge." | **Mergeable**: "No merge conflict, checks are passing, and the review requirement is satisfied." | | Merge button | Hidden | **Shown** | ### New tests Each renderer test below failed before its change. - `pr-display.test.ts`: a `none` PR is Mergeable and reads "No review required"; `blocked` and `unstable` PRs are not Mergeable; `approved` and `none` PRs with unresolved human comments are not Mergeable. `review_required` and `changes_requested` stay not Mergeable (these passed before too and guard the rule). - `SessionInspector.test.tsx`: Merge is offered for a `none` PR without "Review pending"; not offered for `review_required`, `changes_requested`, or unresolved human comments. - `action_service_test.go`: the daemon merges a PR whose decision is `none` with only a `COMMENTED` review (passes on `main` too; it pins existing behaviour). ### CI jobs run locally Run on `f79eca38c`, rebased onto `cadde8c9f`. - **Go** (`golang:1.25.7` container, `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` resolving to go1.26.5 as `go.work` requires): gofmt, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean. `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...`: 167 packages ok, including `internal/service/pr`. 2 packages failed, neither touched here, both explained by the container rather than this change: - `internal/mobilebridge` write-failure tests: the run was as root, which ignores the read-only permissions they rely on. body:
## What

The cloud fixes that are deployed and tested on the staging control plane (task-def :102) but were not part of #5023. This lands exactly the deployed CP state on top of #5023.

## Commits (all cloud/ or cloud-gated frontend)

- perf(cloud): launch preinstalled Coder worker, plus make the Coder harness link idempotent (was PR #4795, cherry-picked here).
- fix(cloud): stage the non-empty-workspace checkout inside the workspace (coder checkout-permission fix).
- fix(cloud): three coder UX fixes (terminal reconnect storm, empty-repo race, report fan-in) plus migration 00037 (allow queued fan-in turns).
- fix(cloud): state-driven cloud terminal attach (remove SSE-wait and timeout hacks), plus two earlier terminal iterations that net into it.
- fix(cloud-worker): boot the agent PTY at 80x24 instead of 120x40 so the intro banner never garbles.
- fix(cloud): close a superseded epoch's terminals at retire so stale terminals reconnect state-driven, with no liveness poll.
- fix(cloud): orchestrator inspects before spawn; workers report tersely (see Orchestration fixes below).

## Orchestration fixes (from a live 10-worker run on project l-a, lottie-android)

Two agent-guidance bugs surfaced by the run, fixed in the orchestrator/worker system prompts and the using-ao skill (both compile into ao-worker):

1. Inspect before spawn. The orchestrator invented file names when decomposing a task, so two workers were handed paths that do not exist in the repo (AnimationValueCallback.java, PathInterpolator.java) and blocked with no PR. The orchestrator prompt now requires confirming a file, class, or path exists in the checkout before naming it in a worker prompt.

2. Terse worker reports. Worker ao report messages were multi-paragraph, so a long one landed in the orchestrator conversation looking like an injected prompt. Reports are now constrained to one or two sentences (outcome plus PR number, or the single blocking reason) with no diffs, logs, or file contents.

command_test asserts both rules. Neither touches local-app behavior.

## Testing

Deployed on staging as ao-cloud-staging-api:102 and exercised end to end (coder + nodeops). cloud module gofmt, build, vet, and test are green; no cloud-client codegen drift. The orchestration fixes ride the ao-worker binary, so a CP redeploy propagates them to workers via self-update.

## Notes

- Adds migration 00037.
- Supersedes #4795, which should be closed (its commits are included here).
- All changes are cloud path or cloud-gated; no local-app behavior change.

Follow-up to #5023.


## Resume reliability fixes (added)

Four cloud resume/terminal reliability fixes, cherry-picked as clean commits:

1. Restore terminal 410 (TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED) handling in the state-driven mux. The state-driven redesign dropped it, so an exited-agent 410 looped the ticket mint (stuck "Connecting"). This restores it.
2. Auto-rebake the coder workspace image on deploy, so the baked ao-worker SHA always matches the control plane and resumes skip the slow PTY upload.
3. Coder HTTP self-heal on a preinstalled-worker miss: fetch the correct worker over HTTP before falling back to the slow PTY upload.
4. Keep a resuming coder box alive through an idle-stop race, so a slow restore is not idle-killed mid bring-up.

Note: the backend false-positive 410 fix is a separate PR (#5477) because it corrects #5350 code that lives in main, not in this branch.

title: bug(docs-site): download page shows Intel button on Apple Silicon Macs
body:
## Bug

On an Apple Silicon Mac the download page's main Desktop button says "Download for macOS (Intel)" and links the x64 dmg. Wrong file for the machine, and the label makes M-series users think there is no native build.

**Source:** [Discord #bug-triage](https://discord.com/channels/1476302178913357958/1491735678156013588/1548657412125491401) | **Reported by:** @somewherelostt | **Analyzed against:** `a33d1ac40`
**Confidence:** High on the code path, Medium on the exact trigger (reporter's browser unknown)

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/main/.issue-assets/download-page-intel-mseries/maaz-download-page.jpeg)

## Reproduction

1. Open the download page on an M-series Mac.
2. The Desktop card button reads "Download for macOS (Intel)" and downloads `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.dmg`.
3. The correct "Mac (Apple silicon)" dmg is only listed further down under Stable.

## Root cause

`detectMacArch()` in `frontend/src/landing/src/app/hooks/useOS/useOS.ts` picks the arch from one signal: the WebGL `UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL` string. No "apple" in it means the Mac gets classified Intel.

That fails on Apple Silicon whenever the GPU string is missing or masked: Safari with locked-down settings, some privacy extensions, or software rendering. Each of those shows an Intel button on M-series hardware. The fallback direction is also backwards for this audience: when in doubt, arm64 is the safer guess.

## Fix

Treat the WebGL string as a hint, not proof. Add a second signal, e.g. `navigator.userAgentData` high-entropy `architecture` in Chromium or a WebAssembly feature probe, and default to Apple Silicon when signals disagree or are missing. Also consider showing both Mac downloads instead of one best-guess button, so a misdetection can never hand a user the wrong dmg.

## Impact

M-series users get pointed at the x64 dmg, which needs Rosetta or fails to make sense at install time. First impression is "no native build for my Mac".

title: feat(chat): support /compact for Claude Code and ACP providers
body:
## What

Implements `/compact` in Chat UI for Claude Code and all ACP-based providers (`claudeacp`, `cursoracp`, `opencodeacp`, etc.) using the official Agent Client Protocol (ACP) session compaction specification.

## Why

Compaction was previously only available for Codex via its private JSON-RPC method (`thread/compact/start`). For Claude Code and other ACP agents, `/compact` was unavailable in Chat UI.

## How

- **Capability Negotiation**: Negotiates `session.compaction: {}` under `ClientCapabilities.Meta` during ACP initialization per the official ACP Session Compaction specification.
- **Provider Capability Exposure**:
  - `claudeacp` advertises `ports.ChatCapabilityCompaction: true` so the Chat UI exposes the `/compact` command.
  - Generic `acp` driver dynamically enables `ports.ChatCapabilityCompaction: true` when any ACP agent advertises the `compact` available command.
- **Managed Compaction Turn**:
  - Implements `ports.ChatCompactor` on `*conversation`.
  - Dispatches `/compact` asynchronously as a managed prompt turn.
  - Suppresses intermediate `agent_message_chunk` and `agent_thought_chunk` deltas during the compaction turn so the timeline does not get polluted with raw assistant chatter.
  - Calculates token reclaim metrics (`tokensBefore`, `tokensAfter`, `tokensReclaimed`, `contextWindow`) from usage updates and emits `ports.ChatEventCompacted`.

title: feat(onboarding): infer worker and orchestrator defaults from role-specific usage
body:
Fixes #4493.

## Problem
New-project onboarding computed one generic authorized-agent default and assigned it to both Worker and Orchestrator, ignoring role-specific session history. Both fields commonly opened as Claude Code.

## Root cause
The sheet only consulted the agent-readiness catalog. It had no role-filtered usage signal, so both untouched fields received the same catalog-priority result.

## Fix
- Subscribe the sheet to the shared workspace query while open and flatten local session history (this sheet creates local projects only; cloud uses CloudProjectCard).
- Rank eligible agents independently per role by usage count in the last 48 hours (ROLE_HISTORY_WINDOW_MS), then newest matching session, then the existing Claude Code-first priority order. A heavy harness from months ago can no longer outvote current habits; undated sessions are excluded since their age is unknown.
- Role matching reuses isOrchestratorSession, so legacy -orchestrator ids and kind-less sessions behave exactly like the board. Its parameter is widened to a Pick; no caller changes.
- Touched-field protection is unchanged: async refreshes never overwrite a manual selection.
- Removes the now-unused single-default defaultAuthorizedAgent.

## Safety
- Suggestion-only; saved project configuration and session history are untouched.
- Unavailable historical harnesses are never selected; empty or stale history falls back to Claude Code, or the next authorized agent when Claude Code is unavailable.

title: feat(cloud): relay terminal traffic to workers
body:
## What

Implement the Docker-local version of the cloud terminal relay architecture.

Terminal traffic now uses a live relay path between the Electron client and the worker’s outbound terminal stream, while preserving an asynchronous durable mirror in the control plane/Postgres. The change also distinguishes an exited coding-agent terminal from a worker that is still provisioning.

## Why

The existing cloud terminal path made the control plane’s durable transport the synchronous data path for every keystroke and output frame. This added avoidable latency and made terminal responsiveness dependent on the queued transport path.

It also treated an exited agent terminal the same as a cold worker. The UI therefore retried indefinitely on an old/exited session and remained stuck on “Connecting…”.

## How

- Add a feature-flagged terminal relay fast path:
  - Electron → control-plane terminal relay → worker outbound stream → PTY → coding agent.
  - Worker output is delivered live to the connected browser, then mirrored asynchronously into Postgres for replay and audit.
  - Sequence numbers preserve byte ordering between live relay frames and durable replay.
  - Existing durable/Postgres transport remains as the fallback path.
- Add relay diagnostics for forwarded input, delivered output, and asynchronous mirroring.
- Add a stable terminal routing key to ticket responses for future affinity-aware deployment.
- Keep the relay embedded in the control-plane process for now. This validates the architecture locally without introducing a separate relay service or changing existing production routing.
- Return `410 TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED` for an agent terminal that has already finished, rather than returning retryable worker-unavailable state.
- Stop the frontend retry loop for exited terminals and show a clear terminal error instead.
- Retain retry behavior for genuine cold-start/provisioning cases (`409 WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`).

title: chore(mobile): build preview APKs for ARM only
body:
## Summary

The `preview` profile builds a universal APK with all four ABIs. This narrows it to the two its installs run, `armeabi-v7a` and `arm64-v8a`, without moving the OTA runtime version. That makes each APK about 49 MB (40.7%) smaller.

- **`production`** is unchanged: it builds an app bundle, and Play splits that per device.
- **`development`** is left as it is. It sets `developmentClient: true`, but this package does not depend on `expo-dev-client` (`packages/mobile/README.md`), so that profile does not produce a dev client today. Narrowing it can wait until it is buildable.

Closes #4879.

## How

`eas.json` sets `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures` under `preview.android.env`. Gradle reads `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_*` environment variables as project properties. React Native's plugin reads `reactNativeArchitectures` (`ProjectUtils.kt:102-110`) into `defaultConfig.ndk.abiFilters` (`NdkConfiguratorUtils.kt:58-62`), which filters every packaged `.so`, prebuilt ones included, unless ABI splits are enabled.

On the EAS side, eas-cli 22.6.0 reads `eas.json` from the project directory (`@expo/eas-json` `accessor.js:99`), merges the platform `env` over the profile's (`resolver.js:48-51`), and copies it into the job's builder environment (`build/android/prepareJob.js:58-60`).

This is neither of the two routes the issue proposed:

- **`expo-build-properties.buildArchs` in `app.json`** would move the runtime version. `fingerprint.config.js` ignores `eas.json` but not `app.json`, so that change would have to land at a native-release boundary.
- **A `gradleCommand`** means naming the Gradle task EAS would otherwise pick, and the eas.json reference documents it as a task, not a place for arguments. An environment variable applies to whichever task runs.

## After merge, on the publishing machine

`eas.json` is `skip-worktree` there, because it holds local App Store Connect submit credentials (README, "`eas.json` is `skip-worktree`"). Two consequences:

1. A `git pull` that includes this change aborts with "Your local changes … would be overwritten", and `git stash` reports nothing to save while the bit is set.
2. eas-cli builds the job environment from the on-disk file, so the local copy has to carry the new `env` block before the next `eas build --profile preview`.

Both are handled by merging the change into the local file:

```sh
git update-index --no-skip-worktree packages/mobile/eas.json
git stash && git pull && git stash pop   # local edits are in `submit`, this change is in `build`
git update-index --skip-worktree packages/mobile/eas.json
```

## Numbers

Local `assembleRelease` on the same prebuilt tree, three builds varying only the environment variable:

| Build | APK bytes | vs. all four | Native libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| all four (today) | 121,309,407 | — | arm64-v8a 22,649,424 · armeabi-v7a 15,481,612 · x86 24,886,732 · x86_64 24,095,352 |
| without x86 | 96,207,418 | −25,101,989 (−20.7%) | the other three unchanged in size |
| **`preview` (this PR)** | **71,937,128** | **−49,372,279 (−40.7%)** | ARM only, both unchanged in size |

The libraries are stored uncompressed, so they cost install size as well as download.

## Verification

- **Runtime version unchanged.** `npx expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve` gives `android 8290ea0d05c8…` / `ios ad3999c715b0…` on `main`, with the `eas.json` change, and with the variable set in the environment.
- **The ARM-only APK runs.** Installed on an arm64-v8a emulator (API 36 image): `primaryCpuAbi=arm64-v8a`, `am start -W` reports 1,740 ms and the onboarding screen renders, and logcat shows no `UnsatisfiedLinkError` or `dlopen` failure from the app.
- No JS changes, so there is nothing for typecheck, vitest or `expo export` to see.

## Not verified

- **No EAS build.** I have no EAS access. The eas-cli path above was read in its source; that the EAS worker hands the builder environment to Gradle is from the eas.json reference, not observed. The numbers are from local builds.
- **No x86_64 emulator.** The only emulator image on this machine is arm64-v8a. On an x86_64 image, a `preview` APK now relies on ARM translation, which Google added to its Android 11 emulator images; where an image lacks it, install fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS`. Keeping `x86_64` in `preview` would cost the 24.1 MB back.
- **No 32-bit ARM device.**

title: fix(mobile): ask the daemon about a session the board does not list
body:
## Summary

`app/session/[id].tsx` looked an id up in the board's two cached lists and, on a miss, refreshed those same lists and then said "Session not found." It never asked the daemon about the id itself.

Those lists do not hold every session. `getSessions` keeps one orchestrator per project (`bestByProject`: the first live one in session-number order, else the newest), so every other orchestrator is dropped, and a `needs_input` notification from one still routes to `/session/:id` (`notificationTarget`). The same screen also said "not found" when the refresh never reached the daemon.

Closes #4844.

## What changes

On a miss, the route asks `GET /sessions/{id}` and shows what the daemon said:

| State | Screen |
|---|---|
| no machine paired | the board's own "No desktop paired" state (checked before the lists, which still hold a forgotten machine's sessions) |
| listed on the board | the session, as before |
| found, terminated | This session has ended |
| found, live | the session, from the lookup |
| 404 / 410 | Session not found |
| board not connected, no answer yet | "Not connected to your desktop", with Open board |
| board connected, lookup failed | "Couldn't load this session", with Retry |

The rules are pure and tested in `lib/session/sessionRoute.ts`: `sessionRouteView` decides the screen and `sessionLookupDue` decides when to ask. `lookUpSession` (`lib/session/sessionLookup.ts`) is the request itself, and the route only wires them together.

**When it asks.** Only while the board's own poll holds an open connection to this machine. The store sets `open` only after a tick succeeds with the current password, and on a rejected one it leaves `closed` and stops polling. So a rotated password costs this screen no auth attempts: it never adds to the daemon's five-failure lockout, the trap `getSessions` probes `/sessions` first to avoid. A lookup that failed is asked again when the board reconnects. An answer the daemon gave (found, or 404/410) is never asked again. In the render where the paired machine changes, `connection` still describes the previous machine, because the store restarts its poll from an effect that runs after the route's. `machineChanged` skips that render.

**Not diagnosing the link twice.** While the board is disconnected the route sends nothing and points at the board. The board already tells a rotated tunnel from a rejected password from an unreachable machine (`tunnelMayHaveRotated`), and a second copy of that rule in the route would drift. #5349 rewrites the board, so extracting that logic into a shared helper now would conflict with it.

**Why an ended session is reported, not opened.** The session screens restore an ended session from their banner. A restored old orchestrator would be the first live one in session-number order. That is the one `bestByProject` keeps for the phone, and the one the daemon names as orchestrator in new workers' prompts (`activeOrchestratorSessionID` in `session_manager/manager.go`), so it would displace the orchestrator that replaced it.

**One extraction.** "404 or 410 means the session is gone" already existed as `interfaceTransitionSessionGone`. It moves to `connectionError.ts` as `isSessionGone`, so the route and the interface-transition scheduler read one rule. Its comment moved to the call site; the scheduler is unchanged.

`TerminalSessionScreen` takes the resolved session as a fallback for `known`, so a live unlisted TUI session gets its `terminalHandleId`. The board's lists still win whenever they hold the id.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on ios and android.
- `npx vitest run`: **789 → 830** (+41).
- **Mutation checks**, each fails at least one test: the old rule (unlisted means not found) fails 18. Asking while `closed` fails 1. Dropping the machine-change guard fails 1. Checking the lists before the paired state fails 1. Showing a retry instead of "not connected" while the board is down fails 6. Mapping every request error to 404 fails 1.
- **Fixtures.** The orchestrator records are copied from a daemon built from `main` (`dc93038d1`): project `scratch` has two orchestrators, the first terminated. The `/sessions` mock is trimmed to those two, and the 404 body is the daemon's with its `requestId` renamed. The first test asserts the precondition, `board.orchestrators` is `["scratch-2"]`, before looking up `scratch-1`. The third uses a `TypeError("Network request failed")` rejection.
- **Simulator, iOS Debug build, dev daemon from `main`.** Navigation was driven through expo-router over the Hermes debugger. Request counts are from the daemon's HTTP log.

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| open replaced orchestrator `scratch-1` | "Session not found.", 0 requests for it | "This session has ended", 1 `GET` → 200 |
| open `no-such-session` | — | "Session not found", 1 `GET` → 404 |
| open listed `scratch-2` | chat screen | chat screen, 0 requests for it |
| board not connected, open `scratch-1` | — | "Not connected to your desktop", with Open board |

## Not verified

- **Request counts while the board is disconnected were not measured on device.** The rule ("never asks while the board is `closed` or `connecting`") is covered by the tests and mutation checks above. I could not reliably get a rejected password to reach the dev daemon from the simulator, so I did not count those requests.
- **No renderer in `packages/mobile`** (zero `*.test.tsx`), so the route's effect wiring is covered by the device rows above, not by a test.
- **A session opened from the lookup is not refreshed.** The board's poll refreshes listed sessions, but nothing re-fetches a looked-up one. The only live session that reaches this path is a second live orchestrator the board dropped, or one fetched moments before the board lists it. For that second orchestrator, a Chat/TUI switch or a kill is not reflected until the screen is reopened. Neither live-unlisted case, nor a TUI session through the `TerminalSessionScreen` fallback, was exercised on device.
- **Cold start from a notification tap** was reasoned through against `store.tsx` (`connection` starts `closed`, and `loading` is true until the first tick), not run.
- **The restore hazard above is read from the code:** I did not restore a replaced orchestrator.
- **Android** was checked by `expo export`, not run.

The fix for #4878 adds one line at the end of this route file. I test-applied both changes on `main` in each order: no conflict, identical result.

title: fix(mobile): show a fallback instead of terminating when a screen throws
body:
## Summary

No route in `packages/mobile` exports an `ErrorBoundary`, and expo-router only installs one where a route opts in, so a render-time throw on any screen terminates the app. This adds two fallbacks and installs them on every route that is only reached by navigating, except five that #5349 is changing:

- `RouteErrorBoundary`, for screens: **Try again**, plus **Go to board** when there is nothing to go back to.
- `SheetErrorBoundary`, for sheets: **Close** only.

Part of #4878: the five routes #5349 changes (below) still need the same line once it lands.

## Where a boundary must not go

The issue's constraint decides the placement. expo-updates takes a launch's first content as proof the launch worked: `ErrorRecovery.handleContentDidAppear` (`ErrorRecovery.swift:306`; Android `ErrorRecoveryHandler.kt:76`) marks the launched update successful and keeps only `waitForRemoteUpdate` and `crash` in its recovery pipeline, dropping `launchNew` and `launchCached`. A fallback rendered as that first content would record a broken over-the-air update as a good launch that can never roll back.

So the four routes that can render first content get none:

- `app/_layout.tsx`, `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` and `app/(tabs)/index.tsx`, which every normal launch renders.
- `app/pair.tsx`. The desktop's pairing QR is `aomobile://pair#…` (`ConnectMobileContent.tsx:148`), so scanning it with the system camera cold-starts the app straight into it.

Every other route is reached by navigating from content that has already appeared: `OnboardingGate` replaces to `/onboarding` from an effect, and `PushManager` navigates a cold-start notification tap only once navigation is ready. By then rollback is already off, so the choice is only between a fallback and a crash. A fixed update still arrives either way: `checkAutomatically` is `ON_LOAD`, and `UpdatesManager` checks again on a resume after `MIN_BACKGROUND_MS`.

**Residual exposure, stated rather than hidden:** expo-router maps every file route to an `aomobile://` URL. A hand-made link could cold-start straight into a covered route, and if that route threw on its first render, the fallback would be first content. Nothing AO produces links anywhere but `pair`; push payloads carry no URL and are routed after navigation is ready.

## Why two fallbacks

- **Sheets close instead of retrying.** A sheet's opener parks a callback that the route releases on unmount (`sheetResult.ts`; for example `useEffect(() => () => releaseSheetResult(resultKey), …)` in `sheets/model.tsx`). A throw unmounts the route, so an in-place retry would bring back a sheet whose choice goes nowhere. Opening it again parks a fresh one. One side effect to know about: `sheets/store-update.tsx` reports `dismiss` from that same cleanup, so a throw there counts as a dismissal.
- **Screens with nothing to go back to get Go to board.** `onboarding` is entered with `router.replace`, with no header and gestures off, so "go back" would name an action that does not exist. The fallback checks `router.canGoBack()`, the same rule as `MinimalBackButton`.

Both call `haptics.error()` each time they show, so a Try again that throws again is not a silent no-op. Both report through `captureMobileException` with `category: "render_crash"` and `operation: "react_render"`, the category and operation the desktop's boundary ends up with (`telemetry.ts:808` maps its `react-error-boundary` source to `render_crash`). That report is a no-op until the Sentry SDK is installed (`loadSdk()` returns `null`). The screen fallback also clears `headerRight`, because header options outlive the route in the navigator; preview's Reload button would otherwise stay over the fallback and act on nothing. A successful retry remounts the route, which sets its own header again.

## Routes

- **Screens:** `onboarding`, `session/[id]`, `shell/[handleId]`, `preview/[id]`.
- **Sheets:** all nine under `app/sheets/`.
- **Deferred:** `(tabs)/prs`, `(tabs)/orchestrator`, `(tabs)/settings`, `notifications` and `spawn`. #5349 deletes `(tabs)/orchestrator.tsx` and `(tabs)/settings.tsx` (Settings becomes `app/settings.tsx`) and changes `prs.tsx`, `notifications.tsx` and `spawn.tsx` through their last lines. It also adds `(tabs)/projects.tsx`, `project/[id].tsx`, `settings.tsx`, `sheets/conversation-actions.tsx` and `sheets/conversation-rename.tsx`.

`RouteErrorBoundary.test.ts` lists every file under `app/` and fails unless each one is on exactly one list: launch, screen, sheet or deferred. It also fails if a launch route mentions `Boundary`, `componentDidCatch` or `getDerivedStateFromError`, which catches a hand-written class boundary around the layout as well as expo-router's export and `screenErrorBoundary`. **For #5349:** once this is on `main`, that PR's five new routes fail this test until each is placed, and the deferred five should move to the screen list at the same time.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on ios and android.
- `npx vitest run`: **789 → 807** (+18).
- **Mutation checks**, each fails one test: an unplaced new route under `app/sheets/`, a sheet given the retry fallback, and a `TelemetryBoundary` import added to `app/_layout.tsx`.
- **Simulator, iOS Debug build.** I added a temporary `throw` behind a global flag to `session/[id]` and `sheets/theme`, drove navigation over the Hermes debugger, and removed the throws afterwards. Buttons were pressed by calling their `onPress` through the React tree, since taps do not reach the simulator.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| throw on the pushed session screen | fallback, header back button intact; the component stack shows expo-router's `Try` above the route |
| flag cleared, Try again (run before the header and Go to board changes to the fallback) | the session's chat screen renders |
| throw in a sheet | "This sheet hit an unexpected error" on the sheet's surface; Close dismisses the sheet |
| throw on a session screen replaced into the stack (`canGoBack` false) | Try again and Go to board |

In a Debug build LogBox also shows the error over the fallback; each result above was read after dismissing it.

## Not verified

- **No Release build.** Try's only `__DEV__` branch lets a `MetroServerError` through to LogBox (`Try.js:45-53`), so a Release build should take the same path, but I did not run one.
- **Launch-time rollback was not exercised**, because none of the four launch routes changed, and the test fails if one ever gets a boundary.
- **Go to board was seen, not pressed**; onboarding's own fallback was not triggered (it needs an unpaired first launch). A throw after a sheet had mounted (data arriving later) was not triggered either; it takes the same Close path.
- **Android** was checked by `expo export`, not run. The haptic was not felt (simulator).

The fix for #4844 rewrites `app/session/[id].tsx`, where this adds one line at the end. I test-applied both changes on `main` in each order: no conflict, identical result.

title: fix(app): keep sidebar order stable on restart and keep the app visible during update
body:
Fixes two things users see on the desktop app.

## 1. Sidebar reordered itself after launch

On restart the backend re-hosts saved sessions and was stamping their `updated_at`/`last_activity_at` to "now" in worker-pool order. The sidebar sorts newest-updated first, so the list visibly reshuffled after first paint even though the user changed nothing.

This adds a lifecycle path (`MarkSpawnedRestored`) that preserves a re-hosted session's existing sort timestamps, and routes the restore relaunch through it. Genuine user actions still bump to "now" and still reorder. The renderer-side animation suppression that hides startup churn already landed on main; this is the root-cause backend fix that stops the reorder from happening at all.

## 2. Updating the app left it looking closed for up to a minute

There is no single 60s timeout. The gap is stacked waits, and the largest piece (the OS-level bundle/installer swap) is native to the updater and not reducible by us. What this PR fixes is that the app showed nothing during that window and the new backend was slow to come back:

- Instant paint: a static splash inside `index.html` removes the blank frame before React mounts, on every OS and on both cold and post-update launch.
- "Updating / Restarting AO" copy: a cross-platform post-update marker (`update-relaunch-flag`) lets the loader tell the user an update is in progress instead of a generic "connecting" (previously only macOS knew). New i18n strings across all locales.
- macOS helper: presents its window on the normal close/install path so the swap window is not blank.
- Backend boot trimmed: agent-readiness warming (~24 subprocess probes) is moved off the synchronous boot critical path into the post-ready callback, reducing contention with the port-gating work. Safety fences are untouched and still run before the port binds.

## 3. Boot robustness

Terminal handoff artifact cleanup on boot is made non-fatal (logs a warning instead of failing startup); it is best-effort maintenance, not a safety invariant.

## Verification

- Backend: `gofmt`/`build`/`vet` clean; `lifecycle`, `session_manager`, `daemon` suites pass. New tests cover timestamp preservation and non-fatal cleanup.
- Frontend: `typecheck` passes.
- Update timing across OSes is validated by reading the code paths and simulating the post-update marker, not by a live packaged update per OS (that needs a packaged build and a real release channel, which cannot be exercised from a dev checkout).

## Out of scope

Keeping the daemon alive across the update (removes the backend re-boot but touches supervisor lifecycle and SQLite single-owner guarantees) and reducing the native OS installer swap (not reducible by us).
