title: fix/5365: Agents peer of Projects
body:
## Summary

- The standalone agent workspace rendered as a trailing "Ad hoc agents" **project row** and only appeared when projectless sessions existed, so it read as a leftover project rather than a first-class sidebar section.
- Rename the synthetic workspace to "Agents" and always include it in the workspace model so the section is durable even when it has no sessions.
- Render an "Agents" section as a peer of "Projects" with its own "New agent" header action and empty state, and exclude it from project reorder drag & drop.
- Count only real projects when gating the board's first-launch welcome/import state so the durable empty Agents workspace cannot make an empty board look populated.
- Expose both peer section labels as level-2 headings so the regrouped sidebar stays navigable for screen readers, and add `shell.agents`, `shell.newAgent` and `shell.agentsEmpty` to all locales.

Part of #5365. Also hides SCM/PR controls for standalone sessions.

## SessionInspector: capability-driven summary

Standalone sessions live in the durable Agents section and have no project repository or workspace, so the Summary view should not render pull-request cards, PR timeline events, or SCM status pills for them.

- Add `sessionCanHavePullRequests(session)` and `isStandaloneSession(session)` helpers in `SessionInspector.tsx`.
- Gate the PR section, PR timeline rows, and SCM pills on the capability check instead of only on `prSummaries.length`.
- Make `SessionInspectorSummaryView` `pullRequestCards`/`pullRequestTitle` optional in `@aoagents/product-ui` so the section can be omitted.
- Assert standalone, orchestrator, workspace-worker, and project-worker capability visibility in `SessionInspector` tests.
- Add `inspector.timeline.createdStandaloneSession` for the standalone timeline label.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh data dir → create a standalone agent session → return to sidebar → "Agents" is a peer section of "Projects", above or below it, not a trailing ad hoc row under "Projects".
- [ ] Empty data dir → sidebar shows "Projects" + "Agents" (empty "No agents yet" state + "New agent" header action); board first-launch welcome/import state still opens for a brand-new install.
- [ ] Drag/drop reorder test in sidebar: Agents section is not a reorderable project row.
- [ ] Standalone session inspector: no PR card, no PR timeline events, no SCM pills, shows "Created standalone session" activity entry.
- [ ] Orchestrator session inspector: no PR controls.
- [ ] Project/Workspace worker session inspector: PR controls and SCM pills remain visible.
- [ ] All touched test files pass: `useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx`, `Sidebar.test.tsx`, `SessionsBoard.tsx` consumers, `ShellTopbar.test.tsx`, `SessionInspector.test.tsx`, `_shell-index-home.test.tsx`.
- [ ] Locale files: `shell.agents`, `shell.newAgent`, `shell.agentsEmpty`, `inspector.timeline.createdStandaloneSession` present in en/de/es/fr/ja/ko/pt-BR/zh-CN.

## Manual parity proof for Vitus/Windows

Reproduced the same bug on `upstream/main` before this branch, and the fix is platform-neutral:

- `useWorkspaceQuery` grouping, `Sidebar` section rendering, and `SessionsBoard` demo-workspace selection have no `isMac/isWindows/darwin/win32` guards around the standalone workspace path.
- `lib/platform.ts` and `Sidebar` platform branches only affect topbar visibility, logo span, and shortcut join character — not workspace sectioning.
- So Windows and Vitus get the same peer-section behavior as macOS once this lands on `main`.

title: Feature request: per-session effort/reasoning-level flag for ao spawn
body:
### Feature request

`ao spawn --model <id>` exists, but there is no equivalent flag for the agent's effort / reasoning level (e.g. Claude Code's `/effort` setting).

**Problem**

When spawning workers with `--model`, there is no way to also control the effort/reasoning level for that session only. Effort is a harness-level setting (e.g. Claude Code's `/effort max`), so today the only options are:

- manually setting effort inside each spawned session, or
- changing the harness-wide default in settings, which affects all sessions, not just AO workers.

**Proposal**

Add an effort-style override to `ao spawn`, mirroring `--model`:

```bash
ao spawn --project my-proj --name "fix-bug" --model glm-4.7 --effort max
```

Semantics could match `--model`: a per-session override that does not change project/role config. A corresponding project/role-level config key (e.g. `worker.effort`) would also be useful as a default.

**Why**

Workers doing hard implementation or review tasks benefit from a higher effort level, while routine workers don't need to pay the token cost — the same reason `--model` exists as a per-session override.

title: fix(pi): detect OAuth logins in auth probe
body:
Code changes: +17 -2
Tests: +34 -0
Others: +0 -0

Fixes [#5265](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5265)

## Bug
Pi shows as not logged in after `/login`, even though the user authenticated.

**Reported by:** @jfoley13 (AO 0.12.12, packaged, MacIntel) | **Analyzed against:** `2bc5a88`

## Root Cause
Pi's `/login` flow stores OAuth credentials in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` as
`{"provider": {"type": "oauth", "access": "...", "refresh": "...", "expires": N}}`,
but `piAuthEntry` in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/pi/auth.go` only
deserialized `type` + `key`. OAuth entries have no `key`, so
`piAuthKeyIsResolved("")` returned false and the probe reported `unknown` —
only `api_key` entries (or env vars) were ever detected.

## Fix
- Extended `piAuthEntry` with `access`/`refresh`/`expires` and added
  `piAuthEntryIsOAuth()`: an `oauth` entry with a non-empty access token
  reports `authorized`. Expiry is ignored since Pi auto-refreshes tokens,
  so an expired token still indicates a login.
- Added `TestPiAuthJSONStatusAuthorizedWithOAuth` (fresh, expired,
  access-only tokens) and `TestPiAuthJSONStatusUnknownWithOAuthMissingAccess`.

## Test
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/agent/pi/...` — pass (new tests fail
  on the pre-fix code with `("unknown", false)`, reproducing the issue).
- `go test ./internal/service/agentauth/... ./internal/adapters/agent/registry/... ./internal/adapters/agent/omp/...` — pass; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Manual: real daemon on scratch `AO_DATA_DIR` + fixture `auth.json` —
  `POST /api/v1/agents/pi/probe` returns `unknown` for `{}` and `authorized`
  for an OAuth entry with the fix, `unknown` without it.

## Impact
- Pi users who authenticated via OAuth (`/login`) are now correctly shown as
  signed in; API-key detection is unchanged.

## Screenshots
Manual verification with a real daemon on scratch data (`AO_DATA_DIR` +
`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` fixtures; tokens shown are fake test values).
No login — probe reports `unknown`:

![pi probe with empty auth.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohitGoyal09/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-pi-login-5434/.issue-assets/pi-login-5434/pi_probe_empty.png)

OAuth login present — probe reports `authorized`:

![pi probe with OAuth auth.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohitGoyal09/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-pi-login-5434/.issue-assets/pi-login-5434/pi_probe_oauth.png)

`ao agent ls --refresh` shows Pi as `installed / authorized`:

![ao agent ls pi row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohitGoyal09/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-pi-login-5434/.issue-assets/pi-login-5434/pi_agent_ls.png)


## `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` structure
Map of provider id to credential (verified against live file + upstream
`auth-storage.ts`; secrets redacted). The probe previously only understood
`api_key` entries — `oauth` entries like the one below were invisible:

```json
{
  "anthropic": {
    "type": "oauth",
    "access": "<access-token>",
    "refresh": "<refresh-token>",
    "expires": 9999999999999
  },
  "openai": {
    "type": "api_key",
    "key": "sk-..."
  }
}
```

title: fix: stop session file tab icon from sticking hidden after click
body:
## What

Stop the language icon in a session's file-tab bar from getting stuck hidden after a tab is clicked.

## Why

`WorkspaceEntryIcon` hid on both `group-hover` and `group-focus-within`. Hover clears when the pointer leaves, but `focus-within` stays true as long as the tab's activation button holds focus, which it does after a click since nothing moves focus elsewhere afterward. That left the language icon hidden indefinitely once a tab was clicked, and it only came back once the user clicked something else entirely.

Fixes #5398

## How

Dropped the `group-focus-within:opacity-0` trigger from the icon's classes, keeping only `group-hover:opacity-0`. Hover-driven hiding self-corrects the moment the pointer leaves, so the icon's visibility no longer depends on sticky focus state. The icon's existing `dirty && "opacity-0"` behavior (hidden in favor of the unsaved-change dot) is unchanged.

Added a regression test that clicks the tab, confirms it retains focus (reproducing the exact precondition for the bug), and asserts the icon is never tied to that sticky focus-within state, closing the coverage gap where the previous test only checked the icon existed in the DOM, not that it stayed visible.

## Testing

- Reproduced the bug live in the AO desktop app (isolated dev data): reverted just this fix in a running dev session, confirmed the icon stuck hidden after clicking a file tab and moving the mouse away, then restored the fix via hot reload and confirmed the icon stayed visible on the same click-and-move-away sequence.
- `npm run typecheck` (frontend)

Code changes: +1051 -79  
Tests: +2346 -16

## What

Adds end-to-end experimental support for the `fx` coding agent in AO:

- registers `fx` as a TUI harness with auth and model discovery
- supports spawning, native restore, lifecycle observation, and TUI agent switching
- persists `fx` sessions through the daemon/API/CLI contract
- exposes `fx` in desktop and mobile agent selectors with official branding
- adds an **Install** action in Global Settings → Agents using the official `https://fx.sh/setup.sh` installer

AO could not previously create, restore, monitor, switch to, or install `fx` sessions. This change makes `fx` available through the same daemon-backed workflows as the existing TUI harnesses while preserving the rewrite architecture and keeping the frontend a thin API client.

- Introduces a dedicated Go adapter for command construction, model discovery, provider credential detection, and native resume.
- Adds a Herdr-compatible local lifecycle socket with per-launch generation fencing so stale processes cannot overwrite current activity.
- Extends the harness domain, readiness catalog, installer plans, API schemas, CLI validation, session switching, and SQLite constraints.
- Uses the shared Global Settings harness controls for installation, documentation, refresh, retry, and verification. The automatic installer downloads the official setup script and expects `~/.local/bin/fx`.

title: Bug: ao browser screenshot always fails with SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE while other ao browser commands work
body:
### Bug report

`ao browser screenshot` consistently fails with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, while all other `ao browser` commands work fine against the same session target.

**Environment**

- Platform: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), AO desktop app
- Browser runtime: connected (`electron-webcontents-debugger`)
- Session: an orchestrator session with a static file opened via `ao preview index.html` (AO preview origin, `http://ao-preview.<id>.localhost:3001/index.html`)

**Observed behavior**

Every `ao browser screenshot` call returns:

```
The service is momentarily unavailable, please retry. (SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)
```

with a request id. Attempts spanned ~10 minutes, so this is not a momentary blip:

- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-022151`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-022458`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-022774`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-023066`
- `request MacBook-Pro/RvYLQRjxRQ-024650`

Both variants fail identically: `ao browser screenshot <path>` and `ao browser screenshot <path> --json`.

**What works fine on the same target (so the runtime/page are healthy)**

- `ao browser status` → connected
- `ao browser get url`
- `ao browser snapshot --interactive`
- `ao preview` open/clear

**Expected behavior**

`screenshot` writes a PNG of the current tab, or returns a meaningful error if capture is genuinely unavailable.

**Notes**

Looks like the daemon-side capture/screenshot service is down or misrouted while the rest of the browser control plane is healthy. A clearer error distinguishing "capture service unavailable" from transient unavailability would also help.

title: fix(runtime): replay negotiated terminal modes to late attachers on the PTY host
body:
Code changes: +420 -25  
Tests: +631 -15  
Others: +0 -0  

Fixes #5039

## Problem

On 0.12.12 the mobile app can't scroll a TUI (Qwen Code, Claude Code, …) once the session has produced more than ~1000 lines. A desktop pane that re-attaches after a relaunch has the same problem.

New Linux sessions moved to the native pty-host in 0.12.12 (#4727; macOS got it in #4473). The host replays its ring buffer to every new attach, and the ring keeps the last 1000 lines, so the alt-screen / mouse-tracking / bracketed-paste handshake a TUI prints once at startup is the first thing to fall out of it. A client that attaches after that renders everything in the normal buffer with mouse reporting off, and its scroll gestures never reach the program. tmux re-sends those modes on every attach, which is why 0.12.10 works and sessions created before the upgrade (still on tmux) keep working. `internal/terminal/attachment.go` already describes this exact failure as the reason the mux relies on the runtime re-sending the modes.

## Fix

`conpty/modes.go` tracks the DEC private modes as output flows through the host. On attach the replay is prefixed with the modes it no longer contains. The state model follows xterm.js 5.5, which is what both the desktop pane and the phone's WebView run: one mouse protocol, one mouse encoding, one alt buffer, the keyboard/paste/focus flags, and the two default-on modes (auto-wrap, cursor visible). DECSTR and RIS reset what xterm's soft/full reset reset.

The prefix is diffed against a second pass over the replay bytes, so a client that attaches while the ring still holds the handshake gets the bare ring exactly as before, and shell output from before the TUI started stays in its normal buffer.

Left out on purpose: modes 6 and 45 only affect how the replay paints and the next repaint corrects them; 12, 1048 and 2026 aren't state in xterm.js; 1005 and 1015 are no-ops there.

## Testing

- `TestLateAttachReceivesNegotiatedModes` fails without the `Restore` call in `handleConn` and passes with it. Early attach and attach-after-exit cases pin the no-prefix behaviour.
- Tracker unit tests plus a fuzz test: never panics on arbitrary bytes, byte-at-a-time writes match a single write, and prefix + replay ends in the same state as the full stream at any split point. Benchmark: 0 allocs/op, ~400 MB/s; this is the only per-byte work added to the pump.
- `go test ./...` green, the package also under `-race`.
- Reproduced and verified end to end on an isolated daemon with Qwen Code 0.23 and the iOS simulator: before, a drag on the phone's terminal left the screen unchanged; after, the same drag scrolled Qwen's history. Feeding the captured attach frames to headless xterm.js confirms the client state (normal buffer / no mouse before, alternate / drag after).

Prasad's attach-race review is covered by deterministic `TestOutputWaitsForAnAttachInProgress` and `TestOutputDuringAttachIsDeliveredOnce`: ring append, mode update, and broadcast now share the attach-ordering lock, so a chunk is either in the snapshot or delivered afterward, exactly once. Both tests passed repeatedly under `-race`.

Not run: Windows ConPTY (same host code), a desktop relaunch.

title: Fix/files changed only toggle resets on navigation
body:
## What

Stop the "Changed Only" toggle in a session's Files view from silently resetting to on whenever the user navigates away from the Files tab and back.

## Why

`SessionInspector`'s generic tab-switch handler (`setView`) unconditionally called `onOpenFiles` whenever the destination tab was Files, forcing the changed-only toggle back on every time, even for a plain rail-click switch with no chat or review context involved. Since switching to another tab and back is an ordinary navigation action, the user's toggle choice was getting clobbered on essentially every visit to the Files tab, not just when returning to a specific file.

Fixes #5431

## How

Removed the automatic `onOpenFiles` call from `setView`, so tab switching only switches which tab is visible and no longer triggers a content-level preference reset as a side effect.

This is safe because the two flows that genuinely want the changed-only reset don't depend on that side effect:
- Opening a file or a turn's review from chat already calls `setFilesChangedOnly(sessionId, true)` explicitly via `handleOpenFiles`/`handleOpenReviewFile`/`handleOpenFile` in `SessionView.tsx`, unaffected by this change.
- The "Show Files" call-to-action button in the empty Files state calls `onOpenFiles` directly on click, independent of `setView`,  also unaffected.

So the reset stays intact for its original intended purpose (landing on the changed-files diff view when reviewing what an agent just did), and is only removed from plain tab navigation, which never had a legitimate reason to touch it.

## Testing

- Updated the existing "Files tab opens" test to drop the outdated assertion that clicking the tab calls `onOpenFiles` (that assertion encoded the bug).
- Added a regression test: click Files, click Summary, click Files again, assert `onOpenFiles` was never called.

title: fix: stop worker processes on desktop app quit
body:
## Summary

Closing the desktop IDE left every agent worker process behind: 9 `ao` processes + 8 worker processes eating ~1.4 GB RAM, surviving indefinitely with no UI and no owner. This PR makes orderly app quit put all sessions away (work stashed, worker processes stopped, one-shot restore markers written) so the next launch restores sessions cleanly via the existing `RestoreAll`/`reconcileLive` path.

Relates to #3537, #2523, #4317, #4850.

## Problem

Three compounding causes:

1. **Quit never tore anything down.** Both daemon shutdown paths (`SIGTERM` and `POST /shutdown`) deliberately preserved sessions for next-boot adoption — correct for restarts, wrong for IDE quit, where no next boot adopts them.
2. **Chat-mode workers were unkillable.** `saveAndTeardownOne` only destroyed runtime handles, but chat sessions (opencode as worker/orchestrator) own an app-server child process — never stopped, leaked every time.
3. **Windows TUI kills orphaned the real agent.** conpty used bare `Process.Kill()` on the `agent-process supervise` wrapper; the real agent (`opencode.exe`/`claude.exe`) survived as an orphan (same mechanism as #4317).

## Fixes applied

- **Quit-time teardown wiring:** `POST /shutdown` accepts optional `{"teardownSessions": true\}`. Empty body (how `ao stop`, daemon replace, and the supervisor watchdog shut down) preserves adopt-on-restart behavior. The flag is first-wins and read by the daemon after `Run` returns, which then runs `TeardownForAppQuit` bounded by `ShutdownTimeout`.
- **Chat gap closed:** `saveAndTeardownOne` now stops chat controllers (same split as `Kill`); new `TeardownForAppQuit` adds a best-effort second pass for branchless/scratch sessions the save path skips — workers stopped, rows left live, worktrees untouched.
- **Windows tree-kill:** conpty force-kill and pty close now use `taskkill /PID /T /F` with direct-kill fallback; Unix unchanged (Linux session sweep + Darwin group signal already reap trees). Includes a fail-closed self-PID guard and a swappable `killTree` seam for tests.
- **Desktop hook:** `before-quit` POSTs teardown for app-owned daemons only; headless `ao start` and `AO_KEEP_DAEMON` daemons stay persistent. Best-effort, 3s cap, never blocks quit.

Deliberately unchanged: restart/update adopt behavior, `ao stop` semantics, crash/SIGKILL fallback (adopts on next boot; the external guardian from #3537 remains future work).

## Files affected

- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` — chat stop in `saveAndTeardownOne`; new `TeardownForAppQuit` + `teardownQuitSkippedSession` (incl. shell-terminal drain).
- `backend/internal/session_manager/manager_test.go` — 2 new regression tests + shell-terminal assertions.
- `backend/internal/httpd/router.go`, `server.go` — `ShutdownRequest`, body decode (fail-closed to plain shutdown), first-wins flag.
- `backend/internal/httpd/control_test.go` — 6 teardown-flag cases + flag-gating test.
- `backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go`, `lifecycle_wiring.go` — quit-only teardown hook + interface entry; `wiring_test.go` fake + dispatch assertions.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime.go`, `host_conpty_windows.go` — tree-kill in `Destroy` force path and pty close.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/killtree{,_windows,_unix}.go` (new) — OS tree-kill + self-PID guard; `killtree_test.go`, `killtree_windows_test.go` (new) — live tree-kill test.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime_test.go` — stubbed `killTree` seam in force-path tests.
- `frontend/src/main/quit-teardown.ts` (new), `quit-teardown.test.ts` (new) — testable quit module (7 tests); `frontend/src/main.ts` — before-quit hook + updated teardown comments.

## Tests ran

- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `go vet` on session_manager, httpd, daemon, conpty — clean
- [x] New Go tests: `TestSaveAndTeardownOne_StopsChatController`, `TestTeardownForAppQuit_StopsSkippedBranchlessSessions`, `TestShutdownTeardownSessionsFlag` (6 cases), `TestTeardownSessionsRequestedFirstWins`, `TestKillProcessTreeRejectsNonPositivePID`, `TestKillProcessTreeRefusesOwnPID`, `TestKillProcessTreeKillsChildTree` (live tree-kill on Windows) — all pass

title: [Feature]: Let AO's embedded Browser panel remember a default browser profile
body:
## Problem

As a user of AO's in-app Browser panel, I need opening a link (e.g. a GitHub PR/issue link) to reuse a browser profile I've already chosen, because right now every new AO session starts with the profile unbound — the panel shows "Temporary" and I have to pick my profile again before signed-in sites like GitHub work. With many sessions per day, re-selecting a profile every single time is a real workflow tax.

## Root cause (from investigation)

`browser-view-host.ts`'s `ensureSession()` resolves a new session's profile only via `browserProfileStore.getSessionProfileId(sessionId)` (a per-AO-session binding). When that lookup misses — which it always does for a brand new session — `profileId` is `null` and the view gets a throwaway `ao-browser-${randomUUID()}` partition. There is currently no concept of a default/preferred profile in `BrowserProfileRegistry` (`shared/browser-profiles.ts`) for a new session to fall back to.

## Proposed direction

Add a global default browser profile:
- `BrowserProfileRegistry` gains a `defaultProfileId: BrowserProfileId | null` field (additive, no registry version bump needed).
- `BrowserProfileStore` gains `getDefaultProfileId()` / `setDefaultProfileId()`, clearing the default when that profile is deleted.
- `ensureSession()`'s fallback order becomes: session-specific binding → global default → temporary.
- Expose "set as default" in the existing Manage Browser Profiles settings UI.

A per-project (per-workspace) default was also discussed, but needs new plumbing (Electron main currently has no notion of `workspaceId`/project, only `sessionId`) — proposed as a possible follow-up, not part of this first pass.

## Alternatives considered

None — this is purely an AO-side behavior; it's unrelated to OS/Chrome default-browser-profile settings (confirmed `shell.openExternal` isn't involved here, since this is about AO's own embedded Browser panel, not system browser links).

title: [Bug]: ao session kill fails permanently when the workspace is already gone, and cleanup cannot recover it
body:
## Summary

A session whose worktree has already been removed can never be terminated. `ao session kill` fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR`, which means the session's `terminated` flag is never set — and `ao session cleanup` only processes **terminated** sessions, so it skips it forever. The two code paths disagree about whether a missing workspace is an error, and the session is stuck visible in the sidebar permanently.

## Reproduction

1. Have a worker session with a git worktree.
2. Kill it once. In my case the first kill returned `INTERNAL_ERROR` but *did* remove the worktree and set `status: exited`.
3. Retry `ao session kill <id>` — it fails every time thereafter:

```
Internal server error (INTERNAL_ERROR) [request EID-.../...]
```

4. `ao session get <id>` shows the contradictory state:

```
status: exited
activity: exited
terminated: false
```

5. `ao session cleanup --project <project>` never offers it. Other sessions in the same state *are* offered and report `Already gone: <id> (workspace was missing; nothing reclaimed)` — so cleanup handles a missing workspace gracefully.

## Expected

Either:
- `kill` should treat an already-missing workspace as success (idempotent) and set `terminated`, **or**
- `cleanup` should be able to reclaim sessions that are `exited` but not `terminated`.

Right now neither is true, so the session is unreachable by any path.

## Actual

Permanently stuck. The only observable difference between this session and its siblings that cleaned up fine is that its `terminated` flag is `false`.

## Notes

- Reproducible on Windows 11, ao daemon healthy (`ao doctor` all green), the rest of the session lifecycle working normally.
- `ao session cleanup` output confirms the graceful path exists — `Already gone: ... (workspace was missing; nothing reclaimed)` — it just isn't reachable for a session that never got marked terminated.
- I have not read the kill path's source, so the above is observed behavior rather than a diagnosed root cause. The asymmetry between the two paths' handling of a missing workspace looks like the likely culprit.

title: Codex account card jumps while metadata refreshes
body:
## Report

In the production app, expanding a Codex account's metadata card makes the account row and surrounding list visibly jump/flicker before the usage details settle.

Steps shown in the recording:

1. Open **Settings > Subscriptions**.
2. Expand the active Codex account row to view its plan and usage details.
3. The active row briefly loses its stable position/state, then moves back while the card opens.

Expected: the card expands in place. The `In use` state and row order stay stable while that account's metadata refreshes.

Actual: the active row/list visibly jumps during the expansion.

Production recording: https://screen.studio/share/vDypfkWI

## Agent-collected evidence

Checked against `main` at `d6c7d6018`.

- Expanding a row calls `ensureAccount(account.id)`.
- That targeted request asks for authentication/capacity/usage for one saved account.
- The backend currently starts device-global reconciliation for every ensure request, including this targeted metadata refresh.
- Reconciliation publishes a temporary `checking` snapshot with no verified active account.
- The frontend correctly hides `In use` for that unverified snapshot and sorts active rows first, so the row briefly loses its badge and position. The following `verified` snapshot restores both, producing the visible jump.
- The transition is more visible when the packaged/native request takes longer.

No matching open or closed issue/PR was found using the account-card jitter/flicker symptom.

## Proposed fix

Keep device reconciliation and account metadata refresh as separate operations:

- A targeted ensure request with explicit account IDs should refresh only those saved accounts' authentication/capacity/usage data.
- It should not start device-global reconciliation unless reconciliation is explicitly forced.
- Full account refreshes (no explicit account IDs), Settings-open/focus refreshes, and explicit reconciliation retries should continue reconciling the global credential.
- Keep the current truthful frontend rule: during a real reconciliation, no stale account is shown as `In use`.

Add a regression test proving that a targeted metadata refresh does not start reconciliation, while a full or forced refresh still does.

title: feat(telemetry): classify project repo owners as user or organization
body:
Code changes: +305 -33
Tests: +506 -6
Others: +7 -0 (docs)

## Why

`github_org` has never distinguished a personal GitHub account from an organisation. It is just the first path segment of a project's git remote, so the name asserts a distinction the code never makes and org-vs-person is unknowable in the exported data.

This is the **non-PII half** of that fix. It adds a classification and an honest name. It does not change what identity data AO sends, does not touch consent, and does not touch the privacy page.

## What changed

**`repo_owner_type` — new property, `User` or `Organization`.** Resolved from GitHub's public `GET /users/{owner}`. The new `internal/adapters/repoowner` adapter reads only the `type` field from the response; the rest of the `/users` payload (name, email, company, avatar) is never decoded, so it cannot reach a payload by accident. Any value other than the two known account types is rejected rather than forwarded, so a future GitHub account kind cannot silently widen the property's value space in a dashboard.

**The lookup never sits on the project-add path.** `Add` returns without waiting; the classification runs off-thread under a 5s bounded context and emits when it settles. `OccurredAt` is stamped at add time, so a delayed send still reports when the project was actually added. Every failure mode — offline, rate limited, unknown owner, unexpected type, invalid owner — omits the property and changes nothing else.

**`github_org` → `repo_owner`, with `github_org` still shipping.** Both are emitted in parallel for one release so existing PostHog queries and dashboards keep resolving. `github_org` is marked deprecated at the emit site and in the allowlist.

**Allowlist.** Both `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added` gain `repo_owner` and `repo_owner_type`. Payloads are strictly allowlisted, so a property missing here is dropped silently — there is now a test asserting both entries carry exactly the expected key set, and a second asserting neither ever allowlists repository-identifying keys.

**Buffered sinks no longer panic on a late `Emit`.** Emitting after the originating call has returned makes an `Emit` racing `Close` reachable; both `LocalSQLiteSink` and `PostHogSink` would have panicked on a send to a closed channel and taken the daemon down during shutdown. They now drop the event. Verified as a real regression: reverting the guard makes the new test panic.

## Deliberate decisions

**The GitHub call carries no credentials.** The brief anticipated an authenticated lookup degrading to omission when unauthenticated. `GET /users/{owner}` is public, so this ships unauthenticated instead. That is both simpler and better coverage: the installs currently missing owner attribution are disproportionately the ones with no GitHub token, and they get classified just as well. It also keeps this PR completely free of credential handling, which is the point of the split. The trade is GitHub's 60 req/hour unauthenticated budget per IP; exceeding it degrades to an omitted property, the same as any other failure.

**No call at all when telemetry is off.** The classifier is wired from the consent-resolved config, so a user who declined telemetry never has their machine call GitHub for a property that would never be exported. `Deps.RepoOwners` left nil keeps the previous inline-emit behaviour exactly.

**The owner is validated before it reaches a request path.** It is a path segment of a remote URL AO did not author, so it is checked against GitHub's login grammar rather than trusted; a crafted remote cannot steer the request off `/users/{login}`.

**Still only the owner segment.** Never the repo name, never the full URL. Asserted in the service test and in the allowlist test.

## Tests

Narrow first, then the CI-equivalent suites.

- `internal/adapters/repoowner` — account-type mapping, unknown-type rejection, 404 / rate-limit / 5xx / malformed-body degradation, owner validation (traversal, spaces, over-length, leading/trailing hyphen), context cancellation, and an assertion that no `Authorization` header is sent.
- `internal/service/project` — `repo_owner` + deprecated `github_org` emitted together; `repo_owner_type` stamped for both User and Organization; omitted on classifier failure without losing `repo_owner`; **`Add` returns while the classifier is still blocked** and the events land after it answers; no lookup at all for a non-GitHub remote.
- `internal/adapters/telemetry` — allowlist coverage and rejection of repository-identifying keys on both project events; sanitizer keeps the new keys and drops a remote URL; `Emit` after `Close` drops instead of panicking on both buffered sinks.
- `go test -race` clean on `internal/service/project`, `internal/adapters/repoowner`, `internal/adapters/telemetry`, `internal/daemon`.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` (the CI-pinned version): 0 issues across the touched packages.
- Full `go test -race ./...`: green except `internal/session_manager`'s four `TestSpawn_*Binary*` tests, which **fail identically on unmodified `origin/main`** on this machine (environment-dependent agent-binary probe). Unrelated to this change; verified in a clean worktree at `d6c7d60`.

## Scope

Deliberately out of scope, and split into a follow-up precisely because it cannot ship without privacy and consent work in the same PR: capturing the authenticated user's `github_login`. `distinct_id` remains the anonymous `ins_<uuid>` install ID and `$process_person_profile: false` is untouched here.

Note for reviewers: `docs/telemetry.md` already discloses that the owner segment is sent and that for a personal repository it is the user's own GitHub username. The landing privacy page does not yet mention it at all — a pre-existing gap that belongs to the follow-up, not to this PR.

title: feat(telemetry): derive workspace GitHub owner from child repos
body:
> **Stacked on #5473, which is stacked on #5471.** Base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-342/repo-owner-parser`. This PR's diff contains only PR B; merge #5471, then #5473, then this one. Draft until both land.

## Problem

The project-added payload derives the repo owner from the project's own `RepoOriginURL`. For a **workspace** project that field is the *workspace root*, which is normally a plain container directory holding several repos — AO initializes it as a git repo with no origin. So the owner was essentially never captured:

| Project kind | Root has git remote | Owner captured | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspace | yes | 36 / 110 | 32.7% |
| workspace | no | 0 / 1,168 | 0% |

Workspace overall: **36 / 1,278 = 2.8%**.

Meanwhile `prepareWorkspaceProject` has already enumerated the child repos, and `workspace_registration.go` sets `RepoOriginURL` on every child record. Those records are in scope at the emit call site. The data was simply never consulted — no new git subprocesses and no new plumbing are needed.

## What this changes

`emitProjectAdded` now takes the workspace child records (nil for single-repo projects) and, for workspaces, derives the owner from them.

**`RepoOriginURL` is deliberately untouched.** It is load-bearing well beyond telemetry — `session_manager` feeds it into session spawn context, and tracker intake uses it for provider inference, repo parsing, and host resolution. Repointing a workspace project's `RepoOriginURL` at one of its children would silently change which issues get polled and what repo context sessions spawn with. This change is purely additive on the telemetry payload.

### Multi-repo owner policy

A multi-repo workspace has no single owner, so rather than invent one:

1. The **root's own remote still wins** when it has one — no behaviour change for the 36 workspaces already attributed.
2. Otherwise, **exactly one distinct owner** across the children populates `repo_owner`.
3. Children with **different owners leave `repo_owner` unset**. Picking the most common owner would attribute a workspace to an owner of only part of it; omission is the honest answer.
4. A new **`repo_owner_count`** property (distinct owner count, workspace events only) keeps the mixed-owner and no-owner cases countable, so case 3 is visible in analytics instead of looking identical to "no data".

A derived owner is an owner like any other, so it flows into #5471's `repo_owner_type` classification and into the deprecated `github_org` alias exactly as a root-derived owner does. Neither behaviour changes, and the one-release `github_org` compatibility now covers workspaces too.

Only owner *segments* are ever emitted — never repository names or remote URLs. `repo_owner_count` is a bare integer with no identifying content, allowlisted on both `ao.projects.created` and `ao.onboarding.first_project_added`.

## Tests

- `TestWorkspaceRepoOwners` — no children, same-owner dedupe, mixed owners sorted, missing/non-GitHub remotes ignored, no-GitHub-remotes.
- `TestWorkspaceRepoOwnersIsOrderIndependent` — enumeration order cannot leak into the payload.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceDerivesRepoOwnerFromChildren` — end-to-end through `Add`; asserts `repo_owner` **and** the `github_org` alias, and that the stored `RepoOriginURL` is still empty.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceOmitsRepoOwnerWhenChildrenDisagree` — both `repo_owner` and `github_org` omitted.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceIgnoresChildrenWithoutGitHubRemotes` — a child with no remote plus a GitLab child.
- `TestManager_AddWorkspaceWithoutGitHubChildrenReportsZeroOwners`
- `TestManager_AddSingleRepoOwnerPayloadUnchanged` — single-repo payload unchanged, no `repo_owner_count`.
- `TestSanitizeRemotePayloadKeepsWorkspaceOwnerCount` — the new property survives the allowlist while repo name / origin URL still do not.
- #5471's own `repo_owner` / `repo_owner_type` tests all still pass on this branch.

Ran locally after the rebase, with the telemetry env stripped: `go test ./backend/internal/service/project/ -run 'Workspace|Owner|Telemetry|RepoOwner'` (32 tests) and `go test ./backend/internal/adapters/telemetry/ -run 'Sanitize|Allowlist|RepoOwner|Owner'` — both pass. Local `golangci-lint` is built against Go 1.24 and refuses this module's 1.25.7 target, so lint is left to CI.

## Notes

- `docs/telemetry.md` said the owner segment was "the one GitHub-derived value AO does send". That was already understated by #5471's `repo_owner_type`, and `repo_owner_count` makes a third, so the privacy doc now names all three.
- Linearized above the parser-coverage PR #5473 (previously a sibling). #5473 moves `githubOwner` out of `service.go` into `owner.go`, so `workspaceRepoOwners` now lives in `owner.go` beside the parser it calls — the workspace owner is derived through #5473's widened parser, not the old five-prefix one.
- `docs/telemetry.md` keeps every statement from all three PRs: #5471's owner-type bullet, #5473's GitHub Enterprise and token-in-remote limits, and this PR's workspace sentences. Nothing was taken wholesale from one side.
- Does not touch consent (#5264). Non-PII either way.

## Risks

- Behaviour change is confined to the telemetry payload for workspace projects. No storage, API, or spawn path is affected.
- Workspace projects that previously made no owner-classification request may now make one, since a derived owner feeds #5471's lookup. That lookup is already off the `Add` path and bounded by its own timeout.
- `repo_owner_count` counts *GitHub* owners only; a workspace of GitLab repos reports 0.

title: fix(telemetry): recognise the GitHub remote forms the owner parser missed
body:
Stacked on #5471 — **base is `ao/agent-orchestrator-341/repo-owner-type`, not `main`.** Retarget to `main` once #5471 merges. `githubOwner`'s body is byte-identical on #5471, but #5471 rewrites the enclosing hunk (`emitProjectAdded` through `githubOwner`) and the function's doc comment and call site, so developing this against bare `main` would conflict in exactly the region it needs to edit. Review this PR's own commit only.

## Problem

`githubOwner` matched five literal prefixes — `git@github.com:`, `https://github.com/`, `http://github.com/`, `ssh://git@github.com/`, `git://github.com/`. Anything else returned `""`, so the project-added event shipped no owner at all. Verified against the old implementation, every one of these yielded nothing:

| Remote | Old |
|---|---|
| `https://ghp_…@github.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `https://octocat@github.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `git@github.com-work:aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `ssh://git@github.com-work/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `ssh://git@github.com:22/octocat/hello.git` | `""` |
| `https://github.com:443/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `https://GitHub.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `git@GITHUB.COM:aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `HTTPS://github.com/aoagents/x.git` | `""` |
| `github.com:aoagents/x.git` | `""` |

The token-embedded and SSH-alias forms matter disproportionately: they are what credential helpers and multi-account setups write, i.e. exactly the developers worth attributing.

It also emitted junk from malformed paths — `https://github.com/../x.git` returned `".."`, `https://github.com/-aoagents/x.git` returned `"-aoagents"`.

## Change

Parse the remote's structure instead of prefix-matching it, in a new `owner.go` (moved out of `service.go` unchanged in behaviour apart from the fix):

- Split both the URL form (`scheme://[userinfo@]host[:port]/path`) and the SCP-like form (`[user@]host:path`).
- **Discard userinfo without inspecting it** — it routinely carries a token, which must never leave the function.
- Drop an explicit port; compare scheme and host case-insensitively; the owner segment keeps the case git recorded.
- Accept `github.com`, `www.github.com`, and SSH config aliases of the shape `github.com-<name>`. A hyphen suffix is the documented multi-account convention; a dot suffix (`github.com.evil.example`, `git@github.com.work:`) is **not** accepted.
- Require the first path segment to look like a GitHub login (≤39 chars, alphanumeric plus `-`/`_`, no leading/trailing hyphen), so path noise is no longer exported as an owner.

## GitHub Enterprise is deliberately out of scope

A GHE host (`github.mycompany.com`) is **not** matched, and there are tests asserting that. An owner there is a different, private namespace from a github.com org; folding the two into one `repo_owner` would make the property ambiguous and unqueryable. Capturing GHE at all would need a distinct signal (a separate property, or a hashed host) and its own decision — raising it here rather than deciding it silently.

## The privacy rule is unchanged

Only the owner segment ever comes out — never the repo name, the host, or the URL. `TestGithubOwnerNeverLeaksBeyondTheOwner` pins that against remotes that embed a token and a private repo name. **No raw remote URL or repo name was added to telemetry**, which is also why the cause split behind the missing-owner gap cannot be measured from PostHog: the candidate causes above are reasoned from the parser, not a measured breakdown.

## Scope

Pure telemetry. `githubOwner` has exactly one caller — the `ao.projects.created` payload. Nothing outside the event changes: no `RepoOriginURL` behaviour, no tracker intake, no session spawn, no consent (that is #5264, untouched). `docs/telemetry.md` gains the github.com-only / GHE-excluded statement.

## Tests

`backend/internal/service/project/owner_internal_test.go` is table-driven over every accepted and rejected form: default git forms, six credential-embedded variants, four SSH-alias variants, four port variants, five case variants, shape tolerances, non-github hosts, lookalike hosts, three GHE forms, local/relative/Windows paths, unsupported schemes, and six malformed-owner rejections, plus the 39-character boundary and the no-leak test.

```
go vet ./internal/service/project/
go test ./internal/service/project/ -count=1   # ok, 109s (full package)
```

Local `golangci-lint` is built against go1.24 and cannot load this repo's go1.25 config, so lint is left to CI.

title: fix(cloud): stop false-positive agent-exited 410 on resumed terminals
body:
Code changes: +32 -2  
Tests: +14 -12  
Others: +0 -0

## What
Fixes a false-positive "agent terminal has exited" (HTTP 410 TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED) on any resumed cloud session.

## Why
`IssueTerminalTicket` decided the agent had exited if ANY agent terminal for the session was `closed` or `failed`. But every resume closes the previous agent terminal and opens a fresh one, so a session that has been paused and resumed even once always carries a closed terminal. The result: the browser terminal-ticket mint returned 410 in a loop for a live session, and the UI showed "Connected" with no terminal. This came in with #5350 and only surfaces once a session has been resumed.

## How
The agent is treated as exited only when a dead terminal exists AND no live one does. Both occurrences of the check in `worker_transport_store.go` now require `NOT EXISTS` an `opening`/`open` agent terminal, so a resumed session with a live open terminal is no longer misreported.

## Testing
cloud gofmt, build, vet, and `go test ./internal/httpapi/` pass. Verified against the l-a run where a resumed orchestrator with a live open terminal was being 410-blocked.

title: fix(updater): progress-based macOS staging watchdog with retry
body:
## Problem

macOS updates could fail with "macOS stopped responding while preparing the update" on slow machines, and with a cryptic ditto pkzip error when the disk was low. Two root causes:

1. Native staging (Squirrel.Mac: ditto extract, code-signature verify, swap prep) was bounded by a fixed 3-minute wall-clock deadline. Squirrel exposes no progress event and no cancel API, so a slow disk that was still making progress got killed at 180s. The only recovery was a manual quit-and-reopen.
2. A full disk hit a separate path and surfaced ditto's raw "No space left on device" text (report in https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5170).

## Change

- Replace the fixed timeout with a progress watchdog that polls the ShipIt staging directory for growth and only gives up after a stretch of no progress (90s inactivity). Fixed caps remain as a fallback when the growth signal cannot be read at all (6-minute no-signal, 15-minute absolute). All reads are read-only against the OS updater cache under `~/Library/Caches/*.ShipIt` and fail open to the fixed caps, so a stat failure never trips the watchdog. AO writes nothing there and keeps no AO state there.
- Add a free-space preflight before handing off to ditto, so a full disk stops early with a short actionable message instead of a partway pkzip failure.
- Surface short, user-readable messages; the full ditto/pkzip/codesign detail is logged, never shown. The remap is deliberately narrow: only known extraction/verification failures are rewritten, and any other error (for example a restart-handoff failure) passes through unchanged so its own recovery and messaging stay intact.
- Retry now restarts AO (`updates:relaunch`) instead of re-invoking `install()` against a Squirrel that cannot be reset in-process. A fresh process re-checks the feed and re-stages cleanly. This is a plain restart, not an install, so it does not touch the post-update relaunch marker.

## Size (for review)

16 files, +225 / -36.

- Production code: +179 / -20 across 5 files. The bulk is `auto-updater.ts` (+152): the watchdog, the staging-dir and free-space probes, and the short-message mapping. The rest is small: the `updates:relaunch` IPC handler (`main.ts`), its preload/bridge wiring (1 line each), and the dialog's Retry action (`RestartToUpdateDialog.tsx`).
- Tests: +38 / -16 across 3 files. Existing timeout tests were rewritten to drive the watchdog deterministically through a filesystem test seam (`__setStagingProbesForTesting`) rather than the real disk, plus the dialog's retry-by-relaunch and hide-install-on-quit cases.
- i18n: +8 / 0. One `update.restart.retry` key added to each of the 8 locale files.

## Verification

Run on this branch checked out clean off `main`, not on the development branch:

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `vitest run` for `auto-updater.test.ts`, `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`, and `i18n/instance.test.ts`: 204 passing. The i18n test confirms the new key exists in every locale.

The disk-full and slow-disk staging paths themselves are macOS-native (Squirrel) and cannot be exercised in unit tests; those are covered by the deterministic test seam plus the free-space and message-mapping logic, not by a live staging run.

title: feat(cloud): PR tracking for cloud workers and PR details in the sidebar
body: > **Stacked on #5379.** This branch is built on `fix/cloud-pr-tracking-and-workspace-checkout`, so the diff includes #5379's two commits until that merges. The new work is the last three commits: `feat(cloud): track worker pull requests…`, `feat(desktop): show cloud session pull requests…`, and `fix(cloud): build against the pinned backend contract`. ## What Cloud sessions now get the pull request tracking and sidebar PR details that local sessions have. Ported the local implementation to cloud sessions - **Control plane:** a PAT-backed tracker finds the PRs a worker opens from its session branch and keeps each one's CI, review, and mergeability current. - **Session list/get responses:** now include each session's `prs` and `scmStatus`. - **Desktop:** the sidebar, board and inspector show cloud PRs the same way they show local ones. ## Why On a deployment without a GitHub App (the setup #5379 fixes raise/claim for), cloud PR tracking stopped at `ao claim-pr`: - `prstatus.Scanner` only runs with an App. PRs raised or claimed with a PAT stayed at their initial state and never got CI, review or mergeability updates. - A PR the agent opened any other way (`gh api`, the browser, an MCP tool, or `gh pr create` output the wrapper couldn't parse) was never attached to the session. The local daemon's SCM observer finds these PRs by matching the session branch. - The desktop mapped cloud sessions with `prs: []`, and the inspector always asked the **local daemon** (`/api/v1/sessions/{id}/pr`) for PR detail. So the sidebar and inspector never showed a cloud PR, even when the control plane had one. ## How **Control plane (`cloud/`)** - `githubapp.PATPullRequestTracker` works through every live session (sandbox not deleted or terminated): - **Finding PRs:** only for running sandboxes. It lists `pulls?head=owner:&state=all` and claims any PR that no session in the org tracks yet (`PullRequestTracked`), so it never reassigns a PR another session already has. - **Refreshing PRs:** for each of the session's open PRs, it records CI, review and mergeability through `UpdatePullRequestObservation`. - It authenticates with the session creator's PAT, the same credential worker checkout and push already use. Sessions without a PAT, or on a non-github.com remote, make no GitHub calls. - **Wiring:** it only runs when no GitHub App is configured (`githubService == nil`). App deployments keep the existing scanner, unchanged. It reuses the scanner loop through the new `prstatus.NewFunc`, and polls at `max(AO_CLOUD_PR_STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL, 1m)` because each call counts against the user's own GitHub rate limit. - **Shared code:** - `observePullRequest` is used by both the App refresh and the PAT tracker. - `sessionGitHubPAT` is used by both `WorkerGitHubPAT` and the new `SessionGitHubPAT`. - `httpapi.GitHubPATAssociatedData` exposes the PAT's encryption associated data so the tracker can decrypt it. - **Database access:** the cross-org session scan reads only `ao_sandboxes`, which the service context can already read. Session rows are then read with `withOrg`, so no new RLS policy or migration is needed. - **Response shape:** `GET /sessions` and `GET /sessions/{id}` now return the same shape as the children listing (`sessionChildResponse`). The additions are `prs` and `scmStatus` (derived with the same `contract.DeriveSCMStatus` the local daemon uses). Kanban column and display status are not sent: the cloud module builds against a pinned `backend` version (the Docker build has no `go.work`) that predates the Kanban reducers, so the desktop places the card from the session status, as it already does when the daemon omits a column. The change is additive; existing fields are unchanged. **Desktop (`frontend/`)** - **Board:** cloud sessions map `prs` and `scmStatus`, and derive their board column from the session status, so status dots, board columns and PR chips follow the same rules as local sessions. - **Inspector:** `useSessionScmSummary(session)` reads cloud PR detail from the control plane's `/sessions/{id}/pull-requests` route and maps it to the daemon's `SessionPRSummary` shape. It polls every 15s because no daemon event stream invalidates it. The control-plane URL is read from the settings cache when fetching (as `useTerminateSession` does), so local-only renders don't subscribe to the cloud auth hooks. - **Local-only actions:** the local-daemon merge button is hidden for cloud PRs, and the local reviewer query is skipped for cloud sessions. **Intentional omissions** - The control plane doesn't track review threads, failing-check logs, or CI/review auto-inject yet; those fields take empty defaults. - No server-side Kanban column/display status until the cloud module's `backend` pin is bumped to a version with the Kanban reducers. - PR discovery through the App path (branch matching with an installation token) is not added; App deployments behave exactly as before. - Like the existing scanner, the tracker runs on every replica, and claims are idempotent upserts. ## Testing - `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && GOWORK=off go build ./... && GOWORK=off go vet ./... && GOWORK=off go test ./...`: all pass, both standalone (the pinned `backend`, as the Docker build uses) and through `go.work`. `docker build --target control-plane` succeeds. `go test -race` passes for `githubapp`, `httpapi` and `prstatus`. - New Go tests: - `pat_tracker_test.go`: finds and refreshes a PR; skips PRs already tracked; paused sessions only refresh; no GitHub calls without a usable PAT. - `resource_handlers_test.go`: PRs and SCM status on the response. - New SQL checked against a throwaway `postgres:17` with migrations applied, run as the non-privileged `ao_cloud_app` role under RLS: - `PullRequestTrackingSessions` excludes deleted sandboxes and marks paused ones inactive. - `SessionGitHubPAT` resolves the credential. - Claim, then `PullRequestTracked`, `OpenPullRequestRefsForSession` and `UpdatePullRequestObservation` all behave as expected. - `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`: passes. - New and updated vitest: `useSessionScmSummary.test.tsx` (local vs cloud source, shape mapping, unconfigured control plane) and `useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx` (cloud PRs and SCM status). - Full `npx vitest run`: **18 failures remain, and they fail identically on the base branch** (landing analytics/download tests, `browser-history-store`, `browser-profile-import`). `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx` fails only under full-suite load and passes on its own, both with and without this change. - **Not verified end to end:** I didn't run this against a live control plane with a real GitHub PAT, and I didn't take UI screenshots; the sidebar/inspector rendering code itself is unchanged, only its data source. ## Checklist - [x] Continuing an existing PR branch (stacked on #5379) - [x] One focused change - [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending remote CI)

title: fix(session): stop provider chrome and never-messaged Chat from failing interface switches
body:
## Summary

Two interface-switch failures from #5482, both root-caused against live sessions and fixed:

1. **`DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT` false positive on an empty composer.** Drain-time draft detection treats any non-dim rune after the last `❯` inside the composer rules as human input and aborts on the first such capture. Claude Code 2.1.273 paints provider-owned non-dim content into that region: a bare `Claude Code` product label on the prompt row between the rules, and a multi-line statusline below the lower rule (which the footer-free fallback scans when rule geometry does not match). One transient frame permanently failed the switch. Fixes: the draft refusal now requires the same repeated stable samples as the idle decision; a horizontal rule below the prompt closes the footer-free composer scan; adapters can name provider chrome labels that never read as a draft.

2. **`NATIVE_SESSION_MISSING` from a never-messaged Chat session.** Entering Chat reserves a provider conversation id, but the durable conversation row is materialized only when the Chat controller starts (first turn). The chat→Terminal freshness proof demanded that row, so a session that had never been messaged — nothing to resume, nothing to discard — could never reach Terminal. Fix: the Chat emptiness proof accepts `domain.ErrNoConversation`; generic history read failures and every other guard (prompts, checkpoint facts, transcript evidence, turns) stay fail-closed.

title: fix(mobile): allow plain HTTP to the tailnet on iOS so iPhones can pair over Tailscale
body:
Fixes #3852

## Problem

Since iOS 17, App Transport Security applies to IP addresses, and `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` only exempts the local ranges (RFC 1918, link-local, `.local`). Tailscale's `100.64.0.0/10` is RFC 6598, so a plain-HTTP connection to the daemon's tailnet address is refused before a packet is sent. The pairing code carries exactly that address, so an iPhone off the LAN can't pair or reconnect over Tailscale.

#5485 makes the daemon advertise the TLS proxy from #3707 instead, which fixes it wherever secure pairing can run. That still needs the `tailscale` CLI on the Mac's `PATH` and HTTPS certificates enabled on the tailnet, and a `100.x` address typed by hand with TLS off keeps failing. Android already allows it (`usesCleartextTraffic`).

## Fix

Two `NSExceptionDomains` entries in `app.json`, and nothing wider:

- `100.64.0.0/10` — CIDR keys are accepted from iOS 17, the same release that started blocking. On iOS 16 and earlier ATS never applied to IP addresses, so nothing changes there.
- `ts.net` with `NSIncludesSubdomains` — the MagicDNS name, for the same daemon reached by name instead of by address.

Not `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`. The exception only reaches hosts inside the user's own tailnet, where the link is already WireGuard-encrypted; any other `http://` host stays blocked. The daemon still advertises the `tailscale serve` proxy when secure pairing is active (#5485); this is for the tailnets where it isn't, and for the manual entry. `lib/ats.test.ts` pins the two entries and asserts nothing else is waived, so the block can't drift back or widen. README and the desktop's TLS comment updated to match (the frontend change is a comment).

This changes the native fingerprint (runtime version `ad3999c7` → `8685992b`), so it ships with the next store build, not over the air; builds before it keep needing #5485's TLS path. App Review may ask for a justification for `NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads`; one that fits: "The app connects to a daemon on the user's own computer over the user's Tailscale VPN (`100.64.0.0/10`, `*.ts.net`). That link is WireGuard-encrypted, and the daemon has no public hostname to hold a CA certificate for."

## Testing

- Native build from this branch on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5), `fetch()` from inside the app over the Hermes debugger, against a plain-HTTP server bound to a `100.100.100.100` loopback alias: `http://100.100.100.100:3099/api/v1/identity` → 401 from the server, request logged server-side. `http://1.1.1.1/` → still "App Transport Security policy requires the use of a secure connection", so the exception is targeted. LAN address unchanged. On `main`'s build the same probe to `1.1.1.1` is refused the same way; the `100.x` probe was only run on this branch's build. The built `Info.plist` carries both entries; the `ts.net` one wasn't exercised (no DNS for a fake name here).
- `ats.test.ts`: both tests fail with `app.json` reverted. 860 → 862 vitest, `tsc` clean, `expo export --platform ios` bundles.

Not run: a physical iPhone on a real tailnet (Tailscale is stopped on this Mac, no cert domains). ATS is enforced the same way in the simulator.

title: ao spawn: SPAWN_TIMEOUT leaves session started but initial prompt never delivered
body:
## Summary

`ao spawn --project <project> --name <name> --claim-pr <N> --no-takeover --prompt "..."` timed out client-side with `SPAWN_TIMEOUT`, but the session was actually created and started. The initial prompt was never delivered to the agent, so the session sat idle and had to be manually recovered with `ao session claim-pr` + `ao send`.

## Observed behavior

Two spawns were issued back to back for the same project, different PRs. Both CLI calls failed with:

```
Session spawn timed out before the agent could start (SPAWN_TIMEOUT) [request <host>/<req-id>]
```

After the timeout, `ao session ls` showed both sessions existed and were idle, but:
- They were on the default `ao/<session-id>/root` branch, not the requested PR branch
- The `--name` flag did not appear to be applied
- No PR was claimed (so `--claim-pr` / `--no-takeover` did not take effect)
- The agent had received no prompt

Manual recovery worked: `ao session claim-pr <session-id> <pr>` succeeded (printed `checkout: already on PR branch` and `taking over from <old-session>`) and `ao send --session <id> --message ...` delivered the task.

## Expected behavior

Either the spawn succeeds end to end (session created, branch/name/PR claim applied, prompt delivered), or it fails atomically with no partially-initialized session left behind.

## Suspected area

Timeout path in the spawn flow: the daemon appears to create and start the session before the CLI gives up waiting, and the prompt delivery (plus name/branch/claim application) never happens afterward. Observed with the kimi harness; may be harness-specific startup slowness exceeding the client timeout.

## Environment

- AO CLI/daemon: local dev build, macOS (arm64), 2026-09-16
- Harness: kimi
- Impact: 2/2 spawns failed this way in one batch; sessions silently idle until manually noticed

title: fix(acp): report rejected session/load and back off history settle polling
body:
Code: +104 −9
Tests: +284 −0
Files removed: 0

## What happened
Switching a Claude Code session from Terminal to Chat hung for 45 seconds, then failed with a vague "resume failed" toast.

## Issue solved
Fixes #5292. The second history load (`session/load`) ran inside the 45 s settle window with no bound of its own, so one slow load ate the whole budget. The `-32603 "context deadline exceeded"` in the report is the SDK echoing AO's own expired deadline, not a provider refusal.

## What we did
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go` — each refresh load gets its own 30 s deadline; a bound hit returns `ErrChatHistoryLoadFailed` right away. Retry wait now grows 100 ms → 2 s.
- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/driver.go`, `history.go` — a `-32603` from `session/load` maps to `ErrChatHistoryLoadFailed` only when AO's context is still live; AO's own deadline keeps its context error.
- `backend/internal/session_manager/interface_transition.go` — the switch reports `TARGET_HISTORY_LOAD_FAILED` and does not restart the target a second time.
- Tests: stalled load returns within the attempt bound; provider `-32603` vs AO deadline classified apart; backoff schedule; transition code. Touched packages pass `go test`; I did not run the full `-race` suite or `golangci-lint` locally (lint crashes on go1.27 here).

title: fix(update): stop restart dialog jittering on workspace refetch
body:
## What

Stop the restart-to-update dialog from jumping every ~15 seconds while it is open.

## Why

The dialog renders a "Current worker state could not be confirmed…" line whenever `workspace.isFetching` is true. The workspace query polls the daemon on a 15s `refetchInterval`, so `isFetching` flips true during every background poll even though the last-known session list is still in hand. The line inserts and removes on each poll, and Radix re-centers the dialog on any height change, so the whole dialog bounces every 15 seconds while a build is staged.

`isFetching` is the wrong signal: on a background refetch the worker list is not actually unknown. The genuinely-unknown cases are already covered by `!workspace.data` (first load, nothing yet) and `isError` (fetch failed).

## How

Drop `isFetching` from the condition. The warning now shows only on `isError` or `!workspace.data`; a routine background refetch no longer toggles it.

## Testing

- Focused suite `RestartToUpdateDialog.test.tsx`: passes (the one failure under `TZ=Asia/Seoul` is the pre-existing hardcoded "Sep 2" assertion tracked by #5283 / open PR #5318, unrelated to this change and not present under UTC).
- Change is renderer-only; verified by reading the query's `refetchInterval` behavior and running the unit suite. Not verified against a live staged build.

title: Open agent reports reliably and improve dark-mode output readability
body:
## What

Fixes several usability issues in agent chat output and the AO Browser:

- Makes code comments and quoted syntax readable on dark backgrounds.
- Opens local report links inside AO instead of sending unusable filesystem paths to the external browser.
- Adds right click actions for opening verified workspace files in Files.
- Makes link behavior consistent between AO Browser and the system browser.
- Adds a compact Copy URL button to the AO Browser address bar.

## Why

Agent-generated reports could be difficult or impossible to open:

- Windows absolute paths could be removed by Markdown URL sanitization because drive letters resemble URL schemes.
- Local paths that had not yet appeared in the workspace file index were treated as external links.
- Absolute workspace paths did not receive the normal link context menu.
- Filesystem paths passed directly to Chromium produced empty or unusable tabs.
- Some syntax-highlighted comments used the passive text color, which had insufficient contrast on the dark code-block surface.
- The Browser address bar displayed a shortened hostname but had no direct way to copy the complete URL.

## How

### Report and workspace links

- Normalizes relative, POSIX, Windows, encoded, and `file://` workspace paths.
- Resolves known files to their workspace-relative paths.
- Sends newly created or not-yet-indexed report paths through the existing session preview resolver.
- Keeps filesystem access confined by the backend workspace validation.
- Opens normal HTTP and localhost links in AO Browser by default.
- Preserves explicit system-browser behavior for web links through modifier-click and the context menu.

### Link context menu

- Shows **Open in AO Browser** for browser-compatible links.
- Shows **Open in Files** only when the link resolves to a verified workspace file.
- Shows **Open in external browser** only for HTTP(S) links.
- Keeps **Copy link** available without automatically opening the link.

### Browser URL copying

- Adds a Copy URL control beside the existing external-browser button.
- Uses the same compact `23×23px` styling with a 4px gap.
- Copies the complete underlying URL, including path and query parameters.
- Replaces the copy icon with a checkmark briefly after success instead of showing a global toast.
- Retains an error notification if copying fails.

### Output readability

- Uses the normal muted-text token for highlighted comments and quotes instead of the much darker passive-text token.

## Testing

title: fix(scm): keep UNSTABLE PRs mergeable instead of downgrading to blocked
body:
## What

Move the `UNSTABLE` check above the draft / CI / review blockers in the SCM observer's two mergeability derivers, so an `UNSTABLE` PR is recorded as `Mergeability = unstable` rather than `blocked`.

## Why

Fixes #2401.

`mergeabilityObservation` (`backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go`) and its byte-identical twin `mergeabilityFromProviderFacts` (`backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go`) checked `draft` / `ci == failing` / changes-requested, set `MergeBlocked`, and returned — before ever reaching the `UNSTABLE` branch at the bottom.

Because an `UNSTABLE` PR's status rollup aggregate is `FAILURE` (→ `ci = failing`), that bottom branch was effectively dead for the common case, and a genuinely mergeable PR was persisted as `blocked` with blocker `ci_failing`.

`UNSTABLE` means the PR *is* mergeable but a non-required check failed or is pending (a *required* failure yields `BLOCKED` instead). `doc.go` in the same package spells out the priority — rule (3) `UNSTABLE` outranks (5) changes-requested and (6) CI-failing — and the sibling `mergeabilityFromGraphQL` in `provider.go` already implements that order. The two observer functions didn't, and the `UNSTABLE` observer path was untested, which is how the divergence slipped in.

## How

- `UNSTABLE` now returns `MergeUnstable` immediately after the `DIRTY` / `BEHIND` / `BLOCKED` handling, matching `doc.go` and the GraphQL sibling.
- **Deliberate deviation from the issue's suggested fix:** the `BLOCKED` branch keeps falling through instead of returning early. `BLOCKED` and `UNSTABLE` read the same `state` field so they are mutually exclusive anyway, and an early return there would truncate a blocked PR's blocker list to just `blocked_by_provider`, dropping `draft` / `ci_failing` / `changes_requested` detail — a regression the issue didn't ask for.

Reviewers may want to focus on the downstream consumers of `MergeUnstable`, which this change makes reachable for the first time in the common case:

- `lifecycle/reactions.go:405` (`mergeabilityClearsConflict`) already documents `unstable` as a definitive non-conflicting state.
- `service/session/pr_summary.go:404` (`mergeabilityReasons`) already handles `MergeUnstable` and derives reasons from the PR's own fields, so the UI still surfaces `ci_failing` for an unstable PR even though the observation's `Blockers` list is now empty.
- No auto-merge gate keys on `Mergeability`.

## Testing

Added table tests for the previously untested `UNSTABLE` observer path in both packages, covering the issue's repro (optional check fails, rollup `FAILURE`, review approved) plus guard rows for the paths that must not change: conflicting still wins, blocked still collects every blocker, `CLEAN` + failing CI still blocks, `CLEAN` + approved still mergeable.

- Verified the new tests **fail without** the source fix (`State = "blocked", want "unstable"`) and pass with it, so they aren't vacuous.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/scm/... ./internal/observe/...` clean.
- Full `go test ./...` across the backend passes. The first run showed two failures in `adapters/agent/fake` and `adapters/agent/pi` — both timing-sensitive, unrelated to SCM, and both passed on a clean re-run.

title: fix(tabs): pin the tab overflow action to the tab's right edge
body: ## Problem In a session tab, the `⋮` overflow menu sat immediately after the end of the title text instead of at the tab's right edge. With a short title like `hii`, the button floated in the middle of the tab. ## Cause `TerminalTabFrame` renders its trailing action as an overlay positioned `right-1` inside the tab's inner row. That row was `inline-flex` with no width, so it sized itself to its content rather than to the frame. The frame itself is a fixed `--size-shell-tab-connected` (148px), so for any title shorter than the tab, the overlay anchored to the end of the text rather than to the tab. ## Fix Let the inner row fill the frame (`w-full flex-1`). The action then anchors to the tab's right edge for every title length. Text stays left-aligned and truncation behaviour is unchanged. This applies to every tab family built on `TerminalTabFrame` (agent, reviewer, shell, file tabs), so their close/overflow buttons are now consistently right-aligned too. ## Verification Measured in a real layout engine, rendering the frame at its normal 148px width with the title `hii`: | | `⋮` x-position | inner row width | |---|---|---| | before | 55–71px | 75px (shrunk to text) | | after | 127–143px | 147px (fills the tab) | `143px` is `right-1` (4px) from the 148px right edge. title: fix(session): require consecutive dead probes for orchestrators and notice on replace
body:
## What

Requires two consecutive `ProbeDead` runtime reaper observations before terminating orchestrator-kind sessions, and sends a durable continuity notice with predecessor ID and transcript path when `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)` replaces an unexpectedly terminated predecessor.

## Why

Fixes #2501.
Orchestrators are long-running and execute unhooked sub-agent/tool operations where intermediate activity hooks are not fired. A single transient probe jitter or lag meeting the stale-activity window was enough to terminate them prematurely. Subsequently, navigating back or refreshing in the UI triggered `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)`, which found no active session and spawned a replacement with a blank transcript, leaving the user with no explanation of what occurred or where the previous transcript was.

## How

1. **Consecutive dead probe gate (`backend/internal/lifecycle/manager.go`)**:
   - Track `consecutiveDeadProbes map[domain.SessionID]int` guarded under `m.mu` in `m.mutate`.
   - Require `orchestratorDeadProbeThreshold = 2` before `KindOrchestrator` sessions transition to `IsTerminated = true`.
   - Reset the counter on any non-dead probe, activity signal, or launch mismatch.
   - Workers and other session kinds retain historical single-sample termination so short-lived tasks are not prolonged.
2. **Predecessor continuity notice (`backend/internal/service/session/service.go`)**:
   - When `SpawnOrchestrator(clean=false)` finds no active orchestrator, look up the most recent terminated orchestrator within `orchestratorPredecessorStaleWindow` (30 minutes).
   - If found, inject a plain-text continuity message into the newly spawned session referencing the predecessor ID, termination timestamp, and `NativeTranscriptPath`.
   - Best-effort delivery mirroring `sendRetireNotice`.

### Intentional Omissions
- Did not touch worker termination threshold: workers need fast failure detection to avoid hanging task queues.
- Did not alert on predecessors older than 30 minutes: projects reopened days or weeks later are deliberate fresh starts, not silent reaper races.

## Testing

- Added `TestRuntimeObservation_OrchestratorRequiresConsecutiveDeadProbes` in `backend/internal/lifecycle/manager_test.go` covering 1-sample non-kill, 2-sample kill, counter resets on alive probes, and worker single-sample kill.
- Added `TestSpawnOrchestratorNoCleanSendsContinuityNotice` in `backend/internal/service/session/service_test.go` covering cold spawn without predecessor, recent predecessor notice, ancient predecessor bypass, and newest predecessor selection.
- Added `TestSpawnOrchestratorNoCleanIdempotentDoesNotDoubleNotice` verifying no duplicate notices on re-render/retry.
- Full test suites passed:
  - `go test ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/session`
  - `go test -race ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/session`
  - `go vet ./internal/lifecycle ./internal/service/session`

body:
## Summary

Fixes #5341

Adds zcode (Z.AI GLM terminal coding agent) as a first-class harness adapter, following the grok adapter pattern:

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/zcode/` — clean-room adapter (launch, restore, readiness hints, auth checker, config spec, table tests)
- Migration `0148_allow_zcode_harness.sql` — admits `'zcode'` in `sessions.harness` CHECK, handling both the normal and the legacy `'qm'` schema variants from the 0095 era
- Registration chain: `registry.go`, `harness.go`, `dto.go` enums, `openapi.yaml` + `schema.ts` regenerated and committed together
- Frontend: `zcode` added to product-ui `AGENT_OPTIONS`/`AGENT_LABELS`

## Design notes

- **Interactive TUI + after-start prompt delivery** (not `--prompt`): zcode's `--prompt` is a headless single-turn path; workers need the interactive composer. Prompt is injected once `PromptReadinessHints` match.
- **Auth checker reads `~/.zcode/v2/credentials.json`** (OAuth access token JWT) and decodes `exp` locally — structural `apiKey` presence in `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` cannot distinguish logged-in from OAuth-expired (observed live).
- **Restore falls back to a fresh launch** when no native `agentSessionId` was captured; `-c/--continue` deliberately rejected as a resume fallback.

## Intentional omissions

- No `doctor.go` probe spec, `systeminstall.go` targets, `agentauth/plans.go` login plan, or `activitydispatch.Derivers` for zcode: `CoverageForHarness` returns `SignalCoverageNone` and `agentSessionId` is not captured — self-consistent with the no-AO-managed-hooks stance and the fresh-launch restore fallback.
- No AO-managed workspace hooks: zcode gates workspace-scoped hook files (`zcode.json`, `.zcode/config.json`) behind an interactive trust review an orchestrator cannot complete unattended.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `domain.AgentConfig.Validate()` hardcodes Amp's mode vocabulary (`low|medium|high|ultra`), so project-config validation rejects the modes zcode's own `GetConfigSpec` advertises (`build|edit|plan|yolo`). The adapter validates modes itself at argv-build time, but the domain validator contradiction remains.
- Resumed sessions may not mount the welcome banner, so readiness hints can time out (best-effort 10s, delivery proceeds anyway).

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` (zcode, sqlite, httpd), `go test -count=1` on zcode, storage/sqlite, registry, httpd/... — all green
- Live end-to-end: daemon spawned a real zcode worker in a worktree, TUI booted `--mode build`, prompt injected, permission dialog approved, file created; kill/restore round-trip verified
- Binary surface audited against the real zcode 0.16.5 CLI (no invented flags; the `--prompt` headless path deliberately avoided)

## Verification gap

- Frontend `npm run typecheck` and the api-drift CI job could not run locally (`node_modules` not installed in this worktree; `openapi-typescript` unavailable). Spec regen was verified drift-free via `npm run api:spec` (zero changes), and schema.ts changes were regenerated earlier in the branch. Please let CI confirm the TS side.
