Two dogfooding reports on a nightly build:

1. A red "Update check timed out. The update service did not respond in time." error appeared on launch, after the app had been idle for a day. A manual "Check for updates" then worked. The error was for a background check the user never asked for.
2. An "Installing and reopening AO" window appeared during the update install/restart. It is not needed on a normal update; the app should just reopen to its own loader.

## Change

Three focused fixes. All build on the already-merged staging watchdog (https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5479); none of that work is touched here.

- **Suppress the check-timeout error for automatic checks.** The deadline timer in `checkForUpdatesWithDeadline` broadcast a red error to the Settings panel even for a background launch check. On a cold network that stranded a failure the user could not act on. The timeout now surfaces only for user-initiated checks (manual and return-home); automatic timeouts still route through the existing UI suppression and the failing-checks nudge, so a persistent problem is still reported, just not as a startup banner.

- **Collapse the automatic re-check cadence to once a day on every channel.** The 15-minute nightly and hourly stable polling were redundant background work: a fresh check already runs on every launch, so the interval only governs sessions left open for a long stretch. Frequent polling on a cold network was also a source of the launch-time check errors above.

- **Keep the macOS progress helper hidden on a normal update.** `UpdateProgressState.stage()` previously surfaced a window after 30s of a slow-but-healthy quit and kept it up through install. It now stays hidden (accessory, no window) for the full three-minute budget and only presents a recovery window if the update is genuinely stuck (no close or no reopen after three minutes). The normal path is: AO closes, macOS installs silently, AO reopens to its own loader.

## Verification

Run on this branch checked out clean off `main`:

- `vitest run src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`: 176 passing, including the rewritten interval/cadence tests and the split automatic-vs-manual timeout assertion.
- Swift `StateTests` compiled and run: passing, including the new slow-but-healthy close/reopen cases and the three-minute recovery deadlines. The helper `main.swift` still compiles against the changed state module.
- Full-project `tsc --noEmit` could not be run to completion in the sandbox used here; CI runs it on this PR. The changes are type-local: a renamed numeric constant, an underscore-prefixed unused param, and an added guard on an existing module variable.

The slow-disk and disk-full staging paths are macOS-native (Squirrel) and are covered by 5479's test seam, not by a live run here.

title: [Bug]: Notification sound never plays on Linux — shell.beep() is a silent no-op for desktop-launched apps
body:
## Bug

With **Sound notifications** enabled (the default), the desktop app plays no sound on Linux when an agent needs input or a PR is ready to merge. Toasts and taskbar flashing still work; only the audible signal is missing.

**Source:** local observation (Arch Linux, Hyprland/Wayland, packaged AppImage 0.13.0) | **Reported by:** @Pyasma | **Analyzed against:** `f006182a5` (main)
**Confidence:** High

## Reproduction

1. Linux desktop (tested: Arch, Hyprland, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`), launch the AO desktop app from the launcher / AppImage (i.e. not from a terminal).
2. Settings → General → leave **Sound notifications** on.
3. Unfocus the AO window and trigger a `needs_input` notification (any agent asking a question), or in a dev build call `__testNotif("needs_input")` from the renderer devtools.
4. Toast appears, window flashes, **no sound**.

## Root Cause

The only sound path is `shell.beep()`:

- `frontend/src/main.ts:2447-2449` — `notifications:show` handler
- `frontend/src/main.ts:2468-2470` — dev-only `notifications:devBounce`

Electron's Linux implementation of `shell.beep()` (`shell/common/platform_util_linux.cc`, v33) is:

```cpp
void Beep() {
  // echo '\a' > /dev/console
  FILE* fp = fopen("/dev/console", "a");
  if (fp == nullptr) {
    fp = fopen("/dev/tty", "a");
  }
  if (fp != nullptr) {
    fprintf(fp, "\a");
    fclose(fp);
  }
}
```

For a normal desktop launch both opens fail, so the call returns without doing anything and without reporting an error:

- `/dev/console` is `crw------- root root` — not writable by the user.
- `/dev/tty` needs a controlling terminal; the app has none when launched from a launcher/AppImage (`ps -o tty` shows `?`, stdin/stdout are `/dev/null`).

Even in the rare case one of the opens succeeds, `\a` is the PC-speaker/TTY bell, not audio output — on most modern desktops (Wayland especially) that is inaudible as well. So on Linux the "Sound notifications" toggle is effectively a no-op, and `soundNotificationsEnabled` defaults to `true`, so users expect a sound that can never arrive.

The beep was introduced in [PR #4051](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4051) and behaves as intended on macOS (`NSBeep`) and Windows (`MessageBeep`); the Linux branch is what is broken.

## Fix

Play a real audio asset instead of relying on `shell.beep()` on Linux (or on all platforms, for consistency):

- Bundle a short default sound in the app resources and play it from the renderer via an `<audio>` element / `Audio` — main cannot play audio itself, so `notifications:show` would send a `notifications:playSound` message back to the shell webContents (the same mechanism the closed custom-sound [PR #5282](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5282) used for user-supplied files).
- Alternatively, on Linux only, shell out to a system player (`canberra-gtk-play -i bell`, `paplay`, `pw-play`) as a fallback — heavier and less portable, so the renderer approach is preferred.
- Keep `shell.beep()` for macOS/Windows if a native beep is desired there.

The custom-sound work in [PR #5282](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5282) already contains the renderer playback plumbing; a minimal fix could land just the "bundled default sound played by the renderer" part without the file-picker UI.

## Impact

- Every Linux user: the sound toggle does nothing, so agents blocked on input are missed unless the user notices the toast / taskbar flash.
- The toggle is on by default, so this reads as "notifications are broken" rather than "feature unavailable".
- No error is logged anywhere, which makes it hard to diagnose.

## Related

- [PR #4051](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4051) — introduced `shell.beep()` for `needs_input` / `ready_to_merge`
- [#5035](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5035) / [PR #5282](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5282) — custom notification sound (closed); contains renderer-side audio playback that would also fix this

Adds a read-time worker watchdog that surfaces sessions needing a human, derived from durable facts only (never persisted), plus a new `switch_recovery_pending` verdict for agent switches wedged on an ambiguous ownership boundary.

- `AttentionReason` vocabulary extended with `switch_recovery_pending`; `domain/watchdog.go` owns the reason and the project-resolvable thresholds (`stalled`, `questionPending`, `consecutiveInfraErrors`).

- Detail names the harness pair, the stable error code, and how long the saga has been wedged, with the Restore affordance; `lastWorkerErrorAt` anchors on the switch's `UpdatedAt` (falling back to `RequestedAt`).
- `List`/`Get` load the active switch once and reuse it for both the `ActiveAgentSwitch` projection and the verdict — no new query, no migration for the switch path.
- Worker-error classification: TLS/certificate handshake failures (`certificate`, `cert`, `tls`, `ssl`) now classify as transient retryable errors instead of unknown.
- Durable worker-error log: migration `0148_session_worker_errors.sql`, sqlc queries + store, recorded from `SettleTurn`/`SettleTurnByID`, bounded per session.

title: fix(chat): swallow settled-turn 409 on Stop instead of trapping the composer
body:
Code changes: +14 -2
Tests: +40 -0
Others: +0 -0

## What
Pressing Stop on a Chat turn that already settled returned red 409 CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN ('there is no turn in flight to interrupt') and left it as a persistent red composer banner. Since the backend 409s only when in-memory tracking AND SQLite agree no turn is running, the rendered 'running' row is necessarily stale — the end state the user wanted is already true, and the mutation's onError refetch reconciles the view. Surfacing the 409 as an error traps the user into pressing Stop into the same 409.

This filters CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN out of the interrupt error surfaced in commands.error (genuine failures — network, provider refusal — still surface; the onError snapshot refetch is unchanged).

## Tests
- frontend: useConversation.test.tsx 45/45 pass, incl. 2 new tests (409 swallowed with refetch triggered and no error; non-settlement interrupt failures still surface)
- ChatComposer / TaskComposer / event-transport suites: 175/175 pass
- frontend typecheck: 0 errors under src/ (only pre-existing missing-module errors under ../packages/product-ui from the partial monorepo install)
- No backend changes; live-checked the running daemon to confirm the 409-vs-snapshot invariant (snapshot running rows match durable running rows outside the reported stuck state)

## Risks
- If a snapshot refetch itself fails, Stop stays visible with no error shown until the next press surfaces the real failure. Acceptable: the alternative (today) is a guaranteed-misleading red 409.
- No API, migration, or generated-file changes.

title: cloud: robust worker self-heal so a stale baked binary is a non-event (nodeops helper-path mismatch + coder PTY-stream reliability)
body:
## Problem

Every control-plane deploy that changes the `ao-worker` / `ao` binary silently breaks cloud sessions until the provider templates are manually rebaked, because the worker's baked-in copies go stale and the self-heal does not actually land the fresh binary where the runtime uses it. This has recurred on both providers (nodeops capture breakage; coder worker-bootstrap failures) and is currently worked around with manual `publish-nodeops-template.sh` / `publish-coder-workspace.sh` rebakes per deploy.

Goal: a stale bake becomes a **non-event** — the worker self-heals the current binaries to the exact paths the harness, hooks, and bootstrap invoke — so no template rebake is required for a worker change.

## Root cause 1 — nodeops helper-path mismatch (breaks event-based capture)

- The claude Stop hook (and the other activity hooks) invoke a **hardcoded absolute path**: `cloudHookBinary = "/usr/local/bin/ao"` (`cloud/internal/workerexec/activity_hooks.go:9`, used at :45 and :88).
- `healHelper` heals the current `ao` helper **only into `$AO_DATA_DIR/bin/ao`** and depends on it shadowing the baked copy *on PATH* (`cloud/cmd/ao-worker/selfupdate.go`, `healHelper`). It never writes `/usr/local/bin/ao`.
- The worker runs as `ao-worker` (uid 1001) and cannot overwrite `/usr/local/bin` (root-owned), so the baked helper stays stale.
- Result: the Stop hook runs the **stale baked** `/usr/local/bin/ao`, which lacks `pokeCheckpoint`, so durable-restore capture never fires. (Observed on staging: baked helper `20dd1ba…` vs CP-expected `cd4149b7…`; capture produced 0 rows until a manual per-sandbox overwrite + template rebake.)

### Fix options
- (Preferred, no elevated perms) Stop pointing the hook at `/usr/local/bin/ao`. Point `cloudHookBinary` and `AO_WORKER_HELPER_PATH` at the **healed** path (`$AO_DATA_DIR/bin/ao`), which the worker owns and self-heal keeps current. The bootstrap already sets `AO_WORKER_HELPER_PATH`; make the hook use it (or the healed override) instead of a hardcoded absolute path.
- (Alternative) Have the bootstrap install the healed helper to `/usr/local/bin/ao` using the elevated perms it already has (it runs the launch via `sudo`), so the absolute path everything uses is always current.

## Root cause 2 — coder PTY-stream fallback is unreliable (breaks worker bootstrap)

- #5329 added preinstalled-miss detection (`__AO_PREINSTALLED_MISS__`, `errPreinstalledWorkerDoesNotMatch`) and a `bootstrapWorkerThroughPTY` fallback in `cloud/internal/sandbox/coder/client.go`.
- When the baked worker is stale, the fast path correctly misses, but the fallback fails with `coder: read workspace PTY before worker upload: EOF` and `AO worker exited during startup __AO_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED__` — so a stale coder bake fails to bootstrap instead of cleanly streaming the current worker. (Observed on staging: coder workspace baked worker `d6ce491…` vs CP-expected `0eea515…`; sessions could not connect until the workspace image was reseeded.)

### Fix
- Make `bootstrapWorkerThroughPTY` robust to the PTY read (retry/handle the EOF, ensure the launch/upload handshake completes) so the streamed worker path reliably delivers the current binary whenever the baked SHA does not match `AO_WORKER_EXPECTED_SHA256`.

## Acceptance

- Deploy a CP with a changed `ao-worker`/`ao` **without** rebaking either template. A fresh nodeops session auto-captures on turn completion (Stop hook runs the current helper), and a fresh coder session bootstraps its worker via the stream fallback. No manual `publish-*-template` step required for correctness (rebakes remain a pure launch-speed optimization).

## Context / related
Documented in prior debugging: the nodeops rebake process gap and the coder reseed. Deploys that change the worker currently MUST go through `deploy-staging.sh` (which rebakes both templates) — this issue removes that hard dependency for correctness.

title: feat(cloud): session delete and restore, with terminal-epoch reconnect, first-click delete, and worker self-heal (#5518)
body:
Cloud session delete and restore, plus the reliability fixes surfaced while validating it end to end on staging.

## Feature
- Delete a cloud session (or project) and restore it later under the same session_id: the conversation and uncommitted work are captured to `ao_session_transcripts` (durable transcript blob + a preserved git ref) and rehydrated into a fresh sandbox on restore. Capture is event driven off the harness Stop hook. Provider agnostic (nodeops + coder).
- Migration `00039_session_restore` (renumbered from `00037` to avoid the collision with `00037_turns_allow_queued_fanin`).

## Reliability fixes (found and fixed during E2E)
- Terminal reconnect on the worker epoch: the cloud terminal is now keyed on the session's `workerEpoch`, so a resume from idle-pause, a restore, or any re-provision re-mints the terminal against the live agent instead of clinging to the dead epoch's exited terminal. Fixes the "connected but TERMINAL ENDED / can't type" loop, where nothing attached and the session then idle-paused again.
- Delete terminates the session on the first click: `deleteSession` now sets `is_terminated=true` and requests the sandbox teardown atomically (new `TerminateSession`, the inverse of `RestoreSession`), instead of only setting the sandbox `desired_state` and racing the idle scanner. The board archives it immediately; no more repeated clicks.
- Robust worker self-heal so a stale baked binary is a non-event (Closes #5518, part 1): the harness hooks now invoke the self-healed helper at `<dataDir>/bin/ao` instead of a hardcoded `/usr/local/bin/ao`, and `healHelper` always keeps that path current. This stops the recurring stale-bake breakage where the Stop hook ran the stale baked helper (no `pokeCheckpoint`) and durable capture silently stopped until a manual template rebake. Coder PTY-stream reliability (part 2 of #5518) remains open.

## Testing
Validated on staging: capture on turn completion, delete then restore round trip (conversation + uncommitted work returned), resume from idle-pause reconnects, delete archives on first click. Cloud module `go build/vet/test` green; renderer typecheck + vitest green.

Closes #5518

title: feat(telemetry): attach operator GitHub handle to product analytics
body:
## What this does

Sends the operator's authenticated GitHub login with product telemetry, so the most active AO users can be identified and ranked in PostHog for outreach. Today product analytics are anonymous and the only GitHub-derived value is the repo owner, so individuals working on org-owned repos are invisible and unreachable.

The handle is part of product telemetry with no dedicated control: it is sent whenever it resolves to a human account, and it stops when telemetry is turned off (the master `AO_TELEMETRY_*` switch), because the session-start carrier event is then never emitted. An earlier revision added a separate Settings > Privacy toggle for it; that was removed because it duplicated the existing telemetry off switch and advertised the tracking.



## What gets sent

On `ao.session.spawned` only, when the SCM identity resolves, the identity is human, and the login is non-empty, the daemon attaches:

- event property `github_actor`
- PostHog person property `$set.github_actor` with `$process_person_profile: true`

Every failure mode (no token, `GET /user` failure, offline, org or bot token, no resolver) degrades to anonymous. Every other event keeps the anonymous default. Turning telemetry off stops the event itself, so the handle stops with it.


## Location (aggregate, anonymous)

Every daemon event now sets `$geoip_disable: false` so PostHog derives coarse location (country, and where available region and city) from the connection IP at ingestion. This powers aggregate "which areas use AO" breakdowns. It applies to all installs, stays anonymous (no precise coordinates, AO stores no IP, no person processing unless a consented event opts in), is not tied to the GitHub handle, and has no separate opt-out (turning telemetry off stops it). Disclosed in README, docs/telemetry.md, and the privacy page.

## Disclosure

Documented honestly in `README.md`, `docs/telemetry.md`, and the privacy policy page: the handle and the aggregate location are part of telemetry, what is sent and where, and that turning telemetry off stops both.


## Testing

- `go test ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/adapters/telemetry/... ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/ports/...` pass.
- `gofmt` clean and `go vet` clean on the touched packages.

Note: the branch was rebased onto current `main`; the backend `ScopedIdentityResolver` port it depends on already exists there.


## Size

The diff is about 270 lines (9 files, +241/-29). Reused the existing `ScopedIdentityResolver` port instead of adding a new one, so the ports and daemon SCM wiring now match `main` and the change is production logic plus tests and disclosure:

- About 100 lines of tests: `github_actor_test.go` (+62), `posthog_test.go` (+34), and `service_test.go` (+5), covering resolver nil/error, non-human identity, empty login, the `$set`/`$process_person_profile` derivation, the `github_actor` allowlist entry, the `$geoip_disable` assertion, and the anonymous default on a real spawn.
- About 90 lines of docs and disclosure: `docs/telemetry.md` (+54), the privacy page (+30), and `README.md` (+6), required because this sends a real identifier.
- About 80 lines of production wiring: the `githubActor` helper and `emitSpawned` payload plus the resolver field (`service.go`), the session construction and typed-nil guard (`lifecycle_wiring.go`), and one `$set`/geo block in the sink (`posthog.go`).

title: fix(session): ensure spawn rollback uses detached context on timeout (#5489)
body:
Fixes #5489

### Summary of Changes

When `ao spawn` experiences a timeout (e.g. `SPAWN_TIMEOUT` during `deliverAfterStartPrompt` or `StartChatTurn`), the rollback cleanup steps (`runtime.Destroy`, `rollbackPreparedSpawnWorkspace`, and `markSpawnFailedTerminated`) were previously called with the already-cancelled/timed-out caller context (`ctx`).

Because `ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded` (or `context.Canceled`), all cleanup calls immediately failed without executing. This left:
1. The agent runtime process still running in the background.
2. The git worktree active and locking branches.
3. The session record remaining in SQLite in an active/started state instead of being parked as terminated.

This change:
- Introduces `spawnRollbackContext(ctx)` which detaches cancellation from the caller's context via `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` while bounding cleanup to a 30-second budget (`spawnRollbackBudget`).
- Ensures all spawn rollback paths (`manager.go:Spawn`, `chat_spawn.go:spawnChatSessionController`, `manager.go:rollbackSeedSpawnWorkspace`, and `relaunchSessionWithPolicyAndGeneration`) perform cleanup using `spawnRollbackContext`.
- Adds unit tests in `manager_test.go` and `chat_spawn_test.go` verifying that when prompt delivery times out, the runtime is destroyed, the workspace is removed, and the session is marked terminated using an active detached context.

title: fix(session): recover interrupted orchestrator spawns
body:
Code changes: +25 -0  
Tests: +35 -0  
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #4079

## Summary

- During synchronous startup safety, terminate only a non-terminated session that has neither a workspace path nor a runtime handle. This is the durable seed row left when the daemon is hard-killed after persisting a spawn but before worktree creation.
- The row is terminated through the lifecycle manager before the daemon accepts requests, so the next orchestrator request creates a replacement rather than returning an unusable coordinator.
- Sessions that retain either a workspace or a runtime handle are deliberately left on their existing recovery paths, preserving work and live runtimes.

## Reproduction

1. Start an orchestrator for a throwaway project and hard-kill the daemon while its worktree is being created.
2. Restart using the same AO data directory.
3. Before this change, the incomplete active row has no runtime or workspace handles; Resume agent fails and future orchestrator requests keep returning it.
4. With this change, startup terminates that row before serving requests, allowing a fresh orchestrator to be created.

## Verification

title: [Feature]: Offer guided setup when Git is missing during onboarding
body:
## Problem

On a fresh computer without Git, AO blocks onboarding after detecting the missing dependency. The recovery text only tells the user to install Git from git-scm.com and restart AO.

This affects first-run onboarding across supported platforms. A first-time or non-technical user must leave the app, find and complete the appropriate installation for their operating system, understand that environment changes may require a restart, and manually retry the interrupted workflow. This stops the user before they can create or clone their first project.

Expected: AO should provide a guided, platform-appropriate recovery path, verify that Git is available afterward, and let the user continue the original onboarding action.

## Proposed direction

Offer an explicit, confirmed in-app setup action appropriate to the current platform, or evaluate a maintained embedded Git distribution. Platform-specific options could include a trusted package manager where available. Keep manual installation as an alternative. After installation, re-run the Git check and resume or clearly prompt the user to retry.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-09-17 from AO `v0.13.0` and current checkout `7d6e08f3a` using read-only source inspection (`git show` and `rg`).

- `InstallDependencyDialog.tsx` treats a missing required Git installation as a blocking startup requirement.
- The shared Git section only renders the localized instruction: “Install git from git-scm.com, then restart Agent Orchestrator.”
- The same dialog already has in-app install actions for some other dependencies, but Git has no install, progress, or automatic retry action.

This confirms the shared recovery experience; it does not prescribe whether platform package managers or an embedded distribution are the preferred long-term implementation.

No screenshot is attached because the available capture contains private account information.

title: [Bug]: Repository names with spaces fail creation with an unrelated invalid-URL error
body:
## What went wrong?

On AO 0.13.0 on macOS, preparing a local project without a GitHub remote fails when the proposed repository name contains spaces.

Steps observed:

1. Open a local project without a GitHub remote.
2. Continue to **Prepare project**.
3. Select an available repository owner.
4. Leave the repository name as `AO Desktop App`.
5. Select **Create repository and continue**.

Actual: setup stops and shows `Project setup failed — Enter a valid HTTPS, SSH, Git, or file URL.` The form does not contain a URL field, no field is highlighted, and the repository is not initialized.

Expected: AO should either accept/normalize a valid repository name or identify the repository-name field and explain how to correct it. It should not report a URL-entry error for an internally generated URL.

Workaround: replace spaces with hyphens before retrying.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-09-17 from tag `v0.13.0` (`15e9ea971`) and confirmed in current checkout `7d6e08f3a` using read-only source inspection (`git show` and `rg`).

- `CreateProjectFlow.tsx` builds the future remote as `https://github.com/{owner}/{name}.git` before submitting project preparation.
- `isValidProjectRemote` rejects any value containing whitespace.
- On rejection, `prepareProjectGit` reports the clone-flow localization key `createProject.cloneInvalidUrl` and returns before `POST /api/v1/imports/prepare-git`.
- The repository-name input can contain spaces, so the generated remote fails validation even though the user never entered a URL.

This code path supports the observed symptom and explains why repository initialization never begins.

No screenshot is attached because the available captures contain private account information.

title: [Bug]: Stable macOS builds never create the implemented menu-bar tray
body:
## What went wrong?

After installing the stable AO 0.13.0 desktop app on macOS, no AO status item appears in the system menu bar.

Expected: the macOS menu-bar tray should be available in the stable desktop app so users can see sessions needing attention, jump to a session, show AO, or quit the app.

Actual: the stable app never creates the tray. This makes the implemented menu-bar feature unavailable to normal release users.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-09-17 from tag `v0.13.0` and current checkout `7d6e08f3a` using read-only source inspection (`git show`, `git blame`, and `rg`) plus GitHub issue/PR search.

- The original request, #3530, is closed as completed by merged PR #3531.
- `frontend/src/main/tray.ts` contains the working macOS tray implementation, including attention-session entries, **Show Agent Orchestrator**, and **Quit**.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` creates the tray only when `isTrayEnabled(...)` returns true.
- `frontend/src/main/tray-lifecycle.ts` returns true only for macOS development builds or packaged versions containing `-nightly.`. Every packaged stable version therefore returns false.
- The same condition is present in the `v0.13.0` tag, and its test explicitly expects packaged stable macOS builds to be disabled.
- Review on PR #3531 identified that stable users would not receive the feature. The response described this as an experimental dev/nightly rollout, but no matching open issue or PR now tracks completing that rollout.
- The 0.12.0 changelog says macOS gets an attention tray icon, without stating that stable builds are excluded.

This evidence confirms why the tray does not appear. It does not establish whether additional validation is still required before the rollout gate can be removed.

No screenshot is attached because code inspection fully demonstrates the stable-build exclusion.

title: feat(config): per-harness model and effort overrides
body:
Code changes: +268 -27  
Tests: +310 -0  
Others: +47 -0 (generated OpenAPI + TS types, i18n translations for 8 locales)

## What

Lets a user pin **model + effort per harness** (and per profile/config) once in project config, instead of passing `--model` on every spawn or burying effort in prompt text.

- **Domain/config surface** — `ProjectConfig.harnessConfigs` (map keyed by harness) carrying `model`, `mode`, `effort`, `permissions`. Layering order: base `agentConfig` → `harnessConfigs[<target harness>]` → role override (worker/orchestrator/reviewer, gated by the role's pinned harness) → per-spawn/CLI override. `PUT /projects/{id}/config` therefore accepts per-harness settings; `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated.
- **Daemon spawn path** — the target harness is now threaded through `effectiveAgentConfig(harness, kind, cfg)` via a new `projectAgentConfigForHarness` layer, so a harness-specific model/effort applies to spawned sessions, agent switches, chat spawns, and interface transitions without touching role overrides.
- **CLI passthrough** — `ao project set-config` gains `--harness-model` / `--harness-effort` (`--harness` selects the entry, defaulting to the project's primary harness). Response DTO mirrors the config shape; usage errors exit 2.
- **Dashboard UI** — Project Settings gets a "Harness overrides" section: one row per configured harness with model / mode / reasoning-effort pickers, an add-row picker that excludes already-configured harnesses, and per-row removal. Effort validation is now shared with agent rows via `useModelTuning`. All new strings are translated in the 8 supported locales.

## Tests

All commands run on the rebased+squashed commit (`ao/agent-orchestrator-9/model-effort`).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cd backend && go build ./...` | pass |
| `cd backend && go vet ./...` | pass |
| `golangci-lint run --path-mode=abs --timeout=10m ./...` (v2.12.2) | 0 issues |
| `go test ./internal/domain/... ./internal/httpd/...` | pass |
| `go test ./internal/cli/` | pass (needs `env -u AO_SESSION_ID`) |
| `go test ./internal/session_manager/...` (minus 4 spawn tests, see gap below) | pass |
| `npm run frontend:typecheck` | pass |
| `npx vitest run ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx i18n/instance.test.ts ModelTuningControls.test.tsx AgentModelCombobox.test.tsx` | 4 files / 77 tests pass |
| API drift: `go generate ./internal/httpd/apispec/...` + openapi-typescript 7.13.0 regen | no diff |
| Full `npx vitest run` | 4574 passed / 10 failed — all pre-existing environment failures, see gap 2 |

New coverage: per-harness layering (harness entry beats base config; role override wins only when its pinned harness matches the launch harness — regression test for #5129 semantics), CLI flag parsing/usage errors, and UI add/load/save/remove of harness override rows asserted down to the `PUT /projects/{id}/config` payload.

### Local environment gaps (verified pre-existing, not introduced here)

1. 4 `TestSpawn_*` tests in `session_manager` cannot run on this macOS host: the suite replaces `PATH`, hiding the installed `tmux`, so it fails with `prerequisite missing: tmux required on macOS`. Reproduced identically on baseline `b696ac35f`; CI (Linux + tmux) covers these.
2. Full frontend suite: `src/landing/**` (missing built `@ao/shared/constants` + `cheerio` in this worktree), `src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts` (Electron binary not installed), and load-sensitive flakes (`GlobalSettingsForm`, `browser-history-store`, `KeyboardShortcutsSettingsDialog`) pass in isolation. None touch this diff.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Semantics note:** role-override model/effort/mode only apply when the role's `harness` is empty (any harness) or matches the launch harness; permissions still always inherit. This is existing mainline behavior (#5129) and the per-harness layer sits *below* it, so a harness override never silently leaks to other harnesses.
- Unknown harness keys in `harnessConfigs` are accepted and stored but only take effect once that harness is launched; no schema-level enum enforcement yet.
- Effort values are validated against the model catalog when the catalog is available; with an empty/unavailable catalog any effort string is accepted rather than blocked (avoids test-time dependence on network catalogs).

title: fix(frontend): optimistic session-kill navigation (fixes #5142 bounce)
body:
Code changes: +226 -55  
Tests: +350 -20  
Others: +0 -0  

Builds on #5143 with the navigation goal from #5142, and fixes the two bugs we hit while reviewing that PR in a real Electron build.

### Problem (in #5143 as-landed)
1. **Navigation never ran from the sidebar.** Kill used `mutate({ onSuccess })` after `markTerminated` removed the row from the cache. That unmounted `SessionActions`, so TanStack Query skipped the mutate callback (`hasListeners() === false`) and the route stayed on the dead session.
2. **Optimistic remove flickered.** Even after moving nav earlier, CDC/workspace refetch could write a still-alive snapshot back, then the completed kill removed it again.

### Fix
- Navigate + mark terminated in `onMutate` (optimistic).
- Track pending kill IDs and re-apply them in `fetchWorkspaces` so refetch/CDC cannot resurrect the row mid-kill.
- Cancel in-flight workspace queries on mutate; reinforce + await invalidate on success; roll back on error.

### Test plan
- [ ] Open a project with 2+ worker sessions; view one; sidebar trash → switches immediately, row stays gone (no bounce).
- [ ] Kill last worker → orchestrator or project board.
- [ ] Topbar / inspector kill still navigate consistently.
- [ ] Failed kill restores the session in the list.

Supersedes the review feedback on #5143; prefer landing this branch (or cherry-picking the tip commit onto #5143).

title: fix(browser): make agent screenshot resilient and report command timeouts correctly
body:
Code changes: +51 -6  
Tests: +134 -0  
Others: +15 -0 (generated API artifacts)

Fixes #5437.

## Problem

`ao browser screenshot` always failed with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` for pages living in AO's hidden `WebContentsView` (e.g. anything opened via `ao preview`), while every other `ao browser` command worked. Three cooperating defects:

1. **The capture stalled.** `screenshot` was the only native action that bypassed `queueNativeOperation`/`ensureNativeActiveTab`, and CDP frame capture never resolves against the hidden/occluded WebContents.
2. **A timeout race.** The Electron-side native timeout (`COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 60s`) exactly equals the daemon's 60s REST `middleware.Timeout`, so the daemon deadline always fired first.
3. **The deadline was mis-mapped.** `writeBrowserError` has no context-error case, so the raw `context.DeadlineExceeded` fell through to the envelope's generic transient branch and was rendered as a retryable `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — hence the report's "momentarily unavailable, please retry" forever.

## Fix

**Electron (`browser-view-host.ts`, `agent-browser-runtime.ts`)**
- Screenshot now goes through `queueNativeOperation` + `ensureNativeActiveTab` like every other native action.
- New `SCREENSHOT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30s` threaded through `run()`'s optional `timeoutMs`, so a stalled capture fails well inside the daemon's 60s REST deadline.
- On native `AGENT_BROWSER_TIMEOUT`, fall back to `webContents.capturePage()` — the same mechanism the working interactive screenshot path uses on hidden views — enforcing the existing 5 MB cap and returning the same result shape. Empty captures raise `SCREENSHOT_UNAVAILABLE`; non-timeout errors propagate unchanged.

**Daemon (`controllers/browser.go`)**
- Request deadlines now map to **504 `BROWSER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`** ("Browser command timed out waiting for the desktop browser runtime") instead of the misleading 503; native `AGENT_BROWSER_TIMEOUT` maps to 504 as well (previously 422). No CLI change needed — it already surfaces envelope code/message/request id.
- OpenAPI spec + generated TS types regenerated (`npm run api`).

## Verification

- `go test -race` on all touched `httpd` packages: green; new controller cases cover both timeout paths.
- Focused vitest (158 passed, incl. 5 new cases: native passthrough, timeout → `capturePage` fallback, empty fallback, non-timeout passthrough, timeout forwarding); full `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Manually in a dev instance against scratch data: created a session, `ao preview index.html`, `ao browser screenshot` — PNG produced (previously 100% `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` in this setup).
- Full backend/frontend suites show only pre-existing environment-dependent failures (missing `goose`/`tmux` binaries, landing-site deps not installed), verified identical on the clean tree.

title: fix(desktop): play a bundled notification sound instead of shell.beep()
body:
Code: +101 −15
Tests: +76 −4
Files removed: 0

## What

The desktop app plays a bundled notification sound for `needs_input` / `ready_to_merge` instead of calling `shell.beep()`. On Linux it rings for every agent question regardless of window focus.

## Why

Fixes #5514. On Linux `shell.beep()` writes `\a` to `/dev/console` or `/dev/tty`, and a launcher-started app can open neither, so the sound toggle never made a sound there. On top of that the renderer dropped a `needs_input` notification whenever it believed the user was already watching that session — a belief Wayland makes unreliable (a window on another workspace still reports focused and visible), so even a working sound stayed quiet.

## How

- `frontend/src/main.ts:337` — main sends `notifications:playSound` to the shell renderer; `shell.beep()` stays only as the fallback when no shell is alive or the renderer reports `notifications:soundFailed`.
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/notification-sound-player.ts` — plays `assets/notification.mp3` (78 KB, Pixabay content license, no attribution required) through `new Audio()`, reporting once on decode error or rejected `play()`.
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/notifications.ts` — the renderer always forwards the notification and passes `watched` as a hint instead of swallowing it.
- `frontend/src/main.ts:2379` — on Linux the sound ignores focus/`watched`; macOS and Windows keep the previous gating (sound and toast only when unfocused and not on that session). Toast, dock bounce and taskbar flash still skip when the user is looking.
- `frontend/src/main.ts:2394` — the OS toast is `silent` whenever our sound plays, so macOS and Windows stop layering the system chime on the beep (that double sound predates this PR).

title: fix(session): bound spawn readiness and rollback
body:
Code changes: +117 -36  
Tests: +206 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## Summary

Fixes the two failure modes behind the partial `ao spawn` state reported with Kimi:

* Caps prompt readiness polling against the caller deadline and reserves five seconds for fallback prompt delivery.
* Runs every rollback stage with its own detached, bounded cleanup context, including early seed row failures, TUI runtime cleanup, Chat controller cleanup, workspace cleanup, and final session termination.
* Avoids the shared rollback deadline bug in #5523, where a slow first cleanup step could starve all later cleanup.

Addresses #5489 and #5536. Supersedes the rollback approach in #5523.

## Tests

* Added exact 90 second readiness versus 60 second request deadline coverage, plus end to end fallback delivery coverage.
* Added TUI rollback coverage where runtime cleanup exhausts its budget before workspace and lifecycle cleanup.
* Added Chat rollback coverage where controller shutdown exhausts its budget.
* Added early workspace creation timeout coverage for detached seed row rollback.
* All focused regression tests pass.
* All other `internal/session_manager` tests pass when excluding four preexisting macOS tmux lookup failures.
* `go vet ./internal/session_manager` passes.
* golangci-lint v2.12.2 passes for the changed package.
* Frontend typecheck could not run because this worktree does not have the `vite/client` and `vitest/globals` type dependencies installed.

## Risk

The fallback prompt may be sent before the harness readiness marker when the HTTP deadline is close. This is the existing timeout fallback behavior, now reached before the request is canceled. Rollback remains best effort, but each stage receives an independent 30 second budget so one stuck cleanup cannot suppress later lifecycle cleanup.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode sessions do not expose AO approval modes
body:
### What went wrong?

OpenCode sessions do not provide AO’s approval-policy controls (for example, default/manual approvals, accept edits, auto-approve, or approve-for-me).

In Chat mode, OpenCode advertises its own `mode` options (such as Build, Plan, and custom agents). AO treats that as a provider-owned mode and hides the generic approval picker, but does not map any OpenCode configuration to equivalent approval policies. Users can select an execution mode but cannot control permission behavior.

In TUI mode, AO currently maps only `bypass-permissions` to OpenCode’s `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. AO’s `default`, `accept-edits`, and `auto` policies all launch OpenCode identically and defer to the user’s existing OpenCode `permission` configuration.

Expected behavior:

- OpenCode sessions should expose only permission choices AO can apply faithfully.
- Either map AO approval policies to supported OpenCode permission configuration, or show an explicit two-choice control such as “Use OpenCode configuration” and “Allow all permissions.”
- The Chat and TUI surfaces should communicate the same effective permission behavior.

title: bug(settings): Claude Code shows Logged in when claude auth status says loggedIn:false
body:
## Bug

**Settings → Harness** shows Claude Code as **Logged in** / authorized while the local Claude CLI reports `loggedIn: false`. Chat correctly surfaces the existing **Sign in again to keep going** banner (`claude auth login`), so Settings and Chat disagree.

![Settings Harness shows Claude Code Logged in](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-settings-logged-in-false-positive/.issue-assets/claude-settings-logged-in-false-positive/attachment-1.png)

![Chat reauth banner asks for claude auth login](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-claude-settings-logged-in-false-positive/.issue-assets/claude-settings-logged-in-false-positive/attachment-2.png)

**Source:** live reporter observation in AO chat | **Reported by:** @prateek | **Analyzed against:** `a185d24bad8aedfbe6a57a81d58b623246a9111b`
**AO:** `dev` (daemon on port 3001) | **OS:** macOS arm64 Darwin 25.5.0 | **Claude Code:** firstStartVersion `2.1.275` (native install)
**Confidence:** High — live `claude auth status`, `~/.claude.json` shape, `/api/v1/agents/readiness`, and `AuthStatus` code path agree.

## Reproduction

1. Have Claude Code installed but not logged in (or logged out). Confirm:
   ```bash
   claude auth status
   # {"loggedIn":false,"authMethod":"none",...}
   ```
2. Ensure `~/.claude.json` still has a non-empty `userID` from first start (no `oauthAccount` required).
3. Open **Settings → Harness** (or hit refresh).
4. Observe Claude Code row: **Installed** + green **Logged in**.
5. Meanwhile `/api/v1/agents/readiness` returns:
   ```json
   "authentication": { "state": "authorized", "reason": "Claude Code appears signed in." }
   ```
6. Spawn / use a Claude Code chat session → Chat shows **Sign in again to keep going**.

## Live evidence (this machine)

- `claude auth status` → `loggedIn: false`, `authMethod: none`
- `~/.claude.json` keys include `userID` / install metadata only — **no** `oauthAccount`, **no** `hasAvailableSubscription`, **no** Anthropic env credentials
- `GET /api/v1/agents/readiness` → `claude-code.authentication.state = "authorized"` (fresh check)
- `GET /api/v1/agents` lists `claude-code` under `authorized`

No credential contents were inspected beyond redacted key presence.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/claudecode.go` `AuthStatus` short-circuits on `claudeLocalAuthStatus` **before** running the authoritative `claude auth status` probe.

`claudeConfigAuthStatus` treats a non-empty `userID` in `~/.claude.json` as proof of login:

```go
if strings.TrimSpace(userID) != "" {
    return ports.AgentAuthStatusAuthorized, true, nil
}
```

That `userID` is written on first Claude Code start (install/analytics identity) and survives machines that never finished login / are logged out. The CLI probe that correctly returns `loggedIn: false` never runs.

`HarnessSettingsSection.tsx` then maps `authentication.state === "authorized"` to the green **Logged in** affordance.

## Fix

1. Prefer the bounded `claude auth status` CLI probe over durable config identity markers; keep env credentials (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) as a fast definitive path.
2. Stop treating bare `userID` as authorized (even as a config fallback) — same change proposed in closed [PR #3289](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3289).
3. Use `oauthAccount` / `hasAvailableSubscription` only when the CLI probe is unavailable / unparseable.
4. Regression tests: config with only `userID` must not short-circuit to authorized; full `AuthStatus` must honor `loggedIn: false` from the CLI.

## Impact

- Settings falsely reassures users that Claude Code is ready.
- Spawns / chat still fail and require `claude auth login`, creating a confusing Settings-vs-Chat split.
- Same false-positive class as catalog root cause in [#4937](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4937).

## Related

- [#4937](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4937) — Claude OAuth expiry bypasses reauth banner; documents the same catalog `userID`/config short-circuit (this report is Settings-facing + never-logged-in, with Chat banner working).
- [PR #3289](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3289) — prior unmerged fix for bare-`userID` false positive.
- [#4973](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4973) — Codex Settings auth disagreeing with launch readiness (sibling class).

title: feat(onboarding): add the desktop onboarding flow (first-run)
body:
Code changes: +3734 -100  
Tests: +866 -0  
Others: +581 -0

## What this is

A first-run flow for the desktop app. `/onboarding` gets a new machine ready and drops the user into a project.

Eight screens: welcome, feedback, GitHub, cloud, project, orchestrator, workers, guide. The counter shows six, because project setup is one stage spread over three screens.

What it does. Installs `gh` in place when it is missing, then runs `gh auth login` in a daemon-owned terminal, and will not let you continue until that account is connected, since agents cannot open pull requests without it. Cloud sessions are optional, saved to settings, and never block the flow. The project step takes a git clone, a local folder, or a cloud project. The agent steps install and sign in without sending anyone out of the flow.

Installing and signing in also moved out of Harness Settings into a shared `AuthTerminalPanel`, which settings now reuses. That deletes 76 lines from `HarnessSettingsSection`.

## Scope

This touches onboarding and the two shell files it needs. Three things that used to be here are gone.

The landing previews. The step previews were the landing app's `FeedbackLoopDemo` and `FleetBoardDemo`, rewritten to render inside the renderer. `FeaturesSection` renders both, so that quietly changed the marketing site. Onboarding carries its own copies under `components/onboarding/previews` now, and the landing files match main again.

The home route. `_shell.index.tsx` was swapping the home screen for the board and adding a redirect to `/projects/scratch` when that was the only workspace. It now does the first-run gate and nothing else. Finishing onboarding lands on the home screen, which is what main does.

38MB of unreferenced assets under `assets/onboarding`. Nothing imported them.

## Checked

Ran the CI validation jobs locally against this head, using the workflow commands:

- `frontend`: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`
- `frontend`: `npx vitest run` with the pinned agent-browser binary. 334 files, 5127 passed, 6 skipped
- `frontend`: `npm run test:e2e:renderer`. 60 passed, run at `AO_E2E_PORT=5299` to stay off the Electron app on 5173
- `frontend`: `npm run browser-runtime:prepare`, and `npm ci --prefix src/landing` with `npm run icons:check --prefix src/landing`
- `packages/cloud-client`: `generate`, schema drift check, `typecheck`, 21 tests, `pack --dry-run`
- `packages/product-ui`: `typecheck`, 130 tests, `pack --dry-run`
- `mac-update-helper`: both `node --test` suites, helper builds for x64 and arm64 verified with `lipo`, and the Swift state tests

One gap: the `scan` job runs gitleaks, which is not installed on this machine, so it cannot run locally. It passed in CI on the previous head and this branch adds no secrets.

## Review findings

All seven inline findings are addressed in `610a58520`.

The gate no longer catches upgraded profiles. It waits for the workspace list and treats a profile that already has a registered project as established, then sets the flag so the decision sticks.

The folder row hands off to the create project flow, which owns the picker, the validator and the prepare-git steps, so a repository that still needs a remote now goes through them instead of advancing with an empty setup requirement. That deletes the step's own picker, validator and branch read, and with them the `repositorySetup` field that only that path ever set. The flow also shows its validation error in onboarding now, where the source picker's banner does not render.

The agent catalog refresh writes to the query cache instead of a local snapshot, so an install's invalidation is no longer outranked by a stale copy.

The GitHub step renders the installer's command for the unsupported case with the existing manual-command UI.

The project rows use the create project keys, so their copy is translated.

`onboardingTrigger` lost `remoteUrl`, which no caller supplied. The folder variant stays reachable, which is the change the review asked for.

## Second review round

All three P3 findings from the second pass are addressed in `8ccc82924`. The `AgentPicker` wrapper is gone and the step calls `AgentRolePicker` directly. `OnboardingProjectSetup` lost the write-only `lastPreparedPath` ref and the `preparedProject` prop it was seeded from. `useHarnessSetup` imports the active-install-job predicate instead of keeping a byte-identical copy.

That commit also adds a gate the reviewer did not ask for. The first agent step now holds Continue until at least one harness is installed and signed in, with a line under the picker saying so, because the flow previously let a user finish setup with an orchestrator that could not start. Two tests cover it: nothing installed, and installed but signed out.

title: feat(mobile): UX pass on the revamp — projects, workers, chat, Android sheets
body:
Mobile UX work on top of the merged revamp (#5349), audited screen by screen against comparable apps and then fixed in order: foundations first, then screens. 59 commits, all inside `packages/mobile`.

## Native dependencies — this cannot ship as an OTA

Four packages arrive: `react-native-reanimated`, `react-native-worklets`, `react-native-keyboard-controller` and `react-native-svg`. `runtimeVersion.policy` is `fingerprint`, so this needs a new build on both platforms. Everything else here is JS.

Worklets also closes an existing gap: `@expo/ui` peer-depends on it and it was not installed, so every bottom sheet in the app was running against an unmet peer.

## What changed

**Foundations**
- Shared spacing, radius, type and motion tokens, adopted only in files this work rewrites.
- Reduce Motion honoured app-wide, consumed inside `Dot` so every call site inherits it.
- Dynamic Type caps on shared primitives.
- A screen-state model, so a list whose poll has died stops looking live: a stale banner above the list, and the same unpaired state on all three tabs.
- One keyboard mechanism across spawn, the board and chat. The old sites listened for `keyboardDidShow`, which fires only after the IME has finished animating — that was the Android lag.

**Projects**
- Flat rows like the Workers list: the project name, its status, and a footer with the worker count and a compact orchestrator pill. Counts were chips that outranked the orchestrator; they are quiet text now.
- A project page: Workers / Needs you / Ready / Archived counts, the orchestrator as a row at worker-row height that opens from anywhere on it, then that project's workers through the Workers board itself — same grouping and row actions, archive included, rather than a second list that would drift.
- "Needs you" counts a waiting orchestrator, not just workers.

**Workers**
- Rename, pin, unpin and delete in the row's context menu, with the swipe rail and long-press coordinated so one rail is open at a time.
- Rows animate between sections. The board is one `FlatList` rather than a `SectionList`: a row changing section has to stay mounted to animate, and a `SectionList` unmounts it.
- The board's list is now shared with the project page.

**Chat**
- A pending request replaces the composer instead of sitting above it, swipeable between questions, restoring a typed draft and a chosen answer when you come back.
- Provider errors are reported once. The timeline used to show the same failure three times.
- Status banners take the desktop's shape: a one-line headline, at most two lines of detail, no raw provider text — and the informational ones close, keyed by what they report so they return when that changes.
- Turn settings say what they will actually do: model · effort · permissions.
- Delete session in the ⋯ sheet; renaming a session updates its title inside the session too.

**Notifications**
- The renderer's own lucide glyphs, drawn from its path data, one component for both platforms.
- Desktop's behaviour: a terminated session does not open on tap; it gives a haptic and says so, and restores only from its own button.

**Android**
- No sheet opens inside a sheet any more. Turn settings and Spawn show their choices as a page inside the sheet that is already open; Settings expands the theme choices and the update prompt in place.
- Row dividers draw every time. A hairline is under one physical pixel of dp, so rows on fractional positions rounded some away.
- Long-press menus carry icons, matching iOS.

**Drawer and chrome**
- Workers and Pull Requests draw lucide's Layers and GitPullRequestArrow, so both platforms show one glyph instead of per-platform lookalikes.
- The headers keep their title alone; the drawer's mark doubles as the connection lamp.
- Chat send buttons and the mic drop the blue: the mic sits on system glass on iOS and a frosted circle on Android.

**Report a problem**
- Opens the repo's own bug form, on this repo, labelled `bug` and `comp/mobile`, with the build, update, platform, device and daemon state filled in.
- Every report carries a `reported-from: ao-mobile` marker, because GitHub drops labels a reporter cannot apply — `is:issue "reported-from: ao-mobile"` finds them regardless.
- It opens in the browser on iOS, where the GitHub app takes the title and silently drops the form, and the whole report is copied to the clipboard as a fallback.

## Deliberately not done

- **Terminal keyboard** stays on the legacy listeners. It needs `keyboardDidShow` as well: `willShow` reports a height that still includes the accessory bar that screen hides, and its `didShow` corrector is what closes the resulting gap. Four of five keyboard sites are unified; the fifth carries a comment saying why.
- **Settings stays a sheet on Android** and the drawer keeps its edge swipe, both reverted after testing on device.
- **Android Spawn presentation** keeps `transparentModal`: it is a deliberate fix for the native sheet jumping detents when the IME appears.
- **Lock-screen presence** (Live Activities and an Android equivalent) is out of scope; its prerequisites are recorded, including a backend change, since the push payload carries no `requestId`.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` and `npm test` clean: 1,164 tests in 118 files. `expo export` builds for both platforms. Every screen was exercised on a physical iPhone 13 and a physical Android through a real daemon — spawning workers, letting them block on input, answering from the phone, killing the daemon mid-session to check the stale and error states — in both light and dark, with Reduce Motion on and off.

The lockfile is 271 lines of real change. Installing the native deps rewrote all 17,930 lines with spaces; it is reindented back to tabs.

## Draft

Draft because it wants a second pair of eyes on the native gate before it becomes a build, and because the four new packages mean nobody can take this as an update.

title: fix(chat): enclose the sent user message in light theme
body:
## Problem

In light theme a sent user message renders as bare floating text — no bubble around it at all.

The fill resolves to **one value step off the canvas**: `#f9f9f9` on `#fafafa`, a contrast ratio of **1.0087:1**.

Two things combine to cause it:

1. Light theme defines `--card` and `--background` as the same near-white (`oklch(0.985 0 0)`), so `--color-bg-secondary` cannot sit above the canvas. The rule's `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-bg-secondary) 78%, var(--color-bg-tertiary))` therefore washed the tertiary step almost entirely back into the canvas.
2. The same rule declared a `border-color`, but only the **queued** variant carries a `border` utility. On a sent bubble `border-width` stayed `0`, so that hairline never painted.

Dark theme was unaffected — its fill separates cleanly (`oklch(0.269)` on `0.185`).

## Fix

Take the unwashed `--color-bg-tertiary` step and actually paint the declared hairline. The hairline is needed because the surface stack alone cannot carry the enclosure when two of its levels collapse to one color — `--color-bg-tertiary` by itself is still only 1.05:1 against the canvas. This matches DESIGN.md, which reserves borders for structure a surface shift cannot supply.

Dark theme is deliberately left untouched, where a border would be decoration rather than structure.

The queued variant moves to its own rule so it keeps reading as not-yet-sent. Its `bg-transparent` was previously overridden by the unlayered fill; it now stays unfilled behind its dashed outline. A `data-queued` attribute carries the sent/queued distinction into CSS.

## Result

Rendered with the real light-theme token values:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Before** — sent | bare text, no chatbox |
| **After** — sent | enclosed bubble, visible hairline |
| **After** — queued | dashed, unfilled — still clearly unsent |

## Verification

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` — clean
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/` — 25 files, 680 tests passing, including a new test covering the `data-queued` DOM contract the light-theme CSS depends on
- Visually confirmed both themes against the real token values

title: P1: ao session restore cannot recover exited sessions
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem

`ao session restore <id>` only handles sessions marked `terminated`. A session can also be recoverable while marked `exited` with `isTerminated: false`, which is the state used when the agent process stops but AO preserves the worktree, terminal identity, and native conversation for in-place recovery.

For example, `agent-orchestrator-329` was reported as:

```json
{
  "status": "exited",
  "activity": {"state": "exited"},
  "isTerminated": false
}
```

Running `ao session restore agent-orchestrator-329 --project agent-orchestrator` returned `SESSION_NOT_RESTORABLE`.

## Current workaround

The backend resume endpoint works:

```text
POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/resume-agent
```

Calling it for `agent-orchestrator-329` returned HTTP 200 with `resumeMode: native` and moved the session to `idle`.

The current CLI exposes `restore` but does not expose `resume-agent`, so users cannot recover this state through the CLI.

## Requested behavior

Add exited-session recovery to the CLI. Possible designs:

1. Make `ao session restore <id>` dispatch to native resume when the session is exited and not terminated.
2. Add `ao session resume-agent <id>` and make `restore` explain which command applies based on session state.

The implementation should preserve the existing distinction between an exited agent process and a terminated AO session. It should not mark an exited session terminated just to make restore work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ao session restore <exited, non-terminated id>` successfully resumes the agent in place, or emits a clear redirect to a new `resume-agent` command.
- Terminated sessions continue to use the existing restore path.
- The CLI supports project scoping for the new or updated path.
- Tests cover exited orchestrator sessions and terminated sessions separately.

title: feat(review): support multiple configured reviewers
body:
## What

Add end-to-end support for multiple configured PR reviewers.

Previously, `--reviewer` accepted multiple reviewers but the review flow only used the first configured reviewer. This change makes all configured reviewers participate in the review lifecycle.

## Why

Fixes #5465

Multiple reviewers are useful for cross-provider reviews, but the existing implementation silently ignored reviewers after the first one.

This change ensures every configured reviewer evaluates the same PR HEAD and that the final review state reflects all reviewer results.

## How

* Execute all configured reviewers sequentially against the same PR HEAD.
* Track each reviewer independently with its own review/run state and harness attribution.
* Aggregate reviewer results at the PR level:

  * All reviewers approve → `up_to_date`
  * Any reviewer requests changes → `changes_requested`
  * Any reviewer fails, is cancelled, or has no verdict → `needs_review`
  * Any reviewer is still running → `running`
* Scope aggregate results to the current PR HEAD so previous commits cannot satisfy a new review.
* Update trigger, cancel, restore, and switch lifecycle paths to correctly handle multiple reviewer handles.
* Add `reviewerTerminals` to the API so multiple reviewer terminal states can be surfaced.
* Update frontend consumers while preserving the existing single-reviewer fallback behavior.
* Keep execution sequential for now; concurrency is intentionally left out of this change.

Reviewers should focus on the aggregation logic in `planner.go` and the multi-reviewer lifecycle handling in `review.go`, particularly restore/switch behavior and preservation of individual reviewer handles.

No database migrations are required.

## Testing

Validated locally with:

* Review package tests: **117 passed, 1 skipped on Windows**
* Frontend tests: **250 passed**
* Frontend TypeScript typecheck: **0 errors**
* `npm run api` — generated API output verified
* `git diff --check` — clean

Added regression coverage for:

* Multiple reviewers creating independent review runs
* Cancelling all configured reviewers
* Restoring multiple reviewers
* Switching reviewers without destroying selected reviewer handles
* Listing multiple reviewer terminals
* Preserving single-reviewer behavior
* Invalidating previous reviewer results when the PR HEAD changes
* Aggregate review states across multiple reviewers

The Windows skip is for a pre-existing `nodeRuntimeDir()` behavior and is unrelated to this change.

## Checklist

* [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
* [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
* [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
* [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
* [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat: reveal tab close button in the icon slot on hover
body:
Code changes: +47 -70
Tests: +10 -15
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Shell terminal tabs and session file tabs previously revealed their close button on the **trailing** edge of the tab on hover. Now, matching common browser/editor tab behavior:

- **Terminal tabs** (connected session strip): hovering or keyboard-focusing a tab fades the terminal glyph out and reveals the × in the icon's slot on the left.
- **File tabs**: same treatment — the × overlays the file icon's slot and appears on hover/focus. Dirty files keep the always-visible unsaved dot in that slot, which swaps to the × on hover.
- **Removed the per-tab "+" (add feedback) button** from file tabs. Whole-file feedback remains available from the file workspace header; the unused `files.addFileFeedback` i18n key is removed from all locales.

## Implementation notes

- Both tabs reuse `TerminalTabFrame`'s existing `actionLayout="overlay"` / `actionPosition="leading"` path — no new chrome was added; the close control stays a sibling button (never nested inside the tab button), so keyboard traversal and aria roles are unchanged.
- The glyph only fades when a close action actually exists (not while renaming or for optimistic terminals).

## Testing

- `SessionFileTabs.test.tsx`: asserts the icon hides on hover, the close button sits in the leading overlay, and the dirty dot swaps to the × on hover.

title: perf(landing): cut first-load weight from 2.8 MB to 0.96 MB
body: ## Why `https://orchestrator.inc/` shipped **2.8 MB** on first load, **2.2 MB of it images**, and almost all of those images were fetched at preload priority *before* the hero could paint. Root causes, in order of weight: 1. **`public/app-icons/cursor.svg` was 1.5 MB** — a 36×36 icon wrapping a 2000×2000 base64 PNG (1.17 MB gzipped over the wire). It was preloaded in ``, so it competed with the LCP image on every visit. Two lines in `FleetBoardDemo` referenced it; an identical **542 B** vector mark already existed at `app-icons/agents/cursor.svg`. 2. **47 image preloads in ``.** React 19 hoists a `` for every non-lazy `` rendered on the server, so every agent mark in every below-the-fold demo was fetched at top priority. 3. **`layout.tsx` preloaded five feature backgrounds on every route** — 374 KB downloaded on `/blog`, `/docs`, `/privacy`, where they are never rendered. 4. **No responsive delivery.** `output: "export"` forces `images.unoptimized`, so `next/image` emitted a single fixed-width source: phones downloaded the same 1440–1600 px art as desktops. 5. **Oversized icons**: agent marks at 384 px and 128 px rendered at 12–32 px; `ao-logo.svg` a 57 KB path blob for a 20 px mark. 6. **Duplicated libraries**: `framer-motion` *and* `motion` both installed and both imported; `geist/font/mono` (71 KB) preloaded for two below-the-fold demos next to the IBM Plex Mono the rest of the site uses. Separately, `public/` held **43 MB of PNG masters no page references**. `output: "export"` copies `public/` verbatim, so all of it was deployed. ## What changed - `app-icons/cursor.svg` deleted; `FleetBoardDemo` uses the vector mark. - `loading="lazy"` + `decoding="async"` on below-the-fold ``s. Preloads in the served HTML: **47 → 10**, and all 10 are hero elements. - Route-wide preloads removed from `layout.tsx`; the hero preloads itself through its own ``. - Hero: single-format WebP `srcset` (720/1080/1440). Single-format on purpose — with a `` the preload scanner and the element can pick different candidates and download the hero twice. - Feature backgrounds: `` with AVIF + WebP fallback at 640/960/1280, lazy. - Icons regenerated at 64 px; `ao-logo.svg` run through SVGO. - Source art moved to `assets/` (outside `public/`); `scripts/optimize-images.mjs` (`npm run images:optimize`) regenerates every shipped variant from it. - `framer-motion` removed (12 files now import `motion/react`); Geist Mono dropped for the site's IBM Plex Mono; `@sentry/nextjs` loads only if the error boundary fires. - `DEPLOYMENT.md` documents the Cloudflare cache rules for `/_next/static/*` (GitHub Pages serves everything `max-age=14400`, including content-hashed chunks, and Actions-based Pages deploys ignore `_headers`). ## Benchmarks Headless Chrome over CDP against both builds served from the same local static server (brotli for text, cold cache, fresh profile per run). **Runs are interleaved before/after per iteration**, so machine drift lands on both variants. Medians; LCP range in brackets. Harness and raw output: see "Reproducing" below. ### Desktop — 1440×900, 30 Mbps / 10 ms, no CPU throttle, median of 6 | Metric | Before | After | Δ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **LCP** | 336 ms [332–444] | **200 ms** [196–316] | **−40%** | | FCP | 144 ms | 116 ms | −19% | | `load` | 799 ms | 254 ms | −68% | | **Transfer** | 2820 KB | **959 KB** | **−66%** | | — images | 2224 KB | 452 KB | −80% | | — fonts | 168 KB | 98 KB | −42% | | — JS | 337 KB | 320 KB | −5% | | Requests | 100 | 73 | −27% | | CLS | 0.0007 | 0.0003 | — | ### Mobile — 390×844 @2x, Slow 4G (1.6 Mbps / 150 ms), 4× CPU, median of 5 | Metric | Before | After | Δ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **LCP** | 6080 ms [6068–6112] | **1652 ms** [1644–1696] | **−73%** | | FCP | 1028 ms | 988 ms | −4% | | `load` | 12764 ms | 3245 ms | −75% | | **Transfer** | 2486 KB | **648 KB** | **−74%** | | — images | 1906 KB | 154 KB | −92% | | Requests | 85 | 58 | −32% | | Total blocking time | 42 ms | 7 ms | −83% | | CLS | 0.0082 | 0.0029 | −65% | The run-to-run spread is ±2% on mobile and ±1% on desktop except for first-iteration warm-up, which is why the ranges are printed. ### Per asset (bytes on disk) | Asset | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `app-icons/cursor.svg` | 1,575,673 | **removed** | | hero background | 221,118 (1 size) | 152,500 @1440 / 87,232 @1080 / 37,304 @720 | | `feature3` | 143,680 | 69,808 webp / 40,283 avif @1280 · 6,688 avif @640 | | `agents/aider.png` | 93,930 | 4,132 | | `agents/agy.png` | 25,278 | 3,026 | | `agents/muse.png` | 20,037 | 3,189 | | `ao-logo.svg` | 57,373 | 22,540 | | `app-icons/terminal.png`, `coverage-aider.png` | 150,000 | **removed** (unreferenced) | | **Deployed `out/`** | **62.8 MB** | **17.6 MB** | ### Visual verification Full-page screenshots of both builds at 1440 px, captured after a stepped scroll so lazy art loads: - Page height identical: **7572 px → 7572 px** (no layout shift from the markup change). - Mean per-pixel difference across 8 horizontal bands: **≤ 2.4/255**, concentrated in the animated demo panels and attributable to re-encoding plus the mono-font swap. - Re-encoded art vs the old files at matched size: mean difference 2.5–2.7/255. - `ao-logo.svg` rasterized at 128 px before vs after SVGO: **max channel difference 1/255**. ## Honest caveats - **The Sentry change is hygiene, not 60 KB.** `@sentry/nextjs` was already mostly code-split; the eagerly-loaded chunk containing SDK code was 16 KB raw (~5 KB br). After the change no chunk on the landing page's initial graph contains it. My original estimate for this item was wrong; the measured first-load JS saving is ~2 KB, and the rest of the −17 KB JS is the `framer-motion`/`motion` de-duplication. - **Cache rules are documented, not applied.** They are Cloudflare dashboard config; repeat-visit gains are therefore not measured here. - **Lazy feature art can pop in** if a visitor scrolls faster than Chrome's ~1250 px lazy threshold loads. This is the trade for taking 374 KB out of the critical path. - The two terminal demos now render in IBM Plex Mono rather than Geist Mono. This is the one intentional visual change. - Benchmarks run against a local static server, not GitHub Pages behind Cloudflare; they isolate this diff rather than predicting absolute field numbers. - `sharp` was already a devDependency; `svgo` is added as one. Neither ships to visitors. ## Reproducing ```bash cd frontend/src/landing && npm ci && npm run build # out/ # serve out/ with brotli, drive headless Chrome over CDP, interleave A/B, # report medians (harness kept out of the diff; happy to add it if useful) ``` `npm run images:optimize` regenerates every asset under `public/optimized`, `public/app-icons` and `public/ao-logo.svg` from `assets/`. ## Verification run - `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean (only the pre-existing `Cannot find module 'vitest'` errors in test files, unchanged by this PR). - `npm run build`: succeeds. - `npm run icons:check`: passes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(lifecycle): an agent's own review-thread reply is nudge-eligible - AO delivers the agent's own comment back to it as review work
body:
## Bug

An agent's **own** review-thread reply is nudge-eligible, so AO delivers the agent's words back to it as review feedback to "address and push fixes" for. Nothing in the nudge path checks whether the comment author is the identity the session itself comments and pushes with.

**Source:** maintainer local report (desktop app, macOS, this machine) | **Reported by:** maintainer | **Analyzed against:** `3e46ad3b4` (origin/main), observed on branch `8c4285c62`
**AO version:** `dev` | **Confidence:** High for the self-nudge mechanism; Medium for the resolved-state disagreement in Secondary below
**Priority:** medium - wastes agent turns, and becomes a feedback loop for any agent that replies to a review thread without resolving it

## Reproduction

1. Give a session a PR and set `sessions.auto_inject_review = 1`.
2. Have any reviewer (here: React Doctor, a GitHub App) open inline review threads.
3. From the session, reply on those threads using the same account AO pushes with (`gh api graphql addPullRequestReviewThreadReply`).
4. Wait for the next SCM poll.

The session receives a nudge whose body is its own reply, prefixed with *"The following 1 unresolved review comment(s) are on PR ... Address each comment and push fixes."*

## Live evidence

Session `agent-orchestrator-9`, [PR #5573](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5573):

| Time (UTC) | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 06:31:13 | React Doctor opens 12 inline threads (all `github-actions`, `__typename: Bot`) |
| 06:50:16 | Agent replies on all 12 threads as `AgentWrapper` (`__typename: User`) and resolves each via `resolveReviewThread` |
| 06:50:42 | SCM observer writes 12 threads `resolved=1, is_bot=0`, 12 bot comments `is_bot=1, resolved=1`, 12 agent replies `is_bot=0, resolved=1` |
| 06:50:42 | One nudge fires, keyed to the agent's own reply |

`pr.last_nudge_signature` recorded one attempt whose `seen` value is the pair
`PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6jpPWf` + `PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7xEbOT` (thread and comment IDs, NUL-separated).
`PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7xEbOT` is the agent's own reply on `RoadmapSlideshow.tsx:3`; the delivered
message quoted it back verbatim and told the agent to address it and push.

## Root Cause

Bot-ness is computed per *thread* as "every comment is a bot comment", so one reply declassifies the thread:

```go
// backend/internal/adapters/scm/github/observer_provider.go - scmThreadFromGraphQL
allCommentsBot := len(commentNodes) > 0
for _, cn := range commentNodes {
    if !isBotAuthor(author) { allCommentsBot = false }
    ...
}
out.IsBot = allCommentsBot
```

Persistence inherits that down onto comments, so the agent's reply lands as `is_bot=0`:

```go
// backend/internal/observe/scm/observer.go:1830
comments = append(comments, domain.PullRequestComment{..., Resolved: th.Resolved, IsBot: c.IsBot || th.IsBot, ...})
```

And the nudge filter only knows about `Resolved` and `IsBot` - never about who AO itself is:

```go
// backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:642 - prCommentObservations
if comment.Resolved || comment.IsBot { continue }
```

`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:265-283` then emits one nudge per surviving comment, so every self-authored reply is one more nudge (bounded only by `reviewMaxNudge`).

### Secondary, lower confidence

The delivered message asserted the comment was **unresolved**, yet every persisted row for that PR reads `resolved=1`, and the `resolveReviewThread` mutations completed 26 s before `pr.review_observed_at`. Either GitHub's GraphQL returned a stale `isResolved` for that one thread immediately after the mutation, or nudge evaluation and the resolved write disagree within a single poll. Pinning this needs daemon logs from the poll at `06:50:42Z`, which were not available locally; treating it as a separate, smaller defect is reasonable.

## Fix

Skip comments authored by the session's own provider identity when selecting nudge candidates. The identity is already available - `pr.author` is `AgentWrapper` on the PR row, and the SCM adapter authenticates as that account - so the filter can sit next to the existing one:

```go
// prCommentObservations
if comment.Resolved || comment.IsBot || isSelfAuthored(comment.Author, prAuthor) { continue }
```

Sourcing it from the SCM auth identity (a `whoami`-style lookup, cached per provider) is more correct than `pr.author`, since a human can also open a PR that a session later claims. Either way the check belongs in the lifecycle, not the adapter.

No fix pushed: choosing where the session's provider identity comes from is a design call, and getting it wrong would silently drop legitimate human feedback. Worth spawning an agent once that decision is made.

## Impact

- Agents burn turns "addressing" their own comments, and an agent that replies without resolving can be re-nudged up to `reviewMaxNudge` times with its own text.
- Interacts badly with [#2827](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2827): today bot review comments are dropped entirely, so agents rarely reply to bot threads. Fixing #2827 means agents *will* reply to them, turning every reply into a fresh nudge unless this is fixed first or alongside.
- The notification text is actively misleading - it labels a resolved, self-authored comment as an "unresolved review comment" needing a push.

## Related

- [#2827](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2827) - bot-authored review feedback never delivered (same filter, opposite failure mode; same live PR)
- [#2400](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2400) - deduped CI-failure nudge starves review/merge-conflict nudges (same nudge-selection code)
- [#1943](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/1943) - review-backlog dispatch path uninstrumented (why the Secondary section is unprovable from local state)
