title: fix(cloud/terminal): ignore zero-dimension resize instead of closing the socket
body:
## Problem

A cloud agent terminal in the browser connects, then flashes blank and reconnects in a loop (reported as "connected, then Connecting, then a glitch, then the terminal again", and "connected, blank screen, then the terminal"). Each cycle the user sees the screen wiped and repainted.

## Root cause (confirmed on staging with per-close diagnostics, not inferred)

The browser's first frame after every attach was a `resize` with `columns=0, rows=0`. A pane that fits while its element is not yet laid out (hidden behind the connecting cover, or mounted before layout) proposes a 0x0 grid.

The control plane treated a zero-dimension resize as invalid and closed the socket (`connection.Close(StatusPolicyViolation, "invalid terminal size")`). readTerminalInput returning ended the stream, so the client reconnected, which replays from sequence 0 with a screen reset (the blank flash), whereupon the pane fit at 0x0 again and the socket was closed again. An endless reconnect+flash loop.

Evidence from staging logs while the loop was live:
- Every looping socket died with `close_source=read`, nil error, `connected_ms` around 550 to 720ms.
- The first frame on those sockets was `type=resize columns=0 rows=0`.
- The one terminal in the same window that sent a valid `102x37` first frame never looped.
- After this fix, those exact terminal ids attached once more and held a stable open socket with no further closes.

## Fix

Ignore a zero-dimension resize (`continue`) instead of closing the socket. The frame carries no size to apply; the PTY keeps whatever size it already had, and the next real fit sends valid dimensions. This makes the control plane resilient to any client (a stale build, a parked or off-screen pane, a third party) rather than amplifying a benign client hiccup into a session-killing loop.

The renderer already guards `sendResize` against 0x0 in `cloud-terminal-mux.ts`; this closes the gap on the server side so the control plane never turns a 0x0 frame into a dropped session.

Also logs one line per socket close (`close_source`, `ws_close_status`, `connected_ms`) so a future terminal drop names its own cause without a redeploy. That is how this root cause was pinned.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/httpapi/`, `go test ./internal/httpapi/` all pass.
- Deployed to staging (surgical task-def swap, control plane only, no worker change). Verified in live logs: the two terminals that had been looping every ~2.5s each attached once more and then held an open socket with zero further closes; no short-lived (<2s) closes appeared after cutover. Deployment reached steady state on the fixed image.

## Scope

Control plane only. No migration. No worker binary change (no nodeops rebake needed). The renderer needs only a reload to pick up its existing 0x0 guard; no renderer code change is required for this fix.

title: feat: limit OMP model picker to providers with configured credentials
body:
Code changes: +265 -12
Tests: +202 -0
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

`omp models --json` lists every model in OMP's registry — including providers the user never authenticated — so the AO model picker offered choices that could only fail at launch (on a typical install: 321 models across 3 providers, only 2 configured).

Discovery now filters the parsed catalog against OMP's own credential stores — the same stores the adapter's auth probe (`omp/auth.go`) reads:

- `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` → `auth_credentials.provider` where `data` is non-empty and `disabled_cause IS NULL`
- fallback `auth.json` → entries with a non-empty `key`
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (project env, then process env) overrides the config dir, matching the auth probe

The configured provider set is folded into the catalog fingerprint, so enabling or disabling a credential invalidates the cached picker without a manual refresh.

Edge semantics:

- **No credential store at all** → fail open with the full catalog (covers env-var-only API-key setups AO cannot enumerate)
- **Store exists, every credential disabled** → empty catalog with a warning
- **Store unreadable** → unfiltered catalog plus a warning (never empties the picker on a probe error)
- Models without provider attribution are kept (fail-open if OMP changes its output shape)

Implementation: `modelcatalog` keeps ownership of per-agent discovery config reading (same pattern as claude/qwen/goose); the generic command-runner was extracted as `runModelCommand` with unchanged behavior for all other agents. No frontend or API contract changes — the picker consumes the same `GET /api/v1/agents/omp/models` response.

## Tests

- 10 new unit tests in `omp_test.go`: agent.db / auth.json / merged / disabled / empty / missing store cases, filter behavior (unattributed models kept), fingerprint stability + invalidation on provider-set change, binary-missing dispatch. All pass.
- Real-binary smoke check on a machine with `kimi-code` + `vercel-ai-gateway` configured and `moonshot` unconfigured: catalog filtered 321 → 304 models, all 17 `moonshot` entries removed, fingerprint populated (throwaway test, removed after passing).
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, gofmt clean; `omp` adapter package tests pass.

## Known gaps / risks

- Full `go test ./...` could not be validated on this Windows dev host: ~90 pre-existing failures at baseline (confirmed identical via `git stash`) from environment issues (temp-file ACLs, codex account sandbox expectations, git URL validation) plus 2 env-dependent modelcatalog tests (autohand/continue read the real home dir). These must be verified in CI.
- `golangci-lint` is not installed locally; the pinned v2.12.2 was run via `go run` on the changed package and reported only CRLF line-ending artifacts (untouched baseline files flagged identically; git normalizes to LF on commit).
- Providers authenticated purely via environment variables (e.g. `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`) with no credential-store entry cannot be enumerated; the filter fails open in that case by design.

title: fix(workspace): render untracked child-repo diffs in the Files inspector
body:
Code changes: +77 -18
Tests: +132 -1
Others: +8 -0 (i18n catalogs, one new key)

Closes #5363

## Root cause

Not a race or a slow request. A workspace-project session leaves every git-state section and the commit list zero-valued, so the Files review pane can only ask for the `combined` scope. That scope resolves diffs with `git diff <base> -- <path>`, which reports **nothing for an untracked file** — and a file an agent has just created is untracked.

So `/workspace/diffs` answered HTTP 200 with an empty patch. The renderer found no metadata for that path and fell through to a fallback card whose caption had no state that could ever replace `Loading diff...`. That is why every backing request succeeded while the visible render state never advanced, and why the reporter's audit saw healthy responses throughout.

The **File** action worked in the reported screenshot because the single-file `GetWorkspaceFile` endpoint already synthesizes this patch. Only the batch endpoint did not.

## Changes

**`workspace_review.go`** — the combined scope now synthesizes the added-file patch for untracked targets, exactly as `GetWorkspaceFile` already does. Tracked paths still go through `git diff` unchanged. git's own output is concatenated first so the 2 MB group cap drops synthesized content before anything git already reported.

Scoped deliberately to `combined`: it is the only scope that compares base..worktree, where an untracked file is a genuine addition. `staged`, `unstaged` and `committed` have no untracked side by definition and are untouched.

**`WorkspaceReviewPane.tsx`** — the fallback card now distinguishes a batch still in flight from one that settled without a diff. A settled miss reaches `Unable to load this diff.` with a **Retry** action beside the existing **File** action, so a future gap here is visible and actionable instead of an indefinite spinner. `Load diff` and `Retry` are mutually exclusive by construction, so the card never grows a third button.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A changed file in a multi-repository workspace renders its diff
- [x] Rendering reaches success or a retryable error — the card resolves the moment its batch settles (~350 ms in the reported audit) rather than hanging
- [x] The error state includes Retry and Open file actions
- [x] A two-repository integration test verifies this path

## Tests

`TestGetWorkspaceDiffsIncludesUntrackedChildRepoFile` builds a root workspace repo plus `alpha` and `beta` child repos, creates an untracked file in one and a tracked modification in the other, and asserts both patches arrive. `TestGetWorkspaceDiffsCombinesUntrackedAndTrackedPathsInOneRepo` covers the mixed single-repo case. The renderer test covers a two-repository group response: one group renders, the other settles empty and offers Retry.

Both new backend tests were confirmed to fail against the unfixed code before the fix was written.

## Validation

Backend, post-rebase, on an idle machine: `go test ./...` 169 packages green, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `go build`/`go vet` clean. Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean post-rebase; the full renderer sweep (147 files, 2521 tests) was green pre-rebase and the remaining post-rebase sweep is left to CI.

## Intentional omissions

- **No client-side timeout.** The state resolves when the request settles. An artificial abort risks false failures on slow large workspaces, where the server's own budget is 15 s.
- **No `diff_rendered` / `diff_render_failed` telemetry.** Requested in an issue comment but not in the acceptance criteria, and framed there as instrumentation to size production impact. It needs session kind and workspace kind plumbed into a component that does not receive them today — better as its own PR.

## No API contract change

`dto.go` and `openapi.yaml` are untouched, so no regeneration is needed. The only consumer of `GetWorkspaceDiffs` is the `/workspace/diffs` controller.

title: fix(board): keep a crowded PR row inside the card
body:
## The bug

A session with many open PRs renders them as one row per state. On a board card
with ten open PRs the numbers ran into each other and past the card's right edge,
clipping the trailing ones:

`#5146#5147#5148#5149#5217#5218#5219#5221#5223#5290`

## Why it still happened

#5565 let that row wrap, which fixed the common case. But wrapping was only the
row's *preference*, not its floor: every entry kept `min-w-0` and the default
`flex-shrink: 1`, so any layout that put more entries on a line than fit still
compressed them — and the PR number is a bare `<span>` with nothing to clip it,
so its glyphs painted straight over the neighbouring entry and out past the card.

Measured on the pre-fix row, ten open PRs overflowed their own links by 43px and
escaped a 237px card.

## The fix

Make wrapping the only way a crowded row can resolve.

- `shrink-0` on each entry, so a row that runs out of width wraps instead of
  squeezing its entries into each other.
- `max-w-full` plus a truncating number for the one case wrapping cannot fix —
  a single entry wider than the whole row — which now ellipsizes inside the card
  rather than escaping it.

## No visual change where the board actually renders

Board lanes are `>=256px`, and at every width from 200px up the rendered layout
and the card's measured height are identical to `main`. The change only takes
effect in the states that were already broken.

## Verification

- New regression test in `SessionsBoardView.test.tsx`; it fails on `main` and
  passes here.
- `packages/product-ui`: typecheck clean, 129 tests pass.
- `frontend`: typecheck clean, `SessionsBoard.test.tsx` 48 tests pass.
- Checked in the running renderer with a ten-PR and a twelve-PR card (mixed
  states, a 7-digit number, review comments): zero overflow, zero overlap.

title: fix(cloud/ui): cloud task composer + terminal connecting/connected UX, and the fresh-session blank flash
body:
## What

Cloud project UI/UX fixes for the New Task composer and the agent terminal's connecting/connected surface, plus the fix for the fresh-session terminal blank flash. Frontend only: 16 files, zero control-plane or Go changes. This is the branch that has been running on staging for review.

## Fixes

**Task composer (cloud projects)**
- The harness dropdown on New Task now lists only the harnesses a cloud project actually supports (claude-code, codex, cursor), instead of the full local catalog.
- The model selector no longer shows a spinner when no harness is selected; it shows a static placeholder until a harness is chosen, then the real model combobox.

**Terminal connecting / connected surface**
- A connected agent terminal shows a single small status dot, not the full "Connected" button.
- After a terminal is revealed there is no dot at all (no lingering green dot top-right).
- While connecting, the pane shows ONE centered "Connecting" cover and ONE elapsed timer (top-right), replacing the three overlapping loaders that used to stack.
- The connecting cover no longer flashes back over an already-visible terminal on a transient reattach (it is latched on first reveal).

**Fresh-session blank flash (worker-epoch flip)**
- A fresh cloud worker attaches optimistically before its sandbox is up, when the worker epoch is still unknown; the moment the worker comes online the polled epoch flips from undefined to its first value. That value was folded into the terminal cache key, the reconcile-loop dispose test, and the connecting-cover identity, so the flip tore down the just-attached pane and remounted it: a from-0 replay with a screen reset that the user saw as connected then blank then terminal.
- Fix: treat the unknown to first-known transition as the worker coming online for the SAME terminal and adopt the epoch in place. The worker cache key no longer carries the epoch (only handle plus restore nonce); a change BETWEEN two known epochs (idle-resume or restore) still re-mints via the reset nonce (new advanceEpoch action); the connecting-cover latch keys on the handle only. Restore and idle-resume re-mint are preserved.
- Confirmed on staging: each fresh session logged exactly one browser attach to the same terminal id and epoch (before the fix, two attaches with a clean close between).

## CP dependency

The blank-flash fix has a small control-plane half that is already deployed on staging: a zero-dimension terminal resize is ignored instead of closing the socket (see #5584). This renderer change is independent of it (different files) and does not require any further CP deploy; the shared staging CP already carries it.

## Testing

- Component tests updated and passing: TerminalPane (retained-cache remount and connecting-cover behavior, plus a new regression test that the first-epoch flip does not remount), SessionView, XtermTerminal, terminal-reset-store.
- i18n keys added or updated across all 8 catalogs (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, zh-CN).
- typecheck clean for the changed files.

## Scope

Frontend only. No migration. No control-plane change. i18n coverage updated.

title: test(browser): pin wedged-runtime broker behavior for #5369
body:
## Summary

Regression tests for the browser-runtime wedge behind #5369: a desktop (Electron) main process that is busy, asleep, or network-wedged keeps its broker socket attached, so every `POST /api/v1/browser/commands` waits for the caller's context while `GET /api/v1/browser/status` keeps reporting `connected: true`. The deterministic repro (`kill -STOP` / `-CONT` of the Electron main process) and the fingerprint proposal were posted in [#5369 (comment)](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5369#issuecomment-5734580482); this PR turns that scenario into Go test coverage.

Test-only, complementing the open #5484 (reconnect wait + typed codes) and #5552 (command timeout reporting): the attached-but-unresponsive runtime path is not covered there.

## What is covered (new `broker_wedge_test.go`)

- **Bounded deadline failure with a silent runtime** — `Execute` with an attached runtime that never answers returns `context.DeadlineExceeded`, emits a `cancel` frame on the wire for the expired request id, and leaves the pending registry empty. The deadline path had no coverage; cancel frames were only exercised for explicit `context.Canceled` (#3732).
- **Next command after a wedge stays bounded** — fresh request id, same typed deadline failure, and a late result for the expired request is ignored without disturbing the registry; the broker keeps serving commands afterwards.
- **Status during a wedge** — `Status()` reports `Connected: true` while a command is in flight unanswered. Pinned as the documented current contract; surfacing a degraded state remains up to the #5369 fix.
- **Replacement connection recovers the broker** — a second runtime handshake fails stale in-flight commands with `ErrUnavailable` and then carries new commands end to end.

## Testing

```
go test ./internal/browserruntime -count=1        # pass
go test ./internal/browserruntime -count=1 -race  # pass
gofmt -l .                                        # clean
```

New tests complete in ~0.3 s total; all existing package tests pass unchanged.

Refs #5369

title: fix(desktop): offer Resume agent when an agent exits but its session lives
body:
Code changes: +245 -81  
Tests: +421 -8  
Others: +0 -0  

Fixes the "no way to spin it back" dead end: an agent that exits without terminating its session (`/exit`, Ctrl+C, a provider usage limit) left the pane showing **TERMINAL ENDED — "This terminal process ended, but the session is not marked terminated yet."** with no control anywhere.

Refs #4936, #3875.

## The bug is in the UI, not the daemon

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/resume-agent` already recovers this state perfectly — it returns `resumeMode: "native"`, i.e. a real `codex resume` of the original conversation. Worktree, branch, and history are all intact. `ao session resume-agent <id>` has always worked.

What broke is that every recovery affordance was gated on `sessionIsActive`, which reports **row** liveness:

```ts
sessionIsActive = session.isTerminated !== true && session.status !== "terminated"
```

A Ctrl+C'd session is *not* terminated, so that returns `true`, so `canRestoreSession` is `false`, so the strip renders the message and no button.

**Orchestrators had no path at all.** `ResumeAgentControl` was the one surface with the correct gate (`activity?.state !== "exited"`), but it lives on the inspector's Summary view — and `SessionInspector.tsx:207` filters the view list down to `["browser"]` for orchestrator sessions, so it can never be reached. Workers had one escape hatch via the rail; orchestrators had zero.

## Changes

- **Extract `ResumeAgentControl`** and mount it on the terminal-ended strip — where you are standing when the agent dies. It self-gates, so the strip needs no knowledge of when resume applies. The inspector's wrapper `div` moved to its call site so the component is layout-free and usable in both.
- **`sessionAgentExited`** added beside `sessionIsActive` in `types/workspace.ts`, naming process liveness as distinct from row liveness.
- **`showEndedState` now includes it.** An agent can exit while its tmux pane survives on a `cat` keep-alive (#3875), so the mux never reports `exited` and the strip — carrying the only recovery control — stayed hidden in exactly the state it exists for. Without this the fix only covers harnesses that happen to close their PTY.
- **Clicking Orchestrator resumes an exited orchestrator** instead of navigating to a dead terminal. `newestActiveOrchestrator` counts an exited-but-alive orchestrator as active, so the button routed you straight back into the dead pane.
- **Auxiliary terminals ignore the worker exit state.** The keep-alive fallback now applies only to the worker target, so an attached shell or reviewer terminal stays unobscured when the worker agent exits.
- **Active agent switches keep ownership.** Both orchestrator launchers open the existing session instead of calling `resume-agent` while `activeAgentSwitch` is present.
- **Resume failures stay visible and in place.** The shared launcher returns mutation errors through its existing board/topbar feedback; the sidebar uses the existing error toast and does not navigate into the dead terminal.

Restore (terminated rows) and Resume (live row, dead agent) are now both reachable and mutually exclusive — they never both render.

## Why click-driven and not automatic

Auto-relaunching on the exit event was considered and rejected. `cli/agent_process.go:74` does `_ = child.Wait()` — **the exit code is discarded**, so `/exit`, Ctrl+C, OOM, and a usage limit all post the identical `{state: "exited", event: "process-exited"}`. There is no signal to branch on, and auto-restarting the usage-limit case (the original report) is a hot loop against a metered API; #3875 is the same shape, where every relaunch reproduces the identical failure.

This also matches the boundary the daemon already draws: `reconcileLive` auto-relaunches when the *runtime* died (reboot, tmux server killed) but adopts and stops when only the agent exited. A click is the intent signal.

## Tests

Regression coverage includes:

| Test | Regression it catches |
|---|---|
| posts resume-agent from the strip for a worker / orchestrator | wrong endpoint or hidden button |
| shows the strip even when the mux never reported an exit | the `showEndedState` hole |
| keeps attached shell/reviewer terminals unobscured after worker exit | false ended strip over a live auxiliary terminal |
| opens a switching orchestrator without resuming from either launcher | guaranteed `resume-agent` conflict during agent handoff |
| surfaces rejected orchestrator resume requests from both launchers | silent board/topbar failure or sidebar navigation into the dead terminal |
| offers restore and not resume once the row is terminated | the two actions colliding |

The auxiliary-terminal regression fails for both targets without the worker-target guard; both launcher regressions fail without the switch guard, and rejected-request coverage verifies both visible feedback and no dead-terminal navigation.

- `npm run frontend:typecheck` — clean
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.test.tsx` — 55 passed
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/ShellTopbar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx` — 147 passed

Two renderer tests (`SettingsDialog`, `TopbarOpenEditorButton`) fail only under full-suite parallel load and pass in isolation; both are timing-sensitive and untouched by this diff. `src/landing/**` failures are local-only — `@ao/shared` is not installed in this worktree, and CI installs it.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Ceiling: the strip still needs to mount, so a harness that neither closes its PTY nor reports an exit is out of reach. That's the supervisor-side half — PR #5014 is raising it for OMP.
- The strip's copy (`terminal.sessionEndedNotTerminated`) still narrates the dead end. Left alone deliberately: it reads fine beside a button, and rewording it stales 8 locale files.
- Not touched: the command palette's resume item (still excludes orchestrators and calls `/restore`), and the orchestrator inspector's Browser-only filter. Both are separate calls.

**#4936 is assigned to @ronishrohan** — flagging so this doesn't collide with work already in progress.

title: [Bug]: persistenthost package fails to compile on Windows — host_race_test.go uses syscall.Kill with no build tag
body:
### What went wrong?

Went to run the backend suite on Windows and it dies before any test runs:

```
# github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost [.test]
internal\adapters\chatdriver\persistenthost\host_race_test.go:86:33: undefined: syscall.Kill
internal\adapters\chatdriver\persistenthost\host_race_test.go:95:34: undefined: syscall.Kill
FAIL	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost [build failed]
```

`host_race_test.go` uses `syscall.Kill(-pid, syscall.SIGKILL)` in two `t.Cleanup` calls to tear down the spawned hosts. That's POSIX-only — killing a process group via negative PID doesn't exist on Windows.

The file just has no build constraint on it. Looks like an oversight rather than intent, since everything else platform-specific in that package is already split properly (`child_unix.go`/`child_windows.go`, `spawn_unix.go`/`spawn_windows.go`). Came in with #4766 by the looks of the history.

Sticking `//go:build unix` at the top fixes it and keeps the tests running everywhere they currently pass.

Couple of things that make this more annoying than a normal platform-skipped test:

- It's a *build* error, not a test failure, so `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` both blow up on Windows regardless of what you touched. Took me a while to convince myself it wasn't my own change.
- persistenthost is the detached host layer behind Codex and the ACP chat providers, so none of the restart/reconnect behavior has any Windows coverage right now, and a real regression there would be hidden behind this.

Doesn't look like a dupe of #3687 — that one's about tests that run and fail on Windows (path assumptions, TempDir cleanup). This one won't compile at all.

Probably worth flagging on #5416 too, since that turns on Windows Go tests in CI and will hit this straight away.

One thought for later: those two tests cover genuinely cross-platform behaviour (stale descriptor handling, the `O_EXCL` launch lock), so a Windows equivalent would be better than just excluding them. The build tag is enough to unblock though.

Windows 11, go1.26.5, on main @ 8e486821.

title: fix(chat): dock the agent question on the composer
body:
Code changes: +619 -466  
Tests: +70 -11  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

A structured question (`activityKind: "user_input"`) rendered as a full-width accent card in the transcript, and it **stayed there after it was answered** — an `AGENT NEEDS YOUR INPUT` banner with an "Answered" receipt, permanently occupying scrollback for a decision already made.

## Change

The question moves to the composer, where the pending approval already lives:

- **Pending** → docks directly above the input bar, below the queued-message dock.
- **Answered / expired** → renders nothing. `TimelineItem` now returns `null` for `user_input` in *all* states, so the transcript keeps only the conversation.

`ElicitationCard.tsx` → `ElicitationDock.tsx`, rendered from `ChatComposer`'s stack via a new `elicitation` slot instead of from the timeline. Git scores the test file at 96% similar, so it moves as a rename; the component is rewritten far enough (47%) that it sits below git's default 50% threshold, so `git log --follow` will not cross it without `-M30%`. Treat the component as a delete-and-add for history purposes.

## Design

The dock borrows the **queued-message dock's** chrome — `--radius-chat-composer`, `border-border-strong`, `bg-surface`, `shadow-sm`, the same header metrics and `min-h-10` row height, and the `queue-dock-enter` entrance — so the two things that can sit on the composer read as one surface. The footer uses **`ApprovalCard`'s** pill idiom, since both are a decision the turn is waiting on.

The question is the header, with a quiet `1 of 3` pager; each choice is a row with its radio/checkbox in the leading slot where the queue puts its `Circle`. Selection is a soft `logo-accent` tint rather than a per-row border (DESIGN.md flags isolated borders as migration debt).

## Behaviour preserved

Claude question paging (Back/Next, per-question validation, answers submitted together), generic MCP all-fields forms, the free-text "Other" companion, boolean and numeric fields, URL consent with unsafe-scheme refusal, Cancel/Skip/Decline, and the rule that a pending question blocks Escape-to-interrupt. All 8 original elicitation tests pass with unchanged assertions.

## Deliberate omissions

- **No `Esc` / `⏎` key hints.** The composer editor keeps focus while the dock is open and `handleChatKeyDown` already swallows Escape whenever an interaction is pending, so those chords would not fire from where the reader is typing. Advertising them would be false.
- **No number-key shortcuts**, despite the numbered layout in the design reference — that would be new behaviour, not a restyle.
- Option labels, the question header (2-line clamp) and the consent URL **wrap rather than truncate**. A queued message echoes text the reader wrote, so eliding it is safe; these are what they have to read to answer, and a clipped consent URL hides what is being approved.
- The `Waiting on: user_input` thread-state banner in `ChatStatusBanners.tsx` is untouched — that is session status, not the question card.

## Also in this diff

`latestPendingInteraction()` extracts the pending-interaction scan that `pendingApproval` already used, now shared with `pendingUserInput` — two real call sites with identical scoping rules.

## Review follow-ups

Addressed from @ronishrohan's review:

1. **Boolean invalid state** — a boolean field set `aria-describedby` to an error id it never rendered, so a required checkbox that failed validation pointed at nothing. It now draws the error with the same wording and placement as the other single-field branch.
2. **Placeholder-as-label** — the free-text "Other" row's title is now a quiet visible label above the field, per DESIGN.md §9. Rendering it showed the row's input had no visible affordance once the placeholder left, so the field takes the bordered chrome the dock already uses for generic text inputs, indented into the column the choices keep for their radio.
3. **Hand-rolled pills** — `QUIET_ACTION`/`PRIMARY_ACTION` were byte-identical copies of `ApprovalCard`'s. Both now come from `action-pill.ts`, shared by the two call sites. It stays a pill rather than shadcn `Button` on purpose, and the module says why: that primitive is `rounded-md` at the form-control height, so every call site would have to override its radius, height, type scale, and press transform. The extracted class sets match the originals exactly — the one delta is a no-op `gap-1.5` on `ApprovalCard`'s other-decision pill, which has a single text child.
4. **Rename history** — the claim above is corrected.

Both behaviour fixes have tests that fail against the previous component and pass against this one (verified by re-running the new tests against the pre-fix file). Re-verified in both themes.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run ElicitationDock.test.tsx ChatWorkspace.test.tsx renderer-coverage.test.ts` → **131 passed**
- `npm run typecheck` → clean
- Visually verified in both themes by rendering the real `ChatWorkspace` with a pending question against a Vite dev server.

Two new tests in `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` are genuine regression guards: the old card rendered the property title as a `<legend>` in the conversation log, and rendered `detail.message` in its answered state, so both would fail against the previous behaviour.

### Pre-existing failures, not from this change

- `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts` — 18 failures locally from a `better-sqlite3` native-module ABI mismatch (`NODE_MODULE_VERSION 130` vs `131`). Environmental; CI rebuilds the module.
- 2–3 flaky `getByRole("log")` failures in minimap tests when the chat directory runs in parallel. Confirmed pre-existing by stashing this branch and re-running the same suite on a clean tree.

title: feat(desktop): show link preview cards on hover for web links
body:
Code changes: +998 -5  
Tests: +566 -0  
Others: +147 -0 (generated OpenAPI spec + TS types)

## What

Hovering any external web link now shows a preview card (title, description, OG image, favicon/site name), Codex-app style.

- **Daemon:** new `GET /api/v1/link-preview?url=...` endpoint. Fetches the page server-side (the renderer CSP blocks external `connect-src` fetches), parses OG/meta tags with a dependency-free head scanner, resolves relative image/icon URLs, and caches in memory (30 min hits / 2 min misses, 256-entry cap). Errors map to the standard envelope: 400 invalid URL, 404 non-HTML, 502 upstream failure.
- **Chat/UI links:** `AppLink` — the single chokepoint for UI web links — is wrapped in a new shadcn-style `HoverCard` (`radix-ui` umbrella, no new dependency). The existing right-click context menu is preserved on the same anchor.
- **Terminal links:** `XtermTerminal` drives the same card from the web-links addon's hover callbacks, anchored at the cursor using the zero-size fixed trigger pattern the terminal context menu already uses. 300 ms open dwell, 300 ms close grace so the card itself is hoverable.
- Fetches are lazy (first hover only), cached per URL for the session, and silent on failure — a link with no preview behaves exactly as before.

## Testing

- Backend: table-driven controller tests through the real router with an `httptest` origin (OG happy path, title/description fallback, invalid-URL validation, non-HTML to 404, upstream 500 to 502, cache hit/miss behavior). `go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` clean on touched files; `internal/httpd/...` suites pass including route/spec parity.
- Frontend: new tests for `useLinkPreview` (URL-change regression, lazy fetch, error), `LinkPreviewCard`/`AppLink` (render, fallbacks, silent failure, context-menu intact); typecheck clean.
- Manually verified in the Electron dev app against isolated data: chat/TUI links and markdown links both show correct per-URL cards.

## Intentional omissions / notes

- Full backend `go test ./...` has failures in `session_manager`, `cli`, `tmux`, and `systemcheck` that reproduce identically on clean `origin/main` on this machine (environment-dependent); `claudecode`/`goose` flaked once under full-suite load and pass in isolation. The frontend full suite has pre-existing failures in `src/landing/**` and `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, also reproducing without this change.
- No SSRF/private-IP guard on the fetch: the loopback listener is unauthenticated by design and this mirrors "renderer asks daemon to fetch" trust. Can be added at the service level later if wanted.
- No Twitter-card tag fallbacks; OG + standard meta only.

title: Strip coding-agent support except OpenCode; remove agent switching and telemetry
body:
Code changes: +1604 -75294 (SQL migrations and shell scripts included; 17 binary files)
Tests: +2872 -79505
Others: +2805 -14004 (includes generated sqlc, OpenAPI spec, schema.ts, i18n locales, landing lockfile, docs, workflow config)

## Summary

Makes OpenCode the only coding agent in Agent Orchestrator. Removes the agent
pick/switch surface (`ao session switch-agent`, `agent-switch`, `handoff`),
drops the harnesses for non-OpenCode agents across backend, cloud, and e2e,
and deletes every telemetry collector, endpoint, client, and config, while
keeping the TUI↔Chat interface transitions and the worker/reviewer harnesses
running opencode.

### Backend
- New SQLite migrations:
  - `0148_allow_opencode_usage.sql` — rebuilds `usage_bindings`, adds
    `opencode` to the harness CHECK (leaves `usage_sources` untouched).
  - `0149_drop_agent_switching.sql` — drops the agent-switching tables.
- Deletes the agent-switch CLI commands (`ao session switch-agent`),
  handoff/agent-switch domain+service code, dashboard DTOs, pricing entries
  for removed agents, and telemetry (collectors, `/v1/telemetry` endpoints,
  event types, storage, config, CLI flags, test fixtures).
- Removes the `codex` account catalog/management surfaces.
- Dead `backend/cmd/gencodexproto` removed.
- The backend `e2e/` chat suite (gated on `AO_CHAT_E2E=1` + a codex binary)
  is left as-is: intentional omission — it is skipped in CI.

### Frontend / desktop
- Removes the agent-switch UI (switcher modal, global settings switch options,
  handoff messages) and the telemetry client/context; regenerated
  `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`.
- i18n: 1738 dead keys removed across 8 locales; live values → "OpenCode".
- Landing: removes Plausible/Sentry-less analytics components and the
  `LaunchAnalytics` tracking; deletes the `deploy-landing.yml` workflow.
- e2e: deletes the agent-switch specs; new-task-focus coverage is retained via
  the project-menu New task tests.
- `packages/product-ui`: worker options are opencode-only; injected logo
  rendering stays generic for any provider.

### Cloud
- Worker/orchestration harnesses are opencode-only; deletes the
  claude-code/codex/cursor harness Dockerfiles and fake-claude e2e shim;
  removes agent-switch/credential handling for removed agents.

### Docs
- Rewrites STATUS/architecture/CLI/README + all 8 translated READMEs to the
  opencode-only, telemetry-free model. Historical docs (DESIGN.md, ADRs,
  posthog cost-controls notes, superpowers plan) intentionally keep their
  original Codex/telemetry mentions as history.

## Validation

Mirrored the CI workflows locally where possible (post-merge state, after
merging upstream/main — 29 commits — into this branch):

- Backend: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint v2.12.2` (under
  `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.5`), full `go test ./...` (one exception, below), CLI
  `-tags e2e` suite, and the targeted `-race` subsets from go.yml.
- Cloud module: build, vet, full `go test ./...` all green.
- Frontend: typecheck, typecheck:e2e, vitest (3963 passed / 7 skipped locally;
  the 308 remaining failures are the environment gaps below), Playwright
  renderer smoke (`@T0|@P0`), `node --test` script suites
  (`ao-e2e-pod-gate`, `build-update-helper`, `build-mac-repair-installer`).
- Landing: `icons:check` green. product-ui: typecheck, tests (129), and pack
  green. cloud-client: contract regen (`git diff --exit-code` clean), typecheck,
  tests (21) green.
- `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api` regenerate to the committed output (no drift).
- Fixed two merge-time CI drift bugs found by mirroring go.yml locally: the
  `-race` steps referencing the stripped `pi`/`omp`/`primeagent`/`goose`
  adapters (deleted by this branch) and the `GlobalSettingsForm` report-problem
  test that predated upstream's Windows email-provider handoff (#5564).

### Known local gaps (environment, not regressions)
- Electron-chain vitest files: `auto-updater.test.ts`, `mac-differential-v2*`
  and `blockmap-reconstruction` `.test.mjs`, and `browser-profile-import.test.ts`
  (308 tests) cannot run here — this box cannot fetch the Electron binary
  (GitHub API 403) nor the `zip` helper (missing from PATH), and
  `better-sqlite3`'s native module is not built (npm install-scripts gating).
  All are unrelated to this branch; CI runs them on its runner (frontend.yml).
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` panics under this box's default Go 1.27.1 toolchain
  (staticcheck IR builder: `buildir: package "poll": unexpected expr:
  *ast.KeyValueExpr`). CI resolves Go 1.26.5 (committed `go.work` +
  `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` from `setuptoolchain`), under which the same pinned
  golangci version is green; verified locally by rerunning with
  `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.5`.
- Full-repo `go test -race` exceeds the 20 min job budget locally (sqlite alone
  took 23.6 min here); the sqlite race suite passed locally and CI is the arbiter.
- `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` (tmux integration)
  fails on this box's tmux 3.7c ("no current client" when `send-keys -l` targets
  the supervised `exec cat >/dev/null` keep-alive pane). The tmux package is
  byte-identical to main (zero diff); manual repros of the same pane state show
  the same intermittent error — a newer-tmux-only quirk. CI's runner tmux passes
  this long-standing test (main since #2980).
- Playwright: two idle full-suite runs were 53/54 with a different single 5s
  mount-timing flake each run (smoke-datadir, then chat-retry), both in specs
  untouched by this branch. Residual vite-dev/locale timing, not a regression.
- Docker fresh-install container check (`cli-e2e.yml`), the macOS native
  update-helper job, and the `packages/mobile` suite (202 upstream-only files

title: fix(cloud): correctly nest worker and orchestrator agents in cloud project config
body:
Code changes: +4 -1
Tests: +8 -2
Others: +0 -0

## What

Fixed an issue where agent selections (worker and orchestrator) were not persisting properly when creating a new cloud project. The agent selections are now nested in the config payload as `{ worker: { agent: ... }, orchestrator: { agent: ... } }` instead of flat keys.

## Why

Fixes the issue where `CreateProjectFlow` submitted agent overrides with flat keys (`workerAgent` and `orchestratorAgent`), but the rest of the application (e.g. `ProjectSettingsForm`) expects them nested as `worker.agent` and `orchestrator.agent`. When creating a cloud project, this mismatch caused the UI to fallback to the default agent and falsely display the same agent for both roles.

## How

- Updated `CloudProjectCard` in `CreateProjectFlow.tsx` to match the expected schema shape when passing the `config` payload to `client.createProject`.
- Updated existing integration tests in `CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx` to assert the correctly nested configuration payload instead of the old flat keys.

## Testing

- Ran `npm run typecheck` to verify TypeScript typing for the modified config object.
- Updated and ran the test suite for `CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx` using `vitest`; all 49 tests pass successfully.

title: feat(spawn): Chat task-create faster
body:
Code changes: +2770 -243  
Tests: +4076 -41  
Others: +441 -9 (generated OpenAPI, sqlc, and TS schema)  

## Before → now

| Step | Before | Now | Earlier measured cost |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Default-branch fetch | Ran after **Start Task** | Begins when New Task opens | ~1.2s |
| Worktree creation | Ran after **Start Task** | Starts while the user types; Start claims it when ready | 1.7–2.5s |
| Agent ACP startup (Claude measured) | Blocked the API response and navigation | Runs in the background after Start | 0.22–0.24s to initialize; 1.45–2.84s for `session/new` |
| Conversation | Appeared only after provisioning finished | Opens once the session and opening prompt are durably saved; further messages queue and drain in order | — |

The Git work overlaps composing, and agent startup no longer blocks opening the conversation. The underlying work is not eliminated. This applies to desktop-created Chat workers, not TUI or CLI spawns.

## Measured end-to-end result

One matched local run on the same repository and prompt, with a 3-second composer dwell: main `1c888193c` versus PR `8282175c5`. These measurements predate the current PR head ([data](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5626#issuecomment-5770367779)).

| From **Start Task** | Main | PR | Saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Task visible | 9.312s | **0.234s** | **9.078s** |
| Claude ready | 9.31s | **1.45s** | **7.86s** |
| First `READY` reply | 12.70s | **4.63s** | 8.07s |

The reply time includes variable Claude generation (~4s on main, ~2s on the PR); task visibility and readiness better isolate the provisioning change. [Latest desktop E2E recording](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/raw/evidence/pr-5626/speculative-worktree-e2e.mp4).

title: perf(sqlite): clone migrated snapshots and cache the Go build
body:
Code changes: +0 -0
Tests: +167 -528
Others: +11 -16

Part of #5116.

## Summary

`Go / build-test` is 12-19 minutes because `backend/internal/storage/sqlite` is the critical path. Two independent costs, one change each.

**Migration fixtures replayed from zero.** 76 `upTo(t, db, N)` call sites and ~40 fresh-database `migrate()` calls each rebuilt their starting schema by applying migrations 1..N, against 147 migrations. Under `-race` the pure-Go driver costs ~30x per operation, so the package grew as O(tests x migrations) — 3.5s in July, 925.6s now.

This generalizes the snapshot cache that #4466 already added for two tests: build one database image per goose version, ascending and one migration at a time, then clone the bytes per test. Cost is now O(migrations). The 147 separate `UpTo` calls that build every image cost the same 11.65s as a single `goose.Up`.

Two details that keep it honest:

- The builder opens without WAL, so a committed migration is always in the main file when `os.ReadFile` takes the snapshot. In WAL mode a snapshot could silently capture a stale schema.
- It opens with `foreign_keys(ON)` to match production. FK-off is a property of the clone, not the image, via `openMigratedDatabaseCopyNoForeignKeys` for tests that seed rows without parents.

Coverage is unchanged: migration, repair, reconciliation and production-`Open` tests all still run for real, and the ~40 seed-then-migrate tests still call `migrate()` — they just start from a snapshot instead of replaying to version N first. `migrate_fixture_test.go` is removed; its isolation assertions move into `TestMigrationSnapshotsMatchTheRequestedVersion`, which also covers a high-then-low request order.

**Every run recompiled the race build from scratch.** `setup-go` ran with `cache: false` in every Go job. In run [35341859885](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/35341859885) the first package result landed 55s into the Test step, but the SQLite package did not start until ~296s — that gap is race-instrumented compilation of its dependency tree, `modernc.org/sqlite` most of all.

Scoped to `build-test` alone. `cloud-build-test` runs in 25s with nothing worth caching, and `windows-workspace` is 4m46s and never the critical path, where a second large cache would only compete for the repository's 10 GB quota against the one that matters.

## Measured on CI

Baseline [35341859885](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/35341859885) against this branch's warm-cache run [35435481761](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/35435481761). Every test executed in both — 0 packages reported `(cached)`.

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `build-test` job | 21m36s | **13m40s** |
| `Test` step | 20m21s | **13m05s** |
| `internal/storage/sqlite` | 925.6s | **556.4s** |
| whole suite | 2408 package-seconds | 2091 |
| first package result | 55s into the step | **2s** |

Locally, the same package under `-race` went 1051.9s to 463.6s across the same 78 tests.

The build cache is what collapses the startup: `Build` and `Vet` now finish in about a second each, and the first test result lands 2s into the Test step instead of 55s. Compile cost, backend module, empty `GOCACHE` versus warm:

| | cold | warm |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| whole module, compile only | 173s wall / 295 CPU-s | 73s wall / 55 CPU-s |
| SQLite race test binary | 43s wall / 90 CPU-s | 1.8s |

### `-count=1` is load-bearing here

Restoring `GOCACHE` also restores Go's test-result cache. The first warm run on this branch reported **158 of 170 packages as `(cached)` and executed 12**, finishing in 9m6s — a green required check that skipped 93% of the suite. Go's test cache is content-aware for Go inputs but does not track what these tests actually reach: subprocesses, `PATH` contents, the network. `build-test` now passes `-count=1`, so only result replay is disabled and compilation stays cached.

## What this does not reach, and what would

This is short of the 5-minute target in #5116, so I am leaving the issue open.

The remaining waste is scheduling, not compilation. `go test` launches packages in list order under `-p=4`, and `internal/storage/sqlite` sits late in that list: it starts 229s into the Test step and then runs 556s largely alone. The step is 785s against a work bound of 2091/4 = 523s.

That makes sharding worth more than I first estimated. Giving the SQLite package its own job starts it at t=0, leaving the other 169 packages at 1535 package-seconds — roughly `max(556s, 384s)`, a Test step near 9m15s. I have not done it here because splitting `build-test` renames the required check and that is a branch-protection decision.

Beyond that the levers are `internal/service/chat` (320s) and `internal/session_manager` (250s), 37% of the non-SQLite work. Their test sleeps are 5-150ms, so that cost is genuine race-instrumented SQLite work, not waiting.

For the record, my first projection put the SQLite package at ~405s by applying the local 0.441 before/after ratio; the runner's actual ratio is 0.601. Slower cores make the remaining per-migration work relatively heavier, and the 78 clone writes are ~58MB against runner disk.

## Validation

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l` clean
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` on `./internal/storage/sqlite/...`: 0 issues
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/storage/sqlite`: 78/78 pass, 463.591s
- full backend suite: 164 packages ok. 5 fail — `adapters/agent/{claudecode,fake,goose,omp,pi}` — all timing symptoms under load (`signal: killed` on `--version` probes, `context deadline exceeded`, a speedup assertion), all passing in isolation, in packages that do not reference `storage/sqlite`. This branch changes only `_test.go` files inside `package sqlite` plus the workflow.
- workflow YAML parses; all three jobs resolve `cache-dependency-path` to an existing `go.sum`

title: Phantom session stays in sidebar forever if app closes mid-spawn
body:
## What happened

Create a new task/session, close the app before the workspace finishes creating (while the "Preparing the worker terminal..." screen is showing). The session never launches, but it stays in the sidebar forever — non-terminated, un-killable, stuck on "Preparing the worker terminal. This can take a moment while AO creates the workspace and starts the agent."

## Why

`Spawn()` in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go` creates the session's DB row (`CreateSession`) before the workspace/runtime exist; that metadata is only committed at the very end (`MarkSpawned`). Closing the app kills the daemon (`killDaemon` in `frontend/src/main.ts`) with no grace period, so if this happens mid-spawn, the row is left in "seed" state (no workspace, no runtime) permanently.

On the next daemon start, `reconcileLive()` checks non-terminated sessions and, for one with no workspace, just does nothing:

```go
if rec.Metadata.WorkspacePath == "" || (...) {
    return nil // no-op — leaves the phantom row forever
}
```

Since AO derives displayed status from durable DB facts rather than a separate status field, this phantom row shows as a live session indefinitely.

## Fix

Reuse the existing `rollbackSpawnSeedRow` helper (already used for ordinary in-request spawn failures) instead of the no-op, so an interrupted spawn is cleaned up the same way on the next boot.

Fix + regression test (`TestReconcileLive_InterruptedSpawnSeedRowIsRemoved`) are ready on branch `ao/agent-orchestrator-211/root`.

title: fix(cloud): combined terminal, orchestrator, and checkout fixes (supersedes #5631 #4999 #5594 #5584 #5616)
body:
## What

One branch combining the cloud terminal + orchestrator fixes that were spread across five open PRs, plus a worker checkout-hardening fix, verified together and deployed to staging CP (task-def rev 126, image cp-combined-16fccb872).

Supersedes and should close on merge: #5631, #4999, #5594, #5584, #5616.

## Included changes

- **#5584** (cloud) ignore a zero-dimension terminal resize instead of closing the socket (stops the reconnect+reset flash). Already the code running in prior CP revs.
- **#5631** (cloud + frontend) stabilize single-replica terminal input: remove the half-built multi-replica affinity code and relay stat counters (dead-code removal, input delivery unchanged with the durable fallback intact), and switch cloud terminal input to line-buffered local echo. Deploy scripts pin the CP to one replica.
- **#4999** (cloud + worker) inject control-plane-authored role prompts for claude, codex, and cursor (cursor now handled via a session plugin dir). Switches harness prompt delivery to file-based flags.
- **#5594** (frontend) cloud task composer cleanup (harness list limited to claude/codex/cursor, no model spinner until a harness is chosen), connecting/connected terminal UX (one centered Connecting cover plus one elapsed timer, connected shows no persistent badge), and the fresh-session blank-flash fix (the worker-epoch flip from unknown to first-known no longer remounts the terminal pane; a real epoch advance still re-mints).
- **#5616** (frontend) write cloud project agent overrides under the nested worker.agent / orchestrator.agent shape the read paths expect, so a project's chosen worker and orchestrator agents are honored.
- **checkout hardening** (cloud/worker, new here) a stalled git clone or fetch previously hung until the whole sandbox was torn down, so the agent terminal never came up. Now git aborts a transfer that stays under 1 KB/s for 60s (GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT/TIME), which targets stalls not slow-but-progressing clones and is a no-op for local git ops; the git-credential and gh-wrapper curls get connect and max timeouts too. A failed clone exits the worker and the reconciler recreates the sandbox, turning an indefinite hang into fail-fast recovery.

## Verification

Each source PR was reviewed independently for correctness, regressions, races, migrations, secrets, and edge cases; all reported safe. The five PRs merge onto main with zero conflicts (verified by real sequential merge). No database migrations in any of them. Combined tree: `cd cloud && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` for httpapi, roleprompt, workerexec, worker, and ao-worker all pass. Frontend typecheck and the terminal/composer/i18n vitest suites pass.

Deployed to staging via surgical task-def swap (28 secrets and all provider env preserved), rev 126, healthy on /readyz with zero boot errors.

## Conscious-accepts and one live validation

- #5631 applies line-buffered input universally, including inside agent TUIs, so interactive single-key programs (vim, less, htop, single-key menu prompts) do not receive keys until Enter. Intentional tradeoff; ships in the app, not the CP.
- #5631 pins the CP to a single replica (removes horizontal autoscaling); this is already the de-facto state.
- #4999 changes the claude launch to a file-based system-prompt flag. This depends on the baked rootfs claude accepting it, which unit tests cannot prove. Validate a real claude session produces output on staging before promoting further.

## Scope

Control plane plus worker plus frontend. No migration. Frontend ships in the desktop app/DMG; the cloud half is what deploys to CP.

title: fix(lifecycle): give each review-comment nudge its own dedup slot
body:
Code changes: +17 -1  
Tests: +46 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## TL;DR

A nudge is AO's automated message telling a worker that its PR has unresolved review feedback. Before this PR, every comment on one PR shared the same dedup/retry slot: comments A and B overwrote each other's “already notified” state, so old comments could be delivered repeatedly while consuming the shared three-attempt budget and causing a later comment C to be missed.

After this PR, each comment has its own slot keyed by comment id. A and B each notify the worker once, repeated polls stay quiet, and a genuinely new comment C still gets delivered.

## Summary

Every unresolved review comment on a PR built its nudge under the same `comment:<url>` key while carrying its own signature, so the single dedup slot held whichever comment happened to be appended last.

```go
// reactions.go:282 — one key for every comment
key: "comment:" + o.URL

// reactions.go:298 — the sibling loop, fifteen lines below, already keys per review
key: "review:" + o.URL + ":" + review.ID
```

Dedup is one equality check (`m.react.seen[key] == sig`), and `m.react.attempts[key]` is counted against `reviewMaxNudge` under the same key. Two consequences follow:

- **Re-sends.** A poll writes comment A's signature, then B's, then C's; the slot ends holding C. On the next poll A's signature no longer matches, so A is nudged again — indefinitely, even after it is addressed.
- **Starved budget.** The three-attempt cap is shared, so a PR with more than three comments exhausts it in a single poll and the remaining comments are never delivered.

Both were observed on #5604: five unresolved comments produced three nudges for comments already fixed and resolved, and the last two never arrived.

The fix keys each nudge by comment id, falling back to thread id only when a provider supplies no comment id. Comments in one thread still need independent slots because each carries its own signature.

## Tests

`TestPRObservation_ReviewCommentNudgesDedupPerComment` asserts that five comments produce five nudges on the first poll and none on the second. It fails on the old key with:

```
first poll sent 3 nudges, want one per comment (5)
```

`go test ./internal/lifecycle/` and `go vet ./internal/lifecycle/` pass.

## Scope

The merge-conflict nudge is untouched: it uses a single key with a single signature, so it has no rotation problem. The one stale conflict alert seen on #5604 came from an observation snapshot taken while the PR really was conflicting — poll lag, not dedup.

The `resolved` sync is also untouched and works: `UpsertPRComment` persists the provider's `isResolved`, which `observer_provider.go` reads. Resolved comments stop nudging once a poll lands; the shared key is what kept re-firing them in the meantime.

## Risk

Existing `seen`/`attempts` entries under the old `comment:<url>` key are orphaned by the rename, so each comment on a PR mid-flight may nudge once more under its new key before settling. Signatures are persisted per PR and self-heal on the next poll.

title: fix(lifecycle): don't flag-terminate a merged-PR session whose agent is still working
body:
Code changes: +16 −0  
Tests: +45 −4  
Others: +0 −0  

Closes #2879

## Summary

A session whose agent merges a PR mid-climb was immediately flagged `is_terminated`, which drops the session off the SCM observer roster.

Since applying a PR observation only reacts to live, observed sessions (the roster comes from `ListSessions` without a termination filter), the agent's next PR — raised in the very same still-`ActivityActive` session — was never attributed: no `pr` row, no sidebar entry, no nudge. The agent looked "done" purely because one PR had merged, even though it was still working (#2879).

## Root cause

`sessionComplete` in `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go` judged completion from PR rows alone (`≥1 merged ∧ none open`) and never consulted `rec.Activity.State`. The merged/closed lane then called `terminateCompletedSession` → flag-terminated the session regardless of whether the agent had actually quiesced.

## Fix

`backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go:185` — the merged/closed lane now gates termination on genuine agent quiescence instead of PR-state alone.

The new guard is:

    if rec.Activity.State == domain.ActivityActive {
        return nil
    }

While the agent is still `ActivityActive`, `ApplyPRObservation` returns `nil` and the session stays live + observed, so the follow-up PR raised in the same session is attributed, enriched, and nudged as before.

Termination now fires only once the agent has genuinely quiesced (`ActivityExited`), matching the issue's prescribed direction.

## Tests

- Added `TestPRObservation_MergedOnStillWorkingAgentDoesNotTerminate` (red before the fix: asserted the terminator must not fire while the agent is still working; green after).
- Re-pointed the four existing merged-lane tests that had encoded the bug (they seeded a still-working `working()` session and asserted termination) onto a genuinely-quiesced `exited()` fixture, preserving their true contract.
- Verified: `go test ./internal/lifecycle/`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` all clean across the backend.

title: fix(chat): stop a queue held behind a failed turn
body:
Code changes: +50 -5  
Tests: +160 -2  
Others: +0 -0

A failed turn holds its queue instead of cascading it into the same outage (#5188). The hold is released only by a turn that *completes* (`controller.go:3041`), an interface-handoff drain, or interrupt reconciliation — so through a run of failures the queue just sits there, and a new send dispatches straight away rather than draining those rows. Observed live: conversation `201f7828` had a turn fail at 10:01 on a spend limit with two turns queued at 09:54, and 44 minutes later they were still `queued`.

`activeTurn()` is `running ?? queued`, so the conversation kept showing a Working bar counting up against work nobody was doing, the composer promised "this sends when it finishes" (untrue — a new message jumps the held rows), and Stop refused with `CHAT_NO_ACTIVE_TURN` because `Interrupt` only looks for running turns. The held queue was unstoppable except by cancelling each dock entry by hand.

## Changes

- **`controller.go`** — with a queue present and nothing in flight, `Interrupt` directly cancels the durable pre-Stop queue while holding the dispatch lock. Cancellation failures reach the caller, and `ErrNoActiveTurn` is still the answer when there is genuinely nothing to stop.
- **`ChatWorkspace.tsx`** — the live-turn bar and composer share a working-turn check. Queued sends still show Working while the provider accepts them. Only work queued before the latest failed or recovered completion is treated as held; a fresh send after that completion shows Working even if older held rows remain.
- **`ChatComposer.tsx`** — Stop is no longer gated on `willQueue`, so it stays available for queued work. `onInterrupt` is already only passed when there is an active or queued turn.

## Tests

- `TestStopCancelsQueueHeldByFailedTurn` — a held queue is cancelled by Stop, the provider never receives the queued prompt, and a second Stop returns `ErrNoActiveTurn`.
- `TestStopReportsHeldQueueCancellationFailure` — an injected durable cancellation failure is returned from Stop rather than reported as success.
- Renderer regressions: held queues after failed or recovered turns show idle and retain Stop; first sends and fresh sends after completed, interrupted, failed, or recovered turns show Working and queue hints during dispatch.
- Rebased onto main (`4d2c139636`), preserving startup queue hints and hiding Working while provisioning. Local validation: 5,349 frontend tests pass (six skipped), all 136 ChatWorkspace tests pass, both TypeScript checks pass, and all 60 browser smoke tests pass. Shared-package checks and docs build pass.
- The full local chat race suite and HTTP-controller suite pass. The broader local backend run was not green: inherited AO tmux settings affected tests, and other tests hit timing limits, including the SQLite race-suite timeout. Cross-platform validation is covered by CI, not claimed as a local pass.
- The first rebased CI run passed 13 checks but hit `TestServerShutdownEndpoint`'s five-second shutdown race. Main's subsequently merged fix is now included and passes ten repeated race-enabled runs locally. CI is rerunning on the final rebased head.
- Backend chat-service and HTTP-controller tests passed for the preceding cancellation-error fix.

## Known follow-up

- A held queue is not inert: the next *successful* completion drains it oldest-first, so a prompt written before an outage can reach the agent much later, unannounced. Pre-existing; this PR does not change it, but Stop now gives the user a way to clear it first.
- The daemon still dispatches a fresh send ahead of a held queue rather than behind it. Real ordering wart, left alone here.
- Rollback, compaction and inline-edit busy still key off `Boolean(turn)`, so with a held queue the chat reads idle while those stay blocked until Stop.

title: fix(session-manager): stop kill stranding a session it cannot fully tear down
body:
Code changes: +86 -53  
Tests: +254 -12  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

After a stop request, the agent may be gone while worktree removal fails or times out; previously `ao session kill` could return `INTERNAL_ERROR` before marking the session terminated, leaving it stuck in the sidebar and skipped by cleanup. This PR gives the termination write its own timeout, and marks the session terminated despite workspace removal failures without force-deleting files. Runtime teardown failures still fail the kill.

Fixes #5463.

## The bug

`Manager.Kill` records terminal intent as its **last** step, so a failure anywhere in teardown returns before `terminated` is set. `Manager.Cleanup` opens its loop with `if !rec.IsTerminated { continue }`, and the CLI's preview asks the API for `active=false`. The row kill refuses to mark is the row cleanup refuses to see: the session stays on the board with no path out, and every retry returns the same `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

Two paths reach that state, plus a runtime path that turned out not to be real.

**1. Slow teardown blows the budget.** `Kill` detaches from the caller's context and runs under `killTeardownBudget = 90s`; `lifecycle.MarkTerminated` starts with `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return err }`. A large worktree on NTFS can spend the whole budget being unlinked, so the budget expires *after* the agent is stopped and the worktree is gone, and the one remaining write is refused. This is consistent with the report's first kill (*"returned INTERNAL_ERROR but did remove the worktree and set `status: exited`"*), but the exact Windows failure path was not observed locally.

**2. Unnamed workspace refusals.** Only `ErrWorkspaceDirty`, `ErrWorkspaceRepoUnavailable` and `ErrWorkspaceDeferred` were tolerated. A locked worktree git will not prune, or any other registration leftover, failed the kill. `Destroy` never force-removes, so the worktree was being preserved either way; all the allowlist decided was whether the session row survived alongside it.

**3. (Not a real path.) A runtime that is conclusively gone.** Every runtime's `Destroy` already returns `nil` when it confirms absence (tmux via `confirmedAbsentOutput`, conpty when the registry has no entry), so any `Destroy` error means the runtime may still be live. An earlier revision tolerated `ErrRuntimeUnavailable` and then re-probed `IsAlive`. Both were dropped: no real `Destroy` returns that error, and conpty's `IsAlive` dials a listener that `Destroy`'s graceful shutdown has already closed, so a hung pty-host would read as gone.

## The fix

- Terminal-intent writes move into `recordTermination`, on their own short context detached from the teardown budget. By the time `Kill` reaches them every destructive step is done; refusing the bookkeeping is the one outcome that cannot be recovered from. Nothing above them is retried.
- Every workspace teardown failure preserves the worktree and terminates the session. Nothing is force-removed, so `ao session cleanup` retries the release and reports the reason instead of skipping the row silently. The typed predicate is kept (renamed `expectedWorkspaceRefusal`) and now only decides log volume.
- **Any `runtime.Destroy` error still fails the kill**, unchanged from `main`. That includes `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, whose port contract says the runtime may still be live and callers "must not recreate, destroy, archive, or otherwise treat the session as dead". Terminating there would leave a possibly-live agent running with no row pointing at it, which is worse than a visible stuck session. Every other runtime error stays fail-closed, as do the steps that can hold live work: a scoped shell, a reviewer pane, a native agent session.

## Tests

- `TestKill_TerminatesEvenWhenTeardownBudgetExpires` — fails on the parent commit with `kill mer-1: context deadline exceeded`
- `TestKill_UnnamedWorkspaceErrorPreservesAndTerminates` — also asserts `ForceDestroy` is never called
- `TestKill_RuntimeDestroyErrorFailsClosedEvenWhenProbeReadsGone` / `TestKill_InconclusiveRuntimeProbeStaysFailClosed` — a `Destroy` error stops the kill even if `IsAlive` would read the session as gone
- `TestKillAndCleanupReachASessionGitWillNotRelease` — real git + real SQLite + real `Manager`: locks a worktree, removes it out of band, drives kill + cleanup end to end

`fakeLCM.MarkTerminated` ignored its context, unlike the real `lifecycle.Manager`. That is why no existing test caught path 1; it now honours `ctx.Err()`.

The fail-closed regressions (`TestKill_RuntimeDestroyFailureLeavesSessionActive`, `TestKill_ReviewerTeardownFailureLeavesSessionActive`, `TestKill_NativeTerminationFailurePreservesRuntimeAndWorkspace`, `TestKill_RefusesWorkspaceTeardownWhenShellTerminalsWontClose`, `TestKill_WorkspaceProjectAlreadyAbsentStaysFreed`) all still pass.

Verification: `go vet` clean, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `go test -race ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/integration/`. Four `TestSpawn_*` failures in `internal/session_manager` are pre-existing on `main` (confirmed against a clean HEAD worktree), unrelated to this change.

## Known gap, left open deliberately

A conpty session stuck on an unresolved-ownership registry reservation is **still** permanently unkillable after this PR. `scanLocked` retains PID-0 prelaunch reservations forever by design, and a session recovered from the registry after a daemon restart gets `currentOwner=false`, so `Destroy` returns `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` on every attempt. Reached by an interrupted spawn (crash, forced reboot) followed by a daemon restart.

That is an adapter-lifecycle bug, not something `Kill` should paper over by declaring a possibly-live session dead — filing separately.

Related: the durable retry query `ListTerminalCleanupCandidates` exists in the store but has no Go caller, so the retry path for a preserved workspace is `ao session cleanup` only, not automatic. Wiring the terminal-resource reconciler would close that.

title: fix(mobile): links tapped in the conversation leave the app instead of opening in-app
body:
### Problem

A web link tapped in the conversation leaves the app. `packages/mobile/lib/chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx:126` hands every link to `Linking.openURL`, so the user lands in Safari or Chrome and has to come back to AO by hand. Reported by @illegalcall in Discord `#dev-chat` ("On mobile: links don't open in AO browser").

On desktop the same tap opens the page inside the session's AO Browser inspector (`frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionBrowserLink.ts`, `components/AppLink.tsx`); only a modifier-click or the context menu goes to the system browser.

Two consequences beyond the context switch:

- **A github.com link in the conversation skips the app's own rule for github.com.** `lib/openGitHub.ts` opens a repo or PR in the GitHub app when it has a screen for it (that is where the user's session lives; a private PR in a browser is a login wall or a 404) and falls back to the browser otherwise. PR cards and worker rows use it; `ChatMarkdown` does not, so the same URL is routed by two different rules depending on where it sits.
- **A `localhost` link the agent prints is opened as the phone's own localhost.** The preview screen already maps the agent machine's loopback onto the AO host (`lib/api.ts`, `mobileReachablePreviewURL`); chat links do not go through it.

### What this is not

- **Not a job for `app/preview/[id].tsx`.** That WebView shows the workspace's detected `index.html` or the session's advertised `previewUrl`, with AO's auth header. A tapped link is a third-party page that may need a login, cookies, a share sheet or an address bar — a raw `WKWebView` has none of that, and ATS refuses plain `http` to anything but local hosts inside it.
- **Not the elicitation "Open link" button** (`ChatTimeline.tsx`): the desktop sends that to the system browser too, and the flow behind it belongs to the desktop machine.
- **Not the "Review is not available" half of the same report.** That is a missing feature (no caller of `/sessions/{id}/reviews*` exists in `packages/mobile`), not a bug, and needs a product decision first.

### Proposed direction

Open links in the platform's in-app browser — `SFSafariViewController` on iOS, a Chrome Custom Tab on Android — through `expo-web-browser`, which is what chat apps do with a tapped link: the user stays in the app and gets a real browser with a Done button.

- `ChatMarkdown` reports the tap; the conversation screen decides how it opens (it knows the AO host).
- Map the loopback with `mobileReachablePreviewURL` first, then go through `openGitHub`, so github.com keeps its app handoff and a tapped link and a PR card follow one rule. `openGitHub`'s browser fallback becomes the in-app browser; non-web schemes (the iOS bug report's `x-safari-https://`) still go to the system.
- New native module, so the runtime version changes: ships in a store build, not over the air.

### Alternatives considered

- **Route into `preview/[id]`** with the tapped URL. Works, but is a hand-rolled browser — see above.
- **`NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent`** to make the WebView route viable for plain-http links. Widens ATS for the whole app to solve the wrong problem.
- **Leave it.** Safari is not broken; it is the wrong place, and it drops the github.com rule and the loopback mapping the app already has.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(mobile): open conversation links in the in-app browser
body:
## Summary

A web link tapped in the conversation called `Linking.openURL` (`ChatMarkdown.tsx:126`) and left the app for Safari. On desktop the same tap opens the page inside the session's AO Browser inspector.

Links now open in the platform's in-app browser — `SFSafariViewController` on iOS, a Chrome Custom Tab on Android — via `expo-web-browser`. The user stays in AO and gets a real browser: address bar, share, password autofill, reader, Done.

Closes #5646.

## Changes

- **`ChatMarkdown` reports the tap; the conversation screen decides how it opens.** `MarkdownLink` takes its handler from a `ChatLinkProvider` that `ChatSessionScreen` provides; without one it defaults to `openGitHub`, so a reuse of the renderer elsewhere loses only the localhost rewrite, never the in-app browser. The handler maps a `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` link from the agent's machine onto the AO host with `mobileReachablePreviewURL` — the rule the preview screen already uses, since the phone's own localhost is never the dev server the agent named — then calls `openGitHub`.
- **`openGitHub` stays the one rule for a web URL**: the GitHub app when it has a screen for it, otherwise the browser. Its browser fallback is now the in-app browser instead of `Linking.openURL`, so a github.com URL behaves the same in a PR card, a worker row and the conversation. A non-web scheme still goes to the system: the iOS bug report deliberately arrives as `x-safari-https://` (`bugReportOpenUrl`) to dodge the GitHub app's universal-link claim, and the in-app browser rejects it. If the in-app browser refuses a web URL (on Android, nothing resolves the intent), the system browser is the last hop as before, and when that fails too the tap fires the error haptic — the signal the old chat handler had.
- **`createTask: false` on Android**, which is androidx's own Custom Tabs default. expo's default launches the tab through a proxy activity in a second task, and in 57.0.3 that task outlives the tab as a dead AO card in Recents (reproduced below). The trade, stated in the comment: relaunching AO from the launcher while a tab is up tears the tab down instead of returning to it.

**Behaviour change outside the conversation:** PR cards, worker rows and Android's Report a problem now fall back to the in-app browser rather than Safari/Chrome. On iOS that means a private GitHub page, without the app installed, shows GitHub's sign-in where Safari may already have been signed in — the sheet has its own cookie store; password autofill works there.

**Not changed, on purpose:** the elicitation "Open link" button (`ChatTimeline.tsx`) stays on the system browser, as on desktop. A url-mode elicitation is usually a sign-in or OAuth flow, and the system browser is where the user is already signed in — the iOS sheet has its own cookie store, so it would ask them to sign in again. That leaves two link behaviours on the conversation screen, deliberately. Relative workspace-file links, which the phone's markdown never linkifies.

**Native module**, so the runtime version moves (`5c16b388…` → `e9b0c4ea…` on iOS, resolved with and without the dependency): this ships in the next store build, not over the air.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx expo export` bundles on ios and android. Lockfile diff is the one package.
- `npx vitest run`: **1164 → 1172**. `openGitHub.test.ts` pins the order of hops and the non-web-scheme branch, mocking `expo-web-browser`, `Linking` and `haptics`; `ChatMarkdown.source.test.ts` pins the provider default. The provider wiring in `ChatSessionScreen` itself has no test: it sits over two rules that already have them — `githubAppUrl` (`githubLink.test.ts`) and `mobileReachablePreviewURL` (`chatModeApi.test.ts`) — and a test of it would only restate the line.
- Library behaviour read in the installed source, not assumed: a second `openBrowserAsync` while a sheet is up resolves `{type: "locked"}` on iOS (`WebBrowserModule.swift:25-27`), so no guard is needed; on Android the promise resolves as soon as the tab launches.
- **iPhone 17 Pro simulator, Debug build from this branch, paired to a real daemon.** Taps are real.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| tap `https://github.com/…/pull/2` in a **terminated** session | `SFSafariViewController` over AO: Done, title, reader, share / open-in-Safari |
| Done, then the other link | back on the chat; second sheet opens |
| Settings → Report a problem | Safari, as before (`x-safari-https`) |

- **Pixel emulator, Debug build from this branch, same daemon.**

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| tap the same link | Chrome Custom Tab **inside AO's task** (`topResumedActivity … CustomTabActivity t115`) |
| Back | the chat; no new entry in Recents |
| the same tap with expo's default `createTask` | tab in the proxy's task (`.webContainer`); after closing it, that task stayed in Recents as an AO card |
| Settings → Report a problem | Custom Tab |

## Not verified

- **A physical device.** The GitHub app is not installed on either simulator, so the app-handoff branch of `openGitHub` was not exercised here; it is the branch that already existed.
- **The `createTask: false` trade-off** (AO relaunched from the launcher while a tab is open) is read from the library's comment, not run.
- **No renderer in `packages/mobile`**, so the provider wiring in `ChatSessionScreen` is covered by the device rows, not by a test.
- **The last-hop fallback on a device.** The in-app browser cannot be made to refuse an `https://` URL on the iOS simulator, and on Android the only way is to disable every browser, which fails the system hop too; the order of hops is covered by the unit test, not a device row.
