| Total | 147 | 35 |

title: bug(lifecycle): PR-wide review nudge budget duplicates old comments and suppresses new feedback
body:
## Bug

AO keys review-comment delivery deduplication and its attempt budget to the whole PR rather than to an individual comment/thread or feedback signature. Multiple unresolved comments therefore compete for one remembered signature and one three-send budget.

This produces two failure modes:

1. Different comment signatures overwrite one another, so a previously delivered comment can look new on a later poll and be injected again.
2. Once the shared attempt counter reaches `reviewMaxNudge`, a genuinely new comment on the same PR is silently suppressed.

**Source:** maintainer report while dogfooding PR #5742
**Analyzed against:** `bfaa1aa61f142b306beca4149d790f82915d7284`
**AO version:** `dev`
**Confidence:** High; confirmed from GitHub state, AO's persisted PR/comment rows, and the lifecycle delivery state.

## Concrete incident

PR: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742

AO successfully observed and persisted the new unresolved human comment:

- Comment: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742#discussion_r4069029633
- Comment ID: `PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7yiHcB`
- Thread ID: `PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6kn0Nt`
- GitHub review state: `COMMENTED`
- AO policy snapshot: `auto_inject_review = true`

But the comment was not delivered to the worker. The persisted reaction state for the PR was:

```json
{
  "seen": {
    "comment:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742": "PRRT_kwDORPZUAc6kndp6 + PRRC_kwDORPZUAc7yhl_I"
  },
  "attempts": {
    "comment:https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742": 3
  }
}
```

The new comment has a different signature, but `sendOnce` checks the already exhausted attempt count for the shared `comment:<PR URL>` key and returns without sending it.

## Root cause

`ApplyPRObservation` creates one pending nudge per unresolved comment, but every one uses the same key:

```go
key: "comment:" + o.URL
```

Each comment's signature is independently derived from its thread/comment IDs. `sendOnce` stores only one `seen[key]` value and one `attempts[key]` counter.

With comments A and B, delivery can behave like:

```text
send A -> seen[key] = A
send B -> seen[key] = B
next poll sees A -> A differs from B, so A is sent again
```

The three-attempt budget eventually stops this ping-pong, but it also prevents later comment C from being delivered.

Relevant code:

- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`, review-comment nudge construction
- `backend/internal/lifecycle/reactions.go`, `sendOnce`

## Expected behavior

- Each newly observed actionable comment/thread is delivered once.
- An unchanged comment is not repeatedly injected on later polls.
- A new comment remains eligible even if older comments on the PR exhausted their own retry or safety budget.
- Resolution stops further delivery for that comment.
- Deduplication remains durable across daemon restarts.
- A broader rate limit may protect against comment storms, but it must not permanently discard later feedback.

## Acceptance criteria

- Scope the delivery identity and attempt accounting to the actionable feedback rather than only the PR URL.
- Add a regression test with two simultaneously unresolved comments proving they do not alternate/replay.
- Add a regression test where comment A exhausts its budget, then newly observed comment B is still delivered.
- Preserve identical-comment deduplication across repeated polls and daemon restarts.
- Make a budget-exhaustion suppression observable enough to diagnose without querying SQLite directly.

## Related

- #5574 — self-authored review-thread replies are nudge-eligible; adjacent selection/delivery bug, not a duplicate.
- #1943 — old pre-rewrite review dispatch observability report; similar symptom, different implementation and cause.

title: bug(UX): review feedback is mislabeled as Changes Requested and disappears while agents work
body:
## Bug

AO conflates two independent dimensions — agent activity and SCM/review state — into one primary session status. It also maps any unresolved review comment to `changes_requested`, even when GitHub has no formal changes-requested review.

This produces misleading and unstable UI:

```text
Idle · Changes Requested
        ↓ agent starts working
Working
        ↓ agent becomes idle, comment still unresolved
Idle · Changes Requested
```

The review feedback never disappeared. Its tag vanishes solely because active agent state has higher precedence than SCM state.

**Source:** maintainer report and screenshot while dogfooding PR #5742
**Analyzed against:** `bfaa1aa61f142b306beca4149d790f82915d7284`
**AO version:** `dev`
**Confidence:** High; confirmed from GitHub, AO's stored state/event history, backend status derivation, and frontend timeline logic.

## Concrete incident

PR: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742

GitHub reported:

```text
reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

AO stored:

```text
review_decision: review_required
reviewComments: true
```

AO's SCM event history never recorded `changes_requested` for this PR. The outstanding thread came from a `COMMENTED` review and was explicitly described by its author as an optional, non-blocking nit:

https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5742#discussion_r4069029633

Despite that, the inspector showed `Idle · Changes Requested`. When the agent became active, it showed only `Working`.

## Root causes

### 1. Unresolved comments are treated as a formal changes-requested decision

`backend/pkg/contract/status.go` derives the PR pipeline status using:

```go
case pr.Review == ReviewChangesRequest || pr.ReviewComments:
    return StatusChangesRequested
```

This collapses these distinct facts:

- GitHub formally reports `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
- A PR merely has one or more unresolved inline comments from a `COMMENTED` review.

### 2. Active agent state replaces SCM state

Session status derivation returns `working` immediately for an active agent, before evaluating SCM status. This is reasonable for a primary activity label, but it becomes lossy because the UI relies on that same primary status to recover the unresolved-comment signal.

### 3. The frontend cannot independently reconstruct review feedback

`scmTimelineStates()` adds the tag only when:

```text
session.status == changes_requested
or
pr.review == changes_requested
```

When the agent is active:

- `session.status` becomes `working`.
- `pr.review` correctly remains `review_required`.
- The unresolved-comment fact is therefore no longer represented by either condition.

Relevant code:

- `backend/pkg/contract/status.go`, `DeriveStatus` and `prPipelineStatus`
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx`, `scmTimelineStates`

## Expected behavior

Activity and SCM feedback should remain independently visible because both can be true simultaneously:

```text
Idle · Review feedback
Working · Review feedback
```

Reserve `Changes Requested` for a formal provider `CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision. An unresolved comment from a `COMMENTED` review should use distinct language such as `Review feedback` or `Comments to address`.

The feedback indicator should remain visible until the underlying feedback is resolved, regardless of whether the agent is currently working, idle, or waiting.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Changes Requested` is displayed only for a formal changes-requested review decision.
- Unresolved actionable review comments have a distinct presentation.
- Activity state and SCM/review feedback can be rendered concurrently.
- Starting work does not hide an unresolved-feedback indicator.
- Resolving all applicable comments removes the feedback indicator.
- Add backend coverage for `review_required + reviewComments = true` without deriving the formal `changes_requested` meaning.
- Add frontend coverage for an active/working session that still has unresolved review feedback.
- Keep multi-PR and stacked-PR aggregation behavior explicit and covered.

## Impact

- Optional, non-blocking feedback appears as a formal blocking review.
- The same PR condition appears and disappears as agent activity changes.
- Users cannot reliably tell whether feedback was resolved or merely hidden because the agent started working.

title: feat(desktop): desktop app optimisation pass v1
body:
Code changes: +1011 -218  
Tests: +569 -145  
Others: +0 -0

## Opening the app

You quit from a session. Next time you open the app, the old screen shows a loader until the daemon is up and the project list comes back.

Now you see that session's title and the composer immediately. You can type. Send stays off until the daemon says the session is real, and what you typed is still there. If you quit from the board instead of a session, you still get the loader.

## Starting a task

You hit Send on a new task. The old app waits for a git fetch to finish before the agent can talk.

Now the folder is ready first, the agent starts, and the fetch runs after that. The agent can talk while git is still fetching.

## Saving a long answer

The agent writes a long answer as many small saves. The old app wrote the database once per save. A 96-save answer was 96 writes, and any other open session waited behind them.

Now those saves are written together, about every 32 of them, or every 8 KB, or every 40 ms. That same 96-save answer is 3 writes. If the app crashes in that short gap, the agent can replay the unsaved tail.

The finished answer takes the same space on disk. The saving is how many times SQLite is written while the answer is still coming in.

## Disk cleanup

This pull request does not clean the disk. Nothing new labels ~/.ao, and nothing new deletes cache, prompts, or worktrees. That work was left out.

## A long chat that is already open

A page is one fetch of up to 200 rows, messages and tool rows together. Opening a long chat already loaded only the newest 200. Scroll up and the older 200s load. That part did not change.

What changed is a chat where you have already scrolled, so several of those chunks are open. You send a message and the reply streams in. Before, each save fetched every chunk you had open. Four chunks open, and one sentence that lands as one refresh, meant all four chunks came back. Now only the newest chunk is fetched again. The ones above it stay as they are.

If a save skips a row, or changes a row up in an older chunk, every loaded chunk is fetched again, once.

## Several sessions in one sitting

You open ten sessions. The old window kept a full chat copy for each of them.

Now it keeps the one you are looking at and the one you just left. Go back to an older one and that chat loads again. The agent is still running. That drop is not the session ending. Terminals keep their text.

## How a burst shows up

A sentence can arrive as one lump. The old playback typed for a moment, then gave up after 200 ms and dumped the rest, so it looked smooth and then jumped.

Now the lump stays buffered and comes out one word every 10 ms. A word with no space after it waits until the space arrives, or until the reply ends. Text that was already on screen when you opened the session is not played back from the start. [REFERENCED VERCEL'S SMOOTH STREAM FOR THIS]

## Summary

Accounts Manager adds an AO-owned account inventory, encrypted credential lifecycle, explicit session bindings, and coordinated account controls around the embedded CLIProxyAPI `v7.3.8` runner.

Draft checkpoint. Exact descendant retirement/deletion recovery, pending-switch restart, model compatibility, native-platform acceptance and current-main integration remain open. The user chooses accounts; the service must never silently choose a replacement or fall back.

Device-global credentials and the existing Subscriptions and native account-switching surfaces remain unchanged. Routing is disabled by default.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[Settings and session controls] --> API[AO loopback API]
    CLI[Thin HTTP CLI] --> API
    API --> Service[Account control service]
    Service --> DB[(Bindings and operation journals)]
    Service --> Runner[Embedded accounts runner]
    Runner --> Vault[Encrypted credential store]
    Runner --> Engine[CLIProxyAPI engine]
    Launch[Session launch] --> Service
    Service --> Child[Explicitly bound child runtime]
    Child --> Runner
    Runner --> Selector[Exact account selector]
    Selector --> Engine
```

## What is included

### Embedded runner and lifecycle

- Vendors the MIT-licensed engine with a bounded SDK callback listener/address extension documented in `accounts-manager/UPSTREAM.md`.
- Bundles the runner and supervises it from the daemon with authenticated reattachment, lease expiry, bounded restart backoff, and safe status reporting.
- Keeps management, lifecycle, data-plane and routing credentials separate. Listeners and callback transport remain loopback-only.

### Account lifecycle

- Browser and device login, API-key and credential import, verification, refresh/reconnect, enable/disable, models, and safe inventory projections.
- Encrypted durable storage with admission checks and refresh shutdown joining. Invalid credential verification does not become successful account authorization.
- Durable removal journals, impact/confirmation, stop/revoke acknowledgements, retry/cancel boundaries, tombstones and recovery. Exact retirement of escaped descendants is still a blocking defect.
- Only public-safe account/operation IDs and redacted errors cross the public boundary. Credentials, raw provider responses and private endpoints remain private.

### Accounts UI

- Dedicated Accounts settings alongside the existing Subscriptions page, inline login/import, verification, account details and provider-reported usage.
- Per-session selection, pending versus committed state, policy/revision/operation/request IDs, and switch retry/cancel controls.
- Removal impact preview with exact revision and confirmation. Unavailable service or usage remains explicit; no optimistic completion or invented quota.

### Routing and strict session pinning

- Explicit managed-account or native selection, with durable per-session/provider bindings.
- Reuses the selected binding for launch, restore and switch. No automatic fallback or silent repinning.
- Journals switch progress, preserves pending queues, fences runtime ownership and authorization revisions, and supports restart recovery.
- Selected-account failures remain actionable failures. Unrelated sessions must continue unchanged.

### Provider launch integration

- Child-scoped Responses API routing for the supported terminal integration and gateway environment routing for the supported CLI/ACP integration.
- Conflicting credentials are removed only from the routed child's environment.
- The app-server Chat integration remains on its native device account. Device-global auth/config files are not rewritten.
- Setup-token classification, usage eligibility, native Harness status integration, and the supported subscription-authentication design remain incomplete.

## Security and failure behavior

- Runner binds only to `127.0.0.1`; account control routes remain unavailable through Connect Mobile.
- Route capabilities are opaque, authenticated-encrypted, session/account scoped, and backed by a private persistent key.
- Credentials and route tokens stay out of public DTOs, logs, argv and persisted runtime metadata. Public errors preserve request IDs without provider bodies.
- Runner failure degrades account controls without failing daemon readiness. Native routing-off behavior remains available.
- Release HOLD: strict retirement refusal prevents unsafe completion, but five positive recovery cases across three groups still fail. Linux containment primitives remain unwired. This checkpoint must not be treated as complete teardown safety.

## Storage and API

- Routing migration `0165` plus `0166` through `0172` add bindings, switch/removal journals, ownership, history decisions and queue obligations after reconciling the branch with main. The obsolete duplicate `0148` from the original remote series was not reintroduced.
- SQLite stores public-safe account IDs and durable operation facts, not raw credentials.
- Public account/session controls delegate through service/port boundaries; the CLI remains a thin HTTP client.
- sqlc, OpenAPI and frontend API types are regenerated and checked for drift.

## Validation performed

- Backend and runner build/vet/pinned full lint pass on the preserved source snapshot.
- Complete backend ordinary suite: 10,882 passing, 10 failing, 75 skipped cases. Complete race suite: 10,887 passing, five failing, 75 skipped cases. Five retirement failures remain reproducible; intermittent descriptor-publication failures are documented separately.
- Complete runner ordinary and race: 297 passing cases each, no failures/skips.
- Complete engine ordinary: 10,043 passing cases, eight skips. Complete engine race: 10,038 passing, one media-relay failure reproduced on unchanged control source, 11 skips.
- Complete frontend on Node 22 and Node 24: 5,626 passing cases, six existing skips; both typechecks pass.
- API/SQL generation has no drift. All 91 protected paths, 33 generated entries and five guest-design/evidence entries retain their hashes.
- Linux package builds and the no-network installation smoke pass with the documented isolated packaging tools. Native installation/update and Windows/Mac certification are not claimed.
- Fresh pinned offline scans of the current changed source and all 71 PR-selected commits found no credential leaks under the repository rules.
- Real-account tests establish the bounded outcomes above, not permanent deletion, full runner/vault cold recovery or provider-side billing attribution for every request.

See [the current checkpoint](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/d6ff87eebd9d0e78d438ddcf00e79cb399435c4f/docs/plans/accounts-manager-completion/PUBLISH-2026-09-29.md) for full commands, retained failures, scope and native/live-provider gaps. Historical slice clearances apply only to their sealed snapshots.

![Account inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/04e12ca3dc78ba96674a63c2039ac6b0b271b52f/docs/plans/accounts-manager-completion/evidence/accounts-overview.png)

title: fix(frontend): make dev:web work on Windows
body:
## What

- replace the POSIX-only environment prefix in `dev:web` with a small Node launcher
- set `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1` in the child process while preserving Vite's normal `development` mode
- forward Vite arguments and resolve the frontend paths independently of the caller's working directory
- add focused launcher and process-start regression tests

Fixes #2589.

## Why

npm runs scripts through `cmd.exe` on Windows, where `VITE_NO_ELECTRON=1 vite ...` is treated as an executable name. The command therefore exits before Vite starts, blocking both the renderer-only development loop and Playwright's renderer web server.

The launcher uses Node's process environment API, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux without adding a dependency or changing the lockfile. Unlike a custom Vite mode, it preserves the existing `import.meta.env.MODE === "development"` behavior and does not introduce `.env.web` loading.

## Packaged Windows app

The packaged `.exe` is unaffected by this bug: `dev:web` is a source-development npm script and is not referenced by the Electron development, packaging, or runtime paths. `VITE_NO_ELECTRON` is set only inside the new launcher, so packaged renderers continue to leave the preview flag undefined and use the real daemon.

## Testing

Windows 11, Node 24.12.0, npm 10.9.1:

- `npx vitest run scripts/dev-web.test.mjs` — 2 passed
- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` — passed
- `npm.cmd run dev:web -- --port 5199 --host 127.0.0.1 --strictPort` — Vite started successfully and forwarded the arguments
- fetched the served preview module — confirmed `MODE: "development"` and `VITE_NO_ELECTRON: "1"`
- packaged-path audit — no Electron development, packaging, or runtime path invokes `dev:web` or the launcher

The previous revision's remote frontend test, renderer-smoke, mac-update-helper, and secret-scan jobs all passed. The updated revision reruns them.

title: feat(usage): show turn count and token throughput (tok/s) in USAGE & COST panel
body:
## Summary

Implements [#5747](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5747): the SessionInspector **USAGE & COST** panel gains two derived metrics, rendered inside the metrics grid (fresh input / cache reads / output / cache hit rate / **turns / throughput**):

- **Turns** — the number of assistant turns in the session. The usage pipeline ingests one usage event per assistant message, so this is a `count(*)` over the same visible-event scope the token totals use (AO's synthetic `<synthetic>` notices excluded). Always known.
- **Throughput (tok/s)** — **output** tokens divided by the span of the usage-event timestamps: `OutputTokens / (last_event_ts − first_event_ts)`. Generation speed is what the model writes per second — counting the input (and its cache reads) in the numerator inflates the rate to physically impossible numbers on cache-heavy sessions. `null` (rendered as "—") when any input is unknown: uncounted output, an event without a timestamp, or a single event leaving no elapsed time — a partial window never silently shortens the divisor.

## Implementation

- New storage query `GetUsageSessionEventWindow` (event count + `MIN`/`MAX(created_at)` + known-timestamp count) over the same visible (non-synthetic) scope as `AggregateUsageBySessionHarnessModel`; the synthetic filter matches the existing service-level rule (`lower(trim(model_id)) <> '<synthetic>'`). The per-model aggregate is unchanged.
- The `MIN`/`MAX` aggregate loses the declared column type, so the store parses the raw text back. The sqlite driver (`modernc.org/sqlite`) writes `time.Time` as its `String()` form (`2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999999 -0700 MST`), so that format is parsed first, with common fallbacks and RFC3339Nano accepted.
- `GET /usage/sessions/{sessionId}` (`SessionUsageResponse`) gains required `turns: number` and nullable `tokensPerSecond`; `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated via `npm run api`, sqlc gen via `npm run sqlc`.
- The inspector renders Turns and Throughput as two more cells of the existing metrics grid (`UsageMetric` conventions: `dt/dd`, aria labels, "—" when unknown). Throughput shows one decimal below 100 tok/s and rounded integers above. Labels added to all eight locale catalogs.

## Tests

- `backend/internal/service/usage`: `TestSummaryReaderGetDerivesTurnsAndTokensPerSecond` — turns from the window, output/span math, and the unavailable paths (NULL timestamp, single-event window).
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite`: full `TestMigration*` suite green (ledger + spec-drift tests included).
- `backend/internal/httpd/...`: route parity, embedded-spec match and controllers tests green.
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `SessionInspector.test.tsx` — 123 tests pass.
- Live check on a long-running install: a 376.6M-token session reports `turns: 2292`, `tokensPerSecond: 3.35` (160.7K output over the span) — physically plausible where the processed-based formula produced 7862 tok/s.

## Note on branch history

The branch was rewritten to a single squashed commit. It supersedes the earlier version pushed from the same AO session, folding in follow-up corrections: the numerator switched from processed to **output** tokens (the processed-based rate was physically unreachable on cache-heavy sessions) and the two stats moved from the outer header into the metrics grid. The event-window storage design of the original branch is kept.

Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Upgrades the pinned `agent-browser` runtime from 0.33.1 to 0.38.1. This PR only bumps the version: it changes `VERSION` and the five per-platform SHA-256 checksums in `frontend/scripts/prepare-agent-browser.mjs`, and one version number in a comment in `agent-browser-runtime.ts`. It adds no new commands, flags or `ao browser` actions.

## Why

With 0.33.1, agent mouse input in the desktop Browser panel is unreliable. I ran the same action suite through `ao browser`, in the real Electron app with the Browser panel open, on both versions:

| Browser panel open | 0.33.1 (current) | 0.38.1 (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `click` / `dblclick` change the page | ❌ report success, but the page doesn't change | ✅ |
| `screenshot` | ❌ hangs 60s → `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | ✅ 0.17s |
| Mouse actions (click, hover, check, …) | ~5s each | ~0.05s each |
| Toast appears, list re-renders, link opens a new tab | ❌ | ✅ |
| fill, type, press, select, focus, scroll, `act`, frames, tabs, network, console/errors, devtools, waits | ✅ | ✅ |

The upgrade also brings, with no AO changes:
- **Persistent snapshot refs (0.38):** an element keeps its ref when the page re-renders around it. Removed refs are listed in `removedRefs` and never reused.
- **Stream input latency fixes (0.33.2)**
- **New tabs inherit the session's headers, init scripts and routes (0.37)**
- **CDP transport recovery and dropdown label matching (0.38)**

Refs #5437: with the Browser panel visible, screenshots now succeed. With the panel hidden, capture still stalls on 0.38.1, so this PR does **not** fix #5437. The AO-side fix for hidden views is #5552.

## How

- The checksums are the SHA-256 digests GitHub publishes for the `v0.38.1` release assets. I also downloaded all five binaries and hashed them locally; they match.
- AO still depends on these parts of agent-browser's output. I checked each against the real 0.38.1 binary:
  - a ref that no longer exists still fails with `Unknown ref: eN`, and a ref whose element was removed with `Could not locate element with role=…`. Both strings still match `STALE_REFERENCE_MESSAGE`;
  - `_boundary` (`nonce`, `origin`) is still sent at the top level of the response when `AGENT_BROWSER_CONTENT_BOUNDARIES=1`;
  - the three licence files downloaded from unpkg still exist at the same paths for 0.38.1.
- Out of scope on purpose (follow-up PRs): `snapshot --delta`, `screenshot --if-changed`, `record`/contact sheets and `--pin-tab`. All of them need new command and flag handling in AO.

### Existing bugs found while testing (not caused by this PR, not fixed here)

All of these reproduce identically on 0.33.1 and 0.38.1:

1. **`act` never retries on a stale ref when run against the real binary.** agent-browser exits with code 1 when a command fails, so `AgentBrowserRuntime.run()` throws `AGENT_BROWSER_COMMAND_FAILED` before `parseAgentBrowserJSON` can map the error to `STALE_REFERENCE`. The unit tests stub the binary to exit with 0, which hides this. #4783 adds `AGENT_BROWSER_WAIT_TIMEOUT` mapping in the same code path and has the same problem. No existing issue; I'll file one.
2. **`ao browser get checked <ref>` always fails** (`Unknown subcommand: checked`). agent-browser has `is checked`, not `get checked`. No existing issue or PR.
3. **`ao browser wait --text-gone` is always blocked:** `agent-browser flag is managed by AO: --state`. #5171 recommends `--text-gone` in the browser skill docs. No existing issue or PR.
4. **Screenshot stalls when the Browser panel is hidden** (#5437). The fix is in progress in #5552.

## Testing

All CI jobs this change triggers were run locally with the workflow commands:

- `frontend / test` (macOS arm64, Node 24.21.0): all steps pass, including cloud-client (generate/diff, typecheck, 22 tests, pack), product-ui (typecheck, 133 tests, pack), `browser-runtime:prepare` from a clean state (fresh 0.38.1 download plus checksum check), landing `icons:check`, `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, and `npx vitest run` with `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TEST_BINARY` set: 339 files, 5201 tests, including the native compatibility test against the real 0.38.1 binary.
- `frontend / mac-update-helper`: passes (node tests, x64/arm64 helper builds, Swift state tests).
- `gitleaks` (pinned v7.4.0 image and repo config, PR commit range): no leaks.
- `frontend / renderer-smoke`: run in the pinned `playwright:v1.60.0-noble` container under x86 emulation on Apple Silicon. 7 specs failed; the same container on `main` fails 12, including all 7, so these come from emulation rather than this change (agent-browser isn't used in this suite). Relying on the CI run for this job.
- Real desktop app (`npm run dev`, isolated `~/.ao/dev` data): about 55 `ao browser` actions on 0.33.1 and on 0.38.1, with results in the table above.
- Not executed locally: the darwin-x64, linux-arm64 and win32-x64 binaries (checksum-verified only). CI runs the linux-x64 native test.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense (no new behaviour; the existing native compatibility test covers the upgrade)
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.): all pass locally except renderer-smoke, which only fails under local emulation (same failures on `main`); verifying in CI

title: fix(attachments): raise attachment size limits to 50 MiB per file / 100 MiB total (#5739)
body:
Code changes: +224 -81  
Tests: +427 -45  
Others: +0 -0  

## Summary

- raise single-file attachment limit from 10 MiB to 50 MiB across backend store, HTTP controllers, desktop client, and mobile package
- raise total attachment payload budget from 25 MiB to 100 MiB for multi-file batches
- update oversized body checks and request limits to accommodate larger video and media files
- keep rejection boundaries and client-side error messaging consistent across desktop and mobile
- check count and total size before base64 reads; serialize mobile picker additions
- keep provider-native chat images at 10 MiB per image and 25 MiB total, with larger chat images available by workspace path
- reject cloud tasks with attachments because the cloud create API does not support files
- allow larger attachment uploads to finish over slower mobile connections without extending ordinary mobile request timeouts
- mark attachment-bearing requests so the daemon keeps its ordinary timeout for text-only calls
- use a stable `.mov` extension for QuickTime video on all platforms

Closes #5739

## Demo

### Before (10 MiB limit rejected)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba7f3edf-af0d-4be3-8ff7-dd1a96b39974

### After (50 MiB limit accepted)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb92f586-e316-4927-a289-ab4d4cd91511

## Testing

- Focused desktop attachment and queued-edit suites (167 tests passed); frontend and mobile typechecks passed

## Local validation gap

Full repository-level end-to-end container checks require a local Docker socket unavailable on this Windows host. Scoped Go unit/integration tests, backend builds, and frontend/mobile Vitest suites passed locally on Windows. The changed Go packages passed race tests, and the changed frontend suites passed.

title: feat: add CommandCode (command-code) harness + worker effort support
body:
I want CommandCode in AO as a first-class harness — https://commandcode.ai/ (docs: https://commandcode.ai/docs).

From their docs, the integration surface is small and maps cleanly onto our existing adapter pattern (`opencode/opencode.go`, `omp/omp.go`):

- Binary: `command-code` everywhere, `cmd` on POSIX, `cmdc` on Windows (`npm i -g command-code`). Needs `binaryutil` PATH + npm-global resolution like opencode.
- Launch (headless-first): `cmd -p "<prompt>" --output-format json --max-turns 100 --skip-onboarding` — NDJSON `event` frames + final `result` line with `sessionId` (`docs/headless`). Resume via `cmd -p --resume <id>`, `--continue`.
- Hooks: `.commandcode/settings.json` with `PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / SessionStart` (`docs/hooks`) calling `ao hooks command-code …`, same shape as our `GetAgentHooks` + `activitydispatch` drivers.
- Auth: `cmd status --json` / `cmd whoami`. Models: `cmd --list-models`, `-m <id>`.
- Flags we must forward: `-m/--model` and `--effort <low|medium|high…>` (`docs/reference/cli`).

The gap — model/effort in the client:

Chat already does effort: provider catalog returns `efforts[]` (`dto.go:1865`), frontend `TurnSettingsBar.tsx` renders model + effort, drivers forward it (`codexappserver/driver.go`, `claudeacp/driver.go`).

Worker sessions don't: `domain/agentconfig.go` only has `model/mode/permissions` — no effort. `agentbase` only has `ModelConfigSpec` / `AppendModelFlag`, and `opencode` only forwards `--model`. I searched PRs for `effort` — no merged worker-effort PR found, so copying opencode for CommandCode would repeat the same hole: `--effort` would be silently dropped when the catalog has no `efforts`.

Robust fix proposed:

1. Add `effort` to worker `AgentConfig` (+ `ConfigSpec` field, `AppendEffortFlag`, validation, CLI `--effort`, DTO/OpenAPI regen) so `command-code --effort` and future `opencode`-style flags work even when `efforts[]` is absent — with empty = adapter default.
2. Then add `command-code` adapter on that plumbing (launch/restore/hooks/activity/auth/model catalog).

Happy to split into two PRs (effort plumbing first, harness second) — flagging here so we don't ship another model-only adapter.

title: fix(reviewers): disable declared MCP servers so Cursor reviewer panes never stall on approval
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5707. Cursor reviewer panes no longer stall on Cursor's "MCP Server Approval Required" screen: `PreLaunch` now disables every MCP server the checkout or host config declares inside the isolated reviewer profile, so an unattended auto-review runs to completion.

## Problem

In any repository with a checked-in `.cursor/mcp.json`, every Cursor auto-review hung ([#5707](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5707)). Cursor asks interactively to approve the server, nobody is watching the reviewer pane, and the review stays `needs_review` with no verdict. Approval state lives in the reviewer profile, which is keyed on `sha256(ReviewerID)`, so a manual click unblocks only that one pane � the next reviewer prompts again.

## Fix

- `(*Reviewer).PreLaunch` collects server ids from the workspace's `.cursor/mcp.json` and the host's `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, then runs `cursor-agent mcp disable <id>` for each one, with `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` set to the isolated reviewer profile and the workspace as cwd. Cursor records these in the same per-project `projects/<slug>/mcp-disabled.json` it writes itself (verified against `cursor-agent 2026.09.10`).
- The launcher calls `PreLaunch` on both fresh and restore paths, so this one site covers both.
- The launch argv is unchanged � deliberately no `--approve-mcps`, because auto-approving branch-declared servers would execute repo-controlled commands during review. This is Option 1 from the issue (disabled by default), consistent with [#2844](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2844), [#3745](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3745), and [ADR 0002](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-secure-interactive-reviewer-gateway.md).

## Validation

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/` � clean.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/ ./internal/adapters/agent/cursor/ ./pkg/agentruntime/ -count=1` � pass, including 5 new tests: disable wiring for project and user configs with dedupe and stable order, no-declaration fast path that spawns nothing, malformed config fails closed, argv/cwd/`CURSOR_DATA_DIR`-override builder, and validation plus context-cancellation guards.
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/reviewer/cursor/` � pass.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2` on the touched package � clean for this change.
- Behavioral repro on Windows with `cursor-agent 2026.09.10`: a fresh profile plus a workspace `.cursor/mcp.json` shows `not loaded (needs approval)` in `cursor-agent mcp list`; after `mcp disable` it shows `disabled`.

Known local-only failure excluded from the above: `TestPreLaunchWritesIsolatedReviewerConfig` asserts Unix mode `0700`, which NTFS reports as `777`. It fails identically on a pristine checkout on this Windows machine and is untouched by this change.

## Not in this PR

- Worker path (`pkg/agentruntime.buildCursorLaunch`) � untouched.
- API/DTO changes � none, so no `npm run api` regeneration.
- Opt-in auto-approval for trusted repositories (issue Option 3) � planned as a separate follow-up PR.

title: feat(inspector): show session artifacts in the Summary panel
body:
## Summary
- Adds an Artifacts panel to the session Summary view, shown in place of the "no PR opened" empty state when a session's output is artifact files rather than a pull request (`outputType === "artifact"`), listing each artifact by name.
- Clicking an `html` artifact opens it through the existing Browser preview flow (same mechanism as any other AO Browser link).
- Clicking a `markdown`/`file` artifact reuses the existing Files-inspector open flow (`onOpenReviewFile`), exactly like opening any other workspace file.
- V1 keeps PR presentation unchanged: PRs always take priority over the artifacts panel when a session has both.

Closes #4803 (frontend slice of #4514).

### Dependency note
This is the frontend slice; the backend slice (#4804, PR #4805) that actually populates `session.artifactFiles`/`outputType` is still open and its branch is currently ~200 commits behind `main` (doesn't rebase cleanly). Rather than block further, the pending wire shape (`SessionArtifact`, `Session.outputType`) is typed locally in `useWorkspaceQuery.ts` as an additive augmentation of the generated `ControllersSessionView` type, instead of hand-editing `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` (that file is generated from the backend's openapi.yaml and verified byte-for-byte by the `api-drift` CI check, so hand-patching it doesn't survive CI). Both fields are optional and simply absent at runtime until #4805 lands; once `schema.ts` is regenerated with the real fields, the local augmentation type in `useWorkspaceQuery.ts` can be deleted.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (frontend) — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` (frontend) — full suite: only pre-existing, unrelated failures remain (missing native `better-sqlite3` bindings under `--ignore-scripts`, missing landing-site env/deps); zero failures in files this PR touches
- [x] Added focused tests: `workspace.test.ts` (`sessionArtifacts` helper) and `SessionInspector.test.tsx` (panel rendering, PR-takes-priority, HTML→Browser click routing, markdown/file→Files click routing)
- [x] Added `inspector.artifact`/`inspector.artifacts` to every locale catalog (enforced by `i18n/instance.test.ts`)
- [x] Reproduced the `api-drift` CI check locally (`go generate ./internal/httpd/apispec/...` + `openapi-typescript` regen) — `schema.ts` now matches `main` exactly, no drift

title: feat(browser): expose agent-browser 0.38 snapshot deltas, human pointer and annotated screenshots
body:
Code changes: +313 -37 Tests: +605 -5 Others: +42 -9 (docs) ## What Exposes the agent-browser 0.38 features that AO can use today, after the runtime upgrade in #5776. All three are opt-in; every existing command behaves exactly as before. - `ao browser snapshot --delta`: the first call returns the full tree; later calls return `unchanged` or only the structural changes since the snapshot the agent last received. `--delta --full` returns the full tree and resets the baseline. `--full` without `--delta` is rejected. - `ao browser click --human` and `ao browser drag --human`: the pointer approaches along a curved path instead of jumping, for pages that ignore instant clicks. - `ao browser screenshot [path] --annotate`: numbers interactive elements in the PNG and lists the matching refs (`[3]` → `ref=e3`), in text, `--json` and `--base64 --json`. ### What this PR adds, and what it does not **Added in this PR (3):** | Feature | Version | What an agent can now do | |---|---|---| | `snapshot --delta` / `--delta --full` | 0.38 | Get the full page tree once, then only what changed | | `click --human`, `drag --human` | 0.38 | Move the pointer along a curved path for pages that ignore instant clicks | | `screenshot --annotate` | 0.38 | Get a PNG with numbered elements plus a legend mapping each number to a snapshot ref | **Already working since the #5776 upgrade, no AO code needed (5):** | Feature | Version | Why nothing was needed | |---|---|---| | Persistent snapshot refs | 0.38 | Default snapshot behaviour | | Stream input latency fix | 0.33.2 | Inside the runtime; fixed clicks landing late in the panel | | New tabs inherit session setup | 0.37 | Applies to the tabs AO already opens | | CDP transport recovery | 0.38 | Internal to the runtime's connection | | Dropdown label matching fix | 0.38 | Bug fix in `select` | **Not added, and why (6):** | Feature | Version | Why not | |---|---|---| | `screenshot --if-changed --threshold` | 0.38 | **Deferred, not blocked.** It changes the same function #5552 rewrites, and that PR's fallback capture bypasses agent-browser, which would make the changed/unchanged comparison wrong. Follow-up once #5552 merges | | `record`, contact sheets, recording cursor | 0.37–0.38 | **Deferred, bigger piece.** `record` is not in AO's allowed native commands; needs a new `ao browser record` action, an ffmpeg dependency AO does not ship, and recordings kept inside session storage. Its own PR | | Human pointer as a session default (`--input-mode`) | 0.38 | **Cannot, as things stand.** It is set when the browser session starts, and AO owns that launch; the per-action `--human` in this PR gives the same behaviour where an agent needs it | | `--pin-tab` | 0.34 | **Not needed.** It pins a session to one tab when several sessions share a Chrome; every AO session already owns its browser bridge | | Auth vault (`auth login --no-navigate`) | 0.38 | **Out of scope.** AO exposes no part of agent-browser's credential vault, and adding one is a security decision of its own | | WebMCP tool discovery | 0.36 | **Out of scope.** Experimental upstream, and it lets a page offer tools to an agent — a new trust surface that needs its own review | Nothing else in 0.34–0.38 needs AO work: the Linux CA-certificate flag, the Windows headless and ARM fixes, and the dashboard hardening are all launch-level or platform changes. ## What this looks like Nothing here changes the desktop UI — these are agent-facing CLI features, so the "before" and "after" are what an agent receives. ### `screenshot --annotate` Same page, captured twice. Each interactive element is numbered in the annotated image, and the numbers map onto snapshot refs (`[3]` → `ref=e3`), so a screenshot and a snapshot can be talked about in the same terms. | Before (`ao browser screenshot`) | After (`ao browser screenshot --annotate`) | |---|---| | | | The annotated run also prints the legend, inside AO's untrusted-content markers because the names come from the page: ```text Saved /tmp/shot.png (1228x1508) Annotated elements: <<>> [1] heading "Compat page" (ref=e1) [2] button "Alpha" (ref=e2) [3] button "Remove Alpha" (ref=e3) … <<>> ``` ### `snapshot --delta` What an agent receives when it re-checks the same 150-row page after each action. Before, every check resends the whole tree; after, the full tree arrives once and later checks carry only the change. | Before (`ao browser snapshot`) | After (`ao browser snapshot --delta`) | |---|---| | | | Measured on that page: full tree 8,506 characters, the delta after one click 272, an unchanged check 55.
The same transcript as text ```text # before: every check resends the whole tree $ ao browser snapshot <<>> - heading "Delta page" [level=1, ref=e156] - button "Add row" [ref=e157] …150 rows, 8,506 characters every time <<>> # after: the full tree once, then only what changed $ ao browser snapshot --delta # first call: the same full tree $ ao browser click e157 # add a row $ ao browser snapshot --delta Snapshot delta from revision 14 to 15 (apply to the revision 14 tree, or rerun with --delta --full): <<>> add @e622 button "Added row" replace 0 line(s) starting at 0-based line 7 with 2 line(s): - button "Added row" [ref=e622] - listitem [level=1] <<>> $ ao browser snapshot --delta # nothing changed since Snapshot unchanged since revision 15 (now revision 16). ```
## Why **Deltas.** Agents re-snapshot the same page after every click, save or reload, and each check resends the whole tree. On a 150-row test page a full snapshot was ~8.7 KB of output; after adding one row the delta was ~0.3 KB, and an unchanged page is one line: ```text $ ao browser snapshot --delta Snapshot revision 14 (full): <<>> - heading "Delta page" [level=1, ref=e467] - button "Add row" [ref=e468] …(150 rows, ~8.7 KB) <<>> $ ao browser click e468 && ao browser snapshot --delta Snapshot delta from revision 14 to 15 (apply to the revision 14 tree, or rerun with --delta --full): <<>> add @e622 button "Added row" replace 0 line(s) starting at 0-based line 7 with 2 line(s): - button "Added row" [ref=e622] - listitem [level=1] <<>> $ ao browser snapshot --delta Snapshot unchanged since revision 15 (now revision 16). ``` Deltas are opt-in because applying one requires the tree the agent already holds. agent-browser's own skill treats `--delta` the same way. The agent-facing skill doc now recommends it for repeated checks of the same page. **`--human`** helps with pages that ignore a pointer that teleports. **`--annotate`** gives an agent an image whose labels map onto snapshot refs, so a screenshot and a snapshot can be discussed in the same terms. ## How - **CLI** (`backend/internal/cli/browser.go`): the new flags, plus output per delta shape (`full`, `unchanged`, `delta`, and a "no element changes" line for an empty delta) and the annotation legend. All page-derived text stays inside the `UNTRUSTED EXTERNAL CONTENT` markers, including the fallback for a result kind the CLI does not recognize. - **Runtime** (`agent-browser-runtime.ts`): maps `delta`/`full`, `human` and `annotate` to native flags. Annotations are read from the native envelope and carry its `_boundary` nonce, like every other page-text channel. `--human` maps only to `click` and `drag`, the two native commands that accept it. - **Host** (`browser-view-host.ts`): after each delta snapshot the host stores a baseline per session: active tab, `--interactive` or not, and the revision delivered. It requests a full tree when there is no matching baseline, after tab and frame switches (agent-driven, user-driven, and profile switches), after a plain `snapshot`, and when native output is measured from a different revision. A request that must be full and is answered with anything else fails as invalid output, and a baseline is not stored if the active tab changed while the snapshot was in flight. So an agent is never handed a delta against a tree it did not receive. - agent-browser keeps a separate revision counter per tab (verified: a new tab starts at revision 1), which is why the baseline is keyed by tab. - **Docs:** `skillassets/using-ao/commands/browser.md` (agent-facing) and `landing/content/docs/cli.mdx`. Worth knowing: `--compact` snapshots omit text that has no ref, so a paragraph changing from "Not saved" to "Saved at …" is not in the tree and a delta correctly reports `unchanged`. That is existing compact-snapshot behaviour. ### Known limitation, shared with #5437 `--human` clicks and screenshots both need the Browser panel to be actually on screen: when the AO window is hidden or occluded, Chromium stops producing frames. `--human` actions now refuse immediately with `BROWSER_PANEL_HIDDEN` when the panel is hidden, rather than running to the 60s deadline and failing as a generic timeout, and the agent-facing docs say to ask the user to bring the panel forward. Ordinary clicks and every text-based command are unaffected. Screenshots can still stall on an occluded window — that is the defect #5437 describes and #5552 fixes. With the panel visible, a `--human` click completes in well under a second. Review follow-ups are in the last two commits: `--annotate` now reports when a capture came back with no annotations (in text and `--json`, including against a desktop host that ignored the flag) and surfaces a native annotation failure instead of an ENOENT; an unresolved `act` drops the delta baseline because it hands the agent a snapshot of its own; and a delta response no longer reinstates a baseline that was invalidated while it was in flight. ## Testing - **New tests** (`+495`): CLI flags and every output shape, including the empty delta, the unknown-kind fallback and `--json` annotations; runtime flag mapping and annotation/boundary passthrough; host tests for first-call full, `unchanged`/`delta` passthrough, revision-mismatch refetch, an explicit `--full` that is not answered with full, `--interactive` switches, tab and frame switches, plain-snapshot reset, invalid output, and `--human` forwarding for click/drag only. The native compatibility test now also exercises `--delta` against the real 0.38.1 binary. - **Real desktop app** (`npm run dev`, isolated `~/.ao/dev` data, Browser panel visible), through `ao browser`: the delta sequence above, `act` between deltas, `--full`, `--interactive`, reload, tab switch and frame switch; `--human` click (page reacted, under 1s) and `--human` drag; `--annotate` producing the legend and a PNG with numbered boxes over each element. - **CI jobs run locally** for this commit: - frontend `test` (Node 24): typecheck, typecheck:e2e, icons, fresh `browser-runtime:prepare`, full vitest with the native binary — 5233 passed, 6 skipped. - go `build-test` (Go 1.26.5 per `go.work`): gofmt, build and vet clean. In the full `-race` run, `agent/claudecode`, `agent/goose` and `internal/httpd` fail only under parallel load and pass when run alone; `adapters/runtime/tmux` fails identically on `main` on this machine. This PR touches none of those packages. - go `lint` (golangci-lint v2.12.2): 0 issues. `api-drift`, `sqlc-drift`, `cloud-build-test` and `cli-e2e` native (macOS) all pass. react-doctor reports no issues. - CI on this PR: everything passed except the frontend `test` job, which failed in `src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`'s cleanup with `ENOTEMPTY` while its 5232 other tests passed. The updater writes its staged state fire-and-forget, so a write can land while that test's `afterEach` removes the state directory. A second commit makes the removal retry; the test file is unrelated to this change and is included only to keep CI green. - **Not run locally before opening:** `renderer-smoke`, the `cli-e2e` container job and `gitleaks` — Docker is unavailable on this machine right now; relying on the CI run. Also `windows-workspace` and the Linux/Windows `cli-e2e` runners. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) — except the three Docker-dependent jobs noted above, which CI will run

title: feat(terminal): copy on select, and keep wrapped lines joined when copying
body:
Copying text out of the desktop terminal has two rough edges. Both are in the terminal copy path — `frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx` — and both are things the user hits on every paste.

## 1. Selecting text does not copy anything; Cmd+C has to be pressed while the mouse button is still down

What I do: drag-select a sentence in a running Claude Code session. What happens: nothing reaches the clipboard when I release the button, and the highlight itself disappears a moment later — the agent TUI repaints continuously and xterm drops the selection on buffer updates. The only way to copy is to keep the button held and hit Cmd+C before the repaint lands; let go first and the selection is gone.

What I expect — and what every other terminal on this machine does (Ghostty, Terminal.app, iTerm2): releasing the mouse button after a selection puts that text on the clipboard. No key, no race against the repaint.

From the code, copying runs only from the DOM `copy` event and a keydown shortcut (`copySelection()` around line 768, listeners around line 996); nothing fires when a selection is completed. xterm 5.5 has no `copyOnSelect` option, so this has to live in the app: copy on `pointerup` while `term.hasSelection()`, or subscribe to `term.onSelectionChange()` (debounced, so a drag doesn't write to the clipboard on every change). A setting to switch it off would be welcome as well — I'd just leave it on.

## 2. Copied text is cut by a newline exactly at the window width

What I do: select a paragraph wider than the terminal. What I get: the text arrives with a hard line break at the right edge of the window, mid-sentence, so nothing copied out of the terminal is usable for pasting anywhere else.

Why: the agent TUI lays its output out to exactly the terminal width and does not use its own newlines for prose, so xterm never marks those rows as wrapped and `getSelection()` joins them with `\n`.

Suggested: in the copy path, after `term.getSelection()`, rejoin lines whose untrimmed length equals the terminal width. It is a heuristic, but for these TUIs it matches what the user sees as a single line. `getSelectionPosition()` plus the buffer API would allow a more precise join if you prefer.

## Environment

- AO desktop 0.13.0, arm64, macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0). Sessions run under AO's own pty host.
- Agent in the terminal: Claude Code 2.1.278 (its fullscreen renderer).
- Repro for both: open a session, let it print a long response, drag-select across the right edge, release — the clipboard stays empty and the highlight vanishes; hold the button and press Cmd+C — the text arrives broken at the window edge.

Related: #3640 (same component). That issue explains why mouse reporting to the PTY is suppressed to keep selection working — I am not asking to revisit that trade-off; clicking in an agent TUI's input box not moving the caret was closed as expected behavior and I accept that. I am only asking for the copy half to be pleasant.

Happy to send a PR for either or both if you want one — small and localized, with a test next to `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`.

*Reported from my own use of the app; the wording and the analysis above were drafted with my local coding agent from my observations, and everything is reproducible with the steps listed.*

title: feat(cloud): coder template picker + multi-repo dev kit at project setup
body:
## Summary

Adds a Coder dev-kit picker at **project setup**. When adding a cloud project on a coder-enabled org, you pick a template plus its curated form (size, optional startup script) and any additional repositories. The choices are stored on the project, and every coder session of the project inherits them, so sessions spin up exactly as they do today. Default (no template, single repo) is unchanged.

## How it works

- The config lives on the project's existing `Config` jsonb under a `coder` key, so there is no migration.
- `createProject` validates and stores it. `createSession` loads the project (new `GetProject`) and applies template/size/startup to the sandbox plan. The worker clones the project's extra repos beside the primary checkout at launch.
- The coder client gains `ListTemplates`, exposed via `GET /orgs/{orgId}/sandbox/coder/templates` (coder-entitled orgs only).
- The Azure template (`coder-azure-vm`) declares `size` (mapped to an Azure SKU) and an optional `startup_script` coder parameter. The size default maps to the prior SKU, so an unset value is a no-op.
- Frontend: `CoderTemplatePicker` in the cloud Add-Project flow, gated on the org offering coder. Its choices flow into `createProject`. The new-task composer is unchanged.

## Zero-regression baseline

Default (no coder config) sends nothing and behaves exactly as before at every layer. Size and startup are only sent with a chosen non-default template, because the default template does not declare those rich parameters.

## Verification

- cloud `go build` / `vet` / `test` green, including new provisioning and validation tests.
- frontend `typecheck` clean. TaskComposer, NewTask, CreateProjectFlow, cloud-cp client, and i18n coverage tests pass.

## Not yet live (needs infra)

- `terraform validate` plus a `coder templates push` of the updated Azure template so size and startup take effect.
- A live coder run to validate extra-repo cloning and its on-disk placement (currently under `<dataDir>/repos`).
- Arbitrary private third-party extra repos need per-repo grants. Today the worker reuses the session grant token, so same-installation repos work and others fail non-fatally.
- OpenAPI contract update deferred (the cloud-client drift job is path-filtered and `provider` is already absent there).

title: feat(terminal): copy on select, and keep wrapped lines joined when copying
body:
Code changes: +109 -1
Tests: +290 -2
Others: +8 -0

## Summary

Two fixes to the desktop terminal copy path (`XtermTerminal.tsx`), from #5785:

**1. Copy on select.** Releasing the left mouse button after a selection (drag, double-click word, triple-click line) now copies it to the clipboard — the behavior every native macOS terminal (Terminal.app, iTerm2, Ghostty) has, and identical for every agent pane since it lives in the app, above the PTY. xterm computes the selection continuously during `mousemove` and its own `mouseup` handler does not touch the selection, so copying on `pointerup` reads an already-final selection model and cannot race the TUI repaint that later drops the highlight — no keys, no Cmd+C race. Arming happens on `pointerdown` inside the terminal (left button only), so releases elsewhere in the app (context menu items, the scrollbar) never re-copy a lingering selection. Only a left-button release consumes the armed flag (an in-between right-button release does not eat the drag), and `pointercancel` / window blur disarm it — those never deliver the `pointerup`, so a stale flag would otherwise copy on the next unrelated click.

A "Copied to clipboard" toast confirms the copy, reusing the existing copy toast. A settings switch (Settings → Sessions → "Copy on select") turns it off; it defaults to **on**, and follows the same ui-store + localStorage mechanics as the other settings switches (`ao.terminalCopyOnSelect`).

**2. Wrapped lines stay joined when copying.** Agent TUIs repaint full-screen with absolute cursor moves, so visually continuous rows never get xterm's `isWrapped` mark and `getSelection()` returns them with a hard newline exactly at the window edge. The copy path now walks the selected buffer range via `getSelectionPosition()` and drops the newline between adjacent selected rows when the upper row fills every column of the grid. Fullness is measured the way xterm itself composes cells: the row is full when its untrimmed composed text (`translateToString(false)`, null cells compose to spaces, a wide char covers its continuation cell) does not end in whitespace. That is cell-accurate — a row packed with wide (CJK) characters is full although its UTF-16 length stays below the grid width — and keeps xterm's own wide-char-safe text extraction untouched. The join applies to every copy path (shortcut, native copy event, context menu, copy-on-select) since they all route through the same `copySelection()`.

## Testing

- Unit: `XtermTerminal.test.tsx` — copy on pointer-up (+ toast), no copy when the setting is off, no copy for releases that did not follow a left-button press inside the terminal, right-button release mid-drag keeps the left drag armed, `pointercancel` and window blur disarm the pending selection, full-width row joining, wide-character (CJK) rows joined by cell coverage, xterm-wrapped rows staying merged; `ui-store.test.ts` — setting default on / persistence / opt-out read-back; `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx` — settings row renders.
- Real desktop app (this checkout, isolated dev instance): running Claude Code session, drag-select across the right edge, release → clipboard filled via `pbpaste` with wrapped lines joined (no hard break at the window width); a 79-column full row joined with its continuation (91-char line in the clipboard) while non-full boundaries kept their newline; toast shown; Settings → Sessions switch default on, off → no copy on release. Same release-to-copy verified on a Codex pane (the codex agent turn itself could not complete in the isolated dev environment, so joined-lines were exercised on the Claude Code transcript).

## Risks / follow-ups

- The full-width join is inherently a heuristic — a genuine paragraph line that happens to end at the last column joins with the next. No on-screen marker exists to disambiguate; this matches the trade-off the issue accepts.
- Copy on select fires on double-click word and triple-click line selections too (same as native terminals).

Fixes #5785

title: fix(desktop): prevent unsafe channel downgrades
body:
Code changes: +30 -20  
Tests: +37 -15  
Others: +0 -0  

## Why
Nightly migration 0146 removes columns that the older Stable daemon reads during startup. If an updater channel switch installs that older Stable binary after Nightly has migrated the database, the daemon exits before its API becomes ready. The main-database copy also contains standalone sessions that older Stable cannot read.

## Change
- Keep `allowDowngrade` false after setting every update feed channel, so a channel choice waits for a newer release instead of replacing the app with an older binary.
- Show the pending channel state after a successful check and discard persisted older staged builds across channels.
- Cover newer and older targets in both channel directions, saved preferences, startup recovery, and staged-build handling.

## Verification
- Reproduced the daemon exit with isolated Stable → Nightly → Stable → Nightly and Nightly → Stable → Nightly sequences, including published macOS daemon binaries and a copy of the main database.
- Full frontend Vitest suite: 5,300 passed, 6 skipped (347 files); focused updater suite: 191 passed. Typecheck, production package build, cloud client and product UI package checks, macOS update-helper tests, and native state tests passed locally.
- Linux renderer smoke: see CI checks. The macOS renderer smoke run passed 56/60 tests; four unrelated chat renderer tests could not find their expected UI on this local host.

## Limits
This prevents updater-driven downgrades once a patched app is installed. It cannot make already released older binaries read a newer database, prevent manual installation of an older app, or recall a macOS native installer already armed before the patch. Publishing remains the release conductor's responsibility.

title: fix/5320
body:
## Summary
Adds a "Reload window" action that reloads the Electron renderer shell 
directly, separate from the existing browser panel reload. Fixes #5320 

## Problem
The app had no way to refresh the renderer shell without a full app 
restart. The existing "Reload" in the titlebar View menu and native app 
menu follows the *focused* web contents — so if the browser panel had 
focus, it would reload the panel instead of the shell, which isn't the 
behavior needed for recovering from renderer-side glitches or stale state.

## Changes
- New UI: "Reload window" button in General Settings → Advanced 
  (`GeneralSettingsSection.tsx`)
- New IPC wiring: dedicated main/preload channel that explicitly 
  targets the shell's web contents (`main.ts`, `preload.ts`) — sender is 
  restricted to the shell itself, so this can't be triggered from the 
  browser panel's context
- Existing behavior reused, not duplicated: the action goes through 
  the existing chat-draft unload guard (`confirmUnsafeChatDraftLeave`), so 
  unsaved draft state is protected the same way it already is elsewhere — 
  no new confirmation dialog was built
- Out of scope, untouched: `BrowserPanel.tsx` and the existing 
  View-menu "Reload" behavior are unchanged

## Decisions (per the issue's open questions)
- Audience: available to all users, not developer-only
- Placement: General Settings → Advanced
- Confirmation: reuses the existing draft-loss guard rather than 
  adding a second dialog

## Testing
- Added coverage for the new button in `GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx`
- Manually verified the actual bug scenario: with the browser panel 
  focused, "Reload window" reloads the shell, not the panel
- Full suite: 5,220 passed / 0 failed / 6 skipped (341 files) — verified 
  against an independent, isolated run of unmodified `main`, which showed 
  the same 23 pre-existing failures (better-sqlite3 Node ABI mismatch, 
  missing nested dependencies, incomplete Electron install) unrelated to 
  this change
- TypeScript typecheck and `git diff --check` pass

## Translation note
CI enforces locale-key parity, so "Reload window" translations were added 
to every locale. They were spot-checked for meaning and consistency with 
the existing `titlebar.reload` wording, but are machine-translated and 
haven't been reviewed by native speakers.

title: fix/5758
body:
## Summary
Excludes merged and closed PRs from the "CI Failed" timeline badge in the 
session inspector's Activity view. Fixes #5758.

## Problem
The Activity timeline's `scmTimelineStates()` derived `ci_failed` by 
iterating every entry in `session.prs` and checking `pr.ci === "failing"`, 
without filtering to open/draft PRs. A merged PR with a stale, pre-merge 
`ci_state=failing` would surface a "CI Failed" badge even when the 
session's current open PR had fully passing CI.

## Root cause
`openPRs()` elsewhere in the daemon's SCM derivation already correctly 
filters to open/draft PRs. `scmTimelineStates()` didn't use it — it had 
its own independent iteration over the full `session.prs` list.

## Changes
- `scmTimelineStates()` now checks CI failure membership against 
  `openPRs(session)` instead of iterating all PRs unfiltered
- `openPRs()` itself is unchanged — it was already correct
- Review and conflict timeline states are unaffected; this only scopes 
  the CI-failed derivation

## Testing
- Added the exact regression scenario the issue described: one open PR 
  with passing CI (#5753) + one merged PR with failing CI (#5754) → 
  asserts no `ci_failed` timeline state is produced
- Baseline: 347 files, 5,296 passed, 7 skipped. After: 347 files, 5,297 
  passed, 7 skipped (the +1 is the new regression test) — zero regressions
- TypeScript typecheck passed
- Manually verified in the running app with the real PR data from the 
  issue (#5753 open/passing, #5754 merged/failing): Activity now shows 
  "Exited · Conflict" with no CI Failed badge

## Note
Two runs under high worker concurrency hit an unrelated `browser-history-store` 
timeout; it passed 3/3 in isolation and the full suite passes under normal 
concurrency. Pre-existing flake, unrelated to this change — flagging in case 
CI catches it mid-flake.

title: bug(browser): tab chip drifts horizontally outside inspector and overlays session content
body:
## Bug

The embedded Browser panel's page-tab UI can drift horizontally outside the inspector and render over the main session content.

In the observed state, the active page chip (favicon plus page title) appears over the conversation pane, while the Browser panel itself remains docked on the right. The tab UI is therefore no longer anchored or clipped to its browser toolbar.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session in the desktop app.
2. Open the Browser inspector and navigate to a page.
3. Resize or otherwise change the width/layout of the Browser panel.
4. Observe the active browser page tab while the layout updates.

## Expected behavior

Browser tab UI remains anchored inside the Browser panel toolbar and is clipped to the inspector bounds during every layout transition.

## Actual behavior

The active page-tab chip moves horizontally across the app and overlays the session conversation outside the Browser panel.

## Environment

- Windows desktop app
- Nightly build
- Exact build/version not captured
- Reproducibility still needs confirmation

## Visual evidence

The reporter supplied a screenshot showing the "Fastest AI Inference Cloud ..." tab chip floating over the center conversation pane while the Cerebras browser content remains in the right inspector.

## Acceptance criteria

- Browser page tabs never render outside the Browser inspector bounds.
- Resizing, docking, maximizing/restoring, and switching browser tabs do not move tab UI over session content.
- The active tab remains aligned with the browser toolbar at narrow and wide inspector widths.
- Add regression coverage for the layout transition that causes the drift.

## Related

- #5184 tracks native browser-surface instability during resize/maximize/overlay transitions. This report is specifically about the browser tab UI escaping its inspector bounds and overlaying the session content.

title: fix(cloud): multi-repo checkout on production + default app to production CP
body:
## What

Two related cloud fixes, one for each half of getting a fresh app build working end to end against the production control plane.

### 1. Multi-repo checkout works on the production control plane

A cloud checkout token minted through the GitHub App was scoped to the project's primary repository alone (`repository_ids: [primary]`). Sessions whose project declares coder dev-kit extra repositories could clone the primary repo but got a 403 cloning the siblings, because a least-privilege GitHub App installation token only grants access to the repositories it names.

This worked on staging and broke on production for a subtle reason:

- **Staging** has no local GitHub App (it is production-gated), so a worker checkout authenticates with the session creator's broad user PAT, which can read every repository the user can. Extra repos cloned fine as a side effect of that breadth.
- **Production** has the GitHub App configured locally, so the checkout path mints a per-repository App token scoped to the primary repo only. Any extra repo outside that scope 403s.

The fix broadens the checkout grant (`Service.IssueCheckoutGrant`, the path production actually uses) to cover the primary repository plus any declared extra repositories that resolve within the same installation:

- Extra repo URLs are read from the project's coder config and resolved to numeric IDs by enumerating the installation's accessible repositories, so an out-of-installation or unselected extra is simply dropped instead of failing the whole token mint.
- Any error loading or resolving the extras falls back to a primary-only token, so broadening the scope can never regress the primary checkout that already worked.
- Push and pull-request grants stay primary-only, matching where a worker actually writes. Only the read-only checkout is broadened.

Known limitation: an extra repository under a different GitHub owner/installation than the primary cannot be covered by a single installation token and is left out. That is an inherent GitHub constraint, not something token scoping can work around. Same-owner sibling repos (the common case) are covered.

### 2. Default the app's control plane to production

`defaultCloudControlPlaneURL` now points at `https://api.aoagents.dev` instead of `https://staging-api.aoagents.dev`. This is an app-side default only (what a desktop build dials when nothing overrides it); it does not change anything inside the control plane. `AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` still overrides it for local testing against either environment.

## Testing

- `cloud`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` all pass; `gofmt` clean.
- `backend`: `go test ./internal/config/...` passes (pinned-default assertion updated for the new URL).
- New unit tests in `cloud/internal/githubapp/checkout_scope_test.go`: repo-URL parsing, installation-scoped ID resolution (match, case-insensitivity, dedup, out-of-installation drop), the broadened mint asserting `repository_ids` and `contents:read`, and both fallback paths (extras error and no extras declared).

title: fix(sessions): present session teardown as archive, not delete
body:
Fixes #5768

The control that archives a session carried a `Trash2` icon and red danger styling on every surface, so it read as a permanent delete — hiding both what the action does and that an Archive section exists to restore from. The sidebar row also archived on the bare click while the session page asked first, and that prompt was an inline popover rather than the shared modal.

## Changes

**1. Archive icon instead of the trash icon**

`Trash2` → lucide `Archive` on the sidebar session row and the session-page top bar (the two surfaces the issue names), plus the board card and inspector, which drive the same action.

The danger-red treatment went with it (`variant="killIcon"` → `"icon"`; `hover:bg-error/10 hover:text-error` → neutral). A permanently-red control signals "delete" as loudly as the icon did, and the board's own `ArchiveRestoreButton` already uses exactly this neutral treatment.

The **"Remove project"** trash icons are untouched — that one really does delete.

Labels followed the icon: "Kill session" / "Terminate session" now read "Archive session" across all 8 locale catalogs. That is what tells users the Archive section exists and that their work is recoverable.

**2. The sidebar confirms before archiving**

`SessionActions` called `terminateSession()` straight off the click. It now opens the same confirm every other surface uses.

**3. The popover is now the shared modal**

`SessionTerminationPopover` → `SessionArchiveDialog`, built on the existing `ConfirmDialog` (the settings / new-task modal frame):

- title "Are you sure you want to archive …?"
- subtext "You can always restore … from the Archive section later."
- buttons **Confirm** and **No**

`ConfirmDialog` gains optional `cancelLabel` and `confirmAriaLabel` props, both defaulting to today's behavior.

One deliberate deviation from the issue text: the title names the session ("…archive fix login?") when it has one, rather than the literal "the session". The old prompt already did this and it is more informative — easy to change if you would rather match the issue exactly.

## A real bug caught while testing

React portals re-dispatch synthetic events up the **React** tree, not the DOM tree. Confirming from inside a board card therefore also fired that card's `onClick` and opened the very session being archived. The old popover guarded against this with its own `stopPropagation`; `ConfirmDialog` now does the same on both content and overlay. An existing board test caught it.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- 402 tests across the 9 affected files pass (Sidebar, ShellTopbar + linux, SessionsBoard, SessionInspector, ConfirmDialog, i18n ×3, CommandPalette), including a new Sidebar test asserting nothing is archived before the confirm is accepted.

Not done, flagged honestly:

- **No clean full-suite run on this machine.** The failures it did surface were checked against the base commit: `browser-profile-import` (18) and `browser-history-store` (1) fail *identically at `1c88819` without this change* — `better-sqlite3` native bindings do not load locally. `TaskComposer` (1) was a flake under parallel load; it passes 36/36 in isolation on this branch and passed on base. CI should be the judge.
- **No visual check in the real desktop app** — `ao` was not available in the environment this was written in. Since the issue is explicitly about how the dialog looks, a reviewer eyeballing the new modal would be worthwhile.
