title: feat(cloud): connect GitHub via the control plane GitHub App (secure, works in release builds)
body:
## Problem

The cloud New Project "Connect GitHub" ran a **desktop-side** OAuth flow (`connectProviderAuth`) that reads `AO_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `AO_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` from the app process environment. Two problems:

1. Nothing bakes those vars into a released build (no CI injection, no vite/forge define, `.env.local` is git-ignored and dev-only). So a normally installed app hits `GitHub OAuth is not configured. Set AO_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID...` and cannot connect GitHub.
2. The flow would require the GitHub App **client secret** to live on the desktop, which is extractable from the app bundle.

## Fix

Wire the desktop into the GitHub App flow the control plane **already serves** (the same endpoints behind the install callback). This is the secure, hosted path:

1. Connect GitHub calls `POST /orgs/{orgId}/github/installations/start`; the control plane builds the install/authorize URL (it holds the client id and secret).
2. The desktop opens that URL in the system browser (existing `openExternal` bridge). The user installs the app on their repositories.
3. GitHub redirects to the control plane's own callback, which performs the code exchange server-side and records the installation. No GitHub secret ever reaches the desktop.
4. The desktop polls `GET /orgs/{orgId}/github/installations` until an active installation appears (bounded, cancelable).
5. The dialog lists the installation's repositories (`GET /orgs/{orgId}/github/repositories`) and creates the project by repository id (`POST /orgs/{orgId}/github/projects`), carrying the coder dev-kit config nested under `config.coder`.

The manual personal-access-token path stays exactly as before, as the fallback.

Because the project is now backed by a GitHub App installation, cloud checkout uses least-privilege App tokens. That composes with the multi-repo scope broadening in the companion PR (#5817): this PR gives production a working GitHub connection, that one makes multi-repo checkout work over it.

## Scope

**Client-side only. No control plane, Go, or OpenAPI contract changes** (the endpoints already exist). Files:

- `lib/cloud-cp/types.ts`, `lib/cloud-cp/client.ts`: add the GitHub App connect methods (`startGitHubInstallation`, `getGitHubUser`, `listGitHubInstallations`, `syncGitHubInstallation`, `listGitHubRepositories`, `createGitHubProject`) and their types.
- `components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx`: rework `CloudProjectCard` (connect + poll + repo picker + `createGitHubProject`); the desktop-OAuth secret path is removed, the PAT path is kept.
- i18n: 10 new keys added to all eight catalogs (en/de/es/fr/ja/ko/pt-BR/zh-CN) with real translations.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx vitest run` for `CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx` (56), `lib/cloud-cp`, and `coder-session-options-store` (10): all pass. Two obsolete desktop-OAuth tests were rewritten to the App flow (connected create by repo id; install initiation opens the CP URL and involves no desktop secret).
- The only failing files in the full suite are pre-existing and environmental (a `better-sqlite3` NODE_MODULE_VERSION mismatch in `browser-profile-import`, and the `src/landing` sub-package whose deps CI installs separately); they fail identically on the clean base with these changes stashed.

## Interactive verification (needs a person)

The end-to-end path needs a one-time browser step (install the app on a repo). Ready to run through it on production once reviewed.

## Problem

The desktop app never says what AO is costing the machine. When the fans spin up there is no way to see whether AO is holding 500 MB or 5 GB, which session is the heavy one, or what that session is actually running — the board shows tokens and cost, nothing about memory or CPU.

#5511 asks for this as a CLI (`ao ps`). The same attribution is missing in the app, where most people are looking when the machine gets slow.

## Proposal

A Diagnostics view in the desktop app, in two places that share one component: the board's memory light opens it as a window, and Settings has it as a page.

- **Machine** — how much AO holds against what is free, and a CPU line graph for the machine and AO's share of it.
- **Sessions** — one row per live session with its memory and CPU, expanding into its process tree (each process named with its PID) and the agent's recent tool calls.
- **Agent Orchestrator** — the daemon and app as their own row, so AO's own cost is not hidden inside a session.
- **Copy report** — the whole reading as plain text for pasting into a bug report: the machine, then every session with its processes and recent steps. No PIDs and no command arguments in the text; they mean nothing to a reader and can carry paths.

Visibility only. Nothing in the view ends a session — killing stays on the board card where it already lives.

## Related

- #5511 — the CLI half of the same attribution problem.

title: feat(board): memory and CPU diagnostics for AO and every session
body:
Code changes: +3886 -53  
Tests: +2809 -9  
Others: +975 -16

## What
A Diagnostics view that shows memory and CPU for all of AO: the daemon and app, every session, and every reviewer, on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Why
Fixes #5836. When a user says "AO is slow", nothing showed which part of AO was using the machine.

## How
- `backend/internal/procmem` reads the process list on each OS. `service/usage/memory.go` adds up each session's process tree, AO's own processes, the tmux server and reviewer processes.
- If AO can't measure a session, it shows `-` (or `null` in `ao session top --json`), never 0.
- If the app dies, the daemon no longer counts the whole machine as AO (`daemon.go`). A failed Windows read no longer turns the panel off until restart (`snapshot_windows.go`).
- Another machine's board shows no memory figures, since they would be this machine's (`SessionsBoard.tsx`).
- On Mac and Linux, `npm run dev` now runs the daemon it already builds, not `go run`. This makes dev count the same processes as the real app. After a backend change, run `npm run build:daemon`.

## Testing
`go build`, `go test` for `procmem`, `usage`, `cli`, `lifecycle` and `daemon` pass. `GOOS=windows go vet` and frontend `tsc` are clean. Vitest for the board, memory panel and dev launcher passes (96 tests). I haven't tested on a real Mac or Windows machine.

## Checklist
- [x] Continuing an existing PR branch
- [x] Links the related issue
- [x] Tests added for the review fixes (`steps_test.go`, `daemon-launch.test.ts`)

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

title: fix(agent): skip Kiro model discovery while signed out
body:
## Summary
Background model discovery runs `kiro-cli chat --list-models --format json`. When Kiro is signed out, that command opens the browser sign-in page (`app.kiro.dev/signin?...redirect_from=kirocli`). Discovery runs on daemon start, on wake, on binary/config change and on every failure retry, so the sign-in page kept reopening without any user action.

- **Sign-in check next to the discovery spec.** Kiro's `modelcatalog` spec now carries a sign-in check. Before the model command, discovery runs `whoami --format json` with the same binary, working dir and env. `KIRO_API_KEY` counts as signed in.
- **Model command runs only after the check passes.** The check passes on a recognized signed-in response, or a clean exit with no signed-out text. Otherwise the model command never runs, so the sign-in page can't open:
  - **Clear signed-out answer:** returns `ports.ErrAgentModelDiscoverySignInRequired`.
  - **Timeout, or failed exit without recognizable status:** an ordinary discovery failure, recorded and retried like any other.
  - **Caller cancellation:** returns the context error.
- **Signed out is not a failure.** The agent service handles the sign-in error separately from real failures:
  - No retry budget is spent and no retry timer is set.
  - A cached catalog keeps its models, drops any earlier stale marker or failure warning, and stores the warning "Kiro is not signed in; sign in to load its models", so cache-first reads show it too.
  - A first load stores an idle placeholder with the same warning.
  - Both have their validation times cleared, so they are due for revalidation even if models loaded earlier the same day. A sign-in made anywhere, including from a terminal outside AO, is picked up by the next picker read or daemon start. No manual refresh is needed. The refresh state stays `idle` because the picker shows a spinner for `queued`.

## Tests
- `modelcatalog`: every probe outcome maps to the right result:
  - model command runs: signed in; unrecognized output with a clean exit; API key.
  - sign-in skip: signed out; signed-out text with a clean exit.
  - ordinary failure: failed exit without status; probe error; timeout.
  - cancellation: caller canceled.
  - Harnesses without a sign-in check never probe.
- `service/agent`:
  - A signed-out first load stores an idle placeholder whose cache-first reads carry the sign-in warning, and it loads after sign-in.
  - A cached catalog that previously failed (stale, "timed out") becomes non-stale with only the sign-in warning, keeps its retry budget across repeated signed-out refreshes, and reloads after sign-in.
  - A catalog loaded earlier the same day, followed by a sign-out skip and a sign-in from outside AO, is due on the next cache-first read and reloads in the background. This test fails without the fix.
  - An ordinary discovery failure still spends a retry.
- Pre-existing failures on this Windows machine are unrelated to this change and fail the same way without it: Codex account file-mode tests, two modelcatalog config tests that read local agent config, and a daemon temp-dir cleanup lock.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Not verified against a real Kiro CLI (not installed on the dev machine). If Kiro's signed-out `whoami --format json` output contains no recognizable signed-out text, it is treated as a failed check: retried and surfaced as an error rather than "not signed in". The sign-in page still does not open.

title: fix(cloud): Coder multi-repo extra-repo clone + first-class extra repos in agent context
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes for the coder dev-kit multi-repo feature, from a root-cause investigation of "I set up a project with two repos but only the primary got checked out."

### (a) Coder extra-repo clone permission (commit 2d43b6e4e)

Extra repos never cloned on the **Coder** provider. They are cloned as siblings of the primary checkout (`…/repository` -> `…/<name>`), but the worker runs as the worker user while Coder owns the durable root (`/home/coder`) and leaves it group-unwritable. Creating the sibling dir failed with `could not create work tree dir '/home/coder/<name>': Permission denied` (confirmed from the live ao-worker log). The primary works only because its dir is pre-chowned to the worker; nodeops is unaffected because its image chowns the whole workspace root to the worker.

Fix: grant the worker's group write on the durable root itself (non-recursive, so Coder's own home contents are untouched) without transferring ownership.

Ruled out with tests: not auth/scope/#5817 (a primary-only installation token still clones the public repo fine; GitHub serves public repos regardless of token scope), not repo availability, not size/timeout.

### (b) First-class extra repos in the agent context (commit 41c98decc)

Extra repos were cloned but second-class: the shared project prompt named only the primary repo, so an orchestrator coordinating a multi-repo project never learned the extras existed, and the cloud task composer showed only the primary. Now the extra repositories are named in the shared roleprompt project context (both roles become aware the project is multi-repo), and the task composer lists the full repo set for cloud projects. The worker still gets its concrete on-disk sibling paths from its own launcher note. Also corrects the stale comment claiming orchestrators have no checkout.

## Testing

- cloud: gofmt/build/vet clean; tests pass for roleprompt (new: extras listed for both roles, omitted when none), sandbox/coder (new: startup script grants durable-root group write), httpapi, workerexec.
- frontend: typecheck clean; TaskComposer 44/44.

## Deploy note

(a) lives in the CP-generated coder startup script, so a CP redeploy makes new sessions pick it up (no template rebake). Existing sessions need a re-spawn.

title: feat: add OpenHands CLI harness
body:
Code changes: +671 -20
Tests: +583 -3
Others: +129 -7

## Summary

Adds [OpenHands CLI](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI) (`openhands`) as a selectable Terminal UI harness.

**Adapter** (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/openhands/`)
- Launch: `openhands [--llm-approve|--always-approve] --task=<prompt>`. `--task` queues the prompt into the interactive TUI, so the terminal stays open afterwards. The `=` form keeps prompts that start with `-` from being parsed as flags.
- Resume: `openhands --resume <id>`, using the `session_id` OpenHands hooks report (verified to be the ID `--resume` accepts).
- Permissions: default and accept-edits → always confirm (OpenHands has no edits-only policy, so AO doesn't escalate); auto → `--llm-approve`; bypass → `--always-approve`. Tool allow/deny lists are rejected rather than ignored.
- Model: `env LLM_MODEL=<m> openhands --override-with-envs`. With saved settings, OpenHands applies a partial override for that process only. The `env` prefix works under both tmux and ConPTY.
- Version: requires ≥ 1.12.0, the first release that loads `hooks.json`. It is checked once per binary at launch, not in `ResolveBinary`: `openhands --version` takes about 6s (Python startup) and readiness allows only 2s.
- Auth: `~/.openhands/agent_settings.json` (or `$OPENHANDS_PERSISTENCE_DIR`) with a model → authorized. Missing file → unauthorized, since the TUI would otherwise open its first-run wizard.

**Hooks and instructions**
- Installs `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit` and `Stop` in `.openhands/hooks.json` and uses the standard activity deriver (complete coverage).
- OpenHands ignores `SessionStart` output and reads `additionalContext` only at the **top level** of hook stdout, not under `hookSpecificOutput`. `ao hooks openhands user-prompt-submit` therefore emits `{"additionalContext": <system.md>}`, and `system.md` is required for OpenHands launches.
- OpenHands drops top-level event keys when a `{"hooks": …}` wrapper is present, and rejects files that spell one event two ways. Before installing, the adapter rewrites existing direct-format or mixed-spelling user files into the wrapped PascalCase form so the user's own hooks keep firing.

**Wiring**
- Harness enum and registry.
- Migration `0192_allow_openhands_harness.sql` — rebased off `0156` onto the next unburned version after `main` advanced through 0191. It rewrites both current post-OpenCode-v2 constraint variants (with and without the legacy `qm` value), inserting `'openhands'` before `'fake'`.
- Burned-version ledger gains `192`; `reconcileHarnessConstraint` now knows about OpenHands via the same `'fake'))` anchor the DeepSeek repair uses, so any recognized pre-OpenHands shape (Gemini/FX/MiMo/DeepSeek/OpenCode-v2 era included) widens correctly, and verification fails closed with a specific error otherwise.
- Install plans: `uv tool install openhands` everywhere (the package pins Python 3.12, which uv resolves), plus the upstream installer on macOS/Linux.
- Auth "Set up OpenHands" plan, which opens the native first-run settings.
- Direct model entry in the model catalog.
- API enums with regenerated `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` (openapi-typescript 7.4.4, same as CI).
- Avatar (official OpenHands app icon, MIT) and agent list.
- Docs: `docs/harnesses/openhands.md`, in-app agents table, `ao spawn` skill doc.

## Testing

Run locally on Windows 11 against a real OpenHands CLI 1.16.0 install:
- After the rebase onto current `main`: `go test` passes for every touched package: `openhands`, `registry`, `activitydispatch`, `domain`, `modelcatalog` (PR-relevant tests), `cli` (hooks + full suite), `agentauth`, `systeminstall` (plans), `storage/sqlite` (migration 0192, burned-version ledger, startup repair), `skillassets`, and `httpd/apispec` (spec drift).
- `TestMigrateAllowsOpenHandsHarness` covers both paths on a 0191 base: fresh migration 192, and repair of a profile that burned 192 but still carries the pre-OpenHands CHECK.
- Full `go test ./...` compared against a clean current-`main` checkout on the same machine: every failing package (aider, copilot, crush, fake, kilocode, kimchi, kimi, modelcatalog env tests, pi, primeagent, codexappserver, cursoracp, persistenthost, processenv, reviewer/agy) fails identically on `main` — Windows-environment causes (missing POSIX `sh`/`tmux`/`true`/`sleep`, `AO_SESSION_ID` leakage, machine-local auth/config discovery).
- golangci-lint v2.13.2 on an LF checkout: zero findings in any touched file (the only full-tree findings are in `_windows.go` files, which Linux CI excludes). `gofmt` clean.
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean; vitest passes for `AgentAvatar`, `agent-options`, `agent-select-options`, and `HarnessSettingsSection`. product-ui typecheck and all 157 tests pass.
- Live contract test (`AO_LIVE_OPENHANDS=1`): version and required flags checked against the real CLI.

**Not verified locally:**
- A full interactive AO session with a live LLM (no API key on this machine).
- The Linux/macOS CI jobs and the docs site build.

## Known risks and follow-ups
- Once AO creates `.openhands/hooks.json` in a worktree, OpenHands stops reading the user's global `~/.openhands/hooks.json` there (OpenHands uses the first file it finds).
- If a repo commits its own `.openhands/hooks.json`, installing AO's hooks modifies a tracked file. Gemini and Goose have the same problem.
- Instructions are appended to every user message. This costs context, but they survive OpenHands' history condensation.
- `--override-with-envs` also picks up any `LLM_API_KEY`/`LLM_BASE_URL` already set in the session environment.
- Follow-up: an ACP Chat driver via `openhands acp`.

title: feat: add harness updates, logout and model defaults
body:
Code changes: +10608 -1846 Tests: +9250 -354 Others: +1510 -69 ## Summary ### Update - The notification stack also offers Update all beside Show all. It updates eligible, undismissed notices in place, expands progress/error cards, skips busy/manual/login-required targets, rechecks version and installer ownership, blocks duplicate submissions, and continues when one target fails. - Add Update all for eligible installed harnesses on the selected host. It rechecks each target, skips busy or unsupported harnesses, prevents duplicate submissions and continues if one update cannot start. - Add an Update operation for supported harness package managers (npm, Homebrew, Winget, Bun, uv, pipx). - Run the harness's own self-update for vendor installs: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode (pinned to the approved release with `--method curl`), Cursor, Goose, Kimchi, OMP, Autohand, Amp (`--porcelain`), Grok, Kimi, Droid, Qwen, FX, Pi (`update self --no-approve`) and Prime Agent. The command runs from the resolved binary sessions launch, not whichever copy `PATH` finds first. - Remove the Setup guide button from installed harness actions. Manage each harness on its own page (see Harness page below), with active-session safeguards, progress, retry, diagnostics, and translations. Update starts without a confirmation step; Logout asks first. - Show stacked update notices from the shell after startup readiness. Each notice offers Update, Login, Update manually or View details; dismissals are remembered per release. An update started from a notice that fails stays explained there until it is dismissed, even when a refresh then reports the harness current (an updater can replace the binary and still exit with an error). ### Harness page - Settings → Harness keeps the sorted harness list beside the open harness when there is room (720px and wider) and opens the first harness automatically; narrower layouts keep list → page → back. The list keeps the existing order (authentication, then installation). - List rows show only the logo, the name, a muted update icon when a newer release is confirmed, and a status dot only for harnesses that need login or failed. Versions and status text live on the harness page; not-installed harnesses stay in place but recede. - The open harness has underlined Account, Models and Health tabs. Each section groups its rows in one card with dividers; the harness name uses the section-title size. - Models pages catalogs ten models at a time and leaves out effort text for models without effort levels. - Carries main's harness-row changes onto the page: a configured setup harness reads as Configured and keeps its setup action, documentation-only setups offer "View documentation" (#6470), and a harness AO cannot install links to its installation guide (#5856). ### Account and Health details - Show the adapter-resolved executable in Health and copied diagnostics, shortening paths under the daemon host's home to `~`. The path remains available when update checks are disabled, no release feed exists, or the executable's version probe fails. - Add `POST /agents/{agent}/logout`, backed by a fixed, supported native logout command and the same terminal workflow as login. The client cannot supply an executable or arguments. Unsupported harnesses omit the action. - Confirm logout on the selected host, then refresh authentication, readiness, and model catalogs. An unknown or still-configured result is not shown as a successful logout. Short-lived logout terminals retain their exit notification. ### Authentication diagnostics - Health keeps authentication compact: status and the detected credential/source, with a single last-checked row. Executable appears immediately above Detected credential in the Status card; versions and maintenance method remain visible. Individual auth checks, repeated timestamps, cache age, provider responses and next steps stay in Copy diagnostics. Missing files and CLI executables are not presented as detected credentials; failed rechecks show a short message while the report retains correlation details. - Claude Code records its CLI result and provider validation evidence: credential source, provider, HTTP status, cached result timestamp, and expired-but-renewable login guidance. Cursor, Kiro and Devin record their local credential or bounded CLI check evidence, including timeout, command failure and unrecognized output. Codex retains native CLI failure details and explains pending account reconciliation or fallback from its account store. Pi, OpenCode and OMP report missing, unreadable or malformed credential stores; Pi explains unresolved environment references and deferred credential commands, while OMP explains disabled credentials. Remaining harnesses keep their native verdicts and receive an actionable fallback when a check supplies no detail. - When an environment token overrides stored credentials, Health names the variable rather than the stored login: Copilot follows its documented order (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, then its stored login, then `gh auth token`) and never attaches the hosts.yml user to a token from the environment, and Kimchi reports `KIMCHI_API_KEY`, which Kimchi uses ahead of its config at launch. Health's Detected credential row shows the credential the readiness check selected. - Explain local-login versus AO discrepancies with the actual check executable, selected credential source, selected host and timestamps. Native stored-login evidence plus provider rejection gets a specific explanation; unproven terminal/profile differences remain possibilities. The copied report explains that AO checks its own process environment. Unknown results remain distinct from signed out. - Auth diagnostics add actionable next steps while preserving existing auth decisions. They never include credentials, raw CLI output, provider response bodies or raw transport errors. - Health rechecks and post-login verification retain failed request code/request ID, display the failure on the selected host, and include it in copied diagnostics. Successful rechecks clear the request failure. - Include backend and UI regression coverage and regenerated API artifacts. ### Shared model catalogs and model selection - Remove the hardcoded Claude model fallback and its unused cross-scope alias-labeling path. Failed discovery retains the matching persisted provider catalog; without a matching cache, manual entry remains available. Explicitly configured defaults remain alongside successfully discovered models. - New Task selects a replacement only when filtering hides a model marked as the catalog default. If no default is reported, filtering an unrelated model preserves the blank override and the harness’s native model/provider selection, including FX. - Claude context variants keep independent model switches, and a live alias retains its concrete catalog entry when that model is disabled so its current label stays accurate. Credential badges parse dotenv comments, quoting and final assignments; Aider includes Anthropic keys; Prime Agent reads only its own credential directory, including tilde expansion. - Harness Settings, New Task, project role settings and reviewer pickers use one persisted model catalog and one discovery/refresh pipeline per harness and scope. Settings skips session-history recency; task pickers retain it. Cached reads remain available during background refresh, and global catalog change events refresh both Settings and affected project pickers. - The shared catalog includes native command/configuration/ACP/app-server output and each supported harness's own local provider catalogs: OpenCode, Kilo, MiMo, Pi, Kimchi, Prime Agent and OMP. Models from unconfigured providers remain visible; providers without models are omitted from the Models page. Configured badges report credential presence, not provider acceptance. Context windows and text/image inputs appear only when reported by the catalog. - FX discovery includes Gateway, Codex, Grok and custom profile connections. Connection-qualified selections distinguish identical native model IDs across connections; launch and restore decode them into process-local `FX_PROVIDER` and `FX_MODEL`. Saved FX settings and existing raw model overrides keep their behavior. Partial refreshes retain cached models only for failed connections, with a warning. - Remove the separate Settings `BrowseAll` switch and cache scope, the test-only discovery wrapper, and the obsolete Claude/Muse-only warmer. Tests use the production discovery and scheduler. Old Settings-only cache rows are ignored. Project and cloud credential scopes retain their boundaries; cloud credential discovery does not expand from device-local catalogs. - Settings → Harness → Models controls the shared picker filter through `disabledModels`, stored per computer in `harnessDefaults` (migration `0198_harness_defaults`, `PATCH /settings/harness-defaults/{agent}`, `GET /settings`). Empty means every catalog model. Already selected models remain visible, and a list disabling every available model falls back to the full catalog. Live chat keeps its protocol-supported choices and applies the same filter, including ACP model options. - This changes offered choices, not launch-time defaults. Codex terminal model/effort validation remains best effort when catalog evidence is unavailable. Existing picker display ordering remains; equal-label catalog entries have a stable ID tie-break. - Regression test sources cover shared-cache reuse and refresh, broader discovery, cloud-scope isolation, FX connection selection/restore, partial refresh, scheduler behavior and cross-view catalog invalidation. ### Ownership: update the copy sessions actually run - Resolve the exact executable selected by the harness adapter, run its bounded version probe, and prove which package manager owns that path before checking for or applying updates. - Read the owner from the binary's own location (Homebrew Cellar and Caskroom, npm `node_modules` including scoped packages and Windows `.cmd` shims, uv tools, pipx venvs), confirm it with that manager, and list the confirmed owner among the harness's methods. Harnesses installed through a supported manager under a package AO does not list (Goose from `block-goose-cli`, Devin from the `devin-cli` cask) are now maintainable. - When a Homebrew install receipt names a different tap from the formula AO lists (for example `my-org/tools/opencode` rather than `anomalyco/tap/opencode`), the receipt's package replaces the listed one for both the release check and the upgrade. - Recognise npm installs outside the daemon's own `npm root -g` (nvm, fnm, Node tarballs, installer prefixes such as `~/.local`) from the binary's npm prefix after checking the package name, and run updates against that prefix with its own Node and npm. - Treat any binary outside a package or version manager whose harness ships a self-update command as vendor-maintainable. Prime Agent's installer npm-installs a release tarball the registry lacks; its npm layout belongs to the vendor installer. - npm never claims a binary in Bun's, pnpm's or Yarn's `node_modules`, so an npm update cannot write into another manager's directory. Version-manager shims (Volta, asdf, mise) and pnpm/Yarn layouts stay advisory-only. - Ownership and runtime probes that parse a manager's output (`npm root -g` and its pnpm/Yarn/Bun equivalents, `pipx list --json`, the owning prefix's `node`/`npm --version`) read stdout only, so a manager warning on stderr cannot fail the check. - Before an update, the daemon re-proves that the chosen method installed the binary the harness adapter runs; otherwise it refuses with `409 INSTALL_OWNER_UNCONFIRMED`. A binary that no longer runs can still be repaired through the method of AO's own successful install. - Serialize same-harness launches with reinstall, update, and the existing protected Droid/fx installs; operations for different harnesses remain independent. - After an update the daemon re-probes the binary and fails the job if it did not reach the approved or announced release. ### Update availability - The daemon checks installed harnesses once after startup readiness, without blocking startup, then re-checks them every 6 hours with a fresh lookup (`AO_HARNESS_UPDATE_INTERVAL`, default `6h`, minimum `1h`). Each pass re-reads readiness, so newly installed harnesses are included. `AO_HARNESS_UPDATE_CHECKS=off` disables checks for offline or policy-restricted machines. - At most 2 checks run at once, enforced inside the installer service so every caller (timer, Settings, notices) is limited. A check runs the harness CLI's `--version` (30–240 MB each while it runs), so a burst across ~15 harnesses could otherwise take 1–1.5 GB for a few seconds. Harness Settings and the notices still share one in-flight check per harness. - The app only reads the daemon's cache: it polls every 15 minutes, also while the window is hidden or minimized, and retries after 5 minutes if the fetch itself fails. A cached result is served however old it is. Only these start a check: daemon start, the 6-hour timer, a harness with no result yet (first request, or after an install/update job clears it), and clicking Update. There is no "Check now" button. - Updates always install the `latest` release, so every source is checked against `latest` only (no per-prerelease channel). An install newer than latest, e.g. a beta, reports `ahead_of_latest` ("Newer than latest") and is not offered an update, which would be a downgrade. - npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun read `registry.npmjs.org` dist-tags first (the full package document exceeds 1 MB for popular harnesses) and fall back to the manager only when the public registry is unreachable, e.g. behind a mirror. - Homebrew core formulae and casks read the live Homebrew API instead of local metadata that is only as fresh as the last `brew update`; tap packages keep the local lookup. - Vendor releases on GitHub read the tag from `releases/latest`'s redirect (no REST rate limit), with the REST API as fallback. - Version schemes per harness: Cursor (`2026.10.01-e373342`), Amp (`0.0.1791388870-g4d32fb`) and Muse (`1.4.3-R5018.1`) carry build identifiers, not prereleases, and are ordered by their numeric core; same-version rebuilds report `build_unordered`. Muse's `1.4.3 (1.4.3-R5018.1)` output is accepted. - An unproved owner, unsupported source, unparseable version, prereleases of different channels or failed lookup yields `unknown`, never "current". A `lookup_failed` result (network or registry error) is checked again on the next read after 30 minutes. Other unknowns (no release feed, unconfirmed owner, unparseable version) wait for the next 6-hour pass. - Harnesses with no installable method (Unreal Agent is built into AO; CodeWhale, Kiro on macOS, and Devin, Muse, Prime Agent and FX on Windows require a manual install) show their own reason instead of an ownership warning. ### Reliability - Add `TestLiveHarnessReleaseFeeds` (`AO_LIVE_HARNESS_FEEDS=1`), which queries every vendor feed and package registry the advisory reads, and a daily `harness-release-feeds` workflow that runs it, so a vendor endpoint that moves or changes format fails CI before users see `unknown`. - Regenerate OpenAPI and frontend types. ## How it works ### Update check ```mermaid flowchart TD UI["Harness settings / update notice
poll every 15 min"] -->|"GET /agents/{agent}/update-advisory"| Cache{"Cached result?
served at any age; lookup_failed
retried after 30 min"} Cache -->|yes| Result Timer["Daemon: startup, then every 6 h
(AO_HARNESS_UPDATE_INTERVAL)"] -->|fresh lookup| Slots Cache -->|"no, one shared check per harness"| Slots["At most 2 checks at once"] Slots --> Probe["Resolve the binary sessions run
and probe its version"] Probe --> Owner{"Which installer owns it?"} Owner -->|"package manager
(npm, Homebrew, Winget, Bun, uv, pipx)"| Registry["Read the latest release
npm dist-tags, Homebrew API, Winget, PyPI"] Owner -->|vendor installer| Feed["Read the vendor release feed"] Owner -->|cannot prove| Unknown["unknown: ownership_unconfirmed"] Registry --> Compare{"Compare installed with latest"} Feed --> Compare Compare -->|older| Behind["behind_latest: offer Update"] Compare -->|same| Current["current"] Compare -->|newer, e.g. a beta| Ahead["ahead_of_latest: no update offered"] Compare -->|not comparable or lookup failed| Unknown Behind --> Result["Advisory shown in Settings and notices"] Current --> Result Ahead --> Result Unknown --> Result ``` ### Running an update ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as Harness settings participant D as Daemon participant PM as Package manager or vendor CLI User->>UI: Click Update UI->>D: Re-check advisory (refresh=true) D-->>UI: behind_latest, latest version UI->>D: POST /agents/{agent}/install
operation=update, expectedVersion D->>D: Refuse while a session of this harness runs (HARNESS_ACTIVE) D->>D: Re-prove the method owns the running binary
else 409 INSTALL_OWNER_UNCONFIRMED D->>PM: npm/bun pkg@latest, brew upgrade, ...
or the vendor's own self-update PM-->>D: exit status D->>D: Re-probe the binary alt reached expectedVersion D-->>UI: succeeded, "Updated X to Y" else did not D-->>UI: failed, with diagnostics end ``` ### Models in pickers ```mermaid flowchart LR Sources["Native harness output and supported provider catalogs"] --> Refresh["One discovery and refresh pipeline"] Refresh --> Catalog[("Shared persisted catalog per harness/scope")] Catalog --> Settings["Harness Models page: enable/disable models"] Settings -->|"disabledModels"| Preferences[("Host settings")] Catalog --> Filter["Shared picker filter"] Preferences --> Filter Filter --> Pickers["New Task, project roles and reviewers"] Preferences --> Chat["Filter live chat protocol choices"] ``` ### Logout ```mermaid flowchart LR Click["Account tab: Log out"] --> Confirm["Confirm on the selected host"] Confirm -->|"POST /agents/{agent}/logout"| Term["Terminal runs the harness's fixed native logout command"] Term --> Recheck["Refresh authentication, readiness and model catalogs"] Recheck --> State{"Still signed in or unknown?"} State -->|no| Done["Shown as logged out"] State -->|yes| Warn["Not shown as a successful logout"] ``` ### How each harness is checked and updated AO first works out which installer owns the binary sessions run. **If a package manager owns it**, AO asks that manager's registry for the latest release and updates through it. **If the vendor's own installer owns it**, AO reads the vendor's release feed and runs the harness's own self-update. Without a confirmed newer release, AO shows "Update manually" or nothing, never an Update button. How each package manager is checked: | Package manager | Where AO reads the latest version | Update command AO runs | | --- | --- | --- | | npm | `registry.npmjs.org` dist-tag `latest`; `npm outdated` / `npm view` if the registry is unreachable | `npm install -g --prefix @latest` | | Bun | npm registry `latest`; `bun pm view` as fallback | `bun install -g @latest` | | Homebrew | `formulae.brew.sh` API (core formulae and casks); local `brew` metadata for taps | `brew upgrade [--cask] ` | | Winget | `winget upgrade` listing; `winget show --versions` | `winget upgrade` for that package | | uv / pipx | PyPI | `uv tool upgrade ` / `pipx upgrade ` | | pnpm / Yarn | registry, then the manager | none (advisory only) | Per harness ("mac only" means AO offers that method only on macOS): | Harness | Package managers AO updates through | Vendor self-update AO runs | Vendor release feed AO checks | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | Homebrew cask `claude-code` (mac only), npm title: docs.aoagents.dev shows NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID
body:
## What happened

Opening `https://docs.aoagents.dev` in Brave on Windows shows **Your connection is not private** with `NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID`. Expanding **Advanced** says the site uses HSTS and cannot be visited.

## Expected behavior

The documentation site should load over HTTPS with a certificate valid for `docs.aoagents.dev`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open `https://docs.aoagents.dev`.
2. Observe the browser privacy error.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected on 2026-09-24 at approximately 20:11–20:12 IST against checkout `2137dd3ff39c825ad9612b837615e143d4f4228a`.

- `curl.exe -I --connect-timeout 15 https://docs.aoagents.dev/` fails with error 60 / `SEC_E_WRONG_PRINCIPAL`: the target principal name is incorrect.
- A read-only TLS handshake shows the server presents `CN=*.github.io`, issued by Let's Encrypt. Its SANs cover GitHub domains but do not include `docs.aoagents.dev`.
- `Resolve-DnsName docs.aoagents.dev -Type CNAME` returns `untrivial-ai.github.io`, so the hostname is currently routed to GitHub Pages.
- `gh api repos/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pages` reports `cname: docs.aoagents.dev`, `html_url: http://docs.aoagents.dev/`, and `https_enforced: false`.
- Searches across open and closed issues for `docs.aoagents.dev`, `ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID`, `connection is not private`, `documentation certificate`, and `GitHub Pages HTTPS` found no matching report.
- Related deployment change: #5824 introduced the dedicated GitHub Pages docs deployment and custom-domain cutover.

**Hypothesis:** GitHub Pages custom-domain certificate provisioning did not complete after the docs-site migration. The observations confirm the hostname/certificate mismatch, but do not expose the repository's Pages certificate provisioning state.

title: fix(cloud): robust extra-repo checkout resolution + cloud loading loader z-index
body:
## Summary

Three fixes on one branch (rebased onto latest main). Two need a control-plane deploy, one ships in the desktop app.

### 1. Multi-repo checkout robust resolution (control plane)

When a declared extra repository is missing from the installation's eventually-consistent repository listing (for example a repo just made private, or freshly granted), `resolveInstallationRepositoryIDs` now falls back to a direct `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` with the installation token:

- 200 means the App can access the repo, so it joins the checkout token scope.
- 404 means it is genuinely ungranted, so it is reported as unresolved rather than silently dropped.
- `checkoutRepositoryIDs` logs a WARN naming any excluded extras (loud, instead of a silent narrowing to primary-only).

This fixes a private extra repo (for example ChartSnip) failing to clone when the installation listing momentarily lags behind a grant or visibility change. Every included ID is still one the App can mint a token for, so the broadened checkout token never 422s.

### 2. Cloud session loading loader z-index (renderer)

`CloudSessionLifecycleLoader` used a raw `z-[200]`, far above the app z-scale (max `z-overlay: 50`). While a cloud session loaded, any shell modal opened over the main pane (the New Task dialog, a project three-dots menu) rendered behind the loader and was invisible, while its Radix modal still set `body { pointer-events: none }`, freezing the whole UI including the sidebar. Lowered to `z-chrome` so modals render above the loader and stay usable. Local sessions never render this loader, which is why the freeze was cloud-only.

Ships in the desktop app, no control-plane deploy needed.

### 3. Cloud session display-name length (control plane)

`validSessionInput` capped `displayName` at 80 bytes, but the renderer derives a cloud session's name from the task brief with a 100-character slice (raised from 80 by #5125). Any brief longer than 80 chars produced an 81 to 100 char name that the control plane rejected with `422 validation_error` ("Session project, kind, harness, name, or prompt is invalid"), blocking cloud task creation. Raised the cap to 100 and switched to rune count (not byte length) so a multibyte name is measured the same way the renderer slices it. `display_name` is a `TEXT` column, so no migration.

Confirmed in prod CP logs: repeated `422 POST /api/cloud/v1/orgs/{orgId}/sessions` for the affected user. Requires the same control-plane deploy as fix 1.

## Tests

- Three new githubapp checkout-scope cases: fallback resolves a private extra, an inaccessible extra is excluded while the primary still mints, the resolver surfaces unresolved names.
- New `validSessionInput` boundary test: 100-char name accepted, 101 rejected, and 100 multibyte runes accepted (the case a byte cap would have wrongly rejected).
- A SessionView loader z-index regression guard (asserts `z-chrome`, rejects a raw `z-[...]`).
- CP: `go build ./... && go vet && go test ./internal/httpapi ./internal/githubapp` green.
- Renderer: 141 SessionView tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: fix(telemetry): clear stale build properties from PostHog person profiles
body:
## Problem

PostHog person profiles show a stale version. The install labelled `github_actor = illegalcall` runs `0.13.1-nightly.202609232348`, but its profile reads `ao_version` / `app_version` = `0.10.4-nightly.202607181358`. All 99 handle-labelled profiles have a stale `ao_version`.

Older renderer builds wrote `ao_version`, `app_version`, `build_mode`, `platform` and `surface` to person profiles before profiles were turned off in July. Nothing has written them since: the only identified update is the once-per-process `$set` from #5521, which carries `github_actor` alone.

## Change

That same update now also sends `$unset` for those five keys. It clears them rather than copying the current version in, because a copy would go stale again on the next update, would only refresh on one send per daemon run, and every event already carries the current values. Version breakdowns should use event properties.

No new identified events: the `$unset` rides the existing once-per-process update. Later events stay anonymous.

## Change size

| | Files | Added | Deleted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| Tests (1 new test) | 1 | 58 | 0 |
| Other (comments, blank lines, docs) | 3 | 9 | 1 |
| **Total** | **3** | **69** | **1** |

"Code" is `posthog.go`'s 2 code lines. "Tests" is `posthog_test.go`'s 58 code lines. "Other" is 1 blank line in `posthog.go`, 3 comment and 2 blank lines in `posthog_test.go`, and 3 added / 1 removed in `docs/telemetry.md`.

## Verification

- New test `TestPostHogSinkClearsStalePersonProperties` goes through `NewPostHogSink` and the real send path, and checks the wire body: the first spawn carries `$unset` for all five keys, the second stays anonymous.
- Ran the daemon against a local stand-in PostHog endpoint (nothing reached real PostHog) and started two sessions. The first `ao.session.spawned` sent `$set = {github_actor: Pulkit7070}` and `$unset = [ao_version, app_version, build_mode, platform, surface]`, with the event's own `ao_version = 0.13.1-nightly.202609232348`. The second sent no `$set` or `$unset`.
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/telemetry/...` and `golangci-lint` pass.

## Limits

Profiles are cleared the next time each install starts a session on a build with this change. Profiles without a GitHub handle are never written by the daemon, so they keep their July values; nothing should read versions from profiles.

title: fix(review): guard reviewer panes against no-op tool-call loops (#5701)
body:
Code changes: +230 -0
Tests: +226 -0
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #5701

## What

Reviewer panes can degenerate into dozens of consecutive no-op tool calls and burn the whole turn budget until a human types into the pane. This adds a loop guard to the reviewer PreToolUse hook (claude-code review sessions only). Two independent rules, because the verified transcripts show two distinct degeneration shapes:

- **Probe stream** — 5 consecutive no-op Bash probes: `true`, `:`, or bare `echo`/`printf` with no operator, pipe, or redirect. The commands differ on every call (`echo marker-1`, `echo marker-2`, ...), so this rule keys on the no-op shape, not on identical input.
- **Identical repeats** — 5 consecutive calls with the same tool and the same canonical input (Bash compares the whitespace-collapsed command; other tools compare the compacted `tool_input`, so `Read` repeats with the same offset/limit trip it while offset paging does not).

On a trigger the hook answers `permissionDecision: deny` with a corrective message ("Emit the real tool call you already planned, or state in text what is blocking it"). A denial surfaces as model feedback, which reliably breaks the pattern. Counters live in a per-reviewer state file under `AO_DATA_DIR` (each hook invocation is a separate process) and reset at turn boundaries (`stop`, `user-prompt-submit`) and after every denial — legitimate consecutive repeats (`git rebase --continue` retries, `pnpm test` reruns after edits) are untouched.

The guard is scoped to review sessions (`AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID` path in `ao hooks`); worker sessions are unaffected.

## Transcript evidence (issue verification)

The 8 hung reviewer sessions from the issue thread were scanned with a streaming parser (model `glm-5.3-flash`, thinking enabled in all of them). Review targets are anonymized to letters — they are private projects; session-id prefixes are kept so the report can be matched against local transcripts:

| Session | Target | Loops | Breakdown |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0779a2bc` | project A | yes — probe streams | 5 series: **81 + 33 + 24 + 20 + 18** calls over 44 min (03:14–03:58 local, transcript timestamps), ~26M input tokens as recorded in `usage`. The intended action (a `Write` of the review JSON) is already composed in thinking/text immediately before each series. 3 series broken by human interrupt, 2 by the model's own text / a budget hook |
| `c45fff1e` | project B | yes — identical repeats | 34–36 consecutive `Read <reviewed-file> [offset=281 limit=9]` (2 series, ~2.2M input tokens), broken by the model's own text |
| `c8e8f202` | project A | no series ≥ 4 | longest identical streak 5: `git rebase --continue` retries with changing non-empty results — legitimate |
| `5e614574` | project B | no series ≥ 4 | max identical streak ≤ 2 |
| `910f9cf4` | project C | no series ≥ 4 | max identical streak ≤ 2 |
| `c0845281` | project D | no series ≥ 4 | max identical streak ≤ 2 |
| `6bcb55d0`, `7190e096` | project E | no series ≥ 4 | max identical streak ≤ 2 |

Facts that shaped the fix (diverging from the issue's assumptions, worth noting):

- Probe-stream series emit a **fresh command every call** — an "identical calls" rule alone misses 176 of the observed calls; hence two rules.
- Probe results are **non-empty** (`echo ok` → `ok`), so denying empty-output commands or `true`/`:` alone misses most of the drift; the guard keys on repetition shape.
- Thinking was **enabled** in the looping sessions — the pathology is not correlated with thinking-disabled here.
- Burn figures quoted in the issue don't match the `usage` sums recorded in the transcripts (e.g. `0779a2bc`: 46.1M recorded vs 35.2M reported; `c8e8f202`: 36.1M vs 13.4M). The table above states the measurement method instead.

## Test plan

New tests in `backend/internal/cli/reviewloopguard_test.go`:

- regression: synthetic hook-payload series reproducing both observed patterns (probe storm with varying markers; identical `Read` repeats) — the 5th call is denied with the corrective message, the 6th is not (post-denial reset);
- legitimate shapes stay un-denied: real work between probes, offset paging, `printf | ao review submit` shapes, chained/piped commands;
- state resilience: corrupt state file starts fresh; turn-boundary reset verified end-to-end through `ao hooks claude-code pre-tool-use` / `stop`.

The synthetic payloads are the wire form of the transcript's `tool_use` blocks (what `ao hooks claude-code pre-tool-use` receives for exactly those calls), which is why the regression uses hook payloads rather than replaying jsonl.

Local gates: `gofmt -l .` clean on the whole backend, `go build ./...` ok, full `go test ./internal/cli/` — single failure `TestSpawnResolvesProjectFromCWD`, caused by this machine's `AO_SESSION_ID` leaking into the spawn test's project resolution (environment-only; CI runners don't set it, and the test is untouched by this diff).

title: fix: present session teardown as archive, not delete
body:
Code changes: +150 -113  
Tests: +128 -73  
Others: +120 -128 (UI copy, 8 locale catalogs)

Fixes #5768 

The control that archives a session carried a `Trash2` icon and red danger styling on every surface, so it read as a permanent delete — hiding both what the action does and that an Archive section exists to restore from. The sidebar row also archived on the bare click while the session page asked first, and that prompt was an inline popover rather than the shared modal.

## Changes

**1. Archive icon instead of the trash icon**

`Trash2` → lucide `Archive` on the sidebar session row and the session-page top bar (the two surfaces the issue names), plus the board card and inspector, which drive the same action.

The danger-red treatment went with it (`variant="killIcon"` → `"icon"`; `hover:bg-error/10 hover:text-error` → neutral). A permanently-red control signals "delete" as loudly as the icon did, and the board's own `ArchiveRestoreButton` already uses exactly this neutral treatment.

The **"Remove project"** trash icons are untouched — that one really does delete.

Labels followed the icon: "Kill session" / "Terminate session" now read "Archive session" across all 8 locale catalogs. That is what tells users the Archive section exists and that their work is recoverable.

**2. The sidebar confirms before archiving**

`SessionActions` called `terminateSession()` straight off the click. It now opens the same confirm every other surface uses.

**3. The popover is now the shared modal**

`SessionTerminationPopover` → `SessionArchiveDialog`, built on the existing `ConfirmDialog` (the settings / new-task modal frame):

- title "Are you sure you want to archive …?"
- subtext "You can always restore … from the Archive section later."
- buttons **Confirm** and **No**

`ConfirmDialog` gains optional `cancelLabel` and `confirmAriaLabel` props, both defaulting to today's behavior.

One deliberate deviation from the issue text: the title names the session ("…archive fix login?") when it has one, rather than the literal "the session". The old prompt already did this and it is more informative — easy to change if you would rather match the issue exactly.

**4. Focus goes back to whatever opened the confirm**

Radix's `Dialog.Content` returns focus on close to a `DialogTrigger`, but these confirms are opened programmatically, so dismissing one dropped keyboard users on `<body>`. The old popover wrapped its trigger in `PopoverTrigger`, so Radix knew where to go back to; moving to the modal lost that. `ConfirmDialog` now remembers what had focus when it opened and restores it, falling back to Radix when that element is gone (a confirmed archive removes its own row). This also fixes the existing remove-project confirm, which is opened the same way.

**5. Keys and names follow the copy** (review follow-up, `1d3516932`)

The retitled strings kept their kill/terminate keys, so `en.json` read `"shell.killSession": "Archive session"`. The 16 affected keys are renamed in all 8 catalogs: `termination.*` → `archive.*`, `shell.kill*` / `shell.terminate*` → `shell.archive*` / `shell.archiving*`, `inspector.terminate*` → `inspector.archive*`. `shell.killSession` and `shell.terminateSession` had identical copy in every locale, so they are one `shell.archiveSession` now. `TopbarKillButton` is `TopbarArchiveButton`. No copy changes.

The daemon route `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/kill` and the hooks and callbacks that wrap it keep their names on purpose: the CLI, mobile app, and cloud agent call the same route, so renaming it is an API change, not part of this fix.

## A real bug caught while testing

React portals re-dispatch synthetic events up the **React** tree, not the DOM tree. Confirming from inside a board card therefore also fired that card's `onClick` and opened the very session being archived. The old popover guarded against this with its own `stopPropagation`; `ConfirmDialog` now does the same on both content and overlay. An existing board test caught it.

## Verification

Ran the `frontend.yml` jobs locally on the rebased branch (macOS, Node 23.6.1; CI pins Node 24):

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean.
- Full `npx vitest run`: 332 of 333 files pass (5262 tests passed, 6 skipped, 1 failed). The one failure is `src/main/browser-history-store.test.ts` hitting its 20s timeout under full-suite load. It's a main-process test, and this PR touches nothing under `frontend/src/main`. Every test file this PR touches passes with nothing skipped, including the new Sidebar test that nothing is archived before the confirm is accepted.
- `packages/cloud-client` and `packages/product-ui` verify steps, and the `mac-update-helper` node tests: pass.

Not run locally, so CI should be the judge:

- **Renderer smoke (`test:e2e:renderer`).** This machine doesn't have the Chromium build Playwright 1.60.0 pins, so no spec launched.
- **The docs install/build step, the `mac-update-helper` compile and state tests, and gitleaks.**

After review, on `1d3516932` (same machine and Node):

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean. Full `npx vitest run`: 332 of 333 files pass; the one failure is the same `browser-history-store.test.ts` timeout under load, and it passes on its own (3/3).
- **Real desktop app.** Ran the branch as an isolated Electron dev instance with throwaway sessions and opened the confirm from the sidebar row, top bar, board card, and inspector, in light and dark. The copy renders from the renamed keys, No and Escape return focus to the control that opened the dialog, and confirming from a board card archives the session without opening it.

title: fix(kiro): read whoami's JSON so auth status stops reporting unknown
body:
Fixes #5048 · Refs #5843

## The bug

`kiro-cli whoami --format json` answers in JSON, but the probe classified it with `authprobe.StatusFromText`, which looks for English phrases like "not logged in". Neither state contains one, so **both** reported `unknown` — the probe could never tell signed in from signed out, and `ao agent ls` could never show Kiro's real status.

Measured against the installed `kiro-cli 2.21.0` on macOS, with an isolated `HOME` and a stubbed browser opener (no account touched, no browser opened):

```
signed out:  {"account":null}                             exit 1
signed in:   {"accountType":…,"email":…,"startUrl":…}     exit 0
             followed by a plain-text "Profile:" block
```

The trailer is why the signed-in payload is not valid JSON as a whole — the half @nikhilachale documented in #5048.

## The fix

**A null account is a CLI saying "nobody is signed in" in JSON**, so `authprobe` learns it alongside the `"loggedin":false` / `"authenticated":false` patterns it already reads. Generic, and it sits with its peers.

**The signed-in shape is Kiro's own**, so the adapter decodes the leading JSON value — which also skips the trailer — and `authprobe` grows an optional per-adapter classifier (`CLIStatusWithClassifier`) so it can. Existing callers are untouched; `CLIStatus` and `CLIStatusWithTimeout` keep their signatures.

Anything unrecognized still falls back to the shared classifier and still answers `unknown`. Nothing asserts a state it cannot read.

## It also fixes how #5843's gate fires

[#5843](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5843) skips Kiro model discovery while signed out, which is the right behavior — but the payload read as `unknown`, so the skip only happened via the fail-closed `err != nil` branch, i.e. **because the CLI exits 1, not because anything recognized the signed-out state**. Two consequences:

- The skip is recorded as an ordinary discovery failure, spending retry budget rather than taking the clean sign-in-required path that preserves the cached catalog.
- If Kiro ever exits 0 while signed out, the gate silently stops firing and the browser sign-in from #5307 returns, with no test catching it.

With the classifier fixed, the gate recognizes the payload directly. `TestKiroSignInGateRecognizesTheSignedOutPayload` pins that; on `main` it fails with:

```
err = kiro sign-in check failed: exit status 1,
want a recognized ErrAgentModelDiscoverySignInRequired
```

## Tests

All new tests fail on `main` with the reported symptom:

```
--- FAIL: TestStatusFromTextReadsANullAccountAsSignedOut
        StatusFromText("{\"account\":null}") = "unknown", want unauthorized
--- FAIL: TestKiroWhoamiAuthStatus/signed_in
        status = "unknown", want "authorized"
--- FAIL: TestKiroWhoamiAuthStatus/signed_out
        status = "unknown", want "unauthorized"
```

They use the verbatim payloads above. `TestKiroWhoamiIgnoresExitCode` pins that status comes from reading output rather than the exit code, since the two states differ on both. Negative cases cover unrecognized JSON, non-JSON, and blank identity fields — all must stay `unknown`.

`go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, `golangci-lint` **0 issues**, and `adapters/agent/...`, `service/agent/...`, `ports/...` all pass.

## Scope

Two source files, 76 lines. No interface changes, no behavior change for any other adapter — `authprobe`'s new pattern only fires on output containing a null `account`, and the classifier hook is opt-in per call site.

Supersedes my [PR #5321](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5321), which #5843 made redundant; this is the one piece of it that still had independent value.

title: fix(desktop): hide the session actions menu for harnesses without Chat UI
body:
Code changes: +19 -4  
Tests: +44 -2  
Others: +0 -0

## What
Hide the session tab's ⋮ (Session actions) for harnesses that don't support Chat UI. Harnesses with Chat keep it unchanged.

## Why
For harnesses without a Chat driver (goose, aider, amp, and so on), clicking the ⋮ opened an empty dropdown that showed up as a bare pill under the tab.

This regressed in #4572. `SessionActionsMenu` hides itself only when it receives no items, but `SessionView` always passes a `TerminalSwitchAgentButton` element. That element renders nothing outside Claude Code and Codex, and the Chat/Terminal item is already hidden for `CHAT_UNSUPPORTED`, so the menu opened with zero items.

## How
- A session now counts as unable to switch into Chat when either:
  - its interface status reports `CHAT_UNSUPPORTED`, or
  - the daemon's `chatHarnesses` list (`/api/v1/settings`) doesn't include its harness.
- The list is known before the per-session status loads, so the ⋮ doesn't flash in and out on first open. It also covers terminated sessions, whose status only reports `SESSION_TERMINATED`. If the list is empty (settings still loading), the status decides.
- In that case `SessionView` passes no tab action at all, so the tab drops the ⋮ and the space reserved for it. No action is lost: agent switching is limited to Claude Code and Codex, and both have Chat.

## Testing
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: passed.
- `SessionView.test.tsx`:
  - Four cases fail without the fix and pass with it: the updated `CHAT_UNSUPPORTED` cases (worker and orchestrator) and the new harness-outside-the-Chat-list cases (before status loads, and once terminated).
  - A new case checks that a Chat-capable harness keeps the ⋮ with "Switch to chat UI".
- Full `npx vitest run`: 331 of 333 files passed, including all renderer tests. The 2 failing files are local-environment failures in files this diff doesn't touch:

title: fix(cloud): prefer the GitHub App grant over a stored PAT for worker checkout and push
body:
## Summary

Worker git checkout and push preferred a stored GitHub PAT over the GitHub App installation, unconditionally. Because a PAT's `validation_state` is a cached snapshot, a PAT that was valid when saved but has since expired or been revoked was still used, and GitHub rejected it with **"Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported"**, failing the clone of the primary repo and every extra repo in a multi-repo checkout, even when the App installation could mint fresh, working tokens.

This flips the preference: **use the freshly-minted GitHub App installation grant when available; fall back to a stored PAT only when the App path cannot serve the project** (no installation, not App-connected, or the mint fails). A rotted PAT can no longer shadow a healthy App installation.

## Root cause (verified against prod)

- Failing session's project was App-connected (`github_repository_id` set), in an org whose App installation is **all-repos** and grants the repo.
- The session creator had a `github`/`default` PAT with `validation_state='valid'` (a cached snapshot from days earlier).
- `workerCheckoutGrant` tries the PAT first, so it used that stale PAT; GitHub rejected it for every repo in the checkout.
- Confirmed live: the App installation mints tokens for both the primary and the extra repo (HTTP 201 each) - so the App path would have cloned everything.

## Scope

- `workerCheckoutGrant` and `workerPushGrant` are flipped to App-first with PAT fallback.
- Deployments without App credentials (e.g. staging's REST-only broker) keep working: the App mint fails there and the handler falls back to the PAT.
- `workerRaisePullRequest` is intentionally left PAT-first: some deployments run a write-incapable broker that cannot create PRs, so PR-raise must keep preferring the PAT.

## Tests

- New `worker_checkout_grant_test.go`: App grant preferred over an existing PAT (the regression), PAT fallback when the App path is unavailable, and 403 when neither is available.
- Existing PAT/PR tests unchanged and passing.
- `go build ./... && go vet && go test -race ./internal/httpapi ./internal/githubapp` all green.
