title: feat(desktop): add browser login for Cursor provider credentials
body:
Code changes: +120 -12
Tests: +172 -0
Others: +241 -1

## What

Adds **"Log in with Cursor"** to the desktop provider-credential dialog, and fixes the control-plane validator that rejected the resulting key for free-plan accounts.

## Why

Repro on `main` (free-plan Cursor account):

```
AO Cloud could not save the provider credential
(HTTP 422, code invalid_credential, request 66fabb20-13a3-4b66-b225-948997ed50c8):
coding-agent credential is invalid or expired
```

The browser login had succeeded and Cursor had minted a working key. The credential was never invalid.

Cursor's actual contract, measured live with a freshly minted key (`crsr_…`, 69 chars) against `api.cursor.com/v1/me`:

| credential | status | body |
|---|---|---|
| missing / empty / malformed / garbage | **401** | `Invalid User API Key` |
| valid key, **free plan** | **403** | `{"error":{"code":"plan_required"}}` |
| valid key, Pro plan | **200** | user payload |

`validateBearerEndpoint` collapsed 401 and 403 into a single `errInvalidAgentCredential`, so a valid free-plan key was reported as *"invalid or expired"*.

Two hypotheses were tested and ruled out first:

- **Extra headers.** Cursor's SDK sends `x-cursor-client-type`, `x-cursor-client-version` and `x-ghost-mode` alongside `Authorization`. Replaying `/v1/me` bare, with the client headers, with ghost mode only, and with all three returned the identical 403 — headers are not the cause.
- **A different probe endpoint.** All four `api.cursor.com/v1/*` routes the SDK uses (`/v1/me`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/repositories`, `/v1/agents`) return the same 403. There is no ungated alternative.

This matters because AO's cursor runtime is the **local `cursor-agent` CLI** (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/cursor.go:91`), not the Pro-gated Cloud Agent API that `/v1/me` belongs to. The credential is genuinely usable; rejecting it was wrong.

## Changes

**Desktop (15 files)**

- `provider-auth-flow.ts` — new `cursorAuthFlow` calls `Cursor.auth.login()` from `@cursor/sdk` (`store: null`, nothing persisted client-side), opens the sign-in through `shell.openExternal`, 5-minute abort, and returns `credentialType: "api_key"` for the existing save route. Codex/Claude/GitHub flows and `findCodexAuthFile` are untouched; the previously-added `isAllowedAppExternalURL` / `extractCursorAuthURL` interception was dropped as dead code.
- `cloud-auth.ts` — `providerCredentialSaveFailure` surfaces the control-plane envelope (`HTTP <status>, code <code>, request <id>`, plus `message`/`error`) instead of a bare `request failed`, which is what made this bug diagnosable.
- `CloudCredentialDialog.tsx` — `LOGIN_COPY` map for per-provider copy; `disabled={busy || credentialOptions.length === 1}` (cursor gaining a second credential option made the old literal-union comparison a `TS2367`).
- 8 locales — `cloudCredential.cursorLoginDescription`, `cloudCredential.loginWithCursor`.
- Packaging — `@cursor/sdk` is **externalized** (not bundled), following the `better-sqlite3` precedent: `vite.main.config.ts` `rollupOptions.external`, plus the `PACKAGED_EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES` allowlist and a `packageAfterPrune` guard that fails the build if `node_modules/@cursor/sdk/package.json` is missing from the packaged app. Login does **not** need the optional `@cursor/sdk-win32-x64`-style platform packages — verified by renaming them away and re-requiring.

**Cloud (2 files)**

- `agent_credential_validator.go` — `validateBearerEndpoint` gains one `accepted func(status int, body []byte) bool` parameter and keeps the body (previously discarded). No new packages, types or interfaces; 3 call sites.
  - `cursorBearerAccepted` — 200 / 429 / **403 carrying `plan_required`** → valid.
  - `defaultBearerAccepted` — OpenAI and GitHub keep the previous 401/403 rejection, unchanged.

## Verification

Run locally on this branch:

- `cd cloud && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race -count=1 ./internal/httpapi/...` → **pass**
- `npm run frontend:typecheck` → **pass**
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck:e2e` → **pass**
- `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/main/cloud-auth.test.ts` → **14/14 pass**
- Full `cloud go test ./...` was compared against a clean-tree baseline with these changes stashed: the failure set is byte-identical (`sh` missing, CRLF, mode/permission and workspace tests, all Windows-only). None of the failing packages import `internal/httpapi`.
- Full `frontend` vitest suite has 173 pre-existing failures on this Windows box, measured identically on a stashed clean tree — zero attributable to this branch.
- Live API probes against `api.cursor.com` produced the status table above.

## Gaps to verify in CI (not run locally)

- `renderer-smoke` and `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --all` — require Docker; the daemon is not running on this machine.
- `go.yml` / `frontend.yml` ubuntu-only jobs (`go test -race ./...` full backend, ubuntu vitest) — cannot be reproduced on Windows.
- `golangci-lint` — CI's lint job runs with `working-directory: backend`, so cloud is not linted; `backend` is untouched here. The repo-level `npm run lint` wrapper never completed on Windows (its `go test ./...` short-circuits on the known Windows-only failures).

## Maintainer follow-up

**The cloud half cannot be tested end-to-end until the control plane is rebuilt or redeployed** — the 422 comes from the control plane, not the desktop app. Please deploy and then run through the steps below.

## Risks / accepted trade-offs

- `@cursor/sdk` declares `"engines": {"node": ">=22.13"}` but Electron 33.4.11 embeds **Node v20.18.3**. Empirically the module loads and `Cursor.auth.login` is a function under `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, but this is unsupported territory — please exercise the packaged app, not just `npm run dev`.
- Each login mints a **new 90-day API key** that stays visible in the user's Cursor dashboard until revoked (the SDK mints rather than reuses). Consider whether AO should revoke or reuse on repeat logins.
- The validator reads the response body for the `plan_required` sentinel. If Cursor renames that code, free-plan users regress to today's behaviour (rejected) rather than silently accepting a bad key — the regression test pins this.
- Alternative considered and rejected: accepting any 403 for cursor without reading the body. Looser, and the sentinel is cheap to check.

## Testing steps

1. Use a Cursor account on the **free** plan.
2. Rebuild/redeploy the control plane so `cloud/` picks up the validator change.
3. In the desktop app: **Settings → Connect provider → Cursor → "Log in with Cursor"**.
4. Complete the browser sign-in; the dialog should return to the credential form with the credential saved, no 422.
5. Negative check: paste a garbage key as **API key** → expect `invalid_credential`, not acceptance.
6. Confirm `@cursor/sdk` and its 13 runtime dependencies ship in the packaged app (`node_modules/@cursor/sdk/package.json` present after `packageAfterPrune`).

title: bug(browser): in-app Browser blocks PDF viewer navigation
body:
## Report

A user reported that the in-app Browser tab is not able to open PDF files. Expected: a PDF preview target (for example a workspace `report.pdf` opened via `ao preview`) or an HTTP(S) PDF URL should render in the AO Browser panel, or at minimum show a clear supported fallback. Actual: PDFs fail to open/render in the in-app browser.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected from checkout `4bbb00b32` on 2026-09-25.

- Duplicate search: `gh issue list --repo Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator --state all --search 'pdf'`, `... --search '"Unsupported browser URL" PDF OR pdf'`, and `... --search 'chrome-extension browser Unsupported browser URL'` found only #3436 (bare filename handling), not an existing exact PDF-rendering issue.
- The daemon preview path appears to support PDFs correctly:
  - `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:1959-1974` resolves workspace-local preview targets to the confined preview origin.
  - `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go:544-547` serves non-Markdown files with `http.ServeContent`.
  - `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions_test.go:1892-1943` explicitly covers `artifacts/report.pdf` and expects `Content-Type: application/pdf` from the preview origin.
- The desktop Browser host then loads the preview URL through `WebContentsView.loadURL` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:1523-1534`) and hardens all page-driven navigation/redirects with `blockUnsafeNavigation` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:2860-2890`).
- That hardening currently allows only `http:` and `https:` (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:506-519`) and treats anything else as unsupported (`frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts:524-530`, `2877-2882`).
- Chromium's built-in PDF viewer is implemented as an internal extension page. Chromium's own PDF extension tests assert the viewer extension URL `chrome-extension://mhjfbmdgcfjbbpaeojofohoefgiehjai/index.html` when a PDF is loaded: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/pdf/pdf_extension_test.cc

## RCA

The likely failing layer is the Electron Browser hardening, not the daemon static-file preview. AO serves PDFs as `application/pdf`, but Chromium hands PDF display to its internal `chrome-extension://.../index.html` viewer. AO's `will-navigate` / `will-redirect` guard runs `isAllowedBrowserURL()` against that internal viewer URL, rejects the `chrome-extension:` scheme, calls `preventDefault()`, and reports `Unsupported browser URL`. That would prevent the built-in PDF viewer from taking over the tab, so the PDF cannot render even though the original preview URL was valid HTTP(S).

This is distinct from #3436: #3436 is about bare filenames being misclassified before a preview URL exists; here the preview URL can be valid and the failure occurs during the browser's internal PDF-viewer navigation.

## Suggested fix direction

Keep direct user navigation limited to safe HTTP(S) targets, but handle PDFs without blocking Chromium's viewer handoff. Possible approaches:

1. Safely special-case Chromium's internal PDF viewer navigation/redirect after a valid HTTP(S) PDF response, rather than allowing arbitrary privileged schemes from the address bar or page content.
2. Or avoid Chromium's internal extension by routing PDFs through an AO-owned/PDF.js viewer served from the confined preview origin.
3. Add a regression test that simulates a PDF load followed by `will-navigate`/`will-redirect` to the Chromium PDF viewer extension and asserts the browser does not surface `Unsupported browser URL` for that trusted path.

## Verification gap

I did not run the full Electron app in this pass; the RCA is based on the current daemon/desktop code path and Chromium's documented/source-tested PDF viewer behavior. A fix PR should confirm with a real Electron Browser panel using `ao preview <workspace-pdf>`.

title: bug(browser): remember last selected browser profile for new sessions
body:
## Report

The in-app Browser does not remember the last selected browser profile across sessions. Right now, users have to open the Browser profiles tab/menu in each new Browser/session and choose the last-used profile again and again. Expected: AO should persist the user's last-used browser profile so new Browser sessions start with that profile automatically, unless the user explicitly chooses another profile.

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected from checkout `4bbb00b32` on 2026-09-25.

- Duplicate search: `gh issue list --repo Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator --state all --search 'browser profile persist session last used profile'` and `... --search 'browser profiles selected profile session persist'` did not find an existing matching issue.
- Current desktop profile storage appears to persist profile bindings by worker/session ID:
  - `frontend/src/main/browser-profile-store.ts` has `getSessionProfileId(sessionId)` and `bindSession(sessionId, profileId)`.
  - `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts` initializes a Browser session from `browserProfileStore.getSessionProfileId(sessionId)`.
  - `switchProfile(...)` writes the selected profile back with `store.bindSession(session.sessionId, normalizedRequestedProfileId)`.
- This explains the reported UX: selecting a profile can be retained for that specific worker/session ID, but a new AO session with a new session ID has no binding and starts temporary/unprofiled, forcing users to manually select the same profile again.

## Suggested direction

Add a durable default/last-used Browser profile preference that applies to newly created Browser sessions. Keep per-session bindings for explicit overrides, but when no binding exists for a new session, initialize from the stored last-used/default profile. Update that preference when the user selects a profile, and consider how selecting the temporary profile should behave.

title: feat(cloud): add two-way Chat and Terminal UI switching
body:
Code changes: +6946 -365  
Tests: +5327 -15  
Others: +698 -13  

## Summary

Add two-way Chat ↔ Terminal UI switching for Cloud sessions. Cloud Chat uses the existing `ChatWorkspace` presentation, while the Cloud worker and control plane coordinate which agent controller owns the conversation. The implementation carries the provider's native conversation identity across the handoff, retains terminal history, and exposes model and reasoning-effort controls in Chat.

This work is an adapted port of [vanshx999's PR #4683](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4683). The Cloud interface-transition design, worker handoff, and initial Chat integration originate from that work. This branch selects that feature slice, integrates it with the newer `main`, and includes subsequent fixes and tests. It should not be presented as an independently invented implementation.

## How the current switch works

The session has one committed interface, `tui` or `chat`. A switch request creates a durable transition. The coordinator checks the current controller, waits for work to finish or requires explicit interruption, stops that controller, and starts the other using the same native conversation identity. Accepted prompts are held while ownership is uncertain and released when a usable controller is confirmed. A failed handoff retains recovery state instead of silently displaying a ready interface.

**This is a controller handoff, not yet the proposed view-only switch.** Switching currently exits one agent controller and starts the other. The later idea of retaining one TUI process and changing only its presentation is not implemented in this PR.

## File responsibilities

| Area | Files | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud startup and configuration | `cloud/.env.example`, `cloud/cmd/ao-cloud/main.go`, `cloud/internal/config/config.go` | Configure and start the interface-handoff reconciler. |
| Worker startup | `cloud/cmd/ao-worker/main.go`, `cloud/cmd/ao-cloud-agent/main.go`, `cloud/cmd/ao-cloud-agent/codex_transcript.go` | Start the appropriate worker controller and recover provider conversation information. |
| State vocabulary | `cloud/internal/domain/session_interface.go`, `cloud/internal/domain/types.go`, `cloud/internal/domain/sandbox.go`, `cloud/internal/interfacehandoff/interfacehandoff.go` | Define interface modes, transition states, and the Cloud-specific handoff rules. |
| Transition API | `cloud/internal/httpapi/session_interface_transition_handlers.go`, `server.go`, `resource_handlers.go` | Accept, read, cancel, and acknowledge interface transitions; register the routes and store boundary. |
| Chat and terminal API | `cloud/internal/httpapi/event_handlers.go`, `terminal_handlers.go`, `worker_handlers.go`, `worker_session_handler.go`, `worker_transport_handlers.go`, `workspace_review_handlers.go` | Serve Chat events/messages and model choices, and keep terminal and worker requests aligned with the committed interface. |
| Handoff coordinator | `cloud/internal/interfacereconcile/coordinator.go`, `transport_driver.go` | Drive durable stop/start/recovery phases and dispatch the worker operations. |
| Persistence | `cloud/internal/postgres/session_interface_transition_store.go`, `worker_transport_store.go`, `worker_turn_store.go`, `worker_session_store.go`, `event_store.go` | Persist transition ownership, held prompts, terminal state, turns, and conversation events. |
| Related persistence | `cloud/internal/postgres/auth_store.go`, `orchestrator_store.go`, `project_session_store.go`, `sandbox_store.go`, `cloud/internal/reconcile/reconciler.go` | Enforce transition constraints and keep session, sandbox, and reconciliation reads consistent. |
| Migrations | `cloud/internal/postgres/migrations/00051_session_interface_transitions.sql`, `00052_interface_transition_worker_requests.sql`, `00053_chat_model_worker_requests.sql`, `00054_chat_steer_worker_requests.sql` | Add durable transitions and worker requests for handoff, model selection, and chat steering. |
| Worker execution | `cloud/internal/worker/protocol.go`, `activity.go`, `tui_stop.go`, `cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go`, `models.go`, `chat_output.go`, `supervisor.go` | Carry protocol data, determine TUI idleness, build provider commands, discover models, and project headless output into Chat. |
| Worker terminal transport | `cloud/internal/workertransport/interface.go`, `stream.go`, `supervisor.go` | Execute interface commands, fence terminal input during handoff, and reopen the terminal after Chat. |
| API contract and client | `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, `packages/cloud-client/src/client.ts`, `types.ts`, generated `schema.ts` | Describe and type the transition, Chat message, and model APIs. |
| Chat renderer | `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/CloudSessionChatSurface.tsx`, `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionInterfaceSwitch.tsx` | Project durable Cloud events into the shared Chat UI and display the two-way switch. |
| Session renderer | `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`, `CenterPane.tsx`, `ShellTopbar.tsx`, `TerminalPane.tsx` | Select Chat or terminal presentation and keep the switch and terminal attachment available. |
| Renderer data and routing | `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionInterfaceTransition.ts`, `useAgentSwitches.ts`, `useWorkspaceQuery.ts`, `frontend/src/renderer/lib/cloud-cp/client.ts`, `types.ts`, `cloud-session.ts`, both Cloud session routes | Resolve Cloud sessions through the control plane, call the correct transition API, and refresh the displayed state. |
| Fixture | `frontend/src/renderer/lib/mock-data.ts` | Supply the interface mode in demo session data. |

The remaining **36 changed test files** cover the coordinator, worker and terminal behavior, persistence and HTTP boundaries, typed clients, and renderer switching.

## Comparison with PR #4683

I compared this branch with the locally fetched `vanshx999/fix/cloud-interface-transition-monorepo` snapshot (dated 24 September 2026). That snapshot changed 102 files against its base; this branch changes 118 files against current `main`. Those totals are **not a direct reduction metric**, because the bases differ.

- **Retained from #4683:** durable two-way handoff, Cloud Chat rendering through `ChatWorkspace`, worker-owned controller transitions, native conversation continuity, event projection, recovery handling, and model/effort support.
- **Adapted for current `main`:** Cloud migrations use the current sequence (`00051`–`00054`) rather than copying the source branch's older migration numbers. The transition state table is Cloud-scoped; this branch does not add the source PR's backend interface-handoff package as a new `main` change.
- **Further fixes in this branch:** TUI idle proof before stopping, terminal-ticket and scrollback continuity when returning from Chat, protection against input during handoff, prompt fencing during recovery, Cloud session lookup that does not fall back to the local daemon, and typed-client coverage for Chat models and message settings. Review follow-up also fixed migration ordering, message admission during transition creation, claimed Chat turns during interruption, and coordinator work after a lost lease.
- **Left out of this branch's diff:** the source snapshot also changes workflow, Docker/dependency files, and broader credential, workspace, sidebar, and task-composer surfaces. Those are not part of this selected Cloud Chat feature delta against current `main`.

## Verification

The formatting fix remains a standalone commit (`4a4470605`) and can be squashed with `d4dd5f5` when the PR merges.

At `93b09b8c2`, Cloud race tests passed (643 tests in 31 packages). Cloud build, vet, formatting, and the focused PostgreSQL interrupt and drain test passed. Frontend typecheck and 332 focused renderer tests passed. The Cloud client typecheck and its 24 tests passed.

At `3f8d62d7c`, Cloud build, vet, formatting, and the race-enabled Go suite passed locally (646 tests in 31 packages). With PostgreSQL, the upgrade from migration `00050` to `00054` and the concurrent message admission test passed. The admission test fails on the old code and passes with the fix.

At `70eff5426`, the Cloud race suite passed (650 tests in 31 packages). Cloud build, vet, and formatting passed. The new full-path tests checked both directions: a busy TUI process exited before Chat started, and a claimed Chat turn stopped before TUI started. Cloud client typecheck, build, and all 26 tests passed. Frontend typecheck and `npm run cloud:check` passed.

At `a2847f02f`, the Cloud race suite passed (652 tests in 31 packages). Cloud build, vet, formatting, and diff checks passed. The busy TUI test now checks that the source process has exited when the Chat start command is sent. Cloud client typecheck and all 26 tests passed locally.

At `77036fbfe`, Cloud workerexec passed 106 race-enabled tests, vet passed, frontend typecheck passed, and gofmt found no changes. New ACP tests cover Claude modes, Cursor launch flags, permission decisions, and cancellation. The cancellation test failed before the fix and passed after it.

A full PostgreSQL-enabled run on `3f8d62d7c` passed 678 tests and failed `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`. The same test failed on the untouched `4a4470605` head with a fresh database. All 10 GitHub Actions checks passed on `70eff5426`. No deployment or release publish was run.

title: bug(standalone): Switch agent dialog shows project-ID validation error
body:
## User report

Opening **Switch agent** from a standalone session displays the red error `Project id failed storage-path validation`.

The agent switch itself still completes successfully. The dialog should not show a project-validation error for a supported standalone session.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a standalone agent session.
2. Open **Switch agent** from that session.
3. Observe the validation error above the agent and model controls.

## Agent-collected evidence

- Collected 2026-09-26 on macOS in the real Electron app with isolated AO data.
- Build under test: PR #5849 at `fe899699711de4583f6e61193afa30d00b400af2`.
- DevTools recorded `GET /api/v1/projects/__standalone__` returning HTTP 400:

  ```json
  {
    "error": "bad_request",
    "code": "INVALID_PROJECT_ID",
    "message": "Project id failed storage-path validation"
  }
  ```

title: feat(review): daemon-owned GitHub publication with a single submit contract
body:
Fixes #5701

## What

A reviewer now records its review with exactly **one** `ao review submit` call, and the **daemon** publishes the single GitHub COMMENT review. Reviewers lose direct GitHub publication access entirely.

- **CLI**: the full Markdown body is piped from stdin (`--body -`); inline findings are repeated `--comment-path`/`--comment-line`/`--comment-body` trios paired by occurrence. Incomplete groups, blank/multi-line finding bodies, zero lines, legacy `--reviews` batches, file-path `--body`, and caller-supplied `--review-id` all fail with clear errors. Identical resubmission returns the recorded result instead of duplicating.
- **Daemon**: new `ports.SCMReviewPublisher` (GitHub adapter posts `pulls/{n}/reviews` with `event=COMMENT`, commit anchor, inline comments; multi provider delegates). The run row persists `findings` + a `publish_state` machine (`pending → publishing → published | failed | uncertain`, migration 0156) **before** the external call. A `publishing` state that survives a daemon restart resolves to `uncertain` and is never blindly reposted; `failed` retries on resubmission; concurrent submissions serialize. Obsolete inputs get `422 REVIEW_INPUT_OBSOLETE`.
- **Reviewer sandboxes**: claudecode, opencode, kilocode, kimchi, kiro, and copilot adapters drop `gh api` from their allowlists and keep only read-only `gh pr view/diff/checks`. Prompts teach the new single-command contract with no publication step.

## Why (evidence)

The old contract asked the reviewer to compose the full review as one-line JSON inside a shell single-quoted `printf`, twice (once for `gh api`, once for `ao review submit --reviews -`), then carry the GitHub review id back. The measurements from the closed #5863 investigation thread stay valid for #5701:

- Session `0779a2bc`: 81+33+24+20+18 = **176 consecutive no-op probe calls over 44 minutes (~26M input tokens)** — the intended review-write was already composed in thinking immediately before each series; the model could not bring itself to emit the fragile giant call.
- Session `c45fff1e`: 34–36 identical `Read` repeats (~2.2M tokens).

Reproduced the old contract failing on quote-bearing markdown (the shape every real review has):

```
$ printf '%s' '{ "event": "COMMENT", "body": "The message "user's home not found" is wrong",
"comments": [ { "path": "handler.go", "line": 12, "body": "don't call os.Getenv" } ] }' | jq -c .
{ "event": "COMMENT", "body": "The message "usershomenotfound is wrong,/tmp/...: comments:: command not found
```

The unescaped apostrophe corrupts the shell string before `gh api` ever runs, and literal newlines inside the mandated one-line JSON fail JSON parsing (`Invalid string: control characters … must be escaped`). Three escaping layers (shell + JSON + one-line) is the root cause the hook guard in #5863 could only observe, not remove.

**After**: the same document — quotes, apostrophes, fenced code block — goes through `ao review submit … --body -` via stdin verbatim, with zero escaping anywhere:

```
$ ao review submit --session … --run … --verdict changes_requested --body - \
    --comment-path handler.go --comment-line 12 --comment-body "guard err before dereferencing" < review-body.md
review: not found: review run "demo-run" (REVIEW_NOT_FOUND)
```

(The daemon parsed the full stdin body and answered with a semantic error for the demo run id — composition is no longer a failure surface.) Every layer's byte-exact survival of quote-heavy markdown is covered by new tests.

## Test plan

- `internal/cli`: stdin body verbatim (quotes/code blocks), trio pairing by occurrence, incomplete/multiline rejection, legacy-input obsolete errors, publication-outcome printing, retry with identical payload across daemon restart and uncertain transport failures, no-retry on invalid JSON, hook allowlist regex for the new command shape
- `internal/service/review`: publish-once idempotency, 0/1/N findings, failed→retry republish, restart→uncertain without republish, 8 concurrent submissions → 1 publisher call, findings in worker feedback and delivery
- `internal/httpd/controllers`: findings on the wire, obsolete-input 422s
- `internal/adapters/scm/github`: POST payload (`event=COMMENT`, commit anchor, comments), id/html_url parsing, missing-id error
- adapters + prompts: `gh api` absent from every reviewer policy, new command shape allowed
- Gates: `gofmt -l .` clean (whole backend), `go build ./...` ok, `go test` green on `internal/cli`, `internal/service/review`, `internal/review`, `internal/httpd/controllers`, `internal/storage/sqlite/...`, `internal/adapters/scm/...`, `internal/adapters/reviewer/...`, `internal/daemon`; sqlc regen reproduces the committed gen files; OpenAPI + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated

## Risks / follow-ups

- Frontend `tsc`/vitest not run in this worktree (no `node_modules`); the schema change is types-only and grep-verified that no code references the removed `SubmitReviewInput.githubReviewId`/`SubmitReviewItem` (the remaining `githubReviewId` uses are the review-run field, which stays).
- Three vitest files fail on this machine's non-en-US locale (upstream #4691) — pre-existing, untouched.

title: feat: add worker effort plumbing for TUI spawns
body:
Covers the effort-plumbing half of #5781 (the harness half is #5417). Stacks with #5417 without duplicating any of its files: this PR only adds the shared plumbing #5417 needs for `--effort`.

## What was missing

Since #5075, `domain.AgentConfig` carries `Effort` and `POST /api/v1/sessions` + `DelegateTask` forward it, but `ao spawn` had no `--effort` flag, so per-spawn effort was unreachable from the CLI. Adapters also had no shared helper: Codex hand-rolls `-c model_reasoning_effort=` and its `ConfigSpec` did not advertise `effort`, so copying that pattern for Command Code would repeat the hole #5781 flags (effort silently dropped when the catalog has no `efforts`).

- `agentbase`: new `ModelEffortConfigSpec` (model + effort fields) and `AppendEffortFlag` (trimmed append, empty = adapter default, so it works when `efforts[]` is absent).

- TUI spawn needs no manager change: `effectiveAgentConfig` + `applySpawnAgentConfig` already carry `Effort` through, and empty still means adapter default. No OpenAPI regen: `SpawnSessionRequest.effort` already exists on main.

title: fix(updater): calm, bounded retries for a build that fails verification
body:
## Summary

A macOS staged build that fails Squirrel verification was shown to the user as a red error on the very first failure, with raw wording ("the downloaded copy failed verification"), even though AO re-downloads and re-prepares it automatically on the next check. A routine, self-healing condition read as a hard failure.

This reports it calmly instead:

- While automatic retries remain, a new non-error `retry-scheduled` state shows a muted status line ("AO couldn't verify the downloaded update. It will try again automatically in about 15 minutes."), never a red failure and with no raw Squirrel detail.
- The retry bound goes from 2 to 3. Each retry rides the 15-minute automatic-check cycle (re-download + re-prepare).
- Only once the retries are spent does AO stop re-downloading and show an actionable error: "AO couldn't install this update automatically. Download the latest version manually from GitHub Releases to update."
- The out-of-disk-space staging message is reworded to plain language.

Verification and code-signature failures are the same Squirrel rejection path (`did not pass validation` / `failed to get static code`), so both are covered by this change.

## Not changed

The macOS staging-stall case ("Couldn't finish preparing the update. AO stayed open") is left as-is: the progress-based ShipIt watchdog and the disk-space preflight already handle it, which matches how electron/electron and electron-builder recommend handling a stall with no cancel API.

## Testing

- `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.test.ts` and `UpdatesSection.test.tsx`: 193 tests pass.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Not exercised end to end in the running app: the `retry-scheduled` state only appears on a real Squirrel verification failure, which could not be triggered live.

title: feat(cloud): unified harness credential onboarding in Harness settings + opencode
body:
## What

Moves cloud coding-agent credential onboarding into the **Harness settings** section (one place), instead of a separate Cloud credentials entry point. One login per harness now serves both local and cloud sessions: capture a portable credential once, use it locally, and push a copy to the control plane so cloud sandboxes run the same credential. Also adds **opencode** as a cloud harness.

## Why interfaces

Per-harness business logic is encapsulated behind interfaces + registries so adding a harness is a small, localized change:

- Worker injection: `harnessCredential` registry (`cloud/internal/workerexec/harness_credentials.go`) owns each harness's default binary + how a credential becomes env/files.
- Control plane: `agentCredentialSpec` registry (`cloud/internal/httpapi/harness_spec.go`) owns accepted credential types + validation. `validAgentProvider` / `validAgentCredentialType` / `Validate` delegate to it.
- Frontend: `ProviderAuthFlow` for browser-capture harnesses; api-key harnesses use the credential dialog. Session-creation pickers (task composer, create-project, orchestrator) all derive from the single `CLOUD_AGENT_PROVIDERS` list, so a new harness appears everywhere with one edit.

## opencode

opencode's interactive login lives in a local sqlite db (not a portable file), so its cloud credential is a provider API key injected as the matching env var (`OPENCODE_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). Its launch + `OPENCODE_CONFIG` generation live in the cloud module (self-contained; no new backend `agentruntime` dependency, so the CP image builds against the pinned backend).

## Notes

- claude local sessions get the captured setup-token injected only when no native login is present, so an existing local login is never shadowed.
- Running an opencode cloud session additionally needs the worker image rebuilt with the `opencode-ai` binary (follow-up); this PR covers Connect + the CP/worker credential plumbing.
- The staging GitHub-App gate change and the #5746 merge used for staging validation are intentionally not part of this PR.

## Testing

Backend + cloud build (against the pinned backend, CI-like), `go vet`, cloud unit tests (first tests in these packages), and frontend typecheck all pass. Validated on staging: opencode Connect succeeds and the CP boots cleanly with the harness credentials.

## Current limits

- Remote Cues are hidden because their API is still local; the all-host board and global terminal shortcut remain local.
- AO Files and managed previews work remotely. Open in Editor/VS Code, arbitrary host-local previews, and unattended agent browser automation are not part of this PR.
- Quick-tunnel URLs can change; clients must update the saved address. Desktop probes SSE once per connection, then polls every two seconds if stream delivery fails. User-owned stable tunnels are not configured by this PR.
- The new one-command bootstrap has passed script and installer checks but has not yet had a clean-VM live retest. Native Ubuntu Chat, edit, push, PR, service, and reboot flows were demonstrated through earlier manual setup. Physical iPhone, macOS LaunchAgent, browser-callback login, and AO Cloud coexistence remain unverified.

## Questions users will ask

### Why use it?

- **What can I do that local AO cannot?** Leave the host running while your laptop is off, then reconnect to its sessions from another device.
- **How is this different from AO Cloud?** The daemon, agents, projects, and credentials run on your machine; AO Cloud's managed sandboxes are a separate option.
- **Can I still use local AO as before?** Yes. Remote hosts are opt-in; local projects and sessions stay local.
- **Can I try this without moving existing work?** Yes. Add a host and one project there; your local projects are unchanged.
- **Does this add an AO fee?** This PR does not create an AO Cloud sandbox. You provide the machine and any model/provider plan; it makes no pricing promise.

### Setup

- **What goes on the other machine; does it need Electron?** Use the [headless setup guide](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/codex/remote-hosts-integrated/docs/self-hosted-remote.md) for the current PR or released one-command Ubuntu setup. It installs the daemon, bundled runtime, tmux, service, and optional tunnel; Electron stays on the client. Install the chosen agent from desktop Harness settings afterward.
- **Can the host be a laptop, headless PC, VM, or Docker container?** Yes. Use a non-root user and persistent `~/.ao`/project storage; for Docker, install with `--install-only` and supervise `ao daemon` with the container entrypoint instead of the default OS user service.
- **Which operating systems are proven?** A native Ubuntu 24.04 x64 VM completed fresh-user install, logout persistence, desktop pairing, task work, service restart, and full reboot; Linux arm64 Docker and macOS arm64 install-only smokes also passed. macOS LaunchAgent, Windows host setup, off-LAN native-desktop use and physical-phone E2E remain untested.
- **How does it survive logout or reboot?** The Ubuntu systemd user service with linger restarts AO after logout or reboot. Projects and conversation history persist; stopped agents are resumed individually by the user.
- **How do I connect and name a host?** Turn on **Settings → Remote hosts → Connect to remote hosts**, then add the host address, connection password, and a label such as “Home PC”.
- **Can I connect five hosts?** Yes. Each configured host and its projects appear separately in the sidebar.
- **Where do I install and sign in to OpenCode/Codex/etc.?** Select the host in desktop Harness settings; installation and terminal sign-in run there, not on the laptop. Claude Code/OpenCode installation on A, Claude Code installation on B, desktop-triggered Codex installation on a clean host, and Aider installation on Ubuntu were verified; browser-callback logins were not.
- **Where do GitHub credentials, SSH keys, and dev tools go?** On the host when its agent needs them. Laptop credentials are not automatically copied over.

### Daily work

- **Where do I choose local, Cloud, or Host A?** Choose where the project lives when adding it; start tasks from that project. A task does not move between locations afterward.
- **What if the same repository exists on A and B?** They are separate project copies with host badges; changes do not sync automatically.
- **Can I add, remove, and configure projects on the host's filesystem?** Yes. The remote folder picker and project actions target that daemon; workspace-folder import uses the host API, without local-only scan and branch helpers.
- **Do remote projects have New task, Orchestrator, board, settings, Chat, Files, and terminal?** Yes for project sessions, using the owning host. The global all-project board and terminal shortcut stay local; the remote projectless-agent entry point is not exposed yet.
- **Can one orchestrator spread workers over several hosts?** No. Its workers run under the orchestrator's owning host.
- **Can I move a running task between A, B, and my laptop?** No. A session remains on the daemon that started it.
- **Can the agent create a branch and PR?** Yes, when Git, repository access, and GitHub credentials are configured on that host; the Docker demo did this twice.
- **What familiar features still differ?** “Open in Editor” (including VS Code) is disabled for remote sessions and files. Session `+` shells can manage previews but not run browser automation. Unattended headless browser automation, global remote `⌘T`/`Ctrl+T`, and an all-host board are absent.
- **Does the session's `+` terminal open on my laptop?** No. The owning host opens the PTY in the session worktree (or project root if needed); the laptop only displays it over the authenticated terminal connection. Standalone/global terminal creation is not host-routed yet.
- **Can the agent verify a website in a browser after I close my laptop?** Not with this PR's preview proxy. Open [Cloud browser PR #5543](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5543) proposes headless Chromium in a cloud worker; adapting it to self-hosted hosts would be follow-up work.

### More than one device

- **Can I close my laptop and continue on my phone?** That is the intended flow when the host stays running and the phone can reach it. The Android emulator paired both hosts, created and chatted with a B task, and recovered A after an outage; a live approval prompt and physical-phone E2E were not verified.
- **Does mobile require my desktop to stay open?** No. Mobile connects directly to each paired host daemon.
- **Can a second laptop open that same session?** Yes. Pair that laptop with the same host, then open the host-owned session.
- **Must I pair every device separately?** Yes. Saved hosts and connection credentials are per client, not in a global directory.
- **Can two devices watch or message one session; what about simultaneous approvals?** They share the daemon's session state, but coordinated concurrent approvals were not validated for this PR. Avoid relying on a specific race outcome.
- **Can mobile start tasks, answer approvals, review changes, and receive notifications?** Task creation and Chat on B were verified on the Android emulator. Live approval, review, and notification journeys still need separate E2E checks.
- **Will desktop alerts cover every host?** Connected local/A/B alerts share the notification center with host-qualified actions; QA verified count, navigation and clear. Remote session headers now show the same combined bell.
- **Must I switch the phone between A and B?** No. Workers and Projects show both together and messages route by owning host; simultaneous chat with both was not part of the formal mobile QA.

### Connection and security

- **Must I be on the same Wi-Fi; can I connect while travelling?** LAN works nearby. Away from home, host setup `--tunnel` binds the authenticated listener only to loopback and starts AO's Cloudflare quick tunnel. Direct `ao remote-host enable --tunnel` intentionally keeps LAN access too. You can also use your own VPN/tunnel; the quick-tunnel URL changes on restart.
- **Is it SSH, HTTPS, VPN, or something else?** AO uses HTTP for API calls and WebSockets for terminals. The optional Cloudflare endpoint uses HTTPS/WSS; SSH is only for machine setup. Desktop tries SSE for live updates first and falls back to two-second polling if delivery is not observed.
- **Is traffic encrypted; may I expose the port publicly?** The opt-in LAN listener is password-protected but plaintext HTTP. Never expose its port directly to the internet. The optional Cloudflare tunnel encrypts traffic in transit, but Cloudflare terminates TLS and can see the bearer password, conversations, and terminal traffic.
- **Does AO relay my code or conversations through AO servers?** Not through AO servers. Direct connections stay on the network path you supply; the optional quick tunnel sends traffic through Cloudflare.
- **What can a paired client access?** It can use much of the daemon API, including sessions, project files, and shell terminals. The password is not a read-only or per-project credential; some local-only control routes are blocked.
- **Where is the password, and how do I revoke a lost device?** The host stores its listener password in `~/.ao/data/mobile/config.json`; desktop saves its copy in `~/.ao/remotes.json` (both owner-only on POSIX), and mobile uses secure storage. On a headless host, run `ao remote-host disable` then `ao remote-host enable` (or `enable --tunnel-only` for tunnel-only access) for a new password and re-pair clients. There is no per-device revoke. The latest retired password gets 401 without locking out a newly paired client, including after one daemon restart; older credentials still count toward lockout.
- **What if the host IP changes?** Update its saved address. Clients send the paired Host ID on requests; a cooperating daemon rejects a mismatch with 421 before executing writes. The ID is not cryptographic authentication, so use a trusted private network or encrypted tunnel. Quick-tunnel URLs change after restart, so clients need the new URL; mobile discovers advertised endpoints only after reconnecting.
- **Can teammates safely share one host?** This is not a multi-user isolation feature. Anyone holding its connection password gets broad host capabilities.

### Failures and recovery

- **Does the agent keep working if my laptop sleeps or loses internet?** Yes, if the host and its agent process remain running.
- **What if the host sleeps, restarts, runs out of disk, or loses power?** Work cannot continue while that host is unavailable. A service manager can restart the daemon; live processes and terminals may not survive, while persisted data depends on the host disk.
- **After reconnecting, do I get the same conversation and terminal?** Conversation history remains on the host. A still-running PTY can reattach; a PTY killed by a host restart cannot.
- **How do I tell connection loss from an agent stopping?** A connected session reports agent status. An offline or password-rejected host shows a separate connection error and Retry; it cannot verify current agent state until reconnected.
- **Could retrying a failed command run it twice?** Task creation, mobile Chat and mobile steer retain request IDs. Chat rejects reuse of an ID with changed payload (409); other writes are not all idempotent, so check host state after an ambiguous failure.
- **If I remove a host from Settings, do its tasks stop?** No. That removes this desktop's connection; the daemon and tasks remain on the host.
- **Where are projects, history, and backups?** AO state is under the host's `~/.ao` (or `AO_DATA_DIR`), with project repositories on that host. Back up both; this PR adds no cross-host backup service.
- **What if the host is permanently lost?** Restore its data and repositories from your backups. The laptop has no automatic copy of its running sessions or files.
- **Must client and host AO versions match?** Current desktop/mobile clients accept host API version 1 and reject a missing or newer version with update guidance before credentials are sent. This is a guard, not full compatibility negotiation; older released clients cannot gain it retroactively.
- **Does an offline host reconnect automatically when it returns?** Mobile retries each paired host independently. Desktop also retries transient startup-offline hosts every 15 seconds; identity mismatches and rejected passwords still require a corrected connection.

title: feat(mobile): add "Keep this Mac awake" option to Connect Mobile
body:
## Summary

A Mac that idle-sleeps drops every paired phone, so agents become unreachable from mobile as soon as the user walks away (the default macOS idle sleep can be as short as 1 minute). This adds a macOS-only **Keep this Mac awake** toggle to Settings → Mobile.

- **Daemon-owned:** the daemon runs `caffeinate -i -w <daemon pid>`. `-i` prevents idle system sleep only, so the display can still turn off and the screen can still lock. `-w` makes caffeinate exit on its own if the daemon dies, so a crash can't leave the machine awake.
- **Scoped to the bridge:** the assertion is held only while the user has opted in **and** the mobile connection is serving. Turning mobile off releases it but keeps the preference. It is restored on boot and released on shutdown.
- **Off by default**, persisted in `~/.ao/mobile/config.json` (`keepAwake`).
- **macOS only:** elsewhere the daemon reports `supported: false` and the renderer hides the row. An older daemon that omits the block also hides it.
- **Laptops:** the daemon detects an internal battery (`pmset -g batt`), and the UI adds a note that closing the lid still sleeps a MacBook.

API: new `POST /api/v1/mobile/keep-awake` (`{enabled}`). Mobile status gains `keepAwake: {supported, enabled, active, hasBattery}`. OpenAPI spec and `schema.ts` are regenerated. Strings are added for all 8 locales.

## Tests

- `go test -race ./internal/mobilebridge ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/daemon` pass; golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues on the touched packages.
- New unit tests cover:
  - the bridge: unsupported platform, the option following bridge enable/disable, `Enable` preserving the preference, toggling while running, boot restore/shutdown, and the route including a bad body;
  - the `KeepAwake` process lifecycle, using a fake binary.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean. Vitest passes for mobile settings and i18n (231 passed), including new tests for hiding/showing the switch, toggling it, and the laptop note.
- Manual run against a scratch daemon on macOS, checking `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` at each step:
  - opt in with the bridge off: nothing held;
  - enable the bridge: held;
  - disable: released;
  - re-enable: held again;
  - opt out: released;
  - `kill -9` the daemon: caffeinate exits;
  - restart: restored.

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- Not visually checked in the native Electron window: screen capture was unavailable while the display was asleep. The row is covered by the component tests, but it needs a quick visual pass on Settings → Mobile.
- A possible follow-up: detect when the Mac already has auto-sleep disabled and say so instead of offering the toggle.

title: fix(sidebar): sort sessions by the message age they display
body:
## Summary
Each sidebar session row shows the age of the user's last message (`lastUserMessageAt`, added in #4533). The list itself was sorted by `updatedAt` (#4132), which changes whenever the agent does something or PR/CI state refreshes. Rows could then appear out of order compared with their labels, for example a `6m` row below a `28m` row, or `34m` below `1d`.

`sortedWorkerSessions` now sorts newest first by:
1. `lastUserMessageAt`, or `createdAt` for sessions that have never received a message
2. `updatedAt` as a tiebreaker
3. `id`

As a result, the list only reorders when the user sends a message, not while agents work in the background.

## Tests
- Replaced the Sidebar ordering test. The new test covers: a busy agent whose recent `updatedAt` must not push it above a more recently messaged session, the `createdAt` fallback for never-messaged sessions, an invalid `lastUserMessageAt`, and the `updatedAt` tiebreak. The test fails against the old sort.
- `npm test` in `frontend/`: 333 files, 5309 tests pass.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors outside `packages/product-ui`. The errors there are because that package's dependencies weren't installed in this worktree.

## Risks
- A session with an active agent no longer rises to the top on its own. That's intentional, so the list matches the displayed ages.
- Drag-reordered session order (in-memory `sessionOrder`) still takes precedence and is unchanged.

title: fix(session): pass terminal theme hints to every agent
body:
## Summary

Claude Code sessions in AO's **light** terminal draw plain code text and line numbers in near-white. You can only read them by selecting the text. The cause is a theme mismatch:

- Claude Code's `auto` theme looks up the terminal background with an OSC 11 query, and falls back to `COLORFGBG` if that fails.
- Inside AO, the OSC 11 reply doesn't make it back across the mux in time. This is the same issue that led AO to add `termtheme` for Cursor.
- `COLORFGBG`/`TERM_THEME` were set only for Cursor (`cursor.AugmentRuntimeEnv`). So on a light AO canvas, Claude Code (and other theme-following CLIs) fell back to **dark**.

I confirmed this on a live session: the `claude` process had `TERM`/`COLORTERM` set but no `COLORFGBG`/`TERM_THEME`, while `~/.ao/data/terminal-theme` was `light`. Setting `/theme auto` in that session still rendered dark.

## Change

`termtheme.Apply(env, m.dataDir)` now runs in `Manager.augmentAgentRuntimeEnv`, after the adapter's own augmentation. Every spawn, restore and agent-switch launch goes through that hook. The only `runtimeEnv` calls that skip it are a history probe and workspace cleanup, neither of which launches an agent.

- The value comes from the theme the desktop app last wrote (`~/.ao/data/terminal-theme`: resolved light/dark matching the xterm palette), read when the agent starts.
- An explicit project-env `TERM_THEME`/`COLORFGBG` still wins (`Apply` never overrides it).
- With no theme file (headless daemon), nothing is set and nothing is guessed.
- Cursor's own call is left in place: it also serves the native ACP chat driver path, and `Apply` is idempotent.

## Limitations

- This fixes agents that **follow** the terminal. A user who explicitly sets `"theme": "dark"` in Claude Code still gets dark, which is correct because that was their choice.
- The hint is read at process start. Changing AO's theme mid-session takes effect on the agent's next start (restore or restart). Live OSC replies are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `runtime_env_theme_test.go`:
  - a light theme file sets `TERM_THEME=light` / `COLORFGBG=0;15`;
  - a project value is kept and the adapter's augmentation still applies;
  - no theme file sets no hints.
- `go test ./internal/termtheme ./internal/adapters/agent/cursor` pass. golangci-lint reports 0 issues on `internal/session_manager`.
- Four `TestSpawn_*MissingBinary*` tests in `internal/session_manager` fail locally because they can't find tmux in the test environment. They fail the same way on unmodified `main`.

Stacked on #5864 (base: `ui/worktree-panel-layout`). Merge that first; this PR's diff is only the one commit on top of it.

## What

Picking a pull request in the Files picker now offers **Commits ›** with that PR's own commits, the way the Workspace source already does:

- **Changes** (the whole PR, the default) sits on top, then **Commits ›**, then **Branch ›**.
- Picking a commit narrows the file tree and the preview to that commit, and the trigger shows its short SHA. **Changes** returns to the whole PR.
- Staged / Unstaged / Untracked stay Workspace-only: they are local, uncommitted edits, which a PR does not have.

Why: with two PRs in one session, Workspace only shows the checked-out branch, so an earlier PR's commits couldn't be seen anywhere in the Files panel, and the picker's Commits entry disappeared as soon as a PR was selected.

## How

**Backend**
- `GET /sessions/{id}/pr/{n}/files` now returns `commits` (base..head, newest first), each with its changed files.
- `GET /pr/{n}/file` and `GET /pr/{n}/file/revision` accept `commitSha`. The SHA must be one of the PR's commits; a commit's before side is its first parent. They dispatch to new `GetPRFileAtCommit` / `GetPRFileRevisionAtCommit`, mirroring the Workspace's `…AtCommit` methods, so the existing whole-PR reads are unchanged.
- Reads stay revision-only and never touch the session worktree, so per-commit file sizes are not read: the list only picks and filters files, and opening a file reports its real size.
- The commit list is best-effort: if a PR's log can't be read, its files still load, just without the menu.
- `gitCommitLog`'s two git passes moved into `gitCommitLogChanges`; the Workspace path produces the same output as before.

**Frontend**
- `SessionFileExplorer` builds the PR's menu in the same `ReviewSourceMenu` shape the Workspace review publishes, so both render through the one dropdown. The picked commit is keyed by PR URL, so it never carries over to another PR.
- PR file and revision fetches pass `commitSha` and key their caches by it.

## Testing

Run locally from this branch, following the CI workflows:

- **Backend (`go.yml`):** `gofmt` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, golangci-lint v2.12.2 `0 issues`, api drift (the spec and `schema.ts` regenerate identically). `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes for everything this touches. 6 tests in three untouched packages (`adapters/agent/claudecode`, `fake`, `goose`) timed out under full-suite load and pass when rerun alone; none of those packages import the changed code.
- **Frontend (`frontend.yml`):** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, landing `icons:check`, and `npx vitest run`: 5381 passed. 2 `src/main` tests timed out under load and pass alone (191/191).
- **Renderer smoke (`@T0|@P0`):** run against the installed Google Chrome instead of Playwright's Chromium, which isn't downloaded locally. 53 passed; 7 chat/terminal/focus tests timed out late in the 9-minute run and all pass when rerun alone. None of them touch the Files panel.
- **Not run locally:** `windows-workspace` (needs Windows), `cloud-build-test`, `sqlc-drift`, `mac-update-helper` (untouched areas). Left to CI.

New tests:
- **Go:** a real two-commit PR repo covers the commit list, one commit's file and diff, before/after sides, an added file's missing before side, and rejection of a file outside the commit and of a SHA outside the PR. Controller tests check that `commitSha` routes to the new methods and that commits are returned.
- **Vitest:** picking a PR commit narrows the tree and preview, and Changes restores the whole PR; commit-scoped cache keys; the preview sends `commitSha` on file and revision reads.

Manual check in `dev:web` with mocked PR data: PR #1's three commits list in the picker, picking one narrows the tree and preview, every file and revision request carried `commitSha`, and the Workspace picker behaves as before.

title: bug(httpd): TestServerShutdownEndpoint flakes ~1/3 under -race — Shutdown waits on a spare keep-alive connection
body:
## Summary

`TestServerShutdownEndpoint` (backend/internal/httpd) fails intermittently under `-race`: roughly 1 in 3 runs on a clean checkout (verified on upstream `main` with no local changes). The test is not flaky because of load — it loses a race against `http.DefaultTransport`.

## Mechanism

1. The test POSTs to `/shutdown` using a client backed by the shared `http.DefaultTransport`.
2. After the response, the transport dials a **spare keep-alive connection** (speculative dial for connection reuse) with no request attached.
3. The server accepts it and sees `StateNew` — an idle connection with no completed request.
4. `Shutdown` waits for active connections to become idle… and keeps waiting for the spare connection until the full `ShutdownTimeout` expires → test timeout/failure.

## Repro

```
go test -race -run TestServerShutdownEndpoint ./internal/httpd/ -count=10
```

Observed: 3–4 failures per 10 runs on clean `main`. Non-`-race` runs are much less likely to expose it (timing), which is why CI stays green.

## Fix

Test-only, no production behavior change: issue the POST from a client with `DisableKeepAlives: true` so no spare connection is dialed (#5935, +7/-1 in `server_test.go`). Verified: `-race -count=10` → 10/10 green.

title: Supervised session launches a second daemon on the live AO_DATA_DIR → intermittent SQLITE_BUSY: guard, support, or document?
body:
## Question / design discussion, with a real incident

**What happened.** A worker session (Claude Code, managed by the AO desktop app) was asked to reproduce a UI bug in the real desktop app. It launched a second AO instance: dev Electron (electron-forge) plus a second daemon (`ao daemon`). The launch partially isolated itself — own `AO_RUN_FILE` and own Electron `userData` — but reused the live **`AO_DATA_DIR`**.

Two daemons then wrote the same SQLite database (`ao.db`, WAL mode). Within minutes the live daemon's log filled with:

```
level=ERROR msg="scm observer: DB write failed" err="write pr observation: database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)"
level=WARN  msg="usage source ingestion failed" err="apply usage chunk: database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)"
```

Spawning orchestrators hung in "Spawning…", and projects unrelated to the worker's task turned red in the UI. The worker had no way to know it was sabotaging its own host — from its perspective it had "isolated" the second instance (separate run file, separate userData).

**The question:** is a supervised session launching another AO instance against the live data dir considered a supported scenario, a footgun AO should prevent, or user error?

Options as I see them:

1. **Mechanical guard in the daemon**: a second daemon targeting an already-locked data dir refuses to start (advisory lock on the data dir / DB) with a clear error, instead of limping along on intermittent `SQLITE_BUSY`. This is the layer that cannot be forgotten.
2. **Safe parallel instances**: repro-style launches (dev Electron + dev daemon) default to an isolated data dir unless explicitly overridden — e.g. warn loudly when `AO_DATA_DIR` is inherited from the environment rather than set.
3. **Docs-only**: declare concurrent instances unsupported and rely on prompt-level discipline. Fragile: the worker genuinely believed it had isolated the launch; it just missed one env var.

Observations that may matter:

- WAL kept reads working (`readyz` stayed `ready`, list APIs responded, just slowly), only writes failed intermittently — so the breakage surfaced as random UI flakiness ("Spawning…", red dots), not as one clear error. A quiet failure mode.
- The dev daemon used a separate `AO_RUN_FILE`, so the supervisor/takeover logic had no reason to consider it a conflict with the live daemon.

For transparency: as a local stopgap I've installed a session-level guard (a Claude Code PreToolUse hook denying daemon/app launches from supervised sessions). That protects my install but is prompt-layer, so I'm not proposing it as *the* fix — interested in maintainers' view on whether the daemon-level guard (1) is the right layer.

Happy to send a PR for (1) if that's deemed the right approach.

---

**Source:** live observation on a long-running install | **Reported by:** @axisrow

title: fix(sessions): give managed sessions project-owned temp dirs with ownership records
body:
## Summary
Managed sessions now get project-owned temporary folders with an ownership record, instead of inheriting the daemon's shared OS temp location. All worker, chat, and agent-switch launch paths pin `TMPDIR`/`TEMP`/`TMP` at the session's own folder and refuse clearly when the scratch root is unusable.

## Problem
[#5933](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/5933): the worker-launch code never assigned a project-owned temporary directory, so worker processes inherited the user's shared OS temp location. After a session crashed or was killed, its leftovers could not be distinguished from files belonging to other applications. Only `pi` reviewer processes used a private temp folder; nothing provided a consistent ownership and cleanup mechanism.

## Fix
- New `backend/internal/sessiontemp` package: per-project scratch root under the AO data dir (`session-temp/<project>/`, with a `standalone` bucket for projectless sessions mirroring the scratch workspace layout), per-run `<session>/tmp` folder plus an `owner.json` ownership record, writability probe, race-safe creation, and report-only orphan discovery that never deletes anything.
- `session_manager.Manager.runtimeEnv` pins `TMPDIR`/`TEMP`/`TMP` at the prepared per-run folder (AO values always win over project env, case-insensitively on Windows) and returns `ErrTempRootUnusable` instead of silently inheriting shared temp. Wired through every covered launch path: `launchRuntimeEnv` / `prepareWorkerLaunchEnv`, chat spawn and resume, agent-switch worker and chat flows, and the interface-transition probe. Workspace cleanup degrades to AO-only env with a warning when temp is unavailable.
- `restoreSessionWorkspace` verifies the project scratch root before touching saved work.
- `agentlaunch.WriteTempDir` scopes launch-spec files to a given session temp folder; `WriteTemp` keeps its historical behavior for callers without one.
- A blank data dir (focused tests and embedders) configures no scratch root and keeps the historical behavior; production always resolves a real data dir, where the pin always applies.

## Validation
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the touched packages: clean.
- New tests pass: `sessiontemp` package suite (creation, idempotent reuse, concurrent first launch, standalone bucket, unusable-root refusal, mismatched-owner refusal, report-only discovery) including a `-race` run; launch-pinning tests (`TMPDIR`/`TEMP`/`TMP` pinned, project override rejected, unusable root refused); `WriteTempDir` round-trip tests.
- Full `backend/internal/session_manager` suite compared against a clean-HEAD baseline worktree: the only failures are the ones that also fail without this change on this machine (missing WSL/`claude` binary/node toolchain, Windows file-mode semantics, branch-namespace expectations). Five tests that regressed during development (projectless standalone sessions, prompt-file fallback fixtures using a fully blocked data dir) were fixed by supporting the `standalone` bucket and blocking only the `prompts` subtree in those fixtures.

## Not in this PR
- No automatic deletion of temp leftovers: discovery is report-only by design.
- The `cursor` reviewer still inherits OS temp; only the `pi` path isolates temp via the existing review gateway, which this change does not alter.
- tmux/conpty adapters needed no changes: both already export the full `cfg.Env`, so the pinned temp vars propagate, and neither strips them.

title: fix(lifecycle): tear down reviewer panes on every terminal-state write
body:
Fixes #5948.

## Problem

Reviewer panes are runtime handles (`review-<worker>`) with **no row in `sessions`** — their durable state is `reviews.reviewer_handle_id` plus a ptyregistry entry. When a worker is terminated by any path that bypasses `session_manager.Manager.Kill` (tracker-facts termination, reaper-driven `ApplyRuntimeObservation`, …), nothing destroys the pane: the `ao pty-host` + agent keep running detached (Setsid → PPID=1) behind a terminated session. Observed in #5948: an auto-review reviewer ran 8+ hours (~300 MB) after both a daemon restart and the worker's termination.

## Fix

Mirror the #2652 container-reap pattern: wire the review service into lifecycle as an optional late-bound `ReviewerTeardown` dep (same shape as `SetCompletionTerminator`), and call it best-effort from exactly the choke points `reapSessionContainers` already covers — both `MarkTerminated` exits and `ApplyRuntimeObservation`'s reaper-driven terminal transition. Every `is_terminated` write in the backend funnels through these two functions, so the invariant becomes: *any* termination takes the reviewer pane down.

- Uses `Engine.TerminateReviewer` (same method and body `Kill` uses): cancels running review runs, idempotent on cleared handles, never reads the session row — the duplicate call after `Kill`'s own teardown is a cheap no-op.
- Fire-on-repeat (like the container reap) for self-healing on repeated terminations.
- Best-effort: errors are logged, never block or fail the termination.

## Testing

TDD, red→green:

- `TestMarkTerminated_TearsDownReviewer` + `TestRuntimeObservation_ConfirmedDeathTearsDownReviewer` reproduce the leak (before the fix: `SetReviewerTeardown undefined` / reaper-driven termination left the pane alive; after: green).
- Contract pins: teardown failure doesn't fail termination; fire-on-repeat; non-terminal workload-death doesn't fire.
- `go test ./internal/lifecycle/ ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/session_manager/ ./internal/review/...` green; full backend suite green except pre-existing environment-bound failures in `adapters/agent/{crush,goose,modelcatalog}` (reproduced on a clean tree without this diff; machine-config leakage, tracked upstream as known flaky/environment-sensitive).
- `gofmt -l` clean on the whole backend module; `go vet` clean on touched packages.

## Known residual (follow-up, not here)

- Crash window: a daemon death between the flag commit and the hook, or between `runtime.Create` and `upsertReview`, still leaves an untracked pane. A boot-time sweep of `ptyregistry.Scan()` against live session/review handles (and/or a pty-host idle exit) would close that class.

title: fix(updates): treat a check timeout as a network failure
body: ## What An update check that hangs (rather than failing fast with a Chromium `net::ERR_*` string) now counts as a network failure, the same way #3700 already treats a fail-fast wedge: 1. A manual "Check for Updates" that times out now shows the restart guidance ("Restarting the app usually fixes this") instead of a plain "Try again". 2. Automatic (background) checks that time out now count toward the 3-in-a-row restart nudge, instead of resetting that streak on every timeout. ## Why `checkForUpdatesWithDeadline()` gives every check a 60s deadline and throws `UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE` if nothing answers in time. This is the same wedged-network-stack condition #3700 already detects and guides users to restart for — it's just the hang variant instead of the fail-fast variant. But `isNetError()` only recognized Chromium's `net::ERR_*` strings. A timeout doesn't match that, so: - On a manual check, the timeout fell through to the generic error path and told the user to "Try again" — which fails the same way until the app is restarted. - On automatic checks, `recordAutomaticCheckFailure()` treats any non-net error as proof the network stack reached a server, and resets the consecutive-failure streak. A timeout is the opposite of that, so a run of automatic checks that keep timing out never crosses the threshold and the install goes silently stale, exactly the failure mode #3700 was meant to catch. Reproduced on my own machine: two update checks in the same app run (one at launch, one manual) both hit the 60s timeout while the same three requests answered in under a second from `curl` moments later, with no proxy or VPN on the machine — consistent with the same per-process wedge #3700 already handles, just hanging instead of failing fast. ## How - `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`: - `isNetError()` now also matches `UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE`, so the existing `net::`-only check now covers both variants of a wedged network stack. `isNetErrorMessage()` itself (the Chromium-specific, shared helper) is untouched. - `checkForUpdatesWithDeadline()`'s deadline timer broadcasts an error immediately for manual/return-home checks, before the check promise even settles. That broadcast now also carries `netError: true`. ## Testing `npx vitest run src/main/auto-updater.test.ts src/shared/update-telemetry.test.ts` — 197/197 pass, including: - extended the existing "aborts a hung check" test (manual/return-home) to assert `netError: true` on the timeout status - new test: three consecutive automatic-check timeouts trip the same `staleCheckNudge` the net::ERR_FAILED case already covers `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` - [x] One focused change; extends #3700 to the hang case it didn't cover - [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(lifecycle): reap ownerless conpty pty-host panes on boot, bound exited-host keep-alive
body:
Follow-up to #5948 (first fix: #5953 — lifecycle `ReviewerTeardown` hook for flag-only terminations). This closes the remaining leak classes: **crash windows** that leave a conpty pty-host with no owner, and the **unbounded keep-alive** of an exited-child host.

## Problem

After a daemon crash (kill -9, reboot, app force-quit), the boot reconcile adopts non-terminated sessions and reaps terminated ones — but several pty-host panes have no one left to destroy them:

1. **Reviewer pane of a terminated worker** — daemon died between the `is_terminated` commit and the #5953 teardown hook. The `review-<worker>` pane keeps running detached (Setsid → PPID=1). This is the exact pane observed in #5948 (8+ hours, ~300 MB).
2. **Pane whose owner row was never written** — daemon died between `runtime.Create` and the reviews upsert.
3. **Previous-app-run shell terminals** (`shellterm-*`) — rows are filtered by app run after a restart, so the API can never reach them again.
4. **Stale prelaunch reservations** (`PtyHostPID == 0`) — `Scan` retains them forever and they block a future same-id `Create`.

Additionally, a pty-host whose PTY child has exited stays alive indefinitely by design ("keep-alive" for scrollback) — even with zero viewers, so any leak above persists until reboot.

## Fix A — boot sweep (`ReconcileOrphanedPtyHosts`)

Runs synchronously in daemon boot, **before the API listener accepts traffic** (no fresh pane can appear mid-sweep) and before the adopt pass (which only ever adopts keep-set members, so no race by construction).

For every `ptyregistry` entry: keep it only if it is a non-terminated session's own handle or that session's `review-<id>` reviewer pane; otherwise `Destroy` it. Ownerless prelaunch reservations are unregistered (`Destroy` refuses them). Handles are built with the `ptyhost-v1` scheme (`runtimeselect.DirectHandleID`) so a hybrid runtime routes them to conpty — a bare id would be dispatched to tmux and miss the registry. tmux-only daemons no-op on the empty registry. Per-item failures are logged and skipped.

The keep-rule derives solely from non-terminated session ids: the reviews table is not a liveness signal (handles persist after agent-switch clears, terminated workers keep theirs), and `session_manager` cannot import `review` (import cycle).

## Fix B — bounded keep-alive (idle exit)

A pty-host whose child has exited now shuts itself down after `hostIdleExit` (5 min) with no attached client. An attached viewer keeps the host up indefinitely; shutdown fires within `[hostIdleExit, 2*hostIdleExit)` after the last detach — never early. The window is read once per watcher (tests mutate the package var; the race detector caught the naive per-iteration read).

## Testing

TDD, red→green per fix:

- `TestReconcileOrphanedPtyHosts_DestroyOwnerlessKeepsLiveWorkerAndReviewer` — live worker + its reviewer kept; terminated worker, ownerless ghost destroyed (with scheme-prefixed handles); ownerless reservation unregistered. Compile-red without the method.
- `TestReconcileOrphanedPtyHosts_EmptyRegistryIsNoop` — tmux-only daemon no-op.
- `TestIdleExitNoClientsAfterChildExitShutsDown` — timed out waiting for `Serve` before the fix; passes after.
- `TestIdleExitKeepsHostWhileClientAttachedThenShutsDownAfterDetach` — pins the keep-alive contract.
- Full `go test ./... -race` green in the touched packages (`session_manager`, `conpty`, `daemon`); `gofmt`/`go vet` clean; `GOOS=windows` build of the touched trees clean. Unrelated `adapters/agent/{crush,modelcatalog}` failures are machine-config leakage, reproduced on a clean tree without this diff.

title: fix(models): show configured Claude alias default with its real label
body:
## Problem

In the New Task composer (and other model pickers), a Claude Code session could show a raw lowercase model id (e.g. `sonnet`) or **"Model not reported"** instead of the model actually configured for the local CLI.

### Root cause

On first-party Anthropic, provider discovery succeeds and returns **concrete snapshot IDs** (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `claude-opus-4-8`, …), but the local CLI default in `~/.claude/settings.json` is an **alias** (`sonnet`). `applyClaudeConfiguredDefault` compares the configured value against discovered IDs; since no concrete ID equals `"sonnet"`, it appended a phantom `{ID:"sonnet", Label:"sonnet"}` entry marked default. The frontend then rendered that raw id — or, against a catalog cached before the model was set, fell through to the "Model not reported" fallback.

## Fix

When the configured default doesn't match a discovered model, carry it with the **human label Claude Code uses for the alias** (`sonnet` → "Sonnet", `opus` → "Opus", `opus[1m]` → "Opus (1M context)", …), falling back to the raw id for custom aliases and pinned snapshots so no name is ever invented. This surfaces **only** the local CLI's configured default.

Verified against a real machine with `settings.json` = `{"model":"sonnet"}` and successful provider discovery: the catalog default is now `id="sonnet" label="Sonnet"`, so the picker renders **"Sonnet"**.

## Tests

- Added `TestClaudeConfiguredAliasDefaultCarriesHumanLabel` (alias → human label, single default).
- Added `TestClaudeConfiguredUnknownDefaultKeepsRawLabel` (custom pin keeps raw label, never renamed).
- All existing Claude catalog tests pass.

_Note: two unrelated tests in this package (`autohand`, `config` discovery) fail in the sandbox for lack of CLI binaries/fixtures; confirmed pre-existing on the clean tree, untouched by this change._

## Risk / follow-up

Low risk — scoped to the Claude configured-default labeling path. Provider-sourced catalogs (Bedrock/Vertex) are unaffected. Separate/out of scope: when the local CLI has **no** model configured at all, there is still no default to show (the CLI's built-in unconfigured default isn't exposed by `/v1/models`).

title: bug(updater): restored staged update loses release notes after app restart
body:
## Problem

The restart confirmation can say “No release notes were published for this build” even when the target GitHub release has a complete release body.

This happens after an update has been downloaded and staged, but the app process starts again while the older build is still installed. AO restores the staged version, timestamp, and channel, but not the release notes that were attached to the update in memory.

## Observed state

- Running build: `0.13.2-nightly.202609271025`
- Staged build: `0.13.2-nightly.202609271750`
- Platform: Windows
- Update channel: Nightly
- Automatic updates: enabled
- The pending installer is present and complete in the updater cache.
- The target release contains generated notes: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/releases/tag/v0.13.2-nightly.202609271750
- The restart dialog displays: `No release notes were published for this build.`

## Cause

`directFeedReleaseNotes` and `offeredReleaseNotes` are process memory. `persistStagedBuild()` writes only:

- `version`
- `stagedAt`
- `channel`

`restoreStagedBuild()` restores the same three fields. After a process restart, the UI still knows that the update is staged, but `releaseNotes` is undefined, so the restart dialog renders its empty-state message.

This is an application-state issue in `frontend/src/main/auto-updater.ts`. The private release repository successfully published the release body and does not own the staged-update state.

## Expected behavior

A restored staged update should show the same release notes that were available when the build was discovered and downloaded.

## Suggested fix

Persist the normalized release notes with the staged-update record and restore them into `offeredReleaseNotes`. Alternatively, reattach the fetched release body when the restored staged version matches the discovered release.

Keep existing staged-update files compatible when the optional notes field is absent.

## Test coverage

Add a regression test that:

1. Stages a build with release notes.
2. Persists and restores the staged-update record in a fresh updater instance.
3. Reads the restored downloaded status.
4. Confirms the status still includes the release notes.
5. Confirms an older staged-update record without notes still restores safely.
