title: fix(mobile): show user-facing errors instead of raw API and network text
body:
## Summary
An audit of mobile error handling found that most screens rendered `error.message` as-is. Users saw wire strings like `409 Conflict - …`, `503 Service Unavailable`, or fetch's `Network request failed`. Only the board tabs and pairing flow used the human copy in `connectionError.ts`.

- **`userFacingError()`** (pure, in `connectionError.ts`) picks one sentence per failure:
  - Desktop never answered: "Couldn't reach your desktop…"
  - 401/403/429: the pairing copy.
  - Other 4xx: the daemon's own message, without the status line.
  - 5xx: generic copy plus the daemon's request ID for log lookup.
  - It never renders a status code or reason phrase.
- **Typed errors:** `req()` throws `UnreachableError` for timeouts and failed fetches. `ApiError` gains a `detail` field. `message` keeps its status prefix for logs and Sentry.
- **Call sites:** chat, terminal banners, sheets, board row actions, notifications, preview, and interface switching all go through the helper. Removed "No AO server configured", "The daemon did not return…", and similar strings.
- **Bug fix:** `spawnErrorCopy` passed an empty host and port, so an offline spawn read "Reached nothing at :.".
- **Terminal:** status reads "Live" or "Reconnecting…" instead of `live`/`disconnected`/`error`. The daemon's raw Go terminal errors and exit codes are mapped to user copy (`session/terminalCopy.ts`).
- **Desktop disconnected:** chat shows "Not connected to your desktop" and reloads when the board reconnects. The Projects and PRs tabs now share the Workers tab's failure copy, including the rotated-tunnel case (`useBoardFailure`). The session not-found and ended states get an "Open board" action.

- **Spawn sheet offline:** it used to show three lines for one cause: a false "No installed agent… supports Chat" (the warning fired on any empty catalog, including a failed load), a bare "Your desktop disconnected" (`agentErrorCopy` returned only the title), and the model catalog's failure. It now shows a single "Not connected to your desktop" line (`lib/spawnNotices.ts`) and reloads its data on reconnect. `agentErrorCopy` uses the helper, which also fixes the agent sheet.
- **Notifications offline:** a "Not connected to your desktop" state with Retry, a banner over already-loaded items, and a reload on reconnect. The reload is keyed on the reconnect, so a request that keeps failing while connected can't loop.

## Tests
- `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 137 files, 1,283 tests pass (18 new, covering `userFacingError`, `daemonDetail`, typed unreachable errors from `req()`, the terminal copy, and the spawn notices).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Manually tested on the iOS simulator with Connect Mobile turned off: notifications, chat, terminal, spawn and the board tabs. Android was not tested by hand. The 401/429/5xx messages are covered by unit tests only.
- 4xx messages now come straight from the daemon's error envelope, so any daemon message that is still developer-worded will show through. Those should be fixed on the daemon side.
- File-attachment and voice errors still show native messages. They are local and never come from the daemon.

title: fix(spawn): reuse display freshness for launch auth checks (#5890)
body:
Code changes: +11 -4
Tests: +43 -0
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #5890: local Start task takes ~6s to show Chat UI.

Root cause (measured, not hypothesized): every session spawn blocks on EnsureAgentReadiness(launch), which re-probes authentication whenever the 30s launch TTL expired — practically every real start. The auth probe shells out to a Codex account capacity read: 776ms cold-join, 1291-1694ms fresh here, 10s timeout by design. Installation probes cost ~ms. So spawn paid seconds for freshness its own gates don't need (they only block on binary-missing and fresh-unauthorized-codex).

Fix: neededChecksLocked now gives installation the purpose TTL (launch stays 30s) while authentication always uses the display horizon (5m). Explicit invalidation (sign-in/out, launch failures) still forces immediate rechecks, so both spawn gates behave exactly as before.

Benchmarks (this Mac, Codex standalone, POST /api/v1/sessions):
- Cold daemon: 2.27s -> 1.48s
- Warm, 45s after last check (past old 30s TTL): 2.40s -> 0.91s (launch ensure now cache_hit, zero auth re-probe)
- Mount queries (projects/sessions GETs): 0.1-1.8ms, unchanged

Verified:
- New coordinator test LaunchReusesDisplayFreshnessForAuth fails pre-fix, passes post-fix.
- go test ./internal/service/agent/ ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/httpd/controllers/ all green; go vet clean.
- Full frontend suite untouched by this change (backend-only); the 3 ContextMeter/ChatWorkspace failures reproduce on clean main.

Omissions:
- Mount render + terminal-attach time not separately timed (browser preview cannot mount chat; needs Electron CDP harness). Mount API calls measured sub-ms; remaining reporter-side gap is consistent with slower auth probes on their machine, now removed from the path.
- The composer mount double-ensure was already removed from TaskComposer by #5626; remaining mount fires are fire-and-forget and unaffected by this change.

title: Markdown rich preview resets after switching sessions
body:
## Summary
Markdown files do not remember the **Rich preview** display mode after switching away from a session and then returning to it.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a worker session that has a Markdown file in its workspace, for example `README.md`.
2. Open the file in the session file workspace / Files panel.
3. Switch the file from normal file view to **Rich preview**.
4. Navigate to a different session.
5. Navigate back to the original session.

## Expected
The Markdown file should still be in **Rich preview** mode.

## Actual
The file returns to the normal file/code view.

## Why this happens
The selected file display mode is kept as local React state inside `frontend/src/renderer/components/FileContentPane.tsx`:

- `mode` is initialized from `initialMode`.
- Clicking the toolbar buttons only calls `setMode(...)` locally.
- When the user switches sessions, the pane for the previous session unmounts/remounts.
- On remount, the effect resets `mode` back to `initialMode`.

For center file tabs, `initialMode` comes from `activeCenterFileRequest?.mode ?? "file"` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx`. That request records how the file was originally opened, not later toolbar toggles such as switching to Rich preview. The current persisted per-session UI state in `frontend/src/renderer/stores/ui-store.ts` keeps Files tab state like `filesChangedOnly` and `filesSource`, but not per-file display mode.

## Suggested fix
Persist the file display mode per session/path (or update the center-file request state when the mode toolbar changes) and feed that value back into `FileContentPane` when a session is restored. A focused regression test should cover: open Markdown file -> switch to rendered mode -> switch sessions -> return -> rendered mode is still selected.

This should be a small, bounded frontend-only task and is suitable as a good first issue.

Follow-up to #5936, for @kvnloo's [review comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/5936#issuecomment-5859203907).

## What

- **The commit list is bounded.** A Commits menu (the PR's and the Workspace's) now holds at most the newest 250 commits, and reads at most 2 MiB from each of its two `git log` passes. Both files responses report when older commits were left out: `commitsTruncated: true`.
- **Opening a PR commit reads only that commit.** A file or revision read with `commitSha` no longer lists the whole PR. It checks that the SHA belongs to the PR, then reads that one commit, so a commit older than the cap still opens.

## How

**Bounded list** (`gitCommitLogChanges`, shared by both menus)
- `--max-count=251`: the extra commit tells a full list from a cut one.
- Both passes go through `gitWorkspaceOutputCapped` with a 2 MiB cap, the same as the diff-group cap. 250 matches GitHub's pull request commits API.
- A commit is listed whole or not at all. A pass that hits the cap drops the commit it stopped in. If the `--numstat` pass stopped before the `--name-status` pass, commits past its last whole one are dropped too; without counts, their text files would show as binary.
- `commitsTruncated` is optional and omitted when false, so existing clients and TS fixtures are unaffected.

**Direct commit read** (`prCommitFile`)
- Accepts only a full lowercase SHA (40 or 64 hex), so a request value never reaches git as an option.
- Membership: ancestor of head, and `git rev-list --count <sha> ^<base>` > 0. That is exactly `base..head`, and a failed git call rejects.
- Reads the commit as `<sha>^!` through the same parser as the list, so its files, renames and counts match what the menu showed.

**Also**
- `gitWorkspaceOutputCapped` now sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GCM_INTERACTIVE=Never`, like `gitWorkspaceOutput`, so the commit log keeps its no-prompt environment after the move. The diff-group reader gets it too.

## Not in this PR

- The UI doesn't show `commitsTruncated` yet, the same as the file list's existing `truncated` flag. A note in the Commits menu needs copy in every locale, so it's better as its own change.
- A single commit whose changes alone pass 2 MiB (tens of thousands of files, e.g. a committed `node_modules`) can't be listed. The list stops just before it and sets `commitsTruncated`, and reading it directly returns `PR_COMMIT_TOO_LARGE`. The whole-PR Changes view still shows its files (capped at 5,000).
- The Workspace `…AtCommit` reads still rebuild `ListWorkspaceFiles` on each request and check the SHA against that list, now capped. That predates #5936 and is unchanged here.

## Testing

Run locally, following the CI workflows. The full suites ran before a rebase onto the current `main`; after it, build, vet, lint, api drift, typechecks and the full Go suite were rerun.

- **Go (`go.yml`)**: `gofmt` clean; `go build` and `go vet ./...` clean; golangci-lint v2.13.2: 0 issues. api-drift and sqlc-drift regenerate identically. `cloud/`: gofmt, build, vet and `go test -race` pass.
- **`go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...`** (after the rebase): 174 of 178 packages pass, including every package this touches. The 4 failures are in untouched packages that don't import the changed code:
  - `adapters/agent/claudecode` and `adapters/agent/fake`: pass when rerun alone.
  - `adapters/agent/goose` (`binary not found on PATH`) and `session_manager`'s claude-code subtests (`agent requires authentication`): fail the same way on a clean `upstream/main` checkout on this machine.
- **CLI e2e (`cli-e2e.yml`)**: `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...` passes.
- **Frontend (`frontend.yml`)**: `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, the cloud-client and product-ui checks, the docs build and the mac-update-helper steps pass. `npx vitest run`: 5405 passed; 5 failed under full-suite load (GlobalSettingsForm, ProjectSettingsForm, browser-history-store), and all 3 files pass when rerun alone (101/101). The only frontend change is two optional fields in the generated `schema.ts`.
- **Renderer smoke (`@T0|@P0`)**: 60/60 passed, run against the installed Google Chrome because Playwright's Chromium isn't downloaded here. Playwright still exited 1: a worker didn't exit within 300s after the run and was force-killed.
- Node 23.6.1 locally; CI pins 24.
- **Not run locally**: `windows-workspace` (needs Windows); the cli-e2e container job and gitleaks (need Docker). Left to CI.

New tests:
- **A 260-commit PR** built with `git fast-import`: the list holds the newest 250 with `commitsTruncated`. The oldest commit, past the cap, still opens (file and after-revision). `base`, a commit outside the PR, a short SHA, an uppercase SHA and `--output=<path>` all get `PR_COMMIT_NOT_FOUND`, and the path is never written.
- **A byte-cap sweep** over a 4-commit range, including commits whose `--numstat` output outgrows their `--name-status` output. At every cap the result is the newest commits, each identical to the uncapped read, and `truncated` is set exactly when some were left out. Commit caps of exactly 4 and of 3 are checked too.
- **The Workspace list** stops at 250 with `commitsTruncated`. Controller tests check the field on both responses.
- Each new test fails when its part of the fix is reverted: the numstat trim, the partial-commit drop, the ancestry check, the SHA format check, and the extra commit.

title: fix(prompts): forbid PR attachment during review-only tasks
body:
## Problem

The injected AO worker prompt tells workers to claim or attach an existing PR before continuing it, but it does not explicitly exclude review-only tasks.

This ambiguity caused a worker given a strict review-only task to run `ao session claim-pr`, mutating AO ownership metadata even though the task only authorized reading the PR and submitting a review.

## Source

The worker prompt is generated in `backend/internal/session_manager/prompt.go`.

Two instructions currently reinforce the ambiguous behavior:

1. The task-source rule says to attach when a task is to claim or continue an existing PR or MR.
2. The session-lifecycle rule says to claim or attach before continuing an existing PR.

Neither instruction states that reviewing a PR is not continuation.

## Required behavior

The injected worker prompt must explicitly state:

- If the task is review-only, do not claim or attach the PR or MR.
- Review-only workers should inspect the provider data and submit only the requested review.
- Claiming is reserved for implementation, CI recovery, review-comment follow-up, or other authorized work that continues or changes the PR.
- Explicit restrictions such as review-only take precedence over PR workflow defaults, including ownership metadata changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The generated worker prompt contains an explicit prohibition against `ao session claim-pr` for review-only tasks.
- Prompt tests assert that prohibition.
- Existing implementation and review-follow-up workflows still instruct workers to claim the PR before changing it.
- A review-only prompt regression test proves the worker is told to leave AO PR ownership metadata unchanged.

title: fix(files): remember the file display mode across session switches
body:
## What this fixes

A Markdown file switched to **Rich preview** in a centre file tab falls back to the normal file view after navigating to another session and back.

`FileContentPane` keeps the display mode in local state and resets it to `initialMode` whenever the pane remounts. `SessionView` keeps the tab and its open request across the switch, but `initialMode` records how the file was *opened*, not the Rich preview picked afterwards.

The fix keeps the toolbar pick in `ui-store`, next to the existing per-session Files state (`filesChangedOnly`, `filesSource`):

- `ui-store`: per-session `fileDisplayModes` (path → `{ mode, requestKey }`) with `setFileDisplayMode` and a `rememberedFileDisplayMode` selector.
- `FileContentPane`: an opt-in `rememberDisplayMode` prop that records the pick and restores it when the pane comes back for the **same open request**. Opening the file again, or asking for its diff, still uses that request's own mode.
- `SessionFileWorkspace` (centre tabs) opts in. The maximized Files panel numbers its requests separately, so it doesn't opt in and is unchanged.

One deliberate behavior change: `sessionId` is now part of the pane's reset effect. Before, the same path with the same request key in two sessions kept the pane's state across a switch, including an unsaved edit.

Closes #5984.

## Testing

- `FileContentPane.test.tsx`: mode restored after remount and after switching sessions and back; not shared across sessions; a new request picks its own mode; non-opted panes unchanged; no unsaved edit carried across sessions. These fail on current `main`.
- `SessionView.test.tsx`: a tree-opened file tab keeps the same open request across session navigation.
- `SessionFileWorkspace.test.tsx`, `ui-store.test.ts`: centre tabs opt in; the store matches on session, path, and request.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test`: 5,413 tests pass. (`browser-history-store` "caps entry count…" can time out under full load, taking ~10s of its 20s budget alone; it's unrelated and passes on re-run.)

## Notes

Out of scope, happy to follow up:
- `cloud-workspace/CloudFileContentPane` has the same pattern for cloud sessions.
- A file revealed from a review is re-opened in File view each time you return to its session (`SessionFileExplorer`'s `revealRequest` effect re-runs on session switch).



## Also fixed after first review(requested in review):
- Request keys now come from a process-wide counter, so after `SessionView` remounts (e.g. via the board) a new Open diff / Edit can never pick up a remembered Rich preview.
- A file opened from a chat/terminal link (a reveal) is now one-shot: it no longer reopens after being closed, or takes focus from the agent tab, when you return to the session. Files opened from the Files tree were never affected.

Out of scope, happy to follow up:
- `cloud-workspace/CloudFileContentPane` has the same local-mode pattern for cloud sessions.

title: fix(mobile): show live desktop status in settings and hide disconnect when unpaired
body:
## Summary

Settings' **Connected desktop** row said "Paired" whenever an address was saved. So once the desktop stopped answering, it still read as fine directly above a **Test connection** row reporting "Your desktop disconnected". **Disconnect from desktop** was also shown even with nothing paired.

- **Live status row.** Driven by the store's `configured` + `connection` + `errorStatus` instead of a separately loaded config. Labels: Set up / Connecting… / Connected / Offline / Password rejected / Locked out / Desktop error / Address changed. The rotated-tunnel case uses the same rule as the board.
- **Test connection re-races.** It calls `reloadConfig()` (every known endpoint) before pinging, instead of pinging only the last stored address. Afterwards it starts a poll in the background so the status row agrees, except after a rejection, where a second request would count toward the daemon's lockout. The spinner doesn't wait for that poll, which against a dead address would add another full request timeout.
- **Disconnect only while paired.** Keyed on the saved pairing, not the live connection, so an offline desktop can still be forgotten. Settings waits for the store's first resolve, so the row never pops in after first paint.
- **Failed disconnect is handled.** If `forgetServer()` throws, the config is re-resolved instead of an unhandled rejection leaving the screen stale. If the pairing survived, an alert asks to retry; if only leftovers failed, it carries on to onboarding rather than asking to retry from a row that has already disappeared.
- `reloadConfig` now returns the config it resolved. The label mapping is in a new pure module, `lib/desktopStatus.ts`.

## Tests

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npx vitest run`: 1275 tests passing, including the new `lib/desktopStatus.test.ts`, `lib/settings-connection.source.test.ts` and `lib/connectRuntime.test.ts`
- Checked in the iOS simulator: an unreachable pairing shows a red status instead of "Paired"; with nothing paired, the row shows "Set up" and Disconnect is hidden

## Follow-up

A store re-race already in flight when Disconnect is tapped can still `saveConfig()` the old endpoint after `clearConfig()`. It needs a generation guard and is out of scope here.

title: fix(mobile): improve drawer and settings responsiveness
body:
Code changes: +157 -38  
Tests: +133 -2  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Make the Android hamburger control reliably open the drawer on affected Pixel devices while preserving the smooth native drawer animation. Also remove avoidable Settings wait states and give the iOS Appearance selector enough width for its selected label.

## Why

The original fixed edge-swipe target could overlap the hamburger control on devices with tall status-bar or cutout insets. Physical Pixel testing then exposed a second React Native/Fabric failure mode: while the natively transformed content frame is settling, Android can deliver touch-down, touch-up, and the pressed visual state but omit `Pressable.onPress`.

That explains why the control looked pressed without opening and why the issue was more visible on some Android devices and during rapid close/reopen interactions.

The drawer also stayed logically open until its closing spring completed. A second swipe during that interval was therefore calculated from a fully open drawer even when the drawer was almost closed, which could snap it back open.

The Settings sheet had two separate wait sources unrelated to the hamburger changes:

- It reloaded configuration directly from AsyncStorage/SecureStore even though `AppProvider` had already resolved the same configuration, gating the entire sheet behind a spinner.
- Disconnect awaited the normal 12-second API timeout before clearing local pairing state when the desktop was unreachable.

The native iOS Appearance picker was hosted in a 96-point-wide container, which was too narrow for “System” plus the menu indicator and caused the label to wrap.

## How

- Start the closed-drawer edge-swipe target below the safe-area-adjusted header.
- Expand the hamburger hit target asymmetrically without overlapping the title.
- Preserve the native spring animation and hide its visible scrim immediately when closing starts.
- Delay the drawer's final closed interaction state until the spring settles.
- Allow either horizontal direction to interrupt a settling drawer, stop the spring, and continue the gesture from the drawer's live progress instead of assuming a fully open or closed endpoint.
- Add an Android-only guarded tap recovery path when Fabric omits `onPress`: it accepts only an uncancelled touch within tap movement tolerance and yields to the normal handler first, preventing duplicate activation.
- Render Settings from the configuration already held by `AppProvider`, retaining only its initial store-resolution guard rather than performing a second storage load.
- Limit the best-effort daemon unpair request to two seconds while preserving local cleanup ordering.
- Widen the iOS native Appearance picker host from 96 to 124 points.
- Add compatibility assertions for the gesture boundary, animation interruption, animation/scrim lifecycle, hit target, guarded fallback, Settings loading path, disconnect timeout, and Appearance width.

## Testing

- `cd packages/mobile && npm test` — 139 files, 1,285 tests passed
- `cd packages/mobile && npm run typecheck`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `git diff --check`
- Physical Pixel 9 / Android 17:
  - reproduced `press-in` / pressed UI / `press-out` without `onPress`
  - reproduced the failure while the closing native spring was still settling
  - verified the guarded fallback opens the drawer for that exact sequence
  - verified repeated normal and rapid open/close/reopen taps with the user
  - verified the enlarged target and rightward edge-swipe gesture
  - verified the dark scrim no longer lingers after close

## Validation gaps

- The new mid-spring swipe reversal is covered by focused gesture and source-boundary tests, but has not been rechecked on the physical Pixel because it is no longer connected.
- The installed iOS simulator development client is stale and fails before rendering with a missing native `RNGestureHandlerModule`, so the 124-point native picker width has automated source coverage but still needs a visual check in a current iOS build.
- `npm run lint`: backend tests reached an unrelated existing Codex app-server conformance failure because the locally installed provider declares newer protocol methods than this branch's generated fixture.
- `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --all`: cannot start without the repository secret `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused mobile responsiveness change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] All repository CI checks pass locally (see validation gaps above)

title: fix(settings): keep confirm dialogs above the settings surface
body:
## What broke

Turning on the Cloud toggle in Settings (General, under Developer mode) did nothing, while turning it off worked fine. This turned out to be the visible tip of a wider break: **anything that opens from inside the Settings dialog and portals to the page** was invisible, including

- every ConfirmDialog (global **and** project settings, same component): Cloud enable, browser profile delete, account removal
- every dropdown and select: Session Interface, terminal shell, theme, language
- every popover and tooltip

## Why

#5873 ("keep dialog above blurred backdrop") fixed the settings dialog rendering behind its own scrim by raising the dialog content to `z-[calc(var(--z-overlay)+1)]` (computed 51). #5944 then deduped the class list and kept that value.

Every popup in the app lives on the `z-overlay` layer (50) and portals after the settings dialog. With the settings surface at 51, each one painted under it: present in the DOM, visually buried, unusable. Enabling Cloud is confirm-gated and disabling is not, which is why the toggle looked dead in one direction only.

## The fix

One class change in `SettingsDialog.tsx`: the content drops back to `z-overlay` (50). It still paints above its own scrim because the content portals after the overlay and equal z-index ties break by DOM order, the same mechanism every other dialog in this app already uses (ConfirmDialog's box and scrim are both `z-overlay`). Confirms, dropdowns, and popovers opened from Settings portal later than the dialog, so they paint above it again.

## Tests

- `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`: the #5873 assertion now expects `z-overlay` and rejects the `+1` class, with a comment recording the invariant.
- New e2e `settings-cloud-confirm-stacking.spec.ts`: opens Settings, enables Developer mode, clicks Cloud, and asserts the stacking rule itself, computed z-index plus DOM order. Plain visibility and click checks cannot catch this class of bug: Radix marks the covered background `pointer-events: none`, so an occluded confirm still has size and still receives synthetic clicks. Verified the spec fails on unfixed code (`{"settingsZ":"51","confirmZ":"50"}`) and passes after the change.
- Full `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` suite: 15 passed. Frontend typecheck: clean. Manually verified in the Electron dev app: the confirm now opens above Settings and Enable Cloud flips the toggle.

## Risk

Low. One class on one element. The remaining `+N` layers in the renderer are the global toast (51, intentional: notifications float above dialogs) and a transient notice inside the keyboard shortcuts dialog (52). Anything else on the `z-overlay` layer resolves against the settings dialog by portal order, same as before #5873 for every case except the scrim bug it fixed.

title: feat(cloud): keep sessions warm through idle (no VM teardown)
body:
## What

Makes a cloud session behave like a local one *after* it has spawned: it no longer tears the sandbox VM down on idle, so the worker stays connected and the terminal never has to cold-boot / reconnect under a new `worker_epoch` on resume. Initial spawn/boot is unchanged.

Gated by one knob — **`AO_CLOUD_IDLE_PAUSE_THRESHOLD=0` = keep-warm (idle-pause disabled)**. `0` was previously rejected; it now means "disabled." The default stays `1h`, so **merging this changes nothing unless the env var is set to `0`** — it's opt-in, default-off, zero-regression.

## How (3 touch-points, all in `cloud/`)

1. **`config.go`** — allow `IdlePauseThreshold == 0` (was `>= 1m` only); add `Config.IdlePauseDisabled()` helper.
2. **`cmd/ao-cloud/main.go`** — don't start the idle-pause scanner when disabled (so AO never marks a session paused — covers **all** providers), and pass `KeepWarm: cfg.IdlePauseDisabled()` into the reconciler.
3. **`reconcile/reconciler.go`** — new `Options.KeepWarm`: when set, the reconciler keeps extending the provider deadline (e.g. Coder's autostop) even for an idle session, and refuses to *accept* a provider external-idle stop (restores instead). With the scanner off + the deadline kept alive, a session is never paused for idleness.

Net effect when enabled: VM stays up through idle → worker stays connected → `worker_epoch` never bumps → the terminal never resets → typing/reconnect is instant, matching local.

## Trade-off

Continuous compute for every non-terminated session while enabled. A long *non-zero* threshold (e.g. `12h`) remains available as a backstop instead of pure never-pause. No Coder template change required (AO controls the workspace lifetime via the deadline it extends).

## Testing

- `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean; new reconcile tests: `TestKeepWarmExtendsIdleCoderDeadline`, `TestKeepWarmRestoresIdleStoppedCoderWorkspace`; config `0`-threshold validation covered.
- **Deployed + verified on staging** (control-plane td:157→160, `AO_CLOUD_IDLE_PAUSE_THRESHOLD=0`): idle-pause scanner confirmed not started, clean boot, sessions stayed warm through idle with no terminal reconnect.
- No migrations.


## Problem / fix

Tracker intake starts one worker session per eligible issue with nothing bounding how many run at once, so enabling it on a project with N matching open issues starts N agents inside a single one-minute tick. A user hit this with 5 assigned issues: all 5 sessions ran lint and the Go test suite simultaneously and capped the machine's CPU, and killing the sessions did not help, because `seenIssueIDs` counts only live sessions, so a terminated session frees its issue for the very next poll. The only escape was disabling intake on the project.

`AO_TRACKER_INTAKE` moves that decision to whoever runs the daemon, defaulting off. A project's own `trackerIntake.enabled` no longer does anything on its own. Rollback is `AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on`, not a revert.

Gated off, the observer is never constructed and `startTrackerIntake` returns a nil channel, which the shutdown await in `lifecycle_wiring.go:170` already nil-guards. It does still read the project list once at boot, to report how many projects hold an enabled-but-inert config. That scan gates nothing, because a boot-time scan deciding whether to start the loop is the regression covered by `TestStartTrackerIntake_RunsEvenWithoutEnabledProjects`.

`TrackerIntakeConfig`, the settings UI, the adapters and the OpenAPI schema are untouched, so the in-flight multi-provider intake work in https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4655 and https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4635 keeps applying cleanly. The `--tracker-intake` CLI help string is updated, because it claimed the flag enables intake and that is the command the corrected docs send readers to.

Context: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2344 and https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3921. This fixes neither; it stops the unbounded spawner running by default while they are worked.

## Validation

Screenshots do not apply, this is daemon-side. Proven by running the real `ao daemon` binary against an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` under `~/.ao`, on a project whose stored config the daemon itself reported as `{"trackerIntake":{"enabled":true,"assignee":"..."}}`.

Gated off, 3m28s of uptime across three tick windows produced zero intake polls, and `ao session ls` returned `(no active sessions)`:

```
level=WARN msg="tracker intake: gated off, set AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on to enable" projectsWithIntakeEnabled=1
```

The escalation is conditional, not unconditional. With no projects, and with a project whose intake was cleared, the same boot logs `level=INFO` with no count attribute.

Negative control, so the silence above means something. With `AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on`, the same project polled about 1s after boot and then every 60s:

```
23:40:15.692 level=ERROR msg="tracker intake: list issues failed" project=verifygate err="github tracker: issue not found: Not Found"
23:41:15.694 level=DEBUG msg="tracker intake: project in failure backoff" project=verifygate
23:42:15.695 level=DEBUG msg="tracker intake: project in failure backoff" project=verifygate
```

`tracker intake: list issues failed` has exactly one emitter, `observe/trackerintake/observer.go:188` inside `pollProject`, so it cannot come from anywhere but a real poll. The project origin pointed at a repository that does not exist, deliberately, so the credentialed spawn path was never exercised and no session was ever spawned.

A malformed value fails closed and names the variable, binding no port and writing no run file:

```
$ AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=maybe ao daemon
AO_TRACKER_INTAKE must be off|on
EXIT=1
```

Every gated-off run shut down with `msg="daemon stopped cleanly"`, which also demonstrates the nil channel does not hang the shutdown await.

Reproduction. The daemon has to be running before a project can be registered against it, and the boot log is only observable on a restart, so the order matters:

```bash
cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao-gate ./cmd/ao
export AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/verify-intake-gate/data
export AO_RUN_FILE=~/.ao/verify-intake-gate/running.json
export AO_PORT=3457

# 1. daemon first, then register the project against it
env -u AO_TRACKER_INTAKE /tmp/ao-gate daemon 2> setup.err &
/tmp/ao-gate project add --path <a-repo> --id verifygate --name "verify gate"
/tmp/ao-gate project set-config verifygate --tracker-intake --tracker-assignee <user>
/tmp/ao-gate stop

# 2. restart gated off: expect the WARN with a count, and no polls
env -u AO_TRACKER_INTAKE /tmp/ao-gate daemon 2> off.err &
sleep 95 && grep -iE "tracker intake" off.err && /tmp/ao-gate stop

# 3. negative control: expect a poll ~1s in, then every 60s
AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on /tmp/ao-gate daemon 2> on.err &
sleep 80 && grep -iE "tracker intake" on.err && /tmp/ao-gate stop

# 4. malformed value
AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=maybe /tmp/ao-gate daemon; echo "EXIT=$?"
```

Static checks, all run at this branch tip:

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | `go build ./...` | clean |
| Vet | `go vet ./internal/config/... ./internal/daemon/...` | clean |
| Lint | `golangci-lint run ./internal/config/... ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/cli/...` (v2.13.2, CI's pin) | 0 issues |
| Race tests | `go test -race ./internal/config/... ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/observe/trackerintake/...` | pass |
| CI | all 15 checks | pass |

Two honesty notes on the checks. The locally installed `golangci-lint` v2.12.2 refuses this module, since it is built with go1.26 and the module targets go1.27.1, so the result above comes from CI's pinned v2.13.2 installed to a temp GOBIN. And a full `go test ./...` run on the backend produced one failure, `TestACPReplayLoadLargeHistoryThroughSDK` in `internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp`, with `notification queue overflow` at `capacity=1024 queued=1024`. It passes in isolation and that package imports neither `internal/config` nor `internal/daemon`, so it is a load test starved under whole-suite parallelism rather than anything from this change. CI's `test` job is green.

New tests: `TestLoadTrackerIntakeToggle` covers all eight values `parseToggleEnv` accepts (`on|true|1|yes` and `off|false|0|no`) as subtests, with the default and a malformed value as two separate tests. `TestStartTrackerIntake_GatedOff` covers the nil channel, the INFO-versus-WARN escalation, and that the reported count tracks the real number of stranded projects rather than a hardcoded 1. I confirmed the gate test can fail by temporarily replacing `if !enabled` with `if false`, which fails.

## Known gaps

The boot log is not a sufficient operator signal, and I want to be precise about what it does and does not buy. It fires once, at `startTrackerIntake`. If you enable intake on an already-running gated-off daemon, which is what the settings UI and the documented CLI recipe both do, you get no warning at all until the next restart. Verified: enabling intake against a live gated-off daemon produced no further intake log lines for the rest of that process's life.

That compounds the real gap, which is that the settings UI still offers an intake toggle that now does nothing on its own, and the gate reaches no API surface so the renderer cannot say so. The precedent for fixing it is `settingssvc.OfferingFromConfig`, which already carries `AO_LOCAL_OFFERING` to `GET /settings`. Deliberately out of this PR to keep it reviewable; filing a follow-up, and the right fix there is a signal at config-set time plus a UI notice, not a louder boot log.

Gated off is now the only path doing synchronous DB work at boot, which is backwards relative to the observer's own non-blocking-startup rationale. Measured at 1.3ms for 25 projects and 10.3ms for 5000, so not a readiness-budget risk. Left as is rather than adding a goroutine for a log line.

The `must be off|on` error understates the accepted vocabulary. Pre-existing and shared with four sibling variables, so not changed here.

Unexercised: the credentialed spawn path, so this PR does not demonstrate the unbounded-concurrency behavior it mitigates, only that the observer no longer runs. The `projectScanErr` branch has no test and no reproducible trigger against a healthy store. macOS only. The Electron renderer was never launched, so the stale toggle above is a read-level finding.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode 2 TUI rejects the --model and --agent flags that AO passes at launch
body:
### What went wrong?

OpenCode 2 rejects the `--model` and `--agent` flags that Agent Orchestrator's OpenCode launch command uses:

```
$ opencode --model opencode/big-pickle
DESCRIPTION
  OpenCode command line interface
...
ERROR
  Unrecognized flag: --model in command opencode

$ opencode --agent ao-test
ERROR
  Unrecognized flag: --agent in command opencode
```

Both exit with status 1. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--auto` are still accepted.

I found this while investigating #6009 on my machine. I have **not** tested an actual Agent Orchestrator spawn with OpenCode 2, so I do not know whether it fails in the same way — I only observed the CLI rejecting the flags.

- Agent Orchestrator 0.13.1 (AppImage)
- OpenCode `opencode v2.0.16` at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`
- Aurora (Kinoite) 44, kernel 7.1.8-200.fc44.x86_64

title: [Bug]: OpenCode 2 does not load V1-API plugins, so AO's activity plugin cannot run
body:
### What went wrong?

OpenCode 2 does not load plugins written against the OpenCode 1 plugin API. On this machine, OpenCode 2 logs:

```
level=WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=/var/home/chris/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-loop.ts
  cause="PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function. (cause: SchemaError(Expected object at [\"default\"]))"
```

and the TUI status line shows `1 plugin failed`.

OpenCode's own V2 migration guide lists the plugin API as one of three intentional breaking changes and states that V1 plugin implementations do not run in V2: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1

Agent Orchestrator installs an OpenCode plugin of its own at `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/assets/ao-activity.ts`, written against the V1 `@opencode-ai/plugin` API:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"

export const aoActivity: Plugin = async ({ directory, client }) => {
```

I found this while investigating #6009. I have not run an OpenCode session under Agent Orchestrator with OpenCode 2, so I do not know how much of AO's session tracking is affected in practice.

title: fix(chat): label the merged recommended model with its version
body:
Fixes #5989

## Problem

The Claude Code chat model picker (orchestrator chat composer) had **no Opus 5.5 row**, while `Opus 5`, `Opus 4.8` and older versions all appeared as explicit rows — so Opus 5 read as the newest Opus available. Settings pickers, which read AO's provider catalog, showed "Claude Opus 5.5" at the same time.

Verified live against the reporter's session (`claude` 2.1.280, Windows). The ACP model option is:

```
["default","Default (recommended)","Opus"]
["opus","Opus","Opus 5.5 · Best for everyday, complex tasks · ~2× usage vs Sonnet"]
["sonnet","Sonnet","Sonnet 5 · Efficient for routine tasks"]
["claude-opus-5","Opus 5","Newer version available · select Opus for Opus 5.5"]
...
```

Claude Code names the newest model of a family with the bare family alias and carries the version only in the description; older pinned IDs keep versioned names. `resolveImplicitChoice` (`TurnSettingsBar.tsx`) merges that alias into the implicit `default` row so two rows don't select the same model — correct — but labelled the merged row `concrete.name`, i.e. "Opus". That discarded the only place "Opus 5.5" was visible, because descriptions surface only as a hover `title`.

## Fix

Add `concreteChoiceLabel()`: take the label from the description's leading segment (before ` · `) when it is a version-qualified form of the same name. The merged row now reads **"Opus 5.5"**, and **"Use agent model (Opus 5.5)"** when the alias is explicitly pinned. Wire values are unchanged — the row still sends `default`, so "follow the provider" behaviour is preserved, and the label tracks whatever the provider's newest version becomes.

The guard is deliberately narrow: the description segment must begin with the choice name plus a space. A prose description ("Best for everyday, complex tasks") falls back to the family name, so non-Claude harnesses are unaffected.

## Tests

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/TurnSettingsBar.test.tsx` — three cases built from the real ACP payload above:
- merged row is labelled "Opus 5.5", coexists with the distinct "Opus 5" row, and still sends `default`
- pinned alias offers "Use agent model (Opus 5.5)"
- prose description keeps the family name

Verified these fail without the change (2 failures) and pass with it.

```
vitest run TurnSettingsBar.test.tsx   →  94 passed
npm run typecheck                     →  clean
```

Backend untouched.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Label is derived from a provider-supplied description. The narrow prefix guard means an unexpected format degrades to today's behaviour rather than producing a wrong label.
- Overlaps in spirit with #5834 (resolve vague "Default" labels to concrete values) and PR #4923 (family/version picker); this is the minimal targeted fix for the missing row and does not pre-empt either.
- **Not addressed here** (separate bug, found in the same investigation): the new-task composer's remembered per-agent model in `localStorage` (`ao.taskComposer.preferences.v1`) overrides the project role model at `TaskComposer.tsx:435`, so workers can launch on a stale model — e.g. `claude-opus-5` — regardless of the project setting. Worth its own issue.

title: feat(agent): add DeepSeek Harness adapter with ACP chat
body:
Code changes: +726 -60
Tests: +951 -10
Others: +105 -13

## What

Add a DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) adapter under the `deepseek-harness` harness id, with an ACP Chat driver, a headless terminal launch, model discovery from the session's own catalog, and the install/auth/docs/product-UI wiring every shipped harness carries.

## Why

AO could already run headless DeepSeek Harness tasks, but a previous attempt at this adapter (#4058) was closed as stale before it landed a Chat binding. DeepSeek Harness now ships an automation-only ACP v1 stdio server (`dsh --profile acp`), so AO can drive it with the same reusable transport it already uses for OpenCode, Cline, Kimi, and others instead of scraping a terminal.

Fixes #6039.

## How

**Harness identity.** `domain.HarnessDeepSeek` is `deepseek-harness`, matching the id the earlier attempt used so project config and stored rows stay compatible. Migration `0166` widens the `sessions.harness` CHECK for both current constraint variants, and `reconcileSchema`'s harness repair also learns the new harness: a database that skipped an earlier harness migration matches neither exact string (migrations run before that repair), so the repair is what widens it. `usage_bindings` keeps its deliberately narrower harness set, as prior harness migrations left it.

**Terminal launch** is one headless task per session, `dsh --profile headless <task>`, the same shape the earlier attempt chose. The headless profile takes no model or effort flag, and a task of exactly `-` makes Harness read stdin, so AO rejects that literal rather than blocking until the supervisor kills it. There is no system-prompt or hook surface, so standing instructions are not injected for terminal sessions.

**Chat** is the complete path and launches `dsh --profile acp`. Model and reasoning effort arrive as ACP config options. Model values are opaque — Harness encodes each as a JSON array string such as `["deepseek-official","deepseek-v4-flash"]` — so AO passes the advertised value back unchanged. AO's effort vocabulary is mapped onto the four levels Harness offers (`off`, `low`, `high`, `max`), because a project-level effort configured for another harness would otherwise fail every Harness session.

**Model discovery** reads the ACP session catalog rather than the CLI listing. The `Discoverer.ClineOptions` field became `Discoverer.ACPOptions`, a map keyed by harness, so both Cline and DeepSeek Harness use it while each supplies its own command line. This is deliberate: for OpenCode the picker and the session read different catalogs and the picker offers models the session rejects (#6012). Project-scoped reads use the project directory; project-free reads use a private AO-owned directory under the configured data root, so models are available before a project is registered.

**Activity**: Harness has no workspace hook file to merge into, so the adapter installs no hooks and registers no activity deriver; Chat activity arrives through the ACP stream. That also means terminal sessions report no activity signals.

## Rebase note

Rebased onto `main` after #5893 added the MiMo Code harness, which touches the same lists. Every shared enumeration now carries both harnesses: the domain constants and `AllHarnesses`, the agent and Chat registries, the model-catalog entry mode, the API `harness`/`agent` enums, the install targets and their job enum, the agent-auth and install plan tables, the product-UI options/labels, the avatar map, and the CLI/skill docs. Migration numbering moved to `0166` because MiMo Code took `0165`, and this migration's exact constraint strings were regenerated from the post-`0165` schema rather than the pre-MiMo one.

## Intentional omissions

- **No reviewer binding.** Harnesses opt into the reviewer registry separately, and the preceding harnesses (Gemini, fx, MiMo Code) added none.
- **No logo work beyond the shipped asset.** The asset is the one produced by the earlier attempt, so the avatar renders the real mark rather than a fallback initial.
- **No `dsh` install beyond npm.** One Node CLI boots every profile, so npm is the only method offered.

## Testing

Backend, on this checkout (Linux, Go 1.27.1):

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` — clean
- `go test ./...` — passes except two failures that also fail on `main` here, because both assert against the *locally installed* provider CLIs: `TestOpenCodeCredentialScopeListsProviderModels` (this machine's OpenCode 2 lists no `anthropic/*` models under that credential scope) and `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` (the installed Codex provider declares methods the generated protocol lacks). Neither touches the files in this change.
- `go test -race -count=1` for every touched package — clean
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2` — 0 issues

Against the real runtime, not a fixture:

- `AO_LIVE_DEEPSEEK=1 go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/deepseekharnessacp/ -run Live` drives the installed `dsh` through AO's own ACP client and asserts the session advertises the model select (with JSON-array values) and the four `reasoning_effort` levels.
- A daemon built from this branch, run headlessly against a scratch data directory, lists 32 supported harnesses including both `deepseek-harness` and `mimo-code`, reports DeepSeek Harness installed and authorized, applies migration 0166 so the sessions constraint admits both harnesses, and discovers three models with `source: acp` for a registered project: `deepseek-v4-flash` (default), `DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, and `DeepSeek-V41-Flash`.

Frontend:

- `npm run typecheck` — clean. This caught a real gap: the install-job `target` enum is a hand-written tag in `systeminstall`, not derived from the target list, so it also needed the new harness.
- `packages/product-ui`: `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (133 tests) — clean.
- `npm test`: 5299 passed, 7 skipped. Two files could not run in this environment — `src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts` and `src/main/provider-auth-flow.test.ts` — because the `electron` package's binary was never downloaded here (`node_modules/electron/path.txt` is absent, so importing `electron` throws `Electron failed to install correctly`). Both are Electron main-process tests that do not import anything this change touches, so they are left to CI rather than claimed as locally passed.

Not verified: an actual AO session started against a real DeepSeek Harness project from the desktop app. The transport is exercised end to end above, but the first real task run is the remaining gap.

title: fix(status): separate unresolved review comments from formal changes-requested
body:
Code changes: +67 -28  
Tests: +83 -3  
Others: +20 -2 (generated openapi.yaml/schema.ts, i18n locale strings)

## Summary

Fixes #5765. A pull request's unresolved comment thread from a GitHub `COMMENTED` review (`pr.ReviewComments`) was mapped to the same `StatusChangesRequested` as a formal `CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision (`backend/pkg/contract/status.go`, `prPipelineStatus`). Combined with agent activity taking precedence over SCM status in `DeriveStatus`, this produced the reported flicker:

```
Idle · Changes Requested
        ↓ agent starts working
Working                              <- feedback silently disappears
        ↓ agent becomes idle, comment still unresolved
Idle · Changes Requested             <- reappears, still mislabeled
```

- **`Changes Requested` is now reserved for a formal provider decision.** `prPipelineStatus` no longer folds `pr.ReviewComments` into `StatusChangesRequested`; a new `StatusCommented` ("commented") status covers the non-blocking-comment case, threaded through the domain layer, OpenAPI enum, `product-ui` presentation (styles/zone/timeline pill), and all 8 locale catalogs. Named "Commented" to match the wording the repo already uses for this exact concept (`displayStatus.commented`, `inspector.review.commented`), rather than inventing a second phrase.
- **The feedback indicator survives agent activity.** `SessionInspector`'s `scmTimelineStates` now reads the raw `pr.reviewComments` fact directly (already shipped to the frontend independent of `session.status`) instead of relying on the activity-collapsed session status, so the "Commented" pill renders concurrently with "Working", not just while idle. Gated on the PR still being open, so a stale comment on a merged/closed PR can't keep the pill around.
- Blocked stacked-PR children with only unresolved comments still surface (added to `isActionableChildSignal`), matching the existing "problem signals surface through a blocked stack" behavior for CI/draft/changes-requested.
- `packages/mobile`'s `attentionOf`/`statusVisual`/`workerStatusGlyph` now handle `commented` the same way they handle `changes_requested`, so the phone board keeps flagging these sessions for attention instead of silently downgrading them to "working" (`orchestratorView.ts`'s blocker surfacing derives through `attentionOf`, so it's covered by the same fix).

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./pkg/contract/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/service/session/... ./internal/httpd/...` — added backend coverage for `review_required + reviewComments=true` no longer deriving `changes_requested`, and for the blocked-stacked-child case.
- [x] `npm --prefix packages/product-ui run typecheck && npm --prefix packages/product-ui test` — 133 passing, including the widened `SessionStatus`/`AttentionZone`/pill exhaustive maps.
- [x] `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` and targeted `vitest run` on `SessionInspector.test.tsx` / i18n coverage — regression tests for: unresolved comments + `activity: active` renders "Commented" (not "Changes Requested"); a merged PR with a stale unresolved comment does not show "Commented".
- [x] `npm --prefix packages/mobile run typecheck && npm --prefix packages/mobile test` — 1247 passing, including new cases for `attentionOf`, `statusVisual`, `workerStatusGlyph`, and `projectBlockerLine` on the `commented` status.
- [x] Regenerated `openapi.yaml` + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` via `npm run api` and committed together, per the code-first API contract.
- [x] Full frontend `vitest run` (5253 passed) and full backend `go test ./...`; the only failures (`session_manager` PATH-pinning warning, `terminal` attachment timing) reproduce identically on the unmodified base branch, confirmed via `git stash` — pre-existing environment flakiness, unrelated to this change.

## Known follow-ups (out of scope here)

- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/pr-display.ts:180` has the same `changes_requested`/`hasUnresolvedHumanComments` conflation in PR card presentation (not named in the issue). Left untouched to keep this change scoped to the two files #5765 calls out; tracking as a follow-up rather than widening this PR.
- `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` (`SessionStatus`) and `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` don't yet declare `commented`. `cloud/internal/domain/types.go`'s `Session.Status` derives through the same `contract.DeriveStatus`, so once `cloud/go.mod`'s backend pin is bumped past this change, the cloud API can emit `commented` while its hand-maintained contract still lists the old enum (`npm run cloud:check` regenerates TS from that YAML, not from the backend, so it won't catch the drift). Needs a coordinated follow-up when the pin is bumped.

title: fix(settings): hide the intake section when the daemon gate is off
body:
```
Code changes: +55 -24
Tests: +129 -3
Others: +4 -0 (generated openapi.yaml + schema.ts)
```

> Stacked on https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6008, which adds `AO_TRACKER_INTAKE`. Base that first; this branch targets `fix/gate-tracker-intake`, so the diff here is only the UI change.

## Problem / fix

With the gate from #6008 off, project settings still offered "Enable issue intake", subtitled "Auto-spawn worker sessions from matching tracker issues". Ticking it saved, read back correctly, and spawned nothing, with no signal anywhere a desktop user could see. The create-project sheet had the same control. The gate reached no API surface, so the renderer could not have warned even if it wanted to.

The section is now hidden rather than disabled with an explanation. A control the daemon will ignore is noise, not something to explain, and it matches the existing precedent where scratch projects omit intake entirely. It needs no copy change either: the existing strings are true whenever the section is visible, so the eight locale files and `renderer-coverage.test.ts` are untouched.

`cfg.TrackerIntake` now travels through `settings.Offering` and out of `GET /api/v1/settings` as `trackerIntakeEnabled`, the same route `AO_LOCAL_OFFERING` already takes.

Three things that were easy to get wrong, each with a test:

Intake validation is gated on visibility, not just project kind. A project configured through the CLI can hold enabled-without-assignee; with the section hidden that cannot be corrected, so it must not block an unrelated save behind an error with no control to fix it.

The create sheet submits no `trackerIntake` at all when hidden, rather than an empty object, so creation cannot persist config the user was never offered.

A stored config survives a save made while hidden, so turning the gate back on restores what the user had.

## Before / after

Project settings, same project, gate off in both. Before, the Issues section offers a toggle that saves and then does nothing. After, Worktrees runs straight into Pull requests.

**Before**

![Project settings showing the Issues section with an Enable issue intake toggle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/assets/pr-6023-screenshots/docs-assets/pr-6023-before.png)

**After**

![Project settings with no Issues section, Worktrees followed directly by Pull requests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/assets/pr-6023-screenshots/docs-assets/pr-6023-after.png)

## Validation

Driven in the real desktop app from this branch, against an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` under `~/.ao`, not `dev:web` or mock data.

Gated off, the live daemon reports the new field, where on the previous build it did not exist at all:

```
"localEnabled": true,
"cloudEnabled": false,
"trackerIntakeEnabled": false
```

In the window, project settings for a real registered project renders Worktrees straight through to Pull requests with no Issues section between them, and no "Enable issue intake" control.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run frontend:typecheck` | clean |
| Go build | `go build ./...` | clean |
| Go lint | `golangci-lint run ./internal/service/settings/... ./internal/httpd/...` (v2.13.2, CI's pin) | 0 issues |
| Go tests | `go test ./internal/service/settings/... ./internal/httpd/...` | pass |
| ProjectSettingsForm | `vitest run src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx` | 54/54 |
| CreateProjectAgentSheet | `vitest run src/renderer/components/CreateProjectAgentSheet.test.tsx` | 22/22 |
| Sidebar | `vitest run src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx` | 129/129 |

Two honesty notes. My first typecheck reported 25 errors that were entirely missing `packages/product-ui` deps, not this change; CI installs the workspace packages separately and the real run is clean. And a full `vitest run` locally shows 22 failures in `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which fail identically on the base branch because `better_sqlite3.node` will not load against this Node ABI. That file is untouched here and CI is green on it.

`Sidebar.test.tsx` needed the same hook mock the other two suites now carry. Its `apiClient` mock has no case for `/api/v1/settings`, so the real hook threw on the undefined result and retried five times per its own `retry: 5`, and those extra render cycles shifted when the agent catalog resolved, failing three unrelated agent-dropdown assertions. Caught by running the suite on the base branch to separate mine from inherited.

## Scope

This hides a control; it does not add a second enforcement point. The daemon-side gate in #6008 is what stops intake, and it is boot-only and immutable at runtime: `AO_TRACKER_INTAKE` is read solely by `config.Load`, `Offering` is assigned once in `New` with no setter, and there is deliberately no PATCH route for it.

`ao spawn --issue` and `POST /api/v1/sessions` with an `issueId` remain ungated, deliberately. Those are explicit requests to work one named issue, which is a different thing from a poll loop draining a backlog unprompted, and gating them would break the documented way a person works an issue.

## Known gaps

Three test suites now carry a near-identical `useSettings` mock, and any future suite rendering project settings or the create sheet will hit the same trap. The right home is shared test setup, but a global mock touches all 345 test files, which is too wide to bundle into a change at this tier.

Not exercised: the create-project sheet in the real window (covered by unit tests only), and the gate-on state was verified via the API and unit tests rather than a second live launch at the time of writing.

title: fix(review): reviewers override inherited shell-hygiene rules; add review submit --body-file
body:
Fixes #6021

**Stacked on #5904** — merge that first; this PR then shrinks to its own two commits. Against `main` the diff shows the single-submit contract plus this follow-up, because the follow-up patches that contract.

## What this adds on top of #5904

1. **Headless reviewers must override inherited shell-hygiene rules.** The reviewer system prompt now states plainly: you run unattended — no human in this session to approve anything; the exact submit shape is allow-listed by AO's permission hook and never prompts anyone; any global rules against long multiline inline shell arguments or heredocs do not apply in this sandbox — emit the submit command exactly as the task shows, and do not stage files or route around it. Evidence for why this is needed: session `585ec38e` (analysis in #6021) — a reviewer fully composed a ~20 KB review in thinking, then refused to attempt the sanctioned printf shape because its inherited operator rules discourage multiline inline arguments, tried to stage a file first, and the generator collapsed to a literal `PLACEHOLDER`; ~300 no-op calls, zero submits.
2. **`ao review submit --body-file <path>`** for operators and scripts, mutually exclusive with `--body`. Reviewers keep the stdin-only path: their sandbox has no write tools, so nobody can stage a file for them. This is the gh `--body-file` / git `-F` convention, applied to the one actor that can actually create a file — a human.

## What stays open for upstream

#6021's core ask — a single-submission channel that does not require the model to emit a multi-KB body as one shell argument — is a design decision this PR deliberately does not make. Candidates recorded in the issue: a structured submission tool whose `body` field carries the complete review in one call (no shell quoting anywhere), or any other shape preserving the single-submission invariant (piecewise/chunked assembly protocols are ruled out there). The emission ceiling that motivates the ask is unmeasured: somewhere between 2 KB (hundreds of small commands succeeded in the failing session) and 20 KB (the observed collapse, which happened on a heredoc — the sanctioned printf shape was never reached).

## Test plan

- `internal/cli`: `--body-file` happy path (file bytes verbatim — quotes, apostrophes, code fences survive), mutual exclusion with `--body`, missing file → clear usage error, the `--body <path>` obsolete-input message now points at `--body-file`
- `internal/review`: system prompt asserts the override text
- `gofmt -l .` clean on the whole backend module; `go build ./...` ok; `go test` green on `internal/cli` and `internal/review`

title: fix(chat): stop ACP replay overflow from falsely marking sessions Exited
body:
Code changes: +245 -11  
Tests: +402 -0  
Others: +6 -0 (ADR note)

Fixes #5790

## Root cause

Reproduced against the real detached chat host with a fake ACP provider. `TestPersistentACPRealHostReplayBurstSurvivesReattachment` fails on `main`.

1. The daemon restarts or updates while a Chat turn is running. The persistent host keeps the agent alive and journals everything it outputs.
2. On startup, the replacement daemon reattaches (claiming a new controller generation) and opens the reader. It does this before the controller is published and before anything drains events.
3. The host replays the whole journal in one burst. Past about 5k `session/update` notifications (a 4096-event buffer plus the SDK's 1024-slot queue), acp-go-sdk logs `failed to queue notification; closing connection` and shuts the connection down. AO never closes its side, so the host still sees an attached socket.
4. The controller treats the stream end as provider death and writes `chat.controller.stopped` → `ActivityExited` under the new generation. The sticky-exit guard then keeps the row Exited while the agent keeps running.

This matches every fact in the issue: the exit ~0.6s after startup, fenced to the replacement generation; the host and provider still alive; the established attachment; no provider events persisted; and busy sessions across harnesses affected.

## Changes

- **ACP read backpressure** (`acp/legacy.go`): at most 512 `session/update` notifications are handed to the SDK before one has been handled. A replay burst now waits in the socket instead of overflowing the SDK queue. A 2s stall bound falls back to the old behaviour if a release is ever lost, so the connection cannot deadlock.
- **Heal rows already stuck as Exited** (`session_manager/manager.go`): on daemon start, a durably Exited Chat session is reattached only when its persistent host is demonstrably alive (`persistenthost.Alive`: live PID behind the descriptor). The reattach uses a live-only start (`ChatControllerStart.RequireLiveReconnect`). It refuses before claiming ownership and destroys anything the driver opened in place of a vanished host (`ErrChatProviderNotLive`), so it never launches or natively resumes a provider. A dead or unverifiable host leaves the row Exited for an explicit Resume Agent. Explicit Exit Agent terminates the host, so a live host behind an Exited row can only be a false exit. This also closes a gap on `main`: reconcile used to relaunch *every* non-terminated Chat row, including genuinely Exited ones.
- **Stale-exit clearing:** a live reconnect clears a durable Exited back to idle, or to active if a running turn was adopted. It uses a current-generation, revision-fenced activity signal.
- **Attribution logs:** the controller-stream exit and the failed-relaunch exit are both logged with their generation. The SDK's overflow error was already routed to the daemon log.

Once this ships, a plain daemon restart heals the currently stuck sessions whose hosts are alive, without restarting their work.

## Tests

Each new test fails on `main`:
- `acp`: `TestPersistentACPLiveReconnectReplayBurstKeepsConnection` (pipe transport) and `TestPersistentACPRealHostReplayBurstSurvivesReattachment` (real detached host: mid-turn detach, journal replay, turn completes after reattach).
- `persistenthost`: `TestAliveDistinguishesLiveDeadAndUnknownHosts`.
- `service/chat`: `TestLiveReconnectClearsStaleExitedActivity` and `TestRequireLiveReconnectRefusesReplacementProvider`.
- `session_manager`: `TestReconcileLive_ExitedChatSessionHealsOnlyWithLiveProviderHost` covers a live host (heals via a live-only start), a host that dies mid-heal, a dead host, and an unverifiable host. In the last three cases the row stays Exited, with no relaunch and no runtime, workspace or lifecycle side effects.

Local validation (macOS arm64):
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2: 0 issues.
- Focused `-race` runs pass for `acp`, `persistenthost`, `service/chat`, `lifecycle`, `session_manager` and `daemon`.
- Full `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (with the AO worker's `AO_*` env unset) passes except two tests in untouched packages:
  - `codexappserver/TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` compares against the locally installed `codex` and fails identically on `main`.
  - `goose/TestResolveGooseBinaryUsesValidFallbackAfterPathCollision` hits a ~2s probe budget under full-suite load; it passes in isolation.

## Intentionally left out

Defense-in-depth layers were considered and left out to keep this PR minimal:
- Gating every controller stream end on host liveness.
- Automatic reattach after such a stream end.
- Keeping a failed startup relaunch out of Exited while its host lives.

No observed occurrence requires them once backpressure is in place. The Codex app-server reader has no equivalent backpressure. It could get a similar treatment separately if it is ever implicated.

title: feat(modelcatalog): order Claude models newest-first by family
body:
Code changes: +591 -44  
Tests: +783 -19  
Others: +72 -0 (generated OpenAPI/sqlc/TypeScript and translations)

## Summary

Orders model pickers newest-first by version and puts the models the user ran most recently first.

### Claude ordering (`SortClaudeNewestFirst`)

- Sorts by the model version parsed from the ID, or from the label when the ID has none: Fable 5.1 → Fable 5 → Opus 4.8 → …. Family does not decide the order; unknown families also sort by version.
- Same version: newer release date first (provider `created_at`, else the snapshot date in the ID).
- Models with no version (bare aliases such as `opus`, `sonnet`, `opus[1m]`, `default`) keep their relative order after every versioned model.
- Parses first-party, Bedrock (`us.anthropic.…-v1:0`), Vertex (`…@20251101`) and legacy `claude-3-x-<family>` IDs the same way.
- Applies to the session-launch catalog and to the Claude ACP chat `model` option. Grouped choices and every other option keep the agent's order.
- The configured default is marked `isDefault` but is not pinned to the top; it sorts by version like the rest.
- A configured family alias (`sonnet`) marks the newest catalog model of that family as the default instead of adding a separate alias entry.
- Custom-gateway fallback models (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL`) stay in configuration order.
- Cached Claude catalogs invalidate when the ordering algorithm revision changes.

### Recency first (all agents, by design)

- `Models` and `RevalidateModels` stamp `lastUsedAt` on each model from the latest activity of a session whose current model matches it. Scope is the project; a project with no history uses all projects. Stamped models move to the front, most recent first.
- The task composer preselects the last-used model. Precedence: remembered draft → last-used model → project's configured model → catalog default.
- This is intentional: the model a user last ran outranks the project's configured model and the agent default. A configured model applies only until the user has session history for that agent; a fresh install still reads newest-first.

### UI

- The Claude task-composer picker shows the first 4 models and folds the rest behind "Show N older models". A selected model in the folded tail keeps the list open.

## Review follow-up

- Passes the ACP ordering hook into conversation construction before SDK receive goroutines start, removing the initialization race.
- Runs the public ordering hook outside the conversation mutex, allowing safe state inspection from extensions.
- Pins ACP driver setup, Claude binding configuration, `Models`, `RevalidateModels`, and `TaskComposer` wiring with integration-level tests.
- Preserves grouped ACP choices instead of splitting repeated group headers.
- Scrubs ambient Anthropic gateway/default-model variables in order-exact tests.
- Parses legacy `claude-3-x-<family>` IDs and uses snapshot dates as a same-version tiebreak.
- Uses `Activity.LastActivityAt`, not the broadly-mutated session `UpdatedAt`, for usage recency. A session contributes only its current model, matching the durable data available today.
- Reads only `project_id`, `model`, `activity_last_at`, and `created_at` for the selected harness when ranking recent models, rather than decoding every session.
- Documents that `SortClaudeNewestFirst` sorts its input slice in place and applies ordering to ACP discovery as well as live sessions.
- Removes the duplicated `Models` doc comment.

## Tests

- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp ./internal/service/agent`
- `npm test -- src/renderer/components/TaskComposer.test.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck` in `frontend/`
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2` (`0 issues`)

title: test(mobile): fix main's Mobile CI by asserting the unpair timeout by type
body:
## Summary
Main's Mobile CI has been failing since #5977 merged (run 36544228373). One test fails: `lib/api.disconnect-timeout.test.ts` › "abandons the best-effort daemon unpair after two seconds".

**Cause:** #6001 added this test, which asserts `req()`'s old timeout text, `"Request timed out. Is the desktop reachable?"`. #5977 replaced that plain `Error` with a typed `UnreachableError("timeout")` that carries user-facing copy. The two PRs touch different files, so there was no conflict. Each passed CI against a main that didn't include the other, and main doesn't require branches to be up to date before merging.

**Fix:** assert the error type and its `reason: "timeout"` instead of the wording. The test still proves the unpair is abandoned after two seconds; if it weren't, `failure` would be undefined and the type assertion would fail. It also won't break when the copy is reworded.

## Tests
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile` on current main: 141 files, 1,309 tests pass.

Test-only change; no behaviour change.

## Follow-up
Consider turning on "Require branches to be up to date before merging" (or a merge queue) for `main` so PRs are retested against each other before merging.

title: [Feature]: Add DeepSeek Harness (dsh) as a supported harness
body:
### Problem

As someone who runs DeepSeek models for coding work, I need Agent Orchestrator to support DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) as a worker harness, because DeepSeek Harness is the runtime that reaches my DeepSeek account's model routes and credentials, and today I have to leave AO to use it.

DeepSeek Harness ships an automation-only ACP v1 stdio server (`dsh --profile acp`) and a one-shot headless profile (`dsh --profile headless "<task>"`), so it can be driven the way AO already drives OpenCode, Cline, Kimi, and others rather than by scraping a terminal.

There is prior art: #4058 attempted this adapter and was closed as stale rather than rejected.

### Proposed direction

Add a `deepseek-harness` harness:

- **Chat** over ACP (`dsh --profile acp`), with model and reasoning effort taken from the configuration catalog the session itself advertises, so the picker cannot offer a model the session rejects.
- **Terminal** sessions as one headless task (`dsh --profile headless`), which is the first-party non-interactive surface; the profile takes no model flag, so a project model override applies to Chat.

A PR is already open for this: #6014.

### Alternatives considered

- **Run DeepSeek models through the existing `opencode` harness.** Works for models the configured OpenCode provider serves, but it is a different runtime and does not use DeepSeek Harness's own model routes or credential store.
- **Drive the community TUI** (`@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`). It exists, but it is a third-party profile rather than a first-party surface, so terminal support uses the shipped headless profile instead.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [x] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: fix(mobile): honest connecting state on launch, and distinct connection-state icons
body:
## What

On launch, a paired phone on a slow network no longer shows "No desktop paired / Scan pairing code" before it connects. The tabs now show "Connecting to your desktop…" until the first connection check finishes.

## Why

The store's `config` is `null` until the launch endpoint race finishes. Workers, Projects and PRs all check `if (!configured) return <UnpairedState/>` before they look at `loading`. So while the race was running (seconds on a slow network: 3s per probe, and tunnel probes retry for up to 20s), a paired user was told to re-scan. Then the app connected on its own.

`configLoading.ts` already separated "no config yet" from "no machine paired", but only for the loader. The tab screens never used it.

## How

- `lib/store.tsx`: expose `configResolved` on the app state.
- `lib/configLoading.ts`: add `unconfiguredView({ resolved })`, which returns `"resolving"` or `"unpaired"`.
- `lib/UnpairedState.tsx`: render a connecting state (spinner and copy) until resolution finishes. All three tabs share this component, so none of their call sites change. An unpaired phone has no host to race and resolves almost instantly, so new users still get the pairing prompt right away.
- `lib/connectRuntime.ts`: add a 5s timeout (`ENDPOINT_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS`) to the authenticated `/api/v1/endpoints` refresh that runs after the race. It runs inside launch resolution and had no timeout, so a slow network could hold the app in "connecting" after it had already found a working endpoint. A refresh that times out is skipped, and the stored endpoints are kept, as `connectHost` already did for any failed refresh.

**Empty-state icons.** Every connection failure used `wifi-off`, so a rejected password looked like a network problem, and the unpaired state used a generic server icon. Each state now has its own Lucide glyph. The icon comes from `describeConnectionFailure`, so Workers, Projects and PRs all get it from one place:

| State | Icon |
|---|---|
| No desktop paired | `monitor-smartphone` |
| Connecting | `monitor-smartphone`, breathing (reuses `useBreathing`, so Reduce Motion is respected); the separate spinner is removed |
| Password rejected | `monitor-off` |
| Unreachable | `unplug` (also used on the session screen's offline state) |
| Too many attempts | `timer` |
| Desktop error | `monitor-cog` |
| Address changed | `route-off` |

**Title and buttons only.** The unpaired, connecting and connection-failure empty states (Workers, Projects, PRs and the session screen) now show just the icon, title and buttons. The explanatory text below the title is removed. The pairing screen's inline error still shows the full message, including the Local Network hint. The one exception is the disconnected state, which keeps a single short hint: "Check you're on the same Wi-Fi." (or "Check Tailscale is on for both devices." on a Tailscale address). It comes from a new optional `hint` field on the error copy.

Not in this PR: showing the last-known desktop right away and connecting in the background. That would poll a possibly-dead stored endpoint during the race and could flash error states, so it needs its own change.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: all 139 files pass. Added tests for `unconfiguredView`, the refresh timeout and the icon for each failure cause, and updated the existing refresh test for the new `signal`.
- `npm run typecheck`: reports one error in `lib/session/TerminalSessionScreen.tsx` (`XtermWebViewHandle` vs `InjectableTerminalRenderer`). This PR doesn't touch that file; I didn't check whether `main` has the same error.
