title: fix(cloud): make PR claim App-first with PAT fallback (robust for all worker git ops)
body:
## Problem
A cloud worker created a PR via `gh pr create` (PR appeared on GitHub) but tracking failed with **"The pull request could not be tracked"**. Staging logs: `claim worker pull request … GitHub request returned status 401`.

Root cause: **`workerClaimPullRequest` was PAT-first with no fallback** — it used the stored PAT whenever one existed and only used the GitHub App when *no* PAT was configured. A rotted-but-cached-valid PAT (`validation_state` is a cached snapshot) 401'd every claim while a healthy App sat unused. This is the exact "stale PAT shadows App" class we already fixed for **raising** (#5746), **merge**, and the **credential grants** — claim was the last path still on the old precedence (its comment even claimed to "mirror workerRaisePullRequest", which was no longer true).

## Fix
Flip claim to **App-first + PAT-fallback**, identical to `workerRaisePullRequest`: try `checkoutBroker.ClaimPullRequest` (fresh App token, never stale) first; fall back to `patWrites.ClaimPullRequest` only if the broker errors.

## "Everywhere" audit
Every worker git/GitHub op for cloud sessions was checked:
- checkout/push/token grants → App-first ✓
- raise PR → App-first ✓ (#5746)
- merge button → App-first ✓ (#5746)
- **claim PR → PAT-first ✗ → fixed here**
- submit review → App-only by construction (no PAT equivalent in `PATWriteService`)

Claim was the only remaining non-robust path.

## Tests
- `TestWorkerClaimPullRequestPrefersBrokerAppOverPAT` — a healthy App claim must not touch the PAT (regression for the 401 bug).
- `TestWorkerClaimPullRequestFallsBackToPATWhenBrokerCannotWrite` — App error → PAT fallback runs.
- Existing raise/claim tests still pass; build + gofmt clean.

body:
Code changes: +114 -72

## What

1. **Inspector starts closed.** Opening a session no longer auto-opens the right inspector panel. It opens when the user toggles it, or through the existing browser-reveal paths (an orchestrator's first browser activity, clicking a session browser link).
2. **Per-project agent cap in the sidebar.** Each expanded project lists at most **6** agents, followed by its own **Show more / Show less** row. The projects list (10) and Scratchpad (10) keep their existing caps.

## Why

fixes #5884. Opening the inspector automatically on every session open/spawn takes width from the terminal/chat before the user needs it. Long-running projects also push everything below them out of view, so each project now collapses to its 6 most recent agents.

## How

- `ui-store.ts`: the default inspector state is now `isOpen: false`. A new `inspectorIsOpen(sessions, id)` helper replaces the scattered fallbacks (`?? true`, `?? !browserOnly`, `?? !isOrchestrator`) in `SessionView`, `ShellTopbar` and `ChatWorkspace`, so the default can't drift between surfaces again. Inspector state is in-memory only, so a toggle still sticks for that session during the app run.
- `Sidebar.tsx`: the capped-list logic (slice, hidden count, and auto-expand when the active item sits past the cap until the user collapses it again) was duplicated between the projects list and Scratchpad. It is now one `useShowMoreCap` hook, used by those two and by the new per-project agent list.
- Per-project reordering keeps the hidden tail behind the draggable slice, the same way Scratchpad already does.
- The per-project Show more row reuses `ShowMoreRow` and the existing `shell.showMoreAgents` / `shell.showLessAgents` strings, so there are no new i18n keys. It is indented so its label starts on the session status-dot column.

## Testing

- SessionView tests: the worker fixtures start with the inspector open (the old implicit default), since most of them exercise the open rail. A dedicated test now covers the new default (closed on open, then Ctrl+Shift+B opens it on Summary). The ShellTopbar worker-controls test seeds its open state the same way.

title: test(#5038): add opt-in sidebar cache diagnostics
body:
Code changes: +0 -0  
Tests: +828 -11  
Others: +0 -0

## Status

Diagnostic-only follow-up for #5038. This PR does not claim to reproduce or fix the reported missing-sidebar-row bug, and it makes no production behavior change.

## Evidence

- The fake-bridge Playwright investigation exercised six renderer scenarios, including sustained SSE pressure, fetch failures, hidden visibility, withheld events, a large CDC gap replay, and EventSource replacement. In each one the new worker reached the `['workspaces']` cache and its sidebar row rendered. None reproduced the report's restart-only staleness.
- I compared the actual Electron app with and without the candidate `backgroundThrottling: false` setting in minimized windows using scratch AO data. In both runs `document.visibilityState` remained `visible`; a newly spawned worker entered the query cache and its sidebar row appeared within about 6 seconds with the setting and about 10 seconds without it. Neither run reproduced the failure, so this does not establish that background throttling caused the report or that the option fixes it.
- A reviewer also reported that their minimized-window comparison recovered in both builds.

Accordingly, this PR does not include the unverified global Electron setting or its configuration-only test. It avoids imposing the continuous background CPU, animation, and Page Visibility tradeoff without a failing native case.

## Diagnostic tests

The fake-bridge scenarios are tagged `@SIDEBAR_DIAG` and skip unless `AO_SIDEBAR_DIAG=1`, so neither the default `@T0/@P0` renderer CI gate nor a plain `npm run test:e2e` runs them. They test renderer cache/event/poll behavior only and do not emulate Electron background throttling. They are diagnostic evidence, not a regression test for a native mechanism.

How the harness matches production:

- **Stream URL.** The fake's stream controls match `/api/v1/events` with `includes()`, so they find the `?after=latest` stream the app opens since #6611.
- **Gap replay.** On main the daemon replays only on EventSource's own reconnect: `Last-Event-ID` overrides `?after=latest`, while a stream the app constructs starts at head (`backend/internal/httpd/events.go`). The fake models exactly that path. The stream drops to `CONNECTING` and fires `error`, then reconnects after Chromium's 3-second default. It fires `open` before the first replayed frame. Frames are real `session_updated` CDC envelopes (`{seq, projectId, sessionId, type, payload, createdAt}`) that run through event-transport's handlers, in runs of 50 per session.
- **Delivery order.** Nothing is delivered to a stream that is `CONNECTING` or `CLOSED`. While a stream reconnects or replays, every event the fake commits for it (created workers, status changes, removals) is queued behind the gap, which is where the daemon's `Last-Event-ID` replay would put it.
- **Replaced stream.** If the app replaces the stream mid-replay, the rest of the gap and the queued events are dropped and counted, since the replacement opens at `?after=latest`. The replay state then resets, so nothing waits for an event that will never arrive. Replay counters start from zero for each replay.
- **Continuous pressure.** The daemon side sends real `session_updated` envelopes at 2,000/s by elapsed time, so the per-session conversation and editor-handoff invalidations run as they do in production. A backlog that builds while the main thread is busy is handed over one tick's worth (100 frames) per task. The fake yields between chunks so fetch resolution and rendering can run in between, instead of draining the backlog in one task.
- **Visibility.** `visibilitychange` is dispatched on `document` and bubbles to `window`, with `document.hidden` kept in sync.
- **Fetch attribution.** Each workspace snapshot read is attributed to what started it:
  - **Wrapped entry points:** `invalidateQueries`, `refetchQueries`, `fetchQuery` (route loaders; `prefetchQuery` and `ensureQueryData` go through it), and the query cache's focus fan-out.
  - **Poll ticks** are tagged positively. An init script marks `setInterval` callbacks, which TanStack's `timeoutManager` uses for `refetchInterval`, and the tick runs the queryFn synchronously.
  - **Retries** are reads made while `fetchFailureCount > 0`. TanStack resets that count on every new fetch.
  - **Anything else**, such as a newly mounted observer's `refetchOnMount`, counts as `other`.

  The wrappers forward every argument, so event-transport's `{ cancelRefetch: false }` reaches TanStack unchanged.

Findings (fake bridge, Vite dev build; local macOS and CI Linux agree; CI log linked below):

- **Hidden, missed event: the 15-second poll is the only recovery path.** `query-client.ts` sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `workspaceQueryOptions` keeps it, so returning visibility fetches nothing by itself. No workspace fetch ran during 121 s hidden. After restore, the only workspace fetch was the poll (`interval: 1`, every other source 0), and the worker was missing from the cache for 6.6 s in CI (5.7 s locally) after visibility returned. The wait depends on the poll's phase and can last up to one 15 s interval. So a worker whose event is missed while the window is hidden can stay invisible for up to 15 s after the window is restored. An earlier revision of this PR said a focus refetch would recover it first. That was wrong.
- **Large project, no truncation.** With 491 workers in one project, the sidebar lists 6 until Show more, then renders all 491 rows, including the index-443 worker.
- **Refetch race.** A worker created while the workspace query is fetching arrives through the follow-up invalidation.
- **378k-frame gap replay.** A worker created during the replay reached the cache through an invalidation-driven fetch after 4,608 frames, with about 373,000 still queued. All 5 workspace fetches in that window came from `invalidate`; none came from the poll, focus, or anything else, so the replay does not starve invalidation. Ending the replay with a failed reconnect dropped the remaining 371,856 frames, including the worker's own queued event, and the app reopened at `?after=latest`.
- **Replay cost.** Draining a gap through the real handlers runs at about 400 frames/s in the dev build (measured locally). A CPU profile attributes about half of main-thread time to `useCachedWorkspaces` in `useTerminateSession.ts`, whose `useSyncExternalStore` getSnapshot calls `getQueryData` on every query-cache event for each subscribed component. This is a dev-build performance observation, not a demonstrated cause of #5038.
- **Continuous SSE pressure.** Through the real handlers, the renderer handled only a small share of a 2,000/s stream: 9,500 of the 251,100 frames sent over 128 s were delivered in CI (8,600 of 254,500 locally). The workspace list was invalidated 92 (63 locally) times, all fetches came from `invalidate`, and each refresh of the 492-session list holds the main thread long enough that the rest of the stream backs up. The worker was created without its own event, because in production that event would sit behind the backlog. It still reached the cache through a later pressure frame's invalidation 0.5 s in CI (1.4 s locally) after creation, and its row rendered. The previous revision's "246,800 frames in 125 s" came from frames that skipped the real CDC handler and were drained in one task, so it overstated how much the renderer keeps up with.
- **Poll after a replacement stream.** After the replacement stream's `open` catch-up had settled, a worker created without an event was recovered by the poll (positively tagged) 12.2 s in CI (11.5 s locally) later.
- **Exhausted retries.** The interval fetch fails and its one retry fails (`interval: 1`, `retry: 1`); the next interval tick recovers the worker.
- **Hidden, delivered event.** The worker arrives through `invalidate` while the document is hidden. No interval fetches ran during 130 s hidden.
- **Replacement EventSource.** After the stream closes, the error health check refetches once. The app reopened at `?after=latest` 9.8 s in CI (12.6 s locally) later (its 2.5 to 5 s backoff plus main-thread delay), and the new stream's `open` catch-up recovered the missed worker.

## Running the diagnostics

```sh
cd frontend
AO_SIDEBAR_DIAG=1 AO_E2E_PORT=5199 CI=true npx playwright test e2e/sidebar-missing-worker-diagnostic.spec.ts --workers=1
```

Without `AO_SIDEBAR_DIAG=1`, all six report as skipped. Use a free `AO_E2E_PORT` and `CI=true`. With the default port 5173 and `reuseExistingServer`, Playwright silently reuses any other checkout's `electron-forge start` renderer, and the fake project row never appears. `playwright.config.ts` warns about this.

CI run of all six scenarios, using the `renderer-smoke` job's container, Node version, and install steps (a temporary fork-only workflow, not part of this PR): https://github.com/diyaavirmani/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38528355885 (6 passed, 8.7 min)

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- `@SIDEBAR_DIAG` with `AO_SIDEBAR_DIAG=1`: 6/6 in the CI run above (Linux, Node 24) and 6/6 locally on macOS.
- Without `AO_SIDEBAR_DIAG`, `playwright test e2e/sidebar-missing-worker-diagnostic.spec.ts` reports 6 skipped.
- Shared fake-bridge paths: `createWorker` now sends a real `session_created` envelope, which event-transport handles exactly like the old empty frame (a workspace invalidation only). `emit` skips `CONNECTING` streams, and only the replay control creates one. `smoke-sessions.spec.ts`, the other spec that calls `createWorker`, passes locally. The `renderer-smoke` CI job on this PR is the canonical result.
- Vitest was not rerun locally. Both changed files are under `frontend/e2e/`, which `vite.renderer.config.ts` excludes from Vitest; the PR's `test` job runs the full suite.

A failing macOS window with cache, fetch, visibility, and sidebar DOM timestamps is still needed before proposing a runtime behavior change.

Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via DocumentType.name. GHSA-27p8-2357-5qqv
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now validates a processing-instruction target as an XML NCName and rejects a case-insensitive xml, throwing InvalidStateError — a check 0.8.x did not previously perform, preventing PI-target injection via >, ?, or whitespace. GHSA-c7q8-3ch8-vqpv
  • Security: Document.createEntityReference() now rejects an invalid XML Name at creation, and XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } validates an EntityReference nodeName as an XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — preventing XML injection via an entity-reference name. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6
  • Security: the parser now reports a not-well-formed end tag whose valid name is followed by trailing content as a recoverable error instead of accepting it silently, per the XML ETag production; parsing recovers to the byte-identical DOM. Consumers that want strict rejection can escalate the reported error to fatal via the parser's errorHandler. GHSA-6h8r-xr42-gp59

Thank you, @​ericchiang, @​bhaswanthc, @​arpitjain099, @​Paranoidgrinch, for your contributions

0.8.14

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() now also rejects invalid element and attribute names when { requireWellFormed: true } is passed, throwing InvalidStateError for a name that is not a valid XML QName (this covers the namespace prefix, which surfaces in the element qualified name or in a synthesized xmlns: declaration). This prevents XML injection via createElement() / setAttribute(), extending the existing requireWellFormed checks to the serialized name set. GHSA-w2rr-34g9-rvrj GHSA-4w3w-2rp5-g8jm

Thank you, @​bhaswanthc, @​jmestwa-coder, for your contributions

Updates `baseline-browser-mapping` from 2.10.35 to 2.11.26
Release notes

Sourced from baseline-browser-mapping's releases.

v2.11.0

What's Changed in 2.11.0

  • feat: Adds a new getTimeline() method for getting the series of minimum browser changes, either grouped by date or by browser.
  • refactor: Substantial refactoring of the data compression process that replaces the full list of browsers from @mdn/browser-compat-data and downstream-browsers.json and features from web-features (in their very pared down form) with a change-list timeline that reflects which versions supported Baseline (newly available) on a given date. Thanks to @​swwind for the idea!
  • refactor: Some common functions have been moved to a util.ts module for use in other scripts.
  • fix: Removes process.exit() calls when unsupported option combinations are passed to getCompatibleVersions() and getAllVersions() in favour of throwing an Error. There is a small security risk with process.exit() calls that sites accepting unsanitised inputs could be the subject of attacks. Unsupported config options now throw and Error which should allow for more graceful handling. Thanks to @​bnbdr for flagging this as vulnerability CVE-2026-45819 .

Fixes #134

Full Changelog: https://github.com/web-platform-dx/baseline-browser-mapping/compare/v2.10.44...v2.11.0

title: feat(cloud): move cloud harness login to Harness settings, personal credentials only
body:
## Summary

Moves all cloud coding-agent login to the Harness settings page, with personal credentials only, and fixes the local harness login panel. The original "Log in with Anthropic" hang is fixed on `main` by #6082.

### 1. The Anthropic login hang
The original hang ("Log in with Anthropic" stuck on "Connecting…") is now fixed on `main` by #6082, which runs Claude's OAuth loopback flow directly instead of `claude setup-token`. This PR first fixed it differently, by running `claude setup-token` under a pseudo-terminal. When rebasing onto `main`, I kept #6082's merged version and dropped this PR's version and its tests.

What this PR still adds around the login:
- Cancelling a pending browser login stops it, and a user-initiated cancel isn't shown as an error.
- "Log in with Anthropic" saves a **personal** credential, plus a local fallback token for when Claude Code has no local login (section 3).

### 2. Cloud harness login lives on Harness settings
- **Local | Cloud toggle.** While the cloud feature is on, a toggle at the top of the Harness page switches the whole page. Rows never mix local and cloud state, and each row has at most one action.
  - **Local:** every harness with its local status, plus Install / **Login** / **Refresh login**.
  - **Cloud:** only Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode, with Connected / Not connected and **Login** / **Refresh login**. The login expands inline under the row, with no popup. When signed out of AO Cloud, the view asks you to sign in.
- **Cloud login methods:**
  - Claude Code: **Log in with Anthropic** (default; its token is also saved locally, as a fallback for when Claude Code has no local login), then Setup token (with short `claude setup-token` steps) and Anthropic API key.
  - Codex: **Log in with ChatGPT** (default), then OpenAI API key.
  - Cursor: Cursor API key.
  - OpenCode: an OpenCode, Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter API key.
  - Each input names what to paste, and each API key links to the page where it is created.
- **Quieter rows.** Status text is plain, and logged-in rows don't repeat their status in an "Authorized" chip.
- **No login prompt after signing in to AO Cloud.** The onboarding gate's auto-popup is removed.
- **Project creation doesn't handle logins.** On the cloud harness step, if no harness is logged in for cloud, a notice with **Go to Harness settings** opens the harness page's Cloud view over the flow. The step picks up the login when you come back.

### Cloud project creation
- **Starts from the repository.** Before GitHub is connected, or while it shares no repositories, the form offers **Connect repository**. Afterwards, the repository dropdown ends with **Connect more repositories**, which reopens GitHub to grant access to more. Pickers show search only for lists longer than ten.
- **No project name field.** The project takes the selected repository's name. The field was being overwritten on selection anyway.
- **Manual GitHub PAT setup removed** (repository URL + token + "Update Token" recovery). Projects are created through the GitHub App.
- **Repository pickers size to their results** instead of a fixed 18rem list, so one repository is one row.
- **Opens the new project.** After **Create**, the app navigates to the new cloud project's board, as it does for local projects.
- **Coder templates only on Coder.** The Template picker (and coder options sent with the project) appear only when new sessions will run on Coder, not merely when the deployment offers it.
- **Agent pickers** for worker and orchestrator sit side by side. They list only harnesses connected for cloud and end with **Manage harness connections…**, which opens Harness settings' Cloud view. The new-task composer's agent picker on cloud projects behaves the same way.
- **Additional coder session repositories are hidden for now.** The "Add another repository" link and its carousel are gone. The component stays in `CoderTemplatePicker.tsx` so it can be re-enabled.
- **No branch choice anywhere.** Every repository uses its GitHub default branch: the project's is derived server-side, and additional (coder) repositories, if re-enabled, are cloned without `--branch`. The summary box that repeated the repository's name, URL and branch is gone.

### Cloud session startup loader
- The first step is now **Creating the workspace**. It stays active while the sandbox is `requested`/`provisioning`, and completes when the sandbox reaches `bootstrapping` (the provider reports it running and AO starts its worker inside). It used to complete on `sandbox.provisioning`, which the control plane emits just *before* asking the provider to create the sandbox. The later steps are unchanged.

### Harness local login panel
- The panel checked authentication once, the instant the login terminal exited. That first check can fail transiently: for Codex we saw `auth_check_failed` 100 ms after exit, while the daemon's own retry seconds later reported the harness logged in. The panel then showed "Signed out" with a retry button and never closed. It now re-checks up to 4 times, 1.5 s apart. A panel that still couldn't confirm the login closes on its own once readiness reports the harness logged in.
- **Codex (backend):** after a Harness terminal login (`codex login`), every recheck returned "unauthorized" in 0 ms ("Sign in to Codex or add an account in Settings."). Codex readiness answers from the last device-credential reconciliation, taken while signed out, and nothing re-ran it after the login. `Probe` now reconciles the device Codex credential before rechecking. Tests cover a credential reappearing after sign-out and a replaced credential clearing stale "sign in again" evidence; an unchanged credential stays signed out.
- The panel no longer repeats the plan's guidance under its title while the terminal runs ("Choose ChatGPT, device code…"). Guidance is shown only when it asks for an action outside the terminal (the **Open login** button).

### 3. Personal credentials only
- Every cloud agent credential is the user's own (`/me/providers`). The app no longer reads, creates, or lists org-level agent credentials. This covers the harness step, task composer, orchestrator spawn, login dialog and main-process push.
- **Settings → Cloud** keeps the GitHub token and replaces the org agent list with a link to Harness settings.

## Testing
- Full frontend `vitest`: everything passes except `browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which fails locally because `better-sqlite3` is compiled for Electron's ABI (unrelated).
- New or updated tests cover:
  - terminal token extraction and the `script` wrapper;
  - the inline harness login: defaults, per-harness methods, personal save, cancel;
  - harness rows expanding the inline login, and Reconnect;
  - the project-creation nudge to Harness settings;
  - personal-only connection helpers and orchestrator spawn;
  - the cloud agent list (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode).
- `tsc`: no errors in changed files.
- **End-to-end on macOS:** the real `authenticate()` against `claude` 2.1.284 with a real browser authorization resolved with a well-formed `sk-ant-oat01-…` token. The same Log in with Anthropic flow was also confirmed working in the dev Electron app.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Cloud Codex "Log in with ChatGPT" stores Codex's `auth.json`, whose access token lasts 10 days. The control plane doesn't refresh or persist it yet, so cloud Codex needs a reconnect about every 10 days until #6080 lands.
- The control plane still accepts org-level agent credentials. This PR only removes them from the app. Existing org credentials are no longer considered by the app's harness picker or orchestrator spawn, so anyone who relied on one needs to log in from Harness settings.

title: fix(models): show agent default instead of "Model not reported"
body:
Code changes: +615 -11  
Tests: +475 -8  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Follow-up to #5849. When no model is picked for a task and the agent's model catalog does not mark a default, the New Task model picker showed **"Model not reported"**. This PR resolves the agent's real default from its own config where that can be determined for the session AO will launch, so the picker shows the concrete model. When it cannot be determined, the value stays unidentified (per #5834); no bare "Default" option is offered.

### Backend: read the agent's user-level configured model
`modelcatalog/configured_default.go` reads the model each CLI-listed agent's **user-level** config selects and marks it `isDefault` in the discovered catalog.

Repository config is never read. Sessions launch from AO worktrees seeded from a commit chosen per session (project base branch, repository default, or an existing remote branch), so the checkout's copy (staged, uncommitted, untracked, or on another branch) may not be what the session sees. If the repository may hold config for the agent (on disk anywhere from the git root down to the project dir, or at the tip of `HEAD` or any local branch, remote-tracking branch, or tag, i.e. any ref a session could be attached to or seeded from), the default is left unresolved (`repo_config.go`, one `git cat-file --batch-check` for all refs; if git can't answer, config is assumed present).

| Agent | User-level source (lowest → highest) | Repository config that leaves it unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| opencode (v1) | global `opencode.json(c)`/`config.json`; `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` and managed config outrank everything | `opencode.json(c)`, `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`; also no git root, user `OPENCODE_CONFIG`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` winning, conflicting siblings |
| opencode-v2 | only `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` / managed config | always: v2 also reads the launch worktree's ancestors (e.g. `<AO_DATA_DIR>/opencode.json`), which discovery can't see |
| aider | `~/.aider.conf.y(a)ml`, `$AIDER_MODEL` | `.aider.conf.y(a)ml` |
| droid | `~/.factory/settings.json` | — |
| copilot | `$COPILOT_HOME/settings.json` (default `~/.copilot`), `$COPILOT_MODEL` (legacy `config.json` not read) | `.github/copilot/settings.json`, `.github/copilot/settings.local.json` |
| pi | `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` — `defaultProvider/defaultModel` | — |
| crush | `~/.config/crush/crush.json`, `~/.local/share/crush/crush.json` | `crush.json`, `.crush.json` |

Env overrides (`AIDER_MODEL`, `COPILOT_MODEL`) win over every file, including repository config.

- A default the CLI itself reports always wins over config.
- A configured model missing from the listed catalog is appended (it is what the CLI will actually run).
- `"default"` placeholders are ignored.
- The resolved default feeds the catalog fingerprint, so editing it invalidates the cached catalog. With nothing configured the fingerprint is byte-identical to before (no mass cache invalidation on upgrade).

### Frontend: no "Model not reported"
When the default model can't be identified, the pickers list the models with none selected instead of labelling an unknown value (#5834):
- `AgentModelCombobox` (task composer, new task, project settings): the trigger reads **"Select model"** instead of "Model not reported"; no row is checked.
- `ReviewerSelect`: the unidentified model is left off the trigger (`Codex` instead of `Codex · Model not reported`).
- `settings.models.modelNotReported` is replaced by `settings.models.selectModel` in all 8 locales. No "Default" option is added; clearing an override stays the existing "Use agent model" action.

## Tests
- `configured_default_test.go` / `opencode_default_test.go` use real git repositories: per-agent user-level sources, env precedence, repository config leaving the default unresolved when untracked, staged, committed, or committed-but-deleted (from a subdirectory), a real `git worktree add` from HEAD carrying config the checkout deleted, config present only on another local branch (attached with a real `git worktree add`), a remote-tracking branch, or a tag, both OpenCode majors, placeholder handling, JSONC stripping, fingerprint stability.
- `GOWORK=off go test ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/` and `go build ./...` pass locally.
- Renderer tests updated for the "Select model" trigger and the unchecked model list; frontend checks run in CI.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Repository-configured models are never shown as the default; the picker stays unidentified there, and the user can still pick a model. Showing them exactly would need discovery to know each session's seed commit (follow-up).
- OpenCode v2 resolves only from inline or managed config.
- Discovery now runs a few short `git` commands (5s timeout each) per catalog fingerprint/discovery for agents with repository config.
- Cursor and kilocode are not covered yet (config format not confirmed).

title: fix(chat): settle running turns when the agent controller stops
body:
Part of #6064 (pane settle half; closes with the other two halves).

## The bug

When a reviewer/chat agent controller dies mid-turn, the pane becomes a zombie:

- the "Working for Xm" spinner spins forever,
- the composer stays locked with "The controller is not connected",
- the "Stop turn" affordance is gone (`canStopTurn` is false) — no stop, no cancel, no reset; the only way out offered is the banner's Resume.

Without a controller, a running turn cannot be running — but both the spinner and the composer kept treating it as live.

## The fix

Settle the turn at the two selectors that decide liveness, instead of patching each symptom:

- `activeTurn()` ignores running turns while `controller.state === "stopped"` — the spinner (both render sites) and the composer's in-flight bookkeeping stop lying. **Queued turns stay active**: they dispatch as soon as the agent resumes.
- `groupByTurn()` no longer marks those turns `live` — the timeline stops spinning and the plan checklist stops ticking over a dead controller.

Transient controller states (`connecting`, `recovering`) are deliberately untouched: there the turn may genuinely continue after reattach. A stopped controller still shows the existing banner with its Resume/Open-shell actions — they now sit under an honest, settled pane instead of an eternal spinner.

The explicit cancel lever for a live reviewer run is separate and stays tracked in #3745.

## Testing

- New regression test in `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: controller stopped with a running turn → stopped banner present, `live-turn-status` gone, no "Working for" text.
- `vitest run ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`: 129 passed (129).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.

title: fix(review): reach orphaned reviewer panes after the DB handle is cleared
body:
Part of #6064 (the reachability half; the pane-state settle fix is in #6066).

## The gap

The reviewer pane's only address was the volatile `reviews.ReviewerHandleID` column:

- teardown on terminal-state writes (#5953) clears it,
- daemon restarts age it out,

while the tmux pane itself keeps running. With the handle gone:

- `GET /sessions/{id}/reviews` reported no reviewer → the inspector's kill control disappeared (`hasReviewerSession` = empty),
- `POST .../reviews/kill` destroyed nothing — the loop iterates DB handles only.

The pane became an orphan that only a raw process kill could reach, with no UI lever at all.

## The fix

The terminal pane's handle is deterministic — `review-" + sanitized worker id` (launcher.go `reviewerHandleID`) — and `Destroy` is a no-op on an absent pane. Both sides fall back to the stable id:

- **`listLocked`**: when the DB handle is empty (and the row is not chat-mode), probe liveness of the stable id; if alive, report it as `reviewerHandleId`. The inspector's existing kill control becomes visible again — no frontend change needed.
- **`TerminateReviewer`**: when no DB handle produced a destroy, destroy the stable id. Sessions with no review history at all remain a strict no-op (guarded by `len(reviews) > 0`).

Chat-mode reviewers are deliberately excluded from the probe: their handles are session-scoped (`review-chat:<id>`) and cannot be reconstructed from the worker id — those orphans stay tracked in #5948. The broader live-run cancel surface remains #3745.

## Testing

- Updated `TestTerminateReviewerCancelsRunningRunsWithoutReviewerHandle`: a cleared handle with review history now destroys via the stable id and reports it in the response.
- `TestTerminateReviewerNoopsWhenNoReviewHistory` unchanged and green: no history → strict no-op.
- New: `List` reports the stable id when the deterministic pane probes alive; keeps it empty when dead; does not probe for chat-mode rows.
- `go test -race ./internal/review/`: ok. `gofmt -l .`: clean.

body:
Code changes: +1975 -78 Tests: +871 -21 Others: +45 -6 ## Restoration context This PR restores the agentic AO Mobile in-app browser from #6040 after that PR was merged before intended and subsequently reverted by #6052. It reapplies the reviewed feature onto the current `main`, preserving the mobile connection-state refinements that landed after the revert. ## Summary - turns Preview into a full in-app browser with a centered address bar, back/forward/reload, open, share, errors, and adaptive native Liquid Glass chrome - keeps HTTP(S) navigation inside AO, restores the last page per connected host/session, auto-selects the URL for fast editing, and avoids duplicate share payloads - lets the owning AO agent control the exact foreground mobile WebView through the existing `ao browser` command family, including `open`, `snapshot`, ref-based interaction, `act`, and page reads - routes `--surface auto` to a focused mobile Preview first and falls back to the desktop browser, while preserving session ownership and browser-capability checks - reduces interaction latency with direct action matching, batched command guidance, stale-ref recovery, and navigation completion waits ## Behind the hood ```mermaid flowchart TD Task["User gives AO a browser task"] Agent["AO agent"] CLI["ao browser command
open · act · snapshot · get"] API["Loopback daemon API"] Guard["Session ownership + browser capability validation"] Router{"Which browser surface?"} Task --> Agent Agent --> CLI CLI --> API API --> Guard Guard --> Router Router -->|Mobile Preview is focused| Hub["Session-scoped mobile browser hub"] Router -->|No focused mobile target| Desktop["Desktop Electron browser runtime"] Hub <-->|Authenticated LAN WebSocket
command + correlated result| Runtime subgraph Mobile["AO Mobile · foreground Preview"] direction TB Runtime["Focused mobile runtime"] Bridge["Bounded WebView command bridge"] WebView["Live in-app WebView"] Toolbar["Native adaptive glass toolbar"] Store["Per-host/session URL storage"] Runtime <-->|Navigate · inspect · interact| Bridge Bridge <-->|Page state · refs · URL · title| WebView Toolbar -->|Manual navigation| WebView WebView <-->|Save and restore page| Store end Desktop --> Result["Browser result returned to the agent"] Hub --> Result ``` The mobile runtime registers only through the password-authenticated LAN listener. The browser service still validates the owning session and its ephemeral browser capability before dispatch. Preview focus owns the WebSocket lifecycle, so hidden or stale screens cannot compete for commands. ## Validation - `packages/mobile`: `npm run typecheck` and `npm test -- --run` — 160 files / 1,460 tests passed - `packages/product-ui`: typecheck, 134 unit tests, and production build passed - `frontend`: TypeScript typecheck passed - backend affected packages: browser runtime, CLI, HTTP, browser service, and skill-asset tests passed - backend affected browser/HTTP/service packages passed with the race detector - API artifacts regenerated with `npm run api`; OpenAPI and frontend schema have no drift - full repository CI passed across Go, frontend, mobile, CLI E2E, API/sqlc drift, renderer smoke, and security checks ## Scope and follow-ups - Agent control is intentionally foreground-only: the mobile Preview must be focused to receive commands. - Navigation is intentionally limited to HTTP(S) pages for this milestone; app/deep-link schemes remain outside the in-app browser surface. - Downloads, tabs, history UI, and broader desktop-browser parity are deferred to later phases.

Mobile still showed "Default (recommended)", "Default", "Provider default", "Agent default", "Default model" and "Default permissions" in the turn-settings control, both settings sheets, the ⋯ sheet and the spawn model picker. This names the value where the provider says what it is and keeps the `default` wire value, so picking it still follows the provider. Model and effort follow desktop's `resolveImplicitChoice`: a `default` choice whose description names another choice takes that name and the duplicate row goes; with that model picked explicitly it reads "Use agent model (Opus 5.5)"; otherwise "Use agent model" / "Use agent effort". Other harnesses read "Use agent permissions". Codex sessions use this row because only the ACP driver advertises `config_options`.

It now shows the effort the way the iOS row does ("Not reported", or the value as sent), writes only when moved, and labels the follow-the-agent stop "Agent".
- `ConversationActionsSheet`: the Turn settings row showed the raw setting (`opus[1m]`) or "Default"; it now names the model the way the composer does.

With the source back to main's behaviour (new exports stubbed with the old logic), 13 of the 15 new tests and the 3 updated ones fail; the two that pass guard Fast mode and applying the helper twice. Removing any one rule (Codex label, old OpenCode label, `agent` option, Fast mode, the explicit-pick case, the carried description, the summary filter, "Not reported", the native effort label) fails at least one test.
- Fixtures: the Claude config options verbatim from the daemon above, and the rows #6013 quotes from another Claude Code build, which names the newest model "Opus" and keeps the version only in the description. That build folds to "Opus" and keeps "Opus 5.5 · …" as the description, which both settings sheets show under the row.
- `npx expo export --platform ios` and `--platform android`.
- iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) and Android 16 emulator, both paired to the daemon above. The picked-model case ran on real data; the fresh-chat, not-reported and unlisted-effort cases ran by rewriting the app's copy of the GET config-options response over the debugger. The Android runs and the iOS menu tap were behind a fetch wrapper that blocked and logged non-GET requests to the conversation's settings and config options.
  - iOS: the turn-settings menu and the settings sheet show the After column, the ⋯ sheet's Turn settings row reads "Opus 5.5", and the spawn model picker has no "Agent default" hint. The wrapper logged no write.
  - Android: with main's sheet and an effort that is none of its levels, opening the sheet sent `PATCH …/config-options/effort {"value":"low"}` three times in 6 s (all blocked). With this branch, nothing.

Later regression checks: all 1,523 mobile tests across 163 files passed, and `npm run typecheck` passed. The mounted tests cover a failed PATCH causing a rerender and an unrelated rerender during the debounce window.

## Not verified

- Codex on a device (no Codex session on the test daemon); unit tests only.
- What other agents call an unmapped default mode (e.g. Kimchi's `permissions-mode`). The rename is unit-tested on a synthetic option, not against a real agent.

- While the Android slider shows an effort that is none of its levels, its thumb rests on the first level, so dragging onto exactly that level may need a move away and back first. Reasoned, not tried.
- The later Android slider regression is covered by mounted component tests with controlled fake timers. The device passes above predate that change; a repeat device pass was not run.
- `lib/chat/conversationChrome.test.ts` fails under an en-IN locale on main too (`10,00,000`); the counts above are with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`.

- #4930 replaces the approvals list and would make Codex's default use its own permission settings. "Full access" here matches main and desktop today.

title: fix(review): let kill work with auto-review on and re-arm the same SHA
body:
Part of #6064 — the auto-review half. Fixes the "kill is disabled when auto-review is on" dead end (#3745 tracks the broader cancel-stop surface).

## The dead end

With auto-review enabled, the inspector's kill control was disabled (#3338, "disable session kill during auto review") — exactly when it is needed most: an auto-spawned reviewer that hangs could not be killed from the UI at all. The gate was masking a coordinator gap rather than a real safety property:

- `existingHeadReason` treated a cancelled run for the current SHA as an **eternal** veto (`cancelled_same_sha`);
- after a kill (or even the graceful cancel) auto-review would never run a fresh pass for that SHA until the PR moved;

so allowing kill would have created an unrecoverable state, and upstream solved it by hiding the lever.

## The fix — kill under auto-review is a force-restart

The kill endpoint already records a distinct cancel body on the affected runs; it is now a shared domain constant (`domain.ReviewRunCancelledByKill`), and the newest cancel for a SHA decides its veto:

- newest cancel is a **reviewer kill** → auto-review re-arms a fresh pass for the same SHA;
- newest cancel is a **user cancel** or worker teardown → veto stands (a user cancel made *after* a kill still blocks, so the two intents cannot fight — covered by tests both ways);
- running reviews still report `review_running` as before.

On top of that the inspector kill control is simply enabled with auto-review on. Kill → fresh auto pass; if the new reviewer hangs too, kill it again — every respawn follows an explicit user action, so there is no treadmill without one.

## Testing

- New table test `TestExistingHeadReasonReviewerKillReArmsAutoReview`: kill re-arms; user cancel vetoes; newest-cancel-wins both ways.
- Existing `TestEvaluateSessionReportsCancelledAfterStaleRunningReconciliation` unchanged and green (user-style cancel keeps its veto end-to-end).
- Frontend: the auto-review test now asserts the kill button is **enabled**; `SessionInspector.test.tsx` 126 passed.
- `go test -race ./internal/autoreview/ ./internal/review/`: ok. `gofmt -l .`: clean.

title: feat(chat): hibernate idle sessions when their view closes
body:
Code changes: +1778 -186  
Tests: +3036 -56  
Others: +434 -16  

## How it works
- With Developer Mode on, an idle chat sleeps after at least 30 seconds without a Chat view, if its latest visible turn has settled and its provider supports native resume. The 30-second sweep makes the usual delay 30–60 seconds. AO stops the provider process tree and keeps the chat history. Codex and Claude Code stay awake while their native background tasks are running; a failed or unsupported inventory check also keeps it awake.
- Opening the chat or sending a message wakes it automatically. AO-sent messages do too. Agents still working, with queued work, needing input or approval, or running in a terminal stay active.
- The 30-second sweep is skipped while Developer Mode is off. When on, the scan fetches candidate IDs only; eligibility checks the latest visible user turn without loading the full transcript.
- If waking fails, the existing Resume agent control provides recovery. History, drafts, and the saved provider conversation ID remain. Lease renewals do not retry.

**AO sleeps the main Chat agent when all these conditions hold.**

### Conditions for sleep

- **Developer Mode is on.**
- The session uses **Chat mode**, finished starting, and is not terminated.
- The provider supports resuming the saved conversation.
- The agent has been **idle for at least 30 seconds**.
- No window shows its main Chat for **at least 30 seconds**.
- Its latest request has ended—completed, failed, or interrupted.
- No work, messages, approvals, questions, compaction, or agent transition remains pending.
- **Claude and Codex report no background tasks.** A failed or unsupported check keeps them awake.

AO checks every **30 seconds**, so the usual delay is **30–60 seconds** after both the idle and away conditions begin. Switching to another session, a shell, a reviewer, or a file tab counts as leaving the main Chat.

### Conditions for wake

- You **open the main Chat**, before typing.
- You or AO **send it a message**.
- You perform an action that needs the provider, such as changing agent settings.

If you send during wake, the message appears immediately; AO saves it and delivers it when the agent is ready. Concurrent requests share one wake.

### Other rules

- Sleep releases the agent processes; history and the workspace remain.
- Turning Developer Mode off prevents new sleep; existing sleeping chats can still wake.
- A failed wake shows an error and preserves messages; there is no automatic retry loop.
- A running reviewer stays active separately; it **does not currently prevent the main chat from sleeping**.
- Other ACP providers lack the background-task check; that remains our follow-up issue.
- Chat presence is renewed every 10 seconds and expires after 30 seconds; a paused screen process can make an open Chat appear closed.

## Evidence
- [Claude Code before/after interrupted-turn demo](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6087#issuecomment-5974658040): old build kept the host alive; changed build stopped it, woke with history, and slept again.
- [Full macOS demo](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6087#issuecomment-5927431884): Claude and Codex start, reply, sleep with process exit, wake with history, reply again, and sleep again.
- OpenCode ACP on `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3-flash`: a fresh task replied; leaving Chat set `hibernated_at` and exited host/provider PIDs 41475/41480. Reopening and immediately messaging recalled `IBIS-53` using new PIDs 41768/41769; leaving Chat exited both again.
- Review fixes preserve queued messages through failed shutdown, confirm host exit before native resume, and wait for saved reviewer recovery before review reads or triggers. Provider inventory runs outside the dispatch locks; unsupported Codex inventory stays warm without repeated errors.

## QA matrix
| Flow | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Developer Mode gate; idle sleep and process exit | Passed on macOS with Claude ACP, Codex app-server, and OpenCode ACP |
| Open or message to wake with history; concurrent messages queue once | Passed |
| Long command, compaction, open Chat view stay awake; failed/interrupted turns sleep after leaving Chat | Passed |
| Switch session or shell tab; daemon restart; toggle; kill; Chat→TUI | Passed |
| Invalid API input | Missing or null `active` returns 400; unknown fields remain accepted |
| Failed shutdown; next message; explicit Kill | Regression tests passed: lost acknowledgement and shutdown timeout use host cleanup; the next send can finish an earlier failed cleanup and deliver once |
| Chat-service open, send or Kill during background inventory | Regression tests passed: dispatch locks remain available and stale sleep eligibility is rechecked |
| Failed wake | Automated regression tests: stopped-agent recovery stays visible; explicit resume keeps the native ID |
| Restart with a saved Chat reviewer | Prior real daemon startup test passed on macOS; new race regression keeps reads and triggers from failing or cancelling a run before recovery |
| Upgrade an earlier dev hibernation database | All three earlier preview migration versions upgrade without losing sleep state |
| CI on `5cdd0200e` | Running after the main merge; `0515b6ed1` passed all 23 checks |
| Local UI regression tests | All 233 SessionView tests passed |
| Local backend validation | Full matrix on `3fd3bb8df` passed. After merging main, full Claude/ACP and session-manager race suites, HTTP/API tests, build, vet and lint passed |
| Local frontend validation | After merging main: both typechecks and the full Node 24 suite passed (6,411 tests; 6 skipped). Browser integration passed; shared packages and macOS helper passed in the earlier full matrix |
| Local test limits | Goose identity failed on both the previous and new implementation commits; installed Codex protocol conformance mismatches the generated schema. Renderer smoke: 74/75 passed; the pointer-drag assertion still fails on this Mac. These suites pass in CI |
| Pending approval | Unit tested only |
| Codex native background terminals | Passed on macOS: `npm run dev` survived 111 seconds away from Chat; after Codex stopped Vite, the chat slept in 52 seconds and all recorded PIDs exited; reopening recalled port `38119` |
| Claude native background tasks | Passed on macOS: Vite and its native task monitor survived 111.6 seconds away from Chat; native TaskStop worked; after leaving Chat again, it slept in 33.7 seconds and all six PIDs exited; reopening recalled `CLAUDE-PELICAN-7321` |
| OpenCode background command | Passed on macOS with GLM-5.3-Flash: detached Vite kept serving HTTP 200 after hibernation; native resume kept the codeword |
| Other ACP providers’ background tasks | No native background-task guard yet; broader protection remains a follow-up |
| Claude bridge without the private task-check method | Regression passed: method-not-found keeps the chat awake without a warning; genuine provider errors still surface |
| Accepted compaction with no later provider event | Conservatively stays busy; explicit Kill remains available |
| Linux/Windows live app | Not run |

Follow-ups: review reads wait for saved reviewers to reconnect during startup; other ACP providers still need native background-task guards and live tests. The enable switch is shared by the daemon; multiple local clients are not separate policy owners.

title: perf(ci): run backend race tests across parallel jobs
body:

## Why
Across ten recent successful PR runs, the required Go job had a 21m14s median and the SQLite race package had a 14m46s median. A local standalone run of its 95 top-level tests took 896 seconds.

## Change
- Run the SQLite root package in four race-enabled shards. Each top-level test is selected once from `go test -list`, with all of its subtests.
- Run chat in two race shards, and the session manager plus SQLite store on a separate runner. Two core shards cover the other 200 backend packages, 100 apiece.
- Keep `build-test` as the required gate over all of these jobs, so a failed shard fails the existing check.

## Validation
- Full SQLite race package: 95/95 passed in 896 seconds locally.
- Four isolated race shards: 24/24, 24/24, 24/24, 23/23 passed; 398, 191, 218, and 201 seconds locally. The selection has no duplicates or omissions.
- Chat race package passed in 233 seconds; its two isolated shards passed in 130 and 92 seconds. Session manager and SQLite store passed together in 187 seconds.
- Formatting, backend build/vet, cloud build/vet/race, and golangci-lint v2.13.2 passed locally.
- The 200-package core set took 332 seconds locally with four package slots. Its only failure was an intermittent macOS Goose binary fallback test, which passed alone on retry. The local Codex provider conformance test was excluded because the installed provider version differs from this checkout; CI runs it normally.
- The first hosted run passed every Go check, but its required gate took 8m33s; the core job took 7m16s, prompting the second core split.
- The second hosted Go run passed every job. The required gate completed 4m56s after workflow start: core shards 3m31s/4m25s, SQLite shards 3m07s–4m40s, chat 4m48s, and session/store 4m15s. Windows, lint, and drift jobs passed too.
- The final hosted run passed every check. Chat shards took 3m09s/2m21s, and the slowest race shard took 4m43s after runner start. The required gate took 8m01s from workflow start because the critical SQLite runner waited 3m09s in the queue.

This trades additional runner minutes for a shorter required-check critical path. Refs #5116.

title: feat: install OpenCode 2 into a private npm prefix
body:
Code changes: +519 -69  
Tests: +679 -28  
Others: +3 -0  

## Summary

- First-use OpenCode 2 migration gets a separate 30-minute readiness budget and continues when a request stops waiting; daemon shutdown still cancels it. The three-second auth-command timeout starts after migration finishes.
- OpenCode 2 npm installs use a daemon-configured private prefix, validate that private destination instead of npm's global prefix, and report the private binary directory.
- OpenCode 2 data-home resolution rejects relative paths and fails closed; the first v2 operation migrates any legacy shared store into the isolated home without overwriting existing isolated state. SQLite is copied through a consistent snapshot, while migration locking, file copies, and snapshot retries honor caller cancellation.
- OpenCode binary discovery and version probing share one overall deadline. Classified major-version mismatches remain actionable only after a complete search; incomplete searches preserve timeout or cancellation errors.
- Settings keeps installation controls available for a wrong-major binary while showing the actionable mismatch reason in the row and tooltip.
- The system-install service no longer imports the OpenCode adapter; install path policy is supplied by daemon composition through service dependencies.

## Tests

- All 23 GitHub checks passed on `d84221bc30be83610f4125542a781de7058a4342`. Local workflow runners could not start because Docker Desktop rejected the Docker socket bind mount; the frontend runner was stopped while startup was stalled. Native Windows checks were verified in GitHub CI.
- The migration-budget fix adds regressions for migration exceeding the auth-command timeout, readiness work exceeding the ordinary 10-second auth budget, canceled waiters, daemon shutdown, and explicit auth-timeout overrides. title: feat: configure project workspace cleanup commands
body:
Code changes: +386 -66  
Tests: +430 -18  
Others: +117 -0  

## What changed
- Add Project Settings for ordered workspace cleanup commands and expose the existing project cleanup retry action in that page.
- Run cleanup before permanent managed Git worktree retirement in Kill, Cleanup, replacement, and failed-spawn rollback paths. Pass project variables and protected source/worktree paths, with bounded output and value redaction.
- Preserve the workspace and return the failed step when a command fails, so the user can fix it and retry.
- Report a cleanup script failure to Kill callers with a specific, safe error instead of a generic internal error.

## Scope
Scratch directories are excluded. App quit still preserves sessions and does not invoke cleanup commands.


## Review fixes (2026-10-07)
- Cleanup commands still have no execution timer. Daemon shutdown cancels them; a one-second `WaitDelay` bounds output-pipe drainage after shell exit or cancellation.
- Release the project workspace gate while cleanup runs, including failed-spawn rollback. Recheck live ownership under the gate before removal; prevent concurrent cleanup of the same session.
- Save terminal intent and remove restore markers before user commands. A failed orchestrator retirement now remains terminated and reachable by Retry cleanup.
- Return only the failed step and safe status to API, CLI, and UI callers. Keep the bounded output tail in local logs; share the setup/cleanup shell runner, protected environment merge, and longest-first value redaction.
- Detach cancellation only for orchestrator retirement; retain the caller context for the replacement spawn. Shorten the no-time-limit regression to three seconds against a two-second teardown budget.
- Validation on `c02daeed2`: all 23 GitHub checks passed. Full local session-manager and session-service race suites, Go build, Go vet, and pinned golangci-lint passed (zero issues).
- Native macOS Electron QA: started a real Claude Code worker, archived it with a failing cleanup step, verified Retry returned only the step/exit status, then saved a fix and verified `Cleaned 1; skipped 0`. Retry remained disabled during unsaved edits. Current screenshots and the test sequence are in the [October 7 QA comment](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6094#issuecomment-6033761725).
- Local validation gaps: the broad backend race attempt hit disk/cache errors and installed-agent discovery timeouts. The local frontend typecheck was stopped after 16 minutes; complete frontend checks passed in CI. Linux/Windows native checks passed in CI. Shutdown, rollback, and Windows paths have automated coverage; they were not repeated manually in this run. The October 6 notes below describe the prior head.

## Update (2026-10-06)
- Removed the cleanup command timeout, including inherited request and teardown deadlines. Workspace removal gets a fresh bounded context after commands finish.
- Merged current `main` and kept both Environment and Workspace cleanup pages.
- Added a 31-second cleanup regression that verifies command completion, workspace removal, and session termination after the original teardown budget expires. The focused Go race checks, Go build, Go vet, and generated API/sqlc drift checks passed locally. The focused frontend tests passed (2 files, 27 tests). After restoring the Node SQLite build, the full frontend suite also passed locally (395 files; 6,311 passed, 6 skipped). All 23 current-head GitHub checks passed, including full frontend checks, Go race suites, native CLI checks on Linux/macOS/Windows, and renderer smoke.

- Manual check: ran the real Electron app from `codex/project-workspace-cleanup` against isolated data at `~/.ao/dev/pr6094-no-timeout-20261006/data` (renderer `localhost:5175`, daemon `127.0.0.1:31794`). Both settings pages are present; cleanup shows the no-time-limit text. Saved a `sleep 31` command and confirmed it persisted after reopening the page. This settings check did not execute a session cleanup; the 31-second regression covers that path. The dev app was stopped after the check.
- Local validation limits: the full Go run hit an ACP replay timeout and an installed Codex protocol mismatch. Native CLI and product-ui tests also hit timeouts. The first full frontend run had a project-flow timeout and browser-profile import failures. A direct SQLite probe confirmed that Electron rebuilt its native module for ABI 130 while Node requires ABI 137; rebuilding for Node cleared that environment issue, and the full frontend rerun passed. The initial full Go run and long-running local typecheck were stopped. Local lint reported zero issues but exceeded its timer. CI passed all of these required gates on the pushed head.

## Verification before this update
Before this update (`ddf5b66c9`), frontend typecheck, E2E typecheck, and the full frontend suite passed (377 files; 5,978 passed, 7 skipped). Focused Go race tests, Go build/vet, and golangci-lint passed. The isolated macOS Electron run on the preceding head verified the project flows; a new regression test covers local-only settings after merging `main`. The local full Go race run is blocked by an installed Codex protocol conformance mismatch; all 14 current-head GitHub checks passed, including full Go race and Windows workspace jobs.

## Manual testing evidence (2026-10-01)
Tested in an isolated macOS Electron dev build containing PRs #6091, #6092, and #6094, using a disposable local Git project and scratch AO data.

- Saved a cleanup step in Project Settings → Workspace cleanup. Killing `manual-settings-1` appended the dummy project variable and matching `AO_WORKTREE_PATH`/`PWD` values to `cleanup.log`; the worktree was removed.
- Changed the step to `exit 7` and killed `manual-settings-2`. The worktree remained. In-app Retry cleanup reported `Cleaned 0; skipped 1` with `step 1: exit status 7`. After restoring the working step, retry reported `Cleaned 1; skipped 0`, and the worktree was removed.
- Rebuilt the dev app with the CLI error fix and repeated the failure on `manual-settings-3`. Kill returned `WORKSPACE_CLEANUP_FAILED` with a safe instruction to fix the script and retry. The worktree remained until the restored step and in-app retry reported `Cleaned 1; skipped 0`.

### Screenshots

![Successful workspace cleanup retry in the desktop app](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd50cb89-18fe-4d28-89ce-f23c0bd2405f)

![Cleanup log confirms injected value and working directory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a74facb-b96a-4297-9e96-58e43a93e7da)

## Manual QA update (2026-10-03)
In a fresh, isolated macOS Electron app, imported a disposable Git project, saved and reopened two ordered cleanup steps, and created workers through the UI. Clean archive ran both steps once in the worktree and removed it. A failing step 2 preserved the worktree; retry showed `Cleaned 0; skipped 1` and the exit status, then a saved fix produced `Cleaned 1; skipped 0` and removed it. Retry stayed disabled while edits were unsaved. A dirty worktree remained intact and retry reported `workspace has uncommitted changes`; removing the disposable file let retry clean it. App quit left the orchestrator worktree and cleanup log unchanged (18 lines). The app also exposed a stale archive-failure banner after successful retry; this PR now clears it, verified in Electron without reloading. The screenshots above and [QA comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6094#issuecomment-5966276816) show the settings/log and retry UI; remaining rare lifecycle and platform checks are listed below.

## QA plan and remaining checks

Use a disposable Git project and scratch AO data. Have cleanup steps write to a log in the source project so their output survives worktree removal.

### Manual scenario

1. Save three ordered cleanup steps that record their step number, `pwd`, `AO_SOURCE_TREE_PATH`, `AO_WORKTREE_PATH`, and a dummy project variable. Reopen Workspace cleanup and confirm order and persistence.
2. Spawn a session. Confirm no cleanup yet. Let an agent exit while its workspace remains, and separately quit/reopen the app; expect no cleanup from either event and the worktree to remain.
3. Kill a clean disposable session. Expect steps 1–3 once, in order, after its processes stop and while its worktree still exists; then expect the worktree to be removed. Repeat through the explicit Cleanup path.
4. Change step 2 to `exit 7` and put a marker in step 3. Kill another session. Expect `WORKSPACE_CLEANUP_FAILED`, a terminated session, a preserved worktree, no step-3 marker, and Retry cleanup reporting `Cleaned 0; skipped 1` with the failed step. Fix and save step 2; expect Retry to report `Cleaned 1; skipped 0` and remove the worktree. Confirm Retry is disabled while the edited script is unsaved.
5. Make a disposable worktree dirty before cleanup. Expect it to remain intact with an uncommitted-changes reason; do not assume the script is skipped before the dirty-worktree check.

### QA matrix

| Check | Pass condition |
| --- | --- |
| Retirement triggers | Kill, explicit Cleanup, replacement, and failed-spawn rollback invoke cleanup before permanent managed worktree removal. |
| Non-triggers | Agent exit and app quit do not run cleanup while preserving the workspace; scratch workspaces do not run this Git-worktree hook. |
| Execution contract | Nonblank steps run in order in fresh shells inside the worktree, with correct project variables and protected paths; later steps stop after failure. |
| Failure and retry | A failed step preserves the worktree and reports its index; saving a fix and retrying cleans it, while unsaved edits cannot be retried. |
| Worktree safety | Dirty worktrees remain intact; an absent worktree is a no-op; paths outside AO's managed root are refused. |
| Limits, errors, and platforms | Commands have no automatic time limit; output is bounded in local logs and configured values are redacted; API/CLI/UI errors contain only the failed step and safe status; `sh` runs on macOS/Linux and `cmd` on Windows. |
| Settings isolation | Save/reopen preserves step order and unrelated project settings; save failures are visible. |

### Evidence to attach after the run

An uncut recording of failure → preserved worktree → saved fix → Retry success, plus screenshots of the log, exact UI counts, CLI error, and worktree presence/removal. Record pass, fail, or blocked for each matrix row and attach focused results for rare lifecycle and platform cases.

title: feat(agents): apply provider-profile switch to running sessions (exit-agent + resume-agent)
body:
Follow-up to #6095 (provider profiles + settings). That issue covers configuration and new sessions; this one covers applying a provider switch to **already-running** sessions.

## User story

I switch the default provider (or a role assignment) in Settings — and my running sessions keep chatting on the old provider until I restart them by hand. I want AO to offer applying the switch to running sessions, preserving their context.

## Design

The machinery already exists — this is orchestration + UX:

- `ExitAgent` (session manager) stops only the agent controller; the session, its worktree, and the native conversation survive.
- `ResumeAgentWithMode` re-launches through the full env re-assembly path, so once #6095's profile injection lands, every resume picks up the new provider for free. TUI resumes via `claude --resume <native-id>`; chat sessions via the chat resume path preserving the provider conversation id.
- New: `POST /api/v1/provider-profiles/apply` with `{sessionIds?: []}` — empty = all running claude-code sessions whose stamped profile differs from the newly effective one; per-session result `{state: applied|failed|skipped, error}`; bounded concurrency.
- UI: after saving assignments, if stale running sessions exist, a dialog offers "apply now" with a per-session result toast. (Requires the session metadata provider stamp from #6095 to detect staleness.)

## Stated risk

Cross-provider `--resume` is best-effort: the local transcript exists, but model ids from provider A may not resolve on provider B. If the resume is rejected, the session must stay exited-and-restorable (`/restore`) with the error surfaced — never a lost session. The existing force-fresh relaunch policy is the documented fallback for unreliable provider pairs.

## Acceptance criteria

- running TUI worker on z.ai → switch default to Anthropic → apply → pane relaunches without `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, prior transcript visible (resume worked);
- a chat session continues the same conversation after apply;
- a failing resume leaves the session restorable and reports the error without affecting other sessions in the batch;
- gofmt / `go test -race` / vitest clean.

title: [Feature]: Add Hermes Agent to the current supported-agent registry
body:
## Problem

I want to run a heterogeneous local agent team in Agent Orchestrator, using Hermes Agent alongside Pi, Goose, and Codex.

AO currently lists Pi and Goose among its 32 supported coding agents, but Hermes is not in the current supported-agent registry. This leaves Hermes sessions outside AO's project-level task, worktree, lifecycle, and review workflow.

There was earlier Hermes work in #1406, and #1405 records a prior process-runtime lifecycle problem. Issue #1406 was closed because Hermes support did not appear relevant or needed at that point, with an invitation to open a new issue if the need remained. The current use case is specifically a mixed-agent local team, not only controlling AO from Hermes through Discord or Telegram.

Is first-class Hermes Agent support still planned or something the maintainers would accept?

## Proposed direction

If this fits AO's roadmap, add Hermes as a first-class worker adapter with a deliberately small initial scope:

- detect an installed `hermes` CLI;
- launch the native interactive Hermes TUI inside an AO worker and bind it to that worker's repository/worktree;
- map process lifecycle into AO status so the worker does not appear completed while Hermes is still active;
- support stop/restart and conversation resume where Hermes exposes a stable session interface;
- document local setup for the platforms AO and Hermes both support.

Hermes messaging gateways, cross-platform conversation routing, memory synchronization, and Hermes-to-AO remote control could remain separate follow-ups. The initial goal would only be reliable worker execution inside AO.

## Alternatives considered

Running Hermes manually in another terminal or terminal-session manager works for process organization, but it loses AO's shared project context, task ownership, worktree isolation, pull-request/CI state, and orchestrator supervision.

## References

- Previous Hermes plugin request: #1406
- Previous Hermes worker lifecycle report: #1405
- Hermes Agent: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent
- Current AO supported-agent list: https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#supported-agents

## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues / discussions for something similar
- [ ] I am willing to help implement this if maintainers agree on scope

title: bug(ui): Merge button gives no pending feedback — no spinner while the merge request is in flight

## Summary

Clicking **Merge** on a ready-to-merge PR card in the session inspector gives no visual feedback while the merge request is in flight. The button stays visually identical until the merge completes (which can take several seconds on the daemon round-trip), so it looks like the click did nothing — users tend to click again.

title: ao session ls --json omits displayName (session get --json includes it)

**What happened**
`ao session ls --json` does not include a session's display name, while `ao session get <id> --json` does.

**Steps**
1. Spawn a session with a name: `ao spawn --name "#52 (claude-code tiếp quản)" …`
2. `ao session get prime-compliance-29 --json` → `"displayName": "#52 (claude-code tiếp quản)"`

`ls --json` carries `displayName` like `get --json`, so scripts that supervise many sessions can tell them apart (we run AO from an external scheduler and identify release/review sessions by name) without one `get` call per session.

**Environment**
AO 0.13.2 (also 0.13.1), macOS arm64.

title: fix(cloud): stop desktop sign-in tab freezing on the provider page
body:
## Problem
After a successful desktop AO Cloud sign-in, the browser tab stays on Google's dimmed account chooser with a progress bar forever. WorkOS redirects straight to `ao-app://callback`; the browser hands that URL to the OS without committing a page, so the tab keeps showing the last thing it drew.

## Fix
- **Control plane:** new unauthenticated `GET /api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback`. It renders a plain "Finishing sign-in" page (same styling and security headers as the GitHub callback pages), forwards only `code`/`state`/`error`/`error_description` to the fixed `ao-app://callback` target via meta refresh, and adds an "Open Agent Orchestrator" button as a fallback. Nothing is exchanged or stored. The code is useless without the PKCE verifier held by the desktop app. An incomplete callback gets a 400 page and is not forwarded.
- **Desktop:** packaged builds use `${AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL || https://api.aoagents.dev}/api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback` as the WorkOS redirect URI. The loopback callback server now only starts for `http://127.0.0.1|localhost` redirects (it previously matched any http(s) URL). Dev builds are unchanged.
- Docs updated (`cloud/docs/deployment.md`, `cloud/README.md`).

## Rollout (order matters)
1. Deploy the control plane to staging and production.
2. Register `https://staging-api.aoagents.dev/api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback` and `https://api.aoagents.dev/api/cloud/v1/auth/desktop/callback` in WorkOS. Staging and prod share one WorkOS environment.
3. Only then ship a desktop release. Keep `ao-app://callback` registered so older desktop builds can still sign in.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/httpapi -run DesktopAuth`: param allowlist (no open redirect), HTML escaping of provider errors, error forwarding, 400 on incomplete callbacks, no-store/no-referrer headers.
- `vitest src/main/cloud-auth.test.ts`: 15/15, with the redirect URI assertion updated.
- Not yet verified in a real browser end to end. That happens on staging before the desktop release.

## Risks
- Some browsers may hold the meta-refresh protocol hand-off behind a click. The button covers that case, and staging verification will show how Chrome and Safari behave.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
