title: feat(chat): add Command Code ACP Chat driver (v1.74.0 ships cmd acp)
body:
﻿### Problem

Command Code ships a first-party ACP agent but AO has no Chat driver for it, so Command Code sessions are TUI-only and the desktop never offers the TUI ⇄ Chat toggle.

Earlier discussion (#5781, #5958) assumed Command Code exposed no machine protocol. That assumption is now stale: `cmd --help` on v1.74.0 lists

```
cmd acp   Run as an ACP agent over stdio (for Zed, etc.)
```

### Verified capability surface

Probed against a live `cmd acp` handshake on Windows, Command Code v1.74.0 (2026-10-02):

```json
{"protocolVersion":1,
 "agentCapabilities":{
   "loadSession":true,
   "promptCapabilities":{"audio":false,"image":true,"embeddedContext":true},
   "mcpCapabilities":{"http":true,"sse":false},
   "sessionCapabilities":{"list":{},"resume":{},"close":{}}},
 "authMethods":[{"id":"command-code-cli","name":"Command Code CLI login"}],
 "agentInfo":{"name":"Command Code","version":"1.74.0"}}
```

This clears AO `chatProductionFloor` (streaming, approvals, interrupt, resume) because `loadSession: true` provides resume and ACP carries real `session/request_permission` approvals.

`session/new` advertises five modes and two live config options:

| id | name |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Standard |
| `auto-accept` | Accept Edits |
| `plan` | Plan |
| `dont-ask` | Don'"'"'t Ask |
| `bypass` | Bypass Permissions |

Config options: `model` (category `model`, 85 entries) and `effort` (category `thought_level`: off/high/max). Both are provider-owned, so AO needs no hardcoded model list.

### Proposed direction

Add `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/commandcodeacp/`, built with `nativeacp.New` against the existing Command Code agent plugin, and register it in `chatdriver/registry`. Mapping:

| AO permission mode | Command Code mode id |
| --- | --- |
| default | `default` |
| accept-edits / auto | `auto-accept` |
| bypass-permissions | `bypass` |

`plan` and `dont-ask` have no AO equivalent and would stay reachable only through Command Code'"'"'s own UI.

Launch is `cmd acp --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update --trust [--model …] [--permission-mode …]`; the existing plugin still owns binary resolution and auth.

Refs #5781, #5958, and the TUI work in #5959.

### Verification status

Handshake and `session/new` probed directly against v1.74.0 on Windows. A full `session/prompt` round trip was **not** exercised, so streaming deltas, tool-call updates, and permission round-trips still need end-to-end confirmation against a logged-in account.

title: fix(modelcatalog): Command Code TUI picker shows descriptions instead of model names
body:
### Problem

In TUI mode the Command Code model picker shows model *descriptions* where names should be, so the list reads as marketing copy rather than a set of models.

`cmd --list-models` prints an id and a description, with no friendly name:

```text
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    hybrid-attention long-context reasoning
deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash   fast hybrid-attention reasoning (default)
minimaxai/minimax-m3        600B sparse-MoE agentic coding with 1M context
```

#5959 wires `command-code` to the shared `parseAgyModels` in `adapters/agent/modelcatalog/catalog.go`, which treats everything after the id as the label:

```go
label := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, fields[0]))
if label == "" {
    label = id
}
```

That is correct for Agy'"'"'s format, where the trailing text is a display name, but for Command Code it is the description. The picker therefore offers entries like "balances intelligence and cost" and "agentic coding & reasoning" as if they were model names.

Chat mode is unaffected. The ACP catalog supplies real names (`Claude Sonnet 5.5`, `DeepSeek V4 Pro (latest)`) and the correct value/description split.

### Proposed direction

Give `command-code` a parser that prefers the model id as the label, or one that derives a readable name from the id and keeps the trailing text as a description. The id alone is unambiguous and matches what the user passes to `--model`.

Refs #5959.

### Notes

The two `TestResolveBinary*` failures in the same package are unrelated and tracked separately.

title: feat(chat): Command Code ACP Chat driver, and fix TUI model labels
body:
Code changes: +779 -147  
Tests: +1135 -7  
Others: +246 -7 (generated OpenAPI spec and frontend TS types)

## Summary

Two fixes for the Command Code harness, both verified against a real Command Code v1.74.0 install.

Closes Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#6141
Closes Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator#6142

> **Stacking.** This branch is built on `feat/commandcode-tui-5958` (#5959), which is still open and whose branch lives in the fork rather than in this repository. GitHub therefore cannot use that branch as this PR's base, so this PR targets `main` and its diff also contains #5959. The counts above are the full diff against `main`; reviewers should read the two commits on top of #5959 as the actual change.

### 1. Chat mode was missing because the premise was stale

Earlier Command Code discussion assumed it exposed no machine protocol. That is no longer true — v1.74.0 ships a first-party ACP agent:

```text
cmd acp   Run as an ACP agent over stdio (for Zed and other ACP clients)
```

Probed against a live handshake:

| Capability | Value | Effect in AO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loadSession` | `true` | clears the resume requirement of `chatProductionFloor` |
| `promptCapabilities` | `image`, `embeddedContext` | image and embedded-context prompts |
| `mcpCapabilities` | `http` | MCP over HTTP |
| `sessionCapabilities` | `list`, `resume`, `close` | enumeration and resume |

Because ACP carries real `session/request_permission`, approvals are first-class in Chat mode — unlike the TUI path, where Command Code's hook surface has no permission-request event and cannot distinguish an approval from other in-turn work.

`session/new` advertises five modes, so every AO permission mode maps exactly:

| AO mode | Command Code mode id |
| --- | --- |
| default | `default` |
| accept-edits | `auto-accept` |
| auto | `auto-accept` |
| bypass-permissions | `bypass` |

`plan` and `dont-ask` have no AO equivalent and are deliberately left unexposed.

Model and effort come from the provider's own catalog (`model`, 85 entries; `effort`, category `thought_level`), so AO keeps no hardcoded model list. Verified against a running daemon:

```text
id=model  cat=model  n=85   value=claude-sonnet-5-5  name='Claude Sonnet 5.5'
id=effort cat=thought_level n=3  off / high / max
```

The binding launches `cmd acp --skip-onboarding --no-auto-update --trust` through `nativeacp.New`, reusing the existing Command Code agent plugin for binary resolution and auth. Registration in `chatdriver/registry` is the whole capability gate, which is what makes the desktop render the TUI ↔ Chat toggle.

### 2. The TUI model picker offered descriptions as models

```text
fast hybrid-attention reasoning
600B sparse-MoE agentic coding with 1M c...
balances intelligence and cost
```

`cmd --list-models` prints `<id>  <description>`, and the trailing text is marketing copy, not a display name. #5959 wired `command-code` to the shared `parseAgyModels`, which reads everything after the id as the label — correct for Agy, wrong here.

Command Code publishes no friendly name in this listing, so the id is the only label that cannot misdescribe a model, and it is exactly what `--model` accepts.

`TestCommandCodeCatalogParsesTabularModelList` asserted a fabricated format:

```text
anthropic/claude-opus-4-1  Claude Opus 4.1
```

Real v1.74.0 emits bare ids (`claude-opus-5-5`) plus descriptions, with no `anthropic/` prefix. The invented fixture made the wrong behavior look like an intentional contract; it is replaced with real output.

## Validation

Both changes build clean and were exercised against a live Command Code v1.74.0 install on Windows.

Model catalog, run against the real 85-row listing:

```text
parsed 86 models
default model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
every label equals its id
no heading or boilerplate parsed as a model
```

The 86th row is `typesafe/jev`, listed under a separate "Decision models (headless only)" section; the banner's "85" does not count it.

Daemon, run against an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`:

```text
GET /api/v1/settings   -> 14 chatHarnesses including command-code
GET /api/v1/agents     -> command-code, authStatus authorized
GET .../conversation/config-options -> 85 models + 3 effort levels, correct names
```

Tests:

```text
ok  internal/adapters/chatdriver/commandcodeacp
ok  internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry        (TestShippedChatDrivers)
ok  internal/domain
ok  internal/service/chat                        (run separately, 101s)
```

`go build ./cmd/ao` clean, `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean.

### Known failures not introduced here

Confirmed identical on the untouched base:

```text
modelcatalog: TestAutoHandDiscoveryReadsConfigurationWithoutRunningBinary  (autohand not installed)
modelcatalog: TestConfigCatalogDiscoveryAndFingerprint                   (continue not installed)
commandcode:  TestResolveBinaryFindsCommandCodeOnPath
commandcode:  TestResolveBinaryMissingReturnsErrAgentBinaryNotFound
```

The two `commandcode` failures appear only when Command Code is installed locally, which is why CI is green. They are test-isolation gaps in #5959's adapter: the first sets `PATH` but `binaryutil` also searches fixed `WinPaths`, so the real `cmdc.cmd` wins; the second skips on `UnixPaths` being present but never clears the Windows paths.

### Not verified

A full `session/prompt` round trip was not exercised end to end. Streaming deltas, tool-call updates, and the approval round trip against a logged-in account still need manual confirmation.

## Merge status: up to date with `main`

`main` has been merged into this branch, so the PR is no longer `CONFLICTING`. Two things were fixed in the process:

- The harness migration originally claimed number `0171`, which `main` had already taken with `0171_shell_preview_capability.sql`. Two files claiming one version makes goose refuse to build its history, which would have failed daemon startup on every existing install. It is now renumbered to `0179`, past everything currently on `main`, with the ledger, the reconcile comment and the migration tests following. (`main` claimed the intermediate numbers 0172-0178 while this PR was open, so the file moved more than once.)
- The Command Code ACP binding registered a `ValidateTurnSettings` that rejected every real approval change with "restart Chat", even though Command Code implements `session/set_mode`. The transport calls the validator before the runtime setter, so no approval change could ever reach a live session. The validator is gone; `session/set_mode` applies the change, and a provider answering `-32601` still surfaces as `ErrACPSetterUnsupported`.

## Screenshots

<!-- Add evidence images here before requesting review. -->

- [ ] Composer showing Command Code selected and the Chat interface available
- [ ] Chat session with streamed assistant output
- [ ] Model picker before this PR (descriptions as labels)
- [ ] Model picker after this PR (ids as labels)

## Risks

- `cmd acp` is recent. The binding pins no minimum version because `ValidateInitialize` is preferable to a version flag that many stdio agents do not implement. `TestVerifiedModeVocabulary` pins the five mode ids read from a live handshake so a future rename is visible rather than silent.
- The five mode ids come from a live v1.74.0 handshake, not from documentation.
- The model-label change alters what users see for this harness only; no other harness shares `parseCommandCodeModels`.

title: fix(inspector): grow the rail back after a narrow-window tab switch
body:
## Problem
When you zoom in or narrow the window, the inspector shrinks to its 300px floor and its top-bar field (the Browser URL bar or the Files filter) wraps to a second row. That part is correct. But if you switch inspector tabs while it is narrow and then zoom back out, the rail stays at 300px and the field stays on the second row. This affects the Browser and Files tabs.

## Root cause
- **The restore re-runs on every tab switch.** Each tab has its own sizing, so switching tabs gives the rail's `min`/`max` callbacks new identities. That re-runs `useResizable`'s restore layout effect.
- **It writes the narrow cap.** The restore clamps against the live max (300px in a narrow window) and writes that into `--ao-inspector-w`.
- **Nothing writes it back.** CSS `max-width` can only shrink the painted width below the var, never grow it above. Without a tab switch the var keeps its earlier wide value, which is why the rail grows back in that case.
- **Origin:** the restore started clamping to the live split width in #5457.

## Fix
- **Preferred width kept separately.** `useResizable` now remembers the width the user asked for (restored, double-click reset, finished drag, or collapsed-rail expand) apart from the clamped width.
- **New opt-in `reclampOnWindowResize`.** On a window `resize`, which includes Electron zoom, it grows a narrow-clamped width back toward that preference. It is batched per animation frame, grow-only, and skipped during a drag. Only the inspector rail opts in, so the sidebar is unchanged.
- **Why grow-only:** narrowing leaves the var alone and CSS caps the paint, as on `main`. So collapsing the sidebar after narrowing still lets the rail grow back.
- **Handle presses:** a press on the resize handle, or a drag in a window too narrow to resize, no longer writes or saves a width. Before, either could save `300` and pin the rail, even across a reload. This also applies to the sidebar's own handle, where a press without movement no longer re-saves its current width. That is harmless.

### Rejected alternative
I first tried letting the var exceed the painted width and relying on CSS `max-width` for the live cap. A review measured three regressions:
- **Blank band during open/close.** Motion resolves `var()` to pixels at the start of the animation, leaving a blank strip of about 110–190px.
- **Sidebar toggle resizes the Browser rail.** The rail, and the embedded browser view, resized on every frame of the sidebar animation.
- **8px snap at drag start.** The CSS cap and the JS cap differ by 8px.

This version keeps the var equal to the painted width on every path except narrowing, where it matches `main`.

## Tests
- **Unit (`useResizable.test.ts`):**
  - a narrow restore grows back on window resize, including after a profile switch;
  - the re-clamp is grow-only;
  - it is off unless opted in;
  - double-click reset works while narrow;
  - a press, or a drag that cannot change the width, writes and saves nothing;
  - a real drag becomes the preference;
  - a resize during an active drag is ignored;
  - a static max still clamps the restore.
- **Unit (`SessionView.test.tsx`):** Browser and Files grow back after a narrow tab switch followed by a widen, with Files keeping its 460px floor.
- **E2E (`e2e/inspector-width-recovery.spec.ts`, @P0):**
  - Browser and Files grow back and unwrap their field after narrow → tab switch → widen, including after a press on the handle;
  - the rail grows back when the sidebar collapses after a narrow window;
  - toggling the sidebar does not resize the Browser rail.
  - The bug specs fail on `main`. The sidebar-collapse spec fails against a version where the re-clamp is not grow-only.
- **Checks run:**
  - [x] `tsc --noEmit` (app and e2e)
  - [x] full renderer vitest (265 files, 4269 passed)
  - [x] e2e on installed Chrome: `inspector-width-recovery`, `browser-address-centering`, `files-narrow-inspector`, `inspector-toggle`, `resize-clamp` (9/9)
  - [ ] Manual in the desktop app: zoom in until the field wraps, switch tabs, zoom out

## Known follow-ups (not changed here)
- Reopening a closed rail by dragging its collapsed edge while the window is narrow still saves 300px through `onCollapsedPointerDown`. This is the same symptom by a different mechanism.

title: fix(desktop): restore terminal focus after switching session tabs
body:
Code changes: +36 -3  
Tests: +135 -0  
Others: +0 -0

Closes #6140.

What
Fix the desktop terminal losing keyboard focus after switching top-bar tabs within a session. Returning with Ctrl+Tab or a tab click restores the caret to the terminal prompt.

Renderer
Retained terminals are blurred when parked. Focus restoration previously depended on a guarded autofocus attempt when `isVisible` changed. That attempt retried for only two frames and stopped when the terminal was parked again.

- Add `AttachableTerminal.requestActivationFocus`, a deferred focus request. `CachedTerminalPortal` calls it on each activation, and the callback checks the current visibility, focus intent, and focused control before restoring the caret.
- Allow top-bar tab buttons and explicitly marked terminal actions to hand focus to the terminal. Dialogs, menus, text fields, and unrelated buttons still block automatic focus.
- Raise `AUTOFOCUS_RETRY_FRAMES` from 2 to 6 so the visibility-driven attempt can retry after a transient focus holder clears.
- Respect `focusRequested={false}` when the deferred callback runs. This preserves the opt-out for automatically opened login terminals and cancels a queued request if the caller revokes focus before it executes.

The two first-attach `prepareForActivation` call sites remain unchanged and use the mount-time autofocus effect.

Tests
Coverage includes restoring activation focus, retaining focus in dialogs and unrelated controls, handing off from terminal-tab controls, and requesting focus once per cache activation. Two added regression tests cover the explicit opt-out and revocation before a queued callback runs. Both fail on the original PR and pass with the guard. Test fakes include the new terminal handle method.

Validation
The user tested Ctrl+Tab in the real Electron app and reported that it works. All 255 tests across `XtermTerminal.test.tsx`, `TerminalPane.test.tsx`, and `useTerminalSession.test.tsx` passed with the opt-out fix under Node 24 and `NODE_ENV=test`.

All four GitHub checks passed on `5364a922d38607f655636cf36a29ed286d26629c`: frontend, renderer smoke, macOS update helper, and gitleaks. The frontend job passed both typechecks, the docs build, package checks, and 5,982 frontend tests with 6 skipped.

The enabled commit hook passed `npm run lint` with zero lint findings after isolating the validation environment from inherited Git identity, global fixture hooks, and installed agent CLIs.

title: fix(sqlite): eliminate migration test lock contention and snapshot bypass (#6128)
body:
### Summary
Resolves #6128 where the Go CI `build-test` job intermittently encountered a 20-minute package timeout in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite`.

### Root Cause
1. `TestOpenPreMigratedSucceedsForMigratedDatabase` used `openMigratedTestDBIn(t, dataDir)`, which bypassed the cached migration snapshot (`migratedDatabaseSnapshot`) and re-executed all 147 migrations from scratch using `migrate(db)`. Under heavy concurrent load or `-race`, this held `gooseMu` and performed disk-heavy schema replay.
2. In `buildMigrationSnapshots` (`migrate_snapshot_test.go`), `db := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+databasePath+snapshotDSN)` did not restrict `db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)`. During sequential migration playback across dozens of migration steps, SQLite connections could pool and contend for file locks on `ao.db`.

### Fix
- Updated `openMigratedTestDBIn` to clone from `openMigratedDatabaseCopyAt(t, dataDir, version, pragmas)`, reusing the snapshot cache and reducing execution time from >1.2s to 0.02s without replaying migrations from scratch.
- Added `db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)` to `buildMigrationSnapshots` on the temporary checkpoint database handle to eliminate connection pooling lock contention.

title: feat(terminal): start shell terminal PTYs at a requested grid
body:
## What

`POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` accepts optional `cols`/`rows`, and the runtime starts the shell's PTY at that grid instead of the hardcoded 220×50.

- `ports.RuntimeConfig.InitialSize` (new `ports.TerminalSize`) carries the grid to the runtime.
- **pty-host (macOS, Linux, Windows):** takes an optional leading `--size=<cols>x<rows>` argument and starts the PTY and rendered surface at it.
- **tmux:** uses the size for `new-session -x/-y`.

This is PR 1 of 2. The renderer change that measures the terminal and sends the grid is the stacked follow-up PR.

## Why

A new terminal shows a stray reverse-video `%` above its first prompt. The shell starts at 220 columns before any viewer attaches. zsh pads its partial-line marker (`PROMPT_SP`) for 220 columns, and when that output is replayed into a narrower xterm the line wraps, leaving the `%` on its own row. You can reproduce it outside AO in a narrow window with `stty cols 220; zsh -f`.

## How

- **No regressions for existing clients.** Size is optional, and a request without it behaves exactly as before (220×50). That covers current desktop and mobile builds, headless agent spawns, and Settings command terminals. Sending only one of `cols`/`rows`, or out-of-range values, returns 400 `INVALID_TERMINAL_SIZE`.
- **pty-host argv stays backward compatible.** The `--size=` argument is only added when a size is set, so unsized spawns use the exact legacy positional argv. A host started with the legacy argv (for example by a still-running older daemon after an app update) parses as before. Session ids never contain `=`, so the flag can't be mistaken for one.
- 220×50 now lives in one named default per runtime (`defaultHostSize`, `defaultSessionCols/Rows`), used only when no grid was supplied. Follow-ups: mobile and command terminals send their size, then the size becomes required and the default is removed.

## Testing

- `go test ./...` (backend, clean environment): passes, except `codexappserver` `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider`, which fails identically on `main` because it depends on the locally installed Codex version.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on the touched packages: 0 issues. `go vet` passes for `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=linux`.
- New tests:
  - pty-host argv round trip and rejection of invalid sizes; the unsized argv stays legacy.
  - `Create` passes `InitialSize` to the spawner.
  - `newConPTY` starts at the requested winsize (darwin, linux).
  - tmux `new-session` args with and without a size.
  - Shell-terminal service passes the size to the runtime.
  - HTTP: size passed through, an omitted size stays zero, invalid sizes are rejected.

title: fix(terminal): create shell PTYs at the new tab's measured grid
body:
## What

A new shell tab no longer shows a stray `%` above its first prompt. The tab's xterm mounts and measures itself before the shell exists, and the daemon creates the PTY at exactly that grid. The same xterm then attaches to the created PTY instead of being replaced.

**Stacked on #6174** (backend: optional `cols`/`rows` on create). Merge that first.

## Why

The PTY used to start at a hardcoded 220×50 before any viewer attached. zsh padded its partial-line marker for 220 columns, so in a narrower panel the marker wrapped and the `%` was left on its own row. This follows Orca's approach: spawn a terminal only once its pane has measured its grid.

## How

**Measure first, then create** (`eedab5e91`)
- The pending tab mounts the real terminal, which fits and calls `AttachableTerminal.measureGrid()`. That returns xterm's own fit proposal, or `null` while the host can't be measured.
- The open mutation waits for that grid, then `POST`s it as `cols`/`rows`.
- When the shell is created, the terminal cache re-keys the pending entry to the created handle before any pane renders it. Portals use a stable `portalKey`, so the measured xterm carries on and attaches.
- `lib/pending-shell-terminals.ts` coordinates the mutation, the pending terminal and the cache. If xterm can't start, the creation fails and the tab is dropped.

**Fixes found while testing the real desktop app**
- **Parked terminals keep their grid** (`b1b3401a1`). With several tabs opened quickly, a tab hidden before its handover was fitted to the parking slot (2 columns) just as the shell's first output arrived. That left a `%` and a doubled prompt in every hidden tab. Now parking abandons a pending hidden-allowed activation fit, and a parked terminal attaches at its measured grid.
- **Tabs keep their place** (`55af1238a`). The session's tab order is keyed by tab key. A created tab was treated as new and re-appended behind still-pending tabs, so tabs bounced around the strip. The stored order now maps pending handles to created ones.
- **Closing a pending tab cancels its creation** (`3d0a2b94d`). Quickly creating and closing terminals left terminals nobody kept. Closing a still-pending tab sent a DELETE the daemon answered with 404, while its creation carried on and later published a real shell. Now a creation still waiting for its grid never asks for a PTY, and one already in flight deletes the shell it gets back.
- **Pending tabs survive list refetches** (`7653e542a`). Closing a terminal and opening a new one flashed the session's chat view. The close's list refetch landed before the new PTY existed, and the daemon can't list a shell it hasn't created yet. Pending tabs are now kept in every list response until their create request settles.

**Review fixes** (`77b2b695e`, `f7da26040`)
- An unmeasurable pending terminal (zero geometry mid-layout, unready fonts) retries each frame until it can measure, then fits and reports.
- When a refetch already lists the created shell next to its pending row, the success handler drops the pending row.
- `open()` is the only place a pending tab is created.

**Speed** (`9c3ae86c2`)
- A terminal created at the grid it just measured attaches without a second activation fit, saving about 50 ms.

**Existing clients and scope**
- Mobile and older desktop builds send no size and keep the daemon's 220×50 (see #6174).
- Cloud shells and the browser preview build don't wait for a grid.
- Keystrokes typed before the PTY exists are still dropped, as they are today.

## Testing

**Automated**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Full frontend suite: passes. The only failure seen was `browser-history-store`, which flaked under parallel load and passes on its own.
- Tests cover:
  - Waiting for the grid before creating, and the handover before publishing.
  - Init failure dropping the tab, and the same xterm surviving adoption.
  - A parked handover attaching without a fit, and a measured grid attaching without a second fit.
  - Tab order, pending tabs surviving refetches, and the duplicate pending row.
  - Retrying a transiently unmeasurable grid.

  Each regression test fails without its fix.

**Real desktop app** (combined with #6174/#6196/#6203, isolated data)
- **Seven tabs opened quickly** (scripted via DevTools): 21/21 terminals clean across three runs. Before the parked-grid fix, Terminals 1–6 showed the `%` every run.
- **Tab order** recorded during seven quick opens: tabs only ever append.
- **Close-and-reopen loop:** 0/6 chat flashes, versus 6/6 before.
- **Speed, production renderer build:** click to tab about 42 ms, to visible prompt about 100 ms. The development build is about 278 ms. Orca measured about 220 ms on the same machine with a screen-capture method.

title: fix(review): let Codex Chat reviewers reach the network
body:
## Summary

Codex reviewers in Chat mode could never finish a review. Reviewer Chat starts Codex with a read-only sandbox and approvals off (`approvalPolicy: never`). Codex's read-only sandbox has no network by default, so the reviewer could neither use `gh` nor call `ao review submit`. It also couldn't ask for access mid-turn.

This PR adds `networkAccess: true` to the per-turn read-only sandbox policy. Workspace writes stay blocked. Only reviewer-owned conversations set `ReadOnly`, so worker Chat is unaffected.

## Evidence

Observed on worker session `agent-orchestrator-70`, reviewing PR #5928, review `eb57bd82…`. The Codex rollout for the reviewer thread shows:

- The `ao review submit` call failed with: `call daemon: Post "http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/agent-orchestrator-70/reviews/submit": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:3001: connect: operation not permitted`
- Codex's final message: "GitHub posting failed due to network access. AO bookkeeping also failed because access to the local daemon was denied."
- The turn ran with `sandbox_policy: read-only` and `approval_policy: never`.

## Scope

This PR fixes only the sandbox. The 22-minute "Working" stall from the same report has a separate cause: reviewer provider events are dropped by the worker-session generation fence in `projectProviderEventTx`. Open PR #6118 already fixes that, and doesn't touch the Codex sandbox.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/codexappserver/ ./internal/service/chat/` passes with a CI-like `PATH`. The conformance test fails locally only because the installed Codex CLI (0.159.2) is newer than the generated contract; this is unrelated.
- Ran against a real `codex app-server` 0.159.2 with `sandbox: read-only` and approvals `never`:
  - Without `networkAccess`: `curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/` fails with `Couldn't connect to server`.
  - With `networkAccess: true`: the same curl connects (HTTP 404 from `/`).
  - With `networkAccess: true`: `touch` in the workspace still fails with `Operation not permitted`.
- I did not run a full end-to-end review submission, because Chat reviewer events are dropped until #6118 lands.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `review.reviewer_activity_state` stays `active` after a Chat review is cancelled or ends. It has no visible impact today, because the inspector only treats a review as live while a run is running.
- Reviewer Chat has no model selector. The reviewer conversation API has no settings endpoint, and #4568's picker only applies to the project settings, the inspector and the TUI launch.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode ACP method-not-found leaves steering delivery handles reserved
body:
### What went wrong?

`ao send --steer` to a running OpenCode Chat session reports `CHAT_STEER_UNCERTAIN`, and repeated `--recover-only` calls remain unresolved. A definite JSON-RPC “method not found” response should be reported as unsupported/rejected, rather than as potentially delivered guidance. This prevents the orchestrator from knowing whether a correction took effect or can safely be resent.

### Environment

- AO macOS arm64 desktop: `0.13.4-nightly.202610021833`.
- Bundled daemon build metadata: revision `a0e7b33430a01700a5348cf87576e3d004a7a8fd`, `vcs.modified=true`.
- OpenCode: `1.18.33`, Chat mode through `opencode acp`.
- Source analysis uses that revision. The same ACP error branch is still present in the default branch when checked on 2026-10-03. I have not rebuilt the installed daemon.

### Observed AO behavior

While an OpenCode turn was active:

```sh
ao send --session <opencode-session> --steer --message '<guidance>'
# exit 1, CHAT_STEER_UNCERTAIN
# preserve the delivery handle printed by AO

ao send --session <opencode-session> --steer --recover-only \
  --client-message-id <original-handle>
# remains unresolved and was not resent
```

Four separate OpenCode handles remain `reserved` with empty `provider_turn_id` and NULL `settled_at`. The first has remained unresolved for over two hours. In the same project, 31 Codex handles have `accepted` receipts. This comparison is an observation, not proof of a general harness-wide guarantee.

### Isolated protocol reproduction, without any model request

Start a fresh `opencode acp --pure --cwd <empty-repro-directory>` with isolated XDG config/data/cache/state directories. Exchange `initialize` successfully, then send this request and wait for its response:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"_session/steering","params":{"sessionId":"ao-repro-no-session","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"Probe extension support only; no session or model call."}],"_meta":{"steering":{"idleBehavior":"promptRequired"}}}}
```

OpenCode replies immediately:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"\"Method not found\": _session/steering","data":{"method":"_session/steering"}}}
```

No `session/new` or `session/prompt` was sent. The owned process exited normally with code 0 after stdin EOF. This proves that this OpenCode version rejects the extension; it does not claim that the isolated probe exercised AO's entire active-turn path. The real AO calls and durable rows above provide the separate delivery-state observation.

### Source path

At the build revision:

- [ACP steering](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a0e7b33430a01700a5348cf87576e3d004a7a8fd/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/steer.go#L52) wraps the `CallExtension` error without normalizing a method-not-found response.
- [ACP driver](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a0e7b33430a01700a5348cf87576e3d004a7a8fd/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/driver.go#L679) already has `isACPMethodNotFound` for JSON-RPC `-32601`.
- [Steering service](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a0e7b33430a01700a5348cf87576e3d004a7a8fd/backend/internal/service/chat/steer.go#L393) reserves the handle before dispatch; only a definitive refusal settles it. Other errors leave it uncertain. Recovery of a reserved handle returns uncertainty again.
- [Generic classification](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/a0e7b33430a01700a5348cf87576e3d004a7a8fd/backend/internal/service/chat/history.go#L87) recognizes errors implementing `ChatRefusal()`. The pinned [ACP SDK RequestError](https://github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk/blob/v0.13.5/errors.go#L11) has no such method.

### Expected behavior / suggested fix

Treat a received `-32601` response for this optional extension as definite unsupported steering and persist a rejected delivery receipt. Preserve uncertainty for actual transport failures. Capability handling should reflect providers that lack the extension.

Do not automatically resend it as a new prompt, start a detached turn, or rewrite old uncertain handles without evidence. A regression check should verify that method-not-found settles the handle and that recovery returns the same explicit refusal without another provider call.

I searched existing issues for `CHAT_STEER_UNCERTAIN`, method-not-found steering, and OpenCode steering; I found no issue matching this specific refusal-to-uncertainty path. Ordinary worker-report batching and long orchestrator-turn queues are separate from this bug.

title: fix: align macOS titlebar across zoom and sidebar transitions
body:

title: fix(terminal): keep closed shell tabs from reappearing during rapid closes
body:
## What

Closing several shell terminals in quick succession no longer makes an already-closed tab flicker back for about half a second.

## Why

The user found this while testing #6174/#6175: open 5 terminals, close them all quickly, and one reappears briefly. It's independent of those PRs; the close path is unchanged there and on `main`.

Each close removes its tab optimistically, sends `DELETE`, and refetches the list when it settles. When one close settles, its refetch can reach the daemon before the other pending deletes have been processed. That response still lists those shells and overwrites the optimistic list, so a closed tab reappears until its own close settles and refetches again. Each close only cancels list requests already in flight when it starts, so it can't stop a refetch that a later-settling close triggers.

## How

- A module-level set records the shells whose close is in flight, per host (local or a connected remote machine). `fetchShellTerminals` drops those handles from the daemon's response.
- A handle is added in `onMutate` and released in `onSettled`, before the existing invalidation.
- A failed close still restores its tab: `onError` puts back the previous list, and `onSettled` releases the handle before refetching, so the refetch shows the still-live shell.

## Testing

- New test that reproduces the race: two closes are in flight, the first settles, and its refetch still lists the second shell. It fails on `main` with the closed tab back in the list, and passes with the fix.
- `useShellTerminals` tests (14) pass, and so do the `SessionView.remote` tests (repeated 3×).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Full frontend suite: everything passes except two files that also fail on `main` in this local setup:
  - `browser-profile-import`: the `better-sqlite3` native module is built for Electron here.
  - `annotate-preload`: Vite refuses the symlinked `node_modules` in the temporary checkout.

title: fix(chat): reattach ACP sessions the agent forgot
body:
## What

When an ACP agent says it no longer knows AO's session (`Session not found`), AO now resumes the same session ID on the live connection before the turn's prompt is sent. It then retries the turn's settings once. Before this change, every message failed until a new chat-host was spawned.

## Why

Part of #6200 (first of the problems reported there; the issue stays open until the rest are fixed). Chat sessions failed every turn with:

```
set ACP session option "model": {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"Session not found"}}
```

Root cause, from the bundled `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0 (`dist/acp-agent.js` ~L3405–3433): when the Claude child process dies (`ProcessTransport`, `process terminated by signal`, … which is likely under the reporter's memory pressure with swap at 7.0/8.0 GB), the adapter runs `delete this.sessions[sessionId]` but keeps its own process and ACP connection alive. AO's conversation still held the old session ID, so every later turn's first call (`session/set_config_option` or `session/set_mode`) got `Session not found`. Because the chat-host persists across daemon restarts, `Driver.Resume` took the live-host path and trusted `live.SessionID`, so the failure also survived a daemon restart (evidence §2). The earlier `The connection to Claude was lost.` turns are the matching `transport_lost` failure from the moment the child died.

## How

- `isACPSessionNotFound` recognizes ACP's `-32002` resource-not-found, and also `-32603` whose `data.details`/`data.error` is `Session not found`. That second form is how claude-agent-acp's thrown error reaches AO.
- `Start`, `Resume` (load/resume path) and the live persistent-host reconnect path each record a `session/resume` request. It holds the same session ID, cwd, additional directories, MCP servers and session meta.
- `SendTurn` reattaches once on a session-not-found from `applyTurnSettings`, then reapplies the settings. claude-agent-acp's `resumeSession` → `getOrCreateSession` recreates the evicted session with `resume: sessionId`, so the transcript on disk and the conversation context carry over.
- `runTurn` also reattaches and resends once when `session/prompt` itself answers `Session not found`. That happens for a turn with no settings to apply: Claude with the default permission mode and no model or effort override never calls a setter. claude-agent-acp rejects an unknown session at the top of `prompt()`, before doing any work, so resending can't run the turn twice.
- Safety: the setter reattach happens before `session/prompt`, so no work can run twice. Agents that don't advertise `session/resume` behave exactly as before. If the reattach fails, the original error is returned and the failure is logged.

**Intentional omissions**
- Load-only agents (no `session/resume`) are not reattached. `session/load` replays history notifications into a live conversation, and avoiding duplicate events there needs separate handling.
- Still open on #6200 and to be fixed in follow-up PRs against that issue (from its second comment): about 20 orphaned `ao chat-host` processes (PPID 1) left over from earlier daemons, and the orchestrator TUI session being marked terminated rather than auto-resumed after the 21:33 app relaunch.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/... ./internal/service/chat/...`: all pass except `codexappserver`, whose conformance test compares against the locally installed Codex CLI. It fails the same way without this change.
- New `session_reattach_test.go`:
  - `TestACPSendTurnReattachesSessionTheAgentForgot`: the fake agent answers the setters with claude-agent-acp's exact `Session not found` shape until it is resumed. The turn succeeds with one `session/resume` for the original session and cwd, and model and mode are applied. **This test fails on `main` with the exact error from the issue.**
  - `TestACPSendTurnKeepsSessionLossErrorWhenAgentCannotResume`: an agent without resume still gets the original error, and no resume is attempted.
  - `TestACPPromptReattachesSessionTheAgentForgot`: a turn with no settings, so `session/prompt` is the first call. **It fails without the prompt-path fix** with `ACP session/prompt: … Session not found`.
  - `TestIsACPSessionNotFound`: error-shape matrix, including that "peer disconnected" and other `-32603`s do not match.
- Not run locally: `golangci-lint` (not installed here; CI covers it). End-to-end check against the **real bundled `claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0** (isolated daemons on scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`s, standalone Claude Chat session on Haiku 4.5). Turn 1: "my favourite colour is teal". Then `kill -9` only the Claude Code process under the session's chat-host, which leaves the chat-host and adapter alive:
  - **`main` (control):** every later turn fails in ~8 ms with the exact #6200 error, `set ACP session option "model": {"code":-32603,…"details":"Session not found"}`, and the session stays stuck.
  - **This PR:** the next turn logs `chat: ACP agent lost its session; reattaching` with that same error, the adapter starts a new Claude process, and Claude answers **"Teal"**, so context is preserved.
  - **This PR, across a daemon restart** (the reporter's case): after killing Claude again, I ran `ao stop` (the chat-host survived as PPID 1) and restarted the daemon. It reconnected to the same chat-host, reattached, and answered **"Teal"**.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added for user-visible behavior
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass (pending)

title: perf(terminal): show a new terminal's first output without the replay cover
body:
## What

A newly created terminal now shows its prompt as soon as the shell prints it, instead of sitting blank behind the initial-replay cover. On this machine's dev build, the median time from opening a terminal to its prompt being visible dropped from about 600 ms to about 285 ms.

## Why

Terminals opened in AO felt much slower than in Orca. Timed the same way on the same machine (⌘T, then window captures every ~110 ms against an on-screen millisecond clock):

- **Orca:** prompt visible at about 220 ms.
- **AO:** about 1.1 s, including ~700 ms of blank terminal.

The blank stretch is the initial-replay cover in `useTerminalSession`. It exists so reattaching to a terminal doesn't visibly scroll through its history: it buffers the first output until it goes quiet, then runs a reveal fit. A terminal created moments ago has no history; its first bytes are the program starting (a shell's prompt). So the cover only holds a blank pane through the quiet window and fit.

## How

- The renderer already marks handles it just created (`markTerminalHandleFresh`: new shells, cue runs, requirements installs) and treats their first bytes as live output (`initialWriteSource`).
- The replay gate now skips those handles, so their output streams straight into xterm.
- The fresh mark is consumed on the first connect, so reattaching, remounting and reconnecting still cover the replay as before.

## Testing

- New test: a fresh handle starts uncovered and its first bytes are written straight to xterm. It fails without the change.
- `useTerminalSession` suite: 59 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Full frontend suite: everything passes except `browser-profile-import`. It also fails on `main` in this checkout, because the dev app rebuilt `better-sqlite3` for Electron.
- **Real desktop app (dev build, isolated data), six opens each:**
  - Median prompt bytes received and visible at **285 ms** (range 251–385). The cover never appeared.
  - `main` measured the same way revealed at about **590–630 ms**.
  - Screenshots at 100–800 ms show the prompt from the first frame, with no blank flash and no `%` artifact.

## Related

Independent of #6174/#6175. Those PRs size new shells correctly; this one removes the wait before their first output is shown.

title: fix(lifecycle): keep restart-preserved sessions out of the reaper
body:
## What

Sessions that boot reconciliation preserves after a failed relaunch are no longer terminated by the runtime reaper's next tick. They stay `exited` and can be resumed, which is what #4553 intended.

## Why

Part of #6200 (the orchestrator problem in its second comment). After the app relaunched at 21:33:49Z, the project's orchestrator (a TUI session) went to `exited, isTerminated:false` at 21:33:52. Five seconds later, at 21:33:57, it was `isTerminated:true`, with no cleanup or agent-switch rows. `ao session restore` brought it straight back with the same native session, so it was resumable the whole time.

Root cause:
1. `reconcileLive` found the old pty-host dead and the in-place relaunch failed. `preserveFailedReconcileRelaunch` then recorded `exited` so Resume Agent could retry, as designed in #4553.
2. The reaper ticks every 5 s (`DefaultTickInterval`). It still probes the stored runtime handle, which is dead. `hasRecentActivity` returns false for `exited`, so `runtimeClearlyDead` holds and `ApplyRuntimeObservation` terminates the session.
3. `ResumeAgentWithMode` refuses terminated sessions (`ErrTerminated`), so the recovery path that preservation exists for is closed. For an orchestrator, this left the project with no coordinator and no visible reason.

The existing integration test `TestReconcile_PreservesFailedLiveSessionAndReapsLeakedTmux` only checked the session after `Reconcile` and never ran a reaper tick. With a single reaper tick added, it fails on `main` with exactly this termination.

## How

- `lifecycle.Manager.HoldExitedForRecovery(id, launchID)` is an in-memory hold keyed to the runtime launch reconciliation knows is dead. It's memory-only because every boot reruns reconciliation and re-establishes it.
- `ApplyRuntimeObservation` skips termination while a session is held, still `exited`, and on the same launch. It checks in both its read pass and its guarded write pass. A new launch (Resume Agent / restore) gets a new launch ID, which drops the hold, so the session's later runtime death terminates as usual.
- `preserveFailedReconcileRelaunch` places the hold **before** recording `exited`, so the reaper can't slip in between. It also places the hold when the row is already `exited`. TUI only, because the reaper never probes Chat sessions.

- **Second commit:** the reaper loop now waits until boot reconciliation finishes. It started ticking at `startLifecycle` (`daemon.go:375`), long before reconcile fences live sessions: the listener, the persistent chat-host sweep (up to 5 s per host), and task-preparation cleanup all run first. A session whose runtime died across the restart could be terminated in that window, before reconcile relaunched or preserved it, so the hold above would never apply. `ReconcileRuntime`'s doc already says runtime observation belongs after reconciliation. `reaper.Config.Ready` holds the loop. The daemon releases it via `defer` in the boot goroutine, so a failed pass still releases it, and an unreleased loop still exits on cancellation. The mass-death breaker only covers the reboot case, where most sessions are dead, not a single dead orchestrator.

**Intentional scope:** exited sessions *without* a hold behave as before: an agent exit followed by its runtime dying still terminates. The new `TestRuntimeObservation_UnheldExitedSessionStillTerminatesOnRuntimeDeath` pins this. I first tried a broader rule ("exited is never auto-terminated"), but `TestRuntimeObservation_RetriesAfterRevisionChangesDuringFinalization` deliberately encodes crash-time termination. Changing that is a product decision beyond this report, so I backed it out.

**Not determined:** why the orchestrator's relaunch failed in the first place. The reporter's install produced no daemon log. This PR makes that failure recoverable instead of terminal. Reconcile already logs `reconcile: live pass failed` with the cause.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/observe/reaper/ ./internal/integration/...` passes.
- `TestReconcile_PreservesFailedLiveSessionAndReapsLeakedTmux` now runs a reaper tick after `Reconcile` and asserts the preserved session is still live. **It fails on `main`.**
- `TestStart_WaitsForReadyBeforeTicking` and `TestStart_UnreleasedReaperStopsOnCancel` (run with `-race`); `go test ./internal/daemon/` passes.

title: feat(review): give Chat reviewers the worker Chat surface
body:
Stacked on #6118. This needs #6118's reviewer event fix, because without it a reviewer conversation shows no messages. Retarget to `main` once #6118 merges.

## Why

Reviewer Chat was a reduced surface. It had five routes and was missing:
- the model and settings controls;
- steer, queue, edit, retry, rollback and compact.

It also dropped the reviewer model set in Settings. A reviewer conversation is the same Chat as a worker's, so it should use the same implementation, not a copy.

## What changed

### Backend
- **Owner-based commands.** Every Chat command in the chat service resolves a conversation owner: a worker session, or a review. The session methods are now thin wrappers, so worker behaviour is unchanged.
- **Mirrored routes.** All 23 session conversation routes are also mounted under `/reviews/{reviewId}/conversation`, on the same handlers. The reviewer OpenAPI operations are generated from the session ones in `specgen`, so the two can't drift.
- **Review-owned fences.** For a reviewer conversation, branch activation and edit delivery use the review's controller generation, never the worker session's.
- **Read-only fix.** Edit, branch switch and recovery relaunches previously dropped `ReadOnly` and used the worker's host ID. An edited reviewer would have come back without its read-only sandbox, on the worker's provider host. They now keep both. A regression test covers this and fails without the fix.
- **Worker model untouched.** Picking a model in reviewer Chat never rewrites the worker session's model.
- **Approvals locked.** A reviewer's approval mode can't change. That includes the permission `mode` config option. The new error is `CHAT_REVIEWER_READ_ONLY` (409).

### Frontend
- **Shared hooks.** The conversation hooks accept a reviewer target and route it to the reviewer endpoints. A type-level check fails the build if any session conversation route lacks a reviewer twin.
- **One surface.** Reviewer Chat renders through `SessionChatSurface`, so it gets the same composer, model picker, settings and history controls. `ReviewerChatSurface` and `useReviewerConversation` are removed.
- **Worker-only state stays with the worker.** That means agent switches, interface-handoff work reporting and "remember for this project".
- **Approval control.** Reviewers see a disabled "Read-only" control with an explanatory tooltip.
- **Resume agent.** In reviewer Chat, Resume restores the reviewer (`POST /sessions/{id}/reviews/restore`).

## Tests
- **Backend:** new service tests cover:
  - a reviewer turn completing through the shared path;
  - the reviewer model picker not touching the worker's model;
  - approvals staying locked;
  - an edit relaunching read-only on the reviewer host under the review fence.

  A new HTTP test drives seven commands through both route prefixes. The httpd, chat, store, review and daemon suites pass.
- **Full `go test ./...`:** `runtime/tmux` and `session_manager` fail on this machine. They fail the same way on #6118's unmodified head, so it's the local environment, not this change. `agent/goose` failed once under load and passed on three reruns.
- **Frontend:** `tsc` (app and e2e) passes. The full Vitest suite passes: 356 files, 5742 tests. One hook test, `useConversation` "keeps each accepted turn attached…", failed once in a combined run and passed in five later runs.
- **Not yet done:** I launched the real Electron app with isolated data, but it closed before I could exercise reviewer Chat. A native-window check is still pending, so this is a draft.

## Follow-ups
- #6177 (separate PR) lets Codex reviewers reach `gh` and the daemon from their read-only sandbox.

fix(frontend): restore nested @pierre/theme lock entry for npm 10 release builds
body:
## Summary
The nightly release failed ([conductor run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/ao-releases/actions/runs/37173051092), [build run](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37173088836)). `npm ci` failed on all four platforms with:

```
npm error Missing: @pierre/theme@1.1.0 from lock file
```

**Cause:** #6145 added `@pierre/trees@1.0.0-beta.6`. That package pins `@pierre/theming@1.0.0`, which has an optional peer dependency on `@pierre/theme ^1.1.0`. The top-level `@pierre/theme` is 2.0.0, so it doesn't satisfy that range. npm 11 (Node 24, used by `frontend.yml`) leaves the nested entry out of the lockfile and accepts the result. npm 10 (Node 22, used by `build-artifacts.yml`) requires the entry and rejects the lockfile. PR CI passed, but every release build fails.

**Fix:** I ran `npm install --package-lock-only` with npm 10. It added the single nested `node_modules/@pierre/trees/node_modules/@pierre/theme@1.1.0` entry (optional peer). No other lockfile changes.

## Tests
- `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` against `origin/main`'s lockfile: npm 10 fails with the error above (same as the release build), npm 11 succeeds.
- With this change: `npm ci --dry-run` succeeds under both npm 10.9.8 and npm 11.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Regenerating the lockfile with npm 11 removes this entry again, which would break release builds the same way. The lasting fix is to make `build-artifacts.yml` (Node 22) and `frontend.yml` (Node 24) use the same Node version, or to have CI run `npm ci` on the release build's Node version. I'm keeping that out of this PR because it changes the release toolchain.

title: fix(chat): stop a reconnect replay from wedging persistent ACP hosts
body:
## What

A Chat session whose daemon restarts mid-turn can become **permanently non-resumable**: every "Resume agent" fails with "The service is momentarily unavailable, please retry." This PR fixes both defects behind that:

1. **Flow control under the ACP SDK.** AO now hands the SDK at most 512 `session/update` notifications it hasn't finished handling. A reconnect replay burst then waits in the transport instead of overflowing the SDK's queue.
2. **Release the host socket when the SDK connection ends.** For persistent transports, `watchConnection` now calls `proc.stop()` so the host detaches. It deliberately does not consume `closeOnce`, so a later `Terminate` can still shut the host down.

## Why

Part of #6200. Found by root-causing a live occurrence on a dev machine ("Reviewer Chat Triage", AO killed under memory pressure mid-turn) and then reproducing it end to end.

**Chain (each link observed):**
1. On reconnect, the persistent chat-host replays the in-flight prompt's whole journal to the new daemon in one burst. That was 3,020 notifications in the field.
2. For persistent transports, AO's `emit` blocks until the controller projects each event (SQLite plus ack), on purpose, so journaled frames are never dropped. The SDK can't propagate that backpressure: its notification queue is a fixed 1,024 slots (`defaultMaxQueuedNotifications`), and on overflow it logs `failed to queue notification; closing connection` and shuts down receive.
3. AO emitted `stopped` (0.28 s after `ready`) but never closed the host socket. The reader chain (gate → legacy forward → pipe → SDK) stopped draining it.
4. The host stays blocked in `replayTo`, writing to that socket **while holding `h.mu`**. Every later attach waits on `h.mu`, hits the 1 s handshake deadline, and returns `ErrOwnershipInconclusive` wrapping `DeadlineExceeded`. The HTTP envelope maps `DeadlineExceeded` to 503 "momentarily unavailable". Restarting AO doesn't reliably help, because boot recovery replays the same journal again.

**Live evidence from the stuck machine:**
- `netstat` showed the daemon's socket to the host with 479,684 unread bytes and the host side with 343,596 bytes queued.
- 12 abandoned attach sockets were stuck behind it.
- A snapshot daemon with the #6210 log captured `chat host ownership is inconclusive: context deadline exceeded` after 1.006 s.

**Isolated reproduction** (scratch data, real bundled `claude-agent-acp`, a Haiku turn writing 1..12000, `kill -9` of the daemon mid-turn, then restart):

| | journal replayed | result |
|---|---|---|
| unfixed | 1,311 | reconnect held (below the overflow rate on an idle machine) |
| unfixed | 4,002 | `notification queue overflow capacity=1024 queued=1024`, `ready`→`stopped` in **0.27 s**, turn failed, session `exited`, sockets 467,464 / 146,816 bytes stuck, `resume-agent` → 503 "momentarily unavailable" in 1.008 s, i.e. the field failure exactly |
| **this PR** | 4,009 | no overflow, controller stays `ready`, queues drain to 0, the turn completes with **all 12,000 numbers exactly once** across the kill/replay boundary, and the next turn recalls prior context |

## How

- `session_update_flow.go`: `sessionUpdateFlowReader` frames the SDK input and reserves a slot per `session/update` the SDK will dispatch. `dispatchesSessionUpdate` mirrors the SDK's own unmarshal plus `Validate()` gate, so every reserved slot is released by exactly one `SessionUpdate` call. Slots are released in `SessionUpdate` and the flow is closed when the connection ends. The limit (512) leaves headroom for other queued notifications.
- `watchConnection` releases persistent transports. Non-persistent providers are unchanged: their `conn.Done` already means the process ended.
- `extension_reader.go`: frame reading is extracted into `readACPFrame` for reuse. No behavior change.

**Deadlock review.** The reader only blocks while 512 updates are unhandled. The SDK's single notification worker releases slots as AO's projection drains. The projection goroutine only waits on agent responses from `drain` after a turn completes, by which point the preceding updates have been handled. Requests and responses aren't gated.

**Intentionally not in this PR (follow-ups on #6200):**
- **Host-side defense.** The host writes to its client under its only lock with no deadline, so any client that stays connected but stops reading still wedges it. A plain write deadline would also disconnect healthy-but-slow daemons, the exact memory-pressure case, so it needs a progress-based design rather than a per-write timeout.
- **Error surfacing.** A persistent `ErrOwnershipInconclusive`/`DeadlineExceeded` shouldn't be shown as transient "momentarily unavailable, please retry".

## Testing

- New `session_update_flow_test.go`:
  - `TestPersistentReplayBurstDoesNotOverflowSDKNotificationQueue`: 6,096 updates against a stalled consumer. **It fails on `main`** with "SDK closed the connection while AO was still projecting the replay"; with the fix it passes and all updates arrive.
  - `TestPersistentTransportIsReleasedWhenSDKConnectionEnds`. **It fails on `main`** with "persistent transport was left open".
  - Classification and pass-through tests.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ -race` passes. `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/... ./internal/service/chat/...` passes, except `codexappserver`'s conformance test against the locally installed Codex CLI, which fails identically on `main`.
- `golangci-lint v2.13.2` reports 0 issues on the package.
- The end-to-end before/after reproduction is described above.

title: fix(chat): settle native checkpoint turns the transcript moved past
body:
## What

Terminal → Chat switches no longer get permanently blocked by a Claude turn that can never complete. This is the third problem reported in #6200 ([comment](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/6200#issuecomment-5974402625)).

## Why

Part of #6200. `verifyCheckpointTranscript` required **every** observed native turn to end in `end_turn`. Because observations are kept for the whole conversation, one turn that never completes blocks the switch forever (`TARGET_HISTORY_UNSETTLED … observed native turn not completed`), and the UI's strict retry can't succeed. The reporter found two shapes:

1. **A turn cut off mid-tool by a crash** (assistant `tool_use`, no result), followed by later, normally completed turns.
2. **Two queued `ao send` prompts** written as consecutive `user` records and answered by Claude in one `end_turn` reply. The first prompt's turn had no assistant record. This needs no crash: any busy terminal-mode orchestrator can hit it.

A third shape turned up while investigating stray `<task-notification>` blobs: a `queueTranscriptOnly` user record (a background task's stop notice) is never sent to the model. As the tail of the transcript, it blocked forever.

## How

`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/checkpoint.go`, a small change to one function:
- **Settle turns the chain moved past.** The native transcript is append-only, so a prompt followed by another can receive nothing more: a reply, an interrupt or a process exit ended it. Every turn before the tail is settled. A prompt with no reply of its own takes the next turn's reply, which is how Claude Code answers queued input.
- **The tail must still be complete**, so a turn Claude is still working on keeps blocking. That's the safety the check exists for.
- **Answers are still checked.** Stop-text matching is unchanged, so an observed answer must still match its own turn.
- **Skip `queueTranscriptOnly` user records.** Across 101 real transcripts this flag appears only on a task notification, never on a human prompt (`typed`, `sdk`, `queued`, `suggestion_accepted`). Answered task notifications stay as turns, matching Claude's own handling.

## Testing

- New `TestNativeCheckpointSettlesTurnsTheChainMovedPast`. The crash-cut, queued-pair and transcript-only-tail cases **fail on `main` and pass here**. The guards (a pending tail still blocks; a superseded turn's answer must still match its own) pass on both.
- All existing checkpoint tests pass unchanged: queued ID collisions, delayed Stops, unflushed later turns, cross-turn answers and turn companions.
- **Real-data comparison:** old and new parsers over the 101 most recent real Claude transcripts on a dev machine, with every prompt observed.
  - **0 regressions.** Every transcript the old parser accepted gets the identical boundary.
  - **8 newly settled.** All previously failed with `observed native turn not completed`.
  - **Remaining failures are legitimate:** two live or unanswered tails, plus six 15-day-old transcripts ending in `stop_sequence` (out of scope here).
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/ ./internal/service/chat/...` passes. `golangci-lint v2.13.2` reports 0 issues.
- Not tested against the reporter's own transcripts, which aren't available here. The shapes come from their read-only analysis.

title: fix(chat): stop replaying Claude task notifications as user turns
body:
## What

Resumed Chat sessions no longer show Claude Code's background-task notices (`<task-notification>…</task-notification>`) as user messages in "This turn was recovered from an earlier session" turns.

## Why

Part of #6200 (found while investigating the same recovery paths on a dev machine).
- **What the notices are.** When a background shell command an agent started stops, Claude Code writes a notice into its transcript as a `user` record, marked `origin.kind: "task-notification"` and `promptSource: "system"`. Live Chat never shows them; the adapter treats them as autonomous work.
- **How they leak.** On resume, history replay (`session/load`) gets them as ordinary user messages, because the Claude Agent SDK's `getSessionMessages` keeps only `{type, uuid, session_id, message, parent_tool_use_id, parent_agent_id, timestamp}` and drops the `origin` and `promptSource` markers. AO then added each one as a recovered user turn showing raw XML.
- **Scale on one dev machine:** 16 such turns across 5 sessions, all `recovered`, none with a reply.

## How

`acp/history.go`: `captureHistoryUserChunk` ignores a replayed user chunk that is a task-notification block, so it starts no turn and renders as no user message. A reply Claude gave to the notice stays with the turn it followed, matching live Chat.

The check is text-based because that's the only signal left after the SDK drops `origin`. The tags are Claude Code's own format, and the adapter already filters local-command records the same way.

**Not in scope:**
- **Existing rows aren't cleaned up.** Already-imported notification turns stay in history.
- **The upstream adapter replay could also drop these records.** That would only reach users after an adapter release and an AO version bump, so it doesn't replace this fix.

## Testing

- New `TestACPHistoryReplaySkipsClaudeTaskNotifications`: a replayed history with a prompt, an answered notice and a trailing unanswered notice. **It fails on `main`** with both notices replayed as user messages. With the fix there's one user message and one turn, and both replies are kept. Plus `TestIsTaskNotification`.
- **Real data:** reading a real affected session's transcript through the bundled SDK's `getSessionMessages`, the same call the adapter's replay uses, gives 368 messages and 8 user text messages. The filter matches exactly the 2 notices that appeared as blobs, and nothing else.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ -race`, `./internal/adapters/chatdriver/claudeacp/` and `./internal/service/chat/...` pass. `golangci-lint v2.13.2` reports 0 issues.

title: fix(session): report an unrecoverable chat-host reconnect as a conflict
body:
Code changes: +7 -0  
Tests: +3 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

When AO can't safely reconnect to a session's still-running chat provider, "Resume agent" now returns **409 `CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE`** with an accurate message and the cause. Previously it returned **503 "The service is momentarily unavailable, please retry."**

## Why

Part of #6200. Chat recovery fails with `ports.ErrChatRecoveryInconclusive` when a detached provider host may still own the session. When the host is wedged (root cause and fix in #6215), that error wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded` from the 1 s attach handshake. `mapSessionError` had no case for it, so the HTTP envelope's `isTransient` check mapped the deadline to 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`:
- **Wrong message.** The failure repeats identically on every retry, so "momentarily unavailable, please retry" was false and invited endless retries.
- **Hidden failure.** `frontend/src/shared/observability.ts` deliberately skips reporting `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as retryable contention, so a permanent breakage never reached error tracking.

## How

One case in `mapSessionError`, placed next to the sibling `CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE`, which already returns a 409 with the error text when a host fails to start. The message keeps the cause chain, so a user (or support) can see that the host didn't respond.

## Testing

- **Unit:** a new mapping-table case uses the exact error chain from the field (`resume chat: chat conversation recovery is inconclusive: persistent ACP host: chat host ownership is inconclusive: context deadline exceeded`) and expects 409 `CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE`.
- **End to end:** on an isolated daemon built from this branch, with the real bundled `claude-agent-acp`, I wedged a live chat-host the way the field failure did: a client attached mid-replay and never read, giving the same socket signature (146,880 bytes stuck host-side, 527,983 unread). I then restarted the daemon and ran `ao session resume-agent`:
  - **before:** `The service is momentarily unavailable, please retry. (SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)`, 503
  - **now:** `AO could not safely reconnect to the session's still-running chat process: … chat host ownership is inconclusive: context deadline exceeded (CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE)`, **409**
- `go test ./internal/service/session/...` passes. `golangci-lint v2.13.2` reports 0 issues.
