title: [Bug]: ACP replacement prompt can erase an unacknowledged terminal receipt and wedge the persistent host
body:
## Summary

A transient OMP ACP `session/prompt` rejection can become a persistent **AO host acknowledgment wedge**. Once a second prompt is attempted before the first terminal result is acknowledged, the second host-local rejection overwrites the ACP adapter's `terminalEventID`. A subsequent acknowledgment of the original, durably committed result silently returns nil without sending `_ao/persistent_prompt_ack`. The persistent host retains its pending result and rejects every later prompt with:

```json
{"code":-32602,"message":"previous ACP prompt is active or not acknowledged"}
```

I reproduced this with the real AO ACP adapter, real persistent host and real ACP SDK, using an isolated deterministic provider process. No OMP or model API is needed to reproduce the AO defect. Timely acknowledgment is the passing control.

## Environment

- Windows 11 x64.
- Installed desktop: `0.13.4-nightly.202610031727`, release commit `a2a8917c22e2246bf63b98e06a97c417f3b3fb76`.
- Installed OMP reports `omp/18.6.0` at investigation time. This is not a captured version handshake from the original long-lived provider process.
- Reproducer executed against upstream `b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e`, ACP Go SDK `v0.13.5`.
- Compared the installed release with this revision: `acp/conversation.go` and `persistenthost/acp_relay.go` are unchanged.

## Observed incident

Sanitized UTC timeline from a read-only query of AO's `conversation_turns` and `conversation_provider_events`. No user prompts, credentials or raw session dumps are included.

| Time, 2026-10-04 | Recorded event |
| --- | --- |
| 07:36:26.405 | Previous turn completes as `interrupted` |
| 07:36:32.714 | A steer delivery is durably rejected as `no_active_turn` |
| 07:36:32.770 | Replacement turn has already been bound/started in `conversation_turns` |
| 07:36:32.777 | Original prompt failure is archived with code `-32003`, `providerData.reason=session_busy`, and a nonempty `ao.persistentEventId` |
| 07:36:32.804 | Replacement fails with AO's `-32602` acknowledgment error, no provider event ID |
| Through 07:52:37.045 | Eleven subsequent host-local acknowledgment rejections observed in total, including the replacement |

The raw OMP error was:

```json
{"code":-32003,"message":"Agent is already processing. Use steer() or followUp() to queue messages, or wait for completion.","data":{"reason":"session_busy","hint":"steer|followUp|wait"}}
```

AO wraps its error data with `ao.persistentEventId` and `providerData`. The busy failure was durably archived with the same event ID, so this is not simply a missing event ID on error responses.

## Confirmed mechanism

References pinned to the reproduced revision:

1. [`acp_relay.go:361-376`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/acp_relay.go#L361-L376) retains the provider terminal response in `PendingResultEventID`, including errors.
2. [`acp_relay.go:219-220`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/acp_relay.go#L219-L220) rejects a new prompt while that receipt is outstanding. This host-local rejection has no persistent event ID.
3. [`conversation.go:619-624`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go#L619-L624) extracts the original error's event ID correctly. But [`finishPrompt:682-705`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go#L682-L705) unconditionally assigns `c.terminalEventID = eventID` for **every** completion and releases the turn before the controller's durable acknowledgment.
4. A replacement's host-local error therefore assigns `terminalEventID = ""`.
5. [`AcknowledgeProviderEvent:984-993`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/conversation.go#L984-L993) silently returns nil when the original receipt no longer matches that mutable field. The host never receives its ACK and stays blocked.

### Production entry path to investigate

[INFERENCE] The incident's rejected steer followed by a replacement dispatch is consistent with the `SteerOrSend` fallback race:

- [`SteerOrSend:455-527`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/service/chat/steer.go#L455-L527) holds `sendMu`, receives `ErrNoActiveTurn`, and calls `sendLocked(ctx, msg, false)`, bypassing the normal busy queue.
- The driver may have released `activeTurn`, while the controller has not yet committed/acknowledged its terminal event.
- [`Controller.project:2541-2579`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/b2461dc5955bb11b4ee1213871e6a2157e68da0e/backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go#L2541-L2579) needs that same `sendMu` before it can project and acknowledge terminal events.
- A fast replacement rejection can overwrite the receipt before projection gets the lock.

The diagnostic below forces this ordering at the public driver boundary; it does **not** claim to have replayed the complete HTTP/controller scheduling of the live incident.

## Deterministic reproduction

In a checkout of the revision above, place the program below at `backend/cmd/acp-busy-probe/main.go`, then run:

```sh
cd backend
go run ./cmd/acp-busy-probe
```

It uses fresh temporary data, terminates its own provider host and removes its scratch state. It does not access an existing AO installation's data or any model service.

Observed output:

```text
delayed=false first: state=failed event_id_present=true typed_busy=true
delayed=false second: state=completed event_id_present=true error=<nil>
delayed=true first: state=failed event_id_present=true typed_busy=true
delayed=true second: state=failed event_id_present=false error=ACP session/prompt: {"code":-32602,"message":"previous ACP prompt is active or not acknowledged"}
late original ACK returned nil
third after original ACK: state=failed error=ACP session/prompt: {"code":-32602,"message":"previous ACP prompt is active or not acknowledged"}
CONFIRMED: delayed ACK is silently lost after a subsequent host-local prompt rejection
```

<details>
<summary>Standalone diagnostic program</summary>

```go
package main

import (
 "bufio"
 "context"
 "encoding/json"
 "fmt"
 "os"
 "strings"
 "time"

 "github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp"
 "github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost"
 "github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/domain"
 "github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/ports"
)

func must(err error) { if err != nil { panic(err) } }

func provider() {
 scanner := bufio.NewScanner(os.Stdin)
 prompts := 0
 for scanner.Scan() {
  var req struct { ID json.RawMessage `json:"id"`; Method string `json:"method"` }
  must(json.Unmarshal(scanner.Bytes(), &req))
  if len(req.ID)==0 { continue }
  var result any = map[string]any{}
  switch req.Method {
  case "initialize": result = map[string]any{"protocolVersion":1,"agentCapabilities":map[string]any{},"agentInfo":map[string]string{"name":"busy-probe","version":"1"}}
  case "session/new": result = map[string]any{"sessionId":"probe-session"}
  case "session/prompt":
   prompts++
   if prompts==1 {
    must(json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(map[string]any{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":req.ID,"error":map[string]any{"code":-32003,"message":"Agent is already processing. Use steer() or followUp() to queue messages, or wait for completion.","data":map[string]any{"reason":"session_busy","hint":"steer|followUp|wait"}}}))
    continue
   }
   result=map[string]any{"stopReason":"end_turn"}
  }
  must(json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(map[string]any{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":req.ID,"result":result}))
 }
}

func turn(ctx context.Context, conv ports.ChatConversation) ports.ChatEvent {
 ref,err:=conv.SendTurn(ctx,ports.ChatUserMessage{Text:"diagnostic"}); must(err)
 must(conv.(ports.ChatDeferredTurnStarter).StartDeferredTurn(ref.ProviderTurnID))
 var terminal ports.ChatEvent
 for {
  select {
  case e:=<-conv.Events():
   if e.Kind==ports.ChatEventTurnCompleted { terminal=e }
   if terminal.Kind!="" && e.Kind==ports.ChatEventControllerState && e.ControllerState==ports.ChatControllerReady { return terminal }
  case <-ctx.Done(): panic(ctx.Err())
  }
 }
}

func run(delayed bool) {
 ctx,cancel:=context.WithTimeout(context.Background(),20*time.Second); defer cancel()
 dir,err:=os.MkdirTemp("","ao-acp-busy-probe-");must(err);defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
 exe,err:=os.Executable();must(err)
 driver:=acp.New(acp.Config{Harness:domain.AgentHarness("omp"),Launch:func(context.Context,acp.LaunchConfig)(acp.Launch,error){return acp.Launch{Command:exe,Args:[]string{"provider"}},nil}},nil)
 conv,err:=driver.Start(ctx,ports.ChatStartConfig{SessionID:"probe",DataDir:dir,WorkspacePath:dir});must(err)
 defer conv.(ports.ChatProviderTerminator).Terminate()
 ack:=conv.(ports.ChatProviderEventAcknowledger)
 first:=turn(ctx,conv)
 if first.Err==nil || !strings.Contains(first.Err.Error(),"session_busy") || first.ProviderEventID=="" { panic("busy fixture failed") }
 fmt.Printf("delayed=%v first: state=%s event_id_present=%v typed_busy=%v\n",delayed,first.TurnState,first.ProviderEventID!="",strings.Contains(first.Err.Error(),"session_busy"))
 if !delayed { must(ack.AcknowledgeProviderEvent(ctx,first.ProviderEventID)) }
 second:=turn(ctx,conv)
 fmt.Printf("delayed=%v second: state=%s event_id_present=%v error=%v\n",delayed,second.TurnState,second.ProviderEventID!="",second.Err)
 if delayed {
  if second.Err==nil || !strings.Contains(second.Err.Error(),"not acknowledged") { panic("missing host rejection") }
  must(ack.AcknowledgeProviderEvent(ctx,first.ProviderEventID))
  fmt.Println("late original ACK returned nil")
  third:=turn(ctx,conv)
  if third.Err==nil || !strings.Contains(third.Err.Error(),"not acknowledged") { panic("expected wedged result") }
  fmt.Printf("third after original ACK: state=%s error=%v\n",third.TurnState,third.Err)
 } else {
  if second.TurnState!=domain.TurnStateCompleted { panic("timely ACK did not recover") }
  must(ack.AcknowledgeProviderEvent(ctx,second.ProviderEventID))
 }
}

func main() {
 if len(os.Args)>1 && os.Args[1]=="provider" {provider();return}
 if len(os.Args)>1 && os.Args[1]=="chat-host" {
  must(persistenthost.Run(context.Background(),persistenthost.Config{SessionID:os.Args[2],DataDir:os.Args[3],Workdir:os.Args[4],Protocol:persistenthost.Protocol(os.Args[5]),OwnershipFingerprint:os.Args[6],Argv:os.Args[8:],Env:os.Environ()}));return
 }
 run(false)
 run(true)
 fmt.Println("CONFIRMED: delayed ACK is silently lost after a subsequent host-local prompt rejection")
}
```

</details>

## Expected repair and acceptance

- Keep a pending durable terminal receipt acknowledgeable until its matching ACK has been delivered. A later local rejection must not erase it.
- Serialize replacement dispatch with terminal projection/acknowledgment, including the `SteerOrSend` no-active-turn fallback. Do not bypass the host guard or acknowledge before durable commit.
- Regression coverage should delay terminal projection while a steer loses the active-turn race, attempt the replacement, then commit/ACK the original result. A subsequent prompt must reach the provider and complete exactly once.
- Cover both successful and failed original terminal results, plus a replacement error with no persistent event ID.
- Preserve restart replay and the guarantee that uncommitted results are not discarded.

## Relation to OMP and existing work

OMP's original busy rejection is separately documented in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/10707 and https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/9157. The upstream discussion treats `session_busy` as transient and explains why blindly steering a new ACP prompt into an ownerless autonomous turn is unsafe. This report concerns AO losing its own acknowledgment, not changing OMP's response ownership semantics.

#6215 addresses reconnect replay queue overflow and an unreleased transport socket. This reproduction requires neither a restart nor a replay burst and identifies a different receipt-lifetime bug.

Investigation only. No production source changes or live-session restart were made.

title: [Bug]: link-preview parseTag loops forever on a stray byte inside a tag; each hover leaves a goroutine spinning a core
body:
### What went wrong?

**Symptom.** Daemon CPU climbed in steps (about +100% per step: 40% → 80% → 130% → 200% within 20 minutes) and stayed there, while `/healthz`, writes and sessions were all fine. A 3-second `sample` of the daemon put almost all running samples in `internal/service/linkpreview.parseTag` (plus `strings.ToLower` / `slicebytetostring` from it). The CPU stayed up after the pointer left the window and dropped to the normal ~20% only when the daemon was restarted: a few request goroutines that never finished, not request volume.

**Root cause.** In `parseTag` (`internal/service/linkpreview/service.go`), after `skipSpaces` the loop assumes the next byte is `>`, `/` or an attribute-name byte. For any other byte (a stray `"` or `'`, a lone `=`, a `<` inside the tag) the name loop consumes nothing, `name == ""`, nothing is stored, and the loop repeats at the same index forever. Real pages produce this (for example `<meta name="description" content="x"">`). The parse runs on the request goroutine with no deadline check, so the UI client going away does not stop it; each hover on such a page adds one spinning core until the daemon restarts.

**Reproduction.** `parseHead([]byte(`<html><head><meta name="description" content="x""><title>T</title></head></html>`))` never returns. The attached test feeds four malformed tags under a 2-second guard; three of them hang on main 72af13ff.

**Fix (patch below).** When the name loop consumes no byte, skip that byte and continue. The test passes afterwards and the package's existing tests are unchanged. Suggested follow-up, not in the patch: bound the parse by the request context (or a wall-clock budget) so a future parser bug cannot outlive its request.

**Environment.** AO v0.13.3, macOS, hover cards over terminal output that contained links to a large SPA portal.

<details>
<summary>Patch (2 files, +41, against main 72af13ff)</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/parse_hang_test.go b/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/parse_hang_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..f3f97983
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/parse_hang_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+package linkpreview
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+)
+
+// A tag byte that is neither '>' nor '/' nor a name character (a stray quote,
+// '=' or '<') must not stall the parser: the daemon parses hovered pages on
+// request goroutines with no deadline, so a non-advancing loop spins a core
+// forever and survives the request. Observed 2026-10-04: three hovers, three
+// cores, until the daemon was restarted.
+func TestParseHeadAdvancesPastStrayTagBytes(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := map[string]string{
+		"stray quote after attribute": `<html><head><meta name="description" content="x""><title>T</title></head><body></body></html>`,
+		"lone equals sign":            `<html><head><link rel="icon" = href="/f.ico"><title>T</title></head></html>`,
+		"angle bracket inside tag":    `<html><head><title <>T</title></head></html>`,
+		"stray quote at tag start":    `<html><head><meta "><title>T</title></head></html>`,
+	}
+	for name, doc := range cases {
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			done := make(chan headMeta, 1)
+			go func() { done <- parseHead([]byte(doc)) }()
+			select {
+			case m := <-done:
+				if m.title != "T" {
+					t.Fatalf("title = %q, want %q", m.title, "T")
+				}
+			case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
+				t.Fatal("parseHead did not return within 2s: parser loop does not advance")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
diff --git a/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/service.go b/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/service.go
index 9191dc9f..6100240a 100644
--- a/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/service.go
+++ b/backend/internal/service/linkpreview/service.go
@@ -432,6 +432,13 @@ func parseTag(doc []byte, start int) (map[string]string, int) {
 		for i < len(doc) && isNameByte(doc[i]) {
 			i++
 		}
+		if i == nameStart {
+			// Not '>', '/' or a name byte (a stray quote, '=' or '<'): skip it.
+			// Without this the loop re-reads the same byte forever, and the
+			// request goroutine spins a core until the daemon restarts.
+			i++
+			continue
+		}
 		name := strings.ToLower(string(doc[nameStart:i]))
 		i = skipSpaces(doc, i)
 		value := ""
```

</details>

title: fix: prevent parser loop hang on stray tag bytes in linkpreview
body:
Fixes #6223.

Code changes: +7 -0 Tests: +28 -0 Others: +0 -0

## What

Prevents a CPU-locking infinite loop in the linkpreview package by gracefully skipping stray non-name bytes (such as quotes or angle brackets) inside HTML tags during parsing.

## Why

Fixes #6223.

Previously, if the linkpreview tag parser encountered malformed HTML containing characters that weren't >, /, spaces, or valid attribute name bytes, the inner parser loop index would fail to advance. Because there is no strict deadline on the request context, this resulted in a permanent infinite loop that pinned a daemon CPU core at 100% and leaked a request goroutine for every single hover event on affected pages.

## How

* In backend/internal/service/linkpreview/service.go inside the parseTag function, we now verify if i == nameStart after attempting to parse an attribute name.

* If it hasn't advanced, it signifies a garbage character (like a stray " or <). We explicitly advance i by 1 and continue to safely skip it without locking up.

* In addition to preventing the hang, this safely skips lone = characters, which prevents subsequent valid attributes from being accidentally swallowed/discarded as the value of an empty attribute.

## Testing

* Reproduction: Wrote a standalone scratch script wrapping parseTag and fed it the 4 edge cases from the bug report (stray quote after attribute, lone equals sign, angle bracket inside tag, stray quote at tag start). Verified that 3 of the 4 hung permanently prior to the patch.

* Validation: Ported the bug reporter's timeout-guarded test suite into service_test.go (TestParseHeadAdvancesPastStrayTagBytes).

* Commands run locally: go test ./backend/internal/service/linkpreview/... -v to ensure the new tests pass instantly and that existing legitimate parser behavior wasn't regressed.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(settings): one-click device removal with undo
body:
## Summary

Reworks the **Connected devices** list in Settings → Mobile.

**Remove: one click, 2s Undo (replaces the inline "Confirm remove" text)**
- Clicking the trash icon immediately turns the row into "*{name}* removed · **Undo**", with a hairline countdown along the row's bottom edge. The `DELETE` is only sent when the 2s window ends.
- Undo cancels the timer — nothing reaches the daemon, so no tombstone is written — and returns focus to the row's trash button.
- Closing settings mid-countdown commits the removal (the row already looked gone).
- A failed `DELETE` brings the row back with the error shown below the list.
- Why undo instead of confirm: removal is soft on the daemon side. Phones share one connection password, so a removed phone can still reconnect, and it comes back muted via the tombstone. An undo window fits that better than a confirm step, and it fixes the old confirm prompt that never reset (no cancel, no timeout, and the row shifted width). No nested modal.

**Bell / notifications switch**
- While a mute request is in flight, only that device's switch is locked (previously every switch was).
- A switch disabled because the phone has no push token now explains why on hover ("Notifications are off on {name} — turn them on in the AO mobile app"). No new visible row copy.

**Other**
- 4 new strings in all 8 locales; `mobile.devices.confirmRemove` removed.
- In the web preview build (`dev:web`, no daemon) the section uses three in-memory sample phones, so the flow can be demoed without touching a real roster.

## Tests

- `MobileDevicesSection.test.tsx`: new cases for one-click removal after the undo window, undo never sending `DELETE` (plus the focus handoff), committing on unmount, a failed remove restoring the row, and the per-row mute lock; the tokenless test now also checks the hover hint.
- `vitest` over `components/settings`, `i18n`, `GlobalSettingsForm`: 24 files, 289 tests pass.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean for `frontend/` (the only errors are in `packages/product-ui`, whose dependencies aren't installed in this worktree).
- Not yet visually verified in the running app; `dev:web` shows the flow with sample devices.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Esc doesn't trigger Undo: the settings dialog handles Esc first (it closes the dialog, which commits the removal).
- 2s is short for screen-reader users to reach Undo; the row is announced via `role="status"` and Undo gets focus right away.

title: fix(chat): render native citations as source links
body:
Code changes: +395 -0  
Tests: +238 -0  
Others: +0 -0

When Codex emits native inline citation markers, AO stores their private-use characters as assistant text. The chat shows unrelated glyphs, including after history replay, even though the provider's `webSearch.results` contain the cited URLs.

This change defines portable Markdown as the assistant-message boundary. A provider-neutral formatter turns cited spans and verified source URLs into numbered links, with an unavailable-source label for missing or unsafe destinations. The Codex adapter parses its native markers and source IDs at that boundary for both live deltas and native history. It buffers incomplete markers during streaming and preserves literal examples in Markdown code.

Live citation state is keyed by native provider thread as well as turn and item IDs, so multiplexed root and child notifications cannot overwrite one another.

The shared formatter can serve other adapters that expose citation annotations. This PR decodes only the confirmed Codex wire format; it does not infer citations or destinations from prose in other harnesses.

title: perf(terminal): make heavy terminal output ~16x faster without changing persistence
body:
## Summary

Heavy terminal output in AO was 7–14× slower than in Orca, Conductor, Superset and T3 Code: `seq 1 100000` took about 2.6 s on screen, against 190–340 ms for the others. This PR brings it to about **150 ms** end to end, without changing how terminals persist or are shared. Profiling found four causes; there's one commit per layer.

### 1. pty-host: stop throttling programs (`perf(terminal): stop the pty-host from throttling programs on heavy output`)

The pty-host ran every output byte through its `vt-go` mirror inside the loop that reads from the PTY. `vt-go` scrolls at about 0.4 MB/s (`DeleteLineArea` and scrollback allocations), so the read loop fell behind, the PTY filled and the kernel paused the program. `seq` itself took about 1.9 s to run, against about 65 ms for the same command in a bare PTY.

- **The mirror moves off the read loop.** It catches up on its own goroutine (`asyncSurface`), applying the same bytes and resizes in the same order. A styled-output read waits until it has caught up, so `GetStyledOutput` returns exactly what it did before. A backlog over 8 MiB is dropped and rebuilt from the ring on the next read.
- **Shell and command terminals skip the mirror.** Only agent sessions are ever probed for their rendered screen (the composer and interface-transition checks), so shell and command terminals now build it only on first read. This is a new `RuntimeConfig.LazyStyledOutput` option, passed to the pty-host as `--surface=lazy`. Agent terminals keep the mirror current, as before.
- **Slow viewers are no longer dropped.** With the read loop fast, viewers couldn't keep up, were dropped, and reconnected to a ring truncated at 1,000 lines, silently losing output.
  - Output now waits for a full viewer queue to drain, pausing the program as a real terminal does; Superset does the same.
  - A viewer that frees no space for 3 s (`slowClientGrace`) is still dropped, so a stalled viewer can't hold the PTY.
  - Status probes, attaches and input never wait on a viewer's queue.
  - Frames already queued are written in one call.
- **Options type.** The spawner's `startOnAttach bool` becomes `conpty.HostOptions{StartOnAttach, LazySurface}`. Hosts spawned without the new flags, for example by older daemons, behave as before.

### 2. daemon: fewer, larger messages (`perf(terminal): send bursts of terminal output in fewer messages`)

Every small PTY read crossed the daemon as its own read and its own JSON WebSocket message: about 20,000 messages for one `seq`.

- The attach stream's `io.Pipe` is replaced with a `bytePipe`. A read now returns all output buffered so far. Writes still block at 1 MiB, so backpressure is kept, and buffered output is delivered before the close error.
- When output for the same terminal is already queued behind the WebSocket writer, new output joins the frame before it (up to 256 KiB). Base64 encoding now happens once per merged frame, at write time.
- About 2,500 messages now. Switching these two changes off takes the end-to-end time back from about 150 ms to about 400 ms.

### 3. renderer: fewer parse cycles, no per-scroll timer churn (`perf(terminal): batch live terminal writes and stop per-scroll timer churn`)

- **Batched live writes.** Live output keeps one `xterm.write` in flight; output that arrives while xterm is still parsing goes into the next write. Bursts cost a few parse/render cycles instead of one per message. An isolated chunk, such as a keystroke's echo, is still written immediately, so typing latency is unchanged.
- **Cheap scrollbar reveal.** The macOS overlay scrollbar's reveal ran on every scroll event, which streaming output fires continuously, re-creating its hide timer and rewriting a data attribute each time. That was about 100 ms per `seq`. It now records a timestamp, and its single hide timer re-arms itself while scrolling continues. The visible behaviour (shown while scrolling, hidden 700 ms after it stops) is unchanged.

## Measurements

macOS, production renderer build, `seq 1 100000; echo AO_DONE`. Times run from Enter until the `AO_DONE` marker reaches the renderer; medians of 5–6 runs.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| End of output in renderer | ~2.4 s | **~150 ms** |
| `seq` runtime (shell `time`) | ~1.9 s (program paused) | ~125–140 ms |
| WebSocket messages | ~700 (small PTY reads at the throttled rate) / ~20,000 once unthrottled | ~2,500 |
| pty-host CPU during output (shell terminal) | ~1.75 s per run | ~0.07 s per run |

For reference, the earlier screen-level benchmark gave T3 Code 188 ms, Orca 246 ms, Superset 296 ms and Conductor 338 ms.

## Tests

- **New Go tests:**
  - async surface: writes don't wait for the emulator; reads wait for queued output in order; overflow rebuilds from the ring; lazy build on first read; real emulator output;
  - flow control: a slow viewer gets every frame and isn't dropped (fails if the grace is 0, i.e. the old instant drop); a stalled viewer is dropped after the grace while a fast viewer keeps receiving;
  - `bytePipe`: one read returns all buffered output; the writer waits when full; buffered output arrives before the close error;
  - out-queue merging and its size bound;
  - `HostOptions` argument round trip and spawner passthrough;
  - shell and command terminals request lazy styled output.
- **New frontend tests:** live output arriving during a write is joined into the next write; held output is flushed on teardown; continuous scrolling keeps the scrollbar up until 700 ms after the last scroll.
- `go vet` passes for darwin, linux and windows. The conpty, terminal and shellterm packages pass with `-race`. The terminal frontend tests pass (266).

## Risks / follow-ups

- **New flow-control rule.** A slow (not stalled) viewer now briefly throttles output for the terminal, including other viewers of the same terminal, instead of being dropped and missing output. A viewer that stops reading is dropped after 3 s instead of immediately.
- **Windows.** Builds and vets; not run on Windows.
- **Agent CLI output, follow-up.** `Ring.Append` re-joins the current partial line on every chunk, so full-screen TUIs that redraw without newlines make it progressively more expensive. Separate change.

title: fix(chat): release untouched project conversations on terminal switch
body:
Code changes: +2 -1\
Tests: +61 -0\
Others: +2 -1 (generated sqlc)

## What

A fresh, never-prompted orchestrator can now switch from Chat to Terminal. `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider` also matches project-scoped conversations, so the untouched Chat provider binding is released and the controller epoch commits.

## Why

Fixes #6235.

Orchestrator conversations are project-scoped: `conversations.session_id` is NULL and ownership lives in `current_session_id`. The release query only matched `c.session_id = @session_id`, so for an orchestrator it updated 0 rows and the epoch commit failed with `release untouched Chat provider for <session>: empty root proof changed`. The switch then ended in `recovery_required` and left the orchestrator stopped.

In the original report, "Resume agent" afterwards returned a 500, which looks like the symptom in #5922. This PR does not change that resume path, so #5922 should stay open.

## How

- The subquery accepts either the existing session-scoped owner (`c.session_id = @session_id`, unchanged) or a project-scoped conversation (`c.scope = 'project' AND c.session_id IS NULL`). All other guards are unchanged: `current_session_id` must be the switching session, the root branch must belong to it, `latest_sequence = 0`, and there are no turns.
- This matches how the Go side already reads ownership: `conversationToDomain` maps `SessionID` from `current_session_id`, so the untouched-conversation preflight in `interface_transition.go` already passes for orchestrators. Only the SQL disagreed.
- I kept the change narrow instead of dropping the `session_id` check, so session-scoped behavior is unchanged.
- Intentionally not addressed: after the failed epoch commit, restoring Chat also failed (`... persist browser capability verifier: session controller ownership changed before browser capability rotation`). With this fix that rollback is no longer reached in this scenario. The rollback path itself is a separate issue and is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

- New `TestFreshInterfaceEpochReleasesUntouchedProjectConversationProvider` (`store/session_interface_fresh_test.go`): a fresh orchestrator with a project-scoped conversation releases the provider binding and commits TUI; with a provider turn it is refused and ownership is unchanged. The `fresh` case fails on `main` with the reported error and passes with this change. The existing session-scoped test still passes.
- End to end on Windows 11 against two isolated daemons (private `AO_DATA_DIR`/`AO_RUN_FILE`/port) built from `main` and from this branch: Claude Code orchestrator in Chat, controller `ready`, no prompt sent, then `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interface-transition {"targetMode":"tui","policy":"drain"}`.

title: Validate release lockfiles with the same Node and npm toolchain used to build artifacts
body:
## What happened
The [October 4 artifact build](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/37173088836) failed during npm ci with:
```
Missing: @pierre/theme@1.1.0 from lock file
```

#6214 restored the missing nested optional-peer entry and the later nightly shipped. That repairs this lockfile, but leaves the condition that caused the failure.

## Cause
On current main, .github/workflows/frontend.yml uses Node 24 while the frontend install in .github/workflows/build-artifacts.yml uses Node 22. The PR documents npm 11 accepting a lockfile that release npm 10 rejects after #6145 added @pierre/trees. Regenerating with the newer npm can remove the compatibility entry again.

This is a desktop artifact-build issue, separate from the private landing repository's missing weekly changelog run.

## Fix
Pick and pin a tested Node/npm toolchain for both PR validation and artifact builds. If both runtimes must remain supported, add a required clean-install matrix that checks the committed lockfile with the actual release npm version. Keep signing/publishing out of this validation job.

## Done when
- [ ] Document and pin the supported Node and npm versions.
- [ ] A clean PR install reproduces the artifact-build dependency resolution.
- [ ] The pre-#6214 lockfile fails the added release-toolchain regression check.
- [ ] Current lockfile passes all supported install environments.
- [ ] Verify unsigned artifact builds on Windows, Linux and both macOS architectures.
- [ ] Do not treat the one-entry lockfile repair alone as the permanent fix.

Related bootstrap work: #4396. This issue is specifically the release/PR validation mismatch.

title: fix(cloud): bump backend pin so the CP image builds with agentruntime.Effort
body:
## Problem

The control-plane Docker image does not build from current main. `#6163` added cloud code that uses `agentruntime.Effort` (in `agentruntime.RestoreConfig` and `agentruntime.LaunchConfig`), a backend field introduced on 2026-09-24 by `#5208`. But the `#6163` merge did not bump `cloud/go.mod`'s backend `replace` pin, which still points at an Aug-12 commit (`...20260812094327-5da0ce157982`) that predates the field.

Local and CI builds pass because the repo `go.work` makes them use the in-repo `backend/` (which has `Effort`). The control-plane Docker build has no `go.work` and compiles `cloud/` against the pinned backend, so it fails:

```
cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go:150: unknown field Effort in struct literal of type agentruntime.RestoreConfig
cloud/internal/workerexec/command.go:167: unknown field Effort in struct literal of type agentruntime.LaunchConfig
```

This affects both the official `deploy-staging.sh` / `promote-production.sh` flow and any manual CP build, so main is currently not deployable.

## Fix

Bump the `cloud/go.mod` backend `replace` pin to the backend module at main HEAD (`168f09b74`), which is exactly what `go.work` and CI already build against. `go mod tidy` pulled the three transitive `golang.org/x/*` minor bumps the newer backend requires.

## Verification

Compiled every binary the control-plane Dockerfile builds with `go.work` disabled (`GOWORK=off`), which is the same module resolution the Docker build uses:

```
GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/ao-cloud ./cmd/ao-cloud-migrate ./cmd/ao-cloud-healthcheck ./cmd/ao-worker ./cmd/ao-cloud-agent
```

All succeed. Note that CI cannot catch this class of regression on its own, since CI builds through `go.work`; a cloud change that uses a newer backend API needs the pin bumped in the same change.

title: feat: terminal auth readiness for all harnesses + council multi-model fan-out
body:
## What & why

Two features plus a follow-up fix, from a request to (1) make terminal-based provider authentication work for every harness and (2) be able to run several models on one task.

### 1. fix(agentauth): refresh harness readiness when a login terminal completes
Previously only Codex's login terminal had a daemon-side completion watcher. For every other harness, a finished sign-in was only noticed if the Settings panel happened to be polling, so the harness could stay "needs auth" after a successful login. Now the daemon watches the login command of **any** harness and, on exit, invalidates + re-checks that harness's readiness. Additive and opt-in via `EnableLoginCompletionRefresh`; no API or migration changes.

### 2. feat(sessions): council fan-out (several models, one task)
New `POST /api/v1/sessions/council` and `ao council` fan one brief out to 2-8 harness/model members, each its own worker session, all tagged with a shared `councilGroupId` so clients can compare the cohort side by side. Best-effort: each member returns its session or its spawn error.
- Backend: `ports.CouncilInput/Result`, `Service.SpawnCouncil`, `SessionMetadata.CouncilGroupID`, controller + DTOs, regenerated OpenAPI + `schema.ts`.
- CLI: `ao council --name ... --prompt ... --member harness[:model[:effort]] ...` + telemetry classification.
- Frontend: `useSpawnCouncil` hook.

### 3. fix(sessions): keep council group id through spawn/restore metadata rebuilds
The TUI spawn, Chat spawn, and restore paths rebuild `SessionMetadata` from a fixed field list, which dropped `CouncilGroupID` — found via live testing (council members lost their cohort link after launch). Carried over in all three paths, with a test.

## Testing
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean.
- Targeted suites green: `service/session`, `httpd/...`, `agentauth`, `cli`, `telemetrymeta`, `daemon`, plus the new council tests and the spawn group-id test.
- Verified **live** against a dev daemon: `ao council` created worker sessions across codex/copilot/autohand sharing one `councilGroupId`.
- Frontend typecheck clean for touched files (`src/renderer`, `src/api`).

## Notes for reviewer
- Two pre-existing integration tests fail without real agent binaries and fail on clean `main` too - not introduced here: `session_manager/TestInterfaceTransitionNativeHistoryOwnership` and `codexappserver/TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider`.
- Council v1 is manual side-by-side comparison; an auto-judge/aggregator is intentionally left for a follow-up.
- `golangci-lint` and the full frontend build / `packages/product-ui` were not runnable in the dev environment - please confirm in CI.

title: feat(review): let agents request AO native review of their own PRs
body:
Code changes: +982 -410  
Tests: +1339 -459  
Others: +155 -37 (generated OpenAPI/TS schema, i18n, docs, skill text)

## Why

A worker (worker100, PR #6258) repeatedly asked the orchestrator for an independent review. The orchestrator spawned a generic worker (worker106) instead of using AO's native reviewer, and the conversation then drifted to GitHub's "authors can't approve their own PR" rule, which is a separate boundary. PR #6258 sat at `needs_review` with **zero** native review runs.

The native reviewer was mature. The gaps were in how agents reach it:

1. The worker prompt never mentioned native review and sent "review help" to the orchestrator.
2. The orchestrator prompt said to spawn a worker for *every* code-review task.
3. `ao review trigger` required an explicit session id.
4. A review reached the worker twice: once as AO's verdict message and once as the reviewer's GitHub comments, which turned optional suggestions into required work.
5. Agent-requested passes were labelled `manual`, the same as a person's click.
6. Only per-adapter allowlists stopped a reviewer from triggering reviews.

## What

Behavior agreed with the user before implementation:

- **The worker reviews its own PR.** `ao review trigger`, `ao review ls` and `ao review cancel` default to the calling session (`AO_SESSION_ID`).
  - `trigger` takes `--agent/--harness`, `--model` and `--effort` per pass.
  - Runs are recorded with the new trigger source `agent`; the inspector labels them "Requested by agent".
  - The command refuses to run inside a reviewer pane (`AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID`), so reviewers never start reviews.
- **Same-commit policy.** If a head already has a review, or a review is still running on it, `trigger` exits 1 with `409 REVIEW_HEAD_ALREADY_REVIEWED` or `REVIEW_ALREADY_RUNNING`, and the message says what to do next.
  - `--rerun` really reviews the same commit again. #6118's migration 0177 narrows the unique key to *running* passes; the #242 double-spawn guard is kept and tested.
  - There is no cap on review rounds. The desktop Run review button keeps its existing reuse behavior.
- **Parallel reviewers.** Reviewers with different agents can run on the same head at once (e.g. `--agent opencode --rerun` while Claude Code is running).
  - Trigger and worker restore no longer tear down a reviewer that is still working; only idle panes are released.
  - Stale-pane cleanup is scoped to one reviewer, and cancel stops every reviewer.
  - The list API exposes `activeReviewers`, and the inspector offers Open for each live reviewer.
- **Feedback loop (one channel).** AO's reviewer reaches the worker the same way any reviewer does: the SCM observer forwards its inline GitHub review comments. AO no longer sends a separate verdict message. This removes the pre-existing changes-requested verdict delivery (lifecycle `ApplyReviewBatch` and the review service's delivery step). Results are still recorded in AO and shown by `ao review ls` and the inspector.
  - The reviewer prompt requires an inline comment for every finding that needs a change, design-level ones included, and keeps optional suggestions in the summary only. Inline comments are all the worker receives, and it treats each as required.
  - Auto-inject stays a session setting. `ao review trigger` turns it on, since it controls review-comment forwarding, unless you pass `--no-inject`. Auto-review and the UI's Run review never change it.
  - An approval adds no comments, so the worker checks `ao review ls` for the verdict before reporting done.
- **Policy.** New project setting **Workers request AO review** (`workersRequestReview`, off by default), with a Settings toggle and a CLI `set-config` round-trip.
  - On: workers request a review once their PR is ready, and again after each fix.
  - Off: workers are taught the feature but ask the user or orchestrator first.
  - Either way, workers are told never to spawn a reviewer worker.
- **Orchestrator.** It never spawns workers to review code. It runs `ao review trigger <worker>`. For a PR that no AO session owns, it asks the human how to proceed.
- **Reviewer defaults.** Session reviewer choice, then the project reviewer config, then the project's **default worker agent with its model and effort**. Worker permissions are never inherited. Settings shows the inherited model truthfully.
- **Unchanged.** Merge rules, branch protection and GitHub credentials are untouched. The reviewer still posts `COMMENT` reviews from the author's account.

No provider issue backs this task (it is a freeform task from the user), so nothing is linked.

## Rebased onto main with #6118 and #6291

- **Migration:** #6118 shipped the identical approved-head migration as `0177_review_run_rerun_same_head.sql` (same blob). This PR no longer adds its own; `TestMigration0177AllowsRepeatApprovalsButNotDoubleRunning` now covers up/down for `0177`.
- **Trigger contract unified:** #6118's `TriggerOptions{Harness, Config, Source, InterfaceMode, Rerun}` gains `RejectReviewedHead`. All HTTP triggers go through one service path (`TriggerRequested`); `TriggerWithMode`/`TriggerWithOptions` stay as wrappers.
- **Rerun policy:** a person's rerun (`manual`) keeps #6118's behavior and reuses an active pass from the same reviewer (200). An agent's rerun (`agent`) gets `409 REVIEW_ALREADY_RUNNING` instead, so it knows nothing new started. Agents may now rerun; #6118 allowed only manual.
- **#6291 archive:** an archived reviewer is never listed in `activeReviewers`, and worker restore still skips it.

## Changed after real-agent testing on the rebased build

- **One feedback channel (decided with the user):** see "Feedback loop" above. It fixes a review being delivered twice and optional suggestions being escalated to required work.

- **Fresh PR facts on trigger:** a requested review (manual or agent) fetches the worker's open PRs from the provider first, through the session claim path, and then decides what is due. It is bounded at 10s and best effort for tracked PRs; on failure it falls back to stored facts. Auto-review does not refresh. Right after a push the provider itself can lag 1 to 2 seconds, so the already-reviewed message says to retry after a few seconds.
- **`ao review trigger --pr <url>` (`prUrl`, same names as #6136):** reviews only that PR. A PR AO doesn't track yet is attached first and never taken over from another active session (`409 REVIEW_PR_OWNED_BY_OTHER_SESSION`). With no tracked PR, the error points at `--pr`.
- **Failed or cancelled runs:** nothing reports these to the worker, so its instructions say to re-trigger when `ao review ls` shows `failed` or `cancelled`.

## Follow-ups found testing with real agents (included)

- The inspector refreshes a session's reviews on `review_run_created`/`review_run_updated`. Before, a review an agent started, or a reviewer finished, stayed invisible until something else refreshed.
- When the selected reviewer is idle and another is working (an agent used `--agent codex`), the inspector offers to open the working one and the Reviewer tab shows it. The selected-reviewer fields in the API keep meaning the selected reviewer; clients read `activeReviewers`.
- Worker restore no longer cancels a running Chat reviewer for having no pane; Chat reviewers are recovered by `RecoverChatReviewers`.

Verified in a dev Electron build with real Claude Code and Codex agents on a private playground repo. The worker requested its own review; Claude and Codex reviewers approved and posted COMMENT reviews; verdicts were delivered to the worker (that build still had verdict delivery; see the change above); same-commit re-trigger was refused; the inspector updated live.

Then, on the head with the forced refresh and `--pr`, against the same playground:
- Push, wait until GitHub reported the new head, then trigger at once, with AO's stored head still on the old commit: the run reviewed the new commit (`b745ebe`).
- A trigger within about a second of the push saw the old head, because GitHub's API had not updated yet; it reported the new head 1 to 2 seconds later. That build answered with a local-git probe (`REVIEW_HEAD_NOT_OBSERVED`); AO's review then showed the probe misfires when the provider is ahead of the local ref, so it was removed and the already-reviewed message says to retry after a few seconds.
- `ao review trigger --pr <url>` right after `gh pr create` (PR #4, untracked by AO) attached the PR and started its review within 1 second; the reviewer posted an inline comment.


## Changed after AO's own review of this PR

- Removed the local-git pushed-head probe and `REVIEW_HEAD_NOT_OBSERVED`; the provider refresh covers it.
- `List` keeps the selected-reviewer fields meaning the selected reviewer; the client picks a working reviewer from `activeReviewers`.
- Removed trigger entry points with no production callers (service `Trigger`/`TriggerWithMode`/`TriggerWithOptions`, engine `Trigger`/`TriggerWithSource`/`TriggerWithSourceAndMode`) and the unused `MarkReviewRunDelivered` writer. The `delivered` status stays for existing rows.
- `Engine.Cancel` cancels legacy harness-less runs once.

## Verification

Local runs used the CI commands. The Go suites ran with the AO session environment unset, as on CI:

- Backend: `gofmt`, `go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint v2.13.2` (0 issues), `npm run sqlc` (no drift), `npm run api` (spec and `schema.ts` regenerated, no further drift).
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`: 187 packages ok. Three unrelated failures, each checked:
  - `codexappserver/TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` also fails on clean `origin/main`; it compares against this machine's installed `codex`.
  - `goose` and `conpty` failed once under heavy concurrent load and passed `-race -count=3` on this branch (and on main).
- Frontend: `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, full `vitest run` (383 files, 6136 tests passed), `test:browser-postcondition-integration`, docs build, and the product-ui and cloud-client checks all pass.
- **Isolated daemon end-to-end run** (scratch `AO_DATA_DIR`, lab pty host, fake `claude`/`opencode`/`gh` binaries, so no model spend and no GitHub writes in this phase). With a real spawned worker and a seeded PR:
  - The worker's system prompt contained the opt-in section.
  - `ao review trigger` from the worker started a Claude Code run labelled `agent` and turned on inject.
  - A repeat trigger was rejected with `REVIEW_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
  - An OpenCode reviewer ran **in parallel** without cancelling the first.
  - Submitted verdicts were delivered into the worker's pane on that pre-change build. Verdict delivery has since been replaced by PR-comment delivery (see above).
  - The reviewed head was rejected with `REVIEW_HEAD_ALREADY_REVIEWED`; a simulated push started a new review; cancel stopped both reviewers.
  - `--rerun` on an approved head started a new run (the real index).
  - The reviewer pane's environment carries `AO_REVIEW_SESSION_ID` and no `AO_SESSION_ID`, and the CLI refusal fires there.
- **Isolated Electron run** (dev build of this branch, separate profile and run file, the same scratch data): the inspector listed two live reviewers with Open (opening OpenCode switched the reviewer tab), the run showed "Approved · Requested by agent", and Settings showed **Workers request AO review** on.

### Not verified locally

- Windows, macOS-update and Docker CLI e2e jobs.
- Local Node is 22; CI uses 24.

Remote checks on the previous head all passed, including the Windows, macOS and Linux native jobs, which cover the gaps above.

## Risks and follow-ups

- **Overlap with open review PRs.**
  - #6118 touches `service/review` and `review/review.go`.
  - #5571 adds sequential multi-reviewer aggregation. This PR keeps "latest run wins, but running has priority" per head and does not aggregate verdicts.
  - #6136 adds per-PR targeting.
  - #5753 changes the reviewer prompt only (no overlap).
  - Expect small rebases.
- **Parallel reviewers share one reviewer tab.** The tab follows the reviewer you open; it is not one tab per reviewer.
- **Pre-existing crash found during the Electron run (not fixed here).** `SessionPRMergeabilitySummary.Reasons` serialises as `null` for an open PR whose mergeability is unknown/mergeable, and `pr-display.ts` calls `.includes` on it. The inspector crashes for a PR the SCM observer can't read. Worth a separate fix.
- **Prompt changes apply at spawn.** Existing workers keep their prompt until they are respawned.

title: fix(api): never serialize PR mergeability reasons as null
body:
Code changes: +3 -1  
Tests: +19 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Why

Opening the session inspector for **any open PR that is mergeable** crashes the desktop session view with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'includes')
    at prCardPresentation (renderer/lib/pr-display.ts)
    at PRSummaryCard (renderer/components/SessionInspector.tsx)
```

The daemon's session PR summary sends `mergeability.reasons: null` when a PR has no blocking reasons (a mergeable or not-yet-observed PR). #6163 made `pr-display.ts` call `pr.mergeability.reasons.includes(...)` for every open PR. Before that, `null` was never read on this path.

Found while testing #6262 against a real GitHub PR in a dev build. Payload from `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/pr` for that PR:

```json
"mergeability": {"state": "mergeable", "reasons": null, "prUrl": "…/pull/1"}
```

## What

`newSessionPRMergeabilitySummary` always sends an array (`[]` when there are no reasons), the same way `conflictFiles` beside it is already kept non-null. The fix sits at the one HTTP boundary every PR summary passes through, so all clients get the shape the contract (`string[]`) promises. No renderer change is needed.

## Verification

- New `TestSessionPRSummaryReasonsAreNeverNull` fails before the fix (`"reasons":null`) and passes after, for both mergeable and unknown states.
- `gofmt`, `golangci-lint v2.13.2` (0 issues).

title: fix(cloud): recover missing Claude ACP conversations in Chat
body:
Code changes: +55 -26  
Tests: +238 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Fix Claude Cloud Chat failing with `restore ACP session: Resource not found` when AO retains a native conversation ID that the ACP adapter can no longer restore.

The CLI command builder's missing-transcript check changes only its local turn copy and CLI arguments. The ACP runner still receives the durable conversation ID and previously failed immediately when the adapter rejected it.

- Keep the ACP adapter authoritative: restore available conversations normally.
- On Claude's explicit resource-not-found error (`-32002`) from `session/load`, create a replacement session using the same workspace and standing instructions.
- Publish the replacement native ID through the existing durable activity path before sending the prompt, so subsequent turns and interface handoffs use the new ID.
- Preserve authentication, cancellation, internal, transport, and other restore failures instead of treating them as missing history. A failed identity write stops prompt delivery.

This restores usability when native history is gone; it cannot reconstruct a deleted Claude transcript. No Restart conversation button, deployment, or production configuration change is included. Includes the terminal test stabilization from #6248 because the inherited flaky test failed this PR’s backend CI. The frontend release version update remains separate in #6248.

## Regression coverage

The regression drives the real Chat supervisor and ACP process protocol through a local fake adapter, covering successful restore, missing transcript, adapter rejection despite a transcript being present, authentication/internal/cancellation errors, failed durable identity publication, and the following turn resuming the replacement ID.

## Validation

- Before the fix, both missing-session cases reproduced the exact `-32002` restore failure.
- Full cloud `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` passed.
- Full cloud race suite passed: `go test -race -count=1 -p 2 ./...`. Package parallelism was bounded to avoid local resource contention.
- Claude restore regressions and cross-harness standing-prompt tests rerun after merging upstream main.
- `git diff --check` clean.

The initial remote cloud build/test, Windows workspace tests, lint, secrets scan, API drift, and sqlc drift checks passed. The backend build and vet passed, but the terminal stall test failed during the race suite. The terminal test now sends one frame beyond the maximum in-flight batch plus queue, reliably exercising the stall timeout; no terminal runtime behavior changes.

The updated terminal regression passed 20 race-test repetitions with `GOMAXPROCS=1`, and the full terminal package race suite passed. Updated remote CI remains pending; the local run was on macOS.

## Repeated sign-in callback fix

Clicking the browser’s Return to Agent Orchestrator button after a successful sign-in now quietly focuses the signed-in app without showing a verification-error popup or exchanging the single-use login code again. Concurrent callbacks are serialized. The verified callback digest is retained with the protected auth store so repeating it does not interrupt a newer pending login. Pending sign-ins still validate PKCE state; sign-out removes the callback receipt. Existing accounts saved before this fix also return quietly when no sign-in is pending.

Validation: all 31 WorkOS/local auth tests and the full frontend typecheck passed. Regression coverage includes sequential/concurrent callbacks, legacy stored accounts, sign-out, and preserving a newer pending login. No package manifest or lockfile changes were made.

title: fix(chat): settle Claude turns stuck after background-task cycles
body:
Code changes: +369 -26
Tests: +441 -0
Others: +0 -0

## What

Build-time patches to the pinned `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0, added to `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.mjs` and applied by `build-acp-runtime.mjs` next to the existing retry/context patches, plus a persistent chat-host watchdog.

- `patchClaudeFoldedPromptSettlement`: a `task-notification` result that names a pending prompt in `user_message_uuid(s)` now settles that prompt. Port of agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp#1233 for issue agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp#1145.
- `patchClaudeStaleIdleDebt`: drops the adapter's unpaid trailing-idle debt on an idle→running transition. Port of the sweep upstream shipped in claude-agent-acp 0.79.
- `patchClaudeSteerSettlement` (new): a result naming a steered message in `user_message_uuid(s)` retires the steer lane and settles through the ordinary result path. Port of the exact-result acknowledgement path upstream in claude-agent-acp#1166.
- `patchClaudeSteerIdleGuard` (new): the idle-debt absorption branch no longer consumes the one coalesced terminal idle of a *completed* steer sequence (echo replayed and steered result recorded). Incomplete steer sequences keep absorbing, so their terminal idle is still ahead.
- `patchClaudeSteerDebt` (new): steering a turn that recorded a held result hands that result's trailer to the steer lane's idle, and an autonomous result the pending steer aborted shares the steered sequence's single idle instead of owing its own. When the settlement patch has already retired the lane, a steer-answering result owes no fresh trailer.
- Persistent chat-host watchdog (new): an in-flight `session/prompt` that has heard nothing from the adapter for 15 minutes gets a terminal `-32603` error instead of hanging the session's Working indicator until restart. This is a backstop for adapter state losses this PR does not (yet) settle, e.g. a lost subagent task-end bookend.

## Why

Claude chat sessions keep showing "Working for N min" long after the agent has finished, until the user presses Stop or sends another message. There are three triggers:

1. A message sent while Claude is handling a background-task notification gets folded into that cycle. The cycle's result keeps `origin: task-notification`, so the adapter treats it as autonomous and never answers `session/prompt`, and the AO turn stays `running`. Reproduction steps are in a comment below.
2. When a background task's notification arrives before the turn that started it ends, Claude Code emits a single idle for both. One owed idle is never paid, and it later swallows the idle a steered turn settles on, so that steered turn hangs.
3. Even with fixes 1 and 2 installed, a live session still hung "Working forever": a human result held open for a background subagent, steered during the subagent's hand-back cycle, ends with the steered answer recorded in the steer lane — and the single idle the SDK emits for the whole wake+steer+steered sequence was absorbed as owed trailing-idle debt *before* the steer lane could run. The debt reset from `patchClaudeStaleIdleDebt` cannot help because there is no idle→running transition anywhere inside that stretch. This PR fixes that live case end-to-end.

No upstream release fixes #1145 yet (latest is 0.85.1). These patches should be removed once we bump to a release that includes all of the fixes.

## How

- All patches use the same tripwire style as the existing ones: an exact anchor match, so packaging fails instead of silently skipping the patch if upstream code changes.
- The fold patch sends a result down the ordinary user-turn path only when it names an unsettled turn that isn't held open for background subagents. Results without the uuid stamp behave exactly as before; Claude Code older than 2.1.268 doesn't stamp them, so that case still hangs, with no regression.
- The debt reset fires only on a real transition into `running`. An idle that arrives late for the previous turn is still absorbed, so the adapter's #825 stuck-turn detection is unaffected.
- The steer settlement patch tracks injected steer UUIDs separately from the replay-echo bookkeeping, so a stamped result retires the lane even when its echo frame was lost. Cancelled turns are untouched, and unstamped results keep the prior idle behavior (covered by the idle guard and debt accounting instead).
- The watchdog stamps the last adapter output on every frame, runs on a 30s check under the host mutex (never racing `forwardProvider`), resolves only same-generation prompts (reconnect-recovery owns earlier ones), and stays terminal — it cannot fire twice, and the session accepts a new prompt once the controller acknowledges the synthetic completion.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.test.mjs`: 36 passed. The tests run the patched code itself, not just string checks.
- The upstream 0.70.0 adapter suite run against the patched dist: 812 passed, 0 failed. A 9-case steer-into-held-turn regression suite (replaying the captured live frame sequences) passes 9/9 on this patch set; the pre-steer-fix composition failed 3 of its 9 cases.
- Real end-to-end with Claude Code 2.1.292 on an isolated daemon: the exact trigger (async subagent, held human result, steer during the hand-back cycle) hung 2/2 against the previously-installed patches (3 results + 1 idle, turn running forever, queued message undelivered); with these commits the same choreography settles in milliseconds and the queued message is delivered. Plain-steer, folded-prompt, held-turn-no-steer, and followup-at-turn-end controls all settle with no failed turns.
- The `no-task-notification` sequence (lost task-end bookend) still stalls the adapter and is intentionally not fixed here; the watchdog converts that hang into a terminal error after 15 minutes instead.

title: fix: Claude Code shows signed-out on expired OAuth; stuck session can't be deleted
body:
Code changes: +105 -0
Tests: +106 -0
Others: +0 -0

## Why

Two bugs that together made Claude unusable in AO and left a session stuck and undeletable:

1. **Auth false-negative.** The Claude auth ladder's network probe reads the short-lived OAuth access token from the keychain and calls `GET /v1/models`. A Claude Max subscription access token expires routinely while the user stays signed in — Claude Code refreshes it from the refresh token, so `claude auth status` keeps reporting `loggedIn`. AO saw the `401 "OAuth access token has expired"` and classified the credential as Invalid, rendering a working, signed-in user as **"Signed out"** and blocking Claude launches.

2. **Undeletable wedged session.** A switch stuck at `source_restore_unconfirmed` ("Codex could not be restored") can be neither recovered (the source relaunch keeps failing) nor auto-failed (its retained recovery marker must never sit on a failed row), so it holds the switch/input gate forever. `Kill` acquires that gate first, so it refused with `ErrSwitchInProgress` — the session could never be removed and its terminal stayed locked.

## What

1. Treat an **expired-but-refreshable** OAuth access token as inconclusive (`StateUnknown`) instead of a decisive rejection (mirrors the existing `IsResolverBug` downgrade). The ladder then defers to the CLI/local rungs → "Configured", and launch is allowed (Claude refreshes the token on start). A revoked token ("... is invalid") does not match and stays a decisive rejection.
2. `Kill` now finalizes a retained stuck switch (`source_session_terminated`) and releases its gate before acquiring the kill gate, so a wedged session is removable. It acts only when the gate is held as a retained recovery fence, never racing a live switch worker. `reconcileAgentSwitch` gains the same terminated-session handling so a reaper-terminated session self-heals on boot instead of re-quarantining.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `go test` on the touched packages: green. New unit tests for both fixes (`TestValidateResolvedLocalTreatsExpiredOAuthAsRefreshable`, `TestValidateResolvedLocalKeepsRevokedOAuthInvalid`, `TestIsRefreshableOAuthExpiry`, `TestAbandonRetainedAgentSwitchForTerminationReleasesStuckGate`).
- Verified live in the real Electron app: Claude Code flipped from "Signed out" to "Configured", a Claude Code session launched (ACP connected, all start stages OK), and it responded correctly in-session.

title: fix: unify the effort picker and select a default effort
body:
Code changes: +354 -105  
Tests: +328 -19  
Others: +80 -0 (translations)

## Summary

Extract the effort picker UI from #6236 into an independent PR targeting `main`, and make sure a model that offers effort levels never shows an unselected effort.

- Share effort menu rendering across New Task, project settings, and native/ACP chat.
- Show only concrete, localized effort names (Medium, High, Extra high, ...) in menus and selectors. No Default, Use agent effort, or Effort not reported rows. Levels a provider reports that AO does not know are shown as reported.
- Use consistent effort row typography and short, compact menus; remove explanatory fallback paragraphs.
- Hide empty effort controls; retain saved values and an explicit Clear effort action for unavailable saved selections.
- Select an effort when the model reports levels but no usable default (see below).

## Default effort when the provider reports none

When a model offers levels but the provider names no default for them, AO picks the middle level (`fallbackEffort` in `lib/effort.ts`) and treats it as the real selection, so the level a picker shows is the level the run uses. A provider that reports a default among its levels is always left in charge, and a level the user picks always wins.

| Surface | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| New Task | Shown as selected and sent when the task starts. |
| Project settings | Shown as selected and saved when the user chooses a model. Opening settings does not write anything. |
| Chat (ACP and native menu) | Set when the user switches model, and on open only for a conversation with no turns yet. Reopening an existing local conversation does not change the effort it was running with (cloud chat has a known gap, see below). Nothing is set while the chat controls are disabled (controller stopped, connecting or provisioning, or a config change in flight). |

Selecting the provider's reported default level behaves differently by surface: on ACP chat pickers that expose a reset choice it sends the provider reset token; on New Task, project settings, and the native chat menu it clears the explicit choice so the agent default applies.

Also in this PR: a saved effort for a model missing from a loaded catalog is flagged invalid again, while a listed model whose provider reports no efforts keeps its saved effort.

## Scope

Frontend only. Model fetching, caching, account handling, model catalog ordering, additional models, and backend effort transport remain in the existing PR stack. This PR can merge directly into `main`; it does not require #6234, #6236, or #6251.

## Validation

Run on the current head, after merging the latest `main`:

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- 54 affected test files (effort picker, composer, project settings, chat, i18n): 1,197 passing.
- Full renderer suite on the previous head: 6,150 passing, 22 failing. All 22 are in `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch, and come from a `better-sqlite3` native-module ABI mismatch (built for Electron, not the test runner).
- CI (`test`, `scan`, `renderer-smoke`, `mac-update-helper`) was green on the previous head; re-check it on the latest.
- Checked by hand in the desktop app on isolated data: with Claude Code and Sonnet 5.5 (five levels, no default) New Task shows High checked and sends `reasoningEffort: "high"`; the alias model with no levels shows no chip; an explicit level survives a model switch in chat; project settings shows `Sonnet 5.5 · High` and saves `worker.agentConfig.effort = "high"` when the model is chosen.

Known limitations (follow-up):

- Cloud chat can set an effort on an existing conversation that has no saved effort, if the model list arrives before the conversation history. The cloud snapshot is empty until its events load and its controller never reports `connecting`, so "no turns yet" is briefly true. Effect: the next turn runs at AO's level instead of the provider default; the user can change it in the picker. Fix: pass a history-loaded signal from `CloudSessionChatSurface` into `ChatWorkspace`.
- Cloud re-syncs the native model catalog and can reset `reasoningEffort` to what the provider reports, which clears AO's level until the model changes again. This is the previous behavior, not a new one.

Not verified:

- The native chat menu (cloud sessions) has no live check, only unit tests.
- The ACP "default names no level" branch needs a harness that resets the effort to `default` on a model switch (OpenCode does). It is covered by unit tests; I did not exercise it live.
- The earlier local checks (product UI, cloud client, docs build, native helper, renderer smoke on macOS) were not re-run for this head.
