title: fix(chat): recover untouched Chat sessions across interface switch, rollback, and resume
body:
Code changes: +252 -33  
Tests: +688 -1  
Others: +64 -3 (generated sqlc)

## What

Fixes three defects that together left an untouched Chat session (no messages sent) stuck with "The agent controller stopped" and an "Internal server error" on **Resume agent**:

1. Switching an untouched **orchestrator** Chat to Terminal always failed with `empty root proof changed`.
2. The rollback of that failed switch failed with `session controller ownership changed before browser capability rotation`, leaving the transition in `recovery_required`.
3. Resuming an untouched Chat whose persistent provider host had died failed with ACP `session/load` `-32002 Resource not found`.

## Why

Fixes #6267

- **Switch:** orchestrator conversations are project-scoped (`conversations.session_id` is NULL, the active orchestrator is `current_session_id`), but `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider` (added in #5053) required `session_id` to match.
- **Rollback:** when the controller epoch never committed, rollback relaunched with `fresh=true`, which clears the provider id only in memory. The database still held it, so the expected controller owner mismatched during browser capability rotation.
- **Resume:** Claude Code reserves a session id when a Chat opens but writes no transcript until the first prompt. With the host gone, reloading that id can never succeed.

## How

One commit per defect:

- **`fix(chat): release untouched orchestrator Chat…`**: the release predicate accepts a project-scoped conversation currently bound to the session. The empty-history guards (`latest_sequence = 0`, no turns) are unchanged, so a conversation with history, another session's conversation, or a reviewer conversation is still never released.
- **`fix(chat): start fresh when resuming an untouched Chat…`**: a surviving host still holds the session in memory and must be reattached, and only the driver knows whether it is alive. So the fallback lives where a reload actually fails:
  - Session Manager always offers the stored id. It sets `FreshIfProviderConversationMissing` only for an ordinary resume with durable proof the conversation never started (the adapter finds no persisted history, and AO recorded no turns or messages). This reuses `persistedNativeConversationID` / `nativeConversationNotStarted`.
  - The ACP driver opens a new session on the freshly spawned connection only when the reload returns `-32002` and the flag is set. Other errors and non-ACP drivers are unchanged.
  - The Chat service accepts the different provider id only with the flag and without a live reconnect, and skips native-history import.
  - `ControllerReady` moves the session and its untouched root branch to the new id in one guarded transaction (`ReplaceUnpersistedChatProvider`). The root **keeps its provider scope**, which is part of the persistent host's ownership fingerprint. The `conversation_branch_root_provider_update` trigger only fires for `'' → id`, so the root update is explicit.
- **`fix(chat): restore the durable Chat owner when a switch rolls back…`**: rollback starts fresh only if the epoch committed or the source is not Chat. TUI sources and committed rollbacks are unchanged.
- Compatible with #6254's reconnect-only startup health check: the fresh-start fallback is disabled when `ReconnectOnly` is set (driver and Session Manager), so a health check never opens a new provider session.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- Clearing the stored id before resuming broke reattach to a live host ("fresh ACP start found an existing initialized session").
- Rotating the root's provider scope broke the host fingerprint ("provider launch configuration changed").

**Known limitation (pre-existing, not addressed):** if a still-untouched project conversation is rebound to a *second* orchestrator, the next Chat→Terminal switch is refused cleanly at the same release check. It ends in `failed`, not stuck. Tracking as a follow-up.

## Testing

From `backend/`:

    GOWORK=off go vet ./...
    GOWORK=off go test -race -count=1 ./...

New tests, each of which fails without its fix:

- `store`: `TestFreshInterfaceEpochReleasesUntouchedProjectConversation`, `TestReplaceUnpersistedChatProviderMovesSessionAndRoot`
- `acp`: `TestACPDriverResumeStartsFreshOnlyForMissingSessionWhenAllowed`
- `service/chat`: `TestResumeAcceptsFreshProviderOnlyWhenAllowed`
- `session_manager`: `TestResumeUntouchedChatStartsFreshWhenProviderNeverPersisted`, `TestInterfaceTransitionRollbackRestoresUncommittedChatSource`

Manual, in the desktop app (isolated dev data, macOS):

- Untouched orchestrator Chat → Terminal: the switch completes.
- Claude Code, host alive: quit and relaunch, then Resume. The session reattaches with the same provider id.
- Claude Code, host killed: Resume returns 200, the log shows `ACP session missing; started fresh`, and the session and root move to the new id with the same scope and no child branch.
- Codex orchestrator start: unaffected.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat: add CLIProxyAPI account management and routing
body:
Code changes: +6021 -10234\
Tests: +10479 -8419\
Others: +3743 -5045

## What

Account Manager: several Claude and Codex accounts in AO, with each session's model requests sent to that session's account through a small helper process built on the CLIProxyAPI SDK. It replaces the Codex subscription management, which this PR removes.

The daemon owns accounts, per-provider defaults and session routes. The detached helper (`ao-proxy-host`) holds the sign-ins, forwards requests and counts what passes through each account; it knows no provider response shape.

Started by @whoisasx. After review the PR was taken over; [Changes after review](#changes-after-review) lists what changed since.

## What a user gets

- Sign in to Claude and Codex accounts inside AO: browser sign-in, Codex device code, API key, or credential JSON import. A browser sign-in opens the provider's page, and the page it returns to says whether the sign-in worked. A label typed with an API key names its account. AO copies nothing from the computer. An agent whose provider has no account in AO keeps the computer's own setup (its login, an API key, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, `apiKeyHelper`, a custom Codex `model_provider`), as on `main`.
- Settings > Accounts, a list beside a detail:
  - plan, limits with reset times, resets and extra usage, a default per provider, rename, renew sign-in, sign out, remove, move sessions; the list shows each account's limit with the least left;
  - what AO sent through the account: tokens per day for 14 days, today, 7 days and since counting began, the share of each model, and the models the account can use, newest first;
  - health: the last refused request, refusals by kind, and the typical time to the first word;
  - the account's sessions by name with today's tokens, each one openable or movable, and an estimated cost of those sessions;
  - three settings: keep the account in reserve, switch its sessions to another account when its limit is reached, and warn when little is left;
  - a link to the provider's own plan page.
- "Device" marks the AO account with the same email as the computer's own login.
- On the harness pages, an agent whose provider has AO accounts shows them and a button to the Accounts page, instead of its own login and logout.
- Pick an account when starting a task; switch a session's account from the session menu. An account in reserve is not offered for a new task.
- Model pickers list the models of the session's account. A Codex sign-in lists only the models OpenAI offers that account.
- "Switch agent" between Claude and Codex keeps working. The session goes on its account for the target provider (the default the first time), and a switch back returns it to the account it had.
- A Codex session moves only between accounts of one kind, ChatGPT plan to plan or API key to key: Codex sends its earlier encrypted reasoning back on every turn, and the other kind cannot read it.
- Signing an account out moves its sessions to the replacement when they can go there. The others wait, and go on when the account signs in again. The sessions of a removed account go on the next sign-in they can move to.
- Sessions that predate Account Manager move onto their provider's default once it has one, chats and terminals alike, within about 30 seconds of the first sign-in. A session is moved when it is idle, never while it works or waits for an answer. A terminal is moved once nobody types in it, on screen or not: no text typed for 30 seconds and none typed since its turn ended. Its agent exits and is resumed on the account, with keystrokes held back for those seconds.
- Chats, side chats, terminals, background tasks and reviews all run on their session's account.

## How

- **One source of truth.** Account state is one JSON document in SQLite (`0199_provider_accounts.sql`). A change asks the helper first, then saves; the daemon re-sends the whole route table to the helper at start and every 10 seconds.
- **Managed providers.** AO manages a provider once it holds an account for it, signed in or not. Until then its agents run as on `main`, and old sessions are moved only onto a default account.
- **Routes and tickets.** A session has one route per provider it uses: its own agent's under the session's id, any other as `id/provider`. Each has a ticket derived from the session and the provider (an HMAC under the helper's ticket key), so an agent switch renames routes but moves no ticket, and an agent still running on the provider the session left keeps its account. Related work (a reviewer, a side chat, a background task) runs on the session's route for its own provider and never moves the session's own route. A terminal switch prepares the target's account without moving the route, and moves it only after the source agent has stopped.
- **One busy rule.** The helper refuses a sign-out or removal while one of that account's requests is in flight. A sign-out between two requests of a turn is accepted and the turn continues on the replacement account.
- **One helper interface.** `ports.AccountHelper`, implemented by `adapters/proxyhost.Client`. Usage, plan and reset shaping live in the daemon only.
- **Helper updates.** The daemon starts the helper with a build id (a hash of its binary), and `/ao/status` reports it. A running helper of another build is asked to stop (`POST /ao/stop`, refused with 409 while a request is in flight) and replaced once idle. The identity is kept in `run/host.json` and in `host.json`. A lost or broken copy is restored from the other, so a running helper and its sessions carry on. With both copies gone, AO starts on a new identity, and a helper whose identity was replaced stops by itself once idle.
- **Security boundary.** Control key and session tickets are separate; a ticket reaches only the inference paths and the model list; the helper selects exactly the session's account with no fallback; credential files are owner-only; account routes refuse foreign web origins and are absent on the LAN listener. The helper sets no management secret, so the SDK's management routes and its Redis-protocol listener are off, and AO registers the management handlers it needs behind its own boundary. Every request with an `Upgrade` header gets 501. The helper runs with umask 077, and at start it makes sign-ins saved earlier 0600.
- **Refusals.** A model the provider refuses (400, 404 or 422 that is not about the credential) returns the provider's own answer for that request and leaves the account available. A session whose account is signed out or removed gets one answer its CLI does not retry (403 for Claude Code, 400 for Codex), saying to sign in on the Accounts page.
- **Resets.** A reset whose answer was lost or unknown is sent again with the same request ID, so the provider answers `already_redeemed` and does not spend a second one.
- **Counting in the helper.** A usage plugin on the SDK counts tokens per account, model, day and session, and refusals by kind. Daily counts are kept across a restart in `run/activity.json`, keyed by a hash of the account; nothing but hashes and numbers is stored.
- **Readings are paced.** An account's limits are read every five minutes. A reading that fails is retried after a minute and the last good one stands for half an hour. What the helper counted itself is read on every request.
- **Moving old sessions.** At most four at once; a move starts when a turn ends and again at a check every 30 seconds. The sessions are listed again whenever the providers with a default account change, so a sign-in reaches sessions started while their provider had none.
- **Reports missed while closed.** At start the daemon applies the last end-of-turn report each session made while it was down, so a terminal that finished meanwhile reads as idle and can be moved.
- **Typing.** The terminal mux records when it last took input that carries text. Reports a terminal sends by itself (focus, theme, colour replies) and keys that only move or edit do not count, so they do not hold a move back. The resumed agent is reported idle, so it does not read as "No signal".
- **Six API operations** under `/api/v1/provider-accounts`, including one `actions` endpoint for per-account changes.

## Changes after review

Each item answers a review thread or a test report on this PR.

- AO no longer copies the computer's logins or keys, so renewing an account no longer signs the computer's `claude` or `codex` out; providers with no account in AO keep their own setup (6bb1ad169, af3564edc).
- A broken `host.json` gets a new identity (b93004960); an AO update replaces a running helper once it is idle (21a0b0370, 549d4a1b0).
- Every Claude and Codex launch runs on its session's account: side chats, reviewers on the other provider, and a switch into Claude or Codex (33992a1a9). Switching between Claude and Codex works again (33992a1a9, 7a39fbfe3), and background tasks no longer move a route (ec0426b3b).
- The helper refuses every upgrade request (d3c0cb460) and no longer runs the Redis-protocol listener (a07863e0f).
- Codex sessions move only between accounts of one kind, in the daemon and on the page (2fa074cb2, b96b3a56c); waiting sessions keep their kind (7a39fbfe3, f1d65f9df). A retried reset spends nothing twice (2fa074cb2).
- A refused model gets the provider's answer, not a retried 503 (30194de30); a Codex sign-in offers only the models OpenAI lists for it (435090450), newest first (bab05076b); calls made as a Codex account carry its account id and originator (ebbaa22a0).
- The account row shows the limit with the least left (661741ecb).
- Remote hosts can log in to Codex again (c5916f15f); the headless host bundle ships the helper (fedd5a28e).
- Any signed-in account can replace the default, and sessions it cannot take wait (d6349d8c1); the session menu asks for a sign-in while the session's account is signed out (6f698c42e); moving a session from the account page moves its route for that account's provider (347dd99d8).
- A desktop run with real accounts found nine more issues. Eight are fixed:
  - A browser sign-in opens the provider's page. The page it returns to waits for the outcome and says it, also after Deny. (0062a0da2, 878c8621a)
  - "Managed sessions need you to sign in again" shows only when all of a provider's accounts are signed out. Only the sessions an account serves now count as using it. (0062a0da2)
  - Request counts are live. A key's label names its account. A Codex kind refusal names the kind. (c3a522f32)
  - The helper identity is kept twice and restored, and a replaced helper stops. Sign-in files are 0600. (bfb667494)
  - A session waiting for a sign-in gets one clear answer instead of ten retried 401s. (682f6a7d9)

  New accounts keep their generated names for now.
- A test of moving existing chat and terminal sessions (matrix in the QA comment) found these, now fixed:
  - Signing in the first account of a provider moved no idle session until its next turn or an app restart. It now moves them within about 30 seconds, and a chat whose turn-end move was skipped is tried again. (c1a05c737)
  - A terminal on screen sometimes restarted in front of the user, and text typed but not sent was lost. A terminal now moves once nobody types in it, as above. (c1a05c737)
  - A moved terminal showed "No signal" until its next message. (c1a05c737)
  - A chat waiting on a question or an approval during an app restart stopped ("The agent controller stopped") and could not be resumed: the replayed request broke its unique key. This also happened on `main`. (e92740161)
  - A side chat of a session that had not moved listed the session under the account. (c1a05c737)
  - The first sign-in said saved sessions "can use it again". It now says the sessions on this computer's own sign-in move to the account. (c1a05c737)

  A moved Codex terminal's footer drops "fast", but its requests keep the priority tier: Codex sends `service_tier` to the helper, and the helper forwards it.
- `main` took 0197 and then 0198 meanwhile, so the account migration is now 0199. `main`'s new harness pages show a managed agent's AO accounts in place of its own login.

## Known limits

- New Account strings are English in the seven other languages (two labels outside the page are translated).
- A terminal moved while it is on screen shows "Terminal ended" for about a second and is blank for about a second more, then shows its conversation again.
- Text typed into a terminal before an app restart and not sent is lost when that terminal is moved: the daemon sees typing only from its own start.
- Claude Code on an AO account shows "API Usage Billing" and turns off claude.ai connectors; both come from Claude Code when it runs on a routed token.
- Helper counting starts when this ships; today's tokens per session are held in the helper's memory and start again when it restarts.
- The low-limit warning and the "sessions moved" notice are desktop notices, not entries in AO's notification list.
- "In reserve" is applied by the app when it offers accounts; the daemon accepts an explicit choice of such an account.
- Once Claude has accounts in AO, a session runs on its AO account, also over a project's own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. That key can be added as an API-key account.
- If both copies of the helper's identity are lost while it runs, the sessions running then need their agent restarted, because their tickets were made with keys no daemon knows anymore.
- A database that ran an earlier build of this branch: press "Make default" once per provider; accounts copied from the computer stay as accounts, so remove them and sign in inside AO; sessions started on such a build need a restart, because session tickets changed.

## Testing

On `c3eb123f2`, which merges `main`:
- Backend: `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean, and `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues. `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=30m ./...` passes in every package but one. `opencodev2` fails only on this Mac: its test picks up a real OpenCode 1.19 from `~/.opencode/bin`, and its code is the same as on `main`. Three packages failed under the full run's load and pass when run alone: `claudecode` (a child that times out at 3 s), `fake` (a timing check) and `service/agent`. `service/agent` failed because of the managed catalogue test that the merge adapted.
- Helper (`GOWORK=off`): `gofmt`, build and vet are clean, it also builds for Windows, and `go test -race -p 1 -count=1 ./...` passes.
- `npm run sqlc` and `npm run api` leave no drift.
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. `npx vitest run` passes 469 of 470 files (7,938 tests). The last file, `useBrowserView.test.tsx`, failed once under the full run's load and passes 3 of 3 when run alone; this branch does not touch it. `packages/product-ui` type-checks and its 161 tests pass.

On the final commit (`2e7a42050`, which merges `main` again): `go build ./...` and `go vet` are clean, `golangci-lint` reports 0 issues, and `go test` passes in `session_manager`, `terminal`, `service/provideraccounts`, `storage/sqlite/store`, `service/chat`, `lifecycle`, `daemon` and `domain`. `npm run sqlc` leaves no drift, `npm run typecheck` passes, and the 24 settings and terminal test files pass (432 tests). The fixes were checked again in the desktop app on old sessions made by `main`: a first sign-in in a fresh lab moved both old sessions about 20 seconds later; a terminal on screen moved; a terminal with unsent text was not moved until the text was sent; moved terminals stayed idle past the 90-second "No signal" mark; and a chat waiting on a question through a restart kept working, as did one that `main` had left stopped.

Before the review, on earlier code: 106 manual checks in the desktop app against two Claude and two Codex accounts; moving old sessions in two runs of 20 and one of 4; 49 account checks against three Claude and three Codex accounts; a real Codex reset spent from the page; and a user test run on 11 and 12 Oct (34 scenarios pass, results in the checklist comment). After review, the desktop app was run again on this branch with two Claude and two Codex accounts. The results and the issues it found are in the desktop-run comment; every fix was checked again in the app.

No release, deployment, or publish was performed.

title: feat(files): add ask in chat for selected lines
body:
Code changes: +577 -2\
Tests: +597 -0\
Others: +8 -0 (i18n strings)

## What

Highlight one or more lines in the Files review list, a file opened in the centre, or a diff opened in the centre, and an **Ask in chat** button appears at the end of the selection (also **Cmd/Ctrl+L**). It puts a `file#L2-L4` chip into the session's chat box; when sent, the chip expands to the selected code with its language tag (```` ```ts ````) or diff markers (```` ```diff ````). The user types their question after it.

The button appears only in Chat sessions (TUI sessions have no chat box).

## Why

Requested on Discord by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari: "ask questions by highlighting a line or several lines, that context is automatically sent to the agent so that we can ask questions about that line in the chat UI". Today the only line action is the gutter **+ → Send feedback**, which covers one line and sends a change request, not a question.

## How

- **Selection tracking** (`diffs/useCodeSelection.ts`): reads the selection inside Pierre's shadow root and maps it to rows. In split diffs, old-side rows keep old line numbers. It keeps the state in a small store that only the button subscribes to, because re-rendering the surface would redraw Pierre's rows and drop the selection.
- **Electron 33:** its Chromium reports a shadow-root selection as collapsed even while it holds text, so the range is built from the selection's anchor/focus points instead of `isCollapsed`/`getRangeAt`. Without this the button never appears in the desktop app.
- **Button** (`diffs/SelectionAskButton.tsx`): sits just past the selected text and follows a drag in progress, ignoring the pointer until release so it doesn't disturb the selection. It uses AO's menu surface tokens (`bg-card`, `border-border`, `shadow-md`).
- **Chip** (`lib/chat-context-bus.ts`, `ChatComposer`, `ComposerEditor`): a small bus hands the reference to the session's Chat composer, keyed by the host-scoped session key so remote AO machines work. `SessionView` brings Chat forward when asked from a file tab.
- **Gutter +:** behaviour unchanged, but it now sits beside the line number instead of 12px over the start of the code. Otherwise a drag starting at column 0 presses the + instead of selecting text. This is the only change to existing UI.

**Intentional omissions (possible follow-ups, happy to add any):**
1. An **Explain** button that sends "explain these lines" straight to the agent.
2. **Modify…** for ranges: the existing feedback box, for several lines.
3. Hiding the gutter + while text is selected, or folding it into a selection toolbar.
4. Persistent review comments that stay on the diff (bigger change).

**Notes: previous related work**
- #3492 added inline file feedback: the gutter + and **Send feedback**, modelled on GitHub PR review comments (one line, a change request sent to the agent as a message; nothing stays on the diff).
- #4252 kept that "GitHub-PR-style review flow" alongside the new file explorer.
- #5175 rebuilt the viewer on Pierre and removed the older floating selection menu (Copy / Explain / Make changes); this PR brings back selection-based asking in the Pierre viewer, scoped to Ask in chat.
- #5921 (multiple AO machines) introduced host-scoped session keys; the chip is routed through them.

## Testing

Ran the Frontend workflow's steps locally (Node 24), after installing `product-ui` and `cloud-client` dependencies as CI does:

- `product-ui`: typecheck, tests (134), pack. `cloud-client`: generate (no schema drift), typecheck, tests (26), pack. Docs build.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite, 6154 tests): all pass except `browser-history-store` "caps entry count…", which times out at 20 s only under the full-suite load. It passes on its own and fails the same way on `main`.
- `npm run test:browser-postcondition-integration`: passes.
- `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 73/73 in two consecutive runs on a clean checkout.
- New e2e `e2e/files-ask-in-chat.spec.ts` (10 scenarios), run in **Chromium** and in **AO's own Electron 33** (`AO_E2E_ELECTRON=1`), ×3 in two rounds, all passing:

  - Cmd/Ctrl+L;
  - removed + added lines;
  - split-diff old side;
  - button following a drag;
  - hiding on Escape, scroll-away, and redraw;
  - plain click shows nothing;
  - gutter + still opens feedback and sits clear of the code;
  - TUI sessions show no button.
- New unit tests: chip format (language tag, diff markers, old side, fence safety, long selections), remote-host routing, selection reading (including Electron 33's collapsed selection), and the button.
- No backend changes, so the Go workflow isn't affected.

title: fix(chat): improve chat ui ux overall
body:
Code changes: +1349 -601  
Tests: +858 -188  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

Makes chat message submission optimistic and stabilizes streaming reconciliation, so a sent message appears once, stays in place, and doesn't flicker between composer, queue and timeline states.

- Inserts user messages immediately and reconciles them in place with server state.
- Keeps queued attachments, send journals and drafts stable across remounts and session transitions.
- Preserves final assistant component identity across live-to-settled transitions and main's 50 ms streaming delay limit.
- Restores attachment-only drafts without exposing the wire payload; scopes optimistic recovery to the correct host.
- Stabilizes Working/Worked rows, timeline ordering, scrolling, composer menus and action controls.
- Workspace-unavailable recovery distinguishes definitive missing-worktree errors from transient probe failures.
- MCP startup failures are informational and shown once per session; the manual MCP Reload action is removed.
- Exposes `clientMessageId` on `ConversationMessageResponse` (`openapi.yaml`, `dto.go`, `conversations.go`, `schema.ts`) so optimistic prompts can be matched to persisted ones.

## Why

Optimistic sends flickered and could duplicate across composer, queue and timeline. This is a standalone rebuild of #6048 on current `main`, using it as the reference. It does not depend on the #6047/#6049 stack: only the `clientMessageId` API exposure is taken from #6047.

## How

- Core logic is in `useConversation.ts`, `ChatWorkspace.tsx` and `ChatComposer.tsx`.
- If renderer draft storage is unavailable, `ChatWorkspace` now mounts an in-memory composer instead of blocking the session behind a retry screen.
- `validation_error` stays in the definitive send-rejection set (now in `lib/chat-send-errors.ts`).
- Intentionally omitted from #6047: session-manager/driver recovery changes, `CHAT_RECOVERY_INCONCLUSIVE`, resume-without-history.
- `schema.ts` was edited by hand to match the generator output; CI's api-drift job regenerates it.

title: fix(chat): attribute CLI steering as automation
body:
Code changes: +247 -74  
Tests: +266 -6  
Others: +48 -8  

## Summary

- Carry the source AO session id through `ao send --steer` requests.
- Resolve source project and display name from durable session metadata.
- Persist sender session, project, and send-time display name on conversation messages and steer activities.
- Render active-turn and idle-target cross-session steers through the same linked Automation presentation.
- Preserve legacy client payload hashes for messages without sender metadata.
- Link the sender label to an encoded `ao://sessions/{project}/{session}` route with raw-id fallback when metadata is unavailable.
- Share the Automation frame, header truncation, body collapse, and safe session-link rendering with worker reports.
- Add sender resolution, durable message metadata, activity metadata, CLI request, payload hash, and renderer regression coverage.

## Diagnosis

`ao send --steer` prepends `[from <AO_SESSION_ID>]` in `backend/internal/cli/send.go`, sends `senderSessionId` through `conversation/steer-or-send`, and the controller persists active-turn steers as `ActivityKindSystem` with `event: "steer"` in `backend/internal/service/chat/steer.go:684`. Idle-target fallback now persists the same sender metadata on `conversation_messages` through migration `0178_conversation_message_sender.sql` and returns it in `ConversationMessageResponse`. The renderer maps those fields in `useConversation.ts` and renders both paths through the shared Automation frame in `ChatTimelineItems.tsx`.

Sender display names are intentionally send-time snapshots. The immutable `ao://sessions/{project}/{session}` link remains stable if the source session is renamed. Plain `ao send --message` attribution is a separate follow-up in [issue #6305](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6305).

## Verification

- `GOCACHE=/tmp/ao-gocache GOMODCACHE=/tmp/ao-gomodcache go test ./internal/service/chat` passes.
- `GOCACHE=/tmp/ao-gocache GOMODCACHE=/tmp/ao-gomodcache go test ./internal/storage/sqlite/store -run TestAppendUserMessageRejectsChangedPayloadForSameClientID` passes.
- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/components/chat/ChatProviderSignal.test.tsx src/renderer/components/chat/ChatMarkdown.test.tsx` passes, 105 tests.
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers` reaches an existing sandbox loopback-listener failure when running network-backed tests.
- `npm run typecheck` reaches unrelated shared `packages/product-ui` errors because React peer dependencies are unavailable there.

## Risks

Legacy messages without sender metadata retain their existing Automation or human presentation. The new structured metadata is optional and does not change provider dispatch, turn attachment, or delivery recovery.

Sender display names are intentionally send-time snapshots. Renaming a source session does not rewrite historical steer rows; the immutable session link remains stable.

## Related

- Relates to [#5388](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/5388), which introduced `--steer` and its attribution requirement.
- Relates to [#3360](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360), which established structural sender session identity.

title: fix(systeminstall): let Cursor's first post-install version probe finish (#5887)
body:
Code changes: +14 -2  
Tests: +57 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Lets the post-install harness verification survive the slow **first launch** of a freshly installed Cursor CLI. When the probe *does* hit its deadline, it now reports a clear timeout instead of the opaque `signal: killed`.

## Why

Fixes the Cursor part of #5887, as the maintainer asked in https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/5887#issuecomment-5999366964.

After installing a harness from **Settings → Agents**, the daemon verifies it by running `<resolved binary> --version` under a hard **5s** deadline (`systeminstall.Verifier`). The host runner SIGKILLs the process group when that deadline fires, so the row failed with `run cursor version probe: signal: killed`.

The probe was slow because of the **first launch of a freshly downloaded binary**, not because of Cursor startup itself. Cursor's installer drops a 148 MB bundled `node` runtime plus an 8.8 MB `index.js`. On its first execution macOS assesses the new binary before letting it run. Measured on the reporter's Intel Mac (i7-9750H, x86_64) against brand-new installs from `https://cursor.com/install` into a scratch `HOME`:

| Run | Wall time | CPU (user+sys) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1st `cursor-agent --version` after install | **12.27s** | ~1.1s |
| 2nd | 0.85s | ~0.9s |
| 3rd | 0.91s | ~1.0s |

Wall time is far above CPU time, so the process sat **blocked**, not computing. Replaying AO's sequence on another fresh install shows the same pattern: the post-install probe is killed at 5.00s, and an immediate **Verify again** succeeds in ~1s, because macOS finishes and caches its assessment even after the probe is killed. Harnesses installed together queue behind each other's assessment, which plausibly explains why retries kept failing for a while during the multi-harness session in the report. That last part is not verified.

## How

`backend/internal/service/systeminstall/verifier.go`:

- **`defaultVerifyTimeout` 5s → 60s.** About 5× the measured worst case, which leaves headroom for several harnesses installed in one session. It still bounds a genuinely hung binary, and it is small next to the 15-minute install bound. Healthy probes still return in ~1s, so nothing waits longer in the normal case. The verifier only runs on the daemon's background install worker (`runAgentVerification`), never inside an HTTP request. The UI already polls the job every second and shows *Verifying…* with no client-side deadline, so no frontend change is needed.
- **Actionable timeout error.** When the verifier's *own* deadline fires (and the parent context is still live), the error now reads `run cursor version probe: timed out after 1m0s (a newly installed CLI can be slow on its first launch; choose Verify again)` and wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`. Before, it only said `signal: killed`. Every other probe failure (non-zero exit, missing binary, daemon shutdown) is reported exactly as before.

Intentionally **out of scope**, per the maintainer's "focus on Cursor for now":

- **Crush / Kimi:** they fail with the same `signal: killed` string and go through the same verifier, so they may benefit too. I haven't reproduced or verified them, so this PR claims nothing for them.
- **Qwen:** the installer download failure is a separate network/download path, untouched here.

## Testing

**Regression tests** (`verifier_test.go`):

- `TestVerifierDefaultTimeoutAllowsSlowFirstLaunch`: uses `testing/synctest` virtual time to simulate the measured 12s first launch against the **default** verifier built by `NewVerifier`. It fails on `main` with exactly the reported `run cursor version probe: signal: killed` and passes with this change.
- `TestVerifierBoundsVersionProbe`: now models the real host runner, which returns the kill status rather than `ctx.Err()`. The old fake returned `ctx.Err()`, which hid the opaque error from the test. It asserts the timeout is named, suggests Verify again, still wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`, and no longer surfaces `signal: killed`. It fails on `main`.
- `TestVerifierKeepsNonTimeoutProbeFailure`: a normal probe failure is reported unchanged.

**Live before/after with the real mechanism.** A throwaway, uncommitted test drove AO's real `systeminstall.Verifier` + `systemexec` host runner + Cursor adapter against brand-new Cursor installs. A fresh install was made for each run, so neither binary had been launched before:

| Verifier | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (5s) | `run cursor version probe: signal: killed` after 5.00s |
| this PR (60s) | success after 9.93s, output `2026.10.01-e373342` |

**CI commands from `.github/workflows/go.yml` and `cli-e2e.yml`, run locally on macOS (Intel, x86_64) / Go 1.27.1:**

- ✅ `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
- ✅ `golangci-lint` v2.13.2, full tree, 0 issues (pinned CI version, checksum-verified release binary)
- ✅ `chat-race` (`./internal/service/chat`)
- ✅ `sqlite-race`, all 4 shards (`./internal/storage/sqlite`)
- ✅ `session-store-race`: `./internal/storage/sqlite/store`
- ✅ `cli-e2e` native: `go test -tags e2e -v ./internal/cli/...`
- ✅ `backend-core`, including `./internal/service/systeminstall`. When the whole suite runs at once on this 6-core Intel Mac, 14 adapter/e2e packages (plus `session_manager`) fail **locally**. To show this isn't the change, I re-ran exactly those packages on unmodified `main` (`b37f90b11`) and on this branch:
  - **None depends on `systeminstall`**, even via tests (`go list -test -deps`).
  - The failures are environmental:
    - 3s version-probe deadlines on fake CLIs under full `-race` load
    - `codexappserver` conformance against the locally installed `codex`
    - `session_manager` expecting tmux, which isn't installed on this Mac
  - **In a side-by-side run, 13 of the 15 got the same result on unmodified `main` and on this branch** (10 failed on both, 3 passed on both). The other two, `e2e` and `primeagent`, flipped between runs. Re-run on an idle machine, both pass on `main` and on this branch.
- Not run locally: `windows-workspace` (no Windows runner) and the `cli-e2e` `container` job. GitHub CI is authoritative for these and for the Linux-only results.

The back/forward buttons show only when the brand does not: with the sidebar collapsed, or while it is still sliding open. This drops the hover tracking, the keyboard-focus reveal, and the cursor feed this PR originally added.
- **Fixes a dead zone in the window-drag strip.** The strip above the sidebar took its width from `--ao-sidebar-w`, which only reaches the strip if it already exists when the sidebar first applies its saved width. A sidebar wider than the 240px fallback left an undraggable gap to the right of the title. `_shell.tsx` now measures the real sidebar width with a `ResizeObserver` and sizes the strip to it, including while the sidebar is resized.
- **Keeps the brand inside the sidebar.** The brand lives in the fixed titlebar row, not the sidebar, so a small window that caps the sidebar below the label's width pushed it over the first tab. It now truncates with an ellipsis at the sidebar's right edge.
- **Sidebar minimum width always fits the whole brand.** The floor is measured from the label's natural width (plus 1px of slack for rounding), so a clipped brand cannot lower it. At the floor the brand is fully visible.
- **Tighter spacing.** The brand's left margin and padding are removed, so it sits closer to the sidebar toggle, and the mascot is nudged 1px up.

## Verification

- `tsc` and the e2e typecheck are clean. The full renderer suite passes (4706 tests).
- `resize-clamp.spec.ts` and `titlebar-alignment.spec.ts` pass (8 of 8). I rewrote the sidebar assertion in `resize-clamp.spec.ts`: it now waits for the brand, drags to the edge twice, and asserts the clamp is stable and never collapses, because the old exact-width check was timing-sensitive headlessly.
- Measured headlessly at 1280px: at the minimum width the sidebar is 250px and the label is not clipped.
- Checked by hand in the Electron app: dragging the window from the empty space right of the title works.

## Limits

- The small-window truncation is verified headlessly only; I did not reproduce the exact small window from the report.

title: fix(modelcatalog): discover Devin models over ACP instead of a dead `devin models` command
body:
Code changes: +10 -4
Tests: +57 -19
Others: +0 -0

## What

Devin's model picker no longer errors. The invented `devin models list --format json`
speculation is gone; Devin's catalog now comes from the config options its own ACP
server advertises on `session/new` (`devin acp`), with direct text entry kept for
typed IDs.

## Why

`GET /api/v1/agents/devin/models` failed on every machine with a real `devin` binary:
`devin model discovery: exit status 2: error: unexpected argument 'models' found`.
Devin has no `models` subcommand, so the task composer showed a red discovery warning
forever. Fixes the devin-only model discovery error in the Create-task dialog.

## How

- `commandSpecs["devin"]` removed — the command never existed in devin 3000.1.27
  (`auth mcp rules skills plugins cloud list update version sandbox setup uninstall acp help`).
- `daemon.go` registers `"devin"` in `Discoverer.ACPOptions`, launching
  `chatdriveracp.DiscoverConfigOptions` with `devin acp` — the same read-only
  initialize + `session/new` handshake already used for Cline and DeepSeek Harness.
- `devin` added to `customModelEntryMode` → `direct` and to `hasDiscoverySource`, so
  the catalog reports `selectionMode: catalog` while loading and still accepts a typed
  model ID.
- **Intentional omission:** the full 267-model list in devin's local
  `model_configs_v*.bin` cache is not surfaced. 264 of them carry Devin's own
  `Upgrade to Pro to access this model` gate and this account is Devin Free, so
  `devin acp` advertises exactly the one usable choice (`swe-1-6-slow`) and
  `devin --model swe-2-high -p ...` exits 1 with `Error: /upgrade to access this model`.
  Showing gated models would need a new gate field on `AgentModelInfo`, OpenAPI regen,
  frontend support, and a parser for an undocumented, versioned protobuf cache.
- **Failure path:** Devin has no config-file fallback, so an `devin acp` failure is
  reported (warning + retry ladder) instead of caching an empty catalog as success —
  matching DeepSeek Harness, covered by extending `TestACPOnlyHarnessReportsDiscoveryFailure`.
- No `openapi.yaml` / `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` changes: no DTO shape changed.

## Testing

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/ ./internal/daemon/` clean.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/ -run 'TestDevinDiscoveryUsesACPModelOptions|TestCustomModelEntryPolicy|TestACPOnlyHarnessReportsDiscoveryFailure'` — pass,
  including the new `TestDevinDiscoveryUsesACPModelOptions` (ACP → models, `source: "acp"`,
  `customModelEntry: direct`) and the extended failure test for `devin`.
- `go test ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/service/agent/ ./internal/httpd/...` — only
  pre-existing Windows baseline failures (codex ACL, `TestListDirs…`,
  `TestBridgeStatusConcurrentSecurePairing`, `TestProjectsAPI_Clone`,
  autohand/continue config discovery), reproduced unchanged at clean `HEAD`.
- Live daemon on an isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` (`AO_PORT=3232`):
  `POST /api/v1/agents/devin/models/refresh` → 200 in 8s (was a permanent error);
  `GET /api/v1/agents/devin/models` → `{"source":"acp","selectionMode":"catalog","customModelEntry":"direct","allowCustom":true,"models":[{"id":"swe-1-6-slow","label":"SWE-1.6 Slow","isDefault":true}]}` with no `warning`.
- `devin auth status` (Tier: Devin Free) and `devin --model <gated> -p …` confirm the
  single-model result is devin's entitlement, not a truncated discovery.

title: feat(chat): one Working row per turn, a smooth handoff to Worked, and an empty-chat welcome
body:
Code changes: +499 -224  
Tests: +134 -23  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

- While a response streams, a turn showed "Working for" twice. It now shows once, with a small spinner and a shimmer on the label.
- When the turn ends, the spinner shrinks and fades while the label slides onto the spot where "Worked for" sits. Nothing shifts and the label no longer blinks.
- The "Worked for" accordion has a chevron that points right and turns down when open. The expanded content lines up with the label, its padding animates with the content, and the status labels can't be selected.
- Live and settled rows both show whole seconds.
- The composer has no border, and neither does the inline message editor.
- A new chat shows "What do you want to work on?" above the composer, with a random starter prompt as the placeholder. The text is `chat.welcome.heading` in all 8 locales.
- The composer's model, effort and mode dropdowns no longer scale on press. Scaling them moved the open menu, because the menu is positioned from the trigger's box. They keep their hover and open states.

This is UI only. The optimistic-send and recovery work is in separate PRs.

## Why

The duplicate row came from the turn group and the final message each drawing their own. Their timers started at different moments, so they disagreed. The old Working to Worked switch animated width, which janked, and the label blinked when the shimmer class was dropped. The expanded Worked content sat 4px left of its label, and its padding sat outside the animated element, so it popped in and out instead of growing with the content.

## How

- The live row stays mounted for 440 ms after the turn ends, then the Worked row takes over. `group.live` and `group.outcome` both come from the same turn state, so the handoff happens in one render.
- The close animates only `opacity` and `transform`, so it keeps running while the main thread finishes the turn. It uses keyframes, not transitions, so it still plays if the row mounts already settled. With reduced motion it jumps to the end state.
- The shimmer strength is a registered `@property`. The highlight fades out while the text keeps the same paint, which is what stops the blink.
- The accordion padding moved to an inner div, since the animated element's height can't shrink below its own padding.

## Testing

`tsc` is clean. I updated the tests for the live row, rollback, Worked triggers and the welcome heading, but haven't run the suite locally. CI will.

title: fix(review): keep AO review findings in AO instead of PR threads
body:
Code changes: +1573 -87  
Tests: +1059 -30  
Others: +943 -42 (generated sqlc/OpenAPI/TS schema, i18n, skill and docs)

Part of #6300 (also tracks #5574, closed as its duplicate).

## Why

AO's native reviewer posted each finding as an inline GitHub comment from the same account the worker uses. The review-comment watcher nudges once per unresolved comment id. So when the worker replied on a reviewer thread without resolving it, AO re-delivered the worker's own reply to it as "Address each comment and push fixes". In an isolated lab, `playground-4` had four such turns queued, each quoting the worker's own reply. Filtering by author cannot fix this, because the reviewer and the worker are one GitHub account.

## What (agreed with the user before implementation)

- **Findings live in AO.** The reviewer submits `findings: [{path, line, body}]` with `ao review submit`. Rules:
  - `changes_requested` needs at least one finding; an approval has none.
  - The findings are stored with the verdict in one transaction (migration `0189`), so a retried submit records nothing twice, and a conflicting re-submit is rejected.
  - The reviewer prompt no longer calls `gh`, and tells the reviewer never to post, reply, or resolve anything on the PR itself.
- **GitHub sees one summary.** The daemon posts a single `COMMENT` review: verdict, reviewer, short head SHA, summary, and a numbered findings list. It has no inline comments, so no threads. A failed post is recorded on the run (`providerPostError`) and shown in the inspector. It is not retried.
- **Exactly-once delivery to the worker.** This is gated by the session's review auto-inject, snapshotted on the run.
  - Each completed pass is delivered once: at submit, on the PR's next observation, or by a one-minute sweep when the worker was waiting for input.
  - A pass that can never be delivered is retired with a reason (`review_run.delivery_skipped_reason`) and leaves the delivery queue: stale head, replaced by a newer pass from the same reviewer, PR closed, untracked or owned by another session, or worker terminated. A worker that only can't take a message right now is retried.
  - Delivery goes through the existing `sendOnce` guard with a dedup key persisted per PR (`ao-review:<pr>:<run>`) before `delivered_at` is stamped. A restart between the send and the stamp does not resend. A crash between the send and the dedup write itself can still cause one duplicate, the same bound as every other AO nudge.
- **Resolution in AO.** `ao review resolve <finding-id>... --note "..."` and `POST /sessions/{id}/reviews/findings/resolve`.
  - Allowed actors: the worker, an orchestrator of the same project (`--session <worker>`), or a person in the inspector (no acting session).
  - Who resolved is recorded from AO session identity only, never a GitHub login. The actor id is cooperative identity on the unauthenticated loopback API, the same model as `ao send`; it is not a security boundary.
  - Reviewer panes cannot resolve. Resolving is idempotent; superseded findings return 409.
- **History.** A completed pass supersedes the open findings of earlier passes on the same PR. Exception: a different reviewer's pass on the same head keeps its own findings. A pass that finishes after a newer one already completed files its findings as superseded on arrival. Resolutions are never rewritten.
- **Read surfaces.**
  - `ao review ls` lists open findings with their ids.
  - The inspector shows findings under each AO run, reusing the existing comment rows. Open findings have Resolve and Send to worker; resolved and superseded ones collapse, with "Resolved by the worker: <note>", "Resolved manually", or "Superseded by a newer review". The run shows a "Summary not posted to GitHub" notice when the post failed.
  - Finding changes emit the existing `review_run_updated` CDC event, so the UI refreshes live without rebuilding `change_log`.
- **#5574 for human and bot threads.** The SCM observer marks `pr_comment.own_reply` on a later comment in a thread whose author is AO's authenticated provider login, and lifecycle never nudges it.
  - A thread's first comment is still delivered, whoever wrote it.
  - With no known identity (bot/app token, lookup failure), behavior is unchanged.
  - The review hash includes that login. Threads stored before this change, or before AO learned its identity, are rewritten once with their marks.
- Worker and orchestrator prompts, the `using-ao` review skill, and the review-loop guide are updated. The worker prompt also says not to poll `ao review ls` in a background loop, since AO delivers the result. A background poll set off the stuck-turn race in #6299.

### Two decisions still pending with the user

My confirmation prompt for these was interrupted, so they shipped with the recommended defaults and are easy to change before merge:

1. The own-reply filter skips only **replies** (not thread starters) from AO's own login. The alternative is to skip every comment from that login.
2. **Approvals are delivered** to the worker as well, with the "not a GitHub approval" wording. The alternative is to deliver changes-requested passes only.

## Verification

**Remote CI:** all 24 checks pass.

**Local CI (macOS, Go 1.27.1)**
- `gofmt`, `go build`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint v2.13.2`: 0 issues. `sqlc` and OpenAPI/TS regeneration leave no diff.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` is green except:
  - `codexappserver/TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider`: fails on `main` too, because of the locally installed Codex version.
  - Three tests in `goose`, `chatdriver/acp`, and `httpd` failed under full-suite load and pass when rerun alone.
- Frontend on Node **24.21.0** (CI's major), with a clean `npm ci` in a fresh worktree of the PR head: `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`, `vitest run` (391 files, 6281 tests), the docs build, and `product-ui:check` all pass. One small difference from CI remains: npm itself was the local npm 10 binary running under Node 24, not the npm bundled with Node 24.
- Not run locally: Windows jobs and the renderer e2e smoke. Both pass remotely.

**Lab 1: seeded PR, real CLI, real worker**
- Setup:
  - Isolated `AO_DATA_DIR=~/.ao/dev/ao112/data`, own Electron profile and run file, port 3112.
  - The PR `ao-lab-6300/fake-playground#5` is **fictitious**. Its PR row and running review runs were seeded in SQL.
  - **No native reviewer ran here.** I submitted each result with `ao review submit` in the reviewer's place.
- What this proves:
  - Findings are stored on submit.
  - The summary post failure is recorded and shown on the run.
  - A real `claude-code` worker got exactly one `[AO review]` message per pass and resolved the findings itself with `ao review resolve`.
  - The Electron inspector (driven over CDP) shows "Resolved by the worker: <note>", "Resolved manually" after a Resolve click, "Superseded by a newer review", and the approval.
  - With auto-inject off, nothing is delivered.
  - `ao review resolve` on a superseded finding returns `REVIEW_FINDING_SUPERSEDED`.

**Lab 2: the real PR, no publication possible**

The target was the private test PR from the #6300 report, in a separate isolated project. Its name is left out here because this repository is public.
- **Phase A, read-only, normal credentials.** I claimed the PR into the lab. The SCM observer read its live threads and marked the worker's four replies `own_reply=1`. The two thread roots stayed unmarked. Auto-inject was off and no review was triggered.
- **Phase B, publishing impossible.** The lab daemon ran with `AO_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GH_TOKEN` set to an invalid value, and the worker's agent was relaunched with them.
  - `ao review trigger` launched a **real native `claude-code` reviewer** on the PR's real head commit, checked out in the lab worker.
  - The reviewer followed the new prompt: it submitted `changes_requested` with two line-anchored findings through `ao review submit`, and kept an optional suggestion in the summary.
  - The daemon's summary post failed with "Bad credentials" and was recorded on the run. The pass was delivered to the worker once.
- A read-only check afterwards: the test PR's review and comment counts and newest timestamps are unchanged from before these labs. **Nothing was published.**

**Not verified, and what would close each gap**
- **A successful summary post** (the `COMMENT` review that GitHub accepts, and the id recorded on the run). Covered only by the `httptest` adapter test. Closing it takes one external action: rerun phase B with valid credentials, which posts **one** COMMENT review, with no inline comments, on a PR the user names (for example the private test PR). GitHub does not allow deleting a submitted review. This needs the user's explicit authorization.
- **Lifecycle skipping a live own reply.** The marking is verified on live data. Suppression of the nudge is covered by lifecycle unit tests, including a mutation check. A live check would need a new, auto-inject-enabled comment and a worker reply on GitHub, which is also publication. I don't consider it necessary.

### Fixed after AO's own review of this PR

- The delivery dedup key originally lacked the PR URL, so it was never persisted. The restart test now fails without the fix (mutation-checked).
- Worker replies stored before upgrade were never re-marked, because the unchanged review hash skipped the write.

## Known limits and follow-ups

- Per-adapter reviewer permission allowlists (Claude Code hook, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Copilot, and others) still allow `gh api … /reviews` POSTs. The prompt no longer asks for them, but a reviewer could still post. Tightening every adapter is separate hardening work, not filed yet.
- Reviewer panes started before this change still follow the old prompt and post inline threads. Their `changes_requested` submit with a `githubReviewId` is still accepted.
- GitLab summary posting is unsupported. The run records the reason.

title: feat(chat): glide to new messages and follow streamed replies smoothly
body:
Code changes: +293 -9  
Tests: +95 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

- Sending a message glides to your prompt instead of jumping, even if you had scrolled up. The glide is the browser's native smooth scroll, so it stays smooth while the app is busy committing the send.
- While a reply streams, your prompt stays at the top and the view holds still until the reply fills the space below it. After that the view follows the end with a smooth catch-up instead of jumping per chunk.
- Only you can stop the follow. Scrolling up by any amount, dragging the scrollbar, selecting text upward, or opening a tool call or section releases it. A wheel that a code block consumes, a click on an empty margin, and opening a menu do not. Scrolling back down near the end picks the follow back up.
- The jump-to-latest button glides too. Opening a chat lands at the end instantly, and reduced motion snaps.

## Why

New messages jumped into view, and streaming either sat still while the answer ran off-screen or snapped along with it. Scrolling up mid-stream could get pulled back down.

## How

- `hooks/useScrollFollow.ts` holds the motion. Both `glideToEnd` and `followEnd` use `scrollTo({ behavior: "smooth" })`, which Chromium animates on the compositor. An earlier version used a script-driven tween, and a trace showed it stalling while React committed the send. When the end moves mid-scroll, the scroll in flight is re-aimed instead of restarted.
- Scroll events are classified by where they land, not when. An event at the position we last wrote, or anywhere along a smooth scroll we started, is ours, including the virtualizer's anchoring writes. Anything else is the reader. Reader input stops a smooth scroll in place. Wheel, scroll-up keys and touch pause the follow for 250ms and let the resulting scroll decide.
- The timeline keeps its prompt spacer. A ResizeObserver resizes the spacer as the reply grows and then follows, so the view only moves once the spacer is used up. The observer reads its handler through a ref, so it isn't rebuilt on every streamed chunk.
- A send is detected when a new local echo appears. For long chats the virtualizer's own `followOnAppend` is off, because it snapped past the prompt spacer. Opening a chat snaps for its first second while long histories measure their rows.
- The approach follows whirl's message scroller: prompt anchored at the top, intent-only release, re-latch near the end.

## Testing

`tsc` is clean, and the chat, hooks, UI and settings suites pass locally (1,593 tests). New tests cover position-based ownership, holding for reader intent, sending after scrolling up, a small nudge up releasing and re-latching, and a wheel consumed by a nested scroller. Tests snap instead of animating (`import.meta.env.MODE === "test"`), so the animation itself is checked by hand in the app.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No additional operational monitoring required. This is renderer-only scroll behavior with no data, API or persistence changes. Validate by hand: send after scrolling up, stream a long reply, nudge up slightly mid-stream, scroll inside a code block mid-stream, open a tool call mid-stream, open a long chat.

title: feat(mobile): order workers by last event instead of kanban lane
body:
## Summary

The mobile Workers board sorted sessions like desktop's kanban, in delivery lanes (In review, Ready, Building, Validating). A phone is opened to answer "what happened since I last looked", so this reorders the board around that:

| Section | Contents | Order |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned | pinned sessions | most recently pinned first (unchanged) |
| Needs you | agents blocked on a person (unchanged rule) | longest waiting first |
| **Recent** (new) | everything else, all lanes together | **newest event first** |
| Archive | terminated runtimes, collapsed | pinned, then newest |

Each row's own status still says which lane it is in. Idle rows show the time of their last event, so the row says why it sits where it does.

### Order held still while the board is on screen

- Re-sorting on every poll would move rows out from under a thumb. The board takes a snapshot of the order when it is opened, refreshed, re-focused or returned to from the background, or when the project or search changes. Rows update in place.
- News waits behind an **"↑ N updated"** pill; tapping it re-sorts and scrolls to the top.
- Three changes still apply at once: moving into or out of Needs you, pinning or unpinning (the user's own action), and termination into the Archive.

### Daemon: `SessionView.lastEventAt`

The order needs "when did something a person would notice last happen". `lastActivityAt` only covers agent state changes, and PR `updated_at` moves on every poll. `lastEventAt` is the latest of:

- an activity-state change (`activity.lastActivityAt`, which is written only on state transitions)
- a PR lifecycle change (`pr.state_changed_at`)
- a CI result change (`pr.ci_observed_at`, which moves only when the CI semantic hash changes)
- a review submission (`pr_reviews.submitted_at`, provider time)

with `createdAt` as the floor. It is derived at read time (`domain.Session.LastEventAt`) and never stored. Comment `created_at` is deliberately excluded: the observer rewrites it with the poll time. Older daemons don't send the field, and mobile falls back to `lastActivityAt`.

## Changes

- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/pr.sql`: both PR-facts list queries project `state_changed_at`, `ci_observed_at`, and the newest review's `submitted_at`. The latter uses a LEFT JOIN so sqlc types it nullable and a PR never fans out into one row per review.
- `backend/internal/domain`, `httpd/controllers`: `PRFacts` change timestamps, `Session.LastEventAt()`, `SessionView.lastEventAt`. The OpenAPI spec and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated.
- `packages/mobile/lib/agentsView.ts`: `groupSessions` returns Pinned / Needs you / Recent / Archive; adds `eventAtOf` plus the snapshot helpers (`snapshotOrder`, `holdOrder`, `updatedSince`). Removes the now-unused `BOARD_ZONES` and `zoneMeta`; `boardZoneOf` and `kanbanColumnOf` are unchanged.
- `packages/mobile/lib/worker-board-list.tsx`: the held order and the updates pill. A project's page uses the same list, so it gets the same order.
- `packages/mobile/lib/api.ts`: maps `lastEventAt`.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npm run typecheck` clean; `vitest run` passes (161 files, 1511 tests), including new tests for event ordering, instant comparison of RFC 3339 times with fractional seconds, and the held order and updated count.
- `backend`: `go build ./...`; `go test ./internal/domain/ ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/ ./internal/httpd/...` passes, with new tests for `LastEventAt` and for the PR-facts timestamps (single and batch queries, one row per PR).
- Before rebasing onto current `main`: full `go test ./...`, `go vet`, golangci-lint (changed packages) and frontend typecheck were green, except `TestSpawn_RejectsMissingBinaryAfterEnvPrefix`, which also fails on clean `main` locally (tmux detection).
- Not yet run on the rebased branch: the full backend suite, golangci-lint, and frontend typecheck. CI covers them.
- Manually checked in the iOS simulator against a paired desktop: sections and ordering render on the current Workers UI.

## Known limitations

- A row that moves into Needs you while the order is held lands by its previous rank rather than in Needs you's oldest-first position. It settles on the next re-sort.
- Needs you includes `exited` agents (existing rule), so on a machine with many exited agents, Recent can sit below the fold.

title: fix(mobile): keep the terminal for merged sessions with a live runtime
body:
## Summary

On mobile, opening the TUI for a session whose PR had merged showed **"Session terminated"** with a Restore button over a terminal that was still running. The daemon reported `isTerminated: false` and a live terminal handle.

`TerminalSessionScreen` decided "dead" with `isTerminalStatus(status)`. That list mixes runtime states (`terminated`, `killed`, `cleanup`) with outcomes (`merged`, `done`, `errored`). Of those, only `terminated` and `merged` exist in the daemon's current status set, so in practice merged sessions were the ones hit.

This change decides "dead" from the runtime instead, via a new pure helper `isRuntimeGone` in `lib/session/sessionRoute.ts`:
- workers: `isTerminated === true` or status `terminated` (same rule as the board's archive)
- orchestrators: `isTerminal === true` or `hasRuntime === false` (same rule as `orchestratorState`)

The "terminal reports itself gone" path (`notFound`) is unchanged. Mobile only; desktop and the daemon are untouched.

## Tests

- New `isRuntimeGone` cases in `sessionRoute.test.ts`: merged/errored with a live runtime keep the terminal, terminated workers and stopped orchestrators are gone
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (mobile): pass
- `npx vitest run` (mobile): 161 files, 1508 tests pass

## Risks

Not exercised on a device. A session whose runtime is gone but still reports `isTerminated: false` now attaches, and falls back to the existing "Session not found" → dead-overlay path.

title: perf(sidebar): unify rows, fix Scratchpad layout, and cut the sidebar's render and style cost
body:
## What changed

A cleanup and performance pass over the whole sidebar, in two parts.

**Look and structure**
- **Search and Automations are one shared row** (`SidebarTopNavRow`), so they hover identically. Search is now a quiet row with a plain `⌘K` hint instead of a filled pill with a boxed key-cap.
- **Row action buttons share one layout** across project rows, session rows and the section headers: 24px targets, a 2px gap, aligned right edges, and their own instant hover fill.
- **Projects and Scratchpad share the sidebar height** with a flex layout. Before, a layout effect ran before its parent's ref attached, so Scratchpad could be pushed out of view and clipped.
- **Even gutters:** rows were 8px from the left edge and 9px from the right (the container keeps a 1px right border). They are now 9px on both sides.

**Performance** (measured on a Chromium trace of closing and opening the sidebar, dev build)
- **Per-frame full-page restyle removed.** `useSidebarChromeGeometry` wrote two CSS variables on `<html>` and read two bounding rects on every animation frame, invalidating style for the whole page. It now keeps the value in a small store, reads sizes from `ResizeObserver` entries, and sets the variables only on the session header that uses them. Style recalculation per close and open fell from 0.89s to 0.08s.
- **Session rows are minimal.** No Motion `layout`, springs or per-row presence animation. dnd-kit's drag transform is unchanged.
- **Toggling one project or section re-renders only that subtree.** Open/closed state lives in a small per-flag store (`sidebarDisclosure.tsx`) instead of in `Sidebar`. In a trace of 12 project toggles, `Sidebar` rendered 13 to 14 times before and once now.
- **Open/close animations kept** for projects, the Pinned/Projects/Scratchpad sections and Show more, using a CSS height and opacity transition (`interpolate-size`, Chromium 129+; Electron 33 is Chromium 130) with no per-row measuring. Bodies mount on first open and then stay mounted (inert, `aria-hidden`, `content-visibility: hidden`), so re-opening never re-mounts rows. Reduced motion is instant.
- **Row-action tooltips are lazy** (`LazyTooltip`): a Radix Tooltip mounts only after the first hover or focus.
- **A single session update re-renders only that row.** Stable props, memoized rows, and handlers read through refs.
- `ResizeHandle` batches its resize syncs in one animation frame.
- **A bug fix found along the way:** toggling the sidebar force-opened the Projects section and lifted every Show more cap. The icon-rail list logic treated "slid away" as "rail mode". It is now tied to the real icon rail only.

## Measurements

Headless Chromium, 4x CPU throttle, median of 10, task time in ms:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Project expand and collapse | 533 | 152 |
| Projects section open and close | 655 | 141 |
| Whole sidebar close and open | 1631 | 689 |
| Background session update | 195 | 83 |

## Verification

- `tsc` and the e2e typecheck are clean. The full renderer suite passes (4752 tests), including new regression tests for the toggle-one-project render scope, sections staying mounted after close, the lazy tooltip, reduced motion, and the sidebar-toggle bug (verified to fail against the old behavior).
- `titlebar-alignment.spec.ts` and `resize-clamp.spec.ts` pass. Six other e2e failures (`shell-terminal-tabs` x2, `titlebar-brand` x3, `updates-settings` x1) fail the same way on the pre-change tree.
- Light and dark screenshots of rest, hover, project open, Show more and the collapsed state were byte-identical to before the performance pass. Checked by hand in the Electron app on a snapshot with 139 sessions: animations, hover and toggling work.
- `DESIGN.md` gains a rule against Motion `layout` and `AnimatePresence` in sidebar lists.

## Limits

- Numbers are from a dev build in headless Chromium, not production Electron.
- Show less now jumps siblings instead of gliding. A session that changes status and re-sorts snaps into place.
- Closed lists stay mounted and still receive background updates (about 3 to 4ms extra in the tick test).
- ESLint is not configured in `frontend/`, so lint was not run.

title: perf(chat): stop re-rendering every turn on each streaming update
body:
Code changes: +37 -3  
Tests: +38 -0  
Others: +0 -0  

## What

While a reply streams, only the turn that is changing re-renders. Before, every turn in the conversation re-rendered on each streamed update, along with its timeline items and tooltips.

## Why

A performance trace of a streaming reply showed 88 `TurnGroup` renders, 170 timeline item renders and 700+ tooltip renders across 11 updates in an 8-turn chat. `TurnGroup` is already `memo`, but three of its props got a new identity on every update even when nothing had changed: the `editableTurns` Set and the `onStartMessageEdit` / `onSubmitMessageEdit` handlers. Each new identity defeated the memo for every turn.

## How

- `hooks/useStable.ts` adds two small hooks. `useStableSet` returns the same Set object while its members are unchanged. `useLatestCallback` gives a function a permanent identity that always calls the latest version.
- `ChatWorkspace.tsx` passes `editableTurns` through `useStableSet` and the two edit handlers through `useLatestCallback`.
- No behavior changes. The handlers still run the latest logic, and the Set still updates when its members change.

`localEchoClientMessageIds` had the same problem on the original branch, but that prop arrives with the optimistic-delivery work and isn't on main yet.

## Testing

`tsc` is clean, and the chat and hooks suites pass locally (1,323 tests). The new `useStable.test.tsx` covers Set identity across equal and changed contents, and that the stable callback calls the latest function. Checked by hand in the app: streaming in a chat with earlier turns, inline message edit (start, type, submit), Worked accordion and tool-call disclosures, and rollback.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No additional operational monitoring required. This is renderer-only memoization with no behavior, data or API change.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`
- [x] One focused change
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [x] Tests added

title: perf(sidebar): stop restyling the page every animation frame and stop session rows jumping
body:
## What changed

Two sidebar performance and motion fixes: the sidebar animation no longer restyles the whole page on every frame, and the only thing that animates in the session lists is the vertical position of rows, so nothing stretches or jumps when the sidebar toggles. The rest of the render-path work (re-render scope, tooltips, project and section animations) is a separate follow-up.

**Cause.** `useSidebarChromeGeometry` watches the sidebar's animating width. On every frame it called `getBoundingClientRect()` on two elements (forcing a layout) and wrote two CSS custom properties, `--ao-sidebar-layout-width` and `--ao-sidebar-collapse-progress`, onto `<html>`. Writing a custom property on the document root invalidates style for every element on the page. Only one thing reads them: the left padding of the session header (`.session-topbar-titlebar-clearance-mac`, in `ChatWorkspace.tsx` and `CenterPane.tsx`). So the whole document was restyled each frame to move one header's padding. In a Chrome trace of closing and opening the sidebar, style recalculation took 2.8s over 653 calls, 161 of them over 5ms, each across about 800 elements.

**Fix.**
- The hook keeps the value in a tiny module-level store (`get` / `set` / `subscribe`; `set` skips unchanged values) and never touches `<html>`.
- It reads sizes from `ResizeObserver` entries (`borderBoxSize`, with `contentRect` as a fallback) instead of calling `getBoundingClientRect` each frame. One synchronous read happens at start.
- A new `useSidebarChromeClearanceRef(enabled)` callback ref sets the two variables on the header element itself with `style.setProperty`, with no React state and no re-render per frame. It initializes from the store, so a header that mounts mid-animation is correct, and it clears and unsubscribes on unmount.
- `ChatWorkspace.tsx` and `CenterPane.tsx` pass their existing mac and fullscreen conditions to the ref hook. The CSS and the variables are unchanged, so padding is identical when collapsed, expanded, mid-animation, in native fullscreen, and when not ready. Non-mac behavior is unchanged.

**Only session rows animate, and only vertically.** The section scroller (`SidebarSectionScroller`) was a full Motion `layout` element wrapping every row of a section. When the sidebar toggled and its available height changed, it sprang to the new size and scaled every row inside it (the "stretching"), and the project row's `layout="position"` made it slide with it (the "moving down"). Both are plain elements now, along with the Show more button. Session rows use `layout="y"` (Motion 12 supports `"x"` and `"y"`; the engine snaps the other axis), keyed with `layoutDependency` to the list order, so Motion re-measures only when the order changes: never on a sidebar toggle, never sideways, never in size. The 500ms start-up guard moved into the session list, and the per-row enter/exit animation and `AnimatePresence` are gone.

## Measurements

Chromium via Playwright, dev build, data set of 14 projects and 12 Scratchpad sessions (about 1,070 elements), 5 close-and-open cycles, median of 3 runs:

| Per close and open | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Style recalculation | 0.892s | 0.080s |
| Total main-thread time | 1.16s | 0.38s |

Style recalc per call fell from about 3.3ms to about 0.23ms. Recalc and layout counts rose slightly because frames are now cheap enough to reach the 60Hz cap, so the counts are not a regression.

## Verification

- `tsc` and the e2e typecheck are clean. The full renderer suite passes (4732 tests; one unrelated test failed once in a run and passed in the next two runs).
- Six new tests for the store and hook cover the store, the initial value, entry-size updates without layout reads, cleanup, and the enabled toggle.
- `titlebar-alignment.spec.ts` and `resize-clamp.spec.ts` pass. The two assertions that read the variables from `<html>` now read them from the session header, and a new assertion checks that `<html>` stays free of them.

**Footer no longer collapses to a bare border.** When the sidebar was toggled off, the footer's expanded content (Settings, Connect mobile, account) was set to `display: none` about 60ms into the slide-out, while the sidebar was still on-screen. The footer shrank from 91px to its 17px top border and left it visible during the slide. `hidden` is now reserved for the real icon rail; `aria-hidden` and `tabIndex={-1}` still keep the footer out of reach while collapsed.

## Motion check

Sampled every animation frame in headless Chromium: through a sidebar close and open, every session row and the project row stayed at exactly 0px sideways, 0px vertical, 0px width and 0px height change. After dropping a dragged session row, only that row moved, and only vertically (about 13px of glide), with 0px sideways and 0px size change.

## Limits

- Measured in headless Chromium on a dev build, not in the real Electron app. Numbers should be lower in a production build. Native fullscreen was checked through the fake bridge only.
- ESLint is not configured in `frontend/`, so lint was not run.

After the repo moved from `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator` to `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, GitHub reports `head.repo.full_name = OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`. The project remote still names the old repo. The SCM observer only accepts head repos whose names match configured remotes, so it skipped the session's own PRs (for example, #6307).
