title: fix(browser): ⌘W on the last tab closes it and the browser panel
body:
## Summary
With the browser focused and only one tab open, ⌘W / Ctrl+W did nothing: the host refuses to remove the last tab (`CANNOT_CLOSE_LAST_TAB`) and the chord was already consumed. Now ⌘W on the last tab closes it:

- `browser-view-host.ts`: last-tab ⌘W moves focus to the shell, releases the browser's focus and shortcut target, sends `browser:closePanel`, then opens a new blank tab and closes the old one through the normal close path. The closed page lands in the reopen-closed-tab list, so ⌘⇧T restores it. Reopening the browser shows one fresh empty tab.
- `preload.ts`: exposes `browser.onClosePanel`.
- `SessionView.tsx`: on `closePanel` for its view, docks a popped-out browser and collapses the inspector.
- Bridge/test mocks gain `onClosePanel`.

A following ⌘W goes to the normal terminal-close handler, which always consumes the chord; the window's Close item is ⇧⌘W, so it cannot close the window.

## Demo
Recorded in the desktop app built from this branch, with isolated data and a throwaway session. The blue captions were added for the recording and name each step; ⌘W/⌘⇧T were sent as raw DevTools key events, which go through the same Electron `before-input-event` path as real key presses.

![⌘W on the last browser tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d74000f509d3b53f935e4065649f33d3c1cdd565/cmd-w-last-tab.gif)

[Full-quality MP4 (34 s)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/d74000f509d3b53f935e4065649f33d3c1cdd565/cmd-w-last-tab.mp4)

1. Load example.com in the only tab.
2. ⌘W inside the page: the tab closes and the side panel closes.
3. Reopen the browser: one fresh empty tab.
4. ⌘⇧T restores example.com.
5. ⌘W with two tabs closes only the current tab.
6. ⌘W on the last tab again: the panel closes.
7. ⌘W with the browser hidden: the app window stays open.

## Tests
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `vitest run src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts`: new test (last-tab ⌘W emits `browser:closePanel`, releases the shortcut target, reports the old tab as closed, leaves one tab with a new ID, no terminal close); the open-focus-close sequence test now expects the second ⌘W to swap in a blank tab instead of a no-op.
- `npm test -- src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView src/renderer/components/BrowserPanel src/renderer/components/SessionView`

title: feat(chat): show session start-up as a step checklist
body:
## Problem

Creating a Chat task showed a bordered "Starting Claude…" banner above an empty timeline, while the opening brief sat in the queue dock above the composer as "Queued · sends when the agent finishes". Then the banner vanished and the layout jumped when the agent started. There was one spinner for 5–25s, with no sign of which step was running.

## What changes

- **Real stages on the session.** The background start (`completeAsyncChatSpawn`) records an ordered checklist on the session row: `fetch`, `worktree`, `setup`, `agent`, each with a status and start/end times. Finishing one stage and starting the next is a single write. The data is a new `provision_steps` column (migration 0179); `sessions_cdc_update` fires on it, so the open session refetches.
- **Only stages that run are listed.** A prepared worktree skips `fetch`, and `setup` appears only when the project has `postCreate` commands, so there is never a "0s" row.
- **Checklist under the brief.** The header sits in the "Working for" slot with the same metrics (spinner slot, hairline). Once the agent stage is done and the first turn is live, the header text swaps in place and the list leaves. A clean start leaves nothing behind.
- **The brief reads as sent.** While starting, the opening brief renders in the timeline, not the queue dock. Later messages still queue.
- **Failures stay inline.** A failed start keeps the checklist, marks the stage it stopped in as failed (the daemon leaves it "running"; a failed session means that stage failed), and offers Retry. `ControllerBanner` goes back to controller health only.
- **Composer hint while starting:** "Claude is starting · messages send in order".
- **Translations:** new strings are localized in all 8 catalogs.

`SessionRecord` is no longer comparable with `==` because of the slice field, so 25 test assertions move to `reflect.DeepEqual`.

## Testing

- `go test` for `session_manager`, `storage/...`, `httpd/...`, `lifecycle`, `domain`: pass. New tests cover checklist ordering with one running step per write, the failed stage left running, the prepared worktree skipping fetch, and the store round-trip with CDC firing only on change.
- Renderer: the full `vitest` suite passes. New ChatWorkspace tests cover the starting state, the clean handoff to the working line, and the failed state with Retry.
- Real daemon with a real Claude Chat task: steps progressed fetch 1.0s, worktree 7.7s, setup 2.0s, agent 10.9s, then ready.
- Not run: `codexappserver` conformance fails locally because the installed Codex is newer than the generated protocol, which is unrelated to this change.

Demo recording to follow in a comment.

title: feat(session): daemon branch state and git actions in the inspector summary
body:
Code changes: +1067 -61  
Tests: +514 -56  
Others: +291 -20 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI, TS schema; i18n catalogs)

## Screenshots

Dev build, dark theme, a session with one uncommitted file on top of a pushed commit.

![Summary tab: branch line, uncommitted and commit rows, Commit & create PR, Files badge, Activity rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/728788ed435b082a0d12e6a6d3c90a49675ce74f/summary-overview.png)

| Git actions menu | Loading state | After the commit |
|---|---|---|
| ![Menu with Commit, Commit & push, Create draft PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/728788ed435b082a0d12e6a6d3c90a49675ce74f/git-actions-menu.png) | ![Button shows Committing…](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/728788ed435b082a0d12e6a6d3c90a49675ce74f/committing.png) | ![2 commits, 1 not pushed, Push & create PR, new commit in Activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/728788ed435b082a0d12e6a6d3c90a49675ce74f/committed.png) |

## What changes

The inspector Summary tab used to open with "No pull request opened yet" and PR-only session controls, even when the session had uncommitted work. Nothing outside the Files tab showed that the session had changes.

The Summary now leads with the session branch:

- **Branch block.** The block shows the branch line (`branch → base`), then two rows: uncommitted files, and commits with their push state (`pushed`, `not pushed`, `N not pushed`). Each row shows +/− counts and opens the Files tab. Uncommitted files come from the workspace manifest; the commit count and push state come from the daemon's `session.branchState`.
- **One split button that follows git state.** The button reads **Commit & create PR**, **Push & create PR**, or **Create PR**. When a PR is open it becomes **Commit & push to #N** or **Push to #N**. The ▾ menu holds the single-step actions: Commit, Commit & push, Push, and Create draft PR.
- **No agent wording in the rail.** The button shows "Creating PR…", "Committing…", or "Pushing…". It stays in that state until the expected git facts appear, or until the session has been idle for a while without them. The pending state lives in a small store, so it survives tab switches.
- **PR policies only with a PR.** "Auto-fix CI", "Auto-fix reviews", and "Archive on merge" (renamed from "Terminate on merge", to match the Archive wording elsewhere) now appear once a PR exists. Standalone sessions keep their Archive row.
- **Files tab badge.** The changed-file count is a corner badge on the Files tab, styled like the notification bell's.
- **Activity rows.** Each event is a single line: dot, label, and time on the right, with no connector lines. Activity also lists the branch's 5 newest commits, refetched only when the daemon's commit count changes rather than on every file edit.

## Daemon branch state

The daemon records each session branch's commit and push facts, so every client reads one observed truth instead of computing git state:

- **`sessions.branch_state`** (migration 0191) holds `commits` (on the branch, not in its base), `remoteBranch` (`origin/<branch>`, empty until the first push), and `unpushed`. AO worktrees track `origin/main` until the first push, so the configured upstream is deliberately not used.
- **Refresh rides on the existing SCM observer's 30s tick**, before its credential gate, so it also works without GitHub. Each tick runs one `git for-each-ref` per repository, which returns every session's branch, `origin/<branch>`, and base tips. A session whose tips didn't move costs no further git; one that moved gets 1–2 `rev-list --count`. The branch comes from the worktree's `HEAD` file, so a branch the agent switched to is followed. A failed git read keeps the last known facts.
- **Immediate refresh while the inspector is open:** the workspace watch, which now also watches `origin/<branch>` and `config`, runs the same check for that session after the file-list refresh.
- **Consumers:** a change streams as `session_updated`, ships on `SessionView` as `branchState`, and `ao session get` prints it. The inspector reads it for the commits row and the button.
- **Freshness:** inspector open → right after the commit or push; inspector closed → within 30s; a push from another machine → only after something fetches that branch locally.
- **Cost:** measured on 25 live sessions across 3 repositories, an idle tick runs 3 git processes (~90 ms) and the first tick after daemon start runs 25 (1.4 s). A per-session design would run ~180 per tick (~3.9 s).

## How the actions run

The buttons send instructions to the session's agent through the existing `POST /sessions/{id}/send` automation relay, the same path CI auto-fix uses. The daemon only observes the results; it does not commit, push, or open PRs itself. The chat transcript therefore shows an "Automation" message for each action.

## Intentional omissions

- **Cloud and orchestrator sessions** get no git rows or actions. Cloud sessions have no local workspace facts, and orchestrators don't ship a branch of their own.
- **No failure reason in the rail.** If the agent can't open a PR (for example, no GitHub remote), the button returns after a settle window. The reason is only in the agent's chat reply.
- **No timed start-up steps in Activity.** Steps like fetch, worktree, setup, and agent start, plus push events, need new daemon events and are not in this PR.

## Verification

- Backend: `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 are clean on the touched packages, and `go test` passes for `storage/sqlite/...`, `service/session`, `observe/...`, `workspacewatch`, `daemon`, `cli`, `httpd/...` and `domain`. New tests cover the reconcile against a real git repo with a bare origin (tracking `origin/main` is not a push, then first push, then a new commit, then no rewrite when nothing changed), following the worktree's branch when the agent left the recorded one, git-process counts (first pass 3, idle pass 1, after one commit 2), the SCM tick reconciling branch state without credentials, the store round-trip with its `session_updated` event, and the migration ledger.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, and product-ui `typecheck`, `test`, and `npm pack --dry-run` pass.
- Inspector, inspector-remote, inspector-rail, `useWorkspaceQuery`, and i18n vitest pass (222). New tests cover each git state, the message sent to the agent, the pending state clearing when the PR appears, request failure, and commit rows in Activity.
- Full `npx vitest run`: 389/391 files pass locally. The 2 failing files are main-process only and untouched by this PR:
  - `browser-profile-import`: `better-sqlite3` is built for Electron's ABI (130), but local Node 26 is 147.
  - `browser-history-store`: one slow test hit its timeout.

  CI's pinned runtime needs to confirm both.
- Ran end to end in an isolated dev Electron build against a scratch repo: uncommitted → **Commit** (agent committed) → "1 commit · 1 not pushed" → **Push** → "pushed" → **Create PR**. The repo had no GitHub remote, so the pending state cleared on its own and the button came back.
- Renderer smoke (`test:e2e:renderer`) is flaky on this machine. It failed 3–10 specs per run under heavy load, and running the same specs on the base commit failed the same way (10, then 4). Relying on CI's Playwright container for this job.
- Not run locally: docs build, `browser-runtime:prepare`, and `test:browser-postcondition-integration`. None of them touch the renderer inspector.

title: feat(chat): agents can show HTML pages inline in chat threads
body:
Code changes: +4338 -108  
Tests: +4571 -12  
Others: +1004 -0 (916 generated OpenAPI/schema.ts, 88 locale strings)

## What this adds

A chat agent can now show a self-contained HTML page (a chart, table, diagram or mockup) inline in its thread, above its final reply.

- **`ao render <file> --title …`** publishes the page. The daemon stores an immutable copy and records a `system` activity with `detail = {event:"render", render:{id,title,height,path}}` on the turn in flight. That is the same discriminator pattern `steer` uses, so there is **no migration**.
- **The page renders inline** in a sandboxed iframe (`sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"`) served from `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/renders/{renderId}`. The route always sends `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms`, so the page has an opaque origin, and `corsMiddleware` refuses its `Origin: null` requests to the daemon.
- **Theme and size**:
  - The page is stored raw. When it is served, a bootstrap script is injected after the doctype, so a page published before a daemon upgrade gets the current bootstrap (`ETag` = bootstrap version + page hash, `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`). The bootstrap applies AO's theme tokens as CSS variables (`--background`, `--chart-1…6` and the rest). They follow light/dark live with no reload.
  - The frame fits the page's reported height (80–2000 px).
  - Links open in the system browser.
  - **Expand page** opens the page in a borderless dialog sized to it: up to 64rem wide, and as tall as the page up to the window, past which the page scrolls inside it. The expanded frame sends `displayMode: "fullscreen"` (the MCP Apps host-context field), so the bootstrap centers a width-capped top-level block (`body>*{margin-inline:auto}`) and shows the scrollbar.
- **`ao render --check <file>`**:
  - Loads the page in a hidden, offscreen-rendered, in-memory-partition window inside the desktop app, over the existing browser-runtime broker. The internal action `__render-check` is not reachable from `ao browser`.
  - Returns a PNG, the content height and console messages.
  - Fails with `503 RENDER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` without the desktop app, and `422 RENDER_CHECK_FAILED` with the desktop app's reason.
- **Isolation**:
  - Render files use a `render-` prefix that `attachmentstore.validateName` rejects, so the preview origin, worktree projection and workspace import never touch them.
  - An Electron guard keeps a render frame on its own page.
  - Remote-host chats show a note instead of a frame. The remote proxy URL carries a capability token, so it must not reach page scripts.
  - The packaged renderer CSP allows `frame-src http://127.0.0.1:*`.
- **Agents learn about it**:
  - A two-sentence "Showing pages in chat" prompt section. The `aoSkillPointer` cap rises from 220 to 260 words; it is now 252.
  - `commands/render.md`, which includes when to use `ao render` versus `ao preview`/`ao browser`.
  - CLI help.
  - A TUI session gets `409 SESSION_MODE_MISMATCH`, which points at `ao preview`.

## Follow-ups added after review

- **`html_preview` / `html_render` MCP tools.**
  - `ao mcp` is a hidden, dependency-free stdio MCP server. Every chat session gets it:
    - Codex receives it through `thread/start` / `thread/resume` `config.mcp_servers.ao`, with `default_tools_approval_mode: "approve"`.
    - ACP agents receive it through `session/new` `mcpServers`.
    - It runs outside Codex's shell sandbox, so it reaches the loopback daemon even in the default sandboxed mode.
  - Both tools are annotated read-only (`readOnlyHint: true`), with bounded inputs.
  - The unreal agent is skipped, because it refuses servers supplied by AO.
  - Codex 0.160 hides every MCP tool behind tool search, so the prompt tells agents to search for the tools when they cannot see them.
  - ACP tool rows now cap stored `input` at the same 8 KiB marker Codex uses, and drop image data from `content`/`output`. Without this, a Claude `html_preview` row would store the page and the screenshot twice.
- **Local images.** `ao render` and the tools inline absolute local image paths as `data:` URIs. Matching rules:
  - Matches are quoted strings or CSS `url()`.
  - A magic-byte check means only real image bytes are inlined, so a symlink to a secret is refused.
  - Each image may be at most 10 MiB, and the page at most 25 MiB.
  - Files are opened with `O_NONBLOCK` and must be regular files.
- **Measured first height.**
  - On publish, the desktop app measures the page at 9 reader widths, in one hidden window. It reads each width in an isolated world, after relayout, so a page that declares `innerWidth` cannot skew the read.
  - The heights go into `detail.render.heights`, and the inline frame opens at the measured height for its width.
  - Measuring is capped at 6 s and never fails a publish. It is skipped when no turn is active.
- **Public-only check.**
  - The hidden check/measure window's in-memory partition goes through an in-process SOCKS5 proxy. The proxy blocks local and private address ranges and connects only to the addresses it checked, so DNS rebinding changes nothing, with `<-loopback>` and WebRTC set to `disable_non_proxied_udp`.
  - Only the render page's own `host:port` is allowed per load.
  - The check output reports each refused request: `AO blocked a request to <host>:<port>`.
- **View source / Save / Open in external browser** in the expanded page's header.
  - `GET …/renders/{id}?source=1` serves the raw stored page as `text/plain`, with the same sandbox CSP and a distinct ETag.
  - Save downloads the served page, bootstrap included, so it renders on its own. The file name comes from the title, with characters a file system refuses removed.
  - Open in external browser passes the render URL plus a fullscreen theme fragment to `shell.openExternal`.

## Session artifacts (integration with #4805 / #6355)

Renders and session artifacts stay separate concepts. A render is an answer inside the thread. An artifact is a deliverable the user keeps. They are connected in three ways:

- **Guidance.**
  - `artifactPrompt()` gains one sentence: in a chat session, a chart, table or diagram that answers a question goes in the thread with `html_render`, not into the artifact directory.
  - `render.md` gains an "ao render or a session artifact" section.
  - `report.md` and `render.md` say that a reported HTML artifact also shows in the thread.
  - The `aoSkillPointer` is unchanged; it stays at its 260-word cap.
- **Keep a render as an artifact:**
  - "Save as artifact" in the expanded page's header;
  - `POST /sessions/{id}/renders/{renderId}/artifact`;
  - `ao render --artifact`;
  - `html_render` with `artifact: true`.

  How it saves:
  - The page is written with its bootstrap into the session's artifact directory as `<title>.html` (`O_EXCL`, `0600`). Repeating an identical save returns the same file.
  - Names are capped to fit NAME_MAX, and Windows device stems are prefixed.
  - `ReconcileSessionOutputType` runs at once, so Summary and the kanban update without waiting for the poller.
  - Publish returns an absolute `artifactPath`, or `artifactError`; a failed save never fails the publish.
- **HTML artifacts inline in chat.**
  - When a chat agent runs `ao report --artifact <file.html>` for a file in its own artifact directory, a `system` activity (`detail.event="artifact"`) lands on the running turn.
  - The page shows in the same sandboxed, themed frame renders use. It is served by a new `GET /sessions/{id}/artifact-files/*` route, which applies:
    - `os.OpenRoot` confinement;
    - regular files only, size-capped;
    - the CSP sandbox on every response;
    - `?source=1` for the raw source.
  - Relative links to sibling files keep working.
  - The expanded page's header adds **Open in Browser panel**, the existing artifact preview.
  - A page already shown in the same turn by a render kept as an artifact is not shown twice.
  - Unlike the Browser panel's `ao-preview-artifact.<id>.localhost` origin, which CORS trusts, the inline frame has an opaque origin and cannot call the daemon.
- **Shared fix.** `previewutil.OpenWorkspaceFile` now refuses non-regular files before opening them. A FIFO at a preview path used to hang the preview poller and handlers.

## Code review fixes

A `/code-review` pass found 15 issues; all are fixed:
- **Agent pages in the chat stay off the local network.** A guard on the app's session refuses every loopback, private and link-local address that render and artifact frames request, except the page's own files (see the second pass below). Pages are served with `worker-src 'none'`, because a worker's requests carry no frame.
- **The html tools never give an agent more network than its sandbox has.** The Codex conversation reports whether its sandbox allows network: none for accept-edits and auto, which run `workspace-write`. For an agent without network, the check and the measure run with network `none`, through their own partition and proxy listener, which refuse everything but the page before any DNS lookup. The output says so. `html_render` is no longer marked read-only.
- **Inline HTML artifacts get a real origin.** They are framed from `ao-inline-artifact.<session>.localhost`, under `sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-same-origin`, so their module scripts, `fetch` and fonts work. CORS refuses that origin everywhere but its own host, the daemon API included. The renderer frames it only from a validated inline origin, and drops a remote host's inline URL.
- **Inline artifact frames are capped at 640 px** and scroll inside the frame. A `100vh` page no longer ratchets to 2000 px.
- **Checks capture what they report.** The capture waits for the resized viewport and captures again if the frame is stale. The window uses `useContentSize`. A screenshot over 3.5 MiB is scaled down, and `imageWidth`/`imageHeight` report the result. The content height is read in an isolated world.
- **Publish no longer waits up to 6 s for measuring.** The row is recorded first, and its heights settle onto it later.
- **A page revalidation is answered with 304 before any file read.** The render ETag is the bootstrap version plus the render id; an artifact's ETag is its size and modification time.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - Frames follow a daemon port change.
  - Claude's Anthropic-format screenshots are dropped from tool rows.
  - Terminal sessions no longer get the chat-only tool guidance.
  - `ao render --check --out` can rerun over its previous file.
  - The `ao mcp` env carries `AO_DATA_DIR`.

Live in the dev app:
- An inline artifact had a real origin and a same-origin `fetch` returned 200.
- That frame's request to the daemon API was refused; `127.0.0.1:8765` and `192.168.1.1` were blocked (the test server saw nothing) and logged; a public image loaded; a worker was refused.
- A `100vh` page stopped at 640 px.
- A check in accept-edits mode blocked `www.google.com` and said it ran without network; in full access the same page loaded it.
- The screenshots were 720x58 PNGs, matching the reported size.

## Second review pass

A second `/code-review` pass found 12 issues; all are fixed:
- **Agent pages reach only their own files on this computer.** Allowed: their own inline origin, the render itself, or their session's artifact files.
  - Refused: other `*.localhost` hosts and every other daemon route. Before, an inline artifact could nest a frame on its session's `ao-preview-artifact` origin, which CORS trusts, and call the API from there. A page could also use routes that answer a request with no `Origin`, such as `link-preview`, which fetches any URL.
  - Requests are judged by the nearest agent page around the requesting frame.
  - The check window applies the same rule to the daemon host and port its proxy lets through, and reports each refusal to the agent.
- **A page made without network is served without network.** A Codex agent in accept-edits or auto could publish through the html tools, which run outside its sandbox, and the reader's frame gave the page public network. Such a page now gets an `offline-` id. The render route serves it with `default-src data: blob: 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; form-action 'none'` added to the sandbox CSP. CSP does not cover WebRTC or a `dns-prefetch` hint; that limit is marked in the code.
- **The network follows the turn in flight.** It is read from the approval mode the running turn was sent with, not the mode picked for the next turn.
- **The navigation guard lets the app move its own frames.** A frame can now move to an artifact's inline origin or to the daemon's new port. A page navigating its own frame is still held.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - Removing an earlier bootstrap touches only the block right after the doctype.
  - Workspace files open with `O_NONBLOCK`, so a FIFO swapped in cannot block a request.
  - Only `system` rows show pages, so a cloud row cannot frame a local page.
  - A publish without a height opens at 400.
  - The artifacts prompt names `html_render` only in chat sessions.
  - The agent page URL rules live in one shared module.
  - The interface address list is cached for 5 s.

Live in the dev app:
- From inside an inline artifact:
  - its own file loaded (200);
  - `fetch` of `link-preview` and `/api/v1/sessions` was refused;
  - a nested frame on the session's preview origin was refused and never created.
- The app moved an artifact frame from the inline origin to the artifact route and back, and the page showed both times. The page's own `location.href = "https://example.com/"` was held.

title: feat: continue stopped conversation turn
body:
Code changes: +381 −30 
Tests: +999 −9 
Others: +43 −10 

## Summary

Add a **Continue** action after the user stops a Chat turn. The composer button changes from **Stop turn** to **Continue turn**. Typing a new question changes it back to **Send message**.

Continue starts a new turn in the existing conversation with “Continue from where you stopped.” and a bounded, provider-only reminder containing the original task and recent partial response. The partial response remains visible, and the timeline displays a **Continued** marker.

This preserves the interrupted task’s context; it does not resume execution at an exact token or instruction.

Related to #4199. Implements the ChatGPT-style Stop → Continue flow described by @Rishet11. Holding automated work until a session is resumed is outside this PR’s scope.

## Changes

- Use backend-owned Continue eligibility so the frontend and backend select the same stopped turn.
- Exclude cancelled, rolled-back, and interrupted queued turns that never reached the provider.
- Preserve eligibility when provider IDs are cleared after an agent or interface switch.
- Reuse one client message ID per Continue intent to prevent duplicate delivery after an ambiguous timeout.
- Allow a fresh Continue intent after Undo or a new interruption.
- Preserve the original task, verified excerpt context, and bounded assistant response tail across repeated interruptions.
- Keep the reminder separate from visible message text and exclude reasoning and tool output.
- Use bounded snapshot reads, with a targeted prompt lookup when the original task is outside the page.
- Preserve accepted context through queued delivery, controller recovery, hibernated intake, and failed-turn retries.
- Match native history against the dispatched prompt without exposing the hidden reminder as a duplicate message.
- Persist and expose the optional `continuation` flag while preserving ordinary-message retry hashes.
- Register migration `0195` without automatic startup rewriting of migration history. Earlier preview databases require explicit out-of-band repair.
- Regenerate sqlc output, OpenAPI, and frontend API types.

## Testing

Added coverage for Stop → Continue, Stop → new question, repeated interruptions, provider-scope changes, swept queues, bounded history, excerpt preservation, pending requests, ambiguous retries, Undo, and the Continued marker.

Backend coverage includes context persistence, queued delivery, retry compatibility, native-history matching, controller recovery, and hibernated intake.

title: feat: link the global ao CLI to the installed app CLI
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Summary
Add a Developer Mode action that links the global `ao` command on the user's PATH to the CLI shipped with the installed Agent Orchestrator app.

## User story
As a developer, I want the global `ao` command to use the CLI bundled with my installed app so that terminal commands and the desktop app stay on the same version.

## Proposed behavior

- Add a Developer Mode action to link or relink the global `ao` executable to the app's supported CLI path.
- Detect and display the current target before changing it.
- Require explicit confirmation before replacing an existing command or symlink.
- Validate that the target belongs to the installed Agent Orchestrator app and is executable.
- Report success with the resolved command path and version.
- Report actionable failures for missing app installation, unsupported permissions, an existing non-AO executable, or a stale link.
- Provide a safe unlink or repair path without touching unrelated binaries.
- Keep the feature gated behind Developer Mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- The action is unavailable when Developer Mode is disabled.
- Existing global commands are never overwritten silently.
- A link created by AO resolves to the intended installed app CLI.
- Re-running the action is idempotent.
- The command can be verified from a fresh shell.
- Tests cover missing targets, stale links, unrelated existing executables, permissions, relinking, and version reporting.

## Open design questions

- Which global installation locations should be supported on macOS, Linux, and Windows?
- Should AO use a symlink, a small forwarding shim, or the existing installer mechanism?
- How should upgrades update the link while preserving user-managed PATH configuration?
- Should the app expose a repair action when the global command points to an older release?

This issue is intentionally scoped to Developer Mode and must not change the normal installation path.

title: bug(automations): timezone-only edits retain the previous execution schedule
body:
Changing only an automation's timezone can update the timezone field without changing when it will run.

### Repro
1. Create a disabled automation with cron `0 9 * * *` and timezone `UTC`.
2. PATCH `/api/v1/automations/<id>` with:
   ```json
   {"timezone":"America/New_York"}
   ```
3. Check `timezone` and `nextRunAt` in the response.

The timezone becomes `America/New_York`, but the next run stays at `2026-10-07T09:00:00Z`. It should move to `2026-10-07T13:00:00Z`, which is 09:00 in New York that day.

Sending the same cron along with the new timezone gives the correct result. Changing between two named timezones can instead return a timezone-conflict error.

The update path [reuses the old RRULE](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd67f2d8184b1df0fd21166ef1e21b42b973ec24/backend/internal/service/automation/service.go#L225-L245), including its old timezone anchor.

**Test notes:** Fedora 44, `dd67f2d818`, tested through the real daemon API on 2026-10-06. The automation stayed disabled; this verifies the calculated schedule, not an executed run.

title: bug(cues): project ZDOTDIR is ignored when loading zsh startup files
body:
A normal project terminal loads the project's `ZDOTDIR`, but a command Cue in the same project doesn't. Functions and other setup from that directory are missing in the Cue shell.

### Repro
1. Create a scratch directory with a `.zshrc` containing:
   ```zsh
   function audit_custom_function() { print -r -- AUDIT_FUNCTION_OK; }
   ```
2. Set the project's `ZDOTDIR` environment variable to that directory.
3. Run this in an ordinary project terminal and as a command Cue:
   ```sh
   whence -w audit_custom_function
   printf 'ZDOTDIR=<%s>\n' "$ZDOTDIR"
   ```

The terminal reports `function` and the configured path. The Cue reports `none` and `ZDOTDIR=<>`. Both should use the project's configuration.

The [Cue startup wrapper](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd67f2d8184b1df0fd21166ef1e21b42b973ec24/backend/internal/service/shellterm/cueready.go#L95-L119) reads ZDOTDIR from the daemon's environment rather than the project's.

**Test notes:** Fedora 44, zsh, `dd67f2d818`. Compared real project-shell output over the terminal WebSocket with output from an invoked Cue. Only scratch configuration was used.

title: bug(browser): Firefox import uses directory suffixes instead of profile names
body:
The Firefox import picker uses the profile folder's suffix instead of its actual name. After a profile is renamed in Firefox, AO can show the old name and mark the wrong default state.

### Repro
Use a profile registered in `profiles.ini` as:

```ini
[Profile0]
Name=Client Research
IsRelative=1
Path=abc123.Work
Default=1
```

Run import-source discovery. It returns `name: "Work", default: false` instead of `Client Research` and `true`.

The picker should use the registered name so users can identify the intended profile. [discoverFirefoxProfiles](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd67f2d8184b1df0fd21166ef1e21b42b973ec24/frontend/src/main/browser-profile-import.ts#L366-L383) currently guesses the name and default flag from the directory name rather than reading `profiles.ini`.

**Test notes:** Fedora 44, `dd67f2d818`. Reproduced with the production discovery code and a disposable profile containing a real SQLite database. The incorrect label was also confirmed in the app's import picker. No personal browser data was accessed.

### Screenshots

The picker shows Work instead of the profile name Client Research.

title: bug(cli): automation list silently stops after the first 50 definitions
body:
`ao automation list` shows only the first 50 automations, with no warning in the plain output and no option to fetch the next page.

### Repro
1. Create 51 disabled automations.
2. Run `ao automation list` and `ao automation list --json`.
3. Compare with `GET /api/v1/automations?limit=100`.

The API returns all 51. The CLI returns 50 and exits successfully. JSON includes `nextCursor: "NTA"`, but `ao automation list --cursor NTA` fails with `unknown flag: --cursor`. Calling the cursor API directly returns the missing entry.

The CLI should either follow pagination or expose it clearly. [The list command](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd67f2d8184b1df0fd21166ef1e21b42b973ec24/backend/internal/cli/automation.go#L127-L147) currently makes one request without following the next cursor.

**Test notes:** Fedora 44, `dd67f2d818`. Tested with the real daemon and CLI. All 51 automations stayed disabled and were deleted afterward; none ran.

title: fix(chat): quiet MCP startup note, clearer workspace errors, and Chat without draft storage
body:
## What changes for people using Chat

- **MCP startup failures are a short note, not a banner.** When a tool server fails to start, a single muted line appears by the composer, for example "Playwright didn't start. Continuing without it." It shows once per session, only while the chat is visible, and fades after about 3 seconds. It does not move the conversation or block clicks. The old banner with the server list, raw errors, Reload and close button is gone.
- **A missing worktree is no longer confused with a failed check.** The daemon now reports "not found" only when the session folder really is missing. A folder AO can't read gets its own plain message ("AO can't read this session's folder. Check its permissions."). A temporary failure shows "Checking workspace…" on the editor button and retries up to 3 times before showing the reason.
- **Chat keeps working when drafts can't be saved.** Before, a draft storage failure replaced the whole chat with a "restore access to local storage" card. Now Chat opens with an in-memory composer and a one-line notice. Editing sent or queued messages is off in that state because it relies on saved drafts. Draft saving comes back on its own when the window regains focus and the composer is empty. A view of an older session incarnation still stops and asks you to reopen the current session, as before.

## Notes for reviewers

- The manual MCP Reload action is removed from the desktop UI on purpose. The backend route stays, because the mobile app still calls it.
- `SESSION_WORKSPACE_UNREADABLE` is returned as 409. `apierr`'s 403 is documented for ownership failures only.
- The workspace error code is passed from the daemon through `main.ts` and the editor handoff to the renderer. Daemon-not-ready, timeouts and non-JSON 5xx responses are tagged `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, so they count as temporary.
- New strings are in all 8 locales, with the plural forms the plural-coverage test requires.
- Most of the `ChatWorkspace.tsx` line count is the composer re-indenting inside a positioned wrapper. `git diff -w` shows the real change.
- Per-control disabling while a composer setting is applying was considered and left out. Config writes are serialised, so the other controls can't take input during a write either. The current brief whole-row disable is the honest behaviour.

## Testing

- Renderer suite, editor-handoff tests, Go session and httpd tests, and frontend typecheck all pass.
- New tests cover: the note showing once per session, not being used up while hidden, fading out, letting clicks through, and showing again for a restarted session; the editor button retrying 3 times then showing the reason; Chat staying usable without draft storage and recovering on focus; the older-incarnation stop; and the backend mapping for missing, not-a-directory and unreadable folders.

title: fix(chat): keep old chats readable while a stopped agent resumes
body:
## Problem

Opening a chat whose agent had stopped locked the entire surface: no scrolling, no model picker, a blank composer with no placeholder. The user saw an empty screen for seconds until the resume finished.

Caused by #6254, which piped the background resume through `controllerTransitioning`. That flag was built for terminal/chat mode switches where the snapshot is in flux and input must wait, so it marks the conversation panel `inert` and blanks the composer.

## Fix

A background resume gets its own `agentResuming` signal, separate from `controllerTransitioning`. It disables only sending (the composer says "Resuming agent…") and hides the stopped-controller banner, but the history stays readable and scrollable immediately. The model picker loads once the agent is back.

Also warms up stopped agents on sidebar hover (300ms dwell) by sharing the same resume request, so the chat is often ready by the time it opens.

## Changes

- `SessionView.tsx`: passes `agentResuming` instead of folding `quietResume` into `controllerTransitioning`.
- `SessionChatSurface.tsx`: threads the new prop.
- `ChatWorkspace.tsx`: `agentResuming` disables the composer and hides the stopped banner, but does not set the panel `inert`.
- `useCanResumeAgent.ts`: exports `resumeAgentOnOpen()` with a shared in-flight promise per session.
- `Sidebar.tsx`: starts `resumeAgentOnOpen` after a 300ms hover dwell.

## Testing

- Typecheck clean.
- 532 targeted tests pass (SessionView, ChatWorkspace, Sidebar).
- Tested in the desktop app against real data with stopped sessions.

Also includes the migration renumber from #6341 (two PRs merged with duplicate migration 0181).

title: feat(models): list Claude Code models by family, fold older ones, open on the last-used model
body:
## What changes for users

The Claude Code model picker now opens short and in a fixed order. It lists the newest model of each family, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, and folds every older version under an **Other models** row. The row expands in place and collapses again the next time the menu opens. Search still covers all models, and a selected older model keeps the list expanded so the current choice never hides.

New tasks open on the model the user ran most recently. With no history they open on the newest Opus. The "Use agent model" row is gone from the model combobox.

A configured family alias such as `sonnet` no longer adds a second "Sonnet" row next to the provider's concrete models. It marks that family's newest model as the default instead.

Other agents keep their reported catalog order.

## How it works

- `splitClaudeModels` in `agent-model-choices.ts` ranks models by family and version, read from the label and then the provider ID. Snapshot dates, suffixes like `v1:0`, and parts like `(1M context)` or `[1m]` are not versions. Models with no family or version stay in the current list.
- The backend stamps each model with `lastUsedAt` from session history on every catalog read (`model_usage.go`). Project history wins, and a project with none inherits the agent-wide answer. Nothing is written to the cached catalog.
- The alias fold runs where the catalog is fetched, so the composer, project settings and agent switch all see the same list.

## Relationship to #6028

This supersedes #6028 and builds on its last-used idea. It is about a third of the size (+400 / −28, against +1,132 / −38) because it leaves out:

- the backend ordering rewrite and its cache-fingerprint invalidation;
- the ACP chat menu ordering;
- the float-to-front reordering by recency, and `releasedAt`.

The chat model menu therefore keeps main's order. Ordering is done in the frontend, so it needs no catalog schema change beyond `lastUsedAt`.

## Testing

- Frontend: 1,842 tests across the picker, composer, project settings, agent switch, reviewer, hooks, lib and i18n suites pass, and `tsc` is clean for the touched files.
- Backend: `go vet` and the agent, httpd and ports tests pass. OpenAPI and TypeScript types are regenerated.
- Run in the Electron dev app against a real Claude catalog: four current rows in order, the Other models fold, no duplicate alias row.

title: fix(browser): default to the imported profile and make profile switches reliable
body: Code changes: +141 -37\ Tests: +195 -15\ Others: +0 -0 ## What The browser panel now uses a configured (imported) browser profile by default, and switching from Temporary to a profile no longer fails or crashes. - A worker with no saved profile choice opens in the first configured profile. It uses Temporary only when no profile exists, or when you pick Temporary for that worker (the choice lasts until the app restarts). - Picking a profile while a page is still loading now switches. The load is stopped and reloaded in the new profile. Before, the pick did nothing. - Picking a profile while an agent is using the browser now waits up to 10s for that agent command to finish, then switches. New agent commands are refused with `BROWSER_PROFILE_SWITCHING` until the switch is done. Before, the switch failed with an error dialog. - A switch to a profile whose pages take a moment to reload no longer crashes the main process. ## Why Reported as: "when I switch from temporary to an already imported profile, I sometimes see an error", and "by default always select a configured profile, not temporary". I reproduced each problem on current `main` in the real desktop app (details under Testing). There were two different errors: 1. **Error dialog "Wait for browser activity to finish before switching profiles".** The confirm prompt ("Switching profiles will reload the browser pages") blocks the Electron main process while it is open. Agent `ao browser` commands that arrive meanwhile are queued. When you click Yes, a queued command can start before `switchProfile` checks for agent activity, and the switch is refused. 2. **"A JavaScript error occurred in the main process: Active browser tab is unavailable".** `rebuildSessionTabs` cleared `activeTabId` and set it again only after every saved page finished reloading in the new profile. After you pick a profile, the dropdown returns focus to the "Browser controls" button. Its tooltip raises the browser overlay, which on macOS calls `refreshLastFocusedPanelSurface` → `activeEntry()`, and that throws. Logged-in pages reload slowly, so this happens often but not always. ## How All changes are in `frontend/src/main/browser-view-host.ts`. - `initialProfileIdForSession`: saved binding, then the first configured profile, then Temporary. It is not persisted as a binding, so it does not add registry writes or count toward the 1,024-binding limit. An explicit Temporary pick is kept in memory for that worker. - `switchProfile` sets `profileSwitching` first, which already makes new agent commands fail with `BROWSER_PROFILE_SWITCHING`. It then stops in-flight page loads, remembering their target URLs, and waits for in-flight work to finish (`waitForBrowserIdle`). That wait and the native operation queue wait share one deadline, `PROFILE_SWITCH_SETTLE_MS` = 10s. If anything is still running at the deadline, the switch fails on time with the existing "still busy" error, and `profileSwitching` is cleared. - The switch has two phases. `profileSwitching` refuses new work at the entry points (`execute`, renderer handlers). `profileReplacing` is set only after the drain succeeds, and only it makes `openTab`/`closeTab` refuse. So an agent `tab-new` or `tab-close` admitted before the switch still completes during the wait, instead of failing with `BROWSER_PROFILE_SWITCHING`. - Each pending navigation is tracked by identity, not by URL, so an aborted older load of the same URL can't clear the newer one's pending URL. - `getProfileSwitchInfo().agentActive` no longer counts renderer page loads, so profile menu items stay enabled while a page loads. - `rebuildSessionTabs` activates the restored tab before reloading pages. All the code up to the first `await` is synchronous, so nothing else ever sees a worker without an active tab. As a side effect, the new tab is shown loading instead of a blank panel. Not changed: browser views that are already open stay in their current profile until reopened. Adding or importing a profile does not switch live workers. ## Testing **Unit tests** (`browser-view-host.test.ts`): new and updated tests for the default profile, switching during a page load, waiting for an agent command, giving up on time when an agent command outlasts the 10s deadline, letting admitted agent tab-new/tab-close commands finish during the wait, keeping the newest pending navigation when an older load of the same URL aborts, and keeping an active tab during the rebuild. Each new test fails on `main`; the rebuild test fails with the exact live error, `Active browser tab is unavailable`. Results: `npx vitest run` on the browser host, profile IPC, profile store, BrowserPanel, and useBrowserView suites: 334 passed. `npm run typecheck` is clean for `frontend/src`. **Real desktop app, before and after.** Setup: - `electron-forge start` in isolated dev data (`~/.ao/dev/ao-253`), with a copy of my imported "Google Chrome" profile. - Claude Code workers, plus a local test server for slow pages (`/slow`: 30s, `/slow5`: 5s). - The same script was run first with `origin/main`'s `browser-view-host.ts`, then with this branch. - Test harness: the native confirm prompt was answered through a `dialog.showMessageBox` patch in the main-process inspector. For S4 the patch blocks the main thread for 2.5s before answering Yes, just as the real macOS prompt does (verified: while the real prompt is open, CDP stops answering and agent `ao browser` calls fail with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`). Error dialogs were shown for real. | Scenario | `main` | This PR | |---|---|---| | S1: fresh worker, an imported profile exists | Opens in **Temporary** | Opens in **Google Chrome** | | S2: pick Google Chrome while a page is still loading | Nothing happens, stays Temporary | Switches; the loading page reloads in Google Chrome | | S4: pick Google Chrome while an agent loops `ao browser get url` | **3 of 3** picks show an error dialog: "Wait for browser activity to finish before switching profiles" | **3 of 3** picks switch, 6 of 6 switches total, no error dialogs, no agent-side errors | | S3: Temporary → Google Chrome on a page that takes 5s to reload | **Main-process crash dialog**: "Active browser tab is unavailable" | Switches; page reloads in Google Chrome; no error | **S1: default profile for a fresh worker** | `main` | This PR | |---|---| | | | **S3: switch to the imported profile on a page that is slow to reload** | `main` | This PR | |---|---| | | | The "after" screenshot shows the "Browser controls" tooltip open: the same overlay that crashed `main` now just refreshes the restored tab. **S4 on `main`, main-process log:** ``` browser profile switch failed: Error: Wait for browser activity to finish before switching profiles at browserError (.vite/build/main.js) at Object.switchProfile (.vite/build/main.js) at selectFromMenu (.vite/build/main.js) ``` Dialogs recorded by the harness on `main`: `warning "Switching profiles will reload…"` → `error "Wait for browser activity to finish before switching profiles"`, three times. On this PR: six `warning` dialogs and no `error` dialogs. ## Risks - Every unbound worker now starts on the first profile, so that profile is "live" whenever any browser view is open. Clearing or deleting that profile is refused while views are open, as it already was for workers explicitly bound to it. - A confirmed switch can take up to 10s when an agent command is running. Agent commands that arrive during the switch get the existing retryable `BROWSER_PROFILE_SWITCHING` error. - Unrelated to this PR: while the native confirm prompt is open, the whole main process is blocked, so agents see `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Showing that prompt as a window-modal sheet, or in the renderer, would remove the block. That is not done here. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` - [x] One focused change - [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior - [x] Relevant frontend checks run locally (vitest suites above, typecheck) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fix Claude chats showing as exited after a restart, and mobile's Needs you list
body:
## What was wrong

After any daemon restart, every Claude Code chat came back as exited, even when its host process was still running. The old startup relaunched agents, so this rarely showed. #6254 changed startup to only reconnect to live hosts. The reconnect goes through `ports.ChatDriverReconnector`, but the Claude driver wrapper (`checkpointDriver`) embeds only the `ports.ChatDriver` interface, so `Reconnect` was hidden. The check always said "host not running" and marked the session exited.

Desktop hides this with a neutral dot and resumes the chat when you open it. Mobile lists `exited` under Needs you and never resumes, so a restart put the whole board there.

## Changes

- Backend: `checkpointDriver` now forwards `Reconnect`. Two tests: the driver implements the reconnector, and a missing host reports `ErrChatHostNotRunning`.
- Mobile: `exited` is no longer in `AGENT_BLOCKED`, so those sessions stay in their delivery column.
- Mobile: opening a chat whose agent has exited resumes it once, quietly. A failure leaves the existing Resume banner instead of an alert.

## Checked

- Real daemon, one Claude chat with a real reply: before the fix it was `exited` after both a SIGKILL restart and a graceful restart. With the fix it stays `idle` after both.
- `go test` and `go vet` for the claudeacp package, mobile vitest for the touched files, and mobile typecheck all pass.

Not changed: terminal sessions are still archived after a reboot because startup no longer relaunches them. That is a separate decision.

title: feat(settings): put memory diagnostics behind a Diagnostics flag

## Summary

Developer mode used to turn on memory and CPU monitoring by itself: MB figures on every session card, the memory light in the archive bar (and the window it opens), and the Diagnostics settings page. This change moves all of that behind its own **Diagnostics** toggle, which works the way the Cloud toggle does:

- The Diagnostics toggle appears in Settings → General → Advanced only when Developer mode is on. It is off by default and saved in `localStorage` (`ao.diagnostics`).
- Diagnostics is enabled only when both Developer mode and the Diagnostics toggle are on (`useDiagnosticsEnabled()` in `hooks/useSessionMemory.ts`). This one check controls the memory queries, so with either toggle off nothing polls `/usage/sessions/memory` or `/usage/memory/pressure`.
- The board's card chips, the archive-bar indicator, and the Diagnostics settings page all use this check.
- The toggle has a one-line description, translated into all 8 locales.

The session inspector's token and cost usage stays under Developer mode alone. It isn't memory diagnostics.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` (frontend)
- `npm test` (full renderer suite): 397 files, 6377 tests passed
- New and updated tests:
  - The Diagnostics toggle appears only in Developer mode and is saved.
  - The board shows no memory figures with Developer mode on and Diagnostics off.
  - The Diagnostics page is hidden or shown according to both flags.

## Risks

- Developer mode users lose the MB figures and the Diagnostics page until they turn on the new toggle. That is the intended behavior.
- I have not checked the change visually in the desktop app.

title: fix: count deliberate orchestrator direction in sidebar recency
body:
Code changes: +389 -108  
Tests: +531 -38  
Others: +71 -7  

A deliberate orchestrator message can activate a worker while its sidebar age and position still reflect an old human prompt. Track a separate durable interaction timestamp and use the latest human prompt or qualifying interaction for sidebar age and sorting. Human-only prompt facts and analytics retain their meaning.

The CLI forwards cooperative `AO_SESSION_ID` identity through send delivery. The store derives sender role and project from durable session rows: an existing, nonterminated same-project orchestrator can advance a worker's recency. Worker reports/sends, unknown senders, cross-project orchestrators, and routine automation remain excluded. No textual sender prefix or client role label grants eligibility. This preserves the existing unauthenticated loopback trust model; it is not cryptographic authentication.

Queued delivery preserves sender, explicit user-authored annotations, and original acceptance time. Accepted active steering records recency without refresh on duplicate activity. Automation retains automation origin in Chat and TUI hooks rather than being relabeled human. SQL and API artifacts are regenerated.

Validation: full manager/store and CLI race suites pass; daemon race suite passes with the production-wrapper regression; all 397 frontend test files pass (6375 tests, 7 skipped). Frontend and E2E typechecks, docs build, Go build/vet, lint v2.13.2, and generated SQL/API drift checks pass. Initial broad race failures from inherited AO environment and timing load were rerun with cleaned environment, and affected adapter suites pass. The broad migration suite caught a missing append-only version ledger entry; that entry is added and its regression now passes. Linux/native/Docker/browser workflow checks remain subject to CI.

Review follow-ups: forward session relays through the production daemon wrapper and test it. Consolidate all Chat relay paths in one options-aware service implementation and one required launcher method, removing conditional dispatch and redundant forwarders. Agent-switch continuations use the same method with empty interaction options; sender metadata, authorship, timestamps, and durable retry IDs remain intact. Full Chat, session-manager, and daemon race suites pass after the simplification, along with lint and vet. Human-initiated inspector review-comment and summary sends explicitly set `userAuthored: true`; UI regressions check that flag and the terminal regression checks human prompt recency and absence of coordination wrapping. After that fix, all 397 frontend test files (6375 tests, 7 skipped), typecheck, focused terminal race regression, and lint pass.

Interaction persistence is owned by each acceptance path: Chat append and transition enqueue record sender interactions transactionally; only direct terminal sends use the separate recorder. Terminal outbox replay skips that write, and human-only sends use their existing human prompt timestamp. Write-count regressions and full manager/store race suites, lint, and vet pass after this change.

Limitations: no historical timestamp backfill or live database repairs, and no fix for the separate clock-tick stale-label issue. Native platform, Docker/browser integration, and remote workflow results remain CI validation gaps.

title: feat(cloud): keep accounts when moving to the WorkOS Production environment
body:
## Summary
AO production currently signs users in through **WorkOS Staging**. To use the `auth.orchestrator.inc` AuthKit domain, which WorkOS only allows in Production, sign-in has to move to the **WorkOS Production** environment. Production issues new user and organization IDs, and AO stores the old ones (`ao_users.external_user_id`, `ao_organizations.external_org_id`, plus project repository grants). Without this change, every existing user would sign in to an empty new account.

This PR keeps existing accounts **without rewriting any stored IDs**:

- **Original IDs at sign-in.** The WorkOS user and organization lookups now read `external_id`. When it holds a WorkOS ID of the same kind (`user_…` / `org_…`), the principal uses that original ID instead of the token's. Only AO's API key can set `external_id`.
- **Transition fallback.** Optional `AO_CLOUD_WORKOS_LEGACY_ISSUER` / `_CLIENT_ID` / `_API_KEY` (and `_JWKS_URL`) keep the previous environment's tokens accepted. Desktop builds still on the Staging client keep working until they update.
- **`cloud/scripts/workos-copy-environment.py`** copies users, organizations (name, metadata/capabilities, domains) and active memberships into the target environment, with `external_id` set to the source ID. It is idempotent, dry-run by default, and prints counts and IDs only.
- Config validation is shared between the current and legacy WorkOS settings. Docs are updated, and the "staging and production share one WorkOS environment" note is replaced.

Nothing changes until the production secret gets Production values. With no legacy settings, behaviour is identical except that `external_id` is honoured.

## Rollout
1. Merge and promote. The change is inert until step 3.
2. Run the copy script from Staging → Production.
3. Point production at the Production client and key (issuer `https://api.workos.com`; WorkOS still issues access tokens from `api.workos.com/user_management/<client>` even with the `auth.orchestrator.inc` AuthKit domain), add the `legacy_*` Staging values plus task-definition secret refs, and redeploy.
4. Set the repo variable `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` to the Production client and ship a desktop release.
5. Re-run the copy script. Remove the legacy settings once old builds age out.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/auth ./internal/config ./internal/httpapi ./internal/postgres ./cmd/...` pass. The new tests cover the following:
  - OIDC verification with real RS256 tokens and JWKS, for a copied user/org and for a user that wasn't copied.
  - Fallback verifier error handling.
  - `external_id` parsing: wrong kind, self-reference, and non-WorkOS values are ignored.
  - Config resolution and legacy validation.
- Copy script dry run against the real environments: 659 users, 32 organizations, 31 memberships to create.
- `go test ./...` also fails in `internal/workerexec` (`TestCloudClaude*`). The same tests fail on unmodified `main` locally, so this PR doesn't cause it.

Verified against real WorkOS tokens. For a Production user linked to a Staging user, a Production token and a Staging token (through the fallback) both resolve to the Staging ID, and the current-only verifier rejects the Staging token.

## Risks
- Password users have no password in WorkOS Production (WorkOS can't export password hashes). They use "Forgot password". Google users link by verified email.
- Sign in with Apple isn't configured in Production. 1 user has an Apple relay email.

title: fix(chat): keep ACP prompt receipts acknowledgeable after a host rejection
body:
Fixes #6222

## Summary

When a Chat prompt reached the persistent ACP host before AO had acknowledged the previous turn's terminal result, the host refused it locally with `previous ACP prompt is active or not acknowledged`. That refusal has no event ID. `finishPrompt` then set `terminalEventID` to the empty ID, which erased the outstanding receipt. When the controller later committed the original result and sent its ACK, `AcknowledgeProviderEvent` saw a mismatch and returned nil without notifying the host. The host kept its pending result and refused every later prompt with the same `-32602` error until the session was restarted or switched to TUI and back. Both reports on the issue match this: the OMP incident, and the Claude Code session that recovered only after a TUI round trip.

The fix: only a durable host receipt (a non-empty event ID) replaces the outstanding `terminalEventID`. A host-local rejection still settles its own turn as failed, but the original receipt stays acknowledgeable. Once that ACK goes out, the host accepts prompts again.

Hosts that are already wedged recover without extra repair work. After the update restarts the daemon, `ActivateLiveReconnect` acknowledges a committed pending result.

## Not in this PR

The issue also asks to serialize the `SteerOrSend` no-active-turn fallback with terminal projection. That moved to #6360. Routing the fallback through the busy queue conflicts with the #4861 failed-turn queue hold, so for now the behavior stays as it is. With this fix, losing that race costs one failed replacement turn instead of wedging the session.

## Tests

- New test `TestPersistentACPLateAckSurvivesHostLocalPromptRejection` uses the real persistent host and a fake ACP provider, with completed and failed originals. It runs the original turn without an ACK, then a replacement turn that the host rejects with no event ID, then a late ACK of the original. The next prompt must reach the provider and complete, and the provider must see exactly 2 prompts. Without the fix both subtests fail: the turn after the late ACK is still refused.
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/persistenthost/` passes.
- I did not run golangci-lint locally because it isn't installed here. `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

## Risks

Low. The only behavior change: a completion without an event ID no longer clears the stored receipt. Persistent host responses always carry an event ID, and non-persistent processes never set one, so for them the field stays empty as before.

title: fix(cloud): disable AZ rebalancing for single-task deploys
body:
## Summary
I hit this while releasing #6357. Both services (`ao-cloud-staging-api`, `ao-cloud-production-api`) now have ECS **Availability Zone Rebalancing** enabled, and ECS rejects the scripts' `update-service`:

> Availability Zone Rebalancing does not support maximumPercent <= 100 % as deployment configuration.

The scripts deliberately use `maximumPercent: 100 / minimumHealthyPercent: 0`, because the terminal relay is process-local and only one task may run. This passes `--availability-zone-rebalancing DISABLED` on `update-service` in both scripts and on `create-service` in promote; rebalancing does nothing for a one-task service. The #6357 release ran exactly these commands by hand (production revisions 52 and 53).

It also updates `deployment.md`: production now reads WorkOS from `ao-cloud/production/workos-next` (WorkOS Production plus the `legacy_*` Staging values).

## Tests
- `bash -n` on both scripts.
- Production rollouts of revisions 52 and 53 with this exact flag and deployment configuration completed, and `verify-ecs-service.py` passed.

## Release follow-ups (not fixed here)
- **Staging can't run `main`.** Staging's control-plane image (`staging-d277703e2-linux-amd64`) is a patched build that accepts GitHub App credentials with `AO_CLOUD_ENV=staging`. `main` rejects that (`config.go`: "GitHub App credentials may only be configured in production"), so `deploy-staging.sh` from `main` crash-loops and is rolled back. `promote-production.sh` therefore can't promote a `main` build. Either the staging allowance belongs in `main`, or staging should drop its GitHub App secrets.
- **The staging migration credential goes stale.** `ao-cloud-staging-storage` uses an RDS-managed, auto-rotated master secret, but `ao-cloud/staging/migration-database-url` holds a copied password. I refreshed it during this release, and the next rotation will break migrations again.

title: bug(desktop): Codex wheel scrolling can be ignored because AO reports pointer at cell 1,1
body:
## Summary

In AO 0.13.3 on macOS, scroll gestures did not move an existing Codex terminal transcript, while Page Up and Page Down worked after focusing the terminal prompt. Scrolling in Settings > Harness worked in a separate control check.

AO's fixed mouse coordinates appear incompatible with the pinned prompt header in newer Codex TUIs. This is a source-based diagnosis supported by the observed symptoms, not a captured trace of the failing wheel event.

## Environment and version limits

- Agent Orchestrator desktop: 0.13.3.
- macOS: 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64.
- The affected session used AO's native PTY runtime (`ptyhost-v1`), not tmux, when inspected during the terminal investigation.
- Installed Codex CLI: 0.160.1.
- Historical rollout metadata records the session's original CLI as 0.144.4. This alone does not establish the executable version during the scrolling reproduction.
- By the later process inspection, the session had transitioned to Chat mode and its resolved Codex executable was 0.160.1. The exact version of the TUI process during the earlier reproduction was not captured.
- The Codex source analysis below is pinned to `rust-v0.160.1`; the AO source is pinned to `v0.13.3` and the installed AO bundle was also inspected.

## Observed reproduction

1. Open a Codex session in AO's Terminal UI with enough conversation history to scroll.
2. Attempt to scroll upward over the transcript. In the observed session, the viewport did not move.
3. Click the terminal prompt and press Page Up (Fn + Up on a Mac keyboard). Earlier transcript content becomes visible.
4. Press Page Down (Fn + Down). Later transcript content becomes visible.
5. Open Settings > Harness and scroll the harness list. The list moves normally.

Expected: a wheel/trackpad gesture over transcript content should scroll that content.

Actual: the gesture did not move the transcript, while page-key navigation worked. The broader claim that scrolling was broken everywhere in AO was not reproduced in Settings.

The previous checks used native UI automation scroll input; the user's original report also described macOS scrolling failing. A fresh controlled reproduction with a hardware trackpad and a known TUI process version would strengthen the report.

## Source evidence

AO synthesizes SGR wheel reports with a constant pointer position:

```ts
function sgrWheelReport(button: number, count: number): string {
  return `\x1b[<${button};1;1M`.repeat(count);
}
```

[AO v0.13.3 XtermTerminal.tsx, lines 354-365](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.13.3/frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx#L354-L365)

The mouse-tracking branch forwards these reports to the process. Other branches use local xterm scrollback or page keys:

[AO v0.13.3 wheel handler, lines 1382-1405](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.13.3/frontend/src/renderer/components/XtermTerminal.tsx#L1382-L1405)

Codex is absent from AO's keyboard-scroll provider set:

[AO v0.13.3 TerminalPane.tsx, lines 937-947](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/v0.13.3/frontend/src/renderer/components/TerminalPane.tsx#L937-L947)

In Codex 0.160.1, rendering a pinned prompt header moves the transcript body's hit-test area down one row:

```rust
body = Rect::new(area.x, area.y + 1, area.width, area.height - 1);
self.area = body;
```

[Codex rust-v0.160.1 transcript_view.rs, lines 197-203](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_view.rs#L197-L203)

The mouse handler returns without scrolling when the reported position lies outside that body and no selection drag is active:

[Codex rust-v0.160.1 transcript_view/input.rs, lines 213-233](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_view/input.rs#L213-L233)

SGR positions are one-based. Crossterm subtracts one, so AO's `1;1` becomes `(0,0)`, which falls on the excluded header row when the body begins at row 1:

[Crossterm SGR decoding, lines 735-739](https://github.com/crossterm-rs/crossterm/blob/master/src/event/sys/unix/parse.rs#L735-L739)

Page Up/Page Down take a different path that scrolls without checking mouse coordinates:

[Codex rust-v0.160.1 transcript_view/input.rs, lines 319-347](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_view/input.rs#L319-L347)

This explains how page keys can work while AO's wheel reports are ignored. The remaining verification is to observe AO's active buffer/mouse mode during a fresh failure and confirm it selects this mouse-report branch.

## Bare arrow keys are separate from the bug

Fn + Up/Down on macOS produces Page Up/Page Down. Bare Up/Down are separate keys. Codex assigns them to composer editing/history when the prompt owns input. They are not interchangeable transcript-scrolling commands.

[Apple keyboard shortcuts](https://support.apple.com/en-la/102650)

[Codex 0.160.1 editor keymap](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/tui/src/keymap.rs#L1697-L1700)

## Suggested fix and validation

Compute SGR coordinates from the wheel event's actual pointer position and the xterm grid rather than reporting cell 1,1. Preserve AO's local-scrollback and keyboard-scroll branches. Simply adding Codex to the keyboard-scroll provider set could be a workaround, but changes wheel granularity and would require compatibility checks across Codex versions and runtime types.

Validate with a pinned Codex prompt header, a pointer over the transcript body, both wheel directions, native PTY sessions, existing tmux-backed sessions, normal-buffer shells, and the existing keyboard-scroll providers. Scroll gestures over the prompt should continue to respect Codex's own hit testing.

## Related reports

- [#2493: Terminal cannot be scrolled when using Codex as agent in AO](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/2493) is closed; it describes the broader symptom without exact versions.

title: fix(scm): attribute PRs listed under a renamed GitHub repository
body:
Part of #6297

## Summary
After the org move, the `agent-orchestrator` project still stores origin `Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator`. GitHub serves that old path, but the PR list it returns names every head and base as `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`. I checked this live with `gh api repos/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pulls`: head and base are both `OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator`, with the same repository id `1156994049`.

Discovery only accepts head repositories configured for the checkout (`candidatesForHeadRepo`), and the checkout only knows the old name. So it dropped every same-repository PR. Session 107's #6262 was never attached. The inspector showed it only as a worker-reported link marked "External repository", and native review couldn't find it.

The fix is in the GitHub list adapter. When a PR's head repository has the same GitHub repository id as its base, the adapter reports the head under the name it was asked to list. The GitLab adapter already does this for same-project heads. Fork PRs still report the fork's full name. Once a PR is attached, its row updates itself to the canonical URL and repository on the next fetch, as #4090 already does.

Once a PR is tracked, it is no longer listed as a worker-reported link, so the "External repository" badge no longer shows for it.

## Tests
- New `TestListPRsByRepo_HeadRepoUnderRequestedName` runs the adapter against a fake GitHub server listing the old path. It fails without this change (head reported as `new-org/hello`) and passes with it. The fork PR still reports `forker/hello`.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/scm/... ./internal/observe/... ./internal/integration/...` and `go vet ./internal/adapters/scm/...` pass.

## Not covered (follow-ups for #6297)
- `ao session claim-pr` with the canonical URL is still refused. `requireProjectPRRepository` compares the URL as a string against the stored origin or `canonicalRepoURL`.
- The frontend's `isExternalRepository` check on worker-reported links still compares strings.
- The stored project origin is not refreshed to the canonical name.

I kept these out so this PR stays minimal; each could follow if wanted.

title: fix(session): let interface switches proceed past unsent TUI text
body:
Code changes: +20 -98\
Tests: +32 -234\
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

Switching a Codex session from Terminal to Chat failed on an **empty** composer:

> AO found unsent text in the terminal composer. The source interface was left untouched; submit or clear the draft and retry, or choose Discard draft and switch

The `Ask Codex to do anything` placeholder is unchanged (bold `›` marker, SGR-dim text). The footer changed. Codex now draws two footer rows, and both contain ` · `:

```
› Ask Codex to do anything                          ← dim placeholder
  GPT-6.1-Sol ultra · Context 94% left · …          ← model/status row (truecolor, not dim)
  ? for shortcuts         ⚠ 3 warnings · f2 to view ← new hint row
```

#6041 already treats the exact `Ask Codex to do anything` text as chrome, but `codexComposerFrame` took the bottom-most ` · ` row as the footer. That put the status row inside the composer region, where it read as a human draft. #5486 fixed the earlier version of this false positive, which assumed a single footer row.

Reproduced by recording a real Codex 0.160.1 PTY stream and replaying it through the pty-host's `renderedSurface` (vt-go): the empty composer classified as `TerminalComposerDraft`. Under tmux the same screen happened to pass, because of the second bug below.

## Changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `codex/terminal_activity.go` | The composer frame ends above the whole contiguous ` · ` footer block, not just its last row. |
| `terminalui/composer.go` | Dim and bold are parsed by one `applySGR` that skips extended-colour payloads. Previously the `2` in `38;2;R;G;B` was read as SGR dim, which could make truecolor draft text look like a placeholder to message delivery. |
| `session_manager/interface_transition.go` | The `drain` policy no longer inspects the composer. An idle provider is enough to switch, and unsent terminal text is discarded. Removes `errDrainDraftPresent` / `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT`, plus the composer-empty gate on the unstyled-runtime fallback. |
| Desktop `SessionInterfaceSwitch.tsx`, mobile `terminalInterfaceRecovery.ts` | Removes the "Discard draft and switch" recovery. "Cancel request and switch" for `DRAIN_DECISION_PENDING` and main's "Terminate and then switch" for an unverifiable source both stay. |

Product decision: a user who chooses to switch interfaces should not be blocked by text left in the TUI composer. Draft detection was a recurring source of false positives (#5486 and this one) that made the switch fail, so the drain no longer reads it.

## Intentional omissions

- Composer-draft detection stays for **message delivery** (`message_delivery.go`, `agent_switching.go`), so AO still never types into a half-written prompt. Only the interface-switch drain ignores it.
- `DRAIN_QUIESCENCE_UNVERIFIED` ("could not verify that the terminal was idle") is unchanged. It still fires when AO cannot recognise the TUI screen at all. One report showed a purple `»` prompt on Codex 0.159.1 that the Codex inspector does not match. That is a separate follow-up.
- Older persisted `DRAIN_DRAFT_PRESENT` transitions still show their stored error text, without the discard button. Retrying the switch now succeeds.

## Testing

- New tests: two-row Codex footer (empty → `Empty`, draft → `Draft`); truecolor draft text (semicolon and colon forms) stays `Draft`.
- Transition tests now assert that an idle draft completes the switch on both the styled path and the unstyled fallback path. Removed the four tests that only existed for draft blocking.
- Real Codex captures after the fix: pty-host surface → `Empty`; tmux capture → `Empty`; typed text → `Draft`.

**Local CI** (the machine ran out of disk mid-run: about 4 GB free, so the full suites could not complete locally):

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| Go: gofmt, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` | ✅ whole module |
| Go: `go test -race` on `codex`, `terminalui`, `session_manager` | ✅ (see flake note) |
| Desktop vitest `SessionInterfaceSwitch.test.tsx` | ✅ 23/23 |
| Mobile vitest `terminalInterfaceRecovery.test.ts` | ✅ 2/2 |
| Full `go test -race ./...`, golangci-lint v2.12.2, frontend typecheck + full vitest, mobile typecheck + test | Not run locally (no disk space). ✅ All 24 PR CI checks pass on `31e9cba`. |

Flake note: `TestInterfaceTransitionUnpromptedChatRoundTrip` hit its 3 s `awaitTransition` limit once in a `-count=5` race run of the whole package, while other race suites were running on the same machine. It passed 20/20 in isolation (`-race -count=20`). Its terminal surfaces are empty composers, and this change only lets drain accept idle sooner, never later.
