title: fix(desktop): spawn AO_DAEMON_COMMAND from a real directory in packaged builds
body:
Code changes: +4 -2  
Tests: +19 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Spawn an `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` daemon from `~/.ao` in packaged builds instead of from `app.getAppPath()`.

## Why

In a packaged build, `app.getAppPath()` returns the `app.asar` archive path. `main.ts` already notes this near its macOS bundle lookup. `resolveDaemonLaunch` passes that value as the spawn `cwd` for a configured daemon. Electron does not allow an archive path as a working directory ([asar archives: "Working Directory Can Not Be Set to Directories in Archive"](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/docs/tutorial/asar-archives.md)). So `spawn` throws `ENOTDIR` before the shell starts, and the packaged app ends up with no daemon whenever `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` is set.

Reproduced with the app's Electron (33.4.11, `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`), using the same spawn options as `startDaemonInner` (`shell: true, detached: true`):

- `cwd` = `…/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` → synchronous `ENOTDIR`. A wrapper script given as the command never runs.
- `cwd` = `~/.ao` → spawns normally.

Dev builds are unaffected: their `getAppPath()` is the real `frontend/` directory.

## How

- `resolveDaemonLaunch`: a configured daemon in a packaged build uses `<home>/.ao`, the same working directory as the bundled daemon. Dev keeps `appPath`.
- `startDaemonInner`: creates that directory first for a packaged configured daemon, as the bundled path already does. Without this, a fresh install could hit the same `ENOTDIR`/`ENOENT` failure.
- Identity checks are unchanged. `configured` daemons keep their existing behavior.

## Testing

- New `daemon-launch.test.ts` case: a packaged `AO_DAEMON_COMMAND` resolves `cwd` to `/Users/alice/.ao`, and the result never contains `.asar`. Test file 12/12 pass.
- `npm --prefix frontend run typecheck` passes.
- Full `npx vitest run`: the only failures are in `browser-profile-import`/`browser-view-host`/`provider-auth-flow`. They also fail on unmodified `main` in my environment (`better-sqlite3` native bindings not built). One `browser-history-store` timeout passed 3/3 when run alone on both `main` and this branch.
- I have not exercised this in a signed packaged build.

title: feat: let AO workers delegate bounded work to native subagents
body:
Code changes: +15 -5  
Tests: +79 -2  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Let AO worker sessions delegate bounded parts of their assigned task to their harness's native subagents or task-delegation tools. The change applies to the desktop worker prompt and the AO Cloud worker prompt. Orchestrator prompts are unchanged.

## Why

The worker prompt currently forbids native subagents outright ("Do not use the agent runtime's built-in subagent or task-delegation tools"). The CI/review follow-up line also tells workers to ask for more AO workers *instead of* native delegation. Harnesses such as Claude Code can run several read-only lookups or disjoint sub-tasks concurrently inside one session. The blanket ban blocks that, even when the work genuinely splits. The only alternative is spawning extra AO worker sessions, which is heavier and needs an orchestrator.

## How

Desktop worker (`session_manager/prompt.go`) and cloud worker (`workerexec/prompts.go`) replace the ban with three rules:
- The worker may delegate bounded portions of its assigned task when the harness supports it. It delegates only work that actually splits, with no fan-out of serial work and no activity for its own sake.
- The worker stays responsible for integrating results, testing, reporting, and its PR/MR. Subagents get no broader authority than the session: the same scope, ownership, execution guards and approval boundaries apply.
- Parallel subagents must be read-only or own disjoint files. No two agents edit the same file concurrently.

The CI/review parallel-help lines now ask for extra AO workers only when the work needs more capacity than bounded subagent delegation provides. The no-orchestrator fallback (continue serially, report to the human) is unchanged.

Intentionally unchanged: the orchestrator templates. Their "AO workers only" lines govern the orchestrator's own implementation delegation, and an orchestrator still delegates implementation to AO workers. Standalone workers had no ban.

## Testing

- `prompt_test.go`: a new positive test for the permission rules.
- A conflict check renders every worker variant (repo + orchestrator, `WorkersRequestReview`, no repo, no repo + orchestrator, standalone) and asserts that no ban phrase remains, including "AO workers only".
- `workerexec/prompts_test.go`: the same checks for the cloud worker prompt, with and without an orchestrator.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run 'TestBuildSystemPrompt|TestSpawnWorker_IncludesReviewCIAndPlanningInstructions|TestSystemPromptGuard'` passes.
- `go test ./internal/workerexec/ -run 'TestWorkerSystemPrompt|TestBuildInteractiveInjectsSystemPrompt'` passes.
- gofmt, `go vet` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 are clean for `session_manager`. golangci-lint reports nothing in the touched `workerexec` files. Its pre-existing findings elsewhere in that package are unchanged.

title: Codex sessions fail to launch when effort is set to `ultra` (Codex rejects unknown variant)
body:
## Bug

Spawning a Codex session with effort `ultra` kills the agent at launch. Codex refuses its config and exits immediately:

```
Error loading config.toml: unknown variant `ultra`, expected one of `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`
in `model_reasoning_effort`
[process exited]
```

The session page then shows the generic "TERMINAL ENDED — this terminal process ended, but the session is not marked terminated yet" strip with a Resume button. Resuming relaunches with the same bad effort and dies the same way, so the session is stuck dead.

**Source:** Discord DM report (screenshot, 2026-10-06) | **Reported by:** @nikhilachale | **Analyzed against:** `cecf04fe9` (origin/main)
**Confidence:** High — full code path traced below

## Root Cause

AO lets `ultra` through its own validation and passes it verbatim to Codex, which rejects it. Two layers, mismatched vocabularies:

1. **AO's config layer accepts `ultra`** — `backend/internal/domain/agentconfig.go:63` validates `AgentConfig.Mode` against `{"", low, medium, high, ultra}`. That enum exists for **Amp**, whose effort scale is `low|medium|high|ultra` (see `backend/internal/adapters/agent/amp/amp.go:67`). The comment on the field says "currently Amp", but the value is stored agent-agnostically and `Effort` is not validated against the target harness at all.

2. **AO forwards it to Codex unchecked** — `backend/internal/adapters/agent/codex/codex.go:192` (`appendReasoningEffortFlag`) passes any non-empty effort straight through: `-c model_reasoning_effort='ultra'`. Codex only accepts `none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh` and treats the unknown variant as a fatal config error, so the process exits before doing anything.

Net effect: a value that AO's own UI/validation admits (or that a user sets via project config for an Amp project, or copies across projects) bricks every Codex spawn that inherits it, with an error that only appears in the terminal — nothing in the daemon blocks it or surfaces a clear message in the UI.

## Fix

Validate effort against the **target harness's** advertised enum at spawn/restore time:

- Reject (or remap) an effort the target adapter doesn't advertise, with a clear API/UI error: "effort `ultra` is not supported by Codex (valid: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh)".
- The model catalog already knows per-model efforts (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/modelcatalog/claude_provider_test.go:270` shows the shape); the codex adapter should consult it or its own enum before emitting the flag.
- Alternatively, clamp to the harness default when the value isn't advertised — but an explicit error is better than silent substitution.

## Impact

- Any Codex session launched with `ultra` effort (set for Amp, or hand-edited config) exits instantly; Resume loops on the same failure.
- Reporter-facing workaround today: clear the effort override in the composer (the "Use agent effort" option) or set it to a Codex-valid value, then resume.

## Related

- [#6272](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6272) — unified effort picker (frontend-only, merged Oct 5; did not touch the Go validation or codex adapter, so it neither causes nor fixes this)
- [#6236](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/6236) — open PR reworking effort pickers/persistence; worth folding the harness-aware validation into it

title: fix(browser): block downloads until the user allows them
body:
Code changes: +191 -16\
Tests: +334 -5\
Others: +40 -0

## What

Downloads in the Browser panel are blocked until the user allows them from the Downloads list.

- **Blocked by default.** The download is cancelled before any bytes are written and shows up in the Downloads list as "Blocked · from <site>".
- **Explicit allow.** Clicking **Download** on the entry requests the file again and saves it to `~/Downloads` as before. The X dismisses the entry.
- **Single-use approval.** An approval covers one request for that URL and expires after 60 seconds, so a later automatic request is blocked again.

## Why

The Browser panel saved every download Chromium started straight to `~/Downloads`. A link opened by an agent (`ao browser open`), a page popup, or a stray click on a file URL therefore put a file on disk without the user asking for it. The reported case was a Go module zip (`v1.54.0.zip`) landing in Downloads while an agent was working on a PR.

## How

- The gate lives in the `will-download` handler in `frontend/src/main/browser-download-manager.ts`, so it does not depend on what triggered the navigation.
- A blocked request is cancelled with `preventDefault()`, not paused, so nothing touches disk. Allowing it calls `downloadURL` on the originating tab, or on its session if the tab is gone, and the approval matches only a request that starts from the approved URL (`getURLChain()[0]`), not one that merely redirects through it. It is also bound to the session, and to the tab when replayed through one, so another profile or tab requesting the same URL cannot use it.
- A repeat request is merged into an existing blocked row only when it comes from the same session and tab; another profile or tab gets its own row. An allowed download is saved under the filename shown on the approved row.
- Blocked entries have their own cap of 20 (oldest dropped first) and never evict real download history.
- Blocked entries are not written to download history, since they cannot be replayed after a restart. The toolbar's Downloads button shows its indicator dot while one is waiting.

Trade-offs for reviewers:

- A download link the user clicks themselves inside the panel also needs the extra **Download** click. Agent-driven clicks and real clicks are indistinguishable to Chromium, so exempting user gestures would reopen the hole.
- Because an allowed download is re-requested, downloads that come from a form POST or a very short-lived URL may fail after approval and need the link opened again.
- The new strings in the seven non-English locales are machine-written and would benefit from a native review.

## Testing

- `vitest`: `browser-download-manager`, `BrowserDownloadsList`, `useBrowserDownloads`, `BrowserPanel`, `preload`, `browser-view-host`, and the i18n suites pass. New cases cover block-without-saving, allow, single-use approval, redirect matching, redirect-through rejection, approval expiry, session fallback, the blocked-entry cap, and the blocked row UI.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean for `frontend/src`.
- Ran the manager in a real Electron 33 process against a local server that redirects to a zip attachment: navigating wrote nothing, allowing saved the file, navigating again was blocked again.
- Not checked visually inside the full AO desktop app; no screenshot of the blocked row.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: feat(files): send several inline comments in one message
body:
Code changes: +354 -147  
Tests: +394 -50  
Others: +24 -0 (locale strings)

## Summary

File feedback could only hold one inline comment at a time: opening a box on another line discarded the one being written. Now each line or file picked for feedback keeps its own box open, across files, and the comments can be sent one at a time or all together as a single message.

- **Opening:** boxes with text stay open as you move to other lines or files. A box left empty still closes when another is started, so writing a single comment behaves as before.
- **Sending:** a box's send button delivers that comment only and leaves the others open. ⌘/Ctrl+Enter in any box delivers every written comment in one message, in the order they were opened, and so does the bar that appears under the files view once two or more are written ("Discard all · Send all 3"). Whole-file comments are included.
- **Cancelling:** Cancel or Esc closes only that box.
- **Failures:** comments stay open for a retry; any that already reached the agent close.

The comment box itself is unchanged; the bar is the only new element, and it stays hidden while fewer than two comments are written. New strings are in all eight locales.

## Implementation notes

- `useFileAnnotation` holds a list of open comments instead of a single target; `FileAnnotationModel` exposes `targets`, `draftFor`, and per-target `setDraft` / `cancel` / `submit`.
- Every consumer of the model renders one box per open comment: the review list, the focused diff and file views, the legacy diff rows, and the cloud equivalents.
- A box hands its text to the model on blur, and tells it when it starts or stops having text, so the bar counts and sends it without re-rendering the diffs on each keystroke.
- `formatFileAnnotationMessages` batches comments. A single comment produces the same message as before. The daemon caps a message at 4096 characters, so a batch that exceeds it spills into consecutive messages marked "message 1 of 2" rather than dropping comments. The cap is not raised here, since that is an API contract change.

## Behaviour to be aware of

- In the single-file viewer, a comment written on one file stays pending when another file is opened and goes out with the next "Send all". The number on the bar's button is the only sign of it there.
- Switching review scope or commit, or collapsing a file, still discards the comments in that view, as before.

## Tests

- New Playwright spec `e2e/files-multi-feedback.spec.ts`: three comments across two files in real Chromium; one is sent from its own box, the other two with the shortcut as one message. Passes, along with the existing `files-narrow-inspector` spec.
- Unit tests added for the batched formatter, the hook (multi-file send, empty-box closing, single cancel, retry after failure), the comment box, and the review list.
- `npm test` in `frontend`: 6230 passed. Two suites (`src/main/*`) could not load locally because the Electron binary was not installed in the worktree, and one `CreateProjectFlow` test failed in the full run and passed when run alone. Both need confirming in CI.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `frontend`: no errors in frontend sources. Local errors were limited to `packages/product-ui`, whose own dependencies were not installed.

## Known gaps

- Not exercised in the packaged desktop app.
- Cloud-session views are covered by unit tests only.
- Backend, Go lint, and the Docker-based workflow validation were not run locally; this change touches only `frontend/`.

title: fix(chat): stream agent text smoothly with a per-character fade
body:
Code changes: +125 -39  
Tests: +148 -35  
Others: +3 -1

Agent text in chat arrived in blocks. This makes it stream smoothly and fade in as it appears.

## Why it was blocky

`useSmoothStreamingText` flushed its whole backlog 50 ms after each snapshot. Snapshots arrive about every 100 to 150 ms, so every burst was dumped at once and the smoothing never had time to play.

## What changed

- **Smoother drain.** Each update reveals a share of the backlog that decays over about 140 ms, at most about 30 updates a second (each update re-parses the markdown). A hidden tab, or one that skipped frames for over a second, shows the current text at once.
- **Per-character fade.** A small rehype plugin (`rehype-stream-fade.ts`) wraps newly revealed characters in a span that fades in once on mount. The spans are dropped 450 ms after the stream settles, so a finished reply is plain markdown again.
- **Bounds.** The plugin only wraps the last block, leaves a block over 4,000 characters plain, skips code, and leaves emoji as text so the emoji spacing still applies. Any error leaves the reply untouched. Reduced motion gets plain text.

## Behavior change to know about

This replaces the "burst fully visible in about 200 ms" limit from #4947. A very large burst now takes about a second or more to finish revealing. The streaming tests were rewritten for the new pacing, and the responsiveness README notes that its old burst number is superseded.

## Known limits

- When markdown restructures mid-stream (`**bo` becoming bold, a paragraph turning into a list), the affected characters fade a second time.
- I could not run the opt-in burst benchmark (`AO_PERF_BENCH`), so the new reveal time is not measured.

## Validation

Run locally on this branch: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, the full `npx vitest run`, and the renderer smoke suite (`test:e2e:renderer`).

- Two failures are not from this change. `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts` (22 tests) fails locally because `better-sqlite3` is built for a different Node ABI. The `chat-composer-text-selection` e2e test fails the same way on a clean `origin/main`.
- Not run locally: the other CI jobs (Go, mobile, docs build, native macOS helper). Those need to be checked in CI.

title: bug(chat): OpenCode image input is refused through ACP but works through CLI
body:
### What went wrong?

Summary

An image attached in AO’s OpenCode Chat displays correctly, but the agent responds that its model does not support image input.

The same model identifies the same image correctly through direct OpenCode CLI. A direct ACP test also reproduces the refusal, so this has not been isolated to AO.

Agent-collected evidence

Environment

  • AO: development checkout at d7369626b58b5ffd0eb3dba3b54c33bc15063eed
  • OpenCode: 1.18.18
  • Model: omniroute/antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-low
  • OS: macOS
  • Test image: a solid red, 128 × 128 PNG
  • Tested October 7–8, 2026

Reproduction

  1. Open an OpenCode session in AO Chat using the model above.
  2. Attach the red PNG.
  3. Send: “Without using tools, what solid color is the attached image? Reply with the color only.”
  4. Compare the response with direct OpenCode CLI and direct ACP using the same model and image.

Expected

The agent identifies the image as red, consistently with the CLI result.

Actual

Path | Result -- | -- AO Chat | Reports that image input is unsupported Direct OpenCode CLI | Answers “Red” Direct OpenCode ACP | Reports that image input is unsupported

AO’s attachment preview loads correctly, including after reloading the conversation.

The direct ACP session advertises image support during initialization, but responds:

I cannot read the attached image because this model does not support image input.

Verification limits

  • AO Chat reproduced the refusal twice on October 7.
  • Direct CLI and ACP controls reproduced the difference again on October 8.
  • AO’s UI interaction was not repeated on October 8 because its browser debugging connection was unavailable.
  • This was tested with one model and provider configuration.
  • The exact cause remains unconfirmed. The direct ACP reproduction means this is not established as an AO-specific attachment bug.

Related

  • #4427 covers attachment delivery presentation and filename handling. This report concerns the different image-input results between OpenCode CLI and ACP.

title: fix(coder): require an explicit template for BYO Coder + action logging for RCA
body:
## Why

Diagnosing why **ahmad@11x** could not start a BYO-Coder session, two problems surfaced:

1. **No template could be chosen, so every session 422'd.** For a bring-your-own-Coder org, session start requires a concrete Coder template (`coder_template_required`); there is no implicit org-default. But the project-create picker (a) pre-selected an **"Organization workspace"** option (empty `templateId`) and (b) curated the list with a hard-coded `startsWith("ao-devkit")` allowlist, which **hid every BYO org's own templates** (they are not named `ao-*`). Result: the only pickable option was the empty default, the project was created with no template, and the session failed later with an opaque 422. The user deleted-and-retried 4×.
2. **The stuck tenant was nearly impossible to trace.** The access log carried only `method/route/status` — no `org_id`/`user_id` — so you could not filter the log down to one org/user to see what they did.

## What

**Commit 1 — require an explicit coder template (FE).**
- Drop the "Organization workspace" (empty) option; the picker starts unselected ("Select a template").
- Replace the `ao-devkit` allowlist with a minimal **internal-plumbing blocklist** (`ao-azure-vm*`, `ao-linux-docker*`) so a BYO org sees its own templates; exported `visibleCoderTemplates` so the gate and picker share one rule.
- Block project creation until a template is chosen: **Create disabled + hint**, plus a submit-time guard. Only applies when coder is active and templates exist.
- Tests: picker offers no default option; create is gated and the chosen `templateId` is sent on `config.coder`.

**Commit 2 — action logging for RCA (CP).**
- Stamp `org_id` (URL-scoped) on every `HTTP request complete` line → the access log is greppable by tenant.
- Structured action logs with `org_id` + `user_id` + resource id: session created, session rejected (coder-template-required), github project created, project created, provider connection saved (covers harness login and coder connect).
- Logging only; no behavior change.

## Verification

- `go build` + `go test ./internal/httpapi/...` pass.
- FE typecheck clean; `CoderTemplatePicker` + `CreateProjectFlow` suites pass (incl. new gating/no-default tests); i18n coverage + parity pass.

## Notes for review

- The internal-template blocklist is name-based and AO-specific; the cleaner long-term home for "which templates are offerable" is the backend lister (follow-up). This change unblocks BYO without regressing AO's own picker.
- Per-org BYO Coder itself is already implemented on main/prod (#6165); this only fixes the template-selection UX and adds logging — **no provisioning changes**. Worth a staging smoke-test against a real BYO Coder before relying on it in prod.

title: fix(coder): restore codex + cursor-agent harnesses on the dev-kit template
body:
## Problem

Codex (and cursor) sessions on the Coder **dev-kit** template hang at "Preparing your repository and agent." Worker log from an SSH'd workspace:

```
codex harness binary "codex" is unavailable: exec: "codex": executable file not found in $PATH
```

The dev-kit image (`cloud/coder/Sandbox.Dockerfile` -> `ao-coder-workspace:local`) baked only claude-code + claude-agent-acp + opencode. codex and cursor-agent were never installed, so those harnesses had no binary. (`coder-azure-vm` bakes all four, which is why codex works there.)

While verifying the fix, opencode also turned up intermittently missing from fresh dev-kit workspaces, confirming the host-local image is unreliable (known image-pipeline gap), so the startup now guarantees every harness rather than trusting the baked image.

## Fix

Covers all four supported harnesses plus the ChatUI path:

- **`coder/main.tf` startup_script** - install `codex`, `cursor-agent`, and `opencode` at workspace start when the image lacks them, and ensure `claude-agent-acp` (the ChatUI ACP bridge for claude - the only harness whose ACP is a separate npm package; opencode and cursor speak ACP via their own CLIs). Each install is idempotent (skipped when present) and non-fatal (a failed optional install never blocks the workspace). Deployable without an image rebuild because the dev-kit templates reuse the existing approved host-local image.
- **`Sandbox.Dockerfile`** - also bake codex + cursor-agent (versions in lockstep with `scripts/bake-coder-azure-image.sh`) so the next image rebuild carries all four permanently and the startup installs become no-ops.

## Verification

Throwaway dev-kit workspaces, all four resolve on PATH:

```
claude:        2.1.228 (Claude Code)
codex:         codex-cli 0.147.0
cursor-agent:  2026.08.11-e8db854
opencode:      opencode v2.0.24
```

Both templates (`ao-devkit`, `ao-devkit-large`) re-pushed to prod Coder with the startup installs live.

## Scope note

This is a Coder-template change (deployed via `coder templates push`), not a control-plane change - there are zero `cloud/internal` edits. The control plane already supports all four harnesses (registered in `workerexec`, credential types in `httpapi/harness_spec.go`); the only gap was the dev-kit workspace binaries.

title: fix(chat): stop queue flashes, bubble replays and scroll jumps on send
body:
## What users saw

- Send a message to an idle agent and it briefly showed up in the queue dock, then came back to the chat.
- The user bubble played its send animation twice.
- Sending from the bottom of a long chat snapped the view up and left it short of the end.
- Queuing behind a running turn looked like a normal send first, then jumped to the dock.

## Causes and fixes

**Queue flash.** The daemon saves every send as `queued` and moves it to `running` 25 to 130 ms later. A snapshot in that gap made an idle send look queued. I reproduced it: 5 of 5 sends showed a `queued` snapshot. Snapshots (session and review chats) now report the turn being dispatched as `running`. A turn that really waits behind another stays `queued`. The marker is cleared on any send that does not dispatch, so a failed dispatch cannot leave a turn stuck as running.

**Replayed bubble.** The renderer dropped `clientMessageId` when it mapped daemon messages, so the optimistic echo and the daemon row never shared a key and the row remounted. The daemon now returns `clientMessageId` (one optional field in `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts`). The item, group and run keys use it, and the enter animation is tracked by that key.

**Scroll jump.** A new turn in a long chat is measured in steps. For a moment the rendered content still carried the 600px estimate, the prompt spacer was sized from it and collapsed to 0, and the browser clamped `scrollTop`. The scroll handler then read that as the reader leaving and cancelled the glide. The spacer now waits until the rendered height matches the virtualizer total. This bug was already on `main`: I reproduced it with all of my renderer changes reverted.

**Queued sends.** A send made behind a running turn is tagged queued and goes straight to the dock as an inert row (no steer, edit, delete or drag until it has a turn id). It hands over to the real row under the same key.

Smaller changes:
- The draft is hidden while a plain send is in flight and comes back after 3 seconds if the daemon has not answered. The send request has no timeout, so this keeps a stuck send from looking like a lost draft.
- The "Sending" note on the optimistic bubble is gone.
- The send animation rises from 16px below instead of scaling.
- The first send in an empty chat no longer makes the composer jump. The welcome heading used to vanish at once while the dock kept its place, so the composer lost 64 px in one frame (409 to 345) before sliding down. The slide now starts from the composer's own position and the heading fades out in place over 150 ms.
- Two log lines in the controller: one when a send is queued behind a busy controller, one when a turn-completed event is ignored because its provider turn id does not match. I could not reproduce the "queued while idle" report from the busy path, so these are for the next time it happens.

## How I checked it

I drove the real Electron window over CDP and traced each symptom before and after.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Idle send shows a `queued` snapshot | 5 of 5 sends | 0 of 10 sends |
| Scroll after a send from the bottom | view jumps up 222 to 240 px, ends 420 to 438 px short | never moves backwards, ends at the end (gap 0 px) |
| Queued send | chat bubble at 111 ms, dock at 394 ms | dock row at 70 to 80 ms, no chat bubble |
| Message sent mid-turn | queued | still queued |
| Spacer while a long reply streams | n/a | shrinks 400 to 0, view stays pinned |
| Composer top on the first send of an empty chat | 409, then 345 in the next frame, then slides to 711 | 409, then slides smoothly to 711 |

Tests added:
- Go: four tests on the real `Service` that take a snapshot in the gap right after the row is saved as `queued`. They cover an idle send reading `running`, a send behind a running turn staying `queued`, and the marker lifecycle (kept after a good send, ignored for duplicates, cleared on a failed dispatch). A DTO test checks `clientMessageId` is returned. I checked that breaking the overlay or the cleanup makes the right test fail.
- Frontend: echo and durable row share one node, queued send shows in the dock and not the chat, `toSnapshot` keeps `clientMessageId`, the draft hides and comes back on failure and on a stalled send.

`go test` for `service/chat` and `httpd/...` passes. Frontend chat and conversation suites pass (921 tests). `tsc` is clean for `frontend/src`.

## Review notes

Five independent reviews of this diff (daemon concurrency, frontend identity and queue, scroll and composer, API consumers, test quality) found no P0. The two P1s are fixed in this PR: the stuck marker after a failed dispatch, and the hidden draft on a stalled send.

Known and left alone, all cosmetic or narrow:
- A queued message plays its entrance animation when it is queued instead of when it joins the chat.
- Older remote daemons that do not send `clientMessageId` fall back to the old matching and remount once.
- A duplicate-send response can release the echo a moment before the real row is cached.
- With more than one queued message, a collapsed dock hides a just-sent pending row.

Mobile and the `ao` CLI do not use the changed fields. I read both, did not run them.

title: fix(settings): load cloud project settings from the control plane
body:
## Problem

Opening **Project settings** for a cloud project hangs on "Loading project settings…" and surfaces "Unknown project". A customer using bring-your-own Coder reported it, and I reproduced it on the released nightly `0.13.5-nightly.202610072244` (which includes #6401).

The cause: the settings dialog always reads the project from the local daemon (`ProjectSettingsForm` → `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}`). Cloud projects live only in the control plane, so the daemon answers `404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND – "Unknown project"`.

This also left template-less cloud projects (created before #6401) without a visible explanation. Their sessions are rejected with `coder_template_required`, and the one place you'd look at the project wouldn't open.

## Fix

- **`SettingsDialog`** identifies a cloud project the same way task creation already does: no remote host, and the ID appears in `useCloudProjectsQuery`. It then renders a cloud settings view. Only the General section is shown; Agents, Environment and Cues are local-daemon features. While the cloud project list is loading, the dialog shows the loading state instead of falling through to the daemon. The local form is used only for a project the local daemon actually lists. If the cloud lookup fails for any other project, the dialog shows the error with a Retry action instead of a misleading "Unknown project". Local and remote projects are unchanged.
- **New `CloudProjectSettingsForm`**, built from the shared `@aoagents/product-ui` settings rows:
  - Project name and default branch are editable and autosaved via `PATCH /orgs/{orgId}/projects/{projectId}`. It uses the same 650 ms debounce, validation and rail save state as local projects.
  - Type and repository are shown read-only.
  - The **Coder template** is shown read-only, resolved to its display name, plus machine size when set. With no project template, the row shows **"Default template"** (the deployment or org default applies; non-Coder providers need none). It shows a blocking warning only for a bring-your-own-Coder org with no org-default template, the one case the control plane rejects with `coder_template_required`.
- Six new strings, added to all 8 locales.

## Not in scope

- Changing the template of an existing cloud project. The control plane's `PATCH` only accepts `displayName` and `defaultBranch`, so this would need a CP change and deploy. It's left as a follow-up.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- New `CloudProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx` covers:
  - details and the template name
  - the missing-template warning
  - the rename autosave call
  - that an empty branch is not saved
- `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` covers:
  - a cloud project renders the cloud form, with only General
  - the loading state while the cloud list resolves
- Targeted run, `vitest` on Node 24: 4 files, 48/48 pass, i18n parity and literal coverage included.
- Full frontend suite: the only failures are in `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`. They're environmental (the `better-sqlite3` native ABI was built under Node 22, tests ran on Node 24) and unrelated to this change.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Verified in a running app:** a dev Electron build of this branch, signed into production, opened Project settings for a real cloud project (`ao-landing`). Before the fix the same dialog hung on "Loading project settings…". It showed name, type (Cloud project), repository, default branch, Coder template (`ao-azure-vm-staging`) and machine size, with only the General section. Renaming in the UI autosaved to the control plane (confirmed via `GET /projects`), then I reverted it. The missing-template warning is covered by unit tests only.
- Note: staging could not be used. On `main` the CP allows the GitHub App only in production (`cloud/internal/config/config.go:552`), so staging exposes no `/github/*` routes and no cloud project can be created there. That's pre-existing and out of scope.
- If a user is signed into cloud, project settings for local projects briefly show the loading state until the cloud project list resolves. The list is usually already cached by the sidebar.
- Follow-up: let users set or change the Coder template on an existing cloud project (CP `PATCH` plus UI).

### What went wrong?

### What went wrong?

In an OpenCode Chat session, a shell command exiting with code `7` is shown as completed without an exit-code indicator.

The command output is available, and the agent can explain the failure, but the activity card does not show the nonzero result.

title: [Bug]: Kiro preToolUse maps to sticky Input needed with no approval observation path
body:
## Bug

Kiro TUI sessions can show Summary → Activity as **Input needed** for ordinary tool use and keep that status sticky until a turn-boundary-style clear. AO installs Kiro `preToolUse` as `permission-request`, and `StandardDeriveActivityState` maps that to sticky `waiting_input`.

**Related:** parent family bug [#6280](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/issues/6280) (Copilot / Cline / Kiro). Copilot will be fixed separately via observe-hooks . This issue tracks **Kiro-only** follow-up.

**Code-path confidence:** High on current main (hook install + mapping). No separate live TUI recording attached here; behavior follows from the same path called out in #6280.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Kiro TUI session and invoke a tool (interactive approval via Kiro’s permission UI, or an auto/trust path).
2. Observe Activity when AO’s `preToolUse` hook runs (`ao hooks kiro permission-request`).
3. After the tool is allowed / while tools continue, check whether Activity remains **Input needed** until `stop` or the next `userPromptSubmit`.

**Expected:** Input needed only while a human decision is actually pending; clear when work resumes after approval.

**Actual:** Every managed `preToolUse` enters sticky `waiting_input`, including tools that never need a human decision. There is no AO terminal waiting-recovery path for Kiro today.

## Root cause

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/kiro/hooks.go` — `preToolUse` → `permission-request` (`ActivityWaitingInput`).
- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitystate/activitystate.go` — name-only sticky `waiting_input`.
- Managed hooks are `agentSpawn`, `userPromptSubmit`, `preToolUse`, `stop` — no post-tool clear; no typed permission-notification hook like Copilot’s `notification.permission_prompt`.
- No `DetectTerminalActivity` implementation for Kiro.
- Real approvals are owned by Kiro’s `permissions.yaml` / interactive UI (and PreToolUse can block via exit `2`); AO’s install does not expose a Copilot-like ask/allow observe contract.

## Fix direction 

1. Stop mapping `preToolUse` → `permission-request` / `waiting_input` (treat as active / tool-use).
2. Restore real Input needed ,add terminal approval detection, and/or use ACP Chat approval events if/when Kiro Chat is available ([#5604](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/5604)).
3. Remap-only without (2) would hide pending TUI approvals until observation exists — same family tradeoff as closed AO PR #2594.

title: fix(cloud): drain the GitHub webhook queue with workers and drop untracked repos
body:
Code changes: +122 -6  
Tests: +242 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

On production, PR status in cloud sessions could stay **"Status unavailable / Checks unavailable" for ~40 minutes** after AO opened a PR (observed on `Pritom14/BusinessManagement` #3: created 21:02 UTC, first refresh 21:43 UTC).

The webhook was delivered and accepted (HTTP 202) but sat in the queue:

- GitHub sends SCM events for **every repository an installation can see**. An install with "All repositories" delivers push / check_run / status / review traffic for dozens of repos that have no AO project or PR, and every one was queued.
- The queue was drained by **one worker processing at most one delivery per second** (`time.NewTicker(time.Second)` around a single `processNext`). Production received ~1–2 deliveries/s, so the backlog grew and a new PR's events waited behind unrelated traffic.

## Fix

Two changes, cloud SCM only:

1. **Filter before queueing** — `EnqueueVerifiedWebhook` drops SCM events (`push`, `check_run`, `check_suite`, `status`, `pull_request*`) for repositories that no organization routed through the installation tracks: no project on the repo, no recorded pull request in it, and no worker branch refs for it (`GitHubRepositoryTracked`). The receiver acknowledges them with 200 and stores nothing.
   - Installation events (`installation`, `installation_repositories`) always queue.
   - A failed tracking lookup **queues the event anyway**, so a database hiccup can never drop an event that matters.
2. **More workers** — `Run` starts 8 workers that drain the queue back to back and pause (1s) only when it is empty. `ClaimGitHubWebhook` already leases rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and keeps installation events in receipt order, so workers never share a delivery or reorder routing changes.

Not changed: GitHub API usage per event (the same refresh runs, just sooner), migrations, config, frontend, or the local daemon.

## Testing

- New unit tests (`githubapp/webhook_queue_test.go`): untracked repos are dropped for every SCM event type; tracked repos queue; installation events queue without a lookup; a failed lookup still queues; a 24-delivery backlog drains concurrently in ~0.16s (24s with the old loop); an empty queue does not spin.
- New PostgreSQL integration test (`postgres/github_webhook_tracking_test.go`, run with `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL`): a project's repository is tracked; a repository with no project and an unrouted installation are not.
- Full `cloud` `go test ./...` passes. With a real database, two pre-existing `internal/postgres` tests fail identically on unmodified `main` (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestMigrateInterfaceHandoffFromMainVersion`) and are unrelated.
- Live check against a local control plane built from this branch, fresh database, signed with the real GitHub App webhook secret:
  - 40 webhooks for an untracked repo → HTTP 200, **0 queued**
  - 6 webhooks for a tracked repo → queued and **processed within 3s**
  - installation event → queued
  - burst of 150 tracked-repo webhooks → **all processed 0.75s after the first send**, no errors

`gofmt` and `go vet` are clean; `golangci-lint` was not available locally, so CI's lint job is the first lint run.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Refresh a PR immediately after AO opens it, and don't treat the insert-time `observed_at` default as an observation (the false "unavailable" window before the first refresh).
- Coalesce repeated refreshes for the same PR, reuse installation tokens, and back off per installation on GitHub rate-limit headers.

title: fix(agentauth): open Pi's login picker automatically
body:
## Summary
Pi has no `login` subcommand, so Settings → Harness → Log in to Pi launched the bare Pi TUI and held `/login` behind an **Open login** button in the terminal header. Users saw only Pi running in the PTY and no login flow.

This switches Pi to the daemon-side auto-input path Kimi already uses: the auth terminal launches `pi`, and the daemon types `/login` once Pi renders a ready marker:
- Pi's footer context stat `0.0%/` (primary). A fresh Pi session always renders it, with or without a selected model and with `quietStartup` on.
- Pi's startup onboarding line `Pi can explain its own features` (secondary).

If neither marker appears within the 10 s ready wait, the daemon still sends `/login` as long as the terminal is alive (new opt-in `SendInitialInputOnReadyTimeout`, used only by Pi). Pi no longer returns `terminalInput`, so the Open login button doesn't render for Pi. Droid, OMP, Prime Agent, Gemini, and Qwen keep the button flow. Kimi keeps marker-only behavior.

## Changes
- `agentauth/plans.go`: `piLoginPlan()` with `initialInput`, ready states, and the timeout fallback
- `agentauth/service.go`: pass the fallback flag to the terminal opener
- `shellterm`: `MatchInitialInputReadyState` (exported matcher used by the ready loop), an opt-in send-on-timeout fallback that skips exited terminals, and an injectable ready timeout for tests
- Tests:
  - Pi markers matched against captured Pi 0.85.1 screens: default startup, `quietStartup` with and without a model, still loading
  - shellterm fallback: opt-in, default-off, and exited-terminal paths
  - the button-flow service test moved from Pi to Droid

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/service/agentauth/ ./internal/service/shellterm/` passes. On Windows, the Kimi trust test fails on unchanged `main` too (HOME isolation), and it's unrelated.
- Verified end to end against a dev daemon with Pi 0.85.1:
  - default startup, model selected: the login picker opened automatically
  - `quietStartup: true` with a model selected (no header): the login picker opened automatically

## Risks
- Pi accepts typing during startup but ignores Enter until startup finishes, and the markers render slightly before that. AO relies on the runtime's ~300 ms pause before Enter. On a very slow first run, while Pi downloads `fd`/`rg`, `/login` can stay in the editor unsubmitted, and the user presses Enter.

title: fix(agentauth): open Copilot's native /login account picker
body:
Code changes: +146 -1  
Tests: +172 -1  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary
Clicking **Login** for GitHub Copilot ran `copilot login`, which always starts the GitHub.com browser flow. Copilot's account picker (GitHub.com / GitHub Enterprise Cloud `*.ghe.com` / Microsoft Entra) only exists behind `/login` in the interactive TUI, so users on GHE or Entra could not pick their account type.

This follows the same pattern as the Kimi fix (#5651):
- **`agentauth/plans.go`**: the Copilot plan now launches the `copilot` TUI and injects `/login` once the composer footer renders. If slow hook and skill loading delays that footer beyond the bounded readiness wait, AO verifies that the PTY is still alive and sends `/login` through the existing timeout fallback.
- **`adapters/agent/copilot/trust.go`** (new): Copilot's "Confirm folder trust" dialog would swallow the injected input in AO's private auth workspace, so the workspace's symlink-resolved path is added to `trustedFolders` in `$COPILOT_HOME/config.json` (default `~/.copilot/config.json`), which is what Copilot records for "Yes, and remember this folder". The `//` comment header and other keys are preserved, the write is idempotent, and unsupported config shapes are left untouched (Copilot then asks for trust interactively).
- **`shellterm/service.go`**: full-screen TUI readiness checks now fall back to AO's rendered terminal surface and normalize ANSI styling before matching. This is required on the native PTY host, where Copilot renders the visible `/ commands` footer with styling that splits the raw byte sequence.

## Testing
- Manual, isolated Electron PR lab: clicking Copilot Login automatically opened the three-option picker (`GitHub.com`, `GitHub Enterprise Cloud (*.ghe.com)`, and `Your organization (Microsoft Entra)`) in both live PTYs, including after startup exceeded the readiness wait.
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/copilot ./internal/service/agentauth -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/service/shellterm -run 'Test(OpenCommandTerminal|MatchInitialInputReadyState)' -count=1`
- `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.13.2 run --path-mode=abs --timeout=10m` (`0 issues`)
- `go build ./...`

The full `npm run lint` test phase was also attempted locally, but this machine's highly parallel run hit unrelated CLI-probe timeouts plus environment-dependent tmux and installed-Codex protocol conformance failures before reaching the lint phase. The affected packages above pass independently, and the linter passes when run separately; remote CI remains authoritative for the complete suite.

## Notes / risks
- The timeout fallback uses the existing terminal-alive guard, so it does not inject `/login` into a PTY that exited during startup.
- Not addressed here: `copilotConfigAuthStatus` parses `config.json` without stripping Copilot's `//` header, so that auth-status check likely never succeeds and falls back to `gh auth`.

title: fix(chat): stop opening turn-diff files outside the session workspace
body:
Fixes #6422

## Summary
Claude Code reports absolute paths in turn diffs, including files it writes outside the session workspace (for example its auto-memory notes under `~/.claude/projects/…`). Clicking one of those rows in the turn's **Files Changed** card opened a file tab that could never load. The tab showed only "workspace path must be relative".

- **Daemon:** the conversation snapshot now checks each absolute turn-diff path against the session's real workspace root (`Metadata.WorkspacePath`):
  - A path inside the workspace gets a new `workspacePath` field with its workspace-relative form.
  - A path outside it gets `outsideWorkspace: true`.
  - Relative paths, and snapshots where the root is unknown (reviewer chats), are unchanged.
  - Nothing new is persisted, and the daemon's workspace confinement is unchanged.
- **Renderer:**
  - The Files Changed card opens `workspacePath` directly when it's present.
  - Rows flagged `outsideWorkspace` stay readable but aren't offered as a click. They are `aria-disabled` and still focusable, and their tooltip shows the full path plus "Outside this session's workspace".
  - Older daemons and cloud sessions keep the current behaviour.

## Not included (follow-up)
A chat markdown link to an absolute path that isn't in the workspace file list goes through `explicitWorkspaceFilePath` and can still open the same kind of broken tab. That path deliberately accepts link-shaped paths for new files that aren't yet in the catalog (#5119), so changing it is a separate decision. Evidence is on the issue.

## Tests
- `go test ./internal/httpd/controllers/ ./internal/service/chat/`: these cover inside, outside, sibling-prefix and relative paths, and check that the snapshot carries the session's workspace root.
- `vitest` across `components/chat`, `hooks/useConversation` and `lib/turn-file-open-path`: 923 tests pass. New cases check that the relative path opens and that outside rows are inert and show the tooltip.
- Typecheck shows no errors in the touched files.
- **Real Electron app**, run in isolated mode with a daemon built from this branch and driven over CDP. A real Claude Code chat session wrote `/tmp/…` and `notes/inside-note.md`:
  - The snapshot returned `outsideWorkspace: true` and `workspacePath: "notes/inside-note.md"`.
  - Clicking the outside row opened no tab and showed no raw error.
  - Hovering it showed the path and "Outside this session's workspace".
  - Clicking the inside row opened `notes/inside-note.md` with its content.

## Risks
- The prefix check is purely lexical (`filepath.Rel` + `IsLocal`). If a provider reports a path through a symlinked alias of the workspace, the file would be flagged as outside. In that case the row is inert, which is the same result users get today.

title: fix(chat): settle ACP steer method-not-found as refusal
body:
Code changes: +178 -1\
Tests: +160 -0\
Others: +18 -1

## What

Treat ACP `_session/steering` JSON-RPC method-not-found (`-32601`) as a definite provider refusal so steer delivery handles settle as rejected instead of remaining `reserved` / `CHAT_STEER_UNCERTAIN`.

## Why

Fixes #6188.

OpenCode answers steering probes with a received `-32601` response. AO reserved the client delivery handle before dispatch, then classified the wrapped error as uncertain transport failure. Recovery kept replaying uncertainty without settling and without another provider call—correct for real transport ambiguity, wrong for a definite unsupported-extension response.

Analyzed against canonical `main` at `6763832d4e8afe13950ab7e4ed33195fb136e962`. No competing fix PR found.

## How

- In `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/steer.go`, reuse existing `isACPMethodNotFound` and wrap `-32601` in an ACP `providerRefusal` that implements `ChatRefusal()`.
- Leave non-`-32601` CallExtension failures as ordinary errors so the service still returns `ErrSteerDeliveryUncertain` and does not auto-resend.
- Service classification already maps `ChatRefusal()` → `ErrProviderRefused` → durable `RejectSteerDelivery` / `provider_refused`.

Intentional omission: no capability-advertisement rewrite and no rewriting of already-reserved historical uncertain rows without evidence.

## Testing

```bash
cd backend && go build ./...
# BUILD_OK

go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ -run 'TestACPSteerMethodNotFoundIsDefiniteRefusal|TestACPSteerTransportFailureIsNotARefusal|TestACPDriverMapsAdvertisedSteeringOntoAO' -count=1
# ok

go test ./internal/service/chat/ -run 'TestSteerProviderRefusalSettlesAndRecoversWithoutRedispatch|TestSteerTransportFailureStaysUncertain|TestReservedSteerStaysUncertainAcrossRetryAndRestart' -count=1
# ok

go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/ ./internal/service/chat/ -count=1
# ok

cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...
# build succeeded; touched packages ok:
#   ok .../adapters/chatdriver/acp
#   ok .../service/chat
# unrelated env failures observed (tmux/OpenCode binary/e2e/session_manager/codex installed-provider protocol), not caused by this change
```

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: fix(chat): keep the Working row below the newest work of a running turn
body:
Fixes #6426

## What

While a turn is running, the "Working for …" row now sits below the turn's newest work (just above the composer when you're at the bottom). Before, it sat directly under the prompt that opened the turn. Once the turn settles, the "Worked for" row still takes over at the top of the turn, as before.

## Why

#6298 merged the turn's two Working rows into one and put it directly under the opening prompt. In a long turn the view follows the newest work, so that row scrolls out of view. Nothing near the work the user is watching then says the agent is still running (reported on a Claude Code scratchpad session in a long video-render step; see #6426).

## How

`TurnGroup` builds the live row the same way as before, but adds it to the end of the turn body instead of between the opening prompt and the work. The settling row (440 ms spinner fade) stays in the same bottom spot. Startup is unchanged: with no work yet, the setup checklist is in the same place either way.

## Testing

- New `ChatWorkspace` test: in a running turn with tool runs and a progress message, the Working label comes after the prompt, the progress message and the latest tool run. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- Updated the mid-turn steer ordering test, which encoded the old placement.
- `vitest` on `src/renderer/components/chat/`: 868 passed. `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `frontend/src`.
- Real Electron lab (this branch; isolated data under `~/.ao/dev/lab-122`, daemon :3012, driven over CDP) with a Claude Code standalone session. During a ~90 s Bash call, "Working for 20s" showed under the newest "Ran command" row, right above the composer. After the turn settled, "Worked for 1m" folded the work at the top of the turn and the final answer sat below it.

## Known follow-up (not in this PR)

Claude ACP leaves a Bash tool call in `pending` until its first update. The lab's 90 s ping stayed `pending` for its whole run, and standalone-9's render call stayed `pending` for 35 s. `ActivityRun` only counts `running` for its spinner, so a long tool row shows no spinner of its own during that time. With this fix the turn-level Working row covers the gap. Treating `pending` as live inside a running turn could be a separate change.

title: feat(telemetry): report the automation create funnel
body:
Code changes: +64 -9  
Tests: +94 -1  
Others: +38 -1  

## What changed

Automations shipped with no telemetry on any surface. The page reported as route surface `other`, and nothing recorded whether anyone opened the create dialog, completed it, or abandoned it at the empty prompt textarea. There was no way to tell which recurring tasks people actually set up, which is the input for deciding which preset templates to offer.

This adds the create funnel in the renderer, where abandonment is visible: `ao.renderer.automation_create_opened` on dialog open, then `_requested` and `_succeeded` or `_failed` around the mutation. Editing an existing automation emits nothing. The automations route now reports surface `automations`.

Only closed vocabularies leave the machine. The prompt never does: a byte-size band stands in for it, so the promise in `docs/telemetry.md` that prompts are never transmitted is unchanged. The project id goes through the existing hashing sanitizer. `docs/telemetry.md` now discloses automation page visits, the four creation events, the allowed properties, UTF-8 prompt-size bands, and the existing opt-out controls.

Incidental behavior change, called out because it is not pure telemetry: a failed create used to let its rejection escape to the global handler, reporting the same failure a second time as an unhandled renderer exception. The dialog already renders that error, so the escape is dropped in favour of the explicit failed event. The edit path still has this duplication. That is pre-existing and left for its own change.

## How to test

1. `cd frontend && npm ci`
2. `npx vitest run --config vite.renderer.config.ts src/renderer/components/AutomationsView.test.tsx src/renderer/lib/telemetry.test.ts`
3. `npm run typecheck`
4. `npx vite build --config vite.renderer.config.ts`
5. To see the real events, launch with a local sink and the dev opt-in, then create an automation:

```
cd frontend && env AO_PORT=3012 \
  AO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.ao/dev/telemetry-verify/data" \
  AO_RUN_FILE="$HOME/.ao/dev/telemetry-verify/running.json" \
  AO_TELEMETRY_RENDERER=on \
  VITE_AO_POSTHOG_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:9898 \
  npm run dev
```

## Useful code paths

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/AutomationsView.tsx`, the funnel inside `AutomationFormDialog`
- `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts`, the sanitizer cases, the `/automations` route branch, and `automationPromptLengthBucket`

## Proof

Static checks, all run: full renderer suite 405 files / 6504 passed / 7 skipped, exit 0. Type check clean across `frontend/src`. Production renderer build exit 0.

Live run against a real daemon and a real renderer, observed as decompressed HTTP POST bodies leaving posthog-js, with nothing mocked inside the renderer:

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Dialog open emits `opened` with no event properties | Confirmed, context keys only |
| Submit emits `requested` then `succeeded` | Confirmed, 1 ms apart, `{project_id_hash, schedule_preset, prompt_length_bucket}` |
| `project_id_hash` is a real hash | Confirmed, 64 hex, matches `sha256` of the daemon's project id |
| Prompt size band | Confirmed, a 103-byte prompt banded `s` (81-240) |
| No user content on the wire | Confirmed, 0 hits for the display name, prompt text, or raw project id across every request of the session |
| Editing emits nothing | Confirmed, zero events of any name during an edit and save |
| Route surface | Confirmed, `route_viewed` with `surface: automations` |
| Failed create | Confirmed against a genuine daemon `404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`: `failed` fires, no `succeeded`, no `$exception`, dialog stays open with the error |

The automation was really created, not optimistically rendered: `GET /api/v1/automations` returned it with the expected RRULE and next run time. All app state stayed under the isolated `AO_DATA_DIR`; nothing was written to `~/Library/Application Support`.

A fresh-context adversarial review drove the real `captureRendererEvent` with a hostile payload carrying a prompt, display name, RRULE and a filesystem path as the project id. Only the three expected properties reached `posthog.capture`. An unregistered event name carrying a prompt emitted nothing, since the sanitizer has no default case.

That review also caught a test of mine that could not fail: the expected object read its own hash back out of the actual value, so deleting the hashing from the sanitizer kept all 57 tests green. It is rewritten to assert the exact key set and a 64-hex hash, and re-mutating the sanitizer now fails it. It caught a real bug too: the size bands counted UTF-16 units while the daemon's 4096 cap counts bytes, so non-Latin prompts banded two steps low. Now measured with `TextEncoder`, with a non-Latin case in the test.

### Confidence

| Area | Confidence | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| No user content transmitted | High | Wire-level capture plus a hostile-payload probe |
| Funnel fires correctly | High | Driven in the real app, all five paths |
| Unpackaged dev build | High | That is what was run |
| Packaged build gate | Unverified | Gated on `app.isPackaged`, read but not run |
| Delivery to the real PostHog project | Unverified | Host was redirected to a local sink on purpose, so a verification run would not pollute production analytics |

### Not fixed here

`hashedTelemetryID` is an unsalted `sha256` of the project id, and project ids derive from directory names, so a common repo name is recoverable from a dictionary. Pre-existing at `frontend/src/renderer/lib/telemetry.ts:383`, but this change routes project ids from a new surface through it. Worth its own decision.

## Documentation follow-up validation

The follow-up commit changes only `docs/telemetry.md`. Local checks passed with Node 24.21.0: the full frontend suite with 6,505 tests and 6 skipped, frontend and E2E type checks, the docs production build, Cloud client and product UI package checks, and the guarded-navigation browser integration. The lockfile dry-run passed with CI's Node 22.23.2. Both macOS helper architectures compiled, passed architecture verification, and passed the native state tests.

The local macOS renderer smoke run passed 73 tests and failed three: `e2e/chat-agent-switch.spec.ts` and `e2e/chat-interface-refusal.spec.ts` timed out waiting for the Chat region, and `e2e/chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts` reported a collapsed pointer-drag selection. The documentation follow-up changes no frontend code. Docker is unavailable locally, so the pinned Linux Playwright and gitleaks containers were not run locally. The local Mac is arm64 rather than CI's Intel runner. Remote checks provide the CI-environment results.
