title: bug(opencode): 3s version-probe deadline in ResolveBinaryForMajor fails on Windows - blocks all OpenCode launches
body:
﻿## Summary

AO refuses to launch OpenCode on Windows when `opencode --version` cannot answer within a hard-coded **3 second** deadline. Measured on the reporter's machine, the probe takes **7.5-9.1 seconds**, so it has never once succeeded and **every OpenCode session fails to start**, through any entry point (board, Settings, new-project creation, chat, restore).

This is **not** an OpenCode 2 compatibility problem and **not** a version-mismatch problem. The installed CLI is `1.18.35` (major 1), which correctly matches the `opencode` (v1) harness. The defect is purely that the deadline is too short for this platform.

Split out of #6443 (which covers this alongside the Codex launch-argv regression on the same install) so it can be fixed and reviewed independently - the fix is small, and a directly analogous fix already merged for another harness.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| AO version | v0.13.5 (Stable; UI reported "you're on the latest version", checked 2026-10-08 22:18:31 local) |
| `ao --version` | `ao version dev` (packaged install; `ao` is not on PATH - see #5464) |
| OS | Windows 11, x86_64 |
| OpenCode CLI | `1.18.35` at `%APPDATA%\npm\opencode.cmd` (major 1) |
| Harness configured | `opencode` (v1) - a correct major match |
| ConPTY | built-in, no external multiplexer required (per `ao doctor`) |
| Data dir | `%USERPROFILE%\.ao\data` |
| Daemon state during collection | stopped (`ao status` -> `AO daemon: stopped`) |

All collection is daemon-independent and read-only: direct CLI probes, `ao doctor`, and file inspection.

---

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected 2026-10-08 against the install described above.

### 1. Measured probe latency versus the deadline

Three consecutive runs of `opencode --version`:

```
run 1 : exit=0  9.12s   1.18.35
run 2 : exit=0  7.94s   1.18.35
run 3 : exit=0  7.52s   1.18.35
```

For comparison, `codex --version` on the same machine completes in **1.28 s**.

AO allows **3.00 s**, hard-coded at `backend/internal/adapters/agent/opencode/version.go:32` inside `ResolveBinaryForMajor`:

```go
func ResolveBinaryForMajor(ctx context.Context, major int) (string, error) {
	probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	binary, err := ResolveOpenCodeBinary(probeCtx)
	...
	cmd := aoprocess.CommandContext(probeCtx, binary, "--version")
	cmd.WaitDelay = 100 * time.Millisecond
	out, err := cmd.Output()
	if probeCtx.Err() != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("opencode: version probe for %q: %w", binary, probeCtx.Err())
	}
```

The probe is **2.5x-3x over budget** on this machine and cannot succeed. There is no retry and no cached-success path: the doc comment at `version.go:30` states the design deliberately does not cache across attempts.

### 2. AO's own health check reports it

`ao doctor --json` runs without the daemon:

```json
{
  "level": "WARN",
  "section": "Agent harnesses",
  "name": "opencode",
  "message": "opencode resolves to C:\\Users\\ACER\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\opencode.cmd, but `opencode --version` failed: exit status 1"
}
```

Note this surfaces as `exit status 1` rather than a timeout message: the probe context kills the child, and the caller reports the child's exit code. That is why the underlying cause is not obvious from `ao doctor` alone.

### 3. Reproduced end-to-end against the live daemon

An existing project configured with `opencode` as its orchestrator agent:

```
POST /api/v1/orchestrators  {"projectId":"<redacted>"}
409 {"error":"conflict","code":"CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE",
     "message":"spawn <id>: chat controller: chat driver unavailable: persistent ACP host: chat driver unavailable: opencode: version probe for \"C:\\Users\\ACER\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\opencode.cmd\": context deadline exceeded",
     "requestId":"<redacted>/9ponzgVu0K-000253"}
```

The wrapped `context deadline exceeded` originates at `version.go:47` (`probeCtx.Err()`).

### 4. Blast radius: four call sites, three of them fatal

`ResolveBinaryForMajor` is shared by both OpenCode harnesses:

| Call site | Major | Consequence of the 3 s deadline |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode/install.go:8` - `Plugin.ResolveBinary` | 1 | Feeds `readinessCoordinator.checkInstallation` (`backend/internal/service/agent/readiness_coordinator.go:518`); times out there too |
| `opencode/opencode.go:113` - TUI `GetLaunchCommand` | 1 | TUI spawn fails (`ErrSpawnLaunchCommand`) |
| `opencodev2/opencodev2.go:46` - `Plugin.ResolveBinary` | 2 | Same readiness failure for the v2 harness |
| `opencodev2/opencodev2.go:56, 72, 269` | 2 | v2 launch/chat/restore all fail |

**This is a shared-helper defect, not a version-specific one.** Both `opencode` (v1) and `opencode-v2` inherit the identical deadline, so the same fix unblocks both.

---

## Is this an OpenCode 2 issue? No - and here is the distinction that matters

There are two different OpenCode failure modes in AO, and they produce different symptoms. Conflating them will send this fix in the wrong direction.

### Mode A - probe timeout (this issue)

Any major version, whenever `opencode --version` exceeds 3 s.

- Readiness: the installation check times out, so `failedInstallation` yields `AgentInstallationUnknown` with reason `install_check_timeout` (`readiness_coordinator.go:544-545`)
- `AgentInstallationUnknown` is **not** `not_installed`, so `isLaunchableAgent` (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/agent-select-options.ts`) still returns true
- **Symptom: the harness is selectable and always fails.** The picker shows it, often with an "Install unknown" warning, and the user gets a failed spawn.

### Mode B - incompatible major version (a different issue)

When the installed major does not match the selected harness, `version.go:61-68` returns `IncompatibleVersionError`:

```
opencode: selected harness requires OpenCode 1, but "<path>" reports OpenCode 2 (2.x.y); select the matching harness or put OpenCode 1 on PATH
```

Readiness maps that to a hard negative at `readiness_coordinator.go:539-542`:

```go
var incompatibleVersion *opencode.IncompatibleVersionError
if errors.As(err, &incompatibleVersion) {
    return successfulInstallation(attempted, domain.AgentInstallationNotInstalled, domain.AgentReadinessReasonInstallIncompatibleVersion, err.Error()), false
}
```

`AgentInstallationNotInstalled` **is** filtered out by `isLaunchableAgent`, so the frontend removes the harness from the picker entirely (`CreateProjectAgentSheet.tsx` filters non-launchable agents out of the menu while the trigger keeps showing the stored value).

- **Symptom: the harness silently disappears from the dropdown.**

### How to tell them apart

| | Mode A (timeout) | Mode B (incompatible major) |
|---|---|---|
| Harness selectable? | Yes | **No** - filtered from the picker |
| Readiness reason code | `install_check_timeout` | `install_incompatible_version` |
| Installation state | `unknown` | `not_installed` |
| Error string | `context deadline exceeded` | `selected harness requires OpenCode N` |

The reporter's install is in **Mode A**: the harness remained selectable, readiness did not report `not_installed`, and the version string is a correct major-1 match.

### Why Mode A matters more soon

Open PR **#6090** (*"feat: install OpenCode 2 into a private npm prefix"*) indicates OpenCode 2 adoption is imminent. Mode A is version-independent, so users who move to OpenCode 2 will hit the same wall unless the deadline is raised. Fixing the shared helper now prevents a repeat.

### Directly analogous fix already merged

Open PR **#6289** - *"fix(systeminstall): let Cursor's first post-install version probe finish"* - is the same defect class for a different harness: a version probe that cannot complete inside AO's budget. The fix there was to let the probe finish. That is strong precedent for the shape of this fix.

---

## What the evidence supports, and its limits

**Supported**

- `opencode --version` takes 7.5-9.1 s on this machine against a hard-coded 3 s deadline, so `ResolveBinaryForMajor` cannot succeed here.
- OpenCode cannot launch through AO on this machine, reproduced end-to-end via `POST /api/v1/orchestrators` (409 `CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE`, `context deadline exceeded`).
- The defect is in the shared helper, so both the v1 and v2 harnesses are affected. Version is a correct major-1 match, so `IncompatibleVersionError` is not involved.

**Not established**

- Only Windows 11 was measured. Whether 3 s suffices on macOS/Linux is untested - a Node-based CLI on a cold Windows filesystem is plausibly the slow case, but that is an inference, not a measurement.
- The reason the probe takes 7-9 s here (cold Node/Bun startup, npm `.cmd` shim indirection, antivirus scanning, or slow disk) was not isolated. `ResolveBinary` does not record probe latency anywhere, so this had to be measured externally.
- No measurement was taken of how often the probe *would* succeed given a longer budget. A raise to, say, 10 s is very likely sufficient here but was not proven.
- Whether the readiness path's own `installTimeout` (`readinessCoordinator.installTimeout`) exceeds 3 s was not confirmed; it does not matter for this failure because the inner 3 s probe fires first, but the two budgets were not reconciled.
- Not confirmed whether an additional *new-project-specific* rejection occurs via `POST /api/v1/sessions`, which sends an explicit `harness` and therefore runs the readiness gate at `backend/internal/service/session/service.go:337-350` before spawning. The structural difference between the two endpoints is confirmed in code, but whether it produced an additional user-visible failure was not established, because the daemon was stopped and live readiness could not be read. Deliberately left open rather than guessed at.

---

## Suggested direction

Not prescribing a fix, but the evidence points at these separable places.

1. **Raise the probe deadline, and make it non-uniform.** A fixed 3 s is too tight for a Node/Bun CLI on Windows and needlessly generous elsewhere. Prefer a per-platform or configurable budget with a floor well above the observed 9 s worst case, rather than one constant for every OS.
2. **Cache the resolved major across attempts.** `version.go:30` deliberately does not cache because both majors share the executable name - but the *detected major* is a property of the binary, not of the requested harness. Caching the probe result per resolved path (with an explicit invalidation hook, which the Codex adapter already has as `InvalidateBinaryResolution`) would make a slow probe a one-time cost instead of a per-launch tax.
3. **Report the timeout as a timeout.** `ao doctor` surfaces `exit status 1` rather than the `context deadline exceeded` that actually occurred, because the child's exit code wins. Prefer the context error when `probeCtx.Err() != nil`, which the code already checks - the information is being lost in the caller's error selection, not at the probe.
4. **Add a readiness state for "installed but probe inconclusive".** `install_check_timeout` currently collapses to `AgentInstallationUnknown`. A distinct, visibly-provisional state would let the picker show "verifying" instead of "Install unknown", and would stop a slow-but-working harness from looking the same as an absent one.
5. **Fix the `opencode-v2` false negative in `ao doctor`.** The same run reports `opencode-v2 not found in PATH`, although `opencode-v2` resolves the *same* `opencode.cmd` executable via `ResolveBinaryForMajor(ctx, 2)`. The doctor probe evidently looks for a differently-named binary, so the v2 harness always appears absent even when OpenCode is installed. Low severity, but it sends users down the wrong path.

---

## Reproduction

On Windows, from any shell:

```powershell
Measure-Command { & "$env:APPDATA\npm\opencode.cmd" --version }
```

If this exceeds ~3 s, AO cannot launch OpenCode on that machine. No daemon and no AO project are required to observe the underlying cause; `ao doctor --json` surfaces the same condition as an `opencode` WARN without needing one.

title: fix(cloud): make bring-your-own Coder work (arm64, no mounted home, slow startup) and fix composer login UX
body:
## Why

A customer (11x) bringing their own Coder could not run a single AO session. Their first orchestrator on prod (2026-10-08) never got a worker, and AO then stopped their workspace while they were inspecting it. Their template is an EC2 arm64 (Graviton) instance with the home dir on the root filesystem and a ~6 minute startup. The same session surfaced several desktop UX problems in the task composer.

## What was broken (prod logs, session 9347b288)

1. Workspace not ready inside AO's 3 minute window, so AO kept "repairing" it.
2. Bootstrap failed on `configured Coder durable root is not a mounted directory` (hard `mountpoint -q` check) and on PTY EOFs.
3. The control plane only built an amd64 worker; an arm64 workspace would get a binary it cannot run.
4. At the 10 minute ceiling AO stopped the customer's workspace.
5. The desktop orchestrator tab just went blank.

Found while testing this branch end to end on an 11x-like arm64 template:

6. On images with sudoers `Defaults use_pty` (Ubuntu default), `sudo -b` left the worker in a background process group on a pty. The checkpoint `git push` prompted for credentials on /dev/tty, SIGTTIN stopped the whole group, and the worker froze right after connecting (state `T`, no heartbeats), so AO later reported "worker never started" for a healthy session.
7. The git credential helper and `gh` wrapper required `jq`, which BYO images may not have, so every credentialed git operation failed.

## What this PR does

Control plane and worker (`cloud/`):
- Builds `ao-worker` and `ao` for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (`/ao-worker-linux-arm64`, `/ao-linux-arm64` beside the existing paths), serves both, detects the workspace arch and uploads the matching build, and never self-updates a worker to the wrong arch.
- BYO connections no longer require a mounted durable root (`requireMountedDurableRoot`, default false for BYO; AO-hosted Coder unchanged). `durableRoot` defaults to the workspace user's `$HOME`.
- Waits for the Coder agent lifecycle to be `ready` before bootstrapping; PTY EOFs before that retry with backoff and do not count as repair attempts.
- Per-connection `startupTimeoutSeconds` (BYO default 1200) for the ready wait and startup ceiling.
- Never stops or deletes a BYO workspace because of an AO startup failure; the session is parked with an error instead.
- Persists a user-facing `startupError {code, message, at}` (migration 00072), exposes it on the session API, and adds `POST /sessions/{id}/startup-retry`.
- Optional project `coder.workspaceNamePrefix` (workspace becomes `<prefix>-<12 hex>`; default `ao-<id>` unchanged).
- Worker runs under `setsid` (no controlling terminal) and defaults `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` / `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`.
- Credential helper and `gh` wrapper fall back to an exact sed extraction when `jq` is absent.

Desktop:
- Cloud sessions show the startup error with Retry instead of a blank pane.
- Project settings show the Coder template name (UUID secondary) and an editable workspace name prefix; create project flow has the prefix too.
- Composer model-discovery errors get a plain message with Log in, Retry and Details. A successful login clears the stale error automatically (daemon and renderer caches). An expired but renewable Claude login is no longer reported as "Signed out". Cloud projects are not blocked by the laptop's local login (non-blocking note, Start stays enabled).
- Claude model aliases show their version (for example "Opus 5.5").
- AO does not refresh the Claude OAuth token itself: the CLI rotates refresh tokens behind a lock, so a second refresher could invalidate the user's login everywhere.

## Testing

Automated (on this branch):
- `cloud`: gofmt, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` all pass; `GOWORK=off` build of all five binaries passes; image contract verified with x86-64 and aarch64 workers in the control-plane image.
- Postgres-backed tests run against a live Postgres 16: the only failures are 4 tests that fail identically on clean `main`.
- Migration 00072 applies on top of a prod-like (main, v71) database and is re-runnable.
- `backend` agent packages: race tests pass. Frontend typecheck clean; 538 renderer tests, 29 cloud-client and 157 product-ui tests pass; no API drift.

End to end on staging (`ao-cloud-staging-api:209`) against an 11x-like BYO template (`ao-byo-arm64-test`: Azure arm64, home on root fs, blocking ~4 min startup, no jq):
- Orchestrator session: AO waited for the agent to be ready (no not-ready loop, no PTY EOF, no mount error), uploaded the arm64 worker, workspace named `byotest-<id>`, Claude ran (`uname -m` -> `aarch64`), and the session stayed `running` on heartbeats.
- Failure path (startup longer than the 20 minute budget): session parked with `workspace_not_ready` and a human message; the workspace was left running (`customer_owned=True`), and `startup-retry` brought the session back.
- Worker session on the jq-less image: checkpoint push succeeded (`refs/ao/preserved/<session>`), agent answered, worker in its own session with no tty.
- The SIGTTIN freeze was reproduced on the first build (worker in state `T`, no heartbeats) and is gone after the setsid fix.

In the desktop app (dev build of this branch, signed in to staging, driven through the Chrome DevTools protocol):
- Cloud project list, BYO arm64 orchestrator terminal rendered live (`uname -m` -> `aarch64`); typed a message through the app and got the reply back.
- Failed session shows "This session couldn't start" with the message and Retry; Retry returned it to the startup loader; deleting the session removed its Coder workspace.
- Project settings show the Coder template name and UUID (layout fix in fa090ab6a: the name no longer truncates), and the workspace name prefix edits and persists; invalid values are rejected inline.
- Create cloud project shows the template picker and the workspace name prefix field.
- Composer: model labels read Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5. With the local catalog forced into an auth error, a cloud project shows the non-blocking note with Log in / Retry / Details, Create task stays enabled, Details reveals the raw error, and Retry clears the note once discovery recovers.
- Settings > Harness (Local and Cloud tabs) and Settings > Coder render correctly.

## Rollout notes

- Needs `--migrate` (00072). No new env vars or secrets.
- Old workers keep working with the new control plane.
- Existing BYO connections keep their stored `durableRoot`; the mount check no longer applies to them. If a BYO workspace user is not `coder`, set the connection `durableRoot` to `$HOME`.
- AO-hosted Coder keeps prod's 3 minute startup timeout; only BYO sessions get the longer budget.

title: fix(frontend): match native window background to the sidebar while a live page shows
body:
Code changes: +60 -2\
Tests: +3 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

While a live page shows in the Browser tab, the gutters around the centre pane and the macOS drag strip above the sidebar rendered noticeably darker than the rest of the shell. They now match the sidebar fill.

## Why

A live browser page is a native `WebContentsView` behind the transparent shell, so the cascade in `styles.css` clears `.app-shell-root`'s `bg-sidebar` while a page is showing. Anything left unpainted then shows the native window background, which was hard-coded to `#0c0c0e`, darker than the theme's sidebar colour.

- The renderer resolves `--sidebar` to `#rrggbb` (`lib/css-color.ts`) and sends it to main over a new `theme:set-window-background` IPC. `syncNativeWindowBackground` uses it ahead of the hard-coded fallback, which still applies until the renderer reports.
- Main accepts only `#rrggbb`.
- The fixed macOS `titlebar-drag-region` strip also paints its own `bg-sidebar`, so it no longer depends on what is behind it.
- The shell root stays transparent over the live page. Painting it opaque would blank the page, which is what the existing cascade and its test guard against.

title: [Bug]: Side `claude -p` run in the worktree overwrites the session's agent id: live TUI session marked exited, send fails, resume attaches the wrong transcript
body:
### What went wrong?

In a Claude Code **Terminal UI** session ("session A"), AO switched the session's tracked agent id to a short side `claude -p` run instead of the conversation it had launched. Because of that:

1. A helper in our setup starts short `claude -p` runs (Claude Agent SDK, Haiku model, prompt "Summarize this agent result…") in the same worktree while the main agent works. Their transcripts go into the same `~/.claude/projects/<worktree-dir>/` folder as the main conversation, and they are usually newer than the main transcript.
2. AO recorded one of these side runs as the session's agent id (`sessions.agent_session_id`). The main process (`claude --session-id <main>`) stayed the same.
3. When the side run finished, AO marked the whole session `exited` (`claude_activity_facts.parentState = "exited"`). The main `claude` process was still alive and working at that point.
4. `ao send` to the session then failed with `AGENT_EXITED` ("The agent process exited; relaunch it before sending another message").
5. Later AO relaunched the session with `--resume <side-session-id>`. That attached the 32-line summarizer transcript instead of the real conversation, so the conversation disappeared from AO's view.

We saw this clearly in one session and suspect it in a second one.

**Expected:** AO keeps tracking the main conversation (the id it launched with `--session-id`) and ignores side `claude -p` runs in the same worktree. It shouldn't mark the session exited while the launched agent process is still running.

**Possibly related, separate observation (Chat mode, "session B"):** the session lost its controller ("The agent controller stopped… service momentarily unavailable", "controller ended before the turn completed") while its `claude` process kept running. `resume-agent` then refused with `SESSION_TERMINATED`, and we had to run `ao session restore`. This looks like the #5069 / #5790 family; I'm mentioning it here only for context.

Related: #4125 (same identity-overwrite symptom, fixed for Chat mode), #5790 (Exited while the agent is still running).

**Environment**
- AO desktop 0.13.5 (bundled daemon `ao version` prints `dev`), macOS 26.2 (arm64)
- Claude Code 2.1.295
- Frequency: seen once clearly, suspected once more; no reliable repro steps yet

Agent-collected evidence will follow in a separate comment.

title: bug(session): panel still shows "N commits pushed" + "Create PR" after the work is squash-merged from another branch
body:
### Summary

The session panel's git summary (added in #6323) keeps showing "N commits pushed" with an active "Create PR" action even after the session's work is already merged into the default branch — when the merge went through a PR from a different branch (e.g. a PR attached to the session via `claim-pr`) and was squash-merged.

### Actual behavior

Real case (single session):

- The session pushed two commits (+212/−5) to a PR branch `fix/claude-proxy-anthropic-peer` — outside the session branch namespace (`ao/<session-id>/root`), because the PR was already open on that branch and was claimed by the session.
- The PR was merged into `main` with "Squash and merge" (so `main` has the content under a new SHA; the original commits are not ancestors of `main`).
- The session panel still shows "2 commits pushed" and an active "Create PR" button proposing `ao/<session-id>/root → main`.
- Accepting that proposal would create a PR with an **empty diff** (the branch sits on the pre-merge base; content-wise there is nothing left to merge).

### Expected

The panel should recognize that the session branch's content is already in the base and not offer a PR for it:

- "Create PR" hidden or disabled with an "already merged" hint, and
- the commits row not presented as "pushed, awaiting PR" — ideally reflect the attached/claimed PR's state (`merged`), which the panel already renders elsewhere.

### Repro

1. Spawn a session on a project; have it push commits to a PR branch outside the session namespace (or claim an existing PR with `claim-pr`).
2. Merge that PR into the default branch using **Squash and merge**.
3. Open the session panel: "N commits pushed" + "Create PR" (`ao/<session-id>/root → main`) are still offered; the proposed PR has an empty diff.

Also reproduces without `claim-pr` whenever a squash-merge lands the same content from any other branch.

### Notes

- A SHA-ancestry check cannot catch squash merges; a content-level check would (e.g. empty `git diff --stat <base>...<branch>` vs the *current* remote base, not the local base ref).
- Related precedent: #3203 fixed the diff viewer comparing against HEAD instead of merge-base — this looks like the same merge-awareness gap in a different panel.

### Environment

- AO desktop, `ao version dev`, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)
- Harness: Claude Code session; PR attached to the session via `claim-pr`

title: fix(opencode): widen the version-probe budget so OpenCode can launch on Windows
body:
﻿Code changes: +58 -5
Tests: +41 -0
Others: +0 -0

## Problem

`ResolveBinaryForMajor` gave `opencode --version` a hard-coded 3s budget. OpenCode ships as a Node/Bun process and on Windows it is reached through an npm `opencode.cmd` shim, where three consecutive runs measured **7.5-9.1s** on Windows 11. The probe therefore timed out every time, and no OpenCode session could start through any entry point: board, Settings, new-project creation, chat, or restore.

Reproduced end-to-end against a live daemon on v0.13.5:

```
POST /api/v1/orchestrators
409 {"code":"CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE",
     "message":"... opencode: version probe for \"...\\npm\\opencode.cmd\": context deadline exceeded"}
```

This is **not** an OpenCode 2 compatibility problem and not a version mismatch: the reported install was `1.18.35` (major 1), a correct match for the `opencode` harness, so `IncompatibleVersionError` was never involved.

## Two budgets, not one

The readiness coordinator was the *tighter* of the two and is the reason a naive one-line fix would not have worked:

| Budget | Before | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Version probe | 3s | `opencode/version.go` |
| Installation check | **2s** | `readiness_coordinator.go` (`defaultInstallCheckTimeout`) |

`checkInstallation` wraps `ResolveBinary`, so with a 2s coordinator budget around a 3s probe, the coordinator cancelled the probe first and reported every OpenCode install as inconclusive - reason `install_check_timeout`, installation state `unknown`. Because `unknown` is not `not_installed`, `isLaunchableAgent` still returned true, so **the harness stayed selectable in the picker and always failed**. That is exactly the reported symptom.

Raising only the probe budget would have left that path broken. Both are widened here, and a test pins the invariant so the two cannot drift apart again.

## Change

- `opencode/version.go` - probe budget is now platform-aware: 15s on Windows (above the 9.12s worst observed, with margin), unchanged at 3s on POSIX.
- `readiness_coordinator.go` - installation-check budget is now platform-aware: 20s on Windows so it contains the probe, unchanged at 2s on POSIX.

Both budgets stay as they were on POSIX, where no probe was observed to exceed them. A harness that is not installed still fails fast, because `ResolveBinary` reports a missing binary from the PATH lookup without ever running the probe - so this does not slow down the common "not installed" case.

## Tests

- `TestVersionProbeTimeoutCoversMeasuredColdStart` - pins the Windows budget above the measured worst case, and asserts POSIX is unchanged.
- `TestInstallCheckTimeoutContainsOpenCodeProbeBudget` - asserts the coordinator budget strictly contains `opencode.VersionProbeTimeout()`, which is the invariant whose violation caused the bug. This is why `VersionProbeTimeout` is exported.

## Why this also unblocks OpenCode 2

`ResolveBinaryForMajor` is shared: `opencode` calls it with major 1, `opencodev2` with major 2. The defect is therefore version-independent by construction, so OpenCode 2 would hit the identical wall. #6090 (install OpenCode 2 into a private npm prefix) makes v2 adoption imminent; fixing the shared helper now prevents a repeat rather than deferring the same failure to the next harness.

## Validation

Run locally on Windows 11, Go 1.27.1, against `canonical/main` (`d26270f84`):

- `go build ./...` - clean
- `gofmt -l` on both touched packages - clean
- `go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/... ./internal/service/agent/...` - clean
- `go test ./internal/adapters/agent/opencode/... ./internal/adapters/agent/opencodev2/...` - pass
- Both new tests pass individually (`-v` verified)
- `golangci-lint run` (v2.13.2, the version CI pins) on both packages - 27 issues, byte-identical to an unmodified `canonical/main` control worktree; none in the touched files

**Reported gap, not a pass:** `go test ./internal/service/agent/...` reports **84 failures on this branch and exactly 84 on the unmodified control**. Every one is `codex directory ancestor ACL is unsafe` from the Codex account/credential tests, which reject this temp worktree path. The count is unchanged by this PR, so it introduces no new failure, but the package does not go green locally and that suite was not verified green. CI on a normal runner is the real check.

The failure is environmental rather than a missing dependency: the ACL assertions live in `codex_secure_fs_windows.go` and evaluate directory permissions, which differ under `C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Temp\...` versus a normal checkout location.

Fixes #6444

body:

## What

Updates the vulnerable packages that ship inside the desktop app, without any major-version bumps:

- `dompurify` 3.4.14 → 3.4.16 (direct dependency).
- npm `overrides` for `js-yaml` (`^4.3.2`, resolves to 4.3.2) and `katex` (`^0.18.2`, resolves to 0.18.10).

This is the dependency half of #6446. The Electron upgrade is in #6462 because it is independent and riskier.

## Why

`npm audit --omit=dev` in `frontend/` reports 7 vulnerable packages in the production tree, i.e. code bundled into the packaged app (1 critical, 2 high, 1 moderate, 3 low):

| Package | Path | Advisories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seroval 1.5.4 | `@tanstack/router-core` | GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c (critical), GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp (high) |
| js-yaml 4.2.0 | `electron-updater` (parses update metadata) | GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m, GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (high, CPU DoS) |
| brace-expansion | transitive | high, DoS |
| fflate 0.4.8 | `posthog-js` | GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98 (moderate) |
| dompurify 3.4.14 | direct; also `mermaid`, `posthog-js` | GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p, GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2 (low) |
| katex 0.16.47 | `mermaid` | GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (low) |

Most of these are not obviously reachable with attacker-controlled input in AO. They are still cheap to fix and they keep the audit output clean, so real findings stand out.

Refs #6446

## How

- The latest `mermaid` release still declares `katex ^0.16`, so an override is the only non-major way to get the KaTeX fix. Mermaid uses KaTeX only for math in diagrams.
- `js-yaml` is overridden because `electron-updater` pins an older range.
- Lockfiles were regenerated with npm 11 (the CI runtime) and then normalised with npm 10.9.8 (Node 22.23.2), so the self-hosted `npm ci --dry-run` compatibility check passes. npm 11's `audit fix` alone drops the optional peer entry `@pierre/trees/node_modules/@pierre/theme`, which npm 10 then reports as missing.
- The remaining `frontend/` findings (40 with dev dependencies) are build-time only: the Electron Forge toolchain (`tar`, `tmp`, `@electron/rebuild`, ...). Fixing them needs Forge 8, which is out of scope here.

title: chore(electron): upgrade Electron 33 (end-of-life) to 44 and enable fuses
body:
Code changes: +20 -9\
Tests: +17 -1\
Others: +105 -65 (forge.config.ts, package.json, lockfile)

## What

- Upgrades Electron from 33.4.11 to 44.7.0 and adapts the code to the breaking changes that affect AO.
- Enables Electron fuses on the packaged binary through `@electron-forge/plugin-fuses`.

Both changes are in one PR because the fuses act on the packaged Electron binary and were validated together with Electron 44. They are separate commits and can be split if you prefer. The dependency fixes from #6446 are in #6461.

## Why

**Electron 33 is end-of-life.** The released app (checked in the v0.13.5 `.deb`) ships Electron 33.4.11. Electron 33 reached end-of-life on 2025-04-28 and no longer receives Chromium or Node security fixes. `npm audit` lists 38 advisories against 33.4.11 (11 high). AO renders arbitrary third-party pages in its built-in browser while the same app has access to the user's repositories, tokens and agent sessions, so an outdated Chromium is the main risk here.

One advisory applies directly to how the renderer is served: [GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw](https://github.com/electron/electron/security/advisories/GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw). `app://` is registered with `supportFetchAPI: true` and without `corsEnabled`. On affected versions, a page from another origin in the same session can `fetch()` `app://` URLs and read the response. I reproduced this with a minimal Electron app: on 33.4.11 a page on `http://127.0.0.1` reads the body; on 44.7.0 the request is blocked and the protocol handler is never called. It is fixed by the upgrade itself; adding `corsEnabled: true` would have the opposite effect.

**Fuses are at their permissive defaults.** `npx @electron/fuses read` on the v0.13.5 binary shows `RunAsNode`, `EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable` and `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` enabled, and ASAR integrity validation disabled. `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 agent-orchestrator -e ...` turns the app into a general-purpose Node.js interpreter, so other local code can run under the app's identity and inherit OS permissions granted to it (for example macOS privacy permissions or Keychain access).

Refs #6446

## How

Electron 44.7.0 (newest supported major, EOL 2027-03-02):

- `electron`: `^33.0.0` → `^44.7.0`.
- Clipboard (Electron 44 moved to an async, W3C-style API):
  - `clipboard.writeText(text, "selection")` → `clipboard.selection.writeText(text)`; both writes are awaited.
  - `clipboard.writeImage()` was removed. `browser-view-host.ts` keeps its narrow `writeImage(image)` dependency, and `main.ts` adapts it to `clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({ "image/png": Blob })])`, so the existing unit-test fakes still work.
- `app.dock` is optional in the Electron 44 types: `app.dock?.setIcon()`.
- Removed the `allowScripts` entry for `electron@33.4.11`. Since Electron 42 the npm package has no postinstall script.
- Refreshed `node-abi` in the lockfile so `@electron/rebuild` (the `prePackage` rebuild of `better-sqlite3`) recognises Electron 44. Without it, `electron-forge package` fails with "Could not detect abi for version 44.7.0".
- Browser postcondition integration fixture: Electron 44 rejects `webContents.capturePage()` with `UnknownVizError` until a view has produced its first frame (Electron 33 resolved an empty image). The fixture's `snapshot` step now retries briefly until it gets a non-empty frame. In the app, `capturePageImage` already treats a rejection like an empty frame; `captureScreenshotFallback` surfaces it as an error, as it does for other capture failures.
- Other breaking changes from 34 to 44 were checked against the code (`clearStorageData` quotas, `plugin-crashed`, `getBitmap`, `showHiddenFiles`, `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT`, renderer clipboard access, ...) and have no usages. Still-working deprecations (positional `console-message` arguments, `webContents.canGoBack`/`canGoForward`) are left for a follow-up.

Fuses (`@electron-forge/plugin-fuses` 7.11.2, matching the rest of Forge, and `@electron/fuses` 1.8.0):

| Fuse | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RunAsNode` | off |
| `EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable` | on (left at default: with it off, Electron unsets `NODE_OPTIONS`, so the daemon, agents and terminals the app spawns would lose a user's `NODE_OPTIONS`; disabling it needs its own change) |
| `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` | off |
| `EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` | on |
| `OnlyLoadAppFromAsar` | on |
| `GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges` | off |

AO does not use `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `--inspect`, `child_process.fork` or `utilityProcess` (checked with `git grep`), and the ACP runtime ships its own Node binary. `electron-forge start` and the Playwright E2E use the unfused `node_modules/electron` binary, so development is not affected. For ad-hoc-signed macOS arm64 builds the Forge plugin re-signs the binary after flipping fuses.

Areas worth a reviewer's attention: the macOS signing/notarization and Windows build pipelines with ASAR integrity enabled, and the Squirrel.Mac/NSIS update path to an Electron 44 build.

## Testing

Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, following `.github/workflows/frontend.yml`:

- `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run` on Node 22.23.2 / npm 10.9.8 and `npm ci` on Node 24.
- `packages/cloud-client` and `packages/product-ui` checks, docs build, `typecheck`, `typecheck:e2e`.
- Full `vitest run`: 6660 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.
- `test:browser-postcondition-integration`: passes on Electron 44 (3 consecutive runs). The fixture change also passes on Electron 33.
- `electron-forge package`: `better-sqlite3` rebuilds for Electron 44; the packaged binary reports Electron 44.7.0 and `@electron/fuses read` shows the values above. `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` no longer drops into Node.
- Earlier, on a slightly older `main`: deb maker, and an app launch under Xvfb (home screen renders and the bundled daemon starts).

macOS arm64: the same patch series, on a slightly older `main`, was built with `electron-forge package` (ad-hoc signed), installed over 0.13.4 and has been in daily use with an existing `~/.ao`: projects, sessions, agent runs, hooks and the built-in browser work, and existing data was intact after the database migrations. Electron 44.7.0 and the fuse values were confirmed on the installed app. The full test suite was not run on macOS.

Not tested: Windows; notarized macOS builds; the auto-update path from a 33-based release to a 44-based one; the renderer Playwright smoke suite (left to CI); copying a screenshot to the clipboard through the UI.

## Checklist

title: fix(chat): keep Claude awake during autonomous background-task cycles
body:
## What

Claude Chat sessions are no longer hibernated while Claude Code is working on its own after an AO turn ends, for example while it answers a finished background task's `<task-notification>`.

Part of #6460.

## Why

In #6460 a Claude worker was hibernated at 08:40:19, about 5 minutes after its last AO turn completed, while it was still running commands that a background task's notification had started. On wake, the native transcript tail came back as `recovered` turns (`<task-notification>` XML, `[Request interrupted by user]`).

Root cause: for Claude, `HibernateChat` relies on the bridge's `_ao/session/can_hibernate` (`patchClaudeHibernationCheck`), which only refuses while `liveBackgroundTasks` holds an un-ended task. A notification-driven cycle is invisible to every other guard: AO has no turn for it, session activity stays `idle`, and the task that finished has already been removed from `liveBackgroundTasks`. Between tool calls (model thinking, short foreground commands) the registry is empty and the check returns `canHibernate: true` mid-cycle.

Reproduced with the bundled SDK (0.3.232) and Claude Code 2.1.295: after the AO turn's result and `idle`, a `task_notification` is followed by `session_state_changed: running` and `idle` again only when the autonomous cycle ends. The live-task registry is empty for most of that window.

## How

The patched `can_hibernate` handler also requires the adapter's `session.lastSessionState` (the SDK's last `session_state_changed`, which the pinned adapter always enables via `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1`) to be `idle`, or never reported. `running` and `requires_action` keep the provider awake. The packaging tripwire now also requires the `lastSessionState` assignment anchor, so an adapter bump that drops it fails the build instead of reopening this hole.

Failure mode if an `idle` event were ever lost: the session simply stays awake (the pre-hibernation behaviour). No retries or auto-resume are added.

## Overlap

- #6217 stops replaying Claude task notifications as recovered user turns. That covers the second symptom in #6460 (raw XML shown as a user message), so this PR doesn't touch replay. `[Request interrupted by user]` appears only because the agent was stopped mid-cycle, which this PR prevents.
- #6270 / #6299 are about turn settlement after background-task cycles, not hibernation; this change doesn't touch those adapter paths. The patches compose: this one adds a `can_hibernate` registration, #6270 patches the consumer.

## Not in scope

- A pending Claude `ScheduleWakeup`/cron while the SDK is otherwise idle still isn't visible to the bridge, so a session with only a scheduled wakeup can still hibernate and lose it. The #6460 evidence shows the agent mid-work at hibernation time, which this fixes. The wakeup case needs a separate signal and is left as a follow-up.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.test.mjs`: 14 passed. The extended `patchClaudeHibernationCheck` test runs the patched handler: `running` and `requires_action` refuse, `idle` allows. **It fails on `main`** (`expected { canHibernate: true } to deeply equal { canHibernate: false }`).
- Applied the patch to the real pinned `claude-agent-acp` 0.70.0 `acp-agent.js`: it applies and passes `node --check`.
- **ACP-level probe** against the real adapter and Claude Code (background `sleep 8`, then on notification a foreground `sleep 6`), polling `_ao/session/can_hibernate` every second: unpatched returns `true` while the autonomous cycle runs. Patched returns `false` for the whole cycle and `true` once it ends.
- **Real dev Electron app** (isolated data, hibernation enabled, Claude Chat worker, no open view; prompt: start a background task, end the turn, then on notification run 30 sequential `sleep 2` foreground commands):
  - Unpatched bridge: hibernated mid-cycle twice (stopped at step 11 and step 13 of 30). The second run's native transcript ends with `[Request interrupted by user]`, the same as the issue.
  - Patched bridge: `can_hibernate` saw `state=running tasks=[]` at both sweeps during the cycle and refused. All 30 steps and the final reply completed, and the session then hibernated on the next sweep (`state=idle`).

title: perf(terminal): WebGL past 16 terminals, batched output frames, faster terminal open
body:
## Summary

Terminal performance pass. Each change was profiled first and then measured A/B against `main` (d26270f84) on the same machine and the same seed data.

1. **WebGL contexts stay under Chromium's cap** (`fix`). Chromium keeps at most 16 live WebGL contexts per renderer and kills the oldest beyond that. Every cached terminal held a context forever, and a lost context was never re-created. As a result, older terminals stayed stuck on the slow DOM renderer once you had about 16 open.
   - A small pool (`lib/terminal-webgl-pool.ts`) keeps WebGL for the 8 most recently shown terminals.
   - It parks older hidden terminals on the DOM renderer.
   - A terminal gets a fresh context when it is shown again, including after a real context loss.
2. **Streaming output leaves the daemon as a few large frames.** The mux writer sent every PTY read as its own WebSocket message. `seq 1 100000` reached the renderer as about 2,300 messages, each costing an event, a JSON parse and a base64 decode on the thread that also parses and draws the terminal.
   - A frame queued after a quiet period is still written immediately, so keystroke echo is never delayed.
   - While output keeps streaming, writes are spaced 4 ms apart, so queued output merges into fewer frames.
3. **The scrollbar follows scrolling once per frame.** xterm fires a scroll event per line feed, so the overlay scrollbar's reveal ran 100,000 times per `seq 1 100000` (about 9 ms of renderer time).
4. **A new terminal's create request goes out before its tab renders.** There were three causes:
   - The click's state updates render synchronously in a microtask, so the POST queued behind the optimistic tab's render.
   - The shared API client rebased every request from its placeholder base URL by buffering the body asynchronously. It now builds requests against the daemon's current address. A request built before the address changed is still rebased.
   - The list refetch after a create also ran twice. Removed the duplicate.
5. **Unchanged shell tabs skip session-view re-renders.** Shell tabs are now memoized with stable handlers.

## Results

All numbers are from the same machine on the same day, `main` (d26270f84) against this PR, each build on fresh copies of the same seed data.

**Screen capture** (real keystrokes, ScreenCaptureKit frames, medians). The command is typed inside the timed window, so typing time adds the same amount to both builds:

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `seq 1 100000` until fully drawn | 238 ms | 227 ms |
| Full-screen redraw ×200 | 670 ms | 635 ms |
| Typing lag | 19.5 ms | 20.2 ms (no change) |
| Open → prompt | 206 ms | 195 ms |
| Close | 57.5 ms | 57.9 ms (no change) |

**In-app** (CPU profiler, debugger network tracking off, 5 runs each):

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| WebSocket messages for `seq 1 100000` | ~2,300 | ~24 |
| First → last xterm parse of that output | ~136 ms | ~95 ms |
| Renderer CPU during that run (JS + native) | ~123 ms | ~90 ms |
| Create request sent after the "New terminal" click | ~19 ms | ~1 ms |
| WebGL contexts lost with ~27 terminals open | 22 | 0 |

An earlier version of this description reported ~256 → ~100 ms for `seq` delivery. That came from timestamping every WebSocket frame over CDP, whose per-event overhead inflated `main`'s ~2,300-frame run. The numbers above replace it.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/terminal/... ./internal/adapters/runtime/conpty/...` passes, `-race` on `internal/terminal`. Added `TestWriteLoopPacesBurstsButNotIsolatedFrames`.
- `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean. `golangci-lint` isn't installed locally, so CI will run it.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- The full renderer `vitest` run passes (6,642 tests), apart from 23 `src/main` failures this PR doesn't touch:
  - 22 are `better-sqlite3` built for Electron's ABI locally.
  - 1 is a timeout that passes when run alone.
- New tests: the WebGL pool, the scrollbar following scrolling once per frame, and the API client calling `fetch` in the same task.
- Terminal Playwright specs show identical results on `main` and this branch locally (4 pass, 8 fail on both because of the local dev:web environment).

## Risks

- **Burst pacing** can delay output that arrives within 4 ms of the previous write by up to 4 ms. An isolated chunk, such as a keystroke's echo, is unaffected.
- **API client:** the local client now stamps the current daemon base URL on every request, which affects every API call. Tests that spy on `apiClient` methods are unaffected because the methods are plain properties.
- **WebGL pool:** a terminal shown after being parked rebuilds its WebGL renderer on activation. In testing this caused no long tasks, and tab switches stayed around 67 ms either way.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Faster open needs a design decision.** Creating a shell waits for the daemon to start a pty-host process (17–50 ms). The service deliberately spawns the runtime before writing the row and issues a per-shell preview capability during that launch window. A pre-warmed host or asynchronous spawn would change that contract, so it should be decided separately.
- **Binary WebSocket frames:** after the pacing change, base64 and JSON costs about 2–5 ms per 1 MB, so the remaining win is small.
- **Ghostty renderer:** tracked in #6238.
- **Browser runtime link reconnect loop:** if the daemon rejects the handshake (for example a token mismatch after the app restarts against a surviving daemon), the client resets its backoff on TCP connect, so it reconnects every 200 ms. That loop re-renders the whole session view about 10 times a second. Found while profiling; not fixed here.

title: Browser runtime link reconnects every 200 ms when the daemon rejects its handshake, re-rendering SessionView ~10x/s
body:
## Problem

When the daemon rejects the desktop app's browser runtime link handshake, the app reconnects every 200 ms forever. Each attempt flips `browserRuntimeConnected` from true to false. That state lives in `useBrowserView`, which is called from `SessionView`, so the whole session view re-renders about 10 times a second while the app is idle. That is roughly 120 ms of React work every 2.5 s, around 5% of a CPU core, and it competes with terminal output and typing.

## Cause

`frontend/src/main/browser-runtime-link.ts`:
- On TCP `connect`, the client calls `setConnected(true)` and resets `backoff = BACKOFF_INIT_MS` (200 ms), then sends `hello`.
- The daemon (`backend/internal/browserruntime/broker.go`) closes the connection when the hello is invalid, for example on a token mismatch.
- The close tears the link down, which calls `setConnected(false)` and `scheduleReconnect()` with the backoff that was just reset to 200 ms.

The result is a connect/close loop at about 5 Hz with no backoff growth. Every state change is broadcast as `browser:runtimeState` to the renderer.

## Repro

1. Start the dev Electron app with an isolated data dir.
2. Kill only the Electron process, so the daemon survives (`ppid` 1), then relaunch the app. The new app generates a new `browserRuntimeToken`, but it adopts the surviving daemon, which still holds the old token.
3. `/tmp/<log>` fills with `browser-runtime-link: connected` (about 2,800 lines in a few minutes).
4. A React commit hook shows about 20 commits a second while idle, with `SessionView` re-rendering because `useBrowserView`'s `browserRuntimeConnected` toggles.

I found this while profiling terminal performance for #6465. After a clean restart (daemon and app together), idle renderer work drops from ~120 ms to ~3 ms per 2.5 s.

## Suggested fix

- Only treat the link as connected, and reset the backoff, once the daemon has accepted the hello. Alternatively, reset the backoff only after the connection has stayed up for some time.
- Consider surfacing a persistent handshake rejection as a visible error instead of retrying silently.
- Separately, `browserRuntimeConnected` should not re-render the whole `SessionView` when the browser panel isn't shown.

title: fix(claude): don't adopt another data dir's transcript when an AO session id is reused
body:
## Problem
A new orchestrator replayed an unrelated prompt from an old conversation ("This turn was recovered from an earlier session").

Claude's legacy session id is `uuidv5(AO session id)`, but Claude keeps every transcript in one global config dir. When a second or wiped data dir reuses an id (`flash-1`), the id maps onto the old transcript, and `--session-id` then continued it. The chat host was launched with `--resume=<old uuid>` and the old turn was imported.

## Fix
`GetLaunchCommand` checks, on a fresh launch with no caller-assigned id, whether the derived id already has a transcript. If so it uses a new random id; hooks capture whichever id Claude ends up with.

## Scope
Restore of pre-hook sessions still falls back to the derived id; that path is unchanged.

## Test
`go test ./internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/ ./pkg/agentruntime/`; new test covers the reused-id case.

title: [Bug]: Renamed orchestrator name is not reflected in the UI
body:
### What went wrong?

When an orchestrator is renamed, the operation succeeds, but the updated name is not reflected in the UI. The orchestrator continues to display its previous name, making it unclear whether the rename was successful.

Expected behavior: After a successful rename, the new orchestrator name should immediately appear in the UI without requiring a page refresh.

Actual behavior: The orchestrator is successfully renamed, but the UI continues to display the old name.

Possible cause: The frontend state or cache is not updated after the rename operation completes.

Suggested fix: Update the local state/cache with the new orchestrator name after a successful response, or refetch the updated orchestrator to keep the UI synchronized with the backend.

## Summary

Adds a project-scoped session switcher, rebased onto the keyboard-shortcut catalog from #6531.

- Hold Ctrl and press ` (backquote) on every platform, including macOS. Shift moves backward. Release Ctrl to open the highlighted session.
- Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab stay the in-session tab shortcuts (chat, reviewer, terminal) on every platform.
- Ctrl+` was also Toggle terminal, and Ctrl+Shift+` was the Windows new-terminal chord that still works while a terminal is focused. Those moved so both features remain: Toggle terminal is Cmd+J on macOS and Ctrl+J on Windows/Linux. A new terminal while one is focused on Windows/Linux is Ctrl+Shift+J. Ctrl+T is unchanged.
- The first press opens a vertical list and highlights the current session. It does not advance. On the project board, that highlight is the live orchestrator.
- Further presses cycle. Releasing Ctrl opens the highlighted session.
- Escape dismisses the list and stays on the current session. The later modifier release does not navigate. If the window blurs before that release, the cancelled gesture is cleared so the next chord opens the switcher again.
- Losing the window also dismisses without navigating.
- Scope is the current project, including a remote host or cloud project open in the shell. Other projects and the scratchpad are not included.
- The live orchestrator is always first. Workers use the sidebar rule: not terminated, ordered by last interaction, then last user message, then creation. Manual sidebar drag order is not used.
- At most seven workers. If the current worker is outside that seven, the list is that worker plus the six most recently active, still in activity order. The orchestrator does not consume a worker slot.
- The list is frozen while it is open. A session that becomes ineligible before release is not opened. A project change closes the list without navigating.
- The orchestrator row title is Orchestrator. Selected row text stays white.
- Commit uses the same navigation as a sidebar row, a kanban card, and a canonical session link (`useNavigateToSession`), including the remote host id. A worker open records the same manual-open identity as the sidebar.

The chord is taken in the main process, including when focus is in xterm, the chat composer, or the embedded browser. The popup does not move DOM focus. While it is open it marks itself as a native browser overlay so the shell paints above the browser view.

Commit happens only when Ctrl itself comes up, including a Control keyUp whose ctrl flag is still true. The backquote keyup is not a commit. With Shift held, Electron reports key "~" and code Backquote, and that still steps backward.

Shortcut conflict search prefers the fixed switcher over an earlier customizable row.

## Tests

- Selection cap, activity order, orchestrator precedence, cancel, and vanished-session commit.
- Ctrl+Tab still sends next-tab on macOS and on Windows/Linux. Ctrl+` steps the switcher. Alt+Tab and Option+Tab do not.
- Release order: backquote then Ctrl, and Ctrl then backquote, each commit once. Backquote and Shift keyup while Ctrl is held do not commit.
- Escape followed by blur, then a fresh Ctrl+`, opens the switcher again.
- Popup render: initial highlight, cycle, release, escape, orchestrator label, and no focus move.
- Frontend `tsc --noEmit` and the shortcut, preload, switcher, and keyboard-help vitest files passed locally. No live Electron pass.

## Risks

- Sidebar drag order is intentionally not followed.

title: feat(cloud): Freestyle sandbox provider and Stripe billing for AO Cloud
body:
Code changes: +5454 -180
Tests: +3528 -6
Others: +419 -8 (i18n strings) ## Summary Adds [Freestyle](https://freestyle.sh) as an AO Cloud sandbox provider for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions, built for fast session start and for wakes that keep the running agent alive. **Provider and startup** - Freestyle VMs boot from per-harness snapshots (`publish-freestyle-snapshot.sh` bakes Claude Code, Codex and Cursor images and records them in the deployment secret). - Each repository gets a prepared snapshot with the repo already cloned, built in a throwaway VM so no session credentials or conversation are captured. Sessions boot from it and only `git fetch`. - Snapshots are keyed by GitHub repository id, shared by every project on that repository, and kept when a project is deleted; a collector removes snapshots unused for 7 days. A snapshot is only used while the project still names the `owner/name` it was cloned from, because the worker rejects a mismatched origin. - Startup waits removed: the first heartbeat, transcript, credential and checkout grant run beside startup instead of in sequence; the reconciler is woken through `pg_notify`; the control plane holds an agent terminal ticket request until the terminal is live, instead of the browser polling 409s. **Wake keeps the agent running** - On Freestyle the agent runs under `dtach`, so pausing and resuming the VM (memory included) and restarting the worker re-attaches to the same agent process instead of starting a new one. A Chat handoff still stops it. **Deployment and config** - Hosted environments accept `freestyle` as a sandbox provider; migration 00073 extends the existing provider constraint rather than replacing it. - Staging and production scripts, task-definition rendering and hosted-settings validation carry the Freestyle secret. **Frontend** - The cloud startup loader stays until the terminal has content, removing the flash of an empty pane between "connected" and the first output. **Billing (Stripe)** - AO Cloud is a paid feature. Plans and their limits are Stripe product metadata (`ao_plan`, `ao_max_active_sandboxes`, `ao_orchestrator_slots`, `ao_window_hours`, `ao_window_session_hours`, `ao_weekly_session_hours`, `ao_manual_resets_per_month`), cached on the organization by a signed, idempotent webhook that re-reads the subscription from Stripe. - Session creation checks the plan inside the transaction that already locks the organization: one reserved orchestrator slot, the rest for workers (including orchestrator-spawned sessions), an entitled subscription (active, trialing, or past_due within 7 days), and usage under a rolling 5-hour window and a weekly limit. - Usage is a ledger of running session-minutes. The weekly window resets automatically; an admin may reset it manually once per billing period. Over-limit organizations cannot start or wake sessions, and running sessions pause between turns. - Settings gains a Billing page: plans priced from Stripe, Checkout and Customer Portal in the system browser, usage meters, slots in use, and the manual reset. - Organizations with plan `internal`, or created before `AO_CLOUD_BILLING_EXEMPT_ORGS_CREATED_BEFORE`, are exempt. Billing is off unless `AO_CLOUD_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is set; staging reads `ao-cloud/staging/stripe` (a Stripe sandbox). - Idle pause counts terminal input and a presence heartbeat from visible sessions, and its default drops from 1h to 15m. ## Measured (staging, eu-north-1) | Session | Created → terminal ready | |---|---| | Large repo, first session (full clone) | ~9.6 s | | Same repo, from the repository snapshot | **4.0 s** | | VM create from snapshot | 0.5–0.6 s | The three latest commits (ticket long-poll, checkout-grant prefetch, per-repository snapshots) are not yet measured on staging; the expected saving is ~0.3–0.8 s per session, and a deleted-and-re-added repository starts at ~4 s instead of a full clone. ## Migrations - `00073` adds `freestyle` to the sandbox provider constraint. - `00074` / `00076` project snapshot table, re-keyed by repository in `00076`. `00076` carries existing rows over; the migration role is subject to forced RLS, so it lifts `FORCE` for its own statements and restores it before commit (covered by a test that runs the migration as a non-bypass role and fails without that step). - `00075` notifies the reconciler when a sandbox is asked to run. - `00077` adds billing: organization subscription columns, the Stripe customer map and processed events, the usage ledger, manual resets, and `last_interaction_at` for idle pause. ## Testing - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` in `cloud/`: all pass. - PostgreSQL integration tests for the new store code and migration pass against Postgres 17. - Frontend: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`, and the touched test files pass. **Known local failures, not from this branch** (identical on unmodified `main` in the same environment): - `go test ./internal/postgres` with a database: `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`. - `npx vitest run`: 43 failures in `auto-updater`, `browser-profile-import`, `ChatWorkspace`, `ContextMeter`. **Not run locally:** the `docker build --target expat-build` CI step and the renderer smoke job; relying on CI for those. **Not yet exercised end to end:** Codex and Cursor sessions on Freestyle (snapshots are baked and selected per harness, but only Claude Code was run on staging). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(session): switch Chat and Terminal interfaces instantly
body:
## What changes for the user

Switching an orchestrator between Chat and Terminal now shows the destination on the click itself. The daemon still does the handoff behind it.

- **Terminal to Chat.** The chat page appears at once with the composer docked at the bottom (or centered if the chat has no messages yet), the startup shimmer and a placeholder that follows the controller. Messages fade in once they load. The old transcript no longer flashes, hides and reappears.
- **Chat to Terminal.** The terminal appears at once with a one-character spinner (`| / - \`) and a short line that changes ("Preparing the orchestrator", "Warming up the agent", ...). The "Terminal ended" strip no longer shows while the new terminal starts.
- **Opening an orchestrator whose agent has exited.** The button opens the chat immediately and the resume runs in the background, instead of waiting about 2s for `resume-agent` to return.
- **Plain navigation is quiet.** Opening a session whose last handoff had already finished no longer replays the shimmer or the fade. A handoff counts as in progress only if this view saw it running or started it.

## How it works

- `useSessionInterfaceSwitch` keeps a click-time `switchIntent` and derives `optimisticTarget` / `renderedMode` from it. A running turn that has to drain keeps the old surface, cloud sessions are unchanged, and a failed or cancelled switch falls back to the committed mode.
- `SessionChatSurface` renders a starting snapshot for the whole arrival (over any cached transcript). `ChatWorkspace` docks or centers the composer from `session.lastUserMessageAt`.
- `TerminalPane` takes a `booting` prop and shows the spinner status instead of the ended or empty chrome.
- Local resume shares one in-flight request per session (`resumeOnce`), so the session page's resume-on-open joins the click's resume.

## Behavior changes worth a look

- A failed resume now leaves you on the chat page with the error shown, instead of staying on the previous page. Two tests were updated.
- A remote-host terminal to chat switch now leaves the terminal at once instead of keeping it up with input fenced. One test was updated.

## Not in this PR

- The reused-session-id fix that stopped a stale prompt replaying is #6471.
- A dotted project name (for example `ronish.dev`) still breaks terminal start with `invalid activity id`. It predates this change.
- The terminal loader text is English only.

## Verification

- Typecheck clean. Full frontend suite: only failures in `browser-profile-import` (22), `ContextMeter` (2) and the `ChatWorkspace` context-usage test (1), all untouched by this PR.
- Checked live in the desktop app: instant switches in both directions, spinner visible, no ended strip, no animation on board to orchestrator navigation.

title: feat(mobile): add phone-mediated Watch inbox and complication
body:
Code changes: +360 -0\
Tests: +116 -0\
Others: +786 -0 (mostly `package-lock.json`, plus README, plists, target config)

Stack 1/2. The follow-up with wrist actions is stacked on this PR.

## What

Adds a read-only Apple Watch companion to the mobile app: an **AOWatch** inbox (list and detail of Needs-you items) and an **AOAttention** WidgetKit complication / Smart Stack widget that shows the attention count. The phone sends the data. The Watch has no network client and no credentials.

## Why

Users should be able to see that an agent needs them without taking out their phone, and the count must never claim "0" when the real count is unknown.

## How

- **Targets:** `@bacons/apple-targets` (pinned) generates the `watch` and `watch-widget` targets from `targets/`. Shared Foundation model in `watch-model/` (a SwiftPM package that is symlinked into both targets). Local iOS Expo module `modules/ao-watch/` wraps WatchConnectivity. Generated `ios/` is never edited. These source dirs are explicit `fingerprint.config.js` inputs, because this needs a new native binary and can't ship over the air (OTA). Requires watchOS 10+. Android is a no-op.
- **Snapshot (`lib/watch/snapshot.ts`, `WatchManager.tsx`):** while AO is in the foreground, the phone publishes a bounded, sanitized Needs-you snapshot every 30s. It reuses the existing multi-host polling and `agentsView` semantics, including pinned workers. Limits: 8 hosts and 8 rows per host. Counts include hidden rows, and hosts that were left out are marked explicitly. Each snapshot goes through `updateApplicationContext` and replaces the previous one.
- **Freshness:** freshness comes from the timestamp of the original successful poll, not from when the bridge delivered it. Data is treated as stale after more than 2 minutes, after failures, or when host coverage is partial. Stale data shows as **N+** (known attention) or **—** (unknown), never a fresh-looking zero. Disconnected hosts keep their last-known rows. The Watch caches the snapshot in a Watch-only App Group shared with the widget. The widget timeline schedules a stale entry at expiry, and its refresh rate is set by the OS budget, so it is not real-time.
- "Open on iPhone" is an instruction to the user. The Watch does not remote-launch iOS.

Reviewers should focus on the snapshot bounds and sanitization, how unknown vs. zero is handled, and the fingerprint/target config.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test` pass on this branch (211 files / 1,894 tests, Node 22.22.2) on `main` `c3e17362a`. CI `check` and `scan` pass. title: feat(mobile): add confirmed Watch permissions and replies
body:
Stacked on #6487

Code changes: +445 -19\
Tests: +254 -0\
Others: +53 -3

*(Counts are for this PR's own commits only. This is a cross-repo PR from a fork, so it targets `main`, and until #6487 merges the diff here also shows that PR's commit. Review only the commits after `feat(mobile): add phone-mediated Watch inbox and complication`.)*

## What

Stack 2/2. Adds confirmed wrist actions to the Watch companion: one-time approve/deny for a deliberately small set of permission requests, and reviewed replies (canned or dictated) to pending input or chat. Every action is reviewed on the wrist, and the phone carries it out over the existing Chat routes.

## Why

The simplest prompts (a read-only command approval, a short reply) should be answerable from the wrist. That must not create a second, weaker path for approvals.

## How

- **Transport:** reachable `WCSession.sendMessage` only. The native bridge (`AOWatchModule.swift`) accepts one live request, and only while phone AO and its JS listener are foreground-ready. It fails closed otherwise. Timeouts are 20s on the bridge and 25s on the Watch. If the response is lost after a write, the result is **Delivery unknown**, not success or failure. There is no background action service, `transferUserInfo`, deferred decision, automatic retry, or Watch-to-daemon network path.
- **Binding (`lib/watch/actions.ts`):** action tokens live only in phone memory and are bound to identity and config: host, session and request. They expire after 60s. The phone re-fetches the current pending context before any write. Duplicate and already-handled requests map to typed outcomes: HTTP 409 `CHAT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING` becomes **Already handled**, and HTTP 400 `CHAT_DECISION_NOT_OFFERED` is preserved.
- **Approvals:** the provider must have offered a semantic `allow_once` / `reject_once` decision, matched by its exact offered ID. Decisions are never inferred from labels. The Codex adapter (`backend/.../codexappserver/conversation.go`) marks the detail `scopeComplete` only when its projection dropped no request field (network context, environment, network policy amendments, approval callbacks or unknown fields), and the Watch requires that flag. Partial projections and older daemons defer to iPhone. The initial allow-list covers Codex approvals for the literal commands `pwd`, `git status`, `git status --short`, `git status --short --branch` and `git log -1 --oneline`, with cwd and reason shown in full. Wrapped, destructive or unknown commands, broad grants, TUI prompts and non-command permissions are deferred to the iPhone.
- **Replies:** a single plain-string input property, or an ordinary message only when a full read proves nothing is pending. Max 500 Unicode scalars. Each reviewed draft gets a stable `clientMessageId` (`lib/chat/api.ts`, `types.ts`) so a repeated delivery creates one message.
- **Watch UI (`WatchActionsView.swift`, `WatchActionState.swift`):** explicit **Confirm and send**, a 60s review window, and no merge/spawn/kill/terminal controls.

Reviewers should focus on the allow-list and binding logic in `actions.ts`, plus the fail-closed paths in the native bridge.

## Testing

That test compares the generated protocol with the locally installed Codex binary, and the binary has drifted on this machine; the change touches neither. `lib/watch/AOWatchModule.source.test.ts` guards readiness across a paired-Watch switch.
- Action boundaries written test-first: `lib/watch/actions.test.ts` covers binding, expiry, offered-decision checks, dedup and typed errors. `lib/chatModeApi.test.ts` covers `clientMessageId`.
- Swift Foundation review-state assertions pass (`ActionTests.swift`, via `./scripts/test-watch-model.sh`).
- `npx expo prebuild --clean --platform ios --no-install` is clean.
- **Rebased** onto #6487's tip `9fd47d95a` (`main` `c3e17362a` + the `AOWatchBridge` rename + the CI test mock). title: fix(tmux): deliver sends as bracketed paste so codex submits them
body:
Code changes: +52 -35  
Tests: +117 -66  
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #3626

## Root cause
Every `ao send` is **multiline**: the message is wrapped in the `<ao-session-delivery id="…">\n…\n</ao-session-delivery>` envelope. The tmux runtime typed the text into the pane with `send-keys -l`. That gives the TUI a burst of keystrokes, not a paste. Codex's paste-burst heuristic then sometimes treats the trailing Enter, 300ms later, as a newline inside the burst, and the prompt sits unsubmitted. That's why single-paragraph ~900-char orchestrator messages also got stuck. The problem was never that the text was multiline. The real issue was that the text arrived as keystrokes.

I reproduced this on a live codex 0.161 TUI in tmux, using AO's exact sequence (envelope plus a ~900-char single-line body, `send-keys -l`, 300ms, `Enter`): the old path left the draft unsubmitted in 3 of 4 runs.

## Fix
- The text is staged in a uniquely named tmux buffer (`set-buffer`, chunked as before to stay under tmux's command-size limit).
- It is then delivered with a single `paste-buffer -p -r -d`:
  - `-p`: tmux adds bracketed-paste markers only if the pane's app enabled bracketed paste. Codex, claude-code and other TUIs get exactly one paste event.
  - `-r`: newlines stay LF, so apps that did *not* enable bracketed paste (shells) get byte-for-byte what `send-keys -l` used to send.
  - `-d`: the buffer is deleted after the paste.
- There is still **exactly one Enter**, with no retries and no new nudge path. Codex's permission safety (#2357/#3231, `EmitsBlockedActivity=false`) is unchanged, so this can never answer an approval dialog.
- Cancellation got simpler and safer. A caller cancel while staging leaves nothing in the pane (the partial buffer is deleted). From the paste onward, paste, pause and Enter are detached as before, so a draft is never stranded.

## Why not #3741
#3741, closed as stale, only lengthened the paste→Enter delay. That narrows the race but keeps the timing heuristic (on a loaded machine, chunks and Enter can still land in one read). This PR removes the race: the bracketed paste tells codex exactly where the pasted text ends. No `confirmActive` change was needed.

## Tests
- New `TestSendMessageUsesBracketedPasteIntegration` (real tmux): a stand-in TUI enables bracketed paste and records the raw bytes it receives. It **failed before the fix** (`"line one\nline two\r"`) and passes after (`"\x1b[200~line one\nline two\x1b[201~\r"`).
- Unit tests updated or added for the command sequence (`set-buffer` chunks → `paste-buffer -p -r -d` → `Enter`), cancel-while-staging, and Enter surviving a caller cancel after the paste.
- Live check against codex 0.161 using the new sequence at the default 300ms delay: 6 of 6 submitted (envelope plus ~900-char single line, a 25-line message, ~3k chars), compared with 1 of 4 on the old path.
- `go test -race` on `internal/adapters/runtime/...`, `internal/session_manager`, `internal/sessionguard`: pass. The full `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes except `codexappserver` `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider`, which compares against the locally installed codex binary (0.161) and doesn't involve this change. `go vet ./...` and golangci-lint v2.13.2 on the runtime packages: clean.

## Not covered
- **ConPTY (Windows)** is unchanged. It writes chunks straight into the PTY and doesn't expose whether the app enabled bracketed paste. Wrapping blindly would inject literal escape sequences into apps that didn't ask for them. I can't verify codex-on-Windows input handling here, so that should be a follow-up if Windows users hit this.
