title: bug(remote-hosts): desktop connects to its own account-synced host
body:
## Bug

A macOS AO host paired from a second signed-in desktop is synced back to its own desktop as a remote host. The sidebar then lists the same local project and session twice: once locally and once with its own host badge.

Reported by Dhruv Sharma in this chat on 2026-10-10, using nightly v0.13.6-nightly.202610092159. Reproduced with real remote-host, registry, local workspace, and remote workspace hooks against main c72956ae6, with synthetic account/transport fixtures. Confidence: high.

## Reproduction

1. Open current AO on Macs A and B with the same AO account and remote-host connections enabled.
2. Enable remote hosting on A and pair A from B.
3. Allow the account host directory to sync on A.
4. Observe A's local project/session again under A's remote host badge.

## Root cause and fix

`useRemoteHosts` imports all account host records and connects every saved host without excluding the current daemon's stable `/api/v1/identity` host ID. Filter the local host from connections/sidebar data while retaining the saved and cloud records for other clients. Do not deduplicate by project name or delete the account host.

## Evidence and scope

The same-host fixture failed deterministically before the fix with two copies of its one project and one session. Separate macOS Mobile QR behavior under tunnel-only hosting is not part of this issue. Screenshots are not republished because they include account/project information.

title: feat: add Letta Code terminal harness
body:
Code changes: +463 -23  
Tests: +459 -2  
Others: +51 -3  

Withdrawn after independent source review: Letta Code v0.34.9 (`cbf9026030c74e60432c246aec2bb0ec08fd49bc`) cannot safely support the private instruction and lifecycle boundaries claimed by this prototype. This PR is closed without merging; no replacement gate-only PR is proposed.

Four concrete blockers in the pinned upstream source:

- **Private instructions can leak into the visible transcript.** `src/hooks/executor.ts:429` accumulates successful UserPromptSubmit stdout; `src/cli/app/use-submit-handler.ts:662-675` prints all accumulated feedback if a later hook blocks. `quiet` suppresses executor logging but not this rendering.
- **UserPromptSubmit is not acceptance.** Later hooks and pending approvals can reject submission (`use-submit-handler.ts:652-712`), so acknowledging an AO delivery there is premature.
- **Stop is not settled idle.** Stop hooks may veto completion and subsequent turn_end mods may continue the conversation (`src/cli/app/use-conversation-loop.ts:1490-1582`).
- **Permission state cannot be reliably correlated.** PermissionRequest omits tool_call_id (`src/hooks/index.ts:179-190`), while permission checking precedes PreToolUse for client tools (`src/tools/manager.ts:2192`); AO cannot reliably clear that blocked observation.

Before closure, the branch removed raw private-context output and unsupported submit, semantic-acceptance, permission-blocked and Stop-idle signals. It retains an unmerged prototype for reference. Native mods were investigated, but the released API has no additive per-process mod file flag, turn_start remains cancellable, turn_end still allows continuation, and llm_start is local-only. A future integration needs a proven common contract that preserves native settings and mods.

The prototype included dedicated conversations, exact conv-* restore, explicit permission mapping, model/install/setup surfaces, API/product registration and migration 0196. These changes are not shipping.

Validation: no local tests, builds, lint, typechecks, installations or provider probes were executed, as requested. Initial remote CI identified a missing exported-constant comment and outdated install-plan count; both source issues were corrected. API artifacts were generated earlier. The closure revision has not been validated and no CI pass is claimed. Live private-context, cancellation, authorization and kill/restore conformance remain NOT_RUN.

title: fix(remote-hosts): exclude this machine from remote connections
body:
Code changes: +105 -13  
Tests: +326 -3  
Others: +0 -0  

Fixes #6491

## Change

Make Electron main, rather than a renderer hook, enforce the current daemon's stable `/api/v1/identity` host ID across remote listing, pairing, connection, account-token forwarding, and preview access. The local project/session stays visible once; genuine other machines remain connected.

Read identity only from the supervisor's confirmed ready loopback attachment. Cache it for that attachment's generation, port, and optional PID; reject stale replies and invalidate it when the attachment changes. Recheck identity and account ownership around authenticated probes.

Keep the saved and account-synced host record intact so other desktops and phones can still connect to this machine. When local identity is unavailable, defer new remote connections without sending credentials; preserve only an exact, already verified live connection with unchanged URL, host ID, and password. Retry through the existing offline error path. No address/name-based deduplication or credential rotation.

## Current revision tests

- Regression coverage exercises the real main-process IPC handlers and registry: self refusal without credential/proxy creation, saved-record preservation, unrelated-host availability, first and late identity outages, account changes during probes, attachment invalidation, and stale replies.
- Renderer tests verify that the main-filtered list leaves local project/session data visible once and preserves other hosts.
- Final focused Node 24.14.0 rerun: six files / 92 tests passed, including the missing-entry correction. E2E and frontend typechecks both passed on final head `88328ecde`.
- CI E2E typechecking found an unsafe optional-chain lookup for an absent live entry and legacy host without an ID. A new test reproduced the runtime crash; the explicit map-entry guard now passes that six-test registry suite. Fresh CI will verify the correction.

The same updater file fails in isolation; a representative failure also reproduces without this PR on the QR-only checkout with identical base updater code. This Mac had only 745 MiB free, triggering the updater's real disk-space guard. No unrelated updater code or test changes are included.

The following results were recorded on the earlier renderer-filter revision `920cc72f`, not the current main-process implementation:

title: fix: refuse to rename the project orchestrator (#6475)
body:
Code changes: +37 -3
Tests: +131 -0
Others: +3 -3 (docs) Fixes #6475. ## Problem Renaming an orchestrator saved a new display name, but every orchestrator surface labels it by its role ("Orchestrator" on the session tab, the chat tab and the sidebar; the project name in the topbar), so the rename looked like it did nothing. The orchestrator could also rename *itself*: its agent can run `ao session rename "$AO_SESSION_ID" …`, and in chat mode a Codex or ACP thread title was copied straight into the orchestrator's display name. ## Fix This does not take the issue's suggested approach of refetching or syncing the name. The project orchestrator is simply not renamable: - **Daemon:** `PATCH /api/v1/sessions/{id}` refuses an orchestrator target with `400 ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`. The check is on the target's kind because the request carries no caller, so it covers the desktop, mobile and `ao session rename`, including the orchestrator renaming itself. Like the existing kind checks (`REPORT_WORKER_REQUIRED`, `WORKER_SESSION_REQUIRED`), it uses `apierr.Invalid`, and 400 is already in the spec, so `openapi.yaml` and `schema.ts` are unchanged. - **Chat titles:** a provider thread title is still recorded on the conversation, but it is no longer applied to the orchestrator's display name. Only orchestrators own a project-scoped conversation. `PUT /conversation/title` refuses that conversation with the same code rather than returning 202 for a name that never lands. - **Desktop:** the orchestrator's session tab, in both terminal and chat mode, no longer offers rename (double-click, F2 or the context menu). This follows the existing pattern of hiding orchestrator-only exclusions. - **Mobile:** the chat actions sheet hides "Rename conversation" for the orchestrator, gated next to the existing `canDelete` and `canPin`. - **Docs:** the `using-ao` skill (read by orchestrator agents) and the CLI reference say the orchestrator cannot be renamed. Out of scope: an orchestrator that already picked up a name (from an earlier rename or a provider title) keeps it in secondary places that read the display name, such as needs-input notifications and `ao session get`. A clean orchestrator restart spawns a fresh, unnamed one. No data migration is included. ## Tests - `Service.Rename` refuses live and terminated orchestrators, and the name stays unchanged. - In chat, a project orchestrator ignores provider thread titles, and `SetTitle` refuses without calling the provider. Both guards were mutation-checked: disabling either one fails the test. - `PUT /conversation/title` maps the refusal to a 400 with `ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`. - `ao session rename` against an orchestrator exits 1 with the daemon's code and does not report success. - Desktop: the orchestrator's terminal and chat tabs offer no rename (double-click, F2 or context menu), and nothing is sent. The test was mutation-checked against the gate. - Mobile: a source test for the `canRename` gate. ## Local validation Run on macOS (arm64) with Node 23.6.1; CI pins Node 24. - **Backend** (`backend/`): `gofmt -l` is clean, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass, and golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues. In `go test -race -count=1 ./...`, every package this PR touches passes (`service/session`, `service/chat`, `httpd/controllers`, `cli`). The full run had failures in four untouched packages: - `claudecode`, `opencode` and `goose` pass when re-run alone (load flakes). - `storage/sqlite` passes alone with `-timeout=45m`; it takes 21 minutes on this Mac under race mode. - `codexappserver` `TestGeneratedProtocolMatchesTheInstalledProvider` fails because the locally installed Codex CLI declares methods the generated protocol file lacks. title: bug(mobile): tunnel-only host has no pairing QR despite ready endpoint
body:
## Bug

Connect Mobile shows “No network address found for this computer” and no QR code after `ao remote-host enable --tunnel-only`, even when the daemon advertises a ready HTTPS tunnel.

Reported by Dhruv Sharma in this Codex chat on macOS with the latest nightly. Analyzed and reproduced against `4273bec7c638ea078fbead68090286315bc1b90a`.

**Confidence:** High. Rendered regression tests reproduce the exact message with a valid HTTPS endpoint and empty legacy LAN fields.
**Priority:** Medium. Manual address/password pairing is a workaround.

## Reproduction

1. Open a remote-capable AO nightly on macOS.
2. Enable remote access with the bundled CLI: `ao remote-host enable --tunnel-only`.
3. Wait for `ao remote-host status` to advertise a ready HTTPS address.
4. Open Settings → Mobile / Connect Mobile.

Expected: the v2 QR contains the daemon's stable host ID, existing pairing token, and advertised HTTPS endpoint. While the tunnel starts, show a pending state.

Actual: a LAN-address requirement suppresses the QR and shows an unrelated Wi-Fi/Ethernet/Tailscale hint.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/ConnectMobileContent.tsx` already builds the v2 pairing payload from the daemon's `endpoints` list. A second `activeHost` check still requires the legacy `status.host` LAN field. Tunnel-only intentionally leaves that field empty while advertising ready HTTPS endpoints.

Two rendered regressions fail on current main with `npm test -- src/renderer/components/ConnectMobileModal.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2 -t 'tunnel-only'`: the ready QR is absent and the starting state shows the wrong hint.

## Fix

Use the daemon's canonical advertised endpoints for QR readiness and connection presentation. Preserve existing LAN behavior, secure-pairing restrictions, host identity, and credentials. Do not change transport or enable new network listeners.

## Related

- #6491 and #6495 concern this machine appearing as its own remote connection.
- #5485 concerns advertising the Tailscale HTTPS proxy in the daemon. This issue concerns the renderer rejecting already-advertised tunnel endpoints.

title: fix(desktop): hide Dock presence when quitting to tray
body:
Code changes: +63 -36  
Tests: +118 -1  
Others: +6 -4

## Problem

After #6472, desktop Quit/Cmd+Q closes AO's window but keeps Electron alive for the tray, daemon, and remote access. The quit path never hides the Dock, so AO still appears as a running Dock application. The requested behavior is tray-only background operation.

## Changes

- Hide the macOS Dock only after the native window successfully closes, preserving canceled unsaved-draft warnings.
- Restore the Dock before reopening; share the focus path across tray, app activation, second-instance/folder launches, sign-in callbacks, and existing-window notification clicks.
- Retry an ignored hide once after 1.1 seconds: Electron 33 ignores Dock hides for one second after a show. Cancel that retry on reopen/full quit/update; recheck tray and quit eligibility before it runs.
- Preserve startup initialization, full tray Quit, updater/system shutdown, and Windows/Linux quit behavior.

User-pinned Dock shortcuts are intentionally not removed. No daemon, mobile API, remote credentials, or installation changes are included.

## Verification

- Red → green native macOS Electron 33.4.11 check using the real lifecycle controller and an isolated BaseWindow/Tray: canceled close retains the window/Dock; desktop Quit leaves zero windows, Dock hidden, tray alive, and the same Electron PID; two rapid reopen/quit cycles restore and hide the Dock; explicit full Quit exits 0.
- 69 focused tests pass: desktop quit, tray, tray lifecycle, draft close/unload guards, window composition, supervisor link, and update quit.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass on Node 24.14.0.
- `git diff --check` passes; independent lifecycle review found no actionable issues.

The native check exercises the controller against Electron/macOS, not the complete AO desktop/daemon/mobile composition. A signed nightly upgrade and a fresh two-Mac run were not tested. Existing AO processes and real user data were left untouched.

title: chore(cloud): retire the NodeOps sandbox provider
body:
Code changes: +3163 -1527  
Tests: +2690 -177  
Others: +82 -76 (docs, config, generated schema, i18n)

> **Stacks on #6478 (Freestyle provider).** Merge after #6478. Until it lands, this diff includes #6478's changes, so the counts above include them. This PR's own commit (`b7c82c1fc`) is: code +245 -1452, tests +417 -189, others +50 -100 (66 files, +712 -1741).

## Summary

Retires the NodeOps (CreateOS) sandbox provider and the dangling `ecs`, `daytona` and `lambda-microvms` provider names from AO Cloud. Old sandbox rows on those providers are now settled safely and no longer retry forever.

## Removed

- `cloud/internal/sandbox/createos/client.go` (CreateOS client)
- `cloud/scripts/publish-nodeops-template.sh` and `cloud/nodeops/Sandbox.Dockerfile` (legacy all-agents image)
- `sandbox.ProviderNodeOps`, `ProviderECS`, `ProviderDaytona`, `NodeOpsConfig`, `rootFSForHarness`, the NodeOps plan branch, and `Spec.Shape` / `Spec.Ingress` (only CreateOS read them)
- NodeOps config fields, env vars, validation and hosted allowlist entries in `config.go`. `ecs` and `daytona` are no longer accepted for `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER(S)`.
- NodeOps wiring in `cmd/ao-cloud/main.go`, including `readSSHPubKeys`, which only NodeOps used
- The `nodeOps` argument of `sandboxresolve.New` and `providerProfile.NodeOps` in the reconciler
- NodeOps parts of the deploy tooling: `lib/deployment.py`, `deploy-staging.sh`, `promote-production.sh`, `render-task-definition.py`, `validate-hosted-settings.py`, `.env.example`
- `nodeops` and `daytona` from the `ProviderName` enum in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml`, with `packages/cloud-client/src/schema.ts` regenerated (`npm --prefix packages/cloud-client run generate`)
- The `createProject.sandboxProvider.{nodeops,ecs,daytona}` labels in all 8 locales

## Moved

- `cloud/nodeops/Sandbox.base.Dockerfile` and `cloud/nodeops/harness/*.Dockerfile` now live in `cloud/sandbox-image/`. `publish-freestyle-snapshot.sh` replays their RUN steps for the Freestyle snapshots, so its default paths, comments and docs are updated. The base `FROM` (ignored by the bake) now reads `debian:bookworm` instead of the NodeOps image.

## Changed defaults

- `defaultSandboxProvider(hosted)` returns `coder` (it returned `nodeops`). `deploy-staging.sh` defaults to `coder`, and the Python renderer and validator default to `coder` too.
- `providersRequireWorkerHome` now covers `docker`, `coder` and `freestyle`. It used to list `nodeops` but not `freestyle`.
- `deploy-dev.sh` inherits the `coder` default, which means it reads the staging Coder secret unless `AO_CLOUD_CODER_SECRET_ID` is set. Its header comment now says this.

## Kept on purpose

- The non-Coder `/workspace` layout in `workspaceLayout`, `Spec.RootFS`, `Spec.AutoPauseSeconds`, the restoring state, the deletion deadline, worker self-update and `DefaultWorkerTokenTTL` (Freestyle and Docker use them).
- The provider CHECK constraint still allows `nodeops`. Historical rows exist (19 prod, 350 staging), migrations are immutable, and no new migration is needed.
- `RETIRED_PROVIDER_ENV_PREFIX = "AO_CLOUD_NODEOPS_"` in `deployment.py`. The renderer always prunes these names from an older task definition, and `validate_task_artifacts` rejects a task that still has them. This is what makes it safe to delete the nodeops secrets after the first deploy.

## Retired-provider behavior

`sandbox.IsRetiredProvider` covers `nodeops`, `ecs`, `daytona` and `lambda-microvms`.

- **Reconciler.** `reconcileSandbox` checks the retired set before `Resolve`. Before this, `Resolve` failed first, so these rows never reached the deletion path or the terminated parking and retried every 5 minutes. That covers the 4 live prod NodeOps sessions failing with 401 for 2 weeks, and the staging `ecs` and `lambda-microvms` rows stuck at `desired=deleted`. Now:
  - `desired=deleted`: calls `CompleteSandboxDeletion` with no provider call and logs any leftover provider id for manual cleanup.
  - Anything else: disconnects workers, records a `provider_retired` startup error ("This session ran on a sandbox provider AO no longer supports. Start a new session to continue.") and parks the row as `terminated`, with a quiet 24h no-op re-check. An already parked row is not re-recorded.
  - The desktop renders this with existing states: `runtimeState=terminated` plus a startup error shows the "This session couldn't start" pane with the reason. Session lists and history still render the old rows.
- **`SessionPlanForProvider`** returns `ErrProviderRetired` for a retired provider and an error for an unknown one. It no longer builds a provider-only plan.
- **Restore** (`RestoreSession`) and **startup retry** (`RetrySessionStartup`) check the sandbox provider first and return `ErrProviderRetired`. `writeStoreError` maps that to `409 provider_retired`. A rejected restore leaves the session terminated.
- **Child spawn.** An orchestrator on a retired provider gets `409 provider_retired` from `createWorkerChild` and no child row is created. Before, this was a 500 "misconfigured" error.
- The OpenAPI startup error code list and the retry endpoint description now document `provider_retired`.

## Tests

Fixtures that used `nodeops` now use `freestyle`, `coder` or `docker`: `worker_orchestration_handlers_test.go`, `resource_handlers_autolink_test.go`, `providers_test.go`, `provider_capabilities_test.go`, `workspace*_handlers_test.go`, `reconciler_test.go`, `test_deployment.py`, and 4 frontend fixtures.

New tests:
- Reconciler: retired deletion completes, a live retired row parks as terminated with `provider_retired`, an already parked row stays quiet. A failing resolver proves `Resolve` is never called.
- Resolver: retired versus unsupported errors.
- `SessionPlanForProvider`: rejects retired and unknown providers.
- Child spawn: `409 provider_retired`.
- Postgres: retry and restore are rejected and the session is left unchanged.
- Config: retired providers rejected, hosted default is `coder`, worker-home set.
- Deploy tooling: retired names are pruned from an older task, a task that keeps them is rejected, retired overrides are rejected, retired provider rejected by the validator.

## Test results (local)

- `cd cloud && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./...`: clean
- `GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/...` in `cloud/`: OK
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` with `AO_CLOUD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointing at a throwaway `postgres:16-alpine`: every package passes except 4 postgres tests that already fail on main (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`). The new `TestRetiredProviderSessionRejectsRetryAndRestore` passes.
- `cd cloud/scripts && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 34 tests OK
- `bash -n` on `deploy-staging.sh`, `promote-production.sh` and `publish-freestyle-snapshot.sh`: OK
- `packages/cloud-client`: regenerating is a no-op against the committed schema; typecheck, tests (29) and build pass
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The touched tests and i18n tests pass (6 files, 127 tests). The full renderer suite has 25 failures in 5 files, all from the local environment and unrelated to this change: en-IN number grouping in `ContextMeter`/`ChatWorkspace`, and the Electron binary and native modules being absent after `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (`browser-profile-import`, `browser-view-host`, `provider-auth-flow`).
- golangci-lint: the CI lint job only covers `backend/`, which this PR does not touch, so it was not run.

## Remaining `nodeops` / `createos` references

`git grep -i 'nodeops\|createos'` still matches the following, each on purpose:
- Migrations `00004`, `00028`, `00031`, `00036`, `00040`, `00041` (immutable history and the CHECK constraint)
- The retired-provider set, its tests, and the deploy `RETIRED_PROVIDER_ENV_PREFIX` pruning plus its tests
- Docs that name NodeOps as retired (`deployment.md`, `execution-readiness.md`)
- `docs/superpowers/*` dated plans and specs (history)
- `createOscColorReportForwarder` in the frontend (case-insensitive false positive)

## Ops follow-ups

- At the next production deploy, drop `nodeops` from production `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDERS` / `AO_CLOUD_SANDBOX_PROVIDER`. The deploy scripts now reject it, and `promote-production.sh` mirrors staging, so deploy staging first.
- After that deploy, delete the `ao-cloud/staging/nodeops` and `ao-cloud/production/nodeops` secrets (and any `ao-cloud/dev/nodeops`). The rendered task definitions no longer reference them.
- Any NodeOps VMs still alive on the provider side need manual cleanup. The reconciler logs `releasing sandbox on a retired provider without provider cleanup` with the provider id when it releases one.

title: feat(mobile): fold a settled turn's work behind a Worked for row
body:
## Summary

Brings desktop's "Working for → Worked for" turn accordion to mobile. Mobile already received all the data it needs (turn state, timestamps, `turnId` on each item), so this is a client-only regrouping of the conversation snapshot. It doesn't depend on the harness: every agent that works on desktop gets the same behavior.

- **While running:** the prompt, then a "Working · 12s" row with a spinner, then the work streaming in below it. This row used to sit at the bottom of the turn.
- **Once settled:** tool calls, interim messages, and approval and question cards fold behind a tappable "Worked for 20s ›" row, closed by default. The final reply, errors and system notices stay visible below. Failed and stopped turns fold too, and keep their "Failed after…" and "Stopped after…" labels.
- **Nothing to fold:** a turn with no work shows a plain, non-tappable "Worked for…" row.
- **Open state** is kept above the `FlatList`, so it survives row recycling.
- **Animation (Reanimated, using the durations in `motion.ts`):** the chevron rotates, the folded work fades in and out, and the content below slides. On the Working → Worked change, the spinner fades out and the label slides into its place. With Reduce Motion on, all of this is skipped.

### Changes
- `lib/chat/timelineModel.ts`: a new `partitionTurnItems` splits a turn into the opening prompt, the folded work, the notices and the final reply, using the same rules as desktop's `ChatWorkspace`. A running or queued turn stays unfolded, so the answer never jumps out of the stream.

title: fix(chat): prevent ACP replay overflow and preserve reconnect ownership
body:
Code changes: +109 -26  
Tests: +614 -7  
Others: +0 -0  

After AO restarts during an ACP Chat turn, retained updates can overflow the SDK’s 1,024-notification queue. AO stops reading but leaves the TCP socket open. The persistent host then blocks replay while holding its ownership lock. Resume times out, and AO fails the unfinished turn although its provider remains alive.

Deliver validated chat updates and host receipts in wire order, so a full AO event queue slows socket reads. Keep JSON-RPC requests, responses, and permission requests in the SDK. Close failed attachment sockets without terminating the persistent host. Preserve unfinished turns and queued messages for recovery. A definitive terminal receipt still settles its turn when a disconnect races the response.

### Before and after evidence

The process test uses real `ao` daemon executables, loopback HTTP, the persistent TCP host, and SQLite with a synthetic ACP provider. Each case uses isolated data. Send a prompt, save one seed delta, stop the daemon, emit 20,543 updates while detached, and restart the daemon. SQLite projection consumes immediately, without an artificial pause.

| Before: main `4273bec7c638` | After: this PR |
|---|---|
| Turn incorrectly becomes `failed`. | Original turn becomes `completed`. |
| Only 3,847 of 20,544 assistant bytes reach SQLite. | Exact 20,544-byte output reaches SQLite once. |
| Archive contains 3,847 deltas and no completion. | Archive contains 20,544 unique deltas and one completion. |
| Provider remains alive behind a failed controller. | Same host survives, with one provider launch. |
| Subsequent attachment can time out behind the leaked socket. | Terminal ACK clears the journal, and a third daemon restart retains the ready conversation. |

Actual daemon process results:

```text
before: turn=failed error="controller ended before the turn completed"
        assistant_bytes=3847 archived_deltas=3847 archived_completions=0
        same_host=true provider_launches=1

after:  turn=completed assistant_bytes=20544 archived_deltas=20544 archived_completions=1
        same_host=true provider_launches=1 journal_cleared=true third_restart_ready=true
        completion after restart=11.138s
        assistant_sha256=fa6c253b7b33ae9d37fbba8fbccf1c2972f403f5b7223bfd8942a9d752f0057f
```

The committed regression exercises the real ACP adapter, persistent host, Chat service, and SQLite. It checks every byte, unique durable event, terminal ACK, and third restart. Against unchanged main, it reproduces the queue overflow:

```text

ACP replay overflowed while the real SQLite projector was consuming
failed to queue notification; closing connection
err="notification queue overflow" capacity=1024 queued=1024
--- FAIL: TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts (3.67s)
```

A baseline diagnostic also reproduced the blocked next attachment:

```text
chat conversation recovery is inconclusive: persistent ACP host:
chat host ownership is inconclusive: context deadline exceeded
```

With this PR:

```text
same host committed exactly 20544 unique deltas, 20544 assistant bytes and one completion; terminal ACK cleared journal
third daemon-style restart reattached ready to the same native conversation
--- PASS: TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts (13.33s)

# Same assertions with the race detector and concurrent suite load:
replay completed after 3m42.964s
--- PASS: TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts (249.71s)
```

Run the committed regression:

```bash

go test -race -count=1 -v -run '^TestACPReplayProjectsExactlyOnceAcrossDaemonRestarts$' ./internal/service/chat
```

For the failing baseline, copy `backend/internal/service/chat/controller_acp_replay_test.go` into a separate checkout of `4273bec7c638ea078fbead68090286315bc1b90a`. Run the same command against that implementation. Use scratch databases and synthetic provider processes only.

- Go 1.27.1: full backend build and vet, complete backend race-package coverage, and full reruns of affected packages.
- All 395 Chat tests pass across both CI-style race shards: 354.889s and 179.014s. The complete ACP and persistent-host race suites pass.
- Complete SQLite race suite passes in 1120.191s. Session-manager and SQLite-store race suites also pass.
- Complete macOS CLI E2E suite passes. Cloud build, vet, format, and complete race suite pass.
- Golangci-lint v2.13.2: zero issues. Gofmt and whitespace checks pass. Gitleaks v7.4.0 scans both commits with no leaks.
- SQLc v1.31.1 and API generation under Node 24.14.0 produce no drift. Trusted leaderboard tests pass.

The initial backend sweep found two installed-provider checks that also fail on unchanged main. The OpenCode fixture finds an installed 1.18.35 binary. Codex protocol conformance compares installed CLI 0.162.0 against protocol 0.146.0. Both complete packages pass in a clean environment matching CI. Installed-provider protocol conformance is not claimed as passed.

The initial replay fixture also exceeded its two-minute deadline under the race detector while projection continued. The final fixture uses a measured five-minute bound and cheaper indexed polling. Both complete Chat shards and the focused race reproduction pass with every content, ACK, and restart assertion intact.

All **21 remote checks pass** on `d1af9046a2f221b639c2725bdb72170920862bbe`, including both Chat race shards and all four SQLite shards.

- [Go CI](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38045190949): complete backend suites, Windows workspace recovery, cloud Docker Expat validation, lint, SQLc drift, and API drift pass.

Docker and native Linux/Windows execution were unavailable locally. The successful remote jobs close those validation gaps.

Additional regressions cover replay order, socket release, full-buffer teardown, preservation of running/queued work, and terminal receipts racing a disconnect.

Related proposed fixes: #6215 and #6027. This PR includes the immediate-SQLite regression and unfinished-work preservation. It does not rewrite turns that previous versions already marked failed. Those sessions need separate recovery.

These controlled-provider tests do not exercise the packaged Electron updater or authenticated vendor behavior. The real OpenCode validation is linked below. The original production SDK exception was not durably stored. Production attribution rests on live socket/journal state and the reproduced failure chain. The **42.667-second continuous recording** includes the complete 39.109-second test. It shows a live process-log viewer while the real processes run. title: fix(mobile): make the Settings notifications switch respond instantly
body:
## Summary

The notifications switch in mobile Settings took ~3s (sometimes more) to toggle. The switch was replaced by a spinner until everything below finished, one after another:

1. **Retrying old turn-off requests.** Turn-off requests for earlier machines that couldn't be reached are queued (up to 10). Each toggle retried all of them first, and each one checks the machine with a 3s timeout (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`). One unreachable old machine added 3s to every tap.
2. **The current daemon.** Turning off waited on an identity probe plus the DELETE; turning on waited on the Expo token and the register POST.
3. **A queued status read.** The row re-read status afterwards, and that read waited behind the re-registration of every connected machine that follows turning push on. The switch often snapped back to its old position before settling.

### Changes

- `lib/push.ts`
  - The pending-unregister retry is queued after `registerForPush` / `unregisterFromPush` resolve instead of inside them.
  - `unregisterFromPush` resolves once this machine's registration is moved into the durable pending-unregister queue (queued first, then cleared), so an app suspended or killed right after the switch shows "off" still retries the DELETE on next launch. Draining that queue (probe + DELETE) is queued at call time right behind it, so a quick re-enable still runs after the DELETE, and the existing flush drops the entry when the same token was registered again.
- `app/settings.tsx`
  - The switch shows the new position the moment it's tapped (disabled while the change applies) and goes back if registration fails. The outcome is applied directly instead of waiting on the queued status read; a refresh still runs afterwards.
  - Renamed "Agent notifications" to "Notifications".
- `lib/push.test.ts`
  - New tests: turning off resolves without waiting on the daemon and with the unregister already recorded as pending; off-then-on sends the DELETE before the register POST and leaves nothing owed.
  - Retry tests now wait for the queue instead of depending on microtask timing.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npx vitest run`: 166 files, 1565 tests pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

title: fix(chat): preserve orchestrator conversation scope during provisioning
body:
Code changes: +6 -1  
Tests: +58 -35  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keep an orchestrator's opening prompt in the project-scoped conversation that its controller uses. A prompt queued before the controller starts now drains after startup instead of remaining stranded in a second, session-scoped conversation.

## Why

Related to #6523. In the reported desktop session, the orchestrator chat was blank and showed a message as queued even though the live controller had already replied.

Agent-assisted diagnosis found two conversation rows with the same current session: a session-scoped row containing the original queued prompt, and a project-scoped row containing the active transcript. `ensureConversation` unconditionally created the former during provisioning, while `Start` correctly created/reused the latter. Snapshot lookup by session could then return the wrong row. The regression test reproduces the stranded opening prompt with the real SQLite store and a fake provider, without account credentials or external services.

## How

Select project scope for orchestrators during provisioning, matching `Start`; retain session scope for workers. Extend the existing queued-prompt lifecycle test across both roles and assert the queued turn starts, the conversation ID is preserved, and the scope is correct.

Intentional omission: this prevents new split histories; it does not migrate already-split conversations or automatically replay their stale prompts. Repairing existing history needs an explicit policy to avoid duplicating work. No schema, generated API, frontend, or installed-app changes.

## Testing

- Regression red/green: worker passed and orchestrator failed on the original implementation (opening prompt remained queued); both pass with this fix.
- Focused race checks: passed for queued-prompt draining (both roles), first-controller startup, ordered provisioning messages and worker-report piggybacking (`go test -race -count=1 -timeout=90s ./internal/service/chat -run 'Test(DrainWithoutControllerKeepsOpeningPromptForLaterStart|FirstControllerAfterQueuedPromptIsNotFencedAsResume|SendWhileProvisioningQueuesInOrder|ProvisioningSendPiggybacksReportsOnlyOnRecordedTurn)$'`).
- `go build ./...`: passed.
- `go vet ./...`: passed.
- Linux fresh-install Docker build and `docker run --rm --init ao-scope-fix-smoke`: passed (`fresh-install check: OK`).
- Native macOS CLI E2E: four daemon-startup/run-file timeout failures. All four also reproduce on unmodified base `4273bec7c638ea078fbead68090286315bc1b90a` (DaemonClosedOutputPipeShutdownRemovesRunFile, Lifecycle, ShutdownGuard, DaemonBindsPortWithRecoverableChatReviewer).
- Full backend race run: not passed; observed timeouts/failures in e2e, OpenCode/modelcatalog and ACP packages, then stopped the broad run. Those additional failures have not all been baseline-verified.
- Complete chat race suite: interrupted for a diagnostic stack dump after remaining stuck for several minutes; stack was opening the temporary SQLite database in `TestResumeAcceptsFreshProviderOnlyWhenAllowed`, before the changed provisioning path. The same named test passes when run alone on the unmodified base; the full-suite stall is not yet isolated. This is not a suite pass.
- golangci-lint v2.13.2: passed with `--timeout=10m` (`0 issues`); first attempt hit the default timeout.
- Upstream Go, CLI E2E and gitleaks runs currently require maintainer approval (`action_required`) for this fork.
- Linux/Windows native runners and unrelated frontend/mobile/cloud workflows are not locally verified on this macOS host. Remote CI remains required.

- [x] Branched from main
- [x] One focused change linked to the reported issue
- [x] Regression coverage for worker and orchestrator startup
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass

title: bug(qwen): adapter reports signed-in from credential presence alone, but the CLI refuses to start without a selected auth type
body:
## Bug

The Qwen Code adapter reports the harness as **signed in** when an API-key environment variable is merely non-empty. The Qwen CLI itself refuses to start in that state. The UI therefore shows "appears signed in", the user launches, and the session dies immediately.

Separately, an OAuth-authenticated user is reported as **`unknown`**, which the readiness coordinator counts as a **failure** and retries on backoff indefinitely.

**Source:** internal investigation | **Analyzed against:** `f8918e986` | **Qwen Code:** 0.25.0 | **OS:** Windows 10/11, Node v22.14.0
**Confidence:** High — reproduced against the real CLI, exact code path traced
**Priority:** high — core feature broken, no user-side workaround

## Reproduction

`AuthStatus` was exercised against the real adapter with a real `qwen.cmd` on PATH:

```
scenario=clean-no-credentials             => AuthStatus="unknown"
scenario=stale-OPENAI_API_KEY-only        => AuthStatus="authorized"
scenario=stale-DASHSCOPE_API_KEY-only     => AuthStatus="authorized"
OAUTH selectedType=qwen-oauth             => AuthStatus="unknown"
```

`authorized` is reported for a key that is present but wrong. Running the command AO generates with that same stale key:

```
$ qwen --approval-mode yolo --model qwen3-coder-plus -p "say hi" --output-format json
[{"type":"result","subtype":"error_during_execution","is_error":true,
  "error":{"message":"No auth type is selected. Please configure an auth type
             (e.g. via settings or `--auth-type`) before running in non-interactive mode."}}]
```

Adding an auth type reaches the provider and fails there instead, confirming the two failure modes are distinct and that the earlier check is about auth *type*, not key validity:

```
$ qwen --bare --auth-type openai -p "say hi" --output-format json
{"type":"system",...,"model":"qwen3.7-max","permission_mode":"default",...}
[{"type":"result","is_error":true,
  "error":{"message":"[API Error: 401 Incorrect API key provided ...]"}}]
```

OAuth-shaped settings (`{"security":{"auth":{"selectedType":"qwen-oauth"}}}`) produce `unknown`.

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/auth.go:44-52` treats a non-empty value in `qwenAPIKeyEnvVars` (`auth.go:31-42`, includes `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`, …) as proof of authentication:

```go
for _, name := range qwenAPIKeyEnvVars {
    if strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(name)) != "" {
        return ports.AgentAuthStatusAuthorized, true, nil
    }
}
```

The same is true of the settings-file and `.env` branches (`auth.go:106`, `auth.go:218`).

This contradicts the port's own contract, `backend/internal/ports/agent.go:54-60`:

> `AgentAuthStatusConfigured` means a credential is present locally but no check has proven it valid. Presence is not validity: a key can be revoked, downgraded, or rate-limited with no change on disk, so only a provider round-trip may report `AgentAuthStatusAuthorized`. Local evidence (a config file, an env var, or a CLI that reports loggedIn) reports `configured` instead, **and must never render as a ready state**.

Downstream effect, `backend/internal/service/agent/readiness_coordinator.go:573-586`:

- `Authorized` → `AgentAuthenticationAuthorized`, message `"... appears signed in."` — a **ready** state.
- `Configured` → recorded as a success but deliberately derives to **not ready** (`:578-583`).
- default branch (which catches `Unknown`) → `failedAuthentication(..., true)` → counted in `entry.failures` and re-probed on backoff (`:491-503`).

So a correctly OAuth-authenticated Qwen user lands in the `Unknown` branch and produces perpetual inconclusive-auth failures, because the adapter never inspects Qwen's OAuth credential state or `security.auth.selectedType`.

Comparable adapters get this right — `backend/internal/adapters/agent/claudecode/auth.go:38` documents the rule in a comment and returns `Configured`; `mimocode/auth.go:48,68` does the same. Qwen (and `kimi`) return `Authorized`.

## Impact

- User with a stale/expired `OPENAI_API_KEY`: sees Qwen as ready, launches, gets an immediate failure with an auth message that contradicts what AO told them.
- OAuth user: permanent "authentication check was inconclusive" failures, repeated on backoff, and no correct remediation surfaced.
- Overstates readiness for a harness whose real launch precondition (a selected auth type) is never checked.

## Fix

1. Return `ports.AgentAuthStatusConfigured`, not `Authorized`, for all presence-only evidence (env vars, `settings.json` apiKey/envKey, `.env`). Reserve `Authorized` for a check that actually validates.
2. Read `security.auth.selectedType` from `<QWEN_HOME>/settings.json` and treat it as configured evidence, so OAuth users stop falling through to `Unknown`.
3. Optionally implement `ports.AgentLaunchAuthValidator` (`backend/internal/ports/agent.go:122`) so a launch-time check can confirm the auth type before spawning — this is the "provider round-trip" the contract refers to.

Note: `qwen auth` is listed as *"(removed)"* in Qwen 0.25.0 `qwen --help`; the in-session `/auth` slash command still exists, so the existing remediation plan in `backend/internal/service/agentauth/plans.go:36` remains valid. Separately, Qwen now reports that the **OAuth free tier was discontinued on 2026-04-15**, so that plan's guidance should be refreshed.

## Test

- `backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/auth_test.go` currently asserts `Authorized` for presence-only fixtures (`:31`, `:55`, `:77`, `:93`) — these encode the bug and must be updated to `Configured`.
- Add coverage: OAuth `selectedType` → `Configured`; no evidence → not `Authorized`; a validated path is the only route to `Authorized`.
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/qwen/... ./internal/service/agent/...`

title: bug(qwen): adapter drops AllowedTools/DisallowedTools, so Qwen reviewer sessions are not actually read-only
body:
## Bug

`GetLaunchCommand` in the Qwen Code adapter silently discards `LaunchConfig.AllowedTools` and `LaunchConfig.DisallowedTools`. These fields are documented as **the enforced read-only guarantee the reviewer relies on**, and the Qwen CLI supports the equivalent flags. A Qwen reviewer session configured to be read-only is therefore not read-only.

**Source:** internal investigation | **Analyzed against:** `f8918e986` | **Qwen Code:** 0.25.0 | **OS:** Windows 10/11
**Confidence:** High — argv captured from the real adapter; flag support confirmed in `qwen --help`
**Priority:** high — security guarantee silently absent, no user-side workaround

## Reproduction

Launch argv captured from the real adapter (`qwen.New().GetLaunchCommand(...)`) with restrictions set:

```
accept-edits + AllowedTools=[read_file] DisallowedTools=[write_file]
  => qwen.cmd --approval-mode auto-edit --model qwen3-coder-plus -i do
     [TOOL RESTRICTION DROPPED]

bypass + AllowedTools=[read_file] DisallowedTools=[write_file]
  => qwen.cmd --approval-mode yolo --model qwen3-coder-plus -i do
     [TOOL RESTRICTION DROPPED]
```

Compare with the same configurations and no restrictions — the argv is **byte-identical**. The restriction has no effect whatsoever.

Qwen Code 0.25.0 supports both flags (from `qwen --help`):

```
      --allowed-tools      Tools to allow, will bypass confirmation  [array]
      --exclude-tools      Tools to exclude  [array]
```

## Root Cause

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen.go:97-125` reads only `cfg.Permissions`, `cfg.Config`, and `cfg.Prompt` from `LaunchConfig`. `cfg.AllowedTools`, `cfg.DisallowedTools`, and `cfg.NativeSessionID` are never referenced, and nothing logs or errors that they were dropped.

The contract these fields belong to, `backend/internal/ports/agent.go:605-612`:

> AllowedTools and DisallowedTools scope the agent to a tool allowlist when it runs in a non-bypass permission mode (allow rules auto-approve, deny rules auto-reject). **They are the enforced read-only guarantee the reviewer relies on**: bypassPermissions ignores both lists, so a restricted launch must leave Permissions off bypass. Empty means no restriction, so worker sessions are unaffected.

Sibling adapters treat a silent drop as unacceptable. `backend/internal/adapters/agent/gemini/gemini.go:75-77` refuses rather than pretending:

> `"tool restrictions require a native policy and are not supported by this adapter"`

Qwen has the native policy — the flags exist — but the adapter neither uses nor rejects them, so the failure is invisible.

## Compounding factor: unsandboxed bypass

Qwen 0.25.0 prints a warning on every bypass launch, which AO triggers whenever `PermissionModeBypassPermissions` is set (`qwen.go:348`, `appendApprovalFlags`):

```
Warning: running headless with --yolo / approval-mode=yolo and no sandbox.
All tool calls (shell, write, edit) auto-execute at this process's privilege level.
```

AO never passes `--sandbox`. Combined with the dropped restrictions above, a Qwen session that is configured as restricted-but-not-bypass still runs with full write and shell capability.

## Impact

- Any Qwen-backed reviewer or restricted launch can write files and run shell commands that the configuration explicitly forbids.
- No error, warning, or log line indicates the restriction was discarded — it looks applied.
- The `ReadOnly`-style guarantee other harnesses provide is silently absent for Qwen.

## Fix

Map the restrictions onto the native flags in `GetLaunchCommand` (and consider `GetRestoreCommand`):

- `AllowedTools` → repeated `--allowed-tools <name>`
- `DisallowedTools` → repeated `--exclude-tools <name>`

AO's `[]string` maps to Qwen's repeatable `[array]` options, so this is a direct mapping. If any value cannot be expressed by Qwen's flag vocabulary, **return an error** rather than dropping it, following the `gemini` precedent (`gemini.go:75-77`). Also evaluate `NativeSessionID` against `--session-id`, which the CLI also exposes.

Worth a separate decision: whether AO should pass `--sandbox` (or at minimum surface the warning) when launching in bypass mode.

## Test

- Extend `backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen_test.go` with argv assertions covering: allowlist only, denylist only, both, and empty (no flags emitted).
- Add a negative test asserting an unexpressible restriction errors instead of being dropped.
- Confirm the reviewer path (`backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/agentrestore/agentrestore.go:47` sets these fields) actually receives them for `qwen`.
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/agent/qwen/... ./internal/adapters/reviewer/...`

title: fix(qwen): report configured, not authorized, for presence-only auth evidence
body:
Code changes: +31 -3
Tests: +75 -27
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #6526

## Problem

The Qwen adapter reported `AgentAuthStatusAuthorized` whenever an API-key environment variable, `settings.json` key, or `.env` entry was merely **non-empty**. That violates `ports/agent.go`, which requires presence-only evidence to report `Configured` and *must never render as a ready state* — a key can be revoked, downgraded, or rate-limited with no change on disk.

Reproduced against Qwen Code 0.25.0:

| Scenario | Before |
|---|---|
| stale `OPENAI_API_KEY` only | `authorized` |
| stale `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` only | `authorized` |
| `security.auth.selectedType: qwen-oauth` | `unknown` |

With the stale key, AO showed "appears signed in" and the launched session failed immediately:

```
[{"error":{"message":"No auth type is selected. Please configure an auth type
             (e.g. via settings or `--auth-type`) before running in non-interactive mode."}}]
```

Adding `--auth-type openai` reached the provider and failed there with a 401 instead — confirming the two failure modes are distinct and that the missing check is about auth *type*, not key validity.

Separately, the OAuth case returned `unknown`, which `readiness_coordinator.go` maps through its default branch to `failedAuthentication(..., true)` — counted in `entry.failures` and re-probed on backoff indefinitely.

## Changes

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/auth.go`

- All three presence-only sources (env vars, `settings.json`, `.env`) now return `AgentAuthStatusConfigured`.
- Added `qwenSelectedAuthType`, reading `security.auth.selectedType`. An OAuth user records the selected auth type instead of a key, so this stops them falling through to `unknown`.

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/auth_test.go`

- Existing fixtures asserted `Authorized` for presence-only evidence — they encoded the bug. Updated to `Configured` and renamed to match.
- Added `TestQwenAuthStatusFromSettingsConfiguredWithOAuthSelectedType` (the OAuth regression).
- Added `TestQwenAuthStatusNeverReportsAuthorizedFromLocalPresence`, a table test guarding every local evidence source against regressing to a ready state.

## Why not just flip to `Unauthorized`

`Configured` is the contract's middle state: it records a definite observation, stops the retry/backoff loop, and deliberately derives to *not ready* (with the user-facing message "has credentials configured, but AO could not verify them"). `Unauthorized` would be wrong — a valid key with no selected auth type is not an invalid credential.

## Intentional omissions

- **No `AgentLaunchAuthValidator` implemented.** Only `claudecode` does this today. It would be the "provider round-trip" that legitimately earns `Authorized`, but it needs a real launch-time probe design and is a separate change.
- **The `agentauth` remediation plan was not touched.** `service/agentauth/plans.go:36` types `i\x7f/auth\r` into an interactive `qwen`. `/auth` still exists in 0.25.0, so it remains valid. Separately, Qwen now reports the **OAuth free tier was discontinued on 2026-04-15**; refreshing that guidance is a content change, not part of this bug.

## Test

```
cd backend
go build ./...
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/qwen/... ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/qwenacp/...
```

Both packages pass. Full suite also run; remaining failures are pre-existing and environmental, verified identical before this change:

- `adapters/agent/registry` — `omp`, `codewhale`, `pi` binaries missing/failing on this machine
- `service/agent` — `TestCodexCapacity*` assert Unix ACL semantics that do not hold on Windows

Not run locally: Windows/macOS CI runners, Docker-backed jobs, and the `qwenacp` live tests (require `AO_LIVE_QWEN_ACP=1` / `AO_PROBE_QWEN_ACP=1` plus a real authenticated Qwen install).

title: fix(qwen): apply tool allow/deny lists instead of dropping them
body:
Code changes: +34 -0
Tests: +109 -0
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #6527

## Problem

`GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand` in the Qwen adapter ignored `LaunchConfig.AllowedTools` and `LaunchConfig.DisallowedTools`. Nothing logged or errored — the restriction was silently discarded.

`ports/agent.go:592-599` describes these fields as:

> AllowedTools and DisallowedTools scope the agent to a tool allowlist when it runs in a non-bypass permission mode (allow rules auto-approve, deny rules auto-reject). They are the enforced read-only guarantee the reviewer relies on: bypassPermissions ignores both lists, so a restricted launch must leave Permissions off bypass.

Argv captured from the real adapter, restrictions set vs. not set, was **byte-identical**:

```
accept-edits + AllowedTools=[read_file] DisallowedTools=[write_file]
  => qwen.cmd --approval-mode auto-edit --model qwen3-coder-plus -i do
```

## Changes

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen.go`

- Added `appendToolRestrictionFlags`, mapping `AllowedTools` → repeated `--core-tools` and `DisallowedTools` → repeated `--exclude-tools`.
- Wired into both `GetLaunchCommand` and `GetRestoreCommand`. Restore was included because a resumed session carries the same risk; without it, restrictions would be enforced on first launch and silently lost on every resume.
- Entries are trimmed and blanks skipped.

`backend/internal/adapters/agent/qwen/qwen_test.go`

- `TestGetLaunchCommandAppliesToolRestrictions` — allowlist, denylist, whitespace padding, empty entries.
- `TestGetLaunchCommandKeepsReadOnlyToolsOutOfAutoApproval` — asserts the allowlist reaches `--core-tools` and never `--allowed-tools`, and that shell plus both write tools are excluded.
- `TestGetLaunchCommandOmitsToolFlagsWhenUnrestricted` — guards against emitting flags for unrestricted worker sessions.
- `TestGetRestoreCommandAppliesToolRestrictions` — the resume regression.

## Review follow-up: why the allowlist goes to `--core-tools`

An earlier revision mapped `AllowedTools` → `--allowed-tools`. That was wrong, and the mapping did not establish the read-only guarantee:

- `--allowed-tools` is **pure auto-approval**, not a restriction. Qwen's own settings reference states it for `permissions.allow`/`tools.exclude`'s sibling: *"This key is PURE auto-approval: it never removes, demotes, or hides a tool, and every built-in stays registered regardless of which tools the rules cover"* and *"`permissions.allow` cannot reproduce this restriction — it is pure auto-approval (#10075)."* So `AllowedTools=[read_file]`, `DisallowedTools=[write_file]`, `auto-edit` still left `edit`, `write_file` and `run_shell_command` callable — and the old test fixture auto-approved `run_shell_command` while excluding only `edit`, so it verified argv construction rather than any denied behaviour.
- `--core-tools` is Qwen's fail-closed allowlist over the core tool set (file, shell, search and related built-ins): a core tool the list omits is **disabled**, not merely left unmentioned. That is the option that actually matches `LaunchConfig`'s allowlist contract.

Both flags exist in Qwen Code 0.25.0 (`qwen --help`):

```
      --core-tools                      Core tool paths  [array]
      --exclude-tools                   Tools to exclude  [array]
      --allowed-tools                   Tools to allow, will bypass confirmation  [array]
```

`--allowed-tools` is now never emitted.

### Why not error like `gemini`

`gemini.go:74-77` refuses when it cannot express a restriction. Qwen can: `--core-tools` is a real allowlist and `--exclude-tools` a real block, so erroring would break launches that work.

## Residual risk, stated plainly

Two gaps remain, both inherent to Qwen's own policy rather than to this mapping:

1. **Non-core tools bypass the allowlist by design.** Qwen documents that MCP/skill tools and synthetic built-ins (`agent`, `list_agents`, plan-mode lifecycle tools, goal tools, `task_stop`, `send_message`, `tool_search`, `tool_call`) are not covered by `tools.core`. That is why `DisallowedTools` still matters: a caller that needs those blocked must name them. AO's restriction lists are per-harness and hand-authored, so they are.
2. **Enforcement is Qwen's own.** `--core-tools` / `--exclude-tools` are only as strong as Qwen's implementation of them. Confirming against a live install that an excluded tool is actually refused rather than merely unlisted needs an authenticated Qwen install and is **not** covered by this PR.

## Intentional omissions

- **Reviewer impact is narrower than the previous revision claimed.** Qwen is not a registered reviewer harness at this base: `reviewer/registry_test.go:96` asserts `qwen` is a *removed* reviewer, and `domain.AllReviewerHarnesses` has 22 entries, none of them Qwen. The only code paths that populate `AllowedTools`/`DisallowedTools` are the claude-code and kimchi reviewers (`reviewer/claudecode/claudecode.go:106-107`, `reviewer/kimchi/kimchi.go:112-113`); the worker launch path leaves both empty by design (`ports/agent.go:596-597`). So there is no live Qwen reviewer session that was silently writable — this fixes the adapter's contract before a Qwen reviewer exists, rather than closing an active hole.
- **`NativeSessionID` was left alone.** Qwen does expose `--session-id`, and the adapter also drops it. That is a separate capability question (does Qwen honour a caller-assigned native id, or does it need to be read back via hooks like the current flow?) and is not required for this issue.
- **No sandbox flag.** Qwen 0.25.0 warns on every bypass launch: *"running headless with --yolo / approval-mode=yolo and no sandbox. All tool calls auto-execute at this process's privilege level."* AO never passes `--sandbox`. Whether to add one, or surface the warning, is a design decision beyond restoring the documented guarantee.

## Test

```
cd backend
go build ./...
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/qwen/... ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/qwenacp/...
go vet ./internal/adapters/agent/qwen/...
go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.13.2 run --path-mode=abs ./internal/adapters/agent/qwen/...
```

All pass; `gofmt` clean. Full suite also run; remaining failures are pre-existing and environmental, verified identical before this change:

- `adapters/agent/registry` — `omp`, `codewhale`, `pi` binaries missing or failing on this machine
- `service/agent` — `TestCodexCapacity*` assert Unix ACL semantics that do not hold on Windows

Not run locally: non-Windows CI runners, Docker-backed jobs, and the `qwenacp` live tests (require `AO_LIVE_QWEN_ACP=1` plus a real authenticated Qwen install).

title: feat(desktop): rethink keybinds and make the app keyboard navigable
body:
## What

AO's keybinds were few and hard to guess, and session switching walked the raw data list, so it jumped to seemingly random sessions. This replaces them with one registry, makes navigation follow what the sidebar shows, and makes the main surfaces usable from the keyboard.

## Shortcuts (Cmd on mac, Ctrl elsewhere)

| Area | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | Cmd+Shift+[ / ] previous and next (also Cmd+Opt+Up/Down), Cmd+1-9 jump, Cmd+Opt+Shift+Up/Down next needing attention |
| History | Cmd+[ / ] (page history while the Browser panel has focus) |
| Tabs | Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab (also Cmd+Opt+Left/Right), Cmd+T new terminal, Cmd+W close, Cmd+Shift+T reopen closed file tab |
| General | Cmd+N new session, Cmd+K or Cmd+Shift+P palette, Cmd+P quick open file, Cmd+, settings, Cmd+/ shortcut sheet |
| Session | Cmd+Shift+A archive, Cmd+O open in editor, Cmd+Shift+C copy session path, Cmd+Shift+M model picker |
| Panels | Cmd+B sidebar, Cmd+Shift+B or Cmd+Opt+B right sidebar (reopens on its last tab), Ctrl+` or Cmd+J terminal, Cmd+Shift+D diff, Cmd+Opt+I DevTools |

Chords are matched in the Electron main process, so they also work while the terminal or the Browser panel has focus. Windows and Linux variants are in `shared/shortcuts.ts`. There, plain Ctrl+T/W/B and Ctrl+/ are readline and tmux keys, so they yield to a focused terminal and have Ctrl+Shift alternatives (Ctrl+Shift+` new terminal, Ctrl+Shift+W close tab, Ctrl+Shift+E sidebar, Ctrl+Shift+B inspector). Saved overrides for removed shortcuts are dropped on read.

The Cmd+/ sheet is a wide three-column modal on the shared settings dialog frame, listing the current bindings, including customized ones.

## Navigation

- Session order follows the sidebar: pinned, projects in drag order, then Scratchpad. It crosses projects and wraps.
- The sidebar expands the target's project, opens closed sections, and scrolls the row into view. Tab strips scroll the selected tab into view.
- While Settings is open, the same chords step through its sections and Cmd+1-9 jumps to one. Session-scoped shortcuts stand down so they never act on the hidden session.

## Keyboard accessibility

- Enter on a menu switch row (Fast mode, Plan Mode) now toggles it. The model picker opens from the keyboard and hands focus back to the composer on close.
- Dialogs restore focus to where it was. Destructive confirms focus Cancel. Esc is ignored while a confirm is busy.
- Toasts pause on hover and focus, and error toasts last 8 seconds.
- A collapsed sidebar is inert (its expand rail stays live). Sessions and queued messages can be reordered with Space and the arrow keys. F2 renames shell terminals.
- The Browser "preview original" button, custom device width, notification row buttons, model refresh and retry, and the reviewer default are reachable by keyboard.
- Maximized Files and Browser panels are real dialogs and close on Esc.

## Not in this PR

- The global focus ring is still off (`styles.css`), so Tab focus is invisible on many controls. This needs a design decision.
- Keyboard reordering of projects, starting a diff line comment from the keyboard, and keyboard-resizable panels.
- The command palette is still gated to dev and nightly builds.

## Testing

- `tsc` is clean for `src/` and the e2e config.
- Full vitest run: 7034 passed, 25 failed. The 25 are environmental and unrelated to this change: `browser-profile-import.test.ts` (native SQLite module mismatch), two in `ContextMeter.test.tsx` and one in `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` (number format).
- Driven in a real Electron instance by synthesizing keys through `before-input-event`: session nav, jump, attention, history, tabs, panel toggles, palette, quick open, settings, new session and terminal, archive confirm, copy path.
- Only covered by unit tests: Cmd+O (it would launch an editor) and Cmd+Shift+T reopen.
- Matching by physical key code no longer fires for plain letters, which made Cmd+/ trigger history on Dvorak. Tests cover Dvorak, German and AZERTY layouts and AltGr output.
- A P0/P1 review pass found and fixed: Alt+Left/Right stealing word-jump from the terminal on Windows and Linux, the shortcut recorder missing conflicts on bracket chords, session shortcuts firing under the Settings page, the collapsed sidebar's expand rail going inert, and the custom width field losing focus on mouse move.

title: feat(themes): 20 dark and light color themes from one palette catalog
body:
Code changes: +714 -508  
Tests: +233 -8  
Others: +0 -0

## What this does

Replaces the 9 named color themes with 20, each with a dark and a light palette, and makes every theme actually own the whole app.

Themes: Orchestrate, Vercel, GitHub, One, Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox, Rosé Pine, Solarized, Kanagawa, VS Code, Monokai, Material, Ayu, Night Owl, Everforest, Vitesse, Flexoki.

Vercel was a community request (a Geist-based dark theme). Nord is the only light palette that is not official: Snow Storm surfaces, Frost accent, Aurora hues darkened for light backgrounds.

## Why the old themes looked off

- A named theme only set the shadcn base tokens. Status colors, error red, links and inline code (a fixed `#79b0dc`), charts and terminal ANSI stayed Orchestrate's in every theme.
- Each palette's lightness was recalculated onto Orchestrate's contrast curve, so canonical colors were replaced and every theme looked like Orchestrate with a tint.
- Light variants like Dracula and Tokyo Night light were made up.

## How it works now

- `lib/theme-palettes.ts`: one catalog. Each theme has dark and light palettes with the same roles (bg, sidebar, panel, element, text, muted, accent, optional primary, and red/orange/yellow/green/blue/purple/cyan).
- `lib/theme-tokens.ts`: derives every color token from a palette (base surfaces, status, links, brand mark, charts, passive text, terminal ANSI and selection) as concrete hex, since xterm reads raw CSS variable strings. It injects one `<style>` the first time a named theme is applied. The hand-written blocks in `tokens.css` are removed.
- Filled buttons pick white text when it reaches 4.5:1 on the fill, otherwise whichever of white or black contrasts more.
- `theme-palettes.test.ts` checks every named theme in both modes: text at least 7:1 on canvas, panel and sidebar; muted text at least 4.5:1; accent and status hues at least 3:1. 41 canonical colors that missed these (mostly light-mode yellows, greens and oranges) were moved in lightness only, keeping their hue.

## Settings

- The color theme dropdown lists all 20 themes. Each row shows the name and a swatch of the theme's canvas with its accent and status colors. The trigger shows a three-dot version on the same side.
- Hovering or arrowing through the list previews the theme across the app. The preview skips the View Transition (its snapshot froze the page and hid the hover highlight) and holds CSS transitions off until the menu closes. Escape or clicking away restores the saved theme. Selecting keeps the preview as-is, so there is no flash.
- Existing selections persist: the storage keys (`ao.theme-style`, `ao.theme`) and all 9 previous theme ids are unchanged, and `theme.test.ts` locks each stored id in.

## Not in this PR

- Syntax highlighting in diffs and file views still uses `github-dark` / `github-light`. Mapping each theme to its matching Shiki theme is a follow-up.
- Open terminals keep the saved palette while hovering a preview and switch on select.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- `npx vitest run` locally: everything in the touched areas passes. 25 failures elsewhere are local environment issues and also happen on `main`: 22 in `browser-profile-import.test.ts` (`better-sqlite3` built for the Electron ABI) and the ChatWorkspace context-usage tests (the same test fails on the base commit locally and passes in CI).

title: telemetry: ao.session.spawned missing for ~57% of sessions created on a local install
body:
PostHog undercounts agent spawns. On one machine, `~/.ao/data/ao.db` has 140 sessions created since 2026-09-17 (136 workers, 4 orchestrators), but `telemetry_event` has only 60 `ao.session.spawned` rows (one per `session_id`), so 80 sessions never emitted the event. The gap covers every harness (claude-code, codex, cursor), both chat and tui `session_mode`, and is spread across most days.

Expected: every successfully spawned agent session emits `ao.session.spawned` exactly once, whatever path created it, without double-counting and without counting a restore/resume as a spawn.

Query used: `sessions LEFT JOIN (select distinct session_id from telemetry_event where name='ao.session.spawned')`.

Related: #3873 (uses `ao.session.spawned` as the denominator for spawn failure rates).

title: fix(telemetry): emit spawn events for desktop new-task sessions
body:
Fixes #6533

## Summary
On the reporter's machine, 80 of 140 sessions never emitted `ao.session.spawned`. The evidence is on #6533. They were all created by `Service.DelegateTask` (`POST /api/v1/orchestrators/delegate`), which the desktop **New task** dialog uses for every daemon project, in both chat and TUI modes. That covers async chat task creation and claimed task preparations. Since #3443, this path has called `manager.Spawn` directly instead of going through `Service.spawn`. As a result, it skipped:

- `ao.session.spawned`
- `ao.session.spawn_failed`, so `spawn_failed` has the same gap
- `ao.onboarding.first_session_spawned`

This PR moves the `manager.Spawn` call and its three emits into `spawnWithTelemetry`. That helper is now the only caller of `manager.Spawn` in the service, and both `Service.spawn` and `DelegateTask` use it.

Every other way of creating a session already went through `Service.spawn` and emitted correctly: `ao spawn` / `POST /api/v1/sessions`, standalone tasks, orchestrators, issue spawns, automation runs, cue invoke and tracker intake. Locally, all 20 CLI spawns, 4 orchestrators and 3 issue spawns emitted, and 0 of the 80 missing sessions came from the CLI.

## Counting rules
- **Task preparation:** an unclaimed preparation row (`is_task_preparation=1`) is a speculative worktree reserved when the dialog opens, and no agent ever starts for it. It does **not** count, and it still never reaches `manager.Spawn`. A claimed preparation counts once, when `DelegateTask` claims it, the same as any other new task. `isFirstSession` already ignored preparation rows, and that hasn't changed.
- **No double counting:** client-request replays return before the helper on both paths (a test asserts this). Restore, resume, `RestoreAll`, `retryFailedChatSpawn` and interface transitions never call `manager.Spawn`, so they still emit nothing.
- Telemetry consent, opt-out and the event allowlist are unchanged. No events were sent to PostHog; the tests use an in-memory sink.

## Tests
- New: `TestDelegateTaskEmitsSpawnTelemetryOnce` checks that a replay emits nothing, a success emits exactly one `spawned` and a failure emits exactly one `spawn_failed`. `TestDelegateTaskEmitsFirstSessionOnboarding` checks the onboarding event. Both fail on main with `events = nil`.
- `go test ./internal/service/... ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/daemon/...` passes, except `service/systemcheck`, which also fails on this machine without the change because AO's bundled tmux binary is missing.

## Known follow-ups (not changed here)
- Async chat spawns, and orchestrators, which are always async, emit `spawned` as soon as the session can be addressed. If provisioning later fails in the background (`failAsyncChatSpawn`), they emit no `spawn_failed`. That path was already like this on main, so failure rates computed from these events (#3873) are still understated for async spawns.
- One small race was already on main: if two requests with the same `clientRequestId` arrive together and one finishes between the service's replay check and the manager's, the manager replays the existing row and the service counts it a second time.

title: [Feature]: fetch the base branch before spawn so worktrees always cut from a fresh origin/<branch>
body:
## Summary

AO never runs `git fetch` itself. `resolveBaseRef` binds a new session's worktree base to whatever `origin/<branch>` remote-tracking ref happens to exist locally at spawn time (`backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go`). If the user hasn't fetched recently, every new session silently branches off a **stale base**: workers then open PRs that are behind the real default branch and conflict on rebase.

The current code only errors when the ref is missing entirely (`ErrBranchNotFetched` → "run `git fetch` then retry"). Staleness is silent — there is no signal at spawn time that the base is outdated.

## Proposed behavior

1. Before creating the session worktree, fetch the resolved base ref (`git fetch origin <baseBranch>` — with a timeout; shallow-safe).
2. Use the fresh `origin/<branch>` as the `worktree add -b` base (this is already the preferred candidate in `resolveBaseRef`).
3. Offline or fetch failure: fall back to today's behavior (use the local remote-tracking ref) and surface a non-fatal warning on the session — do not fail the spawn.
4. Optionally a project-level toggle to disable the pre-spawn fetch for users with huge repos or air-gapped setups.

This complements #3942, which handles the *missing-ref* failure path; this request covers the *stale-ref* path, which today produces silently outdated worktrees.

## Why it matters

The common loop — merge PRs, spawn the next batch of workers on issues — is exactly where a stale base hurts: every worker starts behind main, and the resulting PRs need rebases that would not exist with a fresh base. Multi-repo workspaces multiply this.

## Related

- #3942 — auto-fetch on `BRANCH_NOT_FETCHED` at spawn (missing ref). Shares the same fetch helper; different trigger condition.
- #3873 — parent triage issue for spawn-time git failures.

**Priority:** medium — no data loss, but silently stale bases cause avoidable rebase/conflict churn.

**Confidence:** High — behavior verified against `resolveBaseRef` / `worktree add` path in `gitworktree/workspace.go`.

## Environment

- OS: macOS (darwin 25.6.0), arm64
- Build: desktop app self-built from a fork of upstream main; worktree creation path observed in `backend/internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree/workspace.go` (`resolveBaseRef`, `ErrBranchNotFetched`)
- Workflow: fork-based (origin = personal fork), base branch `main`

title: fix(lifecycle): ignore headless claude side runs in a TUI session's worktree
body:
Code changes: +70 -0  
Tests: +126 -3  
Others: +6 -0

## Summary

Prevent headless Claude side runs from overwriting the identity and activity of an existing TUI session.

A `claude -p` command started inside the session’s worktree inherits AO’s session and launch environment. Its hooks could replace the main conversation’s native ID and mark the session exited while the main agent was still running. Resuming could then kill the main process and open the side run’s transcript.

Fixes #6454.

## Changes

- Forward Claude’s `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` through the existing hook API.
- Ignore hook signals from headless Claude entrypoints: `sdk-cli`, `sdk-ts`, and `sdk-py`.
- Preserve interactive hook behavior, including native identity changes after `/clear` or `/resume`.
- Keep Chat controller signals and hooks without an entrypoint unchanged.
- Refuse TUI resume when the exact agent launched by AO is confirmed alive.
- Regenerate OpenAPI and frontend API types for the optional `entrypoint` field.

## Testing

Reproduced the original issue using AO `0.13.7-nightly` and Claude Code `2.1.296` in a throwaway TUI session.

Added regression coverage for:

- Side-run hooks leaving the main session’s identity, transcript, and activity unchanged.
- Interactive Claude hooks continuing to update the session normally.
- Forwarding the entrypoint only for Claude hooks.
- Rejecting resume of a live launched agent without replacing its runtime or modifying the session.

Latest local checks passed:

- All three new regression tests with the race detector.
- Complete lifecycle, HTTP/API, ports, and session-service suites with the race detector.
- Diff whitespace check.

One LAN identity test initially failed with `EOF`, then passed three isolated reruns and a full HTTP-package rerun.

All **23 GitHub checks passed** on commit `38f6ad1a`, including lint, race tests, API generation checks, and frontend validation.

The live reproduction has not been repeated against the final fix.

## Limitations

- A second interactive Claude process in the same worktree still reports `cli`; distinguishing it requires process-level ownership.
- Missing or failed liveness probes retain the existing resume behavior.
- The resume guard prevents replacing a confirmed live agent; it does not repair an already incorrect exited state.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: [Feature]: add Freebuff (freebuff/codebuff) as a supported coding agent harness
body:
### Problem

Summary

Add support for [Freebuff](https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff), the free, ad-supported AI coding agent, as a new harness in Agent Orchestrator.

Freebuff provides a CLI-based coding agent that can understand a codebase, edit files, execute commands, and run relevant checks. Integrating it would allow users to run Freebuff alongside the other supported coding agent harnesses through the existing Orchestrator workflow.

Motivation

Agent Orchestrator supports multiple coding agent harnesses through a unified interface. Adding Freebuff would expand the available choices and give users another option for running coding agents within their existing workflows.

Proposed functionality

Add Freebuff as a selectable harness when creating a worker session.

Detect whether the Freebuff CLI is installed and provide useful installation guidance when it is missing.

Support launching Freebuff in the appropriate project directory and workspace.

Integrate with the existing session lifecycle, including process startup, output handling, exit status, and termination.

Ensure the harness works with Orchestrator's existing workspace isolation and Git worktree conventions.

Add appropriate configuration, error handling, documentation, and tests.

Follow the existing harness adapter patterns rather than introducing a separate execution flow.

title: fix(mobile): say plainly that closing a MacBook lid stops agents
body:
## Summary
Settings > Mobile > **Keep this Mac awake** runs `caffeinate -i -w <daemon pid>` (`backend/internal/mobilebridge/keepawake.go`). The `-i` flag only holds `PreventUserIdleSystemSleep`. Apple's `IOPMLib.h` says the system "may still sleep for lid close, Apple menu, low battery, or other sleep reasons". So closing a MacBook's lid still sleeps it, and the agents and the phone connection stop with it, unless the Mac is in closed-display mode (on power with an external display).

The settings page already shows a laptop-only note (`mobile.keepAwake.laptopNote`, rendered when `pmset -g batt` reports an internal battery). It said the MacBook sleeps but not what that means for the user. This PR rewords it:

> Closing the lid still puts a MacBook to sleep, pausing your agents and your phone connection, so keep the lid open unless it's plugged in with an external display.

- The main help text is unchanged, and desktop Macs (no lid) still don't see the note.
- All 8 locales updated with machine translations in the same PR, the same way recent copy changes were done (e.g. #6472).
- Docs: `dashboard.mdx` and `configuration/remote-access.mdx` now say keep-awake doesn't override lid-close sleep.

## Tests

- Real Electron app (isolated data dir, dev daemon on :3130), Settings > Mobile. The dev machine is a Mac mini, so `hasBattery` was forced to true in the renderer's fetch to make the note render. The new copy shows under the help text as expected.
