title: feat(mobile): polish multi-host management and fleet performance
body:
Code changes: +4095 -1167\
Tests: +4964 -110\
Others: +36 -0

## What

Complete the mobile multi-host management, recovery, filtering, notification-cleanup, and list/navigation polish developed together in this branch. All 163 changed files are under `packages/mobile`; the branch incorporates current `main` without adding unrelated desktop/backend changes to the PR diff.

- Make machine management easier to find and use: Add a machine outside the dropdown, native Settings/Environments routes, one expanded/edited machine at a time, visible Save/Cancel actions, keyboard-aware editing, and simpler settings rows.
- Preserve each machine's chosen name/icon across workers, projects, menus, sidebar, notifications, and repaired pairings. Move the filled, rotated pin badge onto the session logo instead of crowding the host badge.
- Apply environment/project filters immediately while closing their picker. Provide an environment-only native picker on iOS and a sheet on Android when a selected machine is unreachable; distinguish connecting/offline from a genuinely empty worker list.
- Forget machines locally without waiting for network cleanup. Stop their local activity and persist pending push-unpair work for safe retry, including removal of the last machine.
- Stabilize fleet worker/PR list updates and sidebar navigation; reduce unnecessary rerenders and avoid startup hydration inflating the update pill. A machine's first workers join the held order rather than re-sorting it, so news waiting behind the pill stays held.

### Other user-visible changes

- "Delete session" is now **Archive session** everywhere (board swipe/menu, chat, terminal), with an archive icon. It still calls kill, so it stays destructive: the confirmation says the worktree folder is deleted unless it has uncommitted changes, and that the conversation and committed branch work are kept for Restore.
- The **Exited** worker status is blue instead of red, matching the desktop board.
- Settings no longer has a Disconnect row. Forgetting a machine happens in **Settings → Environments**; forgetting the last one shows an empty state with Add a machine instead of returning to onboarding.
- Chat understands a **hibernated** agent state (rollback and compaction are unavailable while hibernated) and keeps a viewed chat awake through the daemon's chat-view lease.
- The per-machine colour (`tone`) is gone: nothing rendered it and the picker is symbol-only. Values saved by earlier builds are ignored.

## Why

With several machines and many workers, polling/reordering and screen reconstruction caused visible list gaps, overlap, closing-end navigation hitches, and misleading update counts. Machine editing/removal also needed more predictable keyboard, confirmation, and offline behavior before wider production testing.

## How

- Retain lazily visited peer tabs and freeze/detach inactive pages without adding a visible tab bar or delaying navigation until drawer closure. Cache the native page layer while the drawer is open or moving, and release it once closed. The hamburger's appearance and Open navigation handler are unchanged.
- Structurally share unchanged rows/order snapshots, memoize worker/PR/sidebar rows, and keep host-qualified identities/action targets. Retained inactive pages cannot consume another page's scroll-to-top request.
- Use a bounded, memory-only 60-second/256-entry PR-detail navigation cache, separated by host/session/credentials. Pull-to-refresh bypasses it, stale entries revalidate, and failures are not cached.
- Keep verified secondary connections through host switches/display edits; re-verify only the affected runner when its token or endpoints change, and invalidate stale publications by generation.
- Serialize host storage/account-directory updates, cancel stale synchronization and credential refreshes, and guard chat-view lease/hibernated-controller handoffs against late work.
- Queue durable push cleanup before forgetting a machine, with identity checks before presenting credentials and retry on reconnect/relaunch. Retries are bounded: a job is dropped when the verified machine rejects its credential (401/403), after 30 days, or beyond 20 queued jobs, and unreachable machines back off from 30s to 30min (launch/foreground still retry immediately). Offline notification swipes reset if clearing is refused.
- Behaviour change: signing out of the account, or the account directory dropping a machine, now goes through the same forget path, so the phone also queues a remote unpair from those daemons instead of only deleting them locally.
- Route New agent to the explicitly filtered machine rather than silently spawning on the default machine; preserve local appearance during QR repair.

## Testing

- Fresh `npm ci`, Node **20.20.2**, matching the mobile workflow's Node 20 major.
- `CI=true npm run typecheck` — passed after merging latest main.
- `CI=true npm test` — **203 files / 1,852 tests passed** after merging latest main and the review follow-ups (bounded unpair retries, Forget always targets the tapped machine, no duplicate launch race after account sync, held board order across a machine's first load). Includes hook/screen regression coverage for connection handoffs/credential edits, selected-host spawn targeting, refused notification swipe recovery, QR appearance retention, removal/push cleanup, keyboard/footer presentation, row sharing, cache expiry/refresh/credential separation, and focused navigation.
- `git diff --check untrivial/main...HEAD` — passed.
- GitHub CI on the submitted head — **Mobile, gitleaks, and PR Review Leaderboard passed**. [Mobile workflow](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38164236945) ran the Ubuntu/Node 20 install, typecheck, and complete unit suite.
- Repository-pinned **gitleaks v7.4.0**, compiled from that exact source for Apple Silicon, scanning the two introduced commits with the repository configuration and redaction — passed. The official Linux binary/job will also be checked in GitHub CI.
- Read-only independent code review identified three important edge cases and one appearance-retention issue; all were reproduced/covered and resolved before submission. Follow-up review found no new blocking functional issues.
- Earlier local **Release** builds were installed over the existing Samsung SM-M317F and iPhone 13 apps without resetting saved hosts. The user subsequently reported smoother list/navigation behavior. Those installations precede the small pre-PR edge-case fixes above; this is not a claim that the exact final commit has been reinstalled/device-profiled.
- Samsung repeat-navigation evidence improved aggregate janky-frame counts from 241/474 (50.84%) to 193/508 (37.99%) in a two-active-host/100-PR workload. This was not an isolated A/B benchmark or an FPS measurement; long tail frames remained. Final full three-active-host retesting was limited by one offline host. Manual five-host testing earlier found no persistent gaps/wrong-host rows, but residual jitter was reported before the latest rerender changes.

Validation limits: local checks ran on macOS, not the workflow's Ubuntu runner. Docker is not running locally; backend/frontend/container suites are outside this mobile-only PR's path-triggered CI scope and were not labeled passed. Native keyboard/gesture behavior, actual push delivery, and production performance cannot be guaranteed by unit tests. No store publishing, OTA update, production deployment, or phone data reset was performed.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main`; latest canonical `main` merged before validation
- [x] One feature scope: mobile multi-host usability/reliability/performance
- [x] Follows `AGENTS.md` conventions; no daemon/API contract changes
- [x] User-visible regression tests added/updated
- [x] Relevant GitHub CI checks pass

title: fix(chat): fix excerpt follow-ups and gate Add to chat behind Developer mode
body:
Follow-ups to #6395 from a review of the merged excerpt feature, plus a feature flag for it.

## What changed

**Excerpts from unfinished turns now work.** The daemon only accepted a source message whose turn had `completed`. Chat still offered "Add to chat" on earlier messages of a running turn and on interrupted, failed, or recovered turns, so two common flows always failed with a "reselect it" error that could never succeed:

- quoting the agent's plan while it is still working, to correct it
- stopping the agent and asking about its partial answer

A settled message keeps its revision when its turn later finishes (only still-streaming rows get bumped), so these are safe sources. Queued, cancelled, and rolled-back turns are still rejected. A source turn may also have only one side of the pair now: a running turn may have no answer yet, and provider-started turns may have no prompt.

**Selections that run into a code block now verify.** The code block's language label ("typescript", or "text") was selectable, and the daemon's copy of the message does not include it. `user-select: none` does not help here, because Chromium still includes that text in `Selection.toString()`. The label now paints from a `::before` pseudo-element. It looks the same and never enters a selection.

**Excerpt retries keep the duplicate check.** A retry with excerpts reused the stored fingerprint, so any payload under an existing client id counted as a duplicate. It now hashes the request like any other send: the same payload is a duplicate, a different one returns a conflict. `SendForOwner` now fingerprints before hydration so both paths hash the same way.

**Translations.** "Add to chat", the "N annotations" label, and the navigation errors now go through i18n. The strings #6395 added to non-English locale files were still English; those are translated too.

**Feature flag.** A new "Chat excerpts" switch sits under Settings > Advanced. Like Diagnostics, it only shows in Developer mode and is off by default. With it off, chat does not offer "Add to chat" and the composer hides and withholds any draft excerpts. A journaled delivery still retries with its original excerpts, and excerpt chips on sent messages still show.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/service/chat/...` passes. New coverage: excerpts from a running turn (queued, then delivered with the paired turn) and from an interrupted turn; conflicting excerpt retries; prose-into-fence selection verification.
- Frontend typecheck passes. Focused tests pass for the composer, timeline, markdown, drafts, annotation navigation, selection positioning, and settings, including new tests for the toggle and for withholding excerpts while it is off.
- Full frontend suite: 3 files fail for local reasons. `browser-profile-import` fails because the dev launch rebuilt `better-sqlite3` for Electron. `ContextMeter` and one `ChatWorkspace` test fail because this machine formats 258,400 as "2,58,400".
- Checked in the desktop app (isolated data) on this branch:
  - the toggle shows only in Developer mode and persists
  - with it off, selecting assistant text shows no "Add to chat"
  - with it on, the button appears and adds a "1 annotation" chip to the composer
  - turning it off hides the chip
  - the pseudo-element label renders and is left out of a selection that spans prose and a fence

title: fix(chat): keep orchestrator history and queued prompts on the project conversation
body:
Code changes: +340 -25\
Tests: +493 -1\
Others: +236 -1 (generated sqlc)

## What

The project orchestrator's Chat now shows its real history, and prompts typed while it was provisioning drain in the conversation its controller uses. Before this change, the orchestrator's chat could show a blank history with a message stuck under "Queued", while the session showed Idle.

## Why

Fixes #6523.

A message sent to an orchestrator while it provisions is queued by `ensureConversation` in a **session-scoped** conversation, because no controller exists yet. When the controller starts, `Start` opens the **project-scoped** conversation, which is where orchestrators keep their narrative. Both rows then have `current_session_id` set to the orchestrator.

`SelectConversationBySession` was `WHERE current_session_id = ? LIMIT 1` with no ordering. On the `current_session_id` index it returns the older row, which is the provisioning one. Every session-keyed read (the snapshot, steer, the queue editor, the handoff lookup) therefore saw a conversation holding only the stranded prompt. Meanwhile the controller drained and wrote to the project row.

## How

1. **One write at first start.** When an orchestrator's **first** controller opens the project conversation, `Start` calls `CreateProjectConversationAdoptingQueue`. In one transaction under `writeMu`, it:
   - rebinds (or creates) the project conversation;
   - records the context-reset boundary;
   - **moves** the provisioning row's turns, messages, activities, and queued-edit receipts into it;
   - detaches the provisioning row.

   The rebind and the move share that transaction, so a prompt sent meanwhile lands either in the provisioning row, and moves with the rest, or in the project row after them. Queue order and the timeline agree.
2. **Rows keep their IDs.** Turns keep their ID and `requested_at`, so a turn ID the queue editor already holds still resolves for edit and cancel, and queued-edit receipts keep a retried edit idempotent. Messages and activities are offset past the project row's latest sequence, which puts them after the boundary just recorded. Excerpt references in queued delivery content are retargeted from the provisioning conversation to the project conversation, because drain checks each reference against the conversation it runs in.
3. **Nothing is left where no lookup can find it.** Every turn in the provisioning row moves, whatever its state, including one an interrupted drain left reserved (`promotion_started_at` set) and one with no user message. The only exception is a turn whose prompt already reached the project row under the same `client_message_id`, since moving it would break that row's unique client id. That turn is cancelled before the row is detached. A retried start finds nothing to move.
4. **A queued append checks its row is still bound.** `AppendUserMessage` for a pre-controller turn now checks, inside the same write, that the conversation's `current_session_id` is still the session. A Send that read the provisioning row before the move gets `ErrConversationRebound`, looks the session's conversation up again, and queues in the project row.
5. **Migration 0197** detaches the stale session-scoped row on databases older builds left bound to both rows. That fixes every other `current_session_id` consumer at once: the 0190 hibernation CDC trigger's unordered lookup, the branch-root triggers (0087, 0101, 0149), `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider`, and `ResetConversationAgentOverridesForSession`. A session still waiting for its first controller is left alone, because its start moves the queue itself. The stale prompts on already-split rows are not replayed: once that orchestrator has run, replaying an old opening prompt would repeat work.
6. **Lookup safety net.** `SelectConversationBySession` still orders `scope = 'project'` first, with a deterministic tiebreak.

Only a session that is still provisioning, has never had a controller, and has no provider history counts as the first controller. `Start` reads the session once and shares that one check between the move and `queuedBeforeFirstController`.

**Why not bind the project conversation during provisioning?** That's the smaller change: create the project-scoped row in `ensureConversation`. But it files the queued prompt *before* the context-reset boundary that `Start` records for a fresh orchestrator, and `LoadConversationSnapshotPage` hides everything at or before that boundary. The prompt would drain but never show in the timeline. `TestOrchestratorOpeningPromptDrainsInProjectConversation` fails that way, for both a new project and a replacement orchestrator, when the scope is changed in `ensureConversation` instead. Binding early would also expose the queue for the whole provisioning window to the controller of an orchestrator being replaced, which can still be running on that conversation (see follow-up).

**Intentional omission:** no unique index on `conversations.current_session_id`. That would be a schema change with its own rollout.

**Follow-up, not in this PR:** `RetireForReplacement` does not stop a Chat orchestrator's controller. `terminateNativeSession` only handles TUI sessions, unlike `Kill`, which calls `stopChatBestEffort`. I confirmed this by reading the code, not live. It is outside this fix.

## Testing

Regression tests, on the real SQLite store with the fake provider:

- `TestOrchestratorOpeningPromptDrainsInProjectConversation` (`new_project`, `replacement`): the prompt queued during provisioning drains in the project conversation and is visible in the paged timeline.
- `TestQueuedSendRacingFirstStartLandsInProjectConversation`: a Send that read the provisioning row before the move queues in the project row, after the moved prompt, in both the queue and the timeline.
- `TestStrandedPromptFromEarlierRunIsNotReplayed`: an orchestrator that is already split shows its project transcript, and the stale prompt is not replayed.
- `TestFirstOrchestratorControllerMovesProvisioningQueue`: the move keeps turn IDs and order, places the prompts after the boundary, retargets excerpt references, keeps a queued-edit retry idempotent, moves a turn an interrupted drain reserved, settles a turn already delivered under its client id, detaches the row, and is a no-op on retry.
- `TestQueuedAppendRefusesConversationTheSessionNoLongerHolds`: an append to the moved-out row returns `ErrConversationRebound`.
- `TestConversationForSessionPrefersProjectNarrativeOverProvisioningRow`: the session lookup returns the project row.
- `TestMigration0197DetachesSplitOrchestratorConversations`: the migration detaches the stale row, keeps a still-provisioning session's queue, and leaves unrelated rows bound.

Red/green: on unmodified `main`, the service tests and the lookup test fail with the reported symptoms. The orchestrator reads the session row, the replacement's prompt never drains, and the split session shows the provisioning row. All pass with this change.

Local runs of every CI validation job that can run here (macOS, Go 1.27.1, with `-race` and the shards CI uses):

- `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`: clean.
- `lint`: `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 (the version CI pins), 0 issues.
- `sqlc-drift`: `npm run sqlc` (v1.31.1) produces no changes. `api-drift`: `npm run api` produces no changes to `openapi.yaml` or `schema.ts`.
- `chat-race`: both shards pass.

- `sqlite-race`: all 4 shards pass, including the 0197 migration test.
- `backend-core`: shard 0 passes. In shard 1, 7 agent-adapter packages failed only on CLI-probe deadlines (`probe ... --version: signal: killed`, `context deadline exceeded`) while every package ran in parallel under `-race`. Rerun with `-p 1`, 6 of them pass. The seventh, `opencodev2`'s `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects/malformed_version`, picks up the OpenCode 1.18.31 binary installed at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` on this machine. It fails the same way on unmodified `main`, and this PR doesn't touch `internal/adapters`.
- `cloud-build-test`: gofmt, build, vet, and `go test -race ./...` pass.
- Not run locally, and passing in this PR's CI:

- Remote CI on `d2524d2`: 20/20 checks pass.

title: fix(desktop): back off when the daemon refuses the browser runtime link
body:
Code changes: +262 -73\
Tests: +391 -75\
Others: +24 -0 (locale strings)

## What

When the daemon refuses the desktop app's browser runtime handshake (for example, it holds another app launch's token), the link no longer reconnects every 200 ms and no longer re-renders the whole `SessionView` about 10 times a second while idle. The daemon now says explicitly whether it accepted the hello. On a refusal the link stops, and the Browser panel says the daemon refused the runtime and how to recover, instead of flickering "Browser runtime disconnected."

## Why

Fixes #6466.

`browser-runtime-link.ts` treated a TCP `connect` as success: it called `setConnected(true)` and reset the backoff to 200 ms before the daemon had read the hello. The broker answered an accepted hello with nothing and closed the socket on an invalid one (`broker.go`, `serveConn`). Every refused attempt therefore went connected → disconnected → redial after 200 ms, forever.

Each flip was pushed to the renderer, where `useBrowserView` held it in `useState`. That hook lives in `SessionView`, so the whole session view re-rendered on every flip, although only the Browser panel's runtime alert reads the flag.

## How

**Daemon (`backend/internal/browserruntime/broker.go`)**
- `serveConn` answers every hello. A valid one gets `{"type":"hello-ok"}`, written before the connection is published, so it is always the first frame the runtime reads and no command can overtake it. An invalid one gets `{"type":"hello-rejected","error":{code,message}}` before the close. The codes are `BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_REJECTED`, `BROWSER_RUNTIME_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` and `BROWSER_RUNTIME_BAD_HELLO`.
- Both frames are additive. Older desktop apps already ignore frame types they don't know, so the protocol version stays 2.

**Link (`frontend/src/main/browser-runtime-link.ts`)**
- **Accepted on the daemon's answer, not a timer.** The link is connected on `hello-ok`. An older daemon never sends one, but it writes commands only to a runtime it accepted, so any other frame from it accepts the link too. The 250 ms acceptance window and the 5 s stable-link timer are gone.
- **Refused only when the daemon says so.** `hello-rejected` sets `rejected` and carries the daemon's code as `rejectionCode`, logs the code and message once, and stops redialing, since the same token would be refused again. Reconnect, or a new daemon identity, builds a new link.
- **Transport failures are not refusals.** A close before any answer can come from a local hello write failure (EPIPE/ECONNRESET), an unreachable daemon (ECONNREFUSED), or an older daemon closing on a hello it refused. None of these sets `rejected`. They back off to the 2 s cap, and nothing but a `hello-ok` resets the backoff.
- **`connecting`.** `BrowserRuntimeState` is now `{connected, connecting, rejected}`. `connecting` is true while the link's first handshake is in flight, and again while the redial after an accepted link dropped is pending. That covers launch, Reconnect, and a daemon restart's first redial. A redial that fails turns it into a plain disconnect.

**Main process (`frontend/src/main.ts`)**
- Replacing a link (Reconnect, a new daemon identity) no longer publishes an intermediate "disconnected". The new link reports "connecting" itself. Tearing the link down for good (daemon not ready, shutdown) still publishes "disconnected", as before.

**Renderer**
- `useBrowserRuntimeState` is one shared IPC subscription, built on `useSyncExternalStore` like `useEventsConnection`. It subscribes before reading, so a late snapshot never replaces a newer push, and it tears down when the last consumer unmounts.
- `useBrowserView` no longer holds or subscribes to runtime state. `BrowserPanelView` reads it directly, so link changes re-render the Browser panel only. Nothing in the renderer subscribes while no Browser panel is mounted.
- The runtime alert shows only when the link is down and not `connecting`, so it doesn't flash on every launch, relink, or quick daemon restart. For a refusal it names a cause only when the daemon's code identifies one:
  - `BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_REJECTED`: "The AO daemon refused the browser runtime because another AO launch started it. Run `ao stop`, then reopen AO."
  - `BROWSER_RUNTIME_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH`: "The AO daemon refused the browser runtime because it comes from a different AO version than this app. Run `ao stop`, then reopen AO."
  - Any other refusal (a malformed hello, a code this app doesn't know, or none): "The AO daemon refused the browser runtime. Run `ao stop`, then reopen AO."

  The strings are in all eight locales, and the shown text is also the alert's `title` because the alert truncates. The main-process log keeps the daemon's code and message. A refusal hides the Reconnect button, because Reconnect resends the same token.

**Why `ao stop` and not "restart AO".** On launch the app replaces a daemon from another launch (`browserDaemonOwnershipDecision`), unless `AO_APP_RUN_ID` is pinned or inherited so the run ids match. In that case the app attaches to a daemon that holds an earlier launch's per-launch token, and a plain restart attaches to it again. Stopping the daemon lets the next launch spawn its own.

**Not in this PR:** changing that ownership rule, so a pinned run id with a different token is replaced instead of attached. This PR makes the state explicit, cheap and visible.

## Testing

- `broker_test.go`:
  - `hello-ok` is the first frame of an accepted runtime, enforced by a shared `handshake` helper in every runtime test.
  - A wrong token, a missing token, another protocol version, and a non-hello first frame each get `hello-rejected` with their code. The next read must return `io.EOF`, so a connection the daemon left open fails the test on the read deadline instead of passing.
- `browser-runtime-link.test.ts`. Backoff and refusal tests use fake `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` and wait on socket I/O, with no fixed sleeps. They passed 6 of 6 repeated runs locally.
  - `hello-rejected` sets `rejected` with the daemon's code once, logs the code once, never reports connected, and makes exactly one connection over 60 simulated seconds.
  - A close before any answer never sets `rejected`, and redials at exactly 200, 400, 800, 1,600, 2,000 and 2,000 ms.
  - An unreachable daemon reports `connecting` → disconnected, never `rejected`.
  - An accepted link that drops reports `connecting`, not disconnected, and is connected again after one 200 ms redial. If that redial fails, it reports disconnected.
  - An older daemon that never sends `hello-ok` is accepted on its first command.
  - The existing command, cancellation, UTF-8 and reconnect tests now ack the hello like the broker.
- `useBrowserRuntimeState.test.tsx`: hydration and pushes, a late snapshot never replaces a newer push, and one subscription shared between panels and torn down with the last.
- `useBrowserView.test.tsx`: the hook no longer subscribes to runtime state.
- `BrowserPanel.test.tsx`: no alert before the first state or while `connecting`, the refusal copy for each code (token, protocol, malformed hello, none) without a Reconnect button, and the existing Reconnect flow.

Red/green: on the original `browser-runtime-link.ts`, the refusal test fails, because the link reported `connected` on refused attempts.

Local runs (macOS, Node 26, Go 1.27.1):

- Frontend:
  - `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
  - Full `npx vitest run`: 460 of 463 files, 7,500 tests pass. The other three (`browser-view-host`, `provider-auth-flow`, `browser-history-store`) need a working Electron binary, which this worktree's npm install skipped. With the package's `path.txt` restored they pass on their own (212 tests).
  - `test:browser-postcondition-integration`: passes against a complete Electron 33.4.11 (`ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH`), because this worktree's copy lacks the Electron framework.
  - Renderer smoke wasn't run locally; the `renderer-smoke` job passes on this PR.
- Backend:
  - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l`: clean. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 (the version CI pins): 0 issues.
  - With `-race`: `./internal/browserruntime`, `./internal/service/browser`, `./internal/httpd/controllers` and `./internal/daemon` pass.
  - The rest of the Go suite doesn't depend on the broker change and runs in this PR's CI.

## What

When a session has artifacts, opening one no longer hides the workspace / PR file changes in the Files inspector. Artifacts and workspace changes now coexist.

## Why

title: feat(artifacts): Artifacts entry point, create flow, and artifact-output spawn
body:
Code changes: +707 -24  
Tests: +799 -4  
Others: +323 -9 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI, TS schema, route tree; i18n; docs)

## Summary

Adds an **Artifacts** entry to the sidebar, under Automations, that lists every artifact agents have written and takes you back to the session that made it. It also adds a one-click path to start an artifact session. This implements "Artifacts in Agent Orchestrator: Entry Point & User Flow" (Oct 11, 2026) as one slice, in the plan's order.

**Part 2: artifact-output spawn (backend and CLI)**
- `POST /api/v1/sessions` accepts `requestedOutput: "artifact"`. Any other value returns `400 INVALID_REQUESTED_OUTPUT`, so the enum can grow later.
- The kind is persisted on the session row (migration `0195_session_requested_output`). Restore and agent switching rebuild the same worker prompt. Generic `UpdateSession` writes cannot clear it.
- Artifact workers get an `## Artifact Output` system-prompt section: write the finished deliverable to the session artifact directory (HTML for visual work, Markdown for documents), don't open a PR, and ask first if the request is unclear. The section is added even when no artifact dir is configured, and an artifact-output spawn is refused with `400 ARTIFACT_OUTPUT_UNAVAILABLE` when the daemon has no data dir.
- Derived status, `outputType`, and Kanban rules are unchanged.
- `ao spawn --output artifact`, with the CLI mirror struct, drift test, `docs/cli/README.md`, and the using-ao skill all updated.
- `requestedOutput` is exposed on the session read model so the renderer can recognize an artifact session before any file exists.

**Part 1: Artifacts screen**
- New `/artifacts` route. Artifacts are grouped by project, with the Scratchpad as its own group. Rows are newest first within a group, and groups are ordered by their newest artifact. Each group header shows a count.
- Rows show a kind icon, the file name, the session title, and a relative time. A spinner replaces the icon while the session's agent is working. Copy and open actions appear on hover or focus in a fixed slot.
- Search matches file name and session title. The project filter defaults to All. When nothing matches, the screen shows "No matches" with Clear filters.
- Clicking a row opens the generating session with the artifact showing. It reuses `main`'s `requestWorkspaceFileOpen(sessionId, path, hostId, "artifact")`, which `SessionView` already resolves: html in the Browser panel, everything else in the Files viewer.
- The sidebar row uses the same top-nav row as Automations, with a count badge and the collapsed-rail tooltip. The shell topbar shows an Artifacts identity on Windows/Linux.

**Part 3: Create artifact**
- With artifacts listed, a **New artifact** button beside the project filter opens the same menu and flow. It is disabled, with a tooltip, when no agent is ready.
- The empty screen shows a heading, one line of copy, and one primary **Create artifact** button. Its menu lists the Scratchpad, a divider, then each local project.
- Choosing an entry spawns a worker with `requestedOutput: "artifact"`. The agent is the project's worker agent, then the global default, then the first ready agent. The app then opens the new session.
- While the session starts, the button shows a busy state. Failures show the daemon's message in a toast and keep the user on the screen. With no ready agent, the screen says so and links to agent settings.
- Telemetry: `ao.renderer.artifact_create_{requested,succeeded,failed}` carries only a `scope` enum (`standalone` or `project`), documented in `docs/telemetry.md`.
- **Artifact chat welcome:** an empty artifact session opens on "What do you want to create?", with three sample prompts and an artifact-specific placeholder. Clicking a sample fills the composer through a new `ChatComposerHandle.setDraft`.

**Part 4: in-chat card**
- The artifact `RenderFrame` gets an **Artifact** label, the file name, and an inline open-in-panel action. The action uses the same `useOpenArtifactPreview` handler as the inspector.

## Decisions and intentional omissions

- **Cleanup on removal:** this follows the doc's recommended "hide only" option. Archived and terminated sessions drop out of the list, and their files stay on disk. There is still no hard-delete trigger.
- **Opening prompt:** the daemon accepts a promptless spawn, so Create artifact sends no seeded prompt. The session lands on the artifact welcome, and the system prompt tells the agent to ask what the artifact should contain.
- **Local host only:** sessions on remote hosts and cloud projects are not listed (part 1 limit).
- **Locales:** non-English files carry the new keys in English, matching how the Automations keys landed.
- **Page title:** uses the 21px `text-heading` token, shown only where the shell topbar is hidden (macOS), like Automations.

## Testing

Test plan, with both automated and live end-to-end checks: `artifacts-test-plan.md` (session artifact).

Automated (all run locally):
- Go: controller accepts/rejects `requestedOutput`; prompt section only for artifact workers, kept after restore; store round-trip that survives `UpdateSession`; migration ledger; CLI `--output` flag and usage errors; DTO drift. Full `go test ./...` passes in a clean environment, and `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 reports 0 issues.
- Frontend: grouping, view (groups, search, filter, clear, click-through, empty state, picker order, Scratchpad and project spawn bodies, failure toast, no-agent state), Sidebar, ShellTopbar, SessionView pending open, RenderFrame card, ChatWorkspace artifact welcome, telemetry sanitizer, and i18n coverage. `tsc` and `typecheck:e2e` pass.
- Full vitest: 429/429 files, 7,085 tests pass. `tsc` and `typecheck:e2e` pass.
- Not code issues: when run in parallel with the dev Electron app, a few unrelated timing tests (goose, tmux, ACP, e2e restart) flaked; all pass when run alone. `electron-forge start` rebuilds `better-sqlite3` for Electron, so `npm rebuild better-sqlite3` is needed before running main-process tests under Node.

Live, in the real Electron dev app against isolated data (`~/.ao/dev/lab-224`, port 3902):
- A fresh database migrates to 195. The API rejects `requestedOutput: "slides"`, and the CLI exits 2.
- `ao spawn --output artifact` persists the kind and writes the prompt section. A real Claude Code session wrote its note into the artifact dir.
- Empty state, then Create artifact menu (Scratchpad, divider, demo-app), then a Scratchpad or project session is spawned and opened. The failure toast shows when the repo has no default branch.
- The list grouped by project with counts and a sidebar badge, plus search, no-matches, clear filters, and project filter.
- An html row opens the Browser panel on the artifact preview. An md row opens the Files viewer.
- Killing a session removes its rows and decrements the badge. The artifact welcome shows the sample prompts, and a click fills the composer.
- Checked in both light and dark themes.

## Known follow-ups

- A real delete-session action that calls `cleanupArtifactDir` (the doc's first cleanup option).
- Translations for the new strings.

title: fix(cli): accept session ids from dotted project ids
body:
## What

Sessions in a project whose id has a dot (for example `ronish.dev`) now start in TUI and report activity.

## Why

Project ids may contain dots, and session ids inherit them (`ronish.dev-2`). The CLI checked session ids against `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, which rejects the dot. Two things broke for those sessions:

- `ao agent-process supervise` exited with `invalid activity id` before starting the agent. Switching the session to TUI showed "Terminal ended" with that message.
- `ao hooks` returned early, so every agent activity report for the session was dropped.

## How

`sessionIDPattern` in `backend/internal/cli/hooks.go` now allows single dots between other characters: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*$`. Leading dots and dot runs are still rejected, so the id can never be `.` or `..` in a request path or in the `prompts/<id>/system.md` path the hooks read.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/cli/` and `go vet ./internal/cli/` pass.
- New tests fail on the old pattern:
  - `TestAgentProcessSuperviseAcceptsDottedProjectSessionID`
  - `TestHooks_DottedProjectSessionIDReportsActivity`
- `TestAgentProcessSuperviseRejectsDotPathSessionIDs` covers `.`, `..`, `../ao-7`, `.ao-7`, `ao..7` and `ao-7.`.
- Manually tested in the desktop app (isolated dev data): a Claude TUI session in project `ronish.dev` failed with `invalid activity id` before the fix. With the fix, `ronish.dev-5` starts in TUI and its hooks post to `/api/v1/sessions/ronish.dev-5/activity` (200).

title: fix(projects): derive a valid project id from any folder name
body:
## What

Folders with special characters in their name can now be added as projects. The project id is derived from the folder name instead of being rejected.

| Folder | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `app+web` | `INVALID_PROJECT_ID` | `app-web` |
| `app (v2)` | `INVALID_PROJECT_ID` | `app-v2` |
| `café` | `INVALID_PROJECT_ID` | `cafe` |
| `Résumé_Tool` | `INVALID_PROJECT_ID` | `resume_tool` |
| `_tools` | `INVALID_PROJECT_ID` | `tools` |
| `日本語` | `INVALID_PROJECT_ID` | `project` |
| `My App`, `ronish.dev` | `my-app`, `ronish.dev` | unchanged |

## Why

Without an explicit id, `defaultProjectID` only lowercased the folder name and turned spaces into `-`. Any other character outside `[a-z0-9._-]`, or a leading `.`, `_` or `-`, failed `validateProjectID` with "Project id failed storage-path validation". The desktop app's add-project request sends only the path and has no id field, so these folders could not be added from the app. The only workaround was `ao project add --id`.

## How

`defaultProjectID` in `backend/internal/service/project/service.go`:

- folds accents to plain letters (Unicode NFD, then drops combining marks);
- turns every run of other rejected characters into one `-`;
- squashes `..` to `.` and strips leading characters that are not a letter or digit;
- falls back to `project` if nothing is left.

Explicit ids are validated exactly as before. A derived id that is already taken still gets a number appended (`app-x` then `app-x1`). `golang.org/x/text` was already in the module graph and moves from indirect to direct for `unicode/norm`.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet` and `go test ./internal/service/project/` pass.
- New tests fail without the fix:
  - `TestDefaultProjectIDFromFolderName`: 17 folder names, each checked against the expected id and `validateProjectID`.
  - `TestManager_AddDerivesValidIDFromSpecialCharacterFolderName`: adds a repo named `Café (v2)+web` with no id and gets `cafe-v2-web`.
- Manually tested against the desktop app's dev daemon with the same request body the app sends: all 10 special-character folders that failed before now register. A Claude TUI session in the `café` project (`cafe-1`) starts and reports activity.

title: feat(chat): link session artifacts with hover preview and open-on-click
body:
Code changes: +500 -27\
Tests: +309 -5\
Others: +21 -1

## What

When the orchestrator tells the human about a document a session created, the document is now a hyperlink:

- **Route:** `ao://sessions/{project}/{session}/artifacts/{path}`, where `{path}` is relative to the session's artifact directory.
- **Hover:** a card with the artifact name, owning session, last-updated time, and a text excerpt (first ~480 chars; HTML uses the page title and visible text, without scripts or styles). If the session no longer lists the file, the card says "Artifact unavailable".
- **Markdown frontmatter:** a Markdown artifact's hover card shows its frontmatter `name` and `description` (plain text, clamped), with the body below rendered as compact formatted Markdown (headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code; links and images inert, tables unwrapped) and the raw `---` block removed. The parser (`lib/markdown-frontmatter.ts` and its tests) is copied unchanged from #6502, so the two PRs add an identical file.
- **CSV/TSV:** the hover card shows the leading rows (up to 6) and columns (up to 4) as a table; the parser handles quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded line breaks, CRLF, and a BOM.
- **HTML:** the hover card shows a scaled, non-interactive render of the page from the artifact's `inlineUrl`, in the same sandbox chat uses for agent pages (`allow-scripts allow-same-origin` on the page's own inline origin). Remote hosts have no inline origin, so they keep the text excerpt.
- **Click:** navigates to the session and opens the artifact: HTML in the Browser panel, other files in Files. This matches how the inspector opens artifacts. Artifact links still open after the session has terminated, because its artifacts are still served.
- **Inline code fallback:** inline code that names a listed session artifact, as `{session}/{path}` or as a path containing `/artifacts/{session}/{path}`, renders as the same link. This covers orchestrators that list artifacts by path instead of writing a link.

## Why

The orchestrator knows which artifacts workers have produced but referred to them as plain paths. The human had no way to preview them or jump to them from chat.

## How

- `session-links.ts`
  - Adds a strict `parseArtifactLink`. It rejects `.`/`..`, encoded `/` or `\`, `?`, `#`, and malformed escapes.
  - Adds `artifactLinkForPath`, which matches only artifacts the session actually lists in `artifactFiles`.
  - Raw-link linkifying and `chatUrlTransform` accept both routes through `isAoLink`.
- `use-session-link-navigation.ts`: for an artifact link, records an artifact `workspaceFileOpenRequest` (with `source: "artifact"`) before navigating. `SessionView` consumes it through the existing artifact open paths (`useOpenArtifactPreview` / `handleOpenArtifact`).
- `SessionLinkPreviewCard.tsx`: adds `ArtifactLinkPreviewCard`, which loads the excerpt through the existing `sessionArtifactFileQueryOptions`. Markdown artifacts get their frontmatter `name`/`description` from #6502's parser. The hover for workspace `.md` links stays in #6502.
- Orchestrator system prompt and the `using-ao` session guide document the route and tell the orchestrator to build these links only in messages to the human.
- Worker report delivery is intentionally unchanged. It is agent-facing, so it keeps plain artifact paths with no links.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run Prompt`, `./internal/skillassets/...`, `./internal/service/report/...`, `./internal/service/chat/...`: pass.
- `npx vitest run` for `src/renderer/components/chat`, `TerminalPane`, `SessionView`, `session-links`, `SessionLinkPreviewCard`, `use-session-link-navigation`: 40 files and 1,328 tests pass in the chat/terminal/SessionView sweep, plus the link and preview suites.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean for the renderer.
- Desktop lab against isolated data (`AO_DATA_DIR`): reproduced the orchestrator listing worker artifacts as inline code, which motivated the inline-code fallback. The fallback is covered by unit tests but not yet re-checked in the lab.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)

title: fix(spawn): launch Claude models from the last-known-good catalog after a refresh hiccup
body:
## Summary

Creating a Claude Code task could fail with:

```
spawn: model capabilities unavailable for model "claude-sonnet-5-5": catalog is stale
```

even though `claude-sonnet-5-5` was in the catalog with the selected effort.

**Root cause:** `resolveAgentConfig` forces a live provider model discovery on every Claude spawn (`Models(..., refresh=true)`). When that refresh fails briefly (provider/network hiccup, timeout), `loadModels` returns the last successful provider catalog for the same inputs, flagged `Stale` (`service/agent/service.go`). The spawn check then rejected any stale catalog, so a short provider blip blocked every Claude launch. The stale check came from #5208 to stop launches from using model IDs left from a different provider or credential. But a stale flag doesn't mean the credentials changed.

**Fix:** a stale catalog is trusted for spawn validation only when it is the last-known-good discovery for the current inputs: `LastSuccessAt` is set and, for Claude, `Source == "provider"`. The catalog service clears `LastSuccessAt` when the inputs changed, and the static alias fallback reports `Source: "catalog"`, so those cases are still rejected. Missing models (`ErrUnsupportedModel`) and unsupported efforts (`ErrUnsupportedEffort`) are still rejected too.

## Tests

- New `TestResolveClaudeModelAcceptsLastKnownGoodStaleProviderCatalog` covers four cases:
  - A stale last-known-good provider catalog launches the model at a supported effort.
  - It still rejects an unsupported effort and a missing model.
  - It still rejects a stale alias fallback.
  - It still rejects a stale catalog with no success time.
- Without the fix, the new test fails with the exact user-facing error above.
- The existing `TestResolveClaudeModelWithoutEffortRejectsUnknownAndStaleCatalogs` still passes.
- `go test ./internal/session_manager/` on Windows: the same 12 tests fail with and without this change (Windows path/PATH environment tests, unrelated). No new failures.

## Risks

- A model the provider removed since the last successful discovery could still be launched during a refresh outage. The CLI would then report the error at launch time, the same as for any model before #5208's check existed.

title: feat(artifacts): strict design rules and live app theme for agent pages
body:
Code changes: +715 -61 (includes the embedded guide.md and kit.css)  
Tests: +461 -16  
Others: +28 -37 (skill docs)

## Why

Agent pages (chat renders and saved HTML artifacts) looked different for every model. Rendered pages had loose theme hints, saved artifacts had none, and saved artifacts opened in the Browser panel did not get the app theme at all.

## What changed

**One guide for every page.** `renderpage/guide.md` is the single design contract for a page shown in chat and an HTML artifact. It is in every session's system prompt, the `html_render` tool description, and `ao render --guide`. Pages are semantic HTML plus a fixed set of `ao-` classes: no style blocks, no colors, no fonts, no libraries.

**AO page kit.** `renderpage/kit.css` is injected with the theme bootstrap. It styles the skeleton, tables, stats, lists, timelines, callouts, status, bar charts and SVG charts using only the theme tokens, so pages follow theme and light/dark changes live. The bootstrap tells the kit where the page shows (inline, expanded, or standalone) so pages never set their own width or padding.

**Enforced, not suggested.** `renderpage.Lint` checks a page against the guide.

- `ao render` / `html_render` refuse a page that breaks a rule.
- `ao report --artifact <file.html>` refuses a local HTML file that breaks a rule.
- `ao render --check` and `html_preview` return the findings; `ao render --lint` works in any session, including terminal ones.

**Live theme in the Browser panel.** The artifact preview origin now serves HTML with the theme bootstrap (`?raw=true` and workspace previews are unchanged). The renderer sends the current theme to main, which posts it to artifact pages on theme change and on every load.

## Experiment

Same vague prompt ("Make an artifact summarizing what changed in this repo over the past week") in an isolated dev instance. Pages from Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.1, Grok 4.7 (terminal session, saved artifact) and Kimi K3 all passed the lint and came out as one design: same header, stats row, bar charts, divided tables and lists. Differences were content only (section choice and commit range). Two kit bugs found this way are fixed here: wrapping bar values and list items that start with a bold name.

Not covered: Droid models failed on billing, and Cursor models ignored AO's standing rules entirely and wrote Markdown into the workspace. That Cursor gap predates this change.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, gofmt, golangci-lint v2.13.2: clean
- `go test -race ./...`: all packages this PR touches pass. Six adapter packages fail locally (opencode, opencodev2, acp, codexappserver, opencodev2acp, reviewer/opencodev2) on version and protocol probes against the agent binaries installed on this machine. This PR does not touch them, so CI is the check there.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: clean
- `npx vitest run`: passes. Locally, 2 files need `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` (this machine is en_IN) and `browser-profile-import` needs `better-sqlite3` rebuilt for Node; both pass that way.
- `npm run test:browser-postcondition-integration`: passes
- Checked in the desktop app with the isolated dev profile, dark and light

title: [Bug]: Clicking an absolute-path file link in chat shows "workspace path must be relative"
body:
## What went wrong?

When I click a link to a file with an absolute path in a session chat, the file does not open. The pane shows **"workspace path must be relative"** with a **Retry** button, and Retry never helps.

Expected: the file opens, or AO tells me clearly why it can't open it.

---

## Agent-collected evidence

Collected by a coding agent on 2026-10-09 by reading the code at `main` (`b407badf8`) and tracing sample paths through the path helpers with Node. The exact link the reporter clicked was not captured, so which of the failing cases below was hit is not confirmed. The mechanism is confirmed.

### How the error is produced

1. **Link click.** `MarkdownLink` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx:309` matches the link against the session's known workspace files. With no match it falls back to `explicitWorkspaceFilePath(href)`, which returns the absolute path as-is and still treats it as a file to open in Files.
2. **Path resolution.** `revealResolvedWorkspaceFile` in `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:1525` calls `matchWorkspaceFilePath`. With no catalog match it returns the absolute path unchanged (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/workspace-file-path.ts:122`).
3. **Daemon rejection.** `cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` in `backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go:2494` rejects any absolute path with `INVALID_WORKSPACE_PATH: workspace path must be relative`. `FileContentPane` renders that message with a Retry button that can never succeed.

### Which links fail

Traced with a file catalog containing `frontend/src/App.tsx` and `README.md`:

| Link | Sent to the Files API | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/…/worktrees/p/s/frontend/src/App.tsx:12` | `frontend/src/App.tsx` | opens |
| `/…/.ao/data/artifacts/s-134/report.md` | same absolute path | error |
| `/…/worktrees/p/s/.ao/attachments/shot.txt` | same absolute path | error |
| `file:///Users/me/notes/plan.md` | `/Users/me/notes/plan.md` | error |

So an absolute link works only when the file is in the session's file catalog. It fails for:

- files outside the worktree, most commonly the session artifact directory (`~/.ao/data/artifacts/<session>`), where agents are told to write deliverables and then link them;
- files inside the worktree that the catalog omits (git-ignored files such as `.ao/attachments/*`, files past the 5000-entry cap, files newer than a stale catalog).

### Which change introduced it

- **#5119** "Open chat file paths in Files" (`93e2ead39`, 2026-09-23) added the `explicitWorkspaceFilePath` fallback. Its own test expects `/repo/src/new.ts:12` to resolve to `/repo/src/new.ts`. The aim was to open files newer than a stale catalog, but nothing checks that the path is inside the workspace.
- `fb55fdc15` "restore file viewer navigation state" (2026-10-04) is not the cause. It moved chat file links from the Files inspector to a centre file tab, which made the same failing request more visible.
- The daemon check dates from the original Files panel (#2772) and is a deliberate guard, not a regression.

### Related defect found while tracing

`matchWorkspaceFilePath` also matches by path suffix and by unique basename. A link to `/Users/me/other-repo/README.md` therefore opens the session's own `README.md` without any warning. This is the opposite failure (wrong file instead of an error) from the same root cause: the renderer guesses where an absolute path belongs.

### Duplicates

No open or closed issue or PR matches `"workspace path must be relative"` or absolute-path chat file links (searched 2026-10-12).

---

## Desired fix

The renderer is deliberately not told where a session's worktree lives (see the comment on `DesktopWorkspaceLocationResponse` in `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go`), so it cannot strip the worktree root itself. The daemon should decide which root owns an absolute path.

1. **Daemon classifier.** Add `ResolveWorkspacePath(ctx, sessionID, rawPath)` to the session service. It classifies a path as `workspace`, `artifact`, or `outside` against the session worktree and artifact directory, and returns only a root-relative path. It must handle symlinked roots (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`), files that do not exist yet, `~/` paths, `..` escapes, and sibling directories that share the root as a string prefix.
2. **Route.** `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/resolve?path=…` returning `{ sessionId, kind, path }`. Never return an absolute path. Register it in `specgen/build.go` and regenerate with `npm run api`.
3. **Renderer routing.** In `revealResolvedWorkspaceFile`, send every absolute reference to the daemon before opening:
   - `workspace` → open the centre file tab at the returned relative path;
   - `artifact` → open through the existing `handleOpenArtifact` flow;
   - `outside`, or the request fails (for example a remote host on an older daemon) → fall through to step 5.
4. **Stop guessing.** `matchWorkspaceFilePath` keeps exact matching but no longer matches absolute references by suffix or basename. Relative references keep both.
5. **Clear message.** `FileContentPane` does not fetch an absolute path for the workspace source. It shows "This file is outside the session's workspace, so it can't be opened here." with no Retry button (new i18n key in all eight locales).

`cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` stays as it is; the file, blob, tree and PR routes keep rejecting absolute paths.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Absolute link to a tracked worktree file, with a `:line` suffix, opens that file at that line.
- [ ] Absolute link to a git-ignored worktree file opens that file.
- [ ] Absolute link to a file in the session artifact directory opens it as an artifact.
- [ ] Absolute link outside both roots shows the outside-workspace message, with no Retry button.
- [ ] An outside path that shares a basename or suffix with a workspace file does not open the workspace file.
- [ ] "workspace path must be relative" never reaches the UI from a chat link.
- [ ] Remote-host sessions on a daemon without the new route degrade to the outside-workspace message.
- [ ] Go tests cover the classifier; Vitest covers the helper change, the `SessionView` routing, and the `FileContentPane` message.

### Out of scope

- Opening outside-workspace files in the OS or an external editor.
- Cloud sessions, which open files through a separate branch in `SessionView`.
- Multi-repo workspace projects whose child worktree lives outside the session workspace root.

title: [Feature]: Ask whether to keep a session's artifacts when it is terminated
body:
### Problem

When a session is terminated (archived in the UI, `ao session kill`, or terminated by the reaper), AO keeps its artifact folder, `<dataDir>/artifacts/<sessionId>/`, forever. Nothing removes it. The only code that deletes it is the spawn-rollback path for sessions that never started. Archive, kill and workspace cleanup all leave it alone.

That is the right default for deliverables, but it means:

- Users who archive a session to tidy up have no way to say "I don't need this session's artifacts" and reclaim the disk space.
- Users who do want the output have no explicit confirmation that it is being kept.
- The artifact folder grows without bound, and planned artifact versioning (#6573) would add snapshots on top of it.

### Proposed direction

Add a control that decides what happens to a session's artifacts when the session is terminated:

- A setting (name to be decided, for example "Ask whether to keep artifacts when a session ends"). When it is **on**, terminating a session asks the user whether to save the session's artifacts.
- **Keep:** the artifacts are retained exactly as today, and stay available if the session is restored.
- **Don't keep:** the session's artifact folder is deleted. If versioning (#6573) has landed, its snapshots and version rows are deleted with it.
- When the setting is **off**, behaviour stays as it is today (artifacts are kept, no prompt).

Details to settle in the PR:

- **Prompt:** this should reuse the existing archive confirmation dialog ("Confirm, archive session") rather than adding a second dialog. Sessions with no artifact files should not show the question at all.
- **Which terminations ask:** a user-initiated archive can ask. The reaper and CLI kills have no user in front of them, so they must not delete artifacts. The reaper in particular can terminate many sessions at once, and a wrong mass termination must never destroy output. Unattended terminations keep the artifacts.
- **Deletion is irreversible:** restoring a session whose artifacts were deleted starts with an empty artifact folder. The dialog should say so. Consider listing the file count and names.
- **Output linked to a PR:** a session whose output is `pr_artifact` still has a PR, but the artifact files are separate and can be deleted. The dialog should make clear that only the artifact files are removed.
- **Scope of the setting:** global versus per project, and the default when the setting is first introduced.

### Alternatives considered

- **Always keep (today):** simplest, but unbounded disk growth and no user choice.
- **Always delete on archive:** reclaims space, but makes restore lossy and contradicts the new Artifacts screen, which exists to list deliverables.
- **Time-based expiry for archived sessions:** reclaims space without asking, but deletes output the user may still want, and needs a retention policy nobody has chosen yet.
- **A separate "delete artifacts" action on an archived session:** keeps archive non-destructive and puts the choice later. Worth considering as a follow-up or as a replacement for the prompt.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A setting controls whether terminating a session asks about its artifacts.
- [ ] With the setting on, archiving a session that has artifacts asks to keep or delete them; choosing keep leaves the folder untouched, and choosing delete removes it.
- [ ] Sessions with no artifact files are archived without the extra question.
- [ ] Reaper, CLI and other unattended terminations never delete artifacts.
- [ ] Deleting artifacts removes the folder, and any version data if versioning exists, and the Artifacts screen and the session's `session_output_type` reflect that.
- [ ] Restore after deletion works and starts with an empty artifact folder.
- [ ] The behaviour is the same on macOS, Linux and Windows, and state stays under `~/.ao`.

### Open questions

1. Should the setting be global, per project, or both?
2. Should "off" mean "keep silently" (as proposed) or "delete silently"?
3. Should the prompt also appear on `ao session kill` when run from an interactive terminal?
4. Should there be a later separate "delete artifacts" action for already-archived sessions?

## Summary

- **Migration `0196_session_artifact_versions`**: rows keyed by `(session_id, path, version)` that store `sha256`, `size`, `content_type`, observed `mtime` and `created_at`. Indexed on `(session_id, sha256)` for the blob reference check.
- **New `internal/artifactversions` package**
  - **Blob store**: `<artifactDir>/.versions/blobs/<sha[0:2]>/<sha>`. The file is streamed once through a sha256 hasher into an `incoming-*` temp file, then renamed into place. Content already in the store is not written twice. All blob operations go through an `os.Root` at the artifact directory, so a `.versions` symlink pointing outside it cannot redirect writes (there is a test for this). Leftover `incoming-*` files are swept the first time each session is seen after the daemon starts.
  - **Capturer**:
    - A file is captured only when its size and mtime differ from its latest version and stay the same across two consecutive observer ticks.
    - If the file changes while being copied, the copy is discarded.
    - If the content hash equals the latest version's hash, no row is written. The file is marked as checked in memory so a touch without a content change is hashed only once.
    - At most 50 versions are kept per path. A pruned blob is deleted only when no row of that session still references it.
    - Files over `attachmentstore.MaxFileBytes` are skipped.
    - Each call copies at most 64 MiB; one file is always allowed. The rest waits for the next tick.
- **`observe/artifacts`**: after the existing `ReconcileSessionOutputType` call, the observer passes each live session to the capturer. The capture therefore runs outside `reconcileMu`, and a failure in it is logged at debug level without stopping other sessions.
- **`sessionartifacts.List`** skips the top-level `.versions` directory, so snapshots are not listed as artifacts and do not count toward `session_output_type`.

## Intentionally out of scope

- **Artifact ↔ session lifecycle**: removing `.versions/` when a session is deleted, and capturing a last change made just before a session terminates (the observer still skips terminated sessions). The table keeps the `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign key from the plan's data model, so version rows follow the session row. Only the directory cleanup is deferred.
- The live `artifact-files` route is unchanged; `?v=N` and the versions list belong to Slice 2.

## Tests

- `internal/artifactversions`:
  - two-tick debounce, plus an edit-in-progress case
  - re-capture after an edit, and no re-capture when the file is unchanged
  - touch without a content change
  - reverting to earlier content creates a new version that reuses the blob
  - identical content under two paths shares one blob
  - 50-version cap prunes only unreferenced blobs
  - oversize file skipped
  - interrupted writes swept
  - snapshots are not listed as artifacts
  - escaping `.versions` symlink refused
  - per-call byte budget
  - missing artifact directory
- `store`: append, list, prune, and count by sha against real SQLite.
- `sessionartifacts`: `.versions` skipped at the top level only.
- `observe/artifacts`: capture runs for live sessions even when the reconcile fails, and terminated sessions are skipped.
- Local runs:
  - `gofmt -l .` is clean.
  - `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.
  - golangci-lint v2.13.2 reports 0 issues on the touched packages. The full-tree lint run timed out locally because it ran alongside the test suite.
  - `go test -race ./...` passes except for the tmux, goose, opencodev2, cli, systemcheck and session_manager packages. Those fail identically on unmodified `origin/main` on this machine (no tmux or goose binaries installed), so they are environmental; CI is the check for them.
- Windows: blob names are hex only and paths use `filepath.Join` through `os.Root`. Not run on a Windows machine locally, so the Windows CI job is the check.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Observations are held in memory. After a daemon restart, the first capture of a changed file is delayed by one tick.
- Open questions from the plan (which file kinds to version, retention budget) still use the defaults: all kinds under the size cap, and 50 versions per path.

title: fix(chat): open absolute-path file links instead of failing with "workspace path must be relative"
body:
Code changes: +364 -70  
Tests: +562 -4  
Others: +162 -0  

## What

Clicking a chat link to an absolute file path now opens the right file, or says clearly why it can't, instead of showing "workspace path must be relative" with a Retry button that never works.

- **Daemon:** new `GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/resolve?path=…` classifies a path as `workspace`, `artifact`, or `outside` and returns only a root-relative path.
- **Renderer:** an absolute reference is sent to the daemon before opening. A workspace result opens at the relative path, an artifact result opens through the existing artifact flow.
- **File pane:** an absolute path for the workspace source is not fetched. The pane shows "This file is outside the session's workspace, so it can't be opened here." with no Retry.

## Why

Fixes #6577.

#5119 made every absolute link a Files target. When the path was not in the session's file list (artifact directory, git-ignored files, files past the list cap), the renderer sent the absolute path to the Files API, which rejects it by design.

The same guessing also had a quieter failure: a link to `/other-repo/README.md` opened the session's own `README.md`, because the renderer matched absolute paths by suffix and basename.

## How

- The renderer is deliberately not told where a session's worktree lives (see `DesktopWorkspaceLocationResponse`), so the daemon decides which root owns a path. The response never carries an absolute path.
- `ResolveWorkspacePath` compares both the symlink-resolved and as-written spellings, so macOS `/var` → `/private/var` roots and files that do not exist yet both classify correctly. It also handles `~/`, `..` escapes, and sibling directories that share the root as a string prefix.
- `cleanWorkspaceRelativePath` is unchanged. The file, blob, tree and PR routes still reject absolute paths.
- **Fallback for older daemons:** when the resolve request fails (a remote host on a build without the route), the renderer falls back to the previous file-list matching. Only an explicit `outside` answer skips that guess. The existing remote-session test for absolute turn-diff paths covers this and passes unchanged.

Intentional omissions:

- Files outside the session are not handed to the OS or an external editor; they get the message only.
- Cloud sessions use a separate open path and are untouched.
- A multi-repo child worktree located outside the session workspace root still classifies as `outside`.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/service/session/ ./internal/httpd/...` passes, including the new classifier and route tests and the spec drift/parity tests.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 on the changed backend packages: 0 issues.

- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable

Frontend failures include missing Electron installation, sandbox-denied loopback tests, and timeouts. Full typecheck is still running. These are not reported as local passes.

title: feat(cloud): GitHub organization members see the App repositories they can access
body:
## Problem

A GitHub organization **member** (not an owner) saw none of the organization's repositories in AO, not even the ones the owner had already selected for the AO GitHub App.

- AO only connected an organization's App installation for **owners** of the GitHub organization (`UserCanAdministerInstallation` requires the org `admin` role), so a member's AO organization never got any repository grants.
- The desktop's **Connect repository** opens GitHub's install page, and GitHub itself stops a member there ("This action must be performed by an organization owner"), so the member never reaches AO's callback for that organization.

## What changes (server only)

**User-scoped installation connections.** A member can now connect an organization's installation *user-scoped*, into their **personal AO organization** (one where they are the only member):

- AO grants only the repositories GitHub says the member can access within the installation (`GET /user/installations/{id}/repositories`, with the member's own GitHub authorization). It never grants the whole installation.
- Owners keep whole-installation connections, and a later user-scoped connect never narrows one.
- User-scoped connections into a team AO organization are refused (409 `github_user_scope_personal_org_only`), so one member's GitHub access never reaches AO teammates who lack it.

**Connecting your own account connects the rest.** The App installation callback now keeps the user's GitHub authorization, and connects every other installation that authorization can see: whole where the user administers it, user-scoped otherwise. So after connecting their own account, a member sees the organization repositories they can access. This step is best effort and never fails the callback.

**Access follows GitHub, and fails closed.**

- **Sync:** every sync of a user-scoped connection, including webhook-triggered ones, lists repositories with the member's authorization. If that authorization is gone, or GitHub no longer lets the member reach the installation, the grants are revoked.
- **Tokens:** before AO mints any checkout, push, pull-request, review or merge token through a user-scoped connection, it re-checks the member's access live (`GET /repositories/{id}`): read for checkout, push for writes. A session's extra repositories are filtered the same way.
- **Polling:** listing installations refreshes a user-scoped connection that is more than 5 minutes stale. The desktop polls that list while picking a repository.

**Schema:** migration `00081_github_installation_user_scope.sql` adds `access_scope` (`installation` | `user`, default `installation`) and `scope_user_id` to `ao_github_installations`. Existing rows are unchanged.

**API:** `GitHubInstallation` gains `accessScope`. No new endpoints, and no desktop change is needed: the app already lists every repository granted to the AO organization.

## Tests

- **`githubapp`:**
  - a user-scoped sync grants only the member's repositories;
  - every fail-closed path: authorization gone, GitHub 404 and 401 revoke everything, while a transient 5xx changes nothing;
  - live checkout and push checks, including extra repositories;
  - connect scopes the installation by ownership;
  - the installation callback connects the user's other installations.
- **`postgres` (real Postgres):**
  - user-scoped bind works in a personal org and is refused in a team org;
  - a whole connection is never narrowed;
  - the scope survives reads;
  - the user's authorization is saved from the callback.
- **Full suite:** all Go tests pass, except 4 Postgres tests that also fail on `main` (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`).

## Out of scope

Repositories on accounts where the AO App is **not installed at all** (e.g. a personal repo you collaborate on). GitHub never returns those to an App, even acting for the user; showing them would need the user's own token.

title: feat: keep mobile access awake with the MacBook lid closed
body:
Code changes: +1088 -39  
Tests: +804 -2  
Others: +391 -2  

Adds an explicit **Keep awake with lid closed** option to Connect Mobile on Apple Silicon MacBooks with macOS 13–27. Enabling lid mode also enables Keep awake in one request; turning Keep awake off clears lid mode, while turning only lid mode off preserves idle wake. With mobile access enabled, AO can arm native lid control so mobile work remains reachable when the laptop closes. It remains enabled through phone disconnects; disabling mobile access, switching the option off, or quitting AO withdraws the daemon's lease.

The daemon manages preferences and mobile lifetime. A bundled, unprivileged Swift helper uses launchd, identity-checked renewable leases, and a persisted ownership journal to recover after crashes without releasing another AO instance's live lease. Battery below 10%, unknown battery state, and critical thermal state release lid control and latch the stop until explicit off/on. The helper darkens the panel when closed and undocked.

### Latest review follow-up (`c97b9443a`)

The main Keep awake switch now explicitly sends `lidClosed: false` when switching both on and off. Its optimistic cache also clears the lid preference and active flag. A legacy saved lid choice therefore cannot silently arm closed-lid mode or flash as checked while the main switch request is pending. Closed-lid mode still requires using the lid switch. The final settings suite passes (54 tests; 6 skipped), including a regression covering the pending POST and settled refetch.

### Prior review follow-up (`c86286f49`)

- Treat the lid option as a mode of Keep awake: enabling lid mode enables idle wake; disabling idle wake clears lid mode; disabling only lid mode preserves idle wake. An inactive remembered lid choice is shown unchecked.
- Align both switches at the trailing edge. The child row uses matching label typography with indented, muted supporting text.
- Include macOS 27 in the explicit native capability range without raising the app minimum OS. An older registered helper whose capability probe fails produces the existing manual upgrade instructions.
- ADR 0005 records Prasad’s basic macOS 26 lid-close/phone-connectivity pass. Model and power source were not reported. Interactive work, panel darkness/locking, battery/charger transitions, multiple daemons, disable/quit, daemon/helper SIGKILL recovery, login/reboot, update/removal and macOS 13/14/15/27 physical coverage remain unreported.
- Native policy/recovery tests, arm64/x64 builds, helper packaging-script tests, and final focused settings/mobilebridge tests pass. Complete local suites are running. Remote CI is not yet claimed for this head.

### Review follow-up (`bbc4dc0df`, `52e003b6f`)

- Native protocol 2 binds coordinator state to the default durable root (`~/.ao/data/wake`). Existing protocol-1 registrations require the documented lid-open/off/unload/re-enable upgrade procedure and are never replaced automatically.
- Require private permissions only on the wake subtree, preserving the daemon's 0750 parent.
- Complete registration before saving a new lid opt-in; native activation failures report `LidReason` without failing ordinary Keep awake.
- Serialize registration and reuse compatible registered helpers without booting out other builds; fresh registration cleans obsolete helper copies. Native helper upgrades require opening the lid, disabling all leases, unloading the old registration, and opting in again.
- Keep status readable during cleanup, allow a 30-second freshness margin, and use Standard launchd scheduling for fresh registrations.
- Request display sleep only on transitions into an owned closed/undocked state. Use the existing UUID dependency and explicit lid interfaces.

On the preceding head, all CI checks passed, including the complete frontend/typecheck/docs/renderer suite, both native helper builds, CLI coverage, backend race shards, lint, and API/sqlc drift. The unrelated ACP replay stress timeout passed on a failed-job rerun. Local regression tests, affected backend race suites, pinned lint, native policy tests, arm64/x64 builds, cross-platform Go compilation, frontend typechecking, and docs builds pass. Five broad-run frontend timeouts passed in complete isolated file-suite rechecks (204 tests); the unrelated local ACP package also passes on recheck. The original validation results below describe the preceding head.

### Validation

- Affected backend race suites, pinned golangci-lint, and API regeneration drift checks pass.
- Full frontend: 451 test files, 7,445 tests passed; 7 skipped. Frontend and E2E typechecks pass.
- Native policy/recovery regression tests and arm64/x64 compilation pass; helper build-script tests pass.
- Desktop packaging, docs build, shared package checks, and guarded-navigation browser integration pass.
- Full backend race run: 195 packages pass; four OpenCode adapter packages fail and reproduce on the unchanged implementation base (`e06b1a824`).
- Renderer smoke: 49 pass, 27 fail outside the changed mobile settings flow. This is an outstanding validation gap, not a local pass.
- Docker/pinned Linux container validation was unavailable locally. Remote CI remains required.

### Release gate and follow-ups

Keep this PR **draft** until colleagues verify physical lid operation on the supported macOS versions: AC/battery, charger transitions, panel darkness, locking, multiple daemons, disable/full quit, daemon/helper crashes, login/reboot, and update/removal. Prasad reported a basic lid-close/continued-phone-connectivity pass on one macOS 26 MacBook. Remaining physical checks, especially daemon/helper SIGKILL recovery, are pending. This implementation session ran automated checks and read-only probing only; no host power controls were exercised. `lidActive` reports that the native command is armed, not physical verification.

The native lid control is a global kernel control with no ownership token. AO instances of the same login using the default `~/.ao/data` durable data root coordinate through `~/.ao/data/wake`. Custom or scratch data roots disable native lid control so they cannot alter production state or host power; ordinary Keep awake remains available. Concurrent unrelated lid utilities and other logins do not participate in that protocol and are unsupported. No administrator installation, new network listener, or persistent `pmset disablesleep` setting is added.

Phase two remains separate: awake session presets/timers, broader automatic activation, advanced display/battery/thermal policies, pausing apps, agent/network extras, and expanded recovery controls. The desktop application's minimum macOS version remains unchanged.
