title: fix(chat): don't hibernate agents mid-work, and stop replaying Claude's notes as user turns
body:
Code changes: +61 -8\
Tests: +85 -7\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Chat no longer hibernates an agent while it is working on its own after an AO turn, and a woken Claude chat no longer shows Claude Code's own transcript notes as user messages.

Fixes #6460. Supersedes #6464 (its commit is included unchanged, so its author keeps credit) and #6217 (same replay filter, extended to the interrupt marker).

## Why

After an AO turn completes, Claude Code keeps working on its own when a background task's `<task-notification>` arrives. AO has no turn for that work, and session activity stays `idle`. Every AO-side guard in `HibernateChat` passes. The Claude bridge's `_ao/session/can_hibernate` only looked at live background tasks, and the finished task had already left that registry. So the sweep stopped the host mid-work.

On wake, `session/load` replays the transcript tail. AO turned each Claude-authored user record into a `recovered` user turn: the `<task-notification>` XML, and the `[Request interrupted by user]` marker that Claude Code writes when its host is stopped mid-turn.

## How

| Harness | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Harness | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Claude (ACP) | bridge checks background tasks only | also requires the SDK's last `session_state_changed` to be `idle` (from #6464), and waits 10 s after a task ends |
| Codex app-server | an autonomous `turn/started` is adopted as a running AO turn | unchanged: the running-turn guard in `HibernateChat` already covers it |
| Other ACP agents | no provider check | unchanged: none is known to work without a prompt |

- `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.mjs` (from #6464): the bridge reads `session_state_changed` in one consumer loop for the whole session, so the state is `running` for the whole autonomous cycle, including a silent tool call.
- `frontend/scripts/build-acp-runtime-helpers.mjs`: the bridge drops a finished task from its registry before the SDK reports the notification cycle as `running`. I measured that gap at 79 ms on Claude Code 2.1.296. The check now refuses for 10 s after a task ends, so a sweep cannot land in the gap.
- `acp/driver.go`, `acp/history.go`: a new `HistoryNotice` hook on the ACP driver config. Only the Claude binding sets it. Replay starts no turn for a user message the hook matches, so the agent's output after it stays in the turn before, as it did live.
- `claudeacp/checkpoint.go`: the Claude check matches a message that starts with `<task-notification>`, or that is a `[Request interrupted by user…]` marker. It matches on the opening tag because Claude Code can add text after the closing tag, for example a check-in for a long-running shell.
- `claudeacp/checkpoint.go`: the checkpoint verifier for TUI → Chat handoffs treats the same notes, and `isMeta` records, as notes. Replay never shows `isMeta` records, because `getSessionMessages` drops them. A note with the same prompt as the turn before (an interrupt marker) adds no turn. When the latest native turn starts with a note, the boundary names the user turn before it, which is the turn that replay produces. Without this, a TUI session whose last cycle answered a task notification or a peer message, or that had any interrupted turn, could not switch to Chat.

The transcript records carry a structured `origin.kind`, but the SDK's `getSessionMessages`, which the bridge's replay uses, returns only the API message. So the check uses the text.

Not in scope:
- A pending Claude `ScheduleWakeup` or cron while the SDK is idle with no live tasks is still invisible, so such a session can hibernate and lose the wakeup.
- Notification turns that were already imported stay in history.
- Replay sees only the text, so a human prompt that starts with `<task-notification>` is also treated as a note.
- A Claude query that never reports `idle` again keeps its host awake. That is the safe side.

## Testing

### Before and after, in the desktop app

The prompt asks Claude to:
1. Run `./test.sh` in the background and end its turn.
2. When it is notified, run `./build.sh` (40 s) in the foreground.
3. Run `./check.sh 1` through `./check.sh 8` as separate foreground calls.
4. Reply "Verified."

The user leaves the chat as soon as AO's turn completes.

title: fix(kiro): map preToolUse to active and detect approvals via terminal
body:
Code changes: +298 -3
Tests: +150 -0
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #6415. Kiro TUI sessions showed Input needed for ordinary tool use and kept it sticky: AO installed Kiro `preToolUse` as `permission-request`, and the name-only deriver maps that to sticky `waiting_input`. Since `preToolUse` fires for every tool invocation (including auto-approved/trusted tools) and Kiro installs no post-tool clear, Activity stayed parked until `stop`/`userPromptSubmit`, with no terminal recovery path.

- `kiro/hooks.go`: `preToolUse` now installs `pre-tool-use` (active); install strips the legacy `permission-request` entry so upgraded workspaces stop emitting the old signal.
- `kiro/activity.go` (new): deriver maps `pre-tool-use`/`post-tool-use*`/`permission-resolved` and legacy `permission-request` to active; continuous terminal detection reports genuine approval dialogs (Yes/Trust/No bar, classic `Allow this action? [y/n/t]`) as `waiting_input`. Detection requires actual dialog controls (classic marker, or a header plus short approve/deny option labels incl. key hints like `No (Tab to edit)`) and stops at answered prompts — same-line echoes and separate-line answers — so scrollback cannot flip a finished turn back to waiting.
- `activitydispatch`: `kiro` uses its own deriver.

Verified: `go build ./...`, `go test` on `kiro`, `activitydispatch`, `activitystate`, `lifecycle`, `observe/activity` green; `go vet`, `gofmt` and `golangci-lint` clean on touched packages. One `cli` failure (`TestRenderCheckReplacesItsEarlierScreenshot`) reproduces on clean main — Windows symlink privilege, unrelated.

Intentional omissions: Copilot stays as-is (separate observe-hooks fix per #6415); ACP Chat approval events (#5604) left as future work — approval clears at turn boundary until idle/active TUI markers are captured.

title: feat(chat): complete native conversation-fork integration in ChatUI
body:
Complete native conversation forks in ChatUI wherever the provider API supports them. A fork must retain the provider’s context, keep the parent and child independent, and recover on its own provider host.

This issue covers native ChatUI forks and their lifecycle only.

## Provider audit

Audited all 14 registered Chat drivers against main `1cb8416eba29a4bee6a69141e45a1819db45eeb7`. Installed ACP capability responses were collected on 13 October 2026 without sending prompts. Capabilities are negotiated for each running conversation; the table is evidence for these versions, not a permanent provider-name allowlist.

| Chat provider | Native fork API / evidence | Implementation scope |
|---|---|---|
| Codex | Existing native app-server `thread/fork`, with completed-turn anchors | Preserve exact historical forks; add whole-conversation isolated forks and regression coverage |
| Claude Code | Bundled official Claude ACP 0.70.0 advertises `session/fork`, load, resume, close, delete | Wire current-context native forks into independent side chats; activate and configure the child |
| OpenCode 1 | Installed 1.18.35 advertises `session/fork`, load, resume, close | Shared ACP fork integration |
| OpenCode 2 | [Upstream ACP service](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/cli/src/acp/service.ts) advertises and implements fork | Shared ACP fork integration; preserve isolated OpenCode 2 ownership IDs and data home |
| Kimi | Installed 2.0.0 advertises fork, load, resume, close, delete | Shared ACP fork integration; older versions without this advertisement retain reconstruction |
| OMP | Installed 18.2.4 advertises fork, load, resume, close | Shared ACP fork integration |
| Pi / pi-acp | [The supported adapter](https://github.com/victor-software-house/pi-acp/blob/main/src/acp/agent.ts) advertises and implements fork | Shared ACP fork integration; existing Pi permission/admission limits remain |
| Unreal Agent | Pinned SDK 0.1.1 exposes `sessionstore.Store.Fork` | Connect native anchored and isolated forks; translate AO request IDs to native SDK turn boundaries |
| Droid | Installed 0.237.0 advertises load/list/resume; no fork | No native fork to expose on this ACP version |
| Cursor | Installed ACP initialize advertises load/list; no fork | No native fork to expose on this ACP version |
| DeepSeek Harness | Installed ACP agent 0.0.1 advertises close/list/resume; no fork | No native fork to expose on this ACP version |
| Kimchi | [Upstream ACP server](https://github.com/getkimchi/kimchi/blob/master/src/modes/acp/server.ts) advertises load/list/close; no fork | Do not treat the CLI’s internal fork machinery as an advertised ACP fork |
| Qwen | [Upstream ACP agent](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts) advertises load/list/resume; no standard fork | Standard ACP support is capability-gated; private serve-control branch extensions require a separately verified contract |
| Command Code | Existing adapter’s recorded v1.74 handshake has load/list/resume/close; no fork; not installed locally | Shared integration will enable native forks when the running ACP agent advertises them |

The remaining registered harnesses have no Chat driver: Aider, Grok, Amp, Agy, Crush, Gemini, Copilot, Goose, Auggie, Continue, Devin, Cline, Muse, Kiro, Kilocode, Vibe, Prime Agent, Autohand, FX, Codewhale, MiMo Code, and OpenHands. Terminal or internal CLI fork support alone does not establish a usable ChatUI fork API.

## Required behavior

- [x] Negotiate ACP `sessionCapabilities.fork` and implement `session/fork` on an independent host using the existing typed SDK.
- [x] Distinguish current-context forks from historical turn-anchored forks. A current-only capability must not enable historical message editing.
- [x] Expose existing side chats for admitted local Chat sessions; select native versus reconstructed context through live capabilities, including after parent hibernation.
- [x] Keep the workspace, model, effort, permissions, standing instructions, additional directories, MCP configuration, and child identity consistent.
- [x] Activate the child before prompting, including adapters that return only a persisted fork ID. [Claude ACP’s newer activation regression](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/issues/1110) makes this necessary.
- [x] Preserve child setup and ownership across detached-host reconnect; reject malformed, parent-equal, or already-owned destination IDs.
- [x] Keep a current-only fork’s parent quiescent until its snapshot is captured. Reject a changed cutoff rather than inheriting later parent messages; preserve frozen transcript reconstruction when a current-only fork cannot represent the requested boundary.
- [x] Connect Unreal’s existing native fork API, including requests spanning tool turns and compaction, without replaying inherited work as new instructions.
- [x] Terminate failed/closed child hosts and delete positively owned child sessions only when the provider offers deletion; never delete the parent. Providers without deletion may retain their durable native history.
- [x] Cover protocol, reconnect, cutoff/race, cleanup, and all 14 Chat providers’ UI eligibility with deterministic tests; verify retained context and independence live with available authenticated Claude.

An independent fork shares the existing workspace and Git state. Forking provider history does not copy filesystem state; this issue does not add a new-session fork flow that silently creates a different worktree.

## Implemented behavior

ACP adapters that advertise resumable `session/fork` now fork on an independent provider host and activate the child through load/resume before its first prompt. Claude's checkpoint wrapper forwards the optional fork interface. Reconnect adopts the child identity and saved setup, preserving model, effort, permissions, standing context, directories and MCP configuration. Codex retains historical anchors and gains whole-conversation isolated forks. Unreal uses its existing SDK fork with AO request IDs mapped to the final native turn, including tools and compaction.

Current-context-only ACP forks are distinct from exact historical forks and do not enable historical message editing. The service wakes hibernated parents, leases them through setup and fences parent intake while copying. A busy parent or unsuitable cutoff uses frozen transcript reconstruction; a cutoff that changes during native setup fails closed. The child shares workspace files and Git state, while provider history and host ownership remain independent.

Cleanup rejects parent IDs, terminates failed or closed child hosts, and deletes only registered children where the provider supports deletion. Cleanup records retain their original harness identity so changing the parent provider cannot delete a different provider's session. Providers without deletion retain their owned native history and pending cleanup ID.

## Verification

- **Passed:** deterministic ACP, Claude wrapper, Codex, Unreal and persistent-host race suites; Chat service race shard 0 and focused fork/wake/side regressions; 61 focused ChatUI tests; frontend and E2E typechecks; lint with zero issues; API/sqlc drift; docs build; Cloud Go/client and product UI tests/typechecks; native macOS CLI E2E; native helper checks; guarded-navigation Electron integration.
- **Passed live:** official Claude ACP 0.70.0 retained parent context, isolated parent/child changes in both directions, recovered the child after host termination, and cleaned up (`TestLiveNativeACPForks/claude-code`, 189.37 s).
- **Passed in the real Electron app:** `/btw` created an independent Claude side conversation, which recalled synthetic marker `FROZEN-LAB-42` from the parent without a transcript seed. A sanitized screenshot is saved locally; it has not been uploaded to GitHub.
- **Incomplete model-backed checks:** Kimi requires authentication, OpenCode's configured account has insufficient balance, and OMP's endpoint fails DNS resolution. OpenCode 2, Pi ACP and the other audited upstream adapters are not installed locally; Codex and Unreal have deterministic native-fork coverage for this change but no new model-backed run. Shared-protocol tests are not a claim of live success.
- **Broad local validation gaps:** Chat shard 1 timed out in the unchanged 20,544-event ACP replay test; the unchanged OpenCode 2 malformed-version fixture selects the installed OpenCode 1 fallback; the unchanged browser-profile import suite crashes in native SQLite/Node teardown. The full frontend run completed 7,506 tests with one native worker crash; local renderer smoke finished 46 passed / 30 startup-screen failures, while CI’s renderer smoke passed. Chat shard 1’s retry ran out of disk space, and the broad backend run and local container builds were stopped as disk space ran low. CI results and remaining checks are recorded on the implementation PR.

Implementation: [PR #6616](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6616), commit `14d5a7ed7`. Final validation evidence is recorded in the comments on this same issue and the PR.


**Final CI result:** all 24 checks passed for implementation commit `14d5a7ed7`, including the full frontend suite and complete backend Chat, SQLite and session race shards. [PR #6616](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6616) is ready for review. Live model-backed verification remains limited to Claude as described above.

title: perf(desktop): cut startup JS and idle background work
body:
Code changes: +415 -80\
Tests: +314 -15\
Others: +469 -0 (plan doc, generated tray catalog; plus 1 binary: smaller mascot PNG)

## What

Frontend-only performance work for the desktop app: less JavaScript before first paint, less work while idle, and fewer redundant fetches. No daemon, API, schema, or settings changes.

Startup:
- Cache compiled renderer code across launches (`codeCache` on the `app://` scheme).
- Keep the window hidden until the renderer has loaded, with a 2.5s fallback, so the first frame is the app instead of an empty native frame.
- Attach to a running daemon without waiting for the login-shell probe (still awaited before spawning one).
- Load non-English catalogs on demand through an i18next backend; only English ships at startup.
- Give the tray its own 9-key catalog instead of bundling every renderer catalog into `main.js`.
- Load PostHog inside `initTelemetry` instead of at module load.
- Lazy-load xterm and the orchestrator starting chat, warm both when idle, and contain a failed chunk to its own panel.
- Ship the startup mascot at 256px instead of 1254px.

Idle and sync:
- One owner for the workspace poll timer instead of one per subscribing component.
- Event stream starts at the newest event (`?after=latest`) instead of replaying the change log on every connect; on open, every event-routed cache is refreshed. A daemon that rejects the cursor falls back to the old stream.
- Skip the lifecycle refresh when main re-pushes an unchanged daemon status. Attached to a daemon it did not spawn, that refetched every open conversation and the workspace list every 10s.
- Keep the daemon status and update status objects when nothing changed, so the shell and sidebar stop re-rendering on each poll. Waiting update states poll every 30s.
- Side-chat state backstop poll 500ms to 5s (the renderer already captures after every change).
- Shell loader dedupes workspace fetches within 2s.

The plan doc in `docs/plans/2026-10-13-desktop-performance-overhaul.md` has the full audit and the larger follow-ups (cached data instead of the startup splash, session switching, chat streaming).

## Why

The app spends most of its startup parsing JavaScript it does not need yet, and a lot of idle time refetching data that has not changed.

Measured A/B, same machine and Electron, real data (45 sessions), medians of 5 runs, `origin/main` vs this branch:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main.js` | 2,259 KB | 780 KB |
| JS before first paint | 2,636 KB (742 KB gzip) | 846 KB (259 KB gzip) |
| Launch to first paint | 620 ms | 488 ms |
| Launch to usable | 2,164 ms | 1,991 ms |
| Reload to usable | 1,037 ms | 593 ms |
| JS heap | 23.3 MB | 15.9 MB |
| Idle CPU (app) | 2.2% | 1.4% |
| Session switch, revisit, settled | 364 ms | 253 ms |

Cold launch to usable only moves 8%: about 1.5s of it is the daemon starting behind the splash, which this PR does not touch.

## How

- Lazy locales use an i18next backend, so every `changeLanguage()` waits for its catalog. Test setup preloads all catalogs into the shared instance; `instance.test.ts` covers the lazy path. `all-messages.ts` is test-only.
- `LazyChunkBoundary` reuses existing translated strings (`appError.title`, `titlebar.reload`).
- `scripts/sync-tray-catalog.mjs` regenerates the tray catalog; `tray-catalog.test.ts` fails if it drifts from the renderer JSON.

Intentional omissions: no daemon changes (per-token DB writes, pty ring byte cap, background pollers are listed in the plan doc). A bound on the stable diff cache was tried and reverted: evicting a mounted diff can trip Pierre's identity check.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `frontend/src` (`packages/product-ui` needs its own install locally).
- `npx vitest run`: 456 files, 7,512 tests pass. Run with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`: `ContextMeter` and one `ChatWorkspace` test format numbers with the system locale and fail on `main` too under `en-IN`.
- `npx playwright test`: 91 passed, 24 failed, 4 skipped. The same 24 fail on the base commit in this environment; none fail only on this branch. One CI-only race fixed in `cross-platform-focus.spec.ts`: the test clicked the project menu while the startup screen still covered it (faster startup made this likely); it now waits for the startup screen, 60/60 cold runs pass.
- Upgrade smoke on throwaway state: the `origin/main` build seeds a profile and data dir with Japanese saved and a project added, then this build launches on it. Usable in about 2s, Japanese UI, project listed, terminal opens, reload recovers, no uncaught exceptions (10/10).
- Three review passes (correctness, async/races, build and standards): no open P0 or P1.

Not covered locally: a signed packaged `.app` (benchmarks and the smoke test ran the production bundles under stock Electron to avoid install relocation), Windows and Linux.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [ ] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable (several small perf changes with one goal; see the plan doc)
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`test`, `renderer-smoke`, `mac-update-helper`, `scan`)

title: feat(desktop): macOS window transparency behind a Developer Mode flag
body:
Code changes: +207 -2  
Tests: +3 -0  
Others: +16 -0 (translations)

https://jumpshare.com/s/NgQ2TB3pNYQch7XDJVlr

## What

A new Developer Mode toggle, **Window transparency** (macOS only, off by default), that lets the desktop show through the app window with a native blur.

## How it works

- The window uses macOS vibrancy (`under-window`). With an opaque window Chromium's compositor hides the blur, so the macOS window is now created with `transparent: true`. With the flag off it still paints the normal theme color.
- The shell paints one tint layer at 70% of the theme color. Everything else in the chrome is clear, so translucent layers never stack into darker patches.
- Cards, buttons, the composer and hover fills become light foreground overlays, so they read one step up from the material instead of as solid blocks.
- Menus, popovers, tooltips and dialogs (including `z-overlay` custom menus) keep their solid theme colors.
- A live browser page sits below the shell, so `useBrowserView` publishes the page rect and the tint is masked out over it. Without this the existing native browser rules cleared the tint and the whole window brightened.

## Performance

Measured over 3 alternating runs of 8s chat scrolling at 120Hz:

- Frame pacing is the same: about 119 fps, p95 9.0 vs 9.1 ms, p99 9.3 ms in both modes.
- Renderer style and layout time is unchanged.
- The one real cost is WindowServer redrawing the blur when content behind the window changes. It reached about 25% of one core in one idle run with a busy terminal behind the window.

## Not covered

- No new tests, and typecheck and the test suite were not run before opening this.
- `transparent: true` now applies to every macOS window, even with the flag off. It looks the same, but it was not benchmarked against a fully opaque window.
- Content that scrolls under a header that only had the canvas color can show through.
- Only dark mode was checked by eye.

title: Browser panel: endless "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getURL')" main-process error after signing in through a popup tab
body:
While working with a standalone agent session in the Browser panel (signing in to ElevenLabs, with a second `elevenlabs.io/__/auth/…` tab open), the desktop app showed **"A JavaScript error occurred in the main process — Uncaught Exception: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getURL')"**. Dismissing it with OK just brings it back immediately, every time. The app is completely stuck, and ⌘Q doesn't quit it.

- Version: 0.13.8-nightly.202610122149, macOS
- Expected: the browser keeps working (or at worst the failing tab goes away), and the app stays usable / quittable.

title: fix(browser): drop tabs whose page closed itself
body:
Code changes: +56 -6  
Tests: +66 -0  
Others: +0 -0

Fixes #6619

## Problem
A page in a Browser panel tab can close itself with `window.close()` when the tab has only one history entry. OAuth popup handlers (for example Firebase's `/__/auth/handler`, which ElevenLabs sign-in uses) do this after sign-in. Electron destroys the WebContents and `WebContentsView.webContents` becomes `undefined`. The tab stayed in the session, so every `browser:setBounds` IPC hit `applySessionBounds` → `entry.view.webContents.getURL()` and threw inside an `ipcMain.on` listener. Electron showed "A JavaScript error occurred in the main process" again on every layout change, so the dialog looped and the app was unusable.

## Fix
- Listen for each tab's `destroyed` event and reuse the existing close path with cached identity, navigation metadata and Electron session. Never dereference the destroyed contents.
- Remove a dead tab before activating its replacement, so the previous-view layout code never touches the destroyed native view. Stop network capture, clear native targeting/snapshot state, remove the child view and publish the closed tab event.
- Match current main's empty-browser behavior: self-closing the last tab leaves zero tabs and returns focus to the shell. A later new-tab action recreates a usable tab. Release the last tab's shared network watcher using the cached Electron session.
- During session teardown the ownership guard prevents duplicate cleanup. During profile replacement, drop the old mapping and let the rebuild proceed.
- Retain the defensive `webContents?.getURL()` check in `applySessionBounds`.

## Validation
- Focused browser-host suite: 204 tests passed on Node 24.
- Real Electron guarded-navigation integration passed.
- Added regression checks for a self-closed popup, layout calls on destroyed native views, empty last-tab state, network-watcher cleanup and opening a new tab afterward.
- Product UI and Cloud client typechecks/tests/packaging dry runs passed; macOS packaging configuration tests and update-helper builds/state tests passed.
- Complete frontend suite, typechecks, renderer smoke and docs build are being rerun with bounded concurrency after an overloaded local run. Remote checks must pass before merge.

This PR fixes tab cleanup only. Preserving OAuth popup handles/opener communication is a separate follow-up; successful ElevenLabs login was manually verified with that follow-up applied.

title: fix(import): let workspace import continue past child repos without a remote
body:
Part of #6623

## Summary
The Import workspace dialog disabled **Continue** when *any* child repo lacked an origin remote or a first commit, and its "Setup required" badge had no action. Users were left with only Cancel or Back. #5122 introduced this when it removed #4945's inline per-child setup.

The daemon never required this. `detectWorkspaceChildren` registers those children as `needs_init`, sessions skip them, and the import fails only when **no** child is ready (`WORKSPACE_NO_READY_REPOS`; covered by `TestManager_AddWorkspaceAcceptsChildWithoutOriginAsNeedsInit`).

This PR is frontend only:
- When at least one child repo is ready, Continue is enabled. Each child without a remote or commit is labelled explicitly, e.g. **"No remote · Not included"**, and the dialog says: *"The repository marked below has no commit or origin remote yet. AO will import this workspace without it, and agents will not work in it."* No defaults are applied silently; the dialog states what will happen.
- When no child is ready, the dialog behaves as before: Continue is disabled and "Set an origin remote…" is shown, because the daemon rejects that case.
- New strings are added to all locales.

## Tests
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.test.tsx src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n`: 251 passed
- Two of these tests fail on `main` and pass with this change: the new `CreateProjectFlow` test (one ready child plus one remote-less child) and the updated `Sidebar` test (one ready child plus children without a commit or remote).
- `npm run typecheck`: passes
- **Real Electron app**, run against isolated data (`~/.ao/dev/ao132`, daemon on `127.0.0.1:3002`) with a fixture workspace: `reevo-warehouse` has a commit but no origin, and `harvey-legal-workflow` and `pulse` have origins. The dialog showed `reevo-warehouse — No remote · Not included` with Continue enabled. Continue → Create workspace and start created the workspace project. The daemon registered `harvey-legal-workflow` and `pulse` as `ready` and `reevo-warehouse` as `needs_init`, the parent `.gitignore` lists all three, and the orchestrator opened.

## Risks / follow-ups
- An excluded child is left out for good: it stays `needs_init` even after the user adds a remote, because children are detected only at registration. A follow-up could re-detect children, or bring back an inline "set remote" action in this dialog.
- Remote-less children still can't host agent worktrees. Making remotes optional (#5623, closed without merging; related #4679) is a separate change.

title: feat(sessions): keep or delete artifacts when archiving a session
body:
Code changes: +341 -56 (includes +54 locale strings)
Tests: +347 -4
Others: +31 -1 (generated OpenAPI spec, TS schema, sqlc) Refs #6580 ## What changes When you archive a session that has artifact files, the archive dialog shows one extra option, unchecked by default: > ☐ **Delete 2 artifacts** > This can't be undone, and a restored session starts without them. - Left unchecked, Confirm archives the session and keeps the files, same as today. - Checked, Confirm turns red and archives the session, then deletes its artifact files. - The box resets to unchecked every time the dialog opens. - Sessions with no artifact files, and cloud sessions, get the old dialog unchanged. This follows the direction from the Discord thread: no new setting, just a choice in the dialog we already show. The shared `ConfirmDialog` now takes `children` for options like this. It also drops the divider under the header and above the footer, which changes all confirm dialogs. ## How it works - `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/kill` takes an optional body, `{"deleteArtifacts": true}`. With no body it behaves exactly as before. - After the kill succeeds, `Service.DeleteArtifacts` refuses a session that is not terminated, or one whose stored artifact dir is outside the current data dir. Then it calls `Capturer.DeleteSession` on the artifact version capturer: - It holds the capture lock, so a capture already running can't write snapshots or version rows after the files are gone. - It renames `/artifacts//` into `/artifacts-trash/` first, which moves all of it or none of it. A locked file (Windows) fails the delete with every file still in place, not halfway through. The trash is then removed. Anything left behind is retried on the next delete. - It recreates an empty artifact folder so a restore starts with one. - It deletes the session's `session_artifact_versions` rows. - The service then reconciles `session_output_type` (`artifact` becomes `none`, `pr_artifact` becomes `pr`), even when the delete failed. - If the delete fails, the request still returns 200 (the session is already archived) with `artifactsDeleted` left out, and the daemon logs a warning. Failing the request would make the UI roll back an archive that actually happened. - When the user checked the box and the response doesn't confirm the delete, the UI shows an error toast: "Session archived, artifacts kept". This also covers a remote host whose daemon predates the option and ignores the flag. - Only the archive dialog sends the flag. `ao session kill`, cleanup, and the reaper never delete artifacts. ## Testing - Go: controller tests for no body, the delete flag, a failed delete still returning 200, and a malformed body returning 400. Capturer tests against a real SQLite store: files and version rows are gone and the folder is empty; a capture after the delete records nothing; a failed move leaves every file and version in place; leftover trash is cleared. Service tests: the delete goes through the capturer; a live session is refused; an artifact dir outside the data dir is refused; the output type is reconciled even when the delete fails. Store test for the new delete query. The delete and capture tests pass under `-race`. - Vitest: the box shows "Delete N artifacts" with the warning and no file names; unchecked sends no body; checked turns Confirm red and sends `deleteArtifacts: true`; the box resets on reopen; the error toast shows only when the daemon doesn't confirm the delete. - Manually in the isolated desktop app: archived a session with 4 files and deleted them. The folder was empty, `outputType` went to `none`, and restoring the session worked with an empty artifact folder. Also checked the final checkbox dialog without the dividers. - `golangci-lint`: 0 issues. `go test ./...`: everything passes except the opencode adapter packages, which fail locally because they read this machine's `~/.local/share/opencode`. These packages aren't touched here. - `npm run typecheck` and `typecheck:e2e` pass. Full `vitest run`: 25 local failures, all unrelated. 22 are in `browser-profile-import.test.ts` (the `better-sqlite3` native module wasn't rebuilt in this checkout) and 3 are context-meter tests (this machine's locale formats 262,144 as 2,62,144). ## Not in this PR - A per-project or global setting from the issue. The checkbox replaces it. - A "delete artifacts" action for sessions that are already archived. - A prompt for `ao session kill` in an interactive terminal. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_014pPZSCXpZabYeL4hDdqvz6

title: feat(chat): recall sent messages with Up/Down in the composer
body:
Code changes: +220 -24  
Tests: +683 -3  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

While the chat input is focused, **Up/Down recall the conversation's sent messages** into the composer for editing or resending, like shell history.

- **Up** with the caret at the very start of the input (always true when it is empty) steps back to older sent messages; **Down** steps forward and, past the newest, restores the draft the user had before browsing. Every step leaves the caret at the start so either key continues; Down also continues from the end after reading down a long message.
- Browsing **never sends**, and a recalled message is **never saved as the draft until the user edits it**: leaving mid-walk keeps the user's own text. Editing a recalled message (typing, accepting a completion, pasting an image) makes it the draft and ends the walk; sending ends it too.
- History is the active conversation's **human prompts and human steers as the timeline shows them**, in sequence order. It excludes assistant output, automation messages and automation steers, rolled-back and queued turns. Unmatched local echoes are included without duplicating their durable rows. AO's attachment and worker-report footers are stripped, and consecutive repeats collapse.
- A walk keeps the list it started with while messages stream in, but **activating another branch or conversation drops the walk and restores the draft**, so abandoned-branch prompts are never recalled.
- **The saved draft stays intact during a walk:**
  - Moving the caret through a recalled `/skill` never auto-completes it.
  - Removing an image while browsing also removes it from the held draft, and saves that.
  - Recall waits while attachments are being read or staged, so a pasted image's inline chip is never lost.
- Native behavior is preserved inside multiline text, for text selections, modifier chords, IME composition, and while a `/` or `@` completion menu is open (the menu keeps the arrows).
- Recall is disabled during queued-message edits, pending or uncertain deliveries, and when the composer is disabled. Excerpt references are untouched.
- As with any non-empty composer text, recalling a message dismisses the current Tab prompt suggestion.

## Implementation

- `ComposerEditor`: `setText` takes an optional caret placement; new `caretBoundary()` reports whether a collapsed caret is at the document start/end. It resolves the **live DOM selection** (`$createRangeSelectionFromDom`), because Lexical adopts a native caret move only on a later `selectionchange`, which a quick second arrow press can beat.
- `ChatComposer`:
  - Optional `sentMessages` / `sentMessagesScope` props, the walk state, and the key handling after the completion-menu block.
  - Suppresses eager skill completion during a walk, and strips a removed image from the held draft (through a shared draft-text save).
  - Refuses recall while attachments are preparing.
- `ChatWorkspace`: derives `sentMessages` from human prompts, human steer activities and local echoes (stable across streaming deltas), and passes `conversationId:activeBranchId` as the scope.
- `messageAttachments`: `removeInlineImagePath` mirrors removing an inline image chip at the text level.

Side chats (`IndependentSideChats`) are intentionally unchanged.

## Tests

- `ChatComposer.test.tsx` (18 recall tests):
  - Basic walking: order and draft restore, start-boundary entry, multiline native movement, completion-menu priority.
  - Native keys left alone: modifiers and IME, text selection, a stale Lexical selection.
  - Draft durability and sending: durable-draft behavior, send only on Enter.
  - Guards: queued edit, disabled composer, a delivery still settling.
  - Review fixes: no auto-completion while browsing, an accepted completion counts as an edit, image removal, staging, paste into a recalled message, Tab suggestion interplay.
- `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx` (7): history sources and exclusions, human steers in order without automation steers, same-branch updates, branch and conversation changes, remount and send persistence, session scoping.
- `messageAttachments.test.ts`: `removeInlineImagePath` edge cases.
- `e2e/chat-composer-history.spec.ts` (2, `@T0`): rapid native caret moves followed by recall, and arrowing through a recalled `/skill` keeping the saved draft across a reload.
- I mutation-checked each fix and guard: removing it fails its test. Each review scenario was also reproduced in real Chromium with native keys: all four fail before the fix and pass after.

## Local validation (merged with main at 038547a74)

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`: pass.
- Full `npx vitest run`: 464/464 files, 7807 passed, 6 skipped.

title: feat(frontend): add Alt+N as a New session shortcut on Windows/Linux
body:
Code changes: +16 -9
Tests: +37 -2
Others: +0 -0

Continues the cross-machine handover branches `handover/ryzen/ctrl-n-new-agent-shortcut` (39182fa) and `handover/ryzen/alt-n-new-agent-shortcut` (551cd7d), which were based on a September main. The newer Alt+N branch supersedes the earlier Ctrl+N attempt: plain Ctrl+N is a live terminal keystroke (readline/vim "next line"), and Ctrl+Alt+N collides with AltGr on international layouts (Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt), while terminals treat Alt+N as an unbound meta sequence. The Ctrl+N branch's only unique change — a `browser-view-host.test.ts` chord swap — was only needed because that branch made plain Ctrl+N match, so it is obsolete under Alt+N and intentionally not ported.

## What

- `new-session` gains `Alt+N` as the quick Windows/Linux chord; `Ctrl+Shift+N` stays as the second default, macOS keeps `⌘N`.
- Alt+N deliberately does **not** join `YIELDS_TO_FOCUSED_TERMINAL`: it is terminal-safe (unbound meta sequence in shells), so it keeps working with a terminal focused — same app-wide behavior as the existing `Ctrl+Shift+N` chord.
- Comment updates in `preload.ts`, `GlobalNewTaskDialog.tsx`, and the shell route so docs don't drift from the binding.
- Alt sits where ⌘ sits on Mac keyboards (beside the spacebar), so the chord keeps the same hand motion across machines.

The binding lives in `defaultShortcutBindings`, so the ⌘/ shortcuts dialog and the settings panel pick both chips up automatically (there is no other hardcoded copy of the shortcut in the UI, and no native menu accelerator collides).

## Tests

- `shortcuts.test.ts`: Alt+N matches on Windows/Linux, not on macOS; plain Ctrl+N stays reserved for the terminal. Existing guard suites (readline ownership, AltGr, Alt+Shift layout-switch) pass unchanged.
- `new-session-shortcut.test.ts`: main-process forwarding consumes Alt+N via `preventDefault` and delivers `NEW_SESSION_SHORTCUT_CHANNEL`.
- `browser-view-host.test.ts`: Alt+N also forwards from a native Browser-preview WebContentsView, focusing the shell first.
- `KeyboardShortcutsDialog.test.tsx`: the shortcuts dialog lists both `Alt+N` and `Ctrl+Shift+N` chips on Windows/Linux.

## Validation

Local (mirroring CI): `frontend` vitest suite, `typecheck` + `typecheck:e2e`, guarded-navigation browser integration (real Electron), update-helper/repair-installer node tests, native `UpdateProgressState` Swift tests, cloud-client and product-ui checks, backend `go vet` + `go test ./...` + `golangci-lint`, and the containerized `agent-ci` workflow gate. Two pre-existing environment-dependent failures verified identical on the pristine base commit and unrelated to this diff: `auto-updater.test.ts` (frontend) and `TestCrushLocalAuthStatusDoesNotUseProviderCatalog` (backend). The `src/docs` build job needs the private submodule, which is not available locally — deferred to CI.

title: feat(desktop): hide session cost and token usage from cards and inspector
body:
## Summary

Session cards showed an estimated cost (e.g. `$5.46`) and, on hover, a raw processed-token count (`41,965,667 tokens`). The cost is computed at API prices, and ~98% of those tokens are cache reads. So the numbers look far more alarming than what users actually pay. One user took it as a sign that AO was burning through their plan.

This PR stops showing them:

- **Board cards (active and archived):** removes the cost chip from the footer and the cost/tokens hover tooltip.
- **Session inspector (right sidebar):** removes the "Usage & cost" section. Before this change it showed when Developer Mode was on.
- Removes the `useSessionUsageSummaries` / `useSessionUsage` fetches from the board, standalone archive, and inspector, because nothing displays their data anymore.

The backend usage endpoints and the hooks stay. The memory panel's copy-to-clipboard debug report still has its `Usage` line.

## Tests

- `npx tsc --noEmit` (frontend): clean
- `vitest run` on `SessionInspector`, `SessionsBoard`, `SessionsBoard.remote`, `StandaloneArchiveView`, `SessionMemoryPanel`: 5 files, 251 tests passed
- Removed the tests that checked the cost/token display. Added a test that confirms the inspector shows no usage and makes no usage request in Developer Mode.

## Risks / follow-ups

- If we want usage visible again later, a better approach is real billing context (subscription vs. API, with cache reads broken out), not a raw total. `git revert` brings back the old views if needed.

title: fix(mobile): make the iOS notifications toggle visible when on
body: ## Summary On iOS, the **Settings → Notifications** toggle was nearly invisible when on in dark mode: the knob and the track were both white. **Cause:** on iOS, `@expo/ui`'s `Host` `seedColor` is applied as the SwiftUI tint, which colors a switch's "on" track. title: feat(cloud): every org picks Coder or Freestyle; Freestyle always paid, Coder free with the coder capability
body:
## What

Every organization can now choose its cloud sandbox provider, Coder or Freestyle. Billing follows the provider and the org's WorkOS `capabilities`.

| Org | Default provider | Freestyle | Coder | Custom Coder settings page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No tags, new users, personal orgs | Freestyle | Paid | Paid (same plans and limits) | Hidden |
| `capabilities=coder` | Coder | Paid | Free (no plan, no limits) | Visible |

Freestyle is paid for every org, including contract, internal and grandfathered orgs.

## How

- **Selector.** Settings → General → Advanced shows a provider selector under the Cloud toggle (`DefaultCloudSandboxRow`). It saves through the new `PUT /sandbox-provider` endpoint into `ao_organizations.settings.defaultSandboxProvider`. Only admins can change it, and it appears only when the org has more than one provider. The Create Project modal no longer has a sandbox picker.
- **Gating.** Only Coder and Freestyle are open to every org. Any other provider in `AO_CLOUD_CAPABILITY_GATED_PROVIDERS` still needs its WorkOS capability. The `coder` capability is read from WorkOS metadata alone, so emptying the gate can't make Coder free for everyone.
- **Projects don't move.** A new project records its provider at creation, in every create path including scratch. A project with Coder config stays on Coder. Migration `00083` pins each existing project to the provider its latest session ran on, `coder` or `freestyle` only. It runs per org under the tenant context, because RLS is forced on these tables.
- **Default provider** (`defaultProviderForOrg`):
  1. the org's saved choice;
  2. otherwise Coder for `capabilities=coder` orgs and Freestyle for everyone else.
- **Per-sandbox billing.** A new `ao_sandboxes.billed` column is set once, when the session is created:
  - Freestyle sandboxes are always billed.
  - Coder sandboxes are billed unless the org has the `coder` capability.
  - Spawned workers inherit their parent's flag.

  Background jobs (enforcer, usage sampling, wake) have no principal, so they read the flag through `(sb.provider = 'freestyle' OR sb.billed)`. Other providers are explicitly unbilled; they stay gated by capability.
- **Idle billed Coder.** Billed Coder sessions idle-pause on the Freestyle threshold, and presence keeps them awake, as with Freestyle. A quiet session stops using plan minutes. Coder for `capabilities=coder` orgs is unbilled: it never idle-pauses and is never paused for being over a limit.
- **Custom Coder page.** `Offering.customCoder` controls the page. The three custom-Coder config endpoints now require the `coder` capability (`requireOrgCustomCoder`). Template and parameter endpoints still serve AO's shared Coder.
- **Feature paywall.** The contract, internal and grandfathered exemption still applies to `OrgHasFeature`, but no longer to sandbox billing.
- **Scan allowlist.** Two glibc CVEs (CVE-2026-5435, CVE-2026-19499) were added to the deploy-time image-scan allowlist, in both `deploy-staging.sh` and `promote-production.sh`. The image currently on staging has the same findings, and Debian trixie has no fixed package yet. The comment in the scripts has the assessment.

## Merge order

Migrations `00082_sandbox_billed.sql` and `00083_project_sandbox_provider_backfill.sql` are numbered after `00081` from #6587, which staging has already applied. Goose does not run out-of-order migrations here, so **merge #6587 before this PR**.

## Testing

- `go test ./cloud/...`. New tests:
  - `coder_billing_store_test.go`: Coder billed vs free, child inherits, org default provider.
  - Provider selection and offering tests.
  - Handler tests for `PUT /sandbox-provider`.
  - Gating of other providers, the capability ignoring the gate, project pinning and the Coder-config rule.
  - Idle-pause thresholds for billed vs free Coder, plus a store test for the billed flag and presence.
  - The 00083 backfill, run as a non-superuser role under RLS.

  Billing tests were updated: internal, grandfathered and contract orgs now need a plan for Freestyle.
- Frontend: vitest suite passes, including the new `DefaultCloudSandboxRow` and `cloud-offering` tests.
- The OpenAPI contract and the generated `packages/cloud-client` schema were updated together.

## Not deployed

The staging rollout of this branch rolled back. The control plane crashes at startup with `GitHub App credentials may only be configured in production`, because staging now has GitHub App secrets and `main`'s config check refuses them outside production. The crash comes from `main`'s config check, not from this PR, and staging is still on its previous revision. Nothing was deployed to production.

title: feat(browser): show a remote or cloud session's agent browser as Browser panel tabs
body:
Code changes: +7426 -248\
Tests: +3937 -18\
Others: +430 -3 (generated OpenAPI spec and TS types, translations, Docker files, docs)

## What this does

A remote session's agent drives a Chrome browser on its host, and an AO Cloud
session's agent one in its sandbox.
This PR shows that browser inside AO's Browser panel.
Each agent page is an ordinary tab: same tab strip, address bar, buttons.
You can watch the agent work, and click, type or browse yourself.
Remote previews also load much faster, over one HTTP/2 connection.

## How it works

1. A **browser service** runs next to the agent on the host.
2. It runs headless Chrome; the agent drives it with agent-browser.
3. It streams each tab as JPEG frames (CDP `Page.startScreencast`).
4. Your clicks and keys go back to it as CDP input events.
5. A **daemon route** relays the stream: `/sessions/{id}/agent-browser/*`.
6. The daemon adds the service's token; the desktop never sees it.
7. The **desktop proxy** gives the agent browser its own `ao-preview-*` origin.
8. A small **viewer page** draws the frames inside each agent tab.
9. The viewer reports its page to AO: URL, title, icon, history.
10. **AO's main process** turns those reports into normal-looking tabs.
11. It keeps exactly one tab per agent page as pages open and close.

**In AO Cloud** the same service and viewer run in each session's sandbox:

1. `ao-worker` starts the service on first use, as a child running its own binary.
2. The agent drives it with `ao browser <agent-browser command>`.
3. The sandbox opens no port: the worker holds a control socket to the control plane.
4. For each connection it needs, the control plane asks; the worker dials a stream socket.
5. Each stream carries one HTTP/1.1 connection, the viewer's WebSocket included.
6. The **control-plane route** `/orgs/{org}/sessions/{id}/agent-browser/*` relays them.
7. The worker adds the service's token; nothing is persisted.
8. A **desktop proxy** gives the viewer its own origin and adds the cloud bearer.

## Why this way

- One tab at a time beats streaming a whole desktop (VNC): sharper, lighter.
- Screencast is built into Chrome: no video encoder, no GPU needed.
- Frames flow only when the page repaints, so idle tabs cost nothing.
- The person and agent share one browser: same cookies, same logins.
- Going through the daemon reuses AO's existing authenticated link to the host.
- One owner (the main process) keeps the tab list, so tabs never duplicate.
- Previews stay local: clicks take ~15 ms, a stream can't hide network delay.

## Others doing this

- Chrome DevTools mirrors remote Android tabs with the same screencast API.
- Browserbase's Live View embeds a live, clickable remote browser session.
- agent-browser, which our agents use, streams the same way for "pair browsing".

## What works

- The agent opens a page: a new tab appears, in front if you watch.
- The agent closes a page: its tab closes and you return to the opener.
- You close an agent tab: the page closes for the agent too, even before it loads.
- Address bar, Back, Forward, Reload and Stop drive the agent's page.
- So do Cmd+R, Cmd+[, Cmd+] and Cmd+W, as in any tab; Cmd+F searches the agent's page.
- Tab icons show, the agent's localhost pages included.
- Pickers, logins, uploads, downloads and permission prompts work in agent tabs.
- Only the tab in front streams. A tab the agent opens behind yours loads its viewer when you first open it.
- A browser restart reopens the agent's tabs without duplicates.
- A host reconnect or a profile switch keeps agent tabs as they were.
- Open in browser and Copy URL give addresses that work outside AO.
- A 585-module app preview: 18.7 s → 1.2 s at 80 ms round trip.
- Through a Cloudflare tunnel: 51.9 s → 2.6 s.

In AO Cloud, all of the above works the same, tested on the local Cloud stack:

![The agent browser in an AO Cloud session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/98b106a6eff382abca1e19bb157580fec40d2046/pr-6652/6-cloud-agent-browser.gif)

[Full recording](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/98b106a6eff382abca1e19bb157580fec40d2046/pr-6652/6-cloud-agent-browser.mp4): the agent opens and closes tabs from the sandbox's shell; a click and the address bar drive the sandbox's page.

## Known limits

- Remote hosts: the browser service runs beside the daemon; this PR sets it up with Docker.
- Remote hosts: agents use the `browser` command; `ao browser` there doesn't reach it yet.
- Remote hosts: one agent browser per host, shared by all of its sessions.
- Cloud: one browser per session, so logins don't carry from one session to the next.
- Cloud: the relay is process-local, like the live terminal relay: one control-plane replica.
- Cloud: Chromium, fonts and agent-browser add about 800 MB to each sandbox image.
- Cloud: pages see the sandbox's time zone and language, not the person's.
- Cloud: a customer's own Coder template needs Chromium and agent-browser (cloud/docs/bring-your-own-coder.md).
- DevTools opens on the viewer page, not the agent's page; Annotate is off in agent tabs.
- Open in browser is off for an agent page on the remote host's own localhost.
- Headless Chrome paints one tab at a time: a screenshot of a tab behind it times out.
- If the agent brings a page forward while you type, yours pauses until clicked.
- If you close the last agent tab, new pages appear after a reopen.

## How to try

Remote host:

1. Run an AO daemon in a container (the remote host).
2. `NETNS=<that container> experiments/remote-browser-poc/up.sh` starts the browser beside it (it fetches the pinned agent-browser build).
3. Start the daemon with `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
4. Also set `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rbpoc-token)`.
5. Give the agent `experiments/remote-browser-poc/browser`, with `RB_TOKEN` set.
6. Open the session in the desktop: the agent's pages appear as tabs.

AO Cloud, locally:

1. `npm run cloud:local` builds the stack; its worker image has the browser.
2. Run the desktop with `AO_CLOUD_OFFERING=on AO_CLOUD_CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081` and sign in.
3. Open a cloud session; in its sandbox the agent runs `ao browser open <url>`.
4. The page appears as a tab in the session's Browser panel.

## Changes

**Daemon**
- `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_URL` (loopback `http` only) and `AO_AGENT_BROWSER_TOKEN` (required with it) configure the route.
- It proxies only viewer paths: `v/cdp`, `ws/cdp`, `stats`, `upload`, `download/*`.
- It drops the caller's credentials, cookies and `Origin` before forwarding.
- Download names must look like the browser's IDs; redirects lose its token.
- It skips the 60 s request timeout: the stream is a WebSocket.
- The remote listener speaks HTTP/2 without TLS.
- `/api/v1/tunnel` carries HTTP/2 inside one WebSocket (Cloudflare caps requests in flight).
- Requests in the tunnel are locked out by the tunnel client's own address.
- Previews: dev-server text of known length (up to 4 MiB) is gzipped whole, then sent; streams pass untouched.
- Previews: a body the dev server cuts off is aborted, never cached as complete.
- Previews: HMR sockets skip the request timeout.
- Previews: escaped paths (Turbopack's `%40swc`) are unescaped once.

**Desktop**
- `remote-proxy.ts`: one HTTP/2 session per host, HTTP/1.1 as fallback.
- The session is pinged (any bytes from the host count as alive), opening it has a deadline, cut streams fail as cut.
- Previews leave 20 of the 100 request slots to the app's own calls; a GOAWAY moves queued requests to a new session.
- A host behind a path prefix works through the tunnel.
- Previews also answer over plain HTTP, which Open in browser and Copy URL hand out.
- Previews over HTTPS with AO's own pinned certificate, so Chrome speaks HTTP/2.
- Stable preview origins per host, session and kind: reconnects keep logins.
- New `agent` origin kind and `agentBrowserUrl()` for the agent browser.
- `shared/remote-tab.ts`: parses the viewer's report; only web URLs pass.
- `browser-view-host.ts`: believes reports only from AO's agent origin, in tabs opened as agent tabs.
- It binds each agent tab to one agent page for life, across profile switches.
- One per-tab driver handles navigation, state and closing for both tab kinds.
- A background agent tab loads its viewer when first shown, not when it opens.
- Closing, shortcuts and the menu act on the agent's page, never the viewer.
- Icons arrive as image data; the desktop never fetches a page-chosen address.
- Agent tabs are numbered `a1, a2, ...`, apart from `t1, t2, ...`.
- That keeps local browser automation's tab numbers in step with AO's.
- `useBrowserView.ts`: asks for the agent browser (and asks again if it isn't up yet); previews skip agent tabs.

**Browser service** (`cloud/internal/agentbrowser/host`)
- Chrome, CDP screencast viewer, input, and page helpers; `-data` roots its files.
- It loads tab icons in the remote browser and sends them as data URLs.
- Clipboard writes need the person's own recent input; pastes into the viewer's fields stay there.
- A dropped CDP connection restarts the service.
- Sign-in challenges are spotted through Fetch on documents, not the Network domain.
- `cloud/cmd/rbhost`: the standalone binary for a self-hosted host.
- `experiments/remote-browser-poc/browser`: the agent's command there; files travel with it both ways.
- `Dockerfile`, `up.sh`: fetch the pinned agent-browser and run it next to a daemon.

**AO Cloud**
- `cloud/internal/agentbrowser`: starts the service on first use, restarts it, stops it with the worker (SIGTERM on worker death too).
- It serves the agent on loopback (`RB_URL`, `RB_TOKEN`) and the relay's streams through a pipe.
- The relay allows only the viewer's paths, adds the token and strips AO's credentials.
- A stats probe never starts a browser; the desktop uses it to decide on an agent tab.
- `ao browser`: agent-browser commands from the sandbox; the agent's prompt and skill mention it.
- Control plane: worker control and stream sockets, and the desktop route; callers need write access to the session.

title: fix(cloud): bring-your-own Coder sessions work in the template's checkout; cloud projects get Setup/Cleanup scripts
body:
## Why

A customer with their own Coder (11x) reported that cloud sessions "work but are janky". Their template prepares everything under `~/work/<repo>`: the checkout, a mode-600 `.env` and a Docker stack. It only reports Ready once that is done.

AO ignored all of it:
- **Started too early.** AO launched its own worker before the template had finished setting up.
- **Separate clone.** It cloned the repository again into `~/repository`.
- **Different user.** It ran the agent as a separate `ao-worker` user, so `make` targets got "Permission denied" on the template's `.env`.
- **Wrong path in the agent's instructions.** It told the agent the project lives at `/workspace/repository`, which does not exist on Coder.
- **Unreadable workspace names.** Workspaces were named `ao-<hash>`.

The customer also asked for:
- startup/shutdown scripts,
- a way to set where the agent lands,
- a guide for templates,
- and Claude kept away from `.env`.

All of this reproduced on staging with a replica of their template (`ao-11x-replica`, their `main.tf`).

## What

**Bring-your-own Coder connection (Settings > Coder > Workspace setup).** The options that already existed but were hidden from the UI are now visible, along with two new ones:
- **Run the agent as the workspace user** (`workerUser: workspace`), so it has the same access as the template's user.
- **Use the template's existing checkout** (`reuseExistingCheckout`).
- **Working directory** (new, `workingDirectory`, for example `~/work/{repo}`). AO adopts the checkout there: it switches to the session branch and stashes any local changes. If the directory is missing, AO clones into it. If it holds something else, the checkout fails with a clear message.
- **Ready check** (`readyProbe`), which waits for the template's own "Ready" signal.
- **Keep the agent out of secret files** (new, `protectSecretFiles`, on by default), for Claude Code and Codex:
  - AO writes Claude Code `permissions.deny` rules for `.env` and `.env.*`. They hold even in `bypassPermissions` and also stop the file commands Claude recognizes in Bash (`cat`, `head`, `grep`, `cp`).
  - `ao-worker secret-file-guard` runs as a `PreToolUse` hook on the shell tool for Claude Code (Terminal and Chat) and Codex (Terminal, exec and Chat). It blocks commands that name a `.env` file, such as `python3 -c "open('.env')"` or `. ./.env`, which the deny rules miss. For Codex `apply_patch`, only the files a patch touches count. Codex Chat's app-server records the hook's trust hash (`hooks/list` + `config/batchWrite`), since it has no `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`.
  - Commands and `make` targets that load `.env` without naming it still work. `.env.example`, `.env.sample` and `.env.template` stay readable. Cursor and OpenCode are not covered, and the docs say this is not a hard boundary.

**Project Setup/Cleanup scripts for cloud projects.** These reuse the local Project settings > Scripts feature (`postCreate`/`preRemove`) with the same semantics:
- **Setup** runs in the session's working directory after checkout and before the agent starts. Each step has a 10 minute limit. A failed step keeps the agent from starting.
- **Cleanup** runs before the session's workspace is deleted, never on stop or pause. It currently runs on Coder only; the UI says so for other providers.
- **Environment.** Scripts get `AO_WORKTREE_PATH`, `AO_SOURCE_TREE_PATH`, `AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_SESSION_KIND`, `AO_SESSION_BRANCH`, `AO_PROJECT_ID`, `AO_PROJECT_NAME` and `AO_REPOSITORY_URL`.
- **Retrying Setup.** A failed Setup shows on the session's startup screen (`project_setup_failed`) with the step, exit code and output. Retry, or reopening the session, re-reads the project's current Setup commands.
- **Current Cleanup.** At deletion, Cleanup uses the project's current commands.

**Other fixes**
- **Instructions path.** The agent's instructions now name the real working directory instead of `/workspace/repository`.
- **Readable workspace names.** Bring-your-own Coder workspaces now default to a project-named prefix, for example `alice-e0f014617de5`. Existing sessions keep their names. The session top bar shows the workspace name with a link to it.
- **Late `claude` install.** The worker now waits for a `claude` binary that the template installs late. Before, it never launched the agent.
- **Checkout failures.** Repository checkout and working-directory failures now also show on the startup screen instead of an endless spinner. This gap existed on main.
- **Deletion stall.** A running worker's heartbeat no longer postpones a sandbox deletion.
- **Clearing Workspace setup settings.** The control plane keeps any Coder setting a save leaves out, so the form now sends every Workspace setup field to a control plane that knows them. Before, a saved ready check or working directory could not be cleared and the workspace user could not be turned off.
- **Clean `git status`.** The Claude and Cursor hook files AO writes into the checkout (`.claude/settings.local.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`) are added to the checkout's own `info/exclude`, scoped to the working directory. A working directory that is the user's checkout no longer shows an untracked `.claude/`.

**Docs.** New `cloud/docs/bring-your-own-coder.md` covers:
- the template requirements and what belongs in the template versus Setup;
- readiness;
- working directory and secret-file protection;
- per-session Docker stacks with `AO_SESSION_ID`;
- troubleshooting.

## Compatibility

- **Existing connections and sessions.** Connections that set none of the new options behave as before. The one exception is `protectSecretFiles`, which defaults to on for new sessions. Sessions keep the profile they were created with.
- **Old workers.** An older worker never sends the new `workspace.startup` / `workspace.setup` events and behaves as before.
- **New worker, old control plane.** The control plane rejects the new event with a 400; the worker only logs a warning.
- **No migration.** The new project keys live in the existing config JSON.

## Testing

**Unit tests**
- `go test -race` passes on sandbox, sandbox/coder, worker, workerexec, httpapi, domain, roleprompt, reconcile, cmd/ao-worker and postgres. The postgres run used a throwaway database. Four postgres tests fail identically on main:
  - `TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`
  - `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`
  - `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`
  - `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`
- `packages/cloud-client` regenerates with no diff; its typecheck and tests pass.
- Frontend: vitest passes on the touched files (257 tests), and tsc is clean on the touched files.

**Staging (td:245, our Coder, template `ao-11x-replica`).** I reproduced each problem on main first, then repeated the same steps with the fix:

| Check | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace name | `ao-ba369e0016f4b4ad42daeb70` | `alice-e0f014617de5`, linked from the top bar |
| Start timing | worker and `~/repository` clone while the template shows "Installing tools" | worker starts after the template reports Ready |
| Agent directory / user | `/home/ubuntu/repository`, `ao-worker` | `/home/ubuntu/work/coder-11x-demo` on `ao/<session>`, `ubuntu` |
| `.env` via a `make` target | Permission denied | works (the target printed the replica host) |
| Claude reading `.env` directly | Permission denied (by file mode) | refused by the permission check |
| Instructions path | `/workspace/repository` | `/home/ubuntu/work/coder-11x-demo` |
| `claude` installed late by the template | agent never starts | worker waits, then launches |
| Setup | not available for cloud | runs as `ubuntu` in the working directory before the agent |
| Failing Setup | n/a | agent blocked; startup screen shows step, exit code and output; after editing the script, reopening runs the new commands and the agent starts |
| Cleanup | n/a | current commands run as `ubuntu` in the working directory; the workspace is deleted about 5s later; a failing Cleanup does not block the delete |
| `python3 open('.env')`, `. ./.env`, `cat .env` (td:248, Terminal and Chat) | allowed by the deny rules alone (python, source) | blocked with the AO message; `make -f local.mk db-host` still prints the host |
| `git status` in the adopted checkout | untracked `.claude/` | only the template's own files |

**Claude and Codex through the desktop app (staging td:248, ao-11x-replica; Claude Code 2.1.299, Codex 0.162.1 as the template installs them).** Sessions were created with + Task and checked in Terminal and then Chat.

| Check | Claude | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Folder, user, branch | `~/work/Agreemint`, `ubuntu`, `ao/<id>` | same |
| Setup ran first, as `ubuntu`, in the working directory | yes | yes |
| Instructions name the working directory; nothing cloned into `~/repository` | yes | yes |
| Terminal: commands naming `.env` (`cat`, `wc -c`, `ls -la`, `test -f`, `python3 open`, `. ./.env`) | blocked (Read tool by the deny rule) | blocked by the PreToolUse hook |
| Chat: the same commands | blocked | blocked (app-server trust step works) |
| `make -f local.mk db-host`, `cat .env.example` | work | work |
| apply_patch: `.env.local` line in `.gitignore` / new `.env.local` file | n/a | allowed / blocked |
| `git status` shows no AO files | yes | yes |
| Failing Setup: startup screen, no agent; Retry or reopen after the fix runs the current steps and starts the agent | yes | yes |
| Archive from the sidebar runs Cleanup as `ubuntu` in the working directory, then deletes the workspace | yes | yes |
| No ready check: the worker waits for the template to install the agent, then starts it | yes | yes |

Also through the app: Settings > Coder shows Workspace setup and saves (including clearing the ready check), the project form shows the Other repository field and the project-named prefix, and the Scripts tab saves without a stuck spinner. Codex may decline a `.env` command on its own before the hook sees it; harmless commands such as `ls -la .env` show the hook block.

## Not in this PR

- **Shared workspaces.** Several sessions sharing one Coder workspace through worktrees. The customer asked for it; it is a separate design.
- **Empty `~/repository`.** An empty `~/repository` directory is still created when a working directory is set. It is harmless.
- **Cloud orchestrator auto-start and archive.** Creating a cloud project doesn't start an orchestrator, and a cloud orchestrator has no Archive action, on main as here. Both are frontend-only gaps that weren't part of this report.
- **Cleanup on other providers.** Cleanup does not run on providers other than Coder, which have no graceful pre-delete path.

title: bug(project): derived project ID from folder names with commas/spaces fails INVALID_PROJECT_ID
body:
## Summary
Registering/opening a git repo whose folder name contains commas and spaces fails, because the project ID AO derives from the folder name is then rejected by its own storage-path validation.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Have a valid git repo at a path like `/home/<user>/<dir>/Some Folder Name, 12`
2. Run `ao project add --path "/home/<user>/<dir>/Some Folder Name, 12"` (or open the folder in the desktop app)

## Actual
```
Project id failed storage-path validation (INVALID_PROJECT_ID)
```
The desktop app fails to open the folder as well, with no actionable hint.

## Expected
The derived ID is slugified into a valid ID (e.g. `some-folder-name-12`). Failing that, the error should explain the cause and suggest `--id`.

## Workaround
Pass an explicit ID: `ao project add --path "..." --id some-folder-name-12 --name "Some Folder Name, 12"`

## Environment
Linux, `ao version dev`

title: perf(desktop): show the board sooner on launch
body:
Code changes: +101 -120\
Tests: +120 -33\
Others: +0 -48 (i18n strings)

## What

The board shows up sooner when the desktop app launches or reloads.

- **Reload to usable board:** about 600 ms down to about 115 ms (5 runs each).
- **Cold launch:** about 1.9 s down to roughly 0.6 to 0.8 s on a data dir with 600 sessions. The machine was busy during these runs, so treat the cold launch number as an estimate.

The startup loader now shows only the AO icon, without the text under it.

## Why

Most of the wait on launch was not real work:

- The first workspace fetch ran before the daemon was ready, failed, and then sat out a retry backoff even after the daemon came up.
- TanStack Router holds a pending screen for at least 500 ms by default (`defaultPendingMinMs`), so the startup screen stayed up half a second after the data arrived.
- The daemon only started after the window finished opening, and it then waited for the login shell probe (0.2 to 2 s).
- The daemon ran `cloudflared --version` before it started listening (27 to 117 ms, 5 s timeout).

## How

- **`useWorkspaceQuery.ts`:** a fetch made before the daemon is ready throws `DaemonNotReadyError` and does not retry. The existing ready triggers (status change, SSE open, the `_shell` startup fetch) fetch right away instead.
- **`router.tsx`:** `defaultPendingMinMs: 0`. This only affects first-time route matches. Session switching is unchanged: session routes have no loader, and the `_shell` loader refreshes in the background.
- **`main.ts`:**
  - On macOS and Linux, the login shell probe starts with the process, and the daemon boots alongside the window instead of after it. `createWindow` already links the browser runtime when the daemon is ready first.
  - If the early probe failed under launch load, the daemon start probes once more before falling back to a bare PATH.
  - Windows keeps the old order. Its probe depends on the terminal shell from UI settings, which are not loaded that early, and nothing in CI launches the desktop app on Windows.
- **`daemon.go`, `mobile.go`:** the cloudflared lookup runs in the background after the daemon listens. Mobile status and enable wait for it, so Connect Mobile never sees an early "remote access unavailable". If the boot lookup finds nothing, enabling looks again, as before.
- **Startup loader:** icon only. I removed the rotating phrases, their styles and their i18n keys. The `updates:isPostUpdateRelaunch` IPC is now unused by the loader and is left in place.

I left `ReconcileStartupSafety` (about 50 ms of daemon boot) alone because it is what stops sessions from being started twice after a crash.

## Testing

- `useWorkspaceQuery.test.tsx`: a new test checks that the fetch happens as soon as the daemon is ready. It fails without the fix.
- `mobile_tunnel_boot_test.go`: new tests check that status and enable wait for the boot lookup, and that an empty lookup looks again later. The first two fail without the wait.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite): 7560 passed, 3 failed. The failures are in `ContextMeter.test.tsx` and `ChatWorkspace.test.tsx`, and they fail the same way on unchanged main on my machine.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e`: no errors outside the known local `packages/product-ui` dependency errors.
- `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer`: 75 passed, 1 failed (`chat-composer-text-selection.spec.ts`). That test passed 3 out of 3 on rerun, so it looks flaky.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass. `go test -race` passes for `internal/httpd/...`, `internal/daemon/...` and `internal/mobilebridge/...`. The OpenCode adapter tests fail locally because they read my own `~/.local/share/opencode`, and they fail the same way on main.
- **Manual testing:**
  - Ran built bundles on a throwaway data dir with 600 sessions.
  - Ran them on a real data dir, with the installed app stopped.
  - Booted the daemon and called `/api/v1/mobile/status` the moment it was listening: 200, with `tunnel.supported=true`.
- **Windows:** a teammate ran this branch on Windows and it worked. Windows keeps the old startup order, so that run covered the other changes.
- **Not tested:** a desktop launch on Linux, which gets the new startup order.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene

title: [Bug]: Artifact viewer shows "Binary file preview is not available." for PNGs although markdown artifacts can embed the same images
body: ### What went wrong? In the Artifacts list, selecting a `.png` file renders the placeholder **"Binary file preview is not available."** in the content pane. The same image renders fine when it is **embedded in a markdown artifact** (e.g. a `report.md` with `![](shots/01.png)` shows the image inline), so the bytes are servable from the artifact preview origin — the image viewer just isn't wired for the artifact source. Repro: 1. A session writes artifacts containing a markdown report plus PNG screenshots (e.g. `report.md`, `shots/01.png`). 2. Open the session's artifact list, select the `.png` file → content pane shows "Binary file preview is not available." 3. Select `report.md` → rendered markdown shows the same PNGs inline. ### Cause (current `main`) - `frontend/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionWorkspaceFiles.ts` → `fetchSessionArtifactFile` builds the artifact `WorkspaceFileDetail` with `binary: true` for non-text bytes but **never sets `imageMediaType`**. - `ReadOnlyFileView` only renders the `` branch when `detail.binary && detail.imageMediaType`, otherwise it falls back to the "Binary file preview is not available." message. - Even when that branch fires, it builds the image URL with `workspaceRawImageUrl(...)` — a **workspace** endpoint. Artifact bytes live on the **artifact preview origin**; their raw URL is already known (`rawUrl`, passed from `ArtifactFileView` into `FileContentPane` as `source.rawUrl`) but is never used for image rendering. So PNG artifacts are detectably binary, displayable bytes, and the app itself proves it by rendering them inside markdown — but the direct file view can't. ### Suggested fix Detect an image media type for artifact responses (response `Content-Type` header or file extension), set `imageMediaType` on the artifact detail, and render the `` from the artifact `rawUrl` instead of `workspaceRawImageUrl` when `source.kind === "artifact"`. ### Environment - macOS (Apple Silicon); packaged desktop app and browser renderer, both show the placeholder; no console errors. - Verified the code path is present on current `main` before filing.

Cline is currently TUI-only: `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/registry.go` has no driver for `domain.HarnessCline`, so `Driver(cline)` returns `ports.ErrChatUnsupported`, Cline is absent from the daemon `chatHarnesses` capability list, and the desktop never renders the TUI ⇄ Chat toggle for it. `ao send --steer` cannot target Cline either.

**Source:** local dev session | **Reported by:** @ApexYash11 | **Analyzed against:** `untrivial/main` @ `70d62ce9e`

## Why now

Approval changes are launch-fixed, so the binding needs `ValidateTurnSettings` (same as `ompacp`).

1. New `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/clineacp/` binding (`Configure`, `SessionOptions`, `ValidateTurnSettings`, `VersionProbe` for the 3.x CLI line).

4. No frontend harness list to edit (Chat UI is capability-driven); verify the TUI ⇄ Chat toggle, steer vs steer_restart labeling, and `ao send --steer` against Cline.
5. Doc note for the binding's launch shape and deliberate limitations (no standing instructions in ACP mode).
