title: feat(inspector): give Artifacts its own tab with Finder/Terminal shortcuts
body:
## Summary

- **Artifacts is a regular inspector tab.** It sits after Files and uses the same `FileText` icon as the sidebar's Artifacts entry. The ⋮ menu that used to hold it is gone, because Artifacts was its only item. The tab shows only when the session has artifact files; otherwise the inspector falls back to Summary. It checks the same `artifactFiles` list the Artifacts view and chat artifact links use, so those links still open correctly. Artifact rows in the Summary card, the Artifacts list and board cards now use `FileText` instead of `Shapes`.
- **Open the artifacts folder in Finder or Terminal.** The Artifacts header has two icon buttons that reuse the existing "open workspace" launcher. Labels follow the platform: File Explorer / Command Prompt on Windows, File Manager / Terminal on Linux. The main process gets the session's artifact folder from a new loopback-only daemon route, `GET /api/v1/desktop/sessions/{sessionId}/artifacts`, so it matches the daemon's `AO_DATA_DIR`. If opening fails, the reason shows in the header for 5 seconds. The buttons appear only for local sessions that have at least one artifact.
- **Welcome-screen prompt suggestions sit above the composer.** The order is now heading, suggestions, composer. The suggestions still fold away once you start typing.
- The Browser and Files tabs reserve space so their topbar field doesn't overlap the tabs. That reserve now follows the actual tab count (`--inspector-tab-count`) instead of assuming four tabs.
- **One header row for an open artifact.** It used to have two rows that both named the file. Now one row holds the back button, the file name as a dropdown, and the viewer's source/rendered/feedback buttons. The back button stays visible while the file loads or fails. `FileContentPane` gained a `toolbarHost` prop so it can render its buttons into a header the host owns, following the pattern the Files and Browser topbars already use.
- **File-name dropdown.** It has three items: "Show in Finder" (File Explorer / File Manager on other platforms) reveals the file; "Show in Terminal" opens a terminal in the file's folder; the third item reads "Copy as Markdown" for `.md` files and "Copy contents" for anything else. The first two appear only for local sessions. In the main process, `openArtifacts` takes an optional `path` and rejects paths that resolve outside the session's artifact directory, comparing them after `realpath` so symlinks can't escape it.
- **Delete artifact.** The file-name dropdown ends with a destructive "Delete artifact" item that opens a confirm dialog. On failure the dialog stays open and shows the reason. It's available for local and remote-host sessions, not cloud sessions. The backend side is a new daemon route, `DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/artifact-files?path=`. It deletes only a regular file that appears in the session's artifact list, and it opens the directory through `os.Root`, so `..` paths and symlinks can't reach anything outside. The response is the session with its refreshed artifact list. `openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated.

- e2e typecheck (`tsconfig.e2e.json`): clean. The e2e fake bridge was missing `openArtifacts`, which failed both `test` and `renderer-smoke`.
- New tests cover the header dropdown (reveal/terminal with the file path, copy as Markdown vs. copy contents, remote host, delete confirm/failure/cloud), path-escape rejection in the handoff, and also the hidden Artifacts tab, the folder buttons and their error path, and the artifacts-folder handoff in the main process.

title: fix(workers): drop parent-session identity markers from worker environments
body:
Worker processes inherit the daemon's full `os.Environ()`. When the daemon itself was started from inside a Claude Code session (agent terminal, `rebuild-ao.sh`, desktop app opened from one), the environment carries that session's own identity markers — `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, etc. Every worker then starts with a false "I am a child session" identity: the worker's own claude-code misreads the unrelated parent session as its own, with the follow-on behaviors documented in #2951.

This adds `internal/envfilter`, a small filter that recognizes the parent-session marker set, and drops those keys at the three places worker environments are assembled — unless the key was configured explicitly by the user, which always wins:

- `adapters/chatdriver/processenv`: the merged env for spawned chat drivers;
- `adapters/runtime/conpty`: the interactive terminal env;
- `adapters/runtime/tmux`: exec and attach env — the important one, because tmux's persistent server keeps the environment of the first CLI call for its entire lifetime, so one leaked marker poisons every later worker on the host.

Refs #2951 — this addresses the identity-marker half of that report (the "inherited CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION marker" symptom). The issue's headline problem — workers inheriting `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` and the inability to *remove* an inherited variable rather than override it — needs an env-replace design and is deliberately not attempted here.

title: fix: verify process ownership across recovery paths
body:
Code changes: +1186 -325  
Tests: +2272 -92  
Others: +25 -0  

Fixes #6695. Share OS process ownership checks across Chat recovery, desktop orphan-daemon takeover, native PTY/ConPTY cleanup, and managed cloudflared cleanup.

## Shared recovery rule

- Save the PID and OS start identity when a process starts.
- Signal only a matching owner.
- Reclaim only the old generation's record when the owner is gone or its PID was reused.
- Keep the record and block a replacement when ownership is unknown.
- On Linux, compare boot ID plus kernel start ticks; wall-clock changes do not change that identity.

Desktop takeover checks the exact observed run-file hash under an OS lock. Native cleanup retains launch ownership during recovery. Tunnel cleanup waits for confirmed exit, and an unresolved owner blocks only the managed connector until a later retry.

## Verification for this extension

Runtime evidence was built from `792b1e90ad23dccdf2108fc869c2fa6ac0166616`. Final head `dd7a1a0455ccd0c4e101a66c1a4259c688dacc47` changes only the Windows CI test selection and a deterministic test fixture; all runtime implementation files are identical.

- 21/21 real-process end-to-end cases: five Go CLI, eight native PTY, five daemon/tunnel, and three actual Electron startup cases.
- Ten complete affected-package Linux race suites passed; the Linux PTY shutdown regression also passed 20 consecutive race runs.
- PID-reuse cases preserve the unrelated live process; unknown-owner cases preserve the exact record and block a replacement. Reuse is emulated by pairing an actual old OS identity with an unrelated live PID.
- Five Windows targets compiled locally. The [native Windows ownership regressions passed](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38957469520/job/117165226615) on the final head with Go 1.27.1, `-race -count=1`, including matching, reused, unknown and exited owners.
- Full local macOS frontend/typecheck/CLI/HTTP/lint checks did not all pass under severe host contention; exact failures, interruptions, and commands are retained in the evidence. Full affected Linux suites passed. All **23 CI checks passed** on final head `dd7a1a0455ccd0c4e101a66c1a4259c688dacc47`: [Go](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38957469520), [Frontend](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38957469603), [CLI E2E](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38957469484), and [Gitleaks](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38957469534).

[Download the shared ownership E2E evidence](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33572635/6718-shared-ownership-evidence.zip) — 678 files, 1,504,431 bytes. SHA-256: `f05e3e2b67b87bc2d6bfd001e468536e7714296c55311575e5a69441c58a96a4`. Includes baseline/fixed observations, actual Electron screenshots, regression logs, source/build provenance, and checksum verification. The immutable archive records CI as incomplete at collection; it does not claim final CI passed.

[Download the final CI evidence](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33574834/6718-final-ci-evidence.zip) — final 23/23 check snapshot, all four successful workflows, and native Windows ownership-test logs/source verification. 15,870 bytes; SHA-256: `c375475b198178759f5c738348e15fa2b3d880cace4c756920b0a84b75299709`.

<details>
<summary>Earlier Chat recovery and Linux clock-step evidence</summary>

Latest `main` (`df4cabc54`) was merged first. The Linux clock-step fix is committed as `0f95762ac`; its regression and API end-to-end proof are attached below.

## What

Resume recovers an exited persistent Chat host when its saved PID now belongs to another process, while other projects keep running.

## Why

After a restart, PID reuse made AO treat a dead host as a live owner despite its closed loopback port, blocking the orchestrator's Resume action. Fixes #6695.

## How

- Persist and verify the OS process start identity in host descriptors and launch locks at every host ownership probe.
- Share process identity reads with preview cleanup through `processalive`: Linux boot ID/start ticks, native macOS start identity, Windows creation time, and legacy `ps` dates.
- Preserve legacy Linux records while their PID is live because `ps` dates shift with the clock. Modern Linux boot/start identities still detect recycled PIDs; other platforms retain the legacy timestamp fallback.
- Hold a permanent per-session OS lock through stale-lock reclamation and host cleanup to prevent competing hosts.
- Cover legacy adoption/recovery, genuine and unknown owners, simultaneous starters, owner death, and recovery while another provider retains its PID and token.

The hello protocol is unchanged, so older binaries can attach to live hosts. After downgrade, an older binary fails closed when reclaiming a new JSON launch lock after host loss; the persistent-host ADR documents this limit.

## Testing

Current head: `0f95762acc3a9bb1e172e3c7a45d73ca5bec619b`.

- Linux clock-step regression reproduces **two providers before the fix** and retains **one afterward** in both legacy descriptor and pre-publication lock cases.
- Exact-commit Linux daemon/API end-to-end run passes **31/31 checks**, including repeated Resume, another daemon restart, original-provider reattachment, retained history/worktree, and an unchanged busy peer. The sanitized archive and binary provenance are attached below.
- Complete focused `processalive`, `previewserver`, and `persistenthost` race suites pass on macOS and Linux.

| Target host PID **59 → 126**, despite unchanged original `/proc` identity | Target host PID **377 → 377**, same boot ID/start ticks and original legacy descriptor/plain PID lock |
| New provider replaces durable ownership while the original continues | Releasing only the predecessor connection permits **200/native** resume on the same host/provider/native UUID |
| Busy peer remains available | Peer provider PID **407** remains busy and unchanged; normal target input returns **202** and completes |

All **31 fixed-version checks pass**. The baseline records 10 expected observations of the duplicate. The fixed binary embeds exact revision `0f95762acc3a9bb1e172e3c7a45d73ca5bec619b` and `vcs.modified=false`; all Go source files were independently matched to their commits. Fixed binary SHA-256: `aeae6b5eb3a9b9d51109f4b4c8d43bbb24339c64e8ef4f285e7e39fdc07ebe4a`.

The API synchronization loop also observed 89 startup-overlap responses (`409 AGENT_RESUME_IN_PROGRESS`) before the three completed held requests. title: fix(desktop): drop topbar and tab motion, keep tab strips scrolling
body:
Code changes: +48 -91\
Tests: +7 -4\
Others: +0 -0

## What

- The topbar no longer animates. The board label had a shared-layout spring, and the left padding sprang when the sidebar toggled. Both now change instantly. The settings page header shared the same padding hook, so it changes instantly too.
- Session tabs (terminal view and chat view) snap into place when a tab opens or closes, instead of sliding.
- Tab strips keep scrolling under a trackpad. Before, scrolling across the tabs would randomly stop.

## Why

The motion felt busy, and the tab strip scrolling was unreliable.

## How

- **Topbar:** `useTopbarPaddingLeft` returns a plain number instead of a spring-driven motion value. The header and label are plain elements.
- **Tab snapping:** `Reorder.Item` turns layout animation on by default. Both tab strips keep layout measurement, because drag reorder needs it, but set `transition={{ layout: { duration: 0 } }}`. The scroll containers are `motion.div` with `layoutScroll`, so positions are measured correctly while the strip is scrolled.
- **Scrolling:** the strip only handled vertical wheel input and left horizontal swipes to the browser. Chromium locks a whole trackpad gesture to the scroller it picks at the start, so a swipe that began slightly vertical could lock onto something else and the tabs stopped moving. `useTabScrollEdges` now handles every wheel event over the strip, on whichever axis dominates. All four tab strips use this one handler: session terminal, session chat, Browser panel and side chats. It replaces three copies of the old vertical-only handler, and the chat strip had none.
- **Terminal strip snap-back:** the effect that reveals the active tab depended on arrays that are rebuilt on every render, since file tabs carry JSX. Any update, such as terminal output, smooth-scrolled the strip back to the active tab. It now runs only when the active tab key or the set of tab keys changes.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass.
- Full `npx vitest run` passes except for tests that fail the same way without this change on this machine:
  - `ContextMeter` and one `ChatWorkspace` context-usage test fail under the `en_IN` locale and pass with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`.
  - `browser-profile-import` fails locally because `better-sqlite3` is built for the Electron ABI.
- Updated the `CenterPane` wheel test: horizontal input is now handled by the strip and calls `scrollBy`.
- In the desktop app (isolated dev data), I drove real wheel input into the chat tab strip over CDP. Horizontal swipes, diagonal swipes that start vertical, and a vertical mouse wheel all scrolled the strip through its full range. Closing a terminal no longer slides the remaining tabs.

title: perf(desktop): make session switching instant with no layout shift
body:
## Why

Switching sessions felt slow. Sessions with the inspector open animated their width on arrival, the topbar actions slid around, and the chat replayed entry animations every time. A dev trace showed every click blocking the main thread for 580 to 830 ms.

## What changed

**No animation or layout shift on switch**
- The inspector rail uses plain CSS instead of `motion`. Motion applies even instant targets after paint, so the first frame of a new session showed the old width. Width and slide are now inline style and CSS keyed on `data-state`. A transition runs only for an open or close inside the current session (`data-motion="animated"`), and it expires once the slide lands.
- `useSessionSwitchSnap` sets `data-session-switching` on `<html>` when the router starts a navigation to a session. It clears two frames after that navigation renders. While it is set, the topbar reserve and compact-label transitions are off.
- Opening a chat no longer replays animations. A reply that was still streaming used to fade its whole last block in again. Text already on screen when the chat opens now renders plain, and only characters that arrive afterwards fade. The conversation scrollbar shows at once instead of fading in.

**Less work per switch**
- One `SessionView` now serves both project sessions and scratchpads (`LocalSessionHost` in `_shell.tsx`). Before, switching between the two remounted the whole session surface. The session routes now only match the URL and await the lazy chunk, and the previous screen stays up until it loads.
- Sidebar: rows get stable handlers, `ProjectItem` re-renders only when the switch affects it, and `SessionRow` is memoized behind the dnd-kit wrapper. That last part matters because opening a session refreshes its project, and dnd-kit's context used to re-render every sortable row. Components rendered per switch went from about 6,900 to under 2,800 in a dev trace.

title: feat(config): envRemove — project-configured subtraction from worker environments
body:
Workers inherit the daemon's full environment, and project `env` config can only add or override — a user cannot *remove* an inherited variable from a worker (#2951). The concrete failure: a daemon launched from a shell with `HTTP_PROXY` set forwards that proxy to every worker, and stream-based agents break against a proxy they never chose.

This adds `envRemove` to `ProjectConfig`: a list of exact variable names stripped from a worker's launch environment.

**Two layers of one mechanism.** #6710 (separate PR) ships the built-in denylist — known-bad parent-session identity markers stripped with zero configuration. This PR is the user-facing layer of the same subtraction: whatever else a project wants gone (proxies, locale oddities, ambient CI variables). The layers compose; neither depends on the other.

**Pins always win.** Removals are applied in `spawnEnvForOS` after the project-env merge but *before* the protected `AO_*` and PATH setters, so a configured removal can strip inherited values yet can never strip an AO-owned pin. Validation mirrors `env` (name grammar, case-fold dedup) and reserves the `AO_` prefix.

**Ambient names need runtime cooperation.** Map-level deletion cannot reach names that live in the daemon environ *outside* the merged map — a tmux server's inherited environment, the pty-host base, a driver's `os.Environ()`. `RuntimeConfig.EnvRemove` and the Chat start payloads therefore carry the list to each exec boundary:

- tmux emits `unset 'K';` in the pane launch command for names it does not also export (a configured value re-applied by the export is a pin and is never unset);
- the conpty pty-host drops removed names from its base environment (explicit configured values and argv assignments win);
- chat drivers filter their inherited environ through `processenv.Merge`, with overlay values winning.

Reviewers, shell/cue terminals and managed preview servers apply the same removals — their UI copy promises the project environment too.

Known ceiling: a tmux pane's *recovery shell* (after the agent exits) sees ambient values again — the removal scopes the agent's launch, not the server's lifetime.

Closes #2951

title: fix(preview): stop Linux previews after a wall-clock step
body:
Code changes: +74 -5\
Tests: +83 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What this fixes

AO refused to stop a Linux preview server after the wall clock stepped (a VM resumed from a pause, an NTP step). It identifies a running preview by its launch time before signalling its process group (issue #3475), and it read that time from `ps -o lstart=`. ps derives lstart from the boot time, which moves when the clock steps, so the preview no longer matched its own record.

## How

- On Linux the launch identity is now the boot id plus the start in clock ticks since boot (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22). A clock step doesn't move either.
- The boot id matters because the process registry outlives a reboot: ticks alone could match an unrelated process that started at the same tick after a reboot, and the startup reaper would kill its group.
- The boot id is read on every check, so one failed read can't keep the daemon on lstart. If it can't be read, a new preview is recorded with lstart as before, and a boot-ticks record is refused with the read error instead of being compared with ps.
- The stat parse rejects a line without `)` or a non-numeric start time, as conpty's reader does.
- macOS keeps ps's lstart. The kernel stores the start there, so a clock step doesn't move it; a time zone or locale change still does, and this PR doesn't change that. Linux records in the old lstart form are still checked with ps.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/previewserver/` on macOS, and on Linux (golang:1.27.1 container) with `-race`: pass. The Linux-only tests passed 20 runs in a row.
- New: the start time carries this boot's id and a non-zero tick count; a record from another boot doesn't match; an earlier process's record doesn't match a later process in the same boot (the #3475 case); an lstart record can still be stopped.
- Reading the wrong stat field (`fields[18]`, always 0) or dropping the ticks now fails three tests; before, the package still passed.
- `golangci-lint` for darwin and linux: 0 issues.

Split out of #6652, where it was found while testing remote previews in a VM.

title: fix(desktop): keep window transparency on after reopen, reload, and during startup
body:
## What was wrong

macOS only. With Window transparency on (Developer Mode), the blur often went away and stayed off.

- **Reopening the app.** On macOS, Quit closes the window but keeps the process running in the tray. Main stored the transparency flag once per process, not per window. When the app was reopened from the Dock, the new window asked for vibrancy, main saw the flag was already `true` and skipped it. The new window never got the blur.
- **Startup loader.** The renderer only set the transparency attribute after the shell mounted, and main only turned on vibrancy then. Until that point the window and the startup loader painted solid.

## Fix

- `main.ts`: reset the flag when the window closes, and apply vibrancy on every request instead of skipping when the value looks unchanged.
- New `lib/window-translucency.ts`: reads the saved setting and applies it from `apply-initial-theme.ts` before first paint. Main gets the vibrancy request before it shows the window. The shell effect uses the same helper when the setting is toggled. `ui-store.ts` imports the storage keys from it.
- `styles.css`: under transparency, the startup loader drops its background and shows the bare blur behind the mascot, instead of painting solid.
- `styles.css`: when a loader shows over the running shell (remote host loading, missing dependency), the shell is hidden behind it so the sidebar and panels do not show through.

## Testing

- Manually tested in the dev app on macOS: transparency stays on after reload, after Quit and reopening from the Dock, and from the startup loader onward.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes. Renderer tests for stores, theme, routes, and the native composition cascade pass. New `window-translucency.test.ts` covers the saved-flag read and the re-apply on every call.

title: fix(session): unstick sessions left locked by failed interface and agent switches
body:
## Part 1: stuck Chat-to-Terminal switch

### Problem

A customer on v0.14.0 (local, single-repo project) reported an orchestrator stuck with:

> Interface switch needs attention: release untouched Chat provider for 11x-3: empty root proof changed; source restore: switch interface 11x-3: session: incomplete teardown handle

Every retry of the Terminal switch fails the same way, Resume agent returns 409 "Session is missing runtime or workspace handles", and reinstalling the app changes nothing because the state lives in `~/.ao`.

### Root cause

It happens when a Chat session whose controller never started (for example its start failed) is switched to the Terminal UI.

1. That Chat has no conversation row. The Chat-to-Terminal freshness proof (`nativeConversationNotStarted`) accepts "no conversation row" as an untouched Chat, so the switch proceeds with an empty native id.
2. The controller epoch commit (`commitSessionControllerEpoch`) then requires `ReleaseUntouchedConversationProvider` to update exactly one root branch. There is none, so it fails with "empty root proof changed" and the mode stays Chat.
3. Rollback resumes the Chat source because the epoch did not commit (#6273). The session holds no provider conversation id, so the relaunch fails with `ErrIncompleteHandle` and the switch ends in `recovery_required` with no controller.

### Which PRs

- #5053 (`09effe55b`) added the "exactly one released root" requirement to the commit.
- #5486 (`974a5d06b`) made "no conversation row" satisfy the freshness proof without changing the commit, so the two disagree. Its tests used a fake store, so the real SQL never ran.
- #6273 (`0ca80cfc3`, v0.13.5) fixed the same error for orchestrators that do have an empty row, and changed rollback to resume an uncommitted Chat source. That turned this case into the permanent recovery state.

### Fix

- **Store:** commit the fresh Terminal epoch when the session has no conversation row at all. A conversation with history still fails closed.
- **Rollback:** start Chat fresh when the Chat source holds no provider conversation id, instead of failing with an incomplete handle.
- **Up-front guard:** when a session's start failed before its workspace existed, refuse the switch with reason `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE` ("Retry start before switching interfaces"). Neither controller can run without a workspace, so the switch could only fail into recovery. Sessions still provisioning are not refused. The desktop status poll rechecks this reason, so the switch enables once Retry start succeeds.

Already-stuck sessions recover after upgrading: the Terminal switch now completes, and a session without a workspace shows Retry start, which brings it back.

### Testing

**Unit tests (real SQLite store and controller epoch):**
- `TestInterfaceTransitionNeverStartedChatSwitchesToTerminal`: fails on main with the customer's exact error, passes here.
- `TestInterfaceTransitionRollbackStartsNeverStartedChatFresh`: fails on main with "incomplete teardown handle", passes here.
- `TestInterfaceTransitionRefusesSessionWithoutWorkspace`: covers start failed, no provisioning record, and still provisioning (not refused).
- `TestCommitSessionControllerEpochFreshTerminalWithoutConversation`: fails on main, passes here.
- `TestCommitSessionControllerEpochFreshTerminalRefusesTouchedConversation`: guard that history still fails closed.
- `useSessionInterfaceTransition.test.tsx`: `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE` is polled until the switch is supported.

**Suites:**
- `go test` for session_manager, storage/..., lifecycle, service/session and httpd/... all pass.
- `go test -race` on the InterfaceTransition tests passes.
- `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Live in the desktop app, isolated data, main vs this branch:**

| Scenario | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator whose Chat start failed, then Switch to terminal UI | stuck, exact customer banner | switch disabled with "Retry start before switching interfaces"; no transition created |
| Orchestrator with a workspace and no conversation row, then Switch to terminal UI | stuck, exact customer banner; Resume agent 409 | switch completes, Claude Code running in Terminal |
| Upgrade: open both sessions stuck by main in this build | | the session with a workspace switches to Terminal. The other recovers via Retry start (200, Chat ready), then switches. Remove project returns 200 |
| Control: healthy untouched Chat, then Switch to terminal UI | completes | completes |

## Part 2: "This session already has an agent switch in progress" (delete blocked)

The same customer could not archive the session or remove the project. Their worker row read "Claude Code needs restoration", which is the agent-switch quarantine state.

### Root cause

1. A worker's Chat agent switch (Claude Code ↔ Codex) whose target fails to start leaves the target's provider host behind. Each session has one persistent host (`persistenthost`, keyed by session id).
2. Rollback reopens the source, and `ConnectOrStart` refuses it because the descriptor still names the target's protocol while that host is alive: `chat host incompatible: host protocol="acp" requested=""`.
3. The switch parks on `starting_target` / `source_restore_unconfirmed` and retains the session's switch gate. Recover deliberately does not retry a source restore (`TestSwitchAgentRetainsRecoveryWhenSourceRollbackFails`), and startup quarantines the session again on every launch.
4. Kill hits the retained gate and returns 409 `AGENT_SWITCH_IN_PROGRESS`. Archive fails, and Remove project fails because it kills every session. Reinstalling changes nothing.

### Fix

- **Rollback:** stop the failed target's controller and host before restoring the Chat source. The source comes back and the switch ends `failed` instead of quarantined.
- **Archive takes over the quarantine:** Kill may take over the gate of a switch parked on `source_restore_unconfirmed`, where the source is stopped, the target never took ownership, and nothing runs. Kill stops every controller the session has, then the switch closes as `source_session_terminated`, the same settlement as a kill that wins the source-stop race. Any other retained switch (for example unconfirmed source stop, where a live process may exist) still refuses.

### Testing

**Unit tests:**
- `TestSwitchAgentChatTargetFailureStopsTargetHostBeforeRestoringSource`: fails on main (`starting_target / source_restore_unconfirmed`), passes here.
- `TestKillTerminatesSessionQuarantinedOnSourceRestore`: fails on main ("switch already in progress"), passes here.
- `TestKillStillRefusesSwitchWithUnconfirmedSourceStop`: the guard, passes on both.

**Suites:**
- session_manager, service/..., storage/..., lifecycle, httpd/... and daemon all pass.
- `-race` on the switch and kill tests passes.
- `go vet` is clean.

**Live in the desktop app, main vs this branch, same steps:**
1. Worker in Chat on Claude Code, then Switch agent to Codex (completes).
2. Relaunch with a Claude Chat runtime whose adapter exits on start.
3. Switch agent back to Claude Code.
4. Remove project.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Step 3 | switch parked `source_restore_unconfirmed`, worker shows "Codex needs restoration" | "source restored after target failure", switch `failed`, worker back on Codex and idle |
| Step 4 | 409 "This session already has an agent switch in progress" (also Archive, also after restart with a healthy runtime) | 200 |
| Upgrade: data locked by main, opened in this build | | still loads quarantined. Remove project returns 200, switch closes `failed / source_session_terminated`, all sessions terminated |

title: feat(artifacts): full-screen, editable artifact viewer with selection feedback
body:
## Summary

The Artifacts inspector viewer becomes one combined surface, modelled on Claude artifacts:

- **Full screen**: an expand icon in the viewer header covers the whole app window (the window itself is not made full screen). Escape or the shrink icon returns it to the inspector. The viewer moves between the two places instead of remounting, so an edit in progress survives the switch. Markdown is centred at GitHub's 980px reading width; on macOS the header clears the traffic lights unless the window is natively full screen.
- **One view per artifact**: the File/Rendered mode switch is removed for artifacts. Markdown renders; other text files show as code.
- **Edit in place**: the pencil swaps the same pane to the existing markdown editor. Save returns to the preview with the saved content. Hidden for cloud sessions and for truncated or binary files.
- **Selection feedback**: artifact text is now selectable (the app shell is `user-select: none`). Selecting rendered text opens the app's standard feedback composer (`FileAnnotationComposer`) under the selection, and the comment goes to the worker with the selected text. It shares the artifact's feedback model, so several comments go out together through the existing send-all bar.

### Backend

New `PUT /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/artifact-files` (`UpdateArtifactFileRequest` → `ArtifactFileResponse`):
- writes only a listed, regular file inside the artifact directory (`os.Root`; symlinks and `..` refused → 404)
- requires `expectedFileFingerprint` (hex SHA-256 of the content the edit started from) and returns **409 `ARTIFACT_FILE_STALE`** if the file changed underneath, so a save never clobbers a worker's write
- rejects non-UTF-8 or NUL content (400)

`openapi.yaml` and `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` are regenerated.

### Other changes
- `FileAnnotationTarget` gains an optional `quote`, which is part of its key, its label ("selected text"), and the message ("Location: Selected text").
- Artifact text reads now compute a SHA-256 fingerprint and mark complete text files editable.
- New i18n string `files.selectionFeedbackTarget` and the full-screen labels, in all 8 locales.

## Tests

- `go test ./internal/httpd/...` passes, with new tests for a successful save, a stale-fingerprint 409, and unlisted/symlink/outside/directory paths plus bad content.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Vitest for the artifact viewer, file content pane, diff/annotation components, and i18n: 118 passing. New tests cover: no mode switch, edit and save with the fingerprint, read-only and truncated artifacts, the selection composer sending with the quote, a click-away closing an empty composer, full screen keeping the same viewer, and Escape/back exiting it.
- Full renderer suite: the only failures are `src/main` browser-import/history-store tests, caused by `better-sqlite3` being built for Electron in the local worktree. They are unrelated to this change.

## Risks / follow-ups

- The selection composer covers rendered markdown. Code artifacts keep the existing "Ask in chat" selection button.
- Saving rewrites the file in place; a UTF-8 BOM, if present, is not preserved.

title: fix(mobile): keep selected text readable on Android
body: ## Summary On Android, selecting text in a text field showed a solid block with no visible text. This happened in the Environments host editor, the "Name this machine" sheet, the connect sheet, and most other inputs in the app. **Cause:** Android paints a `TextInput`'s `selectionColor` as the highlight itself, at full opacity. The inputs passed `t.accent`, which is the same color as the text (near-white in dark mode, near-black in light mode), so the selected characters disappeared into the highlight. iOS adds its own transparency to the highlight, so it was only broken on Android. **Fix:** a shared `textSelectionColors(t)` helper (`lib/textSelection.ts`), spread into every React Native `TextInput`: - **Android:** a translucent accent (`accentBorder`) for the highlight, plus the solid accent for `cursorColor` and `selectionHandleColor`. Without those, the cursor and handles would take on the translucent color. - **iOS:** the solid accent, unchanged. `spawn-prompt-input.android.tsx` already used this split, and so did the selectable chat text (`ChatMarkdown`, `HighlightedCodeText`, #6441). All of them now go through the helper. **Inputs fixed:** - **Opaque highlight (the bug):** Environments host editor (`EnvironmentMachineRow`), `sheets/machine-name`, `ManualConnectSheet`, worker search, worker rename, elicitation text field (also used by conversation rename), terminal session composer. - **No colors set (stock Material teal):** chat composer, reviewer reply, request card answer, model picker custom field, skills/files search, worker search fallback, iOS spawn prompt (same colors as before). ## Screenshots Android emulator, dark mode, long-press to select a word. **Environments → Edit machine → Host** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | **Name this machine sheet** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ## Testing - `lib/textSelection.test.ts`: - Checks that the Android highlight is translucent in both themes, the cursor and handles stay solid, and iOS gets the solid accent. - Source guard: fails if any `TextInput` under `app/` or `lib/` skips the helper, or if a selection color is set directly from a `t.*` token. - `ChatComposer.quotes.test.tsx`: added `Platform` to its `react-native` mock, since the composer now reads `Platform.OS` through the helper. - `packages/mobile`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vitest run` 1912/1912 passing. - Built a fresh debug app from this branch, installed it on an Android emulator, and captured the screenshots above. Each "before" uses the `upstream/main` version of that one file, cold-started the same way. ## Notes - JS only, no native changes. - Light mode was not captured. It uses the same split (`rgba(20,21,25,0.24)` highlight on near-black text), and the unit test covers both themes.

title: feat(artifacts): version history menu with restore
body: ## What Slice 2 of #6573. Version capture (#6583) records every artifact version but nothing could read them back. This adds the read and restore API and a History menu in the artifact viewer. ## Backend - `session_artifact_versions` gets `source` (agent or user), `harness` (which agent was running) and `restored_from`. Migration 0200. - Saving in the app records a user version right away, while the edit lock is still held. - `GET /sessions/{id}/artifact-versions?path=` lists a file's versions, newest first. It only reads. - `POST .../artifact-versions/sync` records any settled edit the observer has not seen yet, then returns the same list. The menu calls it when it opens. - `GET .../artifact-versions/{version}?path=` reads one version's text. Content over 256 KiB is cut short and marked `truncated`. - `POST .../artifact-versions/restore` writes an earlier version back. It first keeps the current content as a version and then writes only while the file still holds that content: - If the content cannot be kept, nothing is written. That covers the agent still writing (409 `ARTIFACT_FILE_STALE`), a file over the 50 MiB version limit (400 `ARTIFACT_FILE_TOO_LARGE`), and a blob store error (500). - If the agent writes between the snapshot and the write, the restore gets 409 `ARTIFACT_FILE_STALE` instead of overwriting it. - The restore is stored as a new version, so history is never rewritten and a restore can be undone. - A save first records any settled agent edit that has no version yet. Its own fingerprint check still guards the write. - `GET /github/status` also returns `login`, the GitHub username AO is signed in as. It comes from the SCM provider (`AO_GITHUB_TOKEN`, then `gh auth token`) and is empty when unknown. The lookup is capped at 2s and a miss is remembered for 30s. ## Frontend - A History button in the viewer header opens the same dropdown menu the file name uses. Versions are listed newest first, eight at a time with Show more. The first is marked Current. - Each row shows the agent's logo, or your GitHub avatar for a save made in the app. - Choosing an older version previews it in the viewer with Restore and Back to current. An edit in progress is kept. Markdown renders; other files, HTML included for now, show as source. A truncated version says so. - History is hidden for cloud sessions and for binary files such as images. - Strings are in all 8 locales. ## How to test 1. Start a session whose agent writes a markdown artifact, then ask it to edit the file. 2. Open the artifact, edit and save it once yourself. 3. Click the clock icon in the viewer header. You should see three versions: yours as Current with your avatar, then the agent's two with its logo. 4. Click an older one to preview it, then Restore. The file goes back and a new Current version appears. 5. Open an image artifact. There is no clock icon. ## Notes - `harness` is best effort: it is the agent running when the version was recorded, so an edit made before an agent switch but recorded after it shows the new agent. Versions recorded before this change have no `harness`, so the menu shows the session's current agent for them. - Not covered by tests yet: the preview and restore flow end to end in the UI, and the 2s timeout of the GitHub username lookup. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_015RmYFdH4Ww1hyoFWSg8tv3

title: feat(settings): gateway provider configuration with write-through Claude settings persistence
body:
Fixes #6095

## What

Adds Anthropic-compatible gateway configuration (any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`-fronted endpoint) as a settings feature, at the scope #6095 describes:

- **API**: `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/gateway` (+ `POST .../gateway/probe`). `GET` accepts `?projectId=` and returns the app-scope entry, the project-scope entry, and the effective merge. `PUT` validates the scope and applies tri-state key updates. The probe reuses the existing `agentcreds` validator and returns its verdict plus the gateway's reported models.
- **Persistence: write-through.** There is no new store. Entries are written into the same Claude settings files the daemon's resolution chain already reads: app scope → `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (or `~/.claude`) `settings.json` `env` block, project scope → `<project>/.claude/settings.json`. A hand-edited file and a UI save can never disagree, and model discovery picks gateway models up with no changes on our side.
- **UI**: a "Gateway providers" section in global settings, and a Gateway tab in local project settings showing the project override next to the inherited app-wide values, with an effective line. The probe's model list feeds a datalist on the model input. Translations for all eight locales.

## Design decisions

- **Concurrency with the CLI**: last-writer-wins, saved atomically (temp file + rename; Windows falls back to remove+rename). Files are re-read on every write, so external edits between saves are not clobbered beyond the usual last-writer-wins window.
- **Foreign keys survive**: the file is parsed as raw JSON and only the three known keys inside `env` are mutated; formatting is normalized (2-space JSON + trailing newline) on first write.
- **`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` respected**: the writer resolves the app-scope path through the same exported `agentcreds.ClaudeConfigDir` helper the reader uses, so writer and reader cannot drift.
- **Empty string = delete.** Writing `""` into these env keys would shadow inherited values (the resolution chain treats empty as set), so clearing a field removes the key instead.
- **`settings.local.json`**: the UI writes only `settings.json`; `settings.local.json` is still read and wins in the effective merge. One open question for maintainers: a project-scope token lands in `<project>/.claude/settings.json`, which is typically committed — should the project-scope write target `settings.local.json` instead (or split base URL and token across the two files)?
- **Known gaps, proposed as follow-ups**: the model catalog cache isn't invalidated when an entry is saved (gateway models appear after the next discovery refresh), and config that lives only in process env is invisible to the UI — the effective line could gain an `env` source in ~8 lines if wanted.

## Testing

- `backend/internal/service/gateway`: tri-state persistence, project-over-app effective merge, `settings.local.json` winning in effective, foreign keys and file mode preserved, validation rejects bad scopes/URLs.
- `controllers`: 501 when unwired, scope/project validation, query propagation, error mapping.
- `frontend`: section renders stored entries, tri-state PUT bodies, probe verdict + model datalist, project override editor.

title: [Bug]: Browser panel cannot scroll or click pages that declare `app-region: drag` (e.g. Linear)
body:
### What went wrong?

In the Browser panel, some pages cannot be scrolled with the mouse wheel or trackpad, and clicks on parts of the page do nothing, while the same page works normally in Chrome. Linear's narrow layout is a reliable example: open any Linear page in the Browser panel with the panel at a narrow width, and wheel/trackpad scrolling and clicks are ignored. An agent driving the same tab with `ao browser` can still scroll it, which made it look like a human-only problem.

### Expected

Pages in the Browser panel accept wheel, click and scrollbar input the same way they do in a normal browser.

### Environment

- AO desktop dev build from `main`, mid-October 2026
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon)

### Analysis (agent-collected, separate from the observation)

Linear declares `app-region: drag` on a full-viewport container for its own Electron desktop build. Chrome ignores the property, but inside AO's embedded `WebContentsView` Electron honours it: native hit-testing returns no view for those regions, so real input never reaches the page while CDP/`sendInputEvent` scrolling still works. Injecting a user-origin `app-region: no-drag !important` rule into browser pages fixes it; a PR with that change and a test follows.

title: fix(browser): stop page app-region drag areas from eating scroll input
body:
Code changes: +15 -1  
Tests: +86 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Inject a user-origin `app-region: no-drag !important` rule into every page the Browser panel loads, so page CSS can no longer claim AO window-drag regions.

## Why

Fixes #6756.

Some sites ship `app-region: drag` for their own Electron builds (Linear does, with a full-viewport container on its narrow layout). Chrome ignores the property, but inside AO's embedded `WebContentsView` Electron honours it: native hit-testing returns no view for those areas, so wheel, click and scrollbar input never reaches the page, while CDP and `sendInputEvent` scrolling still work. The page looks driveable by an agent and dead to the human.

The rule is appended to the stylesheet `browser-view-host.ts` already injects into each page, so there is no new injection point and no per-site list. AO's own titlebar drag regions live in the shell renderer, not in browser pages, and are unaffected.

title: fix(usage): stop conflicting sources from looping session_updated events
body:
Code changes: +44 -2\
Tests: +496 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A usage source whose replay is rejected as `source_event_conflict` no longer flips its binding between `partial` and `finalizing` every two seconds.

- A replay that names no billing route now matches a stored attribution and keeps it, the same way a stored NULL attribution already matches.
- A source that hits a conflict is parked in memory at that cursor: no retry is scheduled and later passes return before reopening the binding. Reactivation, a replaced transcript's new generation, or a daemon restart earns another attempt, so sources parked by an older build heal once this ships.

## Why

Fixes #6757. Related: #6219 (part of the `usage_bindings_cdc_update` write rate measured there comes from this loop).

A source whose replay `ApplyUsageChunk` rejects keeps its cursor in front of the rejected chunk, so its transcript always looks longer than what was ingested. The conflict path also returned the finalization `RetryAt` computed earlier in the pass, and `MarkUsageSourceState` cleared `next_retry_at`, so the quiet period never settled. Every two seconds the ingestor reopened the idle partial binding to `finalizing`, hit the same conflict, and settled it back to `partial`: two `usage_bindings` updates and two `session_updated` change_log rows, forever, per source.

The conflicts came from replays of transcripts whose stored rows the legacy repairer had attributed by inference. Live parsing never infers a billing provider, so the replay arrived unattributed and the disposition compared `"anthropic"` with `""` and called it a conflict. A reboot that renumbers the volume changes every file identity (`unix:dev:ino`) and replays every source from byte zero, which is how a whole machine's worth of sources got stuck at once.

## How

- `usage_store.go`: an unattributed replay event matches any stored attribution (one more case in the replay disposition).
- `ingestor.go`: a per-source in-memory park set, checked before the binding is reopened and cleared on reactivation or a new generation.
- No migration. `usage_bindings_cdc_update` cannot tell a meaningful update from a no-op one, because `TouchUsageBinding` is an `updated_at`-only UPDATE that relies on the trigger to publish real usage changes.
- Intentional omission: no retention or janitor change; that is #6219's scope.

## Testing

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/observe/usage/...`: ok. New: `TestIngestorParksConflictingSourceInsteadOfReopeningItsBinding`, `TestIngestorRetriesParkedConflictAfterReactivation`, `TestIngestorReplayAfterIdentityChangeKeepsRepairedAttribution`, `TestIngestorHealsSourceParkedByEarlierBuild`, `TestIngestorStopsRetryingConflictingNativeEvent`.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/storage/sqlite/store/` (usage/replay/attribution tests): ok. New: `TestApplyUsageChunkUnattributedReplayKeepsStoredAttribution`.
- `gofmt -l`, `go vet` clean on both packages; `go build ./...` ok. `golangci-lint` is not installed here, so `lint` is verified in CI.

title: fix(mobile): pin the quick tunnel connector to HTTP/2
body:
Code changes: +9 -0\
Tests: +4 -0\

## What

Start the managed cloudflared quick tunnel with `--protocol http2`.

## Why

Fixes #6760.

A quick tunnel starts on QUIC and never falls back, so behind a VPN or proxy in TUN mode that drops UDP to the edge it redials forever and never registers. HTTP/2 runs over TCP and registers on both kinds of network. Measured on such a network: QUIC had not registered after fifty seconds (cloudflared's own precheck suggested http2), while HTTP/2 registered about a second after the hostname was issued.

## How

One extra argument in `CloudflaredArgs`, with a comment explaining why, and the existing argument test extended to pin it. Intentional omission: no runtime fallback from QUIC to HTTP/2, since cloudflared does not expose a reliable signal for "QUIC is blocked" before it gives up.

title: fix(mobile): withdraw the tunnel endpoint while its edge connection is down
body:
Code changes: +88 -12\
Tests: +150 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Track the quick tunnel's live edge connections by `connIndex` from cloudflared's own log lines, withdraw the tunnel endpoint while no edge connection is up, and log each edge connect and disconnect at INFO.

## Why

Fixes #6761.

cloudflared outlives an edge disconnect and re-registers on the same hostname, but `TunnelLog` only counted registrations, so a tunnel whose only edge connection had dropped still read as ready and kept being advertised to phones and the Connect Mobile panel. The raw connector output is debug-only, so a flapping tunnel (measured: 18 drops in three hours on one link) left no trace in a normal log.

## How

- `tunnel.go`: `TunnelLog` keeps a set of live connections keyed by `connIndex`, fed by "Registered tunnel connection", "Lost connection with the edge", "Connection terminated" and "Serve tunnel error" lines; readiness requires at least one live connection. Each transition is reported as an `EdgeChange` with the edge's location, protocol and, for a drop, cloudflared's reason.
- `tunnel_runner.go`: the runtime withdraws the endpoint on the last connection dropping and re-advertises on the next registration, and logs the transitions.
- The test fixture is a cloudflared log shaped like a real flap; hostname, connection ids, addresses and times in it are synthetic.

title: fix(desktop): rebuild the window when the shell renderer dies
body:
Code changes: +330 -15\
Tests: +237 -0\
Others: +82 -10 (i18n JSON, generated main-process catalog)

## What

When the shell renderer process dies, rebuild the window instead of leaving a blank one, and make every entry point that would show a dead window rebuild it instead.

- Rebuild after `render-process-gone` (any reason but `clean-exit`, not while quitting or closing), restoring bounds, maximized, full-screen and minimized state. An automatic rebuild does not take focus. A crash-loop guard allows three automatic rebuilds per ten minutes, then asks once in a native dialog.
- Tray "Show", notification clicks, a second launch and Dock activate rebuild a window whose renderer has died. Tray session targets wait for the replacement renderer.
- A dead renderer's chat drafts no longer block the close, and a rebuild is not treated as the close a background quit waits for.
- Log shell unresponsive/responsive, main-frame load failures, helper `child-process-gone`, and a per-process memory summary every five minutes. Start a local-only crash reporter with dumps under the Electron `userData` directory (which `main.ts` already pins under the AO data dir).

## Why

Fixes #6762. Related: #6134 (crash screen for renderer-side errors; this PR is about the renderer *process* dying).

When the shell renderer crashed (a PartitionAlloc OOM after a few hours, see #6763), Electron kept the window but nothing painted into its transparent shell view, so AO showed a blank white window until the user quit from the tray and relaunched. Tray "Show", notification clicks and a second launch all just re-showed the dead window.

## How

- `main/shell-recovery.ts` holds the pure decision logic (should this `render-process-gone` trigger a rebuild, crash-loop accounting, snapshot/restore of window state) so it is unit-testable without Electron. `main.ts` wires it to `BrowserWindow` events and to the existing tray/notification/second-instance paths.
- `main/process-diagnostics.ts` formats the periodic `app.getAppMetrics()` summary and resolves the crash dump directory.
- The dialog copy ships through the generated main-process catalog (`scripts/sync-tray-catalog.mjs`, which already carries the tray and zone strings), so `main.js` still does not import the renderer locale files (#6611). The four `desktopRecovery.*` keys are added to all eight locale JSONs and the catalog is regenerated.
- The rebuild creates the window hidden and shows it inactive, so it composes with `showWhenRendererLoaded`: the window is already visible when the renderer finishes loading, and no focus is stolen.
- Intentional omission: no renderer-side changes. The refetch rate that led to the OOM is addressed separately in the PR for #6763.

## Testing

Scrolling down the chat toward the bottom no longer jitters and snaps to the end.

## Why

Inside the 64px band at the bottom, `onScroll` re-pins the chat to the live end. That re-pin runs `syncScrollLayout`, which does a follow pass and writes `scrollTop` to the very bottom while the reader is still scrolling. Even a few pixels away, the view jumped.

## How

The re-pin sets `skipRelatchFollow`, and the next layout pass skips that one follow. The reader is already at the end, so there is nothing to catch up to. New content still follows once pinned. Requested glides (send, jump to latest) are unaffected. The change is in `ChatWorkspace.tsx`.

## Testing

Chat workspace tests pass, including the existing re-latch test. One test, "shows live provider context usage", fails on number grouping (`2,58,400`), a locale issue on my machine that this change doesn't touch.

title: fix(mobile): keep the worker board on screen across a quick background
body: ## Summary Opening the Workers board, backgrounding the app, and coming back within a second showed the full-screen loader again instead of the workers that were already loaded. **Cause:** on background, `store.tsx` drops the connection on purpose, because a LAN address can point at a different machine after the phone wakes. The cached rows were kept, but `sessionRowsForMachine` only shows rows for the connected machine. With `config` null that machine was `""`, so the board was empty. Loading was on while the endpoint race ran, and empty plus loading shows the loader. Once the race finished, `reloadConfig` compared the selected host against the cleared `cfgRef` and wiped the rows as if the user had switched machines. **Fix:** - On background, remember the machine and host id the board was showing (`heldMachine` / `heldHostIdRef`). While `config` is null, that machine stands in, so the cached rows stay visible during the reconnect. - `reloadConfig` checks for a host change against the held host id, so resuming on the same machine no longer clears the board. - The held machine is released when the user switches hosts, when the host is version-incompatible, and once a config resolves. - The bearer connection is still never reused after waking. Only what's displayed changed. If the machine is unreachable on resume, the board shows the cached rows with the stale banner (same as a dead poll on a populated board) instead of a spinner. ## Before / after Recorded on the iOS simulator, paired to a local daemon over loopback: open the Workers board, press Home, and reopen the app about a second later. Loopback is the fastest possible reconnect, so the loader shows here for only ~250 ms. Over LAN or the tunnel on a real phone it stays up longer. | Same moment after returning | | --- | | | **Real speed** **Slowed 4x around the return** The "Open debugger to view warnings" toast comes from the dev build and isn't related to this change. ## Tests - `npx tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `store.tsx`. - `npx vitest run`: 1907/1908 pass. The one failure (`uitextview-selection-color.test.ts`) needs the `patch-package` patches applied and isn't related to this change. - `store.tsx` can't be imported by vitest (React Native), so there's no new unit test. ## Risks - After a wake, the rows shown are from the previous connection until the first poll lands. They are still keyed to the same host id, so another machine's rows are never shown. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bug(command-code vendor): cmd acp accepts --mod but silently ignores it
body:
## Problem

Command Code's Chat mode accepts `--mod` and then ignores it. There is no error, no warning, and the ACP agent starts and runs normally — so a caller that relies on a mod gets a silently inert mod.

This is a vendor bug in `CommandCodeAI/command-code`, not in AO. Filed here because AO is blocked on it and because the failure is invisible.

## Evidence

Tested on **v1.79.2** and again on **v1.82.3**.

A mod whose factory writes a log line at load time, at `appendSystemPrompt` invocation, and at `onRunEnd`:

| Mode | Declaration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| print (`cmd -p`) | `--mod ./mod.ts` | ✅ `factory:ran`, `hooks:registered`, `appendSystemPrompt:invoked`, `onRunEnd:fired` |
| ACP (`cmd acp`) | `--mod ./mod.ts` | ❌ **no log at all — mod never loaded** |
| ACP | `settings.mods.paths` (absolute) | ❌ never loaded |
| ACP | `settings.mods.paths` (relative) | ❌ never loaded |
| ACP | `<project>/.commandcode/mods/` | ❌ never loaded |

The print-mode result rules out an invalid mod file: the same file loads and its hooks execute there. The ACP session itself starts cleanly and answers prompts, so the failure is isolated to mod loading.

## Why this matters beyond AO

The same gap appears to disable **shell hooks** on the ACP path. `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `Stop` are documented to fire, and they do in practice — but `SessionStart` is the one hook never fired under ACP across every test. A consumer relying on `SessionStart` under `cmd acp` gets nothing, again silently.

## Reproduction

```bash
# sentinel.ts
import { appendFileSync } from "node:fs";
appendFileSync("/tmp/mod-events.log", "factory:ran\n");
export default function (cmd) {
  cmd.hooks({
    appendSystemPrompt: () => { appendFileSync("/tmp/mod-events.log", "appendSystemPrompt\n"); return "X"; },
  });
}
```

```bash
cmd -p "hi" --mod ./sentinel.ts   # /tmp/mod-events.log  -> "factory:ran", "appendSystemPrompt"
cmd acp --mod ./sentinel.ts       # /tmp/mod-events.log  -> does not exist
```

Driving the ACP session over stdio requires only `initialize`, `session/new`, then `session/prompt`.

## Requested behaviour

Either:

- load `--mod` / configured mods on the ACP path, matching print mode, **or**
- reject the flag on `cmd acp` with a clear error instead of accepting and ignoring it.

The second is far less useful but would at least make the limitation visible to integrators. The mod API is documented as experimental, so treating this as a known gap is also reasonable — but it should be stated in the ACP documentation rather than discovered by trial.

## Upstream

https://github.com/CommandCodeAI/command-code

Docs: <https://commandcode.ai/docs/mods>

Not filed upstream yet — say the word and I'll open it there with this reproduction.

title: test(command-code): Chat-mode activity tracking and native session-id capture never verified end-to-end
body:
## Problem

AO's Command Code **Chat** activity tracking has never been verified end-to-end. We know the underlying hooks fire under `cmd acp`, but we have not observed AO's `activity` field actually updating during a real Chat session.

This is a verification gap, not a reported bug — nothing is known to be broken.

## What is established

**Hooks fire under ACP.** Tested with a live `cmd acp` session against a workspace `.commandcode/settings.json` carrying all four hooks, logging each invocation:

| Hook | ACP |
| --- | --- |
| `SessionStart` | ❌ does not fire (TUI-only) |
| `PreToolUse` | ✅ fires |
| `PostToolUse` | ✅ fires |
| `Stop` | ✅ fires |

**Terminal mode works.** A live spawned Command Code worker reported:

```
status: working
activity: active
```

So Terminal activity is confirmed.

## What is not established

- Whether a Chat session's `activity` transitions to `active` during a turn and back to `idle` afterwards.
- Whether AO captures Command Code's native `session_id` in Chat. In Terminal this comes from the `SessionStart` hook, which never fires under ACP, so the Chat native-id capture path may be silently empty.
- Whether restore works for a Chat session as a consequence.

That last two matter beyond cosmetics: if native-id capture is empty in Chat, `session/load` restore has no identity to resume against.

## Why it was worth separating

An earlier pass in #6778 claimed all hooks were dead under ACP and that Chat activity tracking was broken. **That claim was wrong** — it came from a probe whose ACP session had timed out, so the hooks were never given a chance to run. The correction is recorded in #6657. This issue exists so the remaining *unverified* surface is tracked rather than assumed either way.

## Suggested verification

1. Register a project with `command-code` as both orchestrator and worker agent.
2. Spawn a **Chat** session (not Terminal) and send a prompt that forces a tool call.
3. Watch `ao session get <id>` during the turn — expect `activity: active`, then `idle` after.
4. Inspect session metadata for `agentSessionId` and confirm it is non-empty.
5. Confirm the Activity column moves in the desktop app for that session.

## Notes

- Terminal-mode activity is unaffected by any of this and is covered by existing tests.
- No code change is proposed here; this is a verification task. If step 4 shows an empty native id, the fix is a separate change — the ACP path has no hook to capture it from, so it would need `session/new`'s response id.

title: fix(cloud): start a cloud Claude terminal on the upgraded Claude Code
body:
## Problem

Found live on prod after #6587 shipped. On a fresh Coder workspace the first cloud terminal (TUI) session runs the Claude Code the image ships (2.1.228), and current models refuse it:

> API Error: 400 Claude Code 2.1.228 does not support this model; version 2.1.280 or newer is required.

#6587 upgrades Claude Code into `~/.ao/tools` at worker boot. Chat turns wait for that upgrade (`claudeCodeTurnWait`, 90s), but the terminal launch picks the binary with `defaultClaudeCode.current()`, which never waits, so it starts the old install while the upgrade is still running.

## Fix

`workerexec.AwaitClaudeCodeUpgrade(ctx)` waits for an upgrade in progress with the same 90s bound Chat turns use. The worker calls it before building the interactive Claude command and the reviewer command. It returns at once when nothing is pending (the workspace's own Claude Code is current, or the upgrade already finished) or when an earlier upgrade failed (retries run in the background, see #6587's backoff).

Cost: the first terminal start on a fresh workspace can wait for the npm install, up to 90s, instead of starting a CLI that fails its first turn.

## Tests

`TestClaudeCodeAwaitRunsTheTerminalOnTheUpgrade`: a pending upgrade is waited for and the launch uses the upgraded binary; a stuck upgrade is bounded by the wait and falls back to the existing install. `workerexec`, `cmd/ao-worker`, `worker` pass; `-race -count=3` on the Claude Code tests.

title: fix(browser): preserve native popup handles for OAuth sign-in
body:
Code changes: +78 -33  
Tests: +160 -24  
Others: +0 -0

## Summary

Preserve native popup handles and opener relationships in AO's Browser tabs so popup-based OAuth can complete.

AO previously denied Electron's native popup and opened an unrelated tab. That made `window.open()` return `null` and removed `window.opener`, breaking Firebase popup authentication such as ElevenLabs Google sign-in.

- Adopt the exact guest `webContents` Electron supplies to `createWindow`, keeping the real WindowProxy, opener, browser profile, and Chromium-owned navigation intact.
- Apply AO's sandbox, context isolation, disabled Node integration, and preload preferences before native guest creation; retain unsafe-URL and renderer-origin restrictions.
- Support `about:blank` popup bootstrap and Electron's no-guest link fallback, preserving its referrer and POST navigation options.
- Defer tab activation until native popup creation returns, avoiding queries/layout against an incompletely initialized guest.

## Regression coverage

- Tighten the unit fake to reject unrelated guest contents, matching Electron's identity check.
- Cover exact guest adoption without resetting OAuth navigation, blank bootstrap, unsafe popup destinations, and the no-guest fallback.
- Extend the existing native Electron CI integration with real `window.open()` handles, cross-origin two-way `postMessage`, profile sharing, unavailable Node globals, self-close, and tab-registry cleanup.

## Validation

- Focused browser host suite: 207 tests passed.
- Native Electron guarded-navigation and popup integration: passed on macOS arm64.
- Docs production build, Cloud client generation/typecheck/29 tests/package dry-run, product UI typecheck/160 tests/package dry-run, Node 22 lockfile dry-run, 13 macOS packaging tests, both helper architecture builds, and Swift state tests: passed.
- Full renderer smoke: 81 passed, 2 failed locally (chat text selection and command-palette focus). Focus passed on both the baseline and final-branch reruns. Text selection fails with the same assertion on both the unchanged merged-#6620 baseline and final branch. These renderer-only tests do not execute the changed Electron popup handler. The local renderer suite is not claimed green; the complete Linux renderer-smoke CI job passed on this PR head.
- Full frontend suite: 474 files passed; 8,032 tests passed, 6 skipped (Node 24, three workers).
- Frontend and E2E TypeScript checks: passed.
- User manually completed ElevenLabs Google sign-in in the local AO app with this popup implementation plus the #6620 cleanup, reaching onboarding.

## Dependencies and scope

Based on main after merged #6620. This PR contains only the popup-opener follow-up and tests; the already-merged self-closed-tab cleanup is not duplicated.

This does not implement macOS WebAuthn/passkey fingerprint support (#6782). Automated integration uses local fixtures, not real Google credentials. The native Intel macOS helper CI job and Linux renderer-smoke CI job passed; the main frontend CI test job is still running.

title: fix(harness): stop false "update did not reach" failures for Kimi, Crush and silent self-updaters
body:
Code changes: +205 -42\
Tests: +201 -8\
Others: +0 -8 (locale strings)

## What

Fixes three ways a harness update shows a red failure when nothing is actually broken, or without saying why:

1. **Kimi**: `the update finished, but the installed version 2.0.2 did not reach the requested version 2.2.0`. Two users reported this, one at 2.0.2 and one at 0.41.0.
2. **Any vendor self-updater that exits 0 without updating** (Droid seen in the field: `0.159.1 → 0.242.0`): the error never said what the updater printed.
3. **Crush** (and other harnesses that release often): `v0.98.1 is now the latest release. Select Update again to install it.`

This PR covers all three on purpose, at the reporter's request. They share one cause: the update flow treats an exit code or a cached advisory as proof of the outcome.

## Why

**Kimi.** AO ran `kimi upgrade -y`. Reading Kimi Code's bundled updater (2.0.2 and 2.2.0, `handleUpgrade`), that command exits **0 without replacing the binary** in three cases:
- Its own rollout channel says nothing is newer: `Kimi Code is already up to date (…)`. AO reads `code.kimi.com/kimi-code/latest`, which can be ahead of that channel.
- The install source is Homebrew or unsupported: it prints `To update manually, run: …`.
- On native installs it runs `__update_download`, which only **stages** the new binary. The swap happens on a later launch, and that launch skips the swap if another instance holds the swap lock or the smoke check fails.

AO's `--version` check then still sees the old version, and every retry fails the same way.

**Error text.** The updater's output was already kept in the job's output, but the card only showed the generic message, so users and maintainers couldn't tell which case happened.

**Crush.** A card's latest version comes from the cached advisory, which the periodic pass refreshes every 6 h by default. The click-time `refresh=true` check often finds a newer release for fast-moving harnesses, and `useStartHarnessUpdate` then refused and asked the user to click again.

## How

- **Kimi re-runs its official installer on every OS** (`installerUpdateTargets`): `install.sh`, or `install.ps1` on Windows. `bindKimiInstallerUpdate` binds the run to the copy sessions use:
  - It applies only to Kimi Code's default native install, `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` (`kimi.exe` on Windows). The match is exact on macOS and Linux, and case-insensitive with either separator on Windows. A `kimi` anywhere else (`~/.local`, `~/.cargo`, `/usr/local`, a legacy Python `kimi-cli` entry point, a uv-copied `kimi.exe`) may belong to another tool, so it is refused with "update it manually" rather than replaced.
  - `KIMI_INSTALL_DIR=<root>` and `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`, so shell rc files are not edited.
  - `PATH` without `<root>/bin`. Both installers skip their legacy-shim migration (which renames the first legacy `kimi` on PATH to `kimi-legacy` and deletes the rest) only when `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH` is set **and** their own bin directory is off PATH. With this, an AO update replaces only `<root>/bin/kimi`, plus the installer's `kimi.bak`.
  - `KIMI_VERSION=<approved release>` through `pinVendorUpdate`, so the installer and AO's verification agree on the target.
  - The update advisory applies the same check (`vendorMaintainable`), so a `kimi` outside `~/.kimi-code` gets manual-update guidance instead of an **Update** button that is always refused.
  - A staged binary left by an earlier `kimi upgrade` can't downgrade this install. On startup, Kimi's `maybeRelaunchWithStagedNativeUpdate` discards a staged update that is not newer than the running version (`if (!semver.gt(staged.version, currentVersion)) discard`), in both 2.0.2 and 2.2.0.

  `vendorMaintainable` counts installer-updated targets, so Kimi stays updatable from AO. Grok's Windows destination override now shares the new `withInstallerEnv` helper (behaviour unchanged, still covered by the existing Grok tests).
- **Failed updates quote the updater's last line** (`lastOutputLine`). It is shown as a terminal would show it: ANSI CSI/OSC sequences removed, only the text after a line's last `\r`, and capped at 200 runes. This applies only to command-based updates, not installer scripts. Example: `…did not reach the requested version 0.242.0; the update command reported: "Droid is already up to date."`
- **Click-time newer release.** `useStartHarnessUpdate` no longer takes `latestVersion`. When the fresh advisory is still `behind_latest` through the same maintenance method, it installs `fresh.latestVersion`, which it already sent as `expectedVersion`. The daemon still refuses a target at or below the installed version (`ErrUpdateVersion`). A changed method is still refused (`updateMethodChanged`). The hook returns the advisory it acted on, so a failed update in `HarnessUpdateNotice` keeps showing the release it actually tried. The unused `settings.harness.updateTargetChanged` string is removed from all locales.

### Similar problems in other harnesses (audit, follow-ups not in this PR)

I read each vendor self-update command in `vendorUpdateCommands` from its shipped bundle or source, without running them. Almost all can exit 0 while the next `--version` still shows the old release:

| Harness | Exit-0 no-op cases | Suggested follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| Droid | `Auto-update is not available for npm installations.`, `✓ Already up to date!`, `Update to X was skipped.` (directory not writable). Its latest comes from `downloads.factory.ai/factory-cli/LATEST`, not npm `droid`. | Re-run `app.factory.ai/cli`, as for Kimi |
| Autohand | Runs `curl … \| sh` without pipefail, so it prints `Successfully updated` even when curl failed. Its installer defaults to `~/.local/bin`. | Re-run `install.sh` with install dir and version, as Windows already does |
| OpenCode | `Upgrade failed` still exits 0. The installer only writes `~/.opencode/bin`. | Refuse other locations, and treat `Upgrade failed` as a failure |
| Claude Code | `stable`-channel users get "up to date" (2.1.292) while AO compares to `latest` (2.1.301). Also exits 0 when another Claude process is running or updates are disabled. | Respect `autoUpdatesChannel` when choosing the latest version |
| OMP, Cursor, FX, Pi, Grok, Prime Agent | Each "already up to date" against its own channel or feed, which differs from AO's source | Align AO's latest-version source per harness |
| Goose | GitHub's `stable` tag can lag a new release by minutes | Retry later |
| Qwen, Kimchi | "update with brew/npm" messages | Covered by the quoted-updater message |
| Codex, Amp | Effectively safe | — |

The quoted-updater message in this PR already turns every one of these from a generic failure into a self-explaining one.

## Testing

Per the reporter's request, validation runs in this PR's CI. Locally, only `go test ./internal/service/systeminstall/` was run (passing). The full repo suites, the frontend typecheck and the vitest run were not run locally.

New or updated tests:
- `TestKimiUpdateReinstallsAdvisoryReleaseIntoConfirmedDirectory`: an end-to-end update runs the installer, never `kimi upgrade`, with `KIMI_INSTALL_DIR`, `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`, `KIMI_VERSION` and a PATH without `<root>/bin`, and verifies success.
- `TestKimiUpdateBindsOnlyKimiCodeDefaultInstall`: `~/.kimi-code` is accepted on macOS, Linux and Windows. Other tools' `~/.local`, `~/.cargo` and `/usr/local` copies are refused, as are a case-mismatched `BIN` or `kimi.exe` outside Windows, and an empty path or home. Homebrew plans are untouched, and the original plan is not mutated.
- `TestKimiUpdateAdvisoryOffersUpdateOnlyForDefaultInstall`: the advisory's maintenance method is `official-installer` for `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` and empty for `~/.local` and `~/.cargo` copies.
- `TestKimiUpdateKeepsItsBinDirectoryOffInstallerPath`: `<root>/bin` is removed from PATH (Unix exact, Windows case-insensitive) and other entries are kept.
- `TestLastOutputLineShowsWhatTheTerminalWouldShow`: covers empty output, blank lines, ANSI colour, OSC title, `\r` progress (including a trailing bare `\r`) and 200-rune truncation.
- `HarnessUpdateNotice.test.tsx`: a failed update keeps the card on the newer release the click-time check chose.
- `TestFailedUpdateQuotesWhatTheUpdaterReported`: the exact failure text includes the updater's last line.
- Updated `TestVendorInstallerUpdateUsesHarnessSelfUpdateCommand` and `TestWindowsVendorUpdatesUsePowerShellInstallers`, so Kimi uses `install.sh` / `install.ps1`.
- `HarnessSettingsSection.test.tsx`: a newer click-time release now starts the install with `expectedVersion` set to the fresh release. The `different-target` case is dropped from the "does not run an update" table because that refusal is the behaviour this PR removes.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [ ] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable. Three related update-false-failure fixes are combined at the reporter's request.
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.). Checks are validated in this PR's CI.

title: feat(harness): open update failure diagnostics from the notice
body:
## Summary
Users hitting harness update failures had no direct path from the update notice to the diagnostics they need to report the problem.

- **Notice:** when an update fails, the card shows a **Show diagnostics** button under the error.
- **One click:** it opens Settings › Harness on that harness with the failed job's diagnostics already expanded, and focuses **Copy diagnostics** (which includes the health report and machine info).
- **No job:** if the failure happened before a job started, it opens the harness's **Health** tab instead, which has its own copyable report.
- **Fix:** the Harness page used to collapse diagnostics for any *installed* harness on every readiness refresh. That hid update failures, because the harness is still installed after one. Diagnostics now collapse only when a harness goes from not installed → installed.

The `showDiagnostics` option is passed through the same path as the existing `startLogin` shortcut: `openGlobalSettings` → `SettingsDialog` → `GlobalSettingsForm` → catalog → `HarnessSettingsSection` → `LocalHarnessContent`.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI (typecheck, unit tests)
- [ ] Force a harness update failure → the notice shows the error plus **Show diagnostics**
- [ ] Click it → Harness page opens on that harness with diagnostics expanded and Copy focused; copying works
- [ ] A failure with no job → the Health tab opens
