title: perf(preview): avoid loading session history on every poll
body:
Code changes: +41 -13  
Tests: +155 -2  
Others: +42 -0 (generated sqlc)

The preview poller reads and decodes every historical session every 250 ms, then discards terminated and nonworker sessions. Large prompts and checkpoints make this recurring read expensive on long-lived hosts, even when few previews are active.

Read only session ID, workspace path, preview URL, and preview revision for nonterminated workers through a dedicated SQLite projection. Keep blank previews in the result so a deleted preview file can still be restored when it reappears. Polling cadence, explicit preview selection, and service writes stay unchanged.

Regression tests cover active/terminated/nonworker filtering, standalone workers, blank and external previews, cancellation, and forgetting terminated previews. A synthetic benchmark with 1,000 workers (990 terminated, 4 KiB prompts) measured a median read time of 8.83 ms → 0.163 ms and allocations of 10,590,888 → 4,232 bytes per read across three runs.

This was found during mobile/Cloudflare disconnect triage. It removes confirmed avoidable daemon work; whether that work contributes to the observed connection drops still requires live validation. No network, tunnel, authentication, or reconnect behavior changes are included.

Validation with Go 1.27.1 (concurrency limited locally):
- Full backend race coverage on macOS and Ubuntu; SQLite uses the four CI shards on Linux, and permission-sensitive suites were rerun successfully as an unprivileged user.
- Focused preview/store tests and full race tests for both changed packages.
- Backend build and vet; golangci-lint v2.13.2 (zero issues).
- Native macOS and Linux CLI E2E; fresh-install Docker smoke check.
- Full Cloud build/vet/race suite and the Expat build target.
- Pinned sqlc and API regeneration with no drift; gitleaks v7.4.0 scanned the one introduced commit with no leaks.

All 21 GitHub checks passed for this commit, including native Windows CLI/workspace checks and amd64 Linux race coverage ([Go](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38834322030), [CLI E2E](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/actions/runs/38834322040)). Local Windows execution was unavailable; local Linux containers used arm64.

title: fix(browser): keep dialogs and notices above the native browser view
body:
Code changes: +209 -49\
Tests: +122 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Keeps dialogs and floating notices, such as the "Agent updates available" notice and the New task dialog, above the native browser page instead of underneath it.

It also stops the update notice from blocking the browser: before, you couldn't click or scroll the page while the notice was showing.

## Why

The browser page is a separate native `WebContentsView`. When an overlay opens, the main process raises the transparent shell above it. Two problems broke that:

1. **New tabs were added above the raised shell.** `browser-view-host` calls `contentView.addChildView(view)` with no index for each new tab, which puts the view on top. Any tab created while an overlay was open (from the user, `ao preview`, or an agent's `ao browser` action) covered the overlay until the overlay closed and reopened. The update notice stays mounted with `data-state="open"`, so it was hit most often.
2. **Overlay tracking was per hook, not per document.** `SessionView` and `BrowserPanel` can each have a `useBrowserView` instance mounted at the same time. Each kept its own `overlayOpenRef` and sent `setOverlayOpen(false)` on cleanup, so unmounting one lowered the shell while another still saw an overlay as open and never re-raised it.

3. **The update notice blocked all browser input.** The notice is long-lived and flagged as a native overlay, so the shell stayed raised over the page the whole time it was showing. A raised shell covers the full window and receives every click and scroll, and Electron can't make a single view click-through for just one region.

## How

- `window-composition.ts`: new `restackShell()` raises the shell back to the top when an overlay is open, and does nothing otherwise. Ordering is shared with `setOverlayOpen` through `placeShell`, so the macOS surface refresh still applies.
- `browser-view-host.ts`: optional `onNativeViewAdded` callback, called right after each page view is appended. `main.ts` wires it to `windowComposition.restackShell()`.
- `renderer/lib/browser-overlay-sync.ts`: a single ref-counted `MutationObserver` for the whole document, using the same selectors and `data-state` filtering as before. `useBrowserView` subscribes to it instead of running its own observer. The shell is lowered only when the last subscriber unmounts.

- `HarnessUpdateNotice`: no longer flagged as a native overlay. A new `useLiveBrowserViewportRect` hook measures the live browser viewport, which is exactly the native view's bounds. `noticePlacement` then keeps the notice in its corner, moves it beside the page if it would overlap, or hides it while the page leaves no room (maximized browser, or a very wide inspector rail). The notice comes back when the browser is restored.

The stacking fix covers every surface that already matches `OPEN_BROWSER_OVERLAY_SELECTOR`, so individual dialogs or notices don't need changes.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/lib/browser-overlay-sync.test.ts src/main/window-composition.test.ts src/main/browser-view-host.test.ts src/renderer/hooks/useBrowserView.test.tsx src/renderer/native-composition-cascade.test.ts`: all pass.
- New tests:
  - `restackShell` raises the shell only while an overlay is open.
  - The host calls `onNativeViewAdded` after each `addChildView`.
  - With two overlay subscribers, unmounting one does not lower the shell.
  - An overlay that is already open when the tracker subscribes raises the shell.
  - The notice never sets `data-browser-native-overlay`.
  - `noticePlacement`: default corner, page elsewhere, move beside a docked page, hide when there's no room.
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in `frontend/src`.
- Manual check in the Electron desktop dev app (macOS) on this branch: the update notice and the New task dialog stay above the live browser page. The notice-input change (second commit) still needs a manual check.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

title: fix(harness): turn Droid's own auto-update switch back on for its update
body:
## Problem

Updating Droid from AO could fail like this, even for the copy at the official installer's location (`~/.local/bin/droid`):

```
Error: the update finished, but the installed version 0.159.1 did not reach the requested version 0.242.1
Output:
Auto-update is not available for npm installations.
Run: npm update -g @factory/cli
```

`droid update` checks Droid's own auto-update switch. When `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED` is `false`/`0`, or the build turns auto-update off (as Droid's npm build does), it prints that message and exits 0 without updating. The message is misleading: an official-installer copy prints it too. Reproduced with `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false droid update` on Droid 0.242.0, installed with the official installer.

## Fix

When the user asks AO to update Droid through the official installer, `droid update` now runs with `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=true`, which overrides that switch (Droid reads a truthy value before its build default). This applies only to vendor self-update commands, through a small per-target `vendorUpdateEnv` map, so another vendor with the same kind of switch can be added there.

## Tests

- `TestDroidUpdateTurnsDroidsAutoUpdateBackOn`: the update command runs with `FACTORY_DROID_AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=true`.

title: feat(agents): per-folder Claude Code and Codex accounts
body:
Code changes: +3637 -126  
Tests: +1184 -2  
Others: +1818 -17 (generated sqlc, OpenAPI spec and TS schema; 8 locale catalogs)

## Summary

**Developer-mode preview.** Turn on Settings → General → Developer mode to see it. Accounts are managed on Harness → Claude Code (or Codex) → Account, and each session's Summary shows its account. Without developer mode nothing changes from `main`: Settings keeps its Subscriptions page with the Codex account switcher, and no account UI appears. Not gated, on purpose: the two general fixes below (Codex v0.162 terminals, graceful chat stop) apply to everyone; migrations 0210–0212 run for everyone but stay inert until an account is added; accounts added in developer mode stay in effect if it is turned off later (the daemon does not see that renderer setting).

Adds Claude Code and Codex **subscription accounts that are plain CLI config folders**. AO launches the unmodified `claude` / `codex` binary with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` pointing at the account's folder. Sign-in is each CLI's own (`claude auth login`, `codex login --device-auth`). There is no proxy, no service to run, and AO never reads or stores a token.

- **Your CLI's own login is an account.** The login your CLI already has shows up by its email, tagged "CLI login", with no setup. AO launches it with the CLI's own folder untouched. Accounts are named by their email everywhere; a Claude CLI login that reports no email (a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` login) is "OAuth token"; AO does not read the token to tell tokens apart.
- **Add more accounts in AO.** Switching in AO never changes the CLI outside AO.
- **Each task runs on an account.** New tasks use the provider's default. Sessions on different accounts run side by side.
- **Move a session after its turn.** Chat and terminal both work. The move is a transaction: B's agent resumes the same native conversation before the session is rebound, and a failure leaves the session on A. A turn that is still working, for example one waiting for the old account's limit to reset, can be stopped and moved after a confirmation.
- **Every limit of every account.** Claude's 5-hour, weekly and per-model windows plus extra usage come from the CLI's own `get_usage` control request. Codex windows and reset credits come from its app-server. They appear on each CLI's Harness Account tab and in each session's Summary.
- **Statistics.** Tokens each account used in AO over the last 30 days. Usage is attributed through a time-stamped session→account binding history, so a moved session's usage splits correctly.
- **The right account.** Each folder is checked against the login it was added with. Credential env vars (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) are cleared for account launches. A login that already exists is refused, the computer's own included. A picked account must be signed in.

- **Upgrades keep old sessions where they are.** Migration `0210` binds every existing session to the computer's own login at its creation time. No running agent restarts.
- **Also fixed: Codex v0.162 terminals.** Codex v0.162 draws its composer as `»`; AO's screen reader knew only `›`, so no idle Codex terminal could be switched (Terminal → Chat on `main` too) or moved. Separate commit `c9316cf`, easy to split out.
- **Also fixed: a stopped chat agent no longer leaves its command running.** AO stopped chat agents with SIGKILL at once; Claude Code stops the commands it runs only on SIGTERM or SIGHUP, so a dev server or build kept running with no agent. Chat stops now send SIGTERM, wait up to 2 s, then SIGKILL (`process.TerminateGroup`), as terminal sessions already do. Commit `c0e9cd5`; `837b824` widens the daemon's wait for the chat host to exit from 5 s to 10 s to cover the longer shutdown (on a loaded machine a move otherwise ended in `SOURCE_STOP_UNCERTAIN`).

- **Changes made on an account stay there.** Settings and MCP servers are shared key by key (`env` and `mcpServers` entry by entry). A key follows This computer until it is changed on the account; from then on the account's value stays. A small `.ao-shared.json` in each folder records what AO last wrote.
- **A folder that cannot link is refused.** If an account folder cannot link to this computer's history, sign-in, binding and moves refuse it (`AGENT_ACCOUNT_UNSHARED`) instead of letting the CLI start history of its own there. On Windows the links need Developer Mode.

History stays shared, so a resume works across accounts. Each folder keeps only its own login, settings copy and app-server daemon state. Everything a conversation needs (`projects`, `sessions`, history, skills, plugins, …) is a link back to the computer's own folder, recreated at every launch.

## How it works (two-minute version)

An account is a separate config folder for the CLI. AO picks the folder per session, and moves a live session between folders with the same durable handoff the Chat ↔ Terminal switch uses.

1. **Accounts are folders.** Claude Code reads `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and Codex reads `CODEX_HOME`. Each extra account is a folder under `~/.ao`, signed in by the CLI's own login in an embedded terminal. AO never reads or stores a token; it asks the CLI who is signed in and what the limits are. The computer's own login is the implicit "device" account.
2. **Shared history, private login.** Each account folder links the device folder's history and project data, so every account sees the same conversations. `settings.json` and MCP servers are shared key by key through a ledger (`.ao-shared.json`), so an edit made on one account stays there. Login files stay private to each folder.
3. **Binding.** `session_agent_accounts` records which account a session uses, with history for usage attribution. `runtimeEnv()` applies that account's env on every launch path (spawn, restore, resume, chat, terminal). The migration binds existing sessions to the device login.
4. **Moving a live session** reuses `session_interface_transitions`, same mode, different account:

   ```
   preflight B (A still running) -> drain or interrupt -> prove A stopped -> start B -> commit binding
                    failure before commit -> stop B, restart A on A;  daemon crash -> boot recovery
   ```

   The binding is the commit point, and only one writer per conversation runs at any time.
5. **UI (developer mode).** Harness → Account lists accounts and limits; the session Summary shows the session's account and switches it.
6. **Fixes found on the way (for everyone).** Chat agents get SIGTERM before SIGKILL; `exit-agent` keeps terminal sessions live (`runtime_released_launch_id`); the Codex `»` composer.

## Design: an account move is a transaction

**Problem.** The first version moved a session by stopping the agent, rebinding it, then resuming it. During that gap the session was saved as *Exited*, so the chat screen showed "The agent controller stopped" for about 20 s. A failed resume left the session stopped and already rebound.

**Constraint.** A provider allows one live writer per conversation (Codex `thread-writer-locks`, Claude's single transcript file). So B's agent cannot start while A's still runs: the gap can be shortened and made safe, but not removed.

**Design.** A move uses the durable handoff saga that the Chat ↔ Terminal switch already uses (`session_interface_transitions`). It names a source and a target account, and the mode stays the same. Everything that can fail runs first; the binding is the commit point.

| Phase | What happens | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| preflight | A keeps running. AO checks B's login, launch auth in B's environment, and that B's folder can see the conversation. | Abort. Nothing was touched. |
| drain | The current turn finishes, or is interrupted after the user confirms. | Abort. Nothing was touched. |
| source stop | A stops, and the stop must be proven. | Unproven stop → `recovery_required`; AO never starts a second writer. |
| target start | The conversation resumes with B's environment (an in-memory override); the binding still names A. | Stop B, restart A on A. |
| commit | The session is bound to B. | Same rollback. |

**Continuity.** Preflight proves that B's folder can see the conversation. If the provider still cannot resume it when B starts, a terminal follows the [ordinary Terminal restore policy](docs/architecture.md) and starts fresh, as any terminal restore on `main` does; Chat rows stay intact.

If the daemon exits mid-move before the commit, recovery stops anything started under B, and the binding still names A. If the binding already names B, recovery keeps B's agent.

**Why this shape.** There is one state machine for every controller replacement: the interface switch, the account move, and later auto-switch at a limit. The move inherits its message queueing and input fences, cancellation before the stop, rollback, crash recovery, and the UI's in-progress state. Every client shows "Switching to B…" instead of the stopped-controller banner.

**Schema and API.**
- Migration `0211` adds `source_account_id` and `target_account_id`, and widens `CHECK (source_mode <> target_mode)` to `… OR target_account_id <> ''`.
- `PUT /api/v1/agents/accounts/sessions/{id}` starts the move and answers `202` with the transition.
- Progress uses the existing `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interface-transition`.

## Terminal sessions stay live after their agent exits (`3967cbd`)

**Problem (also on `main`).** `ExitAgent` (used by `ao session exit-agent` and by account removal) destroys a terminal agent's runtime and keeps the session. The reaper then probed the dead runtime and the lifecycle read it as a crash: an exited agent never counts as recent activity. The session was terminated and dropped out of the sidebar.

**Fix.** `ExitAgent` records the launch it releases (`sessions.runtime_released_launch_id`, migration `0212`) before it stops the terminal, inside its agent operation, so no reaper tick lands in between. The lifecycle leaves an exited session whose *current* launch was released live. The marker names one launch: a new launch has a new id, so a crash of any later launch still ends the session. That includes the existing race where the dying agent's exit hook lands before the reaper (`TestRuntimeObservation_RetriesAfterRevisionChangesDuringFinalization` still passes unchanged). A general "exited sessions are never terminated" rule broke that crash case, so it was not used.

Lab run with real agents:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove an account bound to a live Claude terminal | `exited`, `is_terminated=0` through five reaper ticks (25 s); terminal gone; still in the sidebar |
| Open that session | Resumed on the default account and replied `STILL-EXITED-THEN-BACK` |
| `exit-agent` on a Codex terminal, three ticks, `resume-agent` | `exited|0`, then replied `CODEX-RESUMED` |
| `kill -9` a live terminal's host (a crash) | Still terminated (`exited|1`) |

## "Stop and move" shows the switch, not a failure (`7af5b77`, `33ec910`)

Moving an agent mid-turn stopped the turn, and the chat then showed "The agent ran into a problem" (or "interrupted by you"). The old agent's reply to the cancel races its shutdown, so the turn could settle as failed. When the move commits, the stopped turn now settles as interrupted and carries an `account.switched` notice: "Switched to <account>. The agent stopped here for the switch. Press Continue to resume this turn, or send a new message." The turn stays continuable. The confirmation says what the agent is doing (still working, or waiting for your decision) instead of guessing at a usage limit.

## Design notes

- `domain` / `ports`: `AgentAccount`, limits and usage types; the `AgentAccountProviderCLI` port, with one adapter per provider in `adapters/agentaccount`; `AgentAccountStore`; `AgentAccountLaunchEnv`, which is the only thing Session Manager depends on.
- `service/agentaccounts`: the catalog (device accounts plus saved ones), cached readings (5 min), the sign-in flow in an embedded terminal, defaults, bindings, usage and the right-account checks.
- Session Manager: account env is applied in `runtimeEnv`, so every launch path picks it up (spawn, restore, resume, chat, terminal). It wins over project env. A session is bound at spawn (rolled back on failure). `StartAccountTransition` runs the move as a controller transition (see the design above). Claude workspace trust (`PreLaunch`) writes to the account folder's `.claude.json`, and the setup-token injector stays out of account launches.
- Storage: migration `0210_agent_accounts.sql` adds `agent_accounts`, `agent_account_defaults`, and `session_agent_accounts`, a binding history that cascades with sessions.
- HTTP: `/api/v1/agents/accounts…`, under the same strict-origin CORS gate as the Codex account routes and blocked on the LAN listener.
- UI (developer mode): a Subscriptions group on Harness → Claude Code / Codex → Account, next to the CLI's own login. The session Summary shows the session's account, its limits, and the switch. In developer mode the Settings Subscriptions page is hidden.

New tests:
- The store attributes usage through the binding history: one session moved between accounts splits its tokens correctly.
- Folder sharing for Claude and Codex: history and config are linked, login and app-server daemon files stay private, and the code is idempotent.
- Credential env vars are cleared for account launches.
- Changes made on an account stay, entry by entry, while untouched keys keep following This computer; a value set back to the computer's follows again.
- A folder that cannot link is refused at sign-in, at bind (default or picked) and at a move; This computer is never refused.
- The service refuses duplicate logins and signed-out or mismatched picks, and binds default accounts.
- The account move: phase order for chat and terminal, rollback on a failed start or bind, a failed preflight leaves the agent running, refusals, boot recovery of an uncommitted target, and boot recovery that keeps a committed one.

- Migration `0210`/`0211`/`0212`: old sessions bound to the computer's login at creation; the widened `CHECK`.
- Lifecycle: a released launch's runtime death keeps an exited session live; an earlier released launch, or none, still terminates. The store writes the release only for the current launch, and a full-row update leaves it. `ExitAgent` records the release before the runtime is destroyed.
- Removal exits only the running agents bound to the account, and a stop that fails keeps the account signed in; a move of an exited agent restarts it on the new account (chat and terminal).
- Sign in again: refused for This computer, cancel keeps the folder, another login is `mismatch` and signed out, the same login comes back on the same account.
- The accounts panel: "Sign in again" only on a signed-out saved account, a closed sign-in is not checked again, and the remove dialog starts without an old error.
- Codex: the history probe follows a linked sessions folder; v0.162 `»` frames read as idle, draft, active and not-started.

Failures I saw locally that are **not caused by this PR**. CI needs to confirm them:
- `opencodev2` `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects` and `integration` `TestClaudeResumeHookConfirmsNativeIdentityForCurrentLaunch` fail identically on a clean `main` checkout on this machine.
- These are load timeouts that pass when run alone: `claudecode` `TestClaudeAuthReportIgnoresStderrJSON` (5/5 alone), `fake` `TestFullLifecycleSpawnToTermination`, Vitest `GlobalSettingsForm` and `SessionMemoryPanel` (`SessionMemoryPanel` compares "38s" against a `Date.now()` offset).

- 24 renderer e2e specs failed under load. All re-passed with `--workers=2` except `chat-composer-text-selection` › "visibly selected". That one also fails in this worktree with `main`'s `frontend/src` checked out, so it is environmental here.
- Windows, mobile, cloud module and docs jobs were not run locally.

## Intentional omissions and follow-ups

- **No account picker in the New Task dialog.** Use "Make default" before starting a task.
- **No automatic switch when an account hits its limit.** It was out of scope for this PR.
- **Main's legacy global Codex account switch is not removed.** Without developer mode it is still the Settings Subscriptions page; in developer mode that page is hidden. Removing or adopting the old code is a follow-up.
- **A move still has a short gap with no live agent.** Providers allow one writer per conversation, so B starts only after A stops. Messages sent during the gap are queued and delivered after the move.
- **MCP OAuth is per account folder.** Claude asks to authenticate MCP servers again on a new account.
- **No sweep of unsaved sign-in folders.** If the daemon restarts mid-sign-in, the unsaved folder under the state dir stays behind.
- **The server's window labels are English** ("Session (5h)", "Weekly · Opus").

This PR is independent of #6274 and does not build on it.

title: feat(chat): copy and save images from the chat via right-click
body:
## Summary

Images in the chat had no way to be copied or saved. Right-clicking an image now opens a menu with **Copy image** and **Save image**. It works on attachment thumbnails, inline image chips, agent-prose images, and the full-size image dialog.

- **Copy image** writes a PNG to the system clipboard. Other formats are re-encoded first. Shows an "Image copied" toast.
- **Save image** opens the native save dialog, defaulting to Downloads with the image's own file name (e.g. `attachment-1.png`), or a name derived from its label.
- Failures show an error toast.

### How

Chat images are cross-origin to the renderer (daemon, remote hosts), so canvas reads would be tainted and `fetch` hits CORS and misses cookies. A new main-process module, `frontend/src/main/chat-image-ipc.ts`, fetches through the sender's own session. It accepts only http(s) URLs and `image/*` responses, capped at 64 MB, and owns the native clipboard and save dialog. Suggested file names are reduced to a base name so they cannot leave the chosen directory.

- New IPC: `chatImage:fetch`, `chatImage:save`, `clipboard:writeImage`, exposed through preload, with browser-preview fallbacks in `bridge.ts`.
- `data:`/`blob:` sources are read in the renderer.
- Menu strings added for all 8 locales.

Images that are themselves links keep the link's existing context menu.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- New `chat-image-ipc.test.ts` and `ChatImage.test.tsx`, plus the ChatMarkdown, i18n and preload suites: 141 tests pass.
- Manually verified in the dev Electron app (isolated data):
  - Right-clicking an attached image shows both items.
  - Copy put a 732×648 PNG on the macOS clipboard matching the attachment, with the toast.
  - Save was confirmed by hand.
- The full frontend suite had unrelated failures in this environment: two suites needing the Electron binary, and two timeouts under load that pass in isolation.

## Risks / follow-ups

- `nativeImage` decodes only PNG/JPEG, so other formats rely on the renderer's PNG re-encode.
- SVGs without intrinsic size may copy at an unexpected size.

title: feat(cloud): multi-repo and standalone cloud projects
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6839.


A cloud project can now work on several repositories at once, or on none. It works the same way on every sandbox provider: Freestyle, managed Coder and bring-your-own Coder. This addresses 11x's feedback (they work across 2 or 3 repositories at once and open linked pull requests) without anything specific to 11x. Every new setting is a normal project setting.

| Need | What this adds |
|---|---|
| A project spans several repositories | A main repository plus up to 10 additional ones (`config.repos`), chosen at creation and editable later. Every session clones them side by side and checks out the session branch in each |
| A shared folder like `~/work/<repo>` | The bring-your-own Coder working folder is now a project setting (`workingDirectory`) that overrides the organization connection's |
| Dev stacks must start before the agent | Each Setup or Cleanup step can name the repository it runs in. Setup still finishes before the agent starts |
| The agent follows each repository's instructions | The agent starts in the main repository with access to the others (Claude `additionalDirectories` and trust, Codex writable roots, secret-file rules on every checkout). The new "Agent starts in: folder with all repositories" setting starts it in the shared folder when that is safe |
| Linked pull requests | The agent can open a PR in any project repository, through the PR socket's `repository` field or `gh pr create` in that repository. AO records them, and webhooks attribute them. The review and files views have a repository switcher |
| A template that brings its own code | Standalone cloud projects: a quiet "No repository? Start without one" link in the create dialog, no repository to pick. Sessions start in an empty git folder or in the configured working folder |
| A custom prompt | Instructions (agent and orchestrator rules) can be edited in project settings. The worker already injected them, but there was no way to set them |

## Also in this PR: cloud Codex Chat failures (fixes #6839, previously #6865)

- **The failure now says why.** A failed cloud Codex Chat turn showed only "Codex turn ended with failed". The worker now reads Codex's own error (from `turn/completed`, the `thread/read` poll, and final `error` notifications). It shows that error's message and details. A lapsed ChatGPT sign-in adds "Sign in to Codex again for Cloud".
- **An unsupported model no longer fails the turn.** Before each Chat turn, the worker checks the requested model against its Codex's `model/list` for that sign-in. A model the sign-in can't run is dropped, the turn runs on Codex's default model, and a notice in the turn says so.
- **Root cause of #6839.** The reported production session (`bb25ca80`) requested `gpt-5.6-sol` with a ChatGPT `auth_json` credential. Reproduced on staging (Codex 0.163.0), Codex rejects it with 400: "The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account." The desktop builds the cloud Codex model list from the local Codex, not the cloud credential, so it offers, and can default to, that model.
- **Follow-ups, not in this PR** (#6080):
  - Cloud should get its own Codex login instead of a copy of the desktop's `auth.json`, whose single-use refresh token goes stale.
  - The control plane should be the single refresher, through `chatgptAuthTokens`.
  - The desktop should list cloud Codex models from the cloud credential.

## Design and compatibility
- The create dialog keeps its existing layout: a new project runs on the organization's default sandbox (Settings), with no per-project sandbox picker.
- No migration. Everything lives in `ao_projects.config`. Projects with none of the new keys behave exactly as before; the legacy `coder.extraRepos` is still read.
- Steps in another repository are stored as plain commands that `cd` into that repository's folder (`domain.RepoScriptCommand`). A control plane rollback or an older desktop release still reads, runs and keeps them.
- Workers advertise `workspace.multi-repo`. The control plane only describes per-repository PRs and where the agent starts to workers that have it.
- An existing sibling checkout, for example one the template already cloned in bring-your-own reuse or working-folder mode, is adopted like the main one. AO stashes local changes, checks out the session branch and never writes to that checkout's `.git/config`.
- The parent folder is refused when it is `$HOME`, `/` or contains AO's `.ao` folder; the agent then starts in the main repository and the prompt says why. The agent's start folder is pinned per session, so conversations still resume after the setting changes.
- Additional repositories must have an active grant in the main repository's GitHub App installation. This is checked when the project is saved and again whenever a token is issued. Folder names that start with a dot are refused.
- Changing repositories, Instructions, where the agent starts, or the working folder is restricted to owners and admins, the same as scripts.
- Deploy order: control plane first, then the desktop release. Older desktop apps keep working against the new control plane.

## Testing
- Unit and integration tests for the domain rules, settings PATCH and create paths, token issuing, PR raise, claim and webhook attribution, the worker's clone, adopt and branch logic, the PR bridge, agent access, parent mode, pinned start folder, repository-scoped review, and the UI create, settings and scripts flows. `cloud`: `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass. Frontend typecheck passes. The renderer suite passes except files that also fail on main in this environment (`browser-profile-import`, `annotate-preload`, `ChatWorkspace`, `ContextMeter`, and a timing-dependent `remote-proxy` test).
- Staging, end to end through the desktop app, on bring-your-own Coder with an 11x-like template. Main repository plus 2 additional repositories:
  - Every checkout lands at `~/work/<name>` on the session branch, and per-repository Setup ran in the right folders before the agent started.
  - The `.git/config` of a template-cloned sibling stayed byte for byte unchanged through adoption, a push and a PR.
  - The agent opened PRs on two additional repositories, both tracked with repository labels; `gh pr create` from a sibling was claimed.
  - Cleanup ran in the additional repository on delete. Instructions were followed, and the repository switcher works.
  - Parent mode works on `~/work` and falls back on the managed layout.
  - A standalone project worked, and the single-repository regression passed. Invalid edits were refused with clear messages.
- Second staging pass (release with the fixes): every fix verified. It found that Claude, started in the main repository, never loaded a sibling repository's `CLAUDE.md`, because the settings' `additionalDirectories` grants access only. Claude terminals now open each sibling with `--add-dir` and Chat passes them as ACP `additionalDirectories`, both with `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1`. Verified live on staging (Claude Code 2.1.301): in both the terminal and Chat, a fresh session loads the main and the sibling `CLAUDE.md`, and single-repository sessions get no `--add-dir`. Codex follows only the starting repository's `AGENTS.md`, and Claude's `AGENTS.md` handling varied between runs. So a multi-repository session's prompt now lists each checkout's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` and asks the agent to read and follow them before working in that repository.
- Third staging pass, on Freestyle and Codex (a test org given a temporary staging entitlement, restored afterwards):
  - Freestyle with Claude:
    - Three repositories land under `/workspace` on the session branch.
    - Setup ran in each repository before the agent, and the sibling `CLAUDE.md` loaded.
    - PRs were opened in additional repositories, through the socket and through `gh pr create`.
    - The repository switcher works, a Chat round trip works, and "folder with all repositories" falls back to the main repository with the prompt note.
  - A standalone project and a single-repository project both work on Freestyle.
  - Codex on bring-your-own Coder works in both the terminal and Chat: commits in a sibling with no sandbox denial, a PR in an additional repository, and `.env` blocked.
  - Codex Chat on Freestyle works, including a PR in an additional repository.
  - The #6839 fallback works on staging, in both a fresh Chat and a terminal-to-Chat switch where the thread was created on `gpt-5.6-sol`: the notice shows and the turn runs on Codex's default model. The first version of the fallback only changed the turn's model, and the thread kept the old one; that was fixed in `6a1b3cb07`.
- The instruction-file note was verified on staging on bring-your-own Coder. Each of three repositories had only its own `AGENTS.md` (main: end with KIWI; Assignment20: start with LIME; Assignment11: start with PLUM). Claude in the terminal, Codex (GPT-5.6-Terra) in the terminal, and Claude in Chat all answered questions about each sibling repository with "LIME ... KIWI" and "PLUM ... KIWI".
- Bugs found on staging have been fixed in this PR: the settings dialog could not be closed after an invalid edit; `{repo}` was silently ignored in a standalone working folder; standalone workers got a 403 on startup; standalone settings still showed branch and PR options.

## Known limits
- AO's background branch-head reporting and PR commit checks still cover only the main repository. PRs on additional repositories are created, recorded and attributed from webhooks. Extending those checks needs a schema change, left as a follow-up.
- Admin-only enforcement was not exercised with a member account on staging; unit tests cover it.
- Sessions still each get their own workspace; several sessions sharing one machine through worktrees is a separate follow-up.

## Seen while testing, not caused by this PR
- `.env` protection is only on for bring-your-own Coder connections (`protectSecretFiles`). On Freestyle and managed Coder the agent can read `.env` files in every repository, the main one included.
- A Codex terminal session started on a model its sign-in can't run (the New task default `gpt-5.6-sol` with a ChatGPT login) fails its first turn with the 400. The terminal has no fallback; the real fix is listing cloud Codex models from the cloud credential.
- After a failed Codex terminal turn, the session stays "working", so "Switch to Chat" only offers "Finish work, then switch", which never finishes.
- A session whose only PR is in an additional repository shows no repository label; the label appears once a session has PRs in two repositories.
- Claude Code 2.1.287 and later shows "Make auto mode your default permission mode?" in every new cloud terminal, which blocks typing and AO's injected messages until answered. `permissions.disableAutoMode` would hide it, but AO offers Claude's auto permission mode, so it needs its own fix.
- In Chat, "Use agent permissions" maps to ACP mode "default", so Claude asks before every edit, while the same session's terminal runs without prompts.

title: fix(mobile): ask for notification permission after a QR scan
body:
## Summary

Freshly paired devices never get registered for push notifications unless the user finds the Settings → Notifications switch. Since #3399, the automatic post-connect registration in `PushManager` runs with `{ ask: false }`, so it never shows the OS permission prompt — and nothing else in the scan/pair flow asks.

This restores the native permission prompt at scan time: after a successful QR pair, `pair.tsx` calls `registerForPush(result.config, { ask: true })`.

- **New device:** native "Allow notifications?" prompt appears; if allowed, the device registers with the paired machine immediately.
- **Already granted** (e.g. adding a second machine): no prompt, just registers.
- **Permanently denied:** OS won't re-prompt; no-op (Settings switch still routes to system settings).
- **Simulator / failed scan:** no-op.

Automatic post-connect/foreground registration is unchanged and still never prompts.

## Notes

- Only the QR scan path prompts; the manual-connect sheet does not.
- No custom priming UI — just the native OS prompt, as before #3399.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` (packages/mobile) — passes
- `npx vitest run` (packages/mobile) — 214 files / 1908 tests pass
- Not yet verified on a physical device.

title: fix(mobile): say when a pairing code only works on the local network
body:
Code changes: +152 -9  
Tests: +148 -3  
Others: +32 -0 (translations)

## Problem

Away from home on 5G, re-pairing failed with **"Reached nothing at 192.168.88.7:3011. Is Connect Mobile still on, and is your phone on the same Wi-Fi?"** even though remote access was on and the Cloudflare tunnel was healthy (verified from outside the network).

Decoding the photographed QR that was scanned showed why. It carried only two endpoints, **LAN and Tailscale, with no tunnel**. Since #5981, the desktop shows the QR as soon as any endpoint exists and adds the tunnel 30–60 s later. A code captured in that window looks identical to a complete one. The phone can only race what the code carries, and its error then named the first endpoint (always LAN) and blamed Wi-Fi.

## Changes

**Desktop (Settings → Mobile)**
- New `localOnlyReason()`: when the displayed code has no **public tunnel** because remote access is still starting or failed to start, a note under the address says so. A LAN-only code is labelled "works on this network only". A code that carries a Tailscale address is labelled "no public tunnel — away from this network the code works only over Tailscale", since the tailnet does reach the machine remotely. The "starting" note has a spinner and tells people to wait for the code to update. The note disappears once the tunnel is in the code.
- The LAN code still appears immediately (keeps #5981's behaviour). Missing cloudflared (`remoteAccessUnavailable`) and `noPublicTunnel` are not double-reported.
- 4 new strings in all 8 locales.

**Phone (pair screen)**
- `describeUnreachableCode()`: when nothing in a scanned code answers:
  - **No public tunnel, but a Tailscale address** (including Tailscale only): says "This code has no public tunnel", lists what it tried, says that away from that network it only works over Tailscale, and asks to connect Tailscale on both devices or rescan once the code includes remote access.
  - **LAN only:** says "This code only works nearby" and to rescan once the code includes remote access. The iOS Local Network hint is kept, because the person may be at home.
  - **Tunnel in the code but it failed too:** says the machine couldn't be reached on this network or over the internet, without blaming Wi-Fi. On iOS, when the code includes a home-network address, the Local Network hint and Settings button stay, because a tunnel that's briefly down plus a denied permission fails both probes.
- `pairFromCode` `verify-failed` now carries the HTTP status and the endpoint that won the race. A rejected password reads as a rejection at that address instead of "Reached nothing at <LAN>".

## Screenshots

Captured with the repo's fake bridge and a mocked `/api/v1/mobile/status`:
- Remote access starting: LAN-only code, spinner and note
- Remote access failed: LAN-only code, static note

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `npm run typecheck` ✅, `npm test` ✅ (214 files, 1914 tests)
- `frontend`: `npm run typecheck` ✅, `npm run typecheck:e2e` ✅, `npx vitest run` ✅. The first run had 2 failures in `src/main/` (`browser-view-host`, `provider-auth-flow`) because the Electron binary hadn't finished installing locally; they pass after installing it (220 tests). Neither file is touched here.
- Not run locally: `npm run build`, docs build and the renderer Playwright smoke suite. These will be checked in CI.

## Not in this PR

Quick-tunnel hostnames still rotate whenever cloudflared restarts, so a correctly paired phone that's away from home can still lose the machine. The planned follow-up is to publish the current tunnel address to the account so the phone can rediscover it without rescanning. That's a separate PR.

title: fix(browser): center the address bar between the inspector tabs and actions
body:
Code changes: +13 -16\
Tests: +39 -12\
Others: +0 -0

## What

The Browser address bar in the session inspector header now sits centered in the space between the left tab icons and the right-hand actions, however many tabs are shown.

## Why

The header used three columns with equal-width outer columns, which centered the address field on the whole inspector. A session starts with 3 left tabs, then gains Files and Artifacts. As the tabs grew, the field ended up crowding the left icons and leaving a large gap before the right icons.

## How

- `.session-inspector__topbar--browser` now uses `max-content minmax(0, 1fr) max-content` columns. The field is centered inside the middle column (`justify-self: center`, `width: min(100%, 240px)`), so it re-centers itself whenever the tab count changes. This is the same layout the Files tab's filter field already uses.
- While editing, the field still widens to `min(100%, 52cqw, 560px)`. Below a 440px container width it still moves to its own row (that rule is unchanged).
- Removed the `--inspector-tab-count` / `--inspector-tabs-reserve` width math. Content-sized side columns make it unnecessary, so `SessionInspectorShellView` no longer sets the inline variable.

## Testing

- Checked in an isolated Electron dev instance with sessions showing 3, 4 (Files) and 5 (Files + Artifacts) left tabs. The address bar stayed centered between the two icon groups in each case.
- `npm run product-ui:check`: typecheck, 160 tests, build all pass.
- `frontend`: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` pass. In `npx vitest run`, 486 of 487 files pass. The one failing file, `src/main/browser-profile-import.test.ts`, fails locally because the `better-sqlite3` native module was built for a different Node version. That file is unrelated to this change; CI is the source of truth for it.
- Browser centering Playwright coverage now checks the midpoint between the tabs and actions, compact-row centering, and added tabs through six. Both focused cases pass.
- Full `CI=true npm run test:e2e:renderer` on local macOS / Node 26: 86 passed, 2 chat tests failed (`chat-agent-switch` and pointer-drag text selection). Both browser-centering cases pass. A focused rerun passes agent switching; pointer-drag selection still fails locally. Docker is not running, so the pinned Linux / Node 24 environment is verified in GitHub CI.
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` passes after the test update.
- `test:browser-postcondition-integration` was not run locally; the initial GitHub Frontend test job passed it. On commit `536aebeba`, remote renderer-smoke, mac-update-helper, and secret scanning pass. The broader frontend test job is still running.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable

title: feat: add desktop Stay Awake sessions, automation, and Low Power Mode
body:
Code changes: +4899 -53  
Tests: +2503 -0  
Others: +2339 -0  

AO can keep this Mac awake independently of Connect Mobile. Add an indefinite quick control below Archive in Summary session controls, session/AO scope, AO-wide toolbar controls, and a dedicated Stay Awake settings page using the current grouped settings layout.

The settings page offers indefinite, duration, end-at-time, running-app and AO browser download sessions; uptime; lid/display defaults; automatic activation rules; battery/critical-heat protection; and automatic Low Power Mode. Requests and rules are daemon-owned and persisted in SQLite. Desktop/mobile leases remain independent; all new routes are loopback-only.

Low Power Mode now includes:
- Explicit macOS administrator authorization for one root-owned, account-specific sudoers fragment. It allows only four exact battery/charger Low Power Mode on/off commands, each with a five-second timeout. AO's executable stays unprivileged, and background policy never prompts.
- Revoke authorization in Settings durably disables automation, restores AO-owned changes, and requests administrator approval to remove only the exact account-specific grant. Cancellation keeps automation disabled. A shared native lock, live-owner checks and durable interruption barrier prevent removal from racing new power claims. The [uninstall FAQ](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/54218bba74feddb0e43fd00f8c848f7e6c52bddd/frontend/src/docs/content/faq.mdx) documents cleanup and a manual fallback.
- Battery threshold with three-point hysteresis, serious-heat activation on the current power source, current effective mode, and explicit recovery. Critical heat still stops wake requests.
- A journal persisted before changes, last-owner restoration, preservation of pre-existing preferences and detectable manual overrides, and retained recovery state for failed writes/restores or previous-boot ambiguity. Disabled policy does no host work.

The bundled native helper uses protocol 5 and retains independent monitoring and bounded lease ownership. Existing older registrations require the documented lid-open/off/unload/re-enable upgrade procedure; no live coordinator is silently replaced. See [ADR 0006](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/54218bba74feddb0e43fd00f8c848f7e6c52bddd/docs/adr/0006-desktop-awake.md).

Scope is complete for this PR. The remaining advanced settings controls—display/keyboard/audio effects, selected-app pausing, saved-network recovery, guarded agent reconnection, browser actions and general recovery/history UI—are deliberately deferred. Non-default deferred settings are rejected at the service boundary even on capable hosts; startup durably clears older saved opt-ins before activation and fails closed if that reset cannot be saved. Deferred capabilities report unavailable. The browser-action route, controller operation, generated contract and frontend action are removed. Internal backend/native foundations remain for a later PR and cannot be activated through the shipped settings API. Their scope and acceptance criteria are in [the follow-up document](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/54218bba74feddb0e43fd00f8c848f7e6c52bddd/docs/awake-follow-up-controls.md).

title: [Bug]: Cloud Codex Chat turns fail with a bare "Codex turn ended with failed" and no cause
body: ## Report **Reported by:** @somewherelostt In a Cloud project (`fairly`), a Codex Chat session (`competitor-research`, GPT-5.6-Sol Medium, Full access) fails every turn. The timeline shows "The agent ran into a problem" and then only "Codex turn ended with failed". There's no detail about why it failed or what to do next. The first turn failed after "Worked for 3s". A second message ("Reply with just OK.") also failed, this time after "Worked for 34s", with the same message. Expected: the turn runs, or, if Codex fails, the provider's actual error is shown. ## Agent-collected evidence Collected 2026-10-16 ~22:30 IST on Windows 11 (10.0.26200). Installed app `0.14.3-nightly.202610152038`. - **Reproduction:** confirmed in the installed desktop app (not a dev build). A fresh message to the same cloud session failed again with the identical text. Screenshot is saved locally; I couldn't attach it from the CLI. - **Not checked against the dev build:** a local dev build from `main` uses isolated data with no Cloud sign-in, so it can't run this session. The cloud worker runs server-side, so the deployed control plane/worker version is what matters, and I couldn't determine it. - **Where the message comes from:** `cloud/internal/workerexec/codex_runner.go` (at `main` `f1adfb41b`). The cloud worker produces this exact string in two places, and both include only the turn status: - line ~333: on `turn/completed`, if `event.Turn.Status != "completed"`, it builds `fmt.Errorf("Codex turn ended with %s", event.Turn.Status)`. The payload is decoded into a struct that holds only `ID` and `Status`, so any error detail on the turn is dropped. - line ~398: the 2s completion poll returns the same error when `readCodexTurnStatus` reports `failed`/`interrupted`. - **Hypothesis (not confirmed):** the real cause is in the Codex app-server's turn error (for example auth/ChatGPT login expiry like #6080, or an unsupported model like #6673), but the cloud runner doesn't pass it along. I couldn't read the cloud session's turn records or the worker logs from this machine. ## Related (not duplicates) - #5289: the same "bare failure with no detail" symptom, but for **local** ACP Codex turns (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp`). This report is the cloud worker path. - #6673: cloud native worker failing on an unsupported model (GPT-6-Luna). The model here is GPT-5.6-Sol, and the error text differs. - #6080: cloud Codex ChatGPT logins expiring. A possible cause, not confirmed.

The vendor bug (cmd acp accepts --mod but silently never loads it) cannot be fixed in this repo; this PR records the limitation and locks in our avoidance of the broken channel. No runtime behavior change.

What this does
- commandcodeacp configure(): documents why --mod/--mod-option are deliberately omitted on the ACP path (verified on v1.82.4/v1.83.0: sentinel mod logs under cmd -p --mod, nothing under cmd acp after initialize + session/new).

Verification
- go test ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/commandcodeacp/... passes (incl. new test).
- Targeted session_manager Chat-spawn hook test passes; go vet + gofmt clean on touched files.
- Pre-existing local-only failures, unrelated and unchanged: TestResolveBinaryFindsCommandCodeOnPath and TestResolveBinaryMissingReturnsErrAgentBinaryNotFound fail on machines with command-code installed globally (this machine has cmdc.cmd on PATH); the touched diff does not cover that package.

Upstream root cause (for the vendor report): createAcpCommand registers zero options and runAcp never calls setModPathsOverride/setModOptionsOverride, while bindAgentSession loads the mod host with projectMods:!1, which also gates settings mods.paths. Minimal vendor fix is forwarding the global flags in the acp action and dropping the projectMods:!1 override; the cheaper alternative is rejecting --mod on acp with a clear error.

title: fix(deepseek): deliver AO role prompts on terminal and chat paths
body:
Code changes: +365 -10
Tests: +206 -7
Others: +16 -3

Slice of #6752 — DeepSeek Harness role prompts (Terminal + Chat).

## Install

```bash
$ npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh

changed 608 packages in 1m
```

## Live terminal tests (AO_LIVE_DEEPSEEK=1)

```bash
$ AO_LIVE_DEEPSEEK=1 go test -v -count=1 -run "TestLive" ./internal/adapters/agent/deepseekharness/...

=== RUN   TestLiveHeadlessRejectsAnUnknownSessionID
    live_test.go:85: an unknown --session-id was accepted; output:
--- FAIL: TestLiveHeadlessRejectsAnUnknownSessionID (0.26s)

=== RUN   TestLiveHeadlessBlocksWithoutATask
--- PASS: TestLiveHeadlessBlocksWithoutATask (15.02s)

=== RUN   TestLiveLaunchCommandIsAcceptedByTheBinary
--- PASS: TestLiveLaunchCommandIsAcceptedByTheBinary (0.28s)

=== RUN   TestLiveCredentialStoreLayoutIsAccepted
--- PASS: TestLiveCredentialStoreLayoutIsAccepted (0.25s)
```

3/4 pass. The one failure is a pre-existing expectation mismatch (binary accepts unknown `--session-id`) unrelated to this PR.

## Live chat test (ACP)

```bash
$ AO_LIVE_DEEPSEEK=1 go test -v -count=1 -run "TestLive" ./internal/adapters/chatdriver/deepseekharnessacp/...

=== RUN   TestLiveDeepSeekACPModelCatalog
    live_test.go:43: discover DeepSeek Harness ACP options: chat driver incompatible: ACP initialize: {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"error":"peer disconnected before response"}}}
--- FAIL: TestLiveDeepSeekACPModelCatalog (0.27s)
```

ACP needs credentials; the initialize handshake disconnects without them.

## Windows npm shim: command line too long (review evidence, fixed)

The review showed the terminal path failing on Windows: npm installs `dsh` as a `.cmd` batch shim, and Windows hands batch files to cmd.exe, whose `/c` input line is capped near 8,191 characters — while the task with generated standing instructions measured 15,812 characters. The short pre-PR control passed, isolating the failure to the length.

Reproduced locally with a 9,314-character prompt:

```text
# via the npm dsh.cmd shim (what the runtime resolved before this commit)
cmd.exe /c dsh.cmd --profile headless "<9300-char task>"
  The command line is too long.        exit 1   # dsh never started

# via the shim's own target, started directly (what the adapter now rewrites to)
node "...\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh\lib\bin.js" --profile headless "<9300-char task>"
  (process started)                    exit 0
```

The fix rewrites the launch argv when the resolved binary is a batch shim whose npm shape parses: the Node runtime beside the shim (or on PATH) plus the package entry point run directly under CreateProcess's 32,767-character limit. The rewrite is conservative — a shim AO cannot parse, with a missing entry point, with a non-Node interpreter, or without a locatable Node runtime keeps the original argv so the original path still reports its own error, and native `.exe` binaries are never rewritten. Semantics mirror the generic `agentlaunch` resolver proposed in #6239; once that lands at the session-manager boundary, this package-local rewrite is a no-op there.

## Chat: independently verified by review

The reviewer verified the Chat path in the real Electron desktop app with a standing-instruction canary appended verbatim on the first and second turns (`AO6845_ROLE_OK`), in `chat` mode — the preamble is delivered and followed across turns.

## Terminal role prompt injection

Standing instructions prepended to the positional task:

```
dsh --profile headless "Standing instructions from Agent Orchestrator. Follow them for this whole session:
<ao_standing_instructions>
You are an AO worker. Follow AGENTS.md conventions. Use `go test` before committing.
</ao_standing_instructions>

Task:
Add a health check endpoint"
```

Inline wins, file is the fallback. Empty task still fails loudly instead of hanging on stdin. Applies to launch + `--session-id` restore.

## Chat role prompt injection

`SessionPreamble` text block on the first turn of a fresh conversation (same shape as agyacp). The shared ACP driver does not repeat it when resuming a session that already has prior turns, so it is never duplicated mid-conversation.

## What changed

- Terminal: standing instructions prepended to the positional task with `<ao_standing_instructions>` delimiter.
- Chat: `SessionPreamble` text block on the first turn of a fresh conversation.
- Windows: npm `.cmd` shim launches resolved to the shim's Node target directly, so a long task survives CreateProcess's 32,767-character limit instead of dying on cmd.exe's 8,191 cap.
- Docs: `docs/harnesses/deepseek-harness.md` updated (delivery model, first-turn-only preamble on resume, shim limit note).

## Intentional omissions

- No live `dsh` run with a real role prompt on this machine verifying the model obeys the delimiter vs. treating it as task text (no DeepSeek credentials here yet); the Chat path has reviewer desktop verification (marker above). The launch/test acceptance tests pass but terminal model behavior is not asserted by a test.
- Other #6752 harnesses (Cursor, AGY, Kimi, Autohand, Copilot) left for follow-up slices. Command-Code already covered elsewhere.
- The generic session-manager shim resolution itself ships in open PR #6239; this PR scopes the equivalent rewrite to the DeepSeek adapter so this harness is fixed now and stays a no-op when #6239 lands.

title: feat(shortcuts): add Open orchestrator keybind (⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+G)
body:
## What

Adds an **Open orchestrator** command to the keyboard shortcut catalog.

| Platform | Default |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | ⌘⇧O |
| Windows / Linux | Ctrl+Shift+G |

Windows/Linux can't take Ctrl+Shift+O: that is already **Open in editor** there (plain Ctrl+O is a readline key, so that command carries Shift). G reads as "go to orchestrator". The binding is customizable in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts like every other command.

## Behavior

The shortcut does exactly what the topbar Orchestrator button does for the project in scope, via the same `useProjectOrchestratorAction` hook:

- running orchestrator → navigate to it
- exited orchestrator → resume and open
- none yet → spawn (cloud projects spawn a cloud orchestrator)
- no orchestrator agent configured → open project settings

It is a no-op on the root board (no project in scope) and stands down while the Settings page covers the session, matching archive / open-in-editor / copy-path. Only one `ShellTopbar` is mounted at a time, so it fires once; the hook's `isMutating` guard also dedupes a double press.

Delivered through the main-process `before-input-event` matcher like the rest of the catalog, so it works while xterm or the native Browser view has focus.

title: feat(mobile): add the desktop color themes to the mobile app
body:
## Summary

Brings the desktop app's 20 color themes to the mobile app. A new **Settings → Theme** screen lists every theme with a swatch and applies it on tap. The existing Appearance row still picks light, dark, or system, and each theme has both versions.

- **Shared catalog.** The named palettes and the OKLab color math move from `frontend/src/renderer/lib/` to `packages/shared/theme/`. The desktop modules re-export them, so desktop behavior and imports are unchanged.
- **Mobile palette.** `packages/mobile/lib/themeDerive.ts` maps a shared palette onto the mobile `Theme` slots and keeps the phone's conventions:
  - Buttons and other primary actions stay colorless (the theme's text color), so a filled button can't be mistaken for a worker state. Catppuccin and Dracula use the same purple as "merged" for their accent.
  - State colors keep their mobile meanings: orange is working, the palette's yellow is "needs you".
  - Light themes use the grouped-list layout: a slightly darker base under lighter cards.
  - Text and state colors are adjusted until they reach 4.5:1 contrast on the base they render on.
- **New `highlight` and `selection` slots.** `highlight` carries the theme's accent for links, text selection, and the cursor. It falls back to the text color when the accent sits within 0.08 OKLab of an attention state (working, needs you, failing, ready). `selection` is a translucent `highlight` for Android text selection. For Orchestrate both match today's values, so the default look is unchanged.
- **No flash on launch.** The root layout reads the saved theme while the splash screen is still up, so the first frame already uses it.
- **Persistence and terminal.** The choice is saved under `ao.theme-style`, the key desktop uses. The terminal's ANSI colors follow the theme, built the same way desktop builds them.

Syncing the theme from desktop ("Match desktop") is left for a follow-up. Desktop keeps its choice in local storage only, so that needs a small daemon change.

## Screenshots

Settings → Theme on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator, for all 20 themes in dark and light.

Grids of all 20 themes, with each theme's name under its screenshot, are in the comments below: [dark](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6857#issuecomment-6232029456) · [light](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6857#issuecomment-6232029639). The images live on the asset branch `ao/agent-orchestrator-mo-198/mobile-themes-screenshots`, which is not meant to be merged.

## Testing

- `packages/mobile`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run`: 2085/2085 passed. New `themeDerive.test.ts` checks every theme in both modes: all slots filled, text, state and highlight colors at 4.5:1 or better on the base, faint text at 3:1 or better, colorless primary actions, light cards lifted off the base, and complete terminal colors.
- `frontend`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; theme and settings tests passed (613).
- Manual: a debug build on a simulator, paired to a local daemon. Checked the board, the theme picker, and a session in several themes. Tapping a theme applies it immediately and it survives a relaunch.
- Manual: a Release build installed on a physical iPhone 13.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Light themes look darker on the phone than on desktop, because the contrast adjustment darkens state colors on the darker base (e.g. Catppuccin light orange `#f15800` becomes `#a43900`). This matches how the default light palette already darkens them.
- In themes whose accent matches an attention state (Monokai, Ayu, Everforest, Vitesse, Flexoki, and Rosé Pine light), links, selection and the cursor use the colorless text color instead of the accent, so they never pass for a status.

## Bug

In the desktop app's **light theme**, the terminal pane becomes unreadable: the pane background switches to white, but the transcript text keeps light-theme-incompatible light colors — the content is still there (faint white-on-white "ghost" lines, partially visible when scrolling), but practically invisible. The rest of the UI (sidebar, inspector, status line) renders fine.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session with terminal/chat content in the desktop app.
2. Switch the app theme to **light**.
3. Look at the terminal pane: transcript text is white-on-white "ghosts"; session history and agent output cannot be read.

## Expected behavior

Two acceptable fixes, in order of preference:

1. **Terminal keeps its own palette in both themes** — this is what the project's own `DESIGN.md` already prescribes ("the terminal keeping its own palette"); the pane should stay dark regardless of UI theme.
2. At minimum, when the pane background goes light, the xterm theme must switch foreground + ANSI palette to dark-readable values.

The current state — background themed, foreground not — is the worst combination: the pane looks themed but the content is unreadable.

## Notes

- The agent CLI (Claude Code) only emits ANSI text designed for a dark terminal; it does not control the pane background. The broken layer is the renderer's theme switch.
- A screenshot is available on request; omitted here to avoid exposing unrelated workspace details.

**Priority:** high for light-theme users — primary working surface (transcript) is unreadable; no workaround except staying in dark theme.

**Confidence:** High — reproduced live on the current desktop build.

## Environment

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64)
- Build: desktop app self-built from a recent upstream `main` (nightly line 0.14.x)
- Surface: session terminal pane (xterm-based transcript) in light theme

title: fix(cloud): a failed Codex Chat turn says why
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6839. A cloud Codex Chat turn that failed showed only "Codex turn ended with failed".

1. **The failure now says why.** The worker read the failed turn's status but dropped the error Codex attaches to it. It now reads that error from `turn/completed`, the `thread/read` poll, and final `error` notifications (`willRetry: false`): the `message`, `additionalDetails` and `codexErrorInfo` fields. The timeline shows Codex's message and details, bounded to 600 characters. A lapsed ChatGPT sign-in (an `unauthorized` reason, or "refresh token was already used" or 401) adds "Sign in to Codex again for Cloud". With no reason given, the turn still says "Codex turn ended with failed".
2. **An unsupported model no longer fails the turn.** Before each Chat turn, the worker checks the requested model against this Codex's own `model/list` for its sign-in. A model the sign-in can't run is dropped, the turn runs on Codex's default model, and a notice in the turn names the model that was dropped. If the list is unavailable, the requested model is used as before.

## Root cause

Production session `bb25ca80` (project "fairly", Freestyle, Codex), checked read-only:
- The Chat turns at 16:33 and 17:58 UTC on Oct 16 each failed about 3 seconds after Codex started. The second turn requested `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- The user's cloud Codex credential is a ChatGPT `auth_json` login.

Reproduced on staging with a ChatGPT `auth_json` credential and Codex 0.163.0, where the New task dialog had defaulted to GPT-5.6-Sol. Codex's own error was:

```
{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
```

With that account, Codex's model list is GPT-6-Luna, GPT-5.6-Terra and GPT-5.6-Luna.

The desktop builds the cloud Codex model list from the local Codex catalog, not the cloud credential (`TaskComposer.tsx`; only opencode is scoped by credential). It therefore offers, and can default to, a model the cloud sign-in can't run. The worker then reported that 400 only as "Codex turn ended with failed".

## Related risk, not changed here

The cloud credential is a copy of the desktop's `~/.codex/auth.json`, and this user's copy was saved on Oct 1 and never updated. ChatGPT refresh tokens are single-use, so the copies go stale once either side refreshes. Part 1 of this PR makes that failure readable with sign-in guidance. Preventing it needs the #6080 follow-up: Cloud gets its own login and the control plane is the single refresher, with Codex's `chatgptAuthTokens` login mode. A related follow-up is to list cloud Codex models from the cloud credential in the desktop.

## Testing
- `TestCodexTurnFailureSaysWhy`: no reason, empty reason, message plus details, `unauthorized`, refresh token reused, and length bound.

title: fix(remote): stop resetting small complete responses over the tunnel
body:
Fixes #6866

## Summary
Since #6652, the desktop remote proxy sends an HTTPS host's requests over HTTP/2 inside the `/api/v1/tunnel` WebSocket. `relayResponse` treated a body as cut off if its upstream stream was already `destroyed` at `"end"`. Through the tunnel, a small answer's stream closes (code 0) in the same read as its headers. Node emits `"response"` on nextTick, so its own `end → kMaybeDestroy` listener runs first and destroys the **finished** stream before the proxy's check. Every small complete response (`/api/v1/identity`, `/projects`, `/settings`, `/healthz`) was then reset as "upstream stream ended" (`TypeError: terminated` in the renderer). That made quick-tunnel remote hosts unusable in both directions.

The fix judges a cut by the session instead: `session.destroyed || rstCode !== NO_ERROR`. A host restart or closed tunnel destroys the session, and a host reset carries a non-zero code, so both still fail as before.

## Tests
- New regression test: `relays a small body whose tunnelled stream closed before its end`. It uses a tunnel daemon that answers after a short delay and sends its frames as one WebSocket message, as the Cloudflare edge does. It fails on `main` with `TypeError: terminated` and passes with the fix.
- Existing cut-stream tests still pass: tunnel closed mid-body, session destroyed mid-body, preview reset or drop, HTTP/1.1 cut.
- `npx vitest run src/main/remote-proxy.test.ts`: 63 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `verifies the host once per upstream session, before the credential`, whose `afterEach` hook times out on `h2upstream.close()`. It fails the same way on unmodified `main` in this environment, so it is unrelated to this change.
- `remote-registry` and `remotes-main` tests pass (39). `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors under `frontend/src`.
- Live check from the Mac mini against both machines' real quick tunnels, using this branch's `startRemoteProxy`: before the fix, identity/projects/settings fail with `terminated`. After the fix, all of `/healthz`, identity, projects, settings and sessions return 200.

## Risks
- A complete response whose session is destroyed in the same tick, before `"end"`, now fails instead of passing. That fails safe and the renderer retries.

title: fix(ci): build Linux native modules with clang++-15 for Electron 44
body:
## Summary
The Linux x64 desktop artifact build has failed since the Electron 33 → 44 upgrade (#6462). That blocks every nightly, because the release conductor needs all four platforms. Today's nightly (ao-releases run 39017499597, building `5a1ba26a9`) failed in `build (ubuntu-22.04, linux-x64, linux)`. macOS and Windows built fine.

When node-gyp rebuilds `better-sqlite3` against Electron 44's headers on `ubuntu-22.04`, it hits two problems:
1. **GCC 11 can't parse the headers.** `v8-primitive.h:658` declares `class [[deprecated(...)]] __attribute__((visibility)) Value`, and GCC 11 rejects a GNU attribute after a C++11 attribute in a class head (`expected identifier before '__attribute__'`).
2. **clang 14 (the runner's default `clang++`) is too old.** It fixes (1) but fails on `v8-source-location.h`. The 22.04 libstdc++ 11 only provides `std::source_location` when the compiler has `__builtin_source_location`, which arrived in clang 15.

The Linux job now sets `CXX=clang++-15`, which is preinstalled on the 22.04 image. Only C++ changes:
- tmux, ncurses (`--without-cxx`), libevent and the C half of better-sqlite3 still build with GCC.
- The job stays on `ubuntu-22.04` for the glibc baseline (#4616).

## Verification
- `frontend/release-workflows.test.ts`: 6/6 pass.
- Real runner: I dispatched `Desktop build artifacts` from this branch (run 39018823637, version `0.14.3-cxxcheck.2`, no release created). The Linux build succeeded. The first attempt with plain `clang++` (run 39018530045) failed on `std::source_location`, which is why this pins clang 15.
- I downloaded the Linux `.deb` from that run. Its `better_sqlite3.node` requires at most `GLIBC_2.34` and `GLIBCXX_3.4.29`. Ubuntu 22.04 provides glibc 2.35 and `GLIBCXX_3.4.30`, so the Linux floor doesn't move.

## Risks
- If a future runner image drops `clang++-15`, the step fails immediately at `command -v clang++-15` rather than producing a different build.
- I haven't launched the Linux app itself. I only checked the native module's symbol requirements.

title: feat(cloud): let ao spawn start a worker on an existing branch
body:
Code changes: +160 -51  
Tests: +387 -4  
Others: +23 -3 (cloud contract, generated cloud-client schema, using-ao skill doc)

## Why

A Coder customer asked to start a worker on an existing branch. The main case is resuming after a worker stops partway: its branch is already pushed, and a new worker should continue on it. Today every cloud session gets a generated `<prefix>/<short id>` branch cut from the default branch, and the cloud `ao spawn` has no way to name one. Local `ao spawn` already has `--branch`. The agreed direction is to ask the orchestrator rather than add a field to the new-task form.

## What changed

- **`ao spawn --branch <name>`** (`cloud/cmd/ao-cloud-agent`). The branch is sent only when given, so other spawns are unchanged.
- **Control plane.** `POST /worker/children` passes `branch` into `domain.CreateSession.Branch`, which is `omitempty` so the idempotency payload of every other create is unchanged. `createSessionTx` enforces `domain.ValidSessionBranch` on every create path. It refuses names that break git's branch-name rules, the project's default branch (a worker would push to it directly), and the session prefix (its ref would conflict with every generated `<prefix>/<short id>`). The API reports `invalid_branch`.
- **Worker checkout.** A branch that already exists on the remote is continued from its commits instead of being cut from the default branch:
  - Fresh clone (`ConfigureWorkerGit`): `checkout --no-track -B <branch> origin/<branch>` when there is no local branch yet. If local files block that switch, the worker cuts the branch at HEAD as before instead of failing startup. A restarted worker keeps its local branch.
  - Adopted template checkout (reuse existing checkout, or the connection's working directory): adoption bases the branch on `origin/<branch>` when present, and stashes tracked changes even when the checkout is already on the requested branch. Adoption reports whether it created the branch. After the fetch, a branch it created (so with no work of its own) moves onto `origin/<branch>`. That covers a template that cloned before the branch was pushed and a branch rebased since. Any other branch only fast-forwards.
- **PR attribution.** A pull request whose head is in a fork is never auto-claimed for a session, even when its branch name matches a session branch.
- **Contract and docs.** `CreateWorkerChildInput.branch` is in `contracts/cloud/openapi.yaml` (client regenerated). The flag is documented in the `using-ao` skill, the CLI usage text, and the orchestrator prompt. To resume another worker's branch, kill that worker first and have the new one run `ao claim-pr <number>` if a PR exists.

Side effect: if a session's sandbox is re-created after the session already pushed its generated branch, the session now resumes from those commits instead of restarting from the default branch.

## Intentionally not included

- No new field in the desktop new-task form. This is orchestrator-only, per the agreed direction.
- Booting the Coder workspace itself from the branch (passing it into template parameters) is left out. It is only needed for testing template changes and depends on each template's parameter names.
- No guard against two live sessions on one branch. The docs tell the orchestrator to kill the old worker first; enforcement was deliberately left to the user.
- `AdoptedNow` is still not persisted. A worker that restarts between adoption and the post-fetch advance keeps the adopted base. This predates this PR, and the outcome is non-destructive: a push of a diverged branch is rejected.
- The branch length limit counts bytes, like the existing `defaultBranch` validation.
- Extra repos keep their configured branch.

## Validation

- `cloud`: `gofmt -l .` clean, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` all pass (32 packages).
- Each new test failed when its code change was removed: continuing a remote branch on a fresh clone and on an adopted checkout; moving onto a branch pushed after the template cloned, or rebased since; stashing on an already-checked-out requested branch; startup falling back when local files block the switch; not claiming fork PRs; the `invalid_branch` mapping; the CLI request body; and the branch rules (domain table test).
- Postgres store (CI skips these tests): ran `internal/postgres` against a local PostgreSQL 15. 220 tests pass, including `TestCreateSessionKeepsRequestedBranch` (keeps a requested branch, generates one when absent, and refuses the default branch, the prefix and invalid names). Four other tests fail in the same way on unmodified `origin/main` in this environment (`TestCIFailureNotificationPersistsAndResolvesUnderRecipientRLS`, `TestQueuedTurnDoesNotOverrideIdleWorkerActivity`, `TestReviewsSnapshotIndependentReviewerAndSeparateAutoReviewFromInjection`, `TestDisconnectSettlesRunningChatTurnFromRetiredWorker`), so they are unrelated to this change.
- `packages/cloud-client`: `npm run generate` leaves no diff after commit; `typecheck`, `npm test` (29) and `npm pack --dry-run` pass.
- Not run locally: the cloud job's Docker-based "Test Expat security backport" step, because no Docker daemon was available. Left to CI.
