title: fix: bound spawn remote lookup and detach seed-row rollback
body:
## Summary

Two defects together turned a stalled git remote into a silent spawn zombie: the session row appeared in the UI and sat on "Almost there" forever, with no error ever reaching the CLI or any log.

- `gitworktree.Workspace.ResolveDefaultBranch` ran the live `ls-remote` with the raw request context — the only remote call in the spawn path without its own budget (the other two use 5s). A stalled route wedged the whole spawn until the outer REST deadline. Give the lookup the same `defaultBranchResolutionBudget` and fall back to the cached remote HEAD.
- `Manager.rollbackSpawnSeedRow` unwound on the already-canceled context after that deadline fired: both `DeleteSession` and the `markSpawnFailedTerminated` fallback failed silently (`context canceled`), stranding the seed row as a phantom. Run the rollback with the sibling `spawnRollbackContext` helper (detached + `spawnRollbackBudget`), so cleanup survives the deadline and a wedged store write cannot hang the rollback goroutine.

Fixes #6754 — the reported failure mode (spawn wedged on a stalled remote, eternal "Almost there" phantom rows, no error surfaced). Measured reproduction and the code-level anatomy are in the issue. Follow-up scope from that report, intentionally out of this PR: daemon proxy support, the UI failed-state surface (`provision_error` rendering), and the timeout-path error envelope.

## Tests

- `TestResolveDefaultBranchBoundsStalledRemoteLookup` (new): a `git ls-remote` shim that stalls 30s must not hang resolution — the resolver must fall back to the cached `origin/HEAD` within the budget. Fails on the old code (30s > 9s assertion).
- `TestRollbackSpawnSeedRow_SurvivesCanceledContext` (new): rollback on a canceled context must still delete the seed row. `fakeStore.DeleteSession` now mirrors the sqlite driver and fails on a dead context, so this pins the fix.
- `go test -race` on `internal/session_manager`, `internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree`, `internal/gitdefault` — ok. `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — clean.

## Known risks

- The rollback now completes even when the request is gone; sessions that previously leaked as phantom rows will now be properly deleted (or parked terminated if they progressed past seed state). That is the intended behavior, but if anything downstream depended on seeing phantom rows, it will notice.
- The 5s budget on the default-branch lookup matches the two existing remote budgets; repos on very slow but working remotes now resolve from cache instead of waiting longer than 5s for a live HEAD.

title: feat(files): add audio/video previews and fit media to panes
body:
Code changes: +123 -58  
Tests: +446 -4  
Others: +2 -1  

Includes one binary test fixture: an 11,770-byte WebM clip.

## What

Add native audio/video players in Artifacts and current workspace Files, and fit raster image/video previews to the available pane with vertical centering.

## Why

Opening a recording currently shows a binary-file placeholder. Small media also stays at its original dimensions near the top of large file tabs.

## How

Reuse the existing confined streaming routes and native playback/seek controls. Read media headers with GET and immediately cancel the body instead of applying text-file limits, and share the explicit loopback artifact URL between metadata and playback.

Workspace binary fingerprints include nanosecond file modification times from the existing stat result, so equal-size replacements refresh without restarting unchanged playback or reading the whole recording.

Streaming responses include an ETag based on file size and nanosecond modification time. Browser clients can read the header, and private, no-cache responses require revalidation; rapid artifact replacements update the media URL while native range streaming stays intact.

SVG keeps main's rendered/source views. Historical/staged audio/video and cloud-workspace media transport are outside this change; playback depends on Chromium's supported codecs.

- Artifact regression: actual preview/files route tests failed before the fix and pass for PNG, WebM and MP3. They cover same-size rewrites one millisecond apart, size-only changes, browser-readable ETags, cache revalidation, unchanged 304s and If-Range seeking. - Workspace regression: equal-size binary rewrites change the fingerprint in untracked and scratch workspaces, including writes one millisecond apart. All 39 FileContentPane tests passed, covering replacement refresh and unchanged playback.

title: fix(autohand): deliver AO role prompts on the session-start hook
body:
Code changes: +22 -7
Tests: +86 -0
Others: +0 -0

Slice of #6752 — Autohand role prompts on the session-start hook.

## What changed after review

Both review comments were correct, and I verified each against the upstream sources you linked before changing anything.

### 1. Autohand: wrong response shape (your second comment)

Confirmed against `HookManager.parseHookResponse` (`JSON.parse(trimmed) as HookResponse`) and `HookResponse` in `src/types.ts`:

```ts
export interface HookResponse {
  decision?: 'allow' | 'deny' | 'ask' | 'block';
  ...
  /** Additional context to add to conversation */
  additionalContext?: string;
}
```

Autohand is a flat `JSON.parse` of stdout with no `hookSpecificOutput` envelope, so AO's nested shape was silently dropped. Autohand now shares OpenHands' top-level branch, and `openHandsContextHookOutput` is renamed `topLevelContextHookOutput` since it no longer serves one harness. `TestHooks_AutohandSessionStartInjectsTopLevelSystemPromptContext` asserts the top-level field is populated **and** that `hookSpecificOutput` is absent, so a regression back to the nested shape fails the test.

This also confirms the fix reaches the reported case: `HookContext.sessionType` is `'startup' | 'resume' | 'clear'`, AO installs the hook with no `matcher`, so it fires on `autohand resume` too — which is where `--sys-prompt` is unavailable.

### 2. Kimi: dropped from this PR (your first comment)

Confirmed against both sources. `runHook.ts` parses only:

```ts
const HookJsonOutputSchema = z.looseObject({
  message: OptionalStringSchema,
  hookSpecificOutput: HookSpecificOutputSchema,  // { message, permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason }
});
```

and `SessionExternalHooksService.triggerSessionStart` is `Promise<void>` — it awaits `this.runner.trigger('SessionStart', ...)` and returns nothing. There is no field in that schema that reaches Kimi's model context, and the result is discarded anyway, so AO cannot inject standing instructions through a Kimi `SessionStart` hook at all. My change would have printed the asserted JSON while both fresh and restored Kimi sessions still received no instructions — exactly the "tests validate AO's emitted JSON, neither consumer accepts it" failure you described.

Kimi is therefore removed from this PR entirely, including the `systemPromptFileRequired` entry. Kimi has no working context channel in AO today: `.kimi/AGENTS.md` is not read by the current loader, and the hook channel is dead upstream. I traced its `sessionAgentProfileCatalog` but stopped short of guessing at the on-disk profile shape, since a wrong guess is another no-op. Kimi needs its own investigation — I'll track it separately rather than ship another unverified change.

## What the PR now does

`autohand/hooks.go:113-118` already installs `{Event: "session-start", Subcommand: "session-start"}` into `~/.autohand/config.json`. `shouldEmitSessionStartContext` now serves it. Nothing else changes: no adapter argv, no hook schema, no new event name.

`systemPromptFileRequired` gains Autohand. The hook reads `<dataDir>/prompts/<session>/system.md`, so a silent write failure would drop the role prompt rather than degrade to a fallback this CLI does not accept — matching gemini, agy, command-code, devin and openhands.

## Verification

```text
$ go build ./...
$ go test ./internal/cli/ -run "TestHooks_" -count=1
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/cli	19.056s

$ go test ./internal/session_manager/ -run "TestSystemPromptFileRequired" -count=1 -v
--- PASS: TestSystemPromptFileRequiredCoversHookDeliveredHarnesses (0.00s)

$ go test ./internal/adapters/agent/autohand/... ./internal/adapters/reviewer/autohand/... -count=1
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/agent/autohand	1.838s
ok  	github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/autohand	1.171s
```

New tests:

- `TestHooks_AutohandSessionStartInjectsTopLevelSystemPromptContext` — the exact flat contract, with an explicit negative assertion on `hookSpecificOutput`.
- `TestHooks_AutohandSessionStartWithoutSystemPromptFileStaysSilent` — a missing `system.md` must not emit an empty context block.

`golangci-lint` on `./internal/cli/... ./internal/session_manager/...` reports the same 19 pre-existing issues as on a clean `canonical/main` checkout, none in the files this PR touches. The 13 `session_manager` and 2 `kimi` package failures on this Windows machine are also identical with the change stashed.

## Intentional omissions

- **No live `autohand` run.** Autohand is not installed here. The wire contract is taken from the upstream source at commit `3b840ca` that you cited, not from a live session — the same basis as your own review, so a maintainer with Autohand installed would still be the one to confirm end to end.
- **Kimi is out of scope** for the reason above. Cursor and Copilot CLI are in the companion PR (#6896).

Brings back build identity in the titlebar, and fixes how the brand row behaves around the sidebar toggle.

title: fix(agy): deliver AO role prompts through an always-on workspace rule
body:
Code changes: +112 -2
Tests: +171 -0
Others: +0 -0

Slice of #6752 - AGY Terminal UI role prompts on fresh start and resume.

AGY has no system-prompt flag at launch. AO can fire a session-start hook, but on a live agy that output never reaches the model. So managed AGY sessions came up with no AO role prompt, including after resume.

I left .agents/hooks.json alone. #6752 warns that adding SessionStart without a verified contract can make AGY reject the whole file and break Kanban tracking from #4085.

Fix: GetAgentHooks now writes .agents/rules/ao-agent-orchestrator.md with trigger: always_on and AO's standing instructions. AGY loads that on fresh start and on resume. prepareWorkspace calls GetAgentHooks before both. The prompt file wins over inline text. The rule is gitignored. We refuse to overwrite a non-AO file at that path. Uninstall only deletes it if it has AO's marker. Project AGENTS.md is untouched.

Verification: go test ./internal/adapters/agent/agy/... -count=1 passed. Live canary with the rule installed (agy 1.4.2): fresh and --continue both returned HAS_AO_ROLE_PROMPT. Before the fix, installed AO returned NO_AO_ROLE_PROMPT. Also checked that hooks.json still only has PreInvocation / PostToolUse / Stop, and that the rule is gitignored.

title: fix(accounts): read limits again soon after an answer with no windows
body:
Code changes: +13 -1\
Tests: +39 -2\
Others: +0 -0

## What

An account's limits answer with no windows is now kept for 30 seconds instead of the 5-minute cache window, so the next one-minute poll reads the account again.

## Why

After adding a Claude account (a Team login), the session's Account panel showed no limits. The first read ran right after sign-in and Claude's `get_usage` came back with no windows; that is not an error, so the daemon kept it as fresh for 5 minutes. A forced refresh a few minutes later returned Session (5h) 1% and Weekly · Fable 3%. Worst case before this change: about 6 minutes with no limits (5-minute cache plus the 60-second poll). After it: about 1 minute.

## How

- `needsReading` uses a 30-second window when the last reading has limits with no windows; readings with windows keep the 5-minute window.
- Identity checks (`DefaultSignIn`, `pick`) are unchanged: they care about sign-in, not limits.
- Trade-off: a plan that never reports windows is read on every poll, one CLI call a minute while the panel is open.

## Testing

- `TestLimitsWithNoWindowsAreReadAgainSoon`: an empty answer is read again a minute later; an answer with windows is kept. Fails without the fix, passes with it.
- `go test ./internal/service/agentaccounts/`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run ./internal/service/agentaccounts/...` (0 issues).

title: fix(billing): show plan limits apply only to cloud agents
body:
## Summary
The Upgrade page made every plan limit look like it capped all agents. The cloud control plane enforces them only on billed cloud sandboxes (`cloud/internal/postgres/billing_store.go`: `admitCreate` and `sandboxBilledTx`). The local daemon has no plan checks.

- Paid cards and Enterprise list their limits under a sentence-case **Cloud agents** label (an `aria-labelledby` list).
- **Free:**
  - Unlimited local agents on your machine.
  - 2 devices logged in at once.
  - Same-network connectivity (no cloud relay).
  - "No cloud agents" shown with a muted dash instead of a check.
- **Starter** adds the cloud relay for seamless connectivity across devices, and unlimited devices including mobile (bring your own). Cloud agents: 1 cloud project and 2 simultaneous cloud agents.
- **Pro:** Everything in Starter, plus "Bring your own Coder deployment" (moved from Enterprise). Starter's "Instant VMs or Coder dev workspaces" line is removed; the Cloud agents section already covers it. Cloud agents: 5 cloud projects and 20 simultaneous cloud agents.
- **Enterprise:**
  - Adds "Collaborate on cloud agents".
  - Cloud agents: unlimited cloud projects, unlimited simultaneous cloud agents, and no session-hour caps.
- Removed from the cards: total sessions, session-hour windows, the weekly limit and usage resets. The Usage section still shows usage.
- Simultaneous cloud agents = the plan's running slots (`ao_max_running_sandboxes`), with each cloud project's orchestrator on top. Cloud projects = orchestrator slots.
- All 8 locales are updated. Strings that are no longer used are removed.

No marketing/landing pricing page lives in this repo.

## Copy only: enforcement follow-up
This PR doesn't change enforcement. Until the control plane changes, it differs from the cards:
- Orchestrators still use slots from the running pool, so today Starter allows 1 agent beside its orchestrator and Pro allows 15.
- The total-sessions cap (`ao_max_active_sandboxes`, 8 / 30) is still enforced.

A separate change from the cloud team will make enforcement match.

## Tests
- `vitest run BillingSection.test.tsx src/renderer/i18n`: 37 passed.
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in the changed files.
- Checked in the real Electron app (isolated data). I signed in through the dev-only local sign-in against a throwaway loopback stub control plane that returned the Starter and Pro limits, then captured the Upgrade page.
